title: fix(wear): show chat replies after Voice input
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: replies and chat failures stay off-screen when a connected Wear OS user submits Type or Dictate from Voice without an active Live Talk.

## User Impact

Accepted ordinary input now opens Chat, where its reply or error appears. Canceled, empty, and locally rejected input stays on the current page. Active Live Talk keeps its existing Voice routing. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both input results already send ordinary chat, while Voice displays only the Live Talk transcript. Successful local submission now asks the existing navigation owner to open Chat, without recreating the composition, resetting pending replies, or copying ordinary messages into Live Talk.

## Evidence

Final tested head: fb7c5923272a4728154c411e14553405ca7927df (tree 5ae920585f97d993da2ee0b7f41d974906ca45c5). The full 289-test Wear suite was rerun on this exact head; the earlier focused checks and screenshots cover the identical tree.

- Real MainActivity + Compose + activity-result boundary regressions: Type displays an ordinary reply; Dictate displays a remote error; canceled/empty/rejected results retain Voice; ordinary Chat submission and repeated warm launches preserve pending reply ownership.
- Both outcome regressions failed on original production code at 4d28246be9e5b99c48e50f450cbe36d9806836ae because accepted input did not open Chat, then passed with the fix.
- Full Wear unit suite: **289 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Focused navigation/microphone sibling run: **16 passed**. Wear Android lint, Kotlin formatting checks, and repository changed checks passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Existing active-Live routing and warm-launch retention tests remain passing.
- Screenshots below are inspected native-graphics Robolectric captures of the real app with a synthetic phone transport, not mockups. No connected Android device was available; physical-watch, OEM keyboard/recognizer, paired-phone and live-Gateway acceptance were not run.
- Exact-head GitHub [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35285077284): **passed** (including Android Play, third-party, Wear tests, Kotlin formatting, and CI gate).

| Before: Type sends, but Voice hides the reply | After: Chat displays the reply |

title: fix(plugins): recover channels after pending service cleanup settles
body:
Related: #150953

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes channels remaining unavailable after plugin replacement times out observing service cleanup that subsequently finishes successfully.

## User Impact

Affected channels can recover automatically once the original cleanup and admitted work settle within the existing recovery window, instead of requiring a manual retry. The requested replacement still fails; recovery restores the captured previous code and configuration in fresh registrations, not the rejected candidate.

Permanent or mixed cleanup failures, channel-stop failures, failed candidate cleanup, and an exhausted recovery window remain blocking. Manually stopped accounts stay stopped. This does not accelerate slow cleanup or change which plugins a reload selects.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service owner already retains one physical stop promise. This narrowly extends the documented recovery policy to recognize host stop-observer timeouts and observe that original promise before disposing old resources or registering the previous runtime again. It does not call stop twice or reopen the stopped instance.

The shared five-second stop observation deadline, 60-second recovery window, backoff, resource handoff barriers, and existing restart/invoker fences are unchanged. There are no configuration, schema, dependency, or UI-rendering changes. The behavior takes effect when the candidate code is loaded through a normal update/restart; it cannot retrofit an already-running old Gateway.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original exact-head CI failure through the real Gateway `plugins.reload` RPC: the old fixture awaited the reply before releasing its synthetic cleanup, and switched fake/real clocks while recovery was pending. The unchanged test passed with the original production implementation; the revised real-clock regression fails that original implementation at missing recovery.
- Production code is unchanged from the first PR commit. This follow-up repairs the real-RPC fixture and adds mixed permanent/pending service and channel failure controls; it does not lengthen a production, RPC, test, or teardown deadline.
- **534 tests across 39 files passed**, including the entire previously failing 35-file/470-test CI shard on CI-matching Node 24.19.0, plus 64 service ownership tests. Types, type-aware lint, formatting and line-cap checks passed on the same captured inputs.
- Fresh independent source review and the required staged-candidate autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects. The initial index-only finding was resolved by staging the exact reviewed fixture changes, not waived.
- All selected canonical changed-file checks passed on the staged candidate, with no skips or weakened gates.
- Package Acceptance run 35284595674 passed the published `openclaw@2026.9.4` → first candidate `a3356194` custom-plugin-siblings cell, including actual plugin executions and source/state preservation. That is old-head evidence, not qualification of this revised head.

**Exact-head qualification completed:** CI [35288905910](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35288905910) passed for `0e8a27d5b18ead5311a6602e5305c127d382e429` (139 successful jobs, 16 unselected/skipped, zero failed), including the previously failing lifecycle shard. Canonical package/installed-runtime checks and Package Acceptance [35289302727](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35289302727) passed on that same product head and immutable hosted tarball. Published `openclaw@2026.9.4` updater cells proved real plugin executions and configured-channel settings preservation.

**Configured-channel response proof completed:** Package Acceptance [35297547260](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35297547260), attempt 1, passed the scoped cell in 233 seconds with zero retries. The original published `openclaw@2026.9.4` updater installed the unchanged `0e8a27d5b18` artifact (SHA-256 `b9e06e0501e9866ee75306b8e0baf962cf63ad24d81c46d37f46138c90bc37ac`), reporting exit 0 / success / repair false, with captured post-core exit 0. A preconfigured synthetic channel produced distinct nonce-bound replies before and after update; the worker socket generation advanced and the same native session retained both conversation markers. Strict projected configuration/plugin/source preservation and both stages' CLI opt-out readbacks passed.

The separately reviewed QA tooling fixes only fixture preparation and optional-field snapshot representation; it does not change this product candidate or weaken preservation checks. All earlier failed fixture receipts remain retained and are not counted as passes. Sixteen local actual-module round-trip/negative checks reproduced the old snapshot defect and reject real configuration/source mutations.

**Limits:** synthetic loopback channel/provider proof, not live Discord/browser evidence; explicit owned foreground stop/start with native `--no-restart`, not updater-managed service restart or downtime qualification. Native output is bounded/truncated; explicit exported update gates and post-core result bind the outcome. No exhaustive zero-egress or independent post-removal container inventory is claimed. Broader replacement selection remains outside this repair. Normal final owner review and native landing remain required.

title: feat(android): keep chat calls visible while sharing photos
body:
Related: #151078, #150178

## What Problem This Solves

Android users need a dedicated conversation page without changing their active call or original chat. The previous inline card did not provide that view, and the first full-page layout left the avatar oversized, Details in the middle, technical diagnostics on the main screen, and speech captions and controls poorly grouped.

This also fixes valid locally admitted photos displaying “Unsupported attachment” and needing to leave the conversation page just to send them. The mascot no longer loses its mouth when idle or thinking. Native Talk also stops inserting fixed Talk/ElevenLabs instructions into the user's visible chat message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Android shell, red mascot, Talk, camera, attachment renderer, composer/outbox and foreground-service owners. Conversation activity is a bounded, read-only projection of the captured conversation—not another speech-result or chat-history writer. Call **End** remains separate from agent-task **Stop**.

The cleanup consolidates duplicate completion/reset logic and question metadata, removes unused state and delegation wrappers, and repairs demonstrated ordering and ownership defects at their existing owners. No new transport lifecycle, audio/avatar engine, decoder or second assistant.

## User Impact

- Native Talk and push-to-talk now send only the recognized utterance. Existing history is not rewritten. Reply style follows the active agent's instructions instead of a per-turn concise-tone override; configured speech synthesis and optional response voice directives remain.
- A fixed header places **Go to chat** on the left, the captured agent identity once in the center, and **Details** at the top right. Technical activity diagnostics are inside Details; genuine connection/microphone failures remain visible.
- The existing red avatar is smaller and balanced in available space: preferred cap **216 dp instead of 264 dp**, shrinking on short screens. Its mouth follows actual playback and remains visible as a closed mouth during pauses/thinking; reduced-motion behavior is retained.
- A restrained, theme-aware caption surface shows up to **four lines** of the latest real user/assistant utterance, with a small left-aligned role label. No empty caption box or second chat. Captions stay with their captured call, including when speaker audio is muted.
- One concise status reflects real listening, speaking, thinking, reading, writing/editing, searching, tools, approval/input waits or errors. Lost activity coverage is recorded and recovered from existing authoritative metadata, rather than silently treated as idle.
- Camera choice, photo previews and explicit **Send photos** are grouped above persistent **Audio / Photo / End** controls. Existing safe-area handling and bounded scrolling keep actions accessible on short screens and at large font sizes.
- Front/rear still capture uses the existing camera owner and original bytes. Only the displayed photo snapshot is sent through the original conversation’s canonical outbox; hidden drafts, other files and newer/replaced attachments remain untouched. Capture never sends automatically.
- Talk reopens the existing call. Go to chat, Return to conversation and Android Back change the view without restarting or ending it. Final speech roles remain in canonical chat history without mirroring, duplicate turns or automatic speech from observed finals.
- Foreground-admitted chat-call continuity is retained across navigation/background transitions; actual connection, permission or ownership loss retires the affected call. Reconnecting does not silently start another call.

No Gateway/protocol, provider implementation/configuration, authentication, global-default, permission-policy, dependency, SDK, schema, release or phone-installation changes. **No continuous camera/video streaming:** the original live-vision objective remains outside this still-photo scope.

## Evidence

**Current head:** [`3f6ba0f03963dd8c6d30e2ef530f206eb1128a27`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3f6ba0f03963dd8c6d30e2ef530f206eb1128a27), parent `83167ee2003775f150b492e3a7ae050c61c4a25c`. Exact final tree: `f51b683ebed2298fa3cb474c0c2934bbaef733ae`. Normal hooks and a fast-forward push preserve existing history; no force push or PR merge.

- **Native-input regression:** five cases failed on the old producer's exact prefixed wire message. Coverage spans the production Shell/normal-chat history, generic native Talk, captured calls, PTT and before/after-ACK completion orders, including multiline and instruction-like speech. The fixed path sends the utterance directly; there is no display filter, second writer or hidden instruction field.
- **Final-tree validation:** **771 tests across 22 suites passed with zero failures, errors or skips on the exact final tree**, retaining all 771 prior test IDs. Play/ThirdParty debug APK builds and Play, ThirdParty and Wear-shared Android lint completed without lint errors. **Kotlin formatting is still red:** `:app:ktlintTestSourceSetCheck` reports 37 formatting diagnostics in `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/node/CameraCaptureOwnershipTest.kt` (unchanged by this follow-up). The quality command exited 1; the aggregate ktlint gates are not claimed passed. The six production-camera formatting errors are corrected. [Runner provenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35444877121); proof manifest SHA-256 `ad220ae2e575b292ab84b8a7a622054d8a799c672bf9b8d4a372383b60ab64e8`. Command/JUnit receipts establish these outcomes, not the enclosing workflow conclusion after lease cleanup.
- **Fresh independent follow-up review:** P0–P2, normal local mode over the complete staged fourteen-path follow-up against the published parent; scoped-clean, exit 0. Report SHA-256: `f50c71a70e4853967363c5f52cdb563bd6caa3b8e8ade4bbfab3b6cce65ea977`. This is not a zero-finding review of the older complete PR; that qualified review is retained below. The interrupted whole-PR attempt produced no final report and is not counted as approval.
- **Complete-PR cleanup:** all 41 source-owned PR paths were audited separately from the ordinary review. Removed unused ViewModel forwarding APIs, the duplicate request-only draft snapshot, an unrendered speech-mouth calculation, an unused effect restart key, and duplicate attachment-width plumbing. Shared gap-test setup keeps both original named cases. Call/generation/lease/cancellation, CameraX, question/sequence, draft recovery and snapshot-sensitive attachment protections remain. No tests were deleted.
- **Follow-up LOC:** production +21/−48 (**net −27**, including formatter-only camera layout); tests +62/−44; docs +6. The functional cleanup removes a net 33 production lines before the required camera formatting correction. No generated localization output, dependency, schema or protocol changes.
- **Hosted PR CI:** The exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35446568616) was **skipped**. No hosted product-suite success is claimed. Local/Testbox results are not substituted for this head's hosted status. The PR remains a draft for normal review and physical-device acceptance.

title: fix(ui): resolve named-project PR links to the correct repository
body:
Closes #151047

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: assistant-chat PR references can link to the checkout repository instead of the named project, and bold/italic formatting can change a PR into an issue link.

## User Impact

User impact: in an OpenClaw chat, **Original ClawSweeper PR #1558 merged** and **Follow-up ClawSweeper PR #1576 opened** link to ClawSweeper when the registered project uniquely identifies it. An OpenClaw reference in the same message still links to OpenClaw.

Existing explicit links retain their destinations. Ambiguous or hidden project names stay plain instead of selecting the checkout. No permissions, private-preview policy, model prompts, protocol, storage, or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repository selection now happens **per reference at the href producer**, not once for the whole message or later in a hover card. A single connection-scoped registered-project read is shared by New Session and chat, including direct cold chat. The old picker-local project task is removed. Names come only from existing authorized project display names/origins and the session repository; there is no GitHub search or guessed owner.

Formatted, persisted, streaming, expanded, and sidebar content use the same resolver. Normalized alias identity participates in Markdown and transcript invalidation. Old client, connection, principal, or scope results cannot populate a new context. Checkout fallback waits for successful catalog resolution, preventing transient wrong links while lowercase names load or the catalog fails.

## Evidence

The exact original reproduction failed on head 0f2fe8fd5b5f6573924a554c428bd89debe93beb: expected ClawSweeper, received OpenClaw. The corrected bundled Control UI checks **href, preview request, and hover title destination** for all three targets in one message:

| Authored reference | Repository / request kind / number |
| --- | --- |
| Original ClawSweeper PR **#1558 merged** | openclaw/clawsweeper / pull / 1558 |
| Follow-up ClawSweeper PR **#1576 opened** | openclaw/clawsweeper / pull / 1576 |
| Same checkout: OpenClaw PR #1576 | openclaw/openclaw / pull / 1576 |

**September 19 replacement candidate:** `40eac74b211770f91c6a9825367749a30dc9997d`, rebased onto main `ad74de529f8b7313d946dda4ec478eeb62f100c2` after a fresh request to resolve conflicts and merge. This is still the same PR, not a replacement PR.

The conflict integration retains the generic link-reader migration, `image-lightbox.types.ts`, injectable New Session gateway and default-selection preservation, HumanMention handling, `entryRef`, both cache identities, and main’s async-question cache revision. The original/late-catalog browser fixtures now advertise `TEST_LINK_READER` and use the mock descriptor’s `forge.preview` URL contract and `.link-reader-hovercard`; no retired provider is restored. Production uses the GitHub plugin’s `github.preview`/`github.detail`.

Fresh review reproduced and repaired an invalidating-refresh bug: the shared catalog now retires old aliases immediately, not only request generations, before loading replacement data. If that read fails, stale links stay retired. One canonical retirement path replaces the duplicate scope/unmount reset paths; the repair adds one production line.

Parser syntax remains based on authoritative known aliases and explicit qualifiers, not guessed title-case prose. New regression controls preserve Tools/Widgets/Clawsweeper aliases with ordinary Original/Follow-up wording and casing variants; a known unresolved complete alias wins over its resolved suffix. Reviewer-created assumptions about arbitrary unknown multiword names were rejected rather than adding an English modifier allowlist. Read-only display-name aliases remain unresolved without inventing undisclosed origin basenames or adding a new permission requirement.

Current validation: the corrected generic-reader suite passed **17/17** on predecessor f08d3649, including the original three-destination message and delayed lowercase catalog. All 21 routing tests and focused owner/cache/mention/New Session checks pass. Both the full independent P0–P2 review and the final CI-repair delta review are scoped-clean. The first failed isolated run was a fixture capability omission: the generic reader requires both preview and detail methods; two missing `forge.detail` advertisements were repaired without changing production filtering or timeouts.

Normal CI on f08d3649 exposed two further failures, retained rather than hidden by retries. Repository subscriptions now live with the existing session owner, preserving invocation and LIFO cleanup order while removing lifecycle-file line-cap growth; line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets pass. The unchanged service-backup fixture failure was independently fixed on main by #152795 (88e037f773bbec71d8acdb0dbbe6db71aff17cb1). The final rebase incorporates that upstream repair and drops our duplicate test commit. All six retained UI commits are patch-identical; the final PR has **no daemon changes**, and all **59** upstream receipt tests pass. No assertions, permissions, service runtime or recovery guards were weakened.

The final exact-head browser suite passed **17/17** on 40eac74b211770f91c6a9825367749a30dc9997d (Blacksmith Testbox run 35440920347, lease tbx_01m2wqpafp99hqx9vy7y8jr2zm). title: fix: keep CLI validation available when worker permission is denied
body:
Related: #147866

## What Problem This Solves

CLI startup misclassifies healthy SQLite as unavailable when Node's permission model denies Worker creation. This sends restricted invocations into runtime recovery before their command arguments can be validated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SQLite capability owner now runs its existing literal `:memory:` probe in the current process when `process.permission.has("worker")` is explicitly false. Normal invocations retain Worker isolation. The same memoized result, database cleanup, NUL round-trip checks, and WAL-version requirements apply in both cases.

## User Impact

Permission-restricted CLI invocations can reach existing argument validation without granting Worker, child-process, or filesystem-write access. No configuration, storage, migration, or permission-grant changes are introduced.

## Evidence

Current-main source and Node's permission implementation confirm the missing owner-level distinction. The downstream runtime-recovery repair does not supersede this change.

- 170 focused owner/sibling tests passed. All three new permission regressions fail against the old owner; 18 capability/Worker controls passed again after restoring the repair.
- All 29 built CLI cases passed, including the eleven original permission-restricted invalid-input cases. The native E2E harness completed full typed runtime preparation, AI build, integrity verification, and cleanup without skipped build gates.
- A real Node 24.21.0 permission-denied probe changes from unavailable SQLite to a healthy capability result while Worker, child-process, and filesystem-write permissions remain false. Unsafe WAL and NUL-corrupting results remain rejected.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0, no accepted/actionable findings. Syntax, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Production +10/-5 (net +5); tests +80/-0. The five production lines distinguish Worker permission from SQLite capability at the existing owner, without duplicating the probe.

The candidate is rebased onto main and excludes the former release-preparation commits. Exact-head [CI run 35242354184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35242354184) is pending; historical failures on the obsolete release-based head are not used or waived as passing evidence. Native review initialization is blocked by the canonical checkout's `tsx` 4.23.12 versus the trusted-main requirement 4.23.13; see the [stop-report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150896#issuecomment-5717250209). No prepare or merge command was attempted. This fix is absent from the 2026.9.5 cut at `4b38266964828d528ecb7823a1dde833b8b25d75` and is recommended for that release after main landing and qualification.

Human credit: @steipete, @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc.

Related: #150856, #150364

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes private-transcript memory tests leaving fixture-owned MCP runtimes in the shared process after deleting their workspace.

This narrow producer cleanup is part of an explicitly requested update recovery. The original failure was observed in [CI run 35214051496, job 105178287063](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35214051496/job/105178287063). [The related maintainer investigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150856#issuecomment-5714047457) independently identifies this producer and calls out complementary teardown work; it is context, not an approval of this exact patch.

## User Impact

No production or user-visible behavior changes. The fixture no longer leaves its foreground and hidden session runtimes behind for subsequent tests. No migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run disposal releases leases, but session-lifetime runtimes need session closure. After the fixture's work settles, its teardown now awaits disposal only for sessions whose runtime workspace exactly matches its unique workspace, before fixture state removal. Other workspaces are preserved; there is no global reset.

Main `8d6decdecafe2dae4f609a0c809091a609eada0c` independently changed the requester test to compare inherited runtime keys, superseding #150856. That consumer change is complementary, not this producer cleanup: the producer is still unchanged there. This PR does not alter or revert the consumer assertion, and does not claim the historical assertion failure remains on current main.

## Evidence

- Exact historical base `448b7740ddf9eb77368a9ba52d2bd42130edfc43`, Node 24.20.0, canonical non-isolated fast configuration with explicit producer-before-requester order: **2 passed / 1 failed**, reproducing three generated `internal-session-effects-*` keys plus `private-memory-source`.

Earlier missing-object/package-resolution failures and an interrupted retry are retained, not represented as successful aggregate runs.

A later unregistered turn in the same child session could overwrite a pending subagent's frozen result while completion delivery was retrying. This is a maintainer-requested repair for `release/2026.9.5`.

## User Impact

A completed child keeps its own result instead of adopting an unrelated later reply. Authorized continuations still preserve task/requester lineage and deliver the complete answer from their own run. No configuration, schema, retention, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep completion with the existing registered-run and task-replacement owner. Remove the obsolete session-key-only refresh path rather than weakening exact-run reads or adding another result cache. Paused rows, pending generations, and retired predecessors are covered through the lifecycle listener.

The lifecycle fixtures now use explicit producer run IDs, matching synthetic timing reads/writes, and real registry persistence for atomic continuation replacement. The earlier visible-child stall was a fixture mismatch, not a claimed SQLite, browser, or MCP runtime defect.

- Causal red on `c0ef8ff5badc8735b85d802f4102c98b1ed45d70`: 14/15 cases passed; an unadmitted visible reply changed the frozen result to `Unrelated later answer`. The admitted continuation already passed once its real persistence contract was represented.

It fails against the historical writer and passes the complete **181/181 registry seam suite**, the changed gate, and fresh complete-candidate P0/P1 autoreview.

title: fix(tests): honor sticky plugin lease refusal in update proof
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release qualification's retained-updater proof reusing a plugin lifecycle generation after deliberately triggering its sticky authority refusal.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Qualification now verifies refusal within the original lifecycle generation and successful settlement under a genuinely fresh one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Nested plugin scopes deliberately share their first authority refusal. Starting another updater inside that same lease cannot restore its authority. The fixture now closes the refused generation before acquiring a fresh recovery lease.

Old commit and rollback handles remain refused under both generations. Every retained-package/backup byte and directory-identity assertion remains; only a new transaction may settle. Production authority and rollback guards are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Separate, explicitly requested release-2026.9.5 qualification repair for run 35182718648, job 105081434754; not an unrelated main-CI cleanup.

title: fix(update): preserve serving SQLite files during repair
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes staged update repair changing the serving SQLite shared-memory file while inspecting state that must remain untouched.

## User Impact

Artifact-preserving reads keep the serving database, WAL, and SHM bytes, inodes, and modification times unchanged while still reading current committed rows. Ordinary reads and owned disposable views keep cached-reader reuse. Live cached writers now use the existing private snapshot path when artifact preservation is required, so those reads incur its normal copying cost.

No schema, retention, permission, or rollback-policy changes. This cannot retrofit reads performed entirely by an already-running published updater. Published-driver × candidate acceptance passed for the original PR head: see the linked Docker proof below.

## Why This Change Was Made

A cached writer can advance SHM read marks after another connection commits. The preservation reader incorrectly bypassed its snapshot owner in that case. This five-line correction retains existing scoped private snapshots and routes only artifact-preserving live reads away from the cached writer.

The repair-isolation oracle keeps every existing comparison and now identifies whether bytes, inode, or modification time changed.

title: fix: guide phone pairing when the Gateway is local-only
body:
Related: #98242

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw qr` stops at a configuration-heavy error when a phone cannot reach a local-only Gateway.

## User Impact

Interactive users can choose their local network, confirm the exposure and restart, and continue to a pairing QR without editing configuration. Cancellation before confirmation leaves settings unchanged.

LAN access listens on all interfaces: use a trusted network and keep the firewall enabled. Plaintext LAN pairing remains limited. Authentication and the authored port are preserved; temporary port overrides are not saved. Automatic Tailscale activation is deferred so this flow cannot claim an operator-owned Serve route; already-configured Tailscale and explicit secure URLs remain supported.

Default interactive LAN pairing now verifies the Gateway process and the listener at the exact phone address before issuing credentials—even on a retry after failed activation. An unrelated HTTP-200 service is not proof of readiness. If a save has already succeeded when activation fails, settings remain saved and the command gives recovery guidance without a setup code. Machine output, noninteractive runs, remote mode, and explicit endpoint/auth overrides retain their existing read-only contracts and never enter recovery.

Recovery reuses setup-owned network defaults, guarded config writes, and Gateway restart. The foreground restart correction reloads saved bind settings while preserving explicit CLI binds. The pairing resolver remains the URL and bootstrap owner; its caller-admission hook lets the default interactive LAN command check the resolved endpoint before minting a token. title: fix(gateway): stop input effects after caller authority closes
body:
Related: #135838

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers remains enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users cancelling or replacing a delegated request could still see a session reset, queued input, saved media or a reset confirmation. Also fixes retries that repeated a completed reset or incorrectly reported success after confirmation delivery failed, and old request cleanup overwriting a newer request’s status.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compose the existing caller/session guards with canonical reservation ownership across preaccept effects, interruption, cleanup and lifecycle rotation; release caller-admission assertions only when input synchronously transfers to the accepted child. Retain the original reset and reply outcomes without repeating effects, while preserving client-authority forwarding, operator cancellation, sessionless/recovery/settle-wake paths and existing test coverage; remove duplicated first-key cleanup/interruption policy.

Production: **+156/-60 (net +96)**; tests/support: **+1862/-26**. Production growth supplies previously missing live authority and all-key ownership checks plus committed-reset/error reconciliation across existing owners; no second store, fallback execution path or cached authorization is added.

## User Impact

- **No new RPC field, client/provider version cutoff, plugin SDK signature, configuration, protocol or database-schema change.** Valid ordinary and delegated callers keep their supported interfaces.
- Closed or superseded callers cannot obtain new input or confirmation-send admission. A reset already adopted by its lifecycle owner may finish; that does not authorize a fresh suffix or ACK. Already-accepted input retains independent child custody.
- **Retry behavior also affects ordinary callers.** A same-key retry does not repeat an already-committed reset. If strict confirmation delivery fails—including a write followed by an uncertain error—the retry preserves the original failed RPC outcome rather than reporting success or sending again. Best-effort requests retain their original delivery-status result.
- An unstarted suffix must be submitted separately. A reset-only receipt is not channel-delivery proof. The existing process-local dedupe window remains bounded to five minutes / 1,000 entries; this is not durable cross-restart exactly-once behavior.

Contributor credit: @sallyom and @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/70f8933b-db6b-4809-b9a8-941957263614)

Normal-hook source **`f36be495d0330fd3377e6f6c33caa4fe2d21cc14`**, parent `8ccaaaae043181a9a7861ef4b4c8ad1dfe614351`, tree `bdb45af3662396a775f060f44e625c014acfc6c1`. title: fix(workers): stop checkpoint writes after authority closes
body:
Related: #135838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cloud repository edits could continue checkpointing after their owning operation closed or the workspace revision changed. Also fixes the P1/P2 review concern that larger publication snapshots multiplied synchronous Gateway database work for each distinct blob.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep fresh caller/revision checks at metadata, preparation, queued import and final Git-input boundaries. Remove the redundant Gateway publication-copy tree: the existing computation worker now prepares the companion directly through the same bounded, file-backed Git input writer and importer used for ordinary checkpoints. No cached authorization or second import path.

## User Impact

Closed or superseded operations cannot admit a new checkpoint import or publication. Already-admitted private preparation may finish, then is rejected and cleaned up. Recovery custody, idempotent cleanup, and valid live edits remain intact. Publication blob count no longer multiplies staging authority/database checks.

No provider cutoff, user configuration, persisted format or SQLite schema change. The additional input variant is private to the co-located computation worker.

Contributor credit: @sallyom and @vincentkoc.

title: fix: stop repeated reply-skip text and child reply loops
body:
Related: #150488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated `REPLY_SKIP` text and stale `RE` fragments in live chat during multi-agent work, and stops native parent/child sends from entering reciprocal peer reply loops.

## User Impact

Control replies remain invisible while streaming and after completion. Real short answers and late child results remain deliverable. Independent peers, ordinary UI threads, ACP completion, and isolated scheduled-job announcement behavior retain their existing contracts.

No configuration, schema, or migration changes. This PR does not blanket-hide substantive coordination messages; it addresses the reply-loop and control-marker paths in the linked issue.

The live classifier recognized complete controls but missed the next partial token in a buffer of repeated replies. Once a completed token became suppressed, the Gateway omitted the update rather than retracting a snapshot already shown to the UI.

The repair keeps classification and retraction in the Gateway's existing display owners. Native spawn lineage is checked in both directions; delayed related-session results get one handoff rather than a peer exchange. Isolated scheduled jobs keep their existing no-requester-wake policy.

title: fix(cli): prevent agent shell reports from appearing as human input
body:
Closes #150467

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading user turns when an agent sends a shell-generated report through the operator Gateway CLI instead of the attributed session tool or child-completion path.

## User Impact

Recognized agent-exec message commands fail before opening a Gateway connection, with guidance to use attributed delivery. Ordinary human terminal commands, backend tool dispatch, diagnostics, and embedded one-shot agent execution retain their existing behavior.

This intentionally changes scripts that invoke Gateway-backed `openclaw agent` or raw operator message RPCs from an agent's `exec` tool. They must use the available session tool or normal completion rather than retrying through another operator RPC.

The existing `OPENCLAW_SHELL=exec` marker is denial-only—not authenticated identity or hostile same-OS-user isolation. Stripped environments, direct sockets, backend transports, and unrelated transcript mutations remain outside this guarantee. No server authentication or tool-policy changes, new credentials, schema changes, or historical transcript rewriting are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The operator RPC adapter cannot preserve the source agent's provenance. Silently translating it into a session-tool call would also change receiver-timeout and steering semantics. One shared guard therefore refuses the unsupported substitution at the CLI facade, direct CLI transport, and Gateway-backed agent-command entry. It includes initial turns supplied with session creation and runs before connection overrides or explicit scopes can skip the check.

The normal attributed messaging and child-settlement owners remain unchanged. Recovery guidance no longer suggests using an unspecified alternative route after an accepted inter-session send fails. Runtime production delta: +27 net lines, for the shared admission check and its entry-point wiring; no new manager, store, credential bridge, or configuration option.

## Evidence

- Existing baseline: **60 tests passed**.
- Before the fix, the new unit regression failed for all four operator message RPCs. The real-process regression also failed for all four exec cases while all four human controls passed.
- After the fix, **403 tests passed across six Vitest shards** on the final source, plus **43 exec-environment tests**: CLI facade, real CLI subprocesses, Gateway transport, Gateway-backed/embedded agent command behavior, input provenance, and attributed A2A delivery.
- The eight real-process cases use an isolated loopback protocol fixture. Recognized exec calls produce **zero connections and zero message requests**; each human control connects and sends exactly one request. Cases include the high-level agent command with a model override.
- Independent structured Codex Autoreview: **no accepted/actionable P0 findings**, confidence 0.98.
- Full build completed successfully before the behavior-neutral type/identity consolidation. It reported a UI startup bundle-budget warning (354.2 KiB versus 354.1 KiB), recorded separately without changing budgets. Final-source canonical `check:changed` passed (exit 0), including line-growth, formatting, core and core-test typechecking, typed lint, and runtime/storage guards. No budgets, assertions, or guard thresholds were weakened.

No live release session, production Gateway, external channel, or provider was used by the reproduction. The process fixture proves CLI dispatch/refusal, not a new server-side authorization boundary. This PR is separate from active release work and does not introduce a release gate.

title: fix(agents): preserve restart ownership and explain runtime refusals
body:
Closes #150323
Fixes #159918

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes channel-plugin tasks stalling during Gateway restart when the raw inbound runner lacks an explicit reply dispatcher, and makes native runtime-selection refusals distinguishable without changing selection or authorization decisions.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish native runtime refusal reasons through trusted diagnostics; the public refusal message and selection behavior are unchanged.

Pending replies from that entry point retain their owning Gateway and participate in its restart cancellation and recovery. The additional diagnostic observations make restart ownership and admission testable without treating a terminated CLI as proof of success. They do not grant authority or change admission, target checks, signal delivery, or RPC results.

**Compatibility scope:** routed plans without an explicit dispatcher deliberately select their owning Gateway rather than ambient state. Third-party plugins depending on ambient selection have not been validated. Explicit dispatchers, prepared turns, and standalone use remain covered. Maintainer acceptance of this documented compatibility risk remains required before merge; it is not assumed.

The optional `gateway call --traceparent` carries only existing diagnostic envelope context. Core owner/admission events stay internal; raw owner objects, session identities, and private trace associations are not published by the harness.

**Runtime-diagnostics SDK compatibility:** `DiagnosticEventPayload` gains the `model.runtime_choice` variant. Exhaustive TypeScript consumers may need an explicit case when rebuilding, including an intentional no-op. This does not change installed configuration, auth, ownership, selection or persistence behavior. The existing SDK/security-owner compatibility decision remains separate before landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The raw-event path now uses the existing instance-bound reply dispatcher. The deprecated inbound/turn alias continues to share that owner-bound runner.

For the missing evidence, core observes the actual admitted owner immediately before each tool-hook handler. A separate native event records the actual restart-admission result. Fresh diagnostic spans associate those facts across the CLI process boundary; no RPC-time async-local-owner inference remains. Observations never invoke authority assertions or replace authorization.

The conflict-driven main refresh preserves upstream Cron requester issuance, composed revocation checks, device-token storage fences and caller-lifetime cleanup alongside the existing observation contract. Main still needs the raw-dispatcher fix; no retired path was restored.

Runtime-selection diagnostics record versioned, content-free preparation and validation facts through the trusted diagnostic stream. Delivery remains asynchronous, cannot reenter the final commit guard through trace preparation, and stays outside OTel export and support-bundle retention. Shared event, delivery and recorder policy owners now serve both changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes channel-plugin tasks stalling during a Gateway restart when they enter through the injected raw inbound runner without an explicit reply dispatcher.

## User Impact

Pending replies from that entry point retain their owning Gateway and participate in its restart cancellation and recovery. The standalone public SDK wrapper and configuration/authorization guards are unchanged by this G3 repair.

**Compatibility scope:** for routed plans without an explicit dispatcher, the injected runner deliberately selects its owning Gateway rather than ambient Gateway state. Third-party plugins depending on ambient selection have not been validated. Explicit dispatchers, prepared turns, and standalone use remain covered. The current review leaves acceptance of this documented compatibility risk to a maintainer before merge; that acceptance is not assumed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime already has an instance-bound reply dispatcher, but the raw-event path was not supplying it to routed plans. This change fills that missing dispatcher at the runtime boundary. Explicit dispatchers, adapter receivers, prepared/assembled turns, and genuinely ownerless standalone use keep their existing behavior. The exact-owner cancellation guard is unchanged.

A broad callable overload supports core/provider delivery unions, while the final default overload preserves existing `Parameters`-derived caller types and their required `deliver` method. Raw-input/result generics and the standalone public SDK wrapper remain unchanged.

title: fix(test): prevent native worker startup timeouts in extension batches

title: improve(models): explain native runtime selection refusals
body:
> **Superseded by [#150493](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150493).** The complete runtime-diagnostics branch is retained in the consolidated PR; this source PR is closed unmerged.

Closes #150323

## What Problem This Solves

Native runtime selection refusals share one public error, so diagnostics cannot distinguish missing prepared ownership, auth and resolution failures, runtime ineligibility, or a revoked commit guard.

## User Impact

No user-visible selection or error-message change. Trusted diagnostic consumers can inspect closed, content-free preparation and validation decisions without changing native auth, ownership, or persistence guards. No migration or configuration change is required.

**SDK rebuild compatibility:** `DiagnosticEventPayload` gains the `model.runtime_choice` variant. TypeScript consumers that exhaustively switch on `event.type` may need an explicit case when rebuilding against this SDK, including an intentional no-op for consumers that do not handle runtime-choice diagnostics. This source-compatibility implication is separate from installed configuration and selection behavior: no configuration migration is required, and the existing auth, ownership, and persistence decisions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The decision owner now emits versioned `model.runtime_choice` facts through the existing trusted diagnostic subscription. Every check explicitly records its reached result or `not-reached`. Delivery is asynchronous and excludes synchronous exporter preparation so observers cannot reenter the final guard.

Diagnostics remain best-effort and are not authorization or persistence receipts. Missing events, unknown fields, disabled diagnostics, and dropped events remain indeterminate. Consumers must isolate their observation window and project only closed allowlisted fields; dispatcher trace metadata is not report-safe.

title: fix(agents): retain completed results in detached recovery replies
body:
Related: #142168

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a detached task could lose the results of completed actions when the task needed a final recovery answer. The actions had already finished, but the final answer was prepared from an empty conversation instead of the task's existing transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restricted finalization now retains the original session manager and detached persistence mode while preserving its tool-free, capability-restricted contract. The live test pool also runs on process main threads, as required by the shared-state broker, with a credential-free regression exercising the actual plugin-state range read.

## User Impact

Recovery answers can use completed task results without repeating those actions. No model, thinking, authentication, tool-permission, or persistence-policy defaults change.

## Evidence

- Focused finalization unit and sibling coverage: 37 tests passed on this branch.
- Credential-free live-pool broker regression: passed on this branch. The unmodified pool reproduces the exact host-broker admission refusal.
- Retained deterministic before/after replay for the patch-identical finalizer owner: the original finalization request loses a committed receipt; the fixed request retains it. The fixture executes the receipt action once and never repeats the unfinished write.
- Production types, selected test types, targeted lint, formatting, and fresh independent P0 review passed before publication.
- Exact-head CI run 35150485516/1 is blocked in `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` during dependency installation: `@matrix-org/matrix-sdk-crypto-nodejs@0.6.6` receives HTTP 403 downloading its native asset, then its postinstall throws `ReferenceError: err is not defined`. The ratchet commands never started. Dependency manifests, lockfile, and the install action are unchanged by this PR. [Failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35150485516/job/104977592556). CI is not claimed green.

No live-provider requests or package build were run for this focused fix. Diagnostic response fixtures and private logs are not committed. This PR does not qualify or alter a release candidate.


<!-- pr150300-ci-recovery-20260916 -->
### CI recovery and remaining blockers — September 16

The original attempt-1 Matrix download failure is retained above. After verifying a successful same-asset download in another Ubuntu job from that attempt and a direct public download matching the published SHA-256, one job-specific recovery was requested on this unchanged head. [Attempt-2 ratchet job 105001771544](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35150485516/job/105001771544) executed the normal postinstall download and the ratchet commands successfully. No dependency/Node pins, postinstall behavior, or source code changed. Only that job and its dependent CI gate executed again; other attempt-2 records retain earlier execution times.

The overall run remains failed because four earlier test-shard failures are retained. No additional retry is being requested here.

The late review finding is also independently confirmed: an actual detached finalization retained its receipt but persisted one internal recovery instruction as a user turn. The original manager's already-installed guard ignores the newly requested one-shot suppression. No production fix has been applied in this CI recovery, and this PR remains blocked pending the guard-owner repair and remaining CI resolution. The diagnostic fixtures and logs are not committed.

title: fix(macos): restore strict-concurrency chat handoff builds
body:
Related: #149763

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the macOS app build failing under Swift 6 strict concurrency when compiling the primary-Gateway chat handoff.

## User Impact

The macOS app builds again without changing the web/native experience, selected Gateway, conversation route, or draft handling. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`PrimaryGatewaySnapshot` retains a non-Sendable configuration dictionary. Its creation and consumers already belong to the main actor, but the snapshot type did not declare that isolation. Marking the type `@MainActor` enforces its existing owner boundary rather than using unchecked sendability or removing stale-route checks.

This is one added annotation. The navigation implementation, snapshot capture timing, presentation-generation checks, canonical Gateway checks, and physical server-lease checks remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Apple Swift 6.3.3 / Xcode 26.6 / arm64 macOS 26.6.2 produced `Build of product 'OpenClaw' complete! (819.95s)`. Swift lint/format and the native schema check also passed.

The existing isolated native launcher ran the tests on disposable CI, not an operator desktop.
- **Real pre-fix failure:** [macOS release build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35134688081/job/104924709922) on Source `e2319746461d17ff818f886874ec7af6a3d7a347`, with the same Apple compiler/toolchain: `AppNavigationActions.swift:77:83: sending 'primary' risks causing data races`. Both relevant owners were byte-identical on the fresh Main base used for this repair.
- Independent precommit review through P2 was scoped-clean with no findings. Patch applicability, `git diff --check`, and byte-level one-annotation verification passed. No UI, test fixture, baseline, or workflow changes.

The broader standalone CI run is **not** claimed green: it also reports Control UI catalog fallback-baseline drift, an iOS `TalkRealtimeConsultCancellationTests` expectation failure, and a Node worktree sparse-isolation test timeout in inputs unchanged from pre-repair Main. Those failures are outside this one-line macOS repair; no locale regeneration, fixture changes, or weakened checks are included. Optimized-build proof used the existing public CI workflow, not FRV or private release jobs.

At native-proof handoff, the broader run still had an unrelated iPad screenshot capture running under its existing CI budget. All requested macOS jobs and ordinary PR CI had finished successfully; no GitHub jobs were cancelled.

title: fix(release): keep complete SDK reports within artifact limits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes regular-release qualification rejecting complete SDK change reports when beta and latest point to the same predecessor.

## User Impact

Release operators can retain complete SDK evidence within the existing 16 MiB artifact limit. No SDK comparison, logical digest, acknowledgement requirement, or publication check is weakened.

Dual-selector JSON uses explicit shared-comparison formats (`diff-set/v1` and `release-evidence-set/v2`). Historical v1 evidence remains readable; single-comparison output and Markdown summaries are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer already shares comparisons by predecessor commit, but the JSON writer serialized the same full comparison twice. The existing evidence owner now preserves that sharing, with paired writer/reader and channel-consumer support.

This is the smallest trusted-Tooling repair for an observed release blocker. It does not update product Source or requalify old artifacts. New Tooling requires new matching canonical preparation/qualification; cross-Tooling package rebinding remains rejected.

## Evidence

- Observed producer: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35134689601/job/104924090525; original SDK artifact `10462579090` retained unchanged.
- Actual diff: 20,792,775 → 10,456,445 bytes; evidence: 21,032,717 → 10,457,335 bytes. Both fit the unchanged 16,777,216-byte limit. Whitespace-only compaction did not fit.
- Complete structural round-trip preserves both selectors, all 1,346 exports, 1,418 declaration changes, two added entrypoints per selector, all declaration text and identity fields. Logical digests are unchanged.

title: fix(codex): keep ordinary chats out of personal history
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ordinary OpenClaw chats and background work appeared in personal Codex Desktop/CLI history when an existing native login silently selected the user home. It also completes detected-Codex setup for users who need an OpenClaw sign-in after isolating that home.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime preparation, native-login discovery, model discovery, and setup now honor the existing agent-home default. Detected Codex reuses eligible OpenClaw credentials or invokes the existing OpenAI sign-in owner before verification. Saved credentials retain the selected runtime settings for retry, and cancellation cannot promote the route. No new credential import or refresh owner is introduced.

## User Impact

Ordinary sessions stay isolated and durable, regardless of an existing native Codex login. Explicit `appServer.homeScope: "user"`, native-session adoption, and supervision remain supported. No personal history is moved or deleted.

Users who relied on automatic native-login borrowing can select detected Codex in Model Setup to sign in, or use `openclaw models auth login --provider openai`. Existing explicit user-home settings remain unchanged; remove that setting to isolate ordinary sessions. A failed verification retains the saved sign-in for retry without another login.

## Evidence

title: fix(apple): native chat rejects sends when an agent choice is required
body:
Related: #126315

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the per-sender Apple chat routing rejection when a multi-agent Gateway requires an explicit choice but the app constructs its send fingerprint from the display default.

## User Impact

**Draft for Colin's Mac testing, not merge-ready.** Native chat should wait for an agent choice instead of treating the displayed default as an owner; after selection, sends retain the existing routing-change guard.

**Cold-start limitation:** the unchanged legacy cache does not store selection metadata. Per-sender cached metadata is display-only until a live roster refresh; new cold-offline sends wait for that refresh. Existing queued commands keep their captured target, fingerprint and idempotency key. Global fixed-store routing and the broader pre-existing QuickChat cross-Gateway remembered-selection/retry issue are not claimed fixed by this draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

The unchanged Gateway already exposes the needed per-sender distinction through `selectionRequired`. The existing in-memory Apple routing identity now uses that fact for its send fingerprint while keeping its real display default separate. iOS's direct roster consumer and macOS's live refresh use it, and native send admission honors required selection. Navigation metadata stays navigation metadata; `unowned` is never installed as a display/default agent.

The cache writer declines ownerless metadata that the existing cache projection cannot round-trip, rather than adding storage fields or reparsing the send fingerprint into an agent. No Gateway production changes, new wire fields, protocol/version bumps, SQL statements/schema/migrations, or dependency changes. Existing SQL-backed storage is still used; this is not a claim of zero SQL use.

Historical approach: closed #126316, #126330 and #126366. None is reopened or reused as the implementation base. Their native recordings and CI belong to their original revisions, not this draft. Upstream #146246 already fixes the owned non-first-primary variant. Use a Gateway containing that fix for this control; this draft is not a compatibility patch for older Gateways with the incorrect owned-default projection.

## Evidence

- Pinned implementation base: `98b321fce638620713efafb39f85fbec3bde5fce`. Branch: `fix/apple-routing-existing-api-20260915`. Draft head: `ea2ac1e9b8208080f11b68a9842a90cd69581ed2`.
- Actual unchanged `chat.send` handler: three counterfactual tests pass—owned non-first primary accepted; ownerless display fingerprint rejected before dispatch even with a canonical key; correct fingerprint from existing metadata accepted.
- Existing post-admission routing-change/idempotent-retry regression passes. Total: **4 focused TypeScript tests passed**. Wire inputs are synthetic; this is not execution of the Swift serializer.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.0 ran over the changed Swift files. Native localization inventory regenerated through its owner and verified. `git diff --check` passes.
- Fresh independent candidate review: full candidate reviewed through P2; final review returned no actionable findings. The first review’s global-fallback regression was corrected and re-reviewed. Committed tree equals the reviewed candidate. This is static review, not native compilation.
- **Not run here:** Swift compilation, Swift tests, Xcode/iOS simulator tests, native QuickChat UI, or new before/after screenshots. The Linux host has no Swift/Xcode. Added native regressions cover decoder separation, selection/canonical targets, QuickChat choice/reopen and cache safety; these need execution on the Mac lane. No native-green claim.

### Colin's Mac handoff

Use Xcode 26.4+ / Swift 6.3 and the repository-supported Node/pnpm versions. Check out this draft's exact head, then:

~~~sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw
pnpm mac:package
open dist/OpenClaw.app
~~~

Packaging uses the normal signing requirements; see `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md` and `apps/macos/README.md`. Exercise **native QuickChat/the native chat window, not the embedded Dashboard**.

1. With an explicit multi-agent, per-sender fleet and no ambient owner, open fresh native chat. Confirm sending is blocked until an agent is chosen; choose `primary` and confirm delivery to its intended session.
2. Repeat with configured non-first `systemAgent=primary` as the already-fixed control. Check history/startup/cost against the same chosen owner.
3. In the full native chat window, reconnect to the same Gateway and test a queued message without changing its target or idempotency key. Cold-launch offline behavior must match the limitation above; this does not add an outbox to compact QuickChat.
4. Change main key/scope/owner after capturing a draft and confirm stale guarded delivery is refused. Same-ID/different-Gateway selection and retry remain a separate known acceptance gap—do not interpret this draft as proving them safe.

Run native automated suites only in the disposable macOS test environment described in the dev guide, not against operator credentials/state. Focus on `ChatGatewayAgentCatalogTests`, `ChatTranscriptCacheStoreTests`, `ChatViewModelTests` and `QuickChatModelTests`; the shared and macOS packages own those suites.

title: fix(ai): avoid retrying conflicting Responses terminal statuses

title: fix(ai): retain usage and provider errors after rejected Responses tool calls
body:
Related: #147040, #147611

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Responses tool-call rejection can discard final token usage and provider failure details when an item completes with an unfinished status or malformed JSON arguments.

## User Impact

Rejected and subsequent tool calls remain non-executable, while already-admitted work settles and reported accounting is retained. Malformed JSON is neither repaired nor automatically classified as token exhaustion. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing admission latch to retain completion-validation errors and drain terminal facts before reporting the rejection. Cancellation and provider refusal/failure retain their precedence. Runner recovery and terminal diagnostic contracts are unchanged.

The September 21 conflict resolution retains main’s output-identity tracking and parse-once argument selection. The terminal validator is now unchanged from main; no competing argument-selection path remains. No unrelated baseline-CI repair is included.

## Evidence

- Original regressions reproduced lost usage, lost provider/cancellation details, and missing rejection details at EOF. Coverage includes incomplete/in-progress/malformed/truncated completions, provider failure/filtering, EOF, and cancellation.

title: improve(ios): inspect beta distribution without another upload
body:
Closes #149006

## What Problem This Solves

Release maintainers cannot inspect an already-uploaded iOS beta through protected CI when its distribution verification fails, without selecting another upload or an inapplicable recording operation.

## User Impact

Operators can request a protected, read-only view of the exact TestFlight build, actual group access, and the canonical next release plan. There is no app UI change. The existing iOS environment approval is still required; this does not recover a missing upload intent or declare a beta published.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a separate `inspect` operation to the existing release workflow. It executes trusted workflow-SHA tooling, treats the validated candidate as data, reuses the existing planner and group policy, and rechecks live authority before credentials and artifact retention. It has no signing, upload, audience mutation, intent emission, or release-ref writer.

Inspection artifacts explicitly state `publicationVerified=false` and cannot establish the provenance of a historical binary. Existing writer jobs, release permissions, and missing-original-intent rejection remain intact. API/transport failures abort inspection; deterministic plan rejection can be reported as an observation without a usable plan.

The review-found Bundler issue is corrected by keeping `BUNDLE_DEPLOYMENT=true` at the **inspection job** level, so installation and later wrapper calls use the same locked gem location. It does not affect the upload or recording jobs.

## Evidence

- On the refreshed head, 224 tests passed across eight files, including the seven release suites and all six runtime-preparation thinking cases; canonical changed-file checks over all eight changed files and final source/diff checks passed after synchronizing this worktree to the unchanged committed lockfile.
- The new separate-shell regression failed on the original workflow and passes after the deployment-environment fix. It executes the actual workflow shell bodies through the repository wrapper with a credential-free bundle shim.
- Additional **real Bundler 2.6.9 / offline synthetic-gem** proof reproduces the install-to-execution mismatch: original subsequent `bundle check` and wrapper exit 1; corrected subsequent shell exits 0. This is not real Fastlane or store proof. The local Ruby 3.3.8 cannot satisfy the actual Gemfile's 3.4.10 requirement; that refusal was retained, not bypassed.
- The correction previously passed 114 inspection/authority cases and 96 inspection/wrapper/gate cases. One earlier invocation hit its outer 180-second execution allowance; its replacement passed in 184.62 seconds with repository test/watchdog limits unchanged.
- Fresh independent P2 review of the Bundler correction found no actionable findings. The earlier planner API-error classification finding was also corrected with retained failing/passing regressions.
- Parent verification confirms the refreshed branch preserves all eight reviewed file bodies and human credit. The broader workflow assertions preserve the writer jobs and authority boundaries. SwiftLint was unavailable on Linux; no Swift code changed.

The prior CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34959044042 failed in registry, model/auth, image-policy, and setup fixtures. Those failures are retained; this branch was refreshed onto the existing main repairs #149004, #149016, #149001, and #149023 without adding unrelated fixes. **Exact-head CI is now green:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34973236349 attempt 1 completed successfully on `edccccc02e3b73bdec9f5779fa4b0049043dac7a`: all 98 jobs terminal, 85 success and 13 skipped; required `openclaw/ci-gate` job 104427489978 succeeded. The earlier failed runs remain historical failures, not passing evidence.

The second CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34965115192 tested merge `7d7b3d3d` (the prior PR head into main `80936b0933a`) and failed the six unchanged runtime-preparation thinking cases, plus a separate checkout job before its tests. The already-merged #149049 supplies the missing runtime auth-store fixture reader; this patch-identical refresh incorporates that correction without changing the eight inspection file bodies. All six cases now pass locally in an isolated, credential-free HOME/state. The checkout job exhausted five approximately 120-second attempts without useful underlying diagnostics; no timeout or retry settings were changed. Neither earlier failed run is counted as passing evidence.

### Guarded operational rollout

The remaining review risk is unverified hosted macOS/locked-Fastlane and App Store behavior, not a newly identified source defect. The mitigation is a deliberately non-publishing first execution: after ordinary exact-head CI and merge, select `inspect` for the existing candidate/build, require the existing protected iOS environment approval, execute trusted workflow-SHA code, and inspect the live result before making any release decision. No credentials are exposed by merging this PR alone.

If that first read fails, stop and repair the inspector; do not fall back to upload, audience mutation, fabricated intent, or release-ref recording. Successful inspection still cannot prove historical binary provenance or beta publication. Existing writer permissions and recording acceptance remain unchanged. This rollout plan is not a claim of live proof and does not waive the CI or environment gates.

**Not yet verified:** the protected inspection operation on hosted macOS with the locked Fastlane bundle, and live App Store state. Those require the newly landed inspection operation and a fresh environment approval. This PR alone is not beta-release completion.

title: improve: reduce work when archiving old session history
body:
Related: #119720

## What Problem This Solves

Cold-storage maintenance spends unnecessary CPU and temporary memory reading old, idle transcript windows as the retained session inventory grows.

## User Impact

When cold storage is enabled, large inventories require less metadata allocation and decoding during protection checks. Existing protection for running work, recovery, queued inputs and referenced history is preserved. No configuration, schema, archive-format or retention-policy change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stream protection metadata, decode each logical session once, and filter ordinary old windows in SQLite before creating JavaScript row objects. Recovery-owned or unreadable logical sessions retain the conservative whole-window streaming fallback. The same protection owner still runs inside the worker's guarded mutation transaction.

This is a narrow maintenance improvement. It still scans logical-session metadata and does not bound the ordinary session-list cache or make total archival work constant-time.

**Scope decision:** The accepted criterion for this repair is fewer temporary row allocations and one JSON decode per logical session, with identical protection results. Unmeasured end-to-end Gateway maintenance latency is an explicitly accepted, non-blocking limitation—not a claimed deployment-wide speedup. The change stays inside the existing protection owner, preserves conservative recovery fallback and fresh transaction rechecks, and leaves broader persistence starvation tracked separately in #119720.

## Evidence

- The original-code capacity regression hydrates **1,002 windows instead of 1**. The candidate hydrates the one recent window and decodes the logical-session JSON once.
- Refreshed source base: `c84c67002fa552e057f45e22ef9efbb89ff2d979`.
- **39/39 tests passed** across the focused protection suite and the complete existing cold-storage owner suite. Coverage includes archive/restore integrity, live work admission, authority revocation, concurrent appends, recovery, corrupt metadata, cross-generation references, timestamp boundaries and pending-input schema variants.
- Production typecheck, targeted typed lint and whitespace checks passed.
- The test-typecheck partition guard is blocked on this base by duplicate existing secrets-test ownership in `agents-tools` and `state-logging`. The same failure was reproduced with both candidate files removed/reverted; no partition rules or limits were changed by this patch.

title: fix(ui): avoid optional discovery blocking new sessions
body:
Closes #148701

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes New Session waiting for unrelated cloud discovery before a ready paired device can be selected and started.

## User Impact

Users can start on their intended ready device while cloud options load. Previously discovered Cloud destinations remain selectable and startable during background refreshes, catalog outages, and exhausted refresh retries; the selected profile and machine are preserved, with final Gateway validation. Cloud keeps its own loading/error/retry feedback without disabling known choices. No configuration or operator action is required.

Selected-device authorization, live capacity, connection checks, model/worktree validation, and frozen submission targets are retained. An unavailable remembered destination is not silently changed to Local.

## Why This Change Was Made

New Session now requests lightweight, runtime-scoped inventory automatically using the optional `includeProfiles: false` request field. Cloud metadata has a separate loading lifecycle; its completion cannot replace node inventory or clear a node-start error. Existing callers still request full profile details by default. Full-list consumers retain the existing per-profile best-effort metadata behavior: an optional provider callback failure keeps node inventory, the affected profile summary, and other profiles’ options available. The Cloud retry state handles request or transport failure without changing that contract.

Text-only New Session entry also defers optional speech discovery until dictation is requested; existing Chat behavior and capture checks are preserved.

Preference reads resolve saved intent before migration writes finish; migration remains serialized ahead of subsequent writes and cannot reapply a late snapshot. This removes the blocking dependency rather than adding preference prefetch or another cache.

## Evidence

<!-- main-refresh-current:b23f058db9d29a3bf7368c9557e8893d34772fc1 -->
**Current verified head: `b23f058db9d2`.** [Fresh measurements, canonical CI repairs, screenshots and recording](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148703#issuecomment-5687241316). Controlled cold assistant reply was **8.84 s**, separately measured. This is a fresh post-refresh measurement, not a newly matched baseline comparison.

**274 PR-tooling, 2 Codex, 198 UI, 21 Chromium and 76 Gateway tests passed**, with types/lint/builds and fresh review. The retained-Cloud negative control still proves the real Gateway rejects an unconfigured profile without initial-turn or Local fallback; no live Cloud execution is claimed.

Fresh exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35016243395) and automated review are the remaining gates. No merge or deployment.

### Earlier retained-Cloud correction evidence

<!-- retained-cloud-correction:e283ad98996edc0eaa1ede179e0eb2ee68cd4329 -->
**Recorded correction (`e283ad98996`):** [retained-Cloud proof, screenshots, and recording](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148703#issuecomment-5685208440). Known Cloud destinations remain usable during refresh failures and retries, while real Gateway validation is preserved. **178 UI tests, 20 Chromium cases, and 76 Gateway tests passed**, along with UI production/test types, focused lint, and fresh source/autoreview. The built-Gateway negative control rejects a deliberately unconfigured profile without an initial turn or Local fallback; it does not claim live Cloud execution. The recording is slowed 4× and explicitly labels its synthetic catalog.

The earlier e283 CI failures are retained as historical evidence; the current branch includes their canonical fixture repairs. Preserving known Cloud usability is not an open owner decision.

### Earlier source-labeled performance and UI proof

<!-- integrated-proof-complete:c94 -->
**Recorded matched actual-Gateway proof (`c94d51c`, source-labeled historical evidence):** [audited timings, before/after videos, and accepted-message screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148703#issuecomment-5676711410). Matched main `d02f206` took **36.10 s** to enable Start under delayed optional replies; the C94 candidate took **1.14 s**. Across four C94 Local trials, Gateway create/initial-acceptance ACK forwarding was **194 ms median / 291 ms maximum**, and the initial user message was observed in chat **0.50–0.76 s after Start**. A real isolated Gateway/UI and synthetic loopback model were used; cold synthetic assistant reply was **9.31 s**, separate from acceptance. The report defines timing endpoints, records ancillary metadata races, and makes no live remote-worker or instant-inference claim. These measurements remain labeled with their actual source revision; validation of the retained-Cloud correction is recorded separately.

<!-- actual-create-send-proof:historical-b23 -->
**Recorded actual-Gateway create/send proof (`b23d44c`):** [timings, before/after videos, and accepted-message screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148703#issuecomment-5675031181). With unrelated replies held 30.5 seconds, fresh New Session readiness changed from 36.145 s to 0.945 s. Across four final Local trials, creation was acknowledged 90–278 ms after Submit and follow-up messages 261–310 ms after Send. This uses a real built Gateway/UI and a controlled loopback model, not live remote-worker execution; assistant response time is separate.

- Backend promise-deferral regressions hold machine or OS discovery unresolved for 30 seconds of simulated time while lightweight node inventory responds.
- 28 bundled Control UI browser regressions passed, including exact selected/automatic-device dispatch, offline/capacity rejection, reconnect/recovery, model/worktree validation, and preference migration.

Before: restoration stayed blocked for a measured 30.5-second injected catalog hold, with no create or dispatch. After: the selected node was submit-ready while Cloud was pending; the exact mocked dispatch named `paired-runner` while an unrelated cloud response stayed unreleased for 30.5 seconds. The after recording also opens/reopens the dropdown and shows loading, error/retry, and completed options.


### Initial UI-only recordings

The initial screenshots and videos below record commit `26a99ff47b9` using the actual Control UI with deliberately delayed mocked Gateway responses; its UI tree was unchanged in compatibility correction `298a23ce282d`. They are retained as supplemental historical dropdown proof, with original source labels and raw recordings. The linked create/send proof above records `b23d44c` with an actual isolated Gateway and built UI; the recorded integrated-source comparison is linked above. Neither proof claims live remote-worker provisioning or live-provider inference latency.

All historical matched Local-fixture evidence is preserved with its original source labels. The retained-Cloud requirement is to preserve existing usability, not introduce a new availability restriction.
