title: fix(worktrees): prevent cleanup failures on large ignored trees
body:
Closes #148599

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes idle managed-worktree cleanup failing when large ignored dependency or temporary trees exceed Git's buffered filename-output limit.

## User Impact

Eligible worktrees can be cleaned up while retaining restorable local edits and owned staged inputs. Nested repositories, origin mismatches and other protected worktrees remain retained. No configuration, retention-policy or schema change is required.

This bounds buffered Git output, not total traversal time. A flat ignored-file inventory can still exceed the unchanged capture limit and fail closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request compact ignored-directory records from Git and walk those directories incrementally instead of buffering every generated descendant filename. Cleanup inspection and safety snapshots share that inventory owner. Preserve raw filename bytes through Node's unknown-directory-entry fallback, do not follow directory symlinks, and retain existing nested-repository and staged-input ownership checks.

## Evidence

- Original overflow reproduced with 64 empty generated files and a test-only 256-byte capture limit through both registered worker operations and actual managed-worktree garbage collection; the same cases pass after the fix.
- Two additional regressions reproduce the raw-directory `DT_UNKNOWN` fallback failure before the review correction and pass afterward using real Node `Dir` type resolution and filesystem lookup.
- Seven relevant suites passed: **83 tests**, covering worker lifecycle, garbage collection/restoration, snapshots, origin/canonical paths, provisioning, run-end cleanup and private staged inputs.
- Final focused rerun: **6 tests passed**. Canonical changed-file checks, typechecks, formatting, lint and dead-export/lifecycle/import guards passed.
- Linux/Node 26.8.2 proof. Invalid-byte cases are POSIX-only; the deterministic unknown-entry fallback injection runs through the production dispatcher in-process. Existing worker-lifecycle tests cover separate-thread operation. No production-scale tree or live cleanup was used as proof.
- Independent review identified the unknown-entry fallback issue; it was corrected with fail-before/pass-after coverage. Renewed independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean with no actionable findings.

title: fix: allow independent placement of persistent spawned sessions
body:
Closes #147603
Related: #148423

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could not move or pin a persistent follow-up session because the sidebar treated every session created by another session like a subordinate subagent run. Clearing a group also put the conversation back beneath its parent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persistent conversations now have independent sidebar placement; only actual subagent runs remain under a labeled Subagents section. Existing parent navigation, completion routing, workspace bindings, and permission ancestry are preserved. Confirmed group changes use the shared session-update owner so moves also reach sessions loaded only through a parent detail list.

## User Impact

Users can drag persistent spawned sessions into another group, return them to ungrouped, pin them, and follow their parent backlink without changing the underlying execution relationship. Subagent runs remain visibly subordinate and cannot be independently pinned or moved.

## Evidence

The Control UI browser scenario fails on the original source at the persistent session's `draggable=false` state. It passes after the change: move to Engineering, return to ungrouped, pin, and navigate back to the parent while the actual subagent stays nested. The scenario also covers a persistent session available only in the parent detail cache.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary full-tree downloads when mobile beta CI archives trusted release scripts from a partial clone, consuming much of the pre-upload authority deadline.

title: fix(heartbeat): avoid timeouts for busy scheduled polls
body:
Closes #148332

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: periodic heartbeat monitors can stay running behind foreground work, delay shutdown, and be recorded as failed after an ordinary Gateway restart.

## User Impact

User impact: a plain, event-free monitor poll that has not started preparation finishes as skipped and waits for its next scheduled tick. Busy foreground work no longer creates a false heartbeat failure.

Queued events, scheduled tasks, direct manual wakes, and work already prepared or admitted keep their retries and eventual success/failure accounting. Genuine execution deadlines remain errors. No configuration change, migration, permission change, or SDK contract change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing wake owner settles a poll only when the heartbeat runner proves it carries no pending work. Eligibility is conservative across coalescing, and a sticky work-started fact prevents later busy attempts from discarding admitted work.

This refresh preserves RoboClaw's original implementation and commit ancestry, incorporates the current scheduler/recovery ownership, and adds real-flow coverage for skipped monitors across restart. It updates this canonical PR without replacing its author credit.

## Evidence

- Baseline regression on `2d3dd99f5642`: idle/no-route settles, but a busy monitor fails to produce a finished event. The candidate proves prompt settlement, persisted next-tick cadence, unchanged restart state, zero error backoff, immediate cron drain, and no model/notification calls for skipped polls.
- 213 distinct affected/owner/sibling tests passed across 10 suites on the refreshed sources (175 infra; 29 existing real-flow/payload cron cases; all 9 busy-poll cases after the fixture corrections below). The affected and sibling test selection covers queued payloads, coalesced task success/failure, late admission, handler replacement, cancellation, module identity, store replacement, and genuine execution timeouts.
- Core source types, infra and services-cron test graphs, all changed-file formatting/lint, and relevant ownership/schema/import guards passed; the full repository suite and all test type graphs were not run locally.
- Fresh AutoReview completed on the exact final patch with no actionable P0–P2 findings; independent source review also found no actionable correctness issue. AutoReview used a sanitized source-only export with the exact selected diff and relevant owner/caller/dependency context. Exact-head hosted CI remains required before merge.
- The scheduler refresh exposed a fixture-only cross-thread clock mismatch: fake `process.hrtime` in the parent was incompatible with real SQLite-worker admission deadlines. The fixture keeps native hrtime while still simulating heartbeat cadence and watchdog timers; no production guard or assertion was weakened.

Tests use fake scheduling timers, isolated SQLite state, real command-lane blocking, and injected model/channel boundaries. This is deterministic scheduler/runner proof, not a live provider or deployed Gateway test. No Gateway restart, live schedule/configuration change, deployment, or merge is part of this update.

<details>
<summary>Regression cost</summary>

Earlier single-worker `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall measurements: private disposition 4.56 s (67 tests), module identity 9.16 s (1 test), real heartbeat flow 29.05 s (19 tests). Their test-time portions were below 30 seconds per file. Final refreshed busy-poll suite: 43.22 s wall (9 tests), with test execution 63% of the 39.67 s Vitest duration, below the 30-second per-file test-time budget. The real-flow suites retain CronService, wake ownership, heartbeat preflight/admission, and SQLite composition because fabricated busy results miss the original defect. CI timing will be available on the pushed revision.

title: fix: Side chat times out while searching session history
body:
Related: #148240

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Side chat stalling while answering questions that need session history and displaying “Side chat cannot answer right now.”

## User Impact

Side chat keeps its three read-only tools directly available and searches the selected session without paging through unrelated conversations. Its selected-session limit remains a hard ceiling even when the observed discussion has a plugin grant to another session. Ordinary granted reads remain supported outside Side chat.

No new configuration, schema change, production migration, automatic retry, or timeout increase. The existing 60-second deadline remains; this does not prevent every provider timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured-runtime admission correctly replaces stale caller configuration. Side chat had put its per-invocation restrictions in that replaceable config. These core-only controls now survive admission without replacing authoritative runtime configuration or widening public plugin inputs.

An omitted search target defaults to the host-selected session and uses targeted authorization instead of global enumeration. History and search enforce the selected-session ceiling before plugin grants. File reads retain the existing workspace-containment owner.

## Evidence

- Independent P2 autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable findings.
- **Exact-head CI is green:** [run 35093775422](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35093775422), attempt 2. The changed mechanism is covered by real-backend selected-session proof, provider-backed browser proof, and access/runtime regressions; this PR does not claim to eliminate every provider or Side chat timeout.

title: feat: give agents scoped, resumable session inventories
body:
Closes #147955

## What Problem This Solves

Agents managing many sessions cannot select a useful inventory by responsibility or workspace, or reliably continue a limited result.

## User Impact

Agents can find sessions by owner, creator, user involvement, project, workspace, sidebar group, pin/archive state, and live activity, then page through compact metadata without shell joins or transcript reads. Self-relative queries require the authenticated requesting user; metadata never grants access.

The default page is 100 rows, with at most 200 applied and a 64 KiB serialized budget. Larger positive limits remain accepted. Follow `hasMore` / `nextOffset` with the same filters; pages are a live view, so concurrent changes can require deduplication or restarting the inventory. Oversized optional previews fall back to metadata with `enrichmentOmitted`; metadata that cannot fit still fails explicitly. Embedded mode cannot provide `activeOnly` without live Gateway state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the Gateway’s canonical visibility, identity, metadata, and run-state projections rather than add another task or inventory service. Metadata selectors run before paging; associations support follow-up operations, while transcript previews remain opt-in. Existing owner facets and cooperative metadata/search reads are preserved.

This bounds tool work and output, not the entire database scan: the Gateway retains its existing metadata scan and caches. No configuration migration or database version change.

## Evidence

- Real tool → Gateway → SQLite proof finds all 37 matches among 3,474 sessions in one Gateway request, without transcript reads.

title: feat(sessions): select cloud OS and size when spawning sessions

## What Problem This Solves

Agents cannot select the cloud profile, operating system, and machine size when creating a visible worktree session, even though those choices already exist in the cloud placement flow.

## User Impact

User impact: hosted agents can discover configured cloud choices and start a visible worktree session on the selected profile, OS, and size. The task starts only after cloud placement succeeds; it never silently falls back to running locally.

title: fix: allow independent placement of persistent spawned sessions
body:
Closes #147603

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could not move or pin a persistent follow-up session because the sidebar treated every session created by another session like a subordinate subagent run. Clearing a group also put the conversation back beneath its parent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persistent conversations now have independent sidebar placement; only actual subagent runs remain under a labeled Subagents section. Existing parent navigation, completion routing, workspace bindings, and permission ancestry are preserved. Confirmed group changes use the shared session-update owner so moves also reach sessions loaded only through a parent detail list.

## User Impact

Users can drag persistent spawned sessions into another group, return them to ungrouped, pin them, and follow their parent backlink without changing the underlying execution relationship. Subagent runs remain visibly subordinate and cannot be independently pinned or moved.

## Evidence

The bundled Control UI browser scenario fails on the original source at the persistent session's `draggable=false` state. It passes after the change: move to Engineering, return to ungrouped, pin, and navigate back to the parent while the actual subagent stays nested. The scenario also covers a persistent session available only in the parent detail cache.

### Before
![Persistent session and subagent are both trapped beneath the parent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/485087c0-77e4-4a82-875d-e4be235d0e12)

### After
![Persistent session moved to Engineering while the subagent remains under its parent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e99be39c-23c9-49f9-99c5-9b429fd1ff83)

Screenshots use the real Control UI with a deterministic mocked Gateway. [Evidence discussion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/147603#issuecomment-5657497231).

- Affected UI tests: **653 passed** across sidebar, menus, navigation, and shared row-provenance coverage, plus **36 passing chat-header tests**. The menu fixture and visibility-boundary cases were rerun after their final cleanup.
- Session maintenance and stored batch-operation tests: **73 passed**.
- Gateway patch/list/RPC tests: **397 passed** in the broad run. The remaining workspace-detection fixture passed on rerun with `TMPDIR=/var/tmp`; the host's normal temp roots contain `.git` markers, invalidating that test's unrelated no-Git-ancestor assumption. No assertion was weakened.
- Three focused original-source navigation/projection regressions fail before the fix and pass afterward.
- Final changed-surface checks passed, including typechecking, lint, formatting, styles, i18n, dead exports, import cycles, and storage guards. Independent P0/P1 review found no actionable defects.
- After final cleanup, **468 sidebar/navigation tests**, **26 Gateway tests**, and the **real browser interaction** passed again.

Validation ran in an independently installed local checkout after Testbox authentication and AWS workload admission were unavailable. The unused AWS lease was released. No live provider or production session state was used.

<details>
<summary>Implementation scope</summary>

Production: **+90/-132 (net -42)**. Tests and test support: **+666/-341**. Documentation: **+5/-3**.

The change removes category-dependent child promotion and ancestry-dependent pin policy, uses real subagent identity for subordinate controls, and keeps cached group receipts in the existing scoped field-reconciliation path. Existing nested-run fixtures now use subagent keys; persistent-session cases assert independent placement. No storage schema, runtime ownership, retention policy, or permission contract was added. Existing pin protection now applies to the newly pinnable persistent conversations.

</details>

title: fix(ui): stop streamed updates from reopening task progress
body:
Related: #147295

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Task progress reopening and pulling the conversation downward when the agent streams new paragraphs after the reader scrolls slightly into history.

## User Impact

The card stays compact and the reading position stays put while new output arrives below it. An explicit return to Latest resumes normal following. Existing manual disclosure choices and motion settings are preserved.

This is the stability repair, not the proposed elastic/gesture-driven redesign.

## Why This Change Was Made

Closing the card can enlarge the transcript viewport and clamp it to the physical bottom. The geometry layer mistook that clamp for permission to follow; the next streamed update then reopened the card. Geometry, automatic end commands, and typing follow now consume the existing page-owned reader policy instead of granting themselves permission from position alone.

The existing end-anchor state and algorithm moved into a small helper to keep the virtualizer host within its file budget; it does not introduce another follow-policy owner.

body:
Most changed lines replace buffer tests and add regressions; production uses one durable Telegram cache.

## What Problem This Solves
Telegram group context disappears after Gateway restart. Reuses cached history and adds bounded message reads. Replaces #143892.

## Why This Change Was Made
One cache and one eligibility selector replace competing history paths. The other writers are admission and media enrichment; one shared lock orders all writes. Repair removes 70 production lines.

Restarts retain context; `/new` clears its window. Albums retain every admitted caption. Reads preserve chat/topic scope and bot replies, including shared-main DMs. Cache failures surface, including in DMs, instead of silently losing history.

Eight defects reproduced before repair. 1,040 selected Telegram tests and two Gateway authority tests pass. Typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, architecture and runtime build pass. Live Test Server restart/reset and actual history-read proof pass; the read returns both human and bot messages.

## Compatibility
Existing SQLite namespace, version and 3000-entry limit. Legacy rows remain reply context but need admission for ordinary history.

## Consumers
Telegram prompts and message reads share policy checks.

## Invalidation
Current policy, conversation scope and active session identity govern reads.

## Tests
Admission, paging, topics, albums, resets, identity and storage failures.

## Contention
Real SQLite race fails before repair; live and reopened rows agree after it.

title: fix: keep linked people consistent across mentions and sign-ins
body:
## What Problem This Solves

One person can appear as separate mention recipients with different avatars after signing in through multiple GitHub accounts. Full-name searches also stopped at spaces, and selected mentions rendered as ordinary text.

## User Impact

Explicitly linked accounts keep one person, avatar, preferences, and mention Inbox across sign-ins. The picker searches display names and every verified GitHub handle. Selected mentions retain their literal copied text and open an accessible person card with keyboard, mouse, or touch.

**Accepted downgrade risk:** this adds a nullable primary-account field without changing the shared-state schema version. Older single-account writers can discard secondary links or split the person again; re-upgrading does not reconstruct those links. Keep a backup before downgrading and explicitly relink affected profiles. The maintainer accepted this tradeoff rather than imposing a new database version.

## Why This Change Was Made

Verified account membership and the primary public GitHub identity are separate responsibilities. Explicit profile merges preserve all verified accounts and the target’s primary/credit choice; secondary sign-ins do not change that choice. Username/email reuse isolation remains intact. This adds no name-based automatic merging, permission expansion, or notification from rendering.

Current-main integration preserves the shared-transcript page cache while selecting the primary public identity, and stages resident profile-catalog updates before merge observers run. Main now owns the earlier startup and CI-fixture prerequisites and their regression coverage; duplicate changes have been removed from this PR.

## Evidence

- On `69dcb2b0930fc3940a71717624cbaf115494a7f3`: **57 focused identity/catalog/Markdown tests**, **102 message/composer tests**, UI typechecking, and **11 freshly bundled Chromium cases** pass. Browser cases cover typed search, keyboard/mouse/touch cards, stale replies, unavailable profiles, and adjacent dashboard flows.
- Earlier red-before regressions cover split-profile/re-login, lost shared avatars, literal dollar sequences and backticks in selected labels, and reference-style Markdown links. See the [mention regressions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ed9b0e285cf355f007ca0e8b63e08c8e1bb6656d/ui/src/components/markdown-human-mentions.test.ts) and [profile/linkage regressions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ed9b0e285cf355f007ca0e8b63e08c8e1bb6656d/src/state/user-profiles-multi-account.test.ts).
- Production avatar-handler proof gives both linked accounts 200 with identical stored PNG bytes; revoked or reassigned identities get 403 and a mismatched principal gets 401. Negative cases do not read the avatar.
- Current integration `b786face46a94aa4d4f030da65f76a5ca7076685` also passes **14 freshly bundled browser cases**, including all six streaming-runtime budgets, and **81 planner checks**. The browser budget probe now waits for committed startup roster work; counters, budgets and assertions are unchanged. Main owns the concurrent planner-fixture repair.
- Required CI and native landing gates remain bound to the actual pushed head; local checks are not a substitute.

**Proof limits:** authorization tests invoke the production handler, role policy and SQLite in-process, with mocked external Access/GitHub responses—not a live-provider login. Upgrade proof uses populated legacy-schema fixtures and reopening, not an old release binary. Captures use synthetic identities. No live profiles, Gateway configuration or deployment were changed.

title: fix(ui): keep chat images in place while loading
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading chat would see an attachment card disappear, a blank gap, and then an image push later messages down while metadata and thumbnail requests completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the image frame in the existing image-resource lifecycle throughout metadata checks, fetching, decoding, and failures. Known dimensions reserve the preview geometry; unknown dimensions use a stable contained preview. Raster attachments now share that owner instead of using a separate dimensionless image branch. Existing permission checks, loaded-image history handoff, ticket renewal, galleries, and image actions remain intact.

## User Impact

Images load in place with a subtle CSS shimmer using the active theme’s surface tokens—no visible icon or Loading text and no SVG asset request. This removes the file-card/blank/image transition. Failed managed previews remain visible and retryable. Current single-image limits, tiny-image sizing, and compact phone/desktop galleries are preserved.

## Evidence

- The new Chromium regression fails on the current-main baseline because the pending managed image has no frame, then passes with this fix.
- 282 chat rendering, media-lifecycle, and transcript-invalidation tests pass.
- 16 Chromium geometry/action cases pass: landscape, portrait, tiny images, narrow panes, unknown dimensions, local attachment/image-block metadata checks, phone/desktop galleries, tiny/tall action containment, and failed-fetch retry. Single-image shapes run for both assistant and user messages.
- 15 existing responsive image/gallery cases pass in Chromium and WebKit.
- All 8 transcript image/disclosure E2E cases pass, including delayed native image decoding and scrolling away/back through a virtual transcript. The image case now asserts unchanged pending/decoded geometry rather than the obsolete expectation of late image growth.
- UI production and test typechecks, targeted typed lint, formatting/stylelint, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent review of the complete corrected candidate and the final test-only repairs is scoped-clean through P2.
- Inspected screenshots below use the actual production renderer and styles with sanitized fixtures and delayed responses, not a live deployed Gateway. The following-message position changes on the baseline and is identical before/after loading with the patch.

A review caught a single-user shrink-to-fit regression during preparation. It is corrected with a definite intrinsic width plus the existing max-width bound, and protected by failing-before/passing-after browser coverage. The old handwritten tiny-image fixture was replaced by equivalent assertions against the production renderer.

### Before — loading

![Before: the generated preview is absent and the local image uses a file card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd6c02d5-a94b-4b28-9b76-0258f7096441)

### After — loading

Managed blob and local metadata cache reuse are checked across unmount/remount. Local image-byte caching is a separate task; permission checks and mutable-file HTTP revalidation remain unchanged.

Requested by @steipete; shimmer and video refinements requested by @vyctorbrzezowski. AI-assisted implementation.



<details>
<summary>Single-user width correction</summary>

The same production component tree reproduces the prior 0×0 regression when only the old percentage-width declaration is applied. Removing that override restores the corrected definite width. The corrected 400×267 frame remains identical through loading, decode, and rerender.

The pending image uses the existing CSS skeleton animation and surface tokens, with no icon, visible Loading label, extra asset request, or animation timer. Operators lack a dedicated machine workspace, and a docked desktop competes with conversations for space.

title: fix: let visible subagents select managed projects
body:
Related: #136011

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent cannot start a visible child session in a different registered project or GitHub repository through the managed-project selection flow already available in New session.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can select `projectId` or `projectGitUrl` when creating a visible child, optionally with a separate managed worktree. Arbitrary external `cwd` still requires admin authority; sandbox containment, inherited tool policy, and setup-script permissions remain unchanged. Hidden and ACP runs reject these visible-only selectors. No migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose and forward the existing project selectors rather than translating project selection into a raw host path or duplicating registry, clone, or credential logic. The Gateway remains the single owner of project resolution, URL validation, and selector conflicts. Omitting all source selectors preserves same-parent managed repository inheritance. Recovery guidance now points to the supported selectors.

## Evidence

### Direct and worktree sandbox containment

The creation owner now resolves the effective sandbox requirement while holding lifecycle custody, before binding a direct project root. The existing worktree-preparation owner validates that same prepared requirement before Git/worktree preparation. Deferred project preparation still validates the saved child policy. All three worktree-preparation callers pass the canonical configuration. No raw-path, setup-script, role, or sandbox permission is widened.

| Production-path scenario | Published pre-fix production (`e21c1adc424`) | Repaired candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Required parent, global sandbox off, direct external registered project | Did not reject during creation; regression failed | Rejected before child transcript/workspace binding, run registration, or dispatch |
| Required parent, immediate external registered-project worktree | Creation accepted; regression failed | Rejected before worktree allocation and child persistence |
| Required parent, deferred registered/GitHub project selection | Earlier repair retained | No worktree allocation or model dispatch |
| Required parent, contained direct project | Allowed | Allowed; inherited sandbox requirement and selected contents verified |
| Unrestricted registered/GitHub selection, direct or worktree | Allowed | Allowed; selected project, contents, and ownership verified |

- Ran the two new direct/immediate regression cases against the unchanged published production files: **2 failed for the expected missing-rejection assertions**. Restored the staged repair and verified its exact tree.
- Repaired tool-to-Gateway and root-containment matrix: **30 passed** across `server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn.test.ts` and `session-create-root.test.ts`; unrelated cases were excluded from this focused run. Tests use the real creation/preparation owners, real Git repositories/worktrees and persistence; model dispatch and remote clone I/O are mocked.
- Earlier full run of those files: **50 passed, 2 unchanged local baseline failures**, both expecting the old non-Git-workspace error text. Both had already been reproduced on the untouched base; this change does not weaken or alter them.
- Fresh complete-candidate autoreview: **scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings**.

title: fix(ui): clear duplicate prompts after successful session creation

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted prompts remaining in the New Session composer when draft cleanup, reconnects, or navigation interrupt the handoff to the created session.

## User Impact

Successfully submitted text, mentions, and attachments no longer remain available as a duplicate draft. Rejected first messages remain retryable in the session that was already created. No configuration or migration is required.

The submission owner records confirmed acceptance and consumes the draft synchronously before awaiting durable cleanup or navigation. Direct, cloud/device placement, background, and terminal starts share this cleanup path; background notifications no longer own composer state. Durable cleanup captures the original content before attachment custody is released.

title: improve(ui): make empty-group visibility explicit and personal
body:
Closes #147356

## What Problem This Solves
The sidebar could hide empty groups while its checkbox was off, without explaining the automatic behavior or offering a personal override.

## User Impact
The existing **Hide empty groups** row now shows **When filtering**, **Always**, or **Never**. Choices are personal to the signed-in user and Gateway in this browser; filter changes never rewrite them. Narrow screens use an in-menu choice list with Back.

An existing browser choice is adopted once by the first resolved viewer: on becomes Always, and off becomes When filtering. Other viewers do not inherit it. Preferences remain browser-local, not cross-device. Session access, group membership/order, catalogs, and team-mode agent groups are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
One explicit policy replaces the independent checkbox and automatic-filter hiding branches. The preference owner restores the right user before sidebar projection, distinguishes reconnects from account/connection changes, and rejects retired-menu writes. The existing submenu layout is reused; the menu host type contract is separated without a new lint suppression.

## Evidence
- 464 focused sidebar, projection, and preference-controller tests passed. The menu-choice regression fails on the original checkbox implementation and passes with the change.
- Eight Chromium production-bundle scenarios passed across the empty-group and existing owner-picker suites: personal filters, explicit overrides, keyboard navigation, large owner rosters, RTL, narrow-screen Back, selection, and reload. Geometry checks prevent clipping/overlap and preserve the established compact width.
- Hosted CI caught a compact owner-picker width regression. The follow-up limits widening to desktop and stacks this preference’s value in compact mode; the unchanged sibling regression now passes.
- UI and core-test typechecks, i18n, changed-file guards, and final targeted lint/style checks passed. The initial changed-check run found the controller line limit; a type-only host-contract split resolves it, with no suppression.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable defects in the feature or the compact-width follow-up. The host-contract extraction is type-only and passed UI typecheck and lint.

title: fix: keep new session workspace setup responsive during cleanup
body:
Closes #147355

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes new worktree-backed sessions waiting behind unrelated background cleanup inspection.

## User Impact
Foreground workspace preparation can finish while a slow cleanup inventory waits. Existing capacity, ownership, Git-write, cancellation, and shutdown safeguards remain in force. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made
Preparation and maintenance shared one serial Git worker. Keep both workloads serial, but give maintenance its own pool under the existing owner so a pre-lease cleanup scan cannot monopolize preparation. The extra worker uses the existing idle retirement and global pending-operation bound.

Removal that already holds the shared allocation lease still serializes with creation; this patch does not bypass that safeguard.

## Evidence
- Original implementation: both added worker regressions fail after approximately 10 seconds waiting behind held maintenance.
- Patched implementation: 71 tests pass—11 Git-worker lifecycle tests plus 60 worker-pool, capacity, and removal-lease tests. Cancellation, subprocess cleanup, snapshot ownership, HEAD changes, restart settlement, and disk-headroom serialization remain covered.
- Isolated real-service before/after: held a pre-lease ignored-file inspection in ManagedWorktreeService.gc and called ManagedWorktreeService.create in another repository. Original code timed out after 10 seconds; patched code created and registered the verified checkout in 133 ms while maintenance was still held.
- Independent autoreview: scoped-clean through P2.
- Complete changed-file gate passed, including core/core-test typechecks, lint, formatting, and guards.
- Full `pnpm build` passed on the unchanged published head in a clean sequential run. The first attempt hit the compiler input-consistency guard during concurrent validation; the retry required no code changes or guard bypasses.

Found while investigating chats that timed out with unfinished workspace setup. The exact historical timeout source remains uncertain; the blocking defect above is independently reproduced. Archived user sessions were not restored or modified by the repair.

Reported by @VACInc.

Closes #147271

## What Problem This Solves

Expanded task progress takes space from older chat messages, but automatic disclosure must not fight a user's manual choice.

## User Impact

Task progress folds into its current-step summary while reading history and expands upon returning to the live bottom. Manual expand/collapse wins through updates and the final response, then resets for the next accepted task/run. The existing collapse-by-default preference remains supported. No new setting or migration is required. Closing uses a gentle 240 ms ease-in-out fold, with the content fade and chevron moving together. Opening stays quick, interrupted closing reverses without a jump, and reduced-motion mode closes immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing disclosure owner now combines task-scoped manual intent with the transcript's settled reading position. Issuing a smooth return is distinct from arriving, and dock resizing or stationary/upward contact cannot reopen the card. Explicit already-at-bottom returns and toward-end wheel, keyboard, and touch input settle correctly. Disclosure remains local to the mounted view, as before.

title: fix: Control UI shows stale PR and publishing state
body:
Closes #147182

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale PR badges and misleading “Publishing” states during read-only lookups or after shared-publication reconnects.

## User Impact

Users see the actual PR state, distinguish loading from publishing, and recover a shared publication’s recorded outcome without running publication again. Status refreshes share cached state and coalesce overlapping hints. Existing personal-account confirmation and session permissions are preserved; no configuration or database migration is required. Pending receipts without valid bindings still fail closed instead of being rebound or replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication coordinator now exposes scoped shared receipt reads through the existing options/status methods. Committed receipt changes use the existing session event stream; the UI restores the applicable receipt on reconnect, preserves unknown outcomes by their original invocation key, and retires stale workspace/connection results.

Inline PR badges consume the existing preview state, while read and write activity are represented separately. Refresh failures remain visible alongside correctly scoped last-known PR data. Independent publication recovery no longer strands other workspaces behind one unfinished Git operation.

## Evidence

- Baseline regressions reproduced stale badges, false Publishing labels, missing shared receipt recovery, and stale workspace ownership.
- **155 focused tests passed for the final follow-up:** 129 shared/personal/legacy-receipt cases and 26 qualified-owner/store-lookup cases.
- **All 804 Gateway protocol tests pass** after reproducing and completing the remaining shared-options schema fixture. The test now includes the required `latestShared` field, accepts a closed shared receipt, and rejects malformed/authority-bearing fields in both recovery descriptors; the production schema and existing assertions were not weakened.
- **Exact-head CI is green:** [run 34807144577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34807144577) on `496aefc06a93067ff6699a3981abc73f55a8ab7a` completed all 144 jobs (134 successful, 10 skipped), including the required `openclaw/ci-gate` and configuration shard. The earlier config include-lock failure was investigated; causal attribution remains uncertain. No speculative or unrelated configuration repair was added.
- The late compatibility finding is repaired at the existing receipt reader. Four retained-state cases and two real options-RPC cases failed before the fix, then passed. Published and failed receipts without lifecycle bindings remain historical/unqualified; cold database bytes and sidecars are unchanged, personal confirmation remains discoverable, and no bindings are invented. The retained layout matches the inspected [v2026.9.1 writer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ad6fe23aecb9b833d68139b0ddc9f239b894d2f1/src/gateway/github-publication-store.ts).
- The failure in [CI run 34798004362](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34798004362/job/103835385023) was **PR-related**, not dismissed as baseline noise: the qualified-owner options fixture lacked the new shared reader. Its exact assertion was recovered from the log and reproduced locally. The fixture now supplies that dependency, expects the new response field, and additionally verifies the correct agent/session reaches shared discovery.
- **23 built Control UI browser tests passed** after rebase, including mock-WebSocket reconnect and cold completion recovery. Five publication hints coalesce into one in-flight read and one trailing refresh; observation/reconnect makes zero publish calls.
- Core and core-test type checks and scoped typed lint passed for the compatibility repair; the CI fixture also passes scoped typed lint. Protocol checks passed. The complete changed-file gate and 288 focused tests passed before rebase. SwiftLint was unavailable on the Linux host; generated Swift protocol output was checked.
- Fresh P0–P2 autoreview is clean for the legacy repair; prior full-candidate and post-rebase reviews are retained. The additional CI fixture correction is test-only and preserves, rather than weakens, its ownership assertions.
- Inspected before/after screenshots are embedded below and attached as image blocks in the originating chat. Browser proof uses synthetic Gateway/GitHub responses, not a deployed Gateway; no production publication was used as a test.

![After: recovered shared publication](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8dab656c-263c-4ee8-b4e5-ac338a05d1df)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale release-test setup and expectations that prevent the existing OTel, external-state ownership, and channel-progress fixtures from validating their intended runtime contracts.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Maintainers retain meaningful release coverage without changing test deadlines, skipping scenarios, relaxing Doctor, or weakening ownership and message-identity assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

These are the maintainer-requested Main-side fixture repairs from the [September 12 FRV child failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34682987877), separate from the release-source bundle in #146170.

- Match the existing approved root OTel SDK version while preserving independent plugin/preloaded-SDK identity checks.
- Apply the existing production SQLite busy policy to the fixture's deliberately separate writer connection.
- Test failed-tool detail according to the existing tool-progress setting: present when enabled, absent when disabled. The suite injects group messages only, so close the adapter's unused DM defaults before real bootstrap/Doctor checks; do not bypass those checks.

The OpenAI fixture is deliberately unchanged. Its frozen-harness provenance defect belongs to the reusable workflow and is handled separately in #146955. The Unicode-label work in #135277 is a separate change and is not replaced here.

## Evidence

- Canonical independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Formatting and targeted lint pass on all three files (0 warnings, 0 errors).
- Fresh isolated runtime proof passed all three complete fixtures: **24 tests passed** (2 OTel, 7 external-state, 15 progress), with wrapper exit 0 and retained detailed logs. Carrier: [34766653307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34766653307). The verified raw source tree `7c81f99f23dda5f46fd8fdf9c14cf3acb8d2a6e6` exactly matches the original signed commit `28c9db4a242fc3f68226d90d6a1c4de078026326`; all three fixture hashes match before and after the controls.

title: fix(ui): isolate strict HTML previews and save reopened drafts
body:
Related: #146672

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes strict HTML previews allowing forbidden descendant-frame requests and **Save** silently doing nothing when a retained HTML draft is reopened before **Source**.

## User Impact

Strict mode keeps the sandbox resource restrictions while disabling the document’s scripts. Reopened HTML drafts can be saved directly from Preview, with the same conflict detection, Reload, and Overwrite controls as Source.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both modes now use the existing separate-origin sandbox host. Only the untrusted inner document loses script permission in strict mode; the host’s CSP, descendant-markup guard, origin validation, and frame retirement remain in force. Ordinary files still receive no widget capability bridges.

Save and conflict recovery consume the existing retained text when no editor is mounted, preserve its expected hash, and clear or retain dirty state according to the actual save result.

## Evidence

- The new browser regression fails on the original strict renderer because its forbidden iframe reaches a controlled loopback HTTP receiver. The fixed renderer rejects it before I/O in strict, scripts, and strict → scripts → strict transitions.
- 46 attachment/transport tests, 19 Chromium file/editor tests, 16 isolated sandbox/HTTP tests, and all 10 affected Chromium E2E cases pass. Coverage includes saving before Source, retained conflict hashes, Reload/Overwrite without an editor, exact HTML transfer in strict mode, and closing root-distinct files through their filename tab.
- Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

- The earlier full `check-changed` and runtime/UI build passed. Fresh build, live proof and exact-head CI now pass for the Reload/editor-initialization repair. Startup limits remain unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway + Chromium, with no mocked network, passed scripts and strict rendering, original downloads, retained state, and forbidden-descendant checks across both transition directions. The reopened draft sent one `sessions.files.set` with its retained expected hash, updated the disk bytes, and cleared Save without ever mounting Source.

Controlled-receiver diagnostics from the real-Gateway runs:

```json
{"scripts_strict_scripts":{"controlRequests":1,"forbiddenRequests":0,"guardRejections":3},"strict_scripts_strict":{"controlRequests":1,"forbiddenRequests":0,"guardRejections":3},"reopenedDraft":{"saveCalls":1,"expectedHashPreserved":true,"editorMounted":false}}
```

Upstream #146862 fixed the stale sidebar-test imports; #146803 fixed the independent agent-shard cap. The previous `03b36445821` test-merge passed that shard guard. This PR does not change either prerequisite’s code or raise limits. Both stale UI test expectations found by CI have been migrated, without weakening their content, identity, or detachment assertions.

## Owner Involvement

This work was directly requested by @steipete in the [originating Team task](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4b64800e-a084-4012-84dd-bc98a70933e7), including sandboxed HTML rendering. Live GitHub membership checks on September 13, 2026 confirm active `openclaw-secops` maintainer and organization-admin roles. This records existing owner involvement for the scoped sandbox repair; it does not claim a separate GitHub approval or waive any enforced review/CI gate.

The real-Gateway captures are inspected and retained. GitHub attachment upload returned HTTP 400 (`Bad Content-Length`), so the transport diagnostics above are supplied inline.


## Reload / Source Race Follow-up

The latest review identified a real ordering defect: Reload could finish while first-time Source language loading was pending, after the editor had captured the discarded draft. The editor now reconciles from the panel’s current text after asynchronous creation and before installation or registering draft callbacks. Existing ownership/version checks remain in place.

A deterministic Chromium regression delays the real HTML language loader, finishes Reload first, then resumes editor initialization. It fails on `a9aea76da8b` with the old draft visible and passes with the repair. Editable and read-only reload outcomes are covered; the editable case then saves a new edit with the reloaded hash. Independent P0–P2 review of this change is scoped-clean.

## Startup Budget

The current-main control also exceeded the existing startup limit. To repair CI without changing budgets, the sidebar normalizer now reuses prepared IDs and active-panel selection, using the existing string readers. Legacy layout migration, blank versus missing main-panel IDs, plugin slots and expanded-side behavior are unchanged.

All 35 layout tests pass, as do 10,000 deterministic before/after normalization cases. The canonical source comparison reports **355,702 gzip bytes** against the unchanged **355,719-byte** startup ceiling. Typecheck, type-aware lint and the coercion-declaration guard pass; independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. No baseline, limit or test assertion was weakened.

The branch was refreshed onto main for the failing integration guard; range comparison preserves the production changes and drops only a filename-tab test migration already upstream. Fresh exact-head CI and runtime replay are complete.

## Final Validation

For head `d917e89713d1f1d96d4f57aa56f7f2007a4db973`: full runtime/UI build completed, both real-Gateway scripts/strict replays and all 10 affected bundled browser E2E cases passed. Opening another file replaces the current side-panel preview, and HTML attachments cannot be viewed as interactive documents.

title: fix: stop stale messages replaying after upgrades
body:
Closes #135191

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes old messages being sent again when an upgrade imports abandoned legacy delivery queues and a channel reconnects.

## User Impact

Pending legacy messages at least 72 hours old, or with an unverifiable enqueue time, are preserved for manual review instead of automatically delivered. Normal SQLite delivery and retry policies do not change.

Original files and queue-owned attachments are retained as private migration backups with no automatic expiry. Review them before explicitly sending a new message; do not restore archived files into the queue. Complete any reported cleanup before running an older build.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared migration owner now applies the cutoff to both outbound and session queues using the original enqueue time. Source receipts commit with the queue decision, making cleanup retries idempotent. Attachment custody remains recorded until verified copies exist. Delivered evidence applies to duplicate queue IDs and is retained while malformed matching sources need repair.

Safely preserved old entries produce recoverable warnings, not a failed upgrade. Malformed or conflicting data remains in place for repair. There is no new schema, configuration option, or general delivery TTL.

## Evidence

- Red/green regressions cover both namespaces: the 72-hour boundary, invalid timestamps, delivered duplicates, malformed-source repair, archive retries after consumption, attachment-copy failure followed by garbage collection, and reappearing sources.
- 44 focused migration/recovery/media tests passed after the final marker-cleanup correction. The migration, SQLite, recovery and recording-adapter paths run without live channel sends.
- A broader 473-test run across 20 files and a full build passed before that final narrow correction; affected tests were rerun afterward.
- Core and test typechecks still report the unchanged TS2741 in `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts:416`, also reproduced on the clean base. They are not claimed green.
- The published-updater × candidate integration cell was not run: Docker was unavailable during that earlier proof run. No live platform delivery is claimed.

Maintainer follow-up evidence:

- Fixed premature delivered-evidence retirement when a malformed duplicate remains. Both the marker and the original ID-bearing twin remain available, including opaque legacy markers; unreadable IDs conservatively retain delivered evidence until repair.
- Added eight regression cases across outbound/session queues, opaque/canonical markers, and malformed JSON with/without a visible ID. Against the original migration code: eight failures, including `expected { n: 1 } to deeply equal { n: 0 }` after repair. With the fix: eight passes and no runnable duplicate.
- Removed the migration helper's dynamic import of the full media-spool runtime. Migration and spool now share only the existing filename/path validator; the migration implementation remains behind the Doctor owner's dynamic import.
- Final focused proof: 203 tests passed across `test/scripts/tsdown-config.test.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.delivery-queues.test.ts`, `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-file-migration.test.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts`, and `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-spool.test.ts`. The retained-config bundle regression changed from one failure/25 passes to all 26 passing.
- Final `pnpm build` passed with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings. `pnpm check:import-cycles` reports zero runtime value cycles.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed its early guards but stopped at the existing TS2741 in `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts:416`; that file is byte-identical to the PR base. The selected infra/messaging test typecheck reports the same error. Remaining planned lint, schema, database-first, coercion, deprecated API, dead-export, media, sidecar, webhook, and pairing guards were run separately and passed.
- Maintainer delta: production +42/-19 lines; tests +36/-0 lines. No schema or schema-version change, configuration option, dependency, or normal SQLite queue TTL was added.

Previous-head CI: [run 34729886861](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34729886861) completed for `3bff4acdbf19cb7e76e3f6967930a4369b368bb4`: 113 jobs succeeded, 16 skipped, and two failed (`checks-node-compact-small-32` plus the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`). The underlying failure is four assertions in `test/scripts/upgrade-survivor-plugin-registry.test.ts:356`: the newer main-side shell helper passes an extra `discord` argument. Both fixture files are unchanged by this PR, and all four cases pass on this branch. The matching assertion fix is already on main in #146606 (`01eb021ea972d25ac79202ee09699419514b074c`). The landing fixup triggered fresh CI against the current merge ref.

Worked on by: @IWhatsskill


## ClawSweeper review

Applied the archive-memory finding: unused archive paths rename without reading the source; collisions use the existing bounded file-descriptor SHA-256 helper. SQLite sidecar archival preserves the database, WAL, existing archives, and numbered duplicate reuse without a whole-file allocation.

title: fix(ui): keep assistant messages intact while tools run
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a streaming assistant sentence breaking into fragments such as “I'll check” and “what” when tool activity arrives during the response.

## User Impact

Assistant messages stay together and grow continuously while tools start, report progress, finish, or replay. Streaming is not buffered until completion. Completed messages, keyed commentary, and user/steer boundaries keep their existing owners.

**Provisional placement:** while persistence is catching up, tool cards can appear above the still-growing text. Once its durable message arrives, transcript order owns placement. The response is no longer cut into completed-looking fragments to position it around tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous revision only removed fragments after completed commentary arrived. @VACInc correctly pointed out that it left the visible in-flight bug intact. This revision withdraws that cleanup-only change and removes the source of the invalid state: `handleAgentEvent` no longer calls `rolloverChatStream` when a tool entry appears. Tool execution timing does not prove an assistant message has ended, including for delayed top-level starts and history replay.

No new stream manager, message identity protocol, configuration, schema, or stored-data migration is introduced. Existing persisted-assistant prefix reconciliation, keyed commentary, and persisted user boundaries remain unchanged. Production diff: **+2/-3 lines**.

## Evidence

- **262 focused tests pass** across the page/Gateway-event flow, tool activity, commentary reconciliation, and stream materialization.
- The strengthened regression fails on the previous cleanup-only revision **before preamble completion**: it renders “I am” and “checking the files and” as separate bodies. The new revision keeps the complete partial sentence in one body after every delta and tool event.
- Added root/nested tool phase coverage and completed-A → tool → persisted-A → growing-B coverage, with persistence both before and after tool arrival. Replaced the obsolete assertion that tool arrival should close the stream.
- New real Chromium/mock-Gateway before/after recordings assert intermediate states throughout the unfinished sentence, including a delayed top-level start among nested starts. Both also show the following answer streaming in three updates. The previous PR produces three in-flight fragments; this revision produces none.
- Both captioned H.264 MP4s (~24 seconds, 1280×800, 25 fps) were inspected and delivered as playable attachments in the linked team session. **These supersede the earlier cleanup-only proof.**
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent autoreview of the staged replacement candidate is scoped-clean through P2.
- Current source: `a05c749ca4f7b25a2bf676be3171d0b008d0b07f`; exact-head CI run 34729969374, attempt 2, completed successfully. GitHub reports no failed or pending checks and a clean merge state. ClawSweeper revision 5 cleared this exact head with no blocking findings. The branch retains mainline #146538.

**Limits:** this is deterministic browser proof, not a replay of the original production WebSocket trace. Public binary uploads are blocked by the current transport: GitHub returns HTTP 400 `Bad Content-Length`, and the approved artifact-store fallback returns HTTP 403 `SignatureDoesNotMatch` with an empty canonical content length. The videos are available in the team session; no unverified public asset URL is claimed.

### CI follow-up

The test-only follow-up aligns reconnect/streaming coverage with continuous messages and expands grouped activity before enforcing the unchanged 50-tool cap and eviction checks. All 47 reconnect tests and 14 browser tests pass locally; type-aware lint and independent review are clean.

The quota-readiness check was intermittent: both automatic and saved-clear cases passed on the exact failing integration revision in diagnostic run 34731210493, and the PR’s own targeted retry then passed the full real-Gateway job and aggregate gate in run 34729969374, attempt 2. No quota assertion, safeguard, or production behavior was weakened. The diagnostic run itself is not used as the PR merge gate.

title: fix(cron): preserve terminal errors across session renames

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing terminal errors when a cron session’s label changes while its exact run is still active.

Closes #146224

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing Control UI could see subagent activity remain running after restart cleanup removed its native run owner. The task kept its last tool name, such as `process` or `sessions_yield`, even though the retained chat session was not proof of active work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Orphan handling now uses the existing completion lifecycle rather than deleting registry entries through a separate cleanup path. Known linked-task write failures keep completion retriable before cleanup, and Gateway maintenance reconciles tasks stranded by earlier pruning only when their live and durable owners are absent.

Actual live runs, queued/yielded work, replacement generations, restart recovery, and pending completion delivery retain ownership. No UI-only hiding, schema/config changes, or changes to execution timeouts.

## User Impact

Orphaned work reaches an honest terminal state instead of appearing to run indefinitely. Existing stranded task records can also converge through normal Gateway maintenance. Genuine detached work stays visible after its parent turn ends.

Reported by @VACInc.

title: fix(doctor): stop stamping config when the release backfill has no work
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` rewrites the operator's `openclaw.json` after a release step that installed nothing.

`maybeRunConfiguredPluginInstallReleaseStep` returns `touchedConfig: !updateInProgress` on the branch taken when there are no configured plugins and no configured channels. The Doctor state runner consumes `touchedConfig` as "persist the config", so a release backfill with zero work still:

- rewrites an authored `openclaw.json`, discarding operator formatting and comments,
- **creates** `openclaw.json` outright on installs that never had one,
- stamps `config.lastTouchedAt` machine state.

The sibling early return directly above it (same "nothing configured" condition, release step not due) already returns `touchedConfig: false`, so the two no-work paths disagreed.

Separately, `scripts/e2e/lib/plugin-update/corrupt-update-scenario.sh` was the only `OPENCLAW_NPM_REGISTRY_UPSTREAM` assignment under `scripts/` still hardcoding the public registry, so prepublish release validation reached npmjs.org instead of the staged prepublish registry that every sibling scenario honors.

## Why This Change Was Made

Report no config touch when no backfill ran. `touchedConfig` is the "I changed config, persist it" signal; a no-op producing it is an ownership violation at the producer, not something the Doctor runner should second-guess. Real repair work still persists its completion write, and deferred/update-time behavior is unchanged — `updateInProgress` still governs `completed` and the deferred post-install Doctor result on the paths that actually do work.

**Scope note — this PR was narrowed.** It previously carried the whole frozen 2026.9.5 release-qualification stack (270 files) on an old cut; merging that would have reverted large amounts of current `main`. Per the maintainer disposition in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146170#issuecomment-5716401394, it is now rebuilt on current `main` (`ee36fb4bdf4`) as the focused owner repair. Previous head for reference: `8b9454a0320a8ee3df9e6b5fbc986790f04e311c`.

Disposition of every other difference the maintainer named, so none is silently discarded:

| Remaining difference | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `agent-roster.ts` full-config `listAgentIds` / `tryResolveDefaultAgentId` overloads | **Dropped here.** Open PR #148446 already implements this against the current `main` owner (`src/agents/agent-roster.ts`). This branch's copy targeted the pre-relocation owner `agent-scope-config.ts` and would have been mis-owned. |
| Vercel Undici override/lock | **Superseded by `main`.** `main` already pins `undici` `8.10.2` in `package.json` and `mailauth@5.0.3>undici` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — ahead of this branch's historical 6.28.1 repair. No dependency change is carried, so no dependency admission is needed. |
| Matrix test cleanup | **Superseded by `main`** via #150697 (`refactor(tests): reuse Matrix deferred fixtures`). Replaying the branch's copy would delete newer Matrix work. |
| Selected-runtime registry reuse (`prepared-model-runtime.inbound-registry.ts`) | **Not carried.** It swaps `reusableGeneration?.pluginRegistry` for `baseRegistry` in a hot runtime path with no stated defect, and `main`'s surrounding selection logic has since changed. Recorded as a follow-up rather than replayed unqualified. |
| Corrupt-update fixture registry selection | **Carried** (one line) — it is a real sibling-consistency defect on current `main`, see above. |
| `scripts/e2e/status-corrupt-plugin-deps.sh` (new 159-line scenario) | **Not carried.** Unreferenced by any workflow; a release-qualification artifact, not a `main` repair. |
| Version bump to 2026.9.5, generated UI/native locales, markdown-it upgrade, plugin CLI callback ownership (#148524), update service env binding (#148061) | **Not replayed.** Already in `main` or release-owned; this PR claims no release authority. |

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor` and update-time Doctor no longer touch `openclaw.json` when the configured-plugin release backfill has nothing to install. Operators keep their hand-authored config formatting and comments, and installs without a config file do not get one materialized by a no-op step.

**Update behavior:** this is a candidate-side Doctor fix. The installed (published) updater runs first and is not patched by it; the fix keys only on markers shipped drivers already set (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS`, `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PARENT_SUPPORTS_DOCTOR_CONFIG_WRITE`, `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DEFER_CONFIGURED_PLUGIN_INSTALL_REPAIR`, `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_POST_CORE_CONVERGENCE`) and takes existing operator state as input. Nothing becomes more fail-closed: the change only removes a write. No config migration is needed — an already-stamped config stays valid.

No config/default surface is added or changed, and no schema, storage, or persistence contract changes.

## Evidence

**Regression proof (fails pre-fix, for the intended reason).** Reverting only the production line and rerunning:

- `release-configured-plugin-installs.test.ts` — 2 failed / 30 passed. The `standalone` and `post-plugin` phases report `touchedConfig: true`.
- `release-configured-plugin-installs.persistence.test.ts` — 2 failed / 4 passed, at the Doctor boundary through the real state runner and real config writer (only external package installation is mocked):
  - `expected { …(2) } to deeply equal {}` — Doctor injected `meta.lastTouchedVersion` / `wizard` into an empty config.
  - `promise resolved "Buffer[…]" instead of rejecting` — `openclaw.json` was **created** where the test asserted `ENOENT`.
  - `expected '{\n  "meta": {\n    "lastTouchedVersi…' to be '// Operator formatting stays intact.\…'` — the operator's authored file and comment were overwritten.
  - `expected '2026-09-17T18:02:31.979Z' to be undefined` — `config.lastTouchedAt` machine state stamped.

With the fix: **38/38 pass** (32 unit + 6 persistence).

Splitting the two suites precisely, because they cover different things:

- **Unit suite** (`release-configured-plugin-installs.test.ts`) covers all three phases a published driver can present — `standalone`, `pre-plugin`, `post-plugin` — asserting `touchedConfig: false` in each.
- **Persistence suite** (`release-configured-plugin-installs.persistence.test.ts`) runs every case under one marker set only: the post-core set (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS`, `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PARENT_SUPPORTS_DOCTOR_CONFIG_WRITE`, `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DEFER_CONFIGURED_PLUGIN_INSTALL_REPAIR`, `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_POST_CORE_CONVERGENCE`). It does not span the three phases. What it adds instead is depth: it goes through the real Doctor state runner and real config writer, mocking only external package installation.

These markers are injected into the test environment, so neither suite is an execution of a published updater. The persistence suite also asserts the positive direction: configured plugin work and configured channel work still persist their completion write, and a genuine config repair plus first-write privacy defaults still commit.

### Published-driver × candidate proof

Ran `scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` with `PUBLISHED_BASELINE=1`, `BASELINE_SPEC=openclaw@2026.9.4`, scenario `base`: it npm-installs the real published release and lets **that** driver run `openclaw update` onto this branch's candidate. `update.json` confirms `before: 2026.9.4-release-3a9d69db306c` → `after: 2026.9.4-5a5ef2904b79`, `status: "ok"`, with post-update `config validate` returning `valid: true`.

The lane's terminal assertion fails on **both** this branch and pristine `main`, identically: `integrity-drift` on `@openclaw/codex@2026.9.4`, same npm outcomes, same exit 1. That is a fixture-registry package-hash mismatch that `main` already has; the pristine-`main` run is the control.

#### The no-work branch, isolated

The `base` recipe always configures channels, so the above does not reach the changed branch. Isolating it needs three conditions at once: the release step **due** (config last touched below the `2026.5.2-beta.1` gate), **zero** configured plugins and channels, and **no other repair pending** — otherwise an independent writer masks the difference. A settled install normally carries `lastTouchedVersion: 2026.9.4`, which makes the step *not* due and yields a vacuous pass.

Harness: install published `openclaw@2026.9.4`, let its own `doctor --fix --non-interactive` settle the install (second pass verified idempotent), backdate only `meta.lastTouchedVersion` to `2026.5.1`, then let that published driver update to each candidate. Both runs start from byte-identical settled configs and report `configured-plugins=0`, `configured-channels=0`.

| | `main` (control) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | `OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)` | `OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)` |
| `update-status` | `ok` | `ok` |
| before → after build | `release-3a9d69db306c` → `c9ab1cff77ec` | `release-3a9d69db306c` → `5a5ef2904b79` |
| `lastTouchedVersion` after | **`2026.9.4`** (stamped) | **`2026.5.1`** (untouched) |
| operator config | **`CONFIG_REWRITTEN`** | **`CONFIG_PRESERVED`** (byte-identical) |

The published updater completes in both cases; only the operator's file differs. This reproduces the defect through a real published driver and shows the repair removing it.

The control's rewrite also persists a `meta.migrations.utilityModelSeparation` marker that this branch does not. Related: #138090 covers the separate terminal wizard and persistence path; this change is limited to Control UI selection rendering.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting settings from an enum could see the wrong option selected or restored when the schema allowed values with identical text but different JSON types, such as `1` and `"1"`, or `false` and `"false"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing type-preserving config-value comparison for both dropdown and segmented controls. This removes the competing primitive-to-string matcher rather than adding another special case. Selection callbacks, rejection handling, defaults, nullable values, and supported JSON enum values retain their existing contracts.

## User Impact

Mixed-type choices remain distinct through selection and rerendering. A rejected change restores the correct typed member, and an inherited default does not silently become an explicit override. Null, unset, and string values remain separate.

## Evidence

- The original source failed 16 of 18 targeted regression cases; two controls already passed. The repaired source passes all 18.
- The maintained three-file Chromium selection passes 74 cases. Parent independently reran the final scalar integrity file: 46 passed, including the 18 regressions, with all three source hashes unchanged. These are overlapping selections, not additive coverage.
- UI test types and the complete 20-check changed gate against 47ce03dbc6994435af783fecf13d5586e7b307f4 pass, including core/UI type checks, all dead-export scans, lint and styles.
- Normal UI build passes and reports no performance-budget violations. Its report-only measurement does not substitute for the separate CI base-comparison check. No budget or measurement settings were changed here.
- Production changes are +3/-25, net 22 lines removed. Test-only brace corrections and a Lit lifecycle wait kept inside the custom-radio branch preserve every selection/recovery assertion; no cast, suppression, sleep or forced action was added.
- Fresh full-diff P0–P2 autoreview completed scoped-clean with no findings, covering the final production and test bytes. All source hashes matched before and after review.

title: fix(ui): render Markdown attachments in the sidebar
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening Markdown attachments in the chat side panel saw raw Markdown instead of a readable document.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text-attachment preview now recognizes `.md`, `.markdown`, and Markdown MIME types and uses the existing sanitized document renderer and sidebar styles. The asynchronously rendered attachment owns the shared Markdown lifecycle, so code overflow, expand, and wrap controls initialize as soon as the file loads. Ordinary text, HTML, logs, and structured-data attachments stay literal. The existing size limit, bounded fetch, download link, and cancellation behavior are unchanged; remote images remain disabled.

Validation also found an existing undefined `retainedMachine` locator in the cloud-picker screenshot test. This PR binds the already-asserted machine locator and reuses it for the screenshot, restoring typecheck and capture-enabled proof without weakening assertions.

## User Impact

Markdown attachment headings, emphasis, lists, tables, and fenced code are readable without leaving chat. Users can still download the original file. Requested by Peter Steinberger.

## Evidence

- Regression first: all eight new Markdown cases failed against the original renderer; the 20 existing text-preview cases passed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing resource-preserving JSON Schema normalizer instead of a competing MCP traversal that relocated definitions while expanding union types. MCP retains its annotation-only format handling; other callers keep their defaults, and older schema drafts retain the existing SDK/AJV path.

With TypeBox 1.3.26, the parent independently ran the same regression against current main production and the candidate: baseline rejects the valid leaf with a false-schema error while still rejecting the invalid leaf; the candidate accepts the valid leaf and rejects the invalid one.

title: fix: keep port clients visible with spaces and colons in process names
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users inspecting daemon status or Doctor port diagnostics would not see an established client when the Linux ss fallback reported a process name such as "node worker:1".

## User Impact

Valid established clients with these names remain visible. IPv6, mapped addresses, exact-port matching, first-process metadata and unknown-process rows retain their behavior. Process text cannot masquerade as listener state. No operator services, network routing or authority rules change.

## Evidence

- Parent executed the new Linux native fixture: an owned ephemeral loopback TCP server/client, process name "node worker:1", and real ss output filtered to that fixture port. Captured rows pass through real inspectPortConnections using the existing command-output fixture boundary. This is not a whole-daemon CLI or native-Windows claim.

title: fix(discord): preserve resolved tokens with unpaired runtime config
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending Discord messages with SecretRef-backed named accounts would receive a configured-but-unavailable token error after command startup pinned unresolved config and command-scoped secret resolution returned a separate resolved config. The send could fail before any Discord REST request even though its supplied credentials were resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared runtime-config selector now replaces a distinct supplied config only when it matches the active snapshot's paired source, including resolution provenance. A pinned cache without a paired source cannot overwrite command-resolved credentials. This fixes the shared ownership boundary rather than adding a Discord-only workaround or an environment-token fallback. Speech requests bind the existing runtime-config reader before asynchronous provider work, so fallback still observes refreshes for a known runtime owner while preserving separately scoped configs.

### SDK compatibility

This intentionally corrects the shipped unpaired-source fallback: a distinct explicit `inputConfig` is preserved when `runtimeSourceConfig` is omitted. Plugins requesting the process snapshot unconditionally can omit `inputConfig`; plugins selecting it for a supplied source should provide the matching `runtimeSourceConfig`. No export, type, or required parameter changes; paired-source and no-input behavior remain covered. This follows the existing preference for passed config and the established agent-tool/cron safeguards. External reliance on the former override is not fully knowable and remains an acknowledged upgrade risk; retaining it would keep the reproduced credential-loss bug.

## User Impact

Discord sends keep their explicitly resolved named-account credentials. Matching active-source selection and no-input runtime selection still work, while genuinely unresolved credentials continue to fail closed. No configuration changes or credential migration are required.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the core regression replaced resolved credentials with a SecretRef and the Discord regression reproduced the configured-unavailable error.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tts/tts-request.resources.test.ts src/config/runtime-snapshot.test.ts extensions/discord/src/client.test.ts extensions/discord/src/token.test.ts`: 69 tests passed. Discord coverage runs `sendMessageDiscord()` with mocked REST, verifies a receipt and exactly one POST, and retains fail-closed behavior. The 30 speech-resource tests include runtime-owned refresh and explicitly scoped config across telephony, buffered speech, and Talk.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts`: 112 tests passed. The corrected queued-reply regression fails with the original selector because its explicit config is discarded; it now verifies requested context refresh and that diagnostic compaction metadata does not become durable compaction accounting. No compaction production code changed.
- Fresh full-candidate structured review passed with no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Focused lint, core typecheck, the messaging and remaining-core test typecheck shards, the core test-root boundary guard, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The current-base UI performance comparison also passed. The branch includes the already-landed config/CLI test-root rebalance; no CI limits were relaxed in this PR.
- Initial CI exposed the speech fallback dependency and a queued-reply assertion that only passed because the old selector erased its configuration. The updated tests cover both cases rather than restoring the broken fallback.
- The later inherited picker failures (line limit, unused exports, cursor policy) are repaired on main by `57674ef82592b712a17507539b6f89609d8547c2` (#145415). This branch was rebased onto that canonical repair, with an identical stable patch ID before and after; no duplicate UI repair or CI limit change was added. On the refreshed base, all 260 targeted tests—including the original 181 and the affected UI cohort—passed, and the formerly failing line-limit lint and full dead-code/dependency gate passed.
- Source review includes command-secret application, Discord account/token resolution, and the existing explicit-config safeguards in agent-tool, model-auth, cron, LINE, queued-reply, TTS, and web-search consumers.

Limitations: no live Discord or production verification was performed. This PR does not claim to fix the separate prepared-model plugin-generation supersession error.

Requested by @steipete.
