title: fix: update triage misses incompatible systemd shutdown settings
body:
Related: #142394

## What Problem This Solves

Structured Doctor and triage output omitted the existing Linux systemd warning for incompatible `KillMode` settings. Operators investigating a failed upgrade therefore missed a relevant diagnosis already available in the service audit.

This PR addresses the diagnostic omission described in the September 11 follow-up. It does not resolve the entire shutdown/recovery incident reported in #142394.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the existing systemd audit findings through the platform-warning collector. Keep repair guidance in `fixHint` so it survives triage message truncation. No additional unit parser is introduced.

## User Impact

- Doctor and triage identify incompatible effective shutdown settings and provide profile-aware repair guidance.
- Existing installation-identity, remote-mode, and Nix exclusions are preserved; macOS behavior is unchanged.
- This is diagnostic-only: it does not rewrite units, change shutdown/recovery behavior, or introduce a schema migration. Warnings remain nonblocking at the updater’s error-only lint threshold.

## Evidence

Validated head: `fce27b7ccc5294a244089bea619a459740742068`.

- Eight new regression cases and 66 existing relevant tests passed. The new registered-check and CLI-handler regressions fail without the change.
- [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34651874783), including type, lint, and repository checks.
- [Package Acceptance passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34651360121), including package integrity, npm 12 installation, and the published 2026.9.3-to-candidate upgrade scenario.

### Native Linux verification

Compared separately installed release and candidate packages against a real systemd user manager on September 11, 2026 (Node 26.7.0, systemd 259.5).

| Package and effective configuration | `KillMode` warnings |
| --- | ---: |
| Released 2026.9.4, `control-group` | 0 — missing diagnosis |
| Candidate, same unit and profile | 1 — expected warning |
| Candidate, `mixed` base overridden to `control-group` | 1 |
| Candidate, `control-group` base overridden to `mixed` | 0 |

The packaged Doctor and triage commands produced the expected diagnosis and profile-specific repair hint. Unit, drop-in, and configuration bytes were unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Observed triage output</summary>

```text
[warning] core/doctor/gateway-services/platform-notes: KillMode=mixed is required to drain active turns before final service child cleanup; inspect unit and drop-in overrides. (~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway-oc145322-before.service: control-group)
Fix: Run openclaw --profile oc145322-before gateway install --force only after verification; inspect drop-ins separately.
```

</details>

These were inactive test units (`MainPID=0`), removed after verification. This demonstrates the diagnostic change, not shutdown with active children or recovery after an injected cleanup failure.

Worked on by:
- @IWhatsskill

**Review follow-ups:** The data-model compatibility item is a review-risk flag, not a persistent-data change: the production diff only reads the existing service audit and emits advisory findings; it adds no schema, migration, backfill, service writer, or retention/recovery change. Exact-head Package Acceptance run [34651360121](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34651360121) passed, including the published 2026.9.3-to-candidate upgrade cell. The native diagnostic proof records unchanged unit, drop-in, and configuration bytes. No actionable code findings remain. Active-child shutdown and cleanup-failure recovery remain outside this diagnostic-only PR and #142394 stays related rather than closed.

title: improve(ui): speed up inline edit previews
body:
## What Problem This Solves

New or changed inline edit previews spend unnecessary CPU and allocation on a boxed two-dimensional longest-common-subsequence table. This work runs on the UI thread when preparing a tool-call diff.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one bounded `Uint16Array` table and one reconstruction loop instead of nested arrays and three separate traversal loops. The existing 600-line comparison bound keeps every table value within range. Deletion-first tie handling, newline normalization, exact/incomplete statistics, context compaction, and preview limits are unchanged. No dependency or public API changes.

This is part of a maintainer-requested production-code simplification campaign. The production diff is +17/-40 (23 net lines removed), replacing repeated mechanics rather than compressing code.

## User Impact

Inline edit previews display the same result with less comparison work. In local 600-line microbenchmarks, median comparison time fell from roughly 11.5–13.2 ms to 1.0–1.5 ms across equal, single-edit, complete-replacement, reversed, and repeated-line inputs. These are comparison timings, not a claim that the entire UI is 8–12 times faster.

## Evidence

- 103 focused tests passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/lib/chat/tool-call-diff.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/tool-call-view.test.ts`.
- Independent differential execution compared 14,641 small input pairs in both compact and noncompact modes against the original implementation: all complete results matched exactly. Five 600-line cases also matched, with 20 measured samples after five warmups per implementation.
- The freshly built Control UI passed three real-Chromium tool-detail flows (dark desktop, light desktop, dark mobile): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-tool-turn-outcome.e2e.test.ts -t "keeps narrated tool details"`. These use deterministic mocked Gateway data; no live provider or external channel is claimed. The other eleven cases in that file were intentionally outside the selected test filter.

title: fix(slack): hide command failures in quiet progress
body:
Related: #140037, #92085

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users in shared Slack conversations would see a persistent list of recovered command failures after a successful answer when quiet progress was enabled. Turning off the ordinary tool log did not remove these rows from native task cards or the Block Kit fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter known intermediate command-failure events at Slack's existing compositor event-projection boundary, before any card publishes them. Both command-output and command-bearing item events use this policy; native cards, Block Kit cards, and compact drafts consume the same filtered state. No new configuration, execution changes, transcript changes, or global error-suppression switch are introduced.

## User Impact

- Quiet progress (the default, explicit `progress.toolProgress: false`, or its preview alias) retains authored progress, plans where supported, and approvals without a recovered-command log.
- Explicit `toolProgress: true` remains unchanged. Existing compact/card selection is unchanged; use `style: "card"` to keep plan cards with explicit `toolProgress: false`.
- Blocked/action-required and unknown outcomes, malformed exit statuses, and unrelated tool errors are not newly suppressed. Final error replies and the unconditional no-visible-reply warning remain intact.
- This intentionally changes the older quiet-mode behavior that retained intermediate command failures. Other channels, including Telegram, are unchanged; this PR does **not** close the Telegram report in #140037.

## Evidence

**Transport-boundary proof, not a live Slack screenshot.** The real Slack dispatch, compositor, native task projection/reconciler and Block Kit renderer were exercised with provider transport doubles. Identical fixtures used six distinct failed commands (four exit 1, two exit 8), authored narration, two plan steps, an approval lifecycle, and then a successful/error/no-reply outcome. No retry was needed to produce the old recovered rows.

Baseline: `7932371ea5a864326078706b98975458a2310abb`.

| Observed output | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quiet native card, successful final | 6 permanent `Recovered: Bash — exit N` tasks | 0 command-failure tasks ever published |
| Quiet Block Kit card, successful final | 6 recovered lines in final card | 0 recovered command lines |
| Native/Block Kit plans and approvals | Present | Present |
| Failed final / failed run without a reply payload | Error card state | Error card state preserved |
| Detailed `toolProgress: true` | Command outcomes retained | Unchanged |
| Compact quiet draft | Transient failed-command rows | Omitted; existing cleanup and no-checklist behavior unchanged |

Representative emitted native task update, repeated under six distinct call IDs **before**:

~~~json
{"type":"task_update","id":"openclaw-attention-fail_0_39de6b49","title":"Recovered: Bash — exit 1","status":"complete"}
~~~

**After:** no command task update is emitted for those six IDs. Plan and approval updates remain, followed by the delivered final answer. Suppression happens before publication because already-published native task rows cannot be removed.

Validation:
- **404 tests passed** across Slack dispatch/projection/renderers/account configuration, core no-reply warning generation, shared quiet composition, and Telegram renderer smoke coverage.
- **30 additional disposable before/after dispatch proof scenarios** cover defaults, the preview alias, compact/card/native/fallback modes, and terminal outcomes. Regression fixtures fail against the exact baseline for the unwanted rows and pass with the candidate.
- Extension production and test typechecks passed with physically checkout-local dependencies. Changed-source format/lint, architecture/ratchet/dependency/dead-export guards, changed-page MDX checks and `git diff --check` passed across the recorded validation runs.
- Mandatory independent autoreview completed scoped-clean at the repository's default P0 threshold. No production behavior changed in subsequent mechanical test-lint corrections.

No live Slack sends or authenticated Slack UI capture were performed. A browser-generated illustration was not substituted for live UI proof. Full synthetic payload captures are retained with the task evidence; the table and excerpt above are taken from those captures. The separate existing inference that eviction can label a quiet row “Recovered” is not changed here.

Worked on by: @Solvely-Colin

title: fix(wear): keep replies bound to the captured conversation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes delayed replies and notification opens losing the conversation the user selected, including recovery after a first-load failure or an older phone's failed Talk Stop.

## User Impact

Text, dictation and model-search results stay bound to their original conversation. Refreshing after a failed notification load keeps the requested destination instead of opening the phone's unrelated active chat. A valid new-phone notification does not inherit an old phone's cleanup failure, while wrong-phone actions and stale callbacks remain rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing conversation owner captures phone, session and generation for delayed actions. Pending notification intent survives failed discovery reads, but every retry must validate the current phone before restoring action authority.

Talk cleanup records the actual phone target under its lifecycle lock. Replacement notifications may change their destination, not the cleanup target; same-phone failures and cancellation remain enforced. No persistent queue, automatic retry or new routing owner is added.

## Evidence

- Context and Stop regressions cover navigation away and back, delayed callbacks, phone changes, replacement notifications, transport failures and pending cleanup.
- Five first-load recovery tests cover failed status/session reads, wrong-phone rejection and explicit supersession. Four failed on the original behavior; all five pass with the fix.

title: fix: restore media uploads through protected egress
body:
Related: #144662

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: destinations requiring a fixed request length reject uploads through protected egress even when the client supplies the correct file size.

## User Impact

User impact: known-length uploads up to 100 MiB preserve their bytes and use the measured outgoing length after authorized secret substitution.

Buffered uploads share a 128 MiB reservation budget, including 256 KiB headroom per request, with at most 64 requests preparing or sending. Capacity exhaustion returns 503; the five-minute preparation/send deadline returns 504. Larger or unknown-length uploads retain scanned chunked streaming and can still be rejected by fixed-length-only destinations. **Listed security-owner acceptance of this operating envelope remains outstanding.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing forwarding owner collects bounded bodies, rechecks current run/destination/credential authority, and reuses the binary scanner before sending. The allocation site also directly validates a safe, nonnegative integer length within the existing 100 MiB ceiling immediately before allocating. Routing, budgets, deadlines, TLS verification, and cleanup are unchanged; no clamping, new configuration, or body-file storage is introduced.

## Evidence

- Frozen head: [d77f100320b6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d77f100320b6241eb02b0ac83b7a26e9027a824c). The private checked allocator rejects non-safe-integer, negative, or above-100 MiB lengths immediately before allocation, without changing admission, budgets, deadlines, or streaming.
- **95 functional tests pass**: authenticated CONNECT/verified TLS, binary/PNG/MP4 byte identity, measured substituted lengths, exact 100 MiB backpressure/hash, refusals, revocation, and reservation cleanup. Production/proxy-test inputs are unchanged by the final companion-plugin test expectation alignment, so this proof remains applicable. Original baseline evidence retains six framing failures before and eleven transport cases passing afterward.
- [Exact-head CI, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34730411904/attempts/2): **success**. The first attempt hit ETXTBSY launching a native compiler in an unchanged tooling fixture. One targeted job retry and its dependent CI gate passed; source, tests, timeouts, and policies were not changed for the retry.

title: fix(release): verify 2026.9.4 split publication recovery

Related: #142291

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where stable release closeout cannot verify the already-published 2026.9.4 npm and Docker artifacts after the original publisher failed during npm propagation readback. The successful npm child retained whole-job logs rather than individual step files, and the recovery verifier recognizes that archive shape only for an older frozen publisher revision.

## User Impact

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual `verifyStablePublishRecovery` entry using the live release evidence and successful [npm child](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34554632555): `no historical runner-header contract for missing step log`.

title: fix(release): publish frozen plugins with valid ClawHub categories
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the frozen OpenClaw 2026.9.4 release cannot publish 31 official plugins because ClawHub requires exactly one category. The [original publication run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34554453979) rejected those packages; Zalo separately lost authorization before submission. Core, npm plugins, Docker, and the signed release tag are already published and must stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing isolated package-manifest staging owner projects reviewed category metadata from trusted tooling onto the frozen candidate. It verifies both plugin ID and npm package name, changes only `categories`, and preserves candidate versions, package manifests, runtime files, generated channel configuration, transaction sealing, and environment approval.

The broader [taxonomy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142759) and [bundled assignments](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142760) are now on main; this branch preserves them rather than duplicating their manifest edits. For exactly the already-published `2026.9.4` package version, a reviewed `agent-runtimes` category is encoded as its existing `runtime` category. The guard requires the original candidate already to declare `runtime`. Both the deployed ClawHub contract and the frozen 9.4 installer accept that encoding. Other versions retain the current taxonomy; this is not a runtime compatibility reader.

Category validation is an unchanged move into a dependency-free package-contract leaf with existing barrel exports retained. The ReleasePlan sparse source closure and its fixture include that leaf, so native Node updater and artifact acquisition paths can load the real owner before compilation.

## User Impact

Unblocks the selected 32-package ClawHub recovery without moving the release tag, republishing npm, changing plugin runtime behavior, or modifying stored user data. The separate 58 stored uploads require owner-authenticated recovery of the existing bytes, not re-upload.

## Evidence

- 235 distinct existing/focused cases passed across updater (87), npm staging (51), ClawHub projection (11), public contract (6), ReleasePlan acquisition (55), and taxonomy (25) suites. The new compatibility pack regression failed before the repair for the intended category rejection.
- Real ACPX and Codex archives contain only the intended category change. Every non-manifest entry and package manifest matches the frozen source. The exact 9.4 installer accepts `runtime` and rejects the newer `agent-runtimes`; this is parser proof, not a claim of plugin activation.
- Earlier pinned-CLI Firecrawl and Feishu sibling comparisons remain valid, including generated channel configuration. Zalo's 24-entry archive is byte-identical to its original, SHA256 `6b3ff427af9c4220d3c7f11ea1c3c22c8f31c42ba3c441e1b8e9446f627f9800`.
- Fresh independent automated review of the complete staged delta returned no findings at its configured P0 threshold. Lead inspection also checked the actual owners, sparse closure, original candidate reader, and deployed ClawHub contract.
- All 36 selected canonical checks passed: 22 completed before an interrupted dead-export scan, then that scan and all 13 remaining lint/guard checks completed successfully. Full core and test types, script/root types, all three Knip scans, targeted lint, package/database/auth boundaries, and runtime import-cycle checks passed. The interruption (exit 143) remains recorded rather than relabeled. The ten committed file hashes match the independently reviewed bytes. A separate exact-selected-set check confirms all 32 recovery category arrays are accepted by the frozen 9.4 vocabulary; final hosted-byte comparison remains a publication gate.
- [Previous-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34562535974) remains failed at attempts 1 and 2. Attempt 1 had 80 successful jobs and 15 skipped; the failing Discord transcript lifecycle shard first timed out and then reported account-state failures. One unchanged-head failed-job diagnostic rerun was requested; GitHub reexecuted the failed reusable group. Attempt 2 again stalled at the same ordered boundary and the unchanged 300-second watchdog terminated its worker. No third retry, deadline/assertion change, or Discord repair was made. Blacksmith Testbox, ARM Testbox, Build Artifacts Testbox, and Workflow Sanity passed.
- A controlled clean Node 24.19.0 run on pre-repair main `b605e78e568b1f8de3c036ce7bf6ae97390a8047` reproduced that stall: all 14 predecessor cases passed, no lifecycle case completed, and the unchanged 300-second watchdog ended the run with exit 143 after 336.752 seconds. The sequence was `native-reasoning-subscription` → `gateway-multi-acquisition` → `transcripts-tool.discord-lifecycle.integration`. Fresh isolated state/caches and repository-owned worker generation were used, without debugger or observation preload. This demonstrates that the category repair is not necessary to cause the ordered stall; it does not prove the exact initiating loader defect or explain attempt 1’s account-state cascade. Original failure evidence is retained, the checkout was restored and hash-verified, and native landing still requires green exact-head CI.

- The follow-up fixture repair explicitly sets `agents.defaults.utilityModel` to an empty string in the Discord capture lifecycle fixture. No primary model is configured, so the real heuristic-summary path remains under test without ambient automatic inference from an earlier file’s metadata. Every lifecycle assertion, deadline, and production file is unchanged. This does not claim to repair global plugin-cache isolation.
- The original three-file order now passes **17/17 tests** on Node 24.19.0 with fresh isolated state/cache: terminal exit 0 in 39.326 seconds. The model-summary sibling suite and all **16** selected canonical checks also passed, including root test types, all three dead-export scans, script lint and targeted test lint. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the one-line fixture change returned no findings. Commit and remote bytes were hash-verified after hooks.
- [New exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34571434041) is attached to `3b3247dd66816e9199fc044031e668a1fbf93185` and remains pending. Native preparation/landing and ClawHub upload approval remain paused until their respective gates actually pass.

Against pinned main `b605e78e568b1f8de3c036ce7bf6ae97390a8047`, this is an eleven-file change: production/tooling +143/-77, tests/support +219/-2, workflow +10/-10. The category owner is moved, not duplicated. Added tooling owns the existing two-SHA projection and exact shipped-version encoding, without a new public runtime/config surface.

Release source stays `3a9d69db306cd7f081e06254cb89c4bcc14a7107`. Exact repair head: 3b3247dd66816e9199fc044031e668a1fbf93185.

### Review disposition and publication gate

The [earlier review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144615#issuecomment-5628974300) requested complete archive comparison, resolution of failed CI, and data-model compatibility evidence. The native import and sparse-closure defects were reproduced and repaired at their owner; exact-head CI is still required. No storage schema, embedding configuration, migration, or runtime code changes in this repair.

Protected publication tooling must first be landed on main. After landing, the selected 32-package hosted transaction pauses at its approval gate: compare every archive with its original, require category-only changes for the 31 repairs and byte identity for Zalo, then approve. That full hosted comparison is not yet claimed complete. The 58 stored uploads and all successful npm packages are excluded from re-upload.

title: fix(gateway): preserve defaults when plugins auto-enable
body:
Related: #143837, #144599.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway startup can silently switch compaction out of safeguard mode and discard other computed defaults when it automatically enables a plugin.

## User Impact

Prepared compaction, provider, and channel settings survive automatic plugin activation and subsequent configuration reloads. Authored configuration remains unchanged; no new settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The early startup handoff now uses the existing activation merge already used by plugin bootstrap and hot reload, rather than replacing runtime configuration with its source form. This supersedes the earlier generic merge-patch approach while preserving legacy-agent handling and secrets ordering.

The missing-model-array crash was separately fixed by #144599. This PR repairs the remaining loss of runtime defaults.

## Evidence

- All five new regression cases fail against the pre-fix startup implementation: four sparse-provider cases and a real Gateway cold-start case that observes effective compaction mode changing from `safeguard` to `default`.
- With the repair, the real Gateway test verifies published runtime defaults immediately after startup and after an actual config-file edit is hot-reloaded. It also checks that generated settings were not written into the source file.
- **197 tests passed across seven focused files**, including Gateway readiness, current catalog credentials/headers, startup/reload behavior, source immutability, activation merging, and provider validation.
- The final suite ran in an existing rootless Node **24.20.0** image with networking disabled except its own loopback namespace, read-only source/dependencies, isolated writable state/caches, and no inherited host proxy or provider credentials. The readiness and catalog-key assertions previously failing in the host environment passed unchanged here. Those two files also passed with the pre-fix startup implementation in the same isolated environment (19 tests).
- Changed-file formatting, lint, production/test types, dead-export scans, runtime import-cycle checks, and repository guards passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview: no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings; final source verification passed.

Proof uses synthetic local data and a real local Gateway. It does not claim upstream model authentication, inference, channel delivery, or host-broker integration.

Production change: +7/-2 (net +5), routing the early handoff through an existing owner rather than adding a new merge implementation.

title: fix(android): simplify setup and recover blocked permissions
body:
Related: #157409

## What Problem This Solves

Android setup shows a long permission list, and a permanently denied permission can leave users tapping a row without a way to recover.

## User Impact

Setup shows four optional choices: Notifications, Microphone, Camera, and Location. Other existing permissions stay available under **Additional features**. Users can continue without granting access. Denied requests offer the existing Android Settings recovery dialog, and rows refresh when users return.

Existing camera/location opt-in, applying choices on Continue, and Gateway reapproval remain unchanged. This deliberately covers setup and denial recovery only—not automatic first-use prompts or background permission notifications.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing setup models and Android launcher; connect its denial callback to the existing `PermissionRequester` recovery method. The earlier notification/agent-attribution system and all `SecurePrefs`, runtime, dispatcher, SMS, and protocol changes are removed from the PR.

The final diff is **6 files, +199/−27 lines**: two production files (+46/−14), two test files, one README line, and the generated source-string inventory. No new storage, migration, dependencies, or permission policy.

## Evidence

- Verified head: `b6c7081f51fb246e140532e8dddad5e327ce0ce1`.
- **164 tests passed, none failed or skipped**: `InitialOnboardingLayoutTest`, `OnboardingFlowLogicTest`, and `PermissionRequesterTest`, in Play and third-party variants. Both debug APKs build. Combined Gradle test/build wall time: **41.43 s**.
- Both new UI regressions fail on pre-PR source for the intended reasons: no Android Settings recovery after denial, and the old setup layout. The corrected tests deliver platform permission results through Android's existing dispatch path; Notifications, Camera, and Location recover, without implicitly enabling camera/location.
- Revision-scoped `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <six changed paths>` (including Kotlin lint and native schema guard), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent review: **P0–P2 scoped clean**, after the final reduction.
- CI: [CI run 36081981557](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36081981557) **passed** on the verified head, including Android Play/third-party/Wear tests, Kotlin lint, both native-access lanes, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The exact-head security/dependency gates also passed.
- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157701#issuecomment-5824929985) completed on the verified head with no actionable findings.
- Production Compose screenshots below: SDK 34, dark theme, 360×720, isolated fixture restored at the permission step. Android result callbacks and Settings intents are exercised under Robolectric; no physical-device/emulator execution is claimed.

title: fix: keep failed idle database cleanup from blocking every agent

Related: #157325. Builds on the merged same-owner cleanup recovery in #159451 and preserves the earlier #157064 contributor history.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: healthy agents lose warm database capacity and useful diagnostics when another agent’s idle database cleanup fails.

## User Impact

Healthy agents keep working while the failed owner retains its cleanup custody. Protected readiness details expose the redacted cause and the next repair step without changing startup, core-agent, drain, or update-canary readiness rules. No database schema, migration, retention, or durability change; do not delete database or lease files to repair this condition.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main already owns worker-error hydration, worker-slot failure settlement, and same-agent cleanup retries. This conflict repair preserves those implementations and the original contributor ancestry. The remaining change excludes failed cleanup custody from healthy idle capacity and publishes fresh non-blocking cleanup diagnostics through main’s current lifecycle and readiness owners.

The changed-PR CI planner also keeps process-heavy system-runtime work serial within its existing two-worker envelope, through the canonical repacking and timing owner. Full-plan defaults and selected test coverage are preserved.

The existing branch was updated with a non-force fast-forward push. The PR remains open and auto-merge is off.

title: fix(codex): stop advertising unavailable subagent tools
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex-backed agents receiving misleading subagent instructions: native collaboration tools were described as deferred OpenClaw tools, and policy-restricted turns still recommended native delegation that their request configuration disabled.

## User Impact

Subagent guidance now follows the tools and calling conventions exposed by Codex. OpenClaw still describes its actual deferred tools, preserves offered OpenClaw delegation, and retains its background-completion handoff. No permissions, model defaults, configuration schema, or runtime delegation capabilities change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex owns native collaboration discovery and invocation. Its v1 and v2 backends do not share the same exposure contract: v2 defaults to direct-only collaboration tools. OpenClaw should not prescribe one backend’s discovery convention to the other.

The prompt owner now honors the existing policy-restricted flag and limits dynamic-discovery guidance to registered deferred OpenClaw tools. Native follow-up and wait conventions remain with Codex instead of hardcoding tool names.

Reported by Vincent Koc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/b2a416d5-f434-4608-a422-f7af41bbae53)

- Three final regression cases fail against the pre-fix production modules and pass against the repair: restricted native guidance, preserved offered OpenClaw delegation, and native-versus-dynamic discovery. The original defects were captured before production edits; an independent actual request-builder probe corroborated the configuration/prompt contradiction.
- Final focused prompt and thread-lifecycle coverage: **253 tests passed across two files**. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-prompt.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; warm-run wall **16.51 seconds**; final refreshed-head runner **43.21 seconds** (Vitest 41.59 seconds, including compiler artifact preparation). - Full changed-surface gate passed on final head `0cbc79a2f33b78a11c784d25b5d7d9d6bf1a842e`, including extension production/test typechecks, lint, import-cycle and repository guards.
- Production delta: **+12/-12 (net zero)**. Tests: +40/-22.

body:
Related: #157568, #157300, #157459

## What Problem This Solves

The catalog expiry regression could miss growth inside a live source capture while its plugin-registration count stayed unchanged.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. This strengthens regression evidence for the 2026.9.7 catalog/capture investigation; it does **not** clear the affected-host soak requirement or establish a general disk/heap quota.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing real-worker expiry test now observes the worker's actual captured entry, requires a nonempty 1 MiB payload, and compares physical capture directory identities, logical bytes, and allocated bytes after each of its three renewal cycles. A shared test helper also preserves the existing explicit-refresh and retirement proof without following linked host SDK trees. No extra worker boots, expiry cycles, timers, or runtime diagnostics are added.

The merged catalog owner already shares unchanged plugin contexts across agents and grows the required plugin set. This PR does not reintroduce the older per-agent/32-registry cache proposal. The affected installation still needs its original configuration measured through startup and a settled post-ready interval, plus working Gateway and local-agent turns.

Requested by @RomneyDa. The expiry capture-identity check also follows the earlier independent validation reported by @goslingmanagment.

The repository wrapper verified source base `85bab529911a284b2d0ef2ee102877eb853ab090` and candidate tree `44b7e537f0847a31f8e0a91dbe7cb1dafba17407` before execution; that is also the committed tree in `fe9bf14872885b92375028f5a22e8c165131e589`.

- Explicit-refresh sibling: **2 captures, 2,112,520 logical bytes, 2,129,920 allocated bytes**, unchanged through refresh, then physical capture-root removal on retirement. Absolute fixture byte totals depend on embedded temporary paths; the assertion compares within one run.
- Observer negative controls detected same-count byte growth and same-byte directory replacement, and excluded a linked host tree. These validate measurement sensitivity, not reproduction of the affected-host leak.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: nested Talk relay test fixtures close database admission owned by the outer fixture and restore storage selectors before relay-owned work has settled.

## User Impact

title: fix: stop identical progress-card updates evading loop protection
body:
Closes #157491

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated unchanged progress-card updates evading enabled loop protection because every successful write returns a new revision.

## User Impact

Enabled loop protection now blocks repeated unchanged card updates while preserving genuine progress, fresh runs, and revision-based refresh acknowledgments. Detection defaults, thresholds, permissions, storage, and public tool receipts are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool records a private snapshot of the saved Markdown and plan on its raw result. The existing outcome recorder compares that snapshot instead of the display receipt. This avoids parsing receipt wording or freezing revisions that clients need to acknowledge refreshes. The snapshot lives only as long as the raw result; it adds no model-facing fields or durable state.

## Evidence

[Complete candidate fixture and sanitized receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157578#issuecomment-5822040792). Published head `7829c570984a4acaca967b9b60457b39610b528e` has the three recorded production blobs below; its metadata-only co-author correction left the code tree unchanged.

**Real Gateway + SQLite before/after proof on Blacksmith Testbox**, not only remote unit tests. [Baseline reproduction and bounded fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/157491#issuecomment-5820490345) were published and read back before production edits.

| Scenario | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Identical direct updates, one run | All 35 writes admitted; revisions 1–35, warnings but no critical block | 20 writes; attempt 21 blocked; one recovery response |
| Identical updates inside one Code Mode exec | All 35 nested writes admitted | 20 writes; remaining 15 nested calls returned actual critical loop denials |
| Model-visible terminal result | Fixture bound ended the run | Both routes delivered PROGRESS-CARD-LOOP-BLOCKED and persisted it in chat history |
| Fresh run, same session and card | Allowed, revision 35 → 36 | Allowed, revision 20 → 21, no loop rejection |
| Genuine progress | 35 distinct card updates accepted | All 35 accepted, no loop rejection |
| Unchanged-content refresh | Accepted baseline 36, saved revision 37 | Accepted baseline 21, saved revision 22 |
| Clear/recreate | Clear returned null, recreation reached revision 39 | Clear returned null, recreation reached revision 24 |

Both candidate Gateways reported confirmed-stopped with no cleanup errors. Independent read-only SQLite queries verified the final card rows. **Nested denial is not claimed to abort the entire JavaScript program:** the bounded guest continued to attempt its remaining iterations, received denial results, and the model then answered. The proof checks the actual critical rejection, model-observed denial, exactly 20 writes, and visible terminal marker separately.

Environment: provider **blacksmith-testbox**, lease **tbx_01m3abywgvda29dgqd29ac4ptz**, [run 36043809636](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36043809636), Linux x64, Node v24.19.0. Baseline driver Crabbox 0.63.0; final driver 0.66.0; Blacksmith 0.4.61. Deterministic localhost streaming provider with synthetic model mock-openai/progress-card-proof; real registered tools, wrapped admission/outcomes, Gateway RPCs, and SQLite. Config explicitly enabled loop detection and selected direct schemas; the second route enabled Code Mode. No external paid model or Codex runtime is claimed.

Pinned base: `c762b23736449d9de045d052acaba26bcd3e21e7`. Candidate was verified by the Crabbox source receiver as capsule `0c415722165705753fd54727a396a7d682c492be`, tree `d7ac75c1af71212f32b6f0b67b8a95fb7ed8d0b0`. Its recorded production Git blobs are:

- detector: `640d7bea55f69be88011b0a327088aa7a2e69da6`
- tool producer: `b2450559e217d784c9b8ded0db671e51a0fe7923`
- private outcome: `e0fb0d78be2b3b5e6144d1f5f8c7a3ac8cb01e2d`

**Validation coverage completed:** production typechecking and all 25 core-test graphs passed across the original run and the [exact-head completion run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157578#issuecomment-5824307110). The six previously missing graphs and all 12 later changed-scope checks finished with explicit completion and exit 0 on unchanged head `7829c570984a4acaca967b9b60457b39610b528e`; no source fix or new push was needed. This closes the prior interruption gap without claiming one uninterrupted full command. Exact-file formatting and code lint passed, and repository Markdown lint passed all 1,309 documents. **Hosted CI passed:** [run 36058956753, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36058956753/attempts/2) completed successfully on 2026-09-25 at approximately 02:29 UTC, on unchanged head 7829c570984a4acaca967b9b60457b39610b528e. The earlier release-priority deferral is resolved; no code change was needed. Current GitHub readback reports the PR open, conflict-free, and with no failed or pending checks. No merge or deployment has been performed.

The owned Testbox is already stopped: native status reported completed and an explicit stop returned “already stopped.” No merge or deployment has been performed.

Focused validation: **168 tests passed across four files**, including the real receipt → detector regression, existing detector cases, original public receipt tests, and the armed post-compaction guard. The original regression failed on unchanged production source (revision-dependent hashes and post-compaction failure); the candidate passes. The final new file has 9 tests; measured command wall time was 50.95s, dominated by cold shared worker transformation (97% of Vitest duration), with test bodies measured in milliseconds. It adds no Gateway boot, timers, or polling to CI. Hosted CI attempt 2 measured the nine new regression test bodies at 6, 5, 4, 3, 5, 3, 2, 2, and 2 ms: **0.032 seconds total test-body time** in [checks-node-changed-compact-large-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36058956753/job/107905902346), at 2026-09-25 02:07 UTC. Shared startup/transformation is not separately attributable to this file in that shard; the 50.95-second isolated local wall measurement above includes that overhead. This records the measured CI cost requested by the fresh ClawSweeper review completed at 2026-09-25 20:38 UTC; that review found no code or security defect.

Fresh independent autoreview completed **scoped-clean at P0/P1**. No accepted/actionable findings. Production net growth is 32 lines for the private producer/consumer fact; tests add 171 lines and docs 6. This keeps revision/refresh contracts intact without adding a generic normalization framework or a prior-card storage read.

<summary>Commands and proof limits</summary>

Remote commands, run serially inside the owned Testbox with a durable exit receipt:

- `env CI=1 OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build`
- `env OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/progress-card-loop-proof.mts candidate`

The provider is scripted, not evidence of natural model frequency or production incident cost. Post-compaction behavior is covered through the real outcome recorder and guard in focused tests, not a live context-overflow turn. No UI rendering, deployed-host, or Codex coverage is claimed. This is a behavior-only change.

</details>

title: fix(test): reap detached children in isolated Vitest runs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: isolated Vitest runs can retain a terminated detached child as a zombie when Node is the container's PID 1.

## User Impact

The local isolated test adapter now uses Podman's native init to reap adopted children, so the existing watchdog-termination assertion can observe actual process disappearance. No product Gateway or test assertion behavior changes.

The existing Podman installation must include its native init helper, normally catatonit. Missing support fails closed; the adapter does not install anything or add a new setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failing watchdog had the same PID and process-start identity before and after resume: sleeping under PID 1 became zombie under PID 1 after the lease disappeared, and remained there through the original assertion deadline. It was not a live watchdog or a reused PID.

Request Podman's existing init and require the created container's HostConfig.Init to be true before starting it. The Node entrypoint still owns invocation and cleanup. Network, credential exclusion, mounts, cancellation, process joining and snapshot-retention controls remain unchanged.

Contributor credit: requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/89b333b5-710d-4f77-9a50-98477d15cf1f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/48b107c4-b60c-4d17-8f38-fe02537fbfdc)

## Evidence

- Native unchanged watchdog case failed before the repair. A temporary observer confirmed the same start identity in sleeping → zombie states; the observer was removed from the candidate.
- With actual **podman-init PID 1 / Node PID 2**, the **original unchanged process-disappearance assertion passed in 211 ms**. Existing Podman **5.7** and catatonit **0.2.1-2build1** were used; no host installation or configuration changes.
- Full watchdog/quiescence siblings: **28/28 passed**, **45.54 s** reported Vitest wall. Adapter and managed-child lifecycle/output/termination/tree suites: **161/161 passed**, **44.28 s**; the adapter's **25 tests took 15 ms**.

- All five owned containers were confirmed absent; owned snapshots were removed. No live owned compute remained.

This is a deterministic local-runner lifecycle repair, not a relay-broker fix or full-main CI recovery. No full 113-file cohort, repeated flake-qualification matrix or real outer-interruption injection is claimed; existing interruption and retention regressions passed. Current-head CI and native landing gates remain required.

title: fix(ui): prevent palette tests racing config publication
body:
**Superseded by [25f07e880f5d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/25f07e880f5d4e05375d14f07bfb6cc416295aeb) on main; this PR was not merged.** The landed fixture observes the browser’s actual config.changed event before the existing replacement-row assertion and read-failure injection, and releases its observer in finally. It preserves the same row-retention, recovery and agent-switch coverage. The browser event path clears the old catalog before notifying the observer; the subsequent DOM assertion supplies the replacement-row barrier, so this PR’s additional request-ID fence does not establish a remaining uncovered contract.

The landed commit records native controlled reproduction, 20 full-file passes and three cohort runs with an explicitly unrelated failure in one cohort. Those are the landing owner’s recorded results, not a new replay here. Main containment was independently verified; no whole-main recovery is claimed. Our exact-head CI and durable review also passed, but a green superseded branch is not a reason to rebase a duplicate fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the real-Gateway palette test can lose its accepted model row when a late config event overlaps the simulated failed read.

## User Impact

Test-only repair; no user-visible behavior or cache policy change. Config and agent changes still retire old display facts. Existing row-count, failure-retention, recovery, navigation and agent-switch assertions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A CLI config write can publish replacement rows before its later config.changed event. Seeing the first row was therefore not enough to start rejecting browser replies: the late event could correctly retire the row while every replenishing read was rejected.

The fixture now waits for that event and a successful native main-agent read issued afterward containing the target model. It retains the existing visible-row assertion before injecting failure. No retries, sleeps, deadline increases or product changes.

Contributor credit: requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- Real Gateway/browser traces show replacement rows can arrive before config.changed. A controlled native event delay reproduces the original **0 ≠ 1** assertion; the same controlled scenario passes with the barrier, including recovery and agent-switch coverage. No synthetic event replaces the native publication.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a rejected model-probe test can skip teardown and leave bundled providers disabled for later tests in its reused worker.

**The initial hosted 100 ms overrun remains unexplained. This repairs demonstrated failure-path cleanup, not that original timing trigger.**

The fixture awaited its possibly rejected operation at the start of a finally block. Rejection skipped resource release, registry resets and direct-environment restoration. That can leave bundled-plugin discovery disabled; an explicit bundled-directory override cannot override this flag.

The same fixture now owns initialization through teardown, releases gates and joins pending work before retiring resources, and continues settled cleanup after errors. A single original error is rethrown unchanged; independent cleanup/child errors are retained together. title: docs(android): explain app and Gateway version compatibility
body:
Related: #141700

## What Problem This Solves

Android users finding an APK from an older release cannot tell whether its version must match their Gateway or whether successful pairing guarantees full feature compatibility.

## User Impact

Users can distinguish release numbers from protocol compatibility and understand the different requirements for chat/UI and device connections.

Documentation only: no runtime, release workflow, version pin, or compatibility contract changes. This does not publish a new APK or promise a supported calendar-version matrix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The APK-discovery correction in #141762 already explains selected-release availability. This follow-up adds the remaining compatibility guidance and links to the existing protocol versioning reference instead of duplicating version constants.

title: fix: delegated tasks stop crediting unrelated shared-inbox participants
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unrelated people receiving Git co-author credit when an agent delegates a new task from a long-lived shared main session.

Stacked companion to #157268, targeting `codex/delegated-git-credit`. This diff extends that PR's contributor-snapshot owner; it does not replace its implementation or take over its branch.

## User Impact

New native, ACP, and visible-session spawns from the shared main inbox carry only the existing host-verified requester profile, when one is available. They no longer copy the inbox's unrelated participant history. Ordinary task sessions still retain all recorded profile collaborators and inherited task lineage, including nested delegation.

**Scope and limits:** this prevents unrelated credit in child snapshots. Direct prompts, commits, and publications in the shared main session are not scoped by this companion, and it does not implement linked-channel Git credit. A stable transport sender ID is not a verified GitHub identity. No channel identity links, permissions, profile data, or historical Git/transcript records are changed. Structured task-specific credit opt-out is separate follow-up work; this PR does not claim that the current profile preference covers it. Existing per-profile consent and incognito handling remain with the attribution owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing delegation snapshot treated the shared main inbox like a single collaborative task. The same owner now uses canonical main-session routing (including custom main keys and global scope) to select the trusted requester instead. Requester selection is host-owned, never a model-supplied co-author list, session assignment, display name, or task-text claim. Child participant counts, access, and visibility are unchanged. title: fix: restore human credit when republishing unchanged work
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated **Publish PR** requests silently leaving human commit credit unrecognized when an existing commit contains coauthor text outside Git’s terminal trailer block.

## User Impact

Republishing unchanged work can restore Git-recognized credit for the session’s currently eligible human contributors. The repair adds a new commit with the same tree; it does not rewrite earlier commits or change who is eligible for credit. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reuse check matched text anywhere in the commit message. It now reads Git-parsed coauthor trailers from the pinned commit before calling an existing published head fully attributed. Missing recognized credit goes through the existing canonical commit composer instead.

Current new-publication ordering and squash composition already handle terminal trailers correctly and remain unchanged. Identity inheritance and consent are separate work in #157268; this change does not modify those selectors or interfaces. The companion workflow guidance is #157381.

## Evidence

**Current candidate:** `cfc1b98f6bcbdc20f7ab7fdefff08200cced17a3` contains the authorized rebase onto `c762b23736449d9de045d052acaba26bcd3e21e7` plus the consent-window correction described below. Its parent `fbea1e62521e0d25a78dc187c8870bada1c2bdbb` passed [fresh CI and required gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36044810651). **Current-head CI is green, but substantive review remains blocked on the shared post-selection consent guard.** [Run 36049663889](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36049663889) passed with 130 successful jobs, 19 skipped, and zero failures; both required `openclaw/ci-gate` instances passed. The [current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157420#issuecomment-5818710940) confirms the trailer-read correction and raises the later consent-to-push window below. This PR is **not claimed review-cleared or merge-ready**. No merge or auto-merge is enabled.

### Review correction: opt-out during trailer parsing

The [P1 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157420#issuecomment-5818710940) was reproduced with real profile identities, participant records, and the stored credit preference: opting Alice out during the new awaited Git read still published her credit on the previous candidate. Trailer parsing now completes **before** the unchanged attribution owner selects current contributors. This closes the introduced read window without copying the separate publication-wide consent guard being developed in #157268.

The new test exercises the real publication coordinator, Git commits, and a bare remote. The opted-in control credits Alice and Bob. After Alice's real preference is disabled during trailer parsing, the final pushed repair commit credits only Bob and retains the previous head as its parent. GitHub API calls remain simulated in this regression; no live profile preference was changed. The test failed before this correction and passes afterward.

### Remaining integration dependency

A temporary diagnostic moved the real preference revocation to completion of the awaited pre-push `ls-remote`, after contributor selection and before the normal action/transport guards run. On this exact head the coordinator still reported publication and the final bare-remote repair commit still carried Alice’s revoked credit. The expected Bob-only final trailer assertion failed in **9.73 s command wall**. This confirms the remaining post-selection finding rather than relying only on source inspection. The temporary test change was restored byte-for-byte to the committed version; no production change or permanent test endorses the unwanted result.

The shared consent-through-commit/push guard is already owned by Peter’s open #157268 (`090dd4a48fedfbd6e88a4d1ef1e9231c139b02e4` at verification). This focused PR must consume that owner through coordinated integration rather than duplicate its guard or alter the human-owned branch. The original trailer-read window is fixed, but the broader final-effect boundary is not claimed fixed here.

### Verification

- Fresh independent review confirmed the introduced read-window correction. Its INDEX-only old-version finding was resolved by staging the exact reviewed working-tree bytes before commit; committed blobs were verified identical. The subsequent current-head review remains blocked on the separately reproduced post-selection gap above.

- The rebased parent additionally passed **99 tests across 7 files in 180.14 s** and full required CI, including the Gateway/Telegram cases implicated in earlier failures. Those results remain parent-head evidence, not a substitute for the correction's fresh CI.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes maintainer guidance that can confuse a publishing account or copied contributor list with the human behind a task, and can report PR acknowledgments as verified Git credit.

## User Impact

This is a workflow-only correction: maintainers verify the human identity and the actual source, publication, and landed commit credit separately. It does not change runtime attribution, link profiles, or rewrite existing commits; runtime repairs are separate companion work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep contributor verification in the existing attribution reference and link it from the publication/landing workflow. The guidance distinguishes task provenance and consent from session ownership and permissions, preserves valid inherited authors, and rejects relabeling agent-generated credit lists as human requests.

It requires Git-recognized terminal trailers and actual published-author readback rather than substring presence. Historical body-only corrections and disputed sender identity must be reported with their limits.

title: fix(test): scope desktop retry requests to the explicit target
body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Superseded:** this repair was independently landed on main in [dbd7453fd2f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/dbd7453fd2ff2db7192fdbef4515404d80be7cc2). This PR was closed without merging to avoid duplicating it. The remaining independent pasted-text repair is [#157375](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157375). Evidence below describes this retained proposal, not a claim that it was merged.

The desktop failure/retry E2E test can count automatic chat discovery as an extra explicit-target retry, failing with three status RPCs where it expects two.

## User Impact

Test-only repair in one file. Production desktop behavior, target authority, timeout settings, retries, and CI coverage are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A chat can already be discovering its assigned worker when a user opens another desktop explicitly. That read-only discovery is not a retry or fallback by the explicit presenter.

The fixture holds real background discovery across the manual open/retry and checks each owner: exactly one failed initial direct-target request, exactly two direct-target reads overall, one correctly targeted observation and one connection. It accounts for the **complete parameterized status journal**, so unexpected targets or a third direct-target read still fail. The original no-observation/error, no-picker/fallback, and exact retry ordering assertions remain. Successful status responses are restricted to the requested target.

Contributor credit: requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/89b333b5-710d-4f77-9a50-98477d15cf1f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a6a286d2-db40-45b2-93f6-8fd4c516c20c)

## Evidence

- Original required failure: [CI 36013302644, E2E job 107680345538](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36013302644/job/107680345538), expected total status count **2**, received **3**.
- First replay used the original **79 executed files / 370 tests**, three workers, Node **24.19.0**, and Chromium **153.0.8010.12 / v1243** on the configured Blacksmith Testbox. All passed. This ordinary non-reproduction is **not claimed as fix evidence**.
- Controlled real-browser ordering held actual discovery while the explicit target failed and retried. With the original global assertion intact, it failed with the same 3-versus-2 result. Captured RPC parameters were **other-worker → worker-desktop-1 → worker-desktop-1**.
- Under that same ordering, the repaired case passed in **1.4 s**. Complete desktop file: **22/22 passed**, **47.39 s Vitest wall** (**104.997 s provider command including source/dependency preparation**).
- Repaired original executed cohort: **79/79 files, 370/370 tests passed**, no skips; **501.83 s Vitest wall**, **549.034 s provider command**. Full source-capsule/tree bindings were checked before each invocation. The task-owned Testbox was stopped and its completed state verified.
- Qualification preceded extraction from the combined repair branch. This one-file PR retains byte-identical desktop, production UI, and E2E inputs; unrelated release and pasted-text test-fixture edits are separate. Fresh exact-head CI remains required.
- Fresh independent P2 review found no actionable issues. All selected repository type, lint, formatting, ratchet and dead-export checks passed for these exact bytes.

Hosted failure telemetry did not retain RPC parameters, so its precise third caller remains unknown. The controlled experiment demonstrates the fixture’s global-count defect, not an unrelated production defect. The original compressed pre-shard inventory was damaged in the supplied log; the replay reconstructed all 79 executed paths without missing mappings rather than claiming identical original shard packing.

Local loopback proxy policy and remote source-privacy exclusions were preserved. Remote proof resumed only after incorporating the independently landed tracked-scratch cleanup in #157308. Provider portal-sync warnings did not alter recorded command/test exit status.

title: fix(ci): stop pasted-text handoff tests racing excerpt loading
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the pasted-text handoff test can fail before a remounted attachment's excerpt finishes loading, as seen in [the failing UI shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36000846700/job/107638152522).

## User Impact

Test-only repair; no user-visible behavior changes. Production behavior, timeouts, retries, assertions, and CI coverage are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture's one-second DOM poll raced the real body read, lazy parser import, and Lit update. A call-through spy now observes and awaits that work, then restores itself in `finally`. The existing excerpt, handoff identity, draft restoration, attachment removal, and payload-release assertions remain intact.

The pasted-text repair remains unchanged. A separate one-line lifecycle fixture cleanup now records the spawned child’s arguments and PID before honoring an already-present release marker. This prevents late startup from becoming invisible to the fixture and causing repeated build/launcher work. No release-fixture, iOS, Desktop E2E, or production change is included.

Contributor credit: requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc; lifecycle fixture follow-up by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/89b333b5-710d-4f77-9a50-98477d15cf1f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/ed15791e-349d-4469-9911-2a67434e984d)

## Evidence

- Controlled prior evaluation with a 1,500 ms real-parser delay: the original excerpt assertion failed at 1,125 ms; the repaired fixture passed at 1,682 ms. Ordinary original-code replays passed and are not fix evidence. Hosted logs do not identify the precise delayed async stage; this does not establish a production defect.
- Fresh isolated-worktree full-file run on Node 26.8.2 and the incorporated main context: **364/364 tests passed**, **9.90 s** wall time with one worker; the repaired case took **68 ms**. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts --project unit src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Fresh two-file `check-changed` run against incorporated main `9ccfc7d1bea21e34da48edbd54afd2e1be57db40`: **all selected checks passed**, including `ui-chat` types, targeted lint (zero warnings/errors), format, graph boundaries, i18n, ratchets, and dead-export scans.
- Fresh independent review: **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. `git diff --check` passed. The repair's stable patch ID matches the previously qualified two-file patch exactly.
- Historical qualification retained, not relabeled as new-head CI: 20/20 full-file runs (361 tests each), 3/3 original-inventory Bun 1.4.3 UI shards (500 files / 8,323 tests each), and 100 sibling tests passed. On incorporated main, the prior broader UI replay passed 464 tests across seven files.
- All three unit-UI shards passed in [CI run 36013302644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36013302644) on the earlier combined candidate. That overall run failed an unrelated Desktop E2E case handled separately. On this PR’s original head, all nine browser jobs and the selected UI groups passed; overall [CI run 36022803218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36022803218) failed the lifecycle case described below. Final exact-head [CI 36029391881, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36029391881) passed. The enforced `openclaw/ci-gate` (integration 15368) passed, and @steipete’s existing auto-merge landed head `a2f239f3c49a030367aa4f21e9e7e2de02cb5c51` as [`9f9b4de9517d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f9b4de9517d52d906d6afede7b585209c1723ea) at 17:01:52 UTC. Main containment and both human co-author trailers were verified.

### Lifecycle fixture follow-up

- The original CI failure missed the child PID readiness deadline and then hit the managed command deadline. The initial readiness delay did **not** reproduce in normal or two-core original-order replays and remains unexplained; this repair does not claim to eliminate that scheduling delay.
- Controlled release-present proof showed that the original fixture exited before recording the child PID, repeated build/launcher work three times, and took 6.699 s. Moving the existing release check after the two synchronous writes recorded the child, reduced builds/launchers to one, and took 3.228 s. Neither controlled run reproduced the original managed-command timeout.
- The unchanged normal signal scenario passed with the repaired fixture: **1/1 selected case**, **8.22 s** Vitest / **9.982 s** wrapper on Node 24.19.0. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --configLoader runner --maxWorkers=1 test/scripts/run-node-lifecycle.test.ts -t 'stops gateway watch when a compile-cache respawn child dies from a signal'`.

Independent scoped review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; formatting and diff checks passed. The original CI failure and its unexplained initial delay remain recorded rather than treated as fixed by a passing replay.

No screenshots are needed: this changes only test synchronization, not visual appearance. Local split qualification did not repeat full E2E or unrelated platform suites; final exact-head hosted CI completed its selected lanes successfully.

title: fix(android): keep translated Wear voice actions readable

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #157355

Fixes: translated Voice actions are truncated or pushed outside a small round watch display, particularly with larger text. A fixed arrangement can also overlap the microphone-recovery message and Talk control.

## User Impact

Complete Voice labels remain readable without reducing the selected font size. The familiar compact layout stays when content fits; otherwise, scrollable controls keep Talk and current feedback first and make Thread, Dictate, and Live fully reachable. Existing gestures and action gating remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uncapping text alone fixed Japanese but still pushed Russian text into the physical edge. The Voice owner now measures the actual localized glyphs and status before choosing compact or scrollable placement. Both layouts share the same action rendering and callbacks. Prepared colors come from the existing page owner. Selecting an action immediately reveals the primary control and its explanation as one group instead of waiting for a later content update. A real four-line Russian recovery message previously extended beyond the display; the grouped owner keeps it visible without another scroll.

Head: `0c7c3126ad0687857d0ad0277238d3e19bfda30f`. Rebased onto `main` after the black-background and splash fixes landed. Conflict resolution preserves `VoicePage`'s prepared canvas colors across the extracted controls; the layout patch remains independently scoped.

The Russian case exposed physical-circle clipping; the final locale regressions were also checked against original production. The one-line restriction is present in the public `v2026.9.4` source.

Scrollable targets are brought into view before testing, not exempted from checks.

body:

## User Impact

Developers can build and pack workspace packages through the bounded declaration producer. Public entries, supported Node engines, dependency externalization and runtime environment behavior are preserved. No configuration option or data migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep test-only ambient augmentation out of production declaration roots while explicitly retaining it in test/editor graphs. All ten standalone package scripts now consume the existing canonical entry/declaration and artifact-ownership contracts instead of a separate whole-project DTS path. The adapter preserves library-specific dependency and environment behavior rather than inheriting application folding. SDK output ownership and ACP's existing nonexported entry are retained, and wrapped unjoined-work errors keep their resource ownership.

Requested by Peter Steinberger during release-verification repair.

## Worked on by

- @steipete

The bounded payload returned **exit 0** and recorded `CUTOVER_ALL_PASS` at 14:01:21 UTC.

| Original complete-cutover check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| All ten real standalone builds and public-output checks | Pass |
| Gateway-client runtime environment behavior and normalization-core external dependencies | Pass |
| Changed canonical package phase | Pass, 2m16s |
| SDK packed external-consumer type/runtime case | Pass, 51.324s |

| Script and root-test type graphs | Pass |
| Targeted changed script/config/test lint | Pass, zero warnings/errors |

Before/after evidence covers the unrelated ambient root and raw standalone declaration traversal. Controlled regressions for dependency bundling, production environment folding and wrapped unjoined-work handling failed before their respective corrections and passed afterward. Production emit graphs exclude the shim; test/editor graphs retain it. Independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. No raw standalone DTS bypass remains among the ten affected package scripts.

title: fix(sqlite): retain healthy handles after automatic rollback
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes otherwise usable SQLite connections being closed after SQLite automatically rolls back a failed outer transaction, which can invalidate retained read admission during fallback recovery.

## User Impact

A failed write is still reported without replay, but subsequent operations can reuse the same healthy database connection. Nested rollback failures and errors after commit starts still fence the handle. No schema, persistence contract, corruption policy, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before commit begins, an open handle with no active transaction means cleanup has no transaction left to roll back. Discard its staged state/publications rather than treating the redundant ROLLBACK error as a broken connection. Track entry into commit processing separately so a durable commit followed by an owner failure cannot take that recovery path.

Requested by Peter Steinberger during release-regression verification.

## Worked on by

- @steipete

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4175b6a2-40ee-4895-a5e5-3d5f66b2f6b0)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/18d3991b-954a-4777-895d-2e1ced236b75)

title: fix: preserve suspended Gateway installation handoffs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Gateway restarting itself during a host-controlled installation replacement, invalidating the suspension that owns the update handoff.

## User Impact

Installation changes made while the Gateway is suspended stay under the host operation’s control. Rollback does not leave a replacement verdict sampled during the suspended operation. Explicit stop and restart requests keep their existing behavior.

This protection applies only when the running Gateway already contains the fix. Installing new files cannot patch an older resident process or retire a recovery journal retained by an external update controller. This PR does not deploy or recover an existing installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installation watcher now consults the existing suspension admission owner before reading or recording a replacement and discards reads spanning any suspension transition, including suspend/resume before the read completes. Missing runtime chunks still report `STALE_INSTALL` without initiating a competing restart. The installation owner invalidates any previously latched replacement when suspension starts. After a managed update helper settles, its callback accepts only the exact current fact; the existing maintenance tick rereads after resume. This also prevents rollback from reviving an older deferred replacement verdict.

The competing watcher path originated in #153078. No new restart owner, configuration, timer, schema, or protocol is introduced.

## Evidence

- Eight new regression cases failed before their respective repairs. All 17 watcher cases now pass, including all suspension phases, asynchronous rollback, helper settlement, callback retirement, and missing chunks.

title: fix: recover uncertain auto-merge requests on the same PR
body:
Related: #156743

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a network failure during auto-merge submission can leave the native PR workflow unable to retry or cancel, stranding the original pull request.

## User Impact

Maintainers can recover on the same PR without deleting the uncertain attempt record or closing and replacing the PR. Recovery requires explicit operator action and preserves normal review, identity, and CI gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

An uncertain auto request is neither a rejection nor a confirmed active request. The existing retry and cancellation paths correctly refuse to guess, but offered no way to make progress.

The new path records and confirms a GitHub draft barrier, keeps the PR unmergeable during repair and exact-head verification, then records a replacement-bound readiness transition. Only a separate explicit recovery can request an immediate merge. Lost responses are reconciled without repeating mutations.

Draft is a no-merge barrier, **not** proof of historical non-execution or a request-generation fence. Because readiness has no atomic expected-head parameter, release now additionally requires an existing, exact-pattern, administrator-enforced read-only lock on the head branch. Force pushes, deletion, and fork syncing must be disabled. The native owner verifies and retains the effective rule identity through readiness and settlement; it never creates, relaxes, removes protection, or deletes the protected branch. A repository administrator owns the narrowly scoped lock setup and restoration—no additional bot privileges are requested.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original refusal through the native Git/process-lock fixture, then exercised suspension, retained capture/provenance, replacement release, explicit immediate recovery, lost replies, and concurrent merges.
- Seven-suite run: 421 passed; one outdated CLI-forwarding assertion was corrected. Affected-suite rerun: 269 passed (98.44 seconds runner wall). Final schema/concurrent-merge cases: 3 passed (23.94 seconds runner wall). The original seven-suite runner took 200.99 seconds.

- Independent review exposed an environment-variable bypass in standalone verification. Replaced it with a strict internal `recoveryMode` contract; the public CLI always selects ordinary verification. Poisoned-environment regression failed before the correction and passes afterward. Final affected verification/recovery suites: 86 passed.
- Cold-wrapper testing exposed four missing transitive source entries in the existing inventory at the base revision. Added only those dependencies; main-refresh and eager-import-closure suites now pass all 90 tests (186.79 seconds runner wall).
- Second independent P0–P2 review is clean, including the strict verification-option correction and full lifecycle sources.

Fresh API reads confirmed each state with the same head and no auto-merge request. The draft event intentionally superseded the first CI start; the final ready state owns the landing run. No auto-merge mutation or original-PR mutation was used for this proof. Native interrupted/lost-response behavior remains covered by the isolated fixtures, not a fabricated live failure.

Repository, ref, head, writer permission, rule identity/pattern and lock flags are bound; an independent canonical Git-ref read follows. Null, forbidden, partial-error, wrong identity, changed-rule and head-drift responses fail closed.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

The V1 Decision data contract cannot preserve native answers such as abstention, fractional scores, sorting, tags, per-question errors and reported accounting.

## User Impact

The existing Decision SDK gains versioned V2 types, bounded validators and explicit lossless codecs. Boolean answers remain distinct from probabilities, and conversion refuses data loss instead of inventing or normalizing answers. The callable V1 runtime remains unchanged; V2 execution follows in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157225.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared finite-JSON validation keeps both contracts consistent. V2 preserves optional provider facts and explicit JSON content while rejecting invalid or unbounded data. Downgrading returns `undefined` when V1 cannot represent the result faithfully.

This continues the original contributor branch. Its Auth parent landed through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156799, and GitHub retargeted this PR to `main`. Requirements contributed by Vincent Koc and Peter Steinberger. The previously approved SDK allowance is +14 exports / +6 callable exports for this data layer; the following runtime layer uses the remaining four type exports. No new SDK subpath, production configuration or model default is introduced.

## Evidence

- 102 focused tests passed across seven files, covering V1/V2 validation, public SDK exports, conversion refusal and canonical model capability metadata.
- Focused production/test types and typed lint passed. Canonical SDK checks at signed head `7a399a7a802e2319ff4a694cea18adcb06c4617d` pass at 155 public entrypoints, 3,788 exports and 2,205 callable exports, with no unauthorized removals or budget overrides.

The export-budget merge retains both the Decision allowance and the parent allowances; 25 focused V1/V2 validation and compatibility tests, normal hooks and whitespace checks pass.
