title: fix(ui): keep collaborator drafts visible during typing pauses
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes collaborator draft bubbles disappearing after a 2.5-second typing pause, which removes and reinserts a transcript row as the person thinks and resumes typing.

## User Impact

Normal pauses keep the unsent message visible in the same bubble, labeled **Paused · not sent**. Sending, clearing or blurring the composer, leaving the session, and reconnecting still clear previews. Abandoned previews expire after two minutes without an edit, including when a browser suspends the timer. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate the short typing-activity timeout from the lifetime of an already visible draft. Paused previews keep their keyed DOM node and geometry, stop the caret animation, and leave the active-typing accessibility announcement. Presence updates retire departed profile viewers without confusing another agent's global session or an unqualified identity.

Closes #157003

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes desktop sidebar scrollbar drags being intercepted as sidebar resizing, leaving the list stationary and showing the resize cursor.

## User Impact

Users can drag the sidebar scrollbar up and down independently of resizing the sidebar. Mouse and keyboard resizing remain available; mobile drawers and settings takeover keep their existing layout. No configuration or migration required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The navigation handle overlapped the sidebar's scroll area, and the shared divider added an invisible 4px hit area beyond each edge. Keep the shared target inside its allocated track and reserve the existing 6px navigation handle width. This also prevents shared splitters from reaching into neighboring panes. title: fix(ci): avoid unrelated Node shards for native inventory changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an Android change that updates the native string inventory causes PR CI to treat that inventory as unowned and run the unrelated full Node test matrix. This blocked [#143220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143220) in [its exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35948134222).

## User Impact

No app runtime changes. Native-app contributors get the relevant inventory-reader tests instead of unrelated Node shards; unresolved owners still fall back. The remaining maintenance fixture now waits for an observed background start or terminal settlement rather than a 1-second wall-clock poll; the analogous SIGTERM fixture was independently repaired on current main in [`441c3df8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/441c3df8b7e2f6316ede9e6f6f75f16abaadd068).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android and Apple i18n tests read `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` by filename, so the import graph cannot find them. Register both as complete policy-watch owners; retain deferred tooling tests only when that specific watch declares complete ownership of the changed path, not merely because any product watch matches. The existing native i18n and Android checks remain selected. The first exact-head CI also exposed a background-maintenance polling race on main. The local harness fixture now uses its recorded start event and session settlement as proof, without relaxing assertions or timing budgets. A concurrent upstream fix already owns the stronger SIGTERM fixture, so the merge with current main retains that file verbatim instead of publishing our redundant version.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, replaying #143220's exact nine changed paths returned `unresolved changed-path owner: apps/.i18n/native-source.json` and a broad Node fallback. The new regression test failed on the original source and passed after the owner repair (1 passed, 278 skipped) on base `fcb8c0a23281`.
- The same test checks that both inventory readers are selected once, an unknown native inventory path still falls back, and absence of the Android native check still falls back.
- ClawSweeper's P2 negative control failed before the exemption was narrowed: a product-only `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.test.ts` edit pulled in the unrelated release-only tsgo test. The same one-worker case then passed (4.52 s test, 7.38 s shard). The mixed Android case still passed (34.26 s test, 37.12 s shard). These are measured local wall times, not claimed per-file CI times.
- Three targeted Android/Apple inventory-reader cases passed; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` found 4,038 entries without drift. Script and test typing, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks are verified locally.
- The first [exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35953273250) failed in a background-maintenance `vi.waitFor` on the original main code (the failing shard was 274.97 s for 38 files / 667 tests; no individual CI duration is inferred from it). On unchanged main under two CPUs/two workers, a sibling maintenance test failed the same 1-second polling assumption; its event-based replacement then passed with its contending neighbor, 24/24. Our independently prepared SIGTERM variant passed with neighboring SQLite tests (31/31) on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35953664195), but was dropped from the final diff in favor of the broader upstream `441c3df8` repair (which reports a same-order 447-test shard). The combined tree then passed [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35956517754).
- A separate foreground-disposal `<50 ms` assertion measured 61.8 ms in an earlier constrained replay; this PR did not widen that limit or change the fixture. After the CI owner fix landed, [#143220’s fresh CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35958323757) passed: the Android inventory reader ran 35/35 tests and the Apple reader 19/19 in small Node shards, without the former large shards. `steipete` was requested as the CI owner reviewer. ClawSweeper's optional per-file CI seconds cannot be reported from aggregate shard logs; local single-worker timings are given above.

title: fix: complete session archiving after the agent finishes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: asking an agent to archive its current session can return “scheduled” but leave the session unarchived after the run finishes.

## User Impact

A deferred self-archive completes after admitted work settles, without another command. Existing access revocation, busy-session checks, and replacement-session protection remain enforced. No schema, configuration, or restart-durability contract changes are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup callback retained the finished request’s authority check, so its later Gateway mutation failed. Transfer the accepted archive to the existing continuation-authority owner instead; it retains the original source restrictions until settlement and releases them afterward.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the built-in session tool, real in-process Gateway router, and isolated SQLite storage. Before the fix, the request-closure case failed with “Gateway caller authority is no longer active.”; after the fix it commits and broadcasts the archive.

- Fresh independent autoreview through P2: no actionable findings.

title: fix: stop GitHub links opening in the read-only reader
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub links open in a separate, incomplete read-only reader instead of following the existing Browser panel route.

## User Impact

GitHub links now behave like other external links: native Mac tabs in the macOS app, or real Agent browser tabs when **Open links in Control UI browser** is enabled. Otherwise they retain normal external navigation. The Browser panel displays the actual GitHub website.

The bundled `github` preview/reader plugin is removed, not disabled. Existing `github` plugin configuration produces retirement warnings rather than blocking startup; `openclaw doctor --fix` removes stale references. GitHub credentials, managed identities, publishing, repository access, and session PR status remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the plugin registration, reader/preview/image RPC implementations, caches, GitHub-only hover enrichment, and obsolete tests/docs. The surviving GitHub transport moves to its core consumers without changing credential selection or network policy. No new preview implementation or routing-priority workaround is introduced.

The shipped generic third-party link-reader SDK remains supported. The old `controlUi.githubPreview` method retains only a nonretryable removed-feature response to preserve its frozen protocol position; it performs no credential lookup or network request. Most of this diff deletes the retired feature and its tests.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway captures click https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155192 from the same synthetic chat at 1600 × 1000, with the same Browser preference and `plugins.allow: ["github", "browser"]` configuration. Before uses base `c6b21f6f086a8f3c16bbd37eb143906c9035a09e`; after uses the candidate build. No mock Gateway, fake native bridge, or composed HTML is used.

After: the click invokes `browser.request` (`/tabs/open`, `/screencast`, `/act`) and shows the actual GitHub website; no retired reader RPC is requested.

The attached after image is a real, inspected Gateway screencast captured by the diagnostic screenshot after a harness readiness assertion incorrectly queried across a shadow root and timed out. The image shows the settled GitHub page, and the request log confirms the real Browser route. That harness assertion was corrected. title: improve(android): show tool outcomes in collapsed work

These describe individual tools, not a failure verdict for the whole answer. Final answers, attachments, live work, and existing tool grouping stay unchanged. No Gateway, protocol, configuration, or storage changes. ## Why This Change Was Made Reuse the existing prepared-work projection instead of adding another activity owner. Counts use current prepared outcomes, respect hidden/suppressed activity, and keep invocation identities scoped to their run. Older raw error flags do not override a newer prepared outcome. ## Evidence - **Landed via squash:** [2701a4929621fc80c158f5ee3c91ec2597c2b8b1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2701a4929621fc80c158f5ee3c91ec2597c2b8b1), September 24, 2026 at 14:30 UTC. title: fix(ios): keep agent narration visible during runs
body:
Related: #156926 (merged web inline narration and top-aligned avatars). Builds on the completed-work disclosure from #148002. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes missing native chat narration during active runs and reconnects, and keeps narration, tool activity, and the answer together instead of presenting every update as a separate response. ## User Impact On iPhone, iPad, and native macOS chat, correlated work appears in one response group. iOS shows one top-aligned agent avatar. Completed work remains expandable above the final answer; individual message actions remain available through context menus. Search keeps individual rows addressable, and overlapping runs never borrow another input's ownership. No Gateway, protocol, dependency, configuration, or storage-schema changes. Current main's scrolling, iPad reading column, streaming rendering, and history-invalidation behavior are preserved. ## Why This Change Was Made Use one transient run/item-owned narration projection and the existing message renderer. Canonical history takes over matching segments; a current, explicitly idle snapshot retires unsaved narration only after pending final output is reconciled. The presentation owner groups known runs, keeps input boundaries separate, and resolves tool results across intervening narration within the same turn/run. Unknown ownership stays separate. The response frame uses the same explicit accessibility shape as the existing message containers, so completed-work disclosures and message actions remain inside its accessible bounds. ## Evidence **Updated and green on `217fd2c5ddfce982a4a4280179168cbe500bd3c7`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36289362408) passed all 20 jobs, including the required CI gate. Merged to `main` as [`b5f3444b442`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b5f3444b442c38b9b9018b421b1c63872bdb43ab).** - Native regression reproduction: the original grouping implementation fails tool-result reconciliation, input-boundary, and unsaved-narration scenarios in [the original RED run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36277755609). [The overlap RED run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36286823225) also reproduced wrong-input ownership and guessed ownership across all four overlap variants; the seven-test suite finished in 0.012s with 24 expected issues. An initial run failed to compile a Swift Testing macro assertion; that test syntax was corrected before claiming reproduction. - [78 tests across five focused native suites passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36289391853) on `217fd2c5ddfce982a4a4280179168cbe500bd3c7`: grouping, transport replay, completed-work disclosure, transcript rows, and session actions. Suite execution 3.247s; full build/test command 271.40s. The four-case overlap regression passed in 0.081s; current main’s hosted streaming regression also passed. Native SwiftFormat checked all 21 changed Swift files and canonical iOS production SwiftLint passed. - [Native Mac interaction proof passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36289391886): 1/1 XCTest, 83.922s. Full window: one send, ordered narration/tool work, tool expand/re-collapse, terminate/relaunch, recovery, completion, and work expand/re-collapse. Quick Chat: active/completed history replay and work disclosure interaction; not a separate Quick Chat send-path test. All 10 captured states inspected. - [Current-head iPhone and iPad interaction proof passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36289391852): 1/1 XCTest on each simulator, with no failures or skips. Active grouping, one top-aligned avatar, reconnect, completion, and completed-work disclosure interaction verified. Inspected before/after images delivered in the originating chat and embedded below. This addresses the latest ClawSweeper mobile-proof concern and Rank-up move. - Shared Apple package CI passed all 1,817 tests across 144 suites (34.882s). - [Pre-fix native Mac accessibility regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36288843438): the visible completed-work disclosure fell outside its response container’s accessibility frame and was not hittable. The owner repair adds the same explicit accessibility shape used by existing message containers. All original disclosure interaction assertions remain enabled. - `git diff --check` and SwiftFormat checks pass. The local changed-gate classifier could not load because this isolated worktree has no dependencies; hosted checks own the full gates. - Fresh integrated-candidate autoreview: complete production candidate scoped-clean P0–P2; test-only cleanup and the owner-level accessibility repair independently scoped-clean P0–P2. - Production Swift: +580/−165 (net +415); tests: +515/−5 (net +510); docs: net 0. Growth adds the requested shared response-grouping capability and transient run/item narration; existing rendering/disclosure is reused, and the old view-local tool merger and redundant message copies are removed. No parallel durable transcript. The native captures use real applications and normal UI interaction against a synthetic loopback Gateway. The unchanged model-choice warning comes from the fixture omitting the model catalogue; the displayed 13-second work duration is fixture data, not a timing measurement. They are not physical-device, live-provider, release-package, or signing/TCC proof. Baseline screenshots use the previously published narration candidate; refreshed screenshots demonstrate the added grouping and integrated current-main behavior. ### Mac — active response Before ![Before: Mac narration and tool activity occupy separate rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85b2c393-fa96-418d-b5ed-294fa4ae7ede) After ![After: Mac tool activity appears between its surrounding narration segments](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3c93f5c-c8c8-48e2-8ee9-4c2d7586f5d4) ### iPhone — active response | Before | After | | :---: | :---: | | | |
iPhone — completed work collapsed
### iPad — active response Before ![Before: separate iPad narration bubbles and avatars](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc77e402-4d87-4b9b-a634-afbb7e05d405) After ![After: one iPad response group in the reading-column layout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b38d585-3412-4c8f-8d48-e19849fe03d2)
Mac completed work — full window and Quick Chat Full window: expanded work retains the final reply. ![Mac completed response with work expanded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4f77450-cf6a-4386-bfbb-68c0c4abeb28) Quick Chat: completed-history replay with work expanded; its existing display options hide tool activity. ![Quick Chat completed response with work expanded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/749fa0a8-c446-4e42-8633-8e705ad5f643)
### Known independent follow-ups - Simulator preparation: one earlier iPad CI job exhausted SimSlim’s documented 10-minute cold-reconfiguration deadline before tests began; the successful sibling iPhone preparation took 329s. This PR does not claim to repair automatic window restoration. - The existing attachment-only iOS test helper can observe fixture readiness before the connected label renders. title: feat(ios): show latest commentary while agents work
body:
Related: #156330; iOS counterpart to #156340.

## What Problem This Solves

iPhone and iPad chat show only generic working activity even when the agent has completed commentary about its current work.

## User Impact

The native working bubble shows the active run's latest completed commentary, replacing the generic rotating phrase. Earlier notes remain in the transcript, and the status clears at settlement. Runs without commentary keep their existing indicator. macOS Quick Chat remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared native chat view model accepts only completed preamble items owned by its selected run, while history can restore explicitly phase-tagged commentary after reconnect. The iOS presentation promotes just the selected item from the displayed transcript, without changing canonical messages, and preserves final-answer blocks in mixed envelopes. Unphased segments need a matching completed item ID **and** text, so an answer segment cannot be mistaken for commentary.

## Evidence

- Independent AutoReview on the final candidate: scoped-clean at P0/P1. Two earlier P1 findings about unphased final-answer segments were corrected before commit.
- New focused Swift regressions cover active-run item selection, duplicate sequence rejection, terminal clearing, history recovery, mixed final blocks, Markdown flattening, and unphased answer preservation. Their wall time is **unmeasured**: this Linux host has no Swift, Xcode, simulator, or connected iOS/macOS device. The 11 JSON message fixtures decode and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Proof still required before readiness/landing:** run focused OpenClawKit Swift tests and the iOS typography test on a Mac; capture inspected, sanitized actual before/after iOS app screenshots on a real iPhone if available (simulator otherwise), attach them in the originating chat and embed them here. Video is optional. No device capture is claimed; the connected nodes at implementation time were Linux-only. CI and native review/prepare gates remain pending.

Contributor credit: implementation requested by Hamed; co-authored with @IWhatsskill. Control UI prior art: @vincentkoc.

title: feat: optionally route active-turn messages automatically in Control UI
body:
## What Problem This Solves

During an active Control UI turn, users should be able to opt into routing refinements to the current task without manually classifying every new message.

## User Impact

User impact: a separate **Auto** switch beneath Fast mode uses the configured Decision model to advise steering versus follow-up, while explicit manual choices and the original message remain intact.

Auto and Decision assistance are off by default. Auto additionally requires its enabled plugin, conversation access, and an effective owning-agent Decision model. Global/plugin/hook disable now hides the control without clearing its browser preference or manual baseline. Existing stored outboxes and transcripts do not acquire Auto intent retroactively. No particular provider is required; no generic completion fallback or new Lab is introduced.

**Draft / remaining gates:** the separate public **input_route** contract and its **three type exports are not approved** by the common Decision SDK's +18 exports/+6 callables approval. The original surface allowance is retained (4,580 actual versus 4,577 allowed). The joined deterministic-provider boundary proof now passes; live-provider quality and newer common-core composition are not established. Cross-stack composition needs a current-main-compatible common artifact; **2ca2fe636d54** has 26 common-owned conflicts with **f510aa6306bc**. The local startup-size check remains red; no budget or isolation guard was weakened. No merge, deployment, production configuration change, or live-provider-charge authorization is implied.

## Why This Change Was Made

An optional bundled adviser uses the first-class Decision SDK. The Gateway retains eligibility, live authority, source order, the exact captured target, original-input custody, and delivery. One 500 ms budget covers optional preparation and advice. Abstention/unavailability preserves the admitted baseline; advice does not prove consumption and never retargets a successor run.

This update integrates main **f510aa6306bc** without dropping its asynchronous caller/injection lifecycle. It fixes cancellation during caller admission through the existing canonical abort receipt owner. Fresh review's two P2 findings are also repaired: ordinary Auto Retry renews an ID only after proven no custody, and inherited server Steer is no longer converted into an explicit browser override.

The [central Decision-powered feature index](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bfec118501396f10e0ce7170d947c2fd141e3613/docs/concepts/decision-powered-features.md) documents actual opt-ins, evidence transfer, and fallbacks. Auto's preference stays in main's existing compact settings owner; the obsolete parallel helper was removed.

## Evidence

- **Joined real-Gateway boundary proof passed at bfec1185013.** Actual UI → Gateway → bundled adviser → Decision SDK → native consumption, with deterministic model providers only. Exact input/transcript ID promotion, pending-custody retirement, canonical target, correction observed by the still-active runtime, and final UI outcome all passed. [Source-bound receipt and retained attempt history](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156932#issuecomment-5842340146). Delegated run exit **0**, 3m12.425s command / 3m16.920s total; owned Testbox stopped. This is not live-provider accuracy/quality evidence.
- **228 regressions / 8 files passed** across actual registered chat-send routing/custody, reply registry, transcript provenance, UI eligibility, durable intent, and preferences. Local run: 67.99 s wall. The two additional review defects were independently red before repair; all **28 focused send-overlay cases then passed** in 2.20 s.
- Literal pre-Auto v4 outbox bytes restore unchanged, retain sender/text/run ID/mode, and retry without inferred Auto. Serialized old transcript rows retain legitimate provenance and cannot gain forged Auto/steer evidence.
- **Four real-Chromium keyboard/control cases passed**; Fast/reasoning behavior and the canonical shuffle shape remain intact. No duplicate shuffle screenshots were published.
- Actual UI/runtime-config checks passed for global plugin disable, Auto entry disable, and conversation-access disable: hidden control, retained preference, and restoration on re-enable; inherited policy stays unset on the send envelope.
- The earlier mock-Gateway GUI flow passed on **Blacksmith Testbox tbx_01m3dhzcmdb63d3taqvfjver9w**; [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36205165026), 17.24 s suite, 3m1s complete delegated run, exit 0, owned box stopped. This is not joined routing proof.
- Core/UI production type checks passed. Scoped eight-graph type/lint/dead-export/i18n checks passed before the final review fixups; final fixups have focused lint/test proof. Line-cap and exact shrink-only assertion checks pass. Documentation links: 14,584 checked, zero broken; config hash generated canonically.
- Current-main review identified two actionable P2s; both now have red/green regression evidence. Final production-diff recheck was **scoped-clean through P2**. Subsequent changes were the canonically generated Workboard asset pointer and manual-fixture corrections, culminating in the passing joined run.

### Visual evidence

[New disabled-plugin Before/After](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156932#issuecomment-5841972019): inspected actual UI with synthetic Gateway data, same configuration and layout, pre-fix predicate versus repaired predicate. Fast and reasoning remain available. This demonstrates availability, not a deployed or joined backend.

[Existing shuffle-icon evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156932#issuecomment-5818523453) remains valid and was not repeated.

### Explicit remaining proof / acceptance

- **Joined proof scope:** the passing manual harness is test/e2e/qa-lab/auto-steer-joined-proof.mts. Clean source/build stamps and served asset hashes were verified. Ordinary input promotion atomically removes its pending row; the proof matches the exact pending input ID to the canonical transcript entry and independently checks target/lifetime/backend consumption. It does not invent a retained collected-source receipt. Runtime-build profile follows docs/help/testing/suites.md; completed, unchanged SDK declaration validation was reused. No per-PR long E2E job was added.
- Host loopback preflight returned HTTP 502. The unchanged secretless 8 GiB container then hit its memory ceiling and recorded **oom_kill=1** before GUI tests. The larger supported Testbox route is used instead; proxy/isolation policy was not bypassed.
- **UI startup:** production assets build, but the latest candidate measured **371,958 B versus 371,332 B** on Testbox Node 24.19.0. The earlier matched-metadata, same-toolchain local main comparison also exceeded the ceiling (371,475 B). The candidate remains red; this is not waived or called CI-green. Tighter raw partitioning keeps the unchanged largest-JS ceiling (214.6 KiB / 215 KiB).
- **SDK question:** accept the public advisory hook and its separate +3 export allowance, or keep public exposure blocked? Context contains bounded visible text, owning agent, signal/deadline and a lifetime assertion; results remain advice only. Relevant rules: src/plugin-sdk/AGENTS.md:71–75 and AGENTS.md:117. No acceptance is inferred from sponsorship or the common SDK approval.

## Credits

Feature requested by Peter Steinberger (@steipete); implementation scope and separate feature lane directed by Josh.

title: fix: keep Back to tasks button compact in task details
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: “Back to tasks” stretches across the task-title column when viewing task details in the Tasks panel.

## User Impact

The back button stays compact and left-aligned instead of looking like a wide bar, in both wide and narrow Tasks panels. Task titles, status details, and Stop controls keep their existing layout. No migration or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heading uses CSS Grid, whose default alignment stretched the button to the title’s width. Align only the heading’s button to the inline start so it keeps its natural content width without changing the shared button styles or its siblings.

## Evidence

Real Chromium captures of the production Control UI bundle with synthetic task data, dark theme, and a fixed clock. Matching 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844 browser viewports; the desktop Tasks panel is expanded using the real Focus control. No live user data. title: fix: keep agent narration inline and avatars top-aligned
body:
Replaces #156856. Related: #156340.

This maintainer-owned replacement preserves the original reviewed change and contributor credit. The original branch could not safely publish its conflict-resolution merge through the configured signing route; its ancestry remains untouched. This replacement landed as `1fa6ad6971cf179be78bbb8d0e4eec1a9ab3fcda`; the original is closed as superseded, not merged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes main-agent narration disappearing into a clipped status line during a run, and agent avatars dropping toward the bottom of tall replies.

## User Impact

Narration stays inline, in order, with normal Markdown formatting and tool activity. After a dashboard turn finishes, its work collapses under **Worked for …**, leaving the final answer visible. Expanding that heading restores the sequence. Agent avatars stay aligned with the top of the turn.

Tool-call grouping, its wording/counts, scrolling, and subagent rows are unchanged. Failed, blocked, unknown, and skipped outcomes remain visible. **Keep commentary** still controls settled history, not whether the active run's narration survives a refresh. No configuration, storage, provider, or harness changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the latest-commentary relocation path and reuse the existing transcript renderer, completed-work disclosure, duration formatter, and outcome summaries. Both harnesses use this shared Control UI path. Commentary still appears when a segment completes; this does not introduce token-by-token commentary streaming or new grouping state. Active commentary retention shares the existing progress owner’s explicit or inferred run identity; the avatar repair changes one shared alignment declaration.

**Maintainer decision:** @vyctorbrzezowski requested this presentation and the avatar follow-up; existing tool-call grouping and subagent rows remain unchanged. The current [maintainer-authorized landing request](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/c2e6adca-cd75-4fad-9f8f-d67c98e9129d) confirms that direction. This is an intentional replacement of the transient-status presentation from #156340, not an accidental reversal. The decision was explicitly approved in the linked human conversation before this replacement was opened. ClawSweeper’s inability to read that session does not create a new undecided product question; the agent is executing that existing approval, not granting it.

## Evidence

- **Landed:** native exact-head squash of `69f068f43b6421b70f28ce317adf2ceb1601f938` after [CI succeeded](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35946291468), security/dependency gates passed, and completed exact-head ClawSweeper review found no code or security findings. Its repeated product-direction question is resolved by the existing human approval recorded above. The native receipt is complete; no signing, CI, or admin bypass was used.

- CI repair: the first exact-head run failed in two lanes on the same older wrapped-footer test, which still required the avatar to be bottom-aligned. Local reproduction matched CI (35px versus the old 4px bottom offset). The test now requires equal avatar/bubble tops and retains its wrapped-footer height, virtual-row containment, and next-row adjacency checks. **No production code changed.** The corrected case passes; all **111 responsive browser tests pass** (24.93s normal `pnpm test … --maxWorkers=1` wall; 24.59s wrapper). Independent review of this correction found no P0–P2 issues. Targeted changed-file gates pass (UI/core-test types, formatting, lint, i18n, dead exports, and repository guards). The original CI UI-lane file execution was 48.56s; fresh exact-head CI will qualify the correction.

- Replacement equivalence: the initial 23-file patch was byte-for-byte identical to the independently reviewed delta from `4ab8c58fbe598d38b08bed4908da29d413092c8f` to `5621b22d4750c3607761d6495edab3cd37144a16`, applied cleanly to main `82a518c90ca4e4ef7e7b19832954edb4c283e5be`. Intervening main commits touch no patch paths. Existing visual contracts, browser proof, and inspected permanent screenshots are reused; fresh exact-head CI and ClawSweeper review apply to this PR.

- Landing integration: merged current main 4ab8c58fbe598d38b08bed4908da29d413092c8f while preserving its queued-input placement and persisted steer-boundary owner. The only conflicted file was the transcript builder; narration retention and working status still share one lazy progress resolver. **852 focused tests pass** across 22 files (16.46 s wrapper), including narration, inferred-run retention, input ordering, progress, disclosure, and transcript rendering. Changed-file gates pass (core/UI types, lint/style/format, i18n, dead exports, and repository guards). Fresh independent review reports no P0–P2 findings. The visual contracts and inspected screenshots below are unchanged.

- The inline-narration regressions fail before the repair and pass afterward. The completed-heading regression run likewise changed from **11 failures / 5 passes** to all passing.
- **460 local tests passed for the original narration/heading candidate**, covering narration/history reconciliation, retention, completed-run timing and ownership, outcome visibility, disclosure behavior, and transcript rendering. The 21 focused cases take 3.36 s through the wrapper; the 394 chat/transcript sibling cases take 17.34 s; the 45 isolated rendering cases take 5.41 s in Vitest.
- Six production-build Chromium narration scenarios already passed: live/reconnected commentary, evicted replay, cursor recovery, pre-steer reload ordering, split-history continuation, and growing-frame scroll following. [Narration browser execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35928760963).
- Completed-run browser proof passes: the heading uses only the matching run’s 13-second duration, survives reload, and expands to the existing tool presentation. The visualization/row-layout sibling also passes. The final focused browser invocation takes 17.05 s; [Testbox execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35933584463) uses `blacksmith-testbox`, lease `tbx_01m389ehtf2h2xgje0denrk4f2`, with wrapper exit 0. An initially incorrect test selector expected a group around a lone tool; inspecting the rendered DOM confirmed the existing single-tool presentation, and the corrected assertion passes.
- Core-test and UI typechecks, changed-file lint/style/format checks, i18n, dead-export scans, and repository guards pass. A lint-only shadowed variable was renamed and rechecked.
- Follow-up validation: **297 chat/progress tests pass** (9.15 s wrapper / 5.47 s Vitest), including three inferred-run cases that fail before the fix: segment identity, tool identity, and cached identity, each with a future queued run present. Retention still removes settled commentary. The earlier review’s inferred-run P2 is repaired by sharing the existing lazy progress result, not adding another identity resolver.
- **Six Chromium avatar layout cases pass** (11.69 s wrapper / 6.32 s Vitest; 100 ms test execution). The desktop avatar assertion failed by 33.59 px before the shared CSS repair. Changed-file static gates pass for all four follow-up files.

Mouse expansion, keyboard collapse, and both avatar variants pass with zero page errors. An initially incomplete sharing response in the capture fixture was corrected; production disclosure code was unchanged.

title: fix(ui): remove blank space from nested tool groups
body:
Related: #156856

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Short groups use only the height their visible content needs. Expanded groups still grow to the existing maximum of `min(420px, 58vh)` and scroll; collapsing them shrinks them again. title: fix: return child followup results after yielding
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a follow-up sent to a native child agent can lose its final answer when the child delegates work, yields, and finishes in a successor turn.

## User Impact

User impact: native-child follow-ups return their final result once after yielding, and a running successor no longer retains its predecessor's misleading yield diagnostic. A separate paused original task stays untouched.

This remains a **same-process repair**, not restart-safe completion delivery. No schema, durable authorization grant, retention extension, configuration, or migration is introduced. Registered detached task runtimes retain their run-scoped contract; the previously reproduced non-core-mirrored runtime binding defect remains outside this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

One task-owned result follows the exact accepted continuation. Its original receipt clears per-execution metadata before successor model/tool work starts, preserving logical task and audit identity. Inline waits and asynchronous delivery share one result, while cancellation, current access, physical-store identity, and Gateway admission stay enforced.

The correction also preserves normalized-DM reply routing, recognizes stored-alias revocation, and settles a never-accepted initial task without touching a paused predecessor. Duplicate liveness policy, reply-context assembly, settlement wrappers, and terminal state were removed or consolidated. #157196 was not imported wholesale.

## Evidence

### September 25 repair — current published revision

Published head: **[c1ffa76dc70f04cf0634b7ac78782cf42e80a30d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c1ffa76dc70f04cf0634b7ac78782cf42e80a30d)**. Readback occurs before any successor tool event. - **Focused tests and types passed:** receipt/SQLite, followup custody, admission, dispatch/tracking, agent-command, and session-sharing boundaries; core plus four affected test type graphs. Paired failing controls also cover normalized-DM routing, stored-alias revocation, and unaccepted initial cleanup. Overlapping reruns are not summed into an inflated test count.
- **Exact final-tree gates passed:** scoped lint/format, full Madge (zero cycles), full Knip, assertion-safety and max-lines checks, plus a fresh supported runtime build. No baseline or budget weakening.
- **Four frozen real-Gateway probes passed:** ordinary/yielded result delivery, paused-original preservation, real device-token revocation preventing all final requester effects, and one inline result with no duplicate requester turn. Provider responses were scripted loopback HTTP, not real-model inference. Gateway/provider cleanup passed.
- **Fresh full-patch autoreview:** no accepted/actionable P0-P2 findings. The review is source/evidence-scoped, not a substitute for new-head hosted CI.

[Final remote proof run 36196663684](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36196663684): exact tree above, command exit **0**, REPAIR_GATES_PASS and REPAIR_REAL_PROOFS_PASS, 491.846 seconds command wall. - **142 focused local tests / six files** pass (43.24s wrapper wall); **61 isolated SQLite/routing/child-coordination tests / four files** pass across the scoped runs. The new five-case helper suite cost 40.94s cold compiler/wrapper wall; it adds no Gateway boots.
- The unchanged frozen primary and paused harnesses plus real source-revocation probe pass on final source capsule `86adc5ca0fa8929276e866044d3bead406f9e920`: [Testbox 35950377575](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35950377575), lease `tbx_01m38pa8aq22ac63eaf4fetgvs`, command exit 0 in **238.931s**. Both allowed results arrive/store once; the exact yielded predecessor is empty, exact successor supplies `B_YIELD_DONE`, the separate original remains paused, and revocation produces no requester effect. Gateway/provider cleanup and exact stopped lease status verified.
- Final scoped review of the actual working-tree correction reports no actionable P0/P1 (0.87 confidence); limited to the supplied diff/evidence.

### Registered-runtime upgrade proof: reproduced preexisting owner-contract defect

The earlier map-backed fixture stopped during initial requester bootstrap and did not establish followup behavior. That fixture limitation is now superseded by a real existing-conversation comparison, not waived.

The repaired fixture first boots the normal runtime, performs actual native `sessions_spawn`, waits for the original child task to complete and its `B_READY` reply to be stored, then **cold-stops/restarts the same owned Gateway state** with a manifest-activated plugin. It verifies a changed Gateway PID, unchanged real child session ID and retained original reply. Only then does the freshly authenticated requester call `sessions_send(mode:followup, timeoutSeconds:0, watch:true)` to that child. The loaded plugin registers the public `DetachedTaskLifecycleRuntime` API, implements scoped `findTaskRun` for its non-core-mirrored records, and returns `null` for unrelated tasks as the public creation contract permits. No private core import, fabricated spawn ownership, authority mock, guard bypass, production plugin install or external user delivery is used.

[Paired real-Gateway trace: Testbox 35952488056](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35952488056), provider `blacksmith-testbox`, lease `tbx_01m38r1qawyrsp6pk0tb7xqz47`. Candidate source tree `86adc5ca0fa8929276e866044d3bead406f9e920` exactly equals published head `2f7ef4e35b7a7e35bdf89eea4a27f22183332a08`; wrapper capsule `393c03eca4dd90dd6afb6659b7d14edc0a059cee`. Pre-PR baseline is `4f6eb26b1beda60044ee9b94cd352f37c63718e9`, tree `95eee5045d591a11a59595ba936ab2b3eb0d0edd`. Both use identical harness SHA-256 `44b020aa385dd60b05639ff9554c9a955f87c02c2708b658b976658efc910876` and separately rebuilt runtime/build stamps.

| Observation | Candidate | Pre-PR baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Normal native child/original task completed before plugin enable | yes | yes |
| Cold restart, same real child incarnation, plugin loaded | PID 5971→6071 | PID 7056→7155 |
| Actual followup accepted/queued/watched | yes | yes |
| Registered plugin selected and creates exact followup task | yes | yes |
| Live-run binding | refused: `Task no longer belongs to this live run.` | same refusal |
| Target model calls after restart / successful result produced | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Plugin task final state | failed | failed |
| Probe exit / Gateway+provider cleanup | 1 / verified | 1 / verified |

Candidate followup `c23d6d22-b686-455e-acc6-9a0e455e4583` owns plugin task `11851d15-f9c8-4e13-8d3b-ae2017180e8f`; baseline followup `dc33f24f-1dae-4df5-8c54-cec5274d11f6` owns plugin task `0906100e-83ba-4e23-8532-854461196360`. The plugin records actual creation and failed finalization; the requester receives failure rather than the expected result. Aggregate command exit **1**, 229.605s command time; the owned Testbox is independently verified completed/stopped with no IP. These are deliberately retained red proofs, not a passing integration claim. Scripted HTTP model, real Gateway/auth/session/runtime lifecycle; not live inference.

**Named followup: registered-runtime live-run ownership for non-core-mirrored tasks.** The [public contract explicitly permits non-mirrored records](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2f7ef4e35b7a7e35bdf89eea4a27f22183332a08/src/tasks/detached-task-runtime-contract.ts#L193-L213), but [legacy Gateway dispatch binds through the core owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2f7ef4e35b7a7e35bdf89eea4a27f22183332a08/src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-dispatch.ts#L652-L656), whose [unchanged guard requires a canonical core task row](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2f7ef4e35b7a7e35bdf89eea4a27f22183332a08/src/tasks/task-run-owner.ts#L55-L65). Baseline repeats this after actual followup acceptance, so this is a preexisting integration defect for this documented adapter shape, not just the initial-spawn fixture limitation or a demonstrated regression from this PR. The bounded investigation ends here: successful registered-runtime result return/settlement remains **unproven**, and the claimed shipped success path cannot be certified for this shape until the owner-contract mismatch is repaired. No conclusion about every external adapter or historical release is inferred. No safety fence was relaxed and no second task owner/backend was invented to manufacture green proof.

**Scope:** the repaired feature follows an existing **native child conversation**; its followup activity is represented by a `cli` task. This is not ACP or general external CLI-harness support. Registered-runtime comparison is nonyielding legacy compatibility only; no plugin-runtime yielded-successor feature is claimed.

**Historical CI uncertainty retained:** the earlier wrapper `status:null` failure remains unexplained. Later successful wrapper runs and the exact-head green CI are not evidence of its root cause or a fix; this proof update changes no wrapper or product source.

**Previous proof head:** `2f7ef4e35b7a7e35bdf89eea4a27f22183332a08` (tree `86adc5ca0fa8929276e866044d3bead406f9e920`). [CI 35951064819](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35951064819) reached terminal **success**, with all 159 jobs terminal and no failed jobs. Both originally failing gates—`check-dependencies` and `check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture`—passed on this exact head. Run elapsed time was 13m39s; this is elapsed CI time, not a billing estimate. This PR is not being merged or deployed by this repair.

The original Phase 1 evidence below is pinned to `dbfea9001451ab15e66d41f7cb763186a6574b98`. Verification of the subsequent CI and compatibility corrections is recorded in the later subsections; the original full build is not represented as a later-head build.

A frozen harness exercises a real, isolated, nonminimal Gateway with native tools and lifecycle handling. Only the loopback HTTP model is scripted; this is not real-model inference.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nonyielding followup | Returned once | Returned once |
| Followup yields to held C; C finishes; exact B successor returns B_YIELD_DONE | A receives no result within 30 seconds | A receives the exact result once |
| Original B task remains paused while a separate followup yields | — | Followup returns once; original task remains running/paused |

C is released only after agent.wait confirms the exact predecessor yielded with an empty reply. Both Gateway and provider cleanup are verified. The before and after use the same frozen primary harness.

Independent autoreview found no actionable P0/P1 findings. Focused contracts cover repeated yield, inline-to-async consumer transfer, cancellation, canonical empty replies, exact successor adoption, revoked authority, and the unrelated paused task.

- 258 focused tests across 11 files passed in 210.51 seconds (six shards, including compiler setup and real SQLite boundaries).
- Production typecheck and six affected test type graphs passed. Scoped lint, formatting, line-size/assertion ratchets, and runtime import-cycle checks passed.
- Measured new-file costs: completion-owner tests (11 cases) 5.86 seconds wrapper wall; retained-authorization tests (3 cases) 17.51 seconds cold wrapper wall, with 19 ms test body. No new per-test Gateway boots; the real end-to-end harness is manual proof, not added per-PR CI work.
- Full production build passed. Both frozen real-flow probes passed on the same final source capsule (`735bfc07633867ecf25d627c05d715203ec6bcc3`), with pre/post source and build guards, explicit result assertions, and verified Gateway/provider cleanup.
- Final proof used Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m38h31xhv2a05pee9baj82n5`, associated with [Actions run 35943902956](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35943902956). Command wall: 173.225 seconds, exit 0. Lease stop was independently verified. The workflow provisions the lease; this is a command receipt, not a claim that a cancelled provisioning workflow is green CI. Hosted PR CI cost is not yet available.

Local SQLite tests initially failed because the host's /tmp filesystem had no free inodes; native tracing and a baseline comparison confirmed the environment failure. Those tests passed on the isolated Testbox without removing shared lock files. The first final probe was interrupted when its Testbox workflow was cancelled after the full build passed; only the remaining probes were completed on the fresh lease, without source changes.

### CI correction and revoked-requester proof

The initial head failed the full Knip export scan and full Madge static/type dependency gate. Commit `fbdcb93288a120a484e5a72b985b9200e0f0d284` extracts a type-only followup owner contract, makes the locally used custody type private, and restricts generic task-owner metadata to its liveness consumer. All callers moved to the leaf contract. Runtime owner identity, cohort custody, and settlement logic are unchanged; no ignores, suppressions, or baseline growth.

- Reproduced both failures before editing; **full `pnpm deadcode:full` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` now exit 0**, with zero Madge cycles. The earlier runtime-value-cycle check was not equivalent to the full Madge gate.
- Production plus gateway-other/agents-tools/state-logging test typechecks, scoped lint/ratchets, and **69 focused regressions across four files passed** (45.09s wrapper wall). Fresh independent review reported no actionable P0/P1 finding for the correction.
- Additional real proof: [Blacksmith Testbox run 35945510454](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35945510454), lease `tbx_01m38jc1f4mn0by41pjsp3anrh`, command exit 0 in 188.245s. Both the allowed yielded-result flow and a real device-token revocation case passed; Gateway/provider cleanup succeeded and the stopped lease was independently verified.

The negative case uses a real signed device-token connection (no shared-token/cache fallback), real pairing/token storage and Gateway RPCs, and the production followup/announcement path. An independent admin revokes the original requester device **after the exact successor is admitted**, while the scripted HTTP provider holds its result. No authority, session-fact, or effect guards are mocked. Redacted trace:

```text
02:05:13.902 device.token.revoke -> original requester token revoked
02:05:13.909 sessions_send announce flow admission failed
             error="Followup completion authority was revoked."
02:05:13.924 successor -> operator source authority is no longer active
02:05:13.933 requester WebSocket closed with code 4001
02:05:13.934 held provider attempts B_YIELD_DONE after revocation
02:05:13.938 exact successor agent.wait -> error, stopReason=rpc
02:05:13.951 finalRequesterRunCount=0; finalProviderInvocationCount=0

```

This proves in-flight source revocation prevents the resumed result from producing a final requester Gateway effect, rather than merely checking a mocked custody predicate or observing a timeout. It is not a claim about every post-commit/crash timing window. Models remain scripted; authentication, revocation, admission and lifecycle handling are real. No Phase 2 schema, durable authority or permission change is included.

### Registered-runtime compatibility

Commit `e9b866f73397cf23bf242cc5a522d895fc84e6f7` preserves the existing `registerDetachedTaskRuntime` contract. Registered runtimes select their prior run-scoped path **before** core completion custody is prepared. Core task receipts retain the yielded-result fix. The Gateway guard remains fail-closed if a core request was already prepared and the runtime changes; there is no post-admission downgrade or new permission grant.

- Two focused regressions cover real active-registry selection and legacy Gateway admission; the existing core-request refusal remains covered. The compatibility/registered-runtime suites pass **57 tests across three files in 14.29s**. Full Knip, full Madge, production/affected test types, lint and review pass. No additional per-test Gateway boots.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes failed sidebar sessions growing a second, truncated error line instead of showing the details in the session hover card.

## User Impact

Failed session rows stay compact. Hovering or keyboard-focusing a session shows its full failure above Agent Notepad, including failures reported by a child session. The existing failure icon, red state, and attention lifecycle are preserved; no configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hover card now reads the same projected session tree as the sidebar, so parent cards retain child-failure attribution rather than losing it in a flat-row lookup. title: fix: SQLite readers miss committed worker changes
body:
Related: #143220

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a SQLite reader can reuse stale schema or session-entry facts after a write from another connection completes. Three Node/SQLite checks on Android Talk PR #143220 show compatible failures, but their full-shard causality still requires exact-head CI. This separate fix does not change the Android feature.

## User Impact

Worker-backed reads can observe a committed table, session-group edit, or newer schema at the next asynchronous boundary instead of serving stale facts. No config or database-schema version changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admitted schema cache previously held a `PRAGMA data_version` result until `setImmediate`. A worker's completed write can resume its caller earlier, in a microtask. Shorten only that cache window while preserving coalescing for synchronous reads; update the existing cross-connection tests to exercise the actual asynchronous boundary without relaxing their expected data.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the focused foreign-connection regression failed on trusted main base `a5f1d0996a1f80a789628af19ec304c08369607b`: raw `sqlite_schema` saw the new table, while the admitted cache still said it was absent.
- With the fix on the same base, seven focused SQLite/Web Push/session-group/worker test files passed on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m38dme6znxghk5vsn943b864`. Existing cross-connection data-version and migration assertions were retained. Targeted format check and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged` passed on the exact six-file patch (including all core-test type graphs, lint, schema guard, and cycle check). The lease was stopped after proof.
- Fresh uncommitted P0–P2 AutoReview: no accepted/actionable finding. Full exact-head hosted PR CI has not run for this separate fix; do not treat prior Android PR checks as its proof.

title: fix: Side chat silently drops images on text-only models
body:
Related: #156840

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Side chat answers an image question without seeing the image when its selected utility model is text-only.

## User Impact

Unsupported image questions now fail visibly before provider inference. The configured model is not silently replaced, and the existing failed-image **Retry** state retains the attachment. Text-only questions and image-capable models keep working. No permissions, storage contracts, migration, or Gateway deployment change. Text-only questions remain supported. Visible rejection of unsupported image input is intentional: the previous path discarded the image rather than providing working image support. Automatically switching the configured model/provider would change the selected route; this repair does not do that.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the refreshed [text-only-model finding on #156840](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156840#issuecomment-5804569343), which I consumed after that PR merged. The [first review of this corrective PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156900#issuecomment-5805782761) then identified a catalog-fallback mismatch and duplicate dynamic discovery in the initial preflight.

Revision `72533a07fbeff3243558f777e4a6b9743f6aaca0` removes the preflight entirely. Side chat supplies a fail-closed input assertion, and the existing embedded dispatch owner calls it on the **already prepared executable model**, before workspace/backend dispatch. Catalog fallback, provider discovery, model choice and auth-profile resolution therefore keep their single existing owner. Retries retain the assertion and check each attempt’s actual model. The Side chat error type is shared from a leaf owner; no new protocol field or permission is introduced.

Latest revision `a15884f343e3f030492aa95d31938dcb05cec4df` also fixes the reviewed UI mismatch: unsupported images have a distinct `image-input-unsupported` reason and localized image-capable-model guidance. The wire response remains `retryable: false`; the existing UI offers an **explicit user-action Retry** that resends the retained image without taking a newer draft. Missing-model and other failure states retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- **Latest UI/wire RED → GREEN:** the new mounted controller/renderer recovery scenario failed before the change (**1 failed / 45 passed**), and the exact registered-RPC wire assertion failed on the old reason (**1 failed / 11 skipped**). The implemented revision passes **84 focused tests** (12 Gateway ask + 46 rail/controller/renderer + 26 image retry/history), **39.52 s** cold two-shard wall. It proves accurate guidance, no automatic retry, original image resent only on click, newer draft preserved, and image payload released after success.
- New English copy passes keyless i18n baseline/verify (**9,923 keys**, 102 unchanged raw-copy entries); no generated locales were edited. Independent review of the fully staged candidate with actual UI/RPC contracts is **scoped-clean through P2**. The committed-head built-browser run is now complete: **8/8 scenarios passed**, including exact retained-PNG retry and newer-draft preservation. title: fix(ui): keep desktop chat tables sized to their content
body:
Related: #156750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: desktop chat tables expand farther than their content needs, while dense comparisons can scroll instead of wrapping.

## User Impact

Compact tables stay at the reading width; larger tables borrow only the room their content needs. Desktop controls are icon-only and closer to the header, with more balanced space below. **Mobile and phone-landscape sizing, scrolling, labels, and touch controls are unchanged.**

No prompt, configuration, dependency, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the browser’s intrinsic table layout within the existing pane-relative width ceiling, rather than forcing every table to that ceiling. Desktop cells can wrap before horizontal scrolling is needed; genuinely irreducible content still scrolls inside the table viewport. The existing geometry and interaction owners are unchanged.

The refinement is limited to wide conversation panes and explicitly excludes the existing phone-landscape layout. Accessible button names and keyboard behavior remain intact.

## Evidence

- All 11 table browser cases pass, covering compact 4-/8-column tables, prose and dense comparisons, 1920/1440/1280px desktop views, 760/390px mobile views, 932×430 phone landscape, saved 82% width, RTL, Files, copy, expansion, sticky headers, links and focus return. - Sixteen Chromium geometry/focus cases pass. CSS replay of the actual rendered hierarchy in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit verifies bounded placement, painted wide edges and no transcript horizontal overflow. This is **CSS-boundary proof**, not a Firefox/Safari full-application tour; local WebKit full-app navigation was refused by the host egress proxy.

title: feat(ui): opt into configured defaults for fresh sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh-session drafts restore remembered model, runtime, and reasoning choices, so an operator cannot make new sessions start from configured agent defaults without restricting later model selection.

## User Impact

Operators can opt in with `gateway.controlUi.newSessionModelDefaults: "configured"`. The default remains `"last-used"` for other deployments. Fresh `/new` and command-palette sessions inherit the selected agent's configured model, runtime, and thinking defaults; users can still choose another allowed model or reasoning level for the current draft.

Explicit choices survive reload with the current unsent draft and retire with an accepted submission. Fast Mode and placement preferences remain available, historical preferences are not deleted, and existing conversations are unchanged. There is no database-version, retention, or permission change. Configure the desired model and `thinkingDefault` on the agent or agent defaults; this option does not hardcode a model or reasoning level. Refresh or reconnect the UI after changing the setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh-draft initialization now distinguishes remembered defaults from deliberate draft intent. The existing draft persistence owner reconciles saved content before publishing model-only edits, including canceled or failed restoration, and account-local model overrides retire with their draft. This is an opt-in UI initialization policy, not a model-access restriction. The configuration surface grows by one optional key because the existing permission and selection-scope settings do not express that policy.

**Maintainer decision:** @vincentkoc approved this narrowly scoped opt-in policy and the optional draft-intent fields in the existing browser store, then explicitly requested landing the presented implementation in the linked work session. `last-used` remains the default; existing unsent content and attachments must survive. This records the existing decision, not a new approval request.

## Evidence

- **Landed:** `6be8e0f993332bbf36203a948f44c2ed23ab3cfb` is verified on `main`. Exact reviewed head `d824f7756680b5698a804794c796607cce18273b` passed [CI 35941685708](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35941685708), including GitHub Actions `openclaw/ci-gate` check 107453753032. Current-head ClawSweeper review completed with no actionable findings; its remaining compatibility checklist was [confirmed with the upgrade evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156866#issuecomment-5805775802). No release or Team deployment is implied.

- Focused selection, metadata, account, persistence, submission, and palette suites: **199 tests across 11 files passed** (15.32 s wrapper wall, one worker).
- Regressions were observed failing before the owning fixes, including lost saved content after a canceled restore and a consumed personal-account model carrying into the next draft.
- UI production/test typechecks, changed-file lint, formatting, config metadata, line-cap and relevant static guards passed. Independent local review of the final candidate had no actionable P0-P2 findings.
- Updated isolated Chromium mock-Gateway proof: **14 tests across two files passed** in 37.84 s (including a production UI bundle build). This covers the original pending-folder regression, browser-local/authenticated preferences, deliberate draft choices, subsequent fresh defaults, and palette submission. The upgrade case independently seeds the pre-change `60d9d104` IndexedDB row format, with no `modelSelection` and a Blob attachment, then checks restored text/name and exact attachment bytes in the session request. This is a legacy-format fixture and browser boundary proof, not an old installed binary or live production Gateway claim.
- [Before / after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156866#issuecomment-5805106214): synthetic 1280×900 fixtures, inspected and verified rendered in the PR (both images decoded at full resolution).

**CI repair:** non-draft run [35937667496](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35937667496) exposed a model-policy hydration callback restarting pending remembered-folder validation. A new two-policy regression failed red; the owning fix refreshes only model state and leaves the folder request intact. Its focused controller/folder/submission/palette invocation passed **64 tests across four files** in 8.24 s. The browser test also now waits for the independent authenticated-preference mirror before asserting its persisted value, without increasing timeouts or weakening the assertion.

**Other CI failure investigated:** that run’s `checks-ui (3/3)` failed while opening an unchanged Web Awesome dropdown. Replaying its 495-file selection with three workers did not reproduce that failure; the dropdown passed, but the replay ended with two browser-launch failures with `pthread_create: Resource temporarily unavailable` at the unchanged sandbox PID limit and one page-target crash. The isolated replay uses Node 26 rather than hosted Node 24/Bun, so it is not equivalent green CI and does not establish the original failure’s cause. No dropdown behavior, assertions, retries, or runner limits were changed. The replacement-head hosted CI subsequently passed.

**Known validation gap:** the canonical isolated full-runtime `ciArtifacts` build did not pass. Both this feature and its pinned pre-change baseline were OOM-killed in tsdown invocation 2 at the unchanged 8 GiB runner limit (`SIGKILL`, `oom_kill=1`, no build timeout). This is a demonstrated baseline runner-capacity failure, not a claimed green build. The ordinary exact-head CI and review gates passed before landing; the local full-runtime build is not claimed green.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

Single-file runs used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`, the repository wrapper without dependency reconciliation. Times are wall seconds, including startup and transformation.

| `src/gateway/config-reload.operation-policy.test.ts` | 81 | 32.21 s |
| `ui/src/app/config.test.ts` | 19 | 2.15 s |

The existing 81-case reload-policy file added one policy row; 98% of the measured Vitest duration was cold transformation, not new test work. The Chromium file needs real page reload, IndexedDB persistence, and rendered/request-boundary checks; unit tests alone cannot prove that browser lifecycle. title: fix: keep agent narration inline and avatars top-aligned
body:
Related: #156340

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes main-agent narration disappearing into a clipped status line during a run, and agent avatars dropping toward the bottom of tall replies.

## User Impact

Narration stays inline, in order, with normal Markdown formatting and tool activity. After a dashboard turn finishes, its work collapses under **Worked for …**, leaving the final answer visible. Expanding that heading restores the sequence. Agent avatars stay aligned with the top of the turn.

Tool-call grouping, its wording/counts, scrolling, and subagent rows are unchanged. Failed, blocked, unknown, and skipped outcomes remain visible. **Keep commentary** still controls settled history, not whether the active run's narration survives a refresh. No configuration, storage, provider, or harness changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the latest-commentary relocation path and reuse the existing transcript renderer, completed-work disclosure, duration formatter, and outcome summaries. Both harnesses use this shared Control UI path. Commentary still appears when a segment completes; this does not introduce token-by-token commentary streaming or new grouping state. Active commentary retention shares the existing progress owner’s explicit or inferred run identity; the avatar repair changes one shared alignment declaration.

**Maintainer decision:** @vyctorbrzezowski requested this presentation and the avatar follow-up; existing tool-call grouping and subagent rows remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- The inline-narration regressions fail before the repair and pass afterward. The completed-heading regression run likewise changed from **11 failures / 5 passes** to all passing.
- **460 local tests passed for the original narration/heading candidate**, covering narration/history reconciliation, retention, completed-run timing and ownership, outcome visibility, disclosure behavior, and transcript rendering. The 21 focused cases take 3.36 s through the wrapper; the 394 chat/transcript sibling cases take 17.34 s; the 45 isolated rendering cases take 5.41 s in Vitest.
- Six production-build Chromium narration scenarios already passed: live/reconnected commentary, evicted replay, cursor recovery, pre-steer reload ordering, split-history continuation, and growing-frame scroll following. [Narration browser execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35928760963).
- Completed-run browser proof passes: the heading uses only the matching run’s 13-second duration, survives reload, and expands to the existing tool presentation. The visualization/row-layout sibling also passes. ## What Problem This Solves

Plugin config validation can accept an incomplete URL such as `https://` and reject email/UUID values whose formats are intended to be annotations because compiled checks and validation errors use different format callbacks.

Found during follow-up release verification for #156346; this is a separate schema-validation defect, not a change to operator model permissions.

## User Impact

Plugin URL settings follow the existing URL validation contract again, while annotation-only formats remain non-restrictive. Cached validation and error details agree. No dependency changes, new configuration, or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

TypeBox captures format callbacks while compiling a validator. Apply the existing plugin-specific format scope during compilation as well as interpreted error reporting, and restore the global registry in both paths. The format cases move into a focused sibling suite so the already-oversized general suite shrinks rather than growing its line-cap exception.

title: fix(telegram): prevent lost replies when idle sockets close
body:
Related: #156466.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Telegram replies when a pooled idle connection closes just as a new message starts sending.

## User Impact

Initial previews, ordinary text replies, and terminal errors use fresh connections in the built-in Telegram transport. Existing-message edits, polling, and control requests retain pooling. Each new plain or rich-text message pays an additional connection/TLS handshake; no configuration or migration is required.

A response lost after Telegram accepts a message is still ambiguous. This does not promise exactly-once delivery or retry those sends. Caller-supplied transports and dispatchers remain caller-owned. If Telegram never received an ambiguous failed request, the send can fail rather than trying another transport. That is the deliberate tradeoff for not duplicating a message Telegram may already have accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a separate bounded, non-reusing pool within each existing transport attempt instead of guessing from ECONNRESET whether a send landed. The same owner retains proxy/DNS policy, fallback selection, request authority, and dispatcher shutdown. Text-send fallback now requires the existing proven-no-send classification: the socket regression also exposed an accepted message being sent three times after a connection closed before its response.

Keep the existing duplicate-send guards. Update the socket-lifecycle fixture to exercise pooled edits alongside active fresh sends, and isolate loopback cancellation proof from ambient proxies using a matching Undici fetch/dispatcher pair.

## Evidence

- Real grammY Api + production client-fetch/transport + local HTTP sockets: before the repair, both plain/rich idle-reset cases failed and the accepted-then-close control recorded three accepted requests. After the repair, all five cases pass on Node 26.8 and Blacksmith Node 24.19, including reset, clean close, and truncated-response negative controls. No sleeps or retry-until-green behavior was added.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Users can drop or paste images into Side chat, preview/remove them, and send them with a question or by themselves. Images stay out of the main chat composer. A failed question retains its image for retry without consuming a newer draft.

Side chat remains read-only. Images are request-scoped; the existing bounded text-only Side chat history does not retain image bytes for later questions. No migration, new tool permission, or live Gateway deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Side chat lacked both attachment intake and an image-bearing request path. Reuse the shared composer attachment/read lifecycle and Gateway image validation, then pass the validated image bytes into the existing restricted companion runner. title: fix(chat): retain discussion audience and actual reply authorship
body:
Related: #156797

## What Problem This Solves

Shared-session history can lose the distinction between human discussion and an agent assignment, and a reply to another human can be mislabeled with the current sender's name.

## User Impact

Later context retains the explicitly selected discussion audience and the referenced message's recorded author and role. Compaction and native quoted-history adapters do not turn human discussion into an assignment. Unattributed older messages stay unattributed rather than borrowing the current connection's identity.

This does not change transport ChatType, access control, agent-run admission, or existing stored message bytes. It adds no classifier, configuration, schema version, or dependency.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core draft already carries audience through the embedded model boundary. This final slice keeps that fact in the compaction formatter and Codex quoted-history adapter, and resolves bounded reply context from the actual stored target. Untrusted names and reply bodies remain per-turn user context, not stable system instructions. The existing metadata string sanitizer is extracted unchanged to respect the source-size limit.

**Review order: 3 of 3; depends on #156838, which depends on #156820.** Its base is the UI draft branch. Keep the coordinated series draft until reviewed; no merge, ready transition, or deployment was performed.

title: feat(ui): post human discussion without waiting for the agent
body:
Related: #156797

## What Problem This Solves

Human discussion needs an explicit audience choice without competing send buttons or losing the selected-recipient context.

## User Impact

The ordinary send arrow stays in place. A labeled **Run agent** checkbox sits on the right of the existing **Will notify** strip: checked allows agent work; unchecked posts discussion only. A human reply without selected mentions exposes the same control in its reply row, without claiming anyone will be notified. Selecting a person still defaults to agent participation; a human reply defaults to discussion and permits an explicit checked override.

The choice belongs to the current draft, not a session setting. Clearing/submitting the draft, changing the conversation or incarnation, removing its context, navigating input history, or entering queue editing resets the local override. Failed drafts keep their selection; accepted outbox items keep their recorded audience across retries. Discussion remains text-only in an existing signed-in conversation. No deployment, configuration, protocol, or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This revises the original draft’s **Ask agent / Post to people** buttons following UX review. The **Will notify** renderer was not removed: both its owner and registered call were unchanged in the original stack. title: feat(chat): record human discussion without activating the agent
body:
Related: #156797

## What Problem This Solves

A message intended for another human in a shared Control UI conversation currently enters the agent-send lifecycle.

## User Impact

Signed-in Control UI clients can explicitly record human discussion without starting, queueing, steering, interrupting, or recovering agent work. Ordinary requests and follow-ups retain their existing behavior; mentioning a human does not automatically suppress a request to the agent.

This first contract is deliberately **text-only in an existing session**. Attachments, new-session creation, goals, and outbound delivery overrides are not supported in discussion mode. No protocol/database version bump, configuration change, or deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing chat owner branches on explicit `participation: "humans"` before agent admission. It reuses authenticated authorship, durable input custody, transcript publication, and committed mention delivery, and acknowledges a committed message with `status: "posted"` instead of pretending a run started. An immutable authenticated fingerprint prevents a consumed message ID from accepting different discussion text.

**Review order: 1 of 3.** The dependent UI draft is #156838; the remaining reply/compaction/native quoted-context draft is #156839. This core already includes the embedded model-boundary audience reader. Keep the coordinated series in draft for review, and do not land the core alone before the client flow is ready.
