title: feat: support plugin-owned model credentials
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Providers with plugin-owned credentials could enter ordinary agent authentication or retain usable credentials after their plugin owner was disabled, replaced or revoked.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can declare credential ownership in provider and catalog metadata. OpenClaw resolves those credentials through the matching live plugin instance and keeps that authority attached through exchange, model preparation and dispatch. Ordinary agent-scoped providers retain their existing account selection. No production configuration or default model changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared auth owner rejects agent profile pins for plugin credentials and pins the exact live owner, registration and secrets generation. A private process-local validator survives preparation and model copies; guarded HTTP checks it immediately before every request, including local-service health redirects. Plugin-owned credentials use guarded HTTP instead of native WebSocket transports that cannot enforce this lifetime. Shared local-service startup settles before another caller can acquire its lease.

This continues the original contributor branch and builds on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156621. Requirements contributed by Vincent Koc and Peter Steinberger. The public ownership declaration and optional managed-fetch selector are additive.

## Evidence

- The retained-credential, health-redirect, shared-startup and WebSocket regressions were reproduced before correction. Current credentials succeed; revocation after asynchronous preparation causes zero HTTP or WebSocket dispatch. Existing lease owners survive rejected concurrent acquisitions.
- Focused auth, preparation, lifecycle, compaction and transport checks passed: the 81-case auth matrix, 57 WebSocket cases, 46 additional sibling cases and 31 health/sentinel cases across their recorded focused runs. Counts describe separate runs and are not an aggregate unique-test count.
- Production and affected test types, typed lint, formatting, privacy inspection and the mock-export ratchet passed. Scoped independent review and two final signed-head audits found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The full build at 3faa336c75506591f2d7cea9a494c488db2cf50f passed in 2m41s, including 97 plugins, 54 native module checks, 155 SDK exports, 14 runtime postbuild phases and the UI build.
- Signed head 3f14c05236f10ad9a833770ee5962d4dd6c22110 preserves the reviewed auth implementation while integrating current `main` at a09c26b193b44610fbb565478963bceca30fe951. The conflict resolution keeps plugin credential authority through direct compaction while retaining `main`'s SecretRef egress and non-secret synthetic-auth guards. The four affected auth and compaction shards passed (92 tests); the earlier lifecycle fixture repair remains covered by its 148 passing tests.
- Codex dependency inspected at 414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6: codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:893 and codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs:325. Authentication is applied at handshake; retained native connections do not enforce the private OpenClaw validator.
- Exact-head CI run 38910881416 attempt 1 completed with one non-aggregate failure: `checks-ui-e2e (8/9)` job 117007068604 timed out waiting for the existing `Color mode: Light` menu item; the aggregate gate failed downstream. The other 95 UI E2E files and 400 tests passed.
- The CI checkout was merge c1ded896b785bf02a6bfe12b6bcdfb7f89d54548, with protected-main parent 0e6818f076d304fe363dad62a1a070f084dffb49 and Auth parent 3f14c05236f10ad9a833770ee5962d4dd6c22110. Its failed test, harness, theme/menu owners, shell event path and Solid bridge are byte-identical to protected main. Diagnostics showed the unchanged menu remained open, visible and focused with a healthy renderer, but its System-mode click produced no theme mutation. This is admitted as an inherited main failure, not green CI.
- Named follow-up: repair the main-owned Control UI theme-mode event path so a visible System-mode menu click cannot leave both application and toggle state at `system`.
- Overall production delta: +738 net lines for credential ownership and dispatch enforcement; tests +1685 and documentation +23. No vendor live request is claimed by these deterministic credential/lifecycle tests.

title: fix(ci): stop obsolete security review reads after new pushes
body:
Related: #155170

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Security Review keeps reading obsolete PR data and waiting through diff recovery after a newer push supersedes the revision.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Superseded reviews stop admitting read-only work at a cooperative checkpoint rather than finishing long pagination or the entire diff-recovery wait. Required security approvals and the combined CI gate stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing review owner now checks the live PR between reads after 30 seconds and during non-quota recovery waits. It reuses the existing superseded-head outcome instead of canceling Actions jobs by event arrival order. Per-SHA publication serialization, approval revocation, final authority checks, and autoscrub writes/cleanup are unchanged. No workflow concurrency, permissions, main/manual/release behavior, or live runs are changed.

Limits: this is cooperative stopping, not an in-flight request kill. Requests retain their 30-second timeout; quota-directed waits must finish before another API call. Checkout and runtime setup are outside these checkpoints. The tradeoff is at most one additional PR observation per 30 seconds of read admission, plus checkpoints during non-quota recovery.

## Evidence

- Isolated real script-entrypoint proof: the old code failed four stopping assertions. The change stops diff recovery after one 30-second checkpoint in detect/autoscrub/enforce modes, and exits before requesting the next slow file page. No post-supersession writes or approval are published. The unchanged-head control completes successfully.
- 126 entrypoint tests pass. `pnpm test test/scripts/security-review-script.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`: **13.36 s wall**, **12.14 s Vitest duration**. The eight new checkpoint cases take **1.11 s** including the test harness when selected alone.
- Guard sibling run: **360 passed, one environment-specific failure**. The unchanged setup-action fixture expects a fake npm executable, but this host’s noninteractive Bash startup prepends `/usr/bin`, selecting real npm instead. The failure reproduces with the workflow file alone; a direct isolated shell trace confirms the PATH rewrite. The workflow/action and failing test are unchanged. The other 36 workflow trust-boundary tests pass.
- Changed-file guards, root test typechecking, dead-export scans, formatting, and targeted script/test lint pass (the initial `prefer-const` lint error was corrected).
- Workflow checks pass, including actionlint, zizmor, CI-owner generation and composite-action interpolation checks. The scanner required removal of an empty `GITHUB_TOKEN` from its subprocess environment; no token or identity was replaced.
- Independent pre-commit and final committed-branch autoreviews: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. The implementation is `4b3566e89ca457321b72a7a24c391d4778ab5d2d`, based on `60d9d1042375f014944b94006f4b1c2b2f5af9c0`. The published head is `8dbfaf4ffe8a240f874fcc65346b6fa4ce6fcb58`; its attributed publication-marker commit has exactly the tested tree. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35926232490) completed successfully, including the native and combined CI gates. CI file-seconds have not been extracted. [SecOps code-owner approval](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156798#pullrequestreview-5299283924) was submitted by @vincentkoc on this exact head at 2026-09-24 03:20 UTC, resolving the sole remaining approval gate. title: fix(ui): preserve cloud runner choices and prefer smaller defaults
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cloud runner pickers choosing the first listed machine when an unconfigured profile offers a smaller machine, and placement dialogs showing one choice while omitting it from the submitted request.

## User Impact

Explicit, saved, recovered, and provider-configured choices remain authoritative. For unconfigured profiles, the UI prefers the first machine whose reported CPU and memory are no greater than every compatible option. Unknown resources or CPU/memory tradeoffs retain catalog order. This does not infer price or workload suitability.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared selection policy now owns the fallback, and the Solid dispatch, move, and restart dialogs use that same selection for both display and submission. Class names cannot rank capacity across providers or operating systems: for example, a Windows Standard runner can be smaller than Small.

This updates the original contribution by @roboclaw-bot for the current Solid UI and preserves its authorship. The original Small-over-Standard rule and screenshots no longer describe this change.

## Evidence

- Independent source review and autoreview: no actionable findings.
- Focused tests against the unchanged production baseline: 7 expected failures; repaired candidate: 19/19 pass.
- Coverage includes configured and explicit choices, recovered placement, every dialog mode, incompatible OS options, missing metadata, tied minima, and CPU/memory tradeoffs.
- Fresh Chromium production builds passed. The original large-first picker failed the new selected-state assertion; the repaired candidate passed all 3 scenarios (unconfigured smaller, configured Standard, explicitly selected Standard), including exact intercepted dispatch payloads. The Gateway was mocked; no cloud runner was provisioned.
- Upgrade scope: no persisted draft format, configuration schema, or backend API changed. Explicit-choice and recovered-placement tests pass; the full v2026.10.3 release-upgrade matrix is outside this scoped UI repair.
- Production change: +23/-8 lines. The added policy represents a resource comparison that cannot safely be inferred from class names; duplicate dialog selection was removed.

Full CI repeats after each admitted main push while the branch is changing rapidly.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. Full main validation moves to hourly GitHub Actions; CodeQL, workflow security checks, and push-range ratchets remain event-driven. PR checks and release/publishing prerequisites stay intact.

Set repository Actions variable **`OPENCLAW_CI_ON_PUSH=true`** to restore the previous path-filtered per-push full CI and cache warming. Unset/empty/false leaves hourly-only full CI; deleting the variable rolls back to that default. No repository settings or variable values were changed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hourly dispatcher reuses the existing full manual CI path (including Android) instead of filtering only the last main commit. The child workflow and checkout use GitHub's immutable dispatch SHA; hourly children share a non-canceling, coalescing concurrency slot separate from pushes and ordinary manual/release CI. Auxiliary checks and nonpublishing plugin artifact preview also move hourly. Docs Agent keeps its full-CI prerequisite through verified producer evidence before its write job is admitted.

Use **Main CI Hourly → Run workflow → main** for an immediate full CI run. GitHub cron is best-effort, not a one-hour completion SLA. Unchanged SHAs are deliberately rechecked, and no numerical cost savings are claimed. Full manual coverage is broader than an individual path-filtered main push.

## Evidence

- **Docs Agent review finding repaired:** a separate read-only admission job authenticates the canonical CI workflow, current main SHA, exact completed attempt, successful aggregate, and successful revision-confirmation step. Only then can the contents-write job enter its concurrency slot. Security-only pushes, failed/skipped gates, other targets, stale attempts, superseded main, and arbitrary manual CI are denied; hourly Actions-bot children and explicit authorized Docs Agent manual runs retain their intended paths.
- **After-change boundary proof:** the tests execute the actual YAML verifier script and producer/consumer expressions—not a parallel implementation. **253 tests passed** across Docs Agent, hourly CI, and ancillary admission (**15.55 s** wall); the existing Docs Agent Git/action-ownership guard also passed. The attempt-specific REST job fields were also checked live. No production docs write or pre-merge cron execution is claimed.
- Landing follow-up: hosted CI exposed nine ancillary admission assertions still describing the old cadence/groups. The correction preserves original PR group identities, keeps push/manual/hourly work isolated, and extends the existing admission model with explicit opt-in pushes and skipped-push ordering proof. **208 focused tests passed** (combined hourly/ancillary command: **2.80 s** wall); test-root types, focused lint, workflow checks, and independent P0/P1 review passed.

title: fix(ui): make chat tables readable without unnecessary scrolling
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat tables hide headings and sentence-length cells behind sideways scrolling even when the conversation has room to display them.

## User Impact

Ordinary tables wrap and remain readable inline. On wide panes, top-level assistant tables use spare space while paragraphs keep their normal reading width. Dense comparisons retain horizontal scrolling and a visible **Expand table** action above the table; expanded headers stay visible while scrolling.

No system-prompt, model-guidance, configuration, or column-count-limit changes. No migration required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fit ordinary tables to the available space, allow headers and cells to wrap, and top-align rows. Keep natural widths for dense comparisons rather than turning long notes into a word per line. Keep extra width inside the actual conversation pane, including when a side panel is open. Forwarded/disclosed tables stay inside their own frame.

Available table width uses the existing transcript geometry owner’s resolved column width, rather than reinterpreting a saved percentage inside each table.

Wide table rows preserve the transcript's paint boundary. Browsers without adjustable overflow clipping keep those mounted rows visible; transcript virtualization remains in place.

## Evidence

- 11 real-browser table tests pass: 2-column prose, compact 4-/8-column tables, mobile/desktop resizing, Files pane, dense scrolling, copy, focus and navigation. This includes saving 82% in Appearance and restoring it at 1280/1440/1920px. Test file: 27.15 seconds on one worker; the saved-width scenario takes 2.03 seconds.

The task-only live scenario takes 11.13 seconds (17.75 seconds including its fixture); it is not added to routine CI. The command exited 0 and the lease was stopped; lease-workflow status is separate from the command result.
- WebKit layout-boundary proof reproduces clipping without the compatibility rule and verifies visible wide tables with it. Disclosed tables remain contained. This is CSS boundary proof, not a full Safari application tour.

- Independent review identified the WebKit paint boundary and an unnecessary minimum width on small tables; both findings are addressed and covered by focused proof. The subsequent percentage-width correction also passed a fresh independent review with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

title: fix(decisions): preserve fallback on provider input rejection
body:
Related: #155131

## What Problem This Solves

TypeSafe HTTP input rejections currently count as provider failures, so repeated invalid or oversized requests can open the shared circuit and block a later valid evaluation.

## User Impact

HTTP **413** (Content Too Large) and documented **422** request validation now return the existing `unavailable / unsupported-input` result. Consumers can keep their normal behavior, and those input rejections do not poison provider health. A 422 is **not** labeled as confirmed context overflow.

The consumer supplies bounded useful evidence and makes **one ordinary Decision call** under the existing deadline. There is no preflight token estimate, required model metadata, truncation, retry, alternate model/provider, or new public SDK option/type/export. Cancellation, closed authority and programming/contract errors remain terminal. Stock ONNX already returns `unsupported-input` for overlength input and its production code/limits are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing provider and Decision-runtime owners rather than a new admission framework. TypeSafe error bodies remain canceled without reading them because they can reflect credentials or submitted state. HTTP 401/403 authentication, 429 rate limits, ambiguous 400/404/415 responses and server/transport failures retain their existing classifications.

Shared DEBUG logs contain only outcomes/reasons, dispatch status, elapsed time, supplied JSON bytes/question count, actual reported usage, hashed identifiers and existing trace correlation. JSON bytes are not tokens. Logs do not retain submitted text, criteria, credentials or arbitrary error bodies; DEBUG-off adds no input serialization. Warnings say only that input was rejected and are rate limited. Caller effects remain explicitly unobserved.

This forward cleanup **supersedes the estimated-admission prototype**. The public Decision SDK, original capability metadata, catalog/protocol and registration shapes have **zero net delta versus the base**. The separate provider-budget lane and its SDK-approval request are canceled. No prefilter changes are included.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `f880e116d92eb513c083f3c19adb00fb42c6fe14`; merged base `a5f1d0996a1f80a789628af19ec304c08369607b`, tree `384a909bfc95720fbd21e1ab86405c33c76dd9b5`. This ancestry-preserving refresh incorporates the landed [Codex settlement fixture timer repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d1a3a33acc1ca10d2e8f4cb3bf4a24a3d104ab18). Main ancestry and actual source were verified: real timers are restored before releasing the held transcript writer. The repaired predecessor CI ran the same 12-file group successfully (107 tests, including all 17 settlement cases). The prior `f922a659` CI failed in this fixture; its two earlier failing jobs passed. [Fresh exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35938784414) is running; predecessor proof is not claimed as this head's green CI.

The introduced **11-file / +373 −17** patch is unchanged (stable patch ID `9aea5e06b1a0d516d8f8277130fa5e6be17ef240`). Decision, TypeSafe, ONNX, public SDK, logger/trace, core tool and registry/runtime helper bytes match `f922a659`. Main's package changes concern a Windows test command and a WebAwesome UI patch, not model dependencies. The original HTTP and stock-ONNX proof bindings below remain historical evidence; no model inference proof, SDK change, budget/provider lane, full build or independent CLI review was repeated for this mechanical refresh.

- **Fresh combined-source checks:** 293 tests passed across 19 explicit Decision/runtime, core-tool, TypeSafe and ONNX sibling files in **45.16 s**. Core and extension production types passed (13.22 s / 17.99 s); focused typed lint reported zero warnings/errors; all 11 changed files passed formatting and `git diff --check`. These are scoped regression tests, not a new live model trial.
- The prior `f922a659` refresh passed its 198-test selection and repeated the registered native-HTTP recovery trace: **6 calls / 6 HTTP requests**, four 413/422 fallbacks and successful same-host recovery with private-body-safe logs. That trace is reused, not relabeled as fresh-head execution.
- On the prior `fc14af21d277467eaab58b09defe73604cbf8457` head, core and extension production/test types, focused lint, SDK exports/surface guards, import-boundary guard, full build and documentation link checks passed. A strict consumer of generated SDK declarations accepts ordinary calls and rejects the removed policy/cause fields.
- Prior independent AutoReview and ClawSweeper Revision 4 on `f922a659c0dc4d191a2593fa1b9ce7ff3ca56ecd` found no actionable/blocking defects (Before merge: None). Their patch review is reused for this mechanical, patch-identical refresh; a fresh dispatch is not a completed substantive review.

Related: #156680.

## User Impact

The prebuilt setup declares the existing shared assets contract in the root Vitest context as well as the UI peer context. The UI module remains the single owner of the payload shape. All new imports and declarations erase at runtime; no guards or payload checks change.

title: fix: keep failed update report uploads in the CLI
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an unsuccessful update-failure report upload exits the interactive CLI, forcing users to rerun lengthy Doctor/update diagnostics before trying again.

## User Impact

Users keep their completed diagnostics and sanitized report in the action menu. After a known failed submission, they can explicitly retry or choose **Report in browser**, including when the GitHub CLI is missing. An uncertain submission offers **Check report status** without creating another issue or offering a browser handoff.

Successful reporting, explicit exit/cancellation, and noninteractive behavior retain their existing behavior. No new reporting service or configuration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the prepared report in the existing interactive loop and let the existing receipt owner decide whether publication is safe. Status reconciliation cannot become a fresh submission when a receipt is missing. A transport exception after publication was admitted retains the uncertain outcome, so the next action remains a status check even if the receipt disappears.

The final report owner also preserves main’s prepared-receipt projection and shared `recordCreatedIssue` handling. The temporary result module is removed; the existing owner retains the publication-admitted uncertainty rule and status-only reconciliation.

This changes the updater containing the fix; it cannot change an already-running older updater. Update execution, rollback, and diagnostic work are unchanged.

The published v2026.9.6 [failure-triage caller](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-triage.ts#L33) captures the reporting handler before running the update and calls that retained handler after failure. That caller and the [receipt store](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b/src/infra/update-failure-report-receipt-store.ts) are byte-identical in this candidate. An older updater therefore keeps its old menu for its current invocation; the new choices apply when the candidate CLI is subsequently invoked. There is no new receipt format or candidate-side callback that the old updater must discover.

## Evidence

- Causal checks on the original candidate failed the browser/status menu cases and showed that a missing-receipt status call could create an issue. The additional thrown-upload regression failed directly on the missing status action before its owner-level fix.
- The real Doctor flow, update failure handler, report preparation, durable SQLite receipts, and shared GitHub transport are exercised with CLI process responses mocked. Diagnostics run once across attempts; report bytes are retained; browser handoff needs no host CLI; uncertain sends never issue a second POST.
- On the candidate composed with fixed main `3fb84b0522092a363ec7efb4bbf9d269a477e767`, **158 tests passed across seven files** with one worker per shard in **102.45s**. This covers the Doctor and CLI menus, real receipt/transport boundaries, and Gateway reconnect sibling.
- The first published CI exposed the Gateway reconnect fixture’s obsolete always-report choice as an 8 GB worker OOM. Its scripted choice now exits the retained pending menu; all 46 sibling tests pass and their receipt/privacy/reconnect assertions remain intact. The original six-file run also passed 112 tests before main composition.
- All **31 selected changed-scope checks passed** on the final three-path repair, including production typechecking, all 25 selected test type graphs, core lint, formatting, runtime import cycles, all three dead-export scans, and owner guards. `git diff --check` passed. The initial nonstaged ratchet invocation compared the uncommitted merge against its older common ancestor; the supported `--staged` invocation checked the sealed candidate against the selected main revision. No source or baseline exception was needed.
- A later textual conflict with main’s report-owner simplification was resolved in the existing owner, without changing dependencies. The source-only three-way merge against main `163cd10bfa831c47c02c697248e9f6c1fe2d0c64` is clean; final integration still requires the new head’s CI.
- The repair’s first focused run exposed two existing expiry fixtures polling for asynchronous validation with Vitest’s one-second default. Both now await the existing deferred validation-start signal, retain the exact assertions, settle their owned submission, and restore the clock. The failed run is retained. Before the final promise-gate consolidation, **99 infra/transport/CLI tests passed in 92.62s** in their original shard order. The next selected check caught a five-line test-file overage; reusing the existing deferred-promise helper removes six lines without weakening assertions or changing the limit. All **65 affected infra tests then passed in 51.51s** on the final fixture; the unchanged **34 CLI** tests from the preceding run are reused. The unchanged Doctor **13** and Gateway **46** tests passed before the earlier infra failure and are reused.
- Fresh independent review of the full repaired candidate and a further scoped review of the final promise-gate consolidation: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The fresh manual CI run [36034827210](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36034827210) passed all five type stripes and the central type tail, resolving the earlier 20-minute selection timeout. It exposed three existing maintenance fixture races on the old branch: two one-second startup polls and a 50 ms disposal assertion. - Main subsequently refined the foreign-maintenance fixture to race its startup signal against the owned deferred promises. Its status assertion then used internal executor IDs instead of the released persisted keys. The helper now expects `global update` and `global update (omit optional)`, matching the existing ledger writer; both `ENOENT` assertions and every retention/status-only check remain intact. Syntax, formatting, scoped lint, and fresh P2 review passed. The final artifact-only run below completes the uncertain-status and preservation assertions without a product rebuild. Both failed runs are retained.

- Final [Package Acceptance 36070651960](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36070651960) **passed**. Harness `d5d9040f` consumed the original byte-identical `d522e200` tarball (`f1a560b62fb9761c97af9a5696940b8001dd5e255c529663e4a152a637c2a9c8`). Published 9.6 replacement succeeded, then both actual candidate CLI failure flows passed. Retry made exactly two POSTs with identical report content; uncertain submission made one POST and two status lookups, offered no repost/browser action, and retained the exact report bytes. Both flows kept exit code 1 and preserved the installed application payload, config, and synthetic operator note. The report phase took **32.058s**; the full survivor lane took **432s**, with cleanup joined. title: fix(ui): old interrupted requests appear below recent replies
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes old interrupted or cancelled requests appearing below recent replies, making conversation history look out of order.

## User Impact

Saved attempts appear in the **existing composer queue**, with aligned status badges and explicit **Send / Discard** actions. Expand a row to inspect and copy its text or view available attachments. There is no separate panel or automatic replay.

**Search is preserved:** an explicit, nonblank conversation search still finds matching loaded saved attempts, with their original source identity and status. Clearing or closing search restores queue-only presentation; it does not put saved attempts back into the normal conversation.

Saved rows do not execute or change queue order. Native held/failed messages keep their existing recovery controls. Send accepts complete user-authored text through normal admission and preserves the draft; system/forwarded inputs stay read-only. Discard hides this viewer’s queue row in this browser—it does not cancel work or delete retained content.

**Limit:** server-only media or structured/incomplete payloads cannot be resent safely and fail visibly rather than sending a partial prompt. No Gateway schema, retention, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Owner-selected design:** Queue-native placement is the default requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, who also requested landing. Explicit search remains available.

Separate inactive saved presentation from executable queue ownership. The existing custody owner retains active-custody discovery and receipt retirement, including accepted requests that are running rather than waiting in the queue. This fixes stale-page duplicate Send and hidden held-row controls without changing the scheduling/drain engine.

The previous review’s search-compatibility concern is addressed by retaining the existing search path, not by accepting a loss of search. Matching pending results keep the existing no-reply/no-rewind guards. Queue placement remains the requested default.

## Evidence

**Local correction — not yet published; this PR remains at `8218a2a0751`:** a failed or volatile browser send must not permanently hide the retained Gateway attempt. Local admission and native held/failed handoff now suppress only the current client’s duplicate row. Persistent retirement waits for a qualifying current Gateway acknowledgment; receipt-free `in_flight`, terminal errors and stale connections do not qualify. Explicit Discard remains browser-persistent. A later native Retry/reconnect can conservatively reoffer the original saved attempt in a fresh client rather than silently lose it.

- **Current integrated recovery proof:** 999/999 tests across 14 queue/send/custody/attachment/camera/handoff files pass (54.62 s wrapper). Three real admission/outbox cross-tab-loss regressions failed before correction. Current accepted ACK, terminal/transport failure, receipt-free preregistration, stale epochs, same-client duplicate prevention, FIFO barriers and draft preservation remain covered.
- The complete integrated PR source and added fixture delta have independent P0/P1 scoped-clean reviews. UI production and affected test types, scoped lint, formatting and unchanged performance limits pass. Existing visual evidence below remains applicable; this correction does not redesign the queue.
- **Browser fixture ownership:** adapted only the initial-document setup from @steipete’s [maintainer proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159549), not its broader refactor. The real sandbox receives the intended document on its initial navigation. The original **1,000 ms readiness poll**, source checks, opaque sandbox, auth/epoch checks and navigation/order assertions remain. Seven fixture cases and the complete **115-file / 1,465-test Chromium suite pass** (46.60 s). A wrong-document control fails at 1,000.9 ms with zero navigation. This does **not** establish the original concurrent timing cause of [#159679](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159679).
- Earlier roster, attachment, tooling-fixture and MCP lifecycle prerequisites reuse their canonical main fixes. Ordered MCP predecessor/consumer proof passed both targeted cases and all 134 sibling cases on verified isolated source; main integration retains that fix without PR-specific production MCP changes.

**Publication prerequisite remains unmet:** local candidate `de5577e956b4` is committed and reviewed; this PR still points to `8218a2a0751`. Native build and full static checks pass. The latest [verified-source Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449754111) failed the existing `agent-bundle-mcp-retention.test.ts` at its 180,000 ms deadline. Native publication then refused with `Missing required artifact: .local/gates.env`. No full-suite pass, new publication, or merge is claimed.

The same retention source passed in 136,112 ms in the preceding prepared-head run; that does not prove a fix. A bounded local original-entry probe hit the separate 120,000 ms no-output watchdog. Proof-only nested tracing preserved both deadlines and exposed a 60,000 ms inner optional-memory timeout before observed inference HTTP traffic. Explicit projection settlement completed but did not repair that wait. The underlying cause remains unresolved; no speculative production change, timeout increase, test skip, or unchanged full-run retry was used. Diagnostic source copies are removed, and task-owned validation allocations are stopped/completed.

A preceding run exposed stale lifecycle-error mocks in two state-lease test files. Reused the exact [canonical main repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fa63d9bb844b823ee07644ef6f0ab6d09accf3b4): eight redundant mock lines removed, both result blobs match upstream, and all 12 cases pass under the native configuration (5.58 s). Existing assertion, expiry, scope, cleanup and forbidden-storage guards remain intact; lint and independent P0/P1 review pass.

<details>
<summary>Earlier failed validation attempts and their disposition</summary>

The f1878 run passed 32,806 tests in five completed suites but recorded tooling-fixture failures before an outer two-hour interruption; it was not green. Missing fixture dependencies and packaged-worker setup were repaired from upstream and 588 owner tests passed. A later run exposed three MCP global-manager lifecycle failures; original order reproduced the defect, the canonical owner repair was adopted, and ordered isolated proof passed. The 57c2 run passed native build/check but failed the plugin-frame readiness helper before navigation assertions. Bounded unchanged replays did not prove a fix; the narrow initial-document fixture repair above preserves the original deadline. Each interrupted/failed task-owned Testbox was stopped and verified terminal. No retries, longer assertion deadlines, skipped tests, raised baselines, or fabricated gate receipts were used to conceal these failures.

</details>

- **1,956 tests passed across all 36 direct custody/thread/search consumers** on published head `8218a2a0751` (integrating main `8e57f5447ed`) (29.08 s wrapper wall, one worker per shard). Redundant mocked paths and implementation-only assertions were removed; added regressions protect reproduced failures rather than implementation details.
- Real outbox regressions cover FIFO, draft/attachment preservation, held barriers, native retry across reconnect, and rejection of internal/system provenance before I/O. Eight stale-page cases cover ID/run matching before/during reads, for waiting and running custody.
- Independent review exposed two further failures, both reproduced before repair: older-page browsing could hide a running input, and cancelled custody could conceal a late-restored held owner. The existing pagination regression now covers waiting/running display and interrupted/cancelled native recovery. A separate boundary check confirms stale same-input replies are reread while a fresh cancellation still retires live custody.
- Actual source UI in Chromium passes durable Discard, full-message inspection, explicit Send, offline reorder → reconnect → FIFO delivery, and saved-search matching/nonmatching/clearing. Searching sends or aborts nothing and keeps the draft and ordinary queue intact.
- The saved-search notice regression failed before the repair, then passed. Focused independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues in that delta. Existing system-notice identity and normal-transcript omission remain covered.
- Exact UI-chat test types, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, scoped lint, formatting, style/i18n checks, production build and explicit performance check pass. Startup JS is **372,326 B**, within the current-main **372,347 B** limit, with no budget or baseline exception. title: fix: apply shared plugin model policy to decisions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin Decision calls can bypass the consumer model restrictions that already apply to ordinary plugin completions.

## User Impact

Decision calls now enforce the registered consumer’s existing `llm.allowedCompletionModels` before provider dispatch. The released V1 contract remains intact: agent-owned work supplies its owning `agentId`; omission selects the global Decision role. Neither case requires a new override permission or falls back to a conversational model. No model defaults change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both completion paths use one model-policy owner. Host and plugin restrictions intersect, and request fields cannot impersonate another plugin’s authority. Ordinary LLM agent-override policy, operator model policy, and lifecycle checks remain intact.

The earlier review’s owner-agent compatibility finding is resolved: a Decision runtime is bound to its consumer, not to an agent. Applying the LLM override guard there incorrectly rejected the owner-agent call documented in the released `DecisionRuntimeV1` API. This branch preserves that contract while enforcing the selected model’s consumer allowlist.

Prerequisite https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156554 is merged; this PR targets main. Original contributor history is retained. Design and requirements contributed by Vincent Koc and Peter Steinberger.

## Evidence

Candidate: `bff869544e661feab68ed061698bbea68f72dbab`.

- 114 tests passed across Decision runtime, shared policy, ordinary and isolated LLM completion, and operator-policy siblings. Registered calls cover owner selection with override permission absent/false/true, omitted global selection, disabled roles, denial before dispatch, spoofed consumer identity, wildcard intersections, cancellation and revocation.
- Focused production/test typecheck, typed lint, formatting, privacy and whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. A separate contract audit verified the owner-agent API against release `v2026.10.4`; the root review checked its actual registry adapter and selection owner.
- The unchanged shared-policy extraction previously passed the SDK strict-smoke build, declarations, CLI import guard and 155 SDK subpaths. The focused test runner rebuilt its affected compiled-worker generation. Full exact-head PR CI is the broad gate.
- Production net +141 lines, tests +194, docs +16. The shared owner removes duplicated policy from the LLM caller and applies it at the Decision boundary.

Registered-host proof uses synthetic providers; it establishes policy and dispatch behavior, not provider quality or live vendor availability.

title: feat(models): allow multiple aliases for one model

Adding a second shortcut name for a model currently replaces the name users already rely on.

Models can have several case-insensitive aliases while existing `alias` configurations keep working. CLI writes and provider setup preserve existing names, settings, and alias targets. Additional names work in `/model`, shorthand commands, policy validation, and Doctor/runtime routing.

title: refactor: explore removing Tasks and TaskFlow
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Explore removing the generalized Tasks/TaskFlow layer instead of maintaining a second execution and lifecycle ledger alongside Cron, subagents, ACP, media generation, and sessions.

## User Impact

**Large-change review:** @steipete approved the documented review-size exception; `size: accepted-large` is applied and the original draft is reopened. This does not waive the merge blockers below.

**Exploratory draft—not ready to merge.** Removes the Tasks page/rail, CLI, RPC/events, TaskFlow APIs, and TaskFlow-only Webhooks plugin. Cron execution/history, session controls, native subagent delivery/cancellation, media operations, and Workboard session-based planning remain. Removed integrations intentionally break; there is no automatic workflow conversion.

Following the [approved storage-retirement decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156532#issuecomment-5798987497), **shared schema 19 drops `task_delivery_state`, `task_runs`, and `flow_runs`** after preserving retained Cron history and provably bound released native subagent outcomes. Only Task/flow lifecycle bindings are removed; independent audit facts, Cron bindings, native sessions/results/receipts, recovery archives, and unrelated data remain. History does not become execution authority. Unknown dependencies refuse migration rather than risk unrelated data.

**Upgrade/rollback:** main’s shared schema 18 and agent schema 23 are preserved. Existing old-updater content/publication deferral remains intact. A downgrade after retirement requires a verified pre-migration backup, not lowered schema markers. No live database has been migrated.

**Known merge blocker:** initial native Codex children that have not reached requester completion admission still lack a durable replacement for the removed cold/cross-parent recovery path. Gateway restart or native-parent replacement can lose that completion obligation. Preserved accepted follow-up receipts and admitted completion recovery do not close this gap; this draft does not claim restart-equivalent behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surviving responsibilities stay with their native owners. Cron owns a small history table with its existing identities, details, partitions, and retention; native subagents retain completion/cancellation custody. A fenced atomic migration extracts supported historical outcomes before retiring the generalized tables. Obsolete persistence, repairs, runtime projections, and Tasks-only tests are removed instead of renamed.

Validation also repaired native wait ordering: published facts no longer discard pending read/cleanup custody, and cancellation joins that work before returning. Native admission again preserves persistence-failure context and refuses untracked dispatch. No new lifecycle ledger was introduced.

Published head: `22c5772d632d57a17c5068295a5fcc5b5ea02ae6` (the publisher’s metadata commit has the exact reviewed source tree). The candidate integrates pinned main `264c3355f0d5db50c223f286df21c8f9e437049d`; GitHub still reports conflicts with newer main, which must be resolved before merge. It also repairs retained Cron transcript sizing and keeps main’s attribution, accessible roles, and close-focus behavior. Page-owned styles no longer get absorbed into measured JavaScript boot groups; no styles, size budgets, or baselines were relaxed.

- Schema/history/audit proof: **156 tests / 7 files passed**, including retirement, released-outcome extraction, rollback/refusal, publication deferral, and read-only admission.
- Native recovery/cancellation closure: **228 tests / 5 files passed**, 49.73s wall. Gateway admission/continuation closure: **337 tests / 2 files passed**, 65.31s. These include the real failed wait/publication/abort boundaries, durable replacement rollback, persistence refusal, and the original registry ordering.
- Broader Cron, Gateway, backup/update and native suites were exercised in selected batches, not the full repository suite. Native archive E2E: **25 tests passed**, 33.23s Vitest plus a 363.7s runtime build. Synthetic Codex retry-policy fixture: **19 tests passed**. All cited runtime batches used `--maxWorkers=1`. Integration builds passed; final package/old-updater proof is separate.
- Canonical UI build and performance checks passed. Largest/startup CSS is **51,144 bytes gzip**; all budgets unchanged. The bundle regression fails on the original style owner. **27 focused tests / 2 files passed** (9.74s wall), with production-bundle Chromium smoke for new/chat/plugins.
- Native locale cleanup carried all existing translations through the owning generator: **zero translation/model calls**. Canonical protocol, SDK, database types/inventory, and localization artifacts were regenerated; docs link audit passed.
- Actual-source synthetic UI captures were inspected and delivered in chat: [initial removal comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156532#issuecomment-5795714072) and [retained Cron transcript comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156532#issuecomment-5804126330). Both pairs are embedded in GitHub.

**Published 9.2 acceptance passed:** [Package Acceptance attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35950915786) completed successfully in **36m51s**, with workflow, tooling, frozen admission, and package source all bound to `22c5772d632d57a17c5068295a5fcc5b5ea02ae6`. The actual installed `2026.9.2` updater upgraded to candidate `2026.9.5`/schema 19. The single `legacy-operator-state` lane passed, including the corrected already-current no-op, clean Doctor, formerly-bundled-plugin Doctor, and subsequent completion checks. Nine jobs passed; 15 unselected jobs were skipped and are not coverage.

The inspected [published proof artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35950915786/artifacts/10790140029) records `passed` / `published-updater-import-preserved`: two retained history rows, the import receipt, and unrelated state were preserved; retired Task/Flow tables and indexes were absent; content schema 19 coexisted with published markers 15 while the old updater remained active. The qualifying Doctor already saw migrated content on entry, so this is preservation proof—not a claim that this particular Doctor first migrated it. No-op/Doctor outcomes are backed by executed source assertions, phase receipts, and successful log markers; their raw standalone reports are not separately published. Backup rollback is not applicable to the 9.2 lane.

The [harness-only no-op correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e1540139144e59cd385aae39428c1474fe2cbe4b) fixed the first run’s advisory misclassification without changing runtime code. Native source updates spend unnecessary CPU time validating large bundled worker artifacts.

## User Impact

Speeds up native build validation without skipping any build step, declaration output, syntax check, or import check. No configuration or update protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Walk the same own enumerable AST properties without allocating a two-element key/value array for every property. - **Serialized ABBA benchmark on the identical complete native build:** baseline 35.07 s / 37.29 s, candidate 32.61 s / 32.32 s. Mean 36.18 to 32.46 s: **3.72 s / 10.3% less guard wall time**. Every run exits 0 with identical stdout and empty stderr. This is a guard-stage improvement, not a measured whole-update percentage.
- Complete `OPENCLAW_BUILD_CACHE=0 pnpm build` succeeds: 327.99 s wall. Unified declarations 147.4 s, SDK declarations 59.0 s, guard 32.2 s, packages 28.9 s, runtime 19.5 s, UI 13.9 s; export, postbuild and UI budget checks all run.
- Output equivalence: all **13,386 regular dist files plus 303 symlink entries**, including **443 declaration files**, retain identical SHA-256 bytes or symlink targets before/after all four guard runs. Manifest SHA-256: `ce16e6ac34b07c21104062cb477c3ca8848dbe9f0bcd78d0a80e917d2fdad176`. The changed script is read-only; generators and profiles are unchanged.
- Environment: Linux x64 7.0.0-31-generic; 32 logical AMD EPYC-Milan CPUs; 128792484 KiB RAM; Node 26.8.2; pnpm 12.4.0; pinned Acorn 8.18.0; isolated physical frozen dependency installation. Fresh runtime artifacts total approximately 102 MB across seven deploy entries. Source baseline f66f68271fd; exact candidate source a5f04e5e8c9. Coverage includes nested imports/require/createRequire, module syntax errors, duplicate bindings/exports, forward exports, string/comment exclusions, and complete build-step selection. title: fix: Gateway fixture cleanup races participant persistence
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway fixture cleanup racing accepted participant writes after a request has finished.

## User Impact

No user-visible feature or configuration change. Best-effort participant bookkeeping no longer keeps a completed Gateway request active, while shutdown and test cleanup still join the persistence they own. Schemas, retention, and write authorization are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request-root completion is not a storage completion signal. Participant persistence remains tracked by its async work scope; fixture retirement now joins the canonical agent writer queue without rejecting pending writes. Directory-scoped cleanup drains only its own stores, keeps their selectors until writes settle, and preserves the existing read-context disposal. The drain lives in test support rather than adding a test-only production export.

## Evidence

### Observed after-change behavior

Proof is applicable and executed, using isolated Gateway state rather than a live operator deployment. At this PR head, the [real SQLite retirement regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f7d8db39f62c49f64f6bfebfc9556905f7aaa1f/src/gateway/test-helpers.server-rpc.test.ts#L202-L237) passed with these observations:

1. Hold the canonical agent writer, queue a real participant write, and start fixture retirement.
2. While that write is blocked, the Gateway root count is **0**, and **both store selectors still point to the original store**.
3. Release the writer. The persistence result is **fulfilled / inserted**; retirement then leaves the selector unset and the database absent from the open-handle registry.

The [participant lifetime regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f7d8db39f62c49f64f6bfebfc9556905f7aaa1f/src/sessions/session-participant-recording.test.ts#L35-L94) separately proves root release while its tracked async scope still waits, for both persistence success and rejection. Its persistence callback is mocked; the retirement regression above uses the real SQLite path.

Latest local execution excerpts:

```text
PASS participant persistence resolves without retaining caller root (65 ms)
PASS participant persistence rejects without retaining caller root (1 ms)
PASS fixture release joins queued participant persistence before deselecting its store (689 ms)
```

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35819090116) completed successfully: **144 successful jobs**, with **17 skipped jobs excluded from passing proof**. The [required CI/security gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35820008586) also completed successfully. CodeQL was neutral, not counted as success.

### Regression coverage and static checks

- Both regression checks failed before the fix: participant work retained a request root after its caller released it; fixture retirement deselected a store with a real participant write still queued.
- Current integrated candidate: **154 focused tests pass**, including the participant regression, Gateway storage-retirement tests, and the larger chat fixture suite.
- Full `agentic-control-plane-agent-chat` plan through `scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts`, default scheduling/forks: **81 files / 1,165 tests pass twice**, in **230.79 s** and **220.86 s**. No timeout increases or worker-policy changes.
- Earlier focused agent-a/chat/auth-refresh trio: **105 tests pass**. Persistence/queue sibling selection: **37 tests pass**.
- New real-write regression measured **0.942 s** in the existing Gateway suite; the 12-test fixture file took **13.42 s** with one worker. Participant resolve/reject cases took **2 ms / 1 ms**. No extra Gateway boot was added per case.
- Fresh independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Line-cap and dead-export guards pass. The full current-base `pnpm check:changed --base 0e79899fedc26ae9a90a196a8bc41b97fd39d7e5` run **passed**, including all selected typechecks, lint, dead-export scans, and guards. GitHub CI and review remain enforced merge gates.

Local proof ran on Linux/Node 26 in the isolated task worktree. Initial unrelated mock-provider/CLI failures reproduced with ambient host settings: proxying loopback returned HTTP 502, and an inherited Gateway password changed token-only CLI auth-mode classification. The controlled rerun passed all nine affected tests after removing that password only from the test process and setting `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` to `127.0.0.1,localhost`; external proxy settings and authorization checks remain intact. No unrelated production workaround was added.

Medium default, saved-off→adaptive/low, and omitted display through both adapters were verified without rewriting requests. Isolated home removal and lease release were verified.

The original alias regression failed through both registered setup paths; an independently identified legacy/canonical collision also failed before repair. title: fix: chat turns fail when session state is briefly busy
body:
Related: #155975

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat turn can fail with a raw storage error when opening a cold session database overlaps state-lifecycle contention.

## User Impact

User impact: brief contention can clear while the original turn waits, without sending another message; longer contention produces a calm warning with Check status and expandable, redacted details. Stop remains available.

This does not automatically replay an interrupted turn. The historical incident's exact holder and acquisition callsite remain unknown; the reproduction below establishes a specific reachable cold-admission defect, not that historical cause.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cold reply admission used a synchronous native acquisition that could prevent the host from servicing the work needed to release contention. Admission now waits asynchronously at the physical database owner's acquisition boundary. Each request retains one bounded five-second acquisition budget, independent cancellation, and request/storage authority checks, even when physical preparation is shared. The operation itself and cleanup are not retried. The host-side native acquisition waits share that retry policy. Their retained worker cleanup does not require new-read admission; the request owners still validate new operations. The executing worker’s newer checked late-custody delegate handoff from main is preserved unchanged.

Reported by and implemented at the request of @jalehman.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/767cab96-667e-4062-85ef-1639fb0f12c7)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/e66496e6-5418-4afa-90d9-3d1a63c3a909)

## Evidence

Before

![Before: raw contention failure during cold admission](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6a771ce-68b5-4cdf-92a9-0279c83033ae)

After

![After: the original turn resumes exactly once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9490ed4-dd39-4bca-8277-9706322fbf6d)

### Behavior videos

The refreshed recording uses the integrated runtime at `bcf8fc40375` plus the fresh, lockfile-built Workboard manifest subsequently committed in `09172c28033`—the only source-tree difference. title: feat(discord): require direct bot tags for guild messages
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord operators need an option that admits ordinary guild messages only when someone tags the bot directly, rather than through reply pings or other mention shortcuts.

## User Impact

User impact: Set `requireMention: "explicit"` on a Discord guild or channel to require a literal bot user tag in message content, including in threads. Existing `true` and `false` behavior remains unchanged; native slash commands and interactions retain their separate access checks. Existing installations require no deployment or configuration migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord message preflight checks the raw inbound message text for an unescaped bot user tag outside Markdown code before normal mention admission. The mode takes channel precedence over guild policy and cannot be bypassed by text commands, reply metadata, broadcast mentions, or auto/bound threads. The public schema, config hints and documentation expose the new value; the shared group policy still receives a boolean.

## Evidence

- Focused Discord schema, policy, preflight and monitor tests: 225 passed (4 files; wall 16.14s, maxWorkers=1).
- Core, extension and extension-test TypeScript checks passed; config metadata generation check, docs config examples, formatting, lint and `git diff --check` passed.
- CI on the reviewed head [`79945e0`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35806409842) completed: 133 successful jobs, 16 skipped, no failed jobs; required `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded. Earlier CI exposed config-baseline, line-cap, assertion-ratchet, and public SDK export-count failures; the branch now passes their exact checks.
- Latest focused repair validation: 179 Discord tests across four files passed (22.18s wall); the extracted explicit-mention suite alone passed 10 tests (8.025s wall, maxWorkers=1). Extension production/test types, config-docs baseline, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets, and SDK surface count/test passed.
- AutoReview on final exact head `79945e0` with the unchanged raw-tag parser supplied as context returned P1 scoped-clean. A prior dirty-tree review flagged escaped/code tokens, but the parser excludes both and the preflight tests reject both. No live Discord connection was exercised; validation uses the Discord preflight boundary.

## Compatibility and owner decision

Existing `requireMention: true`/`false` configurations and defaults remain accepted; there is no stored-config migration. The shipped Plugin SDK types `DiscordGuildChannelConfig` and `DiscordGuildEntry` expose these fields, so TypeScript readers must now discriminate `boolean | "explicit"` (for boolean policy, treat `"explicit"` as `true`). SDK and security owner acceptance of this source-incompatible type widening is **still pending**; this PR must not merge before that decision.

Contributor credit: Vito (VACInc).

title: fix(test): wait for participant writes before asserting idle roots
body:
Related: #155164 (CI investigation only; its branch is unchanged).

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway tests can report an extra active request root after an agent command finishes because legitimate deferred participant-history persistence has not finished yet.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This is test-only: production persistence, root ownership, cancellation, and timeout semantics are unchanged.

**Validation limitation:** the three targeted cases pass, but the original full shard still has six other failures. Two additional chat-case failures remain causally unresolved; this PR does not claim a green full shard or that those failures are unrelated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The trace shows the RPC and agent-execution references being released while participant persistence still holds the last request-root reference. It eventually releases normally, after the original test polling deadline.

Use the existing async-work scope in a test observer to join real participant recording before sampling the unchanged root count. The observer neither fakes writes nor releases roots. It changes the fixture's async-work scope, not Gateway's separate root-admission context; it proves settlement, not successful persistence or shutdown behavior. An existing agent-send assertion block is extracted to respect the chat test's file-growth guard.

Production delta: **0**. Tests/support: **+41 / −15, net +26** across four files. No timeout increase, retries, worker pin, serial configuration, or production test seam.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixes cramped long skill names in the chat composer's Skills menu without making those names unreadable on touch screens.

## User Impact

Touch-capable and no-hover layouts show the complete name by wrapping it before a tap changes the skill. Skill enablement and permissions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the Skills list and its selected-skill actions a shared viewport-bounded 320px width, remove unused icon space, and preserve separators in long menus. Restrict the single-line presentation by input capability rather than screen width; long unbroken identifiers can also wrap on touch. Preserve main's checkbox accessibility and inert decorative switches.

title: fix(ui): composer hides behind the mobile keyboard
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Addresses a viewport-layout gap that can hide the Control UI message composer when a phone keyboard opens. The reported symptom is intermittent in the Add to Home Screen standalone PWA, not in a browser tab.

## User Impact

Users can keep the composer and its actions above the keyboard while task progress and branch context remain in the normal footer. Keyboard close, viewport panning, rotation, and standalone safe-area spacing are preserved without shrinking the layout during pinch zoom. No configuration or migration is required.

The reporter’s intermittent standalone-PWA trigger has not been reproduced on a physical iPhone. Hosted Chromium proof uses an injected viewport contract and the actual standalone CSS rules; it verifies the layout response, not native iOS keyboard/event timing. Repeated keyboard activation and background/foreground recovery in the installed PWA remain unverified. Passing these tests does not establish that the reported intermittent symptom is fully resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell previously relied on viewport CSS units and `interactive-widget=resizes-content`, which do not cover visual-only keyboard resizing. The existing shell lifecycle now owns the visible height, including both standalone body insets. Removing the competing landscape transcript minimum lets the existing footer budget keep controls reachable.

## Evidence

**September 28 rebase and hosted verification:** current head `77aa7852d5f28936b9d3ca7871778b2abfdca8d9` preserves the reviewed nine-file patch on main `dd3fb2bd9cf2aedf1a86eebc388e4f3386b35b98`. Both requested coauthor trailers are present on all three rewritten commits. No merge, auto-merge, or deployment was performed.

[CI run 36416448790, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36416448790) reached a terminal **cancelled** result after an assertion failed and native fail-fast cancelled remaining work. Checkout logs and commit parents bind execution to merge `e41c5212380366c21d4c292b0e3e36be8e0c38ef`: tested base `2e37299b10dcb8e4825d4b5a67a6f40cc5af7ee0` plus this exact PR head. The overall CI gate is **not green**.

### Actual current-head test execution

| `chat-keyboard-viewport.e2e.test.ts` | 1 passed before shard cancellation | 1.530s test / 1.663s file | [E2E 8/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36416448790/job/108909442019) |
| `question-guest.e2e.test.ts` | 1 passed before shard cancellation | 7.197s test / 7.373s file | Same E2E 8/9 job |

| `shell-viewport.test.ts` | 7 passed; job succeeded | 18.77ms module | [UI 3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36416448790/job/108909441791) |
| `app-host-lifecycle.test.ts` | 2 passed; job succeeded | 152.16ms module | [UI 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36416448790/job/108909441802) |
| `chat-footer-layout.browser.test.ts` | 14 passed; job succeeded | 21.574s module | Same UI 2/3 job |

The keyboard and Guest-question passes are explicit log results recorded before cancellation, **not** a successful whole-shard claim. All three UI jobs succeeded. E2E 6/9 passed 411 tests across 80 files (451.48s Vitest duration). Module/file durations above are not job wall time.

Local validation after the rebase passed 23 viewport/lifecycle/footer tests across three files in **11.78s wall** (9.71s runner duration); UI types, scoped lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Two selected current wrapper-closure checks also passed; the old wrapper inventory failure is historical, not this run's failure. No redundant review was added for the patch-identical rebase; the prior independent review remains limited to its stated P0 scope.

### Remaining CI failure and investigation limit

[E2E 4/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36416448790/job/108909442290) failed `session-management.rename-composition.e2e.test.ts`, “keeps the rename draft during modern composition Escape until ordinary Enter.” At line 119 the rendered title remained `Original session` instead of `確定した名前` after the test observed the expected patch request, input detachment, and a later list request. The [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36416448790/job/108912879342) failed downstream; all 59 jobs settled (31 success, 2 failure, 5 cancellation, 21 skipped).

[Concurrent scheduled-main evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36416233754/job/108908250303), on the tested base's immediate parent, independently failed the same line-119 expected/actual title assertion in the **modern Enter** parameter case; its Escape case passed. The rename test, renderer, mutation owner, and fixture state implementation are unchanged by this PR. This supports an existing reconciliation failure signature, **but does not establish that the exact PR Escape-case failure is unrelated or fixed**.

The configured **blacksmith-testbox** route was available and used without a provider override: lease `tbx_01m3kyxfk03a9wsn5v74ptq026`, [hydration/lease run 36420402178](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36420402178), Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.5.1. Clean temporary checkouts compared the exact hosted merge `e41c5212…` and exact tested base `2e37299b…`. Candidate rename cases passed **5/5** (7.688s file); base passed **4/5**, failing the same final-title assertion in **legacy Enter**, not modern Escape (17.223s failing case / 24.496s file). Modern Escape passed on both. Both test subprocesses exited 1; the comparison driver completed collection successfully, which is not a test-pass claim.

No speculative product fix, weakened assertion, timeout increase, baseline change, blind CI rerun, or additional push was made. The bounded investigation did not establish a PR-related rename regression; the original CI gate remains red and exact modern-Escape causality remains unresolved. The 22 downloaded evidence files were hash-verified, and the owned Testbox lease was stopped with native status `completed`. title: fix(ui): guide setup before selecting unconfigured decision models
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes selecting an unconfigured Decision model without being offered provider setup, and missing decision-only providers in the connection picker.

## User Impact

Users can connect a Decision provider from either the model picker or **Connect provider**, using the same centered setup dialog. Canceling or a failed save preserves the previous selection; saving a key requires an explicit **Use** action before selecting the pending model. Provider-only setup never changes a model selection.

Credentials remain global to their plugin and are stored as protected references. **Configured** does not mean a key, local server, or model artifact was verified: setup does not make paid inference calls, download weights, or probe external services. Existing external credential references stay at their original source.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin-owned setup metadata and readiness now feed both entry points, including local-server and local-model guidance. A generic administrator-only credential operation uses the existing config publication owner and SQLite workers, checks live authority before mutation, and preserves exact rollback/CAS behavior. Successful saves remain successful when their own runtime refresh invalidates the connection.

Requested and shaped by Josh (@jalehman) and Vyctor (@vyctorbrzezowski).

title: feat(labs): add Decision assistance opt-in foundation
body:
Related: #155314, #155317

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic Decision experiments need one explicit, persisted opt-in that future consumer PRs can share without treating model selection as consent.

## User Impact

Settings → Labs gains a default-off Decision assistance switch. **Foundation only: no automatic consumers are connected, and enabling it starts no inference.** Saved opt-in remains visible without a model; each participating agent still needs an effective Decision model. Unreadable or stale configuration is shown as unknown, not disabled.

The explicit `decision_evaluate` tool is exempt and unchanged. Shared Decision execution, provider registration, credentials, downloads, consumer modes, and action authority are unchanged. This does not complete or close the broader integration issues.

## Why This Change Was Made

- UI and manual config share the optional Boolean `agents.defaults.experimental.decisionAssistance`. Only explicit `true` opts in. Off/reset preserves sibling settings and model selections.
- Core-only `isDecisionAssistanceEligible(config, agentId)` requires strict opt-in AND an effective model from `resolveDecisionModelSetting`, preserving inherited defaults and explicit empty agent overrides. It consumes prepared config and a trusted owning agent ID without provider probes, secret resolution, polling, or inference.
- Existing Labs patch/revision/refresh and save-generation handling remain the owners. No plugin SDK expansion or new Decision registry.
- The authorized Boolean intentionally raises the generated core config-field budget from 2454 to 2455.
- The consumer-free core module has a narrow Knip source entry. Remove this entry when the first automatic consumer imports the helper; no fake production invocation was added to satisfy unused-export checks.

## Evidence

Verification for source commit `dfba736e220f81992bc9e4281c35230c39c1a871` is reused, without rebasing or feature expansion.

title: fix(ui): keep mobile goal controls above expanded text
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: expanded mobile Goal controls sit below the objective and compete with token usage, making goal management hard to find and causing overlap on narrow phones. Paused goals also inherited warning styling despite being a normal stopped state.

## User Impact

Edit, Pause/Resume, and Clear appear as compact labeled buttons above the full goal text on narrow mobile screens, only while expanded. Paused goals use a neutral icon, label, border, and card surface instead of warning styling. Desktop controls and action permissions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the existing controls a full-width row instead of sharing the metadata row. Use 28px-minimum chips with short labels and wrapping space; keep usage and elapsed time below the objective and status note. Per the requester’s correction, exclude paused goals from the existing warning selectors; blocked and limited goals retain their warning treatment.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the 320px layout in the real Control UI using synthetic Gateway data: Clear overlapped token usage below a long objective. The controls existed in the DOM; this is a responsive layout repair, not a change to goal authorization.

title: improve(android): keep tool activity in one compact disclosure
body:
Closes #155466

## What Problem This Solves

Android expands live tools into a large panel, then replaces it with a separate completed-tool disclosure as history arrives.

## User Impact

Tool activity stays in one compact, expandable disclosure while work runs and results arrive. Expanded rows retain command output and live diff information; failures and blocked actions remain visible when collapsed. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The timeline now owns a single presentation over the existing separate live and transcript data sources. Turn-scoped disclosure keys, run-qualified call ownership, and a short-lived presentation bridge prevent duplicate rows and preserve expansion through delayed history, concurrent runs, and run-ID acknowledgement changes. Completed-turn **Worked for…** behavior stays intact.

Thanks to @IWhatsskill for the report and requested implementation.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @IWhatsskill](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/f9f3ae0c-d776-447c-8775-2274da72c9bc)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/79ea15ff-5f9c-4451-b824-aed4e257a06b)

## Evidence

- **194 focused Android tests passed** through `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest`: real ChatScreen interaction, timeline/history projection, concurrent/rekeyed run ownership, completed-work grouping, reader scrolling, and full-message ownership.
- Android `:app:ktlintCheck`, `:app:lintPlayDebug`, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent precommit review finished scoped-clean at P0/P1/P2 after the ownership/status findings were fixed.
- The first CI run caught two obsolete extraction sites left by removing the old live panel. The generated source inventory is now synchronized and `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes; the reviewed Android source is unchanged.
- Release-only strict translated/generated parity still reports the retired “No result” ID in existing locale artifacts. This PR follows the source-only localization gate described in `docs/ci/local-proof.md`; no translation/runtime resource refresh is claimed.
- The same real ChatScreen regression **fails on the original source** because live activity has no collapsed disclosure. It passes after the change, including expanded command output across tool completion/history refresh and collapsed blocked status.
- Native Compose/Robolectric captures below use the same 360 × 800 dp viewport and synthetic scene. **No physical Android device was attached; this is not a device or live-Gateway claim.**
- Targeted Gradle test invocation: **59 s wall**. Per-suite test time: controller replay 5.459 s; unified activity 0.003 s; real completed-work layout 9.071 s; timeline 0.028 s; tool result projection 0.011 s; Worked summary 0.008 s; reader layout 2.777 s; full-message ownership 25.363 s. The layout fixtures exercise actual runtime/Compose ownership that pure projection tests cannot cover.

### CI fixture correction

The [initial Play CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35740982682/job/106792303127) failed `SidebarGatewayPickerTest.stoppedVoiceNoteReleasesGatewaySwitchWithoutReleasingOtherImports` before recording began. The fixture sent its terminal event before asynchronous history adopted the screenshot run, so the controller correctly ignored that unowned event and recording remained unavailable.

A controlled delayed-history probe reproduced the same missing “Record voice note” assertion; waiting for run adoption and ViewModel retirement made both stopped/disposed scenarios pass. title: fix(test): preserve worker clocks during placement cleanup
body:
Related: #155357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent placement-cleanup validation failures when the fixture runs real SQLite workers while globally faking the parent clock. This is a maintainer-directed repair for the 2026.9.6 release campaign.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The existing cleanup, timeout, and recovery assertions keep their original coverage and limits.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only fake the provider timeout's `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` pair. Blanket fake timers reset the parent's `process.hrtime`, but the SQLite worker uses a real monotonic clock to evaluate cross-thread acquisition deadlines. That can turn brief lock contention into an immediate failure.

## Evidence

- Original failure: [CI placement-reclaim lifecycle job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35693131665/job/106634438390), `resume-owner-close`, `StateDatabaseCoordinatorContentionError`.

- Baseline replay also passed 164 tests; the historical timing-dependent failure did not recur, so this is not claimed as a red-green reproduction.
- Selected `check-changed` gate and `git diff --check` passed. Independent P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable findings.
- One test file, two additions / one deletion; no production changes, new tests, larger timeouts, weaker assertions, retries, or gate waivers.

Current PR CI also found two unrelated lint errors already present in the captured main base: async cleanup in `src/plugins/registry-registration-resources.ts:91` and fixture mapping in `src/plugins/registry-inspection-resources.test.ts:152`. [Failing lint job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35695354772/job/106641285788). Both were subsequently fixed on main by commit `0051fa8f8f3126c487c9cfc91284f105eac045dc`. This PR was rebased onto that exact commit to obtain corrected CI; `git range-diff` confirms the one-file placement patch is unchanged. Reviewed head: `db196b54481c416140701bdf4d23c79a9efd08e4`; [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35696576568) completed successfully with all 45 jobs completed and no failures. body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: retained document attachments disappear from model context after conversation replay, and workspace-only sessions cannot read uploads left outside their execution workspace.

## User Impact

Agents recover document text and PDF pages on later turns and retries. Local uploads are staged into the admitted execution workspace, including managed worktrees, without widening file-tool access.

**Before-merge decision:** plugin-host replay uses current read grants, not an attachment’s former workspace as an access grant. An inaccessible original file requires reattachment from a permitted location; managed uploads remain readable. Area-owner acceptance of this recovery contract is still pending. This PR is being prepared for review, not merged; no transcript migration or new permission setting is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing document extractor, staging owner, and canonical recorded-prompt projection. Keep saved text stable while recovering missing PDF pages. Carry exact page-to-attachment indexes from live preparation so replay does not confuse a saved text field, a paired retry, or an existing photo with available PDF bytes. Preserve media order, read denials, cancellation, and configured remote ownership.

## Evidence

- Candidate: `ea23bde5b24e22f99fea3e49114a2db226abe7b8`; current-main reconciliation: `b1c3004f73cad1c1b68786e592d025fcdc048f68`. The retired prompt marker stays removed.
