The original 58,602-byte plan and workspace-only read regressions remain covered.
- Fresh independent review of the full **17-file** candidate found **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. Review inspected source; test execution is reported separately. The [current-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155476#issuecomment-5771836649) has **no code/security findings** and **platinum-hermit patch quality (4/6)**. Its latest review requested stable-to-candidate compatibility proof; the new install-over result below addresses that request. The separately recorded area-owner decision remains explicit above.
- Core types, all 27 test-type graphs, typed lint, formatting, ratchets, and architecture guards passed. `pnpm build` passed in **286.53 s**, with a nonfatal Control UI startup-asset budget warning; this PR changes no UI source. The inherited Knip findings are recorded below. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38014591282) **passed: 46 successful and 24 skipped jobs**. The separate CI-gate, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses also passed. The PR is non-draft and conflict-free; no merge or auto-merge was requested.
- **Latest-stable install-over compatibility: passed, 2026-10-10.** Published `openclaw@2026.9.9` (`bcfc88812a35243893585dbeca87ca41b48272ca`) produced text, two-page vector-only PDF, and mixed photo/PDF conversations through its installed CLI and real Gateway. Candidate `ea23bde5b24e22f99fea3e49114a2db226abe7b8` was installed over the same prefix, HOME, profile, database, and workspace without reset/reseed. Doctor and a new Gateway process loaded the old sessions; all three continuations completed with readable histories. The provider received the text sentinel once, two PDF pages, and one photo followed by two PDF pages. All **28 original decoded transcript rows stayed byte-exact**; nine new rows were appended. Four session identities and tested settings were preserved.
- Earlier unit/harness rasterization was synthetic; the new installed-runtime proof used the shipped extractor and **real PDF rasterization**. Provider replies were mocked on isolated loopback, not a model-comprehension claim. No production Gateway, real user attachment, user credential, or live user state was used.

<details>
<summary>Regression controls, test cost, and audit limitation</summary>

The full local changed-check command stopped at inherited Knip findings: `isTelegramReadOnlyControlLaneText` in `extensions/telegram/src/sequential-key.ts`, `buildDirectChatContext` in `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts`, and the unused `resolveContextTokens` re-export in `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`. Their repair supplies a readable staged document and asserts admission directly while preserving rendering/fallback checks. The full steering/ordering selection subsequently passed in CI. </details>

<details>

title: refactor(mentions): keep Inbox database work off the Gateway thread
body:
Related: #153801
Backend prerequisite for #153812.

## What Problem This Solves

Mention delivery and Inbox policy checks need to leave the Gateway thread without losing access checks, durable state, or notifications; prefix-only excerpts also hide selected names in long messages.

## User Impact

The existing Inbox and personal session visibility use database workers, and new entries retain recipient-specific context. Message-commit ordering, current access checks, dismissal, replay suppression, and retention limits remain intact. Transient notification failures do not suppress unrelated recipients or strand other connected views.

No new setting, permission, table, column, index, or database version is introduced. Older writers may discard the optional preview/highlight metadata when rewriting a source; retained IDs, dismissal and expiry survive, and the candidate uses its plain-text fallback. [Accepted excerpt design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153812#issuecomment-5766660909).

The earlier compatibility proof covered the **shared Inbox store at `5e74fbbcf71`**, not whole-installation rollback. It used version-local agent metadata without bypassing schema guards. The current rebase inherits newer main schema versions; that historical roundtrip is not a downgrade test of this new head. This feature adds no further database version.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Inbox remains the owner of ordering and retention. The existing shared-state broker owns writes; read-only workers prepare policy facts. Cache lifetime now retains canonical target-revocation authority, and synchronous guards revalidate permissions at transaction and commit. Committed-input observers join accepted asynchronous work before acknowledgment.

This separates the backend prerequisite from the notification-card UI, keeping the presentation change independently reviewable.

## Evidence

Current head: `51e8c1ae26a5b5f2e587e8ba17da47115de2b637`, based on main `4d1c5d19ecc893ecef7b52cf7b3be002c794e770`. Both related PRs remain open; **no merge or auto-merge is requested**.

- Resolved current-main conflicts without restoring retired APIs. Recipient aliases are reconciled inside the authoritative transaction, and failed view publication recovers at FIFO settlement. Mixed-cohort expiry and record/list/dismiss recovery have failing-original regression controls.
- Final owner batch: **40 tests / 4 files passed**, 84.24 s. Earlier current-main boundary and sibling batches passed **273** and **340** tests; these overlap and are not a unique combined count.
- The preceding rebase `fd768fec797` passed core types, all 25 test-type groups, generated Swift parity, packaged worker syntax, and full build (**302.19 s**), with a scoped-clean whole-candidate P0–P2 review. Current CI repairs additionally pass core/scripts/Gateway test types, typed lint, and two scoped-clean independent reviews. No new full-build result is inferred from the earlier build.
- The full local changed macro reports an unchanged-main max-lines error in `context-engine-maintenance.ts` (710/700). The file matches main exactly. Existing hosted-CI policy treats limit diagnostics as warnings; no rule, assertion, deadline, or limit was weakened here. The upstream Mermaid 12 size excess is likewise retained, not claimed as a local performance pass.
- Reproduced and repaired the first hosted-CI failures: moved unchanged DTOs/codecs into leaf contracts, removed worker imports through the host validator registry, registered the exact required SQLite binder ABI, sorted the canonical test inventory without changing membership, and retained canonically regenerated Workboard assets. Madge and runtime-value graphs both report zero cycles; 41 export-guard tests retain unrelated-module rejection.
- Full planner/CLI-ownership regression files pass **510 tests**, 51.56 s. title: fix: visible work sessions belong to the requester

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes visible Team sessions created by `sessions_spawn` being assigned to the spawning agent even when the verified human requester owns the parent session.

## User Impact

New visible child sessions inherit human ownership only when the trusted active requester profile matches the parent session's effective human owner. Different owners, unlinked or missing requesters, agent-owned parents, and system-triggered spawns keep the requesting agent as owner. Existing target ownership is never replaced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now derives ownership from the lifecycle-locked parent, canonicalizes merged profile aliases through the resident profile catalog, and commits the owner atomically with a genuinely new child. The same requester authority crosses local, signed-runtime, and worker-backed spawn paths. Owner reassignment shares the session lifecycle fence, so a queued or revoked caller cannot race child creation. Required-sandbox creator provenance remains intact without masquerading as human ownership.

Related: #143334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a completed subagent’s result is retained but never delivered when its requester yields and the spawning execution releases its operator authority.

## User Impact

User impact: yielded requesters receive the completed child result without restarting the Gateway. Cancellation and operator revocation still stop child execution and deliver cancellation notices. No configuration or data migration is required.

This addresses the reproduced inactive-operator-authority mechanism, not every queued-input starvation or restart-time timeout reported in the linked issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing registry retains the original restricted completion context while its source is live, independently of the execution that spawned the child. It shares the delayed-session-reply capture mechanism, transfers custody across same-task replacement or a freshly admitted explicit retry, and releases it after committed settlement, retirement, or source/Gateway revocation. Failed persistence does not discard custody.

Successful result batches validate every original source and exact registry member. Cancellation-only notices retain their existing independent cancellation caller; mixed waves cannot borrow another or revoked operator’s source. Retired callbacks fail closed. title: fix(ui): keep task progress collapsed when sending messages
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Task progress can reopen when a message starts or completes a run, and a replacement card can inherit the previous card’s choice. Light mode also adds a second white rim around task progress.

## User Impact

A card keeps its open, closed, or partial state through messages, updates, completion, and same-connection revisits. Only a confirmed replacement restores the initial default: open on desktop unless the existing collapse preference is enabled, closed on mobile. The single light-mode border now uses the same outline color as the resting composer.

Presentation memory remains scoped to the current page/Gateway connection. Unobserved clear/recreation conservatively preserves the old choice. Reload persistence is outside this PR; no protocol or storage schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Direct baseline proof was captured at **main b7f616e43264bcc98bc220702d136f6ddae49b76**; the relevant progress-card owners remain unchanged through the refreshed **1ce767157d4b5af5633783a249267cdbd872ece4** base. Its actual Control UI reproduces header-close → Enter → accepted chat.send reopening the card from **44 to 160 px**. Its run/completion disclosure policies and extra light-mode inset frame are still present. The PR composes cleanly with that main; adjacent main changes affect goal styling, not the progress owner.

The repair removes run-driven disclosure policies. The shared progress store owns card-lifetime facts; the disclosure controller owns the user’s choice. The border reuses the existing composer outline token without changing queue, goal, or dark-mode styling.

## Evidence

- **Upstream fixture repair retained:** the group-race CI failure reproduced locally, and the independently developed async-writer repair passed all 29 real-worker cases. Main then landed the same repair in **46dfea6a420** with a stronger error assertion. This PR now uses that upstream version unchanged; its duplicate repair was dropped. The seven remaining PR commits are patch-identical after refreshing onto **1ce767157d4b5af5633783a249267cdbd872ece4**, and local merge composition is conflict-free.

- **Review disposition:** refreshed full-PR review found the group repair sound. Its sole P2 claim about ordinary session events resetting disclosure is rejected by the existing reset/delete-only guard in session-progress-cards.ts and the passing ordinary-patch lifetime regression. No code change was made to satisfy that false positive.

- **CI recovery is test-only:** the e3 run passed all UI/E2E lanes but failed Gateway suite teardown with a SQLite I/O error. Inspection found two registry fixtures deleting state before worker closure and a dispatch-clock fixture using a shared /tmp session path. body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CLI state-custody tests failing before reaching the lock scenario when authentication/handshake work consumes their incidental two-second deadline.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. CLI timeouts, authentication, state lifecycle, and production code are unchanged. This makes the integration proof about storage custody, while short-deadline behavior stays independently enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give only the three custody cases a bounded 10-second RPC integration budget, retain the explicit 2-second channel probe payload, and record elapsed handshake/custody/exit phases. The real CLI subprocess must authenticate before custody is acquired, receive hello while custody is held, make exactly one intended RPC, exit successfully, and leave state byte-identical.

Extend the existing fake-clock Gateway-call timeout table with a hello at 4ms of a 5ms budget, teardown settlement, no late dispatch, and timer cleanup. Move that table into narrow test support to respect the existing file-growth ratchet without duplicating its mock fixture.

title: fix: prevent deleted session groups from reappearing
body:
Related: #142863

Reworked directly on main, replacing the retained foundation from #153828. This no longer depends on the defaults PR or the held migration drafts.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes deleted groups reappearing when deletion overtakes session creation or category assignment before catalog registration settles.

## User Impact

Group deletion waits for earlier committed session writes and their registration. Bookkeeping failures warn and reload the catalog instead of falsely reporting that an already-saved session write failed. Reassigning the same category can repair missing bookkeeping. Session updates retain their place in the writer queue, and closing a session database no longer hangs behind revoked cleanup waiting for that same writer. Already-admitted writes still settle before close.

The catalog remains global. No agent-owned-group activation, schema change, new configuration, public RPC change, or Gateway deployment is included. Fresh creation remains isolated from unrelated archive-export failures; existing-session and alias adoption retain their historical retry and visible failure behavior. Canonical bytes, retention protection and explicit recovery are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the original physical writer through commit settlement, existing publication and registration, with live authority checked before committing and installing results. Remove late duplicate registration and the redundant replacement wrapper.

Touched durable access now uses the existing history reader, agent executor and shared-state reader. Supported aliases retain canonical replacement and native deletion custody. CI-exposed custom-store and first-creation identity defects are repaired at those existing owners; no parallel registry, writer or archive-retry manager is introduced.

## Evidence

- Actual registered create/patch versus group-delete races demonstrate the original defect and its repair. Proof includes close joining, physical-path/environment changes, transaction/commit revocation, uncertain publication, native rollback and rejected/no-write suppression.
- Unchanged guarded SDK suite: **24/24**. Creation/replacement/archive owners: **36/36**. Registered Gateway race/siblings: **14/14**. Reclamation repair: **73/73**, including the original board and Zalouser failures. These selections overlap earlier proof and are not combined into a larger total.
- Historical adoption-triggered archive retry is restored. Real collision/recovery fixtures verify exact bytes/hash, attempts, retained transcript/metadata, publication ordering and zero host data SQL. Fresh creation and generic recovery controls remain intact.
- Static dependency-cycle and test-inventory defects found by hosted CI are corrected. Architecture checks pass; both original routing suites pass **501/501**.
- Fresh independent review (R3) of the complete revised candidate is **scoped-clean through P2**, with no actionable findings. It reviewed source/evidence, not an independent execution of the tests. The subsequent mechanical removal of an unreachable snapshot wrapper migrated its three test callers to the existing connection-bound kernel; final snapshot/type/lint/export/build checks cover that cutover.

- A subsequent hosted-CI teardown race is repaired: read-admission retirement no longer loses an already-acquired exact lease receipt needed after native exit. A real-worker regression fails on the published predecessor and passes with the base owner and repair; this substitutes one owner, not a full baseline. **109 focused tests pass**, including original failing consumers, with core/test types and typed lint clean. Fresh independent R4 review of this two-file correction is **scoped-clean through P2**; it did not rerun tests.

- The next hosted run exposed replacement callbacks losing their FIFO turn and a planning-close deadlock. Exact database locators now reserve the existing queue before worker-owned schema discovery; revocation removes only pending maintenance admissions. Unchanged original cases reproduce RED and pass after repair. Final-source ownership proof is **93/93**, with production/test types, typed lint, formatting and delta ratchets clean. Independent R5 review of the 11-file correction is **scoped-clean through P2**; tests were not independently rerun by the reviewer. A separate final integration applied the frozen repair to the actual failing CI merge `27bf437c`, including its main-side worker-runtime changes: the original config lane passed **90 files / 1,654 tests in 189.63s**, on Node 24.19.0 with two workers and retries disabled. This is local exact-merge integration, not a substitute for current-head hosted CI.

**Current-head Claw review (c3860f0f, September 23 at 16:52 UTC):** no actionable introduced or security defect was found. Its explicit source assessment withdraws the prior generic migration-proof request and confirms no schema, serialized representation, retention-policy or public-RPC change. The generated checklist still repeats that withdrawn request; it is not an unresolved source finding. Existing-state alias, archive-recovery, authority and lease-cleanup evidence above remains applicable. Current-head hosted CI and native merge gates remain required.

**Qualified integration baseline (11cc34f5):** production and all source core-test type graphs, revised-candidate typed lint, all three canonical unused-export scans, and canonical build passed. After the final mechanical cutover, creation snapshots passed **13/13**, production/session-test types and two-path typed lint passed, all three unused-export scans reported zero entries, and the final build passed in **225s**. All 48 source hashes stayed unchanged through that baseline qualification and publication. The subsequent seven-line production receipt-lifetime correction and its regression have separate focused qualification above; at that stage the other 46 paths were unchanged. The later FIFO/cancellation correction has separate proof above; no fresh full local build is claimed for it. Current-head hosted CI remains required.

**Retained limitation:** the earlier full-tree core lint scan failed on unchanged `src/cron/service/timer.test.ts` (1,022 counted lines versus its 1,000-line allowance). Its Git blob is identical to the selected main base. No allowance was raised; the full changed-check wrapper is not claimed green. Earlier local proof used Node 26 versus hosted Node 24.19. New FIFO/cancellation reproduction and qualification use verified Node 24.19.0. No live-Gateway, native-platform or published-driver upgrade proof is claimed.

**Unresolved timing evidence:** hosted predecessor CI observed dirty session describe at 124.39ms against its unchanged 100ms assertion (zero transcript reads; 1,995 rows still pending). One original-order attempt stopped earlier in the separate cron process on six real-HTTP delivery cases, including a 120s timeout (1,567 passed); those failures remain unexplained and were not retried. The still-unexercised 89-selector Gateway plan was then run once, with unchanged assertions: describe 32.62ms, dirty describe 15.25ms, zero transcript reads and 1,983 rows pending. The Gateway shard itself was not green: 29 failed, 974 passed, one skipped and two unhandled errors; HTTP cases observed the host secret-egress proxy refusal/502 response rather than their expected local endpoint payload. That transport boundary was not bypassed. The latency case is a non-reproduction, not a timing fix or CI waiver. Local Node 26 differs from hosted Node 24.19; no timing limit was changed.

<details>
<summary>Regression attribution, review dispositions and measured costs</summary>

The custom-store transcript failure came from reinterpreting a prepared physical database as a logical store. Reading its already-resolved owner fixes the producer; transcript guards are unchanged.

The original board deletion failure directly showed an unresolved host shared-state identity versus the worker's first-created physical identity. Restoring only the baseline deletion lookup made the unchanged test pass. The repair publishes first creation through the canonical admission owner before unchanged receipt checks, and settles errors through existing failure/termination handling. This was a narrow counterfactual, not a whole-baseline run. Board 22/22, Zalouser 5/5, reclamation custody 33/33, shared-state lifecycle 11/11 and the extended owner file 2/2 pass.

The earlier Signal-alias P2 was reproduced at the actual admitted entry point and repaired. R2 alleged a newly missing original-snapshot CAS across an asynchronous creation callback. A deterministic comparison with the old entry/projection owners showed the same low-level lost-update behavior in both; newer persisted ownership survived. Normal Gateway create/patch retain the lifecycle fence and caller/session checks. That finding remains disposed as inherited, not claimed fixed; the comparison substituted two owners, not the entire baseline. The earlier archive comparison restored 22 production paths, likewise not a full-baseline run. Revised archive tests fail on the pre-repair candidate and pass after restoring the historical retry.

Measured standalone test commands use the canonical repository runner with `--maxWorkers=1` (direct wrapper when avoiding dependency reconciliation):

- Revised archive file: 8/8, **19.24s wall**, including 2.505s warm worker preparation; canonical/alias adoption 2.368s/2.422s; max RSS 866,692 KiB.
- Earlier reclamation file: 2/2, **38.70s wall**, including 29.43s cold compilation; test bodies total 1.507s. No new test case or worker boot. The 71-case boundary batch took 96.02s.
- Latest reclamation file: 3/3, **33.60s wall**, including 26.148s cold compilation; new real-worker late-receipt regression 966ms. The 106-case sibling/consumer batch took 102.29s. Neither passing uncontrolled replay proves the CI interleaving was fixed; the deterministic RED/base-owner/GREEN regression establishes the repair.
- New queue-cancellation case: changed file **12/12, 31.70s wall**, cold compiler dominated; new case **1ms**. Revised replacement-worker file: **7/7, 22.74s wall**; new unkeyed shared-owner/zero-host-SQL case **1,656ms**. Final 93-case owner batch took **51.99s**. The real worker case proves schema discovery and the no-host-SQL boundary that a mocked publisher cannot. Hosted cost for these new cases is not yet available.
- Creation-worker: 34.01s cold wall, including 18.074s preparation; its three alias cases total 4.011s. Prior unchanged-owner measurements: replacement-worker 14.64s, creation-snapshot 19.97s, create/category 23.58s, patch effects 2.69s, registration 24.10s, catalog 48.41s, create preparation 18.36s, atomic initialization 13.82s.

One counterfactual compiler subprocess exited 139 before tests. One prerequisite retry with supported bounded compiler concurrency completed. That tooling crash remains unexplained, not relabeled as a product failure or claimed fixed. No manual CI reruns, weaker assertions, relaxed limits or modified baselines were used. The isolated exact-merge proof initially lacked workspace-local `quickjs-wasi`/Markdown dependency links; its own frozen install repaired that setup, and the single prerequisite retry passed. Shared candidate dependencies and source were not changed.

55 files, +2,477/−460: production 42 files, +1,151/−331; tests/support 12 files, +1,315/−125; owning documentation 1 file, +11/−4. Growth comes from required worker adaptation, pending-admission cancellation at the existing queue owner, and lifecycle/data-preservation proof—not another queue or presentation-module extraction.

The [failed predecessor run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35878886549) tested merge 27bf437c (2ab085b9 plus main 60d25b94). title: fix: plugin category filters wait for the full catalog
body:
Related: [CLAW-1027](https://linear.app/my-openclaw/issue/CLAW-1027/align-plugins-page-header-and-accelerate-category-chip-loading)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dynamic category filters stay invisible until the installed inventory and full plugin catalog finish loading on the Plugins discovery page.

## User Impact

User impact: category navigation can appear while catalog cards are still loading, with chip-shaped placeholders, usable All / Featured / Trending filters, and an explicit retry if categories fail. No configuration migration or backend change.

The visible Plugins title and left-aligned Plugins / Skills / Skill workshop tabs are **already present on the verified current-main baseline**. This PR preserves and rechecks that layout at the reported 1200×928 viewport and on mobile rather than adding a second header or changing the individual plugin configuration editor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Previously the route awaited plugins.list, then plugins.catalog.browse awaited its own local inventory read before the remote overview could deliver category metadata. Start the existing lightweight category RPC as soon as discovery connects, independently of both inventory and cards. Keep the overview's canonical categories as a fallback/refresh: a fast overview can settle the chips and retire a slower category request. Category state is connection-scoped, empty results settle, failures do not auto-loop, and late replies cannot republish a retired connection's navigation. Warm filter changes reuse category state.

ClawHub already exposes a categories endpoint; no coordinated ClawHub PR or new endpoint is justified. Its live response was smaller but often slower than the cached overview, so **this removes client-side serialization; it does not make the remote endpoint faster**. It adds one initial category RPC/GET per discovery-page connection context, not one per filter; explicit retries can add requests. Skeletons estimate the observed 22-category footprint; taxonomy, labels, and ordering remain server-owned.

## Evidence

- Tested/published head: 39b9abe380bb8ef2d110e778e8ad1ac2bc7abc78 (tree f11e78519c1058cbb7893df06a02568eec81006f). Baseline: 06ce6c415dd293f139181085c9518abe5d47ce36, freshly fetched before edits. Header provenance includes a91f1202d9d (#126061); current screenshots confirm the already-fixed title/alignment.

Final focused unit/page suite: **92 tests passed** (5 files; 5.68 s wrapper wall, 4.75 s Vitest). Covers pending inventory/cards, empty/error/retry, overview-first completion, warm filters, and connection invalidation.
- Changed-check type, guard, i18n, and dead-export lanes passed. One new-test brace-style lint finding was fixed; final changed-file oxlint, stylelint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Production UI build passed (Vite 21.70 s; index-Dt8b5rs4.js, plugins-page-B04INho0.js).
- Separate actual-Chromium route assertions passed: categories begin before the deferred installed inventory, error → retry settles chips before cards, and a warm Featured selection does not refetch categories.

**Formal UI E2E verified in CI (2026-09-22):** [CI run 35669387593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35669387593) completed successfully for exact head 39b9abe380bb8ef2d110e778e8ad1ac2bc7abc78, including all 13 UI E2E shards and openclaw/ci-gate. Inspected [shard 5/13 logs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35669387593/job/106562482900): plugins-hub-navigation.e2e.test.ts passed all 6 tests in 6.947 s; the new independent-category/error-retry regression passed in 1.091 s. CI ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner --shard "5/13"`. This resolves the formal-suite evidence gap; the earlier local proxy/isolated-pnpm startup failures were environment limitations, not successful local E2E runs.

- Independent AutoReview of the final diff: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Real Chromium captures of the actual /plugins page with a mocked Gateway, dark theme, 1200×928 and 393×852. The final categories-ready/card-loading capture measured **0 px vertical movement** of the catalog body at both viewports. Placeholder geometry is an estimate, not a promise of zero shift for every future taxonomy, font, or viewport. Reduced-motion uses the existing skeleton primitive; decorative placeholders are nonfocusable and hidden from assistive technology, with one loading status.

**PR-page media rendering verified (2026-09-22):** inspected the actual GitHub PR document in the managed Chromium browser, expanded the visual-matrix disclosure, and successfully decoded all nine embedded screenshots. All image elements report complete=true and their expected natural dimensions: five 1200×928 desktop images and four 393×852 mobile images. The before/after pair and wider state matrix render from the published PR body; this resolves the previously recorded PR-rendering gap and the review’s publication-verification request. No images were re-uploaded.

The original Linear attachment could not be retrieved in this environment (web fetch exposed only its loading shell and the shared browser connection failed). These are fresh baseline/current-source captures, not a claim to have inspected that attachment. No Linear labels, including sardine, were changed.

### Timing: controlled browser comparison

Linux x64 Team host, Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.4.0, Playwright 1.63.0 / Chromium 153.0.8010.12, Vite source server. Same synthetic Gateway schedule in both revisions: inventory 300 ms, browse/cards 1000 ms, category response 150 ms. Delays belong only to the uncommitted benchmark fixture, not the committed regressions.

title: fix(ui): restart recovery appears as a user message while resuming
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session resuming after a Gateway restart briefly shows the internal recovery instruction as a user-authored chat bubble.

## User Impact

Restart recovery uses the existing compact system-event divider and short summary from the moment the input is pending through its promotion into saved history. It no longer displays the raw recovery prompt or attributes that instruction to the viewer. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending inputs bypassed the system-notice classification used by saved history. Both now share that projection, preserving existing notice copy, styling, turn boundaries, and collapsed injected-context behavior. Cached notices also compare canonical boundary identity so promotion updates execution ownership without changing the row key. The placement lookup recognizes turn-starting notices as ceilings for earlier live work, while run ownership remains message-backed. Classification requires structured system provenance; a user's literal `[System]` prefix remains an ordinary message.

<details>
<summary>Regression cause and maintenance assessment</summary>

Source history identifies [#132887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132887), commit `6c9954cbb69880960257eb7811581b0b5dedc774`, as the introduction of the bypass: accepted turns became durable pending inputs, and the new pending renderer emitted ordinary message items after the saved-history loop had already applied system-notice classification. Structured system provenance was preserved, but only the history path consumed it. This is source-level attribution, not a historical browser replay.

The repair extracts the established presentation rule into one shared projector rather than duplicating a restart-specific condition. The existing notice-kind registry still owns labels, summaries, collapse behavior, and turn semantics; no new state, configuration, CSS, or protocol is added. The focused lifecycle test covers the previously missing pending-only composition path and subsequent promotion without duplicate notices.

The original CI failures were separate: historical baseline preparation read `baseline_version`, while two upgrade fixtures skipped normal initialization. Upstream commit `6ee9578ab7bfd16f219e7fd7a3b1b34292552c36` repairs those fixtures and is included by this refresh.

</details>

The required CI gate passed. Native rollup verification reconciled eight superseded historical contexts.

The full-thread matrix covers notice presentation, spoof protection, attribution, search, uninterrupted pending-to-history promotion, canonical boundary refresh, and the actual assistant group inside its agent-run frame. The live-to-terminal regression covers ordinary and system custody, keeping the response and working indicator above the pending notice while preserving frame identity and leaving pending execution ownership unset.

<details>

Main’s pending-custody ordering change is preserved: pending inputs follow visible history, while promoted notices return to canonical transcript order. title: fix(protocol): expose suspension result validators to lifecycle clients
body:
Closes #155257

## What Problem This Solves

External lifecycle clients lack ready-to-use suspension result validators and can reject valid `writeCustody` evidence when duplicated response-field allowlists drift from the Gateway contract.

## User Impact

Client developers can validate prepare/status responses through the public protocol package. Existing external clients must adopt these exports; this does not automatically repair their parsers or change Gateway suspension behavior.

Qualification also exposed cold device-auth preparation occurring inside a later CLI connection deadline. The repair completes command-runtime preparation before connecting, without changing timeout budgets, token freshness, permissions, or storage policy. No protocol, schema, version, or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Export two validators compiled from the existing canonical result schemas. Preserve omitted custody as unknown, empty/positive custody as supplied, and unfamiliar owner-phase strings. Wire validation does not replace the controller's process, lease, expiry, or readiness checks.

The initial CI run failed three existing Gateway-backed CLI cases before a connect RPC. Actor-open preparation had become insufficient after feature loading was deferred until the first worker command. A private `deviceAuth.prepare` command now goes through the existing device-auth owner; worker preparation loads the canonical handler, and the command returns before accessing token data. All original read/write handlers and authority checks stay in place. No retry, relaxed assertion, test-environment override, or increased timeout was added.

Production delta: +5 lines overall (+2 public exports, +3 preparation repair). Tests: +107 net; docs: +8. Removed the duplicated no-op preparation path; no alternate parser or controller.

## Evidence

title: feat: edit personal instructions on multi-user gateways
body:
Closes #155255

## What Problem This Solves

Signed-in users can have a personal `USER.md` but cannot edit it themselves through Profile settings or reliably ask an agent to update it from a project session. Follow-up to #153966.

## User Impact

On multi-user Gateways, users can open **Settings → Profile → Personal instructions** or ask an agent from any authenticated Gateway chat session to create/edit their personal instructions. The chat path works independently of the session owner and project worktree. Both paths use the requesting person’s file with `operator.read`; shared bootstrap files and other people’s files remain outside that authority.

**Single-user Gateways use only the existing workspace-root `USER.md` (Agents → Files).** They get no personal-instructions editor, Settings-search entry, chat tool or catalog entry, personal-file API access, or per-profile prompt overlay. Previously created personal files remain untouched on disk; they are not loaded, deleted, or silently merged into the root file.

Personal files are enabled only by the existing multi-user policy: at least two distinct, unmerged person profiles, excluding the shared Owner from the count. The server rechecks this policy before reads and immediately before writes; Control UI picks up a changed roster policy on reconnect. Within multi-user Gateways, requester binding, session-selected prompt context, local-workspace restrictions, the 4,000-character budget, provenance checks, and normal tool/agent permissions remain. No new configuration option or storage migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Agents file editor is intentionally admin-only and limited to shared bootstrap filenames. A Profile editor that follows the existing Settings-sidebar agent selection and the `personal_instructions` chat tool share the same narrow authenticated-self API rather than widening general file-tool access. The canonical profile and path come from the live connection or the exact host-issued original-requester authority of an admitted chat turn—not session ownership, tool arguments, or a copied profile on a synthetic client. Safe filesystem operations reject aliases and recheck the source, run, scope, role, Gateway, and workspace before mutation. Other personal APIs retain their existing synthetic-caller restrictions.

Saves require the loaded content hash and use the existing workspace save queue. Conflicts with independent host editors remain **best effort**, matching the shared editor: avoid simultaneous UI and host-process edits. Failed requests and transient reconnects retain the draft without exposing it under a different profile or Gateway. Changing the Settings agent retains unsaved drafts separately for each agent; it never retargets an in-flight save.

## Evidence

### Current follow-up: Profile spacing and startup budget (`35636541ffe6bd8e1e252637953c68f5abd7a585`)

- The empty personal editor stays mounted for draft recovery, but its host is now hidden on single-user Gateways. Real Chromium shows **80 → 40 px** between Identity and Connected accounts, with unchanged multi-user editor geometry and zero single-user personal-file requests. [Matched before/after and exact-head review request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155256#issuecomment-5788085682).
- The previous head's [performance failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35809933323/job/107019284412) was a 93-byte startup-JS gzip overage. Editor-only English now loads with the Profile component; search metadata remains eager. The complete composed English catalog is byte-identical. The same pinned-base performance comparison passes at **371,031 B**, down from **371,425 B**, against the unchanged **371,332 B** limit. No budgets, allowances or baselines were raised.
- **122/122 focused tests passed** across Profile, Settings search and i18n tooling (44.86 s command wall). UI production types, localization verification, focused lint/format, and fresh P0–P2 autoreview pass. No new recurring tests were added for this small layout correction; real browser geometry verifies the visual contract.
- **Hosted CI:** [run 35811553649](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35811553649) completed **success** for exact head `35636541ffe6bd8e1e252637953c68f5abd7a585`, including the repaired performance gate and iOS/Android lanes. **ClawSweeper:** [Revision 15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155256#issuecomment-5769032192) is ready on that same head, with no findings, no security issues, and nothing listed before merge. Older receipts below belong to their named earlier heads. Deployment is not part of this change.

### Final landing audit (September 23; unchanged head `35636541ffe6`)

- **Test-audit:** Reviewed all 17 changed test suites and the extracted handshake test helper. Retained cases protect real file effects, live authority/revocation, bootstrap selection, protocol/tool discovery, and observable draft/agent/profile transitions. No low-value deletion or new test-only production seam was identified; no new sleep/polling or per-test Gateway boot was added.
- **Deslop:** Inspected the full merge-base-to-head diff; no actionable behavior-neutral cleanup found, and no source was changed. The existing exact-head P0–P2 autoreview and ClawSweeper Revision 16 remain applicable; the fresh direct landing review also has no findings.
- **Flake triage:** Earlier CI failures, bounded investigations, suspected boundaries, and unresolved uncertainty are preserved below and tracked in [the follow-up checklist](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156502). A later green run or isolated passing replay is not claimed as a fix. No retry, timeout, assertion, mock or performance-budget relaxation was used to manufacture green.
- **E2E scope:** Actual Chromium production-component read/edit/save uses a mock Gateway. The separate real in-process chat-tool/Gateway/filesystem regressions verify persistence and authorization. Single-user UI sends no personal-file calls and shows the normal 40 px gap. This is compositional boundary proof, **not** a single live browser → running Gateway → model conversation test. Remote workspaces remain explicitly unsupported, and simultaneous independent host edits retain the documented best-effort conflict contract.
- **Current base:** The exact head composes conflict-free with main `5706a0626359b52daa5feb12fe98c260153525c3`; the Profile heading and shell callback changes remain intact. Live rules do not require strict up-to-date status; required CI is green, with no pending/failed check.

<details>
<summary>Measured cost of all changed test suites</summary>

All 17 suites passed again with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` (172.99 s total sequential command wall). Local wall includes wrapper/compiler/import/setup cost and mixed cold/warm compiler generations. title: fix(agents): sessions_yield misreports no pending child when an earlier turn already waits on a running session
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions_yield` tells the model "No pending child completion is owned by this turn. If the assigned work is complete, return its result normally" when an earlier turn of the same session spawned a visible child session that is still running (and already armed its completion wake). The model has no supported way to wait, so it falls back to `sessions_send` notify/steer loops and ends every turn with "Continuing…" while nothing is visible to the human until they nudge again.

## User Impact

User impact: a coordination session that spawned a visible work session in an earlier turn no longer misreports that nothing is pending. A later `sessions_yield` returns `status: "already_pending"` with the pending children (session key, label, start time, running/completing/paused, whether the wake is armed) and tells the model to end the turn normally because the child's completion resumes the session on its own. No user-visible change for sessions with no pending children, sub-agent `waitFor: "message"`, cron, or collector runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The yield claim (`markRequesterTurnYielded`) only matches registry rows bound to the *current* run ID. After turn 1 yields, settlement clears `requesterTurnRunId` and arms `requesterSettleWake`, so turn 2 owns nothing and the generic error's guidance ("return its result normally") is wrong while the child is still running. The yield callback now asks the registry, after every existing claim path fails, for this requester session's announcing children whose completion is still owed (latest generation per child session; collector, killed, suppressed, delivered, and stale rows excluded) and reports them instead of the generic error. The registry query is read-only: it never claims, re-arms, or mutates rows.

title: fix: prevent provider stream errors from hanging behind response clones
body:
Related: #117397

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes provider response errors hanging indefinitely when JSON-to-SSE synthesis or SSE sanitization fails while another response clone remains unread.

## User Impact

Consumers receive the original stream error promptly, while outstanding cleanup and cooperating work remain owned until they finish. Explicit consumer cancellation remains awaited. Successful streams, network authority and local-service ownership are unchanged; no configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two error paths now start best-effort cancellation under the response's captured work owner without delaying error delivery. Starting cleanup there—not merely observing an already-started promise—also retains cooperating cleanup work. If that owner has already closed, cleanup starts once outside work scopes without restoring old authority. The current HTTP, guarded-body, proxy and local-service implementations remain intact.

## Evidence

Signed publication head a9127703721bd44400bf4a73a9663a276c4a532b preserves the exact tested tree c07a34a710191f7148ed3b29c80ceb966decece9 and parent b485dd0b988f40b6cdcd94fc516623f73c776a15.

Normal commit hooks preserved the exact tested and reviewed source. This local commit identifies the tested source; the signed publication binding is recorded separately.

- **Real RED/GREEN:** unchanged main failed both held-clone error cases. The two-void-hunk control fixed visible errors but failed seven ownership cases. An already-started-promise control passed eight cases but failed all three foreign-scope cases. The candidate passed all **11** cases.

Assertions check original-error precedence, separate native cancellation and guard-release settlement, cooperating-descendant ownership, original versus consumer drain, open/closing/closed scopes, exactly-once cleanup, no unhandled rejection and explicit awaited cancellation. These are real native streams/clones with mocked network/lease callbacks, not physical process-exit proof.
- **174 tests passed across seven focused files**, preserving the existing provider coverage and exercising HTTP, shared guarded-body, fetch authority/release and async-work ownership. The new 11-case file took **1.73 seconds wall** using `pnpm test src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.clone.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (642 ms Vitest duration). Hosted CI timing is pending.

title: fix(ui): prevent duplicate bullets in Safari chat lists
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes overlapping bullet dots in chat lists on Safari, including the mobile Web UI.

## User Impact

Unordered lists show one bullet per item. Numbered lists, task checkboxes, nested-list indentation, and chat/thinking text keep their existing presentation. No configuration changes or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat draws a custom `::before` bullet but relied on `::marker { content: "" }` to hide the native one. [Safari has incomplete support for styling marker content](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Selectors/::marker#browser_compatibility). Suppress the native list style on ordinary unordered items instead of relying on that property.

title: fix(ios): assistant files are not downloadable in chat
body:
Closes #155189

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: assistant-generated documents appear as inert attachments instead of downloadable files in native iOS chat, even when the same conversation works on the web.

## User Impact

Users can tap **Download file**, then use the system share sheet to **Save to Files** or send the file to another app. The shared macOS native chat uses its save panel. Existing image, audio, and video presentation remains separate.

**Validation:** real native red/green and inspected screenshots are complete, including original-chat delivery. Exact-head CI and native landing checks passed. Squash-merged to main as `65821c2c48692648d3006cc08293c2918318b7eb` on 2026-09-22 at 10:01 UTC; issue #155189 closed. No release or deployment was performed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already supplies managed documents in a nested attachment envelope. Native decoding discarded that envelope's file metadata, and the renderer only offered actions for image/audio/video attachments.

Decode the existing envelope and extend the existing scoped artifact download owner for files. Preserve ticket renewal, Gateway-route checks, custom ingress headers, TLS pinning, and bounded transfers (the existing Gateway document limit is 100 MiB). Never open assistant-supplied local paths or arbitrary URLs. Reuse one system file-sharing view for attachments, transcripts, and workspace files; uniquely owned temporary copies are removed when export releases them. Added production code owns the previously missing download control and export lifecycle, not a competing network or authorization implementation. No protocol, schema, or credential changes.

## Evidence

- **Actual native proof:** [inspected before/after, system share, and expiry captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155195#issuecomment-5770243318). All four images are embedded in that comment and their rendering on GitHub was verified. The originating conversation also received the representative Before/After images; delivery receipts were sent and settled.
- On [run 35673180468](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35673180468), the iOS job passed. The actual baseline decoder failed specifically on lost filename metadata, and its real UI failed on the missing download action after history loaded. The candidate passed 29 focused native tests and the actual download/share/relaunch/expiry UI flow. The loopback Gateway alone is synthetic; no hand-built before card or injected production UI state was used.
- Proof provenance: head `823c597170fff80b93dae568f2af7dbddd4cac9d`, tested merge tree `e25fc1f4c686c3d8ce25fdc0b80cf78603048f82`, baseline `46375679b7cc9ef787f50fe21af345db0f665ca4`, iPhone 18 Pro / iOS 27.0. Raw lifecycle artifact **10673697996** retains logs, all four xcresult summaries/bundles, exported images, and fixture digest.
- Measured candidate test runtime: decode/cache 0.010 s, loader/typography Swift tests 4.197 s, real UI flow 95.757 s. Complete historical baseline/candidate proof took 54m03s including builds/startup/failure diagnostics. Accordingly, the long UI flow remains registered in full-manual native validation; fast decoder/loader/typography regressions join the existing mandatory PR smoke invocation. No existing voice, lifecycle, Watch, logging, or artifact checks were removed.
- The old overall run failed separately: fixture import ordering and the artifact-contract expectation were reproduced and fixed, then verified locally. Android callback override compiler errors originated in its main-branch merge input (#155038); two unchanged Control UI E2E cases also failed, with their root causes not established by this task. No unrelated Android/UI source was modified.
- The exact seven-suite smoke execution assertion was also repaired, preserving all original suites, one invocation, and normal Debug signing. Focused follow-up validation passed 16 selected tests across the three native workflow-contract files (3.16 s wrapper wall); unrelated cases were excluded. The broader guard-file attempt hit a 180 s local tool timeout and is not counted as a full-suite pass.
- Local follow-up checks passed: focused artifact-contract tests (3 tests, 1.42 s wrapper wall), scoped fixture lint/wire check, formatting/whitespace, workflow actionlint/zizmor and repository guards, plus fresh P0–P2 autoreview after each substantive correction.

Follow-up commits change only CI/test wiring and fixture import placement; production Swift and captured UI code are unchanged. Current-head CI completed successfully; screenshot inspection, PR rendering, and original-chat delivery are complete.

**Review disposition / coverage limit:** macOS compilation and package/shared temporary-file byte-lifecycle tests passed, but interactive `NSSavePanel` and bytes written to a user-selected destination were not exercised. The scoped iOS defect has actual native red/green proof and independent source review with no correctness or security findings. At these widths, loading and loaded category areas have the same height. No native-app or live-Gateway screenshot claim.

### Category critical-path benchmark

| Replay condition | Metric | n / phase | Before median | After median | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Slow first-open replay | Visible categories | 3 | 4613 ms | 2053 ms | -2560 ms (-55.5%) |
| Slow first-open replay | First catalog card | 3 | 4615 ms | 4202 ms | -413 ms (-9.0%) |
| Warm-inventory replay | Visible categories | 5 | 656 ms | 586 ms | -70 ms (-10.6%) |
| Warm-inventory replay | First catalog card | 5 | 659 ms | 565 ms | -93 ms (-14.2%) |

The cold category dependency is removed. Card work is unchanged; small card/warm differences include browser scheduling noise. Warm category samples ranged 579–1,037 ms after versus 578–887 ms before, so this is **not** a warm-tail latency improvement claim. An additional run concurrent with other browser tests was kept as diagnostic evidence, not mixed into this comparable standalone table.

<details>
<summary>Methodology, live endpoint measurements, and limits</summary>

Linux x64 Team execution host; Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.4.0, Playwright 1.63.0 / Chromium 153.0.8010.12. Browser runs used the same rootless, network-isolated Playwright image, 4-CPU/8-GiB limits, fresh browser contexts, the real production UI bundle, and deterministic mocked Gateway responses. No production service was changed.

Before editing, measured the production inventory owner against separate synthetic state (174 plugins; 66,564 JSON bytes): three process-cold reads were 3,681 / 1,600 / 1,467 ms, and 12 warm reads were 6.8–14.0 ms. Browser replay uses the observed **slow first-open** inventory read of 3,681 ms versus 9 ms warm, with 1,306 ms categories and 177 ms overview. It is a controlled critical-path experiment, not a claim that every production inventory takes 3.7 seconds. Hold plugins.list, plugins.catalog.categories, and plugins.catalog.browse independently, release each after its delay from dispatch, and measure navigation-to-visible-Channels and navigation-to-first-card separately. Repeat the same scenario before/after; do not serialize independent responses. Small browser samples support the dependency improvement, not a precise production tail-latency guarantee.

Live public HTTPS probes from the host (10 alternating samples per endpoint per phase, all HTTP 200; no CDN flush or explicit authentication headers; time includes body consumption):

| Endpoint | Before p50 / empirical p95 | After p50 / empirical p95 | Decoded JSON bytes | Observed cache policy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| categories | 1,306 / 2,362 ms | 922 / 2,651 ms | 6,712 | no-store; Age 0 |
| overview | 177 / 872 ms | 77 / 439 ms | 127,164–127,224 | public, max-age=60; varied CDN Age |

Live endpoint differences are network/CDN variation, **not** backend improvements from this UI patch. The category endpoint already returns the canonical taxonomy without catalog queries, so another endpoint was not justified. Its inconsistent latency is why the UI also accepts the overview's categories. The extra category payload is about 5.3% of the overview payload; requests remain bounded to one per connection load and none on ordinary filter/search changes. Gateway envelopes, compression, and headers are not included in byte counts.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Independent review disposition</summary>

AutoReview completed at P2 scope with two lifecycle findings, not a scoped-clean verdict. Both were checked and rejected against the implementation, installed @lit/task 1.0.3 source, and passing regressions:

- Invalidation already calls disconnect(), which supersedes the category task using run([null]); Lit aborts the old signal and fences late results using its call ID.
- Lit's initialState branch sets INITIAL **without invoking onComplete**, so disconnect cannot mark an empty taxonomy loaded.

Late-result tests deliberately use promises that ignore cancellation; the disconnect test also proves a subsequent category load dispatches and completes. No workaround or duplicate generation counter was added for these incorrect findings.

</details>

title: fix: Side chat blocks typing while answering
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Side chat disables its question box while answering, preventing users from drafting a follow-up.

## User Impact

Users can keep editing the next question during an answer. Sending still waits for the active answer; disconnected controls remain disabled. Drafts survive answer completion and errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The textarea incorrectly shared the send button's busy guard. Keep its normal placeholder and let the existing thread status show that an answer is pending. Focus tests now wait for the pending exchange and explicitly establish the foreground input they intend to protect.

The failing cron recovery test compared process-wide work counts before and after an asynchronous operation. An unrelated root finishing changed 1 to 0 despite correct recovery. Recovery tests now borrow each timer's exact admission scope and verify it becomes unusable when that tick settles. This also detects a leaked tick even if unrelated work finishes. Startup, durable repair, events, reservations, and error-settlement assertions remain covered. Cron production code is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Final [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672089372) and enforced merge gates passed for `d267c75cb0527f6d5ea4e8e908a58343b1713797`. The hosted cron cohort passed 1,562 tests across 126 files in 137.16 seconds; the three batch recovery cases took 975/24/24 ms. Merged as `368ec5c22d8cb1a3a5d106d305fee47eb3b08891`.
- Controlled before/after: releasing an independent request during held recovery makes the original assertion fail with the same expected-1/observed-0 result as [CI run 35655193743](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35655193743). The repaired three-file recovery suite passes all 36 tests (11.01 seconds wrapper wall).
- Mutation proof: temporarily omitting the timer's admission release makes both timer batch cases fail the new assertion; startup still passes. The mutation was removed before final validation.
- Full cron service cohort: 125 files, 1,557 tests passed with two workers (195.48 seconds Vitest). Side-chat component/history/lifecycle: 71 tests passed (5.83 seconds wrapper wall). Production-bundle Chromium focus suite: all 23 tests passed (30.87 seconds), including mobile, deferred mounting, pane switches, and newer input intent.
- Targeted type-aware lint and formatting passed. Changed-file checks passed repository guards and i18n, then stopped on unrelated configure/doctor types: this local install has Clack 1.5.1/1.8.1 from newer main while this head pins 1.5.0/1.8.0. Both core test-type shards passed on the exact head with frozen dependencies in [CI run 35672089372](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672089372); those local errors do not reproduce there.
- Fresh independent autoreview found no P0 issues; the existing full side-chat review found no actionable issues through P2. The latest [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155183#issuecomment-5767395120) has no findings or rank-up moves.
- Production delta: +2/-2, net zero. Tests and support: +144/-21, net +123. No new production seam, reset, retry, timeout, or dependency change.
- The existing real-app screenshots below were inspected, verified to render in this PR, and delivered in the maintainer task. They use deterministic Gateway responses and the same 1440 × 900 viewport.

<details>
<summary>Investigation limits and follow-up</summary>

The original CI root's producer was not identified. Focused, predecessor-order, and complete shared-worker local runs did not reproduce that ambient root. The controlled concurrency scenario proves the count assertion is invalid; it does not claim an unidentified production leak was fixed.

Follow-up: inspect completion ownership in `src/cron/service/ops.run-admission-capacity.test.ts`, case "keeps saturated scheduled work unreserved when it is rescheduled". A diagnostic trace showed its immediate capacity recheck still open at file teardown; the case waits for listener removal rather than tick settlement. It ran after the failed recovery case in CI, so it cannot explain that failure.

Runtime deployment is separate; no hosting Gateway was restarted.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: typing in the session composer becomes slow after selecting someone to mention.

## User Impact

Continue typing normally after selecting a person. Recipient tracking, dismissal, name overflow, resizing, and retained-composer recovery remain intact. No appearance, configuration, protocol, or storage changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary text edits were redrawing the entire chat pane while any mention existed. The unchanged “Will notify” strip then repeatedly changed visibility and widths before measuring them, forcing synchronous style/layout work.

- Chromium, real Control UI with a mocked Gateway and 100 synthetic messages: replaying 44 characters took **1,193 ms before**; **82 ms after**, versus **68 ms** without a mention in the final run. title: fix(test): prevent premature media retention fixture expiry
body:
Related: #154930

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent media-retention CI failures when tests advance a fake logical clock but SQLite workers expire fixture rows on real time.

## User Impact

No production behavior or expiry-policy changes. The tests still verify the same 100 ms URL lifetime, 100 ms serving grace, retained-row capacity, and explicit cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the fixture an independent backing-store lifetime through the existing expiry resolver, so real worker delays cannot remove rows before the logical-clock assertions. The physical storage-base TTL changes only in test data; logical deadlines, clock checkpoints, assertions, and test timeouts are unchanged. This also prevents automatic backing expiry from satisfying a broken cleanup assertion.

Follow-up found while reviewing @VACInc's #154930.

## Work sessions

title: fix: delayed session replies stop after the caller finishes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: accepted `sessions_send` replies can fail to wake their requester after the originating invocation or connection ends, logging `Gateway caller authority is no longer active.` even though the target finished its work.

## User Impact

Delayed cross-session replies can continue the requesting session without a manual nudge. The original operator identity, permission ceiling, device/profile/role revocation checks, and Gateway-instance boundary remain enforced.

This fixes a process-local reply handoff. It does **not** make pending `sessions_send` replies survive Gateway restarts or claim that every idle session is stalled. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detached reply flow shed its tool-call context but retained a request-lifetime authority callback. Its later reply admission tried to capture authority from that expired request.

Retain the existing operator source through the reply flow using the normal dispatch/authority owner, then release it in `finally`. The registered tool passes the actual detached promise to that owner instead of returning immediately from a `void` callback. Ordinary cleanup keeps its existing contract.

## Evidence

- Original RED: the real A2A reply flow and in-process Gateway facade captured the target result, then failed with the expired-authority error and admitted zero requester turns. GREEN admits one turn; device revocation and Gateway replacement still refuse it, and holds release after settlement.
- Review follow-up RED: with `gateway.roles` enabled, normal clientless dispatch succeeded but the continuation wrapper rejected the same request as `FORBIDDEN`. The existing resolver now receives the same system-actor hint as ordinary built-in dispatch. GREEN proves real clientless admission and keeps already-scoped unknown callers rejected.
- [The original exact-head CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35648574885/job/106495596380) was a stale explicit `in-process-gateway` mock missing the new async continuation helper. The full `sessions.test.ts` reproduced **58 failures / 50 passes** before the mock repair and passed **all 108 tests** after repair, before the extraction below. No broad partial mock or weakened assertion was added.
- Roles/mocks follow-up before extraction: **165 tests passed** across the continuation, authorization, full sessions, and registered-tool admission files. This includes the original hold-lifetime and revocation cases.
- Fresh scoped autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Core and affected test-graph typechecks, formatting, and lint passed; unchanged guard receipts from the initial fix remain applicable.
- Single-worker wall (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): continuation **12.29 s** (13 tests), pre-extraction sessions **9.76 s** (108 tests). The unchanged admission file previously measured **18.24 s** (5 tests). Compiler/import work dominates; no sleeps or real-time polling were added.

- CI ratchet follow-up: reproduced `sessions.test.ts: 1934 -> 1935 counted lines (cap 1000)` locally. Moved the two self-contained stored-assistant-text suites intact into `chat-history-text.test.ts`; all **8 tests / 11 assertions** are byte-for-byte preserved. The retained sessions suite passes **100 tests** and the extracted suite passes **8**, preserving the original **108** total. No production code, guard, baseline, or suppression changed.
- The pinned-base line-cap ratchet now passes. The affected test type graph, formatting, lint, and fresh scoped autoreview also pass. Latest one-worker wall cost is **21.50 s** for the retained sessions suite (including compiler preparation) and **1.77 s** for the extracted text suite; no additional runtime setup or timers were added.

title: fix(codex): retain recent answers after tool-heavy thread rotation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex forgets its recent answer when a tool-heavy conversation leaves only assistant/tool history in the bounded window and a new native thread starts.

## User Impact

Follow-up requests such as “give me the TLDR” retain the recent explanation after native thread rotation. Existing history limits, tool-payload omission, provenance boundaries, and resumed-thread deduplication stay unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A fresh thread now recognizes nonblank assistant text as useful continuity even when the earlier user turn has fallen outside the retained window. The existing bounded, quoted-context projection still owns rendering. Empty, whitespace-only, and tool-only histories do not activate this new path.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite bounded-history regression asserts actual `turn/start` text. Fresh and tool-schema-rotated cases failed before the production fix; fresh, rotated, resumed, empty, and tool-only/whitespace cases now pass. Synthetic fixtures only.
- Fixed all three source-relevant failures from [the initial hosted run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35646585374): hook/diagnostic assertions now match the actual quoted request while public diagnostics remain payload-free; prompt-hook coverage verifies the existing one-build/empty and two-build/continuity paths without duplicating the current request or plugin decorations; the new SQLite suite is registered with its existing database-worker owner. No discovery assertions were weakened or skipped.
- **681 tests passed** across seven complete files: 191 run-attempt, 16 hooks, 7 bounded-continuity, 43 context-engine, 4 durable-context, 64 context-projection, and 356 test-discovery/routing cases. This includes the unchanged exact-once normal full-suite discovery assertion and the existing stable developer-instruction checks.
- Full current-source `check:changed` passed for all five PR paths: production/test types, formatting, full extension lint (10,335 files), script lint (1,123 files), all dead-export scans, plugin boundaries, and applicable source guards. `git diff --check` passed.
- CI-repair autoreview: **scoped-clean through P2**, no actionable findings. The original production-review proposal to exclude all assistant messages carrying tool calls remains rejected: nonblank text can be legitimate quoted history, unlike textless tool traffic; tool payload omission is unchanged.
- **[Hosted CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35648960474)** on exact head `4c52c43627ac638b5726faea71298ddeae1b1724`, including the CI workflow’s aggregate gate job. The formerly failing named jobs—changed-extensions-config-19, changed-extensions-config-20, and compact-small-1—all completed successfully.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and lifecycle rationale</summary>

Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: bounded-continuity **50.11 s wall** (including 18.86 s shared worker preparation), hooks **11.93 s**, and the existing 191-case run-attempt suite **104.88 s**. The combined seven-file proof took **247.81 s**. The bounded regression needs the real SQLite selector and native request boundary; a projection-helper-only test did not cover the skipped continuity gate. The changed hook case was moved out of the oversized main suite and extended with the empty-history sibling rather than growing that file. The canonical pipeline builds developer instructions before native thread startup, then rebuilds turn input if the actual startup action requires continuity. The repair does not add another hook lifecycle: assistant-only histories now use that existing path. Both builds retain the raw `currentUserMessage`; `llm_input`, private model diagnostics, and failure snapshots match the submitted model-bound prompt.

</details>

This is current-source harness/request proof, not a live provider rerun of the original conversation. The original thread-rotation trigger was not retained; the regression exercises a deterministic tool-schema rotation.

title: fix(ui): stop Cmd+K results jittering while typing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes jittering Cmd+K search results and excessive session-search requests while typing.

## User Impact

Text stays responsive; results update after a short 200 ms pause instead of on every keystroke. Enter applies the current query immediately and opens an available matching command; it never selects an old result. Clearing restores commands immediately. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Local filtering and remote searches now share one debounce. Settled results remain visible but cannot be selected for an unfinished query, and older requests are invalidated immediately. Closing, changing context, and IME composition cancel pending work without breaking native prompt editing. Enter uses the same search owner and resolves the new result list synchronously; later remote responses never trigger deferred navigation.

CI repair is inherited from [#155111](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155111), now merged into this branch from main. It replaces readiness polling with real publication/acceptance signals and owns request cleanup. The Cmd+K delta remains patch-identical; no duplicate approval-test patch is included here.

Cc @jalehman.

title: fix: personal USER context changes when another participant joins
body:
Follow-up to #153966.

## What Problem This Solves

Personal instructions followed the latest sender rather than the person responsible for the session, and workspace paths could misclassify shared `USER.md` as personal.

## User Impact

Each session selects **one personal `USER.md`: its assigned human owner, otherwise its authenticated human creator**. Shared workspace `USER.md` loads first; the selected personal file supplements it. Another participant can steer normally without substituting their own file or encountering a personal-profile-only restriction. Existing operator, permission, tool, and delivery rules still apply.

Reassignment takes effect on the next new turn, including queued execution—not during a running task. Missing personal files or qualifying human metadata leave shared defaults. Internal, synthetic, and delegated input remains excluded.

For example: Alice creates the session, so it uses shared `USER.md` plus Alice's personal file. Assigning it to Bob changes that to shared plus Bob's personal file on the next new turn—never both personal files. If Bob has no personal file, only shared defaults apply. With no personal file configured, ordinary single-user prompts and steering stay on the shared-default path, without additional personal prompt text or UI.

This intentionally replaces latest-sender selection with the session-owned policy requested in the work session. No UI, schema, configuration, file migration, or live Gateway changes. This is prompt selection, not filesystem or history isolation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse authoritative session ownership/creation metadata and the existing canonical profile loader. Carry external-turn eligibility through queued and collected execution, and refresh queued profile selection from current session metadata. Personal preferences are no longer part of tool-authority comparison.

The earlier path fix remains: only loader-marked files receive personal budgeting and prompt/CLI handling; directory names cannot activate it.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc
- @steipete

## Work sessions

- **ClawSweeper overflow finding repaired:** ordinary summaries, compacted sources, and deferred retries now preserve external-turn eligibility. The new queue-to-execution regression changed from **3 failed / 9 passed** to **12 passed**, while mixed/internal/unknown sources remain excluded. It also verifies current-owner refresh and exactly-once source adoption/settlement.
- **229 adjacent queue/execution tests pass** in 28.81 s. The new 12-case file took 49.45 s wall including cold compiled-worker preparation; individual cases took 3–27 ms. Hosted CI ran all 12 in `checks-node-compact-small-11` / `auto-reply-reply-state-routing`: **0.052 s summed test-body time** (2–12 ms per case, excluding runner/import overhead). The shared fixture now exposes the real pending-input binding rather than another stub.
- Fresh scoped P0–P2 review of the overflow repair is clean. Scoped changed checks pass (core and test types, lint, dead exports, cycles, and policy guards). **Exact-head verification complete for `a46799c1b8896ce82122437b28d095d568a42632`:** [CI run 35646892461](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35646892461) passed on attempt 1 (131 successful jobs, 16 skipped, zero failures). Both the Actions check and classic `openclaw/ci-gate` status succeeded; [Security Review 35649231050](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35649231050) also passed.
- [ClawSweeper Revision 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154980#issuecomment-5763982517) reviewed that exact head, resolved the overflow finding, and reports **no actionable findings or security findings**; ready for maintainer review (4/6). This does not substitute for maintainer approval or authorize merging.

- Real persisted-creator and guarded-file coverage rejects sender-file substitution; owner-selection and queued-refresh regressions cover precedence and reassignment. Other coverage protects shared-first/one-personal-file ordering, missing-file fallback, aliases, provenance, and read/budget boundaries.
- Registered steering accepts a participant change without changing the running personal context, while genuine operator/source/permission changes still reject. Internal effective provenance and synthetic ingress remain excluded; collected and overflow metadata retain eligibility only for wholly eligible external sources.
- **128 non-personal context combinations remain byte-identical** to the published path-fix head. No additional default single-user prompt text.

title: fix: avoid false failures while an agent waits for a child
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a successful pause while waiting for a child can display a false agent failure and discard previously streamed commentary.

## User Impact

Waiting turns retain their commentary without a cleanup-generated failure message. Genuine failures and unresolved tool diagnostics remain available. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main already suppresses stale tool warnings during a successful yield (#153779). This repairs the remaining producer: the aborted cleanup assistant is not authoritative when terminal settlement records a successful pause. Payload generation uses that pause outcome and attempt-local text, while the original tool-error state and diagnostic metadata remain intact.

Credit: Dallin Romney for the report and requested repair.

## Work sessions

title: fix: show when a timed-out session send may still arrive
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session send reports a generic failure when the Gateway response deadline expires even though the original request can still take effect.

## User Impact

Callers can distinguish an unconfirmed dispatched request from one that was not sent, retain the original operation and target identities, and avoid blindly duplicating input. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the typed client-timeout facts at the send-result owner and in its strict output schema. A dispatched request is not an acceptance receipt: the timeout result remains an error and does not by itself assert sentBeforeError; a higher-level retained followup receipt may independently establish acceptance. The result explains reconciliation before another send. The existing deadline, cancellation, and retry behavior are unchanged. Cron fallback errors retain the actual dispatched parent/key instead of the abandoned original identity. The typed result extends main’s existing canonical schema owner; the already-landed extraction is preserved.

Credit: Dallin Romney for the report and requested repair.
