title: fix(doctor): check the operator state volume during mixed lint
body:
Related: #117415

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor lint missing critically low free space when a disk-space check runs alongside a plugin check whose private snapshot is on a healthier volume.

## User Impact

The opt-in check measures the operator’s state volume during mixed lint runs. Existing thresholds remain: below 100 MiB is an error; 100 MiB through less than 500 MiB is a warning. Ordinary environment fallback, selection, severity filtering and post-update readiness behavior are unchanged. This fix requires no schema migration or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registered detector forwards the lint context’s existing environment to the existing disk-space owner. Plugin checks retain private-state isolation, and current coverage is preserved.

## Evidence

Tested candidate: `99b82f2b4c3a661e3e5cfcf05dc37d16f907dafd`  
Base: `761725d03f294aaddc399a759a0755d34a0e1ecf`  
Tree: `be44f932acfe01475186e0bd85337f599694f8a3`

Signed publication head: `943fa8cf8637ce9d729104c6f39713fa5e22e6d1`. Its tree and single parent exactly match the tested candidate; publication changed commit metadata, not source bytes.

| Check | Result | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current mixed-lint and post-plugin snapshot regressions, one worker | Exit 0; **2 selected tests passed**, 21 outside the filter | 33.81s; tests 2.913s / 2.772s |
| Exact-base/head selected changed aggregate | Exit 0; selected types, lint, formatting, config docs, dead-export scans and guards passed | 578.76s |
| One canonical full build, pack and tarball integrity check | Exit 0 | 542.89s; build 487.9s |
| Published `openclaw@2026.9.4` → candidate, maintained `projects-doctor` cell | Exit 0; one attempt, original-driver update succeeded without follow-up repair | 95.71s runner / 83s scenario |
| Generated release checks | **Exit 1**: plugin-version and UI fallback-catalog drift | 76.05s |
| Full release integrity/size check | **Exit 1**: unpacked-size budget exceeded; tarball integrity itself passed | 78.12s |

**Release qualification remains red.** The frozen candidate needs version alignment for `@openclaw/facetime`, `@openclaw/onnx` and `@openclaw/typesafe`, plus a Control UI fallback-catalog baseline update. Unpacked size was **256,945,332 bytes**, above the **246,415,360-byte** budget. These inputs are unchanged by this patch. No version/baseline/budget exception or baseline-size comparison was used; successful bug-specific checks are not a release-ready claim.

**Regression:** disk capacity is injected, but the registered lint/config/snapshot flow is real. It covers critical findings, the exact 100 MiB boundary, filtering, exit status and source SQLite preservation. The earlier reproduction failed before the repair. No live low-disk proof is claimed.

**Compatibility:** the unmodified published 9.4 driver installed this exact candidate. The harness verified both application payloads and ran installed Doctor twice while preserving project/workspace state and snapshot lifecycle. An ordinary first-hop advisory warning was retained; no zero-warning assertion was added. This is not Gateway startup/restart, health/readiness/RPC or live-disk proof.

Package SHA-256: `583c4395671cb425c268df01ccfb28c77b4575bc9b0da5e1fa250d771a0cee46`. Build-info identifies the candidate commit. [Testbox carrier/hydration run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35588797238) is not PR exact-head CI.

At inspected main `28dbfcc05f2fceb49fb29a17c7d9a60133b5dde5`, the lint route, affected owner and nine direct inputs are unchanged from the tested base. Lint still preserves captured `sourceEnv`, private plugin state and explicit `coreCtx.env`; the collector only resolves the path and reads capacity. No contrary call-graph interaction was found. Frozen-candidate compatibility remains valid for that candidate; latest-main runtime execution is unproved. Current exact merge-ref CI must exercise integration, and native drift guards still apply.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence and preserved execution failures</summary>

- **220 tests** previously passed on `14ad80a1aea9dfac39bca02410d722f444a1027e` / base `47f1d6ad8eb67a0e22db2191f9da9a386eb08e5b`. This is old-input evidence, not 220 tests rerun on the current candidate. The identical patch’s independent P2 scoped-clean review was reused.

title: feat(skills): add opt-in Skill Search lab
body:
Related: #43950 (local skill discoverability; this is Code Mode search, not a registration service).

## What Problem This Solves

Agents cannot discover otherwise eligible skills omitted from the prompt directory, but expanding discovery must be an explicit experiment rather than a default behavior change.

## User Impact

**Skill Search is a Labs feature, off by default.** Enable it in **Settings → Labs → Skill Search** or opt in through config:

```json5
{
  skills: { experimental: { search: true } },
}
```

It requires Code Mode; the switch does not enable Code Mode itself. With the flag absent or false, `skills.search` is not installed or advertised, and `skills.list/read` retain prompt-admitted scope. With it enabled, agents can search and read the full policy-eligible catalog without expanding the prompt directory. Manual-only, unavailable-secret, and tool-execution exclusions remain enforced. Existing worker resource-transfer limits still apply.

Changes apply to future agent runs without restarting the Gateway. Turning the lab off narrows the next catalog again, including after a cold session resume. No live Gateway settings were changed during development.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing local BM25 ranker and skill-snapshot owner, not a separate search service. The same boolean gate controls catalog breadth, interactive/headless guest exposure, host dispatch, and guidance. Cached snapshots retain the selected mode so opt-in and opt-out invalidate the right projection. Sandbox/remote remapping preserves the bounded prompt directory.

Inspired by [SkillRanker](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/skillranker), this local-first version adds no inference provider, network ranking calls, dependencies, transcript capture, learned reranker, or native Codex discovery API.

## Evidence

title: fix(daemon): keep native service checks within their timeout
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native service inspection can reuse its full timeout at successive stages, start additional Windows process/listener checks after the budget is spent, or accept late observations as current service state. Cleanup failures can also be hidden by ordinary diagnostic fallbacks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry one remaining inspection budget through command, registration, runtime, and Windows Startup/process/port reads. Stop admitting work after expiry, keep expired ordinary diagnostics unknown, and preserve strict-operation failures. Join admitted parallel reads before returning and propagate cleanup/ownership refusals.

The absent-Gateway status fix is already on main through #154637. This PR now contains only the remaining native-inspection work; the superseded status adapter, readiness shortcut, status documentation, and associated tests have been removed. Existing systemd target selection, Windows structured diagnostics, and main's startup/legacy-owner safeguards are preserved. Related: #154549.

## User Impact

Diagnostic reads share the caller's existing budget. Explicitly timed Windows reads retain exact positive process matches and report unknown when incomplete process or listener evidence cannot establish a stopped service. Untimed lifecycle defaults remain unchanged. No configuration or stored-data format changes.

## Evidence

- Refreshed onto main `4acdf1a4f3b` while preserving the original authored commits. Reduced the introduced diff from 31 files / +2,597 net lines to 25 files / +1,297 net lines. The existing maintenance fixture table moved to its support module unchanged to respect the line cap.
- Focused shared-service, Windows, and existing diagnostic-readiness suites passed. The exhausted-budget regression failed on current main and passed on the candidate. Two PID-0 regressions failed before the review correction and passed afterward.
- Final Windows deadline plus maintenance run: 96 tests passed with `--maxWorkers=1`, 35.72 seconds wrapper wall. The earlier Windows/diagnostic group passed in 31.47 seconds; command-reader/deadline/maintenance group passed 140 cases in 18.26 seconds. These groups overlap and are not additive. Most cold-run wall time was compilation.
- Full `pnpm build` passed in 11m55.6s before the final PID-0 predicate/test correction and unused-export cleanup; the behavior correction passed focused tests and fresh review, and final production types passed. Repository changed-file checks: production types, all 25 core test-type groups, formatting, lint, and required static guards passed. The aggregate run initially stopped at unused exports; those were removed, then the failed and remaining checks passed separately.
- Fresh independent review through P2 found no remaining actionable findings after fixing PID 0 incorrectly preventing a stopped observation. Native evidence remains conservative for unreadable real process rows.
- Validation recovery: a timeout fixture initially expected the full allowance instead of the remaining budget; a controlled clock preserves its exact assertion. One post-extraction test attempt ran no tests because the concurrent build changed package resolution during compilation; the serialized final run passed. The line-cap failure was resolved by the unchanged fixture extraction, with no removed cases or assertions.
- Refreshed onto main `48f886998765` without changing the production patch. The prior Windows Crabbox PID-reuse assertion failure passed on the refreshed head. A related status fixture still assumed no elapsed wall time; its clock is now controlled, with guaranteed restoration, and the complete case moved into existing service-inspection test support to satisfy the line cap. All 133 status tests and 16 deadline tests passed; fresh review found no actionable findings.
- Addressed ClawSweeper’s cleanup-propagation finding: the registered status command now preserves cleanup refusals before diagnostic sanitization. Its regression failed before the fix; all 134 status tests pass after it. Restored the systemd absence-probe contract: a present or unverifiable system owner means absence is not proven, while actual ownership changes and cleanup failures remain fatal. The original three CI failures reproduced locally; all 17 unchanged absence tests plus 16 deadline tests pass after the producer repair. Fresh review, changed-file checks, production/service types, and targeted lint pass.
- Final-head CI: [run 36199443125](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36199443125) passed for `d36ae040a6069759ebb3489b07a80d36fd877210`, including all five Windows shards and the previously failing status/service-absence shards. ClawSweeper reviewed the same head with no actionable code findings and platinum hermit patch quality; the overall gold rating reflects the installed-platform and updater qualification gaps below.

Installed Windows 11 ARM64 qualification now covers the exact candidate’s Scheduled Task and Startup lifecycle, required-RPC health, real native inspection expiry, deferred-repair state preservation, and completed normal repair recovery. [Detailed Windows evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154565#issuecomment-5841879868). The published 2026.9.5 updater installed the candidate but failed its schema-handoff/autostart recovery; this is not a clean published-upgrade pass. title: fix(exec): avoid approval prompts for read-only audit suppression searches
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Read-only searches mentioning `security.audit.suppressions` were receiving the extra approval intended for suppression edits. Related: #82728.

## User Impact

Trusted, completely analyzed file inspections can avoid that extra prompt, while ordinary exec/node approval rules still apply. Writes, mixed commands, redirections, executable-bearing options, uncertain analysis, dispatch wrappers, and startup-bearing shells remain gated. The shipped direct config get/schema/validate exception and existing full/off behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared policy consumes the existing authorization plan, executable resolution, root-option parser, and shell-startup owner. Both lexical and canonical executable paths must be trusted. It distinguishes new file inspections from legacy direct config reads so hosts can preserve the inspected command through final execution.

Gateway inspections use the existing pinned renderer without loading saved shell aliases/functions. The actual implicit shell must also be an absolute, trusted, startup-free POSIX transport; unsupported envelopes retain approval. Nodes use the existing planned-argv and identity checks through final dispatch, including the companion request. This prevents a checked reader from being replaced by a snapshot function, dispatch wrapper, or intervening PATH change.

Duplicated option parsing and repeated policy-drift fixtures were consolidated without removing assertions. The full diff against pinned main `202336dcd5f7032bc53b23069220a2c51da44749` is **+1,001/−543, net +458 across 19 files**. It is not net-negative: closing the demonstrated final-execution gaps adds binding logic and real regressions. Upstream deletions are not credited to this cleanup. Main was integrated only for the actual Gateway fixture conflict.

## Evidence

Latest tested source: `45a3c775d4f885a91945f2706f6a80d69b885c56`.

- **217 passed / 2 platform skips across six suites** on the dispatch correction: node system.run (97), Gateway approvals (50), suppression policy (44), real Gateway execution (14 + 1 skip), SDK review input (6), and node allowlist (6 + 1 skip). The implicit-shell qualification then passed the Gateway/integration suites and three new envelope cases. Final focused validation passed **79 tests**: ordinary policy (70), SDK (6), and shell envelopes (3). These overlapping scoped runs are not added into a misleading single total.
- Core production types and affected test graphs passed. Scoped lint reported **0 warnings/errors**; formatting, diff checks, current-base line-cap checks, and runtime cycle checks passed.
- Real `createExecTool` proof first reproduced a saved `grep` function mutating the synthetic audit file under full/on-miss. Direct and pipeline inspections now read the unchanged fixture without starting the snapshot; full/off still executes the writer control. The same test supplies an inherited writer-bearing `BASH_ENV` and proves the actual environment owner removes it.
- Real node execution first reproduced a reader inserted earlier in PATH during policy commit. Direct/payload drift now fails before runner invocation or I/O; transport drift uses the pinned original shell. Workspace reader/dispatcher, nested wrapper, symlink, and startup negatives remain, with full/off writer controls.
- Independent reviews completed and findings were checked against the actual owners. The snapshot finding is repaired. The conditional `BASH_ENV` concern is rejected with producer source plus real Gateway and node proof. The final transport review identified an unconditional Windows qualification; that branch now conservatively returns false, leaving legacy direct reads unaffected.

### Compatibility and limits

The helper shipped through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime` in v2026.9.6. Its boolean API and legacy `{command, segments}` direct-read exemption remain, with or without raw segment text. Legacy source is independently reanalyzed and must match one complete segment and argv. Failed analysis, writes, mixed commands, forged argv, and generic readers without authorization plans remain gated. Three legacy read regressions failed before the compatibility repair and passed afterward.

Current real execution proof is Linux Bash/sh/grep. Windows analysis is exercised in policy/Gateway/SDK tests; native Windows/macOS execution is not claimed. The implicit zsh/tcsh/PATH-shell tests prove rejection at the envelope boundary, not native shell execution. Prior real zsh/fish proof is retained only for the unchanged explicit-node startup classifier. No live profiles, configuration, or deployment were changed.

ClawSweeper revision 11 completed on published head `991ad1f0431e078805ec4e90b5fa14f46c57bae6` at 2026-09-29 22:43 UTC: no actionable code/security findings, and real behavior proof is sufficient. Landing is paused for a scope decision about the shared startup classifier: non-login zsh/fish commands unrelated to suppressions can also lose auto-review eligibility, affecting headless workflows. Related: #154079 (replacement; the original PR remains untouched).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release validation rejecting the frozen 2026.7.35 candidate because current tooling expects newer plugin setup and native filesystem APIs that it does not ship.

## User Impact

No installed runtime change. Release managers can validate the explicitly selected frozen candidate against its actual contracts. Current, unknown, prerelease, and native-consuming candidates remain strict; this does not authorize publishing a retired release line or waive release gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

This release-manager-requested backwards-compatibility workaround extends the existing exact-version records, rather than changing frozen product bytes. Only the candidate SDK consumer omits the newer setup fixture; the separate released SDK consumer still compiles. Native proof remains required unless the existing explicit frozen-source permission, distinct tooling SHA, canonical extended-stable ancestry, exact dependency, and Python-only source checks all pass. The compatibility records can retire when this frozen candidate is no longer an admitted validation target.

Source proposal: #154079 by @RomneyDa. Independently reimplemented and verified on current main for this replacement.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/664185d8-1ca6-44bb-b54b-09964fcca899)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/353ec067-1f8c-4473-bccb-c0ea34ae43fd)

## Evidence

- Reproduced both regressions on base `ce96471e68b116d2f3baf6135584c02dcfc42963`: the new SDK case returned false; the 2026.7.35 native-contract case returned required. The remaining 57 tests passed.
- `pnpm test test/release-check.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 51 passed; wall 13.48 s (Vitest 11.85 s).
- `pnpm test test/scripts/resolve-fs-safe-native-contract.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 passed; final wall 14.29 s (Vitest 6.64 s, test bodies 3.10 s) on the shared host; earlier equivalent run 2.65 s wall. Covers frozen permission, current SHA, changed dependency, native markers, unknown versions, and prerelease SDK strictness.
- Exact-source resolver CLI for `690ddec83b6931e7a4410159f919a6afcac3abce`: required before, not-applicable after; canonical containing branch verified.
- Downloaded the original prepared npm artifact from [run 35536670766](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35536670766), verified tarball SHA-256 `7ae6d2634901e75e717eef88a5bec00ac090972b93bc4af08613784146689f60`, and inspected its declaration signatures: no setupSurface. Its failure log records TS2353 at that fixture. [Candidate run 35536969625](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35536969625) records the missing fs-safe durability export. Registry metadata independently confirms fs-safe 0.4.1 exports neither native nor durability.
- Full selected `pnpm check:changed -- <four changed files>` passed, including script/root-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, dead-export scans, and applicable guards. The initial test-fixture indexed-access type error was corrected and this complete gate rerun passed.
- Independent pre-commit AutoReview completed scoped-clean at its default P0 threshold.

title: fix(ui): reduce chat composer typing lag
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces chat-composer typing lag, reported in Arc with both English and Chinese input after several conversation turns.

## User Impact

Typing no longer repeatedly rebuilds height-query-dependent parts of the chat layout. The composer still grows and shrinks with its draft, respects short-pane height caps, and preserves transcript scrolling and bottom anchoring. No configuration, API, storage, or migration changes.

This fixes a reproduced Chromium layout hot path; it does not claim that message count alone explains every slowdown or that the reporter's Arc installation has already been verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Cause

`.chat-main__conversation` was both a flex-sized item and the `chat-conversation / size` query container. Synchronous textarea autosizing repeatedly flushed a layout that also had to resolve that container's size. Traces showed repeated changes and reattachments in query-controlled layout objects, including footer-related objects and position-rail markers, despite unchanged settled bounds and no transcript DOM mutations. This is layout-tree churn, not a re-render of every historical message.

### Fix

Add a small outer frame that owns flex allocation, and let the existing conversation size-query container fill that definite region with `position: absolute; inset: 0`. Keep the internal flex layout, named queries, height caps, wheel handler, and conversation contents intact. Update the affected layout fixtures and add a deterministic regression for the repeated layout invalidations.

The fix does not remove responsive queries, hardcode a pixel height, freeze the editor, or debounce user input.

## Evidence

### Test plan and results

- **13 Chromium layout tests passed**, including the new regression and existing footer/swarm layouts. The regression exercises the complete grid/flex chain and synchronous textarea measurement; the original sizing reproduced footer-related reattachments, while the fixed sizing produced none. It also checks unchanged settled bounds and that the short-pane query still activates at 260 px, lowers the editor cap, and leaves transcript space without overlap.
- **379 chat-view/footer-view tests passed**. Total focused coverage: **392 passing tests**.
- **Actual-source full-UI browser checks passed** with a mocked Gateway at 1440×900, 390×844, and 600×320: a 40-line mixed English/Chinese draft grows and caps; clearing it shrinks the editor; the footer stays inside the pane; typing at the end stays bottom-anchored; typing while reading older messages does not jump to the tail; resizing still updates the layout.
- Targeted formatting, stylesheet lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent autoreview identified one test-typing issue; the textarea callback now explicitly uses `HTMLTextAreaElement`, matching the installed Playwright generic contract, and the affected browser suites were rerun.
- Measured local test cost with `--maxWorkers=1`: the new browser regression took 0.790 s; both layout suites took 4.03 s wall time (2.93 s reported by Vitest). The two view suites reported 6.63 s. CI timing is not yet available. The regression uses structural trace assertions, not a wall-clock performance threshold.

### Optimization results

Controlled comparison using the actual source UI based on `ac638483c78` plus this patch, 200 loaded synthetic messages, a 1440×900 viewport, 32 ASCII input events, and no CPU throttling. Both samples used Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 / Playwright 1.63.0 with CDP tracing enabled. The before case restores the previous sizing via CSS on the same candidate; it is not a separately built old release or a measurement on the reporter's machine.

| Measurement | Previous sizing | Fixed source |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cumulative style recalculation time | 928.768 ms | 23.948 ms |
| Cumulative layout time | 58.420 ms | 14.590 ms |
| Median input-to-next-animation-frame interval | 19.4 ms | 8.0 ms |
| Footer-related `Added to layout` trace records | 198 | 0 |
| Position-rail marker `Added to layout` trace records | 3,861 | 0 |
| Pane render calls | 3 | 3 |
| Transcript DOM mutations | 0 | 0 |

The style-recalculation total dropped by about **97%** in this diagnostic sample. Conversation, transcript, footer, and composer bounds were identical. These are scoped microbenchmark results, not a universal input-latency guarantee; input-to-animation-frame timing is not INP or a paint-completion measurement.

### Landing CI follow-up

Hosted CI found two issues in the regression test, not in the production layout repair: Playwright declares generic trace records as string dictionaries, and the Promise executor returned the event emitter. The test now validates the structured Chromium records it consumes with a runtime schema, fails on malformed records, and returns void from the executor. All 13 layout tests passed again (4.63 s reported by Vitest; regression 1.374 s), with scoped type-aware lint and UI test typechecking also passing.

The separate `release-check` fixture timeout in the original CI run has an upstream fixture repair already on main ([#154335](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154335), `868ad470d0e`). It removes repeated full CLI/tarball work while retaining validator and CLI coverage. The exact original subprocess stall is not claimed to be infrastructure-only or deterministically reproduced. No release code, timeout, or retry policy is changed here; fresh exact-head CI must validate the updated candidate with current main.

### Verification limits

The standard `chat-footer.e2e.test.ts` launcher stopped before tests at an inherited-proxy loopback preflight (HTTP 502). The separate full-UI mock-Gateway browser checks above passed; they are not reported as a passing standard E2E run. That initial checkout also could not run type-aware lint because its compiler dependencies were borrowed. Landing verification now uses an isolated checkout with its own frozen dependencies: scoped type-aware oxlint and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` both pass. The reporter's actual Arc session and complete CI remain unverified.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and benchmark procedure</summary>

Equivalent focused commands in a normal dependency-ready checkout:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/pages/chat/chat-footer-layout.browser.test.ts \
  ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-swarm-progress.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts \
  ui/src/pages/chat/chat-footer-view.test.ts
```

Local runs used the same UI config with only `cacheDir` redirected into the task worktree because the selected dependency installation was immutable; no tests or guards were disabled.

For the browser comparison:
1. Start the source Control UI with `startControlUiE2eServer` and `installMockGateway`; seed 200 alternating user/assistant messages. Use fresh contexts, the same viewport, and a settled focused composer.
2. Keep the patched layout for the fixed case. For the control, set the frame to `display: contents` and restore the conversation's `position: relative`, `inset: auto`, and `flex: 1 1 auto`. Retain all size queries in both cases.
3. Type the same 32 characters at a configured 12 ms key delay. Compare CDP `Performance.getMetrics` deltas and timeline layout invalidations. Record input-to-next-animation-frame samples separately.
4. Confirm equal settled geometry and zero transcript DOM mutations; then separately exercise draft growth, clear, scrolling, and viewport changes against the unmodified fixed source.

</details>

- @hxy91819

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/a7a90d12-18eb-4e56-81e7-09105c1d560f)

title: fix(exec): stop rejecting valid JavaScript script contents
body:
Related: #12836

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: exec rejects valid JavaScript files containing dollar-prefixed identifiers, ordinary dollar text, or a `NODE:` label before Node can run them.

## User Impact

User impact: valid JavaScript runs normally, and genuine syntax/runtime errors return Node’s diagnostics and nonzero exit code instead of misleading shell-injection advice. Statements before a runtime error may already have executed; this is normal interpreter behavior, not side-effect-free validation. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only the two JavaScript source-content heuristics and their obsolete advice, with no replacement scanner or syntax-check subprocess. Skip the now-unnecessary JavaScript content reads after command classification. Keep Python lexical checking and guarded reads, complex-command restrictions, approval/revalidation, and sandbox routing unchanged.

Retarget filesystem-safety fixtures to Python and replace obsolete JavaScript rejection expectations with real execution and native-diagnostic checks.

## Evidence

### Current-head hosted acceptance

**Required CI is green for `0023fb0b44b094ebbf922e9534e66c5d806c5b71`.** [CI run 35569616540](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35569616540) completed successfully: 147 successful jobs, 15 skipped, zero failures. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` publications and dependency/security-sensitive statuses succeeded. Skipped jobs are not execution proof.

- [Original corpus group](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35569616540/job/106238547492): same ten-file order/config and two-worker pin; **59/59 passed in 279.04 s**.
- [Full hosted Discord envelope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35569616540/job/106238547880): **289 files / 4,079 tests passed in 107.21 s**, including the repaired lifecycle case (369 ms) and pacing case (3,296 ms). Hosted Discord used three workers, not the two-worker local setup.
- Hosted tests ran synthetic merge `ea7f01dd444819102363d5beb489e55cad74e436` (candidate plus main `591f7bad7e333a6a879e38cfffab7bbc17055800`), not literally the local candidate tree.
- ClawSweeper revision 3 reviewed this exact head, accepted the production-boundary proof, and found no actionable defects.

The earlier failed local Discord envelope remains documented below; hosted acceptance does not relabel that local run as green.

### After-change runtime proof — real execution, no mocks

Executed on Linux / Node 26.8.2 at exact PR head `5cd8bbbe40e721019f635aae4dbbc7972a12d7d3` on 2026-09-21. The runner imported the production `createExecTool` and invoked `.execute()` with **gateway / full / on-miss**, so JavaScript preflight was not skipped via full/off. Approval routing, preflight, process launch, and output handling were unmocked. A fresh isolated HOME/config/state directory and an environment containing only PATH plus those isolated paths kept the live Gateway and real credentials out of the proof. This is direct production-tool boundary proof, not a live Gateway-server or sandbox-platform test.

**Observed results (all assertions passed):**

| Input / scenario | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `const $FOO = 7; console.log($FOO);` | exit 0; stdout `7` |
| Comment `$COMMENT` plus `console.log("$HOME")` | exit 0; stdout `$HOME` |
| `NODE: { console.log("label-ok"); }` | exit 0; stdout `label-ok` |
| `NODE "$TMPDIR/hot.json"` | exit 1; native `SyntaxError: Unexpected string` |
| `console.log("before-error"); const value = $DM_JSON;` | stdout `before-error`, then exit 1 and native `ReferenceError: $DM_JSON is not defined` |
| Python `payload = $DM_JSON` | rejected before spawn by retained Python preflight |
| `cat case-0.js \| node` | rejected before spawn by retained complex-interpreter policy |
| Separate tool configured `security: "deny"` | rejected before spawn with `exec denied` |

Captured diagnostic excerpt (only the task-local workdir was redacted):

```text
file://<proof-workdir>/case-3.js:1
NODE "$TMPDIR/hot.json"
     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
SyntaxError: Unexpected string
(Command exited with code 1)

before-error
file://<proof-workdir>/case-4.js:1
console.log("before-error"); const value = $DM_JSON;
                                           ^
ReferenceError: $DM_JSON is not defined
(Command exited with code 1)

exec preflight: detected likely shell variable injection ($DM_JSON) in python script: bad.py:1.
exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run without script preflight validation.
PASS: 8 real-exec scenarios
```

The native-error cases asserted `status: "completed"`, `exitCode: 1`, the actual interpreter error, and absence of `exec preflight:`; the runtime-error case also asserted that the earlier stdout survived. The three valid JavaScript cases asserted exact output and exit 0. No production code changes were needed for this proof.

### CI follow-up and refreshed-candidate proof

Published head **`0023fb0b44b094ebbf922e9534e66c5d806c5b71`** is a GitHub-verified signed merge. Its tree `6719903786e4de3c71013f5f5681a575f706253f` exactly matches the locally tested candidate `8fe32107a37aa0eb8e5b67dece0af8400436d8ef`; both preserve parents consisting of the original PR head and pinned canonical main. No source differences were introduced by server-side signing.

ClawSweeper revision 2 accepted the production-boundary evidence and reported no actionable findings. Initial hosted CI nevertheless failed; **the refreshed head has now passed the required GitHub checks**.

- The failed Discord worker fixtures came from main, not this PR. The prepared candidate includes the complete canonical repair [6319111d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6319111df2121b72478de3be5691360ecb6d7e5c), which compiles worker fixtures once without increasing deadlines or weakening assertions. Both originally failing cases now pass in the full local envelope (529 ms and 3510 ms) and in an isolated two-case run (2/2, 8.12 s).
- The original corpus group was replayed in its original 10-file/two-worker configuration: **59/59 passed**, 251.65 s test duration (296.16 s wall). Exact-base CI had also passed those 59 cases in 262.56 s, versus 1469.52 s on the failed PR runner, whose unrelated worker compilation/startup phases were substantially slower too. This supports an environmental performance anomaly; the exact mechanism is unproven, and the local Node 26 run is not an exact reproduction of the Node 24.19 CI host.
- Refreshed local candidate `8fe32107a37aa0eb8e5b67dece0af8400436d8ef`, based on main `67e53329fa7278c69b1bf930d884d5d30ba57dcc`: exec regressions **76 passed / 4 Windows-only skipped**, plus **8/8 unmocked production-tool scenarios passed again**. All five PR file contents and the PR patch remain unchanged.
- **Local environment limitation:** the entire Discord envelope was not green: 3915 passed, 163 failed, one unhandled error. Failures include managed secret-egress proxy HTTP 502 refusals in HTTP fixtures and channel-target policy refusals. Those guards were not disabled; the passing focused cases do not erase this failed broad run. Full-envelope hosted acceptance is now recorded above.

### Regression and static checks (original reviewed head)

- Before the production fix, all five focused regressions failed through `createExecTool`: valid identifiers/text/labels were rejected, and genuine errors were intercepted by preflight.
- After the fix, the two focused files pass: **76 passed, 4 Windows-only cases skipped on Linux**. Includes native `SyntaxError`/`ReferenceError`, output before runtime failure, preloads, Python lexical/path/symlink/bounded-read behavior, complex Node commands, and approval operand revalidation. Node/Python execution is real; gateway approval routing is mocked in the existing harness.
- `check:changed` on all five changed files: **passed**, including core/core-test typechecks, changed-file lint, formatting, and repository guards. `git diff --check` also passed.
- Independent autoreview: **scoped-clean through P2**, no actionable findings.
- Per-file cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): `bash-tools.exec.script-preflight.test.ts` **34.45 s wall** (75 passed, 4 skipped), `bash-tools.exec-script-preflight.growth.test.ts` **1.64 s wall** (1 passed). The execution-path file pays for the existing exec harness and shared subprocess compilation; actual script launches exercise the boundary that classifier-only checks missed. The grouped run took 20.83 s. The initial hosted CI failures and follow-up are recorded above.
- The original local proof did not run the full repository suite or native Windows; current-head hosted acceptance is recorded above.

title: fix(skills): stop quarantining safety guides for prompt keywords
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Workshop quarantines legitimate safety guides when they mention hidden instructions, quote prompt-injection examples, or tell an agent not to run tools without approval.

## User Impact

Users can create, revise, and apply those guides without a keyword-only veto. The shared skill scanner and installed-skill audit stop treating these phrases as critical findings. Literal-credential rejection/redaction, other scanner rules, containment, revision/target integrity, approval policy, blocking evaluator decisions, and live-authority checks remain unchanged. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three prompt-keyword rules at their shared scanner owner rather than adding phrase or negation exceptions. Words alone do not establish an instruction override; this intentionally removes keyword detection for both benign quotations and actual override wording, without changing the agent instruction hierarchy or execution approvals.

The regression exercises real Workshop create → apply → update → revise → apply with both skill text and supporting guides. It also corrects fixture cleanup to the current agent-owned Workshop directory and registers the new suite in the existing SQLite database-worker lane.

## Evidence

### Original implementation proof

Historical evidence for preserved commit `aeb28826d7c4db57671b333f06f16c1858081314`:

- Before: all three benign-guide cases reproduced durable quarantine through real proposal creation/application.
- After: **150/150 tests passed across eight files**, covering the actual Workshop flow, installed-skill auditing, credentials, containment, revision races, evaluator blocking, and approval policy.
- Additional proof: 28 library tests, 3 tool-availability tests, and 2 routing-registry tests passed.
- Changed checks passed (exit 0), including production/test types, formatting, type-aware lint, dead exports, and repository guards. Routing-file lint/format passed.
- Independent autoreview against the pinned base was scoped-clean through P2 (exit 0).
- New integration suite: approximately **581 ms test time**; the eight-file regression run took **23.18 s wall time**. These are local measurements, not CI timings.

The original proof did not include live Gateway execution. Recovery proof below uses isolated QA fixtures, not a production Gateway.

### September 22 recovery and refreshed proof

Merged September 22 at 02:09 UTC as `70446423d62683d6253b673b8eb4c04622e58d89` through native guarded recovery, with completed hosted gates and preserved outcome history. Reviewed head: `8ff59fcb5d91b6210fb997ca7994c977ce9f61cf`. Its parent refresh commit `cfee6fa487af3519368666bf553a737fa60f6e36` retains the original implementation commit as its first parent; the latest commit only repairs a required CI test fixture.

- Full local `pnpm build` passed in **3m 59.9s**; private QA runtime builds passed. **Both complete original three-scenario smoke groups passed (6/6, zero failures or skips; both CLI exits 0)** on production-identical refresh `cfee6fa487af`; the later commit changes only the provider-timeout test fixture. Suite durations were **75.146 s** and **47.245 s**. The direct-completion scenario passed visible, silent, fallback, private, and restart cases. Empty completion succeeded with `delivery=not_applicable`, exactly one requester acknowledgment, zero terminal sends, and zero post-restart provider/completion requests. Assertions and deadlines were unchanged.
- [Refreshed-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35675089113) exposed one further test-fixture race: `provider-project-preparation.test.ts` used a real 20 ms provider deadline, which could expire during the asynchronous provisioning-state transition before the fixture captured the provider callback. This was the sole test failure in that 4,294-test shard (4,291 passed, two skipped).
- The latest **test-only** repair freezes timeout scheduling, waits for provider entry, then advances the **same 20 ms** deadline. All post-closure authority/no-write assertions remain intact. The unmodified narrow file passed 16/16 locally, so that replay is not claimed as a reproduced or repaired failure. After the deterministic repair, the owning file and two neighboring lifecycle suites passed **89/89 in 46.36 s**; changed type/lint/format/ratchet/dead-export checks passed; independent autoreview was scoped-clean through P2. The original eight-file Workshop fix and production behavior are unchanged; the overall PR now also includes this one fixture file.
- [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35677204371) **passed** for `8ff59fcb5d91b6210fb997ca7994c977ce9f61cf`; the exact-head CI watcher completed with a successful rollup and zero pending checks. The formerly failing `checks-node-compact-large-12` job passed in **919 seconds** (job wall time, not individual test time). Earlier-head CI is not substituted as new-head proof.
- Preserved the original commit and merged canonical main `da27b336c0e96cce29e8417cb82da863a57380bd` to include already-landed fixes. The eight-file Workshop delta is unchanged, with matching stable patch ID `d5f4fb60001cbabbe919997f7ff5c487e92861ca`; no new production fix, relaxed assertion, or timeout change was introduced.
- Refreshed-tree Workshop regressions: **150/150 passed** across the same eight files, **25.39 s wall time**. **Protocol check passed**, including the version guard and generated Swift/Kotlin consistency checks.
- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154441#issuecomment-5755642997) re-reviewed final head `8ff59fcb5d91b6210fb997ca7994c977ce9f61cf` at 02:05 UTC on September 22: no actionable findings or blocking introduced defects, including in the timeout-fixture repair.
- [Original PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35562686872) passed but **skipped QA Smoke CI**; it is not evidence that those scenarios passed. A [later all-skipped duplicate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35562696027) superseded it in the combined status selector.
- [Exact-old-head recovery CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35565793851) then failed the protocol version guard and two subagent smoke scenarios. The visible smoke diagnostic shows one provider request, no planned tool call, and no child task: the old mock provider recognized direct spawn/Code Mode but not the declared catalog dispatcher, so it returned a generic reply and never spawned the child. title: feat(workers): run native inference on dedicated workers
body:
Closes #154388

## What Problem This Solves

Operators need native model inference and coding-tool execution in a dedicated worker environment without placing its provider credentials on the Gateway.

## User Impact

**Windows worker-local inference is deferred.** Existing Windows Gateway/proxied-worker and CLI secret-input behavior is unchanged. The new native-inference configuration is rejected explicitly on Windows; the shared secret-input helper and its tests are byte-identical to the PR base.

An explicitly configured paired-device profile can run the native agent loop, model requests, and authorized shell/file tools together on the worker. Set `settings.inference: "worker"` to opt in. Omission or `"gateway"` keeps Gateway inference; existing embedded agents and Gateway-proxied worker inference remain the defaults. The UI labels the routes **Through Gateway** and **Direct from worker**.

Configured-default New Session creation and active worker-session follow-up messages no longer require an unused Gateway provider credential. This exception applies only to the selected published worker profile or an authoritative active worker placement. Ordinary cloud/device placements, explicit model/runtime selection, model existence, authorization, and runtime/profile compatibility checks remain enforced. Raw profile settings and credentials are not exposed.

The old device-profile spelling `runtime-local` and existing stored snapshots remain compatible; `openclaw doctor --fix` normalizes authored profile config to `worker`. The internal worker launch value remains `runtime-local`, so this naming/UI update does not change that wire contract. No database-schema, dependency, or default-mode changes. Startup credentials now travel over a private one-shot pipe rather than the initial worker environment; use compatible node-host and worker builds together.

After a worker-inference turn has been admitted, losing the Gateway connection ends that turn; reconnecting does not resume its model request. A fresh turn requires fresh admission.

The feature is opt-in, but rollout still requires compatible Gateway, node-host, and worker builds. Older nodes do not understand `nodeHost.workerRuns.nativeInferenceConfig`; retire worker-inference placements and remove native profiles/config before downgrading. The new mode is not an OS sandbox. Interactive worker exec approvals, worker LLM-review transport, automatic compaction/retry, arbitrary provider-plugin loading, and an additional OpenClaw-managed nested container remain unsupported. Approval-required execution is denied rather than approved or rerouted. Worker inference currently requires the built-in `device` provider.

**Remaining integration limit:** worker-held credentials do not make explicit model/runtime selection available in the Gateway catalog. Use the configured-default UI or CLI/API flow; explicit selection still requires Gateway-published availability. This is not a global auth bypass.



**Mandatory dedicated default (optional):** set `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile` to the native worker profile ID. Control UI removes the placement/workspace chooser and uses the agent’s configured default model. The Gateway automatically prepares and dispatches ordinary sessions under their existing create/run permissions; manual profile dispatch remains admin-only. API and channel turns enforce the same policy. An unavailable required worker blocks the turn rather than running it locally. The existing initial-message Retry/Stop and uncertain-delivery flow remains the owner.

Enabling this policy does not silently move an existing bound workspace. Existing local-folder sessions without a managed workspace need an operator-led transition or a new session. Sessionless model helpers and standalone local CLI runs are intentionally unavailable under the policy. Leave `requiredProfile` unset for existing optional placement behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse existing placement, admission, process supervision, coding tools, transcript commits, and live events instead of introducing another execution protocol. The node captures trusted model metadata and credentials at startup and projects the authorized grant to each worker. The Gateway retains session and policy authority; worker inference cannot silently fall back to Gateway inference.

The UI reads an optional, validated placement fact from the recorded profile snapshot. Only an active exact worker-turn binding publishes worker session metadata. Missing metadata means Gateway behavior. Setup, compatibility, and limits are documented in `docs/gateway/cloud-workers/native-inference.md`.

## Evidence

### Worker label — current copy update

Commit `4197fab8e3e03846f3eee3c8f3288fdf1e56f0a8` replaces the deployment-specific label with **OpenClaw worker**; the generic fallback is **Worker**. Copy only: placement, provisioning and permission behavior are unchanged.

Validation: 11 focused UI tests (5.15s wrapper wall), UI types, scoped lint and i18n checks passed. Both built-UI mocked-Gateway scenarios passed with capture enabled (17.32s Vitest); no real worker-node provisioning is claimed. The temporary Testbox was stopped and independently confirmed completed.

**Before**

![Before: Dedicated OpenClaw label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f42220a0-2378-4a16-8be7-82deffe99d36)

**After**

![After: OpenClaw worker label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37eda5e5-0bd2-46a7-99e6-dd2a2480b9e0)

### Mandatory dedicated default — current update

Commit `63681e2c7bc9d88ee21245c809d06a6440eba005`. The server policy is optional and additive; no database schema, shared Windows pipe mode, or protected baseline was changed.

- 354 existing routing/admission/recovery/protocol checks passed, plus the new required-policy/configuration checks. Real handler and channel-initialization composition uses actual SQLite and managed worktrees; only worker dispatch is a boundary fixture.
- Required and optional UI flows pass in the built Control UI against a controlled Gateway, including creation, first message, and follow-up. Required mode uses ordinary write scopes and does not advertise or call manual dispatch. [Before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154390#issuecomment-5841740169).
- Core/UI production and ten affected test type graphs passed. Documentation link/config-example and i18n validation passed. Fresh review: two independent P0–P2 review passes; canonical-agent and shared-physical-owner findings were repaired and reproduced red/green. Incognito source selection was also repaired through the existing exact-entry reader.
- Browser proof: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3dgwg777qfhmbksjhn8zwmw`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36203957267); 2 tests, 18.57s lane wall / 3.84s test time. Lease stopped and verified completed. Local browser preflight was blocked by the host loopback policy; it was not bypassed. This is not a live platform/provider deployment test.

**Landing remains held:** the protected configuration baseline now reports **2465 > 2463**, plus hash drift (the native-inference key and required-profile key). Those files were not changed without approval. Existing Windows native-inference deferral remains in force.


**Required-profile CI follow-up:** The failed type stripe in run [36207005670](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36207005670/job/108305778634) found two stale async task-projection calls inherited from main, in a file unchanged by this PR. The exact upstream repair already exists in [#158520](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158520); no competing patch was created. Cancelled CI jobs are not passes, and the protected config-baseline gate remains separate.

<details>
<summary>Review repairs, change size, and measured test cost</summary>

Mandatory placement now receives the canonical run target before model preparation. The target resolver itself is read-only: ordinary RPC/channel admission creates real sessions; sessionless helpers are not given fabricated sessions. Exact-entry preparation retains the canonical physical database owner independently of the logical session agent, including private and shared stores. The full seven-case handler/channel/SQLite/worktree composition and nine target-owner sibling cases passed after the source-owner repair.

Production delta: +1186/-85 (net +1101); tests +1223/-157; docs +83. Growth provides server-owned automatic placement across existing entry points and the locked UI, with explicit source/operation lifetime. It reuses the existing dispatch coordinator and workspace lifecycle; no new runtime state store or parallel execution protocol was introduced.

Measured local whole-file wrapper wall times, serial --maxWorkers=1:

| Test file | Wall |
| --- | ---: |
| `src/gateway/server.required-worker-profile.test.ts` | 34.98s |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/required-profile.test.ts` | 8.62s |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-orchestrator.required-profile.test.ts` | 15.34s |
| `ui/src/pages/new-session/required-placement.test.ts` | 3.37s |
| `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-placement-required.test.ts` | 3.41s |
| `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-place-browser.test.ts` | 2.89s |
| `ui/src/pages/new-session/palette-session-draft.warm-roster.test.ts` | 3.32s |
| `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-submission-flow.test.ts` | 3.77s |
| `src/agents/session-placement-required-profile.test.ts` | 4.63s Vitest (single-file lane) |
| `src/config/zod-schema.cloud-workers.test.ts` | 1.42s Vitest (single-file lane) |
| `ui/src/e2e/worker-inference.e2e.test.ts` | 18.57s Vitest on Testbox |

The 34.98s composed Gateway test includes cold handler/worker-runtime preparation, real SQLite ownership, and real managed-worktree creation. Pure dispatch mocks would miss canonical-agent, incognito, and shared-store regressions. No per-test Gateway process or new serial test configuration was added. Exact-head hosted test cost remains pending CI.

Scoped lint has no remaining non-size diagnostics. Seven touched modules exceed the local 700-line limit; the repository’s canonical CI limit policy reports these as advisory. No rule override or baseline exception was applied.

No live platform deployment or real Windows native-inference execution was claimed.

</details>

### Earlier native-inference proof — conflict refresh and startup custody (September 25)

Head `d4de9f8ffbdc8e0e10c2f2db0d42cfd43d48fa67`, tested tree `1035e260eb272334e916d86f859816b678f076d0`. Rebased with merge topology preserved onto main `e74db47ae34c31afb78bb85faeaacd449b4cc1bc`. Original contributor commits through `844c0e90eb94f688de595d7b218c4bd01aee8a7b` remain ancestors. Previous merge-owned security repairs and both follow-up corrections are retained; the final tree exactly matches an independently composed pre-rebase head plus current main with the conflict resolved. The newly overlapping worker-runtime declaration now uses main’s shared `WorkerTranscriptClient` / `WorkerLiveClient` types while retaining `nativeInference`. Its type-erased executable JavaScript is identical to the pre-rebase module. The Windows deferral remains intact, and both shared secret-input files still have zero diff from the new base.

**Earlier conflict resolutions are preserved.** The composition retains main’s role/model restrictions, catalog freshness, selected-agent defaults, async inference admission, original-session-store authority, preparation summaries, and runner inventory. Worker-only credential handling now uses those current owners rather than restoring older parallel checks. Taking main’s UI side without that adaptation reproduced four failures; the owner-level repair and relevant UI siblings pass. Five native-proxy denial assertions now await the updated async API.

#### Review findings addressed

- **P1 — initial-environment credential exposure:** independent AutoReview found that deleting the startup variable after exec does not erase Linux `/proc/<pid>/environ`. A real permitted worker `exec` tool reproduced the exposure using synthetic credentials on the pre-fix composed tree: ordinary environment checks were false, but `initialCarrierHasCredentials` was true. The identical security observation is false after the repair. Startup JSON now uses the existing one-shot `SpawnSecretInput` pipe; the environment carries only fd `3`. Both producer and reader enforce a 2 MiB bound; the reader drains and closes the descriptor before tools, and delivery buffers are cleared. No credential file, new protocol variant, or environment fallback.
- **P2 — Windows reader/handle mismatch:** The earlier global standard-pipe change is removed. It affected existing Windows secret-input callers rather than only the new opt-in, so this PR now restores the shared implementation and tests exactly to main at its merge base. Only explicit `nodeHost.workerRuns.nativeInferenceConfig` is rejected on Windows, before registry/credential reads. Undefined configuration remains a no-op; POSIX private-pipe delivery is retained. **Follow-up: Windows worker-inference transport** must use an opt-in-compatible solution and prove native Windows large-payload delivery, closure/cancellation and unchanged existing callers before enablement.
- **Cancellation proof follows main’s intentional contract:** #156452 stops new transcript submissions after cancellation. The native process test now requires unchanged committed history, no additional transcript submission, an aborted finishing event, and its durable ACK. Provider HTTP still must close. Replacement proof checks no readmission, no duplicate provider call, and no stale output rather than a timing-dependent final stderr string.
- Corrected the E2E fixture’s runtime typing, a shadowed Doctor variable, and a projection test’s duplicated expected-value construction.

The first automated review reported the P1; it was not a clean verdict. Follow-up inspection found the Windows P2; Windows native inference is now explicitly deferred instead of changing shared transport defaults. These dispositions and observed regressions are the basis for the repair—not a claim that a subsequent full automated review returned clean. This closes the identified carrier exposure, **not** the broader same-UID host-isolation boundary; the worker mode is still not an OS sandbox.

- **CI follow-up:** [the exact-head dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36140524578/job/108089539033) found three unused internal exports. Earlier independent reviews remain scoped to their named changes; no new full automated review, browser, paid-provider or installed-bundle run is claimed for this mechanical composition.

body:
Related: #137719. Replaces the draft publication #154369 with the same reviewed tree and complete human credit in the PR commit history. The original source PR remains unchanged.

Removes duplicated promise/resolver plumbing from the Doctor maintenance-lock test.

No user-visible behavior changes. This maintainer-requested cleanup preserves every existing lock assertion and all 20 Doctor test cases; production code is unchanged.

Use the existing shared deferred helper for the start and release gates. This replacement leaves the original PR branch and its historical evidence unchanged.

Contributor: @steipete.

- Replacement commit `ab415ab47a25a9c3af35384c8a572ee1f71132c2` contains only the original +7/-12 test delta. Fresh exact-head CI [35558614483](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35558614483) passed; the changed-file check step took 22 s and changed-boundary check step 28 s. The separate CI/security status completed automatically. Native prepare and merge completed on September 21, 2026, at 04:10 UTC as `07d2a0ca5f7d4a920f12844a4af21f225a8dc9f1`, verified on main. No live Gateway behavior change or proof is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Chat delivery status and its recovery actions look crowded and equally prominent, making it harder to distinguish the status from Retry and Discard.

## User Impact

Delivery status uses normal theme text, Retry uses the link color, and Discard stays secondary. Middle-dot separators have balanced breathing room, and long recovery rows wrap without stranding a separator. No badges, button chrome, changed send behavior, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

title: fix: share startup compile cache with SQLite workers
body:
Related: #153399

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SQLite workers selecting a different compile-cache directory from their parent when OpenClaw enables the cache programmatically.

## User Impact

Packaged OpenClaw and its SQLite workers can reuse the same native cache namespace. Explicit cache and disable settings keep their existing precedence. No configuration, dependency, schema, or cache-format change is required. This fixes the observed directory mismatch; it does not claim a measured CPU improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node's cache getter returns its version-specific directory, but child environment configuration expects the original base. Forwarding the getter adds another native directory suffix. The existing environment owner now retains the absolute input from OpenClaw's first successful cache enable. The packaged launcher supplies the same fact before runtime imports; repeated, failed, and foreign enablement never invent or replace it.

The regression tests use real SQLite children and workers, native directory equality, worker retirement/reopening, explicit policy controls, and separately bundled launcher consumers instead of mocking the getter into returning a base.

## Evidence

- Fresh independent P0–P2 source review: no findings. All six reviewed source hashes survived the rebase onto `47f1d6ad8eb67a0e22db2191f9da9a386eb08e5b` unchanged.
- Retained Node 24.21.0 proof reproduced the original native-directory mismatch and passed all 130 SQLite tests after the repair, including 11 store-policy and 18 read-only-policy cases.
- A later continuation recorded 23 entry tests and 17 selected launcher tests passing, but its changed-check process did not settle successfully. These are checkpoints, not complete qualification; the failed run and its cleanup receipts remain preserved.
- Blacksmith Testbox proof at `95504d24ba2` before the reviewed type-only correction, on Node 24.19.0: **184 passed, one skipped** across the three changed test files with `--maxWorkers=1`. The skipped case is the existing opt-in real-Bun test; all seven new native launcher controls passed. [Proof run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35557729083). Native command exit 0 and independent stopped/no-IP readback confirm completion; the backing Actions lifecycle may show cancelled after one-shot cleanup.
- `git diff --check` passes. [Initial CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35557256531) completed: the new launcher fixture needed literal tuple inference for root-test typechecking, and one unrelated shard was cancelled before acquiring a runner (zero steps). The one-line `as const` correction is independently reviewed with no runtime or assertion changes; [Corrected-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35558213831) completed successfully in 1,293 s (21m33s); the root-test typecheck passed in 419 s. The required commit status succeeded. Native preparation and merge completed, and the reviewed patch matches landed commit `8cf71ee0d120d9d49918d112af9d204b28462b45`. No full release or performance pass is claimed.

The CLI autoreview helper returned `reviewer_unavailable`; the completed independent native review supplies the source review above. No test assertions, deadlines, budgets, or checks were weakened to recover the interrupted proof.


### Changed test costs

Measured with one worker on the exact PR source and frozen dependencies. These are summed, millisecond-rounded test-case durations from the canonical reporter, not whole-job wall times.

| File | Passing tests | Test time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `sqlite-readonly-worker.test.ts` | 64 | 32.67 s |
| `sqlite-worker-store.compile-cache.test.ts` | 11 | 16.37 s |
| `openclaw-launcher.e2e.test.ts` | 109 | 16.97 s |

The combined two-project command took 79.50 s. Read-only coverage exceeds the 30-second target because each cache-policy case needs a fresh native Node cache lifetime and the actual synchronous, asynchronous, or scoped SQLite transport. Node cannot reset an enabled cache; mocking its getter previously hid this defect. Existing snapshot integrity and cleanup assertions remain intact.

The launcher uses the same `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1` setting as the existing CI launcher lane: its fixtures bundle their own entry points. This is not build qualification; the separate exact-head CI build remains required.

title: fix(ui): simplify voice notes and recommendation cards
body:
Related: #119123

## What Problem This Solves

Voice notes in chat are cluttered with file metadata, incoming notes open as files instead of playing inline, and large waveform swings distract from the conversation. Recommendation descriptions also sit too far below their titles.

## User Impact

Incoming and assistant voice notes now use a compact player-only row with restrained, audio-derived waveforms, play/pause, seeking, time, and mute. Voice notes no longer expand into the attachment sidebar; ordinary audio files retain their existing metadata and expansion. Unavailable audio remains explicit rather than showing a fake playable waveform.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing audio player and media lifecycle rather than introducing another renderer. Tighten recommendation subtitle spacing and refine the shared official seal without making it a button. Preserve attachment control clicks through SVG replacement so muting audio does not accidentally open the sidebar.

## Evidence

- 336 focused tests passed across audio/video players, attachment routing, media sources, message rendering, and recommendations.
- Real Chromium mock-Gateway checks cover play/pause, mute, keyboard seeking, preparing/ready, unsupported fallback, expired-ticket recovery, desktop/mobile, dark mode, and no voice-note sidebar expansion. Original and refined UI screenshots are provided below.

title: fix: queued automations lose authority after a native reply
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted manual automations failing before they start when the native OpenClaw caller finishes its reply before queued activation.

## User Impact

An acknowledged automation can activate after a normal reply without being mistaken for a cancelled request. Genuine cancellation, permission revocation, and queue clearing still prevent execution. No configuration, schema, permissions, or UI layout changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native attempt now retains its tool-generation cleanup and real cancellation listener through accepted admission using the existing async-resource owner. The reply still returns promptly, and resources release at activation rather than waiting for the independent automation payload.

This completes the native-attempt lifetime boundary left outside #153865. It repairs the real failure rather than adopting the synthetic provider-reply hold from #153738. Discovered while landing #153836; that keyboard fix does not modify the automation runtime.

## Evidence

### Exact-head hosted result

[CI run 35567575945, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35567575945) **passed on 859e220a7b84146e79e4af2da118ec3c41316090**: **141 successful jobs, 17 skipped, zero failed or pending jobs**. The aggregate Actions CI gate passed, and the substantive review is pinned to this exact head with no actionable correctness/security findings or before-merge items.

The initially stale legacy status was refreshed successfully by the ordinary Security Review owner in [run 35570747989](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35570747989). All three enforced status contexts—CI, dependency review, and security-sensitive review—are **successful** on this head. No status was written manually, and no test or merge safeguard was bypassed. Standalone CodeQL was neutral for this run, not a passing analysis.


### Current canonical-owner integration

Current head **859e220a7b84146e79e4af2da118ec3c41316090** consumes main’s canonical repairs rather than retaining parallel fixes:

- The inventory now exactly matches main’s [f76d38a4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f76d38a4ac5e5f4e6c5a5320436db169e33d5c8a). Our opposite-occurrence removal had combined with that change to leave zero registrations in the CI merge, causing misrouting and missing-broker errors. Our inventory delta is now removed, and the worker test appears exactly once.
- The readiness fixture now exactly matches upstream [bb956411](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bb9564112c4069605536f90864c76e17a7ef885e): its atomic phase record owns all implementation PIDs, replacing the racy secondary receipt. No alternative production deadline or cleanup owner was added.

The PR is back to **three files**: native attempt ownership, its regression, and the existing Cron clock fixture. Those three files are byte-identical to the preceding candidate. Focused integration proof passed **103 owner cases**, **3 selected routing cases**, and the **readiness-deadline case**. The worker negative-identity fixture was run with the ambient `GH_CONFIG_DIR` reference removed from that test process; no credential configuration or assertions changed. Fresh exact-head CI remains required.


### Cron fixture correction

Clock-fixture head **ba244357b8500f1234ae1251d1c797f6005ebfe6** reuses the existing ready-gated process-watchdog fixture for the Cron shell timeout test. Only the initial command watchdog waits for the same live-child readiness condition; process-group exit observation and scoped cleanup use real time. The **500 ms command timeout, all result/descendant-exit assertions, and abort/kill cleanup are unchanged**. No production cleanup guard was weakened.

The preceding [CI run 35562289792](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35562289792) cleared preflight and failed only the Cron test “kills shell process groups on timeout”: it expected `command timed out` but received `Command cleanup could not confirm that owned work stopped` after a 37 ms test run. That fixture had advanced the command deadline and both cleanup windows with global fake timers while process exit remained an OS event. A single unchanged local probe passed, so this is not claimed as a deterministic local reproduction.

After the fixture correction, **42 tests pass** (15 Cron and 27 termination/scope siblings), including the fail-closed uncertainty controls. Core-test types, targeted lint, formatting, and independent P0–P2 review pass. Runtime repair bytes remain unchanged. Fresh exact-head CI is required before landing.


### CI inventory repair

Inventory-repair head **faf90ac507b5243f25e9f212a69e5427bfa3b648** also removes one duplicated `src/worker/worker.runtime.test.ts` entry from the canonical database-worker inventory. Main integration had included that path twice, causing [CI preflight 35561125401](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35561125401) to reject a repeated split-timing generation before any tests ran. The earlier entry remains; no test or duplicate-detection guard was removed.

The existing “every infra test exactly once” regression failed before the repair (1,417 entries versus 1,416 unique), and the **full 115-test planner suite passes afterward** in 89.49s. Independent P0–P2 review is clean. The runtime implementation and its regression remain byte-identical to the earlier green candidate. Fresh exact-head CI is pending. GitHub’s supported branch update also reconciled its stale base projection; the PR now reports the three intended files, not the inherited main-history listing.


### Conflict resolution before the inventory repair

The green head could not merge because main added shared fixture diagnostics in #154259. The duplicate diagnostic change has been dropped in favor of that existing owner. Conflict-resolution head **dc890ea407b4812432a226278db4a5da18783ea7** changes only the native attempt and its regression; both files are byte-for-byte identical to the green 230866644a24 candidate. Published ancestry was preserved and the update was pushed normally, without force. That head then exposed the inventory defect described above.


### Green CI before conflict resolution

[CI run 35559221974, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35559221974) passed on **230866644a2414a29430a981f8bf9f47d0c04632**: **142 successful jobs, 17 skipped, no failed or pending jobs**. The formerly failing staging shard passed. CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses are successful. The exact-head substantive review has no actionable correctness or security findings.

Standalone CodeQL is **neutral**, not a passing analysis: it reported 16 missing main-branch configurations and could not determine introduced alerts. The applicable required security gates passed. The original staging timeout cause remains unknown; this successful run does not prove that diagnostic logging repaired it.


### Terminal-error follow-up

CI run 35554869055 exposed an introduced signal-boundary mistake: normal prepared-generation drain aborted the signal captured for later terminal-error transcript persistence. The follow-up keeps the logical attempt signal unchanged and routes parent resource cancellation only through the existing disposable abort bridge. No transcript authority check or assertion was removed.

- Current correction: **31 ownership/transcript tests pass** (7 native automation cases plus 24 transcript-lifecycle cases), core types and owning lint pass, and fresh full-candidate P0–P2 review is scoped-clean.

The subsequent exact-head hosted CI verified those provider-flow cases.
- The independent staging timeout did not reproduce in one local run: **16 tests passed**, including the formerly timed-out case in 18.447s. Its cause remains unproven; no timeout or test was changed.
- An additional Blacksmith proof attempt failed during provider warmup before a lease ID or test result was returned. No repeat allocation or unowned resource was used. This is an environment-proof gap, not a passing check.

The second failure is the aggregate CI gate. The local 16-case staging replay passed, but its CI timeout cause is not established and no passing replay is claimed as a fix. That historical run’s CI gate failed; the final exact-head result is recorded above.

### Earlier failure-context follow-up (now supplied by main)

The earlier, now-superseded test-only change recorded a per-fixture command index, PID, elapsed time, observed exit/close state, and bounded output tails **only on command failure**. It preserves the original thrown error, all deadlines, assertions, and whole-tree cleanup. This is diagnostic evidence—not a claimed repair of the unexplained timeout. The unchanged 16-case fixture passes locally in 65.89s; root-test types, targeted lint, formatting, and independent P0–P2 review pass.

An additional replay used the exact failed merge source 887fd990d9557c12e5dd742757ede322f086d2bb and the recorded 32-file execution order, with the canonical shared-worker configuration. On this Node26 host it failed earlier in a CLI stdout-gate test and was stopped by the runner’s existing no-output watchdog before reaching staging. That replay is incomplete, not green; CI used Node24. Main’s shared fixture-lifecycle observer now owns that diagnostic purpose; no parallel logger remains in this PR.

### Initial admission-repair evidence

- The exact failing CI merge reproduced the automation failure in the original 32-file real-Gateway suite: **61 passed / 1 failed**, with the sanitized Gateway error “agent tool caller authority is no longer active.”
- A deterministic regression uses the real native attempt/generation lifecycle, automation tool, caller fence, in-process router, Cron service, and durable reservation. Original source: **5 failed / 2 passed**. Candidate: **7 passed**, covering execution, cancellation before and after the reply, parent-owner cancellation, permission rotation, authority revocation, and queue clearing. It verifies release before payload completion and does not hold the model reply open.
- **20 standalone runs passed 140/140 cases** (median wall 14.96s; range 13.51–27.33s). A subsequent test-only review correction also verifies the replacement permission generation; all 7 final cases pass in 22.19s. Those repeated runs predate the terminal-error follow-up above; the current ownership checks are recorded separately.
- **113 sibling tests across 10 files passed** in 46.09s. Final core/core-test types, owning core lint, formatting, and the selected boundary/architecture guards passed. The combined changed-check command reached its outer limit at the final pairing-account guard; that guard then passed separately.

The leases for those completed proof runs were stopped. Hosted PR CI is a separate gate, not claimed from this environment link.

The full suite uses a real isolated Gateway, the real Telegram plugin with synthetic Crabline transport, and a deterministic local provider. It is not live-provider or physical-device proof.
