title: feat(linux): bundle a self-contained desktop runtime
body:
## What Problem This Solves

New Linux desktop installations need a separate Node/CLI installation before they can run their Gateway or desktop node.

## User Impact

Linux bundles include an offline-ready OpenClaw runtime: no system Node, npm, global OpenClaw, or network program-code installation is needed for bootstrap. Existing CLI installations and externally managed services retain their ownership. Remote connections do not start a local Gateway.

Accounts, optional plugins/models, browser downloads, VNC setup and OS permissions remain onboarding. This changes Linux production packaging only; macOS/Windows test-port runtime discovery remains unchanged. The host still needs the documented native ABI and `libatomic1`, which the Debian package declares.

**Size tradeoff:** the tested SEA is 341,687,492 bytes and materializes 667,368,509 bytes. It deliberately contains a compressed pristine Node copy as well as the SEA executable; this is not a size-optimization claim. App-owned versions are retained for running workers and app rollback. A running Gateway changes runtime on its normal service restart, not when the desktop app merely updates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing canonical package/install tooling builds the full runtime closure. Node 26.8.2 SEA embeds that closure and a pristine Node executable, then hands off with `execve`. The normal launcher continues to own ESM/TLA, lazy plugins, native modules and subprocess semantics—there is no replacement JavaScript loader and no dependency on a future SEA filesystem feature.

Preparation is lazy, digest/version checked and confined to content-addressed app data. The existing service wrapper contract provides a stable executable outside AppImage mounts. The package is intentionally outside npm's global layout so a host npm cannot claim it as an update target. The existing desktop/package updater owns distribution updates.

Tagged packaging now uses the canonical release-identity policy: the release tag, checkout, and any correction base tag must resolve to the same validated source SHA. The manifest records the desktop release version separately from the unchanged package version and executable digest; runtime version equality is not relaxed.

Related overlap: #152057 adds the Chrome runtime adapter. Its branch was inspected and coordination posted; no patches were imported.

## Evidence

**Remaining hosted gate:** [CodeQL check 106229822194](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/runs/106229822194) reports cache poisoning through `workflow_dispatch` at the runtime-build step on this head. That event cannot enter this job: both release admission and `build_linux` require `workflow_run`, and the guard tests explicitly reject dispatch. The actual permitted event has [read-only default-branch cache access](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#cache-access-for-low-trust-workflow-triggers), with no write-capable `cache-mode` override here. This is an event-reachability false positive requiring CodeQL/security-owner adjudication; no finding was dismissed or suppressed, and no CI run was retried to clear it. [SecOps adjudication was requested](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154240#issuecomment-5756151251), and the team review request is present. The scanning summary also warns that 17 baseline configurations were not found; this is not a claim of complete scanning coverage.

[Inspected native before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154240#issuecomment-5754148204) show the unbundled setup path and the included runtime opening the real Gateway. No new UI presentation change follows those captures.

- **Repaired native paths:** recovery source `bb5cebde0244` passed **299 Rust tests** (nine existing platform/manual tests ignored; main suite 3.07 s), a rebuilt real Tauri Debian first run, canonical Gateway restart/stop/start/readiness, remote mode without changing the running Gateway or service definition, and saved SecretRef reconnect plus rotation with unavailable private-runtime storage. Provider: **blacksmith-testbox**, lease `tbx_01m30y8gwbwb213a1rmqkep53h`, [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35555785366).
- **Recovery and rollback:** native broken/outdated managed-CLI cases selected the explicit reinstall path with a **stubbed network installer**. An injected candidate-bootstrap failure was rejected by the real desktop app; the prior stable launcher remained selected and its real systemd user Gateway successfully restarted. These are not claims of a live network reinstall or signed updater deployment.
- **Offline distribution:** the earlier unchanged-runtime proof built the canonical complete package and exercised native PTY, sqlite-vec/fs-safe, plugins, Gateway readiness/shutdown, and desktop-node pairing/cancellation. A read-only Ubuntu 22.04 container with no system Node/npm/OpenClaw bootstrapped with networking disabled (2.137 s cold). It also verified that host npm does not own the private package.
- **Correction identity:** six regressions failed before repair and pass afterwards, covering matching releases, same-source correction reuse, selected-SHA/tag/base-source mismatches, and installed-package/source-version disagreement. They exercise the real packager and Git identities, replacing only SEA compilation with a small executable fixture. Combined identity/extraction proof took **1.58 s wall** locally; the six identity cases took about **108 ms test time** on Testbox.
- **CI integration:** on isolated Node **24.19.0**, the original two-worker, 32-file failing shard passed (**1,059 passed, three skipped; 317.92 s**). All **971 workflow/config/extraction tests passed** (172.65 s). The final identity/wiring delta then passed **10 focused cases** (7.61 s wall). Both Knip audits, root-test typechecking, lint, workflow checks, formatting and the line-growth guard passed. Fresh independent **P0–P2 review is scoped-clean**. Provider: **blacksmith-testbox**, lease `tbx_01m317s8jysycfy1x5xygmn404`, [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35565551140).

<details>
<summary>Red/green recovery controls and historical CI diagnosis</summary>

The exact original Rust installer and resource-owner modules from `0157c774ada1` were compiled in a bounded boundary harness: broken managed reinstall, outdated managed reinstall, and failed-candidate launcher preservation all failed on their intended assertions. The same three cells passed with `bb5cebde0244`. Source bytes were hash-bound to those commits; Tauri handles, CLI selection and the installer were explicit fixtures. This complements, rather than substitutes for, the native desktop/service proof above.

CI defects were missing executable-root registration, an extraction test outside every Vitest owner, and runtime staging inserted between pinned AppImage verification and its consumer. Those are repaired without weakening the ownership or ordering assertions. The release job now states its existing workflow-run-only admission explicitly; manual dispatch remains mirror-only.

The historical hosted Crabbox staging command timeout did not reproduce in its unchanged full shard; the target case passed in 11.201 s. Its stalled subprocess/syscall remains unattributed. No timeout, retry, or assertion was weakened, and the passing reproduction is not presented as proof of the historical timeout's cause. Local broad fixtures that reached host tools were discarded in favor of the isolated Testbox results.

</details>

All task-owned proof leases are stopped. On final head `82c06a5967fb162aa68e432b252a4c2059eae982`, [primary CI run 35566578083](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35566578083), attempt 1, completed successfully: **98 jobs passed, 15 skipped, zero failures** (113/113 jobs across two pages). [Linux App run 35566577992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35566577992), attempt 1, passed all three Linux/macOS/Windows companion jobs. The manual-only Linux runtime/bundle/first-run/AppImage steps were skipped in that hosted workflow; retained Crabbox package proof above supplies that separate coverage. The commit statuses for dependency review, security-sensitive review, and `openclaw/ci-gate` are successful. **The separate CodeQL scanning check remains failed, so this PR is not merge-ready.** The final tree changes packaging identity and CI integration, not the native runtime owners proven above.

This is a program-resource manifest change, not an operator-config/account/database-schema migration. Existing content-addressed resources remain available for rollback. Linux x64 was exercised; Linux arm64 and live macOS/Windows test-port execution were not. No signed release or paid Mac resource was published/provisioned.

title: fix: restore session owner assignment for non-owner agent turns
body:
Related: #125057

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent can create a visible work session but cannot assign it to the verified channel requester when its turn lacks Gateway-owner authority.

## User Impact

Live admitted agent turns can assign responsibility to a registered person or configured agent and read back the stored owner, including for non-admin Discord requesters. Non-owner channel turns receive assignment only unless they already have operator-write authority; those operators retain their existing bounded archive, restore, and Stop controls. Settings, deletion, global group changes, and cloud-profile discovery remain owner-gated. Senderless system management and explicit tool denies are preserved.

The administrator-attested channel/profile link is still required to identify “me.” Assignment does not create identity links, grant the assignee’s privileges, change creator/sharing authority, migrate existing owners, or change conditional visible-spawn inheritance. Another registered human remains a valid handoff target under the existing UI/RPC contract. Their personal USER.md supplies preferences on later eligible turns; personal prompt selection is not a secrecy boundary or permission to access that person’s credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose a narrow assignment action through the existing sessions tool, bind it to a live admitted turn, and retain the canonical assignment writer and dispatch/commit authorization checks. CLI tool projection and the final MCP grant consume the same admission. Standalone HTTP or attached sessions cannot gain assignment merely through transport binding.

The conflict repair preserves current main’s scoped session controls, multiperson user selection, personal-tool execution wrapper, and collector Stop restriction. Original contributor ancestry is retained. The previously landed CI planner and SQLite export repairs are now inherited from main; the separate row-packing PR is not a dependency.

## Evidence

- Current candidate `b0ce03d35a85` (tree-identical signing of reviewed `237f7e2d709c`) passed **268 distinct cases across 11 files** (269 executions, including one CLI replay after restoring current-main fixture cleanup). Initial selection: 266 cases / 10 files, 297.38 seconds wrapper wall. The additional multiperson selection and cleanup replay passed in 97.07 seconds wrapper wall.
- The real MCP HTTP case resolves the admitted Discord fixture, creates an agent-owned session, assigns a human, reads the persisted owner back, and preserves creator/visibility. It also covers standalone attach and revoked grants, plus foreign-human bootstrap without borrowing the assignee’s authority. Case duration: 20.662 seconds. No assignment writer or MCP dispatcher is mocked.
- Existing operator-control final effects and revocation/replacement negatives: 10 passed. Archive/restore/Stop/collector composition: 13 passed. Full CLI preparation: 117 passed. These counts overlap the 268-case total.
- Three affected type graphs, targeted lint on 27 TypeScript files, formatting, diff checks, and staged line/suppression ratchets passed. Independent Codex P0–P2 AutoReview completed both chunks with zero actionable findings (**scoped-clean**, not an unrestricted whole-repository review). The only subsequent source edit was a mechanically equivalent boolean simplification.
- All four changed docs passed MDX checks. The broad anchor audit has 53 failures identical to pinned main, with no introduced or resolved failures; external ClawHub fragments remain unverified.

This is keyless, isolated Linux production-boundary proof, not live Discord/model execution or a Team deployment. No full build or full repository suite was run, and CI was not manually dispatched or rerun. Hosted review and required CI are tracked separately on the published head.

<details>
<summary>Prior regression evidence and human-target review clarification</summary>

Earlier revisions passed 382 initial focused cases, 52 channel-authority cases, 39 MCP-cache cases, 37 compatibility cases, 60 restored senderless-management cases, and a 22-case integrated replay. Those are historical scoped results, not current-head full-suite evidence. Restoring the old whole-tool owner gate reproduced missing-tool discovery; restoring the overly restrictive absent-owner predicate reproduced the real senderless list-to-archive failure. Fixed bytes passed both controls.

The hosted revision-4/5 foreign-human finding identified a reachable personal-context effect, but requester-only targets would change the existing assignment contract. The public RPC/UI permit handoffs to any registered person by an identified, appropriately scoped caller with session visibility. Assigned-owner personal-context selection was deliberately introduced in #154980; it does not select the current sender or grant the assignee’s authority.

The expanded real MCP fixture assigns a different registered administrator, reads back that owner, prepares fresh member-sender admission, and exercises the bootstrap boundary. The assignee’s preferences are selected as documented; requester metadata remains the member, senderIsOwner stays false, no operator principal is created, and personal-instructions access still requires authenticated requester authority. This joined bootstrap/admission proof remains in the current passing selection. No requester-only restriction or assignee-privilege borrowing was introduced.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

title: feat(ui): move and remember the System busyness panel
body:
Closes #154161

## What Problem This Solves

System busyness is pinned to the lower-right corner, where it can cover the work being monitored, and switches abruptly between compact and expanded views.

## User Impact

Drag the title bar with a mouse or touch to place the panel anywhere inside the window; this browser remembers that placement after reopening or reloading. Expanding and minimizing now animate in 160 ms, respect reduced motion, and keep the controls reachable when the window changes size. The focused title bar also supports arrow keys (Shift moves farther).

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared frame owns placement and motion for both loading/retry and ready diagnostics. Its interaction runtime loads only when the panel opens, without a new dependency or Gateway state/configuration. Temporary viewport clamping does not overwrite the preferred compact position.

Requested by and co-authored with Peter Steinberger (@steipete).

title: fix(test): retire shared read pools between files
body:
Closes #154205
Related: #154160

## What Problem This Solves

Shared Vitest workers could carry a mocked read pool into another test file, causing real workspace snapshot reads to receive `fleet.list` replies.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The fix removes an order-dependent CI failure without weakening workspace validation, authority checks, or test assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The read pool registers cleanup callbacks only when its global singleton is first created. Test teardown retired its state-database lifecycle but not the pool singleton, so later pools could lose their cleanup owner. Add that existing singleton to the existing drain-before-retire map.

The expanded native regression walks three reader generations and reaches the actual workspace snapshot consumer. It fails with the same CI exception before the mapping and passes afterward. This repairs the owning test infrastructure rather than changing the downstream readiness tests.

A direct main hotfix was attempted after qualification and refused by GH013 (changes must be made through a pull request); no bypass was used.

## Evidence

- **Landed through native guarded merge:** exact head `78d6474dad01ff081ae2e5a1b0a687a3b5b4c0b7` passed [hosted CI 35547821032](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35547821032). Native review, hosted preparation, and merge completed; merge `93d69d5a747432362027bbdf71eb06c96aac6eb6` is on current main. All three landed files equal the reviewed head, both human coauthors are preserved, issue #154205 is closed, and the retained native receipt is `complete`.
- Native fail-before/pass-after: the third reader generation throws `Unexpected workspace state snapshot result` before the mapping; all five ordered fixture files pass afterward.
- **20/20 independent regression invocations pass**, 77s total. One complete local invocation is 3.01s wall (2.26s Vitest, including 1.93s native child proof); no new wait budget or persistent worker pin.
- [Blacksmith Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35547203402), lease `tbx_01m30n55w5nbc83bvbvy3vh710`: original 218-file failing cohort passes **3/3** runs; each has **216 passed files / 2 skipped, 2,841 passed cases / 16 skipped**. Vitest walls: 114.36s, 103.07s, 104.02s. Existing runner/lifecycle siblings also pass (two files, three outer cases; 15.44s command wall). Command exit 0; lease readback confirms completed.
- The trusted source capsule binds the synchronized checkout; all three modified source hashes were asserted remotely before execution.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reports shows each member’s activity but does not link directly to that person’s OpenClaw conversations. Related: #154020.

## User Impact

Adds direct session links to person-history pages and daily, weekly, and monthly member sections, including quiet members and alias-filtered reports. The links are labeled **Current work / owned sessions**, separate from historical activity.

Only sessions visible to the current viewer are shown. Unlinked or ambiguous identities are explained instead of guessed. A permission change during rendering fails closed; refreshing evaluates the new policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse verified linked GitHub profiles, canonical owner-filtered session discovery before pagination, and the existing conversation-navigation bridge. Identity lookup and session pages are request-local; member queries are deduplicated and limited to four concurrent calls. Stored reports, historical counts, summaries, Markdown and JSON remain unchanged.

## CI dependency

Hosted run `35546855732` failed four Claw workspace-snapshot tests in `core-unit-src-security-3`. The owning defect is a shared test read-pool singleton surviving file teardown, allowing a mocked `fleet.list` reply to reach a later real `workspace.snapshot` consumer. The separate repair is #154206; it adds the missing singleton retirement and an ordered fail-before/pass-after regression. No workspace/schema repair is added to this Reports diff.

A clean exact-main replay at `67358cf64e2191d17327b21a24dcbf8cf6174434` passed both focused tests and the original 218-file cohort (2,841 passed, 16 skipped), but does not guarantee the hosted per-worker assignment and does not clear the failure. The owning repair landed as `93d69d5a747432362027bbdf71eb06c96aac6eb6`. Reports is now refreshed onto that repaired main at `050cfe88ce336420edc7232a44e22c8c82efae5b`; the 13-file feature patch is byte-for-byte unchanged. The source capsule verified head and tree; the owned lease was stopped and independently confirmed completed. [Exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35548875395) passed, including the required `openclaw/ci-gate`. Tested merge `b4b125c207969c267224af8f3bc8a8e35b71df9c` has the same tree as head `050cfe88ce336420edc7232a44e22c8c82efae5b`.

## Evidence

- Actual Reports renderer before/after captures using synthetic data; person pages and a daily card filtered by a GitHub alias.
- 88 Reports identity/HTTP/render tests and four production-cookie HTTP tests passed remotely, including ownership beyond the global first page, private/incognito/archived/automated exclusions, role changes, and cookie expiry/rotation.

The existing cookie authority now invalidates an in-flight response when the effective role policy changes. The corrected production-boundary regression is green: **130 targeted tests passed** (5 real HTTP cases, 37 auth/runtime siblings, 88 Reports tests). title: refactor(update): simplify update execution and finalization
body:
Closes #154157

## What Problem This Solves

The updater retained parallel execution paths and could repeat plugin completion and activation preparation.

## User Impact

Updates use the existing staged installation and activation owners without duplicate finalization work. Rollback compatibility, retained recovery material, native-service ownership, and installed-version handoffs remain intact.

The CI follow-up also fixes two existing keyboard-focus defects: opening an attachment menu could replace File/Photo focus with Camera, and the chat position rail could publish a current marker before its keyboard entry caught up. No package version, database schema, configuration default, retention, or permission changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use one private-inspection Git update path and the CLI-owned Doctor instead of a second standalone runner.
- Require staged package installation; keep publication and rollback with the existing swap owner.

title: fix(ui): recover hidden progress refresh startup and canceled retries
body:
Related: #154044

## What Problem This Solves

Progress refresh can abort during hidden session preparation. Retrying a canceled queued refresh can also replay its old acceptance without starting an update.

## User Impact

Hidden status refreshes can prepare their session without becoming visible chat turns, and canceled queued requests can be retried with a new intent. Existing authorization, cancellation, replacement and terminal-run fences remain enforced. No UI layout, configuration, schema or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the six-file correction for the two later review findings on #154044, which merged while these repairs were being verified. Hidden presentation is no longer mistaken for loss of admission liveness. Queued cancellation records its canonical receipt while the exact owner still exists, before removal; stale owners cannot overwrite successors.

title: refactor: remove compaction checkpoints
body:
Closes #154045

## What Problem This Solves

Retires the separate compaction-checkpoint management feature and its additional branch/restore workflow.

## User Impact

The checkpoint link, history cards, and checkpoint branch/restore actions are removed. The dedicated `sessions.compaction.list`, `sessions.compaction.branch`, and `sessions.compaction.restore` RPCs are intentionally retired. Ordinary Fork/rewind, conversation history, compaction, and token-savings reporting remain available.

No SQLite tables, columns, indexes, schema-version bump, migration, or live-data purge are introduced. New compactions stop creating checkpoint metadata; optional post-compaction token measurements stay with the ordinary transcript marker. Read-only legacy references continue protecting old history from cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is an end-to-end maintainer-requested removal, not a hidden button: it deletes checkpoint capture/persistence, runtime stores, RPC handlers and schemas, client state, UI rendering/styles, generated protocol models, obsolete helpers, and tests for the retired feature. Adjacent session and compaction paths are simplified without adding a replacement feature.

Before initial publication, cleanup was limited to unused imports, braces, and a shadowed parameter name; no behavior changed. The two import-cleaned test files also passed all 45 tests.

The complete `deadcode:full` inventory (including exports), max-lines/line-cap/assertion-safety ratchets, configuration docs, plugin inventory, root-test types, focused lint, and 40 storage tests passed. The 12-case owner file passes on this composed candidate; the upstream PR records deterministic failure proof and 20 standalone/3 original-shard passes. No competing implementation was introduced.

Malformed references fail closed. Existing markers without optional token fields remain readable; no user configuration key/default, SQL schema, migration, or purge is changed.

title: fix(voice): keep audio flowing while the Gateway is busy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord and GPT Live audio stutters when work saturates the Gateway's main event loop.

## User Impact

Established voice media can keep playing while the Gateway handles other work. No configuration change or data migration is required.

Speaker admission, agent execution, transcripts, and microphone forwarding remain on main; this does not eliminate every latency source. GPT Live still owns response interruption: room controls flush buffered local playback without permanently muting the continuous stream that carries their spoken result.

### Compatibility and upgrade review

The complete inventory now contains **110 files**, including the private socket-contract consumers and the new direct-playback regression. All production paths were checked; a truncated file preview is not evidence of a stored-data change.

- No user configuration schema, option, or default changes. Manifest changes only declare private build-time worker entries; dependency versions are unchanged.
- `RealtimeVoiceBridge.setAudioOutputPort?` is optional and capability-gated. Providers without it retain the existing callback path; source and compiled package layouts were checked.
- Worker handles, port fences, and recording epochs are process-local memory, including `SharedArrayBuffer` recording clocks. No persisted schema or migration is changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moving codecs alone leaves socket I/O and packet timing on the saturated event loop. Discord's voice connection, codecs, capture deadlines, and playback clock now share a worker owner; GPT Live WebRTC and WebSocket media also run in workers. A bounded direct PCM port connects continuous provider output to Discord without a per-chunk main-thread relay.

The cutover preserves admission and recording ownership, bounded queues, cancellation, final transcript drain, and orderly replacement/teardown. The additional worker/IPC code is needed to move the timing-sensitive ownership together rather than maintain competing media paths.

## Evidence

- A deliberate 500 ms main-thread stall delivered **0 packets on the old WebSocket path versus 25 worker packets and 25 direct PCM chunks**. WebRTC and real Discord encoded-audio pacing regressions also pass.
- On the refreshed candidate: **774 Discord voice tests**, **32 Gateway E2E tests**, and **8 transcript integrations** passed. The original **47 materially changed test files** also passed individually with one worker; one optional Bun check was skipped. The additional direct-playback file and updated port test have fresh measured costs below.
- The new capture-order regression fails on the pre-fix owner and passes after the repair. It holds SDK close after decoded EOF and proves a replacement subscription cannot overtake physical finalization.
- Root and standalone OpenAI/Discord builds, extension type checks, targeted lint, formatting, and line-cap checks passed. Native compiled workers launch and close in the shipped bundled OpenAI and standalone/staged Discord layouts.
- Independent autoreview completed. Its genuine capture-order finding was repaired. Connecting-close and continuous-clear concerns were checked against the actual state/stream contracts and covered by explicit late-open and post-clear playback tests; no unsupported provider-cancellation policy was added.
- Proof ran on **Blacksmith Testbox**, lease `tbx_01m30bgh0efqy4j7jdrtycn8dc`, [run 35538800275](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35538800275), using repository test/type/lint/build runners. No credentialed Discord/OpenAI call or production deployment was used as evidence. Exact-head PR CI remains required before landing.

- **CI correction:** [the initial suppression-inventory failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35541291690/job/106159447870) was reproduced with its original two-group shard plan on head `13e9273`. Commit `4a0474027bc49411dee732fad9a1d5c93b978797` replaces six Node-message suppressions with explicit, typed empty transfer lists; the allowlist and lint policy are unchanged. The same plan now passes **894 tests (3 existing skips)**, plus **10 worker-message regressions** and type-aware lint. [Repair proof: Blacksmith Testbox run 35542213619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35542213619), lease `tbx_01m30fdp93rja30a2xn2w9jdq3` (stopped). Current-head CI is being verified separately.

- **Cold-catalog repair:** the CI trace showed capability-catalog construction loading host execution/logging through the eager worker-socket import. Default factory loading now belongs to the existing abort-aware sideband admission owner. Injected factories and WebRTC selection are preserved; the strict import traps are unchanged. The final scoped review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- **Validation of that repair:** both original plugin-contract groups passed (**1,145 tests**); all OpenAI tests passed (**1,362 passed, 1 optional skip**); type-aware lint, unchanged line caps, and the root build passed. The isolated OpenAI entrypoint profile passed at **127.27 MiB max RSS** (81.03 MiB above its empty-process baseline). These are actual source-matched Testbox results, not an exact-head CI claim. The old cold-import trap did not reproduce in the isolated Testbox, so its captured CI failure remains the red evidence and current-head CI remains decisive.
- **Shared-state failure:** [upstream #154138](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154138) fixes the archive test that restored environment-derived filesystem mode as a programmatic override, bypassing a later Claw close-failure injection. Its producer-owned patch and regression evidence were checked. This branch was refreshed onto `b73d0e4541eff60e3f24eb50c84c26b98a77d30f`, which contains merge `b6a518ec8c52d8a1935220ba0364022c4366dfe6`; all four existing commits remain patch-identical under range-diff. This was a diagnosed base repair, not a blind CI rerun.
- **Import-cycle correction:** the architecture failure on `0c76dec4` was reproduced. Unchanged socket types now live in the existing shared leaf, and every private caller was migrated. The complete architecture gate, **1,362 OpenAI tests** (1 optional skip), **18 catalog tests**, lint, and extension production/test types passed. No import guard or baseline was weakened.
- **Direct speech retention:** changing voices now retains only speech whose playback has not started. A shared, request-scoped epoch records worker progress even before main receives its event. Epoch-tagged events and invalidated completion markers prevent old playback from retiring a newer request.
- **Ordered completion:** provider completion round-trips a bounded flush marker through the existing direct-port credit owner. This orders already-submitted PCM before completion, handles a completed response with no audio, and prevents a queued idle event from bypassing a pending flush. The receipt means local media admission—not audible playback or future provider silence. The SDK documentation states that distinction; the permanent close fence and optional bridge method are unchanged.
- **Final regression proof:** the original owners fail **4 of 5 selected regressions**; removing just the final pending-flush predicate separately reproduces the stale-idle failure. Restored final source passes **8 direct-playback tests**, **2 port-protocol tests**, **13 OpenAI worker/port tests**, and **106 Discord playback/voice-selection/pacing tests**. Type-aware core/extension lint, unchanged line caps, extension production/test types, formatting, and matching source fingerprints passed. [Blacksmith Testbox run 35545964196](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35545964196), lease `tbx_01m30ktkc9zag9cs0468ebpv0p`, is stopped. Independent review findings were accepted and repaired; no clean reviewer exit is claimed for the passes that found them.

- **Recording-fixture correction:** CI exposed a synthetic speaker that never entered the SDK speaking map, allowing the real 2-second silence deadline to cut off a long backlog scenario. The fixture now models ongoing speech and explicitly advances the owning deadline. Removing only the speaking-state assignment fails both cases. The corrected file passed **20/20 standalone runs** and **3/3 full original two-group shard plans**, preserving the 128-job, 64 MiB, 34-file, reconnect, cleanup, and resume assertions. Standalone wall time was 12.47–15.58 s (mean 13.09 s). The original uncorrected shard passed locally; the original failure is captured CI evidence, not a claimed local red.
- **Callback-admission repair:** main-thread admission and natural worker retirement now compete on the same atomic status word. Starvation cannot discard already-admitted PCM or PCM still awaiting packet preparation; explicit cancellation remains fenced. A deterministic delivery barrier covers both orderings and cancellation in response and continuous modes. The original owners fail **4/6 cases**; the repaired **6/6 pass**, including ordered playback and truthful marks. The full voice owner passed **54 suites / 788 tests**, full 113-file voice lint, extension production/test types, unchanged line caps, formatting, and the runtime-preparation build. Matching eight-file source fingerprint: `691540ed84bc2f0718504a926a96d3f853fa9e4a3a0dcf1737fb4d56c2fc6cb0`. Independent P0–P2 autoreview was scoped-clean. The missing `continuous-flushed` exhaustive-switch case is also repaired.
- **Historical CI timeout—explicit uncertainty:** prior CI's release-tooling subprocess fixture timed out at 120 s. The original ordered shard passed at the PR head (case 11.5 s), and a second replay of the **exact historical CI merge `4b3a30a6150c1ceffbc280d8dac596aebea81b0a`** also passed with Node 24.19.0, two-core affinity, the original two-group plan, and process-state capture: 2,215 tests passed / 98 platform skips; the case took 14.97 s. No hang was observed, and no causal release-tooling fix is claimed. No release-test assertion, timeout, retry policy, or production release code was changed. Run `35552465186` subsequently completed with only the diagnosed stale-export failure and aggregate gate; all other selected jobs succeeded. The historical failure and reproduction gap remain recorded, and the final head must pass required CI.
- **Completed diagnostic, not a causal fix:** replacement Testbox run `35556028176` successfully ran the original two-group plan and 20 standalone release-fixture runs on historical merge `4b3a30a6150c1ceffbc280d8dac596aebea81b0a`, with temporary phase/PID/exit/close instrumentation. All 378 commands returned without command errors; maximum command time was 1.123 s and maximum exit-to-close gap was 1 ms. Every start had an exit and close. Assertions, deadlines, and retry policy were unchanged; instrumentation was restored and the lease was stopped. The prior diagnostic launch ran zero tests because its ignored script was not transferred; that transport mistake was repaired, not counted as proof. Retained metrics from the **actual failed job** show a quiet CPU interval (0–1.5%, mean 0.43%), at least 6.58 GB available memory, and no OOM events. Its retained thread profiles do not identify the Node/npm subprocess phase or pipe lifecycle. Therefore no root cause or owning code fix can be claimed. The updated `AGENTS.md` best-effort policy allows proceeding under normal CI/review gates after this bounded investigation, with the original failure and remaining uncertainty recorded. No assertions, deadlines, retry policy, or guard baselines were weakened.
- **Final cutover cleanup:** CI correctly found `DISCORD_AUDIO_OUTPUT_STATUS` no longer had an external consumer after the shared-word helper migration. It is now a private constant. Both full dependency/dead-code scans, all six admission regressions, targeted lint, and formatting pass; no guard baseline was changed.

- Current candidate: `d5b5d6d3b1feddf659bfcceb00e23461569a7935`. [Its exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35553602398) **passed**. Native preparation also completed without a rebase or push. The bounded historical-timeout investigation is complete. Under the updated best-effort failure policy, this unexplained historical failure is documented rather than an extra landing gate. Current required CI and review gates remain mandatory; no passing replay is represented as a causal fix.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

Measured serially with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`. These are command wall times including compiler/setup overhead. The E2E commands include a required cold root build; their test bodies are not several minutes long. CI timing will be added when the PR run completes.

The real-SDK playback suite needs its packet clock, Opus encoder, FIFO, interruption, and retirement paths; replacing those with fake timers would not prove isolation under actual main-thread starvation. The independent-thread probes likewise need a real 500 ms stall. No serial configuration or permanent worker pin was added.

CI metrics come from [run 35552465186](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35552465186), head `f9a800750efdfe5a0aba0fa3d2405f7d2a8b710a`. title: docs: keep update requests owned through acceptance
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Update requests can be treated as finished after a busy deferral or recovery to the old version, while stale hourly-timer guidance can conflict with the operator's configured scheduler.

## User Impact

Operators get continued ownership through native acceptance or a concrete blocker, preservation of the configured single cadence, and brief, clear results. These are operator-skill instructions only; this PR does not deploy a server, change a scheduler, or change runtime or migration behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested by maintainers steipete and vincentkoc. Keep recovery, one-time latest-main target selection, bounded interruption, and verification with the canonical deployment owner. Preserve native persistence, migration, maintenance-authority, and branch-protection checks; require ordinary reviewed PR landing for code repairs. A successful observer or healthy incumbent is not a successful requested update.

## Evidence

- Canonical docs-only changed-file checks passed for both skill files: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- .agents/skills/openclaw-update/SKILL.md .agents/skills/update-team-server/SKILL.md`.
- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` passed.
- Fresh independent exact-commit P2 autoreview passed with no actionable findings; separate lead review also found no substantive issues.
- The entire schema/migration safeguards section is byte-identical to the parent version.
- Scope is exactly the two updater skill documents. No local runtime tests or live deployment actions were performed for this documentation-only change.
- Exact-head hosted CI run 35540625094 completed successfully, including `check-docs`, `docker-seed-e2e`, and its `openclaw/ci-gate` job.
- ClawSweeper completed its exact-head review with no actionable findings; the native completed-review gate accepted comment 5753046841.
- Landing is currently blocked by the required combined `openclaw/ci-gate` status: security review selected newer all-skipped CI run 35540666422 rather than successful run 35540625094. The selector in `scripts/github/security-review.mjs` picks the highest run ID before requiring its gate job to succeed. No CI rerun, rebase, bypass, or status override was used.

Co-authored-by: steipete <58493+steipete@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: vincentkoc <25068+vincentkoc@users.noreply.github.com>



## September 21 notification and repair follow-through update

At Peter's explicit request, extend this existing PR rather than create a duplicate: Team notices occur only immediately before actual planned downtime and once service is verified back. Successful updates include concise highlights from the exact previous/new accepted serving-commit range; non-actions and blockers stay private, and rollback is restoration rather than update success. Confirm actual defects at the failing path, use isolated worktrees/subagents where useful, land tested reviewed repairs through normal CI/PR gates, and retain ownership through verified update acceptance.

Validation: targeted oxfmt, git diff whitespace checks, frontmatter/relative links, and independent P1 autoreview passed; the original schema-safety section is byte-identical. No deployment or lifecycle operations were performed. Prior exact-head CI/review evidence above applies only to b80861750e73; the substantive new guidance needs fresh hosted checks and review. The earlier combined-gate selection failure remains recorded above, not claimed fixed by this edit. Direct non-force main push was refused with GH013 (changes must be made through a pull request); no protection bypass was attempted.

title: feat: enable structured Tool Search by default
body:
Closes #154005

## What Problem This Solves

Hosted OpenClaw runs require an explicit setting to use structured discovery for large tool catalogs.

## User Impact

Structured Tool Search is now the default for embedded and Copilot runs when `tools.toolSearch` is unset. Set `tools.toolSearch: false` to keep direct schemas. Explicit booleans and objects keep their existing semantics; generic Code Mode still takes precedence and Codex-native discovery is unchanged. No configuration file is rewritten.

Small catalogs can cost more, and extra discovery turns can offset initial payload savings. This rollout does not claim a universal latency or token-cost improvement. Explicit `toolSearch: true` still selects the legacy Node code bridge, including its existing wall-clock deadline; the unset default does not use that bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable the shared structured surface while repairing the readiness gaps found in the full review: discovery follows final prompt-hook policy, MCP/client metadata retains its untrusted boundary, sequential calls remain exclusive until implementations settle after cancellation, and client-tool append preserves parked cells' saved results. Labs reflects the default and provides an opt-out.

## Evidence

- Original readiness defects reproduced on the baseline, then repaired with focused regressions.
- Default-on candidate: 521 focused tests passed, plus ten real OpenAI/SSE cases across small and larger catalogs: direct, unset default, and explicit tools/code/directory. Each case verifies an execution-generated nonce, denied-tool exclusion, direct-only visibility, deferred schemas, and transcript delivery.
- Labs: 42 tests passed; actual Chromium/mock-Gateway proof covers the initial default, disabling, restoring the default, and reload without an unsolicited configuration write.
- Real-provider proof is OpenAI/SSE with synthetic catalogs, not a cross-provider reliability benchmark.
- Independent P0–P2 review identified one config-less local-model limit edge. A red/green regression now verifies that local runs retain their 5/10 limits even without a config object; 29 focused cases passed after the repair.
- Broader construction, registration, prompt, metadata, cancellation, and saved-result coverage: 288 tests passed. All selected static gates passed: five typecheck lanes, i18n/config-doc validation, dead-export scans, lint, and ownership/security guards. The remote wrapper ended without a terminal receipt after the type/lint prefix; the seven unfinished tail guards were rerun successfully against the same staged tree locally.

- The initial landing refresh merged current main without rewriting published ancestry. The only conflict was the generated config-documentation hash; canonical regeneration and config-doc/i18n checks passed. The feature patch is byte-equivalent by stable patch ID outside that generated hash.

- A later upstream conflict required merging main `aed59efc4b1` (including #154001). The merge preserves main’s JavaScript-only Code Mode API and canonical `API.read(...).content`, while retaining both before-cell and parked-cell append regressions. The config hash was regenerated, frozen dependencies reconciled, and 319 affected tests across 12 files passed in 95.79s. Independent P0–P2 review of the feature against that new baseline found no actionable issue. Earlier stability proof remains identified with its exact pre-refresh tree; the new head requires fresh hosted CI.

## Landing CI repairs

The first exact-head CI run was diagnosed rather than retried to obtain green. The final head is `60e240a8946`. Exact-head CI `35544902070` passed: 164 successful jobs, 12 skipped, zero failures; the required `openclaw/ci-gate` is successful. Native preparation verified the hosted evidence without changing the head.

- **Active Memory product regression:** embedded prompt-hook authority saw only provider-visible discovery controls, so it suppressed memory recall before any provider request. The adapter now forwards the existing shared owner's filtered, reachable callable catalog while preserving hook caps and live authority. Six mode/cap cases fail before this repair; 46 prompt/authority cases pass afterward. The original two-file Gateway shard passes all three cases with Tool Search still at its default; the synthetic recall calls `memory_get` through `tool_call`, and the grounded-but-terminally-failed result remains excluded from the main prompt.
- **Direct-tool fixtures:** existing scripted Copilot, Gateway publication/yield/fallback, media settlement, and scheduled-message fixtures now explicitly opt out where they test direct-call contracts. Assertions, permissions, timeouts, and delivery checks remain intact. Focused results: 115 Copilot/model-policy cases, 21 Gateway cases, 33 reply/cron cases, and 19 cwd/prompt cases passed.
- **Inherited Doctor failure:** incorporated the landed owner repair from #153988 (`1c2bdf3e26532e71ae3fbb189b5bc58671f288f6`); all nine identifier cases pass.
- **Type-graph capacity:** reused Peter's canonical sessions-subtree split from #153943 (`8e7756d561f579359843bfc6e44cf5ac02aa5656`) after reproducing 703 roots against the unchanged 700-root headroom guard. All 24 graph tests pass; caps, existing stripe assignments, and concurrency are unchanged.
- **Final fixture repairs:** unchanged SDK invocation helpers moved into the existing Copilot test-support owner to satisfy the line-cap guard without suppressions or lost coverage. The inherited migration caller-mode fixture no longer loads 22 unrelated bundled Doctor runtimes: it uses a real isolated contract, verifies that exact module, and retains all mode/plan/receipt assertions. The CI refusal did not recur in isolated local runs; the overbroad loading boundary was demonstrated and corrected.
- **Stability qualification:** a clean Blacksmith Testbox completed 20 consecutive full-file runs (13 cases each), three original 49-file CI shard runs (570 passed / 5 skipped each), and seven owner-sibling files (113 passed). The verified synced tree exactly matches the committed tree. Run `35541572558` completed with wrapper exit 0; the task-owned lease was stopped.
- **Last inherited failure:** `compact-large-8` failed only the Claw archive close-error fixture. The exact repair already landed in #154120 (`a342c6913e008007a6e1ba7211ce63cc656b8ad6`): explicit fs-safe native configuration overrides its environment flag, so the fixture now selects/restores mode through the same configuration owner. This branch reuses that file byte-for-byte. Installer-before-Claw order reproduced the original failure; all 59 cases pass after the fix, with one existing skip. The complete Claw file passes 28 cases / one skip with exit 0. The owning PR supplies Linux/macOS order proof and a green hosted job. A fresh independent review found no issue. Local ordered runs additionally hit a temporary-directory cleanup `EACCES`; that wrapper failure is recorded separately, not counted as a passing command.
- Final repair review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Scoped typecheck, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Runtime build and actual Gateway proof pass.

Compatibility/upgrade review: only an unauthored `tools.toolSearch` value adopts structured discovery. Explicit false, true, and object values keep their previous meanings. The Tool Search rollout itself requires no config rewrite, schema migration, compaction-threshold change, generic Code Mode change, or Codex-native discovery change. The explicit opt-out remains available.

<details>
<summary>Measured repair proof cost</summary>

All focused commands used one worker except the five-file Gateway fixture lane. These are measured suite walls, not invented per-file timings: original refreshed 483-case suite 106.67s; Copilot/model 56.92s (model 22.88s, Copilot 31.97s); five Gateway files 95.84s; reply/cron 57.85s (reported test time: dispatch 23.783s, cron 23.039s); cwd/prompt 33.62s; authority/prompt 20.28s; Active Memory original two-file shard 33.85s Vitest duration (Active Memory 8.374s); graph guard 25.89s. Gateway compositions exercise real admitted runs, provider requests, publication, and cleanup rather than mocked helper results. Live provider tests remain opt-in. The final clean-machine stability command took 29m33.14s; individual caller-file runs and original shard durations were recorded in its terminal log. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the final three-file fixture delta was clean. Exact-head hosted CI completed successfully on September 20, 2026; the required gate passed at 23:47:06 UTC.

</details>

title: feat: report update outcomes by default without identifiers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Daily version checks do not tell maintainers whether an update succeeded, failed, or rolled back, or whether the resulting version was verified running.

## User Impact

Update-outcome pings are **on by default**, like the existing update check, under the current default-on update-check policy. No feature-statistics opt-in is required; optional feature statistics remain off by default.

Set `update.checkOnStart: false` or `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` to stop automatic checks and outcomes. Nix and CI suppress outcomes too, including CI with a custom endpoint. `telemetry.enabled: false`, `openclaw telemetry off`, and `DO_NOT_TRACK` affect feature statistics, not default update checks/outcomes. Invalid/unreadable current configuration fails closed.

**Maintainer privacy decision — approved:** Jason (@fuller-stack-dev) approved Option A on 2026-10-26: default-on update outcomes may be sent even with `DO_NOT_TRACK` or `telemetry.enabled: false`, using the existing automatic-update-check opt-outs. See [the explicit decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154067#issuecomment-6420924172). Production rollout and delivery verification of the compatible receiver and separate outcome dataset (openclaw/telemetry#23, merged) are separately authorized work, not proved here. The client sends no outcome POST unless the receiver advertises the required capability.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing update ledger owns the result. A closed schema-2 projection includes release-format before/target/resulting/running versions, fixed platform/install/channel/outcome categories, coarse duration, observed verification, rollback and allowlisted failure codes: exactly 18 fields, no run/install/user identifiers, raw diagnostic text, logs, paths or config. PATCH is a sequential release-train number (`2026.8.33`, `2026.8.123`), canonical 0–999999; private labels, metadata and leading zeros map to `unknown`.

Before any outcome body is sent, the client makes a body-free HEAD request to the exact configured endpoint. Only HTTP 204 with `OpenClaw-Update-Results: 2` permits the POST; legacy 405 and unconfigured 503 suppress it. Both requests share one three-second deadline, refuse redirects, and use the fixed `User-Agent: openclaw-update-result/1`. Custom endpoints never fall back to the Foundation endpoint.

Bounded local bookkeeping claims an attempt before network dispatch: one attempt per hour, no historical scan/backfill, no durable retry outbox or exactly-once guarantee. Reporting cannot fail or roll back an update. The first upgrade from an older updater has no admission marker and does not report.

### Refreshed design on current main (this head)

The previous head was ~20k commits behind and conflicted with main's worker-owned update writers. This head re-applies the feature to current main's owners as one commit:

- **Worker-safe storage** (`src/infra/update-result-claim.ts`): eligibility admission and the hourly claim live in the existing `config_machine_state` table and run inside the same state-database transaction (SQLite or PostgreSQL) as run creation / terminal settlement, in a nested savepoint. This module never imports host configuration, fixing the prior P2 (`update-run-interruption-store.ts` → telemetry → `config/io`).
- **Host policy and dispatch** (`src/infra/update-result-telemetry.ts`): reads current update-request policy (lazily loading the config reader) and sends HEAD/POST. It is not in the shared-state worker graph.
- **Owners wired**: worker `updateRuns.create` admits from a host-read `reportResult` flag; worker `updateRuns.finish` and the interrupted-completion settlement return a claimed payload that the host dispatches only after commit; sync CLI terminal writers (`openclaw update`, finalize/repair, Windows task recovery, pre-activation signal interruption) and the shipped `dist/cli/daemon-cli.js` `finishUpdateRun` recovery entry pass a host reporter to the existing ledger finish. Main's asynchronous reconciliation and worker-owned writers are preserved; no retired synchronous API is restored.
- **Policy check points**: admission (new runs only) and immediately before the HEAD and again before the POST. The separate settlement-time check from the old head was dropped as redundant: a revoked policy still sends nothing; it only consumes that hour's local attempt slot.
- **Bookkeeping cannot fail the update write**: admission and claim run in the existing nested savepoint (`runSqliteImmediateTransactionSync`, both engines). A failed bookkeeping statement rolls back only the bookkeeping; on PostgreSQL it previously aborted the whole transaction (`PostgreSQL transaction rolled back instead of committing`). Dispatch still happens only after the outer commit.
- **Never-attempted chat refusals** (`owner_required`, including a revoked requester) are excluded like abandoned/superseded: not reported and not counted against the hourly attempt.
- **Tests cannot reach the production receiver**: the shared test environment (`test/test-env.ts`) points `OPENCLAW_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` at a refused loopback port, which spawned CLI/Gateway children inherit.
- The old head's madge cycle (`update-result-payload` ↔ interruption contract) is gone.

Contributor credit: Json (@fuller-stack-dev), Peter (@steipete), and Vincent (@vincentkoc).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @fuller-stack-dev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a62b8ab5-1773-445c-a645-f08708eed3ca)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/6a2d3e00-d395-4898-91aa-779478893c54)

## Evidence

The focused suites and CI recorded below target head **`e212c8cbd152ca30ef2b81c91b801d328fab601f`** (base `592df0b4c67`). The earlier focused local runs used a sanitized environment with inherited service variables, `HOME` and `CI` unset and a private `TMPDIR`. The new receiver proof uses an explicit private HOME as described below. Shared managed-update handoff stores were snapshotted before/after the local proofs and were unchanged. Historical failures are identified separately; no prior-head upgrade proof is claimed for this candidate.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused suites: all `src/infra/update-run-*.test.ts`, update-run watcher, shared-state worker import boundary, `update-result-telemetry.test.ts`, affected CLI (`update-command-run`, finalize lifecycle/refusal, Windows task, mutable signals, lifecycle, admission ledger), gateway (`update`, restart, host-owned, campaign), startup campaign/apply-error/startup, migrated finalize worker, doctor settlement, eager import closure, daily-check `telemetry`/`telemetry.async`/`telemetry-cli`, `shell-env`, `test/setup-home-isolation.test.ts` | **50 files: 888 passed, 1 skipped**, 333 s |
| PostgreSQL conformance (`update-run-admission.conformance.test.ts`, pinned `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` locally) | 5 passed, 1 skipped (the new case is PostgreSQL-only) |
| `pnpm check:changed` | Every lane passes (format, core + core-test + test-root typecheck, core/scripts/test-root lint, SQLite worker/dialect ratchets, mock-export ratchet, import cycles, …) except the dead-export scan, whose findings are a subset of the same scan on current main `56d940f529c` and touch no file in this PR |
| `pnpm check:architecture` | Passed, 2 m 08 s: 0 runtime cycles, 0 madge cycles |

**Bookkeeping failures (review P2 #1).** A trigger rejects every `telemetry.updateResults` write after the run was admitted:

- PostgreSQL conformance: worker run creation and terminal settlement both commit and nothing is sent. Against the previous claim module the same case fails with `PostgreSQL transaction rolled back instead of committing`.
- SQLite (`update-result-telemetry.test.ts`): sync admission + settlement, worker settlement and verified interrupted completion all commit with nothing sent. These also pass against the previous claim module, because SQLite's `RAISE(ABORT)` only backs out the failing statement; they guard the contract rather than prove the regression. Worker *creation* can't take this trigger (its full schema verification refuses unexpected triggers); it runs the same admission function as the sync case.

**Test network leak (review P2 #2).** A fetch probe in `update-startup.campaign-apply-error.test.ts`, run without `CI`: the previous code made three outcome HEAD requests to `https://telemetry.openclaw.ai/api/latest-version` (intercepted by the probe). With only the new shared test default they go to `http://127.0.0.1:9/…`. With the full change (shared default + the file's sender mock) there are none. `test/setup-home-isolation.test.ts` now asserts that a case emulating production (`VITEST` cleared, `NODE_ENV=production`) only reaches loopback. Other suites that clear the runner markers and can settle runs (`update-startup.test.ts`, `client-credential-update.test.ts`, `gateway-external-state-ownership.e2e.test.ts` via child processes) are covered by the shared default.

**Mutation checks** on `update-result-telemetry.test.ts`, each caught: a per-request POST deadline (stalled-POST case), `owner_required` reported, plus the earlier four (post-HEAD recheck, capability header, eligibility gate, hourly limit).

### Other review items

- Activation admission: `openclaw update` now reads reporting policy before its final package-activation admission check, so nothing yields between that check and run creation.
- Transport tests: a capable HEAD followed by a stalled POST settles at the original deadline (only the first deadline is shortened; a per-request deadline would hold the POST for 10 s). POST redirects are refused. Endpoints with URL credentials or a non-HTTP scheme send nothing. The assertion that mirrored the 3000 ms constant was removed.
- Not excluded: an automatic campaign retired after its run was recorded but before the updater started settles as `failed` with `unexpected-error` (or the error's code). Main records the same reasons when the updater actually ran and threw, so excluding them by reason would drop real failures; doing it properly needs a distinct ledger reason, which is a separate user-visible change. Documented in `docs/gateway/telemetry.md`. Ctrl-C before activation settles as failed and is reported (also documented), as is the up-to-three-second CLI exit delay while a report is in flight.

### Exact-head CI

[CI on `e212c8cb`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40275326021): **all 96 checks pass, including `openclaw/ci-gate`** and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards; the new PostgreSQL bookkeeping-failure case ran and passed there. The two earlier main-owned failures are gone on this base: `checks-node-changed-2` (fixed on main by #184188) and `checks-node-changed-compact-large-22` (the settle-replay harness test passes on this run).

### Old-head CI failures, diagnosed

- `check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture` ([log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36086734857/job/107920601128)): madge cycle introduced by the original head. Fixed; `check:architecture` passes on this head.
- `checks-node-compact-large-6` ([log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36086734857/job/107921448814)): `src/state/openclaw-state.worker.imports.test.ts` failed because the shared-state worker reached `config/io` through the telemetry module. Fixed; that test also covers the lazily loaded `update-run-dispatch.worker.ts` and forbids `update-result-telemetry.ts`.

### Exact-head ledger → real HTTP → receiver Worker proof (2026-10-26)

**Passed on client `e212c8cbd152ca30ef2b81c91b801d328fab601f`**, tree `948cdc04203ca7919f24bd20d548ada92282f8db`, against unmodified **openclaw/telemetry main `e4954d7b90c20808646c6f43e698d2359cdc1799`**, tree `7512c1fd89345d65aa104fdaf881237f5308a4c6` (includes merged #23). Native Node 26.12.1 on macOS arm64; real workerd 1.20260926.1 via Miniflare 5.20260926.1-alpha. **46.996 seconds; all five cases passed.** This replaces the prior `424228e6` receiver claim for the current candidate.

The harness uses the actual async ledger owners: `createUpdateRunAsync` → state-worker admission → `recordUpdateRunVerificationAsync` → `finishUpdateRunAsync` → committed terminal result/claim → real host configuration reader → unmodified default `fetch`. It asserts durable settlement and admission/attempt bookkeeping. The receiver is the actual bundled source running under workerd, not a synthetic response handler. A transparent loopback proxy holds the **real** HEAD response while the opt-out is written to disk, then releases it. Negative cases are observed beyond the complete three-second request deadline.

| Case | Observed HTTP | Outcome writes | Daily writes | POST body |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Newly admitted, settled success | HEAD **204**, capability **2** → POST **200** | **1** | **0** | **18 fields, 407 bytes** |
| `update.checkOnStart:false` written while HEAD is held | HEAD **204** only; **no POST** | **0** | **0** | none |
| Outcome binding absent | HEAD **503** only; **no POST** | **0** | **0** | none |
| Admitted with policy disabled/no marker, then policy enabled | **No requests**; no attempt claimed | **0** | **0** | none |
| `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` and `telemetry.enabled:false` | HEAD **204**, capability **2** → POST **200** | **1** | **0** | **18 fields, 407 bytes** |

Both POSTs carried `User-Agent: openclaw-update-result/1`; wire traces assert no cookie, authorization, referer/referrer and no run ID or path in the exact closed 18-key body. The only external response stub is the receiver's npm lookup; any other Worker outbound URL is rejected. Count instrumentation delegates each observed write to Miniflare's real local Analytics Engine binding. The local AE simulator is not production ingestion: **this proves receiver write routing, not deployed dataset delivery**.

title: fix(update): keep diagnostic artifact links readable after redaction
body:
Related: #153795

**Superseded:** the complete reported defect is fixed on main by [#153662](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153662), commit `e8ced6be50f96e32316a6ff8795f86b2c9821369`. Our unchanged seven-case regression file passes against that canonical production, and its five canonical cases plus 55 owner siblings also pass. No duplicate producer merge is needed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update failure report links to a nonexistent diagnostic file when a generated UUID ends in a long decimal component.

## User Impact

Operators can open the complete lint inventory and bounded diagnostic JSON linked from update failure reports. Privacy redaction still masks real secrets and personal identifiers. Existing caller-selected paths, ledger run IDs, file permissions, and stored reports remain unchanged; no migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The artifact writer used hyphenated UUIDs. Support redaction intentionally masks standalone runs of nine or more digits, so an all-decimal UUID tail became `<redacted-id>` inside a link. This is a product input-shape bug, not test-order noise.

Encode separators in internally generated artifact IDs as underscores. This preserves entropy and length while preventing numeric UUID components from becoming standalone identifiers. Apply the same owner operation to lint inventories, default failure JSON, and detached/generated report IDs. Do not weaken redaction or change caller-provided paths or real ledger IDs.

The installed updater and recovery protocol do not change. Existing frozen released-reader coverage, source-checked against v2026.9.4, reads the new generated paths with its original size limits and redaction behavior.

## Evidence

- The valid synthetic UUID `7070f794-196a-4f08-91dc-123456789012` reproduces the original broken inventory path. New normal and detached report-link cases also fail against the original writer with the same ENOENT.
- After repair: **7/7 tests passed**, including released-reader compatibility, unchanged ledger filenames, secret/phone redaction, and POSIX private-file permissions.
- **20 consecutive standalone runs passed** with no retry; **3 original 123-file CI shard-plan replays passed** (1,724 tests passed and one conditional skip each), followed by **55 owner-sibling tests**. Replays used the normal CI sequencer rather than forcing the historical execution order; the strengthened test moved earlier after its two added cases.
- Measured cost: `pnpm test src/commands/triage-update-rollback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took **1.915 s wall**, approximately **147 ms test time**. Repeated whole-file runs took 1.716–1.979 s. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35537020565/job/106147878821) passed all seven receipt cases in **0.116 s summed reported case execution** (excludes setup/transform); its 61-file group passed 961 tests with one conditional skip.
- Focused commands typecheck and both-file lint passed. The broader changed-check gate originally stopped on the separate stale codec import in #154048. That independently verified dependency is included and has separately landed in #153988; the two-file receipt repair is byte-identical.
- Independent full-candidate autoreview through P3 is scoped-clean, with no actionable findings or hostile changes identified. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35537020565) passed at `8046512de8c`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. ClawSweeper also completed review with no actionable correctness or security findings. The native landing inputs subsequently advanced, first to `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.17 and then to updated CI/landing scripts. Current head `8859d96c358c6bc9785d5beea0f6074c92ffdb41` incorporates trusted main `691da4f147a`; its two-file repair is byte-for-byte unchanged. On the fs-safe 0.17 baseline, seven rollback cases passed in **3.566 s wall** and **55 owner-sibling tests passed**, with no failures or retries. Those owner files and dependency versions are unchanged in this final mechanical refresh. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35538998930) passed on `8859d96c`, with all 164 jobs terminal and the required `openclaw/ci-gate` green. The native merge stopped before dispatch on the now-redundant same-file conflict. No merge request was sent; its retained operation lock was recovered through the supported command after verifying no child tools remained. The earlier `8046512` run is retained as prior-head evidence; the new gate is independently verified.

title: feat(ui): mention people in the quick composer

Closes #154032

## What Problem This Solves

The Cmd/Ctrl+K quick composer cannot select people to mention when starting a task.

## User Impact

Users can type `@`, choose eligible people with the keyboard or pointer, and see a compact **Will notify** row before starting the task in the background. One, two, and multiple recipients stay compact; existing image paste and the foreground draft are preserved.

Mentions do not grant access or change session visibility. Typed or pasted `@name` text remains ordinary text until a person is explicitly selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing people picker, access-scoped new-session directory, selected-recipient strip, and first-message mention annotations rather than introducing another editor or notification path.

## What Problem This Solves

When a chat turn contains several videos, watching them currently requires closing the expanded player and opening each clip separately.

## User Impact

Move between videos in the same turn with Left/Right arrow keys, previous/next buttons, or a horizontal swipe on the picture. Native playback controls retain their keyboard and touch behavior; navigation stops at turn boundaries. No settings or migration required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing image viewer, navigation controller, keyboard handling, and swipe logic. Videos skip image decoding; the same gallery controller disconnects the previous player on navigation or close. A small selected-video adapter calls the unchanged attachment resolver and existing playback source controller for tickets and retries.

Preserves current main’s lazy attachment viewport, shared playback retry, original download filenames, and Shift+Arrow image panning. The small modal-focus and drawer guards keep gallery input from interfering with native controls.

title: feat(ui): refresh work progress without adding a chat message
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A saved task-progress card can become stale while work continues. Refreshing it currently requires a visible chat request, which adds noise and does not distinguish requesting an update from receiving a saved update.

## User Impact

Adds a small refresh button to expanded and collapsed composer progress cards. It asks the agent to reconcile the card with current work, blockers and next steps without inserting a visible chat message. Pending, retry and updated states preserve the draft, transcript, disclosure and previous card. Success requires a newer authoritative saved-card revision. Read-only projections remain read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses a typed, authorized progressCard.refresh RPC and the existing trusted internal steering path rather than a browser-generated chat.send. The original caller principal and session lifecycle checks are retained. A standalone refresh has restricted tools and hidden transcript/delivery projections; steering existing work does not replace its tools or visible reply. Refresh input cannot answer pending human-input requests, and an unconfirmed steering receipt cannot abort independently authorized work.

Requested by and implemented with @steipete.

## Evidence

- Initial complete changed-file gate passed: formatting, line caps, generated schema consistency, i18n, core and test types, UI types/styles, lint, portable platform checks, database and authorization guards.
- pnpm build passed on the configured isolated Blacksmith Testbox.
- Focused runtime, authorization, transcript visibility, human-input isolation, UI store/component and pane tests passed. Registered-Gateway integration covers idle dispatch, rejected-steer fallback, confirmed and unconfirmed active steering, concurrent visible human messages and read-only denial.
- Actual-browser proof passed for desktop expanded, 390px collapsed and failure/retry scenarios. Before screenshots use a clean base snapshot; after screenshots exercise the implemented UI against a controlled Gateway fixture. No live-provider result is claimed. Sanitized before/after screenshots are embedded below; these capture the implemented application, not the design preview.

The real enqueue/drain/lifecycle and followup runner are exercised with controlled provider/session edges: separate runtime ID, progress, terminal no-update, abandonment, consumed steering and replaced-controller cases. Three regressions fail before the queued repair; all 38 tests across four focused Gateway suites pass afterward.
