title: fix(update): avoid size failures and memory spikes in Git updates
body:
Related: #145501 (Git update transfer and recovery).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Git-checkout updates fail above a 256 MiB candidate pack and unnecessarily retain and copy the whole pack in the updater process.

## User Impact

Large Git updates no longer hit the fixed size cap or allocate a pack-sized JavaScript buffer. Git reads the already-open staged file directly, without copying its contents through JavaScript, IPC, or a stdin pipe.

The staged pack and Git's installed pack still exist on disk: Git retains responsibility for validating and publishing the imported objects. This is not a zero-disk-copy claim. Already-installed updaters retain their old behavior until replaced; candidate code cannot repair that first blocked update.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the process runner's native stdin-descriptor convention instead of creating a custom Git object-store installer. Pin the safely opened file before admission, and close it on every exit before deleting the inspection checkout. Preserve complete-object checks, offline partial-clone activation, keep-file ownership, concurrent-repack protection, and rollback.

The original cap was added in Jason's (@fuller-stack-dev) maintainer commit `3b461b99`, then merged with Dallin's original PR on September 12, 2026 UTC. It bounded the retained buffer; it was not a free-disk-space check.

## Evidence

- **Exact-head CI passed:** [run 35536679490](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35536679490) for `86ce28abfb7f1e221068e392021caec4f499cc10`; the native watcher finished `GREEN`, including the required security-review aggregation.
- Real Git before/after with a valid **269,504,993-byte pack**: original code rejects it at 268,435,456 bytes; fixed code imports, checks out a 257 MiB blob, verifies its hash, and releases its owned keep file. During fixed preparation, the observed retained ArrayBuffer delta was **352 bytes**, not a pack-sized allocation. Isolated fixture removed; no operator Gateway touched.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-runner-git-transfer.test.ts src/infra/update-runner-git-admission.test.ts src/process/exec.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **108 passed, 1 pre-existing platform skip**, 26.32 s wall time across two routed shards. The process test file took 5.24 s including setup, with about 3.6 s of test execution. Coverage includes descriptor inheritance/parent close, removed staging pathname, competing input rejection, offline imports, admission refusal, retry, rollback, published-checkout moves, retained pack ownership, and descriptor release.
- The first admission run exposed the fixture's byte-only stdin adapter; extending that real-Git fixture to forward descriptors fixed the resulting early-EOF failures. No retry-based workaround.
- Targeted typed lint: zero warnings/errors; `git diff --check` and core production typecheck pass. Fresh independent review of the complete staged candidate: no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- CI run `35536155647` passed all three core-test typing jobs but found the new native-descriptor assertion lacked the required adjacent `// SAFETY:` marker. The same guard failure reproduced locally; moving and marking the existing explanation fixes it without changing code behavior. No baseline exception or job rerun was used.
- Includes the same two-line import-owner repair tracked in #154048: a baseline task-identifier test still imported `bindSubagentRunRecord` from SQLite storage after #153838 moved it to the codec. This was the sole core-test type error. The existing nine tests now pass (9.25 s wall); no runtime/schema/assertion changes. The local core-test rerun has no retained terminal receipt; all core-test typing jobs subsequently passed in exact-head CI run `35536679490`.
- The local Git proofs are transfer-boundary plus existing update-flow tests, not native Windows execution. No large every-PR fixture was added.
- **Published-driver × candidate CI proof:** [run 35536679490, artifact `docker-seed-upgrade-survivor-proof`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35536679490/artifacts/10613262168) passed the `legacy-operator-state` cell in **229 s**. Published `openclaw@2026.9.4` used its own updater to install the candidate tarball (`2026.9.5`, merge tree `fe4bc1e8a996`, whose PR parent is `86ce28abfb7f`), with `auto-auth` restart and a successful update outcome. Serving probes, legacy agent/cron/plugin survival, repeat-update/Doctor checks, and backup rollback passed; update/restart took **121 s**. The optional post-core exit snapshot was unavailable. This is package-upgrade proof, not a claim that an old Git driver can bypass its existing pack cap.

### Original-issue regression verification

Verified the original #145494 failure, not just the new size limit:

- A real filtered partial clone and the production private-inspection helper reproduce the legacy local-fetch failure: exit 128 with `lazy fetching disabled`, `could not fetch ... from promisor remote`, and `bad pack header`.
- Against the same fixture, the new descriptor path prepares before admission, then imports successfully after the upstream directory is made unavailable. The candidate HEAD and target blob hash match, Git verifies every installed pack, and the invocation-owned keep file is removed.
- **260 tests passed**: the original four updater regression files (**206**) plus CLI post-update recovery (**54**), **47.85 s** total wrapper wall time. This covers offline stable/dev updates, downgrade/divergent targets, staging failure before admission, failed import with valid/invalid/changed retained runtime, and recovery-restart eligibility and terminal reporting.
- The broader run identified one remaining byte-only test adapter and ambient Git identity contamination. Forwarding canonical command options and isolating fixture identity fixed them; exact committer assertions remain intact. Fresh independent review of these test repairs is clean through P1. The original-issue follow-up changes only test fixtures; the later CI repair only relocates and marks the existing descriptor safety comment, without changing production behavior.
- This original-issue proof is Linux real Git plus service-boundary regression tests, supplemented by the published-package upgrade cell above. It is **not** a new native macOS LaunchAgent restart or a large-pack Git update driven by an old installed updater. The original installed-driver first-hop limitation is unchanged.

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-runner-git-admission.test.ts src/infra/update-runner-git-candidate.test.ts src/infra/update-runner-git-transfer.test.ts src/infra/update-runner.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

Fixes: the composer fade returns over the last line of a multiline draft when users move between letters or words with the keyboard, even though the viewport has not moved.

title: fix(ui): avoid repeated waits in the people picker
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated waiting in the human-mention picker when reopening it or starting another `@` mention.

## User Impact

Recent searches show people immediately in both existing-chat and New Session composers. Results older than five minutes refresh in the background while remaining selectable. New searches still use the Gateway’s authoritative matching rules. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker already cached exact searches, but discarded them on close and on a new mention token. Keep its bounded cache for the same connection, profile, and session instead. Refreshes share one request, preserve the selected person, and recover from stalled reads after 15 seconds. Access/identity rejection invalidates the cache; transient failures back off, and successful snapshots expire after 30 minutes. Recipient access is still rechecked by the Gateway when sending.

## Evidence

- Second inherited CI repair: the next hosted run passed every UI, browser, performance, and docs lane, but an unrelated task identifier test still imported serialization from a retired SQLite export. The seven failures reproduce on clean main; importing the existing codec owner makes all nine tests pass without changing runtime, schema, or assertions. The import-only correction passed fresh P2 autoreview.
- Public hosted validation: [run 35534028928](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35534028928) passed all three UI shards, all thirteen UI E2E shards, real-Gateway UI E2E, Control UI performance, and docs; its aggregate failed on the task-test import above. The earlier Testbox leases were explicitly stopped after command exit 0, so their overall workflow records show cancellation rather than a full hosted-CI success.

- CI recovery: the first hosted run passed all picker/UI checks but failed an inherited `changed-lanes` expectation on the synthetic merge. The same failure reproduces on clean `main` (`71fe55536b6`) without this PR. Include the existing picker-layout TypeScript fixture in the exact stylelint target list, matching the selector and its sibling tests; seven focused selector cases now pass. This is a one-line test correction, with no additional production change. Fresh P2 autoreview of the correction is clean.

- 116 unit tests passed, including both composers, refresh ordering, owner changes, denial, expiry, retry pacing, bounded cache size, and real request-deadline recovery.
- Four built-Control-UI Chromium tests passed at desktop and mobile widths: cached reopen, background refresh, selection preservation, exact-query matching, and cold-loading behavior. The new reopen assertions fail against the original implementation.
- UI typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh autoreview is scoped-clean through P2; its context-switch race finding was fixed and covered by two regressions.
- Exact candidate bytes were checked before remote execution: [final unit/static proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35532216920) and [built-UI browser proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35525768111). Fixes: message-recovery work is hidden behind an account-footer count when outgoing submissions fail or delivery cannot be confirmed.

## User Impact

Users can find compact recovery entries in **Inbox → System** and choose **Review** to open the existing chat controls. Ordinary queued work stays in chat; identity and connection indicators no longer carry delivery counts.

Existing browser-tab/Gateway ownership remains unchanged; per-person isolation (#129188) is outside this PR's scope. No storage-format, authentication, or retention changes. Global entries omit message content, attachment names, command arguments, and private diagnostics.

Only submissions requiring recovery belong in Inbox. Entries read the canonical outbox state and cannot be independently dismissed. The compact row uses plain-language status, conversation context with an adjacent Offline label, and one Review action. Longer guidance stays in its tooltip. Offline Inbox exposes local review entries without enabling server-dependent actions.

Also fixes a producer-state bug: an exact pending-input receipt could leave a message marked unconfirmed. title: feat: personalize USER bootstrap with authenticated profiles
body:
Closes #153965

## What Problem This Solves

A shared agent workspace has one USER.md, so preferences cannot automatically follow the authenticated person currently requesting work.

## User Impact

Operators can add an optional `users/<canonical-profile-id>/USER.md` in the agent workspace. OpenClaw loads shared USER.md defaults first and the current person’s preferences second, without selecting people from display names, message text, or session ownership. Missing personal files keep shared defaults.

This is prompt selection, **not filesystem secrecy or conversation-history erasure**. Internal/delegated turns, ACP, realtime sessions, remote worker execution, and existing embedded continuation-skip suppression remain outside this per-turn selection. The shared local owner remains one shared identity. No schema/config migration or live Gateway change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the authenticated ingress participant and canonical profile owner rather than introduce another identity map. Personal files use guarded, bounded reads and the existing memory-eligibility rules, stay outside shared bootstrap snapshots, and are omitted whole when they exceed their budget. Collected mixed-person turns have no personal overlay; incompatible steering follows the existing queued-turn path. Native Codex keeps personal files turn-scoped, and generic CLI reuse refreshes when personal context changes or disappears.

Worked on by @VACInc.

title: fix: keep model refresh indicators compact and accurate
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the model picker’s prominent “checking models…” row and refresh indicators that can remain stuck when discovery returns an unchanged catalog.

## User Impact

Background refreshes use a compact spinner while existing models stay selectable. Provider details work by hover, keyboard, or tap; completion preserves search focus. Large model searches remain usable with reduced motion enabled. Empty, offline, and failed states remain explicit. No cache lifetime, configuration, permissions, or storage changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawRouter already caches discovery for 60 seconds; the picker reuses published catalog snapshots. The problem was presentation plus a missing completion notification: unchanged successful renewals suppressed both the catalog-status signal and the metadata notification. The patch notifies consumers without rebuilding unchanged model/command projections.

Requested and reported by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4eb30b92-3e3a-40de-a182-ec24c5fbb966)

## Evidence

- **72 backend regressions and 99 final UI unit tests passed**, covering catalog settlement/cache identity, refresh focus, and reduced-motion cleanup.
- **26 final browser cases passed** across chat and new-session flows, including 1,000-model typing in normal and reduced-motion modes, keyboard/touch details, refresh settlement, and bootstrap ordering.
- Replayed the three original failing shard selections: **5,359 passed, 5 skipped**. The concrete upstream repairs are listed below.
- UI production typechecking, core test-type stripes 3/5 and 4/5, i18n verification, targeted stylelint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Fresh full-candidate autoreview is clean through P2.
- These are real UI renders with synthetic Gateway/provider fixtures, not live-provider discovery claims. Before/after and keyboard-settlement captures were also delivered in the originating discussion.
- Blacksmith Testbox proof: [run 35545688983](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35545688983). Commands returned exit 0; the proof lease is confirmed stopped. Its Actions lifecycle is separate from individual command results.
- Published source: `aa0d6f8853495cec9f07df58021f3d00b3f97f22`. Required exact-head CI and the required publisher gate passed; native preparation also passed.

### CI root causes and rebase

The branch was rebased onto `b73d0e4541e` after tracing the failed run to concrete upstream repairs—not rerunning an unchanged red head:

- **Registry import/type failure:** #153988 (`1c2bdf3e265`) imports `bindSubagentRunRecord` from its codec owner after serialization moved out of the SQLite store. This fixes the same seven runtime failures and the test-type error without restoring a retired re-export.
- **Checkout-dependent Stylelint expectation:** #153979 (`68a2efb8302`) owns explicit TS/CSS fixtures and covers both present and deleted TypeScript inputs. The original expectation changed when a real UI test file appeared in the checkout.
- **Task-fixture worker lifetime:** #154083 (`fc7c481d118`) drains worker-backed state before deleting temporary fixtures. Its regression proves cleanup occurs while the directory exists. The historical admission failure did not record its invalidating caller; inode reuse is a source-supported explanation, not a directly observed event.

Fresh review also found a keyboard-focus regression when the transient refresh button disappears. It reproduced for ready/error/offline settlement before the repair. The existing picker DOM-sync owner now restores search focus—or the stable trigger if the catalog becomes empty—without stealing moved focus or reviving a closed/detached picker. Seven lifecycle cases cover the repair; the full presentation file passes 18 tests in 1.94 s wall, and UI typechecking passes. The /chat and /new browser flows now assert the same handoff.

The retained reduced-motion failure was investigated rather than dismissed as an unrelated flake. A four-cell browser experiment separated screenshot effects from live motion changes: only reduced-motion cells stalled. Input handlers finished before the second keyboard dispatch stopped responding. Disabling popup autosizing, preserving a transform, or disabling row-only transitions did not repair it; setting the global transition duration to zero did. The old positive duration enabled otherwise-static transitions, including scrollbar color and focus outline changes.

The repair changes that existing stylesheet policy to zero-duration transitions. Toast cleanup already handles reduced motion directly; hovercard cleanup now does too, without waiting for a transition event that will not occur. The retained /chat regression fails at the unchanged 10-second typing action before the CSS repair, and both final routes pass afterward. The original normal-motion benchmark remains intact. No timeout, assertion, baseline, or CI gate was weakened.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

Standalone commands used one worker (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, or the owning `pnpm test:ui:e2e` entrypoint). Wall time includes startup/build/transform cost; original backend and bootstrap file measurements are retained for unchanged test source. The final model-control and cleanup sources were measured separately. All three browser files also pass together after the motion repair (100.39 s wall).

title: feat(sessions): support explicit local placement for child sessions
body:
Related: #153863

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_spawn` has an explicit cloud target but no explicit local target, so callers must omit placement to request local execution.

## User Impact

Callers can now use `placement: { kind: "local" }`, or omit `placement` to take the same local path. This works for hidden native runs, ACP runs, and visible local sessions under their existing runtime and visibility rules.

Cloud selection remains explicit: `{ kind: "profile", profileId, os?, machineClass? }` requires `visible: true` and `worktree: true`. Invalid or mixed local/cloud selectors, `null`, and cloud-placement failures remain errors; they never silently become local execution. No permissions, persistent schema, or configured cloud defaults change. The restricted cloud-worker tool retains its existing parent-profile inheritance.

## Why This Change Was Made

One closed local/profile schema owns both advertised tool arguments and input validation. Valid explicit-local requests normalize onto the existing local dispatch path; omitted placement keeps that default. Documentation, model-facing guidance, and generated tool snapshots describe both choices.

This adds the local selector requested in the follow-up; it does not establish which component produced the original placeholder values.

title: feat(control-ui): notify everyone with access to a shared chat
body:
Closes #153886

## What Problem This Solves

Team members need an intentional way to notify everyone who can already read a shared conversation, without selecting each person individually.

## User Impact

Select **@everyone** from the people picker to notify eligible human profiles, including offline teammates. The notification strip stays aligned on mobile and desktop, with a rounded accent background behind the group icon.

The option appears for a lone bare `@` or a matching substring such as `@ev` or `@yon`; a second bare `@` offers individual people instead. Person substring searches remain intact. Typed or pasted text alone never pings. The sender and agents are excluded, existing access and notification preferences apply, and the audience is bounded to 1,000 people.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing mention directory, pending-input custody, and Inbox remain responsible for delivery. Private audience receipts never enter pending-message, transcript, history, or model-context JSON. Accepted queued or interrupted input retains its original audience, including across restart; current access is checked again before delivery.

Touched persistent Inbox and input-custody operations now use the existing database workers, with live authority checked at commit and accepted completion joined before shutdown. This required updating the existing admission and completion callers, not just the UI. Large audiences use atomic ordinary ten-recipient Inbox records, preserving released-reader compatibility, dismissal, deduplication, and expiry. No table, column, schema-version, permission, or configuration migration is introduced.

## Evidence

- Actual Control UI proof covers explicit selection → submission → transcript in ordinary, new-session, and quick composers. UI integration passed **348 focused unit cases and five type lanes**; final browser proof passed **53 codec, 24 Chromium layout, two ordinary-send, and three quick-composer cases**. Inspected desktop/mobile captures are below. These use synthetic fixtures, not a production-wide ping.
- Worker, custody, current-access, private-audience, restart/replay, notification, and shutdown proof passed. The pre-CI integrated backend run passed **213 cases across eight files plus nine first-message cases**. Actual **v2026.9.5** Inbox/history/model modules also passed compatibility checks with **107 recipients in 11 ordinary rows**, unchanged schema/version markers, preserved dismissal/replay/expiry, and no audience IDs exposed in messages. This is tagged-source proof, not an old packaged-Gateway update rehearsal.
- CI exposed a real reservation race: awaiting a no-op retry lookup let concurrent Goals bypass reservation checks and delayed Stop-visible preregistration. No-read preparation is synchronous again; real reads retain current-authority/target checks, followed by fresh conflict inspection before the claim. **The existing Goal-collision and Stop/reclaim suites passed unchanged.**
- CI-repair verification passed the worker boundary, **14 Gateway integration files**, and **436 runner/selection cases**. Targeted closure passed **63 pre-admission/embeddings, 10 canonical-completion, and 18 read-only-worker process cases**, with clean typed lint. A complete caller inventory found and closed the final two broker-lane omissions; their queue/schema suites passed with joined fixture cleanup.
- The last auth failure depended on upstream concurrent-approval behavior, so it was tested in the **exact failed CI merge**, not only the feature checkout. The corrected fixture holds the SSH probe through the pending-response assertions without changing authorization. The full original auth shard passed **57 files / 795 cases / zero skips**; the feature fixture also passed **10 cases**. [Exact-merge Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35714172088) exited **0**; its owned environment was stopped.
- The Telegram replay fixture now joins actual queue deferral, preserving abandonment/retry/watermark assertions. Its original **9-file / 436-case** CI plan passed. The survivor-tooling plan passed **47 files / 1,565 cases, 73 skipped** with diagnostic-only changes; its earlier failure remains unclassified. [Bounded fixture proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35724902639): typed lint clean, wrapper **exit 0**, owned Testbox stopped.
- Core/types, lint, assets, dead-code/import/size guards and prior SDK/UI builds passed in recorded scopes. Both projection regressions are retained. **Final combined-head CI remains required.**
- Independent P2 review found and closed the earlier profile-merge, missing-target, and embedded-token defects. A separate **one-pass review of the CI-repair delta** found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Later fixture corrections preserve the assertions and asynchronous contracts; no safety guard, timeout, or baseline was relaxed.

No live push-provider trial or production deployment is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Repair ownership and remaining limits</summary>

Existing worker, custody, projection, and fixture owners handle the cutover. Fixtures join retirement, restore configuration, preserve physical store identity, and keep fault injection on the actual connection. No sleeps, timeout increases, new per-case Gateway boots, assertion cuts, safety exemptions, or baseline changes were added. The Telegram fixture builder moved unchanged to its existing test-support owner to keep the line cap intact.

The unrelated retained-Doctor hardlink defect was fixed upstream by [e99e75e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e99e75e2e60a48875d63f6d84a3db4882ca00252); its original regression and 46 companion cases passed. No duplicate fix was published.

New broadcast selection needs updated Gateway/UI. Tagged-source proof is not a packaged updater, full downgrade, or mixed-native-client rehearsal.

Earlier Windows native teardown, compile-cache deadlines, and survivor-service inspection failures lack proven source causes. Bounded subsequent checks passed, but passing replay is not a causal repair. The survivor assertion now reports its full inspection result if it fails again; behavior and timing are unchanged. Failed attempts remain recorded separately. Current-head CI/security/review gates still apply.

title: feat: let agents request attention in sessions
body:
Closes #153807

## What Problem This Solves

Agents cannot bring a teammate’s attention to a session when a decision, review, or requested handoff is ready. Plain `@name` text intentionally does not notify anyone.

## User Impact

A Gateway-hosted agent can explicitly request an eligible person’s attention from its current session. The existing Mentions Inbox shows the configured name and avatar—such as **Atlas mentioned you**, with no **Agent:** prefix—and opens the saved source message. Existing session access and notification preferences still apply; mentioning someone never grants access or assigns human authorship.

The first version supports trusted in-process, current-session agent runs only. Raw prose remains inert. Older builds safely omit the new agent alerts and may discard them during maintenance; existing human mentions and SQLite/protocol versions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `sessions` tool gains bounded `mentionable` discovery and an explicit `mention` action. It commits a real assistant note, then reuses the current mention owner for Inbox entries, involvement, push notifications, retention, and replay protection. Results distinguish recording from skipped delivery and never claim that a person received or read a push.

No duplicate toast system, background people scanner, recurring reminder service, or live deployment is included. The companion mention-toast work can consume the same `mentions.changed` event and typed Inbox items.

**Product requirement confirmed September 21:** agent mentions must follow the same lifecycle and reliability rules as human mentions. No special rollback-loss exception is accepted. Older builds may hide the unsupported agent UI, but returning to a supporting build must preserve eligible retained alerts under the normal dismissal, expiry, access, and capacity rules, without replaying notifications. The preservation fix and current worker-thread integration are in progress; the published head is not merge-ready.

Separate pinned old-Inbox lifecycle proof also confirmed unrelated maintenance preserves untouched agent payloads.

title: fix: distinguish session group names from the create action
body:
Related: #142863

Rebased directly onto `main`. The former multi-module extraction is removed; this is now a focused category-control repair.

## What Problem This Solves

Selecting a group named `__new-group__` opened the New Group action instead of assigning the session to that existing group.

## User Impact

That group name now behaves normally. The New Group action, permission checks, drag-and-drop, labels and visual layout are preserved. No group-ownership, schema, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identify the action through explicit option metadata rather than a reserved category value. Use the selected option’s index, and replace two DOM assertions with actual element guards. Keep the existing view owner instead of introducing presentation/dialog wrappers.

The two existing category tests move out of an oversized test file so the new regression does not expand it; their prior permission and assignment assertions are retained. Existing shared fixtures are reused.

## Evidence

- Actual selection regression failed on main (one failure, two passing controls), then all three category cases passed. This covers the colliding name, ordinary assignment, the positive create action, drag/drop and denied writes.
- Measured per-file commands with `--maxWorkers=1`: category suite 3.61s wall; remaining view suite 51 passed in 2.55s wall. The new collision case took 13ms in the passing run.
- Canonical changed gates and UI test types passed, including lint/format, core-test/UI types, dead exports, line limits and the exact assertion-ratchet reduction from eight to six. Independent P0–P2 review: scoped-clean.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes New Session doing nothing while keyboard-shortcuts help is open, and the composer losing focus when reopening a warm New Session page.

Related: #153537.

## User Impact

Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O closes shortcut help and focuses a New Session draft. Cmd/Ctrl+/ closes help without navigation. Returning to an already loaded New Session page keeps typing in the composer. Existing drafts, permissions, approval dialogs, and archive safeguards are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Help owns its two permitted navigation chords and releases its modal before handing off to the existing session action. Drawer cleanup restores focus only when the drawer was actually open, rather than stealing focus during ordinary desktop navigation.

## Evidence

### Compiler-policy repair

Published branch commit **9e04a1306f8ed9839b27e307fd36f33b41c19758** carries the existing approved Node compiler flags through all six SQLite reliability subprocess launch paths. The CLI shim and proof workers share the same existing four-flag filter; loaders, evals, and debugger arguments remain excluded. The test entrypoint uses the canonical test Node invocation.

The existing full smoke proof checks actual main-thread descendants with a preload guard. With the selected parent policy but original launches, the writer fails the missing-policy guard. With the repair, **all 7 SQLite proof tests pass** (25.51 seconds wall; smoke 20.229 seconds), retaining every snapshot, crash, restore, publication, index-repair, compaction, and child-settlement assertion. **Four selected real shim cases pass** (1.81 seconds wall); script/root-test types, lint, formatting, and independent P0–P2 review pass. No deadline, payload, assertion, or database guard changed.

CI run 35580513015 reached its one-hour job limit: the first benchmark attempt timed out at 241 seconds, its CI-managed replay passed at 123 seconds, and other tooling tests plus a later no-output stall also consumed the budget. This repair proves a compiler-policy propagation defect; it does **not** claim sole attribution of that job timeout or treat the replay as a fix. The earlier auto-merge request was retired and its native cancellation confirmed before this replacement was published. Completed exact-head CI and review remain required for landing.


### Current CI integration

Integration **d0d778888be441544a44580afea1aa65ba9026e6** includes the canonical [database-fixture teardown repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/103115f2f0b11844d5cf5766424b6ab8e1e5cf01): await agent-database resource drainage before shared-state closure and temporary-directory deletion, while preserving validation resets and asserting settled custody. It directly matches the ENOENT database-drain failure in CI run 35577677441; that run’s UI lanes and staging repair were not the failing jobs.

After integration, **all 9 affected library tests and all 16 staging tests pass** (32.05 s and 40.46 s wall). The UI implementation, lazy facade, and acquisition tests remain byte-identical to the reviewed repair. The staging fixture also preserves main’s [Node compiler-policy forwarding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7205715961f0222bab7f77811d37d83b7bccada0). No database identity guard, deadline, assertion, or cleanup requirement was weakened. Fresh exact-head CI remains the landing gate.


### CI repair: keep protected local recovery lightweight

Repair commit **a72aa1b448cd008f8d71974c2e7b70f3e8feb7db** makes the existing Crabbox acquisition API lazy. Binary discovery remains synchronous; acquisition delegates to the unchanged managed-binary owner only when called. The static eager repository-module closure falls from **186 to 18** for the wrapper, and **171 to 2** for its public API facade.

The real protected-recovery CLI regression rejects command/PTY-runtime loading. It fails on the original eager boundary and passes on this repair. The full **16 staging tests and 36 binary/acquisition tests pass** (73.39 seconds wall); the affected staging case took 10.188 seconds. Production plugin types, root fixture types, formatting and both owning lint checks pass; independent P0–P2 review is clean. No command timeout, recovery assertion, process-tree cleanup, writer hold, or permission was relaxed.

The historical 30-second CI timeout remains unattributed; this repairs the concrete unnecessary startup dependency, rather than claiming a diagnosed Node shutdown/cache bug. Normal exact-head CI and review still gate landing. Keyboard/focus implementation and existing visual evidence are unchanged.


- Refreshed-head verification: **80 focused UI tests**, production UI types, and UI fixture types pass after integrating the landed runtime dependency. Fresh exact-head CI remains required. Prior browser/performance evidence below is retained with its original source bindings.

title: fix(skills): allow short commands for personal library skills
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes personal library skills requiring long generated slash commands even when their selected instructions have a simple name.

## User Impact

Selected skills can be invoked with short commands such as `/review #123`, including through autocomplete, `/skill review`, and inline `$review` references. Existing identity-based text commands still work. When names collide with another selected skill or an existing command, the picker retains the unique identity command rather than choosing a skill by discovery order.

The short name comes from the pinned `SKILL.md` name, not its mutable library slug or display title. Changing it for an existing session requires explicitly refreshing that skill selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original identity suffix protects skills belonging to different owners and remains unchanged. Command discovery now adds a friendly invocation only after reserving existing commands. Skill IDs, pinned revisions, sharing and authorization, prompt identities, and native command limits stay intact. Bundle commands cannot inherit a managed skill’s alias by copying its identity.

title: refactor: retain session ownership during post-commit work
body:
Related: #142863

## What Problem This Solves

Session writes currently release their physical writer before an awaited follow-up can finish, allowing later lifecycle work to overtake that follow-up. This is the storage foundation for the agent-owned group stack split from #142863.

## User Impact

No group behavior or database schema changes in this PR. Existing callers keep their current behavior. Later stack layers will use this bounded continuation to prevent delayed category registration from reviving deleted groups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an optional `afterCommitted` continuation to creation, lifecycle mutation, and canonical replacement. It runs after successful SQL commit/publication but before the existing physical writer is released. Its context retains the original revocable native owner and captured environment; close revokes authority and joins completion. Post-commit failure does not mean the durable write rolled back.

**Scope:** seven storage files only. No Gateway/UI/native-client activation, schema migration, or upgrade-driver changes. Most added lines are regression coverage.

Extracted from the work requested by @vyctorbrzezowski in #142863; the original contribution and PR remain preserved while the smaller stack is prepared.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/28feaf46-a23c-468e-bfad-ab44a1d5ac7b)

## Evidence

- 82 tests passed across the commit-continuation, lifecycle-publication, prepared-admission, handle-lifecycle, and incognito suites on fresh main.
- Core production and config/CLI test type graphs passed. Scoped lint reported zero warnings and errors; the source line-growth gate passed.
- Independent P2 review found an explicit-environment propagation gap. A regression failed with the wrong state root before the fix; replacement projections now pass the caller environment into the existing captured-scope owner and the full selected suite passes.

title: feat(ui): show session mention notifications
body:
Closes #153801

Stacked on backend prerequisite #155419 so this diff remains UI-only while both PRs stay unmerged. **No merge or auto-merge is requested.**

## What Problem This Solves

People working in another session can miss a new mention unless they open the Inbox.

## User Impact

New mentions show a compact card with a side avatar, sender and session, the highlighted selected username, immediate message context, and **View session**. Long messages use context around the mention—not the beginning of the message.

Each tab stays quiet for sessions already visible there, including desktop split panes. Hidden narrow-screen panes can notify; making the pane visible retires its active or queued card. Closing or timing out a card leaves the shared Inbox entry intact. Hover and keyboard focus pause the five-second timeout. The first accepted Inbox snapshot is the baseline: it never toasts; subsequent fresh IDs notify. Reconnect and temporary loss/restoration of session visibility do not replay retained mentions.

The Inbox and notifications share escaped, recipient-specific excerpts and explicit selected-name spans. The backend prerequisite supplies optional excerpt metadata in existing retained records; old records remain plain text. No new setting, dependency, permission, retention rule, or database table is introduced. [Accepted persistence design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153812#issuecomment-5766660909).

## Why This Change Was Made

Matches the approved side-avatar reference, with compact mobile actions and the selected username using the active theme’s accent rather than a fixed color. The existing mention capability owns arrivals and the shared toast owner owns timing, cancellation, and FIFO. Notification presentation loads lazily without activating unrelated Inbox health or model-auth work on Settings pages.

title: chore(deps): refresh dependencies with a seven-day cutoff
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshes workspace dependencies without adopting releases published within the last seven days.

## User Impact

Uses mature upstream maintenance releases across the runtime, plugins, and development tools. No configuration migration or public API change is intended. Incompatible upgrades and existing patch/override constraints remain pinned.

## Why This Change Was Made

Updates 13 dependency packages using **September 13, 2026 at 14:50 UTC** as the fixed publication cutoff. The existing strict seven-day cooldown, exceptions, patches, and overrides are unchanged. All 15 newer resolved versions, including two transitive updates, meet the exact cutoff.

The normal build also refreshes Workboard’s immutable asset-manifest paths because its browser bundle embeds the updated Zod runtime.

<details>
<summary>Updated packages and intentional holds</summary>

Updated: Zod 4.6.4, p-map 7.0.8, marked 18.0.13, pako 3.0.2, AWS Bedrock/Bedrock Runtime/S3/S3 presigner 3.1131.0, Twurple api-call/auth/chat 8.2.0, Lobster 2026.9.11, and Tokenjuice 0.8.4.

Retained:
- YAML 2.9.0 is held because the release producer verifies its exact version, integrity, and retained-tree digest, and the security-review action has the same frozen runtime. The first CI run exposed this integration constraint; the hold restores it without changing enforcement code.
- TypeScript 6.0.3 supplies the in-process compiler API; the native TypeScript 7 CLI remains separately installed.
- LanceDB requires Arrow <=18.1.0, Slack Socket Mode requires Undici 7, and Baileys requires audio-decode 2’s AudioBuffer contract.
- Slugify 3 changes published documentation anchors.
- A2UI 0.11 changes component DOM/style contracts; Mermaid 12 changes layout/look defaults; newer CUA releases require native artifact and adapter migration. These separate compatibility migrations are not included in this maintenance refresh.
- All patched dependencies and global/version-scoped overrides remain unchanged, including Codex ACP, Vertex SDK, mailparser, and zca-js constraints.
- Existing reviewed releases newer than the cutoff are retained, never downgraded. No new cooldown exemption is added.

</details>

## Evidence

- Final exact-head [CI run 35520400755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35520400755) passed: 170 successful jobs, 11 skipped, zero failures, including hosted Control UI performance.
- [Security and merge-gate reconciliation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35521175227) passed dependency review, security-sensitive review, and openclaw/ci-gate for f81040c12ca4ebbbec20fc58f085b3a2007b2a56.

- pnpm check — passed, including npm-lock validation, all typecheck lanes, lint, formatting, and repository guards. The first exact-head CI run found YAML integration failures; these were repaired by retaining YAML 2.9.0. Final exact-head CI is green.

On the committed repaired candidate, all 108 release-plan producer tests pass; three representative full-release publication-admission paths also pass. The release/security verifier sources and all integrity checks are unchanged. title: fix(plugins): avoid redundant parsing during packaged startup
body:
Related: #153399

## What Problem This Solves

Packaged Gateways parse plugin JavaScript for source-SDK rewrites even when no source-SDK target can resolve.

## User Impact

Removes unnecessary startup parsing without changing native loading, source fallback, or plugin behavior. No configuration, dependency, persisted-state, or public SDK change is required. This does not yet establish that the release CPU gate is satisfied.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing SDK owner can cheaply rule out source resolution from its current materialized alias map or generation-owned source-directory fact. The loader skips the source-only inspection only in that case. Positive cases retain the demand-driven validation order introduced by #150840; this does not eagerly scan unrelated aliases.

The unchanged workspace alias inventory moves to a sibling module to keep the existing line-growth limit intact. Its entries and selection policy are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Real native-module fixtures with prepared and explicit compiled aliases fail on original code: the source-reference visitor is called once despite a successful native load. Both pass after repair, returning the same exported value with no source parser call.
- Complete selected suites: **123 passed**, one existing Windows-only skip. Source fallbacks, private boundaries, alias generations, normalization and native loader siblings remain covered.
- Full runtime build and the memory-core entrypoint profile completed. Complete changed-file checks and diff checks passed; exact-head CI is required after publication.
- Independent full-source review found one missing export in the inventory extraction; the one-line correction was verified by the same reviewer. Final frozen five-file source is scoped-clean at P0–P2.
- Original CPU failure remains distinct: the correlated diagnostic locates avoidable parsing but is instrumented and is not release qualification. An uninstrumented changed-head comparison is still required.

Proof ran on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35509971059). title: fix(android): expose screenshot emulator startup failures

title: fix(codex): preserve long tool output after history reload
body:
Closes #153295

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long Codex-native tool responses lose their tail in saved history, so users cannot inspect or copy the complete available result after a reload.

## User Impact

Users can open the saved tool response as plain text, copy it, or download it without relying on the inline preview. Known capture loss in older records is explicitly marked unavailable. No migration, dependency change, or new RPC is required.

The exposed Codex response is **not a universal receipt of the final model input**: Codex can subsequently truncate or normalize its history copy. The UI labels that distinction. Existing redaction and inspection limits remain, including the Gateway’s existing 2,000,000-character-per-field inspection limit; capped retrieval is not presented as complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve response text at the Codex transcript producer rather than applying the preview cap before persistence. Keep bounded history previews, carry the original result message and tool-call IDs through UI grouping, and reuse `chat.message.get` for scoped inspection. Execution-only output remains distinct from provider responses, and unknown Code Mode response formats are retained without inventing patch success.

Current main’s canonical text-block tool-result shape is preserved. There is no parallel output store or guessed reimplementation of Codex’s model-context truncation.

title: fix(update): complete schema upgrades from 2026.9.2
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes schema handoff failures when updating an existing installation from published OpenClaw 2026.9.2.

## User Impact

The normal package updater can complete backed-up state migration and restart an authenticated Gateway while preserving transcripts and cron ownership. Missing-plugin migrations can remain pending until the plugin becomes available. Unverified database ownership or backup coverage still produces a concrete refusal and recovery instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old updater can still roll back its package while invoking the replacement Doctor. That early phase now validates private database copies. After package commit, the actual continuation enters the existing executor with the original run record and live parent authority. Managed 9.2 continuations borrow the unchanged shipped handoff row; later drivers keep their existing routes.

Before live migration, Doctor verifies canonical recovery coverage for every pending registered database. The schema owner rechecks authority and physical file identity at write and commit boundaries. Descendants and leases settle before the old parent sees success. Schema versions, stored formats, and public backup metadata are unchanged.

Package rollback cannot reverse migrated state. A post-core failure retains its recovery archive and directs the operator to finish repair with the compatible installed build; there is no automatic archive restore. The compatibility adapter can retire when 2026.9.2 is no longer a supported upgrade source.

## Evidence

- **Real published 9.2 update passed:** legacy operator state migrated before candidate probes, transcripts and cron owners survived, and update-owned authenticated restart replaced the running supervisor. Update/restart took 107 seconds.
- **Missing-plugin sibling passed in its documented manual-restart mode:** the Gateway served while migration was pending; Doctor completed migration after the plugin became available. This is not a claim of automatic restart for that sibling.
- **First and future second updates passed:** both ran in-process self-update with new service PIDs and zero updater residue. The fixture future package had no legacy compatibility chunks. Per-hop inputs, tarball hashes, build identities, and summaries were retained.
- These package cells used diagnostic source `0462333dc0171d4b081169ebaeb2dc798b24b1da` and canonical core tarball SHA-256 `cdbddec7e94e923913153a7c1416e91996601f0e16dbf61ced61124bd6645155`. [Isolated Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35497401452). All 73,114 archived evidence entries were hash-verified; archive SHA-256 `77344aa95d93dbb77a0315d11e49f9da17ea3fcf6648e19d302852583d5485a1`.
- Guard/backup tests cover revocation, cancellation, missing coverage, WAL state, and replaced database identities. The final continuation passed 45 native/caller cases, eight selected built-CLI cases, and complete changed checks. Its two defect-isolated controls failed before repair. Pnpm physical-root transitions have built-CLI/native proof, not a published pnpm package-manager campaign.
- Fixture process cleanup passed nine native cases, complete changed checks, and the pinned precise scanner. The materialization/downgrade follow-up reproduced both CI defects, then passed 35 tests with one existing Darwin-only skip. Its complete changed checks also passed; exact-head PR CI remains pending.
- The subsequent CI fixture repair reproduced all three completion-owner/config-write assertion failures on Node 24.19.0, then passed all 551 tests across the two complete affected files and the complete changed checks. Stable boolean fixture data and exact-once authority assertions are repaired; production bytes and the successful package proof are unchanged. All 23 evidence files were independently hash-verified.
- Captured-main integration against `03e1d2043091cc9c2d50fd122443c21823c5cc71` passed **613 integration tests**. A defect-isolated control reproduced quarantine recovery files being mislabeled as global-state ownership facts; the correction preserves archive restoration and reports only the actual global/agent ownership facts.
- The existing agent-lease write adapter was extracted with its transaction body and schema subset unchanged. All **73 affected-owner tests** and the complete changed-code checks passed afterward, without increasing line limits. The final 38 source-file hashes and seven evidence-file hashes match the sealed archive `7985b68aff84b2a5364a1379ff6f9fc9bcb87503d16a557639e5b40afe3a0772`. [Integration proof host](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35502997343) is stopped. Fresh PR CI and final candidate qualification remain required.
- A subsequent main advance to `2889a999b1eb12393cedb2813df1b8a3376dfd08` conflicted only on adjacent lease-writer/validation imports. Both are preserved; all 38 per-file added/removed edit sequences match the proved patch, and the 32 non-overlapping files remain byte-identical. New main service reconciliation and validation metadata are retained. Formatting and diff checks pass; fresh exact-head CI is required for these new main inputs.
- Independent native P0–P2 reviews are clean. The CLI reviewer was unavailable earlier in the campaign and is not counted as a passing review.
- [Validation-only npm producer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35496710414) passed package preparation, dependencies, SDK, and contents/lifecycle checks. **Overall qualification remains incomplete:** its source-check runner lost communication. That attempt and its exact prepared bytes are retained; no publication or gate waiver is implied. The final selected release candidate still needs fresh qualification.

<details>
<summary>Original failure evidence</summary>

The original release candidate refused the shipped 9.2 schema handoff and rolled back. An intermediate diagnostic package validated private state but then reached a plain post-core Doctor without delegated authority: the package had committed, the agent database stayed at schema 19, and the Gateway stayed stopped. The actual continuation repair above resolves that reproduced entry-point failure. Historical failed input/proof records remain retained separately from the successful cells.

</details>

title: fix: reduce Gateway memory when shared-state workers start
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes increased Gateway memory usage when shared-state commands initialize their worker runtime.

## User Impact

Shared-state workers no longer load unrelated host plugin/config discovery, reply threading, and every Gateway protocol validator. No configuration, schema, authorization, persistence, or public API changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pure payload helpers now live in the existing reply-payload owner. Audit and approval validation uses narrow modules that preserve the existing public exports and validator identities. All affected internal consumers use these owners; high-level reply consumers retain their facade. Sent-media normalization moves unchanged into the existing delivery-evidence owner to preserve the line-cap guard.

## Evidence

- Both worker import-boundary regressions failed before their respective repairs and pass afterward. Retained focused proof includes 158 initial tests, 77 extended boundary/payload tests, and 126 final command/reply tests; one pre-existing Windows-only case is skipped on Linux.
- Independent P0–P2 review is clean for the complete 18-file memory repair. Relocated functions preserve the original behavior, including speech-only payloads, sent-media deduplication, and validator identity.
- Current head `c6e250c4294ae90f6ffea6bca83c9a88d5811e39` preserves contributor ancestry and incorporates main through `47f1d6ad8eb67a0e22db2191f9da9a386eb08e5b`. The memory repair retains stable patch ID `f811b5e35beab7e6b0f8b8aeee139e13ee2fe272`: 17 files are byte-identical to the preceding integrated head; the validator registry additionally preserves main's progress refresh and compaction retirement. No repair behavior, assertions, budgets, or timeouts changed.
- The [current-head CI build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35557171757/job/106203102678) passed the canonical `build:ci-artifacts` profile: runtime/worker bundles, 13 postbuild phases, SDK declaration/export checks, UI/assets and all four CLI startup-memory cases. This is not an unrestricted full-profile declaration build or a full release performance pass.
- Direct current-head log inspection verifies all 12 completed-delivery cases, including speech-only and queued speech; 63 outbound-payload cases; and the worker import-boundary regression. The current Gateway handler suite also passes all 352 cases. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35557171757) completed successfully with no failing jobs; no historical head is substituted.

### Review follow-up: import-boundary test cost

The fresh exact-head ClawSweeper review has no correctness or security findings. Its timing-documentation follow-up is addressed with retained measurements, without repeating the performance lane:

- **Isolated file:** `src/state/openclaw-state.worker.imports.test.ts` ran alone in its unit invocation (one test file and one test worker): **2.94 seconds** Vitest wall time; **1.098 seconds** in the passing test. This is retained September 20 final-diff evidence, not a new timing run. The test bytes still match SHA-256 `21dd7ecc80287f98e7b3b65b201359584de840b2d897dcab60d3dd8a8574acb0`.
- **Current CI:** the same test passed in **649 ms** in [compact-large-15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35557171757/job/106203103968). Its containing unit-src shard took **90.22 seconds** for 108 passed and one skipped files; the packed test step took **6m 18s**, and the full job **7m 14s**. These shared-shard/job times are not standalone test-file costs.

### Memory measurements and retained release failures

The [frozen a61 three-repeat performance run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35488453352) passed all RSS gates: pressure Gateway-tree peaks were **1154.0 / 1174.5 / 1165.3 MB**, below the unchanged **1200 MB** ceiling, versus the original candidate's same-harness **1270.6 MB** median. Its full result remained **12 PASS / 1 FAIL / 2 BLOCKED** because of CPU gates. This measures import-cost reduction, not a heap-leak diagnosis; its candidate version metadata differs from this main-targeted repair.

The latest retained [integrated-head performance run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35513782413) used exact `174a1c3cfd42a947b79e8a4fe42a39a4dba58f26`, pinned Kova `c2de7c24`, Node 24.21.0, and the canonical five-entry mock-provider sweep with three samples each:

- **7 PASS / 4 FAIL / 4 BLOCKED**. The source/report evidence adapter passed; the performance gate failed.
- All configured RSS gates passed: maximum primary Gateway RSS **998.3 MB**, maximum Gateway-tree RSS **1165.3 MB**.
- Startup sample 2 failed CPU: **281.1–312.2%** against **250%**. The other two startup samples passed.
- All three agent cold/warm samples failed the existing 10-second status threshold: **61.415 / 61.570 / 61.455 seconds**.
- Four CPU-accounting cells remained inconclusive and blocked. They are not waived or reclassified.

Archive SHA-256 `8937558b4bf3371aeccdd72ee03870f71cadef1246efdf32ca5eb7e385ec8c7a` and all 46 evidence hashes were verified. The nested diagnostic bundle `351eda5be9316d8c70211f19c8aefb1057d157d459f7e8580d1420d96be9c6c2` retains all 282 members. Owned environments, services, runtime, and Testbox were cleaned up.

Earlier evidence also remains unresolved: the original **285.9%** CPU lower-bound failure and the exact `f0de08a4` startup result (**1 PASS / 1 FAIL / 1 BLOCKED**, failing lower bound **262.7%**, inconclusive interval **249.1–272.4%**). Narrow instrumented captures and isolated passing cells do not clear these failures.

### Independent failure owners

Current main includes the Gateway fixture repairs [child cleanup ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153785) and [task/Gateway settlement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153877). Their fixture-lifecycle producers explain the old pre-agent SQLite identity rejection; the latter landed with three complete **352-case** Gateway passes and green exact-head CI. The old diagnosis is historical evidence, not a remaining unclassified memory-patch failure. This PR still requires its own current-head CI.

CPU and status qualification remain with separate repair lanes:

- The compile-cache producer in `openclaw.mjs`, `src/entry.compile-cache.ts`, and `src/infra/node-compile-cache-env.ts` passed Node's versioned cache leaf as a worker cache base, nesting the versioned leaf again. A separate reviewed repair propagates the configured base; required gates and performance impact remain pending.
- `src/cli/daemon-cli/diagnostic-readiness.ts` and the daemon service-inspection owner waited the full readiness window even for authoritative no-service absence. The separate repair preserves the original status threshold and strict absence checks; final proof remains pending.

Neither diagnosis establishes that this memory repair caused the retained CPU/status failures, nor proves those release gates repaired. No broad unchanged-head performance rerun, threshold relaxation, release qualification, or publication is claimed here. Final release acceptance remains separate.

title: fix(tasks): prevent failures during concurrent task reads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent task lookups can fail prompt preparation even when no task records are changing.

## User Impact

Parallel agent turns can read task context without failing with “Task activity did not stabilize.” Real mutation invalidation and authority checks still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share one projection refresh/install for the same database identity, store, and epoch. Each caller still revalidates its authority after awaiting. The existing state owner retains snapshot publication, dirty obligations, accepted-event fences, FIFO, and write settlement; the three-attempt policy is unchanged.

The cohesive async preparation moved into a narrow sibling module to remain within the existing file-size limit.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the frozen release candidate: eight simultaneous owner reads yielded five failures; eight actual media-prompt preparations yielded seven failures and 69 redundant snapshot reads. Serial controls passed, and the held mutation made no writes during either wave.
- After: eight of eight actual prompt preparations succeeded with one snapshot read. Independently rerun by the release lead.
- Extended the existing fixed-prefix/held-terminal regression to one and eight readers; demonstrated failure before the repair.

title: fix(ui): chat image clicks look unresponsive while originals load
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat image clicks appearing unresponsive while an uncached full-resolution image downloads.

Reported and requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/3f7ff2b7-2eac-4c49-b059-e8b763369c53)

## User Impact

One click opens the existing preview immediately, with a loading indicator. The decoded original replaces it when ready. A failed download keeps the preview visible with an error, and closing the viewer discards late results without showing a stale error toast.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lightbox was already loaded: the opener waited for the entire original-image download before showing anything. Repeated clicks shared that request but gave no visible acknowledgement. The existing lightbox controller now owns the original load, decoding, cancellation, and resource release, alongside gallery navigation. The opener retains the preview until the viewer closes. External-window and non-managed image paths keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence
