title: feat(talk): preauthorize exact installed-app launches
body:
## Superseded by split draft PRs

This combined proposal is superseded by the following separately scoped **DRAFT** stack:

1. [#159693 — truthful source execution outcomes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159693), head 6ff285da40af30dad5135b0edc6928e5717a742c, targeting main.
2. [#159695 — constrained Linux app discovery and launch with ordinary confirmation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159695), head fc3c91ad930385e0bb182f2b78290421aaf67bd6, based on #159693's branch/head.
3. [#159697 — optional scoped repeat preauthorization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159697), head 728319629289470659e5a2fffdaf783ba4348068, based on #159695's branch/head.

All three replacements remain drafts. Supersession is not a merge-readiness, full-CI or deployment claim. The original branch openclaw/talk-scoped-preauthorization-153092 and head af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b are preserved.

The original proposal and historical evidence below remain as context; their earlier source/package/live results are not relabeled as proof of the split heads. Each replacement main body records its own executed behavior proof and limits.

---

Related: #153092

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated voice requests to open the same approved desktop app otherwise require another Talk confirmation every time. This change adds an operator-managed, expiring preauthorization for one exact installed-app target without granting general command execution.

It also repairs the failures found while exercising that path: ordinary continuation must not inherit another client's authority; native consultation must retain its admitted Gateway and operational tool-execution record; a spoken one-shot approval must not survive an overlapping policy-authorized launch and later authorize a replay after policy revocation; and Linux Desktop Entry labels and executable strings must be decoded correctly without admitting shell commands or arguments.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Talk confirmation owner reads `talk.realtime.appLaunchPolicies` from committed runtime configuration. Grants bind the agent, paired voice device, target node, installed app, revision and expiry. Each consultation carries its own fresh authenticated ingress authority; call records and persisted diagnostic data cannot restore a grant.

The Gateway rechecks policy, originating-device revocation and node authority after preparation, then issues a short-lived invocation-bound permit. The node independently revalidates execution permission and the current installed-app descriptor immediately before non-shell dispatch. Preparation remains non-consuming; the final app-effect boundary consumes a matching spoken grant even when a reusable policy independently permits the same action. Revocation prevents effects that have not crossed the authoritative dispatch boundary, not an already admitted launch.

The native-consultation repairs bind the existing admitted Gateway resolver and publish canonical operational start/terminal facts independently of optional diagnostics. They do not fabricate a downstream execution record or remove the missing-record guard. Cancellation is forwarded through the existing invocation path. Existing config, diagnostic and node helper owners were extracted coherently; no second execution mechanism was added.

This refresh is the existing reviewed commit `af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b`, tree `036639cb8a35a41999169700fb877021afb7f5d5`. The frozen review/comparison base is `aac3e8a6ed27301bd56cfe4e97dbf96d88bb53f7`. The earlier published candidate `2daadf0d944d0c48c0e5bae54c484621506eacc1` is an ancestor, not a substitute for this head's proof.

## User Impact

Operators can opt into narrowly scoped repeat app launches while ordinary Talk confirmations, pairing, installed-app sharing, explicit node-command allowlisting and independent execution policy remain in force. Absent or empty policy lists preserve ordinary behavior. A signed device identity used with a shared Gateway token is not equivalent to paired-device-token authentication.

**Still DRAFT: no readiness, merge or deployment claim. The UI performance gate requires explicit disposition.**

Boundaries and compatibility:

- Coverage remains top-level Linux XDG Desktop Entries resolving to a native ELF executable with zero arguments. Shell/script launchers, arguments, field codes, custom working directories and other platforms are outside this contract.
- `Name` and the first stage of `Exec` now use strict Desktop Entry string decoding. Valid paired escaping remains supported; malformed escaping is rejected before the existing quoted-executable parser.
- The existing bounded app-ID schema was not broadened. The installation/filesystem remains a trusted installed-software boundary, not a new isolation guarantee against hostile local writers.
- Ordinary continuation from a different or unknown origin still works, but cannot inherit the prior client's reusable grant. Realtime provider/mode normalization preserves policy lists; canonical schema validation rejects malformed policy values.
- No feature-specific SQL migration or new stored-record version was introduced by these follow-ups. Older strict schemas reject the new policy key even when it is `[]`: an authorized downgrade must revoke/apply, drain in-flight launches, and remove that key before using the older schema.

## Evidence

### Exact source, completed review and focused validation

The full requested branch/local review cycle completed; its final branch-wide **R12 review was scoped-clean, with no accepted findings remaining**. Earlier interrupted attempts were not counted as successful verdicts. This is the retained review outcome for the bounded implementation, not a new merge-readiness review or a claim of current full CI.

- **201/201 focused tests across 12 files** passed on recorded code/test tree `1c98f99628f399c249c4e0ebf6fae67d0519e58c`. Its difference from the final tree is only `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`.
- **37/37 additional ingress/revocation/continuation tests across four files** passed on final tree `036639cb8a35a41999169700fb877021afb7f5d5`: **238 focused tests across 16 files** with the stated input provenance.
- Coverage includes six registered app-launch cases, 15 native Codex integration modes, 29 Linux parser cases, both node launch suites, confirmation/store/cancellation lifetimes, and runtime/manifest behavior. The grant/policy overlap regression failed before the repair with two launches where one was expected, then passed with final-boundary consumption and non-consuming preparation. Malformed Exec escaping likewise had a recorded failing-before/passing-after regression.
- All **12 selected validation steps** passed: 11 static steps plus the behavior-suite step. These covered line/max/assertion ratchets, the core import graph, three hard-zero Knip scans, scoped core/Gateway/Talk-node/root-test TypeScript, and whole-change core/root-test lint. Docs formatting and diff checks passed.
- This does **not** claim full repository CI, every type shard, a fresh installed-plugin/provider matrix, or an automatic waiver of the performance result below. Newly triggered CI must be judged on its actual head and result.

Relevant public scenario sources: [registered app-launch boundaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b/src/gateway/talk/app-launch.registered.test.ts), [native consultation integration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b/test/plugins/talk-app-launch.codex-native.gateway.test.ts), [authenticated runtime scenario](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b/test/talk-app-launch.authenticated.e2e.test.ts), and [Linux parser regressions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b/src/infra/installed-apps-linux.test.ts).

### Real Behavior Proof — executed, with separate evidence scopes

The following are sanitized technical records, not raw private logs or transcripts.

**P1 — isolated authenticated runtime / visible native effect**

- **Claim / surface:** the installed-app path can cross the real Gateway → node → OS boundary and produce a visible native application effect.
- **Scenario / environment:** the authenticated scenario linked above used the `af640b6` source Gateway, a freshly built node process, and a native ELF GUI fixture under Xvfb on isolated Linux x64. Only inference was a deterministic loopback fixture.
- **Observed result / reference:** the selected real-runtime test passed; the retained result records one passing scenario and an observed native window. This is the same-source runtime record, separate from the later delivered archive identified in P2.
- **Limits:** not actual user speech, not a live provider call, and not an installed-tarball upgrade matrix. A fixture window is not the operator's desktop.

**P2 — complete candidate npm archive / integrity and delivery**

- **Claim / surface:** the complete package was built from the intended immutable source and survived transfer without changing bytes.
- **Scenario / environment:** one canonical package build on isolated Linux x64 using Node **24.18.1**, pnpm **12.4.0** and npm **11.16.0** after frozen dependency installation. Actual Git HEAD/tree/index were checked before and after packaging.
- **Observed result / artifact reference:** canonical helper exit **0**; tarball inventory/import-graph checks passed; embedded identity and gzip integrity matched; complete transfer/download copies matched the archive's size and SHA-256. The operator independently confirmed the same identity and 12,395 safe tar members with the required CLI and Gateway-SDK entries.
- **Artifact identity:** `openclaw-pr153299-af640b6-private.tgz`; **77,805,135 bytes**; SHA-256 **6a2740bdd9cf080c426d797c56f790589b9fa31d9bf81f980d8a08a93b2af639**; build **2026.9.5-af640b6de9de-2026-09-22T11-18-39.000Z**; commit/tree as stated above. No public artifact URL is supplied here.
- **Limits:** the enclosing execution reported exit **1**, not an all-green run; see P4. No new installed-plugin acceptance/upgrade matrix is claimed for these bytes. Source-equivalent P1 and historical package CI are not relabeled as that matrix.

**P3 — bounded human-operated live smoke on the delivered build, 2026-09-23**

- **Claim / surface:** an actual voice confirmation can launch the installed Linux calculator, and an operator-observed negative confirmation can leave it closed.
- **Scenario / environment:** the isolated Gateway, Linux node, CLI and external client's Gateway SDK were selected from the P2 candidate. The actual client connection reported the matching build and device-token authentication. The node command surface remained `device.apps` and `device.apps.launch`; no app-launch policy was added for this smoke.
- **Observed result / reference:** operator attestation for this dated scenario reports a confirmation request, affirmative response followed by visible app launch, and both conversation bubbles. In the separate negative case, cancellation was acknowledged and the operator explicitly confirmed the app remained closed. The reported final client state was connected and idle, with `active=false` and `requested=false`.
- **Limits:** this is operator-observed no launch, **not an independently captured no-dispatch/no-spawn trace**. It does not claim a complete refreshed replay/expiry/wrong-target matrix or full call trace. In particular, no-policy yes/no interaction is not a fresh live test of overlapping spoken/reusable grants and replay after revocation; the scoped automated regression covers that invariant. External-client presentation work did not change OpenClaw core bytes.

**P4 — helper-0 / enclosing-1 diagnosis, 2026-09-23**

- **Claim / surface:** successful payload completion can be followed by a nonzero runner exit at noninteractive login-shell logout.
- **Scenario / environment:** one corrected harmless native Crabbox 0.63.0 SSH/`--shell` probe preserved the original `set -eu` login-shell conditions with no TTY. The prior `set -u` control was retained, not rerun. The corrected probe did not require an OpenClaw build.
- **Observed result / sanitized trace reference:** payload statuses **0 / 0 / 0**, then requested `exit 0`; `.bash_logout:6` invoked `/usr/bin/clear_console -q`; that cosmetic command returned **1**; active errexit propagated **raw SSH exit 1 → Crabbox exit 1**. An ERR observer only printed the existing status; it changed no shell options and installed no EXIT trap. No logout file was changed or skipped.
- **Disposition / limits:** the failure mechanism is runner-image logout after a successful payload, not evidence that the canonical package helper failed. It explains the retained helper-0/enclosing-1 split under matching strict conditions, but **does not retroactively instrument or relabel the historical failed run**. The earlier native control also omitted the unavailable repository JS launcher and the original errexit option, so it was not full invocation-equivalence proof. The proposed TTY-only, best-effort cosmetic logout cleanup has not been applied by this PR.

### UI performance gate — measured and explained, NOT passed

One baseline-only UI build used the immutable reviewed base **aac3e8a6ed27301bd56cfe4e97dbf96d88bb53f7**, tree **edbb5e6e96d3f016cc4c7b178b5c32d6e544b44d**, with matching external tools: Node 24.18.1, pnpm 12.4.0, npm 11.16.0, Vite 8.3.0 and Pako 3.0.1. Frozen dependencies and generation inputs were checked. Candidate UI build identity was an explicitly logged **measurement-only seed** to hold metadata constant; actual baseline Git provenance remained the base, not the candidate. The standard helper that rebuilds both sides was not run; retained candidate sidecars were reused.

| Seven startup JS assets | Shipped gzip bytes | Over unchanged 364,774 B limit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Frozen reviewed baseline, matched measurement inputs | **364,777** | **3 B** |
| Retained `af640b6` candidate | **364,815** | **41 B** |

The limit is **364,198 B recorded baseline + 512 B growth allowance + 64 B build-variance allowance = 364,774 B**. The measured pair difference is **+38 B**; both raw startup totals are **1,183,608 B**.

The bounded offline artifact comparison found all seven startup payloads identical after accounting for verified generated asset-name hashes; one was already byte-identical. Gzip headers matched. Per-pair gzip deltas were **+15, +20, +1, +1, 0, +1, 0 B**. Referenced targets were followed rather than blindly normalized: there were no conflicting target mappings or missing executable targets, and one deferred target had a genuine **40-byte raw reduction**. That target difference was retained, not treated as equivalent; source-map payload equivalence is not claimed.

Thus the observed +38 B startup gzip difference is compression of changed generated filename strings, **not added authored startup payload in this artifact pair**. This is one controlled pair, not a repeatability study or a license to change application behavior to chase a different hash. The served-byte measurements and failing gate remain real. Packaging intentionally runs the performance checker in report-only mode, which explains why a printed violation can coexist with a successful package helper.

**The UI gate still needs explicit disposition. Neither name normalization nor the baseline's 3 B excess is a passing score or automatic waiver. No source, lockfile, budget threshold or baseline was changed for this investigation. Readiness is not claimed.**

### Historical evidence retained separately

- **`2daadf0`:** repaired missing native tool-execution recording by publishing canonical operational facts independently of optional diagnostics; preserved the guard, approval and permit boundaries. Its focused native integration, earlier review and operator live acceptance remain earlier-source evidence, not `af640b6` coverage. [Selected Package Acceptance run 35645485296](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35645485296) passed its 11 executed jobs, including package integrity, npm 12 install.sh acceptance and selected Gateway/config/onboarding lanes. Fifteen unselected jobs were skipped. Its package SHA-256 was `70dfd6c4123d89d910a9586be0aea887411a2122f670704e8399e9f1dc7408b4`, build `2026.9.5-2daadf0d944d-2026-09-21T19-35-15.413Z`. Those are not the P2 archive or a full current-head CI result.
- **`96c28a9` and earlier recorded trees:** retained admitted-Gateway binding, continuation/lifetime, config-normalization and authority-chain evidence remains historical. The controlled authenticated chain covered shared-token/wrong-device denial, intended-device launch/repeat, policy revocation and originating-device-token revocation. Earlier routing/effect-record failures and their repairs are not erased by the new bounded smoke. [Earlier selected package acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35627427760) is likewise not current-head proof.

The native integration's dependency boundary was personally checked at upstream Codex **8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4**: [dynamic call identity emission](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1085-L1114), [response routing](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs#L18-L52), and [dynamic-tool protocol fields](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs#L1652-L1668). Codex transports call identity/arguments and responses; OpenClaw owns the operational mutation classification and retained Gateway authority.

title: fix(agents): stop replaying consumed child results after yield

title: feat(ui): identify cloud providers in session pickers

Cloud environment profiles currently share a generic cloud icon, making configured backends hard to recognize, especially after a profile is renamed.

title: fix(ui): prevent chat crashes after copying a message
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Chromium can crash the chat renderer when a user copies a message and then right-clicks that message. This also blocks the toolbar fix in #153241.

**Landing status:** While this revision was in CI, #153260 merged at 00:54:21 UTC on September 20, 2026 (`03328bcdb525d61eca0f3a32e61c0a343a57964b`). That change removes the same focus-driven row-containment switch and moves tool-summary focus rings inside their controls. This PR now conflicts with that landed repair. Preparation and merge are paused rather than reintroducing the removed containment rule.

## User Impact

Copy and message context menus work together without crashing. Keyboard focus rings remain visible, and unrelated offscreen rows keep their layout-skipping optimization. No settings, dependency, or test-expectation changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The focus-ring repair in #149002 switches a virtual row from visible content back to automatic containment when mouse focus leaves its Copy button. Keeping the row visible while its message bubble is hovered avoids changing containment during the same native mouse operation, while preserving the original focus-ring repair. Metadata-only hover retains automatic containment and the existing top-layer tooltip path; the separate focus selector also remains active on touch devices.

## Evidence

The unchanged tooltip test now passes, together with all 25 E2E cases across message actions, content copy, focused-row retention, collapsed replies, and history prepend, plus all seven end-follow browser cases. title: improve(ui): show CI in native PR readers and keep login links ordinary
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native PR reader makes status and CI hard to scan, and GitHub login/general-page links can incorrectly receive a generic hover preview.

## User Impact

PRs gain a clearer header, change counts, branch information, section shortcuts, and expandable checks for the exact head commit. Failed, pending, passed, skipped, empty, and unavailable results stay distinct. Login/OAuth, profile, repository, and general GitHub links remain clickable ordinary links and are not fetched for previews. Genuine issue/PR anchors and supported subviews keep working.

The reader remains public-only and read-only. CI uses two bounded anonymous requests per uncached PR snapshot; unavailable or partial results never imply success. Refresh fetches the current head again. This does not determine merge readiness.

## Why This Change Was Made

GitHub owns CI reads and interpretation; the existing passive document model owns presentation. The shared preview-eligibility gate now reuses the canonical GitHub resource parser for hover, keyboard focus, and prefetch, rather than allowing the generic page fallback to preview authentication URLs. The implementation preserves the recently landed compact previews, author links, and co-author metadata.

Requested by @steipete; the login-link regression was reported by Vyctor.

## Evidence

- Login/eligibility regressions failed before the repair; 392 targeted parser, Markdown, hover, focus, and prefetch cases passed afterward.
- Reconciled onto main commit `8e7443e653ff6366969f0941b446d426c5e60b3a`. The final 12 focused UI/GitHub suites cover 580 cases; the retained detail suite was rerun successfully after updating its precise branch-metadata expectation.
- Fresh independent review through P2 is scoped-clean after reconciliation. UI/plugin typechecks and `pnpm ui:build` pass. Scoped lint, style, formatting, and diff checks were run; the full repository gate was not run end-to-end.
- Real Chromium source-UI proof with a deterministic mock Gateway: the login link produces zero cards and zero preview requests, keeps its original href, and genuine PR/issue links still preview. Before/after captures use synthetic URLs and contain no real authorization data.
- CI coverage includes exact-head binding, duplicate job names across independent workflows, partial/unavailable pages, empty results, refresh/head changes, bounded results, and credential omission.
- Three built-UI Chromium flows passed on Blacksmith Testbox before main reconciliation; source-UI captures and the UI build were repeated for the reconciled candidate.

The initial hosted run exposed a startup-JavaScript budget overrun. With one local toolchain, the exact CI base measured 363,680 B and the original merge candidate 364,085 B. title: fix(ui): restore JSON tree and raw views in chat
body:
Related: #125243, #125227

## What Problem This Solves

Restores the requested JSON Tree/Raw experience and fixes bare JSON assistant replies bypassing the shared code-block presentation.

## User Impact

Completed JSON objects and arrays now offer expandable **Tree** and literal **Raw** views in the same quiet code-block shell, whether supplied as a whole reply or inside a fence. Copy preserves original values, duplicate keys, key order, escapes, and numeric spelling. Raw retains existing preview, reveal, and wrapping controls. User-message JSON uses the normal message-level Show more/Show less disclosure when long. User-message fences and passive New Session previews remain plain code; unfinished or oversized content remains readable without expensive tree construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Tree/Raw prototype in #125249 was removed before merge (`959e3eedd8d0`); the separate whole-message JSON chip also survived the fence redesign. This restores the explicitly requested capability at the shared renderer rather than reverting subsequent source-fidelity, clipboard, streaming, or accessibility repairs. The old chip renderer and its CSS are removed.

The tree uses the pinned, already repository-used `jsonc-parser@3.3.1` source-offset AST, not reserialized JavaScript values. JSON size/depth/token budgets bound tree work; the existing literal-text renderer still owns larger-message limits. Code-block labels follow the existing lazy English catalog contract rather than increasing startup work. No configuration, persistence, or protocol change.

Original design and restoration requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Evidence

The resource owner now cancels that stale timer. Both render/click regressions fail before and pass after; 54 related unit tests and all seven unchanged auth-recovery/JSON Chromium scenarios pass on tree `d57342c4340888187cc57afb36746f2acfb5eca7`. All 226 related tests, Gateway-server types, typed lint, line-count ratchets, and incremental P0–P2 review pass. Production scheduler behavior is unchanged; the historical CI log did not record the third call’s reason.

title: improve(ui): place adjacent images side by side when they fit
body:
Closes #153222

## What Problem This Solves

Adjacent assistant images stack vertically even when their normal previews could fit beside each other.

## User Impact

Images within one reply now sit side by side when there is room and wrap onto the next line when there is not. Their existing preview sizes, aspect ratios, image actions, and lightbox behavior are retained. Captions and other content separate image sets; separately delivered messages remain separate. User-upload grids are unchanged.

There is no carousel, horizontal scroller, gallery fade, extra navigation, forced thumbnail sizing, or cross-message merging. Nothing is deployed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adjacent images are grouped by the existing ordered-media renderer and wrapped with CSS. One bounded image anchor remains under the existing transcript virtualizer; it respects reader input, explicit scroll commands, and clipped forwarded content. Omitted and expired-image notices keep their position between image sets.

The branch incorporates main at `ee5a62621763934696491dfe00832c4ab0b656c6`, preserving its incremental Markdown rendering and reader controls. Geometry reads are batched, precise observer measurements are retained across CSSOM rounding, and backward maintenance is distinguished from reader movement. Profiling also found empty-composer sizing repeatedly forcing whole-conversation layouts; empty one-row editors now use native/CSS height while populated drafts retain measured sizing and clearing a tall draft preserves the reading position.

## Evidence

**Merge hold:** the requested no-performance-regression condition is not met. The mixed text/image workload still uses more CPU. This PR remains a draft; it has not been merged, submitted for auto-merge, or deployed.

- 541 transcript/image checks passed across 25 files (39.73s), covering resize, virtual remounts, native-input takeover, streaming growth, disclosure clipping, scroll ownership, image loading, and boundaries.
- The final composer repair passed 428 chat-view/composer/new-session checks across three files (5.87s). The new four-case composer regression file passed in 0.637s wall with one worker; its empty-editor cases failed before the repair.
- Final production-bundle full-app proof with a mocked Gateway passed at 320/390/768/1440px with normal and reduced motion. The reading point stayed within 0.2px of its original 80px offset. Drafts, reconnects, virtual remounts, bottom-follow, clearing a tall draft both while reading and at the end, and delayed unknown-dimension images all passed; no page errors occurred.
- Independent code review is clean through P2. UI types, targeted lint, line-cap checks, and PR-diff whitespace checks pass. Shipped-bundle budgets pass without changing any baseline or budget: startup JavaScript 364,987 B gzip / 365,837 B and seven requests; startup CSS 51,151 B / 51,200 B, unchanged against the matched base. CSS has only 49 B of remaining headroom.

### Performance results — remaining acceptance decision

Five alternating-order production-bundle comparisons per workload used Chromium’s explicit thread-CPU clock. Each sequence includes six viewport changes, four history positions, and 30 streamed updates. These are bounded measurements on a shared host, not a guarantee for every workload.

| Workload | Median thread CPU vs base | Median elapsed time | Post-GC heap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text history | −5.9% | +0.5% | +0.02% |
| Mixed text/image history | **+15.5%** | **+5.0%** | −0.19% |
| One 50-image message | −19.2% | −4.0% | −0.27% |

For mixed history, CPU increased from 917 ms to 1,059 ms over the complete stress sequence, and elapsed time from 3,000 ms to 3,150 ms. Mounted rows remained 17; peak transcript DOM fell from 397 to 377 elements. Profiling showed additional style/layout work and different native offscreen-rendering eligibility with denser image rows. The image-anchor scan itself was negligible. The empty-composer repair removes proven redundant layouts, but it does not eliminate the overall mixed-history increase. No acceptance waiver is assumed.

Hosted exact-head CI and native landing remain pending. The standard local Vitest E2E launcher is blocked before tests by the host’s loopback proxy preflight; the production-bundle proof above uses the supported mock-Gateway helper. Hosted timings will be recorded when available.

Native header clearance also accounts for the unread badge’s one-pixel overhang. Browser floating controls keep their existing contrast.

## Why This Change Was Made

The floating Inbox inherited browser overlay decoration after moving into the native titlebar. Limit that decoration to non-titlebar hosts and use the existing native-web-chrome styling boundary. No native Swift, configuration, or migration changes.

## Evidence

Stopping the environment marks its hosting workflow cancelled; that workflow conclusion is not a test-suite result.

These are Chromium renders of the Mac native-web-chrome flow, not native macOS/WebKit runtime captures. Native runtime certification remains untested. This bounded CSS-only repair reuses the existing native-host selector and standard border/background properties; no native integration or interaction behavior changes. All 31 focused native-titlebar, responsive setup, and rail E2E cases passed on exact tree `1de09ee162523d2c7ab91679651725443afedef2` in [CI-matched Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35485791888); the task-owned Testbox completed. ## What Problem This Solves

The Cmd/Ctrl+K new-session composer cannot include a pasted screenshot when starting a task.

## User Impact

Paste images into the palette and start a background session with Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, with or without text. Images use the main composer's small removable thumbnails below the fixed input and actions—no upload button, filenames, attachment counter, or extra helper text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing attachment reader, thumbnail renderer, and session-creation flow. Keep the foreground conversation and draft untouched, retain images when creation fails, and discard unsent images on ordinary dismissal. A cold-loading palette retains pasted files and hands them over once; thumbnails appear when the full palette has loaded. The rebase preserves main’s compact mode for long prompts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the identity-only renderer and expose the sidebar's existing loaded data through a read-only, application-scoped subscription. Both surfaces share rendering and focus repair; opening a chat card does not fetch another session list. Missing presence observations remain unknown rather than implying Offline.

Merge-context prerequisite: main’s focus-time virtual-row containment override reproduced a Chromium crash after Copy → context menu. ## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify and project image attachments once, before rendering, so each visible tile belongs to its message gallery. Remove the late per-attachment image conversion, preserve explicit duplicate uploads, and avoid adding persisted mirrors as phantom neighbors.

Reported and requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

title: fix(ui): preview HTML attachments larger than 256 KiB
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes HTML attachments showing “Could not preview this file” in the Files side panel when they exceed the generic 256 KiB text-preview limit.

## User Impact

Self-contained HTML attachments up to **2 MiB of UTF-8 data** now render in the existing sandbox, with Source and Download preserved. Generic text, pasted excerpts, comments, and workspace file reads/edits retain their 256 KiB limits. There are no new settings or expanded sandbox permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attachment loader and HTML-preview RPC enforced the same text-sized limit independently. They now share the existing HTML protocol budget, while the reader keeps a separate generic-text policy. Retained attachments revalidate their content if their HTML/plain-text classification changes. Relative asset directories and external-resource access are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the fix: three Gateway boundary cases and four attachment cases failed; a 1.7 MB synthetic HTML attachment reproduced the visible error in Chromium.
- After the fix: **40 Gateway tests + 58 UI tests pass**, including exact/over-limit ASCII and multibyte data, missing/underreported lengths, cancellation, forced plain text, and classification changes.
- **Three Chromium E2E checks pass** on Blacksmith Testbox: large HTML in scripts/strict modes, Source and tab retention, and unchanged descendant-frame restrictions under production CSP. Browser proof uses the real UI and isolated sandbox with a mocked Gateway; real-handler tests cover RPC enforcement.
- **AutoReview: scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings at the default blocking threshold.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passes, including core/core-test/UI typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, i18n, import cycles, and repository guards. Protocol generation also passes. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35472069224) passed for `b4c81737c0efae1d39cf53e83a7deb56d81a0f33` (attempt 1; completed September 19, 2026 at 22:34 UTC); required CI and security status checks are green.

title: fix(ui): restore compact PR previews and co-author avatars
body:
Related: #148464

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes GitHub pull-request hovercards losing co-author avatars and overflowing their footer after the shared reader migration.

## User Impact

Pull-request previews again show the primary author, overlapping co-author portraits with a +N remainder, and green/red change counts in a compact, responsive footer. Long names stay readable, missing portraits do not lose author credit, and the full reader keeps its detailed statistics. No configuration or migration is required.

Compatibility: this intentionally restores compact GitHub preview metadata (`+N` / `−N`) rather than retaining the temporary full-statistics/textual-co-author presentation. Consumers needing complete statistics should use `github.detail`; co-author identities now have optional structured fields. The shipped `controlUi.githubPreview` numeric and co-author payload is unchanged, and existing metadata-only plugin payloads remain renderable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve structured author information through the passive plugin contract instead of flattening it into text chips. Keep preview statistics compact while leaving issue comments, commit documents, ordinary-link previews, and GitHub attachment handling intact. Profile links are restricted to the source origin and images retain anonymous loading.

## Evidence

- [Inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153193#issuecomment-5745582117) are embedded in the linked comment. Both images were verified loaded and visibly rendered on GitHub, and delivered in the originating discussion.
- After integrating main’s actionable-error fix (#153181), all 21 browser cases passed again across light/dark, desktop, and narrow layouts, including error/backoff navigation. The refreshed after screenshot is byte-identical to the published image.
- 195 focused UI/seed/page-preview/reader tests and 93 GitHub RPC/detail tests passed on the combined source.

title: feat(codex): route backend-authorized turns to Luna Reserve
body:
Related: #152338

Builds on disclosure already landed in #152383.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw does not transition an eligible pending Codex turn to Luna Reserve when the backend authorizes that separate route.

## User Impact

**Draft — do not merge until genuine-account routing validation succeeds.** This adds account-authorized Reserve entry and ordinary recovery for persistent OpenClaw-owned ChatGPT conversations while preserving explicit model and Fast preferences. API-key, native/adopted, and incognito ownership boundaries remain unchanged. Recovery can use available credits under provider spending controls; it is not a promise of free included usage.

The existing conservative contract is retained: only typed pre-enqueue usage overload can continue the selected ordinary model before any saved Reserve state or known offer. Authentication, timeout, transport and ambiguous quota failures hold input. Saved Reserve intent prevents silent ordinary replacement of an unavailable native thread; reconnecting the original account or explicitly starting a new conversation remains available. No opt-in redesign, public setting, Reserve-specific SQL migration, or independent dependency bump was added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native `turn/start` admits complete settings and pending input together. The plugin saves return intent before dispatch, validates live account/run/thread/binding authority through transport retries, and publishes accepted state only after guarded native acceptance. It never relies on a change-only settings notification or quota percentages as permission.

The current-main refresh resolves the three merge conflicts while preserving main’s home-scope isolation, exact tuple/model-policy checks, native-process ownership and provider-review continuation. Actual caller regressions exposed and repaired three integration problems: acceptance mutating an immutable model tuple, ordinary-model attribution after Reserve acceptance, and an unconfirmed active native turn receiving transition input as a steer. That last case now keeps pending ChatGPT input unsent. Small metadata/path helper extractions preserve their existing ownership and lifetime.

## Evidence

Current head **`bf0232649376aa7ab419d95083d8f763b22ab185`**, tree **`53b51c2ab539ae55133db65293a6cde6d869c8c7`**, integrates main **`229ab8a1fe957d3d4822309a39ddf9c7ec616395`**. The final merge preserves main’s native shell-environment forwarding and combines both test-routing additions. | Additional local tests | **293 passed on the reviewed integration tree** across registered upgrade, provider-review, runtime, lifecycle and metadata coverage; canonical Reserve fork case passed separately. Counts overlap remote reruns and are not summed. |
| Integration static checks | Extension production/test and root-test types, scoped lint, formatting, line/assertion/conflict/import guards passed; 14,594 docs links checked with zero broken. |

## What Problem This Solves

The collapsed browser sidebar spreads its shortcuts across the session header. This draft moves them into a narrow left rail and corrects the integrated history rail's two-sided hover and expensive layout invalidation.

Related: #153095.

## User Impact

The history ticks now expand **only to the right**, with a fixed left edge. Search, New session, Home, and Inbox remain at bottom left; the expand control stays at the top. The rail reserves 52px rather than covering the composer or docked panels. Expanded navigation, narrow-screen drawers, and native desktop titlebars retain their existing layouts.

**Draft — not ready to land.** Dense composer resizing remains expensive; WebKit rail interaction and genuine macOS/AppKit proof are incomplete. Nothing has been merged or deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single history-rail presentation now renders outside the transcript's size-query containers, while the existing transcript still owns scrolling, message navigation, and reader position. A local anchor supplies visibility, geometry, and keyboard order. Real pointer/focus entry delegates to the existing pane interaction owner, including inactive split panes. There is no hover-time reparenting, duplicate rail, synthetic activation event, or global active-session workaround.

Hover updates only the nearby marker wave. The plugin-content spacing selector preserves its matching behavior without broad sibling invalidation. A controlled same-bundle test showed these local optimizations alone were insufficient inside the transcript; the rendering boundary materially reduced style/layout work.

No new settings, persistence, Gateway behavior, or native rail redesign.

The prepared base was `7c665276`; all 15 changed source files and the downloaded UI bundle were hash-verified against reviewed candidate `ad51b345`. These are remote command results, not a claim that full PR CI is green.

Matching 1440×960 dark-browser captures, synthetic conversation data. Before: left edge moves from x22 to x10 as width grows 8→32px. After: x16 stays fixed as width grows 8→32px.

22-second actual browser walkthrough: repeated sidebar open/close, right-only hover, independent rail scrolling and message jumps, composer growth, Search, and Inbox. Synthetic data; normal UI motion; initial loading accelerated. Not native macOS footage.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9930b7c4-7cbb-409e-bb56-d34dd5ec45d8

With 2,000 loaded markers, a matched 60-hover same-bundle probe measured style/layout work of **383/216ms outside** the query-container chain versus **2,719/5,239ms inside**, with identical geometry and hit-tested pointer targets. **Not all dense operations are smooth:** 30 sidebar cycles reached frame p95 about 100ms; 20 composer resizes reached about 733ms. The earlier benchmark's zero frame-time values were invalid and are not used. Historical results from different leases/fixtures are not presented as a controlled A/B.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening a sidebar session in a new browser tab would find the navigation sidebar collapsed, even when it was expanded in their original tab. Reopening navigation for each conversation interrupts the multi-tab workflow.

New session tabs now use the same expanded desktop navigation default as direct links and reloads. Remove the special collapse marker from ordinary and catalog session links, its bootstrap handling, and the unused initial-collapse argument rather than adding another preference or override.

Visibility remains local to each tab; widths remain remembered. This does not force unrelated Home, Terminal, Browser, or session side panels open, and does not change the narrow-screen drawer or native tab gestures.

## User Impact

Middle-clicking or Cmd/Ctrl-clicking a session opens its conversation with navigation visible. People who prefer a collapsed sidebar can still use its toggle or Cmd/Ctrl+B without changing any other tab. The original tab keeps its URL and unsent draft.

title: fix(ui): hide Cmd+K search while composing session prompts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Cmd/Ctrl+K keeps showing search tabs, results, and hints—and keeps sending search requests—when the user is writing a new-session prompt.

## User Impact

Clear prompts get a quiet, compact input without moving the palette. Clearing or shortening the prompt restores search. New-session settings, submission errors, and recovery remain available; Enter does not silently become Send.

## Why This Change Was Made

Multiline text or at least 60 Unicode code points after trimming switches to prompt mode. Single-line input restores search at 50 code points or fewer; between 51 and 59, the current mode is retained to avoid flicker while editing. The palette cancels pending searches and retires late search/catalog results, including across refreshes and reconnects. This is a conservative input-shape rule, not language-specific intent guessing.

The search section fades and collapses over the existing 180 ms motion token. Its outgoing content stays stable for the animation but immediately becomes inert and hidden from assistive technology. The existing top/width anchor and reduced-motion preference are preserved.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

## Evidence

title: fix(ui): keep Cmd+K prompts from jumping to the bottom
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Cmd/Ctrl+K mini composer jumps back to the bottom when users scroll up to reread a long prompt and background results or layout update.

## User Impact

User impact: users can reread the beginning or middle of a task without losing their place. Continuing to type still keeps the end caret visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: shared Control UI conversations jump or briefly lose the active reply when another participant types or sends during a response.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski. AI-assisted implementation.

## User Impact

title: fix(android): bind Talk to its starting conversation
body:
Related: #151079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Android Talk starting for a later chat after delayed permission, canceling its first valid microphone grant, or losing a reply when native Talk and the Gateway use different names for the same conversation.

## User Impact

A Talk gesture keeps its selected conversation and physical operator connection. Stale A → B → A permission results remain cancelled; granting microphone permission for the current conversation no longer replaces that operator connection. Native requests, completion events, and reply-history reads now use one Gateway-confirmed conversation address. Existing global End Talk, generic Talk/PTT, and independent PTT destinations remain intact.

**Write-integrity limitation:** a stored literal `global` conversation outside global session scope cannot be addressed by the existing chat.send contract without redirecting it to main. Native Talk refuses that case before microphone admission and asks the user to select the intended agent conversation. It does not restore legacy-global writing or silently redirect. Unverifiable owners are likewise refused. Relay alias resolution and its previously documented legacy limitations are unchanged.

No Gateway production/protocol/schema change, transcript writer, provider feature, or new background-call behavior is included. This does not claim protection against every hot-server routing reconfiguration during an established call.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the chat owner and request lease before permission. Refresh Android node permissions/capabilities at the node connection owner without replacing the operator socket or bootstrap owner; genuine Gateway replacements still retire their leases.

For captured native Talk, read bounded `chat.history` metadata through that lease before microphone admission. Validate `sessionInfo.key`, agent, and main classification, then retain the immutable address for the call, including recognition restarts. Use it consistently for sends, early/remapped finals, cached text, and terminal-ACK history fallback. A retired preparation cancels without publishing a stale failure. The relay adapter continues using its own proven request-alias contract.

This remains the independent extraction against main, not a stack on either earlier split. Main's spoken-input formatting is preserved.

## Evidence

- **Red before repair:** both first-grant/operator-lease regressions failed before production edits. Three native-route cases reproduced wrong-thread sending or ignored canonical finals; the valid global-scope control passed. Original failed logs and JUnit receipts are retained.
- **Green candidate:** 242 affected Android tests passed, zero failures/errors/skips, plus all Android Kotlin lint tasks; 108.67s combined wall. This includes 133 Talk manager cases, 48 physical-session reconnect cases, permission/ABA and fallback UI coverage, generic/native/relay/PTT behavior, early/remapped/duplicate/retired completions, held preparation retirement/replacement, two turns with one preparation, and terminal-ACK history ownership. The unchanged R1 owner also has its prior 91-case green proof (31.30s wall).
- **Cross-language contract:** one 12-row table is checked by actual Gateway history and send-preparation owners and consumed by the Android manager fixture. Covers fresh/stored global, main aliases, explicit/legacy keys, and distinct agent-qualified global. Gateway test: 2.068s test time, 11.46s wall. Normal current config canonicalizes mainKey to main; legacy/custom-hello Android cases additionally prove that returned metadata—not a guessed prefix—is used.
- **Measured Android test cost:** permission file 1.643s, manager file 17.528s, existing bootstrap/auth file 6.975s in its R1 run. The seven added manager tests totaled 2.601s in the final matrix; the shared 12-case matrix took 1.311s. Gradle wall times include compilation/setup and are not individual CI test costs.
- Canonical Gateway test-graph typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and native-source verification pass. Native inventory remains 4033 entries; generated translations are unchanged. Normal Mermaid generation ran after task-private frozen dependency recovery; it was not skipped for this repair.
- **Final independent P0–P2 review:** no actionable findings; final source/evidence verification passed. The helper subsequently failed exporting its receipt (exit 1). The observed verdict and original export failure are preserved; no canonical success status or extra review is claimed.

**Proof limits:** local Robolectric, real Kotlin Runtime/GatewaySession, MockWebServer/audio boundaries, and direct real TypeScript handlers—not physical-device, live-provider, APK, full repository, or full Wear-platform proof. Existing published CI on `238b1dae1df4ebad21c9b395808ac30dcbe00285` predates this repair and does not validate it. Repair commit `852d0efb450959a1900ff817c5165770f4d0f67a` is now published to this existing PR; its tree is the tested `75bb6236a3c57bf7c1560f533b62a45817784eb3`. Android Play, third-party, Wear and Kotlin lint jobs all succeeded. The openclaw/ci-gate status was verified successful on September 21, 2026, at 00:51 UTC. No new PR or merge was performed.

title: fix(android): isolate camera captures and preview staged photos
body:
Related: #151079

## What Problem This Solves

Android camera captures can compete or wait on an inactive Activity, while staged photo attachments have no image preview in the composer.

## User Impact

Camera requests reject competing captures and recheck permission, camera enablement and foreground access. An Activity stop cancels its capture without cancelling an otherwise-live caller. Staged photos gain a bounded thumbnail and open the existing image viewer; filename, remove and editor controls remain available.

Incoming inline-image limits are unchanged. This does not add call-photo APIs, background-call continuity, accepted-send attachment retirement, or conversation/Talk changes. Physical-camera/device acceptance is not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one process-wide capture owner for stills and clips, releasing only each request's CameraX use cases and temporary resources. Pass the composer image policy through the real attachment strip and existing decoder instead of increasing the untrusted inline limit. Preserve the image viewer already landed on main.

This second extraction targets `main` directly and does not depend on the first split PR. The original draft remains unchanged.

## Evidence

<!-- camera-ci-budget-20260922 -->
### Forked test-worker budget correction — 026bbbdf8b535e9ad8dad881a03677ad4227aebc

- **Diagnosis:** the complete ThirdParty suite reproduced the original failure: **3,548 tests / one OOM**, at RealtimePlayoutTest.kt:101. The original merge checkout and PR have identical Android source trees. Exact Java 21.0.12.1+1, Gradle 9.7.1, SDK 37.0 and the original 512 MiB worker ceiling were preserved; runner hardware is not claimed identical to hosted CI.
- An unchanged full replay passed all 3,548 cases in the original class/method order but incurred **298 full GCs**, retaining approximately **498/512 MiB** immediately before playout. Its overall build failed on a deprecated observation-only callback; that diagnostic defect was corrected, not suppressed. The next diagnostic replay reproduced the OOM and captured the heap.
- **Owner / repair:** the dominant retained arrays are Robolectric framework resource buffers through CppApkAssets and NATIVE_APK_ASSETS_REGISTRY; class/method-handle instrumentation is another major consumer. The existing 3 GiB Gradle **daemon** setting does not configure forked Test workers, whose dependency default is 512 MiB. Configure a finite **1 GiB test-worker ceiling** at the existing Android-application test owner. This is measured test-runtime provisioning, not a claim of repairing a camera leak. No application heap, SDK selection, worker recycling, assertions or PCM fixture changed.
- **Green countercheck:** **3,548 ThirdParty + 3,415 Play + 326 Wear = 7,289 tests**, zero failures/errors/skips, plus all four Kotlin lint targets. Combined Gradle invocation **12m 10s**, BUILD SUCCESSFUL; GC logs confirm the 1 GiB ceiling. ThirdParty full collections fell from 298 to **8**. [Blacksmith Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35680316721); the owned lease was stopped after evidence collection.
- Validation tasks: :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest, :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest, :wear:testDebugUnitTest, :app:ktlintCheck, :benchmark:ktlintCheck, :wear:ktlintCheck and :wear-shared:ktlintCheck, with --no-daemon --build-cache --console=plain and a GC-only observation init script. Mermaid generation ran normally; no test suite was excluded.
- Fresh independent **P0–P2 autoreview: scoped-clean**. Follow-up delta: **application production 0; test logic 0; build configuration +3/-0**. Earlier commits and contributor credit are preserved.
- **Hosted status:** [exact-head CI run 35683016239](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35683016239) completed **SUCCESS** on 026bbbdf8b535e9ad8dad881a03677ad4227aebc: **Play, ThirdParty, Wear, Kotlin lint and openclaw/ci-gate all pass**. No merge/automerge.
- **Device-evidence scope:** additional physical-device capture is outside this follow-up’s requested CI-only scope. The device-evidence rank-up is intentionally not performed here. Existing hardware-shadowed tests and native composer captures remain labeled as such; no physical-camera acceptance is claimed.
<!-- /camera-ci-budget-20260922 -->

**Historical hosted failure (superseded by the diagnosis above):** Play, Wear and Kotlin lint pass, but the [ThirdParty job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35676821442/job/106585149342) reports 3,548 tests with one failure: `RealtimePlayoutTest.pcmByteBudgetRemainsIndependentOfEntryCapacity` throws `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` while allocating the existing 12 MiB byte-budget fixture at line 101. The aggregate gate remains failed.

The playout implementation and fixture are unchanged by this PR. A bounded isolated replay of the complete `RealtimePlayoutTest` class passes 23/23 cases (57s Gradle wall; 1.725s test-class time). That isolated pass does **not** reproduce the original full-suite order, establish the heap-retention cause, or prove a repair. No heap increase, assertion change or blind CI rerun was applied. The full-suite follow-up is documented above; the isolated replay alone did not establish a repair.

### Historical repaired-main refresh — `e5890e26299dcb15f8b2d48d78a864b081985fa2`

- Rebased both commits onto main `4311a4ecdf96add7ae6d20b1b059ae72c875cde3`; `git range-diff` confirms both patches are unchanged. Human co-authorship is preserved.
- The incorporated main contains the NSD/Robolectric compilation repair `48f664ca009522fbe1bdacee869357494243736a` from #155214. The earlier hosted run below failed on those main-owned test-shadow signatures before camera assertions ran; that failure remains historical evidence, not a passing rerun.
- On this committed head with Robolectric 4.17: **51/51 selected camera/ownership/handler/dispatcher/JPEG tests and all four Android Kotlin lint targets pass**. Final Gradle invocation: **63s**; the nine new capture regressions: **1.648s**. The same focused command below was used; no production change was added during this refresh.
- [Current hosted checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153033/checks) are separate from local proof. No physical-camera or successful hardware-capture claim is added, and no merge is part of this update.

### Historical capture-boundary regression follow-up — `30d48e2d097500babb1df88beef657d856988f66`

- Added **9 regressions through the real `CameraHandler` and `CameraCaptureManager` entry paths**, with CameraX replaced only at the hardware boundary. They cover photo/video contention during recording and finalization, cancellation during warmup and still capture, capture/finalize failures, preserving unrelated bindings after a failed bind, and Activity-stop settlement without cancelling the caller.
- The Activity-stop cases also assert that production-created temporary capture files are deleted, request-owned bindings/recordings are released, and the next request can enter CameraX again. The retry intentionally receives a synthetic camera error: this proves re-admission, **not a successful physical photo or video**.
- **Red:** the same source-compatible 9-test cohort on unfixed main `208132c299208871dbda7fe855aa0bbd9107ce9b` has **6 intended assertion failures**, no compile errors or timeout. Its camera-manager blob matches the earlier unfixed baseline. Final baseline invocation: **37s**.
- **Green:** **51/51 selected camera/ownership/handler/dispatcher/JPEG tests passed**, with no failures, errors or skips. The 9 new cases took **2.178s**; the final Gradle invocation, including all four Android Kotlin lint targets, took **43s**. A formatting violation in the new helper was corrected before this final passing run.
- Fresh independent **P0–P2 review of the new regression delta: scoped-clean**. Normal commit hooks passed; the committed test blob matches the verified bytes. Follow-up delta: **production 0; tests +420**. The existing stronger process-wide capture owner is unchanged; no duplicate camera implementation or gallery-layout changes were added.
- [Fresh exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35671358041) is separate evidence for this commit. Earlier green checks on `aad95ae4a765` are not claimed for this head. The September 19 ClawSweeper report covers that earlier head; this follow-up requires a fresh current-head review.
- The unchanged native composer before/after images below were re-inspected, confirmed embedded and decoded on the public PR page, and delivered as actual image attachments in the linked follow-up discussion. No screenshot acknowledgement or inspection of the requester’s browser is required.
- **Limits:** no Android device was connected during the follow-up preflight. CameraX hardware is shadowed; no physical-camera teardown, successful physical capture, installed APK, emulator or live Gateway acceptance is claimed. Focused runs exclude the unrelated Mermaid asset generator.

<details>
<summary>Follow-up validation commands</summary>

Run from `apps/android` with the Android SDK configured:

```sh
./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CameraCaptureManagerTest -x :app:generateMermaidAssets --console=plain --no-daemon

./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CameraCaptureManagerTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CameraCaptureOwnershipTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CameraHandlerTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CameraFacingPreferenceTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.InvokeDispatcherTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.JpegSizeLimiterTest :app:ktlintCheck :benchmark:ktlintCheck :wear:ktlintCheck :wear-shared:ktlintCheck -x :app:generateMermaidAssets --console=plain --no-daemon
```

The first command is the unfixed-baseline run; the second is the final PR-candidate run. No new broad app-build or UI test matrix was run.

</details>

### Original implementation evidence

- **Red:** two source-compatible baseline regressions fail through the existing camera handler and production `ChatScreen`: immediate refusal for an inactive Activity and visibility of an admitted large photo. The camera case uses cancellation cleanup to avoid waiting indefinitely on baseline CameraX.
- **Green:** 46 focused camera-ownership, handler, codec, composer and existing viewer tests pass, with no failures, errors or skips. No new broad test matrix was run.
- Kotlin formatting and `ktlintCheck` pass **with the task's changed-file filter**; staged whitespace checks pass. This is not an all-repository formatting claim.
- Fresh normal-index P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Its unchanged-repository context was limited; lead inspection additionally covered the capture owner, production wiring and resolved CameraX 1.6.2/coroutines 1.11.0 contracts.
- Commit `aad95ae4a765ac1c6cace29f90f60d3eb9d3095d`, directly based on main `2b341cd3cef75ce4b728d0587d95c9b98fd75c6a`; tested tree `7ca1e7e37b9e52b44532d16155ca8c25c206e3fd`. Six production files +149/−46; five test files +357/−0. The production growth implements shared capture admission, lifecycle cancellation and scoped cleanup rather than a parallel capture path.
- Tests ran locally with owned dependencies. No remote lease, emulator, live provider, installed APK or physical-camera test was used. This original proof is historical; current-head CI and review are tracked in the follow-up section above.

### Before / after — staged photo preview

Matched 360×720 production Compose captures under Robolectric native graphics, with the same synthetic JPEG and chat fixture. Before: filename chip only. After: image preview, existing viewer access and retained remove/editor controls. The chat viewport reflows as the composer gains the thumbnail. These are not device screenshots or camera-capture proof.

title: fix(android): stop adding instructions to recognized speech
body:
Related: #151079, #150178

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Android native Talk and push-to-talk adding app-written tone and ElevenLabs instructions to the user's recognized message.

## User Impact

Spoken messages reach the agent without extra prompt scaffolding. The agent's instructions govern response style instead of an Android per-turn demand for concise speech. Existing recognition trimming and PTT segment merging stay unchanged.

Android-only: Apple behavior is not fixed here. No model/provider selection, authentication, audio routing, TTS directive parsing, call lifecycle, or UI-layout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the prompt-building helper at the input producer and send the transcript through the existing `chat.send` owner. Two existing native/PTT tests now check exact outgoing messages, including multiline and instruction-like speech.

title: fix(automations): current-session announce fails in WebChat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: creating an announced current-session automation fails in a WebChat conversation, including condition-triggered agent turns.

## User Impact

Users can keep `sessionTarget: "current"` with `delivery: { mode: "announce" }` instead of disabling delivery. The existing canonical conversation completion remains responsible for the result. No configuration migration or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creation-time inference helper copied internal WebChat coordinates into an external-channel route, which the Gateway correctly rejected. Keep internal coordinates out of inferred outbound delivery and do not replace a live internal context with an older stored external route. Explicit external destinations and normal configured-channel validation remain intact; runtime remembered-source routing is unchanged.

- Reproduced the original failure through the deployed `automations` tool using a disabled condition watcher. The disabled no-delivery control registered and was removed; it was not used as a workaround.
- Three creation regressions fail on the original source with the external-channel validation error and pass with this change. Coverage composes the real tool, Gateway handler, isolated scheduler persistence, and live authority validator.
- The original candidate passed 694 tests across eight files and the full changed-file checks. The patch-identical current-main refresh passed 67 focused creation, routing, canonical completion, and session-result tests across five files.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long names crowd the composer menu, and inconsistent spacing and flat connector actions make its submenus hard to scan.

## User Impact

- One 320 px menu width, clamped to 296 px at a 320 px viewport. Long names wrap and scroll without overlapping; labels and click targets are not shrunk.

No modal, migration, backend/configuration change, or permission expansion is introduced.

This refines the existing native menu rather than adding another browsing surface. Shared spacing and fixed icon columns remove the unintended 3 px jump between views. Native dropdown items remain direct siblings, preserving keyboard selection and focus behavior.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

> **Superseded by [#153020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153020), merged September 19, 2026 at 19:43:18 UTC.** The original macOS managed-helper ancestry refusal is repaired on main by commit `99ce0ed8812f6ce8aade38b839adee3b14176657`. This alternative activation implementation is not being merged. The investigation and test evidence below are retained as historical evidence.

Fixes macOS Control UI and chat updates that finish validation, then fail with `managed-service-preflight` because the updater remains a descendant of the serving Gateway.

Related: #145252 (update and recovery reliability).

## User Impact

Managed macOS updates can ask their supervised helper to stop the old Gateway before activating the new version, without weakening the refusal for ordinary descendant callers. Linux uses the same supervised exchange; Windows Scheduled Task recovery is unchanged.

This repairs the updater once installed. It does not retrofit an already-running affected updater or claim that the reporter's existing installation has been upgraded. No changes or retries were made against the reported Business Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore the existing `park` / `parked` protocol inside the maintenance owner's lifecycle lock, after service admission and before package/source mutation. Capture the exact current helper/executor lease, recheck it before dispatch and after acknowledgment, and retain an observed stop even if authority is subsequently lost. Direct service-stop ancestry checks remain intact.

The helper now joins dispatched native stop work on failure as well as success before retiring the updater. Failed control-pipe writes retain their error listener through Node's paired error event. The command-start scripts and connected process fixture were extracted into sibling modules rather than growing grandfathered oversized files.

## Evidence

- **Reproduction:** the new connected regression failed against the original maintenance code with the same `inside the gateway process tree` refusal. It has a real OS process chain (Gateway stand-in → generated helper → updater) and a current helper lease; it does not reproduce the issue by manually printing a `park` request.
- **Boundary coverage:** successful launchd-shim and systemd-shim activation; serving Gateway retained through validation; no direct-stop fallback; invalid metadata and revoked leases; acknowledged-stop retention; native-stop settlement before updater retirement; failed-write callback/error ordering.
- **Verification results:** 326 focused/sibling tests passed on the isolated Linux Testbox (217 infra + 109 CLI). After the final lint and fixture-cleanup changes, all 23 activation unit/integration tests passed again. Final lint on all 11 changed files reported zero warnings/errors; formatting, whitespace, structural ratchets, and the remaining native-state/database/import/auth guards passed. Core and core-test typechecks passed on the pre-lint snapshot; those full typecheck lanes were not rerun after the final cleanup.
- **Build caveat:** final `pnpm build` exited 0, but its Control UI performance report flagged startup gzip at 363326 B against a 363282 B limit (44 B over). This patch changes no UI, manifests, lockfiles, or performance baselines; the size warning is not claimed as resolved. Hosted PR CI is not yet verified.
- **Independent review:** final P0–P2 review is scoped-clean after resolving native-stop settlement and failed-write cleanup findings.
- **Native macOS gap:** the available Mac node is disconnected. Launchd coverage uses real helper/updater processes on Linux, simulated Darwin policy, and synthetic service-manager adapters. The Gateway process is a disposable stand-in, and the updater child calls the real shared maintenance owner. This is not native launchd/systemd service proof, a full macOS Git-install/Control UI upgrade, or a successful published-driver × candidate end-to-end test. Host-supplied before-fix reports cover executing `4da02cb3cf5c` → target `ec9c1a13db89`; those private artifacts are not republished here.

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Web UI links give little context before opening another tab, unlike specialized GitHub previews.

## User Impact

Hover or keyboard-focus an ordinary external link to see its favicon, social image, title, and description. Keyboard navigation, Escape, touch navigation, and text-only fallbacks remain usable.

The existing automatic-favicon opt-out disables this enrichment. When enabled, deliberate hover or focus sends the eligible URL—including path and query—to the Gateway for bounded anonymous fetching; browser cookies and site credentials are not forwarded.

title: fix(macos): prepare integrated tab logins before opening links
body:
Related: #152663

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a website in integrated Mac tabs does not use the user's existing browser login, and fresh passkey sign-in remains unverified in this embedded browser.

## User Impact

Before the first HTTP(S) link loads, the app offers a native chooser for one Chrome, Brave, Edge, or Chromium profile. With explicit consent, it imports cookies into the **actual Mac-tab WebKit store before navigation**. Concurrent opens and a Settings-initiated import share that operation; users can decline or explicitly reimport later. Existing pages are not reloaded automatically. Cookies remain on the Mac even with a remote Gateway.

**Draft / partial delivery:** browser-wide platform passkeys still require Apple's approved browser capability, browser eligibility/signing work, and signed-Mac authentication proof. This rework adds real permission/status integration, not a claim that the reported passkey failure is fixed. No passkeys are imported, no restricted entitlement is added to unapproved builds, and no external-browser fallback replaces integrated support. Device-bound sessions and non-cookie storage can still require fresh sign-in. The linked issue remains open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses Peter's existing CookieSyncManager and Browser plugin producer from #123494 (commit 2ef92d0bbe9f8a37a50957ac52c47df5559f9f98): listSystemProfiles → readSystemProfileCookies → system-chrome-cookies. **Deletes the duplicate 274-line MacTabChromeCookies extractor/decryptor.** The version-matched bundled local runtime returns cookies over dedicated app-owned pipes, not a Gateway request, SSH route, generic command logger, or JavaScript bridge. Existing remote domain-allowlisted cookie sync stays separate.

WebKit mapping retains host/domain, path, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, expiry/session lifetime, protected-Gateway exclusion and the current persistent/private store. Retired documents cannot continue consent/import/navigation. The shared producer now rejects schema-24 host-digest mismatches instead of importing corrupted credentials.

Apple explicitly documents that [WKWebView handles website WebAuthn automatically](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/authenticationservices/passkey-use-in-web-browsers). The new platform-passkey row reports browser entitlement/authorization and can explicitly request system permission on eligible signed builds. WebKit still owns ceremonies and origin checks. Platform/provider, security-key and hybrid routes are not conflated. The [managed capability](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/entitlements/com.apple.developer.web-browser.public-key-credential) requires Account Holder/Apple approval and functional HTTP/HTTPS browser eligibility; current packaging does not establish these. Missing entitlement is **not proven to be the cause** of the original unseen failure.

## Evidence

- Real red/green regression: a schema-24 cookie database with tampered hosts returned corrupted cookies before the producer fix; afterward both rows are rejected. Four new platform-passkey UI states also failed before the UI change, then passed.
- Focused UI/bridge, canonical producer, private adapter and remote cookie-sync suites: **88 passed**. TypeScript/changed-file checks and package build: all TypeScript projects and source/dead-export guards passed. Full core/extensions/scripts typed lint and stylesheet lint passed after mechanical brace fixes (three pre-existing max-lines warnings). Package build, refreshed UI/plugin typechecks and native i18n verification passed after current-main reconciliation.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview found a manual-import/first-link race; both now join the same operation, with regression coverage. Follow-up full-candidate reviews were scoped clean after fixing manual-navigation and shared-store rollback races, including a fresh review against current main. A real main-branch conflict was resolved by retaining Gateway health refresh and removing only the replaced import offer.
- Native tests authored for first-request cookie delivery, repeated/manual setup, retired-document and iframe denial, private subprocess/error boundaries, protected cookies, host-only sibling exclusion and Secure delivery through a loopback proxy, in persistent and private WebKit stores. **Native execution status: [exact-head native/full CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35478916296) dispatched for 3453368b06f4e01b50afdc9932e97c72840f70af; results pending. Previous-head macOS optimized build, real Darwin Swift lint/format and iOS Release build passed on Xcode 26.6 / Swift 6.3.3; native tests caught an invalid closing-tag escape in the new iframe fixture before execution. That syntax is corrected without weakening assertions; tests must still execute on this head.** Linux checks are not native execution proof.
- No real profiles, Keychain secrets or personal accounts were used. Interactive consent, packaged-runtime Keychain access and signed real platform/provider/security-key/hybrid authentication remain unverified. The available Mac node is offline; no-spend Mac provisioning preflight lacks broker administration. These proof gaps keep the PR draft.

### UI before / after rework

Actual Control UI in Linux Chromium with synthetic native capability/permission state. This is **not native WebKit, Keychain or passkey sign-in proof**; native before/after consent captures remain outstanding.

![Before rework: separate manual Mac-tab import only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db055db7-5cdb-4490-a1a3-2708eaccff15)
