title: fix: sandboxed sessions cannot edit managed projects
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sessions that must run in a sandbox cannot reliably edit and run Git in an authorized managed project outside the agent workspace.

## User Impact

Sandboxed project sessions get a private standalone checkout without the host repository's shared Git metadata, credentials, setup scripts, or ignored provisioning. Accepted edits remain available to the canonical workspace, publication, and archive/restore.

Docker and Podman support this local projection. Explicit read-only access stays read-only; unsupported backends fail rather than executing on the host. Podman still needs its init helper on the engine host; this change does not install production packages.

**Admission tradeoff:** after initial preparation, new host-only paths must be staged in the canonical Git index before entering an existing projection. Editing ignore rules alone cannot admit host data. Existing admitted edits and guest-created files, including ignored files, continue to reconcile. Invalid UTF-8 source paths are rejected. Incomplete Git sources must be hydrated through the trusted host workflow before retrying; projection packing cannot run lazy-fetch helpers.

Projection custody is additive in shared state schema 17, with no version bump or change to the existing provisioned-file ledger. Settle active execution/reconciliation before downgrading. Older versions do not implement projection recovery; full older-Gateway recovery execution is not claimed.

The requesting maintainer explicitly approved this scope: private Docker/Podman projections for sandboxed managed projects, none/rw mapped to the private checkout, explicit ro preserved, and explicit refusal for unsupported local backends rather than host fallback. The supporting-version recovery contract and additive projection/recovery owner were also approved in the original discussion linked below. This is not a request to silently change those choices during review.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registered source authority stays with session preparation, including deferred children after their parent retires. The canonical managed worktree owns accepted changes; private execution uses the existing manifest, staging, reconciliation, rollback, and renewable-lease machinery. Execution and browser writers are fenced during settlement.

The same owner persists exact source admission and constrains publication. Canonical recovery snapshots retain host data under their existing rules, but restore does not confer guest admission. Accepted ignored guest content survives archive/restore through the existing pending-result receipt. Host materialization and streamed packing use the existing trusted Git configuration scope instead of repository programs. Runtime skill mounts remain protected without excluding ordinary project content under .openclaw.

## Evidence

- Hosted CI for `bc442c6787f398920e62aab7c425f44e866d0888` passed in run `35445791362`, including Windows. A subsequent main conflict was only adjacent additive wrapper-manifest entries; both were retained. The introduced patch is unchanged, verified by identical zero-context stable patch ID and per-file change counts. The refreshed main integration passed 49 projection/retirement/wrapper tests, the complete changed-file gate, and a fresh serial build in **3m36.8s**.
- The latest retirement regression was reproduced through the actual settlement entry point for both execution and browser runtimes. Quiescence now retains the exact physical generation and bridge instances through archive/reset, including stopped allocations. Destruction never falls back to a reusable name; metadata cleanup requires unchanged registry and bridge custody. **113 focused tests pass**, including four running/stopped replacement cases and eleven retirement custody cases.
- **Real Podman retirement proof passed:** running and stopped same-name replacements survived stale retirement with their registry retained. Normal `withSettledLocalWorkspace` retirement preserved accepted edits and removed the runtime and registry. All proof-owned runtimes and state were cleaned. Browser engine and bridge shutdown effects are mocked, with real registry custody; real Docker browser retirement is not claimed.
- Backend execution and termination also retain validated immutable container IDs. A real Podman replacement with a copied execution marker survived stale cleanup, while revoked execution stayed denied. The actual Codex input lifecycle proof passed again after that change.
- Full-candidate independent P0/P1 review against the integrated main baseline completed scoped-clean. The complete changed-file gate passed after mechanical brace fixes, and the fresh serial build passed in **3m35.4s**. Source/index matched afterward. Those local results were followed by exact-head hosted CI and native landing, recorded below.
- Retained Codex input now carries the child’s captured authority through pipe, PTY and HTTP writes, including authority loss during startup readiness. Two pipe/PTY cases failed before repair; 100 Codex sibling tests and six focused input/readiness cases passed afterward. A real required-Podman proof used the actual startProcess/writeProcess entrypoints, accepted an authorized command, rotated the durable session lifecycle, rejected the next command, and verified termination, zero remaining owners and no unauthorized bytes.
- CI’s remaining personal-delete and repository-archive failures were stale fixture store paths, not relaxed production guards. Both consumers now use the harness’s actual canonical store; all 137 personal/repository/restart/boundary tests passed. The combined follow-up passed independent P0/P1 review, changed-file gates and a fresh build (3m14.2s).
- Integrated current main while preserving its newer Codex PTY, readiness, interrupt, HTTP and settlement behavior and publication maintenance settings. The combined publication/Codex integration suite passed **193 tests**; the focused pause/recovery suite passed **10 tests**.
- **Real required-Podman lifecycle passed** (53.95s total): private source and Git, protected skills, selected repository subdirectory and relative writes, revoked reconciliation stays frozen, a fresh live owner resumes, revoked interrupts are denied, child termination, accepted changes, publication snapshot, archive/restore and expiry. The engine's paused-but-not-running state and per-runtime recovery receipts are covered. This uses a process-local init helper, not a production installation.
- A separate proof used the **actual Codex subprocess owner with the production required-Podman context**: the guest writer started, revocation denied new execution, termination produced exit 143, no child owners remained, bytes stopped changing, and the revoked checkpoint was rejected. All task-owned proof runtimes and state were cleaned.
- Before the latest integration, the full changed-file gate passed, including core/plugin/test types, all core/plugin/script lint, SDK boundaries, dead exports, schema version 17 and runtime-cycle guards. The integrated build passed in **3m39.3s** and source hashes/tree matched afterward. Four line-count warnings are in files unchanged from main; the UI build reports an advisory CSS size warning, not a hard-limit failure.
- Full-candidate independent review identified pause-lifecycle issues that were reproduced and repaired. Its final inventory/fsmonitor finding was **rejected with executable counterevidence**: raw Git executed a configured sentinel monitor, while both actual inventory APIs blocked it through the existing requireGitBuffer → runGitBuffered → gitEnvironment(core.fsmonitor=false) owner. No duplicate Git policy was added.
- Earlier real-entry regressions cover root/nested de-ignore exposure across turns and database reopen, publication/archive admission, invalid UTF-8 filename aliases, and missing-object lazy-fetch helper execution. The fixes retain host data without admitting it to the guest or publication and preserve the existing recovery ledger.


Earlier hosted runs found a Windows watcher timeout and a shared-worker registry mock failure. The current integration preserves main’s newer watcher diagnostics unchanged; it does not weaken assertions or timeouts or claim those historical failures were repaired by the sandbox change. Final exact-head CI passed before landing.

**Landing status:** merged into `main` through native TESTBOX preparation and `merge-run` on September 19, 2026 at 14:29 UTC. Exact reviewed/CI-green head: `1473d22e57ba0272a1658dfb7bbddf119e1fdd2f`; landed squash: `28d8ee4f096b5d4cd99489e12d7a495a97750599`. Hosted CI run `35447669452` and both required aggregate checks passed. Main ancestry, the human coauthor trailer, and native branch/worktree cleanup were verified.

**Proof limits:** no authenticated guest model-provider turn, actual GitHub publication from a sandboxed guest, native Windows Git-view run, or full older-Gateway projection recovery is claimed. Additive schema-17/reopen and unchanged legacy-decoder recovery are covered. Production init-helper installation and Gateway deployment remain outside this PR.

title: fix(macos): show live status for connected saved gateways
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: connected saved Gateways stay gray in the Mac app's Gateway picker and sidebar when they are not the primary Gateway.

## User Impact

Saved Gateways turn green when connected and update when the connection drops or recovers. Users do not need to reconnect or change their primary Gateway to get accurate status. Multiple windows for the same Gateway stay green while any one is connected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Dashboard now reports its actual connection state to the native window owner, which updates the shared Gateway catalog and menu. Reports are bound to the current trusted document and expected endpoint; replaced, closed, or signed-out documents cannot leave stale status behind. Existing menu probes remain responsible for unopened Gateways. No new polling, credentials, or settings.

Reported by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/249ab89d-98f4-45ad-a98e-1fc9133f06ed)
- [CI repairs, verification and landing](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/840d24d0-abaf-4950-a07e-d64793f7a8a3)

## Evidence

- The startup regression failed on the original code and passes with the fix; 51 focused UI tests passed. A new red/green regression covers non-retrying first-connect failure and intentional stop.
- Bundled Chromium E2E passed: saved Gateway connects → green, connection loss → red, reconnect → green; selection, primary marker, and unopened Gateway status stay unchanged.
- Before/after screenshots replay the original and fixed UI source with the same sanitized fixture. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes generated working-context JSON appearing inside a person's message when they send from the Home dock, making the conversation noisy and mixing reference data into copy/edit actions.

The inspector exposes the captured session, page, agent, workspace, file, and selection, with raw JSON under **Technical details**. The send-time snapshot survives queues, retries, and reloads; copy, queued edits, rewind, and fork keep authored text separate.

Older messages without attachment metadata retain their original interpretation. No configuration, permission, or database-version change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry a bounded snapshot through the existing send, outbox, and transcript owners. The model still receives quoted, untrusted reference data; display projections consume recorded metadata. Hook redaction and continuation rewrites cannot restore the original display text.

Maintainer-requested CI repairs also make the history-fling fixture independent of browser-call latency, join session disk-measurement workers before fixture handoff, and apply the existing test-runtime argument policy to Vitest forks. The native shutdown mitigation is limited to test processes: it prevents a proven Node/V8 concurrent-compiler/GC deadlock while retaining synchronous baseline compilation.

title: feat(desktop): add a consistent Keep computer awake setting
body:
Closes #152388

## What Problem This Solves

Tauri users cannot keep their computer awake from OpenClaw, and the equivalent Mac setting is difficult to find under “Unattended desktop hosting.”

## User Impact

Tauri gains an off-by-default **Keep computer awake** checkbox beside **Start at Login**, with the preference retained across restarts. The native Mac setting uses the same clear name without changing its saved preference or existing connection, hosting, and lock safeguards.

On Linux, idle inhibition can also delay display dimming and automatic locking; manual locking and explicit sleep remain available. Windows and macOS Tauri request system idle-sleep prevention without keeping the display on. A saved setting that cannot activate is explicitly marked **inactive** and can still be turned off.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native app owns one sleep request and releases it on disable or quit, while closing to the tray leaves it active. Preferences reuse the existing credential-backed store. GNOME uses its acknowledged session-manager API; other Linux desktops use the idle-inhibition portal. This avoids both logind-only coverage gaps and a GTK portal acknowledgment that can precede an unsandboxed application-ID failure.

title: fix: prevent plugin-state failures during database maintenance
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin-state operations can fail during overlapping database maintenance, leaving a memory indexing lock behind.

## User Impact

Memory indexing can release its lock reliably when host database maintenance overlaps worker dispatch. No schema migration, permission change, timeout increase, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Writable plugin-state commands now join the existing host lifecycle admission before worker dispatch, including comparison observations. Existing-only reads keep their current behavior. This repairs the shared custody gap rather than adding cleanup retries.

## Evidence

The regression tests use real worker threads and real SQLite databases. They intercept only the dispatch boundary to acquire a competing native lifecycle owner **after broker preparation and before forwarding the original message to the worker**. No worker response is mocked. The observe case must return the retained value; compare-delete must apply and a subsequent lookup must show the row is gone.

Deterministic before/after output (synthetic isolated state):

```text
Before lifecycle admission:
  observe       FAIL: PLUGIN_STATE_READ_FAILED
  compareDelete FAIL: PLUGIN_STATE_WRITE_FAILED
  cause: StateDatabaseCoordinatorContentionError
         another OpenClaw process owns state-lifecycle
  Tests: 2 failed

After lifecycle admission:
  shares lifecycle custody ... during observe        PASS
  shares lifecycle custody ... during compareDelete  PASS
  plugin-state worker suite: 12 passed
```

Node 26.8.2: before 3/3 failed at ready; after 3/3 passed (1094 / 885 / 859 ms).** These are complete test durations, including cleanup, not just startup timings.

Final candidate tree `926d4a003fb637c4222dedb3e4f6c4f6687ba624`; wrapper reported exit 0. The owned lease was stopped after proof.

The changed-file gate passed, including extension test types, lint (0 warnings/errors), formatting, dependency/boundary guards, and dead-export scans. `git diff --check` passed.

Known independent validation limitation: the neighboring unchanged command-lifecycle test fails in an unbuilt source checkout because its own esbuild fixture resolves `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` through missing `dist` output. Recorded separately rather than widening this one-file fix; both Mantis suites passed in the same 20-test run (19 passed, that one failed).

<summary>Diagnosis, historical sample, and reproduction</summary>

The test already has a readiness handshake: the child emits ready inside the callback after Mantis installs its signal handlers, and the parent waits before signaling. The defect is that fresh `node --import tsx` startup and the transitive source import graph consume the same three-second window. Prebuilding removes that work from the timed child phase rather than relying on a warm cache or relaxing the assertion.

The original and rerun checked out merge snapshot `86887430079e44eeed945cd33746cba77ed24e07`. The original job detected 2 CPUs and used 2 workers; the rerun detected 4 CPUs and used 3 workers. Whole QA execution took 685.61 s versus 106.34 s. Historical logs have no per-child CPU/throttling timeline, so they do not establish the exact host-level cause of the slowdown; the controlled contention run establishes the harness's startup-budget sensitivity.

Bounded history sample: all 2,698 jobs from 30 CI runs immediately preceding/including the target were inspected for eligible shards (25 PR runs and 5 main pushes). Ten first-attempt PR jobs ran these three Mantis cases: the target failed, and nine earlier jobs passed. Observed 1/10 eligible jobs, **not a repository-wide flake-rate estimate**. No earlier exact failure was found in the bounded main/PR search.

The process test was introduced in `1e4e407ba3a34de0b1c4f3815dbbdddb9ebf162f` (#111051). The neighboring QA lifecycle process fixture already uses compilation before its readiness window (introduced by #125738); this applies that existing approach without changing the production interrupt owner.

```sh

node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/cli-interrupts.process.test.ts
```

Contention reproduction: select the first CPU from `/proc/self/status`, launch seven `taskset -c CPU node -e 'const end=Date.now()+90000; while(Date.now()<end) Math.sqrt(Math.random())'` children, then run the process-test command through the same CPU affinity with a fresh `TMPDIR`. The driver awaits the test, kills/joins its owned competitors in `finally`, and removes its temporary directory. Before and after use the same driver; all final tests finish while the 90-second competitors remain active.

Production LOC: unchanged. Test LOC: +34/-13.

title: fix: show full commands and live status in the task sidebar
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the task sidebar cutting off command input and showing “Activity unknown” for a background shell process whose live state is available.

## User Impact

Users can read the complete redacted command, including multiline input, and see live process status and activity updates without refreshing the open inspector. Long detail headings wrap. Previously stored truncated inputs are not backfilled. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Background exec stored its compact label as the prompt, while detail lookup applied another text cap and assistant-prose cleanup. This preserves command source separately from compact labels and removes only protected runtime context. Status now reads the exact promoted process owner; output and cleanup publish through the existing coalesced activity path without durable per-output writes or output retention. Silence does not imply completion or a wait. The existing POSIX PATH wrapper is extracted into a focused sibling module so this repair does not grow the grandfathered oversized exec runtime; no exemptions were added and no test coverage was removed.

Related: #152329 (live agent-run status for CLI tasks). That work uses the agent-run owner; this fix covers detached shell processes and sidebar input display.

## Evidence

- 200 focused tests passed across task lookup, exec lifecycle/cleanup, activity publication, UI detail/state handling, and desktop/mobile browser flows. Regressions failed before their repairs.
- Full changed-file gates passed for all PR files, including core/core-test/UI typechecks, dead-export scans, lint/style checks, runtime import-cycle checks, line-cap/suppression ratchets, formatting, and repository guards. Additional PATH, runtime, notification, cleanup, and lifecycle regressions passed after the behavior-preserving extraction.

title: feat(meetings): add durable participation foundation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Meeting integrations need duplicate-safe participation requests and caption evidence that survives replay, corrections, and retention without granting fresh authority to stale observations.

## User Impact

Adds the experimental participation foundation and Google Meet `participation_context` / `participate` surfaces. Live context retains up to **1,024 sources** with the existing two-minute first-observation expiry; unchanged replay preserves references and guards.

Retained rows and snapshots now preserve independent observation provenance, including speaker and native self/other/unknown facts, even when a row has no actionable source. This is a **retained-snapshot model, not a complete revision journal**. Existing utterance metadata stores the envelope without a new database schema or archive.

**This is not native chat/reaction/hand-control support.** Google Meet still advertises no native participation capabilities. Cancellation after browser dispatch remains best effort: an `uncertain` result may already have produced an effect and must not be retried under a new request ID.

**The SDK budget failure is resolved.** [@canvrno-oai approved](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152327#issuecomment-5803780896) the four-type, one-callable contract and its +5 public exports/+1 callable budget increase. Against the newly integrated `main@e74db47ae34`, the same approved +5/+1 delta gives **4,577 public exports / 4,577 limit** and **2,685 callables / 2,685 limit**; the canonical SDK gate passes. Other review/proof requirements are not waived. Issue linkage remains deferred.

Teams/Zoom transcript reads now survive legitimate browser-tab recovery. Non-participation capture may rotate the tab ID, but session identity, lifecycle, URL, transport, and node checks remain enforced; participation-backed capture stays pinned to its original tab.

**Accepted new-feature P2 limitations:** delayed-source freshness, trusted authorization for source-free actions, and the lifetime source-capacity limitation remain unresolved. The maintainer accepts these specifically for this incremental participation implementation after the existing-consumer compatibility check below. The current Google Meet adapter advertises no native participation actions; the concerns apply to the shared contract when an adapter enables them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared meeting owner retains durable claims, recorded results, bounded corrections, freshness, and session/capability checks. Provenance now survives browser parsing, runtime/context snapshots, and transcript persistence without becoming action authority.

A disappearing duplicate DOM row no longer finalizes a still-visible source. Marker changes and historical replay cannot rehabilitate sticky own echoes or superseded unknown observations. After a known pre-insertion quota rejection, the ledger retries atomic admission once after bounded cleanup, even when another caller reclaimed the rows; unknown write outcomes are not retried.

## Evidence

### Current main refresh and parser integration

Published [`31517565ef9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/31517565ef9869304745abd7bfda87a6eb5c5c32), incorporating `main@e74db47ae34`. **Maintainer direction now permits guarded landing after the existing-consumer compatibility check and required gates pass. The three P2 issues confined to the new participation implementation are accepted for this incremental feature; they are not described as fixed.** A later inspected main snapshot, `0b5cd5179788`, also composes conflict-free with this exact candidate.

- **Parser integration:** main centralized transcript row validation in a shared Zod schema. The resolution reuses that canonical row schema, adding only the caption source/provenance projection. Invalid rows are discarded; optional legacy fields retain their shape; source identities remain epoch-checked and excluded from status `recentTranscript`. The final projection allocates a fresh row without conditional object spreads or mutating the caller.
- **Integration regression found and fixed:** main removed an `asParamRecord` import which the participation request parser still needs. The existing registered-tool regression failed with `asParamRecord is not defined`; restoring a direct import from the canonical SDK owner made it pass. The retired re-export was not restored.
- **Local behavior proof:** 797 tests passed across 65 source-level meeting/Google Meet files and four projects in 163.80 seconds. The final parser file passed 19 tests in 38.53 seconds wall (including 23.65 seconds of shared worker preparation). New assertions cover mixed invalid/valid rows, optional fields, pending sources, provenance, and the status/source-identity boundary.
- **Checks:** canonical SDK check passed at 4,577 public exports / 2,685 callables, retaining the approved +5/+1 delta. Core production types, scoped core lint, format, conflict/size/assertion/dependency/boundary guards passed. The broad local test-type pipeline was stopped after partial progress; it is not claimed as a full pass. Scoped extension lint subsequently passed after verified task-local artifact-lock recovery. The runtime-dependent Chrome startup suite was not run locally; the hosted CI result is reported separately.
- **Local environment limitations:** the initial 66-file selection stopped before tests because Chrome startup requires runtime bootstrap and this host’s Gateway artifact guard could not complete its service inspection. No guard was weakened or Gateway stopped. The subsequent source selection excluded only that declared runtime-dependent file. The cancelled local test-type process retained its fail-closed artifact lock. After verifying the owner, child, compiler, and related processes had stopped, the documented recovery removed only that task-owned lock; extension lint then passed with zero warnings/errors. No artifact guard was disabled.
- **Independent review:** completed P0–P2 review found no new actionable parser/registration defect. It did identify an additional P2 capacity problem in unchanged participation code, independently reproduced below; the overall review is therefore not clean. The final allocation-only lint adjustment was separately checked with the parser regression and scoped lint.
- Fresh CI for `31517565ef9`: [run 36183174153](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36183174153), attempt 1, **completed successfully: 130 jobs passed, 20 skipped, no failures**. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` job and its posted status passed; dependency/security-review statuses also passed. GitHub reports a clean, conflict-free merge. This does not resolve or waive the review findings below.

### Existing-consumer compatibility check

Pinned candidate: `31517565ef9`. Baseline: current-main snapshot `4975542b5c45`; later inspected main `3272581f081` has no changes in the relevant parser or Google Meet/Teams/Zoom consumer paths.

- Traced every in-repository `MeetingPlatformAdapter.create` production consumer: **Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom**. Teams/Zoom use the ordinary runtime facade and do not opt into the new participation owner; the three accepted P2s are therefore outside their existing execution paths.
- **343 tests passed across 34 files / three projects (111.33 seconds)**: all existing Teams/Zoom suites, the shared parser/runtime/transcript-store cases, and Google Meet adapter/registered-tool regressions. Coverage includes captions and retained snapshots, normal/malformed status, optional/invalid fields, URL/session/lifecycle checks, and browser recovery.
- **4,020 legacy comparisons passed** using the exact production parser/schema declarations from main and the candidate, with known-good and malformed-input sanity oracles. Outputs and errors matched for legacy rows, mixed valid/invalid input, absent/invalid optional fields, dropped counts, epochs, and owner flags. This complements actual consumer suites; it is not a claim of live-browser or universal third-party testing.
- **No existing-consumer regression was identified.** Legacy parser shapes are preserved when no new participation fields are supplied. No additional product code was changed by this compatibility check.
- Scoped disposition: retain the three documented new-feature P2 limitations for incremental development. This acceptance does not waive required CI/reviews, authorize unrelated existing-feature regressions, or claim unperformed live-action/upgrade proof.

### Accepted new-feature limitations and remaining proof gaps

1. **Delayed-source freshness:** the owner initializes the authority clock when it first captures an identity, rather than its earlier provider observation. An isolated probe against the production owner admitted a finalized caption carrying a ten-minute-old observation timestamp, exposed its source ID, and called a synthetic capable executor. This confirms the admission behavior, not a live browser effect. [Review thread](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152327#discussion_r4087964417).
2. **Source-free authority decision:** `sourceId` is optional, and omitting it skips source freshness and the per-source claim. A second owner-level probe reached the synthetic executor without a source or operator grant. The documented direct-operator path is intentional, but the request contract cannot attest operator origin. This needs a host-bound authorization design or an explicit owner decision, not a silent guard change. [Review thread](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152327#discussion_r4088949374).
3. **Newly identified P2 lifetime source-capacity limit (pre-existing):** after 10,000 distinct observation identities in one session, no new sources are admitted even when all previous live sources have expired or the document epoch changes. A bounded production-owner probe admitted 10,000 identities, retained 1,024 live references, then showed zero live references after expiry and rejection of fresh identities; a new session admitted a source again. No native actions or persistence were used in this probe. This is unchanged from `51b1736e9a1`, affects the new participation source context rather than ordinary transcript ingestion, and is not caused by the parser refresh. It remains open; replay protection was not weakened or retention silently redesigned.
4. **Evidence gaps:** capability-enabled final browser/provider effect proof and existing-state upgrade/rollback qualification remain unverified. Existing real-SQLite persistence/restart/concurrency tests and the synthetic owner probes are not substitutes for those boundaries. Current Google Meet native participation capabilities remain empty, limiting immediate impact but not resolving the shared SDK contract concerns.

The completed, exact-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152327#issuecomment-5738102945) reviewed `31517565ef9` at **2026-09-25 20:19 UTC (revision 14)** and remains **blocked / needs human decision**. It lists the three P2 participation findings above; none is a new parser/registration finding. It also retains the host-bound operator-authority decision and final-effect/existing-state proof gaps. The repeated risk/checklist entries are not eleven independent code defects. **Guarded landing is now authorized by the maintainer after the existing-consumer check; no existing-feature regression or enforced gate is waived.**

title: feat: show favicons and social previews on browser cards
body:
Closes #152310

## What Problem This Solves

Browser-tab cards show only a generic globe and URL when a live screenshot is unavailable, making pages difficult to recognize in chat history.

## User Impact

Public pages now show their favicon and social preview image. Existing live screenshots remain preferred; missing or broken images leave a usable plain card. The existing `gateway.controlUi.automaticallyFetchFavicons: false` setting disables these automatic metadata/image requests too.

Requests are anonymous and Gateway-proxied, with no browser cookies or site credentials. They disclose the public page URL and Gateway address to the destination and its declared image hosts; the operator browser never contacts those hosts directly.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single bounded public-page metadata owner serves browser cards, with strict DNS/redirect checks, validated image bytes, shared requests, and connection-scoped UI caching. Stale replies cannot replace a newly selected page, and failed requests recover on reconnect. No new dependencies or configuration keys. Generic link hovers are a separate follow-up; GitHub custom hovercards are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Anonymous live fetch of the public OpenClaw GitHub repository returned its real favicon and a 640×320 social image.
- Actual Control UI before/after captures inspected in light and dark themes and at a 390px mobile viewport; before/after images also delivered in the originating discussion.
- Focused coverage includes absent/broken images, screenshot precedence, config opt-out, stale replies, same-client reconnect, cache expiry, redirect/SSRF boundaries, document base URLs, bounded bodies, RPC registration, and scopes.
- Implementation validation at ba9bd8d2388141472be30e47bf19765651fa29e5: focused Gateway/UI run: **77 tests passed**. Bundled Chromium E2E: **2 tests passed**, including mobile rendering and the no-metadata fallback. Method registration, scope, and release-train coverage also passed.
- Original-implementation proof: `pnpm build`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, targeted type-aware lint, Lit stylesheet lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Original-implementation AutoReview through P2 is scoped-clean. Its document-base URL finding and the independent reconnect-cache finding were both reproduced, repaired, and re-tested. The final exact-head CI result is recorded below.

### Network and opt-out proof (September 19, 2026)

Ran the real `controlUi.linkPreview` RPC handler and production metadata owner at `515a220e89cdc8c622747044636d8e2d6d0ebebc` with live public requests (no fetch mocks). Undici transport diagnostics recorded request header names and response status codes, without header values or credentials:

Current-node sharing also authorizes retained pre-reset history. Regression coverage checks generation replacement and visibility changes during readiness without dropping valid historical matches.

The candidate also preserves an authoritative empty external-auth discovery result during durable bookkeeping updates, avoiding false invalidation of an admitted model-auth read. Fixes opaque Podman sandbox startup errors when the engine host is missing its container-init executable.

## User Impact

Operators get the correct host-side repair instruction instead of a bare exit-125 error. The setup documentation now names the prerequisite that minimal package installations can omit. **The operator must still install the helper or repair Podman’s configured helper path; this change does not install system packages or relax sandboxing.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Podman resolves its init executable on the engine host, including inside Podman Machine. A sandbox-image installation or a client-side PATH probe is not an adequate substitute. The existing container-command error owner now appends guidance only for Podman create failures matching the two upstream init-dependency errors, preserving the original error, stdout, stderr, and numeric exit code.

body:
Closes #152264

Related: #152322, #152426

## What Problem This Solves

The compact System busyness CPU tile does not distinguish Gateway CPU from whole-host load or show which threads consume it.

## User Impact

Operators can see host utilization beside the unchanged Gateway headline and inspect main-thread, tracked-worker, and estimated other-thread CPU without enlarging the widget. Hover, keyboard focus, and tap reveal the breakdown. Missing counters show a dash, not zero. Bun currently omits unreliable worker counters and their residual; independent host and main-thread readings remain available.

The CI recovery also incorporates the existing retained-asset cleanup repair from #152322. Failed old-file cleanup now warns without discarding a verified published generation; deferred files can temporarily exceed the on-disk budget until later cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use native counters at the existing sampler and worker-lifecycle owners, and reuse the shared tooltip for details. Gateway/thread percentages keep 100% = one logical CPU; Host uses total host capacity. Child processes, remote workers, and container CPU allowances are not silently conflated with those readings. No configuration, persistence, permissions, dependencies, or protocol-version changes.

To resolve the recurring Windows CI failure, this branch adopts @steipete’s existing atomic cleanup-claim repair from #152322 rather than adding retries or weakening assertions. The CPU implementation is unchanged by that repair.

A later main change introduced a separate credential-refresh race in model selection. This candidate integrates the existing repair from #152426; the three CPU/cleanup commits remain patch-identical after rebase. Auth selection retries one typed stale read after joined cleanup, without relaxing account pins, source admission, or cleanup errors.

The Work sessions link below points to that conversation. PR-side image decoding and rendered dimensions were independently checked in the browser.

With the adopted repair in `4bba50067af673f9d82683d71fb80dcec00df862`, all 58 retention tests pass, including native concurrency, cancellation, integrity, and serving-budget coverage. title: improve(ui): apply theme defaults when switching themes
body:
Closes #152229

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing a different Control UI theme currently carries over manual fonts and accent colors instead of applying the theme's complete default look.

## User Impact

Selecting a **different theme** now restores its interface font, chat font, and full light/dark accent palette. You can customize them afterward. Same-theme selections, reloads, reconnects, incoming profile updates, and mode toggles preserve later customizations. Language, text size, chat display, and imported theme definitions remain intact.

This is a deliberate UX change, not a claimed diagnosis of a pre-existing synchronization defect. Existing preferences are not migrated or reset at startup. The new explicit accent value, `theme`, suppresses lower-precedence gateway accent/seam colors without changing other profiles' gateway settings; existing unset and hex values retain their meanings.

### Compatibility

Existing unset and hex accents retain their meaning; upgrades do not migrate saved preferences. Older Control UI readers that do not recognize the profile value `theme` fall back to inherited colors. Before downgrading to a Gateway that only accepts hex values in `ui.prefs.accent`, remove a configured `theme` value or replace it with `#RRGGBB`. No database schema version or preference key is added.

The requesting maintainer accepted this documented downgrade-cleanup tradeoff on September 19, 2026 and authorized guarded landing; compatibility instructions remain applicable. See the original discussion linked under Work sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

A theme selection should apply a coherent design rather than a mixture of old overrides and new defaults. Theme activation and font clears now share the existing preference write path. The explicit theme-accent state leaves the theme's own CSS responsible for its colors in both modes. Imported-theme activation/removal uses the same selection operation, while inactive definition edits preserve customization.

title: fix(ui): keep reopened tooltips visible
body:
Related: #151947 (investigation follow-up; the original CI failure is not proven to share this cause).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes tooltips disappearing after they are reopened before an earlier hide animation finishes, even while their trigger remains focused.

## User Impact

Users can move focus away from and back to a tooltip trigger without leaving its information invisible. Sent-comment previews benefit from the shared repair. Hover, touch reveal, Escape dismissal, and reduced-motion behavior remain supported; no configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Web Awesome tooltip now gives each accepted transition its own lifetime. Superseded or disconnected work cannot publish visibility or completion, animation cleanup finishes before its classes are reused, and interrupted or vetoed public show/hide calls settle. Initial mounting and reconnect use the same current-intent owner.

This extends the existing Web Awesome package patch, including its normal/CDN builds and declarations. It does not add an annotation-specific visibility owner or alter the original selection E2E's waits, timeout, or assertions.

## Evidence

[Matched before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152240#issuecomment-5737402261) show the focused sent-comment chip losing its preview before the repair and retaining it afterward. Both images were also delivered and verified in the originating discussion.

- The hide/reopen regressions fail on the original dependency and pass with this repair, including a verified zero-duration animation case. Additional red/green coverage prevents a reentrant reposition listener from publishing a stale opening completion after hide or disconnect.
- **86 focused tests pass:** 48 tooltip unit tests, 24 native/wrapper tooltip browser tests, and 14 annotation browser tests. They cover public request settlement, vetoes, mounting, disabled state, reconnect, input-trigger precedence, and keyboard/pointer dismissal.
- All **11 unchanged selection E2Es pass**, including desktop/mobile, touch, editing, persistence, and sending. UI production/test typechecks, formatting, and the package-patch guard pass.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable correctness issue.
- The branch incorporates main `95b8e03354505bd05875dd7a94e0f67d6fa528cb`, including the already-landed auth-read and concurrent asset-pruning repairs. Their 34 focused owner tests pass locally; fresh hosted CI is still required for this PR revision.

**Approved size-baseline refresh:** the committed baseline is 363,407 B gzip. The canonical current-base check passes at 363,421 B (a 14 B repeat-build difference within the existing variance allowance), versus 363,276 B on pristine main; raw startup JavaScript is 825 B smaller. The existing **355 KiB committed-baseline cap**, 512 B growth allowance, and 64 B build-variance allowance are unchanged.

**Data compatibility:** `config/control-ui-startup-budget-baseline.json` is repository build/CI budget metadata, not persisted Gateway/user data. Its only reader is `scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts`; the remaining tracked references are CI file-selection rules and tests. title: feat: show mentioned sessions in Involving me
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes sessions staying absent from a mentioned person's **Involving me** sidebar list until they reply or take ownership.

Closes #152072.

## User Impact

A committed explicit @mention brings the accessible session into the recipient's filtered list immediately. **Hide from Involving me** hides it only for that person; a fresh explicit mention brings it back. **All owners → Show in Involving me** restores it manually. Inbox dismissal and expiry do not change this preference, and normal session activity does not undo a hide.

The personal Hide/Show menu entry is visible only when the Gateway reports more than one identity, across sidebar, chat-header, Sessions-page and compact menus.

Access permissions, session membership, shared archive state, authored participation and Git contributor credit are unchanged. No configuration or SQLite schema/version migration is required. Existing transcripts are not scanned for backfill.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session owner now retains private per-profile discovery state separately from contribution history and the temporary Inbox. It survives logical-session reset, relocation and Gateway restart, is removed with the session, and is not inherited by forks. A committed-source watermark prevents old message replay from undoing a hide, including after profile merges and Inbox expiry. Sidebar, chat-header and Sessions management-page menus expose the same personal operation.

The behavior and durability choices were explicitly approved in the linked work session. Older builds do not apply the new filter preference; no existing schema, permission or Inbox-retention contract changes.

title: feat(browser): unify local Chrome setup across desktop and terminal
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chrome setup has separate desktop and terminal entry points that can lose the selected local profile and disagree about installation, approval, and connection readiness.

## User Impact

CLI, TUI, macOS, and the Tauri desktop app share host-local inspect, install, and verify actions. Desktop startup prepares the native helper without opening Store windows; Chrome still owns extension installation and permission approval. Existing pairings, disabled installations, and deliberate opt-out remain intact.

Windows support delegates to the separate compatible `OpenClaw.BrowserBootstrap.exe` owner. Missing/incompatible helpers and uncertain outcomes remain explicit; the CLI cannot silently switch between native Windows and Companion-managed WSL. The separate Windows Companion PR and its live acceptance are not prerequisites for landing this main-repository change, and no completed Windows live acceptance is claimed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser plugin owns setup and readiness. Both desktop adapters use the existing native-device-settings transport, with a shared UI component. The Mac app calls a narrow browser entry point retained in its sealed private runtime; the full CLI and Gateway remain outside that bundle. Tauri uses an isolated version-matched runtime without changing a Gateway service.

The current-main integration preserves installed-versus-enabled Chrome detection, desktop settings revision/FIFO behavior, and the immutable native-host launcher publication/repair owner. Saved browser profile and configuration selections survive repair and supported bundle relocation. Legacy POSIX launchers without a saved selector retain the first configured extension profile; read-only checks reject a different requested profile before relay access. Explicit installation is required to retarget an owned launcher. Canonical setup refuses a different effective state/config selection before installation or relay access; an explicit browser profile does not authorize rebinding the config file. Matching explicit/implicit default paths remain compatible, and the separate manual install/repair contracts are unchanged. The released Mac install request remains supported. Superseded task-publication and transcript-fixture repairs were removed in favor of the owning fixes already on main.

title: feat(ui): add a selectable Carapace theme
body:
Closes #152033

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot select the shared OpenClaw Carapace palette as a built-in Control UI theme.

## User Impact

Choose **Settings → Appearance → Theme → Carapace**, with Light, Dark, or System color mode. Existing defaults, layouts, behavior, and personal font/accent overrides stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a preset through the existing lazy theme loading and profile/config preference contracts, including first paint. It adapts the canonical Carapace v0.6.2 palette: neutral surfaces, coral actions, sea-green accents, and documented system-font fallbacks. Light muted/selected text is adjusted for Control UI contrast guarantees.

No component migration, plugin SDK expansion, new dependency, or new font assets. Those broader efforts are separate from this selectable theme.

title: fix(wear): make long assistant replies fully readable
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long assistant replies ending early on Wear OS when either the eight-line bubble or the phone’s compact transcript preview hides the rest.

## User Impact

User impact: users can open **Read full reply**, scroll through the text, and move between bounded parts without losing the end of the answer. Chat and Talk keep their compact previews and existing input and speech actions. Remote full-text retrieval requires the updated phone companion as well as the updated watch app.

Older peers, unavailable text, changed replies, and replies beyond the supported full-read budget show explicit outcomes rather than presenting an excerpt as complete. Live Chat is labeled as a preview until a stored reply is available. Talk readers close when their source entry changes, so reopening reads the updated answer. Explicit warm Chat or Voice launches dismiss the reader without recreating the conversation or stopping active Talk.

New reader labels currently use the English source-language fallback in the German locale. Existing German translations remain intact; translated artifacts belong to the managed native locale workflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reader uses the existing Wear scrolling and navigation components. Chat reads use the canonical transcript entry through the phone and the existing Gateway visibility checks. Talk retains full text in its active relay owner and derives the compact wire preview from it.

Each part is bound to its source and content revision. Existing wire limits remain unchanged; no persistent transcript storage, credentials, dependencies, or Gateway permission expansion are added. Full reads retain the existing Android one-million-character budget, with explicit unavailability for larger replies.

## Evidence

Verified source head: `f35346eff1512ac3c4262a688549d4c983dac293` (tree `f5c74b74bf78e1940848fb37df00d51fdf22e3b5`).

- Warm-navigation regressions: **3 failed before the production fix, 3 passed afterward**. They cover a stored reader followed by Voice, repeated same-destination Chat requests, cancellation/reopening of an in-flight page, and preservation of active Talk routing.
- Fresh full Wear proof with screenshot capture disabled: **326 passed, zero failures/errors/skips**, including the actual MainActivity repeated-warm-launch/pending-reply test. Wear lint, Kotlin checks, debug APK build, changed-file guards, and diff checks passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the navigation correction found no actionable findings.
- [Current exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35396751961) **passed**, including the required `openclaw/ci-gate`, Wear, Play and third-party phone tests, Kotlin checks, native source localization, and preflight. The exact-head watcher finished GREEN with no pending checks.

<details>
<summary>Earlier feature and correction evidence — previous source heads</summary>

- `:wear:testDebugUnitTest` — **323 passed**; `:wear-shared:testDebugUnitTest` — **13 passed**; `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.wear.*' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatFullMessageOwnershipLayoutTest.wearFullRead*'` — **126 passed**. No failures or skips.
- `:wear:lintDebug`, `:wear-shared:lintDebug`, `:app:lintPlayDebug`, all three modules’ `ktlintCheck`, `:wear:assembleDebug`, and `:wear:assembleDebugAndroidTest` passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`, `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/native-app-i18n.ts verify`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings in the locale-ownership correction after removing test expectations that would prevent future managed translations. Earlier full-text and response-validation reviews remain documented below.
- The hosted Wear lane exposed a test assertion that relied on optional screenshot capture to wait for Compose. The exact assertion now uses `runOnIdle`; the failure was reproduced locally without capture, and all **323 Wear tests** pass with capture disabled. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings in this one-line test correction. Product code, resources and the proof images below are unchanged by that follow-up.
- Normal PR-context changed-scope validation failed before the correction and passed afterward with the guard unchanged. The generated German resource file now has no diff in this source PR; native source verification and eight existing locale-scope guard tests pass.

- Pre-fix regressions demonstrated the missing open action, dropped canonical lookup identity, and lost Talk tail. The corresponding candidate flows reach trailing text beyond the compact preview limits.
- Real production Compose tests exercise open, scroll, next/previous parts, back/swipe, English- and German-locale round layouts, including actual English fallback labels, enlarged fonts, old peers, unavailable replies, stale revisions, and context retirement.
- Phone tests cover the actual projection/RPC/codec boundary; existing isolated Gateway-socket tests verify independent watch selection and physical connection retirement.
- Unicode and escaped-control tests validate actual serialized frames against the existing byte ceiling.
- Full-response validation rejects missing, empty, whitespace-only and non-text-only content as a retryable failure instead of opening a blank reader. Eight invalid-content variants, valid short/Unicode controls, and the actual reader failure/retry flow pass. The unchanged standalone Java probe passes its positive control and rejects all four invalid responses.
- Independent review identified stale live Talk text after finalization. The reader now retires when the owning entry changes, including tail-only changes represented by its producer-owned revision; regression coverage protects both cases.

</details>

Native instrumentation APKs build, but physical-watch and TalkBack/rotary acceptance have not been performed. The task-owned software Wear emulator did not become responsive enough to install the app. The captures below use production Compose under Robolectric, not device acceptance. [Previous CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35385090258) passed preflight, native source localization, and both phone variants, but exposed the Wear test synchronization failure corrected above. [Earlier CI on `e6d5f285455`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35387471046) **passed**, including preflight, native source localization, Play and third-party phone tests, Wear tests, Kotlin checks, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. German-locale proof below reflects the real source-language fallback, not a forced English locale.

### Warm Voice launch with a reader open

Production Compose under Robolectric; identical English, dark, 192dp round fixture at 100% text. Both captures follow the same explicit warm Voice launch, before the regression assertion. No physical-device execution is implied.

| Before: old reader obscures the requested destination | After: Voice controls are visible |

| ![Before warm Voice launch: stale reader remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c981e881-0dfe-4058-9ab8-67f58c2cf085) | ![After warm Voice launch: reader dismissed and Voice visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bdf1290d-041e-4b00-a66b-724b7a3f38c8) |

### Before and after — compact reply

| Before, 192dp | After, 192dp |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: eight-line compact limit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d813dc3-e33d-4225-bb08-38bf4a2e2cd8) | ![After: Read full reply action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8c193c1-c08b-44d5-b4fe-6507bcebc6dc) |

### Retrieved reply ending

title: fix(subagents): unblock launches after late completion delivery
body:
Closes #151948

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes new subagent launches remaining blocked when an expired completion is subsequently delivered to its requester.

## User Impact

A confirmed delivery clears the completion's expired-delivery block and reconciles the durable task and mirrored flow with the actual result. Permanent delivery failures, cancellations, and missing deliverables are not promoted to success.

The existing 50-result admission limit and seven-day retention remain unchanged. No schema or configuration migration is required. This change does not infer delivery, replay, or discard historical suspended results; deployment and any explicitly scoped backlog recovery remain separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing transaction now accepts a positive receipt for an expiry-suspended completion only after its current run, task, generation, and frozen cohort checks. It restores the canonical execution/result verdict rather than unconditionally declaring success, and commits the task, delivery, and wake changes together.

## Evidence

- New real-lifecycle/SQLite regressions: **five failures on the unchanged base, all nine passing with the repair**.
- **86 tests passed across six completion/recovery/pressure files**, covering persisted reload, mirrored flows, missing deliverables, negative receipts, permanent blocks, changed owners/generations, and transaction rollback.

title: fix(wear): preserve update-required diagnosis after refresh
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: refreshing an incompatible Wear connection removes the update-required diagnosis and leaves only a generic offline state.

## User Impact

User impact: the watch keeps the phone's current update guidance after Refresh, while real disconnections and compatible reconnections replace it correctly. No protocol version, storage schema, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Connection events already carry a typed diagnosis, but status snapshots omitted it and the watch discarded the status text. Status and Gateway-control responses now project the phone runtime's current diagnosis; the watch applies the same decoder used for connection events, including the shipped status-only fallback. title: fix: keep Gateway responsive and preserve completions during SQLite contention
body:
Related: #137332. Related prior work: #140956.

Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/b2a27e7d-4225-4ad2-86f8-08f672e48cc8)
- [Continued implementation, verification and landing](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/be0cd141-59c8-452d-84ff-777334d5153f)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway pauses during online archive cleanup and repeated or partially settled requester wakes when SQLite state persistence fails.

## User Impact

Online cleanup no longer waits through the normal five-second SQLite lock timeout. Requester completion bookkeeping commits atomically and retries persistence before permitting another transport attempt, preserving known delivery outcomes and newer requester generations.

Normal write/retirement timeouts, storage schemas, retention settings, and permissions are unchanged. Failed-write outcome custody stays with the live lifecycle owner until SQLite accepts the commit; restart still uses the existing durable attempt and recovery rules. This does not identify the original unowned shared-state reader or make checkpoint disk I/O asynchronous.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use nonblocking admission for optional online checkpoint/vacuum work. Preserve wake object identity on rollback. Compose completion, task, blocked-alert, wake consumption, and retirement mutations in their existing transaction owner with one post-commit publication. Retain failed persistence operations in the lifecycle owner, independently fencing surviving batch members so an unrelated rearm cannot reopen their transport path.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Gateway before/after proof in Crabbox's Blacksmith Testbox, Node 24.19.0, with an external SQLite reader pinned for 6.75 seconds:

  | Measurement | Before | After |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Contended checkpoint | 5006 ms | 0 ms at diagnostic resolution |
  | Largest Gateway main-isolate heartbeat gap | 5055.3 ms | 157.9 ms |
  | Failed health/readiness samples while reader held | 116 / 130 | 0 / 130 |

  The after-proof reached the actual main-thread archive-pruning owner with a cached connection and an incomplete checkpoint. The public visibility write completed in 14 ms and the concurrent follow-on write in 36 ms while the reader remained pinned. Public cleanup, writes, and listing recovered; the transcript hash/canary survived a fresh Gateway process, SQLite quick-check was OK, and foreign-key checks were empty. All four candidate Gateway process groups exited cleanly.
- A second real-Gateway cell injected a SQLite failure at the second member of a canonical synthetic startup-replay batch. Both wakes remained durable during failure; public health completed in 4 ms. The candidate recovered in-process after the fault was released and again through a new-process restart. The baseline also recovered in this cell: it is recovery coverage, not a red baseline and not live model/provider or fresh `sessions_spawn` proof.
- Both checkpoint regressions and all eight initial real-store settlement regressions fail on baseline `b46071e5ec659b5ad0d877d3e3769677cccefd2f`. Candidate scope: 317 requester/settlement tests, 67 reclamation/admission tests, and 27 completion-store tests passed. The two files affected by final fixture/lint cleanup were rerun: 240/240 passed, with assertions retained.
- Full `pnpm build`, targeted lint, and the remaining changed-source guards passed. The original base's whole core-test typecheck stopped on an unchanged duplicate `childList` declaration in a UI test; main already fixes it in #151417. That historical failure is not counted as a pass. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35322856655) subsequently completed successfully on `40080574ae14c7dea5fc6559307bd70eb349c359`, including the full test-type graphs; required `openclaw/ci-gate` passed.
- Independent P0–P2 review was scoped-clean after two sibling-ownership findings were repaired with real-store red/green regressions. A later exact-head CI run exposed a writer winning admission between checkpoint and vacuum; the deterministic real-SQLite regression failed first, then all 74 reclamation/admission/cold-storage tests passed. Only pre-callback lock refusal is deferred; post-entry and non-lock errors still propagate. The final repair received another scoped-clean P0–P2 review. A type-only contract move removed the Madge cycle without changing emitted runtime JavaScript; Kysely guards, core types, and targeted lint passed.
- Integrated final head `40080574ae14c7dea5fc6559307bd70eb349c359` was built and exercised in one serial command, source tree `d620d0fff1aa6e3c1b9691bd2dbe92f32b2f6d3b`. Full `pnpm build` passed in 5m59s and both real-Gateway cells passed with the table above. [Testbox host workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35322911967) identifies the leased host, not PR CI. Raw observations, source/result receipts, canary snapshots, build log and process-cleanup events were checked; the owned lease is stopped.
- The conflict with #151569 is resolved by preserving main's execution-only cancellation classification inside the shared atomic completion mutation. All 108 integrated requester-wake, cancellation-retirement, pressure and restoration regressions passed, as did core types and targeted lint. The fresh integrated build, both live cells, and exact-head hosted CI all passed.
- Final fixture corrections passed 233 registry/restoration tests plus 18 admission tests, with an additional 181-test rerun after extracting the unchanged mock-call helper. Targeted test-type graphs, lint and line-cap guards passed. An independent P0–P2 fixture review found no actionable defects; canonical durable rows and pending obligations replaced incomplete mock-only setup.

<details>
<summary>Scope and review notes</summary>

The agent-database archive-pruning stall and shared-state requester settlement defects are independently demonstrated; this PR does not claim they were one proven production incident. No provider/model inference was needed for the live SQLite responsiveness proof.

Atomic batch composition replaces per-member commit/publication followed by a second wake write. Persistence retries carry the actual failed transition/outcome, not an inferred delivery state. They remain fenced to current rows and generations; absent or superseded ownership is not permission to settle newer work.

Current net change: +399 production lines and +747 test/support lines. Production growth supplies exact-batch transaction composition and retained persistence-outcome custody; the existing block mutation policy is extracted and reused rather than duplicated. No schema, sidecar, fallback store, or parallel transport owner is added.

PR #140956 was inspected as prior art without copying or executing its fork code. Its broader historical queue/orphan reconciliation is not claimed as superseded here.

</details>

title: fix(subagents): settle cancelled wakes and deduplicate backlog warnings
body:
Related: #137332

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated requester-settlement failures after a cancelled child has no captured reply, and repeated backlog warnings when the suspended-delivery count has not changed.

## User Impact

Cancelled child notifications can settle without endlessly reporting that their owner changed. Operators still receive backlog warnings when pressure changes. The 25-warning / 50-admission thresholds, seven-day retention, valid cancellation notifications, and existing retry/dismiss controls are unchanged. No schema or configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A yielded child can be cancelled with a durable execution outcome and matching cancelled task but no captured reply. Rejected delivery settlement incorrectly reused the full task-projection builder, whose capture requirement made that valid pair look stale. The completion owner now classifies terminal execution independently of reply capture; full task finalization keeps its existing capture requirement and settlement keeps its owner/generation checks.

The existing sweeper remembers its last reported suspended count and reports retained pressure after expiry, including failed sweeps. It does not prune results to silence warnings. Pressure coverage shares the existing recovery test fixture rather than growing that suite beyond its line cap.

This is narrower than #140956: it does not introduce atomic queue/wake reconciliation or accept missing historical execution outcomes.

The first required CI run exposed an unrelated baseline failure: messaging had 701 typecheck test roots against the unchanged 700-root guard. This branch reuses @steipete’s exact three-file rebalance from #151564, moving channel tests into the existing plugin-sdk graph without dropping coverage, raising limits, adding jobs, or changing concurrency.

## Evidence

- Production diagnostics identified cancelled tasks with pending delivery and absent reply capture. A supported private SQLite snapshot confirmed the structural state; the snapshot is not published. All suspended deliveries in that snapshot were still inside retention.
- Synthetic real-registry/SQLite restore-and-sweep regressions failed on the original code for both ordinary and yielded cancellation wakes. With the fix, each rejected wake settles once, preserves the cancelled task facts, and permits normal retirement without replaying execution.
- Existing in-process cancellation dispatch and real-store admission/rollback tests passed, preserving legitimate parent notifications and stale-owner refusals.
- Additional tests cover uncaptured failure/timeout outcomes, invalid terminal evidence, pressure escalation, recovery/reset, same-pass expiry, and sweep failures.
- Final focused run: **339 tests passed across 9 files** (real-store admission, requester wakes, cancellation dispatch/retirement, lifecycle, sweeper recovery, and pressure).
- CI repair: reproduced the 701-root failure locally; all 24 existing shard tests and both affected type graphs pass after the rebalance. Independent review of that follow-up is clean through P2.
- Independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Line-cap, formatting, and diff-whitespace checks pass. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed its selected formatting, production/test typechecking, lint, dead-export, storage, and import-cycle gates. The final requester-wake test file also passes targeted lint and formatting. [Required CI run 35319520883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35319520883) passed on exact head `6cac661615f063e39e43de1e3ae6603d78e1114f`. Native review validation and `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 151569` also passed on that head.

This PR does not deploy to or modify the running Gateway's delivery records; post-deployment verification remains separate.

The page mistook an agent-qualified main alias and its canonical `global` spelling for different conversations. title: fix: preserve text-block boundaries in conversation summaries
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes words and role labels running together in conversation-summary input when a message contains multiple independent text blocks.

## User Impact

Future compactions preserve the boundaries between visible blocks instead of feeding merged words to the summarizer. Existing summaries are not rewritten. There are no configuration changes or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction content collector concatenated blocks without a separator. It now joins nonempty visible blocks with a newline while retaining all whitespace inside each block. Empty and omitted blocks do not introduce extra separator-only lines; omission markers remain bounded. Token estimation uses the same representation.

This is reachable through actual MCP projections: embedded resource text and resource links become individual text blocks, and retrieved prompts project their description, role labels, and message content as separate blocks. Dedicated resource-read results remain a single JSON text block and are not the multi-block trigger. The regression test exercises the prompt-shaped case through the real `generateSummary` request construction with an intercepted stream function.

## Evidence

- Before the fix: regression run reported **6 failed / 79 passed**.
- After the fix: compaction and message-conversion suites reported **141 passed across 8 files**, independently rerun with the same result. Coverage includes user/tool-result/custom messages, whitespace preservation, omitted content, separator token accounting, and the actual constructed summarizer request.
- Scoped checks passed through formatting, production and test typechecking, lint, dead-export analysis, and the native schema guard. The aggregate command hit its 600-second deadline during the database-first guard (exit 143); that guard and all six remaining guards were then run individually and each exited 0. This is aggregate scoped evidence, not a claim that one uninterrupted command passed.
- Independent source review found no correctness issues. Required commit-scoped autoreview returned **scoped-clean at its default P0 threshold**, with no accepted findings or suspected credentials. Normal commit hooks passed, and the committed blobs match the tested/reviewed files.
- Proof uses synthetic messages and an intercepted provider stream, not a live provider or live MCP round trip. It confirms this serialization defect, not the root cause of any broader reported spacing incident. Full repository build/test suites were not run; normal GitHub review and CI remain required.


### CI repair — September 20, 2026

Updated the branch with main at `cbd370d7ae8393fd9d85c4a1d1bdcaada7006c5f`, preserving the original two-file patch byte-for-byte. This incorporates the existing upstream repairs for missing full-suite test registrations (#151349) and CI worker-policy assertions (#151427, #151900), rather than duplicating them in this PR.

title: fix(plugins): keep unchanged plugins running across metadata refreshes
body:
Related: #151216

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unrelated plugins and live channel accounts being replaced during an install or reload when equivalent plugin metadata or settings have a different object-key order.

## User Impact

Unchanged plugins keep their registrations, callable methods, and running channel accounts. Actual metadata/configuration changes, ordered-list changes, and explicit reload requests still replace the selected plugin. No configuration migration or permission change is required; the behavior takes effect after updating and restarting into the new code.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retention compared captured JSON strings byte-for-byte. Keep that fast path, then compare the captured JSON values when the strings differ. This preserves JSON omission/null behavior and the immutable registration-time snapshot without treating object insertion order as a runtime change.

This is a reproduced retention defect, not a claim that key ordering was the exact trigger of a historical outage. Pending-cleanup recovery is a separate repair in #151216; this PR does not relax drain/resource ownership or change global model-runtime invalidation.

## Evidence

**Current rebase (September 21):** Head `8f1c88edf33f2f7bff692d798b4bf3358eeb4c3e` is rebased onto `cf5a64e7a65c72f22bd964a5eb49ef425fa92841`. The only conflict was documentation; current workspace-provenance, retained-work admission, cleanup, and live-channel custody architecture is preserved. No production design change was added. Fresh P0–P2 review is scoped-clean and canonical changed-file checks passed, including core/test types and type-aware lint. The prior inventory failure is repaired upstream by #151349; the current inventory suite passes all 348 cases. Four semantic-retention cases and eight metadata/recovery/ownership sibling cases pass. Against current-main production code, the manifest/config ordering regressions fail while the install-record/entry-policy controls pass. Full `pnpm build` passed in 4m 12s; an earlier attempt was invalidated by a newly created local proof JSON path changing the compiler namespace, then passed with topology held stable.

**Current validation gap:** The real Gateway test now fails before the metadata-ordering step: `config.patch` is rejected because the selected plugin still has active retained work. The same failure reproduces with current-main production code and its unchanged Gateway test. Two unchanged webhook siblings also encounter this environment’s loopback HTTP 502 restriction. No lifecycle guard, assertion, or network safeguard was weakened. Hosted [CI 35577336745](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35577336745) nevertheless passed on this exact head: 142 successful jobs, 16 skipped, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. All three Gateway channel tests and all four semantic-retention cases passed in their normal hosted shards. The local retained-work failure remains a documented environment/order-sensitive gap, not a claimed product fix. Current-head Package Acceptance completed successfully, including package integrity, npm 12 installer acceptance, the published-updater cell, and its final aggregate. Results below for the previous head remain historical, not current-head proof. Separate Security Review resolver runs failed before review with GitHub installation API rate-limit HTTP 403; no code finding was produced and no blind rerun was requested.

**Measured local cost:** `pnpm test src/plugins/loader.semantic-retention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21.10 s wall including compiler preparation, 2.06 s tests. The modified Gateway file: 28.93 s wall / 27.31 s Vitest duration (failed as described); the unchanged-main fixture on the same repaired loader: 31.60 s wall / 29.88 s Vitest duration, with the same failures. Hosted changed-test execution: semantic-retention 2.673 s total; Gateway channel cases 8.622 s total (the changed case 5.180 s), without retries. This extends an existing real-Gateway fixture rather than adding another boot or E2E file; its watcher/ledger/channel-account identity contract cannot be proven by the cheaper loader checks alone.

**Current-head update qualification:** [Package Acceptance 35577371490](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35577371490) passed the published `openclaw@2026.9.4` → this exact candidate `custom-plugin-siblings` cell in 171 seconds, one attempt, zero retries. The original published updater reported success; captured post-core child exit was 0. Six actual canary plugin executions and post-update runtime loading passed, with original sibling source files preserved. Tarball SHA-256: `4a072e2cc7288f5907f93155407a8660fd4d0e997dd2b576565b2bba38594b62`; immutable producer artifact `10629765471`, attempt 1. This is the canonical sibling-plugin upgrade contract, not a rerun of the historical configured-channel response extension or updater-managed service restart/downtime proof.

<details>
<summary>Historical proof for the previous head (not requalification of this rebase)</summary>

- Red/green real-loader proof: unchanged manifest and nested-settings key reordering rejected retention before the fix; repaired preflight and executable replacement preserve the same callable registration. Installation/entry-policy controls, ordered-setting changes, changed manifest values, and explicit replacement remain covered.
- **52 relevant tests passed**: 10 semantic/persisted-metadata/recovery loader cases, 33 registry-ownership cases, all eight installed-package recovery cases, and the real Gateway regression below.

- Core production and all core test typechecks passed. After two mechanical test-lint corrections, the affected test graph and type-aware lint passed again; all remaining selected architecture/state/security guards passed. Formatting and whitespace checks passed.

**CI fixture correction (`0cf13474eb25e46821dc8d7b7bcc215903629705`):** The original hosted failure was in this PR’s new real-Gateway test, not the retention comparison: the explicit reload raced the watcher’s still-owned lifecycle lease after its new registration became callable. The probe now waits for the existing real reload-settlement signal before checking bindings or issuing its one-shot reload. No production guards, timeouts, or assertions were weakened. The revised regression passes the repaired loader and fails the original loader at the changed sibling instance. Fresh P0–P2 autoreview and all canonical changed-file checks passed. The captured 35-file group also passed this regression and all eight installed-package cases locally; its full run was stopped after unrelated loopback HTTP requests received host-proxy 502 responses.
