The cell passed in 226 seconds with one attempt and no retries. The original published updater reported exit 0 / success / repair false; captured post-core exit was 0. A preconfigured synthetic channel produced distinct nonce-bound replies before and after update, advanced its socket generation from 1 to 2, and preserved the same native session with both conversation markers. Strict projected configuration/plugin/source preservation and both stages’ CLI opt-out readbacks passed. Installed build identity matched the candidate commit.

**Historical CI blocker (fixed upstream):** [CI 35302636644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35302636644) completed with 137 successful jobs, 16 unselected/skipped jobs, and the test-inventory check plus its aggregate gate failing. `test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts` reports two unowned tests added on the newer main merge context by #151001: `run-attempt.native-config.test.ts` and `run-attempt.subscription.test.ts`. title: fix(sessions): omit nested tool results from filtered history
body:
Closes #162891

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes nested tool-result cards appearing in `sessions_history` when tool output is explicitly excluded or omitted by default.

## User Impact

Conversation recall no longer spends its bounded history window on nested tool-result cards when `includeTools` is false. Explicit tool inclusion, unrelated custom messages, assistant tool-call blocks, embedded prose, and pagination retain their existing contracts. No permission, schema, storage, or visibility-policy change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Public history projects nested activity as a custom-role card, but the shared filter recognized only top-level tool roles. Reuse the nested-activity owner’s existing type constant in that shared filter instead of adding a history-only workaround or a generic visibility filter. History, list enrichment, run-wait, and subagent logs consume the same classification.

The existing history-pagination case now checks omitted/false/true inclusion, both conventional tool roles, a display-enabled nested card, and preserved non-tool forms. There is no additional test boot or new test case.

## Evidence

- Actual pre-fix native history output exposed the nested card; private transcript contents are not published.
- Before the fix, a production shared-filter assertion failed with one nested card instead of zero. Afterward, the shared-filter smoke passed for stored/projected activity, retained forms, and nonmutation (1.14 s).
- The production history tool executed against synthetic Gateway responses successfully. Parent independently repeated the case with `display: true`: default/false exclusion, true inclusion, pagination, preserved other forms and nonmutation passed in 7.81 s. title: fix(ui): queued prompts stall after reconnect until page refresh

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI prompts can stay queued while the agent is idle when reconnect overtakes an in-progress send preparation, until the page is refreshed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes typing going into the chat draft instead of filtering models after opening the model picker.

## User Impact

Users can open the model picker in Chat or New Session and type to search without changing their unsent message. Keyboard opening, reopening, and Escape dismissal keep their expected focus behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker focused its trigger but never transferred focus to the search input, so the composer's printable-key handler took over. The picker now performs the handoff after its anchored popup opens. title: fix(webchat): keep saved replies visible during history refresh
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved background reply can remain missing, or disappear after appearing, when its WebChat transcript update races an older history request.

## User Impact

User impact: completed results remain visible without asking the agent to repeat them or manually reloading the conversation. No configuration, storage schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A transcript commit must invalidate a history read that began before it. Previously, idle panes could reuse the stale read without fetching the new result, while an active pane could admit the reply and then lose it when that stale snapshot advanced its transcript leaf.

The event handler now retires the older read before run settlement and uses the existing history loader's single queued refresh. Identity-only transcript invalidations use the same refresh contract. Session/connection fencing, branch replacement, message identity, and ordinary final delivery remain unchanged; there is no new retry loop or cache.

Contributor credit: Vito reported the missing final result and requested this repair.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/09225428-6e0e-4e76-923a-ad7dfc41ab0a)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/1595be28-33d9-4e11-8347-76e7d1f93a56)

## Evidence

- All four mounted-pane regression cases fail on the original production code with an empty conversation result, then pass with the repair: late background reply, identity-only invalidation, active reply followed by an older leaf snapshot, and a reply whose event observes run settlement. The active cases first verify that the live report was actually admitted before the stale read resolves. Each case verifies one fresh read and one reply after reload.
- **151 focused and sibling tests passed across seven files**, including ordinary final/abort handling, in-flight history, cursor replay, retired-session fencing, successor-session isolation, and shared pane events.
- UI production typechecking, all UI test-type shards, changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh AutoReview is scoped-clean through P2. An independent source review identified both history races before the final repair.
- Actual Chromium with the real Control UI and synthetic Gateway events reproduced **zero visible replies / one history read before**, and **one visible reply / two history reads after**. Sanitized before/after captures are shown below.

### CI follow-up

The first ready-PR CI run failed `checks-ui (1/3)` at `chat-state.test.ts:2637`: an older peer-message test still expected the superseded history request to be the only read. The same case failed deterministically in the CI UI configuration with three workers. This was a stale test expectation, not a transient runner failure.

The follow-up changes tests only: separate stale/fresh snapshots, three peer commits sharing exactly one successor read (two total RPCs), unchanged one-frame/canonical-message assertions, and an awaited history owner instead of polling. **302 selected tests passed across eight files** in the CI UI configuration with three workers. The corrected `chat-state.test.ts` also passed all 151 cases with one worker (**3.63 seconds wall**); UI test types, lint, formatting, and fresh AutoReview through P2 passed. Exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper readiness remain required.

title: fix: preserve parent wakes when sibling completions race
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: parent sessions can lose their child-completion wake when two siblings try to defer or settle the same result batch at the same time.

## User Impact

User impact: concurrent child completions share one batch decision instead of competing for its pending persistence operation. A stale reader does not block a healthy sibling from continuing.

No configuration, schema, retry-budget, or permission changes. This does not restart a Gateway or replay results lost by an older build.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing exclusive batch guard covered final delivery but not earlier deferral and no-delivery settlement writes. Both sibling callbacks could enter those writes and replace the current commit owner.

Use that same guard for every prepared batch decision. Read-only preparation remains independent; ownership is acquired only before a mutation or delivery and released in the existing finalizer. The existing batch-state module now holds the claim and its Gateway-lifetime check.

The separate ended-requester authority failure found during investigation is already fixed by #162299 and is not duplicated here.

title: feat: retain required results without model polling
body:
Related: #143701. Follow-up to #162303, which repairs collection guidance rather than enforcing collection.

## What Problem This Solves

Agents can return an answer while a needed command result remains uncollected, or spend repeated model turns polling a still-pending tool or collector.

## User Impact

`required: true` lets a caller make command or collector results a runtime-owned prerequisite for finishing the call. Required Code Mode work stays active and resumes from completion events without model polling or replaying completed actions. Explicitly detached servers keep their current behavior, including `notifyOnExit=false`.

This is opt-in at call admission, not semantic judgment of a plan or retroactive tracking of previously detached handles. Ordinary announcing children keep their existing `sessions_yield` protocol. Required calls occupy their existing execution capacity; Stop, source replacement, and run/tool/process deadlines still apply. Only off-VM tool waiting pauses the Code Mode execution allowance; computation, checkpoint/restore work, and guest timers remain charged. No new configuration, persisted schema, retention policy, scheduler, or notification setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep required work at its existing producer and pending-call owner instead of adding a competing task ledger or blocking a native Stop hook. Shell exec collects its terminal result; collector waits join all requested authorized results through registry events; Code Mode retains the exact continuation and its unused execution allowance. A normal final cannot bypass the still-pending call.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI run 36865914071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36865914071) passed; both required `openclaw/ci-gate` entries were green. [ClawSweeper’s completed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162707#issuecomment-5932188463) pins `e722df18cf1508ce7ec437b9ad9617f6a337973c` and reports no findings, security concerns, or before-merge items. Verification completed at 13:19 UTC; @VACInc merged the PR at 13:58:50 UTC on October 1, 2026.
- Initial registered-exec/AgentSession reproduction on pinned base `4d199b32c789175c20d3123449dcae93c52f8e85`: the required-result case failed because finalization completed while the process remained pending; the detached control passed. The repair moves enforcement earlier, to the pending execution owner.
- 84 focused tests passed across the execution boundary, collector ownership/replacement, Code Mode waiting, existing headless budgets, detached-process cancellation, and native dynamic-tool suites. The extracted boundary and required-collector files were rerun after the mechanical helper/test split.
- A simulated 60-second wait produces **zero additional model requests**. Completion supplies the result to the existing continuation exactly once. Two simulated minute-long tool waits preserve the original guest allowance (`1000 → 900 → 800 ms` with controlled execution costs), not fresh slices. Failure, cancellation, replacement, guest-timer exhaustion, explicit-yield refusal, and detached controls are covered.
- Native parity is an app-server boundary fixture with the real OpenClaw exec producer and host capability, a controlled process supervisor, and one pending native tool request. title: fix: chats fail to open when session metadata changes during approval replay

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chats failing to open with “session approval replay unavailable” when ordinary session activity or label metadata changes while pending approvals are loading.

## User Impact

Users can open active conversations without harmless metadata updates canceling their message subscription. Real access revocations, session replacement, and approval-replay failures still reject the subscription. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The subscription retained a full metadata snapshot across the asynchronous approval read. Updating a label, token count, or activity timestamp therefore looked like losing access. That error was wrapped as an unavailable approval replay and promoted to a chat error by the Control UI.

Reuse the existing access-only retained-read option already used by branch listing. Session identity, lifecycle, creator, visibility, incognito, physical-store, and live-requester checks remain in place; this does not suppress errors, remove approvals, or add retries.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the exact error through `handleGatewayRequest` with real isolated session storage and approval replay. Before the fix, both ordinary and scoped readers failed when activity/label metadata changed during replay; unchanged sessions succeeded.
- After the fix, both reader cases pass all six scenarios: unchanged metadata, activity/label updates, visibility revocation, session replacement, lifecycle replacement, and incognito changes. Rejected subscriptions retain no observers.
- **13 focused tests pass** across the new regression and the existing approval opt-in, display-row wait, and concurrent-replay suites.

title: fix: follow-up messages miss steering while a reply prepares
body:
Related: #161045. Complements #161046's downstream preflight path; this fixes explicit Gateway `chat.send` admission.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes follow-up messages waiting for separate answers when Send arrives while an existing reply is preparing its backend.

## User Impact

The follow-up is acknowledged promptly and can join the same reply once its backend is ready. Queue modes, cancellation, permissions, media checks, and genuine-rejection fallback remain intact. No configuration or schema migration is required.

Only an existing reply owner is eligible. Requests arriving before any reply owner exists retain their current behavior; the fix never discovers an arbitrary future owner or redirects steering to a replacement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway previously recorded explicit steering as rejected even when preparation prevented any injection attempt. The existing reply-operation owner now publishes its first running backend (or retirement), and Gateway admission can retain that exact owner across readiness. Waiting happens after the ACK; injection reuses the existing authority, transcript-custody, and terminal-receipt checks. A changed owner, key, or ready backend cannot inherit the input. Legitimate same-owner compaction lineage remains supported.

title: refactor(sessions): unify in-memory turn, queue, and stop ownership
body:
Related: #160737

## What Problem This Solves

Session turns, queued inputs, cancellation and mutations rely on overlapping owners, making it difficult to keep stale callbacks and unfinished cleanup from interfering with the next turn.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is consistent ordering and cancellation across channel, Gateway, native and scheduled work, with successors and mutations waiting for the correct outstanding work to settle.

**Draft for design/code review, not merge-ready.** Full latest-source reply E2E and some isolated integration proof remain incomplete. This is a broad in-memory ownership cutover, not a claim of measured performance or maintenance-time improvement.

**No SQLite schema change:** no tables/columns, schema-version bump or migration; no durable mailbox is introduced. Existing persisted write/delete formats remain, but their admission and cleanup ordering change, including session deletion, maintenance preservation, startup orphan checks and delivery enqueue admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing reply-operation owner into a physical-session controller rather than add another scheduler:

- One mailbox/selector for queued inputs and native work; adapters retain authorization, routing, batching and delivery policy.
- Exact store/incarnation, operation, source and backend-attempt identities for late callbacks, steering and cancellation.
- Shared Stop and mutation coordination; an abort or terminal outcome is not proof of raw writer/source settlement.
- Controller-owned progress/watchdog state; global capacity and database write fences remain separate owners.

The goal is correctness and maintainability, not a net line reduction. The implementation is larger and still uses imperative mailbox/lifecycle/Stop modules around a narrower pure phase/outcome reducer.

### Umbrella issue coverage

“Addressed” below means implementation is present in this draft, not that each issue's full acceptance criteria are complete. No issue is auto-closed.

| Issue | Coverage in this draft | Remaining qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Related: #160738 — statechart, invariants and model tests | **Partial:** controller documentation, pure phase/outcome reducer and seeded models driving real boundaries | Not the proposed complete pure controller transition/effect model; full shared acceptance and cost accounting remain open |
| Related: #160739 — busy state and run ownership | Canonical controller ownership and attached native attempts replace independent turn ownership | Distinct busy/admissible/injectable/settled projections remain intentional; cross-surface acceptance pending |
| Related: #160740 — queueing and steering | Canonical mailbox, interrupt priority, collect/source custody and shared admission; old queue/adoption owners retired | Full current reply/channel E2E pending; guarded steering during compaction preserves supported runtime behavior rather than blanket rejection |
| Related: #160741 — Gateway chat.send and agent RPC | Shared input/turn admission; RPC source correlation replaces Gateway-owned queue/abort decisions | Complete mixed-surface, UI and restart acceptance not claimed |
| Related: #160742 — Stop entry points | Common captured-target cancellation with retained cleanup and source-specific scope | Preserve legitimate source-specific effects/hooks; complete entry-point QA pending |
| Related: #160743 — mutations and per-session lanes | Reset/delete/compaction coordination through controller; per-session turn lanes retired | Global capacity, persisted fences and subordinate physical-effect custody remain; isolated integration proof pending |
| Related: #160744 — watchdog | Operation-owned progress/deadlines/recovery, without session-lane reset as recovery | Cancellation timeout cannot declare abort-insensitive work settled; complete issue-level acceptance remains open |

**Not addressed:** #160745, the separately reviewed durable mailbox / restart-persistence stage. No SQLite schema work is included.

## Evidence

Current focused evidence after pre-publication review corrections:

- Required independent review completed all **11 passes**. Its **7 findings were reproduced in 12 failing boundary cases**, then corrected; this is a reconciled review, not a claim of a clean pre-fix verdict.
- **92 passing cases across 9 complete owning test files**, combining applicable receipts without double-counting. Coverage includes exact-input admission, physical-store dedupe, incarnation-scoped mutation, retry custody, deadlines, RPC execution projection, bounded lifecycle responses and seeded models.
- Representative measured runner durations: archive lifecycle **18 cases / 20.59 s**; queue dedupe **16 / 3.15 s**; native lane controller **7 / 3.80 s**. The final lifecycle-only rerun was **11 / 42.45 s**, with 97% attributed to cold worker transformation, not sleeps; these tests exercise the real ownership boundary with deferred work/fake clocks.
- Production core types and all **26 affected canonical test graphs passed**; final local context-reuse cleanup received another core/owner-graph refresh. Scoped production/test lint, formatting, source line caps, assertion safety, import cycles, whitespace and all three native Knip scans passed (zero Knip entries).
- Earlier broad-candidate proof included a normal full package build (**318.67 s**) and **35 type execution graphs (322.41 s)**. That build preceded the final review corrections; it is not presented as a rebuilt final-head artifact.

**Known gaps / failures:**

title: fix(ui): keep chat and drafts usable when connections fail
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: slow or interrupted connections replace usable chat and visualizations with errors, strand message delivery, and prevent previously signed-in users from reopening their work offline.

## User Impact

Users can keep reading cached conversations, editing text and attachment drafts, and queuing messages after a connection loss or an offline reload. Recovery appears in the existing bottom-left connection indicator, not a second chat banner. Loaded widgets retain their local interaction state.

Offline reload requires a prepared browser cache and an explicit browser-offline signal. Server actions and uncached external resources still require a connection. Previously signed-in proxy, Tailscale, and password users gain local access without storing their password or new bearer credentials; sending waits for account revalidation. People with access to the browser profile can read retained local data.

**Migration:** the derived transcript cache moves from IndexedDB version 3 to 4; unscoped old history is discarded and refilled online rather than assigned to another account. Unsent legacy drafts and queues remain available for explicit recovery, never automatic reassignment or sending. Retention limits remain unchanged; rollback does not turn account-qualified input back into an unowned queue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep presentation alive independently of connection authority. Retry transient reads within their existing recovery windows, reconcile uncertain writes using the original message ID, and scope local work to its Gateway/account. Same-client account replacement, stale handoffs, cross-tab retirement, and explicit credential-forget cannot transfer another account’s input. The service worker prepares only integrity-bound build assets and a generic shell, retains native online HTTP-auth navigation, and resumes interrupted preparation without holding updates indefinitely.

The offline-access and account-isolation contract was explicitly accepted by @steipete in the linked work session.

## Evidence

- **Full UI inventory exercised: 1,605/1,605 files**, once each, on the checksum-pinned CI Bun runtime. The run recorded 23,795 passing tests, five stale retention assertions in one fixture, and one existing opt-in skip. The five assertions were corrected without changing production code; the corrected fixture and boot-owner siblings then passed **63/63 tests** with zero lint warnings/errors. The original full run is retained as-is, not relabeled green.
- **Final isolated browser suite: 133/133 tests across all 17 files passed**, with no skips. This includes real-Gateway Inspector pairing, offline/recovery fences, account-scoped drafts and attachments, queued delivery, loading deadlines, navigation, widgets, and reconnect reconciliation. Official Playwright 1.63 image; one worker; owned container positively removed.
- **Fresh production build and unchanged performance budgets passed.** Latest rebuilt startup JS: 372,295 B gzip, 52 B below the enforcement limit. Startup CSS: 50,705 B, 495 B below its hard ceiling; the existing advisory warning remains. Chat/New boot use 32/27 requests, below 35. No budget or baseline relaxed.
- **Production Chromium/SW proof passed all eight account/offline stages and four native HTTP Basic proxy stages**, with zero page errors. Offline navigation came from the service worker while a network probe failed. Original-account retention, different account/Gateway fencing, return to the original account, and “Forget this browser” were exercised. Proxy proof observed 17 native challenges and 113 authenticated asset requests.
- Production UI types and all five canonical UI test type graphs passed, with scoped typed lint, formatting, line-count and assertion-safety ratchets. All tracked source, dependency and runtime fingerprints stayed unchanged during final browser/build proof. The account/proxy proof used build 2026.9.7-64b426373e23-2026-10-01T21-06-21.168Z; build/performance checks also passed after the private-export cleanup at 53ed9b1.
- Independent review findings were reproduced and repaired. The final automated routing warning was rejected after inspecting the sole production getter and router call chain: offline defaults are null while connected, scoped to the current account/Gateway, and refreshed by live discovery; focused runtime-owner tests passed. No unresolved actionable P0–P2 finding remains. **Hosted exact-head CI/review gates are still separate requirements; local proof is not a hosted-CI or merge claim.**

- **Hosted dependency failure repaired:** the obsolete global roster-generation export is now private, its test observes the existing account-scoped getter, and an unused legacy test helper was removed. Both complete Knip scans, 44 focused tests, affected production/test type graphs and typed lint pass. No dead-code suppression or production behavior change.
- **All eight cases in four additional browser files pass in scoped runs.** Speech hydration now inspects the authenticated snapshot key; elapsed-time proof advances heartbeat callbacks chronologically and verifies one connection/send; catalog readiness keeps the same enabled-control assertion. Worker-update tests use the exact staged build-plus-digest cache, real install gate and generic shell. Instrumented reproduction established that network-isolated Chromium reported offline despite reachable loopback; a native online-state precondition preserves network isolation. The final diagnostic-free worker suite passed 4/4 in 38.96 seconds, with all draft, activation, asset-SHA and exact-one terminal-attach checks intact. No timing budgets or skips changed; WebKit was not run.

### Integration and recovery repairs

Actual conflicts with main were resolved while retaining live-only agent discovery, warm pre-hello routing, history supersession, and Mermaid 12 worker handling. Existing landed CI prerequisites remain integrated unchanged. No main refresh was performed merely to chase branch movement.

- Valid credential non-admission no longer deletes another document’s boot record. Explicit retirement, failed publication, and cross-tab cache cleanup affect only their captured owner; shellless sign-in/approval documents cannot retire an authenticated Chat tab.
- Legacy recovery uses verified inactive, account-bound staging before publishing a destination. Throwing/silent/commit-then-throw failures, source resurrection, reopened storage, different-destination retries and Blob custody are covered. Required recovery writes reject before mutation if bounded retention would drop the destination or existing unsent input; ordinary cache retention is unchanged.
- Memory-only, unconfirmed input survives A→B→A under its original opaque owner without exposing it to B or reviving stale send authority. Peer durable edits supersede dormant copies; returning in-flight input remains held for explicit action.
- All chat sends share a finite acknowledgment deadline. A real browser-client wire test keeps heartbeats healthy while withholding an approval-command ACK: at 30 seconds it restores original text/attachment bytes, reports delivery unconfirmed, preserves the active run, ignores a late ACK, and sends nothing again on reconnect.
- Production asset admission uses the canonical route selector rather than counting mutually exclusive preload templates together. Limits and integrity checks remain unchanged; type-only outbox dependencies use existing leaf owners without an import cycle.

title: fix(chat): prevent jumps to latest after viewport resizing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the chat transcript can jump back to the latest message when the reader has moved away and a temporary viewport resize settles.

## User Impact

Readers keep their position through resize and later message growth instead of being pulled 100 pixels downward. Instant and smooth “latest” scrolling still reach their destination. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing scroll-command owner now retires a completed end request on arrival, including no-op requests that produce no native scroll event. Delayed idle can no longer turn a resize-clamped reader position into permission to follow. In-flight smooth scrolling must reach the exact endpoint; the existing one-pixel idle rounding tolerance remains.

## Evidence

- All four new browser regressions fail against the original production source (expected offset 860, actual 960) and pass with this repair. The original 17 browser assertions remain unchanged.
- 21 browser tests and 115 related unit tests pass, covering auto/smooth requests, no-op/real journeys, reader takeover, measurement growth, restoration, and prepend ownership. The final browser file took 8.58 seconds wall time with `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-end-follow.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (5.724 seconds in its 21 cases; the four new cases total 2.30 seconds). The browser-plus-60-unit command took 11.45 seconds; the remaining 48 unit cases took 6.59 seconds. The seven continuity cases also pass on Node (3.37 seconds wall) and stock Bun 1.4.2 using the CI UI configuration (12.16 seconds wall). That local Bun run was not the checksum-pinned CI fork (steipete/bun 6b9148b17a6df4d02776fbf4aeb0c874e2ff955a); it is additional cross-runtime evidence, not an exact CI-runtime replay.
- Independent P2 review: no actionable findings. All 21 scoped static components passed for the production repair, and all 19 selected components passed for the sibling-fixture correction. This includes types, lint, dead exports, and ratchets.
- Local runtime: Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.5.1, Vitest 5.0.1, Playwright 1.63.0, Chromium 1243. The original Node 24 full browser run was not replayed; this is focused causal proof, not a full CI-green claim.

The first [hosted attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36817615812) at `d88cd65` failed three sibling-fixture assertions that expected the old single smooth-scroll call. The corrected head awaits its enforced CI; canceled lanes from the first attempt are not passing evidence. No workflow rerun was requested.

The same production transcript controller, layout, and styles with synthetic deployment notes in a dark 800-pixel-wide fixture. After the same resize/idle sequence, the original source jumps to offset 960; the repair preserves offset 860. This is component proof, not a live Gateway capture.

title: fix: source publication fails after inheriting target workflows
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: source-only GitHub publication is rejected after a branch incorporates unchanged GitHub Actions updates from its authenticated target branch.

## User Impact

Session-scoped and scheduled publishers can catch up with target workflows without gaining full operator write authority. New workflow edits and conflicting resolutions still require a maintainer.

Repository-only checkpoints deliberately remain conservative when the source base has diverged or earlier copied workflow contents lack merge ancestry. No permission grants, identity selection, persistence schema, or configuration change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous two-way check confused target-main updates with author-created changes. One shared policy now compares exact workflow paths, modes, blobs, and absence against the published head and authenticated target ancestry. Current-authority checks, remote-head leases, and recovery behavior stay intact.

title: fix(ui): keep reply attribution above same-turn tool activity
body:
Related: #150549, #160612

## What Problem This Solves

Same-run tool activity can appear above the **Replying to** strip when a history window omits the prompt or completed work spans an automatic resumption.

## User Impact

The reply line heads its completed work and answer, including the existing agent/participant avatars and connector. The strip, typography, colors, spacing tokens and footer styling are unchanged; there are no CSS changes.

Execution IDs remain unchanged. Peer inputs, forwarded sources, system markers and steers still separate presentation segments. Live mixed-run activity remains its existing separate log rather than being assigned to an arbitrary reply. No protocol, configuration, storage or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completed-work projector already knows which terminal reply owns a rollup but discarded that presentation fact. The frame builder then required uniform nested run IDs and a loaded prompt boundary, leaving work outside its reply frame.

Carry the selected reply’s display ownership through that handoff, and use a frame-local identity for a known run whose prompt is outside the loaded window. Recovered failures stay visible in work without poisoning the later successful reply’s outcome. Forwarded work cannot borrow local framing even when its execution ID matches.

## Evidence

- The actual `buildChatItems → projectTranscriptChain` path and production-bundle browser scenario fail on original base `80680fb3428a5d06bbccafaccaaade703da651ef` and pass with this repair. The retained projection matrix also catches a deliberately reintroduced forwarded-boundary defect.

Shared extraction/setup and dashboard/channel lifecycle cases are consolidated; one lower-level projected-source row is removed in favor of its stronger real-builder matrix. Distinct promptless-run, stream-boundary, notice, recovery, navigation and visual-interaction coverage remains. Final PR delta: production **+47 net**, tests **+434 net**.

title: feat: choose when sessions can send and receive messages
body:
## What Problem This Solves

People need per-session control over messages to and from other sessions without expanding an already busy menu.

## User Impact

**Session settings** contains appearance, assignment, and separate **Always / Ask / Never** choices for sending and receiving. It is a submenu, not a side panel. Both defaults remain **Always**, configurable through `session.communication.send` and `session.communication.receive`.

Existing tool, privacy, sandbox, and sharing restrictions still apply. Ask requires a live authorized human decision. Changes govern new peer admissions; already accepted work keeps its completion contract. Older versions do not enforce these preferences.

**Landing status:** **merged into main** at `550fc182c1dacdf0f23dafb333cc52a7df14de43` on October 10, 2026, 09:44 UTC, from reviewed head `ab596f29367e1bcfc542fa747655033b22a64c00`. Exact-head ClawSweeper completed with no actionable findings. Native inherited-failure admission verified current security and review policy and the executing writer’s CI-only bypass authority; the failed CI attempt remains explicitly recorded below. The native receipt and cleanup are complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

One admission path checks the sender and recipient, binds exact messages across approval waits, and uses the existing delivery/completion owners. New children inherit preferences; adopting an existing session cannot overwrite its protected policy. Shared menu and creation helpers were consolidated rather than adding parallel state or lifecycle managers.

## Evidence

Earlier focused proof, retained for unchanged contracts:

- **78 runtime tests passed**, including real queue/transcript custody, pre-enqueue revocation, task continuation, and accepted replies.
- **209 metadata, model, reset/recovery, protocol, and UI tests passed** after cleanup. Public router/SQLite adoption regression was demonstrated red before the fix and green afterward; the five-case authority/reset/reopen suite also passed after typed fixture cleanup.
- Real human-question, hosted-caller, and worker-family checks passed. Actual-app UI capture verified sparse directional mutations with `expectedSessionId` and mobile Back navigation.
- Production/UI and 27 core-test type graphs, scoped lint, format, config/protocol generation, size ratchets, import and storage/auth guards passed. Independent final P0/P1 review found no actionable defects. Full-suite and live-provider execution are not claimed.

### Retained integrated-candidate proof (`7b9a517`)

- **210 tests passed across 17 files**: seven public-router/SQLite creation, authority, reset/reopen, and sparse compatibility cases; 203 row/event/schema, promotion, shared-menu, and archive-tree/lifetime regressions.
- **Eight type graphs passed** (production core/UI plus Gateway and UI test graphs), along with config documentation generation/check, formatting, diff checks, and the line-cap ratchet.
- Independent complete-candidate P0/P1 AutoReview was scoped-clean. Main conflict resolution retains child promotion, `sidebarRoot`, independent grouping, and archive-tree behavior alongside the settings submenu.
- Compatibility proof starts with stored metadata lacking `communication`, verifies Always/Always and configured defaults without storage backfill, patches Send alone, and retires/reopens the real SQLite fixture before checking preserved sparse policy and unrelated fields. This is pre-feature metadata compatibility, not a claim of running an entire stable-release binary upgrade.

### CI integration repair proof (`c3ba87b`)

The first published-candidate run exposed incomplete fixture and dependency migrations. This candidate includes the protocol leaf in the native wrapper inventory, regenerates the two new config-tier snapshot entries, removes the two type-import cycles, and updates existing browser/send consumers without weakening their assertions or runtime gates. Canonical main aliases now bind the same sender/recipient identity that admission approves. Target incarnation and result ownership remain separate; the Cron fixture explicitly owns completion instead of leaking a detached reply into its worker-placement assertion.

- Wrapper extraction **2 passed**; config-tier **18 passed**; full Madge import graph **0 cycles**.
- Existing send **33 passed**; runtime sibling **57 passed**; real Gateway authority **15 passed**; human-question **7 passed**. The original seven-file Cron cohort is **161/161** after the completion-owner correction.
- Shared menus **58 passed**; people/sidebar **76 passed**; appearance/terminal/operator-scope E2E **10 passed**; assignment/companion/mobile E2E **39 passed**. Existing screenshots remain representative: production rendering is unchanged by these repairs.
- Production core/UI and affected agent, Gateway, and UI test types pass; scoped lint, format, diff and size ratchets pass. Independent P0/P1 review of the repair delta found no actionable defects, composing with the earlier complete-candidate review.
- Test cost: send file **19.50s** Vitest / **27.05s** wrapper; Cron cohort **40.01s** / **43.33s**; runtime siblings **120.12s** / **174.28s**; Gateway authority **72.57s**. UI file times: people **7.56s**, sidebar **10.95s**, color **5.98s**, terminal **3.89s**, operator scopes **5.50s**, assignment **25.26s**, companion **26.03s**, mobile **15.89s**. These preserve existing public-boundary contracts, not added per-test Gateway boots.

### Composed Ask authority and remaining consumers (`7bf8002c`)

The existing final-enqueue suite now composes **real sessions_send → real QuestionManager → public question.resolve router → real guarded steering → reopened SQLite transcript**. This is one connected approval-to-effect flow, not separate mocked decisions:

- A peer without recipient authority and a synthetic model/admin cannot approve; the question stays pending, the input queue remains untouched, and the transcript is empty.
- The authorized recipient creator approves. Revoking the admitted sender while approval is pending prevents delivery; changing receive policy after approval but before final enqueue also leaves zero input effects.
- Live authorized input is persisted exactly once. Closing the sender or changing policy after acceptance does not withdraw the accepted guidance.

The expanded **eight-case suite passed** in **42.72s** (51.35s wrapper). Only read-only session resolution and external provider streaming are fixtures; approval, admission, queue, and persistence owners are real. Existing human-question and public-router/SQLite compatibility evidence remains complementary.

Remaining raw-child fixtures now seed a real replacement ancestor and exercise guarded V2 injection; original completion custody and foreign-agent isolation assertions remain. The original two failures reproduced; **9 raw-child tests and 28 sibling tests passed** before the expanded queue proof above. Sidebar navigation passes **11 tests** (24.51s); its final child cases pass **2 tests** (4.55s). Phone stale-build recovery reproduced both obsolete root-Assign failures, then passed **both service-worker modes** (61.55s including a 22.05s artifact build) after one Session settings tap, retaining artifact, reconnect, selected-owner, and zero-model-wake assertions.

The four-file delta changes tests only. A follow-up retained main’s equivalent explicit topology assertions to resolve the sole merge conflict without rebasing unrelated production changes; both child-session interaction cases passed again (5.29s), and Git’s merge-tree is clean. Focused lint, affected test-type graphs, formatting, assertion safety, timeout-race and line-growth ratchets passed. Independent P0/P1 delta review was scoped-clean; it is static review composed with the observed execution above, not another execution claim.

The prior c3 CI attempt exposed dashboard-pin and guest-publication failures in the newer main Details UI, plus non-reproduced color-refresh and history-snapshot failures. Dashboard and guest failures reproduced on exact main `699636375966` and tested merge `f19dd09afd36`, with identical implicated owners. The later `38036561899` failure was the missing initial snapshot, before stale geometry was injected. Baseline and exact-CI-equivalent replays passed, which was not treated as a repair or inheritance proof. The causal fixture diagnosis below supersedes the earlier unresolved snapshot assessment.

The earlier hosted run also found unrelated Board-incognito, session-status profile, and video-gallery failures; each reproduced independently on trusted main with matching relevant source and diagnostics. Any inherited-failure landing exception must still be qualified against this candidate’s actual CI attempt. No rerun or synthetic push was used to obtain green.

### Causal snapshot fixture repair (`ab596f`)

The original mock roster omitted required `kind`. A real public `sessions.changed` invalidation republished that row into transcript metadata; durable schema validation rejected `/kind` and evicted the expected snapshot while leaving the live transcript visible. This was reproduced both **before the first durable write** and **after a confirmed initial IDB commit**. Adding `kind: "direct"` made both ordering cases persist naturally and complete the original reload, older-history fetch, and no-phantom-gap assertions. The original CI logs cannot establish its exact event ordering; the controlled public-flow proof establishes the concrete fixture defect, not a generic timing guess.

The final change is one test file (+9/−1): a typed `GatewaySessionRow` reused in the roster and both startup responses. Production code, validation, timeouts, and existing assertions are unchanged. Both ordering probes passed; the final original test passed in 2.08s, snapshot-owner tests **47/47**, canonical UI E2E types, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent P0/P1 correction review was scoped-clean.

The preceding exact merge `8299bbdc76e81bafbda9e8f0327d8084fbe0f547` also passed the original **51-file / 222-test**, three-worker, cold-ordered cohort on Node 24.19.0 and managed Chromium 153 (revision 1243), using configured Blacksmith Testbox: [runtime replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38038528964). That pre-fix green replay is environment evidence only. The repaired fixture proof used the supported local Node 26.8.2 runner.

### Exact-head hosted CI qualification

[Run 38040444525, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38040444525) tested merge `fd9975bdc6cb` (baseline `4ea40f2b890e` plus head `ab596f29367e`). ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents lose the manual result-collection guidance after checking a still-running command when `tools.exec.notifyOnExit=false`. The initial exec result contains the warning, but later process observations omit it.

## User Impact

Running `process poll`, `log`, and `list` results continue to explain that required results must be collected before ending the turn unless another continuation is arranged. This preserves information for both ordinary tool responses and structured Code Mode callers.

Notification settings, process lifetime, cancellation, and scheduling are unchanged. This is an informational repair, not a guarantee that a model will follow the guidance or complete a task.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the notification policy already captured by each process, share the existing guidance with exec, mark affected running entries in lists, and stop advertising it after completion. No new configuration or state store.

Follow-up to #158884, which added the initial exec warning. Related #120414 adds a general caution to initial exec output; it does not repair the later process observations addressed here.

## Evidence

- Regression through exec, the process supervisor, and process poll: before the production change, **1 failed / 5 passed** because the running poll lacked structured `followUp`.
- Repaired boundary and sibling tests: **20/20 passed** across `bash-tools.exec-liveness`, `bash-tools.process.poll-timeout`, and `bash-tools.process.activity`. Covers poll/log/list with notifications enabled and disabled, terminal collection, cancellation, output ordering, and retained process activity.
- Extended the existing fake-clock fixture rather than adding process boots or test cases. The two collection-policy cases took **7 ms and 6 ms**; the three-file run took **31.68 s** including compilation.
- Independent review: scoped-clean through P2; no actionable findings.
- Complete six-file changed check **passed**: production types, all 27 selected core-test type graphs, formatting, lint (0 warnings/errors), dead-export scans, and repository guards. `git diff --check` passed.
- Gateway publication adds an attribution-only commit; its tree is identical to the reviewed and tested candidate. Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36805911473) completed successfully; both required `openclaw/ci-gate` entries are green. title: fix(webchat): keep waiting replies visible after yielding
body:
Related: #87321

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a waiting acknowledgment can be missing from WebChat, or disappear after refresh, when an otherwise-silent agent yields for ongoing work.

## User Impact

User impact: explicit acknowledgments and the default waiting reply appear once and remain in history for direct and queued WebChat turns. A storage failure is reported instead of silently treating the acknowledgment as delivered. No configuration, schema, or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebChat now persists the public continuation payload through the existing assistant-transcript owner before publishing it or settling continuation delivery. The transcript transaction consumes the original live authority check after awaited preparation. Canonical acknowledgment messages stay separate from neighboring notices, so live events and history reconcile to one row. Native model completion remains distinct from a later host-delivery failure.

This does not read private yield context, promote tool-result text, or change quiet-turn/visible-reply suppression and child-wake policy. #87471 is an older replay attempt; historical tool-result migration is not part of this repair.

Contributor credit: @jalehman identified the affected workflow and drove this repair.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/b952bba7-dc20-43b1-9018-a22f14c666ad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/e363e26f)

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway boundary:** all 19 WebSocket/history cases pass for direct and queued turns, explicit/default acknowledgments, media, duplicate delivery, mixed notices, and reload. The actual Gateway-client projection reconciles live/history events in either order without duplicating the acknowledgment or exposing private context.
- **Authority and settlement:** deferred abort/replacement and reentrant revocation cannot commit or publish a transcript row. Native and queued storage failures, plus post-dispatch source preparation failure, produce an error and failed replay instead of premature success. Queued execution is preserved. Two real UI-handler cases verify separate late-error presentation and newer-run isolation without relabeling completed model execution.
- **Verification:** 180 focused tests and 25 requester-wake E2E tests pass on the exact candidate. Ordinary writers, aliases/storage environments, cold restoration, Goal turns, media and cancellation siblings also passed during the repair. Fresh AutoReview is scoped-clean through P2. Independent full-source re-review of commit `3d038b6405e211fea4e83f3e5615c66bf0ea8f44` also found no actionable P0–P2 issues and verified all three earlier findings resolved.
- **Full changed-file plan:** all 32 maintained check-plan commands pass, including production types and all 27 core test-type graphs, formatting, lint, i18n, boundaries, schema and safety guards. The supported full-stripe typecheck runner used concurrency 4; Vitest stayed serial. [Blacksmith Testbox environment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36799325649), Node 24.19; this is prepublication proof, not PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

Serial runs use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

- `server.chat-queued-followup.test.ts`: 19 cases, 57.34 s wall including compilation; the 13 added cases take 12.76 s combined. One suite-level Gateway is reused.
- `transcript-write-context.test.ts`: 26 cases, 23.55 s wall including compilation; the seven added cases take 1.20 s combined.
- `chat-gateway.late-delivery-error.test.ts`: two cases take 18 ms combined; its isolated UI shard takes 2.26 s.
- PR CI timing is not yet available. Added tests use controlled promises and observable completion, not sleeps or polling.

</details>

### Before and after

**Before** — the public waiting acknowledgment is absent from replay.

![Before: waiting acknowledgment absent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e81e1f22-2b3f-44a1-b350-59c7bd861b37)

**After** — one public waiting acknowledgment remains visible.

![After: one durable waiting acknowledgment](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffcaf34e-71c5-4a68-af43-21dde646cbb8)

Boundary proof uses controlled upstream execution; Gateway dispatch, WebSocket delivery, SQLite persistence, history RPCs, and client projection are real. The inspected screenshots use the actual unchanged Control UI with a sanitized synthetic history replay of those proven Gateway outcomes. They show rendering/reload behavior, not a fresh live-provider conversation.

<details>
<summary>Scope and line-count accounting</summary>

Production: +247/−66 (net +181); tests: +612/−1 (net +611). Growth supplies missing durable host-reply publication and settlement, consumes the existing live-owner assertion at the transaction boundary, and preserves canonical message identity across mixed notices. It reuses existing transcript storage and removes the competing media-write path; there is no new store, schema, protocol, dependency, or configuration surface.

</details>

title: fix: prompt snapshots fail with configured media credentials
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes prompt snapshot checks failing when media-provider credentials are configured in the developer environment.

## User Impact

No user-facing runtime change. Snapshot generation stays independent of optional media credentials, without changing the committed prompts or tool catalogs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture constructed optional media tools before excluding them from its catalog. Capability checks then loaded provider policy modules through the source loader. It now excludes those four factories up front using the existing tool policy; the final catalog projection remains intact. Synthetic OpenAI and Z.AI keys exercise the original failure without real credentials.

Main independently repaired both unrelated failures exposed by the first hosted run. The branch incorporates those canonical fixes and retains main’s wrapper assertion instead of the redundant local correction. The final PR delta is again only the two snapshot fixture/test files.

title: fix: clear obsolete publication failures after work is published
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an obsolete publication failure keeps warning users after the same work has already been published and merged.

## User Impact

Users no longer see recovery actions for a failed attempt when GitHub proves its accepted work is already published. Failures for newer or unverified work remain visible; no manual dismissal is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Making the warning smaller was not enough. Discovery now compares the failed attempt’s accepted snapshot with matching PR history, and the UI clears obsolete recovery when that authoritative result changes. Exact request history remains unchanged.

Coverage requires an identical published tree or verified committed ancestry. Missing history, unavailable GitHub reads, and rate limits retain the warning rather than guessing that work landed. No schema migration or configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Verified the originally reported accepted commit/tree is included in the merged PR head through live GitHub comparison metadata.
- Regression tests cover immutable receipt history, local and repository-only workspaces, authorization revoked during reads, unrelated/newer work, unavailable candidates, and rate-limit cooldown without credential fallback.
- Real Control UI browser regression covers automatic retirement, same-head retry after inconclusive reads, reload, starting new work, and a new unpublished failure; publication/confirmation writes remain zero.

The team roster maintained a second reader, event reducer, subscription, and request queue outside the canonical session owner. It now observes the canonical window. title: chore(tests): deduplicate baseline-independent survivor assertions
body:
Related: #160922

## What Problem This Solves

The Tool Search survivor version matrix repeats baseline-independent negative checks and identical no-intent checks. Each assertion starts a real Node CLI and creates fresh JSON fixtures: 27 executions for 17 distinct version-sensitive or outcome contracts.

## User Impact

No upgrade, migration, Tool Search or product behavior changes. Tests still cross the actual Node CLI, module, environment and JSON-file boundaries. Ten equivalent executions are removed without replacing subprocess proof with mocks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep all nine baseline checks for absent, 2026.9.6 and published 2026.9.7 receipts, plus successful survival for each version. Run the four common survival rejections and identical no-intent acceptance once in a separate named case. The assertion owner only reads baseline version behind the baseline-stage branch; survival's mode/disabled/legacy-timeout policy is shared.

All production and helper bytes, fresh fixture creation/finally cleanup and recipe tests are unchanged. The test count increases **182 → 183** because the common checks are split out; no unique outcome category disappears. Future baseline-specific survival branches would need their own coverage—this is not a claim of exhaustive equivalence for hypothetical future code.

title: fix: Daybreak hides supported xhigh and max reasoning
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Daybreak Blue and Red omit supported `xhigh` and `max` reasoning choices, and advanced API requests can be reduced to `high`.

## User Impact

Users with Daybreak access can select advanced efforts without replacing the requested alias with a snapshot. Ultra remains a separate runtime orchestration mode. Blue keeps reasoning enabled; Red supports Off. No migration or new access entitlement.

Known pre-existing limitation: inference-gated setup can reject a successful Daybreak reply when it reports the backing snapshot instead of the alias. **Follow-up: record requested/returned model identity at the inference owner**, rather than adding a stale snapshot whitelist or weakening winner validation. This PR repairs reasoning selection and payloads, not that setup guard.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI plugin now owns the Daybreak capability facts, and its reasoning profile honors declared effort metadata instead of losing it to model-name heuristics. Exact registered rows retain configured capabilities and Ultra opt-outs. Account discovery remains authoritative; offline subscription fallback does not invent Daybreak availability.

## Evidence

- Authenticated OpenAI Responses probes on September 30: Blue and Red each completed successfully with `xhigh` and `max` (four HTTP 200 responses). Blue resolved to `gpt-6.1-sol`; Red to `gpt-5.6-cyber`. No credentials or raw account data included.
- ClawSweeper’s requested Red Off proof: authenticated `POST /v1/responses` at 18:01 UTC with model `gpt-daybreak-red-latest`, `reasoning: { effort: "none" }`, `max_output_tokens: 64`, and `store: false` returned **HTTP 200**, `status: "completed"`, model `gpt-5.6-cyber`, effort `none`, and output `OK`. This confirms the advertised Red Off contract; no credential, account identifier, or response identifier is published.
- Regressions failed before the owner repair, then passed through the registered provider profile/materialization and actual final Responses request builder. Includes narrower/empty/disabled capabilities, configured Ultra opt-out, alias identity, and native/account boundaries.
- Focused tests: 197 passes across six files, reusing unchanged-path proof. Extension production/test types, relevant AI package types, docs links/MDX/formatting, and generated metadata checks passed. Changed-surface lint passed with zero warnings/errors. Independent autoreview of the unchanged production repair completed scoped-clean with no findings; the subsequent source change only relocates payload tests.
- Initial CI [run 36754561342](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36754561342) correctly rejected a plugin-manifest import in the AI package test. The two alias payload cases now live under the OpenAI plugin; the AI package test is restored unchanged. The failing test-ownership check and core TypeScript graph boundary check both pass locally, without guard exceptions. Updated-head CI [run 36756970256](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36756970256) passed the boundary shard and the OpenAI provider group (88 files). Its recorded root failure is an inherited unused `reconcileCronExitWatchers` import in `src/gateway/server-cron.ts:113`, outside this PR’s changed files; the CI gate failed and 24 sibling jobs were cancelled by fail-fast. The canonical repair [d5e602f0bcf8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d5e602f0bcf8d6d1c5cbfc502a4ae6c35e36f70a) is now integrated through main `112df95f5ee65`, without changing any of the nine Daybreak patch files. Focused lint on both canonical Gateway files passed with zero warnings/errors (11.9 s), and the seven model-materialization/final-payload cases passed on the integrated base (4.71 s Vitest; 8.80 s wrapper). Current-head CI [run 36760088024](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36760088024) is **green** for `5daa856a81a93cd77105902c5d69288188a8517b`: 41 successful jobs, 24 skipped jobs, no failed or pending jobs, and a successful PR check rollup. The earlier overall runs were not green.
- ClawSweeper [Revision 4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162024#issuecomment-5916839009) completed at 18:53:44 UTC on current head `5daa856a81a93cd77105902c5d69288188a8517b`: **no findings, no security concerns, and no before-merge actions**; ready for maintainer review. It acknowledges the authenticated API observations and distinguishes them from supplemental mocked request-builder tests. Its `needs-human` marker means maintainer review remains; it is not a formal approval or merge authorization.
- Official [Daybreak guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/daybreak) and [Blue](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-daybreak-blue-latest)/[Red](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-daybreak-red-latest) references: aliases move with access programs; preserve the request alias.
- Personally inspected upstream Codex [Blue catalog](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json#L554-L613), [Red catalog](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json#L671-L730), [effort resolution](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models/reasoning_effort.rs#L10-L41), and [client](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs#L839-L855). Native live execution was not run.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost and scope</summary>

Each command used `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| Changed test file | Tests | Local wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `extensions/openai/openai-provider.models.test.ts` | 5 | 17.25 s |
| `extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts` | 69 | 16.03 s |
| `extensions/openai/thinking-policy.test.ts` | 25 | 1.99 s |
| `extensions/openai/openai-provider.responses.test.ts` | 2 | 1.84 s |

The provider wall times include local compiler preparation/cache work; new configured-row cases took 3 ms each. The relocated payload cases took 40 ms and 3 ms; the unchanged AI Responses suite also passed (28 tests, 1.97 s wall). Initial CI spent 99.09 s on the boundary test shard before fail-fast cancelled the provider jobs. Updated-head CI: boundary test step 64 s; OpenAI provider group 113.84 s for 88 passing files, including the changed thinking-policy, materialization, and final Responses payload cases. The enclosing multi-group job was cancelled after that group completed; this timing is group-level wall time, not added-test overhead. Current green run: boundary test step **59 s**; extension-bundle-1 Node test step **190 s**. The latter encloses multiple provider groups; it is step-level elapsed time, not OpenAI-only time or added-test overhead. Existing routing coverage moved into the focused materialization file without dropping it. No timers, sleeps, new worker pins, dependencies, baselines, or suppressions.

Production delta: +48 lines, chiefly declarative catalog rows. Existing transport and picker owners consume metadata; no consumer-only guard or parallel request path. Alias price estimates follow the unknown-cost convention; docs explicitly say they are not free-price claims.

Exact-head CI and ClawSweeper follow-through is complete. With @VACInc’s authorization, the native guarded workflow merged source head `5daa856a81a93cd77105902c5d69288188a8517b` into `main` as `ddb870a8b5f4752fd213c032d5ef6b348d74d236` on September 30. The clarified squash title explicitly names supported `xhigh` and `max`.

</details>

title: chore(ui): make durable chat scenario videos opt-in
body:
Related: #160922

## What Problem This Solves

Six composer/outbox scenarios encode incidental diagnostic videos on every routine run.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The existing `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1` flag restores these recordings; default runs keep stage screenshots, request reports, assertions and failure diagnostics without the six video outputs. Existing ACK-loss recordings retain their separate gate.

**Tradeoff:** default first-failure continuous timelines are no longer available. A capture-enabled replay cannot recover the original failed run's timeline. These six scenarios retain 23 stage screenshots and their existing failure diagnostics.

**Implementation decision:** accept opt-in video for these six screenshot-rich scenarios within the delegated test-cost work. The 23 retained stage screenshots, request reports, assertions and existing failure diagnostics are sufficient for the routine regression contracts; continuous first-failure video remains useful but is not an assertion input. This accepts the diagnostic loss described above rather than claiming replay can recover it. It does not change scenarios that inspect recorded frames, native-media proof, or the existing ACK-loss recording policy. This is the implementer’s scoped tradeoff assessment, not a claim of a separate human approval or a waiver of CI/review gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate only three recording options in legacy uncertain-send recovery, the selected-model desktop/mobile matrix and the PNG capacity matrix. Preserve all 23 cases, real image decoding, native IndexedDB ownership, send admission/order, model recovery, waits, cleanup and artifact allocation. No production or shared-helper change. A supporting UI-unit fixture repair also adopts the existing lazy-dialog readiness helper and cancels/joins pending model selections before disposal; all 26 consent, authority and no-replay cases remain.

## Evidence

- Original baseline, warmup and six matched candidate runs: **23/23 passed** each. Relevant full sibling files: **14/14 passed**. Full selected changed checks passed, including UI E2E types, formatting, lint, guards and dead-export scans.
- **Six fewer recording jobs; 0.94–1.18 MB less WebM output per invocation.** Every run retained **40 PNG + 3 JSON**, with identical scenario/filename inventories. Three already-gated ACK-loss videos remained enabled identically in both measurement arms and are excluded from savings.
- All six newly optional videos and three unchanged ACK-loss videos finalized and fully decoded. All six affected timelines and 23 stage screenshots inspected. For the three recording files, AST and normalized remaining-byte parity verify that only recording initializers changed. Independent review of the complete four-file candidate through P2 is clean.
- **No reliable total-CPU benefit or fixed end-to-end speedup established.** Paired on-minus-off wrapper differences were **−1.15, +1.78 and +6.81 seconds** under variable host load. Median total CPU was **197.00 s on / 215.97 s off**. Encoded-video duration is not CPU or test time saved.

**Original hosted CI failure (attempt 1, head `25347b7b7469`):** [Run 36749624755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36749624755) failed in the separate UI unit lane: `chat-model-restriction-recovery.test.ts` → `requires explicit consent and handles a rejected recovery=false without replay` timed out waiting for a confirmation dialog (`expected null not to be null`, 1,014 ms). That lane excludes `*.e2e.test.ts`, including all three edited files; its failure-owner sources are unchanged from the tested merge parent. A bounded local full-file replay passed **26/26 in 3.42 s** under Node, but it did not reproduce the hosted Bun/whole-shard conditions and does not prove a fix. The latest scheduled main UI lanes passed, so this is **not qualified as a matching known-main failure**. Fail-fast cancelled the E2E shards and other unfinished gates.

**Supporting repair:** the unit fixture started its one-second DOM deadline before the recovery module finished loading. A controlled delay in the real Vite loader reproduces the original first-case null-dialog failure/slow-second-case pattern; the repaired fixture passes the same experiment without prewarming or increasing the timeout. It reuses `waitForConfirmDialogActions()` and cancels/joins outstanding selections, including release of a held test response before cleanup. The hosted occurrence did not reproduce naturally, so the exact cause of that runner’s loading delay remains unknown.

On the exact tested merge with the repair, three complete pinned-Bun UI shard 2/3 runs passed **527 files / 7,647 cases**, with three existing skips. Twenty standalone runs passed all **26 cases**; six owner/predecessor sibling files passed **85 cases under both Bun and Node**. A forced early assertion still fails while repaired teardown joins pending work. The required single-worker target command took **5.53 s wall / 3.53 s Vitest**. These are local repair proofs, not a claim that the failed remote gate has cleared. Shard membership matched, but worker scheduling was not identical to the hosted run. The first local original-source shard also hit Chromium Unix-socket path setup failures from an overly long task `TMPDIR`; only that launcher override was removed so the unchanged runner could allocate its normal private paths.

**Repaired candidate:** `610f5784e8f3148ace331eaf250394946a9deda8` adds only the supporting fixture repair to the original recording change. On the publication checkout, the 26-case target and full combined changed checks (UI-chat and UI-E2E types, lint, formatting, guards and dead exports) passed. The complete four-file independent review is clean. The revised-head hosted run below passed; the original red run is retained above rather than relabeled green.

**Original-head hosted cost observation:** the eight launched E2E shards each consumed **378–380 s job wall / 296–307 s test-step time before cancellation**. These are incomplete, post-change whole-shard observations—not per-case completed timings, CPU/billed cost, or paired savings. No completed hosted affected-case timing is claimed. Security-fast and the dependency/security-sensitive checks passed; the enforced CI gate did not.

**Repaired-head hosted CI:** [Run 36754903198, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36754903198) passed at `610f5784e8f3148ace331eaf250394946a9deda8`, including all selected UI/E2E, type, lint, guard and security-fast jobs and the Actions CI gate. All 23 recording-file cases passed. Reported file durations were **18.760 s catalog (12 cases), 33.156 s recovery (8), and 14.469 s capacity (3)**. The 26-case supporting recovery fixture passed with **0.254 s reported test duration**. Containing E2E jobs took **509 s (shard 4) / 418 s (shard 2)**, and UI unit shard 2 took **295 s**. These are post-change hosted observations, not paired savings or CPU/billed-cost measurements.

**Review disposition:** the completed exact-head ClawSweeper review found no patch/security defect but requested an additional human decision on first-failure video. The diagnostic risk is accepted by the implementing/landing owner under the existing delegated test-cost task, as stated above; no separate human approval is claimed. The maintainer workflow requires substantive findings to be resolved or their rejection explained, not adoption of every bot-proposed approval gate. Live branch rules require zero general approving reviews, and current CODEOWNERS has no matching owner rule for these four test paths. All enforced review/security/CI rules remain mandatory; this disposition does not bypass them.

<details>
<summary>Timing context</summary>

| Metric | Capture on median | Capture off median |
|---|---:|---:|
| Whole wrapper | 49.97 s | 44.19 s |
| Six affected cases, summed | 18.259 s | 16.377 s |
| Total user + system CPU | 197.00 s | 215.97 s |

Same-host supported wrapper, unchanged configured concurrency, off/on–on/off–off/on ordering. Every invocation retained its canonical UI build (9.73–13.91 s); no prebuilt/artifact-fence bypass. Case sums are not parallel wall time. This is real Chromium against synthetic mock-Gateway fixtures, not live Gateway, external-service or OS-device proof. Local observations do not establish paired CI savings.

</details>
