title: feat: use MCP plugin apps across conversations and workspace files
body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP plugin apps need to work as interactive tools across conversations and workspace files, rather than only as inline results after a model tool call.

## User Impact

With the existing opt-in MCP Apps host enabled, users can open advertised apps directly, change server-owned settings, attach app resources and text/image context, use file viewers/editors with conflict-aware saves, and answer rich forms. Setup skills run only when explicitly requested.

This does not enable apps by default, install native Codex plugins, grant access to ChatGPT accounts, or introduce another runtime. Existing session, requester, tool-approval and workspace boundaries remain in force. App-supplied context remains untrusted conversation data.

File saves follow the upstream optional precondition: `ifMatch` prevents stale overwrites; omitting it writes without a version check. Apps should send the read ETag when protecting concurrent edits. Neither form grants access beyond the opened writable file.

Native Codex Apps keep the existing conversation-owned connection and approval policy. Interactive forms work with prompting modes such as Guarded/Workspace; Codex can decline them under its `never` policy in Full access. Native calls to one server/conversation cannot overlap, and background previews share the existing per-view request limits. These restrictions are documented; there is no fallback connection or policy bypass.

## Why This Change Was Made

The implementation extends the existing MCP sandbox and reuses the conversation, file, approval and native Codex connection owners. App instances retain their conversation identity; deep links and display-mode changes preserve the instance, and pending input remains reachable above fullscreen apps.

Requested by and co-authored with @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/ccb0f6e8-2cff-4b08-a507-aa5ce4d979ce)

## Evidence

- Live interoperability uses the official Bits & Bolts 0.1.11 server in credential-free isolation, the real Gateway, Control UI, and direct/native MCP transports with synthetic workspace data. The built-in model endpoint is a deterministic local fixture, not a real ChatGPT account.
- Direct proof covers discovery/global/thread launch without a model call, settings and readback, resource mentions, image context at the next model endpoint, item removal, STL edits and stale-save conflicts, 36-choice canonical answers, origin-bound uploads, fullscreen, quick-action confirmation, in-place deep links, rich messages to current/new conversations, and explicit onboarding. A fresh mounted App also completed an ordinary model turn and then read/wrote through the **same view**, with per-call approval.
- Native Codex proof covers cold/concurrent discovery, real global/thread/settings/resource/file workflows and conflict handling. In Workspace permission mode, the authenticated native App route delivered a 36-choice form to the real Control UI and returned canonical answers and uploaded resource URIs. This last form test launched an unmounted file view through the public RPC to avoid competing demo thumbnail calls; it was not a mocked transport.
- Final product build passed in **331.33s**. The unchanged strict UI performance gate passed: largest ordinary JS **214.9 KiB / 215 KiB**, startup JS **366,579 B**. Interactive question controls now load lazily. No budget, baseline, or dependency change.
- Regression proof includes 140 UI tests across 9 files; 37 focused lazy-card/keyboard tests after the canonical-value correction; 20 runtime-authority tests (10 failed before repair); 4 real-router/onboarding custody cases; and 41 native lifecycle/catalog/ownership cases. New native lifecycle file: 6 tests, **12.86s** standalone Vitest wall, new queued-caller case **152ms**. Onboarding: about **3.8s** test execution / **17.35s** warm wrapper wall (cold compilation **60.6s**). Earlier integrated checks: 68 tests in **85.75s**, 13 registry/connection elicitation cases in **3.97s**. CI timing remains to be attached to the published head.
- Core/UI/plugin and affected test types, scoped lint, assertion ratchets, protocol registry/native generators, release-train guard and UI i18n checks passed. Independent reviews resolved startup cancellation, ordinary-turn invalidation, onboarding custody and concurrent native startup defects. The queued native-borrow review concern was rejected against the existing SDK warm-borrow contract and a real Alice/Bob policy-isolation regression; contract-aware re-review was clean.
- CI-driven ownership repairs remove type-import cycles, a test-only production export, and a Node database fixture from the UI runtime tree. Madge reports **0 cycles**; the exact storage-boundary test and affected form/native suites passed (**71.27s**), as did focused UI cases (**7.07s**). The changed loading regression costs **126ms / 2.57s** standalone wall. Core/UI/extension and affected test types, scoped lint, and canonical production/script/full-tree export scans passed. Raw full Knip locally reports only three unchanged, untracked generated Apple Mermaid files; the hosted failure and all tracked-source findings are addressed without scanner exceptions.
- The next hosted UI shard passed 8,018 assertions across 532 files but correctly failed on four unhandled errors from an incomplete chat identity test context. The fixture now supplies the existing Gateway helper and a static agent-selection subscription; production UI and the identity assertions are unchanged. The original test reproduced the failure locally. All seven focused identity/context/catalog tests now pass in **2.71s**, with no unhandled errors; affected UI test types, lint and independent review also passed.
- Accepted the native overload-retry P1. Native tool calls now carry both the runtime-owner and per-call grant assertions into the existing client’s final pre-write boundary, including every retry; sibling status/resource requests carry their owner guard. No retry policy, cancellation, or elicitation ownership changes. Four forbidden retry writes were reproduced before repair; all seven boundary cases now pass, and the related four-file suite passed **58 tests / 13.83s**. The final seven-case run took **35ms** test execution / **57.40s** cold wrapper wall (44.39s compiler preparation). Scoped dependency-closure types, lint and assertion ratchet passed; independent P0/P1 review is clean.

<details>
<summary>Native retry final-I/O evidence</summary>

The checked-in `native-mcp-app.authority.test.ts` exercises the production adapter and production Codex client with the existing in-memory transport. The wire supplies `-32001` before enqueue, then changes authority during backoff without aborting the signal. Counts below are observed transport writes, including the initial rejected request. This is deterministic boundary proof, not a claim that the live native server was overloaded; separate real-server acceptance is described above. No credentials or user data are involved.

| Operation and authority | Writes before repair | Writes after repair | Final result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Tool, owner revoked | 2 | 1 | Refused before retry I/O |
| Tool, per-call grant revoked | 2 | 1 | Refused before retry I/O |
| Catalog, owner revoked | 2 | 1 | Refused before retry I/O |
| Resource, owner revoked | 2 | 1 | Refused before retry I/O |
| Tool/catalog/resource, still authorized (three controls) | 2 each | 2 each | Successful retry |

The shared client remains open in every case. Upstream Codex was inspected at `8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4`; its ingress overload response rejects before queue admission.

</details>

- Harness limitations and diagnoses: the native transport-loss investigation reproduced a test-launcher hazard: Linux killed `bwrap --die-with-parent` when its spawning thread exited, even with the parent process alive. A stable proof supervisor preserves the same sandbox flags; the control reproducer and a real native settings round-trip after 15s idle passed. Initial Full-access native form attempts were declined by upstream policy; a later guarded attempt overlapped a background call and was rejected. Swift/macOS execution is unverified on this Linux host. Earlier browser-conformance container compilation was killed before assertions, not counted as a pass. Android canonical-answer coverage passed (39 tests).

Before/after images below show the same live reference app moving from an inline tool result to a conversation-side app with removable context.

### Before

![Before: the reference app in an inline tool result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43304587-e19a-4ab1-abe0-df972d3e0e8c)

### After

![After: a conversation-side app with removable text and image context](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f23f92a3-d096-4c24-8a16-422dd9329245)



## Maintainer landing notes (October 2026)

- **Installed-client answers (ClawSweeper P1, fixed).** Released Android and pre-PR Apple clients submit the option *label* for rich-form choices. `QuestionManager.validateAnswers` now resolves every submitted string to one canonical answer: an exact `option.value` match wins; otherwise a label match (exact for form/secret questions, trim-insensitive otherwise) that identifies exactly one option resolves to that option's `value ?? label`; anything else stays free text and is accepted only for `isOther` questions. Label-sending and value-sending clients converge on the same stored answer with no capability negotiation. The regression tests fail on the pre-fix code.
- **Unconditional saves (owner decision: accepted).** `mcp.app.writeResource` keeps the upstream extension contract where `ifMatch` is optional. An omitted `ifMatch` is a last-writer-wins save, limited to the file the same view already opened writable, under the same session and requester authority. Apps that protect concurrent edits send the read ETag, as the docs state. No force-save or broader file grant exists.
- **Integrated with current `main`.** Main now generates the Kotlin and Swift protocol models from the schema at build time (#162251), so this PR's hand-written model edits were dropped; the generated models carry `QuestionOption.value`, the form fields and the `mcp.app.*` methods (`pnpm protocol:check` passes for both). Conflicts with main's Gateway and UI refactors were resolved on main's owners; the moved cleanup export and the retired sync workspace-root helper (removed in #162885 with its last consumer) were re-homed at their owners; the agent-runner MCP context projection moved to a sibling module for the line-cap ratchet with identical logic.
- **Startup budget.** The Control UI startup gate measures the eight initial-entry chunks. On the merged tree the PR added about 1.2 KB gzip there (main alone 372,857 B); deferring the MCP app link parser behind a cheap scheme/host probe in the document click handler and registering the MCP app English strings from their lazy consumers (the repo's `register*English` pattern) brings the landing head to 373,137 B, under the unchanged 373,454 B limit. No baseline change. The link probe only intercepts the `/<plugin>/app/<tool>` shape, so ordinary ChatGPT plugin pages keep default navigation.
- **File subscriptions on busy macOS Gateways.** `mcp.app.subscribeResource` watched the file's directory, and FSEvents directory watches drop events under load on macOS (the same failure #162487 fixed in the checkout fixture; reproduced on the landing host: 0 directory events, 1 file event). Subscriptions now watch the file itself (kqueue) and re-arm on atomic replacement.
- **Formatter blind spot.** `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` ignored `apps/` unanchored, which also excluded `ui/src/pages/apps/`; it is now root-anchored and the four affected files are formatted. Root `apps/` stays excluded.
- **Local proof on the landing head** is recorded in the PR comments by the landing chain; Android compilation is not available on the landing host (Kotlin generation and contract checks pass instead).

title: fix(exec): remove audit-suppression command approval heuristic
body:
Related: #154534 (replaces the read-exemption approach; does not carry its branch changes).

## What Problem This Solves

Commands that mention audit suppressions can trigger extra approval prompts even when they only read or discuss configuration, while inspecting command text cannot reliably protect configuration writes.

## User Impact

Suppression-related commands follow ordinary exec/node approval policy, including normal auto-review eligibility. This intentionally applies to both reads and writes: after upgrading, `security="full"` with `ask="on-miss"` no longer adds a human prompt just because a command changes suppressions, and otherwise eligible approval misses can reach automatic review. `ask="always"`, deny/allowlist policy, command binding, and other existing execution guards remain in force. Suppression configuration and audit filtering are unchanged; this does not introduce a config-write protection boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the dedicated gateway/node/reviewer conditions and nine tests that only enforce the retired runtime gate. No replacement heuristic or new test scaffolding. The existing system.run auto-review test now passes the suppression key as an ordinary argument. A small table in the existing policy suite protects the separately shipped SDK behavior.

The public `commandRequiresSecurityAuditSuppressionApproval` export [shipped in v2026.9.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime.ts#L90). Preserve its exact signature **and legacy results** through the existing `infra-runtime` retirement window, including `true` for suppression writes. The implementation is unchanged from v2026.9.6 and v2026.9.7 apart from its deprecation comment; only the deprecated SDK reexport consumes it, with no internal execution callers. Existing plugins may retain the call; plugins intentionally adopting ordinary exec policy can remove it. This fixes ClawSweeper’s SDK compatibility finding without reinstating a runtime gate or claiming a versioned breaking change.

## Evidence

- Started from clean pinned main `41a62e9a736d1fabc3bebbfd80031f6958c4b384`; no commits imported from the old PR.
- The adapted system.run low/medium-risk cases both failed on the original code because the reviewer was never reached, then passed after removal. This uses the existing execution entrypoint harness, not a detector mock.
- **Runtime-removal proof at `3d019740b93b`: 273 tests passed across six focused files:** gateway exec, node exec, direct system.run, ordinary node/exec policy, and SDK review input. Two existing audit-filtering cases also passed (15 unrelated cases deselected). No live Gateway or remote node was changed.
- Core production and affected `agents-root`/`other` test TypeScript checks passed. Changed-file lint/format, line-cap ratchet, SDK export/surface checks, three-page MDX check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview of the full corrected candidate found no working-tree P0–P2 defect. Its only finding was the older no-op still present in the index; staging the reviewed correction resolved that index-only finding before commit.
- SDK repair at `e46eccade00ee`: **full `pnpm build` passed** (7m 4.9s); all **74 policy-suite tests passed**, including four legacy-result cases. A consumer importing the built public `infra-runtime` export preserved all four shipped results; the prior no-op failed both `true`-result fixtures. Source trace confirms zero internal runtime callers.

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

The manually opened, top-right panel keeps related information together and stays bounded by the conversation and composer on desktop, mobile, split panes, and beside Browser. This replaces the earlier standalone floating-progress implementation rather than adding another placement preference.

title: fix(codex): stop replaying diagnostic-log notices in chat
body:
Closes #161610

**Landing authorized after the scoped test audit. No deployment is included.**

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a single Codex diagnostic-log failure is repeated as a System notice in concurrent and later chat turns, even after native logging recovers.

## User Impact

These known process-wide log-loss notices are recorded once per native notification in Gateway warning logs instead of being replayed into chats. Other task-specific, changed, and unrecognized warnings retain their existing routing.

**Tradeoff:** Gateway logging is best effort and follows configured levels and available sinks. If that logging is disabled or broken, these operator-only notices do not fall back to chat. A thrown diagnostic-sink error must not disconnect the shared Codex client.

This PR does not repair native SQLite, change the Codex version, upload diagnostics, or change authentication, approvals, permissions, or storage schemas.

## Why This Change Was Made

The decision now happens when the client receives a notification, before it is copied or cached for individual turns. The existing service-tier and Code Mode log-only rules move to the same plugin-local owner; the projector no longer makes a second routing decision.

Only the two exact upstream diagnostic-log messages with `method: warning` and `threadId: null` receive the new treatment. Extra details, changed wording, thread-specific instances, and other warning types are not broadly suppressed. Existing subscription and startup-configuration buffering code moves intact into `client-notifications.ts`.

## Evidence

The main proof used the **real managed Codex 0.158.0 binary**, normal OpenClaw client startup/parser/router, the production warning sub-projector, and the actual Gateway file logger. It used isolated homes, no credentials, and no inference or feedback-upload request. A held SQLite writer lock caused the real native warning; releasing it let logging recover.

| Observation: two current routes and one later turn | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Native diagnostic-log notifications | 1 | 1 |
| Chat diagnostic-log notices | 3 | 0 |
| Gateway warning records for that notice | 0 | 1 |
| Separate actionable rules-error notices | 3 | 3 |
| Native log rows persisted after unlocking | 32 | 32 |

Both native runs remained responsive, passed the log database quick check, and closed cleanly. Independent review caught a potential disconnect in the initial candidate if the logging sink threw. That failure was reproduced with a real throwing console sink and a same-chunk notification/RPC regression, then corrected. The final native probe also survives the sink failure before notification observers exist.

- Five routing regressions failed before the production change; the final focused suite passed **83/83**.
- Adjacent runtime, frame-decoding, private-transport, and turn-router lifecycle tests passed **84/84**.
- Changed checks passed, including production/test types, lint, boundaries, dead exports, import cycles, and six Doctor contract tests.
- `pnpm build` passed, including external plugin output and UI build: **6m 58.7s**.
- Final P0–P2 AutoReview found no accepted/actionable findings. Subsequent mechanical fixes resolved a private-field/test-double name collision and a strict test type; the checks above were rerun.
- One-worker repo-runner elapsed time: `client.test.ts` **12.66s**, `turn-router.test.ts` **13.57s**, `event-projector.reasoning.test.ts` **13.17s**. Most time is transform/import preparation; test bodies remain below the per-file budget. Hosted CI timing is not claimed here.

**Limits:** the native proof reserves synthetic thread/turn routes; it is not a live model-turn or conversation-persistence test. The original reported incident’s exact SQL failure remains unknown. The separate upstream locking repair is not in the inspected stable 0.159.2 release and is not included in this PR.

### Test-audit follow-up

Consolidated duplicated logger-failure setup: **14 fewer test lines, no production changes and no removed cases**. The active-observer case retains warning → ordinary notification → RPC response in one transport chunk; the startup case retains no replay or second log attempt after registration.

Both consolidated cases failed when the known unguarded logging fault was temporarily restored, then passed with the unchanged production repair. The final three-file suite passed **83/83** in **16.90s**; the changed client file passed **47/47** in **10.02s** (8.66s Vitest, test bodies 5%). Changed-file gates and fresh whole-PR P0–P2 AutoReview passed. Previous native-process, sibling-suite, and build evidence remains applicable because production sources are byte-identical.

### Visual comparison

**Normal-chat example — no deliberately broken rules file.** Actual Control UI with a synthetic conversation, using the diagnostic-log notice from the native before/after receipts. Both captures use identical content, viewport, theme, and run state; only that notice changes. This illustrates presentation, not a live model turn. The separate malformed-rules regression remains covered in the runtime evidence above, not in these screenshots.

**Before** — the diagnostic-log notice interrupts the chat.

![Before: normal chat interrupted by the diagnostic-log notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f87ebea-0d6b-4afa-b56c-61d935027f44)

**After** — the same chat continues without that notice. The diagnostic is routed to Gateway logs.

![After: the same normal chat without the diagnostic-log notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f16658f9-cd10-4e28-9b35-28f9ebbf4914)

<details>
<summary>Review guide: what to look at</summary>

1. **The cause of repetition:** the native warning is process-wide. The turn router caches global warnings and replays them into later routes; it does not know whether logging recovered.
2. **The fix location:** `client-notifications.ts` decides log-only versus normal delivery before that router sees the notice. The existing client still owns account updates, request settlement, and connection lifetime.
3. **The safety boundary:** exact-message matching is intentional because Codex exposes no diagnostic code. Future or more detailed warnings remain visible. No permanent deduplication flag can hide a new process’s failure.
4. **The failure rule:** logging these notices is best effort, not a new chat-failover system. The transport and following RPC frames keep working if the sink throws.
5. **What stayed separate:** native SQLite repair requires an upstream release containing the actual fix. Merely bumping to 0.159.x would not provide it.

Dependency source personally checked: Codex `rust-v0.158.0`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/log_write_warning.rs:14–61` and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/notification.rs:31–35`.

AI-assisted implementation and verification.

</details>

title: improve(ui): collapse inter-session receipts into activity rows
body:
Closes #161651

## What Problem This Solves

Inter-session receipts crowd the conversation with machine-oriented text, repeated source labels, and avatars.

## User Impact

Routine receipts become a compact updates-from row. One click or keyboard activation reveals the full original messages and timestamps, with a source-session link inside the expanded view. Stored messages, transport, run ownership, configuration, and permissions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Group only consecutive updates from the same source after causal transcript projection. Human messages, local answers, other sources, and conversation markers remain boundaries. Reuse the existing scoped session-title decorator for noninteractive summary labels, including its lazy activation, rather than adding a second title cache or extra network reads. Search and reply navigation reveal the original messages.

## Evidence

- Resolved the actual merge conflicts with main’s automation-history link fix, retaining its run destinations and base-path handling in the shared attribution owner. After integration: **83** focused attribution/activity/automation unit tests, **2** bundled browser flows, UI typecheck, and the actual base-aware performance gate pass. The refreshed required CI and security gates passed for resolved head `91cd03e`; merged as `c582ad7209d7` on September 30, 2026.
- Final base-aware performance gate passes against integrated main: **214.2 KiB** largest ordinary JS, below the unchanged **215 KiB** ceiling. Five existing geometry/layout modules now join their existing transcript-layout chunk. This adds no requests versus the previous candidate, at a tradeoff of approximately 1.1 KiB more compressed route bytes. No runtime behavior, styles, budgets, or baselines changed.
- Final production-bundled activity/reply/messaging E2E: **23/23 passed**. Chunking, geometry and scroll-ownership checks: **71/71 passed**.
- Review follow-ups preserve explicit receipt reply links and keep search-visible receipts in position indexing without changing saved disclosure choices. Focused regressions pass.

title: improve(tests): replace Rust session fixture delays with signals
body:
Related: #160922

## What Problem This Solves

Four Rust session fixtures use elapsed sleeps to guess when events are buffered or activity subscribers are ready.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Real TCP/WebSocket buffering, lag, Ping and malformed-frame activity checks remain intact. The fixtures synchronize explicitly and run faster in serial execution; default-concurrency runtime did not meaningfully improve. This continues the test-performance campaign requested by @steipete.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retention fixtures send a normal request/response barrier after the event frames on the same socket, then keep the socket open until assertions finish. Activity fixtures release peer input only after the actual client subscription exists. Production still publishes every event, activity update and response. No fake clock, internal buffer access, timeout reduction or production seam is added.

## Evidence

Pinned Rust 1.93.0, same host and native Cargo commands; ten warm samples per variant/mode, including reverse ordering:

| Median | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Four cases, serial | 289 ms | 220 ms |
| Full session target, serial | 1.270 s | 1.207 s |
| Full session target, default concurrency | 608 ms | 610 ms |

Observed serial saving: **69 ms / 23.9% for the four cases**, or **63 ms / 5.0% for the full serial target**. **No default-concurrency or CI speedup is claimed.** The source-derived 190 ms delay estimate is not the measured gain. Installation, compilation and warmups are excluded.

- All 23 test names, original assertions, their order and timeouts remain. Reversing only the fixture changes reproduces the original file byte-for-byte. The oversized-event case also explicitly checks that the session remains open.
- Four temporary owner faults fail both baseline and candidate at the original checks: capacity255, lost oversized-event lag, omitted Ping activity and omitted malformed-frame activity. Production restored byte-exact after joined runs.
- Rust workspace **148 tests passed**, including full client, TLS, node-host, event-consumer and sidecar siblings.
- Workflow-exact locked Rust formatting, Clippy/all-targets with warnings denied, and documentation with warnings denied all passed. Conflict-marker, attribution and diff guards passed.
- Generic Node planning was inspected after a task-local frozen pnpm install. It classifies Rust as an unknown surface and falls back to all Node/TypeScript lanes. Those unrelated broad checks were not run; the scoped proof is the actual Rust conformance workflow above. No planner, baseline or CI policy was changed; enforced hosted gates still apply.
- One extra timing block overlapped workflow gates and encountered Cargo locks; the entire block was excluded and replaced after both processes joined. RSS raw high-water marks were not used as per-command measurements.
- Toolchain and build state stayed inside task artifacts with no global profile/config changes or cloud allocation. This is real owned-loopback protocol proof, not an operator Gateway action.
- Fresh independent preservation review through P2 completed clean (confidence 0.91), including final source verification. Exact-head [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36670971627) and [Rust workspace conformance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36670758136/job/109745043789) passed. ## What Problem This Solves

Recurring automation guidance needs to distinguish mechanical reuse from model judgment without adding prompt bulk.

Agents are guided to script mechanical work while keeping interpretation and judgment with the model, rather than inventing heuristics just to avoid a model call. title: fix(ui): keep recent sessions stable in open person hovercards
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: recent-session links move under the pointer or keyboard focus when several sessions update while a person hovercard is open.

## User Impact

Recent links stay in place until the card closes. Reopening selects the latest sessions from the loaded, caller-visible roster. Timestamps remain live; links that become ineligible disappear without replacement. Viewing now continues to follow presence. Sidebar and transcript-mention cards share this behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lit now owns the selection for the lifetime of the existing card root, instead of both callers keeping and resetting separate state. The card holds at most three identities and resolves them against one current authorized-roster map. No debounce, extra polling, persistent cache, or frozen session facts.

## Evidence

- **142/142 sidebar people tests pass.** The existing projection fixture now covers initial loading, stable links/focus, live timestamps, roster removal, ownership changes, no resurrection/backfill, known-empty selection, and fresh selection on reopen. All platform, misleading-host, privacy, and distinct presence/lifecycle cases remain; duplicated setups and overlapping disappearance assertions were removed.
- Production-bundle Chromium checks pass for both sidebar and transcript cards: a stationary-pointer click still opens task 1 after ten updates; keyboard focus stays on its session; reopening refreshes the list. The inspected rendered UI is unchanged from the [published before/after evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161493#issuecomment-5902398444).
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean. Core/UI typechecks, formatting, scoped lint/style checks, i18n, dead-export checks, and source guards pass. The consolidated regression was also rerun against the original renderer: it fails at the stable-link assertion and passes with this fix.
- Test cost: the consolidated projection/lifecycle case took 114 ms; the full 142-case suite took 25.43 s in Vitest / 26.33 s wrapper wall with one worker. These timings are observations, not an isolated test-speedup claim.

### Scoped timing recheck

Production Chromium 153, same synthetic Gateway workload and 1440×1000 viewport; three 10-second runs per workload, excluding startup/recording. The trimmed owner produces zero reshuffles in all six runs.

| Updating / loaded sessions; total updates per second | Reshuffles per 10 seconds, original → trimmed | Card work, ms/second, original → trimmed | Refresh p95, original → trimmed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 / 11; 2/s | 19 → 0 | 2.53 → 0.76 | 1.6 → 0.5 ms |
| 50 / 201; 10/s, stress | 99 → 0 | 20.00 → 6.36 | 2.6 → 1.1 ms |

Card work is synchronous sorting/rendering/positioning, not total browser CPU or subsequent paint. This is not an app-wide speedup claim.

title: feat(ui): add CI popup automation controls
body:
Closes #161487

## What Problem This Solves

The CI popup reports checks but cannot keep a PR moving through CI fixes, review feedback, merging, and session cleanup.

## User Impact

Users can independently enable **Auto-fix CI & address comments**, **Auto-merge when ready**, and **Auto-archive on merge or close** without leaving the popup. Existing job and step details remain available, including on narrow screens.

These are opt-in agent automations, checked every five minutes while the Gateway runs, and consume model usage. They survive closing the browser and use existing permissions, approvals, and repository workflows. Archiving may clean up the session worktree; it defers while unrelated work remains. Turning an action off requests cancellation, but does not undo an already accepted external action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing durable Cron owner rather than adding another scheduler or browser-only settings. Each action is bound to the selected repository and PR number, with independently cancellable jobs. Other PRs in the session neither join this automation nor block its merge. Repair/merge keep their PR target across conversation resets; only archive captures an exact session ID. The popup reconciles saved settings after reconnects or uncertain writes, surfaces scheduler/run failures, and links to automation history. Repair and merge use the saved task workspace; archive runs separately so it can wait for an idle session.

## Scope and review follow-up

The selected PR—not the original transcript incarnation—is the repair/merge target. The earlier review correctly found that the original incarnation promise was only in a prompt; that unnecessary promise has been removed rather than adding a new Cron contract. Existing named-session admission, current permissions, workspace leases, and repository landing gates still apply. Archive uses the existing `sessions.patch` exact-session-ID precondition and does not archive a replacement. Its idle check is advisory; native archive retains its normal work-drain semantics.

## Evidence

- Initial baseline: 230 tests passed: 144 focused UI tests, 78 existing Cron/workspace/pane-owner tests, and the 8 browser scenarios below. Coverage includes recipe/protocol validation, CAS updates, uncertain writes, late-response isolation, durable declarations, active-run cancellation, and saved workspaces.
- Initial production-bundle browser proof: all 8 scenarios passed: toggle writes, uncertain-save recovery, read-only/no-check state, stale CI responses, and desktop/mobile/landscape job details.
- `pnpm ui:build` passed (14.44 s build); affected production/test typegraphs, lint, stylelint, i18n, formatting, and repository guards passed. Initial line-cap/type/lint findings were repaired; final focused reruns completed the affected gates.
- Refreshed independent AutoReview: **scoped-clean at P0/P1** on the staged full candidate. Earlier index-only and draft-key compatibility findings were resolved by reviewing the actual staged candidate and verifying there are no live draft CI jobs on this Gateway; this unmerged feature introduces no released-data migration.
- Follow-up: **20 focused UI tests and 4 scheduled-owner scenarios passed**. The inventory regression first failed on the old implementation, then passed: resetting the conversation retains the selected PR’s repair/merge jobs, excludes another PR, and does not adopt the old archive job.
- **10 browser scenarios passed across the correction runs**, including two PR chips where only the opened popup creates an auto-merge job. The retained-pane Escape regression from [the initial CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36656578964) is fixed by selecting the outer disclosure’s immediate summary. A brittle prompt field-order assertion exposed non-canonical recipe serialization; canonical target fields fixed it, and the selected-PR browser case passed on rerun.
- The new scheduler test uses real `cron.add`, persisted reload into a separate Cron service, clock-driven execution, and the existing runner. A **synthetic model endpoint** receives only the selected PR after reset; disabling that job leaves the other PR’s job separate. Real archive handling commits the matching session and disables bound jobs, while a mismatched session ID rejects the archive without changing the replacement. The matching archive records the existing Cron cancellation outcome when cleanup disables its running job.
- Scoped `check-changed` passed, including eight affected test typegraphs, UI types, i18n, lint, formatting, guards, and dead-export scans. Additional Cron/browser typegraphs and lint passed for the new proof. The browser build passed; visual layout is unchanged from the screenshots below.
- Browser proof uses synthetic Gateway responses. No live PR was merged or real session archived as a test; agent execution still depends on its configured model, tools, permissions, and repository workflow.

Real browser coverage is needed for anchored-popup geometry and native input behavior. The follow-up scheduler file passed 4 scenarios in **19.16 s wall** including compiler/runner startup (about 7 s of fixture execution). This composition checks durable job transport, cancellation, and the real archive mutation owner; it does not run a model or mutate GitHub. The selected-PR browser case took **1.27 s**, with **34.95 s wall** including its fresh production build. The initial hosted UI shard passed its other 392 tests and failed only the now-fixed retained-pane Escape selector; updated-head CI remains the native landing gate.

title: fix(ui): hide worktree settings for non-Git folders
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: New session can retain or display a worktree setting for a folder that is not a Git checkout.

## User Impact

Non-Git folders no longer offer checkout settings in the New session composer or command palette. Valid Git worktrees, remote repository clones, and new remote workspaces remain supported. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remote placement’s isolation requirement was written into the local checkout selection. Clearing cloud placement could leave that forced worktree behind, even after the folder was known not to be Git. The selection action also persisted an invalid worktree choice before checking it.

Placement now derives its own isolation requirement without mutating local checkout intent. The repository controller rejects ineligible selections before writing preferences, and both composers consume the same checkout-visibility decision. A failed Git check still preserves an existing isolation request and explains that Git could not be verified, rather than falsely calling the folder non-Git; it never silently starts an unisolated session.

## Evidence

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36659245841) is green for `f460d919e77993180ca7f74fa89202bc5ae81e57`, including the repaired UI and browser cases.
- Final CI test execution: placement 1.64s; palette 3.30s; checkout chip 0.05s; submit gates 0.50s; title handoff 0.23s. Browser file totals: device dispatch 18.02s (13 cases), instant thread 44.94s (19 cases). These change existing boundary fixtures; no new browser boot or serial configuration was added.
- Four owner-level regression cases failed before the fix: non-Git workspace, non-Git custom folder, cloud-to-local clearing, and selection during Git discovery. Two more cases reproduced the false non-Git warning after rejected/unavailable discovery.
- 125 focused UI tests passed, plus native terminal startup and accepted-worktree-preference siblings. The final warning cases passed all 17 submit-gate tests.
- Fresh independent autoreview of the final patch completed at P0–P2 with no actionable findings.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3qvn7qcf2yrqp2dw2gkge4m`: the changed-file gate passed, including all selected type graphs, lint, formatting, i18n, and export checks. The final warning delta passed focused tests, lint, and i18n verification. [Runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36650875628).
- Real Chromium + mocked-Gateway proof on Linux: non-Git controls disappear; plain-folder creation omits `worktree`; verified Git creation sends `worktree: true`; failed discovery preserves isolation and sends no create request. The screenshots below use synthetic fixtures, not the private report screenshot.
- Changed-test cost with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: draft-place-state 7.85s wall (43 tests), palette-session-draft 8.39s (30), checkout-chip 4.39s (27), submit-gates 4.62s (17). Test execution itself stays below 5s per file.

<details>
<summary>CI follow-ups and additional regression proof</summary>

The first CI run found one stale title-handoff fixture: it selected a worktree before its asynchronous Git discovery completed. The strengthened admission correctly rejected that early selection. The fixture now settles its existing fake clock and asserts Git eligibility before selecting, while retaining the explicit title/worktree-name assertion. That fixture repair did not change production code.

The exact failure reproduced standalone; all 11 title-handoff tests and 63 placement/title/name sibling tests now pass. Targeted lint and fresh full-candidate P0–P2 autoreview passed. The corrected title file costs 9.15s wall / 0.18s test execution locally. The failed initial CI UI test step took 274s; cancelled sibling lanes are not counted as passing proof.

The next exact-head CI run exposed a missed persistence producer: a saved remote `worktree: true` describes required remote isolation, not a Local checkout choice. Restoring that flag as local intent could block an explicit switch from an unavailable paired/auto device to Local. Preference restoration now restores local intent only for local or legacy-local preferences; remote isolation remains derived from placement. Three new cloud/device/auto owner regressions failed before this correction and pass after.

After the correction, 43 placement tests and 87 preference/palette/gate/title sibling tests pass. [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36656360146) passed all 20 device-dispatch, preference-restoration, and empty-workspace browser cases, plus UI types and targeted lint. The original two failing Local-switch assertions are unchanged. Held remote-restoration cases now assert no provisional Local worktree while retaining all submission gates and positively checking remote `sessions.create` still sends `worktree: true`. The device-dispatch file took 11.44s for 13 cases; the three-file browser suite took 25.38s. Fresh full-candidate P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable issue. Both proof runners have been stopped.

The third CI run found an existing navigation fixture racing durable draft restoration: Playwright could select an empty textarea, then insert after the retained `old admission` text arrived. The fixture now waits for that retained text before replacing it, while keeping the old navigation held and preserving every submission, rejection, and URL assertion. The original shard/worker replay did not reproduce this particular race (all 19 instant-thread cases passed); 21 unrelated video-recording cases were blocked by missing Testbox FFmpeg, so that replay is not claimed as a passing full shard.

The corrected candidate passed all 39 instant-thread, device-dispatch, preference, and empty-workspace browser cases on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36658302175), with the 19-case instant-thread file taking 26.02s and the four-file suite 39.94s. Targeted lint/format and a fresh full-candidate P0–P2 autoreview passed; the lease is stopped. This follow-up changes only the fixture precondition, not production behavior.

</details>

title: fix(ui): stop clipping forwarded message previews mid-line
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes forwarded cross-session message previews fading out halfway through a text line, often in the middle of a sentence.

## User Impact

Incoming and outgoing forwarded bubbles now end at a complete sentence when practical, with fully visible text that wraps naturally on narrow screens. **Show more** still opens the complete message. Ordinary non-forwarded user-message disclosures are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the forwarded-only 2.5-line height clip and fade with a bounded excerpt of the existing sanitized Markdown output. Native sentence/word segmentation chooses the endpoint without slicing Markdown syntax. Links, emphasis, paragraphs, and lists keep their structure; long code and media use compact read-only excerpts or labels, with the original rendering available on expansion.

The preview aims for 280 characters and three logical lines/blocks, allowing a first sentence up to 420 characters. It is not an exact visual-line clamp: narrow screens may show more complete lines. Very long sentences and unbroken text use an explicit ellipsis.

## Evidence

Real Control UI captures with synthetic mocked-Gateway messages, dark theme, identical 1280×800 and 390×844 viewports. Images are cropped only to focus on the conversation; no private transcript or user screenshot is published.

Five async-stream regression cases spend roughly 0.7 seconds polling events their own callbacks already observe.

Closes #161397

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw does not yet recognize GPT-6.1 Sol with its own routing, reasoning capabilities, and pricing.

## User Impact

Users with account access can select `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` through the existing OpenAI API-key or ChatGPT/Codex route. Existing selections and the Astra setup default stay unchanged. GPT-6.1 Sol cannot disable reasoning; it defaults to medium.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: accepted nested child work stalls after `sessions_yield` when a harmless session-metadata update overlaps the completion handoff, surfacing an access-fact error instead of resuming.

## User Impact

The requester automatically continues through the reproduced handoff races without a manual “continue.” Revocation, reset, replacement, cancellation, and unknown-outcome safeguards remain in place. No schema migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing publication owner retains an already-acquired access snapshot only when the native transaction proves unchanged sharing policy and session incarnation. Accepted work also retains its captured operator source after the selecting turn ends, while admission still checks that turn. Registry staging preserves unchanged delivery identity instead of revoking another prepared publication. No blind retry, new authority, revived writer, or parallel scheduler is introduced.

This covers the reproduced races, not every historical writer-claim or continuation-authority failure.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto pinned main `68ef53a4a6050cbfa70fde200e1a96d68a2a191c`. Exact candidate: `deaa7858756e576c206ab5bf045ef25fa9ed0f43`, tree `45deb947739e21d529906236ea0111216ff9510f`.

All four real-Gateway scenarios passed: child already completed before yield, active child, already-accepted successor, and delayed terminal persistence. Each checks exactly one successor and one persisted final result.

One inherited stale max-lines exception was removed under the shrink-only policy. Independent P0–P2 review: no actionable finding.

- Nine SQLite/publication controls cover metadata, revisionless metadata, lost result, membership revocation, visibility, archive, reset, replacement, and unknown outcome. These and cancellation/authority controls are owner-level tests, not whole-Gateway negative scenarios; unknown outcome is not injected worker death.

## What Problem This Solves

The snapshot ownership test spies on caller-realm process creation even though token processes now launch inside the native owner, causing CI to fail.

The test still requires exactly one real token child across three concurrent allocations and a nested fourth allocation. It checks every directory and verifies the recorded process is alive while held and gone after child-before-parent cleanup. A Worker-handle count does not substitute for this evidence.

The deliberately unreceipted allocation is separated from this healthy-lifetime scenario: the canonical native-resource tests already require cleanup to fail closed unless native not-started proof exists. That production policy is unchanged. Every successful sibling allocation retains cleanup custody, and scoped environment restoration follows joined cleanup. All 14 ownership cases remain.

title: fix(ui): keep the PWA composer inside the visible screen
body:
Related: #160388

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the chat composer extending below the visible screen when an installed PWA reports a larger CSS canvas or a keyboard leaves a short conversation pane.

## User Impact

Users retain a usable editor line, reachable Send/Stop controls, and scrollable composer context without adding device-specific padding or changing the existing desktop/mobile gutters and control sizes.

**Validation limit:** installed-iPhone Safari, the user's actual viewport origin, and native keyboard behavior remain unmeasured. The captures and browser checks below use the real bundled UI in Chromium with explicitly injected viewport contracts, not physical-iPhone evidence.

**Short-pane trade-off:** when very little height remains, typing, actions, and the context scrollport take priority; the transcript can temporarily have no visible height. Pinch zoom remains browser-owned rather than forcing a reflow that pins the toolbar at every zoom level. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Stop promoting standalone mode to 100lvh. Keep the smaller dynamic CSS canvas and native-scale visible bottom; separate that bound from keyboard detection and consume physical safe areas once.
- Fit the short-pane editor through its existing layout policy, rather than pushing overflow upward with flex-end.
- Keep default and short-pane transcript insets in the same stylesheet owner. Bundled New Session → Chat navigation exposed a real CSS loading-order override that source-preview testing missed.

WebKit reports independently support the suspected installed-PWA coordinate mismatch, without substituting for device acceptance: [316008](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=316008) and [301994 comment 12](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=301994#c12).

## Evidence

| --- | --- |
| Canonical bundled E2E, original production code + final test assertions | **10 failed**; 24.93s test report |

The canonical E2E covers full New Session/Chat entry, a merged-PR chip and completed progress card together, coordinate-touch Send/Stop requests, actual draft editing and first/last-line scrolling, context scrolling, desktop and zero-inset phones, landscape, sub-keyboard occlusion, keyboard pan/dismissal with retained focus, pinch behavior, and the missing-VisualViewport fallback. The original and repaired runs use the identical final E2E test file (SHA-256: 47fbfd376229c3bb24cab42a45db99cf87c9c4be66cf64b019ac85f9ccd8a28f).

title: fix: show automation details and pause outcomes when archiving sessions
body:
Closes #160999

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: archiving a session hides which attached automations it affects and can report success without revealing skipped or failed pauses.

## User Impact

The archive confirmation shows each visible automation's name, schedule, and pause status, including jobs already paused. Partial failures and missing pause permission are visible instead of being logged silently. **Unarchive and Undo do not re-enable automations.** Existing administrator and read-access boundaries are unchanged. If the automation inventory is unavailable, an explicit unknown-details confirmation offers **Archive anyway** instead of blocking archiving.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the visibility-scoped automation inventory for the preview and report automation effects separately from the committed archive. Preserve successful pauses when another job fails, keep receipts and Undo across view changes, and forward the outcome through the Control UI, CLI, and agent session tools. No database migration or protocol-version bump.

## User Impact

Full Gateway scenarios still require their local adapter, Gateway health checks, and (when selected) mock model server; this is not proof that those scenarios can run without local networking.

## Why This Change Was Made

The unchanged leased-fetch lifecycle lives with its run scope and is shared by readiness, Gateway probes, and published-upgrade scenarios. title: improve(twitch): reduce durable ingress test setup cost
body:
Related: #160922

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated database startup and polling dominate the Twitch durable-ingress tests.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. All ten ingress behavior cases remain, with real SQLite writes and monitor lifecycles; one new fixture-isolation regression protects the shared test-state lifetime. No production code or test case is removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tests now keep one canonical state lifetime per suite while creating fresh queues and ingress instances for each callback. The first real case still opens a cold database. The fixture joins every tracked ingress before purging the exact account queue, and refuses reuse if cleanup fails. Canonical cleanup closes storage before restoring the environment. Recovery still restarts the monitor on the same queue within one callback; duplicate and shutdown boundaries are unchanged. Explicit cold/warm database ordering and namespace-purge contracts remain covered by their core owner tests.

Terminal assertions wait for the real monitor to settle and then check the durable verdict once. The obsolete polling helper and two real sleeps are removed. Shutdown uses actual append-commit-before-stop ordering, not a timing guess.

## Evidence

| Additional fixture-isolation regression | 0 | 1 |

title: fix(ui): gate portal discovery and startup reads by scope
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-only viewers received a denied `portal.list` error. A restored or command-opened portal panel targeting a starting machine also called `environments.status` without `operator.read`, then misleadingly reported that the machine could not start.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Portals page now uses one read-scope gate for both request paths and one permission notice. Startup status requires the same `operator.read` access as portal discovery; viewers see that requirement without a denied request or a misleading retry.

## User Impact

Read-capable viewers can open the chat portal panel. Read-only summaries remain redacted; authorized writers retain previews and close actions. Viewers without read access get an accurate permission notice.

## Evidence

Fresh [before/after and authorized-flow captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160984#issuecomment-5960543691). [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37058278777) passed at `4f60a48678fa8e14869b8b72aa24f6df0645772b`.

Validation against main `c10b24f024432658a37e025660795a4f1034ebc1`:

- Four new regression cases failed before the repair: initial listing/startup reads and both paths after reconnect with revoked read access. The repaired portal page, Gateway capability helper, and server portal contracts pass all 48 focused tests. Authorized startup, unknown method catalogs, reconnect cleanup, redacted summaries, and writer previews are covered.
- Fresh Chromium recordings of the production Control UI with a deterministic mock Gateway show `portal.list` requests changing from 1 to 0, and a real `ui.command`-opened startup panel changing `environments.status` from 1 to 0. Both replace the denial with “This action requires operator.read access.” Local before/after screenshots were inspected directly.
- Fresh Chromium authorized flows through the production Control UI and deterministic mock Gateway both list once: read-only viewers see the write-access requirement with no iframe or launch link; writers load the real synthetic app in the preview iframe. The live sidebar computes the portal slot as available for both. Both screenshots were inspected directly.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview (default GPT-6 Sol/high, P0 threshold) is scoped-clean. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base c10b24f024432658a37e025660795a4f1034ebc1` passed, including all eight selected core-test typecheck graphs, UI typecheck/i18n, formatting, policy guards, all dead-export scans, and changed-file lint.

Stack refresh: only the three portal files from `18905f968ad5290b02156e0f12b38e48747dcae6` → `3a752d4cf29c3c30f60a14494c495d6cfdbec49b` were transplanted onto current main. Parent-stack changes and the already-landed sidebar spacing tolerance were excluded. The repair adds 22 net production lines for the shared scope owner and permission presentation; regression/test-support changes add 85 net lines. No server authorization, stored state, configuration, or dependency contract changes.

title: fix(ui): gate system information at the shared reader
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Session-only operators trigger denied host-information reads when opening chat, Devices, Connection settings, Appearance, New Session, or System busyness.

## User Impact

User impact: These views remain usable without host-information access. Authorized readers retain host statistics, platform labels, shared polling, and platform-specific workspace actions, including pages opened in the background. Server scopes and grants are unchanged; no migration or configuration action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

All automatic `system.info` reads now use the existing shared reader and the Gateway's advertised method plus `operator.read` grant. The reader also checks the current connection and permissions before exposing cached or delayed results. This removes the chat header's permanent per-client cache and the separate advertisement-only helper; presentation gates stop unavailable polling.

## Evidence

- [Current chat-header scope proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160982#issuecomment-5960747397).
- [Catalog/sidebar test repair evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160982#issuecomment-5961148000).
- [Debug fixture before/after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160982#issuecomment-5960902378).

- Before editing, the mounted Devices regression and eight shared-reader cases failed on current main. The bundled chat-header test sent one denied `system.info` request for session-only scopes. After the repair it sends zero; read-only and read+admin each send one, and admin retains **Reveal in Finder**.
- 232 tests across ten owner/caller files passed with `--maxWorkers=1`: the final main run took 17.21 s wall and the Config observer run took 2.88 s. Coverage includes cached/in-flight retirement, shared cancellation, reconnect/provider changes, authorized polling, Appearance, Debug, and New Session. Regression cases also prove background-to-visible resumption and delayed header results after connection replacement; both foreground-resume cases failed before their lifecycle repair.
- 18 production-bundle browser scenarios passed in 23.89 s across the dedicated chat-header, Systems workspace, and New Session suites. The harness rebuilt the bundle before running. Synthetic mock-Gateway request observations and inspected screenshots establish UI behavior; this run did not alter a live identity or Gateway.
- CI exposed a stale shared browser fixture: it supplied `system.info` responses without advertising the method. The unchanged Debug diagnostics flow reproduced the failure locally; adding the current core method to the default mock catalog restores it. Seven Debug/header browser scenarios pass in 30.11 s, including vitals while session-list reads are held. No production change was needed.
- Broader CI exposed two test-target defects: the Models publication flow released an earlier Appearance prepared-only request, and the sidebar owner filter matched the distinct People filter. Both reproduced locally (2 failed / 11 passed); after targeting the Models projection and exact sessions control, all 13 scenarios passed in 26.48 s on the final typed candidate. Production and behavioral assertions remain unchanged. Final changed-file checks and fresh default-priority review also passed.
- `check:changed` passed all gates, including eight core test type graphs, production UI typecheck, format, coercion, unused-export scans, and changed-file lint.
- Independent Codex review: no P0–P2 findings; final default-priority review also found no actionable findings after foreground-resume and type-import fixes. [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37063152814) passed at `2bbaedb4490f743345b28cbfdb3a8be0ae857127`, including every bundled and both real-Gateway browser shards.

The original Devices before/after images below are retained as historical evidence from `18905f968ad5`; they are pixel-identical because this is a request-suppression fix. Current chat-header proof likewise preserves the menu while reducing denied traffic.

**Before**
![Before: Devices same visual state with denied reads](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/287b9956-0b7d-4db4-a0be-2b1415f9a7cc)

**After**
![After: Devices same visual state without denied reads](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/335fecd4-f004-404d-9bdf-44937a3b0c54)

<details>
<summary>Review notes and proof scope</summary>

The architectural owner is `ui/src/lib/system-info.ts`; all automatic UI requests now converge there. The existing `canCallGatewayMethod` and shared operator-scope implications remain authoritative in the renderer. The server descriptor still requires `operator.read`.

Production delta: +37 lines (103 added, 66 removed); tests and test support: +346 lines. Growth adds final owner/permission validation, stops unavailable compact-tray polling, and resumes deferred foreground reads, while removing duplicate caches and gates. Header menu opening remains immediate while the existing reactive platform label updates asynchronously. No config, protocol, dependency, or stored-data surface changes.

[ClawSweeper revision 9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160982#issuecomment-5884116417) reviewed final head `2bbaedb4490f` on October 2 at 20:55 UTC: no actionable findings, before-merge actions, or Rank-up moves; browser proof accepted. The local measurements above apply to the repaired candidate; the final test-target repairs are included in that review. Final-head CI also passed.

Named follow-up: chat workspace-menu loading still issues `worktrees.list`/`worktrees.branches` without corresponding read/write presentation gates. Those separate methods retain server authorization and are outside this system-information owner repair.

</details>

title: fix(ui): respect read scopes for publication, PR status, and discussion
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI used advertised methods to start publication, PR-status, and discussion reads even when the connection lacked the method's read scope. Reconnects could also leave retained PR details and Discussion callbacks attached to obsolete permissions.

This cumulative PR includes the PR-status/sidebar repair from [#160979](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160979) and the Discussion repair from [#160980](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160980), both already merged into this branch.

## User Impact

- Chat, sidebar badges, session menus, and the sessions page stop issuing forbidden general PR-status reads. The shared snapshot owner retires cached details and pending loads when read access disappears.
- Discussion probes, saved panels, header actions, and retained loaders use the current connection and the separate read/open permissions. Saved tab placement survives a reconnect, while obsolete content and callbacks are retired.
- Session-scoped guests keep shared GitHub publication, including publication receipt recovery. The existing shared method-scope classifier incorporates [#162984](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162984) and [#162988](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162988); the old assumption that `sessions.github.options` always requires broad `operator.read` is no longer valid.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns authorization. The UI now reuses `canCallGatewayMethod` at the snapshot store and its consumers instead of interpreting advertisement as permission. Three store admission/cache checks share one predicate that reads the current Gateway snapshot on every call. Existing connection retirement, request cancellation, waiter settlement, and saved-tab placement remain the lifecycle owners.

Production delta: +89/-46, net +43 lines across seven production files. Store cleanup absorbs the duplicated gates and is net -1 line. Remaining growth carries concrete revocation cleanup and retained Discussion generation/client checks; there are no new configuration, storage, or server-authorization contracts.

Regression tests and test support: +424/-6, net +418 lines; no generated or lockfile changes.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `4e529baa8f6dc431fd93f8591859a022d29858fb`, preserving all four original authored commits. Fixed one test-fixture merge conflict and two expectations that predated shared guest publication.
- Captured the obsolete publication assertion failing on the composed branch (40 passed, 1 failed), then corrected the fixture to represent an actually unauthorized connection. Existing guest publication tests remain positive assertions of the newer capability.
- Focused UI proof: **166/166 tests across nine files**. After absorbing the shared-store predicate, **66/66 owner, deadline, and sidebar tests** passed. These cover no denied subscriptions/retries, cache downgrade and upgrade without revival, and saved Discussion tabs rejecting retained loaders before resuming on restored access.
- Chromium proof: **22/22 tests across five files**, covering publication outcomes, shared guest publication and reconnect/reload recovery, discussion toggling, desktop/mobile archived actions, and scope revocation. The final scope test additionally waits for the delivered handshake, asserts both sidebar badge and chat chip are absent, and verifies the connected session-only scopes after capture.
- Fresh same-route captures use the canonical settled viewport/CDP capture. Before revocation, the sidebar badge and composer PR chip are visible; after revocation both disappear while the transcript remains visible. The browser records no additional `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.subscribe` request. Guest proof shows `Publish PR` → `Open PR` with no general PR subscription, personal publication, or confirmation request.
- These fresh browser flows use the real production UI bundle and a deterministic mock Gateway. The original isolated real-Gateway authorization receipts below are historical proof; no new live role grant or external GitHub publication was performed for this refresh.
- Bounded `check-changed` against the pinned base passed: repository guards, eight affected test type graphs, UI typecheck, i18n verification, all three Knip scans, formatting, and lint. `git diff --check` also passed.

## Review Notes

Fresh full-candidate structured autoreview against `4e529baa8f6dc431fd93f8591859a022d29858fb` completed `scoped-clean` with no accepted/actionable P0 findings. This is the requested priority scope, not a claim that every lower-priority issue was exhaustively reviewed.

The [latest ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160978#issuecomment-5884092411), October 2 at 19:41 UTC on `596081aa`, identified the stale publication fixtures and the unresolved main composition. Each before-merge item and both Rank-up moves are addressed:

- **Unauthorized-reader coverage (P2):** the unit denial case now grants no scopes. The browser case now positively verifies permitted shared discovery while retaining zero broad PR subscriptions. Existing guest publication tests independently cover the shared action and personal-account restrictions.
- **Merge risk (P1):** rebased onto `4e529baa`, resolved the fixture conflict, and preserved main's shared/personal permission split and guest discovery coverage.
- **Integrated validation (P2):** the 166 focused tests, 22 Chromium tests, and final scope assertions above exercise the composed publication, PR-status, and Discussion paths. Both Rank-up moves are the same fixture-separation and conflict-validation work and are applied; none is skipped.

The current review is less than twelve hours old and the follow-up changes address its findings, mechanically compose main, and deduplicate an unchanged permission predicate. No extra re-review is requested. Exact published-head CI remains a separate landing gate.

## Original Proof and Contributor Context

The images below are retained from the original implementations. They do not depict the final rebased tree. In particular, the original publication options 1 → 0 wire reduction predates the session-scoped shared-publication contract and must not be treated as current expected guest behavior.

title: fix(ui): hide redundant publishing account controls
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Publishing a PR shows an account picker and several paragraphs of unrelated guidance even when there is only one account to use.

## User Impact

One shared account now means one **Publish PR** button. Multiple accounts get a compact menu with account names and a selected checkmark. A sole personal account uses an explicit **Publish as @account** action, without a redundant picker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Account discovery no longer shows setup advice for an unused personal account. Missing-account and personal-workspace blockers remain short and inline; publication confirmation, retries, permissions, and exact account/generation binding stay intact. Connecting a personal account never changes the shared default, and discovery alone never selects personal credentials.

title: improve(zalouser): avoid repeated policy-test storage startup
body:
Related: #160922

## What Problem This Solves

Zalouser group-policy tests repeatedly rebuild and retire durable storage for every scenario, dominating the suite’s runtime.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The group-policy suite runs substantially faster while retaining all 26 scenarios and real durable ingress processing. No production code, test cases, payload fixtures, or authorization assertions are removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the group-policy file opts into one file-owned state lifetime. Monitors, histories, listeners, and per-case runtime setup remain case-owned. Every callback receives a fresh real queue with the original `zalouser/default` identity. After the monitor stops, the existing queue purge removes pending, claimed, completed, and failed rows. Canonical state cleanup still closes workers before restoring the parent environment. Existing cases reuse message IDs across callbacks, so stale tombstones cannot silently suppress later scenarios.

Lifecycle, credential-listener, account-scope, and parent-environment teardown tests keep callback-owned state. Terminal-verdict checks use the existing committed-write observer followed by one real durable verdict read, rather than repeated enqueue polling. A five-second failure guard remains; it does not delay successful work.

## Evidence

Individual Linux/Node 26.8.2 observations using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, with compiler outputs warm for the table:

| File under `extensions/zalouser/src/` | Cases retained | Before wall | Final wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `monitor.group-gating.test.ts` | 26 | 25.46 s | **11.78 s** |
| `ingress.test.ts` | 14 | 16.06 s | 20.69 s |
| `monitor.account-scope.test.ts` | 2 | 10.05 s | 12.42 s |

The group file’s Vitest duration changed from 23.77 s to 9.19 s. The cold-lifetime files are not claimed as timing wins; these are shared-host observations, not a statistically established whole-suite or CI speedup. One final ingress probe rebuilt worker artifacts and took 55.10 s; that cold preparation is excluded from the warmed table, not counted as a saving.

- `pnpm test:extension zalouser`: **306 passed across 32 files**, including the unchanged parent-environment cleanup regression and real listener timeout/reconnect proof.
- After restoring the final five-second terminal wait guard, all **42 affected consumers** passed again in focused runs; extension-test types, lint, formatting, line-cap and public-import guards passed again. The remaining successful full-plugin and changed-gate evidence is reused for unaffected contracts.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <four changed files>` passed before that final guard restoration, including plugin contracts, types, lint, formatting, ratchets, and dead-export scans.
- Final independent autoreview through P2: **scoped-clean**.
- Hosted-review correction: the monitor can no longer satisfy the fixture wait by returning before messages are processed. A temporary early return in the real production monitor made the original sender-denial case pass; the corrected helper rejects it with the explicit early-exit error. Production source was restored byte-for-byte. All 26 group-policy cases pass afterward (8.88 s Vitest / 10.32 s shard wall), and independent correction review through P2 is scoped-clean. The single-file `check-changed` gate passed again, including extension types, lint, boundary guards, and all three dead-export scans.

title: improve: speed up large-buffer regression tests
body:
Related: #160922

## What Problem This Solves

Large-buffer regression tests spend seconds traversing every byte as a generic JavaScript object.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The same media-staging and realtime-audio regressions run faster without shrinking fixtures, sampling bytes, or dropping test cases.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use native `Buffer.equals` for large, ordinary Buffers. It checks exact length and every byte. Audio checks still assert the exact number of chunks and compare each position separately, preserving boundaries, FIFO order, copied ownership, capacity accounting, and cancellation behavior. The staged input remains 1 MiB + 19 bytes, covering two full 512 KiB copies and the tail.

The tradeoff is a labeled boolean mismatch instead of a potentially huge generic byte diff; the staging check also reports a length mismatch directly. Small-buffer assertions stay unchanged. No production code, SDK exports, dependencies, or fixture sizes change.

## Evidence

Same Linux/Node 26.8.2 host, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, with compiler outputs warmed before comparison:

| Test file | Cases retained | Affected case time, before → after | Wrapper wall, before → after |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `src/media/playback-transcode.staging.test.ts` | 7 | Complete staged input: 1,305 → 36 ms | 7.67 → 7.47 s |
| `src/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice.test.ts` | 22 | Copied audio: 1,351 → 3 ms; byte budget: 1,185 → 2 ms | 10.60 → 8.20 s |

These are individual local observations, not a statistically established whole-suite or CI saving. Wrapper time includes setup, imports, and compiler-cache verification; cold preparation is not counted as a saving.
