title: fix: continue steered chats after plugin reload
body:
Related: #156353

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chats failing after a plugin reload when a steering message has changed the transcript generation.

## User Impact

The original request can continue with refreshed tools without another prompt or repeating completed actions. Stop remains effective during continuation. No configuration, schema, retention, or permission change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Confirm steering at the transcript producer: validate the exact original and incoming messages, then install both private receipts from that same commit before publication. The native attempt joins accepted input through receipt installation before reload or terminal cleanup retires its handle. Genuine stale or revoked admissions still fail closed; there is no receipt recapture or whole-turn retry.

## Evidence

**Rebase update:** current head `6e1aba7c8c2976735d04ccc056e7f9d27c963656` is rebased onto main `6326f5c3702a5027f406ff483451e21f7154402b`. The database-worker registry conflict was resolved by preserving both sets of registrations; main entries and both steering registrations were checked. Exact-head runtime/compatibility validation is in progress. The results below belong to the original head `69e2648563106c0902f2c28c020897edea56b1ba`, not the rebased head; skipped draft checks are not CI success.

**Historical real failing-before/passing-after proof on original head `69e2648563106c0902f2c28c020897edea56b1ba`.** [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36506278348), lease `tbx_01m3nb51vtfynn46jjdr78eget`; Node 24.19.0 and native Codex 0.158.0. Standard `pnpm build` passed in **4m 43.3s**. The final remote receipt records `settled:true`, `exitCode:0`.

| Scenario | Original messages | Completed effect | Final replies | Reloads | Outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Baseline: steer then reload | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | Admission identity error |
| Fixed: plain reload | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | Pass |
| Fixed: steer + repeated reload | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | Pass |
| Fixed: ungated steering/reload ordering | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | Pass |
| Fixed: Stop during continuation | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | Pass: expected RPC abort |

Actual scenario test times: **47.506s / 55.618s / 56.783s / 47.793s**, respectively. Each fixed scenario passed one test/file. Cancellation preserves the completed effect and emits no late final reply. These are dedicated runtime controls, not a claim that the linked hydration workflow ran the full CI suite.

The proof uses a real built Gateway, authenticated RPC, installed native Codex, SQLite persistence, a real file-writing tool action, and actual `plugins.reload`. Only model inference is synthetic and deterministic through a local HTTP server; this is not an external-provider live test.

- Baseline source: `fb503c9e1f25d8c3877881e55e83d4378eda3676`. Plain reload passes. With confirmed steering, the plugin reload succeeds and the original continuation fails at the transcript-admission fence; the side effect remains exactly once. A separate recovery prompt succeeds without repeating it.
- Focused current validation: 248 core/storage/lifecycle tests; 44 Codex sibling tests; five production-composition lifecycle cases. Core, extension-test, all 21 source-test type graphs, root-test types, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Review caught and reproduced legacy confirmation compatibility, premature native retirement, and a logical-store-alias rejection. All three were repaired with regression coverage. Final independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean.

Known validation limit: the complete changed-check command stops at the inherited environment-variable budget (477 names versus 476 allowed); the scanner reports the same 477 on baseline and candidate, with no added names. No budget exception was added. The full repository test suite was not run. The historical incident build is unknown; this proves the reproduced invalidating transition, not that it was the only possible trigger in that incident.

<details>
<summary>Safety coverage, implementation cost, and reproducible checks</summary>

Coverage includes ordered/batched steering, unchanged original content and boundary, projection/raw-cursor invalidation, reset/branch/writer/database changes, copied-recorder refusal, live source revocation at commit, cancellation, unconfirmed input, and post-commit notification/cleanup failures. The transcript read-fence file is byte-identical to baseline.

Historical source tree: `3090224361cecef7571dfa47daa0860edd6fe0de`; changed-file content fingerprint: `062b80dbd96a8ea5d5cc695726c8d086502d0db595bfff17df0b73e9a18470ab`. Both were verified before execution, and the local source fingerprint was rechecked after completion.

Production growth is needed to validate and commit this transition through the existing SQLite worker broker rather than add main-thread SQL or a weaker generic rewrite. The old steering rewrite was removed; no generation-alias registry, competing continuation manager, new production SDK hook, or retry loop was added. title: fix(plugins): expose blocked hook permissions and recovery
body:
Related: #155227 (host-observed diagnostics milestone; declared permission requirements remain deferred).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: operators cannot discover why plugin hooks are blocked when the plugin is enabled and the Gateway remains healthy.

## User Impact

Plugin pages now explain **Limited functionality** and provide **Review permissions** directly to the highlighted existing control. Current warnings also appear in the Inbox, update results, and selected memory-plugin status. Saved, applied, and failed states remain distinct, with **Apply saved settings** recovery after a persisted activation failure.

Permission defaults and authorization are unchanged. Explicit denials remain intentional choices; upgrades never grant access automatically. These controls govern host hook registration, not a sandbox for trusted plugin code, and registration is not evidence of execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implementation scope directed by @jalehman: implement the host-observed diagnostics milestone across the existing Control UI surfaces, defer manifest-declared permission requirements, and validate the requested rebase/CI repair. No merge or deployment is authorized.

The Memory page changes render existing plugin diagnostics only; they do not change persisted memory, vector/embedding metadata, retention, or grant defaults.

The existing hook-policy producer now records structured refusals in its runtime registry. Existing request-owned plugin snapshots and generation-fenced UI readers project those facts; no log parsing or separate permission store is added. Configuration writes, application, and recovery stay with the existing configuration owner. title: improve(ui): keep live tool purposes visible in activity summaries
body:
Closes #160870

## What Problem This Solves

The expandable web tool-activity row loses the agent’s useful purpose text between calls and falls back to counts, forcing users to open the log to follow the work.

## User Impact

Users can glance at one expandable line to see the current operation. Within each disclosure, titles get a three-second reading window; rapid updates coalesce to the latest title. The last purpose remains between calls, and counts return immediately when the run ends. Failed/blocked outcomes and existing approval indicators stay visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse prepared, public operation titles in the existing disclosure rather than adding another progress strip or model request. The progress-card X could be inert on unfinished cards, and a successful click cleared the saved card for every client. X should remove it only from the clicking chat pane.

## User Impact

title: fix: clarify errors during Gateway restarts and shutdowns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes confusing “Gateway is draining” and “This turn ended before a reply” errors when a request cannot finish during a Gateway restart, update, shutdown, or temporary pause.

## User Impact

New failures use plain language, for example:

> Your request couldn't be completed: Gateway is restarting. Please try again shortly.

Shutdown and pause messages describe their actual state instead of promising a restart. Existing saved notices are not rewritten. There are no configuration, API, storage, or recovery-policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the reason already supplied by the lifecycle owner and use it for the shared admission error. Preserve error identity, admission checks, cancellation, and reset behavior. Replace “turn” with “request” in the failure notice and related busy-server message.

## Evidence

**Current candidate:** `aaba5b53ccb4462695d120402d60d4e13c111a7e`, tree `04096e59f79945918501d6c5eb6dc0b272a47f11`.

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36521426452) **passed: 145 successful jobs, 20 skipped, none failed or canceled**. Required CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses are successful.

The existing SIGUSR2-then-SIGINT startup scenario first reproduced the wrong restart message. The accepted stop now reaches the shared admission owner, so subsequent refusals say **Gateway is shutting down**. Admission stays closed, the original abort signal/receipt is unchanged, and a later restart mark cannot overwrite the stop message. Removing the redundant run-loop latch and reset callback keeps this decision with one owner.

The regression now waits for actual startup entry rather than assuming listeners exist after one event-loop tick. It passed in **3ms**; the new stop-promotion/single-abort regression took **0ms**. title: feat(google-meet): send and answer in-call chat
body:
Related: #2717 (the broader meeting-chat assistance use case; this PR does not integrate Vexa).
Builds on #152327.

## What Problem This Solves

Google Meet agents can participate through audio but cannot yet read and answer the meeting’s native in-call messages.

## User Impact

Chrome and Chrome-node meetings can observe native chat and send exact written replies through `send_chat`, the CLI, or generic participation requests. Agent/bidi modes can answer fresh incoming requests in writing; observe-only mode never replies automatically. Native-chat-triggered speech requires a current participant request explicitly asking for voice. Ordinary manual speech and Teams/Zoom behavior remain unchanged.

Requests retain stable IDs and durable results. Cancellation after native dispatch remains best effort: an `uncertain` result may already have produced an effect and must not be retried under a new request ID.

**Inherited participation limitations remain:** source age starts at first host observation, the 10,000-identity session bound fails closed, and direct source-free written requests do not gain a new host-attested operator-versus-model origin grant in this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Port the native-chat layer onto the merged participation owner instead of replaying its old foundation. The plugin owns native message discovery and delivery while the shared runtime continues to own source authority, replay protection, speech readiness, and cleanup.

The migration preserves transcript provenance and speaker metadata, pinned browser routes, corrections, literal guarded speech, and the written-default response policy. It also prevents a slow optional chat inventory read from holding the browser-tab lock long enough to terminate existing meeting audio. Inventory reads stay outside the audio-critical lock; page evaluation remains serialized and revalidates the session and URL.

## Evidence

Refreshed onto `main@76beb5685887`; tested candidate `5ca7f4ecaca0` (tree `0371b163aaa2`). Both attributed commits are preserved. The audio-lock fix replayed unchanged.

- **Tests:** 786 passed across 31 files, zero failures/skips, in 173.17s. All seven native invocations completed and joined; original JSON reports match the requested selection. Coverage includes every changed suite plus shared meeting, Talk, browser transport, Google/OpenAI/xAI voice and SDK siblings.
- **Compile/static checks:** the complete 67-path changed-check plan passed in 24m 26.7s, including core production, all 27 core-test type graphs, extension production/test and script types, formatting, lint, SDK/boundary/storage/import guards. Three nonblocking max-lines warnings are byte-unchanged from the pinned main base; no lint errors.
- **Clean build:** normal guarded `pnpm build` passed in 7m 8.7s. Build metadata matches this clean commit. Frozen dependencies; Node 26.8.2 and pnpm 12.5.1.
- **Integration review:** conflict resolution preserves upstream shared parameter-type ownership and combines both test inventories. No additional runtime behavior was introduced by this refresh; previous behavior reviews are retained for unchanged code.
- **Reliability fixes retained:** explicit leading voice intent, final native-source freshness, retired provider audio/transcript fencing, cancellation cleanup, and preserving consecutive exact spoken replies. These have failing-before/passing-after regressions from the preceding local work and pass on this refreshed head.
- **SDK:** 3,651 public exports / 2,113 callables; 151 public entrypoints and zero public wildcard re-exports. The existing browser-lock helper remains +1 export / +1 callable; this refresh adds no SDK surface.

**Still draft / before merge:** no live Meet, authenticated provider or device proof was run. The existing review’s source-free-send authority, page-session capacity and session-visible observer-error concerns remain open. Local validation does not resolve those concerns or establish merge readiness.

title: fix(test): prevent SQLite pathname failures in shared Gateway shards
body:
Related: #153340

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent SQLite pathname-changed failures in shared Gateway test shards when a preceding file imports the shared-state worker owner without its operation adapter.

## User Impact

No product runtime behavior changes. Gateway CI fixtures now retire their worker resources before later tests reuse temporary database paths. SQLite admission guards, permissions, assertions, and deadlines are unchanged; no migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker owner moved into `openclaw-state-worker-owner.ts`, but the non-isolated runner still associated its singleton with the old adapter module. The surviving owner kept cleanup callbacks attached to a retired database lifecycle, so even an awaited canonical close could miss a live worker.

Track the actual owner module and extend the existing cross-file lifecycle proof to verify that canonical close reaches the next file's resource. No new process boot or serial test configuration was added.

## Evidence

Verified against pinned main `3da238d5e385`, with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.5.1 on secretless AWS m7a.large runners (2 vCPU, approximately 8 GB RAM):

- **Fail before:** the original physical plan reproduced the same SQLite guard error in three deletion-lifecycle cases: 602 passed / 3 failed across 59 Gateway files. The nine title cases passed on this newer main snapshot; they are not presented as fail-before evidence. A cold-order diagnostic replay reproduced the same three failures.
- **Pass after:** the unchanged original Gateway group passed **605/605 tests in all 59 files**, plus its preceding **294 dispatch tests**. The original-plan wall time was 1000.21 s. Vitest result caches were moved aside to preserve cold file ordering rather than rerunning with failure/duration-based ordering.
- **Causal real-worker probe:** two ordered files reproduced a worker still holding one reference, with no retirement underway, after canonical close and fixture replacement. It failed before and passed after (12.58 s / 12.57 s wall).
- **Regression:** the expanded existing lifecycle test failed before because the second generation's resource was not closed, then passed after. One-worker command cost: 6.92 s before / 6.06 s after; it reuses the existing child-process fixture and preserves the existing failure-custody and skip assertions.
- **Selected checks:** the complete staged `check-changed` plan passed, including all four root TypeScript partitions, formatting, lint, dead-export scans, and applicable guards (678.82 s wall). No check was skipped or waived.
- Independent autoreview through P2: no actionable findings. The verified tree `1ddd228f8f43` exactly matches signed commit `16b08d69020d4`.

**Separate catalog limitation:** the public catalog-startup case passed in 71.502 s on untouched main, but a peer worker was OOM-killed, leaving that wider replay incomplete. title: feat(ui): recover saved attempts without replacing the draft
body:
Related: #156625. Third focused replacement, stacked on #160792. **Draft only; landing remains paused.**

## What Problem This Solves

Adds explicit recovery of saved attempts without replacing the current draft, replaying old runs, or creating a second queue.

## User Impact

**Send** refreshes the exact saved input and submits complete plain user text as a new message from the current user. It follows ordinary idle, queue, Steer, or interrupt behavior and preserves the composer draft, attachments, and reply. **Discard** hides the saved presentation in this browser; it does not delete Gateway data or abort a run. Incognito decisions stay in memory.

Send intentionally rejects commands, system/forwarded content, incomplete reads, and messages requiring attachment, reply, mention, or work-context metadata. Those retain inspection/copy or native outbox Retry rather than losing information in a partial resend.

**Limit:** persisted retirement follows a qualified ACK from the initial delivery only. If the replacement waits in the queue or needs a later retry, the original saved source can still appear after reload or in another tab, even after eventual delivery. There is no cross-tab exactly-once guarantee or automatic replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing saved-input reader supplies current source and viewer facts; recovery uses the ordinary outbox and send path. Same-client guards prevent duplicate admission, while only explicit accepted ACKs—not local admission, malformed replies, or receipt-free preregistration—persist retirement. Native Retry keeps ownership of its complete payload, including across run-ID rotation. Saved-source ownership is scoped to the current physical session without deleting older outbox payloads.

## Evidence

- Actual failing-before/passing-after cases cover malformed ACK retirement, unchanged-source refresh during Send and ACK settlement, native Retry rotation/removal, and a physical reset retaining an older outbox entry with the same run ID.
- **1,062 unit/consumer tests across 20 files pass**, covering real admission, FIFO, ordinary send modes, current-user attribution, draft/media/reply preservation, native recovery, settings, and scoped races. Submit and ACK normalization are not mocked.
- A real Chromium regression removes the first clicked row, verifies another row moves under the same pointer coordinates, and proves click two cannot Send or Discard that different input. Both cases fail before the click guard; the existing copy interaction remains covered.
- Full-source-app Chromium proof with a synthetic Gateway verifies refreshed complete text on the wire, local-only Discard, the unchanged draft, and ordinary queued follow-ups. This is not live-provider/channel proof.
- Production UI and relevant test types, lint, styles, i18n, line/assertion ratchets, production UI build, and independent P1 review pass. Docs MDX/formatting pass; standalone local markdownlint was unavailable. No dependency, timeout, serial-test configuration, scheduler, or hard-budget change was used.

The combined 20-file unit/consumer run took 14.10 seconds. CI timing is not yet available.

Fixes continuation scheduling being blocked when an unrelated configured MCP integration is not authenticated.

Agent-created continuations capture the currently executable, authorized subset and report excluded integrations in `warnings`. Explicit unavailable or unknown tool selectors fail before saving instead of silently disappearing. Trusted runtime aliases retain their canonical executable identities. Later login does not expand a saved tool ceiling; current permissions and approvals still apply. No configuration, storage schema, or protocol version changes.

**Intentional upgrade behavior:** older finite lists could silently drop unavailable names. New creates and explicit tool-policy edits reject those names, including named requirements alongside `*`; remove unavailable selectors or restore access. Existing stored caps are not rewritten.

Keep the materializer's policy/approval-filtered tools, carry its exclusions into scheduling results, and replace earlier interactive configured-tool bindings with the fresh scheduled snapshot. title: fix: prevent pre-reset history from entering plugin context rebuilds
body:
Related: #160613

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing host contract that lets context-engine plugins reimport pre-reset history when rebuilding context after a same-identity session reset.

## User Impact

Context-engine plugin authors can obtain canonical reset-eligible message IDs and payloads, then persist their prepared import under host-owned final acceptance. Raw and visible archive/search history remain unchanged; host compaction is not treated as reset eligibility.

Consumers must adopt the new `api.runtime.agent.session.readTranscriptAdmission` / `acceptTranscriptAdmission` methods for bootstrap and rebuild. This is the host-side dependency, not a change to Lossless storage or its summary DAG. The new snapshot contract supports durable SQLite sessions; incognito keeps its existing commit path. No schema migration or SDK subpath is added.

**Callback constraint:** acceptance and durable turn commit hold the agent database writer queue until plugin persistence settles. Prepare expensive work outside the callback; commit briefly to plugin-owned storage only, await every effect, and do not invoke host session mutations or nested acceptance there. This is lifecycle serialization, not a distributed transaction across databases.

**Draft compatibility blocker:** the new default queue hold can deadlock an existing v1 commitTurn callback that awaits a host session write. A versioned opt-in preserving v1 scheduling is proposed and awaits the required protocol decision; this PR is not merge-ready. The proof also observed duplicate current-prompt input on both versions. It was traced to an unchanged provider-loop assembly call that omits the current-turn fence; initial assembly/bootstrap are fenced. This separate pre-existing limitation is documented in the proof comment and is not claimed fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the canonical branch/reset/tool-group selector and history-worker owner to combine eligible entries with durable transcript/reset identity. One-use, plugin-scoped acceptance rechecks the captured facts under the existing writer queue, closing the read/persist race. Reset, branch/rewrite, session replacement and append invalidate detached work; ordinary reader-cache retirement does not.

Durable outbox replay uses the same acceptance owner. Retired ready turns retain their payload as blocked evidence rather than entering a fresh context. Transient projection unavailability remains pending, not permanently stale. Reset notifications are documented as idempotent current-snapshot reconciliation hints so delayed or duplicate hooks cannot archive a newer consumer conversation.

## Evidence

title: fix: prevent compacted context from expanding after engine recovery
body:
Related: #148569

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes compacted context expanding again on the next turn when a configured context engine recovers after process quarantine.

## User Impact

Queued and standalone context-engine compaction now operate on the configured engine's frontier, just as the next ordinary turn does. An unavailable or failing engine reports compaction failure instead of silently reducing only legacy history. Native-harness-owned compaction and native no-ops remain independent. No configuration or storage-schema migration is required. Existing configurations with an unavailable plugin now report compaction failure rather than legacy success; repair the plugin or explicitly select/disable it in favor of `legacy`. This intentional failure-path change requires maintainer acceptance before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry now pins fresh compaction selection without changing process quarantine or replaying a started operation through another engine. Pinned instances keep their actual plugin policy owner. Existing source retention, cancellation, watchdog, writer fences, maintenance, and disposal remain authoritative.

Native routes run before allocating an unrelated context engine. The obsolete CLI dual-path compaction guard and native context-engine projection were removed. Process-scoped subagent lifecycle fallback and fresh-turn retry are retained.

Inference and the independently persisted plugin are synthetic; Gateway, auth, lifecycle and SQLite worker are real. title: feat(release): qualify frozen candidates with their own harness
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Frozen release candidates currently depend on newer qualification tooling, so their tests and usable evidence can change as main advances.

## User Impact

Release operators can qualify a candidate with its own committed harness while independently trusted tooling admits the request and authenticates the originally qualified npm/Docker bytes. There is no end-user runtime change.

Candidates must contain the qualification contract and coverage policy. Missing capabilities require a deliberate backport and a new candidate SHA; there is no newer-main fallback. **Maintainer decision: approve this explicit cutoff for fresh qualification of unchanged pre-contract candidates.** Retained historical requests keep their original identities and recovery paths.

Publication approvals, protected refs, artifact integrity, leases, registry readiness, and rollback gates remain separate. **Hosted, nonpublishing permitted-versus-revoked final-effect proof, including delayed recovery, remains outstanding before merge.** Local fixtures are not hosted proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing SHA dispatch helper remains the sole dispatch/reconciliation owner. The candidate normally owns qualification; independently trusted admission binds the candidate, workflow, operator, normalized request, coverage, and captured upgrade baselines. Publication consumers authenticate this evidence without requiring candidate ancestry to the publisher or rebuilding qualified payloads.

Original and current identities survive child dispatch, exact/changelog reuse, and recovery. Reuse of product evidence does not permit old source-SHA artifact bytes to substitute for the selected release SHA. Explicit main qualification remains available for nightly/diagnostic work. Repository permissions alone do not prove that candidate code was reviewed.

The current-main integration retains strict selected-job success, rejection of retired advisory evidence, signed release-tag object binding, ClawHub publication-state admission, and the shared SDK/cache owner. Docker seed validation uses the existing frozen-catalog owner and distinguishes executable from assertion-only scenarios.

The latest repair carries authenticated admission authority to final publication effects. Docker checks it after payload/registry reads and immediately before every external mutation command, including channel promotion. npm runs the pinned publisher’s shell/planner/CLI and reauthenticates admission after preparation and publisher checks, immediately before each companion/core publish. No callback is serialized or reconstructed from unverified receipt JSON. Revocation is checked before each external command, not midway through an in-flight registry command.

## Evidence

**Current head: `15af7dc4a7bf8c0419dca8c60c7851927fc955d6`.** The branch is conflict-free after integrating `main`; exact-head CI is running. The preceding exact-head CI failures were attributable to stale conflict-era test resolutions and are superseded by this cleanup. No PR merge, auto-merge, release dispatch, or release publication was performed.

- **Causal final-effect proof:** on the untouched preceding production source, 13 Docker and five npm negative cases failed because writes continued after revocation—not because of fixture setup or missing exports. The repaired flow denies later writes after acquisition, asynchronous OCI reads, publisher checks, intervening package/registry writes, and manual recovery. Allowed paths retain exact artifact bytes, expected tags, OIDC arguments, and historical lineage behavior.
- **Affected tests:** 221 cases across eight suites passed across the final runs, plus four targeted workflow checks. The initial combined run had one incorrect expected refusal string; correcting that assertion yielded all nine npm authority tests passing in **8.76 s** wrapper wall. Docker red-before proof took **2.79 s**; npm red-before proof took **7.12 s**. The full CI run recorded 13,250 summed elapsed job-seconds across its executed jobs; that includes setup and unrelated selected checks, not just the incremental cost of these tests.
- **Static/review gates:** scripts and all four root-test type groups, scoped lint/format, runtime-cycle check (zero), all three unused-export scans (zero), line-cap ratchet, canonical actionlint/zizmor/generated-owner/composite checks, and independent P1 review passed. No limits, suppressions, validation rules, or authority checks were relaxed.
- **Broader retained local proof:** admission → source inventory → strict full-release evidence → both npm/Docker consumers; non-ancestral candidates; exact/changelog reuse; altered tuples/digests/attempts; moved trust refs; missing/skipped required jobs; frozen baselines; historical request recovery. Late-main conflict integration passed 609 release/policy/consumer tests, 193 checkout tests, and 325 post-export-correction consumer tests. These remain evidence for unchanged inputs, not substitutes for current-head CI.
- **Code scanning:** all seven Security High jobs passed. The aggregate CodeQL check remains **neutral** because 17 main-baseline configurations are missing; this is not universal scanning clearance.

The latest ClawSweeper review on the preceding merge head confirms that both stale-authority code findings are repaired. Its remaining P1 requested an explicit decision on the pre-contract cutoff; that decision is now recorded above. Hosted final-effect proof remains a separate proof concern rather than a demonstrated code defect. A fresh exact-head review is requested after this update.

No dedicated hosted qualification trace, credentialed OIDC/environment-approval flow, native signing, release-level cross-platform qualification, Docker publication, or registry publication was performed. Human-review readiness is distinct from merge and release clearance.

title: fix: keep node completion follow-ups in their originating conversation
body:
Closes #160602

Worked on by: @brokemac79

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @brokemac79](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/2299c100-01da-45ec-9a37-1db7b9b8f918)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/6db3530c)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes node-command completion and delivery-error follow-ups escaping their originating Telegram topic into the operator's DM.

## User Impact

Completion follow-ups retain the authenticated command's original account, conversation and thread, even when the saved session route or heartbeat destination changes. Existing notification opt-outs, target:none, direct-message restrictions and current delivery authority still apply. Legitimate direct-origin and explicitly requested DM work remain supported.

Legacy nodes may still produce foreground output plus their normal completion follow-up, both in the original conversation. This change does not introduce a duplicate-suppression protocol or a lost-invoke-result recovery guarantee.

## Why This Change Was Made

The synthetic completion turn was using execution/heartbeat sender context as its delivery conversation. The fix snapshots authenticated source facts before awaited raw/plugin node dispatch and carries them through the existing registry, completion event, conversation owner and finalizer. Captured exec routes are isolated before model input; unrelated generic/cron work keeps its existing owners.

The candidate has been deliberately reduced. The proposed result-first ordering, protocolFeatures negotiation, terminal-to-invoke recovery, second authority-state class, generalized generic-event holding and cron route-continuation/retirement changes are removed. Current-main features are preserved. The reduced repair retains 40 changed paths against pinned main 3856df48f5c953b26d17938b6888dfa2f3fa826d, rather than the earlier 83-path proposal. Current-main conversation continuations and host-generated notice policy are preserved.

A review also found that holding every failed completion could strand work when queue admission failed before any delivery owner existed. Native no-publication facts and actual intent/dispatch boundaries now distinguish that case: the original-route event remains eligible for the existing bounded wake retry. A queued or ambiguous delivery stays with its existing recovery owner and is not regenerated by another model turn. Deferred routes still progress after a permanent rejection.

## Evidence

### October 7 diagnosis and current-main integration

Current source: **3c1dce497dfd5025ca9c8060a96b52328a96ee0c**, tree **f2cf0a2c7e9be6f36ad8c8139e29e7108f77acc1**. After native observation proved a new conflict in `targets.ts`, pinned main **3856df48f5c953b26d17938b6888dfa2f3fa826d** was integrated. Its outbound helper consolidation is retained, including the captured exec discriminator, pre-await route copy, no stale-thread inheritance and exact post-refinement checks. This was conflict repair, not a CI-green refresh. Earlier source cf7fe6d9629ae had integrated main **947b35844d17083b6675224514a292fda61a5ed8** to resolve three actual conflicts, retaining the reduced 40-path scope. The node-event adapter keeps its captured authorization result while deriving types from the registry owner. The shared conversation-completion classifier retains producer-aware routing in both prompt and scheduler consumers. The consolidated rollback case keeps its typed queue/released/no-send assertions.

- **Current resolver and sibling contracts:** **191 tests across seven files passed**, **107.22 s** wrapper / **107.60 s** wall, covering ordinary owner routes, real-plugin captured route refinement, no-replay/custody, rollback sending, and raw/plugin node invocation. A new real-plugin case first failed when the exec guard was removed: an unthreaded captured group was incorrectly sent to saved topic 47. With the guard retained, `pnpm test src/infra/outbound/targets.exec-route-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **18 tests in 17.30 s wall**; it reuses the existing compiler/plugin fixture and adds no Gateway boot. Fresh production and Gateway-root/messaging/Gateway-method test types, changed resolver lint, line caps and diff checks passed. A fresh one-pass independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues; it was static, not execution. Hosted CI seconds remain unclaimed.
- **Earlier cf7 affected contracts:** 99 tests across six Gateway/heartbeat/real-outbound files passed, **291.05 s** test wrapper / **291.43 s** wall. This includes original-route recovery, queued/ambiguous no-replay, legacy bindings, scheduler controls and the actual rollback sender. All **46** classifier tests passed (**335 ms** Vitest / **1.53 s** wall); the new ordinary-producer control first failed against the text-only merged classifier. Four cheap classifier cases were added; no sleeps or new Gateway boots were added.
- Earlier cf7 core production types, Gateway-server/infra/messaging test typegraphs, changed-owner lint, line caps and diff checks passed. Independent chunked static review returned no actionable P0–P2 findings, with attribution limits noted in one context-only chunk. These checks are separate from fresh exact-head ClawSweeper, hosted CI and security admission. Current hosted CI seconds are not claimed.
- **The earlier local injection failure was not the CI regression.** The disposable read-only image mapped the OS account home to a read-only directory; Crabline's recorder failed with EROFS and injection returned HTTP 500. A task-only image corrected that home mapping to its existing writable private temporary home, retaining network-none, read-only root and all runner isolation guards. The native recorder then accepted the event and the same injection returned HTTP 200. No product, dependency, permission or assertion change was used to manufacture that result.
- **The executed Slack settlement failure is inherited, not called flaky or fixed.** CI run [37373053256](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37373053256), job 111975178155, tested merge **c413c4e7fb9fe833e9b22215a36345fd3285bd8a** with ordered parents **0e54386a46344884e0317c21b81d21b29ccdb615** and **f6e47a17328e09cd1545c3654d466a832e7fc1c8**. Under CI-matched **Node 24.19.0**, pnpm **12.5.1**, the healthy isolated fixture and identical diagnostic-only test edits, both that exact merge and its main-parent baseline reproduced the same failure: the preview control passed, then the visible child reached terminal completion with its expected marker but announcement delivery remained pending until the settlement timeout. Each run had **1 passed / 1 failed / 14 unselected**; candidate **160.20 s** test phase (**732.03 s** including build), baseline **166.97 s** (**750.96 s** including build). The original delivery assertions and timeouts were unchanged. Both containers were confirmed removed. This is historical baseline attribution, not a passing current-head E2E claim or a CI exception receipt.

No CI job was rerun to hide these failures, and no generic/cron announcement-settlement feature was added. Older successful review and transport proof remain historical; the successor must pass its own native admission.

### Historical October 5 integrated repair

Historical source: **f6e47a17328e09cd1545c3654d466a832e7fc1c8**, tree **b3fee2a26c8b71abb5b99151a965f86698038118**. GitHub later reported a real conflict with main, so this candidate integrates pinned main **a38b64b2fea5b16aa4352147187a8c8ab2e7413a**. The only overlapping PR owner was `conversation-identity.ts`: the resolution preserves main's removal of redundant normalization while retaining synthetic account/conversation/thread pairing. The source scope remains 40 files; no floating-main refresh loop.

**Affected proof on this repaired candidate:** all **27 tests** in conversation identity and actual delivery-custody routing passed (**97.78 s** test wrapper; **98.16 s** wall), including original-route recovery, terminal rejection and ambiguous/queued no-replay. Core production types, the infra/agents-sessions test typegraphs, source lint, line caps and diff checks passed. A fresh full-candidate independent static P0–P2 review was scoped-clean; executable proof was performed separately. Unchanged prior proof is retained below, not relabeled as new execution.

The preceding 617b head received a completed exact-head ClawSweeper review at **2026-10-05T20:38:45.252Z**, with no actionable findings, and exact-head security review succeeded. Its CI attempt still had never-started hosted-runner failures during the GitHub Actions incident. Those old startup jobs were not rerun against an obsolete conflicting candidate. This new head requires fresh exact-head review and native CI/security admission; no gate is waived.

Prior integrated source: **617b0ed0e78a62157048c8365cd4ce9ede0afe75**, tree **e293891b9a967731edc595d6534450c9f03f709b**. Integrated main **3ae653d838c4cc051739ec691c4c28112751b496** to resolve four real conflicts. The owner was corrected; all **16 affected continuation/notice cases passed** in **77.62 s**. The failed invocation remains failed, not retroactively green. - A native line-cap failure was fixed by moving the unchanged target-awareness helper into the existing session-publication owner, not by disabling the guard. All **5 awareness/lifecycle cases passed**, **54.31 s**. The moved helper body was checked byte-for-byte after normalizing its export keyword.
- Complete **changed-file gates passed on production candidate 7c21bf82b4b3 (exit 0)**: format and line caps, production types, all 27 selected core-test typegraphs, lint, dead exports, import cycles, schema/database and routing/auth guards. Earlier interrupted and failed attempts remain recorded separately. The follow-up passed fresh production types, the selected infra/messaging test typegraphs, type-aware lint, line caps, import-cycle and diff checks. Unchanged gate inputs retain the prior evidence. No guard, security review or permission requirement was disabled.
- The full 7c21bf8 candidate and complete follow-up delta received independent P0–P2 review. The final delta is **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings after repair; its source matches the committed delta. This does not replace current-head ClawSweeper, CI or owner-review gates.
- The subsequent 7c21bf8 ClawSweeper review found a real leak of terminally rejected completion occurrences. The existing native regression failed with a hidden held occurrence; the repair consumes only a published, owner-released attempt with typed permanent no-send proof. The final **55-case custody, event-routing and legacy-binding matrix passed** (**209.73 s**), including original-route recovery, ambiguous non-replay, deferred-route progression and admission of all **20** ordinary notifications after terminal settlement.
- CI on 7c21bf8 found two rollback assertions still expecting the former raw SQLite error shape. They now assert queue-stage/released custody, no-send metadata and the preserved original cause. All **6** real sender/SQLite cases passed (**38.45 s**); the single-send, intent-callback and media-cleanup checks remain enabled. The existing legacy test and a new captured-route variant both failed before repair. All **62 tests across the four affected files passed** (**186.01 s** wrapper), including permanent rejection, no-replay and late-admission controls. Two stale node-event expectations and one non-producer fixture key were corrected to the actual event contract without relaxing authorization. Fresh core/test types, four-file type-aware lint, line caps and diff checks passed; independent P0–P2 review of this complete follow-up found no actionable issues. Earlier CI attempts remain failed evidence, not relabeled green.
- Prior 617b production LOC: **+750/-251** (net +499); tests/helpers: **+1977/-64**. Growth carries authenticated route facts through the existing dispatch owners and validates exact route/custody boundaries; no second retry manager or persistence owner is introduced.

No current-head live Telegram run is claimed for this integration. The prior live evidence below covers the retained reduced behavior; changed continuation/notice composition was tested locally through native owners. Hosted CI and required reviews remain separate landing gates.

<details>
<summary>Historical reduced-candidate live proof and supporting checks</summary>

Historical source: **c1c7f16bfbd7fa1aef720fce9adba529cc166032**, tree **420f4c05e592ce10cc85d34dd8713b8b3cba7c19**. Actual conflicts were resolved against **260a31989937cb1ac3d2d0a2280a65ef5312a81a**; it is an ancestor. No repeated floating-main refresh.

The final commit changes only one test expectation/comment to match earlier scoped-route rejection; all production, configuration and build inputs are byte-identical. That changed test and its type/lint checks passed. Prior-head evidence is not mislabeled as execution of the final test-only commit.

### Real Telegram Test Server — reduced production candidate

Both cases used a fresh dedicated team QA lease, a run-owned disposable forum/topic, the actual built candidate Gateway and an isolated **released 2026.9.4 Linux node** with no result-first feature. Each issued exactly one harmless tagged printf. The model was scripted; Telegram, node execution, routing, message tool and finalizer were real.

| Case (2026-10-03 UTC) | Observed result | Wall time |
|---|---|---:|
| 12:50:28–12:54:09: completion send rejected | One native execution/result, exit 0. Foreground/progress succeeded; only matching completion send #3 received synthetic pre-upstream 400. Native error-final arrived in the original account/chat/topic. Later unrelated wake did not regenerate it. | 220.69 s |
| 12:54:45–12:59:04: completion and error-final rejected | One native execution/result, exit 0. Matching sends #3/#4 rejected. Fresh native failed-final settlement retained the original account/chat/topic; later unrelated wake caused no regeneration or additional execution. | 259.06 s |

Both runners exited 0. Native transcripts, tool-result correlation, wire admission/result counts, recorder receipts and rejection records were inspected; each rejection explicitly recorded upstreamForwarded:false. No private sendMessage attempt occurred. **Each unrelated main-session control emitted one private typing action** after that control started; this is not a zero-private-traffic claim and was not a completion/status message.

Cleanup is confirmed for both fresh leases: owned forums deleted, node/Gateway/provider/userbot consumers joined, credential state removed, lease scratch empty, and Gateway/model/Bot API adapter/node-bridge listeners closed. No paid model calls, new cloud allocation, production permission changes, personal Telegram, VPS or Surface access occurred.

### Local/native contract proof and review

- **204 distinct affected tests across 10 files passed after reconciliation.** The broad run took 223.42 s and exposed three diagnostic-expectation mismatches, not delivery failures. The corrected 17-case resolver file and previously unstarted 15-case conversation file then passed in 18.65 s. These overlap; counts are not summed twice. The broad invocation itself remains recorded as failed, not retroactively green.
- Twelve focused custody/provenance cases include real SQLite schema-admission rejection, actual outbound transaction rollback after writer admission, same-origin recovery, queued/ambiguous non-replay, permanent rejection followed by automatic deferred work, mixed unbound/tagged/untagged/invalid routes, and uninspected interval controls. The initial trigger fixture hit schema admission rather than publication; the refined transaction test verifies the actual no-publication reason and zero pending delivery/I/O.
- **10 final-effect authority cases passed** on the same production source (49.85 s Vitest). Real SQLite/session/queue/message owners and the real Telegram HTTP adapter sent to a synthetic loopback sink: allowed topic and explicit DM produce physical POSTs; forbidden account/chat and writer revocation/reassignment after admission produce zero POSTs, including queued recovery. This is native boundary proof, not live Telegram security-negative testing. These tests begin with pending-final custody and are separate from the no-custody regression above.
- Complete changed-file gates passed on the reduced candidate (359.95 s), with affected successor deltas passing (355.82 s and 323.30 s). Format, line caps, core/test typegraphs, lint, dead-export, import-cycle and repository/schema guards remained enabled. Final test-only delta passed formatting, type-aware lint, selected test typegraph and diff checks. No CI runs were manually dispatched; hosted CI seconds are not claimed.
- Fresh whole-candidate precommit/committed reviews identified actionable edge cases; each was repaired and regressed. The final whole-candidate P0–P2 committed review is **scoped-clean**. At that historical publication, the automatic ClawSweeper assessment was still pending; older b040 reviews did not cover that update.
- Exact production build passed, **371.82 s**, Node 26.8.2 / pnpm 12.5.1; pnpm build includes UI. The build report flags startup JS 365.0 KiB versus 364.7 KiB and CSS above its advisory target but below the hard ceiling. No all-budgets-green or independently proven baseline-attribution claim.

### Limits and historical context

The injected 400 is the existing Test Server adapter's definite pre-upstream rejection, **not** genuine server-generated thread-not-found or accepted-but-unacknowledged delivery. Negotiated recovery is no longer part of this PR. No blanket security, migration, deployment or merge clearance is claimed. This patch adds no persistent schema or numeric protocol-version change.

Historical evidence is retained: operator-reported **6f84cb9** failed with an error-final DM spillover; it remains withdrawn. **b040d3c** later passed an operator legacy topic-retention cell and two qualified team Test Server cases, but is not the final candidate. title: fix: preserve drafts during native CLI handoff
body:
**Contributor:** Vyctor Brzezowski

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/78cbd373-7500-4ea2-8a32-a670b5cb8ff7)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes losing an unsent draft or changing its saved model when switching between a normal model and a native CLI target.

## User Impact

The same composer, prompt and attachments survive successful switches in both directions. Rejected navigation keeps the previous selection and model preferences. The agent subtitle stays unchanged. Native CLIs still use their own account and configuration; this does not create an OpenClaw chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing handoff owner carries the admitted target through navigation, and the model choice commits only after navigation succeeds. Cleanup cancels only its exact prepared entry. Agent, placement and privacy changes stay locked during the short admitted transition, while ordinary host discovery remains cancellable. Cached route data cannot consume the new handoff before its loader receives it.

## Evidence

- Reproduced draft loss on successful CLI selection using the frozen preceding PR; compared the same viewport, prompt and theme with this PR. The textarea remains mounted, and the corrected state keeps both prompt and picker.
- Rejected/stale navigation and abandoned prepared-entry failures were reproduced before repair and pass afterward. A separate regression reproduced an agent change during admitted navigation and now keeps the draft owner stable.
- The full browser flow found a repeat-selection defect: normal → CLI → normal → CLI performed three targeted reads instead of two. A mounted-page regression using the real router and registered loader reproduces the failure and verifies two reads after repair, with edited draft and textarea identity retained.
- Final cached-route repair: 59 page/route/selection tests passed in 5.37 seconds. Mounted-page file: 17 tests, 6.60 seconds wall; new real-router regression approximately 461 ms. Earlier handoff/account/runtime/persistence sibling coverage: 286 tests in 17.86 seconds.
- UI production types, UI-pages test types, scoped lint and formatting passed. Exact cached-route delta independently reviewed scoped-clean through P2. Equivalent admission cases are consolidated at the draft owner rather than duplicated.
- Captures use the actual Control UI with a mocked Gateway. The registered E2E runner remains blocked by loopback HTTP 502 preflight; no live Claude launch is claimed.
- Verification isolated only the known PR160210 duplicate-export build prerequisite and restored it byte-for-byte. No prerequisite change is included.

title: fix(ui): include signed-in user in Online roster

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Online sidebar omits your own account, even while you are connected, and excludes your sessions from its displayed totals.

## User Impact

Your own account appears alongside other connected people, with open/running session counts, filtering, sorting, and a working activity card. It also remains visible when you are the only person online. Session “other viewers” indicators still exclude you. No permission or Gateway protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Online roster reused a projection intended to hide the current user from collaborator indicators. It now uses the existing complete, identity-deduplicated presence roster; its people card uses the same projection. Multiple tabs still produce one person, and disconnected entries stay excluded.

## Evidence

**Landed:** exact head `dfa6f0f409f2f0b94a07d9840097989d2028243f` passed [CI run 36475941240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36475941240) and the enforced CI gate. Fresh ClawSweeper review reported no actionable findings. Merged as `331628f27c20dcbacdbf4ac8deaec8ba2ee86542` at 20:21 UTC on September 28, 2026, without an admin bypass.

- Reproduced before editing production code: setting the existing sidebar fixture’s authenticated user to Ada caused seven tests to fail with `Missing person: ada`.

- Chromium against the actual Control UI with a mocked Gateway: verified own-user counts, active people card, running filter, deduplication, sole-user roster, collapsed facepile, and navigation to the user’s Activity page.
- Changed-file checks pass: UI and affected test typechecks, lint, formatting, i18n verification, dead-export scans, and repository guards; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Independent AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the production diff or the test-only follow-up.
- Initial CI exposed two stale assertions in the existing sidebar people suite that still expected self to be hidden. Reproduced both locally, updated the roster order/count and collapsed overflow expectations, and audited the matching browser suites for the same assumption. The full sidebar people suite now passes **139/139 tests** (**24.73 s wall**, `pnpm test ui/src/components/app-sidebar.people.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`). No production code changed in this follow-up.
- Current-main integration: CI’s merge result exposed `TS2554` after #160503 added an explicit-null identity test against the roster helper’s old signature. Reproduced the exact error locally, integrated main at `89c0030e4c451`, and kept that regression on the session-viewer projection that still owns self filtering. The failing typecheck now passes; **201 focused tests** pass across presence, sidebar, facepiles, and guest/self-profile handling (31.61 s combined wall). Scoped lint/format and a fresh independent P0–P2 review also pass.
- Browser-suite rerun limitation: host loopback preflight returned HTTP 502; the supported network-isolated runner passed Node/pnpm/Chromium preflight after selecting the pinned native pnpm, but its required runtime build was killed by SIGKILL before tests. This is unrun local E2E coverage, not a passing rerun. The existing before/after browser proof is unchanged; current-head hosted CI subsequently passed before landing.

The initial CI UI shard ran for 258.66 s before reporting the two stale assertions; Final hosted UI shard wall times were 367–418 s; mocked-browser shards 518–644 s; real-Gateway browser shards 395–402 s. ## User Impact

The composer stays within easy thumb reach on phones, with the same side spacing as Chat. Long prompts can still scroll, and desktop recent chats are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mobile welcome fills the available page, hides secondary content, and keeps the incognito notice above the composer. Narrow phones and short landscape use a compact welcome so setup controls still fit. The test change is one focused grow/clear regression rather than another viewport matrix; existing selector and mention coverage stays intact.

## Evidence

title: fix(ui): repeated Stop targets an inactive run
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated Stop clicks can keep targeting a finished run after another run becomes active in the same chat session.

## User Impact

Fresh authoritative history can recover the current run, so the next explicit Stop targets the work the user is now seeing. Recovery never automatically cancels the replacement run or broadens cancellation scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing history observation and run-adoption owners. Replace a stale local run only when the issuance observation is still current, the durable session matches, and the exact active-run set includes the replacement but excludes the old run. Preserve request/client/lifecycle/projection fences, pending sends, and run-scoped stream cleanup.

This is the independent three-file run-recovery half split from #160233 at the requester's direction. The composer visibility fix is not included, and composer sources are identical to this PR's main base.

## Evidence

- On main base fb1ca633ecce897fcc2dcf3e82c29364b3dc8742, added regression tests with original production source: **3 failed, 6 passed** (6.76 s wall). With this fix: **9/9 pass** (3.97 s wall; about 25 ms test execution).
- Relevant history/abort siblings: **266/266 tests across 10 files pass** (11.97 s wall).
- Proportional changed checks pass (313.02 s): formatting, guards, seven affected test-type graphs, UI production types, i18n, dead exports and scoped lint. Independent AutoReview through P2: scoped-clean.
- Actual Control UI source with a mocked Gateway and isolated Chromium passes both full-page and cursor-delta recovery flows (10.17 s). First Stop sends abort A only; the no-active response refreshes history and displays B; B's live delta is accepted; only the next user click sends abort B. No browser page errors.

Observed request order in **both** browser scenarios:

~~~json
[
  {"method":"chat.abort","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","runId":"run-A"},
  {"method":"chat.history","result":"run-B active in the same durable session"},
  {"event":"run-B delta accepted","stream":"Current response B. Continued."},
  {"userAction":"second explicit Stop click"},
  {"method":"chat.abort","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","runId":"run-B"}
]
~~~

The delta scenario additionally asserts history cursor before-B. Tests retain the old run for missing/existing active identities, a replacement session, live events during the read, lifecycle ABA, a conflicting pending send, and a late shared-read consumer.

This is mock-Gateway boundary proof, not live Gateway/provider proof. The first browser proof attempt had a selector collision with the screen-reader announcement; selecting visible chat text fixed the proof without changing product code. No full repository suite/build is claimed. The completed integrated-head CI result is recorded below.

### Inherited CI failure and canonical repair

Run 36460987596 failed in the unchanged Gateway config-commit projection fixture because its call to startGatewayConfigReloader omitted the required scheduler (TS2741). The exact tested base cb3755a3435d and merge cc8ec1cfe38f reproduced the same error; applying only canonical main fix [4bd105408ccd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4bd105408ccdac229eee8f719f082ba143f0c26c) made that graph pass. The 23 fail-fast-cancelled jobs from that attempt remain unrun, not passed.

Integrated main 548a1b899fd0 specifically to include that already-landed repair. The PR still changes only the original three UI files; their source bytes and the run-lifecycle/request owners are unchanged from the reviewed candidate. No unrelated scheduler repair was added to this PR.

On the integrated candidate e3daa5898e6b: the previously failing core-test-gateway-root graph passes (28.09 s wall), all **275/275 tests across 11 files pass** (8.68 s wall), and both actual-UI page/delta browser recovery flows pass (8.99 s wall). Existing red proof and independent review remain applicable to the unchanged patch. Exact-head [CI run 36478651039](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36478651039) completed successfully: 41 jobs passed and 20 were skipped (not passed) (16 min 54 s from run creation to completion, not summed execution time). Both CI-gate projections passed, and the fresh ClawSweeper review completed on this exact head with no actionable findings. The PR merged through ordinary gated auto-merge; no admin exception or gate bypass was used.

title: fix(ui): restore Steer for Gateway-queued inputs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Steer disappears when an unsent message moves into Gateway custody, even while compatible work is still active.

## User Impact

The queued-message chip keeps its Steer action after Gateway admission, with a busy state and a visible refusal when steering is unavailable. The composer draft is preserved. Local unsent messages retain their existing send/reorder behavior; Gateway-held inputs are never resent from preview text.

**Stack:** depends on backend #160275. No merge or deployment is authorized by this task. Both PRs remain drafts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Local outbox and Gateway-held input have different custody contracts. Local Steer stays with the send-action owner. Server-held Steer sends only the original session/run identity to `chat.steer`, then reconciles through the existing authoritative pending-input reader. Empty-composer keyboard steering follows the displayed eligible queue order and retains IME guards.

## Evidence

Refreshed UI head: `ffc9487b23ee568ea3c48c61256864c8db4e2111`, stacked on backend `3b8a4bb07de632056cb7bf1e1340264c59698e83`.

- **60 focused UI cases passed:** 15 compositor/projection, 34 composer-action/IME, 6 queue-custody lifecycle, and 5 retained-input control cases. These cover identity-only control, no `chat.send` fallback, duplicate/busy suppression, refusal reconciliation, retired input and draft preservation.
- Real current-source Control UI in Chromium with a **mock Gateway**: the base renderer had the queued chip but no Steer action; the candidate exposes and drives the control without resending the preview, while retaining typed draft text. This is browser/UI boundary proof, not a live-provider claim.
- Production UI and affected canonical test typegraphs, scoped lint and formatting passed. Backend composed RPC/storage proof is recorded in the prerequisite PR.
- Complete combined local autoreview against `63c25f72daff6906c011027195a3187c8d8b7f06`: P0–P2, two native passes, no actionable findings. The only subsequent change removed `await` from synchronous backend test cleanup; affected lint and standalone tests passed afterward.

Synthetic data; crops exclude unrelated UI and model-picker details. These inspected screenshots were also delivered to the originating chat. [Current proof and scenario details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160275#issuecomment-6580884195).

title: improve: remove model age and tier audit warnings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The security audit recommends changing models based on hard-coded model-name, age, and provider-tier heuristics, even when those names do not establish the risk of a particular setup.

## User Impact

The audit no longer emits `models.legacy` or `models.weak_tier`, or recommends replacing a model solely because of its name, generation, or tier.

**Intentional policy change requested by @jesse-merhi:** remove the entire name-based age/tier advisory feature, rather than keep patching its classifier. This supersedes this PR’s earlier GPT-version-only fix. The follow-up also removes tests asserting that the deleted feature is absent, as requested.

The independent `models.small_params` tool-exposure check remains, along with sandbox, tool-policy, authentication, and network-exposure checks. Model routing, configured choices, and permissions are unchanged. Existing suppression entries for the retired IDs no longer match emitted findings; no configuration rewrite or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete the classification collector and its helpers, audit invocation/export, mock entry, obsolete classification tests, check-catalog rows, and stale audit-guide references. Remove image-model reference collection used only by the retired collector, together with the filter that discarded those references in the remaining exposure check. No replacement warning, registry, or deletion-only test is added.

The narrower generation fix from #140012 has already merged. Main was integrated to resolve the actual classifier conflict. Against pinned main `71ef1c5d5483bb03406ab89ea110641caead6f45`, the final change is **9 files, +1/−236 (net −235 lines)**, including net −133 production lines. The one added line simplifies the existing collector call after removing its redundant filter.

`docs/cli/security.md` and `src/security/audit-config-basics.test.ts` are identical to that base. The original elevated-tool wildcard test is restored unchanged. Test changes are deletions only: the obsolete classification suite and one removed collector mock.

## Evidence

Current tested and published head: `8b049dbe26aab2260763af435ee577a63e90d984`.

- Repository-wide audit, independently cross-checked, covered all 50,717 tracked paths using finding IDs, collector/helper/constants, original messages, filenames, callers, exports, mocks, config/setup, tests, docs, locales, and generated references. No active remnants of the removed model-age/tier feature remain. No absence tests were added.
- Remaining matches were inspected: historical changelogs, general prompt-injection/model-selection guidance, unrelated provider migration/routing, and the live small-model tool-exposure check are not retired-feature implementations. Untracked build output and the separate published-docs repository were not audited.
- Existing suites: `pnpm test src/security/audit-config-basics.test.ts src/security/audit-small-model-risk.test.ts src/security/audit-extra.sync.test.ts src/security/audit-channel-readonly-setup-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **29 passed**, measured **83.09 s wall**, including **69.47 s** worker compilation. The unchanged elevated-wildcard scenario took **2 ms**; the existing channel-fallback test took **126 ms**. No test cases or assertions were added.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed. Focused repository lint on `audit-model-refs.ts` and `audit-extra.summary.ts` passed with zero warnings/errors. Formatting, both changed docs’ MDX checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The earlier full removal passed `pnpm check:changed --base 71ef1c5d5483bb03406ab89ea110641caead6f45`, including all 27 test-typecheck groups and full core lint (one existing max-lines warning in an unchanged UI file). That is prior-head evidence; the focused checks above cover this cleanup. Full monorepo tests were not run.

### Review status

The independent repository audit found no additional actionable remnants. The focused autoreview accepted the test, classifier-reference, and stale-check cleanup but raised one P2 recommendation to restore the guide’s model-choice triage item. That recommendation was not adopted: the item sits under triage of audit findings whose age/tier warnings this PR intentionally retires. The retained exposure check recommends tool/sandbox restrictions, and standalone prompt-injection guidance remains unchanged. This is a recorded scope decision, not a clean autoreview verdict.

[ClawSweeper’s exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160580#issuecomment-5875102063), revision 8 at 2026-09-30 08:15 UTC for `8b049dbe26aab2260763af435ee577a63e90d984`, confirms no concrete patch defect remains. Its **needs-human / blocked** recommendation concerns the policy decision to retire both advisory IDs for existing text/JSON consumers; it is not a passing bot verdict.

**Maintainer direction:** @jesse-merhi requested full retirement of this feature and, after being informed of that exact remaining policy concern, renewed the instruction at 2026-09-30 19:42 UTC: “get it merged please.” The linked discussion records the request. His active organization membership and repository `maintain` role were verified live. This bot-authored record relays the human decision; it is not a formal GitHub approval or a claim that ClawSweeper changed its verdict. Proceeding through the normal native guarded landing workflow on the renewed maintainer direction, without bypassing enforced CI/security/review requirements.

title: fix(sessions): keep steering queued while the target is busy
body:
Related: #160296 (session-control permissions; separate scope).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `sessions_send(mode="steer")` withdrawing valid guidance after 30 seconds when the receiving built-in run is still busy.

## User Impact

Explicit steering acknowledges admission without waiting for a busy model response or tool to finish. The receiving run retains exact-message cleanup, so pending guidance is not carried into a later unrelated turn after abort or handoff.

Acceptance is not proof of transcript persistence or model consumption, and the in-memory queue is not made restart-durable. Existing authorization, explicit cancellation, and already-submitted-input limits remain. No new settings, timeout increase, schema change, merge, or deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admission-only tool path requested a transcript-commit receipt using the reply-wait deadline. Expiry canceled the queued message before the receiving run could consume it.

The correction uses the existing steering lifecycle rather than adding a queue: explicit admission returns after enqueue, releases the completed caller’s deadline/listeners, and leaves commit or terminal cleanup with the receiving session. Calls requesting transcript confirmation keep their existing bounded wait; omitted options retain their existing behavior. Native Codex steering owns a separate queue contract and is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** both explicit-steer cases fail through the real session-send tool and AgentSession when a virtual clock crosses 30 seconds with the target response held. Both non-steer control cases pass.
- **After: 92 focused cases pass:** tool/SQLite persistence boundary (4), queue lifecycle (16), real session lifecycle (23), ordinary session tools (40), and dispatch admission/refusal (9). The tests prove admission before consumption, persistence exactly once after release with provenance intact, no extra target run, and retention of unrelated queued input. No production session was steered or stopped.
- Independent review identified a terminal-cleanup regression in the initial draft. A real abort/new-prompt negative control reproduced it; the corrected lifecycle now passes that control and commit/settled/handoff cleanup cases.
- Prior-head independent P2 review had no actionable findings. Production types, the three affected test-type graphs, type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap and whitespace checks passed on that head.
- [ClawSweeper’s 16:27 UTC exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160490#issuecomment-5872124410) on `f7701d22708d6e31beb1158cbecaec68fb2f67f8` is **Ready for maintainer review**, with no patch or security finding and no before-merge item.
- **Prior-head hosted CI was not green on `ac18338c2322b323ad8b22743a9b299300986ad9`; these results do not describe the merged head.** [Run 36436170082](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36436170082) has two originating failed UI jobs and a failed aggregate gate; 36 sibling jobs were canceled by fail-fast, so they are not passing proof. No CI rerun or unchanged re-push was used.
- [UI E2E 6/9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36436170082/job/108975518144): all three cases in `ui/src/e2e/chat-user-avatar-alignment.e2e.test.ts` time out waiting for `.chat-group.user .chat-avatar:visible`. I did not find the same case failing in the nearby PR runs inspected. Its independent recurrence remains unproven.

The executed merge `fc1d7e15e9446f861e4a042e6a95c77d8659fe3a` has the same `ui/` tree as its main parent `670415932ee7dc54d3d59c2e00870f55ed54004c`. These UI reds are outside this PR's changed files. They remain reported here for the separate flake-fix work; no UI test was edited, and this PR is not claimed CI-green or merge-ready.

title: fix(plugins): keep media-capable providers discoverable in Media
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: locally known model providers disappear from Media browsing when their manifest declares Models as its single primary purpose, despite their media-generation capabilities.

## User Impact

Model providers that also generate media can keep **Models** as their one declared purpose and still appear in **Media** browsing. The Gateway derives Media browse membership from locally declared image, video, and music generation contracts for enabled plugins, then carries it through the catalog join and pagination.

Peter Steinberger's [main fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/09bea762930) already restored the one-category manifests for Novita and Z.AI. This branch is now only the follow-on discovery behavior and its focused proof. Original implementation credit: @roboclaw-bot, with product direction and follow-up from @VACInc.

Requested by @VACInc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/13c21119-0164-41ba-b311-d87301f7f225)

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundled manifest contract permits one primary purpose category. After Novita and Z.AI returned to `models` alone, catalog browsing based only on declared categories omitted them from **Media**, although their video-generation contracts still existed. The before capture below shows the mock Gateway's prior catalog projection: both cards remain in **Models**, but **Media** has only the hosted fal card.

### Behavior and scope

**Accepted by maintainer (VAC), enabled plugins only:** capability-derived Media browse membership for locally known, enabled image, video, or music generation plugins. [Decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160473#issuecomment-5874001827).

The Gateway adds display-only `capabilityCategories` to local catalog facts and joins them with hosted categories before filtering and grouping. This also adds the optional `capabilityCategories` field to `PluginCatalogEntrySchema` in gateway-protocol and to the Swift `GatewayModels` contract. Only enabled plugins gain derived Media membership; disabled plugins keep their declared categories only. Speech/transcription alone do not confer Media membership. Declared purpose, permissions, enablement, provider routing, and execution remain unchanged. Remote-only ClawHub listings still use hosted taxonomy. No stored-data migration or live Gateway change is involved.

Related: #159688 surfaced the category-contract failure but has separate session-recovery scope.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

The real Control UI booted in Chromium against the repository mock-Gateway harness. The before and after captures use the same UI and locally known Novita/Z.AI contracts; only the Gateway catalog projection changes. All names and state are synthetic fixture data; Novita and Z.AI are enabled in both capture states. I inspected all four refreshed 1200×928 captures for the visible cards, selected filters, and private data. Each PNG has only image-data chunks and no embedded text or metadata.

| Catalog state | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Models | Novita and Z.AI | Novita and Z.AI |
| Media | fal only | fal, Novita, and Z.AI |

**Models before**

![Models browse before capability-derived Media membership](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16c03de6-4f13-4976-ba29-2379c9295dc7)

**Models after**

![Models browse after capability-derived Media membership](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14b2f303-f8ea-4ace-8140-920b3ee9ef20)

**Media before**

![Media browse before capability-derived membership, showing fal only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06aec0d3-359f-4708-9595-39bb76b6e373)

**Media after**

![Media browse after capability-derived membership, showing fal, Novita, and Z.AI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfea8a3e-86b6-4567-bdd6-3bd65b4d5f84)

### Verification

- **Head `0a6200970927206816cc5b8bcccd0f3d60bc2a09`:** the existing catalog projection derives `capabilityCategories: ["media"]` only when the plugin is enabled and declares image, video, or music generation. Declared Models category stays intact. Disabled plugins keep only declared categories. The hosted join and later pages consume this one projection.
- **Focused proof:** 95/95 catalog discovery, management catalog, and Gateway handler tests pass across three shards (54.80 s wrapper). The new disabled rows failed against the old projection for the intended Media-membership reason. After ClawSweeper revision 11, the Gateway test was corrected to use an enabled pagination fixture and to verify a disabled provider stays in Models and out of Media; all 23 Gateway cases passed again (30.52 s wrapper). Chromium mock-Gateway catalog case passes 1/1 (16.47 s Vitest): Models stays Novita/Z.AI, Media changes from fal alone to fal/Novita/Z.AI, and hosted pagination keeps one joined card.
- **Static review:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh staged AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 finding on both the behavior commit and the Gateway test follow-up. The updated Gateway test also passed its targeted typecheck, scoped lint, and format check. Measured owner test files: catalog discovery 30 cases/0.72 s, management catalog 42 cases/5.20 s, Gateway handlers 23 cases/43.57 s; the one-case browser capture is 16.47 s including build and browser setup.
