title: fix: prevent worker turns from stalling when group signals are denied
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a completed worker can leave its physical reservation unresolved when the host prohibits process-group signals, preventing the next turn from starting. Command cleanup could also kill the reconciliation watchdog before final workspace validation.

## User Impact

Workspace ownership is now negotiated per node connection. Updating the Gateway or node host first preserves the existing command route; the new route activates only when both peers support it on Linux with Node. Windows, macOS, and Bun do not advertise it. There is no operator setting to change.

Use matching current host/worker builds to obtain the repair on hosts that deny process-group signals. Refreshing only the portable bundle does not update node-host capabilities. Missing or uncertain cleanup evidence still retains custody.

The additive same-version SQLite certificate does not reinterpret legacy lineage receipts or backfill old launches. Released-npm upgrade/rollback and native Windows execution remain outside the bounded proof below.

## Why This Change Was Made

A per-launch subreaper adopts descendants and uses retained child-wait ownership for positive-PID signals. Only kernel ECHILD certifies extinction. Portable workers receive the admitted host helper without native assets in their archive.

Negotiated workspace commands use the existing process supervisor; legacy commands retain their prior executor. A separate fixed-code recovery watchdog is held by the persistent workspace runtime through command gaps and app shutdown. Its exact PID/start and nonce remain validated; release recovers the lease before retiring the retained child over IPC. The node-host PID is never used as a killable watchdog reference.

## Evidence

### Current queued-follow-up persistence join — dd3ce0508364

CI run 36526613589 failed the synthetic queued WebChat timeout case when fixture deletion detected changed SQLite session state. Source tracing identified an unjoined producer: the definitive lifecycle event starts real persistence independently of WebSocket reply completion, and its failure-notice append can prepare outside the writer queue. The fixture now observes and joins the original persistence promise for that exact synthetic follow-up run before deleting its session. The observer delegates the real call unchanged and is restored after cleanup. SQLite deletion guards, delivery assertions, writer drains, and deadlines remain intact; production code is unchanged.

The log establishes a deletion-snapshot mismatch, not the exact racing field/interleaving. The missing producer join is source-supported; candidate runtime validation belongs to fresh CI. No additional local test/type/lint suite was run. On the preceding eae2f0855217 head, the native mixed-recovery assertion passed in compact-large-6 (job 109271950217); the registry fixture lane was cancelled and is not claimed passing.

### Registry teardown fixture correction — eae2f0855217

CI run 36523102722 attempt 3 exposed two residual-root failures in the production spawn fixture after descendant model admission. The fixture called the zero-root assertion without supplying the shared settlement helper's owned-work callback. It now uses the existing finite root-work observer, as the registry's control and timing fixtures do, and joins completion tails before the same zero-root assertion. All model, authority, lifecycle, and cleanup assertions remain intact; no deadline, production code, broad mock, or skip changed. This is one test file (five additions, one deletion). No additional local test/type/lint suite was run; fresh CI and ClawSweeper will validate the candidate.

The preceding Koffi initialization crash on 63b20f4aa58a did not reproduce in its single diagnostic hosted replay: all 24 Gateway files and 272 tests passed. Its precise cause remains unestablished; a passing replay is not claimed as a code fix. Other selected lanes were cancelled by fail-fast, and are not counted as passes.

### Mixed-recovery fixture correction — 63b20f4aa58a

The stop-initialization fixture still expected `owned-anchor` on every supported host. It now strictly expects native cleanup on Linux/Node and the legacy contract otherwise. For native recovery it checks that the descendant certificate is absent before recovery and present afterward, rather than treating the legacy lineage bit as native extinction proof. The unrelated-container failure, preserved pending launches, owner death, and withheld-capacity assertions remain unchanged. The owner identity is retained before the mode assertion so cleanup can still run if that assertion fails. This is test-only; no local suite was rerun, and fresh CI will validate it.

### Main-fix rebase — d194fc1aef45

Main’s unrelated cron lint regression is resolved by [743c2ceb72e7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/743c2ceb72e7d1372845ea6f834bb82993fc9e0e). This branch is rebased onto main `1470a9bb092f`, which contains that canonical fix. The redundant repair PR #160942 was closed, not merged.

The seven commits replayed without conflicts. Every file changed by the worker PR is byte-identical to its `12b4ed3bbe92` version, and the resulting tree exactly matches the independently computed composition with pinned main. Both human co-author trailers are preserved throughout. No local test suite was rerun; previous evidence remains source-bound, and fresh current-head CI/security/review gates still apply.

### Lifecycle fixture corrections — 12b4ed3bbe92

The remaining broker lifecycle assertion on `22377977a146` assumed an intermediate relay on every platform. It now uses the adapter’s admitted `treeOwnership` to require the correct, exact broker-parent relationship for native versus process-group ownership. Root-result, retained-lineage, cancellation, and extinction assertions remain intact. A targeted source audit found the same shared-caller ancestry assumption in the completed-exec cleanup fixture; it now excludes only the exact test-host/broker identities while still requiring every recorded owned process to exit. These are two test-only corrections, with no platform fallback, skipped assertions, timeout changes, or new local suite run.

The follow-up on this head removes the unnecessary object spread in the freshly decoded fixture record, addressing CI’s `oxc/no-map-spread` error on `437fcc317156`. The PID set, assertions, and production behavior are unchanged.

The two app-server/CLI discovery cases in compact-large-12 on `86d3f207cc4e` assumed every MCP server had an owned relay grandparent. With the direct native owner, that grandparent is the shared test host or spawn broker. The fixture now excludes only those exact caller identities, obtained from `process.pid` and the active broker owner, from its per-server PID accounting. It still checks every recorded server-owned process for retention and extinction, including a real relay when present. **This test stays on the normal native path**; no platform override, production change, timeout change, or skipped assertion. No local suite was rerun; fresh CI validates the correction.

### MCP cleanup fixture correction — 86d3f207cc4e

The remaining compact-small failure on `86235f929aed` was six cases in `mcp-stdio-client.cleanup.real.test.ts`: their fault injector specifically intercepts the retained two-process relay, while Linux now selects the native owner directly. This fixture now explicitly selects the POSIX process-group contract via the existing platform mock, restored by its existing teardown. All six cases, cleanup assertions, deadlines, and real subprocess operations remain intact; production selection is unchanged. No local test suite was rerun. The fresh hosted run will validate this correction.

### Retained-descendant fix and conflict rebase — 60f69c15f310

The two failed compact-small shards exposed real contract issues, not CI noise. Ordinary commands now retain background descendants after their root exits; owned-worker exit still triggers immediate native cleanup. Process-group fixtures select that contract explicitly, retain their uncertainty assertions, and reject native certificates. The failing shapes reproduced first. **231 focused tests across 13 complete files passed** in 187 s wall, including the unchanged Claude prompt-retention regression, native owned-worker cleanup, denied-group subreaper proof, and legacy lifecycle siblings. All eight fix files match the successful pre-rebase proof byte-for-byte; both human co-author trailers are retained. No additional local test suite was run after the rebase.

### Prior main-fix rebase — 9cfd86b00b95

Rebased at @sallyom’s request onto main `80864601bf9e`, including the upstream [retired runtime-API guard fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5b76930a9b6fa1819361588e109417db6f7e0ab1). The bot-authored branch history was consolidated before replay to preserve its reviewed merge resolutions. <!-- roboclaw-integration-evidence:start -->
### Prior cancellation/CI follow-up — 1749fc7cd815

The abandoned-acquisition P2 is repaired: the host retains exact lease custody while recovering an undelivered acquisition; fresh-nonce retries join that recovery. An aborted duplicate cannot revoke an already-delivered lease. The Gateway reconciles the original nonce through the existing release contract and clears its capability pin only after a real successful release. Recovery uncertainty still retains custody. No protocol, schema, configuration, timeout, or security guard changed in this follow-up.

- Fresh independent review of the complete six-file follow-up is **scoped-clean through P2**. Production typechecking, both affected test-type graphs, six-file scoped lint (zero warnings/errors), and formatting passed on the reviewed tree.

Published code failed the cancellation/retry and missing-release regressions first. These controller selections ran on Linux; Sally's native Windows testing remains separately attributed below.
- CI run [36503214174, failed job 109199216163](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36503214174/job/109199216163) exposed an old crash-test expectation: killing the native wait owner cannot legitimately free capacity without an extinction certificate. The same failure reproduced locally. The corrected test still proves death of all three witnessed PIDs, and additionally verifies the missing certificate, retained durable launch/slot, and refusal of shutdown to invent cleanup. Legacy and other crash paths still require normal capacity release. **All 80 worker-runtime tests passed in original order** (54.30 s Vitest / 59.91 s wrapper); scoped lint and its test-type graph passed. No CI rerun, skipped assertion, timeout inflation, or production relaxation was used.
- The preceding conflict integration includes main through 27de2f87db28 and warm-worker retention #160265. Earlier connected A/B and package results remain bound to their recorded trees; no current-head stock OpenShell/live-model or published-driver upgrade result is claimed.
- The inherited supervisor size finding remains disclosed: main has 1,322 counted lines versus the 700 cap; the two lifecycle integration lines make 1,324. No limit, suppression, or baseline was changed. This is not described as locally green.

**Maintainer disposition:** retain this PR's existing additive companion-table design and its documented older-reader and uncertain-cleanup behavior. @sallyom explicitly directed landing this implementation on green CI after the blocking cancellation fix, considers the available qualification sufficient, and reports Windows regression testing. The unfinished released-driver upgrade/backup-restore rehearsal is deferred, not claimed as a pass. Required current-head CI/security/review gates still apply; this is not an admin exception.
<!-- roboclaw-integration-evidence:end -->

### Compatibility review follow-up — 43db86221493 (implementation 192467612c424)

- **P1:** The Gateway no longer unconditionally sends typed quiescence to older hosts. A server-capability-gated node declaration selects lease and foreground ownership together. The lease dialect stays pinned; capability withdrawal is rechecked at dispatch. A legacy acquisition remains on its prior route even if the node gains support between selection and invocation.

title: improve(ui): edit model and reasoning while replies run
body:
Closes #160428

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI prevents users from choosing a model or reasoning effort while a reply is in progress, even when they only want to change the preference for waiting work.

## User Impact

Users with existing write access can change model and reasoning preferences during sending, preparation, and streaming. The selector displays the chosen preference immediately, with no next-turn badge or toast. Already admitted turns keep their settings; ordinary waiting messages use the latest successfully saved preference, preserving explicit-turn thinking overrides.

Model-switch-in-progress, offline/backend, sharing/role, model-validation, rollback, and stale-navigation/reconnect protections remain. Fast, account, and context-window controls retain their existing busy guards. No native-app or administrator-policy changes.

**Maintainer direction:** @steipete has requested this busy-time model/reasoning preference behavior and authorized repair and landing. Current-main conflicts are resolved; repaired queued-selection races are covered by regression tests. No deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

This deliberately changes the previous busy-state UX policy; it does not hot-switch an executing model call. The preference selector no longer borrows its label from an active/fallback execution. The now-unused selector-only observation cache is removed; recorded execution metadata is unchanged.

Thinking-only patches now refresh waiting work without rebinding its model/account or clearing fallback provenance. Queued selection is copied at the admission owner's writer fence—not before waiting or after source adoption—so a concurrent committed preference is included, but later edits cannot change the admitted turn or its lifecycle bindings.

## Evidence

- Final-head CI passed: [run 38022861806](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38022861806), head `31892600062dfd9ee4a16f736d7591947978bef9`.

- Red/green regressions for sending/preparing/streaming controls, denied states, and thinking-only queue updates.
- Real `sessions.patch`, storage, queue drain, and admission tests: A stays on X; waiting B/C follow Y; after B is admitted, Z changes only C. Deterministic barriers reproduce and fix the pre-admission stale-copy race and check the post-admission boundary.
- Explicit thinking/default precedence, rejected patches, queued route/auth/fallback preservation, model-switch consistency, settings/send ordering, rollback, stale ownership, and retained execution metadata are covered.
- Fresh Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean after resolving the admission race.
- Actual baseline and candidate production UI builds, matched light theme and 1200 × 853 viewport, with synthetic public-safe models/content. **Screenshots use a deterministic mock Gateway, not paid/live inference.** The interaction proof saves model and effort while the same reply continues; no abort or replacement send occurs.

**Current-main repair:** queued fallback probes now retain their admission-fenced model/account through execution, and thinking-only `/think` commands refresh waiting work without rebinding its route. The bundled browser E2E now passes (1.73 s test time; 29.06 s including build/startup), closing the earlier loopback-preflight gap. Backend boundary tests: 240 passed across 11 files (166.53 s wall including 35.54 s shared compilation). Updated UI coverage: 229 passed across four files; the final two changed test files passed 178 tests in 12.27 s wall. P0–P2 autoreview of repaired production head `77d63d665c4b` is scoped-clean; later commits only align inspected test expectations with this approved behavior. The inherited catalog browser expectations were updated for this intentional display-policy change: both affected browser files now pass all 13 cases (87.66 s including build/compiler startup; desktop/mobile fallback cases 2.67/2.34 s). The remaining runtime-label and mounted-pane expectations were aligned too: 34 cases passed in 12.63 s, with execution-metadata and reentrant-event assertions retained. Core/UI types, all selected test type graphs across completed runs, and changed-file lint pass. One full local check stopped on an intermittent native TypeScript compiler nil-pointer panic in the agents-sessions graph; a scoped repeat passed without source changes. The compiler cause is unresolved, and no single all-green full local gate, live-provider, or full-suite pass is claimed.

The before/after images below are the original PR’s inspected synthetic production-bundle captures; current-main behavior was reverified by the bundled browser test.

### After

title: fix(ui): preview cards ignore external browser preference
body:
Related: #159887

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Browser preview cards now honor **Open links outside OpenClaw**. Their image and **Open** button use the external browser when that preference is on; the menu still offers **Open in OpenClaw** for the managed tab. Turning the preference off restores the managed-tab primary action and **Open in new tab** menu action. The choice updates immediately.

## What Problem This Solves

### Root Cause

The earlier preference change routed ordinary links, but preview cards used their own button handlers. Before this fix, both primary handlers always opened the managed browser panel and never read the browser-local preference. The original web and native card regression cases failed on that behavior while the pre-existing card cases passed.

## Change

The card subscribes to the existing theme preference and uses the existing safe external URL and native-link handoff for external opening. Explicit internal opening retains the original managed tab identity. The settings text and action label describe the actual choice. No new settings, shared configuration, or migration.

## Evidence

### Verification

- **Card routing:** 31/31 focused card tests passed, including live preference changes, both primary actions, web and native external routes, alternate menu actions, and managed tab identity. Focused Vitest wall time: 4.98 s. The card source and tests are unchanged since that run.
- **Real behavior proof:** In the actual Control UI on Chromium with a synthetic Gateway, enable **Open links outside OpenClaw**, render a browser preview card, then click its image and **Open** button. Both opened external tabs. Inspected before/after screenshots below show the menu changing from **Open in new tab** to **Open in OpenClaw**. The focused card cases prove that the alternate action retains the original managed tab identity and that turning the preference off restores internal opening. The native route was exercised at the WebKit bridge boundary.
- **Related UI fixture proof:** The existing lifecycle E2E suite passed 16/16 after settling the Stop mock's canonical state. The existing reasoning E2E suite passed 12/12 (28.30 s Vitest wall including build) after waiting for the effort control's enabled state before its single click. No production behavior, assertions, retries, or timeouts changed in those fixture repairs.
- **Local checks:** UI/E2E types, focused lint, i18n, formatting, line-cap, and whitespace checks passed on the applicable reviewed changes. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defect. [ClawSweeper reviewed the current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160410#issuecomment-5869368377), `57a0f882561b49eee1726e1fac7cc291c8ad3fde`, at 16:33 UTC and reported no findings, security issues, or before-merge items. Its exact-head receiver completed successfully.
- **Exact-head CI is blocked:** [Run 36450892803, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36450892803) failed `check-source-contracts` on nine daemon/update export-name collisions. This is not green CI. The current-head PR-context, dependency, and security-sensitive checks passed; other job coverage must not be inferred from the failed run.

### Upstream blocker

The failing guard scans `src/` definitions, not this UI change. CI checked out merge `e11600cf99f438210041759ec909782571f3d7fe` over main base `abb37032e7f7be346c8aea410ece8cd27e4f2cf2`. The guard and all six collision-bearing modules have identical Git blobs in that base and the tested merge. Running the guard’s exported analyzer on those six modules reproduced the same nine collisions in both trees (a targeted comparison, not a full baseline suite). The affected wrappers were introduced by [the upstream lazy service-entry change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5de949fc4620b4c62d05d780caa11870dad506ac).

This PR does not change CLI/update code or weaken the guard. Green CI remains blocked on an upstream daemon/update export-contract repair. No merge, unrelated CLI repair, or CI rerun was performed.


### CI fixture follow-up

The avatar timeout also occurred on [main before this PR run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36437289300/job/108978848910). Actual Chromium reproduction identified an incomplete fixture, not an alignment change: the owner-sharing header called `session.members.listEvidence`, but the mock returned its generic `{ ok: true }` fallback. Accessing the required members array interrupted rendering and left the loaded transcript hidden behind its initial skeleton.

The fixture now supplies a typed sharing-evidence response with the required arrays and matching session/role. Real-browser own/other avatar checks pass with zero vertical offset and a 10px side gap. All original geometry and multiline assertions remain; no production code, retries or timeouts changed. Scoped types, lint, line-cap, formatting and independent P0–P2 review pass. Full focused Blacksmith Testbox run: **24/24 pass** (avatar 3/3 in 3.588 s; unchanged hovercard 21/21 in 32.623 s, including the 390px/dark case in 1.310 s). Vitest wall time: 49.86 s including build. [Runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36450323618), lease `tbx_01m3md2tttk4ck7e7zs8ba8eh6`, command exit 0; lease stopped. No new cases, browser boots, waits or timeout increases.

The separate 390px/dark hovercard timeout was not reproduced in the direct Chromium check, and the hovercard code and assertions remain unchanged. Its prior CI failure is not claimed fixed or proven unrelated.

### What was not tested

A fresh signed macOS application run was not made. Native handoff is covered at the WebKit bridge boundary. The Chromium proof used synthetic Gateway data, not a live Gateway or real user data.

title: fix(ui): reconcile System theme on foreground restore
body:
## What Problem This Solves

With **System** appearance selected, returning to a backgrounded Control UI can leave the page showing the opposite color scheme until another media-query event arrives. The theme owner currently accepts background observations but does not reconcile appearance when the document becomes visible or returns from the back-forward cache.

This remains reproducible after rebasing onto `162dea17b03112d48c0f5c6f4b73f0da7a025233`, using a controlled root-document lifecycle sequence.

## User Impact

System appearance is reconciled immediately on foreground restoration, without waiting for a Gateway reconnect or a preference change. Temporary background observations no longer replace its last admitted mode. Explicit Light/Dark choices remain independent.

**Limit:** this verifies a reproducible lifecycle defect, not elimination of every physical iOS 26 Home Screen flash. A transient observed while still visible can still be displayed; restoration uses the browser's fresh value rather than a debounce or a guessed settling delay.

**Unverified first-frame risk:** a genuine OS appearance change while the page is hidden is deferred until foreground reconciliation. If the browser presents the old page or a saved snapshot before that handler updates presentation, a visible old-to-new transition can still occur. If reconciliation happens before the first visible paint, it need not flash. The current tests verify DOM state after the handler, not the first restored frame. The blanket hidden-state freeze therefore needs real-device evaluation; this is not a demonstrated fix for the original iOS flash.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one System-mode snapshot in the existing theme owner, shared by presentation and resolved-mode consumers. Refresh it while visible and reconcile it on visible `visibilitychange` / persisted `pageshow`. Palette completion and preference/catalog publications use the same snapshot.

Preserves catalog single-mode precedence, palette generation fences, legacy media-query listener cleanup, and the recent navigation-only preference optimization. No timers, user-agent branches, persistence changes, or Gateway changes.

Production delta: **+30 net lines** for the owner-held observation and lifecycle registration/cleanup; regression tests are separate. The previous independent presentation/getter sampling is removed rather than adding a second theme manager.

## Evidence

- Rebased baseline: **10 failing / 4 passing** in the new 14-case owner regression; the same tests all pass with the fix.
- Focused suite: **53 passing tests** across System lifecycle, presentation/navigation, theme resolution, and catalog behavior.
- Baseline and fixed Control UI production builds pass.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passes formatting, lint, UI production and selected test typechecks, i18n and repository guards.
- New-test cost: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/bootstrap-theme.system.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **1.86 s wrapper wall**, 1.08 s Vitest duration, 14 passing cases. No timers, sleeps, polling, or per-test Gateway boots. CI timing is not yet available.
- Actual built UI in **WebKit 26.6**, mobile 390×844: visible Dark → delivered Light → hidden → raw Dark without delivery → visible. Baseline remains Light; fixed UI is Dark synchronously, before another task or media event. Screenshots use synthetic chat content, not private phone logs.
- AutoReview, local candidate against the pinned base, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**.

### Controlled WebKit reproduction

Both captures are immediately after foreground return, with **System selected and a Dark root query**. This is the actual built UI with synthetic chat content and controlled lifecycle inputs—not physical iOS suspension.

| Before: stale Light | After: reconciled Dark |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before — System retains stale Light after foreground return](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/489c50f5-edd4-42b2-ab7e-9e15be6f790c) | ![After — System restores Dark on foreground return](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bcee9c35-72c2-45c6-9207-9f615ef5e7b8) |

Thanks to @hxy91819 (Mason) for reporting the problem and providing reproduction observations.

title: fix(test): avoid service-permission failures before tests start
body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Fixes runtime-consuming tests failing before the first test starts when the caller cannot read an unrelated Gateway’s protected service environment.

### User Impact

Local Vitest and E2E preparation use the explicit build path rather than invoking the CLI to trigger an automatic rebuild. Fresh artifacts remain reusable without a writable checkout; canceled preparation joins its writers before releasing ownership.

**Boundary:** outputs remain in the selected checkout. This is not a new filesystem sandbox. Preparation uses the existing live-Gateway overlap fence and checks loaded services plus potential Gateway definitions before artifact publication. It refuses when their safety cannot be verified; unreadable unrelated unit files do not block local preparation. Use the existing isolated runner when enforced filesystem isolation is needed. Automatic source-CLI rebuilds and actual update publication retain their strict service/maintenance checks unchanged. No production permissions, configuration, service, credentials, or database state are changed by this PR.

### Root Cause

Test preparation ran `scripts/run-node.mjs --version`. A missing runtime or private-QA entry therefore entered the automatic CLI rebuild’s service-publication transaction, which can require protected environment files before determining whether the checkout is unrelated.

The dedicated prerequisite entry reuses the existing source freshness predicates, explicit build profile, runtime postbuild, checkout artifact ownership, and live-dist fence. It checks freshness before requesting write ownership and rechecks after acquisition. The existing cancelable-command owner carries cancellation through lock waits and compiler execution; incomplete child cleanup still retains ownership. No new agent instructions, build bypass flags, or test-selection changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Local test preparation could enter a CLI rebuild transaction and read an unrelated Gateway's protected service environment before the first test ran. This PR routes that preparation through its owned build entry and keeps artifact writers joined before releasing ownership.

### Service-start concurrency decision

[VAC accepted the documented service-start race](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160392#issuecomment-5874002140). The pre-test build fence rejects physically shared compiler output roots, while a Gateway starting after admission remains a documented local-operator concurrency risk. No service-activation coordination is required for this PR. This head makes no further fence-semantics change.

## Evidence

The real preparation boundary and shared-output fence passed 61/61 focused cases on the prior code head. The final merge-head fixture test passed 39/39, and all root-test type graphs passed. Hosted exact-head CI and ClawSweeper review are in progress.

## Verification

### Real behavior proof

On the published `d890f517761910574aeed6635d4510e28e422535` head, `pnpm test test/scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.test.ts test/scripts/live-gateway-dist-fence.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **61/61**. The real preparation/build-admission boundary refuses before the compiler runs when `dist-runtime` or `packages/sdk/dist` physically aliases a live Gateway's output while `dist` is separate. A disjoint service remains admitted. The changed preparation file alone passed **15/15** (`pnpm test test/scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 39.13 s shard wall, 36.87 s Vitest, 0.238 s test execution). Script and root-test type graphs, focused lint, formatting, diff check, and independent P1 autoreview passed.

### What was not tested

No live Gateway was restarted or modified. The shared-output proof uses filesystem symlinks in an isolated fixture; no real bind mount or production Gateway was used. Exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review are pending.



### Current head: `a366159e4f2794469ece0c7cafea4657d546243c`

- Final, frozen-base merge commit `a366159e4f2794469ece0c7cafea4657d546243c` integrates `origin/main` at `25d771cb8203f5afeea7b7c9dc8060210db8e43d` solely to clear the bounded-Vitest fixture conflict. Main already has the AI-declaration fixture repair from #160532. The resolved `test/scripts/run-vitest-bounded.test.ts` starts from main and differs only in this PR's two `scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs` spawn-matcher substitutions; the duplicate fixture repair from `5b31a0945f6` is gone.
- Focused file passed **39/39** (`pnpm test test/scripts/run-vitest-bounded.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 42.38 s shard wall / 41.16 s Vitest duration). `pnpm tsgo:test:root` passed tooling, scripts, E2E, and other shards. `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head CI settled with the inherited source-contracts failure described below; ClawSweeper re-review is in progress.
- [VAC accepted the P2 service-start race as documented](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160392#issuecomment-5874002140). No further fence semantics were changed. No further main integration will be made on this branch.

### Exact-head CI

- [`check-source-contracts` job 109022525871](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449947535/job/109022525871) failed `lint:tmp:export-name-collisions`. This is inherited from [main commit `5de949fc462`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5de949fc462), brought in by the final merge. It added daemon CLI exports that collide with names already exported in `src/cli/daemon-cli/*.ts` and `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts`. The PR changes none of those files. This failure is not being fixed or rerun in this PR. The exact-head check rollup settled at 47 pass, 3 fail (this job plus two derived `openclaw/ci-gate` entries), 108 canceled, and 49 skipped.

### Previous head: `5b31a0945f67a4da24f8ffab7333dd9b6d7f6d94`

- That head added an AI-declaration fixture repair after exact prior-head CI found two process-count failures. Main independently landed the same repair through #160532, so the duplicate hunk was dropped in the final merge. The earlier local 39/39 and typecheck results are historical evidence only.

### Previous head: `d890f517761910574aeed6635d4510e28e422535`

- ClawSweeper found that the verified QA build fence checked `dist` while the compiler also writes `dist-runtime` and package output roots. `runBuildAllSteps` and runtime-only test preparation now pass the canonical `listTsdownOutputRoots()` to the physical-overlap fence. The fence compares every written root against every serving root, including realpath aliases and inode identity. A shared non-`dist` root refuses before any compiler runs; a separate checkout remains admitted.
- Focused tests: 61/61; the changed test file alone 15/15. Script and all root-test type graphs, focused lint, formatting, diff check, and staged P1 autoreview passed. ClawSweeper cleared code findings and requested the service-start decision above. CI then exposed the newly merged AI declaration fixture mismatch, repaired on the current head.

### Previous head: `2a05b84769933a3bf977d65eb2e374f060f2ffb3`

- Merged current `main` while preserving Windows Startup discovery. Strict inventory now checks systemd XDG, runtime, generated, transient, control, and system unit paths; Windows inventory checks every scheduled-task action and custom launcher.
- ClawSweeper's two later systemd findings are repaired: location-only inspection reads no service account or protected environment, while normal service operations keep their account checks; strict inventory also reads loaded manager units, including a running custom-profile Gateway after its unit file disappears. An unreadable unrelated, unloaded unit no longer blocks preparation; unverifiable loaded or recognizable Gateway units still do.
- Local proof: 19/19 user and 12/12 system paths reported by `systemd-analyze unit-paths` are covered; the real read-only inventory returned one managed service with zero errors. Focused daemon tests and the strict fence case passed. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed on the prior merge head; final-head core and core-test type graphs, formatting, lint, line cap, and diff checks passed.
- Windows CI on an earlier head failed before any Vitest shard during strict live-dist inventory. One unsafe false-positive path was an unreadable unrelated, stopped Task Scheduler entry; this head removes that path. Strict inventory now ignores unreadable actions on unrelated stopped/disabled tasks; unknown, queued, running, selected, and recognizable Gateway tasks remain fail-closed. The focused Windows inventory file passes 28/28, including stopped versus running/unknown state. The full changed-file gate passed on the previous code revision, including core and core-test types, lint, formatting, line cap, and dead-export checks. CI then found a type-only import cycle between `inspect-files.ts` and `inspect.ts` and canceled the Windows job before its verdict. This head moves the shared type to the leaf module. The exact CI architecture command `pnpm check:architecture` now passes, as do core and core-test type graphs, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks. ClawSweeper then found a macOS strict-inventory P1: an unreadable unrelated plist blocked test preparation. This head narrows launchd errors to recognizable Gateway names or marker-bearing malformed content, while keeping known unreadable Gateway definitions fail-closed. The real verified fence path passes with an unreadable unrelated plist and refuses after an overlapping live Gateway plist is added. The focused macOS inventory file passes 5/5 (9.07 s command wall; 6.96 s Vitest duration), and existing inventory tests pass 52/52. Prior-head Linux and Windows CI both failed in the declaration fixture because its copied source tree omitted `src/infra/errno.ts`, newly imported by the fence; this head copies that owner file, and the exact failing fixture case passes locally (15.93 s command wall; 15.03 s Vitest duration). ClawSweeper later found the non-dist output overlap described above. No service lifecycle action was taken.

- **Earlier revision: 509 distinct focused cases passed:** preparation boundary (7), runner build admission (171), E2E global setup (5), existing live-Gateway fence (38), build owner (90), the real bundled-plugin runtime consumer (159), and bounded Vitest process ownership (39). The 7 boundary cases and 159 runtime-consumer cases passed together on published head `4f0fe3918170e6430a2294d8a0bd1608b9040041`, after the final lint corrections (54.34 s command wall). Coverage includes known live-overlap refusal, immutable-deployment refusal, read-only warm reuse, postbuild failure propagation, cancellation/joining, and lock reacquisition. Existing selection, exclusion, preparation ordering, and E2E signal assertions remain intact.
- Native published-head proof: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs` completed successfully in **67.65 s**, including the real compiler, 95 plugin builds, bootstrap import guard, and runtime postbuild. Both private-QA SDK entries were generated, artifact ownership was released, and the subsequent normal `pnpm test` invocation reused the prepared runtime without another build. No service selectors, permissions, credentials, or production configuration were changed.
- Independent P2 autoreview: initial read-only/cancellation findings repaired; final scoped review has no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Selected static checks passed: script types, all four root-test type graphs, formatting, script/test lint, dead-export scans, and the selected repository guards. The initial aggregate stopped on a redundant synchronous `await`; that and a test brace-style error were corrected and the affected lint stages passed. Hosted exact-head CI/ClawSweeper verification for the current head remains pending. The PR is open for review; this is not a landing-readiness claim.

### Test discipline

- **Test audit:** one new owner-boundary file; compiler and native-inspection leaves are modeled while real prerequisite routing, build admission, filesystem effects, artifact locking, and cancellation are exercised. No new Gateway boots, sleeps, retries, serial configs, or coverage exclusions.
- **Deslop:** diff reviewed; reused the existing build, cancellation, freshness, and lock owners rather than adding service discovery or a second cleanup policy.

title: fix(ui): keep mobile layouts inside safe areas with consistent margins
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes inconsistent mobile side margins and controls extending into device safe areas in the installed Control UI, especially when the keyboard opens or closes.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session use the same mobile reading column, with controls kept inside the browser-reported safe area. Phones with zero insets do not gain an extra bottom band, and tested desktop layouts remain unchanged. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

**Known limit:** iPhone PWA, safe-inset, and keyboard cases are simulated browser contracts, not physical iPhone/Safari/WKWebView certification.

## Why This Change Was Made

The application root now consumes physical safe areas once and owns visual-viewport observation, including login and approval/question routes. Ordinary tabs follow the dynamic viewport; installed PWAs use the full standalone canvas. Keyboard-sized viewport reductions adjust available height without treating input focus alone as an open keyboard. Mobile content and fixed/popover surfaces share the same geometry instead of adding independent offsets.

## Evidence

- 11 viewport/lifecycle unit tests passed (2.11s wrapper wall; viewport cases approximately 19ms).
- 38 focused browser tests passed: 7 desktop/mobile/PWA geometry scenarios, 22 login cases, and 9 approval cases. The seven-scenario lane took 26.75s; the login lane took 33.23s. Existing focused footer-layout sibling also passed (148ms test / 2.03s wrapper wall).
- The same seven geometry scenarios on frozen main failed six mobile cases and passed desktop, establishing regression coverage.
- Independent autoreview of the final candidate found no actionable P0–P2 findings. UI typecheck, targeted TypeScript lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Testbox was used because the local browser HTTP preflight was blocked; no security controls were disabled.
- At 390×844 with zero insets, Chat/progress side insets change from 16px to 20px and New Session from 36px to 20px; the composer bottom remains 838px. At 1440×900, New Session, generating, and progress PNGs are byte-identical; idle chat has two background-pixel differences with identical measured boxes.
- The requested self-contained comparison HTML was delivered in the originating conversation, with slider, keyboard controls, scene switching, and persisted/exportable feedback verified.

### Production candidate verification

Fixes: mobile sidebar session titles are cut off too early because stacked gutters and empty metadata slots consume reading space.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Cap the drawer at 336 px (90vw on smaller phones), tighten row inset/gap to 2/4 px, and omit empty metadata slots. Keep 8 px outer gutters for the existing classic-scrollbar clearance contract. title: fix(ui): native capture disappears after camera preview errors

Related: #160253

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the explicit native-camera option disappears after a live camera preview request fails, including permission rejection.

## User Impact

**Use device camera** remains available beside **Upload photo**, **Cancel**, and **Try again** after preview errors. It opens only when clicked; the browser still owns the capture picker and its permissions. Secure preview, retry, and the existing insecure/unsupported fallback remain unchanged. The CI repair also keeps the newest streamed text visible after a smooth follow command that did not need to move, without pulling readers back after they scroll away.

## Why This Change Was Made

A late in-place review update on the original camera PR identified this remaining compatibility case. Reuse the existing draft-scoped native capture handler for error states instead of restricting it to capability failures. No new configuration, dependencies, or permission bypass.

CI exposed a streaming-scroll race: a smooth command already at the end can finish without emitting a native idle event, leaving later row growth without an end anchor. Record that actually reached end through the existing anchor owner. Ongoing smooth journeys and reader takeover retain their existing behavior; no assertions, retries, or timeouts were weakened.

title: feat(ui): select Ultrafast for supported accounts
body:
Closes #160336

## What Problem This Solves

The composer only has a Fast toggle, so people with Ultrafast access cannot select that tier explicitly.

## User Impact

Choose Standard, Fast, or—only when authenticated discovery confirms access for the selected account, model, and runtime—Ultrafast. Standard shows only effort on the composer chip. Unknown or unavailable Ultrafast is omitted, without a disabled option or upsell.

Fast requests ordinary priority processing by default. The existing Codex `enableUltrafast: true` opt-in continues to upgrade Fast and active Auto on supported models, preserving shipped settings. Standard and inactive Auto stay off. Explicit Ultrafast works independently of the plugin-wide opt-in; a preference never guarantees provider fulfillment.

**Upgrade compatibility:** the `v2026.9.7` contract is preserved: saved `fastMode: true` plus `enableUltrafast: true` still requests supported Ultrafast. There is no silent downgrade, migration, new configuration flag, or breaking transition. The new per-session Ultrafast choice is additive.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing composer, session preference, and account-catalog owners. Canonical Ultrafast state is preserved while clients without the decoding capability receive legacy-safe Fast values. Account discovery retains current request and default-link authority through the final HTTP dispatch. Unlink stops pending automatic discovery without deleting credentials or revoking saved session pins and explicit owned selections.

The reviewed SDK change is an optional `ProviderCatalogOutcome.modelServiceTiers` observation on the existing catalog result—not a new hook, endpoint, config option, required parameter, or broader credential capability. Omitted observations keep existing plugin behavior. Only ready authenticated observations are copied; account, model, runtime, route, and current-authority checks govern projection. The provider-catalog documentation records these semantics, and the already-authorized implementation/landing scope includes this additive field.

## Evidence

- **Landed:** exact head `8261e641ea0bf7e591cfca9217402aff1b2808a9` merged as `1caaef4b6f1080556abf26bd78a21f9ed216e2b0`. GitHub’s required CI, dependency, and security-sensitive gates passed ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36682846003)). Native merge receipt and cleanup are complete; main containment and the requested human co-author trailer were verified. Individual hosted test timings were not extracted in the bounded metadata/artifact audit; the measured local wall times below remain explicitly local evidence.

- ClawSweeper’s late `/fast ultrafast` finding is fixed in `8261e641ea0bf7e591cfca9217402aff1b2808a9`: direct command replies, standalone directive acknowledgments, and queued system events now share one formatter and name Ultrafast accurately. Help and docs include the accepted manual value. Three command regressions fail before the fix; all **274 cases across six command/help files pass** afterward (88.35 s wrapper), with focused lint, all seven prompt snapshots, and independent P0–P2 AutoReview passing. Generic native menus still omit an unverified optional choice because their context lacks authenticated account-tier facts. No transport, authorization, persistence, runtime-tier, or composer-layout behavior changed.

- CI `36679465341`, job `109771883754`, exposed two reset fixtures that passed partial caller objects cast as `never`. Both failures reproduced at `client.connect.caps`. The tests now reuse the existing typed session-mutation client factory, with complete handshake/profile data; all 15 reset-model cases pass (14.09 s wrapper / 12.06 s Vitest), and assertions and production capability checks are unchanged. Focused lint and P0/P1 AutoReview pass. Actual conflicts with main `9dc08b1fac6b88355393c3ed281c4e656d09a912` were generated prompt/config artifacts; canonical generation and checks pass. Candidate: `58f0a8ee7279d92a5a4206ae401da10d30e12b05`.

Bare `ws` mocks no longer intercepted the real constructor; the same failures reproduced locally. `9a7f1660b8995be276e3728e3570775cd45911e7` changes only the two mock registrations to the named constructor owner, preserving every assertion, timeout, and production transport guard. The complete 86-file OpenAI shard passes **1,263 tests with one existing skip** (70.19 s wrapper / 67.56 s Vitest), with host proxy/API-key environment removed for deterministic HTTP fixtures. Focused lint and independent P0/P1 AutoReview pass. Prior cancelled CI coverage remains unrun; normal successor CI is still required.

- CI `36675754918`, job `109760578212`, exposed four composer-test failures: the new broad Speed-label selector also matched the fixture model named “Speed only.” All four reproduced locally. Exact section-label matching repairs the test without changing the UI or relaxing the independent control-absence assertions. The complete 13-case bundled Chromium file passes (75.94 s wrapper / 73.65 s Vitest); focused lint and independent P0/P1 AutoReview pass. The subsequent actual conflict with main `982f9f8bcf0f8763a78ff23deb4224709a3ac7ac` was two neighboring Sessions imports; both canonical owners are retained, and all 49 Sessions view cases pass. The standalone node-only UI config lacked source aliases and failed before tests; the canonical UI configuration supplies those aliases and passed.

- Shipped opt-in preservation: 27 cold/warm native turn cases pass (65.50 s wrapper / 62.97 s Vitest), including saved Fast with the opt-in, without it, unsupported tiers, explicit Ultrafast, and Standard. Extension types and focused lint pass; independent delta AutoReview found no actionable P0/P1. No UI appearance changed.

- Real Control UI exercised in Chromium with deterministic Gateway/account fixtures: all selections cross the session-patch boundary; revoking access removes Ultrafast; Standard leaves only effort. Inspected before/after images were delivered in the originating chat and remain embedded below.
- The fresh ClawSweeper default-unlink finding reproduced through the registered `models.list` and `users.unlinkAuthProfile` handlers, real SQLite state, and a physical HTTP listener. Before repair, unlink during auth/DNS still sent one request. After repair, both send zero; the authorized control sends one. Explicit retained account selection remains usable afterward. ```text

```text
links empty; credential retained → dispatch resumed

```

A host-key-sensitive fixture was isolated after a same-source counterfactual proved ambient auth contamination.

title: fix(ui): show pending agent updates in the message queue
body:
Related: #160333 (closed; this replacement preserves queue semantics).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes queued agent updates appearing as completed messages, disappearing during history browsing, and showing their queued time after consumption—without scanning the retained input backlog on every refresh.

## User Impact

Waiting agent updates use the same compact 42 px queue rows as user messages, with a small, muted waiting spinner. They remain queued across Earlier navigation, then appear once in history at consumption time. The source tooltip explains that human messages may take priority: **display order is not a new execution-order guarantee, and the spinner does not promise immediate injection**. Reduced-motion mode uses a static ring.

Scheduling, steering/collect/followup modes, human-first priority, user queue actions, sender permissions, and original stored/model-input timestamps are unchanged. Agent entries stay read-only unless the Gateway explicitly grants the existing queue action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous revision walked retained input pages to discover old waiting agents. The existing custody owner now supplies candidate IDs for a separate active-input snapshot. Exact-ID reads run in the existing SQLite read worker, with ownership rechecked at final response publication; the canonical display projector still owns visibility, redaction and queue-action flags. There is no new scheduler, registry, persistent table or index.

The UI no longer infers complete queue membership from retained history. Completed active snapshots replace membership; partial/failed reads preserve unknown rows, while exact consumption/cancellation receipts and terminal rows retire settled ones immediately. QA also keeps active human custody visible when it leaves the actionable queue, reconciles conflicting retained/active copies, and preserves equal-time ordering across partial pages. Worker scope duplication was removed, but the race guards and the earlier compatibility fallback add code; no overall LoC reduction is claimed.

**Performance scope:** no extra browser history request is needed when the active snapshot fits within 20 records; larger active queues paginate only active candidates. The existing retained-history read is unchanged. This removes request amplification from terminal backlogs on current Gateways; it is not a production latency or unlimited-queue benchmark. **Pre-landing follow-up:** the earlier revision retained a queue-less Gateway fallback, but the current `ui/AGENTS.md` single-version policy forbids older-Gateway compatibility in the Control UI. That fallback still needs removal; this small spinner revision deliberately leaves queue behavior unchanged.

## Evidence

### Pending cue refinement — `66b718159d2d`

The actual Control UI uses the existing **12 × 12 px**, **1.6 s** spinner with the muted theme token. These same-content, same-viewport captures use synthetic Gateway/messages; they demonstrate appearance and motion, not live injection timing. Source tooltip/link, human row/actions, and row geometry remain unchanged.

Browser checks verified both ring dimensions, changing rotation, muted computed color, reduced-motion disabling animation, and zero `chat.send`/`chat.abort` calls. Independent AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The earlier full queue/build matrix below was not rerun for this icon-only change.

### Backlog cost and preserved queue behavior

The same real Control UI fixture has 4,000 retained inputs, three still waiting. Before uses UI head ea151d9c9b0f; after uses the repaired source. Transport is synthetic. Both recordings assert request counts rather than infer speed from playback, and neither scripts a reload.

### Queue implementation baseline — `d138ed866b41`

- **1,448 focused regressions pass across 51 files:** 643 backend/queue/steering cases plus 805 UI cases rerun after the final display repairs. The real Gateway steering and queued-follow-up entrypoint tests are included; provider execution remains synthetic.

<details>

### Execution ordering is not display ordering

This PR does **not** establish one chronological FIFO or one combined next-turn batch across user and inter-agent messages. The queue displays accepted inputs chronologically; execution keeps the existing human-first policy. The production session-lane priority owner classifies inter-session work as background, while ordinary user work is foreground—an intentional behavior from [#132738](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132738). Ordinary agent follow-ups also enter direct agent execution rather than the user follow-up collector. User steering/collect/followup modes and existing caps/cancellation remain unchanged.

A controlled test at head ea151d9c9b0f held an active turn, admitted **user A → agent B → user C** through the production lane and provenance-priority resolver, and executed a real AgentSession against a synthetic model provider. The provider requests saw **A → C → B**; all three inputs reached it, and each had one transcript entry. This is runtime-boundary proof, **not** a full chat.send/sessions_send RPC integration test or an unconditional delivery guarantee. The focused run passed **107 tests** (105 collect/custody cases, the existing human-priority regression, and the temporary mixed-input model probe). The test did not change production scheduling.

### Queue retention and pagination follow-up

Real Control UI, synthetic Gateway fixture: 22 retained inputs, with one user and two agent inputs still waiting. Before is the previous PR head e9079ab0; after is the reviewed pagination repair. No reload is scripted in these clips.

- **Before:** the older agent input is missing initially. Clicking **Earlier** shows it but drops the newer waiting agent input; the user queue stays.
- **After:** all three rows remain through **Earlier**. Consumption replaces only the matching agent row with one canonical history entry; a later Gateway cancellation removes only the other agent row. The user queue and its remove action stay intact. Both agent rows remain read-only, with the same **42 px** height as the user row and a robot source icon. No chat.send or chat.abort calls occur.

**Validation:** the original pagination cases failed before the repair; **527 tests across nine focused UI suites passed** afterward. Coverage includes receipt batches larger than 50, uncorrelated inputs, consumption/cancellation/interruption, source/connection invalidation, navigation/discovery races, and rejection of non-advancing cursors. UI production typecheck, focused lint, i18n verification, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent AutoReview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings; it explicitly noted the discovery-cost tradeoff above. Final post-review changes only added required braces and renamed a shadowed local variable, with the pagination suite rerun.

### Full queued → consumed → history flow

The before/after videos below exercise the actual Control UI and the real Gateway history/live-message display projectors, with mocked transport and a controlled clock. They are not a live production Gateway recording. Both cover the entire transition:

In a separate controlled replay, recorded message arrival retained both existing messages for 312 sampled frames, and an unrecorded actual composer send did so for 320 frames. title: fix(ui): stop older agent updates from sticking below newer replies
body:
> **Draft under reassessment:** the reported agent updates were pending inputs with state queued. This patch moves pending forwarded updates into arrival order; it is not a fix limited to already-consumed messages. If queued inputs are meant to remain at the bottom until consumption, this changes the intended behavior and should not be merged as-is.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes older messages forwarded from another agent session appearing pinned below newer replies while they wait to be consumed.

## User Impact

Forwarded agent updates now stay in conversation order instead of following every new response to the bottom. Normal human sends, the queue dock, and execution scheduling are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript treated every unconsumed input as a ceiling for the active response. Forwarded updates now use arrival-time placement, preserving Gateway input order without claiming execution ownership. The existing forwarded-message classification is shared with turn grouping, including cron forwards.

## Evidence

- Both new forwarding regressions failed on the unchanged base and pass with the fix.
- 73 focused tests pass across input ordering, live-to-final continuity, system notices, and agent-run grouping. Coverage includes continued streaming, later persisted replies, search, and the actual queue dock.

- Chromium recordings below exercise the actual Control UI with synthetic Gateway data: two pending forwarded updates, a continuing response, and final settlement. This is deterministic browser proof, not a live production Gateway capture.

title: improve: stop repeating warnings before external content
body:
## What Problem This Solves

External tool results repeat the same warning paragraph before already source-tagged, fenced content.

## User Impact

New external-content results start with the existing boundary envelope instead of repeated warning prose. Source labels, randomized markers, sanitization, tool policy, and approval enforcement remain intact. Existing transcripts are not rewritten, and no configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the paragraph at its producer—not in the UI—and delete the obsolete warning selection and budget branches across bundled callers. The shipped Plugin SDK `includeWarning` argument remains an ignored, deprecated boolean for source compatibility until the next major; internal callers no longer pass it. Attachment guidance now owns its explicit newline before the content envelope.

### Intentional output change and security tradeoff

This implements Peter's explicit request in the linked original discussion to remove the repeated paragraph from model-facing external content and land the change, not merely hide it in the UI. Full producer removal is intentional; retaining the paragraph behind the legacy SDK option would retain the removed output path.

For external plugin authors, this is an intentional **output-behavior change**: setting the released includeWarning option to true no longer prepends a paragraph. The deprecated field preserves TypeScript source compatibility only, not warning-bearing output. The upgrade path is to remove that option and consume the existing marker/source envelope; this is now documented in the prompt-injection guide. No new toggle is introduced.

Removing that natural-language cue is the requested product tradeoff. Marker/sanitizer regressions prove structural framing and sanitization, **not equivalent model-level injection resistance**; that effect remains unmeasured. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents asked to stop another session have no general Stop tool and send users to a browser login or a manual Stop click instead.

## User Impact

Users can ask an authorized Gateway agent to stop work in another session without resetting, archiving, or deleting the conversation. Session-wide Stop clears queued follow-ups by default; `clearQueued: false` preserves them, and an optional run ID narrows cancellation.

The coding and messaging profiles expose the tool to non-owner callers, while existing tool policy, sandbox visibility, agent-to-agent policy, and Gateway sharing/role checks still apply. Native subagents retain their controlled-tree cancellation; standalone embedded mode and the separate cloud-worker session-tool RPC surface are not expanded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `sessions_stop` rather than exposing the owner-only `sessions` management tool. Cancellation stays with the existing Gateway abort owner. A live admitted agent can stop browser-owned work only for the exact agent/key/session generation admitted by the router, without acquiring admin scopes or browser identity. Ordinary external-client ownership checks remain unchanged. Missing caller authority or an in-process Gateway fails before target lookup, with no credential-based transport fallback.

## Evidence

- 225 focused tests passed across tool registration/policy, stop targeting, Gateway cancellation authorization, queue ownership, yielded sessions, and descendant cancellation.

## What Problem This Solves

title: fix: recheck unfinished plans before an agent stops

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent can end its reply while its newly saved plan still lists unfinished, authorized work, leaving the session idle.

## User Impact

The built-in agent gets one chance to reconsider that stop: continue feasible work, reconcile the plan, or explain a concrete blocker. This can add one model response; it is not a guarantee of task completion. Old cards never restart idle work, and other agent harnesses are unchanged. No stored-data shape or production migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe successful canonical plan saves at the existing pre-terminal boundary. Continue the same logical prompt with its transcript, completed effects, permissions, and deadline—not a replay or rewind. The check is bounded across retries. Cancellation, steering, approval/child/media handoffs, status-only refreshes, and explicit plugin finalization retain priority. Already-shown checkpoints remain in the conversation.

CI prerequisite repairs landed in main while this PR was being verified: [database routing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160349), [Doctor mocks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/162dea17b031), [PID-only readiness](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ee15d2ba1da5), and the [requester-wake clock repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160407). The branch uses those owners unchanged. Our duplicate timer helper and its tests were removed; the original requester-wake assertions remain in main. title: fix: let write operators control their own sessions through agents
body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Agents acting for a write operator can archive, restore, and stop sessions that operator created or is assigned to, when normal session access also allows it. Ordinary active-run sends and explicit steering retain the existing `sessions_send` access rules.

### User impact

`operator.write` users can ask their agents to archive, restore, and Stop eligible sessions. `operator.sessions.write` alone does not expose these controls. Assignment alone never grants access. Self-archive waits for the current reply to finish; Stop targets another session, with an optional exact run ID. Swarm collectors cannot discover or execute Stop. Existing administrator, private-session, settings, ownership, deletion, and standalone HTTP restrictions remain.

## What Problem This Solves

The old discovery gate hid the whole sessions tool behind Gateway administration. This branch carries host-issued operator authority through existing Gateway mutation owners, then rechecks access, creator or assignee, target generation, and current authority at the action boundary.

Earlier PR heads had two send regressions. `startSessionsSendAgentRun` first applied restricted session-control preparation to every non-owner active-run send, including a message with no `mode`. Narrowing that guard to explicit `mode="steer"` still changed the published steering contract: an unrelated write operator who passed the existing send-access check could no longer steer. This head removes the separate control grant and guarded queue path from `sessions_send`, restoring main's existing send and steering behavior while keeping the new archive/restore/Stop controls restricted. Separately, a projection test waited for `facts.kind="unchanged"`, while `assignSessionOwner` publishes `facts.kind="owner"`; the corrected assertion covers the two CI cases that failed on the prior head.

## Evidence

- On head `3cc054c4fc749e396bce34b03cc6fe8f6fc255e0`, `pnpm test src/gateway/mcp-http.session-controls.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` ran against an isolated loopback MCP server: `Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 10 passed (10); real 23.55s` (45.05s on the earlier cold run). Five bearer-bound HTTP `tools/call` cases and five in-process dispatcher cases passed. The HTTP assertions require status 200, an allowed archive result, and a persisted SQLite `archivedAt`; unassigned, reassigned, role-revoked, and replaced targets require an error and no archive on the intended target. Reassignment, revocation, and replacement occur after target preparation and before the Gateway write resumes.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/local-request-context.session-archive.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: `Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 13 passed (13); real 55.80s`. title: fix(chat): safely steer an existing Gateway-queued input
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a message already held in the Gateway queue has no safe way to join compatible active work without being sent again.

## User Impact

Authorized clients can attempt to steer the original queued input, including approved content and attachments. A definite refusal preserves its queue position; possible native commitment must not replay. No configuration, storage migration, or protocol-version bump is introduced.

**Backend slice.** The visible Control UI affordance is stacked follow-up #160593. This task does not authorize merging or deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current session controller remains the only custody owner. `chat.steer` selects the original source by session/run identity and prepared physical-store scope, uses the router's current session-access authority, and shares ordinary steering policy and native settlement. It neither reconstructs the message nor creates another queued input. Incompatible model or authority leaves the input queued.

## Evidence

- Registered Gateway flow uses real `chat.send`, the original prepared queued source, registered `chat.steer`, real session projection/authorization and SQLite; only the model backend is stubbed. It verifies one injection of original content, its original recorder, a completed original protocol receipt, no abandonment, source retirement, and no later execution.
- Final standalone Gateway file: **5 passed, 31.54 s wall**; the new composed case took **2.009 s**. Discovery/authority selection: **24 passed**.
- Unchanged controller contracts: **31 + 1 passed**. Automatic-fallback siblings: **35 passed**; RPC schema: **7 passed** (the latter selections completed in 119.07 s including setup).
- Scoped production and canonical Gateway-test types passed; final typed owner lint passed. Canonical protocol generation, Swift/Kotlin generated-contract determinism and release-train metadata passed.
- Independent local autoreview: complete selected local candidate against `63c25f72daff6906c011027195a3187c8d8b7f06`, P0–P2, two native passes, **no actionable findings**. One subsequent test-only lint correction removed `await` from synchronous projection disposal; affected lint and the standalone regression passed afterward.
- [Inspected current-source before/after screenshots and UI scenario](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160275#issuecomment-6580884195), also embedded in #160593 and delivered to the originating chat.

**Limits:** model delivery is simulated in boundary tests. No live-provider or installed-upgrade rehearsal was run. Native generated contracts were checked, not native application builds. Hosted checks must be read against the published head; local results are not current-head CI. The refreshed code and evidence are published; both PRs remain drafts under this build-PRs-only task.

<details>
<summary>Failure investigation and generated diff</summary>

The registered entry point caught a real wrong-owner defect despite an earlier static review: requiring the legacy mutation target rejected a valid current-router request as “conversation changed.” The handler now consumes current session-access authority and the existing prepared-read owner. ## What Problem This Solves

Messages with no recorded author could borrow the signed-in viewer’s name and avatar. Reply previews and Markdown exports could repeat that false attribution, including for existing history.

## User Impact

Unattributed inputs now show **Message**, with **no avatar**. Recorded authors, qualified own/peer profiles, CLI/source labels, and alignment remain intact. Chat, replies, and exports use the same neutral wording.

This works for old records without rewriting stored messages, roles, provenance, permissions, or replay metadata. An older message that really was yours but never recorded its author also gets this neutral presentation; its author cannot safely be reconstructed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only a verified matching profile establishes that an input belongs to the viewer. The fix stays at the presentation boundary rather than inventing historical sender data. The general avatar helper still supports genuine local-user previews.

title: fix: avoid oversized PR CI jobs when smaller rows fit
body:
Related: #154239

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PR CI can fall back to larger pre-split test jobs unnecessarily when compatible budgeted rows would fit its 130-job limit.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Maintainers can run the same selected coverage in fewer CI jobs. The 130-job limit, 150-second admission budget, ten-group limit, worker/concurrency settings, runner choice, exclusivity, timeouts and build requirements remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consolidate only whole, already-bounded serial rows with identical execution policies, using the existing packing function and canonical policy key. Unknown-cost, concurrent, standalone, oversized and build-dependent rows retain their original execution boundaries.

The current main compactNodeJobCap fallback remains unchanged. Packing finishes at the bounded-row owner before the caller evaluates that fallback, so fitting 150-second rows are retained and genuinely over-cap plans keep the existing canonical fallback.

The existing Git-tooling concurrency comparison also now uses the backend under test rather than silently comparing GitHub/hybrid rows against default Blacksmith routing. Its assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

- Seventeen capacity and policy-boundary regression cases pass; the pre-fix control fails five assertions, including 131 jobs instead of 130.
- Assignment-candidate replay preserves all 5,273 selected targets and the complete child-descriptor multisets: GitHub 147 → 127 jobs (279 groups), hybrid 144 → 124 (308 groups). Every merged row stays at or below 150 seconds and ten groups. This is local planning evidence, not an exact replay of the unavailable hosted synthetic merge.
- The pinned main integration replay naturally selects 273 targets and plans 20 GitHub / 50 hybrid jobs with the workflow cap of 130; the new regression file is selected.
- Scripts/root-test types, formatting, targeted lint, line-cap and source guards, export checks, and independent P0–P2 review passed for the packing repair. The aggregate changed-check command initially stopped on a test-mock export-analysis problem; typed named mocks fixed it and the exact export scan passed. No unrelated exports were removed.
- **338 cases passed across the full changed-planner owner suite and the new regression file** (489.09 s Vitest; 490.00 s wrapper). This includes the backend-fixture correction: two failures reproduced on pristine source, and now pass without weakening assertions. The existing planner suite is slow because it repeatedly exercises real repository owner/import selection; the 17 new synthetic cases took 25 ms in this run.

- Conflict integration: 21 focused cases passed (4.76 s Vitest; 5.64 s wrapper), covering packing before the explicit cap, the inherited fallback/dist-budget behavior and all three backend comparisons. Without packing before the cap, both capped controls select 129 overlong canonical rows instead of 130 budgeted rows. Unchanged contracts reuse the full 338-case proof above.
- The published linear fixup automatically merges with pinned main to the exact reviewed and tested integrated tree. GitHub verifies its signature; no signing or ancestry guard was overridden.

No workflow dispatch, cap increase, selection reduction or full repository test suite is used as proof.

## Worked on by

title: fix(ui): Take photo opens a file picker on desktop
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: **Take photo** opens an image file picker on desktop instead of showing the camera.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session now offer a camera preview with **Capture**, **Retake**, and **Use photo**. Live preview requires HTTPS or localhost and permission from the browser/OS. When that API is unavailable, **Use device camera** explicitly opens the retained native capture picker; the browser may show a camera or file picker. No microphone is requested; the preview stays local, and only the confirmed still becomes a draft attachment. Permission, missing-camera, and capture failures show actionable errors with an explicit **Upload photo** alternative.

The camera stops on capture, dismissal, draft replacement, disconnection, and when a retained chat pane is hidden. Existing photo/file pickers remain available, including **Attach…** on iOS Safari alongside the explicit camera option. No new configuration, schema, or dependencies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTML file-input capture hint does not provide a desktop camera UI. A shared composer camera component now owns the video stream and capture lifecycle, using inline video and canvas rather than the less portable ImageCapture API. Late permission grants and encoding results cannot revive a canceled capture or attach to a replacement draft. Camera copy uses the existing lazy English catalog pattern instead of adding startup payload.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original action opening Chromium's image file chooser with the environment capture hint.
- Chromium with its synthetic camera: capture → retake → confirm in **chat and New Session**, no file chooser and no audio track; desktop/light and mobile/dark preview/review/error/upload flows; hidden retained pane stops the stream.
- 16 emulated browser/platform identities retained the expected explicit camera and existing file-picker options. These are identity/picker contract tests, not device certifications.
- **415 focused tests passed** across chat-view, camera capture, attachment reads, and pane attachment handoff (17.65 s wrapper wall on the rebased candidate, one worker). The final camera-only suite passed **15/15** after lazy-copy extraction (5.54 s wrapper wall; 4.56 s Vitest including setup, about 0.55 s test execution). Existing chat-view suite: 341 cases, 14.95 s wrapper wall in its standalone run. E2E wrapper cost remains unmeasured because of the preflight limitation below.
- UI and selected core-test typechecks, targeted lint/style checks, English catalog verification, and source guards passed. Production UI build and the final-head normalized same-toolchain performance comparison passed: startup JS **372,142 / 372,347 bytes**, 7 requests; startup CSS unchanged against the base. No budget/baseline increase.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. A later upstream clipboard-helper extraction caused one import conflict; the rebase preserves that helper and the reviewed patch otherwise. Focused tests, UI/chat/E2E test types, script types, English catalog verification, and the UI build were rerun after resolving it.

**Validation limits:** this host's proxy blocks the Vitest E2E loopback preflight (HTTP 502) and the WebKit test page. The real Chromium source-browser flows above were used as boundary proof; actual Safari/macOS/iPhone hardware permission behavior is not certified. The screenshots use Chromium's synthetic camera feed and a mocked Gateway. The native OS file dialog is asserted through the filechooser event, not pictured. This PR does not deploy the change.
