title: fix(ui): stop chat disclosure clicks from selecting text
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes text becoming selected and clicks being ignored when double-clicking or rapidly expanding and collapsing chat disclosures.

## User Impact

**Worked**, activity totals, tool rows, and **Raw details** behave like normal controls. Message prose and expanded tool output remain selectable and copyable. Keyboard activation, focus indicators, and expanded-state announcements are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared disclosure style explicitly enabled text selection, and a click guard then suppressed activation whenever the label was selected. Make only the disclosure labels non-selectable and remove the now-obsolete guard from all four callers. Keep the existing native buttons and ARIA state rather than intercepting pointer-down events.

## Evidence

- Reproduced browser word selection in all five disclosure variants before the fix; all five now pass real-pointer double-click checks, Enter/Space activation, and visible-focus checks.
- 263 focused UI tests passed across five files. The final six-case Chromium regression suite also passes after completing its typed fixtures: **5.49 seconds wall time**, approximately **1.08 seconds in test bodies** with `--maxWorkers=1`. In successful [CI run 36473187849](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36473187849), the six-case regression module took **4.58 seconds** of test execution (**6.35 seconds** queued-to-finished, including collection/setup).
- UI production and selected test typechecks, formatting, lint/style checks, and changed-scope guards validated locally. Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- Before/after captures use the actual Control UI with synthetic Gateway data, the same viewport/content, and the same three-click sequence. Chromium proof only; no native Safari or screen-reader certification is claimed.

### Review follow-up

The workspace-file selection finding does not reproduce. The apparent link is an existing native `<button class="chat-tool-row__file-link">`, and `base.css` already applies `user-select: none` directly to buttons. A Chromium probe of the production renderer, both with this PR and with the pre-PR row selection declaration restored, returned `BUTTON`, computed `userSelect: none`, an empty selection after double-click, two file-open callbacks, and no disclosure toggle. The six committed disclosure/keyboard/content-selection cases also passed again. This keeps existing file-opening behavior; expanded content remains selectable. No source change is needed for that finding.

### CI repair

The first ready-transition CI run exposed two stale `userSelect: "text"` expectations in the existing responsive-layout test. All three affected viewport cases reproduced locally. Commit `c4dda6971e1` changes only those expectations to `"none"`, preserving every layout assertion; no production code or test cases were added. The three responsive cases and six disclosure interaction/content-selection cases now pass together (9 targeted tests, 7.64 seconds wall time; unrelated cases were filtered out). In CI, the three existing responsive cases took 1.67, 1.75, and 1.87 seconds; no cases were added. Formatting, focused lint, and fresh full-candidate independent review pass. The repaired head is covered by the successful CI run above; production and screenshot proof is unchanged.

### Baseline CI repair

Run `36461056104` tested merge `858ec0a7e61f` (base `01747d9b2b11` plus PR head `c4dda6971e1`) and failed because the gateway config-reload fixture omitted its required scheduler. The failing fixture and reloader were identical between that tested base and merge. Main already repaired this in [4bd105408ccd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4bd105408ccdac229eee8f719f082ba143f0c26c), so the branch now incorporates main `47646aa21b9a` rather than duplicating the repair. The approved disclosure production files are byte-identical to the prior head. Gateway-root and UI typechecks and all nine targeted browser cases pass on the refreshed candidate; the refreshed head passed full CI and native completed-evidence merge gates.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Steer and interrupt delivery were treated as permission to reverse otherwise unanchored pending messages. Keep their submission order and retained neighboring message through acknowledgment/history handoffs. The existing exception for a recovered reply remains, and canonical history is not timestamp-sorted or rewritten.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the pre-fix reversal as `Second input, First input` in both the transcript projection and the actual Lit-rendered transcript DOM regression.
- All 271 focused tests passed across input ordering, transcript rendering/identity, live-final continuity, and the shared chat-thread suite.

- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the patch.

title: fix(sessions): prevent search failures during session updates
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: message search intermittently reports unavailable during ordinary session activity, and the command palette leaves empty filters and hints beneath that failure.

## User Impact

Search now tolerates ordinary title/usage updates, including activity in excluded background sessions. Genuine database errors, changed access, and session-lifecycle changes are still checked and reported; a failed search never becomes a false “No results found.” The palette retains a compact error message and **Retry**, preserving the query, focus, and foreground draft.

No permission, schema, retention, or stored-data changes. This PR has not been deployed to the reported Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backend treated any pending session-row refresh as a changed search scope. Two harmless updates could consume both transcript-search attempts, even though the authorized session keys and lifecycle identities were unchanged.

Each attempt now joins one existing projection refresh before the original owner, readiness, scope, and generation checks. New dirty work after that refresh still consumes the existing retry budget. The final synchronous authorization/presentation check remains in place. This fixes the cause instead of suppressing its error.

Reported and requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4af9f266-90c5-42af-880f-21bf9666678e)

## Evidence

- Retained live Gateway logs around the report contain sessions.search → “UNAVAILABLE: Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request”. The same error recurs later. No private log payloads are published here.
- Two registered-handler regressions reproduce that exact failure before the fix, using real SQLite/FTS worker reads and committed metadata updates on matched and excluded sessions. With the fix, both return the expected hit and current title with **one** transcript read.
- **12 backend tests pass**, covering ordinary updates; repeated real key-set, lifecycle, and refresh-settlement churn; visibility revocation; physical shared-store ownership; archived-hit preparation; and real FTS rejection. The five added cases take 3.33 s of test execution. Full file: 14.61 s test execution, 47.89 s Vitest duration, 50.60 s wall including 28.01 s cold worker compilation. Real projection/worker/SQLite composition is needed to reproduce this timing boundary.
- Final production and Gateway-methods test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The earlier broader changed-check run also recorded passing repository guards and all selected test typecheck graphs.
- Fresh independent P0/P1 review is clean after replacing the initial proposed unbounded refresh loop with a single refresh per existing attempt. A new regression preserves the error when fresh work arrives as that refresh settles.
- The unchanged UI portion previously passed **82 palette tests** and Chromium checks at 1200×800 and 390×844: same-query Retry, focus restoration, and foreground-draft preservation. Its before/after images below demonstrate the retained failure fallback, not the backend concurrency fix.

## User Impact

title: improve: reduce Online sidebar refresh cost on busy teams
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar's Online block spends unnecessary server CPU and browser rendering work as a busy team accumulates people and sessions.

## User Impact

Online keeps the same appearance, complete access-scoped Open/Running counts, sorting, filtering, and person links, with smaller refresh responses and cheaper large-roster rendering. No migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add `includeOwnerSessionCounts: "only"` to the existing `sessions.list` owner. Boolean `true` keeps its existing behavior; the new mode omits unused session rows and the owner facet without changing filters or pre-pagination counts.
- Avoid repeated allocations and unnecessary projected-run lookups for inactive rows. The request-local candidate index is used only for roster scans; selected-session reads and event publication retain direct lookups. Independent run owners and queued-state checks remain authoritative.
- Skip offscreen rendering work only above 50 online people. Rows stay mounted; focused rows and open person-card anchors remain uncontained, including scaled touch targets. No virtualization, persistence, or refresh-policy rewrite.

## Evidence

[Rendered UI proof — appearance preserved](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160220#issuecomment-5864927237).

Synthetic measurements on pinned baseline `2d39f2f738a89c27e0852943486af5c3971c4098`, then repeated optimization rounds. Gateway figures include the registered handler and JSON serialization, not WebSocket transport; each latency range is two 50-request block medians.

| Workload | Before | Final candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| 50 people / 1,000 sessions, count refresh | 2.52–2.93 ms | 1.47–2.24 ms |
| 500 people / 10,000 sessions, count refresh | 30.50–36.25 ms | 13.07–16.34 ms |
| 50-person response | 13,878 bytes | 4,407 bytes |
| 500-person response | 120,029 bytes | 38,158 bytes |
| 500-person production-UI stressed scroll, median frame | 41.9–48.4 ms | 18.5–26.0 ms |

- Fifty distinct synthetic viewers: a simultaneous 50-request count-only burst over 1,000 sessions completed in 65 ms; all per-viewer counts matched independent access-scoped oracles. At 10,000 sessions the latest burst was 860 ms: this is headroom evidence, not a production-capacity claim.
- No observed warm-read SQLite statements or worker dispatches. No cross-request count cache added.
- Real production UI / mocked Gateway: three samples each at 11/50/200/500 people; two-client event bursts, selected-chat startup priority, pending/trailing refresh, hidden visibility, reconnect, disposal and late replies passed. Desktop and emulated touch focus/card bounds passed at 85%, 100%, and 125% text scale with 500 people.
- Count accuracy/pagination/ownership/queue tests, active-run and keyed-presentation siblings, UI observer/event tests, core/UI typing, all 25 test-type graphs, changed-file type-aware lint, stylelint, formatting, protocol generation/check, and independent P0–P2 review passed. The test-type batch hit its outer time limit; remaining and affected graphs were completed explicitly. Native app builds were not run; generated Swift/Kotlin protocol parity was checked.
- Whole-core lint found one unchanged baseline error in `chat-attachments.ts` (716 counted lines / 700). It is already fixed on main by #160159. This branch merges cleanly with current main; no unrelated repair was copied into this PR.
- The new synchronous regression guards measured 14 ms and 4 ms. The reproducible 50-viewer benchmark is opt-in and remains skipped in normal CI; its measured test body was 8.93 s (35.49 s wrapper wall including compiler preparation).

Reproduce the checked-in opt-in variant:

```bash
OPENCLAW_BENCH_SESSION_VIEWERS=1 OPENCLAW_BENCH_OWNER_SESSION_COUNTS=only pnpm test src/gateway/session-list-viewers.perf.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Use OPENCLAW_BENCH_OWNER_SESSION_COUNTS=1 for the normal page plus counts.
```

Shared-host measurements varied between runs; earlier faster samples are not substituted for the final confirmation. The 50-person renderer was already smooth. Large filter re-expansion still reached 122–147 ms at 500 people; this does not introduce a full virtualizer. No live Team Gateway load, native-device capacity test, CI dispatch, merge, or deployment was performed.

title: fix: restore personal skill reads and release retired plugins
body:
Related: #160259

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes personal skills appearing unavailable in Code Mode and plugin disposal retaining replacement registries. The prerequisite CI owner-routing repair is now incorporated from main.

## User Impact

Agents can read their authorized personal skills, and completed plugin disposal no longer keeps successor registries alive. No settings, permissions, stored-data, or public SDK migration is required. The deployed Gateway is not changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Personal-library results use the existing JSON-result helper, exposing the same bounded projection to Code Mode and text consumers. The 20-entry list, 32-file manifest, whole-text limit, binary omission, and authenticated capability are unchanged.
- Disposal failure classification retains instance identity instead of a callback that captured the disposal scope and successor registry. The original current-instance/host-cleanup-token check remains.
- Main now owns the CI routing repair in [#160324](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160324). This branch incorporates it, with no remaining planner production delta. The retained regression also covers exact native-loader test selection without enabling the default plugin sweep.
- The Gateway omission test now parses the visible JSON rather than requiring compact formatting. It retains the size/binary protections and additionally verifies the omission reason, absent content, and agreement with structured details.

Main’s [native-task GC fixture correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c136ec631464) is incorporated. The redundant Bun-specific production waiter workaround was removed; the real disposal-capture fix remains.

## Evidence

- Personal skills: five regressions fail on the original producer and pass after repair, including real Code Mode catalog-search → list → dependent read and disclosure limits. Prior sibling proof passed 31 cases; all five regressions passed again on the reviewed candidate.
- Retention: the populated-registry regression fails on the original disposal owner under Node and passes with the repair. After incorporating main’s fixture correction, the complete compiled retention suite passes **10/10** under pinned CI Bun. Original assertions, eight collection passes, and child/test timeouts remain unchanged.
- Planner: the complete canonical suite passes **219/219 after integrating main’s repair**. Earlier combined planner proof passed 546 cases; the exact failed manifest changed from 135 jobs over the 130-job cap to 81 with the same 5,066 files. Current-head preflight and required CI gates pass.
- Gateway omission: reproduced the exact hosted assertion failure locally, then **7/7 tests pass** after repair. Replayed the failing job’s complete 11-file group through the native runner: **211 Node + 26 Bun tests pass**, with no skipped tests or relaxed assertions/timeouts.
- Type-aware lint, owning Gateway test types, formatting, and whitespace checks pass for the latest test repair. The earlier scripts/core/root-tooling type and static checks remain valid for unchanged inputs. Independent autoreview through P3 is scoped-clean for the eight-file candidate and the subsequent one-file assertion repair.
- **Verified head `d4fbf46c896f9bc03550f9fdac888dda38feefea`: [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36407249207), both required `openclaw/ci-gate` contexts are green, and [ClawSweeper’s exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160213#issuecomment-5864869979) has no actionable or security findings and no before-merge requests.** CI attempt 1 completed with 122 successful jobs, 22 conditionally skipped jobs, zero failed/cancelled jobs, and none pending. No tests were disabled. The native observer returned `GREEN`; GitHub’s raw rollup still retains 11 superseded cancellations from obsolete contexts, not current-run failures.

<details>
<summary>Root causes, test audit, costs, and proof limitations</summary>

- Filtered in-memory heap inspection identified the real chain: reachable oldest registry → instance → disposal-failure classifier → disposal scope’s `beforeCleanup` → cleanup parameters’ `nextRegistry` → successors. No raw heap or private runtime data is published.
- The old planner routed 442 selected plugin files into generic per-file batches. Main now retains their canonical ownership without enabling the default sweep or changing configs, worker/preparation policies, cost floors, deferred inventories, or the 130-job cap.
- Main’s existing cap handling and retention-helper mapping were already present in the failed run. Rebasing alone, or removing only the redundant waiter change, still emitted 135 jobs. The routing repair was independently necessary. After main landed `81a840ad3d12`, integration of `c3dc06d3738f` retained main’s complete planner owner and our native-loader regression. Publication preserves the existing PR ancestry; its complete tree matches the verified local rebase exactly.
- Test-audit/deslop: the planner regression covers exact real-file ownership, including a native-loader file, without enabling the default sweep. The retention regression reuses the independent GC-child harness. The omission assertion tests payload semantics instead of whitespace and strengthens the disclosure check without adding another fixture.
- Planner owner: `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — after main integration, 219 passed in 151.54s wall / 149.09s Vitest; retained case 699ms; [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36407249207/job/108879464189) 0.849s. Prior changed-owner + integration proof: 328 passed, 743.98s wall. Interrupted runs are not counted.
- Retention: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test src/plugins/runtime.retention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with checksum-verified CI Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+6b9148b17` — 10 passed, 52.88s wall / 49.41s Vitest, including cold preparation. The added populated case passed in [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36407249207/job/108879464694) in 0.489s. Prior head `5723f76ab07a` passed 120 Node lifecycle cases across five files in 35.57s wall and a full build in 6m 49.3s. Its informational UI startup-JS budget report was not green; neither that budget nor that prior build is claimed as current-head proof.
- Personal skill file: five passed, 55.84s wall / 50.50s Vitest on the reviewed candidate, dominated by cold preparation. Original warm `pnpm test src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool-library.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` measurement: 7.36s wall / 5.71s Vitest, about 86ms test bodies. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36407249207/job/108879464102): 0.056s for the real worker case and 0.002s each for the other four regressions. The worker uses synthetic authorized data, not the deployed Gateway.
- Gateway file benchmark: `pnpm test src/gateway/skill-library-authoring.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed before repair (1 failed / 6 passed; 61.35s cold wall / 52.99s Vitest), then passed 7/7 (10.14s warm wall / 7.98s Vitest; changed case 129ms). The prior hosted failing case took 161ms; the repaired case passed in [current hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36407249207/job/108879470161) in 0.225s.
- Failing-group replay: native `ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with the exact selected files/configs and Bun-compatible policy, locally bounded to two workers, passed 237/237 in 69.45s, then again with main integrated in 79.82s. Initial local replay encountered 16 loopback HTTP failures because this host’s environment proxy intercepted localhost. title: fix(browser): Windows Chrome setup fails after saved-profile Store enrollment
body:
Related: #152057 (already merged; this is a narrow follow-up).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automatic Windows Chrome setup refuses a saved extension profile after that profile explicitly requested Chrome Web Store installation.

## User Impact

User impact: selector-free inspect, verify, and install can recover the existing local profile without replacing its Store request. No new flags, configuration, permissions, or protocol changes. Chrome still owns extension approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Windows owner includes the browser profile in Store ownership. Inspecting the default `chrome` context can therefore report a context conflict and a foreign Store even when the saved `work` profile owns both. That observation now permits only bounded, serial read-only discovery. Selection still requires a validated current descriptor and a missing or owned Store request, followed by same-generation confirmation before relay access or the single C#-guarded mutation. Truly foreign, unknown, busy, and changed observations remain fail-closed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the registered setup CLI on base `6bfe76fcd7d31f64629c6889ce34e54368221d51`: all three new Store-requested cases failed while the other 25 cases passed. After the repair, all 35 Windows-selection cases pass, including foreign-Store refusal at candidate and confirmation stages before install/verify.
- 76 sibling tests pass: POSIX saved-profile migration, canonical CLI/setup, real authenticated relay, Windows adapter, and management transport. Total focused coverage: 111 passing tests.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview: scoped-clean. Full changed-scope checks passed, including extension production/test typechecks, typed lint, dead-export/import-cycle checks, formatting and owner-boundary guards (plus six Doctor contract tests). Frozen reviewed head: `6cff547216bd3229446d7cc32a7dae667182ef51`; hosted exact-head CI remains required.
- Test cost: `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-extension.windows-setup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 7.20s runner wall, 5.99s Vitest wall, less than 1s test execution (35 cases). CI seconds will be added once available.

These local tests inject OS/C# boundary facts; they are **not native Windows acceptance**. The existing Windows lane owns exact-consumer native proof. No Windows producer or proof-script changes are included.

title: improve(ui): compact Online people activity rows
body: Related: #130649. Presentation follow-up to #160022. ## What Problem This Solves The Online people list is hard to scan when presence, names, and session counts compete for space in the sidebar. ## User Impact People stay on one line, with long names fading rather than wrapping or showing an ellipsis. A small spinner and running count sit beside a 10px Lucide message-circle (sized to match the 9px spinner) and muted open count. Each pair keeps its natural width; the group rests at the right edge, with a common text baseline instead of fixed digit columns. Hover or keyboard focus reveals a subtle grouping pill without moving the content. Known zero counts are omitted. Unavailable counts have no placeholder line; the row tooltip and accessible description explicitly identify them as unavailable. A failed refresh keeps the last known counts and its retry control. Presence indicators remain separate from running work, and reduced motion keeps the spinner still. All connected people remain visible, including the signed-in user, in Active → Idle → Online order. Within each presence group, people with something running come first, then by name; the order never depends on how many sessions someone has. Existing profile hovercards, accessible names/descriptions, collapse/facepile, and normal or modified-click navigation are preserved. No card wrapper was added. ## Why This Change Was Made This is the approved listing format after design iteration: compact icon-number pairs, useful separation between running and open counts, and no count table or forced numeral alignment. It reuses the existing presence and workload owners and the shared running spinner. No private Team profiles or photos are published. ### Test fixture repairs kept by this branch Two roster-startup test races surfaced on an earlier head (run [36436724473](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36436724473)): keyboard assertions ran before the owner control existed, and a digest test started its no-refresh baseline before the initial list request. Both tests now use the existing roster-hydration wait (`session-owner-filter-keyboard.e2e.test.ts`, `chat-flow.sidebar-presentation.e2e.test.ts`, two lines each). The split-pane startup wait from that period is already on `main` and is no longer part of this diff. ## Risk and coverage - **Removed from the Online list:** the "only people with running sessions" filter, the sort-by-open and sort-by-running controls, and the totals row. title: fix: resume compacted turns after a Gateway restart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an unfinished conversation can fail with “Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn” when a Gateway restart follows compaction.

## User Impact

The built-in runtime can resume the accepted request without saving it twice, while still saving a distinct queued message. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compaction can summarize the current input out of model context without removing it from the transcript. Restart replay validates that durable input, but prompt submission reconstructs it when it is absent from model context. The reconstructed copy previously reached ordinary persistence and collided with the saved input.

Reuse the existing one-shot persistence suppression only after interrupted-turn replay preparation succeeds, and clear it when a differently keyed queued input arrives. The ordinary transcript turn guard and replay ownership revalidation remain unchanged. No new dispatcher, fallback, state, or replay key is introduced.

## Evidence

- A real SQLite cold-reopen regression reproduces the exact keyed-user error on unchanged production code after compaction removes the accepted input from model context. The repaired path preserves one durable original input, completed tool results, and the prior transcript prefix; a separate case verifies that queued steering is still saved.
- Receiving verification after integrating the canonical CI repairs: **87/87 tests across the three replay/transcript-guard files pass** (98.92 s command wall, Linux/Node 24.19.0). The five replay files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head. These SQLite lifecycle tests exercise actual prompt submission and ownership changes, not only a predicate.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean for the unchanged replay diff. Its selected changed-file gates pass, including core types, **27 core-test type graphs**, formatting, lint, dead exports, runtime import cycles, and architecture guards.
- The earlier Bun GC fixture failure was fixed on main in #160200; the main version is preserved and that helper is no longer part of this PR. No CI planner or admission-limit changes are included.
- Before the canonical CI repairs were integrated, the five-file replay candidate passed local manifest admission at **124 hybrid / 125 GitHub Node jobs**, below the unchanged 130-job limit. That is retained planning evidence for the prior head, not current-head hosted completion; this PR changes neither the planner nor its limit.
- The provider is mocked at the runtime boundary. No shared Gateway restart, live-model proof, configuration change, or database migration is claimed. Hosted CI and current-head bot review are checked before native landing.

### Inherited CI failures and canonical repairs

The previous head's [failed CI shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36782810791/job/110117482501) exposed two main-branch defects outside this replay change: an abort/reset fixture deadlock and a collector completion race that left scheduler capacity active. Both were independently reproduced on unmodified main.

Integrated the existing fixes rather than publishing a competing implementation: abort fixture commit [79f0e9bf127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/79f0e9bf1271ec2b40abb00402c6a4d89cba1330) and collector publication repair from #161019. On this combined source, the **exact captured 25-file CI plan passes 376/376 cases** (198.63 s), and the canonical publication owner's **21/21 cases pass** (3.66 s). No skips, retry-to-green, weakened assertions, or CI-limit changes were used. These are local receiving results, not a hosted-CI success claim.

Qualification gap: during diagnosis, a discarded local collector candidate passed six full Stop-file runs, but its seventh stress run exited with native Node 24.19.0 heap corruption/SIGABRT. Core inspection located detection in V8 compilation during worker bootstrap; the corruption's cause remains unknown. That stress sequence stopped immediately and is not claimed green or fixed. The canonical upstream repair—not that candidate—is included here; normal current-head CI and review remain required.

title: fix(ui): prevent chat jumps and prompt flicker when sending
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the transcript snaps when sending a message, and the entering prompt briefly fades out while the composer changes height.

## User Impact

Sending short or multiline prompts now uses one smooth scroll into the conversation and keeps the prompt text visible. Reduced motion and reader scroll takeover remain supported. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queued manual send scroll now owns the viewport instead of racing geometric auto-follow. Smooth sends wait through the first layout measurement before choosing their destination. The existing short upward prompt animation remains, without its opacity fade.

## Evidence

- Reproduced estimated-endpoint snaps in the actual Control UI: 217 px for a short prompt and 364 px for a multiline prompt, followed by range correction. Repaired recordings retained one fully opaque prompt node and issued no instant target displacement in those scenarios.
- 80 focused scroll/controller/entry unit tests passed (2.98 s wall). The CI follow-up also passes all 109 collaborator-typing, scroll-owner, and transcript-ownership tests (2.20 s wall).
- 8 isolated source-browser checks passed: desktop, multiline, mobile, reduced motion, composer growth, nested scrolling, delayed sends with expanding progress, and the Latest control. The updated motion file's four cases took 16.88 s test time / 18.23 s wall; browser layout and native scroll behavior cannot be proved by jsdom.
- Steering-order verification: 41 existing UI boundary regressions, 4 actual-UI browser cases, 3 production chat.send/AgentSession custody cases, and 4 Codex harness prefix-persistence cases passed. Accepted input is distinct from consumed input; post-consumption output is already ordered below the user prompt. No production message-ordering change was needed. The earlier synthetic unsegmented stream is not used as consumed-steer evidence.
- CI found an existing collaborator-typing test still expecting the old one-frame timing. The failure reproduced standalone. It now asserts a stationary measurement frame, introduces a second remote typing actor during that frame, and retains both final-position assertions after the manual command executes. No production code changed in this follow-up; independent P0–P2 review is clean. The changed typing test file passes all 25 cases in 2.04 s wall with one worker.
- UI production and test typechecks, stylesheet lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Hosted CI also caught an unbound scroll-probe method in the browser test. Binding it at capture fixes the lint error without changing production code or motion assertions; independent P0–P2 correction review is clean.
- [Final-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36389563111) passed, including UI, browser/real-Gateway browser, lint, type checks, and the required CI gate. Local full bundled validation remains unverified because its runtime build child was SIGKILLed. Browser proof uses synthetic Gateway events, not a live provider or physical mobile device.

title: improve(ui): show tool icons in sidebar progress previews
body:
Closes #160063

## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar tool activity repeats tool names as text instead of showing a recognizable icon and useful progress.

## User Impact

With previews enabled, a static tool icon appears **only on the second row**, beside public progress text. The tool name stays in the tooltip and accessible label, not repeated in visible text. The title row, compact one-row lists, and team roster stay unchanged. No extra pulsing dot, configuration, or migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing sidebar activity owner retains tool/item identity and explicitly public progress. Hidden or suppressed updates withdraw only matching activity; unrelated items, calls, or runs cannot clear it. Sparse updates retain the known tool name. Raw arguments, output, and argument-derived metadata are never preview text.

Sidebar and chat share one lightweight icon resolver. Execution tools use a terminal icon and search tools a search icon, with the existing emoji mapping and unknown-tool fallback preserved. Chat activity-row layout changes are a separate task.

Requested and designed with @steipete. **Scope confirmed:** second-row-only placement supersedes the earlier title-row proposal.

## Evidence

- 106 focused controller, retry, subtitle, and shared-resolver tests passed (single-worker invocation: 3.65 s). A current-main lifecycle reset regression and the independent review's nameless-progress update finding were reproduced before repair and pass after it.
- Both affected bundled-browser E2E files passed: 8 cases in 57.47 s including the shared UI build. Sidebar presentation: 6 cases / 21.12 s; scoped delivery: 2 cases / 3.29 s. This replaces the earlier local-E2E environment gap.
- Fresh real Control UI/mock-Gateway captures compare pinned main `b725cc7b27f6` with the reconciled candidate. Browser assertions verify second-row-only icons, no visible tool-name prefix, stable compact/roster geometry, and item-only withdrawal. Images were inspected and delivered in the original conversation.
- Control UI build passed in 17.24 s and stayed within enforced performance budgets; startup CSS remains above its existing advisory target, below the hard ceiling.
- Full candidate independent Codex review completed in two passes. Both reported the same optional-name finding; it was verified, repaired, and covered by two regressions. This is a resolved finding, not a zero-finding review claim.
- Exact-head scoped quality gates passed: file budgets, assertion safety, format/i18n, all 27 core test type graphs, UI types, all three dead-export scans, targeted lint/stylelint, and script lint. Exact-head CI [36654970805](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36654970805) passed, and ClawSweeper revision 9 completed with no actionable findings or security concerns. Native replacement recovery merged the reviewed head as `ee5ae483d5b60c0061e979befe94a7a4d4e84225` without bypass or re-arming auto-merge.

### Before — current main

![Before: sidebar repeats tool names](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59f3bf10-c1a9-4d72-9e97-b58b44b1b023)

### After — second-row public progress

![After: static terminal, read, and browser icons beside public progress](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b861c86c-8d2b-4e8a-b699-fd414dc8fc32)

<details>
<summary>Prior evidence and integration history</summary>

The earlier main duplicate-export blocker is resolved by upstream `bb05e779e2a7c`; dependent PR #160197 was closed without merging. This revision incorporates main for two actual narration-owner conflicts, preserves server-paced digests and immediate final updates, and retains the reviewed item-identity repair. Earlier failed/cancelled runs are not presented as current-head CI success. The original auto-merge intent remains retired and its recovery receipt is preserved.

The unchanged stream parser and coherent tool tests were moved into their existing helper modules to preserve file budgets; no coverage or gate was removed.

title: fix(ios): stop failed QR setup from connecting and losing retry state
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iOS Gateway setup can continue connecting after required local preparation or credential saving fails, replacing the useful error and leaving users without a safe retry.

## User Impact

Failed scan, paste, and setup-link actions stop before connecting and keep a useful error visible. Try Again reuses the unapplied setup held in memory; expired codes offer Scan New Code. Endpoint, credential values, and credential ownership change together only after preparation and saving succeed.

**Not merge-ready — native onboarding paste with a bootstrap-bearing code now proves two persistent returned save errors stop connection, followed by successful retry after explicit fault removal. Settings/opened-link coverage, preparation faults, paired-state preservation, crash/Share recovery and retained-state upgrade remain open.** Target-specific cleanup may already have occurred before a later save failure; this fix does not promise rollback of target data. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shared setup operation gates field updates, navigation, and connection behind successful preparation and persistence. Failures retain their retry candidate and keep automatic reconnect paused. Cleanup belongs to the exact attempt so an older cancelled action cannot release a newer action’s pause.

The approved scope now includes the necessary QR-02 recovery work to avoid destructive pairing replacement before durable save. Global reset, scanner redesign, Cloudflare integration and unrelated connection races remain outside this PR.

## Evidence

### Native bootstrap-code persistent-failure/retry evidence — published head 0dd38ea

Colin returned a local Mac evidence bundle for exact commit **0dd38ea32c58785a02214d07a53d9a0624ce2308**, tree **325d7ce532ed1e00ce2a9257000ce12197b2d625**. The archive and all 32 listed file checksums were verified; instrumentation, fixture, test logs, exported summaries and all three screenshots were inspected. These results belong to the published source plus the disclosed task-only instrumentation, **not the unpublished QR-02 repair**. No GitHub workflow was dispatched for this validation.

- **Onboarding paste / Apply → Try Again → Try Again passes:** payload contains a bootstrapToken, not token-only setup. First save and the next retry both return injected Security status -25308 at GenericPasswordKeychainStore.saveStringResult. Each captured fixture state has zero connections and zero requests. After explicitly clearing the fault, the third save reaches the real save implementation and succeeds; the fixture records one node and one operator connect and the native app displays “You're connected.” The rendered UI test passed **1/1**, with **62.838 s** test execution.
- **Supporting native suites:** published **416/416 passed**, zero skips. Original baseline **410/411** on its first run; the failed GatewayOperatorFleetTests assertion (“auth pauses survive reconciliation until connection inputs change”) passed on a same-products full-suite replay (**3/3**). That replay is not a proven fix or the QR regression's red result; the failure's root cause is not established by this bundle.
- **Limits:** the loopback fixture accepts connections without validating credentials; this demonstrates native client failure gating/retry, not production authentication or absence of wrong-secret transmission after recovery. Fault injection returns an error before the Security mutation, not a physical Keychain outage. The debug attempt counter and “Clear Injected Fault” control change the captured failure-card layout, so these are instrumented-flow screenshots, not pristine production-layout proof. No matched before-version run of this persistent/bootstrap scenario is included. Full xcresults remain on the tester's Mac; the supplied command logs and exported summaries were reviewed here, not re-executed.
- **Still open:** Settings, opened-link/reset order, preparation failures, expiry/cancellation/view exit, ordinary manual compatibility, pre-existing paired data/outbox preservation, retained-state upgrade, Share-process races and restart/crash cleanup. The packet intentionally left the recovery candidate unbound. The returned matrix records only the onboarding F02/F03 and instrumented V01 slice as passed; it does not establish full acceptance or close the preservation/cancellation review findings.

Both images below show the **same published revision**; they are failure/recovery states, not a before-code/after-code comparison. Synthetic loopback data only.

**Before clearing the injected fault — second failed save, no fixture connection**

![Published 0dd38ea onboarding after a second injected write failure; debug-only attempt count and fault-clear control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a71a05b-8b0b-4c33-891c-26b65e488cb7)

**After clearing the fault and tapping Try Again — connected**

![Published 0dd38ea onboarding successful retry after explicitly clearing the injected write fault](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a5c8a25-dc69-4f90-8f78-13bcb801f427)

### Earlier portable caller proof (historical, limited as described)

Validation ran locally on Linux with Swift 6.3.3 in Swift 6 language mode, using a network-disabled container. No GitHub workflow was manually dispatched for proof.

| Local source-exact caller harness | Before: b3f4c0aa540b | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Settings/onboarding post-scan, paste, and staged-link callers × four injected failures | 24/24 violate the failure contract | 24/24 pass |
| Healthy setup controls | 6/6 pass | 6/6 pass |
| Retry through the actual caller after clearing each injected fault | New retry path absent | 24/24 pass |

The baseline onboarding callers pass A’s fixture credentials into B’s save/connection calls after preparation fails. The candidate attempts no credential save after preparation failure and no connection after preparation or save failure. All six healthy controls still connect to B with B’s bootstrap credential.

The harness extracts method/type bodies byte-for-byte from the pinned baseline and candidate and verifies full-file/block hashes. It executes the actual Swift caller, auth-selection, preparation, application, and retry logic with explicitly substituted SwiftUI state containers and native I/O boundaries. **This is method-level behavioral proof, not a native app, SwiftUI lifecycle/rendering, physical Keychain/SQLite fault, camera, or wire-level test.**

- Five audited GatewaySetupApplicationTests pass using their actual source in an isolated proof module with the same declared platform substitutes. Test execution: 0.001 seconds; final parent compile/run/verification: 6 seconds with a warm build cache (initial parent run: 11 seconds). Native CI cost has not been measured.
- Strengthening the existing expiry test exposed an invalid-address message for expired retained codes. That assertion failed before the diagnostic-order fix and passes after it.
- Swift parser check passed for all eight changed Swift files. This is not a full Apple-framework typecheck.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.0: 0/8 files require formatting.
- Pinned SwiftLint 0.65.1 under the repository configuration: 0 violations across eight files.
- Staged-link reset ordering was restored to quiesce the existing session before offline preparation. Nine initial/retry ordering assertions failed before that correction and pass after it.
- Independent final source review: no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Repository changed-path checks and git diff whitespace checks passed.
- Inspected native before/after and retry screenshots are now embedded in the [native evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160049#issuecomment-5872505298) and the representative pair was attached in the requesting chat. This covers onboarding paste in light/default text, not every setup context.

### CI correction and review follow-through (`0dd38ea`)

The red `native-i18n` job on `e591cb1` failed because the source-owned inventory omitted the new setup/retry strings. The exact published source reproduced the same failure locally. Running the repository inventory generator changed only `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` (+11/-2); the same `native:i18n:verify` command then passed (4,095 entries, plus Android/Apple source safety checks). No translated/platform-generated artifacts, unfinished recovery code or workflow changes were included. No CI rerun or workflow dispatch was requested; this is a local red-to-green result, not a claim that all new-head CI is green.

Review disposition:

- **Existing-pairing preservation (Codex/ClawSweeper P1): accepted, still open on the published branch.** The repair must keep the same target's credentials, main/share device auth, TLS and queued work until durable commit, and settle committed cleanup after restart. The local recovery candidate, including shared-process Share-extension admission, is not yet published and remains under handoff review; native recovery execution is still outstanding.
- **Canceled async preparation (Copilot): accepted, still open until the recovery change is published and verified.** Generation checks after an await alone are insufficient; preparation and committed cleanup require owner-bound lifetime/settlement checks.
- **Duplicate welcome failure UI mentioned in the Copilot overview:** not reproduced by source tracing. `.welcome` is a separate branch from the Form error section, and `OnboardingWelcomeStep` uses failure-card **else** status text. No speculative UI change was made.
- **Production-boundary/native coverage:** still required. Prior `96a40df` token-only screenshots do not prove bootstrap replacement, cancellation, Share-process coordination or retained-state upgrade. These findings are not closed by the inventory fix or portable test counts.

### Manual-Connect scope correction (`e591cb1`)

A review found the save-failure stop had inadvertently changed ordinary manual Connect in Settings and onboarding. The two-file correction restores its baseline best-effort save behavior and the existing empty-instance guard; QR/setup callers remain gated by GatewaySetupApplication and skip a redundant second save. No extra permanent helper/test abstraction was added.

Local source-exact actual-caller proof reproduced both manual save-failure regressions at `96a40df`, with healthy controls passing and all four baseline cases passing. After correction, all four manual cases pass, retain target-bound credentials, and avoid bootstrap cleanup. The original 54 QR/setup/retry cases and five application tests also pass. Full QR proof compile/run/verification: 5 seconds warm. All eight changed Swift files pass parsing, pinned formatting and configured lint; whitespace checks pass. These are Linux boundary-double checks, not a native execution of this delta. Independent scoped review of the correction found no actionable P0–P2 regression.

The historical screenshots and Mac summaries in the `96a40df` section remain prior-head evidence. The newer `0dd38ea` native pass above supersedes the old-head execution gap for its stated onboarding and focused-suite scope only; ordinary manual Connect under save failure remains unrun natively.

### Native Mac evidence at prior head `96a40df`

Colin supplied a checksum-verified evidence bundle for baseline `b3f4c0aa540be135b722bec27922f105611b598d` and candidate `96a40dfabaedc98f239378ee2003fbbd3d0dc59d`. The screenshot images, instrumentation/UI-test/fixture sources, fault logs, fixture results, and exported native XCTest summaries were inspected. See the [native evidence and screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160049#issuecomment-5872505298).

- Exported native focused-test summaries: before **30/30**, after **35/35**, zero skips/failures. Native UI test: **1/1** on each revision. Mac runner reports pristine builds passing; full build logs and xcresults are retained by the runner, not independently re-executed here. Xcode 27.0 / Swift 6.4, iPhone 17 simulator / iOS 27.0.
- Real onboarding paste/Apply with a **one-shot returned Keychain save error**: baseline continues; candidate shows a usable error and has zero fixture connections/requests at the failure checkpoint. Real Try Again reuses the retained request and reaches the connected screen with operator/node fixture connects.
- **Important limits:** token-only payload, no `bootstrapToken`, so bootstrap preparation was not exercised. Baseline saves again before connecting; the one-shot fault does not establish connection without persistence. The fixture accepts connections without checking credentials, so role/traffic observations are not authentication or cross-target-secret proof. This is native app/simulator evidence with an injected storage result and synthetic loopback Gateway, not a physical Keychain outage or production Gateway test.

### Save-failure decision and compatibility boundary

**Chosen QR/setup behavior: keep the guarded connection.** A scan, pasted setup code or opened setup link must not connect when its required credential save reports failure. This does not change ordinary manual Connect: its existing target-bound in-memory credentials may still be used when a best-effort storage rewrite fails. The accidental extension of the guard into that manual path has been removed. This records the scoped implementation behavior, **not native validation, acceptance of destructive replacement, or merge approval**.

Source tracing at this PR head establishes:

- No Keychain item format, Gateway registry format, storage schema, or upgrade migration is changed. Normal registered-Gateway reconnect still uses the existing controller path, rather than the new setup application gate. This is source evidence, not a native upgrade test.
- Failed setup retains the unapplied request only while the setup screen remains open. Try Again repeats preparation and saving before connection. Expired requests require a fresh code; leaving or replacing setup discards the pending request.
- Bootstrap replacement is not rollback-safe: preparation can remove the target Gateway’s cached data, stored credentials, device-auth tokens, and TLS trust before a subsequent save fails. It also updates selection/auto-connect defaults. This PR does **not** promise that the previous target pairing or its live connection remains usable after that partial preparation.
- The local caller harness demonstrates retention of a different Gateway A’s synthetic stored credentials while B setup fails. It does not establish native Keychain preservation, same-target re-pair recovery, live connection continuity, or an upgrade from an installed earlier app.

### Approved recovery scope — implementation in progress

The unchanged bootstrap-preparation owner can clear the same target's existing credentials, device-auth tokens and TLS state before the new credential save succeeds. A later save failure can therefore leave an already paired target unusable. Surfacing an error/retry does not establish rollback or resolve this risk.

**Colin approved the scope expansion on September 28:** preserve the previous pairing until the replacement is durably committed, including the necessary QR-02 recovery work in this PR. Destructive replacement has not been accepted. Best-effort restoration into an unavailable Keychain is not a preservation guarantee. Implementation is in progress; this approval is not evidence of a completed fix or permission to merge. The recovery implementation and native paired-state/recovery proof remain outstanding.

### Native evidence still required before merge

The P1/P2 native-proof risks remain **open**. Required checks on an isolated native iOS build:

- [ ] Upgrade an installation already paired to Gateway A without resetting its storage; verify ordinary saved-Gateway reconnect.
- [ ] Exercise fresh setup success, a controlled credential-save failure, and successful Try Again through the rendered Settings and onboarding flows. Verify no connection after failed saving and no misleading success transition.
- [ ] With A already paired, attempt B setup with saving failure; read back A’s credentials/trust/state and verify A can still be selected and reconnected. Separately exercise replacement of an already paired target: a failed new save must preserve its old pairing and queued work, and successful retry must commit the replacement without using stale auth. Do not substitute best-effort rollback for preservation.
- [ ] Check expiry, leaving/reopening setup, and retry recovery after the storage fault is removed. Record the actual selection and auto-connect behavior.
- [x] Capture, inspect, sanitize and deliver a representative native onboarding before/after pair in the requesting chat and this PR. The linked evidence comment also includes retry success; PR image rendering was checked. Other materially different contexts remain part of the incomplete entrypoint coverage.

The native Mac pass is partial, not full acceptance. Remaining work: Settings/opened-link success/failure/retry, bootstrap preparation faults and staged-link reset order, persistent failure/recovery on already-paired targets, paired A/B and same-target recovery, expiry/view lifetime, cross-process/crash settlement, and paired-state baseline-to-recovery-candidate upgrade without reset. Physical camera and a previously released signed-build upgrade are conditional on authorized hardware/artifacts. No GitHub workflow is authorized or dispatched for proof. The PR is currently marked ready for review, but remains **not merge-ready**; its readiness setting was not changed. Source inspection or portable tests do not satisfy the remaining native gates.

title: fix(ci): preserve frozen-target managed restart coverage
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes frozen-target upgrade acceptance requiring an absent-containment recovery warning that the selected older runtime cannot produce.

## User Impact

Internal test-harness compatibility only; no product-runtime, stored user data, or configuration changes. Frozen release cuts retain their original native-contained automatic restart coverage instead of being tested against a later runtime contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing verified-source capability resolver inspects the committed terminal-publication owner, not package versions, working-tree edits or post-update results. Older targets use their original native containment; newer targets keep absent-containment recovery and strict warning/result-history assertions. Partial contracts fail closed, and unqualified runs reset to the strict current path.

The selected capability travels through existing Docker arguments and preflight metadata. Sparse preflight acquisition explicitly includes its source owner. The updater, replacement verification, prepared-service auth, serving-turn and survival checks are not weakened; the warning assertion itself is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New boundary regressions: three fail before the repair (3.45 s wall), then 3/3 pass (3.63 s wall; 1.844 s tests). They exercise source selection, host arguments and actual recovery/assertion functions with update side effects stubbed.
- Exact frozen 6106ea5 selects native; introducing runtime commit 018639af selects absent. Uncommitted additions cannot grant capability; mismatched SHAs and partial contracts are refused. Missing warnings, wrong run IDs and missing durable history remain failures on the newer path; old-path auth/update/serving failures remain failures.
- Recovery/config-parking/mobile/cron siblings: 69 passed in 33.35 s wall. Existing upgrade admission group: 22 passed, 85 intentionally unselected in 26.13 s wall.
- Sparse acquisition regressions: 2 passed in 16.26 s wall; removing the new acquisition input makes the negative control fail in 2.86 s. Fetched owner bytes are compared with the committed input.
- Shell syntax, formatting and whitespace checks passed. Parent caught and fixed one missing-braces test lint error before publication; targeted script lint (6.1 s) and all three changed test files (14.1 s) now pass with zero errors.

Independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean: verified-source authorization, strict defaults, sparse acquisition, Docker transport and unchanged failure assertions were inspected. The reviewer did not execute tests.

Native Docker cgroup and installed-package qualification are still pending. This compatibility reproduction does not establish the cause of an earlier inaccessible remote failure.

title: fix: prevent false completion waits and publication stalls
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable stops during authorized work: an agent could be told to wait for a completion it was already handling, scheduled agents were offered actions their runtime always rejects, and ordinary session updates could interrupt publication authorization preparation.

## User Impact

Agents get accurate continuation and tool-capability guidance. Session updates that keep access and identity unchanged no longer abort the protected in-flight permission read. Permission revocation, lifecycle replacement, cancellation, uncertain writes, and PR review/merge gates remain enforced. This does not add automatic retries or resume cancelled work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requester query now excludes its exact executing settle-wake cohort using the existing identity matcher, without marking delivery complete. Scheduled runs receive only their allowed own-job actions. Publication preparation registers with the existing sharing-facts owner before the worker read and reconciles committed entry/member changes without adopting a replacement lifecycle.

The workflow instructions also distinguish transcript delivery from a resumed agent, keep landing ownership when an internal watcher expires, and preserve existing authorization through reviewed same-scope recovery. Explicit replacement-head selection and every native recovery gate remain required.

## Evidence

- **338 focused tests passed** across 10 existing tool, requester-yield, sharing-preparation, and creation-settlement files.
- The current-wake regression failed on original code with `already_pending`; it passes through the actual yield callback/tool while preserving unrelated pending work and wrong-generation controls.
- The restricted-tool regression failed on original advertised actions; normal/admin behavior and foreign-job rejection remain covered.
- Three sharing-acquisition regressions failed on original code. Real isolated SQLite/worker proof covers metadata updates, visibility/member revocation, lifecycle/session replacement-and-restoration, retirement, unknown publication, rollback, and no host SQL during revalidation.
- Independent local review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. ClawSweeper reported no code or security findings; its latest report retained a confidence-only blocked marker, not a concrete defect. Shell syntax and whitespace checks passed. Final changed-file checks passed, including core and all 25 core-test type graphs, type-aware lint, formatting, dead exports, import cycles, and storage/authority guards.

Test cost: the two changed tool/yield files ran with `pnpm test ... --maxWorkers=1` in **19.45 s** combined (schema 5.72 s; requester-yield 11.85 s; new/extended regression bodies 8 ms and 6 ms). The two sharing files ran in **41.00 s cold**, including 23.28 s worker compilation; nine new acquisition cases totaled about 8.1 s. Corrected [CI run 36369733141](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36369733141) passed: 139 successful jobs and 19 skips. The catalog shard took 183 s and the snapshot-check job 67 s including setup, not per-test execution.

CI correction: the first post-ready run failed two checks for the same omitted generated prompt snapshots. The canonical generator updated four fixtures for the intentional scheduler wording; `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` now passes all seven files, and the exact catalog regression passes (10.89 s wall). No assertion was weakened or CI rerun requested.

A full local prompt-test file run was 16/17: its unchanged no-jiti performance assertion observed three OpenAI policy-loader calls, whereas that assertion passed in both the original and corrected hosted runs. This local discrepancy is retained as a validation gap, not called a full-suite pass.

Limits: the historical publication error did not identify its precise throw site; this repairs the independently reproduced acquisition window, not every possible storage error. Unknown changes before physical-source custody still fail closed. The broader publication-requester suite did not execute because runtime-artifact preparation could not verify host service state; no guard was disabled or service altered. No production deployment is included.

title: feat(ui): show open and running sessions beside online people
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Online list shows whether people are active, but not how many conversations they own or have running.

## User Impact

See **Open** and **Running** counts beside each person, sort by either count, or show only people with running sessions. Human presence stays separate from agent work, and totals cover the people shown.

Counts include owned, unarchived conversations you can access across configured agents. Hidden subagents, automation, system, and global/unknown sessions are excluded. Queued work and descendant activity are not counted as direct running sessions. No permission or storage changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

A complete Gateway-owned summary keeps counts accurate when the sidebar is filtered or paginated. The UI reuses managed session-list observation and refresh pacing, fences viewer/connection changes, distinguishes unknown from zero, and preserves the last successful counts with a retry notice after a failed refresh.


## Evidence

- [Real Gateway WebSocket request/response proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160022#issuecomment-5861908438) verifies the new option through handshake, validation, dispatch, and the production handler in an isolated Gateway with synthetic data. Counts remain complete before pagination and exclude another person’s private session/run; disabling the option omits the field. 1 proof passed in 57.22 s including cold compilation (11.191 s test time). No live Team service was changed.
- Real `sessions.list` handler regressions cover cross-agent ownership, pagination, live/queued/stale run states, duplicate runs, reassignment, profile merges, more than 60 owners, access changes, and private/incognito exclusions. Clean summary reads perform no SQLite preparation.
- Controller/renderer regressions cover unknown versus zero, profile/raw identity collisions, an idle person with running work, filtering/sorting/totals, error recovery, stale replies after disconnect/context replacement, and authoritative aggregate refresh after run snapshots.
- Actual Control UI browser proof uses synthetic Gateway data. Sorting, running-only filtering, dark/light themes, and the 390px mobile sidebar pass. [Inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160022#issuecomment-5861810438) are attached in the originating chat and embedded here; both GitHub images were verified loaded at their native dimensions.
- Independent P0/P1 review: scoped-clean. The lead additionally inspected the unchanged managed-list and connection lifecycle contracts.
- Production UI build passes. The explicit asset-budget checker reports an inherited startup-JS limit violation: unchanged source base `72b76842012f` is 372,549 B; the original measured candidate was 372,814 B (+265 B), against a 371,581 B absolute limit. CSS grows by 166 B, within its allowance. No budgets or baselines were relaxed.

Focused final regression run: **39 tests passed** across the Gateway handler, sidebar controller/renderer, and managed-list event tests, with `--maxWorkers=1`. Combined wall time: **46.79 s**, including cold worker compilation; Gateway tests execute in **2.425 s + 0.493 s**, and the UI shard finishes in **3.88 s**. Changed-file guards and core/test/UI typechecks passed; the final lint lane found two missing braces in the new controller. Both were corrected without behavior changes; targeted lint passes (0 warnings/errors, 8.6 s). Existing functional and visual proof remains applicable. Hosted feature-test timing has not yet been isolated; the first CI attempt failed on the two checks described below.


CI follow-up: [run 36366961172](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36366961172) identified stale generated Swift protocol output and a sidebar renderer type-import cycle. The Swift model was regenerated through its canonical generator; the sidebar now imports the people renderer directly instead of through its re-export. Local protocol registry/generation/Swift freshness/Kotlin/since checks pass; Madge reports 0 cycles, UI types and targeted lint pass (0 warnings/errors). The 37 focused UI regressions pass again in 4.59 s. These are mechanical corrections with no visual or behavior change; existing screenshot and Gateway proof remains applicable. No CI rerun or budget relaxation was used.

Startup-admission correction: [run 36367759526](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36367759526) exposed four chat-startup-priority E2E failures: the new count summary could dispatch before the selected transcript settled. Initial count hydration now uses the existing background bootstrap coordinator and fences queued work against the captured observation and connection; manual retry remains explicit. Two fake-timer regressions cover startup hold/release and retirement before admission. All **99 focused UI/managed-list regressions pass** in 8.57 s wall (5.82 s Vitest); UI types pass, and targeted lint passes (0 warnings/errors, 9.3 s) after marking the two intentionally in-flight test calls with `void`. Fresh independent P0/P1 review is scoped-clean. A local full-browser replay was refused by the loopback preflight (HTTP 502), and all nine exact-head hosted UI E2E shards now pass, including the repaired startup-priority shard; no CI rerun, policy bypass, or live Gateway change was used. Existing screenshot and Gateway wire proof remains applicable.

Hosted infrastructure follow-up: [run 36368977950, iPhone screenshot job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36368977950/job/108761441702) stopped before source compilation while Xcode resolved Swift packages: the runner’s cached WebRTC repository directory was missing (exit 74). Uploading its failure evidence also failed with DNS `ENOTFOUND`. The original job log was inspected and retained; this is not a feature-test assertion or Swift compiler error. The first cancellation interrupted proof; attempt 2 subsequently passed all nine UI E2E shards, closing the repaired browser-flow gap. After the run settled as cancelled, one bounded failed-job/dependency rerun was requested at 02:25 UTC for this identified runner-cache/network failure. The unchanged head is pinned to f1dc5eb976530f93461d7d959e7d4a06e6316914; attempt 2 passed the iPhone job but failed the iPad 13-inch screenshot job during a later XCTest application launch, so it did not produce passing whole-run CI. Original failure evidence is retained. No budget or source changes were made for this infrastructure failure.


Latest CI recovery: attempt 2’s [iPad job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36368977950/job/108763350504) successfully captured Control and Chat, then hung in `XCUIApplication.launch()` for the Agent snapshot until the 180-second allowance expired; XCTest reported that the app had no process ID. The retained log and capture-attempt manifest establish the launch boundary, not a feature assertion or a proven root cause inside the app. All nine UI E2E shards, UI checks, and hosted Control UI performance checks passed on this exact head. One bounded failed-job/dependency retry was accepted at 03:14 UTC for this distinct launch failure; attempt 3 is in progress on unchanged `f1dc5eb976530f93461d7d959e7d4a06e6316914`. title: fix(ci): honor loaded stop policy in upgrade fixtures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes upgrade-survivor fixtures rejecting the effective stop-policy query and enforcing a hardcoded 30-second deadline when the loaded generated unit specifies a different budget.

## User Impact

Internal acceptance-harness correction only; no updater runtime or production configuration change. The fixture reports and enforces its loaded unit policy, retains admitted state until reload, and does not report successful stop while owned processes remain or policy inspection failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing loaded-unit parser owns the effective stop budget for the maintenance query, supervisor and outer wait. Ordinary inspection cannot unload a removed on-disk unit. Supervisor-side policy errors trigger fatal cleanup and observed process-group extinction rather than abandoning the child or restarting.

The additional outer-entrypoint finding is also addressed: failed pre-signal policy inspection still signals the supervisor and joins through the existing five-second settlement allowance—not a replacement service timeout. Failure remains nonzero after cleanup; uncertain settlement retains supervisor/custody files. Normal, zero/infinite, reload and process/cgroup guards remain intact.

Existing extracted-supervisor test callers now supply the narrow manager dependency and their original timing budgets through it. Graceful drain, descendant extinction, restart overlap and sanitized-diagnostics assertions remain unchanged. This repairs demonstrated fixture defects; it does not establish the cause of the earlier inaccessible updater failure.

## Evidence

- Original effective-policy mismatch and the outer-stop failure were reproduced through the actual installed shim in isolated state.
- Outer-stop regressions before correction: 3 failed, 1 successful-stop control passed; 3.00 s wall.
- After correction: all 19 stop-policy and 3 cgroup tests passed; 6.78 s wall, 4.936 s policy-test time. Includes a real TERM-ignoring child, unit removal, daemon-reload and outer stop, requiring nonzero failure and extinct process group.
- Tests also cover uncertain settlement and preserving the original query failure when a later settlement check succeeds.
- Caller regression: all 10 originally reported cases plus bootstrap sibling passed; 11/11 in 7.69 s. Combined callers and native-auth siblings passed 13/13 in 13.63 s with command-scoped loopback proxy exclusion.
- Full Docker-helper file: 333/344 passed, not a green suite. Two loopback cases passed scoped replay; nine setup/parser failures reproduced on the unchanged base test file. Hosted exact-head CI remains required.
- Formatting, shell syntax and diff-whitespace checks passed. Test processes were joined.
- All four selected hosted Node rows passed on 3aa2c631; the hosted lint job failed and fail-fast cancelled other static jobs. Its log download was denied. Local reproduction found four fixture-script lint errors and nine test lint errors. The correction is mechanical: braces, a non-shadowing Promise callback name, Number.NaN and sorting a fresh array with toSorted; no assertions or failure behavior changed.
- Corrected full scripts lint passed on all 1,231 files (31.5 s); targeted test lint passed and the policy/cgroup replay passed 22/22 in 6.47 s. A subsequent three-file replay also passed those 22 cases, but the existing full systemd suite could not load because its compiled-subprocess build lacked quickjs-wasi. No full-suite pass or dependency installation is claimed.

Independent reviews cleared the earlier two P2 fixes and caller-only adaptation. Final combined outer-entrypoint re-review is scoped-clean P0–P2; it independently confirmed the caller delta was unchanged. Reviews were static; executed proof is listed above. No installed-package release qualification is claimed.

title: fix(ci): keep upgrade recipes compatible with frozen targets
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes upgrade-survivor validation rejecting an older frozen candidate because newer tooling introduces a Tool Search migration specimen that the selected cut does not contain.

## User Impact

Internal release-validation correction only; no product-runtime, configuration-schema, or stored-data change. Frozen targets keep their supported recipe coverage, while newer targets must still pass the strict Tool Search migration assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Docker harness mounts trusted scripts over the candidate image. The existing frozen-target capability owner now checks the verified selected commit for the Tool Search specimen and forwards a bounded `current`/`absent` result through the existing compatibility arguments. Only that newer specimen is omitted when absent from the selected cut; every other recipe step and accepted intent remains unchanged. Ordinary runs remain strict and inherited overrides are reset.

The assertion code is unchanged. Selection does not use version ordering or the observed post-update configuration: the demonstrated older-capability target is version `2026.9.7`, while newer tooling is version `2026.9.6`. This adaptation requires the existing explicit frozen-target authorization. Manual Package Acceptance now exposes the same existing boolean input as its reusable entrypoint, still defaulting to false. All package, plugin, npm-install, admission and downstream forwarding jobs remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Both new regressions fail against the original owners: 2.16 s wall.
- Corrected boundary suite: 2/2 pass, 4.16 s wall, 1.492 s test time. Exercises actual host policy → recipe CLI → coverage, committed-tree identity, uncommitted specimen refusal, wrong-SHA rejection and unchanged non-Tool-Search coverage.
- Legacy baseline and valid newer migration pass. Unmigrated mode, retained timeout, disabled Tool Search and missing configuration still fail.

title: fix(ui): allow oversized PNG attachments
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat rejects an oversized PNG dropped into the composer instead of preparing a smaller image for upload.

## User Impact

Users can drop, pick, or paste oversized static PNGs in chat and New Session. The browser resizes them to the Gateway-advertised byte limit while preserving aspect ratio and transparency; already-small files remain unchanged. No server limit or configuration changes are required.

Resizing supports static PNG sources up to 25 megapixels. Animated PNGs are not silently flattened, and other formats retain their existing limits. Failed preparation remains visible and does not send oversized bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preparation stays inside the shared attachment lifecycle, preserving pending-send, cancellation, ordering, and destination ownership. A disposable browser worker owns decoding, drawing, and encoding; jobs are serialized to bound pixel memory. Queue waits do not consume another image's processing timeout. Pasted image data also avoids a costly per-byte string-iterator callback.

## Evidence

- Real Chromium regression failed before the fix through drop, picker, and image-data paste; the repaired paths preserve PNG transparency and publish matching, bounded payload bytes.
- 226 focused tests passed across attachment ingestion, chat/New Session composers, typing, cancellation, and pane handoff. A fake-clock regression also proves two individually valid 10-second/6-second jobs do not time out because they were queued.

| Measured operation | Before | Final candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PNG drawing/encoding on the composer thread | Up to 149 ms near 25 MP at 4× | No main-thread drawing/encoding calls |
| ~6 MB data-URL paste handler, normal CPU | 268 ms | 20 ms |
| ~6 MB data-URL paste handler, 4× CPU | 1,056 ms | 68 ms |

Both paste-handler measurements used the isolated harness. Existing FileReader/composer-rendering spikes remain observable under CPU throttling; this is not a claim of universally hitch-free rendering. Chromium was exercised; other browsers were not live-tested.

The full bundled E2E route was unavailable: host loopback preflight returned HTTP 502, then the supported isolated runtime build was SIGKILLed. The focused actual-UI source harness ran successfully in secretless isolation instead; all owned containers/browser processes were cleaned up.

The new browser file spent 368 ms in tests (1.61 seconds including runner overhead); the updated attachment unit file's final standalone run took 4.07 seconds wall time. The command-palette fixture repair passed all 12 tests in 7.13 seconds wall time (5.99 seconds in Vitest); its combined replay with attachment tests passed all 33 tests in 6.68 seconds.
