title: fix: keep runs alive when another user's identity scopes change
body:
Related: #154792

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes active and queued WebChat runs being cancelled when an operator changes another user's identity scopes.

## User Impact

Verified users keep their existing connections and accepted runs through unrelated identity-grant edits. Real permission changes still revoke the original authority, including delegated work. No new settings, schema changes, or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The authentication-policy fingerprint included the entire identity-scope map. Editing one login therefore made every connection's captured policy stale; the committed-source owner correctly propagated that incorrectly broad revocation to its runs.

Bind WebSocket policy generations to the handshake-attested login's canonically resolved grants, and use that same projection at reconciliation, dispatch, retained-source, and worker-mutation checks. Equivalent scope ordering is neutral. Own grant changes remain revocations; restoring a grant cannot revive an already-revoked source.

Callers without an attested identity, pending handshakes, HTTP/cookie authority, and approval-policy snapshots retain their conservative whole-policy fence. Role/device revocation, shared-auth rotation, and browser/proxy checks remain intact. The per-snapshot cache now retains a generation per observed verified identity.

## Evidence

- **Final-effect proof added after [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159939#issuecomment-5860660630):** the managed-reload case now pauses accepted execution at the existing asynchronous exec prelaunch hook. After another login’s scope edit, the original operator authority reaches the real exec runtime and process supervisor, launches a real Node child (observed PID and exit 0), and writes the asserted marker bytes. A delegated execution paused at the same boundary is rejected after its own grant is removed and restored; the marker file remains absent. Authority checks, the supervisor, native spawn, and filesystem writes are not mocked. The original production code fails this allowed-effect assertion with `operator source authority is no longer active`; the candidate passes both outcomes.
- **Review followup:** the configuration reference and operator-scope guide now describe the same per-login reload exception. Production code is unchanged from the first published head. The strengthened regression, owning test type graph, scoped typed lint, config-doc baseline check, formatting, and a fresh P0–P2 autoreview all passed.
- **Hosted CI baseline:** [run 36356525075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36356525075) passed on prior head `0a4e0baad561c00731c7520e9ae06f0d2ddbd4bb`: 119 successful jobs, 20 intentionally skipped, zero failures. Current-head CI remains separately represented by the PR checks.
- **Red → green:** the new managed-reload regression failed on base `8777448a9ffab1d0a5ad39d5abc11640cba849de`: editing another login set the original operator authority's abort signal. It passes after this repair through the real managed config-reload, authenticated-dispatch, retained-authority, delegated-authority, and worker-guard owners.
- **147 distinct focused tests passed across nine files.** Coverage includes unrelated/no-op edits, scope-set equivalence, requester grant downgrade/removal/upgrade, exact-match shadowing, own versus unrelated add/remove races, remove/restore latching, handshake admission, role/device source revocation, shared-auth rotation/rollback, and cancellation custody. Repeated cost/replay runs are not added to that count.
- Core production and Gateway-server test type graphs, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Test-fixture type and brace issues found during validation were corrected.
- Repository `autoreview` completed scoped-clean through P2. A separate source-inspecting review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; the autoreview assessment itself was limited to its supplied change bundle.
- The incident release `e3f3c15ebfe584683f30d5329ef3a504ac77f89c` and inspected upstream `389e035c52c1d7ea0332365dc3472983e4f3597b` contain the same original auth-policy source.

The identity and reload harness uses synthetic users; the final exec runtime, supervisor, native process, and filesystem effect are real. This does not claim a production Gateway replay, external identity-provider test, or live model invocation. No merge or deployment is requested.

<details>
<summary>Changed-test cost and reproduction commands</summary>

Measured on Node 26.8.2 using the repository's direct Vitest wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1` (the documented alternative to `pnpm test` with prepared worktree dependencies). Times are whole standalone wrapper wall time, not CI job seconds. CI timing is pending.

| Changed test file | Result | Wrapper wall |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.identity-scopes.test.ts` — strengthened final-effect case | 1 passed | 44.75 s |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-origin-policy.test.ts` | 23 passed | 6.29 s |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts` | 61 passed | 26.84 s |

The strengthened managed-reload case itself took 11.90 s; its 44.75 s standalone wrapper cost includes rebuilding worker compiler outputs. It composes committed reload publication, worker-backed profile/authority ownership, and a real process effect without booting a Gateway or model provider. The smaller policy tests do not establish that composition. The added handshake case takes about 0.55 s. Existing sibling proof passed 123 tests across seven files in 53.97 s wrapper wall.

Run each changed file with:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <test-file> --maxWorkers=1
```

The initial cold regression run was red at `original.authority.signal.aborted` (expected false, received true); the repaired regression and subsequent-request, delegated, worker-guard, and revoke/restore assertions are green.

</details>

title: improve(ui): make shortcut icons clear and consistently aligned
body:
Related: #151509 (shortcut presentation only; this does not close the broader menu-consolidation work).

## What Problem This Solves

Keyboard shortcut hints use thin, font-dependent symbols and separate renderers across the Control UI.

## User Impact

Shortcut symbols now have natural SVG proportions, consistent weight, and deliberate centering. Each surface keeps its own bare, filled, or bordered treatment. Letters, digits, non-Apple modifier labels, accessible shortcut text, and key matching remain unchanged. Chords can become slightly wider rather than squeezing the icons.

**Startup budget resolved:** committed candidate `1eb1079a3ef` measures **361,266 B gzip** against the unchanged **372,347 B** ceiling (7 initial JavaScript requests). CSS is **50,654 B**, below its 51,200 B ceiling. The optional Web Awesome popup loads on first tooltip use; accessible descriptions and dismissal remain synchronous.

## Why This Change Was Made

One native kbd renderer owns the symbolic drawing and content alignment. Letters now align by their visible cap box rather than the extra ascender/descender space in their line box, with unchanged font sizes, balanced icon strokes, and a small gap between keys. Full chords stay together in tooltips. Its line-height strut preserves each context’s text box, and palette footer groups put keycaps and labels on the same centerline. An earlier unsubmitted draft used character-width sizing and distorted the SVGs; that workaround has been removed.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/450376b7-2a86-41c9-90e9-bea6cfce65da)

The refreshed dialog images include that main-side close-control change; baseline images retain the earlier clean-base close control.

The focused 177-test run passed in 4.74 seconds, including the previously failing Node subprocess import; after the conflict rebase, the 9 affected renderer/dialog tests passed again in 1.35 seconds and all three dialog visual scenarios were recaptured and inspected.

title: improve(ui): move table controls below content
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Table controls reserve a gap between a heading and its table, interrupting the reading flow.

Validation also exposed a history-navigation bug: retargeting smooth end-follow could leave row heights unmeasured and the latest reply below the viewport.

## User Impact

Expand and copy now appear at the bottom-right of Markdown tables on desktop and mobile. The overall block height and position of following content stay unchanged; table scrolling, copying, expansion, and keyboard focus behavior are preserved. Latest history messages also stay visible when automatic end-follow switches out of smooth scrolling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Render the existing toolbar after the scrollable table viewport and move its spacing to the corresponding top edge. Update the existing responsive geometry assertions to require controls below the table and no toolbar space above it.

The CI-blocking history repair reuses the existing deferred measurement callback when an automatic smooth-to-auto retarget bypasses cancellation. It preserves scroll ownership, retires the transcript element before controller teardown, and leaves the failing E2E assertions and timeouts unchanged.

## Evidence

- Actual Control UI with deterministic fixture content: inspected matched before/after captures at 1440px dark and 390px light; copy, keyboard expansion, Escape, and focus return passed.
- 35 focused table, RTL, and streaming tests passed in 44.73s total, using the repository test config with Vite caches redirected to writable task storage.
- Formatting, CSS lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The review-requested chat-guide sentence now describes controls below the table; docs formatting (1,315 files), focused MDX validation, and whitespace checks passed.
- The history failure from [CI run 36356377061](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36356377061) was reproduced on the exact earlier failing merge. The unchanged history E2E file now passes **6/6** in a pinned, network-isolated Playwright container with the normal preflight intact.
- A deterministic regression fails on the original code (4,800 rather than 4,860 measured pixels); the repair and owner/sibling tests pass **124/124** across seven files in **16.62s**. The new regression takes **123ms** locally and **0.062s (Bun) / 0.073s (Node)** in CI. UI typecheck, scoped lint, and formatting passed.
- Final exact-head [CI run 36358159609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36358159609) passed: all 88 jobs are terminal, with no failed or cancelled jobs. The required CI gate and final ClawSweeper review completed successfully with no actionable findings.
- Merged into `main` as `ac5891921c3480e761681f3be830088c94038578`; main containment and contributor credit verified.

title: feat(desktop): let agents resume after manual control
body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a user signs in on a shared desktop, the agent cannot resume until the user manually releases control. An intentional Disconnect also appears as an “unknown reason” error.

## User Impact

Agents can explicitly take over an attached or cloud-session desktop, returning the human viewer to view-only. The persistent paused-input banner is removed. Intentional disconnections now show a neutral status with Reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing desktop owner handles takeover; ordinary agent input still pauses while a human controls the desktop. Takeover invalidates old input references and returns a fresh screenshot. Users can reclaim control at any time. No configuration or provider-protocol change is required.

## Evidence

- Baseline replacement: **233 focused tests passed** — 206 computer/Desktop tests across nine files (103.08 seconds wall), 18 FaceTime helper-RPC tests (7.74 seconds), and 9 helper-supervisor sibling tests (4.45 seconds). The takeover replay and neutral-disconnect regressions remain covered; both conflicting observation regressions were preserved.
- Chromium with the real UI and noVNC parser verified view-only recovery, human reclaim, intentional disconnect, and reconnect to the same desktop. Desktop content and Gateway responses were synthetic.
- The bundled UI E2E attempt was blocked before execution by the environment’s loopback HTTP preflight (HTTP 502); proxy policy was not disabled.
- The baseline replacement passed mandatory independent review with no P0/P1 findings, core and extension typing, targeted lint, formatting, and UI i18n verification. Unaffected earlier proof was reused.

### Desktop control banner

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Control banner before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31bfdfe2-4459-4b11-9e1a-d109b38549b4) | ![Control banner removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29e4472a-a8af-455d-ba89-fab94db0ef19) |

### Intentional disconnect

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Intentional disconnect shown as unknown error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56bd1af7-365c-4a20-b0d0-c2b826a472af) | ![Neutral disconnect status with Reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a031067-242a-4e9a-baa4-dc9e66ca09d0) |

### Replay correction

The hosted P1 review finding is addressed: completed takeover keys now belong to the canonical admitted run, not an individual binding or attachment preparation. Keys remain scoped to the desktop environment and owner epoch. Two existing entry-point tests were strengthened rather than adding a duplicate fixture: both failed on the published revision, and both now reject the replay before closing the reclaimed human viewer. A new explicit takeover still works.

The replay correction is included in the replacement validation above. Both scenarios were demonstrated failing on the original revision before the repair.

The prior hosted CI failure was an untouched Activity run-inspector test timing out while waiting for its error state ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36354822416/job/108720642555)). The exact case passed in two inspected scheduled-main runs; its original CI failure remains unexplained, so it is not being claimed as an inherited-red exception. No workflow was manually rerun or dispatched.

### Conflict and CI repair

Integrated main `246e575c929f` to resolve the actual observation-test conflict, retaining both tests and the new mainline observation outcome behavior. The previous auto-merge request was retired through native recovery before publishing this replacement.

Fixed the observed FaceTime helper test `EADDRINUSE` failure by removing reserve/close/rebind allocation. The real helper now binds port 0, and the fixture reads its still-owned listener address. Deterministic probes showed another listener could claim the old reserved port; with the repaired fixture it cannot claim the port until the helper stops. All existing wire/authentication tests remain; no production API, retries, sleeps, or test cases were added.

### Keyless replay correction and viewer-socket proof

The latest review identified a second replay path: takeover requests could omit their idempotency key. The Gateway now rejects missing or empty keys before touching viewer control. Existing tool-generated keys and canonical admitted-run replay ownership are unchanged.

The existing primary regression now crosses the real worker computer RPC handler, transport owner, desktop registry, observer upgrade handler, and a real loopback viewer WebSocket. It verifies:

- An allowed takeover closes the controller with code **4000**, reason **control-taken:Agent**, and destroys its desktop stream.
- After human reclaim, the same keyed request and missing/empty-key requests leave the viewer connected; each negative case completes a WebSocket ping/pong round trip with its stream still open.
- A new explicit takeover still closes that viewer. Revoking the delegated worker authority then rejects another request while the new human viewer remains connected.

The keyless regression failed on the published revision because the request returned success instead of the required denial. After repair, **88/88 affected tests passed** across takeover, computer transport, and observer-bridge coverage (20.06 seconds wall). The six-test takeover file passed separately in 53.99 seconds wall, including 47.85 seconds of shared subprocess-fixture compilation; its test bodies took approximately 74 ms. No sleeps, polling, retries, production test seams, or extra test cases were added. Core production types, the owning Gateway test-type graph, scoped lint/format, assertion safety, and line-count ratchets passed. Hosted CI timing will be recorded once available.

Independent correction review is complete. Its remaining provider-policy concern was checked against the actual policy owner and rejected: CUA's node-invoke policy classifies provider-native actions; takeover is Gateway-owned viewer arbitration and is deliberately absent from that provider contract. It still checks the node command deny policy and live run, placement, worker, and RPC authority before eviction. Any subsequent native input continues through the existing plugin policy. The provider contract and policy for subsequent input are unchanged.

This is isolated Gateway boundary proof, not a deployed Gateway or live native-desktop proof: the viewer WebSocket and eviction path are real; the remote screenshot provider and desktop byte stream are synthetic. The earlier UI/noVNC and screenshot evidence above is unchanged.

### Bun retention CI repair

The replacement CI run failed two existing plugin-retention assertions under the checksum-pinned Bun test runtime: successor-registry collection and source-recovery owner collection ([failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36380789121/job/108798228889)). The test helper collected from a Promise continuation, where JavaScriptCore can retain completed async frames. Collection now runs in the native immediate callback before resolving the Promise. This is test-fixture scheduling only; all eight existing collections, leak assertions, unowned control, runtime admission, and product behavior are preserved.

- Replayed the original 193-file Bun subshard selection and order before editing. It reproduced successor-registry retention and the sibling bundled-ESM recovery-owner retention assertion. The original source-recovery case passed in that replay, so its exact recurrence is not claimed. The broad local replay also had 40 non-retention failures across six unchanged files (HTTP/provider/MCP fixtures); it is not green proof and those failures were not bypassed.
- After the collection-boundary repair, all **9 retention tests passed on pinned Bun** (57.51 seconds wall, including 31.57 seconds shared fixture compilation) and all **9 passed on Node** (40.15 seconds wall, including 24.43 seconds compilation), each with --maxWorkers=1. No new test cases, extra GC passes, retries, sleeps, skips, or relaxed assertions were added.
- An initial concurrent validation attempt stopped at the compiler snapshot guard because another invocation created its cache metadata. Both processes were collected, then the Bun proof was run serially without changing that guard. Independent P0–P2 review accepted the focused repair with no actionable findings; all 25 selected core test-type graphs, scoped formatting/lint, assertion-safety, line-cap and max-lines ratchets passed. The preceding desktop proof remains valid and is reused.
- The related UI collection-boundary repair in #159975 informed the diagnosis; that separate PR is not changed or landed here. Current-head hosted CI is still required before native replacement recovery.

### CI matrix integration and current proof

The next hosted preflight failed before tests: 206 Node jobs exceeded the unchanged 130-job limit. Integrated upstream main `2b8c65c47fd2`, including the already-landed planner repair `a08479ace1d4` by @steipete, to fix that concrete failure and the branch conflict. The canonical planner keeps compact selected-owner rows when time splitting would exceed the cap; broad plans may use longer rows rather than dropping coverage. No new planner implementation, workflow rerun, or dispatch is included in this PR.

The retention collection fix had independently reached main. The only overlapping merge conflict was its explanatory comment; the mainline comment was retained with identical executable code. All 26 remaining product paths are byte-identical to reviewed `4dd24bd20fcb`. The separate mapping and packing PRs are not prerequisites for this integrated product head.

- Complete 26-path workflow-manifest replay passed: **82 GitHub Node rows / 81 hybrid Node rows**, both with **6,419 selected targets** (49.79 s / 49.77 s). This is local exact-entry-point planner proof, not hosted CI success. The replay used the candidate source and pinned upstream harness, preserving the final 130-job guard.
- Refreshed focused proof: **73/73 tests passed** across takeover, computer transport, and Node retention (83.19 s wall); core production typing and the owning Gateway test graph passed. Prior 233-test, Bun-retention, UI/i18n, and screenshot evidence is reused for unchanged behavior.
- A first local attempt stopped before tests because concurrent proof JSON creation changed the compiler namespace. After the artifact writes finished, the serial run passed with the compiler guard unchanged. An unsupported type-shard selector was corrected to the canonical Gateway configuration; it was a command-selection error, not a product type failure.
- Fresh independent full-candidate P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Reviewed/tested tree: `709a3ac2ca1ac25349432d5bc97ab18ffb79cd35`. Current-head hosted gates remain required for native replacement recovery.

### Update-convergence fixture and handoff-policy clarification

Hosted CI [36393916927](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36393916927) passed the planner and reached tests, then failed two existing consent-handoff cases in `update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts`: the fixture selected `/usr/bin/node`, which was unavailable on that runner. The fixture now uses `process.execPath`; production update behavior and every existing assertion remain unchanged.

- Reproduced the exact two failures locally by making only `/usr/bin/node` unavailable inside a temporary mount namespace while running Node from a task-owned path: **2 failed / 17 passed**. The host executable was not changed.
- With the one-line fixture correction, the same isolated run passed **19/19 tests** with `--maxWorkers=1` in **17.41 seconds wall** (8.17 seconds of compiler preparation; 5.36 seconds in Vitest). No new tests, skips, retries, sleeps, or relaxed checks were added.
- The canonical update test-type graph, scoped lint/format, three-page MDX check, assertion-safety and line-count ratchets passed. Complete **28-path** workflow-manifest proof still fits: **82 GitHub / 81 hybrid Node rows**, each retaining **6,419 selected targets** (48.47 s / 46.16 s). This is local proof, not hosted CI success.
- Fresh independent full-candidate P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Reviewed/tested tree: `44605550cc4a017328117e1fe13dfdfffc1539ec`. Prior desktop behavior and screenshot evidence remain valid and unchanged. Required current-head hosted gates still precede native replacement recovery.

The requested handoff deliberately uses the admitted run’s existing computer-control authority for an explicit `take_control` action. It does not introduce a separate viewer-issued approval token for each resume. Ordinary input still pauses during manual control; current-run, command-policy, owner-epoch, replay, and revocation checks remain enforced, and the human can reclaim control. This resolves the review’s consent-scope question within the existing feature request rather than adding a new permission mechanism. The cloud-worker guide’s stale manual-release instruction and the two computer-control guides now describe the same boundary.

### Retained-custody release regression (superseded)

**Superseded by the reconciliation below:** the earlier one-line updater change has been withdrawn. The current candidate keeps the independently landed mainline release diagnostics and does not change updater production code.

CI [36395310070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36395310070/job/108840709276) reached the tests and failed four existing historical-custody cases. The release owner decoded an incompatible replacement row before reaching its existing unconditional refusal for retained v3 leases. The one-line correction refuses those leases before storage decoding, just as the existing transition and reclamation paths do. It does not release custody, change stored data or schemas, relax source-lock admission, or change ordinary update/cancellation authority.

- Reproduced all four failures locally: **4 failed / 20 passed** in the unchanged 24-case custody file. An expanded baseline also passed the 38 sibling cases while reproducing the same four failures.
- Corrected candidate: **62/62 tests passed** across custody, reclamation, original-owner, retarget, and retired-record suites with --maxWorkers=1, **96.21 seconds wall**, including **65.92 seconds** of compiler preparation. No tests, assertions, skips, retries, or timeouts changed; the fixtures exercise real isolated SQLite rows and service/config sidecars. This is local boundary/retained-record compatibility proof, not a new installed-updater replay.
- Core production types, scoped lint/format, assertion-safety and line-count ratchets passed. The complete **29-path** workflow manifest fits **84 GitHub / 83 hybrid Node rows**, with **7,330 selected targets** (48.10 s / 48.35 s); the 130-job guard is unchanged.
- Fresh independent full-candidate P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Reviewed/tested tree: b2e1767453840bb2983b24c8504b05f1e4204390; published correction: e09707094529631cadcc2a30def391500137cbeb. Earlier desktop, UI, and screenshot evidence remains unchanged. Current-head hosted gates are still required before native replacement recovery.

### Shared compiler scheduling repair and integration

CI [36396951760](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36396951760) failed before extension tests executed: bundle 13 and bundle 14 rejected differing OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_PARALLEL values. Their exact plans pair Telegram parallelism 2 with browser/iMessage parallelism 1. The owning shared repair [#160290](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160290) landed as 7510c4bd528945c6b77c0b9f0b710be8e4f108d4 and is now integrated. This repairs a named failed gate; no separate planner/compiler implementation, workflow rerun, dispatch, or guard relaxation was added here.

- Replayed both captured plans through real scheduling and shared compiler admission. All four child invocations retain their exact selected file lists, per-group parallelism [2, 1], and worker limits [2, 2]. The child callback is substituted; this is not a full extension-suite replay.
- The complete runner suite passed **201/201 tests** (4.23 s wall). The overlapping mainline desktop descriptor changes and this PR passed **71/71 desktop tests** across panel, session, presentation, and availability (6.79 s wall). Neutral disconnect and removal of the paused banner remain intact. No new tests were added by this integration.
- Complete **28-path** workflow-manifest proof passes with **84 GitHub / 82 hybrid Node rows**, retaining **7,330 selected targets** (54.91 s / 49.22 s), on integrated source and the pinned main harness with the unchanged 130-job cap.
- Fresh full-candidate independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Reviewed/tested tree: **18a78cff8563ddaabbe236c1d43755f588c8c489**; integration head: **73925e4531eafa8b9b23378cc315fa914fb2737a**. The earlier update-fixture repair is independently on main and no longer in this PR delta. Existing takeover, retained-custody, UI/i18n and four inspected screenshot proofs are reused where inputs are unchanged. Current-head hosted CI remains required; prior failed and cancelled jobs are not passing coverage.

**Maintainer decision:** Existing-grant explicit takeover is the feature requested by @steipete in the original discussion linked below, including removal of the paused-input banner. This is not a newly inferred handoff policy or a request for a viewer-issued approval token. Admitted-run, command-policy, epoch, replay, revocation and human-reclaim boundaries remain enforced. The three guides describe this deliberate behavior. No native security or review gate is waived by this clarification.

### Published lease-owner compatibility qualification (historical candidate)

This comparison qualified the now-withdrawn release shortcut, not the current candidate. Its published false-versus-throw observation remains historical evidence; it is not claimed as proof for mainline diagnostics or as a completed upgrade replay.

Executed the unchanged lease owner from the integrity-verified **openclaw 2026.9.6** npm artifact (build commit eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b) against this candidate's actual lease source. **Seven cross-version boundary cases passed** on Node 26.8.2: published-generated v2 read/release; reserved and admitted historical v3 custody; and four incompatible-row replacements. Both versions refuse v3 release, including returning false for a retained handle after its row becomes incompatible. Candidate releaseAll also refuses. The six retained-state cases preserve exact SQLite rows and synthetic sidecar bytes, inode, device, and mode; competing acquisition and source admission remain blocked.

The v3 fixtures are explicitly seeded historical input, not records generated by a released updater. Inspected September release tags contain no production v3 producer: published 2026.9.6 acquisition creates v2, ordinary transitions refuse v3, and its update executor refuses unresolved v3 custody before package mutation. The one-line candidate correction restores that released refusal behavior without changing custody or ordinary update authority.

This is **published lease-owner × candidate boundary proof**, not a completed installed-CLI package upgrade or live Gateway restart. Previous-Gateway preservation is supported by inspected admission ordering, not a running-Gateway observation. The canonical upgrade-survivor Docker harness was inspected but not run in this bounded proof (no Docker executable or prepared candidate package). No real configuration, service manager, Gateway, or shared dependency state was changed. The earlier 62-case custody regression and sibling evidence remains valid.

### Hot-reload test routing repair

Current-head CI [36400528839](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36400528839/job/108857573419) reached the tests, then the existing low-level channel hot-reload reply case failed with **Agent admission requires its host owner**. Its real session write reaches host-owned SQLite admission, but the file was assigned to the threaded agents-core shard. The canonical database-worker registry now routes that unchanged file through the existing isolated fork owner. No production guard, fixture assertion, worker limit, timeout, or retry policy was relaxed.

- Replayed the captured **175-file** runtime selection first and reproduced the exact failure. That broad local baseline also hit a separate 120-second MCP discovery timeout; it was bounded and its children settled. It is not claimed as a completed or green full-shard run.
- The new cheap registry regression failed before the route change (**1 failed / 7 passed**). Afterward, **16/16 focused tests passed**: all eight unchanged hot-reload cases through the real forked owner and all eight routing-registry cases. Wall time was **101.48 s**, including **62.68 s** subprocess compiler preparation. The formerly failing low-level reply case passed in **1.473 s**.
- Standalone registry-file proof with --maxWorkers=1 passed in **1.47 s wall**; the one added table case measured **1 ms**. Hosted timing is not yet available for this replacement.
- Root-scripts test typing, scoped lint/format, assertion-safety, line-count ratchets, and whitespace checks passed. Fresh independent full-candidate P0–P2 review is scoped-clean; its assessment did not claim tests were finished while they were still running. Those tests subsequently completed successfully as recorded above.
- Complete **30-path** workflow-manifest proof passes: **95 GitHub / 89 hybrid Node rows**, **7,388 selected targets** (53.81 s / 51.54 s). Every previous 7,330 target remains selected. The hot-reload file appears exactly once under the existing infra/forks owner in both plans; the 130-job cap remains unchanged.

Published correction: **f2098f0708bb9a7f70279fc483ae3c542a117560**, tree **e310c4552f85283430493af75561c12a88bbd91f**, equal to the reviewed and tested source. Desktop behavior and the four inspected screenshots are unchanged. Required hosted gates on this replacement and native recovery remain outstanding; no failed or cancelled prior job is counted as passing coverage.

### Current CI reconciliation

CI [36402532322](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36402532322) identified two root failures; the other stopped jobs were cancelled and are not passing coverage.

- **Keep the canonical updater repair.** Main independently landed fa90c83d1ab83cb73a10d2bb24cc08af20fd2683, requiring an incompatibility diagnostic while preserving retained rows and sidecars. That overlapped with this PR's earlier shortcut returning false. The shortcut is withdrawn: update-managed-service-handoff-lease.ts is byte-identical to the integrated main, with no updater production or assertion change left in this PR. The exact four failures reproduced; all **62 unchanged custody and sibling tests passed** after reconciliation (**63.43 s wall**, including 44.88 s compiler preparation). This keeps the current main contract instead of introducing a competing release policy. Historical proof above is explicitly superseded.
- **Join the actual completion owner.** The completion-exhaustion Gateway E2E polled immediately after a void-returning resume, while its real detached cleanup and delivery-mirror lookup were still running. The test now uses the existing root-work observer to join that work before checking the same suspended/permanent-failure/expiry state. The focused baseline reproduced the CI failure; the corrected test passed in **19.59 s wall**, with **4.741 s** in the test body and 7.31 s compiler preparation. No production change, new test, timeout increase, retry, relaxed assertion, or permissive authority mock was added.
- This is source-Gateway fixture proof using isolated state and the documented fixture-owned build selector, not a deployed Gateway. The original 12-target local shard attempt stopped before tests at package-publication preflight; no system environment or service was changed. The captured 18-file owner baseline reproduced the four custody failures and also had seven local managerless-service inspection failures absent from the hosted job; that broad run is not claimed green.

- Core Gateway test typing, scoped lint/format, assertion-safety and line-count ratchets passed. Fresh full-candidate independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Complete **30-path** workflow-manifest proof passes with **94 GitHub / 87 hybrid Node rows**, **6,481 selected targets** (49.51 s / 53.83 s), under the unchanged 130-job cap. The target count shrank because updater production is no longer changed, not because a guard or test selection was disabled.

Published correction: **c3ca4cda5a19e03482638cdf70df45e8d286aa80**, reviewed/tested tree **c289675eaf28dc4d085eadc8887ea4cd2472d6c8**. Existing desktop, real viewer-WebSocket, UI and four inspected screenshot proofs are unchanged. Required hosted checks on this replacement still precede completed native preparation and retained-outcome recovery.

### Shared ACP fixture integration

CI [36405014807](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36405014807/job/108872254984) failed ten existing ACP lifecycle cases during module import: a test mock omitted the newly introduced `prepareAcpSessionControlRead` export. The cancelled siblings are not passing coverage.

Integrated the existing shared owner’s reviewed [fixture correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b68e77ed7038d14f8555adb9b1819c6d25739fbb) and its pinned main `40ce44117ff2` input, rather than writing a competing repair. Both factories now preserve the real session-control exports through typed `importOriginal` while keeping their explicit test overrides. No production ACP change, new test, relaxed assertion, retry, timeout change, or permission shortcut was added.

- On the integrated desktop candidate, **161/161 tests passed** across ACP commands (73), dispatch lifecycle (74), real viewer takeover (6), and the routing registry (8). Wall time was **77.58 seconds**, including **32.45 seconds** of subprocess compiler preparation. The original ten failing lifecycle cases all pass.
- Core production and messaging test types, scoped lint/format, assertion-safety, line-cap, max-lines, and whitespace checks passed. The shared owner also supplied red-before/green-after proof and broader sibling coverage; those tests were not duplicated here.
- Full **32-path** workflow-manifest proof passes with **94 GitHub / 84 hybrid Node rows** and **6,719 selected targets** (49.30 s / 49.70 s), using the integrated source and pinned main harness. The 130-job cap and selection guards are unchanged. This is local planner proof, not hosted CI success.
- Fresh independent full-candidate P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Published head **3374983c6db402c8ba3e06c37298cda861b0bac7**, tree **99c701927296431aa6ea99ef4d8cd2a41cab99d1**, matches the reviewed and tested source. Earlier desktop, real viewer-WebSocket, UI/i18n and four inspected screenshot evidence is reused where inputs are unchanged.

title: fix(ui): reduce stalls opening large Skills menus
body:
Related: #149361

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable delays when opening a large Skills menu in Chat or New Session.

## User Impact

The complete menu opens with less main-thread work, without changing its design, removing skills or controls, or disabling the pet. Keyboard navigation, checked/disabled states, drafts and selection remain intact.

Dense lists still incur full-list construction cost; this does not eliminate every long task or promise a device-independent latency target.

## Why This Change Was Made

New Session measured composer geometry while the newly inserted menu's custom elements were still updating, forcing an extra style/layout pass. Dirty measurements now coalesce before paint, while ResizeObserver updates still keep collision geometry current in the same paint.

Chat had a separate redundant focus pass: a menu could replace the clicked row before the composer received the bubbling click. Checking the original event path prevents that menu action from being mistaken for a click on empty composer space.

## Evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a085f38-cba9-487e-85d6-ff38136111fd

[Recording details and matched screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159917#issuecomment-5860203675).

Matched actual production UI with synthetic mock-Gateway data, isolated Linux/Chromium 144.0.7559.0 runner, 1440×900, dark theme/reduced motion, no CPU throttling; five pointer opens per condition:

| 300 skills | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| New Session: click → second animation frame, median | 136.6 ms | 107.4 ms |
| Chat: click → second animation frame, median | 173.6 ms | 125.0 ms |
| New Session: aggregate action style work, median | 57.0 ms | 33.7 ms |
| Chat: aggregate action style work, median | 85.3 ms | 47.0 ms |

The ordinary 12-skill controls remain around 30 ms to the second frame without ≥50 ms tasks. Aggregate action task time also decreased; the work was not merely moved beyond the first-frame measurement. These are bounded browser measurements, not INP or exact paint timing. In Chat, unwanted textarea focus during opening changed from once on each of five opens to zero on all five.

- Both new regressions fail on the original code for the intended reasons. **91 owner/sibling tests pass** on the final candidate (all three pet suites plus composer pointer activation, one worker: 2.92 s Vitest / 3.70 s wrapper wall). CI exposed one additional visitor fixture that assumed initial geometry before the first frame; its exact failure was reproduced locally and fixed by advancing the fake initial frame, without removing any retirement/offline/long-run assertions. Production and browser proof are unchanged by this test-only correction.
- **17 existing menu E2E tests pass**, including attachment actions, sparse overrides, access/readiness gates, connector/tool siblings, compact height/keyboard visibility and atomic New Session creation.
- Dense real-flow checks pass for toggle/reopen, first/last keyboard access, 390px and short-viewport resize, light/dark, draft/selection preservation, reconnect, reordered 301-row catalogs and disabled dependency explanations.
- Current-main test-audit applied: removed **10 lines of obsolete margin-inset test setup**, retained all Send/Stop/composition assertions, and added only the two distinct owner-boundary regressions. No new test-only production hooks.
- Independent AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the scoped change.
- UI and core-test typechecks, formatting, i18n, targeted lint/stylelint, and production/full-tree unused-export scans pass. The aggregate changed check remains red on the unchanged script-only audit: `readMergePolicy` / `readRequiredMergeChecks` in `scripts/pr-lib/merge-rest.mjs`. Their existing consumer is `merge-prior-ci.mjs`; that scan explicitly ignores UI, and none of its script/config/import/export inputs changed here.

No live Gateway/configuration changes, dependency changes, caps, caching, search or virtualization. Physical-device, screen-reader and real-IME behavior is not newly certified by this mocked Chromium proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes abrupt, border-like fades where sidebar sessions, queued messages, and the chat transcript meet their clipping edges.

## User Impact

These content edges fade out more gradually without changing scroll controls, draft state, keyboard targets, or reduced-motion behavior. The visual review hold has been cleared; landing is authorized after the requested test cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use eased alpha stops with a small clear margin at clipped row edges. Keep the queue fade at 24px and sidebar fade at 32px, while preserving the transcript’s original 24px geometry instead of applying the attachment rail’s 48px width everywhere. The sidebar’s independent scrollbar mask, RTL placement, transcript gutters, and short-pane exclusions remain intact.

This is the implemented subset of the broader fade audit—not a claim that every surface was changed or browser-certified. Compact text/editor/disclosure fades and existing eased attachment/photo fades are retained. Inbox, Workboard, and Dreams diary received source review only and are not modified here.

## Evidence

CI correction: increasing the transcript fade to 32px changed its padding/layout contract. A controlled same-environment comparison reproduced three failures (200px-high footer containment and both image-handoff orderings), then passed all four existing cases after restoring only the header height and footer token to their original 24px. Eased stops remain. The two trimmed fade-regression cases also pass; transcript screenshots are refreshed for the final geometry.

Test audit: reduced `spatial-fades.e2e.test.ts` from 190 to 131 lines (59 net lines removed). Screenshot-capture scaffolding and duplicate Markdown-table assertions are gone; the canonical table interaction suite retains that coverage. Both viewport cases still exercise real sidebar/queue scroll states, keyboard focus, and every-pixel smoothness checks at both edges. Fixed the CI oracle to sample inside the scrollport rather than its fractionally captured parent border; thresholds were not relaxed. The reduced fade regression passes. The test cleanup does not change production styling; the subsequent geometry correction is documented above. A single-file, single-worker Chromium run measured **18.62s Vitest wall time**, including bundled-server setup, with **3.642s in the two test cases** (Blacksmith Testbox; 81.448s wrapper command time includes dependency/source verification). Exact-head CI timing is tracked separately.

- Chromium: two final wide/narrow scroll-and-raster flows passed; four existing sidebar inset, classic-scrollbar, RTL and focus-containment cases passed. Both light and dark captures inspected.
- The old queue ramp failed the pixel regression (56/255 at the edge versus the <30 threshold); the final test samples every pixel across both fade regions to reject hard jumps and preserve opaque interiors.

title: fix(ui): reduce pauses when searching large model lists

## What Problem This Solves

Large model catalogs can make search pause while retained results are rebound and laid out again.

## User Impact

Search does less unnecessary work without changing the picker layout, labels, available choices, provider groups, collapse behavior, defaults, access rules, keyboard controls, focus restoration, or active-row scrolling. This is a performance-only change: no caps, debounce, virtualization, or removal of information.

Flat nonmatches remain mounted with native `hidden` and a scoped display rule. The tradeoff is retaining the complete current catalog DOM during filtering, rather than only matching rows; the complete catalog was already mounted before opening. Eligibility and commit validation still use the current filtered choices.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep option identities and ARIA targets stable, share one derived section view within each update, and avoid deriving choices for ordinary search-input editing keys. Retaining flat result nodes avoids structural mutations that Chrome's broad sibling invalidation rules otherwise expand into a large restyle. Grouped results retain their original filtered ordering and collapse semantics. Provider-section positions deliberately keep the existing behavior so catalog reordering does not drop native header focus. An attempted global spacing-selector change did not establish a gain and is **not included**.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes extra typing work in **Agent settings → Files** when editing a long document with Preview closed.

## User Impact

The editor keeps the same layout, controls, complete document, statistics, sanitization, draft behavior, and keyboard/focus handling. Initial preview preparation is retained; opening always shows the latest draft.

The hidden dialog was rebuilding sanitized Markdown and its DOM on every edit. title: feat(ui): add a personal external browser preference
body:
Closes #159884

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Maintainers can edit this same-repository branch.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

People who prefer their regular browser currently have to bypass OpenClaw's built-in link readers or native browser panel one link at a time. The existing Control UI browser preference does not override those paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add **Open links outside OpenClaw** under **Settings → Appearance → Chat**, using the existing browser-local preference storage. It overrides automatic reader and browser-panel routing without erasing the existing browser-panel preference. The default stays off, so upgrades retain current behavior.

The setting does not change shared Gateway configuration, change Gateway profile or database schemas, or sync across devices. A small extraction of the local Chat preference bindings keeps the existing settings page within its line-growth limit.

## User Impact

Enable the switch to use ordinary browser navigation on the web or the system-default browser in a native host. Disable it to restore the existing reader/panel behavior. The choice survives reloads in the same browser or app webview and is scoped per Gateway. Internal navigation, downloads, modifier-click behavior, and explicit context-menu choices remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Real Chromium flow with a mocked Gateway: default reader → enable switch → reload → external opening → disable switch → reader restored. Verified both the ordinary browser popup and the native-link bridge handoff; no shared configuration writes. This is not physical-device native-app proof.
- New routing cases fail against the original implementation and pass with the change. Routing, native/browser sibling behavior, preference persistence, shared-config isolation, settings search, and rendered-switch tests passed.
- Changed-surface validation passed: formatting, line-growth guards, i18n, selected core-test type graphs, UI typecheck, dead-export scans, lint, and styles. The first lint pass found an unbound test-cleanup callback; binding it and rerunning the routing tests and affected lint/style checks resolved it.
- UI build passed, including the bundle performance gate.
- **test-audit:** each changed test covers a distinct routing, persistence, isolation, search, or rendered-control contract; no duplicate coverage or test-only production seam added.
- **deslop:** reviewed the complete diff; no unnecessary defensive branches, casts, compatibility paths, or comment cleanup remained.
- **autoreview:** scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings. The only subsequent change was binding a test-cleanup callback for lint.
- **Flake triage:** no product-test flakes observed. Initial proof-script failures came from the standalone TSX serialization helper, switch targeting, and an incorrect assumption that existing panels should disappear; the capture fixture was corrected without changing product behavior or increasing timeouts.
- **Current-head CI passed** on 375ab9bc5a63e55e9639c7ee4a68e8bf24716880: [CI run 36355269004](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36355269004). Required CI, security, and dependency-review checks are successful. No failures occurred in the feature PR's CI run; separate native-proof attempts are reported below.

### Approved wording revision

The switch now reads **Open links outside OpenClaw**, with **Use your browser instead of the OpenClaw built-in browser.** and **Saved in this browser only.** Defaults, storage, and link routing are unchanged.

The existing rendered-control and settings-search tests passed (28 tests); i18n verification, formatting, lint, and whitespace checks passed. Test-audit: only existing copy/discovery expectations changed, with no new cases or test seams. Deslop: no cleanup needed. Copy-only autoreview was scoped-clean at P0–P2. The After screenshot below shows the new wording.

### Review follow-up

[Latest ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159887#issuecomment-5859906910) accepted the saved-state compatibility evidence and reports no actionable code findings. Revision 7 reviewed this exact head and accepted the native handoff proof: **Ready for maintainer review**, no actionable findings, and **Before merge: None**. Ordinary maintainer review is still required; the PR has not been merged.

- **Product direction:** this is a maintainer-requested implementation for @VACInc, with the chosen browser-local opt-in approved in the linked work session. The linked issue tracks implementation, not an unresolved product proposal.
- **Saved-state compatibility:** the persistence test now seeds an older settings blob with the existing browser-panel preference enabled and no external-link field. Enabling the new switch, reading the saved state again, and disabling it preserve both that preference and an unrelated sidebar-width setting; another Gateway keeps its default. All 29 persistence tests passed. title: fix(code-mode): stop bookkeeping changes hiding repeated tool loops
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Code Mode can keep rediscovering the same tools or resuming unchanged work because changing execution titles, telemetry counters, and bridge IDs disguise repeated activity as progress.

## User Impact

With loop detection enabled, repeated equivalent Code Mode activity reaches the existing warning/block/recovery path. Real output, returned data, errors, and changes to pending operations remain distinguishable. Receipts still show their original counters and IDs.

**Scope:** this does not classify arbitrary equivalent JavaScript rewrites, add a scheduler, alter notification settings, or make command processes survive a Gateway restart. No configuration migration, permission relaxation, or production deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detector compared Code Mode bookkeeping as though it were task output. Code Mode now supplies a private, immutable comparison snapshot; suspended work records the actual operation and arguments instead of a fresh bridge ID. Execution titles remain display metadata rather than action identity. Guest-owned fields with the same names retain their meaning. Automatically retained results are compared using the original guest value, not their fresh reference IDs.

Requested by @VACInc.

Closes #159820

## What Problem This Solves

The Lobsterdex needs downloadable coloring sheets and matching full-color guides without changing its cards. A guide must be the **identical coloring sheet filled with color**, not a differently outlined version of the animated pet.

## User Impact

A discreet top-right download icon, opposite the existing link icon, offers **Coloring sheet (PDF)** or **Color guide (PDF)**. It appears on hover/keyboard focus and stays visible on mobile/touch layouts. Bulk downloads provide a ZIP of either format, including undiscovered catalog entries without changing discovery history.

The original card dimensions, padding, layout, artwork, names, lore, dates, and shiny marker are unchanged. Every export is a one-page A4 PDF generated locally; nothing is uploaded by this feature.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both modes now use **one print-art generator**. It owns the same geometry, pruning, unfilled regions, opaque pure-black strokes, widths, caps, and joins. Only the opaque fill colors differ. This fixes missing/thin/colored outlines on details such as Squeaky's antennae, claws, highlights, eyes, connectors, and string.

The separate color renderer and its size-based contour heuristic were removed. Palette fills are resolved in an isolated static light document, with fill alpha flattened onto paper-white so a colored area cannot reveal extra rear outlines or fade the black edges. The PDF layout/ZIP workflow and quiet download menus remain shared and unchanged.

title: feat(ui): add seven character variants to the Lobsterdex
body:
Closes #159814

## What Problem This Solves

Adds the requested **Clawnstantine, Clawie Stardust, Taylor Pinch, Clawtoo Deetoo, Leonardo DaPinchy, Shellvis, and Alexander Graham Shell** characters to the Control UI Lobsterdex.

## User Impact

The collection grows from 42 to 49 entries, with seven distinct rare visitors, signature names, lore, and normal/shiny discovery records. Existing browser memories are preserved; no configuration or migration is needed.

**Intended completion behavior (confirmed by @hannesrudolph):** The golden ledge trim means the **current catalog** is complete; it is not a permanent reward for completing an older catalog. When new lobsters are added, previously complete collections become incomplete until those new entries are discovered. For this update, 42/42 becomes 42/49 and the trim returns at 49/49. Existing discoveries, visitor names, first-visit dates, and shiny records remain intact. Previously earned trim is deliberately not grandfathered.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Clawnstantine:** purple shell, golden laurel, polished imperial sash. “Built an empire. Still rules from the ledge.”
- **Clawie Stardust:** warm peach shell, orange-red claws, and Bowie-inspired red lightning with an electric-blue edge. “Changes shells. Never changes style.”
- **Taylor Pinch:** blonde-gold shell, cherry-red smile/claws, a sparkling lavender outfit, and a claw-held microphone. “Turns every tide into an era.”
- **Clawtoo Deetoo:** silver-white shell, cobalt-blue droid panels, and a small red status light. “Speaks fluent beep. Fixes things anyway.”
- **Leonardo DaPinchy:** parchment shell, soft brown beret, beard, paint-marked olive smock, and a claw-held brush. “Every shell is a canvas.”
- **Shellvis:** dark pompadour and sideburns, white/gold jumpsuit, red scarf, blue suede claws, and a microphone. “The king of rock and claw.”

Related: #142506 ## What Problem This Solves Android users need to operate the agent’s existing browser inside chat without losing the conversation or draft, or getting stuck with a card they cannot dismiss. ## User Impact **Agent browser** shows the exact session tab with expand/collapse chevrons and a separate close icon. Collapse returns space to chat and releases the browser keyboard. Close hides the card without closing the remote tab; **Chat actions → Agent browser** restores it. A dismissed historical result stays hidden across refreshes and navigation while the app runs; a new browser result can appear again. Embedded control retains `operator.admin` and requires an updated Gateway with bundled Control UI. Older Gateways, disabled UI, and custom UI roots show a closable update notice instead of an unsupported WebView. Ordinary links and Desktop are unchanged; external opening remains explicit. No new browser service, persistent store, permissions, protocol bump, deployment, or release. ## Why This Change Was Made The card preserves structured browser-tab identity and reuses the existing authenticated WebView and Browser panel. Android owns presentation/dismissal; the Gateway and Browser plugin retain browser authority. The existing hello capability list signals browser-focus availability and resets with the connection. Shared input handling supports touch scrolling, soft-keyboard text, composition, and ordered input. Unsupported local autocorrection shows a notice rather than appending incorrect replacement text. title: fix(ci): distinguish survivor recovery failure boundaries
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ambiguous upgrade-survivor diagnostics when the managed recovery update fails: command exit, successful-result assertion, supervisor replacement, and installed-version mismatch currently all report `recovery-update-restart`. This is a maintainer-requested diagnostic follow-up to Package Acceptance run 36325677712, job 108641651545; it does not claim to fix that update failure.

## User Impact

No installed-product behavior changes. Release maintainers can identify the failing recovery boundary through the existing bounded failure-metadata transport without publishing command output, paths, environment values, or arbitrary reason strings. No timeout, custody, identity, refusal, auth, or cleanup assertion changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `CURRENT_PHASE` in the existing shell owner with four fixed values: `recovery-update-command`, `recovery-update-result-assertion`, `recovery-update-service-replacement`, and `recovery-update-version-match`. Restore the outer phase on success. The outer started/passed events remain unchanged. A nonzero updater still skips the JSON assertion and preserves its exit code; signals and pre-cleanup capture retain the active boundary and this invocation's recovery observation directory.

Compatibility: the existing phase grammar already accepts all four values. The metadata object and artifact schema are unchanged; regressions compare published artifact bytes after normalizing only the intentionally refined phase value. No postCore fields or raw diagnostics were added.

Separate unresolved fixture issue: the systemctl shim rejects the existing `LoadState,TimeoutStopUSec` query and uses a fixed 30-second child stop deadline despite the generated 330-second policy. This mismatch also exists on main, but no failing-run evidence establishes it as causal. It remains for causal follow-through; this PR neither fixes nor waives it and does not raise deadlines.

## Evidence

- Before: 7 recovery-stage regressions failed against base f0b149f44df9a47ea6822bec2b7b438a938ec54a because all reported the outer phase; success and initial-update control passed.
- After: all 10 cases passed, covering command exits 1/17, JSON failure, false replacement, version mismatch, success/outer restoration, SIGTERM in command/assertion/replacement, initial-update control, observation binding, and capture-before-cleanup.
- Per-file cost: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/upgrade-survivor-recovery-phase.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (supported direct-Node equivalent of `pnpm test`): **2.60 s wall**, **239 ms tests**, 10 passed. No sleeps, polling, package install, or Gateway boots.
- Existing host CLI publication compatibility test: 1 passed, 2.30 s wall, 528 ms test. Existing updater-result suite: 34 passed, 5.09 s wall, 3.179 s tests (initial/recoverable updates, restart ownership, and consent refusal unchanged).
- Scoped oxlint: 0 warnings/errors; shell syntax, diff whitespace, conflict-marker and line-cap checks passed.
- Local root-test typecheck was refused by its declaration-provenance guard because the borrowed dependency installation is outside this checkout. No installation or bypass was attempted; normal PR CI owns that check. Full build/suite and actual package lane were not run.
- The single bounded Codex AutoReview attempt returned `reviewer_unavailable`, `report_produced=false`, engine exit 124 after 240 seconds. This is an explicit independent-review gap, not a clean verdict. The supervising release assistant inspected the complete patch, actual lifecycle/control-flow boundary and regression before publishing for normal hosted CI and independent Claw review. No fallback/retry or merge was performed. Parent retains all review, native landing and diagnostic-dispatch decisions.

title: fix(android): clarify blocked and partial SMS access during setup
body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes misleading SMS recovery advice and hidden partial grants during Android setup. ## User Impact Third-party builds on supported telephony devices show partial SMS access and explain when Android Settings may help versus when an installer or device-policy restriction may prevent access. Google Play builds remain without SMS. No permissions, Gateway capabilities, or defaults are enabled automatically. ## Why This Change Was Made Android suppresses permission prompts for both permanent user denial and hard/system restrictions; lack of a rationale does not identify the cause. The existing `PermissionRequester` now gives conditional, actionable SMS recovery guidance and still names only missing permissions. Setup retains read/send presentation separately while preserving the existing per-permission callback merge and resume refresh. No new permission owner, privileged allowlist queries, pairing changes, or bulk permission request. The source inventory includes the five new strings; generated translations and platform resources remain owned by the serialized native locale refresh workflow. English source fallback is preserved. Coordinated with the independent optional-permission batch-request task ([#159727](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159727)): this change owns SMS-specific recovery and read/send presentation; that change owns batch requests and optional-safe generic copy. The shared `buildSettingsMessage` overlap must retain both the SMS branch and its deduplicated labels/generic fallback. Neither branch includes the other. Worked on by @IWhatsskill. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @IWhatsskill](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f70733f-9118-4e69-8ba3-a97b0490baec) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/9db45a7f-58c5-4574-a9fd-b136bd8d62c2) ## Evidence Verified head: `e8b679ac163698c9f5f12d01bd8fd789cb4157ef` (independent branch based on `e52420e1eea6c614ba7730d3d36980167478c6df`). - Baseline regression: real `OnboardingFlow` → Android ActivityResult → existing `PermissionRequester` produced `Please enable Send SMS in Android Settings to continue.` with read already granted and send denied. The regression fails on the original source and passes with the repair. - Focused JVM/Compose checks: 76/76 tests per flavor, 152 total, in 90.55 s wall including compilation. Covers independent SMS grants, unavailable build/device, denial, returning without a grant, Settings recovery, grant revocation, requester lifecycle, and preserved QR/bootstrap handoff. Native generated-artifact isolation passes (six source files); strict translated parity belongs to the locale refresh, not this source PR. - Full `InitialOnboardingLayoutTest`: 14/14 passed; 14.676 s test time, 29.12 s Gradle wall with `--max-workers=1`. - Earlier capture-head APK build (`f2529135cf2d52e0445960e2149f54560f6d63fc`): `:app:assembleThirdPartyDebug :app:assemblePlayDebug` passed in 45.57 s wall. Packaged Play manifest has no `READ_SMS`/`SEND_SMS`; third-party declares both. Both earlier APKs contain that capture head. Both final APKs embed `e8b679ac163698c9f5f12d01bd8fd789cb4157ef`; source fallback is exercised after removing generated locale changes. - Diff-scoped deslop and independent Codex P0–P2 autoreview: scoped-clean on the complete final candidate, before the mechanical removal of generated locale changes; production/test source is unchanged. Real OS state was `READ_SMS=true`, `SEND_SMS=false`; ordinary Android denial established `USER_FIXED`. The candidate shows partial access and conditional recovery advice. Its Open Settings action opens the real Android app settings; returning without changes leaves SMS partial, with no false success or QR restart. No SMS was read or sent. title: fix(android): keep Gateway picker open while scrolling

## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Android's Gateway picker closes when a finger swipe reaches or starts at the top of its saved-Gateway list. ## User Impact Users can scroll the picker without dismissing it or changing Gateways. Back, outside-tap dismissal, and the explicit accessibility dismiss action remain available. Gateway-scoped drafts and attachments, native-window ownership, and terminal lifecycle revocation are unchanged. The installed API-36 app now passes the native touch/IME/lifecycle test. The earlier Robolectric captures remain labeled separately. ## Why This Change Was Made Material 3's default nested-scroll/drag handling takes unconsumed list movement and settles the sheet to `Hidden`. The original touch reproduction invoked Material's `onDismissRequest`; temporary diagnostics showed no fold-owner rejection. This change disables sheet gestures only for the Gateway picker and preserves the existing handle's explicit accessibility dismissal action, which Material otherwise removes with gestures disabled. The picker, `FoldAwareSheet`, registry, and connection/draft owners are not replaced. There are no timers, automatic reopening, or relaxed lifecycle checks. title: fix(android): keep automation runs out of pinned chats
body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Android mixes pinned cron/system conversations into ordinary chat navigation. Hiding them must not remove the ability to reopen their transcripts. ## User Impact Ordinary Sidebar/Recent lists stay focused on conversations. **Threads → Automations** keeps retained cron and system chats discoverable, including previously pinned ones; tapping a row opens its transcript. The selected chat remains in ordinary navigation. Human-created background work, named work, legacy rows, and all saved pins are preserved. The filter is screen-local, not a new persisted preference. Settings → Automations continues to show schedules and recent run summaries. No Gateway change, migration, deletion, or pin mutation. ## Why This Change Was Made Android now retains the Gateway creation facts needed by the shared Web policy. One native predicate owns both ordinary exclusion and automation discovery; structural cron keys and recorded provenance determine membership, never title keywords or `isBackground` alone. Existing Threads search, row selection, Current, and Archived flows are reused. Filter controls wrap on a narrow phone. This repairs ClawSweeper's P1 finding about previously pinned automation transcripts becoming undiscoverable. The intended scope separates automation pins from ordinary Sidebar Pinned while preserving them in the Automations scope. Creation provenance does not identify who pinned a row; no automatic/manual pin origin is inferred. Individual historical `:run` rows were already excluded from the ordinary Gateway roster before this PR; this change restores the root/system conversations that the PR hid, without adding a new run-history browser. Worked on by @IWhatsskill. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @IWhatsskill](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f70733f-9118-4e69-8ba3-a97b0490baec) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0cff9229-d1d9-4774-9d63-0dade1951465) ## Evidence - **Prepared head:** `b90f1cabf2121fdfd9f284173c6722dcac2df97e`. title: feat(android): request optional setup permissions together
body:
## What Problem This Solves Android setup needs separate taps for every optional permission, even when someone wants to request all available setup access. ## User Impact Users can choose **Request all**, allow or deny Android's permission prompts, and continue setup. Individual choices remain available. The batch visibly lists available additional permissions, including SMS and call logs on eligible third-party devices. Play/unavailable permissions are excluded; notification-listener access remains a separate Settings action. Camera and location features have separate enable controls. Other permissions, such as contacts and calendar, can become usable after Android and Gateway approval. Existing Gateway approval requirements remain intact. ## Why This Change Was Made Individual and batch requests share the existing serialized `PermissionRequester` and permission-row model. User-driven requests remain pending until a platform result or navigation cancellation. Empty callbacks mean cancellation, and optional batches do not force Settings escalation; individual recovery is preserved. The landed SMS work is retained, including independent read/send state, partial-grant presentation, and truthful restriction guidance. Native testing exposed a pre-existing completion hang: a promptable `sms.search` command was required even with SMS denied and its capability absent. The existing approval owner now requires command families only for enabled onboarding capabilities, preserving every granted-permission, confirmed-surface, current-connection, and enqueue-authority check. Gateway command policy is unchanged. No new request manager or Android manifest permissions. Defaults, iOS, schemas, and the production Gateway are unchanged. ## Evidence Verified head: `5822b084fd71f01d9bd05fb264b6bdc7cf6b1255`. - **92 focused tests passed per flavor** (Play and third-party), including optional batch outcomes, cancellation/lifecycle, individual Settings recovery, disclosure availability, independent SMS grants, and approval safety. The denied-SMS approval regression failed before the fix (`phone-request` expected, `null` observed). - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. Deslop completed; fresh independent autoreview is **scoped-clean through P2**, with both disclosure findings resolved. - **[Current-head installed Android proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159727#issuecomment-5858068164):** nine real OS prompts, partial consent including SMS/call-log denial, PackageManager/app-row agreement, preserved capability opt-ins, normal node reapproval, and successful completion to Overview. Individual permanent-denial → Android Settings → grant readback also passed without restarting Gateway setup. - **[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36334959512) passed:** 39 successful jobs, 20 intentionally skipped, no failures. Both app flavors, Wear, Android ktlint, and 4K/16K native Access lanes passed. - **[ClawSweeper revision 5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159727#issuecomment-5857168058):** reviewed this exact head and accepted the current-head native evidence. Real behavior verified; findings, security findings, and before-merge items: none. Merged via squash through the native repository workflow after required CI and review gates passed. Prepared head: `5822b084fd71f01d9bd05fb264b6bdc7cf6b1255`; landed commit: [`4288881dedc61f9bc644532e8ecd6f4f36dba49c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4288881dedc61f9bc644532e8ecd6f4f36dba49c).
Commands, measured cost, and proof limits Run each flavor as a separate Gradle invocation so the test filters apply to both: ```sh node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-android-gradle.mts \ :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \ --tests ai.openclaw.app.PermissionRequesterTest \ --tests ai.openclaw.app.GatewayNodeApprovalTest \ --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.AndroidPermissionSnapshotTest \ --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.OnboardingFlowLogicTest \ --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.InitialOnboardingLayoutTest.setup*' \ --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.InitialOnboardingLayoutTest.deniedSetupPermissionOffersExistingSettingsRecoveryAndRefreshesOnReturn \ --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.InitialOnboardingLayoutTest.smsSetupKeepsPartialGrantsAndExplainsBlockedAccess # Same selection for :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest ``` Local wall: Play **20.26 s**, third-party **19.64 s**. Changed test-file runtime (Play / third-party): `PermissionRequesterTest` **2.662 / 2.562 s**; `GatewayNodeApprovalTest` **0.101 / 0.099 s**; eight selected `InitialOnboardingLayoutTest` cases **8.478 / 8.253 s**. Existing fixtures are reused; the Compose boundary detects duplicate requests, accidental feature opt-in, and queued requests surviving navigation. CI flavor-job timing is linked in the run, not misrepresented as individual test cost. Both final debug APK flavors build. The installed third-party APK hash and native sequence are recorded in the proof comment. Android 12 emulator proof is not physical/OEM, SMS transport, or Android 13+ notification-dialog proof. Installer exemptions were present in this adb installation. The isolated Gateway has no model-provider credentials. Its minimum-height editor still centered short text vertically: rendered top inset was **17 dp** for empty/single-line drafts versus **10 dp** for multiline drafts at normal font scale. The active iOS `.clean` composer likewise top-aligns its full-width draft row above a separate toolbar. ## Evidence - Verified head: `355f65461a8d5b9dde2199777b52f618fb0a685d` (publication-marker commit; tree identical to tested/reviewed `ba098cf27c89466e714672af709233b0d18bc99c`). title: feat(android): give saved gateways persistent local names
body:
## What Problem This Solves Saved Android Gateways use long endpoint names in the sidebar and picker, with no persistent local rename action. ## User Impact Users can rename saved Gateways in **Manage Gateways**, including while offline. Names survive gateway switching, reconnect metadata, app/store reloads, and discovery updates; secondary addresses distinguish duplicate names and long labels are truncated. Clearing a name restores the automatic name. Renaming changes neither endpoint identity/address nor credentials and does not rename the server. **Persistence decision:** add nullable `localName` inside the existing encrypted `gateway.registry` record, keeping its current version. Existing v1/v2 entries decode without a migration and retain their automatic names. No second registry, sidecar, database, or server API is introduced. An older Android app can discard this additive field when rewriting the registry after a downgrade. Forgetting an entry also removes its local name. **Accepted maintainer decision:** @IWhatsskill explicitly accepts loss of these new local display names after downgrading to an older Android app, while endpoint IDs, addresses, and credentials remain intact. The Android guide now documents this limitation and how to restore local names after upgrading again. This resolves the compatibility decision requested by Sweeper. ## Why This Change Was Made The registry owner now exclusively owns local-name changes and preserves the latest override during metadata upserts, including stale updates after a reset. It publishes successful renames only after saving. Sidebar, search, management, and discovery rows derive their labels from that owner. Discovered addresses are retained as last-known display metadata only, never as a connection fallback. Compared with live main `a67c5aac31375417320964c99bdcc5eefba6c056`, iOS has the same overwrite problem and no reusable rename implementation; macOS already separates profile name from endpoint identity. iOS is unchanged. Related open PRs were checked; no direct rename duplicate was found. ## Evidence **Verified head:** `7e6d19576537404865e6dc42fb25875d68118e4c` (independently based on main, not a stacked PR). - **15/15 focused tests passed on the review repair:** 7 real Settings UI tests and 8 registry tests. The accepted maintainer decision was directly verified against the authenticated Team source by a repository maintainer; [verification record](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159714#issuecomment-5857685657). The published [final Sweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159714#issuecomment-5857106047) is **Ready for maintainer review**, with no actionable findings, pending maintainer decision, or required next step. - **CI:** [final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36332873495) **passed** on `7e6d19576537404865e6dc42fb25875d68118e4c`: all Android variants, both native page-size lanes, lint, and required `openclaw/ci-gate` are green. **Merged via squash** as [`1ff9d2c4bc6c9d29a8b221dd11704c10838842d9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ff9d2c4bc6c9d29a8b221dd11704c10838842d9) from the verified head through the native repository workflow.
