title: fix(talk): honor ordinary permissions for voice requests
body:
Related: #153299

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes authenticated Talk requests receiving an extra spoken-confirmation barrier or a different execution context when equivalent text work is ordinarily permitted. Caller-bound replay keeps separate callers’ requests and authority separate.

## User Impact

Text and voice use the same ordinary tool/exec permissions: permitted work needs no extra voice prompt; ordinary approvals, denials, final command checks, cancellation, authenticated caller/device security and source revocation still apply.

**Requested behavior:** authenticated Talk requests use the same ordinary permissions as equivalent text requests, without a second voice-only confirmation gate. This intentionally changes the additional spoken-confirmation behavior documented in v2026.9.7 for fresh and upgraded installations; no opt-in or compatibility mode is added. This is the approved implementation scope. Merge and release review remain separate; no deployment or release is claimed.

**No merge, deployment, release, full-CI or system-service-upgrade claim.** Optional app capability #159695 and independent execution reporting #159693 are not core dependencies. Reporter shipping-floor/host-first versus coordinated rollout remains independent.

**Retained implementation status (2026-10-10, superseded by the October 11 integration above):** HEAD `71476c44abe094418375188baee2a715006e308f`, tree `047cf273106e7f90b4c7d0011ee2e4b4d6e8fa65`, integrates one fixed main revision `5a44564c988637008abbf1c868e127356dd868bd` and preserves published e000 ancestry. The obsolete voice-only confirmation remains deleted. All 368 affected tests passed (12 files); production core types, affected gateway/other/tooling/root/extension types, and changed formatting passed. The default type batch timed out at 600 seconds; full-core lint was killed with an OOM increment; targeted root lint passed but remaining lint timed out at 180 seconds. These are failures, not passes. Canonical build/package binds this exact HEAD. The official latest-stable updater and installed data-preservation/Talk proof now pass at this unchanged HEAD, as detailed below. Current-head CI completed; ClawSweeper R12 found no code correctness issue and requested this compatibility evidence. At this evidence publication, ordinary GitHub re-review remains pending. Main advancement alone does not invalidate the stated tested base. Local ClawSweeper review was skipped at the author's explicit direction. No readiness, merge or release is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Talk reuses authenticated caller preparation, admitted-run lifetime and ordinary execution policy instead of a second permission manager. Canonical chat owns request reservation, fingerprint conflicts and replay. Stable host-prepared caller/profile, verified device and session/call identity bind replay; mutable grants do not mint new intent. Current admission and control checks still apply after reconnect or permission changes.

Installed verification exposed and repaired two owning-path defects: node prechecks now consume the validated agent-scoped PREPARE policy snapshot instead of requiring the non-admin caller to read admin-only raw settings; every exported public consultation callback now retains its original authenticated source through the existing browser lifecycle owner. The raw RPC remains admin-only, snapshot-absent shipped-node compatibility remains conservative, and native current-policy/pre-spawn checks remain authoritative.

The current integration also fixes the committed review’s loading race: accepted work retains per-run authority **before** lazy runtime loading. Ordinary close/disconnect detaches that accepted work and rejects new callbacks; actual source revocation cancels the run and its approval. No timeout increase, principal swap, Full access shortcut, private-provider capability forgery or new authority store was used.

### Retained source integration history

- Candidate **2379099fa087544609f4969b0a2697f26576387b**, tree **412c966e83553bc9d0bf1ecf3c5db28b0d68cf47**.
- Integration commit `ba255ec114d31e7e51245d0fcfd821b7151741eb` retains published `61ec99c2a2e8b00dfd54873e7aeaf2fa60b517f8` and pinned main `0aee279a71af78b8914dced0507ddb94c0d1f5b0` as its two parents. Subsequent corrections adapt existing fixtures, release per-transport authority on replacement close, and preserve implicit legacy retries when their voice record regenerates. This preserves ancestry without a rebase/history rewrite.
- Ordinary main execution permissions, caller/source authority and approval enforcement remain the owners; the additional voice-only confirmation machinery is removed.
- Current-main mergeability is checked separately before publication. The tested pin is not relabeled as a newer comparator.

title: feat(nodes): launch exact Linux apps with ordinary approvals
body:
Related: #153299

## What Problem This Solves

Opening an installed Linux app should not require model-authored shell discovery or wait for a long-lived process to exit.

## User Impact

Adds optional Nodes actions `app_list` and `app_launch` for an inventory-provided app ID/revision on an exact paired Linux node. Text and voice use the same ordinary tool, **host and node** execution approvals; no additional Talk-only confirmation or standing policy is required. Success means **process started with an actual PID**, not process completed, window appeared or application initialized.

Installed-app sharing remains off by default. Launch also requires Linux duplex support, advertised/approved node commands and explicit Gateway command-policy opt-in. A previously stored true sharing setting on Linux now enables inventory and launch advertisement when otherwise supported; **published-driver upgrade behavior and maintainer acceptance of that existing-setting interpretation remain open**. Advertisement does not bypass pairing, command-policy or executable denials.

Eligible entries are bounded, top-level XDG desktop files resolving to one native ELF executable without arguments. Shell/script launchers, field codes, terminal/DBus activation, custom working directories, TryExec and visibility conditions are outside this narrow capability. Higher-precedence entries mask lower entries even when ineligible. Inventory reports completeness and truncation for this supported subset.

**Admission limit:** the invocation-bound permit is valid for at most five seconds from node readiness, including transport. The node rechecks revision, executable/cwd, local execution authority, expiry and observed cancellation before spawn. Delivered cancellation prevents spawn; cancellation still in transit can lose the race. A canceled tool request is not proof that no process started. This is not atomic distributed revocation.

**DRAFT:** product acceptance of core placement, the bounded admission contract and upgrade behavior remains separate. No merge, release, installed-package or full-CI readiness is claimed. The independent upstream voice-default decision in #159697 and reporter shipping-floor decision in #159693 are not resolved by this revision.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app adapter uses the existing ordinary node-exec preparation, HOST+NODE policy combination, approval record/request/decision/continuation and forwarding sanitizer. The node resolves the executable itself; its existing approval plan now includes an optional installed-app ID/revision binding. Wrong device, target, revision or generic-operation replay cannot consume an app approval. Native dispatch returns at process start; ordinary exec retains run-to-completion semantics.

Accepted app work follows the existing admitted run's lifetime through signed node transport. Final permit delivery and cancellation remain observable, invocation-owned operations—not a spoken grant or a new permission manager. The small path/coverage extraction retains generic exec behavior and keeps the existing line cap.

### Source and dependency

- Head: `b890cdd1fbe176cf2b8af68d325210a2f9ee1a3f`; tree: `5870b44798af0a6677ec890cd75515b94be333bc`.
- Actual parent/effective app-only base: [PR #159697](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159697), `openclaw/scoped-app-repeat-permission-pr3` at `98e8ba9615e577b32db473fd65d019511833b83b`.
- That dependency supplies the ordinary admitted caller/session/exec/reviewer/source context across text and Talk. App implementation consumes generic execution owners, not Talk-specific permission helpers. Generic parity works independently without these app actions.
- No reporter dependency, standing app policies, policy attribution, spoken-confirmation carrier or old mechanical exec-policy/system-which relocation is restored. PR1 is independent.
- History is append-only: previous published `fc3c91ad` remains an ancestor through the corrected parity branch. No force push, rebase or history replacement; the closed combined PR stays closed/unmerged.
- The new app binding is optional metadata in the existing approval plan/RPC record. No database schema/version, package/lock or public SDK surface changes are introduced. Installed-version compatibility is not inferred from source tests.

## Evidence

### Exact-head real behavior proof

**Claim:** the same exact app across registered text, direct Talk creation and chat-backed Talk gets the same ordinary permission decision and real native effect, without an extra voice prompt.

**Surface/environment:** one suite-owned Gateway, registered requester handlers with real admitted operator authority, an actual signed reviewer and paired NodeRuntime, real SQLite approval records, canonical Nodes/exec owners and native OS child processes. Requester ingress/model inference/external voice transport are controlled fixtures; this is not live microphone/provider or requester-wire authentication proof. Existing rootless network-none Linux source runner: Node 26.8.2, native pnpm 12.5.1, Vitest 5.0.1, Playwright 1.63.0, private frozen dependencies. No product/qaRuntime build, new image or infrastructure was used.

**Observed after the final commit:** one selected test containing **30 cells** passed; 12 unrelated tests intentionally filtered. Test body **20.224 s**, isolated wrapper **99.41 s**. There were **15 real approval requests, nine ordinarily successful native launches, and three further processes when cancellation was deliberately held in transit**. Repeated approval resolution produced no additional process. Thirty independent `nodes(which)` reads verified routing. The cancellation-in-transit rows are **not successful tool replies** or no-effect claims.

title: fix(talk): preserve source outcomes when native tool presentation fails
body:
Related: #153299

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes successful voice-originated tool effects being reported as blocked or failed when native middleware changes the presented result after execution.

## User Impact

Talk records the execution owner's actual outcome separately from presentation failures and optional diagnostics. This change does not grant execution permission or change ordinary approvals. Generic voice/text permission parity and optional Linux app launch do **not** depend on this reporter.

**Open compatibility finding:** released-host admission is not established for the reporter required by the updated Codex plugin. The previously inspected published 2026.9.6 host lacks it; the pinned main's newer plugin-API declaration is not evidence that this reporter shipped. A real coordinated rollout or host-first release/floor decision and published-driver acceptance proof remain necessary. Do not independently release the updated plugin against unsupported hosts. No release version or floor is invented here.

**DRAFT — no merge-readiness, deployment, full-product-build or full-CI claim.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Execution owners record source facts. Native adapters use an action reporter bound to the admitted run, plugin and tool. Live authority is required to bind or start work; an already accepted handle may record one terminal settlement after cancellation without retaining permission to execute. Diagnostics and model-facing presentation cannot overwrite those facts.

The normal merge preserves main's native participant authority, consolidated timing, extracted failure buffer and asynchronous quarantine cleanup. The touched side-tool composition was moved unchanged to its own module to meet the existing line cap. No permission manager, public free emitter, diagnostic fallback, schema change or cap increase is added.

### Source and dependency scope

- Independent reporting draft targeting `main`; not a prerequisite for the parity or app drafts.
- Head: `0f64900c67abb437cb088658eae49f6af9355f68`.
- Pinned main: `f59e97921315d14e6316598d889009b97710e67b`.
- Normal merge parents are retained head `6ff285da40af30dad5135b0edc6928e5717a742c` and that pin. Nine actual conflicts justified integration. History is preserved; no rebase or force push.

## Evidence

- **14/14 real-source composition scenarios passed on the exact final commit**, 34.18 s. Real filesystem/core-exec effects cross the production wrapper, native request controller/bridge and SQLite voice-effect/transcript owners. Successful effects remain successful after blocked, failed or throwing presentation; genuine denial/failure, cancellation, timeout and the baseline's confirmation lifecycle remain covered.
- **68/68 focused owner cases passed**, 75.59 s, covering host reporting/lifetimes, quarantine and native failure projection.
- Seven selected native cleanup cases passed, 54.21 s. Seven selected side-tool cases passed after extraction, 77.50 s; five overlap the earlier selection and are not additional unique cases.
- Five selected type projects passed. Affected extension types, lint and side-tool cases were refreshed after extraction. Scoped formatting, lint, line/assertion ratchets and SDK registration sync passed.
- **Inherited SDK budget failure remains explicit:** candidate and pinned-main source inputs both report **4,595 public exports against a 4,594 budget**, and **2,699 callable exports against 2,698**. SDK facades, inventories and caps are unchanged; this check is not claimed green.

Exact-commit composition command:

`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts test/client-voice-source-outcome.codex.integration.test.ts`

[Source composition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f64900c67abb437cb088658eae49f6af9355f68/test/client-voice-source-outcome.codex.integration.test.ts) · [Host custody](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f64900c67abb437cb088658eae49f6af9355f68/src/agents/harness/host-capability.execution-reporting.test.ts) · [Native reporting](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f64900c67abb437cb088658eae49f6af9355f68/extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-execution-reporting.test.ts)

One bounded merge/repair review invocation completed in 80.09 s, automatically partitioned into three chunks, with no new actionable P0–P2 findings in that scope. title: fix(sessions): resume the original conversation after restart recovery fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after automatic recovery fails during a Gateway restart, **Resume session** creates a replacement conversation and leaves the interrupted conversation behind.

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

An eligible interrupted conversation now continues in its original session. Explicit Resume clears the failed recovery state and keeps the same key, transcript, owner, workspace, and permissions. Automatic continuation after a cold restart revalidates the original requester's current authority before doing work.

### Root Cause

The old explicit recovery path built a successor and copied transcript state. A failed automatic recovery cycle retired the original conversation, so the visible Resume action could not continue it in place. The new path reclaims the old worker and uses the session mutation owner to clear failed execution state before a fresh continuation. The legacy successor builder and transcript-copy transaction are removed.

## User Impact

Users can resume an eligible failed session where they left off. Already-created historical successors stay linked; they are not merged back. Archived sessions still require restoration first. On Telegram, a user who sends to a tombstoned conversation gets one visible recovery notice with `/reset` or `/new` guidance. A model-locked session instead points to WebChat's **Resume session**.

**Open maintainer decisions:**

1. A sandbox-required operator currently cannot Resume an older unsandboxed session without a provenance stamp. Main can instead create a sandboxed successor. VAC must decide whether to retain an authorized compatibility route or accept this upgrade break. This PR does not assume either answer.
2. The private SQLite recovery envelope now retains the original requester's rights across restarts. It is revalidated before use and does not itself grant live authority. VAC must accept or revise this permission-lifetime contract. There is no schema-version bump; published-driver/storage compatibility proof is linked below.

## Why This Change Was Made

A failed automatic retry should stop replay, while preserving the conversation for an authorized manual continuation. This keeps session identity and transcript ownership with the original session and prevents a stale requester record from bypassing current role or policy checks.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- [Cold-process source proof on the composed recovery code](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36424074671): allowed case made exactly one real exec file effect in the original session after restart, without reconnect or new input (198.730 s); revoked requester made zero post-restart model calls and no file effect (182.273 s). Both passed. The same run passed 7/7 browser recovery cases. This proof is tied to its recorded candidate tree, not relabeled as execution of today's merge head.
- **Published v2026.9.6 storage and rollback proof (earlier isolated run):** the released writer created two original sessions; this candidate reopened them and stored requester custody in both custody-only and active-cycle envelopes. The released schema-18 per-agent reader/writer retained both private envelopes through a metadata write, and the candidate reopened them exactly. A whole-state downgrade correctly refused the newer shared schema 19; the installed released CLI refused too. The released `backup create --verify` → `backup restore` path reopened the pre-update backup with both original session IDs. These earlier checks cover payload compatibility and the existing rollback boundary, not authority after this merge.
- **Telegram Test Server, exact head `8972a74ab01ffd4087a160956f874b6fddb2c53c`:** `node .agents/skills/telegram-e2e-userbot/scripts/run-mock-sut-user-e2e.mjs --dm --scenario <isolated-fixture> --record <private-events> --output <private-summary>` ran with a Convex-leased QA user and bot, Node 24.19.0, an isolated Gateway built from this exact head, and a deterministic mock provider. The first DM at 0.106 s got `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK` at 4.049 s. An isolated session-store fixture set a failed-recovery tombstone through the session accessor (completed at 24.787 s); the runner restarted only its own Gateway (completed at 33.243 s). The next DM at 33.409 s produced exactly one native TDLib SUT message at 35.538 s: `My session in this room ended during restart recovery. Use /reset or /new to start a replacement session.` A second DM at 38.239 s got no duplicate notice through the completed 70 s recording. The run reported `completed: true`, `mockRequests: 3`, both control actions completed, and removed its credential scratch. No runner-owned listener remained. This proves native Telegram delivery and one-notice behavior from a seeded failed state; it does not claim to induce the whole automatic failure lifecycle through Telegram.
- Before and after Control UI screenshots were inspected and both GitHub image links returned HTTP 200 PNG: [before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f16aa024-8010-44dc-85cf-57faab670ff9), [after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3fd67640-b12e-488b-9762-9dc953fe2895).

### Verification

- GitHub reported an actual `mergeable=DIRTY` conflict. The requested **single** `git merge origin/main` integrated `4902e4ae49a669702b92a1df3aeb01b167ec6715`; merge commit `8972a74ab01ffd4087a160956f874b6fddb2c53c`. **Only conflicted file:** `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts`. Resolution kept this PR's self-send runtime identity and main's extracted in-process session creation. Earlier merge `1b919d5ee2ec6abe413a4d6c148370d308a4b709` already included [09bea762930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/09bea762930f9876acb86103a93dc15c4eb648c5), the one-category fix. No more main integration was done.
- On the merged candidate, recovery, requester restoration, session-send, and Telegram notice tests passed **75/75** across four Vitest shards (192.60 s). The inherited `voice-call` runtime API guardrail passed **7/7** after main's owner fix. `pnpm build` passed on the merge head (8m 12.7 s); `dist/build-info.json` matched that commit.
- [Exact PR-head CI run `36449933512`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512) was **red** on `8972a74ab01ffd4087a160956f874b6fddb2c53c`. The PR-caused failures were fixed on the branch after that run: [changed-node small 13](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022751580) expected a successor after `sessions.recover`; the test now checks the original session, 3/3 locally (26.75 s runner wall). Five `gateway-policy-changed` jobs ([small 5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022751151), [small 13](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022751580), [large 15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022751753), [small 19](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022751838), [large 27](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022751903)) saw 4001 disconnects because this PR had bound auth mode into every live client's global policy fingerprint. The fix binds mode to restart requester custody at original WS admission, carries it through the agent-turn principal, and checks it at snapshot/restore. The focused owner isolation test failed 2/12 before this correction and passed 12/12 after; the combined focused tests passed **46/46** across four files (122.01 s runner wall). The real isolated cold-restart self-continuation test then passed **2/2** on the final source: allowed made exactly one file effect in the original session; revoked made none (253.26 s Vitest duration). This is real local proof, not a claim that final-head CI ran.
- P2 AutoReview found an opaque plugin grant ID bug in the merged candidate. A valid `grant-42` failed 1/11 before the bounded identifier fix, then passed 11/11 (44.94 s runner wall). Later P2 AutoReview found the auth-mode capture boundary issue; it is fixed above. Final P2 AutoReview on the last three-file patch found no actionable findings. `git diff --check` passed. The additional cold E2E is release-tier; no new per-PR CI test was added.

**Other red jobs on the `8972` run; no unrelated tests changed here:**

| Job | Failing test/check | Attribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [check-source-contracts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022742301) | Exported-name collisions involving `src/cli/daemon-cli.ts` and `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts` | Inputs are byte-identical to pinned main; a current-main/other-PR CI comparison was not captured. |
| [checks-node-compact-small-12](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022751644) | `test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.integration.test.ts` timed out at 120 s | Test and owner script unchanged vs pinned main; not confirmed on a current-main/other-PR run. |
| [checks-ui-e2e (1/9)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022741995) | `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.models-reasoning.e2e.test.ts > does not reuse catalog reasoning for a different session runtime` timed out waiting for hidden thinking slider | Test and model reasoning surface unchanged vs pinned main; not confirmed on a current-main/other-PR run. |
| [checks-node-changed-12](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449933512/job/109022761234) | `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-agent-artifact-apis.e2e.test.ts > composes agent, environment, and artifact RPCs over one real Gateway` expected `Promise` true | Test and artifact API surface unchanged vs pinned main; not confirmed on a current-main/other-PR run. |

The aggregate CI gate failure is a consequence of these jobs, not a separate defect. [Earlier run `36445019539`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36445019539) was cancelled after an inherited `voice-call` guardrail failure; the main integration fixed that owner test.

### Current state and remaining limits

Maintainer @VACInc [closed this PR unmerged](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159688#issuecomment-5874148286) on September 28 pending the two design decisions above. The remote branch has the repair at `ea93dee2e448c7b4bc1c2fedd18ab16ca0ff44a1`, but GitHub's **closed PR still pins `8972a74ab01ffd4087a160956f874b6fddb2c53c`**. Thus final-branch exact-head PR CI has not run and is not green. ClawSweeper's last durable review was on older revision 30 and blocked on the maintainer decisions; a `8972` review started before closure without a newer durable result. A new `@clawsweeper re-review` request was withheld because the maintainer closed this PR. No merge, draft-state change, live Gateway change, or deployment occurred. Telegram proof seeded a failed tombstone in isolated state; it did not induce full failure exhaustion through Telegram. The cold-process test covers automatic authority and final effect on final source.

## Visual change

### Before

![Before: recovery requires a replacement session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f16aa024-8010-44dc-85cf-57faab670ff9)

### After

![After: recovery resumes the original session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3fd67640-b12e-488b-9762-9dc953fe2895)

Requested by @VACInc. Original branch authored by @roboclaw-bot. PR is closed and unmerged by maintainer decision.

title: fix(ci): expose bounded Docker survivor failure metadata
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing actionable Docker failure metadata in GitHub check annotations when the full logs and diagnostic artifacts cannot be retrieved. This affects the current main reporting owners, not just a frozen release. Maintainer-requested investigation following Package Acceptance run 36301761888. Related: #159617.

## User Impact

No installed runtime behavior changes. Maintainers can see the upgrade-survivor failure phase, exit status and signal, plus the scheduler status and timeout flags, through ordinary check annotations. This does not diagnose or repair the underlying upgrade failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing host-side diagnostics publisher and scheduler process owner. After safe artifact publication, send only the three validated failure coordinates through a bounded private host pipe. The scheduler drains that pipe and emits the annotation only after process-group and log cleanup, independently of its configured log tail. The pipe is not forwarded into the candidate container. Standalone host CLI calls retain escaped annotation output; direct publisher calls remain annotation-free. Reject oversized, duplicate, malformed or extra-field metadata. No logs, commands, paths, environment, configuration, or artifact contents are added to annotations.

No new reporting system, access route, workflow permission, artifact schema, retry, timeout, cleanup, pass/fail decision, or release/tooling selection changes. Existing sanitized artifacts remain authoritative detailed evidence.

## Evidence

- Current-main source/history review found no existing annotation bridge. The landed diagnostics improvement 45061103986 retains no-op output in the existing artifact; it does not surface phase metadata in check annotations.
- Accepted ClawSweeper P2 at 2824714: cleanup displaced the phase annotation from a supported one-line failure tail. Actual scheduler `runShellCommand` + process-group/log join + `tailFile(..., 1)` red/green proof reproduced zero phase annotations on that head and one after the repair. Both retain exit 7 and complete the cleanup trap. Wall time: 213 ms. Only the redactor dependency was stubbed; scheduler/process cleanup code was not extracted or mocked. This is a bounded diagnostic proof, not installed-package acceptance.
- Actual scheduler privacy negatives passed: extra fields, >1024 bytes, multiple receipts, and injected phase are discarded; ordinary stdout JSON is never promoted. The regression also exercises the real aggregate scheduler entrypoint with `OPENCLAW_DOCKER_ALL_FAILURE_TAIL_LINES=1`, unchanged failure status and joined cleanup; full hosted execution remains required.
- Direct final publisher proof passed metadata-only projection, redaction, no direct CI emission, malformed snapshot rejection, failed publication rejection, and successful-publication sibling.
- Node syntax checks, installed oxfmt, syntax lint, and git diff --check passed.
- Reproduced a concrete changed-lint defect from 2824714: `typescript/consistent-return` on `publishDiagnostics` (bare success return versus metadata failure return). Making the successful return explicitly `undefined` preserves its value and eliminates that diagnostic. The first local attempt still lacked Node type definitions; later configured proof reproduced the additional boolean-comparison errors described below. No suppression or lint-rule change.
- Stored-model checklist is heuristic: no schema, artifact format, migration or backfill changes. Compared original main 9ca49c5 against the repair on identical fixtures: `failure.json` is byte-identical (6369 bytes, SHA-256 `16cca7dd7dcafd63d6c8c928eb3bf66813cfac0c0f8168ea4e1d678a94fa9f32`); successful `summary.json` is also byte-identical (1586 bytes, SHA-256 `81aca5d0c0e0bbb42d9a4bc2bb6ac50d519b5a5cf69a6f5205a0fb10341b9ce1`). Regression compares host-CLI artifact bytes with ordinary publication, not an invented migration.
- Regressions cover safe projection, host CLI emission without changing exit status, and existing real scheduler failure/timeout cases without changing their retry or cleanup assertions. No new timers or polling. The diagnostics file executed within the 17.80s three-file attempt; separate full-file wall time was not recorded, and harness/scheduler did not execute. Hosted per-file timing is unavailable; do not equate whole-job seconds with per-file cost.
- Local full focused Vitest was subsequently attempted using a task-owned copy of provisioned dependencies (not frozen-install parity). Diagnostics: 42 passed. Harness and scheduler: failed before execution because canonical compiled-worker preparation could not resolve declared package imports. Complete three-file run 17.80s (outer wrapper 19.34s), not a full pass. No shared installed package was edited, no integrity or compilation guard bypassed, and no repeated installer attempted. Hosted exact-head full tests remain required.
- Initial standalone review was unavailable. ClawSweeper subsequently supplied the accepted tail-clipping P2; this revision fixes it and reopens independent review. Fresh exact-head review and required CI remain mandatory; no clean-review or landing claim.

Parent maintainer retains all review, landing and release-dispatch decisions.

### Follow-up type-aware lint correction

The corrected 1863049 head had two reproducible `typescript/no-unnecessary-boolean-literal-compare` errors in the scheduler annotation: both fields are already typed booleans. Use them directly; output and failure semantics are unchanged. Parent took over the stalled continuation after verifying all owned tests ended and preserving the exact one-line patch. Configured script-group type-aware lint passed with zero warnings/errors in 19.4s, and the three changed test files passed in 14.2s using the existing scripts tsconfig. A separately misselected nonexistent test-tsconfig invocation reached unrelated borrowed-dependency boundary errors; it is not counted as proof. No rule changes, suppressions, type widening or timeout increases.

## Required per-file test-cost record (September 27)

Measured the unchanged exact head `218c2fecdf5429d0cbbf64bb299ef73a4ed1287b` with the repository wrapper, one file per invocation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --maxWorkers=1` (supported equivalent of the pnpm test entrypoint). External wall time includes wrapper/compile/cleanup.

| File under `test/scripts/` | Single-worker wall | Actual result |
|---|---:|---|
| `upgrade-survivor-migration-diagnostics.test.ts` | 5.40 s | 42 passed, exit 0 |
| `docker-all-harness.test.ts` | 64.56 s | 66 passed, exit 0 |
| `docker-all-scheduler.test.ts` | 16.71 s | 49 passed, exit 0 |

The harness file exceeds 30 seconds because its existing owner-level suite proves real process-group custody, signal/exit ordering, joined log publication, and trusted harness/source separation; pure mocks cannot prove OS descriptor and descendant cleanup. The added clipped-tail aggregate case takes **951 ms** and uses the existing fixture/scheduler path. The four new privacy-negative scheduler cases take **65/66/62/61 ms**. No timer, polling delay, timeout inflation, serial config, or permanent worker pin was introduced.

Available exact-head hosted CI: run **36323902839 SUCCESS**, 36 jobs passed and 23 skipped. Changed-test job **108633670859**: **202 s whole job**, including setup; its actual `Run Node test shard` step was **144 s**. Hosted per-file seconds are not available from accessible evidence and are not fabricated or apportioned. Lint/test-types/changed-boundary whole jobs were **121/134/139 s**, respectively; artifact build also passed.

These local timing measurements supersede the earlier two-suite import blockage, not the frozen hosted proof: restored only absent task-local package dependency directories through the repository helper; no source or shared installed-package bytes changed. Local Node26.8.2/Vitest5.0.1 and donor typebox1.3.33 versus declared1.3.34 / QuickJS3.6.0 versus3.6.1 are disclosed timing-environment differences. Exact frozen dependencies are qualified by successful hosted CI.

Compatibility: no stored schema, migration, backfill, or artifact-format change. Existing original/repaired `failure.json` (6369 bytes) and `summary.json` (1586 bytes) are byte-identical with hashes above. The 1024-byte host pipe is ephemeral and carries only validated coordinates; it is not persisted as a new data model. This addresses the heuristic compatibility checkbox without inventing a migration.

title: fix(test): backport bundled MCP aggregate deadline
body:
Related: #157754 and #155931

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the release/2026.9.7 bundled MCP package test rejecting a completed Windows package/offline-install proof at its stale 60-second outer deadline.

## User Impact

No product-runtime or dependency change. The real npm/pnpm pack, offline consumer install, complete patched-runtime byte comparison, CLI version assertion, and cleanup remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backports the already-landed main repair `67e17e56c331acaebe39182cc10d4144da201312` (#157754), retaining this release’s patched MCP 1.8.0. The earlier #155931 backport gave subprocesses 180 seconds but left the enclosing synchronous test at 60 seconds. This reuses the unchanged child limit and the existing main 240-second aggregate budget; negative cases and shared fixture pack limits do not change.

Causal diagnosis: Vitest 5.0.0 calls the synchronous body before checking `deadline.exceeded()`. A failed child or payload assertion throws through its error branch instead. `withTarball` removes the fixture in `finally` before the body returns. Consequently the reported outer timeout occurs after the real process/assertion/cleanup chain completes, rather than identifying a hung child. Per-phase Windows durations are unavailable; we do not infer which phase was slow.

## Evidence

- Exact failure: CI run `36312209616`, Windows job `108600435583` (`checks-windows-node-test-2`), source `eb63221064a3a9166f9cfd3bae0159bbde25864c`, harness `aad795bf312accc62015b533238d06c95f50c6a4`. Annotation identifies the npm package/offline-install case at line 92 with a 60000 ms timeout. Detailed logs/artifacts are access-blocked; no bypass attempted.
- Current release base `3353972ebd418ca3fc1cc86e248edba8bcb4f9ee` differs from that failed source only in unrelated Windows recovery tests. Its MCP fixture, checker and dependency contract retain the failing deadline.
- Main already contains this exact repair. Its hosted Windows job `107981071953` in CI run `36106731010` succeeded; that is historical evidence for the original fix, not proof for this backport head. The original PR records 18/18 package cases and a preceding successful body rejected at 63.455 seconds.
- Local real-entrypoint attempt on Linux Node 26.8.2 / Vitest 5.0.1 stops at a host tool mismatch: the native pnpm selected outside the repository rejects `--package-import-method=copy`. No flag removal, mock, skip, or retry was used to manufacture a pass. The available normal dependency donor also has MCP 1.9.0 rather than this release’s 1.8.0; local proof is not claimed.
- `check:changed --dry-run` cannot plan with that donor: `ts.getParsedCommandLineOfConfigFile is not a function`. No shared dependency installation was changed.
- Targeted oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. Production delta: 0; tests: +9/-5. Current-head hosted Windows proof and ClawSweeper review are pending.

- Parent verified main PR #157754 merged at 67e17e56c331acaebe39182cc10d4144da201312 and independently read its successful historical Windows job. This is an adapted-context backport: it preserves release MCP1.8.0 rather than taking main1.9.0; the added constants and timeout substitutions are the same. Vincent Koc’s source credit is retained.
- The attempted standalone review hit its30-minute overall timeout without a report; no clean local review is claimed and it will not be blindly repeated. Parent inspected the complete diff and original main proof. Fresh release-head hosted Windows CI and ClawSweeper review are required before landing.

title: fix: show idle people accurately while they stay online
body:
Closes #159423

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: connected people look active even when their last interaction is old or unavailable.

## User Impact

Online remains connection status; people now show **Active** for recent interaction, **Idle** after two minutes, or plain **Online** when activity is unavailable. A fresh foreground web visit counts as activity; automatic reconnects, background traffic, and incoming agent output do not. Sidebar rows, person cards, and the Activity page use the same rules.

This is recent OpenClaw use, not physical presence or attention. Reading without interacting can become idle. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the Gateway's authenticated person timing and cross-tab aggregation. The small `presence.activity` request accepts no identity, timestamp, or input contents; the server records accepted interaction time. The web client reports trusted visible input with a 30-second throttle. A shared UI expiry controller updates idle status without network events and handles hidden pages, remounts, and expiry during rendering.

title: fix(ui): stop images reloading while scrolling
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: already-viewed chat screenshots flash a loading placeholder and can download again when scrolling back to a virtualized message.

## User Impact

User impact: recently viewed local screenshots and generated previews return immediately while unseen images still lazy-load. Retention is bounded and remains scoped to the current connection, credentials, session, agent, policy, and valid media ticket. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the decoded native image within the existing metadata resource cache rather than rebuilding it on every row remount. Managed previews consult their existing blob cache before viewport admission. Native nodes transfer exclusively, release their old listeners and parent, and rebind to the new row. This is a rendering-lifecycle fix, not a layout or styling change.

## Evidence

**Access-withdrawal follow-up:** role reassignment already closes the reader connection (`users.setRole` → policy close 4001), and role-definition changes already invalidate the media policy epoch. The missing case was the redacted `sessions.changed` sharing event: it now invalidates the same preview-admission owner before roster refresh. This preserves cached pixels only while the client has not received authority invalidation; it does not claim to retract bytes already delivered or synchronously update an offline browser.

- Expanded real Chromium app proof covers normal scrolling, session visibility/sharing withdrawal, role reassignment, and role-definition withdrawal. The sharing case fails before the follow-up; all four pass afterward (17.02s suite; 3.43–4.28s per case). After withdrawal, a MutationObserver confirms **no transient cached image insertion**, the final UI is unavailable, and the image-byte request count stays at the original one. Gateway WebSocket/HTTP responses are deterministic fixture inputs to the actual Control UI.
- Actual Gateway policy tests pass for a named reader’s saved media ticket after visibility, role-assignment, and role-definition withdrawal. The `users.setRole` producer test also confirms policy invalidation and client disconnection before its response: 4 focused cases pass. An initial harness run overlapped isolated-fixture cleanup and was refused by the compiler input snapshot; the serialized replay passed.
- Follow-up UI and E2E typechecks, code/style lint, formatting, and a fresh independent P0–P2 review pass.

- The new immediate-remount regressions fail on the original implementation and pass with this fix.
- 336 focused tests across six files pass, including scope/ticket invalidation, native reconnect without a host render, optimistic-upload handoff, galleries, and existing media lifecycle behavior. Final combined run: 5.88s Vitest / 6.69s wrapper wall; the changed admission file’s 17 cases each complete in 1–4ms.
- Real Chromium, actual Control UI source-mode app and an 80-message virtualized transcript: the image row detaches and remounts with no loading frame, one metadata request, and exactly one image-byte request despite `Cache-Control: no-cache`. Browser scenario: 4.26s; suite: 5.74s.
- UI and core-test typechecks, targeted code/style lint, tooling lint, formatting, assertion/size guards, and dead-export scans pass. The final listener adjustment was rerun through all 336 tests, the browser scenario, UI/chat-test typechecks, and lint.

title: fix(update): complete native restarts after executor delegation
body:
Related: #159385

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native restart finalization failing with “The update process is still running” after an otherwise successful update on the 2026.9.7 candidate.

## User Impact

Legacy finalizers can complete the real native restart and publish their terminal result. Current authority, receiver binding, child extinction, deadlines, snapshots, and rollback attempted-start protections remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a two-file incremental correction stacked on integration head 3c5ec84cd7bb5edd07580960879e97aa1dd7b5cf, not a duplicate of its backports. Backport c3c20e0241b placed the parent mutation-fence assertion inside the delegated child callback. The child owner deliberately suspends that fence until its process joins, so the assertion rejects before native activation. Check the parent immediately before delegation instead; the child owner still revalidates current authority before running and binding its receiver.

Current main 168ebc5b67080909f825858d16308a94278c5342 does not contain the erroneous inner assertion. This is release-only.

## Evidence

- Isolated exact-base reproduction: both grantless-scratch-owned-parent-pnpm-root-move and grantless-scratch-owned-parent-git-root-switch failed with executor-settlement errors and no result.json. Both pass with the ordering correction (2/2; 25.24 seconds including native worker preparation).
- Existing real native custody scenarios now assert that the parent mutation fence remains suspended when the attempted-start callback fires, and that the callback is observed once before successful activation. No new process fixtures or timeout changes.
- All four related files passed: 65/65 tests across native custody (19), legacy finalization (27), service command (9), and source replacement (10). Total wrapper wall time 143.80 seconds. Existing custody file: 59.63 seconds including worker preparation; the patch adds assertions only, no new native processes. Full wrong-handoff/run/root/version/scratch/parent and revoked/retargeted refusals remain green.
- Standalone P0–P2 autoreview produced no report after 10 minutes and was stopped at the explicitly requested bound. Review is incomplete, not clean; this causally proven patch is published for actual hosted review/CI rather than prolonging the stalled reviewer.
- Both exact legacy cases also pass with pinned Vitest 5.0.0 using a read-only diagnostic resolver (2/2; 28.34 seconds wrapper wall time); no shared package files were edited.
- Scoped formatting and type-aware lint passed (0 warnings/errors); git diff --check passed. Full core typecheck could not start because the borrowed installed tree lacks the target typescript-native/package.json alias; this is an unrun gate, not a passing typecheck.
- Local diagnostic runtime is Node 26.8.2 / Vitest 5.0.1, using the pinned TypeScript 6.0.3 read-only diagnostic resolver and repository test wrappers. A Node 24.19.0 checksum download was refused with HTTP 403; no proxy or supply-chain controls were bypassed. title: fix(plugins): reclaim registry memory after catalog scope changes
body:
Related: #157842

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: native ESM registrations can retain complete retired catalog/plugin registry graphs through their disposed plugin instances.

## User Impact

Successful physical disposal releases the old registry graph while preserving stale-call rejection, admitted cleanup custody, and tool-result delivery when a middleware plugin is removed. No configuration, credentials, stored data, retention policy, heap limits, or worker-recycling settings change. No migration is needed.

This is one additional retaining-edge repair, not a claim that every 2026.9.6 memory-growth report is resolved. Native ESM graphs can remain until worker retirement. Active work and failed/incomplete cleanup still retain their required resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

A module-scoped, identity-sensitive registration keeps its exact PluginInstance alive. After successful cleanup, that instance no longer needs to hold the entire registry and its inspection/prepared resources. Release that reference at the existing physical terminal boundary, retaining the exact revoked value identity. Removed-middleware recovery follows a weak reference to the exact admitting Gateway, never another process-active Gateway.

The interrupted merge is preserved, then composed with main `42ebb9d73483b2d0d55178709b960af363cdd07d`. Main’s known-provider seeding, native payload plateau checks, borrowed registrations, Gateway view identity, reload drain scopes, and by-reference plugin results remain intact. The existing Gateway-owner type is in a leaf contract to avoid the static type-import cycle found by earlier hosted CI.

Composition exposed a second, bounded defect: once a lender releases its registry, a borrower’s authority lookup fell back to itself and recursively overflowed. Borrowers now follow only their existing, non-revoked lender. The regression verifies live authority first, then invalidation and denied reacquisition after disposal.

The catalog-seeding closure repair in #158986 and disposal-classifier closure repair in #160213 address different edges and are preserved.

## Evidence

- Historical pinned main `53cd9aa4aa35b35c22aefd2b373d99d09547812a`: real parent publication/`loadFullModelCatalog` regression retained **4 registries before, 1 after**, while all 4 native exports remained alive. This is historical proof, not today’s-head CI.
- With main’s known-provider seeding, the same real worker path creates **2** captures. The retained-merge negative control, disabling only successful registry release, retains **2 registries**; the repair retains **1**, with both native exports still alive and a weak control object collected. Warm provider scopes plateau, requested hooks stay narrow, per-agent synthetic credentials remain distinct, and the active 100,000-row/1 MiB payload stays usable.
- Current-main composition `5cde374b804e6751cad10c2c4fa1a51eba6a8f7f`: **180 tests / 9 files passed** in 74.97s. The real worker retained 1/2 registries, both native exports survived, and heap/external/ArrayBuffer metrics were recorded separately. These are bounded test observations, not a production RSS claim.
- The added borrower regression fails with **Maximum call stack size exceeded** before its focused repair. Borrower/lender, channel borrowing, physical cleanup, and authority regressions pass afterward. A fresh scoped P2 AutoReview found no actionable findings.
- Verified candidate `c4a6b78c21fb67f8e6150ff00635a8e3c0b13293` and tree-identical broker publication `c5f18987224b8f2dbbda5d5ab9389930c9c0ec34`, tree `4f5973a1df81497cf01de91f1119a70a0f0fa191`: [configured Blacksmith Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37241214017), Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.5.1, passed full `pnpm build` (490.5s), **30 tests in 8 files** (100.02s), **5** real-loader middleware removal/replacement/Gateway-identity cases (22.50s), and **1** wrapper-inventory test (3.99s). The filtered suites deliberately excluded unrelated cases. Canonical package integrity passed.
- The **published 2026.9.6 → candidate custom-plugin-siblings** Docker lane passed (296s), covering the original updater, private plugin Doctor/canary execution, preserved plugin sources/configuration, candidate runtime inspection, and candidate Gateway start/probes/stop. These are mandatory scenario assertions; individual nested JSON artifacts were not separately retrieved before automatic cleanup. The inner wrapper command settled successfully with exit 0; the Testbox was independently confirmed `completed`. A backing workflow cancellation during one-shot cleanup is not claimed as a green Actions conclusion.
- Local core and all 27 core-test type lanes, changed-file lint, static/runtime import-cycle checks, architecture/Kysely guards, formatting, line/safety ratchets, plugin boundaries, dead-export scans, schema/storage/sidecar and webhook/auth guards passed across the scoped runs. An early check invocation stopped on an oversized unfinished-merge comparison; a later run was intentionally stopped for the reproduced borrower repair. Those invocations are not counted as passing; their affected and remaining stages were verified directly afterward.

**Update behavior:** the published 2026.9.6 package updater starts candidate post-core finalization in a fresh process, even for same-version package updates (published `update-command-post-core.ts`). Old CLI cleanup can still retain process-global lifecycle state, but existing instances retain their original disposal methods; candidate success removes its instance from birth caches before clearing registry custody. No live Gateway, reporter installation, or production configuration was changed. Build/package proof uses the configured Blacksmith Testbox; hosted CI, security, and fresh review remain enforced by the native landing workflow.

No production behavior changes. The release test again protects finalizing the existing preview only after Telegram's retry-after deadline, without sending an extra answer or weakening backoff. All five golden files and their full assertions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Release backport f488a8cdfd6 moved flood-wait ownership from the draft stream to the per-token account limiter. Production bot-core installs that limiter on the grammY API. The older trace fixture supplied a hand-made API object and bypassed the new owner entirely.

Use a real grammY API with a recording synthetic fetch and the existing account flood transformer. Only ordinary scheduler pacing uses the existing test injection seam; the real flood gate and final retry policy execute. Reset token-scoped state per scenario and continue rejecting unexpected transport methods. No golden refresh, assertion relaxation, dependency edit, or timeout change.

This is release-only: main intentionally removed this trace fixture and its goldens in de5e31b8958 (#155040). Do not restore retired main coverage or alter production backoff to accommodate an obsolete fixture boundary.

## Evidence

- Diagnosed on c6770887, then rebased the identical one-file patch onto release base 7044fb5 so the PR does not include the parent dependency repair.
- Original exact c6770887 diagnostic: 4/5 trace tests pass; rate-limit case fails because the final edit occurs at 1700 ms rather than 2400 ms after a 1400 ms response with retry_after=1.
- Repaired same-runtime trace: 5/5 pass against unchanged goldens, retaining idle at 1700 ms and final edit at 2400 ms. Trace test time 163 ms; Vitest duration 19.34 s; wrapper wall 21.31 s including worker preparation and verified cleanup.
- Trace plus account-throttler siblings: 22/22 pass, including token-wide backoff, skipped previews, final recovery, cancellation, and overlapping deadlines. Wrapper wall 22.56 s.
- Exact mapped changed-extensions-config-105 selection (10 files): 125/125 pass after repair, versus the original diagnostic 124 passed / 1 failed. Wrapper wall 59.81 s. This remains the diagnostic runtime, not a claim that the entire hosted bundle is repaired.
- Independent standalone autoreview was attempted with the scoped patch and causal context; the reviewer timed out after 600 seconds (engine exit 124) without a verdict. This is not a clean review. No Claude fallback CLI is installed. Current-head hosted ClawSweeper review remains mandatory.
- Formatting and git diff --check pass. Focused lint wrapper is blocked before lint by unavailable typescript-native/package.json in the borrowed diagnostic dependency set.
- Local evidence uses Node 26.8.2 / Vitest 5.0.1 and a process-local cached TypeScript 6 resolver with read-only borrowed dependencies. The installed grammY 1.46.0 and transformer-throttler 1.2.1 match the candidate package pins. It is **not** target Node 24 / Vitest 5.0.0 parity, hosted CI proof, or live Telegram proof. No network requests or real channel messages were sent.

Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review remain required before landing. Parent maintainer owns shepherding and landing; this PR does not resolve the other unexplained release runtime failures.

title: fix(cron): named-session jobs run in the wrong workspace
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes named-session scheduled jobs using the agent’s default workspace instead of their conversation’s saved working directory or managed worktree.

## User Impact

Named-session automation can use its conversation’s project files without moving them or relaxing filesystem containment and job tool restrictions. **Requester-scoped jobs may use a saved workspace only for their owning conversation; trusted operator-scheduled jobs retain broader targeting.** New unbound custom sessions still start in the configured agent workspace; current and isolated runs remain detached.

**Intentional upgrade behavior:** a missing, retired, or mismatched saved worktree stops the job rather than silently running in another directory. Fail-closed behavior was part of the requester’s explicit repair requirements; operators must repair the binding/worktree before retrying. No configuration or stored-data migration is required.

**Maintainer disposition (RoboClaw, under the existing repair-and-land authorization): accepted.** A stale binding must not silently grant a different filesystem root. Recovery is to restore the session’s worktree through its normal worktree controls, or create a valid worktree-bound session and recreate the job from that conversation. Do not remove containment restrictions to make a stopped job run. This decision does not waive enforced CI or review requirements.

This PR does not deploy a Gateway, change live jobs, or re-enable automation. Deployment of the repaired runtime remains separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing persisted-workspace and lifecycle owners, hold the managed-worktree lease through execution and cleanup, and forward the selected workspace/cwd consistently to embedded and CLI runners. Persistent rollover keeps its binding and saved restrictions; detached runs do not inherit them. No prompt path grants authority and no competing database-polling mechanism was added.

The security finding on the original published head was real: an account-scoped job could select a different same-agent conversation’s directory. The correction checks the scheduler’s host-authored principal classification and authenticated job owner before selecting that saved root. It preserves the existing own-conversation resource boundary rather than adding a new permissions system.

## Evidence

- **Latest repair `4d0da578123a9a1c8da50708bf4d3d3a610ccccf`:** addresses the reviewed registry-owner gap with **two production conditions**, using the existing async registry read and lease: the record must be session-owned and its owner must equal the selected session key. This matches session worktree preparation, dispatch, and sandbox projection. Inherited cwd-only and Workboard cwd selections remain unchanged.
- **Latest runtime proof: 3,018 cron tests passed across 254 files.** The authority file now has **7 passing cases**, including real Git worktrees, actual registry rows and actual run leases. Before the two-condition repair, both a foreign-session owner and a manual owner produced a real sentinel file read; afterward both reject before file I/O. The correctly owned control reads successfully with its real lease held, then releases it. These are deliberately mismatched persisted bindings—not a claim that ordinary registry updates support owner reassignment.
- **Latest static/review proof:** core types, affected cron test types, typed lint, formatting, dead exports, import cycles, and the remaining selected guards passed. Fresh independent AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 defect. The broad check runner encountered the untouched inherited gateway fixture error described below; it is not reported as passing.
- **Previous candidate `81f3370d4373b57e7ee9dc4c4318825c87a0afb0`:** reconciles main’s test consolidation (`a57426fa03e99`, #160480) on base `01747d9b2b11f3d96c834423257996641d4c1d93`. Upstream test structure and assertions are retained; four fixture calls now use their exact persistent target keys. **82 focused tests across five files passed**, including authority/file I/O, workspace/rollover, and both conflicted suites. Current cron test types, changed typed lint, line-cap and diff checks pass; fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defect. All seven production files are byte-identical to the previously verified `90d0e21d6f521` candidate. A read-only merge-tree with main `47646aa21b9a6e18437c31fa225d057dfeb090ef` was conflict-free; no additional rebase was performed just because main advanced.
- **Earlier integration:** `90d0e21d6f521f16af08893f629bb84d3722778d` rebases the repair onto main `7e6dd89766ce57499b38962882d12f0caaefb165` to resolve an actual GitHub merge conflict. The only manual resolution combines the upstream `current`-session explanation with the custom-session paragraph; range-diff confirms no production/test patch changes. **All 3,136 cron tests across 263 files and 59 current lifecycle/worktree-lease tests passed** after frozen dependency reconciliation. Fresh core types, the current owner-selected cron test-type graph, changed typed lint (zero warnings/errors), MDX, and diff checks also pass. The inventory difference reflects main’s independent test changes, not dropped coverage in this PR.
- **Earlier verified head `dc3989dd8c6e`: 3,353 cron tests passed across all 260 files** with the authority repair. After the final fixture simplification, its entire **166-test delivery suite** passed again, with all retry/partial-send assertions preserved.
- **Before the conflict rebase, 18 additional end-to-end tests passed across four files:** persisted creation/edit/removal and scheduler reload, delivery/webhook outcomes, execution diagnostics, and scheduled-session retirement through a disposable Gateway fixture. The required private-QA/runtime rebuild also completed successfully (9m 10s), followed by the E2E runtime build and tests.
- **Real authority-chain regression:** creator tool grant → actual cron.add → persisted job/session rows → CronService principal selection → run admission → actual coding-tool file read. The foreign-directory case demonstrably failed before the correction by reading a sentinel its creator could not read directly. It now rejects before file I/O. Own-conversation and trusted-operator reads succeed; an archived owner session cannot execute. The model/runner is controlled; this is not a live provider or production-job claim.
- **Original-bug negative controls:** restoring the pre-fix production owner made the bound-workspace and persistent-rollover regressions fail for the intended reasons. Restoring the repair made them pass. Managed-worktree tests also use real lifecycle interruption during workspace lookup to prove revoked bindings stop before execution.
- **Full changed gates passed on `dc3989dd8c6e`:** core types, all 25 selected test-type graphs, typed lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, dead exports, import cycles, and selected repository guards. Changed-page MDX and diff whitespace checks passed. No check, admission, timeout, or assertion was weakened.
- **Independent AutoReview completed:** full candidate and final correction delta had no actionable P0–P2 findings in their frozen supplied scope. Earlier findings were reproduced and repaired or resolved against canonical contracts; the original security finding is not being dismissed.
- Retained additional proof: **901 adjacent-owner tests passed (one existing skip)** across 40 files before the final authority guard, covering worktree leases, lifecycle admission, rooted/CLI execution, tool containment, Gateway cron ingress, hooks, and heartbeat behavior. The original publication also completed the full pnpm build, including Control UI (6m 38s). Those are earlier-stage evidence, not relabeled as new exact-head runs.

<details>
<summary>Failure classification, test audit, and measured costs</summary>

The initial broad run had 17 fixture failures: 13 cases supplied a session key inconsistent with their explicit target, and four real-adapter cases mixed independent cached session-reader mocks. The fixtures now use their actual target keys and one runner-owned reader. The latter also calls the canonical delivery-plan resolver instead of copying a constant plan; no coverage was removed and the oversized file became smaller.

Six local webhook failures were caused by the host proxy routing loopback traffic externally. An inert local server reproduced that routing failure; merging loopback-only NO_PROXY exclusions restored the unchanged 24-test webhook suite. The external proxy was retained. E2E setup used an explicitly disposable HOME/state/config/profile/service identity rather than modifying or stopping the installed Gateway.

The new authority test is retained under test-audit because helper-only workspace tests missed the creator-to-target authority transfer. It adds no production test seam. Existing managed-lease/lifecycle tests protect different failure boundaries and were retained. The requester-scope correction added 24 net production lines; the managed-owner correction adds only two more conditions. The substantial additional coverage is test code.

Measured with pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1 on Node 26.8.2; wall times include shared compiler/import preparation. The authority row is the latest managed-owner repair; other rows retain the stated earlier-stage measurements:

| Changed test file | Tests | Wall time |

| session.test.ts | 26 | 11.74s (initial publication) |

The latest authority file spent approximately 80% of Vitest time transforming its cold shared closure; the seven actual cases totaled about 9.8s. Its real creator/storage/admission/file-effect contract cannot be established by a cheaper mocked path resolver. The initial workspace-file measurement included 23.26s shared subprocess preparation. Exact-head CI completed successfully. Per-file CI timing could not be recovered because both the normal log download and the log-archive request returned unexpected EOF; the measured local costs above and the clean Testbox timings below are retained. This is a log-retrieval gap, not failed or skipped execution.

The ClawSweeper revision-2 authority finding was resolved and its real-behavior proof marked sufficient. Revision 4’s registry-owner finding is addressed by the new red/green final-effect cases above; its fresh head review remains part of landing. An earlier review’s suggested published-driver-to-candidate upgrade matrix was not run: this patch changes no schema, serialization format, field definitions, updater, or migration path. Existing persisted-row execution, rollover retention, stale-binding rejection, and live admission/lease behavior are the scoped contracts exercised here. The fail-closed runtime choice is accepted above; it is not an unresolved data migration.

The broad local check stopped at pre-existing TS2741 in the untouched `src/gateway/session-row-projection.config-commits.test.ts`: its config reloader fixture lacks the required scheduler. The owning correction is already on main at [4bd105408ccdac229eee8f719f082ba143f0c26c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4bd105408ccdac229eee8f719f082ba143f0c26c). No unrelated fixture edit, suppression, or baseline exception was added here. Core types, the affected cron graph, and all remaining selected guards were completed separately. One compiler attempt also stopped before tests because a new review-context JSON file changed the frozen namespace; final verification used precreated evidence files and unchanged inputs.

No live scheduler run, deployment, or full-repository local test suite is claimed. CLI runner forwarding is boundary coverage, not an authenticated live-provider run.

</details>

### Current integration and clean-environment proof

**Published head: `cfe497ac4de59260f7132f8bfbf14c0b47f51d23`.** Native preparation integrated existing main repair [a46cde88785df](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a46cde88785df6aa867e35f98aa5fabce6cd45e9) while preserving the reviewed `4d0da578123a9` ancestry. The one-shot command returned **exit 0** and the owned Testbox stopped. Total remote command time was 190.854s including dependency preparation. Source admission and the remote source receipt bind `89eef5feb4c6ab161b69aa8d3c0d94b474c1aa0a` to the same full tree as the published integration; this is tree-identical source proof, not a claim that the Testbox checked out the publication commit ID. The backing Actions Testbox step may appear cancelled during normal delegated lease teardown; the command/timing receipt is the execution result.

These failed local runs remain recorded—not relabeled as passing. body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a deterministic managed-service handoff fixture failure in the 2026.9.7 release candidate. Maintainer-authorized release repair following [NORMAL CI 36290577082, Windows job 108539907845](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36290577082/job/108539907845). Related: #156584.

In busy shared conversations, separate collaborator typing indicators can crowd the chat and imply an idle person's draft is still active.

title: fix: stop worker provisioning effects after host authority closes
body:
<!-- Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled where safe under the fork Actions/secrets policy. -->
Related: #135838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could see worker provisioning continue after its host operation closed, leaving allocated resources without settled cleanup or rejecting valid enrollment from the same operation.

## User Impact

Worker provisioning stops admitting new effects after host shutdown or invocation closure, while cleanup keeps its independent authority. Expiring prepared workers retain successful or uncertain capture custody until independent teardown. A checkpoint returned after source closure is kept for cleanup, not made reusable; teardown cannot start a new project capture without live source authority.

Existing external providers keep the source-compatible default `WorkerProvider` type and optional provisioning arguments. `WorkerProvider<1>` opts into required invocation guards; bundled providers use that contract. **No legacy cutoff, removal date, configuration, protocol or database-schema change.** Legacy implementations that ignore the supplied callback remain a documented limitation. This is the provider slice, not completion of the entire linked workstream.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing live owner assertion through provider preparation, allocation and effect boundaries rather than treating a physical cancellation signal as authority. Extend the existing cleanup catch across dispatched allocation, preserve settled cleanup receipts without a second stop, and keep same-operation enrollment valid. The same captured source assertion now gates final reusable-image publication. If publication is refused, only the surviving exact capture selector becomes cleanup debt; ambiguous persistence, admitted publication and successor selectors retain their existing recovery behavior. Independent teardown still collects cleanup debt, but does not recapture an expired project. No new state owner or schema is introduced.

Contributor credit: @sallyom and @vincentkoc.

title: fix(gateway): keep paired diagnostics working across SSH routes
body:
Closes #159121

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes paired Gateway diagnostics losing read access or selecting another Gateway's cached credential when local and SSH-forwarded connections share a loopback URL.

## User Impact

Paired local diagnostics work again. Configured SSH clients and diagnostics reuse device credentials for the selected remote target and Gateway port, independently of the allocated local forwarding port. A busy or permission-denied preferred local port now falls back to an available port; the remote destination is unchanged.

Existing URL-only remote-loopback credentials are not reassigned automatically. Configure `gateway.remote.sshTarget` (or a pinned TLS endpoint) and enroll the selected route once; subsequent paired diagnostics do not need shared credentials. Manually forwarded, unpinned loopback diagnostics still need explicit credentials. Existing manual-direct RPC/TUI credential behavior is unchanged; this PR does not claim to add an immutable Gateway identity to those routes.

Existing implicit SSH configurations adopt client-owned forwarding. Set the existing `gateway.remote.transport: "direct"` option to retain a manually managed forward. CLI/environment URL overrides preserve their selected listener. **SSH aliases are operator-owned route selections, not cryptographic Gateway identities: reassigning an enrolled alias to another destination trusted by OpenSSH can send its saved device bearer there. Use a new alias for a different Gateway.**

No new configuration keys, credential store, schema, protocol, permissions, or server-side pairing policy. Reverting the route code does not delete either credential row; binary rollback across an unrelated schema migration requires compatible pre-update state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing connection resolver applies the native macOS selected-route design. The Gateway client owns SSH startup, cancellation, connection, and joined teardown. Enrollment, RPC/TUI, and diagnostics share its credential scope. The existing port inspector admits only the still-live SSH child's listener; a released port cannot become a reconnect target. OpenSSH alias ports, host-key policy, TLS reference identity, and certificate pins remain authoritative.

Local probes prefer local device credentials, validate an origin-only fallback against the local pairing owner, and use that exact verified token through the handshake. Unmanaged restarts revalidate their process owner before acting. Small helper/type extractions preserve existing lazy boundaries and file-size limits.

## Evidence

Prepared head: `232bd3eb662f5c221c715da58ef6d9d2b8c039d6`.

**Merged via squash.** Landed commit: [`cc70f934a15adab35551a6a1ff547b759c73753b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cc70f934a15adab35551a6a1ff547b759c73753b).

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36351519588) passed: **141 successful jobs, 19 intentionally skipped, no failures**, including all five Windows Node lanes and all five core test-type stripes. [ClawSweeper revision 18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159169#issuecomment-5849928761) reviewed this exact head with no actionable or security findings. Focused maintainer review found no P0–P2 issues in credential/route ownership, transport lifecycle, callers, or SDK compatibility.

- The permission-denied preferred-port regression failed before repair; the SSH owner suite passes **35/35** (2.29 s runner wall). Allocation/listening are real; permission errors are simulated. The original remote destination is asserted unchanged.
- SDK compatibility proof at `16654779312c05d9bb0b28860d3097b2d2ae3c1c`: the strict source consumer failed before the correction and passed afterward (0.23 s). The canonical `pluginSdkStrictSmoke` build passed all runtime and declaration compiler groups, 95 plugin builds, and **158 public SDK entries** in 9m 11.3s; the compiled consumer/export checker took 1.85 s. The runtime constructor remains reference-identical to classic `ws`.
- Focused TLS/Gateway/worker tests pass **163/163** in 66.62 s at that SDK-correction head. Earlier refreshed CLI/SSH coverage passes **238/238** in 64.99 s at `e7a1c25997f2b3362333341bc14b9d5342e1f21a`. These earlier runs are reused, not presented as new runs after every refresh. The final follow-up is equivalent constructor-type syntax, followed by a patch-identical rebase; the strict public consumer and type-aware lint also passed after that syntax correction.
- Selected local production/test type checks, all 25 core test graphs, core/plugin/script lint, export scans and ownership guards passed. Independent canonical P0–P2 review of the SDK correction is scoped-clean.
- Real isolated OpenSSH/Gateway evidence covered enrollment, paired reads after local forwarding-port changes, wrong-route denial, and six TLS identity/pin cases. These preceding-runtime runs were not repeated for the permission/type-only corrections. A controlled receive-side test confirmed the documented effect of reassigning an enrolled alias after OpenSSH trust changed; it was not a full Gateway-authentication test of the replacement peer.
- The integrity-verified published 2026.9.6 client/state transition retained legacy credential rows and recovered reads after route enrollment. Its unrelated schema 18→19 incompatibility required an untouched compatible backup for older-binary rollback; no schema marker was lowered.

Limitations: synthetic isolated state and peers rather than the reporter's installation; no fresh complete UI/package/release build, native desktop/device smoke, full installer/update-driver or old-Gateway-server upgrade claim. An earlier full-build native TypeScript compiler crash did not recur in the complete SDK compiler profile; its cause is not claimed fixed. The inspected published updater's `--preserve-definition` route does not enter the changed unmanaged-restart branch. Local issuance checks retain the existing implicit-local trusted-host boundary.

body:
Related: #135838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a cancelled or replaced dispatch attaching a worker and persisting a credential after its caller loses authority while waiting for the attachment queue or installation packaging.

## User Impact

- A closed caller cannot attach a worker after queue, packaging, or database-admission waits. A different live caller can still succeed.
- An attachment that already committed stays committed; cleanup of the previous tunnel epoch is joined before the existing credential response returns.
- No configuration, wire protocol, database-schema migration, public SDK change, or legacy-provider cutoff. This is the small attachment slice, not completion of the broader #135838 workstream.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the dispatch owner's existing assertion into the credential broker for both cold and prepared attachments. The broker composes it with service and prepared-placement authority, then carries that assertion into the existing native final-COMMIT admission. Postcommit custody and cleanup remain independent of the initiating caller; there is no new authority or persistence owner.

Contributor credit: @sallyom and @vincentkoc.

- [Original discussion with @sallyom](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/70f8933b-db6b-4809-b9a8-941957263614)
