Reviewed candidate: `fdae9a040983406ce86a314ac2e0a081c90e46c4`, based on main `353c6989892e6f01ff7ff63931eb30da58cd99e4`. Resolved the credential-broker conflict while preserving main's service-error and turn-credential refactors. Updated the asynchronous dispatch harness and now-unconditional reader reuse. A later main advance to `dcd48b6aa5f2e68ef1a185872b4ad305e9172963` changes only two UI model-setup files; the refreshed candidate composes with it without conflicts. Removed the obsolete transaction-stage handshake case rather than restoring that retired boundary; the actual native final-COMMIT refusal and rollback/reopen proof remain.

- **Regression:** the seven current cases produce **six intended behavioral failures and one passing committed-custody control** without the production fix; **all seven pass** with it. This covers queued and packaging revocation, service shutdown, final native COMMIT refusal with persisted state checked after reopen, independent callers, cold dispatch forwarding, and joined postcommit tunnel cleanup.
- **Compatibility suites:** 174 passed and two recovery assertions failed across six sibling files. Both failures also reproduce with the PR's two production files and the device-test expectation restored to main, using the same six-file command and order; details below. No test was suppressed or weakened to hide them.

- **Independent canonical review:** scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. Existing unguarded internal callers remain supported by the optional assertion; credential hashing, lifetime, owner epochs, delivery shape, worker protocol, configuration, and stored formats are unchanged.

The proof uses the real service, credential broker, delegated-authority registry, worker-backed SQLite admission/rollback/reopen, and tunnel lifecycle owner with controlled external boundaries. It is not a live cloud-allocation, external SSH-server, or installed-upgrade test. Exact-head public CI and required reviews remain landing gates; this refresh does not merge the PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelling or replacing a delegated request could still allow tunnel startup, workspace synchronization, or repository transfer after the caller's authority ended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing composed caller guard through node and SSH startup, repository preparation, and transfer effects. Keep established tunnel/workspace custody independent of the initiating request. Upload revocation joins the existing disposal owner, and reconciliation takes completed-upload custody before revocation; transfer options retain the existing ten-minute budget.

## User Impact

- Closed callers cannot start new workspace effects after asynchronous preparation or transport waits.
- A cancelled joining caller does not tear down another operation's established tunnel. Accepted reconciliation and cleanup retain their own ownership.
- No new configuration, protocol, database schema, or provider compatibility cutoff.
- This is the transport/workspace slice. Prepared-execution and result-custody caller repairs remain separate; this does not close the whole #135838 workstream.

Contributor credit: @sallyom and @vincentkoc.

title: feat(workers): require configured worker placement for sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Activates the existing `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile` policy through ordinary session creation, first-message handoff, and Control UI recovery, without requiring manual placement privileges. Unset policy preserves optional/local behavior.

## User Impact

Required-worker preparation, Retry/Stop, and first-message handoff use the existing placement owners. Failures retain unsent text and attachments. Cold Send waits for required profiles and submits once. Required drafts survive a released Control UI opening in the same tab.

Committed empty-session creation survives transport disconnect; writer-scope or required-profile revocation still prevents worker setup.

## ClawSweeper Feedback Repairs

Candidate: `27fe0d23c994e10742223d938582138c1c412116`; source tree `99b4b75517236e3f24fb29e4dbcdfc6e0160a903`.

- **P1 disconnect lifetime:** RPC cleanup released the caller capture at the durable requested ACK while detached dispatch still used it. Full-dispatch admission now retains that same capture through awaited dispatch and cleanup, propagated through the existing create/policy guards. Live source, scope, session, and profile checks remain intact.
- **Actual RPC regression:** wait for successful create acknowledgment, disconnect while dispatch is paused, then require both real setup entry points. Scope/profile revocation still requires zero setup effects. No new timers, polling, process boots, timeout increases, or expected-failure exceptions.
- **P2 duplicate routing:** align the Gateway-tool route with main's registration slot. The integrated registry has exactly one route; no assertion or production change in this routing repair.
- **Conflict integration:** pinned main `5b4fb7292031dc3695a6fae10fd044814c5d3ca4` introduced helper/prepared-result changes; later pinned main `7d18cafe121a373f81c4de2380e29a1aa84037e7` introduced prepared local-placement/session-reader changes. Preserve these optimizations together with required-session admission and live policy checks. Release prepared leases before the live claim transaction and on failures/early returns. The two teardown fixtures and local-admission tests now match main. Resolved owner/test bytes match the fresh reviewed candidate; merge-tree against pinned main is clean.
- **Compatibility:** [area-owner acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158903#issuecomment-6025753124) already covers default-off activation, existing-session impact, unavailable-worker blocking, and the config baseline. Revision 63 explicitly says not to reopen it.

## Evidence

### Follow-up CI repair — October 9, 2026

Current head: `7932d7e5788dee3c1299d814f86c6f581ffd7e17`. Repairs the two failed browser cases and shared Swift dead-code finding from head `59a42d4b2791f9e8eb40b14b9920f9b06dee5998`; the failed CI gate was their aggregate.

- [Failed browser job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38022079649/job/114125255985) tested merge `47918995a7fd849e2d4b7a43197b7b87ab330897`, with main base `9948a4b83404b2e969593aa072b932735c1d2cfe`. Both browser failures reproduce on that clean base and the integrated PR: **2 failed / 9 passed**, 90.81s and 93.58s Vitest wall respectively. The clean integration commit has exactly the tested merge tree.
- Main deliberately preserves accepted steer order and holds a pending rename modal open. The stale recovery assertions and modal navigation fixture are repaired by the incorporated [upstream #168195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168195), retaining original authorship. Its executable assertions match the locally verified repair; only title/comments differ. All ordering, pending-mutation scope, pagination, and row-membership assertions remain.
- [Shared Swift scanner failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38022079482/job/114128692624): two reconnect-backoff hooks were introduced on main but called only by package tests, which app-consumer scans do not index. Move those unchanged helpers into the test file through its existing `@testable` boundary. No scanner exclusions, baseline changes, or runtime behavior changes.
- **17/17 bundled-browser tests pass**, including the two repaired files, dedicated rename-modal coverage, and the prior required-draft/defaults regression; `--maxWorkers=1`, **91.77s Vitest wall**. No added tests, waits, timeout increases, or configuration changes.
- Swift package test build passes (**170.52s**); **9/9 path-recovery tests pass** under isolated native execution (**0.020s test time; 9.52s command wall**). SwiftFormat passes.
- All planned changed-check commands pass, including core test type graphs, core lint, three unused-export scans, formatting, repository ratchets, UI i18n, native state-schema guard, and full `pnpm test:macos:ci`. The planner stopped because pinned SwiftLint was absent from its PATH; its exact app-lint command passes separately with the installed **0.65.1** tool, zero violations across all configured scopes. Current candidate: `dc456de153644c4bac51dd90a4a9ad3a95fa5bef`. Conflict-free integration of pinned main `c40ca82d07a490da257e045fe7ae06f32ef320c8`, plus a two-test assertion repair. No new runtime policy, configuration, schema, dependency, timeout, or baseline change in the repair.

- Failed [CI run 37993450619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37993450619) actually tested merge `832a55fa70b3a213a38f817cec5cd3f85aec803d` (head `fe5652fa1845361f32fe2dfeb1c6667f20b70ef6`, main `05464f1c2e3dff0bc8d07b05630849e7bd137b2a`). No new tests or timer/process boots. Original failing hosted shards took 425.29s and 369.96s; new-head CI completed with the distinct worker-test failure recorded below.

Both production type lanes and all **31 test type graphs** pass, as do formatting, source/script/QA lint, all export scans, schema guards, database/sidecar ownership, import-cycle, auth, and webhook checks. - **Exact-head hosted CI completed red:** [run 37999005948, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37999005948) tested `dc456de153644c4bac51dd90a4a9ad3a95fa5bef`. The sole failed leaf is `checks-node-changed-5`; its skill-library worker E2E rejects replacement-worker `chat.send` after abort/`agent.wait` with `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError` (`skill-library-worker-wire.e2e.test.ts:564`, request assertion at line 169). The aggregate CI gate consequently fails. The test itself took 64.30s; the five-target shard took 659.90s. This is distinct from the repaired compact-history assertions and Workboard asset drift, whose hosted lanes now pass.
- The failure's attribution remains **unresolved**: the ordered session-read owner can reject a raced native handle/revision, and post-abort settlement can still be publishing. Those owners and the cancellation algorithm are unchanged versus pinned main, but this PR's admission wrapper can affect timing, so unchanged source is not claimed as inherited-failure proof. The isolated local replay on this exact head was planned for all five original shard targets in the original order. Runtime preparation completed (22m38s main build, 102.7s AI build, 58.9s worker-artifact preparation), and the first lifecycle file reached Vitest. The runner subsequently ended without a file summary or terminal shard-completion record; its termination cause is unconfirmed. The remaining four files, including the failing skill-library test, did not start. This incomplete replay neither reproduces nor disproves the CI failure. Earlier head-bound receipts remain historical. GitHub currently records auto-merge enabled at 2026-10-09T22:35:59Z; the exact-head CI failure and unresolved attribution above remain unchanged. This evidence update did not enable or disable auto-merge.

### Saved draft choices — October 9, 2026

Saved-draft repair head: `fe5652fa1845361f32fe2dfeb1c6667f20b70ef6` (three-file delta from `f54469540415f3c727896ae89a49ddd4d3f18419`). Addresses revision 65's P1 explicit-choice reload finding and its stored-data/original-intent checkpoints.

title: feat(ai): scope transport hosts per runtime
body:
Related: #154388

## What Problem This Solves

Independent model runtimes need transport policy that cannot replace or inherit another runtime’s provider, authentication, routing, fallback state, or cached connection.

## User Impact

Remote and native harnesses can run concurrently without leaking transport authority or connection state. Ordinary runtimes and browser imports keep their current defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a runtime-owned `@openclaw/ai` transport host. Explicit Node runtimes use `createNodeLlmRuntime`; ordinary runtimes keep the process default. Provider factories remain synchronous, while runtime scope is retained across lazy stream operations.

ChatGPT WebSocket reuse and SSE fallback are scoped by runtime host, endpoint, and authority-bearing headers. Managed-transport policy disables direct WebSocket paths, and process-default state remains reachable across host reconfiguration. Fallback history retains eight recent authorities per session, bounding credential retention while avoiding repeat upgrades during normal token/header rotation.

This is the transport-contract slice of the original native worker inference change, based on work by @sallyom and @roboclaw-bot, with contributions from @steipete.

### Maintainer Decision

The public `createNodeLlmRuntime` contract and its inert omitted/partial-host defaults are accepted. Embeddings must supply the managed fetch and credential policy they require; an explicit runtime must not silently inherit process transport authority. This is the intended foundation for the later worker-lifecycle and native-inference slices.

## Evidence

- Focused runtime/authority tests: 95/95 passed in 3.12s wall with one worker.
- Real loopback WebSocket I/O proves that replacing the process default during first-use payload construction still leaves the old authenticated socket reachable for session cleanup.
- Real loopback cleanup proof verifies that cleaning one runtime preserves a sibling runtime, while global cleanup closes every registered owner.
- Boundary proof verifies that credentials and managed fetch policy remain bound to the same captured host when payload construction replaces the process default.
- Lazy-stream and browser-bundle proof verifies that replacing the process default after stream creation cannot move later `result()` or iterator work to a different transport host, drop completion metadata, or make a completed native stream unreadable.
- Completed browser iteration now drains native and delegated terminal events after host replacement while pending provider work still blocks replacement. The regression failed before the repair with `Scoped AI transport hosts require Node.js async context support`; the named browser/host-scope suite passes 13/13 in 2.56s wall.
- Custom browser streams without native completion metadata now have one host-bound source pump and replay-only consumers. Provider results settle independently, post-terminal cleanup runs to actual iterator completion, multiple replay readers remain independent, and cancelling one pending reader does not stop the source pump.
- Native Responses WebSocket final effects and HTTP continuation caches are owner-scoped; session cleanup cannot cross runtime owners, and degraded WebSocket cooldowns expire independently.
- Public-runtime final-effect proof uses real loopback HTTP/SSE and the real OpenAI SDK WebSocket client. For both matching-session and omitted-session cleanup, runtime B continues on its retained continuation/socket while runtime A starts fresh. The 2-test boundary passes in 3.00s wall; both cases fail for the intended cross-owner reason when applied to pre-fix `202ace18b2d`.
- `auto` transport falls back to SSE when a relative endpoint cannot form a WebSocket URL.
- Real loopback I/O also covers managed-transport gating, cross-runtime isolation, fallback stickiness, recent-authority retention, and deterministic eviction after the bound.
- Loopback WebSocket frames are capped at 64 KiB; the affected cache tests pass.
- The original CI failure is repaired at its owner: the automatic-compaction fixture now returns a synchronous provider stream and passes 28/28 in 236.69s wall with one worker after a local worker-cache rebuild. This existing boundary suite is the cheapest coverage for compaction-in-flight admission state.
- Exact-head changed-file checks pass, including core production/test types, lint, dead exports, import cycles, and repository guards.
- AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 issues in the ownership repair (`patch is correct`, 0.79 confidence), the real-client proof (`patch is correct`, 0.88 confidence), the completed native/delegated browser-stream repair (`patch is correct`, 0.72 confidence), or the final custom-stream lifetime/replay repair (`patch is correct`, 0.83 confidence).
- Exact-head CI's two core-lint jobs reproduce unchanged on both its pristine base (`34a0d304a8d`) and current `main` (`558d38a3db5`): unresolved database types and `.sort()` diagnostics in untouched `src/**` files. The PR does not modify those files; this is inherited red-main evidence.

title: fix: warn agents when background commands cannot wake them
body:
Related: #120414

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a missing handoff warning when an agent backgrounds a command with `tools.exec.notifyOnExit=false`: the result previously gave the same generic follow-up instructions as notification-enabled execution, so an unfinished task could stop after a progress-only final with no event to resume it.

## User Impact

Agents now receive an explicit no-wake warning and instructions to collect required results with a bounded `process poll` before ending the turn, unless another continuation is already arranged. The warning reaches both ordinary tool responses and Code Mode's structured `followUp` result.

This is a model-facing handoff repair, not a guarantee of model compliance or a new automatic goal scheduler. Notification settings, process lifetime, approval policy, quiet-success behavior, and goal state are unchanged. No operator configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same effective `notifyOnExit` value that controls command completion notifications to select the follow-up guidance. Keep the guidance in the existing result rather than adding global prompt instructions, another tool, or a scheduler. A persisted active goal is not itself a continuation source. The appended warning refers to the poll action, leaving the existing follow-up prefix free to name a runtime-specific tool alias.

The related PR improves general visible running-state wording; this change specifically exposes the disabled-notification policy in structured results as well.

## Evidence

- Regression through the real exec/process tools and process supervisor, with only child execution controlled by a deferred adapter: the notification-disabled case failed on unchanged production code because the warning was absent; all **6 tests pass** with the repair. The enabled setting remains a passing control, and the returned process handle can collect the terminal result.
- Test cost (`pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.exec-liveness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`): **38.91 s before / 26.59 s final** wall time, including fresh worker compilation (27.17 s / 20.54 s). Test bodies totaled approximately **170 ms / 169 ms**; the new cases take **10 ms combined** after the fix. These are cold compilation measurements, not a claimed performance improvement. The regression adds no real sleeps, polling loops, processes, Gateway boots, or worker configuration. On exact-head [CI job `checks-node-changed-compact-large-3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36243101583/job/108407926479), the six test bodies took **0.194 s** total; the two new cases took **0.007 s** combined.
- `$test-audit`: the new cases protect the effective-policy warning on both tool-result surfaces and an actionable collection handle; no new production test seam or duplicate helper-only proof.
- `$deslop`: inspected all changed hunks; no behavior-neutral cleanup or unresolved slop finding.
- `$autoreview`: initial independent P3 review was `scoped-clean`; the final candidate review identified an index-only hard-coded tool name and explicitly verified the working-tree correction. That reviewed correction is now committed; no unresolved finding remains.
- Flake triage: the expected pre-fix assertion failure reproduced the missing warning; no intermittent failure observed across the focused and sibling runs.
- Selected `check:changed` lint/typecheck/guard checks passed, including core and all 25 selected core-test typecheck graphs; **19/19** background-exec follow-up, liveness, and notification-policy tests passed. The final alias-neutral wording was rechecked with the **6/6** liveness/regression tests and targeted lint; unchanged type/guard and sibling proof was retained. Exact-head [CI run 36243101583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36243101583) completed successfully on `e4df63fce1d59c01b372a69195e327802c75b298`, with both required `openclaw/ci-gate` results successful. [ClawSweeper reviewed that same head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158884#issuecomment-5846435311) with no actionable or security findings and nothing listed before merge.

title: fix: parent tasks report false failures after a Gateway restart
body:
Related: #158363

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: parent tasks report a subtask as failed after a Gateway restart even though its saved continuation completes successfully.

## User Impact

User impact: a recovered subtask can finish its original task and deliver one correct completion to its parent, without rerunning completed tools. Ordinary interrupted, failed, and cancelled children keep their existing recovery behavior. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart reconciliation could publish an interruption before an already-owned child-result continuation was admitted. That terminal failure then overruled the real success. Keep the exact pending continuation with its existing owner, resolve logical/physical store aliases through the canonical store resolver, and revalidate ownership before terminal settlement. This adds neither a new replay path nor message-side error suppression.

## Evidence

Actual built Gateways, native nested subagent/read tools, SQLite, and user-systemd process replacement on separate Blacksmith Testboxes. Same hash-verified driver and unchanged history budget on both revisions:

| Case | Before: 1edc66965f0a | Corrected: e59a72c7d1c5 |
|---|---|---|
| 2 successful reads | Worker resumes once; parent fails; original task failed | Worker resumes once; parent succeeds once; original task succeeded |
| 124 successful reads, keyed input outside raw window | Same false parent/task failure | Same successful original-task/parent completion |

Both corrected cases preserve the saved worker identity, keyed request and completed results; repeat no tools; change the service PID with NRestarts 0 → 1; and retain schema versions/hashes. Exactly one parent completion was observed, followed by a 10-second duplicate/contradiction check. All fixture processes and all three task-owned Testboxes are stopped.

[Proof manifest](https://91b59577e757131d68d55a471fe32aca.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/openclaw-crabbox-artifacts/crabbox-artifacts/v2/org/b3BlbmNsYXc/owner/Z2l0aHViOjU4NDkz/restart-parent-completion-e59a72c7/artifact-manifest.json?X-Amz-Expires=604800&X-Amz-Date=20260926T023100Z&X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=a677a1e59413a4e54bcc2da5fec6164a%2F20260926%2Fauto%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4810b85e6bf79845add2c2a967d59e20ab3ea0c1bf13590aabb8882cd1470c77) · [Download inspected ZIP](https://91b59577e757131d68d55a471fe32aca.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/openclaw-crabbox-artifacts/crabbox-artifacts/v2/org/b3BlbmNsYXc/owner/Z2l0aHViOjU4NDkz/restart-parent-completion-e59a72c7/restart-parent-completion-proof.zip?X-Amz-Expires=604800&X-Amz-Date=20260926T023036Z&X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=a677a1e59413a4e54bcc2da5fec6164a%2F20260926%2Fauto%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=6307a163b39336397bd67cfab73ed6bdeea20b4d21775aefbfb81d5f96c8a496) (signed links expire 2026-10-03). The bundle includes actual parent HTTP inputs, worker held/resumed inputs, results, logs, source/tree attestations and the runnable driver.

175 focused and Gateway/locator sibling tests pass. Full changed-scope checks pass, including core plus 25 test-type graphs, lint, schema/ownership guards and dead-export scans. Fresh staged P0/P1 autoreview is scoped-clean. The 46-test regression file measured 14.10s Vitest / 19.08s wrapper, predominantly shared transformation; test execution was about 1%. No new sleeps, timers or process fixtures were added to it.

Limits: controlled loopback provider, not a live LLM, nested Code Mode, ACP or remote-worker proof. Full prefix/one-keyed-request invariants were asserted at runtime; cleaned final SQLite fixtures are not in the bundle. Builds completed with the pre-existing UI startup JS overage (+409 B) and CSS advisory; this is not a clean UI-budget pass. Portal synchronization timed out after successful execution, but evidence download succeeded.

<details><summary>Implementation scope and contrary evidence</summary>

Production: +83/-1 lines in the existing recovery owner; tests/support: +167/-3; docs: +6. Growth is the exact cohort/session/store/runtime fencing and pre-commit revalidation, not a new manager, store, schema, permission or retry budget. No production paths/files were retired.

The initial candidate passed units but failed both real cases because it compared a logical sessions.json locator with a physical SQLite path. The corrected commit uses the existing asynchronous canonical resolver and realistic fixtures for both forms. The failed intermediate candidate is not counted as passing runtime proof.

</details>

title: feat(android): complete Models settings and provider connections
body:
Related: #158541.

## What Problem This Solves

Android lacks complete Models settings and hides or separates connection choices that the Gateway offers under one provider.

**Confirmed scope:** the requester explicitly expanded the earlier provider-only proposal to complete Android Models parity, including shared model defaults and Installed Agents. The original provider-only limitation in #158541 is superseded for this PR; these sections are not an unrequested expansion. The existing work-session link below records that discussion.

## User Impact

- Edit shared Model, Utility Model, Decision Model, Fallback Model, Thinking and Fast Mode defaults while preserving per-agent overrides. Automatic Utility Model shows its resolved model.
- Manage installed coding agents separately from provider accounts; enabling a coding agent does not authenticate it.
- Choose the Gateway-advertised API-key, OAuth, subscription/token, regional and plan methods under their provider family. Anthropic offers **Claude subscription (setup-token)** beside API key. Computer-only setup remains visible with Gateway instructions.
- Keep provider inventory, credential sources, connection tests, quotas, spend and scoped key removal. Shared-key removal warns about other agents; OAuth/token profiles are preserved. New connections open the chooser; **Edit API key** is reserved for an existing key.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app is a generic client, not a bundle of provider implementations. Provider plugins, authentication execution and credential storage remain on the Gateway. Android and Web group presentation while dispatching the exact original provider/method; setup-only methods are not executable login options. The existing configuration and credential owners remain authoritative.

The updated grouping needs the updated app and Gateway together. Older Gateways retain their advertised choices and omit unsupported optional metadata. No configuration/database schema, credential format, protocol-version, dependency or permission change is introduced. Protected writes, current-authority checks and admission settlement remain enforced.

The current diff is **114 files, +6,516/−1,696 lines**. It includes regression tests, extracted fixtures, generated metadata and **44 provider manifests**, not 44 Android SDKs. The production growth implements the complete Models controls and shared provider presentation. Deslop consolidates parsing and JSON construction; file extraction is not claimed as a net code reduction. The two-file CI follow-up changes only simulator preparation order and its existing executable regression. Current-main cleanup is preserved, including retired ChatController wrappers and the removal of copied NVIDIA manifest assertions.

## Evidence

Candidate: `52a26ed152c1f3e838ee16c0167c25d30a992900`, incorporating main `2b4a2749587ebfbf66c84bdae2ea46d1302f5031`. The conflict refresh preserves main's shared-profile auth-health refactor and this PR's distinction between pending and terminally failed OAuth renewal; it introduces no new UI or provider behavior. The canonical main registry repair and the Session Store benchmark repair from `945ec9ff5611` are incorporated. The latter now owns the exact benchmark source; the temporary PR-local diagnostic extension is removed. Its invariant is zero conventional state-directory discovery in every pinned/automatic list/search case, not parity between unrelated process-wide filesystem calls. Native Android rendering and provider implementation patches remain unchanged. The final Web follow-up removes the duplicate generic key shortcut when an advertised secret method already exists; named OAuth/subscription/key choices and the separate key editor remain available.

[CI and required checks for this PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158582/checks) are authoritative for readiness; local passes are not substituted for that gate. No merge or auto-merge is requested.

### Actual UI and upgrade proof

- [Provider chooser before/after and safe cancellation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158582#issuecomment-5848891149): native MiniMax methods together; Anthropic API key/subscription token and separate computer setup; key editing and masked LongCat/ClawRouter inputs retained.
- [Automatic Utility Model before/after and in-place upgrade](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158582#issuecomment-5849171532): actual Android app and isolated Gateway, same light-theme 480×800 viewport. Native Disabled → Auto writes only `agents.defaults.utilityModel`; readback restores the original configuration hash. Agent overrides, unrelated configuration, one pairing and both credential profiles remain intact.
- [Web chooser API-key deduplication before/after](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158582#issuecomment-5851115286): actual Chromium UI with the same OpenRouter fixture, light theme and 1280×900 viewport. OAuth and the exact masked credential wizard remain; cancellation and the separate provider-card key editor also pass. Two clickable GitHub previews render side by side at 320 px. The inspected comparison was delivered as a structured chat attachment.
- Captures were inspected and delivered as actual attachments in the original discussion. GitHub images render **side by side, clickable and 320 px wide**, including the cancellation image. All six rendered native Models/provider components still match the inspected feature source byte-for-byte.

These are retained native captures, not a new live-device execution of every incorporated main change. The reconciled APK and current tests are verified below. No completed external vendor sign-in is claimed; OAuth/device-code dispatch, masked input, callback validation and credential ownership have isolated boundary coverage. Earlier Web captures predate the grouping helper extraction; the linked deduplication comparison above exercises the final Web helper and does not claim a real vendor sign-in.

### Current checks and review

**Exact-head CI is green.** [Run 36290739286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36290739286) completed successfully on `52a26ed152c1`: **178 successful jobs, 11 skipped, no failed jobs**. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` entries pass. The native watcher confirms an effective green rollup with no pending checks; superseded historical entries remain in the raw GitHub aggregate. GitHub reports this head `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN`. Sweeper R27 found no actionable code or security findings but retains its documented owner-decision status below. The PR remains open with auto-merge disabled; no merge was performed.

| Proof | Result and measured cost |
|---|---|
| iOS CI simulator preparation | Existing executable regressions fail on the original order (3 failures), then **44/44** owner/lifecycle cases pass in **4.59 s** wrapper wall. The changed 21-case file alone takes **2.57 s** wrapper wall, **0.949 s** test time. Scoped changed checks, Bash syntax, `git diff --check`, and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. Cold boot now precedes the unchanged SimSlim reconfiguration budget and final profile verification. Exact-head macOS CI passes: iPhone screenshots **1,230 s**, iPad screenshots **1,467 s**, smoke **1,859 s** (complete job costs, not incremental test costs). Per-file hosted timing for the changed regression was not available in the inspected logs. |
| Conflict refresh against main `2b4a2749587` | **223/223** existing cases pass: auth health, Gateway auth status, discovery credential provenance, Bedrock credentials and explicit profile bindings (**60.26 s + 10.53 s** wrapper wall). Full changed checks pass, including Core types, all **25** test-type graphs, lint and repository guards; generated Swift protocol verification and `git diff --check` pass. Independent review found no P0–P2 integration regressions. The sole conflict retains both main's auth-health refactor and the PR's failed-renewal flag. No new tests or UI changes; fresh CI is attached to the updated head. |
| Android reconciliation | **74/74** cases: agent selection 41, catalog request 7, settings controller 8, provider status 9, provider screen 6, settings panels 3. APK assembly and app Kotlin lint pass. **90.686 s** combined wall, **11.621 s** tests. Native i18n verification passes without generated changes. |
| Gateway/NVIDIA | **113/113**: auth-status 105 plus retained NVIDIA behavior 8, **33.57 s** wrapper wall. The real no-credentials Gateway case fails with the unmodified main NVIDIA manifest lacking `credentialOnly`; it passes with the candidate. This replaces the copied-manifest assertion without adding a separate test case. |
| Z.AI reconciliation | **17/17**, **41.87 s** wrapper wall. Both original credential-only method-run cases are preserved byte-for-byte: API key and Coding-CN create the intended profile/endpoint without an inference probe or default-model selection. |
| Canonical registry repair integration | **93/93** across Talk actions, real history/lifecycle, broadcasts and source preparation, **119.40 s** wrapper wall. Main owns this repair; the superseded PR-local implementation and duplicate lower-level fixture are removed. |
| Canonical benchmark / current Gateway integration | **106/106** on Node 24.21.0: canonical Session Store benchmark plus auth-status cases, **58.00 s** wrapper wall. The benchmark matches main byte-for-byte; temporary diagnostics are gone. Native i18n verification passes with no generated changes. |
| Cloud recovery browser fixture | All **6 cases** pass with one worker in **23.04 s** wrapper wall. Three added lines dismiss the intentionally open machine chooser with Escape and wait for it to become hidden before the existing account/model interaction. Every recovery/request assertion and deadline remains. Full changed checks, including the UI E2E type graph (**26.8 s**), lint and independent P0–P2 review pass. |
| Web chooser deduplication | The extended existing rendered-page case fails on the old duplicate and passes on the repair. **32/32** picker/login/recovery cases pass in **6.81 s** wrapper wall; the changed two-case picker file passes with one worker in **3.28 s**. Real Chromium before/after flow passes in **17.54 / 16.73 s**, including the masked wizard and separate key editor. Full changed checks, UI types, i18n, lint and independent P0–P2 review pass. No new per-PR browser test was added. |
| Review | Independent original feature review and fresh scoped reconciliation reviews leave no confirmed P0–P2 findings. Registry adoption, Kotlin reconciliation and NVIDIA real-handler coverage were reviewed separately; these are scoped reviews, not blanket merge approvals. |

[Sweeper R27](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158582#issuecomment-5842597030) reviewed the current head `52a26ed152c1` and found **no actionable code or security findings**. The earlier duplicate Web API-key action is fixed and covered by the failing-before/passing-after rendered-page assertion, 32 focused cases and inspected browser evidence. No score or review marker was edited.

Requester authorization for the combined Models scope is recorded above; this is not represented as separate product-owner merge approval. A completed external remote ChatGPT login remains **unverified**: callback validation, exchange dispatch, cancellation and persistence have synthetic/isolated boundary proof, not a real account login. Acceptance of that proof limit remains a maintainer decision. Configuration compatibility and retained-state upgrade evidence are documented below; `unknown-truncated-pull-files` describes the capped review inventory, not an identified storage migration. The full 64-method source audit remains below.

<details><summary>Diff size by responsibility</summary>

| Responsibility | Files | Added / removed lines |
|---|---:|---:|
| Android app source | 12 | +2,237 / −466 |
| Gateway, plugin, Web and shared source | 18 | +420 / −153 |
| Provider manifests | 44 | +68 / −2 |
| Tests and fixtures | 31 | +3,526 / −1,007 |
| CI simulator preparation | 1 | +2 / −1 |
| Generated metadata | 2 | +173 / −61 |
| Documentation | 6 | +90 / −6 |

More than half of added lines are tests/fixtures. The 44 manifests add metadata, not provider SDKs to Android. These are source-diff counts against incorporated main, not a claim that moving code between files reduced the total.

</details>

<details><summary>Complete credential-only method audit — 64/64 choices</summary>

Audited all **64 newly opted-in auth choices in 44 manifests**, mapping every choice to its runtime implementation and credential provider (**48 provider IDs; zero unmapped methods**). All new opt-ins are secret/token methods, not newly enabled OAuth. Existing OAuth flows retain their own eligibility and authority gates.

| Runtime owner | Coverage and side-effect contract |
|---|---|
| [Shared API-key owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1c88e7ef7ba05e02a9bd6fb7a5657c8d20ae2dca/src/plugins/provider-api-key-auth.ts#L198) | **54 choices across 42 plugins**. Interactive execution returns credentials and a connection proposal; it does not persist them itself. Credential-only execution skips default-model resolution, including OpenCode starter-model discovery and Radius. Pure configuration callbacks were traced, not assumed safe from metadata alone. |
| [Anthropic setup token](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1c88e7ef7ba05e02a9bd6fb7a5657c8d20ae2dca/extensions/anthropic/auth.runtime.ts#L62) | **1 choice**. Masked, validated input returns a token profile. It does not start Claude CLI or change the agent runtime. |
| [Xiaomi](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1c88e7ef7ba05e02a9bd6fb7a5657c8d20ae2dca/extensions/xiaomi/index.ts#L143) | **4 choices**. PAYG/token-plan regional inputs preserve prefix validation and the selected endpoint. No HTTP call, process execution, persistence or model activation occurs in the auth method. |
| [Z.AI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1c88e7ef7ba05e02a9bd6fb7a5657c8d20ae2dca/extensions/zai/index.ts#L153) | **5 choices**. Credential-only mode skips inference endpoint detection and default selection. Named methods retain their endpoint; the generic method asks for one. Both retained regression cases execute the real method. |

The shared [persistence owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1c88e7ef7ba05e02a9bd6fb7a5657c8d20ae2dca/src/commands/models/auth.ts#L659) keeps profiles/notes and only provider/plugin connection configuration. It removes advisory default models, agent defaults, routing and unrelated configuration roots **before persistence**, skips external CLI import, and reconciles the proposal against current configuration. Model-access consent remains enforced. The Gateway validates current admin authority and the exact advertised plugin/provider/method; the OpenAI setup adapter forwards to its real API-key implementation.

Retained intentional behavior: provider endpoints/transport/catalog configuration, OpenCode and StepFun shared-key sibling profiles, and Arcee's OpenRouter credential binding. Normal post-save catalog refresh can make network requests; the entire lifecycle is not claimed to be network-free. This is exhaustive source/contract coverage, **not 64 live vendor sign-ins**. No provider SDK or auth runtime is added to the APK.

</details>

<details><summary>Complete source, compatibility and retained test evidence</summary>

All original feature **112 changed paths**, **95 prior blobs** and **112 candidate blobs** were read successfully with lazy fetching disabled. The added cloud-recovery fixture path was read in full, reviewed and exercised; canonical benchmark and Android source identity were verified after current-main integration. None of these source paths are missing. Sweeper's 80-file overview cap is not evidence of a storage migration.

The editor uses existing `agents.defaults.*` and `plugins.entries.acpx.config.nativeAgents.*` fields through revision-guarded `config.patch`. Existing schema owners, credential formats and profile-reference semantics remain unchanged. Optional wire additions (`tagsScope`, `renewalFailed`, `groupId`, `setupOptions`) have absence handling. `includeDefaultModels` already existed in the original PR base. Tests cover fresh revision/CAS writes, string/object model forms, retained fallback tails, nullable defaults, authority changes and uncertain-write reconciliation.

Earlier retained proof: 29 focused Android cases; 152 Gateway/Web auth, picker, recovery and helper cases; 101 registered login/wizard/WizardSession cases; 122 credential-binding cases. These overlap and are not summed into a unique-test total. Recorded wall costs: Android 25 s; Gateway auth-status 105 cases 54.99 s cold; Web login 21 cases 7.93 s, picker 2 cases 3.24 s, recovery 9 cases 3.80 s; cancellation 101 cases 38.44 s; binding 122 cases 38.41 s including its 15-case suite at 2.49 s Vitest. The Utility Model follow-up passed 18 cases plus APK build in 15.09 s; its existing request assertion failed before the one-line repair. Earlier scoped review's proposed coding-runtime card change was rejected against the canonical Web owner; the full model catalog remains selectable.

The prior candidate's full CI job costs were 435 s Android Play, 409 s third-party, 442 s Wear and 345 s Kotlin lint. Those are complete job costs, not incremental costs of the new cases. The exact current PR checks remain the final CI gate.

</details>

<details><summary>Original CI failures, canonical fixes and remaining limits</summary>

1. Missing Cron scheduler fixtures were unchanged main code. [Canonical fix c0e6951d6f02](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c0e6951d6f02d3eabd4bc13cf8e9fa9e77d290ac) resolved all four diagnostics. Redundant side PR #159131 was closed without merging.
2. [Run 36268598300, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36268598300/attempts/1) passed the iPad build, then exhausted simslim's fixed ten-minute bootstrap context during reboot. The capture ledger was `attempts: []`; no app test ran. GitHub fail-fast cancelled the remaining smoke job. One diagnosed infrastructure replay reran both screenshot families in the same attempt, as their provenance guard requires. No test or timeout was weakened.
3. [Attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36268598300/attempts/2) exposed `AgentDatabaseRegistryChangedError` in the Talk custody case; 71 Node jobs were cancelled as a consequence. We reproduced the initial discovery race. [Canonical main fix 3d903819c564](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3d903819c5641ed8735aebe55c86844957009952) now covers discovery and revalidation across registration admission/settlement while retaining captured authority and physical bindings. It replaces the temporary PR-local fix; no duplicate production owner remains.
4. That attempt also recorded a macOS presence test expecting two clear calls but observing one at its four-second boundary. MainActor delays make fixture timing plausible, not proven. No authorized local/disposable Mac route was available; no assertion or deadline was changed. The later `df6ba7` [macOS test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36272904113/job/108490413787) passed in 567 s; that pass is not claimed as a fix for unchanged code.
5. An older unchanged Session Store test observed one extra `statSync`. Original shard order passed 268/268 in 240.27 s; a focused run passed 10/10 in 70.17 s with six measured stat counts zero. The extra path was not identified, and local Node 26.10 differed from that CI's 24.19; its cause remains unproven. Passing replays are not called fixes. [CI at the previous head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36274865078) reproduced a related strict-counter failure: two extra `lstatSync` calls during automatic search, with no captured state-directory `existsSync` probe. Both the unmodified exact 22-file/two-worker group and a diagnostic-only replay passed 291/291 on the exact CI merge with Node 24.21.0; the former took 169.67 s. No unexpected filesystem provenance was observed locally; those passes were not claimed as a fix. Main subsequently supplied [canonical repair 945ec9ff5611](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/945ec9ff561180bf509d6f75181ab078c10a8078): require zero state-directory discovery independently in every case, excluding unrelated process-wide work from this specific performance contract. That exact source is now incorporated; the temporary PR diagnostics were removed. Earlier unmerged-base lint failures were repaired on main.

6. [Run 36276792357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36276792357/job/108501301982) failed the cloud-create recovery browser case: a `machine:standard` option intercepted the account/model-picker click. Other jobs were cancelled by fail-fast, not independently failing. Current main was checked first; it had no repair for this UI path. The exact unmodified 79-file/three-worker set passed **340/340** locally in **307.21 s**, so that pass is not claimed as a fix. Source confirms machine choices intentionally keep their menu open; the sibling cloud-dispatch fixture already dismisses it explicitly. This PR now adds that ordinary Escape action and an observed-hidden wait to the recovery fixture, with all six cases and original recovery assertions retained. No product UI was changed.

7. Candidate `ec930791357` subsequently completed [CI run 36278728127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36278728127): **182 successful jobs, 9 skipped**, including both iOS screenshot lanes and the required CI gate. R23 then identified the Web duplicate described above. That completed run is retained evidence for the prior head, not represented as the final head's CI. The current checks link at the top owns the final result.

8. [Run 36287494382, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36287494382/attempts/1) on head `b6bb01e6401` passed 204 check runs but failed the iPhone screenshot job at `XCUIApplication.launch()`: XCTest could not acquire the target app background assertion. The iOS test build succeeded; no screenshot-readiness or visual assertion was reached. The tested merge was `108e4005c57b` (base `e6fae68631f87` plus this PR head). The failure artifact records one failed Control capture; no PNG was produced. The sibling iPad capture, smoke and screenshot-evidence jobs were cancelled by fail-fast. [Attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36287494382/attempts/2) passed iPhone screenshots and iOS smoke, but failed iPad preparation before any test started: the cold boot consumed approximately 8m15s of SimSlim 0.8.0's shared ten-minute boot-and-reconfiguration context, leaving too little time for its required reboot. The iPad artifact contains a successful build log and an empty capture ledger, with no PNG or xcresult. The iPhone recovery is not claimed as a durable repair of its original XCTest launch failure.

   The owning preparation script now runs its existing native cold-boot readiness barrier **before** SimSlim. The pinned upstream `cmdOn`/`ensure` implementation already waits for the post-change reboot and reads back the profile, so the final `verify` remains authoritative. This matches the existing smoke caller's preboot contract. No timeout, test assertion, retry policy, service profile, dependency pin or app UI is weakened or changed. The existing executable Bash ordering/failure cases fail on the original script and pass after the repair; **44/44** owner and lifecycle sibling cases pass in **4.59 s** wrapper wall. Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issue. Exact-head macOS CI now passes in run `36290739286`, attempt 1. Its tested merge `945022f24e7f` has parents main `247f33e105f0` and candidate `52a26ed152c1`. Both device logs show cold-boot readiness, successful SimSlim reconfiguration/reboot, and verification that all 13 expected daemons are disabled. The run-bound manifests and PNG hashes verify **4 iPhone and 4 iPad captures**, each with a first-attempt passed xcresult and zero failed tests. The screenshot-evidence collector and iOS smoke job also pass. This verifies the preparation repair without claiming that the separate earlier XCTest launch failure was durably fixed.

No baseline, retry policy, provenance guard, score, bot marker or timeout was weakened to manufacture readiness. The canonical main benchmark now asserts its named state-discovery contract directly. No merge or deployment is requested by this PR update.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unrelated PR banners appearing above the chat composer when the assistant merely mentions a same-repository PR.

## User Impact

PR mentions remain ordinary message links. The session's working-branch PRs still appear, and the existing recorded publication-result UI is unchanged.

Branch-based chips no longer follow conversational links after a checkout becomes detached or returns to the default branch. This fix does not introduce a history of every PR reviewed in a conversation. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Conversation text is not evidence that a PR belongs to the session's work. Remove transcript-based PR discovery, its cache, and its otherwise-unused cache-version reader; retain the existing branch lookup and publication owner, and remove tests that required the rejected behavior. Update the documented contract and regenerate its worker-inventory reference.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against the original implementation with a real stored assistant message: an unrelated PR was promoted on a feature branch, on the default branch, and with a detached checkout. All three cases now pass and assert that the unrelated PR is not fetched.
- Five focused Gateway suites: **82 tests passed**, covering discovery, branch and fork behavior, publication eligibility, quota backoff, retained state, and session/source invalidation.
- Existing PR/publication UI suite: **39 tests passed**, including publication results, recovery, dismissal, and CI detail rendering (21.26 seconds wrapper wall time).
- Transcript-search suite: **19 tests passed** after deleting the cache-version helper whose only production consumer was the removed banner scanner. The three mention regressions were rerun and passed (71.62 seconds combined wrapper wall time).
- Core and all core-test typecheck shards passed. After the dead-export guard identified the orphaned cache-version reader, it was removed; affected typechecks, production/full-tree dead-export scans, targeted core/tooling lint, format, import-cycle, schema, generated-inventory, and remaining scoped guards passed. Earlier unaffected checks were reused.
- Independent autoreview of the final candidate: **no actionable findings through P2**.
- Before/after captures show the comparison link remains in the transcript while its unrelated banner disappears and the actual branch PR remains. These are inspected **mocked-Gateway UI renderings of verified backend snapshots**, not live GitHub proof.

title: refactor: remove narrowly used helper dependencies
body:
Closes #158499

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw carries four direct dependencies for narrowly used task-checkbox, Telegram sequencing, and duration-helper behavior that can be owned locally.

## User Impact

Task-list markup, duration parsing/display, and normal Telegram ordering remain unchanged; no configuration, public SDK, or storage migration is introduced. The Telegram queue also preserves overlapping-key ordering when one predecessor fails instead of advancing while another conflicting predecessor is still active.

`@grammyjs/runner` and `markdown-it-task-lists` leave the workspace dependency graph. Direct `ms`/`pretty-ms` usage and declarations, plus `@types/ms`, are removed; legitimate transitive copies remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a small Markdown-It token rule and plugin-owned multi-key queue; reuse duration decomposition and one shared unit-factor owner. Script-only timing formatting stays in `scripts/lib`, not the production API. Remove obsolete mocks, declarations, dependency ownership/tooling references, and build/chunk entries. Regenerate the lockfile and measured Control UI boot manifest through their owners.

## Evidence

- **Maintainer proof waiver:** @steipete explicitly waived remaining live Telegram and before/after visual proof on September 27, 2026, and requested CI repair and landing. These checks remain unperformed, not passed. Enforced GitHub CI/review gates are not waived.
- Incorporated the upstream rsync temporary-file race repair from [#158443](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158443) (`0042f8a570d`). Active scans tolerate a renamed temporary file; final quota validation remains strict. This addresses the previous `checks-node-compact-large-10` failure without retries or weakened quotas. After integration, both quota/workspace suites passed: 14 tests, 47.36s wrapper wall; the PR-wrapper import inventory also passed (15.23s wrapper wall). Frozen installation passed. The comparator now materializes base-only dependencies in its private archive while retaining the candidate Vite/compressor. The real base comparison passes, with unchanged CSS (+0 B), and the regression passes on the fix and fails on the original comparator. No budget or baseline was relaxed.
- **1,030 distinct focused/affected-consumer tests passed before the main refresh** across CLI/retry/duration helpers, real grammY `Bot.handleUpdate` sequencing, bot composition/media, Markdown rendering, and tooling consumers.
- **6,086 differential formatting comparisons passed** against retained `pretty-ms` for actual caller options, including BigInt quantities. The script formatter also loads directly through native Node.
- **Pre-refresh `pnpm build` passed** with private-QA artifacts enabled in an isolated proof profile: runtime, package/SDK declarations, plugins, and grouped UI (10m 11.6s).
- After resolving actual main conflicts, **117 affected Telegram tests passed again**, the grouped UI rebuilt, and `ui:check-performance` passed. Fresh browser-based boot-manifest capture reached ready `/new` and `/chat` routes and reproduced the manifest byte-for-byte. `markdown-it-task-lists`, `ms`, `pretty-ms`, and `parse-ms` are absent from the measured startup modules. UI remains within budgets: 7 startup JS requests, 362.1 KiB gzip; no bundle-size reduction is claimed.
- Deslop completed; independent autoreview of the previous candidate and this main-integrated candidate returned **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. The latest two-pass assessment had limited context in its status-only chunk; source assessment did not claim live or screenshot proof.
- Validation passed across all type groups, formatting, three deadcode scans, stylelint, import-cycle checks (zero cycles), dependency/packaging/boundary guards, and extracted-wrapper/declaration import-closure proof. The full semantic-lint sweep found four errors; all four were repaired and their owning files passed focused lint reruns. Unchanged passing checks were reused rather than repeating the entire sweep.

**Verification limits:** Telegram coverage uses real middleware with synthetic Bot API updates, not a live service. The live Test Server attempt passed credential acquisition but stopped during readiness on a secret-egress proxy response from the harness transport. The lease was confirmed released; no test group was created and no live ordering result is claimed. No egress policy was bypassed; the maintainer subsequently waived this outstanding proof. Earlier tooling preflight/compile failures were resolved in an isolated proof profile; the live Gateway was not modified.

The UI performance comparator installs the archived base’s declared dependencies only within its private, disposable source archive. It changes no persisted user data, production schema, or upgrade contract; the review bot’s data-model flag does not identify a migration requirement.

title: feat(gateway): let operators disable client file and image uploads
body:
Closes #158556

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway operators need a way to disable client file and image uploads without disabling normal text conversations.

## User Impact

Set `gateway.uploads.enabled` to `false` to hide Control UI upload controls and reject client upload requests at the Gateway. It defaults to `true` and hot-applies without restarting. Existing attachment drafts remain recoverable; text-only messages still work.

```json
{ "gateway": { "uploads": { "enabled": false } } }
```

This governs client uploads, not agent filesystem permissions or incoming channel media. Downloads, existing media and agent-generated output retain existing policies. Trusted third-party tools writing their own client bytes must use the documented optional final-write callback; this is not a filesystem or DLP sandbox. No stored-data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns the switch and rejects direct API uploads, not just browser controls. Live policy checks reach proposal/library storage and Workboard's final publication. Text-only skill edits retain existing support files by exact revision instead of re-uploading or discarding them.

## Evidence

**Config-help snapshot follow-up:** the feature already intentionally declares `gateway.uploads.enabled` as a common setting, but the exact curated-common-leaf snapshot omitted it. CI run `36363112254` and the local captured config plan both reproduced the same single mismatch. Regenerating the named snapshot adds **only that one sorted leaf**; production visibility, schema, test enumeration, and the exact-set assertion are unchanged. This aligns expected output with the authorized feature, not an exception to the test.

- The captured 59-file config plan changes from **1 failure / 851 passes / 5 existing skips** to **852 passes / 5 existing skips**, in **83.46s**. The full help-quality and tier files pass **34 unique cases in 3.71s**; the nested quality summary is counted once.
- Focused independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean (**9.61s**), and diff checks pass. No TypeScript, production, timeout, budget, or ignore rule changed; prior static/build/UI proof is retained rather than rerun for a generated expected-value entry.
- The broader initial local job replay also hit an unrelated LAN self-reachability proof failure. That check passed in the actual hosted job; the local result is not counted as passing, and no networking or product policy was changed. The reproduced config snapshot failure is independently resolved by the focused and captured config runs above.

**Archive-shortcut fixture follow-up (test only):** the real keyboard action already returns an async header-action promise after its lazy import, archive workflow, and Undo toast. The fixture now observes that real call with a pass-through spy, asserts its exact target, and awaits its completion before the unchanged toast, durable-ID patch, draft, navigation, and Undo checks. No production behavior, mock implementation, timeout, isolation setting, or assertion was weakened.

The original hosted run `36360979826` failed this first toast assertion (zero calls; 1.838s), while the rest of its 225-file shard recorded 3,663 passes and 3 skips. The failure did **not** reproduce in the unchanged local file (24 cases / 4.77s) or valid captured-plan replay (3,667 cases / 91.99s). A cold import outlasting the incidental 1-second poll is a plausible mechanism, but the exact hosted cause remains uncertain; a stale mock identity was not independently excluded. The retained toast assertion would still expose a settled action with no expected toast.

- **After the correction:** 20/20 standalone runs pass all 24 cases; first measured wall **3.49s**, range **3.38–3.53s** (68.94s combined). Three complete captured-plan replays each pass **225 files / 3,667 cases**, in **89.53s, 87.57s, and 90.76s**. These are repeated stability runs, not additional unique tests. Four owner/keyboard siblings pass **106 cases in 11.77s** across normal and isolated UI projects.
- **Review:** focused independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean (11.01s), consistent with the separate source audit; neither claims to have reproduced the original failure.
- **Static checks:** the complete one-file changed-check passes all 19 planned stages, including the ui-chat type graph, zero-warning/error lint, formatting, i18n, all three dead-export scans, and the unchanged ratchets. Existing upload implementation, full-build, asset-budget, and visual proof below remain valid scoped evidence.

The first local shard attempt had four browser-start failures caused by an overlong process-only temporary path, not archive assertions. Restoring the browser runner’s ordinary short OS temporary paths made the unchanged full plan pass; those failed startup attempts are not counted as passing proof. The earlier auto-merge request was retired through native recovery before this repair. Replacement landing must satisfy the native completed-evidence recovery gates.

**Prior conflict-only refresh:** merged main `da04ae795c8dc24b000916161aadbb2e9f352cd2` to resolve the sole conflicted generated config-documentation hash. The upload source patch is unchanged across `src`, `ui`, `extensions`, and `packages` (stable patch ID `dd92e1517bf266745ee8093c6bc45467b1e362ce`); the only intersecting paths were the generated hash, existing assertion-baseline shrink, and Gateway documentation. Canonical config regeneration/check, document formatting, and diff checks pass. The freshly composed UI build passes in **17.59s**, with **372,295 / 372,347 B** startup JavaScript, **50,488 / 51,200 B** startup CSS, and **204.9 / 215.0 KiB** largest ordinary JavaScript. No budget or source-code exception was added. The prior full-build, runtime and independent-review evidence below is retained rather than rerun or relabeled as new-head execution. ClawSweeper revision 17 completed the preceding `cb337ed1e180` head at 23:58:58 UTC with no code or security findings; its policy/budget items retain their documented owner dispositions.

**Prior main reconciliation:** incorporates main `d038d1dbbfcf3ed5010912301a7d6c406003d231`, preserving both histories and the retired Tasks cutover. The only textual conflicts were the generated config-doc hash/counts; those were regenerated through the owning command. The UI boot manifest was regenerated from ready routes. A composed router line-cap violation was fixed by consolidating the repeated exact-handler-identity/policy decision in the existing core-handler owner; both router fences and their ordering remain unchanged. No cap, timeout, assertion, or policy exception was added.

- **Inherited CI fixes:** uses the exact already-landed `b459eb600f23` restart-status fixture and `6ad6f1fbe846` maintenance-error-cause fixture, without changing production recovery or restoring Task state. The captured original restart plan failed 4 cases / passed 923; the corrected PR plan passes **927 cases in 126.75s**. Main proof passes **1,143 cases with 14 existing skips in 132.62s**. Focused restart cost: **27 cases / 48.11s**; maintenance: **15 cases / 17.73s**.
- **Current composition behavior:** all **337 cases in 9 complete files pass in 131.87s** across actual router receipt/new-input admission, send, observer/request lifetime, cancellation, staged uploads, loopback HTTP/native filesystem admission, and config-write effects with main's fs-safe 0.21.1.
- **Current UI:** **46 unit cases and 8 unique bundled browser cases pass in 32.31s**. This uses the actual Control UI with a mock Gateway. Hot-disable removes uploads, preserves drafts, and allows text; the existing inspected images remain representative.
- **Review:** the full two-pass P0–P2 review completed in 161.87s. Its sole finding assumed the session-create upload guard precedes receipt replay; the actual exported handler is wrapped by `idempotentSessionCreate`, whose identity/authority and replay checks precede the inner handler. The real-router accepted-retry test covers this ordering. The concern is rejected on that source and behavior evidence, not relabeled a clean review. Final scoped source review: both the immutable main-composition audit and the final two-file consolidation audit found no P0–P2 regression; the latter verified exact handler identity, both fence positions, complete helper replacement, and preserved lazy handler loading.
- **Build and static:** the serialized full package build passes in **358.75s**, including native declarations, SDK exports, runtime sidecars and the CLI bootstrap guard. Core types, all five selected core-test graphs, UI types, all six selected source-file lint/format checks, i18n, ratchets, config-doc regeneration checks, and import-cycle analysis pass (zero runtime value cycles). The final composed artifact check passes the existing limits: **372,309 / 372,347 B** startup JavaScript, **50,488 / 51,200 B** startup CSS, and **204.9 / 215.0 KiB** largest ordinary JavaScript. The existing @steipete-approved **371,771 B baseline plus 512/64 B allowances** is unchanged. CSS remains above its advisory target.

The first local runtime invocation used two nonexistent file selectors and executed no cases; only the corrected selection is counted. An overlapping build was stopped by its compiler namespace guard when the test runner created metadata. The serialized rerun retains that guard; the earlier build and interrupted static tail are not passing evidence. Enforced published-head CI, exact-head local review, and the native recent-ClawSweeper completion check remain separate landing gates.

<details>
<summary>Earlier implementation and verification evidence</summary>

**Upstream CI fixture follow-up (test only):** adopts the exact correction already landed in `14ef6ab47832` (#159819). Main had retired the `taskId` artifact selector from both the schema and resolver, but one topology assertion still supplied it. Supported run/session authorization and topology checks remain intact; production code and test timeouts are unchanged. The original captured PR plan reproduces **1 failure / 919 passes / 1 existing skip** in 179.26s. With the canonical fix, the complete 69-selector plan passes **1,020 cases with 1 existing skip in 287.32s**, including the isolated leg. The independent main proof passes **1,053 cases with 14 existing skips in 291.97s**; the focused file, Gateway-methods types, lint, formatting, and scoped independent review pass. Initial local Doctor timeouts were isolated to ambient Gateway-auth inputs: unchanged tests pass after removing those inputs only from the test subprocess. Stored credentials, product code, and test timeouts were unchanged. Current-head hosted CI and review are still required.

**Receipt-safe disabling:** accepted chat, session creation, send, and message-action requests keep their authorized cached or in-flight receipts after hot-disable. Fresh input still returns `FORBIDDEN / UPLOADS_DISABLED` before new byte effects. The canonical receipt owners make that distinction; exact handler identity limits router deferral, and overrides retain both fences. Outbound route validation precedes replay, while binding publication and new work follow input admission. A refused request neither caches a denial nor pins a route; re-enabling it uses the current account default. Existing caller, session, runtime, cancellation, final-write, and handoff checks remain intact.

- **Original failure:** four outbound cached/in-flight cases failed in 19.22s; four chat/session/direct-entry cases failed in 42.51s. All failed because a valid retry became an upload denial. An interrupted compilation attempt ran no cases and is excluded.
- **Repaired owners:** 201 cases across the complete three affected files pass in 89.87s. Final standalone costs: send150 cases/13.58s; client-policy14 cases/46.50s; router-policy37 cases/8.81s. The strengthened outbound cases also verify that a rejected request does not retain its old default account after re-enable.
- **Lifecycle and storage siblings:** 525 cases across 13 files pass in 170.99s, including full agent admission, follow-up custody, chat cancellation, session idempotency, archive uploads, and the schema/worker admission tests. Scheduled/read-account coverage adds 14 cases in 26.18s. No assertions, retries, or timeouts were relaxed.
- **UI composition:** 35 unit cases and 8 unique bundled browser cases pass in 38.35s. Inspected fresh before/after captures confirm that hot-disable removes file/photo/camera actions while other composer tools remain. Browser assertions verify draft recovery and text-only sending. Existing published screenshots below remain representative; this uses the actual Control UI with a mock Gateway, not production traffic.
- **Review and static checks:** the full reconciled candidate received a completed two-pass P0–P2 review with no actionable findings (194.06s). Core, all 25 core-test graphs, and UI types pass; ratchets, formatting, config docs, boundaries, dead exports, scoped lint, styles, and architecture/auth guards pass across the successful prefix and corrected type/tail replays (the initial whole-check command is not labeled all-green). Subsequent fixture changes preserve the exact landed upstream test fix and use a fresh UUID rather than widening an inferred test type.

**Main reconciliation:** the candidate preserves the published branch and main `e3f3c15ebfe` histories, including main's Task runtime removal. Old CI's schema-probe failure is superseded by main's `1664e4cf262` / `af9e273f634` reverts; the obsolete local test correction was not published. Main's `c4e67604df4d` removes the exact unused iOS import reported by the old scan. Local static validation found a stale media-test callback; this candidate incorporates the exact already-landed three-fixture repair `0b6f02faae3` (#159836), whose 16 focused cases pass in 79.43s. Fresh published-head CI remains required; these are not rerun claims for the old failed/cancelled jobs.

**Build and approved budget:** the main-composed full package build passes in 459.07s. Its separate asset check passes: startup JavaScript **371,645 / 372,347 B**, startup CSS **50,359 / 51,200 B**, largest ordinary JavaScript **204.1 / 215.0 KiB**. Canonical boot-manifest regeneration was used; no packing or budget exception was added. The existing @steipete-approved 371,771 B baseline and 512/64 B allowances remain unchanged. CSS remains above the advisory target. The later receipt repair changes backend admission and tests, not UI source; exact-head CI owns final published-artifact validation.

</details>

Before — uploads enabled

![Upload actions visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/065704e7-ac36-4107-9e22-5b2b49e768e7)

After — uploads disabled

![Upload actions removed; other composer tools remain](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8bd0a545-4dde-4c30-bc82-ed0bbd8dcf5c)

<details>
<summary>Earlier implementation proof and measured costs</summary>

**Current-main reconciliation and receipt recovery:** merged `ac4c248d7789` while preserving both histories and the existing admission owner. Caller/runtime authority is separate from upload input policy. Stop receipts survive a concurrent disable, and the canonical `agent` RPC reconciles an authorized cached receipt before admitting new bytes; overridden handlers retain the router fence. A fresh idempotency key still returns `FORBIDDEN / UPLOADS_DISABLED`, with no files, inference or leftover reservation. The Stop-plus-disable case fails before repair (15.92s); the real-router retry also reproduces the prior denial (34.41s). The repaired three-file lifecycle/receipt selection passes **431 cases in 161.56s**; final router/upload-policy checks pass **45 cases in 33.66s**. The final nine-case real-writer file alone passes in **22.65s**. The current-main composition also passed **421 cases across 5 files in 190.41s**, including presence and skills flows. Both bundled browser files pass **8 cases in 27.35s** after boot regrouping.

The full package build passed in **351.14s**. Its separate performance check exposed a 99-byte ordinary-chunk excess; canonical ready `/new` and `/chat` boot-manifest regeneration fixed it without changing packing constants or raising any budget. On committed candidate `89f5025563b`, startup JavaScript is **371,616 / 372,347 B**, startup CSS **50,359 / 51,200 B**, and the largest ordinary JavaScript chunk is **214.9 / 215.0 KiB**; all enforced asset budgets pass. CSS remains above its advisory target. Composition with current main `b8894086496e` is conflict-free; this is local composition proof, not hosted CI success.

Current-main static validation passed core, all 25 core-test graphs, UI, plugins, plugin tests and script types; ratchets, formatting, metadata and dead exports also passed. The whole-core lint run found only the unchanged main 701-line projection file, repaired with the exact already-landed simplification from `54c0ae69cb8` (#159473). Fresh scoped lint passes **181 core/UI/package files, 7 Workboard files and the performance script**; style, schema, architecture and authorization guard tails pass. Subsequent receipt changes have fresh core/Gateway types, lint, line-cap checks and zero-cycle Madge analysis. The monolithic changed-check is not relabeled all-green: its valid prefix plus these corrected tail checks supply the evidence. Full current-candidate independent P0–P2 review is **scoped-clean**; the final mechanical request-fact reuse also passes its router tests and lint. New published-head CI remains required.

**Stop during attachment preparation:** replay the existing terminal Stop/timeout receipt instead of returning an attachment error after the reservation ends. Settlement stays with the existing agent-deduplication lifecycle; storage admission and cleanup remain intact. The existing attachment-setup tests reproduced 2 failures before repair (41.63s); the added real-handler/filesystem Stop regression also failed on the original code (17.77s). The complete recorded 67-file Gateway-methods plan now passes **1,685 cases in 292.82s** with a process-only non-Git temp root. After placing settlement in its lifecycle owner, the final real-writer policy/Stop suite passes all **8 cases in 38.80s**, and the attachment-setup selection passes **4 cases in 13.56s** (382 intentionally unselected). Independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. The complete five-file changed-check gate passes, including core plus all 25 core-test type graphs, lint, ratchets, dead exports and architecture/auth guards; separate Madge analysis reports zero cycles. New-head hosted gates are not yet claimed. One intervening compilation attempt executed no cases because newly written local proof metadata changed the compiler namespace; the frozen replay above is the valid run.

Both production adapters already register V2 (`attempt-stream-prepare.ts:478–527`, `run-attempt-active-turn.ts:529–569`); the registry deliberately rejects source-bound V1.
