title: feat(typesafe): support prepared Decision V2 batches
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connects TypeSafe to the prepared Decision V2 runtime while preserving V1 SDK callers and route-specific model capabilities.

## User Impact

Supported requests use the existing transport with prepared credentials. Hosted billing and token limits apply only to matching routes; custom endpoints do not inherit hosted assumptions. Automatic reasoning is supported; explicit on/off modes remain rejected.

The setup guide and package README distinguish matching V2 source development from packaged support. Released OpenClaw v2026.10.4 is V1-only. Packaged use requires a supporting paired host/plugin release; normal release synchronization aligns plugin API and build metadata.

## Current Integration and Proof

Signed head `3e56cc26f889f02d28dc8f45285f8d2e5ac6a639` integrates the frozen main revision `4ba34fdbb69fc1dbeafd93a2c946e362141ff0be` after GitHub reported actual conflicts in three TypeSafe transport tests. Main had extracted their registration and response/socket fixtures into `transport.test-support.ts`; this PR changes registration to V2. The resolution preserves that shared owner and invokes the existing intentional V1 wire-fixture bridge once from the registered V2 helper. Hostile accessor/serializer input still rejects with `DecisionContractError` before user code or transport runs. No assertions or production guards were weakened.

The native three-conflict successor and signed helper amendment produce the independently reviewed tree `5e4e9c6eb6d00e8cca8f5f11f04ec3ad67e9756e`. The final amendment is **test-only +4/-4, production unchanged**. Provider, API client/transport, manifest, live fixture and the repaired benchmark worker retain their prior reviewed bytes.

Fresh proof used frozen merged dependencies on Darwin arm64, Node 26.7.0 and pnpm 12.12.1:

- Four shared-helper consumer suites: **134 passed, 4 files, 0 skipped** (local, registered, remote and direct transport).
- Existing benchmark suite: **8 passed, 1 file, 0 skipped**, preserving exact B/C/S results, token usage, six-request reuse and broken-pool-close rejection.
- Actual compiled benchmark and two-request smoke passed; `responseBytes=714`, `socketsAfterPoolClose=0`.
- Targeted formatting, lint, root-scripts types and focused transport-test types passed. Normal signed precommit and independent scoped reviews passed.

[The remote attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39292071042) failed during provider readiness observation before any payload ran; its owned lease was stopped and joined. The documented trusted local fallback supplied the results above. The builder's clean-HEAD requirement and lint's retained build-owner lock were resolved through their normal contracts; only the blocked surfaces resumed, with the 142 passing tests preserved. No Linux result is claimed for this attempt; current-head GitHub CI supplies that broad proof.

Against frozen main, production/tooling is **+267/-24 (net +243)** across the TypeSafe registration/execution owner and benchmark consumer; tests are +992/-207, counted separately. The growth supplies prepared Decision V2 capability/execution and contract validation plus explicit benchmark lifetime ownership. The registered entrypoint and benchmark no longer use V1 readiness, untagged state or string-only context assumptions. Intentional V1 wire fixtures and codec coverage remain test-only. Sibling coverage includes the generic V1/V2 host integration, registered TypeSafe admission, four transport suites and benchmark fault/drain paths; the authenticated API proof retains its stated structural-response scope.

The earlier Linux benchmark proof remains at 9ed, integration proof at 2784, and authenticated mixed-batch API proof at unchanged 6ea provider bytes, as labeled below. Current-head CI, security and ClawSweeper remain landing gates.

## Earlier Benchmark Correction at 9ed96794

Signed head `9ed9679453d200ed29f9ff65ff657b4528b43ad9` repairs the registered-transport benchmark consumer exposed by [CI run 39238972922](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39238972922) and the exact-2784 ClawSweeper P2. The worker still expected V1 readiness, an untagged state and a string model after this PR registered a V2 provider. This was a PR regression; the failed CI is not waived.

The benchmark now obtains validated Kev model facts from the actual manifest through `normalizeModelCatalog`, calls the registered auth/transport hooks, passes tagged JSON and a typed V2 context, and owns a concrete active/server/signal/deadline admission predicate. It revokes that lifetime before draining the pool. This preserves the registered-transport component measurement and lazy-client boundary; no Gateway bootstrap or test-only V1 compatibility bridge was added.

Only `scripts/bench-decision-transport-worker.ts` changes from 2784: **production tooling +53/-21 (net +32), tests unchanged**. The growth supplies V2 prepared facts and explicit lifecycle ownership. Provider, API client/transport, manifest and live-fixture bytes remain unchanged.

[Remote proof run 39264381306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39264381306) verified the exact source tree `1ba69a4413c5862da66b155f1965069d0c8eedf2`, which is also the signed 9ed commit tree, with frozen Linux Node 24.19.0/pnpm 12.11.1 dependencies:

- Existing benchmark suite: **8/8 passed, 1 file, 0 skipped**, in original order.
- Exact B/C/S answers, token usage, wire body/no-Authorization, six-request connection reuse, first/warm/CPU measurement and broken-pool-close rejection remain asserted.
- Canonical `build-decision-transport-bench.mts` bundle and two-request native smoke passed; `socketsAfterPoolClose=0`.
- Targeted oxfmt, oxlint (0 warnings/errors), root-scripts tsgo leaf and normal signed precommit passed.
- Independent complete consumer/lifecycle review and scoped autoreview found no actionable issue. The sibling scan found no other stale registered V1 consumer; intentional V1 SDK compatibility tests remain intact.

The complete payload passed before the wrapper reported a cleanup timeout (overall exit 1). Native completion was settled, and the exact owned lease subsequently reported completed with no host. No proof was replayed. The prior 15+1 integration result remains attributed to 2784; authenticated API proof remains attributed to unchanged 6ea provider bytes below. The published 9ed head then encountered actual test-fixture conflicts; the current integration below supersedes that head for landing.

## Earlier Integration at 2784c24a

Signed head 2784c24aff28908701662698ed37de083c65417e integrates frozen main 7d487698114326ccdef13b68208886579f994560 through the native baseline-successor workflow. The sole conflict was adjacent imports in src/agents/decision-inference.integration.test.ts; both imports and both test groups are preserved. The actual full tree matches the independently reviewed resolution. TypeSafe adapter, client/transport, manifest, live fixture and admission fixture bytes remain identical to 6ea835ee; main's package release floors are retained.

Fresh proof on the exact successor, using the native verified source capsule and reconciled Linux Node 24.19.0/pnpm 12.11.1 dependencies:

- Full composed generic inference suite: **15/15 passed**, in original case order.
- TypeSafe admission integration: **1/1 passed**.
- Targeted oxfmt/Bun parity, agents-root tsgo leaf and git diff --check passed.
- Independent integration review and scoped P0-P2 autoreview found no actionable issue.

[Remote proof run 39237263780](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39237263780) completed the test/typecheck payload successfully. The overall wrapper returned exit 1 because its subsequent cleanup timed out. The installed wrapper's exact cleanup-success branch and captured streams distinguish that failure from the payload; a separate native status reconciliation confirmed the owned lease completed with no host. No test was replayed.

The authenticated API result below remains attributed to 6ea835ee, whose adapter and live fixture are unchanged. The successor requires its own hosted CI and exact-head ClawSweeper review; earlier green CI is not substituted.

## Earlier Fixture Correction at 6ea835ee

Signed candidate `6ea835ee97442de9122bdad7c438a3fc9e1ead6c` integrates captured main `cc271f85709b3bea38fffecfc1c53ebc9a404109` while preserving the original contributor ancestry. The admission fixture follows the current provider HTTP interception seam and retains its hermetic discovery, prepared runtime, revocation checks and cleanup.

Focused proof exposed a second fixture lifetime issue: the source-plugin SDK test released its prepared runtime between calls and rebuilt cold catalog state inside each 5-second deadline. Two unchanged same-order runs failed before HTTP. A bounded phase trace confirmed repeated preparation consumed the budget. The test now retains the exact prepared runtime across its assertions and disposes it before teardown; deadlines, both SDK results, rejection checks and request counts remain unchanged. This correction changes tests only (+31/-1 lines), with no production change.

- Focused admission: 1/1 passed, including admitted work after opt-out and final-I/O model/config/secret/caller revocation.
- Full generic inference suite: 11/11 passed in original order with the corrected fixture, including preparation and physical-provider deadline cases. The tested fixture blob matches this signed commit exactly.
- Local transport: 21/21 passed, including real loopback connection reuse for IPv4, localhost and IPv6.
- Formatting, diff checks, independent source/lifecycle review and fresh full-candidate P0–P2 review completed. The review's sole INDEX-only finding was resolved by staging the already-reviewed, tested lease fix; no additional code finding remained.
- A focused Testbox allocation queued before execution and was stopped/reconciled. Scoped proof used a task-owned normal checkout with its own frozen dependency install. [Exact-head CI run 39044661240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39044661240) completed successfully, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. The [fresh ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158565#issuecomment-5842271375) covers this exact head, reports zero findings and no before-merge action. Its native-hosted rank-up scenario is now completed by the exact-head live qualification below.

Historical feature proof includes 128 transport tests, registered-host integration, scoped types/lint, and a scoped package build. [Prior CI run38991854961](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991854961) at `4631018a` had only the attributed native-maintenance ratchet and aggregate failure; its separate repair was https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174962. This historical proof does not replace current-head CI.

## Native Live Qualification

Live qualification at `6ea835ee97442de9122bdad7c438a3fc9e1ead6c`: `extensions/typesafe/src/decisions.live.test.ts` passed (1 test, 1 file, 0 skipped). One mixed Boolean/Choice/Score text batch used the plugin-registered V2 adapter with `jev-latest` against `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`. Assertions validate the V2 response, answer kinds, and numeric input/output-token usage.

The source stayed unchanged. The source-reader and native test children joined, and isolated test state was removed. Credentials remained in private process pipes and memory.

This qualifies the registered adapter and external API using isolated prepared config/auth. It does not claim semantic answer correctness, installed-package loading, host SecretRef resolution, or deployed Gateway behavior. The unchanged-head ClawSweeper native-hosted rank-up move is complete; no rating-only re-review was requested.

Separate follow-up: compare the vendor's required-instructions documentation with requests omitting instructions before changing that input contract.

Accounting parent: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157492. Shared auth repair: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156799. Contributor ancestry is preserved.

## Current CI disposition

Exact-head [CI 39296200457/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39296200457) completed with 35 successful and 26 skipped jobs. The only failed root is [the baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39296200457/job/118209926735), plus its aggregate. CI is not green.

The failure is inherited from main: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177499 removed the ACPX backend mock without pruning its exact entry from `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`. The actual CI merge `3f460b2fcf125a6bb0ca12284ea2848d8c52362f` has ordered parents `459ef416e1161408d878d0b3b284693063f4b292` and `3e56cc26f889f02d28dc8f45285f8d2e5ac6a639`; the affected fixture, ledger, scanner/parser/resolver, package/lock/workspace, tsconfig and workflow are byte-identical to that main parent. title: fix(qa): reject history-bearing utility requests without session affinity
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes QA mock-provider requests with conversation history being accepted as standalone utility calls without session affinity.

Follow-up to #158452. That PR merged before its second review correction was published; this PR contains only the remaining history-isolation repair.

## User Impact

No shipped user-facing behavior changes. Genuine standalone JSON and memory-dreaming completions remain supported, while history-bearing requests cannot select shared anonymous QA scenario state after a session has been observed. No stored-data or configuration migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the dispatcher's existing Responses/Anthropic normalization and admit only the actual host-prepared utility shape: leading system/developer text, exactly one final user-text turn, no tools, and no retained response or conversation reference. Transport identity remains authoritative on the original request. Anthropic requests must also contain exactly one raw user message: normalization may discard thinking-only or empty prior turns, so the normalized projection alone cannot authorize the utility exception. Assistant history, calls, reasoning, earlier user turns, and outputs do not gain authority from a utility prompt prefix.

## Evidence

- Five registered HTTP-server regressions failed on the previous head: assistant history, function calls, custom calls, reasoning history, and an earlier user turn returned 200 instead of rejecting missing affinity.
- The local correction passed 32/32 focused tests, including 25 session-identity cases, real HTTP requests through the registered mock server, legitimate utilities across both wire transports, earlier tool-output regressions, and valid-affinity admission.
- All 26 selected changed-check stages passed on the correction: production/test types, lint, guards, dead exports, runtime cycles, and whitespace. The follow-up is a conflict-free cherry-pick onto main; all four changed files are byte-identical to the tested correction.
- Final refreshed-head test result is recorded in the publication follow-up. No live Codex or Full Release Validation pass is claimed.
- Independent local review remained unavailable: its bounded 120-second attempt timed out without a report. This is disclosed, not treated as a clean verdict; hosted exact-head CI and ClawSweeper review remain required.
- Earlier dreaming Gateway E2E results are historical, not fresh evidence for this head. Broader QA artifact-loading and runtime-pair proof gaps remain separate.

Initial publication head (superseded by the hosted-review correction below): 2d24e4d676ba41839d6d9e9216980375c8047ee7 on main b4d60fa5edfc2713a5cb3643fa1c936fec3c3cd0. The exact-head rerun passed **35/35 tests across three files**, 28.06 seconds Vitest / 30.33 seconds wrapper wall. This refreshed run selected Responses-input sibling tests; the earlier run selected input-extraction unit tests. Counts are not additive.



## Hosted review correction: raw Anthropic history

ClawSweeper's exact-head finding on `2d24e4d` was reproduced and repaired in `db75f5b7856a9d3956f6c9aefb8de4cedd5339c8`. The resolver rejects prior raw Anthropic turns before selecting scenario state; it does not change the wire adapter or valid transport-affinity handling.

Registered HTTP before/after observations (synthetic payloads; loopback host and port omitted):

| Request to POST /v1/messages after observing a session | Before | After | Final-effect proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Utility system prompt + prior assistant thinking-only turn + final user text, no affinity | 200 (incorrect admission) | 500, Missing QA session identity | GET /debug/requests is [] |
| Same request with prior redacted-thinking-only turn | 200 (incorrect admission) | 500, Missing QA session identity | GET /debug/requests is [] |
| Same request with prior empty user turn | 200 (incorrect admission) | 500, Missing QA session identity | GET /debug/requests is [] |
| Each history case with x-session-affinity: observed-agent-session | Existing supported path | 200 | GET /debug/last-request records sessionId: observed-agent-session |
| Genuine single-user JSON, dream-diary, and memory-incorporation utilities | 200 | 200 | Existing registered HTTP assertions pass across both transports |

Before: the three added HTTP cases failed on `2d24e4d` (expected 500, received 200); four existing Anthropic history cases passed. After: **38/38 tests across three files passed**, 24.29 seconds Vitest / 26.54 seconds wrapper wall. The session-identity file has 28 cases; new cases took 11, 8, and 8 ms. These are real requests through the registered local QA mock HTTP server, not live Anthropic or Codex model calls. This is an internal QA-only isolation correction, not a claim of a production user-data leak.

Command: `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.session-identity.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.responses-input.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.anthropic-failure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The loopback exclusion was necessary because the inherited environment proxy returned 502 before reaching the server; that fixture failure is not counted as the red regression.

title: fix(qa): cache stability validation rejects native Codex truncation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the large-tool-result cache stability QA scenario rejects valid Codex tool-history truncation when its output has no warning header.

Maintainer-authorized follow-up to Full Release Validation run 36073359097 and its [runtime-pair soak failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36073723162/job/107881722709). Publication for hosted CI and review was explicitly requested after the local review connection failure; this is not a request to merge or restart release validation.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Release validation recognizes genuinely capped Codex results while retaining positive truncation counts, read-call/tool/path correlation, fixture-content checks, and later prompt-retention evidence. No schema, timeout, budget, or migration changes; no user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native Codex history truncation emits `…N tokens truncated…` or `…N chars truncated…` without the separate formatted-output warning header. Accept that positive-count marker only in the correlated tool output. Existing OpenClaw cap markers remain supported. The regression executes the actual YAML assertion actions through the scenario flow runner instead of copying the predicate.

Directly inspected sibling Codex source at `d47e5cc0e2bbd35774dff15c83570519735d2ac4`: `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:156-168`, `codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/history.rs:570-581`, `codex-rs/utils/output-truncation/src/lib.rs:12-29,89-134`, and `codex-rs/utils/string/src/truncate.rs:131-136`. The dynamic handler returns content items; history truncation calls `truncate_function_output_items_with_policy` and `truncate_text`, not the formatted wrapper.

## Evidence

- Red: the unchanged scenario rejected both headerless native markers with `large capped read cache evidence was not observed`; the other 11 original cases passed. The scenario, runner, catalog, and test support remain unchanged between branch base `0e56c40dcf6d96c0ca5acb30b98ed835e31da2f5` and inspected main `b74bd07a2fb`. No matching existing repair PR was found.
- Green: 120 tests across the cache regression, scenario-flow runner, and scenario catalog passed before the final TypeScript narrowing fix. Final-source focused replay passed **16/16**, **11.71 seconds wrapper wall** (9.99 seconds Vitest duration); the 16 displayed case timings total **617 ms** (first case 584 ms, remaining cases 2–3 ms). Vitest attributes 75% to transform, 13% to imports, 7% to tests; compiler-cache preparation alone took 5.266 seconds. This is not an 11.71-second assertion body. Cases cover native token/character and formatted markers, existing caps, absent/malformed/zero counts, markers outside tool output, mismatched call/tool/path, absent fixture content, and missing later prompt evidence.
- Formatting, `git diff --check`, and import-cycle checks passed. The broader changed-scope run passed its guards and core typecheck, then found `TS18046` in the new test; final source narrows the unknown action before reading `set`. Final-source extension typecheck replay (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b tsconfig.extensions.projects.json`) passed; the full changed-scope run is not claimed green.
- **Review:** ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head on September 26 at 00:01 UTC: no actionable code findings, platinum patch quality, gold proof/overall because an actual runtime-pair result is absent. Final local autoreview remains blocked by proxy CONNECT 403; no local clean verdict is claimed.
- **Hosted CI:** [run 36202775211](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36202775211) completed **success** on exact head `34f3da3746f79304d60ef3ea72b30d5d62ff4829`; the PR `openclaw/ci-gate` is SUCCESS. The changed-extension shard passed; its individual test timing cannot be retrieved because the Actions log download is Forbidden.
- **Runtime proof attempt, September 26:** built this clean exact-head checkout with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build qaRuntime` successfully (44.5 s build phases), then ran the canonical single-scenario command below against actual built Gateway processes. The lockfile-managed released Codex binary is `0.155.1` (version probe passed). **Blocked before scenario execution / before the Codex cell:** QA channel polling received HTTP **502**, body `Secret egress proxy refused the request.`; its channel log reports `qa-bus /v1/poll: malformed JSON response`. A same-route native Node HTTP POST reproduced that exact response. No proxy, credential, allowlist, provider route, or assertion was changed. The blocked suite and its isolated Gateway were stopped.
- **Other permitted proof routes checked:** the configured Crabbox backend is Blacksmith Testbox; its read-only list request returned **Forbidden**, so no lease or workflow was started. The existing Release Checks and QA Profile Evidence workflow schemas, inspected at trusted-main `770a8d48871591e77c86df70cadbe34e7c6299b7`, do not expose a single runtime-pair scenario selector (release QA parity selects complete core/soak lanes; profile evidence selects whole profiles). No broad FRV/QA replacement was dispatched and no release priority was changed.

This attempt is **not** a passing runtime-pair result, live-provider soak, or release qualification; the requested platinum/diamond proof level is not claimed.

```sh
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 OPENCLAW_ENABLE_PRIVATE_QA_CLI=1 \
```

This canonical mock-provider lane executes real runtimes and would exercise the changed correlated request/output assertion; it is distinct from both the synthetic 16-case replay and live-provider inference. No code change or test-case deletion was needed for this evidence update.

title: fix(qa): allow standalone utility completions after observing sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: QA mock-provider runs reject standalone JSON and memory-dreaming completions after an agent session has been observed, even though those host-prepared utility calls intentionally carry no session affinity.

## User Impact

No shipped user-facing behavior changes. QA can exercise the utility completion and dreaming flows without assigning utility calls to an unrelated conversation. Agent calls still require transport identity after session observation; quoted utility text and tool-enabled requests do not bypass that requirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize the three existing tool-free system-prompt contracts at the mock session-identity owner. Do not recover conversation identity from prompt text. The registered-server regression covers accepted utility calls and rejected quoted/tool-enabled lookalikes.

This narrowly scoped fix is submitted for hosted CI and ClawSweeper review at the maintainer's explicit request after the local independent reviewer became unavailable. It is not a merge or release request.

title: fix: redundant catalog and local agent plugin registrations
body:
Related: #157568

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes redundant plugin registrations during provider-catalog refresh and local agent turns, and prevents a completed nested local command from retaining callable plugin callbacks.

## User Impact

Provider workers no longer load native-only harnesses or unrelated setup code. Local commands avoid an intermediate discovery registry, while native model inventory, CLI preloading, recipient/account selection, credentials, and resource cleanup retain their existing owners. No configuration, permissions, stored-data, or migration changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loader now records its actual scoped registration inputs together with the exact metadata inventory, including empty provider scopes. Catalog requests consume these facts instead of rerunning broad setup preparation. Local execution binds invocation authority to its already-admitted prepared registry and closes that authority when the command ends.

This replaces the earlier 42-file draft with a 13-file residual repair based on main. The shared inbound registry handoff already landed in #160658 and is not duplicated. The old eager HTTP-provider startup change, full-root borrowing manager, recipient-routing redesign, and supporting mechanical extractions are removed. The previous ambient-recipient finding does not describe this replacement: command preparation and CLI preaction are unchanged.

Requested by @RomneyDa; original incident reported by @hurtlovewow. Related catalog/capture regression work by @htuyer121 remains credited in merged #157300.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @RomneyDa](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/b1aeb723-16b1-4b62-a923-986563624022)
- [Catalog residual audit and implementation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/98e8f674-8181-4339-98bd-7098b867440f)

## Evidence

- Real provider-worker red/green: the baseline executed native registration and unrelated setup import/probes in the worker, producing four capture graphs; the candidate produced two. Native picker rows remained available from the parent. Existing provider-scope growth and request-local credential controls passed.

title: fix: long-running tasks fail to resume after a restart
body:
Related: #142224

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interrupted tasks can fail to resume after a restart when internal bookkeeping pushes their original request outside the loaded history window.

## User Impact

Interrupted work can resume from its existing request and completed tool results instead of failing with `Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn`.

No SQLite schema, migration, configuration, retention, or permission changes. Existing checks still reject completed or superseded turns. This repairs bookkeeping crowding out required history; it does not remove model-context limits or claim to resolve every recovery case in the linked issue.

A separate parent-completion failure remains in the real restart scenario and is also reproduced on the unpatched baseline; see the post-merge evidence below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The raw persistence window is not a complete record of which turn is current, and it is not the same as the model's conversation history. Recovery now uses the existing versioned reader to verify omitted active entries, including metadata without a message anchor, and matches the recovered original user. Model initialization uses the existing bounded model-context reader independently of raw bookkeeping.

Deliberately selected branches and resets keep their selected view. A selection or view change while the model history is being read rejects initialization rather than pairing one branch's messages with another branch's writer. The historical-user guard, exact user comparison, run ownership, and final replay-admission checks remain intact.

## Evidence

- Two incident-shaped cases using the real cache-snapshot producer fail before the repair and pass afterward. They verify an unchanged saved prefix, one original keyed user, completed tool results in their original order, and one resumed provider call.
- Four branch/reset cases fail against the initial candidate and pass after preserving selected views and rejecting changes during the asynchronous read. The eight-case SDK initialization file passes.
- Negative cases retain rejection after later/hidden users, genuine finals, foreign-run or unknown activity, resets, branch changes, replaced writers/sessions/lifecycles, and closed ownership.
- Fresh AutoReview of the final candidate: scoped-clean through P2; no accepted/actionable findings. The prior independent review's branch-selection finding is repaired and rechecked.
- Final candidate: **73/73 tests pass across three files** (78.58 s Vitest; 110.26 s runner wall including compiler preparation). CI timing will be supplied by the PR checks.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

### Additional real-Gateway Crabbox proof (post-merge, 2026-09-25)

**Saved-worker replay is repaired; the complete parent-delivery matrix is not green.** Separate Crabbox/Blacksmith leases ran built baseline `8133be64d156` and PR head `5c56fbf34f5f` through actual native tools, SQLite, public targeted restart requests, and real user-systemd process replacement. The model replies came from a synthetic loopback provider, not a live LLM.

| Runtime scenario | Baseline | PR head |
|---|---|---|
| 124 successful reads; internal snapshots push the saved request outside the raw window | Original same-run keyed-user rejection; 0 resumed provider calls | Same saved execution succeeds; 1 resumed provider call |
| 2-read short-turn control; request remains inside the window | Worker resumes successfully once | Worker resumes successfully once |
| Parent completion after successful worker recovery | Interruption/failure notice reproduced in the short control | Same failure reproduced in both controls |

Both long cases contain 1,052,374 raw bytes against the unchanged 1,024,000-byte window. Assertions verify one original keyed request, unchanged saved prefix, preserved completed results and HTTP tool outputs, no repeated tools, identical resumed execution identity, and unchanged schema/version. All fixture processes stopped and temporary services were removed. Both full `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build` builds passed.

**Remaining follow-up:** parent-completion handling across restart can report interruption even when worker replay succeeds. Its presence on the unpatched short-turn control establishes that this behavior was not introduced by this PR; these tests do not establish its root cause or rule out a later correction. Matrix exit status remains nonzero for that control. The earlier 73 focused tests cover additional boundary cases; they are not relabeled as full-Gateway or live-provider proof.

title: refactor: unify filesystem observation for reloads and refreshes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Consolidates the separate Config, development supervisor, Skills, and Memory observation engines so recovery and shutdown use one guarded filesystem contract instead of parallel Chokidar/native implementations.

## User Impact

Each workflow retains its validation, settling, source-selection, and cache/index policy. Notifications remain advisory: they never authorize reads or silently admit a replacement Root. Shutdown joins owned work and preserves genuine teardown errors without stranding independent resources.

**Dependent implementation draft—not ready to merge or install from the declared registry pins.** This needs [fs-safe #666](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/666) and a legitimate published version exposing /watch. Registry version 0.19.0 does not contain this feature; manifests deliberately do not pretend otherwise.

Native observation is limited to actual Node.js/Linux with trusted procfs. macOS, Windows, Bun, and other unsupported runtimes explicitly select polling by default. CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=false, 0, and empty values remain native-only and may leave observation unavailable on unsupported hosts. Package-owner acceptance of this platform/resource tradeoff remains a before-merge decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

fs-safe owns guarded observation, reconciliation, and physical retirement. Consumers retain accepted/rejected Config include policy, development-source filtering and trusted links, Skills discovery versus supporting-resource invalidation, and Memory dirty→settled→index ordering and host placement.

This removes direct Chokidar dependencies and superseded transports. Admission is bounded: Config four native workers, development four lifetime-pinned Roots, and Memory/Skills sixteen native workers each per process. Starting, retiring, and failed-close workers retain their budget. These are ceilings, not a performance-win claim.

## Evidence

Local qualification uses the immutable unpublished candidate 39c949e88e4de3381db008e8ab18e27faf0bce8d from [artifact 10863096644](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/36132581730/artifacts/10863096644). Both tarballs were integrity-checked; all 608 installed root-package files and two native-package files match. Installation used a temporary package-manager hook—not library patches, vendoring, or type shims. No hook or local artifact dependency is committed.

- Real Config registration ENOENT → joined close → retry → later native edit; genuine worker-termination failure prevents rearming. Canonical include-boundary retargeting cannot silently expand a cached admission. Real guarded-snapshot → source → automatic-poll cases cover both existing and missing files beneath a pinned directory alias, after the initial source read at readiness has completed.
- Real development-source link retargeting and later edits in native and autonomous polling modes.
- Skills entry→directory and directory/missing→symlink startup races: trusted targets are observed before availability, then later native edits reach the cached loader. Supporting create/atomic-replace/delete reaches sandbox copies without discovery invalidation; settling distinguishes observation loss from genuine cleanup failure.
- Memory committed-index replacement/removal/nested edits in native and autonomous polling modes without search/manual reconciliation hiding missed notifications; alias retargeting, dangling targets, and held selected-file settling.
- Real manager shutdown: independent cleanup after observation failure, provider retries, accepted sync work, retained database leases, and held remote transport retirement.

The canonical include handoff’s missing-file case takes ~0.5s; its first existing-file case included ~19s shared worker compilation (~21s total). Measured other local case costs: Skills native admission ~0.7s, supporting resources ~0.9s, Memory alias flow ~0.5s, manager cleanup ~0.05–1s, and committed-index filesystem cases ~8–10s each. Cold worker compilation is separate (~18s). Sixteen Linux subscriptions added ~269 MiB RSS and 112 active descriptors; joined close returned descriptors to baseline.

Whole-candidate AutoReview completed; actionable consumer findings were repaired. Independent scoped reviews found no new P0–P2 issues in the final Config alias and bootstrap corrections. Main integration exposed an extra initial Config invalidation that could supersede restart work: bootstrap reconciliation now retains the former ignore-initial behavior, while detailed startup activity, overflow, and later unknown invalidations remain actionable. The known dependency-release gate remains open.

Earlier focused qualification passed 88 Skills cases. After integrating main and resolving the overlap, 757 Gateway cases, 42 Config cases, 39 affected Skills cases, and all 128 CI routing/Windows inventory cases passed. Gateway wall time was 41.64s; Config was 10.51s. Production and changed-test lint passed. The original five-job/time bounds are unchanged, with all newly added main Windows cases retained; three additional OS-neutral helper/lifecycle files stay in Linux/macOS rather than the Windows list. Portable polling, path-policy, and Windows behavior coverage remains enrolled.

The held-scan/backpressure continuation reproduced both remote workers returning with accepted stdout writes still blocked. One bounded notifier now joins output independently from physical cleanup, preserves final availability ordering, stops admission on output failure, and handles reentrant shutdown. Native Config stop/replacement, native Skills/development shutdown, and real Memory polling scans held across stdout backpressure, EOF, and output failure now have direct proofs. The final affected run passed **73 tests across 11 files in 83.30s**; held-scan bodies take tens to hundreds of milliseconds. Independent continuation AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

**Source-bound local qualification:** code commit `c20b18568c81310af75ab3e6a7c58e6a09e42f26` passed full core and extension production/test typing, SDK export/surface checks, scoped lint, and the documented checkout-local full build (**6m 59.6s**) against the exact candidate artifact. The earlier service-identity refusal was not bypassed: this build used its ordinary checkout-local owner without changing Gateway identity or credentials. Installed artifact bytes were reverified (608 root-package files and two native-package files). This is artifact-bound proof, not a clean registry install. Integration is pinned to main `e124d77e00fadc6108ed5bfc0e57101a40151197`, not a moving target. Memory queue/provider ownership and guarded no-follow sampling are preserved; 23 Memory integration tests passed (45.12s), with Memory typing/lint passing. Earlier worker cases passed 4/4 and Gateway fixture typing/lint passed. The RPC runtime launch was refused by installed-service publication admission; no identity or service was changed.

**Remaining qualification:** clean installation from the declared registry pins and actual consumer macOS/Windows/Bun execution. The declared dependency does not export /watch; a compatible legitimate release must be pinned before that clean-install proof. This host is Linux without Bun or a desktop runtime. [Blacksmith run 36140098730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36140098730) previously lacked authentication to download the exact artifact; its lease was stopped and the unchanged attempt was not repeated. Platform proof needs an approved matching runtime/runner and supported artifact transfer or the released dependency. The package-owner platform/resource decision remains open.

## Contributor

@vincentkoc requested and directed this migration.

title: improve(ui): keep drafts usable while the Gateway reconnects
body:
Related: #152887

## What Problem This Solves

Reconnecting is easy to miss in Chat and New chat, while Settings makes its loaded content—and its connection explanation—inert.

## User Impact

Users get one nonblocking reconnect strip with **Retry now**, can keep reading and drafting, and can explicitly **Queue message** in an existing conversation. New chat explains why Start is unavailable without discarding text or attachments or automatically starting the draft when the connection returns.

The existing two-second grace, persisted outbox, incognito exception, permission/model/history restrictions, and exact-run Stop semantics remain intact. No API, storage, credential, or configuration migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell now presents connection state without treating the entire page as an unavailable action. Gateway-dependent writes stay gated at their existing page owners; local drafting, navigation, and preferences remain separate. Connection announcements have one shell owner, and mobile layouts do not add a second reconnect warning.

Requested and design-approved by @vincentkoc.

title: fix(test): avoid coauthor cleanup failures in fast CI workers
body:
Related: [canonical CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36124483652/job/108041446946)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes co-author fixture cleanup failing in thread-based CI and leaving its state-directory selector active for later tests.

## User Impact

Internal test routing only; production attribution, workspace resolution and database behavior are unchanged. The fixture now runs with the host-owned database broker required by its cleanup fallback. Existing cleanup custody and all assertions remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

All nine attribution assertions passed in the failed run, but cleanup of an exited native worker reached a host-only broker path from a reused Vitest thread. The rejected cleanup left the fixture environment selected; a later workspace-default test then observed that same fixture root.

Register this stateful consumer with the existing parallel infra fork owner and preserve its former unit-fast watch admission. Extend existing registry, explicit/watch routing and compact-planner checks so the file has exactly one appropriate owner. No new worker configuration, serial pin, retry, timeout, cleanup suppression or environment-reset shortcut.

The initiating reason native cleanup became unsettled is still unknown. This repairs the demonstrated host-capability mismatch, not every possible native cleanup failure.

Contributor credit: requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/89b333b5-710d-4f77-9a50-98477d15cf1f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0d269c5d-9227-44e0-8dc2-a1a4b228e3fc)
- [Independent review, integration and publication](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a6a286d2-db40-45b2-93f6-8fd4c516c20c)

## Evidence

- Controlled termination of the real native reclamation worker after test work reproduced the actual fallback: all nine attribution assertions pass, thread-based cleanup refuses host-broker admission, and the following workspace assertion observes the retained selector. The identical controlled boundary in a reused fork completes fallback cleanup, restores the environment, and passes all 11 assertions. This is fault-injection proof of the cleanup boundary, not a claimed reproduction of its original initiating cause.
- Seven routing assertions fail without registration. With the repair, 738 selected registry/planner checks passed in 37.41 s wrapper wall; 1,155 unrelated cases were filtered, not counted as passes.
- Uninstrumented registered-owner proof passed 21 cases: coauthor 9, workspace 2, prompt sibling 10. Combined wrapper wall 36.11 s including 17.77 s worker preparation; coauthor test-body time approximately 1.7 s. All production and fixture/test assertion source is unchanged.
- Full changed-file gates passed in 173.12 s, including root-test typechecking, formatting/lint, dead-export scans and selected guards. Fresh independent review through P2 found no actionable findings (13.51 s). [Hosted fixture job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36132619608/job/108066975566) passed all nine coauthor cases in the intended infra fork config. Its owning group passed 634 tests with 10 skips; the fixture appears in exactly one decoded group and is excluded from all three unit-fast groups.
- **Current merge blocker:** [ready CI 36132619608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36132619608) failed model-list inventory assertions and then cancelled remaining jobs. The discovery-lifecycle case returned no learned rows, and three freshness variants lost expected published rows. Source analysis identified the missing legacy-success discovery facts addressed by the existing [#158113](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158113). That owning repair still needs its own CI/review corrections and landing; no duplicate patch is being added here. Independent base-versus-PR execution attribution remains unproven, and passing fixture qualification is not a green CI claim. Completed exact-head ClawSweeper review found no code/security findings.

title: fix(packaging): accept frozen releases with their shipped MCP patches
body:
Related: #157531. Unblocks package qualification for #157972; does not change that candidate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Package Acceptance rejects a frozen release candidate when main has upgraded its bundled Chrome MCP dependency, even though the candidate still contains the exact previously shipped patched runtime.

## User Impact

No runtime or dependency change. Release operators can qualify supported frozen candidates without importing an unrelated dependency upgrade. Unknown versions, ranges, mixed versions and modified or unpatched bytes remain rejected; no acceptance gate is skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checker now selects the trusted 1.8.0 or 1.9.0 hash contract from the exact package dependency pin and requires the bundled manifest to match. All original file hashes, required assets, ESM and CLI checks remain intact. The other consumer—the node bootstrap producer—keeps its existing 1.9.0-only default.

The 1.8.0 contract comes from shipped v2026.9.6, commit eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b. It stays supported while a supported frozen target pins it, and retires explicitly with those targets. The candidate supplies neither its expected hashes nor an exception policy.

## Evidence

### Current qualification

**Merged at 2026-09-25 21:14:13 UTC as 4acdf1a4f3b835e115f5049b9eec90992c9a0f0d**, from exact hosted head 679f8e89d5ff748911e082cd96e4783913555e1e. [CI 36185669143](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36185669143) and its required ci-gate passed. The landed main delta is exactly the five packaging files; the unchanged carried #158115 fixture correction was already on main. Native closeout removed the PR worktree; all four required human co-author trailers and both work-session links were read back.

The exact-head ClawSweeper review artifact from [run 36186748701](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/36186748701) is complete, high-confidence and without code/security findings. Its archive and review-content digests were verified. The public review comment was still lagging, and native merge admission recorded recent-published-review/head and relevant-mainline-drift warnings under its ordinary policy. No admin or gate bypass was used; those warnings are retained rather than relabeled as clean.

The earlier failure and exact-base control remain recorded in the [owner report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158098#issuecomment-5831962415). A local check of the two fixture files stopped before Vitest at the runtime-publication admission guard, so it supplies no passing test count. No live Gateway was stopped, restricted environment file accessed, or guard bypassed. Required hosted CI is the qualification path. Native publication produced a carrier commit with the exact local prepared tree and retained all contributor trailers.


- [Original failed Package Acceptance attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36125974535): Code dee7003097dbfbfc7154b6bbe95e0458657cc8af / Tooling 8847d9661e913bb49e404887d2a9b573099fb447. Build and pack completed; integrity then reported seven MCP-version/hash errors. Upgrade scenarios did not run.
- The actual shipped openclaw@2026.9.6 tarball reproduced those seven errors, then passed the repaired ordinary integrity check in 51s. Its SHA-256 is 1a7355691bc0e605222ba818f1f72c1787253c78dfeb0df6be2086ec73b71e63; downloaded bytes matched registry SRI and all eight original 1.8.0 hashes.
- 62 contract tests passed (1.79s single-worker wall, 0.636s Vitest); 20 real packing/install integration cases passed (32.33s wall). A 30-case real-byte probe accepted both intact patched versions and rejected mixed, altered and pristine unpatched payloads. Integrated main replay: both files passed in 28.43s.
- Script/root-test types, targeted lint, formatting and single-file docs sanity passed on the prepared repair. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the five-file main integration is scoped-clean.

**Limits:** This does not qualify the rebuilt backport candidate or any upgrade scenario. The shipped npm artifact still fails the separate strict Docker check because it does not bundle the private workspace AI package; that gate is unchanged. No workflow dispatch, version bump, dependency change, release publication or deployment is part of this PR.

## Contributor credit

Prepared during the release-backport work with session contributors @RomneyDa, @vyctorbrzezowski, @steipete and @jalehman. Existing patched-runtime contracts and their upstream attribution are preserved.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/db4d78ac-b19b-4f64-adfb-0ca7973a62e4)

Startup and route-loading placeholders now show a gentle, visible two-second sweep in light and dark themes. Layout and loading timing stay unchanged, and reduced-motion users retain static placeholders. No configuration changes, dependencies, or migration are required.

The screenshot's owner is the initial connection splash, not the static preboot fallback or chat-panel skeleton. This uses the existing transform-only skeleton animation with a translucent text-color highlight scoped to the shared startup/loading surface. Other skeleton consumers are unchanged.

title: fix: delegated tasks incorrectly show human authors
body:
Related: #143080 and #22774

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes delegated tasks showing the authorizing person's name and initials as though that person wrote the agent-generated task.

## User Impact

Task authors, assigned owners, and human participants stay distinct. New delegated tasks show their actual agent author, while genuine human messages keep their person identity. Unknown authors no longer borrow the viewer's name or portrait. Existing saved labels are not rewritten, and this does not change session access, assignment, or execution permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway was correctly retaining human authorization for a synthetic request but incorrectly copying that profile into its sender label. The fix records the qualified agent author separately, keeps unknown synthetic input out of owner-authored memory, and uses one display-name resolver for task footers and settled/streaming reply attribution. Qualified task authors also use the existing bounded agent-avatar loader.

The earlier draft #143080 by @Neomail2 identified overlapping spawning-agent identity loss. Its fork is not writable by this maintainer identity and maintainer edits are disabled. This independently verified repair covers the visible-session reproduction and native admission without adopting that draft's separate ACP/internal-input-provenance changes; the broader draft is not closed by this PR. Hidden subagent transcripts retain their existing no-avatar presentation.

## Evidence

- The real `sessions.create` → initial input → SQLite regression fails on the original code: the generated task saves the human's ID/name and `senderIsOwner: true`, without qualified author identity. It passes after the fix for isolated and forked children, with human ownership and copied human history preserved.
- Native admission coverage proves execution authority is retained while agent/unknown transcript authorship is not human-owned. Explicit accepted-suggestion attribution remains first.
- Four reply-name regressions failed before the UI correction and pass afterward for current/other agents, settled/streaming replies, and renames. A separate avatar regression proves acquisition from `agent.identity.get`, not merely a preseeded render map.
- 565 focused tests passed; coverage-preserving extraction now places them across 15 files. The nine changed test files were also rerun individually on the published candidate. Scoped formatting, Oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex autoreview completed scoped-clean through P2 on the full candidate. Exact-head CI build/typecheck results will be recorded before landing; those are not claimed from the focused runs.
- The screenshots below use the actual Control UI in Chromium with sanitized mock-Gateway data. Both assert matching task/reply labels, unchanged assignment, and zero page errors; they are not live-deployment evidence. The pair has also been delivered to the originating discussion.

### CI follow-through

The first hosted run exposed a warm-reconnect alignment regression before the viewer is known. The correction keeps human alignment neutral until hello while agent-authored tasks remain peer-aligned; 238 renderer tests passed and independent correction review was scoped-clean. The local browser replay was blocked before tests by the loopback preflight, so hosted browser CI remains the verification owner.

The next run failed in the existing model-discovery lifecycle fixture, outside this attribution diff. Its tested merge contained a stricter inventory-retention contract, but the fixture omitted successful discovery provenance. The refreshed head includes the already-merged owning fix, #158115, without weakening assertions or adding retries. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36149377911) is running on `cdcc39407ce4a048e604c37f09478b3d14317c89`; merge remains gated on its result.

title: fix(release): recover stalled updates and preserve retained session data
body:
Related: #157531.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes selected failures that leave updates stalled, Gateways offline, or retained session data unsafe during recovery on the frozen 2026.9.6 source base.

## User Impact

Updates retain the previous runtime safely, Doctor completes restoration after interruption, retained databases stay held when deletion history is unavailable, and plugin reload/discovery failures report their actual outcome. The selected UI repairs restore live commentary and remove nested empty shells. Long-session indexing retains less payload data. Android queued messages retain pending branch reconciliation when a concurrent delivery drain retires.

The latest batch also protects setup authentication and transcript refresh on Android, prevents private input from being persisted or lost to automatic reload, and keeps native service control bound to current update ownership. Browser/visual and live-platform qualification is still incomplete; this PR is not release-ready from unit tests alone.

The source cut stays **eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b**. No re-cut onto main, release tag, artifact publication, deployment, or operator-state mutation. Package version remains **2026.9.6 pending explicit version-alignment approval**; this is not a claim of final 2026.9.7 release qualification.

## Why This Change Was Made

Port the explicitly selected merged repairs through the older baseline owners rather than import unrelated features/refactors. Preserve the stable-only predecessor-stop/systemd fixes and the rebuilt-native dependency pins. Two defects found in independent review were reproduced and repaired: an existing SQLite main store could evade the unknown-history hold, and a successful runtime restore could be destructively replayed after an authority post-check failed.

The memory change is a measured tradeoff: sampled indexing heap growth fell from roughly 200/204 MiB to 31/36 MiB on the same synthetic 196.9 MB fixture, with identical export hash. Full indexing was slower in those two runs (0.455/0.466s to 0.531/0.548s); no indexing speedup or total-memory bound is claimed. Metadata reset reads avoided large-payload parsing. ## Why This Change Was Made

- Catalog persistence moved to a versioned slot in #156535. Read through the catalog owner rather than the retired storage key.

title: fix(testing): honor Code Mode in live tool probes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes MiniMax M3 live qualification failing every tool-read attempt because the probe demands a direct `read`/`Read` interface while the model exposes Code Mode.

## User Impact

No production behavior, credentials, provider privacy settings, retry budgets, or pass criteria change. Native and Docker live qualification can exercise the actual advertised tool surface instead of requiring unavailable direct tool names.

## Why This Change Was Made

FRV run 36073359097, child 36073723162, jobs 107882724160 (native) and 107887638330 (Docker) both selected MiniMax M3 API-key and Portal routes, then exhausted tool-read attempts and correctly failed with zero successful models. The native replies explicitly reported `Tool read not found` and that `exec` accepts JavaScript rather than a shell command. The probe now requests the same file read and shell execution through the advertised interface, including Code Mode, without disclosing readback markers or weakening checks.

## Evidence

- Exact original responses inspected at frozen source `3e4adbb6763aa0befcefeab4a78bb9810f42870a`; both MiniMax failures are tool-probe/interface mismatches, not credential failures or successful skips.

- Existing live-harness contracts: 184 passed, with the two credential-gated live cases intentionally not executed locally; 66.33 seconds Vitest duration (transform 60%, tests 34%). This is contract proof only, not a live pass.

- Native MiniMax Gateway proof: run 36079841107, job 107901511857, completed the Gateway profiles execution step successfully in 153 seconds. This supports at least one selected route, not an independently re-read pass for both routes. The separately cited Docker run 36079892204/job107910547459 passed a different agents test in 140 seconds; **it does not qualify this changed Gateway probe and must not be used as Docker Gateway proof**. The original Docker Gateway failure remains unverified. title: fix: avoid false busy errors after failed plugin reloads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a manual plugin reload fails, the next plugin operation can report that another plugin/config operation is running even though the caller waited for the first reply.

## User Impact

Sequential manual reloads now reach their actual activation result instead of contending with a passive config reload created by the previous operation itself. Legitimate concurrent operations still receive the existing retryable busy response.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit plugin operations need a fresh source observation, not a synthetic file-change notification. Keep the new observation identity and cached snapshot together, while retaining genuine file/write work already pending when the manual operation starts or arriving while it runs. The existing test debounce override moves into its settings resolver so the oversized reload owner does not grow.

title: fix(update): preserve already-current updates and OverlayFS retention
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes package updates failing while retaining the updater on Docker OverlayFS, including an already-current update that incorrectly entered replacement after candidate admission.

## User Impact

Users can keep an identical installed artifact without unnecessary activation. Updates that do replace a package retain worker files safely on OverlayFS instead of failing on their own hard-link copy-up. No integrity checks, timeout budgets, or service-health checks are weakened.

This changes the installed updater; an already-running older driver does not gain these fixes from a candidate. Published-driver compatibility and candidate self-update are checked separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission staging forced replacement even after it resumed before the existing no-op check. Defer that decision to the admitted caller while preserving fresh-profile initialization and explicit replacement.

A real Docker probe showed that linking a lower-layer corepack file preserves dev/inode/size/mode/mtime but changes birthtime and ctime. Use the existing checked copy path on OverlayFS rather than ignoring fingerprint drift. Other filesystems retain hard-link performance. The end-to-end replay also exposed an absent-service no-op being reported as completed service-install maintenance; retain its stderr explanation without inventing a maintenance step. Actual reconciliation and foreign-service warnings are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Original Full Release Validation run 36073359097, child 36073723162, installer update job 107888715952: published 2026.9.5 -> candidate 2026.9.6 succeeded; the candidate self-update failed during updater-runtime-retention with `Plugin entry changed after snapshot inventory: /usr/local/lib/node_modules/corepack/CHANGELOG.md`.
- Dependent aggregate job 107890643252 failed only because UPDATE_CONSUMER_RESULT was failure; all six other dependencies succeeded.
- Exact failed step: Run installer update docker tests. npm package-install itself exited 0. The printed report's package-update step was the original error; restart-unhealthy followed as recovery verification in the intentionally service-free container. No separate failure-report artifact was uploaded by that consumer; the structured report is printed in its job log.
- Added staging-entrypoint and OverlayFS regressions failed before the fixes. Focused package update, retained runtime, and plugin-tree suites passed: 52 tests across four files.
- Changed test cost: package suite 1.30 s test time (4.63 s Vitest wall with cached workers); retained-runtime tree suite 0.16 s test time. Full focused invocation 42.09 s including cold worker preparation and the existing retained-worker integration suite.
- Fresh independent autoreview completed (P1 scope). Its sole finding was the OverlayFS regression’s Linux assumption; the test now explicitly mocks Linux and all seven retained-tree tests pass (2.89 s wrapper wall).
- Exact-head CI attached to 9e689b41e5765feb36a33ca33ded670cc0325b59: run 36078926279. Its main preflight/build/test jobs are intentionally skipped while OPENCLAW_RELEASE_PRIORITY_RUN=36073359097. The aggregate fails with “CI deferred while Full Release Validation 36073359097 holds hosted-runner priority”; the parent drain owns restoring priority. No CI rerun or priority override was attempted. This is not a green full-CI claim.
- The post-update finalization regression failed before its repair and all 54 tests in that existing suite passed afterward (40.69 s Vitest wall, 36.6 s test time; the added case reuses the suite fixture and takes about 0.6 s). This existing integration suite proves service finalization and recovery ordering; the new case exercises the real finalizer, not a reporting helper. Fresh follow-up autoreview was scoped-clean at P1.
- Core production and all 25 core-test type graphs passed; changed-file lint passed after correcting a fixture prototype; remaining planned guards passed. The follow-up core/updater test graph and lint also passed.
- Docker build and tarball integrity passed. Published 2026.9.5 -> candidate 2026.9.6 succeeded; candidate no-op preserved version/build identity. Final smoke rerun includes the absent-service report correction and remains running. The isolated harness hit inherited npm freshness policy first; the retry uses the environment isolation already proposed in #157683, without changing product policy.

title: fix(qa): Telegram validation fails after isolated auth staging
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Telegram release QA aborting before the first scenario and then failing cleanup after the isolated candidate takes ownership of its state directory.

Related: Full Release Validation 36073359097, Telegram child 36074502122 attempt 1, candidate job 107887785260 (frozen candidate `3e4adbb6763aa0befcefeab4a78bb9810f42870a`). Scoped repair/PR authorized by Dallin; no merge or publication requested.

## User Impact

No production Telegram behavior changes. The private QA harness can proceed past packaged auth staging and reach its existing verified shutdown/temp-root cleanup without reading candidate-private state. No permissions, launcher isolation, credentials, cleanup requirements, schemas, or installed-update behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher deliberately makes candidate state private to its separate UID. After packaged mock-auth staging, the parent calls `closeQaRuntimeStores` before starting the Gateway. Its unconditional shared-state close discovers a filesystem identity even when this parent never admitted that database, causing EACCES; final cleanup repeats the same operation and never reaches the existing privileged cleanup callback.

Close only shared-state identities already admitted by the parent lifecycle. Auth readers and agent resources still drain first, recorded native/worker resources retain their canonical close, idle coordinators still drain, and failed closes still preserve state for retry.

## Evidence

- Original implementation: new real-filesystem permission regression fails with EACCES from `inspectDatabasePathIdentitySync → resolveForNative → closeOpenClawStateDatabaseByPathAsync → closeQaRuntimeStores`.
- Repaired implementation: 31/31 tests pass across gateway-child artifacts and lifecycle suites. Extended existing subprocess fixture restricts traversal during auth bootstrap, reaches Gateway readiness, confirms process shutdown and sanitized artifacts, then invokes boundary cleanup while the state is still inaccessible.
- Existing coverage remains green for parent-exit non-recreation, sibling-store preservation, agent/shared close failures, retry, and cleanup failures.
- Combined focused run: 59.63 seconds wall (includes worker compilation); new permission test 5 ms, modified subprocess test 436 ms. Lifecycle file includes its preexisting 11-second failed-process termination proof; no new sleeps or process fixture introduced.
- Fresh Stable autoreview with lifecycle owner context: scoped-clean through P2. Core production typecheck, focused core/extension type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, and git diff checks pass. Final permission regressions pass 2/2 in 16.15 seconds wall after safe catch-variable cleanup.
- Broad root tsconfig is not a clean gate: it reports unrelated existing test typing errors (including Codex sessionFile fixtures and browser expect.element); canonical core production typecheck passes. No errors occur in the changed files.
- Original diagnostics limitation: boundary-evidence aggregation failed after the pre-scenario abort, so the workflow skipped uploading runtime diagnostics. The available candidate artifact is pre-execution, not a runtime log. Old source reproduced the underlying startup failure at `prepareAttempt` line 481 through the actual local QA child entry point (not just the cleanup callback); no original jobs rerun or cancelled.
- Not a full live Telegram qualification: no transport/API contract changed, so proof uses the isolated filesystem and real subprocess boundary; no production Telegram or credentials accessed.

title: fix: stale update receipts block valid updates
body:
Closes #167441

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Git updates and Mac update reconciliation being skipped, blocked, or reported incorrectly when saved update receipts are missing, stale, or cannot be written.

## User Impact

Valid updates use current installation state rather than requiring matching history. Live ownership, pause/profile policy, no-downgrade rules, and unresolved data-recovery protections remain intact. No schema, configuration, or retention changes.

An already-installed older updater still controls the first upgrade and may reject before this code runs; use the documented manual update method without deleting state or recovery artifacts in that case.

## Why This Change Was Made

Receipts describe history and progress, not permission to update. Git discovery, preview, and execution share the live-source resolver. Mac checkpoint writes are best effort, while operation-local results drive recovery; current-target pending work requests repair instead of vetoing it. Welcome delivery still requires a matching durable checkpoint. Optional install history is separate from the authoritative restart outcome.

Main's overlapping package/recovery fixes and shared startup-refresh owner are preserved. A missing remote ref now falls back consistently through refresh and actual update admission, without adding network work to admission.

## Evidence

- **Core integration:** 286 tests / 10 files passed, including shared startup refresh, Git admission/transport, receipt status, CLI dry runs and SQLite receipt recovery (wrapper times 113.33s + 51.78s). After the actual refresh → update.run regression was repaired, 75 tests / 4 files passed in 90.91s. Counts overlap.
- **Static checks:** 24 affected TypeScript files lint clean; production and all 27 test type graphs passed on the integrated candidate, with affected infra/Gateway graphs rerun after the admission repair. An interrupted aggregate is not claimed as an aggregate pass.
- **Native correction:** current head `c54816ba67b9330f120c13dc4d771244437aaa7c` restores established production profile-state resolution and repairs the relocation fixture under the existing isolation lock, including explicit service-hosting policy. Independent P0–P2 review is clean. Pinned SwiftFormat passes; Linux SwiftLint is only partial evidence because three SourceKit rules cannot run there.

title: fix(codex): show repeated ultrafast policy warning once per chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Codex System warnings about an unknown `ultrafast_mode` requirement, including several identical notices stacked before one response.

## User Impact

The same diagnostic is shown once per OpenClaw chat session across notification bursts, later turns, retries, native reconnects, and replacement native threads. New chats and actual resets receive their own first notice. Other recurring policy/security and operational warnings retain normal delivery.

This fixes duplicate presentation, not Codex feature support or enterprise policy. No dependency, feature enablement, or database schema change is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native startup warnings can arrive through both configuration and thread notifications. A receipt/connection-local cache cannot enforce chat-session scope. Successful projection now records a hash in existing plugin-owned session state, bound to the session ID and lifecycle revision. The canonical session writer serializes overlapping delivery; its existing worker path keeps receipt reads and writes off the Gateway thread. The earlier transport-local acknowledgment implementation is removed.

Durable receipts survive Gateway restart. Incognito follows its existing process-lifetime contract. Failed projection can retry. Storage failure or a crash between projection and persistence can permit a repeat rather than hide an unseen warning. State is bounded to 256 diagnostic variants without eviction; additional variants remain visible but are not remembered. Private diagnostic text is not stored in receipts.

title: fix(update): unblock source updates after interrupted compiler cleanup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes source updates staying blocked after interrupted compiler cleanup leaves an artifact-ownership fence, even when the qualified native work has completely settled.

## User Impact

Supported Linux, noninteractive, one-shot source compiler runs can recover an interrupted fence release only when native identity, complete descendant settlement, unchanged inputs and the original lock generation are proven. Unknown custody and legacy identityless fences still refuse with inspection guidance; PID death alone never permits reclamation.

Darwin/Windows, TTY, watch/API/LSP, metrics/preload, generic callback and service-delegating paths retain ordinary explicit release without a recovery certificate. Configuration, history, databases and existing dist outputs are not reset. Integrated compatibility with the published 2026.9.9 source updater remains an external proof gate, not a completed claim.

Native preparation adds overhead separate from compiler work: recent cold samples were 3.9–4.1s, warm preparation 1.84s (852 inputs, 3 outputs), and earlier cold samples 3.8–15s. These are observations, not guarantees. Metadata-only and source-preflight paths do not prepare this runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing artifact owner with process-birth/boot/PID-namespace identity and generation-bound custody. Reuse the compiled Linux subreaper for the fixed compiler entry; require native extinction, drained output, unchanged launch inputs and current lock authority. Recovery checks that the original owner retired and uses fs-safe’s final byte comparison. Generic declaration consumers keep their source graph without loading the optional native bootstrap. Retained ownership emits one actionable diagnostic while preserving raw causes and unexpected filesystem/preparation details.

The new opt-in source-update harness installs immutable published source, uses canonical OS-account state paths in independent COW containers, and records installer-created state without deleting it. Four planned cells cover legacy/escaped-descendant refusal, healthy active update with configuration/history preservation, and stopped/no-restart intent. The fixture uses a real Gateway with a synthetic service-manager adapter; actual Docker execution is still unrun.

The existing generic Docker cleanup owner now retains unresolved container IDs and mounted package inputs after removal failure, including caller cleanup outside logging subshells. Primary failures/timeouts and caller traps/file descriptors are preserved. Seed operations use a private immutable CID; uncertain commit/removal is not automatically retried. Build, logs, wait, commit and cleanup consume absolute budgets. The 270-minute lane and 285-minute outer job are upper envelopes, not measured runtimes. No competing reaper, release, credential, permission, dependency-pin, schema/version or live Gateway change is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real source/native boundary: the pinned baseline refused the interrupted-release fixture; the fixed native entry admitted it while preserving the prior dist sentinel. Linux controls cover escaped independent-stdio descendants, cgroup migration, killed controllers with live descendants, missing/changed settlement, output drainage, cancellation and changed source. PID-reuse/foreign-generation races are modeled, not claimed as forced kernel PID recycling.
- The update adapter refuses before Git mutation or service stop, preserves the owner/cause chain, and avoids repeated stale-lock display fragments. Unexpected inner EACCES and lease cleanup remain covered.
- The unmodified published 2026.9.9 guard/config closure (12 source files and three original manifests) rejects the former per-cell paths and admits canonical OS-account paths. This native guard proof performs no service mutation and is not Docker/installed-CLI acceptance.
- Controlled daemon-boundary proof: the old cleanup owner returned success and lost CID/input after failed removal; the candidate fails and retains both. Forty-eight status/removal/CID/direct-or-subshell combinations and deterministic deadline checks pass. Four source-shell negative cases retain custody without an aggregate success summary.
- Independent reviews completed. The focused correction review found one P2: normal seed cleanup used the work deadline. It was reproduced, fixed at the existing owner call and verified red/green near cutoff. The original findings/incorrect receipt is retained, not relabeled as a clean post-fix review. Lead qualification found no additional actionable P0–P2. No UI behavior changed.

**Remaining qualifications:** selected checks still fail on the unchanged inherited Knip export `observePlacementAuthority`; script exports pass, but the aggregate is not green. The earlier successful full build reported an unattributed nonfatal startup-JS gzip warning (+297B); no baseline UI rebuild was performed. Hosted run 37777739361 at `fd84900b` completed with 75 successful, three failed (two UI jobs and aggregate), and 23 skipped jobs; the previously failing Node siblings passed. The 14 UI failures are maintainer-reported baseline failures ([reported baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167171)); this task has not verified a raw baseline replay. These are prior-head results, not passing CI for this harness update. ClawSweeper’s prior-head review found no code defect but requested published-source compatibility evidence. Current-head CI/review and actual source-update acceptance remain open; no readiness completion is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Validation scope and measured cost</summary>

Focused tests use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs … --maxWorkers=1`, the same runner as `pnpm test` without dependency reconciliation. Local wall times are not CI timings.

- New Docker custody suite: two tests covering 48 combinations plus clock/deadline checks, 3.33s wall; no daemon or Gateway boot. Source-shell negative proof: 0.468s; near-cutoff red/green separately verified.
- Changed Docker helper siblings: 17 selected tests, 31.78s including native test-worker preparation; the entire large helper file was not replayed. Observability sibling: all 11 tests, latest 2.95s wall. Hosted seconds for these changes are pending.

Full scripts lint: 1,333 files, zero warnings/errors, 39.1s; five-file typed test lint: zero warnings/errors, 7.2s. Earlier script types (14.01s), unchanged package/SDK/lock guards and 93 planner tests are reused. Knip remains qualified red.

- Earlier canonical full build: exit 0, 236.26s, including declarations, native/lazy bootstrap checks, plugins, SDK and UI. It preceded the diagnostic-only follow-up; no new full product build or all-platform matrix is claimed for this harness update.

Proof uses synthetic isolated data. The opt-in Docker cells have not run; resource/ref/source admission and explicit dispatch remain separate from publication.
