## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update verification and repair can report recovery while a reachable Gateway still has a starting/disconnected channel, configured-plugin error, event-loop degradation, or unavailable child runtime.

## User Impact

Health reports distinguish `reachable`, `starting`, `ready`, `degraded`, and `failed`. Update and repair verification consume that observation instead of accepting a PID, port, or successful RPC alone.

Compatibility is preserved: `health.ok` still means RPC success; health-command exits, diagnostic status/`--require-rpc` semantics, and HTTP liveness/startup/admission behavior are unchanged. Ordinary standalone lifecycle commands retain correlated authentication/pairing-rejection liveness and report non-ready observations as warnings. The shipped updater marker selects strict verification without requiring a new flag from an older driver. No configuration option, protocol version, storage schema, or migration changes. The health owner projects recorded startup, admission, channel, plugin, and runtime facts into one typed result. RPC/cache publication refresh live observations after awaited collection without new database scans or another admission owner. body:
Related: #154636

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update and repair appear silent during long Doctor integrity checks because parent processes buffer progress until completion.

## User Impact

Bounded stderr progress preserves terminal JSON stdout. Quiet suppresses progress, not completed advisories. An older updater may still buffer candidate output; the fixed updater must own that boundary.

**Not ready for review:** current-head CI passed, but installed repair/quiet/migrated proof is **NOT RUN**. The reported Docker capability gap remains independent of successful local/package proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh Doctor owns allowlisted progress; migrated finalization keeps canonical Buffer forwarding, cancellation-tail and terminal-output ownership. The outer projector is removed. Diagnostics remain redacted/marked at 16 KiB/stream; clipped output cannot prove whole-stderr assertions.

Redundant forwarders are removed with stable paths/bindings/consumers retained. No task-authored dependency/SDK/cap/activation/schema/retention/permission change; frozen-main dependencies were admitted normally.

Required cases restore published schema-19 state after writer quiescence and observe actual quick_check/integrity_check with native holds/heartbeats. Finalization separately proves target/run identity, release ordering, handoff, sessions and terminal JSON; no second check beneath a finalizer skipping healthy migrated stores. Outer streaming tests are separate proof.

## Evidence

Capture stops after unresolved cleanup, preserving both errors and its owner. Wide tables stay contained; dense content scrolls. The task repair adds no retention, permission, activation or SHM changes; diagnostics remain best-effort, without online-backup substitution. title: fix: avoid foreign-listener race in Gateway acquisition proof
body:
Related: #166883 (release-branch fix, now forward-ported to main).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway acquisition validation can fail after correct fixture cleanup when an unrelated listener occupies the released TCP port.

## User Impact

User impact: no production or user-visible behavior changes. Automated validation now checks the fixture's own reservation rather than mistaking a foreign listener for its Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward-port the exact test-only fix from #166883 onto main. Observe the reserved server directly, exercise a real competing listener through stop, and preserve both independent cooperative port-claim checks and post-cleanup reacquisition. No runtime changes, retries, or timeout increases.

## Evidence

Validated on main baseline `301e372903de4e9e04e17da018a1ac2ffdb4c2ff` with this patch:

- Before: a controlled real competing listener makes the original acquisition assertion fail with expected `busy` to be `free`. The fixture and listener were cleaned up; the control was removed afterward.
- After: `pnpm test test/helpers/openclaw-test-instance.acquisition.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 18 passed; 8.01 s wrapper wall time with cached compiled workers; changed scenario 37 ms.
- Sibling: `pnpm test src/test-utils/ports.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 20 passed; 6.66 s wrapper wall time.

- Fresh independent P0 autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. `git diff --check` passed.
- Scope: one test file, +37/-5; production delta 0. Patched file is byte-identical to the release fix (blob `a740fc28048a11e4ad411cd77ac2c3b11158a010`).
- Hosted [CI run 37722501015](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37722501015) passed on exact head `aa6157bee0b1da514ab0b1e4ac8753d53e56e3ff`; all 46 jobs finished successfully or were intentionally skipped, and `openclaw/ci-gate` is green. In [the changed-test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37722501015/job/113133393856), the changed scenario took 31 ms; its containing 13-file lane took 118.62 s (not per-file or incremental PR cost).
- ClawSweeper follow-up: **20/20 additional standalone acquisition-suite runs passed**, 18 cases each (360 test-case executions). Wrapper wall times were 6.06–28.23 s. The existing 20-passing-case port-owner sibling result remains valid.

Each replay accounted for all 56 files: **1,240 passed tests and five reported skips**, with zero failures. Source and test-owner coverage were checked explicitly; no source changes or assertions were weakened.

title: improve: show useful Telegram and Discord progress by default
body:
Related: #101656

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running Telegram and Discord requests can look idle: Discord defaults to no preview, and quiet progress can show only “Working” even when an operation or delegated task is active.

## User Impact

**Maintainer direction:** @obviyus requested useful default-on Telegram/Discord progress without another configuration option and explicitly requested landing on October 8. Changing Discord’s omitted-setting default is intentional; explicit `off` remains the opt-out. The small additive compositor/dispatch inputs support these channel adapters without another state owner or new configuration.

Telegram and Discord show useful, bounded work status by default without enabling detailed tool logs or relying on a model-authored preamble. Discord now defaults to the existing progress mode. Explicit streaming modes remain unchanged; `off` disables previews. No new configuration option, dependency, or data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared progress compositor now supports safe current-operation and delegated-task status on these two channels, excluding command arguments, outputs, and private child prose. Discord transfers only confirmed draft custody to the existing subagent continuation owner, so a yielded parent and queued follow-up cannot erase or take over the retained card. Optional/silent turns remain silent, and transport admission and retries recheck current authority.

Discord’s established durable verbose-commentary behavior is preserved: the draft yields commentary/narration to durable delivery when verbose visibility is active, while bounded operation status stays available. A discriminating owner regression replaces the duplicate mocked verbosity variants.

Other channels retain their presentation. Answer streaming remains a separate choice through the existing modes. This does not promise periodic model narration or change the existing generic yield acknowledgement when previews are explicitly disabled.

## Evidence

**Scoped visual waiver:** On October 8 at 04:38 UTC, @obviyus explicitly waived Discord-only client screenshots, retaining the verified Telegram screenshots and passing real leased-guild Discord/REST evidence. The QA bot-pair fixture has no authorized human Discord client. This waiver does not cover other review, test, authority, or merge gates.

- Red/green regressions cover default progress without a preamble or detailed log, private-argument exclusion, late operation completion, child status, optional-turn silence, retained custody, queued-turn cleanup, authority revocation, and retirement during native rate-limit retry.
- 235 focused dispatch, queued-turn, Discord REST/process, and Telegram HTTP tests pass. The separate 52-test compositor/snapshot set also passes; final mechanical changes were rechecked with 156 passing tests.
- Core and extension production/test typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, SDK surface checks, generated configuration checks, and affected safety/boundary guards pass. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings.
- **Real Telegram Test Server userbot:** default mode and progress with detailed tool logging disabled show “Working / Exec: running” during a real 18-second command; explicit off emits no progress message. All three cells record one final reply and completed canonical cleanup. Baseline default showed only “Working”. These are live transport observations, not client screenshots.

**Additional real-channel proof:** Telegram Test Server userbot exercised accepted isolated spawn → parent yield → same-card child running/completed → one matched requester-settlement final, with 68.6 seconds of post-settlement observation and no private-child leakage. Cancellation after visible progress removed the card with no late final/update. Three injected HTTP 429 responses (`retry_after:5`) on the live final-delivery path retried to one final and cleanup. Real leased Discord guild recordings passed default, explicit off, and detailed-logging-disabled cases: default/no-detail showed current operation, then last activity, then one final and card deletion; off had no progress messages. All completed cells released their leases/listeners and cleaned their credential scratch.

**Landing correction:** Restored the shipped durable verbose-commentary contract identified in review (#121009), without changing default progress, retained custody, or optional-turn privacy. The regression failed on the previously published source and the corrected Discord draft/REST suites passed 48/48 (10.96s wall); extension production/test types, scoped lint, format, line-cap ratchet, and independent P0–P2 correction review passed. Earlier no-verbose live behavior and screenshot evidence remains applicable; it is not relabeled as live verbose-path proof.

**CI oracle correction (`d44b90f04fd`):** Current-head CI run 37729168398 at `588ca691` exposed a stale QA expectation, not private child-output leakage: the private-completion fixture recorded exactly two accepted same-target sends, the new bounded “Working / Last activity: Sub-agent” kickoff and “Worker started.”, with no child nonce, media, or private result. The scenario now accepts only the exact fixture-specific Sub-agent running/last-activity HTML strings on Telegram; counts, targets, attachments, transient edits, protected nonce/media/NO_REPLY, chronology, and restart assertions are unchanged. No production code changed. New oracle cases failed on the old expectation, then 25 oracle/chronology tests and 14 Discord Doctor tests passed (39 total; 22.98s wall across two shards, QA shard 3.84s). Independent scoped P0–P2 review was clean. The actual `qa run --qa-profile smoke-ci --scenario subagent-completion-direct-fallback` entry point passed all visible, silent, fallback, private, and restart cases in 42.963s using the real Telegram plugin, local Crabline provider, and disposable Gateway—not an external Telegram-service claim. Private completion produced zero terminal sends/attachments and two matched private spawn receipts; no restart replay occurred. The isolated QA runtime build passed (44.8s). Full production/test typechecks and affected guards passed; scoped lint had zero warnings/errors, and import-cycle/format checks passed. The previously documented unchanged unused-export failure remains. The failed CI attempt is retained as failed. Exact-head CI run [37731360735](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37731360735), attempt 1, passed for `d44b90f04fdf3169828802f87efaadb860a2db7f`, including all four QA Smoke profiles and required CI/security gates. Profile 4 took 294 CI seconds including setup/build/all assigned scenarios; the three extension-bundle jobs took 284/311/274 CI seconds including their other files, not individual test costs. Fresh exact-head ClawSweeper review completed with no findings or before-merge items.

**Upgrade compatibility / review disposition:** No database schema, stored-state shape, or migration/backfill is added. The flagged `config-ui-hints.ts` change is help text; `doctor-contract.ts` changes only the existing alias resolver’s omitted-mode fallback to the intentionally approved progress default. The 14 passing Discord Doctor tests exercise legacy boolean false → explicit off, explicit modes, inherited account/root streaming, delivery-only legacy aliases, and unchanged canonical configurations. Explicit opt-outs remain preserved. This addresses the automated “data-model compatibility proof” request without inventing a stored-data migration.

**Remaining live coverage:** Discord child/fault combinations and automatic background-exec wakes remain untested live. The Telegram provider-503 cell observed truthful last-activity status during retries, but its 65-second window ended before terminal error delivery. Existing REST/HTTP tests provide narrower lifecycle/fault coverage, not a claim that those live gaps passed. Native landing verified on October 8 at 05:25:53 UTC as `e9c58e9c54cfaa27352bcdd90401c6ec3b84e627` on `main`; the landed tree matches the reviewed head composed with its actual main parent.


### Actual Telegram client — before / after

Official Telegram Web K on the Telegram Test Server, light theme, identical 1280×900 client viewport and request. Baseline `b300e0e` compared with published head `4cc2f48c`. These are inspected, losslessly cropped real-client screenshots, not reconstructed chat images. All 19 changed runtime files matched the published source. The separate 45-second visual fixture leaves the original 18-second live behavior evidence unchanged. Temporary GUI authorizations were revoked and both canonical runs cleaned up.

**Known check/build limitations:** the unused-export check reports `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts: readRecommendedModels`; independently reproduced unchanged on the pristine base. An isolated private-QA build completed before the final generated inventory refresh; the subsequent refresh build stopped in the workboard asset phase, so exact-final full-build success is not claimed.

Baseline: `b300e0edea5e3e1b0aee58a33e188711380d8e22`. Published head: `4cc2f48c39cc756ed90744a95889648e8e75a3f7`; its tree is identical to the reviewed/tested tree. All 33 candidate manifest file hashes match the published checkout. The live-child verifier initially rejected the new intended status strings; its verdict was recomputed offline accepting only three exact synthetic status texts, retaining the original verdict and all identity/privacy/settlement assertions. Focused tests ran through the repository Vitest wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`: 235 tests across five files / three shards took 103.72 seconds wall time (48.51s core, 8.55s Discord, 43.81s Telegram, including compilation). ## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

title: fix: prevent completed conversations from resuming after restart
body:
Closes #166300

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users updating or restarting a Gateway could have a completed historical conversation resume, run tools, and send an unsolicited reply. A legacy failed-recovery row could retain an unmatched runtime fence after its execution and delivery owners had been cleared.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery now distinguishes retained evidence from permission to execute again. A terminal row with only an unowned runtime fence is preserved behind a quiet, zero-attempt recovery tombstone instead of becoming a fresh executable cycle. Startup marking and foreground admission use the same owner-level classification.

This does not guess completion from an assistant final or session age, discard unmatched fences, or change the transcript resume policy. Existing recovery cycles, runtime/writer identities, harness-completion ownership, pending finals, and delivery claims retain their recovery behavior. No schema or configuration changes.

The refactor consolidates the two recovery inspectors and duplicated foreground-claim guards, removes the redundant rollover-eligibility layer, and keeps outcome policy in the existing state owner rather than introducing another production module.

## User Impact

Completed legacy conversations no longer restart themselves from ambiguous leftover state. The original transcript, timestamps, and recovery evidence stay intact, without a new message or notice. If continuation is needed, the existing **Resume in new session**, **/new**, or **/reset** paths remain available.

The intentional tradeoff is that this narrowly identified ambiguous legacy state requires explicit recovery instead of ordinary in-place input. Genuine interrupted work and owed replies remain automatically recoverable.

Reported by @hannesrudolph.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @hannesrudolph](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/7f4e0815-6051-4e36-bd19-165f3ceb3287)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3e18d29a-91d2-4bf1-acfb-44603aef2326)

The net-negative follow-up was implemented and verified in the original discussion session linked above.

## Evidence

- Before the original fix, ordinary and Codex-mirrored completed-final startup cases each dispatched a new turn. The regression cases now verify zero dispatch, zero recovery notices, unchanged transcript/timestamps, retained evidence, and stable repeated scans.
- **216,000 generated before/after transition comparisons** matched the previously published fix, including returned results and state mutations for inspection, observation, adoption, and foreground binding/validation/release across current and stale generations.
- **116 fresh tests passed after the refactor:** 113 recovery/state/startup/claim-lifecycle tests across seven files, plus three public sessions.recover cases. The public cases passed both before and after removal of the redundant helper: absent tombstones are rejected, and repeated recovery reuses its existing successor.
- One helper-only rollover test was replaced with public-boundary coverage; the actual legacy replay regressions and legitimate-work controls remain. The initial candidate's 12 additional selected runtime controls passed previously; they were not rerun in this refactor pass.
- Measured wall times: the seven-file recovery run took 105.63 s; the public recovery selection took 58.12 s before (cold compilation) and 25.19 s after (warm). These are test-cost observations, not a performance comparison. The public selection includes three passing cases and 21 intentionally filtered cases.
- The complete affected-path changed-check run passed against pinned base 51f772aeefbcf0d10a62f65d13eec2591363fb6d: production typechecking, all 27 core-test type graphs, targeted lint, formatting, dead-export scans, and the applicable ownership/schema/import-cycle guards.
- Fresh independent pre-commit review of the entire candidate and unchanged owner contracts completed with no P0–P2 findings. The reviewer inspected tests rather than running them.
- The legacy fixture was generated from the source-extracted July fail_recovery transition and cleanup at d111bef0eed5aefb1e7c5ac59801c1f0924495f1, with source blob identities checked. The precise original July production interruption is not claimed as proven.
- Direct Codex dependency inspection: [completion handling](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1321-L1348) and [completed versus interrupted turns](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1501-L1557). The fix remains provider-independent.

**Production delta: +118/−145, net −27 lines** relative to the original base 51f772aeefbcf0d10a62f65d13eec2591363fb6d (previous candidate: net +61). Tests/fixtures: +269/−45, net +224; docs: +9. The complete PR remains net positive because it retains regression coverage.

Proof uses isolated SQLite/startup and public-handler execution with mocked dispatch, not live provider/channel traffic or an installed-updater run. The full repository test suite was not run. Before merge, recovery-owner acceptance of the documented foreground restriction and published-driver-to-candidate upgrade evidence remain outstanding; this PR stays draft.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reorder grips and color markers crowd or overlap icons when opening the mobile Control UI sidebar with pinned sessions and plugins.

## User Impact

Pinned sessions, plugin navigation, and group headers have clear spacing on phones without hiding navigation or management actions. The drawer width and desktop layout stay unchanged; existing session action menus retain their 44px touch targets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mobile overrides reduced the session inset to 2px and the icon-to-label gap to 4px, putting glyphs into the color-marker gutter. The navigation reorder button also squeezed a 16px grip into an 8px leading target.

Restore the shared desktop session spacing and give mobile reorder controls their own 24px trailing slot beside the other actions. Nested plugin sections keep the control aligned with their parent row. This trades a small amount of title width for separated controls instead of widening the drawer.

## Evidence

Actual Control UI, deterministic mocked Gateway data, dark theme, 390 × 844 CSS-pixel viewport. No private session content is included.

- Mobile: 320, 390, and 768px viewports with coarse and fine pointers; glyph/marker clearance, grip containment, separate pinned-session menu targets, touch and keyboard reordering, and group collapse/expand all pass. Existing title/menu drilldown cases also pass.
- Desktop and nested plugins: four Systems/Workboard alignment cases at 390/1440px pass; the plugin reordering/persistence test passes. The bundled UI built successfully (28.16s).

title: fix(ui): terminal disappears when docking from bottom to right
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a terminal disappears from an existing chat when moved from the bottom dock back to the right, then unexpectedly appears on **New conversation**.

## User Impact

User impact: **Dock to right** returns the same running terminal and its retained output to the currently selected existing chat, without opening a replacement shell. The global bottom dock remains visible across chat navigation, and existing destination tabs remain intact. Docking controls are temporarily disabled while a terminal is opening so a connecting tab cannot be left behind. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

Exited terminal tabs now retain their diagnostic output, exit metadata, and selected presentation in both docking directions; they are not reattached to a dead PTY.

## Why This Change Was Made

The global bottom dock and a chat's right-hand panel have different presentation owners. Switching only the global dock's geometry leaves it hidden on chat routes. This change transfers the existing sessions through their shared intent owner, retires the old presentation, and explicitly activates the destination even when its pane is already mounted. The selected terminal stays selected. Exited emulators move as document-local presentation state, while live sessions use the existing attach path. The queue owns pending transfer cleanup and keeps first-output readiness at its source until the terminal is ready.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real bundled Control UI: open a terminal in chat A, enter a marker, switch to B and back, dock bottom, navigate again, then dock right.
- The two original docking regressions fail on base `2e59936b6747f10c44edb76decd662c2d27305be` at the missing terminal canvas after **Dock to right**, and pass with the fix. They cover redocking into A or the currently selected B, retained Files state, navigation away/back, one terminal ID, one open and zero close requests, and no terminal resurfacing on New conversation.
- The extended regression reproduced wrong selection in populated and retained destinations, an in-flight-open handoff, and stale tabs on a second docking cycle. The final cases preserve three source/destination tabs and the active terminal across pending opens, navigation, and repeated bottom/right moves.
- **25 browser tests passed**, covering original/current-chat destinations, populated and retained panes, pending opens, repeated docking, mixed live/exited tabs, selected live or exited tabs, plus shared Browser, Desktop, Files, and light/dark paths. **107 focused unit tests passed** for terminal lifecycle, restore, cancellation, handoff, pane routing, and dock layout.
- The [exited-tab P2 from the prior review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166213#issuecomment-6021575448) is repaired. Both new browser regressions failed on the previous PR head after **Dock to right**. They now preserve the same diagnostic canvas and pixel-identical output after round trips, with no dead-session attaches, replacement opens, or closes. Additional red/green unit tests cover a live destination sharing the diagnostic session ID and pending catalog first-output readiness; cancellation cleanup is also covered.
- Fresh precommit autoreview completed on the integrated candidate tree `0537ad0cf1b163ee94896eb86063472b620c89db`. Its sole P2 alleged the readiness fixture used the wrong RPC. Call-chain inspection showed this path calls `TerminalConnection.open` → `terminal.open` (not `start` → `sessions.catalog.startTerminal`); the unchanged handoff test passed **3/3**, so the finding was rejected with evidence. No accepted actionable findings remain. ClawSweeper also completed review of `2f41dba` with no actionable findings; all ten original feature files are byte-identical in the final candidate, whose only later delta is the two test-fixture repairs described below.
- Fresh execution on published head `2f41dba74297dbc32d60ebf92415f0d4234c26a8`: **25/25 browser tests in 73.72 s runner wall time**, **107/107 focused unit tests in 10.96 s**, and the full ten-file `check:changed` pass (eight affected test type graphs, UI types, i18n, ratchets, dead exports, formatting, lint and UI style lint). Test cost for the new docking file in the original proof was **34.57 s runner wall / 18.806 s test time**; the new handoff file was **2.14 s / 0.375 s**. Browser routing, retained panes, real emulator identity and pixel retention require the E2E boundary.
- The [previous CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37507166391) failed the inherited MCP production audit and canceled sibling jobs; it is not passing test evidence. The canonical repair landed separately in [#166217](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166217), main commit `c39d9b0692dbaafa5b1bfe02514c9f6411ab5546`, and is now integrated without rewriting the terminal contribution history. `node scripts/ci-production-audit.mjs` passes on that canonical main. There are no independent dependency/security-policy changes.

The full terminal suite also caught an accessibility test clicking before terminal boot completed. The test-only follow-up `54afa4bddbfdbe1f2d5249fd8dfecaf4e134ea2a` repairs teardown via the public panel owner, waits for live/ready docking with fake timers, and checks upload controls before retiring their source. title: fix: hide web search when no provider is configured
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents repeatedly attempting web searches that cannot work because no search provider is configured.

## User Impact

Unconfigured `web_search` is omitted from initial tools, Tool Search, and Code Mode. The agent instead receives a concise setup hint pointing to `openclaw configure --section web` or Settings → Ask OpenClaw.

Explicitly disabled or policy-denied search does not produce a misleading setup hint. Native hosted search and explicitly selected key-free providers retain their existing behavior. Configured-but-unavailable providers keep their actionable execution diagnostics; this is a configuration-presence check, not a network or credential health probe.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared tool assembly previously exposed search based on its enabled flag without checking provider setup. It now uses the search owner’s provider credential contracts and runtime metadata before catalog construction, and carries the resulting fact into initial and refreshed prompts. Existing execution-time credential/configuration late binding is unchanged.

Reported and requested by @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/ae3e0c01-255a-440f-912b-4d9e40bb44fd)

### Landed candidate

Final-head [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37543043449): **88 jobs terminal, zero failures**. Required CI, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses pass. ClawSweeper revision 8 reviewed this exact head with **no actionable findings**.

### SDK correction

Prior head: `83d009c58140e4c29334a221bbb10393f2c0ad81`, tree `c75cbaa14813cf40979c8ad9e9eabdacc122783a`.

The latest review found that the internal prompt callback leaked into both public SDK factory option types. Both public signatures now omit `onWebSearchConfiguration`; internal assembly retains it. The existing private-options regression covers both signatures. Canonical SDK typechecking failed at both assertions before the fix and passes afterward. SDK, search-assembly, and real prompt-callback suites pass **20/20** in **76.50s**. The full changed-check plan for these two files passed in **577.8s**, including production types, all 27 consumer test graphs, SDK boundaries, deadcode, lint and guards. Incremental staged AutoReview is **scoped-clean through P2**.

The prior head `b49b3b88b1` completed [CI successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37538646090), with all 86 jobs terminal and no failures. This remains prior-head evidence; final-head CI and review are recorded above.

The final CI repair does two distinct things:
- Keeps callers’ already-prepared authentication-source facts during asynchronous tool construction. Undefined facts still trigger legitimate asynchronous discovery; source presence still requires a matching provider credential. Execution-time credential late binding is unchanged.
- Places real database-consuming browser-delivery and skill-dispatch fixtures in the existing infra fork lane, with canonical provider-environment isolation. No production guard, assertion, timeout or retry was weakened, and no new test pool was introduced.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing prompt icons and Powerline separators when a Zsh or other shell prompt uses Nerd Font characters, and lets users choose their terminal font.

## User Impact

Users can choose an installed monospace font in **Settings → Appearance → Typography → Terminal font**, or reset to the bundled **JetBrains Mono + Nerd Font symbols** default. Changes update open terminals without restarting their shells.

The setting is browser-local for the selected Gateway; custom fonts must be installed on the browser's computer, not the remote shell host. title: improve(skills): discover eligible skills automatically
body:
Related: #163824, #164969

## What Problem This Solves

Applied Workshop skills should become discoverable without manually adding each new name to a persistent agent list.

## User Impact

User impact: agents discover all otherwise-eligible skills in their configured roots, including newly applied Workshop skills; the agent Skills panel becomes a read-only eligibility inventory.

**Intentional upgrade policy change:** Doctor retires `agents.defaults.skills`, `agents.entries.<id>.skills`, and their historical `agents.list` forms, with visible warnings and the normal private pre-migration backup. **Prior agent-specific restrictions over current and future skill names are not preserved. An old `[]` no longer disables all skills.** Review this change before upgrading if you rely on that persistent curation. Global per-skill disables and session selections remain effective, but are not equivalent preservation of agent-specific restrictions. No agent exclusion becomes a global disable.

`skills.allowBundled`, prerequisites/platform eligibility, publishing/scanning, source precedence and agent-owned Workshop isolation remain separate. Tool permissions, credentials, sandbox and exec-approval controls are not relaxed.

X guest containment previously depended on the empty skill list suppressing outside-repository read exceptions. This PR preserves that shipped restriction through the existing sender-bound, closure-bound read authority and inherited helper lineage instead. Guests and their hidden helpers cannot gain external skill/resource reads from normal discovery. Older hosts refuse guest mode with actionable support guidance; normal maintainer behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persistent positive lists have legitimate role-focus, token-efficiency and behavioral/security-guardrail uses. This deliberately trades that optional persistent catalog curation for automatic skill discovery and learning, rather than claiming the old selection model was pointless or a hard host/tool authorization boundary.

The cutover removes the competing agent-name filter across discovery, prompts, catalog/read/search/slash/status, snapshots, CLI, UI and native consumers. Existing eligibility, session focus and refresh owners remain authoritative. title: fix(telegram): keep delegated progress live after the parent yields
body:
Related: #150995 (same intent; no code reuse). Builds on the progress-continuation contract from #152517 / #153028.

## What Problem This Solves

When a Telegram parent spawns announcing subagents and calls `sessions_yield`, the live progress card is deleted at the yield and replaced by a generic "I'm continuing this work and will send the result when it is ready." The user sees nothing while the children work, until the final answer arrives about a minute later.

## Design

Telegram keeps the card. The waiting-status payload of a yielding turn carries a one-shot `progressContinuation.adopt(draft)` capability (`src/auto-reply/reply/waiting-status.ts`). Telegram's `deliverReply` hands over its **confirmed, still-live** progress stream wrapped as `{ push(item), retire() }` (`retainProgressDraft`). Rendering, throttling, the account limiter and deletion stay with Telegram's own draft stream. If the card is adopted, the waiting ack is not sent and the stream is detached from the finished turn.

**SDK handoff (versioned).** Channels receive the capability as `ReplyDispatchRuntimeInfo.adoptProgressDraft(draft): boolean` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`. **Deprecation:** `ReplyDispatchRuntimeInfo.adoptProgressContinuation(receipt): Promise<boolean>`, which shipped in 2026.9.8, is deprecated and replaced by `adoptProgressDraft(draft)`. The type stays exported and source-compatible, so third-party plugins still compile, until the next Plugin SDK major. The host never offers it, so an adapter written against it keeps ordinary waiting-reply delivery and the host never receives a receipt. Telegram, the only bundled adopter, uses the draft handoff. This is recorded as `reply-dispatch-progress-receipt-handoff` in the compat registry and documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins/status-and-media.md#progress-card-handoff` and `docs/plugins/sdk-migration/compatibility-policy.md#progress-card-handoff`.

**Retirement fence.** `retire()` revokes the retained card synchronously. Every retained edit carries an assertion that the account limiter re-checks at network admission, so an edit still waiting in the per-chat scheduler is rejected before any Telegram I/O. The draft stream now keeps an update's send authority until that update lands or a newer accepted update replaces it. A skipped or failed attempt that a scheduled flush retries is therefore still fenced. A generation reset (rotation, `forceNewMessage`) drops the pending update together with its authority.

Core custody (`src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-progress-draft.ts`, ~230 lines) is process-local and attaches to owners that already exist:

- **Adoption** succeeds only if every announcing spawn's current registry row is still owed to its requester: `requesterSettleWake` is set, there is no accepted suppressing cancellation, and no wake is already dispatching.
- **Updates** carry only child status rows and child tool **names + status**. Child prose, commands, arguments and results are never pushed.
- **Lifetime** follows committed registry state. A projection subscription reconciles the draft on every publication. It follows a task's replacement execution (steer, or a resumed child yield, under the same task id). It drops members that are no longer owed and retires the card once none remain. Settlement, wake retries, `/stop`, `/reset` and row removal all commit through publications, so the card has no settle or kill hooks of its own. A kill intent can still roll back, so only accepted cancellation ends a member.
- **The resumed parent**: the existing settle wake is still the only final-delivery owner. `withSubagentProgressDraft` shows the resumed requester's tool rows on the same card. If that parent yields again, the new cohort joins the same card (`trackSubagentProgressYield` in the yield commit).

### Why the original continuation module was replaced

Credit to the original implementation in this PR (head `2496977694`). It proved the UX and the privacy projection, and its live matrix found the right cases. The rewrite keeps those invariants but removes the second owner of the presentation lifetime:

- `subagent-progress-continuation.ts` (699 lines) is gone. It ran its own edit queue and timer, made edits through `runMessageAction`, did cohort/generation re-checks, and listened for session facts scoped only by key. Telegram's draft stream and committed registry state now cover all of this. The earlier review findings no longer apply: key-only revocation, disabled edit/delete actions, `/stop` with a completed member, and `NO_REPLY` orphaning.
- Also removed: the `AsyncLocalStorage` promote context, the JSON streaming-identity channel-policy fence, the separate presentation module, the canonical-`to` receipt fix, and cron/batch authority moving under presentation. The receipt handoff is replaced by the versioned draft handoff above.
- The queued-follow-up attach is removed. Queued Telegram replies go out through `routeReply` and never reach the adopting dispatcher, so queued turns keep the waiting ack exactly as on `main`.
- A queued turn admitted after an adoption now gets its own fresh answer stream (`createAnswerStream`).

## Discord: dormant path removed

Discord's adopt path (#153028) has had no producer since #159179 removed the Tasks runtime. This PR deletes that adopt path and its tests (−84 prod lines). Discord keeps the ordinary waiting ack.

## Regressions covered (all fail before the fix)

- `subagent-progress-draft.test.ts` uses the real registry, SQLite persistence and settle wake. It covers:
  - retire-once after a visible answer, a NO_REPLY retry, and exhausted silent attempts;
  - refusing a stale cohort;
  - committed vs rejected `/stop` and `/kill` writes;
  - a kill that rolls back because the child is still finishing;
  - following a resumed child execution;
  - a re-yield cohort keeping the same card;
  - no child result text in any pushed item.
- Telegram progress-lifecycle HTTP suite:
  - the same message id is edited and then deleted, with one `sendMessage` and no waiting ack;
  - a queued turn gets its own card;
  - a card whose preview already stopped (for example, deleted by the user) is not adopted, and the waiting reply is delivered.
  - an edit waiting in the real account scheduler when the card retires never reaches Telegram, including an edit retried by a scheduled flush after a failed first attempt.
- `test/subagent-progress-telegram-retirement.integration.test.ts` chains both halves: the real registry adopts the card Telegram retained, child activity edits it, and a real committed `/stop` (`abortControlledSubagents`) or requester reset (`stopSessionResetSubagents`) retires it while an edit is held in the account scheduler, including an edit retried after a failed first attempt. No such edit reaches the Bot API endpoint, and the card is deleted.
- `draft-stream.test.ts`: a failed final's send authority does not reject the next generation's lazy preview, and an ignored late lazy update does not strip a final's authority from its resume attempt.
- `shipped-channel-compat.test.ts`: the 2026.9.8 receipt field keeps its exact released type. `dispatch-from-config.continuation-settlement.test.ts`: the dispatcher offers only `adoptProgressDraft`, never the deprecated field.

## Evidence

### Live proof: Telegram Test Server, real `gpt-6-astra`

Setup: Convex-leased TDLib user plus the Test Bot API. The model is called through a local pass-through proxy, so the Gateway never holds the key. Each run records the chat for 300s. Baseline is `origin/main` `08229175e9b5`. Rows (a), (c), (d) and (e) were rerun on head `d95af00aafbf` (dist built from it, verified via `build-info.json`). The final head `0fb2f9c33e21` is that head rebased onto `main` `9e5692852d60` plus one test-only commit; the PR's production diff is byte-identical. Rows (b) and (f) are from candidate `c58d81987663`, before the final review fixes. Those fixes change the SDK field name and the transport fence, not the card lifecycle. Streaming is the Telegram default `progress` mode with `toolProgress: true`.

| Case | Baseline (`main`) | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) DM, parent spawns 2 announcing children and yields | Card deleted at 21.9s right after the generic ack. Final at 71.3s. | **Final head:** no ack. The same card keeps updating (14 edits): child rows, then the children's `Exec` rows. One final at 85.7s; card deleted at 86.7s. |
| (b) Two successive yields (stage one → stage two) | — | (`c58d81987663`) One card across both cohorts (stage one, then stage two plus its `Exec`). One final at 67.8s; card deleted at 68.4s. |
| (c) `/stop` at 95s, quick child already done (finished by 37s), slow child running | — | **Final head:** card kept until `/stop` and deleted 1.3s after it. Only the existing "Agent was aborted. Stopped 1 sub-agent." follows (97.5s). Nothing else arrives in the remaining ~200s. |
| (d) Synthesis instructed to end `NO_REPLY` | Ack, card deleted, then `main`'s existing incomplete-turn notice | **Final head:** no ack. Card kept through the child's `Exec` and deleted 1.0s after `main`'s same incomplete-turn notice (57.4s). No message beyond what `main` sends. |
| (e) `streaming.mode: "off"` | Ack + final | **Final head:** ack (32.2s) + final (82.7s), no card: unchanged |
| (f) Forum: two concurrent topics | — | (`c58d81987663`) One card per topic, each showing only its own topic's children. One final per topic; each card deleted. Run-owned topics removed afterwards. |

In every candidate run, including all four final-head runs, the card text contained no child prose marker, child result or child command. Final-head runs made 7–9 `gpt-6-astra` requests each, plus `main`'s utility and embedding calls.

## Bounded cost

- At most one retained card per adopted yield. It only exists while the registry still owes that cohort to its requester. Edits use Telegram's existing throttle and account limiter: one draft stream, no new timers.
- Per card, core keeps one registry projection listener plus one agent-event listener per tracked child (and one for the resumed requester). Each registry publication costs O(tracked children × rows for that child session) through the existing child-session index.
- Nothing is persisted. After a Gateway restart the card is not revived; it stays as a stale message, the same as any in-flight progress draft on `main` today. Stopping the Telegram account while a card is retained has the same local-transport limitation; core releases its listeners when the tasks settle.
- Data model: no stored rows, columns, schema or migrations change. The card handoff is process-local, and the registry rows it follows are read, never extended, so upgrade and downgrade see the same stored data as `main`.
- No new config, schema or permissions. No new user-visible messages: an adopted card replaces the ack, and opt-outs are unchanged.

## Not changed

- Final delivery, `NO_REPLY` handling and the settle-wake retry policy. Case (d) shows `main` already re-prompts a yielded requester that answers `NO_REPLY` and then sends its incomplete-turn notice. That behavior is identical on both sides and is out of scope here.
- Queued Telegram turns, `streaming.mode` `off`/`partial`/`block`, quiet progress, Slack, Codex, Discord (waiting ack), cron and collector delivery.

LOC vs `main` (`9e5692852d60`): prod +532/−195, tests +866/−316, docs +54/−27, scripts +1 (the wrapper inventory entry for the new compat record). The original PR was prod +979/−38.

title: fix(ui): close terminal dock after shell logout
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Terminal panel stays open showing `exited (0)` after logging out of its last shell, whether the panel is docked at the bottom or on the right.

## User Impact

User impact: a normally exited shell closes its tab, and the panel closes when no other tool tabs remain. Other terminals and Files stay open; failures, signals, disconnects, and errors retain their output for inspection. Fullscreen terminals keep their new-session control. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing terminal tab teardown for a clean PTY exit, then let the embedding chat pane remove its own terminal slot. This follows the actual process lifecycle rather than recognizing typed command strings or hiding the whole dock.

title: fix(ui): keep dictation available during active turns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI microphone becomes unavailable while an assistant turn is active, preventing users from dictating their next message. Dictation Send also bypassed the normal immediate submission handoff.

## User Impact

You can dictate during a running turn, send the draft through the existing follow-up mode, or keep it until the turn finishes. Dictation Send uses the same pending-feedback path as typed Send. Mobile dictation preserves the original draft/caret so committing the visible preview does not append it twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

Draft input must not inherit the assistant run's busy state. The shared microphone now accepts an explicit availability gate, preserving New Session and Talk-only restrictions. Both dictation entry gestures share draft capture, and Send retains its original input event instead of adding another submission path. Speech-provider, permission, and delivery semantics are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression before repair: both sending/streaming microphone cases failed because the control was disabled; both dictation Send cases lost the original event.
- Mobile browser reproduction failed on the original control with the microphone disabled. The next end-to-end run exposed a doubled transcript from the uncaptured mobile preview; the owner fix preserves a single copy.
- Focused composer, dictation, New Session, and real submit-handoff tests: 120 passed.
- Bundled Control UI browser suite: 13 passed, including starting dictation during a running turn, explicit Send with Gateway ACK held, and retaining the draft when the turn ends during recording. Synthetic microphone and Gateway provider events; not physical-iPhone or live speech-provider validation.
- Fresh independent autoreview: scoped-clean at the repository's default P0 threshold. UI and all eight selected core-test TypeScript graphs, formatting, i18n, and ratchets passed. Targeted lint passed.
- `check:changed` is not a full pass: its full-tree Knip scan reports the unchanged `src/agents/model-catalog.runtime.ts` export `loadManifestModelCatalog (modelCatalogRuntime)`. This UI patch does not change that owner or its consumers.
- Cost: the two added browser scenarios take about 2.2 seconds each; the complete 13-scenario browser suite took 36.69 seconds including a bundled UI build. The final 120-test focused command took 17.48 seconds with a fresh isolated cache. No full repository test suite was run.

### After

title: feat: open public threads at their regular links
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Publicly shared conversations need one regular thread URL that works for signed-out readers and authorized Team members, without making anonymous visitors full operator clients.

## User Impact

- Public threads open read-only at their canonical `/chat/...` URL. Private, missing, and revoked threads show the same generic login prompt.
- **Log in** returns to the same thread; existing membership and write permissions still apply. Anonymous readers get conversation text, not tools, reasoning, attachments, widgets, RPC access, or a WebSocket.
- Visible latest pages refresh automatically every 15–18 seconds, pause when hidden, and honor backoff. Revocation is checked before every response, including `304`.
- X accounts can opt into `autoPublishWorkSessions` for fresh isolated children of verified-public maintainer mentions. It defaults off; guests, forks, private/incognito sources, later turns, and descendants cannot inherit publication authority.

External-login deployments must allow anonymous canonical thread documents while keeping the session-entry login endpoint, operator APIs, WebSockets, and private resources protected. Public responses remain `no-store`; this does not add Cloudflare/CDN transcript synchronization. No production deployment or configuration has been changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing revocable `publicShare` grant rather than weaken Team visibility. The standalone reader shares bounded rendered responses and cold-read work, avoiding operator bootstrap, presence, and roster costs. The X plugin verifies source posts using app-only reads within existing spend limits, carries host-owned invocation authority, and receives confirmation only after the creation owner commits the grant.

The owner-approved config-surface increase is exactly **2 channel paths** (shared default and account override), regenerated on current main from 3872 to 3874. No schema migration or new persistent sharing store is introduced.

## Evidence

**Final candidate:** `3f81bce804c819195120e6d216571ea6144953ec`, integrated with main `fcf275b642608e459130d62b3dc305e215959319`. Fresh full-candidate independent P0/P1 review: no actionable findings.

- **Final CI receipt repair:** the only failed job on the prior head had two obsolete send/steer assertions. Upstream `1c798b4be1afcf9effd732e87e16f2f89f147a22` intentionally persists direct operator input before acknowledgement. The test now requires exact `messageSeq: 1` and matches it to stored history, preserving single-row, text, idempotency and cleanup checks. Same original four-file group: **76 pass / 2 fail before → 78/78 pass after, 219.08 s wall**; scoped types/lint and fresh P0/P1 delta review passed. No production behavior changed. Local Node 26 proof is not presented as an exact Node 24 CI replay.
- **Complete X publication chain:** real X client/parser/public-audience verifier → registered plugin/host ingress → reply/run admission → production tool policy and visible `sessions_spawn` → real `sessions.create`/SQLite → anonymous HTTP handler. Allowed invocation commits a generation-bound public grant and serves the persisted child answer; guest visible spawn is forbidden with no creation; disabling publication during awaited creation rejects it before any child/grant commits. No injected publication capability, seeded grant, or canned creation/read result. X transport and model inference are deterministic; the reader uses the in-process HTTP harness. **1 test / 3 scenarios passed, 7.423 s test, 45.67 s Vitest, 619.79 s including isolated build**, before the behavior-preserving main integration. Final-head ingress/publication/handoff regressions: **8 files passed, 72.10 s wall**.
- **Real authenticated HTTP handoff:** actual TCP listener, production trusted-proxy authentication, SQLite profiles/roles/membership, resident session resolution, and actual built Control UI document. Owner and permitted reader receive the app; authenticated denied user does not; membership change or role revocation after document preparation blocks all app bytes. Anonymous canonical documents ignore spoofed identity; handoff and media remain protected. **5 cases passed, 15.73 s including suite setup, 48.96 s Vitest, 660.06 s including isolated build; 18 sibling cases passed.** This exposed and fixed the missing prepared reader role, using the existing profile preparation owner.
- **CI failure repaired, not rerun away:** reproduced the missing-SHM/SIGKILL in the original 11-file Gateway group. Reused upstream `bba56f6833601f4bd46fa5d0aeebc87e3cad7fd3` to close SQLite before removing test directories; retained later main changes. The isolated worktree-suggestion fixture now initializes its own committed repository. **523/523 cases passed, 163.04 s wall**, on Node 26.8.2 (not claimed as an exact Node 24 CI replay). Refresh/spawn regressions also passed **12/12, 54.29 s wall**.
- The integrated production candidate’s core and **all 27 core-test type graphs passed** (reused for unchanged inputs; the final test-only edit also passed its Gateway-server type graph); scoped lint, format, conflict/line-cap/SQLite/mocking/config/dependency guards, native schema, import-cycle and auth/body-order checks passed. The full changed-check pipeline still reports an unrelated unused `CallBrief` export in unchanged `extensions/voice-call/src/types.ts`; it is recorded, not suppressed or claimed fixed. Prior full build passed **506.45 s**; isolated final-effect runs rebuilt their runtime. Hosted CI is separate and must qualify the pushed head.
- Earlier feature proof remains valid for unchanged behavior: **381 focused cases**, real HTTP bursts of **20 readers per URL form** with conditional reuse/revocation, and live read-only app-token X lookup with explicit public-author metadata. The **280 ms** local burst is not a production capacity benchmark.
- Inspected, sanitized screenshots below show the actual public renderer. Browser proof covered `200→304` refresh, path/hash restoration, and no reader WebSocket/bootstrap. That browser login endpoint was synthetic; the real authenticated HTTP proof above closes the application-owner gap, **not a live Cloudflare/identity-provider login or browser WebSocket session**. One earlier isolated UI prerequisite build terminated before tests; it remains an unclassified build event, not a claimed product repair.

**Deployment boundary:** no Team/Cloudflare configuration or deployment changed. Deploy the handler before exposing only mounted `/chat/*` documents and existing `/share/*`; keep session-entry, the rest of `/__openclaw__/`, operator APIs/WebSockets/media/settings behind authentication. Operators must verify the external proxy/login return flow for their topology.

### Before

### After

title: improve(ui): make agent menus easier to scan
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent tiles truncate names, become hard to scan as the list grows, and leave an awkward empty corner in the three-agent “Show all” avatar.

## User Impact

Agents are easier to recognize and find in horizontal rows. Larger menus can be searched by name or ID without scrolling the menu actions away. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use 56px rows with 40px avatars, two-line labels, a bounded agent scroller, and search above six agents. Duplicate names show their IDs. Existing pinned order, unread indicators, navigation, and hover/click dismissal remain with their existing owners. Reopening reveals the selected agent; hover does not take focus from the composer.

Three-agent groups use an inverted stack with opaque avatar separators, explicit layering, and room inside the selection ring. No new preferences, persistence, pin actions, or dependencies are introduced.

title: improve(ui): pin agents directly from the switcher
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pinning an agent requires leaving the sidebar switcher for Settings, which is inconvenient with a larger roster.

## User Impact

With **more than 3 agents (4+)**, hover or keyboard-focus a row to reveal its pin. Saved pins stay muted and visible; touch users always see the control. With **3 or fewer agents**, this component shows no pin controls, including saved-pin indicators. Settings pinning and the existing saved order are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing browser-profile pin preference and toggle. Pinning keeps the menu open and the active agent unchanged. The menu owns keyboard routing in one place; focus survives pinned-first reordering. The threshold uses the full selectable roster, not the filtered search result.

title: feat(openai): support custom realtime voice endpoints
body:
Related: #114146. Consolidated reports: #164054, #164338, #164339, #164055.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible realtime voice servers cannot be selected because the OpenAI voice bridge always connects to OpenAI's endpoint.

## User Impact

Users can set `talk.realtime.providers.openai.baseUrl` to a full realtime WebSocket URL and use `transport: "gateway-relay"`. The same provider option works for Gateway-side Voice Call and other backend voice bridges. Existing OpenAI and Azure configurations are unchanged.

This adds exactly one configuration option, explicitly approved by @jacobtomlinson. The override is for the GA Realtime protocol, not GPT-Live or browser WebRTC. Mixed Azure routing and unsupported transport/model combinations fail before provider I/O rather than silently sending a custom key to OpenAI. It does not register a DashScope provider or guarantee that a third-party service supports OpenClaw's events, audio formats, voices, and tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI provider owns URL normalization and preserves the parsed endpoint path and existing non-model query encoding. Standard URL parsing applies to raw unescaped characters. HTTP(S) aliases become WS(S), and the selected model replaces only the model query parameter. The existing direct server-side API-key flow needs no client-secret minting or additional auth toggle. URL userinfo, fragments, invalid schemes, and ambiguous Azure combinations are rejected without echoing the URL.

Requested by @jacobtomlinson; thanks to @starship863 and @wangyan411303 for the reports.

[Exact-head CI run 37331889991](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37331889991) passed; its affected extension-bundle job took 163 s including setup (not per-file test time).
- Real local WebSocket smoke: Talk config normalization → provider selection → exact custom path/query → direct bearer auth → GA session readiness → bidirectional audio bytes. This is a synthetic compatible endpoint, **not** live DashScope validation.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passed. Type-aware Oxc lint on all seven changed TypeScript files passed, as did coercion-helper, deprecated-API, import-cycle (zero cycles), and `git diff --check` guards.

Removed that password while retaining the username/userinfo rejection case; all six invalid-URL cases passed afterward. No scanner policy or exception changed. A local TruffleHog 3.97.0 scan reports no findings, but does not establish parity with hosted 3.97.4.
- One intermediate retest failed during compiler snapshot sealing because scanner scratch files were created concurrently; it ran no tests. With the workspace namespace held stable, the six-case retest passed.

title: feat: trigger automations from MCP events
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automations need to react to changes reported by configured MCP servers without polling or keeping an MCP App open.

## User Impact

Users can enable the bundled `mcp-events` plugin, discover an event in the Automation editor, and run existing instructions, tool policy, delivery, and history from signed webhooks.

This is opt-in and implements the OpenAI webhook profile of MCP Events (protocol `2026-07-28`), not every experimental Events feature. Operators must provide publicly reachable HTTPS forwarding **only the callback prefix** to the Gateway. Durable receipt does **not** promise exactly-once external effects or recovery of events the source no longer retains.

Downgrade requires removing event jobs and compatibility with the target release’s database schema; otherwise restore a compatible pre-upgrade backup. In-place downgrade to v2026.9.8 is unsupported because main’s inherited database schemas are newer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin owns subscription leases, signature verification, key rotation, and cleanup. It reuses configured MCP connections and credential authority, durable ingress, the existing Automation scheduler/queue, and native execution/history. There is no second scheduler, inbox, or credential registry.

Admission atomically transfers the exact ingress claim into a Cron receipt. Busy or paused jobs remain pending without consuming retry budget. Disconnect/reconnect cannot revive old callback authority; event payloads remain untrusted data, never instructions or tool grants.

## Evidence

**Merged:** exact prepared head `c72a6a6514a9013889a18f66c67593e1eedf2ee0` landed as `e210870acfe2fd7df6fcd464e4d775fac5a55710` on October 14, 2026, through the native inherited/infrastructure-CI exception. Registry, both RPC boundaries, wrapper runtime closure, core production types, strict scoped lint, and native protocol checks pass after reconciliation; canonical generators are current. The full `a024a09` candidate had a fresh two-pass P0/P1 review with no actionable findings; that substantive review is reused, not presented as a new full-head review. Current-head broad CI completed with the independently attributed failures below; it is not green. The full candidate at parent `119edd244e07834647c2a708b5df9ddff382569f` had independent two-pass P0/P1 review and a successful CI-artifact build. The substantive repair delta has a fresh independent P0/P1 review with no actionable findings.

[CI attempt 38605260303](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38605260303) found issues that focused checks missed; it is **failed**, not waived or relabeled green. The accepted auto request was retired through native recovery before this repair was published.

title: chore(deps): refresh all dependencies with seven-day cutoff
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshes eligible dependency versions across core, plugins, native apps, exporters, and build/release tooling using a seven-day cutoff.

## User Impact

Updates dependencies published on or before **2026-09-28 05:29 UTC**, with regenerated locks, checksums, notices, and compatibility fixes. Existing newer pins are preserved; no releases or live Gateway changes are included.

**Email authentication:** Mailauth 7 follows RFC 9989 DNS-based DMARC alignment. A parent-domain signature without a parent DMARC policy no longer authenticates a subdomain. Affected senders should publish the appropriate policy or sign with the sender domain; configured authentication requirements, sender-bound tokens, and trusted-header rules are not weakened. Permanently rejected messages advance the mailbox cursor and are not automatically replayed after DNS repair. Peter Steinberger (@steipete) explicitly approved this documented compatibility cutover and landing on October 6, 2026.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit includes all 194 npm manifests, three Cargo graphs, Swift packages, Android/Wear dependencies, Ruby/Fastlane graphs, Go modules, ONNX export tooling, binary assets, CI actions, and container/toolchain pins. New selections are checked against actual publication timestamps, including transitives.

Ports the existing Proxyline, Vitest, and Web Awesome patches without changing their behavior; adapts the new native TypeScript source-file lease contract and str0m Opus signature; preserves correctly typed callback contracts and the existing UI startup budget.

Compatibility holds remain explicit: Gradle 9.8 fails the current AGP warning policy; Commander/AXorcist are constrained by Peekaboo; Tauri Git forks still contain required upstream fixes; the protected Crabbox broker and Rust minimum-version CI pins remain intentional contracts. No new overrides, check exceptions, or performance-limit changes were introduced. The documented Mailauth alignment cutover is the material compatibility change.

## Evidence

- Frozen pnpm installation succeeds; **300 newly selected npm package/version pairs** independently pass the cutoff. Cargo locks likewise have no newly selected post-cutoff packages or downgrades. All 36 migrated installed patch target blobs match the verified intended changes.
- Full `pnpm build` passes (9m 13s), including 96 external plugin builds, declaration generation, runtime guards, and the unchanged Control UI performance limits. Production, plugin, script, and root test typechecks pass; npm package-lock validation and all repository preflight/policy guards pass. Full formatting and stylesheet lint pass.
- Android phone: 24 focused tests and Play debug APK; Wear/benchmark: 13 shared tests and APK builds. Ruby 4.0.7 frozen Bundler and Fastlane loading pass for both mobile projects.
- Rust 1.93 minimum-version workspace: 148 tests, check, Clippy with `-D warnings`, and formatting pass. WatchRTC: 13 real engine tests. Linux desktop: native all-target check and linked executable build pass in a task-owned rootless Ubuntu container. Go tests and module verification pass.
- ONNX: real exports of both pinned checkpoint families, plus 16 Python and 16 repository Node CPU inference comparisons pass at unchanged tolerance. CodeQL pack CI and both repository query compilations pass.
- Live Tuwunel 1.9.3 registration and login pass through the actual QA client. llama.cpp archives and aliases are verified across all selected platform assets; Linux x64 CLI smoke passes.
- Native TypeScript/worker/guard regressions pass, including all 76 previously blocked worker-cleanup cases. Final quiet-workspace IMAP/CUA/QA, image worker, proxy, CLI, socket, phone, terminal, and file-transfer regressions pass (68.90s). Web Awesome real-Chromium and MCP app regressions pass (35.54s).
- New-test cost: `pnpm test extensions/imap/src/sender-gate.mailauth.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 7 cases in 27.54s, including cold compiled-worker preparation. `pnpm test ui/src/app/control-ui-chunking.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 6 cases in 12.32s; its new real-build regression fails on the old rule. Those two new suites add no timers or per-case Gateway boots. The repaired existing cron E2E adds one necessary Gateway stop/start for exclusive custody; the complete three-case Gateway suite takes 36.84s in the final container proof. CI seconds are not yet measured.
- Fresh four-pass AutoReview completed on the complete candidate with no accepted/actionable P0/P1 findings. Its static-review limitations do not substitute for the executed contract and artifact proofs above.

**Integrated CI repairs:** After the dependency-specific toolchain and fixture adaptations, all six remaining failure causes on repaired head `81fa487` (run `37276177059`) were independently attributed to baseline defects. CLI JSON, QA cleanup, and Telegram media fixture repairs landed in [#165430](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165430). The catalog startup fixture fix and cloud-worker run-start ownership fix are also integrated from main. The remaining cron fixture now hands exclusive database custody from the stopped Gateway to the offline scheduler and reconnects afterward; production authority policy, timeout limits, and assertions are preserved. Existing stale-service coverage remains intact.

The combined candidate passes a fresh full build in a non-root, network-isolated Node 24.19 container (**12m 54.3s**) and both complete runtime suites (**4 tests passed; 221.56s wrapper**), including the previously duplicated worker reply and cron-authority handoff. All repository preflights and production/UI/plugin/script/root-test typechecks pass after main integration. The October 5 integration did not change dependency pins. The later conflict resolution preserves main’s newer pins as described below. The cron fixture delta received a fresh independent P0/P1-scoped review with no actionable findings; the reviewer did not independently inspect unchanged lifecycle helpers, which were covered by parent source review and the executed cleanup tests.

Original CI runs [37273707509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37273707509) and [37276177059](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37276177059) remain failed historical evidence, not green runs. Native macOS/iOS app builds, Windows/ARM desktop execution, and watchOS device proof were not run locally. Linux compilation is not graphical/package-runtime proof, and native archive verification is not execution on every platform. Hosted exact-head CI/review remains required for landing.

title: fix(agents): keep tool-authored replies from hiding unfinished work
body:
Related: #164558

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes finished tool-authored replies hiding sibling failures, disappearing beside terminal tools, repeating pre-tool narration, or delivering content that result middleware withdrew.

## User Impact

Plugin tools can return a finished answer without a model restatement while unfinished or failed sibling work still receives a continuation. Only the originating input's preamble is replaced; earlier and later answers and errors remain visible. No configuration migration or automatic tool opt-in is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture and completion now share the finalized batch after result rewriting. Codex keeps candidates private until the upstream response closes and every model-emitted call has an eligible result; raw receipts cover late request registration and native siblings. Explicit terminal siblings retain their completion contract without dropping a finished reply. Canonical assistant identity keeps reused call IDs distinct and recovery idempotent.

Reply content comes only from `details.sourceReply`. Calls nested inside Code Mode return data to that program, never an implicit send. Codex's direct-reply fast path requires the model-only `direct-only` catalog. Existing message-tool delivery remains separate.

## Evidence

- Runtime verification executed at `3ace76ecaf4f082c7b00cba861513046b6ff65b6`. The final head adds only a documentation clarification learned from that live run; production and test source are unchanged. Documentation formatting and link audit pass (14,947 links, zero broken).

- Real isolated Gateway, native Codex: **4/4 cases passed** with the actual Codex harness selected. Direct delivery was exact and once, with one raw model response and a terminal-release receipt. A real provider preamble was excluded from final delivery. Nested Code Mode did not auto-deliver its tool result. Both sibling calls were proven to belong to one raw response; the failing sibling caused a visible model continuation and no terminal release.
- Current embedded-runtime controls: **4/4 passed**. Agent-loop requests were 1 for direct/preamble and 2 for nested/sibling. Native evidence spans two authenticated, catalog-admitted model configurations; initial runs that did not exercise direct calls or same-response siblings remain fixture-inconclusive, not passes. No model allowlist or safety bypass was used.
- Red/green regressions cover finalized `message_end` rewriting, reused call IDs, response-only identity, terminal siblings, delayed native registration, and failure visibility. The refreshed 14-file selection passed in 216.56s. The final five-file selection passed 119 tests in 52.27s (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`); a mechanical owner extraction passed 48 related tests in 6.29s, and the corrected consumer fixture passed 13 in 44.44s. These selections overlap; per-test CI seconds are not measured.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw tabs are difficult to distinguish when several agents or Gateways are open.

## User Impact

Choose **Default** or **Agent avatar** in Appearance. The choice is personal to the connected Gateway, follows the explicitly selected agent, and preserves activity/attention dots. title: fix: resume tasks after deferred startup recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tasks can remain stopped after a Gateway restart when database startup inspection is still pending or one child-completion group cannot transfer its retained result.

## User Impact

Interrupted work keeps its resume obligation and retries automatically. A failed requester group no longer stops unrelated groups from recovering. Cancellation, supersession, and database/Gateway ownership checks remain intact. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending inspection is not a failed delivery: retain the existing wake, counters, and replay identity, then retry after 30 seconds. Startup activation isolates failed transfers and retries them under the original owner with existing 1-second exponential backoff capped at 30 seconds. Already-restored runs are not launched again.

## Evidence

- Regressions failed before the repair: pending inspection erased the wake; an invalid prepared cohort prevented a healthy later requester from activating.
- 263 passing checks: 213 lifecycle tests, 28 requester persistence/replay tests, 13 native custody tests, 8 queued-recovery tests, and one real isolated Gateway WebSocket session-create/readback smoke.
- Covers prolonged inspection, cancellation, confirmed inspection failure, persisted reload, per-child retention metadata, healthy groups beside failed groups, hydration order, reset, and Gateway replacement.
- Core and all 27 core-test type graphs passed. Typed lint, formatting, line limits, dead exports, import cycles, and the other selected ownership/schema guards passed after fixture-only type/layout corrections. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- No production Gateway was restarted. Persistence tests use real SQLite with fixture-owned Gateway transport; the separate socket smoke uses an isolated real Gateway.

Measured with the repository test wrappers and one worker: final lifecycle/requester invocation 87.30 seconds total (file durations 18.93 seconds for 213 tests and 49.28 seconds for 28 tests); native custody/queued invocation 52.35 seconds total (file durations 44.66 and 5.04 seconds). The longer existing suites retain native persistence, cleanup, and replay ordering rather than replacing those contracts with mocks. [Published CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37242655175): 46 executed jobs passed, 8053 summed job-seconds across parallel workers, 429 seconds from first job start to final gate completion. These are full-workflow costs, not per-test or incremental costs; conditionally skipped jobs are excluded.
