title: fix(pr): recognize delegated inherited-CI bypass authority
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native inherited-CI landing rejects a delegated writer solely because it is not an organization administrator, even when GitHub grants it bypass of the CI-only repository ruleset.

## User Impact

Operators can use the existing inherited-failure exception with repository write access and a live, narrowly scoped CI-ruleset grant instead of organization-admin membership, **provided the complete protection policy is readable**.

**Deployment limitation:** the current RoboClaw Maintain account can bypass the CI ruleset but cannot authoritatively read classic branch protection. This change alone does not enable end-to-end delegated landing for that account; the policy-read guard continues to refuse. The implementation is being landed separately from that deployment prerequisite. No GitHub permissions, credentials, review/security rules, or Gateway configuration were changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one native landing owner. Operator confirmation remains task authorization, not authenticated human identity; GitHub's writer-specific grant supplies execution capability. The exception still requires exact-head failed-attempt attribution, passing affected proof, independent security clearance, enforced reviews, exhaustive cancellation accounting, and retained-outcome recovery.

Only active repository-owned branch rulesets containing the GitHub Actions `openclaw/ci-gate` check qualify. Recheck both policy and writer authority after CI/security inspection, and retain the grant in the existing outcome. Mixed, missing, changed, revoked, or unknown authority refuses before intent. Delegation does not enable the prior-success conflict-resolution exception or waive PR-caused failures.

A scoped land request covers this independently proven inherited-failure exception without another chat permission round trip. Missing policy visibility remains a blocker, not permission to elevate or switch the writer.

## Evidence

- **Current-head CI passed:** [run 37256492509, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37256492509), all 69 jobs terminal with no failing jobs; both required `openclaw/ci-gate` surfaces are successful. Run wall time: 447 s. Changed-node job wall time: 204 s; its 27-case authority file completed in 0.603 s (wrapper 1.93 s).
- **Current rebased head:** `3fec246990df3fadf7fcdb84c21d2bf62c39d281`, based on `e76032fbab8d02b3d8c360db01440e732ee79a0d`. `git range-diff` confirms the patch is unchanged from the independently reviewed `b5bc7d0c` candidate.
- **Rebased-head local proof:** 115 focused tests passed (88 native-wrapper cases and 27 direct authority cases; combined wrapper 43.63 s, native file 41.81 s). Frozen dependency installation and whitespace checks pass.
- **Live GitHub contract proof:** the production writer-authority function, using the protected `gh` route and live GitHub responses, identified `roboclaw-bot`, accepted its CI-only ruleset `19130959` grant for inherited failures, and refused that same writer for the different conflict-resolution exception. Full admission still refuses at the unreadable classic-protection policy. This is capability/API-contract proof, **not** a live merge or live grant-revocation claim.

The earlier detailed test evidence below is retained at its original pre-rebase revision; it is not relabeled as a fresh execution:

- Reproduced the original refusal through the native wrapper fixture before the repair.
- Focused native + authority suite: **115 tests passed** (88 native cases, 27 fast authority cases). Native file: 42.18 s; authority file: 0.397 s; combined `pnpm test ... --maxWorkers=1` wrapper: 43.87 s. The existing native file exceeds 30 s because it exercises actual wrapper subprocesses, temporary Git repositories, retained outcomes, and dispatch/refusal boundaries; the new permission matrix stays in the cheap direct test layer.
- Native cases cover delegated REST landing, grant revocation before intent, review/security/CI-attempt refusals, and unavailable classic policy. Existing causality and cancellation coverage is retained. The previously interrupted main-drift run was repeated on the preserved candidate: **47 tests passed** (106.26 s). The lost/interrupted receipts are not counted as passing proof.
- Changed-scope ratchets, dependency/format guards, four root-test typecheck shards, dead-export scans, scoped script/test lint, Docker boundary checks, and the HTTP/2 guard passed. The initial changed-check command stopped on lint; the failing owner and test-style issues were repaired, and affected/remaining lanes were run directly rather than claiming that original aggregate passed.
- Stale-head recovery subset: **19 tests passed**, 36 unrelated cases not selected (118.31 s). Total selected tests passed across these runs: **181**.
- Independent AutoReview: scoped-clean at P0/P1; subsequent changes are mechanical lint fixes (explicit equivalent string comparison and test braces).
- Live read-only observations: managed writer has CI-only ruleset bypass, but full policy admission refuses. The same writer sees `branchProtectionRule: null` on protected public branches while `refUpdateRule` exposes real review/check requirements. The proposed null-as-absence fallback was removed.
- The historical pre-rebase evidence did not include a hosted-CI success claim. The rebased-head CI result is recorded above; no manual workflow dispatch or delegated live merge experiment was performed.

## Review disposition

ClawSweeper correctly identifies a remaining **deployment-proof limitation**: no real delegated merge or live grant revocation is claimed. I am accepting the narrow admission change under the scoped landing request, rather than making a new live merge experiment a prerequisite for the unchanged dispatch owner.

- The live receipt below exercises the production authority function through the actual protected writer route. It establishes the external API contract and principal, not full admission.
- Native-wrapper regressions exercise the changed allowed/refused control flow: valid synthetic authority causes exactly one pinned mutation and a retained outcome; revoked authority causes two grant reads, zero mutations, and no intent. The GitHub responses in those regressions are synthetic.
- `scripts/pr-lib/merge.sh` requalifies immediately before intent; `scripts/pr-lib/merge-outcome.sh` dispatches the retained exact head through the existing protected GitHub subprocess owner. These dispatch/identity owners are unchanged by this PR.
- The current managed writer still cannot pass the classic-policy visibility guard. That refusal remains mandatory. No credential substitution, policy waiver, live grant change, or new activation claim is introduced. Required CI/security and native landing checks still apply.

title: fix: keep the composer visible while new chats start
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the composer cannot accept follow-up input while a new chat is starting.

## User Impact

Keep typing, attach files, and queue follow-ups during startup. Messages wait behind the initial prompt and send in order to the confirmed session. Failed creation preserves the original prompt, queued input, and unfinished draft for retry.

Before acceptance, input stays in the current tab with reload protection. A rejected initial prompt keeps its followers paused for review. Existing account, incognito, read-only, and archived-session restrictions remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained creation draft owns input until the confirmed conversation's existing outbox accepts it. The startup view reuses the normal composer and current header/layout without mounting session controllers or querying session-scoped MCP resources prematurely.

Recovery also fixes a concurrent-pane race: once a batch is admitted, another pane cannot reopen it and overwrite a later delivery failure. Interrupted admissions remain resumable. Removed a redundant queue-state helper and startup hint; the editor no longer jumps vertically at admission.

## Evidence

- 101 focused unit tests pass on the final dependency installation (22.99s wrapper / 21.42s Vitest). The concurrent-pane regression fails on the original implementation and passes after the fix.
- All 56 scenarios in five browser suites pass on the integrated source (116.29s). After the frozen dependency refresh and manifest regeneration, all 22 targeted startup, ordering, rename, and model-refresh cases pass again (76.59s).
- Changed browser-file test times: transition matrix 37.506s, instant-thread 25.436s, active-turn recovery 12.707s, mutation scope 10.077s. The existing transition matrix covers real rich-content restoration across viewport, theme, and reduced-motion states; no new matrix cases were added.

- UI and UI-test typechecks, i18n, changed-file guards, targeted lint/style checks, dead-export scans, and production build pass. The build still emits an inherited startup-size diagnostic; no budget was relaxed. Earlier broad core lint found 20 line-limit violations in files byte-identical to the pinned main baseline; hosted lint passed on the first published revision.
- Initial CI caught the obsolete disabled-composer assertion. Its transition matrix now checks enabled input, no empty send, and exact original-prompt restoration. Three secondary failures were reproduced on CI's exact main parent `9948a4b83404` without this patch: accepted-steer ordering, pending sidebar-rename interaction, and intermittent model-refresh visibility. The first two tests now follow main's current contracts. The model-refresh case is unchanged; its passing replay is not claimed as a fix.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a session in a new browser tab briefly labels it “Disconnected” during a healthy initial connection.

## User Impact

New tabs keep their normal title while loading. Actual connection failures and reconnects still show “Disconnected,” and the marker clears after recovery. No change to caching, loading speed, authentication, or connection behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cached shell renders before the Gateway handshake completes. Its title treated every non-connected phase as a disconnect. The title now distinguishes normal startup from failed or lost connections using the existing Gateway snapshot, without new state or timers. Pending approval counts remain hidden until connected because a stale queue is not actionable.

## Evidence

- Three startup regressions failed against the original title logic and pass with the repair. Coverage includes slow initial loading, actual first-connect errors, reconnect/offline/reload-required states, and recovery.
- 102 focused navigation/title tests passed. The changed suite alone: `pnpm test ui/src/app/app-host.document-title.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 21 tests, 3.490 seconds wall time. CI seconds are not yet measured; no new CI lane or fixture boot was added.
- Actual Chromium source-app proof, using synthetic data and a mocked Gateway: an opener-backed new tab with its initial handshake held pending shows the warning before the fix and a neutral title after; a later transport drop and recovery retain the expected warning lifecycle.
- UI and affected test typechecks, formatting, typed lint, stylelint, repository guards, and all three unused-export scans passed. The original aggregate check exhausted its 240-second budget during unused-export scanning; that scan was completed separately with a sufficient budget.
- Independent P0–P2 code review: scoped-clean.

<details>
<summary>CI fixture recovery and verification</summary>

### CI recovery

The first exact-head CI run ([37213702096](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37213702096)) failed the existing desktop CI-details Escape assertion and cancelled one sibling shard. Its diagnostics show a connected Gateway; the title fix does not change that connected path.

An isolated replay passed, so that alone was not treated as a repair. A controlled replay with an active status tooltip reproduced the same popover-left-open assertion: Escape dismisses the tooltip first, as designed. The test now targets Escape at the already-actionable job link, establishing keyboard focus inside the menu rather than leaving it on the titled CI trigger. Both original popover-dismissal assertions remain; no sleeps, retries, or timeout changes were added.

The same active-tooltip replay passes with the focus correction. All 7 CI-details E2E cases then passed, including desktop/mobile/landscape (6.013 seconds test time; 23.30 seconds runner duration including the bundle fixture). Focused typed lint and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. This is a test-fixture correction only; the title implementation and captured visual proof are unchanged.

#### Model-picker expectation alignment

The next run ([37214779310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37214779310)) passed the repaired CI-details shard but exposed two stale catalog assertions after [#164963](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164963) landed on main. That change intentionally removes per-send model spinners; the older desktop/mobile E2E still expected one.

Integrated main at `29c36b7ace8a8c586b42b687930e5100ae5c7c7f` for this named failing gate. Both failures reproduced before the correction. Three assertions now expect a non-busy picker and no spinner, while selection, fallback, recovery, and actual catalog-loading checks remain intact. On the integrated candidate, all 102 title/navigation tests and all 19 catalog/CI-details browser cases pass; formatting, typed lint, and fresh full-candidate P0–P2 review pass. title: fix(ui): keep reply strips and work attached through chat updates
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: live tools can lose their reply strip, and completing, steering, or reloading chat can detach work, absorb another run's failed attempt, or replace an answer's controls.

## User Impact

Known responses keep their tools, answer, and reply controls together. Confirmed steers affect only subsequent output without closing an already-open tool while the same execution is still active. Explicit replies to an older message remain visible while its original is loading or unavailable. Loading earlier history preserves a confirmed post-steer answer's focused controls.

Automatic resumes without a known human binding remain separate and unattributed instead of guessing from the last person who spoke. The strip design is unchanged. No Gateway protocol, storage, configuration, permission, or native-app changes.

**Remaining limits:** an unconfirmed peer input without a target-run receipt can still change a later answer's row key when earlier same-run history loads. The stable prepend guarantee applies to confirmed steers. The independent-run stress case still has measurable projection overhead; this is not a zero-slowdown claim. This PR remains a draft and has not been merged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Establish execution/display ownership before visual rollups can erase it. Keep execution liveness separate from display segments, and keep chronological reply context separate from automatic recipient attribution. Remove the superseded cross-turn reply-ownership path. Skip empty and singleton rollup work and temporary singleton frame arrays rather than pooling unrelated executions for speed.

## Evidence

- Both audit regressions failed through the mounted production transcript on the preceding PR head: a confirmed steer disconnected the focused open tool; an unbound run lost its explicit pending/missing reply strip. Both now pass. Starting a different execution does not keep the old run expanded.
- Final node scripts/check-changed.mjs passed (276.6 s): production and affected test types, lint, styles, i18n, ratchets and dead-export checks. Independent final AutoReview at P0–P2 is scoped-clean. The earlier review's two index-only findings were the reproduced bugs; the staged final repair was re-reviewed.
- Ownership, attribution, failure/recovery, navigation and cache siblings pass. Existing scale tests retain zero rereads of 3,000 historical messages for unchanged/text-only updates. Final changed-owner recheck: 68 grouping/index/cache cases plus 8 mounted control cases; the separate reply suite passes all 29 cases. Counts across repeated checks overlap.
- Final production bundle: **7/7 browser cases passed**, including native tool start/result output opened/closed/reopened with the actual keyboard toggle, and real paginated history loading that preserves the exact focused post-steer Reply button and viewport anchor (≤2 px). The two old browser gaps now have passing proof; the original failed selectors are not claimed conclusively diagnosed. Desktop, mobile and tablet participant controls also pass.
- Browser evidence is the actual bundled Control UI with a synthetic Gateway, not a live provider. Final bounded browser performance is measured below.

### Performance

A fresh balanced B–PR–optimized–optimized–PR–B comparison executes the real builder → chain → index path. Three warmups and 12 observations per process give 24 observations per revision/operation. Immutable props, cache reuse, effective tool/text/final transitions and prior-chain immutability are asserted. Node projection timings exclude rendering.

For 3,000 independent tool-only runs, optimized cold/tool/final medians are **29.905 / 32.203 / 30.235 ms**, versus previous PR **33.962 / 38.217 / 32.739 ms** and base **24.951 / 25.701 / 23.769 ms**. The redundant chain work is reduced, but **+4.955–6.502 ms** remains over base. At 300 mixed runs the residual is **+0.327–0.398 ms**. The corrected projection retains 3,001 execution frames rather than the base's pooled 1–2 rows; not all remaining cost is proven unavoidable. Ordinary 3,000-message structural medians are within −1.055 to −0.033 ms of base; single-active-run medians are +0.125 to +1.241 ms, with overlapping ranges. These bounded measurements do not prove universal equivalence, browser speed, or absence of leaks.

Final actual-browser comparison (B–F–F–B, six fresh-context observations/version): ordinary 3,000-message finalization **100.10 → 100.60 ms**; mixed 300-message text **48.025 → 48.125 ms**. Neither showed a consistent slowdown across balanced pairs. Mixed cold loading remains **516.65 → 556.85 ms (+40.20 ms / 7.78%)**, with positive deltas in both pairs and noisy magnitude. Mixed mounted rows/elements increase **3/62 → 15/326**; ordinary final remains **14/472**. These are render-to-frame opportunity proxies, not hardware paint, backend latency or CPU. Fixtures are newly frozen and identical between versions, not a numeric replay of the earlier audit. **The zero-slowdown objective is not met for mixed cold loads; keep this tradeoff visible during draft review.**

### Before

![Before: live tool activity has no reply strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/618de6d2-7fb4-4bbe-b757-f3aebf1e9085)

### After

![After: the reply strip appears above live tools before the answer arrives](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/481a79a6-e12d-4f44-a100-01c056da10c4)

Existing representative captures: same synthetic conversation, 1440×900 dark viewport, actual Control UI. They show the original strip change; this follow-up repairs lifecycle/attribution behavior without redesigning that strip.

<details>
<summary>Measured local test cost</summary>

One-worker mounted-controls invocation: **4.40 s** total, 8 cases. Reply suite: **5.98 s** total, 29 cases. Grouping/index/cache recheck: **4.33 s** total, 68 cases across three files.

Final canonical browser file: **9.675 s** test time, **34.60 s** invocation, including a **21.43 s** production build. New pagination/native-tool cases take **1.066 / 1.128 s** and guard Gateway admission, native scrolling, focus and disclosure lifetime that projection assertions cannot prove. CI seconds for this revision are not yet available.

</details>

title: fix: reduce Windows startup delays with installed plugins
body:
Related: #164396

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes redundant file admission during Windows startup when OpenClaw captures an installed plugin and its dependencies. Native Windows profiling identified this work as the dominant cost while starting the Gateway and inspecting models.

## User Impact

Installed-plugin capture avoids a second pathname open for each ordinary portable file copy. In a same-machine Windows comparison against the exact unpatched parent, warm Gateway readiness improved by 20.0% and model inspection by 21.3%. No configuration changes or migration are required.

This is an incremental startup improvement: first-post-install startup still exceeded 90 seconds in the fixture, and the reporter’s full 27-minute stall has not been reproduced. This PR addresses the independently measured capture bottleneck; it does not close that broader investigation or attribute it to Node 22 or OAuth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hash the actual copied destination through its still-owned descriptor, then retain the existing pathname admission and content verification when finalizing the receipt. Cached receipts and lazy additions still verify the destination; failed lazy acquisitions cannot be reused through another lookup or recovery. Native-file admission and Linux/macOS reflink copying retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Native Windows Server, Node 26.10.0, same configuration and 490 matching dependency manifest entries; actual built tarballs installed normally, no installed-code patches. Exact unpatched parent `a0af795745b6` → candidate `cd5b2465e0aa`:

  | Measurement | Parent | Candidate |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Warm first `/readyz` 200 | 68.678s | 54.930s |
  | Warm `models status` | 43.537s | 34.276s |
  | Warm Codex plugin load | 35.745s | 26.840s |
  | First-post-install readiness | 152.328s | 146.890s |
  | First-post-install `models status` | 82.764s | 65.250s |

  One run per cell, candidate tested before parent; not randomized or a statistical guarantee. First-run model-runtime subphase regressed from 10.244s to 13.353s despite faster overall commands. All real health/readiness probes reached 200 and model commands exited 0. No authenticated model-turn proof. Earlier published-tag measurements are a different codebase and are not used to attribute this patch’s effect.
- 98 tests across six focused files passed (43.68s Vitest, 45.59s wrapper, `--maxWorkers=1`), covering redundant opens, destination replacement, cold/cached receipts, lazy retry/alias/recovery rejection, source changes, and native siblings. `pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.streaming.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 11 passed, 21.45s wall time including compilation. The three added synchronous race cases took 31ms total locally; hosted CI seconds are not yet measured.
- Changed-file guards, core and all 27 selected test typecheck graphs, and dead-export scans passed. The initial consistent-return lint failure was fixed; the targeted lint rerun passed with no warnings or errors.
- Canonical package build and tarball integrity passed for `cd5b2465e0aa787b9ebd4b419fe5eaa410bb985a`. The unrelated UI startup-JS size warning also reproduces on the exact unpatched parent: 374,724 B versus the 373,454 B limit (candidate: 374,734 B). Both package-integrity checks passed.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings after resolving the destination-admission and failed-lookup findings.

title: fix: Daybreak chats fail with unsupported Ultrafast settings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unsupported Ultrafast settings prevent Daybreak chats from replying, and provider validation failures hide the actual error behind misleading advice to start a new conversation.

## User Impact

Daybreak Blue keeps Standard and Fast; Daybreak Red uses Standard. Unsupported choices are disabled, and stale preferences fall back consistently in controls and requests without rewriting saved preferences. Other native OpenAI tier rejections retry at a slower tier only before output, tool activity, or active-response steering.

Unrecovered validation failures show a bounded, credential-redacted provider diagnostic, such as “Invalid service_tier argument,” as literal text rather than the response body. Provider messages can include noncredential request-value excerpts; this change intentionally preserves the actual diagnostic. Known context, token-limit, and storage failures retain their recovery guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

One provider-owned tier policy feeds request construction and catalog projection. The existing Responses recovery owner handles explicit tier rejection across native SSE and WebSocket without replaying ambiguous failures or already-started output. Account-bound observations keep advertised tier choices accurate; current-main credential identity and harness filtering remain authoritative. No new setting, persistence format, or deployment change.

Explicit low-level serviceTier / service_tier overrides remain selectable; the native API's explicit rejection can trigger the same safe slower-tier recovery. Custom compatible endpoints and native Codex tier policy are unchanged.

Thanks @VACInc for the picker report and implementation direction, and @steipete for requesting actionable diagnostics and safe fallback.

The optional tier-policy hook reuses the existing fast-mode context and changes no trust, authority, persistence, configuration, or required host capability. [Review-policy disposition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164597#issuecomment-5981227115).

title: fix(nodes): restore update headroom for split worker bundles
body:
Related: #160442. Companion budget-gate draft: #164494.

## What Problem This Solves

Thousands of small worker chunks consume the installed-package entry headroom required by the immutable 2026.9.7/2026.9.8 updaters.

## User Impact

Reduces worker deployment files while retaining split-worker startup and memory behavior. **Draft only: final-candidate performance, the full release build, installed-tree count, and the published-driver update cell are not yet proven.** No operator configuration, shipped updater limit, or worker manifest version changes. Optional-feature first-use costs remain a validation risk.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use 64 KiB entries-aware subgroup merging at the existing worker build owner. Keep the cold-start static closure on automatic chunking, and keep normal turn preparation/retained-worker cleanup separate from other optional code. The first turn still loads its runtime after admission. Strict execution order, entry signatures, chunk closure checks, and the v1 manifest/hash owner remain in place.

Rolldown 1.2.9 `minSize` only filters manual groups; setting it alone produced byte-identical output. Blanket grouping pulled 21–38 MB into startup, and protecting only startup increased retained text-turn RSS by over 100 MiB. The phase-aware grouping avoids those prototype regressions. Explicit roots include GitHub profile disposal because every idle-retained result performs that cleanup even without a GitHub assignment.

## Evidence

**Prototype measurements — not final-candidate/package proof.** On one Linux Blacksmith Testbox, using real emitted worker processes and real provider text turns through a synthetic local Gateway RPC owner:

| Measurement | Baseline | Layered 64 KiB prototype |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Worker build chunks | 5,032 | 2,175 |
| Spawn → accepted hello | 138.373 ms | 129.791 ms |
| Retained RSS after three text turns | 273.36 MiB | 250.81 MiB |

All three exact replies completed on the retained worker. The cold static graph stayed at 170 chunks / 1,914,441 bytes / 1,245 modules. These are single controlled observations, not percentiles or full production Gateway/node-pairing proof. The earlier optimization’s published 209 ms / 243.6 MiB measurements used another host/base and are not this comparison’s baseline.

- **Current candidate:** focused checks passed **2 tests; 63 skipped** (21.23 s wrapper wall). Production and test-file type-aware lint passed with zero warnings/errors. Native independent review was scoped-clean at P0–P2; lead review accepted draft publication only.
- **Prior variant only:** full coverage passed 19 worker-deployment cases plus 46 build-config cases (**65 total**), including relocated artifact execution. These are not final-candidate full-suite results. Synthetic-entry fixtures now bind the same chunking helper to their own entry roots.
- **UNRUN for the final candidate:** full release-faithful build, installed-tree count against the unchanged 47,500-entry / 900 MiB budget, and the 2026.9.7 → candidate published-driver cell. Testbox provisioning remained queued without a VM or Actions run; the owned attempts were stopped. No proof was substituted from another pool.
- The attempted prototype live exec/read turn failed identically on baseline and candidate with `Shared-state read and cleanup failed`; no successful live tool-turn RSS or continuity claim is made.

Publication records the implementation for review, not completion of the fix. Keep this PR draft until the remaining Testbox proof is complete. Landing requires explicit approval from Peter.

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

title: feat(sessions): allow directed sends without transcript access
body:
Related: #59149 — implements the send-only proposal from @holgergruenhagen’s deployment report, not the broader per-agent read-scope or inbound-consent redesign.

## What Problem This Solves

Specialist agents cannot ask an approved ops agent for help under narrow session visibility without also opening cross-agent transcript access or using an operator-level workaround.

## User Impact

Operators can keep `tools.sessions.visibility` narrow and configure `agents.entries.<id>.tools.agentToAgent.send` for explicit outbound destinations. Omission preserves existing behavior; `[]` denies ordinary cross-agent sends; IDs and `*` patterns select destinations. Global participation, sandbox limits, incognito restrictions, and existing child/session-incarnation grants remain intact.

The target can return the requested run's reply, but this grants no history, search, listing, status, session-control, or hidden watch access. Sending to a privileged agent is still permission to ask it to act, not a tenant-isolation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session-policy owner now distinguishes send-only grants from read visibility. It evaluates watches at that same boundary and compiles outbound patterns only when needed for a send. Removing an agent prunes exact destinations while preserving an emptied deny-all list. Current destination permission is checked again at input admission after asynchronous preparation. Revoking permission does not retract input the target already accepted or its owed reply.

Configuration, session-tool, and security docs include an explicit multi-agent example, direct `agentId` usage without discovery access, omitted/empty semantics, and trust limits. One optional setting adds three core schema nodes; generated baselines were regenerated for that intentional capability, with no default change.

**Upgrade compatibility:** this adds no database schema, retained field, migration, or config rewrite. Existing configurations omit the new field and keep their previous visibility behavior. `schema.help.runtime.ts` only documents the optional setting. Explicitly configured `[]` is intentionally deny-all; removing an agent preserves that state rather than broadening access.

## Evidence

- **307 focused tests passed** for implementation commit `1f065bf6` with frozen-lockfile dependencies, including authenticated loopback and in-process Gateway/SQLite boundaries. The 13-file run with `--maxWorkers=1` took **142.69 s wall** (including compile/startup).
- **CI follow-up is test-only:** the four existing steering-provenance scenarios now register guarded injection V2 and forward its assertion through the real receiver helper. All four passed in **36.16 s wall** with `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-steering.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; pending-input and transcript assertions are unchanged. Three obsolete mock baseline entries were removed after documenting synthetic isolation. Mock, assertion-safety, SQLite-worker and import-cycle checks pass; no production permission check was weakened.
- **Current-main conflict repair:** only the two generated config baselines conflicted. Regeneration preserved all authored feature source, tests, and docs byte-for-byte. On the combined `dc518bfc` base, **91 focused cases passed in 149.92 s wall**, including both real Gateway suites, steering, policy, queue authority, and config regressions. Core types, config docs, prompt snapshots, mock and line-cap checks pass.
- **Revocation red/green proof:** four actual-tool resolution cases failed before repair. Current tests reject withdrawn destinations by agent ID, key, label, and session ID before dispatch; global withdrawal also denies while unrelated config reloads continue.
- **Final-effect proof:** with the real Gateway writer blocked before pending-input staging, withdrawing permission produces no pending input, transcript change, or target execution. Paired cases preserve input accepted before withdrawal, including withdrawal before the caller receives the acknowledgment. Real steering/SQLite tests also reject before enqueue and retain already accepted guidance.
- **Compatibility:** existing child/scoped grants, same-agent behavior, sandbox/global ceilings, source routing, native followup custody, and standalone operator-authenticated loopback sends are covered. Destination policy uses the existing input-commit guard on hosted calls and the existing wire-dispatch guard for standalone clients; no host callback is sent across the wire.
- Core production and affected test-graph typechecks, changed-file lint (31 files), line-cap/max-lines ratchets, canonical prompt snapshot checks, docs config/link checks, and fresh independent P0–P2 review passed. Prompt snapshots are regenerated, not waived.
- An earlier real-provider, isolated three-agent run verified allowed replies, unlisted/reverse denial, read/watch separation, scoped listing, and no private synthetic-canary leakage. That provider run predates this final admission correction; current revocation evidence is the real Gateway/SQLite boundary proof above. No production configuration or deployment changed.
- **Known baseline failure:** full `pnpm lint:core` reports 13 max-lines errors in files byte-identical to main `42ebb9d7` and still unchanged at `81fd8641`. This PR's changed-file lint and structural ratchets pass; full-repository lint is not claimed green.
- **Final landing:** final-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review completed. The enforced CI gate passed on `e86b6406`; the observed run used 9,493 aggregate job-seconds across 85 jobs (whole-run cost, not feature-only runtime). title: fix: release discarded text behind cached previews and process output
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Small retained process outputs, Memory Wiki previews, and web-fetch protocol fields could keep much larger discarded source strings alive through V8 sliced-string backing storage.

Related: #164361.

## User Impact

Retained results release discarded text while preserving output, Unicode (including lone surrogates), cache behavior, publication ordering, and persisted JSON. No configuration, schema, migration, or TTL changes are needed.

These fixes address independently reproduced retention paths. They do not establish a fix for the broader production completed-turn heap-growth slope.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Process output owns incoming chunk storage and detached truncated tails, including pending poll/replay buffers.
- Memory Wiki publishes its active cache from the already-serialized persistence payload. This detaches every snapshot branch, not just overview snippets, and keeps hot and cold cache content identical.
- Web fetch owns bounded contentType, extractor, and fetchedAt strings, including provider values that arrive already sliced and below their limits.

## Evidence

- **Upgrade/downgrade compatibility verified:** old writer → new reader and new writer → old reader both pass using the real cache publication/read implementations at base fa6623097fedd7644162b446bb20a04f2eafef66 and this PR head. Gzip payload bytes, blob keys, metadata, and generation hashes are identical; Unicode and lone surrogates are preserved. The blob-store fixture is in memory; no migration or stored-format change exists.
- **Exact-head CI passed:** [run 37143243003](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37143243003), 437 seconds elapsed, head 9d88139c6b25b21077d99b783b81a4cdeba80bd6.
- Process regression: eight small retained outputs formerly kept **16,777,256 external bytes** from 16 MiB of discarded donor text; fixed: **40 external bytes**, with **82,344 heap bytes**. Covers live and completed records, chunked callbacks, already-sliced input, staged poll results, output accounting, and Unicode.
- Actual Memory Wiki publication/cache-load probe: eight previews totaling **5,600 characters** formerly retained **16,777,256 external bytes**; fixed: **40 external bytes**. The real publication owner and overview projection ran with an in-memory blob-store fixture, not a live Gateway.
- Web-fetch provider-fallback/cache regression fails on the original code at **6,487,232 retained heap bytes** against a 2 MiB allowance; fixed passes. Covers oversized and already-sliced metadata, cache hits, truncation flags, and surrogate boundaries.
- **123 tests passed across seven files** in **74.17 s**: process registry and exec runtime; web-fetch output contract, provider fallback, and cache; Wiki cache publication and its existing lifecycle integration suite.
- Planned changed-file gates completed: production core/extension types, all **27 core-test type graphs**, extension-test types, changed-file lint (zero warnings/errors), dead exports, formatting, and selected ownership/dependency/schema guards. Validation was resumed after correcting the new fixture's explicit type guarantees and documenting the serialized-payload assertion invariant.
- Independent Codex review: **scoped-clean through P2**, no actionable findings. Subsequent changes only strengthened test-fixture narrowing and added the required assertion-invariant comment.

title: fix: restore missing ordinary iMessage final replies
body:
Related: #160009

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary iMessage final replies disappear when a turn runs with a prepared or filtered plugin registry, even without a Gateway reload.

## User Impact

User impact: the final answer is sent once through the admitting Gateway and retains its platform message ID and delivery custody. Actual reloads still reject changed senders, channel registrations, settings, or closed/superseded Gateway owners. No config or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A different registry object does not necessarily mean a new Gateway publication. Prepared views already inherit the admitting publication's immutable registration snapshot. This fix uses that existing owner-bound snapshot to distinguish an ordinary view from a successor, then selects the live Gateway registry for final delivery. It does not broaden registration equivalence or make sender-preserving handoff optional for actual successors.

## Evidence

- The raw and structured prepared-view regressions fail on base `60f64f5537333e081e828c9fba46c64fe8b506ce` with the original no-handoff rejection, and pass with this fix. Real pending-final persistence advances from prepared to delivered and is cleared after confirmed success, with no queued retry left behind.
- The iMessage monitor regression follows a real inbound notification through binding admission, actual prepared-registry creation, buffered final dispatch, the durable adapter, mocked native RPC, message-sent hooks, and SQLite echo persistence. It also fails on the original runtime and passes with the fix. Only model output and Apple RPC are substituted; successful durable delivery is not mocked.

- Changed-file checks passed, including production and test types, formatting, lint, boundaries, ratchets, and dead-export/import-cycle guards. Independent AutoReview at P0/P1: scoped-clean.

title: fix(ui): saved-message recovery counts cleared drafts as messages
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a confusing saved-message notice that counts cleared drafts as recoverable messages and leaves people guessing what they would restore or delete.

## User Impact

Saved drafts open with their actual text and attachment filenames visible before the actions. Empty records no longer inflate the count. People can review a saved copy without sending it, or explicitly delete it without deleting chat history. Messages with uncertain delivery remain paused and warn before retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery now distinguishes useful input from internal cleared-draft records. It preserves the canonical revision fences and migration receipts while removing empty recovery copies that could fill the bounded recovery list. Restore and confirmed deletion share the existing ownership and transfer checks; IndexedDB deletion retains a newer revision fence while releasing attachment bytes. No schema, permission, or retention-limit changes.

title: fix(update): packaged upgrades fail through macOS directory aliases
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: packaged upgrades fail during package activation when npm temporarily removes an install root reached through a POSIX directory alias such as macOS `/var` → `/private/var`.

## User Impact

Users can update a global npm installation through the normal updater without a false “requires its original POSIX npm directory” rollback.

The update executor records the canonical installation identity while the package still exists. During activation, npm has temporarily removed that leaf; root resolution previously fell back to the raw alias spelling and rejected the same installation. The resolver now canonicalizes the existing parent only when the leaf is genuinely absent. Existing unresolved leaves, including dangling symlinks, remain fail-closed.

title: fix: keep public reads available under cache pressure
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes public conversations and preview images intermittently becoming unavailable when an older render finishes after newer cached results and the cache is under memory pressure.

## User Impact

Successful public reads remain usable instead of immediately becoming stale, while the existing 16 MiB cache budget, publication checks, and revocation behavior remain intact. Preview PNGs also avoid repeated base64 encoding and decoding; their existing five-minute browser-cache policy is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat completing a render as its most recent use before choosing byte-pressure victims. Reuse the same representation cache for PNG Buffers rather than introducing another cache or storage layer.

Requested by @vincentkoc.

title: fix(chat): serve lightweight images and keep mobile viewing responsive
body:
Related: #149361
Consolidates the delivery foundation from #173113 and the mobile viewer correction into one complete main-targeted feature. The delivery-only PR remains supporting history until this replacement lands.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: large chat images waste bandwidth on slow connections, opening a preview can fetch original files and speculative neighbors, and image failures offer an unhelpful Open original escape hatch with clipped error text.

## User Impact

Uploaded/inbound and managed still images use compressed WebP renditions at 480/960/1920-pixel longest-side tiers, capped at 96/256/512 KiB, without enlargement and with alpha/orientation preserved. Failed or stream-only optimized previews never silently transfer originals.

Tap an image to open its cached preview immediately. A bounded, screen-sized rendition loads in place; a slow or failed upgrade keeps the preview and zoom, with a visible Retry action. Error text remains readable on narrow screens.

Uploaded/managed original bytes load only for explicit Download image or Copy image actions. Third-party image URLs retain a secondary browser link because an image can display normally while its host forbids CORS downloads; that link is not offered as managed-preview recovery. Downloads follow the selected gallery item, not the initially opened item. Screen-sized viewing is capped at the delivery layer’s 1920-pixel tier; full original quality remains available through those explicit actions.

Legacy assistant-local file URLs and full animated GIFs retain their existing original-byte rendering contract; they do not falsely advertise responsive rendition URLs or start a duplicate display upgrade.

Artifact connections to a different-origin Gateway or WebSocket-only proxy receive bounded WebP previews through the existing authenticated artifact RPC. Same-origin HTTP remains preferred; an unavailable HTTP route can reauthorize one bounded RPC preview instead of transferring original bytes. Explicit original downloads keep their existing transport policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Let native signed image URLs use density-aware srcset, lazy loading and async decoding. Authenticated blob requests select a bounded viewport/DPR tier.
- Upgrade only the selected image, never speculative gallery neighbors. Keep inline/display rendition subscriptions separate, including artifact-only images, and retain exact-scope blob leases through navigation and close.
- Reauthorize recoverable failed native metadata on explicit retry/download, without bypassing denial. Keep file actions secondary and inside the existing viewer instead of opening another tab.

title: fix(ui): background updates rescan lists and dismiss terminal menus

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unrelated updates repeatedly rescan large management lists, and restoring terminal tabs can steal focus from a menu opened while restoration is pending.

## User Impact

Devices, Plugins and Skills avoid unnecessary list preparation while search, receipt replacements and feedback stay live. Terminal restoration preserves newer pointer/keyboard intent, selected tabs and usable menus.

## Why This Change Was Made

Derive expensive list work from actual replacement snapshots, query and scope. During passive restoration, observe newer input and suppress only the emulator's opening autofocus through its existing per-tab runtime; explicit focus remains unchanged and observers retire on finish/unmount.

title: feat: let plugin tools show native views in chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Let trusted, operator-installed plugins surface their own interactive controls at the point they are useful in a conversation, without sending the user away to a separate page or asking the agent to generate a one-off UI.

For an internal incident-management plugin, that might be a live incident dashboard with an Acknowledge button and a link to its full panel. The agent decides **when** to show it; the plugin owns **what** it is and does. A tool supplies a data descriptor for a pre-existing component, which appears immediately and can later be reconstructed from history as it approaches the viewport.

**Why not sandboxed widgets?** Sandboxed widgets and MCP Apps remain the right choice for generated or isolated content, including interactive experiences through their supported bridges. This use case is different: the operator has already installed and trusted a native plugin whose browser code can use authenticated host APIs, share application state, and open native panels. Requiring its inline view to be a separate sandboxed integration adds cross-frame communication and state coordination just to change where that UI appears. This feature brings the existing native-plugin model into the transcript instead.

The invariant is unchanged: **the agent selects from registered components and supplies data; it never supplies executable UI code.** All executable code comes from the active installed plugin, under the same trust boundary as its native pages and panels.

## User Impact

User impact: installed plugins can show rich, interactive views directly in the conversation, immediately after a successful tool result. Reopening history reconstructs views only near the viewport, without rerunning the agent or tool.

This uses the existing native-plugin trust boundary and Custom plugin UI setting. The agent supplies data, not UI code. Plugin authors remain responsible for safe rendering, current-viewer resource authorization, and repeatable mount behavior; core adds no sandbox, HTML policing, or per-plugin RPC allowlist.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an owner-bound `api.inlineView(viewId, payload, { version, summary })` result helper, a versioned backend declaration, and `host.ui.registerInlineView`. One durable record carries plugin/view identity, the component interface version, payload, and text fallback, associated with the originating invocation. The installed native renderer must explicitly register the same interface version; there is no silent latest-version dispatch or core migration engine.

Payloads are limited to 16 KiB of serialized UTF-8, summaries to 4 KiB of serialized JSON, and interface versions to integers 1–65535. Missing plugins or unsupported versions leave the complete saved record intact and show its summary; a compatible registration can render it when available again. Compatibility/admission is resolved by the current browser catalog, not competing Gateway/browser schema systems.

Data freshness is entirely plugin-owned: a component may render a saved snapshot, fetch current data from a stored resource ID, or combine both. The incident example deliberately hydrates current state and shares it with a panel. Restoration does not rerun the original tool or agent; plugin network reads are allowed.

**Transfer scope:** native Markdown and catalog/Beam mirroring intentionally export the saved summary. Native HTML export retains the complete raw record and invocation metadata, without packaging executable renderer code. Full rich Beam transport and a general rich-session importer are not implemented; external catalog imports remain untrusted text. Text fallback is not claimed as full rich-component transfer.

## Evidence

### Landed and verified

**Merged on 2026-10-23 at 16:26 UTC** as [1c2c8f033c6b34d766fd8ab377bc27417535cacd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1c2c8f033c6b34d766fd8ab377bc27417535cacd), from reviewed source **e31c6388cccce4db019a356335546e5baccef6c4**. The complete landed tree **3b306a2c9ce51e3e73d5f3570d91058fb8c05136** independently matches the reviewed head composed with actual landing parent **e84dae9faea30a740b87d569dc56b72e4c906bd7**. Main containment and both human co-author trailers were verified. [Native completion receipt/comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173135#issuecomment-6369629008) is complete; the PR preparation worktree and branches were cleaned up.

**CI qualification is not an all-green claim.** [Exact-head run 39981087094/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39981087094) finished 101 successful, 19 skipped and two failed jobs. The sole root was [Android 16KB SDK provisioning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39981087094/job/120508973839): sdkmanager could not read the external Google system-image ZIP, before emulator boot, Gradle or application instrumentation. The missing report upload and aggregate gate followed that setup failure. **Android 16KB application coverage was unexecuted; the failed attempt remains failed.** The protected native unrelated-failure route admitted the source-qualified exception after validating exact source, tested merge, artifacts, current writer authority and security/review gates. Actual baseline/tested-merge workflow, toolchain actions, dependency-install shell and Android tree match; the known example-workspace lockfile delta is retained and noncausal. No separately executed failing-main result or underlying archive-corruption cause is claimed.

All Node, UI/E2E, both selected real-Gateway groups, hosted performance and Periphery jobs succeeded. Dedicated WebKit steps were skipped. Latest exact-tuple security-sensitive and dependency reviews succeeded; formal reviews were absent, not approvals. The local fixture correction below preserves finite deadlines and all assertions; it does not relabel historical failures or missing coverage.

One local **beforeEach clock owner** now serves the registration fixture. It replaces the intermediate conversion-only wrapper and duplicate deadline-case setup, reducing the delta by two net lines. The **finite 500ms caller budget, all 28 cases, every assertion, fetch/header/redaction check, and afterEach restoration remain intact**. Only explicit deadline scenarios advance time. Production HTTP/body parsing, credentials, SSRF, proxy and current-authority behavior are unchanged; no timeout, budget or dependency was changed.

One original-order observation passed all 28 cases and showed that the ordinary HTTP-401 and provider-default cases spent **67.6ms and 78.6ms in synchronous request-policy preparation** before their respective correct authentication/ok outcomes. Both used real time, with no observed leaked fake clock. This supports making fixture time deterministic for behavioral tests, but does not establish the historical CI failures' exact phases.

Two deliberate expiry controls kept the original assertions meaningful:
- Holding the **real HTTP 401 error-body reader**, then advancing **501ms**, produced unavailable/transport, one fetch, one body cancellation, negative remaining time and **zero timers**. The original authentication assertion failed.
- Expiring the provider-default caller before evaluation produced unavailable/transport, **zero fetches**, negative remaining time and zero timers. The original success assertion failed.

Both controls were completely removed. **Final owning-file verification passed 28/28 cases with no skips**, including all four original image/response deadline and abort cases. Owning extension types, targeted lint/format and fresh independent P0–P2 delta review passed with no actionable findings. The review examined source and retained proof, not an independent execution. These controls prove protected expiry paths and assertions—not exact historical reproduction or current CI success.

**Preceding [295 CI 39975264956/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39975264956) remains failed:** 101 successful, 19 skipped and two failed jobs, comprising one Levanto job with two cases plus its aggregate gate. HTTP 401 returned transport instead of authentication; provider-default returned unavailable instead of ok. The failed log explicitly shows all five controlled conversion cases and four deadline/abort cases passing. No timeout/DNS/inherited attribution is asserted from duration alone, and no CI exception is claimed.

All three UI jobs, all nine E2E matrix jobs, both selected real-Gateway execution groups, hosted performance and both Periphery workflows passed in that preceding attempt. The earlier service-worker setup timeout remains an investigated historical gap, not a claimed repair. Its local A-only probe completed setup in **25.386s**, versus roughly **114s of production build** in the failed CI setup; runtime, graph and concurrent load differed. No speculative serial scheduling, cache, compression bypass, larger deadline or B-reuse change was added. This publication contains the reviewed fixture-lifecycle correction, not an unchanged rerun for green.

### Retained product and visual proof

Production is byte-identical to reviewed **6cdb24b280f75fb4b7e985be450df084fcfeb3e1**. Its real cold-widget regression reproduced four redundant chrome elements: eligible data was captured before lazy renderer registration, and mounting alone did not republish eligibility. Removing only the obsolete registration predicate fixes that reachable defect while preserving loaded-data/layout checks and current provider/widget/connected-view/session/agent/revision/read-only action guards. This does not claim exact historical CI timing.

The cold regression and three unchanged desktop/mobile/read-only browser cases pass, with **61 owner/sibling tests**, pre-mount no-effect and current/stale-target action checks. Full **88-file review**, build/type/lint and source-bound inline/Gateway/SDK proof remain applicable; the new test-only delta has its own review. The integrated f033 inventory preserves **51 unique files, seven serial and 44 parallel**. No feature proof or old asset hash is relabeled as a newly executed build.

The separate preceding ordinary build's **9 B startup advisory overrun** remains recorded; no allowance or baseline was raised and no normal-build retry erased it. Historical gallery/DNS/reload/menu uncertainty and local WebKit setup failure remain documented. No live model/provider, third-party ACL or rich remote Beam coverage is claimed.

Actual **1280×900** Chromium captures use matching dark theme and synthetic content. They were inspected and delivered as image attachments in the originating conversation. title: fix: keep file editors idle during unrelated panel updates
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unrelated metadata updates to an open file panel repeatedly dispatch editor reconfiguration and decoration transactions.

## User Impact

Open file editors avoid unnecessary editor transactions when only panel metadata changes, without losing focus, draft text, search navigation, or reload behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor adapter skips unchanged editable and line-decoration effects. Decoration reuse also requires the same immutable CodeMirror document, so changed documents still refresh line anchors. The sole production caller derives a fresh readonly match array for each synchronization.

## Evidence

- Ten unrelated panel updates previously dispatched 20 CodeMirror transactions; the regression now observes 0 while preserving the focused editor node and draft.
- Relevant typing, discard, and in-place source-text changes still update the editor.
- All 16 Chromium file-editor scenarios passed in 5.85 seconds wall time, covering search, wrapping, line endings, undo, saving, conflict reload, retained drafts, and teardown.
- The changed-document positive control verifies that the same requested line is decorated again after an in-place source-text replacement.
- Targeted type/lint/format checks and canonical independent P0–P2 review passed. This is structural work measurement, not INP.
- [Primary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38736503824) passed: 28 executed jobs, 5,817 execution-job seconds. Execution-job seconds exclude separate security/advisory workflows and are not billing minutes.

This is a behavior-only change with no markup or styling changes. Component proof is not physical-device or live-provider latency evidence.

title: fix(plugin-sdk): unblock private-QA builds over the declaration limit
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: local private-QA builds stop at the SDK declaration-size check because compatibility-code typing also retains literal migration descriptions and test paths.

## User Impact

Source-checkout validation can build the SDK again without raising its size limit. No runtime behavior, SDK export, compatibility code, metadata record, deprecation window, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compatibility registry already exposes generic metadata records with a finite code union. A module-local typed assembly keeps that union exact without carrying every metadata literal into public declarations. It returns the same array and records.

## Evidence

- Public-entry declarations decreased from **5,390,918 to 5,234,235 bytes**, below the unchanged **5,340,536-byte** private-QA limit. After integrating inspected main changes, regeneration measured **5,233,378 bytes**. No ratchet, variance, enforcement, or environment-spoofing change.
- Matched actual before/after public declarations preserve exact compatibility-code type equality and assignability both ways. Both reject an unknown code, arbitrary `string`, and `unknown` (six expected TS2322 diagnostics).
- All **137 records**, including order and every metadata value, retain byte-identical JSON: 153,190 bytes; SHA-256 `58d004c2beb667912f59f1ac70f97d70387a24f643f3c737da117262b457b240`.

title: fix(chat): large image previews waste bandwidth on slow connections
body:
Related: #149361
Related: #172914

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat image previews can consume excessive bandwidth on slow connections, and an unavailable artifact preview can silently return original image bytes.

## User Impact

Uploaded and managed still images have size-bounded WebP previews, without changing original downloads, transparency, orientation, or access checks.

This PR is retained as delivery-layer review history. The complete delivery + responsive viewer feature is consolidated in #173161, targeting main under ordinary enforced gates. This delivery-only PR will close as superseded after the integrated feature is verified merged; it is not a separate landing target. WebP is not guaranteed to be smaller than every small original image. Animated-image eligibility remains unchanged. Unmanaged assistant-local file routes keep their existing original-byte behavior, including local GIF/APNG/animated WebP; the bounded-compression guarantee here is for uploaded/inbound and managed still images.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one existing thumbnail owner with fixed 480/960/1920-pixel longest-side renditions and 96/256/512 KiB ceilings. Separate rendition cache entries, update WebP MIME handling, and invalidate older immutable previews. Failed or stream-only thumbnail requests are unavailable rather than opening an original stream; original byte and range behavior stays intact.

## Evidence

Current-head CI [38745916201, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38745916201) remains **failed**: the sole root is Mermaid renderer startup in `checks-ui (2/3)`; image-related checks, security, types/lint and UI E2E passed. The failure-report row is job-name-only. Its scheduled-main comparison passed the exact Mermaid case and failed a different palette test, so no matching-signature inherited exception is claimed. Two isolated actual-base Bun controls also passed; the CI startup timeout is not reproduced or fixed. Bounded cold-start and observed eight-file same-session baseline controls passed without reproducing the timeout; no repair or inherited exception is claimed; no CI rerun, timeout increase or assertion relaxation was used.


- Independent first-layer checkout: **115 Gateway tests** and **140 existing-UI tests** passed. The focused commands used one worker; combined wall time was **107.43 s** for the three Gateway files (including 35.11 s cold worker preparation) and **24.04 s** for the three UI files. CI seconds are pending.
- Core production typecheck and focused lint passed against identical Gateway sources. Independent UI typecheck **19.97 s**, fresh production UI build **15.97 s**, and formatting/diff checks passed.
- Real HTTP tests cover rendition-specific bounds and caches, WebP decoding with alpha, EXIF rotation, invalid widths, explicit originals, HEAD/ranges, and unavailable/missing/stream preview bodies.
- Dense synthetic fixture: **258,076 B PNG at 400×200 → 68,296 B WebP at 600×300**. This comparison is a transfer-size/detail regression, not a guarantee for every image.
- Phone-sized Chromium proof decoded a production-encoded **960×640 WebP** and exercised explicit retry. It uses the real production UI with synthetic Gateway/media fixtures, not a physical phone or live cellular connection.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review: no actionable findings in the candidate scope.

### CI follow-up and remaining local gap

The first CI head exposed two stale test expectations (PNG dimensions and the immutable preview version) and an unguarded loopback fetch in a new fixture. The repaired head updates the assertions and uses the existing SSRF guard with only the leased origin allowed and redirects disabled. title: feat(typesafe): support custom decision servers through provider settings
body:
Closes #155155

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot connect TypeSafe decisions to a separate System One inference host or HTTPS reverse proxy through the standard model-provider settings.

## User Impact

Configure `models.providers.typesafe` with `baseUrl`, an optional `apiKey`, `models: []`, and the existing `request` settings. Select `typesafe/kev-latest` as the agent's `decisionModel` for Kev; router-backed servers must use their own routing model IDs. Existing hosted and loopback plugin configuration remains supported. No new TypeSafe-specific network or authentication switches are introduced.

Evaluations send state, questions, and rubrics—user content—to the configured server. The existing provider HTTP(S) contract applies; use HTTPS outside loopback. Configured custom origins get the normal exact-origin LAN/tailnet trust, with the existing `request.allowPrivateNetwork` opt-out/opt-in. TLS verification, localhost pinning, redirect rejection, and managed-proxy authority remain intact. Ambient proxies are not implicitly enabled for configured endpoints.

Explicit bearer/header auth with an empty credential now fails closed in the shared sanitizer instead of silently dropping the override. Valid existing request settings are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuses the shared provider request resolver, SSRF policy, TLS/proxy handling, and exact credential matcher rather than introducing a parallel TypeSafe policy.
- Uses the existing model-provider SecretInput preparation owner. An explicit provider entry never inherits the hosted plugin credential and does not discover ambient/profile fallback. Current route and credential authority are rechecked immediately before dispatch.
- Preserves routing model IDs and sends exactly one request to `/v1/systemone` for origin-only or `/v1` API roots. Known reflected credentials are rejected in raw and decoded JSON, including configured-header credentials.

## Evidence

Only final socket routing maps the synthetic RFC1918 answer to an isolated local server; SSRF policy and TLS stay real.

title: fix(vllm): honor discovered serving context ceilings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw budgets against a configured model window larger than the running vLLM server's limit when wildcard discovery is enabled.

## User Impact

User impact: reply and manual-compaction budgets honor a positively observed `max_model_len` while preserving smaller configured limits. Explicit/manual providers still perform no discovery, and model endpoint/API overrides cannot borrow another route's ceiling. Refresh the catalog after changing the serving limit; prepared turns remain stable. No config migration or new option is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing discovery correctly reads vLLM's limit, but later configured-model overlays can replace it. Carry the serving observation separately through the existing catalog acquisition and runtime publication, then apply it only to the same model and route. Static/cloud catalog defaults keep their existing precedence. This adds no per-request probe or periodic polling.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes generic “OpenClaw couldn't finish this request/reply” messages when native Codex startup throttling or streamed OpenAI usage-limit codes lack recognizable error prose.

## User Impact

Rate limits retain their existing retry and actionable failure guidance in channel chats, including Telegram, and the Control UI. Subscription plans that do not include usage receive billing guidance instead of a generic failure. Temporary throttling does not inherit a subscription reset cooldown. No configuration or migration is required.

The web UI is not an exact copy of Telegram: it can also display lifecycle diagnostics. This fixes classification before either surface renders the outcome, rather than suppressing real failures in Telegram.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the Codex terminal-error normalizer for rejected turn startup so structured status survives into the shared runner. Recognize OpenAI's usage-limit and missing-plan codes in the existing provider classifier instead of depending on provider wording. Unknown startup errors still propagate unchanged.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix regressions: all three startup fixtures failed with the unnormalized native error; the OpenAI code-only classification fixture returned undefined instead of rate_limit.
- Post-fix: 183 tests passed across the startup/lifecycle, terminal projection, provider-review recovery, and OpenAI provider suites. Single-worker command completed in 148.10 seconds. The existing native attempt suite took 59.31 seconds (123 tests); it exercises real attempt resource/terminal settlement, not only a parser. OpenAI provider suite: 17.72 seconds (37 tests). The two Codex projection/recovery files together: 57.31 seconds (23 tests, predominantly cold imports). After extraction, all 14 selected usage-limit/classification/provider-review cases passed again (105.49 seconds across three shards; warm OpenAI file 6.49 seconds). [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38747100943). Changed-test CI job elapsed times (whole jobs, not per-file test time): boundary 192s, extension config 300s, changed-node 582s, extension bundle 226s, compact-large 154s.
- Real ChatGPT Responses stream adapter → prepared OpenAI classifier → user-facing formatter: six synthetic SSE error/response.failed cases passed, including ordinary rate_limit_exceeded controls. Usage-limit cases render “The AI service needs a short break”; missing-plan cases render billing guidance. No external provider requests were made.
- Independent autoreview, including the final test extraction: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The test groups retain their original registration order and suite hooks; extraction avoids growing already oversized test files.
- Targeted source typecheck and typed lint passed with zero warnings/errors, including the extracted test files. Line-cap and assertion-safety gates passed; the retired mock exception was removed using the shrink-only owner command.
- Known inherited local gate failure: the unchanged baseline index at b93b150 reproduces OPENCLAW_* count 455 versus budget 454. This patch changes no counted names or budget entries; tracked separately rather than raising the baseline.
- Live Telegram delivery and the exact original provider payload were not available; this is deterministic provider/runner boundary proof, not a live Telegram claim.
- Upstream contract inspected at Codex e766f7598993ce37cf61b9c26c80cc2ba3a4f2d7: codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs maps retry exhaustion with HTTP status; app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/shared.rs and thread_data.rs retain those structured error facts.

Reported by @vincentkoc.

title: fix(compaction): avoid unnecessary recovery after prompt changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary mid-turn compaction when a tool changes the system prompt or tool definitions after the model has generated a substantial visible response.

## User Impact

Sessions using mid-turn prechecks, including small-context OpenAI-compatible local models, can continue with a fitting prompt instead of entering avoidable compaction recovery. Opaque reasoning and genuinely oversized requests remain protected. Existing opt-in and context-engine behavior is unchanged; no new configuration is introduced.

This is a current-main regression, not a proven explanation of the original Jetson/Qwen incident on OpenClaw 2026.9.4.

## Why This Change Was Made

Without a reusable measured request prefix, the guard estimated the visible transcript and then added the complete measured output again. The fresh estimate now treats measured completion usage as a lower bound, grouping async fragments from the same response, while leaving compaction-budget estimation unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact baseline comparison at `897a824e7ed5`: all three new real provider-admission/tool-loop cases fail on original production sources (3 failures, 14 sibling passes); all 17 cases pass with the repair. Covers system changes, tool-definition changes, and split visible completion.
- 17 provider-admission cases and 8 existing compaction-request-budget cases pass, including opaque reasoning, unchanged measured prefixes, missing usage, and genuinely oversized prompts.
- Provider-admission file: 12.56 seconds wall time (test cases 5–66 ms; wrapper 17.37 seconds). CI timing pending. No new sleeps, polling, or live provider calls.
- Focused lint and formatting pass; core production typecheck and all three agent test typecheck shards pass. The additional broad test-typecheck batch reached its 180-second command budget in the unrelated plugins/platform shard after nine passing shards; remaining broad coverage is left to CI.
- Fresh independent Codex/GPT-6.1 Sol P0–P2 review of commit `12f104d694009157ba9ed3928df81d190689c431`, with intact committed estimator/caller/async-fragment context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Exact-head CI [run 38703122990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38703122990) passed for published head `a7115f2b23f4e844b642e519317ae1b1414e5b21` (the publication commit has the same source tree). No Jetson hardware or incident logs were available.

title: fix(ui): keep New Session typing responsive during session updates
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary model-picker work that interrupts New Session typing when other sessions update, especially with a large model catalog.

## User Impact

New Session no longer reprocesses the entire model list for an unrelated session-row update. Model/default/account changes and connection recovery remain live. No configuration changes, migrations, or visual redesign.

This addresses a confirmed source of background jank; it does not claim to resolve every cause of the reported iPhone slowdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two subscriptions propagated unrelated activity into the draft picker: the sessions owner published row changes, and the catalog reader ignored its cache owner's scope-matching predicate. The view now observes default-field changes separately, and the reader honors the existing invalidation scope. The Gateway and existing model owners retain authority.

## Evidence

- Deterministic reproduction on the production renderer with 2,001 models and 500 sessions: **2,000 model-label preparation reads per unrelated row event before, zero after**, in both WebKit and Chromium. The sidebar still receives the event; no action RPCs or browser errors were observed.
- Extended the existing large-catalog typing E2E: 10 unrelated certified row updates, exact draft text, zero catalog preparation, retained textarea/model-option nodes, updated sidebar text, and zero added RPCs. Passed: **3.30s test / 31.88s command wall** (including bundled fixture setup).
- Mounted view plus existing model metadata/account/identity lifecycle tests: **27 passed / 14.50s wall**; changed mounted-view test **133ms**. The regression failed before repair, including with the incomplete defaults-only fix.
- UI typecheck, focused lint (four files, zero warnings/errors), formatting, and production build passed. Fresh independent autoreview: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, including both invalidation paths.
- Diagnostic warmed 26-character samples with synthetic row events at 4Hz: WebKit beforeinput-to-second-animation-frame p95 **265ms → 63ms**; Chromium **87.4ms → 54.9ms**. These are noisy single-host samples, not INP or real-device latency; Chromium profiling adds overhead.
- Browsers: Linux WebKit 26.6, mobile viewport 440×763/DPR3; desktop Chromium 153.0.8010.12, 1440×900. No physical iPhone, Firefox iOS shell, or OS-keyboard proof. No live Gateway changes or deployment.
- Corrected-head CI [38719516395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38719516395) completed in **1,212s wall (20m12s)**. Production/test types, lint, UI unit lanes, architecture, security-fast, and Control UI performance passed. The initial PR-caused missing fixture `kind` was corrected; its owning type graph and test pass.
- CI remains red on **five independently attributed inherited E2E jobs**, not represented as green. Exact failing tests/assertions were compared with scheduled-main logs; the failing source blobs/trees are unchanged in the tested merge:
  - Logs lifecycle, sidebar nesting/promotion, and PR chip label: matching failures on [main run 38713991924](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38713991924).
  - Sidebar running counts: matching `13 open sessions, 0 running` versus `12 running` on [main job 116375656647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38721065715/job/116375656647).
  - Workboard distribution: preexisting gateway-switch click timeout at the same line on [main job 116330109495](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38707273563/job/116330109495). The failure precedes plugin-route assertions; this PR does not change that fixture or gateway-confirmation owner.
- Landing uses the native, scoped inherited-failure exception after full source/run/security qualification. No CI reruns, ignored tests, or timeout increases.

title: fix(ui): large photos stall mobile chat and hide upload errors
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: mobile chat can download full-size photos just to display previews on slow connections, while rejected oversized attachments leave only a short-lived, easy-to-miss toast.

## User Impact

Uploaded-photo and managed-image previews are limited to 512 KiB. Originals remain unchanged and load through explicit open/download actions. Rejected files and readable recovery guidance remain beside the composer until removed.

Animated or unsupported thumbnail formats show an unavailable preview with access to the original, rather than transferring the original automatically or flattening animation. Existing upload limits and PNG worker resizing remain unchanged. This does not transcode local camera originals or change remote external-image policy. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The uploaded-photo display path requested original media, the artifact thumbnail route could return originals on failure, and its browser fallback could then fetch the full image over WebSocket. Both file-backed preview routes now share a byte-bounded thumbnail owner; failed HTTPS thumbnail transfers no longer invoke the full-size fallback. Explicit originals keep their existing transport behavior.

Reported and co-authored by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/15cd6e63-c5a0-48ba-a5b6-7e302d11a889)

## Evidence
