Exact reviewed head `2e019bddac51bedf6b01e5e03b1ac366670fbd58` passed [CI run 38726505643](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38726505643) without reruns. Whole-run CI wall time: **910 seconds** (11:19:26–11:34:36 UTC; not marginal test cost). Native landing verified the exact head; merge commit is on main.

- Main `5266c8d148624` introduced streamed file downloads while CI was running. Resolved the actual import conflict without changing its stream authority, expiry, backpressure, or abort behavior. Combined HTTP thumbnail/stream suite: 14 passed; current Solid image gallery: 7 passed; 74.99 s wrapper wall including worker compilation. Focused type-aware lint/format and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass.

- CI run 38722062891 failed only `checks-ui (2/3)`: four responsive full-app cases and their nested keyboard suite shared one failed 30-second readiness wait while cold-loading the development UI. The image-specific jobs passed. Local replays passed (71 cases with the exact pinned Bun runtime; 128 across the nearby five-file CI neighborhood), so these replays are not claimed as a causal fix or inherited-failure exemption.
- Fixture repair moves those five unchanged full-app cases to the existing bundled E2E lane, which completes its shared production build before browser navigation. The 66 layout/source-fixture cases remain in place. No retries, weakened assertions, or increased deadlines. `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-responsive.e2e.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 71 passed, 48.04 s wrapper wall; layout 12.50 s, E2E 28.90 s including build, five app assertions 4.91 s. Independent P0–P2 diff review found no actionable findings; it did not establish the historical timeout cause. The final exact-head hosted CI result and whole-run timing are recorded above.

- Follow-up review resolved: automatic managed-thumbnail URLs now use `v=3`, replacing immutable pre-byte-limit renditions. Browser regression loads a legacy `v=2` reference and verifies the new 400 px rendition is requested.
- Integrated main at `97d03398c3e1` for actual Solid-renderer/video-admission conflicts. Persistent errors now live in `chat-attachments.tsx`; existing video preparation is preserved. After integration: 140 attachment/message/lifecycle tests, video-admission sibling, 27 browser image-geometry tests, and 14 bundled mobile/media-flow tests pass. UI typecheck/lint/i18n and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. Latest mobile captures were inspected and preserve the illustrated appearance.

- CI-repair proof: four scroll/remount/access-change browser cases pass (53.2 s including bundle build); gallery/lifecycle 28 tests and command-palette/handoff/admission 70 tests pass. Frame rejection and mobile original/retry recovery pass through the bundled UI. UI typecheck, focused lint/style/format and independent P0–P2 review of the repair pass.

title: fix: refresh PR hovercards after reader status changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a PR hovercard can keep showing Open after the reader panel has already loaded its Merged state.

## User Impact

PR hovercards and inline status now reflect fresh reader details. Explicitly stale previews get one refresh attempt; failed refreshes remain labeled cached and use a short retry backoff. No configuration changes or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two views had independent caches, and the hovercard discarded the server’s stale flag. Fresh reader metadata now updates matching preview caches within the same client, agent, pane session, and reader scope. Late responses cannot overwrite that newer state. Compact preview metrics remain compact.

## Evidence

- Reproduced Open-versus-Merged disagreement in the production-built Chromium UI; both preview-first and reader-first orderings retain Merged status and compact +101/−12 metrics after the repair.
- 91 focused metadata/hovercard/panel/prefetch tests pass, including client/agent/pane isolation, session-scoped stale refresh, backoff, and pending-response ordering.
- Current main was integrated to resolve reader conflicts while preserving progressive section loading and pane/session request fencing. The four previously failing CI browser cases now pass locally using the canonical main corrections: dashboard fullscreen, website split restoration, mobile computer-selector overflow, and sidebar cold-load restoration.
- The merge exposed an unused translation import and a retired test-only screenshot helper; both were removed without weakening assertions. The owning UI production typecheck and targeted lint/format pass. Independent P0/P1/P2 source review completed; its two actionable retention findings were reproduced and repaired.
- Independent review also found that reader-first compact-metrics enrichment could clear known status while pending and lose it on failure. The regression fails before repair (inline Merged becomes unset); fresh reader facts now survive pending and failed enrichment, including repeated failures after backoff expires. Hosted review additionally identified a successful retry after failure reverting Merged to an older Open response. That failure was reproduced and repaired by retaining enrichment state through failure and overlaying known reader facts before clearing it on success. The extended integration case passes afterward; fresh independent review is scoped-clean.
- An additional editor/lint TypeScript graph invocation reports pre-existing missing declarations and native-desktop test ambient types outside this PR; it is not the owning production UI lane. Those diagnostics are retained rather than represented as a passing check.
- Before/after screenshots use sanitized synthetic data and were inspected, delivered in the work session, and verified rendered in this PR. No live deployment.
- Simplification keeps one existing hovercard cache owner and a scoped metadata event, with no persistent store or polling. Explicit needed/pending enrichment state preserves the plugin's compact metrics when reader details arrive first; a captured request scope carries connection/agent/session facts through refresh. The delta against current main is +137 production and +328 test lines; the added code covers scoped synchronization, bounded refresh, and retained failure facts, not a new cache owner.

[Prior-head CI run 39009081508](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39009081508) completed green for ee413483005453cdd32484d142024d0fd8ee8340. The subsequent 89ed54dce350eb76829f4e9b24e17b5b961faf20 run failed its config-test type stripe because main had removed health-store disposal but retained two using declarations. That independent defect was reproduced on clean main (runtime and types). Canonical main correction 7b727f04d23 already supplied the identical repair, so no duplicate fix was published. It was integrated in ad843bde175ee319e163969eaea06b077b07585d without changing the eight reviewed feature files. The 91 focused tests, owning UI production type lane and config-test type stripe pass after integration. Main then converted the reader owner from a class to a factory, creating an actual merge conflict. Current head f58b3da3b02072352fec8de91966301597467a7d preserves the canonical factory and publishes fresh metadata after its committed ready view. The 91 focused tests and both production-built Chromium orderings pass on this integration, along with the owning UI typecheck, targeted lint/format and fresh independent P0/P1/P2 review. [Exact-head CI run39011399166](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39011399166) completed green for f58b3da3b02072352fec8de91966301597467a7d. Superseded same-lane check failures are excluded by the pinned native CI watcher; no failed-current-CI bypass is used. Hosted re-review of this head has no actionable findings.

Earlier CI run 38860703540 failed in three browser jobs on four cases independently reproduced on its exact main parent. Its cancelled merge intent remains retained; this revision uses fresh proof and ordinary guarded landing, not a CI or policy bypass.

title: fix: Activity running counts stay at zero as work starts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Activity can show zero running sessions after a person's work starts outside the loaded session page or agent.

## User Impact

User impact: running-session badges appear as work starts and disappear when it finishes, without reloading Activity. Open-session totals also refresh when unseen sessions are archived. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Whole-roster totals cannot use a sampled page's exclusion proof when the previous row is unknown. Those events now request the existing coalesced refresh. A separate untracked condition in the person-row renderer also kept a badge initially at zero from appearing; it now uses a reactive visibility boundary. Known-row fast paths and bounded refresh pacing are preserved.

CI also exposed a selected-runner test that depended on unrelated full-inventory packing. The existing planner-only repair moves its strict parallel-capacity proof to fixed inputs across both backends, preserving coverage, runner mapping, worker limits and wall-time budgets. No production CI capacity policy changes are included.

Reported by and implemented for @steipete. CI fixture repair reused from [the independently verified planner fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/478a40024202a8e44f371a89fca0f61d796d0942), with credit to @VACInc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/023cb331-8333-4134-91d6-9c3b07bf5057)

## Evidence

- Real Gateway + Chromium: reproduced the zero count on the base, then verified **0 → 12 running → 0**, with 13 open sessions, after the fix. Uses real runtime execution claims and lifecycle events; no mocked count responses or model inference.
- Component regression: reproduced the missing badge while the accessible count had updated; verified appearance/removal without remounting the person row.
- **51 focused tests passed**, including unseen-session start, finish, and archive transitions.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint (0 warnings/errors), and formatting passed.
- **171 planner/capacity tests passed** after the CI fixture repair; root-test typecheck, targeted lint and formatting passed. The initial CI run failed the inventory-dependent assertion; this repair retains strict parallel-capacity checks with fixed inputs rather than changing production policy.
- Independent P0–P2 reviews of the count fix and CI fixture repair: no actionable findings.
- Full CI caught a missing timestamp in the new test fixture; corrected it and passed the exact UI-test typecheck, all 32 roster-event tests, targeted lint, and formatting.
- Exact-head CI run `38703068512`: all selected jobs passed except the inherited Windows partition-overlap assertion and its aggregate gate. The failing test, Windows command lists, and planner inputs are unchanged from CI’s main parent; pinned main planner execution reproduces the same tooling/infra/plugins overlap. This is qualified for native inherited-failure admission, not reported as green CI. Full baseline Vitest startup was blocked by local dependency/compiler preparation; the baseline evidence is the directly executed planner boundary.

title: fix(ui): select new sessions immediately while naming
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the previous conversation stays selected while a new session starts, and “New session” looks like a finished title while automatic naming is still running.

## User Impact

New sessions immediately appear selected in the sidebar. A subtle animated placeholder appears in the sidebar and chat header until naming succeeds or fails, respects reduced motion, and restores the draft if creation is rejected. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep provisional selection in the existing create handoff instead of admitting an uncreated session to Gateway state. Derive naming status from the existing title-request registry and publish both start and settlement, including failed naming. Suppress duplicate rows during admission without changing authoritative session membership.

## Evidence

- After conflict integration: 24 mocked-Gateway browser scenarios passed, including the formerly failing transition/rejected-edit flow. The final lineage-owner adjustment also passed all three pending-sidebar browser scenarios.
- 58 focused UI tests passed; after the final lineage adjustment, 30 sidebar projection/lineage tests passed. Initial implementation proof also covered 64 Gateway tests for title-request eviction/notification ordering, false-clearing events, and late worktree completion.
- [Current-head CI run 38796805372](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38796805372) passed for `56952494dd71d4a67422a0e8b5e11d56d266e9a1`; required CI/security gates are green. Canonical UI typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, and mock-factory ratchet also passed locally.
- The preceding run exposed an unrelated Apple-cache fixture type error inherited from main. Reproduced it on main, fixed its actual workflow context type in `68fed4aa461`, and integrated that repair without conflicts. Root scripts and UI typechecks plus 15 title projection/state/event tests passed after integration.
- New test cost: pending-sidebar browser file 3.1s test time / 32.8s final wall time including bundle build; focused route tests run in the existing unit suite. CI timing will be recorded by the current-head run.
- Simplification: reuse the existing creation and title-request owners; no persisted state or second registry. Route handoff renewal remains connection-validated, and provisional lineage admission now lives at the lineage entry point rather than a sidebar lifecycle wrapper.

title: feat: compress oversized videos without blocking chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Oversized chat videos are rejected without a way to prepare a smaller copy.

## User Impact

Users can choose **Compress to fit**, keep typing while progress updates, and cancel by removing the attachment. Originals remain unchanged. Small files and merely displaying the offer do not load the encoder. Browser codec support varies; Safari, Firefox, and H.264/AAC output are not yet qualified.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing attachment lifecycle with an on-demand Mediabunny worker and the current Solid attachment preview. The retired Lit preview stays removed. Preserve audio and orientation, bound resolution/frame rate, and admit the output only when its actual bytes fit the per-file and remaining batch budget. Unsupported inputs fail visibly instead of dropping audio.

Stream encoded output into a fixed buffer capped at twice the upload budget, reused across attempts. This avoids whole-file MP4 packet buffering and stops excessive output early; a measured overshoot within that cap still receives one lower-bitrate retry.

## Evidence

- 42 focused unit/regression tests and 3 production-bundle browser tests passed on the repaired branch. The new overflow regression failed on the original worker (four output writes instead of stopping after the first) and passes with the bounded stream.
- Verified opt-in lazy loading, editable draft/IME/focus, cancellation, visible failures, playable bounded output, positional header rewrites, and the measured retry.
- Earlier implementation proof: a real audio/video recording compressed from 3,091,704 to 752,337 bytes beneath a 1 MiB test limit; playback and VP9/Opus streams verified. Rotated output retained 540 × 960 orientation and audio.
- Current local proof: production UI build and bundle budgets, UI production and test typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and docs lint passed. The existing stylelint/i18n proof remains applicable; no styles or copy changed in the repair.
- Codex branch autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings.
- Current-main integration: merged main only to resolve its attachment preview cutover; the 39 attachment tests and all 3 production-bundle browser tests passed afterward. Frozen dependency installation passed.

### Final-head CI and unresolved failure

Final head: `8d14e2b5e47fe89a50b5c5304c857f89753f8ca1`. [CI run 38707211555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38707211555) completed with failures. Docs, core lint, dependency lock, production/test types, and the other feature checks passed.

| Failed gate | Attribution |
| --- | --- |
| `check-lint-extensions-2` | Pre-existing: `extensions/line/src/send.test.ts:159` shadows `messageId`, matching [main run 38694591842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38694591842). |
| `checks-ui-e2e (1/9)` | Pre-existing: both sidebar nesting assertions expected zero child rows but received four, matching [main run 38699948035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38699948035). |

| `checks-ui-e2e (6/9)` | Unresolved: mobile pairing timed out after 30 seconds waiting for the Pair a device dialog to reopen at `mobile-pairing.e2e.test.ts:539`. The comparison main run passed this exact case. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` | Failed aggregate. |

The mobile-pairing case passed a focused local replay in 9.7 seconds; a second replay of its complete three-test file also passed (31.3 seconds of tests). These passing replays do not establish a repair or prove the CI failure pre-existing. The CI report's pre-existing label for this shard compares job names only. No CI reruns, test weakening, timeout increases, or unrelated fixes were used. This unexplained failure needs a maintainer decision before landing.

### Dependency review

The new direct UI dependency is `mediabunny@1.61.0` (MPL-2.0). It provides the demuxing, muxing, and WebCodecs conversion needed by this design. Upstream is active (latest `1.61.4`, October 12; upstream activity October 14; about 4 million weekly npm downloads). Its two dependency entries are typings. The original pin is unchanged; this repair adds no dependencies. Safari, Firefox, and H.264/AAC output remain unqualified beyond the original reported proof.

title: fix(control-ui): mentions and person cards show initials for Gravatar-only users
body:
Related: #168640

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: mention chips, person hovercards, owner chips, and offline roster rows show initials for people whose only photo is a Gravatar, while their message avatars show the photo.

## User Impact

User impact: people with a Gravatar-linked email but no uploaded photo now show the same photo everywhere. People with no upload and no email still show initials with no image request.

Tradeoff: people with an email but no photo at all now cost one avatar 404 per page load where they appear as a mention, owner, or offline roster row. Message avatars and presence avatars already requested these, so Peter's reload scenario from #168640 is unchanged (measured below).

## Why This Change Was Made

Message and presence avatars always use the versioned `/users/<id>/avatar` route, which serves an upload and otherwise falls back to the Gateway's Gravatar proxy. The shared profile directory (#168640) only advertised that route when `hasAvatar` was true, which means "uploaded", so Gravatar-only people never reached the fallback. The directory now also advertises the route for profiles with a linked email. The route, its 60-second private miss cache for current revisions, and the in-page loader's 60-second miss dedupe are unchanged; the URL keeps `v=updatedAt`, which matches the revision the route caches.

## Evidence

Offline Gravatar-only person, mocked Gateway, dark theme. The OpenClaw logo stands in for the Gravatar.

Before (main): initials in the mention chip and the hovercard.

![Before: VK initials in mention chip and hovercard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b0600f2-d6b3-4254-b29e-594a1db347c2)

After: the photo in both.

![After: photo in mention chip and hovercard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9a29c43-2d64-4383-9163-aefe1c391b46)

**Avatar request benchmark** (mocked-Gateway Chromium E2E, run on main `3d6a3dc1d820` and this branch). Roster of 10 profiles: 1 upload, 1 Gravatar-only, 7 email-only with no photo, 1 with no email. Three online (presence), four message senders. Playwright routing disables the HTTP cache, so each load is the cold, worst case; in production the route's `private, max-age=60` makes reloads within a minute free, as #168640 measured.

| Scenario | main: requests / 404s | this PR: requests / 404s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard load (#168640's reload scenario: presence + message avatars, no mentions) | 5 / 3 | 5 / 3 |
| Transcript mentioning Gravatar-only, 2 email-only, and no-email people | 5 / 3 | 7 / 5 |
| Users sidebar, **All** filter (offline rows) | 5 / 3 | 9 / 7 |
| Opening the Gravatar person's hovercard | +0 | +0 |

- Each URL was requested at most once per load in every scenario; repeated chips and the hovercard reuse the loader's result.
- The no-email profile made 0 requests in every scenario on both revisions.
- Gravatar-only mention chip: `data-avatar-state` `none` on main, `loaded` on this PR; hovercard photo shown.
- The benchmark is a local measurement file, not committed.

Checks: `pnpm test ui/src/lib/profile-directory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 3/3 passed; `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed; oxfmt and oxlint clean on touched files; autoreview (P0–P2) found no actionable issues.

title: fix(test): retire shared auth ownership facts between files
body:
Closes #172803

## What Problem This Solves

Non-isolated test files retain shared-auth ownership facts from completed files, accumulating temporary roots until later shared lanes reach the process-root limit.

## User Impact

Developers get independent auth ownership preparation across shared test files. This is a test-harness-only lifetime fix: production cache behavior and its 256-root limit stay unchanged, tests remain enabled, and no production test-only export is added. It does not establish a complete-suite pass or the broader >=20% speedup goal.

## Why This Change Was Made

After runtime and storage cleanup join, the existing shared runner clears the existing ownership Map before resetting the source generation. It preserves that Map while SQLite custody remains retained. Clearing in place matters because externalized/native modules can hold the original owner and must observe subsequent preparation through that same Map.

The regression extends the existing real runner child with a producer/observer pair using public auth-owner APIs. The producer pins a fact through afterAll; the next file must see it retired, prepare its own fresh state, and expose that new fact through both the new source getter and a native-held original getter. No extra expensive child process is added.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI run 38680333160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38680333160), attempt 1, passed on `abafa1ff87bc5a9d540d110f9256dd666f21311d` (10m28s overall workflow time, not per-file timing). Native pinned auto-merge landed that reviewed head after required checks passed.
- Before the repair, the real child fails specifically on `prior file auth ownership must retire`: it observes `{ location: "state-db" }` instead of no prepared fact.
- After the repair, the complete existing runner regressions and custom-element sibling pass: 8/8 tests, 41.54s runner wall / 40.41s Vitest. These are validation costs, not a before/after performance claim. The existing runner integration is intentionally seconds-long because a helper test cannot prove cross-file source retirement, native-held references, afterAll ordering, and joined runtime/storage custody; the new cases reuse that one child. Current-head CI workflow timing is linked above; per-file CI timing is not separately reported here.
- Root tooling, scripts, E2E, and root-other TypeScript partitions passed. Targeted lint reported zero warnings/errors; formatting and diff checks passed.
- Fresh independent Codex P0-P2 review was scoped-clean.
- V5 did not complete. Its other ordinary failure clusters are being classified separately; this PR does not claim to fix all reported failed cases. No full benchmark was rerun for this scoped repair. Current-head PR CI supplies broad proof.

title: fix: existing automations fail after account-binding upgrades
body:
Related: #172590

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: existing automations fail after upgrading to required inference-account binding, even when their model was already explicitly selected.

## User Impact

Repairing Doctor can adopt an explicitly selected or sole eligible shared stored account without pinning inherited models or changing fallback lists. Repairs are backed up and idempotent; existing bindings, authored fields, runtime state and valid approval authority are preserved.

Migration is best effort: malformed jobs and recoverable inspection/backup/commit failures produce actionable warnings, not upgrade failure. Ambiguous, unavailable, personal-account, direct-key and native-owned cases are not silently assigned another account. Startup diagnostics do not disable jobs or capture credentials. Managed updates and the standard container entrypoint reach repairing Doctor; manual source upgrades still require **openclaw doctor --fix** before Gateway startup.

Best effort does not mean bypassing account authority or admitting unsafe database state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [reporter evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172590#issuecomment-6183228336) matches missing durable account adoption, not a model-pin requirement. Last-used telemetry may reflect fallback and does not establish account authority.

The existing Doctor owner now inspects canonical SQLite partitions, including stores without legacy quarantine files. Canonical current model/session/config selection and auth planning select an explicit or unambiguous shared account. Exclusive maintenance, credential-preserving CAS, verified backup and live authority checks guard persistence. Binding-only changes preserve uniquely attributable valid scheduled-approval revisions without minting or reviving permissions.

## Evidence

- **55 migration/auth/startup tests**, **99 credential-writer/database-worker guard tests**, **4 heartbeat boundary tests**, and **14 probe/survivor tests** passed (**172 distinct cases**, including the previously counted 5 survivor cases). Real Doctor proof covers canonical-only SQLite, inactive partitions, inherited/default/session/fallback preservation, existing bindings, backup/idempotence, grant consumption and subsequent revocation refusal.
- Negative controls reproduced missing adoption, malformed-row batch abandonment and the absent startup barrier. Fixes preserve bad rows while migrating unrelated jobs. Injected backup I/O failure gives a warning and no cron writes. Exact writer-edge/maintenance-branch registrations retain sibling/unguarded/nested-callback rejection; the real T1 ratchet stays **223 → 223**. Scoped lint/format/syntax, line-cap, diff and Docker boundary guards passed. Independent reviews are clean through P2 after required fixes.
- Migration 5-case cold run: **98.65s**; guard99: **3.83s**; heartbeat4: **46.18s**; final probe/survivor14: **2.44s** (wrapper4.73s). New startup tests virtualize retry time. No provider calls or production jobs were used.
- Current-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38694193888) completed: **62 successful jobs, 2 failed, 25 skipped**. Node tests, production/test types, guards and security-fast passed. The sole root failure is two inherited `typescript(no-generated-empty-object-type)` diagnostics in `chat-composer-types.ts` and `chat-pane-session-controls.ts`; the CI gate is downstream. Actual tested merge `241b6252` has baseline `469837ed` and head `c707a81c`. The entire UI tree, dependency lockfile, lint configuration and runtime wrappers are identical to that baseline. This is source-qualified attribution, not a separately executed baseline lint run; CI remains failed and native inherited-failure admission must still satisfy live security/review/authority checks.
- The final [published 9.7 upgrade survivor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38694280039) **passed** package integrity/install, the published updater and candidate Doctor, canonical SQLite preservation with zero quarantine, two content-verified repair backups, idempotence, installed cron execution under both historical and explicit owners, and transcript continuity. The corrected fixture waits for documented `/startupz` completion before all-agent probes; production readiness, admission, assertions and timeouts are unchanged.
- Inspected run payload binds reviewed harness `c707a81c` to immutable product package `8cbf3c69`, artifact `11951618954` from producer `38687795948` attempt 1. Only four harness/test files differ; product implementation is unchanged. Package SHA-256: `b0e4f30b4938b47d31ec4781ed651a244335bb7ef9bf9a243e48565e64e777c9`. Runtime receipts both returned `ok`; session continuity was preserved. This proof uses manual restart and synthetic system events, not automatic supervisor restart or a live inference-provider request.

title: fix: chat turn splits around the GitHub publication notice
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent's turn in Control UI chat splits in two when the agent publishes a pull request mid-run with `github_publish`. A group footer ("OpenClaw · 1h ago") appears in the middle of the turn, and the "Published … branch …" notice sits outside the turn.

## User Impact

User impact: the publication notice stays inside the turn that published it, live and after reloading history, so the turn reads as one block with one footer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway saved the notice without a run ID, and chat groups a turn by run ID. The publication coordinator now remembers which run requested a publication that it processes inside that run's tool call, and the transcript reporter writes that run ID on the notice. The UI is unchanged.

Tradeoffs:

- The run association is held in memory. If the Gateway restarts after publishing but before posting the notice, the notice is posted without a run ID, as it is today.
- Publications that finish after the turn (worker and cloud sessions, deferred requests) keep today's standalone notice after the answer.
- The notice is now a run-owned assistant message ending in `stop`, the same shape as an intermediate reply in a steered run. If a run is interrupted after publishing and before any later reply, history shows the notice as that run's last reply instead of "Interrupted".

title: feat(ui): plugin themes can ship light and dark backgrounds
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin themes can recolor the whole Control UI and bring their own icons, hats, and critters, but **Appearance → Background → Theme** always shows the neutral plugin artwork, so a theme can't ship the backdrop it was designed around.

## User Impact

User impact: a plugin theme can declare `backgrounds: { "light": "...", "dark": "..." }` in `openclaw.plugin.json`, and people who pick that theme with **Theme** background artwork see the plugin's image for the current color mode, dimmed the same way a custom uploaded background is. A mode with no declared image keeps the neutral artwork. Built-in, personal, and imported themes are unchanged.

Older Gateways reject the new manifest key, so a theme that uses it needs a Gateway that includes this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backgrounds join the existing theme artwork path instead of adding a new owner:

- **Manifest:** `backgrounds` maps `light` and/or `dark` to a PNG, JPEG, or WebP inside the plugin root, using the same containment and duplicate-key rules as other artwork.
- **Gateway:** it captures each image into the plugin metadata (at most 512 KiB, the authenticated image route's cap) and checks its image signature. An invalid image drops the theme with a plugin warning, like invalid SVG artwork does. Bytes are kept as base64 because runtime metadata snapshots are deep-frozen and a Buffer cannot be frozen. The existing `plugin-theme-art` route serves them with a `background/<mode>` kind.
- **Control UI:** it fetches the image with the same authenticated artwork loader and publishes it through `--app-background-image`, which the shell canvas, session backgrounds, and the Settings preview already read. Placement, visibility, and accessibility fallbacks stay with their existing owners.
- **Dimming:** plugin images are untrusted art, so they get the custom-upload treatment instead of the built-in one. The token carries a theme-colored scrim equal to a default-strength upload's opacity (`readBackgroundOpacityLimit` × default visibility, × 0.65 in light mode), so every surface reading the token is dimmed, including the shell canvas for users who never set a background preference. Full bleed skips the extra bundled-artwork cap so the image isn't dimmed twice.

Accepted edge: the scrim is fixed at default visibility, so raising **Image visibility** above the default doesn't brighten plugin art the way it brightens an upload; lowering it still fades it. On light palettes with low muted-text contrast the image is very faint, which is also what an upload would get.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/b9ef4908-ae7e-4224-b975-a3d984feb1b7)

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway built from this branch (`pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated> gateway run`, loopback), Ghost Claw installed with `openclaw plugins install <zip> --force --accept-capabilities`, captured with headless Chromium on the new session page. Background preference left unset (default canvas path).

**Before** (same theme without `backgrounds`: neutral plugin artwork):

![Before: Ghost Claw with neutral plugin artwork, real Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eaabbcc4-fed2-46ce-ab21-be2bae182ff8)

**After** (dark mode, `backgrounds.dark` served by the Gateway and dimmed like an upload):

![After: Ghost Claw dark mode with its dimmed firehouse background, real Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f368ca31-6ce9-4195-be71-56e0d6a75cbf)

<details><summary>Light mode</summary>

Light mode uses `backgrounds.light`; on this palette the upload-equivalent dimming leaves it at about 2% strength.

![After: Ghost Claw light mode, real Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b15c80f5-c11f-42e5-8a61-9253d4d107b3)

</details>

Gateway receipts from that run: `GET /__openclaw__/plugin-theme-art/ghost-claw-theme/ghost-claw/background/dark` → 200 (`/light` → 200 in light mode); root token `linear-gradient(color-mix(… var(--bg-content, var(--bg)) 91.3%, transparent) …), url("blob:…")` dark, 98.1% light.

The live install also caught a real bug the unit tests missed: capturing the image as a `Buffer` made `plugins install` fail with `Cannot freeze array buffer views with elements` once the metadata snapshot was finalized. `theme-catalog.test.ts` now runs the background case through `finalizePluginMetadataSnapshot`.

title: chore(test): cover removed jsdom listener retention in the shared runner
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `checks-ui (3/3)` could go red again without any shared-runner test catching it. PRs based between #172530 and 5e4a1bed (for example #172546, both CI attempts) failed with one Usage retention assertion plus roughly 25 unrelated UI files that reported only `DOM resources failed` teardown errors.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Maintainers get an owner-level gate in the tooling lane for the half of that breakage that still had no direct regression test.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both failures come from the shared jsdom resource tracker added in #172530 (`test/jsdom-resources.ts`). It had two defects. @steipete fixed both on `main` in 5e4a1bed, and #172487 later added stubbed-`window` coverage to the runner fixture:

- **Teardown cascade (covered by #172487).** The tracker stored the live `window` global. `stale-chunk-reload.test.ts` stubs `window` with a plain object that forwards to the native window. File retirement then called native `removeEventListener` on that stub and threw before clearing its list. Because tracking is per shared document, every later file in the same worker failed teardown. How many files depends on worker packing, which made it look like a flake.
- **Retention failure (covered by this PR).** Explicit `document`/`body` removals were never forgotten by the tracker, so removed callbacks and their closures stayed reachable until file retirement. That is what kept the Usage overview payload alive in `usage-page-retention.test.ts`. The only regression signal for this was that UI test, which doesn't run when only `test/` runner helpers change, and that's how #172530 shipped it.

This PR adds that check at the owning boundary: the existing non-isolated runner fixture child. It removes listeners from `window`, `document` and `body` and asserts, with the UI GC helper, that their closures are collectable before retirement. The check is folded into the existing producer test because the harness pins one test per fixture file. Production code is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Crabbox reproduction and proof of the `checks-ui (3/3)` failure.** Direct AWS Crabbox, N = 6 parallel `c7a.xlarge` sessions (4 vCPU / 7.7 GB, plus 4 GB swap). Each session ran the CI shard command pinned to 2 CPUs like the CI runner, with Node 24.19.0 and the pinned Bun 1.4.3. Lanes alternated the pre-fix helper (`test/jsdom-resources.ts` from `5e4a1bed^`) with this branch's helper, 8 runs per lane, all on this branch's tree.

| Helper | Runs | Retention assertion failed | Teardown cascade (`DOM resources failed`) | Whole shard green |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-fix (`5e4a1bed^`) | 24 | 24/24 | 24/24 (1–27 suites per run) | 0/24 |
| Current `main` (this branch) | 24 | 0/24 | 0/24 | 22/24 |

The 2 non-green `main` runs each failed one unrelated test, once: `lazy-shell-action.test.ts > respects the canonical reconnect boundary…` and `app-sidebar.session-promotion.test.ts > drags a nested conversation…`. Neither shows these signatures; I'm recording them as separate follow-ups.

<details><summary>Command, setup, and the earlier batch</summary>

Command: the `checks-ui` "Test Control UI" step from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The group payload was built with `createUiTestShardGroups({ includeReleaseOnlyTests: false, includePrExemptRuntimeTests: true })`, which reproduced #172546's CI include list exactly; the only extra file is one test added on `main` since then.

```sh
CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true OPENCLAW_CI_TEST_RUNTIME_POLICY=bun-compatible \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_CONFIGS_JSON='["ui/vitest.config.ts"]' \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_GROUPS_GZIP_BASE64="<encoded ui groups>" \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONCURRENCY=1 \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_VITEST_ARGS_JSON='["--maxWorkers","3","--reporter=verbose","--reporter=github-actions","--reporter=./scripts/lib/vitest-resource-reporter.mts","--shard=3/3"]' \
taskset -c 0,1 node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts
```

An earlier batch on the same instance type without swap (6 sessions, `main` at `911726f`, 17 runs completed before an orchestration timeout) agreed: pre-fix 8/8 with both signatures, current helper 0/9. Its non-green runs came only from the kernel OOM-killing `chrome-headless` on the 7.7 GB box, which is why the final batch added swap.

Blacksmith Testbox, the repository default, sat `pending` behind the GitHub-hosted queue (about 650 queued runs). Per the Crabbox skill I stopped that allocation and used direct AWS Crabbox, which Patrick had asked for explicitly.

The matching CI failures are #172546's run 38641500904, both attempts (`checks-ui (3/3)` jobs 116121128463 and 116136475451): 26 and 23 teardown-failed suites plus the retention assertion at `usage-page-retention.test.ts:126`.

</details>

**Regression fixture.** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/non-isolated-runner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes about 40–80 s wall on this host; the fixture adds one GC call to an existing child run.
- Current helper: 2/2 passed.
- Helper with only its `EventTarget.prototype.removeEventListener` wrapper removed: fails on the new assertion, `expected [ undefined, {}, {} ]`. The `window` removal was already handled; `document`/`body` closures were retained.
- Helper reverted to `5e4a1bed^`: fails with both CI signatures. The invalid-receiver `DOM resources failed` cascade runs through `11-dom-a-producer`, `11-dom-b-observer`, `13-a-solid-producer`, …, alongside the same retention assertion.

**Gates.** `pnpm tsgo:test:root` passed. `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig.json` on the touched files reported 0 warnings and 0 errors. oxfmt is clean. `pnpm changed:lanes` selects testRoot + tooling.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @Patrick-Erichsen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/35027d72-f77f-4f5a-af79-c690c204faec)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/527489d0-a33d-4e65-b090-6d919cc9ebb5)

title: fix(ui): stop showing reply icons on progress lines before tool calls
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: progress lines an agent writes before a tool call ("Now checking X…") each get their own reply/copy action row when a run renders outside its turn frame — for example, when the loaded history window starts mid-run and tool calls are hidden. Seen with Claude; any provider that doesn't label progress text as commentary is affected.

## User Impact

User impact: only the turn's answer shows reply/copy actions. Progress lines no longer get stray reply icons, whatever the provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The turn footer already picks its action owner with an eligibility rule: the message must have content, must not be commentary, interrupted, an error, or a `toolUse` stop. Plain message groups only hid actions for messages explicitly labeled `commentary`, which OpenAI Responses/Codex set and Claude/Gemini do not. This shares the footer's rule (`assistantMessageCanOwnTurnActions`) and applies it per message in message groups, so reply and inline actions follow the same decision everywhere.

Messages that can't own the turn (progress, commentary, errors) lose their reply button and inline action row in unframed groups too, matching turn frames. A group's footer keeps copy (for example on a transcript search hit) and only drops reply.

## Evidence

Screenshots replay real transcripts in the Control UI with tool calls hidden, starting the history window mid-run (where the run is split by a gateway publication notice).

**Claude** (real Claude Opus session transcript)

Before: every progress line has its own reply icon.

![Claude before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bb7af84-1528-4172-b1c3-fe0fc9736959)

After: only the answer's footer keeps actions.

![Claude after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24cc5a3a-059a-4373-893d-5c475b29efbd)

**OpenAI: unaffected control.** OpenAI's Responses API labels progress lines as `commentary`, so they never had reply icons and the bug can't appear there. This replay uses a real `gpt-6.1-sol` run, split by the same publication notice, to show the fix doesn't change it.

![OpenAI after (same as before)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de9b846f-409b-434b-91d9-3aec427450ce)

The "OpenClaw 1h ago" line in the middle of the Claude screenshots is the normal footer of a message group. It is already present on `main` (see Before). The publication notice is stored without a run ID, so it cuts the run into two groups, and the first group ends with its own footer. This PR only removes that footer's reply icon.

- New Solid regression (`chat-message-group.solid.test.tsx`, "progress before tool calls…", completed and still-working cases): fails on `main`, passes with the fix.

title: fix(gateway): chat activity rows show "Automation" instead of a deleted one-shot job's name
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Chat activity rows for a one-shot automation read "1 update from Automation" instead of the automation's name once the job has run.

## User Impact

User impact: activity rows from one-shot (and otherwise deleted) automations show the name the job had when it ran, e.g. "1 update from Verify PR body after merge". Existing jobs still show their current name, including after a rename. Rows from deleted jobs that never recorded a name keep the "Automation" fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already labels these rows by looking up the job name in the cron store (#150553). One-shot jobs are deleted after they run, so that lookup misses and the label falls back to "Automation". This was the case for the row in the original report: its job `fe38ea23…` ("Verify side-chat indicator PR body") no longer exists, and live `chat.history` returns `senderSession.label: "Automation"` for it, while rows from existing jobs in other sessions resolve correctly.

Each cron run already records the job name in its message provenance (`sourcePromptPrefix`: `[cron:<jobId> <name>]`). The Gateway projection now uses that recorded name when the store has no entry. The format is shared through one small helper in `src/cron/source-prompt-prefix.ts` that both the producer (`run-prepare.ts`) and the projection use. All history paths (RPC pages, HTTP snapshot, SSE, live `session.message`, deltas) share this projection, so no UI change is needed.

Not covered: inter-session deliveries from isolated cron runs identify the job only by session key and carry no recorded name, so they still fall back to "Automation" after deletion.

## Evidence

Dark theme, mocked Control UI rendering the Gateway projection output for a deleted one-shot job (`projectForwardedMessages` with no store entry), before and after this change.

**Before**

![Before: activity row reads "1 update from Automation"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b3b8ae9-0a43-4f9e-bce5-024ba3875f83)

**After**

![After: activity row reads "1 update from Verify PR body after merge"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67627101-169d-4bd5-a989-c7f283c5c0b3)

title: fix: show native Talk speech separately from completed answers
body:
Fixes #172346

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI shows two completed assistant replies after a successful native Talk request: the backing-agent answer and a separately persisted spoken readback.

## User Impact

User impact: native Talk keeps one canonical result visible in chat, with the spoken wording available in an expandable **Voice transcript**. A missing or failed audio response never hides the backing result. Speech-only dialogue stays available, and chat search opens matching transcripts.

This applies to new provider-owned speech records. Typed chat, chat-backed Talk, and older unmarked speech retain their existing presentation. Raw history, exports, and model context keep both records; no migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native speech does not reliably identify which consultation it replaces. Instead of guessing from timing or similar wording, the host marks provider-owned assistant speech for a separate collapsed presentation. The transcript does not claim that speech replaced any particular run, take answer/action ownership, or become completed tool work.

This is the bounded presentation approach approved by the reporter. The reporter authorized merging on October 16 after the review follow-ups were addressed; normal CI, security, and repository review gates still apply.

## Evidence

### Review follow-up — October 16

- Resolved the four reported conflicts by integrating main `8dd2dc0c084390462fa753bcd58ea6d5788e9080`. Speech exclusion now lives in main’s shared `assistantMessageCanOwnTurnActions` owner, covering both ordinary messages and completed frames. The superseded private owner was not restored.
- Two new regressions failed before the shared-owner guard and pass after it. **48 tests passed** across grouping, completed frames, and Solid message groups (5.02s batch wall); the bundled Chromium native-speech E2E passed (17.23s wall including build, 2.132s test). UI production/chat-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and the candidate diff whitespace check passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defect in the candidate diff. Commit `6acd37b9a61ac1671e339be8ec4ca008e0ae84b8` contains the exact reviewed/tested tree `9f81c8edd9681ac685ff1ee42831e9fe1af93a82`.
- **Upgrade/reopen compatibility passed:** real `v2026.10.4` source (`383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`) produced the old Talk settings and history through its config and persistence owners. Candidate maintenance owners migrated shared-state 20→25 and agent 24→27 with backups. All three original raw rows remained byte-for-byte unchanged; the entire config file also remained byte-identical.
- The production `talk.client.create` native callback persisted new marked speech beside a canonical backend answer. A separate candidate process reopened the same databases with all five raw rows and public history unchanged. Public `talk.config` retained settings. Chromium rendered the actual reopened history: old unmarked speech normal, backend result once, new speech collapsed/expandable across reload.
- **Scope of this proof:** source/production-owner upgrade and cold-process reopen, not a published-package installation, full updater/Doctor CLI run, or serving Gateway WebSocket test. The external provider was deterministic; browser transport used a mock Gateway serving the unmodified reopened records. No paid/live provider calls or operator state were used.

| Compatibility stage | Test time | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| v2026.10.4 producer | 1.657s | 8.40s |

Baseline used Node 26.8.2/pnpm 12.5.1; candidate used Node 26.3.0/pnpm 12.10.1; Chromium was 156.0.8078.4. All proof processes exited. No product schema or data migration was added by this PR. Existing screenshots below remain representative; no visual design changed during conflict repair.

### Prior-head evidence

Prior head `f7ed74d04190ee398200539bacf82866520517ad` passed [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38648465781); that is prior-head evidence, not a claim about the new head. Current head `6acd37b9a61ac1671e339be8ec4ca008e0ae84b8` passed [CI run 38935179131](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38935179131); applicable current security/repository gates remain enforced at landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: files in a project worktree session fail to open in the side panel or Files panel with `Session workspace changed during file read`, even when nothing about the session has changed.

## User Impact

User impact: HTML previews and other files from worktree-backed sessions open again in the Control UI. Sessions without a worktree were not affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sessions.files.list` and `sessions.files.get` re-read the session after waiting for sandbox settlement, to refuse the read if the session was reset or moved to a different worktree in the meantime. Since #169757, that re-read used the logical session store path, which the retained-facts reader does not recognize, so it always came back empty and every worktree read was refused. The re-read now uses the session's captured read source, the same way the other retained-facts callers do. The safety check itself is unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Chat activity row ("1 update from Automation ›") changes its text, icon, color and width when expanded ("From 🕒 Automation ⌄"), and its source link is unavailable until the row is expanded.

## User Impact

User impact: activity rows keep the same "N update(s) from <source>" summary in both states and only the chevron rotates. The activity summary passed different attribution options per state (`updateCount` + `linkSource: false` when collapsed, `showAvatar: false` when expanded), which selected different markup branches. It now renders one attribution with the update count and the normal source link in both states. Link clicks are already handled by the transcript's navigation handler, whose `preventDefault` also cancels the summary's toggle activation.

History: #161656 made the collapsed source plain text so the whole collapsed row was one click target, and its tests pinned that; neither it nor #167600 records another reason. This change keeps the row a toggle target everywhere except on the link itself. `linkSource: false` stays for the transcript feed; the now-unused `showAvatar` option and the summary-only `[data-session-title-only]` style are removed.

title: fix(ui): session links outside the sidebar show raw URLs instead of titles
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session links in chat show a raw URL with no title or hover card when the linked session isn't in the viewer's loaded sidebar, such as another person's or an archived session. Titled links also show the raw session key (`agent:<id>:<namespace>:<uuid>`) as a hover tooltip.

## User Impact

Session URLs in messages, including shortened-ID links, now show the session's title and open the session hover card whenever the viewer can access that session. The session-key tooltip is gone. Missing, inaccessible, or ambiguous references stay plain, navigable links.

## Why This Change Was Made

Link titling only matched URLs against the browser's loaded session list, while bare `agent:` keys could already ask the Gateway. URLs the loaded list can't identify now go through `sessions.resolve`, the same lookup the chat route uses when the link is opened, so access rules and short-ID ambiguity handling match navigation. Results are cached per connection (5 minutes on success, 30 seconds on a miss), so each distinct link costs at most one lookup. Titles now load when links render instead of waiting for a hover.

Known gap: the hover card renders only when it has something to show (a sidebar row, a progress card, or pull requests). A session outside the sidebar with none of those gets a title but no card yet. A fallback card built from the session preview would be a follow-up.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `session-link-titling`, `markdown-session-links`, `session-progress-hovercard-target`, and the forwarded-attribution suites pass (97 tests). New cases cover full-key and short-ID URLs outside the roster, an ambiguous short ID staying plain, and no repeat requests or DOM churn on refresh.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, and oxfmt pass on the touched files.
- Before and after screenshots below come from the real Control UI bundle with a mocked Gateway, dark theme, where only the current session is in the sidebar and both linked sessions have progress notes. They use synthetic sessions. Hovering the bare-key link already opened the same card before this change, so that state is not repeated here.

## What Problem This Solves

The account menu has no direct route to update settings, and development checkouts receive the same new-update notifications as release users.

## User Impact

Users can open **Settings → Updates** from the account menu. Only the **stable** and **beta** channels show new-update notifications; **dev** remains quiet. Opening settings never starts an update, and manually started dev updates retain their progress and recovery UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an **Updates** menu item with an **Available** badge, and share release-channel eligibility with Inbox. Keep the badge on the dedicated Updates row instead of the About/build link. Dismissing an Inbox notice does not hide release availability in the account menu. No configuration migration or automatic-update policy change is required.

## Evidence

title: feat: suggest follow-up drafts in the chat composer
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting the next message after an assistant reply can interrupt the conversation; users have no optional follow-up draft to edit.

## User Impact

Adds **Composer predictions** in **Settings → Labs**, off by default. When enabled, an empty active composer can show a muted suggestion after a reply. **Tab** or **Use suggestion** inserts an undoable draft; it never sends automatically. Typing or Escape dismisses it.

Utility is the recommended default model, with Conversation and Default model alternatives. Each active client may add one model request per completed reply. Unavailable model choices skip predictions rather than silently switching. Read-only, imported, and incognito conversations do not show predictions. No breaking changes or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prediction uses bounded recent visible dialogue in a tool-free, isolated request with existing session and operator authority. Results are discarded when the draft, session, connection, visibility, or run changes. The handler waits for the existing terminal-persistence owner so a final event arriving before its database update does not permanently lose its prediction.

Thanks to Json for the feature request and design input.

title: fix(test): retire source DOM resources between shared test files
body:
Closes #172529

## What Problem This Solves

Shared jsdom test workers retain native listeners and observers from completed source modules, allowing stale callbacks to affect later test files.

## User Impact

Developers get cleaner shared-worker test boundaries without removing tests or changing production behavior. External dependency registrations remain alive. There are no visual UI changes, migrations, configuration changes, or required actions. This repair does **not** establish the broader complete-suite >=20% speedup target.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared runner now retires repository-owned long-lived DOM listeners and MutationObservers with each source generation, before resetting the document body. It reuses the existing custom-element provenance policy instead of introducing another ownership rule, and forgets explicit Window listener removals so retirement does not corrupt Vitest error-handler counts. Externalized dependency resources survive. As before, unreadable registration stacks are conservatively retained rather than risking dependency cleanup.

title: fix(cron): accept the first update after a completed run
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the first attempt to edit or disable a cron job being rejected with `CronJobsStoreChangedError` immediately after its scheduled run completes, even when nothing else changed.

## User Impact

Users can update a just-completed cron job without retrying. Genuine definition, private-authority, and running-receipt changes still reject a stale update. No configuration, schema, retention, or permission change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completed in-memory job can retain cleared runtime fields as `undefined`, while SQLite JSON omits them. The guarded update now compares both runtime-state snapshots through the existing persistence codec, including its legacy status alias. Definitions and private authority remain exact, and the host precondition is not rerun. The serializer is shared with the row codec rather than introducing a second normalization policy or additional database reads.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through a real isolated Gateway: the first public `cron.update` after a successful scheduled command returned `UNAVAILABLE/CronJobsStoreChangedError`; rereading and retrying succeeded. This was a representation mismatch, not a competing writer.
- Red-first regression through actual service `updateWithPrecondition`, worker finalization, and SQLite. Covers current and legacy definitions/state plus negative definition, private-authority, and run-identity changes.
- Behavioral head `15e06bee` (unchanged executable inputs after final safety-comment correction): 58/58 focused tests across receipt finalization, worker storage, shared-store runtime, authority, and row-codec suites. Wrapper wall time 85.60 seconds; test-run duration 80.88 seconds including compilation. The changed 13-case file used about 2.01 seconds of test-body time.
- Core and services-cron test typechecks, four-file oxlint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. Final corrected head `c889386ca55389c358a888731f2e9032108f4ffb` rebuilt successfully in 1m 40.2s with a clean build stamp.
- Independent source autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The transplant onto current main is patch-identical and contains only the four intended files; the previously landed scheduler fix is not republished.
- Final-commit isolated Gateway rerun: **6/6 first-call updates succeeded**, immediately after six real scheduled command completions; observed update latency 9–19 ms (not a benchmark). Each job had one successful durable run receipt and remained disabled after a clean stop; no update retries, forced runs, mock clock, model inference, or external delivery. Build/handshake and clean source stamp match `c889386ca55389c358a888731f2e9032108f4ffb`. Two earlier fixture-startup attempts stopped before any job or update ran: the retained synthetic agent DB needed Doctor migration from v26 to v27, then the harness needed to wait for `/startupz` rather than only `cron.status`. Both prerequisites were corrected without changing production source or weakening admission.
- Initial PR CI run 38633913129 correctly rejected the new JSON cast because its `SAFETY` invariant comment was missing. Added that source-inert comment and passed the exact assertion-safety ratchet locally; no waiver or rerun-for-green. Corrected-head [CI run 38635902644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38635902644), attempt 1, passed: 38 successful jobs, 28 planned skips, zero failures; required `openclaw/ci-gate` and `security-fast` passed. Native squash auto-merge landed the exact reviewed head. Two corrected-head probe starts also exposed an inherited environment proxy intercepting loopback WebSockets (502 with proxy, 101 direct); both performed zero cron mutations and shut down cleanly before the direct final probe succeeded. Original failure and preliminary attempts remain recorded.

title: fix(cron): avoid replaying slots covered by completed runs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate cron execution after a restart when the previous scheduled run lasted across later cron slots. Also corrects the documentation for silent subagent results.

## User Impact

Cron jobs no longer replay slots covered by a successful or skipped scheduled run. Genuine slots missed after completion and explicitly pending forced-run occurrences still run. Silent subagents remain subject to the existing required-result recovery contract; there is no change to that runtime behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart catch-up compared cron slots with the prior run start, although normal scheduling already advances from completion. Both restart paths now use the shared run-end calculation without changing failed-run backoff, trigger evaluation, or schedule activation boundaries. No configuration or state migration is required.

## Evidence

title: improve: reduce local full-suite test startup and retention costs
body:
Related: #172464

## What Problem This Solves

Complete local `pnpm test` runs spend unnecessary time starting tiny tooling batches and retaining large shared UI and Gateway worker module graphs.

## User Impact

Developers get less repeated test startup and bounded shared-worker lifetimes, with unchanged test coverage and execution policies. No production behavior, visual UI, migrations, or required actions change. The complete-suite >=20% speedup target remains **unproven**; this PR does not claim to complete it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Batch ordinary tooling and shared UI tests into at most eight files per process, and the shared Gateway database-worker fork into at most fifty. Canonical inventories, owning configs, pools, isolation, worker limits, and exclusive Gateway barriers stay intact. title: fix(cron): child handoffs finish early or reject intentional silence
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: isolated cron runs can finish before their child result when a no-delivery parent returns only `HEARTBEAT_OK`, or report an execution failure when an announce child deliberately completes silently.

## User Impact

User impact: delegated cron work waits for the child and records its result; intentional child silence completes quietly instead of producing a false failure. Timeouts, cancellation, and children that end without a reply remain failures. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize control-only handoffs independently of notification delivery. Spawn-only announce handoffs now use the existing child-owned settlement path already used by no-delivery jobs, rather than waiting for a parent synthesis that will not run. Preserve the distinction between explicit silence and a missing result.

Fixes agents treating an allocated portal or dispatched side-panel command as a usable preview when the requesting browser cannot reach it.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Portal allocation now returns exposure facts; the existing screen presentation flow returns the selected browser’s diagnosis. Network responses, panel dispatch, timeouts, and disconnects remain explicitly unverified rather than proving the app rendered. Capability-aware prompt guidance distinguishes app portals from the agent Browser panel.

Reported by and implemented at the direction of @steipete.

## Evidence

- Final exact-head [CI run 38620476718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38620476718), attempt 1, completed successfully: 74 jobs passed, 21 intentionally skipped, no failures. - Core and Control UI semantic typechecks passed; native Swift/Kotlin protocol contract generation and protocol version-train guard passed.

- Real isolated Gateway + actual Control UI + Chromium 153: local app rendering and click interaction passed; browser-to-tool feedback passed for local network reachability, synthetic remote-ingress blocking, new-tab-required, and deliberately dropped feedback (8.013 s timeout on the corrected candidate). No Team Gateway changes.

Core/UI types, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, docs MDX, protocol generation, native Swift/Kotlin contract generation, line-cap, and assertion-safety checks passed. Commit `89d826b8292db8ca548d0657d97bd1d8a318f036` fixes the producer rather than weakening those callers: only portal preview observations receive additive delivery/presentation metadata; other UI commands retain `{ok:true}`. Fresh real-Gateway/Chromium proof passed all four portal cases again, with no first-show retry. The correction also passed core types, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and independent review.
- Test mock correction `be82a1dafad36eef02f10d7f9103ad2f947e4076`: exact gateway-methods test typecheck reproduced CI’s TS2322 before the fix and passes afterward. The fixture now uses `GatewayBroadcastToConnIdsFn` and canonical payload validation rather than a narrowed transport mock. - Re-presentation correction `2d46a84bc0f0bb26580e9f632fae9ce76dc91c68`: the requester-routing E2E fixture now forwards actual correlated browser feedback to the real Gateway result handler and checks exact portal outcomes, not a fabricated response. That exposed a real repeated-show regression: forced probing detached the iframe and lost app state. Removing that redundant probe preserves the mounted document; explicit Retry still owns fresh network checks. Both Solid/custom-element iframe-identity regressions reproduced red before the repair; all 30 rendered portal tests and the full two-browser requester-routing E2E pass afterward. The E2E preserves the clicked application state across repeated show, and still verifies other-browser isolation. Split sides stay aligned, layout switches and unchanged refreshes preserve manual folds, and a changed patch opens them again.

Unsupported languages, oversized input, incomplete syntax, unsafe shared closing lines, and regions crossing omitted source stay expanded. No dependencies, editor replacement, configuration changes, or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing CodeMirror/Lezer highlighting parse to discover supported complete regions, then project those ranges onto the existing paired diff rows. One per-file presentation owns syntax and manual state above the split/unified branch. title: fix: keep large session diffs responsive
body:
Related: #171935

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the session diff can pause the UI while matching many long changed lines, even when each hunk fits the existing line-pair limit.

## User Impact

Large diffs stay more responsive while keeping every changed line, source order, syntax colors, and bounded word highlights. When matching would exceed the budget, the viewer pairs lines by position instead of searching for the closest match. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old matrix-cell limit did not account for the character work inside each comparison or repeated hunks/files. A conservative character-weighted budget now covers the whole expanded session diff, and prepared rows are reused when switching split/unified views. Tool previews share the same bounded pairing owner. The existing inexpensive inline engine and on-demand context loader stay in place; no renderer or dependency replacement.

Requested by and implemented with direction from @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/afebf434-a10b-4c6e-938b-038b26f7769d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/e7d7d452-7f13-4459-926f-54120370562c)

## Evidence

Actual optimized Control UI in Chromium, synthetic Gateway responses, identical ~90 KB patch (64 old + 64 new 700-character lines), 1600×900 desktop viewport. Median response-release-to-painted-frame over five refreshes per condition:

| Theme / CPU emulation | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Light / 4× slowdown | 300.2 ms | 100.8 ms |
| Dark / 4× slowdown | 308.6 ms | 98.2 ms |
| Light / unthrottled | 77.2 ms | 50.3 ms |
| Dark / unthrottled | 78.9 ms | 48.1 ms |

These are local browser measurements, not a physical mobile-device claim or a timing assertion in CI. Exact DOM-text assertions cover every changed line in split/unified views, refresh, and scrolling to the final row. Additional browser coverage includes inserted lines, repeated lines, Unicode/emoji, whitespace-only reformatting, and multi-file tool previews. Unit regressions cover the deterministic work estimate, cumulative multi-hunk/file budget, fallback source order, and retained inline highlights.

- Focused unit tests: 33 passed.
- Full session-diff browser suite: 12 passed; extracted budget suite: 2 passed; multi-file tool-preview boundary: passed.
- Targeted UI typecheck, lint, formatting, and optimized UI build passed.
- Independent source review: parent review found no actionable correctness issue; AutoReview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Before — expensive similarity matching (light theme):

![Before: large session diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7dcf9da7-67db-4599-af04-ed45242fbd12)

After — bounded positional fallback retains changed-line content and inline highlights:

![After: large session diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef6a9f8b-d0de-4f60-86c4-0b8b377f81ab)

Tradeoff: an oversized run may align an inserted/deleted line less intelligently; no content is discarded. This change does not add virtualization or structural diffing. Browser input is synthetic; no live Gateway was modified or restarted.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Wear OS app freezes when a speech action waits for Android’s text-to-speech engine to finish initializing or respond.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Wear speaker called TTS while holding a lock also used by UI actions. Its initialization, configuration, playback, callbacks, and disposal now share one background queue. Pending replies and stale callbacks remain isolated from stopped or replacement speech, and disposal releases the worker.

Scope is Wear reply speech only; phone speech, realtime Talk, dependencies, and the separate pager fix are unchanged.

## Evidence

- The new controlled-contention regression fails against unmodified base `1592e6dcf9482dcde5d191016548ece1b9a8c71f` with **“UI waited for a blocked TTS call”**, and passes with this fix. It exercises the production speaker’s public speak/stop/shutdown entry points.
- **114/114 tests pass** across `WearReplySpeakerTest`, `WearReplySpeakerThreadingTest`, `WearChatEventFlowTest`, and `WearAudioFailureTest`. This includes pending initialization, focus denial, replacement callbacks, worker shutdown, and existing automatic-speech UI flows.
- Wear debug APK build, Android lint, Kotlin formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed. The combined Gradle verification took 19 seconds.

[CI run 38571407177](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38571407177) completed successfully for this exact head, including Wear, Play and third-party tests, Kotlin formatting, security-fast, native i18n, 4K/16K Android-access checks, and the required CI gate. title: feat: download files from the Files list and preview
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Files list and file preview have no direct way to save a file to the user’s computer.

## User Impact

Users can download original files from the file-row actions or preview toolbar without navigating away. Downloads stream to the browser’s download manager without a separate file-size cap, including files too large to preview. Local files, Full Access host files, active managed repositories, and retained changed artifacts use their existing session read permissions.

Downloads require a same-origin Gateway connection, including same-origin proxies. Folders and unsaved editor changes are not downloaded. Provider-backed node workspaces whose bridge only exposes whole-file reads do not yet support downloads; they return an explicit error rather than buffering or reading a local fallback. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both controls share a small button and request a connection-bound HTTP grant from the session Files owner. The browser handles saving; Gateway and repository delivery use bounded byte windows or immutable Git-blob streams with backpressure and cancellation. This removes whole-file collection, hashing/rereading, browser Blob buffering, and the previous 8 MiB limit and disabled-button logic. Existing access and placement checks remain authoritative during delivery.

Requested by @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a0839d20-361a-4e46-b79a-0a373f65c9f3)

title: feat: use SubQ Snap for typed decisions
body:
## Summary

Adds the optional external SubQ Snap plugin for text/JSON Boolean judgments, choices and rubric scores through the native Decisions API. Operators select `subq/subq-snap-preview` and configure a protected SecretRef; their conversational model stays unchanged. Requests consume provider credits and are not automatically retried.

The plugin is excluded from bundled dist and included in the official external install/repair catalog. Answer maps preserve reserved question IDs such as `__proto__`. Images and richer V2 input remain a separate follow-up.

## Canonical integration

Candidate `d504910f168c07d4c4fef0b2c58dd77a8c5f003e` integrates frozen main `7973f2b300032d15e1f3470125cb9db0c5b6801b` through the native baseline-successor workflow, preserving contributor ancestry. The canonical generator resolved the single config-baseline hash conflict; the native candidate matched the complete generated tree. All SubQ runtime, manifest and test files are unchanged from `04bdc975`.

The shared V1 host repair [#175995](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175995) always supplies its secret/config-generation predicate, including direct core calls without a caller predicate. This resolves the original authority finding at the canonical owner; no duplicate SubQ credential-generation policy is added.

## Validation

- **Fresh `d504910f` focused proof: 43/43 pass.** Six registered-host cases, nine reserved-key result cases and 28 adapter cases. The host cases cover allowed tool, denied model, retired consumer, allowed direct core, SecretRef replacement and secret removal, with final HTTP counts **1 / 0 / 0 / 1 / 0 / 0**.
- Replacement/removal publish real secret snapshots during paused DNS while the caller remains alive. Direct core calls omit a caller predicate; both changes prevent the final POST. Removal also makes credential readiness false, and physical requests drain.
- The earlier counterfactual at `04bdc975` restored only the old conditional host predicate: both mutation cases then sent one forbidden POST. Canonical host bytes were restored; no production host diff remains.
- **Fresh `d504910f` builds pass:** full `pnpm build` (179.26 seconds; SDK declarations/exports, packaged runtime and UI), plus the official SubQ npm runtime build (1 entry/3 files). Canonical config generation/check and `git diff --check` pass. The merged dependency installation was qualified against the new frozen inputs.
- Independent review accepts the mechanical integration; unchanged feature code retains its prior independent and scoped external reviews. This baseline correction adds no production behavior.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39184102353) passed at `d504910f`: 168 successful jobs, 21 skipped, zero failures; both required gate contexts passed. [Current-head Claw review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171965#issuecomment-6236218057) reports no findings or before-merge items; its optional combined shipped-flow rank-up is deferred as described below. [Prior-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39149518663) passed at `04bdc975` (167 successful jobs, 21 skipped); that result is retained as prior-head evidence, not the new head's gate.

## Native proof and release scope

**Authenticated native SubQ qualification passed at `04bdc975` on 2026-10-19:** `extensions/subq/src/runtime.live.test.ts` executed one mixed synthetic Boolean/Choice/Score batch against `https://api.subq.ai/v1/systemone` using `subq-snap-preview`. One test/file passed, zero skipped, exit 0; source stayed unchanged. The protected key reached only the isolated invocation, with proxies and other credentials absent; the native child joined and temporary state was removed. The successor preserves the adapter, transport and live-fixture inputs, so this API-contract proof is retained without another paid call.

This is registered-adapter/native API proof. The separate host fixture covers configured policy, real SecretRef preparation and final-dispatch authority through owned loopback HTTP. A single live SecretRef-to-tool end-to-end run and installed-package qualification were not performed; the broader optional Claw rank-up is explicitly deferred. No deployment or live Codex behavior is claimed.

This remains an unpublished package candidate with documented source-checkout setup. Native image/V2 support is a named follow-up; the current V1 adapter advertises text/JSON only.
