title: fix: keep split diff edits aligned when lines are inserted
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes split file diffs pairing each changed line with the wrong counterpart when a replacement block also inserts or removes a line.

## User Impact

Reviewers can compare corresponding old/new lines and see the changed words or tokens without losing syntax colors. Inline highlighting also appears in unified diffs and tool-card edit previews. No configuration, dependency, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Align adjacent replacement runs by bounded text similarity while preserving each source side's order. One shared presentation owner computes token-level changed ranges; the existing renderer overlays them on optional syntax highlighting without changing or interpreting source text.

Unrelated replacements stay separate. Oversized runs retain positional pairing, and long/token-dense lines retain whole-line coloring rather than doing expensive inline work. This deliberately remains a lightweight text diff, not structural parsing.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the reported insertion-induced mispairing in the actual built Control UI with a synthetic mocked Gateway fixture; the regression fails before the fix and passes after it.
- All 10 session-diff browser tests pass, covering split/unified switching, syntax highlighting, renames, gaps, navigation, refresh, and retained state. Production Vite build passed as part of this flow.
- Focused presentation, panel, and tool-card tests pass. They protect source order, line numbers, context/file/gap boundaries, Unicode, whitespace, punctuation, escaping, unknown languages, and bounded fallbacks.
- UI typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, stylelint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Independent AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Subsequent changes only applied lint-required braces/naming and moved the new tool-card test into its own file to retain the existing file's line budget.

Local changed-file timings (wall / test time; CI timing pending): pairing 4.63s / <0.02s; panel 7.21s / ~1.4s; tool-card inline 5.69s / ~0.85s; browser suite 55.41s including production build / 20.36s (new regression 2.82s). The browser case uniquely proves the real Review navigation, rendered alignment, syntax overlay, and view switching.

### Inherited CI failure

CI run [38530389693](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38530389693) failed only `checks-ui-e2e (5/9)` (plus its aggregate gate): `new-session-page.instant-thread.e2e.test.ts` expected `old admission`, but the accepted draft was already empty. The published table classified this as unknown because no main job matched. I reproduced the same failure in the original file order (14 passed, 1 failed), inspected the unchanged test and acceptance owner on the tested main baseline `315e772a1d303d27471c88f9fd5ef788bf1027e5`, and traced it to the accepted-draft retirement change from #171768. This PR does not change that flow.

The baseline test was independently corrected on main in [0d02ec18729](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0d02ec18729e0255ba34035cd7441ef2afd42194): acceptance consumes the old draft before preview readiness. Native inherited-failure admission retains this failed run and attribution; it is not a claim that the old CI run passed. No CI rerun was requested.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Agents API uses native-owned context management: host compaction flags and thresholds are not reproduced, including an explicit host setting of `false`. Normal OpenClaw keeps its configured behavior.

Endpoint, authentication, headers, custom request parameters, and storage-policy incompatibilities remain strict. No configuration migration or shared-model edit is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An explicit harness capability allows validated host-compaction tuning to be tolerated at runtime selection and catalog availability, across default, model, agent-model, and agent parameters. Prepared transport overrides still take precedence. Agents API remains opt-in; automatic selection keeps strict compaction handling.

Validated `supportsTemperature` and `codeMode` values are capability metadata, not authored request overrides. Metadata-only configurations may consequently become eligible for other native runtimes; configurations with incompatible request policies remain blocked.

title: fix: typing lags on New Session with large model catalogs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow typing on the New Session page when a large model catalog is loaded.

## User Impact

User impact: entering a draft no longer rebuilds the hidden model picker on every keystroke. Model, thinking, connection, and configuration changes still update the controls. No settings changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Model controls now subscribe to their existing state owners and equality-gate their actual inputs, rather than treating a new draft-options object as a model change. The shared picker and its selection behavior remain unchanged.

Contributed with @vincentkoc, who reported the issue and requested the fix.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2b5ec2d1-12da-4a1c-888d-20b608fc269f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/f1e43c1b-3f78-4edf-8d0c-61c9352e85ec)

- [CI repair and landing](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/db8e12cb-eaef-4b8a-9405-630d3a7a281d)

## Evidence

- Production-bundle Chromium flow with 2,001 synthetic models and 500 sessions: ten native keystrokes perform zero catalog-label normalizations after the fix. Reverting only the model view to its original implementation produces 20,000 normalizations and fails the same assertion. Timing is diagnostic, not a machine-sensitive test threshold. The reproduced scale-dependent delay was roughly 137–210 ms/key before the fix versus roughly 33 ms/key after warmup, including two animation frames; the exact reported one-second delay was not reproduced on this host.
- Persistent mounted-view coverage exercises model/thinking selection, owner publications, in-place disconnect/reconnect, context replacement, and unsubscribe on replacement/unmount. Existing model-selection and metadata-lifecycle suites pass.
- Focused file wall times (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): model view 4.99 s; model controls 3.86 s; metadata lifecycle 6.51 s; New Session page 5.36 s. Browser regression: 29.07 s wall including production build, 1.78 s scenario. Current-head hosted test execution: model view 0.098 s; model controls 2.897 s; metadata lifecycle 7.445 s; New Session page 5.260 s (Vitest module duration; worker setup/collection excluded). Browser build/setup overhead is separate from the native-input scenario.
- UI typecheck, changed-file lint/format, line-cap and safety ratchets pass. Fresh independent review of the final production patch found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Broad validation is delegated to PR CI.
- This is a behavior/performance-only change with no visual layout changes; assertions and the native-input boundary probe are the relevant proof.

## CI follow-through

- Corrected two test-only type errors found by broad CI: pass the required session key to the thinking callback and use the canonical `offline` gateway phase. Production code is unchanged from the independently reviewed performance fix.
- The corrected mounted-view test passes (3.90 s wall, 105 ms test time); the UI-pages test typecheck, changed-file lint, formatting, and fresh P0–P2 AutoReview pass. Earlier CI run [38516373995](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38516373995), attempt 1, completed with failures; prior-head CI is not claimed as current-head proof. The SDK/type checks expose database type errors in unchanged baseline source. Separately, `checks-ui (3/3)` (job 115696378551) lost its hosted runner at 05:31:38 UTC: the test step was cancelled and the only check annotation is “The operation was canceled.” The cancellation origin is not verified, so it is not being treated as an inherited failure. That run is retained as prior-head evidence only; no exception was requested for it.

- Integrated protected-main database repair 920ab440dc829 for the eight failing SDK/type gates, at head a12102872a8bd533270fe06bd5712538e306e63e. This was a conflict-free, named-gate integration—not a code rewrite. The authored nine-file UI diff is byte-identical (SHA-256 00efecad0e40f1f745a0aa610208630e6904e71ee33ea1665dee9881867451c8), so prior independent review remains applicable. On the integrated tree, the mounted-view test passes (7.01 s wall / 103 ms test time), and the UI-pages test typecheck passes. Fresh CI [38520781392](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38520781392) and all enforced merge gates remain required.


### Shared-fixture follow-through

CI run 38520781392 exposed six test-fixture failures before its runner shutdown. The shared draft/repository fixtures lacked the application-owner subscriptions consumed by the mounted model view. Reproduced all six locally and repaired only the two fixture owners, without weakening production behavior. All 727 New Session tests across 62 suites then passed (40.89 s wall; 34.51 s Vitest). UI-pages typecheck, changed-file lint/format, and fresh independent P0–P2 review also passed. Reviewed/prepared head: `424ce346f38dd3ae3379373634428f61763c06cd`.

Historical exact-head CI [38523448268](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38523448268), attempt 1, is **failed**, not green: `checks-ui (3/3)` job 115718625741 received a hosted-runner shutdown signal at 06:46:55 UTC, interrupting the test step. The downloaded job log contains no failed test cases before shutdown. All other selected jobs passed, including UI shards 1/3 and 2/3, UI E2E, performance, types, lint, and security-fast. The CI gate failed downstream.

This is not being waived as inherited: the published failure report classifies the UI job as **unknown**. Its referenced main job 115698596492 ended at its 20-minute deadline, which is not a matching cause for this 6½-minute runner loss. Latest scheduled main run 38524323148 failed preflight and provides no comparable UI result. At that stage the PR remained open, with the previous auto-merge request confirmed retired.

Following the existing recovery procedure in `docs/ci/watching-runs.md`, one failed-job retry was issued for the terminal run without changing the source. title: fix: keep recovering from rate limits after successful progress
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long-running agent turns stop recovering from intermittent rate limits even when successful model responses occurred between failures. The final error can misleadingly show only a short provider retry hint.

## User Impact

Agent turns receive a fresh retry budget after a completed successful model response. Consecutive failures remain bounded, and terminal rate-limit errors explain actual automatic retry exhaustion. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failover controller resets the consecutive-outage retry count, backoff, and window only on completed model responses; partial streams and tool activity alone do not replenish them. The outer recovery guard follows the same progress signal. Existing per-attempt timeouts, caller deadlines, cancellation, output-limit continuation caps, and fallback routing remain intact.

Controller-recorded exhaustion now travels through error, payload, fallback, and final-reply paths without replacing raw provider diagnostics. Progressing turns can exceed a single attempt budget in aggregate; no competing whole-turn timer is introduced.

title: fix: recover accepted agent updates after Gateway restart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted agent-to-agent updates being stranded after a Gateway restart and shown with misleading instructions to copy and resend them.

## User Impact

Accepted, unconsumed `sessions_send` updates resume once, in order, when current session permissions still allow delivery. Cancelled inputs stay cancelled; reset, archived, replaced, or access-revoked sessions are not revived. Blocked updates remain saved with a visible reason. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing pending-input owner and normal agent admission path rather than replaying sender tasks or adding a second queue. Recheck session identity and current communication authority before admission, preserve queued recovery claims until their owners release them, and keep private delivery metadata out of history. The UI distinguishes saved agent updates from unsent human messages.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Gateway cold-process test: accept five peer updates, terminate the receiver process, restart, and observe all five in order. title: feat: move sessions between local and cloud from session menus
body:
Related: #132846 (shared session-action parity only; broader menu taxonomy remains separate).

## What Problem This Solves

Moving an existing session between local and cloud execution is hard to discover from the session menus, and interrupted moves need a safe retry that preserves the original destination.

## User Impact

Users can choose **Move to cloud…**, **Move to local**, or **Retry move** from the sidebar, Sessions page, and chat header without losing the session or its history. Managed repository/worktree sessions are eligible; plain unmanaged sessions show why they cannot move. No configuration migration is required. Moves wait for workspace settlement; offline abandonment still requires explicit destructive confirmation. Cloud provisioning is not instantaneous.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared placement-action policy and runtime now serve the menu entry points. Durable retry metadata preserves the original source authority and exact destination across refresh/reconnect rather than guessing generations. Live scope and session identity are checked before dispatch so a delayed picker cannot act on a replacement session. Ordinary Move is disabled while worker files are being finalized. The sidebar integration is adapted to current main's Solid menu owner.

Source integration was tested at a6239afa203490223bfd55639b61321b9a072178 and published with the identical tree as c66a94ae7a26ae74f907fd440eb93ce3a5441ef8 (integration base b656d96a421c54eade946f9c14d209276d602120). title: fix: recover uploaded chat images after loading fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: uploaded and local chat images remain broken without a recovery action when metadata succeeds but the image request fails or its bytes cannot be decoded.

## User Impact

Failed previews now show **Unavailable** with **Retry**. Retry checks current availability and access before loading again; permissions, existing ticket expiry, and tolerance for temporary renewal failures on already-mounted images stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native image errors do not expose an HTTP status. Report them through the existing attachment availability owner instead of ignoring local sources, and require an explicit retry rather than replaying possibly denied or missing requests. Metadata 403/404 responses also wait for an explicit retry. Canonical upload handoff failures use the same recovery path.

Reported and directed by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/73e88a09-84af-49d6-9146-ee44e7356171)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/ba984d5b-ba7f-46f2-9a31-362cc80eda05)

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the fix in Chromium: metadata succeeds, the native uploaded-image byte request returns 404, and no unavailable card or Retry appears.
- Revalidated after integrating main `ae55909c90267aaaf48f03a25883a1f6faa061e9`: **6 Chromium cases passed** covering native 404, 503, network and decode failures, successful explicit retry, and 403/404 retry admission without another byte request. Earlier browser coverage also passed virtual-remount and sharing/role-revocation cases.
- **78 focused tests passed** on the integrated candidate: native image admission, canonical transcript handoff (including error and timeout), ticket expiry, renewal and attachment availability. The two stale CI handoff expectations now prove a recoverable card, no automatic retry or stale-event resurrection, and a fresh authorized retry. Browser-auth restoration cannot silently replay a native failure; ordinary metadata authentication recovery remains covered.
- UI typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent P0–P2 review found the auth-restoration replay edge case; it was reproduced and corrected. The follow-up assessment found no additional working-tree defects; its remaining index-only finding was resolved by staging the reviewed correction.
- Deterministic mocked-Gateway browser tests exercise real native image requests. The original user's exact HTTP failure status remains unconfirmed; this does not claim to reproduce that historical status. No deployment is included.

### Inherited CI exception

Exact-head CI run [38693105647, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38693105647) completed with two baseline failures: `check-docs` (formatting in `wizard-step-controls.ts` and `chat-picker-overlay.test.ts`) and `check-lint-core-2` (`no-generated-empty-object-type` in `chat-composer-types.ts` and `chat-pane-session-controls.ts`). All four failing inputs are byte-identical between that main parent and the tested merge; the lint failures also reproduce on main. The older scheduled-main comparison labels these jobs new because its scope was not compared; direct source and reproduction evidence establishes the inherited failures.

The two formatting failures were separately repaired on main in `d08cd455ce1c6370bb4d0e547b7157120b946d52`. Landing this image fix uses the native inherited-failure exception under the scoped fix-and-land request, with exact-head evidence and live review/security/authority checks. Failed CI is not represented as green.

title: fix: preserve subagent completion delivery outcomes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading blocked-completion warnings and duplicate retry attempts when a subagent's result handoff succeeds but receipt bookkeeping fails.

## User Impact

Confirmed subagent results remain delivered. Real delivery failures retain their concrete cause across retries, and blocked warnings identify the affected child run. No configuration or migration is required; unconfirmed handoffs are not treated as delivered.

title: fix(ui): avoid delayed Safari tint after sidebar closes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone Safari, closing the mobile sidebar reveals the page before the native top and bottom browser bars finish their own tint fade.

## User Impact

The drawer still dims the whole app canvas and closes with the existing animation. Its scrim no longer participates in Safari's fixed-element color extension, so browser chrome stays on the page surface instead of acquiring a separate delayed fade. No settings or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Safari owns that second animation: WebKit's fixed-container edge detector retains the dimming layer's background color until it disappears, then WKColorExtensionView animates the native tint to clear over 100 ms. Matching CSS durations or updating theme-color would not share an animation owner.

Anchor the existing scrim absolutely to the already-positioned app host, preserving safe-area coverage, stacking, swipe handling, and the single page fade. Keep the drawer itself unchanged.

## Worked on by

- @steipete

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/af47e5cf-793f-4830-90ff-5d2f49b705f2)

## Evidence

- Focused production-bundle E2E: all six native navigation/responsive layout cases pass. Portrait and landscape swipe cases additionally check the independent WebKit fixed/sticky sampling boundary, full-canvas scrim hit coverage including synthetic safe areas, and resized viewport coverage.
- Both modified swipe cases fail against the original CSS on the fixed/sticky invariant, and pass after the change.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint/stylelint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The initial CI run caught an inferred coordinate array that needed an explicit `[number, number]` tuple; corrected without changing runtime behavior. The exact `core-test-ui-e2e` type graph now passes locally. Independent AutoReview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Chromium capture confirms unchanged drawer/page geometry and preserved composer draft. These are page-only screenshots, not native Safari chrome proof. The before state overrides only the changed position declaration back to fixed on the same app, data, theme, and viewport.
- Native iPhone Safari was unavailable on this host. The native tint diagnosis is source-backed; actual Safari top/bottom chrome is not live-verified. No live server deployment.

WebKit source at [4681ea866adfe6ae9731ebb2ff0fe0b706446a1b](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/tree/4681ea866adfe6ae9731ebb2ff0fe0b706446a1b): [fixed-container edge sampling](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/4681ea866adfe6ae9731ebb2ff0fe0b706446a1b/Source/WebCore/page/LocalFrameView.cpp), [retained edge color](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/4681ea866adfe6ae9731ebb2ff0fe0b706446a1b/Source/WebCore/page/Page.cpp), and [native 100 ms color fade](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/4681ea866adfe6ae9731ebb2ff0fe0b706446a1b/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/Cocoa/WKColorExtensionView.mm).

### After

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes sluggish typing in the New Session composer, where each input repeatedly rebuilds composer and placement options and forces synchronous layout measurement.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Memoize composer and placement projections once per reactive revision, keep the retained Solid slot props stable across the Lit bridge, and use the same native-input sizing fast path as Chat. Add regression coverage for bounded projection work and zero synchronous geometry reads during native input.

## Evidence

These are local measurements, not a universal timing guarantee.
- Both new regressions fail on the original implementation and pass with the fix.
- After resolving the current-main import overlap, all **117** focused composer/page/model/placement tests pass on `3c0c29b9edc986326294ba3af86813c23a8893ef`. title: fix: mobile scrolling jumps over visualizations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: mobile chat scrolling jumps backward and stops abruptly when a swipe starts over an inline visualization.

## User Impact

Users can scroll through visualizations with continuous tracking and normal release momentum. Mouse-wheel forwarding and widget isolation are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

Physical iPhone/Safari behavior has not been verified; the browser proof uses mobile-emulated Chromium.

## Why This Change Was Made

The touch relay measured movement inside an iframe that its own forwarded scroll moved. title: fix(x): recover allowed mentions when authorization changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an allowed X mention can exhaust model fallbacks and publish a generic error when its authorization snapshot changes before the run starts.

## User Impact

Allowed requests recover against current policy before model execution. Revoked requests and changed routes are dropped deliberately; temporary authorization-storage failures return an actionable retry message instead of silently disappearing. Existing owner, configuration, and use-time revocation checks remain in force. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Renew mutable source authorization once at the existing run-admission boundary, with at most three X policy-snapshot attempts. Retain the resulting synchronous guard for publication rather than renewing an admitted run. Classify authorization failures separately from provider failures so switching models cannot replay stale authority.

The incident's initial snapshot invalidator remains unknown. This fixes the reproduced recovery failure; it does not rebind command-owner/profile authority or weaken public-thread verification.

## Evidence

- **Full CI passes on `23493d4143d6903fcc58cef94f6da0425a718bb0`:** [run 38478061382](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38478061382) completed successfully, including the six-scenario final-effect test, baseline ratchets, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. Exact-head inventory: 71 successful, 68 skipped, 1 neutral; no failed or pending checks.
- **361 focused tests passed** on base `4ff90e65394100f953db0dd5678eea614370172c`: 25 admission/publication tests, 242 X tests, and 94 failover/runner sibling tests.
- The seven-case regression uses real X ingress, host participant binding, run admission, and model-fallback selection. It covers unrelated policy mutation, author revocation, route change, continuous policy churn, one recoverable policy race, owner retirement, and unavailable authorization storage. Model execution is mocked; no live X post was sent.
- A negative control on the original implementation selected a second model after stale authorization, failing the new assertion. The fix selects one candidate; denied/unavailable cases execute no model.
- Independent P0–P2 review completed with no actionable findings.
- Initial CI exposed an error-message mismatch in `x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts`: the renewed guard rejected configuration revocation correctly but returned “configuration changed before run admission” instead of the existing “publication policy changed” message. The guard now preserves that message and its “send a new mention” guidance; no assertion or revocation behavior was weakened.
- In response to ClawSweeper’s final-effect proof request, the existing single-fixture production-owner test now covers six scenarios. A real SQLite allowlist mutation invalidates captured X authority before admission; the allowed request must then reach real `sessions_spawn` → `sessions.create` → persisted public grant → anonymous HTTP read. Separate awaited-creation cases remove the author or retire the actual plugin/ingress owner and require zero new child rows, including private/orphaned rows. Guest, delegation-revocation, and configuration-revocation coverage is retained. This is in-process owner-composition coverage with deterministic X transport and model execution, not live X proof.
- **CI execution at `cc1c27dd77f0`:** the renewed allowed request reached child creation, public-grant persistence, and anonymous HTTP read; the guest, delegation-revocation, and configuration-revocation iterations also completed. The test then failed on a zero-reply expectation in a late-revocation case (15.202s test body; 44.25s Vitest duration, [job evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38473245127/job/115558347125)). The emitted failure did not identify which case, so the full six-scenario result was not passing.
- **Retirement-fixture correction:** the next run (`65cf9f0f45fb`) passed author revocation but failed the owner case with a success reply/link (15.168s test body; 46.60s Vitest, [job evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38475144241/job/115564602659)). Source inspection found that the Gateway test fixture had adopted the plugin into its retained registry; the test retired the old builder registry, not the live owner. The test now resolves the actual record owner, asserts active → inactive at retirement, and checks durable child/grant counts before reply assertions. It permits only no reply or the exact harmless denial text; author removal still requires no reply. This failure does not establish a product publication bypass.
- **Final-effect proof passes at `23493d4143d6`:** [the CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38478061382/job/115574480836) executed the six-scenario composition successfully on the PR merge ref (`0a88ae88`, merging this head into `9690a6d7`). This is one passing test containing six scenarios: renewed allowed publication and anonymous read, guest denial, delegation revocation, configuration revocation, author removal, and actual ingress-owner retirement. Rejected cases commit no new child/public grant; owner retirement exposes no success link. Test body: **10.692s**; Vitest: **28.99s**.
- ClawSweeper’s [exact-head re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171384#issuecomment-6155721175) reports **ready for maintainer review, zero findings, and no remaining “Before merge” items**. This is advisory readiness, not human merge approval.
- The preceding `460a033799fe` run reached all security assertions but failed on the outer Gateway retirement error text (16.593s body, 42.24s Vitest). The final test-only correction matches that existing outer error exactly; it does not change product behavior or weaken the no-child/no-grant checks.
- Existing real registry-adoption tests pass (2 cases, 54.91s wall), as do the Gateway-root typecheck (2.59s), scoped lint (12.72s), formatting, and `git diff --check`. No live X post was sent.
- The same CI run identified a changed closed runtime mock. It now preserves the real module/runtime exports while overriding only logging; the exact obsolete baseline entry was removed (9678 → 9677, no new allowance). The mock-export check passes, and 43 runner lifecycle/provider tests pass in 27.52s; scoped typecheck, lint, and formatting pass.
- Local full-composition preparation remains unavailable: direct preparation refuses unverifiable separation from the managed Gateway; a supported network-isolated attempt failed during runtime build with `Error: oneshot canceled` (127.54s; container removal verified). These are not passing results, and the guard was not bypassed.
- Five scoped typechecks, targeted lint, all-15-file formatting, docs MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Full build gap:** `pnpm build` failed after 124.69s in `openclaw-native-declarations` with a native TypeScript compiler nil-pointer panic. The exact-base comparison was interrupted after 292.2s (SIGTERM), so baseline attribution is inconclusive; this is not claimed as a passing or proven inherited build.

title: fix: archive sessions after orphaned worker cleanup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: archiving a session with orphaned worker provisioning can fail with a retry message even though its cleanup succeeds.

## User Impact

User impact: sessions can archive after successful provisioning cleanup without a spurious retry. Failed cleanup still leaves the session unarchived; workspace recovery and live authority checks remain intact. No configuration or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The archive starts early reclaim to retain dispatch custody. That reclaim can publish a placement change while the archive prepares a strict runtime snapshot, invalidating the archive's own read. Join the already-started cleanup after cancellation and before taking that snapshot. Active-placement drains retain their existing ordering.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through `sessions.patch` with the real placement store and reclaim owner, holding the runtime read through cleanup publication. title: fix: keep Codex commands on the selected GitHub identity
body:
Related: #157500
Builds on merged #171168; this PR now targets main.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex native shell execution can bypass the managed GitHub profile selected for the OpenClaw run instead of using the same credential and authority owner as native/Pi execution.

## User Impact

Selecting a managed GitHub identity now routes Codex commands through OpenClaw's existing host-owned tools, preserving selected-profile launch binding, command approvals, caller lifetime, cancellation, and actionable authentication errors. An unavailable profile does not fall back to an ambient account; restoring or changing the identity through Settings allows recovery. Without a managed selection, native Codex defaults remain unchanged.

Ordinary node execution still uses node-local authentication. Selecting a Gateway GitHub identity or approving a command does not export its reusable bearer token to a paired node. Repository-bound workers keep their separate existing contract, and Gateway-side github_publish remains available. There is no new delegation capability or configuration migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one host-owned credential selection and execution lifecycle rather than introducing a Codex-only token grant. The harness advertises a non-secret host-execution requirement, binds the prepared selection into its tool surface, and disables competing native shell features for that run. Borrowing another agent's tool policy does not change the executing agent's credential identity. This avoids relying on Codex's serialized environment overlay as a credential-authority boundary.

Split from #157500 by @galiniliev, preserving contributor credit. Personally inspected the pinned upstream Codex 0.160.0 source at a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc, including child environment overlay ordering and native shell feature defaults.

title: fix: keep cloud-worker GitHub credentials usable across long turns
body:
Related: #157500

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: repository-bound cloud workers can lose GitHub authentication during long turns, or retain credential authority after their original session writer changes.

## User Impact

Long-running worker turns can renew the same selected GitHub identity without waiting for credential discovery at turn startup. Cancellation, writer replacement, profile removal, and terminal completion stop renewal and settle credential writes before cleanup. Older workers without renewal support are rejected through the existing rebuild/retry path.

This keeps the existing credential-carrying contract for repository-bound worker turns. It does not export Gateway credentials to ordinary paired-node exec, add repository-free delegation, or claim that deleting a local profile revokes a token already copied from it. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The background identity owner prepares the launch snapshot; an admitted turn retains its original caller, session writer, workspace, and account. Heartbeats can refresh that account only while those owners remain current. The worker writes the refreshed token privately for subsequent command launches, acknowledges installation, and joins in-flight writes before removing its per-turn profile.

Split from the worker credential investigation and implementation in #157500 by @galiniliev; preserves that contributor's credit while excluding the proposed broader node delegation.

## Evidence

### Landed — October 15

title: fix: keep local GitHub commands on the selected credential host
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local commands using a prepared Enterprise GitHub profile could read the github.com entry instead, and inherited Enterprise fallback tokens could survive the private launcher.

Related: #157500. This is the independently useful local-credential slice; it does not include cloud-worker lifecycle changes or paired-node credential delegation.

## User Impact

Local Pi exec, Codex gateway_exec, and opted-in Docker/Podman exec use the selected profile host and clear both public and Enterprise fallback variables. Public managed profiles stay pinned to github.com; only the matching public or Enterprise token family is exported. Ordinary paired-node execution is unchanged: it keeps node-local authentication and receives no Gateway-selected bearer token.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the admitted host into the existing private launcher, look up only that host in the private profile, and forward the existing token variables to opted-in containers by name. Missing, insecure, or wrong-host profiles fail before the requested command runs. No new credential store, delegation permission, or configuration setting is introduced.

This extraction preserves the contribution in the original PR by @galiniliev, with continuation and regression work requested by @vincentkoc.

title: fix: agent-requested plugin reloads stall the current task
body:
Closes #170881

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent’s task stalls when it reloads a plugin while its own turn still holds that plugin’s runtime.

## User Impact

User impact: an authorized agent can request a reload through the native plugins tool or a managed local CLI invocation, finish its current turn, and automatically continue the same conversation after replacement settles. Completed actions and the original user request are not replayed.

The initial receipt means **accepted, not applied**. Unbound human CLI calls still wait for their normal completed result. Parked Code Mode programs and unsupported authority/runtime contexts are refused with a manual path. If the Gateway stops before recording an outcome, recovery reports it as unknown rather than blindly repeating the reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requesting turn cannot wait for work that must first drain that same turn. This transfers the accepted request to independent maintenance, waits for physical cleanup of the entire turn and outer dispatch, then uses the normal reload owner and a fresh, source-authorized continuation. It does not exempt retained work or force disposal.

Accepted intent and actual outcome use the existing SQLite delivery queue and write broker. The durable record contains original source/permission facts, not a live bearer credential; reset, Stop, archive, policy changes, and source revocation fence continuation. Existing terminal cleanup removes the payload. No database DDL or schema-version bump is needed; the changed persistence and authorization contract is documented for review. Older queue readers ignore the private namespace, but normal database schema admission still applies: a binary downgrade across schema versions requires a matching pre-upgrade backup.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway and both reload entry points:** the expanded production-path test passed against the rebuilt candidate runtime. One initial `chat.send` performs a native reload, resumes automatically, executes the real reload CLI through managed top-level exec, then resumes automatically again. Physical disposal barriers prevent early continuation; generations advance 1 → 2 → 3, the original request appears once, and the completed file effect occurs once.
- **Final-effect authority:** the same test authenticates a non-admin client and observes real RPC refusal with no disposal/registration; stops an admitted continuation while its provider response is held, then releases a proposed privileged exec and verifies no file was written; and revokes the originating device while disposal is held, verifying the changed candidate is never registered, captured prior code is restored, and a separate authorized conversation still completes. An authorized candidate-edit reload succeeds first, so the revoked case cannot pass merely because edited plugins fail to load.
- **Persistence compatibility:** a separate real-SQLite, source-bound check passed in 4.17s using v2026.10.2 (`b8952d477f0c`) queue source and candidate `6f24c04403b2` queue source, unchanged by the follow-up. Shipped event/media rows survive the actual v21 projection migration and candidate reads; shipped readers read ordinary candidate rows but neither list nor load reload rows. Reload outcomes survive close/reopen; duplicate publication preserves the first outcome. Unmodified queue payload, settings, config bytes, and an untouched session-database sentinel remain unchanged; queue operations add no DDL and integrity checks pass.
- **Build and focused checks:** full `pnpm build` passed on the initial candidate (24m 38s). The follow-up (`2871dbc7438b`) runtime build passed in 80s. The expanded product test took 16.85s, with 48.98s total for `pnpm test test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/plugin-reload-handoff.product-proof.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` using that prebuilt runtime. Follow-up exec/egress/handoff/sentinel tests passed: 80 tests across five files, 74.34s total. Earlier queue, runtime-refresh, installed-package and authority suites also passed. Core and scoped proof typechecks, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, assertion-safety ratchet, and diff checks passed. Hosted timing for the expanded test is not yet available.
- **Review:** independent review completed before the initial commit and again for the follow-up, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. [Fresh hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170992#issuecomment-6144799827) on `2871dbc7438b` reports no code or security findings and accepts the real-Gateway authority proof. Its remaining request is full published-to-candidate upgrade evidence. The only subsequent source change is the explicit isolation annotation on an existing test mock.
- **Published upgrade proof — passed, with limits:** [Package Acceptance run 38399596565](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38399596565/attempts/1) passed all nine selected jobs (15 unselected jobs skipped). The published `openclaw@2026.10.2` updater installed candidate `0aabd6584ae4` in the `legacy-operator-state` survivor scenario: one attempt, 1,238s. Recorded build IDs prove the update despite equal version strings. The cell verifies shared/agent migration 20/24 → 22/26, asserted settings/approvals/skills/agent and cron ownership, candidate health/readiness and an agent turn, legacy pending-final-delivery import, repeat-update no-op, clean Doctor, and isolated restoration of the pre-upgrade backup. [Redacted survivor artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38399596565/artifacts/11819451854); trusted harness `a1e828269c9a`; candidate tarball SHA-256 `1e87586408d529fb0f2a696e7a3ecb3b30bb1c89409ca589b5da1e091c2a8322`. Independent artifact review confirmed these results and the gaps below.

<details>
<summary>Redacted execution output</summary>

```text
[build-all] phase timings: total 1m 20s
✓ plugin-reload-handoff.product-proof.e2e.test.ts
  ✓ reloads resume without replay, refuse non-admin callers, and honor Stop and revocation 16851ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 48.98s

Compatibility report excerpt:
result: PASS
scope: source-bound queue row-format + namespace compatibility, not whole-binary startup or migration
durationMs: 4171
SQLite integrity_check=ok
```

</details>

**Coverage limits:** the end-to-end test uses a deterministic local Responses provider, not an external model or messaging service. Stop is tested after continuation admission and before a late provider tool call, not during an exec-approval wait. Interrupted/unknown-outcome recovery is tested at the canonical queue/authority boundary, not by killing a live Gateway mid-reload. The queue compatibility check directly invokes shipped/candidate queue owner code with shared generic utilities and the real v21 migration kernel; it does not exercise the full published updater or worker broker. The separate package-upgrade cell covers the updater and schema migrations, but does **not** prove candidate readback of historical SQLite sessions/transcripts or old event/media queue rows through that upgrade. Its pending-delivery specimen is legacy session `pendingFinalDelivery`, not a delivery-queue row. Historical session/transcript contents are checked on the restored pre-upgrade backup, not through candidate history. These complementary checks are not an integrated old-queue × full-upgrade test. Restart was manual, and this scenario does not perform a full installed-payload byte comparison. Stable supports schemas 20/24 versus candidate 22/26: rollback requires the matching pre-upgrade backup, not opening candidate databases with the old binary. This is **not full binary upgrade/downgrade certification**; the hosted review’s stronger historical-state request is not claimed fully closed.

**CI and remaining review notes:** the first CI run found a new assertion-safety entry after moving media settlement; the follow-up removes that assertion through the canonical coercion helper and shrinks the old baseline. Exec process grants now have one launch/cancellation/settlement owner, resolving the exec-runtime line ratchet. The single host-issued `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_RELOAD_ORIGIN_TOKEN` name increases the environment count from 455 to 456; the budget remains unchanged because raising it requires owner approval (CI currently reports this as advisory). Current-head [CI run 38399589660](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38399589660) now passes the baseline ratchets: the existing routing-test mock now declares its required process-global isolation, and all 14 plugin-tool tests pass (8.77s runner wall time). Three test jobs still fail with the same streaming-final, queued-RPC timeout, and oversized-history symptoms investigated below; their CI-specific cause is unresolved. The setup-inference failure did not repeat. Passing local replays are not claimed as fixes.

<details>
<summary>First-run CI failure investigation</summary>

[Run 38391006907](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38391006907) tested head `6f24c04403b2` against CI base `2857f1333d07`; the implementation base is `7a5529f4c964`. Failure classification reported the assertion baseline as new and four test jobs as unknown, not established inherited failures.

- **Streaming recovery:** rejected, deferred-rejection, concurrent, and timeout-media cases missed expected final payloads in CI. A local attempt initially failed earlier at synthetic-provider connection. With localhost excluded from this host’s external HTTP proxy, all 13 scenarios pass, including those four. The underlying final-payload owners are unchanged from the implementation base; the enclosing dispatch gains the handoff scope. A causal CI regression or shared-state trigger is not established.
- **Queued RPC restart:** CI timed out before its `RPC_OWNER_BEFORE_CLOSE` marker. The first local attempt likewise never reached the provider boundary. The bounded localhost-proxy-corrected run passes all three tests and reaches both markers, recording queued reply custody before close and interrupted safe-tool recovery afterward. This does not prove the original CI timeout repaired.
- **History and inference setup:** CI reported an unsuccessful oversized-history RPC and an inference-concurrency count mismatch. The exact selected local suites pass (77 history tests and 17 setup tests). Those implementations are unchanged by this PR; the CI-specific cause remains unresolved.

The two proxy-corrected suites took 149.13s including runner preparation. No test assertion, timeout, retry, or production delivery policy was weakened. These results justify no speculative production repair; exact-head CI and the remaining environment-budget decision are not claimed green or waived.

</details>

Implemented with @jacobtomlinson.

title: fix(ui): unrelated catalog sessions appear in Involving me
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unrelated remote/shared catalog sessions appear under **Involving me**, and selecting another owner can show an empty list when their sessions belong to a different agent.

## User Impact

**Involving me** keeps genuinely involved conversations and excludes catalog access that does not establish involvement. Explicit owner selections work across agents without changing the conversation currently open. **All owners** still exposes the full accessible catalog. No configuration, schema, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog projection treated an absent owner ID as an unfiltered view even when Involving me was selected. It now uses backing-session keys admitted by the existing Gateway involvement filter, rather than inferring participation from sharing, creator labels, or cached agent lists. The related owner-selection fix reuses the existing cross-agent scope for every explicit owner.

## Evidence

- Both regressions failed before their fixes. 38 targeted sidebar/controller tests passed (16.85 s command wall time).
- Two Chromium UI regression tests passed on the combined final changes (40.20 s suite wall time). The new browser regression uses the existing suite fixture; expected CI browser cost is approximately its observed runtime, rather than a separate process per assertion.
- Targeted lint, UI typecheck, formatting, diff checks, and `pnpm ui:build` passed.
- Fresh AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Browser coverage retains a genuinely involved adopted coding conversation, excludes unrelated adopted/remote/imported catalog entries, and restores them under All owners.
- These are actual Control UI Chromium captures using a synthetic mock Gateway. Live replay on the Team account was unavailable because the managed browser endpoint did not start. This PR does not deploy or restart the Team Gateway.

### Before

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled PR checks and other agent automations losing the tool needed to inspect or remove their own job when no interactive owner is present.

## User Impact

title: fix(ui): stop repeated warnings while model requests recover
body:
Closes #170798

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated provider-error warnings in chat while a model request is retrying or falling back.

## User Impact

Recovery stays in the working claw row: **Retrying…**, a real retry countdown when available, or **Trying fallback model…**. Only a settled failed run gets one compact failure notice with a line icon, **Try again**, **Change model**, and expandable details. Partial output and unsent drafts remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal lifecycle now owns the durable failure notice. Failed attempt rows cannot suppress it, and history no longer guesses that an attempt was terminal because its run is absent from an active snapshot. Live events, history reloads, and in-flight status replay use the same run identity.

**Try again** sends a continuation asking the agent to check completed actions, rather than replaying the original prompt. Changing models opens the existing picker; neither action clears a draft.

No database schema change or transcript rewrite. Old run-attributed attempts without terminal receipts remain in raw history but are no longer promoted into terminal notices. Unattributed legacy diagnostics retain their existing display. Countdown support follows owner-reported deadlines; native harness-internal retry normalization is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Focused Gateway projection, live transcript, paginated history, and event regressions: **93 tests passed**, combining the unchanged 70-test passing subset and the final 23-test rerun (37.42s wrapper wall time).
- Focused retry-owner, protocol, persistence, and UI clock/status/action tests passed. Recovery-history regression: 2 tests, 3.73s wrapper wall time; UI clock/notice/action batch: 28 tests, 10.41s wrapper wall time.
- Bundled Control UI browser proof: **2 tests passed**, 8.11s test time / 36.92s total. Covers retry → fallback → success, live failure → durable notice → reload, desktop/mobile/light/dark presentation, the existing model picker, and continuation without losing a draft.
- Core and UI TypeScript checks passed. Independent autoreview completed with no actionable P0/P1 findings. Current-head CI completed; inherited-only failures are documented below.
- CI follow-up moved the unchanged failure selector to its lifecycle owner, ported the new notice to Solid, fixed the diagnostic font token, and updated sibling receipt/projection expectations. Recovery regressions: 161 passed (165.88s wrapper); Solid notice/theme-token checks: 12 passed (8.31s); real Gateway/local provider HTTP/MCP spawn proof: 13 passed (122.15s). Lit migration/import-cycle checks, scoped lint, stylelint, and UI types passed. Independent P0/P1 review of the follow-up was clean.
- Final bundled UI recheck: 2 passed, 10.24s test time / 42.32s total; fresh light/dark/mobile and expanded-detail captures inspected after the Solid migration. The representative collapsed before/after appearance is unchanged.
- UI browser I/O uses a deterministic mock Gateway; spawn proof uses local synthetic provider HTTP, not live-provider testing.

### CI result

[Current-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38372035347) completed all 119 jobs. Build, UI tests/E2E/performance, types, lint, docs, Android, and security-fast passed. Two unchanged baseline test inputs failed, plus their aggregate gate:

- `server.sessions.create.titles.test.ts`: two cases still require title generation to wait for dispatch, contrary to main commit `82acd0a1c02a` (start naming before workspace/reply startup).
- `server.chat-membership-authority.product.test.ts`: waits for a membership reread that main commit `ab981e29a670` intentionally replaces with prepared committed authority. The failure occurs before the test performs its revocation.

Both tests and their causal owners are byte-identical between the actual tested main `aea10c9d20e4` and merge `0189dd9a8ad2`. This is source-proven baseline attribution, not a claimed baseline test replay. Landing uses the native inherited-only exception; failed CI is not relabeled green, and security/review gates remain required. Earlier Doctor/requester timing failures were not claimed fixed by these UI changes.

title: fix: prevent chat image loading from shifting messages
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat content jumping when an uploaded image loads from saved history: the preview could shrink from its placeholder to zero height before expanding again.

## User Impact

Image previews keep neighboring messages in place through metadata loading, download, decoding, and the upload-to-history handoff. New uploads retain their actual pixel dimensions, including rotated JPEGs. Older images without dimensions fit inside a stable 3:2 preview; opening the image still shows its full size. No configuration changes or data migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Measure image geometry from uploaded bytes in the existing attachment-processing path and preserve it in durable media facts and the UI projection. Keep each mounted preview’s reserved frame for its lifetime, so a later upload receipt cannot resize an already-visible image. Fresh history mounts use the recorded dimensions. Remove the superseded unsized managed-image rule.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the saved-media failure in Chromium: a 1200×977 fixture reserved 400×267 CSS pixels, collapsed to 0×0 while image bytes were pending, then expanded to 400×326. The following text moved twice. After the fix, frame and next-message geometry stay unchanged at all three stages, with and without recorded dimensions.
- **34 backend tests passed**, including inline/offloaded uploads, incorrect caller dimensions, EXIF rotation, and unreadable headers. Four new regressions failed before the backend repair. Wall time: 37.34s, primarily worker compilation.
- **26 Chromium layout cases passed** (4.06s): sizing, narrow panes, galleries, accessibility, failures/retry, and cache reuse.
- **7 built-app E2E tests passed** (47.90s): canonical saved-media metadata/decode/remount, both upload-to-history event orderings with measured dimensions, themes, and reduced motion. Production UI build passed in this lane.
- Core/UI typechecks, focused lint/stylelint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects. PR CI supplies broad coverage; network timing was controlled rather than a live throughput benchmark.

- PR CI found a stale inline-image integration expectation. Reproduced it, updated the exact expected image geometry, and passed the selected failure plus the text-only upload sibling (2 tests, 42.98s); focused lint, format, and size ratchets passed. No UI behavior changed in this follow-up.

title: fix(ui): steering messages jump above setup-held requests

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

User impact: the original request stays before its steer throughout setup, acknowledgment, and transcript persistence. No changes to steering delivery, queue execution, or saved transcript order.

The initial request can still be held as a pending input when the UI already displays the optimistic steer. Anchor that pending request using the steer’s explicit target, and keep the same relationship when the original request is persisted. This avoids sorting by potentially skewed browser/server clocks. The shared insertion routine moves into a focused sibling module to stay within the existing source line cap.

title: fix: prevent false failure warnings after reply retries
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: users receive a response-failure warning after a final reply was already delivered, when a provider retry returns an empty response.

## User Impact

User impact: a confirmed final reply stays complete across retries without a duplicate send or misleading failure warning. Progress-only, failed, partial, ambiguous, dry-run, and other-destination sends still require a response; a newly accepted steered input needs its own answer. The retry loop now projects the existing reply owner's current-source completion into each attempt before normalization and terminal resolution. It does not treat arbitrary tool side effects as completion or alter replay-safety decisions.

## User Impact

User impact: fallback wait indicators show the current parent idle interval from its recorded lifecycle boundary, including after reload, rather than counting from 1970. The separate total-request timer and single-status layout are preserved. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already persists the parent’s run-end time. The UI incorrectly made that fact depend on finding an explicit yield in the loaded transcript, then substituted zero when it could not. A resumed parent may legitimately finish normally while an earlier child remains active.

The wait producer now requires a valid persisted parent end; transcript discovery affects placement only. Child activity without a completed parent turn does not invent a handoff. This is the current idle segment—not the child’s runtime or the original request total.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Gateway and Chromium: native visible child spawn, yield, parent update with real `already_pending`, normal final, reload, child completion, and automatic parent resume. Only model responses are scripted over loopback; no mocked Gateway/RPC, injected session rows, or WebSocket interception. This is not external-provider inference proof.
- The same strict regression reproduced `startMs=0` and a 20,738-day timer on the coordinated-layout baseline, then passed on the candidate (17.5-second scenario). The current-idle clock retained the same persisted timestamp after reload; all wait indicators disappeared after settlement.
- SQLite lifecycle → resident session projection → UI regression covers empty loaded history, later parent turns, and cold database reopen. This is not a complete Gateway restart test.
- 117 focused unit/integration tests passed on the coordinated layout; 49 lifecycle, wait, and request-lineage tests passed again after reconciling onto the merged layout. The clock producer, renderer, and live-test source hashes are unchanged from the live proof.
- `pnpm build ciArtifacts`, production UI/chat/chat-E2E typecheck graphs, targeted type-aware lint, and formatting passed. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects.
- CI follow-up: all 190 affected inventory/ownership checks pass after registering the new real-Gateway fixture in the independent expectations. Exact membership and serial ownership assertions remain enforced; no production behavior changed.

- Existing wait-lifecycle browser fixture: reproduced the back-navigation timeout, then supplied its missing persisted parent `endedAt`. All existing hydration, token, single-status, settlement, and resume assertions now pass (14.3 seconds test time; 43.1 seconds including bundle/setup). No runtime change or weakened assertion; focused P0–P2 review and lint/format pass.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38327096689) completed on `ec4de6cc`: 50 successful, 22 skipped, two failed UI shards plus their failed aggregate. The remaining failures are inherited: sidebar weight 600 versus the stale 500 equality assertion (main change `01b7ffe`), and three cloud-startup assertions with exact matching signatures on [ancestral main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38322669274/job/115054341573). All selected failing inputs are unchanged between the actual tested main parent and PR merge. Cloud assertions were independently fixed on main in `bac32528c` (#170436). The PR-caused inventory and missing lifecycle fixture fields are repaired; security-fast passed. Landing requires native inherited-failure admission; this is not green CI or a waiver of security/reviews.

title: improve(cron): stop treating task blocker reports as execution failures
body:
Related: #161698, #165811. This removes the failure-marker protocol; it does not add a general unattended-preamble opt-out.

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled agents can turn ordinary task-blocker reports into execution failures by emitting `AUTOMATION_FAILED`, causing failure accounting and exposing a protocol marker in persistent conversation transcripts.

## User Impact

Automation replies explain blockers in ordinary prose instead of using a magic failure prefix. Real runtime errors, cancellation, delivery failures, and intentional `NO_REPLY` silence retain their existing handling.

**Intentional behavior change:** a normally completed model turn does not become a scheduler failure merely because its answer says the task could not be completed. Such reports no longer trigger failure backoff, alerts, or owner-repair requests. One-shot jobs can complete and be deleted under their normal completion policy even when their answer describes a task-level blocker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the marker prompt, parser, parent/child outcome plumbing, and marker-specific scheduler exception together. Keep execution status owned by structured runtime results rather than assistant prose. Current documentation and the existing QA scenario now describe and exercise that distinction; historical release notes and transcripts are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the removal, three targeted regressions failed for the expected reasons: the marker changed the parent run status and stripped child output in announce and no-delivery paths.
- After the removal, 123 focused tests passed across six files, covering parent/child output, delivery, runtime failures, scheduler policy, and silent replies (67.3s command wall time).
- All typecheck lanes passed, including core/UI tests, extensions, scripts, and root tests. Changed-file lint and formatting passed.
- Independent P0–P2 review: no actionable findings.
- A subsequent full local build was interrupted before a verifiable completion receipt; it is not counted as passing proof. Exact-head hosted CI supplies the enforced broad validation.
- Full changed-check did not pass: the production dead-export scan reported three unchanged baseline exports (`hasActiveDeliveryOwner` re-export, `listOpenClawStateFeatureSchemas`, `OpenClawStateFeatureSchema`). Those findings are tracked separately, not suppressed here.
- End-to-end QA could not start because the CLI artifact-publication guard could not verify the host Gateway service environment. No live Gateway was stopped, modified, or bypassed. QA YAML parsing and all 41 embedded expressions passed static validation. Hosted PR CI remains the broad execution gate.

### Refreshed head and validation

Head `1d86338487e5eaa5bb433ef04eb47cf33a2ec5a7` integrates the upstream fixes for both failing fixtures: cron profile preparation (`50f5be4b2520`) and cold identity config bootstrap (`a1cb052ee61c`). The protocol-removal delta remains unchanged. All **137 focused tests in seven files passed** on the integrated candidate (153.80s wrapper wall), including all 14 cron visibility cases. Type-aware lint and formatting passed. The cold identity test could not start locally because the artifact guard could not verify separation from managed Gateway artifacts; no bypass was used. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38353189278) completed successfully: all 82 jobs terminal, no failures, including the repaired cold-process workload and QA smoke profiles.

[CI run 38314802432, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38314802432) completed with 80 terminal jobs. Two workloads failed; all other selected jobs, including `security-fast` and all QA smoke profiles, passed. **CI remains failed, not green.**

title: fix: steered sessions fail to resume after restart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes conversations being permanently marked failed after a Gateway restart when another session had steered the active human-started turn.

## User Impact

Interrupted conversations can resume without requiring a replacement session merely because a steering update was the latest transcript input. Authorization, revocation, delivery, and replay-safety checks remain unchanged. This does not automatically reopen sessions already marked failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Steering updates are context inside the active turn, not a new owner of that turn. Recovery now preserves a retained, source-keyed human Control UI or channel claim instead of classifying the whole turn from its latest transcript entry. Unscoped and internal delegated inputs still fail closed.

## Evidence

- The new human-turn steering regression failed on the original code and passes with the fix.
- Complete recovery-owner suite: **152/152 passed** (180.18 seconds wall time; 174.58 seconds Vitest). After behavior-neutral cleanup, all eight selected recovery/refusal cases passed again.
- Production and agent-session test typechecks, typed lint, formatting, and source line-growth checks passed.
- Independent P0–P2 review and source-aware authority review found no actionable defects.
- Exact-head [CI run 38309902518](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38309902518) is green. An additional **37 authority/currentness tests passed**.

### Isolated live Gateway proof

On this head, an actual compiled Gateway received authenticated public RPCs and a real `sessions_send(mode: "steer")` tool invocation, persisted the original human claim and steering update, then was killed and replaced by a new process on the same SQLite database. Model I/O used a deterministic local HTTP/SSE fixture—not live inference.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Authorized steered human turn | Recovered to `done`, exactly one final reply, and file effects exactly `before\nafter\n`. |
| Original device revoked after recovery admission | Public `device.token.revoke` caused an error/killed outcome; zero final replies or after-effects and no bypass retry. |
| Delegated input without a retained human claim | Durable delegated-authority refusal, zero recovery provider requests, and no after-effects. |

All six Gateway processes and the owned container were confirmed absent afterward; no operator service/state was changed. Production source SHA-256: `63889225b7d642ecf82d70e97e9e8b283bf46d9464fc30bea528ad1243a92bea`.

**Fixture limitation:** the live suite exited 1 (**2 passed, 1 failed**). After the delegated-denial and zero-effect assertions passed, its final notice assertion incorrectly expected an internal reason in `chat.history`. The captured response correctly contained the public replacement-session notice. That one expectation was corrected and checked against the recorded response; the corrected full case was not rerun. This is not reported as a three-test green suite. Cold build: 20m32s; live cases: 93.5s. The temporary proof fixture is not part of the product patch.
