title: fix(doctor): avoid nested-effect failures during chat update cleanup
body:
Closes #168750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor failing near the end of a chat-requested update with `Database maintenance authority check cannot admit a nested effect` when post-repair cleanup rechecks the requester against a retained shared-state handle.

## User Impact

Chat-requested updates can finish Doctor cleanup without this false authority failure. Actual requester revocation still refuses writes. This changes no schema, stored data, permissions, backup/rollback policy, or required user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor leaves its checks callback before runtime cleanup and SQLite post-repair work. Those steps must re-enter the existing maintenance scope before reading requester policy; after that scope drains, they use the still-held native owner. The nested-effect guard, resource settlement, and ownership-release ordering remain unchanged.

Requested and co-authored by @hannesrudolph.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @hannesrudolph](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3abc66a7-06c4-4d00-b4dc-937336161981)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/572399a9-61d2-41fb-8949-03f1a88d4302)

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `84ce5954d111`: the real Doctor maintenance/requester flow, its final startup-history repair, and post-scope runtime cleanup fail with the reported `Object.assertAdmission <- observeOpenClawDatabaseMaintenanceResource` trace for both configured-owner and linked-profile requesters. Without a retained writer, the same path instead falsely refuses offline-maintenance access.
- The extended regression passes with this fix, retaining config promotion, replacement refusal, and requester-revocation checks. Its warm-reader launch budget remains asserted before deliberately draining those readers.
- Focused Doctor/requester, continuation-scope, nested-effect guard, SQLite reclamation interruption, and NOCOW proof passed (34 tests across five files; 71.86 s wall time). The reclamation process proof verifies settled writes and integrity before SIGTERM exit, unrelated database byte preservation, and replacement ownership acquisition.
- Targeted lint and formatting, core and core-test typechecks, and independent AutoReview (P0/P1) passed. Standalone changed-file command `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-maintenance.requester-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed in 29.78 s wall time; CI ran that file in 25.19 s (17.54 s test execution). This extends the existing native-storage/config boundary fixture rather than adding another product boot. [Exact-head CI, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38289347340) passed for `5285a16ae749eb51031c9c42e227167a158cf553`.
- [Published-driver × candidate run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38289295507): the installed `2026.9.5` updater returned `status: ok` after installing build `2026.10.2-5285a16ae749`; activation Doctor exited 0 in 71.243 s, and all three captured delegated Doctor results were `ok`/exit 0. Installed-package identity, automatic migration, and the unavailable-plugin-path configuration-byte preservation checks passed. Frozen artifact admission binds candidate `5285a16ae749eb51031c9c42e227167a158cf553` to package SHA-256 `a4bb626a658d888cd1345c2753015624473e3a3242126f52791b159eb52890dd`; workflow tooling was independently pinned to `e163d81940e34518eac3ce7d52338a38a1fc640c`.
- **The overall package-acceptance run is red:** its later, separate standalone Doctor invocation failed during Codex plugin registration with `Runtime config is not prepared`. That registration occurs inside the checks callback, before the post-repair helper changed here; this PR changes no plugin/config registration code. The targeted update and activation-Doctor results above passed, but the subsequent full preservation/readiness assertions were not reached. This separate plugin-registration defect is not included in this two-file repair; no claim of an all-green end-to-end acceptance run is made.
- Hosted package build, package integrity, and npm 12 installer acceptance passed. The local full build exceeded its 20-minute tool budget while compiling package declarations and is not counted as a successful local build. No live Gateway or operator state was changed.

This regression proves the production Doctor boundary using isolated synthetic state, not the original reporter’s multi-gigabyte dataset or a real systemd/launchd handoff.

title: fix: open command palette with familiar editor shortcuts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: familiar editor shortcuts do not open the command palette in the Control UI.

## User Impact

Users can open the palette with **Cmd+P / Cmd+Shift+P** on Apple platforms and **Ctrl+P / Ctrl+Shift+P** elsewhere, including while typing or using embedded widgets. The existing Cmd/Ctrl+K shortcut and displayed hint remain unchanged. No migration or configuration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

VS Code uses Cmd/Ctrl+P for Quick Open and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P for its command palette; as requested, both chords open OpenClaw’s existing command palette. The aliases share the existing platform-aware shortcut matcher and palette owners, including the cold-loading path and sandbox widget forwarding. Existing modifier, composition, native Mac Control-editing, focus restoration, and widget trust checks remain intact. P chords intentionally replace browser printing inside OpenClaw. F1 remains available for browser help; this small change does not expand the generic matcher to function keys.

Requested by and co-authored with @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/82dd558a-6243-431a-ad08-a9c57401ec12)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/b39338b1)

## Editor shortcut survey

Ten popular editors/IDEs with a built-in command palette or equivalent action search are compared below. This is a cross-editor comparison, not a measured top-ten market-share ranking. Defaults checked on 2026-10-12; custom keymaps and OS/browser interception can change them. “Find Action” and “Feature Search” are explicitly labeled equivalents, not products calling their UI a command palette.

| Editor / IDE | Palette or equivalent command | macOS default | Windows / Linux default | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visual Studio Code | Show All Commands / Command Palette | `Cmd+Shift+P` or `F1` | `Ctrl+Shift+P` or `F1` | [Default keybindings](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/reference/default-keybindings) |
| Visual Studio | Feature Search (command/action search) | Not applicable: current Visual Studio is Windows-only | Windows: `Ctrl+Shift+P` or `Ctrl+Q`; Linux: not available | [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/ide/visual-studio-search?view=visualstudio) |
| IntelliJ IDEA | Find Action | `Cmd+Shift+A` | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | [Keymap / action search](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/mastering-keyboard-shortcuts.html) |
| PyCharm | Find Action | `Cmd+Shift+A` | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | [PyCharm shortcuts](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/pycharm/mastering-keyboard-shortcuts.html) |
| Android Studio | Find Action | `Cmd+Shift+A` | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | [Android Studio default keymaps](https://developer.android.com/studio/intro/keyboard-shortcuts) |
| WebStorm | Find Action | `Cmd+Shift+A` | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | [WebStorm shortcuts](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/webstorm/mastering-keyboard-shortcuts.html) |
| Cursor | Command Palette | `Cmd+Shift+P` | `Ctrl+Shift+P` | [Cursor shortcuts](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts), which reference VS Code as the baseline |
| Sublime Text | Command Palette | `Cmd+Shift+P` | `Ctrl+Shift+P` | Community-maintained Sublime documentation: [macOS](https://docs.sublimetext.io/reference/keyboard_shortcuts_osx.html), [palette](https://docs.sublimetext.io/guide/extensibility/command_palette.html) |
| Zed | Command Palette | `Cmd+Shift+P` | `Ctrl+Shift+P` | [Zed getting started](https://zed.dev/docs/), [palette](https://zed.dev/docs/command-palette) |
| RStudio | Show Command Palette | `Cmd+Shift+P` | `Ctrl+Shift+P` | [RStudio palette](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/ui/command-palette.html), [shortcut reference](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/reference/shortcuts.html) |

JetBrains also documents both platform variants together in its [Find Action guide](https://www.jetbrains.com/guide/tips/find-action/). Double `Shift` opens the broader Search Everywhere UI in JetBrains IDEs; it is not the direct Find Action shortcut. RStudio's shortcut reference additionally lists `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P` for Firefox on Windows/Linux.

**What this means for this PR:** `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` is the dominant direct palette shortcut in this comparison. The other important family is JetBrains' `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A`; Visual Studio additionally uses `Ctrl+Q`, and VS Code supports `F1`. These additional bindings are research findings, not implemented aliases in this PR. Browser conflicts need evaluation before adding them.

`Cmd/Ctrl+P` is Quick Open / Go to File in VS Code and Zed (and code search in Visual Studio), not their direct command-palette shortcut. OpenClaw deliberately accepts it as the originally requested convenience alias, alongside `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` and the existing `Cmd/Ctrl+K`. This survey update changes the PR description only; it does not change the tested commit.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced on baseline `ba3ee866cabf`: all four P combinations failed at the browser-default-prevention assertion. After the fix, all four pass through the production-built Control UI with a mocked Gateway, covering cold launch, cancellation during loading, warm launch/close, and draft/focus preservation. Chromium runs on Linux with Apple and Linux platform/modifier cases; this is not native macOS testing.
- Focused browser run: **5 tests passed**, including the existing authenticated-widget isolation scenario extended to K, P, and Shift+P. **28.42 s** Vitest / **30.42 s** command wall time; shortcut file **4.72 s**, widget file **9.04 s**. The widget scenario proves the real frame/trusted-input boundary, not just a matcher stub.
- `pnpm test ui/src/components/command-palette-shortcuts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **6 tests passed**, **5.07 s** Vitest / **12.66 s** command wall time. Covers non-Latin physical keys, wrong/both/Alt modifiers, dead keys, and IME composition. Existing keyboard catalog and serialized-matcher tests also passed.
- **Full `pnpm build` passed** (309.64 s command wall time); production UI build and asset-size checks passed. Focused lint, stylelint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Core/UI typechecks and all selected test-type graphs passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` did **not** finish green: its broad dead-export scan reports the pre-existing `DurableDirectoryReceipt` export in untouched `src/infra/directory-durability.ts`. All preceding checks passed. Remaining relevant lint/stylelint checks were run directly and passed; no baseline exception or unrelated source change was made.
- Independent precommit code review: **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. This is AI code review, not hosted human approval. Hosted CI timings/status will be available on this PR.

**Landing status (2026-10-12):** original-head [CI run 38260961862](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38260961862) failed in `view.identity-avatar.test.tsx` (two global fetch calls); the hosted log did not identify those URLs, so its exact cause remains unproven. Commit `e78a4d873888` repairs a deterministically reproduced fixture defect: unrelated non-data requests were counted as avatar fetches and received PNG responses. The fixture now routes only same-origin `/avatar/beta` requests to the avatar spy and delegates others. An independent asset request fails with the old fixture and passes after repair; a deliberate duplicate-beta-avatar negative control still fails, preserving duplicate detection. Exact avatar URL, bearer-auth, single-blob, revision, and decode assertions remain. Focused Node tests passed (4 tests, 2.23s Vitest / 4.39s wall); Bun avatar/profile fixtures passed (11 tests, 1.93s Vitest / 4.20s wall). Targeted lint/types and a fresh independent P0–P2 review passed. All three current-head UI shards and all three UI E2E shards passed in CI run 38269364757, along with security-fast. Its only root failure is `check-lint-core-1`: an unnecessary `<void>` argument in untouched `src/gateway/server-methods/users-github.test.ts:679`. The test, deferred helper, and lint configuration blobs are identical between the recorded CI base `f0818acb96e7` and tested merge `3165491cad02`; targeted lint on main reproduces the same diagnostic. The scheduled-main classifier calls it new because that comparison used an older main, but direct source/reproduction evidence establishes it as inherited. Merged into `main` on **2026-10-12 at 15:56:06 UTC** as [`a010ee5721f14`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54) through native exact-head inherited-failure admission. The CI aggregate remains red, not relabeled as successful. Main ancestry, the nine-file scope, unchanged reviewed production source, landing-parent audit, and Jacob’s required co-author trailer were verified. Original palette build/browser evidence remains applicable because production code is unchanged.

Behavior-only change: no rendered layout/copy/hint changes, so browser assertions are the primary evidence rather than before/after screenshots.

People entering a credential through the secrets tool cannot check what they typed without re-entering it.

## User Impact

Users can show or hide the value with an eye button in the secure-entry prompt, both in chat and on its standalone /ask page. Values stay masked by default, and showing a value does not expose it to the agent or transcript. No migration or configuration changes.

The shared question field owns the local visibility toggle. It preserves the typed value, disables the toggle with the input, and resets visibility for a new question or request. title: fix: prevent thinking-only replies from utility models
body:
Related: #153391. Follow-up to #169331.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes empty utility results when a local reasoning model spends its short output allowance entirely on thinking.

## User Impact

Titles, observer digests, progress narration, activity recaps, and transcript summaries request thinking off without changing ordinary chat reasoning, task timeouts, or unrelated model settings. No configuration changes or migration are required. Models that cannot disable reasoning still use their provider's supported minimum and can still exhaust a short budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous reasoning reserve increased output allowances but did not turn thinking off. Utility preparation and the title/transcript callers now select off explicitly; the isolated owner does not add a reasoning reserve for off requests. The final one-shot payload hook keeps configured Ollama and OpenAI-compatible boolean thinking switches from re-enabling it, preserving other payload fields and native provider effort mappings.

## Evidence

- Real title-generation/request assembly against loopback HTTP fixtures passes for native Ollama and OpenAI-compatible transport. Captures verify native think:false, nested and top-level enable_thinking:false, preserved template/sampling/context settings, and unchanged ordinary enabled reasoning. These are wire-contract tests; a live qwen3.6:35b generation was not run.
- Focused utility, isolated-budget, prepared-completion, ordinary embedded parameter, and transcript tests: 92 passed in 52.49s wall time. Final observer/recap/narration/shutdown caller suites: 62 passed in 96.18s. The title transport file: 20 passed, 40.11s test-run duration (native plugin activation and the existing persistence scenarios account for most time).
- Changed owner files through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`: isolated budget 7/7 (10.32s wall); prepared completion 21/21 (9.56s wall).
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. Subsequent mechanical typed-fixture updates carry the new required thinking-off field.

title: refactor(update): simplify cleanup reporting

Simplifies the earlier Git-update cleanup fix so a history-reporting error does not need a new exception class and downstream unwrapping to preserve the original failure.

## User Impact

Ordinary cleanup-reporting failures remain visible as sanitized stderr and cleanup-step warnings, while the original exception keeps its identity and recovery classification. Actual cleanup failures still preserve both errors and block unsafe recovery; nested pending recovery stays closed.

When the update throws instead of returning a result, stderr is the fallback visibility path. This does not fix the original production maintenance collision or prove full managed-service recovery.

Use the existing cleanup and outcome owners instead of a reporting-specific wrapper class, cross-layer callback/list and generic settlement helper. The remaining downstream change preserves pending recovery inside a real cleanup-failure aggregate, not reporting-only unwrapping.

title: fix(update): preserve failures when cleanup reporting is unavailable
body:

Fixes Git updates losing their original failure and skipping temporary-worktree cleanup when cleanup progress cannot be written to update history.

## User Impact

Cleanup still runs when its progress ledger is unavailable. Operators retain the original failure and secondary diagnostics instead of a misleading cleanup-only failure. Reporting alone does not invalidate a successful update or a known pre-mutation recovery classification; uncertain process cleanup still blocks recovery.

This repairs the installed updater's error handling. It cannot patch an older updater already running, and it does not establish the cause of the reported production maintenance collision or prove full macOS service recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record cleanup reporting failures separately from cleanup execution, preserve both failures during unwind, and keep the original admission/revocation classification only for reporting-only aggregation. Existing process-settlement and recovery guards remain active.

## What Problem This Solves

Experimental chat bubbles obscured commentary and tool progress, and repeated square corners did not point to the speaker's identity.

## User Impact

Speech bubbles are now off by default behind **Settings → Labs → Speech bubbles**. Enabling **gateway.controlUi.experimental.chatBubbles** makes Home use bubbles by default; explicit per-session on/off choices remain browser-local and survive disabling/re-enabling the lab. Config changes hot-apply without a Gateway restart.

Only the first message points toward the existing avatar, later bubbles stay rounded, and groups have more breathing room. Commentary remains visible while compact labeled tool disclosures expose the existing cards and output. Ordinary live work retains one dots indicator; startup, approval, and child-wait states keep their explicit controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep conversational output readable without disguising completed tools as typing. Reuse the current Labs/config/bootstrap and UI preference owners rather than adding a separate feature state store. title: feat: opt in to human creators for delegated work
body:
## What Problem This Solves

People need an opt-in way to retain their creator identity on new work delegated to an agent, without changing who executes it or weakening its isolation.

## User Impact

**Off by default:** Settings → Labs → **Human creator attribution** controls `agents.defaults.experimental.delegatedCreatorAttribution`. Enabling it attributes new delegated sessions, subagents, realtime/meeting consults and agent-created cron jobs to the verified human requester, or a retained causal task creator. Off/omitted retains each creation path’s pre-feature attribution behavior. Direct human creation is unchanged.

The setting applies **without a Gateway restart** to subsequent creations. Already-admitted operations keep their captured config; existing sessions/jobs and scheduled runs are not restamped. Execution agent, live requester checks, private isolation identity, required-sandbox restrictions and assignment remain independent. Reassignment does not transfer creator/admin archive or public-publishing authority.

**Public links remain explicitly opt-in and anonymous/read-only.** No auto-publication, URL change or private isolation disclosure.

**Downgrade is NOT cleared by this switch.** Turning it off does not undo stored attribution or private isolation/ACP metadata. Pre-PR binaries reject the unknown config and can misinterpret same-schema feature-written state; schema equality is not sufficient proof. Transparent retained-state downgrade to an unmodified incompatible binary remains unqualified. Restoring a pre-upgrade backup discards post-backup work and is not a substitute for the requested downgrade. The proposed non-lossy guard uses the existing shared/agent database admission owner to refuse incompatible activation while retaining current state; a semantic schema-floor change requires accepted design, and running an older generation with these rows requires a compatible backport. Neither is implemented or certified here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing creator selector consumes the explicit-true Labs setting at native, visible Gateway, ACP, cron and consult creation owners. This reuses the config schema, Labs registry and hot-reload owner—no toggle framework, restart hook, table/version or historical backfill. Consult-created task causality also survives follow-on delegation.

Private immutable `sandboxProvenance` continues to carry the pre-feature execution identity separately from the public creator. ACP rollover retains `spawnedByAgentId` for cleanup. Public projections strip private fields; permissions, routing, quotas, model accounts and runtime agent identity are not gated by the Lab.

## Evidence

**Current candidate:** `71b0bfb7d41cdfa01fc7dea1532d84065ebe6a62`, tree `343b21fc6463871282515792910dadd829a5155d`. This head integrates pinned main `8197f6f8cf48` to resolve actual GitHub conflicts, preserves the new memory-only session owner, and corrects enabled autonomous voice-consult attribution. Current-head broad CI passed as recorded below; older reviews do not certify this head.

Both CI-gate surfaces, dependency review and security-sensitive review are successful. The full exact-head check inventory at20:49 contains149checks (100success,48skipped,1neutral), none failing/pending. The failure-classification reporter timed out its optional comparison, but the complete CI inventory contains no failures to classify. This clears current CI, not the separate retained-state downgrade/latest-stable compatibility gaps. **Current-head ClawSweeper revision21** reviewed this exact head at21:08:16.555UTC on October13 (source revision ba13bd14a61e07240919df082947d6704eb08b2dd8bee63b4cc348cd93b0d699): zero actionable code findings, previous cron blocker resolved, real behavior and screenshot proof sufficient. The durable verdict remains **needs-human / hold=blocked**, not approval: two before-merge items remain—accept the non-lossy schema-admission-floor/backport compatibility design and qualify latest-stable upgrade plus actual retained-state historical activation or refusal. The accepted re-review receiver38467384069 and terminal-finalization38468522830 both completed successfully; neither green CI nor successful review execution settles those compatibility boundaries.

- **Reviewed main-conflict integration and voice correction:** the retired incognito projection files stay removed; complete memory-owned entries carry private provenance through the existing immutable installer and public projection. Independent read-only cutover review found no likely P0/P1/P2 regression. The two fixtures now preserve the complete isolated environment; no production fallback, security guard or schema was changed. Minimal non-lossy protection would use shared and agent schema admission floors while preserving row bytes; it must prove the deferred shared-schema marker cannot be dropped while incompatible rows remain. title: fix(acp): bound sessions lose replies and streamed text
body:
Related: #146365

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ACP-bound conversations failing to select a configured reply runtime and Telegram previews replacing earlier answer chunks.

## User Impact

New raw-harness ACP sessions remain owned by the requesting OpenClaw agent. Existing bound harness sessions retain their original storage and transcripts while dispatching through the inspected channel owner. Telegram keeps incremental answer text visible without concatenating separate final replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep configured ownership separate from the external harness namespace. Preserve participant recording instead of hiding foreign-key failures by disabling it. Mark disjoint ACP text chunks explicitly; ordinary snapshots and final replies remain replacements, including text rewritten in place by delivery hooks. Existing metadata migration/read behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Focused regressions pass: 57 ACP dispatch/cancellation tests, 31 Telegram HTTP delivery tests, and 9 owner/reopen/prefix tests. The prefix regression failed in both partial and block modes before the repair; the old CI cancellation failure was the exact added delta field, now covered without weakening settlement/transcript assertions.
- Live Telegram Test Server + real ACPX process: a native `/acp spawn proof-harness --bind here` creates a main-owned session; the next user message reaches a deterministic ACP protocol peer. The same Telegram message changes from the first chunk to both chunks with one configured `[proof]` prefix. The late session-status notice is a separate message rather than overwriting the answer. This exercises the changed paths, not a normal mock-provider reply; no paid model was used.
- Legacy bound-owner tests preserve the original harness store and transcript, reopen the persisted session with a fresh manager, and reject bindings removed or reassigned after configured runtime selection before any harness prompt executes. No database schema, serializer, or metadata migration changes are introduced; this is not a claim of a full released-package upgrade test.
- Live forbidden-sender control: after the allowed user spawned and bound the ACP session, removing that sender from the Telegram allowlist caused the next real Telegram message to be rejected with zero harness prompt calls. Both live runs released their leases, removed credential scratch, and left no test listeners. An earlier reply-matcher fixture error and restart-interrupted attempts are not counted as passing proof.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the repair delta is clean. Full staged static validation passed (732.3s), including core/extension types, lint, SDK surface, declarations, and architecture/auth guards. The one generic preview helper is accounted for explicitly in the SDK display-surface budget; no permission or persistence capability is widened.
- Current-main conflict refresh was required only by the additive SDK surface-budget edits. Preserved both sets of exports; no hand-resolved runtime changes. The refreshed composition passed all 97 focused tests (174.5s grouped wall), the SDK shipped-surface/removal guard, and formatting. Prior static/live evidence remains scoped to the unchanged repair contracts.
- Timing: ACP dispatch/cancellation suite 8.34s; final Telegram HTTP suite 79.08s; owner/reopen suite 29.98s; prefix metadata suite 1.17s. The original failed CI cancellation file took 9.31s and is fixed, not waived. Current-head CI will run on publication.

title: feat: add per-session speech bubbles and prompt reactions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users need a conversational chat layout without losing streamed replies or access to detailed agent activity, and agents need a way to acknowledge WebChat prompts with reactions.

## User Impact

Session menu → **View → Speech bubbles** selects the mode independently for each conversation, including the main session. Replies still stream; compact **…** previews expand to reveal tool, reasoning, and live-status details. The preference stays in this browser.

Agents can react to the current committed prompt, including queued and consumed steering inputs. Reactions remain agent-attributed and local to WebChat; existing external-channel reactions and send-only recovery tools retain their boundaries. No database schema or config migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The presentation reuses the existing transcript and disclosure owners. Prompt reactions reuse the existing reaction store and events, with the authenticated prompt source kept separate from execution and dashboard-read authority. Retained tools revalidate the current run, source, session generation, and prompt binding at the write boundary.

## Evidence

- **Authenticated source custody:** six composition cases run the real direct-chat admission and dashboard source owner through native recorder custody, queued adoption or consumed steering, the actual message tool, and the durable reaction store. Allowed writes publish one event. Credential revocation at SQLite commit rejects with the source-authority error and no changed row/event. Required membership removal during preparation also rejects without changing existing human reactions.
- **SQLite ordering:** membership removal is committed before the reaction worker obtains its write transaction; revoking membership synchronously while that same database holds `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` would contend with the tested writer. The tests do not replace membership with a synthetic flag. Credential invalidation is explicitly exercised at the commit checkpoint.
- **Refreshed candidate:** 52 focused tests pass across chat admission/reactions, transcript persistence, and the originally failing chat-auth-readiness entry point. The six new cases are included in the 20-case admission suite; the separate reaction suite has 14 passing cases.
- **Existing-data compatibility:** browser tests load a pre-bubble v1 preference record using fields written by `v2026.10.1`, enable bubbles, then save/reopen without losing those preferences. Existing human reaction rows survive successful agent add/remove and rejected additions. The feature changes no database schema/version or existing reaction kernel/types; this is persisted-contract preservation proof, not a full old-package installation upgrade.
- **Follow-up checks:** the gateway and UI test type graphs, changed-file ratchets, format, localization, coercion/deprecation guards, and scoped lint pass. Script, production and full-tree unused-export scans report zero entries on the refreshed base. Nine browser preference cases pass.
- **Prior feature verification:** UI unit suites and 9 mocked-Gateway browser tests passed for session independence, reload, mobile controls, streaming and details expansion. Full build, UI build, core/UI types, localization, stylelint and scoped lint passed on the original feature tree. The test-only proof additions also passed independent review through P2.

title: improve(ui): put everyday session actions first
body:
Related: #132846. Follow-up to #162316; this does not change pane-toggle semantics or trigger naming.

## What Problem This Solves

Everyday session actions compete with advanced controls, while common link copying and owner assignment take unnecessary submenu navigation.

## User Impact

Copy a session link in one click, assign an owner from the root menu, and find less-frequent actions together under **Advanced**. Assignment is hidden when there is only one eligible person or agent. Existing permissions, confirmations, batch actions, and host-specific availability stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared menu now puts pinning, renaming, read state, Copy link, assignment, grouping, snoozing, and archiving first. Advanced replaces Session settings and contains appearance, forking, other copy formats, opening destinations, direct send/receive preferences, and Delete. Personal Hide/Show is prominent only in an Involving me list. Parents have one Archive entry with session-only or confirmed session-and-children choices.

The existing assignment directory supplies distinct typed human/agent choices, retains explicit owners during loading/errors, coalesces pending loads, and discards previous-connection results. Phone submenus replace the menu page; Back returns to the actual parent. The existing picker owns its extracted appearance state so the shared action owner stays under its line cap.

## Evidence

**Current-head result:** CI [38084700218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38084700218) on `9b30ed2e3327260dede1cb670767fad02c326625` completed successfully (65 jobs terminal, no failures). Production UI and component-test typechecks, lint, formatting, and line-cap checks pass. Current-head CI is tracked separately; the failed/cancelled first attempt is not passing coverage.

title: refactor(cron): separate conversation results from notifications
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation results mix conversation history ownership with external notification routing, leaving overlapping completion and mirroring paths.

## User Impact

Agent, command, and script jobs created from a conversation commit their final visible result there before sending any required external notification. Changing the notification destination does not redirect the model transcript or implicitly copy the result into Home. Execution/tool history stays with the run. Existing jobs without a captured conversation retain external-only delivery.

Reset/deleted conversations fail visibly. Cancellation, generation checks, deduplication, channel transforms, media/TTS, and uncertain-send no-replay behavior remain enforced. No live jobs, schedules, configuration, or history were changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one conversation-result owner and one durable notification sender, remove duplicate awareness/mirror paths, and pass serializable prepared commands to the store worker instead of exchanging private transaction callbacks.

**Size:** 1,659 production lines added / 2,602 removed: **943 net production lines removed**. Tests/fixtures are +47 net and docs are −10; total patch is −906 lines. This does **not** meet the requested thousands-of-production-lines target. Further deletion was not justified without redesigning execution/continuation ownership or weakening existing guarantees.

Requested by Ayaan.

## Evidence

- Final focused run: **222 tests passed** across cron RPC validation (133), script/command completion ordering (18), and agent delivery/no-double-send behavior (71). Ran pnpm test with the three affected files and --maxWorkers=1; aggregate wall time 131.22s. Individual suite durations: 31.11s / 87.81s / 9.58s. Hosted CI seconds are not available yet.
- Worker admission/recovery repairs: 34 tests passed. Final conversation/receipt boundary checks: 18 passed. Additional scheduler, receipt, delivery, and lifecycle coverage was run while integrating; failed intermediate fixtures were repaired and rechecked.
- Full build passed. Core production types, cron/Gateway test type shards, root test types, affected-file lint, scripts lint, and structural/import-cycle/auth guards passed. Final post-review edits only fix lint/type declarations; the committed tree matches the verified candidate.
- Independent autoreview found no actionable P0/P1 defects in result ordering, authority, recovery, or uncertain-send handling. This is not a claim of a full live-channel test.

**Known validation limits:** the aggregate changed-file check stops on the inherited UI E2E root budget (722 roots versus 720). Broad core lint also reports pre-existing max-lines violations, and the unused-export audit reports existing exports in untouched files. These limits were not increased or bypassed; mechanical cleanup is deferred per the requester. No live Gateway/channel run or hosted CI result is claimed. title: fix: finish shutdown without disabling V8 compilers
body:
Related: #163788

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes commands hanging after output during forced Node shutdown without retaining the blanket Maglev and concurrent-Sparkplug workaround.

## User Impact

CLI commands and the Gateway finish owned work and cleanup before exiting naturally, with Node's default compiler settings restored. Exit status, Unix signal termination, output, explicit compiler overrides, and system-CA trust are preserved.

The Gateway still joins native skills-watcher retirement. This can retain synchronous FSEvents shutdown latency on macOS; the separate upstream certificate-loader stall is not fixed. Native macOS/Windows qualification is not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing lifecycle owners retain admitted work, native workers, child transports, updater recovery, and watchdogs through actual completion. The boundary guard prevents new forced normal exits. Cleanup dependencies are retained before a command can replace its package, without eagerly importing them into CLI bootstrap. No new configuration, dependency, or schema is introduced.

## Evidence

- Earlier full pnpm build passed on composed tree faaafbe6b1f47e707f8392243898525990f3a452 (the terminal repair plus pinned CI base 97e81ce), including the canonical CLI-bootstrap import gate, in 4m35.7s. The final runtime, one-shot, and cleanup suites passed 40 tests, including red proof of premature watcher loading. Broker regressions: 84 passed; real-process negative controls cover IPC disconnect and Unix signal propagation after output settlement.
- The SIGTERM capture fixture retains its 20-second parent deadline and persistence assertions: red was 99 instead of 143; repaired case passed in 708ms (11.19s wrapper). The latest message/update fixture matrix passed 25/25 (179.52s): synthetic pending resources release only after observed stall diagnostics and join completion; ordered exit listeners remain checked. These later repairs change test/support files only, not production code.
- Latest pinned-main integration preserved QA error reporting without forced exit: 204 QA tests, 10 reconciliation tests, and 6 real service-child relay tests passed. The reconciliation case failed before removing an obsolete admission close. Scoped types, lint, and three-pass review are complete; this integration did not repeat the full application build.
- CI repair qualification: 96 tests across seven files passed (196.15s); final QA integration: 34 tests across three files passed (43.28s). Scoped types, type-aware lint, formatting, and mock-export checking passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 reviews found no actionable issues.

title: feat(openshell): run brokered inference on sandboxed nodes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Run native worker inference behind OpenShell's credential broker without requiring OCE or Kubernetes, with optional canonical agent files shared across its sessions.

## User Impact

Opt-in `openclaw openshell worker create/run/configure` commands provision a dedicated broker-attached sandbox through OpenShell, enroll its ordinary OpenClaw node, and configure the existing paired-device worker-inference profile. Docker and Podman use the same OpenShell gateway/CLI contract; neither engine is managed directly by this plugin. Existing sandbox-only behavior stays unchanged.

Optional `worker.agentWorkspace: { agentId, remoteRoot }` now binds one configured agent to an existing private directory on the paired node through File Transfer. Both Gateway and worker sessions use that canonical document owner; ordinary coding tools still use each session's task workspace. Setup never seeds or synchronizes documents, copies private Gateway state, widens node-command approvals, or overrides an existing File Transfer policy. Prepare the directory/files and review the existing grants before applying the binding.

**Scope and important limits:** one configured model, a qualified operator-supplied Node/OpenClaw image, and a foreground node host. OpenShell v0.1.3+ provider profiles, executable/endpoint policy, egress enforcement, and real provider credentials remain operator-owned. `worker run` owns a **dedicated sandbox** and stops the entire sandbox on exit/cancellation; cleanup failures explicitly report that the remote node may remain active. `configure --required --apply` affects all Gateway sessions and blocks turns when its worker is unavailable. No production deployment, release or production configuration was changed by this task. Assistant-run qualification used no real provider credentials; Sally’s separately reported live test below used her real OpenAI integration.

**Historical standalone Docker E2E passed on October 10**, including broker authorization, revocation, and confirmed remote cancellation. It uses a synthetic OpenAI-compatible HTTPS upstream, not a paid model account. Separately, [Sally's October 15 report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168458#issuecomment-6199208971) records Podman/OpenShell 0.1.4 and real OpenAI fresh-install feature validation at `9131246f6309`; its exercised plugin source matches this head. This is contributor-reported proof, not a new assistant-run test, and explicitly does not establish installed stable-to-candidate preservation.

### Compatibility and operator actions

No breaking change was found in the existing sandbox-only `mirror`/`remote` flow when `worker` is absent: its schema fields/defaults, backend and SSH/mirror paths are preserved; CLI registration launches nothing. This PR adds no core/SDK API, database migration, dependency, or worker-protocol change. **The new worker mode is not a drop-in plugin upgrade for older Gateway/node builds.**

- Released OpenClaw **v2026.10.1** lacks the native-inference stack and `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile`; its strict OpenShell plugin schema also rejects the new `worker` block. Installing this plugin alone does not backport core capabilities. Use matching qualified Gateway/node builds and their supported Node version; generic plugin host/API metadata is not worker-mode qualification.
- For downgrade, finish/stop turns, reconcile pending browser inputs and reclaim native placements on the compatible build first; then remove required/native profiles and `plugins.entries.openshell.config.worker`. Older Gateways do not interpret `settings.inference` as a local-inference requirement. The October 17 cell below proves installed v2026.10.4 core/plugin preservation with boundary-fixtured optional worker configuration; live remote binding after upgrade and cross-version data downgrade remain unqualified.
- **OpenShell v0.1.3+ applies to the new mode only.** Upgrading an older OpenShell deployment has its own breaking migration away from managed inference routes and requires recreating pre-upgrade sandboxes per upstream. This PR does not automatically upgrade OpenShell or migrate those records.
- The workload needs Linux/OpenShell kernel enforcement (including Landlock), a qualified non-root Node/OpenClaw image with Git and POSIX process tools, and an imported provider profile authorizing the actual Node binary and HTTPS endpoint. Native Windows worker inference is unsupported; Docker/Podman selection alone does not establish host capability.
- Initial support is one model using `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`, or `anthropic-messages`, with broker environment placeholders and correct CA trust—not every provider/auth adapter. The runner is foreground and stops the entire dedicated sandbox on exit. `--required --apply` affects all Gateway sessions; unavailable workers block turns. Rotation requires a new node process, and model/state changes are not silently overwritten.

The October 17 installed-upgrade cell establishes v2026.10.4 core/plugin preservation separately from the fresh-install cells. Live post-upgrade agentWorkspace binding and every provider/platform combination remain outside that proof; gaps are not inferred failures. [Setup and rollback guidance](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/openshell-workers#compatibility-and-rollback) records these boundaries; the source-bound historical Docker evidence below remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use existing owners instead of adding another provider or inference protocol:

- OpenShell creates/retains the sandbox with named existing providers and `--no-auto-providers`, then owns attachment readiness through `sandbox provider attach --wait`.
- The remote bootstrap refuses missing/raw model credentials, accepts only OpenShell's injected opaque placeholder, and writes canonical node model config containing an environment reference—not a key. It maps OpenShell's CA file to Node's supported trust setting without disabling certificate verification.
- Pairing uses `connect --target-file` with a private stdin handoff; reconnect uses `node run`. The Gateway profile derives the exact device ID from read-only `node identity --json` inside the selected sandbox, optionally checks an expected ID, preserves unrelated config, and refuses conflicting bindings.
- Core remains the owner of live pairing, admission, device availability, worker-local inference selection, recorded placement snapshots, and rejection of Gateway fallback. No core/SDK runtime changes, new credentials store, or OCE API dependency.

Current OpenShell calls the real provider endpoint, not the retired workspace inference route. API/CLI contracts were inspected at released NVIDIA/OpenShell v0.1.3 (`e1f3c82caa3ed3b65de22889ae7ef32a774878ef`). Placeholder-format checks and provider readiness are not cryptographic custody attestation or upstream model probes; the deployment trust contract remains explicit.

The original default-off worker option adds 15 plugin config fields; the optional agent-workspace binding adds 3 more (18 total over the pinned main base). Canonical config-baseline outputs were regenerated; this growth is intentional, not an unrelated baseline waiver.

## Evidence

### October 17 rebase and v2026.10.4 installed-upgrade receipt

**Installed core-and-plugin preservation passed. Optional worker configuration passed with the external OpenShell identity query fixtured; this is not a live OpenShell/agentWorkspace upgrade qualification.** Earlier failed/interrupted .10.3 attempts below remain historical, not substituted evidence. No merge or auto-merge was performed.

**Exact candidate:** `72d2d262be1691e33030872433988304144fcd7a`, tree `0fd48734bb75170abb97beb47bf598fe5655a6bd`, rebased from `3359c7d0fe3042e3c02a191d71d901f46cae6f3a` onto main `23f8eb5c0e33ed7e4c9cd84a3fbb193cc40548ee`. All production/test blobs and 15/16 nongenerated PR files are unchanged; the remaining documentation blob incorporates main’s canonical ClawHub locator spelling. Later main `0f2545d81d31b77020fa3aa4c7344d672dcc75fc` composed without conflicts.

**Fresh checks:** 123/123 tests in eight files (45.51s wrapper wall), extension production/test types, typed lint on ten files, formatting, config baseline and whitespace passed. Canonical full build/package/integrity verification passed in **295.61s**; the plugin was built separately through the prepublish plugin artifact owner. [Exact-head CI 39038587398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39038587398) succeeded; final readback: **43 successful and 53 skipped check runs**, no pending/failed checks, all three applicable commit-status gates successful, GitHub **MERGEABLE / CLEAN**, OPEN/non-draft. Placeholder paths in this public receipt replace private artifact locations.
- **Result:** updater exit **0**, **411.936s**, durable run `0b65be8c-3037-4b11-9b3f-8ba1db61135f` independently read back **finished/succeeded**. Candidate plugin install exit **0**, **25.382s**; all **8 archive payload files** matched installed bytes and the serving Gateway activated OpenShell. title: feat: organize personal navigation in a compact sidebar rail
body:
Closes #168053

## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar mixes destinations, conversations, and online people, while shared session pins cannot express each person’s preferred shortcuts.

## User Impact

A compact icon rail separates **Pages**, **Sessions**, and **Online**, keeps Home, Inbox, and account controls at the bottom, and supports personal shortcuts for pages, dashboards, conversations, and people. Drag or use menus to pin, reorder, and unpin. Collapsing the list retains the rail; narrow screens retain the drawer.

**Mine** means conversations owned by the current human. **All** means accessible conversations and preserves its saved owner/Involving me filters. Scope controls hide only when authoritative counts and filters prove equivalence. Resolved profileless connections show accessible conversations without overwriting saved Mine; unresolved identities remain private. Pins grant no access and never mutate shared pin/promotion metadata.

Write-capable profiles synchronize shortcuts and scope; read-only/profileless connections retain browser-local choices. Shared navigation imports once from a complete authorized inventory; explicit empty personal pins win. The unchanged 4 KiB value limit rejects oversized imports without blocking appearance hydration. Promotion, tree archive, and scoped Undo remain separate.

**Upgrade recovery:** pending shortcuts saved by v2026.9.9 are migrated using their valid same-profile, pre-upgrade last-seen baseline before hydration. No fresh remote snapshot or invented empty baseline is used. Missing/corrupt baselines retain the local choice, display a recovery notification, and no longer block later appearance saves. Editing a shortcut resumes synchronization; the browser proof exercises the actual Unpin action after reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing preference/session owners preserve concurrent, offline, cross-tab, profile-switch, compare-and-set/retry, and delayed-acknowledgment behavior. Ambiguous raced acknowledgments use one guarded fresh read because the public protocol has no revision; ordinary acknowledgments add no reads. Genuinely baseless new writes still fail closed.

Cold GitHub/hovercard English uses the existing lazy catalog while shared labels remain eager. Wording and ordered hovercard catalog are unchanged. Main’s browser-capability admission and modern browser target are preserved. No database/configuration option, budget increase, artificial delay, or weakened guard is introduced.

**Maintainer-approved migration exception:** @steipete authorized landing this existing Lit rail without expanding the PR into Solid infrastructure. Lit no-growth remains an approved exception—not a passing check.

## Evidence

Locally verified candidate **a9d0066d24d88b26c0d3e39a621154724a54398a**, tree **241df3afc8c52ad0a1e20eea25282622f9838146**. Published head **968087f45c5aab2f66857f3343c2e145addffb0d** has that exact tree and Peter’s coauthor credit. It retains the reviewed stable-outbox repair, main integration, and cold-copy reduction. Production, app-test and E2E-test type graphs pass. The sole textual conflict preserves the already-tested no-creator-chip metadata assertions from #168575.
- Cold-copy delta: **8/8 cold locale/consumer tests**, **44/44 hovercard unit tests**, **6/6 hovercard browser cases (25.30s)**, scoped independent P0–P2 review, production/UI-other types, four-file typed lint, i18n verification and formatting pass. The final type-only eager-key declaration strengthens the checked catalog contract; runtime bytes are unchanged from review.

title: feat: personalize session backgrounds
body:
Closes #153797

## What Problem This Solves

People cannot turn off theme artwork or choose a private background independently for New Session and conversations.

## User Impact

Appearance offers **None, Theme, or a private image**, independent placement switches, **Faded / Full bleed** styles, and adjustable visibility with a temporary Settings preview. The first upload appears on New Session only. Both styles protect text contrast and keep writing surfaces solid; unset preferences preserve existing theme artwork and glass.

Images follow the authenticated person, not the shared conversation. Hiding retains an image; Remove deletes it. Anonymous None/theme choices stay browser-local. Accessibility contrast settings suppress artwork.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Appearance preferences/outbox remain authoritative. One metadata-stripped JPEG per profile lives in the existing SQLite database. Worker-backed replacement/removal and preference selection commit atomically with exact compare-and-set guards; private reads revalidate current identity and permissions after asynchronous work. No originals/history, external image URLs, new dependency, or schema-version bump.

Uploads accept static JPEG/PNG/WebP up to 8 MiB/25 MP and retain at most 2560 px/2 MiB. A static decoration preserves transparent reading surfaces; Faded ends smoothly at the composer without blur or per-frame JavaScript.

**Startup tradeoff:** the explicitly authorized committed-baseline cap increases by 1,407 B (0.38%) to 374,285 B. The previously verified paired build against `3193e15` measured 374,677 B, within the unchanged 512 B growth and 64 B build-variance allowances (374,861 B enforcement limit). title: fix(pr): publish reviewed corrections with pending GitHub gates
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: native preparation refuses to publish an independently reviewed correction when the maintainer selects the default GitHub-pending gate mode.

## User Impact

No runtime or end-user change. Maintainers can publish reviewed corrections and hand required checks to GitHub without misrepresenting pending checks as successful local proof. This intentionally extends the correction policy introduced in #149068; it does not waive signing, exact-head review, CI, security, or enforced reviews.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing gate owner now binds a pending disposition through `HOSTED_GATES_TARGET_HEAD_SHA`, rather than requiring a success-only stamp. Verified publication receipts remain the only way to map the reviewed local candidate to a different hosted commit with the same tree. Sync preserves that binding too.

Ordinary pending-gate merge still requires exact-head auto-merge, completed ClawSweeper review, the enforced `openclaw/ci-gate`, and no known failed required checks. Pending correction replacement recovery remains restricted to the existing explicitly qualified routes. The separately authorized Crabbox path is unchanged. No wrapper trust exception or local self-admission is added.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original refusal in three regression cases before the repair.
- Correction preparation: **45 passed**; publication/sync/resume: **19 passed**; native correction merge/recovery: **23 passed**. These exercise real Git/Bash owners with deterministic external GitHub fixtures, not live GitHub proof. Negative cases retain the incoming NEEDS WORK review and reject stale/missing bindings, changed review authority, missing/failed required gates, missing ClawSweeper review, and unqualified pending recovery.
- Sibling native preparation/hosted/pending merge tests: **44 passed**. Canonical wrapper inventory: **1 passed**, 16 filtered out.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed. Its test-table coverage finding was corrected; the previously unreachable pending-recovery case now executes and passes. The hosted-alias fixture was also corrected to load the real publication owner and supply the complete native receipt.

title: fix: agents lose interrupted requests when asked to continue
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents lose the original request when it was interrupted before execution and the user later asks to continue, even though the Control UI still displays that request.

## User Impact

Built-in and CLI agent turns can use bounded previews of saved interrupted inputs to understand a continuation. This does not replay inputs, restore old permissions, or expose queued, cancelled, hidden, or context-excluded messages. No schema or configuration migration is required. The native Codex harness and the original recovery-run ownership failure are outside this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI renders retained pending inputs separately from model history. Add an escaped, historical conversation-data snapshot through the existing turn-context owners, scoped to the physical session and bounded to three 4,000-character previews from the latest retained-input page. Keep the current request and transcript bytes unchanged.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite accepted-input regression: the original implementation produced empty continuation context; the repaired production prompt-assembly boundary exposes the interrupted request without consuming or replaying it.
- 42 focused tests passed across interrupted-input, embedded-prompt, runtime-facts, and CLI-context suites. The final affected rerun passed all 9 tests in two files (50.05 s command wall time, including cold worker preparation); new integration cases took 1.770 s combined. These are local timings; the current hosted run is recorded below.

Build also reports a non-fatal Control UI startup-size warning; no UI source was changed.

The post-integration focused rerun passed 9/9 tests in 82.79 s command wall time (including cold worker preparation); the new integration cases took 1.812 s combined. - CI on `08d962b2fbad` caught a private CLI media-suffix ordering regression. The unchanged failing test was reproduced locally before the correction. Moving interrupted-input context before the existing media suffix fixes the production ordering without weakening tests. The complete failing shard plus continuation/privacy siblings now pass **205/205 tests** across five files (185.56 s command wall time, including cold worker preparation), and targeted lint passes. New sessions could select devices and cloud workers, but not the existing OpenAI Agents API hosted workspace.

## User Impact

The environment and model pickers agree on the selected runtime and account. Local project, folder, and worktree controls are hidden for hosted execution without discarding their draft intent.

This requires the enabled Agents API plugin, its hosted configuration, and an available OpenAI API-key model. ChatGPT subscription authentication is unsupported. This does not add repository synchronization or multiuser support; the hosted integration remains intended for a personal, single-user Gateway. Files continue through chat attachments. Unconfigured or unavailable choices explain setup instead of starting a different runtime or cloud VM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker consumes the existing model catalog's runtime-specific availability and capabilities. title: fix: keep task replies in their chat and avoid Reef commit-link false positives
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes background task replies going to an old external conversation instead of their originating WebChat, and Reef rejecting ordinary GitHub revision links as secrets.

## User Impact

WebChat task completions stay in WebChat, and mirroring an external send into a transcript no longer changes that transcript’s reply destination. Reef can carry GitHub commit, blob, and tree links without mistaking their revision ID for a credential.

The Reef exception is deliberately syntactic: only the exact 40-hex revision position skips the entropy heuristic. It does not verify that a repository or commit exists or is public, and a synthetic value in that position is indistinguishable locally. Known-credential rules and the model guard still inspect the unchanged full message. No configuration or database migration is needed; saved external routes remain available when explicitly selected or when no captured origin exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

Completion routing discarded a captured internal origin and substituted saved external delivery metadata. Separately, the Gateway send handler treated a transcript-mirror selector as the owner of destination-route persistence. The fixes retain the captured origin and separate destination routing from transcript mirroring.

Reef now distinguishes revision-position IDs from other high-entropy tokens. Whole containing URI-like tokens are recognized first, so query/fragment nesting, apostrophes, Markdown wrappers, and nonhierarchical URI schemes cannot create a broader exemption. Other path segments and message text remain scanned.

## Evidence

- The repaired-head ClawSweeper review found a first-contact mirror regression: a separate missing `sessionKey` could lose its transcript even after successful external delivery. Reproduced through the send handler, real outbound persistence, real transcript mirroring and SQLite readback. The outbound-session owner now uses the existing worker-backed identity-only operation to create a missing mirror, without writing the destination route into it; existing mirror identity and saved delivery metadata remain unchanged. **83 send tests passed in 16.53s**, including missing/existing mirror persistence controls, and **48 outbound-route tests passed**. A fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issue.
- Initial CI found three PR-caused media-routing regressions in `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38028654539/job/114144959682)). Reproduced all three locally; media admission now interprets its internal WebChat sentinel before the shared origin resolver. Interactive WebChat remains internal; internal/inter-session media keeps its explicitly supported saved-route fallback. Existing assertions were unchanged. **78 tests passed** across media lifecycle/preparation/retention and requester-settle dispatch in **88.08s**; fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview, core production types, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed for the correction.
- **ClawSweeper compatibility-proof disposition:** its initial completed review found no discrete defect and requested stable-to-candidate database proof. This PR changes routing selection, not the stored data model: session delivery types, schema, reader/normalizer and `updateSessionLastRoute` storage representation are unchanged. The subsequent mirror repair extends the existing outbound-session owner with its existing worker-backed `ensure-identity` operation; it adds no storage format or migration. Existing canonical saved external records are consumed in the dispatch regression, including explicit external and missing-origin controls; the send-handler boundary proves destination-route writes remain success-gated and distinct from mirroring. The media CI regression above is repaired at its provenance-aware admission owner. ClawSweeper withdrew that database-upgrade requirement in its next review. These focused boundary proofs cover the changed invariant; no database migration or new storage representation exists to qualify. A stable-version upgrade/E2E was not run and is not claimed.

- Reproduced the wrong-route behavior through requester-settle dispatch and Gateway send handlers before repair; explicit external and shared-main controls remain covered.
- **257 routing/delivery tests passed** across send, completion delivery, settle dispatch/watch, and private-parent completion. Combined initial routing/protocol invocation: **125.17s**; the final, disjoint Reef protocol suite passed **80 tests in 9.83s**.
- The exact original 906-byte rejected reply now passes deterministic checks. Protocol tests exercise outbound sealing, inbound acceptance, guard deny/review, credentials beside links, and nested-URI negative controls.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no remaining actionable findings after its two parser findings were reproduced and corrected.
- Core production types, all 27 core-test type shards, Reef package-boundary types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, source line-cap and mock-export guards passed in scoped validation.

title: improve(ui): render readable tweet preview cards
body:
Closes #168212

## What Problem This Solves

Tweet browser-result cards hide available post text behind a truncated page title and URL.

## User Impact

X/Twitter posts now show a readable author and handle, available post text, and a larger preview image. Open and menu actions remain visible on mobile, and a compact usable card remains when metadata is missing. Ordinary browser cards keep their existing presentation and routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

title: fix: Doctor maintenance fails when state inspection is slow
body:
Closes #168031

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor and update repair can fail to enter maintenance on a running systemd Gateway when checking a large state database is slow.

## User Impact

Linux operators can complete maintenance without local database checks being mistaken for an unresponsive service manager. Authority checks and native-operation deadlines remain enforced. No configuration or schema changes are required.

Cold database hashing can still increase total command time; this fixes deadline accounting, not that separate performance cost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Nested systemd inspections now share one scoped clock that excludes only synchronous custody/admission checks. Every check still runs. Manager I/O and asynchronous waiting remain charged, retained peers use the submitting inspection’s clock, and actual service mutations retain a separate wall-clock deadline. FIFO ordering, revocation checks, cancellation, and cleanup joining are preserved.

The regression extends the existing cold-observation test rather than increasing timeout constants or caching authorization. A diagnostic fixture also isolates system-unit discovery so the runner’s own Gateway cannot change its expected user-bus diagnosis.

## Evidence

- The cold-source regression failed before this patch, including after the earlier continuation-receipt shortcut. The focused batch passed **115/115**, including competing-update and final-custody-revocation controls.
- Broader daemon siblings passed **320/320**. Doctor command siblings and both platform-specific diagnostic cases passed after correcting the fixture’s host-unit leak.
- Canonical independent autoreview completed with no P1-or-higher findings. Core and all 27 core-test type partitions passed; final affected typechecks, lint, dead-export checks, architecture guards, formatting, docs validation, and package build/tarball checks passed. Full repository test suite was not run.
- Real installed-package proof used rootless Podman, Debian 12/systemd 252.39, Node 24.21.0, a real user manager/bus, and **95,000 audit rows (~160 MB)**. No privileged mode, host mounts, or operator Gateway were used.
- The published **2026.9.9** updater installed the exact candidate via `update --tag file:<candidate> --yes --json`; running build identity and health were verified.
- Candidate `update repair` and standalone `doctor --fix` both exited 0, restarted the managed service with distinct PIDs, and recovered health. All 95,000 rows survived and full SQLite integrity returned `ok`. Runtime was 130s and 220s respectively. Only the synthetic fixture’s loopback and plaintext-token advisories remained.
- The live baseline repair deferred maintenance with state-owner contention; baseline standalone Doctor completed on this host. The deterministic regression, not an overstated live before/after claim, proves the original timeout boundary.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and validation provenance</summary>

The focused repository runner was `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <six daemon files> src/commands/doctor-maintenance.admission-activation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 105.39s total; the three real SQLite/native-boundary command cases took 69.62s including setup. New clock/queue cases use deterministic clocks, not sleeps. CI seconds have not yet been measured.

An initial changed-check run caught a test-only exported factory; it was made private, then the failed and remaining gates were completed successfully. An initial Linux diagnostic failure was reproduced and traced to a real host system unit leaking into the fixture; all original diagnostic assertions remain intact.

</details>

title: fix(agentsapi): preserve saved sessions across binding upgrades
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: saved Agents API conversations from v2026.9.9 are rejected as invalid binding rows after upgrading to credential-independent session identities.

## User Impact

Existing conversations can continue with the **same remote session ID**. **Keep the original API key and model/environment/MCP configuration until the first upgraded continuation succeeds.** An already-rotated key cannot safely establish what the old combined digest represented; restore the original key/settings, or explicitly reset/delete with a currently authorized key after the original native work settles. After conversion, existing current-format key-rotation behavior is unchanged, including provider access restrictions.

Refused migration, inaccessible sessions, malformed state, and failed cleanup retain the saved binding for recovery. The repair never silently creates a replacement conversation, persists raw keys, deletes remote conversation history, or adopts an executor controller. It does not deploy or modify production state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-owned binding admission validates the historical fingerprint and current API access before its existing leased, generation-fenced owner atomically records the current configuration fingerprint. The host and SQLite worker share the codec. Reset/deletion need authenticated settlement of the saved native identity, not permission to resume under new settings; rollback preserves the original record.

Readable remote metadata is not an adequate replacement for the old digest: persisted MCP transports omit secret headers and environment reads expose effective defaults. Unsupported pre-plugin-ownership executor bindings remain separate.

Update/Doctor drivers, SQLite schema, retention, and the existing pre-upgrade backup workflow are unchanged. Conversion happens at the first admitted continuation. Returning to a release that requires the old format needs its matching pre-upgrade state backup, not a binary-only downgrade.

## Evidence

- Red control: the registered public harness rejected exact stable-format bytes with “Invalid Agents API binding row”; the candidate migrates and reopens the original ID without allocating a replacement.
- Upgrade qualification: executed the archived v2026.9.9 binding writer and its actual original fingerprint expression; its bytes match the regression fixture. This is **shipped-producer → candidate admission proof at the changed boundary**, not a full installed-updater rehearsal. Updater mechanics are unchanged.
- **pnpm test extensions/agentsapi --maxWorkers=1**: **209 tests passed** across 10 files, **200.2s wall time**. Includes credential/configuration refusals, SDK access failures, malformed rows, authority/lease/source drift, restart, settlement, and cleanup. Existing real SQLite fixtures account for the persistence suite's seconds-long cases; mocks cannot prove those ownership/rollback contracts.
- Worker deletion/rollback owner: **10 tests passed**, **69.6s wall time**, including the legacy codec through the real worker and commit compensation.
- Changed-scope typechecks, lint, guards, formatting, and git diff --check passed. Early test-fixture type/lint errors were corrected. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38020945726): the 57-test persistence/environment shard took 124.58s including startup, the other 152 Agents API tests took 30.61s, and the 10-test worker deletion/rollback invocation took 38.14s. The new migration helper runs inside the existing persistence suite; these are shard/invocation wall times, not invented per-file measurements.
- **pnpm build** passed in **286.9s**. An earlier experimental TypeScript declaration compiler crashed with “concurrent map writes”; a bounded reproduction of the exact package stage passed, followed by the complete build. This is not claimed as a compiler fix. The build reported an unrelated nonfatal existing UI startup-gzip budget warning; no UI inputs changed.
- Live official-SDK check: one owned synthetic hosted session passed authenticated migration/readback with the same ID, without inference. Provisioning initially refused cleanup with 409; after connection, deletion succeeded and an independent read returned 404. This is not a whole-Gateway live turn.
- Canonical independent autoreview completed with no P0/P1 findings; separate implementation and migration-safety review found no actionable issue. The final diagnostic-only recovery message has focused test/lint proof.

title: fix(doctor): preserve installed plugins when path safety checks block them
body:
Closes #168066

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor silently disabling an installed local plugin when discovery blocks its path—for example, when a root-run update inspects a service-user-owned plugin.

## User Impact

Blocked plugins keep their complete authored entry, explicit enablement, allow/deny policy, and slot selections. Ownership and writable-path safety checks still reject execution. Genuinely stale references remain repairable, and local-path installations no longer receive a bare plugin-ID registry reinstall hint.

This is candidate-side Doctor behavior, so it applies when an already-published updater invokes the repaired candidate. It does not change the update account, weaken validation, or repair pre-existing cross-user file ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor treated absence from admitted manifests as proof of uninstall, although validation already distinguished **present but blocked**. The existing diagnostic-to-plugin matching now has one shared owner consumed by validation, stale cleanup, migration availability, and install-health reporting. Explicit diagnostic IDs retain precedence over ID-less path fallback.

Blocked migration obligations stay pending, with their blocked-path reason retained through final receipt publication rather than overwritten with install-or-enable advice. The repair does not restore an enable flag after destructive cleanup or globally suppress unrelated validation.

## Evidence

- Final changed-file gates passed: core and core-test typechecks, lint, formatting, dead-export scans, import cycles, schema and ownership guards. Independent P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean on the final candidate.
- Published **2026.9.9 (bcfc888)** reproduced the bug in an isolated Linux container: UID 999 Doctor retained the entry; root Doctor deleted enablement; a subsequent Gateway startup omitted the plugin.
- Published **2026.9.9 updater → candidate** completed with exit 0 and status **ok** in **508.852 seconds on the final head**. Root discovery continued to report suspicious ownership; the complete enabled entry and nested settings survived. The service-account Gateway registered the plugin and reached its listening state afterward.

- Rebuilt and replayed the **exact final head `36438dd7138340e5d84beff48afcaa6b2e34995e`**, including final receipt diagnostics. The canonical package build completed in **3m 54s**, and tarball integrity validation passed. Both direct and linked root Doctor runs retain the **present but blocked** diagnosis through completion; the obsolete install-or-enable message is absent.
- Focused tests cover real discovery → Doctor cleanup → config publication, unchanged rejection, unrelated stale cleanup, policy/slot preservation, identity precedence, missing-path hints, and final migration receipts. Final diagnostic/publication run: **15 tests passed**, 61.71s wrapper wall time (including cold compiled-worker preparation).
- Additional focused suites: **4 matcher**, **51 config validation**, **16 stale cleanup**, **24 install-health**, and **1 bundled-availability** tests passed. Install-health wrapper: 25.88s; matcher suite: 0.813s. Hosted CI status and the remaining failure are documented below.

title: fix(ui): restore inline per-subagent activity
body:
Related: #159179

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the loss of inline per-subagent activity after the Tasks/TaskFlow removal: a parent chat showed only an aggregate waiting count.

## User Impact

Each unfinished subagent is visible again with its name and current activity while the parent works or waits. Rows remain in launch order, distinguish queued and delegated work, and open the correct subagent details. On narrow screens, activity appears below the name.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore the useful presentation without restoring TaskFlow. The view reuses the current child roster and safe observer headlines, with no child-transcript polling or additional execution state. Live headlines are fenced to the current run, session incarnation, agent, and connection. Completed children leave the inline list; existing failure/attention notices and the Subagents panel remain available.

The mocked Gateway now mirrors the existing broad observer-headline delivery contract, while keeping raw messages and tool arguments individually scoped.

## Evidence

- Red/green regression: the initial per-agent projection case failed on base `4ac1a8028b31` before the repair (activity was `undefined` instead of three rows; the other 19 cases passed). The same restored-status coverage passes with the fix. The Before capture also reproduces the missing rows through the actual chat UI.
