title: fix: restricted intake agents cannot delegate coding work
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a restricted intake agent can start a coding session, but its local command/file denials leave that coding session unable to implement the requested change.

## User Impact

Operators can explicitly authorize native handoffs to exact coding agents with `agents.entries.<intake>.subagents.delegateToolsTo`, alongside `allowAgents`, without enabling those tools on the intake agent. Existing configurations and previously created children keep their original restrictions.

The initial handoff requires a deny-only Gateway-native requester and local placement. Restrictive allowlists, sender restrictions, sandbox boundaries, and target policy remain enforced. ACP is unchanged. Unsupported mediated/cloud handoffs and worker execution of an active grant refuse rather than silently start an unusable or insufficiently guarded run. No live deployment or configuration change is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep an explicit target grant separate from the original requester snapshot. Only the requesting agent's local deny layer can be waived; nonlocal denials survive even when they name the same tool. Same-grantee helpers retain the root-bound grant, completions retain their per-edge requester snapshot, and grant removal restores the fallback. Retained tools recheck live authority before effects, including after preparation and file-I/O waits. Already-started effects are not rolled back.

The config baseline grows by two schema nodes for this opt-in array and its item. This is intentional: changing `allowAgents` alone would silently widen existing delegation authority. There is no database schema/version change or inferred upgrade of legacy session rows.

## Evidence

Current repair head: 7e2c4a2a73603717e0695aa683d0878569e0738c. The merge conflict against main bc8f693df3ae is resolved, retaining the reviewed abort-aware catalog-renewal fixture. The independently landed upstream fallback projection repair (#168078) supersedes our temporary workaround, which is removed rather than retained as a second owner. Historical checks below remain labeled with their tested inputs; final-head hosted CI/review remain separate gates.

- Original visible-spawn regression failed with the intake's `exec`, `write`, `edit`, and `apply_patch` denials retained (8.21s wrapper time).
- Integrated focused suite: 96 tests passed across policy, persisted completion, visible spawning, CLI projection, and worker topology (131.81s wrapper time).
- Final authority repairs: 62 tests passed, including plugin/family denial expansion, a paused real host write, existing-session worker refusal, and initial worker refusal/replay (114.07s wrapper time).
- Production and all 27 core-test typecheck graphs passed; affected graphs were rechecked after the authority repairs. Changed-file lint passed with zero warnings/errors. Native schema, database-first, import-cycle, media/sidecar, webhook/auth, docs config examples, and docs link guards passed.
- Independent source review and autoreview findings were repaired. Autoreview's final index-only finding is resolved by staging the integration together before commit.
- The isolated X composition test passed: real ingress, admission, tool assembly, `sessions.create`/SQLite, child file write and command execution, anonymous HTTP read, guest denial, and separate deferred delegation/publication revocation. Assertions: 8.195s; Vitest including compilation: 84.17s; isolated QA build: 288.5s. HTTPS/model boundaries are deterministic, not live X credentials. The fixture remains release-only (0 added ordinary unit-CI seconds); hosted CI timings are not yet available.

Integration at `5aa6d54bb80db8ba29efcd670ab9c4b90c1c4029` resolves the two generated config-baseline conflicts against main `4ac1a8028b3`. The owning generator refreshed them; the upstream memory-flush restriction is preserved. All 132 selected regressions passed (136.51s), including the memory-flush sibling, and the unchanged full X composition passed again on the integrated source (7.921s assertions, 66.03s Vitest). Core typecheck, config baseline validation, and affected lint passed.

Original-base validation observations: the broad dead-export scan reports untouched `isTelegramReadOnlyControlLaneText` and the unused `model-selection.ts` re-export of `resolveContextTokens`. One isolated QA build also produced an unparseable bundled TypeBox `FromCyclic` declaration; identical production inputs built successfully in adjacent runs. This is recorded as an unresolved build-tool failure, not claimed fixed by a passing replay.

Final conflict-resolution head also passes core typechecking and the complete isolated X production-owner composition: 8.806s assertions / 86.90s Vitest, QA runtime build successful, outer exit 0 and container absence confirmed. This re-exercises the updated public entry path, actual child command/file effects, guest denial, and independent delegation/publication revocation on the merged source. Deterministic transport/model boundaries remain as disclosed.

### CLI/plugin mediated final effects

The new `src/agents/harness/mediated-delegation-effects.test.ts` runs both the production CLI authenticated loopback-HTTP path and generic plugin-harness dispatch against real command/file owners. The grant-dependent tools launch a real command and write a file; sender-restricted calls launch nothing; revocation during command preparation or after descriptor opening prevents the final effect. Reconstructed tools restore the deny fallback while retaining read access.

Eight tests pass on `5aa6d54` plus the behavior-preserving import-cycle repair and regenerated prompt snapshots: `pnpm test src/agents/harness/mediated-delegation-effects.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 21.73s wall / 17.67s Vitest / 4.229s test cases. This is real mediated-boundary/final-effect proof, **not** a vendor CLI subprocess, live model-provider or Codex CLI run. Exec policy is full/off: revocation is tested during preparation and final file I/O, **not** an interactive approval queue. The sender-source fixture tests the persisted policy boundary; existing X composition tests cover actual ingress and spawn creation.

### Latest-stable produced-data compatibility

A secretless, network-disabled rootless container used the actual published **2026.9.9** package (`bcfc88812a35243893585dbeca87ca41b48272ca`, npm latest live-resolved and rechecked) to produce config, SQLite sessions and two native child rows. Candidate **`5aa6d54bb80db8ba29efcd670ab9c4b90c1c4029`** built successfully with `pnpm build` (235.9s), then its real Doctor migrated copied stores: state **19→20**, both agent databases **24→25**. All three candidate CLI preflights returned **exact**, integrity **ok**.

Both child rows remained byte-identical, including inherited allow/deny lists, creation attribution, parent/completion links, IDs and revisions. After adding an explicit candidate grant and cold-loading in another container, neither old child acquired `delegatedToolPolicy`, both resolved from `persisted-child`, and exec remained excluded. All preexisting settings values stayed unchanged; **the whole config file is not byte-identical** because Doctor added its webhook migration stamp, four wizard metadata fields, and 31 disabled-unavailable-skill entries.

**Scope:** real stable-produced state → candidate Doctor/admission/read/policy owners. Not a published updater-installation/service-replacement/Gateway-readiness/inference test. Stable's private native-child persistence function was exposed through an export-only loader adapter; its body and installed package bytes were unchanged. Stable does not stamp the present-day sender-source flags, so this does **not** prove retention of an already-present sender flag. An auxiliary parent's hand-supplied legacy webchat origin normalized under the existing migration; it is not external-sender-provenance proof.

<details>
<summary>Compatibility commands and exact row results</summary>

Pinned image: `sha256:2c1f4e0fd6450f43ddb46d60c2a6df30855a8588e165b1f2559fb0eda8d7ff35`; Node 24.20.0; read-only rootfs, no network, capabilities dropped, no operator state or credentials mounted. All task containers were removed.

### CI repairs and retained failures

The static import cycle is removed by relocating the unchanged deny-floor projection and sharing its narrow context contract. Both cycle guards pass. The five changed prompt snapshots were regenerated through their owner and the snapshot check passes. The catalog-renewal fixture no longer starts an extra explicit refresh while trying to join expiry renewal; this repairs the stale test contract introduced with #168050 without changing production refresh semantics.

The earlier CI run 38016450576 exposed a preexisting command-RPC fallback defect: the backup was selected, then retry decoration tried to recapture the immutable user prompt after provider dispatch. title: docs: prefer meaningful integration proof over low-value tests
body:
Related: #168070

## What Problem This Solves

Passing tests that mirror the implementation can miss broken provider requests, recovery, and persisted state. Recent compaction work shipped five such mistakes that unit tests did not catch: a side request sent a different tool set and input from the warm turn (0 cached tokens), a paid result was discarded after a local check, a fallback was logged only at DEBUG, a rejected replay looped because its marker was never persisted, and a default reached auth modes it did not support.

## Fix

- Root `AGENTS.md`: the testing rule becomes a short instruction with a triggered link. The link fires before changing provider requests, fallbacks, recovery, or defaults, not only when writing tests. "Stable conversation context" adds one rule: a side request that reuses a conversation shares the turn's request preparation or carries no cache identity.
- `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md`: one compact section, "Prove behavior at the owning boundary". It covers behavior, red/green slices, final request parity, paid work, durable recovery, default reach, and measured claims.
- Testing, test-audit, PR-maintainer, and review-flow docs link to that section instead of repeating checklists.

## User Impact

Guidance only. No runtime changes, no new test framework, and no deletion of existing tests. Existing test-value and cost limits stay.

## Evidence

- Root `AGENTS.md`: 19,950 characters, under the 20,000-character bootstrap limit.
- `pnpm format:docs:check`: clean (1,326 files). `pnpm docs:check-mdx`: passed (1,340 files). `pnpm docs:check-links`: 14,944 internal links, 0 broken. `git diff --check`: clean.
- No runtime tests or paid benchmarks: no production or test code changed.

title: fix: retry chat initialization after rolled-back maintenance conflicts

## What Problem This Solves

Chat initialization could fail before replying when concurrent subagent maintenance changed prepared facts, even though SQLite confirmed rollback. CI also exposed a pre-existing model-fallback failure: retry instructions attempted to replace an already-dispatched user prompt.

## User Impact

Known rollback conflicts recover through the existing bounded initialization retry. Model fallback retains the original user turn and frozen projection while delivering retry instructions separately. Unknown transaction outcomes, mismatched receipts, and failed native-binding compensation remain terminal. No schema, stored-data, retention, permission, configuration, dependency, or update migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing transaction settlement and serialized mutation-conflict owners, with the exact session-maintenance operation label. Do not add another retry owner. The prompt-state owner treats a fallback as internal continuation only when the factory-owned recorder confirms prior provider dispatch.

CI repairs preserve typed-error, native-write, resource-retirement, archive-retention, and recovery-owner assertions. Current main independently landed the earlier export cleanup and some fixture fixes. Four resulting fixture conflicts were reconciled against `a285e8ba5841732229a931b3ed230b45574e09cc`: retain nonvacuous memory resource/complete-archive proof, and keep main's equivalent recovery fixture and mock explanation. title: feat: organize and archive nested conversations explicitly
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nested conversations need an explicit way to become independent, and archiving a parent must not make its still-active children disappear.

## User Impact

Drag a persistent child to the top level, Pinned, or a custom group, or use **Move to top level**. Ordinary archive affects only that conversation; **Archive session and children…** offers an explicit counted confirmation and Undo.

Promotion preserves the conversation URL, transcript, workspace, origin, permissions, and execution relationships. Hidden worker runs remain outside sidebar organization. This feature adds no configuration change or database schema migration. Upgrading from the published stable release uses the existing Doctor migrations, verified below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sidebar placement is now separate from execution ancestry. Tree archive discovers collapsed descendants, excludes independent/grouped/already-archived branches, and checks the selected sessions and their ancestors again before stopping work or writing. Guarded batches settle deepest-first across stores; partial outcomes stay visible and Undo restores only successful targets.

title: fix: subagent results stop returning after a follow-up
body:
Closes #162761
Related: #167047 — @Oldrich333’s existing owner-only proposal. This repair covers named operators as well, without adding an owner exception or changing that contributor’s branch.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes successful subagent results failing to return when the requester sends a follow-up while the parent is waiting.

## User Impact

Users can continue the conversation without losing accepted child results. Results retain the original caller’s permissions; real source revocation, reset, cancellation, and foreign-requester protections remain enforced. No configuration or storage migration is required. This does not replay historical failed deliveries or deploy to a running Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The automation-management handoff also retained a second copy of general operator authority. A new user turn correctly retired automation privileges but inadvertently made that second copy veto result delivery. Remove the duplicate capture, retention, revocation tombstone, and dispatch wrapper: the existing registry completion-custody owner already checks and carries the original source around the actual settle dispatcher. Its fail-closed source checks and tombstones remain intact.

**Production diff: +15 / −118 = −103 lines.** Tests and documentation are counted separately. The paired regression reuses the existing registry fixture through a coherent sibling support module; no additional Gateway boot, sleep, or polling was added.

## Evidence

### Final Gateway-effect proof (acee199156f2)

The follow-up now reaches the real in-process Gateway requester continuation and SQLite effects. Only provider inference is mocked; announcement dispatch is not substituted in this fixture. The paired cases reuse the existing suite-level Gateway.

| Scenario | Original caller/scopes retained | Final requester input persisted | Execution starts | Pending inputs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Same human sends a follow-up; original source remains valid | Yes, asserted in the admitted requester | Yes | 1 | 0 |
| Same follow-up, then original source revoked while input staging is awaiting | Revoked original source is rejected; fresh caller is not borrowed | No; transcript unchanged | 0 | 0 |

The forbidden case also leaves no accepted idempotency entry and no model call. It fails with `Original completion source revoked during dispatch`, after entering the real input-staging path and before effects.

**Revert control:** replacing only the production owner with its pre-fix version makes the same-human final-effect case fail with `Requester operator authority is no longer current` (64.38 s wall). Restoring the fixed owner preserves all six passing cases; production source is byte-identical to the previously reviewed fix.

```text
enforces same-human follow-up after consuming the pause notice and before starting the next turn: passed (1289 ms)
enforces follow-up source revoked during dispatch after consuming the pause notice and before starting the next turn: passed (1394 ms)
Tests: 6 passed (6)
```

`pnpm test src/gateway/server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **73.38 s wall**. Gateway-server test types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap, timeout-race and mock-export checks passed. Fresh P0–P2 autoreview of this test-only addition: scoped-clean. Hosted CI seconds remain pending.

### Earlier implementation proof

- Red/green through real registration, yield transfer, normal same-human chat admission, and requester-settle dispatch: the valid-source case failed before the repair; afterward it delivers under the original source, without restoring old automation management or borrowing a more privileged ambient caller. Revoked original-source delivery is still refused.
- Seven focused suites: **94/94 tests passed**, covering completion custody, automation management, private results, cancellation, reset, mixed sources, and real Gateway pause/continuation effects. Combined `pnpm test <seven focused files> --maxWorkers=1` wall time: **239.60 s**.
- After final test extraction and cleanup: **56/56 tests passed** in the two directly changed authority suites; command wall **94.75 s**. New paired case bodies: **1.377 s / 2.047 s** locally. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available. These cases exercise actual persisted registration and source lifetime boundaries, not a mock authorization decision.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview of the final candidate: **scoped-clean**.
- Full `pnpm build`: **passed**, **360.18 s** wall. Core production types and all **27 core test typecheck graphs** passed. Targeted type-aware lint: **0 warnings, 0 errors**. Formatting, line-cap, assertion, SQLite-worker, mock-export, dependency, and other completed guards passed.
- **Historical baseline check failure:** the full changed-check command stopped at its unused-export scan (921.60 s wall, including waiting for the build lock). It flags `isTelegramReadOnlyControlLaneText` in `extensions/telegram/src/sequential-key.ts`, `buildDirectChatContext` in `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts`, and the `resolveContextTokens` re-export in `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`. All three files are unchanged by this patch; inspection of the pinned base shows no external production consumers of those exports (the latter two have test-only consumers). This is not reported as a green full check. Remaining selected static checks were run separately, without suppressing the failed scan. The three baseline exports have since been repaired on main by [PR #168048](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168048), merged October 10 at 01:18 UTC.

The initial registry proof uses an announcement stub; the final Gateway proof above does not. Both use synthetic identities and isolated state, not a live production conversation. No production state was changed.

title: fix(agentsapi): follow-up turns fail after native tool use
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Agents API follow-up turns can fail after native tool use even though the cloud turn completed, and session restrictions or lifecycle changes can leave the remote session in the wrong state.

## User Impact

Users can continue hosted conversations across turns and Gateway restarts, transfer files, and stop/reset sessions reliably. Native search honors both the global and session disable setting; Gateway functions retain the session filesystem boundary. Changing effective native-search policy requires resetting an existing session rather than silently retaining its immutable tool surface.

No binding-schema migration, credential persistence, remote-history deletion, or production deployment is introduced. Self-hosted native execution is covered synthetically, not by a provisioned live executor. Controller final-effect authority is additionally proven through real plugin registry dispatch and filesystem I/O. This repairs the existing Agents API integration; it does not add a separate subscription-based Codex Cloud integration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve original run attribution when replaying historical native transcript items while keeping strict idempotency comparison intact. Recover delayed terminal records without resubmitting work, settle hosted/external bindings before removal, and retire controlled executors only after a committed history cut. Reuse the existing host permission policy and scoped transcript fact reader, retaining Codex’s narrower message projection.

Two existing unused-export failures blocked whole-tree validation; this also removes an orphan Telegram helper and a redundant internal model-selection re-export, updates their test consumers, and canonically shrinks one obsolete mock baseline entry. No Telegram routing behavior changes.

## Evidence

- [Exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38012914391) passes, including both CI/security gates.
- [Controller final-effect proof and stable-state qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168067#issuecomment-6092237042): authorized post-commit retirement deletes a real test-owned resource; host revocation during awaited controller work prevents that I/O; retained capabilities reject after completion. The no-op assertion negative control fails on actual unauthorized deletion; restoring the candidate passes.
- Known inherited upgrade gap: authFingerprint-only bindings from v2026.9.9 are rejected by the unchanged current-main parser (cutover in #162948); a stable-to-candidate upgrade is **not** claimed here. The original record remains unmodified. Current-format cold restart is verified below.

title: fix(models): avoid needless ClawRouter catalog refreshes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated ClawRouter model-list requests and avoidable refresh warnings in model pickers and Automations after only a minute of use. Explicit Refresh could also silently reuse a warm response instead of discovering changes.

## User Impact

ClawRouter inventory, including a valid empty result, is reused for one hour per endpoint and resolved credential. New models or grants may take up to an hour to appear automatically; using Refresh discovers them immediately. Current authorization and budgets remain enforced by ClawRouter at inference time. No configuration or dependency changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing catalog owner and shared response cache rather than adding a UI cache. Carry explicit refresh through the retained worker and bypass each acquired response key once, preserving pending-load sharing and credential isolation. Expiry and automatic failure retry continue to honor each underlying feed’s TTL. Preserve current worker admission, failure recovery and shared-auth behavior.

Reported and requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

## Evidence

Automatic account renewal preserves the warm shared metadata feed; explicit scoped refresh fetches new rows without replacing another agent’s inventory.

- Changed-test time: real-worker regression 5.362 s; ClawRouter file tests 216 ms; new shared-refresh cases 4 ms. Full cold invocation included a 114.3 s runtime build and 89.12 s Vitest phase. Hosted CI duration is pending.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes **Take photo** on Android opening a second web-camera preview instead of handing the capture gesture directly to the device.

## User Impact

Android Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Samsung Internet go straight to the existing single-image device capture input. **Photo** and **File** remain separate choices. Desktop preview/capture/retake, iPhone/iPad Safari’s **Attach…** picker, and embedded native-host behavior stay unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The camera owner now selects the native input before requesting a web stream, using the existing picker policy and input callback. Its connected/disabled/aborted-draft guards and shared attachment processing remain the owners of admission and returned files. Android WebViews and unknown app identities are not treated as verified browser picker hosts.

## Evidence

- Regression failed on pinned pre-fix main `999bf5ecc5c04815fdbf85b01711e80611aaad7a`: both Android composer cases observed zero native input clicks. Candidate passes all **26** focused camera/input tests, including inactive, disabled, aborted scopes and the existing preview lifecycle.

Real menu gestures reach the single-image `image/*`, `capture=environment` input without calling getUserMedia; cancellation, file return, reselection, draft retention, desktop capture/retake and conservative Safari/native/unknown-host behavior pass. The shared browser suite is intentionally slower than a unit test because native chooser gesture admission and the real dropdown/app boundary cannot be established in jsdom. These identity fixtures are **not Android OS certification**.

The aggregate changed check records existing dead-export failures in `sequential-key.ts`, `groups.ts` and `model-selection.ts`; those files are unchanged from the pinned baseline and are being repaired separately.

- Android app inspection: native chat uses Compose; `ControlUiWebView` has no file-chooser adapter. This PR does not claim or add native-app camera support.

### Exact-head CI qualification

[CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38010265421) is **not green**. ## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Remove the retired Telegram predicate and model-selection re-export, privatize the direct-chat helper after its production callers moved, and migrate all test/prompt-snapshot consumers to the existing owner entry points. The avatar publication fixture now triggers identity invalidation through the existing capability instead of expecting the intentionally removed TTL. All publication and rerender assertions remain intact. No scanner exceptions or production UI changes.

This is a maintainer-authorized red-main repair. Direct push of the proven fix was attempted first and rejected with GH013: “Changes must be made through a pull request.” This PR is the repository-prescribed fallback, not an unsolicited CI cleanup.

Requested by @steipete; contributor credit is retained in the commit.

Parent reproduced all three unchanged publication-test failures from UI CI run `38008988386`, job `114084573657`; test SHA-256 `fb9bf451d67888ff73a109a8cdb3a9a8abe892477e6c78e5c4af736eaf285ab3` matched main. title: fix(cron): manual runs lose tool access after the starting turn ends
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: manually started automations lose tool access after the chat turn or tool invocation that started them finishes, failing with `operator execution authority is no longer active` or `operator tool invocation authority expired`.

Reported as P0 by @obviyus after repeated automation permission failures. This PR fixes the reproduced manual-run lifetime failure; it does not claim every cron permission error has the same cause.

## User Impact

User impact: accepted manual runs can keep using their scheduled tools and deliver their results after the initiating request ends, just like timer-fired runs. Existing jobs need no recreation, permission expansion, new configuration, or migration.

Real revocation, missing saved accounts, job cancellation, and stored tool restrictions remain enforced. A separate missing repository-workspace binding is not repaired here.

A manual run no longer carries the caller's identity or request scope once it is accepted; it runs like a timer-fired run. A job that only worked when an admin started it by hand now behaves the same way it does on its schedule.

Revoking the caller's device after the run starts does not stop the accepted run, the same as for timer-fired runs. Revocation before the run starts still rejects it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manual command queue preserves its submitting async context. Although it already detached root-work admission and transcript writes, it retained both operator-tool authority and the request-scope client. Those temporary authorities could expire while the accepted cron was still running.

After guarded activation finishes, hand execution and finalization to the existing scheduler-owned Gateway context outside the initiating operator-tool scope. Keep preparation and activation under the original commit guards; the stored job and its run receipt still own permissions, cancellation, and delivery. Direct manual, stream, and on-exit execution converge on this boundary. Do not broadly weaken the generic scheduler or authorization checks.

## Evidence

- Before: isolated reproduction through the real `cron.run` handler, queue, and GitHub-status tool fails with the exact inactive-authority error; an invocation-scope case fails with expired authority; timer control passes. Model execution and the GitHub response are synthetic.
- After: **36/36** focused manual-run, cancellation, queued-caller revocation, FIFO, and transcript-delivery cases pass. **28/28** regression/stored-policy/requester-provenance cases pass (three overlap the first group).
- **7/7** real isolated-agent account-policy/history cases pass, including a manually queued job after invocation closure: its removed saved account is still rejected, model execution stays at zero, and error history is recorded.
- **Authority chain, 4/4** (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.manual-tool-authority.test.ts`). An admin creates the job through the real `cron.add` handler and starts it through the real `cron.run` handler. The request then ends before the job's tool call. From there the run uses the real queue, the scheduler runner, `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn`, the job's stored `toolsAllow`, real tool construction with the embedded runner's allowlist filter, and the real `cron.list` handler. Only the model is controlled.
  - (a) A job allowed to use `automations` reaches the real `cron.list` handler once. It receives the job's restricted caller-scoped inventory, not the admin's view. With the `ops-run.ts` change reverted, this case fails with `operator execution authority is no longer active`.
  - (b) A job whose stored `toolsAllow` is `["read"]` is never offered `automations`, even though the request that started it had `operator.admin`, and the handler is never called. Without the allowlist filter, this case fails.
  - (c) Disabling or removing the job after preparation, before the tool runs, cancels the run. The pending tool call is rejected as aborted and the handler is never called. Without the run abort signal, this case fails.
- After the change, `src/cron/service/run-receipt-settlement.test.ts` expects manual execution to be scheduler-owned, the same as stream, on-exit and startup runs (17/17).
- The failure in `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.recovery.test.ts` is not from this PR. It fails 9/111 on the PR head, on the PR head with the fix reverted, and on clean `main` (`89c0368fe52` and `1f307d61d0f`).
- Test cost, one worker: `pnpm test src/cron/service/ops.operator-lifetime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3 cases, **15.31 s** command wall / 12.41 s Vitest. `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/run.account-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 7 cases, **44.60 s** wall / 42.90 s Vitest including cold compiled-worker preparation; the added negative case takes **309 ms**. Hosted CI seconds are pending.
- Core production and all 27 core-test typecheck graphs pass. Independent autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. No live Gateway, credentials, or automation definition changed during validation.

**Check limitation:** the aggregate changed-file check stops on unused exports in untouched baseline files: `extensions/telegram/src/sequential-key.ts:isTelegramReadOnlyControlLaneText` and `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts:resolveContextTokens`. Their source and scanner configuration are unchanged by this PR; the aggregate is not reported as green. The remaining scoped lint/guards pass when run separately.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes NVIDIA's newly featured models remaining under **All models** while OpenClaw's global recommendations take precedence in model pickers.

title: feat: guide users through the Control UI with visual pointers
body:
Related: #62512

## What Problem This Solves

People asking how to use the Control UI get prose directions instead of seeing the control they need.

## User Impact

Agents can point to real controls, pinned conversations, and visible text with short-lived arrows, outlines, and labeled notes. People keep control of every click; hints do not navigate, type, or steal focus.

**Draft for discussion, not a production rollout.** The result acknowledges dispatch only—not target resolution or a completed user action. Targets are limited to the visible Control UI, not embedded frames or native desktop windows. Missing or ambiguous targets show a waiting label instead of an invented arrow.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extends the existing `screen` / `ui.command` requester-only path rather than adding another core tool. Semantic control IDs, exact session keys, and exact visible text resolve in the browser. Up to four hints replace the current guide; they expire after 30 seconds by default (3–120 seconds), and dismiss on Escape, close, target click, session change, hidden tab, or disconnect. The earlier issue proposed a broader dedicated guide with automatic actions; this deliberately narrower draft adds pointers to the existing session, without a new agent or automatic clicking. Native popover presentation keeps pointers above menus. Crowded layouts fall back to a scrollable instruction list.

Inspired by [big-arrow-on-the-screen](https://github.com/franzenzenhofer/big-arrow-on-the-screen): playful high-contrast pointers, adapted to OpenClaw's interface. No dependency on its macOS executable.

## Evidence

- 41 focused tests pass: screen input/routing (19), Gateway requester isolation (17), and guide lifecycle/layout regressions (5). Combined wrapper wall time: 16.52 seconds; the two new UI regression files take 1.14 seconds including setup.
- Real Control UI walkthrough through the actual screen tool and ui.command handler with a **mock Gateway**, not a live model or production session. Covers Terminal, another panel, pinned session, new-claw menu, Settings, exact text, missing targets, multiple hints, dark mode, a 390px viewport, focus, expiry, and no replay on reload. Screenshot-enabled wall time: 28.82 seconds (13 inspected captures). A capture-free `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` replay passes: 48.16s wrapper wall time, with the browser scenario itself at 2.738s and the five UI regression cases under 0.02s. The normal CI gate is skipped while this PR remains a draft; no hosted test-runtime claim is made.
- Independent autoreview: P0–P2 scoped-clean after fixing the three initial findings. Subsequent edits only made helpers private and normalized braces for lint.
- Core/UI types (including all 27 core test graphs), formatting, oxlint, stylelint, i18n and protocol generation pass. Full `check:changed` is **not green**: its unused-export scan reports `createWhatsAppQaAudioWavBuffer` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/whatsapp/whatsapp-live.media.ts`, unchanged from the starting base. The feature’s test-only export was made private; a repeat scan leaves only that inherited finding. Remaining selected guards ran separately. Full build passes (`pnpm build`, including production Control UI and SDK export validation). The UI build reports an advisory startup-JS size warning: 365.1 KiB gzip versus a 364.7 KiB budget.
- No live Gateway was modified or restarted.

### Example tool calls

```json
{"action":"annotate","annotations":[{"target":{"control":"side-panel"},"text":"Start here. Open your side panel."}]}
```

After the person opens an empty panel:


If it already has tabs, point at `panel-new` first. For a new claw, use `agent-menu` then `agent-new` after the person opens the menu. `{"action":"annotations_clear"}` removes the guide.

title: fix(ui): preserve custom favicons in Firefox
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the selected Agent avatar or Lobsterdex browser tab icon reverting to the red OpenClaw icon in Firefox after an appearance refresh, while the selected setting stays unchanged.

## User Impact

Your chosen tab artwork stays visible through refreshes and activity updates. Default icons and status dots keep their existing behavior; no settings migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Firefox batches favicon candidates and prefers an SVG candidate over a later PNG. During artwork refreshes, a briefly restored default SVG can therefore win over the selected raster icon even though the page's final icon links are correct.

The compositor now embeds its already-rasterized personal artwork in a self-contained SVG, keeping the newest choice equally preferred. This does not embed the original avatar source, change image loading, or add timers, polling, or browser detection.

## Evidence

- Reproduced and verified the repair in **Firefox 155 on Linux with native vertical tabs**, using the actual production Control UI bundle and a mocked Gateway: choose blue Lobsterdex, then change Color mode. Before: the native tab turns red while the setting and DOM icon remain blue. After: the native tab stays blue. Reloads and Agent avatar selection/status updates also verified.

title: fix: compaction keeps stale decisions after corrections
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: compaction can leave superseded dates and pending verification status in its main Decisions section when later corrections are retained as recent-turn or split-turn context.

## User Impact

The compacted handoff updates current decisions and task status instead of presenting contradictory old and corrected facts. Unaffected facts and explicitly historical verbatim excerpts remain available. No configuration change or migration is required.

**Tradeoff:** the reproduced split-turn case now makes two summary requests (main summary plus prefix) rather than one prefix-only request; larger preserved windows can require additional chunks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recent-turn preservation could remove every main-summary target. OpenClaw then copied the stale previous summary through a deterministic fallback, while a separate prefix request merely appended the correction. Strengthening the main prompt alone did not fix a prompt that was never invoked.

The main summary now reconciles the prepared, post-pruning history together with preserved turns and split-turn progress. Instructions require corrections and observed results to update the main sections, distinguish completed failed checks from pending work, and label superseded history. Existing window, pruning, pairing, budget, quality-check, cancellation, and persistence boundaries remain intact. Shared test fixtures were extracted so the regressions do not grow already-oversized files.

## Evidence

- Replayed the supplied correction fixture through real OpenClaw SDK `AgentSession.compact()` using `openai/gpt-6-astra`; disposed/reopened SQLite and inspected the persisted summary. Assessed the saved state against the supplied YAML criteria, not just an assistant reply.

The prompt plus input-routing fix passed **3/3 exact-candidate runs**, and a further compaction retained the corrected facts: Maya remains owner; confirmed launch date October 15; verification ran and failed because approval is missing; preparation unfinished; no pending date-edit task.
- The regression suite passes **85 tests across four files**. The three correction-routing cases failed against unchanged routing. The new cases prove model-input routing; mocked output is not presented as semantic-model proof.
- Scoped formatting/lint, core production and test typechecks, line-cap/max-lines/assertion guards, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Canonical AutoReview completed on the final six-file candidate at P0–P3 with **no actionable findings**. This is independent AI source review, not a human GitHub approval.

**Limits:** this is an available-OpenAI-model SDK replay, not the original Nvidia-model/external-judge run or a Gateway/CLI end-to-end test. It does not establish broad cross-model or long-history reliability. Raw request traces, fixture databases, and private attachments are not included in this PR. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes large automation prompt bubbles crowding the conversation while inter-session updates already use compact activity rows.

Related: #161656 (the existing compact inter-session view).

## User Impact

Each automation input remains separate, including jobs sharing a conversation and repeated session-incarnation IDs. No stored transcript, scheduler, configuration, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing activity renderer and one shared presentation classification for rendering, announcements, reply navigation, and position indexing. Keep inter-session aggregation separate from automation execution boundaries. Recorded automation provenance supplies the history link even when a job runs in an ordinary conversation; the actual source session still owns file links.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iPhone and iPad Safari users see both **Take photo** and **Attach…** in the + menu even though the existing single-picker flow already provides camera, photo-library, and file choices.

## User Impact

The dedicated camera preview, capture/retake controls, and explicit attachment actions remain unchanged on desktop, Android, other iOS browsers, and native app hosts.

title: fix: keep resumed Goals running after Gateway restarts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Goal explicitly resumed by an operator can stop after a Gateway restart instead of continuing automatically.

## User Impact

Resumed Goals retain their authorized restart continuation. Pressing Stop still prevents recovery. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal Resume is an authenticated operator action, but its hidden transcript message is marked as internal. That marker inadvertently excluded the action from restart-authority capture. Classify only the validated Resume operation as operator input for this capture, without changing its transcript provenance. Existing live-authority, scope, execution-lineage, and incognito checks remain in place.

## Evidence

- Strengthened the existing public Goal Resume boundary regression: it fails on the base because the acknowledged Resume has no recovery source, then passes with this fix. The existing hidden-input and idempotency assertions remain intact.
- 83 focused tests pass across Goal chat admission, Goal RPC operations, restart recovery, and requester recovery.
- A real isolated Gateway and production agent, using a synthetic loopback HTTP model, survive two actual process crashes after Resume. Each replacement process automatically makes a new model request; the final response reaches public chat history. A stopped sibling remains killed across both restarts. No manually seeded recovery state or recovery RPC.
- Gateway and root-E2E test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and diff checks pass. Independent autoreview reports no actionable P0–P2 issues, including a complete-context authority-boundary pass.

### Live model and recovered-effect verification

- A separately isolated, compiled Gateway using real OpenAI inference passed public authenticated Goal Resume across process replacement. The recovered model executed its barrier command again and delivered the expected result to public chat history; a stopped sibling did not restart. The live case passed in 39.14 seconds.
- The committed cold-process test now also verifies a real recovered exec write exactly once, plus a separately authenticated operator revoked through public `device.token.revoke` while its recovered model response is held. Releasing that stale tool response produces no filesystem effect, no follow-up provider request, and no success reply; neither stopped nor revoked control resurrects on the next restart. This run passed in 29.54 seconds.
- Revocation occurs during an already-admitted provider request, before subsequent tool/provider effects—not before the initial recovery provider call. The revocation fixture uses a synthetic HTTP model; the separate restart smoke uses a real provider. Gateway and command processes and disposable state were verified removed. Hosting Gateway state was untouched.
- This follow-up changes tests only. Its typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, and fresh P0–P2 independent review passed. The published Git tree matches the tested tree.

title: fix: recover queued follow-ups after missed completion
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a queued follow-up stays stuck behind stale Working/Waiting state when the original browser misses the previous run's completion.

## User Impact

Queued follow-ups can resume after the Gateway reports the previous run idle, without refreshing the browser. Existing queue ordering, edit holds, and steer/interrupt behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

A new queued follow-up now asks the existing serialized outbox owner to reconcile activity from authoritative history. Passive event-driven wakes keep their known-active shortcut, avoiding a large history read on every streaming event. Each foreground reconciliation request is consumed before awaiting history, so a passive rerun cannot reuse it; a new foreground request arriving during the await remains pending. No new timer, persisted state, or Gateway policy is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced in the production-built Control UI: the original browser stayed busy with a local queued follow-up after 65 seconds of virtual time; a fresh browser was idle; refreshing the original released the follow-up exactly once.
- Initial stale-busy reproduction fails on base `d0931ba3d436f91d5793868d51954193e74e9207`. The current two-case work-count regression fails on previous PR head `7bfb0fa86f3aec80cfa13e7059a4ecfa60c6abc6` and passes after the passive-rerun repair.
- Original production browser regression passes: with terminal events withheld and authoritative snapshots idle, Queue sends exactly once without a refresh and removes the stale run display.
- 372 focused outbox/send tests pass on the repaired candidate. UI production and test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass. The exact candidate was built with `pnpm build` and `pnpm ui:build`.
- Independent autoreview of the follow-up repair: scoped-clean for P0–P2. The reported passive-rerun finding is covered by active-history tests with an interleaved passive wake and an additional foreground request.

### Before

The original browser still shows the previous run as active, with the follow-up retained in the local queue.

![Before: stale active run and queued follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d649fb1a-2b44-4ace-8eff-4038814dfffb)

### After

Without refreshing, the follow-up has been sent and the stale previous run is gone. The waiting indicator now belongs to the newly submitted request.

![After: follow-up sent without refreshing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f10d29e6-d60e-48b3-b17e-f2ad9b901a86)

### Isolated live Gateway and model

The screenshots above show the original synthetic-Gateway reproduction. An additional run used the production-built UI, a disposable real Gateway, and the real OpenAI model `gpt-4.1-mini`. No Gateway history or send responses were replaced. At the browser transport, the proof withheld terminal notifications and matching session-row updates; provider responses and RPC traffic were not replaced.

- The original run completed while its follow-up remained queued in the stale browser.
- A new foreground follow-up triggered real authoritative history before the first queued send, on the original connection.
- All three real assistant replies arrived in order: `INITIAL_LIVE_DONE`, `FIRST_FOLLOWUP_LIVE_DONE`, `SECOND_FOLLOWUP_LIVE_DONE`. Exactly three unique sends occurred, with no browser document reload.
- The owned Gateway, synchronization gate, and temporary state were cleaned up.

![Real assistant replies after queued recovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/750d70b5-745f-49a3-9811-3437633caacd)

**Retained live-harness failure:** the extra no-WebSocket-reconnect assertion failed (expected 3 sockets, observed 4). The fourth socket was opened with two sends already recorded: the initial request and first recovered follow-up. Thus authoritative reconciliation and first recovery dispatch happened on the original connection. Browser document identity remained unchanged; FIFO and exactly-once send checks passed. This is not a fully passing live-harness run.

**Failure classification after bounded source/artifact inspection:** the injector also withheld matching `sessions.changed` / `session.message` updates until recovery dispatch. Browser connections negotiate session-row deltas; suppressing those updates can leave their connection-owned baseline stale even though transport sequence numbers are preserved. The unchanged [row decoder and reconnect owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a7b188e241b9b22eabaa1bf516805c0927131a5c/ui/src/api/gateway-chat-events.ts#L69-L76) intentionally reconnect on a missing baseline, with [existing regression coverage](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a7b188e241b9b22eabaa1bf516805c0927131a5c/ui/src/api/gateway-session-row-events.node.test.ts#L193-L221). This provides a concrete injection-induced explanation, not evidence of an outbox regression or a no-reconnect product requirement. The retained run lacks close code/reason and per-frame timestamps, so the exact trigger remains unconfirmed. No live replay, weaker assertion, or production-guard change was used to claim green; the original failure and this uncertainty are retained under the test-failure policy. The original cause of missed terminal delivery and a live rate-limit trigger remain unproven.

Thanks to @steipete for initiating and directing this reliability audit.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a31b883-0124-4d45-8df4-9f83973e9f4a)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/914884fa-b8ca-454c-9dd2-aa33aacbe7ee)

## Worked on by

- @steipete

title: feat: preview Control UI themes before applying them
body:
Related: #151479 (reuse of shared radio/option-card controls; this does not complete the consolidation tracker).

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing a Control UI theme needs a compact, keyboard-friendly way to try it across the window before saving, including matching colors in the embedded terminal.

## User Impact

Users can hover, focus, or tap a theme to preview the current window; Apply theme or Enter saves it, while Cancel, Escape, or leaving Appearance restores the current selection. Other windows and saved preferences are unchanged during preview. All 11 built-in names/IDs are preserved, with palette descriptions and Beacon identified as the high-contrast option.

Arrow keys browse, Home/End jump, and Space previews without saving. The visible keyboard guide is scoped to the picker, not text fields. Plugin and personal palettes use the existing catalog, including cancellation when a previewed plugin disappears.

Themes may optionally author 16 ANSI colors. Existing terminals and scrollback repaint without restarting the shell; explicit true-color output remains application-owned. No database migration or operator configuration change is required. The approved temporary ghostty-web 0.4.0 repair includes rebuilt embedded WASM and generated ESM/CJS/declarations, with pinned sources, hashes, rebuild instructions, and removal gates in patches/README.md and the packaged source patches.

This is Omarchy-inspired groundwork, not an official collaboration or an installed Catppuccin/Tokyo Night theme pack. New wallpapers, continuous animation, and external CLI theming are outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing application theme owner now holds transient preview state separately from canonical preferences and rejects stale palette completion after cancellation. The picker reuses shared native radio navigation instead of adding a second keyboard model; the real window is the preview surface rather than a floating miniature. Preview and commit share the font/accent reset policy.

The terminal updates native color defaults directly rather than injecting OSC into the PTY parser, preserving split escape sequences and active-theme reset baselines. The canvas also paints literal-black cell backgrounds correctly. Existing clipboard-success and disposal repairs remain intact. Most patch bytes are reproducibly generated dependency output, not a second terminal implementation.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI browser flow: window preview, all scoped navigation keys, explicit Apply/Enter, Escape/Cancel/route exit, no writes before Apply, a second window retaining its selection, touch, plugin preview/withdrawal, and saved-profile persistence.
- Chromium Appearance consumer suite: 20 tests. Focused keyboard/preview consumer also passed in WebKit. Focused owner/preference/configuration suites: 169 tests, including late palette completion and Gateway-scope retirement. Contrast matrix retains AA, with Beacon AAA for the sampled text pairs.
- Full terminal browser suite: 6 cases, including cold authored palettes, live reload/fallback, clipboard outcomes, input, memory isolation, and disposal. Native regressions cover all 16 colors, scrollback, explicit RGB, cursor preservation, fragmented CSI/OSC, and reset defaults.
- The literal-black canvas regression was red before the renderer repair and green afterward: SGR 40 paints [0,0,0], while untouched default background remains [30,30,46]. A fresh-store frozen install reproduced both generated runtime formats and the native WASM hash.
- UI production typecheck, scoped lint/style/format, docs MDX, and i18n verification passed. Independent P0-P2 review is scoped-clean after resolving the black-background finding. PR CI provides the broad suite; no remote CI or whole-repository typecheck success is claimed.

- After GitHub reported an actual conflict, integrated main at `c64eaf54ad0b609a114d580e29135acd93433bfd`. Kept the new canonical Settings preference owner rather than restoring duplicate bindings. On that exact base, all 9 browser cases, affected Settings/preview owner regressions, UI production typecheck, scoped lint/format, and fresh P0-P2 review passed. The integrated After capture is byte-identical to the image below. Earlier unchanged-contract proof is retained, not relabeled as remote CI.

- Hosted-review follow-up: completed the remaining browser-only `ApplicationTheme` fixture and corrected the radio test callback's return contract. The UI-components test typecheck leaf now passes, along with that browser test and all 5 shared-radio tests. These follow-up edits are test-only; production behavior and the inspected images are unchanged.

Existing persisted preference and theme-definition shapes are unchanged, and ANSI tokens are optional. A full v2026.10.6-to-candidate upgrade run was not performed; it remains an explicit qualification gap rather than a claimed pass.

The earlier editor/test type graph (before base integration) reported errors in untouched native-desktop, quota-reset, and regexp declaration inputs. That broad graph was not rerun or claimed fixed; this is not a clean full-project gate run. No live Gateway was modified or deployed. Browser evidence uses synthetic Gateway fixtures.

### Visual walkthrough

**Revision provenance for every Before/After comparison below:**

- **Before = main at [d75915ee88343c26565b6855fde235525d112ba3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d75915ee88343c26565b6855fde235525d112ba3)**, fetched into an isolated, clean checkout for this recapture.
- **After = pushed PR head [da36d69fe3933fe1675201b26622972a7327b066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/da36d69fe3933fe1675201b26622972a7327b066)**. The capture checkout's Git tree exactly matches the published commit tree (777b6ea8a27dab54d4656a994a92fe40f70177fc); it contains no unpublished product changes.

Both revisions ran the same scenario script and synthetic Gateway fixtures with matching viewport, locale, color scheme, and reduced-motion settings. Each used its own dependency installation and lockfile. These are real rendered Control UI captures, not design mockups or previous design iterations. Fixture footer version/build strings are synthetic; the source revisions above identify the code being compared. No code was pushed for this description/evidence update.

**How to read the picker:** the checkmark identifies the saved theme; the highlighted/focused radio identifies the preview target. “Previewing … — not saved” is an unsaved window-local state. “Current: …” and disabled Apply/Cancel mean there is no pending theme choice.

#### Main versus PR: hover Tide while Claw is saved

Identical action on both revisions: open Appearance with Claw selected, then hover Tide. Both use a 1440 × 1200 viewport.

**Before — main d75915ee: hover/tooltip only; the window stays Claw**

![Before on current-main snapshot d75915ee: hovering Tide leaves the window in Claw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f2e11f8-783a-498c-880c-bfc786c8bffc)

**After — pushed PR da36d69: the whole window previews Tide, with Claw still saved**

![After on pushed PR da36d69: hovering Tide previews the whole window without saving](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efeee2cf-26ea-48d6-b44d-74f88b96d688)

| Same action | Main d75915ee | Pushed PR da36d69 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hover Tide | Window remains Claw; 0 theme-selection requests | Window previews Tide; 0 theme-selection requests |
| Click Tide | Window changes to Tide and sends 1 theme-selection request | Window previews Tide but sends 0 theme-selection requests |
| Separate commit step | None: selecting the theme commits it | Apply/Enter commits the preview; Cancel/Escape restores the saved theme |

The comparison scenarios asserted these rendered states and request counts on both revisions. The PR preview includes typography as well as colors, so surrounding copy can rewrap; the captures do not normalize away that layout change.

#### PR-only state and persistence walkthrough

The following gallery and state sequence are **all from pushed PR head da36d69**. They illustrate individual PR interaction states, not additional main-versus-PR comparisons. This separate PR-state capture checked the rendered window, browser preference mirror, and outgoing **themes.set** requests:

| Action | Window displays | Saved theme | Theme-selection writes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Claw | Claw | 0 |
| Hover/focus Tide | Tide, unsaved | Claw | 0 |
| Escape | Claw restored; focus retained | Claw | 0 |
| Preview Tide again, then Apply | Tide, current | Tide | 1 |
| End from the picker | Miami, unsaved | Tide | still 1 |
| Escape from that keyboard preview | Tide restored | Tide | still 1 |
| Tap Tide in a fresh mobile scenario | Tide, unsaved | Claw | 0 |

Cancel and leaving Appearance use the same saved-selection restoration path. Applying uses the existing preference owner; it does not create a separate theme engine. Other browser windows do not inherit the transient preview.

**Important scope distinction:** Light/Dark/System retain their existing immediate preference behavior; the new Apply button stages the **theme choice**, not every Appearance setting. The light-mode image below is after explicitly choosing Light, not a claim that Cancel rolls color mode back.

**Observed interaction edge for review (not fixed by this metadata-only update):** after Escape, leaving and returning to the exact previous pointer coordinates can leave the saved theme visible until another in-card movement, focus change, or click. The capture reproduced this, then explicitly clicked Tide to continue. It is not presented as repaired behavior.

<details>
<summary>PR-only gallery: saved, Cancel/Escape, and applied states</summary>

**New picker at rest — Claw saved, no pending choice**

![New picker at rest with Current Claw and Apply/Cancel disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6a58fa5-acfd-44fc-97a9-44ca1a691949)

**Escape state on the PR — Claw restored, Tide still has keyboard focus**

The focus outline is not a saved-selection indicator. The Claw checkmark and “Current: Claw” remain authoritative; no theme-selection write occurred.

![Escape restores Claw while retaining focus on Tide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c23b668-56ef-4534-bbef-9b9bd08b46c5)

**Applied state on the PR — saved checkmark moves to Tide**

“Current: Tide” replaces the unsaved-preview status. Apply/Cancel are disabled again. The capture observed one theme-selection request and the saved mirror changed to Tide.

![Applied Tide with saved checkmark and Current Tide status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8d31de4-37f6-4de2-98b2-cbb7f9950554)

</details>

<details>
<summary>PR-only gallery: keyboard navigation, light mode, and touch layout</summary>

**Keyboard — End previews Miami while Tide stays saved**

The actual window and typography change, the Miami focus/preview target is visible, and the saved checkmark remains on Tide. The same run exercised Home, ArrowRight, and Escape and verified no additional theme-selection request.

![Keyboard End previews Miami while saved selection remains Tide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d17a31d-f249-42e5-b1db-5273a3d37d00)

| Key, with focus in the picker | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Move through choices and preview |
| Home / End | First / last choice |
| Space | Preview without saving |
| Enter | Apply the focused choice |
| Escape | Restore the saved theme, retaining focus |
| Tab | Normal navigation into/out of the native radio group and actions |

These bindings do not intercept the import URL field or other text inputs; that boundary is exercised by the browser flow.

**Light mode — applied Tide, with real light palette swatches**

![Applied Tide in Light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/168e1254-8cbf-483a-9df6-98c6daf51bd7)

title: fix: allow retry after Side chat times out
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a timed-out Side chat question offers no Retry action and can release its source context before the canceled run finishes cleanup.

## User Impact

User impact: timed-out questions can be retried after cleanup, without losing earlier answers or appending a late answer. The 60-second execution deadline and 1,200-character answer budget are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return a typed, retryable timeout and keep the request's source facts and busy slot alive until internal-session execution and cleanup settle. Ordinary requests still time out promptly while waiting only for context. This matches the existing incognito lifetime rule without adding another cleanup owner.

A provider that ignores cancellation can still delay settlement; this change does not increase the execution budget or diagnose the original slow answer.

## Evidence

- Red on the base, green with the fix: typed timeout recovery and the real RPC/native-session path retaining source authority through cancellation, cleanup, late-answer suppression, and successful retry.
- Five Side chat suites: 64 tests passed, plus the incognito source-lifetime sibling test. Final changed-file runs: 25/25 and 18/18 passed (51.69s and 19.82s wrapper wall time). The one new regression took 1.32s; no new fixture or suite.
- Production and Gateway-test typechecks; targeted lint/format; documentation MDX/Markdown checks; diff sanity passed. Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- The broad changed-test graph selector hit pre-existing graph-size limits (725/729 roots vs. 720); the matching Gateway test graph passed directly instead.
- The initial production-path regression uses a controlled model loop; the real-provider confirmation below covers the production execution path. The original slow-answer cause remains unknown. No UI layout changes.

### Rendered timeout recovery

Production Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses: the old timeout has no Retry action; the new typed timeout exposes Retry. The browser test also clicks Retry, verifies the recovered answer stays in place, preserves earlier Side chat and main-chat content, and observes no main-chat sends or resets. One focused browser test passed (3.07s; production build plus test 31.28s). This proves rendered recovery behavior, not the cause of the original live-provider timeout.

Screenshots embedded below: **Before** (first image, no Retry action) and **After** (second image, Retry available).

### Real-provider deadline and recovery

A newly created, isolated Gateway and its actual production Control UI ran against OpenAI GPT-4.1 mini on head `1e5f238116932acde951cb1a2796abf965c90860`. All six provider requests completed upstream with HTTP 200. A local relay deliberately withheld one genuine provider response; neither Gateway RPC responses nor model output were synthesized.

The unchanged deadline returned the typed, retryable timeout after **60.254 seconds**. The Gateway canceled the held request and completed cleanup before exposing Retry. Releasing the held response afterward could not deliver a late answer. Clicking the actual UI Retry button made a new real-provider request and answered the contextual question correctly (Thursday), in place. The earlier Side chat answer (Friday) and main-chat transcript were preserved; no reset or extra main-chat send occurred.

The focused live browser test passed (74.39s; runner 153.80s). Process exit, isolated state deletion, relay closure, and a clean source worktree were verified. Only the disposable Gateway was started/stopped; the hosting Gateway was not modified. The third image below shows the actual recovered live-provider result.

**Limit:** latency was deliberately induced. This verifies deadline, cancellation, cleanup, and Retry behavior—not the cause of the original slow answer.

Credit: @steipete for requesting the reliability audit and repair.

title: fix(cron): preserve final replies after automation self-removal
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled operator continuation loses its final reply when it removes its own follow-up automation.

## User Impact

Automations can clean up their own schedule and finish replying. Removing or disabling a job from another turn, or pressing Stop, still cancels its active run. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion retired the job's source row before the post-commit ownership check, so the legitimate removing run was treated as an operator cancellation. Keep full caller/source validation before the mutation, then recognize only the exact still-live admitted run after commit. Its continuation keeps the existing live operator, session, and delivery checks without requiring the deleted definition to remain present.

This reuses the existing occurrence marker, removal guard, and delivery fence; no new scheduler mode or state owner. The admission assertion's type now preserves its existing scope-only check. Net production growth is 18 lines; the regression coverage adds 76 lines.

## Evidence

- The real scheduled shared-session/Gateway-tool regression fails on base `d0931ba3d436f` with `Cron job removed by operator.`, then passes with this repair and a successful completion summary.
- Fresh disposable Gateway built at exact head `88c03ac0a835a7387239b8b475e10b571222937d`, real OpenAI `gpt-4.1`: the agent created a disabled same-conversation automation; a forced run removed it; the final assistant reply was readable through public `chat.history`; the job was absent from `cron.list`. Separate live streaming runs proved both Control UI's session-owned Stop RPC (`sessions.abort` with the exact run) and external `cron.remove` produce failed completion receipts, with no final reply. The three-scenario fixture passed in 26.73 seconds of test execution (84.77 seconds total); the owned Gateway and disposable state were verified removed. This exercises public RPCs, not browser clicks. No live operator state was changed.
- Post-removal authority proof uses real scheduler, admission, source-restoration, session-state, and publication-action owners with synthetic model/GitHub I/O. Self-removal precedes inspect/merge: current authority permits the expected merge PUT; committing operator-role revocation or source-session replacement during awaited preflight rejects with zero PUTs. This follow-up changes tests only.
- All 16 continuation cases passed on the updated tree (70.57 seconds wall time, 33.16 seconds test execution). This owner composition is needed to check final I/O. The earlier 90-test run covers companion self-removal/admission boundaries, including closed, aborted, copied, stale, and other-run guards.
- Core types plus cron, agent-root, and Gateway-method test type graphs passed. Changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent autoreviews of the implementation and the post-removal proof found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

The composer documentation does not distinguish source-supported video preparation paths from the device, audio, and mixed-track compatibility evidence that is still missing.

title: fix: prevent duplicate optional-question answers across viewers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate optional-question answer popups and submissions when several viewers share a conversation, including when the first answer is queued.

## User Impact

The first accepted answer is shared across panes and reloads as **Answer queued** or **Answer sent**. A stale second submit does not send another message. Normal typed corrections remain ordinary messages. Explicitly withdrawing a queued answer makes the question answerable again; interrupted custody does not release it. There are no new configuration options or database migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the canonical question reference with the existing input and enforce uniqueness through its authoritative actor state before queued or direct custody. Incognito public staging applies the same guard at its storage-command effect. Shared presentation derives from accepted inputs, and confirmed withdrawal releases the submitting pane’s retained hint even when cancellation redacts the message. There is no separate question registry. The follow-up simplifies the SQL guard and consolidates repeated fixtures and scenarios.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original duplicate popup, retained-pane withdrawal, and previously missed public incognito staging path before fixing them. Two consolidated shared-state Chromium scenarios plus 15 existing scenarios passed: **17 total**, covering mounted viewers, confirmed queue removal, stale-submit reconciliation, outbox retirement, reload, and canonical confirmation.
- **65 focused backend/storage tests across five files passed.** Public durable/incognito active/idle cases race two answers, retry the actual winner, reject same or contradictory stale submits, distinguish cancellation from interruption, and preserve invalid-source rejection, ordinary corrections, and new same-worded questions.
