title: improve(ui): download about 3.3% less JavaScript over gzip
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/121497. Preserves the Brotli quality-10 improvement in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180972.

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI clients using gzip download more JavaScript than necessary with the current build-time encoder.

## User Impact

**About 3.3% less complete-route JavaScript over gzip, with identical decoded assets and unchanged requests.** Brotli quality 10, HTTP encoding, browser code, and performance budgets are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

The tradeoff is build-only CPU: the measured gzip stage adds about 2.27 seconds wall / 2.19 CPU-seconds per 40.3 MB corpus. This is not a page-load latency claim. The new dependency is an exact, integrity-pinned WASM package, not a host-native library; cross-OS validation and reproducible upstream WASM compilation are not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `libdeflate@0.1.0` at one uniform level 11 in the existing sidecar producer. Level 12 saves only another 1,685 bytes over all 2,076 top-level JavaScript/CSS assets while costing about 1.56 seconds more per encoding pass. Keep final-on-disk input reads, source-map exclusions, four-at-a-time compression and joined failure cleanup, and existing cache invalidation. Pako remains only as a development/test comparison, not an alternative production encoder.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, set before measurements: meaningful gzip savings around 3% at initial entry, ready New Session/Chat, and first session creation; identical decoded assets/request graph and Brotli; unchanged strict gates. Compare actual portable levels 11/12 on the same current-main build, not previous native-library measurements.

Source baseline: `6893519fbd6062612b2c0c9e809369608b3aadc2`. Same-source production builds, Linux x64, Node 26.12.1. Browser rows use the real production HTTP handler/background file owner over loopback, fresh Chromium contexts, gzip responses, synthetic RPCs and a valid strict-JSON config fixture. They are not live-provider/full-Gateway authorization tests.

| JavaScript workload | Requests (unchanged) | Pako baseline | WASM level 11 | Savings |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial entry | 7 | 315,952 B | 305,152 B | 3.418% |
| Ready New Session | 20 | 957,289 B | 925,674 B | 3.303% |
| Ready Chat | 25 | 1,421,151 B | 1,374,486 B | 3.284% |
| New Session → first created chat, cumulative | 32 | 1,542,453 B | 1,491,728 B | 3.289% |

- Browser captures have identical asset paths/raw bytes/Brotli bytes, zero page/request failures, and a usable composer after first creation. Every requested JS/CSS gzip response matches its sidecar and decodes to the original file.
- All **2,080 gzip + 2,080 Brotli sidecars** decode identically. Every gzip sidecar re-encodes byte-identically on **Node 24.22.1 and 26.12.1, Linux x64**; gzip headers contain no time/name/host variation. All raw runtime assets and Brotli bytes are unchanged. One diagnostic Mermaid sourcemap varies only in generated Rolldown reference IDs; maps have no compression sidecars. No encoder code appears in browser source maps.
- `pnpm build`, actual UI builds, unchanged strict `pnpm ui:check-performance`, sidecar validation, targeted UI-config/test typecheck, focused lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Canonical `pnpm test` runs all **55 tests in four config/precompression/cache/build files** successfully (68.38 s wall, including artifact-lock waits). The changed stronger-gzip regression is red on base (25,158 is not less than 25,158) and green on the candidate. Test CI seconds are pending.
- A subsequent build reuses the content cache and preserves the new sidecars (3.61 s, including validation). The configuration, UI manifest and lockfile already belong to the cache key; no new cache exists.
- **Completed independent AutoReview:** Codex AutoReview, P0–P2, full compression/build/cache-owner context: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer checked source and supplied evidence, not independently rerun tests. Cross-OS/architecture and upstream compiler reproducibility remain unverified. Landing was subsequently requested; no deployment is requested.

Hosted review also completed on the exact published head with no findings or before-merge items: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181047#issuecomment-6353144105.

CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39866290791 (attempt 1) remains failed: its sole non-aggregate failure is the native-plugin composer footer test in checks-ui-e2e (1/9). The test still expects the shadow pseudo-element removed on its main baseline by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181017. Main independently corrected these exact stale assertions in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181063. The classification table says new because the older matching scheduled-main job passed without comparing selected scope; this is not being called matching-signature evidence. Landing preparation retains the failed attempt and inspected source/checkout evidence for the native inherited-failure route, not a green CI claim. All 69 reported jobs are terminal: 43 passed, 24 skipped, two failures including the downstream gate, zero cancelled.

<details>
<summary>Portable encoder qualification and timing details</summary>

Exact npm integrity matches the lockfile. The MIT license includes wrapper and upstream attribution. The [published source revision](https://codeberg.org/EvanHahn/libdeflate.js/src/commit/a5f02605f65b67c9d094f1f4a5cbafe38c226969) pins [libdeflate 1.25](https://github.com/ebiggers/libdeflate/tree/c8c56a20f8f621e6a966b716b31f1dedab6a41e3). Its checked-in Emscripten recipe produces single-file, synchronous WASM with no filesystem dependency; the npm package has no production dependencies or install script. Compiler version is not pinned upstream, and the distributed binary was not independently rebuilt. Package age admission passed without an override. This is not the earlier native libdeflate 1.23 experiment.

`node ui/scripts/bench-gzip.mjs <built-dist> 5`: 2,076 top-level JS/CSS files, 40,263,998 raw bytes. Five serial interleaved passes per encoder; decode/hashing and file I/O outside the timer. Shared host: 128 available CPUs, initial load 42.27/27.75/20.98.

| Encoder | Total gzip bytes | Wall median / p95 (range), seconds | CPU median / p95, seconds |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Pako 9, legacy hash, memLevel 6 | 12,180,203 | 2.964 / 3.356 (2.942–3.356) | 3.038 / 3.362 |
| **WASM libdeflate 11** | **11,750,210** | **5.232 / 5.370 (5.157–5.370)** | **5.232 / 5.384** |
| WASM libdeflate 12 | 11,748,525 | 6.796 / 7.509 (6.590–7.509) | 6.789 / 7.278 |

Level 11 saves 429,993 B / 3.530% across this corpus. Eleven tiny assets grow by just 13 bytes combined (maximum 3 B); no per-file policy/fallback is added. Full standalone builds were 47.56 s baseline and 29.12 s candidate on a busy shared host, **one run each**; that variance does not establish a build speedup. The encoder-only paired measurement is the cost comparison.

Strict build-manifest route accounting independently passes: New Session 953,681 → 922,126 B at 19 requests; Chat 1,417,543 → 1,370,938 B at 24 requests. Browser-ready captures above include the additional observed runtime request instead of hiding it.

Simplification: replace the encoder call at its existing owner, with no new production state, worker, configuration, or serving path. The additional script exists only to make the encoder cost/size comparison repeatable; existing regression suites retain lifecycle and cache proof.

</details>

Credit: Requested by @jacobtomlinson.

title: fix(ui): pinned sessions cannot be reordered and guest drags fail
body:
Related: #178066, #143909, #179023

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: guests cannot drag sessions onto the navigation rail, and dropping a session inside Pinned never changes its order.

## User Impact

User impact: users, including guests, can drag eligible sessions onto the rail and reorder personal pins above or below another row. The order survives reload, including for saved pins outside the loaded session list; rail shortcuts remain independent. Shared-group moves and section reordering retain their existing access checks. No migration or permission upgrade is required. Read-only connections retain the existing browser-local persistence behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session rows incorrectly required shared-group write access to start any drag. Permit pin-eligible rows to start dragging while retaining destination authorization.

Pinned accepted only section-level drops, which called “pin this session” again and did nothing for an existing pin. Top-level Pinned rows now supply a before/after insertion target to the existing organizer and canonical personal-preference writer. This reuses the rail's drop indicator and insertion logic without adding state, storage, permissions, or a second ordering owner. Self-drops are consumed without moving the pin; nested child rows are not reorder targets. A personal-pin drop can also resolve its source through the current pin projection when the session is absent from the loaded roster. Shared-group drops keep their original loaded-row lookup and pin eligibility is still checked.

#178066 is the reported UX context, not a proven introduction point. #143909 identified the older drag-permission gate; #179023 proposes a broader alternative pin-placement implementation. This PR repairs the current Solid sidebar's rail dragging and within-Pinned ordering. Personal groups remain separate work.

## Visual evidence

Same mouse gesture with `operator.sessions.read`: drag Research notes above Reliability Tracker.

### Before

Research notes remains last.

![Before: dragging does not reorder personal pins](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfadc021-4ab3-4524-93d6-3c398a7fb43d)

### After

Research notes moves first; the existing rail shortcut is unchanged.

![After: the dropped pin occupies its chosen position](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dedf7d6f-d3e7-4aaf-aaa5-3c2523d2079f)

<details>
<summary>Original rail-drag evidence</summary>

Before: no shortcut appears with `operator.read`.

![Before: dragging to the rail has no effect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df1a0da9-67f4-42c2-a64f-5e4178cdeb91)

After: the shortcut appears while the full Pinned row remains.

![After: dragging creates an independent rail shortcut](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/936c3de0-26ae-4b50-bacd-b2e7557c7c23)

</details>

## Evidence

- Rail regression: the original base `7951d383ff29c37aacf804ef715222e948a8d119` renders restricted rows non-draggable; Chromium cannot create a shortcut.
- Reordering regression: the previously published rail-only implementation still leaves Research notes last after a native mouse drag to the first position. The same Chromium scenario passes with this repair.
- 244 affected component tests pass: sidebar interactions, sessions, rail, and row rendering. The new regression covers before/after placement, self-drop, inserting an unpinned session, preserving unrelated/unknown navigation entries, and no shared-group/session mutations.
- All 5 Chromium flows pass: admin and `operator.sessions.read` reorder in both directions, self-drop, reload persistence, and independent rail shortcuts; an additional `operator.sessions.read` case exercises three visible descriptor-only pins excluded from `sessions.list`; admin and `operator.read` retain the original rail-drag/add/remove behavior. Browser proof uses the actual Control UI against a synthetic Gateway, not the reporter's live connection.
- UI production and test typechecks, targeted lint (0 errors; 5 pre-existing reactivity warnings), formatting, production bundle, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Follow-up regression on `21ddd965b8718271ee8175b64910e1afe0140437`: a descriptor-only pin was visible and draggable but retained its old order. Both the sidebar component test (cross-agent descriptor) and real Chromium off-page scenario reproduced this failure, and pass with the scoped projection lookup. No shared mutation is emitted.
- Auto Review: scoped-clean at the configured P0 threshold. Independent behavioral review's descriptor-only P2 finding is resolved; no new actionable P1/P2 finding was identified.
- Test cost: affected component suite, 244 tests, 25.59s wall; browser file, 5 tests, 206.41s wall including bundle/setup and shared build-lock waiting (42.46s in the five scenario bodies). CI seconds for the updated head are not yet available.
- Simplification: existing preference writer, drag state, and insertion styles reused. Production delta is +69 net lines; growth supplies the missing row target and event routing. No new state owner or schema.


The attribution and verification history below is retained from the original rail-only revision; the current candidate's results and screenshots are above.

## Worked on by

- Related earlier drag-permission work: @RomneyDa in #143909.

## Evidence

- Fixed: 222 affected sidebar component tests pass across `app-sidebar.interactions`, `app-sidebar.sessions`, and `app-sidebar-rail`.

title: fix: collapse scheduled prompts in conversation history
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: internal scheduled prompts fill the conversation when an automation continues work in an existing session.

## User Impact

Automation prompts stay collapsed while normal replies and human messages remain visible. Existing recorded prompts are fixed on display without modifying transcript history. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

title: feat: configure custom model endpoints in Settings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Settings → Models can manage provider credentials but cannot define or edit an independent custom inference endpoint.

## User Impact

Administrators connected locally to the Gateway can add, edit, and delete independent endpoints, configure multiple models, discover compatible model IDs, and manage saved keys separately. Adding an endpoint does not change the default model.

The first stage supports Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages. Remote endpoint changes remain unsupported; the server preserves the existing verified-local-client boundary. Anonymous authentication remains limited to effective Chat Completions routes. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor separates endpoint definitions from credential-only provider sign-in. It uses the existing configuration writer, revision checks, secret restoration, and credential owners rather than another configuration store.

Existing models submit explicit field edits, preserving omitted metadata, advanced settings, SecretRefs, pricing, and model-level API/base-URL overrides. Configured references must be resolved before removing models/endpoints; endpoint deletion does not remove stored credentials. Official provider and OAuth setup flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

That integration is a normal merge of prior feature head `33ae8050b34fa441fe5b87de9966a068ccc52478` and pinned main `d4ae77eae296fd8eb1f90f7a4ebb5d77fa2e6ad9`, preserving genuine feature history. No original feature PR has been merged into main.

title: improve(ui): download over 5% less JavaScript with Brotli
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI clients negotiating Brotli download more JavaScript than necessary at the current compression setting.

## User Impact

**About 5 extra seconds in build compression saves over 5% of complete-route JavaScript downloaded by Brotli clients, with an identical decoded application.** Gzip downloads and their budgets are unchanged. This improves existing Brotli q9, not a switch from gzip to Brotli. No migration or user action is required; existing cached responses remain valid.

## Why This Change Was Made

Raise the existing build-time Brotli encoder from quality 9 to 10 and update its regression expectation. Keep the same assets, four-at-a-time compression, gzip options, serving/cache contracts, and runtime. No dependency or budget changes. Jacob explicitly accepted the compression-stage time/CPU tradeoff. Quality 11 saves more bytes but its single measured run costs substantially more, so quality 10 is the measured compromise.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: reduce complete cold-route JS response-body bytes by more than 5% versus Brotli q9 on both New Session and Chat, preserving decoded bytes and gzip; accept approximately 5 seconds of additional compression-stage wall time. No UI latency claim.

Measurements below use source **d91197ecafe60db4b85561472ec849b69760cd92**, Node 26.12.1 / Brotli 1.2.0, the same 2,078 assets / 40,265,078 raw bytes, concurrency 4, and retained gzip generation. Five interleaved q9/q10 samples; **q11 is ONE sample**. These are **compression-stage** timings (including verification/file bookkeeping), not full-build times or UI latency. The busy shared host had 1-minute load approximately 24–74; these are not clean-host latency estimates or an exact full-build percentage.

| Brotli quality | Complete /new JS | Savings vs q9 | Complete /chat JS | Savings vs q9 | Compression-stage wall median (range) | CPU median | Samples |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 9 (baseline) | 940,046 B | — | 1,307,266 B | — | 8.734 s (6.913–11.409) | 13.878 CPU-s | 5 |
| **10 (selected)** | **885,989 B** | **54,057 B / 5.750%** | **1,233,638 B** | **73,628 B / 5.632%** | **13.456 s (11.742–16.213)** | **20.887 CPU-s** | **5** |
| 11 (one sample, not a median) | 870,116 B | 69,930 B / 7.439% | 1,209,871 B | 97,395 B / 7.450% | 29.432 s | 46.310 CPU-s | **1** |

q10 adds 4.72 s wall / 7.01 CPU-s to stage medians. q11's one sample is approximately 20.7 s above q9's median and 16.0 s above q10's median. Gzip stays /new 1,020,987 B and /chat 1,426,355 B; initial JS stays 316,034 B gzip. These are complete-route JS totals, not merely the entry chunk or all-page resources. Requests remain 22 /new and 27 /chat. The first slash/emoji union workload also improves: 1,412,580 B → 1,332,720 B (5.653%); nothing moves after readiness.

- Prior investigation production-compressor replay (not a fresh full-build comparison): all 4,156 sidecars decode identically; 4,970 non-Brotli files (including gzip) byte-identical; no source-map sidecars. Browser fixture replay: same JS requests, HTTP 200 + Content-Encoding br, zero page errors.
- Prior real production HTTP handler + background file owner over loopback: 31 unique JS assets / 97 requests; br/gzip/identity body equality, HEAD length, 304, 406, Vary and immutable caching pass. This was **not** a full Gateway with a real agent/provider. No claim of live-provider or cross-browser coverage.
- Implementation verification: updated regression fails against q9, then all 42 focused config/precompression/cache tests pass with q10. Actual UI production build and all-sidecar validation pass; unchanged strict gzip performance budgets pass. UI typecheck, two-file lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and diff whitespace checks pass. Independent AutoReview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, medium; P0–P2) returned scoped-clean with no actionable findings; its source-only scope did not independently execute tests or remeasure route sizes.
- Fresh production build reproduces the exact measured route totals above (22/27 JS requests). 6,802 asset files match the replay candidate; four copied plugin-distribution Brotli sidecars differ but decode identically, and one diagnostic sourcemap differs. This is not a claim that two separate full builds are byte-identical.
- Prior-pin measurements are retained as that pin's evidence, not relabeled current-main measurements. Refreshed remote main cf2558f5639e273dc4fe1f19e9c5f7715dc8d0de has unchanged compressor, regression and lockfile inputs. This nonvisual encoding-only change has no appearance change; no screenshots are needed.

Reproduction entrypoints: `pnpm --dir ui test src/app/vite-precompression.node.test.ts src/app/vite-config.node.test.ts src/app/vite-config-cache.node.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; `pnpm ui:build`; `node scripts/check-control-ui-precompressed-assets.mts dist/control-ui`. The timing table is the retained interleaved investigation measurement, not a timed full-build benchmark.


Hosted CI [run 39852611719, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39852611719) reported an unrelated Claw creator retry/publication failure in `creator-review.e2e.test.ts:204` (`checks-ui-e2e (3/9)`: expected two publish requests, observed one). That test explicitly uses a private Vite **source server**, bypassing the build compression changed here; its test, Claw implementation and source-server inputs are unchanged in the actual CI merge. A bounded exact-head replay passes (1/1), which is **not** a claim the failure is fixed. The failure remains recorded; no CI rerun or source push is used to chase green. Landing is proceeding only through the native attributed inherited-failure path, with security and enforced review gates unchanged.

Simplification: smallest complete change, one production setting plus its existing regression; 3 additions / 3 deletions, no new machinery or tests.

Credit: Requested and tradeoff approved by @jacobtomlinson.

title: fix: preserve accepted chat turns during restart recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted chat input being skipped during Gateway restart recovery when another saved update cannot be delivered.

## User Impact

Accepted chat turns can reach the model in order instead of failing before their first request. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The blocked-delivery warning is hidden from model context but still advances transcript ancestry. Writing it while a recovered turn is preparing can close that turn's already-persisted input. The existing session lifecycle owner now waits non-preemptively for the selected turn before writing the warning; keyed-user, cancellation, live-authority and durable-notice-before-withdrawal guards remain unchanged. A warning can therefore wait for the current session turn to settle.

## Evidence

- Deterministic owning-boundary regression: the real report writer, controller and native keyed-user append reproduce the exact failure on the base, then pass with the fix.
- Recovery owner suite: **47/47 passed** (47.88 s wrapper wall). Latest import-only correction: focused case **2.041 s**, **15.55 s wrapper wall**; targeted typecheck, lint and formatting passed.
- Existing isolated Gateway process proof: **SIGTERM 63.344 s**, **SIGKILL 37.336 s**, both passed without weakened assertions; total wrapper wall 254.34 s including build/transform preparation. These unchanged-production proofs were reused after the direct-owner test-import correction and patch-identical fast-forward base updates.
- Canonical independent P0–P2 review reported **scoped-clean**, complete assessment with 20 intact context files. It did not independently execute tests.
- Source-bound guard checks passed for line caps, assertions, DB worker/dialect, timeout races, mock exports, conflicts, schema version, legacy stores, sidecar loaders and import cycles. On pinned base `759015dc`, the max-lines guard failed on three untouched UI files and an exact clean-index control failed identically. The required main-base advance included an upstream inventory repair that removed two of those reports; the remaining `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx` report is still inherited. No baseline waiver or unrelated edit was made.
- Hosted failure provenance: run **39832966696**, attempt **1**, job **120014021830**, head `f113dde017ecb6dcf91af45e0bf3a4057f867d90`. The original log places the warning at **18:52:36.747**, before CHAT_UPDATE_1's keyed-user failure at **18:52:37.135**. The exact offending transcript row remains unavailable. An unchanged base process rerun also passed once; that passing rerun is not the causal proof.

title: fix: wrap keyboard focus through iframe-created modal controls

title: fix: preserve keyboard focus when audio previews fail
body: ## What Problem This Solves When an audio attachment or voice note becomes unavailable, the player is replaced by a download fallback. If keyboard focus was inside the removed player, focus could fall back to the page body. Users then had to find the attachment again before downloading it. The same loss occurs when playback preparation fails while the ordinary audio card's Download or Open action is focused, even though no native audio error fires. ## User Impact A failed player now moves its existing keyboard focus to the usable Download action after the fallback mounts. Focus already in the composer or another control stays there, including focus moved elsewhere during the failure transition. This covers ordinary audio attachments and voice notes while preserving the existing unavailable announcement, download URLs, playback recovery and pointer behavior. The change requires no configuration or migration. It applies when the updated Control UI is installed and loaded; this PR does not change media authorization or server-side playback preparation. ## Why This Change Was Made Unavailable readiness has more than one producer: a terminal native media error and failed asynchronous preparation. The audio view now observes that existing readiness transition, captures focus before its controls are removed, and performs the handoff after rendering settles. It checks that the view and fallback remain connected, readiness is still unavailable, and the user has not focused another control. The subscription is removed with the view's existing cleanup. The shared attachment card exposes its existing Download link through an optional element reference. The reference callback also preserves the existing Download node when the parent updates its Open callback, so that update cannot discard keyboard focus. Focus policy remains in the audio view; the shared audio/video source owner and its recovery contract are unchanged. ## Evidence At 723cebe2c671a694cabbbdc4b96fce21eb5d70e9, all 79 tests across the five affected owner/importer files passed, together with targeted formatting, lint, i18n checks and 14 selected type graphs. The preparation regression fails for focused Download and Open actions before the correction and passes afterward; its outside-focus control passes in both states. A further regression fails before and passes after the reference correction when the parent updates its Open callback. Existing tests cover both player variants, internal controls, outside focus and newer outside focus. Chromium and WebKit baseline probes reproduce the focus loss through the bundled chat UI. On this head, all 24 native-error cases passed across both engines, covering ordinary audio and voice notes, internal focus, outside focus and focus moved during the transition. Six preparation-failure cases also passed: Download, Open and outside composer focus in each engine, with zero native audio errors. Sixteen actual keyboard downloads matched the original bytes. A native WebKit probe separately confirms that parent callback updates preserve the original focused Download node. The browser fixtures use synthetic Gateway responses and media; they do not certify screen-reader speech or a live provider. WebKit baseline and candidate runs emit the existing `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.` notice, retained separately from the focus assertions. The final Open/outside probe waits for visible layout and scrolling before acquiring the current live node; every post-failure assertion is unchanged. The rebuilt bundle is bound to source tree `f053eff1ea5ccf0cf8fa55ef9d64fbffbd45194f`. [Full hosted CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39930340939) on this head: all three UI unit shards, nine UI end-to-end shards and two real-Gateway shards succeeded, along with every other selected job. `ci:full` was selected before this push. Independent review is clean. Requested by Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm). ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Native media error | ![Native media error: failed preview with focus lost to the page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbe7eeae-1497-4774-b03a-b8ae0b03e981) | ![Native media error: fallback Download visibly focused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1394278f-59b9-4eb6-b381-4b66688e8f2f) | | Playback preparation failure | ![Playback preparation failure: failed preview with focus lost to the page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed611d38-7846-44a1-a068-ca2f660d93fd) | ![Playback preparation failure: fallback Download visibly focused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/119a697c-f95d-4edc-87f7-db1a5d408a1f) | ### Native error and preparation failure, with keyboard focus visible https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa7558c2-76ee-4f22-a134-782c057ec8f1 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 42c0d5a8f9d00e113c48090c3d259977e67b5b5a - Exact head: `723cebe2c671a694cabbbdc4b96fce21eb5d70e9` - Scenario: Keep keyboard focus on the usable Download action when a native media error or failed playback preparation replaces the audio player\. - Runtime/build: Bundled Control UI from source tree f053eff1ea5ccf0cf8fa55ef9d64fbffbd45194f; index SHA\-256 d516e2a5caff2b00efad9b97ee44b2d9c9ce470a5187ebecf5a7c8d3672c0e65\. - Capture: 1100×800 light\-theme viewport; identical750×240 crops at330,60\. - Native media: 24 Chromium/WebKit focus cases passed;16 keyboard downloads byte\-verified\. - Preparation: All six Chromium/WebKit preparation cases passed: Download, Open and outside focus in each engine\. - Recording: Native error at 0\.4× and preparation failure at 0\.5× playback\. - Exact published source tree and emitted bundle source were checked\. - Matched synthetic attachments, route, theme and framing\. - Every source recording frame and the captioned sequence were inspected\. - No screen\-reader speech or live\-provider claim\.

title: chore: remove unused npm test fixtures
body:
Related: #171994

## What Problem This Solves

Package-install tests retain uncalled fixture paths and an assertion module whose last callers were retired.

## User Impact

No user-visible change, configuration change, migration, or required action. No test case or executed assertion is removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retire the unused npm-pack mock and install-assertion wrapper, their unique dependencies, and the now-unreachable assertion module. Inline the remaining npm-view mock into its existing owner instead of retaining a single-caller view/pack abstraction. This removes **97 net test-support lines across two files**, with zero production changes or new helpers/options.

The view mock retains its async two-argument callback, command guard before metadata access, invocation-time metadata reads, exact error and JSON/property order, defaults, closure isolation, and implicit undefined return. The shared command-result constructor, failure cases, and integrity assertion are byte-identical. The last hook callers disappeared in `04a0bdfa025d23ae4831207b549d62c2c5a0094b`; existing install/pack script-suppression assertions remain at their owning boundaries.

## Evidence

- The same **100 tests across three files passed before and after**, with identical reported case names and order. Baseline wall time: 62.27s; candidate: 59.26s. These are preservation runs, not a performance claim; compiler-cache warmth can differ.
- Scoped plugin/platform and infrastructure test typechecks passed (5.41s and 3.90s), as did typed lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, and `git diff --check`. Fresh independent P0–P2 review completed with no findings.
- An additional actual-source callback comparison matched guard-before-getter behavior, callback arity, deferred metadata reads, exact errors and serialized output, undefined fields, ignored options, result defaults, and per-call isolation.
- All three required dead-code commands ran on clean baseline and candidate. They remain **failed**, not waived: dependency findings and unused-file findings match exactly; production exports match; full-tree exports shrink only by the two retired fixture exports, with no additions. The export scan completed production, full-tree, and script phases; the script phase passed.
- Every testcase file is byte-identical, including all three exercised suites. Their executed assertions, hooks, waits, and mock call sites are unchanged, as are production code, public APIs, dependencies, configuration, and defaults. No ignore rule, baseline, or expected failure was changed.

### Hosted CI qualification

The [original exact-head CI attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39840425120) **failed**: 67 terminal jobs, 36 successful / 29 skipped / 2 failed, totaling 6,684 cumulative job-seconds (not billing or a performance comparison). The failed leaf is `checks-node-changed-2`; the other failed job is its downstream combined gate.

Its three failures are existing update-CLI expectations: automatic service-Node refresh, nvm recovery, and the target-schema runtime-refusal reason. The same cases and signatures were observed on ancestral scheduled main in [the Node-runtime job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39823514819/job/119981001379) and [the target-schema job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39823514819/job/119981001158). That checkout (`827aae9c0bf17f8f27b6db0447a68ba9e3e5b42d`) is an ancestor of the actual tested base (`9395f44dccb97c38cec985c0a480daabc43878d9`). The tested merge's ordered parents and full tree were reconstructed and verified.

The refusal producer, failed tests, runtime mocks, engine policy and lockfile are unchanged by this PR. The shared npm helper module does change, but its consumed `createCommandResult` constructor is byte-identical and pure; the changed view mock is not used by these cases. Earlier-main package-version and version-resolver drift was inspected; the failed scenarios use explicit target/engine fixtures. Historical grouping/cache settings differ, so this is **ancestral execution plus scoped source attribution**, not a claimed exact-base replay.

The automatic failure table remains **unknown** because the newer scheduled-main run has no matching job name. This qualification uses the matching individual cases instead; neither the table nor the failed CI is relabeled green. An existing expectation repair is tracked separately in [#180939](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180939); no duplicate fix or CI rerun was started here. The native inherited-failure route must still verify current writer authority, exact head, review, security, complete job accounting, and the retained recovery history.

This is offline preservation proof using synthetic package fixtures and mocked npm execution. No real package installation, operator Gateway, external account, device, or paid-provider run was performed or claimed. Hosted CI remains failed as documented above; native inherited-CI admission and independent review/security gates remain required.

<details>

```sh
pnpm test src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts src/hooks/install.test.ts src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

pnpm deadcode:unused-files

```

Baseline: `1e56117f00f5858e025bdc7f4f396c7567ab32ee`. Test runs used separate temporary roots and filesystem module caches.

Each dead-code command returned exit 1 on both trees. Existing production unused exports/types and the unrelated unused `scripts/perf/doctor-metadata-retention.ts` remain unresolved. Complete normalized findings are identical except for removing `expectInstallUsesIgnoreScripts` and `mockNpmPackMetadataResult` from the full-tree unused-export report. No failed result is represented as passing.

</details>

Contributor credit: @vincentkoc.

title: fix: keep secret reveal focus visible in forced colors
body: ## What Problem This Solves Keyboard users cannot see which secret reveal/hide button has focus in Settings when forced colors are active. The shared control resets the browser outline and relies on a box shadow, which forced-colors rendering suppresses. ## User Impact The focused reveal/hide button gains a system-colored outline in forced-colors mode. It remains visible while revealing and hiding the value and clears when focus moves away. Reveal permissions, disabled controls, secret contents and ordinary-theme styling are unchanged; there are no configuration or migration changes. ## Why This Change Was Made A scoped `:focus-visible` rule restores a 2px `Highlight` outline with a 2px offset at the shared stylesheet owner. It follows the existing forced-colors treatment for segmented controls and does not change reveal handlers or add another styling owner. ## Evidence The production-bundled Settings → Gateway scenario uses Chromium 156, real keyboard Tab/Space, forced-colors emulation and synthetic secret content at 1280×900. On base f113dde017ecb6dcf91af45e0bf3a4057f867d90, the focused button has `outline-style: none` and `box-shadow: none`; the regression fails at the solid-outline assertion. At de7b2f21d2e3d9eadb511e7a0f5e781bbd96ea47, it has a solid 2px outline with a 2px offset. The screenshots show the ring without clipping, and the recording shows focus, reveal/hide and focus departure. All 11 tests in the secret-focus, connection-settings and Settings-controls E2E files passed, as did scoped formatting/lint, keyless i18n verification and the affected E2E type graph. The normal-mode control retains its focus shadow under both requested OS color preferences; it does not separately assert completion of each application-theme transition. Normal-theme preservation also follows from the production rule being confined to forced-colors mode. title: fix: preserve browser zoom shortcuts in image previews
body:
## What Problem This Solves

After an image loads in a preview, the image zoom handler intercepts browser zoom and reset shortcuts. Someone using Ctrl/Cmd to enlarge the browser interface instead enlarges only the image, and browser reset can unexpectedly reset image zoom.

## User Impact

Browser zoom and reset shortcuts remain available while an image preview is open. Ordinary image shortcuts (`=`, `+`, `-`, and `0`), including Shift to type `+`, keep working. Toolbar actions, gallery navigation and keyboard focus retain their existing behavior. No settings or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing keyboard handler calls `preventDefault()` before invoking the image zoom command. Excluding Ctrl, Meta and Alt combinations at that decision leaves those shortcuts to the browser without adding another handler or changing image loading, zoom state or focus ownership.

## Evidence

Native keyboard input in headed Chromium exercised the chat image-opening flow with synthetic data. On the base, Ctrl+= kept browser zoom at 100% and enlarged the image to 135%. With this patch, Ctrl+= and Ctrl+Shift+= changed browser zoom to 110%, Ctrl+- changed it to 90%, and Ctrl+0 restored 100%; image zoom stayed at 100% throughout. Plain image keys and pointer zoom/reset still worked, as did Tab wrapping and Escape focus restoration.

The owning regression fails on the base at Ctrl+= cancellation and passes with the fix. All 29 component/lazy tests and 10 Chromium browser tests passed, along with targeted formatting, lint, i18n and the selected type checks. [Exact-head scoped CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39830324550) completed successfully.

Native browser-zoom measurements cover Chromium on Linux. The ten existing lightbox browser tests also passed in Playwright WebKit on landed commit `d939b467d164f7ca051887f39a3222d30fb53564`, covering focus restoration, zoom retention during image upgrades, responsive controls and neighboring images. Meta and Alt combinations are covered by the component regression; native macOS browser zoom was not exercised. The images below are unedited frames from the native Chromium scenario, with identical initial conditions and the resulting zoom difference preserved.

Full normal UI coverage was qualified from the [source-equivalent scheduled run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39913763515). Its ten failures—nine sidebar geometry cases and one provider-login cancellation case—match the [preexisting baseline run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39906351041) and do not exercise the image-only zoom handler. Those failures remain failures; the full run is not globally green.

title: fix: preserve date and time keyboard editing in custom snooze
body:
## What Problem This Solves

When choosing **Snooze → Choose another time**, pressing Tab moved between the date/time input and the buttons before the browser could visit the input's remaining segments. Keyboard users could not edit the full date and time through the normal native controls.

## User Impact

Tab now reaches each native date/time segment before moving to Cancel and Snooze. Focus wraps at the picker edges, and Escape and Cancel return focus to the chooser. Existing date validation, permission checks, submission and remembered custom times retain their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker intercepted every Tab press and cycled whole controls. This change lets the browser handle Tab inside the date/time input and uses two focus guards solely at the dialog edges, following the existing modal approach. The repair stays in the custom snooze owner; shared menu and overlay policies are unchanged.

The successful entry uses actual keys, then checks the exact snooze request and reuse.
- 66 unit/component cases and six Chromium browser cases pass. Additional Chromium and WebKit scenarios pass native segment editing, forward/reverse focus wrapping, Escape/Cancel focus return and unavailable-action behavior. A disabled submit wraps to Cancel in the compact picker; disabling the desktop parent submenu closes its picker, preserving the existing overlay policy.

title: fix: bootstrap prompts trigger unrequested Git commits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new workspace can steer an agent into unrequested Git commits after delivering a file because the presence of `BOOTSTRAP.md` adds a mandatory commit reminder to its system prompt.

## User Impact

Users can request a document or script without the bootstrap machinery automatically adding Git work. Explicit user and workspace Git instructions remain supported. This does not prohibit commits or change the starter workspace's separate permission for proactive work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [benchmark report](https://x.com/grenlouis/status/2113307026956669289) identified Git detours in all nine reviewed blog, workflow, and rewriting attempts on v2026.10.5. I independently inspected those public traces: the requested files were saved, then commit attempts encountered missing author identity. The report supports removing an unnecessary instruction, not claiming a universal model-behavior failure rate.

Remove the unconditional reminder at the bootstrap owner rather than adding Git detection, identity configuration, or another option. The production change deletes seven lines; two prompt-boundary regressions and a short workspace-doc clarification preserve the intended contract.

## Evidence

- Both new cases fail against unchanged production because the rendered system prompt contains the automatic reminder.
- With the fix, bootstrap preparation, attempt system-prompt, and tool-prefix stability suites pass: **47 tests**. The tests load real workspace files and render the prompt, covering both an ordinary deliverable instruction and an explicit commit instruction.
- Targeted agent-test typecheck, Oxlint, formatting, docs MDX validation, internal-link audit, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent review covers P0–P2 correctness and regression risks with the complete owning source supplied.

**Limit:** a live model/Gateway replay was not completed: the supported CLI preparation could not establish safe offline-state publication, including with a disposable profile. No live Gateway was stopped and no safety guard was bypassed. This proof establishes the prompt correction, not a measured reduction in unsolicited commits or a rerun of benchmark scores.

Reported by Louis Grenard in the linked public benchmark thread; requested by @GrahamMcBain.

title: fix: skip unavailable video links during keyboard navigation
body: ## What Problem This Solves When a gallery video's original URL is still loading, Shift+Tab from Close can focus the unavailable **Open in new tab** link. The link has no destination and is already marked `tabindex="-1"`, but the lightbox's manual focus wrapping still treats it as the last control. Keyboard users therefore land on an action they cannot use. ## User Impact Keyboard wrapping skips the pending link and reaches Next. Once the original link becomes available, it joins the wrap sequence again. Native video controls, intentionally focusable gallery navigation buttons, and focus return to the opener retain their existing behavior. There is no configuration or migration change. ## Why This Change Was Made The lightbox already owns a registry of its controls and excludes disconnected elements and natively disabled buttons when choosing wrap boundaries. This change adds the existing tab-index contract to that filter. It keeps the fix at the focus owner without changing the modal implementation, original-link loading, media lifecycle, or navigation policy. The regression exercises the rendered video gallery with actual browser keyboard input. It checks pending and ready wrap boundaries, native video seeking without gallery movement, traversal through native controls, and focus restoration on close. ## Evidence The regression fails on the base production owner in both Chromium and WebKit: focus lands on the unavailable original anchor rather than Next. The candidate passes all 50 selected unit tests and all 22 browser cases across Chromium and WebKit. Changed-file formatting and lint, UI i18n verification, and the selected production and test type graphs passed. The unit batch took 10.07 seconds and the two-engine browser run took 11.34 seconds in the test runner. The [full hosted CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39955097167) also passed, including all three UI shards, nine UI E2E rows, and both real-Gateway E2E shards. The browser test retains Chromium’s native seeking assertion. A standalone-video comparison confirmed that WebKit does not seek when ArrowRight targets the video host; both engines verify that the lightbox leaves that key uncancelled and does not move the gallery. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Shift\+Tab incorrectly focuses the unavailable original link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/160a6134-44b9-42c1-93b0-8826feb86691) | ![Shift\+Tab wraps to Next while the original link is unavailable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9373230d-6a93-40f3-adaf-a41039aed458) | ### Pending and ready keyboard wrapping https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5162ce90-8b4d-4645-8feb-630333d40be2 ### Visual verification - Baseline: dadde412543848f87df92d76f5ca188234969c5a - Exact head: `6272bd2b164d25fa3cf2a8c49174f0c78bd56837` - Scenario: With the original link pending, press Shift\+Tab from Close and Tab back; resolve the original link and repeat wrapping\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw production lightbox source at 6272bd2b164d25fa3cf2a8c49174f0c78bd56837; Playwright 1\.64\.0 Chromium; synthetic video and controlled original\-link loading - Pending reverse wrap: Unavailable original link before; Next after - Forward wrap: Next returns to Close - Ready original link: Joins the wrap sequence - Actual focus assertions pass in Chromium and WebKit - 22 affected browser cases pass - Original\-link readiness and opener focus restoration remain intact - Before and after use equivalent viewport, media and pending state Contributor credit: Mitchell Etzel requested and authorized the accessibility campaign. ## Worked on by - @etzelm

title: improve(ui): prioritize archiving nested sessions together
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Archiving a session with nested sessions emphasizes the parent-only action without clearly explaining what happens to the nested sessions.

## User Impact

User impact: the dialog asks **Also archive nested sessions?** and offers **Archive all (N)** as the red primary action, counting the complete intended tree, including the parent. **Archive only this session** is secondary; directly nested sessions move to the top level, while deeper sessions stay beneath those children. On mobile, the archive choices stay together when they fit, with **Cancel below**; desktop keeps its existing layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The primary uses the complete collected tree length, not the direct-child count. Mobile choice grouping is opt-in for nested archive only: the actual reading and keyboard order matches the visual order, while Cancel remains initially focused. The other Save/Discard/Cancel choice dialog retains its original layout. Confirmation, live guards, abort, warnings, Undo, and leaf/bulk behavior are preserved; no migration or user action is required.

- @jacobtomlinson

title: improve(ui): select existing photos and videos from the composer
body:
Related: #180298

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the composer's **Photo** action excludes existing videos, so users must discover the general **File** route to attach them.

## User Impact

**Photos & videos** lets Chat and New Session stage existing images and videos together where the browser supports mixed selection. Sending remains explicit. Image-only composers, camera capture and unrestricted file selection retain their existing behavior. This is the media-selection slice of #180298; broader platform picker design remains separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

A dedicated mixed-media input uses the existing attachment admission, preparation, preview, draft and send owners. Camera's image-only upload input stays separate. The integration preserves the deferred camera component and its current property callbacks.

Original contribution by @TheAngryPit, credited as `TheAngryPit <7040636+TheAngryPit@users.noreply.github.com>` in the retained contributor commits.

## Evidence

The real menu → input → attachment-draft regression failed on current-main production files (1 failed / 7 passed), then all 8 tests passed with this change and again after integrating main `233c8b629a38` using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-attachment-inputs.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`.

Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the keyless i18n baseline/verification pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2; the full patch and the later focus-test consumer update were reviewed with their owning code. [Final-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180723#issuecomment-6345056605) also reports no code findings; the CI failures below remain explicit limitations.

The broader local changed-file check encountered shared-install declaration-boundary refusals and unrelated full-repository unused-export findings. The first CI run found a stale `photo` selector in the existing opening-animation test; it now follows the `media` action while preserving focus, cancellation and reselection assertions. Its focused local rerun reached the same Mermaid setup blocker. Chat, New Session, and shared attachment-only composers retain existing attachment labels, native picker paths, image-only restrictions, capability state, permission checks, and override/reset controls. This is a focused UX proposal for maintainer review, not an approved design.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the shared menu's non-interactive section rows and existing typography. Heading nodes remain stable across capability updates, preserving native keyboard focus while translated text stays reactive. The management link reuses the existing muted note style. **No new CSS rules, refocus timers, navigation path, panel, preference, or placement owner.**

Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit) proposed this independently useful menu-clarity contribution. It does not implement or depend on the umbrella's separate media-selection, capture, Files-policy, or panel-anchoring decisions, and does not close #180298.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Members can see the connected Gateway version but cannot identify its running commit or build time when diagnosing a possibly stale deployment.

## User Impact

Settings → About shows the Control UI and the connected Gateway as two entries of one compact identity rail: name, version, commit with copy, and UTC build time. The two builds are visibly separate, so a member can tell whether the Gateway they are connected to includes a fix without assuming the browser bundle matches it. Missing provenance is omitted; a disconnected Gateway shows as unavailable. Host diagnostics and update operations remain restricted.

title: fix(ui): keep named attachment errors beside the draft
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: failed or rejected composer files lose their names and recovery explanations when a short-lived toast disappears.

## User Impact

Draft text and valid attachments stay intact; failed files are never sent. Keyboard dismissal moves to the next or previous notice, then the editor, without scrolling.

Notices last for the current composer lifetime, not across reload. Video compression retains the retry path from #179007.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing attachment-read owner retains small failure records, not failed File objects or encoded payloads. Admission supplies per-file reasons; the shared preview announces new errors politely. title: fix(browser): Browser panel fails to load when the extension relay secret is unusable
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Browser panel shows "Couldn't load browser: extension relay secret exists but is unreadable/malformed <- … already exists (secret-exists)" on every load when `credentials/browser-extension-relay.secret` exists but is not a usable secret.

## User Impact

User impact: an unusable relay secret no longer takes down Browser control. OpenClaw-managed and other non-extension profiles keep working, and the Chrome extension profile fails with the exact problem (for example "is not a 64-character lowercase hex token", "has 2 hard links", "is owned by another user (uid 0)") and the command to fix it. Required action for affected users: move the named file aside and run `openclaw browser extension pair` to re-pair. OpenClaw never replaces a rejected secret automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The relay secret reader returned the same `null` for "missing" and for every state it refuses (malformed, symlink, hard link, foreign owner, non-regular file). `ensureExtensionRelayToken` treated that as missing, tried to create the file, hit `secret-exists`, re-read 50 times and threw a generic error. Browser control awaited that before starting, and the built-in `chrome` extension profile is always present, so one bad optional file failed every profile.

The reader now classifies each read. Persistent rejected states fail immediately with the reason and the `openclaw browser extension pair` hint, and are never overwritten. Empty or changing files still get the bounded wait for a concurrent first writer. Browser control no longer pre-ensures the key: each extension relay already ensures it and its startup failures are already caught per profile.

Scope note: an earlier proposal also added a Doctor repair that renamed malformed secrets. That would add a new core Doctor contract and auto-replace a credential, and the actionable error already names the one-step fix. It is not included.

## Evidence

- **Reproduced** with the shipped `ensureExtensionRelayToken` against isolated state dirs. Healthy, missing, mode 0644, CRLF, BOM and no-newline files work. Uppercase hex, truncated, garbage, hard-linked, symlinked and directory secrets all produced the reported error (cause `FsSafeError secret-exists`) after about 500 ms.
- **Regression test** `control-service.relay-secret.test.ts` runs the real service start with a malformed secret. On the old `control-service.ts` it fails because the whole service throws. With the fix, Browser control starts, the `chrome` relay is not running, the extension profile's relay ensure rejects with the actionable error, and the file is unchanged.
- `relay-auth.test.ts` covers each rejected state: the message names the reason, the file is unchanged, and symlink, directory and hard-link cases fail without entering the retry wait (they run under fake timers).
- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/relay-auth.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/control-service.relay-secret.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 16 passed, 49 s wall (about 45 s transform/import). The new tests take milliseconds; the pre-existing empty-file case still waits its real 0.5 s retry budget.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `run-oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files are clean.
- Autoreview (codex, P0–P1): no actionable findings.

The branch is based on `8f6e418cc4ea1`, the commit just before #179992, because the new pinned pnpm cannot be installed locally under the release-age policy yet. No `extensions/browser` file differs from current `main`, and PR CI covers the merge ref.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen.

Co-authored-by: Patrick-Erichsen <20157849+Patrick-Erichsen@users.noreply.github.com>

title: feat: add Enhanced contrast for built-in Control UI themes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

People who need stronger text, control boundaries, and keyboard focus should not have to replace their preferred Control UI theme.

## User Impact

Adds **System / Standard / Enhanced** contrast independently of theme and light/dark mode for all 11 built-in themes. System is the default and follows each device's increased-contrast preference; explicit choices win. The saved choice follows an authenticated profile, while the resolved OS signal remains device-local.

Theme IDs, body/chat text, fonts, branding, corner shapes, text scale, density, and zoom are preserved. Enhanced uses authored action/link colors without deleting the saved accent; that accent returns when effective contrast returns to Standard. Beacon retains its already-strong text, links, status colors, and focus treatment.

This draft covers the Control UI. Imported, personal, and plugin themes keep their authored palettes with an explicit supported-state notice. Native palettes, terminal palettes, third-party embedded content, already-rendered diagrams, and assistive-technology validation remain qualification boundaries. The measurements below are sampled contrast proof, not a whole-app WCAG conformance claim. No database migration or operator configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

One preference owner and one shared first-paint/live resolver select authored theme variants, rather than applying filters or substituting themes. Contrast-only writes use profile preferences rather than the theme-selection mutation that also resets fonts and accents. Explicit Standard overrides OS increased contrast; forced colors and reduced transparency remain independent. Theme consumers receive palette updates, including widget invalidation, and the composer keeps real enhanced boundaries and focus instead of fading them through its local cascade.

## Contrast repair

- Keep Send hover styling off Stop, voice and dictation controls.
- Respect System contrast intent even when an external palette is active; preserve explicit Standard and saved theme selections during fallback.
- Derive checkmark ink from each accent swatch and strengthen the existing selected segmented state after focus leaves it.
- Associate the existing Contrast, accent and background descriptions with their controls. Keep saved background preferences editable while explaining when accessibility settings suppress their display.

## Evidence

Inspected browser captures use the same synthetic scenarios: **Before = main `3cd9bdd`; After = final candidate**. Additional measurements against the received implementation are internal regression evidence, not the Before screenshots.

Validated System/Standard/Enhanced, imported themes and Claw fallback, blurred selection, Mint/default swatches, Send/Stop/voice/dictation, saved background preferences, and production first paint in isolated Chromium. The existing suite has 24 distinct cases: 22 theme/mode pairs (11 themes × light/dark) and two composer cases. The initial run passed 22; its two Claw cases passed after repairing the mock acknowledgment. Replays are not counted as additional cases. The final focused browser run passed seven scenarios. The background suites passed eight and 24 cases. UI/core typechecks passed after fixing a missing sibling fixture field. Scoped lint passed on 26 source files with no warnings or errors; changed CSS, format and growth checks passed. Fresh independent reviews found no remaining actionable issue.

Measured execution: final focused browser run 51.91s, sibling background suite 3.12s, scoped lint 22.4s. Heavy validation ran on isolated AWS, not the maintainer's Mac. No CI timing claim is made.

### Visual proof

[Four inspected main-to-final screenshot pairs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180295#issuecomment-6347161918): selection after blur, selected Mint, Stop hover and external-theme background settings. Before is main `3cd9bdd`; after is published head `0e0a9e3` (tree `5df5588a`).

title: feat(ui): comment on file, diff, and PDF selections in chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users cannot attach feedback to selected code or PDF text without manually copying the passage and its location into chat.

## User Impact

Select code in **Files** or **Review**, or text in a PDF attachment, choose **Add to chat**, and leave a comment. Sending includes the selected text and its source: file path, line range and diff side for code; document name and page number for PDFs. Saving a comment neither modifies the source nor replaces the existing chat draft.

PDF comments support same-origin attachments up to 16 MiB, one page per comment. Scanned pages need OCR outside this reader. **Open original PDF** retains access to browser printing, search, forms and password entry. External PDFs and workspace binary-file download paths are unchanged. Selections crossing diff sides or omitted lines need separate comments; formatted Markdown previews are outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing comment editor, attachment admission, draft storage and send path. Readers supply coordinates while the current composer owns permission and delivery checks; no separate review store or API is introduced.

The native PDF iframe is replaced by a lazy, single-page PDF.js reader with a selectable text layer. PDF.js 6.4.299 is pinned; worker, fonts and decoding resources are served locally. The existing bounded fetch and byte-revalidation owner remains responsible for downloads, and unchanged ticket renewals retain page and zoom. This does not relax the Gateway CSP or enable PDF scripting/forms.

The requester approved adding PDF support to this same draft. The earlier import conflict with #179908 is resolved, preserving both the file-operation refactor and comment integration. title: fix(ui): preserve keyboard focus when revealing code blocks
body:
Supersedes #180252.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: keyboard focus is lost when a reader reveals the hidden lines of a code block in chat.

## User Impact

User impact: Enter and Space keep focus on the revealed code, with a visible focus outline, working horizontal arrow-key scrolling, and a keyboard route back to Copy. Pointer behavior is unchanged. No migration or configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing one-way reveal hides its own button. Transfer keyboard-visible focus to the code viewport already named by aria-controls, without scrolling the transcript or adding a new tab stop. The viewport also owns horizontal scrolling: its interactive overflow rule now outranks the passive-code pre rules. Reuse the existing focus-ring styling; Markdown reconciliation, code text, copying, JSON modes, and wrapping remain unchanged.

Requested by @jjjhenriksen (Jacqueline Henriksen). This consolidation incorporates and adapts @etzelm’s (Mitchell Etzel) earlier implementation in #180252, specifically its horizontal-reading, exact clipboard payload, and unrelated-focus preservation regressions. Mitchell’s contribution is credited here by Jacqueline’s explicit interim approval; his Git co-author trailer remains pending because the managed publication route cannot currently carry the additional contributor. No Mitchell Git co-authorship is claimed.

- The consolidation regression failed on the prior published implementation: focus reached the viewport, but ArrowRight left its scroll position at zero. The CSS-owner repair passes native Tab/ArrowRight/Enter/Shift+Tab and verifies the exact full source through Chromium clipboard readback.
- Final code-fence and JSON E2E suites: 14 passed in 38.33s; the new reading case took 1.842s. Streaming focus, pointer behavior, wrap, copying, block art, and JSON siblings pass.

title: fix(memory): prevent Forget worker OOM on large live transcripts
body:
Related: #176243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a worker out-of-memory failure when Memory Forget inspects a large live SQLite transcript containing original messages.

## Memory impact

**Historical matched benchmark: 59.67% lower median sampled process-tree PSS high water** — 2,070,743,040 → 835,210,240 bytes (1.93 → 0.78 GiB; 1,178.3 MiB less). This is the median of five per-run sampled maxima, not steady-state memory or a true peak.

**Current PR candidate: memory reduction NOT MEASURED.** Those five interleaved pairs measured an older pre-extraction candidate, before helper relocation, CI metadata repairs and main integration changed shared worker/dependency inputs. They are historical evidence, not performance acceptance for this head.

- Workload: real compiled offline Memory Forget CLI preview, synthetic ASCII transcript, 34,401 events / 463,059,747 JSONL bytes; Node 26.12.1, unchanged 512/32 MiB worker limits. Nominal 25 ms sampling sums observed process-tree PSS, including the timing wrapper; Worker-thread RSS is not added.
- **Main-isolate heap reduction, whole-process RSS reduction and true-peak reduction: NOT MEASURED by this comparison.** No percentage for those metrics or for general workloads is claimed.
- Tradeoff: a 463,162,950-byte private temporary export (about 442 MiB), removed on normal completion; crash leftovers remain possible.
- The earlier cohort still **FAILED** both wall/CPU STOP thresholds (candidate 27.356 s / 16.74 s CPU versus baseline 6.914 s / 8.60 s CPU). Later pairs do not erase that failure or establish its cause; the original archived incident remains unproved.

Exact historical patch/workload bindings, all five paired values, method limits and retained failures are in Evidence below.

## User Impact

Users can inspect/forget large live-session history without a full decoded worker reply, preserving snapshot/reset/provenance/failure ordering. No heap-limit, schema, config, or retention change.

The operation uses temporary disk proportional to the transcript: the measured fixture needs a 463,162,950-byte private export (463,163,392 allocated bytes, about 442 MiB). Normal completion removes it; a process crash can leave that private export behind. The exact archived transcript from the issue is unavailable, so this PR does not claim to reproduce or resolve every retained-archive failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing export owner captures an immutable snapshot under its fence/version contract. The acknowledged exchange returns a compact descriptor. Native reader settlement and validation precede callbacks. Replay preserves originals/order; archive/incognito/public array contracts are unchanged.

Operation-local writer/reader buffers grow as needed and use initialized prefixes, eliminating per-record churn and combining frame writes. No global cache, mutable-page callbacks, heap increase, or skipped native join.

## Evidence

- Regression proof: the base original-snapshot worker reply exceeded the 4 KiB contract (74,283 bytes); the bounded-source candidate returned a 260-byte descriptor while preserving callback snapshot semantics.
- Pre-buffer product proof: Unicode/equal-byte ASCII sources, each 34,401 events / 463,059,747 JSONL bytes, actual 512/32 MiB limits. Preview/apply/repeat/since/refusal preserved source/control/origins/tombstones. Prior-head evidence, not a revised-head large-Unicode/model/Gateway run.
- Revised-head focused proof: 63 tests across nine affected files passed, including real-worker snapshot, callback/reset/read-hold/custody paths. The new framing regression is red before buffer reuse and green after it: exact independent Unicode framing, long-to-short records, independent yielded objects, short I/O, and a truncated tail. Three frames plus a forced short write used one writer backing store / four writes; replay used header and payload stores / eight reads including short read and EOF. Only the narrow framing test mocks its database I/O source.
- Scoped production/test typechecks, typed lint, formatting/whitespace checks, and the canonical build passed. The build retained its existing nonfatal locale-size diagnostic. Broad exact-head CI is reported separately by GitHub, not inferred from local success.
- Normal hooks moved two helpers byte-for-byte into the already-imported projection sibling; 41 consumer tests, types, lint and hooks passed. Build/cost evidence predates that move and main integration.

- Integration follow-up: merged main `4d294053ad54`, including #180315’s native-subagent expectation fix, and repaired the newer scheduled-turns expectation from #180282. That case failed before the one-line fix; six affected cases and 33 transcript tests then passed, plus targeted types/lint/format. Candidate review: 19 partitioned passes, no actionable findings; static only. Old CI run 39722865071 remains failed; new-head CI is separate.

### Completed revised-candidate cost comparison

Five predeclared interleaved pairs ran once each: no warmups, discarded/replaced samples, or forced GC. Once-seeded variants matched transcript/table/control facts, normalized config/runtime/time/workload hashes. Real compiled offline CLI preview retained worker limits. All functional/protected-state/default-limit/process-settlement/cleanup checks passed.

| Pair | Baseline wall ms | Candidate wall ms | Baseline waited CPU µs | Candidate waited CPU µs | Baseline observed tree-PSS B | Candidate observed tree-PSS B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6656.329451 | 4315.143755 | 8260000 | 6730000 | 2116646912 | 835210240 |
| 2 | 5267.495488 | 4256.881545 | 8080000 | 6800000 | 2051841024 | 837079040 |
| 3 | 5039.606078 | 4209.454111 | 7720000 | 6820000 | 2060108800 | 819704832 |
| 4 | 6039.779969 | 5029.855176 | 8310000 | 7640000 | 2089146368 | 835561472 |
| 5 | 7723.621762 | 5821.617906 | 9260000 | 8030000 | 2070743040 | 789981184 |

Written gate: stop immediately if candidate paired wall or waited CPU exceeds baseline by more than 20%, or functional/default-limit/coverage/cleanup checks fail. Require median and nearest-rank p95 wall/CPU to hold or improve, and median observed-PSS reduction of at least min(5 MiB, 2% of baseline median). All five pairs pass. Median wall improves 28.55% (6039.779969 → 4315.143755 ms), CPU 17.43% (8260000 → 6820000 µs), and observed PSS 59.67% (2070743040 → 835210240 B). Median PSS reduction is 1,235,532,800 B versus the 5,242,880 B floor. Nearest-rank p95 with n=5 is the maximum: wall 7723.621762 → 5821.617906 ms; CPU 9260000 → 8030000 µs; PSS 2116646912 → 837079040 B.

**Limits:** nominal 25 ms sampled tree-PSS is observed high water, not true peak. GNU Time user+system covers waited descendants, not orphan/cgroup-total; Node exit CPU only crosschecks it. Known timing-wrapper PSS is included; Worker RSS is not added. A5 maximum interval was 57.297481 ms versus candidate maximum 26.054988 ms. All gaps/variable loads retained, no filtering/noise waiver. Five pairs do not establish population tails. Both used current Node 26.12.1, not the earlier failed cohort runtime.

### Earlier failed comparison remains failed

Before buffer reuse, a separate first pair measured baseline 6913.909567 ms / 8600000 µs CPU versus candidate 27356.483281 ms / 16740000 µs. Both +20% STOP thresholds fired. That cohort remains failed, never replaced. Excess wall followed an early JS exit marker; later-JS/native teardown cause is unidentified. Two unscored diagnostics did not reproduce it and were not clearance. New qualification does not prove buffers/runtime caused the old tail.

Independent review completed four P0–P3 passes with all 15 pre-extraction files supplied in full plus unchanged owners; context was partitioned, not all modules in each pass. Native findings / exit 1 remains: four P2 entries described ONE qualification gap, addressed by independently crosschecked five-pair evidence. No other actionable functional/security defect established.

### Historical benchmark provenance and cleanup

The task-specific 612-line benchmark harness has been removed from this PR's current diff; production code and product-boundary regression tests are unchanged by that cleanup. Results remain above, including the failed cohort and measurement limits. No replacement benchmark PR or new benchmark run was made.

Cleanup verification: the only source change from pre-cleanup `0794052e2497` is deletion of that harness; every retained production and regression-test blob is identical. Reference/whitespace checks, normal commit hooks and a fresh P0–P3 deletion review passed. The PR shrank from 20 files (+1,432/−125) to 19 (+820/−125). An installed npm 11.20.0 `pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` inventory listed 15,617 files with zero matches for the removed harness or `scripts/perf/`. It ran no lifecycle scripts, wrote no tarball and did not build; it checked the current package manifest against existing older dist artifacts, not fresh release packaging or runtime behavior.

The exact historical harness is retained in [pre-cleanup commit 0794052e2497db6e0c76d47a6d31b02c7b1cea65](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0794052e2497db6e0c76d47a6d31b02c7b1cea65/scripts/perf/memory-forget-measure.mjs), SHA256 `56ec30ac3e7acd02a76184fa4257741f9480d8778251ac8cac00671764e9688f`. That commit preserves the harness, not a claim that its integrated production tree was benchmarked. The measured production patch is bound separately below. Historical raw receipts, the failed cohort and two unscored diagnostics remain retained privately; no private logs or heap data are published.

Measured pre-extraction full-patch SHA256 `1725077016f16ea7c5c4dbbb4bdbc7e934bc8429b0c1ef11457c6aaa4e1e1ea0`; workload `56ec30ac3e7acd02a76184fa4257741f9480d8778251ac8cac00671764e9688f`. Build/cost results predate helper relocation, CI metadata repairs and main `4d294053ad54` integration. Shared worker/dependency inputs changed: these are NOT measurements of this integrated head. Synthetic origins prove purge selection, not model promotion. Populated-vector purge uses existing tests, not this fixture. No new large-Unicode product run, exact archived-incident reproduction, crash-leftover cleanup guarantee, or merge/CI approval is implied.

title: fix(macos): Dock icon raises the main Dashboard window instead of the last focused one
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking the OpenClaw Dock icon (or Open Dashboard) raises the main Dashboard window even when another Dashboard window was the last one focused.

## User Impact

User impact: with two Dashboard windows open, switching to another app and then clicking the Dock icon now returns to the Dashboard window you were last using instead of always jumping to the first one. A closed main window is still reopened as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dock reopen and Open Dashboard both present through `DashboardManager`, which already deferred to the last focused window when an experience switch had hidden it, but otherwise always raised the main window. Presentation now also defers to the last focused Dashboard window when it is open and the main window is open too. When the main window has been closed, presentation still reopens it, preserving the existing reconnect contract.

## Evidence

No local Mac was available (Crabbox macOS hosts were unavailable), so proof ran on a GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runner from a proof-only branch that adds one workflow on top of this exact fix commit:
[macOS Dashboard reopen proof run 39716511863](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39716511863)

- **Reproduced on main sources** (`3f8eee902de1`) with the new regression test `reopening returns to the last focused Dashboard window`:
  `Expectation failed: (manager.frontmostDashboard()?.controller → <…0xaffd98500>) === (focused → <…0xafffe8f00>)` (the main window was raised over the focused one).
- **Fixed sources:** the regression test passes (`Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed`).
- **Dashboard suites:** `--filter Dashboard` passes with the fix (`245 tests in 44 suites passed`). The same suites on main sources fail only on the new regression test.
- An earlier version of this fix also redirected when the main window was closed. It failed `endpoint discovery cannot overwrite a reopened main window` in run 39710966531. The fix was narrowed to require an open main window, and that test now passes.
- Fresh local autoreview (codex) on the final diff: no actionable findings.

Gap: this is controller-level proof through `presentDashboard()`, the entry point the Dock reopen handler calls. It is not a recorded Dock click on a physical Mac.
