title: fix(ui): keyboard reading stops after expanding chat code
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: arrow-key scrolling stops after a keyboard user reveals hidden lines in a chat code block because focus stays on the disappearing disclosure button.

## User Impact

Keyboard users can keep reading the revealed code with arrow keys and return to Copy with Shift+Tab. Existing focus elsewhere is not moved by a programmatic disclosure.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Consolidation decision — Jacqueline taking over in #180293

At 2026-10-22 05:00 UTC, Mitchell Etzel requested closing this overlapping PR and confirmed that Jacqueline Henriksen is taking over the shared disclosure-focus repair in [PR #180293](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180293). These address the same defect, not separate bugs. This PR’s branch, source, tests, recording, and contributor credit are retained as prior implementation evidence; this note does not itself claim that GitHub closure succeeded.

The surviving implementation must prove native ArrowRight scrolling after expansion, Shift+Tab/Copy with exact payload, and streaming focus retention on its own final head. #180252’s inner-scroller evidence does not certify #180293’s different viewport focus target. [The hosted consolidation recommendation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180293#issuecomment-6332860563) favors retaining the ARIA-controlled viewport and visible outline while incorporating the horizontal-reading regression.

The shared code-disclosure click owner moves focus into the revealed code only when the disclosure owned focus. It uses the renderer’s existing adjacent code surface and prevents focus-induced scrolling. title: fix(mcp): name the exact sign-in command and say plugin instead of connector
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a failed MCP browser sign-in tells the operator to "run openclaw mcp login with this connector's name", and runtime OAuth errors say "Run openclaw mcp login <name>" for every server. The CLI refuses while the Gateway runs and cannot sign in to plugin-declared servers at all (the Linear report). OpenClaw's own copy also calls plugins and MCP servers "connectors", a concept OpenClaw does not have.

## User Impact

User impact: when browser sign-in fails for a server under `mcp.servers`, the error now leads with retrying in Settings and spells out the terminal fallback exactly, for example `stop the Gateway with openclaw gateway stop, run openclaw mcp login linear, then start the Gateway again` (with `--profile`/`--container` when applicable). For a plugin-declared server, errors point to **Connect** on the plugin's page instead of a command that would fail. Runtime OAuth errors (missing, expired or unrefreshable credentials) follow the same rule. The composer **+** menu entry formerly labeled **Connectors** now reads **Plugins**, and Gateway errors, Control UI copy and docs say "plugin" or "MCP server" instead of "connector". No config keys, protocol fields, i18n keys or SDK exports change.

## Why This Change Was Made

On `main`, `openclaw mcp login` is offline-only (`offlineMcpAction` refuses while a Gateway owns the state) and resolves names only from `mcp.servers`. The operator OAuth identity now records whether `mcp.servers` defines the server (when the caller has config), and one helper in `mcp-oauth-identity.ts` picks the recovery text for both the browser sign-in handler and runtime OAuth errors: offline CLI steps only for `mcp.servers` entries, the plugin page for plugin-declared servers, the channel connect flow for per-requester credentials. OAuth behavior is unchanged; only messages change.

<details>
<summary>Changed strings</summary>

Gateway `mcp.authLogin` (`<name>` quoted; commands via `formatCliCommand`):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Connector sign-in requires an administrator connection. | Sign-in requires … |
| This connector cannot use operator browser sign-in. … | This MCP server cannot use operator browser sign-in. … |
| Open Settings on this Gateway to sign in, or use openclaw mcp login in its terminal. | `mcp.servers`: Open Settings …, or sign in from its terminal: *(same stop/login steps as below)*. Plugin: Open Settings on this Gateway to sign in. |
| Connector sign-in authority is no longer active. | Sign-in authority … |
| This connector changed. Close this dialog … | This MCP server changed. Close this dialog … |
| Authentication saved, … check the connector before trying again. | … check the MCP server … / … check the plugin … |
| Sign-in did not finish. Check the connector settings and try again, or run openclaw mcp login with this connector's name in this Gateway's terminal. | `mcp.servers`: Sign-in did not finish. Check the MCP server settings and try again, or sign in from this Gateway's terminal: stop the Gateway with openclaw gateway stop, run openclaw mcp login <name>, then start the Gateway again. Plugin: Sign-in did not finish. Check the plugin settings, then select Connect to try again. |

Runtime OAuth errors (`mcp-oauth.ts`, `mcp-oauth-provider.ts`): "… Run openclaw mcp login <name>." → `mcp.servers`: "… Sign in from Settings → MCP, or from the Gateway's terminal: <same steps>."; plugin: "… Select Connect on the plugin's page in Settings to sign in again."; no config at the call site: "… Sign in again from Settings: select Connect on the plugin's page, or Sign in on the MCP page."; per-requester: "… Reconnect from the channel through the MCP connect flow."

Control UI English: composer menu **Connectors** → **Plugins** (`chat.composer.menu.connectors`); `mcpServers.signInFailed`, `mcpServers.requesterSignIn`, `toolAccess.noTools` and `adminBlocked` now say "MCP server(s)" instead of "connector(s)".

Other copy: composer config-write note `composer connectors: add MCP server <name>` → `composer plugins: add MCP server <name>`; generated Slack app manifest description `<name> connector for OpenClaw` → `<name> app for OpenClaw` (free text; new manifests only); private `@openclaw/mcp-relay` package description and README "connector" → "plugin".

Docs follow the same wording; `docs/tools/mcp.md` now shows `openclaw gateway stop` before terminal sign-in and states the CLI covers only `mcp.servers`; `docs/web/control-ui/settings.md` says plugin-declared servers sign in from the plugin page (**Accounts** → **Connect**). The renamed `docs/date-time.md` heading keeps its old anchor.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Intentionally unchanged and follow-ups</summary>

Identifiers and contracts left alone:

- i18n keys (`menu.connectors`, `menu.noConnectors`), composer menu view id `"connectors"`, item values (`open-connectors`, `connector:<name>`, …) and `connectorItems()`.
- Package names, keywords, config keys, wire/protocol names: none renamed.
- Native Apple apps (`apps/shared/OpenClawKit`, `apps/ios`) still say "Connectors"; renaming needs the native string catalog and an Apple build, unavailable on this Linux host.
- Release notes (historical, release-owned).
- Third-party or unrelated meanings: Bot Framework "Bot Connector", OpenAI/Codex and Claude/ChatGPT connectors, `api.connectors.invoke`, Cloudflare tunnel connectors, package names, undici/TLS connectors, `ReplyConnector`, grammatical connectors.

Follow-ups (behavior, out of scope for this copy PR):

- `openclaw mcp login` cannot sign in to plugin-declared servers and refuses while the Gateway runs (CLI change).
- Root cause of the generic failure in the report: the `mcp.authLogin` ownership check compares the whole plugin metadata snapshot, so an unrelated plugin reload aborts sign-in.

</details>

## Evidence

Before:

![Composer + menu before: Connectors entry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e23b37b6-46d8-4cd1-b12c-3cbba821b60f)

![Plugin sign-in failure before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69d0bf3a-4c6e-4f2d-91e8-a2720832811e)

After:

![Composer + menu after: Plugins entry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bb9ed21-34d1-4bc1-87a5-deb2fbe3c9ca)

![Plugin sign-in failure after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25e5450c-e9dd-4c6b-9b50-0714aa61c9da)

Real Control UI, UI E2E harness, mocked Gateway.

- CLI behavior on `main`: `mcp login` is wrapped in `offlineMcpAction` (`onForeignOwner: "refuse"`) and `requireMcpServer` resolves only `mcp.servers`. A throwaway Vitest run of the real `registerMcpCli` with an enabled bundle plugin declaring `linear` printed `No MCP server named "linear" in …/openclaw.json.`
- `src/gateway/server.mcp-auth-login.test.ts` asserts the exact `mcp.servers` failure text (`openclaw gateway stop`, `openclaw mcp login docs`) and the plugin text; `src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts` asserts the runtime error for an `mcp.servers` entry (quoted `'Remote Docs'`) and for a plugin-declared server. All fail on `main`. Gateway 30/30 + OAuth 14/14 in 70s (proxy env unset; host proxy breaks the loopback OAuth fixture independently).
- OAuth consumers (`mcp-oauth-*`, `mcp-transport*`, `mcp-event-request`, `mcp-cli.oauth*`): 81 tests passed, 34s.
- `ui/src/components/mcp-servers-card.test.ts`: passed, 4.3s. `extensions/slack/src/setup-surface.test.ts`: 19/19, 16.9s.
- UI E2E `chat-composer-capability-menu`, `chat-skill-library`, `new-session-page.capability-menu`, `new-session-page.config-startup`: 19/19, 59s.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (1099s on the final tree): format, i18n catalog, docs, ratchets and every typecheck (core, core tests, UI, extensions, extension tests) green. Failures are all outside this diff: `max-lines` lint errors in 16 untouched files, the max-lines suppression ratchet (3 untouched UI files), unused exports in untouched files, and the core test shard root budget (726/749 vs advisory 720).
- Autoreview (Codex, up to P2) on both commits: no findings ("patch is correct", 0.9 / 0.92).

title: fix(ui): right-click pinned agents to open the full agent menu
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pinned agents in the sidebar agent roster show a kebab button whose menu only offers Create Claw, so you can't unpin a pinned agent, open its Settings or Sessions, or delete it.

## User Impact

User impact: right-clicking a pinned agent (or pressing Shift+F10 / the context-menu key while it is focused) opens the same agent menu that unpinned roster rows use: Unpin, Sessions, Create Claw when Claws are enabled, Settings, and Delete. Pinned tiles no longer show a kebab. The pin item reads **Pin** with an outlined pin for unpinned agents and **Unpin** with a filled pin for pinned agents. Unpinned rows keep their kebab and also open the menu on right-click.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pinned tiles and roster rows now build their menu from one shared item list and selection handler, so the two surfaces can't drift apart again. Right-click and the keyboard shortcut open that menu at the pointer through the existing point-anchored menu trigger, the same way session rows open their context menus. Unpinning moves keyboard focus to the agent's roster row, matching how pinning focuses the new tile.

Touch: Android long-press fires `contextmenu`, so the menu opens there. iOS Safari doesn't fire it, so pinned tiles on iOS have no menu. That matches the menu-less pinned gallery from before Create Claw added a kebab.

title: fix(ui): page-wide focus ring after uninstalling a plugin in Safari
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Safari and the macOS app, an accent focus ring outlines the whole plugin page after you click **Uninstall** and confirm the removal.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b101421a-141e-49b0-9e7f-4edfae74d942)

## User Impact

User impact: removing a plugin by mouse no longer draws a page-sized ring around the plugin hub. Plugin settings and Skill workshop use the same page container and get the same fix. Keyboard focus is unchanged: the page wrappers stop being an extra Tab stop, and the controls inside them stay focusable.

## Why This Change Was Made

macOS WebKit doesn't focus a button when you click it. Mousedown focuses the nearest focusable ancestor instead. On the plugin pages that ancestor was the page-level `role="tabpanel"` wrapper, which got `tabindex="0"` when the Web Awesome tab panels were replaced (#169901). The confirm dialog returned focus to that wrapper when it closed. WebKit treats script-restored focus as `:focus-visible`, so the global accent outline covered the whole page while the uninstall was pending.

These wrappers hold whole pages of focusable controls, so they don't need their own Tab stop. The ARIA tabs pattern only asks for `tabindex=0` on panels with no focusable content. Without it, focus falls through to the shell's `#control-ui-main` anchor. That anchor already has `tabindex=-1` and never paints a ring.

## Evidence

Before: focus lands on `#plugins-hub-panel` and the ring paints (matches the report)

![Before: accent ring around the plugin page during uninstall](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a17de308-33c0-414b-83ba-4b1dfe2b4df3)

After: focus lands on `#control-ui-main` and no ring paints

![After: no ring during uninstall](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b01888ac-6a58-4cd6-8da0-8aadf039412c)

Screenshots come from the Control UI e2e harness in Chromium with mock Gateway data. An init script makes button clicks behave like macOS WebKit: no button focus, and the nearest focusable ancestor takes focus. Chromium's `:focus-visible` heuristic differs from WebKit's, so the captures force `:focus-visible` on whichever element holds focus. That shows what WebKit paints. Real Safari and the macOS app were not run.

- New regression test in `ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts`, "does not leave page-level focus on the plugin panel after a pointer removal". It fails on main (`expected 'plugins-hub-panel' to be 'control-ui-main'`) and passes with the fix.
- The whole `plugins-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` file passes (10 tests), including the existing keyboard-focus removal tests for the hub and settings pages.
- Autoreview: clean, no findings.

title: fix(ui): plugin card flashes Install after a successful install
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after installing a plugin from the Plugins catalog, the card briefly switched back to **Install** before showing the green enabled dot.

## User Impact

User impact: when an install finishes, its catalog card goes straight from installing to its installed state (for example, the green enabled dot), with no stray **Install** button in between.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ad4a16c3-06d4-4dae-afa4-e9b055544777)

## Why This Change Was Made

The card read its installed state only from the cached ClawHub catalog page. When the install finished, the card dropped its progress state and showed that stale page, which still said "not installed", until `plugins.catalog.browse` refreshed. That refresh can take seconds.

Now the card uses the installed inventory, matched by `catalogId`, whenever that inventory has an entry for it. The `plugins.install` and `plugins.setEnabled` responses carry the same `catalogId` as `plugins.list`, so the row the UI merges from the install result still links to its card. Before this change, that link was missing until the next `plugins.list` read. The protocol docs are updated to match.

## Evidence

- New Control UI E2E test (`install-progress.e2e.test.ts`, "shows a catalog card as installed when its install succeeds"): installs from a catalog card while holding the follow-up `config.get`, `plugins.list`, and `plugins.catalog.browse` reads. It **fails on `main`** (the card still shows Install) and passes with this change. The other four install-progress E2E cases still pass.
- New Gateway test (`plugins-mutations.test.ts`): checks that `plugins.install` (ClawHub) and `plugins.setEnabled` (local) results include the `catalogId` that `plugins.list` returns. It **fails on `main`** and passes with this change. `plugins.test.ts` and `plugins-mutations.test.ts` pass (59 tests).
- Catalog card right after `plugins.install` succeeds, while the ClawHub catalog refresh is held ([capture notes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180163#issuecomment-6330917119)):

  **Before** (`main`): Install button

  ![Catalog card showing Install after a successful install](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36b1a46c-c480-4d67-885c-b5ccb72b60e6)

  **After**: green enabled dot

  ![Catalog card showing the enabled dot after a successful install](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8928e43-fd94-4c89-b3e0-6a81f4821ef9)
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck and the other guards pass. Two guards also fail on `main` without this change: the max-lines suppression ratchet fails even with no diff (`--base HEAD`), flagging `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`; the core tsgo shard root budget is over for `gateway-root` and `infra`; and the dead-export scan reports existing unused exports elsewhere. This PR adds no test files and no new dead-export findings. It also makes the two discovery-ID encoders private now that `pluginCatalogId` is their only caller.
- Test cost: the new E2E case takes about 1.0s in the existing suite fixture. The two Gateway cases take under 10ms each.

title: fix(ui): Side chat exchanges look different from the main chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Side chat exchanges look different from the main chat. Answers end with a bespoke "as of 6:17 PM" line instead of the message footer, a divider separates exchanges, questions have no footer, and the spacing differs.

## User Impact

User impact: Side chat now reads like the main chat. Questions and answers use the main chat bubbles, spacing, and hover footer (sender, relative time with the full date on hover, Copy), and there are no dividers between exchanges. The "as of" line is gone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Side chat drew its own question bubble, answer markup, "as of" line, divider, and gaps. It now renders each question and answer through the main transcript's `MessageGroup`, and the pending state through the main chat's working group (`StreamGroup`), so those parts have one owner. Each group keeps the main chat's turn gap and footer row; the panel only collapses the avatar column, like the main chat at narrow widths.

Identity follows the main chat's rule for a one-person, one-agent thread: names live in the hover footer, and the asker's own name is not repeated. The Reply action is not offered because Side chat exchanges have no reply target.

Questions don't record their own send time in Side chat history, so a loaded question shows its exchange's time. Questions asked in the open tab show when they were sent.

The retired `chat.rail.asOf` string, the bespoke question/answer/timestamp selectors, and the tests pinned to them are removed.

title: fix(ui): align trailing sidebar badges with the archive action
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the sidebar session list, a row's resting PR icon (and other trailing badges) sat flush against the sidebar's right edge, 6px right of the pin/archive actions that appear on hover. Trailing icons did not line up in one column.

## User Impact

User impact: trailing row icons (PR state, cloud, approval, viewer, and timer metadata) now sit in the same column as the archive button. Hovering a row no longer makes the right edge jump between icon positions. In a single owner's inline list, the trailing status glyph (unread, running) moves into that column too.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hover actions are 24px buttons that end at the row's trailing padding, so the 14px archive glyph centers 16px from the edge. The trailing metadata endcap ended at that same padding, so a 12px badge centered 10px from the edge. On desktop rows with a hover pointer, the endcap now gets `(24px - 12px) / 2` of inline-end padding when it has visible content. The inline owner list's trailing 20px status slot gets `(24px - 20px) / 2` of margin.

Scope and tradeoffs:
- Touch (`hover: none` / `pointer: coarse`), the mobile drawer, team roster rows, and child rows keep their current geometry because their actions are always visible or use a different column.
- An empty endcap gets no padding, so rows without trailing metadata keep their full title width.
- Rows with a `› N` child toggle keep the toggle as the rightmost control. Its column is unchanged.

title: fix(ui): announce unavailable audio previews to screen readers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary audio attachments disappear into a download-only card without an accessible failure status when their inline preview becomes unavailable.

## User Impact

Screen-reader users get the affected filename and “Preview unavailable” through a polite status region. The existing download action remains available; playback behavior and visible layout are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Derive the announcement from the existing media-source readiness owner in a persistent, screen-reader-only region. Clear it when the source recovers or changes, keep preparing states quiet, and preserve voice notes’ existing single announcement. Reuse localized unavailable copy rather than adding translation keys or playback state.

The change adds nine net production lines and 25 net test lines. No new effects, listeners, state owner, network policy, or dependency is introduced.

## Evidence

- The extended existing audio-failure regression fails against production base `d220033a2cee0c153875ed866be024eefba8de04` because the status is absent, then passes with the repair. The accessibility tree exposes one polite, atomic status containing “briefing.wav: Preview unavailable,” with the download preserved. Replacing the source with a valid synthetic WAV clears the same status node and keyboard playback succeeds. No page errors.

title: fix(ui): session links show "Panel failed to load" during Gateway suspension
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a Control UI session link while the Gateway is suspending for a deploy (or restarting or starting) shows **Panel failed to load** with the raw `sessions.resolve unavailable during gateway suspension` detail, and the page stays broken until someone clicks **Retry**.

## User Impact

User impact: while the Gateway is suspending, restarting, or starting, the page shows the existing **Starting up** status and loads by itself once the Gateway accepts work again. Real failures still show the error card with **Retry**.

## Why This Change Was Made

During a suspension drain the Gateway refuses new requests with a structured, retryable `UNAVAILABLE` error (`reason: gateway-suspending`; restarts and startup use `gateway-restarting` / `startup-sidecars`). Panel refreshes already treat these as transient (#141040), and the route outlet already waits out agent-database preparation with a calm state and backoff (#164532), but the outlet only recognized the database case. It now uses the shared `isAwaitingGatewayFailure` classification, so route loads get the same wait-and-revalidate behavior.

Retries reuse the existing outlet backoff (server `retryAfterMs`, capped at 5 s) and stop on navigation, disconnect, or retry-context change. The **Starting up** copy is reused unchanged; the footer connection indicator still names the suspension or restart.

## Evidence

- Live incident on the Team Gateway (2026-10-22 UTC): the release deployer's `gateway.suspend.prepare` closed admission at 00:20:16; `sessions.resolve` was rejected with `unavailable during gateway suspension` from 00:20:21 to 00:20:48; the Gateway restarted at 00:20:52 and was ready at 00:23:12, after which `sessions.resolve` succeeded. The opened tab stayed on the error card until a manual Retry.
- New e2e scenario in `ui/src/e2e/chat-loading-deadlines.e2e.test.ts` ("waits through a Gateway suspension, then opens a short session link"): fails on main (error card, no automatic retry), passes with the fix; the whole file passes 10/10.
- New outlet unit test in `router-outlet-presentation.test.tsx`: fails on main, passes with the fix; router-outlet suites pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint on changed files, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `git diff --check`.

title: fix: sharing edits abort running turns in other sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in-flight agent turns and scheduled automation runs in *other* sessions abort with `source execution authority is no longer active | Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. | SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` whenever anyone adds/removes a session member or changes a session's visibility.

## User Impact

User impact: sharing a session (`session.members.add/remove`, `session.visibility.set`) no longer kills long-running turns elsewhere on the Gateway. Previously a multi-minute automation could be aborted at any point by an unrelated sharing edit.

## Why This Change Was Made

`publishSharingChange` emits two `sessions.changed` notifications: a keyed one for the changed session and an unkeyed one so draft recipients refresh their redacted catalog. The unkeyed call also published `{ all: true, scope: "sessions" }` into `sessionChanges`. Every prepared delivery generation (`prepareSessionGenerationLease` in `src/config/sessions/session-delivery-generation.ts`) treats an unscoped `all` change as invalidation, so every in-flight run that held a generation lease was revoked.

The keyed notification (and the storage owner's member fact) already covers the changed session, so the catalog refresh is now emitted as a prepared publication, the same way `sessions.delete` emits its unkeyed list refresh. The redacted broadcast and the access-revision bump are unchanged.

Accepted edge case: the changed session's *own* in-flight turn still re-validates on its keyed change; this PR only stops the cross-session blast radius.

## Evidence

- Production incident (Team Gateway, 2026.10.5, same code on current `main`): at 23:22:31.868 UTC `session.members.add` completed, and within 1–8 s two cron turns in two different dashboard sessions failed with `admitted run authority is no longer active | … SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE`, followed by `source execution authority is no longer active` on the fallback attempt. No restart, config change or storage fault was involved.
- New regression test `keeps other sessions' in-flight delivery generations when membership changes` in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-sharing.test.ts` drives the real `session.members.add` handler against real SQLite state while another session holds a prepared delivery generation. Red on base (`SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError` after the add), green with the fix.
- `sessions-sharing.test.ts` (12/12) plus consumer suites `sessions-public-share`, `sessions-read-cache`, `sessions-sharing.identities`, `sessions-sharing-identities`, `sessions-sharing.patch-worker`, `session-catalog-share-route`, `chat-history-retained-sharing`, `session-change-event*` (10 files, 83/83) pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt clean on touched files.
- Gap: no isolated-Gateway live replay of the incident; test-project typecheck shards are left to PR CI.

title: fix(crabbox): reject incompatible Windows profile setup before allocation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native Windows Crabbox provisioning failing after allocation when an OS override reuses a Linux/POSIX profile setup command in PowerShell.

## User Impact

Incompatible setup/OS combinations are rejected before allocation and omitted from OS and machine choices. To use native Windows with setup, select a profile targeting `windows/normal` with compatible PowerShell setup. Profiles without setup keep all backend-supported choices; POSIX-to-POSIX overrides remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Profile setup belongs to its configured interpreter. Discovery and provisioning now share one compatibility rule, rather than silently dropping or guessing how to translate a setup script. No new config, SDK, dependency, schema, or live Gateway changes.

## Evidence

- The added provider regressions fail on the base (3 failures) and pass with the fix; they cover preallocation rejection in both directions, compatible setup preservation, no-setup Windows selection, and profile-specific catalog filtering without poisoning the shared catalog.
- `pnpm test extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider-platforms.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **11 passed**, 57.34 s wall time including a cold compiled-worker build.
- `pnpm test extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **67 passed**, 12.30 s wall time. The 78 total tests retain the original provider coverage; platform cases were extracted to respect the line-cap gate and remain in the database-worker lane.
- Focused typecheck, targeted lint/format checks, staged line-cap ratchet, routing syntax, `git diff --check`, and docs link audit passed (15,790 links; 0 broken).
- Independent Auto Review: complete, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The new platform file executed its 11 cases in approximately 69 ms locally. CI-seconds are unmeasured; incremental test-body execution is estimated under 0.1 s per lane, with additional file startup/compilation overhead not included or measured in hosted CI.

**Validation limits:** provider/catalog boundary proof mocks external allocation; no new VM or live Windows enrollment was run. The broader Crabbox lane had 782 passes, 10 skips, and 5 Linux XFCE bootstrap-fixture failures in 259.65 s. All five also reproduced on unchanged base production source `9102fe6c62051f888f2ebc60873f235e2553650d`; those failures remain unresolved. The broader lane was not rerun after test-only relocation. One earlier test attempt hit a compiled-subprocess allocator crash before collection; an unchanged retry passed, not claimed as a fix.

### Review follow-up: proof scope and upgrade behavior

The original defect was observed through the real conversation `crabbox` tool on Azure before this patch: `create` with `os=windows/normal` and `machineClass=tiny` reached profile setup, where PowerShell rejected a POSIX `>&2` expression with `ParserError / ExpectedExpression`. That is live **pre-fix failure evidence**, not a successful Windows test of this candidate. No private profile script or credentials are included here.

| Review question | Evidence and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Rejection without allocation | The committed regressions enter the real Crabbox provider and assert `invalid_profile` plus an empty external command log in both interpreter directions. `prepareProvision` resolves the profile before binary resolution and before its allocation closure. This is provider-boundary proof, not a captured tool/Gateway end-to-end run of the candidate. |
| Compatible Windows behavior | A Windows-targeted profile retains its PowerShell setup byte-for-byte and executes the setup operation once in the provider harness. A profile without setup can still select native Windows. External allocation/enrollment is mocked, so this does **not** prove a live Windows VM enrolls. |
| Existing profiles after update | The PR does not change config parsing/schema, Doctor, persisted state, snapshot keys, inspection, or teardown. Existing profiles keep their configured target and setup. The intentional change is at discovery/new provisioning: profiles with setup may no longer override across the POSIX/PowerShell boundary, even if an individual command happens to be portable. Use a separate target-specific profile when crossing that boundary. This is a source-backed compatibility assessment, **not** an executed latest-stable-to-candidate upgrade. |

Source bindings for the reviewed head: [preallocation guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1bcd865e198c76800067d0c80d78c88d64ba844c/extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.ts#L189-L214), [regression assertions and compatible controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1bcd865e198c76800067d0c80d78c88d64ba844c/extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider-platforms.test.ts#L42-L85).

ClawSweeper reported no findings and no before-merge blockers; its entry-point/upgrade request is listed as an optional rank-up improvement. The live Windows and actual upgrade checks remain **unrun**, not replaced or declared passed by the tests above. No source change or duplicate test run was made solely to improve a rating.

title: fix(ui): sidebar session titles misalign when a row shows a status glyph
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the sidebar's single-owner session list ("My sessions" with Group by Person), titles of running, unread, flagged, or failed sessions sat 28px right of idle titles because their status glyph took a leading slot, and the first row sat 23px below the owner picker.

## User Impact

User impact: every session title in that list starts at the same edge. Status glyphs (unread dot, run spinner, question, flag, failure, custom icon, draft ghost) now sit on the row's trailing edge next to the existing PR, cloud, and viewer badges. The first session sits closer to the owner picker (11px instead of 23px). Other sidebar views are unchanged; they already reserve a leading status column for every row.

## Why This Change Was Made

#178846 removed the empty leading status slot in this view so idle titles line up with the owner picker, but rows with a status kept the slot. The status slot now moves to the trailing edge with flex `order`. On hover (and always in the mobile drawer), the reserved space for row actions moves from the title to the link, so the trailing status slides left of the pin/archive buttons instead of being hidden under them.

Known tradeoffs:
- On rows with child sessions, the status sits left of the `› N` child toggle, so status glyphs do not form one strict column.
- The fork glyph is part of the title label and still prefixes "Forked" titles.
- On hover, crowded rows with an avatar, a badge, and status give up more title width.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar group options button tooltip reads "Group options for <group name>", repeating the group name that is already shown in the header right next to the button.

## User Impact

User impact: hovering the `…` button on a sidebar session group now shows a short "Group options" tooltip. Screen readers still announce "Group options for <group>", so repeated group buttons stay distinguishable.

The button's `title` now uses a new `sessionsView.groupOptions` string, and `aria-label` keeps the existing `sessionsView.groupMenu` copy. The accessible name stays row-specific on purpose, matching #178140, which gave repeated row buttons row-specific names. The shared tooltip renders `title`, so only the visible hint changes. title: feat(auth): allow write access without personal credential enrollment
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared Gateway operators need ordinary write access without letting teammates enroll personal credentials outside their managed credential system.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/3049

## User Impact

Adds opt-in `operator.write.no-credential-enrollment`. It blocks personal model-provider API-key/token/OAuth enrollment and personal GitHub publication OAuth enrollment, including reconnects and pending credential installation after permission is withdrawn. Ordinary writes, saved-account use, account status, and disconnection remain available. Shared credential setup remains admin-only.

**GitHub identity/co-authorship is not a publication credential.** Verified GitHub identity from supported sign-in, profile editing, and the Git co-author credit preference remain available. This does not add a manual identity-linking/OAuth feature or make an arbitrary proxy username a verified GitHub account; OCE’s ingress must use an already-supported verified identity path.

Existing `operator.read`, `operator.write`, admin, and default grants retain their behavior. Legacy read permits personal GitHub enrollment, so restricted roles must not also grant it. Grant only the non-enrolling scope, and review unioned device grants or apply a role ceiling. Adding legacy read restores GitHub enrollment; adding full write/admin restores all enrollment. Already-saved credentials, their refresh, and existing session selections are not revoked. This is an API guardrail, not isolation from unrestricted host execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared scope owner keeps grant containment separate from action eligibility. Full write includes restricted write, never the reverse. Because legacy read includes GitHub enrollment, the `operator.read.no-credential-enrollment` subset represents ordinary reads when read authority is capped by restricted write. Without that representable subset, intersection, cookies, or synthetic calls could restore enrollment or lose ordinary read capabilities.

Enrollment retains its original full-write (model providers) or legacy-read (GitHub) authority through provider I/O and credential persistence. Existing Gateway, tool, UI/native, and bundled-plugin adapters consume ordinary action requirements without manufacturing broader grants. No new policy store, database migration, config switch, dependency, or protocol-version change. Simplification keeps one action/grant owner rather than a deny flag or parallel policy; ordinary-read adapters are necessary because legacy read itself enrolls GitHub credentials.

## Evidence

- **2026-10-22 review refresh — a7d517ce8456b9df0feaed8a817a21083745e3bb:** rebased onto `a68d0eb252586b11412bced0ef41e41e5fc6e798`, preserving the scope lattice and upstream self-profile/UI owner behavior. Addressed the production-effect proof request by reproducing four unwanted GitHub HTTP dispatches after authority withdrawal, then carrying the transport’s existing live-authority callback through personal and System/agent device flows. Existing credential-install/store guards remain intact.
- **New execution proof:** 10 GitHub final-effect cases pass through real lifecycle/parser/profile/SQLite owners using a synthetic loopback issuer; 3 shipped-provider/private-store cases pass, including successful real-WebSocket API-key enrollment and withdrawal at transaction/commit admission. This is not genuine external GitHub OAuth, remote provider key validity, or model inference. The final effect/lifecycle rerun passes 54 tests (108.24s); the profile cleanup rerun passes 31 tests (8.67s). The earlier 295-test focused run (162.32s) is separate, not an additional distinct-test count. Six conflict-resolution consumer files also pass 109 tests (48.20s).
- **Current local gates:** core and Control UI production types, Gateway root/server and profile-page test types, targeted typed lint, formatting, and whitespace pass. Independent canonical Auto Review of the complete integration and final repair found no actionable P0–P2 findings; review was static and limited to supplied source/delta, not reviewer execution. [Detailed review response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179959#issuecomment-6353908519).
- **Still unverified:** genuine external OAuth, native builds/device execution, and the stable 2026.10.6 account/selection upgrade lane. The maintained upgrade runner requires Docker, unavailable here; a Podman substitution awaits Sally’s decision. No feature-owned schema migration is introduced, but an upgrade result is not inferred from that fact. Existing screenshots and the live recording below remain historical evidence, not captures of this refresh.

- [Live Gateway recording and result matrix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179959#issuecomment-6346078709) on `3150e352715d`: real browser/WebSocket requests, profile/co-author preference API readback, and four direct enrollment denials under restricted write. Synthetic trusted-proxy principals; legacy controls intentionally stop at schema validation. This supplements screenshots, not external OAuth or OCE/OpenShell qualification.

- 2026-10-22 conflict rebase onto `c5650f3a5e59d6523c913a8ebfff2b787cf58435`: preserved upstream profile/GitHub owner refactors and web-push inlining. The 27-file focused matrix passes (577 tests), four additional profile/GitHub lifecycle files pass (35 tests), and both production-built browser grant scenarios pass. Fresh canonical independent Auto Review completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 across the supplied candidate delta; no reviewer test execution or unchanged-context qualification is claimed. The retained router, real-Gateway, and lifecycle regressions now cover start/poll denial, ordinary status/profile reads, legacy-grant compatibility, and in-flight role withdrawal before credential installation.

title: fix: let members edit their own profile without general write access
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Members with read-only or session-scoped access cannot edit their own display name or avatar in Settings → Profile.

## User Impact

Members can change their own display name, avatar, and Git co-author credit preference without receiving general write or administrator access. Roles, verified identity links, profile merges, other people's profiles, and server-wide settings remain protected. Server upload restrictions still apply. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing self-or-admin profile mutation guard rather than requiring broad write access for cosmetic changes. The Profile editor now follows its personal access boundary, and session-only image requests can retrieve only the authenticated person's avatar. Identity-derived HTTP responses now retain the existing profile-authority guard through their final response boundary, so reassigning a sign-in alias while avatar bytes are loading cannot disclose the old profile’s image. Shared-secret owner attribution and cosmetic edits keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

**Landing verification (October 22):** exact head `9629691c6354204d543155dac2f26ad26b31f6de` passed the CI gate ([terminal job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39843751376/job/120061282383)); its log reports no failed or timed-out prerequisite jobs. The exact-head security-sensitive review and protected CI status are successful. [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179924#issuecomment-6327547975) completed on this head with no actionable findings; the prior avatar-fixture finding is resolved. Earlier failed runs and local review-tool limitations below remain historical evidence, not claims that those attempts passed. Gideon requested landing after review.

- Original self-edit regression: the three narrow-scope cases failed on the base with missing operator.write, then passed with the fix. The expanded owning worker suite now passes all 17 cases (see current-head evidence below).
- 95 related Gateway tests, 38 profile UI tests, and 21 registry/shared-scope tests passed.
- Browser member flow passed for display-name editing, refresh, and credit preference changes.
- An isolated real Gateway passed member name/avatar editing, cross-tab name updates, and avatar persistence after reload.
- Core/UI production typechecks and the Gateway-methods/root/server, UI-pages, and browser-E2E test typechecks passed, as did formatting, documentation MDX checks, and git diff --check.
- Prior-head targeted lint reported an inherited max-lines violation in core-descriptors.ts (701 counted lines; limit 700). Refreshed conflict-resolution lint passes; that historical result is not current-head broad CI evidence.
- [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179924#issuecomment-6327547975) completed on `62e6e3ec1acae537e17f340fb28e79fe09872f2f`: no actionable findings, no security attention items, and authority-boundary proof marked sufficient. The PR has now been marked ready so normal behavioral CI can run. That ClawSweeper assessment applies to the earlier head. The refreshed head now also has a completed P0-only Auto Review; no broad CI pass is claimed.
- Inspected synthetic before/after screenshots are embedded below and were also delivered to the originating conversation.

### Avatar CI fixture repair (October 22)

Published `9629691c6354204d543155dac2f26ad26b31f6de`: only the two avatar consumer test files changed (+9/-3). All three successful-auth stubs now explicitly carry `operator.read`, including the delayed-authorization Gravatar case. Production authorization and test assertions are unchanged.

- Before repair, ordinary avatar cases reproduced the `scopes.includes` TypeError; the bounded red run was stopped after the failure also prevented later waiters from completing.
- After repair, both owning consumer suites plus the real avatar-authority suite pass: **3 files / 45 tests**. The Gateway-root test typecheck, focused lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- A fresh Auto Review could not be verified: the explicit-base attempt failed during target preparation and the subsequent managed-local attempt was interrupted. This is not a clean-review claim. The requester explicitly asked to publish the validated fixture repair after that limitation was disclosed.
- Earlier head `8d75f97e18fc6b760bb0ae4ecc765fb24a98e8ce` also had a failed shard 27 ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39831911362/job/120011171198)). Its managed log omits the earlier failing invocation; `pnpm test:ci-failed 179924` cannot retrieve full logs in this environment because `gh` is unavailable. That failure remains unclassified, not attributed to main or declared fixed by this update. New-head CI must establish the remaining result.

### Co-author consent and ownership verification (October 22)

Added four preservation cases for credit **off/on**, both **before/during** own-PR inspection through the admitted agent tool and real Gateway dispatcher. Canonical preference writes leave the profile/verified identity snapshot unchanged. A fresh own-author check still succeeds and a mismatching GitHub author ID remains rejected; inspection performs no external writes.

A consent change during an already-prepared inspection is **not invisible**: the shared profile-authority fence makes that in-flight request return a retryable profile-verification error. A fresh inspection after the preference commits succeeds. This does not unlink the account, alter roles, change the PR author, or weaken the ownership comparison.

Reran the existing OIDC HTTP/WebSocket admission, multi-account sign-in/identity, publication attribution, and ownership-inspection suites: all passed. The expanded own-PR inspection file passes **26 cases**, including the four new consent cases; its typecheck and focused lint also pass. Existing publication tests exercise opt-out at preparation, before push, and before PR creation, for both local-worktree and repository-checkpoint executors, plus recovery of an unpushed commit with revoked credit.

Publication uses a retained contributor-consent snapshot. A change after that snapshot is captured stops the next guarded side effect with the contributor-credit-changed failure (protocol code `identity_changed`); already-accepted remote effects remain recorded, and existing commits/PRs are not rewritten. Review those effects and reconcile any unpushed prepared commit before requesting a new publication. A change before credit preparation is simply reflected in the newly prepared content.

These are production-owner integration tests with synthetic provider/GitHub I/O, not a live browser OAuth round trip or live GitHub write test. No production behavior changed in this test-only follow-up.

### Conflict refresh (October 22)

- Integrated pinned main `30a24bee8576b47b0d01c441ceafd509b8660e9f` without rewriting the existing PR history. Published head: `975c4df794d38e814e8f679ddcc7be211153ec36`.
- The sole textual conflict was main extracting the profile state owner into `ui/src/pages/profile/profile-state.ts`. Kept main’s `profile-page.tsx` byte-for-byte and moved the existing self-edit permission changes into that new owner. Its action/optimistic presentation and request-retirement lifecycle remain intact; no duplicate inline state owner remains.
- Updated the mock member name-save fixture to hold the actual mutation response instead of pre-changing the self-profile response before Save. The original Save/refresh/credit assertions are retained.
- Refreshed proof on Node 26.12.1 with a normal frozen dependency install: **39 UI tests; 58 authority tests; mocked member browser flow; isolated real-Gateway name/avatar/reload flow; core and UI production typechecks; browser-test typecheck; focused lint and formatting all passed.**
- Fresh Auto Review completed across all five planned chunks: no P0 findings (P0-only scope). Prior ClawSweeper review below remains prior-head evidence, not a review of this refreshed head.

### Final-effect authority proof (October 22)

Production-boundary tests added for the newly admitted principals; no authority decision or persistence operation is mocked:

| Boundary | Principal/scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Same byte-response boundary | Cosmetic display-name update | HTTP 200 and original PNG returned. |

The HTTP fixture fixes only external identity-provider replies and uses in-memory HTTP transport; production profile storage, avatar loading, and final authorization remain real. The worker fixture changes the live caller at native commit admission, then reads persisted profile snapshots. This is deterministic boundary evidence, not a live identity-provider test.

**Red → green:** the new alias-reassignment assertion returned HTTP 200 on the previous implementation, then HTTP 401 with the retained-profile guard. Role revocation already rejected correctly. No new role, schema, setting, cache, or authorization owner was introduced.

title: fix(ui): plan usage stays stale after chat runs
body:
Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the chat composer’s plan-usage popover keeps showing old subscription usage after runs finish.

## User Impact

User impact: subscription users can see updated plan usage after a run without reloading the page. Idle chats do not poll, and refresh failures preserve the last displayed usage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI retained the `models.authStatus` response until the OAuth token approached expiry, so usage did not age out independently. The Gateway also serves usage through a 60-second stale-while-revalidate cache, meaning a refresh request can initially return the previous snapshot.

After each run, the chat requests usage only when its Gateway-provided freshness deadline has elapsed. Ordinary reads stay nonblocking. The existing Gateway usage-cache owner enforces the same lifetime, coalesces provider work, and awaits cold/stale usage for post-run requests without broad auth/catalog refresh or a delayed second read.

`models.usage.cacheTtlMs` configures reuse (default `60000`; `0` disables it). For example, `{ "models": { "usage": { "cacheTtlMs": 120000 } } }` selects two minutes. The setting is documented in one sentence and config-field help; generated config-baseline growth of two paths is intentional for the requested `models.usage` object and `cacheTtlMs` leaf. No migration is required; existing configurations retain the 60-second default.

Codex-backed OpenAI usage first reuses fresh quota notifications from a live shared client with the exact profile/account binding, agent scope, start configuration, and desktop generation. Hits start no child and send no quota RPC. Stale, mismatched, native-home, and setup/runtime-artifact capture contexts retain the existing isolated read. The protocol's sparse-notification contract was checked in sibling Codex `092d3ac`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/account.rs:657`.

There is no idle polling. With stable credentials/config and healthy reads, rapid turns reuse one browser request and Gateway provider fetch per configured interval and scope, instead of forcing a provider fetch per turn. Initial ordinary and post-run modes may each issue one RPC; ordinary reads never wait behind a pending usage fetch. Explicit auth refresh and invalidation may bypass reuse. Provider fallback/auth-refresh paths can add requests. Accepted tradeoff: an inactive Codex notification reused near expiry can be nearly two cache lifetimes old when the Gateway entry expires; this avoids adding another timestamp/persistence contract. Existing credential resolution may still refresh and persist OAuth credentials, but this change adds no persisted state.

Provider errors retain displayed quota; retired connection/session responses are ignored. Provider accounting delays can still leave values unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Adds regression coverage for pasted text attachments disappearing from model context on follow-up turns, as reported in [this X thread](https://x.com/steipete/status/2112989437110227423).

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The existing durable-context fix in #167938 is already present in v2026.10.5 and current main. This PR protects that behavior; it does not reconstruct context previously discarded by an older build.

## Why This Change Was Made

The former prompt path temporarily substituted enriched text while retaining only the original caption and attachment reference for replay. The existing fix records the first model-facing text on the canonical user turn and reuses it on later requests.

Existing projection tests use prepared prompt strings. This regression starts with a >1,000-character base64 pasted-text attachment, runs the real parser and text extractor, persists the user turn before dispatch, and checks complete provider-bound text on the first request, a follow-up, and a reopened session. The assistant deliberately does not echo the supplied fact. The visible transcript keeps its caption and attachment metadata.

Simplification: reuse the existing attachment, transcript, session, and prompt owners; no new runtime state or compatibility path. Production delta: **0 lines**. Test/routing delta: **162 added lines**. A separate test file keeps the existing projection suite within its lint limit.

title: feat(baseten): support elephant-1 and mammoth-1 decisions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Baseten users cannot select or evaluate Base Labs' elephant-1 and mammoth-1 through OpenClaw's Decision role.

## User Impact

Adds both models as decision-only choices using the existing Baseten credential. They support Boolean probabilities, choices, and ordered scores without changing the chat catalog or onboarding default. Requires a host/plugin release with prepared Decision V2 support; no new configuration option or dependency.

**Verification limitation:** authenticated live proof remains unrun because no Baseten credential is available. After this limitation was disclosed, @vincentkoc renewed the instruction to land on October 24, 2026. This is not a claim of live endpoint verification. Required CI and security checks are green on the reviewed head.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both models use native System One, not Chat Completions. One plugin-local adapter uses prepared auth, guarded HTTP, request deadlines, and live dispatch admission; it translates typed rubrics and preserves probabilities, fractional scores, backend identity, and token usage. The existing Decision host remains the sole capability owner; no new tool or core API is introduced. The two models share one protocol, so keeping them in one narrowly scoped PR avoids duplicate adapters.

Verified public model slugs:
- `decision-models/baseten-elephant-9b-latest`
- `decision-models/baseten-mammoth-27b-latest`

Sources: [supported models](https://docs.baseten.co/inference/model-apis/decision-models), [System One request/response contract](https://docs.baseten.co/reference/inference-api/system-one), [launch announcement](https://www.baseten.co/blog/the-best-decision-models-in-the-world-mammoth-1-and-elephant-1/).

Public documentation does not specify hosted token limits or post-promotion rates. Those facts are intentionally omitted rather than borrowing the base model context or claiming permanent zero cost. The free-week promotion is documented separately. Decision-only models are excluded from static, live, and dynamic conversational discovery.

## Evidence

- Regression: both registered-dispatch tests failed on the base because Baseten registered no Decision provider.
- 35 focused Baseten tests pass across registration, catalog, existing chat transport, native decisions, malformed results, HTTP failures, cancellation, and authority rejection.
- Focused TypeScript check, targeted lint, formatting, docs configuration examples, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm build` succeeds. It reports a nonfatal UI startup-size advisory (318.1 KiB versus 318.0 KiB); no UI code is changed here.
- Independent Auto Review: scoped-clean at P0–P2; it did not execute tests or establish live provider compatibility. Author inspection covered the prepared Decision handoff and manifest/chat separation.
- Added opt-in live tests for a mixed Boolean/choice/score rubric on both endpoints. **Not run:** no Baseten credential available. Intended command: `BASETEN_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live -- extensions/baseten/decision-provider.live.test.ts` with the credential supplied privately in the environment.
- October 24 landing checks: `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review passed on `50356f33d9bd38929f3558596e6a35f2856265b9` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40064452707)). ClawSweeper reported no code findings but requested additional live and retirement proof; those proof limitations remain. An additional local integration experiment did not establish retirement rejection: its custom-endpoint fixture omitted required model rows, and the native-route probe reached an authentication failure with a synthetic credential. It is not included in the PR and is not counted as passing evidence.
- Simplification: one native adapter plus existing SDK HTTP/validation owners; no parallel state, retries, new provider credential store, or core capability. New code is required for the distinct System One wire contract.

title: fix(ui): new session skeleton jumps from sidebar top into its group
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: creating a session from an existing sidebar group shows its loading skeleton at the very top of the session sidebar, then the row jumps down into the group once the Gateway admits it.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4d2a33fd-1fc0-4d90-a1c2-371181b719b0)

## User Impact

User impact: a session started from a group's New session action appears in that group immediately, as the first row, and the admitted session replaces the skeleton in place without moving.

## Why This Change Was Made

The New session handoff already sends the group as `category` on `sessions.create`, but the provisional sidebar row only knew its key and title, so the session list always rendered it above every section. The handoff now carries the requested category, and the sidebar renders the skeleton as the first list item of the matching group, which is where created rows land. Creates without a rendered matching group (no group, Person/Project grouping, hidden empty group) keep the existing list-level slot; a collapsed target group hides the skeleton exactly as it hides the admitted row.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real entry point in the mocked-Gateway browser E2E (`ui/src/e2e/new-session-pending-sidebar.e2e.test.ts`): open New session with `?group=Claws`, defer `sessions.create`, start. On `main` the create carries `category: "Claws"` but the skeleton is outside the Claws section (`expected +0 to be 1`). With the fix the skeleton is the first row in Claws, and after admission the real row's top equals the skeleton's top (no jump).

title: fix(ui): put modal primary actions on the right, Cancel on the left
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: confirmation and form dialogs in the Control UI put the primary action (Delete, Save, Confirm, Retry…) on the left and Cancel on the far right, even though modal footers are right-aligned. The reported case was the "Delete group" confirm.

## User Impact

User impact: across the Control UI, modal footers now read dismissive/secondary first and the primary or destructive action last, so the action button consistently sits at the right edge and Cancel/Close/Keep sits to its left.

## Why This Change Was Made

An audit of every `<openclaw-modal-actions>` footer found 21 that rendered the primary action before the dismiss/secondary actions. Those footers are reordered; handlers, disabled states, autofocus targets and form-submit semantics are unchanged (initial focus still lands on Cancel where it did before). The ordering rule is added to the existing "Modal Completion Actions" section of `ui/AGENTS.md` so new dialogs follow it.

<details><summary>Audit: changed footers</summary>

- Shared confirm dialog (`confirm-dialog-view.tsx`): Cancel → alternative → Confirm. Covers every `showConfirmDialog` caller (delete group, archive, stop worker confirms, etc.).
- Shared input dialog (`input-dialog-view.tsx`): Cancel → Save. Covers rename group and other prompts.
- Exec/plugin approval **modal** (`exec-approval-card-solid.tsx`): Deny → Always allow → Allow once. Inline/sidebar cards are left-aligned and keep their order; mobile keeps its existing order.
- Update confirmation (confirm + failure/recovery states), session group defaults, model setup wizard footer, onboarding memory import, lazy-view error, WhatsApp channel setup footer, skill library editor (Save last), device pairing setup, browser sign-in recovery, device pair setup failure, gateway URL switch, dreaming toggle, channel pairing prompt, chat pane confirm, goal editor, private draft recovery, secrets store, memory import/backfill, MCP server form.

Already correct or single-action (no change): agent create, session move, claw publish review, credential editor, plugin consent, camera capture, worker stop, model provider add/login, model setup success, provider review, connect machine, skills install, channel detail, file preview, lightbox, and other single-button footers. Wizard step controls already place `leadingAction` before the primary answer.

</details>

## Evidence

**Before**

title: fix: resume session-only chats after Gateway restarts
body:
## Superseded by the landed fix

Superseded by [#179579](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179579), merged as 8e590f2ee7e95631b2d1900c29c9b512e5110636. The same missing-scope invariant is repaired in the canonical recovery caller; this duplicate implementation will not be merged.

Independent post-landing verification passed on main a731e655ed6e7cdd7993057544529f263461e401 with **no production changes** and the same proof-only test patch: **1 passed, exit 0, 49.668 s wall / 14.978 s test time**. The real Gateway/agent pipeline retained exactly session read/write scopes, refused public agent RPC, survived a disposable process crash, recovered the persisted final reply, and made exactly two deterministic local model requests. All 32 observed test-process identities were absent after cleanup. This is real process-restart proof with a deterministic model endpoint, not live-provider or Team deployment proof.

The exact-main full build exited 1 at the existing SDK declaration-size budget (5,453,023 > 5,340,536 bytes); generated runtime identity and matching UI readiness were independently verified before the passing test. UI also reported a startup gzip overage. No budget, stamp, or gate was altered; the full build is not claimed green.

Original candidate evidence below is retained for provenance. No duplicate merge or live deployment was performed.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chats started with session-only access fail to resume after a Gateway restart because recovery incorrectly requires broader operator write access.

## User Impact

Members and guests can resume their own interrupted turns under their original permission ceiling. Public `agent` RPC and administrative tool restrictions remain unchanged. No new configuration, permission grant, schema change, or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery now reuses the existing host-bound own-session admission path after restoring current operator authority. It carries the validated session, lifecycle, and replacement-run identity from the recovery owner. A requested operator restore with no saved operator source fails closed instead of falling back to a system principal.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on base `303b8ff0aeb0ee7cd23e3fdc57644ab3dc0f26bf` through the real dispatch authorization boundary: session-only recovery failed with `missing scope: operator.write`; write/admin controls passed. The pre-dispatch authorization mock was removed.
- Fixed recovery suite: **25 passed**, 26.74 s wall time (about 17 s test time). Covers original scopes, ordinary public-agent denial, administrative-method denial, missing/revoked authority, exact target mismatches, and retained-owner invalidation.
- Sibling operator-restoration, typed-facade, request-authorization, own-session sharing, and host-bound spawn tests passed. Sharing + spawn + recovery rerun: 49 passed across 3 files, 89.03 s wall time.
- Full build passed (227.36 s). Core and changed Gateway test typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Final lint: 15.05 s; incremental core/test typechecks: 1.73/1.09 s. CI time is not yet available.
- Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable production findings. A later test-only review refresh failed in reviewer tooling and is not counted as an additional completed review.

**Cold-process proof completed:** the scope-verified Control UI probe now passes against the unchanged published production tree at `754972b0b190919d42e226d7addbcebd93c72fab`: 1 test, 20.71 s wall / 13.35 s test time. It checks the granted session-only scopes, rejects ordinary public `agent` RPC, starts a real agent request, crashes the disposable Gateway, observes a different replacement process, and verifies the recovered final reply in persisted history with exactly two deterministic model requests. The earlier `UND_ERR_SOCKET` failure came from routing the loopback fixture through the ambient HTTP proxy; the corrected fixture excludes only its exact loopback host:port while preserving external proxy routing. Earlier failed attempts are retained. The improved E2E fixture remains a local proof change, not yet part of this PR.

**Draft / overlap coordination:** fetching current main for conflict repair revealed that [#179579](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179579), merged as `8e590f2ee7e95631b2d1900c29c9b512e5110636`, already fixes this missing-scope regression by binding the same session run at the recovery caller. It also settles definitive authorization revocation. This PR must be narrowed or retired rather than blindly adding a second binding. No duplicate production cutover, ready transition, or merge has been performed. The cold-process result above is for this PR's production tree, not a claim of a separate current-main run.

Simplification: no second scope policy, recovery privilege, or state owner was added. The existing session-run binding and authorization owners are reused. Delta from base: production +25/−5 lines; test +215/−136 (mostly reindentation of existing scope-parameterized coverage); docs +4. title: fix: stop repeated notices after requester recovery fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a failed requester recovery can trigger another model turn solely to report that its subagent completion delivery failed, adding more attempts and error messages during a provider outage or rate limit.

## User Impact

User impact: both batch settlement and ordinary completion announcements stop generating an extra model turn after recovery has permanently failed to produce a visible reply. Completed child work and the delivery failure remain available for inspection and explicit continuation.

This does not remove provider rate limits, change ordinary retry budgets, or automatically resume stopped sessions. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing completion owner records the failure and retains the result. It now suppresses the additional blocked-delivery system event for permanent `visible_reply_missing` recovery failures. Ordinary announcements retain that structured failure through suspension, so the shared wake owner also refuses implicit replay after reopening the database. Separately admitted yield batches still proceed; other blocked-delivery notifications retain their existing behavior.

This removes a redundant recovery notification without adding a new state owner or retry mechanism. Against the base, the change adds 14 and removes 3 production lines, adds 121 and removes 13 test lines, and adds 5 documentation lines. The added tests protect the two distinct completion routes and durable recovery behavior.

## Evidence

- Batch-settlement regression: the production recovery resolver and completion settlement previously persisted an unwanted system event. After the fix, reopening the database shows no event, retained child completion, permanent failed-delivery state, and no requester wake.
- Ordinary-announcement regression: the production completion/cleanup path previously called the requester wake once after the same recovery failure. After the fix, it retains the child result and structured failure with no event or implicit wake, including after database reopen. An explicitly admitted yield batch still wakes normally.
- 315 focused tests pass across 8 files covering completion receipts, requester wake, mailbox, replay, delivery state, lifecycle, wake retries, and yielded settlement.
- Production-core and agents-sessions test-shard typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The unchanged documentation previously passed its MDX check.
- Independent AutoReview found no additional P0–P2 defects in the combined candidate. Its index-only finding was resolved by including the complete reviewed ordinary-announcement repair in the follow-up commit.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39665392284) passed for `20d70965b5cbf60bcbc0b745e9287fb942dd9df9`; the repository watcher reports GREEN with no pending checks.
- [ClawSweeper revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179675#issuecomment-6322270114) reviewed the exact current head, confirmed the ordinary-announcement finding is resolved, and found no code defects. It requested additional stored-data compatibility evidence.
- Cross-version state proof: the real v2026.10.5 writer created pending, delivered, and failed completion rows in an isolated SQLite database. The current-head backed-up migration owner preserved all three results; its completion mutation suspended permanent missing-visible-reply recovery without queuing a notice. A fresh OS process reopened the database and confirmed the retained result, failure reason, and implicit-wake fence. No additional migration was needed on reopen. This uses the actual database/codec/mutation owners with synthetic run records, not a full Gateway/model E2E upgrade.
- Proof is at the production recovery/settlement boundary; external announcement I/O is stubbed. No live provider rate-limit simulation or deployed-runtime validation is claimed.

title: fix: preserve native CLI sessions across completion turns
body:
Related: #178982
Supersedes the temporary main-branch workaround in #178955.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native CLI conversations losing context or rebuilding their tool/prompt prefix when an attached-client or owner turn is followed by a completion turn.

## User Impact

The conversation keeps a stable tool catalog across those turns. Tools still require the current caller’s authority, client capabilities, and delivery context to execute; a visible declaration grants no permission. This applies to shared runtime and plugin tools, not only Claude CLI.

No schema or configuration migration is added. Upgrading from the #178955 hotfix can cause one native-session reset because the full catalog is fingerprinted again. Saved OpenClaw history remains intact, but automatic replay into a replacement native session still depends on the existing history-account boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Remove #178955’s four-name fingerprint exemption and its documentation; replace its regression with stable-catalog/prompt/reuse proof plus configured-tool-removal invalidation.
- Keep names, descriptions, and schemas stable. Reuse the existing execution gate for client capabilities, task delivery, session controls, and owner-only Codex tools.
- Preserve the same declarations through plugin discovery and wrapping, including class-backed/lazy descriptors. The callback adapter is extracted from the existing plugin wrapper, not a second implementation.
- Distinguish declared process support from currently callable process support, so exec’s schema stays stable without enabling detached execution.
- Settle accepted completion bindings through the existing owner instead of suppressing their persistence. Genuine configuration/catalog changes still invalidate native reuse.

Integrated main at `d1db2f3298050` to resolve the hotfix/test overlap and current widget/plugin changes. Retained main’s scheduled-widget routing and plugin metadata validation. No release-branch changes.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `46f025590788b2a256d9a51c519caea1ddfc44e9`.

- Focused integration batches: **326 tests passed in 12 files**, covering CLI preparation/settlement, prompt-prefix stability, client/plugin gates, sandbox session authority, widgets, and exec continuation. Runner wall times: 104.80s and 112.37s; these are local times, not CI seconds. The final consolidated completion suite also passes all 30 tests (47.43s runner wall time; not added again to the total).
- Full production build (including all 157 SDK subpath checks), core production typecheck, affected agents test-typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, complete changed-file formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Negative control: retaining main’s #178955 fingerprint implementation makes the consolidated regression fail on configured tool removal (`system-prompt` instead of `prompt-tools`); removing the exemption passes. The control restored the exact tested candidate bytes afterward.
- Full-candidate independent AutoReview: **scoped-clean through P2**, with no actionable findings. Review was source-only; the later test-only consolidation preserves the same assertions. An additional independent plugin/Codex source pass also found no actionable issue.
- Simplification: one execution gate, one descriptor-preserving callback adapter, no tool-name exceptions or new persistence. Against pinned main: production/tooling +391/-291; tests +802/-267; docs +25/-12. The retained growth covers the same declaration/execution contract across existing core, plugin, and native-tool consumers; no new manager or state format.
- The first integration typecheck caught a removed presenter lookup still needed by scheduled routing; it was restored before the passing tests. A lint line-limit finding led to folding the configured-tool-removal assertion into the existing turn sequence, without weakening it.

### Retained live and upgrade evidence

- [Authenticated Claude continuity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179363#issuecomment-6316094871): contributor’s Control UI → real child completion → Control UI flow retained one native session on `2edffaf5d811`; the base control reset.
- [Authority and stable-upgrade checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179363#issuecomment-6331081185): denied callers did not reach protected handlers; token rotation rejected an outstanding read result; stable-state upgrade preserved messages and settings. Both base and head had a one-time initial native reset.
- [Fork interruption](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179363#issuecomment-6344815555): on `c19837bc3077`, abort/reset during awaited fork preparation produced no fork dispatch or binding write, while the allowed control succeeded. This is outcome evidence; it does not isolate the specific authority assertion, prove prevention of already-issued reads, or cover every revocation timing.

These are contributor-run, prior-head results, not new exact-head live runs. Earlier exact-head CI and ClawSweeper results remain historical. Current-head CI and a fresh ClawSweeper review are pending; this update does not claim merge readiness yet. The prior formal SDK comparison found one added export (`tool-plugin.gateAgentToolExecution`), no removed exports/entrypoints, and no schema or stored-format change.

Adapted from @Marvinthebored’s [recovery branch](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/tree/fix/178982-stable-tool-declarations), retaining the original contribution and follow-up fixes.
