title: feat(browser): judge page blockers with Decision models
body:
Closes #179360

## What Problem This Solves

Agents need to identify blockers on the browser tab they already control without sending its page text back through the primary model.

## User Impact

Adds explicit Browser `action="judge"` for text-capable Chromium and Lightpanda profiles. It reads up to 6,000 body-text characters, wraps them as untrusted evidence, and sends them to the calling agent's selected Decision model. The response contains target identity, observation size/truncation, and the original typed outcome—not the page excerpt or a “safe to use” verdict.

**Judgments are advisory, provider-dependent, and not calibrated action thresholds.** Hosted inference may charge and sends bounded evidence to that provider. Existing-session profiles are unsupported. There is no automatic provider/engine fallback, waiting, navigation, login, consent, payment, or challenge bypass. Empty observations return unavailable; missing/error/null answers stay unknown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser retains ownership of the existing tab, run binding, node/HTTP routing, and bounded text capture. The caller-bound Decision SDK owns model selection, credentials, admission, current-authority checks, cancellation, and usage. No new core tool, SDK subpath, configuration option, credential store, or second browser session is introduced. The fixed rubric separates loading from completed-empty searches, alongside login/consent walls, challenges, paywalls, errors, and unsupported-browser messages. Reading body preserves dialogs outside article/main.

This replaces the initial recipe-only revision with an implementation. Native Lightpanda `judge()` is deliberately not claimed: October 27 upstream checks still resolve to experimental browser `e04f855d` and Python `7b176011`; Python uses MCP classify, not a same-CDP operation. Release 1.0.2 lacks classify. The native experiment uses hosted TypeSafe, not embedded offline weights. Pinned API/source evidence is in the documentation; no speculative adapter or dependent PR is included.

## Evidence

- **CI remains failed:** [run 40453048484, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40453048484) completed with one root failure in the existing `session-tab-storage-compat.sqlite.test.ts` case and its downstream gate. It fails before key assertions with `PLUGIN_STATE_OPEN_FAILED` / “Shared-state admission requires the host broker.” The identical failure reproduces on independent main `ddf2e9803fc` without this PR. The actual tested merge `a2bb7f5f` has ordered parents `4706d891` / `9c454409`; the failing test, harness, SQLite admission, and lane-selection sources are unchanged. All other planned jobs and `security-fast` passed. Landing uses the supported inherited-failure exception, not a green rerun or a review/security waiver.

- **Current head `9c454409af1ea10f1702110f0831b5488f963c67`:** 127 affected tests passed across six Browser suites and prompt-prefix stability, plus the opt-in real Chromium 153 bridge/action test. Source extension and touched-test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, MDX, and whitespace checks passed. Current-head full build exited 0 and build-info identifies this head.
- **Actual agent → Browser → local model:** A real primary agent invoked status then judge on the same attach-only Chromium tab. Persisted tool receipts show ONNX `gliclass-edge-v3.0`, rubric `browser-page-blockers-v1`, 92 observed characters, no truncation, and all eight typed answers. No page-body read was returned to the primary model. Artifacts came from the production pinned downloader with verified sizes/SHA256; Decision inference used no hosted credential.

title: feat(decisions): tune constrained thresholds with held-out evaluation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Decision-model users need to choose a threshold against their own precision/recall requirements without mistaking tuning performance for held-out evidence.

## User Impact

Source-checkout users can tune saved Boolean scores offline and see separate held-out results plus a 0.50 baseline. Infeasible constraints produce no threshold; held-out misses remain failures rather than silently relaxing targets. Existing runtime and provider behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stack 2 of 2, depends on #179185. Base: `openclaw/decision-threshold-evaluation`. Review/land #179185 first, then retarget this PR to `main`. **Review only; no merge requested.**

Reuses the first PR's metrics and input validation. Threshold candidates and F-beta optimization use tuning examples only. Minimum precision and recall are explicit; exact ties choose the highest threshold. Imports must have matching provider/model/rubric/question identity and disjoint IDs. Reports include scored/unscored coverage, and docs explain fallback, costs, calibration, alias drift, related-trace leakage and preassigned cross-validation splits.

Informed by [Hamel Husain and Antaripa Saha's article](https://hamel.dev/blog/posts/decision-model-evals/index.html). No labeled production data was supplied: this provides validated tuning support, not a newly calibrated model or evidence for changing the experimental tool filter's 0.35 threshold. No new global configuration knob, SDK contract, provider call or automated deployment.

Author simplification: one offline owner, no tuning service or runtime policy machinery. Relative to #179185: implementation +118/-8 lines, tests +108, docs +42.

## Evidence

- 15 real CLI boundary tests pass (181ms test time; 1.36s wrapper wall time on the published head). CI seconds not yet available.
- Synthetic separable scores select 0.4 while 0.50 misses all positives; changing held-out labels/scores does not retune. Tests also cover tied scores, precision/recall weighting, infeasible and undefined metrics, unavailable rows, identity mismatch and overlapping IDs.
- Targeted TypeScript, oxlint, oxfmt, docs MDX sanity and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2): scoped clean. Base parser/metrics were reviewed independently in #179185; the second review covered the dependent diff.
- No real-model quality/calibration or live-provider claim; all behavior is offline. Production deployment still requires representative labels, adequate coverage and fresh held-out evidence.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshes mature dependencies across application, native-client, and automation workflows without silently adopting breaking upgrades.

## User Impact

User impact: compatible dependency updates require no configuration changes or migration; approved forks, patches, and release-age exceptions are preserved.

Linux desktop Cargo upgrades remain deferred because native resolution also lowered existing Windows dependency edges. Gradle 9.8 upgrades remain deferred after reproducing an Android configuration failure. Native packaging and device validation still need CI; this is not a claim that every available dependency was updated.

## Why This Change Was Made

This fresh sweep originally started from main at `54b5607e558451bc7fd44d9cd276f7e2991d4676`. The latest October 22 conflict integration uses pinned main `dfe0396d257f8ab093b54ac8683ecdf9a7d68750`, preserving its later dependency pins, release-age exemptions, and behavior without restarting the sweep. The earlier integration used `5ce3f4f395712a1a3e2120044c4195e3a704d8ab`. The fixed audit instant is **2026-10-21 05:34 UTC**, with an inclusive **2026-10-14 05:34 UTC** publication cutoff. New resolved packages were checked against upstream timestamps; no inherited newer pins were downgraded, and no new overrides, patches, or policy relaxations were added.

<details>
<summary>Applied scope and compatibility decisions</summary>

| Surface | Updates |
| --- | --- |
| pnpm workspace | 12 unique direct packages / 15 manifest placements relative to integrated main; 108 remaining prior-only resolved identities, all cutoff-verified; existing Hono override 2.1.4 → 2.1.5 |
| Standalone npm | Sandbox CLI 4.8.0 → 4.8.1 and SDK 3.7.0 → 3.8.0; regenerated lock and materializer integrity assertions |
| Rust | 5 resolved identities across the crates and Watch locks; Watch license index aligned; Tokio upgrade deferred |
| Ruby | 5 identities / 10 lock placements; Bundler 4.0.23 callers, CI, documentation, and existing tests aligned |
| Automation | create-github-app-token 3.2.0 → 3.3.0; Arch base-20261011.0.609700; installer freshness-test npm 11.19.0 → 11.21.0 |

Workspace updates: AWS SDK 3.1151.0, Copilot SDK 1.0.21, Google GenAI 2.29.1, Azure Identity 4.14.0, execa 10.1.1, oxlint 1.88.0, TypeScript 7.1.0-dev.20261013.1, Mermaid 12.2.0, TanStack virtual-core 3.19.4, and Solid Vite plugin next.50. The original Solid Vite plugin next.50 update is now covered by main. The integration retains main’s Solid rc16 migration and removal of the obsolete rc14 Babel override.

Rust updates: rustls-native-certs 0.8.5, deranged 0.5.9, sctp-proto 0.10.6, and zerocopy/derive 0.8.63. Ruby updates: aws-partitions 1.1295.0, Bundler 4.0.23, domain_name 0.7.20261007, excon 1.7.3, and signet 0.22.1.

All three Cargo graphs, both Ruby locks, Swift package resolutions, Android/Maven/Gradle, Go, standalone npm tooling, Actions/hooks, and container/toolchain pins were audited. Android artifacts and Go direct modules have no eligible compatible updates; no eligible compatible Swift update was established. Three rate-limited Swift release APIs used public tag/feed evidence. Temurin asset metadata remained unavailable, so its inherited pin is retained without claiming exhaustive coverage.

Deferred migrations: Vitest 5.0.4 requiring an approved-patch port; custom-runner Codex Action v1.13 requiring unqualified setfacl/nobody support; Wrangler 4.150 changing source-map upload defaults; pre-commit 4.7 raising Python requirements; Ruff 0.17 breaking defaults; Tauri/Android tooling requiring native qualification. Existing hosted-runner Codex Action v1.13 pins are unchanged.

Mermaid changed cluster IDs to namespaced IDs. Two existing browser-test selectors were adapted after inspecting actual built SVG; all layout, content, and security assertions remain.

</details>

## Evidence

**Current-head main CI (October 22):** [run 39844901220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901220) completed all **191 jobs** (terminal, not 191 passes). Feishu type-aware lint and the realtime bundle passed on head `aa6de7b8b9d3591246da2bc1f215cb7cadda0c11`. This does not repair or reclassify the historical realtime failure: its attribution remains **UNKNOWN**, as documented below. The three remaining main-CI root failures are inherited: [browser default-executable cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901220/job/120056798916), [planner ownership expectation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901220/job/120056807795), and [private Control UI ownership inventory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901220/job/120056798663). The inventory case was reproduced on exact tested main `759015dc1664d02dcb4f3f9f3c98dfdf43492d5c` with the same expected **69**, received **70** and sole added sidebar-pin-placement path (1 failed, 167 unselected; Node 24.22.1/pinned Bun). The case is `ci workflow guards > keeps private Control UI servers and resource-sensitive files under one serial owner` in `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`; the extra path is `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-pin-placement.e2e.test.ts`, absent from `test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`. The workflow-guard file differs only in unrelated token-action assertions; whole-file equality is not claimed. Detailed evidence: `.openclaw/tmp/deps-audit/aa6-workflow-guard/`.

**Separate Linux App failure:** [run 39844901161 / job 120056189820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901161/job/120056189820) passed **330 Rust tests** (3 ignored) and **1 doc test**, then failed native onboarding presentation. Its [retained artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901161/artifacts/12455571588) records the provider setup as configured and native capability installed, but no setup-card heading appeared. `apps/linux/tests/fixtures/onboarding-card.tsx:86` omits the `actions` prop required by `ui/src/pages/custodian/custodian-setup-card.tsx:78–80` and read by its heading at line 113, since main commit [e98056e3e6638cc54fa9f80ac061c12782241e33](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e98056e3e6638cc54fa9f80ac061c12782241e33) (#180580). The caller, component, relevant owners/configuration and render toolchain match the exact tested main. The native driver did not capture the JavaScript exception. This is a source-attributed inherited contract mismatch, not an independently replayed native-main failure; no native or CI rerun or repair performed. Historical failures and native admission limitations remain retained; this is not a claim that all current-head workflows are green.

**Native admission remains blocked (final October 22 observation):** the runs above tested merge `3a06083ed53310028d7a5f9bc4ff8c047b96ed41` of main `759015dc1664d02dcb4f3f9f3c98dfdf43492d5c` and head `aa6de7b8b9d3591246da2bc1f215cb7cadda0c11`. The separate [Linux App run 39844901161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901161) has now completed all **3 jobs**: [macOS 120056189097](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901161/job/120056189097) **passed**, [Windows 120056190038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901161/job/120056190038) **passed, including the installer**, and [Linux 120056189820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39844901161/job/120056189820) **failed** with the source-attributed inherited fixture mismatch documented above. The earlier recovery stopped before dispatch while check suite `107995039635` was incomplete. After suite completion, the parent repeated the supported exact-head cancelled-auto recovery with freshly fetched canonical main `fdf6d47e645b118e5c3ee935f0a96a7bddd499da`. It exited **1**, before intent creation or merge dispatch, with: `Prior-CI admin admission: failed input changed in the tested PR merge: test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`. This is now an **observed source-equality refusal**, not a prospective limitation: the native verifier requires equality of each entire `sourcePath` blob, and this guard file differs due to the unrelated token-pin expectations. The bounded inherited-failure attribution does not satisfy that whole-file requirement. The lock was drained/released, and the retained outcome `0b92166587192d21a57717556cb9b0e7929ccede` was unchanged. The PR remains **open on aa6, unmerged, with no auto-merge enabled**; no bypass or all-green outcome is claimed.

**Feishu async-cleanup repair (October 22):** the e22 head's type-aware [lint job 120046349130](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39841568278/job/120046349130) exposed a PR-caused unhandled promise at `extensions/feishu/src/http.test-support.test.ts:10:5`. The one-file repair retains the streaming fixture's completion promise and awaits it in cleanup after response cancellation and connection shutdown. The unread negative-control assertions still run before cancellation; no suppression, retry, timeout, weakened assertion, or production change. Published head `aa6de7b8b9d3591246da2bc1f215cb7cadda0c11` (repair commit `81c3ef9869bb79236060503a80b25be944421f37`), reviewed tree `27a38d2ae8970123fb77de7caac43f02116751a3`; delta **1 file, +3/−1**. The same owned lint command failed before and passed after; both real-HTTP helper tests passed under Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun; formatting and diff checks passed. Simplification retained only necessary cleanup ownership. Fresh independent Codex Auto Review covered the complete repair with unchanged writer context: **no actionable P0–P2 findings** (static review, not independent runtime execution). No dependency, cutoff, lockfile, or realtime source changes were made. Current-head CI and native landing remain parent-owned.

**Realtime CI attribution remains UNKNOWN, not repaired or proven inherited.** In [run 39841568278 / job 120044592399](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39841568278/job/120044592399), tested merge `0f7369b3903c1b1ba7a087d0a1bc79e31a595a3d` (main `adead1c9d3299f69efa5be1caffc9acc0fa1ed29` plus e22), `realtime-quicksilver-peer-worker.test.ts` failed the direct-sink-false case with initial RTP count **0, expected ≥5**, before the deliberate Gateway stall; the direct-sink-true sibling passed. Unchanged source alone is insufficient: effective dependencies change ASN.1 2.10.0 → 2.11.0 and mediabunny 1.61.3 → 1.61.4.

<details>
<summary>Retained realtime investigation results and limits</summary>

- Exact-main and e22 five-case replays both passed under Node 24.22.1/pinned Bun (42.91 s and 57.04 s wrapper). These were not full CI-group replays and are not causal proof.
- Decoded the actual 41-file CI collection and observed ordering. Temporary diagnostics preserved original assertions, timeouts and network configuration, exposing ICE/DTLS state, worker/receiver errors, queued audio and initial RTP count. The selected failed-case run passed (1 selected, 4 skipped; 48.94 s); the relevant six-file actual-CI sibling collection passed **134/134** (67.44 s), and the same collection restricted to two CPUs passed **134/134** (70.80 s). Initial false-case packet counts were 5, error arrays were empty, and later receiver diagnostics showed connected ICE/DTLS. None reproduced zero RTP; no green replay is presented as a fix.

The only ASN.1 JavaScript delta removes decoder limits in `AsnAnyConverter.toASN`; the mediabunny delta changes MPEG-TS AVC/HEVC timestamps, a path not exercised by this direct-RTP test. These observations do not establish an inherited failure or exclude a dependency-related cause.
- Full hourly-main executions 39834672414/120020262348, 39816730583/119958041634, 39807658472/119926107075, 39798434752/119893011732 and 39782262058/119837068060 passed this exact case. Runs 39825075802/119986678762 and 39789689759/119862843196 did not execute it; 39842546000/120047832509 was still running at the retained read and is not counted. No matching baseline failure was found.
- Diagnostic source edits were restored byte-for-byte; only the Feishu cleanup fix is published. No CI rerun, remote allocation, new override, arbitrary timeout, retry/skip or assertion weakening. </details>

**Latest conflict integration (October 22):** published head `e22ed73dd036d6f5d13e92ae71cae77ea30c37b3`, reviewed tree `b72d7a2f001470e4d08048c31b147c7f4413b64d`, integrates main `dfe0396d257f8ab093b54ac8683ecdf9a7d68750` through merge commit `cdcae45c0e4a5263660abf46ba180dcd5b13be39`. title: fix: interrupted child sessions ignore new messages after a Gateway restart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a child session (for example a visible session spawned with `sessions_spawn`) that was mid-run during a Gateway restart rejects every later human message. The UI shows "Interrupted before the agent started it" and no run ever starts.

## User Impact

After a restart, the next human message in an interrupted child session starts a normal turn again. Children are still not replayed automatically, and the parent still owns finishing its task, as documented. Main sessions keep their existing resume-before-new-input behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Turn admission saves a restart-recovery delivery claim for the interrupted turn, on child sessions as well as main sessions. Main-session restart recovery resumes that claim before new input runs, but it deliberately skips child, cron, and ACP sessions (`not_main_session`). The subagent registry settles the child's run instead of replaying it. Nothing ever consumes the claim on the child session. User-turn admission then threw `RESTART_RECOVERY_CLAIM_CHANGED` for every new message, because an aborted claim from channel or WebChat ingress could only be transferred when it came from `control-ui`.

User-turn admission now retires an aborted claim when the session is not a main-session recovery candidate, using the same preconditions as the existing Control UI transfer: no pending final delivery, no ambiguous `before_agent_reply` state, and no delivery receipt. The retired source is recorded as terminal, so it cannot resume later. Explicit stop and cancel outcomes are unchanged. The skip itself stays as it is: the docs and #172017 state that human ownership and dashboard nesting do not make a child a main-session replay candidate.

<details><summary>Incident trace (team-metal, 2026-10-20)</summary>

- 21:06 shutdown: `skipped restart recovery session … reason: not_main_session` for the child; its run was aborted for restart.
- 21:07 startup: the subagent registry settled the child run as interrupted. It could not restore the parent continuation (`lacks its original operator source`; see follow-ups).
- The child row kept `abortedLastRun: true`, `status: interrupted`, and `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` set to the dead run, with ingress `channel`.
- 23:18 and 23:21: two human messages passed source claim and both barriers, then failed admission silently. Both pending inputs remain `interrupted` and unconsumed.

</details>

## Evidence

- New regression in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-subagent-custody.test.ts` ("starts a human follow-up in a child interrupted by a Gateway restart"). It drives real `chat.send` admission, real chat dispatch, the real restart-recovery claim controller, and the subagent registry; only the embedded model runner is mocked. Its state is the post-restart child row and the registry row taken from the incident.
  - Base: red. The run never starts, and the test times out waiting for the agent run.
  - Fix: green. The run starts, `abortedLastRun` clears, the old source is recorded as terminal, and the follow-up takes native child custody.
- Sibling suites pass: restart-recovery-claim (all five files), reply-turn-admission recovery, runreplyagent e2e, and main-session restart recovery.
- `pnpm check:changed`: core and core-test typecheck, changed-file lint, format, the line-cap ratchet, and the other changed-file guards pass. Three failures are inherited and do not touch these files: new max-lines suppressions in three `ui/src/pages/*` files, the core test shard root budget (`agents-tools`, `gateway-root`, `infra`, and `plugins-platform` are over 720), and an unused export `PluginRuntimeResolver` in `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts`.
- `$autoreview` (branch vs `origin/main`, P1): no actionable findings.

Gap: this was not reproduced against an isolated Gateway restarted in the middle of a real model turn. The proof stops at the owning admission boundary.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- After a restart, a human follow-up row (`replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer` with `preserveCompletedRun`) intentionally drops the completed task's `operatorRecoverySource` and binds only in-memory authority. After a restart, the private parent continuation for that row cannot be restored ("Subagent restart recovery lacks its original operator source"), so the parent is never told about the interruption. Persisting the follow-up's own source changes authority, so it needs a separate decision.
- A child whose interrupted turn also left `pendingFinalDelivery` or a `before_agent_reply` checkpoint still rejects new input, the same as before this change.

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/105aa7fb-a366-4c8e-addf-7e152101ab20)

title: fix(ui): sidebar wraps a single selected owner's sessions in a collapsible header
body:
Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/9807c098-f6cc-4153-9a32-8ae4f433fea9)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with sidebar sessions grouped by Person, selecting a single owner (for example **My sessions**) still wraps that owner's sessions in a collapsible owner header that just repeats the filter.

## User Impact

User impact: when one owner is selected, their sessions render directly in the sidebar with no redundant header or collapse toggle, and session titles line up with the left edge of the owner picker. "Involving me" and "All owners" keep per-owner headers, since those can span several people.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar projection already renders a lone catch-all section headerless; this applies the same rule to the single Person section produced by a one-owner filter. The projection now receives which owner filter is active (`owner` / `involvingMe` / none) instead of a boolean, so it can tell "exactly one owner" apart from "involving me". A previously stored collapse on that owner's section is inert while it is headerless (same as the existing catch-all behavior), so sessions can't get stuck hidden behind a header that no longer renders.

That inline section also drops empty leading status slots and offsets the list's negative inline margin, so titles start at the owner picker's edge (measured: picker and titles both at x=68). Rows with a running or draft indicator keep it at that edge, with their title after it.

title: feat: drop files into new sessions from the command palette
body:
Related: #142880

## What Problem This Solves

Files dropped onto the Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette are ignored, and attaching an image leaves unrelated navigation choices visible. The cold loading input also swallowed native text drops and discarded accepted attachment drafts when dismissed before the palette finished loading.

## User Impact

Drop images or files to prepare a new background session while keeping the current conversation, composer, route and focus intact. The first attachment switches to New session mode. Closing and reopening preserves accepted files and their instructions in memory for the same Gateway/account, including before the first lazy-module handoff. Dropping never submits by itself.

## How It Works

The palette reuses the existing attachment admission, preparation, previews, removal and nested-drag handling. The cold input retains raw Files only until the canonical draft accepts them once. Dismissal cancels queued submission and composition; account/Gateway replacement and disposal clear the draft. Native text drops still insert into the editable cold input.

On mobile, Return remains native editing and the attachment footer shows only the newline key. Use the New session button to submit. Desktop submission shortcuts remain unchanged.

Ordinary attachment failures show the existing toast and remove only the failed item. Text and successfully prepared files remain available for manual submission; failures cancel a queued automatic submission. Removing the last attachment retains new-session intent while instructions remain. Clearing both restores navigation.

## Risk and coverage

- No configuration, dependencies, persistent storage or Gateway protocol changes. Reloading the app does not retain this in-memory draft.
- Final candidate: `32044ab4b7b371e1bedddcd7d3d7159a93888232`, incorporating pinned main `ce9941f4db620f6ad7ff7611ec293c8d4bc7fb1b`. Main now contains the canonical catalog-test correction; its entire test file is retained. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39835730504) completed successfully, including security-fast, UI/E2E and the CI gate.
- On the reviewed pre-integration candidate, **27 real Chromium scenarios** passed across focused runs, with affected cases rerun after repairs: native cold text drops, accepted cold-file dismissal/reopening, lazy handoff, continuous typing under CPU throttling, IME guards, platform shortcuts, mixed image/PDF files, partial read failure, same-account reconnect, account replacement, manual submission and unchanged foreground state.
- **119 focused unit cases** passed across attachment admission/lifecycle, palette draft ownership, lazy shell actions, cold input custody and Gateway presentation scope. Fixed a stale renamed-method test caller and made the preview assertion await its lazy-rendered PDF.
- UI typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, Solid ownership guards, formatting and whitespace checks passed. Production Control UI bundles were built for browser proof.
- Independent review covered the full corrected candidate; no remaining P0–P2 findings.
- [Current real-application before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178842#issuecomment-6346933125): captured main `1bd44907beb` versus the reviewed attachment presentation, desktop dark and narrow light. Synthetic Gateway responses and files; no live provider/model run is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Focused test cost and failure resolution</summary>

All commands used the repository Vitest wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`. The initial browser regressions failed on the original behavior (empty native text drop; lost accepted cold draft). After repair, the first-open suite passed 6/6 in 17.82s runner wall time, including its production UI setup. The 5-file browser run took 54.57s; its one remaining cold-retention failure was fixed and covered by that replay. The 4-case file-drop suite spent 9.03s in tests; the final read-failure fixture replay passed in 15.20s runner wall time including setup.

The six-file unit run took 5.20s and exposed two failure cases still calling the retired `adoptImageFiles` method. After completing the rename, the 30-case draft suite passed in 2.84s; the updated 21-case loading suite passed in 0.91s. The other unit files passed in the combined run. Pre-integration CI run [39786551629](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39786551629) passed all 27 palette browser cases. CI test time: first-open 30.96s, file drops 21.77s, pasted images 22.68s, composition 27.18s, shortcuts 10.36s; focused unit files: loading 1.88s, attachments 9.32s, draft 5.20s. These browser cases exercise native insertion, lazy-module handoff, focus and route ownership that unit tests cannot establish; the first-open suite also retains its existing 8× CPU typing scenario.

The previous CI gate failed on two inherited main-branch fixture expectations: `session-management.sidebar.e2e.test.ts:174` assumes an active child remains the first row after child sorting changed in #172189, and `workboard-routing.e2e.test.ts:156` expects the old aggregate title after #174430 changed it to All boards. Both test files are unchanged by this PR. The original three failing cases were reproduced on unmodified main and pass after the fixture correction. Canonical fixes have since landed in #180666 (sidebar identity selectors) and #180653 (All boards heading); the independently verified combined patch in #180669 became redundant. The integrated candidate includes both canonical fixes and the later Twitch fixture repair from main. Its new CI run validates that integration; previous passing feature cases are historical evidence, not a claim that the current run has completed. title: fix(ui): long picker menus jump while scrolling under the pointer
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the sidebar's owner menu (and other long searchable pickers and multi-selects) jumps while you scroll it with a wheel or trackpad. It happens whenever the pointer passes over a half-visible row at the top or bottom edge of the list.

## User Impact

Long picker menus, such as the session-owner filter with many teammates, now scroll smoothly under the pointer. Keyboard navigation, opening the menu, and search still scroll the highlighted row into view.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pointer hover highlights the row under the cursor, and every highlight change also ran a "reveal" that scrolled the highlighted row fully into view. When the pointer rested over a clipped edge row during a scroll, each reveal pushed the list back against the user's scroll. Pointer-driven highlights now skip the reveal. Keyboard, open, search, and catalog-correction highlights still reveal. The shared picker (`select-picker-view.tsx`) and the shared menu machine's retained-focus reveal (`menu-machine.ts`, used by `MultiSelect`) each had this behavior, and both are fixed.

## Evidence

- **Reproduced through a real pointer in Chromium.** On `origin/main`, a real mouse move onto a half-clipped bottom row scrolls the list on its own: picker 326 → 344px, multi-select 631 → 646px. The new regression tests fail with exactly those values before the fix and pass after it.
- **Keyboard reveal still works.** Each new test then presses an arrow key after the pointer highlight and checks that the next row scrolls into view.
- **Consumers.** All browser test files that cover the menu machine, picker, and multi-select consumers pass: 74 files, 907 tests.
- **Static checks.** `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `oxfmt --check`, and `oxlint` on the touched files are clean. Autoreview (Codex) found nothing at P0–P2.
- **Test cost.** `pnpm test ui/src/components/select-picker.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` takes 10.6s wall time, and `pnpm test ui/src/components/multi-select.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 4.2s. The new tests add about 0.35s and 0.28s respectively, with no timers, sleeps, or new fixtures.
- **No screenshots.** This is a behavior-only fix with no visual change, so the real-pointer browser tests are the proof.

title: improve(ui): use the shared page header on every built-in page
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Built-in pages used three different header treatments. Sessions and Plugins had the stacked hub header, Agents had a smaller stacked variant, and Dashboards, Usage, Automations, Systems, Activity, Meetings, Apps, and Portals put a small centered title in the toolbar row with the description floating underneath.

## User Impact

Every page in the sidebar's **Pages** list now opens with the same header as Sessions and Plugins: a large left-aligned title, the page description with a **Learn more** docs link, actions on the right, and route tabs where the page has them. Settings pages and Memory import keep their existing toolbar-row title.

## Why This Change Was Made

`HubPageHeader` is now the single owner of built-in page headers. It gained optional tabs (Sessions, Worktrees, and Plugins keep theirs), optional docs links, a subtitle override for filtered states (the Automations session filter), and a `wide` variant. Pages whose body spans the full column (Agents, Dashboards, Activity, Apps, Portals, Systems) use `wide`, so the title stays on the content edge instead of a centered 1120px column. The header's mobile inset moved from `settings.css` into its own stylesheet, so pages that don't load the settings styles get the same 12px edge.

- **Systems:** the page header shows "Systems". The selected machine name moves to the workspace toolbar as an `h2` ("Select a machine" when nothing is selected).
- **Activity:** the description now stays visible in Live mode. Activity's and Apps' titles are now real `h1` elements.

title: feat(openai): opt into 12-hour prompt caching
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persistent OpenAI API agents need an opt-in way to reuse stable prompt prefixes across gaps longer than the default cache lifetime.

## User Impact

Users can set `params.promptCacheTtl: "12h"` (or `"30m"`) per model, globally, or per agent for GPT-5.6+ Responses requests. Unset configuration, older models' retention behavior, Chat Completions, and ChatGPT/Codex behavior are unchanged. This requests a minimum cache lifetime, not guaranteed cache hits or a deletion deadline. **12h writes cost more:** 2.5× ordinary input versus 1.25× for 30m writes; reads retain the same rate.

## Why This Change Was Made

[OpenAI's current caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime) specifies `prompt_cache_options.ttl` for the Responses API, distinct from older models' `prompt_cache_retention`. The request-level value also applies to implicit breakpoints; this change does not add explicit breakpoints or change caching mode. [Current pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) confirms total write rates, not additive surcharges. Upgrading valid 30m coverage to 12h charges a new 12h write without credit for the earlier write.

Reuse the existing cache-parameter owner and compatibility gates across provider and managed transports. Preserve `cacheRetention: "none"` precedence, validate invalid TTLs without logging authored values, and account for the higher write rate in local estimates. Existing open-ended provider-parameter schemas already accept the option, so no new top-level config field, schema migration, dependency bump, or parallel cache implementation is needed. The wire contract handles the API's new value without patching or casting around the pinned SDK.

Simplification review retained one lifetime decision owner; production growth is option plumbing and write-cost selection, not new state or infrastructure.

## Evidence

- Regression requests fail on the original implementation (missing TTL) and pass with the change.
- **117 focused tests passed** across Responses builders, write pricing, existing Chat Completions policy, config-to-stream precedence/validation, proxy forwarding, and prompt-prefix stability.
- **3 live OpenAI Responses cases passed** on `gpt-5.6-luna`: unset, `30m`, and `12h`. These prove API acceptance and completed streamed replies, not 12-hour elapsed retention or realized billing savings.
- Production `tsconfig.core.json` typecheck, changed-file format check, documentation config-example validation, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the supplied diff.
- Full `pnpm build` passed (3m 33.6s); changed-file typed lint passed with 0 warnings/errors. An isolated, authenticated Gateway started on its own profile, state, workspace, and port. Its real-agent CLI probe was refused by the agent-exec inter-session attribution guard before inference, so full Gateway-to-model proof remains incomplete. No alternate CLI/RPC route or guard bypass was attempted.

**Live-proof limitation:** full Gateway-to-model proof remains unexecuted because the agent-exec attribution guard refused its CLI invocation. Direct provider API acceptance is proven; this does not claim that missing Gateway boundary. @steipete instructed landing with the documented evidence and limitations; enforced GitHub review, security, and CI gates still apply.

Known verification limits: the changed-test typecheck wrapper failed its existing global test-root budget preflight and was stopped while waiting for generated artifacts (plugins-platform 727 > 720; no test roots are added here). One additional native-worker environment probe failed with `502 Secret egress proxy refused the request`; its other cases passed. No egress guard was bypassed. PR CI is the broad-check owner; CI timing is pending. Local focused suites took 99.5s total (most time in compiled agent-worker setup); test execution stayed below 5s per changed non-live file. Live cases took 24.2s wall time.

**Settlement-baseline repair:** 5aedeae5e5d77891427690607673929543308fd1 integrates existing main settlement fix 4453edcc7db9 via baseline 1c4b27072712 for the launch-wire missing-file failure in [run 39481201843](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39481201843/job/118830768677). The complete feature diff is byte-identical to the original reviewed patch. All **117 focused feature tests passed again** on the integrated head (32.72s). The local full launch-wire attempt hit a synthetic-provider ECONNRESET during baseline inference before the original settlement assertion, so no local full-file pass is claimed. Fresh current-head GitHub CI is required; original build/live evidence above remains prior-head evidence.

**Current repaired head: eeb556b73cacea28c5078ff6beb8f96e931937c1.** The CI package-type error was reproduced and fixed by retaining the complete SDK request shape and the API-optional TTL field; the exact package test-type graph now passes. The review finding about mixed cache lifetimes is also fixed: coherent reported 30m/12h buckets override the request default, with compatibility fallback when absent. Six new pricing cases were red before the repair and now pass through both Responses paths, including zero 12h writes. Current accounting/lifecycle suites: **78 passed**; type-repair caller/request suites: **122 passed**. Typed lint/format/diff checks and fresh independent P0–P2 review passed. body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled follow-up checks repeatedly fill chat with forwarded inputs, tool-only turns, and inferred “Interrupted” labels, making healthy waiting look like failed work.

## User Impact

Consecutive checks from one automation share a quiet, expandable activity row. Current scheduler status and next-check timing update in place; original inputs, timestamps, run links, and tool activity remain available. Human messages, useful replies, media, failed runs, and recorded interruptions stay outside routine folds. Session-only viewers get history counts without additional automation access.

No scheduling, execution, permission, or persistence contracts change. This PR is intentionally **draft**; no deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final transcript projection folds existing typed automation attribution only after causal turn/run grouping. It reuses the existing causal boundary rather than equating client IDs with backend execution IDs. Chat and Session Details now share one scoped compact inventory owner instead of issuing independent reads per row.

## Evidence

- 112 focused tests passed across grouping, navigation, disclosure, run framing, and shared-inventory consumers; UI typecheck, targeted lint/style/controller checks passed.
- Browser E2E covers consecutive checks, keyboard disclosure/focus retention, status events, offline/reconnect/reload, permissions, chronological boundaries, search/reply navigation, and mobile long-label truncation in light/dark themes. Five core scenarios and the separately exercised compact-label scenario passed.
- Real Gateway acceptance passed: a genuine at-scheduled job rearmed itself twice through actual `automations.next_check` execution, three generated inputs folded into one row, scheduler states updated, reload retained original inputs/tool activity, and a useful foreground reply remained outside the row. Gateway and provider cleanup were verified. Only inference used a scripted loopback provider.
- The startup-gzip warning was reproduced on exact base `7538c9e4…` under equal packaging: 325,445 B against the unchanged 325,166 B limit. The source-bound candidate measured 325,422 B (23 B smaller). No budget update or exception was made.
- Independent P0–P2 Auto Review completed; both initial findings (tool media and recorded-interruption boundaries) were repaired, regression-tested, and the revised review is scoped-clean.
- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178580#issuecomment-6296971544) completed on this head with **no actionable correctness or security findings** and sufficient proof. Its only remaining before-merge item is marking the PR ready; that is intentionally deferred to honor the explicit request to leave this PR in draft.
- Author `pr-simplify` pass removed duplicated inventory lifecycles, duplicate frame-option construction, a redundant projection wrapper, and duplicate causal-boundary parsing. The whole-change delta is +495 production lines and +1,430 test lines; growth implements the new presentation/shared lifecycle and the requested browser/real-runtime proof. No competing scheduler or mutable history metadata was added.

### Visual comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: repeated scheduled checks](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d1c5d79-e5e6-4b52-a236-7a6a47f8350c) | ![After: compact automation activity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/452a7a40-d84e-4664-ad76-89e6155cebdf) |

<details>
<summary>Expanded activity</summary>

![Expanded activity retains original inputs and tool activity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54240f6d-a2ea-4394-a9ff-d0d09e808592)

</details>

[Full-size screenshot evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178580#issuecomment-6296669889). All captures use synthetic content.

<details>
<summary>Proof boundaries and cost</summary>

Browser tests use the actual Control UI with a scripted Gateway; isolated-runtime acceptance uses a real Gateway, scheduler, agent, tool execution, and durable history, with only model inference scripted on loopback. No external-model or operator-Gateway claim is made.

The initial before capture shows the pre-integration UI, but was not sealed as an immutable clean-HEAD build. Focused tests took 1.88s wall time; core browser scenarios took 6.022s test-file time / 20.45s invocation, with screenshots enabled separately. Compact-label proof took 2.086s file / 75.44s including build/lease wait. The isolated real-Gateway flow passed in 114.39s invocation, including real scheduler delays, agent/tool execution, browser reload, and cleanup; these producer/transport boundaries cannot be established by the mocked-Gateway suite. Chromium was exercised; WebKit was not run locally. Hosted CI duration is not yet available. Browser transport, retained focus, reload, and original-message navigation are the distinct integration risks requiring these tests.

</details>

Thanks @obviyus for the report and compact-row design direction.

title: fix(deepseek): apply search credential changes during active turns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes DeepSeek search staying unavailable after its credentials are corrected while another agent turn is still running.

## User Impact

With DeepSeek selected as the search provider, operators can change its search key or SecretRef without waiting for unrelated agent turns or restarting the Gateway. Plugin enablement and explicit reloads retain normal lifecycle settlement. This does not change provider auto-detection or activation policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

DeepSeek search already reads the prepared credential from each request. Its key field lacked a narrow reload declaration, so correcting an environment reference to a stored secret unnecessarily selected whole-plugin replacement and waited on unrelated runtime leases before publishing the resolved credential.

Declare only that existing field hot-applicable through the plugin-owned reload contract. Secret preparation, coherent publication, request authority, and genuine plugin replacement remain unchanged. No cache, manager, schema, compatibility path, or timeout change is introduced.

## Evidence

- [Public before/after runtime captures and captured assertion output](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178544#issuecomment-6296089578) demonstrate the corrected Settings-to-search flow with the unrelated turn held open. The captures and local HTTP controls use synthetic credentials; their source bindings match this head.
- Reproduced the actual Chromium Settings edit on deployed revision f6427568d96d, with a synthetic local model holding a real unrelated agent turn open: config.set saved the store reference, but runtime publication stalled on two legitimate leases and the first drain failed after 60,002 ms. Both leases released normally when that turn finished; no leak was inferred.
- Verified the same Settings-to-search flow against the Gateway and DeepSeek plugin built from this patch, using the unchanged deployed Control UI assets and synthetic loopback model/search endpoints. The corrected reference published in 102 ms in that run; there were zero plugin-drain attempts across four credential edits while the unrelated turn stayed open. These are single-flow observations, not a latency guarantee.
- Five real-Gateway controls passed: stale in-flight test rejection after credential change, successful new-credential search, sanitized provider 401, changed missing-store reference failing cold with zero upstream requests, and recovery. Five physical search requests were observed; all used an accepted synthetic credential. Retained work returned to zero after deliberate turn completion.
- Regression demonstrated red before the fix, green after. The full planner file passed 28 tests; focused consumers and affected-write/lifecycle checks bring the focused total to 105 tests across seven files. The added regression took 350 ms; planner invocation wall time was 33.99 s including preparation. CI seconds are not yet available.
- DeepSeek package typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, docs index, production startup build, and built-entry import screening passed. All 29 core-test compiler graphs passed, but the local wrapper still exits nonzero on an existing test-shard root-count budget gate (this patch adds no test roots or imports). That separate gate is not reported green.
- Fresh isolated Auto Review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Re-applied pr-simplify: final production change is one declaration plus its ownership comment; no broader lifecycle changes were needed.

## Contributor credit

Reported by Ayaan.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b19bb3f8-3961-4a85-85b8-d1bf223f72dd)

title: fix(ui): use host zoom for desktop content sizing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Mac app lacks familiar content-zoom shortcuts, and its new page zoom would otherwise compound with the Control UI’s older Text size preference.

## User Impact

- **Mac app:** View → Zoom In / Zoom Out / Actual Size and Cmd-+ / Cmd-=, Cmd--, Cmd-0 resize the Dashboard and full Native chat web transcript, bounded to 50–200%. New windows restore the app profile’s last zoom; existing windows retain their reading size. Native sidebar, Connection window, Quick Chat, and offline native fallback do not scale.
- **Desktop browsers on macOS, Windows, and Linux:** use browser-owned Cmd/Ctrl +/-/0 zoom. The old Text size control and search target are retired without intercepting keys or adding another scaling layer. Its saved value is retained; a page cannot convert it into browser-owned zoom, so choose browser zoom once after upgrading.
- **Accessibility and unqualified hosts:** touch-capable browsers (including mouse-attached tablets), mobile embeds, and native hosts without an explicit zoom capability retain Text size. Unqualified Tauri and WebView2 embeds do not lose their control. This is a supported-host cutover, **not universal Windows native-app parity**; Windows Hub’s separate native renderer is outside this repository’s implementation.

**Draft — not ready for merge. Browser runtime verification and inspected browser before/after captures are now complete. New native migration tests still require a disposable macOS runner. Real-app Native-chat readiness/zoom, full-window native-app visuals, and the earlier product-harness cleanup failure remain unresolved.**

## Why This Change Was Made

One scaling owner—native WKWebView page zoom or the desktop browser—replaces compounded CSS text scaling on supported hosts. Theme/preference refreshes keep their CSS text multiplier at 1. The existing document/device-settings bridge offers only the canonical local legacy value to the native owner; no direct localStorage reader, second zoom manager, new Gateway configuration, migration store, or server preference mutation is added.

On Mac, existing native zoom wins. Otherwise the first foreground document adopts its saved local text size once; background preloads cannot choose the profile default, and an early shortcut/reset wins. A legacy 125% text preference becomes 125% whole-page zoom, deliberately affecting layout and fonts. Cmd-0 means 100%. Legacy and unrelated preferences remain saved. Native chrome insets compensate for page zoom.

## Evidence

Current candidate: 805e4d5a4a4c3f7fe39ffa08e96456e6ef42f50f. A real GitHub merge conflict was resolved by integrating main at c1e6a094ec0e689f00faa9f40cd0629ef87c303f, preserving its shared theme-test fixture and observation-helper refactor. Focused tests, lint, localization, and whole-candidate P2 review were repeated against that exact refreshed base. Older fork results are **not exact-source proof for the new retirement/migration changes**.

- **Current UI checks:** 5 suites / 113 tests passed (19.33 s Vitest; 23.34 s shard): scaling ownership across native/browser/touch/mobile/unqualified hosts, mouse-attached touch preservation, optional native importer, theme refresh and preference preservation, actual Appearance conditional rendering, search retirement, and conversation bridge isolation. Initial native/browser CSS assertions were red before implementation. The component fixture emits Solid strict-read warnings from existing rendering paths; this is not layout/native proof.
- **Static checks:** targeted UI/script lint, formatting, native localization verification, and diff checks passed. UI typecheck still fails with 11 diagnostics in untouched files. An immutable UI/config snapshot from baseline c1e6a094, sharing only unchanged source/dependencies/generated declarations and native fixture assets, reproduced the exact same 11 normalized diagnostics. Its compiler file inventory contained no changed candidate UI source. These are baseline failures, not newly introduced diagnostics; this is not a green typecheck.
- **Independent review:** fresh whole-candidate Auto Review through P2 (all 29 staged candidate files and key owning-source datasets, pinned to c1e6a094ec0e689f00faa9f40cd0629ef87c303f) returned scoped-clean with zero P0–P2 findings. Its earlier P2 finding—mouse-attached tablets losing Text size—was fixed with a conservative touch-capable fallback and regression. Review was static, not independent runtime validation. Simplification reuses the web document, settings transport, theme owner, and shared config/search policy. Necessary growth is confined to zoom/migration and supported-host retirement, with no browser shortcut interception. Against refreshed main c1e6a094: production +286/−43 lines, tests +451/−3, docs +27, generated localization metadata +3. Retained Text size code is intentional accessibility/unsupported-host fallback, not a competing desktop owner.
- **Browser runtime recovered locally:** official signed Debian package metadata and package downloads supplied workspace-local extracted Chromium libraries; only command-local library/font paths were used. No shared host/image, credentials, browser security settings, or product source was changed. Current-head Settings typography/search and Appearance defaults suites passed **13/13** (35.02 s Vitest / 37.07 s shard). The selected native-header 200% browser regression passed **1/1**, with 6 unrelated cases filtered (14.24 s Vitest / 16.07 s shard); this is Chromium native-chrome emulation, not AppKit shortcut proof. Two matched source-server capture scenarios also passed, asserting baseline CSS multiplier 1.25 with five Text size options versus candidate multiplier 1 with none, while both preserve the active saved 125% preference and perform no config writes. An initial capture-fixture scope mismatch was diagnosed and corrected to the actual source-server mock Gateway namespace; failed attempts are retained, not counted as passes.
- **Remaining native runtime gap:** this session has no Swift/AppKit runtime or managed Actions dispatch/artifact tool. Current native migration tests remain uncompiled/unexecuted; earlier fork native proof is historical, not equivalent to the new candidate.

## Maintainer conflict and CI repair — November 4

Candidate `24f979a7ffe91d785a964ba35df906890e4a488b` integrates main `6f975afb9213581bc225dba2417f638c49c828e2` without remaining conflicts. The earlier conflict resolution keeps the current typography section, config state owner, and search visibility policy rather than restoring the retired Appearance implementation.

- Fixed the native-zoom migration calling document-dependent host detection in Node preference-owner tests. The existing native-host adapter is checked first; browser and mobile behavior is unchanged.
- Removed an obsolete screenshot-capture block referencing retired helpers. The 200% native-header browser regression now waits for the required final scaled header height before measuring geometry. No CSS or geometry expectation was weakened.
- Integrated the current device/runner fixture wording and shared native test compile correction from main.
- Moved the unchanged zoom helpers out of the eager connection module into `native-content-zoom.ts`; all three consumers use the single owner. Regenerated the boot manifest using its canonical generator. This is a loading-boundary correction, not a second zoom implementation or delayed first-paint scaling.
- Fresh independent review: CI repairs scoped-clean through AutoReview at P0–P2; module relocation and generated manifest independently reviewed with no actionable findings.

**Focused proof:** the repaired Node settings suites passed 28/28; the final module split passed 79/79 settings/theme/search tests. UI types and targeted lint/format passed. Native-header suite passed 7/7 after the CI repair; the final regenerated bundle passed the selected 200% header regression 1/1 (six unrelated cases intentionally filtered). Canonical boot-manifest capture completed both New Session and Chat routes. These browser tests use the maintained mock-Gateway harness, not native AppKit keyboard input. macOS and iOS Periphery builds passed on prior head `787f3d9c`; these are compilation evidence, not native test execution or exact-current-head CI.

**Performance acceptance:** compare deterministic shipped gzip bytes and request counts with `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 6f975afb9213581bc225dba2417f638c49c828e2`, using one installed Node 26.12.1 / Vite 8.3.5 / Pako 3.0.2 toolchain. Existing budgets and inherited-baseline tolerance remain unchanged. This is a byte-count check, not a runtime latency benchmark.

| JS gzip bytes | Same-toolchain main | Integrated repair before split | Final candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup | 92,383 | 93,070 | 92,390 |
| Chat boot | 1,285,806 | 1,286,814 | 1,286,139 |
| New Session boot | 799,051 | 799,968 | 799,604 |

Startup now passes the differential gate (+7 B); request counts remain 3 / 20 / 15. **Performance is still blocked:** Chat is 77 B over its 1,286,062 B cap; New Session is 361 B over the inherited-base allowance of 799,051 + 192 B. The module split removes unnecessary eager loading but does not eliminate the route-level cost of the zoom behavior. No budgets were increased and no behavior was removed to hide the residual failure.

**Separate inherited test-budget blocker:** pinned main has 6,479,258 test LF against a 6,479,234 ceiling, over by 24 with delta zero. This PR adds exactly 227 LF, covered by its exact 227-line allocation; candidate total 6,479,485 versus ceiling 6,479,461 remains over by the same inherited 24. Baseline and unrelated tests were left unchanged.

**Remaining native proof:** current native zoom/migration test execution, real AppKit input, native chat and full-window captures, upgrade behavior, and distribution/runtime validation remain unverified. Existing historical proof and media below retain their original scope. This repair is not a merge-readiness or green-CI claim.

## Browser before and after

Actual Control UI with the maintained mocked-Gateway harness and synthetic data: baseline c1e6a094 versus candidate 805e4d5a, both 1280×1000, light theme, desktop input, browser zoom unchanged, and an active saved 125% text preference. Baseline UI/config came directly from Git; unchanged shared sources and frozen dependencies were reused without mutating the candidate. These are **browser screenshots, not native Mac app screenshots**. The browser cannot automatically translate the old CSS preference into browser-owned zoom; its saved value remains intact.

**Before** — the legacy control applies 125% text scaling.

![Before: desktop Appearance with Text size and 125% selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f72c026-081d-4d40-bcc9-b589ad0e5b91)

**After** — the control is retired; standard host zoom owns desktop sizing.

![After: desktop Appearance without the legacy Text size control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4902577-bf52-4433-b172-906064bece31)

<details>
<summary>Historical fork proof and remaining native gaps</summary>

[@jjjhenriksen’s full validation comment and provenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178541#issuecomment-6297202064).

Historical source 9d3ce54df1f00a41e30dae6931ddd57a4c3e1485 linked the app but failed test-bundle compilation on nested snapshot-helper require expansion ([original run](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39461410773)). The exact helper split landed at f48d09d30f27f9a87087baa3c92b64a6e149c857; its then-full test file matched fork SHA-256 8224648521d6d7476049706e4b56201124e64bb085e86df524cbf4fb994618d6. That helper remains fixed. This candidate changes native code and adds migration assertions: the old full-file hash/source-equivalence claim is historical, not applicable to the expanded candidate.

[Candidate diagnostic](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39463498627) passed 2 zoom (7.930 s), 4 close-shortcut (4.711 s), and 1 session-shortcut (3.392 s) tests. [Baseline diagnostic](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39463503201) failed immediate numeric zoom assertions; its later 600-second titlebar timeout was separate, not the sole red. Historical browser candidate passed the selected 200% header regression; baseline failed height 116 vs 58. Chromium chrome-emulation proof does not validate this new retirement policy or AppKit input.

[Actual-product run](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39464796089) remained **overall FAILURE**. Registered View actions and NSApplication-posted shortcuts passed zoom/reset/bounds/persistence in 25.477 s on **Model Setup, not chat**. Native-chat loaded no usable document within 194.586 s and performed zero menu checks: unverified, not proven broken. Process-group cleanup failed; hosted cleanup terminated orphans. Both full-window screencapture attempts exited 6. Human-inspected WKWebView captures are not full-window native-app proof. No physical keyboard, full upstream matrix, upgrade, distribution-signing, deployment, or Windows native runtime validation is claimed.

Earlier unchanged launcher checks passed 18/18 (7.95 s Vitest / 11.22 s shard); targeted CSS Stylelint passed for the existing native-header repair. These are supporting historical checks, not validation of the newly added migration flow.

Artifacts: [original native](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39461410773/artifacts/12283238644) · [candidate diagnostic](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39463498627/artifacts/12285710387) · [baseline diagnostic](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39463503201/artifacts/12285880827) · [browser candidate](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39461410773/artifacts/12282513069) · [browser baseline](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39461410773/artifacts/12283726134) · [product/harness receipts](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39464796089/artifacts/12285755901).

title: fix: keep long pastes inline in empty message boxes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long text pasted into an empty Chat or New Session message box unexpectedly becomes a file attachment.

## User Impact

Users can paste a long prompt directly into an empty message box. If text is already present, pastes over 1,000 characters still become attachments; shorter pastes and image pasting are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared paste handler now checks the current draft before converting long text to an attachment, preserving native browser insertion for an empty draft.

## Evidence

- Native Chromium clipboard regression failed before the fix in both Chat and New Session; both now pass for empty-input insertion, nonempty-input attachment creation, and restoring the exact pasted contents.
- 184 focused tests passed across attachment intake, composer rendering, pasted-text recovery, and sidebar behavior (20.57 seconds including runner startup).
- All 9 pasted-text browser scenarios passed, including mobile presentation, Gateway CSP, saved-draft reload, original attachment bytes, and downloads (60.65 seconds including the production UI build; the two new clipboard cases took 1.26 and 1.06 seconds).
- Production UI build, UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and git diff whitespace checks passed. Browser flows use a mocked Gateway and real Chromium clipboard insertion, not a live model call. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39456607589) passed on `f225c88ea6bbfe2dd75da8957bcc21c8c292450f`, including all UI unit and E2E shards; the required aggregate, dependency, and security checks are green.
- CI follow-up: the first ready-head run exposed four New Session attachment-lifecycle cases that still pasted into an empty draft. The fixture now enters text first, preserving all original restoration, dictation, route-change, and disconnect assertions. Those tests fail before the fixture correction and pass after it; 18 focused tests across New Session and successor-event suites pass (6.73 seconds including startup). Targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks also pass. Production code and the 9-scenario E2E proof are unchanged.
- That CI shard also reported a custom-element double-registration error while collecting the unchanged successor-event suite. It did not reproduce in the focused 18-test run; no fix is claimed for that collection error.
- ClawSweeper re-reviewed the implementation and reported no actionable findings on the original production-code head.
- Fresh independent Auto Review found no P0–P2 defects. The reviewer assessed the frozen diff and supplied validation; its sandbox could not execute commands to independently rerun those checks.
- pr-simplify: retained one shared decision owner and no new abstractions, state, or compatibility paths. Net change: +5 production lines, +55 test/helper lines, +1 documentation line. Remaining test growth covers the two distinct composer entry points and preserves existing attachment lifecycle coverage.

title: fix: show repository updates instead of waiting during worktree creation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new worktree session shows the generic "Waiting for turn to start…" while the Gateway updates the repository before checkout, including after the chat is reopened during that wait.

## User Impact

Users see **"Updating repository…"** while the default branch is fetched, then the existing checkout, setup and model progress. Pinned retries and explicit base refs resolve locally and go straight to "Creating worktree…". No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The worktree service already reports `checkout` and `setup` progress. It now reports `base` immediately before the default-branch fetch, and `checkout` after the base resolves.
- Session creation maps `base` to the new `preparing_worktree_base` startup phase; the Control UI labels it "Updating repository…".
- Chat history replay uses the existing session-progress predicate, so an accepted run that has not started yet replays its status after a reload.
- Protocol: one additive startup-phase value. Native apps map unknown phases to no label, so released clients ignore it.

## Evidence

- Real browser against a real Gateway and local bare origin, with the fetch held: base showed "Waiting for turn to start…"; this change showed "Updating repository…", kept it across a chat reload, and checked out the newly published default-branch commit after release. Stop cleared the status with no late checkout.
- `base-ref.test.ts`: against a real remote, the default base reports `base` before `fetch` and ends with `checkout`; an explicit `HEAD` ref reports only `checkout`. Fails on the earlier unconditional emit.
- `chat-abort.history-budget.test.ts`: accepted preparation replays before execution and clears on cancellation.
- `chat-gateway.model-wait.test.ts`: label renders, then yields to model-wait states.

### Before

![Before: generic waiting text during the real repository fetch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ad7fbf2-9d66-48fb-9b2b-658c6f17405f)

### After

![After: Updating repository status during the real repository fetch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3d54ae8-dea6-4694-a9a4-2ca201a75e24)

title: feat: attribute delegated work to the initiating human
body:
Related: #169139 (closed predecessor), #157806 (upstream requester identity plumbing).

## What Problem This Solves

Agent-delegated sessions and automations can appear agent-created even when a verified human initiated the work, leaving that human without creator-only management controls.

## User Impact

New sessions created through agent tools, native/visible/ACP delegations, and agent-created automations retain the verified initiating human as creator. **This is normal behavior, not a Lab. No configuration change is required.** The previously proposed toggle and experimental setting have been removed.

- Creator identity affects discovery, sharing/public-link management, archive/restore, attribution, and creator-based owner/personal-profile fallbacks—not only archiving. Assigned ownership remains separate.
- Existing creators are not rewritten. A selected tool-execution user is not automatically the initiating human. Autonomous work without a retained human stays agent/system-created.
- Execution authority, model/tool permissions, required sandbox containment, and its original identity namespace remain separate from creator attribution. Public links still require explicit publication; anonymous access, exclusions, revocation, and subsequent-message behavior are unchanged.
- Compatible older readers use their original creator semantics and preserve the nested attribution for a later upgrade. Ordinary schema-compatibility safeguards still apply: this does not make unrelated newer database formats downgradeable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Build on the existing requester-provenance path from #157806 rather than treating assignment or selected execution identity as evidence of who initiated the work. Creator attribution is retained inside the immutable creation record; the original actor remains available to isolation owners and compatible older readers. No database schema/version change is introduced.

The creator/admin archive rule is retained. No Labs UI or configuration-schema delta remains against main. Documentation lives in the normal sessions guide.

Requested by and developed with @VACInc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5288680a-9b75-4e62-93a1-b542110788b0)

## Evidence

Latest head: 3f0e121451973deef51ee10f1c63f0e36c6f4319.

**Default-attribution fixture repair:** CI39515202388 exposed eight stale fixture/assertion failures across hosted session scopes, independent input transfer, and cron validation. All eight were reproduced locally. Human-initiated test callers now explicitly carry their authenticated request origin; scheduled/unidentified callers remain un-attributed. Autonomous cron expectations retain the original isolation actor and separately expect agent creator attribution. No production permission or creator logic changed in this repair. title: feat: restore task-boundary and cache-expiry compaction
body:
Restores #178021 after #178425. Related: #6757.

## What Problem This Solves

Long conversations need optional compaction at useful task boundaries and before eligible cache windows end, without repeatedly compacting short-lived caches.

## User Impact

Agents can request task-boundary compaction, and operators can opt into one idle pre-expiry attempt. Every eligible window leaves a **five-minute lead**: **30 minutes → 25 minutes; one hour → 55 minutes; an effective 12-hour Responses TTL → 11 hours 55 minutes**. Windows of **five minutes or less never trigger** this timer.

The timer remains disabled by default and respects `compaction.enabled: false`. Foreground activity cancels pending work; a later successful eligible turn can arm a fresh timer. Maintenance never rearms itself. Normal context-pressure compaction, manual compaction, prompt caching, and model-requested compaction retain their existing behavior.

**Subscription scope:** ChatGPT/Codex OAuth through the **built-in OpenClaw runtime** may use an explicitly assumed 30-minute idle window, giving a 25-minute idle trigger. This is labeled `codex-idle-heuristic`, **not a verified Codex TTL**. Native Codex app-server and generic CLI timers are **not enabled**. In particular, the native standalone compact RPC cannot carry the admitted turn generation required by ChatGPT subscription sharing; this change does not bypass that guard or silently switch runtimes.

Compaction costs inference and can lose detail; cache hits or savings are not guaranteed. No live configuration was changed and no paid-provider cache experiment was run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing scheduler now applies one five-minute margin instead of its previous one-minute maximum. Existing API qualification stays intact: effective one-hour Anthropic markers and qualified direct OpenAI minimum windows still require successful cache activity. The new subscription estimate also requires positive cache usage, OAuth, the canonical `openai` provider, and the official HTTPS ChatGPT Responses backend. Unknown providers, aliases, and custom backends receive no assumed lifetime.

Provider-backed estimates retain request-start timing. The subscription heuristic starts at observed completion of model activity, so generation time is not mislabeled idle time. Existing selection, credentials, configuration, compaction-count, foreground, delivery, and lifecycle checks retain ownership of cancellation and admission.

The original restoration and earlier CI repairs remain in history. The earlier conflict refresh used `bead2a8e542740f943fe57e8391e5e6c11e9773d`. After the inventory repair, GitHub reported a new actual conflict. A history-preserving merge of pinned main `1bd22b28d632ba4082e923d88a2485be61f8c8af` resolved it: the only textual conflicts were the generated config count/hash artifacts, regenerated by their owner. Main’s tool-inheritance refactor and removal of its unused development dependency were preserved. The five-minute classifier, timer, maintenance runtime, and authored behavior docs are byte-identical across this refresh. No unrelated API-retention setting was changed.

CI then exposed a stale dependency entry in the restored plugin: main already requires TypeBox 1.3.37, while its manifest and importer still named 1.3.36. The three-line repair aligns those entries with the existing main pin. The lockfile was regenerated from the verified valid main graph; every other importer, package, and snapshot remains unchanged. No dependency policy was weakened.

## Evidence

Its request fields, defaults, compatibility rules and pricing are preserved. The model-version predicate is shared, and optional idle compaction consumes the same lifetime resolver with the prepared request policy. Qualified direct Responses requests using `12h` now schedule at **11h55m**, not 25m. Completions do not inherit this Responses-only option; the built-in OAuth assumption stays separately labeled 30m/25m. Unknown endpoints and short windows remain excluded.
- **Cross-contract proof:** 175 tests across nine complete files passed in 128.75 s, covering request builders, pricing, parameter precedence, classifier, settlement forwarding, scheduler boundaries, prefix stability and embedded-command maintenance. Three new policy cases failed before the fix. Targeted agent/package test types, nine-file lint, formatting, two-file MDX, canonical config/inventory checks, frozen install and diff checks passed.
