title: fix(android): open and share chat file attachments
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PDF, CSV, and other document attachments appearing only as filenames in Android chat, with no way to open or share their contents.

## User Impact

Users can open or share a file directly from its chat card. Files download only on demand; loading, download success, retryable failure, and a missing viewer have visible feedback. A downloaded file is a temporary cache copy, not a file saved to Downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing chat attachment group now uses the existing authenticated `artifacts.download` loader and Android FileProvider. Document transport matches the shared iOS file contract, including its 100 MiB bound. Read-only content-URI grants expose only the staged file; file downloads do not follow redirects. No new endpoint, permission, dependency, or embedded viewer.

The passive filename branch is replaced with one file-action component. Necessary growth is the Android handoff/state UI and full-ChatScreen regression fixture, rather than a second downloader or cache manager.

## Evidence

Verified head: `bb5f737128d7138032249c91c74ff44e4b4e0cdc`.
Base: `aac3cd07885da4b1fe03a49975a25f49a3422b36` (live main fetched for this task).

- **Red → green:** the same production ChatScreen regression compiles on the exact base, captures the Before image, then fails at the missing `Open release-report.pdf` action. It passes with this fix.
- **CI repair:** reproduced both failing cases from [run 39432099126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39432099126). `ChatMessageViewsTest` now distinguishes message-popup actions from document-card actions. `ChatComposerLayoutTest` checks the real text Surface against its 78% budget and the detached-media envelope separately. Both cases pass in Play and ThirdParty (7.27 s in ThirdParty; build + scoped lint 92 s). Play also passes the 12 file/media cases (14 total, 11.10 s test time; 41 s build wall). No production changes in the repair. Independent AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- **Original 31 focused tests pass:** 2 new full-ChatScreen cases (3.944 s on the final run), 19 Gateway/transport cases (8.558 s), and 10 unchanged media-layout cases (0.932 s in the combined run). The 31-test compile/run took 88 s wall; final affected-test + style + APK validation took 44 s.
- The UI tests traverse real ChatScreen → MainViewModel → ChatController → GatewaySession against a loopback synthetic WebSocket server, then read exact PDF/CSV bytes back through the real manifest FileProvider. They cover lazy download, disabled duplicate actions, immutable reuse, retry, and missing-viewer sharing.
- Transport coverage includes chunked PDF, inline CSV, context paths, ticket/type checks, declared oversize, missing MIME, cross-origin redirects, disconnected loads, and existing image/audio/video behavior.
- Scoped Gradle `ktlintCheck`, `:app:assemblePlayDebug`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `pnpm android:i18n:check`, commit hooks, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent AutoReview: complete, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The later owner-generated string inventory and equivalent Accept-header constant were inspected; affected tests, lint, and APK assembly were rerun.

**Proof context:** genuine production Compose/ChatScreen captures in Robolectric API 34 native graphics, 360 × 800, dark theme, identical synthetic PDF/CSV chat. These are not design reconstructions. These screenshots do not show installed viewer/share-sheet rendering. Installed cross-app handoff and OS permission enforcement are verified separately below; no physical device or live deployed Gateway was exercised.

<details><summary>Focused commands</summary>

```sh
cd apps/android
./gradlew --no-daemon --max-workers=2 :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \
  --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatFileAttachmentLayoutTest' \
  --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatMessageMediaLayoutTest' \
  --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.gateway.GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest'
./gradlew --no-daemon --max-workers=2 --continue -I <changed-files-init-script> \
  :app:ktlintCheck :app:assemblePlayDebug
```

The external init script restricts ktlint to the six touched Kotlin files; repository lint rules are unchanged. Final affected-test rerun includes ChatFileAttachmentLayoutTest and GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest.

</details>

CI for verified head `bb5f737128d7138032249c91c74ff44e4b4e0cdc`: [run 39437672857](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39437672857) **passed**: 34 successful jobs, 26 skipped by the workflow plan, zero failures or running jobs. Play, ThirdParty, Wear, Android ktlint, and both native Android lanes passed. [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178443#issuecomment-6292538039) on the same head (2026-10-20 14:34 UTC) accepts the installed permission proof, reports no findings or Before-merge items, and marks the PR **ready for maintainer review**. Not merged.

### Installed cross-app permission proof — passed

The installed production `ChatFileAttachment`, real manifest FileProvider, intents, and Android system chooser were exercised on Android 12/API 31 x86_64 with SELinux **Enforcing**. The download callback alone supplied synthetic PDF/CSV bytes. Independent recipient APKs ran under different UIDs: owner **10105**, selected **10107**, ungranted **10108**. No production intent interception or test-added grants.

| Action | Selected recipient, exact bytes | Ungranted app | Other existing, never-shared file | New open after revocation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PDF Open | 597 bytes, twice | Denied | Denied | Denied |
| PDF Share | 597 bytes, twice | Denied | Denied | Denied |
| CSV Open | 39 bytes, twice | Denied | Denied | Denied |
| CSV Share | 39 bytes, twice | Denied | Denied | Denied |

**8 exact-byte reads and 12 `SecurityException` denials; `OK (1 test)`, 55.078 s, runner exit 0.** All negative receipts report `PERMISSION_DENIED` and `providerVisible=true`; all positives report `PERMISSION_GRANTED`. A still-granted reread precedes revocation, and the owner first reads the unshared sibling, so missing files, package invisibility, or activity navigation cannot explain the denials.

The fresh APK was built from `e7ca40e72360c044ce99a1169826fa072e9d4b78`; the **only** differences through current head `bb5f737128d7138032249c91c74ff44e4b4e0cdc` are the two CI test selectors. Production inputs are identical. The installed APK was pulled back and matched byte-for-byte to the build: SHA-256 `5ed855778c2598604c7c0a462b5673bec206d88c4172a8ff1c26749953928709`.

**Limitations:** installed attachment-component/OS-boundary proof, not installed full-ChatScreen, live-Gateway, physical-device, OEM, or multi-API proof. Full-ChatScreen/RPC regressions and visual captures above are separate complementary evidence. No live Gateway was changed.

<details><summary>Native commands, fixture sources and per-read receipts</summary>

Built in an isolated source snapshot with this additional androidTest fixture (not production changes):

```sh
./gradlew --no-daemon --max-workers=2 \
  -PopenclawBuildCommit=e7ca40e72360c044ce99a1169826fa072e9d4b78 \
  :app:assemblePlayDebug :app:assemblePlayDebugAndroidTest
adb -P 5067 -s emulator-5630 shell am instrument -w -r \
  -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatFileUriGrantDeviceTest \
  ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner
```

```text

OK (1 test)
INSTRUMENTATION_CODE: -1
```

Receiver manifests declare the explicit OpenClaw package query (visibility only), exported `ReceiverActivity`, and no read permission/shared UID. Only the selected receiver handles `ACTION_VIEW`/`ACTION_SEND` for `application/pdf` and `text/csv`. Each negative probe passes a URI as a string extra only—no data, ClipData, stream extra, or read grant—and performs a fresh `ContentResolver.openInputStream` in the recipient process. The actual sources used are included below; these are evidence-only fixtures, not product code.

Expected synthetic-byte SHA-256:

```kotlin
          val uri = Uri.parse(received.getString("uri"))
          assertEquals(app.packageName + ".fileprovider", uri.authority)
          assertEquals(uri.toString(), received.getString("clipUri"))
          assertTrue(received.getInt("flags") and Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION != 0)

          val sibling = File(app.cacheDir, "chat-files/ungranted-$case.txt").apply { writeText("synthetic never shared") }

private fun uriProofPdf(): ByteArray {
  val text = "BT /F1 14 Tf 36 100 Td (Release checks passed.) Tj ET\n"
  val objects =
    listOf(
      "<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
      "<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
      "<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 300 150] /Resources << /Font << /F1 4 0 R >> >> /Contents 5 0 R >>",
      "<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>",
      "<< /Length ${text.length} >>\nstream\n${text}endstream",
    )
  val pdf = StringBuilder("%PDF-1.4\n")
  val offsets =
    objects.mapIndexed { index, value ->
      pdf.length.also { pdf.append("${index + 1} 0 obj\n$value\nendobj\n") }
    }
  val xref = pdf.length
  pdf.append("xref\n0 6\n0000000000 65535 f \n")
  offsets.forEach { pdf.append(it.toString().padStart(10, '0')).append(" 00000 n \n") }
  pdf.append("trailer\n<< /Size 6 /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n$xref\n%%EOF\n")
  return pdf.toString().toByteArray(Charsets.US_ASCII)
}
```

```java
package ai.openclaw.uriproof;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.content.Intent;
import android.net.Uri;
import android.os.Bundle;
import android.os.Process;
import android.util.Base64;
import android.widget.TextView;
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.io.InputStream;
import org.json.JSONObject;

/** Test APK: never bundled with OpenClaw; reads only the URI delivered to this UID. */
public final class ReceiverActivity extends Activity {
  @Override public void onCreate(Bundle state) { super.onCreate(state); inspect(getIntent()); }
  @Override public void onNewIntent(Intent intent) { super.onNewIntent(intent); setIntent(intent); inspect(intent); }
  private void inspect(Intent intent) {
    JSONObject receipt = new JSONObject();
    try {
      Uri uri = intent.getData();
      if (uri == null) uri = intent.getParcelableExtra(Intent.EXTRA_STREAM);
      if (uri == null) uri = Uri.parse(intent.getStringExtra("probeUri"));
      receipt.put("package", getPackageName()).put("uid", Process.myUid()).put("pid", Process.myPid());
      receipt.put("action", intent.getAction()).put("type", intent.getType()).put("flags", intent.getFlags());
      receipt.put("uri", uri.toString());
      receipt.put("uriPermission", checkUriPermission(uri, Process.myPid(), Process.myUid(), Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION));
      receipt.put("providerVisible", getPackageManager().resolveContentProvider(uri.getAuthority(), 0) != null);
      receipt.put("clipUri", intent.getClipData() == null ? "" : intent.getClipData().getItemAt(0).getUri().toString());
      try (InputStream in = getContentResolver().openInputStream(uri); ByteArrayOutputStream out = new ByteArrayOutputStream()) {
        byte[] buffer = new byte[8192];
        int n;
        while ((n = in.read(buffer)) >= 0) out.write(buffer, 0, n);
        receipt.put("outcome", "read").put("bytes", Base64.encodeToString(out.toByteArray(), Base64.NO_WRAP));
      } catch (Exception error) {
        receipt.put("outcome", "denied").put("exception", error.getClass().getName()).put("message", error.getMessage());
      }
      TextView view = new TextView(this);
      view.setText(getPackageName() + "\n" + receipt.optString("outcome") + "\n" + uri);
      setContentView(view);
      sendBroadcast(new Intent("ai.openclaw.uriproof.RESULT").setPackage("ai.openclaw.app.debug").putExtra("receipt", receipt.toString()));
    } catch (Exception error) { throw new RuntimeException(error); }
  }
}
```

title: fix(android): find setup codes among unrelated QR codes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android rejects a valid OpenClaw setup QR when an unrelated QR is returned first from the same image or camera frame.

## User Impact

Camera scanning skips unsuitable codes and keeps scanning. Both onboarding and Add Gateway gallery imports find the first usable setup code among the results. Existing validation errors and connection flows stay unchanged: Add Gateway waits for **Connect**; first-run onboarding retains its existing connection flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three paths now select through the existing setup resolver. Gallery imports retain the first rejection's diagnostic when no usable candidate exists. No new parsing policy, credentials, dependencies, or connection state. Production delta: +24/−14 lines; +384 test lines cover three production entry points without adding production test hooks.

## Evidence

Verified head: `e5d655b8e1b823adc16811ab2fc2e95323740871`, tree-identical to the locally tested/reviewed candidate. Based on refreshed live main `aac3cd07885da4b1fe03a49975a25f49a3422b36`.

- Three regression tests fail on unchanged main for the intended defects and pass with this fix: CameraX callback, onboarding gallery Activity Result, and Add Gateway gallery Activity Result. They cover empty/invalid results, a later valid candidate, one-shot camera delivery, retry controls, and no connection before Add Gateway confirmation.
- `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.SetupQrSelectionTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.GatewayConfigResolverTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.OnboardingFlowLogicTest`: **140 passed**. Existing `SidebarGatewayPickerTest.addGateway*`: **1 passed**. Final regression-file test time: **8.865 s**; focused rerun plus scoped ktlint: **22 s wall**. Native Compose/Activity Result and CameraX lifecycle boundaries justify the integration-test cost.
- `:app:assemblePlayDebug`, `:app:lintPlayDebug`, scoped `:app:ktlintCheck`, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Auto Review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- iOS camera's validate-before-delivery pattern was checked. Its separate photo-picker first-result issue remains outside this Android fix.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39431593865) completed successfully: Android Play, third-party and Wear tests, ktlint, both native-access checks, native i18n, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The earlier draft run was skipped; it is not passing CI evidence.
- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178442#issuecomment-6292729612) inspected this exact head and native proof: no actionable findings.

### Native before / after

**Actual Android emulator screenshots, not reconstructions.** On the same isolated API 31 emulator (480×900, dark theme), the real Android file picker and bundled ML Kit read the exact same `02-reversed.png` file. Unchanged main rejects it; the fix selects `wss://qr-preview.invalid:443` and reaches the existing confirmation. **Connect was never pressed.**

| Before — unchanged main | After — fixed app |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native before: mixed QR image rejected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6260cbbc-b15a-4b70-ad73-710b8a3994a3) | ![Native after: same QR image reaches confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdffc3e0-7e72-4a9b-8c8c-28f6094472ed) |

**Invalid-only image on the fixed app:** the existing error remains, with manual entry and gallery retry available.

![Native no match: invalid-only image is rejected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dcabf6e-20c4-4f7f-bb73-fb1e98a67a13)

<details><summary>Synthetic input and deterministic callback proof</summary>

The reproduced input contains an OpenClaw setup code and an unrelated open Wi-Fi QR, with no credentials or usable Gateway. SHA-256: `3827c5f7e32cc4e52aaf211120d16f886a7a3b3953b52cb3f236a4cf85babc90`.

![Synthetic two-QR input used for native before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/45c78ac8-5fc6-4629-8553-c2199b3acb68)

The opposite image layout already reached confirmation on the baseline, demonstrating that the defect depends on decoder result order rather than a universal left-to-right rule. The native invalid-only image contains an unrelated Wi-Fi QR and an `.invalid` web URL.

Separate production Compose/Robolectric captures use fixed ML Kit result fixtures (412×900): [before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22913912-1124-4e5e-a495-3f2a5c281e22), [after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe4d05b3-e3fb-4b51-950e-146740fe93fe), and [onboarding no-match recovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba3e0875-3ca8-4c20-972b-9bbc056fe467). The onboarding test holds the external TLS boundary; no DNS, socket, or Gateway is contacted.

</details>

**Limits:** CameraX completion and frame release are regression-tested with simulated scanner results; physical-camera capture is not exercised. The native gallery proof uses the app's existing isolated screenshot fixture. No real credentials, live Gateway connections, or running Gateway changes.

title: fix(android): keep file and provider list endings above system navigation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the end of Android workspace file lists, file previews, and provider lists can extend behind system navigation.

## User Impact

Users can reach the final file, “Load more,” preview text, and model details above the system navigation area. Gesture navigation uses its actual smaller inset; already-consumed insets are not added twice. No configuration changes or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `ClawScaffold` safe-drawing owner by removing three Top/Horizontal-only overrides left over from bottom-app-navigation ownership. The scaffold and sidebar stay unchanged; existing content spacing is preserved.

Production: **−11 lines** across two screens. Tests: **+352 lines** for two production-screen regression cases, including synthetic loopback Gateway data; no production test hooks, new dependencies, or permanent capture machinery.

Co-authored with @IWhatsskill.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5936a51-4929-42e5-a2ac-9a19dd0e0b21)
- [Additional Android regression and visual verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/accae546-8b9b-4542-b0bc-66f422cbbf16)

## Evidence

- Head: `dda6e18952146def7fac9a87856b2b9916afac45`.
- Based on live `main` at `77d9f42c86bf42ee05f997ec5f838ad95d268a0a`; later checked `aac3cd07885da4b1fe03a49975a25f49a3422b36` has no Android changes relative to that base.
- Red/green: both new tests fail on baseline across all three unconsumed screens, then pass with this fix. At a 48dp inset the viewport bottom changes from 796dp to 748dp; at 24dp, to 772dp. All six already-consumed controls pass before and after.
- **7 tests passed**, zero failures/skips; includes **12 geometry cases** through the real screens and `SidebarNavigationShell`. Targeted ktlint and unit-test compilation passed.
- New regression file: **4.477s** test-suite time. Combined focused checks: **45.88s** command wall time. Hosted CI duration: **16m 16s** (run creation to completion).
- Independent Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- CI: [passed on this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39430836938): Android Play, third-party and Wear tests, ktlint, both native-access jobs, native i18n, security-fast, and the required CI gate passed. Skipped screenshot/release-e2e jobs are not counted as passing proof.

<details>

title: fix(android): announce settings toggles as one labeled switch
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes separate, unlabeled switch targets when navigating Android settings and notification app selection with accessibility services.

## User Impact

Each setting exposes one switch with its label and current state. Tapping either the text or the visible switch changes the same setting once, while disabled controls and permission-gated settings retain their existing behavior. Appearance and touch area are preserved; no migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The full row now owns the switch action, role, and state; the inner switch is display-only. Its minimum size is retained, and decorative app initials no longer become part of the accessible label. Existing state owners and permission flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Before / after media

Actual production settings screens captured with Robolectric native graphics, Android API 34, a 420 × 780 dp viewport, dark theme, and synthetic fixture data. The numbered outlines and adjacent cards are **annotations from the measured Compose semantics tree**, not TalkBack focus frames. Both source revisions use the same capture fixture.

**Before — Camera**

![Original Camera row: two measured click targets](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79d4ae69-2765-4f0c-8ba3-b259cda8a42d)

**After — Camera**

![Fixed Camera row: one named switch with Off state](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb7ec7f9-8647-4d92-8274-b69928d02236)

<details><summary>Notification app selection: before / after</summary>

**Before**

![Original app selection: decorated row label and a separate unnamed switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5222ea5f-9338-4581-8eb8-2f967cd8f41f)

**After**

![Fixed app selection: one switch with app label and On state](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eea0e2af-d171-4445-bfb0-8635408112d3)

</details>

The unannotated PNGs are byte-identical between base and head for each matched state, confirming no visual change: [Camera Off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7679472c-db5d-4959-bfb5-78ffe6509bdc), [Camera On](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e36e46b-1a39-494e-ae51-50fc7cf3b7ce), [selected notification app](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9fd71b1e-b498-43c6-918d-e9d19b3e016a).

| Observed runtime semantics | Original main | PR head |
|---|---|---|
| Camera click targets | 2; label on row, role/state on unnamed child | 1; label, Switch role and Off/On state together |
| Camera row bounds | 388 × 60 dp | 388 × 60 dp |
| Notification app click targets | 2; decorative initials included in row label | 1; app name + package, Switch role and On state |
| Notification app row bounds | 364 × 60 dp | 364 × 60 dp |

Expected traversal is row → separate switch → next row before, versus one switch row → next row after. Expected Camera speech is “Camera, Allow camera tools when requested, Off, switch” or “… On, switch”; exact wording/order depends on TalkBack. **Neither traversal nor speech was observed with TalkBack.**

### Reproduced test evidence

The exact regression tests committed in [SettingsTogglePanelTest.kt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b401685e250dcd1191f944d9f2601a5e52e8bdc8/apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/SettingsTogglePanelTest.kt) and [NotificationSettingsScreenTest.kt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b401685e250dcd1191f944d9f2601a5e52e8bdc8/apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/NotificationSettingsScreenTest.kt) were run on both source revisions.

| Focused suite | Original main + identical tests | PR head |
|---|---:|---:|
| SettingsTogglePanelTest | 0/2 passed | 2/2 passed |
| NotificationSettingsScreenTest | 2/7 passed | 7/7 passed |
| Temporary production-screen capture fixture | 2/2 passed | 2/2 passed |

The seven original-source failures are specific semantics assertions, not setup failures: three require `Role.Switch` on the labeled row; four require its `ToggleableState.Off` while notification listener access is missing. With the fix all nine regression tests pass. The temporary fixture additionally captures Camera Off/On through the production screen and verifies notification package deselection. It introduces no production seam and is not part of the source patch.

```text
Original: SettingsTogglePanelTest       tests=2 failures=2 errors=0 time=0.085s
Original: NotificationSettingsScreenTest tests=7 failures=5 errors=0 time=6.115s
PR head:  SettingsTogglePanelTest       tests=2 failures=0 errors=0 time=0.153s
PR head:  NotificationSettingsScreenTest tests=7 failures=0 errors=0 time=7.296s
Capture-only final runs: original 2/2 passed (28s wall), PR head 2/2 passed (29s wall)
```

- Based on main `77d9f42c86bf42ee05f997ec5f838ad95d268a0a`.
- Verified PR head: `b401685e250dcd1191f944d9f2601a5e52e8bdc8`; its complete source tree is identical to tested commit `c3fdfb0c1afec0364dcc3b136cf9515c5929e3b5`.
- Focused Play-debug compilation and Robolectric/Compose tests: **9 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Coverage includes a single labeled switch, on/off state, taps across the row, disabled input, notification package filtering, and forwarding remaining off while listener access is missing.
- Targeted Gradle ktlint checks for all three changed Kotlin files and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent Codex Auto Review: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the complete local diff. The review covered the patch and supplied evidence; runtime checks were executed separately.
- Simplification pass: removed duplicate interaction ownership without adding state or abstractions. Production delta: +9/-5 lines; tests: +138 lines covering the shared control and notification-screen integration.

**Limitations:** This is Compose semantics and interaction proof, not observed TalkBack speech. No real-device TalkBack or VoiceOver run was performed. No visual redesign is included.

<details><summary>Focused validation commands and timing</summary>

From `apps/android`, with the installed Android SDK configured:

```sh
./gradlew --no-daemon --max-workers=2 :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.SettingsTogglePanelTest \

./gradlew --no-daemon --max-workers=2 --continue -I <changed-file-filter.init.gradle> :app:ktlintCheck
git diff --check
```

The temporary lint filter selects `SettingsScreens.kt`, `SettingsTogglePanelTest.kt`, and `NotificationSettingsScreenTest.kt` without changing repository rules. Latest source-bound regression XML reports 0.153 seconds for the toggle panel and 7.296 seconds for the notification screen. Kotlin lint completed in 20 seconds on the unchanged production/test patch. The separate successful capture runs and their wall times are recorded above. CI timing is not yet available.

</details>

CI for the verified head: [run 39428564943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39428564943) **passed**, including Android Play/third-party/Wear tests, ktlint, native-access checks, localization, security, and the required `openclaw/ci-gate`. ## User Impact

Explicit Gateway desktops and focused sessions targeting that Gateway now reuse setup guidance, authorized enablement, and same-host retry. Back is available during setup/sign-in and other nonconnected focused states, including the unselected picker.

Desktop remains admin-only. Enablement requires the existing config authority and explicit action; OpenClaw does not change OS sharing permissions. No new settings, schema, migration, or setup owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

#177888 fixed chat recovery but deliberately left focused windows unchanged. This follow-up wires those missing entry points into the same setup and runtime-config owners rather than introducing another Systems-navigation flow.

The quality follow-up adds only a small admission regression: an advertised Desktop method must still reject a non-admin connection, offer no Enable action, dispatch no config patch/desktop observation, and retain Back. Production code is unchanged by that follow-up.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: tooltips for the left sidebar rail (Pages, Sessions, People, search, pins, new conversation, home) open above the icon and clamp against the window edge, covering neighboring rail buttons.

User impact: hovering or focusing a rail item shows its tooltip to the right of the icon, vertically centered, matching the existing Community entry. Narrow (mobile) layouts keep their existing below-anchor fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar tooltips showed keyboard shortcuts as parenthesized text, e.g. "New conversation (⌘⇧O)", instead of the keycap style used elsewhere.

## Work sessions

User impact: sidebar tooltips now show the label followed by a keycap chip (for example, **New conversation** `⌘⇧O`) with no parentheses. This applies to New conversation, the rail view toggles, the rail search button, Collapse sidebar, the Home toggle, and the collapsed-sidebar Expand/Search/Home controls. `ShortcutHint` was the shared tooltip helper, and it was the code that added the parentheses. It now renders the label, a space, and a `.shortcut-hint__keys` keycap (a tinted chip in `kbd.css`). The sidebar controls that built their own `Label (⌘B)` strings (rail `title` attributes, the collapse toggle, and the collapsed-shell controls) now use `ShortcutHint` inside `openclaw-tooltip`. ## What Problem This Solves

Refreshes maintained dependencies that have completed the seven-day release cooldown, without including unrelated repairs or breaking toolchain migrations.

## User Impact

No intentional user-facing behavior or configuration change. Compatible dependency fixes are included while approved patches, native forks, and supported toolchain contracts remain intact. The SecOps-owned workflow pin bumps moved to #178708, so this PR no longer touches any CODEOWNERS-owned path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixed audit time is **2026-10-20T04:46:41Z**, so every newly selected release must have been published **on or before 2026-10-13T04:46:41Z**. Fresh main base: `b8daeb2a95a8a2bdb07d1bd950568a67b85c745d`; the prior merged refresh is not reused.

- Audited npm/pnpm workspace and standalone tooling, overrides/patches, all three Cargo graphs, both Ruby graphs, Swift resolutions, Android/Gradle, GitHub Actions/hooks, Go, and pinned container/toolchain artifacts using fresh upstream metadata.
- Updated **119 npm declarations across 23 package names**, regenerated the pnpm and standalone Vercel locks, and verified all **62 newly introduced npm package/version identities** meet the exact cutoff.
- Updated seven Rust crate identities, two Ruby dependencies and the MLX helper’s Swift Collections resolution. The two SHA-pinned token-action uses in the SecOps-owned security-review workflow moved to #178708.
- Retained still-valid exemptions and approved patches/forks; no new exclusions or overrides. The Edge TTS release-age exemption stays as on main.
- Regenerated six TypeBox validator files through their owner. Only generated source-path comments changed; no validator logic or schema changes.

title: fix(ui): sidebar agent status drops onto its own line below the row
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the agent-first sidebar, an agent's status (for example the failed-run alert triangle) renders on its own line beneath the agent row, making the row taller and pushing the icon away from the name it belongs to.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen. Follow-up to #178030, which repositioned only the tooltip.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6a9eb3f6-5e97-4e6a-8113-7ead80ed1f1b)

## User Impact

User impact: agent rows with a status keep the normal 44px height, and the alert sits inline at the right end of the row, vertically centered. When the row's `…` menu appears (hover, focus, or touch), the status moves left of it instead of being covered. Rows without a status are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The roster header placed its status slot in a second grid row (`grid-area: 2 / 2`). The header now adds a third `auto` column only when a status is present. The status goes in row 1 of that column, and the link spans the first two. When the absolutely positioned actions are revealed, the status moves left with a margin, so the link no longer reserves the same 32px twice.

title: fix(ui): keep agent settings inside the chat pill and grow it on hover
body:
Related: #178023

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bf357d7f-3f8d-42f9-a04e-7487d3e37970)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the chat agent pill's hover-revealed settings button floats outside the pill (after #178023) instead of being part of the hovered pill.

## User Impact

User impact: hovering the agent name in the chat header widens the pill to the right to show the settings icon inside it; the idle pill stays avatar + name, centered on the chat pane, with no tooltip.

The pill surface (border, background, radius) moves from the popover trigger to the identity wrapper that holds both the trigger and the settings button. Settings is collapsed to zero width until hover or keyboard focus. title: feat: compact at useful task boundaries and before cache expiry
body:
Related: #6757, #138084. The existing tool proposal was reviewed as prior art; no contributor source was copied or cherry-picked.

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running sessions need a model-selected compaction boundary and an opt-in idle trigger informed by the actual provider cache contract.

## User Impact

Users can enable the optional `session-compaction` plugin and allow `session_compact` to compact between substantial task steps, before the next model request. Separately, `agents.defaults.compaction.cacheExpiry.enabled` enables one idle compaction near a qualified cache window. Both are opt-in; unsupported routes and runtimes are skipped. Compaction costs inference and can lose detail; neither timing nor cache savings is guaranteed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool records one current-run request, then reuses the existing settled-tool boundary, controller, compaction writer, and transcript continuation. It preserves unresolved asks and completed actions without replay, coalesces requests across recovery attempts, and retains post-reply maintenance only as a safe fallback. Disabling proactive compaction does not disable required reply preflight or overflow recovery.

The idle trigger reuses cancellable session maintenance. It requires positive cache usage and qualified route/model/authentication facts, counts generation time, and invalidates on foreground work, restart, configuration, credentials, model selection, or intervening compaction. Maintenance never rearms itself. Current qualification is direct Anthropic API-key effective five-minute/one-hour TTLs and direct OpenAI API-key GPT-5.6+ minimum lifetime; other routes receive no guessed universal timer. Provider sources and retrieval date are documented.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Gateway with a deterministic provider: all three cases pass (`pnpm test test/gateway-requested-compaction.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`). Compaction precedes the next successful tool step and final reply; the pending ask survives; an append side effect occurs exactly once; a second tool request does not compact again. Summary rejection resumes the original history, and disabled configuration hides the tool.
- Production retirement proof in that same Gateway test: while the top-level run is still active and the next provider response is paused, a distinct current tool generation remains authorized (`already_requested`); the exact capability retained from the previous allowed tool batch rejects. Provider/summarizer request counts, persisted transcript statistics, and compaction count remain unchanged across the rejected call. No fake cancellation signal or production test hook is used.
- Stable-state upgrade proof: a real isolated npm `openclaw@2026.10.5` installation created settings and a conversation; the candidate at `102f8d5345bf` continued a copied state directory after the documented backed-up Doctor migration. All 21 original setting leaves and all six original transcript events were preserved, the same session continued to nine events, and the old history reached the deterministic provider. This tests data/runtime upgrade, not package-updater/install-over behavior.
- Required-preflight regression passes with proactive compaction disabled. Timer tests cover expiration, foreground cancellation, changed selection/account/configuration, intervening compaction, failed delivery, restart/cleanup, and no idle rearming. Provider qualification and unavailable-telemetry cases pass.
- Production build, core and root-proof typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, related overflow/cancellation and prefix-stability suites, documentation examples/links, and generated plugin inventory checks pass. Independent Auto Review reports `scoped-clean` for P0–P2 on the complete local candidate.
- Exact-commit SDK API comparison (`292ca7a1ff7c` → `7e0f10b4e463`, digest `76c5dd69`) completes successfully: no entrypoint or direct-export changes; 28 distinct reachable declaration changes are expected additive optional capability/configuration/runtime metadata. Later conflict composition changed only the generated config hash in the feature delta; this follow-up adds only proof tests, so the source-bound SDK result is reused rather than presented as a new-head render.
- No live paid-provider cache-hit, exact-expiry, or cost-saving claim is made. The summarizer need not reuse the foreground prompt prefix.

<details>
<summary>Implementation and investigation notes</summary>

The simplification pass retained the existing compaction and maintenance owners rather than adding a second pipeline, persistent timer store, or continuation manager. Command parameters, compaction parameter types, labels, and checkpoint test cases were moved to coherent siblings to satisfy existing line-cap gates without dropping coverage.

The generated configuration baseline intentionally grows by two core paths (`cacheExpiry` and `cacheExpiry.enabled`) and 21 standard registry-wrapper paths for the new bundled plugin. Its plugin-specific configuration schema is empty; the update records the requested opt-in feature, not additional controls or a waived regression.

The Gateway test caught a real retry-copy defect: a duplicate tool request caused a second compaction in the same run. Moving the request latch to the stable run owner fixes it; the strengthened proof is green. Two earlier fixture cases returned without observed provider activity before comprehensive failure diagnostics were added. Instrumented runs did not reproduce those outcomes; they remain unattributed test failures, not a claimed repaired defect.


The strengthened active-run retirement test initially observed a stale count because the test process retained metadata while a separate Gateway process committed the result. The observer now uses the canonical persisted-entry accessor in a fresh read-only scope, retaining the same count and transcript assertions; no production behavior or admission guard changed.

Upgrade commands used an isolated state/profile and deterministic loopback provider: the real stable CLI ran `config set agents.defaults.compaction.keepRecentTokens 4096` and `agent --local --agent main --session-key agent:main:compaction-upgrade-proof --message ... --json`; after a stopped-state copy, the candidate ran `pnpm openclaw --profile compaction-upgrade config validate`, `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions`, and the same local-agent continuation command with a new message that did not repeat the original history marker. The required credential-custody migration initially refused inference until Doctor completed normally. Doctor added seven default/bookkeeping paths and changed or removed none of the original settings. Original decoded transcript payload SHA-256 before/after: `2d26982efd2ff1afdef6ed0d838648d302cf75b26868fa354113b37c985cbb58`. Baseline: version `2026.10.5`, commit `1b58cb9a1b4f`, Node 24.20.0; candidate: `102f8d5345bf`, Node 26.8.2. Original data remained untouched. Test-only edits after that candidate do not affect this proof.

The original low-pressure request regression was red against the original owning implementation (expected one checkpoint, observed zero), then green with the feature. Full candidate Auto Review was scoped-clean for P0–P2; the added production-retirement fixture also received a separate scoped-clean static review. These reviews do not replace executed proof or current-head CI.

CI follow-up on `6ba24c5d82fe`: repaired stale result/catalog/finalization fixtures that omitted `requestedCompaction`, supplied the command fixture’s missing `getRuntimeConfigSnapshot`, and asserted complete schema parse results without dereferencing an optional root. Production code and runtime guards are unchanged. The 37-case attempt-result suite reproduced the missing fixture before repair. All 114 tests selected from failed runtime lanes pass across the repaired replay and the qualified loopback transport rerun; the 26 schema/catalog tests also pass. The `agents-other` and `config-cli` type graphs, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and P0–P2 Auto Review pass. Loopback transport verification used a test-local environment without ambient HTTP/WebSocket proxy variables; no provider or shared host settings were changed.

An earlier CI type error at `ui/src/e2e/session-scoped-delivery.e2e.test.ts:103` is inherited from the exact base `468217681c2b`: both base and PR contain blob `f9099f96aea18071dbf00f1ebb7e627c48e338e9`, whose local case union is `roster | preview-on` while the later branch compares `preview-off`. That unrelated UI file is unchanged. Current-head CI remains a separate gate; earlier failing runs are not relabeled green.

Final CI ratchet follow-up: the only non-aggregate failing job at `7c28ac046b49` was the mock-export ratchet. The shared config fixture now spreads the real `config/io` exports with `importOriginal` and retains its three intentional overrides. The owning `--prune` command removed exactly that obsolete closed-factory baseline entry (8160 → 8159); no exception or guard relaxation was added. `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base 06670bf9c41b2927d980c2818ed78d30fbff7c00 --no-merge-base` is red before this repair and green afterward. All ten shared-fixture consumer suites pass (135 tests), including both command-maintenance suites; the `agents-root`/`agents-other` type graphs, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Independent P0–P2 review of the fixture change is scoped-clean. Production source and its behavior/upgrade/SDK proof are unchanged. ClawSweeper’s durable review of `7c28ac046b49` reported no actionable findings; new-head CI/re-review remain separate checks.

</details>

title: fix(test): Gateway suite cases fail startup when a leftover sweep re-admits deleted state
body:
Related: CI flake on #163685 (run 39361137426, job 118427931731) and scheduled `main` CI (run 39328070942, job 118319144159).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: suite-scoped Gateway tests (for example `server-plugins.activation-health` and `server.hooks-admission`) intermittently fail startup with `Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable … STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED` when an earlier case in the same file left detached work running.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. CI stops failing unrelated PRs (and scheduled `main` runs) on this Gateway-suite flake.

## Why This Change Was Made

The suite-scoped Gateway fixture closes a case's databases in `afterEach`, then deletes and recreates the state directory in the next case's `beforeEach`. Gateway startup activates the subagent registry, which schedules a post-restore sweep 5 s later; that timer survives `server.close()`. When it fires between the fixture's close and its delete, the sweep re-captures a read admission for the old `openclaw.sqlite`. The fixture then deletes that file, and the next case's first shared-state worker binding finds a different physical file at the same path, invalidates the stale admission, and secrets activation fails startup.

The fixture now closes the home's databases again immediately before it deletes the state directory, so a recreated database never inherits an admission taken after cleanup. The owner that deletes the files revokes admissions for them, the same ordering production removal uses (close, then delete).

Production is not affected: the CLI run loop drains Gateway work admission before closing, which refuses the late sweep. The fixture instead reopens admission between cases and deletes state out of band.

<details><summary>Root-cause trace</summary>

Instrumented local run with a 1.5 s pause inserted before the fixture's delete (local only, not committed) reproduced both CI failures, with the same message and stack, on Bun and Node. The trace shows the late capture coming from `sweepOnce → createSubagentSweepReadScope → captureOpenClawStateWorkerContext` after the case's `closeGatewayTestHomeDatabases`, followed in the next case by `publishOpenClawStateDatabaseWorkerAdmission` seeing `file:<new inode>` where the stale record held `file:<old inode>`, i.e. the exact CI stack.

On CI's ext4 runners the recreated file often reuses the old inode number, which hides the mismatch and keeps this intermittent.

</details>

## Evidence

- New regression `src/gateway/test-helpers.server-state-reset.test.ts` performs the same late read after a case's cleanup and then creates the next case's state database through a worker binding.
  - Before the fix: fails 6/6 (Node 3, Bun 3) with `STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED`.
  - After the fix: passes 6/6 (Node 3, Bun 3). `pnpm test src/gateway/test-helpers.server-state-reset.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: ~8.3 s wall (tests ~0.6 s; the rest is transform/import).
- With the local-only 1.5 s pre-delete pause, after the fix: `server-plugins.activation-health.test.ts` 3/3 Bun + 3/3 Node pass; `server.hooks-admission.test.ts` 3/3 Bun + 3/3 Node pass. Without the fix the same pause failed activation-health 6/6 on Bun and 1/2 on Node, and hooks-admission 3/6 on Bun and 2/2 on Node.
- Unmodified CI-shard neighbours pass on Node and Bun (`server-plugins.*` ×8, `server.hooks*` ×2, `test-helpers.server-{env,rpc,storage,state-reset}`: 14 files, 172 tests each runtime); re-run after rebasing on current `main` for activation-health, hooks-admission, storage and the new regression on both runtimes.
- `pnpm check:changed`: line-cap ratchet, typecheck (core + core tests) and lint lanes pass for the changed files. Two lanes are red independently of this diff on current `main`: the max-lines suppression ratchet (untouched `ui/src/pages/**` files) and the advisory core test-shard root budget (`plugins-platform` is also at 726; this PR adds one root to `gateway-root`).
- `$autoreview` (Codex, local, P2): scoped-clean.
- Independent of the PR where it surfaced: that PR only touches channel/plugin-runtime delivery files; the same failure hit scheduled `main` CI in `server.hooks-admission.test.ts`.

title: fix(update): finalization ignores TMPDIR for disposable copies
body:
Related: #177707

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update finalization writes disposable plugin source copies and SQLite inspection snapshots onto the home volume even when its helper has an absolute TMPDIR on another filesystem.

## User Impact

User impact: finalization can use the selected temporary volume for those copies instead of consuming additional home-volume capacity. Normal Gateway cache placement is unchanged. Installed plugin projects, retained native admissions, and recovery/migration backups retain their existing durable placement and still require space on their owning filesystems. There is no schema or configuration migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the update marker and private TMPDIR already supplied by shipped update drivers, including the reporter's beta driver. Reuse the existing temporary capture allocator and private SQLite staging owner; distinguish disposable source copies from native admissions that can be published to the installed index. Snapshot failures now name the applicable environment selector.

This is deliberately a focused repair, not a claim that every symptom in #177707 is resolved. Current main already includes the worker-loss recovery fix in [#176902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176902) (`16f2c2e9fb16`), which the reported `2b85c4c25ea9` beta does not contain. That matching mechanism does not conclusively explain the reporter's authenticated-WebSocket failure.

## Evidence

- Both new regressions failed at their destination assertions against the original implementations, after successfully producing readable copies. With the repair, they verify real plugin capture bytes, retained-native placement, an actual read-only SQLite worker snapshot, byte-neutral source preservation, and snapshot cleanup.
- **144 tests passed across all seven selected files**, with a clean runner exit and completed source-binding verification: migrated update parent/worker suites, capture lifecycle/recovery suites, snapshot/private-directory suites, and all eight agent close-wedge cases. The latter includes actual SQLITE_FULL from real shared-state and agent workers followed by successful writes after clearing the fault, without restarting the host.
- The repository test runner completed its runtime build, CLI bootstrap import guard, 99 external plugin builds, and built control-plane/Doctor closure checks.
- Core typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --noEmit -p tsconfig.core.json`), targeted lint and format checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex P0–P2 review found no actionable defects in the supplied change. Its unchanged lifecycle/environment context was limited; it did not attest a complete upgrade or WebSocket-recovery run.
- Simplification pass retained the existing custody and cleanup owners, with no new cache, state store, retry, or recovery mechanism. Delta: production +25/-3, tests +56/-0, docs +8/-0. The production growth separates transient update placement from retained-native placement.

**Remaining acceptance gap (draft):** a full published-driver-to-candidate upgrade with separate capped home/TMPDIR filesystems, first finalizer failure capture, and authenticated Gateway reconnection after freeing space has not run. This host refuses isolated user/mount namespace creation; no live host filesystem was filled and no operator Gateway was touched. An isolated VM with mounting capability is needed before claiming the complete incident is resolved.

Requested by Dallin; originally reported by @DonnieFi.

title: fix: saved Gateway opens can fail when the Gateways menu closes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Addresses a source-identified race where closing the Gateways menu can disconnect a saved Gateway while its first window is still opening.

## User Impact and Solution

The existing connection fleet owns consumer lifetime. Dashboard configuration acquires demand before native preflight and transfers it to the window; native chat retains demand while opening and in its window record. Hidden windows remain consumers. Close/replacement releases demand. Menu-private opening-task bookkeeping is removed. Explicit credential retirement, profile removal, and fleet shutdown remain unconditional; authentication, TLS, origin, and account-storage policy are unchanged.

## Readiness — November 7

**Product/design recommendation: retain this focused fleet-demand repair.** Fresh independent source review found no proven P0–P2 defect, and no unresolved product-direction decision was identified within this scope.

**Engineering validation, CI, and source publication are not complete.** The existing PR remains open at `fbb30e598cdad1e284058798bc6c6b5eaf80f2e5`. A successor task recovered candidate `e5c39a3b798cb557a779672909006592e6def968`, preserving the PR head and its previously integrated main parent `8e8d5b052457c221a973a2fe66b25f9f08e7302b`. The candidate includes the prior one-line test-formatting correction, not a new behavioral repair. It is preserved locally and has not been pushed to this PR. No additional main integration was performed merely because main advanced.

## Evidence

- **Fresh candidate source review:** local OpenClaw Auto Review, Codex engine, completed the range `8e8d5b052457c221a973a2fe66b25f9f08e7302b..e5c39a3b798cb557a779672909006592e6def968`, through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. Full affected owners and selected sibling lifetime tests were supplied as committed source context. - **Candidate integrity:** contributor ancestry is preserved; `git diff --check` passes. The review checkout and designated task branch have identical candidate commit and tree. Simplification retains one fleet owner and removes menu-private pending-open tracking; production delta remains +86/-54 lines, with 165 regression-test lines.
- **Reusable native evidence on the existing remote head:** the [disposable macOS job](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39361552642/job/118428661548) succeeded. Its [immutable workflow](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/commit/0df832829e6ed9569fe3d9fdbe0d0c95df418135) independently checks out and asserts upstream `fbb30e598cdad1e284058798bc6c6b5eaf80f2e5`, without persisted checkout credentials. The retained job log confirms that test result and the lifecycle suite. This evidence does not cover the merged local candidate or establish a pristine-base failure.
- Historical pinned SwiftFormat passed. SwiftLint's wrapper exited zero with one DashboardManager file-length advisory; this was not zero-violation lint. Syntax parsing is not behavior proof.
- **Outstanding exact-remote-head CI findings:** the [macOS producer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39366649706/job/118445104579) reported `stricter(_:_:)`; the [shared intersection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39366649706/job/118449364907) reported `replaceSocketCredentials(_:expectedToken:)` and `bindNull(at:)`. The local candidate no longer declares `stricter` or `bindNull`, but retains the credential-store API. Neither failed gate is claimed green without a new scan.

Harness primitive calls do not establish every UI flow.

Explicit existing-PR metadata editing works, but publication of the recovered source to this existing PR remains blocked. No replacement PR, alternate credential publication path, merge, or closure was attempted.

These are engineering-validation and mechanical publication gaps, not an unresolved product-design decision. Same-account renewal notification ordering and expiry presentation remain separate incident hypotheses, not silently included in this patch's claimed fix.

title: feat: enable native plugin UI without a Labs opt-in
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installed native plugin interfaces still require a separate Labs opt-in even though the same infrastructure already serves bundled plugins.

## User Impact

Enabled user-installed plugins can show native UI by default, without a Labs detour. Existing explicit `gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlugins: false` values remain off; there is no new configuration key or migration.

**Upgrade behavior:** when the key is omitted, already-enabled plugins may begin loading their native browser UI after upgrading. Native UI is trusted, unsandboxed code running with each signed-in viewer's Gateway permissions. Existing authentication, scope, provenance, asset grants, and lifecycle checks remain unchanged.

Install surfaces explain that plugins may include browser code; installed details and existing enable reviews identify native UI from the inspected manifest. No extra modal, checkbox, or permission gate is added. All plugin APIs retain their existing experimental API-stability policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move browser-execution disclosure to ordinary plugin installation and enablement instead of hiding the whole capability behind Labs. Keep the existing advanced opt-out for compatibility, and share the effective default between admission and browser refresh notifications. Update authoring guidance, agent instructions, and recovery hints so they no longer direct users to the removed switch.

## Evidence

### Test-line offset instead of a ceiling increase (03:08 UTC)

Published head `7139747c6eaee5b00d01dd14196a0246f88bb900` (tree `6cc6c044d709ff11fb32d0f348898ce9f923db48`) merges main `b61ab6deb40cc640aec077b6e6a7b93a44b5422c`. Instead of raising the test-line ceiling, this PR now deletes or consolidates 296 lines of low-value tests elsewhere, so its net test-line delta is **−6**. `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is identical to main; the ceiling changes described in earlier sections are superseded.

| File | Net lines removed | Change | Remaining coverage |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `src/plugins/channel-catalog-registry.test.ts` | 29 | Two mocked ledger-forwarding checks | Real-ledger workspace and load-path tests |
| `src/cli/plugins-uninstall-selection.test.ts` / `plugins-cli.uninstall.test.ts` | 15 | Duplicate ambiguity replay; CLI assertion now checks the full message | CLI test proves rejection before any mutation |
| `src/config/commands.test.ts` | 84 | Repeated resolver scaffolding tabled | All precedence and enabled/disabled cases retained |
| `src/commands/onboard-custom-config.test.ts` | 45 | Alias, auth and context scenarios tabled | Same named cases, inputs and assertions |
| `test/scripts/bun-standalone-worker-source-types.test.ts` | 72 | Shared compiler and temp-root fixtures | All five type cases with real diagnostics |
| `test/scripts/test-live-cli-backend-docker.test.ts` | 18 | Shared Docker/fake-command fixture | Both validation and credential cases |
| `ui/src/components/icons.test.tsx` → `solid/icon.test.tsx` | 33 | Duplicate cases after icons moved to the Solid renderer | Solid icon tests, plus carried-over lightbulb and disposal checks |

Nothing covering security, authorization, credentials, data integrity, Doctor/migration, update/rollback or the native UI opt-out was removed, and no baseline, snapshot or mock-export file changed. All touched tests pass (148 core/tooling, 112 UI, including the native UI harness and Gateway asset tests), along with UI types, generated config, plugin version sync and channel catalog checks. The test-line ratchet passes against main (6294381 of 6295000). The offset was reviewed independently before integration.

### Refresh for landing (23:16 UTC)

Published head `cdfecc61468b3827c4c6ca34da103d3250eccc1f` (tree `1b6bf3cbd8ec874e36d1a235c79b73980f4026a2`) merges main `eec15d7c6db55c618405c6d42205f4d6dfa57352` after GitHub reported a conflict; the only conflict, `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, was regenerated. This also picks up main's fix for the inherited curly-lint errors.

**Test-line ceiling:** main alone is 822 lines over its own ceiling, so the PR's existing +290 authored test lines no longer fit. Following Josh's earlier approval of a minimal adjustment, the ceiling moves `6288829` → `6289941`, the exact combined total with zero slack. No tests were added for the refresh.

**Validation:** frozen install, generated config, plugin version sync, channel catalog, test ratchet and diff checks passed, plus production UI types and 143 focused tests (109 UI, 34 Gateway/upgrade-harness). Native UI source, tests and harness are unchanged.

### Version bump removed (21:53 UTC)

Published head `9af9038160d6233d3adb083d07208592ff3165c1` (tree `f09279358867c39ad253bef2788b096062daab4b`) drops the development-only `2026.10.10-beta.5` source version. The 183 files it regenerated (180 version-aligned plugin/package manifests, macOS metadata, a Bonjour manifest reformat and the Matrix changelog) now match base `577ab8628f35f58903e589efc5ab3ee4a7835b0f` exactly, so this PR no longer changes any `package.json`, peer/plugin-API minimums or the lockfile. The feature itself never needed the bump: it only made the candidate newer than published stable `2026.10.8` so the packaged-upgrade test exercised a real forward upgrade.

**Validation:** frozen install, plugin version sync check, channel catalog check, generated config check, test-line ratchet (6286023 of 6287068) and diff checks passed; 129 focused tests passed (95 UI, 34 Gateway/upgrade-harness). Native UI source, tests and harness are unchanged from the previous head.

**Proof scope:** the direct-AWS `2026.10.8` → candidate upgrade below passed on head `e3ff14114dc2`, which carried the bump. Its native-UI inputs are unchanged here, but it is not a run of this head. Repeating it needs main's next canonical version bump or a separately approved test-only version override. **Current-head CI ([run 40590454937](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40590454937)):** 61 jobs passed; the gate is red on three jobs, none caused by this PR:

- [check-lint-core-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40590454937/job/122496873861): five `eslint(curly)` errors in `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-body.browser.test.tsx` and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx`. Both files are byte-identical to this PR's merge base and reproduce locally; main has since fixed them in `8b2b0997` ("brace single-line branches flagged by curly lint"). The classifier labels this "new" only because main's job now passes.
- [checks-ui (3/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40590454937/job/122496002660): one of 8,067 tests failed, the Activity page "retires the mounted session's activity after an account change". The Activity page and gateway store are unchanged by this PR, and the file passes on a focused pinned-Bun replay; the classifier marks the job pre-existing. That passing replay is not a fix.
- android-test-third-party was cancelled by the runner, with sticky-disk unmount failures; no Android code is touched.

The only lint item in a PR file is a non-failing warning: `catalog-results.tsx` is 701 lines against a 700-line soft limit. No CI rerun was requested. Refreshing onto current main would pick up the lint fix. No merge, release or deployment was performed.

### October 27 conflict refresh (21:15 UTC)

Published head `ab0cfa43e522566027a00da018c2512669c7cf86` has complete tree `c30f7b1320e311feaaf00db47ceeadc42b5b35b9`, identical to validated merge `3f287c70f36066ccc6f774941c6809606fb61110`, incorporating pinned main `577ab8628f35f58903e589efc5ab3ee4a7835b0f`. This refresh was triggered by a confirmed GitHub merge conflict, not merely advancing main or chasing green. GitHub reports the published refresh mergeable.

**Budget resolution:** the sole conflict was the global test-line ceiling. The upstream ceiling `6287068` now accommodates the combined tree (`6286023` lines, `1045` slack), so this PR no longer changes that ceiling relative to its base. The hands-on deslop remains: 56 net test lines and seven redundant cases removed; authored test/support growth remains +290. The earlier approved +334 ceiling adjustment below is historical and has been superseded by retaining upstream unchanged.

**Current refresh validation:** 145 unique focused tests passed (109 UI and 36 Gateway/survivor/prompt-cache cases), including the affected plugin route normalization and native policy/asset consumers. Production UI types, generated config check, frozen installation, test ratchet and diff checks passed. The upstream prompt-cache expectation repair [#186233](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186233) is included and its two-case test now passes. No new authored product behavior was introduced by conflict resolution; the completed independent review is reused for the mechanical refresh.

**Proof scope:** the full direct-AWS packaged `2026.10.8` → `2026.10.10-beta.5` qualification below passed on exact prior head `e3ff14114dc2f9f93b9771ce723ea1f89a02567c`. Native UI policy, asset serving, disclosures and upgrade-harness owners are unchanged by this refresh; that proof remains reusable evidence for those unchanged inputs, not a claim of a new full-package run on `ab0cfa43e522`. New-head CI remains pending. The prior Ollama `ECONNRESET` investigation remains recorded; the passing focused replay is not a repair. No merge, release, deployment, permission change or new cloud allocation was performed.

<details>
<summary>Prior-head full AWS qualification, deslop and CI findings</summary>

### October 27 evening refresh

Published head: `e3ff14114dc2f9f93b9771ce723ea1f89a02567c`; complete tree: `4cdbd34f058e5571af699a875030be733c5fcddc`, identical to independently reviewed merge `49f4a32be588a3fc27ef30bfec20eaa1ab768f87`. Incorporates pinned main `32075f317aff05b0c20f66d69decb89d6458d177`; the sole config-metadata conflict was regenerated. GitHub reports this head mergeable.

- Hands-on test simplification removed 56 net test lines and seven cases, including duplicated private assertion-helper coverage and two test-only exports. Mounted reactive precedence, semantic disclosure/ordering, real Gateway authorization, and package/diagnostic rejection/privacy controls remain. A deliberate production-precedence mutation failed the consolidated test; the source was restored and all 11 settings tests passed.
- 230 focused tests passed: 120 UI and 110 unique core/survivor tests. Production UI/tooling types, targeted lint/format, config/i18n/catalog verification and frozen installation passed. Existing fixture lint warnings remain warnings, not zero-warning proof. Independent full-delta static AutoReview reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Following Josh’s approval, canonical version owners prepared development-only `2026.10.10-beta.5`, newer than pinned stable `2026.10.8`. No release, tag, npm publication or deployment was performed.
- Remaining authored test growth is +290 lines. The refreshed base is already 44 lines above the prior ceiling; the approved minimum ceiling adjustment is therefore +334 (`6286403` → `6286737`), exactly the observed total with zero slack.
**Current-stable packaged upgrade: PASSED.** [Direct-AWS run run_ddeca56f67e6fea24eb02535636af3c5](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ddeca56f67e6fea24eb02535636af3c5) completed on exact published head `e3ff14114dc2f9f93b9771ce723ea1f89a02567c` / complete tree `4cdbd34f058e5571af699a875030be733c5fcddc`. Seven jobs and the aggregate gate remain queued/pending at the last exact-job read. No CI rerun or source push was performed merely to obtain green, and no merge, release or deployment was performed.

</details>

<details>

title: fix(ui): keep default sidebar session rows on one line when previews are off
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the default sidebar, a running session could grow a second line (an agent attention note such as "Unable to read the job snapshot", or a stuck/waiting observer headline) even with session previews turned off.

## User Impact

User impact: default sidebar session rows stay on one line unless the operator turns on session previews. The agent-first roster view keeps its status lines, and attention notes remain available from the row's attention icon tooltip.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSidebarSessionRowSubtitle` already owns the mode-dependent subtitle policy (it suppresses tool activity in roster mode). It now returns no subtitle for the default chip view when previews are off, so the preview-independent lines only survive in the roster view. Preview-on behavior and roster behavior are unchanged; sidebar snapshot capture uses the same resolver, so shared snapshots match.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dd3d6df2-0626-4a96-a067-0241cff18ab5)

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI (bundled build, Playwright Chromium, dark theme, synthetic session data), default sidebar with a running session carrying an agent attention note and previews off:

**Before** — the note renders as a second line under the row:

![before-default-sidebar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f0c9786-616d-4234-8e28-ce96efa38900)

**After** — one line; the note stays on the attention icon tooltip:

![after-default-sidebar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56d2db3b-659b-4e82-9861-e4072d54534d)

The same capture reported `.sidebar-recent-session__subtitle` text `["Unable to read the job snapshot"]` before and `[]` after. The roster view rendered identically before and after (it parks non-pinned session rows behind agent summaries).

Focused checks:

- New `resolveSidebarSessionRowSubtitle` regression in `ui/src/components/session-row-subtitle.test.ts` fails on `main` (default view returned the attention note and stuck headline) and passes with the fix; it also pins roster and preview-on behavior. `pnpm test ui/src/components/session-row-subtitle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 6 passed, ~1.5 s wall.
- Sidebar suites (`app-sidebar.sessions`, `.interactions`, `.people`, `.projection-memo`, `-session-projection`, `-session-row-render`, `-rail`): 353 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint on touched files: clean.
- Autoreview (branch vs `origin/main`, up to P2): no actionable findings.

title: chore(xai): repair monotonic polling regression test after #174227
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts` fails (and no longer typechecks) on `main` after #174227 landed.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Restores a green xAI OAuth test suite on `main`; the #174227 production fix is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#174227's new regression test was written against the older `jsonResponse(body, { status })` helper. Current `main`'s `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env` `jsonResponse` takes a numeric status, so the `authorization_pending` response became a 200, the login ended after one poll, and `expect(pollTimes.length).toBeGreaterThan(1)` failed. This passes `400` directly. The PR's own CI was green on its older base; the helper signature drift only showed up after the squash merge.

## Evidence

title: fix: make Daybreak independent of retiring model aliases
body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Daybreak workflows rely on Blue/Red aliases retiring October 28, 2026, and must retain automatic recovery through authorized Access configuration without changing the selected model or processing speed.

## User Impact

The chat menu uses segmented Access choices matching Speed and shows **Access above Effort above Speed**, but only when the active account/model/runtime explicitly advertises a Daybreak program. Unavailable options are absent; unknown or empty capabilities hide Access entirely. There are no requested/reported status or explanatory paragraphs below Access. **Use model default** clears the session override; Standard is an explicit selection. If account capabilities no longer expose Access, **Clear saved Access** remains available in the model menu. Clearing is explicit; unavailable program choices and explanatory Access paragraphs remain absent.

The advisory Doctor check reports configured retiring aliases without rewriting models or account pins. **Automatic cyber recovery retries the same model once with authorized Blue Access**, without changing the saved session selection. Exact model pins and an empty model-fallback list do not disable this configuration retry. Ordinary configured cross-model fallbacks remain separate. Review saved session overrides and scheduled jobs separately before retirement.

## Root Cause

Only the aliases retire. A replay-safe, structured cyber refusal in Standard/default mode can retry the same provider/model/runtime/account with Blue Access. Existing Blue/Red requests are not retried or downgraded, and `cyberFailover.mode=off` remains authoritative. Current account/credential/route grants are required before submission; there is no entitlement inferred from a model name, auth type, or another account. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove retired `cyberFailover.model` fields through the existing core/plugin migration owners; explicit mode/cooloff settings and ordinary primary/fallback model configuration are preserved. Program selection (`standard`, `daybreak_blue`, `daybreak_red`) remains independent of Fast/Ultrafast. Empty model configuration (`accessPrograms: {}`) leaves selection unspecified; null is invalid.

Authenticated ChatGPT model discovery supplies caller-specific program metadata. The Gateway projects it as optional `availableAccessPrograms.cyber` on each account/model/runtime choice, preserving unknown versus explicitly empty results. The existing account/catalog lifecycle owns invalidation; no new cache or state store is introduced. Saved session overrides are checked again at execution, and native Codex verifies the same client/account model catalog before its turn starts.

This OpenClaw integration supports the native Codex turn-scoped parameter with ChatGPT authentication and rejects explicit programs with native API-key authentication before submission. This is the integration’s current scope, not an upstream limitation: the earlier pinned Codex 0.162.1 rejected API-key programs when its separate feature is disabled and forwarded them when enabled. The integrated upstream runtime is now 0.164.0; its Access enum and metadata shape are unchanged. **Platform API-key discovery now reads explicit caller-specific program metadata from the official Codex models endpoint, using the same selected key.** Public `/v1/models` remains the model-inventory authority; metadata cannot add an unlisted model. No model-name, plan, or approval-label inference and no billable Responses probe is used. Custom routes and header overrides cannot inherit official grants. The existing selected-account refresh now reaches the HTTP cache and publishes changed outcomes to open UI consumers. Native Codex API-key execution remains unsupported by this integration; official Platform and ChatGPT Responses endpoints remain separate. The 60-second HTTP-cache lifetime is not a polling timer or instantaneous revocation guarantee. Selected profile/key and route isolate observations; project/organization request-header overrides are ineligible for default-route grants. Missing, empty or failed metadata hides Access while ordinary inventory remains usable.

References: [Daybreak](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/daybreak), [Fast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode), [Ultrafast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode).

## Verification

### Current main integration (5179f4b15d3)

Merged captured main **77a7ce297e981298390150cdb6c57988bf769925** into previously reviewed **8d08a5c76f8105926b97017471c0d887c62538ba**, preserving contributor ancestry. The three conflicts were mechanical: regenerate the two config baseline outputs, and retain main's complete agents-view test file, which independently contains the same lazy-import readiness fix. No new product behavior was introduced by this integration.

- Configuration baseline generation/check: passed; counts **2559 core / 3977 channel / 4866 plugin**.
- Agents-view tests: **25/25 passed**. Configuration baseline tests: **11/11 passed**. Focused formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- The previous head's [CI run 40222123890](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40222123890) failed the unpublished-schema PostgreSQL admission assertion. Matching main CI passed. title: fix(update): profile-backed updates refuse their own maintenance lock
body:
Related: https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2112230438794367192
Additional report context: https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2112277658918863267

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat-initiated updates can fail with an offline-maintenance error when the update requester's permissions are backed by a linked profile.

## User Impact

Profile-backed updates can continue through post-core plugin preparation instead of refusing their own permission read. Live foreign maintenance still blocks access, requester revocation still stops further effects, and rollback eligibility is unchanged. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resumed updater acquires temporary Doctor database ownership, then rechecks requester authority outside that maintenance scope before releasing it. A profile-backed authority check reads shared state and is refused by the updater's own ownership guard.

Release and drain that temporary database ownership first, then immediately recheck authority before runtime or plugin work. Stopped-service custody remains held; the next Doctor acquires its own database ownership.

The reporter described macOS 27, an npm stable install, and chat-agent `update.run` failures updating to 2026.10.4/.5. The defective ordering is present in both release sources. This PR fixes the reproduced profile-backed path; the original report does not yet establish its requester-authority subtype or full failure trace.

## Evidence

- The new resumed-policy regression fails with the original production ordering and passes with this fix. It uses real native executor, maintenance, and profile-policy owners, with package/subprocess effects mocked.
- Covers configured-owner success, profile-backed success, and revocation immediately after database ownership release; revocation prevents plugin work and publishes failure.
- 24 tests passed across the complete updater Doctor-authority caller suite and Doctor requester-authority sibling suite. Command wall time: 75.87 s, including compiler preparation; changed caller file: 27.83 s wall time. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.
- 11 additional native maintenance-contention and launcher-lifetime tests passed; command wall time: 40.18 s.
- Core and scoped CLI-update test-graph types, targeted lint/format, docs MDX, whitespace, and line-cap checks passed.
