title: fix(ui): Side chat composer lacks the main composer's controls, including model and speed
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Side chat composer is a bare textbox plus Send with three canned starter chips, so people lose the attach (+), dictation, emoji-shortcode, model, and speed controls they use in the main chat composer, and cannot choose which model answers Side chat questions.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/72787ebe-b9a2-42a7-9262-2bd500f48504)

## User Impact

User impact: the Side chat composer now has the main composer's + menu (take photo / attach photo), a microphone for dictation with the same device picker, `:shortcode:` emoji suggestions, and the model and effort (reasoning + Speed) pickers. The pickers choose Side chat's own model per question: **Default** is the agent's utility model with its fallbacks, as today; a chosen model must pass the agent's model allowlist and the operator's role model policy, answers without utility fallbacks, and never patches the main session. Choices follow the agent's sessions for the life of the page. The hardcoded "What changed? / Why did it stop? / What's left?" starter chips are gone. Slash commands, permissions, and Talk stay in the main composer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Side chat now assembles the same shared composer pieces as New Session instead of a one-off form: the shared plus menu (limited to images, which is what Side chat accepts), the shared emoji menu owner, the direct-dictation control (moved from New Session to `pages/chat` as `DirectDictationControl` so both dictation-only surfaces share one owner), and `ChatModelControls` fed from the pane's existing model catalog. Enter/submit while dictating finishes the dictation first so the spoken text is what gets asked.

Protocol (additive, optional fields): `sessions.companion.ask` accepts `model`, `thinkingLevel`, and `fastMode`; `sessions.companion.state` returns `defaultModel` (the resolved utility route) so the picker can label Default. The Gateway validates the model with the same allowlist resolver chat model selection uses, rejects account-pinned refs, and refuses (rather than silently swaps) a model the operator's role cannot use. Runtime choices are hidden because Side chat always answers on the OpenClaw runtime.

## Evidence

Before (Side chat on the right: canned starters, no model or speed control)

![Before: Side chat with starter chips and no model or speed picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c03a4e70-b066-43f5-ae3c-80335f77d1cb)

After (starters gone; Side chat shows +, model, Speed, microphone, and Send like the main composer)

![After: Side chat composer shows plus, model, Speed, microphone, and Send](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9df74007-16f1-46da-a42e-c2c8f7845e08)

<details><summary>Side chat model picker, attach menu, and emoji suggestions</summary>

![After: Side chat model picker open with model search](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/daee64c5-5df3-4303-8bab-94cb0b903db7)

![After: Side chat + menu offers Take photo and Photo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e519dbad-3128-4320-9536-0d723188bfc4)

![After: typing :thumbsu in Side chat suggests :thumbsup:](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d93e64c4-6d08-4fe0-ac6e-f48166cfbae2)

</details>

Checks on this head:

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`: pass
- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-companion-ask.test.ts src/gateway/session-companion.test.ts src/gateway/session-companion-rpc.test.ts src/gateway/session-companion-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/session-companion-ask.persistence.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src`: pass. New: a chosen model, reasoning level, and speed reach the run without utility fallbacks; a model outside the allowlist is rejected before any run; state reports the default model.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-session-rail.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/composer-direct-dictation.test.tsx ui/src/pages/new-session/composer.test.tsx`: pass. New: model choices follow the agent (not other agents) and travel on the ask request; the rail renders Side chat's model picker and no starter chips; Enter during active dictation commits the transcript before submitting.
- Side chat browser E2E suites (`chat-session-companion-{composer,focus,clear,manual-open-focus,retry}`, `chat-side-chat-typography`, `chat-sidebar-panel-contract`): 6 of 7 files pass. `chat-sidebar-panel-contract` times out in its desktop-canvas cleanup step (line 829); it fails identically on `main` at `b8daeb2a95a8`, so it is inherited.
- oxlint on changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors (27 files); oxfmt clean; `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: pass; `pnpm protocol:gen` + native protocol generation clean; `ui/config/control-ui-boot-modules.json` regenerated
- Autoreview (P0–P2): first pass (earlier head) found Enter could submit the pre-dictation draft while recording; fixed and covered above. Latest head: scoped-clean.

Gaps: dictation and the model picker were not exercised against a live microphone or live provider; Gateway behavior is covered by the RPC-level tests above with a synthetic runner. `check:changed` previously reported max-lines suppressions in files this PR does not touch and the core test-shard root budget; both are inherited from `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Extract the existing fixture correction from the held batch-cleanup PR. The fixture waits for the polling owner's semantic log boundary, records that sleep's timer index, and settles both the operation and rejection assertion during cleanup. Fixture-aware table context supplies its abort signal. Existing public deferred/gate/test-lifetime helpers are reused; no new seam, sleep, timer policy, larger microtask quota, or weaker assertion is added.

The original cleanup PR's two production edits, head, and armed merge request remain untouched. This repair adds 21 test lines (+40/-19) because readiness, timer identity, and settlement must be explicit; it removes the arbitrary 100-microtask wait rather than masking it.

## Evidence

title: fix: native tool installs fail on transient receive errors
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: native tool installation exits on a recoverable curl receive error without using its existing download retries.

## User Impact

No user-visible product change. Native CI can recover these tool-download failures without repeating tests. Tool versions, pinned URLs and SHA-256 digests are unchanged; failed downloads and incorrect archives still fail installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing bounded curl recovery to all transfer errors for these immutable GETs, as the sibling simslim installer already does. Keep the existing three-retry limit, transfer/retry time budgets, warning annotations, and checksum-before-extraction ordering. Permanent errors can also consume the same bounded retries; there is no mirror or provider fallback.

The triggering macOS CI step reported curl exit 56 with HTTP 502. This change fixes a demonstrated receive-error recovery gap, not a uniquely established cause, asset, or provider for that event.

## Evidence

- Real curl 8.18.0 through all three installer entrypoints against one secretless loopback TLS fixture: a receive reset exits 56 after one attempt on the base; the fix recovers in 1.027–1.037 seconds with an annotated retry. Persistent resets exhaust four attempts and retain exit 56 in 7.023–7.025 seconds.
- Wrong-digest downloads after recovery use real SHA-256 and exit 1 before extraction. Positive cases use synthetic ZIPs and replace only the digest boundary after exact archive-byte comparison; extraction, installation, and shell-fixture version checks execute normally. This is Linux transport/installer contract proof, **not actual macOS native-binary execution or live CI proof**. The failed runner's curl version remains unverified.
- Regression: six cases fail on the base solely because broad curl recovery is absent. Final installer tests: 11 pass, 158 ms test time and 2.60 seconds command wall time. Bash-selection sibling run: 149 total pass, three existing platform skips. PR CI timing is not yet available.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated “Subagent completion delivery is blocked” notices when a previously blocked child result has since reached its parent.

Existing queued notices work without migration; no configuration or schema change is required. A notice already admitted before recovery may finish, and existing interrupted history entries are not deleted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Blocked warnings had a stable producer key but were retried as generic session events without reconciling the completion they described. Before admitting a retry, the completion owner now checks the durable record for the original requester and delivery generation. Confirmed delivery retires the warning through the normal queue receipt; missing records and read failures are not delivery proof.

This is the smallest owner-level repair: no new stored fields, cache, manager, or retry mechanism (+43 production lines, +75 test lines). It fixes stale warning replay, not the separate initial expiry/source-policy failure.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI locale publication can already be stale before catch-up starts when the finalizer’s initial full-history checkout takes several minutes.

After downloading artifacts outside the checkout, invoke the same pinned checkout action once more, reusing the downloaded full history, before dependency setup or artifact admission. This follows the cache-free recovery landed in #173806; it does not change cache use, credentials, permissions, retention, or publisher freshness checks.

Simplification: reuse the existing checkout owner rather than introduce Git/ref-management machinery. Production delta is 10 workflow lines plus one documentation paragraph; the test delta strengthens the existing publication scenario and adds the distinct further-movement rejection.

title: fix(gateway): preserve public reads and repair suppression ratchet
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: scheduled CI fails its production lint-suppression check after the session-row selection optimization. During validation, a public-read failure also exposed unrelated run-status publications invalidating an in-progress public transcript.

## User Impact

Public transcript and image reads remain available when only live run status changes during a read. Live social cards still invalidate when their runtime facts change. Publication revocation, transcript edits, metadata and topology invalidations, final authority checks, shared admission budgets, and cache bounds remain intact. The suppression ratchet is unchanged; no baseline exception, migration, or operator action is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collect matching rows in a dense, append-only result instead of preallocating a holey array that requires a lint suppression. Keep indexed candidate selection, prepared topology paths, physical competitors, scope filtering, and deterministic result order unchanged. This accepts amortized result-buffer growth in exchange for simpler collection without reserving slots for rejected candidates.

The public representation cache now distinguishes recorded transcript content from live card facts. Representation kind is part of both cache and in-flight identity; all existing HTML, card, and media consumers use the same cache/admission owner and retain its aggregate budgets. Pure runtime, agent-run, and subagent-run notifications invalidate cards without retiring unrelated transcript builds.

## Evidence

- **Required-gate recovery:** [Security Review 39285901330](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39285901330) initially published a CI-only `openclaw/ci-gate` failure despite successful dependency/sensitive-change decisions. Ordinary native admission correctly refused it. The documented, maintainer-selected reevaluation reran only that protected review job; attempt 2 completed successfully and republished all three review statuses as success. Product CI remained successful attempt 1 on the unchanged head. The initial misclassification cause remains unproven; no source/policy change, manual status override, test-CI rerun, or merge bypass was used.
- Corrected-head CI [39279821137, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39279821137) completed successfully for `42d4e0f883fd87837532f59ba69b31b0ce8f910c`: all 72 attempt jobs are terminal (45 successful, 27 intentionally skipped), including successful `security-fast` and the GitHub Actions `openclaw/ci-gate` check. Workflow Sanity also passed. The native completed-hosted-evidence preparation passed for this exact head; no pending-gate stamp, CI rerun, or gate waiver was used.
- At the actual tested merge, a local run through the same shard-owner script with matched runtime/profile/targets and effective serial order reproduced the canonical public-chat HTTP 503 in 55.33 seconds. Request-scoped read-only observations captured a matching-key runtime notification from real subagent terminal completion while the public read was pending; the response stack identifies the nonthrowing cache/admission unavailable branch, with a projection present. No event was injected and no retry, delay, timeout, or assertion was changed. The original CI log lacks this emitter trace, so this is a matching-signature local causal reproduction, not an assertion that the original raw log named the producer.
- Two focused regressions fail on the unchanged owner: a public HTTP read returns 503 during a runtime-only publication, and differing transcript/card work is incorrectly shared. The qualified base run recorded 2 failed / 25 passed in 63.58 seconds. With the fix, all 66 tests across eight affected suites pass in 62.49 seconds, including canonical and bearer HTTP, live cards, media, and real publication/isolation/revocation owners.
- After a fresh private-QA build (70.30 seconds), the same shard-owner script passes all eight tests on corrected production source with the recorded effective serial order (54.63 seconds), without diagnostic instrumentation or E2E test edits. It uses Node24.19 and pinned Bun1.4.4. Local runs explicitly request one outer envelope on the larger host; original CI requested the default two but automatically admitted one on its actual2CPU/8GiB runner. Thus effective order/concurrency match, not resource-admission inputs or hardware. The protected Node compile-cache seed was not reproduced.
- Fresh canonical autoreview of this follow-up against `7c3782b270729ccdf9cd21c272457d6c5b0d2ae8`: complete, scoped-clean through P2, no findings. The candidate passes `pnpm tsgo:core` (2.68 seconds), the owning gateway-root test type graph (3.14 seconds), targeted typed lint across eight files (zero warnings/errors;61.78 seconds including SDK declaration preparation), formatting (0.12 seconds), and `git diff --check`.

- Exact-head PR CI [39266199480, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39266199480) failed `checks-node-changed`: the X publication composition E2E's anonymous canonical public-chat read returned HTTP 503 instead of 200 (`src/gateway/x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts:919`). The classifier reports unknown (no matching main job), not an established inherited failure.
- The original job log is now durably captured. It confirms tested merge `7c3782b270729ccdf9cd21c272457d6c5b0d2ae8`, with base `9505708b4e4d1aa2fbecf0ffee7d67de6c38250c` and PR head `a121070bda7cfa5e5b4078d9131b94ab03912196`. Although global `NODE_VERSION` was 24.21.0, the setup action requested `24.x`, restored its 24.19.0 toolchain, and selected Node **24.19.0**. Bun was checksum-pinned `1.4.4-canary.1+7bd4fdff3`, using the private-QA profile. The actual runner admitted **one outer envelope at a time**: real-auth E2E passed and its process ended, then the separate X composition E2E process began and failed. title: fix(acpx): ACP harnesses inherit the Gateway token and provider keys
body:
Related: openclaw/acpx#889, #73910

> **Do not merge yet.** This takes effect with the acpx release containing openclaw/acpx#889 and needs that dependency bump first.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ACP harnesses (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Kilo, Qwen, pi) receive the Gateway's whole environment, including `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and provider keys, whenever a session is spawned with `/acp spawn`.

## User Impact

User impact: ACP harnesses, their MCP servers and the commands they run no longer receive the Gateway token or provider keys by inheritance. The managed OpenClaw tools bridge keeps working. At startup, the Gateway logs a names-only warning when known provider credentials are set that harnesses will stop receiving.

**Needs action for some setups:** a harness that authenticated only through a key in the Gateway environment (for example Codex with `OPENAI_API_KEY`) must sign in with its own login or be granted the key with `ACPX_AUTH_<NAME>` in the Gateway environment (Codex: `ACPX_AUTH_OPENAI_API_KEY` plus `ACPX_AUTH_API_KEY=1`). Codex runs with an isolated home, so its own login is `CODEX_HOME=<state dir>/acpx/codex-home codex login` (or `--with-api-key`), not a normal `codex login`. A wrapper-seeded Codex API-key login is removed when no key is granted, so a key that was once inherited stops working too; Codex's own logins are kept.

The default-deny itself lives in acpx (openclaw/acpx#889). This PR takes effect together with the acpx dependency bump that picks up that release. It is open for review now; the bump lands on this branch once that release exists, and it is not merged before then.

## Why This Change Was Made

acpx owns the child environment, so the fix is there. This PR covers what OpenClaw previously got by inheritance:

- **Managed MCP bridge:** it locates the Gateway's state and config through `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, which only arrived by inheritance. OpenClaw now passes those two paths (and `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` when set) explicitly in the bridge's MCP `env`. They are paths, not credentials.
- **Codex wrapper:** it seeds `codex-home/auth.json` from `CODEX_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`. With no key granted, wrapper-written API-key auth is now removed, so a key that was once inherited does not outlive the grant. The wrapper writes that auth without `auth_mode`; Codex's own `codex login` and `codex login --with-api-key` always record `auth_mode` (`codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs`, `login_with_api_key`), so native API-key and ChatGPT logins are left alone.
- **Warning and docs:** a startup warning names known provider credentials present in the Gateway environment, never their values. `docs/tools/acp-agents-setup.md#harness-credentials` now documents what harnesses receive, how they sign in, and what environment isolation does not prevent.

Operators grant a harness credential with `ACPX_AUTH_<NAME>` in the Gateway environment. That is an existing acpx input, so this PR adds no config. The grant gives every harness `<NAME>` and answers an ACP auth method whose id normalizes to `<NAME>`. Grants are runtime-wide: every harness receives every granted credential.

## Evidence

A real `/acp spawn opencode` session on a disposable Gateway, launched under `strace -f -v -e trace=execve,openat` plus clone records for lineage. It used a loopback fake provider and 10 unique per-source canaries. The agent ran `env` and walked every readable ancestor's `/proc/<pid>/environ`.

| | before (acpx 0.19.4) | after (acpx #889) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Harness-tree execs carrying canaries (opencode, bun MCP bridge, shells, agent commands) | 197 / 197 | **0 / 185** |
| Canary sources in the agent's `env` | 7 | **0** |
| Canary sources in `/proc/$PPID/environ` (the harness) | 7 | **0** |
| Canary sources in the Gateway's own `/proc/<pid>/environ`, readable by a same-uid agent | 4 | 4 (residual) |
| Provider traffic (headers and bodies, 3 requests) | none | none |

Canaries were searched in raw, base64 (all alignments), hex and URL-encoded forms across kernel exec records, SQLite/WAL, logs, transcripts, provider traffic and written files. After the fix, every remaining hit traces to the Gateway side, or to what the agent read through the residual paths below.

**Real-model Gateway e2e** (this branch at `0bf2cb5` with openclaw/acpx#889). One disposable Gateway per scenario; each harness gets a real `/acp spawn` session. The agent runs `env` in its shell and calls the managed OpenClaw tools bridge (`automations` with `action: status`). Bridge results come from acpx's session record, not the model's reply.

| Harness | granted via `ACPX_AUTH_*` | ambient only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode 1.19.3 | real reply, bridge tool ok | refused (provider auth) |
| Kilo 7.8.12 | real reply, bridge tool ok | refused (provider auth) |
| Codex ACP 2.1.1 (OpenClaw wrapper) | real reply, bridge tool ok | spawn refused: `CODEX_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY is not set` |
| Claude Agent ACP 0.88.0 (OpenClaw wrapper) | real reply, bridge tool ok | refused: `Authentication required` |
| Harness-tree processes with a Gateway canary | 0 / 15 | 0 / 14 |
| Startup warning names | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |

- **Agent shell env, granted run:** only the granted credential names. The ambient `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` canary and the Gateway token are absent.
- **Grant, withdrawal, next managed launch (Codex):** the Gateway restarted on the granted run's state (wrapper-seeded `codex-home/auth.json`, 0600) with the grant removed and the key still ambient. On the first spawn the wrapper deleted the seeded `auth.json`, and Codex refused the session: `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED: CODEX_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY is not set`. The withdrawn key was not reused.
- **Native Codex login, no grant:** real `codex login --with-api-key` into the isolated home (`auth.json` fields `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `auth_mode=apikey`), key only ambient, no `ACPX_AUTH_*` Codex grant. The login survived the launch (`auth_mode=apikey` after), Codex answered with a real reply and called the bridge (`mcp.openclaw-tools.automations` ok). 0 of 5 harness processes carried a Gateway canary. Before this revision's fix, the wrapper deleted this login (red unit test below).
- **Control for the bridge change:** the same granted OpenCode run, but with the base `extensions/acpx/src/config.ts` (no state/config locators). The bridge call failed with `gateway cron.status requires credentials before opening a websocket`, because the bridge read the default state dir. With this PR it succeeds.

**Measured residual risks.** Environment isolation is not a sandbox.

- A same-uid agent can read the Gateway's `/proc/<pid>/environ` (Yama `ptrace_scope=1` does not block it).
- From that, the agent can read `state/.env` and `openclaw.json`. The agent's `cat` opened both in both runs.
- The managed tools MCP bridge runs in the harness tree and loads config, `.env` and agent SQLite in-process. Its environ is clean.
- Whatever the agent reads lands in the harness's own transcript store, for example the OpenCode WAL.

Closing these needs OS-level isolation: a separate user, a container, or a sandbox.

**Real vendor auth** (harness × source, see openclaw/acpx#889). With the fix, an inherited key is denied and a granted one authenticates, for OpenCode, Kilo, Qwen, Codex and Claude. pi passes the credential gate but stalls in `session/new` on base too.

**Tests:**
- `config.test.ts`: the bridge gets its state and config locators.
- `codex-auth-bridge.test.ts`: seeded API-key auth is removed without a grant; ChatGPT auth and a native `codex login --with-api-key` login are kept (the native-login case fails on `0bf2cb5`, passes now).
- `service.test.ts`: service startup logs the warning naming `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and no logged warning contains its value.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes apart from pre-existing upstream findings: Knip dead exports in untouched files (`src/sessions/session-controller.contracts.ts`, `extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-extension.test-support.ts`).

**Not changed, on purpose:** the acpx dependency bump. It needs the acpx release with openclaw/acpx#889, which does not exist yet; it lands on this branch before merge. Existing-data compatibility for acpx session state is covered by the 0.19.6 → #889 upgrade proof in openclaw/acpx#889; for Codex home state, by the withdrawal and native-login runs above.

Reproducible scripts (strace Gateway proof, real-model Gateway e2e, upgrade proof, minimal env, vendor matrix): https://gist.github.com/roboclaw-bot/8d810cb1341ae895756f7c0d8c2be906

<details><summary>Follow-ups outside this scope (not changed here)</summary>

- Exec tool and host shell environment (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-spawn.ts`, `src/process/exec-spawn.ts` defaults to `process.env`)
- CLI harness runner (`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.ts`) and the child supervisor
- Native Codex app-server transport (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/*`), which has its own auth contract
- Non-ACP MCP/LSP transports and the reverse-direction `openclaw acp` client
- acpx flow shell actions (user-authored), which still inherit by design

</details>

title: fix(subagents): delivered children stay pending while siblings run
body:
Closes #166267

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-delivered child remains listed as pending while an unrelated sibling keeps running.

## User Impact

Busy requesters retire redundant single-child wakes without waiting for every worker to stop. Actual grouped and yielded continuations, unresolved deliveries, and their existing retry and source-custody protections remain owned. No configuration, schema, retention-policy, or operator data edits are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing no-continuation decision ran after descendant waiting. Move that decision before the wait and use the existing generation-aware lifecycle completion operation. This fixes the owner rather than hiding results in the renderer or expiring legitimate continuations. Recovery evaluates restored markers through the same owner.

Update affected integration fixtures to represent real completion debt and grouped work: required pending delivery for the liveness check; receipt holds installed only for the yielded cohort they exercise; released source bindings for consumed singletons; and two pending wave members before testing shared-slot rearm. The existing delivery, fault-injection, publication, and rearm assertions remain intact. Separately delivered non-yield singletons no longer produce a redundant aggregate turn.

The production change remains +5/-4 lines with no new state, timers, or policy helpers. The test setup reuses its existing visible-child fixture.

Thanks to @assimetria-ai for the report and @Oldrich333 for clarifying why delivered grouped results can still owe a continuation.

Contributors: @Marvinthebored and @shakkernerd.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/79630ff9-afb5-4b4a-b825-de346e00b533)

## Evidence

- The new delivered-singleton regression failed on the original production source while its preservation controls passed. On the integrated candidate, 87 focused tests across six files passed, including private/yielded continuations, failed/suspended deliveries, liveness, runtime context, and lifecycle retries (121.27 seconds including shared preparation).
- All 33 requester-wake E2E cases passed after repairing the affected fixtures (59.06 seconds Vitest, 65.98 seconds wrapper). This suite exercises real SQLite publication, queued receipt drift, failed writes, source release, restart/activation, and shared-scheduler rearm; those boundaries require more than a helper-only test. The final fixture simplification also passed a targeted rearm rerun (35.78 seconds Vitest, 42.71 seconds wrapper). Exact-head [CI run 39335212550](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39335212550) passed, including all seven changed-node lanes and the required CI gate; per-file CI timing has not been aggregated here.
- Targeted repository lint, core typecheck, formatting, prepared-base mock-export ratchet, and git diff whitespace checks passed. Independent Auto Review (GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) identified the waiting-wave fixture issue; it was repaired and the follow-up assessment found no actionable findings. Reviews were static, not test execution.
- Prior production-flow proof used an isolated real Gateway and scripted OpenAI-compatible model: actual parent tools spawned a long-running child and a short private-completion child; after delivery, SQLite retained the result without its wake, the long sibling still ran, and the next parent model request omitted the pending short-result row. This ran on the original production repair before the upstream integration, not the later integrated head. No live external provider or cold-process Gateway restart is claimed.

### CI repair

The initial ready-head run [39182121588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39182121588) failed on stale liveness/receipt fixture assumptions and an unrelated root-help mock-export ratchet. Main was integrated at afa7fccb9a2f4483d404a6b64814afe5d001ca21 specifically to consume the upstream mock-export repair. The liveness, receipt, and rearm failures were reproduced and fixed without longer test timeouts, skipped cases, weakened fault assertions, or baseline exceptions. A workspace synchronization interruption preserved the pending repairs and was resolved before work resumed. The earlier cold product-probe timeout and interrupted runtime-build attempts are setup gaps, not passing tests. The repaired head f891f6f10762c924a1f8f343a420e8834ff9509b passed fresh required CI and applicable security checks. Exact-head ClawSweeper re-review reports no actionable findings and no before-merge items. The managed squash action has not merged the PR: GitHub continues to report mergeability as unknown, so the guarded action refused before dispatch. No waiver or merge is claimed here.

title: fix: resume interrupted peer work after gateway restarts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: admitted peer follow-ups and returned results can remain interrupted after a Gateway restart, even though their original session and unfinished work still exist.

## User Impact

Peer work resumes automatically in the original session after restart without requiring a manual Resume action or repeating a completed command. Requested replies still arrive when reverse-direction sends are disabled. Stop, cancellation, access revocation, and replaced-session boundaries remain enforced. No configuration or database-schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the admitted operator recovery source, route automatic peer results through the existing durable communication owner, and retain their optional-reply context. Requested replies use authority captured from the accepted request rather than a new reverse-direction send permission. Exact endpoint and current cancellation/access checks still apply.

Make concurrent history reconciliation return consistent interrupted state, and revisit startup orphans after a temporary controller owner releases them. Recovery keeps the original startup cutoff and live ownership checks. Explicitly stopped claims and operations retain cleanup custody but cannot be captured or revalidated as recoverable work.

This does not fabricate receipts for historical deliveries already missing evidence or modify the running Team Gateway.

body:
Related: #176366

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord-originated tasks can credit unrelated people and omit the requester when several conversations share the main routing session.

## User Impact

A verified channel-to-profile link is still required. Unlinked requests get no inferred main-session credit. Existing commits and child snapshots are not rewritten. Direct publication from canonical main, without a task contributor snapshot, adds no automatic human credit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The producer treated a routing-session roster as task contribution. The existing contributor-inheritance owner now selects only the host-verified requester for canonical main. That attribution-only fact travels through native, visible, ACP, and CLI delegation independently of owner/admin authority. Requester trailers stay in per-turn context; changing requesters does not rebuild stable instructions. A different main requester uses the existing follow-up path rather than the original task's tool closures.

Reported and investigated with @obviyus. The incident's parent explicitly supplied wrong trailers to its worker; the worker complied. The original head already lacked the reporter's credit. Historical system/developer prompt bytes were unavailable.

The provider derives trailers from actual product prompts, not expected identities.

The large one-off E2E harness was then removed from the shipped diff; replayable task evidence remains available in the work session.
- **Backend prompt repair:** a producer/actual-CLI-renderer regression failed on absent requester trailers, then passed after using the existing inbound-context append owner. Four suites passed 41 tests in 51.74s, plus five unchanged Codex consumer tests in 28.37s. Core typecheck, lint, and independent source-bound review passed.

title: fix(beam): pause mirrors with unavailable credentials
body:
Related: #128336

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Beam does not register its outbound mirror credential with the Gateway's secret runtime, so unavailable credentials are not isolated as a mirror capability and polling can resolve credentials outside the prepared snapshot.

## User Impact

An unavailable configured mirror credential pauses only outbound mirroring; the Beam receiver, catalogs, and unrelated configured credentials remain available. Restore the credential and run `openclaw secrets reload` to recover. Tokenless receivers remain supported. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register `mirror.token` with the existing capability-secret owner and consume only prepared credentials. Recheck the current prepared credential immediately before upload so a reload during transcript reads cannot dispatch stale credentials. Keep the mirror scheduled while paused so it can recover after reload.

This is the narrow current-main replacement for the still-useful defect from #128336; it does not restore the old core-secret changes or tighten the token schema.

Credit: @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a04f7859-25ce-48c2-8ada-a9b463a0aa9b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/1ed4b37e-027e-4860-bd78-16d6db4bf94d)

## Evidence

- Synthetic boundary proof uses the real secret preparation path, public Beam plugin registration, actual service scheduler, an isolated executable credential provider, and an ephemeral loopback HTTP receiver. It covers cold isolation, healthy unrelated credentials, once-per-preparation resolution, reload-before-dispatch, and recovery. No real provider traffic or live Gateway changes.
- Existing receiver/retry tests: 13 passed; `Beam receiver > closes a declared oversized upload without waiting for its body` timed out at 120 seconds on the original run and a bounded same-shard-order reproduction. The test, Beam receiver implementation, and shared webhook body reader are unchanged. The test waits for response/connection closure after a headers-only oversized request; the precise blocked event remains unresolved. No timeout, assertion, or retry was weakened. This local failure remains recorded for exact-head CI; no inherited-CI exemption is claimed.
- Independent fresh review: no actionable P0–P2 findings across the original production change or the public-entry test repair. The reviewer did not execute tests or independently inspect the omitted core secret runtime.
- Simplification: removed poll-time credential resolution and ambient environment access; reused the existing capability owner. Production delta +43/-27 lines, tests +239/-1. Added code carries the unavailable/prepared distinction, reload-at-dispatch check, and focused regressions.

- Touched mirror tests: 25 passed, including tokenless operation, cancellation, redirects, and retry behavior.
- New boundary tests: both fail on unmodified `bf9843cf955019f65fe7e5855394b659228e063f` (missing capability owner and unresolved exec ref), both pass with the fix. Bundled secret-collector tests: 5 passed.
- Targeted TypeScript, production/test lint, formatting, plugin-inventory generation, and `git diff --check`: passed. The exec fixture is POSIX-only and skipped on Windows.
- Initial exact-head CI found a test ownership violation and a stale assertion allowance. Reworked the integration test through the existing public plugin entry instead of importing private Beam modules; the ownership guard passes (20 tests). Lowered only Beam's assertion-safety allowance from 2 to 1 because the production fix removes the obsolete config cast; no guard or assertion was weakened.
- No live Gateway, real model/provider request, or upgrade test was used; configuration shape and schema acceptance are unchanged.

title: fix: recover blank New Session pages without reload loops
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking New conversation can leave the New Session content blank when its native renderer fails, and draft rollback can display the previous restored page.

## User Impact

New Session render failures have visible recovery instead of an empty page. A failed initial render gets one automatic reload per browser tab; persistent failures stop at Retry. Later render failures retain in-page recovery, without automatically reloading an active draft. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catch render failures inside the native page's Solid root and key restored hosts by their actual identity. Reuse the document reachability and reload-guard owners; persist the automatic-reload marker before navigation and never reset it on mounting, retrying, or a timer. Skip automatic navigation when storage is unavailable or live work blocks it.

## Evidence

- 62 focused lifecycle/reload tests pass (three files, 1.72 seconds).
- Six production-bundle browser scenarios pass (20.74 seconds including setup): one-shot recovery, persistent error without a reload loop, typed-draft preservation, canceled chat load, rejected creation/rollback, and repeated New conversation visits.
- UI and affected test-suite typechecks, targeted lint/format, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 Auto Review: no actionable findings.
- The original screenshot's precise triggering exception remains unconfirmed. Browser proof injects a render exception through the real native page.

title: fix: scheduled follow-ups lose authorized task access
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled follow-ups losing the authenticated operator access needed to finish an authorized task, then stopping when a one-shot check still needs to wait.

## User Impact

New agent-turn continuations explicitly scheduled back into the same conversation can retain their original authenticated source and request another check without another user message. Tool denials, sandboxing, current role/device/access restrictions, session replacement, and occurrence cancellation still apply.

This preserves the original operator scope ceiling for the captured job; it is not a PR-only permission or a blanket administrator grant to automations. Existing jobs, guests, isolated/current targets, scripts, and foreign-session jobs are not promoted. Existing jobs needing this access must be recreated from an authenticated turn. No configuration or database schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing authenticated-source restoration and admitted-run owners, with private source evidence bound to the exact conversation and executable definition. Executable edits retire that source, including across older-reader round trips.

Keep automation management self-scoped. A successful explicit-session one-shot can use the existing next-check owner to rearm the same job through runtime state only, preserving its payload, target, tool cap, source, and deletion policy. No new scheduler, store, or parallel permission reader.

Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b0bb4540-7cef-47ea-82a9-25e67ae5c466)

## Evidence

- **Integrated the actual budget repair:** merged main `b1066a5c49101f28f3cbe4bfd3ca42bc66758036` and reused the exact lazy tool-output renderer change and generated manifest from [#176501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176501) (`123a1c283d01f15f45c4e6f5b646eb569c4cc5df`). Local candidate `461311b219f93c4a162d367349612f32dffce433` passes the production UI build and unchanged strict budget: **1,489,747 B chat-boot gzip, 25 requests**, below the 1,490,000 B ceiling. No threshold, skip, or permission change.
- **Combined-head verification:** 32 UI regression tests and 26 scheduled-continuation/fast-mode tests pass after the merge, including cold tool-output loading, retained native disclosure state, paused force-run, and mid-preflight revocation. UI and services-cron type graphs pass; changed UI lint/format and diff checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the complete candidate against the integrated base found no actionable findings. The UI files are byte-identical to the independently reviewed performance PR; its production-bundle E2E proof is reused, not represented as a new run here.

- **275 focused tests pass:** the original 273 source/admission, private projection, Gateway validation, tool, prompt-prefix, invocation/cadence/restart/management checks plus two new authority scenarios. The complete nine-scenario authority file was rerun after the final repair.
- The authority regression is red on base `1446ecc3939` because the scheduled GitHub schema omits `inspect`; the fixed path exposes `inspect/merge` and reaches the real guarded action owner using fixed external GitHub I/O. Scheduling regressions were independently red for rejected proposals and deleted/disabled waiting one-shots.
- A checked-in real-Gateway E2E now drives authenticated Control UI/WebSocket ingress and deterministic model tool calls through foreground creation → creator completion/disconnect → timer-fired continuation → same-job `next_check` rearm → second continuation → durable transcript and automatic job removal. It verifies guarded session mutations, unchanged schedule/payload/target, and the exact GitHub owner’s no-publication verdict. Only the external model and the host clock are fixtures; no authority is injected.
- The paused “Run now” regression fails before the repair and passes through actual `CronService.run(..., "force")` afterward, leaving the job paused. A second case revokes the operator role during the awaited GitHub preflight after successful inspection and proves no merge PUT occurs. Existing occurrence cancellation and source checks remain authoritative.
- Actual published stable **2026.10.4 → candidate** proof passed: stable Gateway-authored finite-cap jobs survived Doctor’s schema 20 → 28 migration byte-for-byte, with no operator-source promotion; database integrity checks passed. Candidate executed the unchanged read-only script canary, rejected its attempted `exec`, and denied a read-scoped client’s update. This is migration/loading/execution proof, not updater package-swap orchestration.
- Original full `pnpm build`, core typecheck, affected test graphs, changed-file lint/format, Markdown/MDX checks, and independent P0–P2 Auto Review passed. The new E2E additionally passed root-test typecheck. The final paused-run repair received a fresh independent P0–P2 review with no actionable findings; its nine-scenario authority file and 57 active-occurrence/manual-run/queue sibling tests pass, along with the services-cron type graph and changed-file lint/format.
- No live GitHub merge or Gateway restart was performed in the new E2E. Its GitHub inspection deliberately reaches the existing no-publication response; successful inspection/merge effects and durable reload remain covered by the focused production-owner regressions. The new E2E has not been replayed on base. The full build, E2E, and upgrade proof used the original production head; the final change only removes the paused-state rejection and is separately covered by focused tests and static gates.

- **Historical inherited CI failure on prior head `2fde64bb685d77b3127c4e1d11cf2d7e9dc2cea1`:** [run 39166369895, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39166369895), [control-ui-performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39166369895/job/117790534520), measured base and candidate chat-boot gzip at **1,494,464 B each (+0 B)**, both 4,464 B above the existing 1,490,000 B ceiling. [Preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39166369895/job/117790185229) identifies tested merge `560b2f0fa1cc51bfaad01ca6c6999f8a758a6a24` and actual main base `6ef7539e3cf7f2674176b75f1de0423e765895c2`. CI has now completed: all other selected jobs passed or were intentionally skipped; the only underlying failure is this performance check, which also makes `openclaw/ci-gate` fail. The automated failure report labels it “new” against an older passing scheduled-main run (`3020cb46d4737c0a1b1085e9d5eb6985bf33821b`), with selected scope not compared; the paired execution above uses the actual tested main base and establishes zero PR growth. This is an inherited failure, not a passing check or a gate waiver. That prior head was blocked; the integration above repairs the measured cause and will receive fresh exact-head CI.

<summary>Test cost and scope notes</summary>

Vitest wall times include transform/setup:

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Scheduled operator continuation, including paused force-run and mid-action revocation | 9 | 56.69 s |
| Durable source custody | 9 | 8.56 s |
| One-shot persistence/ownership | 17 | 25.43 s |
| Invocation eligibility | 17 | 25.59 s |

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents keep calling a tool that cannot work on this Gateway (no web_search credentials, no paired node, a source reply with no live turn), because the error doesn't say the failure is lasting or what to use instead.

## User Impact

User impact: when web_search has no credentials, exec targets a node that isn't paired, or a final source reply has no live turn, the agent is told the failure won't clear by retrying and is pointed at a working route. Fewer wasted tool calls and fewer replies that blame the wrong cause.

## Why This Change Was Made

An audit of three locally run Gateways found 49 environment-confusion hits in 226 sampled sessions. 31 of them were this pattern: a tool listed as available failed for a setup reason, and the agent retried or reworded. The top causes were no paired node (12), a missing web_search credential (11), and the message tool's terminal-reply path (8).

- **web_search:** providers already return `missing_<provider>_api_key` with setup text, but the tool boundary wrapped all of it as untrusted external content, so models treat it as data rather than guidance. Core now adds its own sentence outside the envelope: search is not set up, retrying or rewording fails the same way, and the agent should use another route (such as fetching a known URL or a browser) only if this session has one. The wording names no specific tool, because `web_fetch` or the browser can be disabled. The provider's setup details stay wrapped. During auto-detected fallback, the selected provider's missing-credential payload now reaches the tool instead of a generic "check configuration and connection" message.
- **exec host=node:** both "no node" errors now say the condition lasts until a node is paired or reconnects, and that the agent should use another exec host or tell the user.
- **message final reply with no turn capability:** the error now says changing channel or target won't help and that `final=false` delivers the message.

No new tools, prompt text, or schema fields. Credentials are still looked up when the tool runs, so a key added later still works without a restart.

## Evidence

- **Live A/B (QA Lab, isolated Gateway, `tool-readiness-errors-live`, 5 runs × 2 cases per arm and model):** each case asks for the action, then makes a second request in the same session. Baseline is this branch with the `src` changes removed.

  | Model | Case | Follow-up turn called the failed tool again (baseline → fix) | First reply named the setup cause (baseline → fix) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | gpt-6.1-sol | no paired node | 5/5 → 0/5 | 5/5 → 5/5 |
  | gpt-6.1-sol | web_search, no key | 0/5 → 0/5 | 5/5 → 5/5 |
  | claude-sonnet-4-6 | no paired node | 5/5 → 5/5 | 5/5 → 5/5 |
  | claude-sonnet-4-6 | web_search, no key | 5/5 → 5/5 | 1/5 → 3/5 |

  GPT stops re-checking the node on the next turn. Sonnet still re-checks once per new turn in both arms (one call, then the right answer), which is reasonable when state could have changed. Neither arm retried more than twice in a turn on the current main; the long retry loops in the audit came from older builds and multi-turn sessions this single-session scenario only partly reproduces.
- **Regression tests fail on the base:** with the production files reverted to the merge base, the four new tests fail (missing-node wording, brave error fixture, trusted guidance outside the envelope, fallback keeping the provider payload); with this change, they pass.
- **Live scenario check:** the scenario now also asserts the failing tool was called at least once, so a run cannot pass without hitting the setup error. Rechecked on the final head: passes on gpt-6.1-sol (follow-up retries 0 and 0) and claude-sonnet-4-6 (1 and 1).
- **Unit and contract tests:** `src/web-search`, web_search output contract and security tests, all provider tests that use `missing_*_api_key` (brave, deepseek, google, moonshot, parallel, perplexity, xai), node phase tests, gateway hosted routing, and the QA Lab scenario catalog tests pass (13 files / 337 tests and 12 files / 215 tests). `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.
- **Not covered:** the message-tool terminal-reply error is covered by the existing routing test only; it needs a channel turn whose capability expired, which the QA flow can't produce.

## Review follow-up (ClawSweeper)

- The web_search guidance no longer names `web_fetch` or the browser unconditionally.
- The live scenario now requires the setup failure to be exercised before judging retries.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/c8c50782-6cfa-4b1b-8160-cc7d2d30fc0f)

## Worked on by

- @obviyus

title: fix: restore OpenCode Go family routing after API migration
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Go models retaining outdated or wrong-family endpoints after OpenCode’s inference API migration, alongside missing truthful client/session headers on native requests.

Original report: https://x.com/steipete/status/2111814502731939939. Routing clarification: https://x.com/shakker/status/2111857457580675267.

## User Impact

Discovered models, saved native Go routes, offline starters, and dynamic fallbacks now select their endpoint by the resolved model API. Saved native URLs migrate automatically; custom proxy URLs and explicit API choices remain unchanged. No new configuration option is introduced. Rejected credentials or unavailable model IDs still require valid account/catalog access and a current model reference.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial PR corrected endpoint attribution but left a separate routing gap: Go defaults and fallbacks still used `/zen/go`, and refreshed Anthropic rows were forced back to that old base. The follow-up moves those producers and API-aware normalization to the current Go routes:

| API | Final request path |
| --- | --- |
| Chat Completions | `/inference/go/openai/v1/chat/completions` |
| Responses | `/inference/go/openai/v1/responses` |
| Anthropic Messages | `/inference/go/anthropic/v1/messages` |
| Gemini streaming | `/inference/go/google/v1beta/models/<id>:streamGenerateContent` |

Discovery uses the distinct `/inference/go/v1/models` endpoint. Anthropic runtime bases omit the terminal `/v1` so the owning transport adds it exactly once. The provider owns family selection; native-route metadata and its packaged mirror stay aligned. Existing header policy, session precedence, Vertex behavior, and authentication behavior are preserved—no new transport, SDK seam, state, or model-name heuristic.

## Evidence

- Five new production-path regressions failed on prior head `da021a7f50fcf059feec150091b6b727a8b65b2a`: fresh Anthropic projection, saved shared native bases across all four APIs, and offline/default fallbacks retained old routes. All five now pass.
- The new suite composes catalog acquisition/projection → registered provider normalization → real family transports/Google SDK. Eight intercepted inference requests verify the exact URLs above and decoded assistant replies; custom proxies remain untouched. Warm file wall time: 4.13s; test time about 0.4s.
- 77 focused current-routing/header/discovery/metadata/prefix tests passed. The existing header suite still covers 16 scenarios / 64 intercepted requests; those hand-built cases alone were not treated as routing proof.
- Full rebuild passed (3m 28.5s). Focused TypeScript, extension/script lint, format, docs MDX, and whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 reviews of the routing repair and the live-fixture follow-up found no actionable findings. The follow-up changes only `src/gateway/gateway-models.profiles.live.test.ts`: it forwards the effective config to both registry consumers and starts/stops the existing CLI proxy lifecycle for live discovery. A new real-registry regression failed before config forwarding and passes afterward; 41 focused fixture/helper tests, targeted TypeScript, lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed. No production routing/security/secret code changed in this follow-up.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39151988201) completed successfully for `a6a2151b81c26f20233492f1e1875351b5e378d6`, with no failed or unfinished jobs. [ClawSweeper's current-head reassessment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176265#issuecomment-6252193480) reviewed `a6a2151b81c26f20233492f1e1875351b5e378d6` at 18:13 UTC with **zero findings**, **ready for maintainer review**, and no before-merge items. That assessment preceded the successful three-model Gateway run recorded below; Google remains blocked by upstream workspace privacy policy. It is not itself merge approval. The prior full build/upgrade evidence remains reusable because the only subsequent source change is the live test fixture.

### Upgrade and saved-data compatibility

- **Actual latest-stable package upgrade passed:** [published-upgrade-survivor / base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39147944160/job/117737275061) installed published `2026.10.4`, updated via the real updater to the candidate tarball, ran Doctor and survival assertions, and booted/probed the isolated Gateway. The lane took 464s. The [downloadable evidence artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39147944160/artifacts/12144696781) records selected source `b8a2efa72eb2827adfba75c4445eb1454849bb31` and installed build ID `2026.10.4-b8a2efa72eb2-2026-10-18T17-08-04.697Z`; the equal package version is not being used as source identity. Config intents, session metadata/user files, post-Doctor validation, health, readiness and RPC status assertions passed. Its first-hop post-core exit snapshot is explicitly unavailable; the final update/survival outcome is successful, not proof that every intermediate state was captured.
- **Go-specific saved configuration loaded and resolved:** an isolated, official published `2026.10.4` CLI wrote and validated eight authored rows (four APIs × native shared legacy base/custom proxy), primary/fallback selections and aliases. The candidate's real `loadConfig()` → `resolveModelAsync()`, using actual plugin discovery/normalization and no fake registry/hooks, resolved all eight with their authored API intact: four canonical native family bases and four custom-proxy routes. No network requests occurred. Saved config bytes, aliases/selections, workspace identity and notes stayed exact. Anthropic proxy runtime trimming of terminal `/v1` matches the same shared policy in the published baseline; its authored URL stayed unchanged on disk.
- **Boundaries:** the packaged survivor fixture is the repository's general base scenario, not an authenticated Go turn. The Go-specific probe is a published-CLI-to-candidate-source read/resolution handoff, not a second package upgrade or a successful candidate CLI/Doctor run. A local source-CLI attempt was refused by the managed runtime-artifact publication guard; it was not bypassed. The separate hosted packaged updater/Doctor run above supplies that boundary. This PR changes neither stored schema nor API/model selections; route normalization changes derived native destinations at read/use time, without rewriting user data.

### Authenticated upstream checks and historical local Gateway limitation

A newly supplied protected Team credential was used only through its `opencode.ai` destination binding; it was never printed or copied into plaintext config. Authenticated catalog GET returned 200. With the existing managed-proxy lifecycle active, the actual Go catalog owner also reported `ready` and projected 36 models. The live fixture had separately omitted its effective config while loading the registry: the same captured discovery produced zero models without that config and 36 with it. The test-only follow-up repairs that missing handoff rather than weakening strict model selection.

**Real upstream inference succeeded through three canonical protocols:**

| Protocol / model | HTTP / decoded result | Elapsed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat Completions / `glm-5.3` | 200; assistant text; `stop` | 6.406s |
| Responses / `gpt-5.6-luna` | 200; assistant text; `completed` | 2.184s |
| Anthropic Messages / `qwen3.8-max` | 200; assistant text; `end_turn` | 6.671s |

These were bounded coding prompts sent directly through protected HTTPS egress with truthful `openclaw/2026.10.4` identification and a stable synthetic `x-opencode-session`. Anthropic used the SDK-native `x-api-key` form, confirming that a mandatory Bearer-only claim is unsupported. These direct API contract checks are **not shipped CLI/Gateway E2E** and do not replace the intercepted transport tests.

**Google triage completed: upstream workspace privacy policy, not a demonstrated routing/payload bug.** The current public `opencode-go` metadata explicitly assigns `gemini-4-argon-contributor` to `@ai-sdk/google` at `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/google/v1beta`, matching the API/base produced by this PR. The prior streaming native-key, streaming Bearer, and non-streaming Bearer controls all returned 400. One bounded diagnostic capture established the precise service rejection (`HTTP 400`, Google-style error code `400`, status `UNKNOWN`):

> Upstream request failed: This Go model trains on request data. Allow paid endpoints that train on request data in your workspace's Privacy settings to use it.

The OpenCode workspace owner/admin must explicitly decide whether to permit paid endpoints that train on request data, or retain the existing privacy policy and choose a permitted model. No privacy setting was changed, no further Google inference was pursued after identifying the gate, and no successful Google reply is claimed. No OpenClaw code fix is demonstrated by this rejection, and filtering by a model-name suffix or changing transport/auth to evade the policy would be inappropriate. The supplied key remains valid: the successful catalog and three upstream protocol checks above are unchanged.

**Historical host-local Gateway attempt reached model dispatch but did not complete inference (superseded by the hosted pass below):** after fixture repair, the isolated Gateway booted, selected `opencode-go/glm-5.3` from 36 discovered models, and attempted its real agent prompt. It ended with a connection failure and no captured inference POST/reply. A separate pre-aborted invocation of the actual guarded model-fetch owner confirmed the protected exec binding is rejected as an unregistered process-local sentinel before sending. The protected-exec-to-model-egress handoff needs an owner-supported integration; no key unwrapping, plaintext substitution, sentinel bypass, TLS weakening, manual proxy-activation flag, or live service mutation was used. This is not evidence that the supplied key is invalid: its catalog and direct inference checks succeeded.

### Full real Gateway acceptance passed

A fresh supported Blacksmith Testbox run completed the actual Gateway live-model test at exact source `a6a2151b81c26f20233492f1e1875351b5e378d6`, tree `1b2acda43f55080cb09115430a0314ca1b01861e` (remote carrier `e26e61cd31517b89b34ae48d8b15e6e412c9fb4c`). [Hosted lease workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39160510905); allocation `tbx_01m588zma4973het1z3dmhycjp`; managed Crabbox `0.77.0`, `.github/workflows/ci-check-testbox.yml` on trusted `main`. Requested standard check profile; observed 4 CPUs and 16,167,124 KiB memory. GitHub's existing workflow credential hydration supplied authentication; the protected Team key was not extracted or forwarded.

The real test command was `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_REQUIRE_PROFILE_KEYS=0 OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS=opencode-go OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_MODELS=opencode-go/glm-5.3,opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna,opencode-go/qwen3.8-max OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_MAX_MODELS=3 OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_SMOKE=0 OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_THINKING=low OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS=90000 OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS=180000 OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 pnpm test:live -- src/gateway/gateway-models.profiles.live.test.ts --testNamePattern 'runs meaningful prompts across models with available keys' --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`, with a passive allowlisted diagnostics observer.

| Model / actual protocol | Meaningful prompt | Read + continuation | Exec + read + continuation | Image |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `glm-5.3` / Chat Completions | passed | passed | passed | not advertised |
| `gpt-5.6-luna` / Responses | passed | passed | passed | passed |
| `qwen3.8-max` / Anthropic Messages | passed | passed | passed | passed |

All **3/3 selected models completed**, zero model failures/skips. The selected test passed in 129.27s; 183 other tests were intentionally excluded by the exact test-name filter, not counted as acceptance. Both test and independent three-model receipt inspection exited 0. Passive observations recorded HTTP 200 on each canonical inference path, `User-Agent: openclaw/2026.10.4`, and presence of `x-opencode-session`, without logging authentication, session values, or request/response bodies. Discovery also returned 200 and `ready` with 36 models.

The outer wrapper initially exited 1 **only during GitHub cleanup settlement**, after the successful test, due to a transient exact-run read failure. Native cleanup was reconciled on the same allocation: remote state `completed`, no host, and exact GitHub run terminal `cancelled` as expected for externally stopped Testbox jobs. That cancelled workflow is not being presented as green CI. The separate PR CI run remains successful. Earlier queued allocation `tbx_01m584bdydz8dr5bdt3g92g69d` exercised zero models and was stopped; it remains a historical capacity failure, superseded by this successful real Gateway execution. Google privacy policy is unchanged and Google inference remains unproven.

Historical hosted runs ([broad Go](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39141895747), [diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39143240057), [canonical control](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39146698145/job/117732142165)) stopped at catalog auth rejection before inference using their existing hosted credential. They remain failed historical attempts, not success or a verdict on the new protected Team key. Upstream retains the old OpenAI/Anthropic aliases, so an old URL alone does not establish an access denial. The reporter's exact version/model/config and claimed status causes remain unverified; the earlier Control UI model-not-found symptom occurs before inference.

**Other retained gaps:** an additional helper-only sweep on this host had 180 passes, one unchanged OpenAI Ultra loopback `UND_ERR_SOCKET` failure, and two skips under both Node and pinned Bun; a narrow Bun reproduction also failed. This is documented, not relabeled green. The broader hosted MiniMax/Qwen lane also has two independently stale selectors (`minimax-m2.7` deprecated, `qwen3.5-plus` absent); strict missing-model checks were not weakened.

Reported by @douglasfugazi; investigation requested by @steipete. PR and expanded verification requested by @obviyus.

title: fix: announce the selected Usage session view to screen readers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: screen readers cannot identify whether **All** or **Recently viewed** is selected in Usage’s Sessions panel.

## User Impact

Assistive technology now exposes the selected session view before and after switching it. Appearance and selection behavior are unchanged. No configuration, migration, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the local override that suppresses the existing segmented control’s pressed state. This reuses the control’s reactive accessibility semantics rather than adding new state or handlers.

## Evidence

<details>
<summary>Captured Chromium accessibility-tree evidence (synthetic data)</summary>

Captured through the real Usage page against the existing mock Gateway. Before source: 137e7b2abc87d14e3be641bd824c064cb0b98e66. After source: the tested candidate whose complete Git tree matches published head 00f55907684a5b7f72ddcbfd18028e2d5972b94d.

Before — All selected visually:
```text
- button "All"
- button "Recently viewed"
```

After — All selected:
```text
- button "All" [pressed]
- button "Recently viewed"
```

After — Recently viewed selected:
```text
- button "All"
- button "Recently viewed" [pressed]
```

Both before states omitted the pressed state. Browser assertions also verified that the inactive button has aria-pressed="false" after the repair. Screenshots are retained separately. On October 18, 2026, the landing requester approved proceeding without PR-embedded screenshots for this nonvisual fix; only that delivery destination is waived.

</details>

- A regression against the actual Sessions panel failed on the original source because **All** had no pressed state. All **8 focused tests pass** with the fix; the test covers initial state and switching in both directions.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Chromium against the existing synthetic mock-Gateway application confirmed both states before and after. Before: neither selector exposes pressed state. After: the current selector exposes `pressed=true` and the other `pressed=false`; switching transfers the state.
- Inspected synthetic before/after screenshots were delivered in the work session below. The corresponding screenshots are pixel-identical, as expected for an accessibility-semantics-only change. PR-only screenshot embedding was explicitly waived by the landing requester; the screenshot files remain retained.
- Independent review: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, no findings.
- Targeted open-PR searches for the selector, its owning file, and pressed-state accessibility found no matching fix.
- Production delta: **1 line removed**. Regression: **37 lines added**. Focused test file: **2.62s Vitest duration**, **3.76s runner duration**. Full CI [run 39139301493](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39139301493) passed for the unchanged published head: **28 successful jobs, 27 skipped**. The required **openclaw/ci-gate passed**. Final paginated exact-head verification found no pending or failed checks.

The published commit is `00f55907684a5b7f72ddcbfd18028e2d5972b94d`. Its complete Git tree matches the tested local candidate exactly; only the intended two files changed, and the required human co-author trailer is present.

Landing was authorized on October 18, 2026. Full CI and the required gate passed on the unchanged head. ClawSweeper found no actionable defects. Only PR-embedded screenshot delivery was explicitly waived; captures and the Chromium trace remain available.

title: feat(agents): agents can check why a tool is missing before saying OpenClaw can't
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents say OpenClaw can't do something when the tool is only missing from the current session (removed by policy or profile), or when one call failed. Agents then give wrong fixes or hand work back to the user.

## User Impact

User impact: when a tool is missing, agents can now see why and name the real setting. For example, they say "`browser` is denied by `tools.deny` in this session" instead of "OpenClaw has no browser" or "add it to `tools.alsoAllow`" (which does not override a deny). Plain `session_status` output is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`session_status` with `capabilities: true`** returns this session's available tools, plus each missing tool grouped by reason. It reads the existing Gateway `tools.effective` inventory, the same check behind `/tools` and the Control UI tools panel, so no new policy logic is added. If the check fails, status still returns and says it could not check.
- **One system prompt line** (Documentation section, below the cache boundary): a missing tool or failed call shows this session's limits, not OpenClaw's. Before saying OpenClaw can't, check `session_status` with `capabilities=true`, then the docs. Each check is named only when the session can run it: `session_status` only when that tool is present; `https://docs.openclaw.ai/llms.txt` only when a web tool exists, otherwise the local docs; otherwise the line asks the agent to say what it could not check. This keeps the existing Documentation rule (aaf3536): advertise readable local references, and don't point at web retrieval the session lacks. This follows the Hermes Agent pattern ("never answer 'can't' from memory") at a fraction of its prompt cost.
- **Runtime line key `capabilities=` renamed to `channel_capabilities=`.** In live runs, Claude read `capabilities=none` (channel rendering features) as "this session has no tool capabilities" and stopped looking.
- **Two misleading strings fixed.** The Code Mode tool summary said `exec` means "never shell", while the same prompt names `exec` as the shell tool. The terminal error told unattended runs to "ask the operator to open one" first. It now says to use `exec` when available and to ask the operator otherwise.

Startup cost: about +324 characters (~88 tokens) of prompt and tool schema across all sessions. Nothing is added above the prompt cache boundary.

## Evidence

**Live model A/B** (QA Lab `session-capability-limits-live`): `tools.deny: [browser, cron]`. The agent is asked to open a page with the browser and to schedule a reminder, and to explain why if it can't. A case passes when the reply names `tools.deny` as the cause. Five runs × 2 cases per arm. The baseline is this PR's head with the capability changes removed (a mutation check).

| Model | Baseline: named `tools.deny` | This PR | Called `session_status` (baseline → PR) | Changed config |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` | 3/10 | 20/20 (two runs) | 0/10 → 20/20 | 0 |
| `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` | 0/10 | 8/10 (after the runtime-key rename; 7/10 before it) | 2/10 → 8/10 | 0 |

Baseline replies cited the wrong setting in 7/10 (gpt) and 10/10 (Claude) cases: `tools.alsoAllow`, `plugins.allow`, `browser.enabled`, or missing provider credentials. The two remaining Claude misses answered from memory without calling `session_status`.

**Real Gateway e2e** (`session-status-capabilities` vitest scenario): starts the full Gateway with `tools.deny`, seeds a real session, and calls `session_status` through `POST /tools/invoke`. The run checks that:
- plain status does not read the inventory;
- `capabilities: true` returns a `live-session` inventory;
- `browser` and `canvas` are listed under `Denied by tools.deny` in both the structured result and the model-visible text.

The first version of this test caught a real bug: legacy bare `main` keys were passed straight to `tools.effective`. That is fixed here.

**Local checks:**
- Unit tests: the summary helper, `session_status` with `capabilities: true` including the failure path, and both variants of the prompt line (with and without available checks).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt on touched files, and `git diff --check`.
- Prompt, prefix-stability, Code Mode and QA catalog/coverage suites.
- Autoreview (Codex, P1): no findings.

**Review follow-up (ClawSweeper):** two findings, both fixed:
- The remote docs index is no longer named without a web tool. A new prompt test covers a sandbox with local docs only.
- Terminal recovery keeps the operator path when `exec` is unavailable.

The branch was merged with `main` and the prompt snapshots regenerated. Re-run on the merged head: the e2e scenario passes; the live scenario passes on gpt-6.1-sol 2/2 and on Claude Sonnet 1/2, consistent with the earlier runs.

**Not tied to this change:** `system-prompt-params.test.ts` fails 3 cases on this host because `~/.cache/tmp` is itself a Git repository.

**Gaps and follow-ups:**
- Sandbox, workspace, network and identity facts are not part of the capability list yet.
- In one baseline Claude run, the `cron`-denied case still produced "Reminder scheduled successfully". This looks like a separate policy gap and needs its own investigation.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/c8c50782-6cfa-4b1b-8160-cc7d2d30fc0f)

## Worked on by

title: docs: document password authentication for logs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `openclaw logs` reference omits its supported `--password` option and tells users connecting with `--url` to provide only `--token`.

## User Impact

Users of password-authenticated Gateways can find the correct flag and a copyable explicit-URL example. Documentation only: no runtime changes, breaking changes, migrations, or required user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Document `--password` among the shared Gateway RPC options, name it alongside `--token` in the explicit-URL guidance, and show an example using `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`. The CLI already registers the option and forwards it to the Gateway.

## Evidence

title: fix(agents): agents claim no shell or hand off when Code Mode and terminal text say so
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents wrongly conclude they have no shell or must hand work to a human. This happens when the Code Mode tool summary says "never shell", or when a terminal tool call finds no shared terminal.

## User Impact

User impact: in Code Mode, agents keep using the nested shell `exec` tool instead of claiming shell access is unavailable. A missing shared terminal no longer makes them ask the operator to open one; unattended runs (for example, scheduled cleanup jobs) continue with their own commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Code Mode tool summary:** the startup tool list described `exec` as "…call exact catalog tools from code, never shell/Python/imports". The same prompt also says "Use the shell tool `exec` for heavier computation". Models read the first line as "no shell". The clause is removed. The `exec` schema still says "`code` is JavaScript, never a shell command", so the warning about what goes in `code` is kept. Net startup prompt change: −3 words.
- **Terminal tool error:** the recovery text "ask the operator to open one in this chat" made the agent stop and hand off. It now says the tool cannot open a terminal and to run your own commands with `exec`.

## Evidence

- Source: a review of 84 real agent self-knowledge failures in team sessions, plus a random sample of 80 sessions. The baseline is 1.8 failures per 100 assistant turns, and these two strings were implicated in several of the failures.
- `pnpm vitest run` passed on `terminal-tool.test.ts` (updated assertion), `system-prompt*.test.ts` and `code-mode*`: 36 files, 503 tests. oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Gap: no model-level before/after result. In cut-at-failure replays on `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, the historical failures reproduced in only 2/50 trials, so a paired eval could not show a difference. Follow-up metric: the failure rate per 100 assistant turns on randomly sampled sessions after release, compared with the frozen baseline.
