title: feat(deepseek): search the web with the standalone Search API
body:
## What Problem This Solves

DeepSeek users cannot use its new standalone Search API through OpenClaw’s managed `web_search`.

## User Impact

Users can select `deepseek` for web search with any model after installing the existing official DeepSeek plugin. Credentials come from plugin search config, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, or the configured model-provider key, with standard SecretRef preparation. Existing auth-profile-only keys are not reused.

This PR is **ready for landing under maintainer direction**; authenticated DeepSeek source-provider and compiled-package verification now pass. The plugin keeps its current installable distribution; this does not bundle it into the host, change search defaults for installations without the plugin, or add DeepSeek Fetch. An installed, enabled plugin can participate in normal credential auto-detection at order 80.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing vendor-owned plugin using the public web-search contract and lazy runtime. Call `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search` directly with query/count and `need_content: false`; return model-oriented summaries with snippet fallback. No model call, new dependency, new core tool, SDK expansion, or additional state owner.

Preflight the 128-Unicode-character query limit and unsupported structured filters before making a paid request. Reuse shared guarded HTTP, cancellation, timeout, error redaction, and cache helpers. Cache identity includes query, count, and a hashed credential scope. Malformed/non-HTTP(S)/oversized source URLs are omitted, valid paid results are retained, and omissions mark the result truncated so provider prose cannot enter raw compatibility output.

Simplification: search-only is the smallest coherent stage; Fetch and richer provider-specific tool surfaces are deferred. The necessary growth is the thin adapter/manifest plus independent request, lifecycle, and production-composition proof; no new framework or compatibility machinery. Against the base: production/config +281/−4 lines; tests +743/−1 lines; documentation +82/−4 lines.

## Evidence

- **71 focused tests pass:** 31 DeepSeek provider/contract tests, 14 real production-tool integrations, 5 existing DeepSeek model-plugin tests, and 21 normalized-output/error siblings.
- Production integrations exercise real manifest/artifact discovery, config validation, readiness and explicit/automatic selection, SecretRef preparation, tool execution, and normalized schema-valid output. Only external HTTP responses are fixtures; provider routing, credential preparation, and normalization are not mocked.
- **Settings/onboarding completeness repair:** mirror DeepSeek search metadata in the existing official external-provider install catalog, so it is offered before the plugin is installed. The shared provider list feeding Search settings and onboarding contains exactly one DeepSeek entry after installation. A fresh-install setup regression fails without the catalog descriptor and passes after it, proving selection, credential configuration, and handoff to the standard package installer (installer I/O is a fixture; no package is installed on the live Gateway).
- Follow-up focused proof: **28/28 pass** across 12 search-setup cases, 2 install-catalog cases, and the 14 production-tool integration cases, in 48.34 seconds wrapper wall. Original provider/live proof remains valid because the adapter is unchanged. Targeted lint/format and independent P0–P2 review are clean. The full repair build passes (3 minutes 1 second), and a compiled install-catalog smoke confirms DeepSeek onboarding scope, package/credential paths, and environment discovery. Real Chromium → isolated compiled Gateway → installed candidate → authenticated DeepSeek Search settings E2E now passes, including persisted provider/enabled settings, live sources, reload, and served-asset identity. [Inspected before/after setup screenshots and uncached benchmarks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175729#issuecomment-6238658524) are published on this PR. The opt-in browser regression passes 1/1; the default path skips without loading the live fixture graph. No Gateway RPC or provider HTTP responses are mocked in this browser proof.
- Coverage includes query operators and Unicode limits; credential precedence; missing/unresolved credentials; disabled plugins; count and cache/TTL/account isolation; malformed/empty responses; 401/402/429/5xx and redaction; cancellation; bounded untrusted prose; and invalid-source URL handling.
- Independent Auto Review (Codex, P0–P2): malformed-URL raw-output finding reproduced with 3 failing integration cases, repaired, then final review completed scoped-clean. A later test-only change narrows the captured request body to a string for lint.
- Built-plugin smoke: compiled public artifact → lazy execution module → guarded HTTP fixture → safe result mapping passes, including invalid-source omission.
- Plugin production typecheck, targeted extension/core lint, formatting, plugin inventory, docs config examples, docs links, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm build`: completes successfully on the final production change (2 minutes 58 seconds). The full build emits non-fatal Control UI size-budget warnings; this change edits no UI source, and baseline attribution was not separately established.

<details>
<summary>Commands and test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/deepseek/web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/deepseek/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-search.deepseek.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-search.provider-errors.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-search-output.security.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/deepseek/tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

Latest provider/model file run: 36 tests, 12.08 seconds wall. Production integration file: 14 tests, 10.33 seconds wall (about 2.5 seconds test execution); sibling files: 21 tests, 27.67 seconds wall. Wrapper compilation accounts for much of wall time. CI seconds are pending.

</details>

**Authenticated live verification (2026-10-17, head `8e236614c49650f9d35d808e568748d8750348a2`):** the opt-in source-provider live suite passes **1/1** with no HTTP mocks (743 ms test execution; 30.61 seconds Vitest wall including preparation/setup). The compiled public artifact and lazy runtime also pass real API checks: a site-filtered search returns 3 usable `docs.openclaw.ai` sources with nonempty summaries in 966 ms; repeating it returns matching results with `cached: true` in under 1 ms; a Unicode query returns 2 results in 684 ms. These timings are individual smoke observations, not a performance benchmark. No code changes were needed after the environment’s secret-host authorization was corrected and a fresh execution run picked it up.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_LIVE_TEST=1 \
  pnpm test:live extensions/deepseek/web-search.live.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

**Remaining live gaps:** broad relevance/quality benchmarks, rate-limit saturation/recovery, and billed-charge verification were not performed. The credential remained in the protected store and was neither printed nor committed. The PR is ready for review; authenticated source and compiled-package search are now verified.

**Stable-to-head upgrade proof — PASS (2026-10-17):** official npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` (build `383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`) produced real persisted configuration/state under an isolated named profile. Its archive SHA512 matches registry integrity, and a standalone module-resolution guard prevented borrowing checkout dependencies. After copying the stable-produced state, candidate Doctor completed successfully; separate candidate CLI processes validated and read back preserved explicit Gemini selection, disabled search, count/cache/timeout, synthetic Google credentials and header SecretRef, MiniMax credential SecretRef/settings, and sibling fetch settings. Complete authored subtrees were compared; Doctor-owned agent/plugin/migration/wizard/skill additions were enumerated. The approved application and exact `@openclaw/ai@2026.10.4` cooldown exceptions were confined to isolated acquisition/installation; shared policy is unchanged.

Nine production-owner consumer checks pass: disabled search remains unavailable; explicit Gemini wins despite available DeepSeek credentials; automatic selection prefers MiniMax order 15, then Gemini order 20, before DeepSeek order 80; DeepSeek is eligible with either config or environment-only synthetic credentials; disabled, uncredentialed, or catalog-unavailable DeepSeek is not selected. These use real compiled discovery/preparation/selection owners, not mocked decisions. Executing candidate build is `af2cd07b25d90a7318a4746714e79fc945f3e38c`; current head `baf7345c357ab31808acec35717da46ebec0641b` changes only the browser E2E and its two inventories, with production inputs unchanged.

**Upgrade proof boundaries:** this qualifies stable-produced state → candidate Doctor/cold-process CLI readback and real owner selection, not a public updater run or live Gateway restart. Positive DeepSeek discovery in this upgrade lane uses the canonical source-checkout contract. A separate optional local-link install was rejected by the scanner for the generated SDK symlink escaping its install root; no guard was weakened. The independent browser E2E above instead installs the ordinary packed candidate tarball successfully and performs authenticated search. Protected credentials were not accessed by the upgrade lane; all fixtures were synthetic.

**ClawSweeper setup-fallback repair:** shared search setup now recognizes the provider-declared configured credential fallback when deciding whether a key already exists, while leaving fallback values and SecretRefs at their model-provider owner. Dedicated-key extraction/storage is unchanged. Six regressions failed before the repair (interactive/quickstart disabled search; reference mode shadowed the existing fallback) and now pass across inline/SecretRef credentials and all three setup modes. The existing setup suite and real DeepSeek production integration pass **32/32** in **42.92 seconds wrapper wall** (18 setup cases, 14 provider-composition cases). title: chore(tooling): type check with tsrs instead of tsgo
body:
Makes tsrs the default repo type checker on supported platforms, with tsgo fallback and release validation retained. The reviewed corrections fix invocation-environment selection, complete declaration consumer fixtures, preserve Go profiling, and retain current-main dependency updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Type checking each large OpenClaw graph with tsgo takes 9–17s wall, 64–127s CPU and 9–16 GB of memory on our dev host. This switches the repo type checker to tsrs, keeps tsgo as the fallback, and keeps a full tsgo pass in release validation.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers and CI type-check lanes (`pnpm tsgo`, every `tsgo:*` script, `run-tsgo-core-test-shards`) would run tsrs on Linux and Apple Silicon, about 4–11x faster in wall time with roughly half the peak memory. Windows and Intel macOS keep running tsgo because tsrs ships no binary for them. `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo` forces tsgo anywhere (for example to compare a suspected tsrs bug), and Full Release Validation sets it, so every release is still checked by tsgo. On this host, `pnpm tsgo:all` took 64s with tsrs and 447s with tsgo.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/run-tsgo.mts` is the single owner of type-check execution, so the switch is one resolver change there: it now asks `resolveRepoToolBinPath` for `tsrs` (resolved through the package's own `lib/getExePath.js`, like tsgo) unless the host has no tsrs binary. tsrs takes the same flags the runner already passes (`-p`, `-b`, `--incremental`, `--tsBuildInfoFile`, `--declaration false`, `--singleThreaded`, `--checkers`, `--pretty false`) and prints tsc-format diagnostics, so the CI static-evidence parser and exit-code contract (0 clean, 2 diagnostics) are unchanged.

tsrs is pinned exactly to `0.16.0-ts7.1.0-dev.20260929` (`Version 7.1.0-dev.20260930.4 (tsrs 0.16.0-ts7.1.0-dev.20260929, microsoft/TypeScript@b85298b6a81f)`). It was published 2026-10-16, inside the 7-day `minimumReleaseAge`, so `pnpm-workspace.yaml` gets a time-boxed exclusion for it and its platform packages (remove after 2026-10-23T16:59Z). The version-specific, time-boxed dependency-policy exception is maintainer-approved; the seven-day minimum remains unchanged for other packages.

Kept on tsgo (`typescript@7.1.0-dev.20260928.1`), because these are not the repo type-check lanes:

- declaration emit (tsdown dts, `native-declaration-emitter`, plugin-SDK boundary dts);
- `check-plugin-sdk-exports`, which smoke-checks a consumer against those tsgo-emitted declarations;
- `check-tsgo-core-boundary` file inventories;
- `tsgo:profile` and ordinary `--pprofDir` / `OPENCLAW_TSGO_PPROF_DIR` requests, which require Go CPU/heap profiling. Prepared profiling args automatically select tsgo; explicitly forcing tsrs with this Go-only flag fails with an actionable message rather than losing the profiles.

`@typescript/native-preview` is no longer a direct dependency on main; it only appears as an optional peer of `rolldown-plugin-dts`, so there was nothing there to remove. Script names, `[tsgo]` log prefixes, `ci-static:tsgo` evidence and `.artifacts/tsgo-cache` are unchanged to keep the diff reviewable; renaming them belongs in a follow-up if this lands.

`resolveTypeCheckTool` (`scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts`) owns the choice: tsrs where it ships a binary, otherwise tsgo. `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo` forces tsgo, and an unknown value or `tsrs` on an unsupported host fails with the next step. `ci.yml` sets `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo` only for `full-release-validation-*` dispatches, so the release's `normal_ci` child runs every type lane with tsgo. PR and main CI use tsrs. Evidence reuse only reuses earlier Full Release Validation runs, so it keeps that tsgo pass.

Native runner fixtures install the selected checker (`materializeTypeChecker`), and `overrideNativeFixtureExecutable` intercepts both native packages. Declaration consumer fixtures now include tsrs through their existing physically private package materializer, including its installed optional native dependency; Go still emits their declarations.

## TS5115 errors: what they were and how they are fixed

tsrs 0.16 reported `TS5115: Instantiations of the following types appear infinitely circular` on five graphs where our pinned tsgo (`7.1.0-dev.20260928.1`) reported nothing. They are **not tsrs-only**. Current TypeScript nightly `7.1.0-dev.20261018.1` reports exactly the same errors on our code and on minimal repros, so the next tsgo bump would have hit them too. tsrs ports TypeScript at 7.1.0-dev.20260929; our pinned tsgo is one nightly older. Both patterns are valid TS that TS 7.1 stops at its instantiation depth limit, and both now pass on tsrs, pinned tsgo and the nightly:

- **zod v4 `z.record(z.string(), z.json())`** (`IsOptionalIn`, `$ZodTypeInternals`, `$InferZodRecordInput`): three lines from `import { z } from "zod"; z.record(z.string(), z.json())` reproduce it. The codex plugin now has one explicitly typed `jsonValueSchema` / `jsonObjectSchema` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/json-schema.ts`), the same lazy union `z.json()` builds. Its three callers use it.
- **postcss-selector-parser's `type Selector = _Selector<Selector>`** (`Container`, `Diff`): any property access, narrowing or structural comparison on `Selector` or the `Node` union reproduces it. The library's types are not ours to patch without a dependency-patch approval, so the two CSS audit scripts no longer touch `Selector`-typed values:
  - `audit-control-ui-dead-css.mts` parses each `rule.selectors` entry into its own `Root`.
  - `control-ui-icon-grid-fit.mts` prints the parent selector in place of `&` instead of splicing cloned nodes, which is equivalent because the result is only stringified and reparsed.
  - It checks compound edges with the library's `isCombinator` guard on an `unknown` sibling.

  Both audits print byte-identical output before and after on the real Control UI CSS.

I also built tsrs from source and tried tsgo-main's fix: publish an interface's own members before resolving its bases. That clears both patterns but loses 2 tsrs conformance passes against the pinned TypeScript baselines (`keyofUnresolvedBaseMembers` and `keyofGenericExtendingClassDoubleLayer`). Since current TypeScript nightly reports these errors too, they are TypeScript 7.1 behavior, not a tsrs bug to file.

## Compatibility and adoption risks

- The maintainer-approved exact-version release-age exception expires after 2026-10-23T16:59Z; the rest of the seven-day dependency policy is unchanged.
- Windows and Intel macOS retain tsgo because tsrs has no released binary for them. Resolver/fallback behavior is unit-tested; no real Intel Mac run is claimed.
- tsrs is a 0.x compiler and its upstream conformance report still lists diagnostic differences, including missed errors. Full Release Validation retains a full tsgo pass as the backstop.

## Evidence

### Landing correction and verification

- Landed as `4693fb922454aaf9c96bd76145fd4078e145ecb8` from reviewed head `4bf735702243edaeb5943121064f426faaf56d8c`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39174293081) completed successfully: all 168 jobs passed.
- Incorporated main `53bcf5095e7` through native baseline materialization to include actual CI repairs. Prior `efa78ef2` CI passed the SDK consumer and UI performance jobs, but failed stale formatter and quiet-Discord test expectations. Main `ec50e320498` already corrects quiet Discord; this PR repairs the formatter test to run the real package script rather than require a direct `oxfmt` binary. All 68 formatter-lane tests pass under `CI=1` (~41s test time, including real formatter parity); 125 focused compiler/formatter tests and `pnpm tsgo:scripts` pass on the current candidate. Full independent current-candidate review found no actionable P0-P2 issue.
- Follow-up CI on `c532196a` completed 169 jobs: formatter and quiet-Discord checks passed, but chat boot was 230 B above the unchanged cap (base and candidate both 1,490,230 B), and a Crabbox cancellation fixture timed out. This candidate incorporates the already-landed UI repair [#176551](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176551), not a budget increase or a new UI change. The cancellation fixture now starts the retained acquisition first and waits for actual abandonment-listener admission; its prior probe barrier did not establish a second waiter and could deadlock. All 36 tests pass under both Node and pinned Bun; extension-test types, targeted lint/format, and an independent review pass. A full independent review of final `4bf73570` also found no actionable P0-P2 issue.
- The formatter-only direct-main repair was rejected by repository rule GH013 (pull request required); the same reviewed repair is included here. No policy, budget, retry, skip or expected-failure relaxation.
- Compiler selection and metrics provenance use the prepared invocation environment, not ambient process state. Both owning-boundary regressions failed before the correction and pass afterward.
- The real prior CI failure was an SDK declaration consumer fixture missing tsrs. Adding tsrs to its existing private package materializer fixes both SDK and unified consumer toolchains. The existing nominal-identity integration test failed on exact incoming `e5f9a1959f3` and passed on repaired `4cd5f27f` through `pnpm test:ci-failed 39167057750 --run`.
- Preserved ordinary Go profiling: both explicit `--pprofDir` and `OPENCLAW_TSGO_PPROF_DIR` select tsgo. A real wrapper smoke previously exited 0 without profiles; with the fix it writes CPU/heap profiles and records the Go compiler version. Explicit tsrs plus Go-only profiling rejects loudly. The new routing/provenance regressions were red before the fix; 57 focused runner/policy/metrics tests now pass.
- Production/test lint, formatting, `pnpm tsgo:scripts` and `git diff --check` pass. Independent full repaired-candidate review accepted the working-tree repair and identified only the old staged snapshot; the fix is now signed/committed and index/worktree are clean. Independent review of the one-line fixture package addition found no P0-P2 issue.
- Earlier full `pnpm tsgo:all` and 16 targeted consumer files passed on `e5f9a1959f3`; that evidence is reused only for unchanged inputs. New profiling and SDK fixture paths have their own proofs above. Native baseline integration retained main's proc-safe 0.4.1 update and exact tsrs age exclusions.
- The previous CI run also hit an inherited UI absolute size ceiling: its actual tested base `436a13161083acc34ae06904a68422c955258205` and candidate both measured 1,494,580 gzip bytes, +0, over the unchanged 1,490,000-byte limit. Historical scheduled-main job [117795289336](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39168070659/job/117795289336) also fails that ceiling (1,494,544 bytes). This is not a claim that the old run was inherited-only: its SDK fixture defect was real and has been repaired. No UI budget is raised by this PR.

**Local proof limitation:** broader local SDK/unified declaration suites have five synthetic-plugin selection failures (`plain` / `fixture-a`, or missing expected fixture declarations). One representative fails on the unmodified incoming head too; four siblings were not individually baseline-replayed. They are investigated and retained, not suppressed or described as passing. The exact PR-caused CI case is green; the completed exact-head CI above qualifies the complete repaired head. A local quiet-Discord baseline reproduction on `d390c9c9` timed out waiting for the accepted final answer before reaching its assertion; no local Gateway pass is claimed. Real Intel macOS fallback was not run.

Host: shared 128-core / 187 GiB Linux box (team-metal), base `origin/main` f20ce151e4a, Kysely types generated first (`node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mts`). Each graph ran cold (`-p <tsconfig> --noEmit --declaration false --pretty false`, no incremental cache): one warmup, then 3 timed runs per compiler under `/usr/bin/time -v`. Table values are the median of the 3 timed runs. Binaries were invoked directly: tsrs `@tsrs/linux-x64-gnu/tsrs`, tsgo `@typescript/typescript-linux-x64/lib/tsc` 7.1.0-dev.20260928.1. The 1-minute load average during these runs ranged from 1.8 to 19.7, because other people were using the host. "user CPU" is summed across threads.

title: fix: restore link reader metadata test loading
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the UI test suite fails to load link-reader metadata tests after the retired panel re-export was removed.

Related: #175255 (blocked by this current-main failure; mobile source changes are not included here).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Restores the existing metadata regression coverage without weakening any assertions. No migrations or user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Import the maintained `.tsx` panel implementation directly, as the panel suite already does. The `.ts` alias was intentionally removed in #175236 and stays removed. This is the smallest complete repair: one test import changed; no production changes or new machinery.

Requested and co-authored by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/7b18c037-f7da-487b-8f1b-2864e7f601f2)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b89c95fb-87f1-472b-bc95-7fa248ff6f2a)

## Evidence

- Reproduced on canonical main `0884553208b2d592249d2027833721128a48453c`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/link-reader-metadata.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed during Vite import resolution for `./link-reader-panel.ts` (4.95 s wall time).
- Same command after the import correction: **11/11 pass**, 5.00 s wall time (3.51 s Vitest). Assertions unchanged.

title: fix: queued internal events fail after another session completion
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes queued internal events being rejected as outside the current transcript turn when another completion advances the same session before the event executes.

## User Impact

Queued restart notices and other internal events keep their input until execution without being mistaken for orphaned user turns. External-user eager persistence, source deduplication, current-policy admission, cancellation, and the strict keyed-current-turn guard remain intact. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Internal events now stage input in the existing durable pending-input owner, adopt lifecycle state without prematurely appending that input, and carry its custody into execution. Settlement joins pending-input cleanup. Policy re-admission retains the stable source identity and transport bytes and uses existing completion tracking; it does not create a parallel queue or relax recovery validation.

Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/ad63e3d4-86e4-499d-bd06-4ae3e4b88338)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/3f95955d-0e16-4018-8211-39efd6354b66)

Current-main integration and final verification were completed in the original discussion session.

## Evidence

- Integrated candidate: 160 focused tests pass across event handoff, real SQLite/actor admission, orphan repair, reply preparation, and all five config-policy re-admission scenarios (including a recoverable channel route).
- Three selected strict replay/pending-history tests passed on the preceding candidate; the strict keyed-current-turn guard remains unchanged.
- Core typecheck, changed TypeScript lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent review after the current-main integration reports no P0–P2 findings. Controller migration conflicts preserve the new operation owner and pending-input custody; the redundant mocked wiring test identified by ClawSweeper was removed.
- Current head `4981970ee26a1e29c9be515adafac28b45cc4d05`: real isolated Gateway and OpenClaw embedded harness completed four authorized OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini` turns (response model `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`), with four HTTP 200 responses. Verified queued input absent from the active transcript before execution, durable pending custody, FIFO event-before-announcement execution, settled pending inputs, successful fresh-user continuation, and no keyed-turn/orphan diagnostics. No shared Gateway changes or real-channel messages.
- The experimental live fixture then hit an incorrect display-count assertion (expected four visible assistant messages, observed three). A zero-inference reopened-state check passed: all four replies are persisted across eight raw messages; the existing pre-session-start announcement-pair filter accounts for the three visible replies. It also verified pre-execution cancellation leaves no transcript input or model call. The original failing test result is not relabeled green.
- Exact-head CI run [39159891785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39159891785) succeeded; final read found all 137 check runs completed without failures and the CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses successful.

The real SQLite/actor boundary reproduced the keyed-input failure. The historical full-Gateway baseline did not reproduce overtaking, and cold-process event re-adoption remains unproven. Durable staging is not a claim of automatic replay permission after restart.

The long experimental Gateway fixture is one-off proof evidence rather than routine CI; the real-model current-head proof and zero-inference assertion reconciliation are complete. The shipped change reuses existing state and authority owners (50 production insertions / 11 deletions); no new recovery manager or storage format.

title: feat(ui): show subagents and background processes with progress in session Details
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session Details panel only listed currently running subagents under a generic "Background tasks" heading, with no counts, no finished or failed children, no plan progress, and no background processes at all, so you had to open separate side panels to see what a session had started and how it was going.

## User Impact

User impact: Details now shows **Subagents** and **Processes** as two collapsible groups. Each heading shows observed counts ("2 running · 3 done · 1 failed") and a segmented bar that stays visible when the group is collapsed. Each group previews three rows (live work first, then failures), "Show N more" expands the rest in place, and "All subagents" / "All processes" open the existing side panels. Running subagents show their live headline, elapsed time, and plan steps (2/4) when the observer stream reports them. Groups with nothing to show stay hidden.

Requested by Peter Steinberger (@steipete).

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/2a9c2885-7734-4d83-8203-3a9ea9a209b4)

## Why This Change Was Made

Subagents (agents you steer) and processes (commands you stop) are different things, so they get separate groups instead of one vague heading with nested folding. Details is the at-a-glance view; the Subagents and Processes panels remain where you act (stop, transcript, full output).

- Subagent rows come from the pane's existing hydrated child roster (`listSubagents`, finished children included); settled-state mapping reuses `endedWithoutFinishing`. The transcript's unfinished-only projection is unchanged.
- Process rows reuse the Processes panel's data owner (`ProcessesPanelData` via `useSessionPanel`), polling only while Details is presented in a pane that can open that panel. No new store or Gateway API.
- Plan steps come only from live `session.observer` digests, because session rows do not carry `planProgress`. Accepted limitation: after a reload the step meter is absent until the subagent's next observer update.
- Running state uses `--info` (the theme accent reads as failure in the default palette); pulse/flow animations stop under reduced motion.

## Evidence

title: fix: active chats stay usable after a database worker fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: active chats can stay unable to access their database after an established database worker fails during an operation.

## User Impact

Later commands can recover through fresh database admission instead of inheriting permanently closed references. Failed operations are not replayed, and old worker authority remains invalid. No configuration, schema, migration, retention, or dependency change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing execution owner distinguishes loss of an established native generation from failure to open storage. It settles and retires only the failed native generation, preserving unrelated logical borrowers. Replacement still waits for native exit and lease cleanup and checks the same physical file and current caller authority. Initial protocol/opening failures and explicit revocation retain conservative retirement; terminal adapter notifications are unchanged.

The preceding worker memory-limit event and its allocation trigger remain unconfirmed causes. This repair addresses the independently reproduced recovery cascade, not the original allocation failure. It has not been deployed to Team.

## Evidence

- Real-worker regression: retain two borrowers, terminate an actual worker during a dispatched command, require that command to fail exactly once, then recover the sibling on the same physical file with a new incarnation. Old claims stay invalid. Original production code fails with `Agent database execution admission is closed`; fixed code passes.
- Final focused run: **50/50 passed** across close-wedge, integrity, idle-lifetime, and V2 terminal/settlement tests. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <four files> --maxWorkers=1`: 47.82s command wall; changed close-wedge file bodies 5.930s, revised regression 0.823s. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.
- Core and state-test graph typechecks, four-file type-aware lint, five-file formatting, MDX, and whitespace checks passed. No test budget or assertion was weakened.
- Independent actual-diff review: no findings. Canonical full-context autoreview: scoped-clean P0–P2, confidence 0.90; reviewer did not rerun tests.
- This is synthetic native-worker boundary proof, not a full Gateway/UI reproduction or proof of the original OOM allocation trigger.

title: fix(ui): clear unread state after overlapping read acknowledgments
body:
Related: #148262

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an open conversation can stay unread when newer activity arrives before an earlier read acknowledgment finishes.

## User Impact

The visible conversation acknowledges newer activity after a successful earlier read. Hidden tabs and reconnecting conversations wait until their transcript is presented. Manual unread reminders, access checks, and paced retries during Gateway drains remain unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session row reconciliation publishes before the acknowledgment promise settles. Release the current parent acknowledgment before reconsidering the selected row through the existing visibility/history admission owner. Hidden-run acknowledgments retain their revision-scoped success latch; failed and unsent writes retain existing retry behavior.

This carries forward the remaining behavior and mounted admission regression from the original proposal without replacing the later drain-storm fix. The visibility-return callback now lives beside the session read owner rather than in lifecycle setup. No new state owner, scheduler, or retry mechanism was added.

## Evidence

- Mounted production pane, real session capability, and synthetic Gateway I/O: all three visible/hidden-tab/reconnect-history cases failed on baseline `efe05bcb8b39d7705f6ee5d7767203afced0534f` and pass with the repair. This is boundary proof, not live-deployment qualification.
- Current head `8fe7bd7b03330154812e8266f598deeb291cb915` merges main `b1066a5c49101f28f3cbe4bfd3ca42bc66758036` to resolve actual conflicts. It preserves main’s owner-driven presentation and consolidated tests; no retired redraw path was restored.

title: fix(update): avoid verifying an old build during package replacement
body:
Related: #174373. Follow-up to #173409.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes package `openclaw update --no-restart` reporting a Gateway as verified when it serves the expected version but an older build.

## User Impact

Operators get an advisory and unverified serving status until the expected runtime build is observed. A successful package installation stays successful; this adds no restart, startup wait, or rollback. Existing update-verification fields are used without a schema migration or changes to sessions, messages, configuration, or plugin data.

## Why This Change Was Made

The package-replacement observation omitted the expected build ID even though the shared readiness verifier already checks it. Reuse the restart-enabled path’s selected identity, including an explicitly retained service identity, and forward both version and build ID. For example, installed version V/build B must not certify a still-serving version V/build A.

This does not disable the intentional installation-replacement watcher. Release delivery and native macOS process/SQLite handoff qualification remain separate work in the tracking issue.

## Evidence

- Before the production change: **6 intended regression failures**, covering old and missing build identities for npm/pnpm/bun; the 9 existing control cases passed.

- Final focused proof: **57 tests passed across 2 files** (`update-command-verification.test.ts` and `restart-health-probe.test.ts`), terminal exit 0; runner wall time **26.01s**, reported test-run duration **24.16s**. The readiness file retains its existing ~3-second HTTP-timeout boundary case; new identity cases complete in milliseconds. CI seconds are not yet available.

- Regressions exercise `maybeRestartService` through the real verifier with synthetic native/RPC observations and local HTTP. They check advisory outcomes, confirmation eligibility, build-mismatch report rendering, retained-identity precedence, and absence of updater restart commands. Ledger writes are mocked: this proves the facts submitted for persistence, not a native published-package upgrade.

- Core typecheck and targeted `cli-update` test graph passed. Changed-file lint and formatting, docs inventory, and `git diff --check` passed.

title: fix(process): avoid native report work when cancelling leaf commands
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the first cancellation of a leaf command on Linux can synchronously collect an unnecessary whole-process report even when no adopted child needs reaping.

## User Impact

Leaf-command cleanup no longer initializes native reaping unless a fresh process-group scan finds an adopted direct-child zombie. Existing root wait ownership, live-descendant polling, cleanup budgets, and inspection-before-reap behavior remain intact. No configuration, dependency, or process-identity contract changes.

When native support is unavailable, discovery can now perform bounded procfs scans before finding a candidate, reaching two quiet scans, or reaching the existing deadline. Genuine first native use can still incur initialization work. This does not claim to fix the separately observed seconds-long Gateway stall or make all cancellations faster.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cleanup owner checked native availability before discovering whether native work was needed. Move that check into its eligible-zombie branch, within the existing best-effort error handling. No cache, second cleanup owner, or identity shortcut is added.

## Evidence

- Owning regression suite failed on the original source: **5 failed / 10 passed**. After repair: **15/15 passed**, including deferred admission, delayed adoption, tracked-root/unrelated-child protection, native unavailability and errors, fresh inspection, longer grace, deduplication, and deadline cleanup. Wrapper wall time **20.73 s**, mostly cold compilation; listed test cases totaled approximately **16 ms**.
- Isolated real-command before/after on **Node 26.8.2 with 16 ready idle Workers**: first cancellation **86.90 → 43.67 ms**, heartbeat excess **63.31 → 0.50 ms**, whole-process reports/native loads **1/1 → 0/0**. Output and cleanup assertions were unchanged. Normal exit and second cancellation produced no reports in either version. Second cancellation measured **43.08 → 54.10 ms**; no general speedup claim or hard timing SLA is asserted.
- Real adopted-child proof passed: tracked root exit code **0**, exactly **one native inspection and one reap** of the expected descendant, no other PID inspected or reaped.
- Canonical core and selected test type checks, targeted lint, formatting, diff checks, and fresh independent P0–P2 review passed.
- Estimated incremental CI test execution cost: **<0.1 s**, not a hosted-CI measurement. Exact-head hosted CI run [38941523098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38941523098) completed successfully; the PR merged at `bbbaf48dca2021d3512da2c441e20be5f2a775f6`. title: fix(gateway): skip startup publication checks without a target
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary background GitHub publication checks during Gateway startup and session updates when sessions have no repository workspace or managed worktree.

## User Impact

Sessions without a publication target no longer add avoidable ordered database reads during automatic discovery. Eligible sessions still prepare asynchronously, and explicit publication requests retain their on-demand fallback. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing discovery owner can use resident session binding facts before scheduling preparation. When a binding disappears, deleting its existing discovery entry also makes the existing queued and in-flight guards discard obsolete work and late results. This keeps one owner and preserves FIFO admission, identity checks, expiry, and shutdown behavior.

This is a narrow reduction in unnecessary background work, not a claim to resolve every startup delay.

## Evidence

- Regression before the runtime change: **3 failed, 6 passed** (28.39 s wrapper). Final discovery suite: **10 passed** (23.22 s wrapper), covering targetless startup/updates/invalidations, adding either target type, queued removal, pending removal/rebinding, and existing explicit-demand/lifecycle behavior.

title: fix(x): retain work references on follow-up mentions
body:
Closes #174302

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing native work-session references when a maintainer follows up in an X thread that already started work.

## User Impact

The X front door can identify earlier work before opening another session, without copying private work contents into the thread. This adds context, not automatic routing: continuation still requires an available authorized session tool. Operator-managed front-door instructions that always require a fresh spawn must also be corrected; that live file was outside this task’s write boundary and was not changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing X origin store to supply a small, deterministic set of session references. Match the account, conversation, and originating front door, then apply current session lifecycle and SDK visibility checks. Guidance distinguishes continuation from a new goal and prohibits duplicate-spawn workarounds when continuation is unavailable.

Guest isolation, original reply routing, public-sharing controls, and manual approval for X replies remain unchanged. No new state store, index, permissions, or tools. Production growth is 86 net lines; bounded references reuse the existing metadata owner.

## Evidence

- Regression failed before the fix: the second mention kept the front-door route but lacked its earlier work reference.
- 79 focused X tests passed across six suites in both implementation and parent verification (parent wrapper 42.95s including cold compilation).
- X package and extensions-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, MDX, full build, and both import-cycle checks passed.
- Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings; static review did not execute tests and did not independently verify every unchanged visibility/store dependency. Parent inspected those owner contracts.
- Built X entrypoint imports successfully; initial profiling was unqualified while the candidate was uncommitted. No performance claim.
- Host/network-fixture proof only; no live X post or automatic-continuation claim. References contain only session keys and public origin post URLs, never private titles/transcripts.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes false append-only history warnings, and failures when prompt-cache assertions are enabled, after live tool results are replayed from stored session history.

## User Impact

Operators no longer receive history-rewrite diagnostics caused solely by missing live tool-result run metadata. This does not claim to fix provider-cache misses or improve cache-hit rates. Provider request bytes, immutable replay inputs, and transcript-only hook edits remain unchanged. No configuration, schema, public API, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The persistence owner attached run ownership to stored tool results but not their live counterparts. Extend its existing assistant ownership publication to fresh mutable tool results before hooks and storage cloning. The same guard serves synchronous and awaited appends, without hiding metadata differences in the observer or copying persisted content into live history.

This completes the tool-result sibling of the assistant-envelope repair in #170901.

title: fix(goals): keep pursuing after delegated work finishes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Goals stopping after delegated children finish, even though the objective remains active and the requester produces a normal final reply.

## User Impact

Built-in chat Goals can continue through the normal follow-up queue after child settlement. Pause, Stop, session/Goal replacement, budget limits, pending user input, and unsettled children still take precedence. Independent command runs do not become autonomous.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the original admitted Goal's reply route and live operator restriction across committed child custody. Record the real requester outcome, then return to the existing Goal queue only after the child completion batch commits. Session Stop also revokes retained returns before enqueue, not only queued work.

This is a same-process handoff, not restart recovery. It deliberately does not migrate a retained return across compaction that replaces the session ID or lifecycle revision; the stale-identity check declines that return. No schema, configuration, or permission changes.

## Evidence

- Current reviewed head: `43d0356c12896c1cc32e4f5d3c49142878b8ebbb`, integrated with main `d48d36d7c2053b464b68e5024f3229612ad09eca`. Existing session-controller, cloud Goal, and descendant owners are preserved; controller custody is reserved before asynchronous Goal admission so Stop covers the pre-enqueue interval.

title: improve: make agent credential requests opt-in

## What Problem This Solves Agent credential requests need deliberate operator opt-in and a clear distinction between the agent's request and OpenClaw's surrounding instructions. ## User Impact The entire agent-facing `secrets` tool—request, list, and delete—is **disabled by default**. Operators can add the exact name `secrets` to `tools.alsoAllow` or an existing restrictive `tools.allow` list, globally or per agent. Wildcards and broad groups do not opt in; normal profiles, provider policies, and denials still apply. Removing opt-in blocks new requests. An already-admitted, still-live form requires an explicit save by a currently authorized human; removing the grant alone does not cancel it. Cancel the original run or request to invalidate the form. The credential form follows the command-approval design: an agent identity header, one neutral inset for the credential name/reason and masked value, editable outbound hosts, a visible replacement warning, and compact Skip/Save actions. Secondary storage guidance is available through **Credential details**. Supported chat channels offer a native **Open form** button, with a working URL fallback for text-only delivery. Settings, the masked CLI, existing credentials, and config SecretRefs remain available. No new config key, schema, credential storage, transport, or authentication mechanism is introduced. Normal Gateway sign-in/session access remains required; a configured hostname is not proof of reachability. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing effective-policy owner records exact opt-in; tool construction and protected Gateway question creation consume it, including after awaited preparation. Shared harness guidance permits suggesting opt-in only when public HTTPS or Tailscale is **already configured**—never automatic enablement, new exposure just to collect a key, or pasting credentials into chat. The UI adapts the [command-approval design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183350) using existing agent identity, icon-button, and popover primitives. The agent supplies **name, reason, and proposed hosts**; OpenClaw supplies the identity sentence, field labels, actions, and secondary details. Repeated generic headings, generated “Provide…” copy, raw session-key narration, and storage boilerplate are removed. The operator can still inspect/edit destinations and see actual prior-store metadata before saving. URL navigation does not answer the request; existing question lifecycle correlation remains intact. Requested by Vincent Koc (@vincentkoc); the explicit opt-in default was requested by Ayaan (@obviyus). The current approval-aligned design refresh was requested by Vyctor Brzezowski (@vyctorbrzezowski). ## Work sessions Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public. - [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7113a88a-142d-45d1-b8be-60bba5c4b463) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b7de32ac-be2d-4a90-be51-41263af9e28a) - [Telegram client verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/89c0d3cf-e418-4345-8cff-644dc5877a75) - [Historical implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/1ce0f32b-ba5e-4265-a973-ad86f878f611) ## Evidence Current head: **c43eb1c9efc2874d0d6e3029bf7d12272ce40799**; integrated base: **310f4102ed85223c74bf613311127898b507440b**. Rebased onto the fetched base above to resolve four conflicts. Both prompt snapshots were regenerated by `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`; no generated text was hand-edited. The existing E2E ownership owner retains main’s read-only-home coverage plus this PR’s credential prebuilt-lane proof. Native discovery retains main’s GitHub-tool-surface/required-human-action cases plus `question-secrets`. No retired owner was restored. **Rebase verification:** 286 backend/prefix/policy/Gateway tests, 184 planner/sharding/native-discovery tests, the focused ownership guard, 49 credential component/page/keyboard tests, and the isolated real credential flow pass. title: fix: stop automatic thinking notices in ordinary channel replies
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary channel replies include an unwanted separate thinking-clamp message when a runtime normalizes the saved thinking preference.

## User Impact

User impact: normal conversations stay free of automatic thinking diagnostics. Explicit thinking/status commands, requested preferences, capability normalization, CLI output, and opt-in verbose or authorized trace diagnostics are preserved. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared diagnostics builder treated clamp metadata as permission to publish a channel message even when diagnostics were off. Restore its existing opt-in gate once for immediate, already-streamed, and queued replies rather than filtering text in individual channels.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, actual reply-runner regressions for embedded and Claude CLI execution returned the answer plus an unwanted clamp payload. Six existing queued/streamed/verbosity cases also reproduced the disclosure.

title: fix(chat): retain replies when transcript publication fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a collaborator’s visible reply disappears when its saved transcript row cannot be read or published to chat.

## User Impact

The reply stays visible through streaming and completion, including later updates to the same saved occurrence. Rows already published successfully do not reappear as duplicates. No configuration, schema, permission, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main already fixes the primary delayed-publication scrollback problem in `1f9022d2af0336ede45b249f259e820e25f0d91b`. This repairs the distinct failure path in that owner rather than applying the older parallel buffering implementation.

The existing occurrence map now records whether history publication succeeded. Failed handoffs remain displayable without undoing durable commitment. A finishing reply is projected after accepted publications settle, using the same occurrence state; normal cleanup still runs immediately and cannot clear a replacement run. Terminal message formatting moves to the existing wire-projection helper. Handled rebuilding/overload failures carry the same failure outcome, and a repeated receipt that later succeeds retracts the live fallback without waiting for another model event.

## Evidence

- Clean-base reproduction failed for both streaming and terminal display loss; the raw terminal content alone incorrectly appeared complete.
- Initial implementation: 227 compiled Gateway tests passed across subscriptions, source projection, commentary history, wire delivery, agent-event lifecycles, error kinds, and control replies. Coverage includes publication failure, a late callback carrying the durable receipt, mixed successful/failed rows, delayed publication, replacement, queued successors, shutdown, and claimed error terminals when persistence finishes before transcript publication.
- Follow-up boundary proof: 106 compiled tests pass across the full subscription, session-broadcast, and session-recovery suites. Rebuilding/overload failures and a successful repeated receipt each failed before their owning repair. Core and affected Gateway test-graph typechecks pass; targeted lint/format and line-cap checks pass. The final simplified paths pass another 12 targeted cases.
- Local `check:max-lines-ratchet` reports three pre-existing, unchanged UI suppressions missing from its baseline (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`); no suppressions or baseline exceptions were added. Both earlier CI attempts (38884768050 and 38888095087) hit session-reset teardown with competing work. Main subsequently fixed the deferred recovery fixture leak in `0fa38d641df`; that concrete fix is now integrated, and the complete 74-test chat file passes. The second attempt also exposed a missed native Talk publication collector type; it now derives the handler result, as does the newly extracted marker-queue test collector. The affected Gateway type graphs and the native Talk consumer test pass. No CI rerun, weakened assertion, or baseline change was used. Final-head CI [38973325173](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38973325173) passed on `032b9079f2b4856d4ebc560471668938f9775a6c`.
- Integrated-main verification: 110 subscription/session-event/recovery cases passed before removing three exact duplicate cases still covered by the recovery table; 74 chat-fixture tests and the native Talk consumer test pass. Both affected Gateway test type graphs, five-file type-aware lint, formatting, and the 15-file line-cap check pass. A fresh integrated-candidate P0–P2 review is clean.
- Independent P0–P2 reviews found claimed-error ordering, handled-reader outcomes, and successful repeated-receipt cleanup; each was addressed with owning-boundary proof, and the complete candidate received a fresh clean P0–P2 independent review. That regression uses an already-admitted, resolved persistence stand-in, not an end-to-end claimed persistence run.
- No live production fault was injected. These are actual Control UI captures with synthetic Gateway events matching the verified before/after server wire frames (dark, 1280×860).

title: fix(line): keep message actions within provider contracts
body:
Related: #117456

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes LINE push and reply messages being rejected when quick replies or actions contain fields unsupported by the selected message surface.

## User Impact

LINE users retain usable buttons and links: invalid quick replies no longer consume the 13-item limit, empty rows disappear, and invalid optional metadata no longer disables an otherwise valid action. No runtime configuration, permission, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the current shared LINE normalizer rather than restore the older delivery implementation. Enforce message-surface action/label rules, keep postback text fields mutually exclusive, and discard invalid optional picker bounds, desktop links, and icon URLs. Opaque callback data remains unchanged; unusable required actions retain the existing visible fallback. The necessary normalization stays in one owner, and push/reply regressions reuse the existing HTTP fixture rather than duplicate transport scaffolding.

Carries forward the useful residuals identified by @steipete in #117456, reimplemented against current main with the current media, retry, and Flex-size handling preserved.

title: fix(agents): keep authorized follow-through working after model fallback
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a requester continuing unfinished work after child tasks settle loses its delegation tools when rate limiting switches it to a fallback model.

## User Impact

Authorized follow-through keeps its OpenClaw session tools after fallback instead of stopping merely because the model changed. Frozen completion reports remain report-only. Existing tool restrictions, operator Stop, and final-effect settlement authority checks still apply. Native collaboration remains disabled for this exception; unsupported CLI backends remain restricted.

This does not fix the separate command-origin final-response → automatic Goal nudge seam, and does not automatically resume paused goals. No configuration, schema, or dependency changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback guard treated every completion input as a frozen result relay. The exception requires an existing private live requester-settle handoff, exact session/model binding, and verified persisted child lineage. An active Goal or provenance text alone grants nothing. Worker-backed lineage preparation stays with the existing policy owner; no scheduler or authority registry is introduced.

The typed host-only mode keeps delegation on OpenClaw's final-effect-fenced tools. Codex native collaboration is disabled on start and resume, including permissive/wildcard policies, and restricted continuations cannot reuse unrestricted loaded threads. Grant readers and cache keys preserve this distinction.

title: fix: omit chat context percentage when its snapshot is unavailable

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now uses the canonical context normalizer, retaining explicit unavailable snapshots instead of discarding them. The Solid footer prefers explicit snapshots across the group, so a legacy row cannot override a real snapshot with larger cumulative billing. title: fix(release): admit near-limit source packs without overflow
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release admission rejects valid near-limit source packs before indexing, and spends unnecessary time searching for deltas in these temporary local packs.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Release admission does less packing work and still accepts sources within its existing raw-byte limits. No release publication, dependency, configuration, or worker-isolation changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the zero-window optimization and allow an additional bounded 1 MiB only for encoded pack output (65 MiB total), covering zlib streams and Git-pack framing for at most 8192 objects. Raw limits stay at 16 MiB per object and 64 MiB aggregate; other Git output caps remain 64 MiB.

Replaces #160821 on current main because its old baseline conflicts with the current admission fixture. The replacement preserves main's tooling-source selection and fixture changes rather than replacing the contributor branch's ancestry.

Original optimization by @steipete; this repair preserves his contribution and commit credit.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a04f7859-25ce-48c2-8ada-a9b463a0aa9b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/6708f6b9-1265-4482-8a70-4632cd433dfb)

## Evidence

- Real 2262-object tooling closure: default packing 348/351/330 ms, 2,881,768 bytes; zero-window packing 257/235/238 ms, 2,895,474 bytes. Both indexed to the identical object list. This is a narrow packing benchmark, not an end-to-end speedup claim.
- The new synthetic incompressible-source regression exercises the real workflow, source admission, retention, indexing, and isolated registry observation. The original implementation fails with `spawnSync git ENOBUFS`; the repair indexes the greater-than-64-MiB pack successfully while raw bytes remain within the limit.
- Current-main focused boundary/source-integrity selection: 12 passed, 98 skipped in 10.59 s (11.94 s runner wall), including the near-limit regression and existing raw-size rejections. The prior-baseline full touched suite also passed 126 tests; that is historical evidence, not current-head CI.
- Independent Codex P0–P2 review of the full staged replacement: scoped-clean; no actionable findings. Review examined code; the separately executed tests provide runtime proof.
- Targeted current-main changed-file checks passed: scripts and test-root typechecks, lint, formatting, repository ratchets and dead-export scans.
- Simplification keeps the existing command owner and one real-boundary regression. No new production seam, state, retries, timeout changes, dependencies, or baselines. The bounded output option and synthetic fixture account for the necessary code growth.

title: fix(agents): preserve blank lines across read pages
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a lost blank line when an adaptive file read consumes a blank-only page before a long line, including reads starting at an explicit offset.

## User Impact

Read continuations preserve the selected file text exactly, including leading blank lines, without adding separators to cursor resumes. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing consumed-page index, rather than accumulated text truthiness, to join line pages and retain a consumed page when the next page exceeds the call budget. The byte/model budgets and typed line/cursor contract stay unchanged; production code remains the same size.

This is a current-main replacement for #120887, preserving Peter Steinberger’s repair while avoiding its stale conflicting baseline. Based on @steipete’s original implementation and regression cases.

title: fix(ci): let locale refresh catch up without a shared cache
body:
Related: #173193

## What Problem This Solves

Locale refresh can spend hours translating, then lose useful work when source changes before publication.

## User Impact

The finalizer catches up once against fresh canonical main using completed translations from the same workflow run. Unchanged strings are reused, while new or changed strings are translated before strict validation. This narrows the stale window without a shared translation cache.

Continuous source movement, failed workers, unavailable artifacts, or a changed locale roster can still require a fresh run. No automatic cross-run recovery or convergence guarantee is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vincent rejected the original shared-cache design. This replacement removes its translation-cache restore/save steps and cache-write guard exception—not the scanner or warning.

Workers export versioned, zero-fallback translation-memory data through existing same-run, one-day artifacts. The fresh-main finalizer validates the complete source/run/attempt and catalog inventory before writing compatible memory. Current canonical memory/metadata corrections, glossary changes, generator-policy changes and ownership changes discard affected worker data. The existing source-hash planner, forced refresh, strict validation and terminal publisher remain authoritative; later input movement still defers publication.

No shared cache, cross-run download, new GitHub permission, longer retention, or public option. The finalizer receives the workers’ existing provider credentials only for catch-up after artifact admission. Worker source, metadata and Git patches are not restored; dependency setup remains restore-only.

## Evidence

**Current head:** 9acabce7a25991e9fa8548f3908d7d4611786d95

- **Real finalizer-effect proof:** actual YAML admission/step order, restore CLI, unchanged generator/planner and SDK request serialization, strict validation, and shared Bash/Python/Git publisher are connected in an isolated local source checkout. Allowed catch-up sends 21 provider requests containing only changed/new fixture keys; unchanged translations survive, deleted keys disappear, and refreshed bytes are read back from the local automation branch. Canonical corrections and compatible/incompatible full-refresh output are checked—not just command arguments.
- Fork/non-main workflow provenance and failed preflight produce zero provider/publication effects. Foreign-run, unsafe-path and fallback artifacts are rejected by the actual restore CLI before any finalizer provider/publication effects. Legitimate workers run before artifact tampering. Removing run identity admits 21 provider requests, six publication-service calls and a branch, making the negative control fail; removing finalizer force also makes its output assertion fail. Both mutations were restored.
- **Proof limits:** GitHub scheduling, checkout/download, token issuance and PR API are external-service fixtures. Provider fetch/SSE is synthetic and real sockets are blocked. This is production-owner effect proof locally, not live hosted Actions authentication or native GitHub permission enforcement.
- Full boundary suite: **10 passed, 171.35s**; retained fast locale suite: **19 passed, 6.57s**; focused publisher/workflow siblings: **14 passed, 20.16s**. The expensive composition uses the existing CI_PROOF_TEST_FILES release/manual tier, not ordinary PR CI, even on direct edits. Direct local invocation and exactly one complete manual/release owner remain; fast locale contracts stay in PR selection. Routing regression failed before classification, then passed (684ms body, 4.07s file; 5.74s wrapper). No new configs, worker pins or old-test exclusions.
- **Named CI repair integrated:** prior-head [CI 39218128591](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39218128591) failed on the retired SubscriptionDeps.load fixture (TS2353), unchanged by this PR in its tested merge. Integrated canonical fix [833bd279](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/833bd279bd369f20639af13e3f3921da93f77281), preserving both sides of the planner and publisher-helper conflicts. The actual failing Gateway-methods type graph now passes locally. The resulting committed tree matches the independently reviewed complete snapshot e643faa1ff3bcb5d3da88b3234edb6443d8d089a.
- After integration: **four affected boundary cases passed, 104.30s** (allowed publication, foreign-run rejection and both force cases); **19 retained locale cases passed, 7.39s**; **18 publisher/workflow siblings passed, 21.26s**; **four routing/inventory cases passed, 7.30s**. Targeted types/lint/format/diff checks pass. Fresh full-candidate independent review against the integrated main: **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. The unchanged full 171-second suite was not repeated merely for routing metadata; affected real-boundary cases were rerun for the changed publisher helper.
- Prior replacement [CodeQL run 39218128442](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39218128442) succeeded and alert 1128 became **fixed by code removal**, with no dismissal. Its aggregate was neutral for 17 unrun baseline configurations, not full CodeQL coverage. Exact-head [CI 39224610927](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39224610927) succeeded, and [review 39224783295](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/39224783295) accepted the supplied effect proof with no remaining findings or before-merge items. Native replacement recovery merged reviewed head `9acabce7a259` as `ea4ed0909884148cd64d1ee47e9ae100f543ea9e` on October 19 at 08:53:44 UTC. Independent readback confirms the landed tree equals the reviewed-head composition at its actual main parent, main containment, and Vincent’s exact coauthor trailer. [Native completion receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173806#issuecomment-6263443376).
- Actual hosted Actions/provider finalizer execution and the separate generated localization PR remain unfinished. CI seconds for the new proof are unavailable until its release/manual owner executes it.

body:
Related: #173193
Follow-up to #173195.

## What Problem This Solves

The compact Community entry remained in English because completed locale generation was repeatedly withheld after source changes overtook the long-running refresh.

## User Impact

The Community entry, its social-link descriptions, accessibility labels, new-tab notice, and configuration help are translated in all 21 non-English Control UI locales. This also brings the existing generated core and Workboard catalogs to the same source revision, including the newly configured Swedish locale.

No configuration migration, runtime behavior, or layout changes are introduced. The already-landed Community design and its visual evidence remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recover the successful locale workers from the existing workflow instead of repeatedly discarding expensive completed translations. Their artifacts were bound to the successful source/run, digest-verified, restricted to their generated paths, and applied only after their baseline generated objects were confirmed unchanged. No translation text was hand-edited or conflict-merged.

The canonical `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` then regenerated against source `7bf56c8aa5029a1bd2b2d5cba762ea7c2b70362b`, translating only 37 missing source keys per locale. Shared fallback metadata, Workboard translations, and its immutable bundle manifest were produced by the existing generator. This is generated output only; the workflow reuse repair is kept separate.

## Evidence

**Publication route correction:** CI preflight rejected the paired Workboard `translated.json` and translation-memory outputs on this maintainer recovery branch. That pairing is intentionally owned by the trusted locale publisher. No merge request was submitted. The verified data is retained as recovery evidence while the workflow-owned reuse repair is landed; a publisher-created replacement will carry the final output. This PR is not ready to merge.

- Source worker run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38791296668 — all 21 workers and strict validation passed, but publication was correctly deferred for changed inputs. This PR does not bypass that stale-output decision: the outputs were regenerated for the current source above.

- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` passed in 16.9 seconds. An earlier invocation was stopped by the command wall-time limit during host I/O contention; no test failure or passing-replay-as-fix claim.
- Canonical source-hash-aware materialization verified all eight `communityInvite.*` keys plus the configuration label/help across 21 locales: **210/210 matching translations**, zero fallback metadata. Placeholders remain checked by the canonical verifier.
- `git diff --check` passed. No source/generator changes or baseline exceptions are mixed into the generated-data PR.
- Independent autoreview covered the complete generated delta in 47 bounded passes and returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. Exact-head CI remains required before landing. No new tests were added: the existing generator/parity checks protect this generated-data contract.

title: feat: localize public conversation controls
body:
Related: #113105

## What Problem This Solves

Public conversation readers stay in English even when a visitor’s browser or saved Control UI preference selects another language.

## User Impact

Reader controls, notices, counts, copy buttons, and refresh/access states follow the saved language or browser language, with Arabic/Persian RTL layout. Conversation titles, messages, tool names, code, and filenames are unchanged. No login, additional request, translation-service call, or saved public transcript is introduced.

Missing translations fall back to English. The initial no-JavaScript document remains readable in English. This source PR registers reader copy with the existing post-merge translation workflow; generated locale memory remains separately owned by that workflow.

A pure shared locale policy replaces the UI-only matcher. title: fix(x): failed requests are posted as public X replies
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the bundled X channel posts failure replies publicly (for example "session creation failed: 'X runtime not initialized'... please resend") when an X mention's request could not be completed.

## User Impact

User impact: X receives only replies the agent declares successful. Failed, untagged, and error replies never reach X. With `channels.x.failureRoute` set, OpenClaw sends a notice with the post URL, the author's handle, and a redacted summary to that channel; without a route the reply is dropped and logged.

**Behavior change:** a reply without `[[x_success]]` is withheld instead of posted. If a model forgets the tag, a good answer is withheld too, but it stays visible in the log or the failure route. To send failures to a Discord channel:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    x: {
      failureRoute: { channel: "discord", to: "channel:1456744319972282449" },
    },
  },
}
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The deleted tweets were ordinary model prose, not `isError` payloads, so filtering on the error flag alone would not have stopped them. The X channel's prompt guidance for replies (`agentPrompt.inboundFormattingHints`) now asks the agent to start every reply to a mention with `[[x_success]]` or `[[x_failure]]`. The monitor's `preparePayload` already decides automatic X delivery, so it now reads and strips the tag and posts only declared successes. This fails closed because the public post is the risky effect. I used a tag rather than a report-failure tool because it adds no model round trip, works with every harness, and is checked where the post actually happens. Once a turn declares failure, later replies in that turn are withheld too. `isError` finals are withheld and routed, and `NO_REPLY` and empty finals are dropped.

`failureRoute` takes `{ channel, to, accountId? }` and is rejected if it targets `x`. Reports go through core `sendDurableMessageBatch` on a best-effort basis, and the result is logged. The summary passes through `redactSensitiveText`, is capped at 500 characters, and has `@` defused so model text cannot ping the channel. Message-tool sends, which are the manual posts from work sessions, refuse `[[x_failure]]` and strip `[[x_success]]`; untagged manual posts still go out.

**Config surface:** `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` channel budget goes from 4035 to 4043. The 8 new paths are `failureRoute` with `channel`, `to`, and `accountId`, at the channel level and per account. Requesters explicitly asked for a configurable failure destination, and the per-account variant follows the existing X account-override shape.

The "X runtime not initialized" error itself was fixed separately in #173667 (@obviyus). This PR is rebased on top of it and does not touch that code path.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/x --maxWorkers=1`: 21 files and 242 tests passed on the rebased head. The new `monitor-outcome.test.ts` drives the real monitor delivery adapter. The fixture now follows core's rule that a `preparePayload` returning `null` suppresses delivery.
  - Negative control: with the X sources restored from `origin/main`, the verbatim deleted tweet gets posted (`api.reply` is called once), a declared failure gets posted, and a success gets posted with the literal tag. With this change, the failure is withheld and logged as `reason=unclassified route=none`, the declared failure goes to `discord channel:1456744319972282449` with the redacted summary, and the success posts without its tag.
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/channel-run-admission.x-recovery.test.ts` passes (7) on top of #173667.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files, `pnpm config:channels:gen`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` are all clean. Local `autoreview` (P1) on the outcome logic found nothing actionable.
- Gaps: nothing was posted live to X or Discord. The dedicated `x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts` tier is outside default CI and refuses to prepare on this Team host because a managed Gateway runs there. Its expectations are updated so denied work-session replies are withheld, but the tier was not run.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen and @joshavant.

title: fix(ui): Recent chats timestamps wrap and misalign in narrow panes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Recent chats timestamps on the welcome / New Session screen wrap onto two lines ("32m / ago") and drift off the shared right edge when the pane is narrow and a row has a long title plus a checkout subtitle.

## User Impact

User impact: every Recent chats timestamp stays on one line, flush right, in every row; long chat titles and checkout subtitles truncate first to make room.

## Why This Change Was Made

The timestamp was an ordinary shrinkable flex item, so its one-line rendering depended only on `white-space: nowrap` surviving the cascade. Once anything allowed that text to wrap, the row squeezed the timestamp to its narrowest word. The timestamp now opts out of shrinking (`flex: none`), right-aligns, and uses tabular numerals, so the name and subtitle are the only parts that give up width.

## Evidence

Before (narrow 320px Recent chats column, inherited text wrapping allowed):

![Before: Recent chats timestamps wrap onto two lines](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc654c86-6c49-44a6-b22a-a8ec908b877d)

After (same state):

![After: Recent chats timestamps stay on one right-aligned line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c6e9cad-2fd4-4037-8741-e7ad84c80e0d)

- New E2E `keeps recent-chat timestamps on one right-aligned line in a narrow column` (`ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.responsive-welcome.e2e.test.ts`): asserts every timestamp is one line, unclipped, and shares one right edge, and that the long title truncates instead. It fails on `main` (`"just now"` renders 37px tall, two lines) and passes with this change; the whole file passes (6/6).
- `oxfmt --check`, `stylelint` on the touched files: clean.
- Limitation: on stock `main` in headless Chromium the timestamps already stay on one line, because `white-space: nowrap` holds; the reported two-line rendering needed wrapping to be re-enabled on that text (as in the user's screenshot). The regression test reproduces that failure mode directly.

Fixes: the chat header **Share** button's icon sits above the label with no gap, and its hover background is taller than the neighboring **Layout** button.

## User Impact
