title: fix(x): public X requests fail to start sessions with "X runtime not initialized"
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: public X requests that ask Roboclaw to start a session fail with "X runtime not initialized" when the agent's model provider runs through a plugin.

## User Impact

User impact: authorized X mentions can open visible child sessions again. Authorization is still rechecked live, and requests are still rejected when access is revoked or the X plugin is unloaded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent tools start while the provider's response stream is being consumed, so they run inside the provider plugin's instance scope. The X publication authorization callback, which ingress keeps for later, then looked up the X runtime in the provider plugin's slot and found nothing. Ingress now binds that callback to its owning plugin instance when it is created, using `wrapCurrentPluginInstance` like the other retained plugin callbacks. The authorization recheck itself is unchanged.

<details><summary>Production trace and regression origin</summary>

On 2026-10-16 at 01:58:54 and 02:00:23 UTC, two X front-door runs failed in `sessions_spawn` → `ChildSessionPublication.assertCurrent()` → X monitor authorization → `getXRuntime()`. The retained callback path came from #171384. The earlier end-to-end coverage ran `spawn.execute` outside any provider stream scope, so it never hit this ordering.

</details>

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts` now registers a second (provider) plugin instance and runs the real `sessions_spawn` inside `runPluginStreamConsumer` for that provider, matching agent-core's production ordering.
  - Without the fix: fails with the exact production error `X runtime not initialized`.
  - With the fix: passes, including the revoked-access and unloaded-plugin cases.

title: fix(message): retain local final replies in conversation history
body:
Related: #186688
Related native-completion work: #111020, #174490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing conversation-history answers when a local message-tool send delivers the current turn's reply, including Discord's prepared core-delivery path.

## User Impact

Confirmed source answers are persisted and made available to context-engine consumers in the accepted-turn range, and prevent unchanged answered requests from being re-injected as recent channel history. Downstream capture still depends on each consumer selecting the answer from that range. Explicit final replies and the normal omitted-final default retain terminal evidence; progress and the existing run-level default-false override remain nonterminal. Failed/partial delivery, dry runs and other destinations do not mark the source answered.

This repairs the persistence portion of #186688, not native Codex interruption. Native completion remains separate; no configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [installation report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187795#issuecomment-6512626002) correctly identified that the initial patch covered only plugin-action fallback, while ordinary Discord sends use prepared core delivery. Move local source persistence to their common settled-send boundary, reuse the existing mirror owner, and persist the actual delivered payload after preparation/hooks. Gateway-owned source persistence stays with its existing RPC owner.

Use the harness's existing finality resolver for transcript evidence and forward its existing run-level default override. This changes no native completion policy and introduces no new state owner.

## Evidence

- Red before repair: the real shipped Discord preparation/outbound adapters, with only network I/O substituted, delivered both explicit-final and omitted-final messages but persisted zero assistant answer rows. Both regressions pass after this repair.
- Composed proof exercises the real message tool, canonical SQLite transcript, accepted-turn outbox and commitTurn consumer, then recent-history reconciliation. It verifies delivered content, source-turn/tool-call identity, terminal versus progress behavior, run-level default override, and failed-send handling. Fallback-plugin cases retain receipt-replay and failure/partial/suppressed/dry-run/other-recipient controls.
- Final candidate: 13 focused files / 290 tests passed (80.57 seconds runner wall time), including source matching, destination history, outbound contracts, shared finality and prompt-prefix stability. This is the selected repair scope, not a full repository test run.
- Agents-tools test typegraph, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, test-line budget and diff checks passed.
- Simplification replaces fallback-only persistence with one shared local settlement call. Gateway RPC retains its separate transport boundary and the same mirror owner. Against the base, production changes are +84/-27 lines; the 442-line integration allocation covers producer-to-capture composition and distinct controls.
- Bound Auto Review completed on base `53071cea572c54568f76c0f487403528bf46508c` and candidate tree `986cf3c944fd5eaa594e573a8f979a00c441745b`: `scoped-clean`, no findings at its P0-only threshold. This is not a review clearance for lower-priority defects. Tests were independently executed by the implementer, not rerun by the reviewer. The reporter-provided live validation below is separate from this review.
- Implementer-run live Discord readiness failed at QA lease acquisition; the implementer did not verify live Discord transport, native Codex completion, or a third-party Universal Capture installation. The local capture assertion uses the real commitTurn boundary with a synthetic consumer.
- Reporter-provided live validation: [lastguru-net’s October 30 follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187795#issuecomment-6530379567) tested the ten-file patch from `7b06dd03108b1e53871c9875e63c25b5822e0579` on main `5f6f15fed0d6ba618cf781c9686a8b93f499564b` with a real Discord/native Codex-backed agent. Explicit `final:true` sends (turns 72–74) and an omitted-final send (turn 75) each delivered one visible answer, persisted exactly one canonical final delivery mirror, and stopped the answered requests from recurring in subsequent history. Ordinary-final turns 70, 71 and 76 served as controls. These are the reporter’s observed results, not an implementer-run live test.
- Separate consumer limitation: the same report reproduces Universal Capture 0.7.1 with `commentary:false` omitting the already-persisted answer because its selector reads only the last row. The valid order is `user → assistant toolCall → assistant final delivery mirror → toolResult`; the accepted-turn contract does not require the assistant answer to be the last row. This consumer-side selection bug is outside this PR and is not evidence of continued canonical answer loss. Native Codex interruption also remains unchanged and separate.
- Hosted [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41088039623/job/124180953526) passed on `7b06dd03108b1e53871c9875e63c25b5822e0579`; its prerequisite results contain only success or unselected/skipped jobs, with no failures or timeouts.

title: fix: preserve failure causes after repeated warnings
body:
Related: #155378. This is a small existing-limit fix, not a replacement for @freeqaz-openai's broader diagnostics draft.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes failed-request notices losing their terminal error reason when repeated launcher warnings fill the beginning of the diagnostic.

## User Impact

Users retain both initial context and the terminal diagnosis in the saved failure notice. The existing 512-character diagnostic limit and 160-character session-row limit remain unchanged, and redaction still happens before truncation.

This does **not** repair the host's jemalloc profiling setup or establish why every affected request failed. There are no configuration, schema, permission, retry, or failure-settlement changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session rows already retain the beginning and end of long errors, while saved failure notices keep only the beginning. Reuse that UTF-16-safe truncation policy for both surfaces instead of introducing another formatter, increasing retention, or suppressing warnings. Short errors and specialized storage-failure guidance remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the production change, the focused Gateway regression run failed three assertions: the allocator-warning tail, the long Unicode-context tail, and the redacted upload-failure tail were missing from the saved notice. The session row already retained the cause.
- After the fix, `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts src/sessions/session-run-error.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **43 tests** across the Gateway lifecycle/persistence and session-error owner suites. This exercises the real lifecycle writer and persisted failure report, not a precomputed summary.
- Test wall times: Gateway file **66.27 s**, owner unit file **1.66 s**, combined wrapper **71.09 s**. The newly added allocator scenario took **464 ms**; most Gateway wall time was compiler preparation and the existing persistence scenarios. CI timings are not yet available.
- Production typecheck (tsconfig.core.json), focused repository lint on the three TypeScript files, pinned formatter check, staged test-line ratchet, and staged diff check passed. Command-local logs and exit receipts were inspected because the host bridge intermittently failed during post-command finalization with the same jemalloc warning.
- Independent AutoReview was attempted against local changes based on `92d61ac49882c9c8c815cf5d24dbe145a47f4238` at its default P0 scope. **Review is incomplete:** the reviewer command was terminated after repeated jemalloc warnings exhausted its bounded output capture (exit 143, output-limit flag set). There is no clean review verdict. Independent review and broad CI remain outstanding; the requester has asked to open the PR for review.
- Simplification: reuse the existing error-summary owner; no new state, configuration, or parallel policy. Net production growth is four lines; the twelve net regression-test lines extend existing persistence cases and have their own matching allocation record.
- No live-host profiling repair or live model/Gateway/browser end-to-end run was performed. The original incident's full failing operation remains unverified; the narrower diagnostic-loss defect has red/green persistence-boundary proof.

<details>
<summary>Incident report and operator follow-up</summary>

On 2026-10-29, repeated Team webchat errors showed only:

```text
<jemalloc>: failed to open "/var/tmp/jeprof/gw.<pid>.<sequence>.u<sequence>.heap"
```

The reported payload was exactly 512 characters and matched a prefix-only cut through the repeated warnings. An independent tiny exec command returned exit code zero with both expected stdout/stderr markers while its captured output also contained 17 fresh profile-open warnings. Warnings therefore do not, by themselves, prove that jemalloc caused the request failure.

An inspected sandbox Node process had neither jemalloc environment settings nor a jemalloc mapping, although warnings appeared before its output. The emitting executable in the host-side launch/bridge chain still needs to be identified. The profile directory was absent inside the sandbox; this does not establish its existence or permissions on the host or in a service-private filesystem namespace.

The operator should inspect the actual emitting process's profiling configuration and hooks. Disable unintended profiling, or provision a private service-writable profile directory in the correct namespace with bounded retention if profiling is intentional. Keep jemalloc itself if it is deliberately used as the allocator. Do not create a world-writable profile directory or treat a sandbox-only directory as a host fix.

The same warning flood reproduced an actual helper failure during independent AutoReview: the helper exceeded its bounded output capture and was terminated. This establishes one failure mechanism in this investigation, not the retrospective cause of every reported request failure.

Correlate one actual failed request with the complete Gateway/helper error, process identity, exit status or signal, and effective profiling configuration. This separates profiling-caused failures from unrelated failures hidden behind profiler output.

</details>

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2d7b1559-ad3a-426d-90ee-61017f75b592)

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

title: fix(ui): Try again posts a visible continue message and keeps the failure notice
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking **Try again** on a failed reply in the Control UI posts "Continue from where you stopped. Check which actions already completed before retrying anything." into the chat as if the user had typed it, and the "Unable to finish this reply" notice stays above the continued answer.

## User Impact

User impact: **Try again** now simply resumes the reply. The failure notice goes away, the agent continues from the existing conversation, and nothing is posted on the user's behalf. This holds after a reload and for other viewers of the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The continuation becomes a Gateway-owned hidden input, using the same trusted internal chat path the Gateway already uses for agent onboarding and progress-card refreshes:

- New `chat.retry` method (`operator.write`, session write access). It accepts only the session's latest `failed`/`timeout` run (optional `sessionId` fence, like `chat.abort`), then admits the existing continuation prompt as `internal_system` input with `display: false` and `provenance.runId` naming the failed run. The ack is the normal `chat.send` ack.
- `chat.history` drops the failure notice of a run that has such a retry input, so the notice stays gone after reload.
- The Control UI calls `chat.retry`, hides the notice immediately, and adopts the new run; on a rejected request it restores the notice and shows the error. The model-facing prompt is no longer a localized UI string.

Accepted edge cases: a history page that ends exactly between a failure notice and its retry input still shows that notice when scrolling back; in a streak of identical notices from different runs, only the retried run's notice is removed.

## Evidence

Before/after screenshots follow (synthetic Control UI e2e Gateway, 1160×760, light theme, captured right after clicking **Try again**).

**Before** — the continuation posts as a user message and the notice stays:

![Before: Try again posts a visible continue message under the failure notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94c9aff8-5748-4deb-bcb8-f14ea7b2d3b0)

**After** — the notice is gone and the reply resumes in place:

![After: Try again resumes the reply with no visible message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14e5bbd1-d7dd-4d18-810f-f09829619d0b)

- New Gateway integration test `src/gateway/server.chat-retry.test.ts` (real Gateway, mock OpenAI Responses provider): the first run fails on every attempt; `chat.retry` starts a run whose model request contains the continuation; `chat.history` afterwards has no failure notice, no continuation text and only the original user message; retrying the same run again is rejected.
- `chat-display-projection.test.ts`: a retry input retires only its own run's notice. `chat-run-failure-streaks.test.ts` and `chat-pane-state.test.ts` cover the optimistic hide and the one-retry guard. `chat-retry-failure.e2e.test.ts` now asserts `chat.retry` is sent, the notice detaches, no `chat.send` is made, no continuation text appears and the draft is kept.
- Passing: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm protocol:check` (registry, Swift/Kotlin models, since-train), format check, `src/gateway/methods`, `packages/gateway-protocol`, and the full `ui/src/pages/chat` suite (5769/5770; the one failure, `chat-html-preview-element.test.ts`, passes alone on this branch and on `main`).

title: fix(sessions): chat looks like it restarts working right after a turn finishes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished chat turn shows the working timer and Stop button again a second later, as if the agent restarted, when OpenClaw runs its post-turn memory flush or compaction on that session.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski with a screen recording from Control UI.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d80a929c-8ab0-4230-b56e-4acef2fed362)

## User Impact

User impact: once the reply finishes, the session stays idle in chat and in the sidebar while background upkeep runs. Upkeep itself is unchanged: it still runs, still yields to a new foreground turn, and still blocks a competing session mutation as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

After a turn, optional session maintenance admits its own controller turn on the user's session so it can safely flush memory and compact. The Gateway's active-run projection counted any unfinished controller operation without a `projectSessionActive: false` attachment, so `hasActiveRun` flipped back to true for the length of that upkeep. In the reported case a memory-flush preparation took about 6 seconds, and Control UI showed a running turn for exactly that window.

`withSessionTurn` can now pass the existing `projectSessionActive: false` presentation fact to its mailbox source, the same flag already used for other hidden work. Optional maintenance sets it. Admission, mailbox ownership, cancellation and writer locking are unchanged; only the presentation of that operation changes.

## Evidence

- **Production trace:** the gateway log for the recorded session shows the turn's final reply at 13:45:10 UTC, then at 13:45:13 a controller turn on the same session, a 5.7s managed-worktree preparation and a `memory flush skipped` at 13:45:19. The recording shows a working timer counting from 1s to 7s with Stop over the same interval, with no new transcript entry.
- **Regression test** (`src/agents/session-maintenance/run.test.ts`): it schedules real optional maintenance against a real SQLite session, holds the flush, and asserts `resolveVisibleActiveSessionRunState(...).active === false`. Red without the flag (`expected true to be false`), green with it.
- **Related suites:** `session-controller.admission.test.ts`, `session-controller.mailbox.test.ts`, `gateway/server-methods/session-active-runs.test.ts` and all of `agents/session-maintenance/`: 101 tests pass.
- **Gates:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean on the touched files.
- **Local review:** autoreview (codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium) in branch mode on base `de25af72ff5` → head `27b42ac2d05`, with the P0–P2 range. Result: scoped-clean, no findings.
- **Gap:** I could not run a live Gateway reproduction on this host. The gateway e2e harness (`vitest.e2e.config.ts`) times out before the first provider request here, and the existing `gateway.compaction-hot-reload.e2e.test.ts` fails the same way. So the test above proves the invariant at the Gateway projection the UI reads (`chat.history` / `sessions.list` → `hasActiveRun`), not through a browser.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:e689b1ed-e7da-44fd-b2de-31797845dbbf -->

## Maintainer verification

- Rechecked exact head `55fd1a890534a31b340463c60c49922d6013099c` on tempbook: 101 tests pass across maintenance, controller admission/mailbox and Gateway active-run projection (60.31 seconds across four test shards). The new regression itself took 564 ms.
- Negative control: removing only the maintenance visibility flag fails the new regression with `expected true to be false`; three sibling cases pass. Original source restored without changes.
- Targeted lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Fresh independent Codex review of the full branch and relevant owners found no P0–P2 issues. Existing tests cover foreground preemption, operational cancellation and settlement; the new test covers scheduling through the real SQLite/controller/projection boundary. No live browser replay was added.

## Risk and coverage

The flag changes presentation only. Maintenance keeps its controller, writer admission and cancellation; new foreground turns retain default visibility. The change adds seven production lines and 25 test lines using existing setup.

CI run [40888085151](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40888085151) remains failed: the only non-aggregate failure is `agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts > passes explicit timeout overrides into agent attempts`, which expected 600000 ms and observed 599999 ms. The fixture froze the wall clock but not the monotonic clock used by the budget. Its test/helpers and budget source are byte-identical between baseline `36383b8` and tested merge `2d778d9`. This independent fixture defect is already repaired on main by [#187763](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187763), commit `6676a9d8022`. Landing uses the attributed pre-existing CI exception; it does not claim that failed CI passed.

title: fix(ui): tool-call rows render oversized on iPhone Safari
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: collapsed tool-call rows in chat render at about 20px instead of 13px on iPhone Safari, so a single tool summary dominates the transcript.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/024ddc78-ce29-40c1-8995-fa0c5068b4b3)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/48380edf-f279-4c36-9888-cb8eec279e7d)

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone Safari shows compact tool-call rows again, matching desktop proportions. Desktop browsers receive the same CSS as before apart from one iOS-only declaration.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ui/src/styles/base.css` already locks `-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%` on `html, body` to stop iOS text boosting. Since the Control UI build started targeting `safari26.2` (#168595), the CSS minifier treats the prefix as unneeded and drops it from the production stylesheet. WebKit only implements the prefixed property, so iPhone Safari's text autosizing stayed on in production (the dev server never minified it, which is why it did not reproduce there).

iPhone autosizing boosts small single-line text inside blocks that are laid out wider than the screen. Long `white-space: nowrap` tool summaries hit that path; the recent tool-row redesign (#186041) made them prominent, but the boost itself comes from the missing prefix. Adding `ios26.2` to `build.target` (the same 26.2 floor already documented for iOS) keeps the prefix in the built CSS.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`ui/src/app/vite-build.node.test.ts`): builds with the real Control UI Vite config and asserts the output keeps `-webkit-text-size-adjust:100%`. Red on `main` (built CSS was `html{-moz-text-size-adjust:100%;text-size-adjust:100%}`), green with the fix. The 15 tests in that file pass.
- **Full production build diff** (`pnpm ui:build` with and without the change): across all CSS chunks, the only difference is `-webkit-text-size-adjust:100%` restored in the connection/boot stylesheet (+30 bytes). Total emitted JS size is byte-for-byte equal.
- **Deployed build**: the currently deployed Team build's CSS also lacks the prefixed declaration.
- **Real-device measurement** from the reporter's iPhone screenshot (390pt viewport): the tool row text measures about 19.7px against 13px specified, while the composer (16px) and chat body (14px) match their CSS. This is consistent with WebKit's one-line autosizing multiplier for 13px text, which only applies when `-webkit-text-size-adjust` is `auto`.
- **Browser captures**: mobile 390×844 (WebKit, light and dark) and desktop 1440×900 (Chromium) of the Control UI with a long exec tool summary show the intended 13px rows. Linux WebKit does not implement iOS text autosizing, so these show the target rendering rather than an iPhone reproduction. Before/after images were delivered in the originating conversation; I could not embed them here because the publishing identity has no supported image-upload path.
- **Local review**: autoreview (Codex engine, default P0 scope) on `origin/main..HEAD`: clean, no actionable findings.
- **Gaps**: no on-device iPhone check after the fix (needs a deploy). `ui/src/app/vite-config.node.test.ts` does not load locally because `@openclaw/net-policy/redact-sensitive-url` does not resolve in this checkout. That import is in an unchanged module, so this is a local setup issue, and CI covers the file.

title: feat: configure chat attachment file and message size limits
body:
Related: #166757

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot configure incoming chat document size limits independently of media processing budgets.

## User Impact

The new attachment controls are **additional to**, not a replacement for, the existing media option:

- `agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb` stays available and active for incoming **images, audio, and video only**. It does not cap PDFs, text, archives, or other documents. Media files must satisfy both the media cap and the general attachment cap; documents use only the attachment caps.

- `attachments.maxFileMb` — **Maximum attachment size**, default 20 MiB per file.
- `attachments.maxTotalMb` — **Maximum total attachment size per message**, default the larger of 20 MiB and the per-file cap.
- All incoming chat files, including media and duplicate entries, count toward the decoded total. The server rejects an oversized batch before attachment preparation/storage.
- Doctor preserves the old inherited file cap when the new field is absent, retaining explicit attachment settings, media settings, and retention.

The approximately 18.56 MiB WebSocket decoded batch ceiling remains. This does not add streaming uploads or change every channel/outbound document contract. **Not release-qualified:** installed latest-stable upgrade and external live-model proof remain unrun. A real isolated Gateway/agent flow with a deterministic provider now passes.

For example: with media set to 5 MiB, per-file attachments to 10 MiB, and the message total to 15 MiB, an 8 MiB PDF is permitted but an 8 MiB video is rejected. Two 8 MiB PDFs exceed the total. Classification is based on sniffed content, not merely the filename or supplied MIME type.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extends the existing attachment policy/parser and config schema rather than adding a second upload owner. Chat, session, agent/node, companion, worker-transfer, handshake and Control UI consumers use the separate budgets. New labels/help expose the actual scope and MiB units; retention is unchanged.

Simplification retained one policy owner, one batch preflight and the existing Doctor writer, with no new transport, persistence system, or permanent document-limit fallback to mediaMaxMb.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: publishing the current session's own checkout fails with `missing scope: operator.admin` when an explicit checkout path is outside the agent's default workspace.

## User Impact

User impact: authorized users can publish their existing session-owned checkout without administrator access. Unrelated checkouts, missing handoffs, and revoked access remain rejected. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publisher applied new-workspace admission before checking existing checkout ownership. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a user's follow-up starts a separate turn instead of redirecting the active reply when the user has session-write permission in a sandboxed chat.

## User Impact

User impact: eligible follow-ups stay with the active reply. Permission changes and revoked access still prevent steering; no configuration changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The comparison now uses the permissions captured when the original run started, rather than whichever caller happens to perform the comparison. Actual tool execution still checks current permissions and revocation.

Provider inputs are captured at call time, not read from mutable mock arguments afterward.

title: fix(ui): catch empty typing avatars in remote-draft tests
body:
Closes #165045

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: remote-draft browser checks pass when the typing avatar loses its content but its frame remains visible.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The existing direct and group browser cases now reject empty or hidden avatar initials. Shipped-entry-point verification remains outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing remote-draft scenario owns this check. It now requires visible Owner initials with the expected text while preserving the avatar frame's absolute-position assertion. No production renderer or additional test scenario is introduced.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and scope</summary>

The original selector accepts either an avatar or its layout slot. A sized frame can remain visible after its content disappears; pending slots also hide their children without hiding the frame. The new descendant assertion checks the initials themselves, not the wrapper or accessible label. The fixture supplies Owner without an image URL. Both direct and group cases use this checkpoint; image/fallback rendering remains unchanged.

The earlier repair, #173786, was closed without merging. This change independently verifies the content-removal control on the selected base.
</details>

## Evidence

Final local checks: isolated Linux container, supported Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Chromium 156.0.8078.4. All three checkpoint controls were repeated on this runtime for both direct and group cases; the older Node 24.20.0 runs are retained separately. Base `50c3ff63fcd42100dbf0bd0ff677c759ffee3178`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Content removed; original avatar checkpoint | Direct and group both pass incorrectly with empty text and classes/role/name retained. |
| Content removed; repaired checkpoint | Both fail at the expected initials assertion. |
| Content restored; repaired checkpoint | Both pass with visible `O` initials and the placement check intact. |

| Independent source/diff review | Complete, P0–P3, for the full two-file diff at `14fee5abe8df86db19134b893b78c7732a473847`: no findings. Simplification steps 1–3 and slop pass clean. |

The mutation probes temporarily stop immediately after the avatar checkpoint, before unrelated later assertions. Their instrumentation is not committed. These runs exercise the existing browser suite with its fixed-response Gateway fixture; they are not real-Gateway proof. The restored checkpoint on supported Node completed in 17.00 seconds including setup; the full fixed file took 19.00 seconds wall time. CI seconds are pending.

title: fix: goals stop pursuing after a background command completes
body:
Related: #186928, #183705

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an active Goal stops pursuing, with no further continuation turns, after a background command completes and its completion takes the next turn.

## User Impact

User impact: a Goal keeps moving after a background exec completion is delivered as its own turn, including when the command was started by a configured command owner. A completion that was explicitly silent (`deliver: false`) keeps its continuation turns silent too, and pause or Stop during that pursuit is still honored. Continuation turns never gain authority the original requester did not have.

Scope limits: this does not address length/token-limit endings (#186928), Goals created mid-turn (#183705 / #183706), Resume after Stop (#185273, landed separately), or non-built-in harnesses. It is not presented as the explanation for every reported Goal stall.

## Why This Change Was Made

A background exec completion is admitted as a session-event turn. When that turn ended normally, `enqueueGoalContinuation` built the Goal nudge from the event run and inherited its `abortSignal`, `internalEventExecution` settlement hooks, and one-shot `queuedFollowupReplyDisposition`. Instrumentation showed two failures: retiring the settled exec occurrence (the `system-events.ts` cancel path) aborted the queued nudge, and a nudge that survived reused the already-settled one-shot delivery, so its operation ended `run_failed` and cancelled the next nudge. The Goal stayed active with `continuationTurns: 0`.

The Goal successor of a session-event turn now owns three things separately, none of them tied to the event occurrence:

- **Cancellation:** only its own cancellation signal.
- **Delivery:** the session's ordinary routed delivery. An explicitly silent event's restriction is carried as run-owned data (`sessionEventOrigin: { deliver: false }`). Follow-up delivery and background producers honor it.
- **Authority:**
  - The successor stays classified as event-originated. It never mints a trusted current-conversation message-action capability from the event's captured route, and command-owner status is not refreshed from that route.
  - If the event carried its requester's command-owner authority (an owner-started exec), the successor holds only that requester's live owner check under current config, or the live operator source for handoffs. It does not keep the event-occurrence check, which would fail once the event settled.
  - Without such authority, the successor holds none.

Non-event sources are unchanged.

## Evidence

Tests that fail on the earlier code and pass on this head (Gateway goal suite; model mocked, real admission, queue and session-event handoff):

- **Background completion:** "keeps pursuing after a background exec completion / an explicitly silent completion takes the next turn". On `main` `9cb5447` both time out at 120s with the Goal still active. On this head, 4 turns run, the Goal completes with `continuationTurns: 2`, and successors of the silent completion run with `sessionEventDelivery: false`.
- **Real exec producer with a captured owner target** (`prepareExecExitNotification` → `maybeNotifyOnExit`, configured owner `telegram:456`). The previous candidate is `70f8bd4`.

| Case | What it checks | Previous candidate `70f8bd4` | This head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Owner completion | Goal continues; completion turn and both successors run as owner (`senderIsOwner: true`) | stalls (120s timeout; successor admission fails on the settled event) | passes |
| Owner, silent completion | Same as above, plus every successor keeps `sessionEventDelivery: false` | stalls | passes |
| Guest (`789`) completion | Goal continues; no turn runs as owner (`senderIsOwner: false`) | passes | passes |
| Owner revoked before the next successor is admitted | Next successor is refused at admission (before it reaches the model or any tool); exactly 3 model calls; Goal stays active | fails: only 1 owner turn ran | passes |
| Owner revoked after a successor is admitted | Inside the admitted owner successor, the run's real admission assertion (the check the runner hands its tools as `assertInvocationCurrent`) allows an owner-only effect, then refuses the next one once the owner is removed from config. The refusal's cause is `CommandOwnerRevokedError`; no further successor runs | added on this head | passes |
| Stop during the successor of a silent owner completion | `sessions.abort` aborts it; no further turns run; Goal resumes once | stalls | passes |

Limitation of the after-admission case: the guarded "effect" is a test-only action (an array append) behind the production admission assertion, not a production tool's `execute`. How individual tools apply that assertion is covered by their existing tests. Temporarily making the successor's owner check always pass makes this test fail, but by a drain timeout (the Goal keeps continuing) rather than at the effect assertion.

- **Pause:** "does not continue past a pause made during … turn" (normal and silent): passes.
- **Channel authority** (`goal-continuation.test.ts`, "binds channel-turn authority only for successors of …"):
  - Uses the real producer and the real capability mint on a Discord route.
  - On `7d36425`, event-derived successors received a current-conversation capability. On this head they receive none.
  - Control: a user-turn successor's capability resolves to that conversation only. It is refused for another session and after revocation.
- **Silent route:** `followup-delivery.test.ts` "keeps a silent source event's successor off every automatic route". On `e3d85dd` the successor's progress and final reply were routed to the external origin twice. On this head there is no route or dispatcher call.
- **Suite results on this head:**
  - `server.chat-goal.test.ts` 52/52.
  - `goal-continuation` + `followup-delivery` + `agent-runner-utils` 131/131.
  - `session-event-handoff` + `session-event-permissions` 51/51.
  - `check:baseline-ratchets` against `main`: all 9 pass.
  - Typecheck (`tsgo:test:src`), format and changed-file lint pass.
- **Test-line allowance:** this branch now carries `main`'s test-line ceiling (6,320,000, #187162). The earlier ceiling change was dropped when `main` was merged in.

Real Gateway proof: an in-process Gateway using a scripted loopback model, a real `exec` background process with completion wake, and `sessions.abort` for Stop. Delivery restrictions were read from the Gateway's live run registry. The harness is task-local and not part of this diff. Limitation: no external channel was loaded in that Gateway, so suppression of an actual outbound send is proven by the follow-up delivery test above, not by a live external send.

| Case | `main` `9cb5447` | previous head `e3d85dd` | this head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/goal start` → `exec` background → real completion turn → pursuit → Stop | stalls after the completion; Goal active, `continuationTurns: 0` | — | 3 continuation turns; Stop aborts the third and no further turns run; Goal active, `continuationTurns: 2` |
| Same, with the background command started by a `delivery: none` scheduled turn in the Goal session (silent completion) | stalls after the completion; `continuationTurns: 0` | pursuit continues, but all 3 successor runs lose the restriction | 3 continuation turns, all with `sessionEventDelivery: false`; Stop aborts and no further turns run |

title: fix: Shift-selection skips pinned sessions across sections
body:
Related: #186229

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Shift-selection skips intervening pinned sessions and selects later section members when a range crosses Pinned and Sections.

## User Impact

Users can select a contiguous visible range from Pinned into Sections or ordinary sessions, in either direction. Duplicate appearances still produce one batch target; collapsed and archived section members remain excluded. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Selection now consumes appearances in the same Pinned → Sections → ordinary-session order that the sidebar renders. This is a one-line production ordering repair using the existing selection owner, with no new state or flags.

title: chore(installer): add Windows Git selector reproduction fixture
body:
Related: #127352

## What Problem This Solves

The Windows Git installer accepts an explicit `-Tag` but can reach dependency installation on its current branch instead of the requested ref. This PR records a standalone reproduction; it does not fix the installer.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This is a manually invoked diagnostic fixture, not an always-on CI test. It is being submitted for review as reproduction tooling only. Omitted `-Tag`, explicit `latest`, and `-NoGitUpdate` policy remain undecided.

**Decision for Dallin — undecided:** For existing Git checkouts, should omitted `-Tag` preserve the current branch, should explicit `latest` select the published stable release, and how should explicit selectors interact with `-NoGitUpdate`? No default policy is selected by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture uses distinguishable commits in a disposable local Git remote, loads the complete installer through its public parameters, and re-enters the real `Main` dispatcher. It records the selected HEAD at `Ensure-Pnpm` and stops before dependencies, build, wrapper publication, Doctor, or service operations. Clone, pull, checkout validation, and selector decisions remain production code. Only explicit main/tag/missing selectors with updates enabled have contract assertions.

Only `test/scripts/install-git-selector.ps1` is added: +196 test lines and zero production lines. A one-line correction selects the first Git `ApplicationInfo`, preserving discovery order while producing a single executable path. Without it, a PATH containing both `/usr/bin` and `/bin` returned two Git applications and the fixture attempted to invoke their combined paths as one command. Production installer behavior, recovery/worktree behavior, and CI configuration remain unchanged; no extra abstraction or policy was added.

## Evidence

### Corrected candidate: Linux PowerShell 7.6.9

The original discussion session executed the following bounded proof in a task-owned Docker environment; this publishing session verified the integrated and published hashes, one-line delta, full tree, and whitespace. This is Linux proof, not native Windows or a full installation.

- Corrected fixture SHA-256: `b630598930e90c05bbfcde860b92ac2cbf6e4cc5f8716673dce18d06e51ef8eb`. The pinned installer from `e135fce9d7b2daeaebb26998b133523563e9509f` is unchanged, SHA-256 `7cd362c179c34825842406c5efe8e07e575b70e7ae57e3f240a5c93a47cf1203`. Integration base remains `5bab0c1454827e1819ca670ac476903483229dc5`.
- Before correction, all 20 cases failed during setup when Git was discovered at both `/usr/bin` and `/bin`; none emitted a `RESULT:`. These are fixture failures, not selector-defect proof.
- After correction, all 20 fresh/existing × five selectors × Git-update-on/off observations completed the real `Main`/Git path to `Ensure-Pnpm`. Six explicit-update contracts were evaluated: five correctly expose the still-unfixed selector defect, while fresh/main succeeds by default-branch coincidence. The other 14 combinations remain observation-only; this is not 20 passing product contracts.
- Three additional existing-checkout main/tag/missing runs with `-AssertExplicitContract` emitted wrong-working-HEAD receipts and exited 1 as expected.
- All four existing worktree scenarios (valid, missing HEAD, broken gitfile, subdirectory) and the unchanged pull-conflict fixture passed. The latter verified a rebase-abort reflog, restored HEAD/status, and no active rebase.
- PowerShell parsed five inputs with zero errors: installer, old and corrected selector fixtures, and existing worktree/pull fixtures. Total corrected-candidate proof time: 14.064 seconds. Fixture roots were removed; no package installation, build, wrapper publication, Doctor, service, or onboarding operation ran.
- The portable official Linux x64 PowerShell 7.6.9 archive was verified against its API asset digest and official hashes file: SHA-256 `1da6d6d6035d651f20e70ddee7c4c15ac6ab8b9fb40ee92240d91263f28a884b`. It was task-local; no shared-host installation or PATH/service change.
- Fresh independent source-only review (P0–P2) of the full corrected fixture found no actionable findings. The reviewer did not execute code or independently hash supplied bytes; the execution owner and this integration bind the reviewed/tested candidate by the SHA-256 above. This is a narrative independent review, not an Auto Review-helper result.

**Supplemental static analysis (2026-10-29):** The original discussion session ran PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 under task-private Linux PowerShell 7.6.9 on the exact corrected fixture (SHA-256 `b630598930e90c05bbfcde860b92ac2cbf6e4cc5f8716673dce18d06e51ef8eb`): **0 errors, 11 warnings, and 11 informational notices**. Findings concern production-name boundary replacements, ShouldProcess conventions in private fixture helpers, signature-preserving unused `InstallDirectory`, the `DryRun` variable consumed by the dot-sourced `Main`, and deliberate positional Git argument forwarding; the existing worktree/pull fixtures show the same applicable categories. No further behavioral defect was established and no suppression was added. This is default-rule diagnostic analysis, not a clean lint gate or native Windows proof, and is separate from the hosted review.

**Current-head hosted review (2026-10-29):** [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187029#issuecomment-6481435031) completed on `d0dff3f78d4290ed0f25363c8ded1f34143b418d` with no actionable findings and a ready-for-maintainer-review assessment, not merge approval. It executed no target code and recorded the native Windows proof gap at review time (13:29 UTC). The native Windows evidence below was collected later, at 15:21–15:24 UTC; that review did not assess or accept these later results.

### Corrected candidate: native Windows (2026-10-29)

Local Codex-reported execution at 15:21–15:24 UTC covered **40 primary cases**: 20 under PowerShell 7.6.9 Core and 20 under Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444 Desktop. Environment: Windows NT 10.0.26200.0, Node 24.19.0 win32/x64, Git 2.53.0.windows.2. Exact inputs were corrected fixture SHA-256 `b630598930e90c05bbfcde860b92ac2cbf6e4cc5f8716673dce18d06e51ef8eb` and unchanged installer SHA-256 `7cd362c179c34825842406c5efe8e07e575b70e7ae57e3f240a5c93a47cf1203`.

- All 40 primary cases reached `Ensure-Pnpm`; no package installation or build was attempted. Each engine evaluated six explicit-update contracts: one true (fresh/main follows the default branch) and five false (the still-unfixed selector defect). The other 14 cases per engine are policy-only observations. **Observation-mode exit 0 is not a passing product contract.**
- A separate initial Windows PowerShell 5.1 attempt had 20 cases: ten fresh-checkout cases failed before the boundary with clone exit 128 / `Filename too long`, while ten existing-checkout cases reached it. A shorter new task path containing spaces resolved that setup failure without source, assertion, or system-policy changes. This is not a long-path bug fix. The evidence therefore contains **60 total observations, only 40 of them primary**.
- The coordinating session independently verified 87 archive checksum/CRC checks, supplied input manifests/source hashes, all 60 log receipts against their result rows, and four before/after bundle checks. It did not rerun Windows. Cleanup was reported; no machine-wide audit was performed. Raw evidence is retained in the original conversation, not at an invented public artifact URL. Archive SHA-256: `4828e94040212fc5b7323c3f9447928f68a22c393c89ca41cfae3c66a13d5ae1`.

**Remaining gaps:** Local Vitest and a full installer run remain unrun. The native Windows evidence is bounded pre-dependency fixture execution, not full-install or machine-wide validation. Parser success is not a clean lint gate, and CI on the prior head is not CI proof for the corrected head. The fixture is not wired into always-on CI.

### Historical evidence and review (2026-10-28)

- The original fixture SHA-256 was `3187a3b895831909b1fa5ca980642fb710f31b0b7904ad3158a42d6ba360611c`. Historical Codex-reported native Windows runs used PowerShell 7.6.9 and Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444: existing-clean-checkout main/tag/missing with updates enabled, three of twenty combinations per engine. All six reached the pre-build boundary at working-remote and failed the explicit-selector contract (exit 1).
- Those six runs used installer source `5962ce779a8a425d1ffc9e1279b6242154c467e9`, SHA-256 `d8c1395e4e463c2e8faef8898fe5b6ac073df021581496851cfa26f3abd5096d`. They do not establish native Windows execution of the corrected fixture or the newer pinned installer.
- Before initial draft publication, local Auto Review terminated with exit 143 after allocator diagnostics exceeded its output limit; no validated review report was produced. Mert explicitly authorized that initial reproduction-only draft publication without a completed review, with the failure and then-unrun tests disclosed. That attempt remains a failed review, not a clean helper result.
- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187029#issuecomment-6481435031) found no actionable findings on prior head `e135fce9d7b2daeaebb26998b133523563e9509f`, executed no target code, and retained the Windows execution gap. It predates this one-line correction.

<details>
<summary>Manual reproduction</summary>

Run in a new PowerShell process with Git and Node already available. Use a new disposable fixture directory; the fixture removes only the root it creates. For example:

```powershell
pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File test/scripts/install-git-selector.ps1 -InstallerPath scripts/install.ps1 -FixtureRoot "$PWD/selector-repro-main" -Checkout existing -Selector main -AssertExplicitContract
```

Repeat with `-Selector tag` and `-Selector missing`, each using a new root. The Linux PowerShell runs against the pinned installer produced a `RESULT:` record with `contractSatisfied:false`, followed by exit 1, for these three existing-checkout assertions. A nonzero exit alone is not reproduction proof: verify that setup succeeded and inspect `buildBoundaryReached`, the selected HEAD, and `outcome`.

Omit `-AssertExplicitContract` to collect observations without failing for the known selector defect. Omitted/latest selectors and `-DisableGitUpdate` combinations remain observations, not selected policy.

</details>

title: feat(sessions): recover session creation after Gateway restarts
body:
Closes #186869

Related: [approved design, PostgreSQL support, and migration decisions](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0705165-5352-4f6e-955d-99ab0c2be386)

## What Problem This Solves

Automation callers need to recover an uncertain session-creation result after a Gateway restart without accidentally creating another conversation.

## User Impact

Clients can opt into durable creation on SQLite and PostgreSQL with a retained operation ID, timestamp-matched physical UUIDv7, and explicit default-agent binding. Retrying returns the original live session without repeating workspace preparation or starting a turn. Changed intent, deleted sessions, and reset incarnations are refused. Existing creation requests are unchanged.

**Migration:** agent schema advances from 38 to 39. Older binaries require the matching pre-upgrade backup; package-only rollback is unsupported. Receipts have a thirty-day wall-clock validity window. Keep the Gateway clock synchronized and treat expiry as terminal; replay protection does not extend beyond retention or survive restoring older operation history.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session writer atomically commits the receipt, session row, and initial transcript. Reconciliation uses committed facts rather than a process-local response cache and checks current caller authority before disclosure. Reset detection reuses the existing lifecycle identity. The versioned migration, backup/export descriptors, and generated PostgreSQL schema ship together; there is no request-path DDL, new background cleanup service, or clock watermark store.

## Evidence

- Registered RPC regressions cover worker reopen, concurrent duplicates, immutable intent/profile/UUID binding, deletion/reset, expiry/skew, explicit agent binding, authority revocation, and no initial turn. Worker-purpose tests verify owned repository/workspace preparation is not repeated.
- Real WebSocket proof passes on SQLite and disposable PostgreSQL 17: concurrent creation, cold Gateway process restart, original-session replay, empty history, a separately requested completed agent turn, and deletion replay refusal. The model is a synthetic loopback provider; no external inference credentials were used. Both wire runs were renewed on exact committed head `6c2c471499f7b72c5fb1adff8d39686d94303e35` after the result-module extraction.
- PostgreSQL transaction/worker conformance passes, including receipt/row/transcript fault rollback, worker reopen, and failed/successful schema 38→39 migration. Generated SQLite/PostgreSQL catalogs have zero unexplained differences.
- Actual published **2026.10.8 binary** proof passes in an isolated Podman-adapted maintained updater fixture: a completed baseline model turn, verified pre-upgrade backup, installed updater → exact candidate, candidate Doctor, schema 25→39, cold restart, and retained session/history. The retained old binary restores the backup, reports exact schema 25, and reads the original session; 32 logical history/session tables match. No creation receipts are fabricated during migration. SQLite scoped-backup/migration tests also pass.
- Existing creation durability and replacement-worker consumers passed (28 tests) before the final result extraction. Its follow-up run passed all 12 new RPC/worker tests and 12/13 existing creation tests; one existing worktree-recovery case returned failed recovery after 23 seconds. Its isolated rerun passed without source changes; the original failure remains unresolved and is not claimed fixed. Core and targeted test typechecks, scoped lint/format, generated artifact checks, docs syntax checks, full public package build, and tarball integrity pass.

title: feat(skills): diet oversized learned skills in daily Workshop maintenance
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Learned skills only grow: each lesson patches more text into `SKILL.md`, which every run that uses the skill reads in full, and nothing in Skill Workshop ever shrinks them. On one production agent, 46 of the 48 learned skills with saved versions grew and none shrank; one doubled to 20 KB over 10 patches.

## User Impact

User impact: in `auto` learning mode, the daily Workshop maintenance pass now shrinks one oversized learned skill per agent per day, with no user action and without changing the skill's rules. Each diet is one versioned change in the skill's history; `openclaw skills workshop restore <name>` undoes it, including the reference files it added. `propose` and `off` modes are unchanged, and there are no config, schema, or SDK changes. An agent whose tool policy denies `skill_workshop` (its documented Workshop opt-out) gets no daily maintenance: no diet, and also no unused-skill archive, which until now ran for such agents.

A diet makes two to four tool-free calls on the agent's primary model and sends the skill's text to that provider (documented).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pick:** `SKILL.md` body over 12 KB (the existing sprawl threshold), unchanged for a day, taken in name order, rotated by calendar day (day N takes entry N mod count). No new state; a skill that cannot be dieted cannot block the others.
- **Rewrite:** the model names whole `##` sections that only some runs need; OpenClaw copies them verbatim into new `references/` files (re-pointing relative links) and the model tightens the rest, ending with a lookup index.
- **Mechanical checks:** every link and heading anchor resolves, including anchors into existing reference files, every new reference is linked, `SKILL.md` shrinks by at least 20%, every file passes normal Workshop validation. Sections with in-page links, and skills with titled or reference-style links, are not moved.
- **Independent review:** a separate model call compares the original and the rewrite rule by rule and reports rules that are missing, weakened, moved out of reach of the runs they apply to, or added. One repair pass; otherwise nothing is written.
- **Authority:** the daily gate skips agents whose tool policy denies `skill_workshop`. Auto mode is read from the live config before every diet model call, again by the completion owner right before dispatch (`assertCurrent`), and again at publish, so turning learning off mid-diet stops further provider calls and writes.
- **Publish:** one versioned `curator` change. Under the skill lock, the file list, `SKILL.md` and every Markdown support file must match what the candidate was validated against; any concurrent edit refuses the diet. A new shared `publishSkillOverlay` helper now also backs draft apply.

The approach adapts [skill-diet](https://github.com/nicobailon/skill-diet) (ideas, no code). An earlier manual pilot found that before/after behavioral tests saturated (both versions passed every task) while a rule-by-rule audit caught real losses, so the audit is the gate.

Accepted edges: the rotation is per day, so a Gateway restart re-attempts that day's skill; a skill that is one long procedure section, or already has broken anchors, is skipped, costing one model call per turn.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway (fresh `--profile`, state inside the worktree, real `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`), seeded with a copy of 85 learned skills from a production agent; live state was never written. Real agent turns triggered the daily pass end to end. OpenAI's implicit runtime selection put these turns on the **Codex harness** (recorded `agent_harness_id = codex`):

| Skill | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `crabbox-provider-preflight` | 20.1 → 7.8–8.0 KB, all 8 branch sections moved to 4 references; reproduced on 4 builds, including the final one |
| `serialized-heavy-check-orchestration` | 12.3 → 7.5 KB, 3 sections moved |
| `github-issue-root-cause-investigation` | Rejected (a single 11 KB procedure; cut only 5%); nothing written |

- **Rule audits** of published outputs by a fresh model: 0 missing, 0 weakened (3 audits).
- **Behavioral eval** (12 scenarios, blind-graded together): original 32/36 vs dieted 33/36 on `gpt-6.1-sol`, 0 forbidden actions; `gpt-6-luna` 8/12 vs 7/12, where 2 of the dieted runs failed on eval-harness tool discovery.
- **OpenClaw harness:** with the model pinned to `agentRuntime.id: "openclaw"`, a fresh session (recorded `agent_harness_id = openclaw`) triggered the same pass: `crabbox-provider-preflight` 20.1 → 8.2 KB, 8 sections moved. The diet runs on both runtimes.
- **Undo:** `openclaw skills workshop restore` returned the skill byte-identical to the original.
- The first iteration exposed a prompt flaw (moved rules were summarized back into `SKILL.md`, only −22%); fixed before the runs above.
- **Tests:** `pnpm test src/skills/workshop/skill-diet.test.ts src/skills/workshop/drafts.test.ts src/skills/workshop/library.test.ts src/agents/harness/agent-end-side-effects.test.ts src/skills/workshop/skill-lint.test.ts`: 53 passed. The new file has 16 tests at about 5.5 s with `--maxWorkers=1`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, oxlint, and oxfmt are clean.
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, up to P2) over the full candidate diff against `8889b596`. Nine passes raised 12 P2 findings, all fixed: reviewer ignoring additions and lost reach, several link/anchor integrity cases, and a reference-creation race. The final pass on the final tree: no actionable P0–P2.
- **Review fixes (`be71053`):** ClawSweeper's four findings and two red guards (`coercion-helpers`, assertion-safety), plus five oxlint errors in the new files. Five new regression tests (in-process, real Workshop library and filesystem, scripted model replies) fail on `9e69799` and pass on `be71053`: an anchor missing from an existing reference, a support file that gains a link into a moved section during the diet, and learning switched off after the first call (no further call, nothing written); the denied agent is proven on the live Gateway below. `198e924` then dropped the mid-diet deny recheck as unneeded. Focused run: `skill-diet`, `tool-policy-diagnostic`, `plugins-cli.inspect`, `agent-end-side-effects`, `drafts`: 63 passed. oxfmt, oxlint, the coercion-helper guard and the assertion-safety ratchet are clean on the changed files.
- **Live Gateway proof of the review fixes (`be71053`):** isolated Gateway (fresh state and config outside every checkout, port 19777, `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_MODEL_TRANSPORT=1`), built from the PR head, OpenClaw runtime, Anthropic key resolved through an exec SecretRef (never in env, argv or files; the OpenAI keys available to this run returned 401). Each agent was seeded with the same learned skill: the bundled `browser-automation` skill plus one learned lesson section, 12.9 KB body, settled for two days. One real turn per case; provider requests counted from `[model-fetch] start` lines.

| Case | Model requests after the turn | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reader`, `tools.deny: ["skill_workshop"]` | turn only (plus one Haiku utility call); no diet call | no maintenance log line; `SKILL.md` hash unchanged |
| `main`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` | turn + 4 diet calls (plan, audit, repair, audit) | reviewer still found 3 weakened rules; nothing written |
| `main`, `claude-opus-5-5` | turn + 4 diet calls (plan, audit with findings, repair, clean audit) | published: `SKILL.md` 12.8 → 6.9 KB, 4 sections moved to 3 references; `openclaw skills workshop restore` returned the original bytes and removed the 3 references |
| `main`, learning set to `off` in the config file the moment the first diet call started | turn + 1 diet call (the plan); no audit call | `skill diet skipped: … Learning is no longer in auto mode.`; `SKILL.md` hash unchanged |
- **Simplification (`198e924`, `37515fb`):** dropped the mid-diet deny recheck (the daily gate already skips denied agents), and replaced the usage-ranked candidate order with name order: usage counts change daily, so rotating a re-sorted list could skip or repeat skills, and the diet no longer reads skill usage. Against `be71053`: production −40 lines, tests −31 lines.
- **Gaps:** the behavioral eval graded plans, not live Crabbox actions; per-diet token use (about 20–45k) is estimated from sizes.

Requested by @obviyus, following an investigation started by @jalehman.

title: fix: recover sessions blocked by aggregate workspace size limits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sessions remain unable to prepare when many individually valid guest-created files exceed the 768 MiB workspace reconciliation payload limit.

## User Impact

Gateway administrators can identify the oversized aggregate, preserve selected new files outside synchronization, and retry without losing authored edits. Recovery still refuses admitted inputs, unsafe paths, active journals, and already-staged receipts.

No size, inventory, worker heap, permission, receipt, or automatic-retention limits change. Recovery remains explicit and administrator-only; no existing workspace is automatically cleaned up.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Report actual aggregate bytes, the unchanged limit, payload count, largest new-file candidates, and an eligible recovery command.
- Extend the existing recovery owner to individually valid nonempty files only while a fresh capture still exceeds the aggregate bound. Preserve existing retry, no-overwrite, cross-device verification, and authority checks.
- Copy sliced worker payloads with an exact-sized typed array and native `set`, avoiding the iterable intermediate that exhausted the worker heap on repeated valid large staged reads.

Project-aware `bin/obj` exclusion was investigated but is deliberately not introduced: a nearby .NET project file does not establish ownership of every descendant, output locations are configurable, and old receipts contain no output provenance. Authored and admitted `bin` paths remain eligible. The docs recommend redirecting disposable build output into checkout-root `.openclaw/tmp/` or using explicit recovery.

## Evidence

- Independent local autoreview of the complete local patch against base `e2184d88492e48ae0fdca20c6db064ffb1024df7`, with unchanged owner context supplied: **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. Subsequent edits only added lint-required braces and strengthened the ignored-output fixture; that regression passed again.
- **126 tests passed across eight focused files**, including real paired-client Gateway recovery authorization, receipt/archive/restart preservation, byte ownership, SQLite transfer, CLI help, and exact aggregate/UTF-8 boundaries. One existing opt-in Podman test was skipped.
- The regression uses **13 individually valid files exceeding the real 768 MiB boundary**, including Git-ignored .NET `bin/obj` output. It preserves the recovered file byte-for-byte, rejects admitted-file and stale recovery requests, prepares successfully again, and retains remaining artifacts plus authored source and `bin` files.
- Red→green: the aggregate failure had no usable recovery. The complete recovery flow then exposed a repeated-large-payload worker OOM, repaired by the native byte copy. A standalone single-64-MiB read was insufficient to reproduce that second defect.
- Focused typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed. No visual change. No live model call, deployment, or modification of the originally affected workspace was performed.

<details>
<summary>Commands and test cost</summary>

`pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-reconcile-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-manifest-worker.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-result-staging.reads.test.ts src/infra/worker-transfer-bytes.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-transfer.test.ts src/cli/sandbox-cli.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/worktrees.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

Eight-file command wall time: **120.616 seconds**. Final ignored-output regression: **13.232 seconds test time**, **46.917 seconds command wall time**, including compiler preparation. Its real byte volume catches the actual aggregate limit and repeated large-read allocation failure; no safety-limit override is used. CI seconds: pending the first PR run.

</details>

title: fix(control-ui): opening prompt hides behind "Show earlier" after stopping a long turn
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the conversation's opening prompt disappears behind a "Show earlier" strip when you stop a turn that ran longer than the chat history tail.

## User Impact

User impact: stopping a long run keeps the whole conversation in place, including the first message; nothing you were already looking at turns into "earlier history".

## Why This Change Was Made

Stop persists an interrupted reply, so the pane's incremental history cursor comes back as a reset. The full read that follows returns only the bounded tail (80 rows), and the pane replaced the transcript it had held from the start with that tail plus an earlier-history boundary. #187219's source-bound older cursors did not change this: the prompt only came back after a separate older-page read.

Now, only on that cursor-reset path, the pane reads the rows before the tail with the tail's own `olderCursor` and merges them before publishing, so the transcript stays continuous. Both the older page and the tail are server rows; held live rows are never trusted as coverage. The read happens only when the pane held its transcript from the start (complete, non-empty, same session), there is no window reset, and everything before the tail fits one older page. Otherwise, or if that read fails, the pane shows the tail plus its retryable boundary, as it does today.

Plain full reads (reconnects, finished turns, session switches), scroll-driven older-page loading, branch/leaf switches, split panes and cache commits are unchanged. The gap logic lives in a lazily imported module so startup JS stays within budget (+2 B gzip vs base).

## Evidence

Before (`main`, frame captured right after Stop): the prompt is gone and the pane shows the earlier-history strip.

![Before: after Stop, the opening prompt is replaced by the Show earlier strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbfefbaf-487b-462d-8f87-176fca51d2e6)

After (this branch, same scenario): the prompt stays; no boundary appears in any captured frame.

![After: after Stop, the opening prompt stays visible above the interrupted turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fcbc976-eeb5-4e91-8de5-8821a2f1179a)

Screenshots come from the new real-Gateway browser test (scripted model, 48 real `exec` steps, then Stop); the rendered result is unchanged on the final head.

Verified on the final tree (branch base `main` 87facf07d6b4):

- New `ui/src/e2e/chat-stop-long-turn.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, registered with the real-Gateway files: fails on base ("rows this pane already showed must not become earlier history"); passes 3/3 on this branch, and also asserts the prompt renders exactly once.
- New unit tests in `chat-history.test.ts` ("full tail after a long live turn"): gap read after a cursor reset when the tail starts after or at a live-held row (both red on base); failed read keeps the retryable boundary; no read for a plain full read without a cursor reset, or when the gap exceeds one older page.
- `ui/src/pages/chat` + `ui/src/lib/chat` unit tests: 630 files pass. `test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts` passes.
- Local browser e2e: 508 chat/history/transcript/scroll/warm-boot/recovery/stop/pane/outbox/session/boot files. Every asserted failure also fails on base locally: `boot-module-boundaries`, `chat-outbox-migration`, `chat-stream-runtime-budgets`, `chat-widget-retention`. Remaining reds are the harness `unsafe cleanup` teardown error in real-Gateway files whose tests pass. `chat-send-pending-handoff`, `chat-history-loading`, `chat-history-prepend-anchor`, `chat-flow.history-recovery`, `warm-boot` and `chat-cold-load-anchor` pass.
- CI on e61d43ad2fde: all checks green, including all `checks-ui-e2e` shards and `control-ui-performance`.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxfmt, oxlint: clean.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium) on 87facf07d6b4...1fd5e6c3fe97 with pane/pagination/snapshot source context, max priority P2: scoped-clean, no findings.

title: fix(ui): published PR handoffs show Interrupted and split the reply
body: Related: #184531 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: chat shows a stray "Interrupted" and breaks one reply into widely spaced separate turns when the agent publishes a PR from its workspace and continues afterwards. ## User Impact User impact: a run that publishes a PR and keeps working reads as one continuous answer — no false "Interrupted" label, and the "Published …" result sits inline with normal block spacing instead of a full turn gap (an invisible footer row plus turn margin) around every publication. ## Why This Change Was Made Since #184531, `github_publish` with a workspace path ends the turn through the shared handoff receipt (`started`/`async`/`yielded`), and the Gateway appends a runless "Published …" report before the next run resumes. Chat only treated `prepare_pr` as a handoff (#180538), so the publishing run, whose last message is a tool call, was marked Interrupted, and the runless report was rendered as its own completed turn. The fix recognizes any paired, confirmed `github_publish` handoff receipt (the receipt, not the action, proves the handoff) and lets a runless assistant report that arrives while a handoff is resuming join the open answer, the same way `sessions_yield` continuations already do. Genuine failures, unpaired results, synchronous publish results, and real aborts keep their existing outcomes. Known limit: with tool details hidden, a handing-off run that has no visible content still shows its report as a separate row (no Interrupted label either way). ## Evidence Mobile (390×844) mocked Control UI with a transcript shaped like the reported session: three `publish` handoffs, each followed by the Gateway report, then an active continuation. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | - Regression tests in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-pr-handoff.test.ts`: both new cases fail on `main` (the report splits the answer into separate turns; the waiting run reads `interrupted`) and pass with the fix; the existing PR-preparation cases, including unpaired-result and failure guards, stay green. - Consumer suites: 13 chat grouping/yield/thread test files, 290 tests passed. - Browser e2e: `chat-yield-acknowledgment`, `chat-subagent-waiting`, `chat-pull-requests`, `chat-interrupted-history` — 15 passed. - `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on touched files: clean. - Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, base `762a2fe60cc3`, head `03ad7df4de28`, P0–P2): scoped-clean, no findings. ## Work sessions - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/9b90ebcf-f60e-4088-89c6-5524f12dccb1) ## Worked on by - @steipete

title: fix(ui): Fast indicator shows for models that cannot use Fast
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the composer's effort control shows the lightning Fast indicator for a model that cannot use Fast, when Fast is on as an agent default or saved session preference. For example, a ClawRouter Claude route with the agent's Fast default enabled shows "⚡ High", even though its effort picker offers no speed choices and requests run at the standard tier.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/02c5a543-cd76-4c64-bcb1-0013a0e6c41b)

## User Impact

The lightning indicator, the "· Fast" suffix in the control's title and accessible name, and the phone gauge's lightning badge now appear only when the selected model can actually run Fast. Models that support Fast are unchanged. A saved Fast or Ultrafast preference is kept and stays visible in the speed panel, so it can still be cleared. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI's speed state already decided whether the selected request can carry Fast. It used that to hide the speed choices, but it still reported Fast as active from the preference alone. Running state, label and tier hints now follow the same applicability check that hides the choices, matching the existing Standard-only behavior.

`models.list` also asked provider speed policies about an unknown runtime for rows that use the implicit OpenClaw runtime, while every sibling projection in the same row already used `openclaw`. Bundled policies return "unknown" for that, so these rows lost their Fast capability, and the UI fell back to a provider allowlist that does not include ClawRouter. Passing the same runtime keeps the capability authoritative. Without this, the UI change would also hide the indicator on ClawRouter routes that do support priority.

<details><summary>Scope notes</summary>

- Intentionally unchanged: `/fast` and `/status` keep reporting the configured preference and its source; they describe the setting, not the request tier.
- Other readers of `supportsFastMode` (guest catalog choices, the New Session draft, the Android and Apple speed controls) now receive the real capability for implicit-runtime rows instead of an unknown value.
- Not in this PR: the Android and Apple apps draw their own lightning from `effectiveFastMode` without checking support. Their presentation code is separate and can follow separately.

</details>

## Evidence

Control UI production build with a synthetic Gateway: ClawRouter `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` with no Fast support, Fast inherited from the agent default.

Before (main):

![Before: lightning shown next to High for a model without Fast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2e103fd-ab12-40cb-9e2e-92d452387182)

After:

![After: High without the Fast indicator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e397183-2696-49ec-9c9e-b8682ad0d858)

Phone width (390px), before and after: the gauge's lightning badge is replaced by the normal effort needle.

![Before: phone gauge shows the lightning badge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d82a9a0b-4efa-49ea-af95-74f314678523) ![After: phone gauge shows the effort needle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f14476d2-4f28-40ff-a9d7-ff4fb1eb32d1)

- Rendered state on main vs this branch for that scenario: `data-chat-fast-mode` `true` → `false`, title `High · Fast` → `High`, lightning count 1 → 0 (desktop and 390px phone). Control scenario, an OpenAI model with priority tier: lightning, `High · Fast` and 3 speed options, identical before and after.
- Regression tests, red on main and green here: `ui/src/lib/chat/model-select-state.test.ts` (saved Fast, inherited Fast, saved Ultrafast on a route without Fast, and a provider without a Fast mapping; unknown applicability still shows Fast), `chat-effort-picker.browser.test.tsx` (rendered indicator), `models-list-result.service-tiers.test.ts` (implicit-runtime rows project `supportsFastMode`).
- Consumers: 16 UI unit files (415 tests), the effort-picker browser suite, and 12 server/provider files (models-list, requester catalog, speed policy, Anthropic/OpenAI Fast policy) pass. `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core, core tests, UI), lint, import cycles and all ratchets pass; formatting applied.
- Gap: `src/agents/clawrouter-service-tier.integration.test.ts` cannot reach its loopback HTTP fixture on the authoring host and fails identically on main (23/26, `Connection error.`); it covers request transport, which this change does not touch. Left to PR CI.
