title: fix: images pasted while the agent is working disappear after the next tool call
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an image pasted while the agent is already working, such as a phone screenshot, is visible to the model for one request. After the next tool call it is replaced by "1 image attachment could not be loaded … ask them to resend", even though the file was received and stored.

## User Impact

Images sent mid-turn now stay visible to the model for the rest of the run. Earlier model requests keep the same bytes, so the prompt cache is no longer invalidated by this rewrite. Images that really failed to load are still reported once, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A steered message keeps a resized inline copy of the pasted image (for example 942×2047 for a 1320×2868 screenshot). The model limit then resizes it again on every request. Replay pinning from #185567 recorded hashes of the *sanitized* image but filtered the *raw* inline blocks against them. For any image that needs resizing, those hashes never match, so the image was dropped and silently counted as a failed attachment from the second request on.

Replay now offers the existing inline blocks to the image loader and keeps only output whose sanitized hash matches the pinned decision. The original guarantee from #185567 still holds: an image omitted on the first request stays omitted. A replay failure is counted only when a previously included image goes missing or changes, so pinned omissions are not counted twice.

## Evidence

- **Production trace (team server):** a mid-run screenshot logged `Image resized … 1320x2868px` then `942x2047px`, followed by `[prompt-cache] message 12 (user) differs … content[1].type, content[1].data, content[1].mimeType, content[1].text`, and the model received the failure note. No `Native image: failed to load` warning was logged. The stored file was intact.
- **Regression test:** `images.replay.test.ts` › "keeps omitted images omitted and resized inline images included on later requests". The existing omitted-image replay case now also carries a steered inline image that exceeds the model limit. It fails on `main`, where the second request drops the image, and passes with the fix. The two unreadable-image cases shared a single fixture and are merged, so the PR adds no test lines (`check:test-lines-ratchet`: net −7).

title: fix(agents): agents_wait drops collector results when a batch includes an announcing child
body:
Related: #186652

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after #186652, `agents_wait` threw away finished collector results when a batch also included one of the caller's announcing children. It also promised a completion message for quiet children (`expectsCompletionMessage=false`), which never send one.

## User Impact

User impact: mixed `agents_wait` batches return their completed collector results again, and the announcing child is reported as `not_found` as before. The "result arrives as a completion message" guidance now only appears when every requested ID is the caller's own announcing child. Quiet and session-mode (possibly thread-bound) children never get that promise.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's review of #186652 (posted shortly before auto-merge completed) found two P2 regressions in the new `agents_wait` diagnostic:

- The guidance branch matched any owned non-collector child, including fire-and-forget children that have no completion handoff.
- The guidance was thrown whenever any requested ID was an announcing child, which dropped completed and pending results for the other IDs in the batch.

The guidance now requires `expectsCompletionMessage`, a non-session spawn mode, and caller ownership. It is thrown only when it covers the whole request. Otherwise the per-ID `not_found` contract from before #186652 applies unchanged. The warning-suppression half of #186652 was not affected.

## Evidence

- `agents-wait-tool.test.ts` covers an announcing-only wait (guidance), a mixed `[completed collector, announcing child]` batch (completion kept, child reported `not_found`), and a quiet owned child and a foreign child (`not_found`). It fails on current `main` and passes with the fix. `agents-wait-tool.native.test.ts` is also green.

title: fix(github): rejected pushes leave publication stuck as unconfirmed instead of failing
body:
Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a554d4a1-ab83-4be0-9fc2-32b7d2489639)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when GitHub rejects a publication push (for example because the publishing account has no write access to the repository), the request is reported as "unconfirmed" and agents are told to retry recovery or ask an operator, even though nothing was pushed.

## User Impact

User impact: a rejected push now fails right away as `push_rejected`. The next step names the account and the repository, says nothing was pushed, and tells you to grant write access (or publish from a fork) and check branch rules. Agents no longer stall waiting for a recovery that can't change the outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

After `git push`, the executor checks the remote head again. If git exited non-zero on its own (not killed or signalled) and the remote branch still holds its pre-push head, the push definitively did not land. That case now settles as a known `push_rejected` failure. Every other mismatch keeps today's unconfirmed handling: a successful exit, a killed or signalled push, or a remote that moved to a different head. So nothing that might have landed gets marked failed. Git's stderr isn't parsed: one next action covers both missing write access and branch rules.

Observed on team.openclaw.ai: `roboclaw-bot` publishing to `openclaw/telemetry` (no write access, so the push was rejected) got the request stuck as unconfirmed recovery, then terminal `unavailable` with a "may already have succeeded" next action.

The test changes also move a duplicated `runCommand` override wrapper into one shared `overrideCommands` test helper. That way the regression test adds no net test lines, as the test-lines ratchet requires.

## Evidence

- New test in `github-publication-history.test.ts`: it pushes to a real bare Git remote whose `pre-receive` hook rejects the push. It fails on `origin/main` and passes with this change, asserting `push_rejected`, the account and repository in the next action, an unchanged remote, and no PR creation.
- All 41 `github-publication*`, `github-personal-publication*` and `github-repository-publication*` test files pass. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` pass, as do oxlint and the format check on the touched files, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (net delta 0), and `git diff --check`.

title: improve(ui): open chat menus without a loading flash
body:
octopool: pr_view served from shared cache (hit), refreshes in 1m59s; set OCTOPOOL_FRESH=1 for a live read
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat and New Session menus show a "Loading…" row on their first open after a page load, where they used to open instantly.

## User Impact

User impact: once a chat or New Session page has settled, the session menu, composer plus menu, model and effort pickers, microphone menu, context breakdown, header panel menus, composer suggestion menus (slash, skills, mentions, emoji), and the New Session project, where and checkout pickers open with their real items.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recent boot-performance work moved these menu bodies out of the boot bundles and into first-open imports, and nothing loaded them again before use. The shell already has an idle owner (`app-shell-idle.runtime.ts`) that warms next-route code after the transcript paints, while respecting offline, data-saver and hidden-tab states. Each menu now registers its existing `lazy()` loader with a small registry (`ui/src/lib/idle-warmup.ts`), and the idle owner calls those loaders after the page settles. Calling the component's own `preload` sets its cached component, so the first open renders synchronously instead of committing the `<Loading>` fallback. Bodies loaded this way can register their own nested lazies, such as the plus menu's capability initializer.

Boot stays as it was: registration loads no code. The added bytes are the registration calls themselves (merge-base comparison: Chat boot JS +831 B gzip, New Session boot JS +440 B gzip, startup JS −3 B). After the page settles, the extra idle download is about 60 KB brotli across the menu chunks.

Accepted edge cases:
- The plus menu creates one `lazy()` per composer surface so its loading tests stay isolated, so it registers per surface. A newly mounted composer is warmed on the next idle pass.
- Opening the plus menu still commits one placeholder row while its capability controller initializes. That row is replaced in the same task and is never painted.
- A speculative load that fails is ignored; opening the menu still owns the error through its existing `Errored` boundary.
- The owner list in the session menu's owner submenu still loads people data on open. That is a data read, not deferred code, and is unchanged here.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI, production bundle, 350 ms injected latency on lazy JS chunks to match a remote Gateway, first open about 6 s after load:

**Before** (session menu, then plus menu)

![Before: session menu first open shows a Loading row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10e2b42a-ec9f-40d7-8fba-b963f389f4f0)

![Before: composer plus menu first open shows a Loading row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e50e554-280a-49ff-a888-71efb478c097)

![After: composer plus menu first open shows Camera, Media, File, Skills, Plugins and Web search](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/988a3d09-3582-4c74-a313-9b4e814a9535)

- New `ui/src/e2e/chat-menu-idle-warmup.e2e.test.ts` (bundled Control UI): waits for idle warmup, then opens the session and plus menus and asserts that no lazy-body loading row is still attached at the next animation frame. It fails on the merge base (the menu bodies are never loaded before interaction) and passes with this change.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint on the changed files, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: pass.
- `pnpm ui:build` + `pnpm ui:check-performance` and `pnpm ui:check-performance:base <merge-base>`: pass, with the deltas above.

title: fix(agents): scheduled runs post a stale "Wait for Agents failed" warning after recovering
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled run that recovered from an early tool failure, recorded a meaningful result with `record_result`, and ended silently still posted only `⚠️ Wait for Agents failed` to its conversation. The trigger in production was `agents_wait` returning `not_found` for the caller's own announcing child.

## User Impact

User impact: a scheduled run that records `progress`, `done`, `blocked`, or `needs_attention` no longer reports an earlier recovered tool failure as its result. Runs that record `no_change`, or record nothing, still show the warning. When an agent waits on its own announcing child (started without `collect=true`), `agents_wait` now says the result will arrive as a completion message instead of claiming the run does not exist.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observed on team.openclaw.ai: a landing automation called `agents_wait` on a helper spawned with `completionTarget: "parent"`. `agents_wait` only tracks collector runs, so it returned `not_found`. The agent moved on with other tools for about 15 minutes, recorded a `progress` result, scheduled its next check, and ended with `NO_REPLY`. Failure tracking clears only on a later success of the same tool, and scheduled runs don't treat `NO_REPLY` as enough to hide a failure. So the only message in the conversation was the stale warning, and the job's diagnostics showed it next to an `ok` run with a real summary.

- **Warning policy:** a meaningful recorded automation result now counts as the run's authored outcome. It goes through the same `hasUserFacingReply` gate that already suppresses the warning when a visible reply exists. `no_change` carries no authored text, so it keeps the warning, matching the downstream rule that `no_change` keeps error payloads. The failure itself is still in the transcript and the progress lane.
- **`agents_wait`:** when a requested run is the caller's own non-collector child, the tool throws an input error that explains completion-message delivery. Unowned non-collector runs still return `not_found`, so nothing new is revealed about other sessions' runs. The output error union is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New regressions fail on the base and pass with the fix:
  - `payloads.errors.test.ts`: on base, a cron run with a recorded `progress` result plus a `NO_REPLY` final returned the warning. The `no_change` control keeps warning on both base and fix.
  - `agents-wait-tool.test.ts`: on base, an owned announcing child resolved as `not_found`. A foreign non-collector still returns `not_found`.
- Consumer suites green (5 Vitest shards): `payloads.errors`, `payloads`, `payloads.tool-authored`, `agents-wait-tool`, `agents-wait-tool.native`, `agent-runner-execution-session-events`, `cron-tool.automation`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core and all 29 core test graphs), lint, import cycles, ratchets, and format all pass. The one failure is an existing Knip unused-export finding in `ui/src/lib/keyboard-hints.ts`, outside this change and also present on `main`.
- The first head's CI failed only `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`. That's the test-line ratchet: the new cases added 39 lines while the tree is already over its ceiling. The regressions now live in the existing warning and `agents_wait` tables, and the PR's net test-line delta is −2.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) on the committed range found no issues.
- Not done: a live replay. Reproducing this end to end needs a model to repeat a specific misuse sequence (wait on an announcing child, recover, record a result, end silently). The production transcript is the bug evidence, and the unit tests cover the owning decision points.

title: feat(codex): host cloud inference on enrolled workers
body:
Related: #154388

## What Problem This Solves

Cloud placements need to run Codex inference with the worker’s authentication and workspace rather than launching the model process on the Gateway.

## User Impact

Opt-in **Full node placements** can run the exact enrolled app-server, execute native tools there, and continue conversations while the existing workspace remains available. Defaults are unchanged; unsupported carriers fail closed rather than falling back locally.

Operators provision **one private worker-only bundle** at the configured state directory’s `worker-provisioning/codex`: `config.toml` and its single Node `.mjs` auth helper. Configuration/helper bytes determine the command identity—no separate environment selectors or manually supplied versions. Use private permissions, allow the exact versioned command through the existing node policy, publish while stopped, then restart/reprovision workers after changes. This replaces the three inputs proposed earlier in this unshipped PR; it adds no configuration field or budget exception.

Worker initialization, inference and later refresh callbacks keep credential ownership on the worker rather than borrowing Gateway profiles. Local GitHub credentials are not forwarded. Selected Platform/subscription account constraints remain enforced; competing profile or supervision ownership is rejected. Dedicated ephemeral non-container nodes retain their own managed-identity transport and platform trust. Shared/container workers do not inherit them. Hosted native GitHub handoff stays disabled; host-owned tools retain managed GitHub execution.

**Limits:** worker validation remains Linux/keyless on the ordinary first-party route with synthetic upstream responses. Separate ordinary-session checks cover the landed native-command contract, not custom-provider-on-worker eligibility or worker secondary-account/keyring provisioning. Neither establishes commercial entitlement/live-model reasoning, cloud bootstrap/platform-identity attestation or Windows/macOS private-config qualification. No retained-disk, worker-loss recovery, replacement-workspace guarantee or immediate pruning deadline is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Private enrollment, production client selection, duplex transport and cleanup use existing placement, invocation and workspace owners. Resource readiness gates effects, not initial tool declaration. The bounded byte framer has real native consumers; caller-owned cleanup distinguishes transport closure from observed native exit.

One Codex provisioning owner validates the private bundle, parses its helper and derives the same identity for enrollment and registration. Lease staging preserves byte-equality checks; runtime verifies both enrolled content and the **captured admitted command**, so replacing content and its version cannot reuse an old admission. No alternate environment-input path remains.

The existing retained HOME also owns native metadata under `.openclaw-worker`. Watchdog custody may outlive teardown; no competing retention owner is introduced. The intentional plugin configuration surface grows by one entry for explicit inference locality (4910 → 4911 against pinned main d67aa608; the earlier baseline was4889 →4890).

## Evidence

**Published head:** `bbef51062b83ec73373ce276ada250022af1fb1c`; complete tree `1a041dc8a80ddbffcaaa256e8c4b1673c71378ec`, identical across all paths to qualified source commit `6a5ddacc1be3913893dea77d87ae2c4a0d4fb1ae`. The publisher added only an empty, Galin-credited attribution/receipt commit. Source6a5ddacc is a history-preserving merge of published `43bbd67690619156d3d717ff60c214d8224672ad` and canonical main `d67aa608643f6583a6c6102c522043794aafe064`, observed once and pinned for the actual GitHub conflict. **Exact-head CI and Darwin passed. At the 2026-10-30 08:10:58 UTC complete readback, GitHub reported mergeable=true and mergeState=clean. This is verified CI evidence, not a merge receipt; protected landing remains with the parent.**

**Generated-only resolution:** the preview and merge conflicted only in the configuration baseline count/digest. The canonical generator wrote and checked the union: core2579/channel4001/plugin4911. Incoming Particle contributes21 plugin entries; P8 retains its previously approved one-entry worker opt-in (pinned target4910 →4911). All **81 non-generated authored blobs and modes** remain identical to43bb; every other path equals the pinned target. The full PR remains83 files,+4724/−309. Accepted enrollment `ea332936d1e03b63f017730102b4de814e2a3219` and refusal consumer `ba72ebbc8c16a263df8b78c1eb9ab8475d77edb0` are unchanged. No new production behavior, native pin, dependency version, public API, permission/schema contract or budget exception was authored.

**New-composition qualification:** **41/41 cases across four files/three configurations passed in94.70s**: incoming NFC-aware local Codex discovery plus resume/cancellation/source-authority controls, existing Codex registration/managed exclusions, worker opt-in parser and config renderer. Canonical generator/check, scoped incoming-owner types/lint, matched-code formatting and diff passed. Canonical budget: **6,291,927 /6,330,931**, slack39,004; scalar/allocations exactly inherited from the pinned target. The first budget invocation printed the same passing result but its receipt-only shell suffix had a malformed exit argument; the unchanged canonical command was then run directly to collect a valid exit0. No source/budget/test change or product-failure repair is attributed to that wrapper error.

**Review/proof reuse:** this is not a fresh independent-review or native-runtime claim. The accepted full P5-compat two-pass normalP0–P2 review plus subsequent normalP0–P2 enrollment and refusal reviews retain their actual source scopes. All10 complete P5 review contexts and the eight enrollment/eight refusal owner contexts are unchanged;52 prior artifact hashes and both accepted draft hashes were reverified. Incoming full owner/caller inspection found only local CLI search normalization near Codex; auth/startup/worker/runner/diagnostic contracts did not change. The separate Particle provider does not widen worker eligibility. The minimal resolution adds no competing owner or compatibility layer. Prior Node/Bun composition, F1 and both causal CI repairs remain source-bound evidence below, not reruns or current-head clearance; broad scans and the historical native upgrade experiment were not replayed.

**Refusal-notice consumer migration:** merged `82ba1ed1074f05b92285258771988efe69a417f5` / [#187883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187883) intentionally replaced arbitrary cause-bearing notices with existing classified guidance or neutral copy while retaining private diagnostics. The [human clarification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187883#issuecomment-6509994482) explicitly keeps unknown failures neutral because raw input does not establish a safe next action. The migrated test retains the exact selected model, **exactly one provider request/no fallback**, exact terminal refusal, one displayed notice and exclusion of the provider’s raw explanation. Both acceptance runs used the maintained rootless, network-none runner and existing immutable image `5db2b4385f40ad14dbbb818648bbca9168eacd2f6b8eef20cb3b87e2f68ce312`, with verified Node26.12.1, native pnpm12.15.0 and pinned Bun1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1. Both containers had runner-confirmed and independently checked absence. No image pull/build, shared install, host credential/config/service change or security exception occurred.

**Investigated local setup failure, preserved:** the earlier9669 replay failed before provider receipt. A source-bound ea3329 diagnostic attempt reproduced that zero-request failure; its first console capture was suppressed by the E2E default silent mode. Supported verbose capture then showed five3–6ms `UND_ERR_SOCKET` provider-transport failures, default retry/backoff, and `agent.wait` timeout while the run remained active. The fixture inherited HTTP/S proxy variables and the production routing helper selected the environment proxy for loopback. The exact proxy-side socket-reset cause is not established. No host proxy/route was disabled: the acceptance runs created a new wholly synthetic stack inside the existing admitted network-none boundary. That stack reached the original CI assertion and then proved the intended contract. Failed host attempts and the original untraced uncertainty remain retained; no timeout increase, retry-for-green, weaker provider oracle or production-network fix is claimed.

**Accepted enrollment repair retained:** ea3329 gates private Codex input loading/delivery on the prepared node runtime’s existing enabled-plugin inventory. title: feat(codex): support command-auth custom Responses providers
body:
Related: #131261 (custom Codex providers and platform credential proxies; this does not implement the historical provider-ID proposal).

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot use a custom Responses provider's Codex-owned token command without OpenClaw looking for unrelated host credentials.

## User Impact

Custom providers can opt into `auth: "native-command"`. OpenClaw selects the provider/runtime without borrowing host profiles or ambient OpenAI credentials; Codex owns its token command and other explicitly configured native authentication, including `gateway_oauth`.

Use an **unowned custom provider ID**, explicitly configure Codex at the model/provider level, and configure a matching native command-auth provider. The effective native route must match the configured HTTPS Responses endpoint. URL credentials/fragments, OpenClaw API keys/profile pins, OpenClaw custom headers and authored request/transport overrides remain rejected. A forced environment runtime alone is insufficient. Native configuration, native headers, primary-auth conflicts and secondary account persistence/refresh remain Codex's responsibility; a native account is not implicitly the Team requester. This adds no OpenClaw login flow or native-to-host credential import.

**Ordinary sessions only:** isolated completions, supervised native sessions, manual compaction and remote-exec cloud placement remain unsupported. Native automatic compaction remains available; final-answer recovery uses the settled-tool fallback rather than another credential. Direct host credential APIs reject this mode. First-party/main-session explicit-profile validation, operator-model policy and approval-review boundaries remain intact. P8 worker-hosted transport is outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared eligibility owner serves availability, harness support and preparation. Dispatch skips unrelated automatic OpenAI accounts and stale automatic pins; the native preflight checks the selected endpoint and command before creating a thread. It no longer duplicates Codex's authentication policy or rejects supported native credential composition.

The PR also retains separately reviewed offline-archive and fixed Node/Bun prerequisites in the existing isolated runner. Neither relaxes isolation or changes native dependency versions.

## Evidence

**Published conflict-reconciled head:** `f96b3a5b7ffee5a722ff4bfb4567efada77f4549`, tree `07e517f73bd4259ff802466fa249795710757dc1`, identical across all paths to reviewed and tested candidate `16543af647ec709450647ab9867edcfde63d81d8`. The publisher added only an empty attribution/receipt commit. **Exact published-head CI and Darwin are now successful; complete gate evidence is below.** The read-only prepublication merge preview against canonical `2ab944733f70a81b16ffca25ccdecbf88de484f5` was conflict-free; that later target was not integrated. GitHub observed `mergeable: true` / `mergeable_state: clean` at the terminal collection on October 30, 2026, 05:54 UTC. This history-preserving merge retains published `cc3a0fc854b5ac81e0de579ebd4ef876816d5e83` as first parent and integrates pinned canonical `bdd4c33d5803429860d39f1b721b2939b9c414fa` as second parent. The sole textual conflict was resolved by the canonical config-doc generator. Whole PR versus that target remains **63 files, +2,010/−353**. All non-generated authored changes are unchanged after accounting for Git object IDs and hunk line offsets; 60/63 authored blobs/modes remain identical, two workflow/test files incorporate canonical changes, and one generated hash file is regenerated. No authored dependency pin, auth policy, guard, timeout or assertion changed.

title: feat(apps): show paused child sessions in native chat
body:
Related: #186387

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS, macOS and Android chat show a subagent that paused on `sessions_yield` as **Done**, drop the parent's waiting line when only paused children remain, and hide a Swarm group once its only unfinished children are paused.

## User Impact

User impact: native chat now matches the web chat from #186387. A paused child reads **Paused** in the Swarm widget (outlined marker plus a "Paused" count in the group summary) and in the macOS session sidebar, its group stays listed, and on iOS/macOS the parent's "Waiting on subagents" line stays open for it — naming it with "· Paused", or counting "N paused" — without the parent looking like it's working. A paused child whose own children are running reads **Running**.

Design by josh (@jalehman).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8cb34bf0-96df-41ab-aa9f-6c710ab3a5fd)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/63387546-d490-4309-8d75-beac336b016c)

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already sends `subagentRunState: "paused"` (#185918) and keeps `status: "done"`; the native projections checked `status` first. Each native owner now applies the web rule (`isPausedChild` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-subagent-wait.ts`) at the same point: the shared Swift Swarm projection and wait resolver (used by iOS and macOS), the macOS sidebar row facts, and the Android Swarm projection. No Gateway or protocol change.

What does not carry over, and why:

- **No elapsed timer:** the Apple wait line never had one, so a paused-only wait already shows no clock. Android has no "waiting on subagents" line at all; it only has the Swarm widget.
- **Post-resume note** ("{name} is paused"): no native surface tracks the `sessions_yield` handoff or resume, so there is nothing to swap. The Apple wait line keeps showing "Waiting on subagents · Paused" while a paused child remains.
- **Android Sessions screen:** it shows no per-child Done state, only Running/Unread/Failed/Attention signals, so a paused child was never misreported there; unchanged.
- **Wear OS Agent Pulse:** the watch payload has no paused state. The phone keeps sending exactly what it sent before (only groups with queued/running work; paused children counted as done). Adding a paused field to the watch is a separate protocol change.

## Evidence

### Android Swarm widget (debug build, emulator, existing `swarm` screenshot fixture plus two paused children)

The capture-only fixture adds one paused child to the research group and a second group whose only unfinished child is paused. That fixture change is not part of this PR.

**Before** (current main, `9a35a81`): the paused child counts as Done (green dot, "2 Done"), and the paused-only review group is missing.

![Android Swarm widget before: research shows 2 Running, 2 Done, 1 Failed; no review group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75fbe620-7320-4b39-91ed-ac172ddc43ae)

**After** (this branch): "1 Paused" with an outlined marker, and the review group stays listed.

![Android Swarm widget after: research shows 2 Running, 1 Paused, 1 Done, 1 Failed; review group shows 1 Paused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/480b2a47-977d-4f2e-ba19-6873f98b51f1)

Not captured: iOS/macOS (no macOS host available, see below) and the Apple wait line.

### Checks

- Android unit tests (`:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` for `ChatSwarmProgressTest`, `WearAgentPulseProjectionTest`, `ChatControllerSwarmProgressTest`, `SessionsScreenGroupingTest`): pass. The new `pausedChildrenReadPausedAndKeepTheirGroupListed` fails with the paused mapping removed (red check run locally).
- `:app:ktlintCheck`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (net delta 0), `git diff --check`: pass. SwiftFormat 0.63.1 (the pinned version) `--lint` on `OpenClawChatUI` and the touched tests: pass.
- **Swift:** new tests in `ChatSwarmProgressTests`, `ChatSubagentWaitTests` and `ChatSessionSidebarRowTests`. This Linux host has no Swift toolchain, so they were not run locally; macOS CI is their proof. I tried a Crabbox macOS lease for Apple proof and screenshots, but its desktop bootstrap stopped with "Sign in to the worker macOS account before dispatching a desktop session", so there are **no Apple screenshots** in this PR.
- Local autoreview (branch vs. `9a35a81`, P0–P2): no findings.

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

title: fix(doctor): unblock historical store imports without losing evidence
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor refuses historical pending-input and worker-placement stores, or leaves historical image reserves unreadable after import.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can import recognized agent-v24, shared-v21 and image-v22 stores without discarding historical evidence or cleanup custody.

Queued inputs become interrupted without losing payloads or recovery envelopes. Incomplete preparation becomes a failed placement requiring cleanup. Incompatible worker claims or malformed images refuse the atomic migration without advancing markers or discarding custody.

**PostgreSQL limitation:** archival input/placement columns are not in the PostgreSQL descriptor. Their port is refused before target publication; keep these stores on SQLite. Image-only data uses existing JSON storage and was ported in earlier proof. **Rollback requires the verified pre-migration backup and matching runtime—not lowered version markers.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing migration and Doctor owners preserve predecessor evidence and derive missing predicates before publication, including the full-schema fallback selected by unrelated lazy-column gaps. Archives never grant execution authority; fresh databases do not acquire them. No P3 schema bump or second migration owner is added.

## Work sessions

title: fix: Goal stops progressing after gateway restart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an active Goal stops progressing after its first successfully recovered reply when OpenClaw restarts.

## User Impact

User impact: an interrupted built-in Goal can continue through successive normal replies toward completion without another human message, subject to current permissions, Stop controls, and Goal limits. Standalone agent commands do not become autonomous.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit the exact reserved recovery input through the existing ordinary reply owner, atomically retiring the old recovery claim. The existing Goal queue and Goal-return flow then own further turns. Retain current authority before that handoff and preserve Stop, compaction, routing, message-tool-only delivery, restart-safe/Code Mode restrictions, and the original scheduling entitlement.

The necessary internal typed plumbing carries custody and source authority through existing admission and execution boundaries; shared start/cancellation observation and focused regression coverage account for the size. It does not add a second pursuit owner, scheduler, schema, configuration option, or permission policy. This is standalone and does not depend on the pending recovery refactor.


The P2 compaction follow-up removes parent-session notification from generic independent-child policy. Only the same-session Goal reply receives that notification; its authority is mapped to plain child policy through the canonical continuation-authority map, including narrowed captures. This preserves the deliberate accepted-child/parent-work separation introduced in [31c93ec](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/31c93ec207f6b42636a1809104c8a52dd0463dd3), rather than ignoring foreign transitions or weakening reset/revocation checks.

## Evidence

- **Reproduction:** pinned base `b61ab6d` recovered a successful final after both cold and strict graceful replacement but left the Goal active with no next turn. The later parent-callback leak was separately reproduced on `c658af7` through actual child capture and child compaction for three non-Goal final-write variants and the recovered Goal reply path. The repair keeps child work current, preserves real final-write revocation, and tests same-session Goal compaction followed by reset.
- **Frozen-source binding:** final local proof used `c658af7235905f1fa4e8d418d4fd3292da7bae1d` plus tracked patch SHA256 `e48a3a1a136497e472fb79d630067ad15ee4dbd2e3382337be6b0a93a38581f8`. That complete source tree was committed unchanged as `be7645610d4736bebe955055a22547c247c1bcf0`, tree `4e206aadf48cfa8b328473b980a8c78676677e2e`. Source and all runtime outputs were unchanged before/after acceptance; the normal commit hook preserved the tree.
- **Shipping checks:** 193 tests in nine owner/sibling files passed across four shards, including full reconnect, authenticated recovery, Goal, compaction-lifetime, and prompt-prefix coverage. Production types and all 29 selected test graphs passed across the broad run and canonical remaining-graph checks. Focused lint, formatting, diff checks, assertion-safety and test-line ratchets passed. Cumulative shipping-test line delta is **0 against `b61ab6d`**, with unchanged ceiling and patterns; all 39 terminal-hook cases remain in their existing owner.
- **Final actual-process acceptance:** cold replacement passed in **16.082s**; strict graceful replacement passed in **34.142s**, requiring real SIGTERM close `[0, null]` before a distinct replacement process. Each retained the original Goal, produced the first recovered final and two automatic continuation turns, executed `update_goal`, and exposed the completed Goal/final in public history without another human input (five synthetic model requests).
- **Old-produced disk compatibility:** a separately built real `b61ab6d` process created the active Goal and durable recovery source through public APIs, then was killed. The candidate consumed the same physical SQLite database in a distinct process, completed the same Goal with five requests and two automatic continuation turns, and passed cleanup. No Goal/recovery/routing fields were seeded at the upgrade boundary. This is old-produced-state compatibility, not package-installer or deployment proof.
- **Real-process revocation effects:** after actual ordinary-input transfer, source-device revocation at the awaited pre-prompt hook yielded **zero recovered provider requests**. Independently, revocation after an actual recovered provider request was observed/held, followed by release of the real forbidden `exec` response, yielded **no forbidden file and no successor provider request**. The latter requires the exact run-correlated authority-rejection diagnostic, not merely a generic RPC stop. Both include successful same-principal real-exec controls and verified cleanup.
- **Separate in-process policy controls:** the real recovery/reply path refused a foreign destination before transfer; refused after an actual public `users.setRole` reduction committed after transfer and the original prepare callback returned normally; and supplied the actual recovered capability to the real message tool. Same-provider account mismatch was rejected before credential resolution/action dispatch; normalized matching and permitted cross-provider routing were allowed. The embedded boundary and external credential/action leaves are stubbed in these controls: they prove policy admission, **not external delivery**.
- **Independent review:** local autoreview completed the lifecycle-repair delta against `c658af7`, priorities P0–P3, with intact required source context and no actionable findings. The publishing parent also reviewed the exact frozen production/test delta. Fresh native review/preparation/CI/landing for the updated head remain separate.

**Recorded tooling failure:** one broad test-type invocation exited **139** without a TypeScript diagnostic. Its canonical graph and all five remaining graphs subsequently passed. This is retained as a tooling failure with successful later checks, **not a claimed fix or explanation of the compiler crash**. Earlier test-fixture type errors were corrected before the final frozen snapshot.

**Applicability limit:** the exact original-RPC-device/late-external-delivery combination is **inapplicable under current supported producer contracts**, not a passed test. Authenticated `chat.send` preserves that operator source but intentionally records internal/WebChat restart delivery; genuine channel ingress uses its own channel principal. The successful fixture transport and actual `create_goal` did not create a channel-classified recovery claim. No source fields were manufactured, no different principal was silently substituted, and no blanket external-channel egress matrix is claimed. Runtime model traffic was synthetic; no deployment or live installation was changed.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and validation boundaries</summary>

- [CI run 40650570310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40650570310) on prior published head `c658af7235905f1fa4e8d418d4fd3292da7bae1d` was read directly before this publication: all **79** planned jobs were terminal (**54 successful, 25 skipped**), run conclusion success. This is prior-head CI, not CI for the new repair commit or a later publisher marker.
- The original [CI run 40647187295](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40647187295) on `a5668229` remains failed: the PR-caused assertion-ledger/test-line ratchets were repaired in the prior test-only update. No failed run is relabeled green.
- The final shipping test wrapper took 300.78s; the final cold/graceful wrapper took 87.43s after official runtime preparation. These are test/fixture wall times, not isolated startup or model latency.
- Long real-process and risk-qualification fixtures remain opt-in task proof, outside the default serial-CI inventory and publication inputs. The shipping regressions remain in existing scoped suites.
- Types, static review, in-process policy controls, real-process effects, hosted CI and deployment are distinct evidence. Updated-head CI and the native landing workflow are not claimed complete here.

</details>

title: improve(ui): stop showing failed counts on grouped agent work
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A group of agent steps shows a red "2 failed" next to whichever step is in its headline, even when those failures happened earlier and the agent recovered from them. While a run is in progress, it looks like the step currently on screen is failing.

## User Impact

Grouped activity rows, live and completed, and "Worked for …" summaries no longer show red failed or skipped counts. Expanding a group still shows each failed step on its own row with its "failed" or exit-code status. A step with nested calls that failed on its own now shows as its own row, so that failure stays visible without expanding. Approval blocks and unknown outcomes still appear on the group.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agents routinely recover from failed commands, so a running count of failures along the way reads as an alarm and pins it on the wrong step. Whether the work succeeded is shown by the reply that follows. If a run actually ends in an error, its own error message reports it. Each row still shows its own outcome. Considered and rejected: flagging a group only when its last step failed. That flag appeared even when the agent's reply right after had already explained the failure.

title: fix(ui): task progress card says no active work while a child session is paused
body:
Related: #186387, #185918, #182832

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the task progress card ignores a child session that is paused on `sessions_yield`, so a card whose only remaining child is paused reads **No active work**, even though the transcript already says **{name} is paused**.

## User Impact

User impact: the progress card counts paused children next to the existing buckets, as in **Delegated work: 1 running · 1 paused** or **Delegated work: 1 paused**. A paused child is shown as unfinished but not as active work, so with only paused children left the card keeps its paused step marker and shows no spinner, consistent with the chat waiting line from #186387.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projectProgressCardRuntime` (from #182832) counted running, queued, waiting, failed and stopped children, but a paused child (`subagentRunState: "paused"`, `status: "done"`) matched none of them. The projection now reuses `isPausedChild` from the same module to count those children in a separate `paused` bucket. The bucket is deliberately left out of the `hasActiveSubagentRun` sum, so a paused child never makes the parent read as working; a paused child whose own descendants are running still counts as **waiting** through its `hasActiveSubagentRun`. The card's runtime line renders the new bucket with the existing `{count} …` wording and ` · ` separator. `docs/tools/progress-card.md` describes the new count.

No Gateway or protocol change.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI e2e (Details → Task progress), light theme, 1100×850, synthetic content. Before = current `main`, after = this PR.

**Only a paused child left** (parent resumed; the transcript already shows "Changelog audit is paused")

In both paused-only captures the current step keeps its paused marker and no spinner is shown. Not captured: dark theme, mobile, and the composer/board placements (covered by the unit test below).

- `ui/src/components/session-progress-card.test.ts`: the composer, details and board placements render `1 running · 1 queued · 1 paused · 1 failed`.

title: fix: keep updates working below recommended Node security patches
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: updates are refused, or an explicitly pinned Gateway runtime cannot restart after an update, when Node meets the previous compatibility requirements but lacks the latest security-only patches.

## User Impact

Users can update on Node `>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0` without first upgrading Node. Updates, Doctor, and `openclaw security audit` prominently warn below Node 24.22.1 / 26.12.1. **Upgrade Node promptly:** these patches reject keys compromised in the October 2026 eMudhra incident; continued compatibility does not remove that exposure. SQLite safety checks, excluded release lines, explicit target-package engines and patched provisioning defaults remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate compatibility from security recommendations in the canonical version policy instead of stranding installations. Audit finding `runtime.node_security_patch` describes the audit process runtime, not an unprobed Gateway, and skips Bun. Audit collectors use a coherent sibling module.

## Evidence

- **Original explicit-pin upgrade:** real AWS Crabbox 2026.10.5 updater → private patched runtime snapshot, unchanged Node 24.21.0 native service pin, exit 0, visible warning and new healthy Gateway PID. title: fix(knowledge): section extraction keeps links and claim subjects intact, and supersede cannot hide its replacement
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the open ClawSweeper findings on two landed Knowledge PRs (#186266 and #186270): `knowledge_supersede` could hide its own replacement claim, and `knowledge_extract_section` could silently break or change links and drop a claim's established subject when moving a section.

Related: #186266, #186270

## User Impact

User impact:

- Superseding a claim by one that depends on it now saves nothing and explains why. Before, it published and then default reads hid the replacement too.
- Extracting a section keeps every link it moves pointing at the same record, in the complete destination page. A move that would break or change a link saves nothing: for example a reference-style link whose definition stays on the source, or a destination that ends inside an open code block. Code samples, inline code and escaped text move byte for byte. Only the parsed link is rewritten.
- Claims cited by a moved section keep all their existing subjects, including the source page, and get the destination as their primary subject. The agent removes the source explicitly with `knowledge_annotate` `entities` when it no longer applies. The tool description, docs and the capture, consolidation and shared publish skills say this.

No config, schema or stored-format changes. Vaults created before either feature load and work unchanged (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Supersede** reuses the `lifecycleImpact` it already computes for the receipt. If the replacement is among the dependents of any superseded claim, it rejects before publication. That is the same rule the correction path enforces in `storage-publication.ts`.
- **Link spans.** `markdown-links.ts` (the existing marked parser owner) gains `linkSpans`: the links `extractLinks` reads, in order, with offsets. marked tokens have no positions, so each token's raw text is located after the previous one, skipping code, escapes and link-like text. `resolveLinks` and a new `resolveLinkHref` share one `resolveHref`, unchanged.
- **Extraction** builds its expected links from the complete source. It rewrites inline relative links inside their parsed spans only, last span first. After the preview scan, `verifyMovedLinks` reads the complete source, shrunk source and destination. The appended section must have the same links, leading to the same records, in order. No other link on either page may change, and the source stub must link the destination. Reference-style links and open fences fail this check with a message saying how to fix the section. The `pageMentions` subject heuristic is removed from relinking.

Accepted edge case: a link whose raw text its container reshapes (a label wrapped across quoted lines) is never rewritten; if it would lead elsewhere, the move is rejected.

## Evidence

**Red on main, green with the fix.** Each new assertion fails with main's four source files and the new tests, and passes with this PR; the three later extraction cases were also run one at a time:

| Finding | Test | On main | With fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Supersede hides its replacement (direct and through a dependent page) | `lifecycle.test.ts` › supersede rejects a replacement that depends on a superseded claim… | ✗ `promise resolved … instead of rejecting` | ✓ |
| 2. Reference definition left behind | `page-budget-writes.test.ts` › moves only parsed links… (Billing case) | ✗ `promise resolved … instead of rejecting` | ✓ |
| 2. Destination ending in an open code fence | same test, Runbook case | ✗ `promise resolved … instead of rejecting` | ✓ |
| 3. Code sample, inline code and escaped text rewritten | same test, byte-exact destination body | ✗ body mismatch: the code-block copy of `[Ledger](ledger.md)` was rewritten | ✓ |
| 4. Short-named subject ("AI") dropped | same test, `entities` of the AI claim | ✗ `expected [ Array(1) ] to strictly equal [ …(2) ]` | ✓ |
| 4. Established source subject kept | existing extraction test, `provider` entities now `[destination, atlas]` | ✗ | ✓ |

**Item 6 (low-value `page-budget.test.ts` case).** The "derives budgets from one default record read" case is not on main. It was at #186270's reviewed head `a6e323a` and was removed by that PR's `69ecc88` ("tighten page budget tests") before the squash landed as `ff2d718`. Nothing left to remove.

**Upgrade and data-model compatibility (finding 5).** This is a task proof run in isolated temporary vaults, never the live vault, and it is not committed.

- A detached worktree at `db7f693` (the parent of `e665f5b`, so before both features) with its own install built a vault through the real service and storage worker. Its settings use the old config shape (`writesEnabled`, `operatorRead`, maintenance `15 3 * * *` UTC, no `pageBudgets`). It holds two pages, six evidence-backed claims with a retained attachment, a correction, a withdrawal, and an Atlas page grown through `save_page` to 28,637 characters, which was allowed before budgets.
- This PR's source then opened that same registry, vault and SQLite state:
  - **Settings:** the old config parses with maintenance preserved and `hubPercentile` defaulting to 90.
  - **Data:** counts are unchanged (7 current, 9 total, 5 current claims). The Atlas file is byte-identical and reads back. History is preserved (2 Atlas revisions), the attachment downloads, the corrected claim keeps `superseded_by`, and the withdrawn claim stays hidden.
  - **Oversized page:** growing it by one character returns `rejected` (28,638 of 24,000) and leaves it unchanged. A shrinking edit publishes, and extracting its Billing section publishes. The cited claim keeps Atlas and gains the new page.
  - **Supersede:** two pre-change claims superseded by a third; stale active bytes written back stay superseded after a restart (durable guard).
  - **Interrupted undo:** the undo is crashed at `after-accept`, after the first record link, after `vault.json`, and `before-receipt`. Each time the journaled plan carries `restored: [red, green]`, reads report the pending publication, and a restarted service replaying the same request publishes `unsupersede`. title: fix: GitHub publish fails with "source authority changed" during subagent and placement updates
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `github_publish` can fail with "GitHub publication source authority changed." when a display-only session notification (subagent progress, or a Gateway placement, catalog or config refresh) arrives while the publication is reserving its rows. The agent then sees an unpushed head and publishes again.

## User Impact

User impact: publishing from a busy Gateway no longer fails for no reason and no longer leads to a second publish attempt. This mostly affects subagent sessions and sessions that have running subagents. A real change to the session, its sharing, its workspace or the requester still stops the publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every publication step prepares a source capability. That capability is revoked if the session changes before the state worker reserves its rows. The revocation listened to every session notification, including display-only ones: subagent run progress for this session, and Gateway-wide `subagent-runs`, `worker-placements`, `worker-environments`, `catalog` and `config` refreshes. None of these change the rows the source captured. One arriving between preparing the source and reserving it refused the publication; on an isolated Gateway that window measured 2–73 ms per publication.

The listener now applies the existing `sessionChangeScopeAffectsStoredRows` filter. Sibling authority owners already use the same filter, for example worktree owner protection, transcript authority and delivery generation. The following still revoke the source:

- stored-row changes and session-store topology changes;
- profile changes, which go through the listener that already exists for them.

The worker still rechecks every captured source fact under its reservation, including the placement row. The grant also rechecks the requester policy.

<details>
<summary>Investigation: the two reported double publishes</summary>

- **Oct 28, 03:30 UTC, subagent session, PR #186455.** The first `github_publish` handoff resumed the session about 4 seconds later with `{"ok":false,"error":"GitHub publication source authority changed.","code":"UNAVAILABLE"}`. The PR head was still the old commit, so nothing had been pushed. The resumed turn retried once, which was the correct response to that result, and the retry published. The deployed build already holds back other turns during the handoff (`fenceSuccessors: true`, since #178756). The only turn between the two attempts was the one that received the failed result, so this was not a concurrent publish. The later `workspacePath is only available for local host publication` error is a separate issue: `edit` never accepts `workspacePath`, and the message is misleading. It has a different owner and is not changed here.
- **Oct 28, 05:16 UTC, PR #186541.** There was no second publish. A human message, queued at 04:05, ran after the publication had already pushed but before its result event. The handoff releases queued successors in FIFO order before it enqueues the result. That turn read the published head with `edit`, and the result arrived afterwards as a late receipt. This ordering is intended and is not changed.
- Team transcripts show the same refusal in at least five other handoff publications on Oct 27 and 28. Of the four failing sessions I checked, three were subagent sessions. Gateway logs do not record which notification revoked the source. The trigger is therefore inferred from the mechanism and the reproduction below, not observed directly.
- Related: #186321 fixed a different false refusal ("session authority changed during snapshot"). #186541 changes handoff completion delivery. Neither overlaps this change.

</details>

## Evidence

- **New coordinator regression** in `github-publication-boundaries.test.ts`: `publishes while subagent progress and placement refreshes keep notifying`. It uses the real publication coordinator and SQLite state with mocked git and GitHub commands, and keeps sending keyed subagent progress and global placement refreshes during the publish. On `main` it fails with the production error, raised by the session-change revoke. It passes with this change.
- **New owner test** in `github-publication.worker.test.ts`. A prepared source now survives the real `publishSubagentRunChanges` producer (keyed and global) and a `worker-placements` refresh, and inserts its row. A stored `session-entry` change still revokes it. The test fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- Both test files pass in full: 35 of 35 and 19 of 19.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes for typecheck (core and core tests) and its ratchets. Its first run found two lint issues and one format issue in the new test, which are now fixed; the oxlint and format checks pass on all three changed files. The dead-export scan still fails on unused exports that already exist in files this PR doesn't touch (`extensions/knowledge/src/page-budget.ts`, `src/cli/completion-runtime.ts` and `src/infra/diagnostic-model-call-types.ts`).
- Independent AutoReview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) on the committed range found nothing actionable. It confirmed that the worker rereads session, membership, placement, profile, connection, workspace and worktree facts under its reservation.
- **Live isolated Gateway on Crabbox (one AWS lease, released): the false refusal did not reproduce on base.** Base is `origin/main` `c14ee716` (includes #186541). After is the same tree with only `src/gateway/github-publication-source.ts` replaced by this PR's file, byte-identical to head `491e8a0`. Every run starts a real Gateway with isolated state and a WebChat operator client. A scripted model calls the real `github_publish` tool with `workspacePath`, so the real handoff, workspace adoption, coordinator, source authority and SQLite worker all run. Real `git` and `gh` then push the branch and open the PR.
  - **Faked:** the model (a scripted Responses server) and GitHub itself: an HTTPS fixture serves the `api.github.com` REST calls and `git http-backend` serves `github.com`, reached through `/etc/hosts` and a lease-local CA. No real repository, token or `roboclaw-bot` credential was used.
  - **Counts** (published out of counted runs; each run's first publication is an uncounted warm-up):

    | Scenario, all traffic from real Gateway activity | Base | After |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Busy Gateway: 3 concurrent publishers, each with 2 running subagents, plus 2 sessions continuously spawning subagents; the WebChat client watches each publisher's PR rows | 20/20 | 20/20 |
    | A subagent publishes (incident A shape), 3 concurrent | 9/9 | 9/9 |
    | Stored-row writes: label edits on the publishing session every ~15 ms during the publication | 9/10 (the 10th: `Session event owner is being deleted`); warm-up refused with `source authority changed` | 9/10 (the 10th: `Session event owner is being deleted`); warm-up refused with `source authority changed` |
    | Negative: `sessions.reset` while the publication's base-branch read is held | 0/5 PRs created | 0/5 PRs created |

  - **Why base did not fail:** in a diagnostic copy of the base file (not shipped), each publication prepared one durable source, open for 2–73 ms before its reservation. Across 31 instrumented publications, 240 session notifications arrived inside these windows, and none was Gateway-wide or keyed to the publishing session, so none revoked. On an isolated Gateway I could not produce the notification classes this change filters inside that window at a meaningful rate. Worker placement and environment refreshes need cloud worker environments, and `config.patch` is rate-limited to a few writes per minute. The production trigger is still inferred, not observed.
  - **What the live run does show:** the harness observes the exact production refusal through the real tool path. On both trees, label edits keyed to the publishing session revoked the source with `GitHub publication source authority changed.` Real stored-row changes still cancel a publication on both trees.
  - **Separate finding, not changed here:** on both trees, a publication's handoff sometimes failed with `Session event owner is being deleted`. The first `workspacePath` publication on a fresh Gateway failed this way in 6 of the 9 runs without subagent activity; in the other 3, the stored-row edits refused it first. It also failed this way once later in a run, after stored-row edits. When subagents were active, the first publication succeeded. No PR was created. This is a second false refusal that also invites a retry. It needs its own investigation.

<details>
<summary>Commands and log excerpts</summary>

The harness is a task proof artifact and is not committed: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/github-publish-authority.proof.e2e.test.ts` plus `publish-proof/{setup,run,matrix}.sh`. It ran from a separate checkout synced to the lease.

```
bash test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/publish-proof/setup.sh    # gh, fixture CA, unprivileged :443
bash test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/publish-proof/matrix.sh   # base/after × 4 scenarios, one Gateway per run
```

```
[proof] SUMMARY base-display scenario=parent concurrency=3 watch=true traffic=display [["{\"status\":\"published\"}",20]]
[proof] SUMMARY head-display scenario=parent concurrency=3 watch=true traffic=display [["{\"status\":\"published\"}",20]]
[proof] iteration 0 outcome GitHub publication source authority changed. prCreated=false 5985ms {"ok":false,"error":"GitHub publication source authority changed.","code":"UNAVAILABLE"}   # head-stored warm-up
[source-diag] revoke … admitted=false at …github-publication-source.ts:304 <- notifyListeners <- session-row-changes install <- publishFacts   # label edit on the publishing session, diagnostic copy of the after file
== source windows (prepare -> first revoke, ms)  n=7 min=25 median=46 max=73   # busy Gateway, base diagnostic copy
```

The results archive (`results.jsonl` plus per-run traces) is kept in the implementation session's workspace with sha256 `7fde015ce98feef6114a1dd482da62b35e626134a5c32359138075e0ab5ba24b`.

</details>

title: feat(telemetry): count reporting installations without identifiers
body:
Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b2a02dc6-36c7-4c22-8d64-e138599c8b3c)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/cd93750e-15f5-4800-b78e-925e17e1ccfd)

## What Problem This Solves

Update-check totals cannot distinguish repeat reports from reporting installations, and explicitly configuring the production telemetry URL could bypass CI suppression.

## User Impact

Compatible receivers can estimate daily, weekly and monthly reporting installation-state histories without persistent identifiers. Existing update checks keep their 24-hour cache and remain available when counting fails. Explicit telemetry off and DO_NOT_TRACK suppress counting; production CI requests remain suppressed, while custom test receivers still work.

These are estimates of reporting installations, not people or human engagement. Delivery loss, reset/cloned state and collection coverage affect accuracy. No historical unique-user counts can be reconstructed.

## Why This Change Was Made

A fresh, valid, unredirected update answer must explicitly advertise counting support and its UTC day. The client then claims that day through the existing SQLite worker before at most one separate empty POST to the same endpoint. That POST has a fixed generic user-agent, a capped day gap, no inventory and no retry/outbox. Unsupported receivers receive neither a count upload nor a claim. Late opt-outs are rechecked before dispatch.

The companion receiver stores only aggregate day/gap totals in a separate optional store. This client does not provision or activate that store. Counting uses no UUID, account identity, IP hash, new configuration option or database schema.

## Evidence

- Focused sender/parser/real-SQLite/asynchronous-policy/CLI tests passed, including red-before-fix capability and cross-installation-scope regressions; redirected-capability regression and direct-path controls passed.
- 16 real CLI inspection cases passed across JSON/text and piped/TTY output; targeted typechecks, lint and formatting passed. Full candidate build passed.
- Real isolated Gateway completed an OpenAI model turn, then cold-restarted on the same disk state. Exactly one update GET and one count-only POST were observed; the restart sent neither again. Actual local workerd/D1 histogram advanced from 2 to 3, matching that single contribution.
- Latest-stable `2026.10.8` (`dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`) produced real settings, consent, transcript and a valid cached update answer. Canonical Doctor migrated state 20→35 and agent 25→38. The source-bound candidate and its cold restart preserved the complete original stored events, cache, consent and auth configuration, with no fresh update/count requests. This preservation lane used a benign synthetic provider; the separate real-provider proof is above. Doctor's only config deltas were retirement of the disabled heartbeat field and addition of wizard metadata.
- CI identified a missing reviewed writer edge. The repair registers only `telemetry.claimInstallationCount` for its fixed `telemetry.installationCount.<endpoint hash>` namespace, never `authProfiles.store`; no worker/file exemption was added. The regression was red before and green after; 120 guard/ratchet tests, tooling/scripts test-typechecks, lint and format passed. The original database-worker ratchet passed locally with unchanged T1 counts (168 and 15 compatibility sites).
- Fresh complete local autoreview against `44de94bab2f484b798169a460b38607cb84ee024`, including custody repair `cd9d04f2bedaab62c7619034fba8eb44896c0de5`: complete, P0–P2 scoped-clean. Published head `f32caebc5d6cf22bb014472bdd8eab512c88b446` has the identical reviewed tree. Runtime files remain unchanged from live-tested `c04e239f433c0d8e52ae412203a68f33c54361a7`.
- Independent source-bound adversarial reviews of client and receiver runtime changes found no actionable findings. Current-head hosted CI remains a separate landing gate.

title: fix(doctor): recover upgrades with unfinished shared-state columns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw doctor --fix` stopping on recognized shared-state column gaps, or entering agent maintenance before those repairs are complete.

## User Impact

Operators can recover databases whose schema version was already published while recognized column repairs remained pending. Original migration backups are retained, unknown schema drift still refuses before agent writes, and unused feature tables remain absent. No schema-version, retention, public configuration, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare shared state through its existing Doctor owner before both agent version-migration leases and update-time additive preparation, including when no agent version migration is pending. Detect missing publication draft columns independently of the published version, and require startup columns in lazy tables that already exist. Ordinary bounded upgrades defer to the existing full repair owner when earlier column repairs remain pending; explicit version-only steps retain their bounded scope.

This is the generic convergence portion of the original contribution, adapted to current main; historical TeamClaw imports, retention schemas, and node-environment changes are not included. Simplification retained the existing repair and backup owners instead of introducing another migration path (production delta: +71/-10 lines).

## Evidence

- Published head `a77858c57e76a1174f866c92a68d3d2e8bfaf3be` has exactly the accepted candidate tree `a0d1e3a15cf0f92cc2052eb93b50de1a399fd9b6`, tested and reviewed as `2eadb6e7023289d257948acb77ead7c919be47c9`. The publisher added only a metadata commit. The candidate integrates canonical main `8889b596023c846cc9076078a000c25715f0ecf0` after the actual v28/v36 migration-import conflict; both owners are retained, and historical fixtures use physical pre-Template identifiers and the current supported version.

The final repair shares the existing startup-column predicate with bounded selection and preserves absent features rather than broadening schema/index validation.
- Current local validation: 37 focused tests passed across publication, admission, Doctor migrations, and frozen-v35 Template cutover; 14 publication/admission tests passed again after the final plan-membership expression. Targeted Doctor/state typechecks, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Fresh Codex `gpt-6.1-sol` autoreview at P0–P2 against the pinned main was scoped-clean after resolving the finding. Explicit version-only and absent-feature cases remain covered.

The unknown-drift control exited 1 before changing the agent database bytes. title: fix(gateway): reject stale exact-run cancellation after session replacement
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: API clients cannot bind an exact-run Stop request to the physical conversation they observed, leaving them without a stale-session guard when that conversation is replaced.

## User Impact

Clients can pass `sessionId` alongside `runId` to reject cancellation against a replaced session or a mismatched local or worker run. Existing callers that omit the fence retain their current Stop behavior. There are no configuration changes or migrations; the fence does not grant additional cancellation permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cancellation authorization owner now resolves the optional physical-session restriction alongside scoped-caller and queued-input restrictions. Exact-run selection applies it before cancellation, while retaining the current source-capture, ownership, sibling-run, and incognito behavior. The protocol schema and generated validator accept the new optional field.

Contributor credit: Adapted from Galin Iliev (@galiniliev)'s reviewed cancellation changes in `fa6b7bc1fb5db71d8a1ef2e0883c01971608ee4e` at his request; unrelated changes from that commit are excluded.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0705165-5352-4f6e-955d-99ab0c2be386)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3656f067-4801-4570-9b95-c36851d2338e)

## Evidence

- Published test consolidation `906f40233625b933d8511892eb59b3f78e12b932` reuses the surviving old local/worker owners after exact current-worker Stop, then proves unreadable fenced refusal and unfenced best effort. Production is unchanged. The two worker scenarios become one; the separate local-owner/sibling scenario remains. Ping/pong barriers and incremental terminal identities/outcomes remain explicit. The file shrinks from 334 to 315 lines (net −19), with no removed helper, import, production seam, or test contract.
- Consolidation validation: all 84 tests pass across the six RPC-fence, authorization, read-error, source-withdrawal, incarnation, and agent-scope files (114.81 seconds command wall time). The changed file also passes alone: 2 tests, 13.24 seconds Vitest / 48.32 seconds command wall time. Baseline: 3 tests, 68.99 seconds Vitest / 73.09 seconds command wall time; compiler-cache/fixture startup differed, so these single observations are not a causal speedup measurement. title: fix(ui): keyboard shortcut hints show on phones without a keyboard
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: menus, tooltips, and hints show desktop keyboard chords (for example `⌘⇧,` next to Settings) when the Control UI is used on an iPhone or Android phone with no hardware keyboard.

## User Impact

User impact: on touch-only phones and tablets, keycaps and shortcut hints disappear everywhere: menus, tooltips, the command palette, question options, the model picker, file preview, and inline hint sentences. Connect a hardware keyboard and press a key only it can send (arrows, Esc, a ⌘/Ctrl chord, or any key outside a text field), and every hint appears at once without a reload. Desktops and touch laptops are unchanged. Mobile Return behavior is unchanged (#157111): Return inserts a line, and Return-to-submit hints stay hidden on mobile.

## Why This Change Was Made

Visibility has one owner: `ui/src/lib/keyboard-hints.ts`. It decides whether hints are worth showing (not touch-only, or a hardware keyboard has been seen) and publishes changes. A single shared projection in `lib/reactive/keyboard-hints.ts` feeds the two central gates every keycap already renders through:

- `Kbd` (and therefore `KeyboardShortcut`, `ShortcutHint`, menu details, and tooltips) renders nothing when hints are off. The shortcuts reference dialog opts out with `always`.
- `ShortcutText` swaps a hint sentence for its keyless `fallback` copy (or nothing).

Cutover: hand-rolled keycaps in question options now use `Kbd`. The model-picker and prediction keycaps read the same projection. The palette's footer hints go through the owner. `isMobileBrowserPlatform()` still governs only Return-key submission hints, because mobile Return never submits, even from a hardware keyboard.

Browsers expose no keyboard-attached event, so the hardware keyboard is detected from its first key press. Accepted edge cases: hints stay visible after the keyboard is detached until reload; an iPad without a trackpad hides hints until its keyboard is used.

## Evidence

- UI E2E (`compact-identity-menu.e2e.test.ts`, touch emulation at 390×844): after typing into the composer, the Settings keycap is hidden; pressing ArrowDown reveals it live in the open menu. The hidden assertion **fails on `main`**; the file passes 2/2.
- Previously failing CI suites pass locally on this head: new-session composer, composer suggestions, palette loading, keyboard shortcuts dialog, kbd, question card (154/154), and Chromium mobile Return, shortcut badge, and menu contract tests (47/47).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, UI test types, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, oxlint (0 errors), oxfmt pass. The test-line ratchet has a net delta of 0: the touch case replaced the existing "Get the apps" e2e, and two small kbd unit tests were merged.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P3): no actionable findings.

Account menu on an emulated iPhone (Playwright `iPhone 13`, mocked Control UI, dark theme):

### Before

![Before: account menu shows Ctrl+Shift chords and truncates System busyness](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee1787c2-e471-404a-bebb-ff58f6825eba)

### After

![After: account menu without keycaps; labels shown in full](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3b20a82-8a11-45a8-b47e-85e223f2e061)

The emulator runs on Linux, so the chords render as `Ctrl+Shift`, not `⌘⇧`. This was not tested on a physical iPhone.

title: fix: recover agent startup during large SQLite WAL contention
body:
Related: #166634, #179231

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent can remain unavailable when its initial schema read encounters transient recovery contention from a large, unclean SQLite WAL.

## User Impact

User impact: background database workers get a bounded opportunity to finish that read instead of immediately retiring and leaving startup admission degraded. Main-thread behavior, ordinary lock failures, write settlement, and database durability are unchanged.

This is a best-effort repair for a reproduced startup failure, not confirmation that Ilya Kuprov's reported ten-minute subagent outages have the same cause. The related issues remain open for their broader symptoms.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retry only the first read-only schema-cookie acquisition for native `SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY` (extended result 261), at most five total attempts on workers, keeping the normal per-call busy timeout. Every failed cursor and statement lease must finish cleanup before another attempt. Each top-level attempt qualifies a fresh snapshot marker; nested reads retain their parent snapshot.

Callback work, cleanup failures, statement-release failures, and uncertain writes are never replayed. No schema, configuration, retention, or admission-policy change is introduced. The added production code owns only this narrow acquisition boundary; the regression fixture protects recovery, bounded failure, non-replay, cleanup, and admitted sibling-schema freshness.

## Evidence

- Natural production-Gateway reproduction on the earlier main revision `25c300f73654074c03edbb2cc8bb97d19bbf2678`: 21,470,892,032 committed database bytes and a 71,504,054,392-byte unclean WAL. The worker's first `PRAGMA schema_version` iterator step failed with native extended result 261, then startup remained unavailable. The affected acquisition implementation is unchanged at this PR's base, `7df9d797166445339ba4ffb880738b8ac248b375`.
- A single-native-connection control required about 23 seconds for the first schema read. This motivates a bounded best-effort retry, not a universal wall-clock guarantee.
- Regression: recovery fails on the base and succeeds with the patch; no callback replay, ordinary BUSY/LOCKED behavior, main-thread exclusion, cleanup, and schema freshness are covered. Four affected suites passed (111 tests); the final refined acquisition suite passed all seven cases.
- Runtime build, scoped lint/format, production typecheck, and storage-test typecheck passed.
- Local autoreview of `7df9d797166445339ba4ffb880738b8ac248b375..671aa8b1b6a2beae2ad88e51a29bb3efb2dcc42c` completed at P0–P2 with no actionable findings. A separate read-only independent implementation review found no P0–P2 production defects; its admitted-schema coverage finding was addressed. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because the only existing runner checkout was dirty and belonged to unrelated work; use the hosted review route when ready.
- Live current-Gateway proof passed on the 21,470,892,032-byte synthetic database: four explicitly injected initial native recovery failures, nine verified real model-backed subagents across three completed parent runs, and three independent-agent replies. All 158 load health/readiness probes passed (p95 2.58 ms). The isolated Gateway stopped cleanly.
- The live fixture was checkpointed offline and upgraded through the canonical stopped-writer maintenance owner, retaining custody, integrity checks, and its synthetic backup. This is controlled native-fault proof, not a successful natural replay of the original unclean WAL or the reporter’s ten-minute outage. Full CLI Doctor setup exceeded the fixture’s five-minute test budget; that setup limit is not a product deadlock verdict. No operator state or live service was modified.
