title: fix(agents): subagent results never reach the parent after github_publish or plugin reload
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a delegated subagent's result never reaches its parent when the subagent calls `github_publish` or `plugins` `reloadAndResume` and finishes in the resumed turn.

## User Impact

User impact: a parent that spawned a subagent and yielded now wakes with that subagent's final answer after the child publishes a PR or reloads plugins mid-task. Before, the child finished normally but the parent kept waiting, and a later unrelated child turn could deliver its own result in place of the lost one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both tools end the turn, run their work after cleanup, and resume the session with a `tool_handoff` internal event. The registry marks the yielding task paused, and #172017 deliberately lets only human replies and operator recovery take over a paused child task; every other internal turn stays a separate follow-up. So the resumed turn ran as an unlinked follow-up and the paused task never completed.

The fix reuses the existing `sourceRunId` session-event provenance (already used by exec completions): the handoff records which run yielded, and the resumed turn adopts the paused task only when that task's pause belongs to that same run and the task was not killed. No new state or binding is introduced; the change is three small hunks in the handoff, the reply-runner gate and reactivation. Kills, resets, replacements and independent follow-up turns keep #172017's behavior. The adopted task keeps its original task text instead of being renamed to the handoff result prompt.

Accepted edge case: the handoff itself is in memory (documented in `session-tool-handoff.ts`), so a Gateway restart between handoff and resume still loses the deferred work and its continuation (related: #185730).

## Evidence

- New regression cases in `src/agents/tools/plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts` drive the real `plugins` tool handoff through the session event queue and reply runner against the SQLite-backed subagent registry:
  - `task`: the resumed run adopts the yielded task (same requester, original task text, running). Red on base (`pauseReason: "sessions_yield"`, run not adopted), green with the fix.
  - `killed`: a kill between yield and resume leaves the task alone.
  - `follow-up`: an independent turn in the child session that hands off does not take over an earlier paused task.
  - Full file: 20/20 pass, ~29 s (pre-existing file cost; the three new cases are ~1.5 s each).
- End to end on an isolated Gateway (built dist, mock OpenAI-compatible model, real `sessions_spawn` → `sessions_yield` parent and a child calling `plugins` `reloadAndResume` then answering):
  - Before: 4 model calls; the child answered, the parent was never woken.
  - After: the parent receives the child's completion wake (5th model call) carrying the child's resumed final answer.
  - Nested: the resumed child hands off a second time before answering; the parent still receives the completion wake, and the task keeps its original text.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), max priority P2: scoped-clean on `bc88ac2ea12b..1237f7936d29` (same tree as head `61e0b34117de`), no actionable findings.
- Exact-head CI on `61e0b34117de`: 133 check runs completed (51 success, 81 skipped, 1 neutral, 0 failing); `openclaw/ci-gate` success.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end model-call traces (isolated Gateway, mock model)</summary>

Each line is one model request: sequence, message roles sent, and the mock model's decision. The mock answers `PARENT-SAW-CHILD-FINAL` only when the parent turn's input contains the child's `CHILD-FINAL-OK` completion. `parentDone` is the harness reading the parent's history.

Base (`bc88ac2ea12b`, built dist):

```text
1 system,user,user                            sessions_spawn {task: "HANDOFF-CHILD-TASK reload the fixture plugin"}
2 system,user,user,assistant+tc,tool          sessions_yield
3 system,user,user                            plugins {action: "reloadAndResume"}      (child)
4 system,user,user,assistant+tc,tool,user×3   "CHILD-FINAL-OK"                          (child, resumed)
parentDone=false   (no 5th request: the parent is never woken)
```

This PR (built dist, same tree as head):

```text
1 system,user,user                            sessions_spawn {task: "HANDOFF-CHILD-TASK reload the fixture plugin"}
2 system,user,user,assistant+tc,tool          sessions_yield
3 system,user,user                            plugins {action: "reloadAndResume"}      (child)
4 system,user,user,assistant+tc,tool,user×3   "CHILD-FINAL-OK"                          (child, resumed)
5 parent history + completion wake            "PARENT-SAW-CHILD-FINAL"                  (parent; task_json = original task text)
parentDone=true
```

This PR, nested handoff:

```text
1 sessions_spawn  2 sessions_yield  3 plugins reloadAndResume (child)
4 plugins reloadAndResume (child, resumed, hands off again)
5 "CHILD-FINAL-OK" (child, resumed again)
6 "PARENT-SAW-CHILD-FINAL" (parent; task_json = original task text)
parentDone=true
```

</details>

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/05e4924c-ecde-4361-9785-513496e48523)

title: feat(knowledge): owners can grant group chats access to private knowledge
body:
Related: #186050, #186066, #186067, #98542

## What Problem This Solves

Group and channel conversations can only use their own conversation partition of an agent's Knowledge store, so an owner has no way to let a team chat read, or read and save, the agent's private knowledge.

## User Impact

An operator admin can grant a group or channel conversation **read** or **read and save** access to its agent's private knowledge from **Knowledge → Settings → Stores & sharing → Conversation access**. Threads and other key-denoted child sessions of that conversation inherit the grant. Read grants also get the Knowledge index and automatic recall; read-and-save grants can also approve automatic recall (`knowledge_recall`); read-only grants refuse saves with a clear error and drop save guidance from the prompt. Removing access returns the conversation to its own partition and fails in-flight work at its next authority check. Ungranted conversations behave exactly as before. There is no save-only grant: saves run against the private partition, so their results (subject matches, duplicates, record IDs) would reveal private records to a conversation that cannot read them.

No new config: grants are Knowledge state stored in its existing `registry.sqlite` (the `meta` table, no schema change), so they persist across restarts and apply immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Knowledge already resolves every call from the host-minted memory audience; a conversation audience carries its stable session key. Knowledge now looks that key (or its nearest `:`-delimited ancestor) up in owner grants and, when granted, resolves the call to the private partition; a read-only grant refuses saves. It never reads session rows. Because the grant is part of the pinned principal, a revoked or narrowed grant fails the existing live checks for work already in flight. A grant change is one compare-and-set in the registry worker and takes effect when it returns, and the settings page lists the viewed agent's group and channel conversations to pick from, marking grants that match no known conversation.

The core memory audience and owner-private paths are unchanged. Recall approval made under a grant is recorded as `approved_by: owner-private`, the existing value, so the record format does not change; history still records which agent and session wrote it.

Accepted edges, named rather than coded around:
- Write tools stay registered in read-only conversations: the feature-plugin tool contract has no per-session availability hook, so hiding them would need a core SDK change. Saves fail with an explicit read-only error, and the prompt builder drops save guidance for read-only grant keys. The pre-compaction flush plan has no session key, so in a read-only conversation its saves fail the same way.
- Granting or revoking read access changes that conversation's system prompt (index and save guidance) on its next turn; the owner's change is the invalidation.
- A revoke racing a save that already passed its last authority check can still publish that one save; unlike assignment cutovers, grant edits don't drain store lanes.
- The registry worker cannot consult the operator's live authority, so `stores_grant` rechecks caller currency and the role's agent ceiling both before the registry write and after it commits, and compensates (restores the previous value) if access ended while the write was queued. A Gateway crash between the commit and the compensation would leave that grant in place, visible and revocable in settings.

<details><summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `access.ts`: `audiencePrincipal` maps a conversation audience to the private partition for granted reads/writes, refuses writes under a read-only grant, and otherwise keeps the conversation partition. Every grant reads; only `read-write` also saves. Feature and provider principals take the live grant lookup; provider principals report `sessionPrivate` (owner audience or read grant) for automatic recall.
- `store-registry.ts`: grants in the registry snapshot and a compare-and-set `grant` operation; `stores.ts` reads them from the published snapshot.
- `store-assignments.ts`: `stores_grant` operator action (operator.admin, revision check, 500-grant cap matching the settings list; caller currency and the role's agent ceiling are checked before the registry write and again after it commits, with a compensating revert) and grants in the settings snapshot.
- `memory-provider.ts`: a provider lease loads the registry before pinning its principal, so a cold lease sees persisted grants.
- `service.ts`: `knowledge_recall` accepts conversations with a read-and-save grant.
- `memory-index-hook.ts`: index for any session whose principal reads the private partition; the opened access must still be private before a pinned index is reused or rendered, so a grant revoked mid-open never serves the old index.
- `conversation-access-view.ts` + `settings-view.ts`: Conversation access section; sessions are listed with the operator's own `sessions.list` access for labels and the picker only.
- Docs: stores-and-access caller-authority table and Conversation access section, memory-provider index/recall/flush notes, plugin overview and Control UI table.

</details>

## Evidence

**Isolated Gateway, real agent and model** (registry-backed grants; later commits reorder the recall check, cap grants at 500, recheck authority at the point of effect, remove the save-only mode, and load grants before provider leases, each covered by tests). A disposable QA Gateway built from this branch (qa-channel transport, live `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, Knowledge as memory slot, empty provider config so no host credentials or state were used) ran the full flow through real agent turns and the real `stores_grant` operator action:

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Owner DM saves "Zephyr launch plan" | lands in `private/` |
| Ungranted `#kg-room`: grep / save / index | `NOT-FOUND`; save lands in `conversations/<id>/`; `INDEX-ABSENT` |
| Grant **read**: grep / index | `CODENAME=BLUE-HERON`; `INDEX-PRESENT: Zephyr launch plan` |
| Grant **read**: save | `FAILED: Knowledge is read-only in this conversation…`; private unchanged |
| Grant **read**: thread `…:kg-room:thread:kg-thread-1` grep | `CODENAME=BLUE-HERON` (inherits) |
| Ungranted `#kg-other` grep | `NOT-FOUND` |
| Gateway restart, then read grep | `CODENAME=BLUE-HERON` (grant persisted in `registry.sqlite`) |
| Grant **read-write**: save | lands in `private/` |
| Ungranted → read → read-write: `knowledge_recall` | not found → `FAILED: …read-only…` → `APPROVED`; record gains `recall.summary` with `approved_by: owner-private` |
| Revoke: grep / index | `NOT-FOUND`; `INDEX-ABSENT` |

**Races through the real owners (no stubs).** Both timing windows ClawSweeper asked about are driven through the production `Stores`, registry worker and storage worker, and assert the final effect rather than a principal check:
- *Revocation while the index opens* (`memory-index-hook.test.ts`): a granted conversation renders and pins its private index; the grant is then revoked inside `stores.open` for the next read with the same session and cutoff. `readMemoryIndex` returns `""`: the pinned private text is not released. Removing the opened-scope guard makes this test fail.
- *Operator access ending during a queued registry write* (`conversation-grants.test.ts`): the operator's connection ends after the pre-write check, the registry commits, and `stores_grant` returns `forbidden`; the settings snapshot no longer lists the grant, and the conversation's own read through `knowledge_records` returns none of the private records. Removing the post-commit recheck makes this test fail.
- *Authorized grant succeeds* is the same flow with a current operator (`applied`, and the room reads private records), covered in the same file and in the live table above.

**Settings → Stores & sharing** (same isolated Gateway; before uses main's Knowledge UI bundle):

Before:

![Stores & sharing before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a46717d-9591-41e8-84a2-15291003d7f4)

After (one granted room, one grant whose conversation no longer exists, picker offering the remaining group):

![Stores & sharing after, with Conversation access](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f4473be-7258-4d26-8e9a-bec4e34563b0)

**Upgrade.** A consistent SQLite backup of this Team host's live Knowledge registry (2 stores, reconciled membership) loaded with this branch's registry code: it reports no grants, grant and remove round-trip, and store bindings are unchanged. The live file was only read.

**Tests.** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge` after merging current `main`: 58/58 files pass; the touched suites rerun green on the final head. New `conversation-grants.test.ts` covers per-mode reads/writes through the service, thread inheritance and the `:` key boundary, read-only prompt guidance, revocation/narrowing fencing an already-opened principal via the registry, admin/revision conflicts, grants surviving a service restart, a memory-provider lease opened first on a cold service, recall approval per grant mode including as the first call after a restart, the operator's agent ceiling lost while a grant waits, and caller authority ending after the registry write commits (each red without its fix); `memory-index-hook.test.ts` covers index injection per grant mode for a thread and the revocation-while-opening race above; `stores-config.test.ts` covers most-specific grant lookup. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, the type-suppression inventory, oxlint on changed files, and format pass.

Test-line baseline: no increase needed after merging main (main's ceiling 6302000 covers this PR's 363 lines); the earlier 6299646 → 6300797 bump approved by @jalehman is superseded. The merged tree measures 6301827 test lines against main's unchanged `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` (173 lines of slack).

Simplification: no config key, schema migration, journal or core contract; grants are one registry `meta` value and reuse the existing principal pinning and settings page.

Fresh review: local autoreview (Codex engine, P0–P2). The first revision's config-lag P1 went away with config storage. On the registry version it found one P2: `knowledge_recall` as the first call after a restart checked grants before the registry loaded; fixed with a regression. A later pass flagged that grants beyond the settings list's 500-entry bound would be saved but hidden; grants are now capped at 500. That rerun was clean. Hosted ClawSweeper then raised three authority findings on the config-backed revision: write-only results disclosing private metadata (resolved by removing the save-only mode, per @jalehman), a pinned index reusable after revocation mid-open, and the operator's agent ceiling not rechecked at the write (both fixed with regressions). Its re-review of `4faf4cb` raised two more: operator authority not rechecked once a queued registry write commits (now rechecked after commit with a compensating revert), and a cold provider lease pinning before grants loaded (now loads first); both have regressions. Its re-review of `fe95306` found no defects and asked for final-effect proof of the two races, added above. Merged current `main` to resolve a one-line import conflict and pick up the current test-line ceiling.

title: fix: avoid false queued recovery Stop test failures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent Gateway CI failures when Stop cancels a queued restart-recovery run while its recorded-input read is still waiting on real worker I/O.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This test-only repair keeps the existing cancellation and restart-recovery checks without treating fake-clock progress as completion of a real worker read. No production, permission, storage, timeout, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe the source's abort signal before starting cancellation, then wait for that signal or the cancellation operation to finish before checking it and releasing the held dispatch gate. All existing abort, no-dispatch, retirement, explicit-cancellation, and retryable-recovery assertions remain.

Contributor credit: @jalehman and @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- Original failure: [CI run 40619461616, job 122590201264](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40619461616/job/122590201264), queued restart-recovery Stop case, expected the abort signal to be true.

Pinned Bun fork, one worker, repository Vitest wrapper. Wall time: 8.28 s before / 8.33 s after.

- Main's original eight-file shard also passed both as a combined replay (455 tests) and in CI's two-config sequence (41 + 414 tests), demonstrating cold-path sensitivity rather than a consistent cancellation failure.

title: feat(ui): show paused child sessions in the handoff wait line
body:
Related: #185585 #185918

## What Problem This Solves

When a parent hands off with `sessions_yield` and a child pauses on its own `sessions_yield`, the Control UI shows that child as **Done**. If a paused child is the only one left, the waiting line disappears entirely, even though the child still owes its task.

## User Impact

- A paused child reads **Paused** in the handoff list, sorted after **Needs your input**. The header counts it, as in **Waiting on 3 sessions · 1 needs your input · 1 paused · 10m**. With a single child, the line reads **Waiting on** _name_ **· Paused**.
- A paused child keeps the waiting line open even when nothing else is running. Paused children are not counted as running, and the parent is never shown as working.
- While every remaining child is paused, the waiting line shows no elapsed time. If any child is still running, the time stays. This follows the children's execution state, not the labels shown on the rows, so a running child that has asked for your input still keeps the time.
- After the parent resumes, if the only children left are paused, the reply ends with a quiet note instead of a waiting line: **CI action pins is paused** (with the name linked), or **2 sessions are paused**. The **Resumed** list shows the paused child with its **Paused** chip.
- A paused child that has its own work still running (`hasActiveSubagentRun`) or a newer active run reads **Running**, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185918 added `subagentRunState: "paused"` to session rows, so the UI can now tell a yielded child from a finished one. title: fix: same-requester guidance queues after reconnecting
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary guidance from the same signed-in person can become a separate turn after reconnecting with different client capabilities or tool bindings.

## User Impact

User impact: same-requester guidance stays with the active turn in the same channel, account, conversation, and thread, without replacing or expanding its prepared permissions, tools, bindings, or approval destination.

Current caller access and the original execution’s live authority still apply. Questions, approvals, explicit cross-session steering, execution-setting changes, backend compatibility, and cancellation keep their existing checks. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

After validating the authenticated requester and exact conversation, ordinary continuation now retains the active execution’s snapshot instead of comparing an incoming connection’s policy projection with it. Dropping protocol-only `usage-refreshing` metadata therefore no longer moves a correction to a new turn.

This PR contains only the same-requester continuity fix, its regressions, and documentation/help updates. It does not change queue notices, TUI behavior, security presets, or collaborative-steering defaults.

## Evidence

- On original pinned base `c2243320434e1c1ae99105f4b070e1a3a4d24479`, all three authenticated `chat.send` regressions failed with `Compatible requester input was dispatched as a separate turn`: capability removal with collaboration disabled and enabled, and binding drift with collaboration enabled. All three pass with the fix, reaching native steering admission, durable transcript targeting, and subsequent model consumption without changing the incumbent owner, authority fingerprint, bindings, or approval destination.
- **174 focused tests passed again** on conflict-resolved composition `d09a06f6e362141954b9f1f5d888ff32b8647b2d` in 236.54 seconds: 20 Gateway custody cases, 39 continuation joins, 11 handoff joins, plus strict requester/question/cross-session, fallback, and prompt-prefix checks. Independent incoming-authority revocation is rejected while the original authority and outer assertion remain live; other-conversation input retains the compatibility path.
- Core production and applicable test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, docs links (16,094 links; zero broken), config examples, generated config-help checks, and normal `pnpm build` passed on the refreshed composition. Formatting and whitespace checks passed; all nine feature source/test/doc blobs remain byte-identical to the previously reviewed candidate.
- The [hosted review's P2 test-line finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186378#issuecomment-6456175921) is addressed by fixture consolidation and removal of three duplicate owner-table rows already covered at the authenticated Gateway boundary. The repair removed 92 test lines; the complete PR is **−8 test lines** against the refreshed target. The unchanged target ratchet passes; this PR raises no ceiling and weakens no primary regression or authority oracle.
- Independent source review and canonical local AutoReview (Codex-backed, medium reasoning, P0–P3) found no actionable findings on repaired tree `5fc62be924ea399f562acaf4bde711c3591cb1a1`. Those reviews are retained for the nine unchanged feature blobs. The later main integration required only canonical regeneration of the conflicting hash file, qualified separately below. Local ClawSweeper's installed checkout was dirty/ambiguous; hosted review is advisory. Broad exact-head proof is tracked in [PR checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186378/checks).
- **Remaining supplemental E2E gap:** on the earlier qualification head, nine real-Gateway/scripted-provider session-lifecycle cases passed, including requester correction, followup, Stop, cross-session delivery, subagent announcement, and compaction steering. The provenance scenario failed at `gateway.sessions-send-provenance.e2e.test.ts:661`, expecting strict cross-human refusal without selecting strict fallback; its pinned base used personal/quiet queue fallback. The people fixture then stalled, and its three cases remain unqualified after the owned run was stopped and joined (exit 143). These legacy scenarios were not rerun on the original base or after the mechanical conflict refresh. This is **not an aggregate E2E pass**; neither their expectations nor upstream defaults were edited to obtain green results.

<details>
<summary>Authority-chain proof and review follow-through</summary>

Authenticated Gateway dispatch and the real native session loop exercise the changed boundary with fixed external-I/O fixtures. Accepted reconnect inputs assert native acceptance before separate-turn dispatch, unchanged incumbent principal/fingerprint/operator authority, persisted `steerTargetRunId`, and exactly two model-stream invocations after steering is consumed. Different-requester refusal controls assert no native steering and only the original model invocation. This is production-path composition with a scripted model stream, not live external-provider qualification.

The independent caller-revocation case uses different revocation controllers and a fresh incoming authority source. After revoking only that caller, the outer assertion and incumbent authority still succeed, `joined.prepareCurrent()` rejects with `Incoming caller revoked`, no delivery occurs, and frozen-state assertions hold. Handoff cases retain no-grant-transfer and frozen-fingerprint checks.

No transport authentication, provider adapter, or final tool-I/O guard is changed by this patch. The hosted review found no concrete authorization bypass; its proof concern is addressed by these admission/effect-boundary assertions and explicit limits, not by treating the supplemental lifecycle suite as reconnect-drift proof.

title: fix: publish and plugin-reload resumes lose owner access and falsely refuse publication
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `github_publish` refuses with "GitHub publication session authority changed during snapshot" on long-lived local sessions, and the automatic resume after a publish or `plugins reloadAndResume` then loses owner-only tools (for example `automations`) until the person sends another message.

## User Impact

Publishing from a long-lived local session no longer fails at random because the Control UI re-read the session, and an authenticated owner's resumed turn keeps the owner access the requesting turn had. Non-owner, guest and system turns still never gain owner tools. No configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

**False snapshot refusal.** Local turn claims and releases only update the in-memory placement replica, while long-lived sessions also keep a durable `state=local` row. Any persisted re-read (for example the session-row projection) replaced the replica's `updatedAtMs` with the row's old value. Publication's snapshot guard compares `updatedAtMs` to detect a turn that starts and ends during the snapshot, so a plain re-read looked like an authority change. The local-turn overlay now keeps the newer in-memory stamp. A real turn during the snapshot is still refused (existing test unchanged).

**Resumed owner authority.** The shared tool handoff already captures and revalidates the requester's live operator source for the resumed turn, but bound command-owner authority only when that source was the Gateway owner profile. Owners admitted through other profiles (for example Control UI admins) resumed ownerless. The resumed turn now carries the yielding turn's own owner decision, recorded with the captured source on the event target, so it never exceeds what the requester had when it called the tool.

Security tradeoff considered: this grants nothing new. Owner binding requires both the yielding turn's owner decision and a live captured operator source; revocation, cancellation, session replacement and scope limits still end or bound the resumed turn; coalesced event batches must agree on the flag; and the event stays `internal_system` with `CommandAuthorized = false`. The residual risk is that tool-result text (for example a remote error message) is read by an owner-capable turn, which is the same exposure the requesting owner turn already had when it read tool output.

## Evidence

- **Production reproduction (Oct 27):** a Team session's handoff publish failed with the exact error; the stored placement row was last updated Oct 19 while the released local claim stamped the replica at release time. A repro on the deployed commit showed the replica's `updatedAtMs` dropping from the release time to the stored value during one `readProjection` re-read, then the publish throwing.
- **New regression** `publishes when a durable local placement is only re-read during snapshot capture`: fails without the overlay fix ("promise rejected … session authority changed …"), passes with it. The existing "local turn that starts and finishes during snapshot capture" refusal still passes.
- **New `operator-owner` reload case** (authenticated admin, not the Gateway owner profile): fails on the previous rule ("continuation settled before the owner-only tool was ready"), passes now. `system` (owner flag with no operator source) and `non-owner` still cannot reach the owner-only tool; revoked/cancelled/replaced still stop execution. The guest PR-preparation handoff asserts its resumed target carries no owner continuation.
- Focused: `plugins-reload-handoff`, `github-publish-tool.handoff`, `github-publication-boundaries`, `session-event-context`, `session-event-handoff`, `placement-store`, `placement-turn-authority` pass (122 tests). Real-Gateway E2E `gateway-plugin-reload-owner.e2e.test.ts` passes (owner-private read and `plugins.inspect` after actual plugin replacement).
- `pnpm check:changed` passes (types, lint, format, ratchets) with the dead-export scan skipped: that scan reports two pre-existing unused exports on `main` (`extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-catalog.ts: runPrompt`, `ui/src/pages/activity/activity-page.test-support.ts: settleActivity`), not touched here. Test-line ratchet: within ceiling, zero slack.
- Test cost: the new boundary case runs ~0.5 s and the new reload case ~1.5 s; `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "snapshot capture"` takes ~45 s wall including worker preparation, and the three changed test files together ~99 s wall. No new timers, sleeps or Gateway boots.
- Independent AutoReview (P0–P2): scoped-clean, no findings; it noted it could not independently inspect unchanged revocation and other `updatedAtMs` consumers, which were checked by hand (drain/reclaim CAS reads only apply to non-local states, where the overlay does not run).

title: fix(ui): reaction picker opens above scrolled messages in WebKit

Closes #184937

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the reaction picker opens far above its message in supported WebKit when a long conversation has scrolled to a nonzero virtualized row offset.

## User Impact

Reaction choices stay beside the clicked message instead of appearing over earlier messages or outside the viewport. No settings, data, or API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Position the existing absolute row window with `top` instead of a transform. WebKit 26.4 omits the ancestor transform when resolving the native popover's CSS anchor. title: fix(macos): prevent duplicate voice sends and false sent feedback
body:
Related: #127557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: manual Send and an already-queued auto-send can submit one voice transcript twice, and an RPC rejection can appear successfully sent.

## User Impact

One coordinator-owned attempt submits each active transcript. Pending sends show progress; only Gateway acceptance produces sent feedback. Rejection preserves editable text for explicit retry.

**Ready for maintainer review.** The conflict repair and Anmol's native compile fixes are published at d6c006bed106d1cb0c58be150d9d902e8f95b881, refreshed onto main dad7cbe17463dd9040f723d69f2826cf8e931fdf. GitHub reports the branch mergeable (no source conflicts). The earlier publication refusal came from a stale upstream Android release workflow in the older prepared base; the supported base refresh incorporated live main's definition. No permission change or guard bypass was needed. Exact-head focused native gates and real rejection/retry proof are now supplied by Anmol below. Ready status was requested by Anmol; no merge has been requested or performed. Skipped native CI jobs are not counted as passing.

There are no authored config, schema, durability, public protocol, dependency, or permission changes. This is not a durable outbox or exactly-once delivery guarantee; cancellation cannot retract an already-submitted RPC.

Contributor credit: @anmol0b requested this fix and supplied native verification, resolution choices, and follow-up compile fixes.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @anmol0b](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f10d7d72-7d35-44c9-858b-62fbb32bf32f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5eee3800-f321-48db-9daf-2f35ae11bae2)

## Why This Change Was Made

The coordinator claims a token before route lookup, retains one task, consumes the result, and retires work at replacement or dismissal start. Identical full payload and resolved route reuse the invocation key; edits or route changes get a fresh key. Queued auto callbacks cannot retry failures. The unowned coordinator forward and unconditional sent timer are removed.

Wake cleanup dismisses only its capture token, preserving pending PTT sends during ordinary lease release. Manual send, immediate/delayed auto-send, and PTT share the owner; the no-overlay wake fallback plays its chime only after acceptance.

The published repair preserves main's removed trace logging, source-free session API, context-free token/chime APIs, single state-bound action owner, canonical routeEntries lookup, and event-based lifecycle waits. It applies Anmol's fixes for mutually inferred lazy fixture types, the routeEntries fixture argument, and the long Forward typealias.

Risk is bounded to native voice submission and overlay lifecycle, with no stored-state migration. Exact-head focused native validation is documented below; no broad native CI pass is claimed. The published delta remains the same 16 task files relative to the refreshed main base.

## Evidence

### Native proof supplied by Anmol — exact published head

[Published-head native gates and live rejection/retry proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186271#issuecomment-6464391677), supplied by @anmol0b for d6c006bed106d1cb0c58be150d9d902e8f95b881 **as-is, with no local changes**, on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Xcode 27.1 / Swift 6.4:

- All 47 tests in the six focused voice suites passed in 0.307s; the suites then passed 10/10 repetitions.
- SwiftFormat 0.63.1: 0/33 files require formatting, exit 0. SwiftLint 0.65.1 reports no violations in this PR's files; the reported whole-run finding remains the preexisting, untouched DashboardManager.swift file-length error (1505 > 1500). This is not labeled an all-green global lint run.
- Localization verification passed on this exact head: entries=4545 changed=false, exit 0.
- The author audited the focused suites' injected Gateway/microphone/defaults/Keychain boundaries, then ran them under sandbox-exec with private HOME/state and restrictions on operator state, preferences, and the live Gateway port. These are author-provided native results, not execution performed by the Linux implementation agent.

![Native gates on the exact published head d6c006b](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1f58385-4869-4b05-801e-fc405af2dea9)

**Live RPC rejection → visible retry UI → explicit retry accepted, on the same published head:** the packaged app used its own profile and an isolated Gateway at 127.0.0.1:19271 with separate state/config. The test Gateway was suspended while the app connection stayed open, producing a real UNAVAILABLE admission response rather than a transport disconnect.

1. A real PTT send was rejected at 13:54:11.630 (242ms). The overlay retained the transcript and Send button, displayed “Send failed. Click Send to retry.”, and neither showed sent feedback nor dismissed.
2. Admission reopened when the suspension lease expired at 13:54:35.449. No automatic agent request occurred before the explicit click.
3. Clicking Send produced one retry request at 13:54:41.667, accepted at 13:54:41.746 (80ms). The overlay progressed through retry/sent feedback and closed. Captures show the retained failure state, the retry, and the dismissed overlay.
4. The same app connection was used throughout: exactly one rejected request followed by one accepted explicit retry, without duplicate or automatic sends.

![Real rejection, retained retry UI, explicit retry and accepted dismissal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d8b653c-a9c9-4496-871e-47865a302178)

The later agent-run 401 at 13:54:52 reflects the isolated Gateway's missing model credentials after submission acceptance; it does not claim successful model execution or external delivery. The earlier [baseline red/green probe and outage proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186271#issuecomment-6460923071) remain supporting history: an outage keeps transport retry pending, whereas an RPC error response surfaces manual retry UI. title: feat(knowledge): agents can no longer grow pages past a read-sized budget, and can extract sections instead
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge page bodies grow without limit when agents append to a page instead of integrating or splitting it. In the Team vault the OpenClaw project page reached 135,706 characters (about 95k in State across 37 subsections), more than eleven default `knowledge_record` reads, even though the knowledge-capture skill already asks agents not to do this.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can no longer grow a page past its body budget: 12,000 characters for hub pages (one default record read) and 24,000 for other pages. Such a write saves nothing and returns a receipt with `state: "rejected"` that names the page's size, budget, hub degree, largest sections and connected pages the content could move to. Edits that keep a body the same size or smaller always succeed, including on pages that are already over budget, so existing large pages need no migration and can only shrink. Facts can always be saved as claims; claims are never limited.

A new `knowledge_extract_section` tool moves one heading section to a new or connected page in one revision-fenced publication.

New optional config: `plugins.entries.knowledge.config.pageBudgets.hubPercentile` (default 90), which josh asked to be configurable. This raises the plugin config-surface count from 4,887 to 4,889 (`pageBudgets` and `pageBudgets.hubPercentile`); `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` is updated for that.

This PR does not change the test-line ceiling: main has since raised it to 6,300,000, and the merged tree is under it (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

Every page-body write already reaches `StoragePublication.accept` as a prepared record plus its previous revision, so the budget is enforced there once, against the same vault snapshot the publication is fenced on. That one check covers `knowledge_save_page` creates and edits, `knowledge_edit_body`, `knowledge_publish_batch` page items (and the ingest, scribe and memory-flush flows that use them), `knowledge_merge` with a combined `body`, and the destination of `knowledge_extract_section`. The rule is: reject when the body would be larger than before and larger than its budget. Corrections cannot replace pages (claims and relationships only), and withdraw, unmerge, annotate, recall, evidence reconciliation and `knowledge_supersede` never change a body. Markdown edited directly on disk is observed rather than gated; that is the one deliberate exception.

<details><summary>Budget, hub classification and extraction details</summary>

- **Budgets** derive from `TEXT_PAGE_DEFAULT_CHARS` (12,000): hubs get one read, other pages two (24,000). Sizes are body UTF-16 code units, as record windows count them.
- **Hub signal**: a page's degree is the number of distinct current pages linked to or from it by wikilinks or Markdown links. Typed relationships and claims do not count. A page is a hub when its percentile (the share of current pages in the partition with a lower degree) is at or above `hubPercentile` (default 90), the partition has at least 20 current pages, and the degree is at least 10. The top decile keeps hubs to a small set of routing pages. Below 20 pages one page spans five or more percentile points, and the degree floor keeps small or sparsely linked vaults from naming hubs.
- **Rejections** are not journaled (no receipt or draft is stored, and replaying the request ID re-evaluates it). `id`/`path`/`revision`/`hash` describe the unchanged target (empty for a create). `budget.pages[]` has current and attempted sizes, the budget, hub status (`degree`, `percentile`, `hubPercentile`, `minPages`, `minDegree`), the six largest heading sections with offsets and subsection counts, and up to three connected pages per section that the section links to or names, with their remaining headroom. The message points to extraction and `knowledge_remember`, and says not to truncate.
- **Extraction** takes source fences, the heading's `sectionStart`, a destination (fences of an existing page connected to the source by a link either way or a typed relationship, or `{title, type}` for a new page), a one-line summary and a reason. The section moves verbatim. Relative Markdown links are rewritten for the destination directory, and any other link that would resolve differently rejects the request. Source evidence whose quote, path or filename appears in the section is copied, and the source keeps all its evidence. The source keeps the heading line plus the summary and a `[[id|title]]` link. Claims the section links to that name the source as an entity get the destination as first entity, and keep the source only when the claim names it. The destination, the shrunk source and the relinked claims are validated together in a preview scan, and the destination's link targets and evidence are verified, before one publication is accepted, so a failure changes no file. The receipt has `operation: "extract"` and history keeps the old revisions. The destination's own budget applies.
- Bundled skills (shared `publish.md`/`publication.md` synced into each skill, plus knowledge-capture, knowledge-claim-consolidation step 5, knowledge-entities and knowledge-ingest) and the Knowledge docs describe the budget and the extract tool. The docs tool count is 38: main's 37 registered tools (including `knowledge_supersede`) plus `knowledge_extract_section`.

</details>

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge` on the tree merged with main at `3bcca4f`: 56 of 57 files passed. The exception, `live-state.test.ts`, fails locally on this shared host because the user's inotify instance limit is exhausted (`fs.watch` returns `EMFILE` even in a fresh process). The file is unchanged by this PR, and PR CI runs it.
- New `page-budget.test.ts` (pure contracts): hub percentile with the vault-size and degree floors and backlink degree; hub budget, nested sections outside code fences, connected candidates a section names; same-size rewrites and claims are never budgeted.
- New `page-budget-writes.test.ts` (isolated test vaults through the tool handlers and storage worker):
  - rejections on `edit_body`, `save_page` edit and create, `publish_batch` and `merge`, with the full payload checked on one, no file change and no stored receipt;
  - `knowledge_remember` and `knowledge_create_claim` still publish against an oversized page;
  - same-size and shrinking edits pass on an oversized page, and extraction shrinks it further (the ratchet);
  - extraction round trip: verbatim move, relative link rewrite, summary link, carried evidence, claim entities moved or kept, history, identical replay;
  - unconnected destination, non-heading offset, stale fence and an over-budget destination all leave the source byte-identical.
- Updated existing tests that grew pages past 24,000 characters (`body-edit.test.ts` large-page edits now replace at the same size; `publication.test.ts` fixture body 28,672 → 23,800 characters) and the policy default in `stores-config.test.ts`.
- **Test-line ceiling.** Main at `3bcca4f` raised its own ceiling to 6,300,000 and totals 6,296,883 lines (3,117 of slack). This PR adds a net 338 test lines, so the merged tree totals 6,297,221, still 2,779 under main's ceiling, and this PR leaves `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` at main's value. The 338 lines are the two new budget test files above (332 lines) plus small edits to three existing tests. They prove the six budget and extraction rules end to end through the storage worker, which no cheaper layer covers. I trimmed them from 474 lines by dropping assertions on static constants and merging overlapping cases.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`, `pnpm config:docs:check` and skill reference sync `--check` on the `3bcca4f` merge; earlier on this branch also `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint on `extensions/knowledge/src`, `test/scripts/type-suppression-inventory.test.ts`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, docs format and markdownlint, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Local autoreview (branch mode against `origin/main`, P1 threshold): no actionable findings.

title: feat(knowledge): consolidate claims by scope and supersede snapshots by their outcome
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge claims pile up on hub pages (one team vault's project hub page has about 1,400 linked claims, 138 of them about 62 individual PRs), but the claim review only ever looked at unlinked claims. A status snapshot replaced by a claim that already exists could only be withdrawn, or "corrected", which writes a duplicate copy of the replacement.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can run one claim consolidation review over the unlinked residue, the claims on one page, or the claims about one subject since a date. The review files claims on their most specific subject page and supersedes status snapshots and replaced claims by an existing claim with the new `knowledge_supersede` tool. Superseded claims leave default reads but stay readable as history, and a supersession can be undone. The scheduled scribe is now **Knowledge Consolidation**; its scheduled runs still review only claims that name no page.

**After deploying:** the review skill is renamed from `knowledge-unlinked-claims` to `knowledge-claim-consolidation`, and the **Review unlinked claims** scribe becomes **Knowledge Consolidation** with the new id `claim-consolidation` (declaration key `knowledge:scribe:claim-consolidation`). There is no migration or alias. An existing **Review unlinked claims** scribe (the Team Gateway has one) goes stale: its automation keeps the old declaration key and a stored run message naming the old skill, and the Scribes tab no longer lists it. Remove that automation (`Knowledge scribe · Review unlinked claims`) from the Automations page, then turn on **Knowledge Consolidation** from the Scribes tab. This PR does not change saved jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Skill structure.** The review skill is renamed to `knowledge-claim-consolidation` and generalized, not split into a sibling skill. The procedure is about 95% of the skill and differs only by starting set, and the shared-reference sync copies every topic to every skill, so a sibling would have duplicated the whole procedure. There is no compatibility alias: the old name never shipped in a release. Step numbering is unchanged.
- **Scribe.** The scheduled scribe matches the skill: title and dialog title **Knowledge Consolidation**, id `claim-consolidation`, and a blurb, purpose and run step that describe the consolidation it does (filing, new pages, superseding snapshots by their outcome, page State). Its scheduled scope is not widened: runs still review only claims that name no page, and the blurb and purpose say so. Its closing counts now include superseded claims.
- **Scope selectors** (step 1): unlinked residue (`knowledge_relink` dry run, unchanged), one page (`knowledge_connections` `direction: "claims"`), or one subject with an optional date (`knowledge_timeline` `entity`/`since` plus `knowledge_grep` `kind: "claim"` for claims filed elsewhere). Existing read tools cover all three, so no new selector tool.
- **`knowledge_supersede`**: one revision-fenced publication marks 1 to 25 active claims superseded by an existing current claim. It reuses the existing superseded lifecycle: each earlier claim keeps its text, evidence, attribution and history and gets `superseded_by` and `lifecycle_change`, like a corrected original. The superseding claim is not rewritten. Validation: claims only; no self-supersession or repeated IDs; `by` must be current in the caller's scope; every earlier claim must be active and share a linked page (`entities` or source page, merge redirects followed) with `by`. Because `by` must be current and every earlier claim active, no cycle can form. `undo: true` restores claims this tool superseded by the same claim and lifts their durable supersession guards when the restore publishes. Undo rejects supersessions made by `knowledge_correct`. Default reads already exclude superseded records; historical reads and `knowledge_history` keep them.
- **Snapshot series** (step 4): a series of status snapshots about one specific item (same PR, commit or decision thread) is superseded by its outcome claim only when every snapshot and the outcome name the same item, the outcome is later and states a final state, and they share a subject page. Otherwise both stay and are reported; unattended runs never guess. "Replaced" claims are now superseded instead of withdrawn; duplicates are still withdrawn.
- **Relinking** (steps 2 and 3): when a subgroup meets the page-creation threshold, the new page becomes the primary subject (first in `entities`) and the broad page stays only on claims that say something about it.

Accepted edge cases: Recent activity does not list supersede publications, which matches merges today. Viewing the superseding claim does not list the claims it superseded; they link to it.

Coordination with #186270 (page budgets and section extraction): this PR does not touch step 5 of the skill or any budget logic. #186270 adds one bullet to step 5 of `skills/knowledge-unlinked-claims/SKILL.md`; this PR moves that file to `skills/knowledge-claim-consolidation/SKILL.md`, so whichever PR lands second must carry the bullet to the new path and check it survived. A trial merge with #186270 at `a6e323a` (before the rename) otherwise conflicts only where both PRs add lines next to each other: the `Receipt.operation` union, `Prepared` fields, the receipt block in `accept`, the `storage-host` registrations, and the tool table and count in `docs/plugins/knowledge.md`. Each conflict resolves by keeping both sides; whichever PR lands second sets the tool count to 37. #186270's `relinkClaim` applies the same subject rule during extraction (destination page first, source kept only when the claim names it), decided by name match inside one publication. The review decides by judgment and writes through `knowledge_annotate`, so there is no server helper to share; a future bulk relink tool could reuse `relinkClaim`.

## Evidence

- Supersede tests in `extensions/knowledge/src/lifecycle.test.ts`, on the lifecycle suite's isolated temp-vault fixture through the real service and storage worker: supersede, then undo, of a snapshot series, with text, evidence, attribution, reason and history kept; a stale active file cannot revive a superseded claim; rejection of self-supersession, repeats, a reverse edge (cycle), other subjects, unlinked claims, pages, stale fences, already superseded or withdrawn claims, and undo of a correction.
- Red/green: with the guard release disabled, the undo test fails (`expected 'superseded' to be 'active'`); with it, it passes.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge` after merging `main` at `eec15d7`: 54 of 55 files and 425 of 426 tests passed. The one failure, `live-state.test.ts` ("Expected watcher notification"), is a filesystem-watcher timing test this PR does not touch; it passed twice when rerun on its own (6 of 6 each time). Within the Knowledge plugin, the later merges of `main` at `b3aa84d`, `beb12fa` and `2262f3d` changed only `extensions/knowledge/package.json`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass; oxlint clean on changed files; `node extensions/knowledge/scripts/sync-skill-references.mjs --check` passes; docs format, markdownlint and `git diff --check` are clean. No earlier skill name or scribe title or id from this PR remains in the repository. `knowledge-maintenance` still appears as the id of the scheduled maintenance pass and its internal agent (`maintenance.ts`, `access.ts`), which predate this PR and are unrelated to the skill.
- **Test-line ceiling set to 6,294,048** (`config/test-lines-baseline.txt`; `main` has 6,293,776), exactly the merged tree's counted total with no slack. Justification: `main` itself is already over its own ceiling. At `2262f3d` it counts 6,293,974 test lines against a ceiling of 6,293,776, 198 over, so any PR that adds a test line fails the ratchet. This PR's net delta is +74 lines, all coverage for the new supersede operation, its undo, and the renamed scribe and skill: +86 in `lifecycle.test.ts` for the supersede tests, offset by sharing the repeated scribe and record fixtures. The supersede tests were moved into the lifecycle suite to reuse its fixture, which cut the delta from +205; going lower would mean rewriting unrelated tests or dropping supersede coverage. On the merged tree, `check-test-lines-ratchet` reports `Test lines OK: 6294048; ceiling: 6294048; slack: 0`.
- Dry run (read only, nothing written) on a real team vault: the 15 claims about one merged PR, all filed only on the project hub page. The review would create one page for the PR and relink all 15 to it, dropping the hub from claims that say nothing about the project. It would supersede five status snapshots by the merge outcome once that outcome is saved as a claim; the vault had none, so an unattended run supersedes nothing and reports the series. It keeps nine proof results and decisions as history and reports one claim as uncertain. The claim-level plan is in the implementation session.
- Gap: no live Gateway run of a model following the generalized skill end to end. The tool is proven through the real service in isolated vaults.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native macOS New Thread hanging and allocating unbounded memory when creating a conversation.

## User Impact

Native Mac users can create a thread through the sidebar or keyboard shortcut without entering recursive session creation. A missing or retired Gateway connection is rejected rather than silently retargeted. No configuration or migration is required.

title: fix(discord): voice autoJoin flaps in and out when joining keeps failing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord bot with `voice.autoJoin[].whenOccupied` flaps in and out of the voice channel about once a second when joining keeps failing (for example, the realtime provider is down or the bot lost access to the channel).

## User Impact

User impact: when an occupied auto-join fails, the bot stays out of the channel and retries after a growing wait (5 seconds, doubling up to 10 minutes) instead of rejoining on every voice-state change. Discord `Missing Access`/`Missing Permissions` failures stop auto-join for that channel with one warning that says to restore the bot's View Channel and Connect permissions, then run `/vc join` or reload the config. A successful `/vc join` or a config reload clears the wait.

## Why This Change Was Made

Occupied auto-join reconciles on every guild voice-state update, including the bot's own leave after a failed start. Only credential-like errors were suppressed, so any other failure rejoined immediately and the bot's own leave scheduled the next attempt. In the reported incident this produced 119 join/leave cycles in under three minutes, then 140+ `Missing Access` lookups, and a voice-state queue backlog of 30–45 seconds per event.

The auto-join owner in `voice-runtime.ts` now keeps one failure record per guild/channel: fatal failures (the existing credential set plus Discord access errors) stay suppressed until a successful join or manager rebuild; other failures get bounded exponential backoff. Voice-state events during the wait return early without a join attempt, and a one-shot scheduler job rechecks the room when the wait expires so an idle room still recovers. Each failure logs one warning naming the next retry; skipped events log nothing. Cancelled joins and shutdown are not counted as failures.

Not changed here: GPT-Live error redaction (separate follow-up), and plain (non-`whenOccupied`) auto-join still retries only on gateway Ready/Resumed, now subject to the same backoff.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/discord/src/voice/voice-auto-join.test.ts` use fake timers through the plugin scheduler:
  - transient realtime startup failure: the bot's own leave and another member's update do not rejoin; retry happens at exactly 5 s, then 10 s, and the third attempt connects.
  - Discord `Missing Access` on channel lookup: no further lookups across voice-state updates and an hour of time; an explicit `join` afterwards succeeds.
- Red on base `364c0d4` (runtime file reverted, tests kept): both new tests fail (`joinVoiceChannel` called 3 times instead of 1; `fetchChannel` called 3 times instead of once).
- Green with the fix: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/voice/voice-auto-join.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 10/10 passed; wall time 41 s cold (Vitest duration 38.1 s, mostly transform; tests themselves ~20 ms), 9 s warm.
- Sibling voice/autoJoin consumers: `manager.ready-listener`, `transcripts-capture`, `transcripts-readiness`, `transcripts-target`, `voice-following`, `voice-receive`, `voice-runtime.e2e`, `voice-runtime.secret-owner.e2e`, `voice-session.lifecycle`, `voice-session.promotion`, `voice-occupancy`, `monitor/provider.lifecycle` → 12 files, 217 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `tsgo -p extensions/discord/tsconfig.json` reports no errors in changed files (its only error is an existing test-support import outside that config's scope); `run-oxlint` on both changed files clean, `oxfmt --check` on all changed files clean.
- Local autoreview (helper `source-sha256:d2b2d03f…`, default Codex engine), branch mode `origin/main` `364c0d4` → `f6afb3d`, max priority P1, with `voice-runtime.ts`, `listeners.ts`, and the scheduler sources as context: scoped-clean, no findings. The reviewer did not execute tests.
- Not run: live Discord e2e against a real guild. The live Team Gateway and its config were intentionally left untouched; the incident timeline above comes from its logs.

title: improve(ui): personal sidebar sections with a two-step editor
body:
Supersedes #185632 (same branch history plus later iterations). Related: #181680, #185348

## What Problem This Solves

Personal session groups looked like shared groups, sat above Pinned under a permanent heading, and their editor only listed sessions already loaded in the sidebar, without saying whose they were.

## User Impact

Personal groups are now **Sections**. Pinned stays at the top; sections follow it among the sidebar groups, marked by a stacked-layers icon instead of a heading, with their menu on header hover. Sessions inside a section follow the sidebar's **Sort by**.

Create a section from **Filter & sort → New section** or a session's **Add to section** menu. The editor has two steps and keeps one height:

1. **Name and source.** Section name, then **Choose sessions from**: My sessions, Involving me, All sessions (including teammates'), or a project.
2. **Choose sessions.** The chosen source is shown above the list; the list comes from the Gateway for that source, search covers every accessible session (not only loaded rows), and teammates' sessions show their owner. Selected sessions outside the source stay listed first under **In this section** (editing) or **Added** (created from a session).

The header shows **Only you** next to the title and "Adding a session doesn't move it from its group." Editing opens on step 2; **Back** returns to the name and source. Sections grant no access, shared groups and **Move to group** are unchanged, guests keep browser-local sections, and the stored preference key is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Product direction (Vyctor): Sections naming, Pinned first, an icon instead of a heading, a source chosen once on step 1, owner context in the list, and a conservative, bounded dialog.

- The session list uses a plain `sessions.list` request (kept out of the sidebar's conditional row cache) with the command palette's session scope and the existing filters (`ownerId`, `involvingMe`, `projectId`, `search`); no Gateway API, permission or storage change. Projects come from the existing project catalog and the option is hidden when none are available; owner-relative sources are hidden without a signed-in profile.
- Enter in the search field filters; it never submits the editor.
- The project picker is the shared select component; dialog styles reuse the shared dialog, field, chip and button classes.
- Saving still only keeps sessions the editor resolved (loaded, fetched, or previously saved).
- The native session menu is unchanged apart from the added entry's label and icon. Dialog styles stay in the lazily loaded dialog stylesheet.

Related: #171994

## What Problem This Solves

The private MCP startup-cancellation regression has an independent one-second watchdog even though its fixture already owns both held cleanup gates and the actual acquisition join. Use the existing test lifetime instead of that separate diagnostic timer.

## User Impact

No shipped behavior changes. Private startup cancellation, shared catalog waiters, cleanup-error identity, lease release, uncertainty reporting, product deadlines, runtime configuration and dependencies are unchanged. A stalled regression is diagnosed at its owning test lifetime; the old 1,000 ms diagnosis latency and custom message are not retained guarantees.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected rows now receive the existing Vitest test signal and await the same cleanup-start promise through withinTest. This is deliberately not the work-scope signal that the test already aborts. Both original finally blocks remain byte-identical: the private-startup fixture resolves both gates, directly joins the actual pending acquisition, then drains its work owner. The catalog-resolves/disposal-fails and catalog-rejects/join-fails rows stay distinct. No fixture, controller, runner hook, grace timer or cleanup owner is added.

Omitting the actual producer's private-startup abort-listener registration makes **both rows fail at the intended test timeout**. Their original finally actions then resolve both gates, actual catalog/disposal/join work settles, the lease callback runs once, the pending acquisition rejects with the exact cleanup-error object, uncertainty remains recorded, and the direct pending join plus work drain complete before the next row starts.

title: fix(imessage): report Automation failures after Gateway updates
body:
Related: #178719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Messages Automation send failures leave the iMessage account green, with no recovery guidance, when a Gateway reply uses AppleScript text, attachment delivery, or the auto fallback.

## User Impact

Failed sends report the affected account and Messages Automation recovery steps. A successful send clears that warning; a successful read probe does not. Delivery error identity and classification are preserved.

**Limitations:** This does not preserve TCC grants across upgrades. Signed macOS upgrade testing was not available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary sends and native attachment actions now share the existing account-warning publisher. The RPC-only publication and duplicated RPC error-message augmentation were removed. Successful ordinary and native message completion clear only a matching Automation warning, not unrelated watcher errors. No options, permissions, runtime identities, or automatic resend behavior changed.

## Evidence

### User-friendly wording update — November 4

The warnings now lead with plain-language explanations and concrete steps: open Messages, approve any permission prompt, and quit/reopen the app if frozen. Permission-denied errors explain that OpenClaw needs permission to control Messages. Both retain Automation settings guidance, the current `bun` entry for app-managed Gateways, and the reminder to check delivery and queued replies before retrying. The original AppleScript diagnostic is retained at the end so successful-send warning clearing remains unchanged.

Copy-only follow-up: 8 lines added / 8 removed in `process-diagnostics.ts`; no changes to matching, sending, or retry behavior. Checked both generated messages, re-recognition of each normalized warning, unrelated-error rejection, and the error-code boundary with a focused Node check of the source function. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. The targeted lint wrapper could not start its package-boundary preparation because this older checkout expects a `typescript/fs` export absent from the available dependency installation. Full plugin and live macOS tests were not rerun for this copy-only update; the captures below remain evidence from the explicitly named earlier heads.

**Fault-injected imsg on Linux:** real shipped Gateway, real iMessage plugin, and real process spawn. The executable emits the exact imsg v0.17.0 Automation diagnostic and exits non-zero. This is not real Messages/TCC testing. RED and GREEN used fresh isolated HOME/state/config paths, separate free ports, and identical stand-in/media bytes. The live Gateway was not touched.

Server and client entry points (targets, paths, ports, and hosts redacted):

```sh
pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> gateway run --bind loopback --port <isolated-port>
pnpm --silent openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> gateway call send --port <isolated-port> --expect-url <isolated-url> --params '{"channel":"imessage","accountId":"proof","to":"chat_guid:[redacted]","message":"synthetic Automation proof","idempotencyKey":"[case-key]"}' --timeout 20000 --json
# Attachment case: message="", mediaUrl="<isolated-workspace>/proof.pdf"; sendTransport=applescript.
pnpm --silent openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> gateway call channels.status --port <isolated-port> --expect-url <isolated-url> --params '{"probe":true,"timeoutMs":2000}' --timeout 20000 --json
```

The following are recorded account-status projections from CLI JSON; `probeOk` is the returned probe's `ok` field. Long recovery text is explicitly truncated after the System Settings destination. Full captured responses remain in the proof folders.

Captured recovery guidance (identical on both GREEN paths):

```text
Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1712. Messages timed out; check for an unresponsive Messages.app or a hidden permission prompt. On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation and allow Messages for the process running imsg. For an app-managed background Gateway, check the current Gateway runtime (bun), not Terminal or the previous node/bun runtime. An app update can change this permission identity. After granting access, verify delivery and queued replies before retrying from the Gateway.
```

### RED — f9c2f84b693bcb36759b2bfe89a9bd767bb0cb31

The baseline preserves the already-working RPC warning; its attachment failure reproduces the green/no-warning defect.

### GREEN — 3d0c4db063e0201fa9c4634faae2ae45017d74ad

### Successful-send control

- `pnpm test:extension imessage --maxWorkers=1` — **823 passed in 59 files**, 305.52 s Vitest wall time. The final assertion/cleanup refinements were then covered by the 38-test send-suite rerun above.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .openclaw/tmp/tsconfig.imessage.json --incremental` — passed. The scoped config extends `extensions/tsconfig.json` and includes all iMessage production/test/support files and canonical ambient declarations.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json <7 changed TypeScript files>` and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check <same files>` — passed.
- `node scripts/lib/plugin-npm-runtime-build.mjs extensions/imessage` — **13 runtime entries built**, passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base a0a998b8 --no-merge-base` — passed: 6,285,650 test lines, ceiling 6,285,000, **net delta 0**. Existing ceiling pressure is 650 lines; this PR no longer adds to it. No ceiling/baseline changes.
- `git diff --check a0a998b8f4748489e041e14f95917b1f46e94b64 HEAD` — passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the whole PR diff — **no findings**. The reviewer inspected source and evidence; it did not independently execute the tests.
- Earlier `d30362d` CI failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: 6,286,277 / ceiling 6,285,587, including 570 lines of base pressure plus this PR's +120. The consolidation above repairs the PR growth instead of raising the ceiling. Final-head CI results are separate from these local gates.

Production delta **+107/-7**; test delta **+53/-53**; documentation **+11/-0**, against `a0a998b8`. The shared account-warning publisher replaces RPC-only publication and duplicate RPC message decoration. Added mock-Gateway scaffolding was removed in favor of shipped-Gateway proof; the existing real-CLI rejection regression now covers both transports. Original boundary assertions remain or are strengthened to exactly-once-with-arguments assertions.

Proof captures: `.openclaw/tmp/p178719/red/` and `.openclaw/tmp/p178719/green-final/`; raw CLI responses are in each `capture/`, with `observations.json`, `binding.json`, and cleanup receipts. Config/state credentials are not published.

title: fix: replies stall after restart with paused child tasks
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: messages receive an acknowledgment but no answer after a Gateway restart with paused child tasks.

## User Impact

User impact: new messages can run while child tasks wait for continuation. The paused tasks remain resumable and can deliver their eventual results. This changes restart-time reconstruction only; it does not clear a running Gateway's existing queue. No migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore treated a yielded child's pending future result as a ready completion and reserved a reply-queue slot. Live delivery correctly left the child paused, so that empty slot never became runnable and blocked later messages. Skip ordinary completion reservations for yielded children, including after awaited requester preparation. Explicit pause-notice wakes keep their separate path.

Contributor credit: @VACInc reported the missing replies and requested the investigation and fix.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0abbf7f4-7c52-4f94-971f-592e6339bb2a)

## Evidence

- Read-only live inspection found two restored, unbound completion reservations ahead of incoming Discord messages, with no active turn. Their persisted child records were paused with no result; ingress repeatedly hit its five-minute admission timeout.
- The added real requester-store/controller regression times out before the fix. With the fix it admits the parent, preserves the paused child, then delivers that child's later completion (463 ms).
- Both focused suites pass: **47 tests** across controller input and requester-settle dispatch, including existing pause-notice delivery coverage.

title: improve(memory): reuse unchanged chunks after ordinary edits
body:
Related: #168777

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary memory-file edits re-embed unchanged chunks when their cache entries are missing, although compatible vectors are already present in the published index.

## User Impact

Indexing can reuse unchanged chunks from the same file and source, including when line numbers shift or the embedding cache and optional vector search are disabled. Existing cache rows and retry reuse are preserved; no schema changes or operator action are required.

This is the recommended **scoped 1a stage**, not the complete storage proposal. Retiring new matching cache duplicates (1b) and existing duplicates (step 2) still require the storage owner's retention/rollback decision. This PR deletes no valid cache copies, claims no database-size savings, and does not close #168777.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing bounded source/path published-vector lookup from full rebuilds to ordinary indexing. Preserve cache precedence and identity, input-format, dimension and publication-snapshot checks; accept a matching permitted identity and reject byte-conflicting published vectors in the requested scope. Record canonical embedding dimensions independently of optional vector-search availability.

Global cross-file lookup and its additional index are intentionally out of scope. Existing cache-based cross-file reuse remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression red on base `3a3246e7c1389c03e933e1f15805306945b1df1c`: a head edit submitted 18 embedding inputs despite 17 unchanged published hashes. With the fix it submits one.
- Actual `pnpm openclaw memory` indexing/edit/search/append/full-rebuild flow, bundled Ollama HTTP adapter and SQLite workers, with synthetic notes and deterministic loopback embedding responses: both cache/vector enabled and both disabled produced initial **18**, ordinary edit **1**, **17** shifted unchanged vectors retained byte-exact, append **6**, full rebuild **0**; search returned the edited file. This is shipped-path fixture proof, not live-model quality or billing evidence.
- Seven focused suites: **115 tests passed** (86.55 s wrapper wall). Final touched SQLite suites: **25 passed** (49.92 s including 31 s cold worker preparation; manager test bodies approximately 11 s and read tests approximately 0.1 s). Covers identity/dimensions, ambiguity, disabled-cache independence, publication rollback/retry, cap/prune and FTS-only behavior. Hosted PostgreSQL execution timings are recorded below.
- Source-mapped extension production/test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, original-candidate pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. The refreshed source passed all **54 touched tests** and both typecheck lanes. [Current-head full CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40522759020/job/122267430514), including exact-scope checks and baseline ratchets; its failure report contains no failed or timed-out jobs.
- **All three current-head PostgreSQL conformance shards passed.** [Shard 1 execution log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40522759020/job/122254999708) explicitly shows the existing rebuild/capacity case and both new ordinary-edit cases passing, not skipped: cache/vector enabled **393 ms**, disabled **211 ms** (existing full-rebuild case 12,286 ms). Capacity one forces cache misses, so the edit cases prove published-vector reuse against real PostgreSQL. [Shard 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40522759020/job/122254999737) and [shard 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40522759020/job/122254999901) also passed. These jobs and the CI gate identify head `7689b902392c55637ca7b488aeb09d098cee0b28`. No production/20k+ PostgreSQL performance benchmark was run.
- Fresh independent Auto Review against the pinned base and exact staged candidate, including unchanged database/publication context: **P0–P2 scoped-clean, no findings**. This is not a hosted rating or maintainer approval.

### Review follow-up and coverage budget

- Reproduced the introduced generic-provider transport-fixture failure, then replaced its unsupported native in-memory placeholder with one real private worker-owned read database. Removed the superseded native handles and cleanup wrappers; all **29 existing real-HTTP tests pass** (12.36 s wrapper wall), preserving Qianfan batching, adaptive splitting, permanent-error and dimension-rejection assertions. Production reuse behavior is unchanged by this repair.
- Resolved the test-line finding while preserving every distinct assertion: the worker-owned transport fixture removes 35 obsolete lines, leaving 188 net scoped test lines. An actual merge conflict then required integrating main `43dc38e6c1370e7682156b8a84ed6fc1abfaa0b7`. Its incoming **6,285,000** ceiling is retained unchanged; the refreshed candidate measures **6,283,120** lines (1,880 slack). This PR no longer changes the budget relative to main and does not weaken tests. After integration, all **54 touched SQLite/real-HTTP tests passed**, and extension production/test types passed.

<details>

The task-owned Node harness ran actual `pnpm openclaw memory index --agent main --force`, ordinary `memory index --agent main`, `memory search --agent main --query "Beta newly inserted header" --json`, append indexing, and a final forced rebuild. The bundled Ollama HTTP adapter called a deterministic local embedding server. Counters below are captured HTTP embedding inputs, not estimates. Assertions also checked 17 shifted unchanged vectors byte-for-byte and verified search returned the edited file.
