title: fix: stop closed macOS dashboards reconnecting after native auth refusal
body:
Related: #168743

## What Problem This Solves

Closing or replacing a natively authenticated macOS Dashboard can leave its committed page reconnecting after that window can no longer obtain native authorization, producing repeated pre-connect warnings.

## User Impact

Closing or replacing a native Dashboard now retires and unloads its document. A retained window reopens its trusted route using the same WebView storage; hiding or minimizing preserves its live document. Exact repeated native-refusal warnings retain the first diagnostic and periodic suppressed counts rather than one warning per attempt.

Real-WKWebView and Gateway evidence is available, with the revision and host limits below. The reporter subsequently supplied an exact-`4abd9e5` packaged-app-to-real-Gateway close/drop/reopen comparison on November 6, linked under Evidence. Historical negative results remain disclosed; no full native-suite green or native execution of a later integration is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stopping WebKit navigation does not unload a committed page. The existing controller now retires that document and its identity at actual native close/replacement, retains its trusted reopen route, and keeps the inert retirement page non-deliverable. Browser identity, origin/account storage boundaries and transient native recovery remain intact; there is no refusal cap or retry-policy change.

The Gateway extends its existing bounded authentication-log limiter only for pre-connect code 4008 and the exact raw reason native authorization unavailable. Code 1006, near-matches and credential-mismatch warnings keep their previous behavior.

The supplied native run also exposed an obsolete notification-test oracle: after closing, it expected the outgoing page to remain at /. The follow-up test repair now requires about:blank while closed, explicitly reopens, then waits for the retained / route instead of the stale notification's completion route. Window identity, closed state and non-close navigation checks are preserved.

## Evidence

### Current integration qualification

The signed, ancestry-preserving integration is `6ca718a2884793bce8863d49eb7f916ab85b2cef` (tree `6fb3ad3c0b439843e9f009f46fde6717c2b11d9b`), integrating protected main `c00f78c93167086887753d75345d4803d4880ee2`. The sole conflict preserves both the native titlebar inset state and the retired-document route. All 12 files retain byte-for-byte identical ordered additions/removals to the original reviewed PR delta; a fresh independent integration review found no P0–P2 findings. Existing runtime proof remains labeled with its original executing revision.

[Exact published-head CI, run 43296884294](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43296884294), attempt 1, completed successfully for `6ca718a2884793bce8863d49eb7f916ab85b2cef`: 59 jobs, no pending or failed jobs. Separate dependency, security-sensitive-review and combined CI commit statuses were also observed successful. This is new-head CI, not a relabeling of the original-head runs below; no new native full-suite execution is claimed.

### Packaged-app proof received November 6

[The reporter's exact-head comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185963#issuecomment-6678794210) used a packaged app identifying `4abd9e5395cd30293cf5ffc625b97a114c6a2ec4` and a real Gateway. The fixed app released its page socket on close, made zero reconnect attempts during the 10.1-minute observation window (and throughout 18.6 minutes closed), then connected a fresh page 0.6 seconds after reopening. The main control retained its socket and made 16 native-refusal attempts after the forced tunnel drop. This is contributor-reported evidence from one run per build on the same Mac/Gateway, with the forced-drop and attribution limits stated in that comment; it is not an independent rerun or proof for a later integration.

The earlier receipts and their negative results are retained separately below.

- The notification replay test is repaired without removing ownership checks. Supplied stock-host focused runs pass **9/9 only with that dirty test patch**; they are not executions of the new commit.
- Real WKWebView evidence denies stale credentials and permits a fresh document after close, replacement and immediate reopen. A selective base overlay actually fails the two immediate-reopen assertions.
- New supplied focused TypeScript proof is **65/65**, separate from the historical **67/5-file** run. The synthetic real-Gateway trace emits **2 native + 3 control** warnings versus **12 + 3** on the selective base overlay; it does not prove app reconnect cessation.
- **Lint is not green:** normal scope has one source-verified inherited file-length violation; a different explicit touched-test scope reports 60 serious diagnostics. Restricted sibling sweeps, crashes, timeouts and omissions are disclosed below—not counted passing.
- **Qualification limits:** the packaged-app proof above addresses the previously missing close/reconnect correlation at `4abd9e5`. Published-head CI and any later integration qualification remain separate. The historical hosted review rated overall readiness 3/6; ratings are advisory. No full native-suite green or native execution of a later integration is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Audited receipts, sanitized excerpts, source equivalence and all negative results</summary>

### Revision, source equivalence and hosts

The [reporter's public evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185963#issuecomment-6552265574) and independently audited supplied bundle concern head f56bd97a670203f386ff71e313f25e50d6562afc and admitted base 3a3246e7c1389c03e933e1f15805306945b1df1c. The audit inspected artifacts; it did not rerun supplied scripts or tests. All 70 declared bundle checksums matched; ZIP SHA-256: 3c684b5ed17f6304d842331974a271b140bfb86ee3a16b288d861b61d99b6bb2.

The [new repair commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4abd9e5395cd30293cf5ffc625b97a114c6a2ec4) changes only DashboardNotificationWindowTests.swift (+4/−1) from that recorded head. Its complete resulting file is byte-identical to the published f56 file plus the audited patch (patch SHA-256 3151270b79163551c9f5082ba0dc15a161bb855139191716f680dd6682235d64; resulting Git blob 7ab8659bf05356f99fddfef4e7a05b4db7236e31). All eleven earlier changed source files still match f56. This establishes tracked-source equivalence, not a new-commit test execution or complete generated/untracked/build-input attestation.

- Host A is reported as stock Xcode 27.1/Swift 6.4 on macOS 27.2 arm64 with a GUI. Library/platform/AppKit records partly corroborate that metadata; the bundle does not contain a complete pinned checkout/toolchain attestation.
- Host B directly records swift.org 6.3.3/SDK26.5 without GUI, substitute SwiftUI/Preview macro plugins, and two omitted XCTest files (SimpleTaskSupportTests.swift and MacNodeLocationServiceTests.swift). Its results are adapted, restricted coverage—not a stock/full native build. Supplied Studio scripts omit untracked files from dirty-state output.
- Head-plus-patch passes still record the old f56 HEAD and a modified test. Base-overlay runs retain the head checkout/tests and restore selected production files, not a clean full-base checkout. Exact overlaid bytes cannot be independently reconstructed from the bundle. No supplied scripts or macro stubs were executed during this audit/update.

### Real WKWebView outcomes — including the original red test

Unpatched f56 is not native-green: “older manager command replay does not cancel a newer notification click” fails refreshed-close and new-window-close, receiving an empty path where its old oracle expected /. The supplied base overlay and head-plus-patch each pass its four cases on both hosts. The source owner inspected the real retirement implementation and wait helper before applying the audited correction above.

| Supplied selection | Audited result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| A, recorded clean-state f56, focused 9 tests / 3 suites | 8 test functions pass; older-manager fails with 2 issues; EXIT=1. The WK ownership matrix (10 cases), forbidden frame/browser-identity cases (3), retained close/reopen (2), replacement unload, device-settings (9 cases) and 3 ControlUIDocument tests pass. |
| A, f56 plus dirty test patch, same selection | 9 tests / 3 suites pass in 31.181 seconds; EXIT=0. Separate older-manager rerun passes 4 cases. Not an exact-new-commit rerun. |
| B, adapted focused selections | Auth bridge 4 tests pass, including 3 + 10 + 2 parameter cases; device settings 1 test / 9 cases and isolated conversation factory pass. Socket-retirement and saved-profile selections crash with signal 5 on both head and base overlay; those are not passes. |
| B, adapted restricted sibling sweep | 252 test-pass records; 253 tests / 46 suites fail with 2 issues, EXIT=1. The completed sweep's failing test is older-manager. Other attempts abort or remain incomplete. No full-suite green. |

The important completed negative control uses the real WK reply boundary: A's selective native base overlay reaches immediate-reopen, delivers a grant to the retired document and fails two assertions. The recorded head denies that stale recipient and completes a fresh current recipient after close, replacement and immediate reopen. It also accepts current/current-password/current-device-only and rejects document/provider/socket/browser-identity stale replies.

Sanitized excerpts below are supplied-log evidence, not independent reruns. Anchors name bundle-relative files; they are not public download URLs. Credential payloads, local paths and endpoint/host values are omitted.

Related: #171994

## What Problem This Solves

The concurrency utility tests layer a fixed one-second diagnostic race over waits whose lifetime and cleanup already belong to the test.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Scheduling, result order, failure isolation, caller context, configuration and dependencies are unchanged. A stalled readiness wait now fails at the owning test timeout rather than a separate one-second diagnostic; this does not preserve a one-second latency guarantee.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing test signal for the five readiness/completion waits and remove their local timer wrapper. Keep every unconditional fixture release, direct runner join and separately joined started task unchanged. In particular, an expected early aggregate rejection is not treated as completion of continue-mode work.

## Evidence

- All six cases pass before and after the change and after restoring the producer controls. Native TypeScript AST comparison preserves all four declarations, 15 expectation calls, every finally block and the complete stop-mode test; collected names, order and statuses match. The allocation test still exercises 32 and 4,096 tasks. The three parameterized cases receive the same boolean rows through Vitest's context-bearing table API; their internal each diagnostic flag changes.

Related: #185585

## What Problem This Solves

The "re-renders resumed lists" test added in #185585 only asserted that the roster cache key changes when a listed child's name or attention changes. It never rendered anything, so it could pass while a settled resumed handoff row kept showing a stale name or status (ClawSweeper review finding on #185585).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Test-only follow-up; no production code changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaces the key-only unit test in `chat-subagent-wait.test.ts` with a test in `chat-pane-run-activity.test.ts` that drives the real chat pane and transcript renderer. It renders a settled parent transcript with a resumed `sessions_yield` handoff, then redraws with the same transcript and only the child roster changed: first a name-only update, then an attention-only update. Each step asserts the rendered Resumed list text (`Docs Done` → `Docs and changelog Done` → `Docs and changelog Needs your input`).

The new test is kept compact (file-level transcript DOM hooks, only the fixture fields the resumed list reads), and the added lines are offset by removing redundant UI tests below. Current `origin/main` is merged in.

title: feat(gateway): report yielded subagent children as paused on session rows
body:
Related: #185585

## What Problem This Solves

A child subagent that called `sessions_yield` and is waiting for a continuation is listed as finished: its session row reads `status: "done"` with `subagentRunState: "historical"`, so a parent's list of waited-on children cannot tell a paused child from a completed one.

## User Impact

User impact: Control UI and other Gateway clients can show a yielded child as paused instead of done. Existing clients see no change: the row's `status` keeps the value they already render, and no client UI changes in this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session rows already carry an optional `subagentRunState` (`active`, `interrupted`, `historical`) describing the child's current subagent-registry run. This adds a fourth value, `paused`, for a yielded run that can still be continued. It is derived from the registry's stored `pauseReason: "sessions_yield"`; nothing new is stored. The check that already chose the `/subagents` "waiting for external continuation" label moves into `isSubagentRunPausedForContinuation`, so the row and `/subagents` share one predicate (kills, failures and timeouts are excluded).

- Precedence: `active` (live or queued) wins over `paused`, so a follow-up turn running in the child still reads as active.
- Transitions: a continuation replaces the paused run (row becomes active); completion, settlement and kill clear the pause; the existing registry publication refreshes the row through `sessions.changed`. The pause survives a Gateway restart because the task can still be continued.
- No acknowledgment text or other child content is exposed on the row.
- No schema or protocol-version change: `subagentRunState` is not part of the TypeBox `SessionRowSchema` (which allows extra properties), so generated schemas, validators and Swift/Kotlin models are unchanged.
- Native clients (iOS/Android/macOS) store the field as a string and only compare it to `"active"`, so they keep today's presentation.

Alternatives rejected:

- A new `status: "paused"` value: `status` is a closed union that existing clients and the generated UI validators check, so a new value would break older clients.
- A separate `paused: true` flag: it would duplicate run-state ownership next to `subagentRunState`.

Known transients, all visible, short-lived and self-correcting:

- While a kill of a paused child is in flight, the registry keeps the pause marker until the kill reconciles, so the row can briefly read `paused` before it reads `killed` (noted in a code comment).
- The registry's pause can publish just before the yielded turn's session lifecycle end, so a row can briefly read `paused` with `status: "running"`.
- While a resume is being admitted, the row read `historical` with `hasActiveRun: true` before it turned `active` (existing behavior, seen in the live trace below). Clients should let `hasActiveRun` win, as the protocol docs say.

Open question: whether `subagentRunState` should become a closed union in `SessionRowSchema`. That would make it a stricter contract, but any future value would then fail the generated validators in a Control UI tab running an older bundle. This PR leaves it as an unvalidated extra field, as today.

The Control UI waiting list in #185585 will consume this in a follow-up after both land. Docs: `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-bootstrap-and-events.md` (client contract) and `docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md`.

Contributor credit: @jalehman requested and approved this design.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8cb34bf0-96df-41ab-aa9f-6c710ab3a5fd)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d2ac72c7-021b-47cd-9ed7-e1bff7a2d709)

## Evidence

title: fix(claude-cli): preserve completion context when queued inputs arrive
body:
Related: #185746, #184098

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude-backed sessions can lose a child's completion context while the parent is busy, or record OpenClaw-supplied context as if the user typed it.

## User Impact

User impact: queued inputs retain their own origin and completion context, while inbound metadata and resume notes stay separate from human-authored text.

Forwarded inputs are marked synthetic in Claude's native history. Their canonical messages remain visible, but their prompt rows are omitted from Claude's fallback-history seed. Private context retains full producer fragments and can use more input tokens than the compact inline form. No configuration change or migration is required.

This does not repair historical transcripts, the remaining static-prompt/bootstrap resume drift, or the separate legacy display sanitizer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #185746 rather than repeating its absorbed fixes. The host forwards per-input provenance and private context through the existing injection contract; Claude associates that context with the queued input UUID, including hook reruns. Initial prompts and same-session completion catch-up use the same private-context boundary. Raw-process transports retain their existing inline path.

A shared provenance predicate replaces separate initial/queued classification, and caller-surface-only tool differences no longer change the native binding fingerprint. Existing canonical transcript and admission owners remain authoritative. #184098's assistant-answer ownership work is complementary and untouched.

title: improve(agents): reduce retained memory for long reasoning replies
body:
Suggested by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a0909f93-e095-40ec-b6fe-10e0f4c71da4)
- [Packaged verification and landing](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/89d93f8d-22e5-4f9e-918f-2f08de896c8c)

## What Problem This Solves

Long reasoning replies retain duplicate detached reasoning strings while the agent keeps both its model result and input-answer snapshot.

## User Impact

Lower retained JavaScript heap for active turns with long reasoning; no intended change to replies, transcript bytes, delivery directives, or source receipts. No configuration or migration is needed. This is not a whole-Gateway RSS or speedup claim: small timing-tail movements and a higher text-only peak heap remain visible below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep both independent native-cloned mutable message trees, but share only reasoning strings already detached by the first clone of the exact same assistant event. Text stays on its original clone/restoration path; sharing text was rejected because it regressed long text-only retention.

## Evidence

Qualified source `9f112e02f39996ec9214baa1a39ba28c577f4809`; base `5cb8bb80941cc4f1192bb9e259adcff6eceeaf2d`. The publisher added metadata-only head `10159999f2caa27198b7e10d1c9f3510c5f64e3a`: both commits have identical tree `1d6391a038f993e09ee17eb0ded2a29efe36eaa1` and an empty diff. Source-bound local/build proof is reused, not relabeled as a rebuild. Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable scoped findings (reviewer did not run tests).

**Exact published-head CI passed:** [CI gate, run 40468407525](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40468407525/job/122072122743), including selected tests, lint, types, boundaries, UI e2e, baseline ratchets, and security-fast. Its complete log reports no failed or timed-out jobs and no inherited-failure exception. The managed landing inspection reports this head mergeable and clean. ClawSweeper is advisory; only its receipt was present at this inspection.

### Handler-boundary memory acceptance

Thirty fresh serial Node 26.12.1 processes: five alternating-order baseline/candidate pairs per workload, 24 held production subscriptions, three warmups. All exited 0; all behavior digests matched; source/workload hashes stayed unchanged. Workload SHA-256: `4f02feb613aca590c248c8be03ba64998ad0bbc5379975af580accbb5355af50`.

| Workload | Baseline retained increment | Candidate retained increment |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 128 KiB reasoning / 8 KiB final | 9,498,752 B | 6,417,728 B (−32.436%; ~125 KiB saved per held turn) |
| 128 KiB text only | 27,074,152 B | 27,049,024 B |
| 128-character reasoning / 64-character final | 1,923,736 B | 1,923,232 B |

No extra full plain-text copy or displaced external-memory growth. External/array-buffer deltas were identical: long/plain 65,640 B external including 65,600 B arrays; short 40 B / 0 B. Arrays overlap external bytes; they are not added.

The predeclared gate was ≥10% retained-heap reduction or ≥64 KiB saved per native long-reasoning turn, matching behavior, no plain-text-copy/external-memory regression, and investigation of material latency regressions. This clears the memory gate. After a silent continuation replaces the completed snapshot, the long kept phase is only 2,752,696 → 2,598,312 B: most saving is active-turn lifetime, not permanent session memory.

Median across process medians / median across process p95s (baseline → candidate): long 3.014/4.228 → 2.912/4.116 ms; plain 35.525/43.738 → 35.478/44.197 ms; short 1.024/1.641 → 1.006/1.656 ms. Individual cohorts overlap and can worsen; no speedup claim. Plain peak heap was 92,696,064 → 94,404,288 B. Host load 10.24–35.47; source-loader/allocator noise dominates RSS. The maintainer accepted conditional progress with the disclosed small short-answer/tail cost, not a waiver for a new material regression.

Commands in separately installed, fixed-revision worktrees with independent disposable HOME/state/tmp:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/terminal-assistant-snapshot-measure.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/terminal-assistant-snapshot-measure.ts --text-only
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/terminal-assistant-snapshot-measure.ts --short
```

<details>
<summary>Timing ranges and local gates</summary>

Per-process median / p95 ranges (baseline; candidate), in ms:

- Long: medians 2.938–3.671; 2.874–3.514. p95s 3.919–5.283; 4.064–6.603.
- Plain: medians 35.061–36.219; 34.457–40.651. p95s 42.996–46.545; 42.629–48.592.
- Short: medians 1.021–1.041; 0.987–1.350. p95s 1.469–1.669; 1.562–1.931.

113 focused tests, targeted core/agents-root/scripts tsgo, targeted core/scripts/config lint, formatting, diff checks, and the native commit hook passed. Full unused-file Knip remains **failed**, only on four unchanged unrelated scripts: chat-history-response-page-measure.mjs, sandbox-retirement-authority.ts, system-prompt-request-measure.ts, worktree-index-metadata-measure.ts. Native production graph reported zero; no owned path appeared. This is not an aggregate green claim.

The harness uses production subscription handlers with stub ingress; it does not measure serialization, live-provider inference, or whole-Gateway savings.

</details>

### Packaged Gateway qualification

Independent frozen install and `pnpm build:runtime` exited 0 on qualified source `9f112e02f39996ec9214baa1a39ba28c577f4809`. Both build stamps bind that source with `inputsClean: true`. `dist/entry.js` SHA-256: `d24178dcdf61ae6791ca666be03aef1245199cb01a26cbc42c6c50584e46ef9e`.

A real disposable packaged Gateway and native agent ran synthetic loopback OpenAI Responses SSE with maintained `attempt-retention`. A task-only controller adapter added 128 KiB visible summaries to its opaque reasoning; a read-only observer used the same compiled production event graph. One warmup plus one measured turn completed through `agent.wait` (`status: ok`) and terminal lifecycle events. The measured cycle observed three actual tools/results, three reasoning responses, two signature replays, one output-limit recovery, and three image requests.

An independent verifier exited 0: all six source receipts matched persisted message IDs and active-message positions; all 131,072 reasoning characters matched; both raw 8,640-character finals matched byte-for-byte, as did the normal 8,639-character trimmed visible projection. Owned Gateway PIDs exited cleanly and both loopback ports were released. No live Team Gateway or external-provider credentials were used.

**Limitation:** the combined controller exited 1 because its history oracle expected >128 KiB messages in a bounded history page. The workload reached `RESULT`; history correctly returned its existing oversized-message placeholder. Full bytes/receipts were independently verified at real producer/events and durable records without rerunning that completed workload. An earlier setup exceeded the documented `maxChars: 500000` cap and was corrected. This is synthetic packaged behavior, not real-provider inference or Gateway performance proof.

<details>

Task-owned HOME/state/tmp/profile and loopback ports 42931/42934; temporary controller adapter and compiled-event observer, no source changes.

title: improve(ui): keep personal collections quiet until used
body:
Related: #181680, #185348

## What Problem This Solves

An unused personal-groups section adds sidebar clutter, while first-time setup needs a discoverable path that does not look like moving a shared session.

## User Impact

The section stays hidden until a collection exists; deliberately empty collections remain visible. Users can create one from **Filter & sort** without selecting a session, or choose **Add to my collections** in the existing native session menu to add a session or create a collection with it selected.

**“My collections” is provisional naming for human review. This PR intentionally remains a draft.** The feature remains available to solo users and guests; there is no multi-user-only gate. Shared **Move to group**, its guest disabled state, and session access are unchanged. No migration or permission change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing native menu and compact Back behavior remain in charge; the session menu gains one organization entry, not a replacement menu. Creation, editing, and adding use the existing personal navigation preference and scoped session owner. Descriptor-only/off-page targets remain eligible, and their observation and explicit agent scope survive menu dismissal through dialog submission.

The explanation is: **“Only your sidebar changes. Sessions stay in their groups.”** Removing a collection never deletes sessions or changes shared group membership. Existing preference identities, browser-local guest storage, child trees, and offline presentation are retained.

## Evidence

- **88 focused tests passed** across seven menu, preference, sidebar, and child-lifecycle files. The final native-menu suite also passed all **52 tests** after its test-host typing correction. The unit runs took 13.47 seconds wall time for the seven-file selection and 8.01 seconds for the final menu-only run; individual changed unit files remain below five seconds of test time.
- **Seven production-bundle browser scenarios passed** in 46.35 seconds wall time, including build/setup: first discovery, preselection, add to existing, no-session-selected creation, deliberate emptiness, last removal, reload, stale-editor rejection, child placement, unavailable references, off-page add/create, and narrow native Back. These scenarios exercise the actual Control UI, not a mockup.
- **The isolated real-Gateway guest flow passed**: browser-local create/edit/reorder/reload/remove, child updates, denied access to another guest’s session, and no shared mutations. It took 108.20 seconds wall time, including isolated startup and compilation; its 41.56-second scenario uses two real guest clients because mocked permissions cannot establish that boundary. No model turn or deployed Gateway change was performed.
- The unused-section regression was **red on the original component** and green with this change. An explicit-agent native-menu case was also red before forwarding the selected target’s agent scope and green afterward.
- Production, UI-component-test, and UI-E2E-test typechecks; focused typed lint; format; localization verification; controller guard; and whitespace checks passed. Fresh independent AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 issues after the off-page repair. A later mechanical test-host typing correction was revalidated with its compiler and all 52 native-menu tests.
- The current production build passed the unchanged same-host performance gate against a8d925edd49e511f2d74a7aa4f3ef71b2896cf63: startup JS **270,448 → 271,101 bytes gzip (+653 B)**, below the existing **271,757 B** enforcement limit; startup requests remain **5**, and startup CSS is unchanged. Chat/New boot growth was **1,182/1,092 B gzip**, within existing limits. No budgets or baselines were raised.

Remaining qualification: Chromium is covered; WebKit was not run. Broad PR CI and final product/naming review remain separate from this draft’s focused proof.

### Visual evidence

Matched synthetic fixtures in the actual Control UI, light theme, 1280×900. The narrow native menu is 390×844. The representative pair was also delivered in the originating discussion.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Unused sidebar before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8751553-f280-4b8b-8b76-3b9f568f9dc3) | ![Unused sidebar after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83a300bc-2a5d-422f-b36f-963de19de25e) |

<details>
<summary>Native discovery, creation, empty collections, children, and narrow menu</summary>

#### Existing native session menu with one additive collection action

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long-running Goals show hundreds of elapsed hours, and Resume remains clickable while another session turn is sending, queued, or running even though the Gateway must reject it.

title: feat(ui): show yield acknowledgments as agent text and list waited-on sessions
body:
Related: #164190, #165378, #173938, #162272

## What Problem This Solves

A `sessions_yield` acknowledgment shows in Control UI chat as a centered, muted system notice (other channels deliver it as a normal reply), disappears once the agent resumes, and the waiting line does not say which sessions the agent is waiting on.

## User Impact

User impact: the agent's acknowledgment reads as its own message and stays in the conversation after it resumes; while it waits, the line names the child session (or lists several, with status in words and attention first, each linked to its session); a "Resumed · 9m 32s later · 3 sessions" rule marks where it picked up. A message wait with no acknowledgment keeps the "Waiting for a message" notice. No Gateway, protocol or config change.

Known limitation: a child paused by its own `sessions_yield` (awaiting a continuation) reads **Done**, because session rows don't carry that paused state; **Needs your input** comes from the child's own attention status, the same signal the sidebar shows. A paused field is tracked separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The acknowledgment already exists only as the confirmed `sessions_yield` result, so the yield projection now adds it as assistant text in the run that handed off, instead of a notice that is dropped on resume. Only the public acknowledgment the result echoes is used; the private continuation `message` stays hidden. Webchat stores no separate assistant copy for agent runs, so nothing renders twice.

The waiting line and resume rule read children from the pane's own access-scoped child query and name nobody until that query is complete (rows seeded from the sidebar can be a partial set). Names link through the shared session route helper; children the pane can't open, or panes without a session opener, show plain text.

**This partly undoes #165378.** That PR removed the "Handed off"/"Resumed" markers and named only subagents. This change brings back a "Resumed" rule, but only beneath a spoken acknowledgment, inline in that reply, carrying the wait duration and an expandable child list; and it names visible non-subagent child sessions, only once the roster is hydrated. The reason: an acknowledgment is the agent speaking, and once it is kept after resume, the reader needs to see where the wait ended and which sessions did the work. @shakkernerd, since #165378 was your deliberate call, a review of that tradeoff would be appreciated.

**Interaction with #162272:** that open PR persists the acknowledgment as a separate assistant transcript row. If both land as written, the acknowledgment would show twice; whichever lands second needs to drop the persisted copy or dedupe against it.

The `sessions_yield` `acknowledgment` parameter now describes a brief waiting status shown to the user and asks for answers in normal assistant text (prompt snapshots regenerated).

Contributor credit: @jalehman requested and approved this design.

title: fix(workers): preserve compile caching in foreground Gateway task workers

Fixes: task workers started by a foreground Gateway miss the launcher-owned Node compile cache.

## User Impact

title: improve: reduce GitHub quota while PR scripts wait for CI
body:
Requested by Peter Steinberger.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3aa3f07b-5905-459d-94ef-59bf8e6d8b74)

## What Problem This Solves

PR scripts repeatedly reload CI run/job data while waiting, even when nothing has changed.

## User Impact

Maintainers waiting with `--completion ci-run` can reuse unchanged responses without spending GitHub primary API quota. This does not change OpenClaw runtime behavior or merge requirements. Requests still reach GitHub and remain subject to secondary limits. The conditional reads use the native caller-authenticated GitHub CLI route, not the pooled relay.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use authenticated REST ETag revalidation for the attached run and bounded, attempt-specific job pages. A valid 304 reuses only its matching process-local response; changed responses refresh it, and missing ETags retain ordinary reads. Native `gh` reports HTTP 304 with exit 1, which is handled explicitly. Completed runs avoid reloading informational job progress.

Fresh PR head/lifecycle/conflict checks, exact run/head identity, host routing, deadlines, and lock-notifier propagation remain intact. The existing lightweight GraphQL rollup path is unchanged. This adopts the useful conditional-request pattern from [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/5d91ab1117ad51ef1288a94717d85c70e7af09fe/packages/source-control-github/src/server/gitHubConditionalChecks.ts), without adding a service, configuration, dependency, or durable cache.

## Evidence

- Three CLI regression cases fail on the base for absent conditional requests and pass with the change: unchanged run/jobs followed by success, failure, or a moved PR head. The fixture includes native gh's nonzero 304 exit.
- **225 watcher tests passed**; wrapper runtime-import inventory and 10 dependency-resolution tests passed. Owning root-scripts and root-tooling typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, native Node syntax, and `git diff --check` passed. The initial CI callback type error was reproduced and fixed using the root-scripts config, which actually includes the new watcher test.
- **127 native PR integration tests passed** after migrating their GitHub fixtures to the REST run identity, completion state, and existing repository aliases. The previous hosted-wait stall was reproduced through the real watcher; the fix preserves scheduled success, pending behavior, and post-CI main refreshes without increasing production timeouts. These existing consumer suites took **578.77s** in Vitest (580.63s wrapper wall).
- **Live GitHub**, [CI run 40451904659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40451904659), head `454ffd3fdf881870ba9d44d8c2fa605ab177437a`: the first run/jobs reads returned 200 with **180,165 captured response bytes**; the next unchanged pair returned 304 with **2,488 bytes** (98.6% less for those two responses, including headers). Fresh PR reads still occurred. A later changed jobs response returned 200 and progress advanced from 51 to 53 completed jobs. The bounded live watch correctly remained pending; this is not a claim that that unrelated CI run had completed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no actionable P0/P1 findings on the implementation or the later fixture repair. The implementation lead inspected the unchanged transport/parser and full fixture owner; the real transport and full consumer suites were also exercised above.
- Test cost: the existing watcher suite plus regression took **145.49s** (150.87s command wall); the three new regressions took **2.68s**, and **1.93s** in the final focused replay. The longer existing suites preserve CLI timeout, notifier, pagination, supersession, and native PR lifecycle contracts. Hosted CI timing is available in this PR's checks.

Simplification: removed the old job-bearing `gh run view` polling branch; one small run reader now owns validators and job-page collection. Growth is limited to that process-local protocol handling, its CLI regression, migrated native test fixtures, and the required materialized-wrapper inventory/docs.

title: feat: make busy-session messages automatic with coherent security presets
body:
Related: #184846, #185381

## What Problem This Solves

Busy-session messages can be refused or require a manual `/followup` resend, while execution and steering defaults express inconsistent trust assumptions.

## User Impact

Default-personal messages steer when compatible and otherwise queue quietly for a requester-owned turn, without automatic queue-status spam or a resend requirement. Explicit strict rejection remains available.

`security.preset: "personal" | "corporate"` supplies coherent defaults across sandboxing, approvals, managed files, steering, conversation reach, and DM routing. Personal is the default trusted-operator/full-access posture; corporate selects session sandboxes and stricter steering/reach defaults. Explicit source and agent/session settings retain precedence; mandatory host, role, access, and approval floors are never granted or bypassed.

**Tradeoffs:** collaboration retains incumbent execution authority—not a permission intersection or causal tool attribution. Shared history remains shared. Corporate is configurable, not compliance certification or hostile-tenant isolation; sandbox networking does not cover every host tool/plugin/browser request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing requester-owned queue instead of dropping input. Expand presets only at runtime configuration materialization, removing the competing persisted steering-default writer from Doctor and fresh configuration paths.

Existing explicit steering booleans, including older Doctor-persisted values, remain unchanged; unset an override to follow the preset. Runtime expansions are not persisted as authored settings. Corporate changes future DM routing keys without deleting or moving prior history. No live configuration, identity grants, public shares, authentication, or deployment is changed.

The documentation compares primary sources for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode, distinguishing approval UX, isolation, and managed policy floors.

Credit: @obviyus identified the dropped-message workflow and proposed automatic queue fallback in #184846. This work adds quiet handling, explicit strict refusal, and the broader defaults requested by @steipete. It retains @jalehman’s landed attempt-scoped preparation/adoption owner from #185381 rather than maintaining our competing identity-only exception; the distinct before-first-call regression remains.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes new conversations keeping an ID-only URL after their generated title arrives, until the browser is reloaded.

## User Impact

The open conversation gets a descriptive URL without reloading, losing an unsent draft, or adding a browser-history entry. Query parameters, message anchors, dashboard/chat faces, short-reference lengths, and newer navigation are preserved. Prepared or cached conversations still wait for authoritative identity confirmation before their URL changes or queued messages are sent.

The session observer updated the tab title but did not notify the navigation owner. URL synchronization now uses the same live name presentation and the already committed session identity. title: fix: other viewers see your Side chat in a shared session
body:
Closes #181215
Related: #181220, #181223

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: everyone viewing a shared session sees the same Side chat, and one person's **Clear side chat** wipes it for everyone.

## User Impact

User impact: each signed-in person now has their own Side chat in a session. Other viewers can't see your questions or answers, and clearing yours doesn't affect theirs. Resetting or deleting the session still clears everyone's. Connections without a personal identity (for example a shared Gateway token) still share one thread, as before. No UI change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Side chat threads were keyed by session and agent only. They are now keyed by session, agent and the requester's authenticated profile, which the Gateway derives from the connection (never from request params). Ask, state and reset only touch the caller's own thread. Session reset, delete and archive still revoke every person's thread, including in-flight questions.

## Evidence

Live video proof, recorded below in a PR comment: a real Gateway with two trusted-proxy users (Alice, Bob) and real providers, one shared session per runtime: **Codex harness, Claude CLI, Gemini CLI and direct OpenAI API**. In each, Alice chats and asks in her Side chat, Bob opens the same session and sees the shared transcript but not her Side chat, Bob asks his own question, and Alice still sees only hers. The recording script asserts the absence of the other person's question at every step. Recorded on a Blacksmith Testbox with the repository's live credentials.

title: fix: goals fail to resume after stopping a run
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Goal Resume fails with “requires an idle built-in local session with recoverable history” after an operator stops a run, even after that work has fully settled. Definitive admission refusals also appear as an unconfirmed update.

## User Impact

Operators can resume the same stopped Goal without resetting the conversation or losing its history. Unsupported admission is reported as a rejection instead of leaving an uncertain operation waiting for reconciliation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit Resume may follow a settled abort, not just the special running-Goal replacement flow. Apply that distinction to local and supported Codex cloud-worker admission, while retaining live-work exclusion, freshness, placement, session identity, and current-authority checks. Use the existing typed Goal rejection contract so the existing UI can retire the refused request. Ordinary chat and Goal Start eligibility are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Integrated main `5516b9086e6092af42dac1ac42e635267e70d3b5` into the contributor branch after the admission-owner refactor. The retired restart-recovery module stays deleted; both current local and worker Resume predicates receive the fix.
- Fresh shared AutoReview of `5516b9086e6092af42dac1ac42e635267e70d3b5..60ff8e09bbe2922b9da9459fd5ca86c5cfe0259b` completed with no actionable P0-P2 findings. A separate independent source review also found no blockers.
- Current candidate: all 42 Gateway Goal tests and all 33 UI Goal recovery tests passed. Restoring the three production files from the baseline, while retaining the regression tests, made both targeted regressions fail for the expected admission defects.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40793088673) completed with one attributed upstream failure: the full-tree mock-export ratchet reports 14 violations in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. [Main independently reports the same 14 violations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792935936/job/123184172493). The two tests, baseline ledger, checker and inspected checker inputs are unchanged between the protected-main parent and the tested PR merge. `security-fast` passed; all other jobs passed or were skipped. CI remains failed and is recorded in native pre-existing-failure evidence for landing; no CI rerun or unrelated source repair is claimed.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Claim:** an operator can Resume the same Goal after Stop has settled, and a definitive unsupported-admission refusal retires the pending UI operation.
- **Exercised surface:** production Gateway Goal RPC admission, queue/lifecycle handling and SQLite state, plus the existing UI Goal recovery owner.
- **Scenario/fixture:** Stop, wait for settlement, Resume with a new operation, complete, and replay the receipt without duplicate execution; unsupported admission retains its typed `goal-invalid` rejection.
- **Command/environment:** Crabbox `provider=local-container`, lease `cbx_bff6cd3713ae`, run `run_76ce59bd0f38`; Linux, `node:24-bookworm`, Node 24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0, one test worker and bounded compiler threads. Canonical baseline source plus the six-file reviewed patch reconstructed tree `116593a9972df7b5c36a050230d4f7bf14ed5d01`, checked before execution; source hashes were checked and restored after the baseline replay.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat-goal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/chat/chat-goals.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
# With the three production admission files restored from the baseline:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat-goal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern='stops automatic pursuit and resumes|keeps an unscoped reply-dispatch hook'
```

- **Observed result:** candidate Gateway 42/42 and UI 33/33 passed; baseline replay failed exactly the two intended regressions. The candidate source hashes matched again after restoration.
- **Artifact/trace:** the executed run produced `green.log`, `ui-green.log`, `red.log`, and `receipt.json`. Summary of the captured output:

```json
{"proof":"goal-stop-settlement-resume","green":{"passed":42},"uiPassed":33,"baselineRegressionFailures":2,"canonicalTree":"116593a9972df7b5c36a050230d4f7bf14ed5d01"}
```

- **Limits:** model execution and worker transport are simulated. This proves the production admission/state boundary and UI rejection contract; no live-model, real cloud-worker transport, deployed Gateway, or production-session mutation is claimed. The initial Windows rsync trial ended before test execution and is excluded from these results.

The proof command exited 0 and its captured receipt was verified. Crabbox's controller subsequently exited 7 on a workspace-owner renewal after lease release; the owned container's removal was verified. This cleanup diagnostic is separate from the executed test results.

title: fix(ui): running tools show unknown after history refresh
body:
Closes #185254

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes running tools showing “Outcome unknown” after chat history refresh, and call-only history being counted as an unknown execution outcome.

## User Impact

Known tool activity keeps its purpose and Running state until an outcome receipt. Incomplete history says “No result available” without inventing success, failure, or an unknown outcome. Backing-session replacement still clears the previous session’s live facts.

## Why This Change Was Made

A saved invocation was incorrectly sufficient to retire live execution state. Retirement now requires a result or terminal prepared receipt; provisional history remains distinct from execution outcomes across chat, completed-work summaries, and subagent activity.

Server replay-budget retention is unchanged. Missing replay facts do not establish whether a call is running or finished.

## Evidence

- Production history-hydration regression: red with the original retirement owner; green with the fix, including later completion.
- 276 focused tests and 16 Chromium tests passed. The lifecycle browser scenario uses production progress capture and in-flight snapshot projection, not an injected unknown status or a live external-model run.
- Initial CI found two stale expectations. The retirement fixture now contains a recorded result, and provisional calls are no longer expected to count as unknown. All 86 tests in those two files passed afterward (3.63 s wrapper wall); production code is unchanged by this CI repair.
- Core/UI/browser-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks passed, including supplementary UI test-type shards.
- Knip production unused-file scan passed with 0 entries. The full-tree scan failed with 20 reports under unchanged `scripts/perf/`; no changed path was reported. A separate baseline scan was not run. This aggregate failure is retained, not marked green or hidden with an ignore/baseline.
- Independent AutoReview: scoped-clean P0–P2 on the complete production candidate; assessment did not independently rerun tests. The final test-only correction was reviewed directly.
- Local focused batches: 110 s, 44 s, and 130 s wall including shared compilation. Full browser batch: 68 s including build/setup; the focused lifecycle scenario takes 2.25 s. Current-head hosted CI is pending.
- All three published images were verified on the actual PR page: decoded labels, visible bounds, dimensions, matching SHA256 bytes, and inspected rendered screenshots.

### Before

Same fixture, with the bounded replay deliberately omitted: incomplete history is incorrectly labeled as an unknown outcome.

title: fix: retain chat prompts when read acknowledgments overlap startup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted chat prompts silently disappearing before the agent starts when a read acknowledgement overlaps turn admission.

Related: #177365 and #175837.

## User Impact

The original prompt remains runnable and executes once after temporary lifecycle contention clears. Cancellation and revoked access still stop execution; a replaced session database is rejected rather than adopted during retry. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lifecycle contention was reported as an active model run even when no run existed. Dispatch then retired a selected input and returned an empty successful result, leaving ordinary prompts without a retry owner.

Distinguish that precise pre-execution refusal, defer and settle its existing mailbox claim, then reclaim the same input through the canonical selector. Retain the initially admitted database incarnation across reselection. Actual active-run queue policy, source authority and admitted-operation settlement remain unchanged. No new queue, schema or durable state is introduced.

## Evidence

- Two independent real-SQLite dispatch overlap cases fail on the original code with no final reply and pass with the fix.
- Five focused dispatch cases pass: allow-live and wait contention, cancellation, source-authority revocation, and same-session-ID database replacement. The replacement control failed on the first candidate before the physical-owner check was added.
- A real isolated Gateway WebSocket test submits `chat.send` and concurrently marks the conversation read through `sessions.patch`. It receives the final reply, confirms no pending input remains, and verifies an idempotent resend does not execute the reply source again. The transport and dispatcher are real; the reply source is controlled, not a live provider call.
- Core, affected messaging-test and Gateway-method-test typechecks pass. Source-scoped lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the complete implementation and lifecycle context found no actionable findings.
- CI run [40426629690](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40426629690) exposed two integration defects in the first published head: a prepared-dispatch type-import cycle and these real-SQLite regressions running without their host owner. The follow-up moves the unchanged retry helper to a leaf and registers the suite on the existing forked database-worker route. Both cycle checks pass; all 23 dispatch-suite tests pass on that route, and all 12 routing-registry tests pass. No retry, timeout, assertion or admission safeguard was weakened.
- Local test cost: initial safety matrix 51.05 seconds wall time; isolated Gateway selection 68.20 seconds wall time, including suite startup (the added case's callback took 7.918 seconds). The complete host-routed dispatch suite took 64.53 seconds after compiler preparation. Current-head CI timing is pending. The Gateway proof reuses its existing suite server rather than adding a second startup.

Fixes: a session’s sidebar spinner can remain inactive or queued after its agent has already begun executing.

## User Impact

No configuration, stored-data, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing controller already owns the queued-to-executing transition, but it did not publish that change. Publish one runtime lifecycle notification there and remove the two later callback-owned notifications. Transcript capture, execution timing, and cancellation arming retain their existing owners.

Fixes the missing work signal when a chat is waiting on subagents or still has task-owned background commands running.

The visible conversation shares the existing process observation with the panels.

Counts cover reconnectable background exec processes, not every foreground tool or OS process. Truncated inventories show a lower bound with "+". title: improve(ui): show Sign in after installing plugins that need an account
body:
## What Problem This Solves

After you install a plugin that needs an account, like Linear, the chat install card shows a green **Installed** chip and the plugin page simply drops its Install button. Neither one tells people they still have to sign in before the plugin works.

## User Impact

User impact: when an installed plugin has an account that isn't signed in, the button that said **Install** now says **Sign in**. This applies to both the chat card and the plugin page. On the plugin page, the button in each Accounts row also says **Sign in** instead of **Connect**. After the account is signed in, both surfaces go back to their normal installed state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both surfaces now read account status from `plugins.inspect`, the same source the Accounts section already uses.

- **Chat card:** for an installed plugin with an account that isn't authorized, the card shows a primary **Sign in** button where the Installed chip was. Clicking it opens the plugin page, which matches how the card's Install button works: the link selects and an explicit click acts. The card only asks for account status when this operator can actually start sign-in (`mcp.authLogin` with admin scope), so other operators still see **Installed**.
- **Plugin page:** the hero puts **Sign in** first, in the primary slot, and it starts the existing sign-in flow for the first account that isn't connected. While **Sign in** is showing, **Ask** becomes a secondary button so the page never has two primary actions.
- **Copy:** the account action and its error messages say "Sign in" / "signing in" instead of "Connect" / "connecting". The **Connected** status label is unchanged.
- **Docs:** the Control UI settings, MCP control UI, and MCP tools pages now say **Sign in** where they used to say **Connect**.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the real Control UI production bundle running against the mocked Gateway E2E harness. The fixture is a synthetic Linear plugin that is installed and enabled, with its account in the `requires-authorization` state.

title: fix: interrupted sessions stall after a Gateway restart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sessions can remain interrupted after a Gateway restart when long-running recovered work blocks the startup recovery scan.

## User Impact

User impact: running sessions resume at the configured agent concurrency after a restart, while interactive replies keep their own execution slots. Explicit Stop/reset, retry budgets, and current-authority checks remain unchanged. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate reconciliation from execution admission: the startup scan prepares each interrupted session and settles completed deliveries without waiting for earlier executions. One tracked FIFO dispatch pump preserves ordered admission, attempt accounting, retained-source cleanup, and joined shutdown. The recovery lane now follows the existing agent concurrency setting instead of its four-slot bootstrap default.

The store scan no longer owns the dispatch lifetime; existing outcome handling moves to one prepared-dispatch owner. No second recovery state machine, queue manager, or durable schema is introduced. Simplification retained this ownership split because it removes scan-wide head-of-line blocking while preserving joined shutdown (production +194/−88 lines; tests +255/−149, including extraction of the saturation cases from an existing oversized test module).

## Evidence

- Negative controls on the pinned base reproduce both defects: later delivered work remains interrupted behind four held recoveries, and a configured six-slot recovery lane starts only four executions.
- 193 recovery tests, 9 lane tests, and 4 interactive-priority consumer tests passed. Both saturation regression variants settle the later delivered row while queued executions remain uncharged and unreserved; FIFO completion and Stop are covered.
- Core, infra-test, and E2E typechecks, scoped lint/format, docs sanity, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Real cold-process Gateway acceptance passed (63.2 seconds): five interrupted turns reached the synthetic local Responses provider together; raw shutdown, managed restart, and SIGKILL recovery completed; Stop/reset remained cancelled; the uncertain tool effect was inspected rather than repeated; history contained one user prompt and one final result per completed scenario. This uses a real isolated Gateway, not a live external provider.
- Earlier acceptance attempts timed out before recovery because inherited proxy settings broke the fixture’s loopback model transport. The successful invocation preserved those proxies and appended only loopback hosts to fixture-local `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy`; no product guard or deadline was changed. One additional run was interrupted by the hosting Gateway restart. Temporary phase logging was removed after the successful run; the committed assertions and production code are unchanged.
- Independent contextual review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. After the mechanical test extraction, both moved regression variants, infra types, lint/format, and the line-cap ratchet passed again.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: closing the last sidebar browser page leaves a generic, empty Browser tab when the native close acknowledgment arrives before the native tab-state update.

## User Impact

Closing a browser page removes that page completely. Other open pages remain available, and closing the final page removes its Browser tab instead of returning to the browser start screen. This also affects directly opened links; it is not limited to links opened from an existing browser page.

The native host commits a close and replies before its scheduled state push reaches the Control UI. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub publication rejects a conversation’s own managed checkout as a different checkout, and later interruptions can replay a stale publication error as an undelivered-result warning.

Validate the selected checkout against the live session-owned worktree rather than its source/skills directory, retaining the existing requester, session, and registry authority checks. title: improve(ui): resolve guest person cards outside a chat session
body:
Related: #185035 ## What Problem This Solves A guest's mention chip with no owning chat session opens a person card that only says "Could not load people. Try again.", even though the guest can mention the same person from the New Session @ menu. ## User Impact User impact: for callers without directory access (guests), a mention chip outside a chat view now opens the same quiet person card as inside one: the person's name and avatar when the guest could mention them, otherwise the mention label with an initial avatar. It never shows the error or "Try again". Staff cards are unchanged. No shipped surface renders mention chips outside the chat view today (inventory below), so nothing changes visibly in the current UI. Without this change, the first non-chat surface to render chips (for example Inbox excerpts or summaries) would show guests the error. ## Why This Change Was Made Item 12 (#185035) resolves guest chips through `users.mentionable {sessionKey}` and left chips without a session on the old status as a deliberate scope limit. Josh lifted that limit. When `users.list` isn't available, the card now resolves in this order: 1. **Session key available** (chip under `[data-chat-session-key]`): unchanged item 12 path. 2. **No session context, caller without directory access:** `users.mentionable {agentId, query}` for the selected application agent, else the gateway default. In `human-mention-policy.ts` this form returns the people who could read a new shared session the caller starts on that agent, after the Gateway checks the caller's role may create sessions there. That is the exact request the New Session @ menu sends, so the card reads it only when that menu is available to the caller (`sessions.create` admitted). It reveals nothing the guest can't already see by typing `@`. 3. **Miss, refusal or skipped read:** the quiet label card. Unchanged from item 12: exact `profileId` match only, the own-chip skip, and the per-handshake cache (5 min for answers, 30 s for failures, 16 entries) that a reconnect retires. Cache keys are now the request params, so the agent and session forms of one label never collide. Presence and activity sections are untouched. Staff stay on `users.list` with the same miss status. Outside a session, a failed staff directory read keeps "Could not load people. Try again." and never calls `users.mentionable` (gated on `operator.read`, the same check the directory uses).
Where mention chips can render, and whether the surface owns a session Chips render only from chat-message bubbles whose message metadata carries `humanMentions`. Raw HTML in Markdown is escaped, so other Markdown surfaces cannot produce chips. | Surface | Renders chips today | Owning session key | | --- | --- | --- | | Chat view transcript, including split panes | Yes | Yes, `data-chat-session-key` on the chat section (item 12) | | Side chat (companion rail) | No: turns are plain text without mention metadata | Yes (`props.sessionKey`), not tagged because there is nothing to resolve | | Pending session create preview | No: passive Markdown without `humanMentions` | Prospective key only; the Gateway has no session yet, so tagging it would invent a key | | Inbox / sidebar mention entries | No: sender avatar and plain-text excerpt | Yes (`mention.sessionKey`) | | Custodian | No: plain text | System agent, no user session | | Session progress card, plugin session summary, meeting summary, cron runs, logbook, skill, agent and file views | No: Markdown without mention metadata | n/a | No surface needed a new session tag.
## Evidence Screenshots come from the production Control UI bundle with a mocked Gateway and synthetic data. Because no shipped non-chat surface renders chips, the capture mounts the production `` element in the app sidebar, outside the chat section (asserted: no `[data-chat-session-key]` ancestor). The guest holds `operator.sessions.write` only. | Capture | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Guest, `@Josh` chip outside chat, light | | | | Guest, `@Josh` chip outside chat, dark | | | Staff, `@Josh` chip outside chat, unchanged (before and after crops are byte-identical): | Light | Dark | | --- | --- | | | | Recorded requests: guest before `users.mentionable` ×0; guest after `users.mentionable` ×1, `{ agentId: "main", query: "Josh" }`, and `users.list` ×0; staff before and after `users.list` ×2, `users.mentionable` ×0. Staff crops are byte-identical before and after, with the same SHA-256 in light and dark. Checks: - `ui/src/components/solid/person-reference.test.tsx`: 26/26. New or updated cases: a guest outside a session gets the agent-form hit by exact id, and the same label inside a session makes its own session-form read (no cache collision); the quiet card outside a session for the guest's own chip (no request), a roster miss, a refused read, and a guest without `sessions.create` (no request); staff outside a session keep `users.list` with no roster call and the same miss status; a failed staff directory outside a session keeps its retry status; reconnects retire the agent-form read like the session form. Item 12's "guest outside a session keeps the unresolved status" test now asserts the new behavior. - Red on base: with the runtime from `f619886505d`, the 6 outside-session guest cases fail; all pass with this change. - Production-build browser E2E: `ui/src/e2e/chat-person-reference.e2e.test.ts` 11/11, including item 12's guest session-roster flow. - `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean. Requested by @jalehman ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4ff43853-805b-4ab6-932c-1622ab5bb1d8) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/51bf9ffd-2ad4-40ef-b7f6-c305accc5a0e) ## Worked on by - @vyctorbrzezowski - @jalehman

title: chore: refresh dependencies with the October 26 maturity cutoff
body:
Closes #185129

## What Problem This Solves

Refresh OpenClaw's dependencies without admitting releases younger than seven days or silently taking incompatible migrations.

## User Impact

Users receive mature upstream fixes across AI clients, email parsing, networking, UI rendering, and native tooling. No configuration migration or user action is required. Existing release-age exceptions remain unchanged; this is not a promise that every upstream feature is enabled by OpenClaw.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sweep fixes the audit instant at **2026-10-26 22:47:27 UTC**, with an inclusive publication cutoff of **2026-10-19 22:47:27 UTC**. Native package managers generated the locks; literal toolchain callers and integrity assertions are aligned. No new policy exceptions, compatibility shims, or production mechanisms were added.

<details>
<summary>Notable updates and deliberate holds</summary>

- OpenAI 7.35.0 → 7.39.0; AWS clients 3.1152.0 → 3.1153.0; Copilot SDK 1.0.22 → 1.0.23 (packaged runtime 1.0.100).
- Undici 8.12.2 → 8.12.3; Execa 10.1.1 → 10.2.0; Kysely 0.29.6 → 0.29.7; TypeBox 1.4.1 → 1.4.2; tslog 5.2.0 → 5.4.0.
- IMAPFlow 2.5.2 → 2.5.8; mailauth 7.3.0 → 7.3.1; mailparser 3.9.40 → 3.10.0; music-metadata 12.2.1 → 12.2.3.
- CodeMirror view 6.43.14 → 6.43.15; PostCSS 8.5.31; oxfmt 0.74.0. The optional OTel exporter peer range adds 0.223 support without removing 0.220 support.
- Go 1.27.3 across module and CI pins; Android serialization 1.12.0; Swift concurrency-extras 1.4.3, subprocess 1.0.2, jinja 2.5.2; both Ruby AWS bundles refreshed; conservative Rust lock updates; Sherpa ONNX 1.13.8.
- Sandbox CLI 4.9.0, Wrangler 4.151.2, immutable ruby/setup-ruby v1.331.0, and the qualified Ubuntu 24.04 digest.
- Deferred npm 12.2.1: native npm-lock validation rejects its bundled minimatch/ip-address versions under existing policy. Retained 12.2.0 rather than adding an exception.
- Deferred ACP 2, Matrix 44, MXC 1, mailauth 8, compiler/trial prereleases, and model-exporter migrations for separate compatibility qualification. Gradle 9.8.2 triggers AGP's existing warnings-as-errors policy. Rust candidates requiring edge downgrades were rejected. Existing intentionally constrained or newer pins were preserved.
- Retained `@tanstack/virtual-core` 3.19.2: 3.19.6 previously broke a nonempty picker after Escape-close/reopen (#182010).
- Retained Muse SDK 1.4.10: 1.4.11 adds a `feedbackNotAccepted` approval-error union member incompatible with the existing handler at `extensions/muse/harness.ts:418`. Exact-head CI run 40440926608 exposed three related failures: production types, test types, and package boundary/declarations. The extensions typecheck reproduced the incompatibility locally before the deferral.
- Deferred oxlint and its platform bindings at **1.88.0**, matching `origin/main`: **oxlint 1.89 changes max-lines counting and adds 220 UI diagnostics; needs its own migration PR**. `oxlint-tsgolint` remains **7.0.2004**, unchanged from main. No caps, baselines, suppressions, or source edits were used to accommodate lint. The independent oxfmt 0.74.0 update is retained.

</details>

## Takeover verification (current head)

The reviewed head is `59d44fcff18da26a4f17bcef3ef3b6256f9e13ef`. The original branch agent concurrently published the byte-identical oxlint deferral, so the takeover adopted it with a normal fast-forward; no duplicate commit, force-push, or rebase was needed.

- Independently queried `npm view <package> time --json`: **all 73 retained candidate versions** qualify against **2026-10-19 22:47:27 UTC**. This covers **70 new pnpm identities**, changed manifest pins/peer versions, and the standalone Vercel lock. Newest publication is mailparser 3.10.0, October 19 at 20:54:22 UTC. Native registry/release/date and exact Ubuntu digest checks also remain qualified. No candidate was removed for age.
- After restoring oxlint 1.88.0, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed. Independent complete-diff Codex review was scoped-clean through P2. No application behavior, lint source, budget, baseline, or policy was changed by the deferral.
- Repeated the full original picker selection **twice on this exact head**: **34/34 passed in 13.51 seconds**, then **34/34 passed in 9.58 seconds**. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-browser.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/components/select-picker.browser.test.tsx ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`. The earlier 33/34 activation/catalog-rerender result was not reproduced; two passing replays do not establish that it is fixed or independent of every dependency. Escape/reopen remains covered with retained TanStack Virtual 3.19.2.
- Exact-head CI [40443903613](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40443903613) passed **every lint job**, production/test types, package boundaries, security-fast, and all three UI browser shards. The earlier Muse type incompatibility and oxlint migration are deferred rather than bypassed.
- A separate strict four-file lint diagnostic still reports max-lines 715/700, 701/700, 705/700, and 703/700 with oxlint 1.88.0 under both the default wrapper and `OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=oxlint`. These files and lint policy inputs are byte-identical to unchanged main; the actual scoped CI lint gates passed. The narrow diagnostic is retained as a failed diagnostic, not represented as the CI command or a passing result.

Third-party plugin tools are difficult to recognize when their previews have only a generic fallback glyph.

title: fix(chat): hide raw tool handoff resume rows after plugin reload or GitHub publish
body:
Supersedes #181290, which conflicts with current `main` and whose publishing session can no longer be continued. This is the same net change ported onto current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: raw tool-result rows such as `Plugin reload result: {...} Continue the original task in this conversation...` appear as user messages in chat after a plugin reload (`reloadAndResume`) or a GitHub publish handoff resumes the conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: after a plugin reload or GitHub publish handoff, chat shows only the agent's reply (and the "could not continue automatically" notice when resuming fails), not the internal resume prompt. Generic plugin session events stay visible. No config, migration or user action needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool handoff resumed through `enqueueSessionEventForHost` with source `"plugin"`, so its resume row was indistinguishable from real plugin events. It now uses a dedicated `"tool_handoff"` source. Chat history, live `session.message` and pending-input projections hide `internal_system` user rows from that source, alongside `exec` and `cron_failure_repair`; the row stays in the model transcript.

`"tool_handoff"` keeps every plugin-source behavior the handoff relies on:

- captured Gateway-owner authority binding in `session-event-context.ts` (the path #180109 / #182929 preserved);
- keyed-retry duplicate refusal in `session-event-handoff.ts` (handoff events carry a `tool-handoff:<uuid>` context key);
- policy readmission, which re-enqueues with the original options and therefore the same source.

Porting notes: on `main`, `SessionEventSource` is now inlined in `SessionEventOptions.source` and #182929 replaced the direct enqueue call in `session-tool-handoff.ts` with a captured `enqueue`; both conflicts were resolved by applying the same source change at the new locations. The keyed-retry dedupe condition and its test are new relative to #181290. I re-checked `src/` and `extensions/` for other branches on session-event source `"plugin"` or `sourceTool: "plugin"`; there are none besides these two.

## Evidence

- New tests: projection visibility (history, live `session.message`, pending inputs hide `tool_handoff`; plugin event and assistant reply stay visible); keyed retry refusal for `plugin` and `tool_handoff`. Both fail on `main` production code and pass with this change.
- Updated tests: plugin-reload and GitHub publish handoff tests assert the enqueue source `"tool_handoff"` with the formatted result text; the reload owner-authority matrix (owner, revoked, cancelled, replaced, system, non-owner, reload failure) runs through real reply dispatch and asserts `InputProvenance.sourceTool: "tool_handoff"`.
- `pnpm test` on `chat-display-projection.visibility`, `plugins-reload-handoff`, `github-publish-tool.handoff`, `session-event-handoff`: all pass (26 + 23 + 23 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: pass. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on touched files: clean.

title: fix: pasted chat images keep the wrong aspect ratio until remount
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pasted chat images keep a padded 3:2 frame until the conversation is remounted, even after their actual dimensions are available.

## User Impact

Single-image previews immediately use the image's aspect ratio and retain it after returning from Settings or reloading. Very wide and tall previews remain bounded without distortion, and their file actions remain reachable. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mounted frame deliberately froze its initial dimensions. It now derives geometry from the existing image presentation owner, using decoded dimensions only when durable upload dimensions are absent. The frame has one dedicated Solid component; no new cache or state owner is introduced. The obsolete untrack allowance and minimum-height letterboxing are removed.

The simplification pass retained the existing resource owner and moved its frame rather than introducing a parallel renderer. Production changes add 47 net lines for reactive geometry and reachable extreme-ratio actions; regression tests add 125 net lines.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the native clipboard paste/send problem against an isolated real Gateway: the 1200 × 563 image remained in a 3:2 frame before the fix.
- Replayed native ClipboardItem paste → send → upload receipt → Settings/back → reload. The patched surface stayed 400 × 187.65625 pixels at every stage. Only model inference used a synthetic loopback provider; clipboard, Gateway, media materialization, history, and browser rendering were real.
- 30 Chromium image-geometry cases, 55 image consumer tests, and 6 browser/Gateway end-to-end cases passed. UI build, TypeScript, targeted lint/format, stylesheet lint, and controller guards passed.
- Independent Codex P0–P2 review: no actionable findings. Its review covered the supplied patch, not executed tests; the live evidence above is from the implementation session.
- Previous-head CI run [40419236001](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40419236001) completed with one inherited failure: `Gateway status with native account identity > keeps shared chat usable without polling operator-only surfaces` expected no operator-only requests but received `board.get` at `gateway-status.e2e.test.ts:63`.
