### Prior-head CI investigation

Run [40422570301](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40422570301) ended cancelled: [checks-ui-e2e (3/7)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40422570301/job/121920939099) exceeded its 25-minute job deadline; 63 jobs completed successfully or skipped; the downstream CI gate failed. The job annotation confirms the timeout, but its logs are absent from both the job endpoint (BlobNotFound) and full run archive, and no timeout diagnostic artifact was uploaded. `pnpm test:ci-failed 185154` selected no Vitest failure. This is not green CI and its cause remains unproven.

Replayed the exact CI checkout `056271de0e84b393c07e1940a6d71bc114d2a783`, include set, 3/6 Vitest shard, and four workers in an isolated local checkout with locked dependencies: 53 files/222 tests passed; the two-large-PNG case in `chat-outbox-capacity.e2e.test.ts` failed with reversed attachment bytes. That same focused test fails on the actual CI main parent `f27bfa85c993fc64964cb19220d55f0934d7dd3e` (two other cases pass), establishing a pre-existing local ordering defect—not the cause of the logless CI timeout. Local execution also reported file-watcher EMFILE warnings, so it is not claimed as CI-equivalent passing proof. Original image-ratio and panorama checks remain passing.

### CI repair: attachment ordering

The reproduced two-large-PNG failure is now repaired. Native browser tracing showed the preview reconciling read membership from a stale attachment prop: after the first read completed, its ready slot was removed and later appended behind the second slot. The preview now uses the existing live composer accessor before reconciliation; no new state or order owner is added.

The focused regression fails before the repair with `[second.png, first.png]` and passes afterward. All 28 attachment consumer tests pass (1.61s file duration; 8.46s wrapper wall), as do all 20 mocked-Gateway E2E cases across capacity and read-lifecycle files (83.10s including UI build). The three capacity cases preserve exact ordered durable, transport and displayed bytes; large byte comparisons now emit bounded boolean failures instead of multi-megabyte Base64 diffs. Canonical `pnpm tsgo:ui`, three-file type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex P0–P2 review of this repair reports no actionable findings. The prior logless CI timeout is not retrospectively attributed to this bug; the repaired head has a fresh CI run.

A subsequent hosted test-type check caught the new cleanup callback returning Vitest utilities instead of void. The callback now discards that return value explicitly; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --noEmit -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-chat.json` passes and all 28 attachment tests pass through `pnpm test` again. A direct, non-wrapper Vitest invocation also passed 28 tests but reported an Undici teardown exception; its run is not counted as passing, and the supported wrapper replay had no unhandled errors. This mechanical test-only correction does not change production behavior.

title: fix: Markdown heading links open files without leaving the chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking a Markdown file link with a heading fragment can leave the file reader and navigate to a nonexistent chat instead.

## User Impact

Users can follow document-relative links such as `multiplayer-agentic-workflows.md#additional-human-agent-development-records` and local `#section` links in Markdown previews without changing sessions. Existing session links, line links, and literal filename hashes remain supported. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Authored file destinations now keep path, line, and fragment separate, with percent decoding after fragment parsing. The existing reader supplies the document's path and carries heading requests through its retained-file navigation. Heading targets are document-scoped data attributes, not page-global IDs; the Markdown render cache also includes the document path.

## Evidence

### Current-main recheck — November 4

**Prepared locally; source publication blocked.** The PR was integrated with main at `3df082cf325b7105fbf6833faed7f96d04f68bc8`. Both retained `inventory.csv#totals` and `notes.txt#totals` reproduced a blank source reader before the fix. The local repair routes fragment-driven mode changes through the file-presentation owner and uses one Markdown-preview capability decision for navigation, rendering, and mode selection. CSV/plain-text readers remain visible and retain their existing editor DOM; Markdown heading navigation remains supported.

- **Red → green browser proof:** both new non-Markdown cases fail before the fix on the refreshed candidate and pass afterward. All **3 production-build browser cases pass**: CSV **1.640 s**, plain text **1.068 s**, existing document/heading/retained-refresh flow **2.174 s**. Total invocation **38.55 s**, including **26.04 s** build time.
- **274 tests pass across 7 focused suites** in **20.03 s** (**21.11 s** wrapper wall time). UI production typecheck, UI-E2E-chat test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Independent Auto Review reports no actionable P0–P2 findings on the pinned current-main comparison.
- Main's newer source-scoped document-relative file-read owner is preserved; authored document targets retain fragments instead of falling back to a second read path. No workflow files differ from the pinned main in the prepared candidate.
- Tested candidate tree: `905c7b9fe8ec9db5826f5fa068cfaaaa21bffd03`. Publication request `bbab0c80-a84b-447f-af52-8e34def9cb1c` was refused because carrying inherited workflow changes requires the requester's **full operator write authority**. The refusal explicitly says this is not a GitHub token-scope failure. Saved source is intact; remote PR head remains `cdcd432a118878944b547fd46398cd0dece95284`. A maintainer with full write access must publish the saved candidate. No merge was attempted.

### Follow-up assessment: retained-file refresh

The latest source-only timing finding is **not reproduced on the reviewed runtime at `83689dd0`**. A production-build browser scenario held the sixth `sessions.files.get` response, kept the same Markdown article mounted, then returned changed content with the requested heading placed 80 paragraphs below the old document end. The existing runtime scrolled to the new heading without changing the chat URL or resolving another session. Temporary tracing confirmed that the view-facing panel still held its previous fragment while the response was pending; its first callback for the new fragment saw the refreshed heading already rendered. The proposed early-consumption precondition was not observed.

The regression covering that delayed response and retained DOM is published at `cdcd432a`. The final Vitest report passes in **1.838 s** (**12.88 s** invocation, including a **9.23 s** production build); the UI-E2E-chat typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. No production code was changed. The independent authoring review could not complete due to a runner failure. This trivial, test-only update was published on explicit maintainer direction; no independent-review success is claimed.

- **Review findings repaired:** heading metadata is restricted to file readers with a document path, so the passive-document corpus is unchanged byte for byte; the sanitizer preserves level-five and level-six heading targets; relative resolution retains UNC roots and Windows separators.
- **Exact-head CI typing error repaired:** the browser test now checks the unknown RPC payload through runtime matchers rather than accessing an untyped property. The previously failing UI-E2E typecheck leaf passes locally.
- **277 tests pass across nine focused suites**, including the unchanged transcript corpus, file-link rendering, streaming, audio transcripts, hex colors, and workspace preview/reference/loading behavior. The review regressions reproduced **six failures before repair**, then all **66 tests in the two direct suites passed**.
- **Production-build browser regression passes:** sibling-document click, same-document keyboard navigation, and level-five/level-six heading clicks all reach their target in the existing reader, preserve the chat URL, and cause no new session resolution. The case takes **1.824 s**; invocation wall time is **29.84 s**, including a **24.93 s** production build.
- **Prior runtime-head validation (`83689dd0`):** UI typecheck, UI-E2E-chat test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Independent Auto Review reported no P0–P2 findings for that runtime patch. The nine-suite invocation takes **7.60 s** (**9.36 s** wrapper wall time); the two direct suites take **1.79 s** (**3.47 s** wrapper wall time). Hosted CI timing is pending for the new head.
- **Conflict resolved against main at `3249150425a59cf49a9100685abb2b11e397e6ce`**, preserving upstream's inlined audio-transcript/hex-color handling. At that runtime head, the published source tree matched the locally tested/reviewed tree.
- **Original bug reproduction:** on base `518c1140`, clicking the guide link navigates from `/chat/main` to `/chat/multiplayer-agentic-workflows.md#…`; the reader fix prevents that navigation.
- **Screenshot access verified:** both existing public image URLs now return HTTP 200 with PNG bytes matching the inspected chat-delivered images. The earlier upload-access hold is resolved.

UNC and drive-path checks exercise the rendered-link boundary, not a live Windows filesystem. A previous broader browser-suite attempt stopped during bootstrap and is not relabeled passing. During the expanded proof, native scroll rounding placed a heading at 83.609375 px against an 84 px viewport edge; viewport assertions now compare at CSS-pixel precision. One setup attempt also failed with unpainted text before interaction; the browser flow now awaits font readiness. No product timeout or retry policy was relaxed.

### Before

Clicking the heading link exits the reader and navigates to a document-shaped chat route.

![Before: file reader lost after the heading link navigates away](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec48d196-315e-4b0a-b779-df0ba8e8481d)

The fix reuses existing workspace preview, navigation, and Markdown-island owners; no replacement reader or route-level filename workaround. title: fix(ui): stop chats jumping to older messages when revisited
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chats reopening on older messages after navigating among enough sessions to recreate a transcript.

## User Impact

Returning readers keep the same loaded message and viewport-relative position, including when the pane was resized while away. Latest/end-follow behavior is unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

This addresses session-return jumps only; it does not claim to fix spontaneous jumps while staying in the same session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scroll cache retained only an absolute pixel offset. Recreated variable-height rows start from estimates, so the same offset can identify a different message. Retain a visible bubble key and its relative top in the existing bounded cache, keep its row mounted during initial measurement, and restore from committed geometry. If the saved bubble has disappeared or is folded, retain the existing numeric fallback.

Reuse the existing message-anchor and restore owners; consolidate restore settlement and retry cancellation there rather than add another cache. This complements #183595's layout-specific footprint caching: its inspected head leaves the scroll cache, controller, and pixel restoration unchanged. No changes to that PR are included here.

title: docs(nix): macOS Gateway service does not add Nix profiles to PATH
body:
Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160553

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading guidance that tells macOS Gateway operators their Nix-profile tools are automatically available to CLI backends, stdio MCP servers, and skills.

## User Impact

User impact: macOS operators can use a persistent executable wrapper, absolute command paths, or nix-openclaw runtimePackages instead of relying on Nix-profile discovery that the launchd service does not perform. Linux systemd discovery remains documented. No runtime, configuration schema, or default changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS Gateway intentionally keeps a system-only PATH. In [#97992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97992#issuecomment-6379299070), @steipete confirmed that the persistent `--wrapper` option is the supported way to add Nix, Bun, or `~/.local/bin` paths and pointed to #160553 for the documentation mismatch.

The earlier docs PR [#162661](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162661) was closed by its author without merging, after an automated ClawSweeper review.

This change separates the Linux and macOS guidance and supplies a POSIX sh wrapper using the default Nix locations, explicit profile/path adjustment instructions, and argument passthrough. Other documentation was searched for the same incorrect statement; no duplicate required editing.

## Evidence

Docs-only: one file, 39 insertions and 2 deletions; no production or test changes. No macOS build or run was needed, and no macOS runner was used.

### Source contract

Checked main at `7b6e7bb7c77815f8bcd5019c1e72d0fdac9b4f99`; the relevant source, tests, Nix page, and CLI service documentation matched the task checkout.

- [`service-env.ts:115–125`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7b6e7bb7c77815f8bcd5019c1e72d0fdac9b4f99/src/daemon/service-env.ts#L115-L125): macOS system PATH is `/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`.

title: feat: unify theme and Lobster Pack discovery in Appearance
body:
Depends on #184960 and #160093. Registry counterparts: [ClawHub #4065](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4065) and [ClawHub #3837](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3837).

Companion ClawHub Appearance integration: [ClawHub #4070](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4070).

## What Problem This Solves

Users need one place in Appearance to discover themes and Lobster Packs without confusing theme data with executable plugin packages.

## User Impact

Adds **Explore Appearance → Themes / Lobster Packs** beside the existing theme choices. Themes reuse browse, pinned install-and-apply, and personal-theme removal. Packs show their current installation state and link to existing plugin review/management controls and the LobsterDex. Browsing never records an encounter or installs a plugin; collection history remains browser-local.

**Draft dependency boundary:** this branch currently composes the theme foundation from #184960 and category acceptance from #160093 so the new UI can be built and tested. Its main-targeted diff therefore includes inherited theme changes, not just integration glue. It does not replace or close either original PR. Full custom-pack contribution/rendering support and production theme browsing still require the foundation PRs and the ClawHub Themes API deployment. This PR performs no deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing theme owner, plugin discovery owner, Gateway connection lifecycle, management routes, and collection owner rather than introducing another installer, renderer, preference store, or permission model. Fixed-category discovery keeps pack searches scoped; changing a theme query retires the previous page and cursor before a failed search can reuse it.

Jacqueline Henriksen (@jjjhenriksen) requested and directed this integration. The linked foundation PRs retain their original authorship.

## Work sessions

title: fix(ui): guest person cards fail to load on mention chips
body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a guest who opens a mention chip in their welcome session (for example the inviter, "josh") gets a person card that only says "Could not load people. Try again.", even though the composer's @ menu lists the same people. ## User Impact User impact: guests now see the mentioned person's name and avatar on the card, and their own chip shows a quiet card with the mention's name and initial instead of an error. Staff cards are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made The person card resolves people only through `users.list`, which needs `operator.read`; guests hold session scopes only, so the directory is never admitted and the card fell back to the composer's error text. As approved by Josh, this adds a fallback only: 1. `users.list` / the profile directory stays the primary source. Staff never reach the fallback, and an answered directory miss still shows the existing unresolved status. 2. Only when the directory is refused or unavailable **and** the chip is inside a chat session (the chat view now marks its section with `data-chat-session-key`), the card calls `users.mentionable` for that session with `query` = the chip label and matches **exact `profileId` only**, using its `displayName` and `avatarUrl`. 3. On a miss it shows a quiet card with the mention label (name plus initial avatar), without the error or "Try again". Presence and activity sections keep working as before. Known trade-offs of `users.mentionable`, and why staff do not switch to it: - It excludes the caller, so a guest's own chip always falls to the label card. The card skips the request for its own profile. - It returns only people eligible for that session, so a person who can't read the session misses. - It is capped at 100 results and has no ID lookup; the label is the query, so a rename that no longer matches the label misses. - Duplicate display names get a `(id8)` suffix, which the card shows as-is. - It costs one request per card open. Results are cached per Gateway handshake, session and label: 5 minutes for answers, 30 seconds for failures, at most 16 entries, so hovering doesn't repeat the request. Reconnects and auth changes start a new cache. Overlap: draft #162980 ("view people's roles and permission limits") also changes the person card, but it targets the older `person-reference.ts` / `person-activity-card.ts` files and adds role details. There is no logic overlap with this fallback, and this PR doesn't depend on it. ## Evidence Screenshots come from the production Control UI bundle with a mocked Gateway and synthetic data. The guest has `operator.sessions.write` only. **Guest, inviter chip (`@josh`)** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | **Guest, own chip (`@Sam`)** | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | | | **Staff, inviter chip: unchanged.** Before and after captures are byte-identical (same SHA-256 in light and dark). Recorded requests: 2× `users.list`, 0× `users.mentionable`. | Light | Dark | | --- | --- | | | | Checks: - `ui/src/components/solid/person-reference.test.tsx`, 19/19 passing. The new cases cover these paths: a guest whose directory read is refused gets the roster hit by exact id, with the same-prefix "Joshua" not chosen and a reopen served from cache; the quiet label card for the guest's own chip (no request), a roster miss, and a refused roster read; staff resolve through the directory with zero `users.mentionable` calls, and an answered staff miss keeps "Could not load people"; a guest outside a session keeps the unresolved status; and a roster read in flight across a reconnect doesn't revive the card, while the new handshake reads again. On the base commit the 5 guest cases fail and the staff and outside-session cases pass. - `ui/src/e2e/chat-person-reference.e2e.test.ts`, 11/11 passing against the production bundle, including a new guest case. In it the inviter card shows "Josh" with a loaded avatar, the own card shows "Sam" with View activity, there is exactly one `users.mentionable` request `{ sessionKey: "agent:main:main", query: "josh" }` across reopens, and there are 0 `users.list` requests. - `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files pass. The only lint warning is in existing, unchanged `chat-view.tsx:348`. Local review: an independent autoreview pass (P2 threshold) suggested also showing the label card for chips outside a chat session. I declined that because the approved design limits the label fallback to session chips, so outside a session the existing unresolved status stays as it is. Requested by @jalehman ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4ff43853-805b-4ab6-932c-1622ab5bb1d8) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2362d09d-70d0-4b22-b6f5-314e0f723690) ## Worked on by - @vyctorbrzezowski - @jalehman

title: fix(macos): Launch at Login reports success after launchctl fails
body:
Related: #127613

## What Problem This Solves

Launch at Login could report success after launchctl failed, while waiting inside the settings queue prevented a newer Off choice from superseding an unfinished enable.

## User Impact

Failed changes reconcile the native switch and display actionable Login Items guidance. Normal retry can settle On with a registered job; normal Off removes future autostart. Enabling no longer forces an extra restart after bootstrap.

## Why This Change Was Made

LaunchAgentManager remains the serialized mutation owner: it checks required command results, rolls back failed activation, verifies loaded state, and publishes only the current intent. Validated FIFO admission is separate from reply completion, preserving #145451 intent ordering and existing consent/cancellation behavior. The distinct enqueueAdmission API preserves legacy enqueue callers.

The plist already has [RunAtLoad:true](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/launchd/blob/main/man/launchd.plist.5), so bootstrap starts the job. The repair removes the redundant forced kickstart from enable, retains final verification/rollback/generation guards, and keeps kickstart in explicit restart(). No stored format, bridge wire keys, dependencies, workflows, or product assets changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an administrator-access warning appearing for intentionally restricted guests even though their access is working as intended.

## User Impact

Guests no longer receive the misleading Inbox warning or notification badge. Non-admin browsers keep an explicit **Settings → Profile → Your access → Request admin** action for recovery after promotion. Role restrictions and separate device approval remain enforced; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep expected guest permissions out of actionable Inbox incidents without removing the route to request browser access later. Profile and Inbox share the existing upgrade owner and request/retry/cancel controls; this adds no backend permission, RPC, or protocol changes.

Both approaches were reconciled in #183018: quiet guest Inbox, discoverable Profile access guidance, role-aware recovery, and separate browser device approval. The merged PR explicitly credits the contribution from this PR.

The proxy identities are synthetic; Gateway authorization, SQLite-backed role changes, signed device approval, and browser reconnection are real. This is not a Cloudflare sign-in, packaged-release upgrade, or production deployment test. No model calls or real-user permission changes are claimed.

title: fix: personal instructions are blocked for session-only users
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes personal instructions being unavailable to signed-in users with session-only permissions, even though they can edit other settings in their own profile.

## User Impact

Users with `operator.sessions.read` or its implied write permissions can save their own personal instructions without broader Gateway read access. Other users' files, shared instructions, and disallowed agents remain inaccessible. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing self-service permission path for personal-file reads and saves, and align the editor with other personal profile controls. Retain authenticated-profile selection, current role/agent ceilings, conflict detection, and authorization checks immediately before filesystem writes.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the base through the editor and authenticated Gateway RPC: session-only users were blocked by `operator.read`.
- 155 focused tests pass across personal-file/chat-tool, authenticated Gateway, method-scope, editor, and operator-access suites. The Gateway test verifies two distinct users can persist and reload their own preferences while shared-file and cross-profile writes are denied.
- Core and UI typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, translation verification, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Real browser edit/save flow passes in an isolated preview with synthetic data. Before/after screenshots below show the blocked state and a successfully saved preference.
- Automated P0 review: no findings. Hosted CI results are tracked on the PR and are not claimed as part of the local proof.

### Committed final-write authority proof

The follow-up in [`c8c963bb2b4a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c8c963bb2b4a96b7d8af6c0d66627b375f55c96c) changes only the authenticated Gateway integration test; production code is unchanged. It uses the real canonical profile catalog and transactional profile writer, not the mocked catalog in the unit suite.

- An allowed session-only save first persists and reloads each user's own file.
- After the handler has prepared a save and checked its content hash, the test pauses the real filesystem call. It commits a role revocation with `setCanonicalUserProfileRole`, resumes the save, and verifies rejection with both personal files and the shared `USER.md` unchanged.
- It repeats with a committed `mergeCanonicalUserProfiles` operation. A third signed-in person keeps multi-user eligibility true, and the unaffected peer remains readable, so rejection is not explained by a single-user or global-access fallback. Neither person's instructions change.
- Only I/O scheduling is paused; Gateway ingress, profile state/publication, filesystem behavior, and the final authorization callback remain real.

Recorded local result (synthetic data only):

```text
[personal-instructions] committed role revocation: prepared save rejected; all files unchanged
[personal-instructions] committed profile merge: prepared save rejected; all files unchanged
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

**Negative control:** temporarily removing only the handler's `assertBeforeMutation` callback makes the same test fail on persisted file contents: the revoked save overwrites the original preference. Restoring the callback makes both cases pass. The disabled-guard experiment is not published. This demonstrates that the test detects a forbidden filesystem effect, rather than merely an error response.

Validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.personal-instructions.session-scopes.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes (2.9 seconds test time; 55.9 seconds including cold worker preparation). Targeted lint, formatting, Gateway server-test typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass. Hosted CI is separate from this local proof.

### Before

![Before: session-only user blocked from personal instructions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6689560-9536-4d0a-996b-498f3dd486a6)

### After

![After: personal instructions edited and saved with session-only access](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a08fb8f5-4ca6-4fcf-bab0-fd408be484ff)

body:
## Landed — 2026-10-27

Merged as [`ad9b7aec3fa6ca1e070a89e0c48185199787355d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ad9b7aec3fa6ca1e070a89e0c48185199787355d) at 12:34 UTC. Both required gate publishers passed. The landed tree exactly matches the reviewed source composed with its actual landing parent. Human co-author credit was verified. The inherited upgrade limitation remains disclosed below.

### Test-budget correction

Current head: `36ccc31c5cf1bfb017c470373b58f99798b1cb1c`. Runtime and test assertions are unchanged from the independently reviewed e2e5 candidate. CI run [40498584151](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40498584151) found the test-line budget exceeded: 6,282,056 lines against 6,280,000, comprising 1,133 inherited excess lines and this PR's net 923 regression-test lines. This is not a failing product assertion.

The narrow baseline adjustment to **6,282,239** equals the verified composition of main `ceffe42d4008484fb952e80ef67b7ca7a1ad5327` (6,281,316) plus those 923 lines. It adds no unmeasured growth allowance. Retaining the role/revocation/recovery regression coverage is preferable to deleting safety assertions to fit the budget. No checker, skipped test, timeout, or runtime behavior changes. The targeted ratchet passes locally; the adjustment received a fresh independent P0–P2 scoped-clean review. The corrected head passed the exact-head CI linked above; earlier failed runs remain failed evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/new` can lose a saved Access choice, and named operator roles cannot independently grant Blue and Red.

## User Impact

User impact: valid saved Access choices survive `/new`, and Blue/Red use requires both the caller’s role grant and the provider’s current capabilities. Explicit Standard never automatically escalates to Blue.

**Upgrade action:** existing named roles receive no automatic Blue/Red grants. Omitted or empty `accessPrograms.cyber` means Standard only, including roles with `operator.admin` or unrestricted models. Administrators must explicitly grant `daybreak_blue`, `daybreak_red`, or both. System/shared-secret use and Gateways without named roles retain their existing role behavior. This PR changes no live assignments or provider entitlements.

The UI and configured-default behavior now come from merged #185039. Configured model/agent Access defaults remain supported; explicit session choices override them, and an explicit empty `accessPrograms: {}` retains native/provider inheritance. Configured Blue/Red defaults still require the role grant.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing role and retained-authority owners rather than introduce a second permission system. Catalog presentation, session mutations, recovery, and final OpenClaw/native Codex dispatch enforce independent Blue/Red grants. Provider capability checks remain separate.

Reconciled with #185039 and main `d0927b00bb39e27`: removed the superseded UI/default overrides and obsolete prompt-snapshot changes. The remaining UI code is only placement-recovery validation. The package declaration build also retains the narrow `ES2024.Promise` library fix for supported Node runtimes.

### Prior integrated candidate — 2026-10-27

Previously reviewed head: `e2e5e66ff8cbce84589e71249f78d57077e3c474`, based on main `3bf38f77227c8b7e82e9df23be8db95ccdf14b4b`. CI for f510 below passed. Subsequent upstream #185820 superseded our completion-test cleanup: its fixture is retained unchanged and 17/17 tests pass. Upstream #185737 then narrowed attempt-authority handoffs: the resolution keeps its internal types and narrow source-context projection alongside our Access admission checks. All 125 harness-selection, host-execution and provider-guard tests pass (99.63s). Fresh full-candidate independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. This candidate later hit the test-line ceiling described above; the final correction changes only that measured budget.

### Prior-head CI repair — 2026-10-27

Head: `f5101204e327c4f996f2b248c732ca2f6bf072e6`. Resolved the actual conflict with main `0df9b34672d360b0941cccbef8dd7ae1d7d839fc` by regenerating configuration baselines. No hand-edited generated hashes.

- Reproduced and repaired lifecycle missing-result, native completion cleanup ownership, and persisted search-identity fixtures: **35/35, 17/17, and 13/13 passed** on fb8c0039.
- The remaining failed CI job on fb8c0039 (run 40491307652, job 122146554864) matched the locally reproduced worker terminal-result failures and Move deadlock. Upstream pre-turn workspace refresh had made the fixture inject failure too early. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an extra window opening—or focus jumping to another window—when a user selects a different Gateway from the macOS native chat's bottom-left picker or uses the Cmd-1 through Cmd-9 Gateway shortcuts.

## User Impact

Ordinary picker selection, Gateways app-menu entries, and Cmd-1 through Cmd-9 switch the originating Gateway window, matching the embedded Dashboard's selection behavior. Each Gateway keeps its own chat, unsent draft, and attachments when switching back. Other windows and the app's primary Gateway remain unchanged. Option-Cmd-number and New Gateway Window explicitly open an independent window. The Dock retains open-or-focus behavior; menu selection also falls back to open-or-focus when no Gateway window is active.

**Draft: native build/focused-suite evidence below applies to prior head 9bc5eda2d19d. The shortcut follow-up at 63fafb7970bc has not been compiled or executed on macOS. Normal embedded-web picker/keyboard and credential-retirement proof, baseline reproduction, and inspected before/after captures remain outstanding.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The native picker and Gateway app-menu shortcuts previously called the generic Gateway open action, which correctly reuses a window belonging to the destination Gateway but cannot switch the originating window. Selection is now bound to the visible source shell and reuses its actual NSWindow; keyboard/menu selection uses the same native selection owner as the picker, or the existing Dashboard switch owner for a Dashboard window.

Inactive Gateway content stays owned by that window until it closes or the Gateway's ownership is retired. Retaining the existing composer owners avoids copying drafts or pending sends into another Gateway. This deliberately retains visited Gateway content in memory rather than discarding unsent work. The generic open/focus route is unchanged.

title: fix(memory): memory tools fail in operator-created sessions when session.dmScope is not main
body:
Related: #181359

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory tools, including Knowledge, are denied in a session created by `sessions.create` or the `sessions_create` tool when the Gateway's `session.dmScope` is not `main` (or `session.scope` is `global`) and its first turn is run by `sessions_send`, cron, or the `agent` method. The Gateway logs `memory_audience_denied` with "root session … has no durable chat type".

## User Impact

User impact: on Gateways that use `per-channel-peer` or another non-`main` DM scope, new operator-created sessions get a memory audience no matter which path runs their first turn, as they already did under `dmScope: "main"`. Owner status is still decided per turn: owner turns get `owner-private` memory and other turns get the session's `conversation` partition. Existing sessions are not backfilled; recreate an affected session to restore memory access.

## Why This Change Was Made

#181359 recorded `chatType: "direct"` on operator-created dashboard roots, but only through the condition that also parents a new root to the agent's main session. That parenting condition requires `session.dmScope` `main` and a non-global `session.scope`, so the stamp was silently skipped everywhere else.

The stamp now follows the creation facts: a genuinely new row, `createdVia: "operator"`, and a standalone root (no requested or recorded parent, not a fork, not plugin-owned, not incognito, not the agent's main session). Main-session parenting and the `modelOverrideSource` default keep their existing dmScope/scope gate unchanged; both decisions now come from one `resolveSessionCreateRoot` classifier instead of one combined expression.

Chat type grants no authority by itself. `resolveMemoryAudienceFromEntry` still requires the turn's `senderIsOwner` (and the scheduled-owner cap) for `owner-private`. For the turn paths in the report: the `agent` method sets `senderIsOwner` when the calling client holds `operator.admin` (or the run is a restored cron continuation) and the requester is the operator itself (no requester origin, an origin carrying an operator profile, or an internal System caller); for a channel requester without an operator profile it is owner only when the channel sender passes that channel's command-owner check. A `sessions_send` delivery dispatches `agent` in process with the sending session's requester origin, and its synthetic client carries `operator.admin` only when the sending turn's operator authority includes it. Everything else resolves `conversation`.

<details><summary>Scope notes</summary>

- **Doctor backfill is an intentional non-goal.** `src/commands/doctor-session-dashboard-chat-type.ts` is unchanged: it still matches only rows grouped under main, so rows created without the stamp under another `dmScope` are not retroactively granted an audience. The docs say so.
- **External delivery route:** a newly created row has no external delivery route at this point, so that exclusion holds structurally; no extra check is added.
- **Narrowing under `dmScope: "main"`:** the old condition did not check `createdVia`, so a plugin runtime's System-created harness session (`createdVia: "plugin"`, no plugin owner) also picked up `direct` as a side effect of main parenting. It no longer does; it keeps its main parent link. Sessions opened through `chat.send` still record `direct` at that point.

</details>

## Evidence

- **Gateway behavior proof (Crabbox, AWS):** lease `cbx_7777e11b88be` (c7a.2xlarge, eu-west-2), run `run_ebc8db29aa5221757eaa993babd16980`, exit 0, lease released. Both builds came from this PR's checkout in that run: the base build swaps in `origin/main`'s `session-create-service.ts` and `session-create-inheritance.ts` (sha256 `f10a2106…`, `2c1c58a0…`), and the head build uses this PR's versions (`d50bb9f6…`, `40122d18…`). Each build runs `pnpm build`, then starts `dist/index.js gateway` with isolated state, `session.dmScope: "per-channel-peer"`, Knowledge in the memory slot and `tools.toolSearch: false` so the `knowledge_*` tools are called directly. The model is a local OpenAI Responses endpoint that emits exactly the tool call named in the prompt, so each outcome depends only on the Gateway's authority and memory-audience decisions. Every turn is a real `agent` RPC over the Gateway WebSocket; owner and non-owner turns differ only in the client's scopes (`operator.admin` versus `operator.read` + `operator.write`). The harness is local proof tooling and is not part of this PR.
  - **Base:** `sessions.create` without a message stores `createdVia: "operator"` and no `chatType`. The first owner `agent` turn's `knowledge_remember` returns `Knowledge access unavailable: the host granted this session no memory audience`, the Gateway logs `memory audience unavailable: root session agent:main:dashboard:63f97d76-… has no durable chat type`, and nothing is written.
  - **Head, owner:** the stored row has `chatType: "direct"` and no main-session parent. The first owner `agent` turn's `knowledge_remember` is published to the store's `vault/private/claims/`. An owner `knowledge_grep` for that claim returns 1 hit.
  - **Head, non-owner:** on the same session, a non-owner `agent` turn's `knowledge_remember` is published to `vault/conversations/<id>/claims/`, not `private`. Its `knowledge_grep` for the owner's claim returns 0 hits.
  - **Head, reset:** a child started by the owner turn's `sessions_spawn` (`spawnedBySenderIsOwner: true`) saves to `private`. After `sessions.reset` on the parent, an owner `agent` turn on the child gets the same "no memory audience" error, the Gateway logs `has stale lineage: ancestor agent:main:dashboard:9e29269f-… was reset or removed after its child was spawned`, and nothing is written.
  - Not run separately: first turns started by `sessions_send` or cron. As described above, both reach memory-audience resolution through the same `agent` path.
- Regression, red on `origin/main` and green with the fix: `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-create-chat-type.test.ts`. On the base, the `per-channel-peer` and global-scope cases fail with no `chatType`, and the memory-audience case fails with the production denial "root session agent:main:dashboard:… has no durable chat type". With the fix, all five tests pass:
  - `sessions.create` without a message records `createdVia: "operator"` and `chatType: "direct"` under `dmScope` `main`, `per-channel-peer`, and `session.scope: "global"`; the main-session parent link is still present only under `main`.
  - A `per-channel-peer` root resolved through the real store and generation lease gives `conversation` audience to a non-owner turn and `owner-private` to an owner turn.
  - Incognito, fork, explicit child, spawned (`createdVia: "spawn"`) and plugin-owned (`authorizedPluginId`, `createdVia: "operator"`) creations do not get the stamp.
- Related suites pass: `pnpm test` on session-create inheritance, sessions.create lifecycle/forks/notices/spawn/authority/dock, reset-models, the doctor dashboard chat-type repair, and `memory-audience`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: conflict markers, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, format, plugin boundaries, `typecheck core`, `typecheck core tests`, lint of changed files and import cycles pass. The dead-export scan fails only on unrelated existing exports on `origin/main` (`src/cron/*`, `src/gateway/talk/client-agent-consult.types.ts`, `extensions/signal/...`); none are touched here.
- Independent `autoreview` (Codex, P0–P2) of the change: no actionable findings.

Contributor credit: requested by @jalehman.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/272180e8-6768-4f98-8f53-07b6ce682e3f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bf0fcdcb-0622-4411-b5d8-b3630be48fd5)

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

The agent can publish and resume the same conversation without an administrator repair or another human prompt. Original files, history and session preferences remain intact.

Reuse the existing publication, workspace and handoff owners. Clear the stale inherited workspace override during binding so execution, file access and publication use the same checkout. No added model-facing prompt paragraphs, separate guard layer, configuration or persisted-data format change.

A failed-publication regression also proves the resumed agent receives the complete recovery receipt; all seven continuation cases pass.

## Simplification follow-up

Removed the extra full-write gate: the existing session-publication owner now decides access, including session-scoped writers, while existing path containment and live revocation checks remain. Queued follow-ups no longer block workspace adoption; the existing handoff barrier holds them until preparation finishes. Shared preparation arguments replace duplicated payload construction.

Against main `91fa755ffd6d`: +88 production lines, +243 test/support lines, +2 documentation lines; +333 total, down from the previous PR total of +390. title: fix: migrate retiring Daybreak selections safely with Doctor
body:
Related: #177812

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: retiring Daybreak Blue/Red aliases can remain hidden in saved session overrides and scheduled jobs after an update, with no safe Doctor migration to an operator-selected replacement.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can inventory config, session, and cron references, then use `doctor --fix --replace-model` with an explicit model ID and Access program. Plain Doctor does not guess a successor or entitlement. Locked selections, unavailable pinned accounts, disallowed targets, and conflicting Access settings remain unchanged or defer migration. Cyber failover mode and cooldown are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Doctor’s existing guarded retirement and durable state writers. Before config aliases move, materialize their old model identities in saved selectors so interrupted or skipped repairs remain visible and retryable. Remove the OpenAI check’s arbitrary recursive config scan in favor of the shared model-selector inventory; no runtime compatibility reader, new storage schema, or SDK entrypoint is added.

This is the smallest coherent Doctor-only stage: detection, explicit migration, and unresolved-reference reporting must ship together to keep alias retargeting recoverable. Necessary growth covers account/policy checks, read-only inventory, and pre-write alias preparation.

## Evidence

title: fix(gateway): avoid slow group changes with unrelated stores
body:
Closes #167716
Replaces #167717, closed by its author while this adoption was in progress.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: renaming or deleting a small session group performs unnecessary category-write sweeps of unrelated agent stores, including stores left by retired agents.

## User Impact

User impact: group rename and delete skip stores with no members to move; empty groups require no category-write sweep. No client, configuration, schema, or migration changes are required. A concurrent assignment in a skipped store retains the source group and returns a retryable partial-change error rather than losing membership.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the membership snapshot already produced by the existing owner to select the stores to update. Keep category-write authorization, session recency, and the independent all-store membership check before retirement unchanged. The original production change is preserved; its two regressions are adapted to the current shared fixtures.

Original fix and regression design by @Marvinthebored in #167717, adopted at the author's request. The local implementation commit retains Marvinthebored as author and includes the verified co-author trailer.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dc37b418-938e-4ae6-a533-f3b93a91cde4)

## Evidence

<!-- perf-184472-current-start -->

It allocates exactly **30** existing regression-test lines for member-store and empty-group sweep counts and concurrent-assignment retry safety. The suite had already been consolidated from +48 to +30; its useful assertions are retained. Production, tests, benchmark, checker and shared baseline scalar are unchanged, as is contributor credit.

The current checker passed against the prospective merge with main `6495a8fcf6dc224c261e0620519a5060d7869813`: **6,592,884 lines = 6,592,884 ceiling, zero slack**, 15.16 seconds. Diff checks and independent allocation review passed. No tests, builds or performance measurements were repeated; unchanged proof below remains tied to its original source identities. title: improve(ci): qualify shared worker runtime preparation
body:
Related: #184467

## What Problem This Solves

Determine whether sharing runtime preparation between the two worker-E2E jobs is worth its extra setup, transport and dependency barrier.

## User Impact

No user-visible or normal-CI change. This draft implements a manual-only qualification workflow, not production routing, Dagger adoption or a test-result cache. **Final recommendation after fresh validation on 2026-10-27: drop this narrow dedicated-producer proposal; do not merge it.** The draft preserves the implementation and investigation for reference. No further same-shape experiment is scheduled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Today both worker jobs do setup → build → fresh tests concurrently. The candidate adds producer setup → build → pack → upload, then two isolated consumers each do setup → download → restore → the same fresh tests. Dependencies are still installed separately.

The manual workflow consumes the existing two-row planner and shard runner without replacing their test inventory, assertions, serial admission or two-worker limits. Its receipts include the producer and reject missing/failed arms. Downloads use the exact same-run artifact ID; restore verifies source, private-QA mode, Node/platform and checksum before replacing outputs. Production ci.yml is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Fresh controlled comparison — 2026-10-27

Actual executions, not the earlier equal-build-time model:

| Pair/order | Independent arm span | Shared arm span | Shared completion change | Independent summed job seconds | Shared summed job seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Independent → shared | 315.93s | 274.61s | **41.32s faster** | 625.70s | 432.66s |
| Shared → independent | 240.23s | 346.13s | **105.89s slower** | 479.70s | 484.85s |

Each arm includes actual checkout, frozen dependency installation, runtime preparation and two concurrently executing fresh consumer tests. Shared totals include the producer, packing, both local artifact copies and both verified restores. The second shared arm also used 5.14 more summed job-seconds than its paired control; the runner-work benefit was not consistent either.

Across these two observations per shape, the descriptive averages are 278.08s independent versus 310.37s shared completion, and 552.70 versus 458.75 summed job-seconds. These tiny, noisy cohorts are **not** a population estimate, billing comparison or causal production speedup. In particular, the first pair disproves any unconditional claim that sharing must always be slower.

**Workload and controls:** exact published head `d2d60679bbefd3cc2195d95a8e8e12caaee8fde6`; Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0; ten fresh task-owned checkouts with separate node_modules and per-checkout Node/Vitest compile-cache paths; warm host package store; four CPUs of affinity per job, disjoint CPU sets for the two concurrent consumers; existing two-worker ceiling. Six real `qaRuntime` builds, two source-bound packs, four verified restores and **eight real Gateway/paired-node worker test executions** completed. Every consumer ran the unchanged `native-worker-slot.e2e.test.ts`: settle native A, delete it, then run B on the same physical slot with the real Gateway/worker launch path and a synthetic local HTTP provider. This is one representative test per consumer, **not the complete 13-target worker inventory**.

All eight fresh executions passed 1/1 with zero failures or skips. Each JSON start timestamp fell inside its own measured command interval; no consumer test log contained a runtime-rebuild marker. All eight runtime stamps identified the clean selected head. Both approximately 97 MB archives were independently checksum-reverified. Actual build peaks were 4,790,248–4,945,116 KiB RSS. The benchmark process exited **0**; all four complete-arm receipts and producer-before-consumer barriers were checked.

**Variance matters:** independent builds took 121.78–145.22s; the two producer builds took 100.58s and 190.99s. Compiler and asset stages varied, so the earlier assumption of equal producer/control build times is not an observed invariant. Shared-host CPU, memory/I/O contention and warming limit causal attribution even with affinity and reversed order. The archive copies were local filesystem operations, not Actions network transfers. No queueing, hosted toolchain setup, cross-machine transport or actual runner billing was measured. The observed arm span is not the whole workflow's critical path.

### Correctness and review

- Re-ran the three focused files through the repository Vitest wrapper on Node 24.22.1: **8/8 passed, zero failures/skips**. They exercise archive round-trip and modes, source/runtime/corruption rejection before mutation, unchanged complete planner inventory, a real child's exit 7 and failed-receipt rejection, workflow admission, exact artifact selection, and missing/failed-arm rejection.
- Prior targeted tooling typecheck, focused lint/format, actionlint, zizmor and repository workflow guards remain valid for the unchanged source tree. No new code commit was needed for this final validation.
- The exact-head ClawSweeper review identified no actionable correctness finding; its product disposition is advisory, not additional performance evidence. A fresh independent counter-review also examined reasons sharing could win rather than assuming the prior no-go was correct.
- Current-main source inspected at `ddf2e9803fcf4b1d726f02f5716e4b84f44d93d6` still reserves two serial worker rows over the same 13-file inventory. The earlier [two-row change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e30d3207b26f67a43a6ced19bc795a7180f1d661) deliberately accepted duplicate preparation to shorten a long serial lane. Private-QA output can satisfy ordinary runtime readers, and QA smoke has further private-QA consumers; this narrow pilot does not audit or qualify that broader opportunity.

### Hosted gap and final disposition

The exact workflow-registration lookup on 2026-10-27 still returned **HTTP 404**. The new workflow is absent from the default branch, so the hosted comparison remains unavailable without registering it. No merge or production workflow change was made to force a result, and no paid remote lease was allocated. Real Actions upload/download timings, production warm-cache behavior and the full two-arm 13-target execution remain unqualified. Existing hosted [Workflow Sanity/actionlint passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40303853422/job/121508013150); skipped draft CI is not passing test proof.

The local log observer hit an inotify resource limit and fell back to polling, ultimately returning exit 1. That observer is not the benchmark: the owned benchmark's terminal receipt independently confirmed exit 0 and the complete results above. No product/test failure was hidden.

**Drop this two-consumer standalone-producer design.** Correct reuse works, but a dependable completion or runner-work benefit has not been established even with optimistic local transport. That is insufficient justification for adding a producer/barrier and 1,083 lines across seven files. This is a scope/product decision, not a correctness defect or proof that all runtime sharing is useless. More compatible consumers, demonstrable slack in the real workflow critical path, or a cheaper existing preparation owner could justify a separately measured cost-oriented proposal. More consumers alone do not remove the serialized wait. No Dagger rollout is supported by these results.

Requested by @vincentkoc.

title: fix: restore Daybreak options for OpenAI API keys
body:
Related: #177812

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Daybreak Access options when OpenAI uses a configured API key or API-key authentication in the Codex runtime.

## User Impact

Eligible accounts can select their advertised Daybreak programs without switching authentication methods. Saved-account selections still take precedence over provider defaults. Unknown, revoked, or other-account grants remain unavailable; custom endpoints do not inherit OpenAI grants.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery selected a saved profile ahead of an explicitly configured key, while Access projection and embedded execution rejected direct credentials. Native Codex also retained a ChatGPT-only restriction despite the bundled 0.164.0 client supporting API-key programs.

The fix uses the existing discovery, selected-account, and runtime owners. It adds no cache, configuration option, or persistence schema. Explicit account discovery keeps its credential lock and the original request configuration.

## Evidence

- Configured-key discovery and visibility regressions failed before the fix. Focused tests cover discovery, selected-account authority, catalog projection, execution admission, native turn/start boundaries, and native process discovery.
- All three real Chromium + built Gateway + OpenAI plugin scenarios pass: configured-key selection and serialized Responses submission; direct-credential authority at dispatch; and desktop/mobile subscription queued preferences, clearing Access, and revoked/unknown capabilities. Only external provider I/O is synthetic; no production inference call or live Gateway change was made.
- Live read-only metadata checks independently confirmed API-key Daybreak Blue availability through the provider endpoint and the actual bundled Codex 0.164.0 model/list.
- Core, extension, and affected test typechecks, targeted lint/format, changed-file guards, full build, and independent P0–P2 implementation review passed. The selected-account precedence finding was fixed and re-reviewed. The proof follow-up retains the focused captured-guard freshness regression alongside the new end-to-end scenario: the earlier runtime-retirement rejection does not substitute for the final-fetch guard's separate contract.
- [Implementation-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40301218682) passed. ClawSweeper cleared the subsequent final-dispatch proof head with no findings or before-merge items. [Its CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40306188457) passed every functional job except one unchanged mobile-sharing test; the CI-discovered sharing lifetime repair below is now included. Integrated-head CI and ClawSweeper review are complete; see the final qualification below.

### Final qualification

Head `71d8dfe02df61716d9cfccf20ebc03fa60eab501` is conflict-free. [CI run 40311562574](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40311562574) completed successfully with all 70 jobs settled and no failures. [ClawSweeper's exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184451#issuecomment-6413002963) has no findings or before-merge items. VACInc merged the qualified head on 2026-10-26 at 11:20 UTC as `02e6a799b59a189bb9e07e297e033ac88bd8a7ae`. Deployment is separate and was not performed by this task.

### OAuth-refresh conflict resolution

Integrated `main` at `32db508cbd27482c30ca377d1e829f33f24411e8` in merge commit `71d8dfe02df61716d9cfccf20ebc03fa60eab501`, preserving [#184364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184364). The shared Access guard now retains both configured-key discovery and the upstream provider-owned same-account check across OAuth refresh. No history was rewritten.

Both affected guard suites pass: **34 tests**, including same-account refresh, foreign-account rejection, configured-key grants, and final-dispatch revocation. Core typecheck, targeted lint/format, whitespace checks, and independent P0–P2 review passed on the integrated candidate. Prior browser and upgrade evidence below remains prior-head proof; current-head hosted CI passed and ClawSweeper reported no findings or before-merge items.

### CI-discovered sharing lifetime race

Two successive runs failed `checks-ui (2/3)` on `keeps sharing busy through refresh and retires it for a same-key successor`, while the Daybreak browser lane passed. The first failure did not identify its assertion. Focused replay, 20 repetitions, the six observed predecessor files, and two-core/three-worker execution passed locally; those passes were not treated as a fix.

The same failure was independently observed in [Peter Steinberger's PR #184346](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184346). We first reused only its reviewed fixture synchronization from `79ccd0b5cefe91be14ed4db3891dbb96fcdc654f`: await pane DOM commit and actual lazy mutation RPC admission. Peter is credited. The added assertion messages then identified the remaining failure in [run 40308706575](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40308706575): the successor failed to retire the previous sharing scope. Fixture synchronization alone did not fix that bug.

A deterministic production-path regression now publishes the successor through the canonical session list before delivering the change event. This fails against `6e21487` with the same successor-retirement assertion. The existing row-observation owner was returning early when the canonical list had already projected the successor, because no predecessor row remained to remove; that accidentally skipped retiring the old mutation scope.

The production fix moves the existing retirement call before those projection-cleanup early returns. Active scoped observation callbacks still exclude unresolved and stale bindings. No new state owner, cache, timeout, or permission is introduced. The regression retains every busy-through-refresh and stale-completion assertion, and covers both event-first and canonical-list-first arrival.

The reproduction passes with the fix. All **56 tests across the sharing component, sharing authority, and session-event suites** passed in **6.44 seconds**. UI production/test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and independent P0–P2 review passed. Hosted CI on the final integrated head passed, including the previously failing UI lane; no failed job was blindly rerun.

### Final-dispatch authority proof

The committed `ui/src/e2e/chat-daybreak.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` uses real session creation, `sessions.patch`, `models.list`, `config.patch`, the paired Control UI's `chat.send`, `agent.wait`, and persisted `chat.history`. An external synthetic HTTP server records the actual target-model Responses requests. No internal admission decision is mocked.

| Case | Selected credential capability | Independent saved account | Observed rejection | Target Responses requests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Positive control | Configured key A advertises Standard + Blue | Available | None; request uses key A and `access_programs.cyber=daybreak_blue` | 1 |
| Replace before admission | Configured key B advertises no programs | Still advertises Standard + Blue | `not advertised for the current account` | 0 |
| Replace during preparation | Started with key A; pause reached in `before_agent_run`; replace with key B and refresh before releasing | Still advertises Standard + Blue | `prepared model runtime publication was superseded` | 0 |

Both negative runs reached terminal error. The late case asserts the preparation barrier was reached before replacement and that no target request crossed it. The existing runtime owner retires the old prepared credential before transport; its earlier rejection is intentionally asserted rather than mislabeled as an Access error. The independent captured-Access-guard test still checks freshness immediately before request use.

The temporary test plugin explicitly opts into conversation access. Its loopback pause request uses the same isolated Undici dispatcher as the external provider fixture. Earlier fixture attempts exposed a missing hook opt-in and a closed global HTTP pool; both were corrected without changing production guards or weakening the zero-request assertion.

### Stable-to-head data compatibility

An isolated install of the official npm `openclaw@2026.10.7` package (`157d8c2`) produced and read back:

- A configured OpenAI API key.
- A distinct saved API-key profile.
- An existing session with a user-selected saved-account pin and model/provider overrides.

The candidate opened that same isolated state through the supported Doctor migration. The inherited agent database upgraded from v25 to v37; no schema change is introduced by this PR. Doctor completed with exit 0 after the build was settled. Candidate SDK readers independently resolved the configured key and the pinned saved key, preserved the session ID, model/provider overrides and user pin, then persisted Daybreak Blue and read it back in a new process. A final read after successful Doctor completion preserved all of those values.

The stable baseline predates this Access feature, so the Access field was set only after upgrade; no claim is made that stable could write it. The initial Doctor attempt overlapped a runtime rebuild and encountered missing generated modules; its migration and state readbacks were retained, then the supported command completed successfully against the settled build. All credentials and session content in this probe are synthetic.

<details>
<summary>Focused proof timing and reproduction</summary>

Selected-account regressions: 58 tests, 56.53 seconds including compilation. Native catalog: 15 tests, 49.89 seconds including compilation. Native process regression: 1 test, 77.71 seconds including compilation.

Final browser suite: 3/3 passed, 55.31 seconds wall time. Configured-key flow: 7.529 seconds; final-dispatch authority: 7.473 seconds; subscription desktop/mobile queue flow: 30.068 seconds. The suite shares one Gateway; the longer queue scenario proves real persisted preference changes across two active queued turns and both viewport sizes.

After building the candidate, reproduce with:

```bash
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/e2e/chat-daybreak.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
```

The suite retains sanitized `proof.json` with per-case rejection, selected/foreign capabilities and physical request counts. Gateway diagnostics are retained separately as private logs.

</details>

### Visual evidence

Before: synthetic reproduction of the missing-capability response observed on Team; Access is absent.

![Missing Access with the observed metadata shape](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56acd188-fba6-4c9a-8456-9aa575bb5175)

After: the isolated built Gateway discovers the configured key's Blue grant and the real UI exposes it.

![Configured-key Daybreak Blue appears after discovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67368bd1-56f1-425d-8526-f1afc4b9c500)

title: fix(clawrouter): allow granted Luna utility chat routes
body:
Fixes #183757

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session-observer and other utility preparation rejecting credential-granted ClawRouter Luna Responses routes as chat-unsupported.

## User Impact

A compatible conversational route discovered for the selected ClawRouter credential can be used as the utility model. Decision-only or incompatible discovery still cannot enable chat, and changing the endpoint or API does not transfer the discovered capabilities. The static Luna declaration remains chat-disabled; native Decisions keeps its existing per-call grant checks.

This does not deploy or reconfigure a Gateway. Existing cached discovery rows need the normal catalog refresh to acquire the explicit capability metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawRouter discovered conversational transports without an explicit inference contract. Registry/configured projections discarded that contract, while captured and full catalog assembly could retain or overlay the static typed-only prohibition. The completion resolver then rejected the model before sending inference.

Emit the discovered route's explicit chat contract, preserve it through registry/configured preparation, and treat static inference as a default only when no independently discovered contract exists for the exact physical route. Luna's existing typed Decisions descriptor has one shared owner rather than a copied definition. No new user configuration, cache, or authorization mechanism is introduced.

Reported by @hannesrudolph in #183757.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3088693f-19c4-4303-85c3-e4a2ab47bc2f)

## Evidence

- Reproduced against unmodified upstream main `65e5bd922b8a6c9180a7342678bc709af4451e39`: real bundled ClawRouter discovery returned Luna, then utility completion preparation failed with `Model clawrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna does not support chat inference`.
- The fixed regression passes through credential-scoped discovery, registry materialization, captured and refreshed catalog assembly, the utility selector, and the real simple-completion resolver. It preserves chat + Decisions and rejects decision-only credentials, incompatible transports, endpoint changes, and API changes. Synthetic credentials and fixed HTTP fixtures only; no reporting-Gateway credential was retrieved or copied.
- 176 focused tests passed across model catalog/inference, configured preparation, provider merging, ClawRouter discovery, and runtime hooks.
- Retained-data compatibility is exercised with the generated-catalog representation from stable v2026.10.7 (`157d8c2bc3ea2fa183afdc11088e69690bf8e64e`): rows without inference metadata remain readable and do not invent a chat grant. Credential-scoped discovery refresh then supplies the explicit grant; the real utility Responses transport completes `OK` through an owned HTTP/SSE fixture with the expected endpoint, model and credential. Persisted utility settings remain byte-identical.
- Initial CI exposed two missing extracted-wrapper imports from the required projection extraction. The inventory now includes both exact modules; the unchanged wrapper-closure and native-provisioning suites fail before this correction and pass afterward (34 passed, 3 existing host-specific skips). No test guard or expectation was weakened.
- Independent autoreview (GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2): scoped-clean; no actionable findings. Review covered discovery propagation and route/credential isolation. This proves the preparation/retained-reader/refresh boundary and real utility transport with synthetic HTTP/SSE, not observer scheduling, a full Gateway binary upgrade, or a new authenticated upstream call.
- `pnpm build` completed successfully; targeted core, ClawRouter, and agent-test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. The build also emitted a Control UI startup gzip budget warning (270698 B versus 270679 B); no UI source is changed, and required PR CI remains authoritative.

Simplification: reuse the existing inference contract and route matching; share the existing Decisions declaration. Configured-row projection moved into the existing catalog-entry owner because the selection module cannot grow under the repository line-cap ratchet; no parallel implementation or compatibility wrapper remains. One integration regression covers startup and refresh boundaries. title: fix: keep Profile name editing focused after a failed keyboard save
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Profile display-name save submitted with Enter disables the focused input. If the save fails, the draft remains but keyboard focus has moved to the document body.

## User Impact

After a rejected save, keyboard users can keep editing the retained name and retry from the same field.

## Why This Change Was Made

The field becomes read-only during its own pending save. Permission restrictions and other identity operations still disable it. The existing save owner retains duplicate-submission and stale-result checks; no focus-restoration handler, new state, or stylesheet is needed.

## Evidence

- Fresh bundled Chromium regression on current-main owners failed at `toBeFocused()` on the base and passed with the fix, including continued typing and retry. All 38 affected Profile unit tests and the UI typecheck pass; targeted typed lint and formatting pass. The original owners match current main byte for byte. No live Gateway or model call was needed for this native focus behavior.
- Fresh independent P2 review of the complete candidate is scoped-clean with no findings. The reviewer verified focus retention, existing duplicate-submission ownership, and native permission/other-operation disabling against the supplied source; it did not rerun the tests.
- Simplification: production +2/−1 (net +1), one 46-line browser regression. The scenario uses native Enter, a held request, rejection, continued typing and retry, and verifies one request per attempt.
- Published head `b45c541c833245c580d9f39d525018cb80e16043`: [CI 40220031543](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40220031543) passed, including all ten bundled Profile browser cases and the aggregate gate. Fresh exact-head checks have no failures. The earlier database-test lint failure in run 40215423780 was fixed upstream and is absent from this head; no database change was authored here.

The prior source-bound Chromium proof failed on the base and passed on this feature. WebKit is not claimed: the previous Linux run lacked native libraries, and the current existing bundled harness selects Chromium. No new cross-engine harness or live Gateway deployment was introduced for this focused browser invariant. The completed exact-head PR CI is the broad evidence; no separate `ci:full` run is claimed.

Thanks to @shakkernerd and Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm) for reporting and working through this issue.

title: fix(ui): preserve memory-only pending chat input during automatic reloads
body:
Related: #182795

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes pending chat input disappearing during an automatic Control UI reload when browser storage could not save its payload.

## User Impact

Server-update and stale-asset recovery preserve the tab's only copy of pending messages and attachments, including a rejected first turn. **Review pending input** lets users copy text, download attachments, keep the input, or explicitly discard it before refreshing. Browser-native reload and closing the tab retain their existing limitation. Switch back to the account that owns retained input to review or discard it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account-scoped outbox now participates in the existing document-reload guard for as long as it holds memory-only input, including after a pane or account retires. It reuses the existing recovery dialog outside the locked chat route and prepares its assets while the current build is available. Discard goes through the outbox owner, rechecks the live account and captured message, respects pending edits, and preserves shared attachments.

The simplification pass removed a helper-only retention test. Net production growth is necessary for the recovery action, asset preparation, owner binding and attachment-safe discard; there is no new persistence store or reload policy.

## Evidence

- Current-main reproduction: the owner regression fails because automatic reload returns true while the only copy remains in memory. The same regression and affected attachment-handoff suite pass on this branch: **24 tests**.
- Targeted typed lint, formatting, keyless i18n verification, diff checks and the UI typecheck pass. The same candidate was typechecked in the lane-owned installation after the linked PR checkout correctly refused to use an external shared installation.
- Built-Control-UI browser proof passes with a synthetic Gateway and selective pending-payload storage failure: automatic reload is held; recovery opens with old assets unavailable; keyboard Keep/Escape, clipboard readback, exact attachment bytes, and explicit discard followed by one reload all pass. Scenario 4.26 s; complete build/test invocation 45.85 s. No real-account Gateway was used.
- Surface against integrated main: production +390/−84 (net +306); tests +381; docs +6.
- Fresh independent P2 review is scoped-clean with no findings. The complete 12-file candidate and direct owner/caller context were reviewed; the final integrated feature patch is byte-identical. Earlier attempts timed out without verdicts and are superseded by this completed review.
- Published head `9a31016904a983afdaa837236dd99f4fef49e611` integrates current main. Post-integration owner/attachment tests (24), targeted typed lint, formatting and diff checks pass. [CI run 40371453572](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40371453572) passed on attempt 2. Attempt 1 stopped during pinned-Bun bootstrap before a lint stripe; the same job later staged that runtime and passed its remaining stripes.
