title: fix(talk): voice requests stall before the backing agent starts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Talk can recognize and acknowledge a spoken request without ever starting the backing agent. A provider callback can register the request under a different Gateway scope; execution then misses that reservation and creates a second input blocked behind the original.

Related: #183597, reported and investigated by @bdjben. His retained-state analysis establishes the failure structure in native Control UI calls. @Suiah98 also supplied independent live recovery evidence for the registration-wrapper portion of this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register each consultation under its captured Gateway and carry the exact registered source into the existing session-controller admission path. Reject stale or mismatched sources and consume each consultation's registration once.

Rebased onto main `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0`, resolving the integration conflicts while preserving metadata-write authority, asynchronous PostgreSQL-compatible call validation, current retained-authority APIs, accepted-work cleanup, and terminal-write settlement.

## User Impact

Voice requests reach the selected agent and return their answers instead of remaining at an acknowledgement. No new configuration or migration is required by this PR.

## Evidence

Validated runtime head: `518f63b332a69bf1f71400706d3fdb88569605f5`. Current head `3ad8007b26ad87bb2d72ea63ee5c152aed06ba19` adds only the test-line allocation record; production and test source are identical to the built and live-tested runtime.

- The scope-mismatch regression fails on unpatched main because it creates two inputs instead of reusing one; the matching-scope control passes.
- All **130 tests across ten focused files** pass on the integrated candidate, including native-plugin handoff, source identity/FIFO/reuse, browser disconnect/close, permission parity, cancellation, relay adoption, and terminal writes.
- Production and Gateway-other test typechecks, six-file type-aware lint/format checks, and whitespace checks pass.
- Full source build passes, including runtime/plugin bundles, SDK declarations and export checks, CLI startup checks, and Control UI assets.
- Independent inspection of the resolved production diff found no concrete integration regression in the two-file scope.
- The documented test-line budget check passes with a 43-line allocation: the repair adds 443 net test lines against the 400-line allowance. The allocation retains distinct public native-handoff coverage and exact-source identity, cancellation, one-shot reuse, and FIFO regressions. It changes no executable code or tests.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43300181834) and the required CI gate passed for current head `3ad8007b26ad87bb2d72ea63ee5c152aed06ba19`, including the repaired test-line budget check.

### Real Behavior Proof

**Claim:** the complete repair lets an accepted voice consultation execute through the backing agent and deliver its answer as speech.

**Surface and fixture:** the installed Omarchy companion and native GStreamer/WebRTC worker, connected to a real VPS Gateway, GPT-Live, and the configured backing agent. Generated speech asks the agent to check the current date. Capture and playback are pinned to temporary private PulseAudio/PipeWire devices.

**Before:** installed revision `753f48d41b0c705661e7c6fdfafc2d547f58c006` transcribed and acknowledged the question but returned no substantive answer within 100 seconds. The correlated source claim waited at mailbox selection with four pending inputs, following an earlier failed request in the same conversation.

**After:** the VPS runs the complete validated main-plus-PR build. On 2026-11-12 UTC, the correlated source claim had **one input** and transitioned from waiting to selected in approximately **1 ms**. The backing agent executed its check and recorded a successful terminal answer. The voice layer returned the correct date after approximately **25 seconds**, with non-silent reply PCM captured at the companion output. Independent offline dictation recognized Thursday, November, and twelfth in that answer audio.

**Trace:** ready 20:12:26.725; source waiting 20:12:40.183; selected 20:12:40.184; agent terminal answer 20:12:51.731; final voice transcript 20:12:57.880. Temporary audio resources were released and desktop audio defaults were preserved.

**Follow-up validation:** a second live call asked for today's date and then tomorrow's date. Both consultations used one input and were immediately selected; both reached the backing agent and returned the correct voice transcripts. Offline dictation of the follow-up audio recognized Friday, November, and thirteenth. The call stayed active for approximately 78 seconds, including approximately 27 seconds after the final voice transcript, with no unexpected session end. Temporary devices were released and desktop audio defaults were unchanged.

**Limits:** these are three completed consultations across two live calls through the external Omarchy client, not an ordinary browser Control UI test. They use generated input and virtual audio devices, so they do not establish human microphone or physical speaker behavior. The live before and after use different main revisions; the separate red/green regression isolates the PR's admission repair on the pinned main baseline. Raw conversation records, credentials, endpoints, and identifying trace values remain private. This does not establish recovery for every provider failure or long-running session.

title: fix: promoted conversations keep their former parent marked busy
body:
Closes #183389

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a former parent conversation keeps showing activity when its child has been promoted to the sidebar top level and that promoted conversation has active descendants. The elapsed duration in the report is incidental, not a trigger.

## User Impact

User impact: the promoted conversation stays busy while its otherwise-idle former parent becomes idle. Ordinary nested conversations and legitimate live controllers continue to show their active work. No configuration, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the promotion boundary only to propagated activity, preserving durable lineage, access ownership, and child links. Carry the promotion flag through compact child projections and use the same live-controller-aware decision for row presentation and its cache fingerprint, so ending control cannot leave a stale busy indicator. Hidden subagents retain their existing behavior.

Related work: #183418 and #183436. @sunlit-deng @lonexreb: this independently prepared alternative includes the distinct-controller/requester case and warm-cache control-retirement coverage; it intentionally preserves child links rather than changing the ownership graph. The overlapping work should be consolidated rather than merged independently.

## Evidence

- Production projection regression reproduced the promoted-parent activity failure on the base and passes with the fix. It covers promotion, repeated reads, a live controller with a different completion requester, controller retirement, demotion, and worker completion.
- Five focused Gateway suites: 38 tests passed. Two existing Control UI consumer suites: 12 tests passed. After strengthening the distinct-requester and warm-read assertions, the presentation and subagent suites were rerun: 16 tests passed.
- Core typecheck, Gateway test typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found no actionable issues in the production patch; the final test strengthening received a follow-up review.
- The five affected files on current `main` at `b3a2d10ce4563a79b69032b936f9e957b0289ec5` match the tested base.

### Real Gateway and Control UI proof

A task-owned Chromium scenario exercised the built Control UI against an isolated Gateway, using the actual chat composer, sessions_spawn tool, running child worker, WebSocket updates, and **Move to top level** menu. The only scripted boundary was the loopback OpenAI Responses provider; this is not an external-provider live test. No WebSocket interception or fabricated busy rows were used.

- **Before:** the original production source failed the visible assertion: the otherwise-idle former parent retained its running ring after promotion.
- **After:** the same scenario passed on this PR's production source. The former parent's ring clears without reloading, the promoted conversation remains busy with its worker still running, and the result remains correct after a reload. Ordinary nesting first marks both conversations busy; durable parent linkage is preserved after promotion.

title: fix: subagent turns fail after session metadata changes
body:
Related: #179289

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes new subagent turns failing before submission when inherited capability metadata becomes stale after an ordinary session metadata update.

## User Impact

An authorized child follow-up can prepare fresh metadata instead of failing with `Session capability metadata changed`. Existing identity, policy-revocation, and closed-owner checks remain enforced. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Asynchronous capability preparation now refreshes a stale inherited read once per affected lookup and reevaluates current policy. Synchronous retained reads still reject stale authority, and a second invalidation fails rather than retrying indefinitely. The shared capability projection is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Conflict resolution (November 2, 2026)

Merged main `c29085dbfeafa2414d943cf5e5ce51500fd33128` into the PR as `ceae29d22a63b526eb15256d921e86d080b71469` without rewriting branch history. Preserved main's model-routing stability and non-retryable capability-error classification, plus this PR's one-refresh limit and terminal retained-read guard. Both documentation changes are retained.

The regression fixtures now change inherited tool policy: model-only changes no longer invalidate capability facts on main. All **35 tests** in the two affected suites passed. The three refreshed-child admission cases fail against main's production implementation with `SessionCapabilityMetadataChangedError`, and pass with this resolution. Messaging and agents/sessions typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. An independent source review found no actionable issues. Local ClawSweeper completed on `c29085dbfeafa2414d943cf5e5ce51500fd33128..ceae29d22a63b526eb15256d921e86d080b71469`: no production/security findings; it identified missing test-line allocation. Follow-up `8981eec95d15081da49a57687d9801cea44feee9` adds exactly 173 net lines of allocation for bounded-refresh and final-effect revocation/reassignment regressions. No production or test bytes changed after that review.

**Known inherited check failure:** the test-line ratchet still reports an 840-line deficit inherited from the integrated main (base: 6,420,543 test lines / 6,419,703 ceiling; candidate: 6,420,716 / 6,419,876). This PR's +173 lines are fully allocated; the shared scalar and inherited debt are unchanged. Focused suite wall times were 37.89s and 38.52s (118.92s including preparation); CI duration is pending. The final-admission tests exercise worker-backed policy and identity checks, not a mocked authorization decision.

The diff against the integrated main is five files, including the allocation record: production +21/-8, tests +174/-1, documentation +6. No additional owner or retry path was introduced. Live evidence below remains evidence for the previous head, not a new live run or current-head CI result.

### Previous-head evidence (`9f0a7a085e1bd3c3fed1bbd0eb50e7ff50494213`)

- **Live completed-child follow-up (same head):** [@Marvinthebored’s verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183501#issuecomment-6397556970) on `9f0a7a085e1bd3c3fed1bbd0eb50e7ff50494213` (October 25, 2026, 12:14–12:16 UTC) used an isolated Gateway and real Codex model processes. A child completed and its parent independently recorded the initial Gateway `announce:v1:` completion. After `sessions.patch` changed the completed child’s model, the parent’s `sessions_send` (`mode: followup`) returned `status: ok` and the expected reply. The child’s own history confirmed that final reply under the new model with the same session ID—no replacement child. Follow-up delivery was synchronous (`delivery.status: skipped`), not a second completion announcement. Six native turn completions and successful cleanup were recorded; production was not deployed or restarted.
- **Red → green through final admission:** all three refreshed-child cases fail on the base with `Session capability metadata changed`; all pass with this fix. The tests perform real session writes, inherit a stale read after a model update, prepare the child, register its host-bound run, and inject the follow-up through the production controller and native-input adapter.
- **Final-effect authority harness:** the authorized case reaches native submission exactly once. Policy revocation or session/parent reassignment after entering the native queue fails with `MessageInjectionAuthorityError` before submission. Authority, database reads, and final worker-backed admission are not mocked; only the native transport I/O is a fixture.
- **Bounds and retained guards:** one intervening publication refreshes successfully; a second invalidation stops. A previously retained synchronous guard cannot be renewed after revocation.
- **Checks:** both affected suites rerun: **34 passed**. Messaging test-shard typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The earlier **79 consumer tests**, core/agents-sessions typechecks, and docs check remain applicable: this follow-up changes only test coverage, not production or documentation.
- **Independent review:** fresh AutoReview on the complete updated candidate returned scoped-clean at its P0 threshold; it did not execute tests or assess lower-priority findings.

**Validation limits:** The live run verifies the patched completed-child follow-up workflow and initial Gateway completion announcement; it is not a base-versus-head reproduction of the stale inherited-read timing and does not establish that the refresh branch executed. The red/green authority harness supplies that narrower causal evidence and the revocation/reassignment negative cases. The exact mutation in the original incident and later `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` retries remain unconfirmed. This PR fixes the reproduced stale-read preparation failure, not the entire broader incident; fallback classification is separate in #179312.

<details>
<summary>Proof path and verification commands</summary>

The refreshed-child regression follows `withPreparedEmbeddedRunToolAuthority → attachActiveEmbeddedRun → queueCurrentReplyRunMessage → createSteeredCliMessageInjection → withMessageInjectionAdmission → native submit`. The negative cases change persisted policy or identity in the native queue, after the initial authority projection but before final admission. They must enter that queue and must not reach its submit callback.

```text
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.worker.test.ts -t 'dispatches a refreshed child'
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.worker.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-capabilities.store.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.worker.test.ts
```

Previously passed and unchanged consumer coverage: requester policy, harness execution, completion lineage, and prompt-prefix stability. Tests use repository wrappers and pinned OpenClaw Bun with the Node 26.12.1 launcher.

Simplification: no new authority owner or parallel recovery path. The existing async preparation owns the bounded retry; retained replay stays fenced. Against the base: production +21/-2, tests +172/-1, documentation +6; test growth is the final-submission security proof rather than new production machinery.

</details>

title: fix(ui): keep guest access guidance in Profile without Inbox warnings
body:
Related: #157182
Related: #182941

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: restricted guests see expected permission limits as Inbox warnings, while role-limited members can be offered an admin request that device approval cannot fulfill.

## User Impact

Your access in Settings → Profile explains the current role and device limits. Guest Inbox stays quiet, and Request admin appears only when the assigned role allows it; separate device approval is still required. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway adds optional `hello-ok.auth.roleAllowsAdmin` from the existing role-policy owner. It is presentation metadata, not authorization. Existing clients ignore the additive field, and absent metadata keeps existing upgrade behavior. Profile and Inbox use the same upgrade owner and controls; pending requests retire when the role ceiling becomes guidance. RPC authorization is unchanged.

The conflict with current main was resolved by preserving main's stronger sidebar alignment assertions. Protocol/schema and native models were regenerated through their owners, with no tracked generated delta. Operator-scope and pairing docs describe the behavior.

## Evidence

The role-ceiling runtime regression failed on base: a pending request remained requesting instead of showing role guidance. The Chromium reproduction also failed on base because a role-limited member was offered Request admin. Both pass with the repair.

200 focused tests passed across the upgrade owner, Profile, Inbox, Gateway auth, and protocol consumers. UI typecheck, targeted typed lint, formatting, diff checks, native protocol generation/determinism checks, and the test budget passed. Independent diff-scoped review through P2 found no actionable findings.

All 16 Chromium browser tests passed (223.1s, excluding cold build). The isolated real-Gateway case passed in 88.4s: synthetic guest → quiet Inbox and Profile guidance → real role promotion → separate browser pairing approval → reload with admin access. Mock-Gateway siblings cover role ceilings, dismissal/reload, pending requests, errors, and unadvertised methods. The real Gateway, proxy, browser, and fresh state were cleaned up by the fixture.

title: fix(codex): context refresh blocks replies on managed inference routes

Fixes replies blocked after a context refresh when a managed inference route still owns background work on the previous Codex thread.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Thread creation fingerprints the logical inference route, but projection refresh compared the temporary relay URL. Passing the same inference context to the existing fingerprint owner makes those comparisons consistent. Preserves the newer main-branch first-reply and native-completion fixes. Also fixes the cleanup callback return type and dynamic-tool discriminant that failed the previous CI typecheck.

Plugin-specific permissions, widget approvals, and MCP App restrictions remain in place; no configuration change is needed. This covers the dashboard inside a conversation; gallery previews and focused dashboard documents remain separate follow-up work. ## Why This Change Was Made The change uses the existing session admission, creator checks, event filtering, and UI capability helpers. Canvas imports also use the normal saved-widget source reader: a narrow caller must have a visible saved receipt in the dashboard conversation, and that source authority remains held through the write. Broad readers and trusted in-process callers retain their existing paths. The Canvas reader is shared by viewing and importing, so archive selection, pending widget presentation, and source-session checks keep one owner. The existing destination and storage guards continue to check the session and requester before accepting changes. ## Evidence - Real dispatch on the comparison base rejects the owner’s dashboard write for missing `operator.write`. On the candidate, the complete selected set of 501 related cases passes across the applicable runs and focused corrections, including ownership, shared-viewer restrictions, hidden sessions, approvals, MCP restrictions, event filtering, and write admission. - The identical final Canvas regression fails on the original PR and passes with the correction. It uses real transcript receipts and the board store to verify permitted content, foreign-source denial without copied state, and source revocation while an import waits. The unchanged internal-caller collision test also passes. The new three-case file takes 5.11 seconds of test execution; its single-worker command with the collision control takes 59.01 seconds including preparation. - Formatting, targeted lint, and affected type checks pass. Independent engineering/adversarial review is clean for `1eda7575c6bfc70765aa23baad6acbff0525b8bf`; supplementary review is clean through P2. - The real built Control UI connects to an isolated Gateway with only `operator.sessions.write`. The same synthetic report request is denied before the change and displayed afterward. The native widget menu sends an acknowledged resize from 6×4 to 8×6; reload preserves the layout and the same narrow identity. Served UI bytes match the candidate build. No model inference is claimed. - [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40398279381) is terminal. Its remaining failure is the upstream subagent-registry assertion that still reads terminal-reply text from a compact resident row. The [same assertion fails on scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40387557460/job/121800283941); source and runtime comparison establish that it is unrelated to this dashboard change. The failing shard and its aggregate status remain visible. Other selected jobs, including UI, browser E2E, performance, and PostgreSQL conformance, passed. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Session\-only guest has no dashboard after the report request is denied](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a9c5969-b03b-432d-acff-6babaa2c73f1) | ![The same guest can open its native report in the dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/648dd86d-874f-4be8-8934-f9ac8fe6fb25) | ### Guest resize and reload with only session\-write permission https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3da052e-7a66-473f-b434-012bc13c5510 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 496f32bef297a28c7fdaea083a123c878936cf44 - Exact head: `1eda7575c6bfc70765aa23baad6acbff0525b8bf` - Scenario: A session\-only guest opens its native report, resizes it from 6×4 to 8×6 using Widget options, and reloads to confirm the saved layout\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 1eda7575c6bf; source tree d6a95b93a52a; served UI bytes matched the build\. - Connection scopes: operator\.sessions\.write only; sessionCap=view - Resize: 6×4 → 8×6; board\.update acknowledged - Reload: Saved 8×6 layout retained; same narrow identity - Real isolated Gateway and built Control UI; synthetic profile and report\. - Same report request is denied on the baseline and succeeds on the corrected source\. - Native menu interaction and persisted layout asserted through the browser connection\. - Recording annotations omit incidental model\-picker details; the menu segment plays at 0\.5× speed\. No model inference was used\. Contributor credit: requested by Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit). ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/602db0a0-0f96-4338-a617-72ad921212e9) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2c20ad55-cfd3-4005-96b7-336d360a3c5d) ## Worked on by - @TheAngryPit

title: fix(zalouser): stop reusing stale sessions across plugin reloads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Zalo Personal sessions and group information being reused from a different managed plugin registration during reload or concurrent inspection.

## User Impact

Zalo Personal registrations keep their own authenticated sessions and group information. In-flight channel calls can finish on their original registration, and retiring it does not clear another registration or standalone session. Saved credentials remain intact; no configuration or state migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bundled modules can survive registration retirement, so module-global session maps can outlive their owner. The existing instance-scoped runtime store now owns the session state, with cleanup registered through the normal full/discovery and setup lifecycle hooks. QR preparation rechecks its captured login before SDK startup and aborts SDK events arriving after retirement. Standalone helpers retain their existing process-local reuse. The session type, store, and cleanup live together, keeping the injected host runtime free of session-owner backedges.

## Evidence

- The cache ownership regression failed on base `99d08a6d92e7b7076fd337cdccb1b662870bc2ba`: the second registration received the first registration's profile identity and group name. The follow-up QR-retirement cases failed on `93035cdac676f0aa24706f3d391f193b316f1ef0`: delayed SDK construction started QR login after retirement, and a first SDK event arriving after retirement did not invoke its abort action. Deferred SDK boundaries and fake timers reproduce the QR cases without real sleeps or network requests.
- CI run [40099334759, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40099334759) on `7c194b82b276ef212d97194c2d87af64e105963a` exposed two **PR-caused** failures, not baseline exceptions: an [all-import cycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40099334759/job/120888471147) through the host runtime's session-state type backedge, and a [closed mock-export factory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40099334759/job/120888471148). Both reproduced locally. The existing session owner now contains its private state type, runtime store, and disposal callback; the injected host runtime is a leaf. The fixture spreads the original zca-client exports and replaces only SDK construction. No scanner, baseline, ignore, or isolation-marker exception was added.
- On `dd04ce4f162a4b7cdea91cdb54a569e97a7f499d`, `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` reports **0 cycles** (**15.57 s**, red count was 1); `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base 99d08a6d92e7b7076fd337cdccb1b662870bc2ba` passes (**10.48 s**).
- Current consumer proof: **29 tests passed** across lifecycle, credential persistence, listener, lazy SDK loading, and setup-status suites (**111.25 s** wrapper wall time, including cold compiled-worker preparation). All **five lifecycle regressions passed** in **0.430 s** test execution. Managed replacement, admitted work, stale-handle rejection, both delayed QR boundaries, standalone reuse, durable credential handling, loopback listener cleanup, and SDK loading deferred until session creation remain covered. Unchanged channel/probe/tool proof is retained from the original 68-test run.
- Registration, channel-call leases, the production setup lifecycle hook, cache operations, and retirement are real. Authentication and credential-storage I/O in the lifecycle regressions are synthetic. A follow-up composition regression connects actual managed registration/retirement to the production SQLite worker: the current registration successfully saves its credential row, and a delayed retired SDK result is fenced at the producer before persistence and cannot replace that row. All **15 real-storage credential tests passed** (**12.33 s** wrapper wall time; **0.594 s** for the new case), including existing ordinary refresh-settlement cases. No production code or authority semantics changed for this proof; it does not claim that new writes initiated after retirement remain authorized. No live Gateway or external channel API verification is claimed.
- For the final test-only delta on `932536d849328260cf8e56fa34d3fe83ed3cbdae`, scoped typecheck passed (**7.77 s**) and touched-file lint passed (**26.82 s**); formatting, line-cap, diff and mock-export checks passed. Fresh final autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Accepted production build/import proof is reused because no production code changed; local timings are not CI execution costs.
- Full `pnpm build` on `dd04ce4f162a4b7cdea91cdb54a569e97a7f499d` exited zero (**471.68 s**; tsdown was the slowest phase at **338.4 s**). Its UI report still notes chat-boot JavaScript above budget (**1,277,003 B** versus **1,275,713 B**); no UI files are modified.
- Entry import cost is explicit: the static runtime-source closure grows from **209 to 219 modules**, adding ten state/cache helper modules, not the vendor SDK or database workers. Session/cache construction remains lazy. The required isolated Zalouser profiler passed with a **qualified cold-import snapshot** bound to this clean commit/tree (**0.93 s**, Node 26.12.1/Linux x64): peak RSS **110.69 MiB**, empty-process baseline **59.76 MiB**. The prior qualified QR-code-tree screen recorded **109.76 MiB** peak RSS with a **57.70 MiB** empty-process baseline. These are single cold-import screens, **not a before/after performance benchmark or leak-reduction claim**; no forced GC or debugger was used.

title: improve(plugins): reduce memory used by package capture workers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary package captures load a source parser even when they never inspect JavaScript source.

## User Impact

Package-capture workers avoid an unused parser module and its initialization. This is a modest per-worker JavaScript heap reduction, not a fix for the native isolate RSS floor or a claimed Gateway latency improvement. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load Acorn only when source inspection requests parsing, resolving its existing ESM entry so native imports and synchronous inspection retain the same parser identity. Selective standalone capture still acquires the parser when needed.

## Evidence

- Import-boundary regression failed on the base and passed after the change: 25 ms test execution, 4.62 s command wall. Inspection suite: 8 passed. Capture/loader consumers: 170 passed, 5 skips; 148.95 s wall.
- Five alternating fresh-process measurements per side, bound to rebuilt baseline/candidate worker artifacts on Node 26.12.1: Acorn modules 1 → 0, file-backed scripts 318 → 317; median collected heap 15.847 → 15.159 MiB cold and 24.614 → 24.105 MiB prepared. The synthetic prepared fixture includes 100 native-admission roots and 5,000 file facts. These are heap measurements, not RSS or live Gateway totals.
- Selective standalone positive control loaded exactly one acorn.mjs and no CommonJS duplicate. CPU profiles showed parser initialization disappearing from ordinary package captures.
- Targeted typecheck, typed lint, formatting, diff checks, full candidate build (165.8 s), fresh independent P0–P2 review, and qualified exact-head arcee entrypoint import profile passed.

The acceptance does not justify duplicating the subsequently discovered upstream implementation or changing budgets, baselines, or dependencies.

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

On the historical published-head comparison, Chat and New Session request 4,349 B and 4,456 B less gzip respectively through the first ordinary composer edit, with the same observed JavaScript requests and CSS. No rendered UI, feature, API, permission, migration, or user action changes.

This is not a byte-flat initial-entry result. The later local repair’s measured tradeoff was explicitly accepted as recorded above; this older published tree is not the accepted repair. No page-load latency improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the 14 shared control/recovery labels in a small route-shared English fragment, rather than loading the complete organization catalog from six eager consumers. Optional menus retain synchronous registration at their existing lazy boundaries. The full organization catalog references the same shared values in their original positions, preserving every composed key, value, and key order. Regenerate the boot manifest with the existing owner. ### Current-main qualification, separate from the published head

The shipped frozen-install helper prepared a new self-contained install for pinned main `79798ed63e1d974179c2bfd7960c04daa7f14dda`, with only the measurement script staged (executing tree `f2a6857758076498f7387c386574aa258fd3185d`). The check’s zero exit status does not mean conflict-free. No failed/unpublished normalizer candidate was applied. ### Historical published-head evidence (retained, not relabeled)

The remainder records the original `a382e18`-based published tree and is not evidence that the current conflict-narrowed branch still removes additional production bytes.

Acceptance was recorded before measurement: meaningful route-ready gzip headroom (prefer at least 4 KiB), unchanged absolute/differential gates, complete requested closure through ordinary first input, and raw/gzip/Brotli/CSS/all-JS accounting. title: fix(ui): restore mobile header controls and refine compact layouts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the mobile header lost its dedicated People, Panels, and Dashboard controls in #181076, while non-project sessions still showed the default agent workspace as a project.

## User Impact

Restores the existing mobile controls and avatar-grid design. The session title is above a real project name; without a project, the title can use two tighter, balanced lines with truncation. The default agent workspace stays hidden without changing file access or workspace roots.

Mobile public access uses a bare globe beside the title. A lone viewer is hidden; two or more current viewers keep the existing grid. At widths up to 349px, Dashboard and Panels move into the native Actions menu. Wider viewports keep direct controls. Controls retain focus identity across resizing, and Sharing opened from People returns focus to People.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the requested iteration on the original mobile design from #176360, #176653, and #176505, preserving the current native host, panel retention, sharing permissions, and lazy-loading owners. Default-workspace visibility is decided by the shared header identity resolver, not display-text matching. The People grid is loaded only when needed and no longer pulls the full People-page stylesheet into chat startup.

The requested reversion also returns mobile Details to its pre-#181076 layout: the separate full-title heading introduced by that compact-header redesign is intentionally removed, rather than retained as a second title display. Long titles remain truncated in the header; this PR does not add a replacement title section in Details.

## Evidence

- 70 focused header, workspace, People, and mobile-composition unit tests passed.
- UI production and test typechecks, targeted lint, CSS lint, formatting, and independent P0–P2 review completed. The final cleanup adds 41 passing performance-budget tests and reruns all eight mobile-header browser scenarios, including reduced-motion red/green proof.
- 25 distinct browser scenarios validated across the full run and the affected sharing rerun (5/5 passing after the focus repair): 320px, 349px, 350px, 390px, landscape, desktop transitions, offline/reconnect, native Details/Panels, sharing, and retained focus.
- All 19 final header captures are pixel-identical to the approved design after CSS cleanup. 19 synthetic-data visual states captured from the production-built Control UI. [Latest before/after, 320px, and long-title evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182599#issuecomment-6384985504).
- Simplification: removed duplicate menu composition and obsolete solo/away grid styles; kept one native navigation/focus owner and separate deferred grid/page assets. Necessary growth is the restored grid and responsive header presentation.

### Current-head validation

At `adde2d0451bb`, the conflict repair passes all seven remaining mobile-header browser scenarios, targeted lint/types, and a fresh independent P0–P2 review. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40103303253) completed with one inherited failing job and its downstream CI gate; all other jobs passed or were skipped by the planner, including security and Control UI performance. Its `check-lint` job failed in the controller guard on `extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/view-selection.tsx:393` (`querySelector`), introduced on main by #182020. That file and the guard inputs are unchanged by this PR; the same failure reproduces locally. This is an inherited failure, not a passing CI result. Landing uses the supported native pre-existing-failure route with exact-head attribution; review and security requirements remain enforced.

### Performance acceptance and cleanup

Vyctor explicitly approved the remaining restored-topbar cost on October 24 and requested landing without changing the approved design. The added styling restores the two-by-two People grid and the responsive title/project/navigation layout removed with the previous topbar. Existing horizontal facepile styles do not implement that approved grid.

A fresh audit removed redundant box sizing and inherited declarations, plus two scroll-fade selectors that never matched the menu markup. This removes 452 minified CSS bytes and 45 gzip bytes compared with the preceding implementation. It also fixes the reconnect spinner's reduced-motion override, with a browser regression that fails on the preceding header stylesheet.

The accepted CSS cost is bounded by fixed bundle ceilings of 303,372 B gzip and 1,595,521 B raw, not an additional per-PR growth allowance. Existing JavaScript, startup, and request-count limits remain unchanged. A 41-test performance suite covers acceptance at and rejection above these ceilings. No runtime configuration or data migration is required.

title: improve: reduce TypeScript plugin startup and reload overhead
body:
## What Problem This Solves

TypeScript plugin startup and reload create outputs for unused source files and repeat compiler and captured-metadata work.

## User Impact

Operators get less startup/reload overhead for TypeScript plugins, especially packages with many unused source files. No configuration changes, dependency changes, or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allocate stable compiler outputs on first resolution, derive Jiti helpers from binding-aware transformed runtime JavaScript, and reuse immutable dependency declaration plans at the captured-metadata owner. Resolve-only paths still exist without compiling; deferred imports, native compilation, package promotion, dependency/link validation, and native namespace freshness retain their existing owners. Failed Jiti transforms preserve source-relative syntax diagnostics through an error-only esbuild pass.

Requested by Vincent Koc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fb976ba8-0da0-4c4a-89de-35557e7f30f0)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/afbedcaf-fb7d-494d-b9f3-3c332d5415fb)

## Evidence

**Real Gateway plugin-management acceptance passed** on the published source tree: a disposable built Gateway with fresh owned profile/state and loopback port loaded the external TS plugin, then completed five ordinary non-messaging CLI RPCs. The running instance retained old / 31 / deferred-old after original source edits. Real `plugins.reload` returned `ok=true`, `restartRequired=false`, and the same Gateway PID served new / 41 / deferred-new. Resolve-only deferred outputs existed as stable zero-byte files until import; three resolved outputs were present with 16 unused TS inputs. Post-capture source edits did not change deferred values. Old/new disposal callbacks ran in order, generated paths were removed, and shutdown exited 0 without force; PID absence and released port were verified. No agent/chat/session/model request was issued.

**Scoped limitation:** a separate agent/model case remains unexecuted because this run has no admitted attributed agent-turn transport targeting the disposable Gateway; the built CLI attribution refusal was respected. No marker was removed and no alternate agent transport was used. That case and model inference are not claimed by this plugin-loader PR. Agent/model/request behavior is unchanged; the changed plugin-runtime contract is covered by the real Gateway management flow above. This is a limitation of the current execution surface, not a global OpenClaw limitation.

The workload uses production `loadOpenClawPluginsAsync` with one TS entry plus 500 unused TS siblings, then exercises 20 deferred TS imports through a real managed instance and disposes all owned resources. This is plugin-loader boundary proof, **not** a booted Gateway, reload RPC, or model-turn benchmark.

Command: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/plugin-source-demand.mts`. Baseline is pinned `43d998d0c6339341c6128ebfe4c8495e7badbd4b`, with identical frozen dependencies and workload. Acceptance was recorded before measurement: remove unused placeholders and the extra successful-Jiti transform, avoid per-demand manifest rereads, and investigate any >20% regression in wall/CPU/RSS.

Five serial baseline/candidate pairs were measured; each process supplied one cold and five warm generations. The table below is the final source candidate's last matched pair (five warm samples each, nearest-rank p95). Earlier pairs exercised the same successful path before the diagnostic-only repair, confirmed identical work counts, and supplied the tail investigation. No samples were discarded.

| Final-candidate work / warm metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup placeholders / generated writes | 501 / 502 | 1 / 2 |
| Combined placeholders / generated writes | 522 / 565 | 22 / 65 |
| Successful source-builder esbuild acquisitions | 22 | 0 |
| Captured manifest reads | 23 | 2 |
| Startup wall median / p95 (ms) | 1194 / 1242 | 1117 / 1140 |
| Combined wall median / p95 (ms) | 1292 / 1360 | 1199 / 1223 |
| Process CPU median / p95 (ms) | 1376 / 1440 | 1290 / 1353 |
| Observed process RSS median / p95 (MiB) | 943.2 / 945.7 | 685.6 / 869.6 |

Warm startup ranges: 1180–1242 ms before, 1081–1140 ms after. Combined ranges: 1278–1360 and 1160–1223 ms. CPU ranges: 1359–1440 and 1208–1353 ms. Cold startup/combined wall: 1995/2128 ms before, 1460/1567 ms after. Final one-minute host loads were 38.05 and 31.77 on a 128-thread host. These are synthetic observations, not universal reload-time or memory-reduction claims. RSS varied with allocator/worker state; this does not claim native ESM unloading. An early small-sample tail increase prompted additional matched pairs; expanded medians and p95s improved. Main-thread CPU profiles were captured; worker launch policy did not emit separate worker profiles. Process CPU includes worker-thread work, not separately spawned esbuild-service CPU.

- Real loader regressions failed on the base for eager placeholders, second-transformer acquisition, and repeated captured-manifest reads, then passed with the fix. Owning generation/regression suites: 100 passed, one runtime-specific skip. Unchanged focused consumer proofs cover package conditions/promotion, JSON/cycles, native admission/freshness, dependency links, and disposal.
- All four type lanes (`tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:test:root`), targeted core/script lint, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed in 400.69 s. Its remaining broad Knip failure is inherited: all 92 unique findings reproduce exactly on the pinned base (112.73 s); no new finding, ignore, or baseline exception was added.
- Full `pnpm build`: exit 0 in 213.78 s. It emitted nonfatal UI gzip-budget warnings (startup 275.8 > 275.2 KiB; chat boot 1247.3 > 1245.8 KiB); no UI/budget files changed. A supported committed `sourcePerformance` build (70.26 s) then produced matching build provenance. Qualified `device-pair` built-entry cold-import snapshot: 81.79 MiB peak versus 59.73 MiB baseline, 109.76 ms process CPU (66.04 ms over baseline), verified child/group cleanup. This checks built import identity, not activation or a before/after performance claim.
- Final standalone `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-module-generation.work.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed; 33.41 s wall including 28.00 s shared worker preparation, 0.302 s test execution. Estimated incremental CI cost: about one second.

title: fix(whatsapp): release cached quotes after plugin retirement
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cached WhatsApp message bodies remaining reachable after plugin retirement and quote metadata being shared between overlapping plugin instances.

## User Impact

Quote metadata stays with the instance that admitted the work: existing replies retain it through settlement, while replacement instances start without retired state. Standalone callers keep their existing module-local cache behavior.

The existing plugin reload stop/drain/dispose sequence is unchanged. No configuration, schema, public SDK contract, persistent-data migration, or additional update/restart step is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing quote cache into the invoking instance's existing runtime-store slot, which the host releases after admitted work settles. This avoids a new cleanup manager and prevents disposing a candidate instance from clearing another instance's quotes. The existing 10-minute TTL and 500-entry bound remain.

title: fix(visitor-access): settle guest welcome sessions across renewal, revocation, and deletion
body:
Related: guest onboarding item 10 (follows #182352 and #182337)

## What Problem This Solves

Guest welcome sessions had unsettled edge cases around renewal, revocation, and deletion: an administrator-deleted welcome session was still reported as ready (so a guest on a new browser was sent to a missing session), revocation during setup answered `pending` or a retryable failure, and `visitor_list` gave staff no view of welcome progress.

## User Impact

User impact: renewing access never starts a second welcome session; expiry and revocation keep the session and transcript; a deleted welcome session stays deleted and the Control UI no longer opens it; staff see each invitation's welcome state and session key in `visitor_list`. No storage or config migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Audit of the requested cases against main (280c7c7d), with what this PR changes:

| Case | Main before this PR | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a. renewal while ready | Handled; covered by `welcome.test.ts` "creates one guest-owned welcome session…" and `visitors.onboarding.test.ts` "renewal keeps inviter, note, and ready onboarding…" | No change |
| b. renewal mid-setup (reservation held) | Handled (invite and the onboarding CAS share one queue; renewal keeps the record and its CAS token), not tested | Test: "keeps one welcome session when access is renewed during setup or after a failure" |
| c. renewal while failed | Handled, not tested | Same test: the next ensure resumes the reserved key; one session, one message |
| d. revoke during setup | Gateway refuses the guest's writes after the grant ends (`server.visitor-welcome.test.ts`), but ensure answered `pending` (ready commit refused) or `failed` (append refused) | Ensure answers `not_applicable`; tests for both steps prove the record is gone and a re-invite starts with a new grant and a new session |
| e. expiry with a session | Handled: the plugin never deletes sessions; sweep removes only the grant record. Covered by "returns not_applicable without an active visitor grant…" and the expiry re-invite test | No change |
| f. re-invite after expiry/revocation | Handled for expiry ("starts a new welcome session for a new invitation after the old one expired") | Revocation path covered by the case d tests; the earlier session stays the guest's and listed |
| g. same person invited by email and GitHub | Two grants; the Gateway admits the first active one (emails before GitHub), so only that invitation gets a welcome. If it ends while the other continues, the other invitation gets its own welcome | Kept per-invitation and documented in the README. See the product question below |
| h. welcome session deleted after ready | Reported `ready` with the stale key; the UI could land a guest on a missing session | Ensure checks the session as the guest and answers `not_applicable` when it is gone, never recreating it; the record stays `ready`. Item 7's UI already hides on `not_applicable` |
| i. legacy grants without onboarding | Handled; covered by "keeps legacy grants working without onboarding metadata through renewal" and "gives a grant recorded by v2026.10.6…" | Listing omits `welcome` for them |
| j. `visitor_list` onboarding | Not shown | Text and details show `welcome` state and session key; setup error text stays in the Gateway log |

Accepted edge case, documented: before setup completes, a retry resumes the reserved key, so a partial session removed after a failed setup is created again with its welcome message. It never carried the welcome, and telling it apart would need another durable state.

Product question for case g (no change made): keep one welcome per invitation (this PR), or adopt another active grant's welcome for the same person. Adoption would need the profile's identity in ensure plus a cross-grant lookup, and still could not help once the first grant has ended and been swept, so I left per-invitation in place.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway: `src/gateway/server.visitor-welcome.test.ts` now has the guest's plugin RPC call `sessions.describe` and gets the session while it exists, then `{ session: null }` after an administrator deletes it. Its first run failed with `missing scope: operator.read`: the guest role holds only `operator.sessions.write`, so the plugin now asks for `operator.sessions.read` explicitly. The unit test pins that option.
- Red on base, green here: both revoke-during-setup tests, the deleted-session test, and the listing test failed with the fix reverted; the renewal test passes on both (coverage for an invariant main already held).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/visitor-access`: 6 files, 107 tests pass. `src/gateway/server.visitor-welcome.test.ts` passes.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and ratchets pass. The dead-export scan fails on pre-existing unused exports in `ui/` and `scripts/`, none in this change.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): the first pass flagged the pre-ready retry case above, which is now documented as accepted; the final pass was clean.
- No storage semantics changed (no new grant fields or states), so no upgrade proof was needed.

Requested by @jalehman

Desktop discovery delegates retirement to the existing transient-layout owner rather than closing manual panels. title: fix: worker startup failures hide their original errors
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker startup failures being replaced by an input-admission error before their real cause can be handled.

## User Impact

Worker launch errors retain their original diagnostics, and node-loss failures retain the typed error needed by existing recovery. Unapproved worker input still cannot reach inference, persistence, tools, or transcript-backed finalization.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admission assertion introduced in #182142 ran before the worker-result parser, masking process failures, connection deadlines, and node loss. Run the existing parser first, then require admission before reading or delivering a transcript-backed result. No new recovery policy or admission bypass is added.

## Evidence

- Startup-exit and connection-deadline regressions both fail on the original code with the generic admission error.
- All 40 focused tests pass across admission, launcher failure recovery, and payload suites (3 files): allow/block paths, unapproved effects and successful results, typed node-loss recovery, and launch payload contracts.
- The unapproved-result fixture now supplies a schema-valid completed result, so it tests admission rather than malformed output.
- Core TypeScript checking, targeted lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent autoreview found no P0 issues.
- Simplification: one existing parser and one admission gate remain; production changes are +4/-1 lines, with no extra parsing or state.

title: fix: WebChat agents lose native reply and attachment guidance
body:

Fixes agents being told that ordinary WebChat turns have no current conversation, causing them to avoid native chat replies and attachments even though those routes exist.

Genuinely routeless turns still require an explicit target, and external-session routes retain precedence. External Markdown image blocking, permissions, and delivery transport are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

The shared reply-guidance detector only recognized external channel destinations. title: improve(ui): open Files directly in supported browsers
body:
Related: #180298.

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing File can reopen a media-source chooser when the user wants to browse files and document providers directly.

## User Impact

On browsers exposing direct file browsing, **Files** opens that route with unrestricted file types and multiple selection. Unknown extensions and `.stl` files use the normal attachment pipeline. Selection stages a draft; sending stays explicit.

**Scope:** this is the supported-browser Files contribution, not final cross-platform separation. Browsers without the direct API retain their existing File/Attach… route. The iPhone experience and final unsupported-browser UX remain reserved to #180298; no overlapping chooser is newly accepted as the desired fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mounted composer invokes `showOpenFilePicker()` from the user gesture, then uses the existing attachment admission, preparation, draft and send owners. Cancellation preserves the draft; failures report errors without silently opening a different chooser. Late results cannot populate a replacement draft or unmounted composer.

Image-only composers, arbitrary documents, file-provider access, upload policy, size checks, lazy camera registration and permission documentation remain intact. No file-type allowlist, custom filesystem browser, persistent handles, permission changes or deployment is introduced.

Proposed and directed by **Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit)**.

title: fix: avoid duplicate fallback notices in web chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: web chat shows both a model-transition divider and an extra assistant status message when fallback activates or the selected model recovers.

## User Impact

User impact: fallback and recovery remain visible in the transcript without an extra assistant reply bubble. DM notices, group/channel suppression, native-client delivery, provider-policy retry notices, and model selection are unchanged. No settings or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The structured transcript event already owns the web status presentation. Mark fallback/recovery companion payloads only when the existing transcript writer confirms the active-model event, carry that fact beside the existing answer-reconciliation marker, and omit only those confirmed assistant blocks in the existing Control UI normalization walk. Keep the transport payload intact for other clients; do not match notice wording or suppress all status messages.

title: improve(decisions): distinguish closing acknowledgments from missing context
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The conversational tool gate can retain optional tools for a closing acknowledgment because its context question asks about understanding prior references rather than the information needed to fulfill the current request.

## User Impact

Clarifies the existing missing-context rubric for completed-work acknowledgments while preserving tool requirements for pending actions, contextual approvals and unresolved references. The strict 0.35 cutoff, two independent Boolean questions, opt-in, explicit-answer/abstention vetoes, privacy projection, 500ms runtime budget and retain-tools fallback are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stack 2: foundation #182448 is now merged; this PR targets `main`. Landing authorized by @vincentkoc in the linked work session. Rubric version advances from 9 to 10. Offline tooling, reference cases and saved provider responses are in [openclaw/maintainers#294](https://github.com/openclaw/maintainers/pull/294), not the core product. The old evaluator stack #179185/#179187 is not needed.

The candidate was selected using independently authored synthetic tuning cases, then frozen before evaluating separate conversation groups. No broad task router, provider-specific default or global threshold configuration is introduced. The two changed rubric strings are the complete production behavior change; tests update the rubric-version contract and docs explain the distinction.

## Evidence

| Same strict 0.35 policy | Cases | Unsafe tool pruning | Unnecessary retention |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| v9 tuning | 24 | 0 | 1 |
| v10 tuning | 24 | 0 | 0 |
| v9 held-out | 12 | 0 | 0 |
| v10 held-out | 12 | 0 | 0 |

- Actual configured TypeSafe Decision-provider calls, one projected case per request, exact source rubric; no reference labels sent. Resolved model and all native scores/usage are retained in the companion capture artifacts.
- Counterexample T05-01: `Yes, thanks. That's all.` after a completed test run. Missing-context probability changed 0.36 → 0.07; tool-need probability remained 0.02. The actual two-question policy changes retained → proposed pruning at the unchanged cutoff.
- Held-out routing decisions tie. **No held-out accuracy gain, calibrated probabilities, production error-rate guarantee, latency or cost-savings claim.** These reference labels have not been human-adjudicated. The implementing agent could see held-out references, but they were not used to revise the frozen candidate.
- All 61 existing prefilter, registered-runtime prompt assembly and prefix-stability tests passed on the candidate (101.79s wrapper wall time, mostly compilation; CI seconds not yet available). Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings. Targeted lint/type/format/docs checks recorded on published head.
- Explicit `decision_evaluate` calls prove source-rubric/provider behavior, not the optional gate's 500ms admission or end-to-end primary-model success. A representative production/isolated-runtime evaluation is still needed before a general performance claim.

Requested by @vincentkoc in this task's discussion.

title: fix: custom DashScope providers miss Qwen hooks on first use
body:
Fixes #171853. The thinking-translation half already landed in #181638 and is unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: custom DashScope providers miss Qwen runtime hooks on first use when the plugin has not already loaded.

## User Impact

Custom providers on declared DashScope endpoints receive Qwen behavior on their first model turn. Explicit plugin disablement, allowlists, denylists, and declared provider/API-owner precedence remain authoritative. No new configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime already identifies the endpoint class, but neither manifest activation nor the prepared model-run generation included its owner. The existing activation planner now recognizes declared endpoint classes, and generation preparation uses that same planner before immutable runtime lookup. Late plugin loading remains forbidden within a captured run generation. There is no Qwen-specific core policy or new public API.

Credit: @steipete for the report and reliability campaign. The thinking-payload translation in #181638 is preserved unchanged.

- **Real separate-process Gateway:** Qwen absent before the public model request, imported during the request, exactly one loopback model request with serialized `enable_thinking: false`, and an HTTP 200 completed assistant reply. The built runtime is bound to commit 4964fa2f59eb932645fb8ae6b4479de0e3834cb8. All 25,724 copied regular build files matched except the two documented fixture changes: a Qwen import marker and the loopback endpoint declaration.

A stronger immutable-generation regression and separate Gateway control also failed on the initial planner-only repair: Qwen remained absent and the completed wire request lacked the thinking field. title: fix(codex): preserve cache when reasoning effort changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native Codex conversations rebuilding their request-level reasoning configuration when users change thinking level between turns. The built-in OpenAI Responses runtime already supports eligible cache-preserving changes; the bundled Codex 0.162.1 still defaults its native feature off.

## User Impact

Managed native Codex threads can use history-scoped reasoning changes on models whose Codex catalog supports them, including with native code mode disabled. Unsupported models and an explicit thread-config opt-out retain ordinary request-level effort. There is no dependency, schema, permission, or public configuration change.

The isolated live Gateway acceptance now passes with GPT-6.1 Sol and API-key authentication. Landing remains subject to exact-head CI and repository checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable Codex's existing reasoning_effort_override feature in the shared thread configuration, leaving eligibility, pinned effort, and replay entirely with Codex. This follows [upstream Codex #56163](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/56163). Latest stable [0.164.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.164.0) also has this flag off; upstream main enables it. Its prompt presets are a separate CLI feature and need no reasoning-cache adapter.

title: fix(slack): recover relay connections after silent network drops
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Slack relay accounts can remain connected but stop receiving messages indefinitely after their relay connection becomes unresponsive without closing.

## User Impact

User impact: an unresponsive relay connection is replaced automatically instead of leaving the account silently offline. Healthy idle connections stay connected; no operator action, configuration change, or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing WebSocket ping/pong keepalive in the relay connection owner. A missed pong terminates the socket and enters the existing recovery path, which still settles pending durable acceptance before reconnecting. Application silence is not a failure signal. Ordinary Slack Socket Mode and its SDK reconnect owner are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before editing, the actual production relay monitor connected to an owned loopback WebSocket blackhole with synthetic authentication and isolated empty state. On base `0a9d5cc49d911e587e78a0bc5600038a8d97f431`, it stayed connected for 80 seconds with zero pings and no recovery. With the fix, the heartbeat timeout triggered recovery and a replacement upgrade at 52,364 ms; the replacement accepted one synthetic routed event. This proof used Node 26.12.1 and the pinned `ws` 8.22.0.
- Both new loopback regressions failed on base because no client ping arrived. The initial fixed candidate passed all 13 relay tests, including existing durable settlement, TLS and proxy cases.
- Final head `6b77c8773070937ccfc097aa0ae3e7e60ecbbe3f`: the focused two-case liveness replay passed after the test-only lint repairs (21 ms / 9 ms test execution; 52.41 s command wall time, dominated by cold compilation). The 80-second proof and full 13-case suite were not repeated.

Formatting and whitespace checks passed. Independent P0–P2 autoreview was scoped-clean, including the complete settlement-owner implementation.

Limits: the loopback proof exercises the production relay transport owner directly, not a complete Gateway/model run or a live Slack/router deployment. title: feat(visitor-access): give invited guests a welcome session from their invitation
body:
Requested by @jalehman

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4ff43853-805b-4ab6-932c-1622ab5bb1d8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7e214f12-a6e0-48c1-88b0-f4b0577ef2d7)

Related: #182044, #182218, #182045 (guest onboarding item 4, including item 3's trigger)

## What Problem This Solves

An invited guest signs in to an empty Team: nothing says who invited them, why, how long their access lasts, or what they can do, and the inviter is not told they arrived.

## User Impact

User impact: the guest Control UI can call `visitor-access.welcome.ensure` on load (item 7) and open a guest-owned "Welcome, <name>" session. Its first message is agent-written: it greets the guest, mentions the inviter, includes the invitation note, gives the access expiry in UTC, and lists what the current guest role allows. The inviter sees the session in **Involving me** and gets an Inbox mention naming the guest. Staff and the Gateway owner get `not_applicable`. No configuration change; renewal keeps the session, and expiry or revocation leaves it in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pull method, pinned contract.** `visitor-access.welcome.ensure` (`{}`, scope `operator.sessions.write`, `profileAccess: "required"`) returns `not_applicable`, `pending { retryAfterMs }`, `ready { sessionKey, agentId, created }`, or `failed { retryable: true, message }`, exactly as pinned for item 7.
- **Invitation from the admitted grant, not caller facts.** A real trusted-proxy guest connection test showed the plugin handler's client carries `internal.operatorAccessAuthority.gatewayAccessGrant = { pluginId: "visitor-access", grantId }` (staff get `null`), so the invitation is selected by that `grantId`. The email/GitHub fallback is not needed; `findActiveInvitation` now takes the grant ID instead of an identity.
- **At most one session per grant.** The call reserves `agent:<agent>:dashboard:<uuid>` in the grant's onboarding record with `compareAndSetOnboarding` before creating anything; concurrent calls in the Gateway get `pending`. It then creates the session as the guest through the caller-bound `api.runtime.gateway.request("sessions.create")` (guest is `createdActor`, so role, agent and sandbox limits apply), appends the message, and marks onboarding `ready`. A retry or restart reuses the reserved key: `sessions.create` adopts the existing key and the message write replays by idempotency key.
- **Narrow host capability for the agent message.** Item 5's mention insert has no plugin surface, and `chat.inject` is admin-only without mentions. This adds `api.runtime.gateway.appendAgentMessage`: inside an authenticated person's RPC, bundled/trusted plugins can add one agent-authored message to a session that person may write (checked through the existing `sessions.send` session-mutation authorization and commit guard), with the caller as the Inbox sender. Text is normalized like typed chat input. The session-mutation commit guard is also passed into the transcript persistence itself, so authority that ends while the append waits for its target or write queue stops the row and its Inbox entry (ClawSweeper P1); this also tightens the existing `chat.inject` commit. The guest role is unchanged; a guest still cannot write other people's sessions through it.
- **Literal host-written text.** Gateway-authored agent messages (item 5's mention insert and the new capability) no longer parse model delivery directives, so a note like `Please test [[audio_as_voice]] replies.` keeps its bytes and mention offsets instead of failing setup on every retry (ClawSweeper finding). Model output keeps its existing directive handling.
- **New invitation, new welcome.** A non-continuous re-invite (after expiry or revocation) now starts onboarding at `pending` instead of inheriting the ended grant's progress, so the guest gets a new welcome session; the old one remains. Continuous renewal keeps `ready` as before.
- Accepted edge cases (documented in the README): if the guest deletes the welcome session, `ready` keeps reporting its key; the in-flight guard is per Gateway process, matching the existing single-Gateway policy assumption.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/server.visitor-welcome.test.ts` (real Gateway, trusted-proxy guest and staff connections, guest default role with `accessPolicyPlugin: "visitor-access"`): the guest handler sees its grant reference and staff see `null`; the session created through the caller-bound request has `createdActor` = the guest; `chat.history` shows an assistant message with the inviter's `humanMentions`; the inviter's `mentions.list` has the item with the guest as sender; a retry on the same key returns the same message ID; the guest cannot append to a staff session ("Session-scoped writes require your own session."); the stored message keeps a directive-like note literally; revoking the guest's real visitor grant at the moment the production transcript append starts (after its last pre-append caller check) leaves that session without a message and adds no Inbox entry. Without passing the commit guard into transcript persistence the same test fails with a second Inbox item; with it, it passes.
- `src/gateway/assistant-human-mentions.test.ts`: directive-like text stays literal with matching mention offsets (red on the previous head: the insert was rejected; green with the fix); a commit guard that starts failing once the transcript append has begun leaves no row and no Inbox entry (red without passing the guard to persistence, green with it).
- `extensions/visitor-access/src/welcome.test.ts`: method registration options, exact message text and mention span, `not_applicable` for staff/owner/unknown/expired/foreign grants, concurrent `pending`, failure then restart resuming the reserved key (one session, one message), a grant in the exact shape v2026.10.6 recorded (no inviter or onboarding) gets a generic welcome, with the existing `index.test.ts` upgrade case covering its load and CAS, renewal keeps the session, new invitation after expiry gets a new session.
- Fresh autoreview (Codex, P0–P1) on the branch and on the repair commit: no actionable findings.
- CI `pdf-tool.test.ts` "reports omitted images for a text-only model and supplies Codex instructions" (`systemPrompt` undefined), red on every PR head and on `main` (CI run 40078639310, `checks-node-compact-small-12`, at `ee855ce573`): root cause is #181356 (`f64e38f`), not this PR. The fixture was a bare `openai-chatgpt-responses` catalog row for a known model with only an API key; #181356 now treats that as a stale catalog and keeps the Platform contract, so the Codex instructions are dropped. Reverting that hunk alone makes the file pass (29/29). Test-only fix: the case now holds the OAuth subscription login a real Codex route requires. Red without it on the merged tree (Node and Bun, run alone), green with it: Node 29/29, Bun 29/29, and the exact CI shard include set (9 files, pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`, `bun-all`) 117/117. No production change.
- `pnpm test extensions/visitor-access` (102 passed), the gateway test file and `assistant-human-mentions.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files.

title: fix(memory-lancedb): stop expired recalls after cold provider startup

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes expired LanceDB recall queries starting or continuing after the caller has timed out when a cold embedding provider initializes slowly.

## User Impact

User impact: automatic recall and `memory_recall` no longer give provider-adapter embedding requests a fresh timeout after cold initialization consumes their existing 15-second budget. The direct OpenAI-client path is unchanged; no configuration, stored-data, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the adapter call's deadline before awaiting shared provider initialization, reject an expired query before dispatch, and give the existing abort timer only the remaining budget. Shared initialization may still finish for later operations; the provider creation API has no caller cancellation signal, and this change preserves shared provider ownership and retirement.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through plugin registration, its registered service start and `before_prompt_build` hook, real embedding-adapter/registry lookup, and a synthetic cold local provider. Both regressions fail on base `0a9d5cc49d911e587e78a0bc5600038a8d97f431`: after 10 seconds of initialization, the request remains active at 15 seconds; after 16 seconds of initialization, an already-expired prompt is dispatched. Both pass with this repair.

title: feat(ui): land invited guests on their welcome session
body:
Related: #182044 (guest onboarding record). The `visitor-access.welcome.ensure` plugin method is item 4, built in parallel against the same pinned contract.

Requested by @jalehman

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4ff43853-805b-4ab6-932c-1622ab5bb1d8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/518ee23e-23e3-47db-a7dc-4d72a5f6c312)

## What Problem This Solves

An invited guest who signs in lands on Home, and nothing sets up their welcome session or takes them to it.

## User Impact

User impact: on a Gateway whose Visitor Access plugin advertises `visitor-access.welcome.ensure`, an invited guest who opens the Control UI on Home is taken to their welcome session once per browser. While setup runs, the composer shows "Setting up your welcome session…". If setup fails, a non-blocking "We couldn't set up your welcome session" band offers Try again. Deep links, such as a session link in the invitation note, are never redirected. Team members, owners, and Gateways without the method see no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core has no first-sign-in hook (#182069 was closed), so the guest UI pulls. A small connection-scoped owner (`ui/src/app/guest-welcome.ts`) calls the method once per connected client, with params `{}`, when the caller is a restricted guest (the existing `isRestrictedSessionGuest`) and hello advertises the method. Its code loads only after a Gateway advertises the method, so other users' startup bundle is unchanged apart from a small handle. It handles the pinned results as follows:

- `not_applicable` is a no-op.
- `pending` polls with `retryAfterMs` clamped to 0.5–5 s. Setup still pending after 3 minutes becomes the retryable failure.
- `failed` and transport errors show the failure band. Try again calls the method again.
- `ready` redirects only while the browser still shows the default Home landing (or the session that startup restored for it), checked after startup finishes resolving that landing, so navigation in the meantime wins. The visit is recorded in local storage so Home stays reachable afterwards. If the browser cannot save that record (blocked or full storage), only the creating call (`created: true`) redirects.

A dropped connection abandons the poll and asks again on reconnect; the plugin owns idempotency. The band reuses the composer status lane from the approved mockup, so it appears beside the route's chat composer. On other pages the call runs quietly.

`bootstrap.ts` is at its line cap, so its existing route-location helper moved unchanged to `bootstrap-location.ts` to make room for the wiring.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/app/guest-welcome.test.ts` (13 tests) covers the state machine: a single call, once-per-browser landing, deep links, missing and readable-but-unwritable storage, the method absent or legacy, team members and admins, `not_applicable`, bounded polling, the pending timeout and retry, failure and transport errors with retry, and disconnect/reconnect.
- `ui/src/e2e/guest-welcome-landing.e2e.test.ts` (6 tests, mocked Gateway responses, production build) covers: a ready redirect from Home with no second redirect, no redirect from a deep link, pending then ready, failed then a transport error then retry (the sidebar stays usable meanwhile), the method absent, and a non-guest.
- `bootstrap-location.test.ts` adds a case where the guest navigates while startup is still resolving the landing; the redirect check then returns false.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` against the merge base passes: startup JS grows by 147 B gzip, total CSS by 59 B raw and 9 B gzip.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, stylelint, `check:control-ui-controllers`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety`, `ui:i18n:verify` and `ui:i18n:baseline` (no change) all pass. The existing `bootstrap.test.ts` and `session-owner-filter-guest-default.e2e.test.ts` pass.

Not covered: the real plugin method (item 4) and a live Gateway; this PR was built and tested against the pinned contract. No upgrade proof is included because nothing existing is read or migrated: the only stored state is a new `openclaw.guestWelcome.visited.v1:*` local-storage key, and a missing key means "not yet landed".
