title: fix(plugins): prevent config-only restarts from hanging reloads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: config reloads stop making progress when a restarted plugin service never finishes starting.

## User Impact

Config-only service restarts now use the existing five-second startup observation budget instead of blocking later reloads indefinitely. A timeout is reported in service health and closes scheduling and managed capability admission.

This does **not** forcibly terminate native plugin work: shutdown still waits for raw startup and physical cleanup. After cleanup, reload the plugin to retry the timed-out service. No stored config or state changes, migrations, or new configuration options are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config-only restart caller omitted candidate startup mode. Reusing the existing replacement path preserves raw-start custody and exactly-once final cleanup without introducing another timeout owner or cancellation protocol. Both immediate and deferred config-only restarts use this owner.

## Evidence

- Before editing, reproduced through actual startPluginServices().reload(), a managed PluginInstance, and a real GatewayScheduler with an owned late native listener. On the base, reload remained pending after 6,000 ms and scheduling was still open. With the fix, startup timed out at 5,000 ms, reload settled, and scheduling was aborted.
- In both runs, shutdown remained pending until raw startup was released; final cleanup ran once for that attempt and left zero listeners. The regression additionally proves a sibling reload can proceed after the timeout.
- New regression failed on the base and passed with the repair. Service-owner suites: **43 passed**; new regression: **7 ms**; wrapper wall time: **62.25 s**, mostly compilation.
- Gateway targeted service-reload consumer: **8 passed**, 103 filtered; wrapper wall time: **75.21 s**.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and git diff --check passed. Independent lifecycle autoreview includes the full owner source.
- Not exercised: full network Gateway/model session, stable-upgrade matrix, or broad build. CI seconds are pending hosted results.

title: fix: avoid partial history when opening hovered chats
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a hovered conversation starts with only a small history preview, then visibly expands when the normal history window arrives.

## User Impact

User impact: hovering or keyboard-focusing an inactive conversation warms the same recent history window used when opening it, so the warm view is not missing most of the initial page. Hover reads can now transfer up to 256 KiB instead of 64 KiB; the existing short intent delay, foreground-load priority, per-session cooldown, active-run exclusion, and bounded snapshot cache remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the separate 20-message / 64 KiB prefetch budget and its override parameter. The existing request owner now applies one 80-message / 256 KiB opening budget to both foreground and hover reads. This does not change request sharing, subscriptions, older-history paging, or live-run replay. Production code shrinks by four lines; the existing browser regression grows to cover a full budget-honoring window.

## Evidence

- Built-bundle Chromium reproduction: on the base, hover warms only items 61–80 of an 80-message transcript and the earliest opening-window message remains unavailable while startup is held. The same regression passes with the fix: items 1–80 are already available before startup returns, and the first message retains its exact vertical position after reconciliation.

title: fix(dev): preserve active replies when stopping the Gateway
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a development Gateway can be forcibly killed during shutdown or watcher replacement before its active reply finishes.

## User Impact

Developers can stop or replace a source-launched Gateway without the launcher cutting short its existing graceful-drain window. Ordinary commands and builds keep their short shutdown deadline. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source runner and outer watcher previously enforced five-second deadlines even though the Gateway permits longer active-work draining. Reuse the existing foreground-Gateway command parser and shared service stop budget, including the supervisor margin for the outer watcher and replacement wait. Preserve the existing narrow Mantis lifecycle-IPC authorization.

## Evidence

- Real `pnpm dev … gateway` entrypoint with an isolated Gateway, real agent run and a deterministic local provider serving a nine-second SSE response:
  - Before: forced exit 137 after **5.309s**, no final reply, zero persisted completion records.
  - After: requested SIGTERM exit 143 after **12.029s**, final reply delivered, graceful drain completed, one persisted completion record.

title: fix: keep v4 apps connected after widget retirement
body:
Related: #182109

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: existing protocol-v4 apps cannot connect after the A2UI retirement because the Gateway requires protocol v5.

## User Impact

User impact: existing apps, including OpenClaw for macOS 2026.10.3, can connect without an unnecessary app upgrade. The shipped v3 node/probe compatibility window remains available.

A2UI remains retired. Existing Doctor backup/removal behavior is unchanged; recreate retired widgets as HTML.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the connection protocol at v4. Retain the old registered-widget wire declarations for parsing, but reject retired widget puts with an actionable error before any board mutation. Restore the v3 node envelope, signing metadata, and session feature ceilings instead of treating v4 as the legacy dialect.

No renderer, plugin registration API, or persisted registered content is restored. The necessary production growth restores the shipped node compatibility path removed in #182109; it does not introduce another compatibility owner.

## Evidence

- A frozen v5-constants negative control reproduces the exact Mac handshake failure: client min/max 4, Gateway expectedProtocol 5. With this fix, the same authenticated WebSocket handshake and health RPC pass.
- Six focused Vitest shards pass, covering Gateway auth/negotiation, retired-widget rejection with unchanged stored state, v4 response parsing, client fallback/signing, node command policy, board persistence, dashboard output, and prompt-prefix stability.
- Production and affected package/Gateway test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Protocol registry/schema checks and deterministic Swift/Kotlin generation checks pass; Control UI validators regenerated.
- Independent review of the final extraction found no actionable P0–P2 findings; staged line-cap ratchet passes without exemptions.
- Final client regression run: 125 tests pass across three files, including three real-WebSocket v3 fallback cases (0.84 seconds of test time); 38.44 seconds wall time including worker compilation. CI timings will be supplied by the PR checks.

Rust workspace and TypeScript contracts passed in [Node Runtime Conformance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40067226115). This is Gateway handshake proof, not a native macOS app UI test. No live Gateway was modified or restarted.

### Inherited CI failures

CI run [40067226183](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40067226183) reports three pre-existing test failures. All three reproduce with the same failure on baseline `4dc5be9f02824634ba58edbe11f98f7d9ded1915`, using frozen dependencies and the captured failing shard inputs:

- [Scheduler E2E](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40067226183/job/120793227526): the test requests `openai/gpt-4.1` while its fixture permits only `mock-openai/scheduler-canary`.

title: fix(claude-cli): finish parent replies after nested background agents
body:
Closes #182175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI parent replies can remain in progress indefinitely after a background Agent launches another background task.

## User Impact

User impact: the parent reply finishes when its own background work settles, without waiting for a nested task's reply on the wrong stream. Top-level background work still keeps its parent reply open. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude identifies nested Agents and workflows with `parent_task_id`, but reserves `owned_by_subagent` for nested Bash tasks. Treat all tasks with a parent as owned by that subagent instead of inheriting ownership of the outer input. Keep the existing completion, replay, and watchdog policies unchanged.

The focused E2E test passed, and its owned Gateway and state were removed. Publication added a metadata-only commit; the published tree is identical to the tested tree.

title: fix: keep unchanged automation checks out of chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unchanged automation checks add conversational noise and obscure the last useful task update.

## User Impact

Automations stay quiet when nothing changes. The desktop and mobile sidebar retain the latest meaningful result, show when the job was checked, and clearly indicate a failed check. Actual results, errors, approvals, attachments, and explicitly requested recurring updates remain visible. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing structured automation result contract instead of guessing whether two messages mean the same thing. Persist meaningful results separately from check freshness, suppress only producer-marked execution inputs and check activity, and pass the previous result back as bounded context for the next check.

## Evidence

- Live and upgrade proof used `626d45b853d6c7c4053a5d53f87fdfc05fbe5183` (tree-identical to published `382f77e3face41130ed12bb6ec3a628457765d7d`). Subsequent CI repair only relocates an unchanged pure payload selector to remove an import cycle and corrects a transcript fixture; the previously proven runtime behavior is unchanged. Final persistent-session settlement regressions: **30/30 passed**, including meaningful results, quiet checks, pending continuations, error handling, and independent conversation publication after message-tool delivery. Core and messaging types, scoped lint/format, production build, and independent review passed.
- **Real isolated Gateway and production UI passed:** meaningful blocked/progress/done results appear; two unchanged checks preserve exact bubbles, unread state, preview, recency, and prior result. A due `fire:false` trigger advances Checked without inference. Desktop/mobile display, hover/focus, retained history, Run Inspector, persisted reload, and Gateway/provider shutdown passed.
- **Latest-stable upgrade passed:** real `2026.10.6` state was produced by the released package, backed up and verified, then opened with candidate Doctor. Original settings, job identity/owner, all 12 original transcript events and old run history survived. The same job produced a meaningful result and two silent checks. A new Gateway process and browser retained that result, complete old/new history, and exact quiet display state. No job recreation or authority bypass. This tests released-state replacement plus Doctor, not the installed updater driver.
- The earlier real OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini run returned structured `no_change`; that valid provider proof is reused rather than repeating paid inference. Earlier affected-boundary regressions and the UI performance gate remain passing evidence for unchanged inputs (CSS −218 bytes raw / +56 bytes gzip, within its allowance).
- **Known limitation:** Doctor warned that its additional pre-repair recovery copy could not open a database. The independent released-runtime backup was verified before migration, and exact settings/history preservation passed; this does not claim the extra-copy warning is fixed. An earlier intermittent fixture shutdown deadline also remains disclosed below.
- **CI repair proof:** 83/83 focused tests passed across five files, including all 16 destination-completion cases. Static and runtime import-cycle checks both report zero cycles; core and cron-test types, scoped lint/format, and independent P0–P2 review passed. The changed cron test file took 27.36 seconds wall time (including transform/setup). The prior CI failure was the old persistent fixture counting audit entries as visible replies; the corrected fixture preserves audit history and still requires exactly one visible result and one send after repeated dispatch. Fresh GitHub CI and native landing checks apply to the repaired head; publication is not a claim of merge.

- **Migrated-authority controls passed** on the preserved built candidate `626d45b853d6c7c4053a5d53f87fdfc05fbe5183`: disposable copies of the same `2026.10.6` archive were migrated by candidate Doctor, then the original device was revoked or the original conversation replaced. Running the same persisted job was rejected before any provider request, model-generated tool call, or visible transcript change. The revoked-device case also retained exactly all 12 raw transcript events; the reset case retained its intentional reset event. Both real Gateways and synthetic providers shut down cleanly. No new job, broadened grants, or paid inference.
- **Conflict and UI repair:** integrated main `64d17747dc13ee17007017ea5db2721b2e0cd7d1`; regenerated prompt snapshots with the owning generator, preserving both quiet-result metadata and `reasoning_effort_override`. The menu CI failure was reproduced with a real active tooltip consuming the first Escape. The three-line test repair moves the pointer to neutral menu padding and waits for tooltip retirement; one Escape must still remove the menu and restore its exact trigger. The forced reproduction changed from failing to passing, and the final case passed in Chromium (2.67 seconds wall time) and WebKit (4.62 seconds). Production menu/tooltip code is unchanged. An initial WebKit run hit a browser-session connection timeout; the run with explicit loopback proxy exclusion passed. Fresh five-file P0–P2 review found no actionable issues. After integration, all 26 inventory/snapshot owner tests, 30 automation-delivery/destination-completion cases, and 3 selected agent check-activity cases passed. The owning UI component typecheck, scoped UI lint (zero warnings/errors), and formatting passed.

- **Stream approval CI repair:** current-head CI `40126113196` exposed a real Gateway timeout after “allow once.” The retry rebuilt an otherwise identical watcher with a new creation timestamp, changing its derived operator-source revision and provoking a second approval. The responsible source is identical on the PR and its tested main parent. The repair carries the original proposal timestamp through the existing private approval and add-mutation path; scheduling and update time still use the current clock, and exact binding, live-authority, and transaction-held consumption checks are unchanged. The same real Gateway test changed from failing to passing (50.59 seconds wall, 18.77 seconds test), including one approval per case, allowed start/removal, denial, revocation, and existing activation/stale-authority controls. A fresh runtime build and full-context independent P0–P2 review passed. All 98 focused owner/integration tests passed (67 job/policy/approval-lifetime cases and 31 stream-approval cases), as did core, cron-test and gateway-root typechecks, eight-file lint (zero warnings/errors), and formatting. The stream-approval integration suite took 71.93 seconds wall time; it retains changed-policy reapproval, denied/expired/cancelled approval, revocation, changed executable, and sandbox guards. Final hosted [CI run 40128810161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40128810161) completed successfully on published head `655045e43f1210fb0dea7ae70796ede03e2f88fc`: 96 successful jobs, 20 intentionally skipped, and no failed or pending jobs. Native landing checks remain separate; passing CI is not a merge claim.

<details>
<summary>Redacted final-effect rejection output</summary>

```json
{"case":"revoked device","status":"error","error":"Restart recovery operator authority changed; start a new user turn.","providerRequests":0,"modelGeneratedToolCalls":0,"visibleMessagesBefore":6,"visibleMessagesAfter":6,"rawTranscriptBefore":12,"rawTranscriptAfter":12,"gatewayStopped":true,"providerStopped":true}
```

The same released job and captured source were retained through Doctor; neither negative case created a replacement job or expanded authority. These controls and the prior successful upgrade are built-candidate evidence; final integrated-head CI evidence is recorded separately above.

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

Reuses the existing structured result, cron state/history, session metadata publication, and display-state owners. Removes duplicate result/summary plumbing and shared-status rendering; adds no notification manager, text-deduplication heuristic, configuration option, or database migration. The smallest coherent stage is the complete producer-to-browser quiet-check flow: backend-only or UI-only changes leave observed chat or recency leaks. Necessary growth covers result persistence, shared status/freshness presentation, and regression proof.

The CI-only repair moves the unchanged pure payload selector into the existing low-level payload owner, removing the dependency edge rather than adding a workaround or another module. The scheduled transcript fixture retains stricter audit-versus-visible assertions. The conflict repair adds the menu test’s tooltip-free precondition and regenerates prompt snapshots. title: chore: validate a bounded Rust WASM media scanner
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Determine whether selective Rust/WASM work would help a real repeated media path, instead of porting helpers solely because they are portable.

Related source: https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2112804374531461546

## User Impact

No user-visible or runtime behavior changes. This is a **draft, validation-only experiment; do not merge or land**. The application, fs-safe policy, shared scanner, runtime dependencies, and default routes stay unchanged. The experiment is not imported or packaged by production code.

## Why This Change Was Made

Source tracing finds base64 validation on accepted attachments and several realtime media frame paths. Large chat payloads already run in the existing compute worker, so this is not a claimed fix for Gateway event-loop blocking. PCM downmix/channel loops were rejected as a port candidate: eliminating both would save only about 0.139% of one core per active bidirectional stream in the bounded 20 ms-frame workload.

The isolated base64 experiment compares the existing source, a simpler JS alphabet-table control, and a no-import Rust/WASM scanner through its complete JS adapter. One narrow experiment is enough; there is no production integration stack.

## Evidence

- Rust 1.99.1 / Node 26.12.1, Linux x64. WASM build and 24,038 differential calls per implementation passed, including dialect/padding/Unicode cases, invalid ABI spans, zero host imports, and memory ceiling checks.
- Final-script seven-sample interleaved medians at 1 MiB: **22.817 / 12.772 / 8.247 ms** (existing JS / JS table / Rust+adapter). At 16 MiB: **362.040 / 238.256 / 127.753 ms**. Includes conversion and JS result/normalization costs; not a pure-kernel benchmark.
- The simpler JS control also helps. WASM adds a linear-memory copy and retained about **22.94 MiB** after the largest input. These tradeoffs and busy-host load are explicit in the README; the complete promotion gate is **not passed**.
- Existing packages/media-core/src/base64.test.ts: **6 passed**. New experiment parity/bounds checks, targeted type-aware lint, formatter check, and git diff --check passed. Independent autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings; it reviewed source, not an independent benchmark reproduction.
- CPU profiles locate baseline scanner/alphabet work and candidate WASM work. README provides build, differential/benchmark, profile commands, workload counts, cold-instance limitations, and results.

**Gaps:** no live production usage telemetry, complete attachment/Gateway flow, browser/Bun/native-app runtime matrix, npm/static-asset packaging, or cold-process performance proof. Per-frame reach is conditional, not evidence of traffic volume. Seven samples do not establish robust p95/p99 latency. Do not promote this experiment as a shipped speedup.

Thanks @vincentkoc for directing and scoping the investigation.

Fixes missing hover cards when chat contains a GitHub commit link, even though the link already has the GitHub icon.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit readers were explicitly detail-only, and the shared hover eligibility gate excluded commit paths. Enable them through the existing preview descriptors, bounded GitHub metadata transport, scoped cache, and generic card rather than introducing another renderer or cache. Public repository admission and session-bound Enterprise authority remain unchanged. Only the existing supported commit paths are added; file, tree, compare, and Actions URLs keep their current behavior.

Requested by @steipete.

title: feat: add animated public link previews with a static fallback
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Public OpenClaw preview links currently offer only a still brand card, so clients that support video previews have no motion asset to use.

## User Impact

Generic `/share/chat/*` and `/share/dashboard/*` links advertise a lightweight, silent animation while retaining a readable PNG fallback. The landing page stays still by default and offers optional native playback without JavaScript. No conversation data or session-existence lookup enters the artwork.

X animation/autoplay is not guaranteed: X still receives a `summary_large_image` card, not an embeddable Player Card. Platform caching and client settings can retain the still. Session-specific public transcript cards and the separately deployed `openclaw.ai` homepage are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One fixed SVG scene supplies the poster and five-second, 1200 × 630 H.264 motion asset (83,544 bytes). The authored MP4 is copied with the UI; normal builds need no ffmpeg or new dependency. Existing public share routing and authentication boundaries are preserved.

The docs distinguish Open Graph video metadata from X Player Cards and describe deployment, caching, playback limitations, and artwork regeneration.

## Evidence

- Share-route regression failed on the original implementation and passes with the change, including configured base paths, anonymous GET/HEAD, MIME type, rejected writes, query privacy, and the static fallback.

- Isolated Gateway + Chromium proof covered actual MP4 playback, a 390-pixel viewport, reduced motion, no JavaScript, and blocked video requests with the still retained.
- Complete-scope independent source/media review found one font-cache invalidation defect; it is repaired at the build-cache owner with a regression that failed before the fix and passes after it (both cache locations). All 18 UI-wrapper tests pass.

The exact failing test was reproduced locally, failed before the repair, and passed after it; the production UI build, UI typecheck, targeted lint, and P0–P2 automated review of the repair pass. title: feat(visitor-access): add invite note and copyable invitation text
body:
Requested by @jalehman

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4ff43853-805b-4ab6-932c-1622ab5bb1d8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c884a094-40b0-448b-894b-86993d1f2efc)

Related: #182044

## What Problem This Solves

After `visitor_invite` succeeds, the inviting maintainer has no ready-made message for the guest and cannot attach a personal note, such as a session link to start from, through the tool.

## User Impact

User impact: `visitor_invite` accepts an optional `note` (at most 1000 characters), and every successful invite or renewal returns short plain `invitationText` the agent can hand to the guest: who invited them (display name when known), where to sign in, which email or GitHub account to use, the expiry in UTC, and the note. Renewal without `note` keeps the stored note, as #182044 defined. There is no pending-share feature; a session link goes only in the note.

The sign-in address now comes from `gateway.publicOrigin` (plus `gateway.controlUi.basePath`) instead of the hard-coded `https://team.openclaw.ai`. Team already sets `publicOrigin` to that address, so its links are unchanged. Without a public origin, or with the Control UI disabled, `signInUrl` is omitted, the tool text names the missing setting, and the invitation text asks the guest to get the sign-in address from the inviter.

Example:

```text
Josh invited you to OpenClaw.
Sign in at https://team.openclaw.ai with your GitHub account @octocat.
Your access expires on 2026-11-07 12:00 UTC.

Note from Josh:
Start in https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/welcome
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin already parsed and stored `note` (#182044); this exposes it in the tool schema with the same limit and description. Invite result formatting moves from `visitors.ts` into `src/invite-result.ts`, which builds the details and text from the committed grant. The note is stored once and appears only in the invitation text; details carry `noteStored`, not a separate copy. The invitation text includes no grant ID, tokens, or other credentials. The sign-in address follows the same `publicOrigin`/Control UI rule as other external Control UI links, using the SDK's `resolveGatewayPublicOrigin`. No new config was added.

Wording of the invitation text is a product choice; it is plain, five lines or fewer, and easy to change in one function.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/visitor-access`: 5 files, 95 tests passed. New coverage: note schema acceptance and 1000-character rejection, sign-in URL resolution (origin, base path, disabled Control UI, invalid origin, missing), invitation text with and without a note, renewal keeping the note in the text, missing public URL fallback, and the registered plugin reading `gateway.publicOrigin` and the inviter's display name.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- oxlint on `extensions/visitor-access` and oxfmt check on changed files: clean. `pnpm format:docs:check`: clean.
- Autoreview (Codex, P1, branch vs `origin/main`): scoped-clean.
- Gap: no live Cloudflare or Team Gateway run; this PR does not deploy or restart anything. The registered-plugin tests run the real tool, state store, and runtime config path with a stubbed Cloudflare API.

title: fix(x): preserve requester ownership and credit for linked senders
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: work requested through X can remain agent-owned and omit the requesting person's Git credit even when that sender belongs to a Gateway profile.

## User Impact

User impact: administrator-linked X requesters are recognized on subsequent turns, receive eligible Git coauthor credit, and become the default owner of new visible work unless a different human owns the parent.

An administrator must link the immutable X sender ID to the existing profile using the exact configured account ID. Allowlist entries and handles do not establish this link. Existing creators, assignments, permissions, sandboxing, and sharing are not rewritten. No schema migration or new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

X polling and Activity streams already obtain native author IDs through the authenticated API, but ingress did not declare that evidence. Use the existing canonical channel-link resolver, retain remote provenance alongside the linked person's contribution, and carry causal requester identity separately from administrator authority. The creation owner uses that trusted identity rather than defaulting channel-originated tasks to the agent.

Requested by @vincentkoc; implemented and verified with their direction.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f60aeb69-6ff4-4d2f-bfbe-cf69d5f02f80)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/bb130bc1-2d60-4ce3-a94e-307ecae4ef46)

## Evidence

- Red on the original production source, green with this patch: linked X requester propagation, nonadmin causal attribution, and default visible-child ownership from a channel parent.
- Host-backed X integration exercises native ingress, account-scoped links, session initialization, participant persistence/readback, and exact Git coauthor output. Linked, unlinked, asserted, and wrong-account cases are covered; remote provenance is retained. The new test takes about 2 seconds (8.18 seconds including warm runner setup).
- Passed: hosted creation/custody (24 tests), X monitor/authority (47 tests), channel authority/negative cases, owner/creator contracts, in-process creation, visible spawning, and prompt-prefix stability.
- Passed: core and X typechecks, five affected test typecheck graphs, targeted lint/format, line-budget gates, documentation link audit, and git diff --check. Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview was scoped-clean.
- Known local inherited failure: 38 queued-owner cases encounter the fixed /tmp/session-store.default.sqlite fixture at schema 31. A representative failure was reproduced identically with all production changes removed. That unrelated fixture was not migrated or deleted; this is not an attribution of any future CI failure.
- CI found a test-only TypeScript graph boundary violation on the initial head: a type import pulled bundled X sources into a core graph. Replaced it with the existing dynamic facade loader’s narrow consumer contract. The unchanged X behavioral regression, affected test typecheck, lint, and exact `lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary` check pass; the repair received fresh scoped-clean review.
- CI also caught a selected-participant ownership regression. Restored existing selected-operator responsibility precedence while retaining linked nonadmin requester fallback and independent causal creator credit. The failing production-boundary case reproduced locally before the repair; `pnpm test:ci-failed 182213 --run` then passed all 79 tests, and X/in-process sibling tests, core typecheck, lint, and fresh independent review passed.
- The separate, non-required [Rust workspace check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40064724897/job/120785453680) fails Clippy’s 100-line limit in `native_signed_connect_preserves_product_fields_and_rejects_invalid_node_manifests` (111 lines). The enforced `openclaw/ci-gate` remains independently required.
- No live X API/model run, deployment, or live identity-link change was performed. Broad validation is left to PR CI.

title: fix(ci): changed-test shards fail when a PR touches the Control UI E2E helper
body:
Related: #182101

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PR CI fails `checks-node-changed-*` with "No test files found, exiting with code 1" whenever a PR changes `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts` (for example #182040, [job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40060467019/job/120772977620)).

## User Impact

User impact: PRs that touch the shared Control UI E2E helper, or the retention census itself, no longer fail `ci-gate` on a test that ordinary CI cannot run. No product behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

#182101 added `scripts/control-ui-retention/dependency-retention.test.ts`, which imports the E2E helper. The changed-test picker's tooling import graph scans `scripts/`, so it selected that file as an import consumer. The file is an opt-in census with its own `scripts/control-ui-retention/vitest.config.ts` ("no long-session loops in ordinary CI"); nothing in PR CI owns it, so it fell through to `vitest.unit.config.ts`, whose include set does not contain it.

The picker now accepts only test files under the roots whose tests have ordinary PR Vitest owners (`src`, `test`, `extensions`, `packages`, `ui`), the same root list it already uses for its test inventory. Files elsewhere keep their own config and command. Today the only tracked test file outside those roots, apart from CodeQL fixtures, is the retention census. #182101's tests are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on clean `origin/main` (971a24242d71b): `createChangedNodeTestShards(["ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts"])` put `scripts/control-ui-retention/dependency-retention.test.ts` in `checks-node-changed-1`. With this change the same call plans the remaining targets and no longer selects the census.
- New regression test in `test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.selection.test.ts` (aggressive and full modes, helper change and direct census change). It fails on the base (`expected [ …(2) ] to not include 'scripts/control-ui-retention/dependen…'`) and passes with the fix.

title: fix: reject invalid worktree names before creating subagents

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a subagent can be accepted and then fail before replying when its managed worktree name includes a branch prefix such as `codex/qa-telemetry-prompt-cache-20261016`.

## User Impact

Invalid names are rejected before a child or work reservation is created, so callers can correct the name and retry without leaving a failed child. Pass a lowercase slug; OpenClaw supplies the branch prefix. Valid-name preparation remains asynchronous. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing strict naming validator at tool and direct native-spawn admission, and expose the same pattern in the tool schema. Explicit invalid names are not normalized. Clarify managed-name versus Git-branch guidance, and keep the existing visible-option checks beside their schema.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guests signed in through Visitor Access see empty-chat and New Session starter prompts such as "Help me configure a channel" and "Check system health", which need operator permissions their role does not have.

## User Impact

User impact: guests (session-scoped grants without `operator.write`) now see starter prompts that fit their access: asking what Roboclaw can do, touring OpenClaw's code and docs, investigating an issue in a sandbox, and fixing a bug in a draft PR. Operators and admins keep the same four prompts as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The welcome block shared by the empty chat and the New Session page rendered one fixed prompt list. It now picks the list from the connected principal's `hello.auth` grant with the existing `hasOperatorWriteAccess` check. The Visitor Access guest policy grants only `operator.sessions.write` (or `operator.sessions.read`), never `operator.write`, so guests get the session-scoped list. Missing auth keeps the operator list, the same way `operator-access.ts` treats legacy snapshots.

Unchanged: the welcome block still shows prompts only when there are no recent chats on that agent.

title: fix: resume completed-task follow-ups after a Gateway restart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a fresh human follow-up in a completed task session cannot resume automatically after a Gateway restart because its recovery source was discarded.

## User Impact

Already-authorized follow-up work can resume from its saved history without another instruction or approval. Current identity, permissions, revocation checks, and the original completion destination remain enforced. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the follow-up’s fresh operator source in the existing registry owner, targeting the exact child session and task rather than borrowing the completed parent’s grant. Restore that source through the child’s session store; preserve the existing parent-target recovery path and completion routing. Add the requested one-line restart-continuation rule to AGENTS.md.

This reuses existing recovery state and admission instead of introducing a second recovery route. Production code grows by 28 net lines; the additional integration coverage checks admission, durable recovery, unrelated-source rejection, and a second restart. Identity-rotating compaction remains a separate, pre-existing limitation; this change does not claim to fix it.

## Evidence

- Authenticated chat admission, cold registry reload, exact-source rejection, and a second restart preserving the task identity are covered through production owners with fixed model I/O.

title: fix: recover queued Codex chats and preserve startup failures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes queued Codex chats staying at “Waiting for turn to start…” after a plugin reload, and startup failures or cancellations being replaced by terminal-accounting errors.

## User Impact

A chat whose old thread already unloaded can resume without waiting for unrelated chats to release the retired Codex process. Startup errors retain their intended reply, and cancellation remains cancellation. Still-loaded threads, genuine session/writer replacements, and active ownership remain fenced; execution is not replayed. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the turn's already-claimed writer through rejected and aborted outcomes. For the separate Codex startup wait, recover a missed closure receipt with one metadata-only read from the exact old client: only a matching thread with `notLoaded` status permits handoff. Native resume still enforces its exclusive persistence writer lock. Process exit, exact closure, and cancellation retain their existing ownership and cleanup paths.

Incorporates @jjjhenriksen's follow-up [#182161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182161) at `2ebd4018179148e3b8fc8faf592050bc79d4af9d`, with an additional real-native regression and updated runtime documentation.

Thanks @jjjhenriksen for the report and reproduction direction.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/fb2548de-8e54-4f34-a3f1-ff4203259127)

## Evidence

- **Original accounting proof retained:** 128 focused tests passed across six suites. Both queued-startup failure and cancellation regressions fail on original source with `Terminal accounting session changed` and pass with retained writer facts. Replacement-session/lifecycle/writer guards remain intact.
- **Codex verification:** 202 tests pass across six lifecycle/client suites, including the imported handoff cases, configured MCP ownership, and two native-binary suites.
- **Real Codex 0.162.1 proof:** start a target and sibling on the old process; complete a real target turn against a credential-free loopback provider; unload the target before installing closure tracking; retire the old client while retaining a sibling lease; resume the same target through `startOrResumeThread` on a second real process and complete its next turn. A loaded sibling remains fenced and completes another turn on the old process while that handoff waits; cancelling only the wait leaves the old client alive. Exactly three loopback model requests complete, with no operator credentials or OpenAI service calls.
- **Red/green:** the native scenario fails against the pre-follow-up handoff implementation at its 20-second deadline; the patched native case passes in 1.1 seconds. The six-suite Codex invocation took 77.1 seconds wall time. A standalone native proof took about 15.5 seconds wall time including harness startup; CI timing for this combined head is pending.
- Canonical extension production typecheck, targeted changed-test typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Auto Review of the combined patch: scoped clean at its default P0 threshold.
- Four production files total (+44/-14 lines). No new state owner, retry loop, or compatibility layer; the additional native test covers the external shutdown/status/resume contract rather than duplicating the fake-transport cases.

<details>
<summary>Native contract inspection and verification limits</summary>

Personally inspected the pinned [Codex 0.162.1 source](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d): `app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs` (`thread/read`), `thread_lifecycle.rs` (shutdown and closure notification), and `thread-store/src/local/live_writer.rs` (resume's writer lock).

This proves the native missed-closure startup mechanism in isolation, not deployment to the affected live Gateway, the complete six-minute incident, or remote OpenAI service behavior. The prior standalone root test command's worker-compilation interruption remains non-verdict evidence; successful runs use the supported repository Vitest entrypoint. An initial package-boundary typecheck selected without its build prerequisites failed setup; the canonical extension/type-aware gates above passed. Documentation link audit reported 15,867 checked links and zero broken links, but its runner aborted after that summary, so a clean audit exit is not claimed.

</details>

title: feat(plugins): let plugins react when a verified person first signs in
body:
Related: guest onboarding (first-sign-in trigger, item 3 of the guest-onboarding project)

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins have no trustworthy signal that a person has just signed in to the Gateway for the first time, so a guest who signs in with a visitor invitation lands in Home with nothing set up for them.

## User Impact

User impact: no visible change on its own. Plugins can now register `api.on("user_first_sign_in", handler)` and receive one event per person after their first verified, admitted sign-in, with the profile id, display name, verified emails and GitHub account ids, and whether the profile is new. The follow-up visitor-access change uses it to create a guest's welcome session.

Delivery never blocks or fails sign-in, and it is at least once per handler plugin, so **handlers must be idempotent**. Profiles that existed before this change get one event on their next sign-in, with `isNewProfile: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway sign-in paths (HTTP request auth and the Control UI WebSocket connect, including deferred GitHub identity attachment) report an admitted sign-in to one owner, `src/gateway/user-first-sign-in.ts`, after the profile is durable and access policies have passed. Only trusted-proxy and Tailscale identities count; shared-secret operators, the Gateway owner profile, paired devices and nodes never do.

The owner records the first sign-in in the existing core plugin-state store (`core:user-sign-in`, retained namespace, no schema change), together with the plugins that had handlers at that moment. Each plugin's delivery stays pending until its handler resolves: failures and 60-second timeouts retry with backoff (5 s doubling, capped at one hour), and pending deliveries resume after `gateway_start` on the next Gateway start. Without any registered handler nothing is recorded, so Gateways without consumers do no extra work. Repeated sign-ins in one process skip the store after the first check.

To stay within the `hook-types.ts` line cap, the private channel-pairing hook types moved unchanged to `hook-channel-pairing.types.ts`. Docs: `docs/plugins/hooks/lifecycle.md#first-sign-in`, the hook reference table, and the SDK events overview.

When an administrator merges profiles, the merge target inherits the merged-in profile's first-sign-in record and any pending deliveries, so a merge never produces a second first-sign-in event.

Storage compatibility: no schema version, migration, or table change. Records live in the existing `plugin_state_entries` table under a new core-owned namespace, so existing databases load unchanged; profiles from before this change carry no record and receive one event on their next sign-in with `isNewProfile: false` (covered by tests).

Accepted edge cases: a plugin registered after someone's first sign-in does not receive it, and `isNewProfile` means "created at most one minute before the first sign-in".

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/user-first-sign-in.test.ts` (9 tests, real state database): fires once across repeated sign-ins and simulated restarts; a failing handler is retried after restart without redelivering to plugins that succeeded; in-process backoff retry; sign-in never waits on the handler; existing profiles report `isNewProfile: false` and late plugins are skipped; after `users.merge` the target keeps the merged-in profile's history and pending delivery (red without the merge handling); a real Cloudflare Access trusted-proxy HTTP sign-in delivers the verified email and GitHub account 101; a person denied by an access-policy plugin and a shared-secret operator record nothing; unverified auth methods record nothing.
- `src/gateway/server.auth.first-sign-in.test.ts`: a real Gateway server with trusted-proxy auth; two Control UI WebSocket sign-ins produce exactly one event. Removing the WebSocket call site makes this test fail.

title: feat(gateway): let Gateway-authored agent messages mention people
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway features cannot add an agent message that @mentions a person. The planned guest welcome message needs to mention the inviter so they get an Inbox entry and the welcome session shows up under **Involving me**, but today only a human's own typed chat message can carry a mention, and the Control UI only renders mention chips in human messages.

## User Impact

No visible change on its own. This adds a trusted, Gateway-internal way to insert an agent message that mentions people on behalf of a signed-in profile, for the guest-onboarding welcome message (item 4) to use. When that runs, the mentioned person gets an Inbox entry ("<Guest> mentioned you") and the session appears in their Involving me list, and the agent's message shows the same person chip as a typed mention. No client or guest can request these messages, and who can create mentions from the client is unchanged.

This is item 5 of guest onboarding. Session creation, the welcome text and the first-sign-in trigger are separate PRs.

## Why This Change Was Made

`injectAssistantMessageWithHumanMentions` (`src/gateway/assistant-human-mentions.ts`) is called by Gateway code only, with no RPC method. It reuses the existing owners instead of adding a new mention path:

- Spans are checked with the same normalizer `chat.send` uses. A mention of the sender and incognito sessions are rejected before anything is written.
- The row is written through the existing `chat.inject` implementation, with `__openclaw.humanMentions` like a human message. That implementation moved unchanged into `chat-inject.ts` so both callers share it. It returns a result instead of responding, and it skips the live broadcast on an idempotent replay.
- After the write, the committed row goes to the existing Mention Inbox. The Inbox applies the current recipient policy (the recipient can read the session, is not the sender, and the session is not incognito) and records involvement and the Inbox entry, with the on-behalf-of profile as sender.
- The caller's idempotency key becomes both the transcript idempotency key and the Inbox source id. A retry replays the same row. If an earlier attempt stopped before Inbox delivery, the retry finishes it, without a second row, broadcast or alert.

In the Control UI, a chat bubble now accepts structured mentions on assistant rows as well as user rows. It uses the same span validation and the same person-reference component.

Accepted edge case: if a recipient can't read the session when the message is inserted, the message still keeps the chip in its text, but that person gets no Inbox entry or involvement. This is the same delivery-time check the Inbox already uses for typed mentions.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/assistant-human-mentions.test.ts` (real SQLite transcript, session store and Mention Inbox; 9 tests). It checks one assistant row with `humanMentions`, one Inbox entry from the on-behalf-of profile, recorded involvement, and a chat broadcast that carries the mention metadata. A retry returns `replayed` with no new row, broadcast or alert. An interrupted delivery is completed on retry. A recipient who can't read the session gets nothing. Self-mention, a span without an `@label`, no mentions, untrimmed text, a missing key and incognito sessions are all rejected before writing.
- `chat-message-markdown.test.tsx`: a Gateway-authored assistant row now renders the person chip. It rendered none on `origin/main`, where this case expected no chip. Tool results still render none. Existing `chat.inject` suites (`chat.directive-tags`, `chat.inject.parentid`) pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, plus oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, all pass. An independent review (autoreview, branch vs `origin/main`) found no actionable issues.

- Test-only change in `chat-send-message-injection.isolated-gateway.test.ts`: the durable-steer test bounded its first `chat.send` at 1s, and that call timed out twice in Bun CI shard `agentic-gateway-methods-hosted-7` (its Gateway import alone took 27s). The other five tests in the file passed in the same process. The test now uses the default RPC timeout. It still fails if the acknowledgement waits for injection, because the older input is retired only after both sends. On a quiet local machine, the first `chat.send` took 4058ms and 1152ms on `origin/main`, against 1129ms and 515ms on this branch, so 1s is too tight on main as well. Importing `server-methods/chat.ts` under Bun took 1442–2149ms with this split and 1504–2104ms on the base, so the `chat-inject.ts` extraction does not slow loading. After the change the whole file passes 6/6 under both Node and Bun.

Screenshots: mocked Control UI, a Gateway-authored welcome message for guest Sam that mentions inviter Josh (synthetic data).

After

title: feat(visitor-access): retain invitation onboarding metadata
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guest invitations need durable inviter and setup metadata so first-sign-in welcome sessions can be created once and recovered after a restart.

## User Impact

Invitations record the authenticated inviter when available, and renewals preserve existing notes and onboarding progress. Older grants continue to work without these fields. This is item 1 of guest onboarding: note tool input, welcome-session creation, and guest UI changes are separate follow-ups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing SQLite-backed grant store and its service mutation queue instead of introducing another store or setup owner. New invitations start pending. Plugin-internal lookup and compare-and-set methods let setup reserve a stable welcome-session key before creation; pending-to-pending updates advance their comparison timestamp even within one millisecond. Inviter attribution uses the trusted Gateway users.self request, never tool input or session ownership.

The simplification pass kept grant decisions in the existing service and moved record/input definitions out of the near-limit service file. Against the base: production +267/−71 lines; tests and test support +300/−4; documentation +31. No SQL schema migration or access-policy change.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/visitor-access --maxWorkers=1`: 103 tests passed, including registered-plugin SQLite persistence/restart/renewal, legacy grants, concurrent onboarding reservations, and caller-lifetime rejection.

On a copy, this head's built CLI ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` (isolated `HOME`/state/config; exit 0, pre-migration backup saved, state schema 31 with 0 pending). title: feat(ui): start guests on the Involving me session filter
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Invited guests land in the Control UI with the sidebar filtered to "My sessions", so the sessions they were brought in for (for example a welcome session where their inviter is mentioned, or a team session that involves them) are hidden until they find the owner filter.

## User Impact

Guests with no saved sidebar owner choice now start on **Involving me**. A saved choice, or any choice they make later, is kept and persisted as before. Team members, admins and shared-token operators keep the existing "My sessions" default.

## Why This Change Was Made

No explicit visitor/guest flag reaches the Control UI today. Instead of adding a protocol field, the UI reads permission facts the Gateway already sends in `hello.auth`: a role-limited `sessionCap` of `view` and no `operator.read` scope. That is the restricted role shape Visitor Access requires (`isRestrictedVisitorRole`: view-only access to other people's sessions, `operator.sessions.*` scopes only). The check (`isRestrictedSessionGuest`) only picks the default the sidebar shows; the Gateway still decides all access.

Accepted edge case: a non-Visitor Access role configured with that same view-only, session-only shape also gets the Involving me default. Those users are guests in every practical sense, and they can switch filters as usual.

The default is computed, not stored, so a guest who is later given a team role gets the normal default unless they have chosen one themselves.

To keep `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts` under its line-cap ratchet while adding the mock's `operatorSessionCap` option, its session URL helpers moved unchanged into `control-ui-e2e-session-urls.ts`, which it re-exports.

## Evidence

- New Control UI e2e (`session-owner-filter-guest-default.e2e.test.ts`): a guest hello (`operator.sessions.write`, `sessionCap: "view"`) starts on Involving me and requests `sessions.list` with `involvingMe: true`; choosing My sessions persists across reload, and choices saved in the existing storage format (`all`, `owner:<id>`, `involving-me`) still win over the guest default after reload. The storage key and value format are unchanged by this PR, so preferences saved by earlier releases load as before. The test fails on `origin/main` (label stays "Owners: My sessions") and passes with this change. The existing owner-filter header e2e also passes.
- Unit tests (`session-owner-filter.test.ts`): guest without a saved choice gets Involving me and nothing is written to storage; saved choices (own, another owner, all) are kept; team member, write role, admin and legacy hello keep the own-sessions default. Red on base for the guest default, green with the change. Related sidebar and operator-access suites pass (6 files, 92 tests).
- Upgrade compatibility: this PR does not change what is stored. The preference key (`openclaw.control.sidebarSessionOwnerFilter.v1:<gateway>:<profile>`), the stored values and `storeSidebarSessionOwnerFilter` are untouched; only the fallback for a missing value changes. The e2e therefore seeds the exact values current releases write and checks that each still wins after reload, which is the code path an upgraded browser takes. A separate latest-stable-to-head browser run would exercise the same read path, so I did not add one.
- Docs: the session owner filter section of `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` now describes the guest default; `pnpm check:docs` passes.
- CI: earlier heads failed `checks-ui-e2e` in `sidebar-complete-roster`, `chat-workspace-directory-race`, `chat-file-links`, `chat-workspace-downloads` and `session-management.operator-scopes`. The same 8 tests failed locally on base `2fc557a9fb060` without this change. The branch now includes current `main` (with #182089, which restores the `sidebar-complete-roster` fixture), and those five files plus the new guest test pass locally (6 files, 21 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, and the line-cap ratchet pass. An independent review (autoreview, branch vs `origin/main`, P0–P2) found no actionable issues.

Screenshots: guest Sam, with no saved filter, opens their welcome session in the mocked Control UI.

After

title: fix: show recovery steps for oversized sandbox artifacts
body:
Related: #181143

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local sandbox session blocked by an oversized generated file reports only a size error, without explaining the administrator recovery that is already available.

## User Impact

User impact: eligible local-workspace failures now show the exact, shell-quoted `openclaw sandbox recover --session … --path …` command, say that pending changes were preserved, and direct the user to a Gateway administrator. Recovery remains an explicit administrator action; this change does not move or delete files automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery operation from #181143 already preserves oversized artifacts, but the preparation failure did not make it discoverable. The local workspace owner now reuses that operation’s existing eligibility checks before adding guidance. Remote failures, already-admitted source files, linked files, and staged results retain their original errors rather than receiving an unsupported recovery promise. Size limits, live-authority checks, and recovery behavior are unchanged.

The added guidance needs a read-only inspection at the existing leased owner boundary; sharing the eligibility check removes duplicate recovery policy rather than introducing another recovery API or configuration.

Reported by @TheAngryPit. Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8b0fe914-1075-447a-927f-09e56da2853f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f2027472-eb06-4498-a8c2-012b0d430166)

## Evidence

- Red on the pinned base: the real local sandbox preparation regression received only `Cloud workspace result is too large: …`, not recovery guidance.
- Green with the change: an isolated Git/SQLite workspace retains the oversized file and source edits across repeated preparation failures, shows a correctly quoted path containing spaces and an apostrophe, completes explicit recovery, and prepares again. Admitted source files and hardlinked files do not receive recovery advice.
- Three relevant suites: 66 passed, 1 opt-in Podman test skipped. The real isolated Gateway/paired-client checks deny write-only, revoked, replaced-session, and rebound-worktree recovery, then verify preserved bytes and source edits for an authorized administrator.
- Targeted lint, gateway-worker typecheck, formatting, documentation MDX, and documentation links checked. Fresh independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- Hosted CI: [run 40045096959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40045096959), attempt 1, tested merge `5c60212269d100ffc5da8ee934518da70441b436` (base `24adbb81e0a36cbac79446ce603ccf3c46b84c64`, PR head `78b6481b8548c11e145eb411c867000c94cd613f`). The leaf job and aggregate CI gate remain red; no hosted rerun or green-CI claim.
- Source-supported inherited attribution: the failing assertion requires a fresh advisory display immediately after the committed move. [The existing maintainer decision in #177581](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177581#issuecomment-6274825170) explicitly accepts a stale display snapshot until a later publication/invalidation/refresh/restart and declines restoration of that freshness mechanism. The fixture, these read/write owners, package manifest, and lockfile are byte-identical between the exact tested base and merge. title: fix: distinguish publication policy refusals from credential failures

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading publication recovery advice when a contributor inspects a bot-authored PR or OpenClaw refuses changes to GitHub Actions workflows.

## User Impact

Contributors can distinguish a linked-author check or an OpenClaw requester-permission refusal from broken publisher credentials, without reconnecting a working account or broadening token permissions unnecessarily. No authorization, identity, private-repository access, or workflow-write policy is relaxed.

The own-PR inspection path now explains that it checks the requesting person's linked authorship, not the managed publisher's credentials, and points to the existing `edit` or `publish` action as appropriate. Private or unverified PRs keep the existing nondisclosing failure. The workflow refusal names OpenClaw's full operator-write requirement rather than leaving the failure open to interpretation as missing GitHub token scopes.

title: fix: expose saved dashboards in session inventory
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: authorized session cleanup cannot distinguish sessions without saved dashboards from unknown dashboard state because the agent-facing inventory omits existing Gateway metadata.

## User Impact

Agents can filter visible sessions by saved-dashboard presence without reading dashboard contents. Missing metadata stays unknown, never empty. Existing session visibility, sharing, incognito exclusions, archival permissions, and pagination bounds are unchanged; there is no migration or new configuration.

Deployment requires a build containing this change and a fresh tool-definition turn/session. No deployment, restart, or live archival is performed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already owns the boolean `hasBoard` and its pre-pagination filter. This patch passes those existing contracts through `sessions_list` instead of adding a dashboard reader, new database state, or broader access. A saved tab counts even without widgets; a saved dashboard face alone does not.

Existing timestamps, run metadata, permitted history/search, and live PR state are sufficient for conservative qualification. Documentation requires completed-work evidence, preserving active/queued or ambiguous work and refreshing candidates before archival. Inventory observations are not atomic archive preconditions.

Simplification review retained the existing owner: production +6/−2 lines, behavior tests +75/−1, documentation +4. Generated prompt artifacts add a separate mechanical +18/−15 delta. Remaining growth exposes one existing fact and protects tool projection, visibility, pagination, and stored-tab behavior; no parallel machinery was introduced.

## Evidence

- Regression-first check: three expected failures on the original implementation.
- Focused inventory/query/projection/privacy/description tests passed (103.26s command wall time).
- Real agent-tool `→` Gateway handler `→` stored/resident-row proof passed over 3,474 rows, including a saved tab with no widgets, explicit no-board rows, both filters, and pagination. Gateway test body: 5.327s.
- Before base integration, the Gateway/query/prefix-stability command passed (126.41s wall time, including cold compilation); prefix stability 8/8 passed.
- Targeted TypeScript, production/test lint, formatting, docs MDX, and `git diff --check` passed.
- ClawSweeper’s P2 snapshot drift was reproduced and repaired using `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. Three canonical artifacts changed; `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` passes all six files on the integrated tree (34.00s), with formatting and scoped whitespace checks passing. No generator, baseline policy, or production behavior was weakened.
- Integrated verified main `377c0fcb1f106b6ebda3f069d554d1d64732998b` for the named failing UI gate; it includes upstream fixture fixes #182056 and #182067. Frozen dependencies were reconciled. On this tree, all 47 focused inventory/Gateway/prefix tests passed (121.07s command wall time), and targeted TypeScript passed. No local UI rerun is claimed here.
- Independent Codex Auto Review completed with no P0–P2 findings on the production repair. The follow-up generated delta and clean base integration were inspected mechanically; the production repair is unchanged. Current-head CI remains pending; no full-suite/full-build claim.
- Live model-driven cleanup and deployed tool verification remain pending redeploy. No real sessions were archived.

### Deployment and verification

After normal review/CI and merge, deploy a release containing the merged commit through the authorized deployment owner; do not change permissions. In a fresh tool-definition turn/session, confirm `sessions_list` accepts `hasBoard` and returns explicit booleans. Query `hasBoard: true` and `hasBoard: false` with small pages, then follow `nextOffset` with identical filters; check a known saved-tab session remains in the true set. Confirm active/queued sessions retain their run state and hidden/incognito sessions stay omitted.

Resume cleanup from a fresh deduplicated inventory, not the old audit as an execution plan: require explicit false, last activity older than 24 hours, completed PR-associated work evidenced by permitted history, and live merged PR state. Preserve pinned, current/main/channel/automation, running/queued, active-descendant, pending-input, or ambiguous sessions. Refresh immediately before each manageable archive batch, pass each listed `sessionId` as `expectedSessionId`, inspect per-item outcomes, and verify preserved sessions remain. Any actual authorization refusal remains a blocker; never use raw state as a workaround.

title: chore: refresh dependencies with a seven-day cooldown
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshes OpenClaw's runtime, development, and release dependencies while keeping a seven-day publication cooldown.

## User Impact

Users and developers receive qualified dependency updates without raising the existing runtime floor. Packages that fail compatibility checks or require unavailable native validation remain pinned; no production deployment or store release is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cutoff is fixed at **2026-10-16T22:58:39Z**, seven days before this request. Native package-manager resolution preserves already-pinned newer versions and rejects dependency-edge downgrades. Existing Chrome MCP and Vitest fixes are forward-ported, artifact integrity records and TypeBox-generated validators are refreshed, and all affected consumers are updated together.

The change adds no state owner or compatibility framework. Matrix now uses upstream fake-indexeddb transaction cleanup instead of maintaining a duplicate pruner. Artifact guards retain their frozen-package verification. The narrow zizmor annotation covers a literal permission-checked reaction workflow with no checkout or contributor-code execution; no security gate is disabled.

## Evidence

- Native pnpm/npm/Cargo/Bundler resolution and frozen-install proofs; all newly introduced versions audited against the fixed cutoff.
- Dependency-edge audits: 3,832 pnpm comparisons and 569 standalone npm comparisons, no downgrades; Cargo/Ruby identities and checksums independently checked.
- Real Chromium Chrome MCP proof: 27 passed; packed npm/pnpm offline-byte checks: 2 passed. Vitest fork-shutdown: 21 passed; cache/invalidation: 6 passed.
- Rust: 147 crate tests and 13 WatchRTC tests passed; Go readonly tests and module verification passed.
- Provider, UI, IMAP, CUA artifact, release CLI, Mermaid browser, and generated-validator tests passed. Final integrated tooling: 330 passed, 7 skipped; native Ruby release gates: 17 unique tests passed both normally and with the pinned Fastlane bundle. Core/plugin/declaration and UI builds, scripts typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, pin and patch guards passed.
- Independent P0–P2 review completed with no actionable findings, including a fresh review of the CI repair delta.
- Post-repair proof: 480 affected UI tests passed, plus the exact bundled 390px picker Escape/reopen regression. Scanner (15), ACP manifest (3), Vitest partition (1), fs-safe relocation (2), and Matrix custody/crypto (38) tests passed. Native root npm lock generation, frozen installation, targeted typecheck/lint/format, and rebuilt UI passed.

**CI repair and attribution:** the first full run ([40039877103](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40039877103)) exposed dependency incompatibilities and stale consumer fixtures; those dependency-caused failures were repaired rather than bypassed. Separate source-attributed baseline failures remain in the Linux onboarding actions fixture, cron model allowlist fixture, hooks stderr escaping assertion, timeout-recovery child handoff barrier, and Telegram overlapping model-catalog replacement. The Telegram retry was reproduced and traced to the unchanged owner reading after the first of two replacement gates; its no-retry assertion is preserved. These are not claimed as passing or as exact-baseline execution replays. Current-head [CI run 40043145833](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40043145833) also exposes inherited contracts on its actual base `98f1a668`: ACK-before-steering fixture assumptions (abort and progress refresh); rollout watcher-cache timing; hidden Files-tree and unrelated Involving-me child fixtures; archive/unarchive pin expectations; and a production Show-in-Files ordering bug that restores the old filter after reveal. All named test/owner inputs match the actual tested merge; attribution uses observed failing operations and control flow, not source equality alone. These unrelated defects are not repaired or labeled green by this dependency PR. The iOS job passed all eight phone/tablet screenshot tests, then Apple’s mounted watchOS 27.0 runtime reported a malformed bundle during simulator boot; no Watch capture ran. This exact-head CI attempt is complete: 190 jobs, 161 passed, 16 skipped, 12 individually attributed failures plus their failed aggregate. All three PostgreSQL shards passed. Failed CI and incomplete Watch capture are retained explicitly for the native inherited-failure landing route; this is not a green-CI claim.

**Investigated local failure:** both isolated Gateway replay tests initially failed because inherited HTTP proxy routing sent loopback fixture traffic through the proxy. A controlled comparison reproduces identical `UND_ERR_SOCKET` / zero-origin-request failures with baseline OpenAI 7.32.0 + Undici 8.11.2 and candidate 7.35.0 + 8.12.2, on Node and the pinned Bun runtime. Both pairs succeed with loopback-only bypasses; the eight fixture/transport owner files are unchanged. The original semantic tests then **both passed** with invocation-scoped `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy`, proving persisted compaction replay and visible no-op continuation through the real isolated Gateway. No global proxy or product policy was changed.

**Limitations:** no macOS/Windows runtime execution, live store upload, or real external-model inference is claimed. The isolated Gateway proof uses a loopback model fixture. Existing Vercel/Zod vulnerability findings remain unchanged, not silently waived.

**Retained updates:** npm stays at 12.2.0 because 12.2.1 conflicts with the existing bundled-dependency security policy; virtual-core stays at 3.19.2 because 3.19.6 regresses picker reopening in Chromium. Codex 0.163.0 fails the required protocol-validation guard; Gradle 9.8.1 fails the existing strict warning gate with AGP. Swift/WebRTC/macOS tools, Matrix/MXC majors, OCM/OpenShell/Tauri and certain Cargo upgrades are retained where compatibility or native proof is missing. [The complete dependency inventory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182010#issuecomment-6376737451) lists every before/after version and explicit deferral.

Requested by @steipete (Peter Steinberger).

title: chore(catalog): recommend Kimi K3.1 Pro ahead of Kimi K3
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Moonshot's new flagship, Kimi K3.1 Pro, is not on OpenClaw's recommended models list, so model pickers bury it under **All models** on providers that serve it.

## User Impact

User impact: providers that serve Kimi K3.1 Pro (including its highspeed tier) list it among their recommended models, directly ahead of Kimi K3. Kimi K3 stays recommended on hosts that do not serve K3.1 Pro yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

`kimi-k3.1-pro` is a new `-pro` class (family `kimi-k-pro`, distinct from `kimi-k`), so per the [recommended-models review rules](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/recommended-models#review-rules) a reviewer chose its slot rather than treating it as an automatic successor. The approved placement is position 20, immediately before `kimi-k3`; every other entry keeps its relative order (30 → 31 unique ids).

Facts behind the addition:

- Moonshot describes K3.1 Pro as its most capable model, post-trained from K3, with a 1M-token context window, vision input and tool calling ([quickstart](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart), [API keys](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/get-your-api-key)).
- OpenRouter serves `moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro` at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, plus a highspeed (priority) endpoint at $4/$20 ([endpoints](https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro/endpoints)). The highspeed tier folds into the base id, so only `kimi-k3.1-pro` is listed.

## Evidence

- `canonicalModelKey` leaves `kimi-k3.1-pro` unchanged and maps `moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro-20261023` and `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` to it, so the publisher's canonical-id check accepts the entry and served ids match it.
- List shape: 31 entries, 31 unique; `kimi-k3.1-pro` at index 19, `kimi-k3` at index 20.
