title: fix: model setup loses authorization while sign-in continues
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes model setup failing with “Gateway caller authority is no longer active” when sign-in, verification, or activation continues after the initiating request returns.

## User Impact

Setup retains its original authorization across asynchronous work and reconnects without changing saved credentials or working model defaults. Early revocation cases rejected the original grant before provider or activation effects. After an originally authorized configuration write had persisted, the observed late-revocation path transiently applied the candidate, then restored the original configuration and active credential through compensation; zero transient visibility is not established. Cancellation remains effective; connection-bound provider login keeps its existing disconnect behavior. No config, credential-format, dependency, schema, or protocol migration is introduced.

**Deployment qualification remains open:** native/live-provider and real install-over acceptance, current-head PR CI and applicable owner review, then an independent security audit of the final immutable deployment artifact. This PR is not deployment clearance; the final audit must remain last before deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the original operator through the existing continuation owner before acknowledging setup, and run the wizard in that retained scope. Keep caller-specific checks, forward the source assertion into actual inference-probe admission, and release custody after runner settlement, including deferred recovery. Retry admission still checks the new caller before cancelling an earlier attempt.

## Evidence

### Production-path authority evidence (2026-10-23)

The following runs exercised the real token-authenticated Gateway setup RPC, wizard, activation, embedded inference execution, HTTP/SSE transport, credential/configuration owners, and production config-reload watcher. Activation, authority, execution, stores, and application claim/settlement were not mocked. The provider and exec-secret backend were owned deterministic local services with synthetic credentials: this is production-path evidence, **not live OpenAI/ChatGPT/native-provider qualification**.

Source binding: published head b5eb9861ef59f99f23f781baad16f5c263ac28d8; complete working candidate tree 06c63c96530ad45be99a543c6cfa2ccf4e6e01a4; eight feature-file hashes unchanged. Official Node 26.12.1 and integrity-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 were used. Normal frozen install and required canonical source runtime build exited 0 with dependency-policy inputs unchanged. The source build retains the original-base build stamp (42c0d5a…, version 2026.10.5), not a fabricated clean published-head stamp; source/tree equivalence was verified separately. This is not upgrade qualification.

| Scenario | Observed production-boundary outcome |
|---|---|
| Allowed completion after reconnect | Start response returned, original socket closed, replacement client authenticated, real HTTP POST/SSE completed; the inactive saved credential became active/static and the new primary/profile binding persisted. |
| Original-device revocation before effects | Revoked through public device.token.revoke at the natural API-key prompt. Cumulative provider requests stayed 1→1; config hash, primary and existing credential summaries were unchanged. Wizard rejected the original continuation authority. |
| Revocation while provider response was held | A genuine second HTTP response was held after authorized inactive staging. Revoked the original device, then released the response. Wizard rejected completion; original config/active credential remained unchanged and the attempted replacement stayed inactive. |
| Allowed deferred application | The actual config watcher hot-reloaded and accepted the revision. Wizard completed; public configRevisionHash equaled appliedConfigHash and the credential was active/static. No synthetic application claimant/settler was used. |
| Revocation after application claim | A same-action exec-secret control succeeded first. A real exec-secret resolution then held candidate application after persistence and watcher preparation. Revoking the original device and releasing the resolver produced an authority error and real compensating recovery: original raw config hash, primary, applied/persisted revision and active credential were restored; the attempted credential remained inactive. |

**Important late-window limitation:** the candidate hot reload occurred after revocation and before compensation restored the original state. This is evidence of recovery, **not proof of zero transient application or prevention of every post-revocation effect**. No concurrent inference was attempted during that transient window. Review is still needed on whether this commit/recovery behavior is sufficient or whether runtime publication must recheck the original grant before exposing the candidate. This packet does not claim security clearance.

<details>
<summary>Redacted late-window trace and reproducible observation method</summary>

P1 and P4 are display aliases for observed synthetic profiles; they were not seeded expected state.

~~~text
16:09:07.537 UTC  Real watcher evaluates candidate P1 (after application.prepare in source order).
16:09:07.596      Actual exec-secret request #5 held; candidate primary already persisted.
16:09:07.606      Public config.get: persisted revision != applied revision.
16:09:07.607      Public wizard.status: running.
16:09:07.616      Public device.token.revoke receipt for the original operator device.
                 Owned resolver response released.
16:09:07.654      Candidate hot reload applied.
16:09:07.657      Candidate source revision accepted.
16:09:07.759      Watcher evaluates compensating configuration.
16:09:07.882      Actual exec-secret request sees restored original primary P4.
16:09:07.917      Recovery hot reload applied.
16:09:07.923      Recovery source revision accepted.
16:09:07.933      Wizard error: Gateway continuation authority is no longer active.
16:09:07.971      Owner reads: original config/primary restored, P4 static, P1 inactive.
16:09:08.338      Owned Gateway closed with SIGTERM; both owned HTTP servers closed.
~~~

The matched candidate-specific watcher log occurs after await application.prepare in the unchanged config-reload owner. Its managed-write listener synchronously claims the attached application receipt. The held request came from real secrets/runtime preparation, corroborated by public pending-revision and running-wizard reads. No public claimed=true field or fake application status was invented.

~~~ts
// Redacted excerpts of executed production-facing requests.
c.request("openclaw.setup.activate.start", {
  sessionId, kind: "api-key", authChoice: "openai-api-key",
  apiKey: "[synthetic-value-redacted]",
  modelRef: "openai/gpt-5.4-mini", nativeSessionCatalogsEnabled: false,
});
await control.client.request("device.token.revoke", {
  deviceId: original.identity.deviceId, role: "operator",
});
await control.client.request("config.get", {});
await control.client.request("models.authStatus", { agentId: "main" });
~~~

The barrier used the documented exec-secret provider with an owned resolver, trusted executable directory, normal path/mode checks and unchanged default timeout. All runs used isolated HOME/state/config/workspaces and per-client credential stores. The late run explicitly scoped logging.file inside its private run directory. Earlier runs used the default temporary log destination; that logging-isolation limit is retained, and no outside-workspace log was read or deleted for cleanup. Exact command receipts and hashes remain in the linked implementation session. Matrix, dedicated application, and the combined same-action exec-secret control/late-negative command exited 0. Owned Gateway/provider/secret-backend processes were stopped and checked absent.

Evidence integrity: production-results.json SHA-256 81f1d759446231c1b0495ab66095a0ef5f3a20e8a073cb30c353239dc5ebcfdb; redacted late observations SHA-256 89aa33a3daea6876799446e55d17b0430f5a0544015d995388aea32260431059; parent-readable proof SHA-256 aea49b6e23e134fc1dd40471480a2eb8af79aaee9331c0ce019009c7aefedb8a. These are trace identities, not a substitute for the observations above.

</details>

Earlier test and baseline-install evidence follows; it is not relabeled as new-head CI or live qualification.

- The real authenticated Gateway reproduction fails on the original base with the reported error. The six-scenario regression passes start-response, reconnect, sign-in and revocation-before/after-capture cases; later authentication cannot revive the original revoked grant.
- Focused unit, Gateway, activation/credential-preservation, remote-CLI and browser cases passed on the original-base implementation. Browser evidence includes a real browser/HTTPS Gateway flow and cancelled/stale callback rejection. External identity/model responses remain fixtures, not live-account qualification.
- The eight-file implementation was independently reviewed on base `42c0d5a8f9d00e113c48090c3d259977e67b5b5a`, candidate tree `06c63c96530ad45be99a543c6cfa2ccf4e6e01a4`: scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings. The helper reported source-context limitations across its evidence batches; the reviewer did not independently rerun tests. This is bounded code review, not the final security audit.
- Separately, the byte-identical eight feature files passed 199 tests, focused type/lint/format checks and a full canonical source build after integration onto base `7d31fe01b636c6b7bf2e3a4cb362658f4b52e5b0`. That separate candidate is supporting integration evidence, not full-tree/current-head CI for this published original-base branch.
- The new real-Gateway regression shares one server across six scenarios because helper-only tests missed the request-completion/reconnect boundary. Retained latest run: 21.1 seconds test time; about 137 seconds command wall time including cold preparation. CI timing is not yet available.
- Released 2026.10.6 was installed in an isolated prefix and its published build identity/lifecycle verified. Real working-state install-over remains unrun. Local packaging stopped at the unchanged dependency-age policy; no package archive or global policy change resulted.

title: fix: confirm objective replacement when a session already has a goal
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Goal submissions in the Control UI, including when the agent is already executing the current goal.

## User Impact

Submitting another `/goal <objective>` (including creation aliases) or using the Goal composer offers **Cancel** and **Replace objective** instead of a creation error or an ambiguous Stop action.

- Cancel or Escape preserves the proposed draft and leaves the running turn untouched.
- Confirming during an executing goal interrupts that exact turn, waits for its work to settle, pauses and edits the same goal, then resumes through normal continuation admission.
- Goal identity, accounting, budget, history, and timer are retained. An exhausted budget is not reset to force a restart.
- Idle and paused replacements remain status-preserving edits. Completed-goal restrictions, explicit management commands, first creation, and textual CLI/TUI behavior are unchanged.

A failed or unverified stage does not automatically resume. The draft and original recovery request remain available. If interrupted output cannot be saved, replacement stops before editing or resuming and tells the operator to preserve visible text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both submission forms share the established confirmation and async recovery UI. The running case uses one lifecycle-owned operation rather than a blind sequence of browser RPCs: existing Stop, Goal mutation, and normal Resume owners retain authority, physical settlement, and durable retry behavior.

The decision is tied to the original session, goal revision, and executing run. Stale decisions cannot stop a newer run, concurrent controls cannot be overwritten, and the admission fence does not cancel unrelated queued work.

## Evidence

- Copy-only refinement on `6504be6f…`: both replacement confirmations now use one clear sentence. The complete 34-test replacement suite and both production-built Chromium flows pass; production UI/E2E-chat types, focused lint/formatting and i18n verification pass. Fresh independent review of the two-file copy/assertion diff found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Runtime behavior is unchanged.
- 121 focused UI tests pass, plus two production-built Chromium flows covering literal and structured submissions, running confirmation, Cancel/Escape, and resumed-run presentation.
- All 42 Goal Gateway tests pass, including 13 replacement cases: exact-run interruption, physical settlement, same-ID replay, partial-stage recovery, stale/concurrent changes, unrelated pending admissions, interrupted-history warnings, allowed/denied session access, and real role revocation during settlement, pause, edit, Resume admission, and recovery. The admission-isolation and warning regressions were demonstrated red before their repairs.
- Latest-stable 2026.10.6 install-over proof preserves the complete original Goal, accounting/timers, both durable operation receipts, all 26 original transcript events and 18 readable messages. Exact old edit replay is idempotent.
- The installed candidate replaces an actually executing goal on one persistent read/write operator connection: the original model stream closes 436 ms before replacement inference begins. Same Goal/budget/accounting baseline retained; interrupt/pause/edit/resume receipts occur once. Cold-process replay changes neither inference count, 43 events, 10 receipts nor 24 history messages. This uses a synthetic loopback model, not live-provider inference.
- The stale restart-safe Goal test caller identified by PR CI is migrated; its complete 32-test suite, both affected strict test-type graphs, and the required failed-CI test selection pass locally.
- Focused Stop, worker inference, budget-policy, prompt-prefix, archive, and compaction consumer checks pass. Production/test types, lint, formatting, i18n, documentation, assertion/timeout/line and SQLite-worker ratchets, and production build are checked separately.
- Fresh canonical independent reviews of the implementation and final test-only CI/authority repair found no actionable P0–P2 defects after earlier findings were repaired. Hosted review and exact-head PR CI remain separately reported.

- Hosted ClawSweeper review completed on `78f955a5ef7af50cfe6091b0ae79353672bc3085`: **no findings**, security concern cleared, ready for maintainer review ([review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181688#issuecomment-6367421480)).

**Current-head CI recovered:** [run 40017700073, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40017700073/attempts/2) completed successfully on unchanged `6504be6f…`: **89 successful jobs, 20 skipped**. Following the documented one-time failed-job infrastructure-recovery route after the Android SDK extraction failure, all three selected failed leaves now pass, including packaged Android native execution and both previously failing Vitest shards. The native CI CheckRun (`120683774920`) and protected Security Review commit status (`57137193413`, [publisher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40032479939)) are both successful. No source rewrite, full-CI redispatch or check bypass was used. Original attempt-1 failures and the exact-merge/main controls are retained; passing recovery supplies missing hosted coverage, not proof that the original causes were repaired or that the tests are flaky.

**Prior-head CI was not green:** [run 40001159263](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40001159263) on `78f955a5…` completed with one subagent-coordination leaf failure plus the downstream CI gate (87 successful jobs, 20 skipped). The hosted failure was not reproduced, not fixed or relabeled green. No source change, base refresh or CI rerun was made for that attribution. The new copy-only head is checked separately; prior-head results are not claimed as current-head CI.

title: feat: add personal session groups
body:
Related: #181038 ## What Problem This Solves Guests and members need to organize accessible conversations into their own sidebar groups without changing shared groups or another person's layout. Grouping a parent conversation must also preserve its child conversations and their live updates. ## User Impact Users can create personal groups, edit names and membership, reorder them by dragging or menu actions, and remove groups without deleting conversations. Pins and shared groups remain independent. Parent conversations retain their loaded children, expansion behavior and child updates in both personal and canonical sidebar placements. Groups are scoped to the current Gateway and profile. Connections with general Gateway write access synchronize through personal preferences; session-only, read-only, and profileless connections retain browser-local behavior. Saved references do not grant access, and unavailable sessions stay hidden. The existing 4 KiB preference limit produces a visible error rather than silently truncating an edit. No migration or permission upgrade is introduced. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing navigation-preference owner stores group labels and session references, including bootstrap, identity changes, offline replay and storage recovery. Group edits persist only their own preference field, preserving independently authored pins. Personal group occurrences consume the sidebar's reconciled canonical rows. Off-page references use the same tree projection and retain their expansion state and child observations across updates. The earlier lookup rebuilt a basic row without its child tree and observation metadata; because personal occurrences appeared first during deduplication, that also displaced the normal row used for child refresh. Separate appearance keys still preserve Alt/Shift range selection, while batch operations target each session once. The group editor retains the native modal height limit and keeps its membership list scrollable with the name and completion actions visible. Its small sizing rules load with the lazy dialog, preserving the upstream removal of optional approval styles from initial page loading. ## Evidence Startup acceptance uses the maintained `ui:check-performance:base` production-sidecar comparison: startup JavaScript must stay within the existing baseline plus 512-byte growth allowance and 64-byte build variance, with all request, route, and style ceilings unchanged. The initial measurement was 272,332 gzip bytes, 106 bytes over the enforced limit. Reusing the existing string normalizer and one authored-field comparison reduced the production measurement to 272,018 bytes; five startup requests and all limits are unchanged. The affected settings and guest proof passed 67 cases. The final target integration measures 270,961 production gzip bytes with the same five requests and limits. - On the incoming contribution, both loaded-child and initially unloaded-child regressions failed: only one child occurrence rendered instead of two. The production-bundle browser scenario independently showed the child under Engineering but missing from Focus. The corrected owner tests cover both placements, subsequent child updates, and collapse/remove recovery. - Required upstream integration exposed the existing long-list regression: the membership list no longer had its own scrollable region. The same test now passes without changing its assertions. - Earlier related coverage passed 2,005 tests in 126 selected files, including 11 browser cases across three files. Coverage includes profile/CAS/storage behavior, bootstrap, child lifecycle, selection deduplication, unavailable references, stale-editor recovery and long-list layout. The selected production and test compiler groups, formatting, typed lint, styles, localization and line-cap checks passed. - Browser tests use the production UI with a synthetic Gateway. They cover administrator and session-read access and verify group edits issue no shared session/group/config writes. These results do not claim live authentication or deployment. - The correction passed 11 child-freshness cases, 209 related Node cases, 12 browser cases, selected UI compiler groups and fast checks. The off-page parent case was red before the correction. - The real-Gateway guest flow passed with only `operator.sessions.read/write`: create/edit/reorder/reload/remove, live child updates in both placements, browser-local persistence, no shared writes, and denial of another guest's parent. It does not run a model turn. - After integrating #185067 and the retained pin/snapshot presentation in #183862, 140 affected cases and selected UI type and fast checks passed. Group trees read the session owner's authoritative row; pins retain their projected presentation. Both use the same invalidation and retirement lifecycle, including revoked access, supplemental replacement, removal and disconnection. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Roster\-resident parent in both placements | ![Focus omits Verification notes while Engineering shows it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e1901bc-ba0e-48b1-9bdb-c3d08ce30eea) | ![Focus and Engineering both show Verification notes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68426b36-96e5-4a07-9c64-cc0cbba5b848) | | Long membership list keeps completion actions visible | ![Long membership list pushes completion actions below the viewport](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e58f5cb3-b914-4a2c-9781-e9eb9101a29e) | ![Membership list scrolls while completion actions remain visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2671d54-e6c9-4746-9c04-43d6cd2230c7) | ### Personal group interactions \(one\-third speed\) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c66f2001-3042-4435-a5b8-62541d7ae8d1 ### Visual verification - Baseline: Child comparison: 33f3c8de2388e7d04ac5c926ebbeddfaa6550ba8; long\-list comparison: 1822b99ae527c9b6d0275eb5305429d9e346c351 - Exact head: `bf8729ebba52f8646431c271c45d698c3380410f` - Scenario: Expand a parent, create Focus, then create, drag, edit, reorder, reload and remove personal groups with synthetic session\-read access\. - Runtime/build: Corrected captures built at 60de397805cfd404cf5b48e1dc7242f7c21eb6d0; their individual before baselines are stated above\. Qualified to bf8729ebba52f8646431c271c45d698c3380410f/tree7fd2e7d1a1cad21ab5e2dc69a083b0143d326cbe through preserved presentation conditions, current owner/snapshot checks and the real\-Gateway guest flow\. Chromium156\.0\.8078\.4\. - Child appearances: 1 before, 2 after - Shared mutations: 0 session, shared\-group or config writes - Matched synthetic fixtures and viewports in each comparison pair - Latest integration passed 139 owner/snapshot cases and the real\-Gateway guest flow - Six earlier personal\-group E2E scenarios remain qualified through unchanged layout and selection behavior - The shipped 2026\.10\.7 persistence transition passed on 407aad4; unchanged persistence owners and current reload proof qualify that result - Long\-list sizing rules are unchanged; the existing long\-list browser regression and captured result remain applicable ## Shipped-app compatibility The actual published `openclaw@2026.10.7` UI passed an in-place browser upgrade against an isolated real Gateway on `407aad4`. That result is qualified to the final integration by unchanged persistence owners and repeated guest reload proof. The package integrity was verified; the same origin, browser context, profile and stored bytes were retained. Shipped navigation controls’ owner wrote the existing navigation preferences, and visible appearance controls created an offline pending dark-theme edit. After the first personal-group save and reload, the dark theme, 320px sidebar width, agent pin and new group remained. Legacy `sidebarEntries` stayed recoverable without being revived as new shortcuts. title: fix(codex): preserve owner threads after subagent completions
body:
Closes #181580
Related: #143386

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a restricted subagent completion replaces its owner's native Codex thread, and preserving that thread alone loses the completion's result on the next owner turn.

## User Impact

User impact: the owner resumes its original native thread with the unseen completion input and answer as quoted context. Completion restrictions and the child's persistent restrictions remain enforced. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify verified inherited completion restrictions as turn-scoped at the existing policy owner. The existing temporary-thread lifecycle then preserves the durable owner binding. On resume, exclude only mirrors from that owner's own thread; reuse the existing history cutoff and context renderer to supply the completion delta once.

Fresh host-admitted rows do not always identify a native thread. Keeping them can repeat quoted context after an accepted but failed turn; that recoverable duplication is preferable to silently losing a completion result. No new state or lifecycle owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- Red on unchanged main production: the policy regression expected `turn` but received `conversation` (29 other cases passed). Both native-mirror and host-admitted continuity regressions omitted the unique child result (the two existing durable-context cases passed).
- With the fix, 70 focused tests passed: requester policy and prompt-prefix stability (41), plus durable completion context, bounded continuity, and restricted-thread continuation (29). The four-attempt regressions exercise production attempt lifecycle and real SQLite transcripts with a mocked app-server transport, including original-thread reuse, result recall, retained restrictions, and no later replay.
- After merging main `478ab60992ab`, all four new policy/continuity regression cases passed again; the integrated replay took 168.52s.
- Measured cold baseline wall time was 179.97s for requester policy and 226.90s for durable context; the 70-test candidate run took 683.57s including compilation and cleanup. The native regression uses SQLite and the complete attempt lifecycle because a history-filter unit test would miss the thread-binding defect.
- Targeted core and extension oxlint, oxfmt on all changed files, the edited page's MDX validation, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The native PR worktree typecheck refused the intentionally shared compiler install (declaration input escapes checkout). The standalone package config also proved unsuitable for source-tree typechecking; exact-head PR CI supplies the full typecheck.
- Production: +8/−4 lines; tests: +167/−2; docs: +6/−1. The four-line net production increase adds the required policy classification and thread-specific exclusion without introducing another owner. The separate transcript-writer cases protect distinct admission paths.
- @Marvinthebored supplied the [pinned authenticated Gateway/Codex A/B replay](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6f89f479d5f678071271efe393ec2bf220448c9f/PROOF.md). Its two runs per revision record owner sequences `A,A,B,A,A` with this patch versus `A,A,B,C,C` on base, retained restrictions, correct result recall, and no fifth-turn replay. The report was inspected in this pass; it remains contributor-run live evidence.

Fresh authenticated native replay was not repeated: the existing pinned A/B replay covers this same production change; the fresh local proof uses a mocked app-server transport. Unrestricted catalog rotation remains separate under #167277.

Reported and reproduced by @Marvinthebored.

title: fix(gateway): avoid automatic profiler hang risk on macOS
body:
Related: #181120

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic continuous CPU profiling exposes macOS Gateways to a native lock-stall risk implicated in #181120.

## User Impact

macOS users no longer need a local patch to keep the automatic CPU flight recorder off. Callback attribution, stall warnings, event-loop delay/utilization, and CPU health metrics stay enabled. The tradeoff is losing automatic trailing CPU profiles on macOS. No configuration change is required; Linux and Windows recording and explicitly requested on-demand profiling are unchanged.

This removes the automatic profiler exposure; it does not fix Apple's lock implementation or claim every Gateway hang is resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate the recorder at its existing owner, before the first native profile starts. Eligible macOS processes emit one explanatory warning per monitor. There is no new configuration, dependency, timer, or fallback profiler. Recording can be reconsidered once the native interaction is demonstrated safe.

Maintainer decision requested: @vincentkoc, could you review this macOS-only safety tradeoff promptly? The reported failure leaves the Gateway unresponsive; this change removes automatic CPU profiles while preserving non-profiling diagnostics, without claiming the native OS/Node bug is fixed.

## Evidence

### October 27 refresh and CI repair

- Refreshed against `main` at `7bce7a61639ae959406736876f2f0cf8cee991ce`; current PR head is `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35`. Resolved the recorder-test conflict while preserving main's interval-object sampling API, 25 ms interval, and timing-attribution tests. The production macOS exclusion is unchanged.
- The newly upstream real-native-profiler test excludes actual Darwin hosts, so its Linux platform mock cannot accidentally enable the unsafe native sampler there. Mocked macOS no-start and Linux/Windows rotation coverage remain active. This is an intentional platform eligibility limit, not a suppressed failure.
- The first refreshed head `e1c3921201ec3d4d5b1d092db5b5a9abcb306cd7` failed the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40512027532/job/122216871729) with a net addition of 27 test lines. This repair removes duplicate mock layers, a forwarding fixture, and repeated lifecycle/redaction setup without dropping scenarios or assertions. All six redaction cases remain; additional cases now also check later-sample recovery and shutdown. The complete PR now has **zero net additional test lines** against the refresh base (75 added / 75 removed); production remains +7/-1. The unchanged ratchet passes locally; no ceiling, baseline, or exemption was changed.
- **Linux / Node 26.12.1: 35 focused tests passed**, including the real native-profiler block test (19 Gateway + 16 recorder; wrapper 21.54 s). The preceding test-consolidation revision passed pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 34 passed / 1 skipped because its native V8 profiling API is unavailable (wrapper 12.05 s); the only subsequent source change restores the erased TypeScript cleanup contract. Removing only the macOS guard makes the consolidated macOS no-start regression fail; restoring it passes.
- CI confirmed the [test-line ratchet passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40515606710/job/122229495293) on `f6ac5a2bd09679ccd07b1e35a9a570feab6a8e33`, then exposed an [await-thenable lint error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40515606710/job/122230905307). The final one-line repair restores the test table's `void | Promise<void>` cleanup contract: skill tracking drains asynchronous work, so removing `await` would be wrong. The exact CI type-aware lint configuration reproduced the error before this repair and passes afterward on all three changed TypeScript files. The gateway typecheck and all 35 Node tests were rerun successfully, and the local test-line delta remains zero.
- Both affected typecheck graphs (`state-logging`, `gateway-server`), targeted lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed on this candidate. Earlier MDX validation remains applicable to the unchanged documentation. **Current-head CI passed**: [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122254287794) succeeded for `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35`, including all selected aggregate lanes, with no known-main-red waiver. The previously failing [type-aware lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122244976210) and [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122243448980) both passed. GitHub reported the PR cleanly mergeable; it remains open and unmerged.
- Fresh independent Auto Review of the complete final local candidate against the pinned refresh base returned `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings. Its final patch pass covered all four files and explicitly checked the consolidated assertions and fixture semantics; earlier passes contained only the staged base-refresh inventory. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6362662214) reported no findings or before-merge items for `e1c3921201ec3d4d5b1d092db5b5a9abcb306cd7`; that is prior-head review evidence, not a claim it reviewed this test-only repair.
- **Proof boundary:** the macOS Gateway A/B below remains evidence for the original head, not a new macOS execution of this refreshed revision. The guard is unchanged; updated sampling and Gateway consumers were checked by the current focused suites.

### Original revision validation

- **Actual macOS Gateway A/B supplied by @Marvinthebored:** [run report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6367004169) and [pinned artifacts](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/aaf4683affe31fde5d83512918ef64610dd31133/PROOF.md) compare original head `00d27c442c5d8b8886f6e40c22b41b241f366c96` with `ded4d430df859f35599fbb4d0ef32d8dec31e3b5` on macOS 26.6.1 ARM64 / Node 26.12.1. Native samples before/after the block contain the V8 profiler thread in stock and none in patched; the patched recorder warning appears exactly once. The corrected comparison uses Gateway-PID-only SIGTERM. I inspected the harness, logs, health snapshots and complete native-sample thread inventories and verified all 40 artifact hashes against the pinned manifest; this is a review of the reporter's run, not a separate execution.
- **macOS-host red/green:** the same two suites pass 33/33 on that original head; restoring only stock recorder source gives 32 passed / 1 failed, specifically the new macOS exclusion test. These recorder tests mock native APIs; the separate Gateway A/B above supplies native-runtime evidence.

- **Limits:** the new successful macOS Gateway A/B supersedes the earlier readiness-timeout evidence gap. Both stock and patched complete this short scenario: it proves removal of automatic profiler exposure with working startup, health sampling and shutdown, not reproduction or repair of the original deadlock or long-term stability. Source execution with tsx does not cover a release distribution, channel/model traffic or manual profiling. Short Node port-churn controls also did not reproduce the native hang; manually requested profiling is not made safe by this change.

<details>

title: fix: respect server retry windows for GitHub previews

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes GitHub hover previews requesting metadata again before the server's retry window ends.

## User Impact

Reopening a preview respects the server's reset time, including after reader-document refreshes. Existing details remain available, ordinary errors keep their existing short backoff, and authentication/access behavior is unchanged. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing preview cache records a retry deadline once instead of replacing every failure with 30 seconds. It preserves that deadline when reader facts refresh, including windows longer than the metadata cache lifetime. Stale-preview fallback now belongs to the cache owner so it cannot hide the structured server delay.

No new manager, configuration, wire contract, or persistent state is introduced. The simplification removes the request helper's separate failure fallback; the complete change adds 16 net production lines and 107 net test lines. Rendering and server-authored error messages are unchanged.

title: fix(update): distinguish unverified recovery from observed failure

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes update recovery reports declaring the Gateway unhealthy or serving when readiness was not actually observed.

## User Impact

A later healthy check can verify the existing process without another restart. Restart and backup-retention policy are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep readiness evidence with the existing observer and distinguish missing evidence from a negative response. Retain actual HTTP responses across an interrupted subsequent probe, and describe an untouched installation with native running status without claiming verified serving health. No new configuration, state schema, or restart behavior is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original false unhealthy/serving claims before the fix. title: fix(update): avoid state capture when a retained build blocks updates

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a source update captures original state before reporting that retained build ownership prevents the update.

## User Impact

Users receive the existing ownership refusal and recovery guidance before the unnecessary original-state capture, while the serving Gateway stays untouched. This requires the installed updater to contain the fix; a newer candidate cannot change an older updater already running.

## Why This Change Was Made

Probe the existing artifact owner after target selection and downgrade confirmation, then release the probe immediately. The normal execution-time acquisition and revalidation remain authoritative, including when a build starts during capture. No PID-based reclamation, new ownership state, configuration, or storage policy is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real `updateCommand` entry with isolated state and a retained owner: the base invoked original capture once before refusal; the fix refuses with zero captures and preserves the owner record.

These tests require the real update entry and native capture/ownership lifecycle; testing only execution would miss the original ordering defect.

title: fix(update): keep maintenance guidance within repair scope
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update repair and cleanup can tell a triage fixer to stop its own Gateway, while bounded embedded repair also receives contradictory restart instructions.

## User Impact

Maintenance advice directs an independent operator outside triage and the Gateway service to perform stop-and-retry maintenance. Embedded repair keeps the orchestrator-owned lifecycle contract. Existing ownership refusals, cancellation, and later operator stops remain unchanged; no migration or new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

State contention can happen before managed handoff discovery, so the error cannot establish that its caller is safe to stop the Gateway. Keep that guidance conservative rather than adding another scope classifier. The bounded repair prompt now reuses the existing sanitized failure projection without embedding standalone triage's broader activation instructions. Standalone triage is unchanged.

The runtime producing the advice or repair prompt must contain this fix; it does not change an older CLI that is already running. Simplification removes the whole external-triage instruction block from bounded repair: production changes are +8/-9 lines, with no new owner or API.

## Evidence

- On base `5f7fa9eb9864def8ef717e11808420913cb560a9`, the public repair early-refusal, changed-history guidance, and bounded-prompt regressions failed for the intended reasons: 3 failed, 63 passed; 110.75 seconds wall time including initial worker preparation.
- Fixed candidate: 7 files across 5 focused Vitest shards; 99 passed and 8 macOS-only cases skipped on Linux; 241.41 seconds wall time including worker preparation. Coverage includes repair and cleanup entry points, failure retention/redaction/8 KiB prompt bounds, repair runtime authority and cleanup, external/self-stop handoff controls, standalone triage, and tool-prefix stability.

The existing public-repair suite exceeds 30 seconds because it exercises real ledger recovery and process-identity boundaries; no cases, timers, or fixture machinery were added. No live Gateway/service mutation, live-model repair, or stable-version upgrade was performed: this change updates guidance and prompt composition, not lifecycle enforcement or stored formats. title: fix: distinguish cached health age from live observations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cached health replies expose changing live diagnostics under only the older snapshot timestamp.

## User Impact

Health JSON consumers can distinguish snapshot collection time from the time the RPC read current diagnostics. The optional additive `observedAt` field requires no migration or user action; `ts` retains its existing meaning and cache age.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stamp both health RPC response paths at composition, without modifying the stored snapshot or pretending that a reused sampler window or queue observation was measured again. Readiness admission, update success policy, cache expiry, background refresh cadence, and passive health events are unchanged.

The change uses the existing serializer and protocol types: six added source/type/comment lines, ten documentation lines, and a net 31 test lines. Existing readiness coverage is extended rather than duplicated; no manager, cache, configuration, or polling is added.

## Evidence

- Controlled-clock tests call the production health handler for repeated cached reads, explicit probes, expiry, changing readiness, latest samples, and sampler reset. On base `5f7fa9eb9864def8ef717e11808420913cb560a9`, six assertions fail specifically because `observedAt` is absent (11 other tests pass; cold wrapper wall time 95.63 s).
- With the fix, the handler, health-state, and delivery-queue cache suites pass all 40 tests. Wrapper wall time: 124.71 s (Vitest: 116.62 s), including cold worker compilation and existing sibling setup. Exact-head CI [39908631521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39908631521) passed. Its eight changed-node/boundary jobs consumed 1,351 aggregate job-seconds (parallel job elapsed time including setup and other tests, not per-test attribution).
- Focused lint: no warnings/errors. The gateway-methods test typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --incremental`), formatting, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm protocol:check` pass, including Swift/Kotlin contract and determinism checks.
- Independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2) is scoped-clean with no actionable findings. Its assessment covers the supplied diff, not the full repository, and it did not execute tests.
- Proof uses the actual RPC handler with isolated fixture state; no live Gateway, service, model call, or operator configuration was changed.

title: improve(ui): simplify the browser sign-in dialog
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the browser sign-in dialog in model setup reads as a cluttered form: a bare provider-name header, two lines that say the same thing, a primary "Open sign-in" button for a tab that already opened, and a footer Cancel under empty space.

## User Impact

User impact: browser and device-code sign-in now shows who you're connecting, one sentence about the tab that already opened, and quiet recovery actions. Device codes are the focus, expiry appears only near the end, and a long wait explains the likely cause (another browser or profile) with a Try again action. Cancel is the corner × or Escape.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen after reviewing a design proposal modeled on established browser-handoff flows (GitHub CLI, Stripe CLI, Raycast OAuth, RFC 8628 device-code guidance). The approved design also dropped the footer status line and Cancel button.

- The runner already opens the sign-in tab, so the copy now says that ("… is open in a new tab. Approve access there. This window updates by itself.") and "Open sign-in" became a secondary "Reopen browser tab", with "Copy sign-in link" as a small text fallback.
- A provider badge with a spinner ring replaces the header bar; the dialog sizes to its content. The waiting status stays available to assistive tech as a visually hidden live region.
- Device-code steps show the code large with Copy, ask the user to check that the codes match, and shorten the phishing warning to one line. Expiry text appears only in the last five minutes; once it passes, the code is replaced with "This code expired. Nothing was connected."
- After 45 seconds of waiting on a redirect, an inline hint explains the tab may be in another browser or profile, and the reopen link becomes the primary "Try again".
- Steps that need Continue keep it and show the provider's own instructions in the new layout. Embedded presentations (custodian setup card, channels) keep their existing sign-in markup.

Client-only; no Gateway or protocol changes. Auto-close on success was left out so the existing "Start a new chat" completion action keeps working.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

title: fix(chat): hide raw tool handoff resume rows after plugin reload or GitHub publish
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a plugin reload (`plugins` tool `reloadAndResume`) or a GitHub publish handoff, Control UI shows a plain "System" row containing the raw tool result JSON and the model-directed instruction "Continue the original task in this conversation. Do not repeat a completed operation."

## User Impact

User impact: the chat no longer shows that internal resume row; users see the agent's own reply to the result. The resume still wakes the agent with the result in its context. Generic plugin session events (for example channel presence notices sent through `api.runtime.system.enqueueSessionEvent`) stay visible as before. If the handoff cannot resume, the existing visible "could not continue this conversation automatically" assistant notice is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool handoff resumed its conversation with a `source: "plugin"` session event, which is indistinguishable from plugin-originated events. It now uses a dedicated `tool_handoff` session event source (recorded as `provenance.sourceTool: "tool_handoff"`), and the chat display projection hides those rows the same way it already hides exec completion and scheduler repair inputs. Because history, live `session.message` events and pending inputs all share that projection, the row stays out of every Control UI path while remaining in the model transcript. The handoff keeps the captured owner-authority binding previously keyed on the `plugin` source.

Note: plugin tool factories that read `toolContext.inputProvenance` on the resumed turn now see `sourceTool: "tool_handoff"` instead of `"plugin"`; that value was not documented.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.visibility.test.ts` case: a `tool_handoff` resume row is dropped from chat history projection, live session-message payloads and pending-input projection, while a `plugin` session event and the assistant reply stay visible. Fails on `main` (resume row projected), passes with this change.
- `src/agents/tools/plugins-reload-handoff.test.ts` and `src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.handoff.test.ts` assert the resume is still enqueued with `source: "tool_handoff"` and the result text; the owner-authority integration cases (success, reload failure, revoked, cancelled, replaced, system, non-owner) pass through the real session-event dispatch with `InputProvenance.sourceTool: "tool_handoff"`.

title: fix(ui): keep chat selection on message text
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat selection including transcript chrome and media/layout regions instead of only the message text.

## User Impact

Message and reasoning text remain selectable without selecting sender/timestamp chrome. The muted-blue family from the reference is lightened to preserve selection visibility: white selected text is 4.77:1, and the fill stays at least 3:1 against page/card/panel surfaces across composed palettes. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript currently opts its entire container into native selection. Make the container nonselectable and opt the existing message and reasoning text owners back in, including the WebKit-prefixed declarations. This uses the browser's existing selection and clipboard behavior; no new handlers or state.

The shared selection color token changes from saturated blue to the requested muted blue. Simplification pass retained only the two CSS changes and their regression coverage (production +11/−4 lines; tests +237/−7).

## Evidence

- Four built-UI browser cases pass: native drag/select-all, unchanged image and turn-gap pixels, visible text highlight, excluded metadata, and reasoning selection in ordinary/expanded bubble layouts. Both reasoning cases failed with empty native selection before the correction.
- Seven focused browser checks passed across selection, app-chrome interaction, and content/context copying. The production Control UI build used by that lane passed.
- Command: pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-text-selection.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 — 32.66s command wall, 6.14s test time for four real-browser cases (the command includes the production UI build). Contrast suite: 11 passed, 2.66s command wall / 1.01s Vitest wall. Highlight-to-surface relationships failed at 2.13:1 before the fix. Final-head CI run 39893399225 passed: the four selection E2E cases took 10.77s; the form-controls file took 10.47s and the contrast file 0.81s (reported test execution durations, not whole-job wall times).
- Targeted stylelint, oxlint, UI typecheck, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

- CI follow-up: initial CI run 39887989805 found the older form-controls browser test expecting the whole transcript to be selectable. All 21 tests in that file pass (5.84s command wall; 4.27s test time), with targeted lint/format and an independent delta review clean. body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the microphone input-device picker's keyboard-focus ring looks off-center because its chevron sits left of the focused button's center.

## User Impact

The revealed microphone-device chevron is centered within its existing focus ring and hit area in Chat and New Session. Focus visibility, button size, and keyboard behavior are unchanged. No configuration changes or user action are required.

title: fix: announce Models provider read failures
body: ## What Problem This Solves Settings → Models displays provider-access and provider-usage read failures, but the existing notices were ordinary text. Assistive technology therefore had no alert semantics for these asynchronous failures. The primary error section could also be recreated as Retry entered its busy state, which would reinsert an unchanged alert before the new request had finished. ## User Impact Both existing read-error notices are exposed as alerts. The primary notice stays mounted while retrying, and successful recovery removes the error. Provider filtering, visible messages, layout, request handling and authentication retain their existing behavior. Refresh and Retry remain disabled while the relevant read is pending; no configuration changes or migration are required. ## Why This Change Was Made `renderProviderNoticeRow` owns the two read-error notices, so the alert role belongs there rather than on the entire provider list. A default Solid `Show` owns the primary error section, keeping it stable while the retry button's disabled state updates. The button remains outside the alert. The existing browser regression covers both the primary auth-status read and independently loaded usage read. It now holds a retry response and verifies that the original alert remains connected while controls are disabled, alongside filtering and recovery. This catches repeated insertion of the previous error without changing the request owners or adding announcement state. ## Evidence The bundled Control UI was exercised with synthetic Gateway responses in Chromium 156.0.8078.4, English/dark at 1440 × 1000. On the baseline, both visible read errors failed the expected-alert assertion with 0 alerts instead of 1. The held-refresh regression also failed on the original implementation: one alert remained visible, but the original alert node had been replaced before the response settled. Both cases pass with the correction. - Changed-file formatting, lint, i18n verification and all selected production/test type graphs passed. - Four related owner test files passed 51 tests. - Both bundled-browser scenarios passed, including provider filtering, stable alerts while retrying, disabled controls, recovery and zero credential-save/logout requests. The test file took 2.856 seconds; its invocation took 24.53 seconds including the 19.77-second UI build. - Accessibility snapshots change the notices from ordinary text to alerts. The independently captured before/after images are byte-identical, as expected for a semantic-only change. This proves browser accessibility semantics and lifecycle behavior, not audible output from a particular screen reader. Hosted checks remain a separate verification requirement. ### Accessibility snapshots Before, each notice is ordinary `text`. On the corrected candidate: ```yaml - alert: Provider access could not be refreshed. Try again. - button "Retry" ``` The supplemental case exposes: ```yaml - alert: Provider usage is unavailable; the last request failed. Refresh to retry. ``` ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Provider access failure | ![Provider access failure displayed as ordinary text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e9029b3-4aa2-490e-aded-14bf8b2f6879) | ![Provider access failure displayed with alert semantics](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e9029b3-4aa2-490e-aded-14bf8b2f6879) | | Provider usage failure | ![Provider usage failure displayed as ordinary text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a572487-1472-494f-83a1-5d88c37b6cba) | ![Provider usage failure displayed with alert semantics](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a572487-1472-494f-83a1-5d88c37b6cba) | ### Visual verification - Baseline: d5ecc7da0ba84072600ddd046fef58fb8c8b58bb - Exact head: `00a35ef42b9e71fd57ed8b4b962e42e420347620` - Scenario: Fail models\.authStatus or usage\.status after Refresh on Settings Models, then recover with Retry or Refresh\. - Runtime/build: Chromium 156\.0\.8078\.4; bundled Control UI at 00a35ef42b9e71fd57ed8b4b962e42e420347620; synthetic Gateway responses - Baseline alerts: 0 for each of 2 visible read errors - Candidate alerts: 1 for each error; 0 after recovery - Credential mutations: 0 authSetApiKey and authLogout requests in both candidate cases - Retained alert: Same alert node survives provider filtering and held refresh in both cases; Refresh and Retry disabled while pending - Baseline failed at missing alert assertion for both methods - Candidate passed both bundled\-browser regression cases - Same 1440x1000 viewport, dark theme, English, synthetic fixture and screenshot helper - Before and after bundles independently built from recorded source - Screen\-reader audible output is not certified - Primary retained\-alert regression failed on original contribution and passed with the default Show correction - Recording omitted: Semantic\-only role change has no honest visual manifestation; screenshots qualify unchanged visible feedback, while browser role assertions and accessibility snapshots prove the contract\. No keyboard, focus, animation or pointer behavior changes\. The two independently captured images in each pair have identical bytes; each pair therefore shares one uploaded asset. The accessibility assertions above establish the semantic difference. Contributed by Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm).

title: fix: recover sessions blocked by oversized workspace artifacts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local managed sandbox session has no supported recovery path when a newly generated file exceeds the reconciliation limit and blocks every later workspace preparation.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can run `openclaw sandbox recover --session <key> --path <relative-path>` to preserve one selected oversized file outside synchronization, then retry the session without losing its remaining source edits. Recovery is explicit and administrator-authorized. Recovered artifacts are retained outside automatic worktree cleanup; the operator owns their subsequent storage and cleanup.

Already-admitted source files, staged receipts, remote-worker workspaces, Git metadata, symlinks, and hardlinks remain unsupported/refused. File-size limits and ignore rules are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A failed oversized checkpoint remains pending, and the next preparation retries it before the agent can run. The recovery command reuses the local workspace owner, reconciliation lease, sandbox quiescence, canonical source inventory, and no-overwrite filesystem move. It relocates only the explicitly selected new oversized retained file; ordinary preparation still owns settlement. A caller-supplied recovery ID permits a safe retry after a lost response.

No new database state, automatic deletion, or blanket cache exclusion is introduced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through real sandbox preparation, Git staging, and SQLite projection state: a 64 MiB + 1 byte retained file rejects checkpoint and repeated later preparations while preserving the pending reference.
- Regression verifies explicit relocation, recovery-ID retry, source-edit settlement on the next preparation, preserved file size/content marker, and refusal of admitted source paths, traversal, symlinks, and hardlinks.
- Seven affected suites passed (119 tests, one existing skip); the final owner/schema and metadata-policy replay passed 104 tests.
- Core production typecheck and the four owning test typecheck graphs passed; scoped lint, formatting, documentation lint, protocol registry, and Swift/Kotlin protocol contract/determinism checks passed.
- Simplification reuses existing state/lease owners and removes duplicate metadata-read configuration. Independent autoreview through P2 found no actionable P0–P2 findings on production head `20ecebdd957b12fb3cd3d7672c8eb2d6af7119d9`. A fresh bounded review of the subsequent tests-only authority delta also found no actionable P0–P2 findings; its reviewed tree `7820431920e840ad321968797ef03eff3332a8db` matches published head `4a92573c7c0ea5d8d0426d526fad3a67cefb4828`. Both reviews included the complete unchanged workspace state/lease/quiescence owners and installed fs-safe implementation; reviewers did not independently execute the tests.
- The broader changed-path type selector encounters existing core-test root budgets (gateway-root 725/720, infra 729/720). This change adds no test-root files; no budget exception or suppression was added.
- Live qualification on `2e58968f56ecce4018767dc17c3af70d750c04dd` (identical Git tree to published head `20ecebdd957b12fb3cd3d7672c8eb2d6af7119d9`): a real CLI command routed to an isolated, ready Gateway and preserved the selected 67,108,865-byte file. After that Gateway stopped, a fresh process successfully prepared the workspace and settled the remaining source edit. The preserved file matched its original SHA-256. This exercised recovery, persistence, and preparation, not model generation. The test Gateway and fixture were removed; no hosting service or unrelated files were changed.

- Added production-owner authority proof using an isolated real Gateway, genuine paired clients, real session/worktree owners, and actual filesystem relocation. A writer-only caller is rejected; an initially authorized administrator revoked during awaited file opening, a replaced session, and a rebound worktree all fail before relocation. Each denial preserves the original artifact hash, source edit and pending reference, leaves the destination absent, and records zero moves. The current administrator positive control performs one real move and retains the hash. No production guard changes were needed.
- Latest tests-only delta: all 9 tests in the owning Gateway method suite pass. The new composed test took 12.468 seconds; the complete shard took 21.09 seconds wall time. The owning `core-test-gateway-methods` typecheck, scoped lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. No new test-root file or budget exception was added.
- Remaining live-proof gap: a post-recovery public chat/model turn was not completed. The attributed CLI rejected child-session messaging before connection, and the parent browser route could not start. The admission guard was preserved; no raw-RPC or attribution-marker workaround was used. title: fix(ui): announce agent file save failures and conflicts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: screen readers can miss a failed agent-file save or workspace conflict while the editable draft remains on screen.

## User Impact

User impact: the existing failure and conflict messages are exposed as alerts, including their existing Reload and Overwrite recovery controls. Normal file information stays nonassertive. No file permissions, write ordering, draft handling, focus behavior, or visual layout changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a parent cannot continue a kept native child after its completed run falls outside the 30-minute recent-run window, even though the child and its stored lineage still exist.

## User Impact

Parents can list, recall, inspect, and continue their retained native children under the existing session-tool scope. This does not grant global visibility or let a parent take over a child occupied by another active controller, including cancellation-in-progress.

Incognito, self-only, sandbox/A2A, sharing revocation, and exact agent/session identity checks remain in force. Archiving keeps its existing behavior rather than erasing lineage. No configuration option, schema migration, dependency, lease, or authorization store is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway relationship owner now separates durable native parent facts from run recency and from the actual current executor/reservation. Lists, exact ownership resolution, history, search, and status consume that canonical relationship projection; terminal and unowned controller snapshots do not confer control.

Send admission distinguishes durable parent access, temporary live-controller access, and independently authorized peer access. Durable parents retain queued notification access despite exact-incarnation binding. Explicit invocation ceilings still prohibit notifications and persistent watches. Temporary control cannot mint persistent completion/watch rights and is rechecked at the final effect. An explicit stored parent remains readable during foreign execution; legacy spawnedBy-only lineage yields to the verified active controller. The released history-only fallback for older Gateways is preserved without extending it to send/search/status.

title: fix(plugins): install native dependencies when stage execution is denied
body:
Related: #193772

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin installation rejecting a complete native dependency when a sandbox denies execution inside the writable install stage.

## User Impact

Staged native packages can pass completeness validation using filesystem metadata. Actual execution still requires existing runtime and OS authority. Missing or incomplete packages still receive one fresh-cache retry; persistent failure preserves the previous generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old installer asks for `X_OK`, which can fail with `EPERM` even when staging filesystem operations are permitted. Check the existing admitted path for a regular file and Unix executable mode instead; Windows `.exe` files do not require Unix bits. Genuine metadata errors still fail verification. Admission, integrity, aliases, native declarations, backup and publication remain with their existing owners.

Thanks to @RalphPepperoni for the report, Seatbelt reproduction and prepared patch in #193772. This adapts the metadata/mode portion only; no verified source-commit identity was supplied for a reporter author trailer. title: feat(ios): open matching chats from push notifications
body:
Related: #193113

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary iOS push notification opens the app but does not take someone to the chat the notification is about.

## User Impact

A push with an optional session destination can open that existing chat on the currently connected Gateway, after checking the current profile's access, without sending a message. Notifications without a destination keep their existing behavior. Missing, inaccessible, or wrong-Gateway destinations leave the current screen unchanged; taps do not automatically switch Gateways.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing `push.test` path and `openclaw nodes push --session <key>` rather than adding a general notification operation or arbitrary deep links. The Gateway resolves the destination and supplies its own identity. APNs sends revalidate through the existing session-read owner, and iOS resolves the destination on its current authenticated route before calling the existing `openChat` owner. Cold-launch handoff and reconnect use existing lifecycle owners, with duplicate-tap suppression and Watch/approval precedence preserved.

This does not add counters, registrations, or background wakes. The public changes in #193491 (unread badges) and #193033 (main-chat discovery) were inspected; this change preserves those owners. The API direction is presented for maintainer review, not as an already accepted product decision.

## Evidence

- Red/green regression: the new optional destination was rejected by the original closed request schema; it passes with the schema and generated runtime validators updated.
- **100 focused tests passed across five files:** protocol schema, APNs payload/refusal behavior, Gateway push handling, existing session visibility, and CLI option forwarding. The CLI test wrapper also completed its runtime build. These are synthetic/mocked boundary tests, not real APNs or iPhone acceptance.

title: fix(update): name and retry busy files during backup capture
body:
Refs #193673. Builds on the diagnostic transport in #187927 by @wr-web (Wang Rui), with both existing Co-authored-by trailers preserved on all commits.

## Problem and behavior

A Windows backup can stop on a descriptor-read EBUSY without identifying the retained source file. The isolated probe now retries Windows EBUSY/EPERM twice, after 50 ms and 100 ms, closing the descriptor before waiting. Persistent failure names the source path and error code and refuses archive publication. Recovery logs a warning. EACCES and non-Windows errors do not retry.

Rebased onto main `225d2f7d4f18`. Main still lacks this busy-file handling; its 4,096-path batching, 10-second child deadline, recursive ETIMEDOUT splitting (#194239), timeout guidance (#193970), and backup snapshot changes (#194230/#194234) remain intact. Tests retain both timeout recovery and busy-file contracts. No source is silently skipped or guessed to be non-SQLite.

#195281 is potentially related, but its redacted package-update EBUSY report lacks the syscall/stack needed to establish the same cause. This fix must be present in the runtime performing backup capture; a staged candidate cannot repair an already-running older updater.

## Current-head evidence

Head `c34128c3d75425bc87928c234da35477905676f4`. This follow-up changes only one test-allocation scalar; source and tests remain identical to tested/reviewed parent `b9347326c65c`.

Linux [Crabbox/Testbox 42512351293](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42512351293), with frozen candidate probe-file hashes matched and tests run serially under `timeout 180`:

| Named file | Result | Wrapper wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.test.ts` | 12 passed, including main timeout recovery | 37.07s (cold worker compile) |
| `src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.test.ts` | 3 passed | 8.18s |
| `src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.windows.test.ts` | 2 skipped on Linux | 7.73s |

The capture regression fails with main's probe modules on the missing path/code diagnostic and passes with the fix; capture uses the real isolated child and preserves the source/no-archive invariant. Six-file targeted lint passes remotely (2.93s). Dependency installation and shared worker compilation were confined to Testbox after local setup proved unavailable.

- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Local lint/test setup encountered stale linked dependencies; these were not repaired on the production Team host.
- Independent local Codex autoreview covered the complete frozen base-to-head delta and backup capture/snapshot callers at P0–P2: scoped-clean, no findings. Source-only review.
- Allocation follow-up: 138 probe/capture lines + 223 native Windows lines = 361 literal LF lines. The original [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42514071205/job/128833652646) rejected 362 credits for 361 lines. The CI-equivalent temporary merge-index check against main `a5888561dd11`, using `--base origin/main --no-merge-base --staged`, now passes: `Test lines OK: 6585343; ceiling: 6585482; slack: 139.` Inherited debt is zero. Current-head [CI 42515751607](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42515751607) is pending.

Prior-head [CI 42106962448](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42106962448) supplied genuine Windows range-lock recovery/refusal and a published-stable Linux upgrade/restore specimen for `8926dd997ae2`. Those are supporting prior evidence, not current-head Windows or upgrade proof. Current-head native Windows, build/typecheck, and upgrade coverage remain pending until the corresponding CI jobs pass. An automatic draft CI skip is not a green gate.

## Scope and limits

Production delta against main: +87/−20 in the two existing probe modules. Retained regression allocations (138 and 223 lines) cover child-I/O/archive refusal and native Windows lock lifecycle; the shared scalar is unchanged. The new tests protect observable retry bounds, accurate classification, named failure, preserved sources, and no incomplete archive publication.

This PR remains **DRAFT**. #187927 remains open.

title: fix: enable dictation for session-scoped guests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-scoped guests could send chat messages but could not dictate them. The microphone depended on operator-wide catalog/config access; recording and transcript delivery also required operator privileges.

## User Impact

Guests can dictate into chats they are authorized to write, including starting from the New Session composer. Transcripts remain editable drafts until explicitly sent. Voice settings and conversational Talk remain restricted; no broader guest role permissions or new configuration options are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse session authorization for a minimal transcription-readiness projection and transcription-only sessions. Keep provider/model overrides and full settings restricted.
- Bind recordings to the authorized session and originating connection. Retain that authority for the relay lifetime and recheck it before provider audio, finalization, readiness, and transcript delivery; revoke and clean up together.
- Carry the same live-authority check into the shared provider WebSocket transport. Recheck after asynchronous connection setup and at actual writes and graceful finalization, so queued/reconnected audio cannot outlive its authorization. Discard and revoked cleanup abort without invoking provider finalization. The callback is optional, preserving existing callers without it.
- Prepare a normal session for new-chat dictation and reuse it for the first send, rather than falling back to a shared session or creating a second chat.
- Preserve the prepared target and message idempotency key through interruption. Terminal timeout/error acknowledgments enter the existing persisted failed-message recovery path instead of being reported as accepted.
- Preserve typed speech-provider configuration and existing exports in catalog test mocks; adapt operator-only catalog tests to explicit read authority. Resolve the upstream provider-context import migration without changing the reviewed dictation behavior.

## Evidence

- Guest admission and UI regressions fail on the base and pass with the fix. Additional red/green proof covers provider audio after backing-session deletion, revoked relay finalization, and persisted initial-turn recovery.
- Real Gateway/provider-wire regression was red on `f9b01e4`: explicit discard sent `audio.done`, and reconnect-buffered audio reached the vendor after backing-session deletion. Both now pass, with authorized audio and normal finalization as positive controls and ordered socket-close barriers rather than sleep-based absence checks.
- A real WebSocket regression also proves authority is rechecked after asynchronous credentials resolve, before opening the provider connection. Shared transport: 26 tests passed. Bundled OpenAI, xAI, Mistral, and ElevenLabs provider compatibility: 4 files, 62 tests passed.
- Backend siblings: 3 suites, 20 tests passed, including real authenticated Gateway WebSocket admission and a real multipart HTTP file-transcription sibling with synthetic providers. Together with the new provider-wire case, the final transport repair passed 109 targeted tests.
- Catalog compatibility: 4 suites, 113 tests passed. Initial-turn recovery: 3 suites, 34 tests passed. Complete browser dictation suite: 12 tests passed, including guest-only and mixed read/write authority; those unchanged paths retain their earlier proof.
- Fresh incremental repair review found no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings in its supplied diff. Its unchanged-source and test-execution limitations are not treated as a full clean certificate; the author inspected the owning lifecycle and bundled callers and ran the boundary tests separately. Earlier lifetime-authority, audio-admission, terminal-ack, and provider-flush/finalization findings were addressed.
- Core source, affected core-test graphs, and UI TypeScript checks pass. Changed-file formatting/lint and diff checks pass. Stale max-lines/assertion allowances were removed; mock-export and test-line ratchets pass.
- The separate 1,465-line test allocation records exactly the measured net regression growth, including 259 added lines for the real provider-wire and asynchronous-connection regressions. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged.
- A prior-head Bun permission-picker focus assertion failed once. The focused six-test replay passed without changes, but did not establish inheritance or a fix. Full CI subsequently passed at `f9b01e4`.
- Final head `d93012e1c5ebfd8ef50a0699d3547d2735cbdd84`: 95 successful checks, 73 skipped, 1 neutral, none failed or pending, including [the CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42131955861). Five CodeQL jobs initially failed during result upload; all cleared after retrying only the failed jobs on the same head, without source changes or gate exceptions.
- [Current-head ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193658#issuecomment-6666229145) reports **Findings: None** and `review-state:ready`; [re-review completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193658#issuecomment-6672103838) is confirmed.

[Before/after screenshots and editable-transcript proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193658#issuecomment-6665731560).

No live server configuration was changed, and paid speech-to-text providers were not exercised. Browser audio and provider transcripts use deterministic fixtures; Gateway, provider WebSocket, and multipart HTTP boundaries are real local transports.

Related: #187612 (production installer work stays separate). Requested by the test-health campaign parent ruling of 2026-11-05 17:32Z.

## What Problem This Solves

The canonical-checkout alias and configured-upgrade Doctor-failure unit fixtures queried the public npm registry while resolving Node engines. Registry availability and latency therefore affected otherwise local installer tests.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Installer unit tests use deterministic engine metadata while preserving the real installer control flow and existing assertions. **test-only; scripts/install.sh untouched**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unexpected non-`view` calls return failure.

All keeper assertions, watchdog synchronization, timeout-owner cases, and deadlines remain unchanged. Test lines remain exactly 3,679 (net 0); production lines net 0. The test-line baseline is unchanged. No new helper or production seam is introduced.

## Evidence

All six timing runs used only `pnpm test test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`, wrapped in `timeout 300`, sequentially. Each passed 228 tests with the existing Darwin-only skip.

Prettier 3.9.10 `--print-width 100 --check test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts` passed, matching the repository's configured width. `git diff --check` passed.
