<details>
<summary>Earlier proposal and evidence, preserved with their original scope</summary>

Related: #187722

## What Problem This Solves

iOS Talk has no microphone mute button separate from ending the conversation.

## User Impact

Adds a microphone toggle to the Talk activity strip. Works across native speech recognition, Gateway relay, and WebRTC, retaining mute across Talk restarts within the app run.

The UI follow-up uses the composer's scaled 17-point medium SF Symbol styling and retains a 44-point hit target. A crossed-out mic is gray when input is on and orange when muted. The collapsed strip is about 48 points tall at normal text size. Idle muted realtime Talk displays **Connected (Realtime)** above **Microphone muted**; thinking, speaking, connecting, and error statuses remain visible. VoiceOver continues to announce the action and microphone state. While Talk is active, the composer's dictation/voice-note microphone is hidden and returns after Talk ends. Mute stays exclusively in the Talk activity strip, not in the dictation button's position.

**Ready for review.** The requester has verified pre-mute word preservation on an iPhone. Returned kit v3 now verifies the Apple build, all 373 selected iOS tests, and all 21 selected shared-package tests for the repaired candidate matching `c22355b8f89a`. Actual normal-size UI screenshots and the requester’s lifecycle recording are now attached below. Remaining physical audio/lifecycle cases, large-text layout, and pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this recording. The confirmed conflict with `main` was resolved in `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`, integrating base `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`. GitHub now reports the branch mergeable. Current-head CI is green (38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures or pending checks at the November 6 check). The requester has also posted current-head targeted simulator red/green results and base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders, summarized below. Earlier Mac-kit results remain evidence for their explicitly identified candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports the Android feature from @davelutztx in #187722, using the existing iOS Talk manager and transport owners. No new configuration, permissions, dependencies, or protocol changes. Shared control defaults leave existing macOS callers unchanged.

Android reference checked on November 5, 2026: still open at `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`.

**Native finalization repair:** [Android feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6547128842) and the [iPhone report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033) showed that immediate recognizer cancellation discards pre-mute trailing words. Native continuous Talk now closes the audio tap/engine immediately and calls `endAudio()`, retaining that recognition generation until a usable final result or a two-second fallback. Errors, empty finals, and the deadline use the latest nonempty partial; settlement submits once and retires old callbacks. Quick unmute/re-mute cannot replace the draining recognizer. End Talk/session teardown cancels it, and gateway replacement invalidates its transcript owner. Realtime mute and accepted reply playback paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Layout issue also observed without the mute button — November 6

**Requester comparison result:** the requester reproduced the intermittent issue with and without the mute button in **the same chats containing very long messages**, and reports **no apparent worsening with this PR**. This is the requester's comparative device observation; it was not independently executed in this session.

This supports treating the overlap as a pre-existing long-message layout problem, **not an observed mute-button regression or exacerbation**. It remains a separate investigation, not a blocker specific to this PR on the available evidence. The earlier blanket merge hold is withdrawn. No layout repair or root cause is claimed, and other review and validation requirements are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Original observation and related investigation</summary>

The supplied recording and four screenshots show lost reading position and newer user/assistant bubbles overlapping older assistant content. The overlap is visible even after the Talk card disappears. No message-role or persisted-transcript corruption has been established.

![Real iPhone screenshot: newer chat bubbles overlap an older assistant response](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b46564f-ae0c-403a-a419-ea7bc374dd7c)

This inspected crop removes model metadata and unrelated surrounding UI; originals are retained unchanged. Seven transcript layout/identity/rendering files are byte-identical to base `0499ce287bb8`. That source comparison alone did not prove baseline behavior; the requester’s subsequent device comparison is the additional evidence.

[PR #192232](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192232) addresses related lazy-height instability causing blank transcripts. It remains an investigation lead, not a verified repair for this overlap. No code from it has been imported, no layout repair is claimed, and no broad device/provider test matrix is requested.

</details>

### Conflict-only integration — November 5

- Published head: `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`; verified ancestry includes main `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`.
- The sole manual conflict was the demo fixture helper extraction: main independently made the same extraction with different helper names. Kept main's names and verified the complete fixture file matches that main revision byte-for-byte. The fixture and shared initializer build repairs are now already upstream, reducing the PR-relative diff to 13 files.
- Native mute manager/regressions, WebRTC mute, relay mute, and Talk-strip UI are byte-identical to the earlier Apple-tested candidate. All 13 PR-relative files plus the two upstream build-repair files were verified against the published head.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,637 entries, no drift); base-relative staged whitespace check passed. Fresh full-candidate Auto Review against the integrated base: P0-only, scoped-clean, no findings. No Apple code was executed in this Linux session; these checks do not replace current-head Apple integration validation.
- [Latest completed ClawSweeper verdict](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6626345064) covers current head `417349df1cf4`: overall Gold, patch quality Diamond, no actionable findings, ready for maintainer review, and no before-merge items listed. It notes remaining declared device-proof gaps separately; this rating is advisory. The targeted source-hunk red/green report and requester device evidence are retained below.
- Current-head CI is green as observed November 6: 38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures/pending checks. This includes iOS screenshot/evidence and Periphery build jobs; the dedicated iOS build matrix is skipped, so this is not a claim that every Apple test suite ran in CI. No merge has been submitted.

- Native repair published at `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7`; the three repair files were verified byte-for-byte against the reviewed workspace matching the locally supplied patch.
- **Requester device report, November 4:** tested the supplied native-finalization repair locally and confirmed that words spoken before mute are no longer cut off. This is a manual result for the supplied local patch. Kit v2 subsequently exposed build blockers; kit v3 confirms the build repairs and automated regressions pass, as detailed below.
- `git diff --check` and staged whitespace check: passed.
- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` added the source-owned UI wording entries; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,549 entries, no inventory drift).
- Fresh Auto Review of the complete local candidate against `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a`: **P0-only**, scoped-clean, no findings. This does not certify Swift compilation or Apple runtime behavior.
- Separate source-only lifecycle review of the finalization changes and tests: no unresolved concrete issues after preserving the latest partial on empty finals and adding automatic-unmute-resume cases. This was an excerpt-based audit, not executed proof.
- Author simplification pass: finalization stays in the existing Talk manager, reuses its recognition and transcript-processing generations, and splits input shutdown from recognizer retirement. The added bounded pending state prevents pre-mute word loss without a second capture manager or configuration option.
- Added gateway-boundary regressions in `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: final results with/without an earlier partial; error/timeout/empty-final fallback; exactly-once send; quick unmute/re-mute, including no-word automatic resume; stale callbacks; End Talk/session replacement. They exercise actual `GatewayNodeSession` `chat.send` framing with synthetic recognition callbacks and a terminal-aborted acknowledgement to stop at the submission boundary. **Passed on the requester's Mac in kit v3:** all seven regression definitions, including their parameterized cases. This is fixed-candidate green execution; automated red-on-base execution was not performed.
- [Requester device results at `7e0def937e73`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033): iOS app build passed; 27 tests in three iOS suites passed; xAI Gateway relay and OpenAI WebRTC mute/unmute worked on an iPhone. Native recognition lost a word spoken before mute. These are **prior-head results**, not proof of the native finalization repair or revised UI.
- The same report found the shared OpenClawKit test target blocked by a pre-existing `ChatViewModelTests.swift` initializer mismatch, so shared relay tests did not run on that host.
- Apple compilation and automated Swift tests were run on the requester's Mac, not in this Linux session. The returned xcresult summary/tree and Swift XML/logs were independently inspected here. Actual current UI screenshots from the requester's recording are now attached below. Remaining physical lifecycle/input/playback cases still need verification; the silent recording does not establish audio behavior. Chat mockups and render-smoke tests remain separate from runtime screenshot evidence.

### Additional requester evidence on integrated head — November 5–6

All reports below name head `417349df1cf4` and base `0499ce287bb8`.

- [Simulator red/green report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6667982238): on Xcode 27.2, the requester reports **red** after reverting only finalization, muted-recognition, and relay-silence source hunks while retaining the tests: 7 mute tests with 21 issues, and 10 relay tests with 3 issues. **Green** on unchanged PR head: 18 tests across `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests` and `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, plus 10 shared relay tests, all passing. Reported mute-suite time: 721 seconds. This is targeted regression sensitivity, **not a literal plain-base test run**. These are attributed results from the comment; raw xcresult/log bundles for this new run were not supplied to this session.
- [Base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669395455): publicly accessible immutable images were downloaded; normal and large-text active/muted examples and large-text connecting were inspected. They show real SwiftUI `ImageRenderer` output from a fixed 393-point test fixture at 3x, not full-app screenshots. Head adds the expected gray/orange crossed microphone and muted wording. At accessibility3 the muted text wraps mid-word (`Micropho / ne muted`); status/transcript text is also constrained. Treat the real chat's large-text layout as unverified, not accepted based on this fixture.
- [Requester's evidence mapping and remaining device checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669410988): simulator assertions cover finalization, fallback, exactly-once submission, Talk-session restart, quick toggles, and teardown. Audible playback and physical-device lifecycle/large-text verification are still pending. The earlier successful native trailing-word device report remains valid and should not be discarded.

**Restart contract clarification:** mute is retained across Talk stop/start and reconnect within the same app run. It is intentionally not persisted across quitting and relaunching the app. A full-app relaunch retaining mute is therefore **not** an acceptance requirement for this PR; the relevant retention check is restarting Talk without terminating the app.

### Requester real-device lifecycle recording — November 5

The requester supplied a 36-second iPhone recording and explicitly authorized use of the test-chat screen. These are **actual device screenshots, not mockups**. The recording does not display a build commit, so this is requester-supplied visual evidence, separate from the hash-verified kit v3 test run.

![iOS Talk lifecycle: active at 00:04, muted at 00:14, unmuted at 00:22, and ended at 00:34](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3f306d3-3bb9-48a0-84e0-4b23fce03bbc)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/271983e6-399c-4788-b066-920970c21f33

Observed in the recording:
- **00:04:** Listening (Realtime), gray crossed-out microphone in the Talk card, and no composer dictation microphone.
- **00:14:** Connected (Realtime), orange crossed-out microphone and Microphone muted label. The Talk controls remain present and the agent reply appears in chat.
- **00:22:** Unmuted; Listening (Realtime) and the gray mute action return.
- **00:34:** Talk ended; the Talk card is gone and the composer dictation microphone is visible again.
- A stop/restart segment is also present. It is not independently counted as proof of mute retention or capture exclusion because the recording does not expose touch events or microphone input.

Publication edits only: the composer model label is covered, the final iOS Control Center transition is omitted (published clip is 34.5 seconds), and the silent audio track and file metadata are removed. Test-chat text and Talk controls are unchanged. The original recording is retained locally unchanged. Its audio track contains no audible signal; this evidence does **not** prove TTS continuity or post-mute speech exclusion. Normal-size current UI is covered; large-text layout and a pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this clip.

### Returned Mac kit v3 results — November 5

**Apple build and both selected test groups passed. No rerun is needed for the collector's summary error.**

Returned archive: `talk-mute-results-20261105T034708Z-0712fe.zip`, SHA-256 `1fb79eeebf7d716ca593c263e4939da1230e34f6cd28980ba55a78909edf715e`. This was the pinned `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7` base plus bundled build-repair SHA-256 `f0c863e5a3c1ffa1b379908840c256d7ef54f77fb9febc1c5f41c21e813a8684`, not a bare-base run. The six manifest source hashes match the reviewed files published at `c22355b8f89a6abb0ebce72dd0eced45cecb0b93` and remained unchanged during the run.

Environment: Xcode 27.2, Apple Swift 6.4.2, macOS 27.2 arm64, isolated iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5. Caller-selected Node 26.12.1 and repository-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 passed preflight. The created simulator was deleted successfully.

| Check | Result | Reported wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS `build-for-testing`, including strict lint | Passed, exit 0 | 568.084 s |
| iOS `test-without-building` | 373 tests passed; 0 failures, skips, or expected failures | 777.116 s |
| Shared `swift test` | 21 tests in 3 suites passed; 0 failures or skips | 174.464 s, including build |

iOS xcresult records 373 test definitions / 429 parameterized invocations. All eight requested suites and all seven required mute regression definitions are present and passed:

- `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: 7
- `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`: 11
- `TalkModeManagerTests`: 51
- `TalkRealtimeVoiceSessionCleanupTests`: 7
- `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`: 258
- `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`: 13
- `OpenClawTypographyTests`: 22
- `LocalFixtureChatTransportTests`: 4

The shared XML and console output independently confirm `RealtimeTalkRelaySessionAudioInputTests`, `ChatTalkControlTests`, and `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests` all passed. This includes relay silence while muted, queued-audio retirement, and preservation of capture/reply playback in the test harness.

**Collector-only defect:** kit v3's top-level summary says `shared: results_unverified` / `attention_required` because it looked only for `shared-results.xml`; Swift emitted `shared-results-swift-testing.xml`. That actual report is present in the returned archive with 21 passing cases and no failures/skips, and the command exited 0. The local collector now reads framework-suffixed reports as well. Its regression reproduces the false warning on shipped v3 and passes after the fix; the original returned ZIP is preserved unchanged. This correction does not alter or rerun the app tests.

The native regression fixtures took approximately 2 minutes for final-result submission and 1 minute 20 seconds each for fallback and quick-toggle groups; these are measured automated harness times, not a physical speech-finalization latency claim. The two-second native finalization deadline remains unchanged. Apple tests are green, but this run does not establish red-on-base automation, physical speech exclusion/playback across every transport, or screenshot acceptance.

#### Earlier v2 blockers — repaired and superseded by v3

Kit v2 reached both builds but executed no tests: strict lint rejected two raw-orange uses in `ChatTalkActivityViews.swift` and the unchanged 210-line demo seed function; shared compilation rejected the old route-lease initializer in `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests`.

The follow-up at `c22355b8f89a` uses existing warning/muted theme tokens, extracts two demo branches unchanged, and updates the routing-test initializer/closure signatures. No lint gate or assertion was disabled; native microphone-finalization code and tests were unchanged. Kit v3's successful build and tests above now verify these repairs on Apple tools.

### Local device test

Check out this PR, follow `apps/ios/README.md` for signing/build setup, run `pnpm ios:gen`, and build/run `apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj` on an iPhone.

- Mute/unmute while an answer plays; verify playback and accepted work continue.
- Speak while muted, then unmute; verify muted speech is not replayed.
- Native regression: say **five four**, mute, then say **three two**. Exactly one request should contain **five four**, excluding speech after mute. Also try muting before the first partial appears, quick unmute/re-mute, and End Talk during finalization.
- Restart Talk while muted, then test standalone push-to-talk after ending Talk.
- Verify the composer mic disappears during Talk and returns after End Talk; mute stays in the Talk card.
- Check the control at normal and large text sizes; capture real before/after screenshots.

The selected automated iOS and shared suites have passed in kit v3; no repeat is requested for unchanged source. The checklist above remains the physical-device acceptance scope.

## Android maintainer handoff (#187722)

The same native lifecycle correction applies to Android: stop new input and ask `SpeechRecognizer.stopListening()` to finalize, rather than snapshotting the current partial and immediately canceling/destroying the recognizer. Preserve the original recognition/session identity until `onResults`, or a bounded `onError`/deadline fallback to the latest partial; settle once before retiring that identity. Muted/draining callbacks must not restart capture or interrupt playback. Quick toggles and End Talk/session replacement must not leak old speech into a new capture or conversation.

The **five four → mute → three two** regression should send only **five four**, once. Also cover a final with no earlier partial, error/timeout fallback, duplicate finals, quick toggles, and teardown. iOS's two-second deadline is an implementation choice to validate on-device, not a prescribed Android timeout. This note is retained here for the Android author/maintainers; no Android code or metadata was changed.

## Worked on by

- @Marvinthebored

title: feat(storage): support read-only PostgreSQL standby inspection
fix(codex): restore physical-exit recovery test controls
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three Gateway recovery tests fail before reaching their physical-exit controls because Codex now spawns its native child inside the stdio Worker (#192543).

## User Impact

Restores the fixture used to verify that recovery waits for physical exit, cancellation prevents reacquisition, and an unconfirmed exit preserves the conversation binding. This changes one test file.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the native-process facade on its real spawn event by matching its input stream to the stdio Worker, and apply the existing retention override to the Worker launch message. The facade's exit notification still comes from the real native child's exit; Worker completion does not supply it. Original prototype functions are captured through typed own-property descriptors, and both spies forward their live receiver with `.call`.

Reuse existing HTTP/model fixtures and share Gateway close cleanup. All seven cases, recovery assertions and deadlines remain. The complete PR is **60 additions / 63 removals**, **664 LF versus 667 on the base: net −3 test lines**. No lint-disable comments, baseline/allocation edits, retries, margin increases, test deletions, or production changes.

title: fix(zalouser): deliver received attachments as readable media
body:
Supersedes #159253, thanks @ceo633.
Closes #159249.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: files, photos, and videos received through Zalo Personal reach the agent as filenames and CDN links without readable attachments.

## User Impact

Authorized attachments reach the agent as stored media with their original document filenames. Failed downloads leave an attachment-unavailable notice alongside the message. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry recognized received attachments through Zalouser's existing normalizer and monitor into the shared media store and inbound context. Downloads run after sender and mention checks, enforce HTTPS and Zalo CDN hosts across redirects, retain private-network/MIME/size protections and deadlines, and honor monitor and ingress cancellation. Recheck sender and command access before downloading and before dispatch; retire newly staged files if access or cancellation rejects the turn.

Production grows by 105 lines because the handoff was missing. There is no dead or duplicate media path in this owner to remove without unrelated changes. The repair adds no transport abstraction, SDK capability, dependency, or configuration option. A separate 219-line regression allocation covers the new durable-ingress suite; the shared test budget is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Synthetic Testbox proof on base `9e59d23aff4d553dd264133d5efeffd10e359a40`: all five initial cases failed because no readable media was materialized; the same cases passed with the repair.
- The final inbound-media suite passes all 16 cases: document/photo/video bytes and MIME at agent input; filename preservation; access, mention, and ordinary-link exclusions; HTTPS, CDN host, private address, redirect, downgrade, and size rejection; revoked/cancelled staging cleanup while preserving a neighboring file. Test bodies take about 7 seconds; the final named-file run took 42.66 seconds including import/worker preparation.
- The existing group-gating, account-scope, and quote/normalization suites pass (36 cases). Exact-head PR CI is the broad proof.
- Touched-file formatting, syntax lint, and whitespace checks pass. Targeted typed lint reports zero warnings/errors and the Zalouser package typecheck passes on [Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41785326306).
- Independent autoreview completed P0–P2 with no actionable findings against the complete local candidate and media/ingress owner contracts. Subsequent test-only corrections use the context builder's canonical empty media array and a void-returning setup hook.
- Follow-up CI repair replaces the inline attachment-record assertion with the existing SDK record parser, removing assertion-safety growth; an independent P0–P2 correction review is also scoped-clean.
- No contributor checkout or execution; no real Zalo credentials, messages, CDN requests, browser, or container proof. The listener and HTTP transport are synthetic; durable ingress, normalization, guarded downloading, media storage, and context building use production paths. Live-account interoperability is outside this proof.

Final head `09d73ac2bbba30845f04ea9731b8ffea8e5f87ca`: 48 checks pass, 58 are skipped, and none are pending or failed. [Linux CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41788003660) and [macOS CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41788003549) are green.

title: fix: reduce session startup stalls under storage contention

- Retry classified native SQLite busy/locked lease-renewal failures asynchronously within the existing retry budget and confirmed expiry. Preserve cancellation, owner replacement, and loss handling; add bounded, sanitized diagnostics.

title: fix(workers): retain admitted GitHub operator authority
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: worker GitHub access can lose the operator authority from its admitted run when later grant preparation no longer has the original caller context.

## User Impact

Admitted worker runs retain their original operator authority for GitHub access. Revocation still stops launch or refresh, and existing cleanup releases the retained authority. Missing authority is not promoted to synthetic authorization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass original admitted authority into the existing GitHub grant owner, which retains and revalidates it and composes its abort signal with the current turn. Keep grant lifecycle and cleanup with that owner.

## Evidence

### Retained authority and refresh
- Existing committed `worker-github-binding.authority-wire.test.ts` covers real admitted-request capture/release/retention, SQLite exact-turn binding, worker credential installation, production refresh dispatch and WorkerConnection delivery.
- Removing retention produces **2/2 failures after request completion**; the repaired combined suite passes **34/34**, with **2/2** passing through the registered runner. Real operator-role revocation and turn reassignment suppress subsequent credential delivery.
- The canonical test-inventory ordering is repaired; its affected selection suite passed **10/10**.

### Actual initial launch after public request completion
New committed [runtime test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a46198f6a0b32b19e18b78945b6a43ca62d9a7b4/test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/worker-github-initial-launch.e2e.test.ts) passes **3/3** against a real built Gateway, public authenticated admission, production node invoke/workspace/bundle/supervisor owners, real WorkerConnection, and a real worker child:

1. **Allowed:** public `chat.send` ACK completes before the held noncredential preparation request resumes. `executeWorkerTurn` and the production launch deliver the initial credential; the worker creates its real `hosts.yml` profile and reaches the provider. The profile disappears after settlement.
2. **Original operator revoked:** a separate administrator uses public `users.setRole` while preparation is held. No credential-bearing launch, worker credential profile or provider request occurs for the original turn.
3. **Cancelled predecessor / legitimate successor:** public `chat.abort` settles the old turn without credential delivery; a legitimate successor receives its own binding, runs and cleans up.

There are no manufactured grants, admission mocks, manual token-frame sends, direct credential-installer calls or direct pairing-store writes. QA password plumbing uses the existing GatewayClient password contract, allowing documented trusted-proxy admission plus authenticated local administration without changing core auth or disabling guards.

### Source qualification and local gates

The earlier one-line deficit on the proof checkout's older baseline does not persist against this PR's actual publication base.
- Fresh independent installed P0–P2 review is **scoped-clean** for the eight-file proof change with all 33 coupled source modules supplied. The later capture-helper correction has its own fresh **scoped-clean** review with complete fixture/caller/command/lifecycle context.
- The earlier CI native-PID observation defect was repaired and qualified in merged [#192539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192539). Current-head CI remains the separate broad landing gate.

### Limits
External GitHub HTTPS and model/provider responses are synthetic. The node test host executes production owners but is not a separately launched node CLI. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker-hosted Codex authentication being handed back to Gateway auth, and ensures current model authority is retained before worker initialization can execute a native auth command.

## User Impact

Workers keep their own native credentials. Normal Gateway model-availability resolution does not replace worker identity or block an otherwise valid worker turn. Explicit/forwarded Gateway profile choices and native supervision remain rejected. Model or placement revocation prevents the corresponding native effects. No configuration or migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing worker-owned handoff for native-command runs, and retain model execution through the existing authority owner before initialization for every worker auth route. A resolved Gateway key can be availability data, not a request to use that account on the worker; the worker handoff never forwards that key.

A full shipped-runtime replay caught the earlier revision incorrectly rejecting that normal availability key. This revision repairs that integration failure rather than changing the fixture to hide it. The Linux composition observer also now reads children across all node tasks, preserving its native-process filter and cleanup assertions; reading only the main task missed subprocesses created by runtime worker threads.

## Evidence

### Actual built Gateway + paired node + native Codex

The repository's supported network-none runner built `qaRuntime` from the candidate and ran the existing full composition through real Gateway processes and authenticated node WebSockets:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  --isolated-image sha256:847f71bbb3f17fc1032d50d75bf6fb3fdcf188b16dff81f24667fe9ae9409e01 \
  --isolated-runtime=bun run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-node-app-server.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- **Red:** the previous published implementation, with only the process-observer correction, built and reached actual `sessions.dispatch`, then rejected the normal availability key before worker auth. This was an execution failure, not setup failure. Source snapshot: `d68636b2dd9d070df0da735547f869ee904a59b89d5298b0d908c813f93e93b5`.
- **Green:** the corrected candidate passed **1/1 full composition test** (47.60 seconds test execution; 95.46 seconds Vitest run after the successful build). Source snapshot: `4291c8ce573583596adc030dd681bfda20995908ea056d26bd59e902ab84c034`.
- The test performs real worktree creation and worker dispatch, holds the actual native auth helper, observes worker-authenticated provider requests, starts and resumes the same native thread, reads the worker-owned thread store, and verifies persisted Gateway history and filesystem results.
- It aborts a real held command and joins process cleanup. While auth is pending, ordinary reassignment remains refused because workspace results are pending; changing the actual session permission from Full to Workspace stops the captured run, helper and native children before their auth timeout. Late release and a subsequent forbidden attempt produce no provider requests or filesystem result.
- Worker observations assert absence of Gateway/provider/forge credentials and runtime injection. The original assertions are retained; native children must stop before node shutdown.
- The selected pinned Bun executable was verified by the runner. Preflight used Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0 and matching Chromium revision 1248. Both runs reported container absence after completion; no live Gateway was changed.

The provider is deterministic loopback HTTP, not an external inference service. This proves the actual shipped Gateway/node/native-client composition, not cloud provisioning, live-provider behavior, or an upgrade.

### Focused regression and review

- Original native-command handoff failure reproduced against the repository baseline.
- Connection and environment siblings: **57/57 passed**. The worker matrix includes resolved Gateway availability keys and verifies no host login/handoff; explicit profile/supervision conflicts still reject.
- Actual native process/provider authority cases: **5/5 passed** via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest.codex-worker-authority.config.ts --maxWorkers=1`. An availability key still results in only the synthetic worker bearer reaching the provider. Model-policy and placement revocation prevent auth/provider effects; an explicit Gateway profile opens no worker duplex.
- Selected-leaf types (`test/tsconfig.codex-worker-authority.json`), typed lint, formatting, diff and full-PR test-line gates passed. The shared baseline is unchanged.
- Fresh independent installed autoreview **P0–P2: scoped-clean**, covering the final delta with complete core auth producer, harness, transport and test context. Earlier reviews remain retained; the full runtime replay is additional executed evidence.
- The native binary used in the focused proof is Codex CLI 0.164.0, SHA-256 `b93f6811d3f653f0fb83be4050d857fb9abbb111dfa2ce160563327daff7f306`. Its inspected sibling auth-command source was pinned separately at `8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4`; no source-to-binary provenance equivalence is asserted.

title: fix(workers): honor profile setup-script opt-out
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a worker can run a setup script even though its selected profile disables setup scripts.

## User Impact

A profile's explicit setup-script opt-out applies during preparation and prepared-image startup, including repository checkout setup. Existing recipe-secret validation is unchanged. No migration or new setting is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the native profile policy take precedence over per-request setup authorization at both existing execution paths. Keep preparation and startup on the same policy.

## Evidence

- Fixed the hosted-review repository-checkout bypass: profile suppression is passed independently of caller setup permission. Profile false skips setup while allowing checkout; requested setup without current admin authority still rejects. Prepared startup applies the same policy.
- Documented the existing `settings.runSetupScript` behavior, including omitted/true semantics and its distinction from `settings.setup`. Removed the invalid undefined JSON-setting fixture.
- Production placement/startup and node workspace owners execute real Git subprocesses, HTTP checkpoint transfer and a setup script. The allowed case writes its result file; profile-disabled, non-admin and authority-revoked-before-command cases do not. Removing only the checkout repair makes the disabled case write that file: **1 failed / 32 passed**.
- Final owner/consumer suite: **50/50 passed**. Final isolated setup cases: **4/4 passed** after eliminating inherited fixture setup. Prepared lifecycle cases use actual subprocess/filesystem effects, including failure before activation.
- Reproduction: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-intent.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-prepared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Direct changed-test-leaf compiler, typed lint/format/diff checks passed. Fresh installed autoreview P0–P2 and supplemental fixture-isolation review: **scoped-clean**. Separate allocation: 196 lines; shared baseline unchanged.
- The earlier owner-level proof used an explicit live authorization callback. The additional native proof below now covers public authenticated dispatch and actual managed Node CLI enrollment; it does not claim live-model completion.


## Native Runtime Proof

The committed `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/worker-setup-policy.e2e.test.ts` exercises a built Gateway, authenticated operator RPCs, actual managed Node CLI enrollment, native Git checkout, worker command execution, and real Podman filesystem/checkpoint effects. No production auth hooks or fabricated grants are used.

| Path | Allowed | Profile disabled | Non-admin | Revoked before effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Repository preparation | `prepare` effect, checkout succeeds | Checkout without setup | Checkout without setup | No setup; operation settles |
| Runtime-image checkout | `checkout` setup effect | Checkout without setup | Checkout without setup | No setup; operation settles |

All **8 native cases passed**. Two input-equivalent counterfactual runs removed only the three setup-policy owner repairs: the disabled repository and image cases then observed forbidden `prepare` and `checkout` effects respectively. These are product-boundary reds, not harness startup failures. All owned containers, checkpoints, Gateways, and retained process groups were verified absent afterward; the supplied image was preserved.

This proof exposed and repairs two adjacent native defects: Crabbox's strict profile allowlist rejected the already-documented `runSetupScript` setting, and initial worker presence maintenance consumed repository capabilities before plugin publication. Presence initialization now uses the existing post-plugin/pre-recovery owner. Recipe-secret validation remains before setup-policy evaluation.

The source-qualified composition used native base `8bc44540c46d8d1e3d80800c7ea1b11277c2db02`, this PR's previously published policy, and the QA/password support subsequently landed in #192540. Integration includes that landed dependency through main `7c2ff8f775acca3e5c93c9c22b6247e37df29bae`: all 17 changed file hashes and all eight dependency hashes matched the executed source on integration. The final follow-up only adds `unknown` rejection typing and a bounded cleanup-error name in two test helpers, plus exactly five allocated lines; focused types/lint/format, all 21 provider tests, and a fresh independent P0–P2 review passed for that delta. Of 48 full-source review contracts, 47 are byte-identical; the remaining sessions-create commit guard adds agent/tool-requester fencing that is inactive for these operator-created cases. This is source-equivalent integration evidence, not a claim that the complete refreshed main tree ran in the original runtime proof.

Supporting qualification: **180 tests passed** (107 startup/presence/integration, 59 policy/provider, 14 prompt-prefix stability), focused types, typed lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and complete-source independent P0–P2 review. The existing recipe-secret checks and native TLS/Git verification remain enforced.

Limits: external GitHub/model/backend responses are synthetic. There is no live cloud allocation, post-setup model-turn completion, or warm-checkpoint-fork reuse claim; the image matrix exercises native `runtimePreparation.source=image`. An earlier model-stage stall is not claimed fixed. Private runtime TLS/config material is excluded from the PR.

title: fix(worktrees): reserve capacity on PostgreSQL
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PostgreSQL-backed worktree creation fails when reserving capacity because its upsert references an ambiguous `owner` column.

## User Impact

Managed Git worktrees can be created and registered on PostgreSQL. Reservation renewal still requires the same owner; a replacement owner remains protected. SQLite behavior and persisted schemas are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Qualify the target table's existing owner predicate. Allocation, leases, worker dispatch, and error propagation remain with their native owners. The new PostgreSQL suite is now included in the existing conformance runner's default targets and CI shards.

## Executed behavior evidence

The committed `capacity.postgres.test.ts` now calls **`ManagedWorktreeService.create`**, creates a real local Git repository, uses the real allocation/lease/capacity worker transport against **PostgreSQL 17.11**, reads the created checkout's `README.md`, and checks the persisted worktree registry. This case does not mock dispatch, database admission, SQL, Git, or filesystem effects. The suite owns teardown of its isolated database schemas, workers, state, and checkout.

The same final suite was executed twice, changing only the production conflict predicate for the negative control:

```text
Original predicate: .where("owner", "=", key)
FAIL creates and registers a real Git checkout through PostgreSQL-backed allocation
error: column reference "owner" is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 42702)
FAIL admits and renews only the current owner capacity reservation
error: column reference "owner" is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 42702)

Fixed predicate: .where("state_leases.owner", "=", key)
PASS creates and registers a real Git checkout through PostgreSQL-backed allocation — 1195 ms
PASS admits and renews only the current owner capacity reservation — 42 ms
Test Files 1 passed; Tests 2 passed
```

The second case separately proves renewal and refusal after reservation-owner replacement with real PostgreSQL; only that case substitutes the transport grant callback. Both cases failed for the intended SQL error on the control. Fixed source bytes were restored and verified afterward.

Reproduce with a disposable PostgreSQL database:

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --list
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_POSTGRES_URL" -- src/agents/worktrees/capacity.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## Validation and limits

- Default conformance selection now includes this file. Existing target-inventory, disjoint-shard, listing, and argument-validation tests: **8 passed**. Their temporary fixture now declares its actual ESM package type instead of triggering an unexpected Node warning.
- Real PostgreSQL green run: **37.08 seconds wall**, including **29.7 seconds** of compiled-worker preparation; test bodies total about **1.24 seconds**. Negative control: **141.45 seconds wall**, including cold worker preparation. CI duration remains available on the current head's checks.
- Existing PostgreSQL/SQLite capacity sibling proof: **21 passed** on the original production fix; the production predicate is unchanged by this follow-up.
- Targeted agents-other and tooling test-type checks, typed lint (3 files), formatting, diff checks and staged test-line ratchet passed.
- Fresh installed independent P0–P2 autoreview of this complete candidate: **scoped-clean**, no findings.
- Full runtime/plugin/declaration build already passed with the original seven independent production fixes composed; this correction changes only regression selection, tests and allocation metadata. Current-head PR CI supplies broad proof.
- The **+85 test-line allocation** covers the two distinct PostgreSQL contracts and the one-line ESM fixture setup. The shared baseline is unchanged. No production API, schema, cache, or test-only seam is added.
- This is real production-owner/database/Git evidence, not a live cloud/model run. It makes no claim about worktree retirement: an exploratory `service.remove` call outside the CLI one-shot scope exposed a separate main-thread PostgreSQL admission refusal and was not included in the allocation claim.

## Public CLI → Gateway → PostgreSQL proof

Executed on 2026-11-04 against PR head 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, not just ManagedWorktreeService integration. The normal pnpm openclaw launcher built and ran the production CLI and two disposable, authenticated loopback Gateways. Both installations used fresh owned HOME/config/state directories and separate databases on PostgreSQL 17.11, with database.engine=postgres and the documented OPENCLAW_DATABASE_DSN env SecretRef. No production dispatch, Git, lease, capacity, or worker transport was mocked. No test admission override was installed.

The project fixture was a clean checkout of the existing PR commit; no fixture source commit was needed. Default worktree acceleration was left enabled, including its normal internal template cache.

### Exact public entrypoint

With the respective isolated config/state/DSN and loopback port selected, the commands were as below. Each gateway run stayed in its own supervised foreground process; health and creation were separate CLI invocations.

```bash
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red gateway run
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red health --json
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red worktrees create "$REPO"   --name capacity-public-red   --base-ref 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba --json

pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green gateway run
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green health --json
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green worktrees create "$REPO"   --name capacity-public-green   --base-ref 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba --json
```

**Red:** the same head with only the capacity predicate reverted from state_leases.owner to the original owner reference. Health passed; public creation exited1. The running Gateway recorded the worktrees.create RPC failing with:

```text
column reference "owner" is ambiguous: code=42702
```

The public list was empty, PostgreSQL contained zero worktree records, the requested checkout was absent, and no worktree leases remained. The uncertain-error receipt was reconciled before proceeding; no blind retry or offline fallback was used for creation.

**Green:** pristine 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, rebuilt by the normal launcher. Health and public creation both exited0. The returned id f1067054-e076-463f-be04-4a0911776531 appeared in the public list and the real PostgreSQL worktrees row, with matching path, branch and base ref. The physical checkout had HEAD 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, clean Git status, and README bytes matching the source (SHA256 368166ce96af9cf49729ef813f1ed5e93b04d26f7b3598c9c8721779d534cbda). No worktree leases remained after creation.

### Executing build binding

title: fix(sessions): allow creation with invocation-time authority
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Keeps a prepared session-creation tool from freezing an early absence of authority into a permanent execution denial. The committed owner-level regression exercises construction before caller admission.

## User Impact

Authorized callers can create sessions after admission; revoked, changed, or absent authority still prevents creation. Tool definitions remain stable across turns. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Evaluate write authority at execution through the existing execution gate, then keep the existing live source/creator checks. This builds on the native session-creation owner and the repository-child inheritance already landed in #190843.

## Evidence

- Committed regression: `src/gateway/server.sessions-create-authority.product.test.ts`. It starts the production Gateway on isolated loopback state, builds the tool before caller admission, invokes through the production in-process dispatcher, then reads the created SQLite session row through the production accessor.
- The allowed idle session is persisted. Absent/read-only callers add no row. Revoking the original source or replacing its stored role while actual cwd resolution is awaited prevents creation and preserves the existing row.
- Exact baseline owner: the same regression fails because the allowed invocation returns `{ gated: true }`. Final candidate: **1/1 product test passes**, **12/12 consumer tests pass**. Prefix-stability proof on unchanged production source remains valid.
- Reproduction: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions-create-authority.product.test.ts` and `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/sessions-create-tool.test.ts`.
- Direct changed-leaf TypeScript, scoped lint/format/diff checks passed. Fresh full-slice installed autoreview **P0–P2: scoped-clean**. The dedicated test-line allocation is 233 lines; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- The authenticated-client fixture is synthetic. Authority capture, current-role checks, admission, dispatcher, creation and persistence are production owners. This tests idle creation, which needs no model call; it does not qualify WebSocket login or non-idle kickoff.

## Shipped-entry-point compatibility and authorization proof

The exact published source `4ffca1552e5ae42d0728a83b88f4a1284675860a` was built by the normal `pnpm openclaw --profile session-authority-green gateway run` owner into a disposable Gateway with its own state/config/home/workspace and loopback port. The source remained clean before and after execution. The external Responses fixture emitted only model protocol/tool-call packets; it did not construct tools, inject caller identity, grant authority, call a dispatcher, or write application state.

1. The normal authenticated public CLI created a non-main parent session, then ran `agent --agent main --session-id <parent> --message <explicit independent-session request> --json`. The model used the offered `tool_search` → `tool_describe` → `dispatch_action` interface to invoke `sessions_create`. The completed agent receipt reported four tool calls (including the nested `sessions_create`) and zero failures. A separate public `sessions.list` read returned exactly one target row labeled `session-authority-green-created`, with an operator-created session identity.
2. A separately authenticated documented `/hooks/agent` request asked for another independent session without an admitted operator. The same real model/tool-discovery path reached `sessions_create`; the tool reported an authority denial and no creation receipt. The subsequent public session list contained zero rows with the forbidden label, while retaining the allowed session.
3. Both task-owned services were terminated through their process owners; terminal results confirmed SIGTERM settlement, exact profile/model processes were absent, and both selected loopback ports were closed.

**Scope of the result:** this is actual CLI/Gateway/model-tool transport and persisted-session compatibility with a deterministic loopback model, not live external inference. The ordinary local-agent run also passed on the original constructor-time implementation; it is not a red reproduction of the late-admission defect. Source tracing confirms that ordinary path installs caller authority before catalog construction. The late-admission red/green evidence remains the committed production-owner regression described above. Non-idle kickoff and an externally reproduced late-caller worker flow are not claimed.

title: feat(beam): preserve live logical conversation handoff
body:
An authorized Beam publisher could open the Team link but could not compose, and repeated adoption created independent transcript copies. Beam now transfers ownership explicitly and retains one live logical conversation for Team and the source client.

Fixes #192520. Receiver merged as `7552558bfb389d57c760cc37a641bbed7a250175` from head `81953d01bb3c95706940a20b9e53e1b7882aa9fc` (tree `cea3dcd0491cf6b6d1d812a6c9d804c001329116`). The companion https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/356 subsequently merged as `4de04c55d02f57caea32176005c6a6c9517200da` from pinned head `b637385f21ab78ada03d87bba25e16aa9f192404`.

- Ordinary publication is a read-only snapshot. Only the authenticated original publisher can release its exact receiver generation with `beam handoff`. Release freezes source history and permanently retires source writes; archive or snapshot expiry cannot restore source ownership. Lost acknowledgments cannot recreate an expired publication.
- First continuation imports bounded untrusted history once. Durable plugin SQLite metadata retains the destination across concurrent requests, retry, restart, deletion and reopen. Exact creation tokens fence rollback/finalization; stale cleanup cannot clear a newer attempt. Reconciliation requires core-verified destination provenance. No schema or protocol version bump.
- Gateway owners authorize source access, destination creation/history and model selection. Destination aliases and provider-owned equivalent versions normalize against available models. An unavailable preference leaves the override unset for ordinary configured-default resolution. Available forbidden models remain forbidden. No credential, account selection or provider runtime session ID transfer.
- The companion uses its existing authenticated Gateway profile/device identity for read/follow-up. Query links resolve through a read-only owner; prefix links retain ambiguity discovery. UI continuation captures draft, attachments and ownership synchronously, fences deferred work and RPC results, and releases only its own unscoped sending state. Optional continuation work stays outside common chat boot preloads.

### Validation

[Final exact-head CI41793020965](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41793020965) succeeds, including all selected unit/browser/native, packaging, type/lint, prompt snapshot, Android and three PostgreSQL conformance jobs. Before publication, pinned-toolchain native archive builds measured153B saved; canonical precompression/comparison checks and34 focused tests passed (24 UI ownership,10 native SQLite store).
- [Joined pinned-client/Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41793020965/job/126451448073) passes the complete scenario in33.858s: normal profile/device authentication, real HTTP publication, dropped release acknowledgment, destination first turn/default selection, client read/follow-up/idempotency, Gateway restart preserving session identity, late-source rejection and ordinary revocation with no additional inference. The shard exits0 after verified process cleanup. The provider is synthetic.

The new SQLite upgrade case seeds a pre-handoff owned row without generation/binding fields, proves list/read and nonmutating premature refusal, preserves owner/createdAt during original-publisher refresh, then releases and reopens one destination. Existing ownerless restrictions remain covered. title: fix: refresh binary availability after relative PATH cwd changes
body:

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Include cwd in the existing successful-probe cache identity only when a nonempty PATH entry is relative. Current main already probes prepared availability afresh, so the replacement repairs only the remaining synchronous cache owner and omits the original branch's unrelated CI backport.

The simplification pass removed the redundant search-to-cache projection and a one-use platform local. Production is +10/-7 (net +3); the remaining growth records the directory-dependent identity. The existing binary lifecycle case now covers both relative and absolute PATH. Removing redundant setup and retaining the both-misses assertion leaves tests +10/-12 (net -2), with no test-budget increase. title: fix(anthropic): Windows Claude turns fail with large tool allowlists
body:
Supersedes #156057, thanks @blazingphoenix7.
Related: #144792

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bundled Claude CLI turns on Windows fail to start when the admitted MCP tool list exceeds the Windows command-line limit.

## User Impact

Windows agents using OpenClaw-generated settings can retry startup with the same exact admitted tools, denials, permission mode, and restrictions. Commands that already fit retain their invocation without acquiring a temporary-file dependency. **Merge is blocked on native Claude validation described below.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Try the original invocation first. Only after Windows reports `ENAMETOOLONG`, place the admitted tool names and OpenClaw's path-independent restrictions in a private settings file owned by that child. The existing process owner rechecks live authority after the write; cleanup covers startup failures and child exit, including warm turns.

Only empty settings or the exact OpenClaw-generated restricted projection can relocate. Custom inline settings and settings paths keep their original error, because [moving caller-owned permission or sandbox paths can change their anchors](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#where-a-pattern-anchors). Tool, permission, sandbox, and execution boundaries are preserved.

## Evidence

- **Exact regression red on main:** [native Windows baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41767148011), test-only commit `29fb561553c889b90e775667a4d91090f53bd9e2` on main `fa997337ede78046bc0e3e790ba452d06e34627b`. Both oversized settings forms fail in the real launcher with `ENAMETOOLONG` (`-4064`).
- **Replacement and siblings green:** [native Windows replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41766984009) of exact head `270d1143697a4f6b1853899299821167924b1148`: four named files, 53 passed, 11 skipped, 115.79 s wall. The eight regression cases total 961 ms and cover exact grants/denials, fitting commands, unsafe custom settings refusal, writes, retirement, retry failure, and child-owned cleanup. Windows exercises the real OS limit; Linux injects only that initial OS error before a real subprocess.
- **Real host-authority boundary:** [Windows authority probe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41774781014), [proof source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8da7e91a7b5cfd6a7e3bc272c52ff0f5500126b9/extensions/anthropic/cli-allowlist.authority-proof.test.ts). Production files are identical to the replacement head. The admitted-run owner permits Read and reads a synthetic file; undeclared Write is denied and creates no file. Closing real admission during the settings write prevents the retry child and removes the settings workspace. These two cases pass; the file as a whole is **not green**.
- **Remaining blocker:** in that same run, installed native Claude Code 2.1.280 reports its version, but the offline configuration probe times out before its loaded grant rules can be observed. Cleanup also reports `EPERM` on the isolated executable. The probe uses an explicitly synthetic startup token and a rejecting loopback endpoint, sends no model prompt, and uses no real model credentials. This failed setup does not establish a product defect or prove native permission enforcement. Native grant loading and cleanup remain unverified; merge and original-PR closure remain blocked on this validation gap.
- **Broad CI retains inherited failures:** [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41767665905), attempt 2: 133 success, 24 skipped, four failed root jobs plus the downstream gate. `security-fast` succeeds. All three failing test files were replayed on clean main `919b0567dd1b5361e5c7f7e0b2c9f6ea6fe7b8bb` with the checksum-pinned Bun fork in [Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41770371008): four failed, 32 passed, with identical signatures. Browser relay profile port/name drift resolves `false` instead of rejecting; QA kill/restart receives two records instead of an empty array; hooks CLI blank-parent-agent output returns the specific error instead of the expected generic prefix. These files and direct subjects are unchanged in the tested PR merge.
- **Existing test-line deficit:** CI reports a 20-line overage. The same checker fails on main `fa997337...` against its parent with that same 20-line deficit and +27 main test lines. The replacement adds exactly 180 test lines and exactly 180 allocation credit; it preserves the existing deficit. A default non-growing main check can pass while over budget, and is not claimed as failure proof. No baseline or excess allocation was added.
- Final local autoreview of the complete candidate is scoped-clean at P0–P2. Its earlier settings-anchor finding was fixed through exact canonical recognition. Touched-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Necessary production growth is 83 lines for serialization, the guarded retry, and cleanup; no equivalent dead code exists in this owner. The separate allocation records the 180 focused regression lines.
- Contributor source was read through GitHub view/diff only and was never checked out or executed. Heavy compilation and tests ran only in CI/Testbox. No CHANGELOG changes.

The shared routing boundary checks the source and admission again after awaiting plugins. title: fix: show Gateway names for linked Slack mentions in Control UI
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI message bodies can show raw Slack mention IDs even after the referenced person has a verified Gateway profile link. Correct sender labels do not resolve inline references, and bot mentions must not be mistaken for the sender.

## User Impact

- Linked human references show the current Gateway display name using the existing viewer/session visibility policy.
- Unlinked people and bots use the Slack name already recorded in the message; unknown IDs, code, and messages without original account scope remain literal.
- Stored/model text, provider IDs, routing, authorization, and mention notifications are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep native syntax and ID normalization in Slack’s pure mention adapter. The Gateway resolves the canonical channel/account/sender tuple and enriches only the admitted display copy. Native pages are enriched before final byte budgeting/encoding, preserving pagination and the webchat fast path. Live fanout asks each reader to reload its canonical view rather than broadcasting a shared person-name projection.

The existing Slack stripping behavior is moved unchanged into the same sibling adapter to satisfy the channel module’s line-cap ratchet. No new persistence, configuration option, or permission is introduced.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen; human co-author credit is retained in the commit. **Patrick requested landing this PR on 2026-11-04. Landing remains subject to the applicable review/proof gates and supported inherited-CI policy. No deployment is requested.**

## Evidence

**Red:** On baseline `57405d6f170a905c1056ae755ec20e259f893abf`, the linked-state RPC and real Gateway/Control UI browser regressions fail on the expected Gateway-name assertion. The serialized-page contract also fails because the original encoder discards the object graph before display enrichment. Setup failures were not counted as regression proof.

**Green:** Real Gateway + native WebSocket Control UI proof passes for initial subscription history and committed live append/publication. Focused Gateway suites passed 155 tests; live-publication/availability/guest suites passed 54. The full touched history/serialization pair was rerun after isolating its adapter fixture from extension runtime graphs. Slack channel and agent-tool prefix-stability suites pass. Core/extension/changed-test type checks, targeted lint, formatting, whitespace, and the line-cap ratchet pass.

Primary reproduction command (run unchanged on baseline and candidate):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/slack-inline-identity.e2e.test.ts
```

Deterministic linked-state regression:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-handler.test.ts -t "projects manually linked Slack"
```

Coverage includes different/missing account scope, unverified viewers, self references, unknown IDs, source fallbacks, code, escaping, expansion, unchanged stored content, and no inbox effects. Fresh independent local P0–P2 autoreview completed with no accepted findings; its chunked/cross-file-context limitations are not treated as runtime proof.

### Browser proof

The attached **baseline → candidate** captures are inspected, cropped, synthetic fixtures through a real Gateway and Control UI (not mocked transport). The sender fixture is Patrick; the separate human target is `Gateway Alice`, the bot fallback is `Roboclaw`, and unknown/code IDs remain visible. Slack accounts are disabled in the fixture; no live Slack API or inference turn is exercised.

### CI follow-up and test cost

The first CI run caught a one-second functional-readiness poll and unattributed test growth. Commit `c8bb79b1cde857f0fd19b1d8c20666e78a042836` waits for the exact initial/live history result with an explicit setup deadline; it does not change production timeouts or performance budgets. Commit `2690183c4fc67f40d813065a3518f4e76314fc25` registers the fixture with the real-Gateway inventory. The correctly routed **ui-e2e-serial** proof passes: **1 test, 70.23 seconds Vitest wall time** after private-QA preparation. The real-Gateway skip flag correctly excludes it from collection.

The separate `config/test-lines-allocations/slack-linked-mention-display-192473.txt` record attributes **432 new test lines** to the account/viewer, serializer, and real native startup/live-path contracts. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged. The pinned CI main base `f38495f7` independently has a **20-line preexisting ceiling gap** at net delta zero; the fully allocated PR preserves that gap. The separate CI admission assertion remains under investigation; isolated passing baseline/feature replays and the failed same-head CI replay are not claimed as a fix. Broad CI is not green.

Delivery is checked against GitHub’s rendered body image elements, and both actual published proof asset URLs load and decode correctly.

### Bounds

Gateway-link reads are bounded to 20 distinct identities per response; remaining references retain their recorded fallback/raw form. Historical messages without captured channel/account provenance are not guessed from text or the session’s current reply route. Broad PR CI remains separate proof.

title: fix: welcome screens show unrelated team chats in recent sessions
body:
Supersedes #178700 (same change, rebuilt on current `main`; that PR conflicts with `main` and is closed in favor of this one).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on signed-in multi-user Gateways, the Recent sessions list on New Session and empty chats shows teammates' unrelated chats, including sessions you personally hid.

## User Impact

User impact: Recent sessions now shows only conversations you own, prompted in, or were explicitly @mentioned in for the active agent. Unread sessions come first, then most recent. Hidden, archived, snoozed, and empty sessions stay out, and access rules are unchanged. Single-user recents and All owners discovery behave as before. No migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both welcome paths share the existing managed session query with `involvingMe`. The Gateway selects personal involvement before pagination instead of the browser filtering a truncated team roster. The separate draft-welcome adapter is removed. Rows use a compact design selected by Vyctor Brzezowski: an unread dot leads the row, and muted "X mentioned you" text sits below the title, with no avatars or accent colors. The list is a narrower 560px column centered under the composer.

Thanks to Jacqueline Henriksen for reporting the problem and defining the personal-recents behavior.

## Evidence

- Verified on `main` at `b24dcc0c95e536480e8f25acfee0edadc4914639`; rebuilt on `main` at `605193d5e72bd60b7e760cdd605eddfb6f5dc6a7`, where the patch applies cleanly and the focused suites (33 tests), `tsgo:ui`, scoped `git diff --check`, and Auto Review (no P0–P2 findings) pass again.
- Bundled Control UI E2E (`welcome-personal-recents`, `new-session-page.responsive-welcome`): 10 tests pass. They cover Alice and Bob on New Session and an empty chat, with 300 unrelated first-page sessions. The personal-recents regression fails on the base and passes with the fix. Layout assertions cover the narrower centered column, shared time alignment, and no overflow at 800px.
- Focused unit and Gateway suites pass: `chat-welcome.test.tsx`, `session-list-order.test.ts`, and `session-utils.filters.test.ts`. They cover unread-first ordering, mention-only involvement, profile-specific hide and show, and pre-pagination filtering.
- These checks pass: UI and test typechecks (tsgo), oxlint with 0 errors and one pre-existing style warning, stylelint, `ui:i18n:verify`, `protocol:gen`, and `git diff --check`.

title: fix(gateway): check Incognito chat leaves against the in-process transcript
body:
## Problem

Every Incognito chat send after the first one failed with `Error: Chat admission omitted its worker-prepared active path` and showed as **Not sent**. Stop failed the same way.

Incognito transcripts live in the Gateway's process-local session actor, which the database read workers cannot open. Admission and Stop compare the browser's `expectedLeafEntryId` against the chat's active path, and for Incognito chats nothing supplied that fact anymore. #174610 removed the in-process Incognito active-path read as "unreachable", but the Incognito admission branch still depended on it. The first message of a new Incognito chat still worked because it has no prior leaf.

## Fix

- `chat-send-session.ts` / `chat-send-active-leaf.ts`: for Incognito sends and Stop, read the active-path relation from the memory session actor (`readSessionTranscriptAnchorsAsync`), then run the existing `assertExpectedLeafActive` check. Durable sessions are unchanged.
- `session-actor-memory-history-anchors.ts`: memory anchor reads now report `activePathRelation` (exact / ancestor / off-path), matching the SQLite projection.
- `session-transcript-anchor-read.ts`: a missing memory transcript reports the empty-root relation, like the SQLite reader.

Accepted edge case (documented in code): the Incognito path read happens just before the entry snapshot. A reset is still rejected by the session-id fence. An append that lands between the two reads is a rare race that the user can retry.

## Evidence

- `chat-send-active-leaf.incognito.test.ts` (real `chat.send` handler, real memory storage): stale and earlier leaves are rejected with `active-leaf-changed` for sends and Stop, the exact leaf is accepted for Stop, and a session-fenced ancestor is admitted and dispatched. Red on base (generic error instead of `active-leaf-changed`), green with the fix.
- New `chat-incognito-send.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: a real built Gateway and Chromium. The test turns on Incognito, starts a session and sends two follow-ups, and every reply appears with no **Not sent**. On a base build it fails at the second reply; with the fix it passes.
- Related suites pass: projection rebuild, stop cascade, both transcript-anchor suites, `session-control.incognito`, `vitest-ui-e2e-config`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes, run with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1` because the full dead-export scan fails on `ui/.../systems-sidebar.tsx: systemKind`, which this PR doesn't touch. `tsgo:core` is clean.
- Local autoreview (P2): no findings.

## Not covered

A live run against real OpenAI showed that Incognito chats fail at the **model run** with `This account action requires a current authorized connection`. The failure is identical on base `main` without this change, and the same flow succeeds for a durable chat. It is a separate existing model-account authority issue and is not addressed here.

## Test cost

The dedicated 193-line allocation preserves the admission/Stop fence regressions and the real-Gateway Incognito follow-up flow. The shared baseline, production code, and existing assertions are unchanged. The staged test-line ratchet passes; the existing functional and CI evidence above is reused.

title: fix(ui): explain missing operator scopes in access errors
body:
## Summary

F3: preserve the Gateway’s existing missing-scope reason in Control UI permission copy, with plain-language next steps rather than raw scope identifiers.

- Read `MISSING_SCOPE` / `missingScope` through the existing Gateway client parser. Authorization, required scopes, grants, retry behavior, and technical error details are unchanged.
- One UI copy formatter covers generic missing-scope failures and existing feature-specific read-access messages (logs, usage, agents, model providers, scheduled tasks, context breakdown, and session history).
- Following Vyctor’s approved wording, display `operator.read` as “read access.” After inspecting `src/gateway/operator-scopes.ts` and `src/gateway/method-scopes.ts`, display `operator.write` as “write access” and `operator.admin` as “admin access.” Other scopes use “the required access,” never a guessed read-access label. Technical scopes remain in the original Gateway error details.
- Preserve “session history,” the distinction between sessions and conversation content, “admin,” curly apostrophes, and “Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}.” Explicit `UserFacingError` messages and unrelated errors retain their handling.

## Before → after

- `permission denied` / `missing scope: {scope}` → `Couldn’t complete this request. Ask an admin to grant {access}.`
- `Couldn’t view {thing}. Ask an admin to grant operator.read.` → `Couldn’t view {thing}. Ask an admin to grant read access.`
- Generic requests: `operator.write` → “write access”; `operator.admin` → “admin access”; any other scope → “the required access.”
- The initial F3 change also replaced `existing chat history` with `session history`.

## Review and validation

- Fresh independent read-only review of the plain-language revision: **no actionable findings**. The reviewer inspected the scope owners, full changed formatter, and corresponding test diffs; no validation commands were run. Review run: `e66a07b4-c233-4fb2-aa2d-451af26ce776`.

- Historical evidence from the initial implementation only: six targeted files / 133 tests, two focused missing-scope cases, and i18n verification passed before this plain-language revision. These are not proof for the final wording revision.

## Gaps and follow-up

- **This revision intentionally has no test, E2E, browser, screenshot, CI, build, standalone typecheck/lint, or new i18n runs beyond the normal hook.** Updated assertions were inspected, not executed. Landing-phase validation is deferred to the parent’s landing lanes.
- Guest/role restrictions, admin-only settings without a missing-scope reason, approval-required policy, and disconnected-device failures remain follow-up work at their owning structured-error contracts. A generic `FORBIDDEN` is not guessed to mean one of these cases.
- Unmapped scopes retain accurate generic guidance rather than an invented permission label.

body:
## Final-head update — supersedes earlier validation figures

Published correction: `0c1c8f13a3878281924b5b99944e63977e62af0a`. Its source tree is identical to the reviewed/tested candidate, with native provenance for CI base `80c59348c20aef94a53a7ee963f54b0856c64c23`.

---

## Problem

The composer chose the first quota group for a provider. With two accounts on the same provider, reversing the response changed which account's quota appeared. Model controls could also use a measured plan belonging to a different account.

## Solution

Carry the measured auth-profile identity through provider usage collection and the account-aware `models.authStatus` projection. Match that identity against the session's account selection before displaying quota or using a measured plan label. Share the exact-account join between the composer and model controls, and show **Quota account unknown** instead of guessing.

The profile identifier remains gated with account identity in `models.authStatus` and is removed from the public `usage.status` response.

## Impact

Quota selection no longer depends on provider response order. Model picker and default-model labels cannot borrow another account's measured plan. Profile account summaries retain their separate account-keyed source. There are no configuration, persistence, permission, dependency, or stylesheet changes.

## Original implementation evidence (pre-correction)

- The two-account regression fails against the original composer on `origin/main` and passes on this branch, including reversed response order.
- Composer, model picker, runtime, and provider-data tests: 57 passed (9.95 seconds). Provider auth/load tests: 11 passed (185.39 seconds). Gateway auth-status and usage-cache tests: 61 passed (36.79 seconds).

BEFORE is on the left; AFTER is on the right. Six comparisons cover 1440-pixel desktop and 390-pixel phone layouts in light/dark, the model picker, reversed rows with Rose dark and a custom mint accent, and automatic/unknown account selection. All displayed data is fictional.

## Edge cases

- Automatic, redacted, missing, or ambiguous account identity stays unknown, even when only one provider row is available.
- Distinct canonical usage providers competing for the selected identity remain unknown. Alias rows reuse the Gateway-owned snapshot rather than comparing presentation labels.
- The selected account is the configured session preference, not retrospective attribution of a previous response.
- Browser proof uses the real UI with a mock Gateway. Credential collection and Gateway projection have separate tests; no live-provider session-to-usage run is claimed.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI slash-command feedback uses inconsistent terms such as “active run,” title-case headings, and failure messages that lead with a diagnostic instead of a recovery action.

## User Impact

Commands use “reply,” “effort,” sentence-case headings, and actionable failure summaries. Diagnostics remain available in a separate paragraph. Slash tokens, command behavior, permissions, and redaction are unchanged.

| Before | After |

| Inject a message into the active run | Guide the agent’s current reply |

| Available Commands | Available commands |
| Failed to get model info: … | Couldn’t load model details. Try again. + diagnostic paragraph |
| Prompt budget (last run) | Prompt budget (last reply) |
| Session capability is unavailable | Couldn’t access this session. Open another session and try again. |

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies the approved Control UI glossary to the slash-command catalogs and moves the executor’s connection-change text into the English catalog.
