- Repair input: the [exact-head local verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191597#issuecomment-6593866579) and [downloadable evidence/provenance correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191597#issuecomment-6593999941). The evidence archive's 19 files were checked against its SHA-256/size manifest. That earlier archive's 3,789-test reference belongs to the initial revision; its `2ef1d3d` result is 172 targeted tests. The separate exact-head `cdc305f8add6` full-suite evidence is recorded below.
- Reset events now retire advertised cursor windows without skipping the existing session-settings publication path. Queued permission writes still observe the replacement physical session identity; snapshot-only metadata refreshes do not gain extra history reads.
- Display IDs remain distinct from canonical transcript entry IDs. Canonical reconciliation preserves display identity across cursor updates without admitting a display ID to a reaction write.
- Reader fixtures preserve the intended ownership contract: remote history does not force-follow; an explicit **Jump to latest** moves the reader; local send admission starts following; final-answer fixture rows and navigation through the reader owner exercise stable-position restoration. Existing session/permission and reader-position assertions were retained, with a negative remote-follow assertion added.
- Latest P2 repair: `parseHistory` uses the current top-level `thinkingLevel`, then the current `sessionInfo.thinkingLevel`, and no longer inherits that setting from `previousHistory`. If both are absent, the existing settings owner retains its confirmed value. Existing generation/pending-mutation guards and snapshot precedence are unchanged.

title: fix(voice-call): keep opening greetings audible during caller interruptions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: early caller speech or noise clears the opening greeting before callers hear it.

Supersedes #159144, thanks @mnowrot. Related: #159139.

## User Impact

The opening greeting plays through, and callers can interrupt subsequent replies normally. Overlapping caller audio and transcripts are discarded during the opening. Input before the first greeting audio remains live; no pre-audio mute, new option, or migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing audio controller protects the opening until its response ends and the existing carrier playback clock drains. It excludes the answering-machine hold acknowledgement, and releases on explicit clear or continuity reset. Provider-side cancellation already caused by input sent before playback starts remains outside this host playback fix. Carrier timing uses the existing send-time estimate rather than adding an acknowledgement waiter.

This builds on #191537's echo admission and leaves #191498's Deepgram UtteranceEnd behavior intact. Production delta is +29 lines net; the redundant audible-output forwarding callback was removed. The remaining state distinguishes the opening from later turns and keeps response completion from exposing its queued tail. The separate 60-line regression allocation covers both interruption owners, a generation gap, the queued tail, complete carrier audio, and resumed later-turn interruption without another test harness.

## Evidence

title: fix(cron): honor explicit failure alert destinations before repair
body:
Closes #169401

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing first failure alert when a conversation-owned automation explicitly routes failures to an alerts destination: owner-conversation repair currently replaces that alert, potentially delaying a daily monitor’s notification until the next day.

## User Impact

An explicit per-job failure destination now receives the alert when due instead of having it replaced by a repair turn. Inherited destinations stay repair-first. No new configuration key or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Honor the operator’s explicit notification choice. Job-level channel, recipient, or account selectors in `failureAlert` or `delivery.failureDestination` bypass repair; policy-only and mode-only overrides do not. Existing opt-outs, thresholds, cooldowns, transient retry holds, incident deduplication, repair settlement, and terminal-notification behavior remain in place.

This implements the destination-specific exception proposed in #169401 following maintainer acceptance of that product direction. The cron notification owner keeps the decision; no new state or parallel delivery path is introduced. The delivery guide documents the exception.

## Evidence

- Red first on base `2be13a6bdc761deaf59efceccb343852bbaee3c1`: both new explicit-destination cases failed because a repair was requested instead of an alert.
- `pnpm test src/cron/service.failure-repair.test.ts src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **52 passed** (46.42 seconds wall time including cold worker compilation). - Targeted cron test typecheck and lint passed; formatting, delivery-doc MDX parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. Proof was run on November 1; the candidate is unchanged.
- Independent Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, GPT-6.1 Sol), complete local candidate against the base above, P0-P2: **scoped-clean**, no findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable in this sandbox. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191570#issuecomment-6592875774) completed for this head: no findings and no before-merge actions. It noted a live-delivery proof gap. The AWS QA proofs (mock and real GPT 6.1 Sol inference) and contributor live comparison below add complementary evidence; successful real-chat announce delivery and account-only selection remain unproven.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41555568784) completed successfully for `1f547521e4f71bb535f3075da3051d2b99180ef7`; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. No CI repair was needed.
- Production delta: +11 lines net; regression tests: +86 lines net with a separate matching test-budget allocation. Tests reuse the production CronService and existing external-I/O fixtures.
- **Real-model behavior proof on direct AWS Crabbox (GPT 6.1 Sol)** (lease `cbx_de8dfffc032f`, eu-west-1; stopped after use): isolated QA Gateway + qa-channel with `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode live-frontier --model openai/gpt-6.1-sol` (fallbacks disabled; `OPENAI_API_KEY` forwarded as a secret, not printed; isolated `HOME`, no forwarded OpenClaw env), same lease for before/after. All turns use real GPT 6.1 Sol: the owner conversation, both cron jobs (no model override), and the repair turns. Each job's real model run fails for a real reason: a long report task with `payload.timeoutSeconds: 4`, which produces `cron: job execution timed out (last phase: model-call-started)`. A cron timeout is not held for transient retry, so alert/repair selection applies. The scenario (not committed) is `cron-explicit-failure-destination-sol-proof`: an owned job with `delivery.failureDestination` set to a separate alerts group, plus an owned control job with an inherited route.
  - Before (only `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts` reverted to `2be13a6`), [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f320d64984bb784e13a5c2007b7cae6e): **fails as reported**. After two real timeouts, `alerts=[]`, and the owner conversation got a real repair turn instead: "Both runs hit the automation’s 4-second timeout while requesting a 3,000-word report. May I increase its `payload.timeoutSeconds` to 300…?"
  - After (`1f547521`, verified source), [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_17beb2c27b8d7d3a6c8d1213cba4d7a7): **pass**. After two real timeouts, the alerts group received `Automation "qa-cron-sol-explicit-…" failed 2 times / Cause: timeout`, with no owner-conversation repair for that job. The inherited-route control job still got the owner repair turn ("Both runs hit the automation’s 4-second timeout… May I increase its timeout to 300 seconds…?") and no alert.
- **Mock-model proof on direct AWS Crabbox** (lease `cbx_0d7f4d42e2b3`; stopped after use): the same Gateway shape with `--provider-mode mock-openai` and scripted turn failures. Before, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_23056f2bcf7ae62ddda0fbd4ef6a8881): `alerts=[] repairRequests=2`. After, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_30fc6af8162f4f24f24bb4f74a334ec4): the alert was delivered with `repairRequests=0`, and the inherited control stayed repair-first.

For the same reason, the existing `cron-failure-repair-owner-conversation` scenario fails on base and head alike (its first run succeeds through `gpt-5.6-luna-alt`). This is pre-existing and unrelated to this change; it is a separate follow-up.

title: fix: iOS reconnects keep replaying rejected push registrations
body:
## Current maintainer review — delivery proof still missing

[Detailed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191565#pullrequestreview-5813972422). The existing rejection-persistence regression fails on main and passes on the private current-main integration. The iOS/Watch build, 24 native tests, 310 selected backend tests, core typecheck, scoped lint and generated PostgreSQL verification passed.

**Still Draft.** These tests do not prove restored alerts or background wake. The laboratory build is ad-hoc `localSandbox`; an authorized official signed physical-device run and hosted renewal-identity qualification are still required. The persistent recovery/retention contract and released-version upgrade/rollback also remain unqualified. No fabricated recovery screenshots, source fixes or merge were performed.

Tested author head `fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5`, private integration `5e97c3c229d6039fcf3ce77291f7cdf0b52be2f9`, frozen main `4d67ec34f59707df2d777912e9de9abd8d44aa32`. Later main `243e1c65` has no relevant input changes.

<details>
<summary>Original proposal and historical evidence</summary>

## Takeover coordination — publication unblocked 2026-11-06

The reviewed source is now published in this same PR at [fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5). Its public GitHub tree exactly matches reviewed/tested tree2975004a114019d7df70785d1f9875c17d8454f2. The final PR diff contains only the32 intended product files. Generated Bun caches caught during publication verification were removed in a follow-up commit; history was preserved. The publication gate was cleared under the authorized request; no global permissions were changed.

@ekinnee — thank you for the [579aa20d product candidate](https://github.com/ekinnee/openclaw/commit/579aa20dc9d9d2167c875de325d2c49435cfea79) and [source-bound handoff/checklist at6296e75f](https://github.com/ekinnee/openclaw/tree/6296e75fdf53bbba143c699a020cbc307a458456/handoff/pr191565). The APNs-specific cleanup was incorporated; unrelated demo/macOS baseline cleanup already superseded by upstream and evidence-only handoff files were not imported.

**Testing help requested:** if your Mac setup remains available, can you rerun the same selected Swift suites and simulator build on fc1fa6bc? Your earlier28-test/native-build result remains bound to579aa20d, not this refreshed source. Separately, can you run the signed-device checklist on your approved iPhone/test Gateway once a signing maintainer supplies an authorized official-relay-capable build tied to the final SHA? Personal Team signing alone is not that proof. Please confirm whether you can install the authorized build through its supported distribution channel. We need actual notification receipt and background-wake observations across rejected-cache recovery, reconnect/relaunch and bounded repeat attempts, without reinstalling/re-pairing as recovery. Share sanitized results only—no signing keys, tokens, grants or private device identifiers.

**Still draft:** maintainer acceptance of the recovery/persistence contract, official signing, current-source native/visual/device qualification and final-head CI remain pending. Restored notification delivery is not claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Official iOS apps can reconnect successfully while continuing to reuse relay enrollment that APNs rejected with `410 Unregistered`, leaving alerts and background wakes unavailable.

## User Impact

This proposes bounded, registration-scoped recovery and an in-app retry path without reinstalling or re-pairing. Permission, successful publication, and delivery health remain separate: renewed/published registration is explicitly **delivery unverified**.

**Draft — not ready to merge.** Maintainer acceptance of the recovery/persistence contract, native Swift build/test/lint checks, before/after UI screenshots, and signed official-device receipt testing remain outstanding. This PR does **not** establish that notification delivery is restored.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway preserves typed relay rejection on the existing registration owner. Republishing the same enrollment cannot erase the rejection merely by advancing its timestamp. Test pushes, wakes, and approval sends share the rejection-recording path; a stale result cannot poison a replacement enrollment.
- iOS consumes the existing authenticated `node.event` result, requests a current APNs token, and forces fresh relay enrollment for one automatic recovery cycle per unchanged token/scope. The existing publication flow serializes overlapping callbacks; failures stop automatic renewal and expose **Retry notification setup** in Diagnostics.
- Scoped Keychain enrollment caches retain rejected enrollment and consumed budgets across relaunches and Gateway switches. A matching shipped singleton is moved only after its scoped copy is saved. A new handle alone does not reset the budget; explicit manual retry or a changed token can authorize another attempt.
- Direct APNs behavior and unrelated registrations, pairings, Gateway credentials, and App Attest keys are preserved. No new RPC, configuration option, dependency, or version bump. Missing-registration #146791 is not folded into this fix.

## Evidence

**Current published source:** HEAD fc1fa6bc25fc3be40d4bac65a875e00aef7a1af5, base2dc6deb7dd2fae392c03da64da175cc842ccdd70, tree2975004a114019d7df70785d1f9875c17d8454f2. Current-tree verification passed326 unique tests across8 selected files /4 wrapper shards (53 infra +78 Gateway +195 schema/catalog tests,106.70s), production core and affected test typechecks, focused type-aware lint on12 files, pinned SwiftFormat0.63.1 on11 files, and scoped whitespace. Fresh independent review completed three chunks with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The32-file patch independently reproduced the exact tree; the published GitHub tree and required human credit were verified. This is not current-source native build/device or broad-CI proof. Earlier dated results below remain historical/prior-head evidence.


**Revision qualification (2026-11-03):** `pnpm test src/infra/push-apns.store.test.ts src/infra/push-apns.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.apns-registration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **52 tests across 3 files**, 66.82s wrapper wall time. The rejection regression now uses real HTTP instead of mocked fetch. The registration regression no longer mocks the event handler or pairing owner. This proves those local boundaries, not the hosted relay, WebSocket authentication handshake, iOS consent/route revocation before actual enrollment/publication, or device receipt. Fresh independent review of the complete candidate completed three chunks with no P0–P2 findings.

The primary regression failed before the production change for the intended reason: after a fixed relay `410 Unregistered` response, store reconstruction and unchanged enrollment republication had no retained `relayRejection`. The seven existing store tests passed on that baseline.

| Local check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Current push transport/store suites | 50 passed; real loopback HTTP rejection, reopen/unchanged republication, zero-I/O suppression, delayed old rejection vs replacement, successful HTTP control, revoked send authority, peer/direct controls |
| Current node.event registration integration | 2 parameterized tests / 6 route scenarios passed through actual handler, paired-device binding, NodeRegistry and worker admission; replacement/invalidation preserve prior and peer registrations at transaction and commit |
| Final store + read-kernel suites | 12 passed, including rejection/reopen/republication, fresh admission of an older-state copy, replacement protection and unaffected peer/direct registrations; 45.31s command wall / 5.02s Vitest |
| Earlier Gateway event/registration/push sibling suites | 79 passed; final modified event suite rerun: 54 passed, 64.02s command wall / 58.14s Vitest (mostly compiler/import setup) |
| Production and targeted infra/Gateway test typechecks | Prior production checks passed; current infra and Gateway-methods test typecheck shards passed |
| Scoped production/test lint; touched TS/JSON/Markdown formatting; whitespace | Passed |
| Kysely/PostgreSQL generation and SQLite catalog checks | Passed; generated outputs verified |
| Staged test-line budget | Passed; owned allocation accurately updated to 289 net TS regression/fixture lines |
| Pinned iOS formatting | SwiftFormat 0.63.1 built from exact tag; six files mechanically corrected; `pnpm format:swift ios` passed, 0/504 files require formatting |

Native Swift regressions are added for cached rejection, reconstruction, same-token renewal, repeated attempts/manual retry, **A → B → A enrollment counts**, changed-token renewal, direct transport, and matching-only legacy-cache migration. They have **not been executed** here: Linux has no Xcode/iOS SDK. The pinned SwiftFormat gate now passes; that is not a native build, SwiftLint, Swift test, or delivery result. No real device received a test push.

<details>
<summary>Review, persistence contract, and remaining qualification</summary>

**Review:** Local Auto Review, P0–P2, completed all four batches against base `bf35e054b0062c64e5577b165a3ae629adc3d2d0` and final candidate tree `cca63b6b6d1a2c7d6ceeb703fbaaaf83c455483c` with no remaining findings. Earlier findings about scope eviction resetting/bypassing recovery were addressed with per-scope enrollment persistence and an enrollment-count regression. This is static review, not human maintainer acceptance or native/device proof. The simplification pass retained one registration owner and removed redundant enrollment-flight bookkeeping; the complete token/publication cycle is serialized at its existing caller.

**Proposed persistent contract:** One nullable `relay_rejection_reason TEXT` column on `apns_registrations`, through existing same-version additive admission; null means no recorded rejection, not verified health. The affected SQL operation is an additive column change, with no row backfill or new index. SQLite STRICT admission may inspect existing rows; production-scale upgrade timing has not been measured. The existing database migration/backup owner is unchanged; no new backup mechanism is introduced. A compatible pre-change shared-state backup and matching runtime are required for rollback qualification. The test uses a closed, isolated older-state copy, not a released-binary upgrade.

Keychain cache/retry state is scoped by installation, Gateway identity, relay origin, environment, profile, proof policy and topic; records persist across scope switches and replace only that scope's enrollment. Matching legacy singleton migration leaves other bindings untouched and removes the singleton only after a scoped save. App Attest state is not reset. This persistence/retention/rollback contract still needs maintainer acceptance before merge.

**Before ready/merge:**
- Run the native build, focused Swift tests and pinned SwiftLint check; inspect and attach sanitized before/after Diagnostics screenshots in chat and this PR.
- Reproduce on the affected signed official device and compare token reacquisition alone, fresh enrollment with unchanged token, and the combined path. Re-establish the rejected baseline between experiments; verify actual alert receipt and background wake, not just APNs 200/publication/a different handle. Do not target unrelated devices.
- Qualify the hosted relay's enrollment identity semantics. If fresh enrollment returns an identical handle/grant, this candidate conservatively retains Gateway rejection; actual renewal semantics and the smallest successful recovery remain unproven.
- Complete latest-stable upgrade/rollback and supported-backend qualification. An integrity-verified 2026.10.10 released-store baseline and WAL-safe SQLite backup were created, but the isolated current-source harness did not complete credential-migration custody; that setup failure is **not** a product migration verdict or passing upgrade evidence. Live PostgreSQL migration and production-fleet upgrade cost were not tested.
- Obtain maintainer contract/security review and applicable CI. CI seconds are not available yet; no hosted review or merge was requested.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

title: fix(google): restore tool calls with Python keyword parameters
body:
Supersedes #143178, thanks @HighervGround.

Related: #143176

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gemini tool calling when a declared parameter is a Python keyword such as `from`, `class`, or `lambda`.

## User Impact

Google and Vertex tools retain their original parameter names at execution. Existing suffix names and nested user data remain intact. This replacement includes only the Google parameter repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shared Google converter chooses unused underscore aliases for declared top-level keyword parameters, restores returned arguments, and reapplies the aliases during signed history replay. GenerateContent, Vertex, Interactions, and explicit prompt caches use the same mapping. Cached requests retain canonical schemas for decoding while omitting cached declarations from the outgoing request.

The duplicate prompt-cache declaration builder is removed. Necessary production growth implements collision-safe schema-based mapping across the existing transports; there is no new cache, setting, persistence format, or dependency.

## Evidence

- Current-main source check: `65a125adc598deff3ded853f155acfa616d39c0c` passes tool properties and returned arguments unchanged. The contributor's captured Vertex bisection reports `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` with `automations.in`, and a valid call after renaming that property. [Google's function-calling documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling) describes JSON Schema parameters but does not document a Python-keyword restriction. No live Gemini API calls were made.
- Red before: on the unchanged main implementation, `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts` had exactly the two new failures (outgoing schema and inbound restoration), with 32 existing tests passing. [Crabbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551852373).
- Green after: 211 tests pass across the four changed behavioral suites (SDK/Interactions, prompt cache, managed Google/Vertex); the 14 prompt-prefix cases and the 28 message-conversion/lifecycle/request-config cases also pass. Touched-file type-aware lint (0 warnings/errors), format, and `git diff --check` pass. [Crabbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41552191472). Final named-test invocation took 45.49 s plus setup; the managed transport file took 10.84 s wall time, with the cache suite dominated by existing compiled-worker setup. Exact-head [CI run 41555285820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41555285820) passed: 45 successful jobs, 28 skipped, 11 min 51 s wall time and 7,810 summed job-seconds.
- CI repair proof: [the first CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41553763628) found an extension test importing a core helper and a declaration-only assertion helper accepting the SDK’s broader tool-list type. Both test-only defects are fixed; production code is unchanged. The boundary guard, managed Google/Vertex transport, and SDK regression file now pass all 167 cases in 57.71 s, with touched-file lint/format green. [Crabbox repair proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41554614333).
- Review: Local autoreview of the complete implementation diff against `65a125adc598deff3ded853f155acfa616d39c0c`, P0–P2, returned `scoped-clean`; no findings. A supplemental P0–P2 review of the CI fixture repairs against `6fe9bc666896375a6ae42fa5e2f925acbaae10f9` also returned `scoped-clean`. Simplification retained one schema/argument mapping owner and removed the duplicate cached declaration projection.
- LOC: production +116/−19 (net +97), tests/support +342/−11 (net +331). The dedicated test-line allocation covers only these regressions: schema projection, execution, signed replay, managed/Vertex transport, Interactions argument deltas, and cached declarations.
- The contributor branch was read through `gh` and was never checked out or run. Validation ran on our reimplementation in Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox. Broad proof is PR CI.

title: fix(memory): recover indexing after embedding request timeouts
body:
Supersedes #144488, thanks @Finn763

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes memory indexing repeatedly sending the same oversized request after the embedding watchdog expires, leaving the indexing pass incomplete on a slow provider.

## User Impact

Indexing retries smaller requests after a watchdog timeout. A single input that still times out fails visibly. Query deadlines and provider-owned timeout defaults stay unchanged; no configuration or reindex is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing batch policy now splits a watchdog timeout immediately instead of spending three attempts on the same payload. Existing network retries, cancellation, malformed-response handling, ordering, and cache publication keep their owners.

Main already includes #167891 (603f60a38cfe658f3b9f1aee509595f39dc4540e), which removed the independent HTTP timeout and bounded deep probes. Sync cleanup also releases the pending promise and preserves dirty work after failure. The remaining defect is batch convergence, not a permanently latched sync. We are declining a new timeout setting: automatic recovery fits the existing provider-owned timeout contract without another public control.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI run 41552993820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41552993820) passed on 3ad47b920f306e84a8f2d7055836b6a66fae25d7, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. No inherited-failure exception was needed.
- Hosted ClawSweeper review of that same head found no actionable findings or before-merge requirements; it notes the disclosed live CLI/transport proof gap.

- On main 9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d, the new manager regression fails for both text and structured batches with `MEMORY_EMBEDDING_OPERATION_FAILED`; the 24 existing manager cases pass.
- Blacksmith Testbox [41551644742](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551644742): both affected suites pass, 85 tests. The real manager watchdog aborts requests of sizes 3 and 2, then returns all three vectors in order through singleton requests, with no unchanged-payload retry or provider degradation. Existing policy tests retain network retries and single-input stopping behavior.
- After a typed abort-error fixture correction: 26/26 manager cases pass again, touched-file type-aware lint reports zero warnings/errors, formatting passes, and `git diff --check` is clean. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Local autoreview of the complete candidate against 9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d, P0–P2: scoped-clean. The subsequent typed fixture rejection was inspected manually; production is unchanged.
- The focused two-file run takes 30.62 seconds including worker preparation; the final manager-only rerun takes 38.49 seconds. Test bodies take under one second. New watchdog cases use fake timers. The successful `checks-node-changed` CI job takes 298 seconds including shared setup.

Proof uses a synthetic provider through the production manager watchdog and split policy. Real single-core llama.cpp hardware and a live agent turn were not exercised. Contributor code was read with gh only and was never checked out or executed.

Simplification: one existing policy owner, no new state, helper, setting, or SDK surface. Production +5/−1 (net +4); no dead or duplicate production code in this narrow owner could be safely removed. Tests grow 30 lines for the missing watchdog recovery boundary, covered by a separate allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

title: fix(sandbox): remove containers when backend preparation fails
body:
Supersedes #143755, thanks @aishwary-dongre.
Related: #143685

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a newly created Docker or Podman sandbox stays running when backend preparation fails after its container has started.

## User Impact

User impact: failed provisioning removes its newly allocated container and registry entry while preserving the original error. Reused containers and the existing revoked-access retention policy are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep backend mount inspection, filesystem bridge loading, and persistent-generation preparation inside the existing container lifecycle lock and cleanup boundary. This reuses immutable-ID cleanup and consolidates the duplicated allocation result; it adds no rollback tracker or attempt-wide custody protocol.

This is a bounded provisioning repair. Failures after a completed backend is returned to agent-attempt preparation remain follow-up work under #143685. No configuration, migration, or operator action is required.

Production delta: +37 lines, including the typed internal preparation callback; most of the backend diff is indentation. Duplicate allocation-result construction was removed. Tests grow by 22 lines, covered by the dedicated regression allocation record.

## Evidence

- Reviewed current main at `9039ceb43cf462dd5c35b9063ad68a5e86361e7d`, existing cleanup from #150713, and the recent Podman timeout fix #188770. The remaining leak was the backend inspection after the lifecycle returned.
- On Blacksmith Testbox, the new fake-runtime regression is red on main: create=1, start=1, remove=0 after backend inspection fails. With this fix, the same regression removes the fresh allocation, preserves a reused runtime, and propagates the exact original error object.
- 73 focused tests pass across `docker.access-lifetime.test.ts`, `docker.partial-create-cleanup.test.ts`, `docker-backend.test.ts`, and `dependency-template.test.ts`. The four-file run took 68.86s command wall time; one stale mock-call expectation was corrected, and its 33-test backend file passes in 41.47s command wall time. Wall time was dominated by transforms. [Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551266696).
- The two affected Gateway checkpoint cases and both cleanup regression cases pass on a fresh Testbox lease (51.40s command wall across two named files). title: fix(update): select PostgreSQL in migrated finalizer
body:
Closes #191542

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: migrated update finalization starts a fresh process without the parent’s PostgreSQL selection. Its first ledger adoption opens the SQLite engine anchor as a state database, reports a missing schema role, and never publishes the final result.

## User Impact

Normal fresh-process finalization now enters the existing updater database scope before executor, ledger, and terminal-result access. It reads the configured engine and environment-backed connection through the canonical owner, preserving PostgreSQL history and the local anchor.

The capability check stays configuration-free. The Windows native Job is retained before any pool worker starts. Doctor, post-core, and plugin-cohort modes retain their existing recovery and configuration owners; cleanup remains the existing best-effort owner with database drains before pool closure. No schema, configuration, credentials-in-wire, protocol, or timeout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Engine selection is process-local and cannot cross the spawned finalizer boundary. Reusing `withUpdateDatabaseEngine` repairs the producer rather than inferring an engine from the anchor or repairing the anchor as SQLite. The extra pool call is retained only for sibling modes; normal finalization uses the canonical scoped preparation.

## Evidence

- **Actual causal RED:** baseline `f381764cf5964d7885ed459f41a9cf8041dfd244` on pinned `bf35e054`, [PostgreSQL conformance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41553655060/job/125648227953). The executed fresh child reports “schema role missing; expected global” for its PostgreSQL anchor, then the regression fails because no parsed child result was returned (13.2 seconds). The infrastructure group had 274 passing cases; both other conformance shards passed. Earlier skipped ordinary-node tests and static assertion-narrowing failures are not product proof.
- The regression retains the actual parent selection, delegated executor, fresh finalizer, PostgreSQL pool and ledger. Only the absent native-service observation is isolated and guarded to owned state. Production child mode excludes test preloads and worker environment-data fallback. It requires the parsed child result, terminal PostgreSQL row, and anchor-only local file, so parent fallback cannot pass.
- The supplied core result intentionally fails to bound the same adoption/publication boundary without unrelated Doctor/package work. This does not claim a complete successful Git update, actual schema migration, or managed Gateway restart.
- Fresh complete independent autoreview against pinned `bf35e054` (Codex, P0–P2): scoped-clean. Focused canonical oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass. Production TypeScript net +12 lines; most diff is lexical scope indentation. Exact allocation181 covers175 PostgreSQL process-test lines, one native-service fixture line and five existing wire/cleanup fixture-isolation lines. No test-only production seam or timeout increase.
- **Actual fixed-head GREEN:** `6dd924b6f93b415ae58e87a75fd7180430005f55` passed the [executed PostgreSQL finalizer regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41557001142/job/125658928774) in 17.561 seconds. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the required exact-head checks succeeded, with planned skips retained. The protected `openclaw/ci-gate`, `openclaw/dependency-review`, and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` statuses also succeeded. CodeQL's aggregate is neutral because 18 other analysis configurations are absent; this is a coverage warning, not proof that all CodeQL configurations analyzed the change. No local product tests were run on the production host. This proves selected-storage finalization and result publication for the intentional failed-core case; it does not claim serving health or a full successful Git upgrade.

Reported by @etzelm. The earlier CLI-role repair #187160 establishes a different bootstrap fact; this change supplies the missing engine selection.

title: docs(macos): explain Gateway Local Network recovery
body:

title: fix(voice-call): ignore echoed caller transcripts during playback
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes phantom caller turns when realtime transcription returns the assistant's own words during carrier playback.

Supersedes #159145, thanks @mnowrot. Related: #159140.

## User Impact

Unconfirmed playback echo no longer enters caller history or independently starts a host-forced agent consultation. Callers can still interrupt through the existing local speech threshold or provider barge-in.

This filters host caller turns. Realtime providers still receive every inbound audio frame and own their VAD, transcripts and responses; provider-side echo interruptions and transcripts arriving after the tail remain outside this fix. Quiet overlapping speech without a barge-in indication can be ignored during the window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing audio controller admits caller partials/finals only after detected caller speech, a provider interruption, or expiration of carrier playback plus a 400 ms tail. Carrier timing accumulates successfully sent audio even after the local pacing queue drains. An admitted partial remains eligible through its final, and finalization consumes that admission.

The original blanket masking of local barge-in is not retained because it also prevents genuine caller interruption. No config, provider implementation or SDK contract changes. The Deepgram UtteranceEnd fix in #191498 is untouched.

Production delta: +34/-1, net +33 lines for the carrier deadline and turn-admission state in existing owners. The simplify pass found no dead or duplicate owner path that could safely offset this necessary growth. title: fix(plugins): recover reply publication after failed replacement
body:
Closes #189579

## What Problem This Solves

A failed serial plugin replacement can retire model/reply publication and fail to restore it, leaving conversations unavailable until a manual Gateway restart. New inbound messages can also exhaust their recovery attempts while a recovery restart waits for admitted work.

## User Impact

Config writes and explicit `plugins.reload` now request the existing work-draining recovery restart when their actual model/reply rollback fails. The plugin operation still reports failure and `committed:false`. Failed model owners use their existing backoff while restart resources remain live, preserving queued replies’ recovery budget. Cancellation or failed emission resumes ordinary recovery.

Ordinary plugin failures whose reply publication survives keep their existing behavior. Already dead-lettered messages require the documented manual resubmission. This fix is not yet released.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin lifecycle owner records actual rollback-publication failure in the existing typed error. The Gateway consumes that fact under current reload ownership and reuses its recovery coordinator, including fresh lifecycle-lease preparation after the failed operation unwinds. The model owner reads existing live restart timers, polls and admission leases. No new queue, schema, configuration, retention policy or mirrored recovery state.

The earlier low-level reply fixture now uses canonical dispatcher settlement, so its retained delivery callbacks release their actual session admissions before subsequent restart tests. No controller reset, drain bypass or timeout increase is used.

## Evidence

- **Original-boundary RED:** baseline `0827b5340d339` on pinned `bf35e054`, [CI 41551456186/job 125640857413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41551456186/job/125640857413). title: fix(ios): share to gateways using approved TLS pins and service headers
body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes sharing from Safari or another iOS app to a Gateway that native chat can reach using an approved TLS certificate or custom service headers. ## User Impact Share uses the connection already approved in OpenClaw. Reconnect the app after upgrading or changing service headers to refresh Share access. The extension cannot approve a new certificate or complete browser sign-in; those actions still require the foreground app. ## Why This Change Was Made Approved pins and service headers use the existing shared Keychain owner, bound to the Gateway identity and URL. title: fix(ios): discard stale wake commands after chat or Gateway changes
body:
Related: #165515 (focused-chat routing; intentionally unchanged here).

## What Problem This Solves

Buffered Voice Wake recognition can outlive a chat, agent, or Gateway change and create another command after the previous command was canceled.

## User Impact

Destination changes discard pending commands and buffered results from the old capture; fresh listening resumes through existing admission gates. This does not fix main-versus-focused-chat routing, which remains separate in #165515.

Gateway session resets and push-to-talk socket invalidation now also tear down and restart Voice Wake recognition, rather than only canceling the pending command. Restart remains subject to the existing listening and admission gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing VoiceWakeManager owns recognition retirement: destination invalidation tears down the old pipeline/generation and cancels its command; internal start/teardown use cancellation-only bookkeeping to avoid recursive invalidation. Phone-focus and selected-agent changes invalidate before assignment independently of Talk's session-key shortcut. Watch-started Talk can already hold the next phone destination or next agent's main key, so that shortcut alone cannot retire the old capture. Current main's focus persistence, selected-agent cleanup, configured-route authority, and restoration ordering are preserved. No new routing owner, generations, configuration, automatic resend, or basic focused-routing callback changes.

title: fix: skip discarded plugin setup captures during startup
body:
Supersedes #154885, thanks @unknowbug.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway startup captures a large installed plugin dependency tree just to run an auto-enable probe whose result is discarded for an already-enabled plugin.

## User Impact

Already-enabled non-channel plugins avoid unnecessary setup capture. Probes still run when channel enablement, a restrictive allowlist, or preference ordering can change selection. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generation capture copies and hashes declared dependency packages to retain immutable source and resources. The auto-enable owner now filters satisfied selections before requesting that work, and readiness stays on metadata. Capture containment, symlink, hardlink, receipt, and native-admission checks remain with their existing owners.

The shared filter serves both asynchronous preparation and candidate detection. Removed the redundant xAI-specific collector and repeated configured-entry checks. Production delta: +3 lines; the remaining growth connects the filter to both callers.

title: fix(deepgram): answer calls when noise prevents endpointing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: callers hear no response when background noise prevents Deepgram endpointing from completing their confirmed speech.

Supersedes #158226, thanks @Weiming-Hu. Credit also preserves @weiming, the other human commit-author identity in the original PR.

## User Impact

Deepgram can complete confirmed caller speech on its provider-detected word gap while the call remains open. A long pause can split a thought into separate turns. This fallback requires interim results and endpointing at most 5000 ms; other configurations retain their existing behavior. No new settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main only completes open turns on `speech_final` or `from_finalize`; its fallback timer is close-only. Enable `utterance_end_ms` using the existing endpointing value (minimum 1000 ms), flush confirmed text on valid `UtteranceEnd`, and ignore the provider's stale `-1` sentinel. Provisional text is never promoted to a completed transcript.

This deliberately revisits the endpointing-only choice in 73b0312e525126200e1ac83c632166112eed16f7 to address the reported noisy-call stall. Deepgram documents the [word-gap behavior and limits](https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/utterance-end). The original PR's new idle-flush option, watchdogs, and retry machinery are omitted.

Production delta: +9 lines net (+14/-5). Removed the single-use `clearFinalizeFallback` wrapper and kept its cancellation in the turn owner. Test delta: +14 lines; the separate allocation covers the stalled-turn, stale-event, and duplicate-terminal regressions.

## Evidence

- Fake Deepgram stream through the real WebSocket session: red against main `054516fb8e11f06358bab0ab2b90d5313c4ac6fb` (confirmed text plus `UtteranceEnd` produced `[]` instead of `["a"]`); green after the fix, **15/15** tests. Existing close, reconnect, bounds, and provisional-gap cases also pass.
- [Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41537201489): named file `extensions/deepgram/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts`; red wrapper wall 48.52 s, green 39.32 s (Vitest 36.77 s, mostly cold worker compilation). [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41538807625) passed on the replacement head in 15m32s wall time across the planned jobs; an individual-file CI timing was not exposed in the retrieved logs.
- Touched-file type-aware lint: zero warnings/errors, exit 0. Touched-file oxfmt check: exit 0. `git diff --check`: pass.
- Autoreview of the complete local candidate against the pinned main above, with full Deepgram owner/test and Voice Call consumer context: **scoped-clean, P0–P2**, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191498#issuecomment-6590379983) also found no actionable findings and recorded the same live-call proof limitation.

title: fix(ollama): embeddings fail for configured local hostnames
body:
Supersedes #149589, thanks @triciah73.
Related: #163315

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Ollama memory embeddings fail when the configured local hostname resolves to loopback or a container host-gateway address, while chat to the same host works.

## User Impact

Memory search can reach the same configured Ollama hostname as chat. The provider-owned endpoint receives the existing chat private-network policy; separate remote embedding endpoints retain their existing SSRF checks. Requests cannot redirect that private-network access to another hostname. The existing Podman exact-origin redirect restriction remains. No configuration or stored-data migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `buildOllamaBaseUrlSsrFPolicy` only when the existing provider-host ownership check succeeds. That shared policy allowlists the configured hostname on every hop. The global guard and public SDK are unchanged.

Production LOC is net zero: resolving the provider base URL once removes the duplicate resolution in this owner. The regression replaces a policy-shape assertion with real adapter/guard/HTTP proof. title: fix(sessions): find CJK text inside transcript words
body:
Related: #140736

Supersedes #143127, thanks @holny

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session transcript searches returning no results for interior Chinese, Japanese, or Korean text, such as `会议` in an unspaced sentence.

## User Impact

After a word search misses, CJK terms can find literal substrings with excerpts around the match. Other terms retain native word, punctuation, symbol, and prefix semantics. The retry scans selected transcript text; narrow the session selection for large histories. Queries that already return hits keep their existing behavior, so broader partial recall remains tracked by #140736.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `unicode61` index treats an unspaced CJK run as one token. A native SQLite probe also found zero `trigram` MATCH hits for the reported two-character query. A query-side retry handles short terms while retaining persisted indexes and avoiding a startup rebuild or schema migration.

Both retrieval attempts execute inline in the existing worker kernel and share filters, active-branch exclusion, ordering, limits, and hydration. Substring-only scans filter mapped sessions before reading text. Residual terms use native word parsers: SQLite probes one bounded query row in a private in-memory FTS5 index built by the existing schema owner, and PostgreSQL uses its native simple parser. This preserves meaningful indexed Unicode symbols without restoring handwritten separator ranges.

Production growth is +102 lines, including the native parser probe needed to preserve the recent punctuation contract. There was no safe pre-existing dead/duplicate owner code to offset this; retrieval retains one query. The 36 regression-test lines extend existing fixtures across both engines.

## Evidence

- Red on unchanged main `3120ab41d8c828a78e045e97d6897b4da53bbadd`: all 5 new CJK cases failed with empty hits; all 15 existing cases passed.
- Residual-punctuation regression red on `dfa2276f7ddefbcb4ac4dca3900bf25893c7306b`: `会议 -` returned no hits, with the other 19 owner cases passing.
- SQLite owner proof on `74deb0802b6f2bf81272b999831e5f778939e121`: `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **20/20 passed**, wrapper **66.59s**, Vitest **64.25s**. Includes punctuation-only remainders and an indexed 🦞 positive/negative control.
- Real PostgreSQL product flow on `74deb0802b6f2bf81272b999831e5f778939e121`: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <isolated-test-dsn> -- src/infra/database-engine/session-search-product.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **4/4 passed**, wrapper **68.93s**, Vitest **66.16s**. Adds CJK punctuation, mixed-word, and missing-word checks. Existing real-worker fixtures and backend setup account for the file wall times.
- These focused commands ran on Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox, lease `tbx_01m6f5bxrp176pqjkh0wzcgb5j` ([lease workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41535859930)); both exited 0 before lease shutdown. Touched-file oxfmt and type-aware oxlint passed with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`; `git diff --check` passed.
- Final schema-owner reuse: existing `buildSqliteMemoryBodyFtsSchema` supplies the private probe, with no new dialect SQL definition. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m6f6xv0f6g16cwx241yt89mv` ([workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41539705281)): SQLite **20/20 passed**, wrapper **76.96s**, Vitest **74.48s**; touched-file format/type-aware lint passed. PostgreSQL inputs are unchanged from the real-backend proof above.
- Final complete-change Codex autoreview at P0–P3, with SQL adapters and the worker entry point supplied as context: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The ClawSweeper punctuation finding is addressed by native token probing and the regressions above. Exact-head [CI run 41540347074](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41540347074) completed successfully for `3528e6c7db8a5b00b018905b94c2146290cab2c3`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, the full selected test plan, types, lint, build, and architecture/baseline checks. No inherited-failure exception was needed.

title: fix(xai): stop OAuth refreshes from retaining a stale expiry
body:
Supersedes #144082, thanks @jensonhirst.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated xAI OAuth refreshes when a successful token response has no usable access-token lifetime and inherits the previous token’s expiry.

## User Impact

Valid refreshed tokens remain reusable until their new refresh window. A response without a usable lifetime now fails sign-in or refresh and requires signing in again. During proactive refresh this can end the old token’s remaining temporary availability earlier; accepting that recovery avoids publishing a false expiry and repeatedly spending rotating refresh grants.

## Why This Change Was Made

Require the shared login/refresh parser to derive an expiry from `expires_in` or the access token’s JWT `exp`, then publish it unconditionally. Keep the existing identity, endpoint, retry, and refresh-settlement policies. xAI already uses the shared safe duration converter; the shared OAuth runtime does not supply a replacement HTTP refresh client.

The five added production lines enforce the missing-lifetime check; both optional-expiry publication branches disappear. The 44-line test allocation covers rejection at login/refresh and fake-clock reuse through the existing usability contract.

## Evidence

- Red on main `3120ab41d8c828a78e045e97d6897b4da53bbadd`: the five new lifetime rejection cases fail because invalid responses are accepted (43 controls pass).
- Green on this branch: 52 tests pass across `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts`, `xai-oauth-refresh-bytes.test.ts`, and `xai-oauth-entry.test.ts` (16.34 s Vitest / 19.85 s wrapper). Fake clocks cover one refresh, reuse, the five-minute proactive refresh boundary, and actual expiry, with both duration and JWT lifetimes.
- Focused tests run on Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox, lease `tbx_01m6f1bkkdv4scs68ezhrbs2ab`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41525298288). No contributor code was checked out or run.
- Touched-file lint passes for both changed TypeScript files; formatter check passes for those same files. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Independent autoreview: scoped-clean through P3, no actionable findings. The helper refused the public `credential-state.ts` filename as context; its exact margin semantics were inspected separately in source and exercised by the focused tests. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; [hosted ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191464#issuecomment-6588770585) with no findings or pre-merge blockers. Its reviewed-head end-to-end proof limitation is stated below.
- Source audit: the OAuth manager validates refreshed credentials with zero margin before SQLite settlement, while ordinary reuse uses five minutes. A still-future inherited expiry therefore previously persisted and immediately refreshed again. No credential schema or storage owner changes.
- No live xAI account or full Gateway run was used; HTTP responses are synthetic fixtures. This proves the plugin lifetime boundary and shared eligibility contract, not live-provider response frequency.

title: fix(discord): keep browser private-network access out of CDN downloads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord attachment and sticker downloads accepting private or link-local CDN destinations when the Gateway enables private-network browser access.

Supersedes #144259, thanks @SebTardif.

## User Impact

Discord CDN downloads ignore browser `allowPrivateNetwork` and `dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork`. Existing installations relying on these broad flags for private-address CDN answers must use an explicit trusted hostname in `browser.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames`. Normal public CDN hosts, RFC2544 proxies, and explicitly enabled IPv6 fake-IP proxies remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select supported fields in the existing Discord policy owner instead of spreading arbitrary browser permissions. Keep hostname and origin exceptions, configured denials, and the narrow IPv6 proxy option. The fixed Discord RFC2544 default makes its old Boolean merge redundant; production code decreases by 6 lines. Slack and Telegram build independent media policies and do not share this browser-policy merge.

## Evidence

- Crabbox/Testbox run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41522872804. Corrected regression fails for both browser flags with main policy blob `39430d5ac880d95492d9456c85c63c332b599bea` from `d316aecc43b9820300ba49b55ab2106abfd32eb6`; that policy blob was also verified unchanged on current main.
- With the replacement, all 38 tests in `message-media.ssrf.test.ts`, `message-media.references.test.ts`, and `message-media.test.ts` pass using `pnpm test <named files> --maxWorkers=1` (44.27 seconds Vitest wall time; the new regression itself takes under one second). The regression runs real `resolveMediaList` → `saveRemoteMedia` → DNS/SSRF checks and media storage, with synthetic DNS and HTTP response fixtures. Public attachments and stickers save exact response bytes; RFC1918, loopback, IPv4 metadata and IPv6 link-local answers reach no HTTP fetch. RFC2544 and opt-in IPv6 ULA downloads succeed.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) found one test-harness issue: directly passing a Vitest fetch spy selected the guard's DNS-free mock branch. A plain async wrapper now exercises real DNS policy checks; red/green was repeated with that correction. Final autoreview of the full local delta against `d316aecc43b9820300ba49b55ab2106abfd32eb6` is scoped-clean through P2, with no remaining actionable findings.
- Touched-file type-aware oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Oxfmt passes for all four touched source/test/docs files; `git diff --check` passes. All compilation and Bun staging required by these wrappers ran remotely.
- The 72-line test allocation covers the new destination-authority regression, including both media types, both broad flags, private/link-local DNS and preserved narrow proxy behavior. No shared test ceiling change.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff` only; it was never checked out or run. No live Discord account, HTTPS CDN network or Gateway/model E2E was exercised. Final-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41530199811) completed successfully in 765 seconds of workflow wall time, including queue time; all required checks passed before merge. The first CI run identified missing required attachment fields and an overloaded DNS mock type; both fixtures were corrected without casts, and the corrected named file passes all 4 tests (78.51 seconds Vitest wall time), touched-file lint/format, and a fresh P0–P2 autoreview of the correction against `fe11e0bc405a7938ab868a1be433421d577f00ae`.

### Real network proof

On the replacement's unchanged production policy, an isolated Crabbox HTTP harness ran real `resolveMediaList` → `saveRemoteMedia` → DNS guard → pinned HTTP sockets → media files, with no `fetchImpl` or mocked HTTP transport. Task-owned loopback aliases supplied RFC2544, RFC1918 and link-local listeners. Main policy blob `39430d5ac880d95492d9456c85c63c332b599bea` sent one private connection/request and saved media (red). Restoring the replacement policy passed (53.42 seconds Vitest wall time):

```text
REAL-CDN proxy {"connections":1,"requests":1} saved=true
REAL-CDN forbidden 10.19.0.144 {"connections":0,"requests":0} saved=false
REAL-CDN forbidden 169.254.19.144 {"connections":0,"requests":0} saved=false

```

Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41527822982. The redirect began at an allowed CDN address and targeted another allowed CDN hostname resolving privately. Exact-host trust was exercised separately after the zero-connection cases. Listeners, aliases and temporary harness were cleaned up. HTTPS and a live Discord account remain untested. No data model, persistence reader/writer, config schema or stored-format contract changes; a stored-data upgrade scenario does not apply. The compatibility impact and explicit-host recovery for existing installations are documented above.

Final-head CI test cost: the four destination-authority regression cases passed in 0.135 seconds of test execution; their `changed-extensions-config-1` shard completed in 87.19 seconds including transforms and neighboring tests. title: fix(macos): prevent first-launch Gateway failures after upgrades
body:
Related: #188683 — this is a separate updater repair; no endpoint changes are included.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app can fail its first launch after an upgrade by starting an old Gateway after credential preparation has migrated state beyond that Gateway's supported schema.

## User Impact

App-managed profiles can complete the upgraded first launch without Retry, relaunch, manual Doctor, or data reset. Explicit pins, installation ownership, service custody, and schema/integrity refusals remain intact. No new schema, configuration option, dependency, or committed version bump.

The native `doctor --client-credentials` operation now also completes pending local runtime-intent migration; it still does not start/stop services or force a runtime choice. Generic Gateway/node credential callers retain their existing ready fast path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Credential readiness and daemon runtime-pin readiness are independent. The narrow credential Doctor skipped the pin handoff, leaving `migrationPending` after schema advancement. Swift correctly preserves the old seed while that handoff is pending.

The native CLI now waits for the existing daemon migration owner after credential maintenance releases custody, retaining the captured engine selection. This also runs when credentials are already ready after a partial attempt. The existing owner preserves pin bytes/timestamps and refuses conflicts while retaining both stores. Swift activation, seeding policy, and pin formats are unchanged.

## Evidence

title: fix: environment-selected dev profiles target the wrong Gateway port
body:

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: CLI/TUI clients and the macOS app select port 38556 instead of the dev Gateway's port 19001 when started with `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=dev` and no explicit port.

## User Impact

Environment-selected dev profiles connect to the same default endpoint as `--dev` and `--profile dev`. Explicit environment/config ports and macOS stored port overrides retain their existing precedence.

An existing dev service explicitly pinned to 38556 keeps that port. Its clients must keep a matching explicit port (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=38556`), or the service must be reinstalled on 19001. ## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lightweight profile utility now owns named-profile port defaults, including the reserved dev port. CLI bootstrap and config resolution share it without importing config-path initialization into early bootstrap. The Swift default mirrors it.

The simplification pass removed the config resolver's inline profile hash, the CLI's duplicate hard-coded dev port, and a redundant environment trim. Production grows by 12 lines for the shared function/imports and Swift dev case; regression tests grow by 9 lines. A dedicated allocation of four test lines covers the four new TypeScript table cases; Swift cases reuse the existing precedence test.

## Evidence

Fixes Active Memory skipping deep recall for English questions such as “What phrase did we use for the deployment plan?” when deterministic retrieval has no strong match.

title: fix(k8s): restore temporary workspaces on non-sticky volumes
body:
Related: #156985

Supersedes #157046, thanks @myagizmaktav.
Supersedes #164067, thanks @cellrishi-code.

## What Problem This Solves

Kubernetes deployments can reject session-observer temporary workspaces because the mounted `/tmp` volume is writable without sticky protection.

## User Impact

Applying the updated manifest supplies a safe `/tmp` for temporary workspaces while retaining the non-root Gateway and filesystem safety checks. Custom temp volumes must be writable by the init container; arbitrary-UID platforms must adapt the init and Gateway identities together.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fsGroup` adds group permissions and setgid, not the sticky bit. Reuse the existing UID-1000 init container to create and chmod its own child directory, then mount that child at `/tmp` with `subPath`. Preparation errors stop initialization with a diagnostic. This incorporates both proposals without adding another init container or image.

Main's private-state temp fallback (#187737) still rejects a group-writable, non-sticky state-volume ancestor, so it does not replace a safe temp mount. No filesystem checks are relaxed.

## Evidence

- On Blacksmith Testbox (`tbx_01m6ehr69awk6s4bnch9azx2k8`, [allocation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41482686669)), ran `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test test/scripts/k8s-manifests.test.ts test/scripts/k8s-deploy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` against trusted main plus the new regression: **1 failed, 6 passed**, with `insecure-permissions` naming the mode-2777 ancestor and missing sticky bit. With the manifest repair, the same files passed: **7 tests**, 1.32 s Vitest duration / 2.82 s runner wall time. The manifest file took 35 ms, including 26 ms for the regression.
- The regression executes the manifest's init shell against fixture paths, models the `subPath` boundary, and uses real fs-safe workspace creation, writing, reading, and cleanup. No Kubernetes cluster or model/provider call was run. Neither contributor's branch was checked out or executed.
- Independent local Codex autoreview of the complete change against `21e7ad20d3e5f56ddaefdb44b59a2716d5ea05da`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings; subsequent edits narrow a YAML value for lint and apply mechanical formatting. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; one [hosted review was requested](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191294#issuecomment-6582837591) under the maintainer workflow. It completed on the final head with no findings.
- Touched-file type-aware oxlint passed with zero diagnostics. Oxfmt passed all three touched source/doc files; markdownlint passed with zero issues (the repository config also includes the docs collection). `git diff --check` passed. After the YAML type narrowing, both named suites passed again: 7 tests, 1.50 s Vitest / 3.47 s runner wall, manifest file 25 ms and regression 19 ms. All Node dependencies, SDK declaration preparation, and Bun staging ran remotely. PR CI supplies broad checks.

The simplification pass retained one existing init owner and one filesystem regression. Runtime TypeScript: +0/-0; manifest: +6/-0; tests: +65/-2 (net +63); docs: +6/-0; test-budget allocation: +2/-0. The six manifest lines are necessary preparation and mount wiring; no dead or duplicate main-branch code in this area can be removed to offset them. The separate 63-line test allocation covers this regression without changing the shared baseline.

Current-head broad proof: [PR CI run 41485045237](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41485045237) **passed** on `31fa1623001ca50489b0b2cdfbe128ccbcca3921`: 28 jobs succeeded, 30 intentionally skipped, zero failures. title: fix(ollama): reuse protected connections during setup
body:
Credit: [Vincent Koc (@vincentkoc)](https://github.com/vincentkoc) for the report and requested behavior.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/bda3a7dd-8232-4846-87ca-2e375baa64d8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b9865f07-ca2c-4999-a2fb-a4415e03eeda)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Ollama setup failing to reuse an existing protected connection when its saved endpoint, credential or custom request settings are needed.

## User Impact

Users can prepare the existing Ollama connection without replacing its saved credential references or changing their current default model. Choosing a different endpoint does not send the previous connection's key or headers to it.

No installation, automatic model-loading policy, public configuration schema or migration changes are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Saved URL reuse and credential identity are one boundary: using the right URL with the wrong auth owner is still a broken or unsafe connection. Setup now resolves only the selected connection's private HTTP inputs and carries the existing guarded transport through discovery, inspection, optional pulls and cloud-status checks. Saved configuration keeps its authored references.

Transport precedence, network/TLS/proxy policy and secret materialization still use existing public SDK owners. The plugin-specific projection remains necessary because the generic bearer-key helper requires authentication and cannot represent every keyless or header-auth local setup. No core wire or SDK export is added.

## Evidence

- Source-only boundary proof: the actual preparation handler, WizardSession, real provider loading, guarded synthetic HTTP and isolated authored-config persistence. This is not native Ollama or live-provider qualification.
- Original baseline `88d2ee6be575aa96ec4951796f9b831f4d522207` fails the actual protected-endpoint preparation regression. The new `/api/me` cancellation case also failed before its owning cancellation repair. Final focused proofs pass, including endpoint replacement and live grant revocation without cancelling the wizard.
- The owner, registration, preparation handler and supporting native request/selection modules were byte-identical on observed GitHub main ea614e5a78e97956762a1cb26d8c939b05c32533, so this fix is standalone. A read-only merge preview against observed main d6c8ad3ff2fe2bd5c540f0a8dd7002a437f08c7c also completed without conflicts; no base integration was needed.
- Final commands are `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Per-file wall times: `src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-setup-ollama.test.ts` 82.71s (1 composed real-handler test; test body 3.04s), `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` 10.11s (30 tests), `extensions/ollama/src/setup.cancellation.test.ts` 8.05s (3), `extensions/ollama/index.test.ts` 12.95s (50), `extensions/ollama/lazy-import.test.ts` 9.06s (1). Existing preparation/concurrency/authority siblings: 3 files / 11 tests, 27.29s combined wall. CI seconds: not run / unknown.
- Selected-agent/profile behavior additionally uses the existing credential owner mocked at its unit boundary; that checks correct admitted store, locked identity and agent directory, not real runtime credential materialization. TLS/proxy policy remains delegated and source-inspected, not live-network qualified.
- Production Ollama package, changed extension-test and Gateway-test typechecks pass. Changed extension/core lint, formatter, `git diff --check`, changed-file line cap, max-lines and assertion-safety pass. The exact net test growth is recorded as 335 lines; no thresholds or ignores are weakened.
- Author pr-simplify pass completed. The first isolated native OpenAI P0–P3 review found one P1 and three P2 issues; all four were verified and fixed (live-caller forwarding, selected agent scope, scoped environment/profile fallback, cloud cancellation). A fresh full final-tree isolated native OpenAI review found no P0–P3 findings and independently traced all four repairs through the actual owners. These are static narrative assessments, not autoreview helper-validated receipts or independently rerun tests.
- Scope remains interactive preparation. The unchanged noninteractive setup and post-selection `ensureOllamaModelPulled` flow are not qualified here for protected-connection reuse. No migration/update behavior changes.
- Not run: full package build, CI, native Windows/WSL/macOS Ollama setup, rendered-UI or real-model inference qualification.

title: fix(cli): recover Windows Control UI publication from temporary file locks
body:
Supersedes #156445, thanks @YangManBOBO.

Related: #156443

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent Windows plugin Control UI build failures when antivirus or an indexer temporarily denies publishing a staged generation.

## User Impact

Windows plugin builds recover from temporary rename denials. Existing immutable generations still require matching bytes; permanent failures retain the original filesystem error and staging is cleaned up.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main treats `EPERM` as an existing-generation collision even when the destination does not exist. Keep publication in its current owner and use the existing async retry scheduler for six attempts, waiting 100/200/400/800/1600 ms. Retry only `EPERM`, `EBUSY`, or `EACCES` on Windows while the destination is absent; true collisions incur no retry delay.

The existing UI-script rename helper is synchronous and the package-update helper is bound to update authority and path-identity checks, so neither fits this async build publisher. No new rename helper or structural refactor is introduced. Production growth is +16 lines; there is no dead or duplicate code in this owner to safely offset it.

## Evidence

[Red-before CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41474967757/job/125379112130) at `450d0059fa06d`: the unchanged main publisher fails 7 cases, with 25 passing, in `src/cli/plugins-control-ui-build.test.ts` (12.91 seconds). Transient `EPERM` reaches a nonexistent-destination read; the other Windows denials are never retried. The same tests cover exhausted retries, other errors/platforms, cleanup, and collision validation.

[Green-after CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41476601885/job/125385273400) at `1c290f39a2261`: the byte-identical test file passes all 32 cases in 8.71 seconds. Plugin UI reproducibility and scaffold compilation also pass. [The full CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41476601885), including lint, type checks, UI checks, and baseline ratchets, passed on this exact head.

Autoreview completed on the full change and supporting source at P0–P2 with no actionable findings. The simplification pass retained the existing owner and validation path. The exact +43 regression-test lines are allocated separately to protect the distinct Windows recovery/error and immutable-collision contracts; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

Two Testbox attempts stopped during setup before tests ran, so PR CI supplies red/green and broad proof. No tests, broad checks, containers, or builds ran on the production Team host. Native tooling used only its managed dependency cache. Windows behavior is covered with injected platform and filesystem errors; a real Windows antivirus hold was not run. The contributor's code was read through `gh` and was never checked out or executed.

Contributor credit: `Co-authored-by: YangManBOBO <pan.xiaobo@xydigit.com>`.
