title: fix(worktrees): keep pack maintenance converging beside fetch
body:
## Problem

Part of the **worktree base latency investigation 2026-11-02**. On the team Gateway, the Control UI "Updating repository…" phase (`preparing_worktree_base`, default-branch base refresh in `src/agents/worktrees/base-ref.ts`) took p50 5.2 s, p90 48 s, p99 261 s and max 302 s over 176 starts. GitHub `ls-remote` takes about 0.95 s. Meanwhile the shared `blob:none` project clone has built up 1,216 packs (1,211 promisor, about 430 GB), no multi-pack-index, and stale temporary pack files.

Live evidence from read-only log and pack-directory inspection (no writes to the live clone):

- **Fetches wait behind maintenance.** The slowest `git/ref-mutation` holds on 2026-11-02 were 807 s (10:57), 429 s (05:34), 298 s (03:32), 168 s (04:30) and 124 s (09:46). Each one ended next to a managed-worktree cleanup pass. A fetch queued behind the 10:57 hold waited `queueWaitMs=229670`. That matches the slowest sample's `baseRefresh=234126`, which happened even though the fetch itself has a 60 s timeout.
- **One lost lease stops pack maintenance until restart.** `worktree Git maintenance suspended (packs) … OpenClawStateLeaseError: project checkout lease … was lost (lease loss: expired; expiredByMs=1 …)` was logged at 2026-11-01 08:14, 2026-11-01 12:59 and 2026-11-02 05:34. Each time, pack consolidation and temporary-pack cleanup stopped for that repository until the Gateway restarted.
- **Some temporary files are never reclaimed.** The pack directory still holds 14 `tmp_idx_*` and 6 `tmp_rev_*` files, some from September (~172 MB of indexes). These are left by interrupted `index-pack` runs. Cleanup only matches `tmp_pack_*`, and `gc.auto=0`, so Git's own prune never runs. The ~1.9 GB of recent ~375 MB `tmp_pack_*` files are interrupted consolidation outputs. The existing 24 h cleanup reclaims those, but only while pack maintenance is not suspended.

## Root cause

All on `main` @ `63c25f72`, in `src/agents/worktrees/git-maintenance.ts`:

1. **L219–236:** `maintainWorktreePacks` runs the whole pack pass inside `enqueueGitRefMutation`: temp cleanup, `verify-pack` of up to 128 MiB of indexes, and the `pack-objects --stdin-packs | index-pack` rewrite, with up to 30 min budgets since #189606. Every `fetch` and `update-ref` on the shared clone, including base-ref refresh, waits for the whole pass. The queue was originally needed for repository-wide MIDX writes and expiry, which #182204 removed. Today the rewrite copies every object of the selected packs regardless of refs, so only retiring the inputs touches files a fetch may be reading.
2. **L560 → L570:** the catch exempts only `ProjectCheckoutBusyError`. A lease lost mid-pass (heartbeat expiry, an `OpenClawStateLeaseError`) reaches `failed.set(repoRoot, state.stage)`. Pack maintenance is then marked failed for the process lifetime, as if the repository were corrupt.
3. **L246:** `/^tmp_pack_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/` never matches `tmp_idx_*` or `tmp_rev_*`.

## Solution

- Only retiring the replaced inputs joins the ref-mutation queue. Verification and rewriting run alongside fetch. The content-slot → ref-queue order is unchanged, and retirement still never overlaps an OpenClaw fetch (on Windows, an open pack cannot be unlinked).
- Any `OpenClawStateLeaseError` (busy or lost checkout ownership) now records a deferred pass instead of suspending. `withOpenClawStateLease` rethrows the loss as that error even when the loss killed the running Git child. A lost pass keeps its hourly slot, so it retries on the next hourly pass. Busy projects keep their existing behavior. Real Git failures still suspend as before.
- Temporary-file cleanup matches every `tmp_<kind>_` file, as Git's prune does. The existing Linux file-lease helper, 24 h age rule and identity checks are unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/managed-worktrees.md` updated for queue scope, lease-loss deferral and temporary-file kinds.

No new config, state or dependencies. Production delta: +46/−37 in one file.

## Impact

- Base-ref refresh no longer waits for pack verification or rewriting. On the live samples, waits drop from minutes to the milliseconds `fs.rm` retirement takes.
- A stalled lease heartbeat costs one batch instead of all pack maintenance until restart.
- Old `tmp_idx_` and `tmp_rev_` files are reclaimed.

### Convergence rate (synthetic repo)

This was a scratch measurement and is not committed. It used the real `createWorktreeGitMaintenance` on a synthetic repo with 40 distinct full-history packs, each one all history up to a different commit, like the live duplicates. Pack metadata was stubbed to the live shape (240 MB pack, 20 MB index). One maintenance pass ran per simulated hour:

| pass | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | 40→35 | 35→30 | 30→25 | 25→20 | 20→15 | 15→10 | 10→5 | 5→1 | 1→1 |
| this PR, lease lost during pass-2 verification | 40→35 | deferred | 35→30 | 30→25 | 25→20 | 20→15 | 15→10 | 10→5 | 5→1 |
| `main`, same lease loss | 40→35 | suspended | suspended | … | … | … | … | … | suspended (all 15 passes, stuck at 35) |

The rate is −5 packs per pass (a 6-pack batch under the 128 MiB index budget becomes 1 pack). For the live clone's ~1,206 full-history packs, that projects to roughly 240 uninterrupted hourly passes (~10 days), before counting new packs arriving.

## Evidence

- **Red on `main`** (the three tests below with the base `git-maintenance.ts`): all three fail for the defect.
  - lease loss: `outcome: "failed"` with `project checkout lease … was lost (lease loss: expired …)`.
  - ref queue: a ref mutation issued during the rewrite times out after 5 s, and the pass ends `stage: "suspended"`.
  - temp cleanup: `tmp_idx_abandoned` survives.
- **Green:**
  - `pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service.gc-performance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21/21.
  - Same file plus consumers `service.gc-lifecycle.test.ts` and `service.removal-budget.test.ts`: 59/59.
  - New tests take 80–224 ms each. File wall time is 191–282 s on this IO-starved host (transform 59–72%). CI seconds pending.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint on touched files, `run-format`, `format:docs:check` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` (under the ceiling, no allocation needed) all pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, branch mode, P2, with the cleanup helper, project-checkout, lease-error and git-exec sources as context): scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.87)".

## Accepted edge cases

- If a real Git failure and a lease loss happen in the same pass, the pass is deferred rather than suspended. The next hourly pass sees the Git failure again and suspends.
- An interrupted consolidation still leaves its ~375 MB `tmp_pack_*` output until the 24 h cleanup reclaims it.
- One batch per pass (hourly) is unchanged. Longer passes would hold the project checkout lease that session creation waits 30 s for, and add IO on an already IO-starved host.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Pack producer.** The live duplicates are full-history commit and tree packs (~720k–980k objects each). In a `blob:none` clone, a lazy promisor fetch of a missing commit uses no-haves negotiation, so it downloads all history again. A synthetic repro turned a 600-object base pack into a new 610-object pack after one `git cat-file -e <new commit>`. Fixing whichever callers trigger lazy commit fetches matters more for long-term convergence than consolidation throughput.
- **Lease heartbeat.** It is still unexplained why the heartbeat misses its 30 s window (`heartbeatAgeMs=30001`) under host IO pressure.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:2c02ef0f-93ed-4073-8394-ee46433fcdb6 -->

## Concurrent registration validation

Independent validation with the benchmark added in #192275 used 1,501 packs, 700,000 shared objects, 62,000 tracked files (~1.14 GB), and six concurrent deferred managed-worktree registrations while real verification was delayed five seconds. Five interleaved A/B pairs plus two A/A controls and a separate allocation pair passed without retries or discarded arms.

Registration median/p95 fell from **17,847.6/19,408.4 ms to 189.2/313.8 ms**; every candidate registration completed during the verification pause. Owner CPU median was **4.848→4.451 s**, process-tree CPU **26.63→24.93 s**, peak-process RSS **730,016→734,288 KiB**, and sampled allocation **99,247,320→99,641,072 B**. A/A owner CPU varied +3.17% and wall time +0.27%. Each arm consolidated 1,501→476 packs and passed retained-object, branch/tree, and full fsck checks. APFS/macOS synthetic owner proof; deployed Linux/btrfs behavior remains unmeasured.

Fresh complete-range Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Focused maintenance/lifecycle/removal suites: **58 passed, one platform skip**, 147.27 s wrapper wall time. #192275 separately bounds any remaining registration queue wait to 30 seconds with a notice and retryable error; resource-limited maintenance placement remains unchanged.

title: fix: hide operator Home from guests and start new sessions by default
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted guests could see the rolling operator Home conversation even when its composer denied participation. Implicit startup also opened Home instead of New Session.

## User Impact

Operator Home rows and transcript reads are withheld from session-only restricted guests. General-read and full-session operators retain explicit Home access. Implicit startup uses New Session while valid explicit links, unsent drafts and non-Home/native restoration remain supported. No new configuration option or permission grant is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session-sharing policy owns Home admission. Discovery, exact readers, HTTP/media, mentions and remote-ingress adapters forward current main-key/scope facts; sharing-cache identity includes the main key. Full-read mention requesters and connect-less internal callers remain supported without exempting restricted session-only grants.

The UI checks Home authority before cached transcript hydration, including literal aliases. Bootstrap owns native restoration before routing. Not-found recovery preserves non-Home conversations while excluding cached Home using canonical identity bound to the navigation-selected owner, including ownerless global keys.

The latest update completes individually audited conversation-fixture entry/navigation cutover through the existing URL helper while preserving intentional New/default, query/hash/history and denial controls. CSP interception and navigation use the same exact session URL. API, service-worker and phone setup repairs preserve their security/recovery assertions.

Denied Home and New Session reuse the existing Welcome status renderer and app-owned handle, preserving pending/failure/retry presentation without a second owner, polling, redirects, permission or locale changes. This minimal integration changes three production files, +14 net LF. Identical menu-locator reuse removes the affected fixture's max-lines violation without an exception.

## Evidence

Latest published head: `88d20b5fb91ba0840495ddda6a1e7104199a73b6`. The direct-5f49 update is 215 paths, 264,481 bytes, SHA-256 `7179c96bdcc202399b2d2794e9b031aa77360700d2a530450ef942479b04dd50`. Original pending failure is retained. Affected sidebar menu: **1 passed /8.80s wall**, ten unrelated cases not selected.
- Integration lint **21.39s**, UI types **1.67s**, E2E types **2.92s** passed. Baseline 1001-line violation was reproduced and repaired at 999 through identical locator reuse; scoped lint **6.14s** passed without suppression.

title: fix(ui): stabilize Details docking checks under load
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent WebKit CI failures when the Details browser test switches a docked inspector to a popover under CPU load.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change. The existing browser test waits for the native popover transition to complete before checking its open state, role, and geometry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resizing reaches the popover through ResizeObserver and Solid's scheduled updates. The test previously sampled native state against the default poll deadline. It now subscribes to the [native `toggle` completion event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#queue-a-popover-toggle-event-task) before changing the width and retains the same assertions. Timeout values, retry policy, production code, and test baselines are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original line-309 signature on unchanged `d934b070ce30`: 1/20 file runs with tests and two CPU burners sharing two CPUs. Alone: 0/20 failures. The original failure capture shows the expected popover layout by screenshot time.
- Post-change Linux AWS Crabbox proof: 0/20 failures alone, 0/20 failures of the changed file in full observed-order WebKit replays, and 0/20 failures under the same two-CPU/two-burner load.
- The complete WebKit project replays contain 73 files / 696 tests. The changed file passed in all 20 replays; 18 project runs reproduced the same baseline `control-theme.browser.test.tsx` color assertion, and two entire project runs passed.
- Named-file oxfmt, the canonical oxlint wrapper with `tsconfig.ui.json`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and `git diff --check` passed remotely. Median standalone file time: 3.58 s; under load: 7.39 s. Fresh CI timing and results are available in the linked run.
- Local autoreview of refreshed commit `bc333e7655380927016bfaab3cf61ab66014878b` against main base `43884ea219f802ba198970185eb2d17cdd9824e5`, through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The one-time base refresh replayed the identical one-file +6/−1 patch without conflicts.
- Fresh exact-head [PR CI run 41483996404](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41483996404).

The original [WebKit CI step](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41430938418/job/125229919809) did not emit queued-module records. The project replays use its first-observed test-start order with three workers; the exact original queue could not be recovered. Additional traced stress probes did not capture another failure, so there is no timing trace of the failing native transition.

The change replaces one test wait: production +0/−0 lines, test +6/−1 lines. No shared test helper changed.

[Performance proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41466789454/job/125350552133).

![Before automation prompt preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5ea51be-ad7d-4a6b-a1b4-2a891c1dfef2)

This remains historical-base evidence; required PR CI against the current target main passes (+11 B / +22 B). No baseline exception or budget change is used.

Visual evidence above: inspected synthetic mock UI in Crabbox, base `0267ad034a067` versus exact head `1e6246219e57b`, identical prompt and 1280×1000 viewport. The source hash matches the published file. Standalone capture only; no browser E2E regression added or run.

CI investigation: original [attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41466789454/attempts/1) failed the mobile-composer attachment-chip polling case. The same case passed on main; a different MCP catalog failure on main was not used to claim an inherited failure. The operator then explicitly authorized one failed-job retry and three named-file head probes to settle flakiness.

At exact head `1e6246219e57b`, [Crabbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41477229967) ran only `chat-composer-mobile.browser.test.tsx` three times with the pinned Bun runtime, two CPUs, and three workers. All three passed: 13 cases each, zero failures, with the requested file verified as the only executed test module. The named-file probes omit `--shard=2/3` so the single file executes. The one operator-authorized [failed-job retry (attempt 2)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41466789454/attempts/2) also passed. title: improve(worktrees): skip the default-branch fetch when origin has not moved
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Default-branch worktree creation unnecessarily fetches when origin still advertises the commit already tracked locally. The redundant fetch also enters the repository's Git ref mutation queue.

## User Impact

Worktree creation skips that fetch for an unchanged default tip. Changed or unavailable advertisements retain fetching and the existing warning/fallback behavior. Hydration, local fast-forward rules, cancellation, and the 30-second preparation reuse window remain owned by the existing preparation flow. To bypass the reuse window, fetch and choose an explicit base ref. No new configuration or cache is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the commit already returned by `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` and compare it with the local remote-tracking ref. This avoids an additional network request. The takeover rebases the original work onto main including `75694cca` and repairs the affected service fixture: creating the new commit directly in the bare remote keeps the local clone stale, so the test still exercises a real fetch and its timeout.

Related: #191130 (refresh deadline; separate change), #194712 (hydration output; separate change).

## Evidence

Rebased onto `7c0d3ab5a28774d2efefee24d535970539b27a1d`, which includes `75694cca`. The original implementation and verified contributor credit are retained.

The original two CI failures reproduce: the service fixture's push updates its own `origin/main`, so fetching correctly disappears and the expected 60-second fetch timeout is absent. Creating the commit directly in the bare remote fixes the fixture while retaining the timeout assertion. The unchanged-tip regression fails on the exact main parent because it performs an extra fetch. Real-Git coverage also checks default-branch switches, force-pushed rewinds, explicit refresh during the reuse window, and cancellation recovery.

Focused validation: 168 passed, 2 existing skips across `base-ref`, `service`, `service-branches`, `git-fetch`, and `git` suites. The repaired two consumer cases pass in 5.24 seconds; the three owner/Git files pass in 100.04 seconds (including transform time). `pnpm build sourcePerformance` passed. An isolated built Gateway's actual `worktrees.create` RPC produced the expected checkout SHA with one advertisement and zero fetches for a matching tip, and one advertisement plus one fetch for an independently advanced tip. No external services or production data were used.

Codex autoreview against the pinned base, including staged repairs and the benchmark, was scoped-clean through P2 with no actionable findings. The original and rebased production module bytes are identical.

### Measurement

Acceptance was fixed in this PR before measured runs: use the real default-base owner, five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs and five A/A pairs with fresh clone paths/processes; require identical selected commits, unchanged-tip fetch count 1 → 0, improved phase wall time/CPU/allocation, and investigate regressions above 20%.

Synthetic local-origin partial clone: 62,000 logical files, 1,142,784,000 target bytes, 600,000 unrelated historical blobs and 1,239 packs. Darwin/APFS, warm/unspecified filesystem cache; no agent/session database populated because this phase reads Git state rather than sessions or transcripts. This measures local owner work, not btrfs, network latency, mutation-queue contention, or complete send latency. Five-sample p95 is the maximum, not a production tail estimate.

| Metric | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseRefresh, ms | 211.93 / 345.15 | 136.02 / 153.03 |
| Main-thread CPU, ms | 17.798 / 19.338 | 12.464 / 13.222 |
| Native Git CPU, ms | 80 / 100 | 30 / 40 |
| Native Git peak RSS, MB | 30.097 / 30.163 | 24.609 / 27.361 |
| Main-isolate allocation, MB | 17.032 / 23.747 | 19.221 / 21.507 |
| Git commands / fetches | 7 / 1 | 6 / 0 |

Every paired wall-time and JS-CPU sample improved. A/A wall medians were 197.97 / 196.00 ms (−1.0%), supporting the 35.8% AB latency improvement. **Allocation improvement was not demonstrated:** its median increased 12.9%, its mean decreased 1.75%, and same-source A/A allocation had substantial spread (median −6.5%, p95 +14.8%). Do not treat the allocation acceptance criterion as passed or claim allocation neutrality. The counts, wall time, and CPU support retaining the optimization.

Reproduce using `scripts/perf/worktree-base-refresh-measure.ts --seed <fixture/seed> --base-file <saved-main-base-ref.ts> --output <new-directory>` through `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`. A restricted Visitor can upload a Beam, but opening its link fails with `missing scope: operator.read` because the UI requests the shared catalog before the receiver can authorize the publisher's own snapshot. Upload success and viewer authorization are separate outcomes.

## User Impact and Solution

Current verified Visitors can read only their own retained snapshots, without `operator.read` or broader shared-catalog access. Links remain authenticated, not public. Foreign and legacy ownerless rows fail closed; guests gain neither continuation nor deletion. `canView: true` describes this narrow server capability, not public sharing or proof that a particular view completed.

- Plugin-owned `beam.owned.list/read` require existing `operator.sessions.write`, an authenticated profile/current Visitor grant, and immutable `publisherProfileId` ownership. Mutable attribution cannot claim ownerless rows.

Upload worker ownership/quota transactions, stale updates, settlement and post-commit behavior are unchanged. No SDK/config/schema change, broad scope grant, Team rollout or release.

title: fix(worktrees): bound default-branch fetch by one refresh deadline
body:
## Problem

"Updating repository…" (gateway phase `preparing_worktree_base`) can hold session startup for minutes. The default-branch refresh is supposed to be bounded by `ls-remote` (30s) plus `fetch` (60s). On the team gateway (worktree base latency investigation 2026-11-02), the slowest start took 270.7s with `baseRefresh=234126ms`, and its fetch **succeeded** without a warning. A borrower sharing that attempt waited `baseWait=120557ms`.

## Root cause

The gateway's diagnostics for that start show that the time was spent waiting in a queue, not in Git or on the network:

```
10:57:40.637 slow Git ref mutation  queueWaitMs=0       queuedOperationMs=807300   (another writer on the same clone)
10:57:44.425 slow Git ref mutation  queueWaitMs=229670  queuedOperationMs=3787     (the default-branch fetch)
```

`fetchRemoteDefault` runs `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<default>:refs/remotes/origin/<default>` with `{ ...options, timeoutMs: 60_000 }` (`src/agents/worktrees/base-ref.ts:473` on `main`). A fetch is a ref mutation, so `withGitRefAdmission` (`src/agents/worktrees/git.ts:198`) first enqueues it on the per-clone `enqueueGitRefMutation` queue (`git.ts:238`). The 60s timeout starts only after the queue admits the fetch and its process starts. While queued, the fetch is bounded only by the caller's signal, and that signal has no deadline here.

As a result, any long ref writer on the same clone (`worktree add`, hydration, pack maintenance, a fast-forward) stretches the "60s" fetch to the length of its own run. In the slow start above, the fetch queued for 229.7s and ran for 3.8s, which adds up to the 234s `baseRefresh`. On Nov 2, the same log also shows other holders running for 123–807s and queued waiters waiting 47–230s.

## Solution

Give the default-branch refresh one deadline. `fetchRemoteDefault` arms a 90s deadline (the existing 30s + 60s budgets) before `ls-remote`, combines it with the caller's signal, and passes the result to the fetch:

- If the deadline expires while the fetch is still queued, the ref queue drops the fetch before it starts.
- If the deadline expires while the fetch is running, the process is stopped like a timeout.

Both cases take the existing fetch-failure path: keep the cached `refs/remotes/origin/<default>`, report `fetchSucceeded: false`, and add a warning that names the 90s budget and the wait for other Git ref updates. This adds no fallback mode, option, or queue policy.

The caller's own signal still owns cancellation and attempt retirement. The deadline applies only to the fetch call, so an expired refresh is not treated as a cancelled owner.

## Impact

- A held ref queue now adds at most ~90s of refresh to a default-branch start, instead of the holder's full duration (230s observed, up to 807s possible). The start then proceeds on the cached default with a visible warning.
- Borrowers sharing the attempt get the same bounded result.
- As before, the fallback does not mark the base fresh, so the next start retries the fetch.

## Evidence

Regression test in `base-ref.test.ts`: "uses the cached default when the fetch outwaits the refresh deadline in the ref queue". It uses a real Git repo and remote, a real ref-queue holder on the same clone, and the real `resolveWorktreeBase`. Only the 90s timer is replaced by a test-controlled signal.

- Base (`63c25f72`): **red**. The test times out after Vitest's 120000ms because the fetch stays queued behind the holder.
- Fix: **green**. The whole `base-ref.test.ts` file passes (51 passed).

Wall-clock repro (a scratch test that is not committed; real timers, real Git, real ref queue, with another writer holding the clone's ref queue for 150s):

| | wall time of `resolveWorktreeBase` | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | 151,482 ms | waited for the holder; `fetchSucceeded: true` |
| Fix | 91,698 ms | cached default, `fetchSucceeded: false`, deadline warning |

Other checks: `git-fetch.test.ts` and `git.test.ts` pass (43 passed). `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files.

Review: local autoreview (Codex engine, branch mode, base `63c25f72` → head `4c0ad6c7`, max priority P2) was scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The reviewer noted limited surrounding context and that it did not run the tests.

## Accepted edge cases

- The local reads before and after the network refresh (`git remote`, `config`, `symbolic-ref`, the cached `rev-parse`) keep their standard 120s budgets. They do not queue, and they are needed to produce the cached fallback. They are slow only when the host itself is IO-starved.
- The `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` update after a successful fetch is also a ref mutation, so it can still queue. It runs only when the remote default branch changes.
- `baseHydration` (`estimateWorktreeGitBytes`) is not covered, because the checkout needs those objects. Its 120s and 240s tails on this host come from local Git reads reaching their 120s budget on a clone with 1,216 packs and no multi-pack-index, and those starts failed. That belongs to clone maintenance, not to this deadline.
- The 807s ref-queue holder on Nov 2 was not identified from the logs. This change bounds its effect on startup but does not shorten the holder.
- I did not measure a remote that hangs. In this sandbox, a synthetic hanging `upload-pack` made `ls-remote` end with a cleanup-uncertain error at its 30s timeout on base. That is a separate path from the queue wait.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: improve: compare large media and audio buffers directly

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The same retained cases preserve exact byte, length, order, and metadata checks while summed retained-file case-time medians fall from **10.699s to 0.619s**, saving **10.079s (94.2%)** in this measured batch.

Use native `Buffer.equals` assertions inside each plugin test. X uses its existing Node assertion; xAI uses labeled Vitest boolean assertions. The earlier shared-helper imports were rejected by the enforced plugin test boundary and are removed without adding an exception. Keep the media chunk indices/sizes and request metadata assertions. For xAI, assert exactly two queued chunks and compare each position against its corresponding original input. Production code, fixture sizes, cases, timers, and cleanup are unchanged.

The update-helper conversion is dropped because its measured whole-file case-time saving is below the approximately 0.3s retention threshold. Both that helper and the consumer held by #156200 are byte-identical to the base. Its measured trial remains in the evidence table for transparency.

title: improve: hand off portal previews in private chats

## What Problem This Solves

Agents without a Control UI side panel are directed to the Portals page even when the user explicitly requests a private app-preview link in chat.

Requested by @vincentkoc in the [original discussion](https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2115408545948852444).

Agents are explicitly guided to return the existing portal's authenticated launch URL for a requested private handoff to the authorized recipient, while retaining the Control UI panel path for in-UI previews. This is an agent-guidance change, not a new transport, automatic message sender, permission grant, or network setup. The agent still needs existing portal tool access and the deployment still needs reachable private ingress. No authentication, tool policy, Gateway configuration, or tunnel behavior changes.

One small, static guidance source now supplies the system-prompt presentation advice, both portal tool descriptions, and open/list results. Existing portal URL generation and proxying remain the single networking owner.

The focused regression extends existing prompt and portal-tool tests; no additional Gateway boot or test harness is introduced. The separate 13-line test allocation covers the exact net regression growth without changing the shared baseline.

title: fix(plugins): distinguish CLI inspection from Gateway state
body:

Supersedes #155761, thanks @Yun-0000.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `plugins inspect --runtime` can report a plugin as loaded even when the running Gateway never loaded it.

## User Impact

Runtime inspection names its local status `CLI status` and reports the running Gateway's state separately. JSON adds `inspectionScope: "cli"` and `gatewayRuntime` (or `null` when no Gateway runtime fact is available). Local hooks/tools remain available; snapshot output is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `plugins.list` RPC already reads the Gateway's active plugin registry, so the CLI reuses it without adding an RPC. Gateway lookup/query failures produce a warning and unavailable Gateway state while preserving the local report.

The simplification pass removed the detail formatter's duplicate runtime flag. Production growth is +39 lines to query and label the two processes, preserve local diagnostics when the Gateway is unavailable, and retain the existing detailed inspection contract.

title: improve(ui): move Draft beside Incognito on desktop
body:
## What Problem This Solves

On desktop and tablet, the new-session **Draft** toggle sat in the composer footer and only appeared while you hovered it. On narrow phones it already sat at the top next to **Incognito**.

## User Impact

User impact: **Draft** now sits beside **Incognito** in the new-session page's top-right privacy rail at every width, and in the header capsule on all phone widths. Draft and Incognito are now found in the same place. The **+** menu still offers Draft.

Draft and Incognito both decide how the new thread is recorded, so both belong to the page, not to the message being written. The rail toggle (`VisibilityToggle`) already handled Draft. It hid only because of CSS breakpoints, so this change removes those breakpoints and deletes the footer chip with its styles. title: fix(ui): preserve New Session test failure diagnostics
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing failure diagnostics when New Session browser tests close their contexts during teardown.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible product change. Developers get the existing diagnostic report and screenshot before the test page is destroyed. No configuration, migration, or user action is required.

**This does not explain or fix the original CI renderer crash. Its cause remains unresolved.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated page opener maintained a second context list and closed contexts directly, bypassing the suite's capture-and-cleanup lifecycle. It now delegates to the existing suite owner; the dedicated New Session factory enables that owner's tracked cleanup. No shared runner, timeout, guard, or diagnostic policy changes.

One native Vitest/Chromium regression verifies the private report is complete when the context closes, the original error and real screenshot survive, public diagnostics exclude private failure text, the next test has no leaked contexts, and the browser disconnects. Only external application-server startup is stubbed. The helper changes remove five net lines; the native regression adds 144 lines, with an exact 139-line net test allocation.

## Evidence

- **Base red → fixed green:** the context-close witness changes from `closedWithReport: [false]` to `[true]`. The fixed native regression passed in 12.347 seconds (57.50 seconds Vitest wall time). Hooks, Chromium, capture, and teardown are real.
- **Affected consumers:** 12 tests passed across responsive-welcome, keyboard, agent-identity, and config-startup, covering multiple contexts, mobile options, nested helper construction, and existing `withPage` cleanup.
- Both affected UI typecheck leaves, type-aware scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, and test-line ratchet passed on the reviewed source.

### Provenance and limits

Standalone head `b88d2f47121ffb2caadf63d4a8da353f53dae836` transplants only that diagnostic repair onto official main `fcf176cc1f600fea3dde30bfab8930b7751ffe7a`; it does not include the synthetic CI-merge or backup feature ancestry. title: feat: schedule automatic updates in Settings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway operators cannot choose when automatic updates start.

## User Impact

User impact: Settings → Updates now offers hourly (the existing default), daily with a time, weekly with a day and time, and a custom cron expression. Times follow the Gateway host’s timezone, not the browser’s.

## Why This Change Was Made

One optional `update.auto.schedule` cron string stores the schedule; presets are UI projections. No timezone field, new package dependency, or storage migration is added. Existing cron calculation and the Gateway scheduler remain the owners.

Configured schedules gate campaign starts, including startup, restart, and interactive Dev refresh. Missed windows are skipped. Stable rollout delays, idle/countdown behavior, restart safety, manual updates, and the one-hour hold remain intact. Schedule changes hot-apply and cancel pending campaigns without interrupting an applying update.

Requested by and implemented for @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a6452bb-b935-4086-8f43-3e795f64d30e)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/7bf59300-3432-4c32-b379-9b13390a8546)

## Evidence

- Built Control UI with a synthetic Gateway: all five Updates E2E scenarios passed (151.20 s total). The schedule scenario exercised hourly → daily 04:25 → Tuesday 04:25 → custom cron → hourly and asserted serialized `config.set` writes. Inspected before/after screenshots and weekly/custom states are embedded below.
- Daily campaign admission failed on base because it started at 10:00 despite a 10:30 schedule. The repaired daily, sub-hourly, skipped-window, hot-rearming, and interactive Git behavior passed. Both final extracted schedule regressions also passed (668.00 s including cold preparation; 7.143 s test execution).
- Initial implementation: scheduler/consumer tests 75 passed, 71.61 s wall; campaign/lifecycle/manual-refresh 41 passed; config 74 passed, 19.20 s; existing cron/DST 13 passed, 1.76 s; Updates view 42 passed, 3.12 s.
- Initial implementation: core/UI production typechecks, infra fixture typecheck, targeted lint, Solid controller guard, i18n verification, changed-document formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Initial canonical autoreview against `fb2c420c4e75ea43884869786f5b0e9b7af36c06`: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.84. The review includes the extracted scheduler and test fixture. Lead independently reviewed campaign admission, hot reload, cron reuse, and UI serialization.
- [Published-driver upgrade proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41439871998/job/125269758422) passed on attempt 1: published npm `2026.10.9` → exact candidate `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852` (`2026.10.9`), with no candidate relabeling. Readiness returned 200, running version and durable-session survival were verified, and package integrity/npm-12 installer acceptance passed. The cell took 435 seconds; the complete workflow took 2,154 seconds. This uses synthetic state and the maintained systemctl harness, not native-systemd qualification.

### CI repair validation

The [first PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41439183580) identified PR-caused import-cycle/extracted-wrapper closure errors, two test static-analysis errors, and omitted config baseline artifacts. The follow-up repair moves the existing cron validator and timezone normalization unchanged into a shared leaf, includes that leaf and the already-pinned `croner` package in extracted wrappers, corrects the test typing/shadowing, and regenerates the baseline. No scheduler policy or visible UI changes were made.

On an isolated AWS Linux runner with 4 vCPUs, 15.3 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1, and one test worker:

- Selected CI regressions: 35 tooling + 16 native provisioning tests passed, with 2 existing skips; 385.577 s wall. All originally failing test cases passed.
- Cron/config/CLI consumers: 99 tests passed across four files; 89.494 s wall.
- Runtime/tooling lint passed with zero warnings or errors (36.996/158.004 s). UI E2E test types passed (19.200 s); architecture check found zero cycles (42.303 s); config generation/check, test allocation, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- All 37 feature/repair source hashes matched before and after execution. Generated outputs were downloaded unchanged and matched the final worktree; 15 retained proof-artifact hashes were verified. The single temporary runner was released after 35m36s, without extending its lifetime.
- Fresh canonical autoreview of the repair delta against `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852`: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.93; final source verification passed.

The config baseline intentionally grows by exactly one core key (2,584 → 2,585) for the requested optional `update.auto.schedule` field. Channel/plugin counts and hashes are unchanged. The 250-line test allocation covers campaign admission/restart, hot policy changes, config rejection, routed UI persistence, and the two additional fixture/import lines needed for the repair; the shared scalar budget is unchanged. Per-test CI seconds are not yet extracted from broad CI artifacts.

### Final CI result and remaining proof gap

[CI run 41455922677](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677) completed with **failure** on head `eaf807dc6c04fe68c7237d9461b2063a3c696372`; all 89 job records are terminal. The sole failed workload was [control-ui-performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677/job/125313331221); the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also failed. The [final failure table](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677/job/125323853067) classifies this as **new**: the matching main job passed, and selected scope was not compared. It is not relabeled as inherited-only.

Both performance builds succeeded. Chat boot gzip increased from **1,278,812 B to 1,278,972 B (+160 B)**, with 20 requests unchanged. Because the base already exceeds the 1,277,887 B fixed cap, only the existing **64 B** build-variance allowance applies: the candidate is **96 B over** its effective 1,278,876 B limit. Startup JS increased 9 B, New boot JS 17 B, and CSS growth was zero.

Logged payload growth is confined to the lazy Settings copy and Updates-page chunks at the log's rounded precision. The same schedule UI source previously produced a -4 B Chat gzip delta against an earlier main base. This suggests generated asset-hash/minifier sensitivity, but it does **not** establish hash-only byte equality or a passing budget. The performance job does not retain the paired distributions, and its helper deletes the temporary base build. A matched base/head build with retained JavaScript, compression sidecars, HTML, and source maps is still required for decisive attribution and any justified fix. No performance budget or variance allowance has been changed.

Validation scope: earlier cold-worker attempts timed out before executing the extracted fixture; the final extracted tests passed. The optional full changed-file gate reached its 600-second local budget after its first six checks passed. Focused repair validation is green, but full CI is not green for the reason above. The upgrade rehearsal remains evidence only for `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852`; the repair changes runtime module inputs, and no upgrade rehearsal of `eaf807dc6c04fe68c7237d9461b2063a3c696372` is claimed. No live Gateway settings or services were changed.

### Password-free rejection fixture (November 4)

Commit `0eaabb3cc7606d7e381cf70b9919c737093fc16f`, published in head `3679341be3efbae7b466a4eb6bb12ee945186f97`, replaces one synthetic negative-URL fixture in `src/config/config-misc.test.ts` with a transparent username-only URL containing no password. The existing expected-false schema assertion is unchanged. The original combined fixture short-circuited on username; this replacement preserves that rejection without claiming independent password-branch coverage. No encoding, runtime reconstruction, scanner policy, or production behavior changes were made.

- Focused config suite: **74 passed**, 42.97 s test time / 45.28 s wrapper wall, with one worker.
- Actual-schema sensitivity proof verified nonempty username and empty password, rejection by the real schema, acceptance of the clean origin, and that masking only the parsed username in an isolated process makes the unchanged expected-false assertion fail. The URL parser was restored and the production owner remained byte-identical.
- Targeted formatting, lint, config test types, and diff checks passed. Fresh canonical autoreview was P0–P2 scoped-clean with no findings, confidence 0.99, and final source verification passed.
- This delta is test-only; existing screenshots remain representative. It does not repair the prior performance failure or extend the old-head upgrade evidence above.

**Hosted review remains blocked before a verdict.** The [November 4 re-review request at 11:01:54 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6628986837) targeted head `3679341be3efbae7b466a4eb6bb12ee945186f97`. Its [correlated status changed to Failed at 11:05:46 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6628989117); [run 41818159154, exact-review job 126534173101](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41818159154/job/126534173101) failed at the `agent_input_scan` stage (`reason_code: findings`, non-retryable), producing no review verdict. The retained manifest reports **two findings**. Only the **first** has been located: the unchanged base synthetic negative-URL fixture at `src/config/config-misc.test.ts:153`, in base revision `fb2c420c4e75ea43884869786f5b0e9b7af36c06`; its blob identity and path hash were independently matched against GitHub. The second finding has not been identified. This is a fresh refusal, separate from the [November 2 refusal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6580594500), and it does not establish that the new username-only literal passed scanning. Base content and removed patch text remain in the review range. No raw fixture values are reproduced here, no scanner policy was changed, and successful local autoreview is not represented as hosted approval.

title: improve(ui): hide self-only People in Session Details
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session Details shows a People section even when the signed-in viewer is the only person associated with the session.

In a single-user OpenClaw setup, a People section that only lists the person already using it feels unnecessary and out of place. On a multi-user server, the same section provides useful ownership and collaboration context. The intention is to remove the self-only noise while keeping People when it tells the viewer about someone else.

## User Impact

The right-hand Details sidebar omits that redundant section. Another person's session and sessions with multiple people still show People. Unknown viewer identity or incomplete people metadata keeps the existing conservative display. No unrelated header, sharing, mobile, or layout changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing deduplicated owner/creator/participant union and compare its sole typed identity with the authenticated viewer. This adds no state or identity-resolution policy. The bundle repair deletes a redundant actor projection and compares the schema-qualified profile viewer by identity type and ID; other namespaces remain distinct.

title: fix(doctor): await inspection snapshots and native repair phases
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can start a synchronous SQLite snapshot from lint, inspection, migration, or a later native repair guard. Large databases then block signal handling and leave expensive images behind. Chrislro’s stack sample in #178359 identified the parent blocked in node::SyncProcessRunner.

## User Impact

The candidate awaits snapshot preparation and repair observations, carries cancellation through worker cleanup, and checks free space when inspection needs a private image. Current admission reads are consumed in the synchronous frame that performs a service, configuration, credential, or database effect, with existing physical ownership and final native checks retained.

Core #190788 already supplies platform boot provenance, cancellation and capacity protection. This PR completes the coupled caller cutover and guards unexpected cold synchronous preparation. Private CURRENT images compare the complete captured family before admission. Unknown provenance still requires the conservative integrity gate. No schema, public configuration, protocol version, or dependency changes.

## Evidence

Assembled head8bd6391d72f4697da9f5378753f8ce6fa9e326b8 includes main714490716002d24b939817366f277872b6ea2825 and the late Reader/Process fixes. title: fix(ui): pin Pages and Users sidebar headers like Sessions
body:
## Problem

The Sessions sidebar header sits above the list scroller, but the Pages and Users headers were rendered inside it. So:

- the Pages/Users header scrolled away with its list, and the scroll fade masked it;
- with a non-overlay scrollbar, the scrollbar gutter took width from the header, so the collapse button sat further left on Pages than on Sessions;
- collapse-button placement relied on per-panel margin overrides (`.sidebar-session-toolbar …`, `.sidebar-online …`), while Pages had none.

## Solution

- Render the Pages and Users headers in the same slot as the Sessions toolbar, above `.sidebar-shell__body` (`app-sidebar-owner.tsx`). The lazy Pages/Users bodies now render only their lists.
- `app-sidebar-panel-headers.tsx` now owns one header shell (`SidebarPanelHeader`: drag region plus collapse toggle) and one filter button (`SidebarPanelFilter`). Sessions, Pages and Users all use them, so the headers can't drift apart again, and chat boot JS stays within the Control UI performance budget.
- Remove the auto-margin rules for the collapse toggle and their per-panel overrides. The title, or the filter button's existing `margin-left: auto`, now pushes the actions to the end of every header.

Builds on #191019 (shared `.sidebar-panel-header__title`).

## Evidence

- `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-users-filter.e2e.test.ts`: at 1280×320, the Users, Pages (scrolled to the bottom) and Sessions headers and their collapse buttons have identical bounding boxes. On `main` the test fails because the Pages header scrolls to `y: -102`. With this fix it passes.
- `ui/src/e2e/native-desktop-titlebar.e2e.test.ts` (web/macOS/Tauri header alignment): passes.

title: improve(ui): clarify chat permission picker copy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat composer's permission picker used internal language ("Execution permissions", "session root", "Guarded", "Workspace", "operator.admin") that doesn't tell people what the agent can actually do in their chat.

## User Impact

User impact: the permission picker now says in plain words what the agent can read, edit, and run in this chat, with one name per mode. Config values and behavior are unchanged; **Ask me** and **Auto-review** are display renames of `guarded` and `workspace`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies the copy Vyctor approved for the permission picker (sentence case, "chat" instead of "session", no internal jargon). Only English source copy changes; foreign locales pick it up through the normal locale refresh.

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trigger tooltip | Choose what available tools may do in this session. This does not change the tool profile. | Choose what the agent can read, edit, and run in this chat. |
| Menu heading / trigger aria prefix | Execution permissions | Permissions |
| Default row title | Default | Agent default |
| Default row description | The agent's configured permissions. | Uses this agent's settings. |
| `read-only` | Read Only · Agent tools can read within the session root, but cannot write or run commands. | Read only · Can read files in this chat's workspace. Can't edit files or run commands. |
| `guarded` | Guarded · A human reviews requests beyond the session root. | Ask me · Asks you before doing anything outside the workspace. |
| `workspace` | Workspace · An AI reviewer checks requests beyond the session root. | Auto-review · An AI reviewer approves actions outside the workspace. |
| `full` | Full Access · No reviewer; files and commands are unrestricted. | Full access · Edits files and runs commands anywhere, without review. |
| Full access locked | Full access requires operator.admin access. | Only admins can turn on Full access. |
| Update failed | Failed to update permissions: {error} | Couldn't change permissions: {error} |
| Saved, refresh failed | Permissions were saved, but refreshing the session failed: {error} | Permissions saved, but this chat didn't refresh. Reload to see the change. |

Notes:
- The **Default** badge on the agent's default mode row and the `Default ({mode})` format are unchanged. The default row's accessible name now matches its visible title: **Agent default (Ask me)** (new keys `agentDefault` / `agentDefaultWithMode`).
- The same mode labels appear on New Session's permission picker (same component), so it changes too.
- Aligned the one other UI string that named the mode: Agents → Tools help now says "Full access" instead of "Full Access".
- The refresh-failed message no longer includes the raw list-refresh error, per the approved copy; the call no longer passes it.
- Docs that quote the UI labels now use the new names (permission modes, tool policy, troubleshooting, sessions/sidebar, panels, dashboards). `docs/gateway/permission-modes.md` gains a "Control UI label" column mapping each config value to its new name.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI (control-ui-e2e harness, synthetic session, light theme), agent default mode `guarded`, before = current `main`:

title: improve(ui): name the effort and speed controls consistently
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The composer's effort and speed controls used several names for the same two settings ("Chat thinking level", "Thinking", "Effort"; "Fast mode", "Fast Mode", "Fast responses", "Speed"), and the tier/speed availability messages read like internal status ("Fast requested, currently served as default").

## User Impact

User impact: the reasoning-level setting is called **Effort** and the speed control is called **Speed** in the composer picker, the Models defaults card, and the Sessions table. The Effort control shows the effective level, the menu marks the default level with a **Default** badge, and screen readers hear "Effort: Default (High)" while a chat inherits the level. Speed availability messages are plain sentences. Config keys, slash commands (`/think`, `/fast`), and saved values are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vyctor approved one name per concept and the copy below. The trigger already showed only the effective level on `main`; this change keeps that and adds the same "Default (...)" accessible name and in-menu Default marker that #191018 uses for the permission picker, so the inherited value stays discoverable.

| `chat.modelControls.fastResponsesAria` | Fast responses: {state} | Speed: {state} |

title: improve(ui): clarify composer action copy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The composer's action copy (context ring, Compact, mic, send, Stop, and the Goal entry hint) used internal or wordy phrasing ("Open context usage details", "Replaces older context", "Tap to talk", "Hold to start dictation", "Write a message to send."), and the Stop button had two names ("Stop" visibly, "Stop generating" for screen readers).

## User Impact

User impact: the composer controls use short, plain chat language. The context ring tooltip now shows how full the context is at a glance, and Stop has a single name with its Esc shortcut in the tooltip.

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context ring tooltip | Open context usage details | Context: {pct}% used |
| Compact button tooltip | Replaces older context with a summary. | Summarizes older messages to free up space. |
| Compact tooltip during a reply | Available when the current run finishes. | Available after this reply finishes. |
| Mic tooltip | Tap to talk · Hold to start dictation | Tap for voice chat · Hold to dictate |
| Mic menu toggle | Hold to start dictation | Hold to dictate |
| Settings › Appearance toggle | Hold microphone button to start dictation | Hold the mic button to dictate |
| Composer Stop button (accessible name / tooltip) | Stop generating / Stop | Stop / Stop (Esc) |
| Send button with an empty draft | Write a message to send. | Type a message first. |
| Goal entry hint | Enter your objective. | Describe what “done” looks like. |

## Why This Change Was Made

Approved copy pass for the composer actions area (one PR per composer area). Only English source strings and two small display tweaks change:

- The context ring tooltip uses a new `contextUsage.percentUsed` string with the same percent the ring's accessible summary already computes (including the `~` for approximate counts); the unused `contextUsage.open` string is removed. When only plan usage is shown (no context percent), the tooltip falls back to the existing accessible summary. The ring is a native disclosure, so assistive tech still announces that it expands.
- The composer Stop button's accessible name is now `Stop` and its tooltip uses the existing `Stop (Esc)` string (Esc already stops the reply). `Cancel reply` is untouched because it cancels a reply-to quote, not the agent's reply.
- Tests that located the composer Stop button by "Stop generating" now use the exact name "Stop".

Known gaps: the subagent pane header/notice Stop buttons and the mobile header menu item still say "Stop generating"; they stop a child run from a different surface and were left for a separate decision. title: improve(ui): simplify model picker copy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The composer model picker used long, technical wording ("session", "compacted", "centrally configures", "Chat only") that does not match the rest of the composer, which talks about chats.

## User Impact

User impact: model picker hints, the switch confirmation, the no-tools badge, and the admin-restricted note are shorter and use plain language. Behavior, settings, and config values are unchanged.

| Key (`chat.modelControls.*`) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selectionScopeSession` | Selecting a model changes only this session. | Applies to this chat only. |
| `selectionScopeAgent` | Selecting a model updates this agent's default. | Changes the default for this agent. |
| `selectionScopeGlobal` | Selecting a model updates the global default. | Changes the default for all agents. |
| `switchWarning` | This conversation is cached for {current}. Switching models means it reprocesses the whole conversation on your next message, which can spend more tokens. Longer conversations may also be compacted. | Switching re-sends the whole conversation to {new} with your next message, which uses more tokens. Long conversations may be summarized. |
| `chatOnly` | Chat only | No tools |
| `chatOnlyHelp` | This model can chat, but it cannot use tools. Choose another model for files, commands, web, or media tasks. | This model can't read files, run commands, or browse. Pick another model for that. |
| `restrictedModelsHelp` | Your administrator centrally configures the models available here. | Your admin chooses which models are available. |

Unchanged on purpose: route labels and details (Claude CLI · native, API · OpenClaw, completion routes), `claudeCliNotReady`, decision-model strings, and the effort/speed strings (separate PR).

## Why This Change Was Made

English copy only, in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-model-controls.ts`. The new switch warning names the model you are switching to, so the confirm-dialog caller now passes `{new}` (the same label the dialog title already uses) instead of looking up the current model. Foreign locales are not edited. Translations whose source text changed are dropped by hash and fall back to English until the post-merge locale refresh, so no locale shows a raw `{new}` or `{current}` placeholder.

The selection-scope strings are aria-only: they are appended to the model trigger's accessible name, for example `Chat model: Demo model A. Applies to this chat only.`. There is no visible surface to screenshot for them.

title: fix(workers): allow cloud dispatch to finish after node enrollment
body:
Related: #188796, #159178, #135838.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cloud-worker dispatch failing immediately after a new node connects when the provider rechecks its live provisioning authority.

## User Impact

Providers can continue setup after their own authenticated node enrollment without mistaking that progress for a replacement owner. Changed operations, epochs, enrolled nodes, setup bindings, resource receipts, caller authority, cancellation, and destroy intent remain fenced. No configuration, SDK, schema, retention, or durability migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provisioning previously reused teardown’s exact-node comparison against a snapshot captured before enrollment. The existing lifecycle owner now distinguishes the still-live provisioning operation from an already-fixed teardown identity and retains the first admitted node binding. Teardown’s exact predicate is unchanged.

The broader open authority work in #159178/#135838 already identifies this distinction. This narrow prerequisite does not import or supersede its V1 SDK rollout or remaining acceptance gates.

## Evidence

- The real enrollment regression fails on base `d9627ecb437b2a0fdaa2215137b291dbbc806137` with the installed failure: `Worker provider operation failed: Worker environment owner changed during teardown`. Both cases reach actual bootstrap token verification/consumption and immutable pairing publication before calling the public provider callback.
- Final candidate `9693b20c7d320d3a0448655914299b181cb1f34a`: **85 tests passed across six owner/sibling files**, including cancellation, replay, confirmed cleanup, generic provisioning, and project preparation. Vitest 74.54 seconds; wrapper 76.59 seconds, including cold compiled-worker preparation. The changed file’s preceding behavior-equivalent standalone run passed 13 cases in 11.78 seconds / 13.45 seconds wrapper; hosted per-file CI cost is not yet available.
- Core production and Gateway consumer-test types, four-file scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, test-line/line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety/database-worker ratchets passed. No baseline exception; test allocation records the 141-line real-boundary regression growth.
- Independent canonical autoreview, P0–P3, final complete five-file scope plus owning contracts: **scoped-clean**, exit 0, no findings, one complete 652,201-byte prompt. An earlier incomplete-context result is retained, not called clean. Unchanged credential-broker source was policy-blocked; complete callers established it is not needed for this provision-attempt assertion, distinct from unchanged completion admission.
- Production delta: +38/−5 across three files; no new persistent owner or public API.
- Published head `2787ffb77a8da26749bb9547880d4f7bdc061e93` preserves the exact qualified tree `cf979f696da04da7e6955b3c5012c96a1a989ad2`; the publisher added only an empty attribution commit atop the signed candidate. [Exact-head CI run 41420259186, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41420259186) **passed**, including the Actions CI gate and `security-fast`.

### Repaired installed acceptance and cleanup

[Package Acceptance 41422166087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41422166087), attempt 1, passed for the published head above. [Installed acceptance run 41430331976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41430331976), local attempt 7, returned controller/native/outer **exit 0 and PASS**. Its Actions workflow later shows cancelled because the retained Testbox was stopped after evidence collection; that is separate from the successful product proof.

- The exact repaired package was installed to an independent prefix. Installed CLI/SDK, managed Gateway process, serving build and pinned TLS matched; the image's preinstalled app was not the system under test.
- Four invalid capability profiles refused before provider allocation or agent turns. Authenticated first node enrollment then reached an active disk-authoritative worker placement.
- A real write-tool invocation produced **48 bytes** on the original worker resource (SHA-256 `00c83c1895290341ecfdd614ecf65f919529915b3f6038c827e019d087102056`). Durable transcript ACK reached **4** and terminal ACK **5**; claim, pending result and journal cleared. Repository/checkpoint and compute expiry stayed unchanged, demonstrating no published Gateway backup—not packet-level absence of transport.
- Public exact-source **Move** returned placement from generation **5 to 8**, exported workspace custody to Gateway and cleared disk authority. Original worker container and volume were absent afterward.
- Gateway and inference processes joined. Outer container, runtime volume and network were absent; remaining native container/volume inventories were empty. **125 evidence files / 444,361 bytes** were retained and rehashed after cleanup.
- Initial normal stop exited **5** at the GitHub-settlement deadline and retained its claim/key. Independent inspection then confirmed complete remote settlement; the same supported owner finalized with **exit 0**. Fresh inspection confirmed completed/not-ready/no-host, complete remote settlement and generated-key-directory absence. Cleanup is complete.

### Final-effect authority qualification

The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191006#issuecomment-6574148884) reported **no discrete patch defect**, but requested installed success and replacement-node/caller-revocation evidence before provider I/O. Both named observations are now qualified for this narrow repair.

A test-only overlay on the exact published production source ran the real bootstrap verification, token consumption and immutable pairing publication, then called the public authority callback immediately before an actual local filesystem write. The current enrolled owner wrote/read successfully; controlled replacement-node and revoked-caller observations both rejected **before the write**, with forbidden files absent; restored current authority wrote/read successfully. The service reached ready, closed its retained guard and completed teardown. **One selected test passed; 12 were skipped**, not counted as passes. The original run completed in 589.70 seconds (Vitest 567.78 seconds, selected case 1,045 ms), under its original 600-second bound, without replay. Production and installed-fixture bytes stayed unchanged.

The installed synthetic provider composes config-owner and core `assertCurrent` checks. Its Docker dispatch checks immediately before process spawn with no intervening await, then checks again after awaited completion. This connects the qualified callback rejection to that provider's final dispatch boundary; no production defect was identified.

**Limits:** replacement is a controlled live-owner read observation, not an actually paired replacement device. Negative effect proof uses real local filesystem I/O in a substituted provider, not a negative Docker/cloud run or a guarantee for providers that ignore the callback. Installed success uses a synthetic local provider and deterministic HTTP inference (two requests), not live cloud providers or paid-model correctness. Neither proof qualifies pause/resume/restart/cold boot, release/adoption or deployment. The earlier installed `8085604` failure and its missing callback-tuple/archive-size evidence remain historical failures; no old native payload was replayed. Broader SDK rollout requirements remain with their owning work.

title: fix: request sound for Control UI Web Push on macOS
body:
Supersedes #163601, thanks @xydigitLybnnnn.
Related: #163544.

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Web Push banners can arrive silently in Safari on macOS even when the user has enabled notification sounds.

## User Impact

Attention notifications request sound, subject to the user's browser and macOS settings. Same-tag approval replacements retain `renotify: false` to avoid another alert.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service worker already calls `showNotification` with a title and body, but omits `silent`. [Apple's WWDC23 Safari guidance](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10120/?time=884) documents that macOS defaults notification sound off and requires explicit `silent: false` to request sound; user notification settings remain authoritative. [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ServiceWorkerRegistration/showNotification#silent) documents the device-default behavior when omitted and the separate `renotify` option for replacements.

Set that standard option at the existing presentation boundary. Inline the one-use title binding without changing its fallback, keeping production LOC flat. Extend the existing approval replacement regression instead of adding duplicate setup; test LOC also stays flat.

## Evidence

- Current main's worker at `6cdd495d50338f3e456dffd88f03e849e33b4a96` still omits `silent`; its bytes match the tested baseline `b2bf8e641ba4c1854cf7fc85729421be2b01d0da`.
- Crabbox / Blacksmith Testbox: `pnpm --dir ui test src/app/service-worker-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Red before: 1 failed / 31 passed, specifically because the worker's `showNotification` options lack `silent: false`. Green after: 32 passed; file duration 0.844s, including existing navigation, avatar, and quiet replacement coverage. [Remote run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41413998489).
- Touched-file `oxfmt --check` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig ui/tsconfig.json ui/public/sw.js ui/src/app/service-worker-lifecycle.test.ts` pass; `git diff --check` passes. [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41414730516) on `5694606ed52293cfd6713f9505248cca480ae417`; workflow elapsed time was 8m14s (whole run). The aggregate required gate also passed.
- Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against `b2bf8e641ba4c1854cf7fc85729421be2b01d0da`: scoped clean at P0–P2, no actionable findings. Simplification reviewed; production delta 0, test delta 0.

Proof limit: the regression executes the production service worker's push handler and checks the options passed to the browser API. It does not prove audible playback on macOS, sound-disabled settings, or Chromium behavior. The Safari repair is based on Apple's documented platform contract. The contributor's branch was read with `gh` only and was never checked out or run.

title: refactor: share channel binding session classification
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord, Telegram and Matrix duplicate ordinary-session versus ACP classification. Landing CI also exposed a pre-existing Matrix restart failure: a queued turn could invoke callbacks after its plugin consumer was released.

## User Impact

Preserve ordinary-session binding lifecycle, canonical ACP/subagent fast paths, main/global metadata aliases and approved opaque plugin targets without arbitrary agent ownership. Unreadable storage and revoked authority still refuse. Queued inbound turns now retain plugin custody through observation/delivery and settlement, rather than producing a closed-consumer failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

One SDK-private classifier behind the existing thread-bindings-session-runtime facade serves all three adapters. The old core implementation/test are removed. Storage stays lazy via the narrow existing reader; managers retain effect authority. Public-operation fixture seams delegate to real classification; private reader policy tests remain SDK-owned. No new public subpath, API/test hook, registry, manager, store, schema, config, dependency or permission policy.

Same-target/public-kind refresh ownership persists without inheritance across child placement, replacement targets or kind changes. Native/action hints are not replayed from stored metadata.

Current head cbf3d3b2beb6fe6015b0c3dda1a4910c6c34c18a adds the owning runtime fix to the reviewed classifier baseline e986cb34d2d09483a78529109db84630221ed993. Matrix supplies a top-level adoption lifecycle; core selected it instead of the custody-bound resolved-turn lifecycle. Deferral therefore never retained custody. The repair binds custody at that actual selection point while preserving prepared-turn identity and the closed-consumer guard.

## Evidence

### Queued-ingress lifecycle repair

The deterministic owner negative control is causal proof; a passing replay alone is not called a fix.

title: fix(auth): resolve Cloudflare email-code user profiles
body:
Supersedes #162507, thanks @ujjalcal.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes authenticated-profile errors when a user signs in through Cloudflare Access with an email one-time PIN.

## User Impact

Email-code users can connect with their existing email profile and role, or receive a separate default-role profile for a new email. Cloudflare Access policies, trusted-proxy admission, and OpenClaw role and access-policy checks remain in force. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize the explicit `onetimepin` provider only after the existing successful Access identity lookup and matching-email check, then reuse the canonical email-profile owner. Missing or unknown providers still fail closed; OTP subject IDs never become GitHub identity or credit. JWT signature and application-policy enforcement remain delegated to Access and the trusted ingress, as in the current deployment contract; this change neither bypasses nor adds local JWT verification.

The production delta is +4 lines. The simplification pass found no dead or duplicate code to remove safely; a provider case and its discriminated result reuse the existing profile path without another owner. Regression growth is +68 test lines, allocated in `cloudflare-email-otp.txt` for real HTTP/WebSocket profile admission, protected dispatch, role revocation, and rejection proof. Existing authority-test setup is shared between Tailscale and OTP.

Reimplemented from current main without checking out or executing the contributor branch. Contributor credit: Ujjal Bhattacharjee <ujjal.b@gmail.com>.

## Evidence

- Red on main `6deb24aa46547acdcee93fcf0aaa8d381383d1c2`: the two OTP admission cases failed at `Cloudflare Access identity provider is unsupported`; the other 32 cases passed. Changed-file baseline wall time: 48.56s, including uncached worker compilation.
- Green after: 116 tests passed across `github-user-identity.oidc.test.ts`, `github-user-identity.test.ts`, `github-user-identity.authority.test.ts`, and `auth.test.ts`; Vitest 103.71s, test wrapper 109.56s. Coverage includes existing-profile reuse through HTTP/WebSocket admission, new-email separation/default role, no GitHub credit, mismatched OTP email, Access rejection despite a matching header, malformed assertions/issuers, and current authority checks.
- Tests ran on Crabbox's configured Blacksmith Testbox (`tbx_01m6dhrj642gnk00fkhkbbn9m1`), [allocation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41405037483). No worker compilation, dependency installation, broad tests, containers, or Gateway changes ran on the production Team host.

- Protected-operation proof added after hosted review: trusted-proxy admission → Access OTP identity → canonical profile → real privileged dispatcher. The owner executes the handler; the same connected profile after role revocation and a different-email default-role profile are denied with no additional handler effect. The owner role is restored before checking the other email, so that negative control cannot pass merely because the owner was revoked.

title: fix(ui): avoid typing stalls in software-rendered chat panes
body:
Supersedes #162418, thanks @DragonLi-Mi.

Related: #162324

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes typing stalls in large Control UI chat panes when Chromium uses software compositing.

## User Impact

Large software-rendered panes avoid the expensive outer superellipse clip. The pane keeps its radius, dimensions, overflow clipping, and layout; its corners become ordinary rounded corners on all platforms, including hardware-rendered browsers. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main (`6deb24aa46547acdcee93fcf0aaa8d381383d1c2`) still applies `corner-shape: superellipse(1.5)` to `.chat.chat` while `.chat` clips overflow. The actual chat view renders this class around the conversation and composer. The contributor's reversible real-page trace identifies this outer clip as the source of repeated pane-sized software repaints, rather than input-handler work. Switch only that declaration to `round`.

The existing curvature test now covers the outer pane in both supported and unsupported browsers, alongside all its existing surface checks. Production LOC is unchanged; the two-line test allocation covers the added table entry and fixture. Simplification retained just the one-line production fix, with its explanation here.

## Evidence

- **Red/green on current main:** Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m6dhrha6ed7mhjb7fqtv77a9`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41405036217). The extended `ui/src/styles/corner-shape.browser.test.ts` fails against unchanged main specifically because `.chat` computes `superellipse(1.5)` instead of circular corners: 1 failed, 2 passed, 2.56 seconds. With the one-line CSS repair: 3 passed, 1.53 seconds. The scaled 17.5px radius and unsupported-browser 14px radius remain intact, and other surfaces retain their curvature.
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/styles/corner-shape.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Touched-file oxfmt, CSS stylelint, test-file oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed. All browser execution and dependencies were isolated on Testbox; no browser, build, or suite ran on the production Team host.
- **Independent autoreview:** local snapshot against the main commit above, P0–P2, Codex; `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Its frozen bundle covered the full change; unchanged test-helper implementation was outside its supplied context. The implementing review separately inspected that helper and the complete existing curvature test.
- The [contributor's real Gateway-served Control UI A/B/A](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162418#issuecomment-5925891664) reports 40 inputs per condition at a 3321×1962 pane: keypress median **200.617 → 7.935 → 205.148 ms**, with the same declaration applied and reverted. This is their software-renderer evidence on 2026.9.7, not a newly measured current-main or physical-GPU benchmark. The computed-style regression verifies current main and the replacement; it does not measure repaint latency. Hardware-specific visual timing was not newly measured; geometry and all existing curvature cases pass. PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Contributor source was read only through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; its branch was never checked out or executed. This replacement was implemented on main.

Inspected, sanitized contributor screenshots below show the exact declaration change on the real page; both attachments decode at 3579×2010. They are reused evidence from the original PR, not new captures of this branch.

**Before: outer superellipse clip**

![Before: contributor's real Control UI with superellipse clip, private content redacted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca93ff2c-d24b-4524-8ca4-df2d74801f3d)

**After: ordinary rounded clip**

![After: contributor's same Control UI with round clip, private content redacted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84a11785-c2db-4889-8622-8623b4685c5a)

### Inherited CI failure

[PR CI run 41405480881](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41405480881) fails `checks-node-changed-boundary` on `test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts` → “keeps plugin-owned behavior suites under the bundled plugin tree”: `test/decision-baseten-admission.integration.test.ts` imports `../extensions/baseten/decision-provider.runtime.js` outside the plugin tree.

This exact assertion also fails on main `6deb24aa46547acdcee93fcf0aaa8d381383d1c2` in an independent [Crabbox replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41406115771), lease `tbx_01m6djamahj39dgb2hsvt13t09`: 1 failed / 10 passed, 61.88 seconds including 43 seconds of uncached worker compilation. The failed test is byte-identical in PR CI's tested merge `ba5931209641caabdafdb10ca4ca5c6561241652` and its main parent `da41e7de25800605ab5750ff52276549d2f2cbd4`. This PR changes neither source. The inherited-failure route retains the red result; no unrelated test is weakened or rerun for green.

All selected PR CI jobs have now completed: UI, UI E2E, performance, security, lint/type, architecture and ratchet jobs passed.
