title: fix(gateway): warn when restart intent cleanup fails
body:
Supersedes #160805, thanks @changeroa.
Related: #153483

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes silent restart-intent cleanup failures when the Gateway state database refuses the deletion.

## User Impact

Operators see a `restart` warning with the storage error explaining why an intent remains. Cleanup stays best-effort so a persistence failure does not interrupt startup or service recovery.

Use the same logger and error context as the existing restart-intent write failure. **Remote proof:** provider `blacksmith-testbox`, lease `tbx_01m6dere8sgamnxzkwgv7mbeen`, [Actions run 41399476426](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41399476426). title: feat(beam): allow owned publication by restricted guests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted Visitors can work in their own sessions but cannot send Beam snapshots without being granted the much broader `operator.write` permission.

## User Impact

A verified, currently invited guest can publish a Beam and refresh only the retained row they initially published. Publication does not grant catalog read, delete, or continuation access. Staff behavior remains unchanged. Guest success receipts retain version-1 compatibility and additionally return optional `canView: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- One plugin-owned upload operation now serves staff and guests inside the existing shared-state worker. It replaces the host observe/CAS retry loop; there is no new SQL schema/version, SDK surface, configuration, shared token, or broad operator grant.
- The immutable initial publisher profile is separate from mutable uploader attribution. Legacy live ownerless rows are not claimable, even when their uploader matches.
- Ownership and creation quotas are checked atomically: 20 unexpired rows per publisher for guest creation; no guest creation at the shared 500-row cap and no guest eviction. Owned refresh remains allowed at either cap; staff oldest-entry eviction remains unchanged.
- The original profile/Visitor authority is captured before awaits and retained through worker transaction and commit admission. Accepted-write settlement stays with the state owner: an authorized commit is not undone or replayed after later closure/revocation. A later HTTP response retains its own live-authority check.

Vincent K, verified as an active OpenClaw organization administrator, accepted this scoped ownership/permission/bounded-quota design in the maintainer task discussion on November 2, 2026. The complete initial patch and existing SDK admission/TTL contract were inspected during the task before initial draft publication; the PR was subsequently marked ready so exact-head CI could run. Both exact patches were inspected during the task. The separately reviewed six-file CI repair and subsequent proven type-only lint repair were accepted for publication. This is not a merge-green claim. Welcome/localization, Beam welcome guidance, and notification groups remain HELD and untouched.

No backfill is performed. Rollback to an older receiver restores staff-only uploads; an accepted replacement by that older receiver may strip the ownership field. After re-upgrade, the resulting ownerless row remains unavailable for guest refresh until deletion/expiry permits creation. Namespace, seven-day retention, timestamp/completion ordering, and staff retention are unchanged. These limits are documented in the Beam guide.

## Evidence

- Actual isolated Gateway HTTP with durable synthetic profiles, restricted roles, real VisitorAccessService, and the real state worker: original guest upload `403`; candidate `200` with `canView: false`. Unauthenticated, read-only, uninvited, foreign, legacy-ownerless, and forged-owner requests refused.
- Actual HTTP races: 21 concurrent same-publisher creations produced 20 successes and one quota refusal; competing same-ID publishers produced one success and one forbidden response; racing the last shared slot produced one success and one cap refusal. Guest refusal did not evict; owned refresh and staff oldest-entry eviction worked at capacity.
- Actual revoke/reinvite and expiry during awaited upload produced no successful acknowledgment and no persisted row under the original capture. A fresh invitation could publish. Aborted local transports surfaced as egress-proxy 502, so this is safety evidence, not qualification of a stable denial status.
- SDK operation suite: **17/17 passed**, including transaction/commit authority rollback, accepted settlement after closure, and lost-ack non-replay.
- Initial targeted Beam production and test-consumer typechecks passed together (29.3 seconds). Formatting and patch whitespace checks passed.
- Two independent initial P0–P2 reviews found no actionable findings. A fresh independent P0–P2 review of the six-file CI repair also found no actionable findings. Both exact patches were inspected during the task.

### CI-discovered consumer repair

Initial non-draft CI run [41399614386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41399614386) exposed three actual failures, not environmental verdicts: extension lint, the real HTTP identity consumer bypassing plugin operation-module capture, and the new guest store suite missing the real host-broker test project. The follow-up uses the operation-aware plugin loader, awaits resource cleanup, routes the guest suite through the existing database-worker project, fixes the reported lint diagnostics, and adds read-only HTTP denials with unchanged persisted transcript assertions.

- The original HTTP identity entry point reproduced red locally with the same Internal-error response as CI.
- The same repaired HTTP consumer plus guest-worker and HTTP-authority suites passed **7/7**, cold wall **78.4 seconds** (worker preparation 39.956 seconds). The consumer proves real HTTP profile isolation, read-only `403` without transcript replacement, close/reopen persistence, and staff/shared-token behavior.
- Completed CI run [41408391127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41408391127), on head `a3ffdd5623215e841fb016d10f2c4a7dccbf1958`, passed all Node test and production/test typecheck jobs. It retained one PR-caused extension lint error: the fixture's generic entries method lacked the SDK return contract. The method now explicitly returns SDK-owned `PluginStateEntry<T>[]`, matching `PluginStateOperationTransaction.entries`, with no executable behavior change or new casts/suppressions.
- In an independently qualified native PR checkout, the unchanged prior head reproduced that exact lint error. Applying the exact accepted two-file patch made `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/beam/src/beam-store.test-support.ts && git diff --check` pass, exit 0: `[plugin-sdk boundary dts] fresh; skipping` and `No problems in 1 file [3.61s]`. That temporary proof patch was then reversed, leaving the native checkout clean. This is scoped lint proof, not a full local build verdict.
- The same completed CI run also failed the global extension-test boundary because `test/decision-baseten-admission.integration.test.ts` imports a Baseten runtime file. The parent investigation compared the actual CI merge checkout with its ordered main parent and found both that Baseten file and the boundary guard unchanged; this is separately attributed inherited evidence, not a reason to ignore PR-caused lint.
- Net regression growth is now **142 lines**, with an exact named allocation. Source updates address observed defects; no check was dispatched/rerun or branch re-pushed merely to obtain green.

### Completed prior-head CI and recovery guidance

- CI run [41410742762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41410742762) completed **SUCCESS** for head `d6e65048363771b8fbe4d7eb5b44cba5a04ade42`. The fresh ClawSweeper review of that head judged overall correctness correct, proof sufficient, and security findings **None**. Its only finding was P3 recovery guidance for an ownership refusal.
- That P3 is addressed by explaining the existing options in the `403` response: publish a new source session with a new Beam ID, or ask a Gateway operator whether the retained snapshot can be removed. The guest HTTP regression checks the foreign-publisher refusal and the new Beam ID guidance. It failed red with the old copy in **37ms**, then passed with the new copy in **24ms**. Canonical formatting, the two-file lint check (**3.93s**), and patch whitespace checks passed in the qualified checkout.
- The subsequent three-file patch changes only that human-facing refusal text, its regression, and the allocation. Authority, status, storage, quotas, ordering, and TTL are unchanged. Earlier HTTP and released-state compatibility evidence covers those unchanged boundaries through D6; it is not a claim that every production byte is identical on the subsequent head.
- New-head CI run [41414124249](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41414124249) is pending for `3415e3af6c0453098a54d8e6f27ba276e9cbf5a1`, not yet green.

### Investigated local oversized-request timeout

The original declared-oversized request socket-close case timed out at **120 seconds**; that failure evidence is retained, not replaced by a passing retry. The qualified checkout reproduced it in the complete, identically ordered 15-test Beam receiver file with the accepted three-file candidate: **14 passed, 1 failed, 130.43s wall**. The observed environment had Node 26 `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, HTTP/HTTPS proxies present, and neither `NO_PROXY` nor `no_proxy` included loopback.

The controlled comparison changed **only the test invocation environment**: preserve every existing bypass value and append `127.0.0.1,localhost` to both `NO_PROXY` and `no_proxy`. With **identical source and full test order**, all **15/15 passed**, **10.46s warm wrapper wall**, **8.75s Vitest**, and the oversized body-close case took **8ms**. This includes ordinary staff HTTP and the complete Beam receiver flows. It qualifies the fixture's loopback transport; there is no product body-close fix, global proxy disabling, timeout increase, skipped/weakened assertion, or claim that repetition fixed the original failure. CI per-file execution cost is unavailable.

### Historical sanitized real HTTP and persisted-state excerpt

This is the retained prior capture from the isolated synthetic Gateway/Visitor/worker harness after the test-only repair, before the subsequent human-facing ownership-refusal text change. The old refusal text below is historical, not the current full response. No real conversations, provider credentials, external Cloudflare login, private addresses, or live Gateway configuration were used. Each STATE line is a fresh real keyed-store lookup at that checkpoint. The revoked-request lookup is **before** the fresh invitation publishes that ID.

~~~text
HTTP unauthenticated 401
HTTP reader 403
HTTP uninvited 403
HTTP guest-A 200 {"canView":false,"ok":true,"beamId":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
STATE guest-accepted {"beamId":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","publisher":"guest-A","uploader":"guest-A","completed":false,"fixtureTextPreserved":true}
HTTP guest-B 403 {"ok":false,"error":"Beam is not owned by this publisher"}
STATE after-foreign-denial {"beamId":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","publisher":"guest-A","uploader":"guest-A","completed":false,"fixtureTextPreserved":true}
HTTP guest-A 502 [local transport after revoked authority]
STATE captured-revoked-request-not-persisted null
HTTP guest-A 200 [fresh invitation, new authority]
HTTP guest-A 502 [local transport after expired authority]
STATE expired-request-not-persisted null
PASS catalog method authority gates, staff read/copy, revocation+reinvite and expiry while upload awaited
PASS real Gateway HTTP trusted-proxy auth + durable profiles + current Visitor policy + worker upload
~~~

Actor names are synthetic labels; successful receipt URLs and repetitive fields were omitted. The 502 observations establish neither a stable denial status nor successful delivery; the independent persisted-state lookups establish no unauthorized write.

### Remaining gates — explicitly not green

- **Newest exact-head CI remains required.** Prior-head D6 CI passed; current `3415e3a` CI is pending as recorded above. The scoped lint commands passed in the qualified checkout. The source checkout's old artifact lock remains preserved; other local checks stopped by that fence are not retroactively qualified. Earlier default Bun-backed lint had timed out without a diagnostic verdict.
- Full `pnpm build` was stopped after reaching tsdown-packages; full local build evidence is incomplete.
- **Released-state component compatibility passed; full Gateway update remains unqualified.** Published stable `2026.10.9 (8b18b55)` actually produced retained disk state. Candidate `67fe909` (production bytes unchanged by the test-only repairs through `d6e6504`; the subsequent patch changes only human-facing ownership-refusal text) consumed that same disk through the real async plugin loader, host broker/worker, and HTTP handler after canonical Doctor maintenance migrated schema **20→39** with full and scoped backups. Synthetic transport authority was used; no publisher was seeded. Staff catalog/transcript read, guest `POST /api/v1/beam/sessions` **403** even matching the legacy uploader, fresh unchanged row JSON+metadata, preserved settings, and independent-process cold read passed; the original backup inventory stayed intact. This does not qualify full Doctor health or live Visitor authentication.
  - In the owned isolated environment, the command prefix was `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts`. Case `extensions/beam/src/released-state.doctor.test.ts` passed **1/1, exit 0**. Case `extensions/beam/src/released-state.compat.test.ts` passed **1/1, exit 0** separately with `BEAM_PROOF_STAGE=candidate-postmigration` and `BEAM_PROOF_STAGE=postmigration-cold-read`.
  - Actual sanitized stdout from the migration case:

    CANONICAL_DOCTOR_RECEIPT {"previousSchema":20,"newSchema":39,"backups":2,"rowUnchanged":true,"settingsSemanticsPreserved":true,"configBytesChanged":false}

- Personal external Cloudflare login and full RPC/UI continuation remain unqualified. Guest expired-row recreation/quota expiry remains a named boundary: the host fake clock tests authority expiry, not transactional worker TTL. No unsupported clock seam, new timers or fixtures were added.
- Local proof used synthetic data only. A clean CI install remains necessary for broad qualification; the local dependency copy differs only in unrelated tokenjuice/optional metadata, and no dependency files changed.

The PR is ready for CI, **not claimed merge-green on the newest head**. No deployment or live credential/configuration change was performed. The parent maintainer owns native workflow and landing; this child does not merge.

title: fix(ui): make workspace repositories easier to find
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Saved repositories are difficult to distinguish and find in the workspace picker, particularly when several repositories share a short name and for session-only connections.

## User Impact

Users can search organization/repository identities of projects they can already discover. Lists with six or more saved/recent entries expose search automatically; the header stays available while the inventory scrolls. Selection shows repository identity in the workspace chip.

This is read-safe display metadata only: no additional discovery, private-content, cloning, remote-search, publication or other permissions. Origin URLs, credentials, checkout paths and observed placement stay outside session-only responses.

## Implementation

The Gateway projects optional `repositoryIdentity` from the raw stored origin through the canonical configured-host Git URL parser. The UI consumes that authoritative projection instead of parsing unavailable origins. Unsupported origins retain display names. UI and Gateway ship together; no older-Gateway fallback is added.

Automatic search returns after passive empty dismissal, respecting explicit collapse. Only the picker opts into row typing to an already-visible search; shared selects retain list typeahead. The existing composer autotype exemption prevents capture stealing row typing. Existing layout CSS keeps search outside the scrolling inventory; superseded sticky CSS is removed without a budget increase. The identity regression uses the canonical RPC invocation helper, not an incomplete cast.

## Reviewed Source and Verification

Reviewed head: `d96b69052ac265fc2a1a980a81a68eab30ecf1ce`. The full initial source and exact six-file follow-up received source inspection and fresh independent bounded review, with no actionable findings.

- Prior-head CI genuinely ran project-list tests: **30 Node + 30 Bun**, including read-safe identity, write-only checkout details and origin redaction; focused identity also passed both. This is handler proof for unchanged Gateway production inputs, not a new router-admission/revocation claim.
- Full `pnpm build` at this head passed in **5m07s** (build owner 5m02.8s).
- Canonical `ui:check-performance:base 7ce05f41e0a69f01503788eb1dbc2b1476e638fa` passed in **56.638s**: CSS raw/gzip zero growth, chat-boot gzip +462B and New Session +410B below fixed ceilings, startup -4B and request counts unchanged. That owner controls build identity/release flags; its outputs differ from the standard build.
- **Standard absolute-budget probe did not pass:** CSS gzip 309591 > 309366, CSS raw 1601636 > 1599319, chat-boot gzip 1278560 > 1277887. Absolute compliance is not claimed; the canonical relative gate and actual CI passed. No cap/baseline increase, timeout increase, skip or assertion weakening was used.

The follow-up repairs source-attributed shared-select typeahead, invalid invocation fixture and incremental CSS growth; current-head CI/build/relative performance evidence is separate from the failures below.

Two old E2E causes remain **unresolved**: moved-authority URL waiting in `chat-snapshot-route.e2e.test.ts` and one WebKit390 upward-reading residual of 1,238px. Neither is labeled infrastructure, proven pre-existing or fixed. The pane's `--visible` class is valid; main's later canonical-path/active-pane fixture alignment is not established as this timeout's repair.

title: fix(auth): ignore invalid credential symlink targets
body:
Supersedes #151739, thanks @Alix-007.

## What Problem This Solves

External JSON credential discovery aborts when a credential symlink points beneath a regular file.

## User Impact

Invalid legacy credential targets are skipped so discovery can continue, and readable credentials keep their existing selection behavior. Other path-resolution errors still propagate. No operator action or configuration change is needed.

title: fix: await native credential migration observations
body:
Doctor's native credential imports and identity repair synchronously inspect database generations around native writes. These reads can block signal handling even though the caller is asynchronous.

Await those observations outside transactions while retaining the existing native custody. One generator supplies the native transaction/admission policy to the synchronous SDK driver and the awaited Doctor adapter. Device auth and identity import/repair consume that adapter. title: fix: await Doctor process and restart lease inspection
body:
Related: #178359, #187900.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor and service inspection can block cancellation while synchronously preparing Gateway process and restart lease observations. Awaited maintenance inspection also needs to follow a legitimately replaced state file rather than a retained admission's old inode.

## User Impact

Process and restart observations await the existing read owner and cleanup. Offline maintenance can inspect the current physical state file after restoration or a database port. Native process signals, service actions and restart-intent writes still require current caller authority and captured process identity. This is the second split stage of the Doctor repair. Not yet released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the canonical awaited snapshot/read transport for Promise-only lease inspection. Descriptive reads use the existing independent warm-source path when the retained writer's physical identity still matches, preserving native-transaction refusal and original-source fallback for replaced paths. Maintenance snapshot admission captures the current physical file under acquired custody while retaining caller admission, cancellation and custody checks after awaits.

Await direct service callers, preserve synchronous native-supervisor callbacks, and share the stale-process cleanup policy between async and native drivers. Restart-intent writes inspect their admitted transaction. Preserve main's live-Gateway copy exclusion.

The 37-file diff contains process/restart inspection, direct callers/tests and allocation records. Inherited backup implementation, auxiliary snapshot, schema, CI prerequisite and temporary diagnostic changes are removed. Previous stage #190870 is landed; #190873–#190875 remain separate. title: fix: explain state lease renewal failures before expiry
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace operations can lose a state lease without showing whether renewal failed or remained pending.

## User Impact

Operators can identify a rejected renewal, an unsettled renewal, or no renewal since the last successful commit. Lease durations, retries, authority checks, and write settlement are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing parent timer records renewal attempts, warns once for the first non-loss failure, and reports the accumulated count at close or expiry. Expiry warnings and the loss cause include the pending start time, the last failed attempt's error classification, or the age of the last successful commit. Logs contain scope/key and bounded error names/codes, including broker codes alongside native SQLite cause codes; error prose, stacks, and database paths are omitted.

The simplification pass consolidated repeated timer cleanup and kept the existing owner. Production grows by 44 net lines. The existing lifetime fixture gains 79 lines for five table cases, including the required mock-isolation explanation. These parent-timer outcomes previously had no coverage; one shared fixture and a separate 79-line allocation keep the regression growth contained without changing the shared scalar.

Complete log and test-only patch are retained in the reliability loop's R17 proof directory. Wall time: 32.77 seconds, 35.68 seconds through the wrapper.

title: fix(sessions): replay creation requests across Gateway restarts
body:
## Problem

Process-local `sessions.create` idempotency loses the original binding when the Gateway restarts. Retrying can create another session and repeat preparation or its initial turn.

## Change

Atomically persist the existing optional idempotency key's namespaced fingerprint and original key/session ID/lifecycle revision with the session row. The existing passive history reader resolves receipts before label/resource preparation. Current requester, sharing, scopes and lifecycle authority still gate replay; stored authorization only restricts replay and never restores authority. Deleted/reset incarnations are refused, including same-ID resets. Renaming the original does not break replay when another session takes its former label.

The five-minute retry window remains. Replay does not allocate a worker, prepare a workspace or resend the initial message. Restart replay returns `creationReplayed: true` and `runStarted: false`: no new turn started, not a claim about completion of the original work. Inspect the original session for recovery. Incognito stays memory-only. No default-agent, SQLite-only, caller-generated-ID or purpose restriction is added.

Agent schema 39→40 uses the existing SQLite/PostgreSQL migration, backup, witness and historical-port owners. The PostgreSQL schema-40 migration also adopts two deletion indexes expressly deferred by its generator; predecessor sealed catalogs retain their exact original contracts. State schema 39 and resource/disk authority contracts are unchanged. No payload backfill or fork retention columns. Rollback requires the pre-upgrade backup and matching binary.

## Current candidate evidence

Head: ea0c33beeb895a6a566e5a981a4ddf8e27b0c990. Base: 4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914. Independent of attended permissions and offline ports.

The following complete-feature results were executed on repair head `ad51a9143047d2ca47dd9b51a491f0befde1c7c6`; unchanged runtime, migration and generated-artifact inputs are reused. The new three-file generator follow-up is qualified separately below.

- **41 focused native cases passed:** public replay/label reuse/reset refusal, requester revocation and membership removal after live authorization, cancellation's structured FORBIDDEN response, protocol, migrations and passive import boundaries. The revocation cases first prove an authorized replay and then assert refusal without metadata disclosure.
- **Real PostgreSQL 17.11:** native worker receipt close/reopen and competing-row rollback pass in the normal host-broker lane. SQLite migration commit/rollback and historical restoration pass. Frozen SQLite schema-27/28 SQL and PostgreSQL schema-35 digest tests pass without changing their expectations.
- Provisioning consumers: **15 passed, 3 unchanged environment-gated skips**. Wrapper inventory, extracted package aliases and retained Darwin dependency inputs: 3 passed through the supported isolated Node runner; container absence confirmed. Missing module registrations, passive-reader dependencies and broker test placement are repaired at their owners.
- Targeted tooling/Gateway/infra types, type-aware lint, formatting, canonical generated-schema verification, Kysely structural guard, line cap, whitespace and exact 631-line test allocation passed. Commit bytes match the qualified source.
- Fresh independent local review of the complete candidate against the base: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**. Static review, not independent execution of the reported tests.

Actual authorization proof excerpts:

```text
PASS durable replay requester revoked after live authorization: no session metadata disclosed
PASS durable replay membership revoked after live authorization: no session metadata disclosed
```

## Process and upgrade evidence

Earlier actual two-process Gateway proof uses a non-default agent, the real agent runtime and deterministic local Responses I/O: persisted first turn, changed PID on restart, original identity after label reuse, no duplicate model call, successful subsequent turn, and reset refusal. It predates final mechanical relocations and these integration repairs; the current owner-boundary proofs cover the changed contracts. This is not live-provider inference.

Actual runner result: one process-restart test passed in 31992ms; wrapper 126.16s.

Latest-stable source compatibility: v2026.10.9/8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41 produced a schema 25 image through its released schema owner. The candidate's real maintenance/migration path upgraded it to 40, preserved all 3 pending states/message JSON, original session-entry bytes, cache and settings, and read a newly written receipt after close/reopen. The producer image hash stayed unchanged. Test 12.600s; wrapper 348.56s, dominated by cold transform/I/O.

That fixture used synthetic data validated by the released entry/configuration readers. It proves source-owner migration compatibility—not package install-over or a released-UI transcript. No package release-age policy was bypassed.

## Integration qualification

Native three-way composition was clean with port head `5d4dc9755af68e99a916ca2e8524df139c919919` and attended-permission head `de78e430a40cdd82c575633eb75b383bca892a68`. Twenty selected cases qualified the combined public permission/replay boundaries, schema 39/40 descriptors, first-use completion, recovery-envelope retirement and real PostgreSQL receipt writer. A native private-copy port also preserved the creation receipt and original session identity. No functional dependency requires stacking these PRs.

The extra port fixture initially lacked `updatedAt` in its synthetic session row; the canonical reader correctly refused it. Correcting that fixture alone produced the receipt-preservation pass. Product source was unchanged. Earlier cold setup timeouts remain recorded; subsequent prepared-worker qualification did not weaken timeouts or guards.

## Scope and remaining gates

Production/tooling delta excluding generated files: 793 added/186 removed lines; tests 654 added/23 removed. Necessary growth is the atomic receipt, replay authority and two-engine migration/compatibility boundary—not a parallel runtime or allocation manager. The repair deletes the retired generator exception and broad reader dependencies rather than adding alternatives.

Current-head CI, hosted review and landing remain separate gates. The three platform-gated provisioning cases were not exercised locally. No merge is claimed here.

## Generator CI repair evidence

Candidate: `b039bdb311e11b6369757899a779eabd7a594d94`, based on published head `ad51a9143047d2ca47dd9b51a491f0befde1c7c6`.

The sole nonaggregate failure in CI run `41415625394` was an obsolete generator assertion: it still expected PostgreSQL to defer the two deletion indexes under schema 39. The authorized schema-40 migration now adopts those indexes. The original assertion was reproduced locally with the same two extra index definitions before editing.

The existing test now verifies both indexes appear in generated SQL and the runtime artifact. The unused omission exemption was removed; its producer was already retired. title: fix: reuse admitted worker transcript and cron stores
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker turns failing at the PostgreSQL thread boundary and Cron session runs reading scratch from a different partition than the scheduler that admitted them.

## User Impact

Worker launch and scheduled session execution retain their admitted transcript and Cron sources. There are no schema migrations, configuration changes, permission changes, or required operator actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the transcript source already held by the history worker instead of reopening the native database on the Gateway thread. Thread the admitting Cron service’s selected store path into session execution; direct callers still resolve their configured store, and explicitly prepared scratch retains precedence. Existing source-custody checks, revocation, and release behavior remain in place. This removes seven net production lines rather than adding another owner.

Integration adapted from Galin Iliev’s requested fixes; commits credit @galiniliev. This PR is independent of the database portability and scheduled-widget changes.

## Evidence

title: fix: use current client capabilities for scheduled widgets

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled turns offering an inline widget when only a remembered client—not the current turn—supports inline rendering.

Authorized scheduled turns without a current inline-capable client use pinned board widgets instead. Ordinary conversations retain their recorded-capability tool catalog, and current inline-capable clients still receive inline widgets. There are no configuration, schema, or permission changes.

Determine scheduled admission before selecting widget capabilities and use only the current client’s capabilities for scheduled turns. title: feat: support attended-session permission defaults

## Problem

Attended users cannot choose a per-agent creation permission default without repeating it on every request. A New Session picker must also show that creation default accurately, rather than label configured Full Access as Read Only.

It applies only to fresh, directly attended, profiled operator sessions—not existing sessions, forks, catalog sessions, autonomous runs, or delegated callers. `full` still requires current `operator.admin`.

Expose the attended creation default separately in agent metadata and New Session. Existing-session Default remains based on its existing tool-policy contract. ## Why This Change Was Made
The existing composer records its graph in the hash-bound archive inventory. Its staged checker consumes that graph against the actual remaining files, and the finalizer uses the same checker. No new graph owner, runtime manager, package identity, or schema version. The maintained checker is staged with the maintained finalizer so their argument contract agrees.

## What Problem This Solves

## What Problem This Solves

Native same-agent children of repository-only sessions incorrectly fall back to the configured Gateway workspace. Creation fails when that directory is not a Git checkout. ## User Impact

Setup-script permission remains the intersection of the parent's permission and the current caller's authority. Reassigned or revoked sources are refused before child copying and binding. Incompatible local selectors and initial local turns remain invalid. Disk-authoritative parents stay guarded here; #190845 adds fresh disk exports. No schema, configuration or resource-receipt migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing parent-source selector and checkpoint fork owner retain responsibility. title: feat(database): recover retained workspace owners without waking workers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partial recovery can leave a retained repository disk without its native environment or placement owner. Restoring an old full state database would revive stale execution authority and unrelated state.

## User Impact

The offline dependency recovery command can restore or repair the selected original retained owner using sealed source and expected-destination images. It preserves exact disk custody but leaves runtime admission closed, revokes worker credentials, and clears turn claims. No provider, node, setup script, pairing, grant, or role is executed or restored. Explicit wake still uses current authorization, node pairing, provider receipt, and runtime admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prerequisite https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190833 has merged; this PR now targets `main`. Current candidate: `f9fe6dd249a4d3b932cf98f2ba36a3c3eed893ec`. Earlier stacked qualification is retained below. Current schema39 native resource receipts, retention, environment/placement writers, and workspace disk binding remain the owners. Both images use current native codecs; source unfinished-work facts are read independently of destination checks. Current configuration fields must match the acquisition; machine/OS/execution selection remains historical metadata. All three owner records restore in one existing offline transaction after immutable skill/checkpoint artifacts. The request refuses drift and does not automatically retry against changed expected records.

No schema migration, donor v37 parser, Enterprise profile repair, Azure special case, or parallel recovery state is added. The retained kernel and command integration are separate reviewable commits in one dependent PR.

## Evidence

- Native kernel regressions: 2/2 passed, 4.476s test bodies /76.93s wrapper; existing workspace and retention siblings: 4/4 passed. Reopen, dormant launch refusal, conflict refusal, source unfinished work, credential removal, pruning safety and rollback covered.
- Offline retained command integration initially passed 1.655s/43.75s with synthetic acquisition; fresh review found production acquisition-field mismatch. Fixed current profile projection and expanded test to real-shaped executionMode/machineClass/os plus genuinely changed settings refusal. Final production-shaped rerun passed: 1.663s test body /43.18s wrapper. Two intervening failures came from the test reusing the first CLI invocation's resident config after a direct file edit; retiring that runtime snapshot between simulated invocations fixed the fixture without changing product admission.
- Existing mirrored command sibling passed after retained wiring.
- Production and command-test types, eight-file lint and final two-file profile repair lint passed. Generated SQL inventory check passed. Formatting/whitespace and exact test-line allocation passed. The command regression uses a separate 329-line allocation; kernel regressions retain their separate allocation.
- Fresh independent review found one P1 profile-projection defect, addressed. Independent review of the complete stack against checkpoint base 63665a92129f0c0ec5f215de74e37223b47e3dce found no remaining actionable P0–P2 findings after that fix. Prior kernel review found missing source-side unfinished work admission; fixed and regression-covered before integration.

- PostgreSQL 17.11 destination qualification passed on unchanged head `f3ba010c31706c2edaa472dbc70afb38d99a42d4`: native state-family port to PostgreSQL precedes the existing retained command test. It checks actual PostgreSQL anchor, genuine settings-drift refusal, dormant owner/receipt restoration, absent credentials and stale expected-image refusal. Retained test 47.501s including native port; mirrored sibling 1.310s; 2/2 passed in 187.97s Vitest /191.29s wrapper with 78.914s compiled-worker preparation. Initial qualification failed due to a fixture switching all database families and leaking engine selection across files; both corrected without product changes. Qualification copies remain local, not committed.

Limits: no live retained node/provider operation or installed-package upgrade is claimed; released-source persisted-data compatibility is qualified below. Earlier host source-CLI preparation was refused; the subsequent supported isolated compiled-CLI qualification is recorded below. No admission bypass or live Gateway modification. Earlier-head required CI passed; repaired-head CI is required separately; full packaged installation remains a separate boundary.

## Review follow-up

The checkpoint authority/diagnostic repair is integrated additively at `eb86b48b3aa6de2552dfa9ad38c0758453c760e1`; current owner validation now also guards final artifact publication. Actual compiled retained CLI recovery passed (9.862 s scenario), including current-profile drift refusal, dormant restoration and stale expected-image refusal. The CLI returned `executionReady:false`; reopened native records retained the exact resource receipt and no worker credential.

Post-restoration native authority qualification passed separately: one scenario, 4.105 s test time /50.47 s Vitest, adapter exit 0. Actual role downgrade during awaited provider preparation blocked final provider mutation and all node sends. Actual pairing removal blocked node dispatch and left runtime admission closed. Fresh authority and pairing reached the native bundle-install and workspace mutation owners. External provider/node responses were explicitly synthetic; no real provider/disk/runner qualification or installed Gateway wire-authentication claim is made. Pairing gates node I/O; existing native lifecycle allows caller-authorized provider wake before reconnection.

Latest-stable upgrade acquisition is blocked by the effective seven-day package-age policy for existing release `2026.10.9`, with no policy bypass. The installed-package acquisition gap remains open; the released-source stored-data proof below addresses a separate boundary.

## Stack and credits

Requested by @galiniliev; commits preserve Galin’s co-author credit. The non-rewriting dependency join is `39671893b44d78bb3e46328d531711709ff803df`, with parents `eb86b48b3aa6de2552dfa9ad38c0758453c760e1` and `296cc42a477590da368f27a99e9112e34fde86a3`. Its complete source tree exactly equals the qualified `eb86b48` tree; prior proof retains that executing source identity. Current-head CI is required separately.

## Released-source persisted-data compatibility

The v2026.10.9 **stored-data** qualification is now complete using the already-admitted release source at `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`. No npm acquisition, alternate download, package-age exception, production change, or live Gateway mutation was used. This is source-owner data compatibility followed by the real candidate compiled CLI—not a packaged installation/install-over claim.

The released source’s native profile, preferences, skill-library, session, cache, and repository-checkpoint owners produced closed shared-state **20** and agent **25** databases. A fresh writable copy then crossed the actual compiled `dist/index.js` boundary:

Existing profiles, email bindings, role fields, preferences, session-entry bytes/pins, skill rows and unrelated cache bytes survived. Original user settings survived Doctor-owned config normalization. Native current readers loaded the old skill revision and verified checkpoint payloads before recovery.
2. An attempted retained conversion of the upgraded legacy mirror exited **1** with `Retained recovery requires the original disk authority`; state stayed unchanged.
3. After sealed current-schema inputs were captured, a controlled partial-loss injection removed only the selected dependencies under real exclusive offline custody. Actual `database restore-session-dependencies --input … --sha256 … --json` exited **0**, restored the original content and checkpoint, and recreated the missing skill privately/disabled without restoring historical grants. Existing profiles/roles, preferences, unrelated session/cache rows and settings remained unchanged.

title: fix(ui): show DM access progress on the pending action

Confirming Dismiss for a DM access request leaves the confirmation idle while the row's Approve button claims to be loading.

title: fix(workboard): clarify status when releasing claims
body:
Supersedes #155650, thanks @mfurkanakinci.

Related: #155367

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: callers can mistake `workboard_release` without `status` for finishing or pausing work even though the card keeps its current status.

## User Impact

The tool description and status-field help now explain that omitting `status` only clears the claim and preserves the current status, including `running`. Callers can pass a status such as `todo`, `ready`, or `review` when pausing or handing off work. Runtime defaults remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue explicitly accepts clarifying this contract. Workboard already permits running cards without claims, release preserves status, and reclaim separately defaults running cards to ready. Inferring a new destination on release would change those semantics. The tool and documentation now describe the existing distinction.

A sealed request selects a closed immutable SQLite capture, one exact existing session and skill pin, and one workspace checkpoint. improve: bound transcript projection inserts to SQLite limits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bounds active-transcript projection inserts at the owning SQL boundary so an oversized supplied chunk does not exceed SQLite’s bind parameter limit.

## User Impact

This is maintenance hardening of the existing internal SQL owner. Large projection input stays inside the caller’s existing transaction; rollback and sibling rows are preserved. Current native reconciliation already sends 512-row chunks, finalization catches up at most 512 tail rows, and current database ports rebuild only FTS, not active projection rows. No current end-to-end native port failure is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing 512-row transcript insert limit instead of building one statement for every active row. No new option, API, schema, transaction owner, or competing implementation. This patch is independently reviewable and not a dependency of the database-port correctness change. Adapted from Galin Iliev’s batching fix. The 71-line regression allocation covers the real SQLite limit, row coordinates, rollback, and sibling isolation.

## Evidence

### Defect proof at the SQL owner

- Real-SQLite parameter-limit regression passed (0.266s), including rollback and sibling isolation; all 9 projection tests passed (38.95s wall, mostly transforms), retained from the original qualification.

Its Git blob cbd995c69f76f9ff1624ed673ad32559d382c124 matches the retained baseline file. Assertions cover exact canonical bytes across close/reopen, active order, FTS identities and mappings, abandoned-branch exclusion, sibling preservation, no-op reconciliation, and zero host data SQL. title: fix(database): preserve recovery images during offline ports
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes offline database ports that run migration SQL against durable network recovery images, reject legally absent first-use agent tables, or reject a recognized historical pending-input recovery column.

## User Impact

Ports keep verified originals and the durable recovery journal intact while migration and source materialization use private local scratch. Resume reconstructs scratch from the recorded migrated image. Failed scratch is retained; only successfully joined work is removed. Set the existing XDG_CACHE_HOME environment variable to local storage when the default cache is network-backed or unclassifiable.

Only the owned agent copy receives missing declared tables or retires recognized recovery envelopes. Original bytes retain the envelopes, and v24 input interruption runs before retirement. Unknown schema shapes still refuse the operation. No schema versions, permissions, state resource/disk contracts, or retention policies change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing port owner now scopes migration/checkpoint/stage to one local image and uses the existing verified file publisher for both copies. The descriptor consumes the existing schema compatibility declarations rather than adding fork schema or runtime compatibility infrastructure. Adapted from Galin Iliev's database portability work.

title: fix: accept signed filesystem identities in recovery receipts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes database-port recovery and local client credential receipt loading when Node exposes a native device or inode identifier as a signed decimal string.

## User Impact

Operators can resume ports and use their existing client credentials on these filesystems. Exact file/root binding remains required: changed identities still refuse admission. No schema version, credential restoration, permission, or retention policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The writers already serialize Node’s bigint identities verbatim. Both readers now accept the same signed decimal representation without normalization or precision loss. Adapted from Galin Iliev’s portability work.

The two existing parsing owners remain; no helper, state, or compatibility path is added. Production delta +6/-4 lines; regression delta +68 lines, allocated for identity round trips and replacement rejection.

## Evidence

### Existing focused qualification

- Baseline: signed receipt round trips fail (2 cases); signed recovery manifest publication fails (2 cases).
- Fixed: 30 tests passed across receipt and recovery suites; wrapper wall time 3.51s, test time approximately 0.23s. Core and infra test typechecks, focused lint/format and whitespace checks passed.
- That original qualification used checkout `41653af9e09596f1190724be941cd46d128d6d15`. Both production owners and both test files are blob-identical to this PR; other changes in that checkout are not attributed to this PR.
- Independent local review and the earlier hosted review found no actionable product findings. The latest hosted Gold assessment preceded the inspectable terminal traces and credential-command proof now included below; it found no product defects.

### Real public CLI and kernel-mounted signed-root proof

On November 4, exact baseline `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914` and exact PR head `b612f55ebf698a6cc87eec12526fc50ae798d539` were exercised through the documented built public launcher, `node openclaw.mjs database port`, using separately bound source/dependency/build artifacts.

A private, unprivileged kernel FUSE mount projects the high bit of the actual backing-root inode. Unmodified Node bigint stat and the real command observe the negative value; there is no mocked stat, product source patch, preload, handwritten manifest, or injected SQLite data. This is an intentionally controlled affected-filesystem fixture, not a claim about naturally occurring Azure/NFS hardware. PostgreSQL 17 uses a disposable local, resource-bounded fixture with synthetic data; the canonical state row is created by the product owner.

The maintained libfuse low-level passthrough inode/refcount owner is retained. Independent source review found no consequential adaptation defects. Native qualification passed nine descriptor operations after unlink, directory/root identity, fsync, immediate staging-directory removal before descriptor close, and normal unmount. Binary SHA-256: `c24df350f980603777275d29bf51258b2f52a8e9420318f8b223fdfa0a86cb3c`.

| Case | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Baseline port on negative root | Refused signed-manifest publication after real capture completed; canonical row present, no active manifest, unchanged config and empty destination. |
| Fixed port interrupted during staging | Qualified external PostgreSQL DDL fault reached the real worker; owner-written preparing manifest retained the exact signed root, hashed artifacts and canonical snapshot; no destination/reference namespace remained. |
| Baseline resume of that unchanged manifest | Refused before staging; manifest, source, config and artifacts stayed byte-identical, destination remained empty. |
| Fixed resume of that same owner-written manifest | Completed real SQLite-to-PostgreSQL conversion, archived the manifest with the same operation/root identity, matched the canonical source row to PostgreSQL, and published the matching live anchor and family-engine config. |
| Independent fixed interruption for root-change case | Produced a genuine signed-root recovery manifest with the same fault/custody checks. |
| Fixed resume after actual root replacement | Refused at the same absolute path after actual root inode changed; device stayed unchanged. Every child inode/byte and protected manifest/source/config/artifact stayed unchanged; destination remained unchanged. The injected SQL fault was removed before refusal. |

Five cases passed in the 37.142-second run; it stopped before the final CLI call because the harness incorrectly assumed remount changes both device and inode. A fresh C-only run (17.178 seconds) repeated only its required interruption and completed the final refusal case. The product compares the complete root-identity tuple; the corrected oracle requires the same path and actual changed inode and records device identity instead of assuming allocation behavior. No earlier blocked run was relabeled.

Functional evidence SHA-256:
- Five-case run and independent cleanup: `cdf20816a824bdc47ffc46c32a56efd8cfdfe30f4117422680c7260a54f33a53` (184 evidence hashes; 95 recorded host PIDs absent).
- C-only completion and independent cleanup: `4a4a9fe988353f421b9e0a952339af72200a23432c1c41ceab12e1231ea0e93f` (134 evidence hashes; 56 recorded host PIDs absent).

Both containers were absent by name and ID, all task mounts and listeners were absent, and native command settlement was normal. A closed TCP TIME_WAIT entry was distinguished from a listener. Original 160/170/1500-second limits and the sole process-settlement owner stayed unchanged.

The public staging error deliberately preserves the worker's anchored `stage:` prefix; the test now parses the actual JSON envelope and saves contemporaneous server fault evidence before classifying it. A phase label alone never substitutes for manifest, row, artifact, namespace or custody checks.

### Limits and investigated earlier attempts

The command-level proof covers port-root signed inode behavior, inode-only root replacement, and the real local credential-loading command on a signed shared-file identity, including invalid-private-key and byte-identical changed-file refusal. Credential migration production, Gateway authentication and negative native device values are not claimed by these commands; signed-device behavior retains focused owner-boundary coverage.

Earlier attempts remain retained: a source-runner timeout with unknown cause, optional full-syscall captures that reached their trace cap, high-level FUSE staging hidden-file/ESTALE fixture failures, and the interrupted public-phase/device-allocation oracle runs. The current proof uses the qualified low-level fixture and documented built launcher; passing runs do not establish the cause of the old source-runner timeout. No CI retry, baseline increase, or product assertion was waived.

title: improve(backup): omit Codex diagnostics from restart checkpoints
body:
## Current-head CI repair — 2026-11-05

Head `e1829e4211e124ff7f8d6dc606344ec8edd3077e` preserves the cache/backup/renderer work below and repairs a stream-follow coalescing defect discovered while investigating the Activity CI assertion. This section supersedes earlier current-head status summaries; historical failures remain evidence, not passing results.

- **Original CI:** [run 41975853878](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41975853878) finished with 56 successful and 24 skipped jobs; Activity UI E2E3/7 and the aggregate gate failed. The original landscape assertion observed a 208px bottom gap. The final classifier labels it new (matching main job passed, scope not compared); it is not reclassified as inherited or a renderer crash.
- **Owner defect:** another content update can replace a pending animation frame after a delayed native scroll changes the live bottom-distance flag. The replacement then loses the already-admitted follow. Keep that decision alongside the existing frame ID across coalescing; preserve enabled/identity checks, native scrollback behavior and disposal. No new listener, timer, threshold, dependency, layout or public option.
- **Proof:** extending the existing helper case with one coalesced update fails on the original source (expected one scroll, got zero), then passes with the repair. Helper plus Update-view consumers: **12/12 pass**, 3.069s wrapper. Strengthened real Chromium Activity suite: **4/4 pass** across phone, tablet, landscape and desktop, 19.791s wrapper. A separate 4x CPU-throttled diagnostic also passes all four cases, 25.299s wrapper, including initial following before the test manually scrolls. Browsers exit normally.
- **Limits:** the first native diagnostic trace observed initial following stall before any user scroll; the old test's manual initial scroll masked it. A subsequent strengthened pre-fix browser attempt passed, so no deterministic browser red/green or exact reproduction of the CI interleaving is claimed. The deterministic owner regression and caller tests prove the repaired coalescing contract; fresh CI must establish the former shard result. The original historical renderer-crash cause remains unknown.
- **Cost/gates:** one net production line and two lines added to existing tests; no new cases or fixture framework. Exact two-line allocation, shared scalar unchanged. Official test-line gate passes **6,479,702 / 6,479,702**. Targeted supported typecheck, lint, formatting and whitespace pass. The first direct `tsgo` lookup was unavailable before compilation; the supported repository wrapper completed successfully.
- **Review:** complete local autoreview of this four-file delta plus full Activity/Update callers: **scoped-clean P0–P2, no findings**. Previous Diamond review covers the prior head, not this repair. Fresh exact-head CI and overall Platinum+ remain required before merge. No CI rerun or gate waiver.

Co-authored-by: galiniliev <5711535+galiniliev@users.noreply.github.com>

---

## What Problem This Solves

Local-companion restart checkpoints unnecessarily capture Codex’s changing diagnostic SQLite log database and its companions.

## User Impact

Local-companion capture omits only the activated Codex plugin’s managed agent-home `logs_2.sqlite` and `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal`. Full backups and unrelated same-name files remain unchanged. Codex state, credentials, session rollouts, and other databases remain preserved. Omitted diagnostic history is not recovered; Codex recreates the log store.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep vendor policy in Codex manifest `backupResources` and add an optional generic `local-companion` profile selector to the existing planner. No global filename exclusion, extra policy owner, schema/version change, or template-exclusion option is introduced. Native backup safety and source-preservation behavior remain intact.

The native contract was inspected in [Codex 8f73cde](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4): `codex-rs/state/src/sqlite.rs:29,59-65,146-148,297-310` separates logs from durable databases and recreates missing stores with WAL; `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/logs.rs:3-57` records bounded diagnostic/feedback history. OpenClaw’s managed-home owner is `extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-start-options.ts:7-42`. Custom external Codex/sqlite homes are intentionally not inferred.

## Evidence

- Standalone head: `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`, directly parented by baseline `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`. Mechanically separated from `1346e4f6f80911f634b77a212aead087089e1143`; no dependency on template-option commit `84f84f4e818851746b93a78e0a29bcf5b652bc8d`. Eleven files have byte-identical added/deleted lines; the remaining archive-create call only expands the baseline formatting to pass `localCompanion`.
- Fresh standalone proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-local-companion.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-backup-resources.test.ts src/commands/backup-resource-inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with a unique filesystem cache: **27 passed**, three files, **44.74s** including compiler preparation. Companion create/verify/restore test **237ms** (runner **7.67s**); plugin declaration runner **3.04s**; inventory runner **1.14s**. CI seconds unavailable.
- Real archive creation, verification, and restore preserve diagnostic source bytes, state/auth/rollout bytes, a similarly named sibling, unrelated same-name database, client credentials, and PostgreSQL anchors while omitting declared diagnostics. Full-archive resource selection retains the diagnostics.
- Targeted `run-tsgo` passed for all eight changed TypeScript files and their import closure; `run-oxlint` passed all eight; formatter check passed eight TypeScript files and two docs; both docs passed MDX validation; Codex manifest JSON parsed and formatter stdin output was byte-identical; `git diff --check` passed.
- Reused original red proof: the same companion regression reached real restore and failed because `logs_2.sqlite` existed instead of returning `ENOENT`. Reused broader original lane proof: **73 passed, 1 Windows-only skipped**, **131.44s**. These are original reviewed-lane results, not new-head broad-suite results.
- Reused canonical autoreview: P0–P3, complete original local candidate against `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. That review included both independent original changes; this separation changes only context and removes the unrelated template change, so no substantive re-review was required. No claim of a new standalone autoreview run.
- Simplify: one profile conditional in the existing resource planner; no new vendor code in core or duplicate exclusion owner. Production TypeScript **+34/-6**, manifest **+24**, tests **+72/-3**, docs **+13**, allocation **+2**. The 69-line test allocation covers one archive/restore regression and independent metadata-profile admission/deduplication contracts.
- Earlier harness proof used a PostgreSQL discovery fixture. The additional exact-head compiled-CLI proof below uses real PostgreSQL and actual plugin discovery. No real-agent inference, upgrade, Windows or PostgreSQL-disconnection scenario is claimed.

## Main integration and refreshed validation

Integrated official main `2777468d26e5f21455b67591a045a40c770aee13` with an ordinary merge, preserving the original Codex head `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`. New head: `c5a610763a84ad8e11f42af69e0a7422febb0796`.

The two conflicts were additive option forwarding in `backup-shared.ts` and `backup-create.ts`. Both `localCompanion` and `excludeWorktreeTemplates` remain supported together. Registered template selection still belongs to the native registry, and exclusion precedence still belongs to the existing resource planner. No new policy owner, schema, version, or configuration option was introduced by this integration.

Fresh proof on the exact committed tree:

- **32 tests passed across four files**: combined companion/template archive creation, verification and restore; compiled CLI template/full backup behavior; native resource inventory; manifest admission and deduplication. Runner wall time **71.00s**, including worker preparation; shard wall times **29.62s / 1.17s / 3.26s**. The existing template CLI case took **5.411s**, and the companion case **0.246s**. title: feat(backup): omit regenerable workspace templates on request
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full backups can include large regenerable managed worktree templates; omitting whole checkout roots would lose live source and uncommitted edits.

## User Impact

Users can select `--exclude-worktree-templates` on backup create. Only exact registered template generations are omitted; full backup defaults, live checkouts/Git data, and nested durable ownership stay unchanged. Source files are never deleted. Unregistered caches remain included deliberately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing worktree registry read, resource planner, override policy, and manifest skipped-resource reporting instead of a basename/global exclusion. No schema changes or new state owner.

## Evidence

- Base CLI create/verify regression failed on the actual missing option: OpenClaw does not recognize option "--exclude-worktree-templates" (full default archive created successfully first).
- Stable final batch: 6 files, 73 tests passed, 1 existing Windows-only test skipped, source-generation verification passed. Includes real CLI create/verify/restore, managed-workspace/resource-policy siblings, manifest verifier, companion capture, and plugin declaration contracts. Final new CLI test 4.243s; 3 runner shards 38.17s + 6.30s + 3.07s; total with compiled preparation 131.44s.
- Earlier all-green assertions were not treated as success because a concurrent lint edit invalidated the source-generation check; the final stable replay supersedes it.
- Targeted typecheck passed including final manifest repair. Changed-file lint passed (five files from first run, repaired manifest on focused rerun); formatting and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Simplify pass: no new owner, wrapper, manager, or exclusion glob. Necessary production growth is option transport plus exact registry/resource integration; the manifest verifier drops one redundant path binding to stay within its existing module budget.
- Independent autoreview: P0–P3, local candidate against 4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914; scoped-clean, no actionable findings (one pass, complete source verification).
- Test growth allocation covers the real CLI archive/restore boundary and nested durable-owner retention. CI seconds unavailable; local cold baseline test 28.391s, runner 119.52s plus 589.301s cold subprocess compilation on busy host. This subprocess test is needed to protect registration/option transport as well as payload selection.
- No live Gateway changes or real user data.

Independent native integration slice from [the release branch](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/tree/galiniliev/teamclaw_release_20261031).

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

## Additional compiled-CLI evidence

Executed the public compiled CLI (`dist/entry.js`) in a disposable, network-isolated rootless container on November 2, 2026. This is **combined-source proof** at `1346e4f6f80911f634b77a212aead087089e1143`: PR190822’s `84f84f4e818851746b93a78e0a29bcf5b652bc8d` plus only the independently documented Codex companion change. No published ref or production source was changed.

The synthetic fixture uses the real template-registry producer and real filesystem. Four separate CLI processes exited **0**, without stderr:

```text
openclaw backup create --output backup.tar.gz --verify --json
openclaw backup create --exclude-worktree-templates --output lean.tar.gz --verify --json
openclaw backup verify lean.tar.gz --json
openclaw backup restore lean.tar.gz --target restored --json
```

Observed stdout fields (complete raw stdout retained separately):

```json
{"create":{"excludeWorktreeTemplates":true,"verified":true},"skipped":{"kind":"worktree template","reason":"regenerable"},"verify":{"ok":true,"entryCount":22,"sqliteInventoryVerified":true},"restore":{"ok":true,"entryCount":22,"sqliteInventoryVerified":true}}
```

The full archive retained `generation/build-output.bin`; the selected archive and CLI-restored tree omitted it. title: fix(database): keep migration archive capture responsive
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes migration captures losing their renewable Gateway suspension when large filesystem archive preparation blocks the capture process.

## User Impact

Externally quiesced SQLite migration capture keeps renewing the existing suspension while archive creation and verification run. Cancellation joins the child before returning. Existing source-artifact preservation, PostgreSQL refusal, exact snapshots, restore behavior, and schema39 remain unchanged. No live Gateway changes or schema migration are required; the capturing binary must contain this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture now delegates blocking archive work to the existing update inspection subprocess owner with a 30-minute deadline, instead of introducing another process lifecycle. The child explicitly calls `verifyBackupArchive` before its bounded verified receipt; the archive creation helper does not consume `verify: true`. The parent keeps its existing revalidation and manifest-publication checks.

Simplification removed in-process archive execution and its ineffective verify flag. The launcher, wiring, and worker share the existing inspection lifecycle. The dedicated 133-line test allocation protects renewal, child settlement, archive validity, and caller-relative workspace contents without changing the shared baseline scalar.

title: fix(channels): preserve ingress retries after lost claim ownership
body:
Supersedes #158083, thanks @YangManBOBO.
Closes #158082.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: recovering abandoned inbound-message claims consumes delivery retries and overwrites the last real failure timestamp, which can cause premature dead-lettering on a later genuine failure.

## User Impact

User impact: messages interrupted by a lost worker retain their delivery retry budget and failure history. Genuine dispatch failures still reach the existing retry limit. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stale-owner recovery returns the existing row to pending without recording a delivery failure. Keep that distinction in the current worker kernel while preserving its existing claim fencing. The ordinary failure path continues to record attempts.

The simplification removes the two recovery-only retry-field assignments and their unnecessary expression callback: production net **-1 line**. The existing drain lifecycle regression gains a stale-owner case with **+3 test lines**, covered by a matching test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- **Red on main `c8f87b2e5163870671510659745f4167239ff50e`:** the production drain/SQLite-worker regression failed because recovery changed attempts from 1 to 2 and lastAttemptAt from 100 to 101, without another delivery failure.
- **Green after:** 80 tests across `ingress-drain.test.ts`, `ingress-queue.test.ts`, `ingress-queue.claim-ownership.test.ts`, and `ingress-retry-policy.test.ts`; named-file command with `--maxWorkers=1` completed in 39.46 seconds including worker preparation (changed drain file: 23 cases, 5.931 seconds of reported case time; changed-channel CI job: 106 seconds including setup). The regression repeats lost-owner recovery three times, verifies preserved retry facts and successful redispatch, then verifies a genuine failure dead-letters at the configured limit. Existing cancellation and claim-fencing coverage also passes.
- Focused proof ran on Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox ([remote environment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41378106033)); PR CI supplies broad proof. No live transport or production Gateway was exercised or changed. Contributor code was read with gh and was never executed; this is an independent reimplementation on current main.

title: fix: await Doctor snapshots and recover same-boot database leases
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can block JavaScript signal handling while preparing private SQLite images for large agent databases. [chrislro’s macOS stack sample](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178359#issuecomment-6566904639) identified `spawnSync` waiting on the snapshot child with an 8.4 GB agent database. Missing macOS/Windows lease provenance also forces repeated full integrity gates after interrupted runs. Related: #178359, #187900, #185879.

## User Impact

Await lint snapshot admission, auth/lease inspection, recovery inventory and converted repair-planning reads through the existing owners. Cancellation reaches the owned snapshot child and joins cleanup. Reports share a read-owned image; writable plugin images remain exclusive. Required copies check database, WAL and rollback-journal sizes against available cache space and report insufficient capacity clearly. Unknown capacity remains best effort.

New macOS/Windows leases reuse the existing platform boot identity reader. Same-boot dead owners can use the existing cheaper recovery gate; legacy, unavailable or mismatched provenance still requires full verification. Existing leases are not backfilled. The candidate Doctor/worker must contain the fix; an older installed updater cannot gain it from the candidate alone. **Not yet released.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Artifact-preserving inspection still needs private images because native read-only SQLite can change WAL/SHM coordination files and some checks need writable private state. Capacity reservation is conservative even where copy-on-write could succeed. Existing admission, quarantine and transaction owners retain their decisions. Released synchronous SDK APIs and native final-effect checks retain their contracts. No new configuration or schema version.

This is the core stage of the complete caller cutover. Remaining session/shared-auth readers, process inspection, native credentials, Cron/daemon reads and repair preservation are in #190870, #190872, #190873, #190874 and #190875. Those stages remain pending.

title: feat(discord): fork threads into independent sibling conversations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord thread conversations need independently routed siblings with inherited context.

## User Impact

/fork [title] creates a same-parent sibling for existing public text threads, private text threads and forum posts. The title is optional. Private forks add only requester and bot, disable member invitations and disclose that source members are not copied; members with Manage Threads may still have access. Media/announcement threads, DMs and top-level channels are refused. Command authorization and native permissions remain required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared core prerequisite is landed. The plugin qualifies source/parent/history access, reuses available required forum tags, creates one sibling, verifies private requester membership and binds the returned destination to the ordinary copied session. Current command/account authority reaches creation, binding and recap. Literal recaps suppress native mentions/embeds. Known created resources survive partial failure; uncertain creates are not automatically retried.

The additional permission-owner refactor https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190949 is incorporated before this main landing. Current head d4c91a7b9d894900c29d45abda588e82952570a7 has exactly the tested tree of 719d171aa43f821419c274ce91e749d5b3be9f9a, based on landed core b515cc7f9f1f6af4f401be45c7464f9f3300e8d1. Qualification-local facts reduce public reads17 to6 and private reads18 to7, while preparation and pre-create independently refresh. No cross-phase/global cache or second permission owner.

title: feat: fork threaded conversations with Telegram support
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Threaded channel conversations need a real context fork, not a fresh thread with an empty session or a subagent. Landing review identified stale nonowner command admission and loss of literal recap protection after a formatting rejection; both are repaired.

## User Impact

`/fork [title]` in a Telegram forum topic creates a sibling topic bound to an independent copy of the selected conversation context. The original retains its session. The sibling receives the last three available visible text excerpts; busy sources copy only the last completed prefix. The title is optional. Manage Topics and existing bindings are required; DMs and unthreaded chats are refused.

Prerequisite https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190763 is landed. Discord, Slack and Control UI typed-command parity remain separate dependent PRs. Existing Control UI menu forks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared command owns authorization, ordinary-session copying, source selection, history projection and recap delivery. A lazy optional channel capability owns native sibling placement and current account/access authority. This copies conversation context, not a Git checkout or external side effects.

The ancestry/header-cut and command-transcript owners commit a copied-session checkpoint before native effects and record the final outcome before acknowledgement delivery. Recap mirrors are display-only. Known resources survive later failures; uncertain native effects are not blindly retried. Command artifacts do not advance the last-completed model boundary, so repeated active forks exclude unfinished model input.

The existing authorization producer now retains a current-policy assertion for admission and awaited effect boundaries. Telegram code-only fallback pages retain native pre entities after HTML/rich rejection. Ordinary prose fallback and per-attempt transport authority remain unchanged. title: fix(channels): preserve ordinary thread session bindings

title: fix(plugins): install local file URLs on Windows

title: fix(exec): preserve no-timeout results from macOS app nodes
body:
Supersedes #185434, thanks @etzelm.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: commands on macOS app nodes lose their result after 20 seconds when `exec` requests `timeoutSeconds: 0`.

## User Impact

User impact: no-expiry commands can return their output after 20 seconds. Gateway invocation bounds, cancellation, configured policy, finite timeout caps, and explicit socket deadlines remain in effect. Delivery requires a macOS app build with the updated bundled node runtime; no Team Gateway deploy is needed for the fix itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway normalizes zero to `timeoutMs: null`, which Swift already executes without a process timer. The socket client must distinguish an omitted timeout (`undefined`, retaining its 20-second default) from explicit zero or null. This repairs that decision at the existing owner without changing Swift or execution policy.

The existing socket tests now cover null alongside zero and verify that an explicit finite socket deadline still overrides null. Production LOC delta: 0; test LOC delta: 0. No new machinery or test harness was needed.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41365038582) and the required `openclaw/ci-gate` pass for `a908e6808cdc25fdc3e3c42f4791952831c1f1ae`, including changed-test lanes, type/lint checks, baseline ratchets, and security checks.

- Main checked at `71becfa19f32a86eb3e62bccf713f5be7107884f`: traced exec timeout resolution → Gateway zero-to-null normalization → node-host forwarding → socket response deadline → Swift nil timeout handling.
- Red before: the null case in `src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts` fails on main because a response timer is installed (1 failed, 15 passed; wrapper 2.59 s).
- Green after: `pnpm test src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts src/infra/exec-host.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 17 passed, wrapper 1.76 s. The real Unix socket receives output after a simulated day; explicit 50 ms override, finite command budgets, omitted default, and cancellation retain coverage. CI timing is reported by the PR checks.
- Touched-file lint, format check, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, final local snapshot against the main SHA above): scoped-clean, no actionable findings. It reviewed the changed files plus the Gateway, node-host, exec timeout, and Swift callers; it did not execute tests.
- Baseline failure retained: the additional `src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` run fails in the malformed matching response case with `read ECONNRESET` at its peer cleanup assertion. The same failure reproduces with the unmodified main socket owner (1 failed, 7 passed). Its finite 5,000 ms command and explicit 1,000 ms response budget are unchanged by this patch; other sibling cases pass. Socket reset behavior remains an investigated baseline uncertainty, not a passing check.
- Local node-host test preparation began compiling the broader worker bundle and was stopped to respect production-host limits. PR CI owns node-host and broad proof. This Linux host has no macOS toolchain; no native app execution or Swift build is claimed. The TypeScript transport regression does not prove native process cancellation.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` only and was never checked out, installed, built, or run. This replacement was implemented independently on main and credits Mitchell Etzel in the commit.

title: fix(discord): avoid false failure notices for queued thread answers
body:

Fixes false Discord failure notices after a queued message is successfully answered in a thread created from that message.

Transfer the source-message route from dispatch into the existing queued delivery-correlation lifecycle before queued execution. The queued run owns its own registration through settlement, including when it starts before dispatch returns. Thread creation alone and replies to unrelated threads do not count as answers.
