title: chore: investigate sandbox checkpoint lease loss
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Investigation of sandbox preparation lasting about 22 minutes before losing its reconciliation lease. **Closed without a verified fix. The proposed five-second reuse probe budget is withdrawn.**

## User Impact

No shipped behavior change. The proposal did not demonstrate a repair of renewal during authoritative synchronization and could pause runtimes sooner on large workspaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lead review corrected the initial attribution: reuse probing precedes runtime quiescence, which precedes authoritative canonical checkpoint synchronization. Both synchronization sites add to one `synchronizeCanonical` timing key. The recorded quiescence phase therefore contradicts attributing the entire failed operation to a lease-aborted reuse probe. The aggregate timing cannot split the duration between sites.

## Evidence

Against original base `5342923d897ad8a8021bdf586753f8cd38cd3094`, temporary isolated production-path probes held canonical scan I/O and post-commit checkpoint acknowledgement beyond the initial custody lease lifetime. Both observed further committed renewals and completed reconciliation with the expected file contents. A controlled-clock test also confirmed repeated phase durations accumulate under one key. Three tests passed across two focused shards in 12.08 seconds.

These passing controls do not establish what blocked the production renewal. The state writer serializes individual native commands, while manifest reads/computation use separate workers and a retained callback alone does not occupy the writer. A busy native writer, delayed renewal reply, or event-loop stall remains unproven. No deterministic red-on-base renewal defect was established, so there is no justified production fix to land.

title: improve(database): avoid repeated PostgreSQL search snippet work
body:
Supersedes #188951, thanks @etzelm.

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL version 2 text searches spend database CPU computing the same headline twice for each snippet.

## User Impact

Search returns the same results and punctuation-preserving snippets with one headline evaluation per SQL result row. No configuration, schema migration, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared PostgreSQL snippet owner now reuses normalized text and its headline through scalar subqueries. Two `OFFSET 0` fences prevent PostgreSQL from expanding those expressions at each reference. Existing candidate limits and ranking stay in their owners.

Production delta is +3/-3 (net 0): the duplicated headline expression disappears. The existing migration test gains 21 lines to pin the returned snippet and inspect the real PostgreSQL plan; its separate allocation covers exactly that regression growth. Simplification reuses the existing fixture without another helper or test setup.

## Evidence

- Acceptance: preserve the result ID and exact snippet bytes, with one headline and one punctuation-normalization expression in the PostgreSQL plan.
- Base `5342923d897ad8a8021bdf586753f8cd38cd3094` plus the regression: expected result and snippet pass; the headline-count assertion fails (four plan occurrences across the Limit/scan outputs; the expression itself contains two evaluations).
- Replacement: 15/15 tests pass across PostgreSQL text migration, engine search conformance, and session-search product flow. This includes ranking, filtering, bounds, literal/prefix matching, and a late punctuation-joined match. Test runtime: 18.90 seconds total; runner including fixture compilation: 53.56 seconds. The changed migration test takes 172 ms.
- Real PostgreSQL in a task-owned rootless Podman container capped at 4 CPUs and 8 GiB. No production database or Gateway state was used. The contributor head was read with `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out or executed.
- Scoped formatting, lint, typecheck (the two changed TypeScript files and their dependencies), and `git diff --check` pass. Broad validation runs in PR CI.
- Independent autoreview (P0–P2) completed `scoped-clean`, with no actionable findings.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41305632844) passed, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Full shard job times were 1,230 / 1,283 / 1,326 seconds, including setup and the broader suite; these are not the incremental cost of this regression.
- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190309#issuecomment-6557864724) found no actionable correctness or security defects on the same head.

This establishes reduced expression evaluation, not an end-to-end latency claim. The PostgreSQL product harness exercises search through the tool and Gateway handler; no live model/Gateway deployment was run on the production host.

title: fix(xai): keep Talk connected after an interrupted answer is replaced
body:
Supersedes #184210, thanks @Marvinthebored

Closes #184207

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes xAI Talk disconnecting when speech interrupts an answer and xAI starts its replacement without sending the interrupted answer's terminal event.

## User Impact

Talk continues with the replacement answer, discarding late output from the interrupted answer. Genuine provider errors and invalid overlapping responses remain errors. No configuration changes or migrations are needed. Accepted edge case: a downstream completion observer that throws remains a logged application fault and may require restarting the call; this fix does not add arbitrary-observer recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The xAI adapter already recognizes the new speech and identified successor, but it replaces its own response ID while Talk still owns the predecessor. Settle that interrupted response as cancelled before publishing its successor, using the existing speech/response state and completion callback.

Production delta: +13/-9 lines (net +4). Removed duplicate response-ID assembly and a redundant guard; the remaining growth supplies cancellation dispatch and its callback-close check without adding state or relaxing shared relay ownership.

## Evidence

- A real loopback WebSocket drives the publicly registered xAI plugin through Talk's production session harness and relay ownership. The regression fails on main `5342923d897ad8a8021bdf586753f8cd38cd3094` with `Realtime provider output has no live response owner.` and passes with the fix.
- Covers distinct cancelled/completed turns, preserved user transcription, discarded stale audio/text/tools, ordinary overlap rejection, provider-error propagation, and fatal malformed-audio closure. The 163-line regression has a dedicated test-line allocation because existing plugin-only tests do not compose relay ownership.
- 54 focused xAI lifecycle tests passed. Targeted type checking, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad validation runs in PR CI.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the final local diff against the main commit above: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The review included the bridge, protocol, relay ownership, session harness/runtime, and existing xAI lifecycle tests.

Proof limits: synthetic provider events over a real local WebSocket; no paid xAI call, physical microphone, or full Gateway boot. Contributor source was read as a diff and was never checked out or executed. Final regression: 409 ms test time, 46.25 s wall time including a cold compiled-worker build (the earlier warm run took 8.76 s). [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41305603606) passed in 445 seconds; the changed-test job took 274 seconds including its other selected tests and setup. Both required CI-gate checks passed.

title: docs(ui): design a bounded held window for deep chat history
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Loading earlier messages in the Control UI gets slower with every page, and memory keeps growing, because the chat pane holds every row the reader has loaded and re-walks all of them on each older page. The 12 MiB cap applies only to the cached snapshot, not to the live pane.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet. This draft proposes how to keep per-page cost and memory flat at any depth. It needs the product decisions listed below before any code ships.

## Why This Change Was Made

The task asked for the smallest safe first stage. I didn't find one that avoids product decisions, so this draft has only the design (`docs/reference/control-ui-held-history-window-design.md`). The design covers:

- **Ownership:** `state.chatMessages` stays the only held array and is still published only through `history-merge.ts`. `ChatHistoryPagination`, which already owns the older edge, gains one optional fact: `gap: { afterSource, beforeSource, newerCursor? }`. `ChatPaneHistory` makes the eviction decision through one pure function. `buildChatItems` emits a single `history-gap` boundary item.
- **Window shape:** a deep block, at most one gap, and the live tail block. The alternative was a detached tail (evict the newest rows). I rejected it because `insertSessionProjectionEntry` places a live persisted row after the newest held row, so with the tail evicted, live rows would land straight after the deep rows. Delta reads, send/steer pending rows, input placement, stream rows, end-follow, **Scroll to latest**, `reconcileHistoryTail`, the snapshot cache and the `chat-history-state` read model all assume the held rows reach the live tail. Keeping the tail block preserves that assumption, so none of those writers change.
- **Eviction policy:** runs only after an older-page prepend, once held rows exceed `K_max` (proposed 5,000 rows or 12 MiB weight); it trims to `K_target` (proposed 4,000). It removes only rows between the deep block (prepended page through viewport plus a two-page margin) and the tail block (latest page plus pending, queued or live-run rows). Cuts fall only where a sequence group ends and a user row starts the next turn, so tool calls/results, reasoning and handoffs are never split. Evicted rows are below the viewport, so the anchor doesn't move. Eviction is paused while search is open, during reply navigation and in catalog sessions.
- **Reloading newer rows:** a gap sentinel mirrors the older one, with the same intent, settle and failure gates, plus an explicit **Load newer messages** action. Requests use `chat.history { cursor: newerCursor }`, or a `messageId` probe when no cursor is held, like today's `needsBoundary`. The gap closes when a page reaches `beforeSource` or returns no `newerCursor`. `windowReset` falls back to `reloadChatHistoryWindow`.
- **Live events and Scroll to latest:** both keep working as they do now. Reaching the tail may drop the deep block and the gap.
- **Cache:** with a gap present, only the tail block is cached (with `needsBoundary`), so the persisted schema doesn't change.
- **Reply navigation:** a target inside the gap fills the gap instead of paging older.
- **Stages:** (1) the gap fact, eviction, the gap row, downward fill without top trimming, and tail-only cache commits; (2) sentinel-driven fill plus top trimming, with `TranscriptPrependAnchor` handling leading removals; (3) reply navigation into the gap and shrinking on **Scroll to latest**.

### Decisions needed

1. **Loaded rows can leave the client.** In-app search filters held rows only, and so do browser find and reply previews. Options: pause eviction while search is open (proposed for stage 1), show a "matches in unloaded history are hidden" hint, or add server-side transcript search.
2. **Gap affordance:** a visible **Load newer messages** divider in the middle of the transcript (a visual change), or invisible auto-fill only.
3. **Bound:** `K_max`/`K_target` (proposed 5,000/4,000 rows, capped by the existing 12 MiB weight).
4. **Sequencing with the incremental-render lanes:** ship the bound after that work or alongside it.

## Evidence

- **Work count per older page (code reading):** at least six full passes over held rows: prepend identity, session projection publish (including `createSessionProjection` / `readSessionMessageIdentity` per row), projection compare/copy, snapshot commit, `buildChatItems` (about nine internal passes) and the transcript chain/index/rows projection.
- **Isolated stage timings:** medians of 3 runs, one 1,000-row older page prepended onto `held` rows, measured with a scratch vitest that was not committed. Host load average was about 17, so treat these as relative.

  | held | prepend | projection | buildChatItems | chain+index |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1,000 | 0.3 ms | 0.3 ms | 8.7 ms | 9.5 ms |
  | 4,000 | 0.8 ms | 0.6 ms | 21.1 ms | 28.6 ms |
  | 8,000 | 1.2 ms | 0.9 ms | 37.9 ms | 49.5 ms |
  | 12,000 | 1.8 ms | 1.3 ms | 59.1 ms | 52.8 ms |
  | 16,000 | 2.7 ms | 1.5 ms | 81.5 ms | 75.6 ms |

  That is linear growth at about 10 µs per held row for these two stages. A 4,000-row bound would hold them at about 50 ms per page instead of 157 ms at 16,000 rows.
- **Lead's end-to-end measurement** (isolated Gateway, production bundle, 30,000 messages): Gateway `chat.history` is flat at 35–75 ms per page. Browser script time per page is about 150 ms at pages 1–5 and about 305 ms at pages 21–25 (4x CPU throttle: about 650 ms vs about 1,350 ms).
- **Gateway prerequisite exists:** both-direction anchored paging is already supported and tested. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --maxWorkers=1 src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-page-cursor.test.ts` passed 21/21, including reversing an older page with its `newerCursor`.
- **Checks:** oxfmt check on the doc passed, `git diff --check` is clean, and local autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`) found nothing actionable.
- **Gaps:** no implementation and no RED/GREEN tests yet, by design. Total memory at 30,000 held messages wasn't measured. The timings above come from a loaded shared host.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(update-repair): preserve repair budgets across wall-clock changes
body:

## User Impact

Repairs retain the operator-granted elapsed-time budget across forward and backward clock corrections, and reported attempt durations remain nonnegative.

## Why This Change Was Made

title: chore: verify native systemd updates in the survivor matrix
body:
Related: #188978, #190179, #190176

## What Problem This Solves

The maintained upgrade-survivor matrix uses manual restart and `--no-restart`, so it does not prove a native systemd-managed stop, updater-owned restart, or recorded service verification. A native managed-service regression can pass that coverage.

## User Impact

The maintained Published driver update job gains positive native systemd coverage alongside its existing Docker cell. Runtime update behavior and manual container flows are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add one native flow under the existing survivor harness, initially published 2026.10.9. It reuses the workflow's checksum-verified candidate, shared state/approval seeds and assertions, and health/readiness probes. A fresh guest account installs the actual published user service and invokes its installed updater with restart enabled. Success requires native unit/cgroup ownership, updater-recorded verification, a changed MainPID, exact authenticated candidate build identity, preserved state, and owned-service cleanup. Exact stable/extended baselines can run sequentially; the extended hop retains `--channel stable`.

The same hosted job adds one fifteen-minute step, with no new runner or matrix fanout. Necessary growth is the native account/service adapter, its plan/assertions, workflow invocation, and docs. Two tests protect flow/channel selection and reject failed/unverified or non-native outcomes even when candidate RPC is healthy.

## Evidence

- Real Linux Crabbox/Testbox proof: published 2026.10.9 → pinned main `f83363193ffbc345fee54c9f7ed5f2d15e9b9bba` PASS. Native MainPID 8910 → 15961; all recorded verification flags true, no plugin errors, exact candidate RPC build, state/approvals preserved, final unit inactive/PID 0. Ubuntu 24.04, systemd 255, Node 24.22.1. [Proof lease workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41297769211) is completed/cancelled after external lease cleanup; its cancellation is not the payload verdict.
- Candidate build `2026.10.9-f83363193ffb-2026-11-01T10-33-56.391Z`, SHA256 `ed0d40edb75477fb244686a758d6fb386bd9e658e1d7da4d36b9eb54a2698e66`; canonical full build, package inventory and import/integrity checks passed on the guest.
- 28 focused tests pass (2 native contract cases + 26 existing published-driver planner/workflow cases), final wrapper 4.04s; new file 6ms, standalone wrapper 1.20s. Targeted types/lint, formatting, workflow validation and diff checks pass. The unused-file check reports unchanged `scripts/lib/gateway-bench-heap-profile.mjs`; no ignore or expected-failure exception added.
- Post-PR autoreview at `e928736baf4c` was scoped-clean. After the named CI repair below, fresh shared-helper autoreview of the complete local candidate against main `fd8424b6dc30` (P0–P2, shared assertions/probes and deferred helper context) is also **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Committed head `a54244aaa5b5295bbe02899a230466e61e9f33ee` has the same reviewed source tree. ClawSweeper acknowledged the ready PR; no duplicate request.
- First exact-head [CI run 41303283219](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41303283219) failed only `check-lint-core-2` and its aggregate gate. Complete job logs identify two redundant `createDeferred<void>()` arguments in an existing workshop test added on main after this branch's base (#190158), outside the systemd diff. Integrated main `fd8424b6dc30` for this named failing gate and removed just those arguments; the helper defaults to `void`, preserving behavior. Targeted type-aware lint reproduces both errors before and passes after. The affected Gateway-drain case passes (1 passed, 18 skipped; cold wrapper 44.67s). The broader local 90-second test invocation completed the 28 survivor/planner tests and 17 workshop cases before its deadline; it is not claimed as a full-file pass. No CI rerun, ignore or gate exception was used. [Exact-head CI run 41304517171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41304517171), attempt 1, **SUCCESS** on `a54244aaa5b5295bbe02899a230466e61e9f33ee`. Final rollup: 57 successful checks, 57 skips, 1 neutral, zero pending/failed; mergeable/CLEAN. No CI exception selected.
- All task leases released; no production Gateway or live state touched.

### Regression qualification

**This fresh native fixture does not by itself reproduce #188978.** It also passes pre-fix `6fd646e86cd7` and `dbd856894bb4` (the parent of #190179). These are unexpected passes, not negative proof. Maintainer direction permits landing this positive managed-stop/restart/verification coverage with that gap explicit.

The existing catcher is the maintained **`2026.9.36/base` manual container cell** in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/run.sh`: deep pass #3 failed on pre-fix `ba1f8c05821a` when Doctor refused the changed SQLite capture, and its fixed replay passed #190179. That evidence remains separate from this native flow.

The difference remains unexplained. Deep3 starts/stops its baseline before adding the legacy survivor seed, while this healthy native fixture prepares that seed with baseline Doctor before service startup. The latter imports approval/workspace/session state before the update. Deep3's original base WAL/SHM bytes and the published snapshot used by #190176 were not available in retained artifacts/catalog. A bounded seed-order probe received queued capacity and was stopped without payload or provider fallback. No failure injection, SQLite/SHM edit, or weakened assertion was accepted as negative evidence.

title: fix(gateway): start restored PostgreSQL homes on the first attempt
body:

title: fix(ui): keep older chat history still while reading it
body:
## Problem

On mobile (reported from iOS Safari), messages jump around while you scroll up through older chat history after it loads. Three things cause it, and each one moves the messages on screen when a row above the viewport changes size:

1. **Rows skipped by `content-visibility: auto` (≤768 px).** Offscreen overscan rows keep their virtual estimate (120 px) until they reach the viewport. Then they render at full size and push the messages being read down, by up to about 1,300 px in the repro.
2. **Corrections land one frame late.** Since #188470, virtual-core applies row measurements on the next animation frame, so it isn't committing the range inside native resize delivery. Rows lay out in normal flow, though, so each estimate→real correction above the reader is painted once as a jump before it snaps back.
3. **iOS defers every correction for the whole gesture.** iOS WebKit cancels touch and momentum scrolling on a `scrollTop` write, so virtual-core holds every correction until scrolling settles. The transcript stays displaced for the whole fling, then snaps.

## Solution

- `TranscriptReaderAnchor` (new, owned by the virtualizer host) watches mounted rows. When a row above the viewport changes size, it corrects during that same resize delivery, before paint, using native geometry only. It never commits the range, so the #188470 contract still holds:
  - Outside iOS gestures, it writes `scrollTop`. Like virtual-core's own path, the write is recorded as maintenance and the native range grows first.
  - During iOS touch or momentum, it shifts the row column instead: a negative margin, mirrored in `scrollMargin` so virtual and DOM offsets still agree. The shift folds into `scrollTop` when virtual-core reports that scrolling has settled. It skips elastic overscroll.
  - When virtual-core lands the measured size, the anchor's predicate reconciles it (no double correction). It also takes over iOS-held corrections that virtual-core would otherwise defer. Restoration, scroll commands, and the prepend and disclosure anchors still own placement while they are active.
  - Hidden panes (collapsed side panel, `clientHeight` 0) report zero-height rows; those deliveries are ignored so a restored panel keeps its reading position.
- The compensation predicate now covers rows above the reader in both scroll directions. Virtual-core's default skipped re-measured rows while scrolling backward, which is exactly when reading older history.
- Mobile rows no longer use `content-visibility: auto`. The virtualizer already limits how many rows are mounted, so overscan rows now lay out (and get measured) while still offscreen.
- The history sentinel's IntersectionObserver now observes anew when it fires during a maintenance correction. It used to drop that notification, and since an unchanged intersection is never reported again, auto-loading at the top could get stuck.
- Row-key commits moved into `chat-transcript-header.ts` (with the existing header-margin helper) to stay under the host's line budget.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/e2e/chat-history-reading-stability.e2e.test.ts`: 30 recent + 160 older variable-height messages. It reads up to the top to load the older page, then reads upward through it for 240 frames, sampling the **painted** frame and following the first visible message.
  - Base (`bf73e1aa`): fails on all three — Chromium 390 px with iPhone UA: 36 shifted frames, worst 1,255 px; WebKit 390 px: 29 shifted frames, worst 1,246 px; Chromium 1280 px: 38 shifted frames, worst 809 px.
  - This branch: 0 shifted frames on all three.
- Existing e2e: `chat-history-prepend-anchor` (all variants, including touch and momentum), `session-dashboard-active-panel` (caught the hidden-pane case in CI; fixed and green), `session-progress-scroll`, `chat-widget-autosize`, `chat-composer-accessory-focus`, `warm-boot`, `post-deploy-session-entry`, `chat-saved-attempt-navigation`, `claude-sessions`, `chat-flow.messaging`: all green.
- Unit and browser: all `chat-transcript-*` tests, chat history, thread, page and session-progress suites — 988 tests green after merging current `main`.
- Real Gateway (temporary harness, not committed): isolated Gateway, a 400-message session, the real `chat.startup` plus `chat.history` paging at 390 px with an iPhone UA, reading upward through about 90 messages (1,109 frames): 0 shifted frames on this branch, so no regression. In that harness the base build also showed 0, because the rows had real sizes cached before they mounted, so this run is no-regression evidence, not a reproduction.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, oxfmt, madge import cycles, assertion-safety ratchet, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`.
- `main` was merged in to pick up the fix for an inherited `check-lint-core-2` failure (`src/skills/workshop/experience-review.test.ts`, untouched here).

## Test change

`chat-transcript-end-follow.browser.test.ts` ("holds the canceled viewport…") used to grow the earlier row in the same task as `cancelScroll()`. Now that is a real resize above the reader, and it gets compensated. The fixture now grows the row while the smooth journey is still in flight, which is the skipped-measurement case the test is about. The assertions are unchanged.

## Accepted edges

- iOS: if you reach the very top in the same gesture that accumulated a column shift, the first rows stay clipped above the edge until the gesture settles (one fold, invisible to the reader).
- A row that grows above the reader and unmounts before its measurement lands has its correction retired instead of reverted.

## Not verified

- No physical iPhone. iOS behavior was exercised through virtual-core's UA-based iOS path in Chromium and Playwright WebKit.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: chore(test): avoid five-second CLI admission lock probe
body:
Related: #156703

## What Problem This Solves

The CLI fallback contention regression test spends five seconds proving that a SQLite write lock is held before exercising the actual fallback flow. This maintainer-directed test-health lane targets the 5.616s case in [CI run 41293098118](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41293098118).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The target case is about five seconds faster, with its real SQLite contention and cold session-reader regression coverage retained. Production code, SQLite busy timeouts, and mocks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the synchronous writable `loadSessionEntry()` precondition with a test-local raw connection to the same shared-state database. Set its `busy_timeout` to zero and assert that `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` fails with `database is locked`. A scoped `using` closes the probe before `runLocal()`.

The awaited agent-database close remains before lock acquisition. The raw probe neither opens an agent database nor reads session metadata. The existing CLI callback still requires the holder transaction to be live when execution is reached, then releases it for settlement. The final assertions still require a successful reply, the existing native session ID and binding, exactly one CLI call, no result error, and no embedded-agent fallback. No incidental coverage was removed.

## Evidence

Three serial full-file runs before and after, on the same Linux host with the repository's default pinned Bun runtime and unchanged runner settings. All six runs passed all 18 tests. Acceptance: remove roughly five seconds from the case median, every after case faster than every before case, and kill the original writable-open mutation.

```sh

  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-admission.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose --reporter=json --outputFile=<report.json>
```

| after 3 | 17.07s | 12.48s | 6.789s | 0.547s |
| **before median** | **23.02s** | **17.96s** | **11.715s** | **5.591s** |

Command wall includes wrapper preparation and cleanup. File test time is the Vitest JSON suite end/start interval; Vitest duration is the reporter's duration. Command: `timeout 600 pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-*.test.ts src/agents/session-placement-admission.test.ts src/agents/session-placement-admission.caller-scope.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`. Net diff: **production 0 lines; tests +5 lines** (6 added, 1 removed). The five lines preserve a real, non-mocked lock precondition and close its raw connection before the product flow; no new helper or production seam is needed. The test-line scalar is unchanged because this is growth; the ratchet passes at exactly 6,373,300 lines against the existing 6,390,531-line effective ceiling (17,231 lines of slack). ### Landing verification

The parent-reviewed head 8f8e7d44a851abef92f01fc8503aa0248512e6a5 merged as 2cd32cfd86762482d9cb6d94a35cd8a6df7d51b1 at 2026-11-01T11:10:19Z after exact-head [CI 41299422489](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41299422489) succeeded and normal native security and required-review gates qualified. title: fix(ui): loading earlier chat messages gets slower with every page in long sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: scrolling up to load earlier messages in the Control UI gets slower with every page in long chats, until each page takes several seconds.

## User Impact

User impact: loading earlier messages stays fast deep into long sessions. In a 30,000-message chat on a crowded Gateway with 4× CPU throttling, the wait for pages 21–25 drops from about 3.3–3.4 s to about 1.6 s, and the longest blocking task from about 2.5 s to about 1 s. Loaded history (count, order, deduplication), the saved cache contents and the rest of the history flow are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each older page rebuilds work across the whole loaded transcript. Two parts of that rebuild got much heavier and grew with depth:

- **Row footprints (regressed in #183595).** Rebuilding the transcript row index re-serialized and hashed every loaded message to compute its saved row height key. Loaded history messages are immutable, so each message's fingerprint is now computed once and reused (WeakMap keyed by the message object). The key changes format, so saved row heights miss once after upgrade, then refill.
- **Snapshot trimming.** Once the cached chat passes its 12 MiB limit, committing a page dropped older rows one group at a time and re-serialized the snapshot envelope (including row display facts, #186512) on every step. That envelope is identical for every trim before the newest 80-row display window, so it is now measured once. Trims inside that window still measure their own envelope, and the stored weight still equals `JSON.stringify(snapshot).length`.

Not changed: the remaining rebuild of display items over the whole transcript on each page (it existed before the regression). That is the next step: append pages without rebuilding, and bound how much history is held. Not changed on purpose: when a tail refresh (for example a run finishing) lands while an older page is in flight, the page is dropped and the boundary shows "Couldn't load earlier messages" with Retry; the next scroll loads normally. That is the existing designed outcome.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, production bundles.** A private benchmark harness (not committed) drives Playwright Chromium against an isolated real Gateway process: real WebSocket, SQLite and `chat.history` paging, with production UI builds of this head and its base `9172615`. Each arm uses its own worktree and build. Workload: 30,000 messages with realistic content (markdown, code blocks, tables, links, 20–220-line tool results; user → tool call → tool result → reply). Crowded profile: 200 workspace skills, 40 other sessions and live `chat.inject` traffic every 400 ms. Each run makes 25 scroll-up pages (25,080 messages loaded). Runs were interleaved base/cand/cand/base on a shared host with load average 7–20.

| Profile (medians) | base `9172615` (2 runs) | this PR (2 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| Crowded + 4× CPU throttle: wait for pages 1–5 | 942 / 967 ms | 913 / 839 ms |
| Crowded + 4× CPU throttle: wait for pages 21–25 | 3431 / 3273 ms | 1570 / 1617 ms |
| Crowded + 4× CPU throttle: script time per page, pages 21–25 | 3247 / 3036 ms | 1322 / 1370 ms |
| Crowded + 4× CPU throttle: longest task, pages 21–25 | 2578 / 2530 ms | 926 / 1011 ms |
| Unthrottled: wait for pages 21–25 | 756 / 747 ms | 405 / 409 ms |
| Unthrottled: script time per page, pages 21–25 | 650 / 653 ms | 304 / 309 ms |

- **Correctness in every run:** all 25,080 loaded messages present, unique and in source order. A separate 8,000-message crowded run loaded all 8,000 messages in order on both arms. Page sizes and page counts are identical between arms.
- **Snapshot commit (unit-level micro benchmark, 12,000 messages, 256 KB envelope):** 606 ms per commit → 2.2 ms. The retained cache contents are identical to base for all 39 measured commits.
- **Regression tests:** RED on base, GREEN here.
  - Index rebuild after an older prepend hashes less than one loaded message's worth of text, with unchanged revisions. Base hashed 118,213 characters.
  - Trimming 4,000 rows measures the envelope at most twice. Base measured it 984 times.
- **Tests and checks:**
  - All UI tests under `ui/src/pages/chat` and `ui/src/lib/chat` pass: 637 files.
  - The changed test files take 2.8 s and 2.2 s wall time (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`).
  - Existing history browser suites pass against this build: real-Gateway `chat-loading-performance`, plus `chat-history-loading`, `chat-history-prepend-anchor`, `chat-cold-load-anchor`, `chat-flow.history-recovery` and `warm-boot`.
  - `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt and the test-line ratchet pass.
- **Review:** local autoreview (Codex, P0–P3, branch vs `origin/main`) is scoped-clean with no findings.

**Gaps:**
- The live team Gateway was not tested. All Gateway runs used isolated real Gateway processes with synthetic transcripts.
- No mobile device or WebKit runs were done; CPU throttling stands in for a slow device.
- Three harness runs (on both arms) ended with a Gateway child-process cleanup timeout after measurements were complete. This is a host load issue in teardown, not in the measured flow.
- The benchmark harness is not committed.

title: fix(infra): release completed SQLite readers and prevent cursor restarts
body:
Supersedes #184076, thanks @ava-perry.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WAL growth when a completed SQLite reader is stepped again on affected Node bindings; returning an old iterator can also rewind a newer reader using the same statement.

## User Impact

Completed readers release their snapshots, checkpoints can finish, and later iterator calls cannot restart queries or disturb successor readers. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing SQLite observer now returns native iterators on exhaustion and remembers completion after either exhaustion or explicit return. Repeated calls receive a terminal result. Remove the superseded iterator capability experiment and its private worker-admission fields together; retain the loaded-library safety and identity query using one `get()`.

Simplification pass: production **−48 lines**, tests **+18 net lines** against `a11289439ae9`. The removed probe/transport pays for the terminal-state handling. The separate 18-line regression allocation covers real WAL checkpoint progress and preservation of a successor cursor after stale calls, after subtracting obsolete probe fixtures.

## Evidence

- Base `a11289439ae9940e6487c82ef439af80da180571`, Node 24.18.0 / SQLite 3.53.1: new real temp-directory database regressions fail. After exhaustion and another `next()`, PASSIVE checkpoints only **3 of 4 frames**; after explicit return, a stale return rewinds the successor and yields row 1 twice.
- Fixed branch on Node 24.18.0: observer + native runtime suites **79 tests passed**, 5.00s total wrapper wall time. WAL fully checkpoints and TRUNCATE returns `{busy: 0, log: 0}`; the successor yields the remaining rows exactly once.
- Node 26.12.1: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/sqlite-native-observer.test.ts src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts src/state/openclaw-schema-metadata.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-schema-facts.native.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **148 passed**, 44.12s wall time including the initial worker build. Test execution remains under five seconds per file. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41298266266) passed, including all three PostgreSQL shards and `openclaw/ci-gate`; elapsed **1460 seconds** including setup and all jobs.
- Focused TypeScript compilation of the six changed TS files plus canonical ambient declarations, targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. No references to the retired probe or iterator flags remain in `src`.
- Shared autoreview, local candidate against `a11289439ae9`, Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no findings**. It reviewed the supplied complete diff and native Node source; unchanged repository context was unavailable and it did not rerun tests. Subsequent changes only remove an unused type import and record the test allocation.
- Contributor source was read through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; it was never checked out or executed. This is an independently implemented, credited replacement. Production Team services were not modified.

- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190242#issuecomment-6556912819), exact head `1dd1097bd13e`: complete, no actionable findings. It records the same full-Gateway proof limitation.

title: feat(ui): show GitHub avatars in the publication account picker
body:
## Problem

The mobile **Publish as** row and account picker showed initials ("R", "V") instead of the accounts' GitHub avatars. `sessions.github.options` only returned `login` and `accountId`, and the picker deliberately rendered initials rather than build remote image URLs in the browser.

## Solution

- `sessions.github.options` now returns an optional, display-only `avatarUrls: { shared?, personal? }`. The Gateway builds each URL from the verified account ID and **that account's GitHub host**:
  - github.com → `https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/<id>?v=4`
  - GitHub Enterprise (`gateway.github.host`) → `https://<host>/avatars/u/<id>`
  - Personal publication accounts are always github.com.
- The host travels with the options identity (`prepareGitHubPublicationOptionsIdentity` / `configuredAppGitHubOptionsIdentity`). On an Enterprise Gateway, a client-built `avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/<id>` URL would show an unrelated github.com user's avatar.
- `src/shared/github-account-avatar.ts` is now the single URL builder. The profile page's existing GitHub identity projection uses it too, with no behavior change.
- `GitHubPublicationAvatar` renders the image with `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` and falls back to initials when no URL is offered or the image fails to load. The selected-publisher row only uses an image when the recorded publisher matches the offered account ID.
- Selections and publication requests never carry avatar URLs.

## Impact

- Cost: one extra small object in an existing response. No extra GitHub API calls, because the URL derives from the already-verified account ID. Each avatar is one browser image request, cached by the browser.
- Privacy/CSP: same as the profile page's existing GitHub avatar (`img-src https:` is already allowed). The security-model docs note publication account choices and the Enterprise host.
- Protocol: additive optional field; older clients ignore it.

## Screenshots

Built Control UI bundle, mocked Gateway, 393×852, account menu open.

| Before (initials) | After (GitHub avatars) | Fallback (avatar request fails) |

| ![Before: initials in the Publish as row and account menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9803b2d-ef51-4fea-bf16-cbfe76d79a00) | ![After: avatars in the Publish as row and both account menu rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7a646af-48b9-411f-a3b6-58f89ccc9dee) | ![Fallback: avatar 404 falls back to initials](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b4ac794-e3df-4bed-bc70-4cbd1e0e8428) |

title: fix(ui): stop iOS Safari panning the page under the composer while typing
body:
## Problem

In mobile Safari, with the keyboard open in chat, dragging up on the composer or on a thread that's already at its end scrolls the whole page. The view jitters and a blank area shows up under the composer (reported with a screen recording from an iPhone).

**Root cause:** iOS Safari draws the keyboard over the page instead of shrinking the layout viewport, so the area under the keyboard still belongs to the document. When no scroller inside the app takes a vertical drag, Safari pans the *visual* viewport into that area. `connectShellViewport` responds to each `visualViewport` scroll by moving `--shell-viewport-height` (`height + offsetTop`). That update lands one frame after the pan, so the shell keeps chasing the viewport (the jitter) while the unused layout area below it shows through (the blank area). `overflow: clip` / `overscroll-behavior: none` on `html, body` don't help because this is a visual-viewport pan, not a document scroll.

## Solution

The shell viewport owner (`ui/src/app/shell-viewport.ts`) already knows when the keyboard is open. Only during that time it adds one capturing, non-passive `touchmove` guard that cancels a single-finger vertical drag when no scrollable element on the touch's composed path can move in that direction. The guard decides once per gesture, as WebKit locks the gesture to one scroller. It ignores:

- drags an in-app scroller can take (the thread, an overflowing composer textarea, popovers)
- horizontal drags (the nav-drawer swipe) and multi-touch (pinch)
- drags that start after a 300 ms press-and-hold (text selection, caret loupe)
- downward drags while the visual viewport is offset (`offsetTop > 0`). Safari often scrolls the header away to reveal the focused composer; dragging down moves back toward it and only shrinks the shell, so it stays native and the header remains reachable

The guard is removed as soon as the keyboard closes or the owner disconnects, so touch handling stays unchanged the rest of the time.

Accepted edge case: a press-and-hold followed by a drag over bare chrome can still pan. This is rare, visible and recoverable, and is the cost of keeping native selection.

## Evidence

- New unit regression `cancels keyboard-open drags that would pan Safari's visual viewport` in `shell-viewport.test.ts`: **fails on `main`**, passes with the fix. It also covers the offset-viewport case: downward drag stays native, upward drag is cancelled. All 12 tests in the file pass.
- Real Control UI DOM check (temporary Playwright probe, not committed): mocked Gateway, 40-message chat at 390×844 with `isMobile`/`hasTouch`. Focused the composer, shrank `visualViewport` to simulate the keyboard, then sent CDP touch drags:
  - on `main`: `touchmove` was never `defaultPrevented` for any drag
  - with the fix: drags on the composer and up past the thread end are cancelled; drags down and up inside the thread are not, and `.chat-thread` scrolled 4877→4849→4999; after the keyboard closes, nothing is cancelled
- Local autoreview (Codex engine, branch mode, base `bf73e1aa822`, head `006c3c5f3c9` = same tree as `00887c1a06e`, max priority P2): `scoped-clean`, no findings; "patch is correct (0.82)". The reviewer also noted that native iOS selection, navigation and pinch behavior can't be verified with synthetic tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` all clean.

**Gap:** Chromium doesn't pan the visual viewport the way iOS WebKit does, so the jitter itself isn't reproduced here. I tried an iOS Simulator run on a macOS Crabbox, but the machine was still provisioning after ~30 minutes, so I stopped it. A check on a real iPhone in Safari is still needed.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(windows): preserve process identity probes across clock changes
body:
Supersedes #184162, thanks @SunnyShu0925.

Human credit in [replacement commit d31ec002facd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d31ec002facd84d7de5eb6c169bc63fae0a67932): `Co-authored-by: SunnyShu <0668000539@local>`. The native squash policy removed this local-domain address from the landed commit; the original human attribution is retained here and in the replacement commit.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows process identity probes can expire early or run beyond their timeout when the system clock changes during Gateway lifecycle checks.

## User Impact

Windows operators retain the requested process-verification time budget across clock corrections. No configuration, identity format, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `performance.now()` convention for the shared native/PowerShell/WMIC deadline and round remaining subprocess budgets up to integer milliseconds. This is a maintainer-owned reimplementation; the contributor branch was read through GitHub and was never checked out or executed.

Production LOC: +3/-3 (net 0). Regression tests: +23, with a dedicated 23-line allocation protecting both clock-jump directions and fractional subprocess timeouts. Simplification retained only the three owner expressions and one parameterized regression.

## Evidence

- Base: `29526f13194aa8b214a40879b477215f16effad4`. Both new cases fail before the fix: a backward jump grants WMIC 21,000 ms within a 1,000 ms request; a forward jump returns no identity before probing.

The changed file alone completed in 0.664 seconds (1.87 seconds runner wall time); all focused shards completed in 45.08 seconds. [Exact-head broad CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41297453197) passed in 468 seconds.

title: fix: invalid Rewind requests interrupt retained sandbox sessions
body:
Related: #190181

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an invalid Rewind or branch-switch selection can retire a usable managed sandbox, and a real workspace conflict hides its recovery instruction behind an ineffective retry message.

## User Impact

Invalid selections leave the retained runtime and workspace edits untouched. Workspace conflicts explicitly ask users to resolve the conflict before retrying, without exposing internal paths or error text. No schema, configuration, permission, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker, native, and memory adapters preflight through the planner's shared semantic selection before workspace retirement. The final transaction still validates the selection and ownership; preflight is not a reservation. It creates no transcript plan, UUID, or editor payload. A fixed typed workspace-conflict error carries only safe recovery guidance through the handler.

The handoff proof now follows an actual handler-generated persisted receipt through owner resolution and the workspace writer, including refusal at the adoption COMMIT boundary and replay after reopening SQLite. Existing pending-reset and next-cut recovery remain covered.

## Evidence

- Red on base `a3751eaf96`: a missing-message Rewind issued runtime removal before rejection; a genuine canonical/private conflict returned the generic retry instead of the resolution instruction.
- **116 tests passed across 9 files**: 10 managed-workspace cut cases, 4 persisted-handoff/replay cases, 87 handler/storage/memory/native siblings, and 15 direct planner/accounting consumer cases. SQLite, Git, handlers, receipts, and owner decisions are real; container-engine I/O is fixture-backed. The landing owner independently reran the 14 critical cases at the published byte-identical tree; all passed.
- Focused TypeScript check, typed lint on all 9 touched source/test files, formatting, whitespace checks, and the staged test-line ratchet passed.

title: fix: keep managed tool downloads from blocking guest turns

## User Impact

Re-downloadable managed tools stay with their runtime, so downloading them no longer prevents source edits from synchronizing or subsequent turns from starting. The size limit still applies to user files.

title: fix(ui): drop empty sidebar disclosure column
body:
## Problem

#189969 removed the hover condition from the disclosure-slot reserve added in #189906. Since then, every desktop sidebar row that has Archive but no child sessions keeps an empty column (about 30px) on its right edge. Only rows with the `> N` child toggle use that column. On every other row, titles truncate early and PR badges and hover actions sit one slot in from the edge.

## Solution

Remove the `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` block that shifts `.sidebar-recent-session__aside` and pads childless rows by `--sidebar-child-session-toggle-width`. Rows with a child toggle keep their existing rule (actions sit just left of the toggle). Childless rows go back to aligning their title, badges and actions with the row edge. That is the same edge the toggle uses.

## Accepted edge case

#189906 kept Archive away from where a disclosure toggle used to be. If a row's last child is removed while the pointer is resting on its toggle, Archive moves under the pointer. That fix relied on the column this PR removes. We are dropping the guarantee because the case is rare, visible (Archive shows on hover first) and recoverable (sessions can be unarchived). Keeping it costs every row an empty column. Its browser regression is replaced by the alignment regression below.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI E2E, desktop 1280×900, nav width 320, hovered childless row under a parent with `> 1`:

| Before (main) | After |

| ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/099a8f61-c50a-4ba8-bb13-cde9bde50f09) | ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3950d9cb-6c66-4a65-83fb-64f466992dfa) |

title: feat(chat): choose how follow-ups interrupt active work
body:
Related: #57208 (prior interrupt/priority-control context; this PR does not implement pause/resume or drop queued siblings).

**Nov 3 update — prepared locally, not yet published:** two feature repairs and additional authority proof are ready, but the managed publisher refused the base integration because this request lacks full operator write authority for the upstream workflow-file changes. A maintainer with that authority must publish the saved candidate. The branch still points to `fcedbe2a1b07b1557154d53af0b8ea73bb40f6c5`; do not treat the locally prepared evidence below as proof that this remote head is repaired.

## What Problem This Solves

Users need a clear choice between waiting, steering at the next boundary, and interrupting current work for a follow-up, across chat surfaces rather than only in the Control UI.

## User Impact

User impact: choose a personal Queue, Steer, or Interrupt & send default, or promote an already accepted queued message without copying and resending it.

Interrupt requests cancellation immediately but waits for the incumbent writer to settle before the selected input runs. Other queued messages remain queued in order. Explicit per-message/session choices take precedence over the authenticated submitting profile's default, which takes precedence over channel/global defaults. Offline TUI controls remain session-local rather than inventing an authenticated personal profile.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a per-item **Interrupt & send** action and explain the three follow-up modes in the Control UI.
- Route interruption through shared `chat.interrupt` and existing queue/admission owners, promoting the original accepted input rather than cancel-and-resend. Keep input identity, scope/incarnation and current-authority checks, sibling ordering, and writer settlement intact.
- Expose common `/followupmode queue|steer|interrupt|default` and `/interrupt list|<id>` controls through the existing shared command catalog/forwarding paths, including the TUI and native/text-channel command surfaces. Active-run-safe controls do not themselves trigger the personal interrupt default.

This is the interrupt-options feature only; it does not claim to fix the separate lingering-steer or acknowledgment-copy bugs.

Contributor credit: @TheAngryPit. The source commit preserves the verified co-author trailer.

## Evidence

### Locally prepared repair candidate (not on the branch yet)

- Pinned base: `d40aa7c6f2ba70e0c59e244d09a325d25e1457b0`. Conflicts were confined to the append-only method table and generated predicates; upstream methods were retained and validators regenerated from canonical schemas.
- Reproduced the overflow case red: running A, queue B/C/D under cap 2, drop-old, then interrupt C. The live writer was not canceled. The local repair follows canceled predecessor ancestry; the regression and held-writer/sibling cases pass.
- Reproduced another defect red through an actual Gateway: changing the personal default during delayed preparation reclassified an already accepted Queue input as Interrupt. The local repair preserves its accepted RPC timing choice; future inputs still use the new preference.
- Six real isolated-Gateway scenarios passed: RPC and shared-command interruption, a caller lacking session-write access, requester membership revoked across the handler’s actual awaited read, revoked queued-source authority, and the delayed-default regression. Observed provider cancellation/execution effects directly; a revoked source also failed at later execution and a fresh authorized input worked. These use a synthetic HTTP model, not a live provider or native Codex.
- 153 affected queue/command/TUI tests and 105 method-scope/prefix-stability consumer tests passed. Core, root-product-test and TUI-test typechecks passed; targeted lint/format and generated-validator/registry checks passed. Normal commit hooks passed; the hook skipped protocol regeneration for the partial commit index, so that check was run separately on the full candidate.
- Complete candidate Auto Review on the bound OpenClaw route: four completed P0–P2 passes, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Reviewed local source snapshot `1ad2c6e8860ef2102cb8b8bd755059b449504439c20addf423cda3e11f4d1d6f`; full candidate tree `bf78e1f2128e247a732f7876935aa121e385a459`. No source/context truncation or reviewer-route switch.

**Remaining proof:** latest-stable upgrade qualification has NOT run. The normal consumer installation of `openclaw@2026.10.9` was refused by the environment’s seven-day package-age policy. No exception, substitute baseline, schema change, or migration was introduced. This is neither proof of incompatibility nor successful upgrade proof. An operator-approved exception for that exact baseline, or its normal admission, is needed.

<details>
<summary>Investigated proof limitations</summary>

An overbroad post-revocation FIFO assertion also observed unrelated retained owner inputs ending with generic errors after the sharing revision changed. The final security cases isolate their distinct contracts: no cancellation/promotion from denied authority, no provider execution from the revoked source, and a fresh authorized request still works. Survival of other retained inputs across sharing-policy mutations is not qualified or claimed fixed. The prior unforced command-ordering failure led to the deterministic late-default regression and its repair; a passing replay alone was not used as the fix.

</details>

Hosted re-review has not been requested on the old head. Publish this candidate and current proof first, then request re-review.
### Previously published candidate evidence

- **Conflict integration against `6c96aff8e06116c47c796cd770ac1645c0312fd5`:** retained both append-only method additions and regenerated validators from canonical schemas with the refreshed frozen-lockfile dependencies. Re-ran 242 Gateway/command/TUI cases, 109 UI cases, and both real-Gateway synthetic-model flows: all passed. title: fix: keep unrelated system Gateways from blocking Doctor migrations
body:
Fixes #190177. Supersedes #190180 with credit to @Satoshi-Kusumoto for the report and investigation.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can mistake another account's system Gateway for the caller's own state and refuse migration; the same incorrect facts can disrupt Gateway workers.

## User Impact

Caller-owned state can migrate when the older system Gateway is proven to use a different database. Shared or unverified state remains protected across accounts. Unreadable files, failed account/path inspection, manager or PAM selectors, and private filesystem mappings retain the restriction. Relative selectors also retain it rather than resolving against the CLI's working directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the service account's default home through NSS and carry incomplete inspection into the existing migration guard. Compare canonical paths and existing database identities, including symlinks and hard links. The systemd reader collects the extra environment and namespace facts under its existing bounded inspection contract; migrations and worker policy retain their current owners.

Unlike the proposed ownership heuristic in #190180, directory ownership never establishes separate state. This repair must be in the candidate CLI; it does not modify the installed updater, service lifecycle, database schema, or live Gateway.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `42d5039f0aa8`: a foreign service with a different account home falsely refuses migration. The shared-home and explicit-shared-state controls correctly refuse. The same run exposed unsafe allowance after unreadable environment/path inspection: 4 failed, 6 passed.
- Nineteen native-reader-to-migration cases pass. They cover separate/shared roots, explicit selectors, symlink and hard-link aliases, unreadable required/optional environment files, failed NSS/path inspection, manager/PAM sources, private binds, root mappings, and denied namespace inspection. Six new safety controls also failed before the review corrections.
- Final affected CLI/daemon suites: 171 tests passed in six files. The unchanged Doctor schema boundary and worker-owner suites also passed (37 tests); the Doctor suite exercised real isolated migration, backup, and refusal paths.
- Targeted production/test typecheck, seven-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- New test cost: about 0.1 seconds of test execution; the final six-file run took 43.21 seconds, predominantly shared compiler preparation. Exact-head [CI run 41292762491](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41292762491) passed all 42 planned jobs on `5d6fc87645d411a299dc47ea0f3de84608aba01c` (attempt 1; 427 seconds wall time). Per-file CI time was not collected.
- Test-audit/pr-simplify: one boundary regression table, 270 justified test lines recorded in a separate allocation. Production grows by 191 net lines to collect affirmative identity facts and retain uncertainty; no ownership walker, account-match callback, or competing migration policy.
- Independent shared autoreview (Codex, local snapshot against `42d5039f0aa8`, P0–P2): scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The first review found manager environment and private-mount gaps, corrected before the final review and covered by RED/GREEN controls. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the current head is already queued for hosted ClawSweeper review, so no duplicate request was posted.

Only isolated, timeout-wrapped local tests were run on the Team host. No production Gateway, operator state, or protected checkout was touched. A live multi-account upgrade/Gateway run was deliberately not performed under that host constraint. The reporter's live EnvironmentFile contents remain unverified; the reproduction uses synthetic, independently specified service facts.

title: fix(agents): retry ready context-engine turns behind old admissions
body:
Supersedes #172102, thanks @Leon-SK668.

Related: #135628

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ready context-engine turns remaining queued when 16 older unresolved admissions from other sessions fill the bounded retry list.

## User Impact

A successful independent turn can retry the ready backlog through the existing finalizer wake path. Same-session FIFO and engine/plugin isolation remain intact. Historical admissions are retained; retiring them remains separate work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select each session's oldest non-blocked row before filtering for readiness and applying the retry limit, in both the database worker and memory actor. No new timer, queue, configuration, schema, or dependency is needed. Work still relies on existing turn/recovery wake paths.

The two single-use worker selection helpers are folded into the existing command dispatcher, and the SQL-filtered, unreachable blocked-row branch is removed. Production delta: +38/-39, net -1. Regression tests add 30 lines; their dedicated test-line allocation covers starvation and non-ready FIFO heads.

## Evidence

- RED on current-main base `3e253689582b00fa7b2e7b0f7f11a3ffd3add1f5`: the real finalizer commits only the current session, skipping the ready backlog behind 16 admissions. The worker negative control reads two non-ready heads; the memory selector also exposes non-ready work.
- GREEN: 54 tests passed in 75.85 s across two focused shards (40.82 s memory, 32.10 s agents; cold compilation dominates memory startup), including unchanged-row and no-dispatch assertions for non-ready heads. Exact command: `pnpm test src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-attempt.test.ts src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-actor-memory-side-effects.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

title: fix: managed sandbox turns fail after Rewind
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: resending or retrying a message fails before the model starts after Stop → Rewind in a managed local sandbox. Branch switching has the same ownership gap.

## User Impact

Users can change local conversation history and continue with the same private checkout and saved edits. Foreign session incarnations remain rejected. This change does not deploy or rewrite any affected live session.

## Why This Change Was Made

History cuts must still rotate transcript identity to fence stale writers. The workspace owner now settles source edits and retires old runtime writers first, then records a private, bounded handoff receipt atomically with the cut. Fresh successor authority can finish that exact transfer after interruption without recreating the checkout or discarding its baseline/recovery state. A subsequent cut or reset consumes an earlier pending handoff before replacing its receipt.

Existing SQLite, reconciliation-lease, checkpoint, and runtime-retirement owners are reused; there is no new table or manager. Necessary growth is +247 net production lines and +233 regression lines.

## Evidence

Together with reset/memory/compound-worker siblings: 41 tests passed across 4 files.

title: fix(macos): recover companion Gateway after an in-place app update

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `GatewayAutostartPolicy` for stale-service eligibility and retain the companion's `--allow-unconfigured` installation flag. No new lifecycle owner or configuration is introduced.

The legacy managed-Node exclusion is deliberate: `ManagedNodeGatewayMigration` separately owns version updates and same-version Node-to-Bun migration. This early bundled-service replacement must not bypass that migration policy or the user's runtime choice. Legacy Node startup recovery is unchanged by this fix.

title: fix(cron): warn when editing command env drops stored variables
body:
Supersedes #171824, thanks @JoernHoppe.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: editing an automation with `--command-env` silently removes stored variables omitted from the new set.

## User Impact

The CLI now names dropped keys on stderr after a successful edit, without printing their values. Help and docs explain that every variable to retain must be repeated. Whole-map replacement is unchanged; the diagnostic is best effort if the stored job cannot be read. Successful reads use the existing configuration-revision precondition.

## Why This Change Was Made

The documented command environment overrides do not promise merge semantics. Keeping replacement avoids changing how callers remove variables. The existing edit owner compares keys using its cached job read; no new helper, flag, or update owner is needed.

The simplification replaces repeated command-field assignments and redundant checks on Commander boolean flags. Production code is net **-3 lines**, tests +121, docs +2, test routing/budget records +3. The dedicated 121-line test allocation funds one regression through real CLI registration, Gateway handlers, and persisted cron edits.

## Evidence

- On current main `4475bed8cf500c9be80257b2f142c1136bd9dfbd`, the new regression confirms the omitted key is removed from storage, then fails because stderr lacks its name.

title: fix(mcp): preserve requester identity for CLI tool policies
body:
Supersedes #171791, thanks @alkor2000.
Closes #170576.

## What Problem This Solves

Owner-aware tool policies reject legitimate CLI-backed MCP calls because the original requester's identity is lost before policy evaluation.

## User Impact

Policy plugins receive the host-verified sender, channel, account, role, and ownership facts for CLI-backed tool calls. Unknown or absent identity remains unproven. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing harness requester projection, captured CLI grant, and tool-hook context. Inline the grant builder's two redundant session-key and elevated-default forwarding helpers; production code decreases by 6 lines overall.

Security note: requester identity comes only from the host-prepared run. MCP headers and tool arguments cannot assert sender, agent, or ownership. Attach grants and generic bearer callers acquire no requester identity. Requester-origin provenance and the live grant checks after awaited policy execution remain intact.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41284797823) passes, with 501 seconds workflow elapsed. The changed-node CI job takes 308 seconds across its selected contracts (not a per-file timing). The [combined CI/security gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41285360806) also passes.

- On main `4475bed8cf500c9be80257b2f142c1136bd9dfbd`, the six real HTTP requester-policy controls produce 3 intended failures (owner denied; guest and unknown-ownership metadata absent) and 3 passing denial controls. Baseline wrapper: 49.15 seconds.
- After the fix, all 97 tests in the MCP HTTP, grant-store, and CLI grant-builder suites pass (66.58 seconds wrapper). The six requester cases take 44 ms combined and cover forged headers and tool arguments, missing identity, unknown ownership, attach grants, and a generic owner bearer. Final grant-builder replay: 15 pass in 6.37 seconds wrapper.
- The CLI preparation/grant-transfer case passes (83.89 seconds wrapper; 111 unrelated cases filtered). The existing worker compiler dominates cold-run wall time; the HTTP owner boundary requires a real listener, capture, admission, and hook dispatch. Tool policy and tool effects are synthetic; no separately launched Gateway, vendor CLI/API, live channel, or deployment proof is claimed.
- Focused production/test import-closure typecheck, six-file typed lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Test growth is 101 lines, allocated in a dedicated record for the six HTTP security controls and existing preparation expectation; the shared baseline is unchanged. Broad proof and CI timings come from this replacement PR's CI.
- Independent Codex autoreview: `scoped-clean`, complete local candidate against main `4475bed8cf500c9be80257b2f142c1136bd9dfbd`, P0–P2, including unchanged requester projection, HTTP authentication/dispatch/cache, and policy bridge context; no findings. The reviewed snapshot matches the submitted source.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` and was never checked out, installed, built, or run. This is a separately implemented replacement, retaining human credit in the commit.

title: fix(memory-wiki): preserve cache publications on unchanged compiles
body:
Supersedes #171166, thanks @alkor2000.
Related: #168784.

## What Problem This Solves

An explicit Memory Wiki compile replaces and deletes its accepted cache publication even when the vault and compiled output have not changed.

## User Impact

Repeated unchanged compiles preserve the publication ID, persisted row, metadata, and bytes. Changed sources or output, missing rows, and corrupt rows still trigger replacement. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing publication writer validates the persisted predecessor before deciding to reuse it. The compiler supplies its already captured source-identity comparison while holding the existing vault mutation lock. Prompt reads keep their existing warm cache.

The replacement adds no reuse wrapper or snapshot-builder extraction. Production grows by 23 lines because persisted validation, cancellation, and owner continuity are needed; there is no equivalent dead code in this owner area to remove safely. Regression tests grow by 54 lines, with a matching allocation for the real compiler/SQLite boundary coverage.

title: fix(database): Team Reports fails to port to PostgreSQL after a successful dry run
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes database port failing before it can record a recovery manifest when a profile contains Team Reports data, even though dry-run succeeds.

## User Impact

Operators can port populated Team Reports to PostgreSQL, resume interrupted publication, and return it to SQLite without renaming existing PostgreSQL schemas or losing retained rows. No schema, configuration, permission, or durability policy changes; SQL quoting and custody checks remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

Team Reports already generates a quoted namespace containing `team-reports`. Anchor and recovery validation now share the restricted native-name contract, including that hyphen, while still rejecting quotes, statement separators, dots, and NUL. Catalog comparison normalizes the quoted namespace qualifier PostgreSQL emits in index definitions so the real schema and temporary reference compare equally. Existing namespaces are not renamed.

## Evidence

Complete fix: forward dry-run and port exit 0; reverse dry-run and port exit 0. Retained `started_at_ms=9007199254740993` verified in PostgreSQL and returned SQLite as exact int64. Other SQLite families remain out of scope.
- **Regression red/green:** original anchor validation fails both new original/intended cases (17 existing passed, 2 new failed); repaired validation passes all 19. Removing only catalog qualifier repair makes the new real PostgreSQL Team Reports command regression fail; restoring it passes interrupted publication → resume (same anchor namespace) → SQLite return with int64 row preserved.

| [src/snapshot/database-backup.operations.ts:220-282](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/snapshot/database-backup.operations.ts#L220-L282) | Every namespace/source interpolation in restore/config/update SQL use imported `quote`; state keys and selected-key lists remain bound values. |

| [src/infra/postgres-sync/bridge.worker.ts:158-185](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/postgres-sync/bridge.worker.ts#L158-L185) | Adapter namespace handoff becomes a double-quoted/doubled identifier, passed as a bound `set_config('search_path', $3, false)` value. |
| [src/infra/database-engine/agent-port-descriptor.ts:77-84](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/agent-port-descriptor.ts#L77-L84), [src/infra/database-engine/agent-port-descriptor.ts:128-137](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/agent-port-descriptor.ts#L128-L137), [src/infra/database-engine/agent-port-descriptor.ts:233-239](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/agent-port-descriptor.ts#L233-L239) | Descriptor metadata SQL uses `pgSearchName(source.namespace)`; generated search callbacks delegate to `postgresSearchSql`. Its [src/infra/database-engine/postgres-search-schema.ts:10-10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/postgres-search-schema.ts#L10-L10) identifier owner doubles quotes. |

The shared imported `quoteSqliteIdentifier` owner is [src/infra/sqlite-schema-sql.ts:180-182](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/sqlite-schema-sql.ts#L180-L182): it wraps identifiers in double quotes and doubles embedded quotes, also valid for these PostgreSQL identifiers. `physical-store.ts` only reads/classifies anchors. Port-provider, orchestration, publication-context and backup facade/worker references pass recorded namespace facts to these SQL owners; they do not build another namespace SQL expression. Diagnostic messages, manifest/config identity fields, descriptor call arguments and catalog JSON/hash namespace replacement were classified separately as **non-SQL**, not counted as quoting evidence. No unquoted namespace identifier was found in the stated SQL scope.

### Why in-place catalog normalization has exclusive local ownership

[src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:403-414](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L403-L414) issues a new native Client query for that invocation, reads its JSON catalog, validates it, then `.filter(...)` creates a **new local facts array**. No cache, shared projection or retained other consumer receives the array or its elements. Before normalization, `some` and the filtered structural comparison inspect it; the separate invalid-index/constraint query does not receive `facts`. [src/infra/database-engine/postgres-catalog.ts:65-100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/postgres-catalog.ts#L65-L100) validates/serializes for equality without retaining inputs. Only after those checks does [src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:452-463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ee44e487d25fcdddaa785c495b60d97f538a694/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L452-L463) replace each local fact's value and return the array to its caller.

Dependency ownership was also inspected, not inferred from the `filter` alone: installed `pg@8.23.1` client.js:687 creates a new Query for the string query; query.js:28 constructs a new Result; result.js:15 initializes `rows = []`. The installed pg-types text parser registers `JSON.parse` for JSON/JSONB (textParsers.js:202–203). `withPostgresConnection` constructs this ordinary Client without a custom row/parser cache. Thus the parsed catalog fact objects are fresh for this call too, not just a fresh array over cached shared objects. Normalization mutates that private result only; it does not weaken definition comparison or SQL quoting.

</details>

Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm).

title: fix(voice-call): guide ongoing errands into call briefs
body:

## User Impact

The initiating model is told to put the ongoing task in `brief.task` and keep `message` as the verbatim opening. This clarifies an existing capability; no API, defaults, or permissions change. Improved model selection or live-call outcomes are not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The per-call brief introduced in #165716 already reaches both realtime speech and agent consultation. Its instructions explicitly govern the conversation after the opening. The remaining discovery gap is the tool's "Intro message" description. Replace that description with a single instruction and align the existing documentation sentence.

title: fix(gateway): honor TLS when probing configured SSH endpoints
body:
Supersedes #171105, thanks @zhangguiping-xydt.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a healthy configured TLS Gateway reporting a failed SSH probe because the diagnostic sends plaintext WebSocket traffic through its tunnel.

## User Impact

Configured TLS Gateways can be probed over their matching SSH route, retaining the endpoint's certificate identity and URL path. No configuration migration or new option is required.

Security note: SSH forwarding does not bypass TLS verification. A saved fingerprint remains enforced before the WebSocket upgrade; without a pin, normal CA and hostname verification remain enabled. Other SSH targets, remote ports, and configured direct transports do not inherit the endpoint's TLS settings. SSH host-key policy is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The probe retains the configured endpoint only when the existing route resolver identifies the selected SSH target and remote port. The existing Gateway client owns forwarding-address substitution and TLS validation. The diagnostic reports the canonical TLS endpoint; its tunnel metadata still records the allocated local port.

Production delta is **+28/-22, net +6**. Removed duplicate origin-scoping branches, redundant default-port handling, nested local-certificate selection, and duplicated result assembly in the same command owner. The remaining growth binds the configured TLS endpoint to its SSH route; no parallel TLS implementation was added. The explicit async result type is retained because closure writes otherwise cause incorrect null-only inference.

## Evidence

- Red on main `e0ed68c7b845b240221e289c1160b5dddced5945`: the seven-case regression has four TLS failures and three passing route exclusions. Matching-pin probes report `socket hang up`; wrong-pin and CA cases never reach TLS verification.
- Green: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/gateway-status.tls.test.ts src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **37 passed**, 36.83 s wall time, including 259 ms for the seven transport cases. Wrong fingerprints report a mismatch and untrusted certificates reject without a WebSocket connection. Tunnels close after each diagnostic.
- Targeted tsgo, type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. [Broad PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41278561812) passed on `7634599046adf1313070ff6f072915c3df1d19c7` (452 s wall; the four changed-test jobs used 570 s combined). Per-test CI timing is unavailable.
- Local autoreview: P0–P2, base `e0ed68c7b845b240221e289c1160b5dddced5945`, complete local candidate and unchanged transport/route owners supplied; **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The original async return annotation was subsequently restored to satisfy the targeted linter; runtime behavior is identical.
- The **200-line** regression allocation covers the public command, real TLS/WebSocket traffic through a real TCP forwarder, trust rejection, route exclusions, and cleanup. OpenSSH process startup is substituted; SSH authentication and a full Gateway/model boot were not exercised. Contributor code was read through GitHub only and was never checked out or executed.

Human contributor credit: `Co-authored-by: zhang-guiping <zhang.guiping@xydigit.com>`.

title: fix(ui): stop chat retries when scroll anchoring makes no progress
body:
