title: fix(ui): match mobile browser chrome to the session chat surface
body:
## Problem

On narrow screens (iPhone Safari), the status-bar band at the top and the band behind Safari's bottom toolbar are a different shade than the chat. Measured on a real iPhone capture with the Absolutely dark theme: chat `#1f1f1e`, bands `#1b1b1a`. Every built-in palette has the same mismatch (e.g. Claw light `#f4f4f4` chat vs `#f8f8f8` bands).

Cause: `syncControlUiSystemChrome` publishes `--bg-content` for every narrow chat-like route (`shell--chat`), both into `<meta name="theme-color">` and into the `html`/`body` canvas Safari shows in the safe areas. The mobile session workbench (`.sidebar-region--mobile-host`, `--chat-surface: var(--bg)`) paints `--bg` over that canvas, so the chrome no longer matched what it borders. Only `/new` and `systems` still leave the shell's `--bg-content` canvas visible at the edges.

The generic mobile `.content` rule also adds a 4px top inset above the session workbench. Desktop chat has none. That inset showed the shell canvas as a thin strip under the status bar. It was hidden only because the band above it was the same wrong color.

## Fix

- `app-host` marks the narrow layout as exposing the content canvas only for chat-like routes without a mounted session workbench (`content--workbench`). Session routes now publish `--bg`, the surface they paint. `/new` and `systems` keep `--bg-content`. The flag and its root class are renamed (`chatShell`/`control-ui-chat-shell` → `contentCanvas`/`control-ui-content-canvas`) to match that meaning.
- theme-color now receives resolved colors (`resolveThemeColor`) instead of raw palette expressions. Named themes derive `--bg` with `color-mix()`, which was being written verbatim into the meta tag.
- The narrow session workbench drops the generic 4px mobile top inset (`padding-top: 0`, as on desktop chat), so its header meets the system chrome without a seam. My first version painted the workbench instead. `theme-background.e2e` rejected that because it put an opaque layer over shell theme artwork, so the inset is removed and nothing is painted.

## Impact

The top and bottom browser bands on mobile session chat now match the chat surface in every built-in light and dark theme. Desktop, settings, `/new` and `systems` publish the same chrome colors as before; only the format changed (resolved hex instead of `color-mix()`).

## Evidence

Synthetic fixture captures, 393×852, iPhone safe areas emulated (`--safe-area-top: 59px`, `--safe-area-bottom: 34px`):

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Absolutely dark | ![before absolutely dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f49204f-0395-462e-9035-1567446e2f4b) | ![after absolutely dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d6104bf-6595-4a94-9e70-84c264de9ef0) |
| Claw light | ![before claw light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f35d5c8-6686-4a71-a216-de2f9cf58158) | ![after claw light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c6dbac5-8c2b-4ae9-92a2-58e7b69f937d) |

Pixel column x=5, before → after: absolutely dark `#1b1b1a` band / `#1f1f1e` chat → uniform `#1f1f1e`; claw light `#f8f8f8` / `#f4f4f4` → uniform `#f4f4f4`. Published theme-color: `#1b1b1a` → `#1f1f1e`, `#f8f8f8` → `#f4f4f4`.

- **Regression (red on base, green on fix):** `theme-surfaces.e2e` now asserts at 390px that theme-color, `html`, `body` and the top-edge painted surface all equal the mobile chat host background. On the base commit it failed for claw light/dark and absolutely light/dark at exactly this assertion.
- **Consumer contracts updated:** `theme-typography.e2e` ("keeps system chrome with the mounted route", "publishes a runtime palette…") now expects the page surface on session routes and the content canvas on `/new`. `control-ui-presentation.test.ts` was renamed only.
- **Green on fix (Chromium, bundled UI e2e):** theme-surfaces, theme-typography, theme-background (shell artwork), mobile-chat-header, mobile-shell-geometry, chat-mobile-latest-clearance, mobile-sheet-motion: 7 files, all passing. Unit: `control-ui-presentation.test.ts` 5/5.
- **Checks:** oxfmt, stylelint, oxlint on touched files, and `pnpm tsgo:ui` all clean.
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main` at `9fbf19b`, max priority P1: `scoped-clean`, no findings. The reviewer noted that unchanged source was not supplied.

Not covered here: real-device iOS Safari verification of the new build. Chromium does not report safe-area insets, so the captures emulate them through the app's `--safe-area-*` tokens. `/new` keeps its existing top edge, where its topbar (≈`--bg`) meets a `--bg-content` chrome band; that pre-existing mismatch is left for a follow-up.

title: fix(cron): prevent overlapping retries after execution timeouts
body:
Supersedes #137274, thanks @xydigitLybnnnn.

Related: #137215.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes overlapping executions when a cron job times out but its original runner continues past the retry deadline.

## User Impact

Timeout retries remain enabled and wait for the original execution to settle. Late completion preserves the single recorded timeout outcome. No public API, configuration, or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker-owned finalizer now retains the active receipt while recording the timeout, then finishes only that receipt after the underlying execution settles. The scheduler owns the subsequent refresh, and startup recovery reuses the recorded outcome.

The older settlement module was removed by #169946, so this is an independent repair of the current owner. The contributor branch was read with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed.

## Evidence

- On main `028723cde2165962d8489b2548e74efaf18e6de3`, the initial fake-timer reproduction started the runner twice while the first execution remained held. The final one-shot and recurring regressions both fail on that unmodified main because the active receipt is prematurely released.
- With the repair: 102 tests across seven focused cron files passed (63.22s total command wall time). After the final scheduler-wake adjustment, all 40 affected tests in the watchdog, receipt-finalization, and worker-finalization files passed again (69.35s including compilation). The regressions preserve retry eligibility with rejected or stalled cleanup, fence execution until settlement, and retain one timeout plus one successful retry. Recovery coverage confirms no second accounting pass after restart.
- The initial CI found six TypeScript narrowing errors introduced by this repair. The correction makes the receipt required at the shared recovery operation; an explicit type check of the worker module passes, as do all 25 tests in the affected watchdog/recovery suites. The earlier local test-import graph did not reach that worker module. Changed-file lint, formatting, assertion-safety, max-lines and whitespace checks passed. The local test-line ratchet exceeded its 120s host budget; its exact-head CI check passed. The allocation records exactly 115 added regression lines.
- Fresh autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) found no actionable findings on the final staged tree `94b655267fb466152564e47e4407e291333cd26c`. A fresh P0–P3 review of the type correction also found no actionable findings. These were static reviews; runtime proof is recorded separately.
- Compatibility: no schema, stored format, migration, or status-enum change. Existing legacy-history recovery and receipt admission/retirement tests passed; the new restart regression preserves job settings and history while settling a recorded timeout. The advisory hosted review requests a latest-stable upgrade run; that operational proof was not run under this task's focused-test-only host constraint. The storage-boundary proof covers the changed lifecycle, with that limitation explicit.
- Candidate: `23805358a80b237f122c1452ed48c28744d6a1d6`. All required exact-head CI passed in [run 41213153484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41213153484), including production/test types, baseline ratchets, tests, lint, and security checks. Merged as `7caee827c5be71496b5f3ab8dcc6eee559b7db83`. No production Gateway or live state was modified.

<details>
<summary>Scope and tradeoff</summary>

Production net +43 lines; regression tests net +115; allocation +2. Removed obsolete host mixed-deferred batch splitting and unused finalizer options in the same owner, plus the superseded marker-retirement recovery fallback. The remaining growth carries execution settlement into the worker-owned receipt lifecycle and preserves accounting idempotency; the zero-growth target was not reached.

A runner that never settles keeps its own job fenced. Failed asynchronous receipt settlement logs a warning and leaves the receipt for startup recovery rather than admitting overlapping work.

</details>

title: fix(ui): keep the mobile composer open while a draft waits
body:
## Problem

On the mobile Control UI, typing a message and then leaving the composer (tapping the transcript, a header button, etc.) collapses it to the one-line resting capsule even though there's an unsent draft. The draft gets cut off on one line, and the +, permission, context, model and effort controls disappear until you tap back into the editor.

The cause: the resting one-line layout in `ui/src/styles/chat/composer-mobile.css` (and the `data-composer-layout="single-line"` textarea reset) applied whenever the composer wasn't being edited, without checking whether a draft existed.

## Solution

Built on the restored in-composer layout from #189454. While editing, the composer is the full surface with its controls row inside it, below the text. At rest, it's the one-line capsule.

- `chat-composer-mobile-interaction.tsx` now owns one presentation fact, `mobileResting`: the mobile composer is resting only when it isn't being edited **and** its visible draft is empty.
- `chat-composer-view.tsx` sets `data-composer-resting` on the shell from that fact, and also drives `data-composer-layout="single-line"` from it, so the textarea reset follows the same rule.
- `composer-mobile.css`: the existing one-line rules are keyed on `[data-composer-resting="true"]` instead of `[data-composer-editing="false"]`. This is a straight selector swap with the same specificity and no new rules.

With a draft waiting, the composer keeps the full editing surface, with the controls row inside it. An empty composer still rests as the capsule. `data-composer-editing` and `onComposerEditingChange` still report real editing, so keyboard handling and mobile-host panel suspension don't change. Nothing from #189264's raised toolbar comes back.

CSS size: 309,275 B gzip / 1,598,970 B raw, slightly below main (309,341 / 1,599,255), so the budget is unchanged.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI at 390×844 (touch, DPR 2) on the current head. Current main is the "before". The flow types a draft, then taps the transcript:

| Before (main): draft collapsed to one line, controls hidden | After: draft keeps the open composer, controls inside | After: empty composer still rests as the capsule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f8c716d-3dda-4937-a2a3-31cf6ec2a452) | ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e86be545-6813-4a03-97c0-f7e25e98734a) | ![after empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35ef5433-f9e8-4408-9aa0-be3f8cdb6100) |

States recorded by the same Playwright flow:

| | `editing` | `layout` | toolbar |

title: fix(ui): restore the two-bolt Ultrafast look as one icon
body:
## Problem

#184760 replaced the Ultrafast indicator (two stacked `zap` icons with a `drop-shadow` gap) with a single `zapDouble` SVG. That made it one icon, but changed the look: softer rounded bolts, a different overlap, and a white-mixed palette.

## Solution

Keep `zapDouble` as a single SVG, but rebuild it from the original geometry:

- **Front bolt:** the regular `zap` polygon at the old 2px/4px offset. The viewBox is `27.43 × 30.86`, which is the old 16×18 box in zap units.
- **Rear bolt:** a precomputed path made from the stroked `zap` outline minus the front bolt and its old `-0.8px/-0.6px` gap. The separation is real transparency, so it works on any background. It needs no mask, no `id`, and no background-colored outline. The rear bolt has `stroke="none"` because the stroke is already baked into its outline.
- **Colors:** the icon now carries the original theme-aware mixes as its own defaults: `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 60%, var(--muted))` for the rear bolt and `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 75%, var(--text-strong))` for the front. `--icon-secondary` and `--icon-primary` remain overrides. The unchecked speed option still mutes the icon. The checked option resets both vars to `initial`, so it falls back to the icon's own colors. The composer trigger no longer needs any color CSS.

The unused `SOFT_ZAP_PATH` is removed. Raw CSS shrinks compared with `main`. An earlier head grew it by 129 B and failed `control-ui-performance`; moving the colors into the icon fixed that.

## Evidence

Screenshots, including mobile at 390×844: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189443#issuecomment-6544631018

- **Visual comparison:** a temporary Control UI e2e scenario (mock Gateway, session `fastMode: "ultrafast"`, dark and light) rendered the composer trigger and the effort/speed menu. It also rendered a same-page comparison of the pre-#184760 two-icon composition, current `main`, and this PR, at 1×, 2× and 5×. This PR matches the pre-#184760 shape and colors in both themes.
- **Mobile:** a scenario at 390×844 and 3× scale rendered the gauge badge with this PR's icon and with `main`'s. The thinner stroke used by the badge is not visible at this size.
- **Current head:** a re-check found the trigger and the checked option both resolve to the intended mixes. Dark: rear `rgb(210 112 116)`, front `rgb(252 130 130)`. Light: rear `rgb(151 79 67)`, front `rgb(150 60 45)`. 2/2 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the touched files.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: feat: prepare retained repository disks for explicit operations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Explicit repository operations could not prepare a paused retained disk, and an interrupted Move requiring a newer worker runtime stayed held even when the original disk remained intact.

Depends on #189346, now landed as `632dced4affb7a338d0def2b7059c246ed33b0af`. This PR targets **main** and preserves the actual landed authority, current-disk I/O, Move and lifecycle prerequisites. Related: #188796.

## User Impact

For an already-bound retained repository, explicit reads, edits, downloads, fresh publication captures and Move use the existing lifecycle owner to await the original node and current runtime. Selected publication snapshots remain immutable: retries neither wake the disk nor recapture later edits, and preserve the landed checkpoint-alias recovery path.

**Disk mode remains unselectable.** Ordinary mirrored sessions and turn admission are unchanged. This child adds no schema, config selector, queue, manager, provider allocation or public protocol. Failed wake preserves durable Move custody for retry; it never substitutes an older mirror or replacement disk. No deployment or controller adoption is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Editor preparation stays inside session/workspace exclusion and precedes result claiming. Downloads retain read authority through preparation and every byte window.
- Move intent and result custody own wake before quiescence. Already-quiesced Move capture does not refresh its native owner. One exact-disk/result predicate serves host refresh admission, native validation and settlement; mirrored Moves, other targets and replaced disks remain refused.
- Runtime refresh preserves the original epoch, disk, pending result and placement. Current requester authority reaches awaited installation and the receipt-writing effect; revocation grants no new turn or input replay.
- The implementation removes a separate pre-drain wake path and reuses existing lifecycle, result and queue owners. Separate measured test allocations are **546** for consumer/recovery contracts, **4** for the Stop fixture isolation/assertion repair, and **6** for the required fixture-contract repair; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Current Candidate and Integration

Signed head **`809b06042d014e178fcd1739577edc678ed13d87`**, tree **`fe9ae23ba585c2af838b49a9a45e6e40059febcc`**: **33 files, +766/−54**, published to this same PR through the native workflow.

The native baseline preserves original hosted `a1b4e4ffe765382bf6137a18fd278e64c3a9c90b` ancestry and actual landed lifecycle `632dced4`. Twenty-four exact conflict resolutions preserve current main for unchanged inherited owners and the qualified child content for S8. Twenty-eight original child blobs match previously qualified `1c0f0225` exactly; the remaining two compose landed checkpoint-alias recovery and current main's test inventory. No unsigned prerequisite side-history or signature override was used.

The integration's three-file repair was **+6/−5**: retain the reviewed isolated Git root and no-recovery-error assertion for Stop, retain its separate allocation, and remove five obsolete pre-poll rejection lines reintroduced by historical replay. The provider readiness module is again byte-identical to landed main and adds no child production delta. The subsequent fixture-only CI repair is recorded below.

## Evidence

### Current integrated source

- **24 boundary cases across three files passed**: repository snapshot/alias recovery, paused retained I/O and revocation, and runtime/Stop recovery. Vitest **339.55s**, wrapper **362s**; cold transformation accounted for 75% of Vitest time, including a 139.225s worker compilation. These are real transport/Git/state-owner paths with synthetic provider, pairing and bundle acknowledgments—not live cloud proof.

Complete accounting: 65 success, 25 skipped, two failed. This was a PR-caused test-contract omission, not infrastructure.
- Signed repair `809b0604` adds an explicit throwing method to both checkpoint fixtures plus an exact six-line allocation: **three files, +8, no production or assertion changes**. The exact failed typecheck reproduced both TS2741 errors before repair and passed afterward. Both affected materialization/publication-handoff files passed **28 cases**, Vitest **268.56s**, wrapper **276s**. title: fix(discord): serve live mentions ahead of recovery backlog
body:
Supersedes #121204, thanks @emeric-dandelion-cult. Human commit-author credit is retained for @gloss-dandelion-cult.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: live Discord mentions wait behind old ambient messages after Gateway recovery because each old message must finish preflight before the channel lane advances.

## User Impact

Recent native bot mentions take priority over pending recovery chatter, while ambient messages still reach normal preflight and history recording. A live turn can start before the remaining ambient context is recorded. Active claims and retry backoff can still delay a mention. Pattern-only mentions, replies without a native bot mention, and DMs retain their existing scheduling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ingress drain now accepts an optional pending-message priority predicate. Discord prefers guild messages with a native bot mention sent within the last 15 minutes. Snapshot order stays stable within each priority, and original indices retain retry eligibility. Normal claim validation and access policy still own delivery. There are no new configuration settings or schema/retention changes.

Production delta: **+15 lines** (+30/-15). Simplified redundant dispatch return-type plumbing in the same drain owner; remaining growth supplies the priority hook and Discord predicate. This replaces the proposed pre-claim expiry/inventory machinery with scheduling only, preserving ambient history.

## What Problem This Solves

title: fix: stop retrying exhausted unadopted channel messages
body:
Supersedes #124337, thanks @karmafeast.

**Withdrawn: this narrow replacement is unsafe without the broader cancellation cutover. Nothing was merged.**

## What Problem This Solves

The proposed shared-owner change bounds genuine pre-adoption abandonment, which still bypasses retry exhaustion on main.

## User Impact

No shipped change. The proposal would also dead-letter explicitly cancelled queued messages at the retry threshold because reply cancellation still reaches `onAbandoned`. It must not be deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared drain's direct abandonment release increments attempts but never consults the existing failure disposition. The proposed handoff fixes that defect, but retaining the drain's `onCancelled` callback is insufficient: `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` drops it, and `abortSessionControllerInput` invokes abandonment during explicit cancellation. Shared debounce, dedupe settlement, and channel-owned lifecycle wrappers also need a complete cancellation contract. That broader cutover is outside this task's bounded shared-owner-only takeover scope; #124337 is not being ported wholesale.

The useful part remains the shared retry-policy handoff and its exhaustion regression, conditional on completing cancellation propagation. Deliberate queue-cap drops remain the separate scope of #182252.

## Evidence

- **Original defect confirmed on main:** Telegram's production ingress monitor and SQLite queue, with a 25-hour-old message and seven prior failures, left the failed ledger empty after the eighth abandonment on `c504abf10afa`. The determining shared owner was also unchanged at `338de6d69998`.
- **Proposed fix:** the same Telegram regression passed; all 23 Telegram ingress tests and 38 shared drain/retry-policy tests passed. Wall times: 46.18 and 42.83 seconds, including worker compilation. Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- **Introduced regression reproduced:** a separate focused probe used real `createChannelIngressDrain` → `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` → `enqueueFollowupRun` → `clearFollowupQueue`, with the existing drain policy `maxAttempts: 1, deadLetterMinAgeMs: 0`. Clearing the queue returned 1; the row then entered the failed ledger with `reason: retry-limit-exceeded` and `message: turn-abandoned`. The identical probe **passed with main's drain restored**, leaving the message pending/replayable. Candidate probe: 12.47 seconds; main control: 36.78 seconds including compilation. This disproves the original statement that retaining the drain callback alone preserves reply cancellation.
- **Review:** Codex autoreview with full owner/caller context reported scoped-clean at P0–P2. Hosted ClawSweeper then identified the P1 cancellation regression; it was verified rather than dismissed. [Review and evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189393#issuecomment-6543596613).
- **Scope:** proposed production +16/-18 (**-2 lines**), regression +48, allocation +2; landed delta **0**. No settings, migrations, dependency changes, or deployment.
- Only trusted main and this independently implemented candidate were run locally. The contributor branch was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and never checked out or executed. No production Gateway or live channel/model was used.

CI completion is recorded in the closure comment; its outcome does not override the reproduced cancellation regression.

title: fix(telegram): show typing while detached children work
body:
Supersedes #134148, thanks @samiralibabic.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram looks idle after a requester yields while its detached child is still working.

## User Impact

Telegram keeps showing typing on the originating account, chat, and topic while an announcement-producing child runs. Quiet children and `typingMode: never` stay silent. Completion, errors, abort claims, requester reset/deletion/rebinding, revoked authority, and Gateway replacement stop further typing. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Gateway lifecycle typing/keepalive owner rather than adding Telegram progress hooks, a second controller, reference counts, or another expiry policy. Registration retains its original requester capability and a predicate over the canonical requester session identity and delivery state; the existing guarded transport rechecks those facts immediately before each send. A route changed before preparation is rejected, and the target is never redirected to a replacement session or chat.

The bridge is cosmetic and best effort, with the existing configured cadence and command timeout budget. It applies to currently registered public-completion children; it does not reconstruct typing after a process restart or expose internal/collector work.

## Evidence

- Regression on unchanged main production code: registered active children produced zero typing sends (expected originating routes); the same regression passes with the bridge.
- Focused production-registration/typing/session-publication tests: 12 passed, including seven lifetime/scoping cases and five existing registration-authority cases. New regression cases take about 7–8 seconds combined; total focused command wall time about 49 seconds including cold worker compilation. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41202350510) passed: 51 successful jobs, 27 skipped; 515 seconds elapsed and 7,237 aggregate job-seconds (shared CI, not per-file test cost).
- Tests retain the real lifecycle typing owner and current session publication; only the final platform transport is substituted. Reset, rebinding, and revocation are exercised while a send is suspended before its final authority check.
- Targeted typecheck passed in rootless Podman capped at 4 CPUs/8 GB; focused lint, formatting, both line ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Autoreview (Codex, local candidate, P0–P2), base `11a8498a17ea959adf021a390adbd322781a39f5`: initially found an already-rebound route could be accepted. Fixed with canonical route validation and a regression; the second review is scoped-clean. Later changes are equivalent abort-check deduplication, optional-source early return, formatting, and documentation.
- Live Telegram Test Server comparison passed in isolated rootless containers capped at 4 CPUs/8 GB. During a real spawned child’s 25-second model-response window, main sent **0** typing actions; this head sent **14**, and the independent TDLib user observed SUT typing. Both recordings completed, neither sent typing more than five seconds after the child response, and both released their leases with no credential scratch remaining. The baseline was main `799de097a30b6272074ebaaefd4481bd0fd153c6`; its relevant production paths are unchanged through current main `f8e492f2c9d1cc3768c222b909a82bd3e4f97455`. Only model responses were synthetic; Telegram ingress, spawn/yield, child execution, typing, and delivery were real. The first setup attempt lacked workspace dependency links, sent no request, and was reconciled and cleaned up before the corrected run.

Production delta: +131 lines, with no new typing controller or timers. Removed two duplicate signal-abort checks in the registration owner: the retained authority's `assertCurrent()` already performs them. Remaining growth binds existing owners across the security boundary; unrelated deletions would not make this repair smaller. Tests: +217 lines, with a dedicated line-budget allocation for the regression contracts; shared baseline unchanged. Docs: +1 line.

Contributor code was read through GitHub only and was never checked out or executed. This is an independent implementation from main, with all human author identities from the original PR credited in the commit.

## What Problem This Solves

`gateway restart` can stop waiting at 60 seconds even after the replacement reports a new startup phase and becomes healthy shortly afterward.

Related: #161158

## User Impact

Restarts and Doctor restoration keep observing a progressing startup within the existing five-minute cap. Verified readiness succeeds; failed and unverified outcomes retain their distinct nonzero exit codes.

This covers native restart progress. The source updater's arbitrary shell callback/exit-2 contract and native `gateway start` deadline remain unresolved parts of #161158, so this PR does not close it. A silent pre-listener startup cannot earn progress credit without observable migration activity.

Count each new `/startupz` phase from the running replacement's own listener in the existing progress watchdog. Repeated phases, foreign listeners, and a later process cannot renew the window. title: feat: hand repository disk custody to Gateway worktrees
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The existing Move-to-Gateway path still tried to reconcile a disk-authoritative repository as a mirror. It refused before a usable local handoff, and interruption recovery needed to distinguish an unimported disk from an already-bound managed worktree before releasing the original resource.

Depends on #189263, now landed as `38978c421475789e9daefda87c98dd8c450ef7c0`. This PR now targets `main`; the verified child-only comparison contains the same 37-path durable Move/handoff and retirement change.

## User Impact

For an already-bound, active exact repository disk, the existing authorized `sessions.move` operation can now hand work to the Gateway:

`draining Move → pending result/original receipt → fresh export → verified local worktree binding → repository custody retirement → exact-resource cleanup → local placement`

Private Git commits and working files survive. A staged index or unavailable history still refuses a lossy export. Missing/replaced disks do not fall back to an old mirror, clone-only reconstruction, or automatic replacement.

**Disk mode remains unselectable.** Paused-disk preparation and final activation are separate. No schema/version change, new queue, manager, config option, or public protocol is introduced; the lifecycle owner’s shared-state v39 reservation is untouched. No deployment or cloud allocation is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Existing pending-result fields retain the fresh export and original immutable resource receipt. The repository owner gains an exact-claim retirement operation; the existing Move and environment owners keep cleanup and completion.
- Before local binding, recovery captures the current original disk again. It can resume an interrupted unbound import only when its HEAD matches the fresh export; unknown local commits still refuse.
- After local binding, recovery never recaptures or reapplies files. The managed worktree/session binding is the handoff receipt; original cleanup and pending-result release resume independently.
- Caller, session generation, writer, exact attachment, and publication exclusion remain enforced. In-memory recovery now preserves its actor/session/writer authority across its own workspace binding, rather than rejecting that binding.
- Claimless restart recovery no longer tries to close worker-tool state for a local claim; worker-owned closure remains unchanged.

Simplification reused the existing Move state, pending result, repository store, managed-worktree binding, and cleanup operations. No additional handoff schema was needed. The production growth covers the two real ownership transitions and crash recovery; 334 net test/helper lines are separately allocated for the actual Move entry and distinct interruption boundaries.

## Evidence

### Current main integration

Signed candidate **`82b400ee1a4a6a2fde04eb00344a2ee29cdda053`**, tree `cf6a958f8aec5444da2b8fbca1cb1468c345d7d3`, preserves original published `f9176e034c0b9efd38065b31c8e09dac8ca5b53b` ancestry and integrates actual landed S6/main. Native conflict resolution preserved the qualified child content and all landed prerequisite repairs, including retained capture aliases. The 37-path delta remains **+1,184/−305**, with the identical stable patch ID; only three inventory blobs incorporate independent main additions. No signature override, recreated PR, or unsigned prerequisite side-history was used.

- **25 current Move/recovery cases passed in two files**: 96.14s Vitest, 98.06s wrapper, including compiler cleanup. These overlap the prior 122-case integration proof and are not added to that count. Real Move, disk export, Git/native stores, restart boundaries and incognito/revocation cases exercise the newly combined capture/result owners.
- Current core and Gateway test typechecks, CI-mode scoped type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), canonical format, whitespace and test-line ratchet passed. Existing 334-line test allocation and shared scalar are unchanged.
- Fresh independent **Codex autoreview P0–P3** covered the full `38978c4..82b400e` range plus eight complete owner-context files: one 208,821-byte pass, **scoped-clean**, zero findings, final source verified. An initial preparation attempt named a nonexistent context file and did not run a review; it was corrected to the actual teardown owner on the same route.

### Earlier implementation and repair proof

Earlier reviewed candidate **`f9176e034c0b9efd38065b31c8e09dac8ca5b53b`**, tree `4b62f52276f0a500bd7509ce6bd6f97467398c93`. It preserves the original Move implementation `0efab5aabb8c4f566195e025bea43a69f8d69769` and adds the owning CI repairs below:

- Reproduced the original authorized `sessions.move` failure: `A disk-authoritative repository cannot accept a mirrored checkpoint`. The same entry now reaches local placement with private HEAD and disk-only bytes intact.
- **13 Move scenarios passed**: normal completion; interruption at intent, import, before export, captured artifact, local binding, before/after cleanup, pending release, and reconciliation; revoked authority; in-memory success and revocation. Real Git, native stores, local node workspace/HTTP transfer, lifecycle barriers, and the real environment cleanup owner are used. Provider destruction and GitHub identity are explicitly synthetic.

title: feat(workers): recover retained disks through exact lifecycle intent
body:
Related: #188796
Depends on #189350 (durable disk Move), above #189263 (current-disk IO), #189106 (disk authority), and #189019 (exact resource receipts). Those prerequisites have landed; this PR now targets `main`.

## Problem and solution

A retained cloud disk needs durable pause/resume intent and exact-resource recovery. A lost provider reply or Gateway restart must not allocate a replacement, extend a work window, discard cleanup custody, or treat resumed compute as a usable worker.

The existing environment writer records immutable acquisition policy and lifecycle operation ID/action/expected claim revision. The provider queue retains the original receipt and operation. **Persisted resume intent is custody, not authority:** maintenance observes pending resume without replaying it; only a fresh authorized wake or same-key creation retry can reopen compute. Pause and lost-reply settlement keep their existing owners.

Crabbox translates the generic contract into Linux Azure Sandbox capability, identity, policy, and independent readback checks. Pending readiness is polled without starting or renewing compute; closed windows still require explicit recovery. Runtime admission stays fenced until the original node reconnects and its current bundle is verified. Unknown observations preserve custody; explicit deletion remains pending until exact-resource stop confirms it.

**Activation remains off.** No profile default, idle-sweep selection, workspace mirroring, disk-authority activation, controller adoption, or Crabbox dependency/release change. Released Crabbox cold-boot readiness is not claimed.

## Internal integration contract

- `createWithRequest` persists explicit retained policy before allocation. A fresh same-key retry revalidates caller/source authority, recovers the original receipt and operation, and resumes provisioning admission.
- `ensureRetainedRunning({environmentId, expectedOwnerEpoch, assertCurrent, signal})` requires exact receipt, live caller/owner authority, finite window, original-node availability, and runtime admission.
- `suspendRetained` uses the same owner and durable operation. Stop retains final-save and confirmed deletion semantics.
- Shared-state **38 → 39**, separate from agent schema 39. The nullable `retention_json` column leaves existing leases unretained. Runtime/Doctor migration, PostgreSQL predecessors, native ceilings, backups and rollback fencing are coordinated. Package-only downgrade is unsafe: settle retained resources and restore the matching backup and binary.

## Current candidate and installed-upgrade qualification

Signed head **`0b2a51db3fc8c1b161d26562a45b5d8cce862597`**, tree **`e670faf0c148fb361ae0470b49ec33c93e8c1a3b`**, was published through the native proof-only path to this same PR. **Installed-upgrade finding R5 is now resolved for this exact candidate**, using independently verified recovered evidence and completed native cleanup. Ordinary exact-head review and merge gates still apply; no transport failure has been relabeled green.

The native baseline preserves original hosted `07fe6572370d5223f7f1f15e797925772fa4e61c` ancestry and actual landed S7 `af7cee29336523d3f8c2f3ae5c6af5f55e570772`. Sixty conflict resolutions retain the previously qualified lifecycle content or unchanged landed owners, with disjoint main metadata merged normally. The **88-path +3,226/−396** child patch is unchanged from qualified `0388b96ec623242b36010fefbb9f9efc82a6c241`: 85 blobs, including every generated catalog and migration, are identical; only package and two inventory files carry independent main additions. No signature override or unsigned prerequisite side-history was used.

## Evidence

### Installed latest-stable → exact candidate

- Immutable [package run 41283351382](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41283351382) supplied the exact candidate. Package SHA-256: `4231d674427c56c67110aa71b82e035e5b18a873b3cd93d6b36e97e8ed28eb5e`. Actual installed and serving build identities verified the transition from stable `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41` to this candidate; the unchanged version string alone was not used as proof.
- In [native run 41315369261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41315369261), the complete installed-upgrade shell finished **exit 0 in 346.377s**. Shared `user_version` and primary schema metadata reached **39**. Both terminal legacy worker rows retained their original fields and SQL NULL retention; no retention opt-in was fabricated.
- Existing placement and staged-unaccepted pending-result rows, NULL disk authority, the durable imported session and selected settings survived update, stop, repeated Doctor and cold reopen. Disabled heartbeat intent was verified in completed migration receipts and both canonical job definitions and indexed fields—not by requiring the retired config path to remain.
- The **actual installed `workerEnvironmentService.get` decoder** returned literal `retention:null` after update and after cold reopen. Reopen used a different process and invocation; final service shutdown recorded the process tree terminated.
- **Recovery and cleanup:** the local controller hit its 600s tool limit; its outer wrapper exited143 and the Python reporting aggregate failed with BrokenPipe. Those remain nonpasses. The already-completed proof was not replayed. Documented native download recovered 152 files, independently checked and rehashed after native stop0 and an independent completed/no-host/not-ready/remote-settlement-complete observation. The Actions run is cancelled by cleanup, not reported as a successful workflow. Retained evidence manifest SHA-256: `5187d1694f78dcb610e571ed4cb5a98d56e62c71c550c8c010f26ca3116d9202`.

The separate post-volume inventory **did not execute** because of the reporting BrokenPipe and is not claimed. Optional predecessor `session_repository_workspaces` was absent and remains **unexercised**; no predecessor DDL was manufactured. Earlier failed proof and admission attempts remain failures.

### Current integrated candidate

- **15 service/store/migration cases across three files passed**: 62.49s Vitest, 64.93s wrapper, with compiler cleanup verified. Includes revoked pending resume, explicit same-operation recovery, initial provisioning retry, runtime/Doctor v38→v39 preservation, transactional rollback and PostgreSQL predecessor descriptors.

Complete PR rollup at qualification: 250 contexts, 195 success, 54 skipped and one neutral; none failed or pending. Activation stays off.

title: fix(msteams): send channel files to the team SharePoint site
body:
Supersedes #136274, thanks @a-tokyo.
Related: #136271

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Microsoft Teams channel file sends fail without a manually configured SharePoint site, and a central configured site can leave team members unable to open the file card.

## User Impact

Standard channels can send files to their own team's SharePoint site without setting `sharePointSiteId`. Explicit sites keep precedence. Group chats and private/shared channels still require an explicit site; no config migration or new option is introduced.

Discovery uses the existing `Sites.ReadWrite.All` application grant and the existing `ChannelSettings.Read.Group` RSC grant in the documented Teams manifest. No new permission scopes are requested. Microsoft documents these grants for [site lookup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/site-get?view=graph-rest-1.0) and [channel lookup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/channel-get?view=graph-rest-1.0).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both file-send paths now resolve the team's actual site through the existing guarded SharePoint Graph request owner. Cold references resolve the AAD group through the existing identity owner and regional SDK client. The site cache holds at most 500 account/tenant/bot/team entries; channel type is checked before using a cached parent-team site.

This is a small reimplementation of the useful fix, omitting the proposed folder option and extra Graph scope. The old require-site-only helper and its obsolete unit test are removed. Production grows by 113 lines for discovery, bounded caching, and the regional metadata operation; no equivalent dead production code was found to remove safely. Regression tests grow by 196 lines, with a matching test-line allocation for the two delivery entry points, cache isolation, cancellation, and audience/explicit-site contracts.

## Evidence

title: feat(memory-wiki): allow owner-scoped bridge reads in shared vaults
body:
Supersedes #129191, thanks @igs-rogenlo.

## What Problem This Solves

Agents sharing a global wiki cannot restrict imported bridge notes to their owners without also separating the native wiki into per-agent vaults.

## User Impact

Operators can opt into `plugins.entries.memory-wiki.config.bridge.ownership: "owner"` so non-sandboxed agents retrieve their own bridge notes while native wiki pages stay shared. The omitted setting and explicit `"sandboxed-only"` preserve today's behavior; sandboxed reads never widen.

Owner mode hides bridge pages without matching ownership, including unowned pages and calls without a resolved identity. CLI calls resolve the default agent unless `--agent` is supplied. This filters wiki query results, not filesystem access or compiled prompt digests; native aggregate pages remain shared. Existing configurations need no migration or action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing plugin-owned visibility filter and validate one optional enum in its runtime and manifest schemas. Delegation and public SDK additions from the original proposal are outside this minimal replacement. Main's `vault.scope: "agent"` separates the entire vault and does not cover this shared-native-pages scenario.

The simplification removes the one-use bridge-page predicate in the same visibility owner. Production TypeScript is **−3 lines**; manifest schema/help is **+8 lines**, for **+5 production/config lines** overall. Tests are **+43 lines**, allocated in a dedicated test-line record for the tool-level regression and independent schema boundary. Generated config artifacts add exactly one plugin leaf (4911 → 4912); core/channel counts are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Red before repair on main `447e14d02460`: owner-mode `wiki_search` returned another agent's bridge page; runtime schema rejected both new enum values. The original two-file run had 3 expected failures and 40 passes (50.60 seconds wall time).
- Green after repair: `pnpm test extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/config.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.reads.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.path-lookup.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.abort.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query-reader.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **64 passed, 6 files**, 46.77 seconds wall time including cold worker preparation; test execution about 2 seconds. PR CI succeeded at the same head: [run 41198930094](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41198930094), all 32 executed jobs passed; the changed-test job took 273 seconds including setup.
- The regression executes the real `wiki_search` and `wiki_get` tools on a synthetic temporary vault, checking omitted/legacy/owner settings, sandboxed and non-sandboxed calls, shared native pages, unowned bridge pages, unresolved identity, and CLI-style default identity. Existing memory-provider seams remain mocked; no live Gateway/model or stable-upgrade run was performed on the production host.
- Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, `config:docs:check`, `plugins:inventory:check`, staged test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad compiler/test proof is delegated to PR CI.
- Independent local autoreview of the complete candidate against `447e14d02460`, including query/config/tool context: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. The [requested hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189336#issuecomment-6543110134) completed with no code findings and asks for broader trusted-runtime and fresh/stable-install evidence. Review addressed by the maintainer ruling: the one optional field preserves defaults and sandbox restrictions; focused red→green proof and exact-head green CI are sufficient. Broader runtime/upgrade runs are not required for this change and were not performed. Applicable security review and `openclaw/ci-gate` have passed.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` only and was never checked out or executed. Human credit from both commit-author identities is retained; agent co-authors are excluded.


Upgrade note: existing configs without `bridge.ownership` validate unchanged and retain current sandbox-inferred visibility; the [runtime and manifest schema test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/34ac5c06226d9239b9a8ddacbe3703df3bd0e176/extensions/memory-wiki/src/config.test.ts#L25) covers the omitted field, and the tool regression covers unchanged default visibility.

title: feat(cli): read bounded model prompts from files
body:
Supersedes #120598, thanks @shad0wca7

Related: #140244

## What Problem This Solves

Automation must put large or sensitive one-shot model prompts in process arguments, where operating-system limits can reject them and process inspection can expose them.

## User Impact

`openclaw infer model run --prompt-file ./prompts/judge.txt` and the `capability` alias accept a UTF-8 file instead of `--prompt`. The file must stay inside the invocation's current directory, with symlinks and hardlinks rejected and a 1 MiB limit. The existing local and Gateway model-run paths receive the resolved text without adding a chat transcript. The selected provider still receives the prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the file at invocation time through the existing fs-safe root owner, then use the existing one-shot execution paths. Exactly one prompt source is required; invalid input fails before inference. This replacement adds one CLI flag and no configuration or Gateway protocol fields.

Production growth is 10 lines for input selection, the existing bounded reader call, and capability discovery. There is no equivalent dead code in this owner to remove safely; reusing fs-safe avoids a new file reader. Tests grow by 79 lines, with a dedicated allocation for the input-boundary regressions.

title: fix(reply): avoid sending blank attachments in normalized replies
body:
Supersedes #128580, thanks @sunlit-deng.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes broken replies when blank media metadata causes an empty attachment attempt, either instead of a text reply or after a valid attachment.

## User Impact

Replies with only blank media send their text normally, and mixed media lists send only real attachments. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original duplicate-text defect is already fixed by #129230, and #128372 preserves singular attachments when plural metadata is blank. Current main still passes whitespace media through its loose-payload normalizer to media senders.

Reuse the existing nonblank-string predicate for both media fields at that normalization owner. Empty strings, whitespace, and null entries are dropped before consumers choose dedupe or delivery; valid strings retain their original bytes, duplicates, order, and precedence. There is no new dedupe path.

Production delta: +3/-5, net -2 lines, replacing the local string/length predicate with the shared predicate. The 21-line test allocation covers two regressions at the public normalization-to-media-delivery boundary; the contributor's large proof runner is not ported.

## Evidence

- Baseline `bc82773a72ebe20a3f8c916998b3cfcbc7b00d78`: both regressions fail. A whitespace singular URL invokes the media sender instead of sending text; a mixed list invokes it for both the real image and a whitespace attachment.
- After: `src/plugin-sdk/reply-payload.test.ts` passes all 33 tests (0.587 seconds total Vitest duration). The new cases exercise `createNormalizedOutboundDeliverer` through `sendTextMediaPayload` and inspect transport callbacks.
- Focused reply-builder, inbound-dispatch, direct-DM, and outbound-contract suites pass (65 additional tests); message-action execution and subagent-completion suites pass (73 additional tests).
- Targeted Plugin SDK/channel TypeScript, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad validation is provided by this PR's CI; per-file hosted CI seconds are not separately available yet.

title: fix(acp): keep completed run conversations resumable
body:
Related: #106696.

Supersedes #107366, thanks @henkterharmsel.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost conversation history and missing asynchronous results when a parent continues a completed ACP run-mode child.

## User Impact

With acpx and a harness that supports loading or resuming sessions, a follow-up to the same child key keeps its recorded conversation, including after a runtime restart. An asynchronous follow-up returns its result to the current parent once. Completion releases workers; reset and deletion prevent reuse. Persistent ACP children retain their existing delegated completion behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main already retains the necessary metadata. Reuse the persisted-handle lookup after completion and let the existing one-way completion owner return the new result. Keep live-task, caller, and persistent-parent completion exemptions. Remove the obsolete private metadata-based helper and redundant metadata overlay.

This independently implements the useful behavior without porting the large proposal or adding state, capabilities, configuration, dependencies, or retention policy. Production code shrinks by 20 lines. Unsupported harnesses and previously deleted legacy metadata retain their existing behavior; #106696 remains open for those cases.

Regression tests grow by 215 lines, with an exact per-change test-line allocation: the real Gateway custody regression replaces the earlier mocked ACP return case and proves three distinct allowed/revoked/replaced outcomes. Docs grow by 2 lines; test routing and allocation add one line each.

## Evidence

- Red on main `2464bd85e0bc2927701c3147bf3dfc6993daaae3`: real acpx over stdio with a synthetic ACP agent returned a different backend session ID and forgot the first turn after completion/restart. Green: unchanged backend ID, history `["first", "second"]`, worker release, and deletion cleanup. The owner suite passed 5/5 (46.87 s command wall; continuity case 4.24 s). Its process cost protects real protocol/restart behavior that a helper test cannot establish. Runtime siblings passed 33/33.
- The production `createSessionsSendTool` regression is also red with main's routing source: accepted input reports `delivery.status="skipped"`. With the fix it returns pending, closes the invocation, then admits exactly one complete result to the original parent through the real Gateway service and completion custody. Device revocation or parent lifecycle replacement while the result is delayed prevents parent execution. All 3 custody cases pass (final Vitest duration 13.13 s; case test time 8.17 s; prior standalone command 24.69 s). Only model execution is synthetic; dispatch, final admission, profiles, authority, sessions, and SQLite remain real.
- [Initial CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41191364263) caught a persistent-ACP scope regression. The repair retains that existing completion exemption; the exact failed coordination file passes 43/43 (77.49 s Vitest duration). Its existing integration cases are needed to protect other child modes. `test:ci-failed` could not retrieve escaped job logs; direct supported job-log retrieval identified the failure, and the exact file was run locally. No inherited-failure exception is claimed.
- Directed send policy 27/27, result consumers 8/8, remaining ACP interaction contract 1/1, and prompt-prefix stability 14/14 pass. Targeted plugin/agent-tools typechecks, lint, format, and diff checks pass. Broad proof runs through current-head PR CI; job timings are available in its check logs.
- Fresh Codex autoreview at P0–P2 confirmed the production custody test and found only the stale indexed persistent-parent regression, explicitly repaired in the reviewed working tree. That repair is included in the merged commit and matches the reviewed working-tree source. No additional P0–P2 source defect was found. The earlier missing completion-owner finding is also addressed.

title: feat: capture explicit repository disk snapshots
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Explicit repository file access, publication and export must use the original attached disk—not an older Gateway mirror. Publication retries must preserve selected bytes and include requests queued after a lost receipt-binding reply.

Prerequisite #189106 landed as `7faf32da36cdb6f6021e662f92cbd9c1de783255`; GitHub automatically retargeted this existing PR to main. No replacement PR or early retarget.

## User Impact

**Disk mode remains unselectable.** Mirrored sessions and ordinary turns retain their behavior. This implements explicit current-disk I/O and snapshot preparation, not full retained-disk activation. No schema, public protocol, product configuration, cloud allocation or deployment is added.

- File reads, hash-checked editor writes, downloads and attachment originals use attached-node bytes. Editor settlement never accepts the old mirror.
- Publication captures under existing session exclusion and native quiescence. Selected/queued request refs and publication companions install atomically. Fresh capture, accepted-checkpoint reuse and retained retry share one ref owner. Lost replies never cause recapture of later disk edits or advancement of SQLite acceptance for artifact-only publication.
- Explicit Gateway export preserves private history/files and rechecks source before binding. Partial staged indexes or unavailable history fail closed, preserving the original disk.
- Paused preparation and final durable Move/teardown remain later work. Missing/replaced disks never trigger stale reconstruction or automatic replacement.

## Solution and Scope

Existing repository/checkpoint, placement, workspace-operation, transport and receipt owners retain their responsibilities. No parallel manager, queue, cache or state store. Authority is checked at the final effect; cleanup custody survives revocation.

Against captured main `c2a39e4c5a8166d1f5ea6703d1dfaa7d7c45de79`: **34 files, +2,106/-129**. Production remains **19 files, +527/-123 (net +404)**; the latest correction changes no production code. Tests/helpers: nine files +1,550/-6; docs +20; four allocation records +8; inventory +1. The 65-line checkpoint-ref leaf was extracted after a real 700-line owner-budget failure, without an exception. The review repair contributed production +97/-33 (net +64) and one boundary regression, now allocated exactly 92 lines after required braces. The existing 50-line accepted-reuse allocation and shared scalar remain unchanged.

Related: #188945, #189016

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Logs wheel scrolling stopping before the newest entry when Auto-follow is off and wrapped rows finish measuring during the scroll.

## User Impact

Readers can wheel to the newest retained log entry while keeping Auto-follow disabled. Idle anchoring and enabled Auto-follow continue to compensate for row resizing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The virtualizer's implicit end anchor can write the scroll position even when its row-size adjustment predicate rejects compensation. The existing reader-scroll policy now suppresses both compensation paths during active travel and restores idle anchoring afterward.

title: fix(doctor): restore Gateway before queued CLI maintenance
body:
Related: #189225

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can leave its managed Gateway stopped when queued CLI maintenance acquires state ownership before Doctor's restoration checks finish.

## User Impact

The Gateway stopped by Doctor gets priority over queued CLI schema preparation until restoration settles. Existing database, update, and native service authority checks remain in place. Doctor and concurrent CLI processes need the repaired runtime; already-running older clients cannot observe the reservation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor must release its database root before configuration recovery and Gateway bootstrap, so holding that root through launch is unsafe. The existing physical state-record owner now provides a temporary fs-safe reservation acquired under Doctor's current ownership. Both new and already-waiting schema/process acquisitions check it; actual Gateway startup remains eligible for the normal physical lock. No TTL increase, new configuration, schema, or ownership stealing is introduced. Unknown native cleanup and open writers retain recovery custody.

title: fix(auto-reply): stop queued turns replaying completed replies
body:
Supersedes #127967, thanks @HermanZeng.

Related: #126813

## What Problem This Solves

Queued messages can prompt an agent to answer an earlier question again after its message-tool reply has already been delivered.

## User Impact

The next queued request receives the confirmed completion context while retaining its own question, including requests to repeat or discuss the prior answer. Queue ordering and delivery ownership are preserved. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The successful execution hands its completion fact directly to the next queued input in the same physical session and delivery route. That input already owns context through preparation retries and consumption, so no separate handoff registry or lifecycle protocol is needed.

Production delta is +32 lines: the new handoff needs a producer and route checks. Duplicate route-key assembly was removed from the queue owner and shared with its existing grouping logic; overflow idempotency bytes stay unchanged. Further deletions would remove unrelated behavior. Regression tests add 139 lines, with a separate exact allocation and no shared-ceiling increase.

## Evidence

- On main `14e3eeccf84af998d84827ea43a8f3184b1e439f`, the new queue regression reached A → B → C once each but failed because B lacked predecessor-completion context. With the fix it passed, checking fresh B/C prompts, one completion directive each, and no automatic redelivery (2.1s test, 47.7s wrapper including cold preparation).
- Queue scope and collect suites: 99 tests passed across two files (64.3s wrapper). The added route cases keep context off other channels, targets, accounts, threads, reply anchors, room events, and later queued inputs.
- The complete touched runner suite (198 tests) and prompt-prefix stability suite (14 tests) also passed (132.5s wrapper; runner tests 68.5s including existing fixtures).
- Targeted typecheck, production/test lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Broad proof belongs to PR CI.
- Autoreview: Codex P0–P2, candidate against `14e3eeccf84a`, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The committed code matches that reviewed candidate; the allocation was checked separately.
- This is queue/execution-boundary proof using synthetic embedded-run delivery results. It is not live Telegram or real-model behavior proof, and does not claim the model can never choose to repeat itself.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed.

title: fix(gateway): reject oversized requests without disconnecting
body:
Supersedes #123122, thanks @sunlit-deng.

## What Problem This Solves

Oversized SDK requests reach the Gateway WebSocket receiver and disconnect the client with a generic `gateway closed (1009)` error instead of rejecting the individual request.

## User Impact

SDK and Control UI callers receive a payload-limit error with the actual serialized UTF-8 size and limit, and can send a smaller request on the same connection. Existing browser draft/attachment recovery is preserved. No settings or server limits change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing browser admission check and typed error into the shared pending-request owner. Apply the advertised hello policy immediately before sending, and reuse the existing 64 KiB pre-auth constant before hello. Remove browser-only payload state and validation. Keep the shared constant in a dependency-free leaf included in the extracted maintainer-wrapper inventory.

Production delta: +31/-25, net +6 lines, versus +69 in the contributor review. The small remaining growth supplies shared pre-auth/reset state and the byte counts in the error. Packaging inventory: +1 line. Tests: +59 lines, allocated for two distinct transport/handshake regressions.

## Evidence

- Both added regressions fail against unchanged main `8b1efb47c13011a10765f264cf46b97e72c12e78`: the real WebSocket SDK test gets `gateway closed (1009): `; the shared handshake test sends the oversized connect without local rejection. Both pass with this fix.
- The real WebSocket test advertises/enforces 8,192 bytes, rejects a multibyte oversized request locally, then completes `health` on the same socket with no close and no rejected request received.
- 295 focused tests across ten files pass: SDK handshake/request/held-request/pending lifecycle, browser Gateway/socket boundaries (including exact UTF-8 limits), chat send, and session startup. Commands complete in under 12 seconds each; [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41187700847) passed (1,414 seconds elapsed).
- The initial CI wrapper-closure failure was reproduced locally (2 failures), repaired by the leaf/inventory cutover, and verified locally (2 passes).
- Focused core/test and UI typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad build and validation passed in exact-head PR CI.
- Autoreview at P0–P2: initial review clean. Follow-up review found only an index-only packaging defect already fixed in its reviewed working tree; staging the complete correction resolves that finding. No additional defects found; reviewer context was limited and tests were not independently executed.
- Production host proof used isolated fixtures only. No live Gateway/model or interactive browser session was started. Contributor code was read through `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out or executed.

title: fix(feishu): show preview covers on outgoing videos
body:
Supersedes #98458, thanks @areslp.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes outgoing Feishu videos appearing with an empty preview.

## User Impact

Videos display a preview frame when cover preparation succeeds. If ffmpeg is unavailable or cover extraction/upload fails, the video arrives as a file attachment. No new dependency or configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [Feishu media contract](https://open.feishu.cn/document/server-docs/im-v1/message-content-description/create_json?lang=zh-CN) documents `image_key` as optional and explicitly says omitting it leaves no cover. Main sent only `file_key`.

This replacement uses the existing ffmpeg runtime, bounded to five seconds and 1280×720, and shares the existing image/file upload validation. Cover upload has a five-second deadline and honors the smaller of the account limit and Feishu's 10 MiB image limit. Direct and thread delivery continue through the shared sender with current send authority.

The production delta is +75 lines for bounded extraction and fallback, with the existing upload closure reused instead of adding a second uploader. Regression tests add 81 lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/feishu-video-covers.txt` to protect cover forwarding, file fallback, timeout, and authority after extraction.

## Evidence

- Base `8b1efb47c130`: six expected regression failures (missing cover keys in direct/thread messages and missing file fallback); 21 existing tests passed.
- Replacement: 29 media tests and 29 real-transport send-authority tests passed. Media file: 10.09 seconds wall time, test bodies under one second; both focused shards: 39.11 seconds. The [exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41187177230) passed; its changed-test job took 283 seconds including setup (individual file timing is not separately published).
- Scoped production/test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview on the complete local candidate against `8b1efb47c130`, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Unchanged helper implementations were outside its supplied diff; those owners were inspected separately.
- Contributor code was read through `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff` only; it was never checked out or executed. This is a fresh implementation from main. Human commit-author credit is preserved for luopei and areslp.
- The attached sanitized screenshot is historical live proof supplied by @areslp: the upper video lacks a cover and the lower video displays an extracted frame. It was inspected and also shown in the task chat. No fresh live Feishu send was performed for this replacement; the current wiring is covered by regressions.

![Historical Feishu comparison: upper video without cover, lower video with cover](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62830c3f-805a-480e-896a-c7642b4385e3)
- Exact-head product CI and the dependency/security-sensitive review statuses passed; final CI-gate publication is enforced by native merge admission.

## What Problem This Solves

title: revert(doctor): restore damaged-state repair admission
body:
Related: #189025, #189039, #189050.

## What Problem This Solves

Reverts #189025 (`4872133405c`) because mandatory pre-repair capture prevents Doctor from repairing supported damaged state, a production defect exposed in large-14, and caused schema-preflight failures in large-19 on [main full CI 41172573619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41172573619).

## User Impact

Doctor can reach its existing damaged-state repair owners again. Standalone original-state capture failures become advisory again; repair-specific backups and integrity checks still apply. Healthy repeated runs also avoid an empty cold-navigation maintenance lease that changed state bytes and prevented capture reuse.

The stalled-inventory cancellation from #189025 is rolled back and needs a fresh forward fix. This revert also rolls back its relaxed foreign-key original-image support; it does not implement mandatory preservation of malformed originals.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary schema admission rejects the supported legacy Workshop index before mandatory capture can finish, blocking the repair that owns that damage. A complete original-preserving forward fix needs independently verified private normalization; a partial capture exemption would not safely restore that contract. This change therefore applies the exact inverse of #189025.

Prerequisite `b11052f9534` avoids leasing an explicitly empty cold-navigation target list. It overlaps Peter's #189039 and open #189050 and is included only as the revert's prerequisite: the revert alone leaves healthy capture-repeat behavior broken. Both were open at the initial fresh-main/PR check; #189039 merged while this PR was being prepared. Those changes address later archive budgeting and projection performance, not the refusing capture boundary, and main still lacks the empty-target return.

## Evidence

- Original failing jobs: [large-14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41172573619/job/124453674872) and [large-19](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41172573619/job/124453674979). After disposable installation setup, the real Doctor entry point reproduces the malformed-schema refusal before repair; unchanged required tests pass with this candidate.

title: feat(skills): read bounded local skill companions
body:
Supersedes #133376, thanks @ericcaiwx-star.

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode agents can read an installed skill's instructions but cannot read the companion references those instructions require.

## User Impact

Eligible local Gateway skills can expose their bundled text references through `skills_read({ name, relativePath })` or `skills.read(name, relativePath)`. Existing skill-read grants now cover files in that skill directory. Sandbox, remote workspace, node-hosted, and required-workspace placements remain instruction-only. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing installed-skill reader and worker bridge with one optional relative path. Current main's one-argument reader still ignores companion requests despite instructing agents to resolve relative resources beside SKILL.md. This is an independently implemented, credited replacement; the contributor's source was read with GitHub CLI and never checked out or executed.

## Evidence

- Red before: at main `7bd53ff28f69fad0190a1f0573e6421c199450de`, the real Code Mode worker returned SKILL.md for a companion request and the native reader ignored relativePath (2 new tests failed, 4 existing tests passed).
- Green after: 41 focused tests across `code-mode.skill-read`, `installed-skill-catalog`, `harness/host-skills`, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability`. After simplification, reran the changed two files: 24 passed. The worker proof uses real temporary files, catalog preparation, native skill tools, and the actual Code Mode worker, without a model or live Gateway.
- Negative cases: parent traversal, absolute/drive/home/backslash paths, file and directory symlink escapes, hardlinks, oversized files, NUL/invalid UTF-8, directories, missing files, replaced roots, restricted placements, and unmarked remote selections with a same-path local decoy. Cancellation and run retirement after filesystem reads withhold the result.
- Targeted typechecks: agents-root and agents-other passed. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, and the test-line ratchet against the pinned base passed. Broad suites are left to PR CI on this production host.
- Test cost: the two new cases took 168 ms and 4 ms; their file's cold wall time was 35.99 s including worker preparation. The full [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41179349256) and final `openclaw/ci-gate` passed on `d67f86128b324ac22acfeb64969940c8e829553f`; CI does not expose separate per-file timing here.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the candidate against `7bd53ff28f69fad0190a1f0573e6421c199450de`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Reviewer did not execute tests. Subsequent changes only renamed a test-local binding for lint and added the test-line allocation.

## Security Review

The explicitly requested permission expansion is read-only and limited to eligible installed local skill directories. The existing placement owner captures an fs-safe Root; reads revalidate that root's identity and realpath containment, reject symlinks/hardlinks, and bound allocation to 256 KiB. The reader rejects invalid UTF-8/NUL bytes and checks cancellation/current run authority after awaited preparation and before publishing content. Required-workspace rebinding clears companion authority. No directory listing, writes, execution, ambient remote-path fallback, new public tool, or new config option is added. Existing instruction delivery and its usage fingerprints retain their whole-document contract.

<details>
<summary>Scope and line budget</summary>

Production: +66 net lines, tests: +190, docs: +17, allocation record: +2 (total +275). This is smaller than the original +408 total. The 190-line allocation covers two integration regressions for the new capability and its security boundary; it does not change the shared scalar.

The production growth consists of local placement/root preparation (+15), confined bounded text reads (+36), existing native tool/schema delivery (+9), instruction-versus-companion formatting (+4), bridge result handling (+1), and clearing authority at required-workspace rebinding (+1). Controller and prompt changes are replacements. The common post-read authority gate and result envelope are reused, and file-host resolution is shared within preparation. There is no equivalent dead production machinery that can safely be removed to offset this capability's required boundary checks.

Contributor credit: `Co-authored-by: ericcaiwx-star <ericcaiwx@gmail.com>` (verified from the original PR commits).
</details>

title: fix(agents): fail stalled provider authentication at the run deadline
body:
Supersedes #93952, thanks @amittell.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent runs that hang indefinitely when provider credential lookup or a runtime token exchange never returns.

## User Impact

Authentication stops at the existing run deadline or cancellation with an error naming the provider and auth step and suggesting a retry. Run deadline and cancellation errors cannot fall through to AWS sentinel handling or further auth attempts. Provider-originated abort errors retain their existing recovery before run expiry. No new settings or credential storage are introduced.

Exchange hooks receive an optional cancellation signal and should pass it to their transport. JavaScript cannot forcibly stop a plugin that ignores cancellation; its late result is still rejected before credential installation. Claimed durable OAuth refreshes retain their existing settlement owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth controller shares one startup budget across lookup and exchange, then consumes the existing execution owner's published deadline, respecting paused or unlimited execution when an auth step starts. An already-running exchange keeps the deadline captured at entry; later deadline extensions do not rearm its timeout. Request-time OAuth lookup and exchange use the same bound and request cancellation. Final teardown cancels auth; temporary cleanup for forwarded harness candidates keeps later API-key candidates usable.

The simplification pass removed the duplicate unavailable-reason adapter and a redundant missing-state check. Production growth is +126 net lines: the shared deadline/cancellation helper, execution-deadline projection and wiring, request-time propagation, and abort/error boundaries are required to close the complete flow. Existing parameter types moved to the existing type module to keep the controller within its file limit. No test-routing registry changed. The separate 159-line allocation covers only this change's regression growth.

## Evidence

- Baseline `e1cd21501dd59366fefc3ff8263d97eeacdc799e`: focused negative control failed 4 of 5 selected cases. Hung lookup, hung exchange and AWS exchange remained pending at 100 ms; cancellation incorrectly installed credentials. Slow success passed.
- Replacement: all 88 focused tests passed across `auth-controller.test.ts`, `auth-controller.binding.test.ts`, `auth-controller.request-auth.test.ts`, and `provider-runtime-auth.test.ts` (70.48 s including compiled-worker preparation). New coverage includes slow success, one shared budget, request-time lookup/exchange deadlines, request-specific cancellation, late-result rejection, and forwarded harness candidate transitions, and provider-originated abort recovery. Existing durable OAuth settlement and account-authority tests pass.
- The initial CI run identified four test cleanup callbacks returning Vitest utilities instead of `void`; the correction uses block bodies. Both affected files pass again: 52 tests in 19.81 s. The correction commit also has a clean P0–P2 autoreview; production source was unchanged by that cleanup correction. The final auth-signal simplification and added provider-abort regression were then validated by the complete 88-test run and a fresh full-candidate P0–P2 security review. Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad build/typecheck/test proof is delegated to this PR's CI; no broad suite ran on the production host.
- Security-focused autoreview of the complete local candidate against the baseline above, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`. Fixed its findings about reset budgets, request-time lookup/cancellation, and temporary harness transitions. No provider or review configuration changed.
- Contributor source was read only with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; it was never checked out or executed. The contributor's Gateway traces support the original diagnosis, but no new Gateway or external-provider proof is claimed for this replacement. The Team Gateway was not modified or restarted.

Contributor credit: Alex Mittell <mittell@me.com>, with `Co-authored-by: Alex Mittell <mittell@me.com>` on the replacement commit.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the isolated publication observation worker exits before its bounded diagnostic and public read because its frozen source inventory omits retry dependencies.

## User Impact

Publication validation can start its verified worker and reach the existing observation checks. No release is published by this change; source verification, isolation, and deadlines remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shutdown-aware retry in `d9837a55eb7` / #189008 imports error diagnostics whose runtime closure is missing from the canonical publication inventory.
