title: fix(mcp): reject mixed command and URL configuration writes
body:
Supersedes #122348, thanks @ooiuuii.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can silently run a local MCP command when the same server definition also specifies a remote URL.

## User Impact

Explicit config validation and new or edited MCP writes reject mixed definitions with the server path and both field names. Existing definitions retain their runtime behavior with a warning. Doctor explains the two explicit repairs while retaining transport and authentication choices. Updates and incremental MCP repairs can preserve other unchanged legacy entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP normalizer owns the shared diagnostic, consumed by strict validation and warning-only reads. Writers compare unchanged legacy definitions against their captured source snapshot before runtime path expansion, including equivalent existing alias normalization. The repaired candidate is fully validated separately; an unrelated invalid legacy entry does not discard the per-server baseline. Doctor keeps its existing migrations and leaves the transport choice to the operator: automatic removal of HTTP/auth fields could enable local commands that node-host or native Codex previously refused. No settings were added.

Doctor and compatibility comparisons now use one retired-key normalizer, removing duplicate migration transforms, separate traversal wrappers, and an iterator. Alias repair on the mixed server itself preserves disabled semantics, timeout units, and canonical precedence. Production delta is +13 lines versus +93 in the original proposal; the remaining growth implements validation and compatible writes. Tests add 240 lines with a matching allocation for the distinct config, update, incremental-repair, and real MCP process boundaries.

## Evidence

- Main baseline `d13bd0f6067d878a4ced96272e20dc1e13c3cebf`: five final regression cases fail because both CLI scopes accept ambiguity and runtime/Doctor warnings are absent. A real baseline probe also confirms embedded stdio registration while the URL remains configured. The incremental-repair regression additionally failed on the initial candidate and passes after propagating the original snapshot baseline.
- Final focused proof: 48/48 pass across config CLI/I/O, MCP mutations, async validation, existing Doctor migrations, and persisted MCP integration. Wrapper wall time: 41.14 seconds including native worker preparation. The two hosted P1 findings reproduced as four failing cases before the source-baseline correction: tilde path expansion blocked update/MCP writes, and unrelated legacy disabled flags blocked Doctor in both roots. All now pass. Same-entry disabled/timeout aliases also failed in both scopes before sharing the migration normalizer and now have regression coverage. An additional strict core-only snapshot regression failed before its two-line orchestration correction and now passes without plugin metadata. Focused type checking and type-aware lint pass. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41179206195) and the required aggregate gate passed; final checks report 67 passed, 56 intentionally skipped, zero failed.
- The persisted proof covers both roots, backup and idempotent alias normalization, retained URL/auth/OAuth/TLS options, then an explicit stdio replacement followed by a real child process and published tool. All four requester-marked cases (both roots, auth present or missing) reject before process I/O. The real update-channel writer and incremental MCP mutation facade are exercised, including rejection of new/edited mixed definitions.
- Isolated upgrade proof: actual npm `v2026.10.9` created config and SQLite state and started successfully, then exact reviewed candidate `0a5895d852ea00abda666bd47b630b13b4cc1001` passed strict rejection, Doctor preservation/warnings, actual update-channel persistence and backup, sibling and same-entry alias repair, and repeat-Doctor byte identity. title: feat: retain repository disk authority through recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repository recovery needs to remember which exact retained disk owns accepted work, rather than treating an older Gateway mirror as the latest workspace after a restart.

Prerequisite #189019 is merged as `ff3ab23502010d1437c4afa5d7657a6d5e23111a`. GitHub subsequently retargeted this PR to `main`; the history-preserving integration retains the original 66-file authority/recovery child scope.

## User Impact

No disk-mode selector is enabled. Mirrored sessions keep their existing behavior. This is an inactive implementation prerequisite, not delivery of retained-disk workspaces.

Shared-state schema v38 adds nullable repository and pending-result authority fields after v37. Existing pending results remain mirrored, optional repository storage stays lazy, and older binaries refuse the upgraded schema. Rollback uses the existing exact predecessor backup.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The existing repository owner binds one immutable environment/resource receipt. The existing pending-result owner records that authority when accepting custody; retries never infer it from a replacement environment.
- Recovery settles only the original attached disk after cleanup. A missing/replaced disk, stale placement, failed cleanup, or transfer stays held: no stale-mirror restore, automatic replacement, input replay, or disk destruction.
- Until explicit disk I/O/export support follows, stored file fallback, new publication fallback, and Gateway materialization refuse disk authority. Previously pinned publication snapshots remain usable.
- SQLite, PostgreSQL, Doctor, predecessor restore, generated catalogs, and native schema-version metadata move together. No new manager, queue, cache, config switch, or public protocol field.

Simplification retained one repository owner and one pending-result owner, reused existing cleanup/settlement, shared migration registration, and one predecessor-schema transform chain for runtime admission and generated catalogs. Against the prerequisite: production/metadata +615/-131, tests +651/-18, generated catalogs +152/-110. title: fix(codex): allow binding before source execution starts
body:
Supersedes #128742, thanks @libaojiang.
Closes #128719.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `/codex bind` rejecting transfer of the current Codex harness session because its own queued reply operation is counted as executing source work.

## User Impact

The next bound message can initialize its native thread and inherit bounded visible user/assistant history while the source reply is queued. Source execution that has actually started still must finish or be stopped. Binding creates a separate native thread; it does not transfer the harness tool catalog or developer instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the host's existing execution-start marker through an optional filter on the existing active-run query. Ordinary callers keep their current semantics, and there are no new SDK exports, hook callbacks, configuration options, or protocol changes.

Reuse the source key already resolved under the binding's currentness guard, removing the duplicate database lookup. Production LOC: **-1 net**. Test LOC: **+28**, allocated for queued history-transfer coverage and the independent execution-start/lane-wait contract. Baojiang Lee's original PR identified and demonstrated the failure; this replacement was implemented from current main without checking out or running the contributor head.

## Evidence

- Red on main `8993eba475bd5a73f415131f2b981a46e4de4210`: the bound-message regression receives `Codex source session has an active run` instead of its expected reply. The execution-only query regression also fails on main by reporting queued ownership.
- Green after: `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/conversation-binding.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **122 tests passed**. Suite wall times: 13.19 s and 45.97 s; combined wrapper time: 62.71 s. title: fix: preserve first-party symbols in diagnostic profiles
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic profiles flatten first-party fs-safe frames to package labels, hiding the write and staging functions needed to investigate recurring Gateway stalls.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish safe `@openclaw/*` function symbols, including `runPinnedWriteNative`, `NativeStagedFile.write`, and `#prepare`. Dependency URLs remain package-only; third-party symbols, paths, arguments, and user data remain hidden.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared CPU/heap/stall frame sanitizer, retaining the existing bounded symbol validation and package classification. No sampling, event-loop-health exclusion, or write behavior changes.

The requested call-site attribution is deferred under the authorized fallback: fs-safe 0.27.0 exposes `Root.write/create` and `stageFileInDirectory`, but `runPinnedWriteNative` and `NativeStagedFile` are internal. Root/parent admission awaits occur before `#prepare` calls synchronous `binding.createStagedFile`; an application wrapper would return its promise before this segment. OpenClaw has no `stageFileInDirectory` callers. Correct attribution needs a package-owned synchronous-segment hook carrying a fixed application owner label, then an application adapter to `runWithMainThreadTask`; it cannot be supplied by wrapping the existing asynchronous API alone.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on base: expected `runPinnedWriteNative`, received `[dep:@openclaw/fs-safe]`; passes with the fix. The same table covers private methods, invalid first-party symbols, third-party redaction, scoped/pnpm layouts, and hidden paths.

Heap and CPU tests include real runtime captures. No live Gateway changes or attribution claim for the deferred write segment.

title: fix: managed updates refuse a valid runtime after Homebrew Node changes
body:
Fixes #189048
Related #188829

## What Problem This Solves

Managed updates can refuse a compatible Gateway after a Homebrew runtime path changes: the early engine check prevents an existing runtime fallback and omits the inspected Gateway install root from its diagnostic.

## User Impact

A compatible managed service Node takes priority over an incompatible PATH Node. An owned writable service can switch to a compatible existing updater or safely discovered runtime when the update will refresh its definition. Protected definitions and `--no-restart` retain their pins. Refusals identify the service/updater runtimes, PATH executable, target engines, and Gateway root.

Engines and later capability/identity checks remain enforced. This repair belongs to the installed updater. A refusing 2026.10.7 driver needs the documented [manual package-manager hop](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating/update-methods#alternative-manual-npm-pnpm-or-bun) to a release containing it, or a compatible service runtime selected by its deployment owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing service observation into early preflight and retain its selected runtime through staging and activation. Execution and preview both use the inherited runtime-recovery environment snapshot, falling back to the explicit native definition environment when unavailable.

pr-simplify removed custom PATH probing in favor of the existing guarded discovery owner. Early admission cannot provision a runtime; diagnostics never execute an additional PATH binary merely for guidance. The production delta is +52 lines; the separate +230 net test-line allocation covers selection, negative controls, guarded execution, preview, and activation. No shared baseline change.

## Evidence

- RED on pinned main `4d76d1d82f705391c461268a5d6b8190b889066b`: incompatible service 26.8.2 incorrectly refuses valid updater 24.22.1; both-old refusal incorrectly reports an unresolved Gateway root. Final guarded discovery passes all 68 existing owner tests; the final entry-point/preview pair passes all 25 tests in 60.65 s. The both-old control still refuses before staging or service stop.
- The complete CLI-update TypeScript leaf, targeted canonical oxlint (0 warnings/errors), formatting, and diff checks pass. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 autoreview r5 is scoped-clean for the complete final candidate; no subsequent source changes. Final head: `8917aaaaf78fecf00caab2d476fd1dc4b6bc30a5`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41176237261) completed SUCCESS in 27m38s: 44 successful jobs, 26 intentional skips, no failed or unfinished jobs.

title: fix(gateway): reject session invitations to invalid human identities
body:
Supersedes #134006, thanks @linhongyu510.
Closes #133956

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes successful but ineffective session invitations when historical human creators are channel handles or no longer identify a current Gateway profile.

## User Impact

Owners can invite current profiles, including people without sessions, while invalid human candidates fail with `unknown identity` without a membership write. Existing orphan rows remain visible and removable. Existing owner access, agent/system candidates, and role-based access rules are preserved. No settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing current-profile directory and authenticated caller as the human candidate sources in the shared picker/admission builder. Stop deriving human admission from historical session creators, whose projection has already discarded provenance. This covers durable and memory-only incognito creators without adding source filters at three indexing paths.

| Member candidate | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current profile, including a sessionless profile | Admit | Admit |
| Authenticated caller / owner | Admit | Admit; ownership authorization unchanged |
| Agent or system creator in the selected projection | Admit | Admit |
| Historical human creator with no current profile: channel, unknown, or orphan profile provenance | Admit | Reject |
| Arbitrary unknown ID absent from all candidate sources | Reject | Reject |
| Persisted orphan member, with no valid candidate source | List/remove; no admission solely from membership | Same; listing is cleanup evidence, never admission authority |

Security review: current-main reproduction demonstrates invalid membership admission and persistence, not an authentication or visibility bypass. Viewer membership still matches a verified profile ID and remains subject to role/visibility policy. Historical human provenance now cannot manufacture a candidate; current profile display facts remain authoritative. Human IDs matching a real current profile remain valid through that directory. Production delta is **-1 line** by removing the redundant historical-human candidate path; no unrelated cleanup.

## Evidence

- Base: `5388ada4c289a9298833ae1019652da8244e2d68` (current main at investigation).
- Red before: the handler/storage regression failed on unchanged main; all six historical human candidates (channel/unknown/profile provenance, each durable/incognito) were listed and successfully persisted. The arbitrary unknown-ID negative control was already rejected.
- Green after: 48 tests across seven focused files (sharing handlers, identity builder, profile display, sharing worker mutations, creator namespaces, and picker invalidation). The final touched suite passed 13/13 in 19.52s wall time (16.67s Vitest duration); CI `checks-node-changed` succeeded in 285 job-seconds (setup and other selected files included; no separate per-file CI timing). [Exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41170570883) completed successfully, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Targeted TypeScript, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- The regression also checks sessionless profile, owner, agent/system additions and removals, actual member mutation access, and list/remove cleanup without re-admission of a historical orphan.
- Local Codex autoreview, P0–P3 security-focused coverage of the complete local diff and owning source context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Final local snapshot includes all three intended files; review completed after the fixture and allocation changes.
- Simplification: one candidate builder owns the decision; the raw creator projection is unchanged, and no provenance-recovery helper, index policy, new settings, or state is introduced.

title: fix: cancel usage pricing preparation when the Gateway stops
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway shutdown can hang on usage backfill while catalog pricing preparation is pending.

## User Impact

Stopping the usage sidecar now cancels its pricing wait and releases its refresh lock. Committed cost-cache rows remain intact; unfinished refresh work is rebuilt on the next startup. No configuration, schema, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidecar already aborts its work scope, but `prepareUsageCostPricing` awaited catalog preparation without observing that signal. The worker runtime holds its refresh lock across this await. Race this optional preparation against the existing scope signal, retaining the existing joins for native workers and admitted cache writes. Shared catalog preparation may finish independently; the cancelled refresh cannot continue to scan or write.

The incident journal identifies the usage sidecar as the only pending named owner at the 82-second shutdown deadline, but cannot identify its inner await. This regression proves a remaining cancellation hole after #187877; it does not establish that every production SIGKILL has this cause. Earlier stops with no pending close steps also recorded service-child cleanup failures, which need separate investigation.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI run 41169213009](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41169213009) passed at `c4b1ba1695b46e903c05425a5ea39659d59e4fc0` with no failed jobs.

- Real sidecar, queue, refresh runtime, and pricing owner; only the inner catalog-preparation step is held pending. On base `9902334873c1c00649c1cfe1ff484621635ece49`, the pricing case fails because stop never settles within 100 ms; discovery and scan-admission cases pass. The fix passes all three cases.
- Focused single-file tests, each timeout-wrapped with `--maxWorkers=1`, using the pinned Bun fork: sidecar **7 passed** (17.15 s wrapper wall time); pricing-context **1 passed** (7.15 s); real incognito close/accepted memory usage and trajectory settlement **1 passed** (14.99 s). Existing sidecar coverage includes committed usage, exact reads, deferred appends, and recovery after restart.
- Focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Full typechecks and broad suites are left to PR CI under the host IO restriction. The initial installed-Bun lint attempts timed out because that runtime invoked the package script; the documented focused oxlint fallback passed.

title: fix(doctor): abort stalled recovery inventories and restore service
body:
Related #187900 #178359

## What Problem This Solves

Standalone `doctor --fix` can leave its managed Gateway stopped while waiting forever for a plugin's pre-repair backup inventory.

## User Impact

A stalled read-only inventory now observes the existing ten-minute capture deadline. If the original-state capture fails, standalone Doctor refuses repair and restores the service it stopped, including suspended Windows task autostart, with backup and retry guidance. Fast preparation and the update driver's existing optional-capture policy are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture timer previously only aborted a signal: plugin inventory did not observe it, and fresh shared-state snapshot preparation did not receive it. Capture failures also returned warnings that allowed standalone repair to proceed. This change propagates cancellation through fresh and reused inventories, keeps the deadline alive while waiting, and refuses unbacked standalone repair. Only the contractually read-only inventory callback is raced; admitted native capture work still settles before service restoration.

Mandatory capture also needs to preserve the orphan rows Doctor is supposed to repair. Under existing exclusive custody of a closed, checkpointed SQLite source, ordinary original capture now uses the existing private raw-copy producer and retains foreign-key findings with a warning. Physical quick checks still refuse corruption; explicit full verification, generic rollback, and durable journal/WAL acquisition retain strict checks. These original images carry no clean generation receipt or automatic restoration authority.

The reported Windows native stack remains unknown. Source also corrects the report's bracket: task suspension happens during stop preparation; `beginMutation()` only disables early recovery. The disabled task therefore does not independently prove that `prepareRepair()` had started. This PR fixes a deterministic never-settling inventory path, without claiming to fix synchronous or unkillable kernel I/O stalls.

## Evidence

- RED on the original owners: inventory cancellation never settles; managed preparation hangs on timeout and permits repair after capture failure. The fast control passes.
- GREEN: focused regression proves timeout/failure refuse preparation, restore task autostart, restart the fake managed service, and verify health; fast preparation remains successful. Late inventory results cannot admit later resources.
- Landlock + Bubblewrap host-contained production `prepareRepair()` proof: a 33,607,680-byte synthetic agent database and all 13 declared plugin payloads were captured, sealed, and verified in 9.665 s of test time (49.90 s wrapper including cold test compilation). No live Gateway, service units, containers, or operator state were used.
- 135 unique focused tests pass across the changed owners and affected siblings. The corrected backup owner passes 37/37 (86.18 s wrapper); all 15 schema-flow consumer cases pass and verify that original capture retains the damaged rows; reuse passes 9/9 (93.29 s wrapper), including native cancellation settlement. Targeted noEmit types, formatting, and diff checks pass. Targeted lint passed before the final malformed-callback guard and archive correction; exact-head CI supplies final broad lint/build proof. No full local product build or published-driver upgrade was run; the earlier lint wrapper automatically prepared SDK declarations.
- First-head CI run 41167390016 exposed four schema-flow failures caused by this PR's mandatory capture. The correction identifies the installation in those standalone fixtures and preserves relational evidence before repair; physical corruption still fails capture. The next head exposed only a fixture `prefer-array-find` lint error; its one-line correction passes the four affected schema cases (71.76 s wrapper) and an independent Codex P0–P2 delta review. Final-head CI results are recorded below.
- Fresh independent shared autoreview, Codex P0–P2, complete staged candidate against `c993c8f2a51a`: scoped-clean, zero findings (final source verification complete). The index-only orphan-repair finding from the preceding review was addressed by staging the correction with the refusal. The subsequent fixture-only lint correction also passed independent Codex P0–P2 review. Platform-specific native stalls were not reproduced by review.
- Simplification: existing cancellation, snapshot, and recovery owners; no new manager, schema, or public configuration. Production growth +64 lines; net regression growth +216 lines, exactly allocated for inventory cancellation/late results, managed-service failure/fast controls, and original-image integrity. The growth in the backup owner is needed to preserve damaged original data while refusing unsafe repair.

- Final exact-head CI: [run 41169622568](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41169622568) succeeded at `9ac0a94ea2ae5442c52d37932961892d02536bfc` (50 successful jobs, 26 skipped, zero failures). title: feat(workers): bind cleanup to recorded cloud resources
body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Cloud worker recovery and cleanup need a durable binding to the original provider resource, rather than relying only on a reusable lease handle after a lost reply or restart.

Original work and design by @galiniliev; extracted and reimplemented at the contributor's request.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1c21e0ea-e918-4f4d-a25f-a46256a029bd)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9e5ce302-c947-42c1-9be1-a5254aa17cf2)

## User Impact

New Crabbox Azure Sandbox workers record exact resource identity before setup/enrollment. Restart recovery refuses replacement identities, unavailable observations preserve ownership, and Stop remains pending until exact-resource deletion is confirmed.

**This is a prerequisite, not retained-disk activation.** Gateway checkpoints, existing idle suspension, and workspace authority remain unchanged. It enables neither retained allocation nor pause/resume nor disk-authoritative workspaces. Legacy environments without receipts keep their fixed-lease cleanup contract and are not silently rebound. Dependent lifecycle implementation is separately published in #189346, above authority #189106.

Shared-state schema **36 → 37** preserves old rows with a null receipt and fences older binaries. Rollback requires settling new environments and pending cleanup, then restoring the matching pre-upgrade backup with its binary; a package-only downgrade is unsafe. PostgreSQL migration and generated predecessor descriptors are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

An optional generic provider receipt contract feeds the existing environment writer, provisioning, inspection, and teardown owners. Crabbox alone interprets Azure-specific identity and CLI flags. Receipt custody commits before subsequent setup effects; retries retain the original allocation and immutable identity. No separate manager, timer, queue, or state file is introduced. SSH bootstrap and Crabbox teardown phases are extracted without changing ownership to keep modules bounded. The **781-line** regression allocation is task-specific; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Initial provider/recovery proof: **56 tests across 5 files**; real-worker store/migration proof: **10 tests**, repeated after main integration. Existing store/projection coverage also passed 25 cases.
- CI repairs fixed receipt-column omissions, PostgreSQL physical column ordering, enrollment/teardown owner handling, predecessor schema composition, optional-fragment foreign keys in historical fixtures, and confirmed teardown settlement during Gateway drain.
- Repair proof included **110 placement/provisioning consumer tests across 6 files**, **13 tooling tests**, **24 lifecycle tests**, and **29 migration/descriptor/provider tests**.
- Later qualified **37 real PostgreSQL integration tests across 2 files** on CI's pinned pgvector image with its extensions and lock setting. This supersedes the earlier skipped PostgreSQL execution. The task container was stopped and reconciled absent.
- **37 migration/credential/cleanup consumer tests across 6 files**, **2 strengthened drain tests**, and **18 affected receipt/image-intent/drain/migration tests across 4 files** passed. Ten unchanged Doctor tests also passed locally; that replay alone was not claimed as a repair of the earlier merge-only failure.
- Targeted production/test typing, type-aware lint, formatting, canonical generation, native schema parity, regression-budget/line-cap checks, and pre-commit passed. Initial committed SDK comparison acknowledgment: **4a99ee35**.
- Fresh independent P0–P3 autoreview covered the original change and subsequent repairs, with source verification and no remaining actionable findings. Generated catalog review was partition-limited; regeneration, complete schema-owner context, and migration tests provide cross-catalog evidence.
- A local fixture CLI exercised the actual stop boundary: baseline deleted a simulated replacement; the fixed implementation refused the replacement and preserved it.

## Current conflict repair and CI

Published head: **f4255b1d506b4bbe135f05c93ede950632172d06**; tested tree: **17b921cb2e20123acfc0fb2a6e430d0fdd728923**. The publisher's attributed marker commit preserves that complete tested tree.

History-preserving main integration at **ef60dd054202b29fc88da7b460f0594266faf2ff** resolved the sole conflict by regenerating the canonical SQLite catalog. Shared-state remains37; authority38 and retained lifecycle39 are excluded. Hosted readback confirms the conflict is cleared, with this PR still open and unmerged.

On the merged source:
- Canonical schema generation/verification and Kysely freshness passed; generator and catalog-equivalence suites passed.
- Receipt store/migration/provider boundary: **15 tests across three files passed**. Crabbox receipt/stop siblings: **14 tests across two files passed**.
- **56 update tests across four files passed**, including the previously failing Node-prefix, incompatible-service-runtime, writable-launcher, and target-schema cases. Main already contains owner fixture repair **20ab8ecd0dacb1e** (#189226); this PR does not independently weaken those assertions. The old candidate-admission suite was reorganized upstream and was not separately selected in this focused replay.
- Script typing and whitespace checks passed. Simplification retained the existing design; no new production mechanism was needed for the merge.
- Fresh three-pass P0–P3 autoreview against ef60dd054 completed. One reported Azure stop-recovery finding was rejected after source verification: receipts are produced/parsed only for azure-sandbox, and provisioning/destruction reject a differing provider before stop, so the azure-only legacy recovery branch cannot receive a valid receipt. Generated-catalog review remains partition-limited, covered by canonical regeneration and equivalence tests.

Current-head [CI run 41208499615](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41208499615), attempt1, completed **failed: 152 passed, 2 failed, 19 skipped**. All update-runtime shards, types/lint, all PostgreSQL shards, and iOS evidence passed. One memory-core assertion failed; the second failure is the aggregate gate. The executed synthetic merge was f37eefb03c0a51b459e1c59acda6799458005a91 (base88b56eea, headf4255b1d). Complete attached-check inventory at finalization: **186 success, 44 skipped, 3 failure, 1 neutral; none pending**. The third attached failure is the separate protected aggregate [publisher 41210377330](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210377330), not another product-test failure.

The remaining failure is manager-publication-admission.test.ts:349, expecting a parent-process PRAGMA integrity_check observation after an unclean reopen. Its test and observer helper are unchanged from main; the admission owner blob is identical at pinned ef60dd054, CI base88b56eea, and this head. Upstream84bfd8a4 (#189247) moved required scans into the integrity worker and changed lease-less unclean reopening to bounded admission. The old helper only wraps its own process DatabaseSync, so its integrityChecked:false result does not establish a skipped required worker scan. This is a source-attributed inherited assertion mismatch, not an observed exact-base replay. A focused local attempt timed out during runtime compilation before a test verdict; no assertion or safety guard was weakened. Failed CI is retained. The finalizer fetched the actual executed merge object, reproduced its tree from ordered base/head parents, and verified all ten determining sources are identical at the actual CI baseline, tested merge and PR head. Any landing uses the native inherited-failure evidence route, with review, security and live writer gates still enforced.

### Prior-head failure evidence

Head8042bdde [run41188657688](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41188657688) failed: **149 passed, 5 failed, 19 skipped**. Four runtime shards contained five update assertions; the fifth failure was the aggregate gate. They reproduced locally (5 failed/54 passed), with determining sources byte-identical to pinned main64daa256. The newer main integration includes the upstream fixture correction; it does not relabel that failed run as passing. PostgreSQL and iOS screenshots passed on the old run; that iOS pass did not establish a fix for the earlier missing Mermaid accessibility assertion.

## Exact installed-upgrade qualification

Native [run 41243053820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41243053820) passed the installed receipt cell in **282.359s**, command/wrapper exit 0 and settled. Actual installed **and serving** identities changed from published stable `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41` to exact candidate `f4255b1d506b4bbe135f05c93ede950632172d06`; the assertion checks build IDs, not the equal version label. title: fix(cron): bound runs before runner startup and retain cancellation
body:
Related: #143624, #123419. Adjacent watchdog work: #184460 and #160804.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation can remain running indefinitely when its runner never reports startup, and disabling it can fail to cancel after run tracking is retired.

## User Impact

Finite automation deadlines now cover admission, setup, execution, and delivery. Disabling an active occurrence still cancels its exact runner after registry retirement, allowing another forced run after settlement. Busy-session waits now consume the configured job budget; unlimited jobs remain unlimited. Existing live-work and receipt fences remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferred watchdog previously armed only its setup timer, which lane waiting clears; the wall-clock timer started only at `noteRunnerStarted`. Start that timer at entry instead. Bind marker cancellation directly to its captured handle rather than looking it up in a registry that teardown can clear. This removes the superseded lookup helper and introduces no new state or options.

A reported shared-session automation remained running past its 1700-second deadline after a Code Mode bridge error, with no active agent run or terminal cron record. The journal confirms that sequence, but does not establish where its agent promise stopped. The bridge catch already settles its failed reply; this repair targets the independently reproduced cron timeout and cancellation gaps rather than changing recoverable tool-error semantics.

## Evidence

- Base: `298546d88934bf05bc7e208d13bf6ce2c538e3f2`. Real cron timer/runner owners with held external runners: both no-start cases fail on base because no `TimeoutError` is raised; durable-disable-after-retirement fails because its controller remains un-aborted. Both pass after the fix, with terminal `timed_out` history, cleared `runningAtMs`, and successful forced re-admission after settlement.

Related: #188796 ## What Problem This Solves An attached cloud session can wait for a reconnect that cannot happen after its enrolled node process exits, even though the dedicated worker and workspace still exist. Retained-worker wake can reach the same dead end before ordinary runtime recovery runs. ## User Impact Recover the same enrolled node on eligible dedicated Linux Crabbox workers without allocating a replacement, reinstalling the runtime, pairing again, rerunning repository setup or replaying interrupted input. Preserve the resource binding, identity, configuration and workspace. Unsupported providers, desktop workers and records without saved runtime identity retain reconnect-only behavior; older runtime packages without the private consumer need an update or manual recovery. Adopt released [Crabbox v0.81.0](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/releases/tag/v0.81.0) through the canonical managed-distribution owner. It contains the landed native command-lifetime repair in [Crabbox #3001](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/3001). Existing configured distributions are not overwritten. No new public timeout/configuration, schema, retention policy, paid allocation or live deployment. ## Why This Change Was Made - Add an optional provider recovery operation under the existing runtime-refresh owner. Current requester/attachment/owner authority, an active dedicated inspection and the exact persisted resource receipt must qualify launch. - Retained wake already holds the environment operation lock. It calls the same internal resumer before waiting for reconnect, without reacquiring that lock or creating a second lifecycle owner. Current main's retention, prepared-intent, lease-inspection and bootstrap owners remain intact. - Compose two ordinary existing Crabbox invocations: read-only saved identity/runtime inspection, fresh host authority assertion, then separately admitted launch. Launch repeats package/PID checks; the canonical runner verifies the saved device, configuration and paired credential. - Private launcher IPC prevents an uncommitted detached child from entering the node runtime after its owner disappears. Publish the PID receipt atomically before commitment and wait for actual child exit on precommit cancellation. Retain an uncertain committed process/receipt for a subsequent probe rather than blindly replaying it. - Use one measured private 120-second work budget across both phases, still bounded by caller admission. Forward the existing cleanup-grace option with 20 seconds for this operation so the controller can finish its existing 15-second cleanup and full 5-second native TERM grace. No new public Crabbox command protocol, identity reader or core manager. ## Evidence ### Source and focused regression coverage Qualified local commit 4a9976e91405f709f96c085ecb933efa8658ba15, tree ac40b5077f476fa38e29d8f561ac5252144dfc9e, integrated with pinned main b2ceef2b5a5fbd8c88ff8497b8a986c692204141 because the published branch conflicted. All 16 production modules match the source-bound released-runtime proof. - Exercised all 11 affected/helper test files across their six owning shards (261 cases in the initial cohort). Preserved failures rather than treating them as flakes: an obsolete offline-cache version, an invalid dormant inspection fixture, an incorrect seeded-credential assumption and unread stderr in the launcher disconnect fixture. - Final complete retained-lifecycle and managed-binary suites: **10 + 33 passed**. Both launcher commit/disconnect cases pass with normal stderr draining and unchanged timeout/assertions. Unmodified passing cases were reused; exact published-head CI is separate evidence. - **Owning-boundary RED control:** both new retained service regressions fail with the exact pre-fix retained owner from pinned main: no restart before reconnect wait, and a replacement resource is not rejected. The qualified owner was restored byte-for-byte; both cases pass with the fix. This is an exact owning-module control within the integration, not a claim that the entire base checkout was tested. - Targeted TypeScript, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace and test-line gates pass. Allocation is exactly **828** net regression lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. - Fresh independent production and final regression reviews found no actionable P0–P3 issues. Committed-range autoreview is **scoped-clean**, with no findings. Its static-review limits do not replace executed runtime proof or CI. ### Actual released controller/native runtime Canonical installation and resolution selected the released distribution with normal adjacent-pack discovery, not a private artifact override: | Input | SHA-256 | | --- | --- | | Linux amd64 release archive | 1d25267b161c1ac6c12c15cd7c4cb96a49a8c1622d365fb932f3ef3bd3123d33 | | Controller | 20d0cb5b592f339a2928139909f1f95990f28f7a03558ee9f570bf9171f3876c | | Adjacent native manifest | f0a5abfc81ccbf1e8f9e8efd61a271dfb97c56110f271c225efeeb7a54985d16 | | Linux amd64 native runtime | 2fa8b9ac1250bdbbe6f291c2084bd1ae0f46a34337ba962de9c7474060f88c7b | An isolated Gateway, genuinely paired node and real OpenSSH ran inside task-owned rootless Debian. The full current generated enrollment/trust command ran real certificate registration before node launch, without modifying host trust. | Case | Observed result | | --- | --- | | Same-device reconnect | 74.1 seconds; existing device/runtime/workspace retained | | Retry | 70.2 seconds; reused the same committed PID and device | | Cancel held read-only identity inspection | Child exited; original dead-PID receipt unchanged; five exact retirements before return | | Revoke host authority during held inspection | Fresh host assertion rejects launch; no new connection; five exact retirements before return | | Cancel actual detached child before commit | Child exited; original receipt preserved; no later node effect; ten exact retirements before return | Recovery and retry each confirmed ten native completion/retirement records before provider return. Production 20-second cleanup and full 5-second native grace were not shortened. A delayed/unobservable remote wrapper remains explicitly uncertain: local exit or absent remote state is never remote quiescence and does not authorize automatic replay. ### Proof limits and retained failures - Two original cancellation harness runs exited 1 because the old oracle counted the canonical enrollment's initial connection. Their raw reports remain failed; an independent corrected oracle verifies no new connection, actual child exit, unchanged receipt and exact retirement. They are not relabeled as original-script exit-zero runs. - QA used the canonical npm-verification branch, not fresh bootstrap-archive installation. The released controller and adjacent native inputs were hashed and real native dispatch/receipts observed; an independent remote executable rehash was not captured before normal cleanup. - The earlier one-shot authority failure and v0.80 retirement defect remain historical evidence. The existing-API split addresses the reported held-probe case; a new public commit protocol was not necessary. Earlier maintenance CI was never proof that the one-shot implementation was safe to ship. - This is local Linux/static-SSH and service-boundary proof, not a new paid cloud allocation or a replay of separate R5/installed acceptance runs. No live Gateway/profile deployment or new Crabbox release occurred. All 15 owned proof containers and three task images were removed after verifying they were stopped; no proof Gateway/node/sshd remains. A temporary compiler-input scan conflict from the proof image filesystem was resolved by owned-resource cleanup, not a guard/ignore change. Original failure logs and source/artifact receipts are retained. Contributor credit: @galiniliev authored the S4 source commit `9501dfaa8de7426a02badffd918e8eddc75c9e27` that informed this bounded extraction, reimplemented against current upstream owners at his request. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1c21e0ea-e918-4f4d-a25f-a46256a029bd) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/d50d6742-c669-438e-9779-276e1117ca73) - [Existing-command split review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/8769e9c5-906b-4f16-988d-626eac19a170) - [CI synthetic-merge compatibility repair](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4489e496-7aa8-43f3-a3fa-d3a5939bee9a) - [Final canonical-owner maintenance review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b1e047e9-2553-47d0-adb4-788ba261b590) - [Final cancellation and settlement review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9fc975e2-8c3b-426a-a370-b55eaccbc29d)
Earlier verification sessions - [Exact-base Stop recovery attribution](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/fafc6631-200a-4324-9b09-b753b63b4048) - [Real transport cancellation investigation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f1c1f0fb-88a9-4f27-9a1d-8f1e187e824b) - [CI synchronization follow-up](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/390ea07d-039d-4083-9d51-32d016ee34c7) - [Local Crabbox controller preparation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/92b15a87-7505-4ee6-9fb5-625340e35cf8) - [Final bounded independent review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2136e4a4-fa16-4804-8ee2-ac906264351f)
## Worked on by - @galiniliev

Related: #188335

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: npm plugins become unavailable when an update rolls core back after replacing them with plugins that require the newer core.

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

## User Impact

User impact: rollback restores the compatible plugin cohort and its settings, while preserving later independent plugin and config changes. This does not backport recovery into older released updater parents.

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain plugin install transactions until activation verification, and journal their owned artifact, record and config preimages in the existing update recovery owner. Reopened repair reacquires live custody and compares before restoring. Database restore retains only the exact recovery pair. The legacy reservation stays unchanged for released readers.

<!--

Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

## Evidence

- Pinned main `edeae71308d8` reproduced the registered-updater failure: core rolled back while an incompatible npm plugin remained installed. The candidate restored the exact plugin artifact, record and settings and retained the verified backup.
- Latest canonical package campaign (frozen `358d34b6` plus corrections to the selected Node path, recovery-pair reads and pending failure reporting) passed registered rollback, restored old-core Gateway readiness/read-only RPC, foreground `update.run` with a fresh ready successor, and an untouched published 2026.10.9 → unstamped/unfaulted candidate upgrade. Both foreground and published-parent installed payloads matched **16,835/16,835 files**, with zero permission warnings. Canonical tar SHA-256: `5231adb743dd59426563aefd207b439b044931ee9621d64c11584d31e2ebdd95`.
- PostgreSQL 17 exact-pair restore/repeat/reopen passed; the three CI-failing credential rollback cases passed through the conformance lane. A populated physical witness passed owned migration restoration and refusal of later independent plugin-index/migration writes. Earlier whole-container death/reopen/repeated settlement and exact installed 10.9 reader/admission/cleanup proof remain applicable to unchanged recovery owners.
- The terminal reporting correction has separate regression proof: retained recovery preserves the captured initiating failure, with lost-authority and release-denial siblings retained. This reporting-only branch postdates the package campaign; that campaign does not claim to cover it. Focused native owner/consumer tests, targeted types, lint, formatting and ratchets pass. Fresh independent canonical Codex P0–P2 review of `358d34b6` → repair snapshot `5edd1ac8` completed scoped-clean in one complete pass, with no findings.
- Prior [CI on `358d34b6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41173224990) failed 26 jobs: 17 contained PR-caused failures addressed by this repair, 7 were wholly inherited, 1 was an unreproduced root-help timeout, and 1 was the aggregate. Doctor/X inheritance was reproduced with matching signatures on the actual CI main parent `96e05f7c`; pinned branch-base tests alone were not used as inheritance evidence. The timeout remains an investigated gap.
- [CI on signed repair `6f542fa2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41181159578) completed **114 passed / 12 failed**: five wholly PR-caused jobs, one mixed, five inherited, and the aggregate. Matching main signatures and the source-pinned X replay are detailed below. R7 fixes failed legacy-Doctor rollback through the existing compatible-schema owner and corrects affected authority, process-copy, foreground, and terminal fixtures. [Exact-head CI 41189435747](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41189435747) attempt 1 completed on signed repair `2e60dcd3350f1bc214ee15704744d65882bbbf68`: **90 passed / 24 skipped / 10 failed**, including the aggregate. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. All 21 original PR-caused errors are absent: the five wholly PR-caused jobs pass, and the mixed job retains only its inherited registry assertion. Seven substantive failures match main. R8 single reruns pass for root-help and service-authority; the parent 10:53Z landing ruling classifies those two as one-off non-PR flakes, separately from inherited failures.


- R8 requested one rerun per then-unattributed job: [root-help / attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41189435747/job/124509785351) and [service-authority / attempt 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41189435747/job/124512997230) both **PASS**. Final latest-three scheduled main logs have no matching root-help timeout, and the exact service case passes all three. The parent landing ruling at **2026-10-31 10:53Z** classifies both original failures as **one-off flakes: not PR-caused, and not waived as inherited**. This is an explicit maintainer disposition, not a claim of a matching main signature. Evidence links are below; no source change or new commit was justified.

- R7 focused proof: candidate activation **14/14**, Windows interruption **1/1**, native populated rollback and independent index/migration writers **3/3**, lease child boundaries **8/8**, terminal outcomes **12/12**, and foreground/index/compatibility consumers **8/8** pass. The strengthened failed-Doctor regression is red on `6f542fa2` and green with the repair, including exact previous package/config bytes. Type-aware lint, targeted CLI-update types, formatting, diff sanity, and the staged test-line ratchet pass. R7 adds exactly **22 LF** to its existing allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.

- Fresh independent canonical **Codex P0–P2** review of `6f542fa2` → staged tree `5add90c9` completed **scoped-clean**, one complete pass, no findings. Signed commit [`2e60dcd3350f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2e60dcd3350f1bc214ee15704744d65882bbbf68) has that exact tree. Modern Doctor delegation also passes **12/12**. Candidate file test time was 223.37s (235.82s Vitest file duration) (26-case command including delegation: 288.31s wall); the longer native fixtures exercise actual process admission, package compensation and SQLite boundaries.

The earlier canonical package and published-parent upgrade campaign predates R7. R7 proof exercises the changed rollback and native process boundaries; no new full package campaign was run.

Rollback failure injection and the foreground next-version stamp are test-only; the published-parent upgrade has neither. Linux proof does not qualify other operating systems or model inference. Older released-parent failed-rollback/backport compatibility and #188335's separate lease issue remain unresolved.

The separate +3,529 regression-test LF allocation covers distinct artifact/index/config, native handoff, cancellation, recovery and affected-consumer failures; the shared ceiling scalar is unchanged. Simplification reuses the existing owner and removes duplicate terminal scopes, hand-built cohort contexts, and a mock-only assertion. Necessary native fixture growth keeps actual delegated executor/Doctor boundaries under test.

title: fix: worktree sessions load their own bootstrap instructions
body:
Supersedes #129413, thanks @krell11

Fixes #129411

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worktree sessions receiving bootstrap instructions from the shared agent checkout instead of their recorded workspace.

## User Impact

Recorded worktree sessions use their own bootstrap files, including `AGENTS.md` and `SOUL.md`, while skill discovery stays anchored to the configured agent workspace. Runs restricted by `workspaceOnly` use their execution workspace. A cwd override alone does not change bootstrap identity.

Missing files have **no fallback to the shared checkout or a packaged template**. A worktree without `AGENTS.md` behaves like running the harness directly in that directory: no project instructions. OpenClaw retains its normal missing-file diagnostics. Rejected symlink paths and workspace escapes are logged and treated as missing; guarded reads remain inside the selected root. Other read failures retain their unreadable diagnostics.

**Native Codex boundary:** native project-document discovery remains Codex's documented loader operating on its cwd and permissions, including native symlink behavior. A native session whose cwd is the worktree already loads that worktree's documents. This PR changes neither native configuration nor the native loader and adds no in-memory defaults.

**Needs deploy:** affects Team worktree sessions directly; deploy after landing. No live Gateway changes were made during development.

## Why This Change Was Made

One selector in `workspace-run.ts` chooses the bootstrap root for embedded and CLI preparation. Bootstrap loading retains its existing session filters, budgets, and guarded filesystem reads. Skills resolve their configured anchor independently, so changing bootstrap cannot move the agent skill tier when a reusable snapshot is absent.

Production delta is **+19 lines**: the selector and its callers establish the recorded boundary, the skills change preserves independent ownership, and the loader preserves its diagnostic while marking typed symlink/escape rejections missing. The orchestrator adds zero lines. Shared workspace input types and duplicate config guards were consolidated in the same owner; there is no registry lookup, new state, or native configuration path. The separate test-line allocation covers 100 net lines of regression/support coverage.

## Evidence

- All five bootstrap/CLI regressions fail on main before the fix, as does the snapshot-less configured-skills regression. All six pass with the fix.
- Consumer run: **258 passed**, including bootstrap privacy/remote/memory consumers, workspace reads/cache, CLI preparation, embedded runtime, configured skills, native workspace snapshots, and prompt-prefix stability. Three existing library-read assertions fail identically with all six changed production modules restored from main: they expect `/regular file/i`, while the maintained filesystem reader reports `symlink path component not allowed`. This is retained as an investigated baseline failure, not counted as a passing test.
- Targeted lint, targeted typecheck of changed tests and their production import graph, formatting, `git diff --check`, and both production/full-tree unused-file scans pass. No full live-model proof was run.
- Final changed-file runs pass: CLI preparation **112 tests / 87.83s wall**, bootstrap preparation **19 tests / 10.63s**, and skills preparation **6 tests / 7.30s**. The correction recognizes only typed symlink/escape failures. The affected workspace/read/bootstrap suites pass **89 tests**, and atomic publication passes **7 tests**; targeted lint and typecheck pass again.

title: fix(visitor-access): reject oversized Cloudflare responses
body:
Supersedes #132491, thanks @RileyJJY.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes excessive Gateway memory use when Cloudflare returns an unexpectedly large Visitor Access policy response.

## User Impact

Responses above 16 MiB are rejected and their streams canceled before the full body is buffered. Normal responses continue to work. The same bound applies to discovery and mutation confirmations, including best-effort provider cleanup; an oversized confirmation requires policy inspection before retrying. Existing durable cleanup retries remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing Plugin SDK provider JSON reader instead of implementing another size limiter. Removing the mutable read result and its surrounding try/catch offsets the SDK import: production code is **−2 lines** (+3/−5). The README documents the limit.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `9f14244a6067e9ca0e22d1a2b8c5150e9cb7c693`: the new production-client regression failed because a valid streamed 32 MiB JSON response was accepted (25 passed, 1 failed; exit 1). With the fix, a 1 MiB response succeeds and a 32 MiB response is rejected and canceled before completion.
- Focused Cloudflare and visitor-service suites: **83 passed**, 1.12 s Vitest / 4.14 s command wall time. Complete `test:extension visitor-access --maxWorkers=1`: **116 passed**, 55.44 s Vitest / 62.44 s wall time, including plugin lifecycle, restart, and cleanup coverage. title: fix(backup): truncated archive verification hangs before restore
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes backup verification hanging before restore when a PostgreSQL archive has a truncated gzip stream.

## User Impact

Damaged archives now fail promptly and close their temporary file handles. Archive verification keeps its existing single-pass behavior and corruption checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The streamed verification introduced in #188518 could throw while canceling an entry without an error listener, leaving another consumer waiting with an open file handle. Cancel every active consumer without re-emitting the error, then stop reading if cancellation occurs during a file write. The existing corruption test also checks that all opened handles close.

title: improve: reduce repeated work while tailing Gateway logs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Each live Logs poll traverses the retained window separately for filtering and key indexing, allocating temporary tuples and row/index objects even when all filters are disabled.

## User Impact

Logs polling performs less preparation work. No visible behavior change is intended; the retained buffer remains capped at 2,000 lines, and filters, export order, row keys, and scroll following keep their existing contracts. No latency improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

One existing view derivation now builds a fresh ordered row array and key-to-index map in one pass, with the default-filter decision made once per batch. This removes the separate mapped index without adding state or caching. Measured-window keys still resolve against the same current snapshot, including index zero; the virtualizer and post-commit scroll compensation are unchanged.

## Evidence

The exact mounted production Logs route/sidebar census driver and one identical Babel instrumenter ran on base `f5381735e51d366879d398db3c622fefa6e4a18a` and the candidate. I/O is an in-process Gateway fixture and layout is synthetic jsdom geometry. The workload seeds 2,000 rows, then follows 100 batches of 20 lines, plus scrolled-up, text/level-filtered, follow-off, status/presence/sidebar and empty-poll controls.

| Count over 100 following batches | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained source row visits | 400,000 | 200,000 |
| Default-path predicate calls | 200,000 | 0 |
| Temporary index tuple arrays | 200,000 | 0 |
| Temporary row/index value objects | 200,000 | 0 |
| Key-index entries written | 200,000 | 200,000 |
| New-line parses | 2,000 | 2,000 |
| Mounted row constructions | 1,597 | 1,597 |
| Virtual key calls | 603,040 | 603,040 |
| Logs scrollHeight reads | 970 | 970 |
| Logs DOM added / removed nodes | 13,943 / 13,948 | 13,943 / 13,948 |
| logs.tail RPCs | 100 | 100 |

Every preserved per-action parse/format, row/list/key, geometry, DOM and RPC count matches; visible rows, retained DOM identity, cursors and scroll offsets match for all controls. Active-search predicates and normalization bytes remain unchanged. Allocations above are observed source literal executions, not a VM allocation profile. The benefit is modest for a bounded window polled every two seconds.

- Regression is red on base (64 level reads instead of six) and green on the candidate; it also checks index zero and independently expected export order.
- Logs view/page/data: 28 tests pass across three files (3.19 s Vitest wall time). Formatting, diff checks and test-line ratchet pass; no test-line allocation is required.
- Production: +5 net lines; tests: +33. pr-simplify completed. Independent Codex autoreview (P0–P3, local candidate against `f5381735`) completed scoped-clean with no findings.

title: fix(normalization): prevent native-value fingerprint collisions
body:
Fixes #133231

Supersedes #133232, thanks @Avi974.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes identical plugin/cache fingerprints for distinct Date, RegExp, Set and Map values passed to the shared stable serializer.

## User Impact

Existing plain JSON values retain byte-for-byte serialization and all existing hashes, including current undefined handling. Native values now have deterministic, distinct type-tagged encodings. Set and Map insertion order does not affect identity; numeric and string Map keys stay distinct.

Compatibility decision: an unsupported native-valued input recorded before upgrade can fail closed when retried against an effect-bearing durable fingerprint. This explicit conflict/rejection is accepted: it prevents duplicate effects and silent acceptance of distinct values. No shipped producer of these native values was found at those durable boundaries. Supported JSON inputs remain unchanged. No legacy-hash fallback, guard weakening, schema migration, or new configuration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared traversal previously collapsed these native values to empty objects. Untagged ISO/regex strings or collection arrays would introduce collisions with ordinary JSON, so this replacement uses `Date(...)`, `RegExp(...)`, `Set([...])` and `Map([...])`. These are canonical fingerprint text, not a JSON interchange format; ordinary JSON output is unchanged. The existing string-returning and streaming entrypoints continue sharing one traversal.

The earlier autoreview P2 requested durable-fingerprint compatibility handling under a cache-miss requirement. The maintainer resolved that requirement on 2026-10-31: durable effect-bearing mismatches must continue to reject. The isolated upgrade proof below confirms the fail-closed behavior; it does not duplicate work. Retaining old collapsed-hash acceptance would keep the collision, and treating an idempotency conflict as a cache miss could repeat effects. The P2 is resolved by this explicit contract decision. Final-head autoreview with this context is clean for P0–P2.

| Effect-bearing durable consumer | Supported input / upgrade behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Pending-input `request_hash` (`session-accessor.pending-input-request.ts:19`, `pending-inputs.ts:356-357`) | Shipped transcript producers build JSON/scalar messages; stored recovery uses JSON.parse. Supported hashes are unchanged. Arbitrary native metadata supplied programmatically can change the hash and explicitly rejects an old accepted-input conflict. Verified with the real isolated SQLite completion owner. |
| Native-subagent collector replay (`plugin-native-subagent.ts:311,335-342`) | Scalar spawn arguments plus JSON Schema; registered profiles enforce bounded JSON. No bundled native schema producer found. An unprofiled plugin supplying unsupported native schema annotations can get a replay conflict after upgrade; the duplicate-child guard remains intact. |
| Code Mode collector replay (`code-mode-swarm.runtime.ts:144,151-155`) | Guest arguments cross JSON.stringify/JSON.parse before hashing. Supported persisted fingerprints are unchanged; actual differing launch requests continue to reject. |
| Worker inference / transcript `request_hash` (`worker-environments/inference.ts:497`, `transcript-commit.runtime.ts:272`) | Parsed/validated JSON worker protocol and scalar claims. Supported stored hashes are unchanged; accepted-request conflicts continue to reject. |
| Worker preparation identity (`worker-environments/preparation-identity.ts:76`) | Normal profile settings are parsed JSON. Unsupported native programmatic settings can select a new cache/workspace identity; attempting incompatible in-place dedicated-node registration explicitly rejects (`node-worker-prepared-workspace-store.kernel.ts:118-129`). No duplicate effect or guard bypass. |

The Google prompt cache is a real cache: a changed native-containing cache-config digest returns null and creates a fresh cache. Installed-plugin index comparisons return false and refresh/recheck the install. Diagnostic digest changes remain readable. The complete caller table below distinguishes these cache/display paths from effect-bearing records.

## Evidence

- **Red before, real caller:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-hash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on main production code: only **7** fingerprints for **21** distinct fixtures; expected 21.
- **Golden compatibility before/after:** seven fixed fixtures pin recursive object ordering, arrays, booleans, null, number formatting, Unicode/escapes, empty containers and existing undefined handling. The golden expectations pass on main and the replacement without changed expected bytes.
- **Green after:** both focused files pass, **22 tests** across two shards. Final wall time **3.87s**; Vitest file durations **0.232s** (plugin hash) and **0.614s** (serializer). Includes native-vs-JSON separation, type-preserving Map keys, Set/Map ordering, cycles, normalization and streaming/hash parity. CI timing will be provided by the attached checks.
- **Upgrade boundary:** synthetic Date metadata accepted/completed through real `stageSessionPendingInput` under main replays as `consumed` under main. Replaying the identical input against the candidate explicitly rejects with `Input completion idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`, as accepted above. This is isolated production-owner evidence, not a claim of a normal-input production incident or a full Gateway/model upgrade test.
- Targeted serializer typecheck passes. Focused lint (including oxlint/Bun parity), formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Test-line ratchet passes with an exact **88-line** allocation for these independent compatibility/collision regressions.
- **Fresh review:** canonical autoreview, Codex engine, P0–P2, base `05b5ac42231c0fbefa1f9aed56401df201052d77` → head `7c1ff6dddc924c1751734612123213700d6e1ca7`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Consequential unchanged durable-consumer source and the resolved compatibility ruling were supplied.
- **Simplification:** production **+18/-22, net −4 LOC**. Consolidated duplicate Error/Uint8Array recursion and array accumulation in the existing owner. Tests **net +88 LOC**; allocation is regression-specific and leaves the shared scalar unchanged.
- Contributor code was read with `gh pr view/diff` only; it was never checked out, installed, built or run. Proof used trusted main and independently implemented source in rootless Podman capped at 4 CPUs / 8 GB, with isolated synthetic state. No live Gateway was changed.

<details>
<summary>All 89 direct production stableStringify/hashStableJson caller files and persistence effects</summary>

Audit pinned to trusted main `05b5ac42231c0fbefa1f9aed56401df201052d77`; listed line numbers refer to that source. No direct extension callers. Native-containing inputs change only where the previously-colliding native types occur. All supported JSON/scalar hashes retain their bytes. The fail-closed unsupported-input outcomes in this table are accepted by the compatibility decision above.

### Agent callers (all 27 production files with direct calls)

All existing plain-JSON bytes remain unchanged. “Native changes” below means only an input containing Date/RegExp/Set/Map; it does not mean the normal workflow admits those values.

| Caller | Persistence and compatibility decision |
| --- | --- |
| `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts:139,943` | No persisted fingerprint. MCP capability/root runtime context key; changed native inputs select/create a separate in-memory client view (`:945-958`). |

The digest is same-operation SQLite worker admission/receipt verification (`:158-180`). `normalizeUserModelAuthProfile` round-trips schema-validated JSON before hashing (`src/state/user-model-accounts.ts:198-208`), so native values do not cross this boundary. |

| `src/agents/code-mode-swarm.runtime.ts:144` | Persisted `swarmLaunchRequestFingerprint`; mismatch intentionally rejects duplicate launches (`:151-155`). Normal inputs are projected scalar fields plus JSON-schema object. Code Mode guest arguments are JSON.stringify/JSON.parse before this caller (`code-mode-controller-source.ts:216`, `code-mode-node.worker.ts:286`); native values are already projected to JSON before hashing, so stored fingerprints do not change. |

| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/google-prompt-cache.ts:117,316,325` | `cacheConfigDigest` persists in custom transcript entries. Native tool-schema values could change that digest; `readLatestGooglePromptCacheEntry` returns null when the key differs (`:102-137`), causing a fresh cache creation path, not an error. The outer match key is strings/scalars. |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-history.ts:42,46,53,110` | No persisted fingerprints. Message/record/value digest WeakMaps (`:20-33`) serve current-process prefix observations; native differences refresh/change observations, not stored-data admission. |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-observability.ts:393,476` | Diagnostic tool-schema/tool-list digests in bounded in-memory trackers and emitted prompt snapshots. Native schema digest changes register a tool change (`:365-371`); no durable fingerprint admission or migration error. |

| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-prompt-state.ts:153-155` | Compares tool parameters against transcript-backed tool definitions, not a stored serializer hash. Native/schema differences mark the tool surface changed and write a new checkpoint (`:213-243`), rather than reject stored data. Published schemas use their canonical JSON fingerprint; restored transcript payloads are JSON. |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-history.ts:137` | No persisted fingerprint. Equality comparison between user transcript/runtime content; native changes affect only that comparison, with timestamp matching fallback (`:141-145`). |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-runtime-prepare.ts:223` | Tool-policy digest retained in transcript tool-surface checkpoints. Inputs are selected config tools/plugin/desktop fields (`:224-227`) from JSON config. Stored JSON fingerprints do not change; changed policy starts a new pin (`session-prompt-state.ts:181-200`). |
| `src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts:211` | Parsed provider-error JSON serialization for classification/presentation; no durable fingerprint. Native types cannot originate in the parsed error JSON. |
| `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-events.ts:156` | No persisted fingerprint; captures one invocation's JSON tool input for rewrite comparison. Raw relay payload type is JsonValue (`native-hook-relay-codec.ts:123`); no native input from transport. |
| `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-codec.ts:120` | Counterpart same-invocation comparison. Plugin hook replacement may contain native data and then correctly counts as a rewrite; no stored fingerprint to migrate. |
| `src/agents/mcp-content.ts:114` | Structured-content JSON presentation, not a fingerprint. Ordinary MCP wire values are JSON, so bytes remain unchanged. Direct non-JSON structured content was not a supported MCP wire contract; the new typed syntax is not JSON.parse-able. |
| `src/agents/mcp-structured-mirror.ts:23` | No persisted fingerprint; compares parsed JSON text with MCP structuredContent to suppress duplicate presentation. Native direct values can cease matching plain-JSON mirrors, which preserves the text rather than rejecting data. |
| `src/agents/media-generation-task-status-shared.ts:18` | No persisted fingerprint; media request key is used in process-local operation Maps (`media-generation-activity.ts:37-42`). Native differences cause duplicate-guard misses, not upgrade errors (`:107-135`). |

Valid inputs contain scalar spawn fields and JSON Schema; registered profiles enforce bounded JSON (`src/plugins/registry.ts:187-193,228`). | `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.fingerprint.ts:5` | Shared digest for model-catalog config/env/credential generation facts. title: fix(update): seal recovery captures on large state directories
body:
Fixes #188897

## What Problem This Solves

Large state directories can leave every pre-update recovery capture incomplete because the inventory exceeds a child process's stdout limit.

## User Impact

Recovery captures can now seal with large inventories. Failed optional captures explicitly warn `NO ORIGINAL-STATE SNAPSHOT` while the update continues; the warning remains in returned JSON and update history.

The fix must be installed in the updater performing the capture. A newer candidate cannot repair an older updater process already running. Older candidate workers retain their existing stdout contract and limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Metadata inventories now run in serial batches budgeted by escaped UTF-8 JSON bytes, with room for result fields, one aggregate deadline, and the same caller cancellation signal. Order, duplicates, missing files, and SQLite sidecar sizes are preserved; failure returns no partial inventory or subsequent child after cancellation. The per-child 1 MiB stdout cap stays unchanged.

The sibling audit also found unbounded database-discovery, backup-receipt, schema/generation, and candidate snapshot results. Both launchers now share an opt-in private result-file transport, read after successful process settlement and bounded like the existing recovery manifest. Legacy stdout interoperability and uncertain-cleanup retention remain intact. Payload capture already runs in process; progress backpressure handling needed no change.

Other open proposals for this issue: #188907 and #188912. This PR implements the requested fixed-cap batching design and covers the sibling result transports and warning behavior.

## Evidence

- **RED → GREEN:** main `ae01f1c113826d3ff41463e74da6c115e5b581ff` rejects 12,000 copies of an existing 160-character path with `output-limit`; the fixed owner returns all 12,000. Original-owner controls also reject the ASCII, UTF-8, and quote/backslash cases.
- **Regression proof:** 12,000-entry ASCII/multibyte/escaped inventories, order/duplicates/missing/WAL sizes, cancellation during a later batch, one aggregate deadline, oversized sibling results, and warning visibility in returned JSON pass. New size tests took 1.437 s; sibling transport tests took 8.521 s. Existing backup/budget/schema/lifetime/inventory tests also passed.
- **Real contained capture:** Landlock + Bubblewrap, private synthetic state, 12,000 distinct payload files plus config and real SQLite. Sealed manifest: **12,007 entries / 4,075,036 bytes**. All **12,002 file payloads** were reconstructed and hash-verified; SQLite integrity and sentinel checks passed. Zero capture warnings. Capture plus verification: 57.823 s. Manifest SHA-256: `1fafd9c4b9379d3c2b9ba4bac41d6e5b269f461739a8b14098c81f8de4615995`. No protected-state access, service execution, or TCP activity. This proves capture sealing and payload reconstruction; it does not claim an installed-package upgrade or automatic rollback over active state.
- **Local checks:** production core typecheck, services and CLI-update test typechecks, focused lint, format, diff check, and test-line ratchet pass. The touched CLI suite has **31 passing / 1 failing** test. The unchanged invalid-dev-target existing-state assertion also fails on untouched base `ae01f1c` with the same missing error callback; its same-order five-test prefix has **4 passing / 1 failing**. No retry/ignore/exception masks it. Both capture-warning regressions pass. The candidate resource/legacy-stdout owner suite passes **25/25** under private umask `077`; this host’s default `0002` also exposes an unrelated explicit-temp fixture permission failure on untouched base. No product guard or assertion was relaxed.
- **Simplification:** one batching owner and one transport shared by the two launchers; no raised stdout cap or new manager/config/schema/cache. Production net +103 lines; tests net +184. The exact +184 test allocation covers the requested scale/cancellation/deadline regressions and distinct sibling/JSON-warning boundaries; shared scalar unchanged.
- **Fresh independent review:** Codex autoreview, P0–P2, against base `ae01f1c` and candidate tree `3155ef3d5b5440be3d8ead464cec865ecc1a8b74`: **scoped-clean, zero findings**. Refreshed after the legacy stdout fixture cutover; one complete pass with all 12 changed files and supplied owner/caller context; the isolated reviewer did not execute tests. Helper source SHA-256: `ea4d3415094d50a670f28a1ee092e928a9dbcf7327103014c3a9f909d9a6ef17`.
- **Exact-head CI:** [run 41155734580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41155734580) completed **success** on `ae632d33a5f6366d661b4e781cb10560370e583f`, attempt 1: **45 passed / 26 skipped**, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Final PR checks: **63 passed / 57 skipped**, none failed or pending. Workflow wall time: **1,504 seconds (25m 4s)**. The initial legacy-stdout fixture failure was corrected and verified; no workflow was rerun to chase green.

Design credit: @ourcoms2018 proposed and tested the fixed-cap batching design. Co-authored with @ourcoms2018 and @steipete; both human credits are preserved in the commit trailers.
