title: fix(byteplus): report token usage for streamed responses
body:
Supersedes #127116, thanks @rrmars.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing token counts for streamed `byteplus` and `byteplus-plan` responses when the endpoint requires an explicit usage request.

## User Impact

BytePlus streaming turns request final token counts so those counts can reach turn accounting. No configuration change or migration is needed. Explicit model-level streaming-usage overrides retain precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both provider IDs now declare support through the existing plugin manifest contract, matching Volcengine. The shared transport already requests and parses final usage chunks; no new runtime branch is needed. BytePlus documents `stream_options.include_usage` as defaulting to false in its [Chat API reference](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/modelark/chat-api).

The simplification pass retained only the two capability declarations and extended the existing manifest test. Executable production code: +0/-0. Production metadata: +14/-0; no equivalent dead or duplicate code exists in this owner to remove safely. Tests: +7/-8 (net -1). Direct JSON import removes redundant file reading/parsing; no test-line allocation or baseline change remains.

## Evidence

- On main `d107cb81b327fc4654dbbaa9f21beba0cf2fc57a`, the updated manifest regression fails on the missing `providerRequest` declaration: 1 failed, 3 passed. With this fix: 4 passed. Command: `pnpm test extensions/byteplus/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Final regression wall time: 12.83s red, 11.15s green (Vitest 6.59s; transformation dominates). The original cold baseline took 58.47s. The [final-head extension CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41138293887/job/124346605101) took 106s including setup. [CI on final head ac0142f57d96](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41138293887) passed, including the test-line ratchet.
- A secretless synthetic SSE probe runs the real manifest-derived capability resolver, compatibility defaults, OpenAI SDK request serialization, and shared streaming-usage parser. Before: both BytePlus routes omit `stream_options` and finish with unavailable usage. After: both send `{"include_usage":true}` and retain 17 input / 3 output / 20 total tokens. The Volcengine sibling remains working, and explicit `supportsUsageInStreaming: false` still suppresses usage requests. Network is disabled for these successful probes.
- `pnpm test:extension byteplus`: 22 passed, 1 live test skipped (no credentials), across four files on the initial head with the same production manifest; 49.09s wall time. The final manifest-test simplification is separately green above.
- Provider-attribution, shared completions usage-parity, and tool-prefix-stability tests: 72 passed across three files.
- Focused BytePlus typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet: passed. Initial CI failed only on the test-line ceiling; removing redundant test setup eliminates net growth and the allocation.
- Shared autoreview: Codex engine, P0-P2, complete final local delta against the baseline above, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; hosted ClawSweeper review of the initial head found no actionable findings or before-merge blockers. The later change only simplifies test setup; production is identical, and fresh autoreview covers the final delta.

Proof limits: the stream probe uses documented protocol fixtures, not a live BytePlus model or Gateway. No live endpoint or stable-upgrade test was performed. The contributor head was read with `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out or executed; this replacement was independently applied on current main. All test execution used rootless Podman capped at 4 CPUs / 8 GiB. No Team Gateway state or deployment was changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on phones, the screen shown while a new session is being created uses a different header and menu button than the chat it turns into, so the header visibly changes when the session opens.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7195c458-7296-47ac-9cc4-88adafeb33c1)

## User Impact

User impact: from the moment you press Start on a phone, the session shows the same header it will keep: the round, outlined menu button, the title placeholder and the Panels/⋯ capsule. Nothing jumps when the Gateway accepts the session. The `/new`, Sessions and other narrow-layout pages also use the same menu button as chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before the Gateway accepts a new session, the pending screen has no mobile panel host, so its header fell back to the squeezed desktop chat header. The pending screen now renders the mobile chat header directly. Details, Panels and the session menu stay visible but disabled until the session is accepted, so the layout does not shift when they become usable.

One `MobileNavToggle` component now serves the shell top bar, the mobile chat header and the merged catalog header, replacing three separately styled drawer buttons. The top bar keeps its connection-status dot.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent mobile release CI test failures when output-limit termination interrupts the process-tree fixture's PID publication.

## User Impact

Developers get reliable native process-cleanup evidence. Release execution behavior stays unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parent spawned an output-producing grandchild before writing both PIDs. Termination could kill the parent between opening/truncating the PID file and writing it; parsing the empty file produced `[0]`.

title: fix(codex): avoid missing native binaries during automatic selection
body:
Closes #90587.

Supersedes #127303, thanks @rajmp999.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes first-message failures when automatic Codex selection finds its npm launcher but no native app-server binary, including Linux RISC-V64.

## User Impact

Automatic selection can use the built-in OpenClaw harness. Explicit and prepared pinned Codex choices retain native ownership and report an actionable error. Custom commands, environment overrides, socket transports, worker-hosted app-servers, and source-built native executables remain eligible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check actual binary presence at the Codex supports boundary using the existing managed resolver. The official npm launcher can throw before spawning on an unsupported platform, so spawn ENOENT alone misses the reported failure. Another platform allowlist would duplicate the existing mapping and reject valid native builds or remote connections. Unsupported is returned without a declared fallback; the existing selector already distinguishes implicit/auto selection from explicit ownership. Version and handshake validation stay at startup.

The earlier extraction and shared command-source wrapper are removed. The final production delta is +58/-14 (net +44), confined to two existing owner files; tests add 49 lines and docs add 8. There is no equivalent dead code in this owner to remove without deleting supported behavior. The necessary net growth comprises the managed-local-stdio eligibility guard and actionable error (+16 plus one import), the actual-presence query over existing candidates/PATH (+20), and synchronous bounded launcher recognition (+7 net, including imports). This reuses the existing platform map, singleton, package resolver and native recognition, with no new module, cache, setting, core or SDK contract. Synchronous filesystem recognition is needed by the synchronous selection contract; it reads only the existing two-byte shebang prefix. Worker-hosted configuration keeps binary validation with the worker; unplaced local attempts retain existing startup validation.

## Evidence

- Regression is red on main `81cf32d99769`: the new missing-native case returns supported; the other 36 harness tests pass. Final repair: all 37 harness and 32 managed-startup tests pass (69 total, 55.56 seconds including cold compilation). The regression preserves custom/env commands, WebSocket/Unix, live worker config and a native PATH fixture under Linux/RISC-V64 simulation.
- Real production selector probe is red on the base (selects Codex) and green on the final head: implicit selects OpenClaw; explicit and prepared pinned Codex reject; configured transports remain eligible. Selection contract tests (26) and prompt-prefix stability tests (14) also pass.
- Final-head focused typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh final-head autoreview through P2, including full frozen resolver/selection context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Full `pnpm build` passes on final head `1123b4d3831f69d9df2859a6defa2ecca42c8da5` in a rootless container capped at 4 CPUs / 8 GiB (3m 28.9s), using the supported `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4352` setting. Cgroup OOM events: zero. Earlier attempts exceeded the cap before that build-owner heap setting was applied.
- The completed build passes an isolated host Gateway turn with private state/home, free loopback port 41019 and native Codex artifacts fault-injected absent. No runtime override or authored request-transport parameters were used. Trace-only instrumentation observes `selected=openclaw reason=implicit_plugin_unsupported_openclaw`; the Gateway process makes a POST to the Responses request boundary, receives a fixture response and returns `PR127303_PROVIDER_BOUNDARY_OK` with CLI status `ok`. The Gateway process and port are confirmed closed afterward. No Team Gateway action was taken.
- Live limitation: no task-scoped provider credential was available. The successful boundary proof uses a synthetic noncredential marker and an intercepted transport, not authenticated model inference. Physical RISC-V hardware remains untested. The native-missing regression and real selector negative control fail on the base, so a preexisting route-based OpenClaw choice cannot satisfy this proof.
- Contributor code was read via GitHub only and never checked out or run. Every replacement commit credits Raj Muppala <54062691+rajmp999@users.noreply.github.com>.

Final-head [CI run 41136992196](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41136992196) completed: 35 jobs passed, 27 skipped. The only root failure is [test-lines](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41136992196/job/124342346729); `openclaw/ci-gate` fails downstream. Security and all lint/type/runtime lanes pass. The exact CI merge `fc8e85a9886eb875205361187098d89ef5e5c1ab` has ordered parents main `32207da50d23edc23c3df35633dde71858748216` and this PR head. Its tree was reconstructed and verified.

title: improve: show gateway commit and build time on About
body:
Original author: Chris Eckert (@ceckert). This is his #180353, rebased onto current `main` so it can land; that branch's managed workspace became unusable during its base refresh, so it could not be updated in place. The branch carries his `Co-authored-by` trailer, so the squash commit credits him.

## What Problem This Solves

Members can see the connected Gateway version but cannot identify its running commit or build time when diagnosing a possibly stale deployment.

## User Impact

Settings → About shows the Control UI and the connected Gateway as two separate sections, each listing version, commit (with copy) and UTC build time; the Control UI section also shows its branch. A member can tell whether the Gateway they are connected to includes a fix without assuming the browser bundle matches it. Missing provenance is omitted; a disconnected Gateway shows its version as unavailable. Host diagnostics and update operations remain restricted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing authenticated hello payload and About page rather than adding another version endpoint or screen. The Gateway reports `server.commit` and `server.builtAt` from the build provenance it captures once at startup, so a later checkout change does not relabel the running Gateway. No changes to `system.info` or `update.status` authorization.

The UI adds no new CSS. Both builds render with the existing Settings facts grid (`.settings-kv`) and the shared `CopyButton`, replacing About's bespoke copy state machine and its styles. `about.css` shrinks versus `main` (6,235 → 4,962 bytes), so the Control UI CSS budget check, which allows no growth while `main` is over its cap, passes.

Rebase notes (relative to #180353): `main` now owns build provenance in `readBuildProvenanceForModuleUrl`, so the Gateway build time is read from that record (`resolveRuntimeServiceBuiltAt`, normalized to ISO, unparseable values omitted) instead of a second build-info reader. About strings live in the deferred `en-about` catalog, and the hero keeps `main`'s Support link. The mocked Gateway carries commit and build time through `main`'s `control-ui-mock-scenario` module.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway handshake (in-process Gateway server, real WebSocket connect, device paired with member scopes `operator.sessions.read`/`operator.sessions.write`, production-shaped `build-info.json`): hello returned `server.commit` (short SHA) and `server.builtAt: "2026-10-30T21:00:00.000Z"`; `system.info` → `missing scope: operator.read`, `update.status` → `missing scope: operator.admin`. This closes the "isolated real Gateway/member handshake" gap listed on #180353.
- Unit: About view/page tests (both sections' facts, copy controls, localized UTC build time, omitted facts and unavailable Gateway), `connect-hello.update-scope` (member hello carries commit/builtAt, update details still omitted) and `version` tests pass.
- Browser (Playwright Chromium, production bundle, mocked Gateway, member scopes): `about.e2e` (both sections' facts, Gateway commit copy, zero `system.info`/`update.status` requests, no horizontal overflow at 375px) and `build-info-unicode.e2e` pass on the current head after merging `main`.
- Current head: UI typecheck, formatting and the line-cap ratchet pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, P1) on the earlier rail layout: scoped-clean, no findings. Not rerun on the reuse-only layout.

### Screenshots

Production-bundle captures of the reuse-only layout (desktop, 390px, dark) were inspected in the landing session: both sections render with the standard Settings card and facts grid, and the copy button takes the Settings 44px touch size on mobile. They are not embedded here because this publication route cannot upload images; the earlier rail screenshots from #180353 no longer match and were removed.

Contributor credit: Chris Eckert (@ceckert) authored this change: he identified the member-access gap and requested extending the existing About page. Design review: Vyctor Brzezowski (@vyctorbrzezowski).

title: fix: repair legacy config during same-version updates
body:
Related: #188694

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw update` refusing an already-current npm installation with legacy config that Doctor can repair, unless the operator also supplied `--channel`.

## User Impact

A plain same-version update can repair supported legacy settings, such as `gateway.bind: "localhost"`, and continue maintenance. The normal config writer preserves the original backup. Unknown fields still fail with actionable Doctor guidance; foreign profiles retain their ownership checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Already-current updates skip candidate admission. Prepare the existing source-bound Doctor plan for the selected maintenance config before installed admission, then let the existing finalizer persist it. This reconnects the repair owner without bypassing validation or introducing options, state, or schema changes.

The masked report does not establish that its five rejected fields match this reproduction. Release 2026.10.9 still accepts `agents.defaults.heartbeat`; main's later heartbeat retirement uses a separate stateful Doctor migration and is outside this config-only repair. Related rather than closing the issue.

The +34 allocation matches measured growth; terminal CI classification follows.

Installed-package proof now passes on Linux x64 / Node 26.12.1 through the real installed CLI, using `openclaw update --no-restart --yes --json` without a channel or tag:

| Installed package | Result | Config and backup |
| --- | --- | --- |

The original and successful canonical-backup SHA-256 are both `f0bd909915af582cb8e48aa3a41604aa47b0767607c4f9f03d00391cd760aff0`. title: feat(workers): keep runtime image reserves ready without browser presence
body:
Related: #188679, merged as `b7563b304095b4d4f329f2a82ada08d9ec8da4c3`, and landed repository authority #188656. GitHub retargeted this PR to **main**. This history-preserving refresh integrates exact main `f461e03db24051da076db81de9796696cb44d872`; it does not land this PR.

**Landing remains coordinator-owned:** current-head CI and the normal landing gates must pass. Earlier-head checks are not approval of this new head; no CI rerun was requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Runtime-image integrations need ready capacity without a connected browser, without unavailable policy blocking cleanup or restart destroying and replacing existing ready workers.

## User Impact

The configured default profile keeps runtime-only workers ready and refills after claims. Restart preserves compatible reserve identities while demand is reconstructed. Disabling capacity drains unused workers without interrupting attached sessions or extending finite deadlines. Ready workers incur running-machine charges until deletion is confirmed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Standing demand reuses the existing pool and environment inventory. Image preparation contains runtime artifacts, not repository contents or credentials. Repository claim/startup and credential authority are supplied by the landed prerequisites. Browser-driven repository demand and empty-workspace activation retain their existing paths.

Demand observation cannot disable expiry or physical cleanup. Pending reconstruction preserves inventory but grants no provider I/O. Actual activation—not a restored reserve’s creation timestamp—supplies independent refill demand, and allocation rechecks current authority and capacity after awaited preflight. Explicit repository builds remain request-owned.

The standing slice adds no pool, schema, retained-disk feature, configuration option or live cloud change. Its unchanged delta remains **190 production lines and 891 regression/support lines**, with matching allocations of **387 + 351 + 153**.

title: fix(macos): avoid startup crashes from invalid custom Gateway hosts
body:
Closes #187602

## What Problem This Solves

Invalid saved custom Gateway hosts can crash the macOS app at startup or endpoint refresh. Configuration errors can also become stuck as ownership failures after the host is corrected.

## User Impact

The app displays an actionable IPv4 configuration error and recovers after host-only correction without silently choosing another Gateway, rewriting settings, or enabling unsupported IPv6 binding. Genuine ownership conflicts remain blocked. No new configuration, dependency, database schema or state owner is introduced.

Scope decision, 1 November: keep this PR focused on endpoint crash safety and configuration recovery. The first-launch updater/runtime-pin ordering failure discovered during validation is a separate repair task; it is not claimed fixed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing endpoint owner validates custom IPv4 binding before URL construction and publishes failures through its unavailable state. The process manager distinguishes retained ownership conflicts from recoverable configuration errors, preserving background activation intent.

The latest commit repairs only regression-test actor isolation and uses existing AppState owner APIs for the companion control; no production API or test-only production hook was added.

## Evidence

Head: b4f7c8a154db40acaf0bddc7238e91707630cf23. Verified source tree: 3435fc0d2bd99465ced7827deadd15675dd5800a. Native execution below was supplied from isolated macOS workers, not performed by this Linux session.

This supersedes the earlier 87/87-only evidence. Remaining-validation ZIP CRC and all 21 listed SHA-256 checks pass. No rerun needed. |
| Actual packaged-app behavior | Both invalid hosts leave the app alive with field-specific errors. A pre-paired live transition recovers after host-only correction under the same app PID, with a new Gateway child and paired-node reconnection. A real cross-profile conflict is rejected while the original remains sole listener. |

This is attributed baseline failure, not a lint pass. Diff whitespace and native localization pass. |

Latest completed ClawSweeper review of this head finds no actionable code defect and accepts app behavior proof. Exact-head CI/security gates and native localization pass; automatic PR planning leaves macOS execution unselected. The separate canceled ClawSweeper dispatcher is not a product test failure. |
| Retained-profile upgrade | A complete paired schema-20 baseline is retained through recovery: the candidate app/child identity is linked, authenticated health and approved paired-node reconnection pass after ordinary relaunch, and schema-36 integrity, host/port/token and pairing data persist. First launch still fails; a separate trace now identifies old-runtime selection after schema migration. Upgrade availability remains red. |

### Actual-app host correction

Both captures use the repaired candidate: they compare configuration states, not base versus fix. The original app archive's CRC and all 21 listed SHA-256 checks pass; native captures were inspected and cropped before publication. Task-only credentialless Tart guests used macOS 26.6.2 / Xcode 27 and were cleaned up without operator-state changes. Packaging is ad-hoc debug, not release-signing proof.

**Before correcting the host — the app remains alive with an actionable error.**

**After correcting only the host — same app process, background recovery.** Health and the pre-paired node independently corroborate recovery. The lower health subrow remains pending and is not claimed fixed.

![Host-only correction: same native app process recovers its configured Gateway in the background](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/277d798f-075f-4e7e-a235-c7de8685856e)

<details>
<summary>Conflict controls and app-proof limits</summary>

Observed listeners/selected route show no substitute Gateway, not exhaustive outbound tracing or zero-credential-exposure proof. Stale/pending presentation rows are disclosed, not fixed. An exploratory 127.0.0.2 bind failure is excluded; successful app runs use real interface IPv4 addresses.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Complete native tests and controlled regression comparison</summary>

The new supplied clean exact-head run uses swift test --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --disable-index-store -Xswiftc -gline-tables-only --filter "GatewayEndpointStoreTests|GatewayProcessManagerTests". Raw output records Build complete! (242.37s), both suites passing and 158 tests passing in 20.886 seconds. Whole-commit endpoint comparison used base 6941b99db5206045d1508a9717990f1f80999486, reversing the complete base-to-head diff rather than replacing one manager file. The same comparison-compatible test overlay compiled on both sides; resulting production-file hashes matched clean base. Base: 71 endpoint tests, eight invalid-host failures (five SIGTRAP and three incorrect unavailable-state results). Restored head: 71/71 pass, including those same eight cases. This proves endpoint regression red/green against the whole original base; it is not a whole-6ba0edd process-manager comparison. The earlier targeted prior-manager substitution separately failed four recovery cases/eight issues; retain that narrower scope rather than relabeling it.

Test-overlay compatibility changes are limited to makeStore visibility and try! bridging of the base's nonthrowing source-snapshot API. The new unmodified-head 158-test run is separate from that comparison overlay. Production remains unchanged from 93d7bdda13036d283cdde9d7b316e38f7b130b47; the latest source successor repairs tests only.

Source/test accounting covers local/custom IPv4 and TLS, tailnet selection/fallback, credentials, direct/SSH routing and unconfigured handling. Remote/unconfigured branches do not construct the unused invalid local URL. Actual-app proof independently establishes completed recovery beyond unit-test admission.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Retained-profile recovery and reproduced first-launch updater failure</summary>

The earlier versioned pack's 14 checksums and CRC pass; it established candidate schema-36 health but lacked complete baseline/parent identity. The new remaining-validation pack supplies a complete SQLite backup API baseline after release pairing: schema 20, integrity OK, one paired-device row, authenticated release health and a connected approved node. Release app/child/listener were stopped before candidate replacement. The candidate build uses PR-head logic with only a guest-only package.json version bump to 2026.10.10, production bundle ID, ad-hoc signature and omitted optional MLX helper—not byte-identical head or signed Sparkle delivery. onboardingSeen was set manually in the disposable profile.

Initial launch failed after five starts with exit 78 in two fresh retained-profile fixtures. Ordinary quit/relaunch recovered the first: Gateway PID 17367 is a child of app PID 16942; executable mapping and health childRuntime.execPath identify candidate Bun. Health returns ok=true/coreReady=true, schema 36 remains integral, and token hash, paired-device row and node ID persist; node status is paired=true, connected=true, approvalState=approved. Native captures show the initial error and later ready screen. A second profile eventually recovered with Retry; its Retry trace does not identify its initial failing child. Neither recovery erases first-launch failure.

A separate first-failure packet (CRC pass; no internal checksum manifest) positively identifies three initial Gateway children under the candidate app PID. At 18:50:36 the database is schema 20 and runtime/current names release 2026.10.9. At 18:50:37 it is schema 36 while the pointer is still the release. At 18:50:40, 18:50:46 and 18:50:50 the captured Gateway executable and entrypoint are all from that old release. The refusal identifies 8b18b55, supporting schema 20, opening schema 36. Only at 18:51:09 does runtime/current name the candidate; the pin readback remains migrationPending. The sampler is not a complete attempt count. title: feat(workers): start repository sessions from runtime image reserves
body:
Related: #188656, now merged as `a4b07c63b60cf3a971c824064c82946c530e1686`. This PR now targets **main**. History-preserving refresh `75275a543acd67edc3e6ec353aff0c73d15d1a2c` merges that exact main into the existing image branch; it does not land this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Repository integrations need to separate reusable runtime capacity from each session's repository access and checkout.

## User Impact

Integrations selecting image-only capacity can claim a compatible runtime worker, or provision one cold, then restore the repository under the current request's authority. Image preparation does not read repository contents or obtain GitHub credentials. Unsupported profiles fail before allocation. Native, paired-device, and repository-capacity preparation retain their existing paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Image and empty-workspace preparation have distinct source, claim, and cache identities. Dispatch selects runtime-only intent without repository preparation inputs; repository startup retains the original host-side credential reader, including admission and current-authority checks. Live profile checks reach allocation and claim, and retries settle stored intent rather than selecting a changed profile.

Rejected, unallocated image requests are terminalized so reconciliation cannot later allocate them. Uncertain provisioning and cancellation retain their existing ownership. Repository authority, native credential return, required-profile admission, and sessions.create caller handling are supplied by the landed prerequisite, not duplicated here.

The image delta adds no standing-demand/refill policy, retained-disk feature, heartbeat, packaging feature, database table, live configuration change, or production test hook. Production growth remains 130 lines; test growth is 1,025 lines with matching allocations of 586 + 326 + 113. Node/transfer and managed-profile fixtures are shared.

## Evidence

### Current main conflict refresh

Tested tree: `4ca284c6ee331f5ead63a56c21758d18537e16b3`. First parent: previous image head `428a4576808c07fc5f1582755bcadf08d9a6dc21`; second parent: exact main `a4b07c63b60cf3a971c824064c82946c530e1686`.

- Five squash-related textual conflicts were reproduced. Every incoming conflict file was byte-identical to the already integrated authority source. Resolution preserves **all 17 image-delta files byte-for-byte**, including RPC repair `92fa442b0ea78784434b9a87f4f780f8c32f94f1`; the complete path set against main is still exactly those 17 files, with no extra base-relative edits.
- **95 tests across six files passed**, in **158.87 seconds**: the meaningful 54-case RPC/image/managed authority suite plus 41 focused runtime-artifact/bootstrap cases for the changed upstream package inputs. These use real local Git, admission, checkpoint and fixture-package effects; no full production package rebuild ran.
- Targeted TypeScript, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Normal attributed commit hooks remained enabled. Existing independent P0–P2 reviews remain applicable to the unchanged image delta; the mechanical resolutions and complete base-relative source preservation were inspected directly.
- The frozen dependency graph is unchanged. Parsed multi-document lockfiles are semantically equal—the textual changes only reorder entries. The root manifest only adds upstream's `runtime-artifacts` export; workspace manifests and package versions are unchanged. Tests use independently frozen read-only fs-safe 0.27.0 dependencies and private generated outputs in secretless Node 24.22.1 containers. No parent mutable dist/cache, live cloud, or live credentials were used.
- The previous `428a…` CI result remains previous-head evidence. Natural CI on this new publication is still required; no workflow rerun was requested.

### Actual authority and checkout effects

- **App mode:** native JWT signing verified by a local HTTP server, synthetic installation credential issuance/revocation, authenticated Git HTTP checkout through NodeWorkerWorkspaceRuntime, and actual SQLite/bare-Git checkpoint storage and transfer. Unauthorized/revoked/reassigned callers cannot issue credentials or perform Git I/O; revocation after authorized issuance prevents checkout. Recovery restores accepted state, excluding unaccepted old-node files.
- **Managed PAT/OAuth:** actual private-profile reads and HTTP credential verification, authenticated checkout and checkpoint restoration. Positive claim/cold controls succeed; denied callers cause zero verification and zero Git/node effects; caller retirement stops checkout. OAuth recovery re-enters current policy and rejects a forbidden fresh caller. The plugin is never asked for a managed bearer.
- **Actual sessions.create:** allowed RPC verifies the managed identity exactly once and checks real file contents. Policy revocation, source replacement, Stop, and caller retirement retain zero-verification/zero-node-command assertions. Runtime allocation asserts image intent without a credential reader. No fixture-only admission is fabricated.

### Retained provenance and compatibility evidence

- Exact prerequisite `b062896364982a2838139025c0497d6e5bfb7712`, tree `2b96a7360603b237e4d4b3facbaff778c25f3cdf`, was integrated through `e56379f…` and tree-identical merge `94fdd2b3…` before its squash landing. That image tree `6455ab40de45e201e3044bcd88d7f146a284a298` passed the 54-case suite in 136.38 seconds with independently frozen inputs.
- The prerequisite owner completed the installed stable upgrade on exact `b062…`: agent schema 25→39, state schema 20→36, configuration, 14 plugins and retained checkpoint proof, with teardown confirmed. That is prerequisite-owned evidence, not a new installed-binary run on this image refresh; no active-worker reconnection is claimed.
- RPC repair `92fa442…`, tree `949676825692d904ecad4b4f32e7c60a03e9850f`, reproduced the [original failing CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41162152493/job/124422139825): one failed/nine passed on `7594c433…`, versus ten passed on exact parent `c6ceb4ae…`. Removing the fixture-only identity call from runtime intent creation preserved actual startup admission. Its 54-case repair run, static checks and ratchets passed; one test line and one allocation line were removed. Those ratchet totals remain historical input-bound evidence.
- Earlier identity/selection, canonical registry, refused-intent reconciliation, and prior-reader revocation negative controls remain recorded. The older 106-case/seven-file run omitted the RPC suite and is not presented as proof of that former failure.
- Released `v2026.10.9` (`8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`) used v1 project-shaped worker records, including empty local workspaces. Runtime-image identity is new capacity metadata, never authorization. This image slice changes no worker SQL table or settings schema. The earlier schema20→state36 synthetic-record spot-check is retained only as prior-head evidence.

### Remaining qualification

Current-head CI and root-owned landing gates remain. Physical provider allocation and authenticated Gateway connection facts are synthetic inputs; credential, authenticated Git, and checkpoint effects execute locally. title: improve: safely reuse qualified offline compositions
body:
Related: #188661, now landed. This follow-on targets **main** and preserves exact prerequisite `f3bdcadb948e1b873b59066cbd0994192da50a42` in its history. Its effective change against reviewed main `adb58af237c2079d8eae388b22b9ce439d19e081` is exactly the five qualified-reuse files.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated offline compositions rehash every dependency payload, while skipping verification of a mutable donor or Docker's `app/` input would admit stale or changed bytes.

## User Impact

Release tooling can opt into qualified dependency reuse and an archive-bound image recipe without changing the strict defaults. Reuse receipts explicitly report partial input verification; neither mode replaces Linux target acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

A trusted, digest-bound receipt from a prior strict composition qualifies the dependency manifest, not the current donor. Reuse still checks complete topology, modes, sizes, link targets/containment and package manifests, then verifies the actual selected copies against that inventory. Unselected payload bytes are not rehashed, and partial receipts cannot qualify another reuse. No caller-written operation report serves as authority.

The landed composition owner's repairs are retained: builtin-named npm dependencies use package lookup and nearest-ancestor deduplication, and legitimate implementation files under paths such as `src/node_modules` are copied and verified. Those prerequisite fixes are not reintroduced as independent owners here.

The optional `--image-input archive` recipe checks the receipt-bound archive/manifest and the small admission inputs without rehashing all of `app/`. Docker copies the archive, checks its exact SHA-256 inside the build, and only then extracts it. The existing finalizer remains the single lifecycle owner. Directory recipes and full-inventory verification remain the defaults.

Source implementation contributed by @galiniliev. Relative to main, this adds no cache, competing operation-report owner, dependency, lockfile or tool pin. Net production growth remains 176 lines. The scoped allocation is still exactly **140** for the **+140** test-line delta; the shared scalar was not changed.

## Evidence

- Published head `712cf21f051338520e61849fa4c7d43acfa1ef3a` preserves tested commit `63593cf109f5737ed238603dec0f1c73d583553c` and tree `dcc577f3532a53cb300ee278b730e4947adc7060`. The exact prerequisite was merged history-preservingly in `aa52afa9975e8cfe3b8eecaec51bf3418a3ae214`. Four squash-lineage conflicts were then resolved against main only after proving all four main-side blobs equal the reviewed prerequisite. No rebase or age-only refresh was performed.
- **53 relevant tests have passing main-context evidence:** 32 composition, 14 bundled-link helper, 4 offline dependency-planner and 3 Docker-digest tests. The first main-context run exposed a test-fixture clone that traversed unavailable unrelated history in a partial checkout. The fixture now clones the real runtime commit at depth one; that case and the four planner tests passed in a focused 59.19s follow-up, including 41.66s cold worker compilation. Unaffected passing cases were reused rather than blanket-rerun. The complete pre-main integration run also passed all 53 tests in 78.46s.
- Builtin-name admission is exercised through the real composition fixture using an npm package named `fs`. Restoring the old lookup makes composition fail with `openclaw requires fs`; the repair passes while retaining nested versions. The existing implementation-file tamper case still fails with the old copy filter and passes with the repair. Genuine first strict receipts, relocation/tampering, partial-receipt rejection, CLI archive admission and native-finalizer boundaries remain covered.
- Fresh main-relative scripts, tooling-test and extensions-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint reported zero warnings/errors; formatting, normal isolated commit hooks and diff checks passed. Frozen dependencies were reconciled only in the task-owned isolated installation; shared caches were unchanged.
- **Fresh main-relative ratchet passed:** 6,315,807 test lines, ceiling 6,347,775, slack 31,968. The earlier 1,042-line overage was measured on the pre-main snapshot and is not stamped onto this checked main-based tree. No allocation was inflated to hide it.
- Fresh independent local autoreview of the final five-file candidate against main `adb58af237c2079d8eae388b22b9ce439d19e081`: **P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. The final candidate was committed unchanged. The dirty local ClawSweeper checkout required the documented autoreview route. The [earlier hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188678#issuecomment-6533057882) also found no actionable defects; it is prior-head evidence, not a current-head approval.
- Retained real offline Podman admission proof remains source-bound to the unchanged Dockerfile: the archive-input stage consumed the original archive despite changed `app/` bytes; archive tampering failed checksum verification before extraction. No broad rebuild was repeated solely for metadata or ancestry changes.

<details>
<summary>Retained archive-consumption trace — unchanged Docker stage</summary>

Successful admission and container readback, while mutable `app/` contained different bytes:

```text
/tmp/installed-runtime.tgz: OK
archive bytes consumed; mutable app excluded
```

After changing that archive while retaining the expected digest:

```text
/tmp/installed-runtime.tgz: FAILED
sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match
```

The maintained build step orders checksum verification before extraction with `&&`; the tampered build exited 1. This is archive admission proof, not full release-image qualification.

</details>

**Current-head CI is green:** the [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41148539662/job/124382281583) passed for `712cf21f051338520e61849fa4c7d43acfa1ef3a`; final readback found no failed or running checks. Full release-image acceptance remains target-owned. Receipts retain `compositionOnly: true`, ABI/libc `requires-target-acceptance`, and lifecycle `target-required`. No live cloud operations were performed.

title: feat: verify warm worker runtime caches without modifying them
body:
Related: #188659 (landed). Current base: `main`; integrated API parent: `ee479a542b773fead85d101d915f8b21d3521853`. Published verifier head: `703d96eaedfea6694c4a32ca1e5774fbdc5402f8`; exact integrated main: `a4b07c63b60cf3a971c824064c82946c530e1686`.

## What Problem This Solves

Image-preparation tooling needs to confirm that a retained worker runtime is usable without silently repairing or modifying its cache.

## User Impact

Operators can run a credential-free warm-cache check and consume a bounded, artifact-matched installation receipt. Missing or corrupt caches fail without installation, pruning, runtime Node binding or enrollment state writes. Verification covers package/build/manifest identity, CLI version and worker archive integrity—not every installed payload byte or live execution authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public lazy Crabbox CLI API shares the existing installer/verifier owner. Read-only verification returns before mutation and uses the runtime wrapper, not bootstrap binding. Producer/parser/tests/docs use `openclaw.runtime-installed:` with no legacy alias or environment option. Bundle receipts distinguish `installed` and `existing-verified`; npm preparation retains its diagnostic contract.

The later history-only conflict resolution preserves the proof through verified byte-equivalent commands and receipts; no package rebuild or archive re-export was performed.

title: fix(skills): selected project skills are missing from the $ picker and slash commands
body:
Related: #187813

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills from a selected project's `skills/` and `.agents/skills/` are missing from the Control UI `$` picker and slash commands, both in the New session composer and in existing project sessions, even though the agent's runtime skill catalog includes them.

## User Impact

User impact: in the New session composer, selecting a registered project shows that project's eligible skills in `$` and `/`, switching projects or back to the agent workspace replaces the list, and a picked project skill is actually invoked on the first turn. Existing project sessions (Control UI, and channel sessions such as Telegram) list and invoke their project skills too. Precedence, allowlists, eligibility and sandbox containment are unchanged; clients that could not create a session in a project never see its skills.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **New session preview:** `commands.list` accepts an optional `projectId` (not combined with `sessionKey`). The Gateway resolves it through the project registry, admits the root with the same session-creation authorization and sandbox containment as `sessions.create`, repeats that admission right before responding, and passes the root to the existing skill loader as the execution root. The composer sends its selected project; the UI command cache and stale-request ownership are keyed by project, and a pending slash refresh is retired when agent, draft or project changes.
- **Invocation:** reply-path consumers (explicit `$` references, slash and tool dispatch) derive the session's execution skill root with the same resolver as the runtime catalog, so a listed project skill is also invocable.
- **Existing sessions:** a session with an execution root (spawned cwd or managed worktree) reads its own `commands.list` instead of the agent-scoped startup command catalog; sessions without a project keep the startup catalog. A republished catalog retires the session's cached copy.
- **File host:** one shared resolver keeps registered and cloned project roots Gateway-owned through preview, creation, invocation and the runtime snapshot, including for agents whose workspace is served by a paired node (File Transfer). The `workspace:<agent>` pseudo-project keeps the agent workspace's own host, using the registry's source classification.

Overlap: #187869 by @yy19971996 independently makes the same session invocation-root change in `chat-commands.ts`; this PR includes it because the preview-to-invocation flow needs it, and uses the same option names so either PR rebases cleanly onto the other. Credit to @yy19971996 for that work. #155867 is untouched.

## Evidence

Control UI New session with project **alpha** selected — both project roots listed:

![New session $ picker with project alpha selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/595a6a70-3327-4437-a45f-c24f2b47ac1a)

After switching to project **beta** — alpha entries gone:

![New session $ picker after switching to project beta](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44910848-9df9-493b-a4cd-75a196247f62)

Back to the agent workspace — project entries gone:

![New session $ picker back on the agent workspace](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18ddac3a-3606-4640-9673-1e4c9e68e3ce)

Existing alpha session `$` picker:

![Existing alpha session $ picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2925aaff-bfee-4799-9f0a-18b3d59502c3)

Project tool-dispatch slash command answered without a model turn:

![Project tool-dispatch slash command reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/866d1e9c-df09-4e57-8b88-7a963a390bb8)

Cache retirement in the shipped Control UI (project session, Library activation succeeds, metadata refresh fails at the transport, a stale in-flight catalog read is released): reopening `$` fetches the fresh catalog once and shows the new pin, and an unrelated session keeps its cached catalog:

![Project session $ after Library activation shows the fresh pin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6112db15-87aa-4d22-8846-f8d39c245aa3)

![Unrelated session $ still served from its own cached catalog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3daff8ae-14f8-4877-9829-de357640839a)

- Focused unit/boundary suites: 250 passed across command discovery, the `commands.list` handler, protocol, runtime preparation and the New session/chat composer, plus the affected re-runs for each later change. Each fix has a regression that fails with the fix reverted, including a new one for invalidating every cached command variant of a session (Library activation, failed metadata refresh, late in-flight read, unrelated session unaffected).
- Real Control UI + Gateway flow (isolated Gateway, synthetic fixtures, fixture model): render and select both project roots, switch projects and back to the workspace, start a session and confirm the first turn carries the explicit skill instruction, open `$` in the created session, and run a project `command-dispatch: tool` slash command without a model turn.
- Shipped Control UI cache scenario (production bundle, visible Library controls, transport-level failures at a mock Gateway): see the screenshots above.
- Authority (real Gateway, trusted-proxy identities, `gateway.roles`, synthetic projects): `commands.list` with a `projectId` returned the project's skills to an administrator and to a member whose role allows the agent. A device granted only `operator.read`, and a role whose agents exclude the target agent, received only the agent catalog. While a slow discovery was in flight, removing the project returned `UNAVAILABLE` ("Project access changed while preparing its commands"), a config patch removing the role's agent access returned `UNAVAILABLE`, and revoking the operator's role closed the connection before any response; no project skills were disclosed. Tightening the agent's sandbox mode mid-discovery was not exercised because that setting requires a Gateway restart.
- Telegram Test Server DM bound to a synthetic registered project: `$skill` reached the agent turn with the explicit skill instruction, and a project tool-dispatch slash command replied directly with no model request.
- Separately launched, paired node with a File Transfer workspace: preview → `sessions.create` → `commands.list` → `chat.send` for a registered project and the workspace pseudo-project, red/green against the pseudo-project host fix. The no-Gateway-path-read claim rests on the node read policy and the observed catalogs, not a per-request node trace.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/project-skills-picker-187813.txt` grants exactly this PR's net +563 regression-test lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. They cover: project preview admission and the disclosure re-check before responding; the `workspace:<agent>` pseudo-project keeping the agent workspace's file host; registered-project roots staying Gateway-owned through preview, creation and invocation; existing project sessions reading their own command catalog; invalidation of every cached command variant of a session, including Library activation followed by a failed metadata refresh and a late in-flight read; New session project-keyed command cache and stale slash-refresh retirement; and the reply-path invocation root for `$` and `/` project skills. One duplicate node-workspace discovery case and one superseded scoped-invalidation block were folded first.
- Compatibility: `commands.list.projectId` is an optional additive parameter; requests without it behave as before. No persisted schema, config, user-state migration, protocol version or updater change, so no upgrade-path qualification applies.

Those repairs are merged into this branch with no conflicts and this PR's own patch unchanged; the repaired tests pass locally on the current head. An earlier `server.chat-steer-direct-command.test.ts` failure (identical on main) and an artifact-download failure before lint did not recur. `pnpm check:changed` passes all lanes except the dead-export scan, which already fails on the base for two files this PR does not touch. CI passed on head fe7d994; all required checks are green.

title: feat: build Linux images from offline runtime packages
body:
Related: #188651 (landed prerequisite); #188678 (qualified-reuse follow-on). This PR targets `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Release tooling needs to turn a portable OpenClaw package and qualified Linux dependencies into installed image assets without rebuilding the package or resolving dependencies online.

## User Impact

Operators can compose and verify Linux/x64 image inputs offline while preserving bundled payloads and importer-relative dependency versions. The default Docker source-build route remains unchanged.

**This is composition, not Linux runtime qualification.** ABI/libc acceptance, entrypoint, provider identity, and runtime-export checks remain target requirements. The installed-assets stage finalizes without networking; shared later image stages can still require network access for OS/operator tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing archive inspector, installed-dependency planner, package lifecycle, and Docker graph rather than introduce another installer. Full input/output inventories bind the handoff, portable bundles retain their bytes, and promoted plugin dependencies use their declared importer instead of unrelated root development packages. Root production dependencies keep root ownership. Private implementation trees inside dependency packages are preserved while installed dependency placement remains planner-owned.

The shared resolver distinguishes declared npm packages from identically named Node builtins, including ancestor deduplication. Codex's fs-safe importer is aligned with the root's already-approved 0.26.15 pin. Qualified reuse and archive-bound optimization remain separate in #188678; this does not import the runtime-artifact API feature.

Net growth against integrated main `65acdfd629e3555f3c876e3fe887d548633e1863` is 1,127 non-test lines (including documentation/configuration) and 833 test lines. Separate allocations cover 798 composition/archive/ownership/tamper/lifecycle/digest lines and exactly 35 shared resolver regression lines. Existing baseline debt and the shared scalar are unchanged.

Source implementation contributed by @galiniliev.

## Evidence

- History-preserving main integration in `d69cf9304cd093585bdf7fb006f2b6922d90e41b` retained both executable-entry declaration sets. Subsequent cherry-picks import only reviewed shared fixes `d4e71ba4a3154f0d3a2e45ff9d7a018bfbbdce30` and `79daa9c3c9563b43f6538dae0faf90a85bc59c56`; their six resulting file blobs match exactly. Reviewed integration head: `ce39deacdc7fa0fbabaeb241924be495bb4525ab`.
- **221 tests across seven affected files passed** after integration in secretless, network-disabled Linux isolation (179.09s): shared bundled links, offline/bootstrap artifacts, composition, tarball inspection, Docker digest classification, and plugin manifest contracts. This includes relocated builtin-name package cycles, nested versions, source-link preservation, missing-package/source-boundary guards, importer ownership, and the real native-prebuild/finalizer boundary.
- Frozen dependency reconciliation passed all 1,727 supply-chain entries. Codex resolves fs-safe 0.26.15; Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 remain unchanged. Tooling-test, composition, and affected Gateway-test typechecks; targeted lint/format; the direct dependency pin guard; and diff checks passed.
- Prior red/green composition controls remain intact: legitimate `src/node_modules` package implementation files survive extraction, while only root installed-dependency placement is planner-owned. Docker ARG-backed internal stages are recognized without relaxing external-image digest pinning. The installed-only Docker graph was built offline from a minimal context without source-build inputs; that is not full release-image acceptance.
- Independent autoreview, P0–P2: the full composition candidate against integrated main was scoped-clean after its payload repair; the fresh six-file integration review from `e3e349754cce1fee3a0629538b35b909f82732f7` through `ce39deacdc7fa0fbabaeb241924be495bb4525ab` is also scoped-clean, with no actionable findings.
- **CI attribution:** [prior-head e3e34975 build-artifacts passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41134719265/job/124334747999). Its [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41134719265/job/124334748753) failed on test-line debt: 1,042 over the ceiling, with its own 798-line delta fully allocated. The new integration adds exactly 35 LF test lines and 35 credit; local accounting remains 1,042 over the ceiling. No unrelated debt was absorbed or guard weakened. ## User Impact

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway worktree recovery test (`worktrees.test.ts`, "fences recovery relocation through real paired requester and workspace authority") fails with `Local sandbox managed workspace owner changed` when startup worktree cleanup runs before the fixture has published the sessions that own its checkouts.

Observed on scheduled main [run 43310185262](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43310185262) (head `21479e2b10`), job `checks-node-compact-large-15` (131504632303).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This is a test-fixture-only fix that restores the `checks-node-compact-large-15` main CI shard; no production code changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197898 (`e3502d33aa08`) made startup managed-worktree cleanup run immediately. The recovery fixture created its `recovery` and `replacement` checkouts before writing the session entries that own them, so cleanup correctly treated those checkouts as orphaned and removed one. The later `prepareLocalSandboxWorkspace` call then saw the owner change and rejected.

The fixture now publishes both live session entries first, then creates the worktrees and binds the recovery entry to its checkout. The cleanup behavior is intended and unchanged. Every existing requester revocation, session replacement, worktree rebinding, file-integrity and authorized-recovery assertion is kept.

## Evidence

Proof ran on an AWS Crabbox (c7a.2xlarge, Node 24.22.1, [run_cc81f18c5e9ea631870710a46d79d312](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cc81f18c5e9ea631870710a46d79d312)) against base `4efd662cc2c`, using a patch byte-identical to this PR's diff (same base, same file blob):

  - Base: exit 1. Cleanup removed the fixture checkout and reproduced the exact `Local sandbox managed workspace owner changed` failure.
  - Fix: exit 0. The checkout was kept and the same recovery-authority case completed.

The idle command-palette browser regression intermittently fails when keyboard dispatch takes longer than the 200 ms search debounce between characters.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. CI can consistently check that usage updates leave idle searches settled and genuine command/model updates still refresh results.

Control the timeout clock while typing, then advance the debounce after the full query and after each usage event. Keep every existing assertion, including exactly one session search. This changes one test file (+8/-1 lines), with no production changes.

- Deterministic reproduction: split typing into `zzidle` and `query`, advancing the timeout clock 200 ms between fragments. Both session-list calls occurred **before** usage events; the strict assertion failed with two calls. Three usage events added zero calls (211 ms test time; 2.807 s wall time).
- One fixed named-file run: 1/1 passed (153 ms test time; 2.698 s wall time). All three runs used the repository UI test command for this file, one at a time with a 120 s timeout. No repeat loops or CI reruns.

title: fix(gateway): restart after slow sidecar cleanup finishes

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an in-process Gateway restart exits instead of restarting when a sidecar exceeds its diagnostic cleanup grace but finishes successfully before shutdown completes.

## User Impact

User impact: a successfully joined slow sidecar no longer prevents the Gateway from restarting. Pending cleanup, rejected operations, explicit retained-resource failures, and fatal shutdown errors retain their existing authority. No configuration, schema, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An expired diagnostic grace was recorded permanently even after the existing required owner join completed the exact cleanup operation. Final shutdown disposition now omits only that operation's obsolete grace warning after successful settlement. It does not increase a timeout, add a retry, reorder shutdown steps, or clear unrelated failures.

In the failing main QA run, the GitHub OAuth sidecar finished after 7.288 seconds and shutdown reported a clean join, but the stale retained-resource classification still forced exit 0 instead of the requested restart.

title: fix: make failed workspace preparation diagnosable
body:
Related: #197849

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed workspace preparation failures discard unmatched Git diagnostics, leaving users and operators unable to identify the initiating clone or refresh failure.

## User Impact

Users receive a diagnostic ID that remains intact after reopening the session. Gateway operators can match it to the original Git process output and exit status. Raw transport output stays out of shared conversations.

The original production clone cause remains unknown. This does not change credentials, cancellation policy, or automatically retry failed workspaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing clone owner now records unmatched failures in its operator logger and returns a short correlation message. Keeping the message within the existing retained-summary bound prevents middle truncation from cutting through the ID. Existing preparation and cancellation owners remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Native Git regression: red on base, green with the fix; 23/23 clone-owner tests passed (39.19 s command wall time, including compiler preparation).
- Workspace preparation/recovery: full file 18/18 passed (57.04 s); final shared-fixture replay 7/7 passed. Covers initial failure, another failure through real preparation/source cancellation, then successful same-session recovery.
- Actual isolated Gateway: `sessions.create` → real Git failure → `chat.send` failed retry in the same session. Both restored complete, distinct IDs from history and matched the original causes in operator logs; clone I/O was not mocked.
- Core and affected-test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): base `5dab86f716c9cc5cc8d4ac4ddfb48a400f3fca01` to the final working-tree snapshot committed as `5543bf00ec80bf927094b4abab8df8553ca6ccc7`; no actionable findings in the supplied diff and summary-owner context.
- Registry sibling coverage: 36 passed; two fixture cases were blocked at `git fetch --depth 1 origin` by this host's linked-worktree shallow-history safeguard, before reaching the changed classifier. The safeguard was not bypassed.

body:

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes healthy proxied model responses failing after 16 MiB of cumulative SSE traffic, even when every event line is small.

## User Impact

Long proxied responses can finish. Each outstanding event line remains capped at 16 MiB, oversized lines still cancel the response, and stalled reads and error bodies retain their existing limits. Accumulated assistant output can exceed 16 MiB.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing reader now charges raw bytes to the outstanding newline-delimited line before decoding, releasing that budget after each completed line. This keeps the current line parsing and reader cleanup while removing the lifetime traffic cap. No configuration or protocol change is needed.

## Evidence

- Real loopback HTTP through `streamProxy` and native fetch: 18 MiB of small valid text deltas completes; an oversized pending line fails and closes the upstream socket. Both regressions fail on baseline `9ca7932563ff3a8d2d3eca37e50d6ea7b031a527` and pass with this change.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts -t 'accepts cumulative SSE traffic above 16 MiB over native HTTP|rejects an oversized pending SSE line and closes native HTTP' --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`: baseline 2 failed, fixed 2 passed (1.53 s wall).
- Entire named proxy test file: 24 passed (1.61 s wall), covering cancellation and reader release, terminal/error outcomes, idle deadlines, error-body bounds, and split Unicode input. Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent isolated autoreview of the final diff and complete owner/test composition: no actionable P0–P3 findings.

title: fix: keep wide public conversation tables readable
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: public conversation tables split ordinary words into one-to-three-character lines when a comparison has many columns, making the conversation difficult to read on phones and desktops.

## User Impact

Readers can scroll wide tables horizontally without crushing their words. Ordinary short tables remain compact, and long cell text and URLs remain contained. A long two-column table can also scroll on a narrow phone instead of forcing its cells to fit. No configuration, public API, dependency, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public Markdown renderer now keeps native table layout separate from its bounded scroll viewport. One intrinsic sizing rule serves short, long, and many-column tables; there is no column-count cutoff. Long cells wrap at the existing chat sibling's 24rem cap. The native table is keyboard-focusable and its viewport has a visible focus indicator, preserving table/header semantics without adding named regions to every short table. Paragraph wrapping is unchanged.

title: improve(ui): show message reactions as one quiet tab on the bubble corner
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reactions on a chat message sat in a row of bordered chips inside the sender's footer row, where they pushed the sender name aside and grew into several rows on busy messages.

## User Impact

User impact: each message now shows its reactions as one small tab on the outer bottom corner of its bubble, so the sender name stays in place and no row is added.

- One reaction shows only its emoji. More show the three most-used emoji and a total.
- Hovering or focusing the tab names who reacted. Clicking it lists every reaction above the usual palette, and any of them toggles in place.
- The hover toolbar keeps its add-reaction button before and after the first reaction.

Things to know:

- Toggling one specific existing reaction is now two clicks (open the tab, press the reaction) instead of one.
- Flat assistant text has no bubble edge, so its tab shares the hover footer row under the end of the text. Under a short reply the tab starts up to 240px in, capped at half the message column so narrow panes keep it reachable. A footer wider than that meets the tab on hover; this is an accepted edge case.
- On touch, names stay hover/focus-only as before; tapping the tab opens the list with counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bubble now owns the reactions anchor, so one placement replaces three (group footer, earlier-message action row, inline). That removes the picker hand-off between the action row and the chip row, and the `compact` picker variant that only the chip row used. A caption under images anchors the tab with CSS anchor positioning, so the tab hangs from the caption instead of the wider image box.

title: fix: recover longer session history text within response bounds
body:
Related: #64970

## What Problem This Solves

Agents reviewing long conversations cannot request visible message text beyond the fixed 4,000-character `sessions_history` preview, even when the complete message fits within the existing response budget.

## User Impact

Callers can opt into `maxChars: 1..64000` for bounded visible-text recovery. Omitting it preserves the 4,000-character default. The 80 KiB response cap, access checks, physical-session checks, and existing reasoning/tool-preview limits remain in place.

This is not an unbounded export: oversized source rows remain explicitly incomplete, and historical/pre-reset discovery is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool requests a bounded read through its existing authorized `chat.history` owner and applies the requested limit to visible text locally. Reads retain at least the existing upstream preview size so smaller text requests do not shorten reasoning/tool previews. It preserves upstream truncation facts and marks a source-row group incomplete when the local byte cap splits its display siblings, rather than silently treating the surviving sibling as complete.

The existing Control UI full-message/export path serves interactive readers; it does not supply this model-facing reader option. Unlike the closed environment-override proposal in #65029, this is a bounded per-call option, not a new global setting or a higher default. It builds on the pagination owner in #97101 and structured truncation in #126342.

## Evidence

Reviewed against upstream `5cef30a310125838abdbd3400a4db3dd334e8220`; tested candidate `a2a5642216e839ad6503e4f95ca0787ba4ae1eeb`, published as `e929d2ae16f1965218bb16778bfd9eeac7529ca3` with an identical tree.

- The supplied regressions fail on the unmodified upstream implementation (9 failing, 27 passing assertions). The final candidate passes 64 tests: 50 history/anchor-budget tests plus 14 prompt-prefix stability tests. Final two-shard wall time: 53.98 seconds; CI timing is not yet available.
- Review found and fixed preview-bound regressions for top-level tool results, supported result aliases/envelopes, nested tool results, and small visible-text limits. Each added regression failed before its focused fix and passes afterward.
- Canonical production typecheck `tsconfig.core.json` and agents-tools test typecheck `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json`: passed.
- Repository `run-oxlint.mjs` scoped to both changed TypeScript files: passed (0 problems). Repository formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.

title: feat(ui): toggle wrapping on code blocks in your own messages
body:
Related: #196070

## What Problem This Solves

Code blocks in your own chat messages wrap long lines, with no way to see the lines as they were written. Long commands, logs, and URLs are harder to read when they are split across rows.

## User Impact

User impact: when a line in a code block you sent wraps, a small toggle in the block's top-right corner switches the block to horizontal scrolling and back. Wrapped stays the default.

- Blocks where nothing wraps look as they do today and show no control.
- Line spacing in these blocks now matches assistant code blocks, so they are slightly more compact than before.
- The pending preview after starting a new chat shows the same block. Its toggle appears once the chat opens.

## Why This Change Was Made

Human-message code fences were passive, so the wrap default from #196070 could not be turned off. They now reuse the wrap control and click handling that assistant code blocks already have, without the copy, reveal, or JSON tools.

The toggle sits in the corner of the first row instead of a toolbar row, so it adds no height to the block. Wrapped text on the first row stops short of the control. With wrapping off, the first row fades out before the control and scrolls clear of it.

The pending new-chat preview renders the same block so rows do not reflow when Chat takes over. It stays passive until then. Aligned block art is unchanged.

Accepted edge case: after turning wrapping off, widening the pane until nothing overflows hides the toggle until a row overflows again. The block reads the same in both states at that width.

## Evidence

Screenshots are the real Control UI build against a mocked Gateway with synthetic messages, at 1180 px in the dark theme and 100% scale. "Before" is the original base `5cef30a310125838abdbd3400a4db3dd334e8220`.

**Before** (original base: wraps, no control)

![Before: code block in a sent message on main, wrapped with no control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca28c5d8-88b7-45e1-9bf0-3b6bcef5bb58)

**After** (wrapped, toggle in the corner)

![After: the same block with a wrap toggle in its top-right corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a1bd1d6-9fed-4e6a-961d-b464d7a4da23)

**After** (wrapping turned off)

![After: wrapping off, lines scroll horizontally and fade at the edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e33c79a-9e1e-45a8-ab02-f91eb86a0123)

<details>
<summary>390 px, light theme</summary>

| Wrapped | Wrapping off |
| --- | --- |
| ![390 px light theme, wrapped](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76cac8f4-e538-4e36-a991-6c240a302b32) | ![390 px light theme, wrapping off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddd62fec-68a1-470b-92c8-d6828b5eb6e3) |

</details>

Author checks on the original candidate:

- `ui/src/e2e/chat-code-block-fences.e2e.test.ts`: 7 passed. The new scenario runs at 1180 px (dark) and 390 px (light) and covers the default wrapped state, Enter and Space on the toggle, unchanged code text, no page overflow, no text under the control, no control on a short block, and the passive pending preview.
- `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.transition.e2e.test.ts`: 8 passed.
- Unit suites for code blocks, chat JSON text, the new-session page, and highlighting: 94 passed.
- UI typecheck, oxlint, stylelint, oxfmt, and the Control UI controller guard pass.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` against the merge base flags this change's stylesheet growth: about 1.2 KiB raw and 0.2 KiB gzip of total CSS. `main` is already over the total CSS cap, so the check allows no growth; it fails locally and is an advisory warning in CI. No JavaScript, startup, or request budget is affected.
- Local autoreview (Codex engine, P0–P2) on the complete local change against `5cef30a`. The first pass found one P2: the toggle could hide after turning wrapping off when a row fit the viewport but not its padded scroll area. That is fixed with a regression test, and a second pass on the final change reported no findings. The reviewer saw the diff only and did not run code.

Not covered: WebKit and Firefox, right-to-left messages, and a live Gateway.

Requested and directed by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Maintainer verification

The review found that the end padding was outside the overflow created by the wide code child: at maximum horizontal scroll, the final characters were still faded. The unwrapped human-message `pre` now sizes to its content (with a viewport-width minimum), so its existing padding remains reachable by scrolling. No new preference lookup, polling, cache, or rendering owner was introduced.

The incoming candidate failed the endpoint proof at 1180px and 390px. The correction passed real wheel scrolling in both directions, the first-row suffix beside the toggle, long-message expansion, and the complete New Session → Chat handoff with unchanged code text. The existing seven code-fence browser cases, UI typecheck, scoped lint/style/format, and test-line guard pass. The two Side chat typography cases also pass after scoping assistant-control assertions to the assistant row and replacing the obsolete no-user-wrapper expectation with checks for the intended short-code behavior. Independent P0–P2 review of the complete corrected candidate found no actionable issues. The runtime logic also retains the previously passing 65 focused unit tests and eight New Session transition cases.

title: fix(agents): keep exec declarations stable across CLI completion turns

Related: #193919 (open since 2026-11-09 by @ensignwesley for message declarations; its `lazy-exec-tool.ts` hunk makes the same declaration/authority split, but it predates #197330 and has had no activity since). This PR repairs only the current main regression.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes restricted CLI completion turns advertising an `exec` schema without `background`, `durable` and `yieldMs`, which made the owner and completion tool catalogs diverge.

## User Impact

CLI sessions keep one stable `exec` declaration across owner and completion turns, so the provider sees the same tool prefix. Call-time authority gates still refuse background continuation where the process tool is not callable.

#176892 requires identical owner/completion declarations with authority enforced at call time. #197330 correctly made the completion-turn denial of the lazy `process` tool visible to callable-tool selection, but the lazy `exec` tool chose its declaration from that callable flag. Declarations now follow whether `process` is offered in the session catalog, while `processToolAvailabilityRef` still tracks callable authority and is passed unchanged to execution. A truly absent `process` tool keeps the restricted declaration.

Related: #195878

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Code Mode checkpoint reads exhausting the transcript worker's memory when a long session is replayed after a cold restart.

## User Impact

Cold checkpoint replay no longer needs to retain every overwritten historical payload at once. This does not delete history, raise the worker heap, or change schemas, retention, permissions, or configuration. Runtime qualification is still pending; this draft does not claim recovery of the affected live session or a measured RSS improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stream selected custom payloads directly into the existing checkpoint collector inside the current SQL snapshot and actor queue. Keep materializing arrays for generic custom-branch responses.
