title: fix: avoid retaining obsolete saved-state snapshots
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary retention of superseded saved-state snapshots when a long session cold-loads its Code Mode store. Replaying all historical payloads into an array before folding the latest values can exhaust the transcript reader worker.

## User Impact

Cold saved-state loads fold each selected payload as it is read instead of retaining the entire historical payload array. Branch selection, missing-leaf failures, historical validation, deletes, and content provenance remain unchanged. No stored data, schemas, dependency pins, context budgets, or worker heap limits change. This does not change the context-meter UI or claim to eliminate every possible long-session memory failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing branch-navigation owner now exposes its selected payloads lazily. Durable and incognito store readers consume them inside their existing snapshot/owner scope; generic custom-branch responses still return arrays. No additional cache, state owner, or recovery path is introduced.

## Evidence

- New deterministic consumption regression fails on base `2890bbe6c47de6dc59f0448af403ff0de1f9d1a0` when the second snapshot is read before the first is folded; it passes with the fix. It observes payload consumption, not garbage collection or an absolute heap ceiling.
- All **37 tests across six affected owner/consumer files passed** through the repository runner with `--maxWorkers=1`, including durable/incognito store replay, branches, admission fences, long-suffix fallback, reports, and store behavior. Total external runner wall time was 86.05 seconds, including cold worker preparation; the new regression file took 0.336 seconds on its red run. Published head `e75bd70b5588ef4173cfd22e707fd845a8b5a2c8` has the identical tested tree. PR CI duration is pending.
- Matching `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json` typecheck passed. Scoped type-aware oxlint passed on all four TypeScript files (2.79 seconds after declaration preparation). Pinned oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent read-only P0–P2 review: no actionable findings. No configured local ClawSweeper entrypoint was found in this task environment; canonical local autoreview against the complete base-to-working snapshot completed `scoped-clean` at P0–P2, with no actionable findings. Its surrounding-source/execution limitations remain; the independent reviewer separately inspected unchanged owners and callers. The initial hosted ClawSweeper request is now reviewing the published head; no duplicate request was made.
- **Additional runtime limit:** a full cold-Gateway guest-binding/restart case was preflighted but not launched because the current exec surface had no qualified attributed agent-turn entrypoint. This is an unexecuted case, not an observed runtime refusal. Executed SQL-worker, durable/incognito actor, and guest tests cover the owning persistence boundary; no full-Gateway restart claim is made.
- **Acceptance rule recorded before measurement:** preserve final value/provenance and stored-row semantics while removing the historical payload array; retain branch/validation/budget behavior without increasing heap limits. Used the maintained `scripts/perf/transcript-maintenance-measure.ts` workload with 512 events of 32,768 bytes, one session, five reads per process, cold replay only. Five baseline/candidate process pairs were interleaved; baseline modules were loaded from exact base blobs via a task-owned loader, with loaded-source hashes checked. This measures the actual SQL maintenance owner and worker transport, not end-to-end Gateway or live-session latency.

<details>
<summary>Paired synthetic cold-replay measurements and limits</summary>

All ten processes produced the same final-value digest. Each traced read visited 1,024 SQL rows and transferred 32,756 reply bytes; those counts did not change. The fixture held about 16 MiB of historical event JSON.

Values below are the median of five per-process medians, and separately the median of five per-process p95 values; they are not a pooled p95.

| Boundary | Before median / p95 (ms) | After median / p95 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Worker owner read | 42.365 / 57.635 | 41.187 / 53.590 |
| Worker CPU | 41.229 / 56.608 | 41.118 / 53.390 |
| Main receive + apply | 0.05235 / 0.09329 | 0.05667 / 0.09058 |

The main-task median rose by about 0.0043 ms while its median p95 fell; no main-thread speedup is claimed. Median whole-process RSS was 652,083,200 → 639,975,424 bytes, but that includes all threads and is not a reader peak-heap measurement. Recorded host load ranged from 10.70 to 12.83 for the first load average. Navigation metadata still scales with history, and live stored values remain retained. The original live worker OOM was not deliberately re-triggered; this proof covers the eliminated eager payload-retention path, not all possible OOM causes.

</details>

title: improve(ui): cap long session menus and search groups
body:
## What Problem This Solves

With many shared groups, the Move to group submenu grew to the full window height, and finding one group meant scanning a long list. Its 1–9 key hints also crowded the check mark.

## User Impact

User impact: Move to group stays at a compact height and scrolls. When there are more than eight groups, a search field at the top filters the list.

- **Same height:** Move to group, Assign to…, and Add to section share one height cap: about ten rows, with half of the next row showing so the list clearly scrolls. Assign to… was taller before, at 420 px.
- **Search:** Desktop search uses the same always-visible field as Assign to…. The phone sheet keeps its existing single search control. Typing on a row goes into the field. Each opening starts unfiltered. If nothing matches, the menu says “No groups match your search.” and still offers the commands.
- **Commands stay reachable:** Remove from group / Move back to groups and New group now sit below a divider, so they no longer read as groups.
- **No number hints:** The 1–9 group shortcuts are removed. Typing now searches instead.
- **Sticky search edge:** On scroll, rows now slide under the search divider instead of showing as fragments above or below it. This applies to Assign to… as well.

No change to short group lists beyond the divider and the removed number hints.

## Why This Change Was Made

The group list is a flat list, and shared groups have no owner, so it cannot be split into “mine” and “everyone’s”. A height cap and the existing search pattern are enough for long lists. Search only appears once the list scrolls, so small workspaces keep a plain menu.

title: fix(openai): new API-key and ChatGPT connections default to Astra
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: fresh OpenAI API-key and ChatGPT connections, reused Codex credentials, and subscription image requests choose Astra instead of the intended Sol default for routine work.

## User Impact

New eligible OpenAI connections select `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` when no model has been selected. This includes API-key setup, ChatGPT browser/device-code login, inference-enabled Sign in with ChatGPT, offline credential reuse, detected native Codex setup, and direct Codex OAuth imports within their existing scope.

- Existing primaries, aliases, profile pins, configured provider-model defaults, and fallback chains remain authoritative. Modern or legacy Astra-only restrictions retain their working implicit default. Login initializes only the target agent; shared-default setup checks agents that would inherit it. Existing installations are not automatically migrated.
- Subscription image requests use Sol as the outer Responses model; the generator remains `gpt-image-2` or the requested override. Unsupported-model recovery uses only explicitly configured OpenAI primary/fallback models, with no hardcoded Astra call.
- Identity-only sign-in selects no inference model or other funding source. Personal-account connections do not change an agent model. Credential routing, entitlements, schemas, and storage mechanisms are unchanged; Hermes is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Based on a report from Sedrak Hovhannisyan. One lightweight Sol reference supplies the setup and image-host recommendation. Existing login, model-policy, and config-write owners initialize an eligible missing selection while preserving existing and concurrent choices. A static starter cannot bypass identity-only consent.

The final production repair also removes an accidental heavy agent-runtime import from OpenAI setup. Permission checks share the existing private onboarding helper rather than loading the execution graph; no registry, timeout, public SDK subpath, configuration option, or migration mechanism was added.

## Evidence

- **219 focused checks across 10 files passed**, including real auth/config persistence, normal login and credential reuse, consent, per-agent modern/legacy restrictions, Codex imports, OpenAI defaults, image HTTP requests, and prompt/tool-prefix stability. The default/reuse/restriction regressions have recorded red-before/green-after proof.
- **A real PR-caused Gateway regression was reproduced and fixed.** The [failed CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43242989175/job/131273623973) tested merge `39474c03` into main `925d17a2`, confirmed by [preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43242989175/job/131272435942). Separate frozen-dependency checkouts running the same handler entrypoint passed **398/398 on main**, reproduced the original merge's 120-second astral-prefix failure, and passed **398/398 on that merge with the exact three-file import repair**. No registry reset or timeout was changed.
- Four targeted typecheck leaves, lint/format/diff checks, and the **full clean-snapshot build passed**. UI startup-JS/CSS budget warnings remain; no warning-free result or UI-budget repair is claimed. Five built-package smoke checks also passed for selection and restriction preservation.
- Qualified OpenAI and Anthropic cold-import snapshots passed with verified process cleanup. This is cold-import proof, not activation/workload memory or an attested whole dependency closure. The build, profiler, and fresh native Sol review cover tree `41dfa86e15e607abde9901b87fccd6c7332c2390`; production inputs are unchanged by the final test-only cleanup.
- **Packaged stable-to-PR preservation: 3/3 cases passed.** Installed the published `openclaw@2026.11.3` package (reported commit `847611d`), created state with its real onboarding/configuration commands, verified backups, installed the PR package over it in a disposable prefix, then ran candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive`. Explicit Astra + fallback/aliases, an unset primary with an Astra-only modern policy, and an unset primary with an Astra-only legacy map all retained their selected fields, credential-profile metadata/counts, and resolved Astra default. A separate fresh packaged API-key setup selected **`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`**.
- **Installed CLI/SQLite conversation and credential continuity passed.** Embedded `agent --local` turns completed before and after the package transition against the repository's loopback Responses fixture. Both requests used the same stored synthetic API credential and retained explicit Astra; the post-transition request contained the earlier assistant response. title: fix: end over-cap rate-limit waits after tool execution
body:
Fixes #168101.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a turn that has already run tools can hold its session lane for hours when the next model request receives a 429 with a long Retry-After.

## User Impact

The saved positive `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` now bounds post-tool waits too. An over-cap unsafe attempt ends with the existing rate-limit error, releasing the turn without replaying completed actions or switching accounts or models. Retrying manually still requires checking work already completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cap incorrectly depended on replay safety. Apply it before any same-model wait; let the existing recovery and terminal owners decide the result. Replay-safe failover, short waits (including equality with the cap), long-window evidence handling, disabled caps, and auth-profile rotation policy remain unchanged. Update the retry policy and stale recovery comment to match.

## Evidence

- Regression on base `407537bc41d8`: the unsafe controller case returns true instead of false, and recovery returns `retry` instead of `proceed`.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0da0223-3f95-4864-b576-136e6b6b99f3)

## What Problem This Solves

The New Session project picker shows the same generic glyph for every project, while the chat header already shows a project's own icon.

## User Impact

User impact: registered projects show their own favicon in the picker rows and on the picker trigger. GitHub search results, recent repositories and a selected GitHub repository show the filled GitHub mark. The trigger's default icon is now `folder-git-2`. Projects without an icon keep a generic glyph.

## Why This Change Was Made

Picker rows have no session yet, so the existing session-keyed workspace icon route can't serve them. A sibling Gateway route, `/__openclaw__/project-icon/<projectId>`, resolves a project through the existing requester-specific visibility owner and reuses the existing workspace icon scanner and cache. The browser only names a project ID it can already list, never a host path. The route requires `projects.list` read access, applies the same per-project visibility policy as the project list, revalidates authority before responding, and keeps the remote-workspace exclusion from the session route. Hidden project IDs return 404 before scanning their checkout.

The UI reuses the existing `openclaw-workspace-icon` element, which now accepts a fallback glyph. The chat header and the picker share one route/auth helper, replacing the header-only version. The session menu's stroke reset was hollowing filled brand marks into outlines, so filled icons now keep their fill there and on the picker trigger. Project artwork loads lazily when a selected project or the opened picker needs it. Existing loading/error boundaries retain the fallback glyph. The boot manifest was regenerated after integration.

## Current maintainer verification

Compared main `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637` with integrated candidate `90430eec1800ac74a755595c0264a67690037004`.

The current-main search field, autofocus, keyboard navigation, scroll area and footer were preserved when resolving the integration conflict. Optional artwork was removed from the unselected New Session startup path.

- Desktop (1280 px), tablet-width (820 px), phone-width (400 px) and dark-theme browser checks passed. These are Chromium viewports, not physical-device qualification. The observed interaction runs recorded no layout-shift score outside recent user input.
- 29 Gateway HTTP/scanner/access cases and 529 UI cases, including mandatory canaries, passed. Coverage includes private registered projects after a writer warms the cache, access changes, unknown projects, local/remote workspaces and selected-trigger fallback.
- Full builds for the candidate and baseline passed. Scoped Gateway/UI type checks, lint, CSS lint, formatting and diff checks passed. The independent integrated-source review found no actionable P0–P2 defect.

The previous security repair remains: a read-only caller cannot retrieve artwork from a private registered project, including through a warmed cache. title: fix: narrow unconfigured GitHub tools in the built-in harness
body:
Related: #197592 (earlier publication of this change; this PR contains the current-main integration).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the built-in OpenClaw harness offering authenticated GitHub operations after the GitHub owner has confirmed that no publishing identity is configured.

## User Impact

Unconfigured built-in listings keep credential-free readiness, setup/status, and original publication-receipt observation without advertising unsupported writes. Public GitHub read/search remain available. Native-default authentication, configured but unhealthy identities, unknown discovery, and possible delegated publishers are preserved; no migration or new setting is required.

**Scope:** Codex and other native/SDK harnesses without the embedded declaration pin retain their existing listings. Omission there is deferred rather than risking warm-thread rotation or adding a native custody lifecycle. Another configured agent conservatively retains the broader surface because it may own a delegated publishing target.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing GitHub lifecycle publishes authoritative configuration facts off the turn path. Tool construction consumes them without reading credentials or probing authentication. Known absence selects a compact readiness-only schema; failed discovery is unknown, not absence. A linked human GitHub account is not treated as the managed bot publisher.

The existing session-prompt owner pins the declaration before catalog compaction, so background discovery cannot rewrite an established provider prefix. Configuration/support changes and explicit refresh re-evaluate it. Fresh execution closures, current authority, private access, direct-only handoffs, and accepted-operation settlement remain with their existing owners.

## Evidence

### Matched built-product before/after

Historical matched qualification used BASE `24819901d92ee379b5b36a957276d3b3657d7b79` and the pre-integration production tree in `bb2b031c95d5869dfb2bec33f8ddd7d2b898e06f`. Both used the actual built Gateway and served Control UI, a separately paired synthetic test viewer, visible composer/Send, and the same neutral loopback provider. No mocked baseline Gateway. Counts are original UTF-8 HTTP **body** bytes, not JSON reserialization.

In this table, “Native empty/configured/unknown” refers to the native GitHub credential backend within the built-in pinned harness, not reduced listings in native/Codex harnesses, which remain deferred.

| Workload | BASE body bytes | FIX body bytes | GitHub actions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Native empty | 160,902 | 154,773 | 9 → 1 |
| Native configured | 160,902 | 160,902 | 9 → 9 |
| Native unknown/error | 160,902 | 160,902 | 9 → 9 |
| Managed configured/unhealthy | 160,902 | 160,902 | 9 → 9 |
| Existing synthetic uncertain receipt | 160,942 | 154,813 | 9 → 1 |
| Code Mode, native empty | 47,359 | 41,230 | 9 → 1 |
| Code Mode, native configured | 47,359 | 47,359 | 9 → 9 |

Exactly **6,129 bytes** are removed from the publisher definition: **6,954 → 825 bytes**. Direct tool JSON is 126,204 → 120,075 bytes; system JSON stays 31,911 and remaining bytes 2,787 (2,827 for the receipt case). Code Mode tool JSON is 16,832 → 10,703; system JSON stays 27,740 and remaining bytes 2,787. These scopes are not added together.

## User Impact

title: fix(ui): sidebar loads older sessions when a session list is collapsed
body:
Related: #192154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: collapsing a sidebar session list makes it fetch older sessions and show "Loading…", its attention dot does not match the unread dot, and "Load more sessions" turns into "Loading…" whenever the sidebar refreshes in the background.

## User Impact

User impact: in the ungrouped view the session list simply continues when you reach its end, and nothing loads or appears under a list you have closed.

- **Ungrouped view:** reaching the end first shows more of the sessions already loaded, then fetches older ones. There is one control at the end of the list instead of **Show more** and **Load more sessions** stacked together.
- **Collapsed list:** no control and no request. Open it again and it continues from its end.
- **Grouped views and People sort:** unchanged layout. **Show more** stays in each group, and one **Load more sessions** sits below all groups, because an older page can belong to any group.
- **Loading feedback:** only a request for older sessions shows "Loading…". Background refreshes no longer dim or relabel the control, and a click made during one is carried out when it finishes instead of being ignored.
- **Collapsed-group dot:** same size, color and finish as the unread dot. Its meaning (a session inside needs attention) is unchanged.

No configuration change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first version of this PR removed the automatic loading and left a manual **Load more sessions** button under the collapsed list. That treated the symptom. These are the causes:

1. **The control was in the wrong place.** In the ungrouped view every unpinned session is in one list, but the control that continues that list was rendered below all sections, outside the list. Closing the list did not hide it. It moved it into view, and that was read as "the user reached the end". The control now belongs to the list's own end, so a closed list has nothing to continue from.
2. **It fetched before showing what it had.** One page is 200 sessions and the list starts at 30. Reaching the end fetched another 200 and revealed 15. With 600 sessions on `main`, two visits to the end fetched 400 more sessions to show 30 more, and then the list stopped at 60 with only a manual **Show more**. Now loaded sessions are shown first, 15 per visit, and a page is fetched only when they run out.
3. **"Loading…" reported the wrong thing.** The control used the roster's shared loading state, which is also set by every background refresh. The sidebar now tracks its own request for older sessions.

Accepted edge case: a short ungrouped list whose end is already on screen loads one older page when the sidebar opens or the list is expanded. That is the existing behavior from #192154 and stays bounded to one step per time the end comes into view.

## Maintainer verification

Current candidate: `252c7c9b488b3766974f37e9aec1ff6b38eb239f`. The visual captures below remain from `738e0022`; production code is identical. Before: main `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637`.

Fixes: Activity recap text, the waiting message above the chat composer, and the summary prose on Team Reports pages render thin on macOS.

The Control UI and the generated Team Reports pages turn on antialiased smoothing for the whole page, which switches off macOS stem darkening. #197458 restored the default (`auto`) for chat prose; this does the same for three more reading surfaces, each at its own rule:

title: fix(agents): omit message when no supported route exists
body:
Related: #169091

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents are offered `message` when their session/runtime has neither a supported source route nor configured outbound messaging capability.

## User Impact

Agents without routes stop receiving an unusable tool. Supported source replies/reactions and configured outbound-only or offline channels remain available. Source-only target/action restrictions still apply at execution. Configuring a channel restores availability through the existing refresh lifecycle. No new public configuration, permission rule, or database schema is introduced; existing WebChat sessions record prompt support on their next operator declaration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery uses existing session metadata and channel configuration owners, not transport health or default schema actions. Omission follows final policy/schema filtering and child/cron capture, so presentation does not become an inherited permission denial. All registered configured senders participate in the absence check; binding-based schema pruning is not an outbound allowlist. Modern text senders and pending synchronous configuration remain supported; payload-only adapters rejected by delivery are not advertised.

## Evidence

Original published history and pinned main `b48d16bf6e98f0b9c1e110548fc46b3b35f2becd` are preserved. The PR is open and **unmerged**. No merge or deployment is authorized.

Core types, scoped typed lint, format, six-file snapshot check and diff check passed.

title: fix(ui): remove automatic browser preview cards
body:
Related: #197528

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated page-preview cards cluttering the conversation whenever the agent browses during a task.

## User Impact

Browser tool calls keep their normal expandable results without automatic preview cards, including inside expanded work. Deliberately shared links, images, and widgets remain unchanged. The Browser panel remains available through its existing controls and retains the session’s latest successful browser target. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Following the requester’s design direction, this removes the card rather than hiding it or introducing a replacement. @vyctorbrzezowski plans to redesign browser activity as a better chat-transcript experience in separate work. The renderer, styles, thumbnail capture/cache, preview-placement selectors, transcript plumbing, unused copy, and obsolete card tests are removed. Browser target selection remains because the existing panel still uses it.

A follow-up review of adjacent code also removed the card-only `browserTab` field from Browser panel open requests. No other producer sends it; panel controls, Gateway panel commands, native links, and session-result routing are unchanged. Browser, settings, security, and configuration documentation no longer describes the removed card or its menu and page-preview behavior. Stale card paths are removed from CI owner metadata and benchmark checks. External-link hover previews keep their existing setting.

The generated boot manifest and config-documentation hash are refreshed; no new state owner or compatibility path is added.

## Evidence

- The removal regression failed in both light and dark themes before the card was removed; it passes afterward.
- After merging current `main`, **3,553 of 3,555 tests passed across 316 of 317 UI unit files** covering chat components, Browser panel, menus, clipboard, and native links. The two failures were mobile session-menu timing tests outside this change; that file passed **17/17 twice** in isolation.
- **30 production-bundle browser tests passed** across 6 suites: light/dark expansion and reload, draft retention, repeated visits at desktop/mobile widths, social URLs, delivered widgets, and host/node Browser panel routing.
- Browser panel tests now route through session results instead of the removed card event. CI owner-selection tests passed.
- UI typecheck, i18n verification, boot-manifest generation, config-documentation and schema checks, Markdown lint, scoped lint, and formatting passed. Earlier production-build validation passed.
- The production build’s advisory size report was over its startup-JS and total-CSS limits (92,176 vs 92,137 startup bytes; 322.8 vs 318.9 KiB CSS gzip). Those warnings are not claimed as passing, and no limit was raised.
- Original author review and simplification completed; current independent maintainer review is recorded below.

Screenshots show the actual Control UI production bundle with deterministic mock Gateway history and an emulated 1200 × 950 viewport, not a live user session. The original before image is from the base above. The collapsed after image is reused because this revision leaves that appearance unchanged; the expanded after image is from the complete removal.

<details>
<summary>Expanded browser result — normal output, no automatic card</summary>

![Expanded browser result without an automatic preview card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11497edc-a193-492a-99d2-b4dd88c282cf)

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

Integrated current main `d4577ec4b31` in `248345613c7`, preserving its newer tool-output and assistant-identity owners. Removed the retired browser-card references from the new inline-command presentation and extended the existing output-preservation test to cover it.

title: fix: WebChat retries NO_REPLY into unwanted replies
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: human WebChat turns retry an intentional `NO_REPLY` into an unwanted acknowledgment, including incidental conversations that mention another person.

## User Impact

The agent can remain silent when no response is useful, rather than manufacture a reply just to complete a model turn. Requests directed to the agent still run; selected human-only messages keep their existing no-agent-turn behavior. Empty answers still recover, and internal tasks and private/subagent runs still owe their required results. No configuration or data migration is needed. This PR does not deploy the running Team Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebChat shares its channel name with the internal routing sentinel. The completion owner now distinguishes human input from internal provenance instead of requiring a visible result from every human WebChat turn. Direct-conversation guidance also explains when to stay silent and how to emit the exact control token, without adding per-turn state to stable prompts.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through a real isolated Gateway with two authenticated Control UI operators and a fixed HTTP model provider: on the base, the provider's `NO_REPLY` was retried into `Acknowledged.`; with the fix, the same flow completes without an assistant message or another model attempt.
- Back-test preserves the first agent request with a copied teammate, human-only mentions during an active run, recipient notifications, subsequent explicit agent requests, and history hiding of intentional silence.
- 48 tests pass across five focused files: authenticated mention delivery (2), reply expectations (10), direct/group guidance (10), required-result/empty-answer recovery (12), and prompt-prefix stability (14). Final run: 117.74 seconds wall time. Changed files: Gateway suite 22.70s, required-result suite 24.80s, guidance suite 3.56s. CI timing is pending.
- Production and Gateway-server test TypeScript checks, focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The first CI run identified stale canonical prompt fixtures. Reproduced the snapshot gate locally, regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`, and verified `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` passes for all six files. The two changed artifacts contain only the reviewed direct-conversation guidance and derived size/hash facts; production source is unchanged from the tested/reviewed candidate.
- Independent Codex AutoReview, P0–P2, on the complete local candidate plus surrounding completion/command/prompt owners: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Candidate source became commit `80827713e92cc8286228ef5c921ca61fd6d3e84d`. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its existing checkout was dirty; hosted ClawSweeper remains the selected fallback review.
- Simplification: reuse the existing completion and conversation-guidance owners; no new state, config, retry machinery, or token parser. Production delta: +17/-3; test delta: +29/-4, plus regenerated fixtures. The separate 25-line test allocation covers the authenticated regression and internal-result preservation without raising the shared scalar.

The fixed-provider test proves OpenClaw's assembled guidance and completion/delivery behavior, not live-model intent accuracy. It does not exercise a deployed Gateway or live external channel.

## Contributor credit

Requested and landing authorized by @vincentkoc, credited as co-author.

title: improve(ui): show the search field at the top of pickers and menus
body:
Related: #189573

## What Problem This Solves

Searchable pickers and menus opened with a title and a search icon on the right, so finding someone or something in a long list (people, projects, agents, devices) took an extra click before typing, and the title repeated what the trigger already said.

## User Impact

User impact: the search field is always visible at the top of a searchable card, and the crowded pickers open ready to type.

- **Where it shows:** Assign to…, the Projects and Where pickers on the new session page, the project list in the command palette's new session settings, the Sessions filters popover, Jump to file in the diff panel, the session menu's member list, and every searchable select picker (owners, agents, models).
- **Focus on open:** the Projects and Where pickers, the palette's project list, searchable select pickers and Jump to file open with the field focused when a hardware keyboard is likely. Touch-only devices and phone sheets leave the on-screen keyboard down until the field is tapped.
- **Assign to…** keeps focus on the first row, so Enter still assigns to you, and typing goes straight into the field, including when the submenu was opened by hover.
- **Typing on a row** moves into the field instead of row typeahead. **Escape** clears a query first and closes on the next press. A clear button appears once there is a query.
- **Phone sheets** keep their title row and show the field under it.

Not changed: the session sharing popover keeps its own Permissions heading with a search toggle, and the composer's skills menu keeps its header toggle. Both are section headers inside a larger menu rather than a card's only header.

## Why This Change Was Made

#189573 moved each card's search behind a header title and a search icon. This keeps that PR's shared header component as the one owner for card search and changes what it renders: a leading search icon, the field, and a clear button. The collapsed state went away, and with it the per-host "searching" signals, the toggle's keyboard routing in the shared menu, and the special cases for a title that swaps with a field.

Hosts line the icon and text up with their own rows through two CSS custom properties on the shared row, so the icon sits on the rows' icon or avatar column and the text on their label column.

Accepted edge: a touch-only device that later gets a hardware keyboard starts focusing the field after the first hardware key press, the same rule the shortcut hints already use.

## Evidence

- The production-bundle project-selection E2E also passed; the current project-search screenshot was inspected. Capture instrumentation was temporary and restored without changing the committed test.
- Maintainer-authorized budget exception: built CSS grows by 334 bytes against a 64-byte tolerance, exceeding the effective limit by 270 bytes. This is PR-attributable growth, not an inherited failure. All other CI jobs passed; the aggregate failure comes from this budget check.

- Maintainer review found that a searchable list could keep keyboard focus while losing its active-option accessibility relationship. The list now keeps that relationship when search is visible, without changing the layout or adding state or lookups.
- The existing browser helper now checks the actually focused element. It failed on the incoming code; after the correction, all 60 relevant Chromium tests and the same 60 WebKit tests passed. UI typecheck, formatting, whitespace, and pre-commit checks also passed.
- Independent review of the complete corrected diff found no actionable P0–P2 issues. It did not execute tests or inspect unchanged files; the maintainer separately reviewed the focus and menu owners.

Screenshots are from the mocked Control UI (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`) at 1280×860 and 390×844, 2× scale, with fixture people and agents added to the mock only for the capture (not committed). "Before" is `main` at 55cac5900c.

Related: #197452

Supersedes the manual-skill proposal in #197453 following the request to keep selection conversational and avoid special commands.

## What Problem This Solves

Deep Research’s tool guidance lacks clear criteria distinguishing conversational research requests from ordinary mentions.

## User Impact

People can ask for Deep Research in ordinary chat without a picker, skill reference or slash command. This clarifies existing model-guided selection, not a new deterministic intent classifier or permission grant. Plugin enablement and tool policy still apply.

Default enablement, portable execution, credentials, retained jobs, retry keys, cancellation and source-authority owners are unchanged. No new start/stop commands, skill, research engine, schema or public configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Put the decision guidance on the existing tool: recognize explicit research requests and retained-job follow-ups, carry current-chat sources and budget, avoid quick answers and explanatory/quoted/code mentions, and report only the returned job state.

The tool description and two docs are the complete change: three files, 27 additions and one deletion against pinned main `5d6a026e43757ea6302e4c1151d6ace28468ced0`. title: improve: make Telegram tool progress easier to scan
body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Telegram's progress draft shows one operation twice when the agent calls a tool through the catalog dispatcher (`dispatch_action`). The dispatcher row stays visible next to the real operation until the turn ends. Tool rows also run the action label into its context, and parallel subagents with the same label cannot be told apart. ## User Impact - A successful dispatcher call collapses into its real operation as soon as the nested result is accepted. Failed or blocked dispatchers stay visible as before. - Tool rows read `🛠️ **Exec** · command…`: the icon stays outside the bold label, and ` · ` separates the action from its context. Running and failed status words stay italic. Completed rows drop the redundant word. - Subagent rows, and progress rows for `sessions_send`, `sessions_history` and `subagents steer|kill`, add a four-character UUID suffix such as `…2633`. An unlabeled child shows `Subagent …a4f0`, not `Delegated work`. The suffix is display only: routing, lifecycle keys and diagnostics keep the full identity. No new configuration, schema or permissions. ## Why This Change Was Made - The existing wrapper-retirement owner (`finalizeToolActivity`) now runs when a nested call's result is accepted, not only at `agent_end`. It records each retirement, so later events cannot retract the same row again. - The Telegram renderer formats the icon, bold label, separator and context. The separator counts toward the row width budget. - One display-only helper, `formatSubagentProgressReference`, makes the short reference. Codex native worker threads pass their own thread IDs; nothing infers a session ID from a task path. - The shared client tool catalog no longer ships Gateway-only `progress` metadata. No web, iOS, macOS or Android client reads it. ## Evidence Live Telegram Test Server run through the real QA user (TDLib recorder) and the official Telegram Web K client. The same scenario ran on the merge base `db964b78` (before) and on this branch (after): exec, read, `sessions_spawn` and `sessions_history` through the catalog dispatcher (`dispatch_action`, because both tools are catalog-only in this config), then a held command. The model is a scripted Responses provider; the Gateway, tools, catalog dispatcher, subagent spawn and Telegram delivery are real. Config: `streaming.mode: progress` with `progress.toolProgress: true`. **Before:** each dispatched operation shows twice until the turn ends. ![Before: progress draft at the merge base](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d055ad3f-5838-49cd-b8c5-9f3417625693) **After:** one row per operation, `·` separators, and the child's short reference. ![After: progress draft on this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/350fd7b8-d2dd-433d-976d-c92c43983f98) A second recorded run shows the same thing in the TDLib edit history (HTML rebuilt from Telegram entities; the child reference changes per run): | | Before (`db964b78`) | After (this branch) | |---|---|---| | Read row | `📖 Read lines 1-20 from feed-proof.txt` | `📖 Read · lines 1-20 from feed-proof.txt` | | Spawn row | `🤖 Start subagent Check marker` ×2 | `🤖 Start subagent · Check marker …707e` ×1 | | History row | `📖 Read session history` ×2 | `📖 Read session history · …707e` ×1 | | Duplicates | visible in every edit from the dispatch until the edit just before the final reply (~11 s here) | none in any edit | Both turns delivered `FEED_FINAL_OK` and retired the draft. The Telegram Web session was terminated by its exact ID, and the lease was released. Focused tests on this head: `progress-draft-preview`, `embedded-agent-subscribe.tool-result-ordering`, `tool-display`, `channels/streaming`, `subagent-control.worker`: **148 passed**. `bot-message-dispatch.preview.telegram-http`: **41 passed** (this head updates its stale `🛠️ Exec` expectation to `🛠️ Exec`). Limits: the model is scripted, so this does not show model commentary. The candidate Gateway ran a `dist` built from `5ed94ec`; this head (`79f4ffb`) differs from it only in that one test file. ## Compatibility and merge risk - **Public SDK:** one additive export, `formatSubagentProgressReference`, in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`. No existing export changes or is removed. - **Two-way door:** no stored state, config or protocol changes. A revert fully undoes it. - **Blast radius:** progress rows on Telegram and the other consumers of the shared display registry (Slack, ClickClack, Codex projection), and when a dispatcher row is retired in the progress feed. Contributor credit: @vincentkoc.

title: fix(ui): side panel resize handle ignores presses on its line
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the chat side panel resize handle does not respond when you press on its visible line, or just past it on the panel side.

## User Impact

User impact: the side panel (Side chat, Files, and the other panel tabs) can be resized by pressing the divider line itself or a few pixels on either side of it, the same way the sessions sidebar already works. The handle is also the same width along its whole length. The trade-off is that the first 5px of the panel's leading edge now belong to the handle; the first panel tab starts 6px in, so no control is covered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The divider paints its line at the trailing edge of its gutter, but the pointer target sat entirely before that line: the desktop side panel is stacked above the divider, so the half of the target meant for the panel side never received input. The target is now centered on the visible line, and only the target is raised above the panel. The line keeps its previous layer, so it stays hidden while the gutter animates in behind an already placed panel.

## Evidence

Maintainer validation: all four existing Control UI rail/column browser tests passed on the published source, including the pointer drag from two pixels past the divider. The before/after target overlays and original failing-base result were inspected. No new cross-browser or native-shell proof is claimed.

Measured in the Control UI against the mock Gateway (Chromium, 1600x900, light theme) by pressing and dragging at every pixel across the divider.

| Dock | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Right, panel body | 10px before the line; the line and the panel side do nothing | 6px before the line, the line, 5px past it |
| Right, tab row | 5px before the line; the line and the panel side do nothing | same as the body |
| Left | 5px before the line, the line, 4px past it | 6px before the line, the line, 5px past it |
| Below | 10px above the line; the line and the panel side do nothing | 6px above the line, the line, 5px below it |

Right dock at 4x zoom. The pink tint is an overlay of the measured grab area and is not part of the UI; the resting appearance is unchanged.

After:

- `ui/src/e2e/chat-rail-columns.e2e.test.ts` now also drags from 2px past the line on the panel side. It fails on the base (`expected 730 to be less than 710`) and passes with the fix.
- Stylelint, format check, and oxlint on the changed files, and `pnpm tsgo:ui`, pass.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unreadable tool-progress rows when session, Knowledge, and node calls surface diagnostic identifiers instead of the operation being attempted, or native subagent notices expose their protocol type as a title.

## User Impact

Users can distinguish operations without reading diagnostic identifiers. Prepared rows separate the operation from context, including ordinary Read paths; native subagent notices have a human-readable title. Verbose diagnostics remain available, and status-only command progress still hides execution titles and commands. No configuration, schema, permission, or runtime tool-shape changes.

**Validation note:** exact-head CI has completed with one independently reproduced, inherited failure—not green CI. The protected pre-existing-failure landing route is being used under the existing scoped land instruction; review, security and writer-capability gates remain enforced. The existing tool-display registry supplies concise progress metadata while preserving diagnostics. Live/history activity and raw channel callbacks consume that owner. Node rows show the operation and target rather than payloads; concise Knowledge progress omits UUIDs. The native Codex owner emits `Subagent` without changing lifecycle or identity. title: feat(ui): start New Session in the background with Cmd/Ctrl+Enter
body:
## What Problem This Solves

New session needs the command palette’s Cmd/Ctrl+Enter background-start workflow without leaving a partial transcript above the next prompt.

## User Impact

User impact: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter starts a session in the background while keeping the normal `/new` screen. The prompt stays in the composer until creation is accepted, then clears and regains focus. The session appears in the sidebar, with the same start, completion, and recovery notices as the command palette.

- With the default **Enter** send shortcut, plain Enter still starts and opens the session; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter stays on New session.
- With **Cmd/Ctrl+Enter** configured as Send, that chord remains the normal start; add **Shift** for a background start. The old shifted background chord keeps working.
- Draft sessions, native coding CLI starts, and mobile Return behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing draft submission owner still owns creation, reconnects, attachments, and recovery. Background starts no longer populate the source page’s foreground transcript preview. The created session retains its own prompt and attachments. The palette and New session now share one acceptance/recovery notice; foreground navigation-failure recovery remains intact.

The shortcut dialog and docs describe the chord. The duplicate shifted-modifier catalog entry found in the original PR was removed in favor of the existing definition.

## Evidence

- **Behavior:** desktop and narrow-width browser checks cover admission without a transcript, cleared/refocused input, typing the next prompt, sidebar admission, and opening the completion notice. Palette creation, preview, and rejected-first-turn recovery checks pass.
- **Real Gateway proof:** two successive background tasks completed successfully; their results were opened through the UI, and returning to New session left a clean composer. No intercepted Gateway RPCs or held responses. The model replies are scripted locally.
- **Focused checks:** 117 owner-regression tests passed (4.14 s wall time); the final keyboard-catalog/dialog/composer/navigation run passed 114 tests (2.98 s). These runs overlap and are not a summed test count. UI/test typechecks, scoped lint, format, and diff checks pass.
- **CI repairs:** the duplicate-chord regression passes. Overlapping foreground recovery tests were consolidated without dropping their assertions; the test-line ratchet now passes with no ceiling or allocation increase. Fresh CI for the pushed head remains the broad verification.
- **Review:** fresh local autoreview (Codex engine, P0–P2) found no actionable issues in the correction against `8f4952190535ff131f035b0555821f4ff186c117`, with full submission-owner context supplied. The subsequent identical-chord deduplication and test consolidation were checked with the focused run above.

title: fix(clawrouter): show friendly names for routed models
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the model picker shows raw labels such as `Anthropic · claude-opus-5-5` for ClawRouter models when the ClawRouter catalog does not send a display name.

## User Impact

User impact: ClawRouter models that OpenClaw already knows now show their normal names, such as **Claude Opus 5.5** or **GPT-6.1 Sol**, in the composer and model picker. Models OpenClaw does not know keep the existing `Provider · id` label until the ClawRouter catalog sends a `displayName`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClawRouter plugin already matches each routed model to the exact bundled first-party model (same provider, upstream id and API) to inherit model facts such as the family and media limits. It now also inherits that model's display name. The label order is: the catalog's `displayName`, then the matching bundled name, then the existing `Provider · id` fallback. Matching stays exact, so aliases and unknown or future models inherit nothing. No UI code changes.

Accepted edge case: when the same model is also configured directly (for example, Anthropic and ClawRouter both offer Claude Opus 5.5), the picker's existing duplicate-name handling adds the provider id, for example `Claude Opus 5.5 · clawrouter`.

## Evidence

- `extensions/clawrouter/provider-catalog.test.ts`: 8/8 pass. The protocol-mapping test now gets `DeepSeek V4 Flash` and `Gemini 3.5 Flash` from the real bundled catalogs. It failed on those labels before its expectations were updated, which shows the new path is used.
- The real bundled resolver gives `Claude Opus 5.5`, `GPT-6.1 Sol` and `GPT-6 Luna` for ids the live ClawRouter catalog serves. `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-fable-5-2` and `gpt-6.1-terra` have no bundled name and keep the fallback.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the commit: format, lint, typecheck, and guards pass. The only failure is the dead-export scan, which reports two existing unused exports in unrelated files (`src/config/skill-library-tool-split-migration.ts`, `ui/src/lib/config/config-saved-notice.ts`).
- Control UI captures (below) use the mocked Gateway with the catalog name each version produces; the rendering code itself is unchanged.

Gap: not run against a live ClawRouter catalog on an isolated Gateway; the plugin test covers the catalog-to-name path with the real bundled catalogs.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Knowledge page prose and claim text render too light on macOS, because the Knowledge page forced antialiased font smoothing on the whole page.

title: fix(ui): stop missing completed device dialog animations
body:
Related: #196687

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent `checks-ui` failures when the Your devices animation test resumes after a short height transition has already finished.

## User Impact

No user-visible change; this is the maintainer-directed flake-hunter lane l49 test repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test polls live `getAnimations()` after awaiting a Playwright click, but the disclosure transition lasts 280 ms and its inline styles clear after 300 ms. Capture real height transitions at the style-mutation checkpoint instead. Seek five progress points for the row-position assertions and finish transitions immediately, deliberately exercising the missed-live-animation branch. Keep the confirmation layout, open/closed disclosure, cascade removal, both viewports, and reduced-motion checks. The test shrinks by two lines; no shared helper, product code, timeout, retry, or baseline changes.

## Evidence

- Original observations: [run 43132492741](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43132492741/job/130900400378) failed at 1440 px; [run 43137144346](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43137144346/job/130915765701) failed at 390 px. Each file execution passed 3 cases and failed 1 at the same disclosure animation lookup. Both used Bun, Chromium, `--shard=2/3`, `--maxWorkers=3`, and `isolate:false`.
- Source establishes the transient-observation race. No local red/green browser execution is claimed. The file is excluded from unit projects and included in the Chromium browser project; browser execution is forbidden on this production host. One `crabbox doctor` attempt failed because the configured `ascii-box` provider lacks `ASCII_BOX_API_KEY`. Original-order shard replay, alone/repeat execution, file wall time, and runtime validation remain for CI.
- Focused formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Local lint could not load `eslint-plugin-solid` in the dependency-free worktree; lint/typecheck remain for PR CI.
- Shared autoreview, Codex engine, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no findings, one completed pass against base `55cac5900c1501824b6e28b11e026805a4a8997b` and the local snapshot committed as `31c55018981`. Static assessment only. A second complete review found the old index-only startup `Promise.all` cancellation bug; its reviewed working-tree `Promise.allSettled` repair is included in the new head, with no additional P0–P2 defects established.
- First candidate CI: [run 43142402622](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43142402622/job/130932915163), motion cases 0/2 passed, reduced-motion cases 2/2 passed (6.6744 s file time). Both motion cases hit `AbortError` in the newly joined startup animations: cancellation rejects `Animation.finished`. The repair now joins those promises with `Promise.allSettled`, matching the production overlay lifecycle. UI shards 1/3 and 3/3 and all other jobs passed. No rerun was requested.
- Current head `0c32d59de62acbdddbbb3bfb28208df5ef815ed9`: [checks-ui (2/3) passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43143626107/job/130936877224), changed file **4/4 passed**, including both forced slow-observation cases. Shard 3/3 and UI e2e also passed; shard 1/3 and the baseline ratchet are pending. No CI rerun was requested. The orchestrator owns landing; this PR must not be auto-merged by this lane.

Stacked on #197388 until it merges; base: openclaw/glow-langoustine-2 at b1501b63c14ebc85c31cd19d5a314fd4fb51d78d. Draft only; no merge requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Installed theme-plugin details do not show what their themes will look like before users select them.

## User Impact

Users can inspect each installed theme’s colors and mode-specific artwork in a compact OpenClaw chat preview without changing their current theme or sending a message. A single-purpose, single-theme plugin uses the same palette chip as Appearance; multi-theme and mixed-capability plugins retain their normal identity artwork. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share the existing palette chip and a narrow compact-chat renderer while keeping palette readiness, supported-mode selection, artwork loading and retry with their existing owners. Recommended prompts reuse the window without changing their buttons, onSelect, busy/disabled state or unsent-draft launch behavior. Their superseded RGB-mask renderer and six exclusive artwork files are removed. There is no new palette cache, loader, route or catalog feature, and the preview does not fabricate a reply.

- Production Control UI with an isolated mock Gateway: public Artemis Canopy 1.0.2 plus Travel Themes palettes and authored light/dark background assets. Appearance chips remain unchanged. No operator Gateway was touched.

Startup JS is unchanged. Shared chip rules live in the existing settings-control sheet: startup CSS +280 gzip bytes, still one request and within its existing growth allowance. The standalone chip stylesheet and duplicate preview chrome are gone.
- Fresh independent Auto Review (OpenClaw, GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P2, reports no findings on the complete candidate against the exact stacked base. Reviewed staged-patch SHA-256: 864e60b65bcc5f55cf7c53cd3b73a27f1f634e850b77b507c9329b46cd7438fe. title: fix(tools): hide unsupported node and desktop routes
body:
Related: #197438 (earlier core-only version).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents are offered desktop and node-plugin routes that the current host cannot support.

## User Impact

Omit unsupported computer, Android-control, File Transfer, local-inference and Canvas routes while retaining discovery/pairing, supported offline routes and configured remote overrides. Inline/pinned widgets remain; only an unsupported device-panel target is omitted. Current-host omissions do not restrict a differently equipped child or scheduled run.

Plugins may optionally declare passive listing support through an additive SDK callback. Existing plugins and synchronous construction remain conservative. No new configuration, migration or permission change is required. Execution retains live target, command, path, approval and authority checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse prepared node/desktop facts and keep support separate from readiness and authorization. Plugin owners decide command/platform support. The host projects only current model/catalog definitions after descendant eligibility capture. Changed definitions pass through existing provider normalization and schema validation before deferred catalog publication. No remote discovery probe, parallel registry or core plugin-ID dispatch; computer images remain direct-only.

## Evidence

Original source base: `24819901d92ee379b5b36a957276d3b3657d7b79`. Reviewed implementation: `c6e086a064b4fd5bd9159ac6d4ab6b9100b5cca6`. Published head: `761864d8b34e88512fa714d89d110e80ecf987c4`; verified identical tree `53a9ed19501400f81ec5fb0c1c14d403dae26ebb`.

- Original full candidate: 299 unique passing tests across 18 files, one unchanged pre-existing skip, full build, types, lint/format, docs, boundaries, unused-file and SDK API/export checks. All three affected plugin entrypoint qualifications passed.
- CI consumer repair: 59 passing cases across seven files, preserving controlled sync/async resolver results and delivery/readiness/OAuth/refresh assertions.
- Provider/catalog repair: 113 unique passing cases across seven files, including prefix stability; full build, final runtime build and Google/Anthropic product replays. Three original-owner regressions failed before repair. A same-name executor issue found by local review was fixed with source-slot normalization; fresh independent follow-up found no remaining P0–P2 issue.
- Guard repair: 41 unique cases across five guard/fixture files passed. Exactly one verified completion-only generator suppression inventory entry was added; allocation 29 → 31 covers its two new lines. Types/lint/format/mock and local owned-growth checks pass. These test sets overlap and must not be summed.
- Renewed full-range audit before the MCP cache repair: fresh independent review covered the complete 56-file original-base-to-`e3fb056b51551a31a91a62520fe382942975a50d` range, not only the allocation, with no concrete P0–P2 findings. The reviewer matched 8/8 manifest source files and 97/97 retained corpus hashes. Full-range local autoreview against the original base was scoped-clean. Reviewers did not independently execute the product or qualify live hardware/provider behavior.
- Important correction to the hosted finding: ordinary final Google HTTP schemas were already clean on BASE due to a later provider pass. The proven defect was earlier raw replacement schemas entering deferred Tool Search/Code Mode catalogs after normalization/quarantine. The repair normalizes only changed definitions, validates them through the existing owner, and preserves canonical execution schemas and distinct source executors. No observed Google rejection is claimed.
- MCP cache repair: the existing immutable local node publication validates early/final cache reuse, construction publication and return; no probe, new registry, TTL or authority change. Three stale-cache regressions failed on BASE. An authenticated admitted-grant HTTP BASE replay kept `tools/list` empty after synthetic pairing. FIX passed 84 tests across seven files plus 14 prefix tests, types, lint/format, mock, budget and runtime build checks; fresh independent and selected local review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. These test sets overlap and must not be summed. Work counts: early path, eight resolves → four constructions/four projections; final path, eight resolves → eight constructions/four projections, retaining two-stage assembly; HTTP, four requests → two constructions/two projections/one synthetic execution. The HTTP proof uses an actual admitted grant, listener, cache, list and call with synthetic node publication and a controlled executor; it is not built-Gateway pairing-RPC, hardware or File Transfer proof.

### Matched transport measurements

Predeclared rule: remove only proven-absent routes while preserving unknown/offline/configured support, descendant eligibility, command/path/approval refusals and direct images; no remote probe. Measure raw received UTF-8 body/value spans with matched request shapes and path lengths, not JSON reserialization or timing.

This table is the plugin-continuation comparison, baseline `3639711bd68474967b1338c10f5b50b31b9d926c` (core fixes present) to `6eb2b018e871e50017f57070561a025ff98d3528`. It is not an overall-base savings estimate and is not added to earlier core-only measurements.

| First main request | BASE bytes | FIX bytes | System BASE → FIX | Tools BASE → FIX | Direct tools | Action entries |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No target | 65,716 | 58,002 | 13,442 → 13,331 | 50,550 → 42,947 | 10 → 4 | 41 → 36 |
| Android online | 74,301 | 73,623 | 13,467 → 13,427 | 59,113 → 58,475 | 12 → 11 | 59 → 56 |
| Android offline | 75,293 | 74,615 | 13,430 → 13,390 | 59,113 → 58,475 | 12 → 11 | 59 → 56 |
| macOS Canvas | 71,739 | 71,739 | 13,454 → 13,454 | 56,564 → 56,564 | 11 → 11 | 57 → 57 |
| macOS offline | 73,308 | 73,308 | 13,417 → 13,417 | 56,564 → 56,564 | 11 → 11 | 57 → 57 |

Built isolated Gateway, actual WebChat/paired-node WebSocket and scripted loopback provider: BASE fails the absence assertion; FIX passes 13 scenarios. Both arms: 26 main/13 auxiliary provider requests, zero deferred/catalog tools in this direct-mode workload, and the same eight synthetic node operations. Denied/offline attempts dispatch none. title: fix(ui): keep macOS font smoothing for chat text in sans-serif themes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat text renders with lighter, thinner strokes on macOS in the default Claw theme and other sans-serif or monospace themes.

## User Impact

On macOS browsers, chat prose in Claw, Knot, Tide and other non-serif themes now renders with normal macOS stroke weight, matching how serif themes such as Absolutely already rendered. Windows and Linux are unaffected because browsers ignore this property there. App chrome (sidebar, labels, composer controls) keeps its current rendering. No settings, schema or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app body sets `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`, which turns off macOS stem darkening. Chat prose only opted back into `auto` when the chat typeface was a serif, so light sans faces such as Instrument Sans kept the thinned rendering. Chat prose now uses `auto` for every typeface, which also removes the runtime helper and its CSS variable. A slightly heavier Instrument Sans weight was considered and not needed once smoothing was fixed.

## Evidence

- Real macOS rendering: production builds of `main` (bc56f785) and this change rendered in Playwright Chromium on an AWS Crabbox `mac2.metal` (macOS 14.8), using the Control UI E2E mock Gateway with a dense synthetic transcript. Text ink (luminance distance from the background, whole transcript, 2x) after vs before:

  | Theme | Dark | Light |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Claw (Instrument Sans) | +13.1% | +10.4% |
  | Knot (Geist) | +16.0% | +9.8% |
  | Tide (IBM Plex Sans) | +16.3% | +10.5% |
  | Absolutely (Lora, control) | 0 px changed | 0 px changed |

  Computed `.chat-text` smoothing went from `antialiased` to `auto` for the sans themes; Absolutely stayed `auto`.
- Regression: `ui/src/e2e/theme-typography.e2e.test.ts` "keeps auto smoothing on %s chat prose only" fails on `main` for Claw (`expected 'antialiased' to be 'auto'`) and passes with this change; Absolutely passes on both.

title: feat(research): add an explicit bounded research workflow
body:
Closes #197452

## What Problem This Solves

People need an explicit, reusable way to request bounded Deep Research using the sources and constraints already in their conversation.

## User Impact

Users can select the plugin-owned manual workflow with `$deep-research`, `/skill deep-research`, or `/deep_research`. It prepares a request for the existing research tool; selection alone is not job acceptance or execution. Ordinary mentions do not load this manual skill, and dollar references inside Markdown code remain literal. Default plugin enablement, portable execution, credentials, and tool policy are unchanged.

This is a model-routed workflow, not a deterministic `/research start` command or a new spending/permission guarantee. Call budgets are not hard token or dollar caps. A deterministic start command still needs original-requester and stable-operation-key custody at the real job-acceptance boundary; this change does not fabricate that contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing manual-skill contract supplies explicit discovery without another command owner, core tool, capability registry, public setting, or schema. The workflow preserves current-chat sources and supported budgets, document-only/no-web intent, stable-key reconciliation, cancellation, and honest returned states. The shared skill-reference parser reuses the canonical Markdown code-region owner so code examples are not selections.

title: fix: keep unused bundled meeting plugins off by default
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Unused Google Meet, Microsoft Teams meetings, and Zoom meetings activate automatically in source checkouts and custom distributions that bundle them.

## User Impact

Bundled copies no longer activate solely because they are present. Users relying on that default must enable the entries they need through the Plugins page, `openclaw plugins enable <id>`, or `plugins.entries.<id>.enabled: true`. Explicit enable/disable decisions, Gateway configuration-driven auto-enable, and intentional installation/selection retain their existing rules. Externally discovered copies retain their existing activation semantics; this is not a universal explicit-enablement requirement.

**Standalone `openclaw agent --local` users must explicitly enable meeting entries, even when those entries contain meeting configuration:** that route does not run Gateway startup auto-enable. The root npm package does not include these three plugins, so there is no meeting-removal benefit for that composition. This PR adds no configuration rewrite or transcript deletion; ordinary update migrations still run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Change only the three existing bundled-default flags and retain the existing activation owner and startup declarations. No new config/SDK/manifest contract, migration, readiness predicate, or setup/consent/authority change. Extend the existing empty-config startup regression by two lines, with a dedicated allocation rather than changing the shared test-line baseline.

## Evidence

Base: `24819901d92ee379b5b36a957276d3b3657d7b79`. Reviewed implementation: `ddfc343cb1f3f5e12ec6606cb96f780b9c33ca76`. Published head: `395222c00bc8c8959cbb1c20fddd5aed330f5b5d`, a metadata-only child with an identical source tree.

- Full BASE/FIX builds and the final clean committed-head build passed. Startup regression: intended failure on BASE, 10 passing tests on FIX. Prefix stability: 14 passed. Targeted typecheck, lint, format, test-line ratchet, canonical inventory generation, and `git diff --check` passed. Inventory generation produced no diff.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2), lead inspection, and a fresh independent P0–P2 review found no findings. The independent reviewer recalculated all 24 request measurements, eight Gateway lifecycle rows, both npm inventories, and the archive comparison. The published source tree is identical to the reviewed tree.
- Exact-head [CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43130732499/job/130897335558). [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197439#issuecomment-6811375180) found no code findings; its requested latest-stable compatibility evidence is now completed below. No code changed after review.

### Latest-stable upgrade compatibility

Verified npm latest `2026.11.3`, canonical tag `v2026.11.3`, peeled commit `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`. The actual clean stable runtime included all three bundled meeting packages; an npm-root-absent artifact was not substituted. Actual stable Gateways created synthetic archives through agent/tool transport, stopped, then the supported candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive` repaired the same private namespaces. Actual FIX Gateways reopened them successfully.

| Stable → FIX control | Active meeting plugins | Started meeting services | Complete archived session/summary JSON | Authored settings |

| Unconfigured | 3 → 0 | 3 → 0 | exact | preserved |
| Explicitly enabled | 3 → 3 | 3 → 3 | exact | preserved |

Lead independently recomputed archive equality and activation counts from primary outputs. Whole configuration bytes are **not** identical across stable→FIX: existing Doctor maintenance adds legacy Workshop migration, agent/provider bookkeeping, migration/wizard metadata, unavailable-skill entries, and configured-meeting auto-enable. These are recorded separately from this PR. An initial non-repair Doctor correctly requested schema repair; the supported repair then succeeded. An initial harness log-readiness timeout was corrected to observe `/readyz`, retaining the failed observation and clean shutdown. No product bypass or repair was introduced.

This qualifies latest-stable **Doctor/Gateway state compatibility**, not a published-updater/package-swap/automatic-service-restart matrix. Stable executable runtime build passed; its earlier full declaration build timed out. No real meeting, recording, audio provisioning, device, external model, or billing qualification is claimed. All owned Gateway/provider processes stopped and all four new loopback ports were verified closed.

### Request and startup observations

Fixed greeting, fresh isolated state, equal-length BASE/FIX paths, synthetic loopback Anthropic Messages provider. Twenty-four first requests cover four compositions and three presentations; no greeting executes a tool action. Raw HTTP body bytes are captured before parsing. These are deterministic counts, not token/latency/CPU/RSS measurements.

| Unconfigured bundled composition | Raw HTTP bytes, BASE → FIX | System JSON bytes | Tool JSON bytes | Direct/deferred count | Catalog entries |

| Directory | 49,600 → 48,992 | 32,692 → 32,084 | 16,403 → 16,403 | 13/40 → 13/37 | 53 → 50 |
| Direct schemas | 135,978 → 128,235 | 26,195 → 26,145 | 109,278 → 101,585 | 50/0 → 47/0 | 50 → 47 |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

<details>
<summary>Workload and measurement method</summary>

Build snapshots with `pnpm build`. ```

For stable compatibility use the stable and candidate `openclaw.mjs` launchers with the same private profiles: stable `gateway`, `agent` manual transcript import and `transcripts show --json`; stop stable; candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `gateway`, `gateway call plugins.list --json`, and `transcripts show --json`. </details>

- Clean committed-snapshot cold-import qualification passed, `qualified:true`, no gaps: `pnpm test:extensions:memory -- --extension google-meet --extension teams-meetings --extension zoom-meetings --skip-combined --concurrency 1`. No comparative CPU/RSS/time claim.

title: fix: hide desktop and Android tools when no supported target exists
body:
Superseded by #197462, which includes the core fixes, review/CI repairs and full plugin listing support. This earlier core-only PR is retained for history and should not be merged independently.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: desktop and Android-control tools are offered in fresh sessions even when the host has no supported route for them.

## User Impact

Agents no longer see the built-in `computer` or `mobile_ui` tool when prepared host facts prove its routes are absent. Node discovery and pairing remain available with an empty inventory. Known offline routes, configured Gateway desktops, configured or attached desktop services, placed desktops, and unknown inventory retain their tools. These runtime omissions do not become restrictions on a differently equipped child or scheduled run.

This is the core computer/mobile slice only. File Transfer, Ollama node inference, and Canvas node-panel listing are unchanged; their owner-controlled listing contract remains a separate decision. No configuration, SDK, permission, or storage migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate passive route support from connected execution eligibility, and apply runtime omissions only after policy/schema eligibility has been captured for delegated work. Execution keeps its existing live target, command, approval, and filesystem checks. The prepared node catalog and desktop-service facts remain the owners; no probes or capability registry are added.

## Evidence

Base: `24819901d92ee379b5b36a957276d3b3657d7b79`. Implementation head: `30b1f43104499837b6025dbd57ef095caefe942d`.

- Both runtime builds passed. **147 tests across nine selected files passed**, including tool-prefix stability, computer schema/target resolution, placement binding, mobile execution, and embedded/MCP descendant-cap capture.
- Five new assertions failed against the original production owners, then passed with the fix. The separate 135-line regression allocation covers support/unknown/offline facts and both durable-capture boundaries.
- Targeted production/test types, lint, formatting, unused-file scan, and whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review found one workload cleanup defect, repaired using the existing bounded child-process cleanup helper. A signal-fault run confirmed termination and release of both ports. No production correctness or authority findings remained.
- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. Local autoreview covered the full precommit snapshot against the base at P0–P2; its one missing workload-acceptance assertion was fixed and exercised. The original finding remains recorded, not relabeled as a clean machine verdict. The selected fallback's hosted review remains pending publication.

### Before and after

Predeclared acceptance: use identical synthetic request shapes on built isolated Gateways; remove unsupported routes without losing discovery, preserve known online/offline tools and established prefixes, retain descendant/cron policy eligibility, and add no per-turn network probe. Measure received raw UTF-8 HTTP request-body/value spans and deterministic work counts, not timing or estimated tokens.

| First main model request | Base raw body | Fixed raw body | Base system / tools | Fixed system / tools | Direct tools | Action enum entries |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No supported target | 56,161 | 47,561 | 11,283 / 44,288 | 11,258 / 35,713 | 5 → 3 | 54 → 36 |
| Known online target | 56,142 | 56,142 | 11,279 / 44,276 | 11,279 / 44,276 | 5 → 5 | 54 → 54 |
| Android observation | 56,143 | 56,143 | 11,280 / 44,276 | 11,280 / 44,276 | 5 → 5 | 54 → 54 |
| Same target offline | 57,134 | 57,134 | 11,242 / 44,276 | 11,242 / 44,276 | 5 → 5 | 54 → 54 |

The committed workload uses a built isolated Gateway, actual paired-node WebSocket transport, and a synthetic loopback provider. These are received bytes, not reserialized estimates. Direct mode has zero deferred/catalog tools. Both arms made eight main and four auxiliary provider requests. Each dispatched one synthetic screenshot, its execution close, and one Android observation; the offline attempt dispatched no device action. The screenshot reached the provider as a direct image block. Settled online/offline system and tool spans were byte-identical; the initial Anthropic cache-breakpoint relocation was retained, not normalized.

The final assertion-strengthened replay passed; its longer artifact path adds seven system bytes to each request, so it is not substituted into the matched-path A/B table. No latency, CPU, RSS, live-model quality, or billing claim is made.

Reproduce after building the head under test:

```bash
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/node-tool-availability.mjs .openclaw/tmp/node-route-proof
```

Hardware/OS permission proof is not covered. Configured/attached/placed route retention is covered at production assembly and transport-owner test boundaries; the full-Gateway raw-request matrix covers paired routes, not a provisioned cloud desktop. Remote CI and enforced human review are not yet complete.

title: fix(ci): report state-worker timing when the SIGUSR2 shutdown proof stalls
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds the missing timing diagnostics for the recurring SIGUSR2 shutdown-proof timeout in main-push `security-fast`. This is diagnostic instrumentation, not a fix for the timeout.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Production code, the 60-second test budget, the 10-second stop assertion and all authorization, custody and no-reuse assertions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The phase trace from #197392 caught a failing run (push `f6d5e173`, security-fast job 130861428077): the child received SIGUSR2, closed the restart-signal fence, and exactly 1000 ms later logged `restart signal settlement exceeded 1000ms waiting for restart-intent consumption`; the passing Bun run in the same job finished consumption after 974 ms. The 1000 ms settlement comes from #188047; consumption runs through the canonical shared-state worker (#167572), which this fixture opens cold. Source inspection cannot tell whether the second is spent opening the worker or executing the consume.

This registers a test-only `onWorkerRequestMetrics` subscriber and sets the existing `OPENCLAW_DIAGNOSTICS=sqlite.worker-timing` switch for the SIGUSR2 child only, printing compact writer open/execute timings on the same monotonic origin as the SIGUSR2 receipt marker. Its output flows through the existing temporary trace. The temporary allocation grows from 25 to 44 lines (19 added); the trace and allocation are removed together with the eventual fix. The extra early import can perturb timing slightly; the diagnostic still does not cover preparation before request enqueue.

## Evidence

- Phase-trace failure and passing sample above, from saved security-fast logs.
- Scoped repository oxlint (including `no-shadow`), scoped formatter, `git diff --check` and the test-lines ratchet (6,667,948 lines; ceiling 6,667,964) pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean.
- The process test was not run locally: it needs a broad compiled graph that is not run on the production Team host. The special shutdown step runs only on main pushes, so its next natural post-merge execution is the runtime proof. No dispatch or rerun is requested.

Related: #197392, #188047, #167572
