## What Problem This Solves

Agents offer generic welcome prompts instead of the tasks their authors recommend.

## User Impact

On an agent’s main/new-chat page:

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse ordinary agent metadata and the existing recents-or-suggestions layout. Optional description and starter metadata travel through `agents.list`; starters share the existing three-prompt/128-code-point validation and whitespace normalization.

Template pages, install-time task selection, bootstrap, and Retry are restored to their pre-PR behavior. Templates may supply welcome metadata in `CLAW.md`, but it is used only by the installed agent’s welcome page. There is no selected-task setup state or additional workflow.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin and personal theme cards show the selected theme’s colors instead of their own in Settings → Appearance.

## User Impact

User impact: users can compare each theme’s background and accent colors before selecting it, in either light or dark mode. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing connection-scoped theme catalog cache to load and preview every listed palette. Single-mode themes retain their available palette, accent overrides do not recolor previews, and failed preview reads use the existing Retry action. Built-in cards and the browser-local import slot keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Reproduced in Chromium on the base: both synthetic catalog themes incorrectly displayed Knot’s background and red/gray accents. The same production-UI regression passes with the fix.
- 50 focused tests pass: 18 theme-catalog, 4 Appearance catalog lifecycle, 4 theme-token, 5 theme-picker browser, 18 Appearance browser, and 1 production-bundle Chromium E2E. E2E covers dark/light palettes, single-mode fallback, accent override isolation, selection/cache reuse, plugin refresh, and inactive-preview failure/Retry.
- Initial E2E test time: 2.9 s; wall time including production UI build: 14.5 s. Focused owner/lifecycle wall time: 3.2 s; theme-picker browser: 1.0 s; Appearance browser: 1.1 s. Hosted CI time is not yet available.
- UI typecheck, targeted Oxlint/Stylelint, formatting, diff checks, controller guards, and staged test-line budget pass. The sandbox needed task-local Chromium libraries and fallback fonts; no live Gateway or shared dependency installation was changed.
- Independent Auto Review (OpenClaw, GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P2: no findings on the complete staged candidate against base `17140700d7b54ac2d960863123273528d1e77553`. Candidate patch SHA-256: `2632cbe1d5725c602b7238617cc361c7ff8b3d3df532441c9499080743281dcf`. Review inspected code; runtime proof was run separately.

### ClawSweeper follow-up

Addressed the [CSS-budget finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197388#issuecomment-6808052002) from `bc6ccd204cd041f6d5ba047fbcc71a26cbd7dfdd`: neutral unloaded-preview values now come from the existing swatch style memo, not an added stylesheet rule. The budget and baseline are unchanged.

- Paired production builds on the same toolchain: total CSS **1,705,417 → 1,705,287 raw bytes (−130 B)** and **331,126 → 331,109 gzip bytes (−17 B)**. Startup, chat, and new-session boot bytes are unchanged. This removes the full 130-byte increase identified by CI.
- The native performance checker passes comparing the repaired build with the reviewed-head build. The full archived target-base wrapper exceeded this sandbox’s 1 GiB temporary filesystem; exact target-base CI remains the authoritative fresh-head check.
- Added a held plugin-palette read to the existing E2E: both chips stay neutral while loading, then switch to the theme’s own palette. The E2E and 23 affected browser cases pass; unchanged owner/token proof is reused. Fresh E2E: 1.3 s test time, 13.8 s including build; browser suite: 1.4 s.
- Fresh UI typecheck, targeted lint/stylelint, formatting, test-line guard, and independent P0–P2 Auto Review pass. Existing screenshots are retained because the intended appearance is unchanged. New-head CI is pending.

### Visual proof

title: feat(huggingface): offer optional Hub tools alongside inference
body:
Related: #197384 (separate publisher-badge fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Hugging Face inference and Hub tools currently require separate plugins, making their setup and authentication easy to confuse.

## User Impact

The bundled Hugging Face plugin offers inference and optional Hub tools in one place. Hub access is off by default and uses a separate OAuth connection; existing inference settings and saved sign-ins are unchanged.

Existing `@openclaw/hugging-face` installations are not removed or disabled. To switch ownership safely, enable Hub tools in the bundled plugin, then disable (rather than uninstall) the old wrapper. An enabled old wrapper remains independent of the new toggle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundled plugin declares the existing Hugging Face MCP endpoint instead of introducing another integration. A plugin-owned opt-in activates it without making inference users connect to MCP automatically. Disabled defaults cannot shadow an active legacy server or its data-directory ownership. Explicit operator MCP overrides still win.

## Evidence

- The settings regression fails against the base manifest because Hub controls are absent, and passes with the new manifest. The production UI starts with Hub tools unchecked, saves the opt-in, retains inference enablement and discovery settings, and preserves the value across reload.
- 12 Hub activation/legacy compatibility tests, 10 bundle-loader tests, 7 Codex projection tests, 3 merged-config tests, and 2 inference-provider tests pass.
- Runtime, plugin-test, and UI-E2E typechecks; focused lint; formatting; MDX validation; diff checks; and the exact test-line budget pass.
- Screenshots use the production Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses. Live Hugging Face OAuth and tool calls were not exercised.
- Additional Gateway OAuth coverage timed out after 180 seconds after one test completed; this is not a passing suite. Exact-head CI and hosted review remain outstanding. Local independent review is unavailable in this sandbox; no clean local-review result is claimed.

Existing configurations and the public legacy package justify retaining compatibility; the README documents the manual ownership switch.

title: fix(plugins): prevent Gateway-thread SQL during prepared worker turns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the main worker-turn PG boundary failure: a fresh worker turn issued two Gateway-thread `select state_key, value_json from config_machine_state where state_key in (?)` queries (key `plugins.installedIndex`) where zero are expected.

## User Impact

Worker turns no longer perform synchronous Gateway-thread plugin-metadata SQL during runtime-registry inspection when a prepared metadata snapshot is already supplied. No behavior or ownership change otherwise.

## Why This Change Was Made

#144252 (`05a2844d39c2`) introduced a private registration cache in `acquireRegistryResources` so inspection-owned resources retire with their owner. The caller already supplies `metadataSnapshot`, but entering only the private cache hid that snapshot from nested readers. OpenCode/OpenCode Go catalog seeding then fell back through `normalizeModelCompat` → `resolveProviderMetadataOwners` → `readPersistedInstalledPluginIndexSync` to a synchronous SQL read.

This change composes the supplied snapshot with the private cache (new optional `cache` on `withPluginMetadataSnapshotScope`) for both inspection acquisition routes, preserving producer ownership and retirement. The boundary test now asserts SQL idleness after each turn instead of only at the end; no allowance, skip or retry was added.

## Evidence

- Main scheduled run 43087124624 at `89b4a45`, job 130754985117: `worker-turn-pg-boundary.test.ts:65` two-`prepare` signature. Reproduced RED on fresh main `4576d881`.
- Strengthened per-turn assertion RED before the repair; GREEN after.
- Named files: boundary, snapshot, inspection-resources and inspection-transfer 50/50 pass; unchanged metadata-worker and model-compat siblings 27/27 pass.
- Scoped type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review scoped-clean through P2.

title: fix(plugins): allow more than 64 feature operations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes feature plugins being rejected when a custom UI needs more than 64 typed operations, even when only a subset are agent tools.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can grow custom UI and backend contracts beyond 64 operations without disabling validation or authorization.

There is no replacement tool-count limit. The separate 64-event limit remains, and no migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A feature operation is a typed session action, not automatically an agent tool. Only operations with a `tool` declaration register agent tools. The reported custom UI already uses 64 operations but about 30 tools and needs room for further UI growth. Removing the arbitrary operation-count rejection preserves that distinction while keeping existing ID, schema, bounded-JSON, and authorization safeguards.

Cheap advisory diagnostics report successful plugin registration and complete embedded tool preparation exceeding five seconds, plus effective session catalogs exceeding 64 tools after final policy filtering. These thresholds are not capacity limits. Registration warnings distinguish registration entries from declared tool names without evaluating lazy factories; preparation timing is separate from total turn duration.

Catalog warnings include native/client and reachable deferred entries, exclude unavailable tools and hidden catalogs behind execution-denied controls, and preserve distinct same-named MCP/client identities without double-counting direct/catalog representations. Code Mode and deferred discovery can advertise fewer definitions to the provider than the effective catalog contains. A bounded 256-fingerprint cache deduplicates warnings by session and catalog; eviction or restart may repeat a warning. No new configuration or execution restriction is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Authenticated Gateway transport:** normal plugin discovery/loading and WebSocket RPC accept an 80-operation/30-tool plugin. UI-only operations 78/79 work through raw `plugins.sessionAction` and `createFeatureClient`; read-only writes are denied, malformed writes do not mutate state, and authorized writes are read back. Existing bounded-error cases remain. The regression is protected exactly once in PR/main/manual isolated-Gateway plans.
- **Built Gateway process:** an isolated `dist/index.js` Gateway loads the real fixture plugin, accepts UI-only calls 78/79, and completes three agent turns through a synthetic loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP provider. Genuine controlled 5,100ms fixture work produces the actual warnings below. The main session warns once across repeated turns; a filtered agent adds no large-catalog warning. Each provider request advertises two Code Mode definitions while the effective main catalog contains 100 tools. This is not paid/live-model evidence or a claim that all 100 tools were executed.
- **Build and focused checks:** full `pnpm build` passes on the integrated candidate (exit 0; build phases 3m25.3s). Authenticated Gateway, built-runtime and CI-ownership proofs pass; all 12 worker-turn-admission cases pass after integrating the concrete upstream fixture repair [#197370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197370). Formatting, targeted lint, canonical proof typecheck graphs, PR-relative diff check and the test-line ratchet pass. Details and retained warnings are below.
- **Fresh review:** independent review inspected all 20 changed files against main `6e0a9350e821f07f10d106600b9597f172b3f1b9` and found no actionable P0–P3 findings. Codex Autoreview assessed the complete candidate against that base at P0–P3: one completed pass, `scoped-clean`, exit 0, final source verification completed. Reviews inspected source and recorded receipts; they did not independently execute the tests.

<details>
<summary>Actual sanitized logs, reproduction commands and proof scope</summary>

```text
[plugins] feature-diagnostic-proof plugin registration took 5111.5ms (>5000ms); 31 tool registrations; 100 registered tool names. Registration completed (advisory only).
[agent/embedded] [trace:embedded-run] tool preparation completed: … totalMs=5385 stages=…openclaw-tools:plugin-tools:5129ms@5308ms,…bootstrap-bundle-catalog:67ms@5385ms
[tools] effective session tool catalog contains 100 tools (agent=main); exceeds the advisory 64-tool threshold. This is not the provider-advertised tool count: Code Mode and deferred discovery may expose fewer definitions. No tools were removed.
```

Ellipses omit synthetic run/session/process IDs and intermediate timing stages only. Thirty feature-tool registrations plus one factory yield 100 names; the extra 70 fixture tools exercise the advisory threshold and are not additional feature operations. Gateway/provider cleanup completed before the passing runtime test returned. No production timers, installed services or real user configuration were changed.

With current built artifacts prepared by `pnpm build`:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.feature-session-actions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts -t "retains recovery and feature transport contracts" --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/feature-tool-diagnostics.runtime.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

| Local proof | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authenticated Gateway regression | 1 passed | 66.14s, including cold compilation; 20.827s test time |
| CI ownership guard | 1 selected test passed | 4.99s |
| Worker-turn admission | 12 passed | 94.24s |
| Built Gateway runtime | 1 passed | 22.44s; 17.036s test time |

Restoring only the exact original operation-count guard made the same normal loader reject the 80-operation plugin with `Feature contracts require a plugin id and at most 64 operations and events`. The test then fails because registration is absent; this is loader-level red evidence, not a direct exception assertion. The fixed source was restored byte-for-byte afterward.

Pinned main `6e0a9350e821f07f10d106600b9597f172b3f1b9` integrated without conflicts and includes #197370 (`8408f1b57558d36d7bb21bf979a6275c46c20099`). title: fix(state): avoid host SQL during worker-owned database close
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes host SQL during worker-owned shared-state database retirement, exposed by two main WAL-close regressions.

## User Impact

Worker-owned close remains off the host SQL path. Native host checkpoints retain the nonblocking reader policy from #197219; accepted writes, native cleanup and clean-close seal requirements are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197219 (`78407f8`) intentionally disabled the busy timeout before retiring host checkpoints, preventing five-second waits behind readers. Its unconditional policy update also touched worker-maintained host handles even though those skip the host checkpoint. Restrict that update to nondelegated handles. Existing WAL assertions remain unchanged; no PRAGMA filtering, retry or timeout increase.

Contributor credit: Peter Steinberger and Ayaan (obviyus).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069)

## What Problem This Solves

Cloned projects cannot use **Current checkout**, even when the selected agent's access and sandbox policy permit working in the existing checkout.

## User Impact

A folder's or another project's saved Current choice does not opt a different clone into direct use; repository URLs and required remote placements remain isolated.

Direct sessions share existing working files. Existing managed or pending sessions must be continued in place or replaced with a new session, rather than switched into mixed direct/managed state.

Honor explicit false intent at the existing admission owner, reuse direct-root/sandbox checks, and scope the draft's direct choice to its project. title: fix(codex): plugin tool denies disable unrelated native apps
body:
Related: https://community.openclaw.ai/t/denying-intent-disables-the-native-codex-github-plugin/423

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native Codex hosted apps disappearing when an agent denies OpenClaw-owned memory plugin tools such as Memory Core `intent`.

## User Impact

Users can deny the audited Memory Core, LanceDB, and Memory Wiki tools without losing unrelated native apps such as GitHub. The named tools remain denied. Unknown or unaudited tools, restrictive allowlists, wildcards, and mixed unsafe policies still isolate the native surface. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared harness policy now recognizes explicitly audited plugin tool identities from the existing configuration- and workspace-scoped manifest metadata, rather than requiring every safe deny to be a core tool. One owner resolves the known audited set for both restriction classification and native-enforcement projection. Manifest ownership alone never grants an exemption or tool execution.

The Codex audit covers the adjacent OpenClaw memory-store and wiki tool families, not just `intent`. An unrelated synthetic plugin regression proves that the mechanism is generic; undeclared and unaudited controls remain restricted. These stores and vaults are separate from Codex native memory and goals. No new state store, cache, permission setting, or plugin manifest field is introduced.

## Evidence

- Before the repair, the exact and normalized `intent` regressions fail because the native surface is restricted. The original seven sibling cases pass.
- Focused policy, environment, harness-selection, and prompt-prefix suites: 145 tests pass. After the final internal helper rename, the changed policy and prefix suites pass again: 31 tests. The expanded policy file uses under one second of test execution; the complete four-file command takes 108.66 seconds including compiler preparation. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Production core typecheck and the selected `agents-tools` test typecheck pass. Targeted core/Codex lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. The Codex lint route also prepares the SDK boundary declarations.
- Independent local Auto Review through P2 reports no actionable findings; this was a static review, not another test execution.
- The 93 net regression-test lines have an exact dedicated allocation. The aggregate test-line ratchet retains seven lines of inherited overage; it is not reported green. The contribution-guide source-wide extension inventory command refers to a file absent in this checkout; no new direct bundled-extension import is introduced.
- Native source inspected at Codex `rust-v0.164.0`, commit `6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`: `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`, the dynamic-tool handler, `ext/goal/src/spec.rs`, and `ext/memories/src/tools/mod.rs`.
- Real macOS Gateway/Codex validation is now reported in [@jjjhenriksen’s completed retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-6803150138), superseding the [fixture-blocked first attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-6788842023). The results and limits are summarized below.

### Real Gateway/Codex behavior evidence

The local validator reports testing exact head `29503a892663d3be00392a59d08a9c0363a9e943` and separately built parent `086d2574a92e5d705b76615716d392e9de7e3ad1` on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node 24.22.1, and the explicitly selected Codex 0.164.0 executable. The fixture used a real disposable Gateway and existing owner-authorized hosted GitHub connection, not an API-key fallback or mock provider.

- **Allowed operations:** an actual Gateway-originated native `codex_apps.github.get_repo` call returned public `openclaw/openclaw` metadata. A real `intent.create` positive control succeeded through the native dynamic dispatcher and persisted an `armed` SQLite record. The positive control used `scope:"anywhere"` with sender scoping because that client entry point did not supply a separate conversation ID.
- **Base/head reproduction:** with only `intent` denied, the Gateway-created base thread returned `unknown MCP server 'codex_apps'` for the real read-only native GitHub RPC. On the fixed head, both a model-originated hosted GitHub call and the identical native RPC succeeded. A forwarding test-only stdio wrapper collected the unmodified Codex server’s RPC replies; it did not fabricate model/tool results or alter production policy/hooks.
- **Denied effects:** actual Gateway `tools.invoke` create/cancel attempts returned `Tool not available: intent`. Relevant full-row snapshots remained equal and no denied-marker intent records were created. The positive-control intent had automatically fired before the frozen comparison; its earlier transition is not credited to denied cancellation.
- **Tightening and resume:** the existing OpenClaw conversation continued under the deny on a safe successor native thread with working GitHub. Explicit reattachment of the old intent-capable thread was refused before inference by the existing Codex-home ownership/adoption guard, including with only `intent` denied; relevant records stayed unchanged.
- **Conservative control:** `deny:["intent","exec"]` again produced `unknown MCP server 'codex_apps'`; removing the `exec` deny restored the real hosted GitHub result.

**Coverage limits:** the retained-thread evidence is a restart/safe-successor plus explicit ownership-refusal case. The old app-server processes had terminated; it does **not** demonstrate revocation of a still-live captured callback after hot policy tightening. End-to-end coverage is for the Memory Core intent scenario and native-isolation control, not every LanceDB/Memory Wiki operation. This summary reviews the validator’s published observations; raw sanitized artifacts remain local to the validator and were not independently replayed here. The validator reports all task-owned Gateway/app-server processes stopped and disposable credentials/state removed, with the normal Gateway unchanged.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen requested the repair; Saul_Burgos supplied the original community report.

title: feat(agents): support required manual-step handoffs in chat
body:
Related: #192713 (effective-tool CLI diagnostics, a separate entry point).

## What Problem This Solves

Agents can end an authorized task when a required human step blocks them, and completing sign-in can leave the waiting task with its old unauthenticated tool catalog.

## User Impact

The existing chat question panel explains the observed blocker and supported manual step, optionally opens a verified link, and keeps the original task waiting. **Ready to recheck** refreshes available tools and resumes that task for authoritative verification; it never grants permission or declares success. **Stop this task**, Skip, and expiry leave the requirement unresolved and stop dependent work.

Existing OAuth, approval, native-permission, and desktop-ownership controls remain authoritative. There is no new configuration, approval layer, or durable restart ledger. Unsupported prerequisites still block the task, and the agent must verify completion before dependent effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing `ask_user` contract with `requiredAction`, preserving its attributed human-input wait, navigation, reconnect, cancellation, and expiry behavior. Advertise the built-in handoff in deferred Code Mode descriptions; client-overridden question tools do not inherit core semantics. After manual Ready, the tool requests the existing runtime-refresh continuation so newly authorized plugin tools become discoverable without restarting the Gateway or replaying completed work. Ordinary decision answers and unresolved manual steps do not request refresh.

The six-file follow-up repairs two gaps observed against reviewed head `723eef051b8954c7ff62686a6a8f2c768884de34`: handoff discovery and post-OAuth catalog refresh. It adds no Linear-specific policy or connector workaround.

## Evidence

### Original-flow replay with a real model and human OAuth

An isolated Linux Gateway used Linear plugin **1.0.1**, deferred Code Mode, the supplied screenshot, and the original uncoached request, “can you try this? for the isntalled linear plugin”. The real-account replay restricted Linear tools to read operations and instructed the agent against writes.

- **Before catalog-refresh repair:** the agent naturally displayed a manual-step card; human OAuth reached **Connected**, but Ready resumed with zero Linear tools. The original task remained blocked.
- **With the final repair:** the agent naturally displayed the card; after human OAuth and Ready, the same original run acquired authenticated tools, successfully called **`linear__get_user`**, finalized `done`, and displayed its success reply. No Gateway restart; zero active work or pending inputs. Run `2dd3c7d6-bab0-4193-b189-668de4096b7f`, completed **2026-11-14 00:33:52 UTC**.
- **Premature Ready without OAuth:** settled as still unauthorized, no repeated card or Linear operation. **Stop this task:** settled with zero subsequent tool calls. Both left no active work or pending input.

This proves the reported browser-account path on the tested configuration. It does not establish recovery for every provider/channel, an unavailable capability, or a plugin-bundled connector that the standalone `mcp login` CLI cannot resolve. Ready remains a recheck instruction; actual credential state determines catalog availability.

### Regression checks and review

- **125 focused tests pass**, covering manual/ordinary answers, Ready with and without a refresh consumer, Stop/cancel/expiry, creator-scope capture, deferred core discovery versus client overrides, normalization, existing runner continuation, and prompt-prefix stability. The repair regression failed before the fix.

title: fix: keep Activity permission errors stable during refresh
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Activity briefly replaces a settled permission error with loading placeholders when unrelated sessions change.

## User Impact

User impact: denied Activity views remain stable during automatic refresh, while Retry, changed filters, reconnection and relevant access changes can still refresh them. Existing rows remain visible during a same-query refresh and are cleared if the response denies access.

This does not grant new access or introduce a limited-readable-person view. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Activity now treats a permission denial as settled for the current selection rather than retrying it for unrelated activity. Explicit retries and authority changes bypass that settled state. Hidden-tab authority updates wait for visibility, and superseded responses cannot restore old rows.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on `09087a32dfc6a609d56147cd59304c63882ca805`: 58 owner/page tests and both browser scenarios passed. In the isolated real Gateway run, an unrelated session event left the settled denial at one request, one alert and zero skeletons; Retry made a new request. The separate held-response browser scenario retained the accepted row during refresh and removed it on denial. Restoring only the prior production owner/page files made two selected cases fail, including four unwanted reads instead of one. The candidate was restored byte-for-byte; no production changes were needed.

- Production-bundle Chromium regressions fail on base `ecaefd29e7f1a23657de41a7eb217ba083c477be` and pass on candidate `2902a87bcc9fb29ac8033772fd225862f7b6072a`.
- Held-response browser proof: an unrelated session event increased denied Activity reads from one to two and showed loading placeholders before the fix; after the fix there is still one read and the permission error stays visible. Clicking Retry recovers to rows. A subsequent held refresh retains the same row element, then removes it when access is denied.
- Isolated real-Gateway proof: a synthetic guest receives a real permission denial for another synthetic person’s Activity. Creating an unrelated session produces a real session-change event without retrying the denied view. Clicking Retry still makes one new request.
- Both browser regressions pass on candidate `2902a87bcc9fb29ac8033772fd225862f7b6072a`; 58 focused tests pass, plus a separate consumer run with 36 unit and five browser-component tests (overlapping coverage).
- UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, test-line budget and diff checks pass.

The reviewer did not execute tests independently and lacked some unchanged lifecycle context; a separate complete-source parent review covered the owner, page state, changed tests, real-Gateway test and refresh coordinator and found no actionable issue. The corrected real-Gateway regression passes (9.7 seconds; 56.4-second invocation), with a clean Gateway shutdown and Chromium exit. title: feat(plugins): guard effects against stale conversation assignments
body:
Related: #196909

> **On hold — draft conversion requested.** No detached-binding incident has been reproduced in Campaign Keeper, and the need for a new public SDK authority surface has not been established. Evaluate the Codex-style plugin-owned lifecycle approach using supported APIs before advancing this proposal. Codex’s owner/admin admission is not a multiplayer authorization policy, and its private harness helpers are not proposed for import into Campaign Keeper. The implementation and test evidence below are retained; they establish mechanics, not the necessity of SDK expansion.

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot safely tie an authorized non-owner participant's later effects to the exact current plugin conversation assignment using an awaited binding snapshot or the existing owner-only command guard.

## User Impact

Adds an opt-in `withCurrentConversationBinding` capability to supporting command and V2 tool contexts, without granting owner privileges or application membership. A callback receives host-bound requester/conversation/session facts, a live assertion, and an opaque restriction that V2 state writers enforce against the native binding row inside their transaction.

**On hold: the need for SDK expansion is being reassessed.** This is a working implementation proposal, not an accepted or released SDK contract. Custom/legacy binding owners, different physical state stores, missing identities, and Control UI/guest principals without an authenticated native channel requester fail closed. Command adapters must provide live host authorization; the text-command path and native Discord dispatch forward it here. No configuration migration, owner-only gate relaxation, Gateway change, deployment, or multiplayer claim is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing plugin lifecycle, session-incarnation, prepared binding-selection, and V2 state owners rather than asking plugins to reconstruct host authority. Preserve the opaque restriction when composing application checks; registered worker operations retain their stores' restrictions too. The native writer compares the exact binding and expiry after the final host commit grant while holding the mutation transaction.

V2's existing host commit-grant ordering remains: later revocation does not retroactively undo an accepted write. Application membership and actor ownership still belong at the application's conditional mutation owner. The reused prepared-selection owner is conservative: binding publications, including benign refreshes, can retire a callback and require a new request. There is no custom-adapter snapshot fallback or new persistent authority store.

The Campaign Keeper consumer remains unchanged and owner-only. Its [handoff](https://github.com/ekinnee/openclaw-agent-templates/blob/feat/campaign-keeper/docs/campaign-keeper-multiplayer-authority-handoff.md) supplies the concrete need, not multiplayer proof. This PR addresses the host-owned seam; it does not expose private capability scope to separate trusted-policy hooks.

title: fix: Home stays unavailable for read-only viewers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Home stays unavailable when a viewer can read the conversation but cannot send messages.

## User Impact

User impact: Read-only viewers can open the existing Home conversation alongside their current page. Sending and session actions remain controlled by the existing session permissions; this does not share Home with anyone new or create a missing Home for a reader.

## Why This Change Was Made

Home's presentation gate incorrectly required both history access and message-send access. Remove the redundant send requirement and leave target-session authorization, read-only composition, and page/dock identity with their existing owners.

This supersedes the proposed product direction in #191795, rather than importing its blanket Home privacy restriction. That proposal was not merged.

## Evidence

Maintainer correction on `6529245927f8e9aef0df8082ec1450e9fb7adf44`: two existing shell expectations now match the approved read-only Home behavior, including offline identity retention. The original expectation failed before correction; 18 dock/retention tests, UI-app types, lint and formatting pass. No production code changed. A fresh full-candidate P0–P2 source review found no actionable issues. The previous popover CI failure did not reproduce in one run at three Chromium widths; its cause is not claimed fixed, and new-head CI remains required.

### Before

![Before: Home is disabled for a read-only session viewer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/886eb200-0b85-4e8c-baf3-4fa8ccb69ac2)

### After

![After: Home shows the existing conversation while sending remains disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8f96a88-aa27-4270-a503-921d15645216)

- Isolated real Gateway + Chromium: the read-only Home button assertion fails on the base and passes with this change; the existing transcript renders with a disabled composer, and a direct send is rejected. The same transcript opens full-page, and changing the target to a foreign draft keeps its content inaccessible after reconnect and in the dock.
- Focused Home/dock/routing/presentation tests: 63 passed. Existing session-visibility policy controls: 10 passed.
- UI production and E2E test typechecks, focused lint/format, test-line allocation, docs MDX, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the complete staged change against `50b29a94f2447772e76b379edbdf9a448a2932b3`: no actionable findings. The runtime tests above were run separately. Reviewed source is committed as `f7cff9da5013f840da2fbc7f8005ef02a87b8334`.
- Simplification: one redundant write requirement removed; no new access policy, state, config, or protocol. The regression growth covers the reported failure plus real read/denied-target behavior.

title: fix: edit sidebar session names inline on double-click
body:
Related: #196829, #90655, #90184, #90833.

Requested by @hannesrudolph.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ce7adceb-0fe2-425c-9599-2ffdc7ed11d3)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: double-clicking a desktop sidebar session name opens a dialog instead of editing that name in its row.

## User Impact

User impact: rename the current session or another session directly in the sidebar, with the name prefilled and selected. Enter or blur saves, Escape discards the edit, and rejected saves retain the draft for correction. Single-click navigation, modifier-click links, read-only access, session actions, the header, and menu Rename remain available as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

This corrects the interaction shipped in #196829. It reuses the existing header input, canonical name normalization, and identity-bound session mutation owner rather than introducing a second rename implementation. The optional row editor loads only when used. The menu path shipped in #104416 still opens its existing dialog; the older closed attempts linked above are historical context, not implementations being revived.

## Evidence

- Production-bundle browser tests: **15/15 passed** on head 79e6293785f2b3b6c7275948cf45f37680570d4b, covering current and initially unselected rows, native double-click, Enter/blur/Escape, identity-bound writes, stale identities, rejected drafts, navigation and live permission changes.
- Focused header/sidebar tests: **77/77 passed** for the retained editor; affected row tests rerun after the context-menu repair: **25/25 passed**. Catalog lifecycle tests: **28/28 passed**. UI typecheck, scoped lint/format, i18n verification and test-line ratchet passed (13 lines of remaining slack).
- Existing bundle budgets passed against base 1651ee19282ca46d4be6639167e10b11ebc0c4d2: Chat boot **1,300,996 / 1,301,131 B**; New Session boot **803,113 / 803,364 B**; largest-JS paired comparison passed. No ceilings increased. Two English catalog registrars now use the existing merge owner, preserving lazy loading, namespace identities and text.
- Fresh independent reviews covered the inline recovery flow, catalog cleanup and native text-menu repair. title: fix: show automation activity while keeping routine checks quiet
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation running in the current conversation can leave the transcript, sidebar, and Task progress looking idle while user messages queue behind it.

## User Impact

User impact: running automations are named in the conversation’s existing activity view, remain visible through waits and reconnects, and disappear when their execution ends. Separate-session work does not make its creating conversation look busy. Quiet checks still leave the last meaningful conversation result, unread state, preview, and recency unchanged.

No configuration changes, migrations, scheduling changes, or new cancellation policy are introduced. Disabling a schedule is distinct from its current execution; Details reports a live run even when its schedule is disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Execution and content visibility now have separate responsibilities. Existing run registrations supply real automation identity to authorized session snapshots. The existing subagent activity renderer presents that identity without creating a child session, duplicate activity store, or independent cleanup mechanism. Conversation lifecycle and automation execution remain separate, including terminal-event reconciliation and Task progress. Desktop and mobile Details share execution-first status wording.

Requested by and developed with @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @Patrick-Erichsen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfee584d-05bd-4ee0-ab2b-f2f11bebcc92)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/506c90c1-aefc-45ef-993d-80901f522192)

## Evidence

- Reproduced through an isolated real Gateway and Chromium on base `3d6699cb9d95dbb326332d8442cae19ba3bc2e17`: a held automation model request reported `hasActiveRun: false` while Automation details showed Running. The regression failed at that exact assertion.
- Final real-Gateway + Chromium matrix passed (1 integration test, 53.37 s; matching built UI and runtime). It proves named activity and reload recovery, exact quiet bubbles/unread/preview/recency, meaningful results/errors, follow-up queue, saved Task progress, origin isolation, disabled forced execution, and one-shot retirement/deletion.
- Focused runtime suites: 80 tests passed; history/startup: 8 passed. UI consumer suites: 163 passed; final row/descriptor/terminal/roster suite: 138 passed. Final Task progress/transcript subset: 54 passed. These are separate, partly overlapping runs, not a summed test count.
- Core, UI, and UI-E2E test typechecks; scoped lint/format, controller guards, and test-line budget passed. Three unchanged Solid callback lint warnings remain.
- Independent source review findings were repaired. Fresh local independent review (P0–P2, full candidate) completed with no actionable findings. Lifecycle, snapshot-recency, and disabled-schedule defects have red/green regressions.
- Simplification: no fake sessions, second runtime owner, renderer copy, or cleanup manager. Existing activity projection and renderer serve both paths; shared status presentation removes competing desktop/mobile decisions. Against the base: production TypeScript +200 net lines; test TypeScript +601 net lines. The dedicated test allocation covers distinct producer, history, row, renderer, and browser boundaries. A 40-line signature helper was moved unchanged to its existing activity module.

### State and transition coverage

| Scenario | Proof boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Same-conversation execution; reconnect while the model is held | Real Gateway + browser |
| Quiet completion; meaningful results and provider failure | Real Gateway + browser, exact bubbles and saved display facts |
| Capacity wait; multiple execution contributions; agent/incarnation mismatch | Existing run-registry → session projection boundary |
| Tool and approval waits remain active | Real event producer → registry projection boundary; not an interactive approval UI claim |
| Disabled and auto-disabled schedules with admitted execution | Desktop/mobile production-renderer tests |
| Previous failed conversation outcome during execution and terminal events | Session snapshots + client row-reconciliation regressions |
| Real child subagent activity and saved Task progress | Existing production-component regression suites |
| Queue, isolated target, disabled forced one-shot and automatic deletion | Real Gateway + browser, including an already-due forced disabled occurrence |

**Limitations:** inference is a deterministic loopback OpenAI Responses fixture; the Gateway, tools, persistence, queue, browser, and session APIs are real. No external provider or Discord/Slack transport was exercised. Approval UI interaction, explicit stop/abort, self-removal/rename during execution, and mixed background-process/subagent concurrency were not all exercised in this browser matrix; those gaps are not claimed as end-to-end proof. Existing external disable/remove cancellation policy is unchanged. Force-running a future one-shot intentionally preserves its scheduled occurrence. Broad CI is pending.

title: fix(workboard): reject more than 12 labels instead of dropping extras silently
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Workboard silently drops labels after the 12th distinct one when a card is created or updated with more labels, while other list fields reject over-limit input.

## User Impact

Callers get an error instead of a card with missing labels. **Breaking for callers that send more than 12 distinct labels and relied on truncation** (CLI scripts, agent tool calls, Control UI bulk "Add labels"). Duplicates and empty entries are still collapsed first. No stored data changes: stored cards cannot hold more than 12 labels.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns labels with the parents/skills caps; follows the open question in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172367. The shared normalizer throws after the first excess distinct entry instead of stopping silently, and the docs are updated with it. No new policy owner, configuration, schema, or migration is introduced.

## Evidence

- Red on the unchanged normalizer: 3 failures (store rejection and gateway create/update), 139 passed; Vitest wall time 80.46 s (runner 90.38 s).
- Green: extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts, tools.test.ts, gateway.test.ts, and cli.test.ts: **149 tests passed across 4 files**, wall time **182.96 s**. Covers 12 distinct labels, 13-label rejection without creation, 30 entries collapsing to 12, failed update preserving old labels, and the 21-parent tool error. No sleeps or timers added.
- Targeted typecheck **passed** through the repository wrapper: node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .openclaw/tmp/tsconfig-workboard-labels.json. Temporary configuration extends the root tsconfig, sets noEmit and rootDir to the repository, and includes the changed implementation and three changed test files plus the repository's src/**/*.d.ts and ui/src/**/*.d.ts ambient declarations. Initial pnpm exec tsgo could not find the executable; the supported wrapper resolved it.
- oxfmt: **passed**, 5 files, 11 ms. Type-aware oxlint: **passed**, 4 TypeScript files, 5.02 s. git diff --check: **passed**.
- Caller/fixture audit: inspected 141 relevant tracked files, 59 static label lists, and their dynamic producers; no existing script, e2e, or fixture sends more than 12 distinct labels. Newly added negative tests intentionally exceed the cap. CLI create, workboard_create/specify/decompose, and RPC create/update/bulk/specify/decompose reach store-core createDirect/updateCard normalization; no label-write bypass found. Parent tool prevalidation retains the store's exact 20-entry error.
- **Control UI scope note:** normal card drafts still trim to 12 client-side. Bulk Add labels unions without a cap and now receives the server error near the limit. Source tracing confirms runWorkboardCardMutation records the server error, applySelection preserves it and keeps the dialog open, and WorkboardErrorToast displays it inside the dialog. UI code is unchanged; this is source inspection, not a live browser check.
- The extension runner unexpectedly expanded beyond the requested files. The expanded run was not green (runner wall time 611.84 s): unrelated Codex transport-orphan.test.ts and transport-owner-exit.test.ts failed with missing ps, child registration/containment errors. These are unrelated sandbox/process failures, not caused by this label-only change, and are intentionally not repaired here. The Workboard shard passed independently as recorded above.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Claim:** more than 12 distinct labels are rejected before a card is created or its labels are updated; duplicates and empty entries are collapsed first.
- **Surface/scenario:** Workboard CLI, agent tools, and card RPCs; compare 12 labels with 13, and preserve labels after a rejected update.
- **Command/environment:** fresh isolated state/config under /workspace/.openclaw/tmp/workboard-label-proof/base, using pnpm openclaw workboard list --json as the CLI preflight. The sandbox failed to spawn Node with EAGAIN before Workboard started; no shared Gateway was used or modified. Automated store/tool/RPC boundary tests provide the local behavior evidence above, not live CLI proof.
- **Result/limits:** Not verified live: CLI/Gateway run; live before/after proof follows from the author's test Gateway.

## Question for maintainers

This turns previously successful calls with more than 12 distinct labels into errors. Is rejecting preferred, or should truncation stay and return a warning instead?

title: fix(ui): restore saved appearance when the startup snapshot is unchanged
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A successful startup preference read can leave the wrong appearance on screen when the saved last-seen snapshot already matches the server. For example, the profile and snapshot contain Knot/Dark while the browser still displays Claw/System.

## User Impact

Restore saved appearance once each field's source is ready. Later unchanged reads do not repeatedly overwrite device-local edits. Marked local choices, pending edits, profile switches and pending resets keep their existing precedence.

## Implementation

Keep restoration in the existing preference owner. Track ready appearance fields and retain each profile's local values with its intent. A last-seen server snapshot remains a record of observation, not proof that the local mirror displays those values. No new preference reader, polling loop or configuration option is introduced.

## Compatibility

The documented adoption policy is profile-first when an older client has already consumed its local-intent marker: that storage cannot distinguish an intentional device-only choice from the stale mirror being repaired. An affected legacy user may need to reselect that local appearance once. Still-present legacy markers and newer explicit local intent are preserved.

Pending null resets use current Gateway defaults and retire acknowledged pending storage, rather than leaving old profile overrides behind.

## Maintainer Verification

The CI follow-up at `e83570080f340b13f3e53dddf8dea25d4ea83627` moves the existing SAFETY comment next to its assertion and registers the startup test consistently in the private-server and serial inventories. Runtime behavior is unchanged. All 15 inventory configuration tests, the targeted CI ownership guard, assertion-safety ratchet, lint and formatting pass. Fresh CI is pending.

On the integrated candidate, 121 preference-owner tests passed across 10 files. The existing reset test was strengthened by making the old local theme differ from the fallback; both immediate and delayed-default cases pass. App/E2E typechecks, lint, formatting and independent review of that test correction passed.

A temporary extension of the existing browser test exercised an isolated real Gateway through actual preference RPCs, with a fresh browser context for each case:

| Stored state | Startup and reload result |
| --- | --- |
| Stale mirror with matching snapshot | Knot/Dark restored |
| Fresh appearance storage | Knot/Dark restored |
| Released retained true markers | Rose/Light preserved and promoted to confirmed local values |
| Consumed-marker absence | Knot/Dark adopted under the documented policy |
| Pending null reset | Different Gateway fallback Dash/Dark applied; profile overrides and pending storage cleared |

The legacy cases also retained navigation width, pinned agents, external-link preference and thinking visibility. Each case checked the displayed theme and selected appearance control. No successful preference response was mocked.

This is compatibility coverage using serialized shapes verified against v2026.11.3 source, not execution of the packaged old app or its writers. The temporary matrix was not added to the permanent suite; its original E2E file was restored exactly. Native WebKit startup was not rerun. Current-head CI is checked separately before landing.

title: fix: improve scrolling in touch dashboard panels
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes dashboard content that cannot stay in view when scrolling an iPad side panel, and prevents expanded Auto widgets overlapping during drag or resize previews.

## User Impact

Gesture previews retain the spacing of expanded Auto widgets without raising the Fixed resize limit.

**Historical practical iPad follow-up PASS at c7decbdf on the reported device (November17): restored split, independent feeds and Auto→Fixed→Auto. This is not all-device certification or a new physical-device trial of the gesture repair.** Auto-height HTML widgets can grow taller on touch layouts so more content scrolls with the board, instead of inside an oversized iframe. The original singleton-page viewport fix is retained.

Existing fixed-height widgets keep their saved sizes. Switching a very tall Auto widget to Fixed can shrink it to the existing fixed-size limit; switching to a fine-pointer mouse layout can also restore compact sizing. The reporter explicitly accepted this tradeoff on November 12. Fixed widgets and documents beyond the larger bound can still scroll internally.

**The previous 6ddce47 iPad grid result remains FAIL / unchanged versus its baseline**, separately from its tall-page improvement. No merge or deployment is authorized. The requester authorized taking this PR out of draft on November17; exact-head CI/review are followed separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

One existing board owner shares the effective content-fit policy across grid allocation, exact card height and gesture previews. Coarse-pointer layouts reuse the existing 240-row document bound; fine-pointer layouts retain the ordinary 20-row bound. There is no new touch relay, schema, configuration, permission, or dependency change.

## Evidence

### November 17 gesture-preview repair — published and locally verified

The fresh review identified a P2 overlap when dragging or resizing among tall Auto widgets on touch layouts. The repair makes initial rendering and gesture construction share the same effective sizing policy, preserves expanded neighboring Auto spans through drag/resize previews, and retains the existing 20-row Fixed resize target limit. **Published repair head:** [`417b7f69d6944339ba3a6ef7752ca098918f34e3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/417b7f69d6944339ba3a6ef7752ca098918f34e3). The before comparison is c7decbdf.

- **Red/green:** the full Control UI with native Chromium CDP touch reproduced approximately 583 px of card overlap on c7decbdf, then passed with the repair. Both drag and resize initiation, pointer movement and cancellation retain separated neighbors and unchanged Auto heights; the resize visibly advances to five rows. A separate pure-grid regression protects expanded drag spans and the 20-row Fixed target bound.
- **Passed:** 11/11 fullscreen E2E (25.43 s invocation), 39/39 board-owner/grid tests (3.71 s), and 26/26 real-Chromium board browser tests (6.86 s); targeted UI-component and UI-E2E typechecks, lint, formatting, controller and test-line guards, and production UI build. CI seconds and new-head CI are not yet available. Build size-budget warnings remain advisory; no bundle baseline was raised.
- **Scope and simplification:** one effective content-fit decision now serves rendering and gestures; no duplicate policy, new manager, cache, configuration, or dependency. This follow-up adds 17 net production lines and 90 net regression-test lines, with a separate 90-line allocation. The full-app check covers event/renderer wiring and geometry; the grid check independently guards resize-limit semantics.

title: fix: Luna utility completions fail through Codex
body:
Closes #196617

Regression introduced by #177227. Related: #196344.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Luna utility tasks fail through Codex because internal sampling defaults are forwarded to routes that do not support them, affecting Activity recaps, session assessments, and progress narration.

## User Impact

Utility completions can retain their selected ChatGPT subscription or API-key route instead of failing or relying on another model. No configuration changes, credential substitutions, or billing-route changes are introduced.

Internal utility sampling and output-budget defaults are advisory on subscription routes. Explicit caller token caps retain required-limit behavior unless the caller explicitly opts into advisory mode. API-key output limits remain intact.

**Draft proof gaps:** live Gateway/Luna verification and the complete SDK-wide API comparison remain unverified; details below. No running Gateway was changed or restarted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex now reuses the normal OpenAI transport's temperature-capability policy, honoring catalog overrides rather than maintaining another model-name rule. The shared utility-completion owner marks internal defaults as preferred, and the existing Codex completion owner omits them for native ChatGPT subscription and token-sharing routes. Explicit isolated requests remain strict by default.

This covers the shared utility path rather than removing temperature separately from each caller. It overlaps the narrower token-sharing advisory-mode proposal in #196344 and adds API-key model-capability filtering plus legacy subscription coverage.

Simplification: one existing temperature policy, one utility-intent owner, no new configuration or state. Production delta is +25 lines; +57 test lines extend existing wire, native-process, account-ownership, and budget-propagation suites, with a matching test-line allocation.

## Evidence

- Published head: [0a6c6d7c1bb111b76fe87925265899df21ac2273](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0a6c6d7c1bb111b76fe87925265899df21ac2273). Its Git tree (5d75b68281a9fc9b300fe2ce1187152398e3fc72) exactly matches tested local candidate 9b92b12d9d16941e27a20119aa75439d6ab49046, based on c6fc5bd784b5bc1c8b94a069247796551eea3b7f.
- **Red/green regressions:** original code sends unsupported temperature in the actual native request, rejects advisory token-sharing defaults, and unnecessarily requires an inference relay for subscription defaults. The repair passes these regressions while retaining explicit-cap and account/endpoint checks.
- **Real pinned Codex 0.164.0 process:** the native integration test captures one serialized Luna request with its 240-token cap and without temperature, then receives the synthetic provider answer. Provider responses and credentials are synthetic; this is not live Luna entitlement or inference proof.
- **129 tests passed across 12 files / 7 Vitest shards**, including affected utility consumers and prompt-prefix stability. Final local wrapper wall time: 174.80 seconds. CI duration is not yet available.
- Core and extension production typechecks, affected core-test and extension-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, SDK export synchronization check, documentation MDX checks, whitespace, line-cap, and assertion-safety checks passed.
- Fresh independent Auto Review through the OpenClaw engine (P0–P2), with relevant unchanged owner/transport context, found no actionable defects in the final source delta. The reviewer did not independently execute tests.
- Personally inspected the pinned native [Responses request contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9/codex-rs/codex-api/src/common.rs); native requests do not own these sampling fields.
- **Incomplete:** no task-scoped API key or ChatGPT subscription credential is available for a real Gateway/Luna run. The SDK-wide API-diff check first failed to allocate its install thread pool; a CPU-bounded retry completed dependency setup but timed out during baseline declaration rendering. Its processes and temporary worktrees were reconciled and cleaned up. Neither check is claimed passing.

title: fix: scheduled chat updates lose images and clutter the thread

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: scheduled updates in a worktree-backed chat can lose screenshots, while fallback notices and tool-only continuations clutter the thread. CI follow-up also repairs Read aloud holding a chat-context change until playback ends.

## User Impact

Scheduled screenshots use the selected workspace and existing permissions. Fallback details remain expandable, and completed tool-only runs retain every operation without an empty assistant footer, in both plain and bubble views. Changing Gateway context can stop old Read aloud playback immediately. No configuration changes or migration are required; sibling workspaces remain inaccessible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Background delivery reuses the normal-reply media authority. Activity classification now preserves supplied complete frame content rather than replacing it with representative-group messages. Read aloud reflects its existing playback lifecycle instead of holding an optimistic UI action open for the full audio lifetime. No new state owner, cache, or retry mechanism is introduced.

## Evidence

- Media regression: both selected-workspace cases failed on base, then passed. Real cron delivery, persisted display content, attachment ownership/download, and sibling/default-workspace denial are covered. 23 consumer tests passed; wrapper 104.59s, changed cron file 39.27s including collection/teardown.
- Final focused history/frame/speech run: 92 tests passed in 2.36s (3.34s wrapper). The two complete-frame regression cases failed before the fix and pass in plain and bubble modes. Five built-UI Chromium scenarios pass in 17.54s including build, expanding the later tool result and preserving event/keyboard/narrow-layout behavior.
- [Original visual comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196602#issuecomment-6764900467) and [complete-frame review correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196602#issuecomment-6765630711) contain inspected before/after captures. The latter uses the real native frame component; the full-app fixture supplements it rather than claiming to reproduce the renderer defect.
- CI [42798704360](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42798704360) exposed cold-mount test readiness and a pre-existing speech/context-retirement dependency cycle. The strengthened native regression fails on base `d553516036b6a44707c51f86a7c3922e2dd52b3c`; manually ending audio unblocks it. The production owner fix passes without that workaround. Speech-owner suites: 20 tests in 1.79s; no assertions removed.
- UI/cron typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, controller guard, test-line allocation and diff checks pass. Existing Solid warnings remain unchanged.
- Full-context local autoreview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) found no actionable defects in the original candidate, speech repair, and final frame-classification correction. [ClawSweeper’s P2 finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196602#issuecomment-6765294848) was reproduced and addressed through the existing classifier, with both callers migrated and expanded regressions. - No live deployment, provider speech call, or resend of the original failed screenshot was performed. Media/native-speech tests use isolated production boundaries; browser fixtures use synthetic Gateway data.

title: fix(gateway): requests go unanswered when a teammate is copied
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new chat request receives no agent reply when a teammate is copied with an incidental mention such as `Please make poster previews. cc @Bob`.

## User Impact

Requests with copied teammates now run the agent and still notify those teammates. Messages beginning with a selected person remain human-only unless the agent is also named. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The human-addressing classifier treated every selected person as the addressee, even when the mention followed an agent request. Require the selected person to lead the message before suppressing the agent. Notification authorization, delivery, transcript persistence, and explicit agent-name overrides keep their existing owners.

This deliberately uses a simple positional rule rather than guessing intent from prose: greetings or other text before a person mention keep the agent turn.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through authenticated `chat.send` on an isolated real Gateway with a fixture model: the first copied-mention request terminated without starting the agent. Three focused incidental-mention cases also failed on the base.
- Final frozen snapshot: **8/8 focused tests passed**, including authenticated Gateway notification delivery, first-turn execution, direct-human no-interrupt behavior, and explicit agent-name override. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat-human-mentions.test.ts src/gateway/server.mentions-committed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; wall time 77.31s including cold worker compilation; Gateway test time 31.48s, unit test time 31ms. CI timing pending.
- Core TypeScript, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, documentation links, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) covered the final local change against base `421fa7fcd556d4d8f0c92dcdcc046dedeb9e086c`: no actionable findings. Reviewer did not execute tests or inspect unchanged dispatch code; the Gateway proof covers that composition. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the last Settings controls cannot be clicked when a failed save card covers them, even after scrolling to the end. ## User Impact Users can keep working in Settings without retrying or discarding an unrelated failed save first. Failed Settings feedback occupies it; Saving/Saved still overlay content without moving fields. The correction removes competing grid definitions from lazy Settings CSS, retires superseded mobile/floating declarations, and drops an unnecessary positioned wrapper. No page-specific padding, measurement state, or extra notice/control. Requested by @vincentkoc. ## Work sessions Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public. - [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a6ad0e49-a833-471e-a888-306441a32cda) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/1e5047c6-e820-4b7a-a6e9-4ef68ed6367c) ## Evidence - Exact built-UI flow: 390×844 Dreams → Turn off → rejected mocked config.patch → Cancel → maximum scroll. The base click hits the failure title; the fixed click expands the wiki while the error remains. The committed regression is red on base and green with the correction, including a 390×500 viewport, failed Retry, and independently scrollable long reason. - Before main integration, eleven actual app scenarios had byte-identical before/after screenshots and equal measured geometry without a failure: desktop/phone Chat, phone New Session, desktop/tablet/phone Settings, native-framed Chat/Settings, embedded Chat/Settings, and expanded board. The extra track was 0px; embedded roots retained their separate two-row grid. This is retained proof of the original correction, not a fresh all-surface comparison against integrated main. - Original owner correction: 19 focused E2Es passed across Settings recovery, config saves, split/expanded-board focus, and Custodian/onboarding headers. After removing the positioned status wrapper, all 3 affected status tests passed again (32.00s including build; new regression 1.91s). - Production remains net **4 fewer lines** versus the integrated main base. No new state/observer/manager. The exact test allocation remains **195 lines**: 184 for Settings reachability and 11 for Logs; the shared scalar is unchanged. - Independent P0–P2 autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol): original shell candidate against 0b911429, Logs delta against 0a2841b, and fresh complete integrated candidate against 5ac21026, all scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The integration review included complete affected owners and main's overlapping CSS/indicator changes; the reviewed source snapshot was preserved byte-for-byte in 9ad1a743. - Native framing is Chromium simulation with canonical flags/classes and 52px inset, not physical macOS/WebKit. No live Gateway, config, or provider writes. No prior-head CI is claimed as current-head proof. ### Main integration for the named prepared-row failure Head **9ad1a74397649424d51e8144c0cb799833b29879** merges verified main **5ac21026addd14fdc5f7df6e0de0d5b1d0c77924** into prior head **25af9860421e8a1320a2dae7edc746fe1cffbae7**. The reason is the prepared-row 26→31 failure in [run 42800618013, job 129777866045](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42800618013/job/129777866045), not a CI rerun for green. The canonical readiness repair [a29d52d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a29d52d73bebf14d113b7ec37e47ee3d83c2379e) arrived through merged #196564 (`71c83b7`). It waits for the real optional prewarmer before the measured work boundary, preserving the strict no-extra-render assertion. The integrated test is byte-identical to main (`4ea7d1e03ef2d76dbac39e95fbe0d771a8d618a4`); no duplicate repair was authored. The merge was conflict-free. Main's phone gutter owner and selector fix are preserved. Main's deferred-save presentation is adopted unchanged and uses the same failure-card layout. Focused integrated checks: - Prepared-row file: **30 passed**, 7.25s. - Sessions Chromium file: **3 passed**, 1.60s. Existing strict-read warnings retained; this is not WebKit proof. - Settings reachability plus current config-recovery E2Es: **6 passed**, 26.75s, including deferred application, partial-publication recovery, maximum-scroll wiki click, short viewport, long reason, and failed Retry. - UI types, seven-file format check, three-file CSS lint, and diff check passed. Unchanged Logs proof is reused. No CI rerun or force push. ### Investigated WebKit failure remains unexplained At prior head 25af986, [run 42800618013, job 129777865955](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42800618013/job/129777865955) failed the Sessions 1280px test at `view.invalidation.browser.test.tsx:147`: expected `[scrollTop, scrollHeight] = [4089, 4763]`, received `[4519, 4763]`. This is the two-frame stability guard **before `draft.focus()`**. The 430px movement matches the viewport shrinking from 630px to 200px, but why it failed to settle is unproven. Seven determining source/test/style files were unchanged from the original PR base; the bare Sessions fixture does not contain this PR's changed shell selectors. That is source binding, not a reproduced inherited-only exception. Local WebKit executed zero tests because the configured egress proxy refused task-owned loopback traffic. No bypass was attempted. The supported remote allocation queued and was stopped; [run 42803465910](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42803465910) was confirmed cancelled. Original failure, transport, and cancellation receipts are retained. A passing replay alone does not explain or repair this original failure. **Current-head CI confirmation:** at `9ad1a74397649424d51e8144c0cb799833b29879`, the verified check rollup has **48 passed / 48 neutral**, with no failures or pending checks. The complete [run 42808883340, job 129805679133 log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42808883340/job/129805679133) records all three actual Sessions WebKit cases passing: native undo **399ms**, 1280px focus/details/page selection **1867ms**, and the 390px case **1373ms**. This establishes current-head WebKit execution and passing results; it does **not** establish the cause or a fix for the prior 25af986 failure. ### CI repair: Logs Auto-follow At 0a2841b, [run 42794812790, job 129758053681](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42794812790/job/129758053681) failed `logs-scroll.e2e.test.ts:135`: the newest row was reachable, but Auto-follow remained false. Native offsets can precede/coalesce that event while an incoming batch renders. The return gesture could then reach the tail without re-enabling following. The repair records the gesture's starting position using existing intent state, preserving manual off-at-tail behavior without changing timers. - The 11-line owner regression is red before and green after. The unchanged failing Chromium E2E passed (8.813s test; 27.93s invocation). Local repair proof targets Chromium; fresh CI owns WebKit. Types/format passed; lint succeeded with four unchanged warnings outside the repair. ### Matched canonical build cost Same-host builds of integrated main and the reviewed candidate preserve both CSS ceilings: | Metric | Main 5ac21026 | Integrated candidate | Delta | Fixed ceiling | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | All CSS raw bytes | 1,712,772 | 1,712,764 | -8 | 1,712,885 | | All CSS normalized gzip bytes | 328,835 | 328,840 | +5 | 328,859 | | New Session boot normalized JS gzip bytes | 803,532 | 803,532 | 0 | 803,364 | CSS headroom is **121 raw bytes / 19 gzip bytes**. No budgets or baselines were raised, and main's other savings are not attributed to this patch. The earlier original-base comparison was -8 raw / +2 gzip; the integrated compression context measures -8 / +5. **Remaining build limit:** New Session boot JS is **168 bytes over its fixed ceiling on both matched main and candidate builds**, with zero growth from this PR. Canonical builds completed in report-only mode; this is not an all-budgets-green claim. ### Visual evidence The same four inspected, uploaded, rendered, and decoded assets are retained. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing elapsed turn time in the assistant message timestamp tooltip, including completed replies without tool calls.

## User Impact

Users can inspect a completed reply's duration as **Worked for {duration}** alongside its existing timestamp and usage metadata. The existing timing projection now serves both completed-work summaries and reply metadata. Matching terminal lifecycle runtime takes precedence. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow archive confirmation for sessions with many hidden worker sessions and incorrect archive counts when a live control relationship points to a conversation nested elsewhere.

## User Impact

Archive confirmation no longer queries every leaf session, and “Archive all” targets the same eligible persistent conversation tree shown in the sidebar. Existing Undo, active-work warnings, paging, and mutation guards remain unchanged. No migration or configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh Gateway rows already carry their complete visible child keys. Reuse those facts to avoid empty child-list requests, and honor child-side navigation ancestry instead of treating live control ownership as sidebar placement. This adds no cache, new state owner, or protocol surface.

## Evidence

- Four production-bundle Chromium archive scenarios pass, including two persistent children, 22 hidden worker leaves, and a foreign-controlled conversation: one child-list read and only the three intended archived keys. The count and leaf-read assertions fail on the original implementation.
- 99 focused tests across archive, batch mutation, child pagination, and Sessions-page outcomes pass (6.20s local wall time). UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Production UI and private-QA runtime builds complete. A real isolated Gateway created and reopened a persistent child, archived parent and child through the visible dialog, and confirmed both persisted archive states. No model turn was needed. Browser scenarios: 26.65s; real-Gateway proof: 50.66s including cold transform, approximately 11s in the test body.
- Independent Codex autoreview, P0–P2: original candidate against `baccc7e152916c7f4a48596b5cb544c12264ac54` and the CI-driven fixture correction against `38809142e8ac53adba6eb046c5434b7e2bcda1e2` both scoped-clean. Hosted ClawSweeper identified the same fixture omission on the old head; that finding is fixed, with original assertions preserved.
- [Current-head CI, run 42776660455](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42776660455): all substantive tests/checks, including the repaired Sessions-page cases, and `security-fast` passed. Security-sensitive and dependency review statuses also passed. CI remains red solely for the inherited test-line budget failure; it is not reported as green.
- The exact tested baseline `cdd7ee54ee8df226291bb97a1077731f40fbd273` independently reports 6,618,989 test lines against a 6,618,696 ceiling: 293 over. CI’s tested merge `7e6ed21333251fb17e0313f0704334f85e68e292` reports 6,619,038 against 6,618,745: the same 293 over.
