title: improve(ui): align settings sidebar and row controls on one rhythm
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Settings takeover mixed control heights, corner radii and left insets: the sidebar header stack stacked a 32px back row, a 40px agent picker, a 34px search field and 32px nav rows, with glyphs landing on 20/21/22px edges and radii split between 10px and 12.5px; the Agents toolbar put a 32px icon button beside 32.6px and 33px buttons with two radii; segmented controls and the emoji trigger in the identity row used radii that did not belong to the field family they sit in.

## User Impact

User impact: Settings controls now read as one system. The sidebar's back row, title, agent picker, search field, section labels and nav rows share a 32px height, one radius and a single 22px content edge; the Agents header actions are one 32px row with one radius; segmented controls and the emoji picker match the fields beside them. No behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vincent's rhythm feedback asked for consistent vertical/horizontal alignment and one control shape per surface. The change only moves existing geometry onto the owners that already define it: `--settings-control-height` (32px) for every control in the sidebar header stack and the Agents toolbar (the toolbar joins the existing "one control height inside settings clusters" rule), and `--field-radius` (10px, 12.5px on corner-shape engines, like `.btn`) for the sidebar back row, search field, segmented tracks and the Agents toolbar's icon button via its documented `--icon-button-radius` context token. Nested controls take concentric radii (field radius minus their inset): segmented items (3px) and the emoji trigger (3px, now 26px inside the 32px field instead of overhanging it). Skeletons were updated to the same heights so loading never shifts.

Deliberately unchanged, with reasons:

- The native macOS titlebar band keeps only the window controls and history chevrons; the "Back to app" row stays beneath it, like a macOS sidebar list under its toolbar. Its box already starts on the same 12px inset as the traffic lights, so nothing in the band and the row below disagrees.
- The Settings scroll container keeps its scroll offset when navigating between settings pages via the sidebar (channels scrolled 300px → Appearance opens at 300px, header hidden). That is a shell-level route-change behavior shared by every route, not a settings stylesheet issue; reported separately rather than patched from settings.

## Evidence

Measured on the mocked Control UI (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`), native-macOS chrome simulated by `installNativeWebChrome`, 1400×900, Chromium:

| Control | Before (h / radius / content x) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar back row | 32 / 10px / 21 | 32 / 12.5px / 22 |
| Sidebar title | — / — / 21 | — / — / 22 |
| Agent picker trigger | 40 / 12.5px / 21 | 32 / 12.5px / 22 |
| Search field | 34 / 10px / icon 22, text 44 | 32 / 12.5px / icon 22, text 46 (= nav labels) |
| Section label | — / — / 21 | — / — / 22 |
| Nav row | 32 / 12.5px / 22 | unchanged |
| Agents toolbar: refresh / New agent / more | 32 / 10px · 32.6 / 12.5px · 33 / 12.5px | 32 / 32 / 32, all 12.5px |
| Segmented track / item | 32 / 10px / 7px | 32 / 12.5px / 9.5px |
| Emoji trigger in identity field | 32×32 / 6px (overhangs 32px field) | 26×26 / 9.5px, 3px inset |

Same results at 820px and in web (non-native) mode; the stack keeps 38px touch heights under `pointer: coarse`.

Tests:

- New `ui/src/styles/settings-rhythm.browser.test.ts` (real CSS in Chromium): one height/radius/inset through the sidebar header stack, one height/radius in the Agents toolbar, concentric emoji trigger, and the Agents menu trigger at 390px. Red on the base (`[32, 40, 34, 32]`, `[32, 32.59, 33]`, `32 ≠ 26`, phone menu `[44, 44] ≠ [38, 38]` on the first reviewed head), green with the fix.
- `corner-shape.browser.test.ts`: `.settings-segmented` moves from the unscaled list to the `--field-radius` scale (10px → 12.5px with corner-shape), still circular.
- Passing: `form-controls.browser`, `sidebar-footer-layout.browser`, `settings-sidebar*.test`, `settings-ui.browser`, `agent-emoji-picker.browser`, `solid/hub-tabs.browser`, e2e `agent-select-layout`, `mobile-page-actions-header`, `native-desktop-titlebar`; `pnpm lint:ui:styles`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxfmt.
- Control UI performance comparison (`scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts` against the CI base): total CSS raw −29 B, gzip +29 B vs base, inside the 64 B variance the already-over-ceiling base allows; the first head's +167 B came from an agent-trigger height override that merely repeated the shared token and was removed.
- ClawSweeper's phone cascade finding (removing the `:root` 38px override exposed a later 44px literal in `agents.css`) is fixed by deleting that literal so the token owns the size at every width; covered by the 390px test above and `mobile-page-actions-header` e2e.
- Layout shift (PerformanceObserver, entering each settings route from /chat/main at 400/820/1280, native and web, mocked Gateway): no shift attributed to the changed sidebar or toolbar nodes; the only entries (content column on first settings entry at 820 web, channel rows arriving, titlebar history controls) are identical on the base.

title: improve(ui): align page toolbar controls on one height and treatment
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Page toolbars on Usage, Dashboards, Logs and Meetings mix control heights and treatments in one row: Usage pairs two bordered icon buttons with a ghost refresh, Dashboards sizes its header icons at 36px while every other page toolbar uses 32px, and the Logs and Meetings header buttons are 38px tall beside a 32px refresh button.

## User Impact

User impact: each page toolbar now reads as one row — one 32px control height (Logs and Meetings header buttons follow the 38px touch height like the fields beside them) and one ghost icon-button treatment for icon-only actions — matching Sessions, which already followed this pattern. ## Why This Change Was Made

title: fix(gateway): agent replies to Team chat messages addressed only to other people
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent replies to a Control UI message that only addresses other people (for example `@nonconsensus some of the stickers are cool`), even though the message was never for the agent.

## User Impact

User impact: in a Team chat, selecting people in a message now addresses those people. The message is posted to the transcript and the recipients get their Inbox entry, but the agent stays quiet: it does not reply, and it does not steer, interrupt, or queue behind a run that is already in progress. That run still lands its own reply. The agent reads the people-addressed message as context on its next turn. To involve the agent in the same message, name it in the text (its identity name, for example `Robo, put them on one sheet.`, or a configured `mentionPatterns` entry). A selected person's own token never counts as naming the agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.send` already knows which people a message addresses (the validated `mentions` spans) and the agent's group-chat mention patterns already define what "naming the agent" means. Request setup derives one `humanAddressed` decision from those owners. Admission skips the steer target and the interrupt capture for such a request, and dispatch returns before the agent turn; the existing reply finalization then commits the human message (which is what notifies the Inbox) and ends the run with no assistant message.

The committed row carries `__openclaw.humanAddressed`, and the prepared-assistant append check treats such rows as transparent, alongside context-free commands and Talk transcripts. Without that, a people-addressed message sent during a slow run would make the active run's next assistant or tool append fail with a transcript conflict. No schema, config, or protocol change; the marker lives in the existing message JSON like `contextFreeCommand`.

The dashboard read-admission object moved into `chat-send-dashboard-authority.ts` so `chat-send-agent-dispatch.ts` stays under the line-cap ratchet; behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New e2e case in `src/gateway/server.mentions-committed.test.ts` (real Gateway, two signed-in Control UI clients, mock model with a deferred first turn; it shares one fixture with the existing committed-mention case): while the agent's first turn is still running, `@Bob some of the stickers are cool` sent with `queueMode: "interrupt"` ends `final` with no assistant message, the model is not called for it, Bob's Inbox gets one entry, and the active run then completes with its assistant reply (no abort, no transcript conflict). Then `@Bob look. Robo, put them on one sheet.` runs the agent and its prompt carries the earlier people-addressed message. Red on `origin/main` (assistant replied to Bob's message); red again without the transparency marker and interrupt guard (active run ended `aborted`); green with the fix.
- `chat-human-mentions.test.ts` covers the decision (people only; agent named beside people; agent name inside a selected person's token). `transcript-append-parent.test.ts` covers the transparency rule (people-addressed row rebases; ordinary newer user turn still rejected).
- Siblings green: `server.mentions-committed`, `server.sessions.create.dispatch`, `chat-send-request`, `chat-send-pre-admission`, `chat-send-admission-authority`, `chat-send-admission.reads`, `chat-send-message-injection`, `chat-send-prestart-steer`, `chat-send-session-binding`, `chat-goal-created-authority.e2e`, `session-manager`, `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-parent`, `user-turn-transcript`, `user-turn-transcript.persistence`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm format`, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`, and oxlint on the changed files: green. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` reports only pre-existing findings in untouched files (`src/agents/plugin-model-catalog.ts` max-lines, Solid reactivity warnings).
- Test-line budget: the e2e case and the committed-mention case now share their Gateway fixture; the remaining +195 net test lines are recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/human-addressed-mentions.txt`. The real-Gateway run is what exposed the active-run abort and transcript-conflict regressions, which no unit layer reaches.
- Local ClawSweeper review on the first iteration flagged the interrupt-mode abort and the active-run transcript conflict; both are fixed and covered by the e2e case above. Two local ClawSweeper attempts on the final range crashed in Codex (exit 101) before producing a report; local autoreview (P0 threshold) on the final range found no actionable findings.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/multi-user.md` (Mentioning people) and `docs/web/webchat.md` (Human mention delivery) describe the rule.

Accepted edge: an agent with no identity name and no configured `mentionPatterns` cannot be named in text, so every people-addressed message in that agent's chats stays with the people.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: typing `/loop`, `/goal`, or another command in front of a pasted prompt can hide built-in completions or consume the first word of the prompt when completing.

Reported by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a13a4bd1-b444-490f-870f-005432b2c10c)

## User Impact

The leading command remains discoverable and completes in place without sending or losing the pasted text. Selecting `/goal` opens Goal mode with that text as its objective. Commands inside prose retain their inline behavior, including completing a colon-terminated skill name with the caret inside its name. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A leading slash token was misclassified as inline whenever text followed it. The existing parser now distinguishes leading commands from inline invocations by their preceding text. Selection replaces only the token; the existing Goal owner receives the objective. The caret-boundary check reuses command relevance ranking and ignores the optional terminal colon when recognizing a complete token.

The simplify pass retained the existing owners and removed a duplicate prefix matcher. Small production growth is needed for token-boundary and draft-preservation behavior; no state store or dispatch authority was added.

## Evidence

- Original regressions were red on base `0ef603bec0c5cc585170378524bd5be30b86b9df` and green with the fix: leading command discovery with dispatch admission open/closed, first-word preservation, and Goal objective preservation.
- Built Control UI / Chromium browser flow with mocked Gateway transport: paste → Ctrl+Home → `/loo` → Enter preserves `/loop Apply…` without `chat.send`; `/goa` opens Goal mode with the objective. Existing [inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196123#issuecomment-6745711440) remain applicable.
- Addressed the hosted P2 finding: edit `Please use /wether:` into `Please use /wea|ther:`, then complete `/weather`. The added browser regression produced `Please use $weather ther:` on the prior published source and `Please use $weather ` after repair. Both browser scenarios now pass: 1.525 seconds test time / 13.58 seconds wall time including the production UI build.
- Repaired candidate: 61 focused unit tests pass across `commands.test.ts`, `chat-composer-suggestions.test.ts`, and `chat-composer-menu.test.tsx` (5.60 seconds wall time). UI typecheck, targeted oxlint/oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The failing `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` job was the test-line budget, not a product test. A separate allocation grants exactly 200 net test LF lines for the dispatch-admission, leading-command/Goal draft-preservation, and colon-token browser regressions. Shared scalar unchanged; the local ratchet passes with zero spare allowance. These tests cover distinct parser/admission and real browser-editing boundaries.
- Fresh local autoreview (Codex, local snapshot against base `0ef603bec0c5cc585170378524bd5be30b86b9df`, P0/P1): scoped-clean. The hosted P2 finding was separately reproduced and fixed, not waived.
- Prior published head `266f24e5101513fa03762a32c83d7f46940f2a57` passed the UI, browser, type/lint, security, and performance checks; current-head CI must complete before landing. Prior CI is not current-head evidence.

- Follow-up gate repair: integrated exact CI base `568d89f3a4e82d13ecca4ed602c46a04bda322f0` to reproduce the failing bundle gate, removed the redundant draft-tail helper/read and combined the common replacement branch. The same-base performance check passes: chat boot 1,298,743 → 1,298,759 gzip bytes (+16); New Session 802,745 → 802,756 (+11); startup/CSS unchanged. No performance ceiling raised.
- After simplification: 192 unit tests pass (9.01 seconds wall), both built-browser scenarios pass (14.06 seconds wall), UI typecheck and targeted lint/format pass. Fresh local autoreview of the simplification through P2 is scoped-clean.

title: improve(ui): tile and sort session files in the Files panel
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Files panel's **Session files** group showed every generated image and attachment as a flat text list, with untitled images all reading "Image", and offered no way to see thumbnails or change the order.

## User Impact

User impact: in the Files panel, Session files can now be shown as a grid of tiles (image previews, large file icons) or the existing list, and sorted by **Default**, **Date**, **Name**, or **Type** from a control in the Files toolbar. The choice is remembered per browser for every session. Untitled images show their picture instead of a generic caption. List view and the project tree are unchanged by default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session-written files, artifacts, and transcript attachments were rendered by two separate lists inside one group, so they could not be ordered together. They now feed one ordered list owned by the Files panel, and the existing admitted image resource exposes its preview URL so tiles reuse the same bytes and viewer as transcript bubbles. Tiles are column-direction rows that reuse the row, filename, and skeleton styles; the view/sort control reuses the toolbar's rail button. The display preference follows the dashboards gallery pattern (`UiSettings.sessionFilesDisplay`, defaults not stored; unknown or retired values fall back to the defaults, so existing stored settings keep loading).

**Date** uses each file's Gateway-reported modification time and each attachment's message timestamp; artifacts carry neither, so they follow dated entries in default order. Default keeps the Gateway's existing file order followed by attachments in transcript order.

title: chore(ci): refresh mature Rust cache for native bindings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The new native-binding CI workflow still uses Rust Cache 2.9.2 and is not covered by the other pending action-update PRs.

## User Impact

No application runtime change. Native-binding CI adopts Rust Cache 2.9.3 while retaining its existing cache inputs, Rust toolchain, build matrix, permissions, and checks. Linux, Android, and Apple consumer builds and ready-PR CI have passed. Native preparation remains blocked before landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The November 9 dependency audit uses the fixed audit instant 2026-11-09T16:04:37.851Z and inclusive seven-day cutoff 2026-11-02T16:04:37.851Z. Rust Cache 2.9.3 was published October 20 at 13:47:43Z. Its dereferenced release commit is 12 commits ahead of the existing pin, with no reverse ancestry.

title: fix: visitor inventories stop at output limits

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes visitor inventories silently stopping when the recorded grants and unmanaged policy targets exceed the list tool's row or text output limits.

## User Impact

Administrators and designated owners can inspect the complete visitor inventory without increasing the invitation cap or using an unsupported data-access path. Existing `{}` calls still return the first page; follow `nextCursor` until it is `null` to finish.

Authorization and disclosed row fields are unchanged. Pages read current policy, identity, access, metadata, and seat observations rather than a frozen snapshot. If the ordered target inventory changes, restart without a cursor instead of silently skipping shifted rows. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add optional `cursor` and `limit` inputs and a machine-readable `nextCursor`. Each page stays within `maxVisitors` and the 12,000-character text budget, while counts and drift describe the whole inventory and `omitted` counts rows remaining after that page.

The active visitor-access service retains serialization, lifetime, and owner authorization. One plugin-local list projection replaces the inline renderer; it adds no cached roster, new authority source, or configuration option. An oversized individual row produces an explicit metadata-inspection error rather than an empty continuation loop.

title: fix(doctor): restore cold transcripts before session repair for renamed agents

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` blocks upgrades when a renamed agent's store contains cold transcripts keyed with the old agent ID and Gateway history cannot restore them.

## User Impact

Doctor can complete canonical session repair while preserving those transcripts, without a manual restore. Missing or damaged archives still stop the affected repair to protect history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical generation preparation now restores affected cold generations through the existing archive owner before copying or archiving history. Restoration uses the physical store owner, runs under Doctor's offline maintenance custody, and retains the existing size/SHA-256 verification and transactional restore semantics. Gateway history ownership checks are unchanged.

This fix belongs in the candidate Doctor; it requires no installed-updater change, config alias, CLI/RPC addition, or schema change. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android onboarding’s “Additional features” disclosure does not expose whether its optional permission rows are expanded or collapsed to accessibility services.

title: fix(android): preserve existing Wear realtime transcript on blank transcript updates
body:
Fixes #195990

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Wear realtime Talk loses earlier transcript text or spaces when the relay sends incremental transcript updates.

## User Impact

User impact: watch transcripts retain the words and spaces received during a turn, while authoritative snapshots and final transcripts can correct them. Whitespace-only snapshots and finals replace retained text; empty payloads remain ignored. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Append nonfinal, nonsnapshot relay deltas to the existing entry for each role; replace that text on a snapshot or final transcript. Empty strings remain ignored; whitespace-only deltas are preserved. This does not ignore whitespace-only snapshots or finals: those are replacements.

Keep the existing reply-retention budget and prevent later deltas from advertising a truncated reply as complete. An authoritative replacement can restore complete text. The issue's proposed `onTranscript`/blank-guard description does not match the pinned source; this preserves the supplied commit's actual delta-accumulation fix.

title: fix(android): switch shell to Settings tab when opening Gateway settings
body:
Fixes #195988

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Back returning to Overview instead of the originating screen after opening Gateway settings from the Android sidebar.

## User Impact

Users can open Gateway settings from the sidebar footer or Manage Gateways and return to the screen they came from. Plain Settings-tab navigation still opens Settings Home and clears the previous detail origin. No migration or configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Handle a requested settings detail through the existing shell navigation owner before any top-level tab selection can erase its return destination. Keep plain home-destination requests on the existing tab-selection path.

The issue’s initial Overview/command-palette description refers to an older navigation path. At the pinned base, those actions already use shell navigation directly; this source commit fixes the one-shot settings-request path and tests sidebar navigation from Providers & Models.

title: fix(android): preserve aggregate contact display name in contacts.search results
body:
Fixes #195966

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Android `contacts.search` returning a linked raw contact's name instead of the aggregate contact name that matched the search.

## User Impact

Search results retain the matched aggregate contact name, while contacts with an empty aggregate name keep the existing fallback. No permission changes, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The search already reads Android's aggregate display name, but loading the contact details can replace it with the first linked raw contact's structured name. Preserve the non-empty aggregate name in search results without changing contact creation or the remaining contact fields.

## Evidence

- [Contributor source and complete two-file diff](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/13b7418f8be7b8c139283ec62af44a4a2aecab25).

The contributor also supplied passing `pnpm native:i18n:verify` and physical Google Pixel 10 Pro XL verification.
- Regression coverage exercises `ContactsHandler.handleContactsSearch` through the system data source with a fixture content provider: conflicting linked names, unchanged single-contact names, and empty aggregate-name fallback.
- Preparation on main `390d069b8a3777c7a6811f2e10b8115c166cd832`: exact source patch applies, both resulting files match the pinned source, stable patch IDs match, and `git diff --check` passes. Independent source review found no blocking correctness issues.

title: fix(android): respect allowed choices in notification replies
body:
Fixes #195949

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android notification replies could send arbitrary text to actions that accept only a fixed set of choices.

## User Impact

User impact: replies respect the receiving app's allowed input while still using a compatible later action or free-form input when available. If no action accepts the reply, OpenClaw returns `ACTION_UNAVAILABLE` without sending it. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate reply eligibility at the notification listener's send boundary, select the first compatible action, and populate only inputs that accept the reply text. Two regression tests cover restricted-choice rejection and acceptance, later compatible action selection, and mixed restricted/free-form inputs.

## Evidence

title: fix: explain MCP sign-in rejection for HTTPS loopback callbacks
body:
Closes #195958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unactionable MCP sign-in errors when a provider rejects a local HTTPS Gateway's loopback callback before consent.

## User Impact

Operators now get a specific explanation and safe recovery: keep Gateway TLS enabled, use an existing provider-compatible HTTPS Gateway address reachable from their browser, or use the supported offline CLI sign-in flow. CLI guidance applies only to configured operator servers and explicitly says to restart the Gateway even when login fails; plugin-declared connections retain plugin-specific recovery.

This does not make an incompatible HTTPS loopback callback acceptable to Executor. No silent HTTP downgrade, alternate listener, new origin setting, or redirect-policy relaxation is introduced.

**Draft hold:** required before/after UI screenshots remain unavailable. The sandbox Chromium setup stopped before rendering because system libraries (including libglib-2.0.so.0) are absent; the official dependency installer requires root, which is unavailable. This is a capture limitation, not a passing visual gate. No personal Gateway was modified or restarted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser-auth owner correctly retains the admitted Gateway origin. The resulting callback is passed explicitly to the MCP coordinator and becomes the provider's registration redirect. Installed SDK 2.4.0 already supplies application_type=native for loopback hosts, including HTTPS; Executor rejects that HTTPS/native combination. Forcing web is rejected too. Rewriting the scheme would not create a matching listener, and a separate loopback listener would break remote-browser delivery.

Keep metadata, callback routing, TLS, PKCE, state/issuer/identity binding and credential custody unchanged. At the existing Gateway registration-error boundary, recognize the typed SDK rejection's invalid_redirect_uri code and submitted HTTPS loopback callback, then select fixed recovery text. Never expose provider response bodies or descriptions.

Related but distinct: #181737 (SDK-owned application type, already implemented), #160243 (CLI registration retry), #175663 (separate public/UI origins).

## Evidence

- Started from current upstream main `0ab37d2048421fc9ea3906ec51c13a943032b6ef`, verified against origin/main at task start.
- **Real Executor registration, no account credentials or consent:** HTTPS 127.0.0.1/native and HTTPS localhost/native returned HTTP 400 invalid_redirect_uri. HTTPS 127.0.0.1/web was also rejected. HTTP 127.0.0.1:8989/native and a synthetic remote HTTPS/web callback were accepted for registration. Remote callback reachability and authorization completion were not tested.
- **Real isolated TLS Gateway + Executor:** authenticated WSS `mcp.authLogin` / `wizard.next` reproduced the old generic error before the patch and the new actionable explanation afterward, before any consent URL. Fresh synthetic state, certificate, device identity and Gateway token; no personal state. This exercises the Control UI RPC path, not an actual browser click.
- **Simulated provider, real Gateway/SDK/store:** 45 login integration tests pass, including HTTPS loopback IPv4/IPv6/localhost, HTTP loopback, exact explicit remote callbacks, SDK native/web metadata, no callback retry/rewrite, no token exchange on rejection, malformed/untrusted errors and existing authority/credential controls. The three HTTPS loopback regressions failed on the unpatched owner for the expected generic-copy mismatch.
- Existing sibling proof: 13 MCP OAuth coordinator tests and 29 browser callback/origin tests passed. Final TLS/live + Gateway run: 46 tests / 2 files passed.
- Targeted Gateway-server typecheck passed; type-aware lint passed with zero warnings/errors; touched-file formatting, one-file MDX sanity and `git diff --check` passed. Configured P0 Auto Review: scoped-clean; this was static review, not execution.
- No live Executor consent, token exchange, credential persistence or six-tool discovery was attempted. The reporter's successful CLI authorization/tool discovery remains reporter evidence. Screenshots are blocked as described above; broad PR CI is not claimed green.

Simplification: retain the existing error owner and CLI instruction builder; consolidate registration/network controls into one test-support table rather than duplicate OAuth policy or create a new flow.

title: fix(test): prevent missing worker compiler cancellation receipts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent missing cancellation receipts in the worker artifact CI checks.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. The compiler cancellation fixture now publishes readiness only after it can handle cancellation. All lifecycle, process cleanup, retained-input, exit-status, and receipt assertions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

In [scheduled job 129081576503](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42593676244/job/129081576503), `owns the real compiler lifetime: cancel while compiling` failed reading `cancel-read`. Its compiler had published `compiling` before installing the SIGTERM handler that writes that receipt, allowing the parent to cancel before setup finished.

Publish both gate receipts after installing the signal handler and timer. The shared gate owns readiness; no retries, timeout changes, skips, or assertion changes are needed. This differs from [#195823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195823): the failing driver already runs on Node, so changing the shared runtime-selection helper would not repair this ordering defect. Production code and net test-line growth are both zero.

## Evidence

- The same case and all 28 file cases passed in [run 42579470599](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42579470599/job/129035051634) and [run 42574663068](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42574663068/job/129019963109). The reported run failed this case alone.
- A controlled probe extracts the actual gate and cancellation branch and sends a real SIGTERM at the readiness write. On CI's Node 24.22.1: base exits by SIGTERM without `cancel-read`; fixed source exits 0 and records `compiler input`. The pair completed in under 0.1 seconds; no compiler, download, or retry was used. This proves readiness ordering, not the complete compiler-owner lifecycle.
- Named-file attempt through `scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/vitest-worker-artifacts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed before collection because the existing dependency tree lacks `@solidjs/vite-plugin` (shard startup: 746 ms). No full-file passing result or changed-file wall-time measurement is claimed. Prior successful CI file times were 135.625 s and 150.802 s; this patch adds no cases or waiting.

Simplification retained one readiness owner and removed the two caller-side publications; the change is 4 added / 4 removed test lines.

No workflow dispatch, rerun, Testbox warmup, broad local suite, container, browser, staging, packaging, or merge was performed. Broad proof is left to normal PR CI.

title: fix(cron): catch missing account selection before enabling automations
body:
Related: #195802

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: enabling or editing an agent-turn automation could appear to succeed even though every scheduled run would stop with `Automation has no recorded inference account`.

## User Impact

**Before:** the job could be saved as enabled, fail on every run, and eventually be automatically disabled. Simply enabling it again could repeat the same failure.

**After:** when an edit would leave an enabled job without the stored account selection its runs require, OpenClaw rejects the edit immediately and names the model and account to select. Disabling the job is still allowed.

**Existing jobs:** installing this change alone is not a blanket repair of older automations. If a job reports the missing-account error, an authorized user can record the intended account with:

```sh
openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model <provider/model>@<profileId>
```

This also sets the job's model; re-enable the job afterward if it was disabled. The equivalent `openclaw cron edit` repair was [confirmed by a user on 2026.11.2 with an isolated Claude CLI automation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195890#issuecomment-6778141386). Existing Doctor adoption for eligible accounts is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Having a signed-in model account is not the same as recording which account a scheduled job is authorized to use. The account may be available to interactive chat while the job still lacks that authorization record; the error does not necessarily mean credentials are missing or expired.

**Why this helps:** it turns a misleading successful edit followed by repeated unattended failures into an immediate, actionable account-selection error. The runtime's safety check stays intact: this does not borrow another account, weaken ownership or revocation checks, or add a fallback.

The PR closes two gaps:

- **Editing an existing job:** use the existing account-capture logic to check the job's resulting state, including when an edit removes native runtime authority. An ordinary edit does not silently choose an account for the job.
- **Re-declaring an existing job:** when `cron.add` matches a job by `declarationKey` and that job has no recorded account, save the account already authorized by the declaring context—even when that is the only change. Existing account bindings are not replaced.

**Scope:** this prevents the supported edit/re-declaration paths from preserving this failure state; it does not fix every way a job can lack an account. Template-created jobs, bundled-plugin scheduling, provider-changing declarations and session-event error propagation are outside this patch. The original incident's creation path is still unestablished, so this is `Related`, not `Closes`.

## Evidence

- Regression tests cover account-only declaration persistence, inherited and Gmail-hook models, and refusal of unauthorized or replaced accounts.
- An isolated Gateway/CLI run demonstrated the refusal and explicit-account recovery; a separate 2026.11.2 upgrade run checked existing jobs and history.
- The current head passed the CI gates, and ClawSweeper's completed review lists no findings.

Live Codex execution is **not** claimed: Codex coverage uses a harness fixture. The live runtime proof used OpenClaw with a loopback provider.

**Upgrade from 2026.11.2 (latest stable at test time) → this branch.** The installer's 7-day package-age policy blocked `openclaw@2026.11.2` from npm, so the stable side was built from the `v2026.11.2` tag source (`b556fdf`). On stable: an unbound job and a declared job were created on a provider-config key, then a stored OpenAI key was added, then a job explicitly bound to it was created and both were run. The branch then ran the normal `doctor --fix` and Gateway. The tested checkout was labeled 2026.11.1, so branch commands used `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1`, as the repo's own upgrade harnesses do; database compatibility checks still apply.

title: fix(cron): scheduled runs refused for a missing account hide the cause and retry ten times
body:
Closes #195802
Related: #191637, #189953, #188946

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled run refused because its automation has no recorded inference account is reported only as "Session event execution failed", and a recurring job keeps retrying it until it is auto-disabled after ten failures.

## User Impact

User impact: automation history, run diagnostics and the failure alert now name the missing recorded account and how to record it, and a recurring job pauses after its first refused run with one alert instead of failing ten times. Chat alerts leave out the stored account; automation history keeps the exact refusal and command, and a webhook failure route still receives the raw last error as before. Gateway startup now also warns about unbound Codex-runtime jobs. Account authorization is unchanged: the guard still refuses these runs, and optional scheduled runs still post no chat failure text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Optional scheduled replies blank their chat failure text, so session-event settlement fell back to generic wording even though the reply operation still held the refusal as its failure cause. The turn owner now passes that recorded cause with its session-event terminal evidence, and settlement uses it when nothing else presented an error, for the run error and diagnostics (redacted through the existing error formatter and diagnostics normalizer).

The refusal is marked when it is created. Cron turns that mark into a permanent classification with a closed failure detail, for both session-event and isolated runs, so the existing failure-alert and auto-disable owners pause the job on the first refusal with fixed copy that names `openclaw doctor --fix` and the `openclaw automations edit` form without the account. Transient failures keep the existing retry ladder and ten-failure limit.

The startup diagnostic (now account-aware after #195905) no longer excludes the Codex runtime: like Doctor, it plans Codex auth through the harness and warns only when that plan would use a stored account. Native or credentialless Codex login and CLI backends that own their login stay quiet.

Accepted edge cases: the paused job records the existing `state.autoDisabled.reason: consecutive-failures` with `consecutiveErrors: 1` rather than adding a new persisted reason. The auto-disable notice now also shows the closed failure detail (such as a command's exit code) for other jobs that carry one.

<details>
<summary>Not included: failure alert "explicit channel required"</summary>

A job whose delivery session has no external last channel (for example a session-target job in a WebChat or internal orchestration session) and no `sourceConversation` resolves its failure alert to `channel: "last"`. `resolveDeliveryTarget` then falls back to `resolveMessageChannelSelection`, which fails with "Channel is required when multiple channels are configured …" when more than one channel is configured. The alert is recorded as not delivered and only reaches the passive in-app fallback queue. The job's own delivery route and session are already the inputs to that resolution, so there is no route to fall back to; choosing a destination (owner DM, Control UI attention, or refusing at creation) is a separate product decision that overlaps #189953 and #188946.

</details>

## Evidence

- New regression tests, red on `4a42d5bd` and green with this change:
  - `session-event-automation-result.test.ts`: a scheduled session-event run whose runner throws the refusal. Base outcome: `error: "Session event execution failed"`, no classification. Now: the refusal text, `errorClassification: permanent`, `failureNotificationDetail: inference-account-unrecorded`, a diagnostics summary with the cause, and no failure text in the transcript.
  - `timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts`: a recurring job is disabled on its first refusal (`consecutiveErrors: 1`) and sends one alert with the cause, `openclaw doctor --fix` and the enable command, without the stored account.
  - `isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts`: the isolated refusal is classified permanent with the closed detail.
  - `store.inference-warning.test.ts`: an unbound Codex-runtime job gets the startup warning; the existing Claude CLI and local-provider jobs still do not.
- Consumer suites passed (19 files, 352 tests): session-event handoff, config readmission, agent-runner session events, GitHub publish handoff, cron session run, failure alerts and persistence, timer, operator continuation, command timeout, cron CLI, Gateway cron session target and repair notifications.
- `tsgo` core and src test shards, oxlint on changed files, oxfmt check, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap, max-lines and test-lines ratchets against the PR base: pass. `session-event-handoff.ts` is unchanged.
- Test-line growth: the four regressions add 124 net test lines against current main, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/195879-scheduled-account-refusal.txt`. Each covers a separate owner boundary (session-event settlement, cron outcome policy, isolated runs, startup diagnostics).
- After the review fixes: the 7 affected session-event and agent-runner suites (120 tests) pass.
- After merging current main (conflict with #195905's startup diagnostic rewrite): the 8 affected cron and session-event suites (186 tests) pass, the Codex startup case fails on main's diagnostic and passes here, and `tsgo` core, oxlint, oxfmt and the line-cap, max-lines and test-lines ratchets pass against `3e4e201e`.
- Auto Review (branch mode, P0–P2): scoped-clean.

title: fix(tests): wait for local alias turns before exiting TUI
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a flaky built-artifact TUI canary that exits while a local alias response is still finishing post-turn maintenance.

Maintainer-authorized main-CI repair for [scheduled run 42579470599, build-artifacts job 129035049364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42579470599/job/129035049364).

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The chat and terminal alias checks still require a model request, the expected prompt and reply, and exit code zero within the existing four-second exit limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reply text is streamed before local post-turn maintenance settles. Wait for idle after that reply before submitting `/exit`, using the same output-offset helper as the local history tests. The offset excludes startup idle frames. Shutdown deliberately joins owned work, even after cancellation grace expires; this alias canary should finish its turn before testing normal exit.

## Evidence

- The failed test rendered `CHAT_ALIAS_RESPONSE`, then `streaming` and `finishing context`, before reporting `timed out waiting for PTY exit` (12.731 seconds for the test). The response assertions passed; process exit was the failed boundary.
- Earlier scheduled build-artifacts jobs [129019959502](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42574663068/job/129019959502) and [128980605575](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42562039354/job/128980605575) both passed. GitHub compare shows no TUI source changes between the most recent passing run and the failure: this is a missing completion synchronization, not an attributed new regression.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2), complete local snapshot against base `9a26486062c8a17cbd3f7cf2e7f038fd81935fef`: scoped clean, no findings. The reviewer verified the reply-scoped idle condition and preserved assertions; runtime effectiveness remains pending.
- `git diff --check` passed. Production delta: zero; test delta: three lines in the existing two-alias case, with no new test, baseline change, retry, skip, or timeout increase. Simplification retained only the completion wait.
- Local repository-configured direct oxlint could not load `eslint-plugin-solid` because this worktree has no dependency installation. A config-free invocation was unsupported by the installed CLI. No successful local lint/typecheck or PTY replay is claimed.
- PTY runtime proof and lint/types are delegated to this PR's CI. Production-host rules prohibit local TUI/SDK builds and staging; this lane also prohibits Testbox/Crabbox warmup and manual CI dispatch. No such action was taken.

title: fix(test): keep worker shutdown fixtures on Node
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent worker-shutdown CI failures when the synthetic wrapper tries to download pinned Bun before publishing readiness.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. The shutdown fixture stays on Node, matching its Node-only preload and child executables. Signal status, disposal, IPC, liveness, and process cleanup assertions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

In [scheduled job 129035056035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42579470599/job/129035056035), `direct wrapper joins disposal work before honoring SIGINT` hit its 20-second managed-child deadline during pinned Bun staging inside its isolated HOME. The later missing `verification-ready` receipt was a consequence of startup never reaching the shutdown exercise.

The fixture drops CI/runtime environment variables. Since [#172625](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172625) changed the default local runtime, this environment invokes Bun discovery. Explicitly select Node for these Node-specific wrapper fixtures. This removes the unrelated download without changing timeouts or adding retries. Net test-line growth: zero; production code unchanged.

## Evidence

- The same scheduled job succeeded in runs [42574663068](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42574663068/job/129019970134) and [42562039354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42562039354/job/128980612517). Classified as an intermittent fixture failure with a confirmed runtime-discovery cause.
- Offline differential probe extracted the actual fixture environment and called the production `resolveVitestTestCommand`. Before: one Bun staging request, intercepted before execution, and the no-staging assertion failed. After: zero staging requests and Node selected. No download occurred.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Independent autoreview: scoped-clean, P0–P2.
- Full named-file test could not reach collection because the shared dependency tree lacks `@solidjs/vite-plugin`; no passing full-file result or wall-time claim. CI's original 26-case file took 63.18 seconds including the failed 20-second startup. No cases or runtime cost are added.
- Focused lint is blocked by missing `eslint-plugin-solid`; touched-file typecheck is blocked by missing `tsrs`. The shared install was preserved. These checks and the complete shutdown file remain pending PR CI.

No workflow dispatch, rerun, Testbox warmup, broad local suite, staging, packaging, or merge was performed.

title: fix(model-catalog): refresh fails behind fake-IP proxies
body:
Fixes #152765

## What Problem This Solves

Remote model catalog downloads ignored the operator’s configured fetch policy. Failed near-expiry catalog adoption could also rearm short retries indefinitely, and failed worker preparation could retain its capture.

The follow-up security repair fixes a stale network grant: an operator could withdraw permission while DNS or redirect preparation was pending, yet the prepared request still reached HTTP.

## User Impact

Operators behind fake-IP proxies can use their existing fetch-policy opt-ins for catalog downloads. Defaults remain unchanged, explicit catalog mirrors retain their origin restriction, failed adoption returns to the normal cadence after three consecutive failures, and failed worker preparation releases its capture.

Catalog refresh now re-reads its applicable **current config** at the transport’s synchronous `beforeRequest` boundary, after preparation and before each HTTP hop. Changed network policy, refresh disablement, or a changed catalog URL blocks that prepared request with a retry message. Equivalent config replacement remains allowed. A policy expansion also retries rather than reusing transport prepared under a different grant; it does not permanently reject the newly allowed destination.

**Network-policy scope requiring maintainer/security review:** catalog downloads inherit the whole `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy`, including private-network and hostname allow/block settings, not only the RFC2544 flag. No new config key, migration, or policy owner is introduced. This PR does not claim to prove or eliminate the reported Gateway hangs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing guarded-fetch, config, scheduler, and worker-capture owners handle the fix. The security repair uses `createRuntimeConfigReader` to follow the owning runtime’s replacement config while preserving explicit scoped configs, and `isSameSsrFPolicy` for normalized policy comparison. It retains a detached preparation-policy snapshot and installs the same final check for default and explicit-mirror requests. The guard invokes it again after every redirect’s preparation, with no await between the check and HTTP initiation.

The isolated [contributor commit c0912ed8a680](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/c0912ed8a680b0b1ee8d738d3c1e6b978270f68d), from `fix/catalog-refresh-policy-and-retry`, was applied onto upstream main `37365600bf67cab28ef5e180c5dfbfb400d88f83`. Its source merge base is `c1b75daf79463773375988651395787efa3374ff`. No contributor-fork writes were made.

Security repair head **`597698b2ef3318e0988ef930aa5bdf3da61e0608`** is a plain fast-forward child of `45d4f9d4cce21163e04373590b1c6a59b6c8227d` on the same PR branch. Simplification replaced the policy-call-shape test, redundant mock-success test, and artificial throwing-getter test with a real HTTP-boundary regression; the bounded failed-adoption regression remains. Relative to the prior head: production +19/-1; test lines **219 → 184**; matching allocation reduced by 35; five files changed, +159/-175 overall. Relative to pinned main: production +70/-14; tests +184; routing +2; allocation record +2. No unrelated tests or shared scalar-ceiling increase.

## Evidence

### Current-policy withdrawal: inline, self-contained red/green trace

Verified candidate tree: `cb01a225f5c3b75e055eb1d669159904df740165`, now published as `597698b2ef3318e0988ef930aa5bdf3da61e0608`. Linux sandbox, Node, real `refreshRemoteModelCatalog`, real SSRF guard and Undici transport, real runtime-config owner, isolated SQLite state, and a real loopback HTTP listener. **Only external DNS lookup is controlled**, to pause preparation deterministically; the guard, fetch, config reader, and HTTP effect are not mocked.

Setup in `src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.authority.test.ts`:
1. Install current config with an explicit `http://127.0.0.1:<claimed-port>/catalog` mirror and `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames: ["127.0.0.1"]`.
2. Start forced refresh. Pause DNS before the first request; for the redirect case, serve one authorized `302 /redirect → /catalog` and pause the second lookup.
3. While paused, replace the owner’s current config using `setRuntimeConfigSnapshot`: replace the allowed-host policy with `blockedHostnames: ["127.0.0.1"]`. Controls replace config with an equivalent permission instead.
4. Resume DNS with `127.0.0.1`. Count actual listener requests to `/catalog`, separately from the earlier authorized redirect response.

Command (same committed test in both runs):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

**Red:** with only production `src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.ts` restored from `45d4f9d4cce21163e04373590b1c6a59b6c8227d`, the direct and redirect withdrawal assertions fail: `expected 1 to be +0`; **2 failed / 2 passed**. Both permitted controls pass. **Green:** restore that production file from repair head `597698b2ef3318e0988ef930aa5bdf3da61e0608`; **4/4 pass** (2.98 seconds Vitest, 38.34 seconds including cold worker preparation).

Observed withdrawal traces (same event sequence for direct and redirected target):

```text
policy grants 127.0.0.1
-> DNS preparation paused
-> current config replaced: permission withdrawn
-> DNS preparation resumed

old 45d4f9d4, direct:   result=unchanged; target HTTP effects=1; prior redirect HTTP effects=0
old 45d4f9d4, redirect: result=unchanged; target HTTP effects=1; prior redirect HTTP effects=1

new 597698b2, direct:   result=error; target HTTP effects=0; prior redirect HTTP effects=0
new 597698b2, redirect: result=error; target HTTP effects=0; prior redirect HTTP effects=1
error in both fixed withdrawal cases:
Error: Remote catalog network policy changed; retry with the current configuration.

Equivalent-permission replacement controls, both heads:
direct:   result=unchanged; target HTTP effects=1; prior redirect HTTP effects=0
redirect: result=unchanged; target HTTP effects=1; prior redirect HTTP effects=1
```

The fixed error is thrown by the new `beforeRequest` current-config check, not DNS cancellation or a mocked guard. Thus the withdrawn target has **zero HTTP effects**, including after redirect preparation; the already-authorized redirect response is intentionally counted separately. The unchanged status in controls reflects fixture catalog age, not a skipped request.

To reproduce the red side from the repair checkout without changing branches: save `src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.ts`, replace just that file with `git show 45d4f9d4cce21163e04373590b1c6a59b6c8227d:src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.ts`, run the command above, then restore the saved file and rerun for green. Keep the repair’s committed test/routing files in both runs.

### Available checks and review

- Focused refresh, bounded-retry, and runtime-config suites: **68 passing tests across four files** via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.test.ts src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.authority.test.ts src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.reliability.test.ts src/config/runtime-snapshot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The final typed authority fixture was then rerun separately for the red/green trace above; other code/test inputs were unchanged.
- Targeted oxlint: four touched TS/MJS files pass. Changed-test TypeScript graph passes via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mts --changed-paths-json '["src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.authority.test.ts","src/model-catalog/remote-refresh.reliability.test.ts"]'` (advisory pre-existing shard-size warnings only).
- Targeted formatting, staged `git diff --check`, mock-factory ratchet, and test-line ratchet pass. Test-line count **6,593,959 / 6,593,966**, preserving seven lines of slack while reducing the existing allocation.
- Fresh independent **bound Auto Review / OpenClaw engine**, local staged delta against `45d4f9d4cce21163e04373590b1c6a59b6c8227d`: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, all five changed paths covered, no findings. Reviewer assessed supplied source and proof; it did not independently execute tests. This is not security-owner approval.
- Historical prior-head checks: the original `45d4f9d4` candidate passed 99 tests across refresh, startup, and worker preparation/cleanup suites. That is prior-head evidence, not a new 99-test run.
- [Contributor-provided macOS/Node shipped-CLI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195792#issuecomment-6773422259) applies to **old head `45d4f9d4`**: benchmark opt-in success vs pinned main, forbidden-address/redirect rejection, and DNS cancellation. It is not Xcode proof or a rerun on this repair. The new withdrawal trace is inline above and needs no external asset download.

**Coverage gaps:** this repair proves the owning HTTP boundary, not a full Gateway deployment, live Mihomo setup, latest-stable upgrade retaining saved settings/catalog data, release build, or the reported hang. No new full CLI/Apple run was performed. Broad CI and maintainer/security approval remain before merge; the requested follow-up review is not itself a clean verdict.

title: fix(macos): keep tailnet gateway discovery within its time budget
body:
Fixes #195766

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: macOS tailnet Gateway discovery can exceed its timeout when Tailscale status candidates are slow or discovery continues after its time budget is spent.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway discovery no longer grants each fallback and later probe a fresh timeout, reducing stalls during picker and onboarding refreshes. Already-resolved Gateways remain available when there is no time left for optional TXT metadata. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share the existing discovery budget across Tailscale status attempts, DNS-SD queries, and Tailscale Serve peer probes. Each operation receives only its remaining allowance, and no new command or probe starts after the deadline. Production and internal tests now use one budget-aware command callback and candidate loop, without legacy whole-status callbacks or alternate constructors. The MagicDNS resolver and credential-free peer-probe behavior are unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Gmail push notifications can remain unavailable for up to 12 hours when watch registration fails at Gateway startup or during renewal.

## User Impact

Transient registration failures retry within minutes instead of waiting for the next full renewal interval. No configuration changes or migration are required.

Retry failed watch starts after one minute, doubling the delay up to the configured renewal interval. Reuse the existing scheduler scope so stopping or replacing the watcher cancels retries. title: fix(signal): deliver replies when signal-cli rejects quote authors
body:
Fixes #195742

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Signal replies failing outright when signal-cli rejects the quoted message's author, and preserves rate-limit details that were previously discarded.

## User Impact

Replies with definitively rejected quote metadata can be delivered without the quote. Other send failures are not replayed. Callers can inspect the server's retry delay and whether a captcha challenge is present without ordinary error rendering exposing its token. CAPTCHA errors now tell operators to complete signal-cli's rate-limit challenge and retry. No configuration changes, migrations, automatic rate-limit retries, or captcha submission are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

signal-cli reports invalid quote authors as RPC `-1` (or REST `400`), rather than the previously recognized `-32602` quote error. The fallback now checks that the rejected value is the quote author—not the recipient or account. A shared `SignalRpcError` retains code/data and safe rate-limit metadata for HTTP and UNIX transports.

This applies @saariuslystoned's existing fix from `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/signal-quote-fallback-rpc-errors`. Validation on current main required restoring the existing string guard before classifying remote UNIX error messages, with missing/malformed-message regression cases. The error-data path and intended quote fallback remain unchanged.

title: fix(android): prevent pending location disclosure after backgrounding
body:
Fixes #195648

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a pending Android location request can return coordinates after the app moves to the background while location access is set to While Using.

## User Impact

While Using requests no longer disclose a fix that arrives after the app leaves the foreground. Explicitly authorized Always access still works. No new settings, permissions, or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

title: fix(macos): keep local socket services available after transient accept errors
body:
Fixes #195592

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app's local socket services stop listening when accepting a connection encounters a recoverable error.

## User Impact

Local app-control and execution-approval clients can keep connecting after transient accept failures instead of losing the listener. Resource shortages use a 100 ms retry delay rather than a busy loop. No configuration changes or migration are required; fatal errors still stop the listener.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep recovery in the shared `LocalSocketServer` owner: retry `EINTR` and `ECONNABORTED` immediately, and back off on descriptor/memory shortages or temporarily unavailable connections. The sleep remains cancellation-aware. The existing accept/cleanup lifecycle stays in place, and unused peer-address capture is removed.

The original publication transferred only the contributor's two-file fix onto upstream main. This review repair removes the test-only backoff callback and directly awaits the real cancellation-aware 100 ms sleep. Regression coverage now uses real Unix-socket ping/pong recovery, shutdown and socket-path reuse under sustained resource pressure, and fatal-error cleanup. No unrelated fork commits or main rebase are included.

## Evidence

- **Verified here for the repair:** inspected the listener, socket-test support and cancellation-test siblings; ran `pnpm docs:list`, `git apply --check`, reverse-patch applicability and `git diff --check`. The applied two-file repair is byte-for-byte identical to the independently inspected 8,196-byte patch. No unrelated files changed relative to the original published head.

The shutdown gate opens immediately before returning `EMFILE`; it does not deterministically establish cancellation latency inside the sleep. These new native tests have not been executed here.
- **Platform gap:** this Linux sandbox has no Swift, Xcode, SwiftLint, or SwiftFormat. No fresh native build, test, lint, format, red/green, or timing success is claimed. Current-head native proof remains pending CI or a macOS runner. Prior-head Periphery and precise-scan failures were HTTP 504 download/setup failures, not evidence of a Swift test failure.

title: fix(macos): stop corrupting names in wide-area gateway discovery
body:
Fixes #195544

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app truncates gateway names containing escaped quotes and corrupts literal backslashes in TXT values returned by wide-area DNS-SD discovery.

## User Impact

Gateway names and other TXT hints retain their quotes and backslashes when discovered through the tailnet fallback. No configuration, protocol, or connection-trust changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing TXT parser reads dig's quoted strings in one pass, decodes escaped octets once as UTF-8, and no longer decodes the resulting values a second time. The separate PTR instance-name decoder and MagicDNS resolver selection are unchanged.

Applied the supplied [fix branch commit](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/d4ecdddc264abe6dfcfbba8f79efd5c362fb6885) unchanged onto fresh main `70e2761fccfc451c6170a197ed00bb02ea54a0f9`. Simplification removes the chained replacement helper and duplicate TXT decoding, retaining one parser owner; production +34/−11 lines and one 20-line discovery-boundary regression.

## Evidence

- **Contributor’s macOS/Xcode runner:** @saariuslystoned reports that the Swift tests ran red before the fix and green afterward. These results were supplied by the contributor, not independently rerun here; runner logs and timing were not supplied.

- **Not run here:** Swift tests/builds, SwiftLint, and SwiftFormat; those tools are unavailable in this sandbox. The added regression goes through `WideAreaGatewayDiscovery.discover` with fixed dig output containing escaped quotes and a literal backslash followed by n, and checks the neighboring gateway port. Existing decimal UTF-8 and resolver-trust cases remain. Real macOS dig comparison and live discovery were not independently exercised; native test wall time is unavailable.

### CI follow-up (2026-11-10)

- Rechecked published head `443795feb2ffbe0dd9ccf882d276cf8ac2b6c365`; no source change was warranted by the observed failures. Local and published trees match, the workspace is clean, and `git diff --check` still passes.

User impact: leaving or canceling an attachment load promptly releases its active download, without waiting for the existing timeout. No configuration or migration is required.

Keep HTTP-call cancellation attached throughout the ticketed download, including response-body reads, while preserving response closure, playback retries, and existing authentication, redirect, MIME, and size limits.

title: fix(plugins): keep repeat updates with current artifacts a no-op
body:
Related: #195653

## What Problem This Solves

A repeat `openclaw update` unnecessarily reinstalls current ClawHub artifacts and reports “plugins updated.” Skipping that installation must still preserve manifest repair and capability-consent review.

## User Impact

Healthy, accepted artifacts produce a clean no-op. Missing/invalid required manifests and stale/missing acceptance follow the ordinary reinstall/review path. Actual installs, host repairs, and record rewrites continue counting as changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawHub retention requires matching source/artifact identity, present runnable entrypoints, healthy host links, and the consent owner's fresh inspection of valid package manifests and current capability coverage. The consent owner preserves its existing official and disabled-update exemptions. Failed retention checks fall through to the existing staged installer and consent handler; acceptance is persisted after review, and refusal is reported normally.

Artifact identity contracts now live with their owner, removing the helper-to-installer import cycle. The added assertions were removed using the real record/union contracts. No config/schema/dependency/release changes.

## Evidence

- `update-noop.test.ts` now exercises the real updater, ClawHub installer, archive installation, and consent owner using synthetic registry/archive I/O. Cases cover healthy no-op, one npm record rewrite, stale/missing acceptance, declined consent, missing/invalid plugin manifests, changed digest, and missing entrypoint. Successful repairs assert usable manifests and persisted current acceptance. The old contract-incomplete installer stub and duplicate ClawHub table are removed.
- Serial named local test attempts (`update-noop.test.ts`, `clawhub.test.ts`) were stopped at cold worker compilation as required on the production host. No local runtime pass or baseline red/green result is claimed; PR CI owns that proof and test timing.
- Touched-file tsgo, oxlint, oxfmt, whitespace checks, and commit-hook ratchets passed. Exactly 51 net repair test lines are allocated separately; PV's 127 + PV2's 51 = 178 final net test lines. Shared scalar unchanged.
- Fresh final local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, base `e08aa74ea39e35d01ba8e8f84e317747aba1bf3f` through the staged snapshot committed as `2edfa6636fd02434644dcbd07827ff0860bd909f`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Static scoped assessment; runtime/complete graph proof remains CI-owned.

### Prior-head CI attribution

All four failed jobs and the separate failed commit status were inspected through the API. These are the five failing entries, rather than five distinct failed jobs:

| [check-guards-architecture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42563087163/job/128984097873) | PR-caused helper/installer all-import cycle. Removed the back-reference and placed shared contracts with the artifact owner. |

No matching scheduled-main job exists, so identical baseline runtime failure is unproven. No unrelated source/test change or retry masks it. |

| [openclaw/ci-gate commit status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42564026955) | Security-review policy correctly propagates failed CI; its review job itself succeeded. |

title: feat(signal): surface read receipts as next-turn context
body:
Fixes #195552

## What Problem This Solves

An agent sending results over Signal cannot tell that an admitted direct recipient has opened a message because inbound read receipts are discarded.

## User Impact

Signal read receipts now become context for the agent’s next turn without triggering an unsolicited reply. Delivery receipts and group read state are not included. Signal’s existing reader-side privacy setting still controls whether receipts are sent; no new configuration is required.

Signal may delay receipts for edited messages and report the revision timestamp rather than the original message timestamp. This change passes through those upstream semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit read receipts through Signal’s durable ingress and reuse the established system-event path used for reactions, with the normal direct-sender access checks and suppression of the account’s own receipts. Other incoming events retain the existing message path; no core contract or new state store is introduced.

Applied [the supplied read-receipts commit](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/b89298b9295a6c562959f2dd93b2b317d9258ad7) to fresh main, then repaired the stale startup-configuration routing found during review. Receipt dispatch now uses the same current-runtime configuration owner as ordinary inbound messages, so live DM-scope and binding changes do not leave receipts routed to an old session. A monitor-level regression protects this repair.

## Evidence

- CI budget repair (`f90847e34207c86c1ed93b79ebe3fdd8369d5d50`): [the failed ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42887505617/job/130080663569) used merge `05efdaa9e79d615bb691866ea18672fbbba3f577` and comparison base `0c5c4754c33dd9a9e7f4eb4493d4472d458a4609`. Reused the byte-identical [canonical 128-line allocation for #196346](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ff392dbeb06bebee505c35038903f9fff924da42/config/test-lines-allocations/196346-drained-capture-in-place.txt), rather than adding duplicate PR-specific credit or changing the shared scalar. Historical merge plus repair passes at 6,635,297 / 6,635,297 (zero slack). A separate index applying this PR to main `ff392dbeb06bebee505c35038903f9fff924da42` passes at 6,641,815 / 6,641,832 (17 inherited slack); the same allocation path/blob prevents double counting. These are local runs of the unmodified CI-tree checker with `--staged --base <exact-base> --no-merge-base`, not a new hosted CI result. `git diff --check` passes. No production, test, or documentation bytes changed; prior focused tests/review remain applicable and were not rerun for this two-line allocation-only repair.
- Documentation follow-up (`f259aee55cb6eb61de9fbc95927cc05b95598978`): clarified incoming versus outgoing read receipts in the Signal guide, including default model visibility, bounded next-turn context, and no unsolicited reply. Targeted format, MDX validation, and `git diff --check` pass. No runtime or test code changed; the implementation proof below is retained from `e8a35e8edb95a7ae441fa58e6871be71ed81f1b7`, not a new live-transport run.
- Refreshed base: `594190c75e5d8e8bc0471f2d7a77792f3417a005`.
- Red/green ingress proof: the new receipt test fails with no receipt dispatched against the original ingress implementation, then passes with the supplied change.
- Red/green repair proof: changing the runtime DM scope from shared-main to per-channel-peer routes the receipt to the old session with the supplied patch; the retained runtime reader routes it to the current session. This exercises the monitor and durable-ingress path and asserts that no reply or last-route update occurs.
- All 42 affected tests pass: 29 monitor lifecycle/reply/reaction cases, 9 durable-ingress cases, and 4 receipt-handler cases. Rerun after the ordered main refresh: 82.50 seconds combined wrapper wall time; Vitest shard durations: 74.70 and 4.44 seconds. CI timing is not yet available. title: fix(signal): preserve native text styles in inbound messages
body:
Fixes #195550

## What Problem This Solves

Signal messages lose native text styles before reaching the agent, so a correction such as “Book ~~Friday~~ Monday” arrives without its strikethrough.

## User Impact

The agent and pending group history retain bold, italic, strikethrough, monospace, and spoiler formatting. Command matching, raw/command bodies, and native quotes continue to use plain text. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Signal mention renderer now carries native style ranges through UTF-16 mention expansion using the shared Markdown range-editing and marker-rendering helpers.

The supplied branch also needed repairs: emphasis now surrounds code instead of becoming literal code content; crossing ranges and paragraphs split into valid emphasis spans; touching ranges merge; code retains line breaks and literal backticks; italics work without word separators. These stay within the Signal renderer rather than introducing a second formatter or changing the shared Markdown API.

Review follow-up: literal backslashes and Markdown punctuation are now escaped before native style markers are inserted. The same range-editing helper maps offsets across these escapes, while generated monospace delimiters and their literal contents are left intact. Messages without native styles retain their previous Markdown behavior.

Source: the one-commit diff from `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/signal-inbound-text-styles` (`ff2943eb9c4c3fd73523ca8b50299129099bb382`), applied onto upstream main `594190c75e5d8e8bc0471f2d7a77792f3417a005`, with the repairs above.

## Evidence

- The original six inbound regression cases failed on unchanged main because the agent body lacked native styles.
- Additional regressions reproduced combined code/emphasis, crossing ranges, whitespace-inclusive selections, intraword italics, adjacent/overlapping code ranges, multiline code, and paragraph-boundary failures before their respective repairs.
- **81 tests passed** across the text-styles, inbound-context, mention-gating, and control-lane suites. The 21 style cases use synthetic receive events through the real inbound runner and inspect the agent-dispatch context. Parser-based assertions verify text and per-character formatting; command/raw bodies and stored native quote text remain plain.
- Three added receive-handler/parser cases reproduced lost backslashes, interpreted punctuation, and literal text beside native monospace on the prior head. All pass after the repair; an additional case protects unstyled Markdown passthrough.
- Signal package typecheck, targeted lint/format, test-line budget, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent full P0–P2 reviews completed. Reproducible findings were repaired and verified. One proposed CJK punctuation failure was rejected after its exact reproduction passed through the production inbound boundary and Markdown parser; that case remains covered.
- A fresh independent full P0–P2 review of the literal-escaping repair reported no findings.
- The requester’s earlier live style proof used an earlier `mentions.ts`; it does not cover the final repair head `1808252f2299d7c3b3590c2b3d26de5a89821932`. The final-head live Signal/model rerun is pending. This repair was tested through synthetic receive events and the real inbound runner/parser, without live Signal side effects. This changes inbound agent context, not a UI surface.

<details>

title: fix(signal): avoid duplicate attachments for complete long messages

Fixes #195549

## What Problem This Solves

Signal long messages arrive as duplicate text-file media, or gain a misleading attachment-unavailable notice, after signal-cli has already merged the complete text into the message body.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter the Signal `text/x-signal-plain` carrier before both ordinary media handling and mention-skipped group history, but only when the raw body’s UTF-8 byte length is at least the advertised attachment size. The production fix is unchanged from the supplied commit `5426df5bed7f2790de5c0fac660debde82c9fd4c` on `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/signal-long-text-attachment`. With production modules from base `df13b6b8994cefe16f311f29f0301bba511ec617`, both complete-body cases fail on the original defects (duplicate media and an extra unavailable attachment); both truncated-body cases pass. All four pass with the fix.
