title: fix(ui): restore saved theme after an initial preference read fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI can stay on its browser-mirrored theme after the first profile-preference read fails, even after the server recovers, until the connection is restarted.

## User Impact

Saved appearance preferences recover automatically without restarting the gateway. Three automatic retries are paced at 1, 2, and 4 seconds; after exhaustion, a later normal synchronization can retry. Successful reads remain cached. No persistence, configuration, stylesheet-timeout, or permission changes are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell retained both initialization readiness and the unsuccessful appearance-read promise as completed work. Keep failure/backoff state with that existing read owner instead: redundant reconciliation shares pending backoff, replacement reads retire its timer, and disconnect/reset cancel it. Existing connection/profile/context guards still reject obsolete results.

The production defect and matching recovery are reproduced independently. Attribution to the original reported native-app incident remains provisional: its original WebView read error was not captured.

## Evidence

Current maintainer validation on `434d2147`: [real Gateway before/after screenshots, lifecycle controls, and exact-head CI qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195657#issuecomment-6733194871).

### Real persisted-Gateway recovery

The production Control UI was served by an isolated **real built Gateway**. Synthetic Knot/Dark, **JetBrains Mono** interface font, and **Lora** chat font were saved through actual `users.prefs.set`, read back, and retained across a Gateway process restart. No profile database/storage shortcut or mocked successful preferences reply was used.

A transparent Playwright WebSocket bridge forwarded traffic to that Gateway. It replaced only the **first actual successful** `users.prefs.get` response with a synthetic `UNAVAILABLE` error. The retry's actual server response was forwarded unchanged (held briefly only to capture the pre-recovery screen). In the fresh recovery browser context:

- Exactly **1 connect**, **2 preference requests**, and **2 actual server replies**.
- Appearance changed from **Claw/System/theme-default fonts** to **Knot/Dark/JetBrains Mono/Lora**, without reconnecting.
- Both preference values were asserted in application state. Computed body and chat-preview fonts were asserted independently; both webfaces loaded successfully.
- Gateway-served production entry bytes matched the local built asset (SHA-256 `725308ab29aa3142165aa7947265a0e98cebe1035f1a51f403f64b69b8a5b039`).
- Real-Gateway scenario: **13.05 s**. Combined real-Gateway + committed bundled-browser recovery proof: **2 passed**, 65.75 s Vitest / 67.97 s wrapper wall time, including setup/build work. These are focused scenarios, not a full-suite pass.

**Before recovery** — the first read failed; the real retry reply is held for this capture.

![Before recovery: Claw and System with theme-default interface and chat fonts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a259c14-989d-4f79-beda-dc450a8f6c7f)

**After recovery** — the unchanged real server reply restores all four saved preferences on the same connection.

![After recovery: Knot and Dark with JetBrains Mono interface and Lora chat fonts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f127fcf-3a21-4036-8159-93f0637b5315)

### Regression, checks, and review

- **Original red → green, bundled UI:** one synthetic initial read failure leaves the unmodified base on Claw/System with no second read; the fixed production UI retries without reconnecting. The existing primary regression now also asserts both saved font preferences and actual computed typography instead of adding a duplicate recovery scenario.
- **Owner/consumer coverage:** original six-file run: 85 tests passed. Current changed owner suite: **48 passed**, 0.98 s Vitest / 3.01 s wrapper wall time, including rejected/protocol-valid `no_durable_identity` recovery, paced exhaustion, later synchronization, deduplication, and retirement.
- **Test contract repair:** the initial CI test-type failure was PR-caused: an accent-shaped inferred mock reply rejected valid replies. The fixture now uses the real `UsersPrefsGetResult` union; no cast or fabricated entries were added. Both `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-app.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json` pass.
- **Other checks:** targeted lint/format, `git diff --check`, and staged test-line ratchet passed. Original UI production typecheck/controller-guard proof remains valid: production code is unchanged by this evidence follow-up. Runtime and production UI builds completed; the UI size report emitted small gzip-budget warnings, not a claimed clean size-budget result.
- **Fresh independent review:** Auto Review, OpenClaw engine / GPT-6.1 Sol, complete updated local candidate against `f0493786e0284f3231ff34358a69d96729ee0f97`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no findings**. This is scoped code review, not a whole-repository review or independent replay of test execution.
- **Limits:** Chromium/real-Gateway recovery is proven; native macOS/WebKit and original-incident attribution are still not claimed. The initial failing external read is deliberately injected, not a captured original incident.

<details>
<summary>CI attribution, earlier browser-suite investigation, and change cost</summary>

Initial-head CI at `239fa7d5119c0ad911ee95db80ecbb165c8403be` was not green. The [PR-caused test-type error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42560085114/job/128975582165) is repaired and both affected test-type leaves pass locally. No claim is made that CI on the updated head is green.

Other initial-head browser failures were investigated separately rather than relabeled by job name:

- Cron's initial-roster failure matches the same test/signature in [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42556669675/job/128964187118); [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42560085114/job/128974787649).
- Native-plugin Built-in 1280 composer-footer `separated=false` matches [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42556669675/job/128964187055); [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42560085114/job/128974787572).
- Three omitted-image variants and the compact subagent-waiting summary failure reproduced in a bounded unchanged-production-base comparison (45.92 s): matching visible-image timeout and summary `getAttribute` timeout signatures.
- **Still unconfirmed:** cron history-processing's duplicate-history-request failure. The bounded base replay passed; main's same test had a different navigation-wait timeout. This individual failure is not conclusively attributed to baseline.

The earlier full theme-boot run also had four intermittent hidden-transcript startup timeouts (1440 px light/dark saved, 1440 px dark/system saved, 390 px light/dark saved, and 390 px light/system unsaved). An unchanged-base run reproduced the same timeout in two cases (1440 px dark/light saved and dark/system saved), not conclusive attribution for every variant. Full patched run: 70.40 s; baseline comparison: 46.88 s. The recovery scenario uses Appearance independently of transcript positioning.

Simplification: no additional read owner or global polling loop; production +32 net lines. The exact **174-line test allocation** covers distinct recovery/lifecycle, protocol typing, font restoration, and browser-transport regressions. The standalone real-Gateway capture script and generated media remain proof artifacts, not additional committed duplicate test scaffolding.

title: fix: updates survive interrupted heartbeat runs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes updates failing in post-install Doctor when Gateway shutdown leaves a legacy heartbeat run marker.

## User Impact

Interrupted heartbeat runs can migrate during updates. Live or unproved work remains pending with a warning. Notification-producing recovery now converges through the next Gateway cron startup instead of repeatedly deferring or quarantining the legacy job. No schema, protocol, or config option changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor revalidates its held offline maintenance owner and uses cron's existing recovery kernel. Ordinary interrupted runs settle before conversion. When recovery needs live notification dispatch, only that recovery attempt rolls back to its savepoint; Doctor still commits the ordinary payload conversion with the original run marker, history, and receipt intact. Gateway startup can then decode the row and use its normal recovery and notification path. Both fresh conversion and resumed config retirement retain the pending execution facts when they disable the monitor, so startup restores its recorded result without re-enabling it.

The live/unproved refusal remains update-advisory because its conversion transaction and config writer do not commit. Lost maintenance authority and integrity failures retain their existing failure behavior. The candidate contains the repair; published updater parents need no new marker.

## Evidence

title: feat: add native Celeris, Fastino, Nace and Perplexity decisions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several native APIs evaluated in Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2 cannot be selected as OpenClaw Decision models.

## User Impact

Adds opt-in text/JSON Boolean, Choice, and Score support for:

- Celeris-1.1 Decision: `celeris/celeris-1.1-decision`.
- Perplexity Decider v1.2: `perplexity-decisions/pplx-decider-v1.2`, with native auth isolated from Perplexity/OpenRouter search.
- Nace Drex Max v1.1: `nace/drex-max-v1.1`.
- Hosted Fastino GLiDE: `fastino/fastino/GLiDE`.

These models do not support chat; credential setup changes no model selection. Images/vendor extensions are not exposed. New packages are development-checkout candidates, not claimed npm releases.

**Accepted proof gap:** on November 12, 2026, @vincentkoc explicitly approved landing with authenticated vendor tests deferred for all four integrations. The live suite discovered **four skipped cases**, not successful inference or account access. This accepts the disclosed uncertainty, not a review/security/CI waiver.

**Exclusions:** Clef silently truncates evidence without a verified reject mode; hosted GLiDE is unversioned, not a benchmark-v1.2 pin. Existing Baseten/OpenRouter/OpenAI/Anthropic support is unchanged. Benchmark inclusion alone establishes no typed Haiku Decision endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

Official contracts determine support. Celeris/Nace reuse the OpenAI Decisions codec; Perplexity uses named questions. Fastino maps fractional `expected_level`, not argmax `score`, and sends `store: false`.

The prepared HTTP executor is shared rather than duplicating authentication, admission, proxy/TLS, deadlines, cancellation, credential-reflection rejection and release. No chat fallback, automatic retry, provider-specific config leaves or benchmark-derived token prices are added.

## Evidence

- Earlier integrated proof: **105 focused cases passed** (native 16, V1 11, OpenAI 39, ClawRouter 23, SDK 2, prefix stability 14), nine publication-contract cases, 24 catalog/install cases and a full build in **223.7s**. Six scalar-JSON cases were red before the V2 eligibility repair. These are fixture/build results, not vendor inference; prior-head evidence applies only to unchanged inputs.
- Independent autoreviews of the implementation, packaging, live-suite and metadata/docs changes found no actionable P0–P2 issues. [Codex repair #196497](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196497) is merged at `cb54d271d89958a6f0a64c2099b4bc993725b866`, already part of main; its six integrated cases passed.
- Actual November 12 config conflicts were repaired by integrating main `7b3c6edf59ca7e8b3f6b849ef544fcc75e569fef`, source merge `2e151b0aadff4a1d35f0b0a056bb5dbc8b4b80a5`. Only two generated baseline artifacts conflicted and were regenerated through their owner. Core **2647**, channel **4005** and their hashes are unchanged from base; plugin **5018→5081** adds generic management paths for the three plugins, not custom provider config. No handwritten runtime repair.
- Repaired candidate: **18/18** registered-provider/catalog cases passed in **50.40s**; config-baseline/inventory/diff checks passed. Pinned-base ratchet **6,669,915 / 6,669,976**, 61 slack, no extra grant. An initial default comparison against the old merge base during an uncommitted merge failed and was superseded by the explicit integrated-base check. Simplification kept existing owners and regenerated only derived artifacts. Lockfile delta is just three workspace importers.
- SDK comparison `568d89f3a4e82d13ecca4ed602c46a04bda322f0`→`2906a94a70b3b7a5586310caf172a320c5bab900`, digest `1c4c47ef`: one entrypoint/three exports added, none removed; equivalent shared OpenAI aliases. Later task changes do not alter this SDK source; historical comparison is not current CI.
- Live suite uses each registered adapter with a synthetic Boolean/Choice/Score batch, explicit opt-in and its own key; running Gateway configuration/auth stores stay untouched. **Four skipped vendor cases remain a deferred proof obligation**, accepted by the maintainer.

### Current CI attribution — not overall green

[Run 43150547442, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43150547442) at `216f01fa632cc94535e13402d9dba1fd0080bfbd` is terminal: **167/167 jobs observed, none pending**. `security-fast` passed. Four root test lanes and their [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43150547442/job/130969058521) failed; no rerun or weaker assertion was used.

Independent diagnosis and source comparison attribute the failures to inherited owners:

- [Memory CLI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43150547442/job/130959017903): orphan-provenance fixture expects exit 1, receives 0. One exact-file replay reproduced the same failure, **57 passed / 1 failed**, 62.54s. The unchanged fixture still expects unconditional FK scanning. Parent inspected the fixture, admission owner and documented policy; no provider execution or resolved dependency change is involved.

No full-scan behavior was restored and no assertion flipped.

The fixture explicitly uses mock conversational Responses and a plugin allowlist excluding the new Decision adapters; its execution/settlement/delivery owners, harness and dependency resolutions are unchanged. That attempt remains historical red evidence, not an automatic exception. Current main integration was for actual generated config conflicts, not merely to chase green.

title: fix(node-host): prevent cancelled commands from running after reconnect cleanup
body:
Fixes #195535

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a node command can run after its caller has cancelled or timed out while the node is still cleaning up a previous connection.

## User Impact

User impact: commands cancelled before they start no longer execute late after reconnect cleanup, avoiding unexpected work and duplicate execution after a retry. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a cancellation marker for every invocation waiting on disconnect cleanup and check it before dispatch. Preserve cancellation of already-running commands and the existing connection-retirement and shutdown behavior.

The contributor's fix is unchanged. The existing update-pause helper is moved unchanged into its own module solely to resolve the observed 700-line lint limit in the current runtime file; no lint suppression is added.

title: feat(signal): edit earlier messages in place
body:
Fixes #195547

## What Problem This Solves

Signal status updates currently require new messages instead of updating an earlier message in place.

## User Impact

Users can edit the account's earlier Signal messages through the existing message edit action, using native or container transports. Signal's own edit eligibility rules still apply.

Revision chains use the existing plugin-scoped keyed state so CLI and Gateway runs can share them across restarts, bounded to 2,000 entries with a two-day TTL. Missing, expired, evicted, or unavailable state falls back to the supplied message ID. Live restart behavior and reaction/pin preservation have not been independently verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose Signal editing through the existing action and send owners, and track the latest known revision for subsequent edits. The reviewed follow-up replaces the process-local map with the existing asynchronous plugin-state keyed store; no new configuration option or database is introduced.

**Repair to the supplied branch:** the container adapter previously dropped the edit timestamp and would send an ordinary new message. Translate it to the REST API’s `edit_timestamp` field, which is supported by the [upstream request contract](https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/blob/787d204e155d0c73840a615a5e90c697bacaa6f1/src/api/api.go#L128-L145) and [send handler](https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/blob/787d204e155d0c73840a615a5e90c697bacaa6f1/src/api/api.go#L564-L567).

The initial container repair adds three production lines in the existing transport adapter. It replaced the mock-only send test with real loopback transport coverage and removed incomplete receipt casts. The persistence follow-up removes the map, adds the plugin-state owner, and routes the existing revision-chain test through a real isolated keyed store. The supplied five-file follow-up originally relied on six lines of base budget slack. The CI repair consolidates the redundant single-edit mock case into the persisted-chain case, retaining recipient, text, and timestamp assertions for both edits. That CI-only repair removed eight net test lines and shrank the allocation from 91 to 89 without changing production code or the shared baseline.

**P2 import-boundary repair:** load the sender dynamically inside the validated edit branch instead of importing it during channel discovery. The existing channel loader remains unchanged; both imports resolve the same sender module without adding a loader abstraction or a circular dependency. This repair changes one production line for one line and adds one 40-line boundary regression with its own exact allocation.

## Evidence

- Applied fork commits `784ac03d68349723b79bddf734e9a286ad46f71f` and `e93a88182b12aede727f82124f74af5cb6e6f7c2` onto refreshed main `ee431f3f2dcd9cc04a86c5c7756d13f88bdf1dde`, then repaired the container translation.

With the repair, discovery leaves it unloaded, and a real edit loads it once and emits exactly one correctly encoded loopback container request. Standalone green: 1/1, 3.047 seconds test time / 41.96 seconds wall time including cold compiler preparation. Hosted new-head timing/results remain pending.
- Signal plugin typecheck, a narrowed test typecheck covering the new regression, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- The repository’s isolated Signal runtime-package build passed (10 public entries). Inspection of emitted code confirms the edit branch and the existing channel loader dynamically import the same sender chunk; no static sender import is emitted in the channel chunk. This is bounded plugin build proof, not a full OpenClaw package/declaration build.
- The requester reports a second review of the supplied follow-up with no P1/P2 findings. This is attributed review evidence, not an independent rerun. The [hosted P2 static-send-import finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195625#issuecomment-6731932236) is repaired by this update.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #195528

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an in-flight background-command follow-up can fail when another agent is added or edited.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Both event types now use the existing per-agent configuration comparison. Unscheduled events retain checks for every channel because their tools retain captured configuration; scheduled message actions re-admit off-route policy at invocation. title: fix: avoid repeated database copies during cron lint
body:
Fixes #195502

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor cron inference-account lint repeatedly copies large agent databases for unbound jobs, making lint take minutes and causing update rehearsals to time out.

## User Impact

Doctor reuses each agent database’s read-only inspection image across jobs, including configured agent directories and symlinked state/store paths, while preserving account warnings and per-job model/account selection. Distinct session and auth/catalog databases each retain their own image. Update rehearsals reuse their already-private database images. The candidate Doctor must contain this fix; no schema or configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inspection scope prepares and owns the image, and session, credential, and catalog workers borrow its captured physical identity. Preparation resolves the configured auth/catalog path through the same owner as those readers. Images are indexed by canonical source path and matched against retained file identity and birthtime, so filesystem aliases share bytes while replaced sources are refused. Source checks, read-only opens, schema ownership, and cleanup remain checked at their existing boundaries.

Snapshot selection and borrowed-image identity validation live in a small sibling module. The session reader remains unchanged at 709 counted lines, below the original base’s 710. Normal cron execution and repair authorization retain their existing paths.

Thanks to @etzelm for the measurements and isolated reproduction: one automation on a 3.4 GiB agent database produced about three agent copies and took 23.8 seconds. Those are the reporter’s measurements, not new benchmark results.

Reviewed both related diffs: #193643 changes readiness warnings and #192376 captures accounts for plugin-created jobs. This change does not alter those policies or touch their files.

## Evidence

- Corrected the production-detector regression to use the same artifact-preserving agent scope as `doctor --lint`. Its table covers default and configured agent directories, four unbound jobs, an existing session model override, unchanged source families, and exactly one preparation per physical database.

This covers scoped lint copy counts, configured directories, aliases, source identity, and cleanup. The shared scalar is unchanged; current CI ratchet validation is pending.

title: fix(muse): a stuck turn fails sibling sessions on the same agent
body:
Fixes #195524

## What Problem This Solves

A stuck or cancelled Muse turn can close the shared host and fail sibling OpenClaw sessions on the same agent.

## User Impact

Cancelling one session no longer interrupts another session’s Muse host. This uses one host per active OpenClaw session rather than one per agent; idle hosts still close after five minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Include the OpenClaw session ID in the existing pool key and retain it during reacquisition. Turns in the same session keep reusing their host, while unscoped catalog reads keep their separate shared host. Update the session documentation to match.

## Evidence

- Applied @saariuslystoned’s [source fix](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/commit/21938bc8296f9de341023c46afa1f18a66fba720), then reconciled through managed base refresh onto `f0493786e0284f3231ff34358a69d96729ee0f97`. The base-relative candidate contains only six Muse fix, test, fixture, allocation, and documentation files.
- Replaced the pool-only direct-close test with a regression through the production harness, SDK, and real stdio fixture. Two different OpenClaw sessions have active turns on the same workspace/credentials. One waits at a real MSP approval; the other acknowledges `turn/interrupt` but never settles. Neither finishes at 4,999 ms. At 5,000 ms the harness force-closes the stuck host; the sibling stays active and successfully completes after its approval is released. The test never calls `runtime.close()` itself.
- Red/green proof: with both production owners restored to the exact base above, the new test fails because the sibling returns `failed` instead of `ok`. Restoring the session-scoped fix makes it pass. The separate same-session host-reuse regression remains.

title: fix(discord): acknowledge interactions during global rate-limit pauses
body:
Fixes #195529

## What Problem This Solves

Discord slash commands, components, and modals can miss their initial acknowledgment deadline when an unrelated bot-global pause holds interaction callbacks. A callback receiving its own global 429 can also retry immediately instead of honoring Retry-After.

## User Impact

Initial interaction callbacks can proceed during an unrelated global pause, while each rate-limited request still waits for its own Retry-After and route limits. Ordinary REST requests remain paused. Follow-up webhook requests are unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies @saariuslystoned’s contributor fix, with review-driven corrections for short route resets and a callback’s own global 429. The existing scheduler selects the next eligible request using its request-specific retry deadline, route bucket, and applicable global pause. Other eligible callbacks remain free to proceed; no second dispatch path or timer owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- Original regression: the callback was held by a global pause on main at `521bfc46880bdecbd39ffa2f67904f768ea03fe9`. The short per-route reset regression also remains covered.
- New regression against prior PR head `83bfd48acc110345682d417f2ccc12be4d0c7653`: a callback with a 100 ms global Retry-After dispatched twice at 0 ms. With the repair it retries at 100 ms, a different callback dispatches at 0 ms, and an ordinary request waits until 100 ms.

title: fix: Pull requests shows an old task's PR when a worktree name is reused
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session's **Pull requests** block shows an unrelated, older pull request when its managed worktree reuses the name of a retired one.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski: a new session on worktree `openclaw/cool-crab-2` (branch created 2026-11-08) listed #154218, which another session opened from an earlier `openclaw/cool-crab-2` branch on 2026-09-21. The new session never read or mentioned that PR.

## User Impact

User impact: the Pull requests block no longer shows another task's PR just because a recycled worktree name produced the same branch name. Pull requests opened from the current branch, and branches checked out from an existing PR, still appear as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Branch discovery asks GitHub for PRs by `owner:branch` name only. Managed worktree names become available again after a retired worktree's registry record expires (30 days), and the older PR on GitHub keeps that head branch name indefinitely.

The checkout context now reads the branch's Git creation entry. When Git created the branch from the default branch, as managed worktrees do, PRs opened before that moment are skipped. Other start points (`HEAD`, `FETCH_HEAD`, a remote branch) may be adopting an existing PR, so they stay unfiltered, as do missing or expired reflogs.

Accepted edge case: a branch created from the default branch and then reset onto an older PR's commits will hide that older PR. Discovery through publication receipts and bound PRs is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Independently ran 37 focused discovery/branch tests on the Tempbook, including current PRs, remote-branch adoption, credential isolation, rate limits and existing branch statistics. All passed (67.32 seconds for the two files).
- Independently created a real local `openclaw/cool-crab-2` branch from `origin/main` and exercised the production session PR loader against the live GitHub API, transported through the authenticated GitHub CLI. The original discovery implementation returned the real older PR #154218; the candidate excluded it. Both calls completed successfully. No GitHub records were created or modified by this test.
- This is real-Git/live-API proof at the loader boundary, not a claim of a full browser or live-Gateway UI test. The temporary experiment was removed afterward; the committed regression retains deterministic external-I/O fixtures and checks that a current PR is not lost.
- A fresh independent P0–P2 code review found no actionable issues. The added work is a bounded 1 KiB reflog-prefix read when checkout context is loaded; there is no new polling loop.
- Added a scoped allocation for the existing 37-line regression. The shared test baseline, production code and passing tests were not changed. The test-line check passes; CI runs on the published correction `52d6682aa06d`.

title: fix(muse): allow slow starts without missing-install errors
body:
Fixes #195521

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Muse startup on a busy host or a large local store could fail after 30 seconds with misleading install/sign-in guidance. Startup cancellation also failed to reach chat acquisition, could interrupt another caller sharing the starting host, and lost non-Error cancellation reasons.

## User Impact

Muse has up to 120 seconds to initialize, and catalog reads allow that window plus 30 seconds. Startup deadlines report a timeout rather than suggesting a reinstall. Canceling a chat or catalog wait preserves that caller's reason without aborting another live waiter. The starting host is stopped when its last waiter cancels. A genuinely stalled startup takes longer to fail. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep host startup ownership in the existing Muse pool: forward the turn signal, race each caller's wait independently, and track live waiters before aborting shared startup. Reuse the existing SDK abort helper. The catalog owner exports its deadline derived from the startup limit. Test gates stay under the suite cleanup owner, with named pipes on Windows.

The supplied timeout fix and prior test-directory cleanup are retained. Main was integrated only to resolve an actual import conflict, preserving upstream Muse usage reporting; the reviewed base is `e08aa74ea39e35d01ba8e8f84e317747aba1bf3f`.

title: fix(muse): prevent long turns from being stopped by the stall watchdog
body:
Fixes #195518

## What Problem This Solves

Long Muse turns could lose their reply when the host's stalled-run watchdog stopped them after about six minutes despite the native turn still running. The initial liveness handoff also waited for host transcript and streaming consumers, leaving an already completed native turn exempt from host supervision if those consumers stalled.

## User Impact

Muse can continue long-running native work under its existing turn budget, including unlimited budgets. Native completion now returns liveness to host supervision immediately, independently of pending transcript writes or streaming callbacks. Cancellation, timeout handling, and final cleanup are preserved. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native turn owns liveness only while it remains open. The harness now observes both fulfillment and rejection of `turn.completed` directly, rather than waiting for `consumeTurn`. Its final cleanup still releases liveness on every exit; the existing host consumers continue draining normally.

The existing completion regression now holds a transcript append pending under an unlimited budget, observes the real SDK turn's completion, and checks that liveness is released while the attempt is still unfinished. Releasing the gate must still produce a successful result. The existing active-turn, cancellation, and failure regressions remain. This focused replacement adds 28 net test lines: the single scoped allocation is now 94 in `config/test-lines-allocations/195518-muse-owns-liveness.txt`; the duplicate remains absent and the global budget scalar is unchanged. Production line count is unchanged after simplifying two adjacent callbacks without changing their behavior.

## Evidence

- Current head: `c74b0455e65a9cc872aef280b1a922cbec4d4f8c`, directly parented by `5681f6cb9f04e8118f111d8acd36f7bcda5ecb4f`. title: fix(auth): recover in-flight runs after shared OAuth token rotation
body:
Fixes #195517

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an in-flight run failing with HTTP 401 after another run rotates their shared OAuth account token, including providers that exchange the OAuth source for a runtime token.

## User Impact

A replay-safe run can recover once using the same account’s canonical credential instead of ending with a sign-in error. Direct OAuth retries require a changed token; runtime-exchange providers can re-exchange an unchanged source when only the runtime token expired. Explicit reconnects and account-identity changes cannot revive the old run. No configuration change or migration is required. Existing outer replay-safety restrictions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical OAuth resolution now has one shared owner for request auth, direct 401 recovery, and runtime exchanges. It omits the captured store, keeps the selected profile locked, settles sibling publication, and retains the run’s captured authorization around lookup and refresh admission. Runtime exchange validates that same authorization before provider egress and again before installing its result. The canonical source and exchanged runtime token remain separate; scheduled refreshes use the same path as auth-error refreshes.

The original fork diff at `462ef9d8d2cff63335a4b4267c45b8a62cc98a96` was applied to main `2995860edbf34e5a4d18793a118a13c273a2bd98`. The exact follow-up commit `a7c0dae964146323bb6eda2b5a1e31aab6b23af8` addressed direct retry authorization. The runtime-exchange correction in `aef09e9b865a3466641dd9ba27d4dcab66439f60` follows PR head `3cfa6cb3fcf5153c690411a3a574b984b3304656` without replacing branch history.

Existing direct-token cases and one-retry checks remain. Net new test coverage is 76 lines, allocated separately from the original 62-line allocation; production line count does not grow.

User impact: the transcript runs right up to the composer and continues behind its rounded corners. The last message still ends above the composer, and the jump-to-latest button stays clear of it, on desktop and phone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation's composer token sets the composer's top margin to 0 instead of 8px. The footer now overlaps the transcript by the composer's largest corner radius. The transcript gets the same amount of extra bottom padding, so nothing is hidden at the end. The scroll-to-bottom button rises by the same overlap unless the measured activity clearance is already larger. Short panes keep their zero-padding layout plus the overlap. The narrow-width 6px rule was removed because the later base rule always overrode it.

## Evidence

Screenshots are below. They come from the mocked Control UI at 1280×800 in dark mode, with the transcript scrolled so a message passes the composer's top-left corner.

- `ui/src/e2e/chat-footer.e2e.test.ts` now asserts that the transcript reaches under the composer's top by at least the corner radius and that the last row ends above the composer. Without the CSS change it fails on desktop (`expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 25`) and on phone (`… 35`); with it, both pass.
- Focused browser E2E: `chat-footer`, `chat-composer-size`, `chat-scroll-dock`, `chat-composer-boundary`, `chat-position-rail-layout`, `chat-panel-layout`: 16/16 passed.
- Focused footer layout browser regression: 15/15 cases passed (4.77 seconds) after replacing obsolete viewport separation expectations with actual content-clearance checks. Short-pane final-message clearance, notice ordering, footer containment, and PR-link actionability remain asserted.
- Exact test-line allocation: 14 lines cover the existing E2E regression (+11) and footer-clearance assertions (+3). This metadata correction preserves all production and test bytes. The prior CI run tested base `99b8d707` and reported 59 inherited lines beyond this PR's own growth; that historical debt was recorded without granting extra allowance. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42553054567) has passed, including the baseline ratchets.
- `stylelint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Independent corrective review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- Accepted edge case: a narrow centered notice pill above the composer now floats over the transcript's bottom edge instead of sitting below a straight cut. Full-width cards, such as the run-failure card and queue, cover it cleanly.

**Before** (current `main`): the transcript is cut flat beside the composer's top-left corner.

![Before: transcript cut flat beside the composer corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f910091c-172b-41d5-8b1a-ec80f2ec2d93)

**After**: the transcript continues behind the rounded corner.

Arm a MutationObserver before releasing session creation or resizing. title: fix: progress-card updates discard unrelated session caches
body:
Related: #178731

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: updating or clearing a progress card invalidates cached session facts even when no session entry or transcript changes.

## User Impact

Progress-card updates and dismissals retain valid session-scoped cache receipts. Schema changes and real session mutations still invalidate them; authorization, commit admission, rollback, and dismissal revision checks are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

This is a narrow write-classification repair, not a demonstrated fix for the Codex child-completion authority failure discussed in #178731.

The card writer leaves its affected session scopes unspecified, so card-only writes conservatively invalidate every tracked session scope. Certify an empty session-impact set only around the two card-row mutation sites. Keep lazy schema creation and the enclosing transaction outside those scopes, and restore any caller's enclosing session-write scope afterward.

Pass the existing candidate-only `cleanupFailure: "warn"` policy through both nested header probes. Reuse the existing warning logger and directory owner, retaining bounded removal retries and later cleanup custody. Cleanup warnings preserve the successful result or original read error.

Related: #195409

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PostgreSQL conformance shard 1/3 timing out on pull requests when its PG17 tests leave too little time for the separate PG16 Gateway cron smoke.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. Storage and updater PRs retain every conformance test and the PG16 smoke within the existing three-job layout and 30-minute job budgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reserve 150 seconds on shard 1 when comparing candidate assignments. The PG16 command took 139.37–141.43 seconds in successful baselines, including a second worker preparation of about 72 seconds; the reservation also leaves a small allowance for its service lifecycle. The planner previously balanced only PG17 work.

All callers retain one deterministic assignment, including scheduled runs without the additional smoke. With the committed timing model and current inventory, PG17 estimates change from 1,582.964 / 1,583.292 / 1,583.315 seconds to 1,500.094 / 1,649.072 / 1,649.034 seconds. title: fix: Gateway retains completed reply runtimes after catalog reloads
body:
Related: #150955, #159373. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: completed replies keep unnecessary model runtime objects alive when native async resources retain their context across catalog reloads. ## User Impact User impact: ended turns release these closed runtime objects without configuration, permission, or restart-behavior changes. This does not establish that the original multi-minute outage is fixed. ## Why This Change Was Made Keep borrowed snapshots, target data, and acquisition references with their existing owners. Separate persistent catalog status/live-generation readers from acquisition and publication-result scopes. Preserve the complete native source-authority metadata, live registration checks, and accepted-write settlement order. ## Evidence ### Original runtime-retention repair Same loopback-only **built Gateway** flow: four sessions, 36 verified native tool captures, eight hot catalog reloads confirmed by models.list, then 65 seconds quiet plus GC. Native callbacks remain cached through the census. | Post-GC ModelRegistry objects | Warm baseline | After eight reloads | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Base | 6 | 46 | | Fixed production candidate | 2 | 2 | Acceptance was written before replay: survivors ≤ warm baseline plus one live successor. All 69 completed health RPCs succeeded; maximum outside intentional snapshot windows was 8.9 ms. Gateway shutdown was clean. The prepared source update, tree **81ccbae40b14c9e63a73eabab9ffc3154d56de16**, changes **only the maintained measurement script** relative to published head **8b2f0ffa0b6f2a80b6ff17e73b8e781b3fc73d2c**: optional 16/24-reload modes and complete intermediate censuses. No broader production fix was added. Measured production code/build remain identical to tree **c6ff6b167bb9decd8d35dfda89e8018f0c652c6e**, verified against retained source/build hashes. **Publication status at this draft:** the script extension is local/unpublished until its exact source update is read back on GitHub. Broader diagnostic harnesses below are private local evidence, not published rerun commands. The original eight-reload command already exists in the PR source: 
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/gateway-catalog-context-retention.mjs NEW_SYNTHETIC_ROOT
The 24-reload measurement completed 100 verified tool invocations with its native callback cache capped at 36. Warm/8/16/24 post-GC registry counts were **3/3/3/3**, with main heap **523.4/633.1/643.7/644.2 MB** (decimal). The last eight reloads added 0.48 MB, below the prewritten 2 MiB/reload sustained-growth investigation threshold. This does not establish universally bounded heap. All 140 completed health RPCs succeeded, but the **28.1-second observer cadence gap** remains unattributed and prevents a continuous-availability claim. ### Failed-turn controls and uninterrupted pressure Recovered the earlier 1,544-failed-turn/225-second workload and profiles. New runs used unchanged built production, synthetic loopback provider, four sessions and a per-session reset every eight turns. Warmed checkpoints followed 65 seconds quiet plus GC. The uninterrupted comparison **does not force GC during load** and takes one bounded five-second CPU sample. | Built-Gateway flow | Verified work | Post-GC main heap (MB, decimal) | | --- | ---: | --- | | Windowed HTTP-400 failures | 1,544 turns | 535.5 / 586.6 / 594.1 / 605.6 / 605.3 | | Matched successful flow | 1,544 turns | 520.3 / 572.2 / 580.8 / 592.9 / 594.7 | | Uninterrupted failures, 225.45 seconds | 1,580 turns after 48 warmup | 568.0 → 609.4 | | Uninterrupted successes, 225.37 seconds | 1,594 turns after 48 warmup | 554.1 → 598.5 | Maximum sampled uninterrupted main heap was 1,006.2/960.2 MB and RSS 4.27/4.39 GB, within declared 1.4 GiB main-heap / 6 GiB RSS stop budgets. Bounded CPU samples attributed 3.56%/5.11% to GC, not complete runtime accounting. Each uninterrupted run had 373 independent HTTP probes and 76 WebSocket-opening probes: no HTTP errors outside explicit diagnostic windows, response maxima 68.2/124.0 ms, observer cadence lag below 4 ms. Quiet lanes had zero active/queued work. Failed-turn window constructor counts were ModelRegistry **3/3/3**, AsyncContextFrame **68/68/69**, AbortSignal **209/211/212**, FailoverError **1/1/1**. A late +7.5 MB window was predominantly compiled-code growth, not another established closed-runtime retaining chain. These bounded diagnostic controls are not a five-pair performance qualification or reproduction of the long-lived multi-GB incident. ### Actual cron/pricing owner - **200 rate-compliant isolated failed cron runs:** post-GC heap **484.6/497.1/504.0/517.5/519.8 MB**. Late +2.28 MB over 48 runs exceeded the prewritten normalized investigation threshold. Its graph was inspected: mixed code/plain-object/map/string growth, without an established unbounded closed owner. There were 807 independent HTTP probes, no errors outside snapshots, maximum 139.4 ms. - Failure-only cron does not exercise billable pricing. A separate **56-success cohort** asserted nonzero recorded usage on every run and confirmed **four hot catalog publications** in the same process. NEW synthetic config omitted complete authored prices to avoid the documented direct-price fast path. Native allocation stacks actually reached **recordCronRunUsage → resolveModelCostConfig → resolveModelPricingContext → buildPricingContext**. - Validated eight-field pricing-context census: **2 at warm baseline, 4 after two reloads, 4 after four**. Qualified strong paths include live WeakMap keys/tables and lead to live WebSocket configuration, current context-window configuration, session-row publication configuration and remote-catalog environment data. No per-run accumulating pricing-context chain was established. Unknown ephemeron forms are excluded from reachability; object counts and positive path conclusions are separate. The first unpaced cron attempt hit the real 30-per-minute cron.run limit. Failed admission and a harness cleanup rejection were retained; only reconciled fixture-owned processes were stopped. The later cohort honored returned backoff and paced calls at least 2.2 seconds after the previous completed call. No quota, authority or configuration guard was disabled. ### Independent observation, not inferred freezes A separate process records its own cadence, controller heartbeat age, TCP connect/HTTP response times and WebSocket opening. A deliberate 3.5-second controller-only block left the Gateway responsive. Conversely, the recovery simulation below produced TCP success with HTTP/WS timeouts while the observer stayed on schedule. The pricing run caught a **13.8-second observer/probe-issuance gap before an HTTP request was sent**. Controller heartbeat age at observation was 808 ms; the next HTTP response took 1.76 ms and WS opening 2.70 ms. This is a coverage gap, not a measured Gateway response freeze. Its host/observer cause is unknown. It does not retroactively explain the earlier **28.1-second gap**; neither blind interval establishes continuous availability. ### Existing five-minute recovery through the built product This source already contains [#194481](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194481), commit [b4fe3d2655c401e8140d0a4ea1e62f38756f0f17](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b4fe3d2655c401e8140d0a4ea1e62f38756f0f17). It is an **existing mitigation**, not new production code in this PR. A normal built Gateway without inspector/profiling/coverage flags ACKed a plain input that reached a held provider and durably exposed a queued followup. A task-owned native-JavaScript stimulus then blocked its main thread with Atomics.wait. Independent observation recorded **144 TCP connects, 143 HTTP response timeouts and 60 WebSocket-opening timeouts**, cadence lag ≤3.96 ms. The packaged observer wrote its real **300,000 ms** recovery fact and killed its own process after **300,067 ms**; the external harness did not trigger that initial kill. The same-state successor produced **one actual resumed agent turn and final reply**, retained original input and left crash-queued input cancelled/unexecuted. Later idle restarts did not duplicate continuation. This uses current-principal crash recovery, not old-execution replay or a guarantee of exactly-once external effects. Fixture qualifications remain explicit: initial successor history read preceded per-agent admission; the supported 250 ms retry continued the SAME state without repeating the five-minute block. A raw request counter included an Activity-recap utility call; its instruction/route and the Gateway's resumed:1 fact identified only one actual agent resume. The stimulus IPC listener initially kept already-shutdown children alive; unrefing that private channel produced two subsequent idle Gateway exits with code 0. Original failures were retained, not relabeled passing. This proves deterministic blocked-main recovery—not prevention or attribution of either reported cause. Safe RPC restart still requires a responsive Gateway; ordinary native-supervisor restart has different owner checks. The original historical restart command/refusal is unspecified. **Pinned stable-source inspection:** at v2026.11.1 commit [4ffdd2047d192dd65554de3c8c46c0e0197c6e2a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4ffdd2047d192dd65554de3c8c46c0e0197c6e2a/src/logging/diagnostic-stall-flight-recorder.ts) and v2026.11.2 commit [b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce/src/logging/diagnostic-stall-flight-recorder.ts), the complete retrieved recorder owner is **5,050 bytes** and does not create the kernel recorder or terminal SIGKILL recovery owner. Retrieved recovery documentation also lacks that terminal path. Kernel/observer path absence was corroboration, not the sole basis. No installed-release replay was performed; the first stable release containing #194481 was not established. title: fix(pr): recover published corrections with pending baseline proof
body:
Related: #193872

## What Problem This Solves

Published corrections can become stuck when newly incorporated canonical main history has signers not trusted locally and required proof still prevents READY.

## User Impact

Maintainers can explicitly produce a signed proof-baseline descendant through the native owner without editing signer trust, rewriting the retained candidate, or falsely qualifying unresolved proof. The new candidate still requires its own exact-source review and proof authorization; ordinary qualification and merge retain their gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuation now excludes only an authenticated signed native baseline also proven to belong to the invocation's private canonical-main checkpoint. All other new commits on every parent remain signature-checked. Ordinary unbound merges receive no exemption.

The explicit proof-purpose producer retains the actual older-preparation/newer-publication lifecycle through the existing materializer, receipt chain, signed version-2 purpose binding and transition journal. title: fix(discord): restore extension package declaration builds
body:
Related: #195437

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord extension declaration emission failing in the scheduled main package-boundary check after #195437.

## User Impact

Restores the extension package build check. There is no user-visible runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The readiness fixture returns its mocked runtime through the Discord test API. Inferring that object exposes Vitest's private `Procedure` type, which native declaration emission cannot name portably. Annotate the object with the existing public `RuntimeEnv` contract; the same mocks and readiness behavior remain in place.

title: fix(android): keep model names during temporary catalog gaps
body:
Closes #195456

Related: #192252 (delayed-picker behavior is not addressed).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android's composer replaces a known model name such as `Beta` with the raw ID `beta` when the catalog temporarily clears, even though the selected model has not changed.

## User Impact

The unchanged selection keeps its familiar name during disconnects and catalog gaps. Fresh catalog metadata replaces that name; changing Gateway, agent, session, or model clears it. Model selection, availability, eligibility, and request ordering remain unchanged.

**Validation limitation — native visual proof remains incomplete.** Local compilation, lint, focused tests, and red/green regression results have now been reported passing; real Android/Gateway before-and-after evidence is still outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a display-only name in the existing composer, keyed by its existing Gateway/agent/session owner and the selected model reference. The current catalog still owns model choices and capabilities. An authoritative blank name clears the remembered name rather than reviving an old alias.

title: feat: custom registry icons for plugin panel tabs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin panel tabs and picker entries all use the same plug icon, making installed features difficult to distinguish at a glance.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can choose an existing Control UI registry icon alongside each panel’s label. Existing plugins keep the plug icon, unknown names safely fall back to it, and manifest-provided SVG artwork continues to take precedence. No manifest changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An optional `icon` field on `ControlUiPanel` reuses the host’s fixed icon registry and shared panel definitions, so tabs and desktop/mobile pickers stay consistent without loading new assets. One typed own-key guard serves panel and navigation icon selection, rejecting inherited names such as `constructor` without duplicate checks or unsafe casts. The existing header memo now tracks icon-only changes.

## Evidence

Eight example browser plugins register panels through the production activation and `host.ui.registerPanel` path. Five request distinct icons; the other three exercise omitted, unknown, and inherited-name fallbacks. The same fixture and viewport reproduce identical plug icons on the base and differentiated icons after the change.

- **Final exact-head CI passed:** [run 42618183870](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42618183870), head `d1817f82ae2bf65fb29872ede6b089472bcd0883`. The assertion, test-line and performance gates pass; no budget increase or inherited-failure exception was used.
- Focused final validation: UI types, lint and assertion-safety pass; 19 consumer unit tests pass (4.03 seconds invocation), including the icon-only Layout-menu regression. title: fix(subagents): preserve paused tasks across requester notices
body:
Related: [#195387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195387)

**Merged as [924a3bc9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/924a3bc9ffb3d359fc3a8709768ef0e2fa305d91). All 29 affected cases pass on tested head `bda867dc`.**

## What Problem This Solves

A requester notice could prematurely fail a paused subagent and lose a retained send after plugin reload. A child could also wait indefinitely after its requester finished: same-task adoption changed the run ID, or a later ordinary turn replaced the completed session row before the sweeper read it.

## User Impact

Keep paused children alive across unrelated notices and close their message waits when the owning requester task finishes, including after same-task continuation or a later ordinary request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe committed session publications instead of raw model-end events. Existing completion custody tracks the requester's completion separately from its original execution receipt. Unclaimed message waits stay with the requester session across ordinary turns. Only a real continuation claim binds the wait to a requester task; the sweeper requires that binding before treating a terminal turn as task completion. Same-task adoption advances that tracking. Accepted terminal bookkeeping records the matching requester's completion before publishing the runtime notification, so later session rows cannot erase it. A real new claim resets the accounting; same-task custody refresh preserves it. Existing live permission and settlement checks remain. No schema, configuration, or public API change.

The existing index class moved unchanged to a sibling module to meet the memory file's line cap. Its five instances and state remain with the original owner. The reload fixture preserves the primary setup exception after cleanup, reports nested causes and relative path diagnostics, and selects its bound temporary root inside the child before scenario imports; the real consumer witness and success checks remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- The unchanged timed requester regression fails on [head `1b4bbdc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42795908804/job/129762178744): a real watched-send claim remains bound to R after ordinary U finishes, but the child stays paused through the full five-second completion wait. On [repair `9abec1258c7c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42798673648/job/129771201823), all five real Gateway cases pass, including this case and same-task adopted requester completion. Closure, lifecycle fencing, and subsequent admission assertions pass. Earlier invalid fixture attempts are superseded by this red/green pair.
- All five requester cases pass again on [final bda867dc, job129815883767](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42811850233/job/129815883767), including real claimed completion before/after parking, retained completion after a later ordinary turn, and adopted requester execution. These are exact-head results; closure, lifecycle fencing and subsequent admission assertions remain.
- The adopted-requester defect also has [pre-fix proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42661219953/job/129314133953). All [19 yielded-settlement cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42798673648/job/129771201749) pass on `9abec1258c7c`.
- Build, ratchets, docs, architecture, lint, production types, and test types pass on [exact bda867dc CI42811850233](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42811850233). Local formatting, docs inventory, diff/privacy checks, and native commit hooks pass. Local runtime/full lint remain unavailable in the dependency-free checkout; hosted results supply those checks. The isolated test-line allocation is exactly284:291 added regression/diagnostic lines offset by7 lines removed when consolidating the completion-order fixture around real watched claims. No test cases are removed. Completion-order rows acquire actual claims; restored done-state rows require continued pause without execution authority.
- The original reload regression is now green on [exact head bda867dc, job129815883831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42811850233/job/129815883831): the owned-process wrapper verifies all three real scenarios (resume, followup, failed-reload), their proof reports and the actual consumer witness. Both allowed/revoked retained-send sibling cases pass in the same job. The [50c9097 diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42809333743/job/129807501322) demonstrate the pre-fix requester-finished settlement and no-paused-child errors. The final correction requires a real continuation claim before a terminal requester turn can close a wait. No original product assertion or isolation check is weakened.
- All [19 yielded-settlement cases pass on bda867dc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42811850233/job/129815883847), including restored unclaimed waits surviving completed turns with no revived execution.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete range 3a48d6f3 → 9abec1258c7c, then incremental ranges 9abc → c092 → f8a053c2 → 81e6d395 → 50c9097c1ea0; all completed with no actionable correctness or security findings. The 50c9097 → d3e6d081 review found two restored-wait test expectations inconsistent with the session-bound contract; those cases now assert retained pause, no outcome, intact writer fence and no revived execution. Missing-session and lost-descendant closure checks remain. The d3e6d081 → bda867dc corrective test range then completed with no actionable findings. Fresh independent source reviews passed the production repairs, fixture correction, diagnostics and both final corrective deltas. These are source reviews. Earlier runtime/static results are prior-head proof; the final correction has exact-head reload, revocation and settlement proof; all affected runtime cases pass and native qualification is complete. CodeQL, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep and Workflow Sanity passed on bda867dc; skipped Security Review is recorded as skipped.
- The separate required-visible-spawn assertion still matches [current main evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42790739830/job/129743799287) at the same test and line. It is an inherited failure, not a passing check. Earlier formatting failures are green on `9abec1258c7c`.
- Queued focused Blacksmith Testbox attempts were stopped and settled without payload execution. No active task-owned allocation or provider change remains. Proof continues through normal PR CI.

Simplification: remove the spawn-time completion fallback and obsolete direct fixture mode; retain one completion owner and one watched-claim fixture. Against source base3a48d6f3, production source is +140/-68 (including the unchanged index extraction), tests +345/-61 (net284), docs +8/-4. Against50c9097, the corrective test delta is net-7 lines.

Native qualification and squash landing are complete. All three PostgreSQL groups also passed. The inherited visible-spawn failure was admitted through the documented native exception, with the failed CI result preserved. The receipt verified the actual landed parent after main advanced during admission. [Native completion and audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195420#issuecomment-6777010291).

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize deliberate, single-touch upward gestures in the shared toast presentation and use its existing dismissal callback. title: fix: avoid Doctor and Gateway failures during NFS snapshot cleanup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor and Gateway startup failures when NFS leaves busy SQLite snapshot cleanup directories behind, while preserving best-effort candidate update checks.

Fixes #195396.

## User Impact

Verified snapshots can finish with a cleanup warning when NFS retains a busy directory. Doctor/Gateway preflight and strict snapshot callers still surface genuine cleanup failures. Candidate checks log cleanup hiccups separately, preserving their successful result or original read error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Close the published target before removing staging. Recognize regular `.nfs*` aliases and defer only classified final-removal `EBUSY`/`ENOTEMPTY` after private snapshot retirement. Keep identity, content, integrity, publication, and backup validation intact.

Related: #162979

## What Problem This Solves

People cannot inspect saved roles and configured permission ceilings from the current Control UI.

## User Impact

Adds read-only **People** and **Roles** views under **Settings → People & permissions**, plus canonical **saved-role assignments** and **View permissions** in both sidebar and transcript person activity cards. Summarizes configured agent, session, sandbox, scope, model and access-policy limits separately from the viewer’s own negotiated grants. Guests remain self-scoped; nothing assigns roles or grants access. No migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the canonical profile directory, applied configuration reader, and Gateway-provided effective roles and assignment sources. Profile changes retire obsolete reads, and open views load policy when read access becomes available. Query decoding stays behind the page’s lazy boundary; shared settings components own selection styling.

This Solid implementation completes the original read-only inspection proposal: canonical saved assignments in activity cards and searchable People/Roles views with understandable configured ceilings. It does not modify the older draft, add role management/invitations, grant access, or introduce another authorization owner.

## Evidence

### Current HTTP fixture readiness correction — 072ec460

Head **072ec4609b5991540d6039e50397510ce3075262**, tree **9f0191ffcf602dc23269704de4006fc87f91dfd4**, directly follows 6fb. This two-file correction prepares the required canonical Control UI HTTP module inside the configured fixture lifetime before declaring startup complete; it does not restore the unused full Gateway test harness. Its real-return initialization-order regression rejects initialization after the fixture's single authoritative startup flag changes. Production HTTP/auth/state code is unchanged. The initial maintenance response still precedes runtime readiness and app bytes; all three original HTTP assertion bodies, routes/query/hash, 6s recovery-request deadline, 20s poll and 180s hook remain unchanged. No permanent artificial delay, wire logging, transport replacement or fake response was added.

**Actual preceding CI failure:** [6fb UI2/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43149691374/job/130956327465) executed the second case and retained the maintenance document at its existing 20s poll (expected0, observed1). This is not the historical beforeAll timeout. The bounded retained CI tail does not establish the other two case outcomes. Source binding was checked against actual tested merge 1f0791050c2763cb9fc856a09f458ca9240fabc5 and comparison 305e5676447fd2edc7a0c82e8fae369bb60c0660. The verified plan selected905 UI files, assigned this fixture to the151-file UI2/7 route at index82, with no production-fixture reuse. Local causal runs used Node24.22.1, four CPUs/workers and worker-cache enabled, with a bounded four-file same-group cohort—not a full cached-shard replay.

**Wire-boundary red/green:** an unforced local control observed the first ready HTML fetch taking about5.83s against its unchanged6s abort, including4.911s real module initialization. Holding only that real module's initialization for25s reproduced the exact second-case20s failure: browser fetches aborted around6.996s and14.996s, another retry began18.996s, and maintenance remained through19.947s with no ready response delivered. Default statusCode200 on an aborted, unended server response was not counted as a delivered200. The original full-harness fixture also failed under the same controlled ordering; restoring it is not a readiness guarantee. These are controlled mechanism proofs, not a claim that CI incurred an actual25s module delay or that this explains the earlier180s hook timeout.

The new no-delay initialization-order regression is red without preparation. With preparation and the same temporary25s gate, all three real HTTP cases and all three cohort sibling files pass: first ready HTML200 at+1.845s, replacement-document navigation at+1.861s, maintenance absent at+1.963s. Final native source, without the temporary gate/probes, passes3/3 in82.566s. Required module work is honestly paid in preparation; no new total-speed or percentile claim is made. title: feat: let agents manage personal session groups
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Guests cannot ask their agent to organize the personal collections they already use in the sidebar.

## User Impact

Agents can read, create, rename, reorder, and remove the current person's collections. Signed-in guests with session-write access now synchronize **only personal collections** through their own profile; their other preferences remain browser-local. Existing profile-scoped browser layouts are adopted before remote collections are applied. Independent changes merge; conflicting edits to the same collection retain the local layout with an error instead of overwriting either copy. Read-only and profileless connections keep browser-local behavior.

Shared groups, session metadata, project defaults, and access grants are unchanged. Agent operations still require the current person's own single-participant Control UI turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing preference and compare-and-swap owners for both the sidebar and agent. The old guest browser-local policy made an agent's server-only snapshot incomplete; this revision explicitly cuts over personal collections without importing unrelated preferences. One shared normalizer serves every caller. Existing queue composition and saved confirmation handle overlapping edits and older queued layouts. Write-only profile operations stay with the existing write owner rather than loading with profile reads. There is no new database schema, permission store, configuration option, or broader role grant.

## Evidence

### Current supported-owner refresh — November 11

Published managed head: `a956e05ae968aa4961cb780d5a57adb729962cbe`. Actual integrated main: `da5333972ac13a707e0003fcd6e423d479a7a6ad`; verified source tree: `b37f83a0dd13374b5e1272441f8929a71c87bc39`.

The original publishing owner used the supported current-main base-refresh operation, with no conflicts. This supersedes the earlier attempt to import a pinned tree through protected sandbox mounts. Those earlier partial imports were recovered; no protected mount, Git guard, budget, assertion, role grant or publication identity was changed.

Compared with the handoff's main reference ae651f1, current main changes 57 paths, including upstream CLI/context/workspace maintenance and Chat geometry/style work. None overlaps the 35 feature paths. The actual base-relative feature has exactly the same ordered added/deleted text as the prepared b87145c reference (SHA-256 67d5fff4da8d4ff5fda43e32af266d9c3c1a98f87dd62a6d466116d9b009e30b). No extra feature behavior or test allocation was added. The handoff's current-main conflict resolutions and upstream fixes therefore remain represented without copying a foreign tree or freezing an outdated base.

On this refreshed source, all **54 collection/navigation cases across four files**, canonical production UI typechecking, and the base-relative whitespace check pass. These are current local results using Node 24.20.0, not hosted-runtime parity or a new model/Gateway proof run. The accepted earlier behavior/authority/upgrade evidence below is reused for the unchanged feature.

The first canonical paired-wrapper attempt stopped before compilation when its source archive exhausted the inherited 1 GiB /tmp filesystem; that setup failure is retained, not called a product regression. A supported local comparison then used an admitted baseline source archive under owned workspace scratch, frozen dependencies without lifecycle hooks, and both normal production-UI build wrappers with the same deterministic comparison settings. Selected Vite, Rolldown, Pako and Solid entry bytes match between the two installs. The existing canonical performance checker with --base-dist exits **0**: Startup JS 91,847 → 91,908 B (limit 92,137), Chat boot 1,302,666 → 1,303,184 B (limit 1,303,711), and **New Session 803,969 → 804,439 B (limit 805,886)**. Both builds exit 0. CSS totals are identical (326,931 B gzip / 1,686,650 B raw), preserving inherited-baseline advisories rather than claiming those fixed debts vanished. No thresholds, checker code, assertions or TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP settings changed. These are local Node 24.20.0 results, not exact hosted Node 24.22.1 parity. The handoff's successful Node 24.22.2 comparison against ae651f1 remains separately historical; these local measurements do not replace the exact-head hosted result recorded below.

Current exact-head hosted CI on `a956e05ae968aa4961cb780d5a57adb729962cbe`: the [required `openclaw/ci-gate` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43078157139/job/130732862368), [aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` context](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43080932260), and [Control UI performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43078157139/job/130724380705) are explicitly terminal **SUCCESS**. This is fresh published-head hosted evidence, distinct from the local checks and historical red runs below. The bounded reader exposes 100 of 134 entries; this records the required aggregate and performance contexts, not an exhaustive all-jobs inventory. No CI rerun, merge, or deployment was performed.

### Earlier November 11 local readiness reference

Earlier prepared candidate: `b87145c447f402d04f7e8246084cac7c564a9e47`, integrating main `ae651f116c7713295d6969b36bb1762ee0196edc` to reuse the upstream boot-path work, including #196320. This is a clean merge: the 35-file feature delta has identical added/deleted lines before and after integration. No additional production behavior, test allocation, budget, or exception was introduced.

The complete prior failed job log is now available: its actual violation was **New Session boot JS**, 803,475 B against 803,364 B, a +163 B candidate/base difference. Chat passed at +55 B; unchanged inherited CSS excess was advisory. This supersedes the earlier truncated-log uncertainty, not the recorded failed run.

On the new candidate, the unchanged canonical paired checker passes against exact main `ae651f116c7713295d6969b36bb1762ee0196edc` with Node 24.22.2, Vite 8.3.5 and Pako 3.0.3:

| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,302,253 B | 1,302,628 B | 1,303,711 B |

title: fix(update): restore LaunchAgent registration after repair contention
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update repair` can leave its macOS LaunchAgent unloaded when restoration encounters a Gateway listener outside launchd supervision.

Fixes #195379.

## User Impact

Gateway respawn entry points refuse an active offline-maintenance owner, and preserved-definition LaunchAgent restoration reloads the job after a restart preflight failure. The original busy-port error remains visible, with the job registered for launchd to retry. Unknown listeners are not adopted or signaled by the recovery path.

**Evidence gap:** the reported detached process's launcher is still unproven. This is a bounded repair, not end-to-end proof of the incident. A restart helper scheduled before maintenance and the stop-to-admission interval remain uncovered. Live macOS reproduction with the app running/suspended is MISSING.

## Why This Change Was Made

`respawnGatewayProcessForUpdate` is the direct detached-Gateway creator that preserves service environment variables. Both that entry point and fresh-PID restart scheduling now consult the existing live state owner immediately before creating a successor or handoff. Normal app service hosting routes through launchd; the restart sentinel delivers work after startup. Source inspection does not establish which path created the reporter's PID.

Preserved-definition restart preflight failures now use the existing LaunchAgent compensation helper, which previously covered only later activation failures. It retains caller authority and native-cleanup checks, preserves the definition/autostart policy, and reports bootstrap failure if registration cannot be restored. No schema or configuration change is required. The running Gateway and restoring CLI must contain the fix.

The related stop-during-restart fix is on main as `6eb7eb5d3351` and in 2026.11.2 as cherry-pick `30f14bde6a8d`. It does not prove this detached/unloaded incident fixed; 2026.11.2 does not contain the changes in this PR.
