title: fix: Telegram restart recovery leaves final replies silent
body:
Related: #141959
Complements: #190006

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a completed Telegram reply can remain unconfirmed after a Gateway restart, while recovery refuses to resend it and the chat receives no explanation until another message arrives.

## User Impact

User impact: when durable final-reply recovery stops, the Gateway immediately hands the existing uncertainty notice to lifecycle delivery in the original chat, rather than waiting for another inbound message. It does not resend an ambiguous answer. Notice delivery remains bounded and can itself fail if the channel stays unavailable; existing route, lifecycle, and permission checks remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared completion owner already records notice debt for an unknown pending final, but only the next inbound turn consumed that debt. Terminal queue recovery now invokes that same notice owner after persisted failed custody and before compacting its recovery checkpoint. An exact-intent check prevents an earlier failure from delivering a successor's notice. The existing process-local live-custody Set is shared through an import-free leaf, so notice recovery does not depend on the turn dispatcher. The failed-completion projection and conditional exact-intent notice handoff form one sibling operation; the queue owner still persists failed custody before awaiting it and compacts only afterward.

This is a complementary residual repair, not a replacement for @sukhdeepjohar's #190006: elapsed flood-budget accounting and wholly-unsent 429 retry classification stay in that PR. No ambiguous-send replay, new queue, schema, configuration, retry-limit, retention, or permission change is introduced.

These are Gateway-owned lifecycle notices, not continued execution under the original model caller. The current Gateway instance authorizes the transport and checks dispatch availability again after provider queue waits; stored route and intent IDs select the debt, not the sending authority. Queued retries use the existing delivery-recovery service admission. This PR does not introduce an original-caller revocation policy.

## Evidence

- **CI repair:** [original architecture job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42520732359/job/128853890254) exposed one introduced Madge cycle on `5703e6f0d85f2d00832c40dabf4190c0ccec6297` (runtime cycles: 0). The canonical commands reproduced it. Moving the existing live-custody registry to a single import-free leaf removes that dependency; `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` now both report **0 cycles**, without lazy-import avoidance, ignores, or a baseline waiver. The complete old-head check set had no other primary failure; its CI-gate failure was aggregate.
- **Line-cap disposition and repair:** On reviewed head `c1d953b2e0f28548792531d16514bf53c9d03774`, [run 42522325771, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522325771/job/128858756181) records `1251 → 1260` as a **warning**, with `[ok] line-cap`; test-lines is the failing ratchet. The CI failure must not be attributed independently to line-cap. However, the same canonical **local** comparator rejects the introduced growth (exit 1). The complete completion-projection-and-notice phase is now extracted into `delivery-queue-failure-completion.ts`, preserving evidence selection, awaited ordering, exact intent, and error propagation. The exact frozen CI merge/base comparator (`da6fbbc3…` against `465c110…`, private index) and the original authoring-base comparator (`a5888561…`) both pass. Runtime and Madge remain at 0 cycles; no compression, ignore, or baseline increase was used.
- **Prior-head architecture:** [the repaired architecture job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522325771/job/128858756016) passes on `c1d953b2e0f28548792531d16514bf53c9d03774`. Other current-head CI is reported separately.
- **Inherited budget hold (prior-head CI snapshot):** On `c1d953b2e0f28548792531d16514bf53c9d03774`, [test-line ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522325771/job/128858756181) failed with 92 lines over the ceiling. The frozen base `465c110e4975690406b48709d58a581756c85b82` already has 6,586,426 test lines against a 6,586,334 ceiling (92 inherited debt; delta 0). The exact CI merge `da6fbbc3d1958be2dff0a180ef0a485dc2d57012` adds this PR's 326 lines and its exact 326-line allocation: 6,586,752 against 6,586,660, still the same 92 debt. The canonical checker reproduces both snapshots through private indexes without changing the worktree. The grant has not been inflated and the shared baseline is unchanged; base-debt reconciliation or explicit budget-owner approval is required. This prior snapshot is not being reported as passing CI or as the new head’s CI result.
- **Authority boundary:** the real Telegram HTTP sender test that closes the Gateway while a notice waits behind a serialized account request passes: retiring that lifecycle principal prevents the notice from reaching HTTP. This is evidence for the existing Gateway-owned sender contract, not a claim that the original ingress caller remains the notice principal.
- **Red on base `a5888561dd`:** real Telegram HTTP transport plus durable queue recovery produced no notice; the original answer was not retried. A full isolated Gateway also reproduced the issue through an inbound Telegram DM, a completed agent/model turn, a Bot API 429, SIGKILL during the flood wait, and a new process on the same disk state. After the existing 60-second send lease expired, recovery logged `send_attempt_started; refusing blind replay` and the expected notice never arrived.
- **Green with this repair:** the same cold-process flow delivered the existing uncertainty notice once, with one attempted original answer and no ambiguous-answer replay. After the settlement extraction, the E2E case was rerun and took 69.6 seconds (111.8 seconds Vitest; 286.2 seconds including runtime preparation). Process replacement, refusal, and delivered chat text are asserted by the test.
- Real Telegram HTTP regressions cover an ambiguous response and exhausted proven-no-send recovery, repeat-drain deduplication, and no answer replay. The notice-owner unit regression covers successor-intent isolation. Both focused files pass.
- Existing recovery, producer-recovery, and pending-notice integration suites: **64 passed** across three files before the dependency-only extraction (96.8 seconds Vitest). After extraction, the affected custody, notice, notice-integration, and real Telegram HTTP suites were rerun: **37 passed** across four files (38.3 and 10.4 seconds across the two Vitest shards).
- After the settlement extraction, **75 affected tests passed** across queue recovery, producer recovery, notice integration, and real Telegram HTTP suites (122.9 seconds Vitest; 127.7 seconds including preparation). Targeted type graphs `core`, `core-test-messaging`, and `test-root-other` pass; targeted lint, format, and `git diff --check` pass. The runtime build used by the E2E runner completed successfully. Hosted CI for the updated head is separate from these local gate results.
- Local Auto Review (P0–P2) found no findings for the original candidate `a5888561dd11438c28591ac57e5951ae1c8e13ce` → `1ac02e7b6ef9e8ccca0e9879983b9b0ee6587e44`, and for the dependency repair `1ac02e7b6ef9e8ccca0e9879983b9b0ee6587e44` → `73a0a93ce92216ce1c1ea1e168d3527fa83e4207`. A fresh P0–P2 Auto Review also found no findings for the settlement extraction `73a0a93ce92216ce1c1ea1e168d3527fa83e4207` → `b0db290d2d899be44d8fe5e1dfda89cb65f45251`. The published repair tree matches that tested/reviewed candidate.
- Simplification: reuses the existing completion, notice, and lifecycle delivery owners; no parallel state or machinery. The live-custody Set has one owner and the superseded custody-module export is removed, not re-exported. The extracted operation owns the entire failed completion projection and conditional notice handoff, not just a renamed forwarding call. Production delta is +66/-20 lines; the +326 regression lines have an exact task-specific test-line allocation. The longer E2E case protects the real process/crash boundary that the faster HTTP test cannot prove.

Proof uses a scripted OpenAI-compatible model and a loopback Bot API with the real Gateway, agent runtime, grammY adapter, limiter, and SQLite queue. No real Telegram messages or live external-model calls were made. This proves the controlled restart/recovery path, not Telegram's external flood-control behavior.

Reported by @KritTone, with an additional incident trace from @Veda-openclaw. Complements the useful partial repair by @sukhdeepjohar. Co-authored with Jason O'Neal.

title: fix(zai): Coding Plan setup rejects retained catalog models
body:
Related: #164327

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Z.AI Coding Plan model resolution reports “Unknown model” when fallback reuses a retained general-API catalog row after discovery is unavailable.

## User Impact

The selected Global or CN Coding Plan endpoint remains usable during fallback. General API, custom proxy, and authored model-level endpoint routes retain their behavior. No configuration, schema, credential precedence, or shared transport guard changes.

This addresses the residual catalog-route failure, not every historical onboarding symptom: the reasoning-token probe failure was separately fixed by #193467. Full source-Gateway setup and chat qualification now passes with deterministic external HTTP responses. Actual Z.AI account entitlement and live service behavior are not claimed. The five-case saved-connection install-over matrix below passes, with explicit manual-install, numeric-version, Doctor, and external-service limitations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider keeps retained model metadata but binds its returned fallback to the selected connection endpoint. It does not mutate the registry row or weaken native route admission. Explicit model-level routes continue through the existing core owner.

Author simplification retained one provider-owned correction, no new helpers, state, or fallback implementation. Production net +5 lines; docs +3; regression +92 lines with an exact dedicated test-line allocation for native route admission, model overrides, and retained-row immutability.

Thanks to @nina-grech for the report and @zjshenxyz for the catalog-fallback diagnosis. Prepared at Jason O’Neal’s request.

## Evidence

- Pinned base: `a5888561dd11438c28591ac57e5951ae1c8e13ce`. Real bundled Z.AI plugin plus `resolveModelAsync`, actual retained manifest catalog and native route admission: both Coding Plan regions fail on base with “Unknown model”; general/custom controls pass.
- Fixed resolver regression: **5/5 passed**, covering GLM-5.3 and Flash, both Coding Plan regions, general/custom controls, explicit model-level routing, and unchanged retained catalog rows. Final wrapper wall time 9.80s; test bodies 53ms combined. Compiler preparation is separate. CI seconds pending.
- Existing plugin/onboarding suites: **13/13 passed**; combined selected wrapper run including the prior four-case resolver regression passed 17 tests across three files.
- Production package leaf typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/zai/tsconfig.json --noEmit` passed.
- Regression typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json --noEmit` passed after correcting complete authored model fixtures.
- Touched-file lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and staged test-line ratchet passed.
- Independent bound Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, local candidate against the pinned base, P0–P2) reviewed all four files and relevant unchanged owners: **scoped-clean, no findings**. Checks were not independently rerun by the reviewer.
- **Real isolated source-Gateway qualification at `c6cfb96d8eca4ae6d88d2c8ebab7bb2269335ba9`:** authenticated `users.self` → `openclaw.setup.activate.start` (`zai-coding-global`) → `wizard.next` activation → `openclaw.setup.verify` (`ok: true`) → `sessions.create` → `chat.send` → `agent.wait` → readable `chat.history`. The created session belongs to the fixture-authenticated operator. All three assembled setup/readiness/chat requests used `POST https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4/chat/completions`, `glm-5.3`, and the resolved synthetic bearer credential—not its profile ID. The retained registry row kept its general-API URL before and after the successful, non-rerouted turn. **1/1 passed**, 50.46 seconds overall / 12.655 seconds test body; compiled-worker receipt `990a0bcb6bb6` verified before cleanup.
- Gateway qualification used the repository-supported global-fetch seam only for external HTTP responses, not mocked setup, routing, admission, agent, or Gateway decisions. fix(test): wait for guest dictation catalog publication
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the guest-dictation WebSocket test failing before its first catalog RPC returns on a cold CI worker. [Scheduled main run 42514980580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42514980580/job/128836211666) failed with `Dictation catalog did not become ready: undefined` and `Timed out in waitFor!`.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The regression keeps the same guest authorization, revocation, and exact catalog payload coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The five-second polling deadline wrapped an RPC with its own ten-second timeout. Replace polling with the existing catalog refresh root release observer, as used by provider-discovery tests: assert the cold warming response, await publication, then read and assert the ready catalog once. No timeout increases, retry loops, assertion weakening, or baseline changes. Production delta: zero; net test lines: zero.

The flaky synchronization was introduced by `14d9d554f7d04b0c036c543ff2c2b4592faf958c` in #193658. #194612 records an earlier matching failure but explicitly leaves dictation unchanged; it does not own this repair.

## Evidence

- Touched-file lint with `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`: passed.
- Touched-file oxfmt and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Codex autoreview of the local change against `44662c4c196431fdabf9ae3b1ddae62368f6857d`, including catalog/admission owner sources: scoped-clean for P0–P2. The reviewer confirmed that snapshot publication precedes root release. No remaining actionable findings.

The attempted run took 24.21 seconds; this is not runtime proof of the fix. The original CI failure is the red evidence; local red/green proof is unavailable.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: read-only Gateway queries show an unexplained filesystem permission error when an installed-release query is invoked through the source-development runner in a nonwritable tree.

## User Impact

Operators receive guidance to use the installed CLI instead of mistaking build-artifact preparation failure for missing Gateway permissions. The command still fails safely; permissions, artifact freshness checks, immutable-release refusals, and lock placement do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explain `EACCES` and `EROFS` where source-runner lock creation fails, preserving the filesystem error as the cause and retaining its error code. Qualify existing repository CLI guidance and clarify the installed lookup in the users and setup documentation. No new runtime prompt directive, automatic fallback, or installation repair is introduced.

The regression verifies the recovery guidance, preserved error code/cause, nonzero exit, and absence of lock/build output. Its immutable-release negative control retains the existing refusal before lock creation. On the base, the permission row fails because the diagnostic is absent while the immutable row passes.

### Self-contained reproduction driver

Use a POSIX nonroot account, a source checkout containing the published six-file candidate and Git base object above, and already-prepared frozen dependencies. This driver installs nothing and changes no tracked source. Save it as capture_pr195374.py, then run:

```bash
python3 capture_pr195374.py "$PR_SOURCE" "$PR_SOURCE/.openclaw/tmp/pr195374-independent-capture"
```

The output directory must not already exist. The baseline overlay contains exact Git entry/owner bytes and shares unchanged, verified imports; the immutable/permission fixtures are independent of that overlay. Source/module byte mismatches, missing expected OS errors, altered inventories, observer outcome changes or unexpected commit paths make the driver fail.

body:
Related: #167078

## What Problem This Solves

Repairs two demonstrated failure paths: a throwing reply-cleanup callback can strand session reset or shut down the Gateway, and a rollover drain timeout can be mislabeled as an LLM timeout in the persisted session row.

## User Impact

Cleanup exceptions remain visible while later releases and safe resets can complete. A genuine rollover timeout now says that previous work has not settled and tells the user to check completed work before retrying, rather than blaming the model. Original diagnostics remain recorded. The existing 15-second drain bound, writer and delivery settlement, configuration, and stored schema are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The after-clear loop stopped at the first synchronous callback exception, skipping later releases and immediate owner settlement; deferred flushing could become an unhandled rejection. The existing listener-notification helper reports each exception and continues unrelated callbacks without releasing their resources early.

The additional investigation traced the misleading row text through real Gateway dispatch-error persistence into the generic failover-copy renderer: an Error prefix plus a timeout phrase manufactured “LLM request timed out.” Both saved failure copy and the row renderer now share a narrow recognition of the existing rollover diagnostic before provider timeout formatting. This does not change provider fallback classification or add replay, force release, or a longer timeout.

## Evidence

This is an incomplete capture—not proof that it passed, did not execute, or had zero refusals. No extra diagnostic iteration was run. The temporary module/import was removed, and both closure owners were revalidated as recorded above.

This revision is **diagnostic only, not a bootstrap fix**. After the existing guard has already refused, a test-runtime-only probe copies passive cached/admitted version and catalog facts, then reads bounded physical version/catalog metadata and metadata/lease-row-existence booleans on that SAME connection and transaction, before rollback. It neither refreshes admissions nor initializes, repairs, retries, changes custody, or reads arbitrary user rows. Catalog identifiers are capped with truncation counters; the path is hashed. The exact outer Error/message is retained, with a bounded JSON Error cause carried by the unchanged worker codec. Test-owned phase labels precede the existing awaits and rethrow the identical error without reordering cleanup.

Local diagnostic contract verification reused the existing negative preservation case: the added cause assertion failed on the uninstrumented guard (1 failed; wrapper 42.38 seconds), then passed 1/1 with the probe (40.02 seconds), including encode → structured clone → hydrate, exact outer Error/message, bounded cause, raw version/catalog, and unchanged database header/catalog/seeded rows/no credential-store creation. This intentionally malformed negative control is NOT a reproduction of the hosted abort failure. The temporary local assertion extension is retained as proof, not committed as a budget exemption. Core production types pass; source type-aware lint, format and whitespace pass; the unchanged test-line ceiling passes at 6,664,638/6,664,639 (one line slack). Native independent Auto Review against eab56ca0 assessed the diagnostic delta at P0–P2 and found no actionable findings; it did not execute target code. The later lint repair only adds required braces. Supplemental complexity/duplication/mutation CLIs are unavailable and were not measured or installed.

Only ONE new-head hosted diagnostic run was performed. Its actual head/base/synthetic checkout and adverse results are retained above. The requested phase/cause execution region was not recovered; no nonrejection or root-cause conclusion is inferred. Temporary diagnostic code has been removed, and the final published tree requires its own fresh CI. No merge or deployment.

title: fix(ui): preserve selected agent when opening new tabs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prevents an older cached sidebar from overriding the selected agent view in a newly opened conversation. The conflicting-cache behavior is reproduced, including a controlled real-menu selection path. The exact trigger for the user's recent onset is not established.

## User Impact

The chosen agent/roster mode stays selected during warm startup and after the live connection takes over. Matching cached sidebars still restore normally; an incompatible cached view is skipped rather than changing the user's selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The saved preference can already be correct while the sidebar displays the wrong mode. The cached presentation overrode that preference, and cache admission did not compare the two modes. Read the mode only from the existing live preference owner, and require a matching mode when admitting or retaining a snapshot.

Historical source comparison shows that [#168206](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168206), in [561d92d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/561d92da3a286857c25d9ec508095d8ee4dc14da), added the snapshot mode override and permissive admission condition. This identifies the old mechanism, not a proven cause of the recent onset. The relevant source in the report-time deployment (`ef1b8b2`) matches the tested base (`3d6914a`). Recent-candidate investigation did not establish an introducing PR or author for the reported incident; the later deployment was not used as incident evidence.

## Evidence

Independent Tempbook verification compares current main `1007cb9e5cdfbcc01227a012dc2cf1efe13d4480` with exact candidate `c99d3df28cc63493d532c7cb4c3841130477e287`.

- Real isolated Gateway, production UI, synthetic agents/conversation, normal dashboard login, actual picker, and native middle-click on the conversation link. Native clocks and unchanged settings: the natural new-tab flow retained chip on both heads. This did **not** reproduce the reported incident naturally.
- Controlled stale-cache comparison: preserve the UI-selected chip preference and restore only an older synthetic roster snapshot generated by the real UI. Hold real Gateway server frames until the IndexedDB read completes; no mock responses or paused clock. Main displays roster during cached boot despite the chip preference, then recovers at live handoff. Candidate rejects the stale roster during boot and displays the selected chip after handoff; the agent chip itself awaits real connection metadata. This proves that specific cache mismatch, not the cause or timing of the recent incident.
- 83 focused tests pass: snapshot owner (38), cached row rendering (25), agent selection (20). They cover matching roster/chip restoration, preference changes before/after hydration, and live handoff. The committed bundled-browser regression also passes.
- Exploratory harness limits: an initial assertion incorrectly required the agent chip before real connection metadata. One later capture restored a matching chip cache, so that run is excluded; its capture variation was not established as fixed. The final instrumented run verified the same stale roster record and timestamp before/after boot, and passed rejection plus live-handoff checks.
- Fresh independent review through P3, including the complete snapshot lifecycle: no actionable findings. The browser test’s IndexedDB observer is storage-coupled but prevents checking too early; no demonstrated brittleness warrants removing coverage. No source repair, rebase, or push was needed.
- UI production and affected component/E2E test typechecks, scoped lint/format, test-line budget, and `git diff --check` pass. UI/runtime bundles build. Build reports contain advisory asset-budget violations on main and candidate; no budget was changed and no performance improvement is claimed.
- Measured local command wall times with `--maxWorkers=1`: snapshot tests 5.33 s, row-render tests 5.86 s, agent-selection tests 2.16 s. Browser wall time: 95.67 s including package-artifact lock wait (1.823 s test body). These are loaded-host check costs, not a performance comparison. CI timing remains pending.

title: fix: conversation disappears after refreshing a tool-heavy session
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a nearly empty conversation after refreshing a tool-heavy session on desktop and phone: the latest tool activity appears, but the user's message and assistant reply stay behind **Show earlier**.

## User Impact

A short restored conversation automatically retrieves its missing earlier messages instead of requiring a manual click. Long, already-scrollable conversations still load earlier history on reader intent. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser retains the latest 80 history entries. When those entries are mostly tool activity, restoring the cache loses the readable opening and marks the earlier source boundary for reopening. Automatic loading previously refused that boundary. Allow the existing loader to perform one boundary probe followed by its one automatic history page, without adding background prefetch or unbounded traversal.

## Evidence

- Reproduced in the actual bundled UI at a 390 × 844 phone viewport: display a user message and assistant reply followed by 80 tool entries, flush the normal browser snapshot, and reload. The readable conversation disappears on the base and returns automatically with this fix.
- The browser test uses real UI rendering, snapshot persistence, and page reload, with **mocked Gateway responses and active-run state**. It is not proof against a real running agent or a physical iPhone.
- 59 focused history/autofill tests and both phone and desktop browser cases pass. Scoped lint, formatting, UI typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview of the complete candidate against `476cce7a8a343ac1524bf12276da839a690cff8a`, including the full history/cancellation owner: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The reviewed snapshot is committed as `0305bcbce820de6`.
- The desktop regression at 1200 × 600 also retains a latest assistant reply in the cached tail, matching the reported symptom of a recent reply without the earlier conversation. It fails against the original loader and passes with the same fix; no desktop-only production change was needed.
- The desktop test follow-up received an independent local review with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Before/after screenshots below show the synthetic phone and desktop conversations after reload.

**Remaining verification:** Live model/provider and tool execution, the Safari application, and a physical iPhone remain unverified. The Tempbook proof below verifies the real Gateway with synthetic persisted history in Chromium and WebKit. The author’s earlier WebKit attempt was blocked by its test environment; the installed Tempbook WebKit completed. This PR does not claim that every similar-looking history failure is resolved.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation and test cost</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history-autofill.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 59 tests passed; 9.21 seconds across the two local shards.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-active-history-refresh.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — both cases passed: phone 2.13 seconds, desktop 1.86 seconds; 17.54 seconds total suite time in the follow-up run.
- tsc --noEmit --declaration false -p ui/tsconfig.json, scoped oxlint, and oxfmt passed for the desktop follow-up.
- The new regression and replaced autofill case add 144 net test lines; a dedicated allocation records this. CI time has not yet been measured.
- Production change: 7 added / 4 removed lines; one existing loader remains the owner.

</details>

### Before and after

Same mocked active session, bundled UI, and phone viewport. These captures demonstrate the cache-boundary regression, not physical iPhone verification.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: after reload, only tool activity and Show earlier are visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f8f5876-9766-49f2-a44b-7e636cceb389) | ![After: the user message and assistant reply return automatically](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cca971d-8917-4d69-81b2-476340ee7127) |


<details>
<summary>Desktop before and after (1200 × 600)</summary>

The cached latest reply remains visible in both images. Earlier user and assistant messages return automatically only with the fix. Synthetic Gateway responses; this is not the reporter’s private session.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Desktop before: latest reply only, earlier conversation behind Show earlier](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22087318-c83f-4b60-bdb0-0ff1180bc99c) | ![Desktop after: earlier user message and assistant reply restored automatically](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a621c973-5fc8-47d8-8d0e-233e806758b3) |

</details>

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski reported the problem and requested this fix.


### Independent Tempbook real-Gateway proof

Current main `2aba6707c06a3907642c0b62207775717194fe0b` reproduces the missing earlier conversation; exact candidate `d336232b5ab97ffeb90db6c15a3d0af368aaaea1` restores it. All four cells passed: Chromium and WebKit, each at 390 × 844 phone and 1200 × 600 desktop.

The isolated Gateway admitted the session through `sessions.create`. With that owned Gateway stopped, the production `SessionManager` persisted 84 messages: a user opening, 41 matched assistant tool-call/result pairs (the first assistant also has readable text), and a latest assistant reply. Restarting the Gateway exposed its actual stored history. There was **no model or tool execution, mocked RPC, fabricated active-run state, or browser-state override**.

Identical steps on both revisions: open the bundled Control UI, let normal persistence commit its latest 80 messages with `needsBoundary`, then use normal page reload. Startup resumed from the real delta cursor and returned zero new messages. On main, the latest reply remained, earlier user/assistant text disappeared, and zero `chat.history` requests were sent; **Show earlier** recovered it. With the candidate, those earlier messages returned automatically through exactly two requests: a one-row boundary probe and one older-page request (limit 1000, four rows returned). No browser errors occurred. History RPC/storage and UI snapshot owners match across the comparison except for the intended loader change.

Focused verification: 59 history tests (12.55 s wall), both mocked browser cases (15.16 s suite wall; phone 1.405 s, desktop 1.274 s), UI types, scoped lint/format, and test/source-line checks passed. A fresh independent local P0–P2 review of this exact head found no actionable issue. title: fix(ui): avoid extra reply blocks after steering
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: steering an active reply can separate its tools, working indicator, and continuing text into extra response blocks.

## User Impact

The earlier response stays above the steering message, and the continuation shares one response block for its text and tools. No configuration changes or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the confirmed target execution consistently when choosing reply boundaries, while the steering message supplies the continuation's stable identity. This keeps the split at the human input without hiding work or redesigning the transcript.

Related: #164982, a broader unmerged reply-ownership change. This patch is limited to the confirmed-steer boundary mismatch.

## Evidence

[Fresh real-flow proof and screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195264#issuecomment-6730793587); visual review remains pending.

No fabricated or replayed socket events or scripted model responses. Both views use a 1280×900 light-theme viewport.

After, the same text continues inside the existing reply without another avatar; the next steering message remains below it.

title: fix: stop completion retries for archived requester sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: completion announcements retry indefinitely after the requester session is archived.

## User Impact

Archiving a session stops completion announce retries after the first archived-session refusal. Recoverable failures, including a workspace that is still preparing, retain their existing retry behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize the specific archived-session work-start refusal in the existing permanent announce error policy. This Gateway path sends only `INVALID_REQUEST` and the message, without a structured archived reason; the client also defaults absent retryability to `false`, so that boolean cannot safely distinguish this refusal from recoverable ones.

The media completion loop lifts its two-minute handoff deadline after any queued result. Once files are delivered, subsequent live completion wakes can therefore retry every two seconds indefinitely, outside the file queue's retry budget. Returning `permanent_failure` exits that existing loop without changing its scheduling policy. The match deliberately follows the existing refusal wording.

## Evidence

- Regression: `reports the direct outcome for archived requester without replay`, through the existing announce delivery/dispatch fixture with an `image_generate` source and a real `GatewayClientRequestError`.
- Red on base `18b64fcfaa6198315aebcea0a1a5050b12475b81`: expected `permanent_failure`, received `retryable`; 1 failed, 20 passed. With the fix, the announce file passes all 21 cases, including pending-workspace and the prior pending/stop/partial-send cases.
- `timeout 120s node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-direct-delivery.test.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 51 passed. Existing media tests cover one wake on permanent failure and continued retry on pending handoffs. Wall time: 55.63 seconds total (38.41 seconds announce, 14.14 seconds media); Exact-head [CI run 42491511409](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42491511409) passed; elapsed 621 seconds (all planned jobs completed).

title: feat(plugin-sdk): let Control UI plugins mount the host inline alert
body:
## Problem

Control UI plugins have no way to show an error the way core screens do. The plugin copy-sweep PRs (#195010, #194986, #195006, #194985, #194983, #194982) each render failures their own way: the raw error inline under the “Couldn’t …” sentence, or a plain native `<details>`. Core uses the shared `InlineAlert` (#194124) with raw detail collapsed under **Show details** and a Copy button.

## Solution

- `host.components.mountInlineAlert(container, props)` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/control-ui`, alongside the existing host component mounts.
- Props: `tone` (`danger` | `warning` | `info` | `success`), `message`, optional `title`, `action` (`{ label, disabled?, onSelect }`, rendered as the alert’s trailing button), `onDismiss`, and `detail`.
- `detail` is the raw failure text. The host redacts it and renders it with the existing `ErrorDetails` disclosure: collapsed **Show details**, monospaced well, Copy at the top right.
- The host renders the shared `InlineAlert`, so tone, live role (`alert` for danger, `status` otherwise), dismiss and layout match core. Callbacks are closure-bound like the other host mounts and stop after the plugin is disposed.
- Documented in `docs/plugins/feature-plugins.md`.

The plugin PRs above switch to this after it lands; this PR does not touch them to avoid conflicts.

## Impact

Additive SDK surface on an existing contract (`ControlUiComponents`); no existing member changes. No new subpath or export barrel. The host module loads lazily on first mount.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-inline-alert.test.ts`: mounts through `createControlUiComponents`, checks the danger alert role and message, collapsed **Show details** with the detail inside, Retry callback, update to an info alert without details, and dispose. Passes.

title: fix(ui): archiving the session you're viewing looks unarchived until Undo expires
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: archiving the session you are viewing hides its sidebar row at once, but the conversation keeps a live composer for the whole Undo window (about six seconds), so archiving looks like it did not work.

## User Impact

User impact: the open conversation shows as archived the moment you archive it. The archived banner replaces the composer right away, and your unsent draft is kept, so **Undo** returns the conversation exactly as it was. During the Undo window, the banner's **Unarchive** cancels the pending archive instantly, just like the notification's Undo, and the notification goes away. Once the archive is already being sent, **Unarchive** shows progress until it finishes.

No change to when the archive is sent: active work still keeps running until the Undo window closes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat pane has a single "is this session archived" check that drives the banner, composer, reactions, header actions and progress card. It now also counts an archive that is held behind its Undo notification. Presentation only: the draft is cleared solely when the archive is confirmed, so cancelling restores it untouched.

Held archives move into a small registry outside the lazily loaded archive runtime, so the open conversation can tell synchronously whether its archive is still cancellable. Cancelling from the conversation retires the notification through a new optional `signal` on toasts. The chat presentation also re-renders when a held archive starts sending, because no session-roster publish happens at that moment.

## Evidence

Before — current `main`, archive held behind Undo: the sidebar row is gone, but the conversation still has a live composer.

![Before: archived session still shows a live composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa6d3b28-acba-4f70-9fb2-413b7559dcaa)

![After Undo: composer and draft restored](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e6e606f-57ea-446a-9ff7-49ecca2daba9)

While the archive is being sent — Unarchive shows progress.

title: fix: keep agents usable after concurrent startup preparation
body:
Fixes #195208

## What Problem This Solves

An agent finishing startup preparation can lose its prepared auth and model owners when a sibling publishes before the first admission becomes publicly visible. Holding publication until native cleanup finishes instead can make one stalled close block the whole fleet.

## User Impact

Concurrent startup preserves usable model/auth owners. A cleanup stall remains specific to its agent, while healthy siblings finish admission. If cleanup fails after publication, the refused agent's retained credentials and model snapshots are withdrawn immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing public read-admission owner to make an inspected, prepared, and published agent visible before physical cleanup, then release its publication turn. The secrets and configured-model loaders already consume this view. Writes remain pending until that agent's cleanup completes; cleanup rejection revokes read admission and records a per-agent failure. Failed publication records its refusal before cleanup, so it also cannot strand the publication queue.

The publisher supplies withdrawal through the existing model-retirement and auth-snapshot owners. A failed admission retires only that agent's model owners before clearing its auth snapshot. Retirement fences in-flight model builds; auth invalidation rejects stale prepared secrets candidates. Effective auth selection honors the read-admission refusal so the agent cannot fall back to inherited credentials. Healthy sibling owners remain usable.

Shutdown cancels startup's cleanup waits while native execution owners retain unfinished-close custody. Queue cancellation rejects the queued publisher; it never permits publication out of order. Opens and migrations remain concurrent, and genuine file, config/auth, deletion, and runtime-staleness checks remain enforced. Accepted migration still settles through its existing owner.

The existing enumerable provider authority survives transport projection, worker model spreads, and helper auth reattachment. title: fix(update): reclaim runtimes despite unrelated processes with unreadable cwd
body:
Related: #195159. That report's PID 1007 turned out to be a same-account `systemd --user --deserialize=29` manager, which main already recognizes via #178117. This PR covers the different-account case the same census rule also blocked.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes updater runtimes accumulating forever when a different, non-root user's Node process has an unreadable working directory.

## User Impact

Later updates and `openclaw doctor --fix` can reclaim abandoned private runtimes while that unrelated process keeps running. Root, same-account, unknown-owner processes, and explicit runtime references remain conservative. The updater performing cleanup must contain the fix; it also handles runtimes left by older versions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The census verifies that the particular runtime is a real directory owned by the inspecting account with no group or other permissions before excluding foreign processes without artifact evidence. Runtime creation already uses private `mkdtemp` directories. Linux credential inspection preserves root in any of the four UID slots, alongside the existing matching-account rule.

Process start time is insufficient: an older process can later change directory or load files. This permission rule follows the existing worker model, which never changes user credentials. Manually handing an open private runtime to another account is outside that model.

PID 1007's owner in the original report is still unknown. The issue's ClawSweeper review correctly calls out that gap; this PR supplies a live reproduction for the different-account Node case and preserves root/same-account uncertainty.

## Evidence

- Main reproduction: both foreign Node forms (`node worker.js`, `node -e 1`) retain the runtime; two cleanup attempts reclaim neither of two abandoned runtimes. These three regressions pass with the fix. Existing same-account and root retention cases are unchanged.
- Census suite: 70 passed; 43.22 s local wall time including cold compilation, 25.78 s on Testbox. Process-owner suite: 35 passed in 1.76 s; its two new root-credential cases also fail with the base reader. Existing pacman and exit-listener suites: 13 and 6 passed in 5.88 s and 1.50 s respectively. Per-file CI test seconds are unavailable for jobs blocked during runtime setup.
- Live Linux, Node 24.22.1, Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m6x9jcq0r76vhv2aytsacez7` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42469474781)): inspector uid 1001, foreign Node uid 65534, cwd read returns EACCES. On two successive attempts main counts the foreign process as a holder; the fix removes each 0700 runtime while that same process remains alive.
- Touched-file lint with type checking, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Autoreview of the full local candidate against `3a25991e37c4bad581b34ebf19f0b9b3e036b5cf`, through P3 with complete owner/test context, is scoped-clean. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review is pending.
- No full packaged upgrade was run. PR CI supplies broad checks; no broad tests or packaging ran on the production host.

The secondary pacman ENOENT spam is already fixed by #186839. The activation listener warning was not reproduced; main already has shared listener cleanup from #191842, whose focused suite passes. A stack trace from a current activation is needed for that follow-up.

CI at this head is red due to download setup failures: [OpenGrep](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42469959244/job/128698178962), [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42469959283/job/128698444384), and [pinned Bun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42469959286/job/128698582768) downloads returned HTTP 504 before scanning/testing. Individual logs confirm setup failures, and `pnpm test:ci-failed 195162` selects no Vitest failures to rerun. No code change or workflow rerun was made for the outage. Production/test types, docs, baseline ratchets, source contracts, additional boundaries, and process-boundary Critical Quality passed. Four lint jobs are still running; hosted ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR but has not reviewed it yet.

Simplification: one census owner, no new cache or lifecycle owner, no format/schema change. Production +31/-7 lines; test growth +91 lines covers cleanup and permission/credential boundaries, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/update-unreadable-foreign-cwd.txt`.

Its shared message lifecycle now consumes a completed input while preserving `processing` until the active controller retires. The extra event is the final controller-owned idle transition; it is not a duplicate queued input.

Keep the strict ordered event assertion, now checking processing with zero queued inputs before message completion and idle with zero queued inputs after controller retirement. Inject the finalization error at queue consumption instead of the obsolete immediate-idle transition; retain the exact rejection and admission-release assertions. Scoped spy disposal replaces manual cleanup. The patch has no production changes and reduces test code by three lines, with no baseline changes. Its hunks are separate from #188301's imports and appended timeout test.

Related: #194907. This is a coordinator-requested repair of the named main failures.

## Evidence

- On base `9a5df3d60f12b6c303225c50abeaa4d17bd27108`, the two named files reproduced both reported failures: 2 failed, 16 passed (66.30 s including cold worker preparation).
- With the fix, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/run.diagnostic-events.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 18 passed, 2 files, 19.65 s Vitest duration / 21.49 s wrapper duration. CI seconds are pending.

title: improve(knowledge): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Knowledge copy
body:
## Problem

The Knowledge plugin's Control UI had ~425 user-visible English strings hard-coded across its views, dialogs, session panel, settings, loading/failure frames, and record panels. They didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary (for example "chat"/"conversation" for the session container, "turn" for an agent reply) or style rules (contractions, curly quotes, sentence case, "Couldn’t …" errors with a next step), and the plugin had no translation catalog, so none of it could be localized.

## Solution

- Add plugin i18n on the existing plugin pattern (`extensions/nostr/browser/i18n`): `extensions/knowledge/src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts,locales/en.ts}`. The browser root is `extensions/knowledge/src` (from `openclaw.controlUi: ./src/control-ui.ts`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` discovers the catalog. `activate(host)` binds `host.locale` once; every view reads copy through `t()` when it renders, so the page, session panel, and dialogs all use the host locale.
- The English catalog is split into `en.ts` (shared/page/search copy) plus `en-records.ts`, `en-scribes.ts`, and `en-settings.ts`, merged under one `knowledge.*` key tree. The split keeps each file under the 700-line cap; key paths are unchanged. All keys live under `knowledge.*`, so none collide with shared core keys.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-facing string the lane owns (the 31 changed view modules). Text written for the model (Ask request drafts, the record reference, scribe prompts, scribe session names) is unchanged.
- Small cutovers that came with moving copy:
  - Scribe catalog presentation fields (`blurb`, `cadence`, `startLabel`, `dialogTitle`, `submitLabel`) moved out of `scribes-catalog.ts` into the catalog and were removed from `ScribeDefinition`.
  - `sourceDateNote` moved from the shared `temporal.ts` (also used server-side) into `record-view.ts`, its only caller, so server code doesn't import Control UI copy.
  - Recent activity save badges key on the change id (`created`/`updated`/`observed`) instead of their English label. The one CSS hook (`[data-change="New"]`) moved to `[data-change="created"]`.
  - The page's source-files rail moved to `record-sources.ts` to keep `record-view.ts` under the line cap. It's a straight move with no behavior change.
  - The evidence excerpt eyebrow is sentence case in the catalog. `text-transform: uppercase` keeps its look.
- Docs that quote changed labels: `docs/plugins/knowledge/scribes.md` (Session not found, Open session) and `docs/plugins/knowledge/control-ui.md` (Ask starts a new session).
- Follow-up commit 8221620 (maintainer decisions): group and channel copy keeps “group chats”, and `docs/plugins/knowledge/maintenance.md` and `docs/plugins/knowledge/scribes.md` now say “reply” instead of “turn” for an agent cycle.

### Notable copy changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Starts a new chat with {agent}. … | Starts a new session with {agent}. … |
| Chat was not started. Your request is still here. | Couldn’t start the session. Your request is still here. |
| Chat was started but the request was not sent: {error} | Couldn’t send your request. The session started; open it to try again. {details} |
| Can’t reach the vault. … | Couldn’t reach the vault. … |
| Refresh unavailable / Search unavailable | Couldn’t refresh / Couldn’t search knowledge |
| This store couldn’t be opened | Couldn’t open this store (body now ends with “Retry, or check Stores & sharing.”) |
| The scribe was not started. {error} | Couldn’t start the scribe. Your choices and prompt are still here. {details} |
| The assignment was not changed. {error} / Access was not changed. {error} | Couldn’t change the assignment. Your choices are still here; try again. {details} / Couldn’t change access. Try again. {details} |
| The run did not start: the automation is paused | Couldn’t start the run because the automation is paused. Resume it, then try again. |
| In this conversation (session panel) | In this session |
| Open conversation · Conversation not found | Open session · Session not found |
| Which conversations · Active conversations · Conversations in your sidebar. | Which sessions · Active sessions · Sessions in your sidebar. |
| Knowledge will start a conversation called … | Knowledge will start a session called … |
| Each run is an agent turn over every unlinked claim … | Each run is one agent reply over every unlinked claim … |
| Conversation not recorded (claim source, Learned in) · Saved in conversation | Session not recorded · Saved in a session |
| … from owner-direct conversations | … from direct sessions with the owner |
| Group chats see only their own conversation’s knowledge. | Unchanged: “group chats” is kept (8221620) |
| No page is named exactly "x". · Search all text for "x" | No page is named exactly “x”. · Search all text for “x” |
| PREMISE · EXCERPT / EXCERPT | Premise · excerpt / Excerpt (still rendered uppercase) |
| cannot / is not / does not / could not / must not | can’t / isn’t / doesn’t / couldn’t / can’t |

Strings moved into the translation catalog: **823 English keys**. That's the ~425 source strings, plus one/other plural forms and conditional variants that used to be assembled in code.

## Impact

- English copy now follows the glossary and style rules. The layout and controls don't change.
- Knowledge copy can now be localized. The post-merge Control UI locale-refresh job owns foreign catalogs; this PR adds no foreign strings, `translated.json`, or `.i18n` memory.
- Raw technical details in errors (Gateway messages) stay inline after the next step. This surface has no shared host “Show details” disclosure, so I kept the detail visually secondary instead.
- Known gaps, intentional:
  - Scribe titles such as “Knowledge Consolidation” keep their current case. The title is the scribe session’s display name, which the Scribes tab uses to find a scribe’s session, and it also appears in scribe prompts and automation names. Renaming it would orphan existing scribe sessions.
  - There’s no `translated.json` yet, so `locales.ts` returns English for every locale. The translated catalog loader needs wiring once the locale refresh creates that file.
  - A locale change applies on the next render of each view, not instantly. Only English exists today.

## Evidence

The checks, tests and review below were run on bc913e8842dc236. The follow-up 8221620 changes only English copy and docs; it was checked with `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` (green, `plugin=knowledge keys=823`) and `git diff --check` (clean).

- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=knowledge keys=823`)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/knowledge/src`: green
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check extensions/knowledge/src docs/plugins/knowledge`: green
- `git diff --check`: clean
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge`: 64 files passed. `scribes-view.test.ts` and `search-date-filters.test.ts` assertions were updated to the new English.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main` (d59f00281eb0216) on head bc913e8842dc236, max priority P1. Result: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer noted that its empty sandbox couldn’t run a build.
- pr-simplify: the catalog fields, the shared `sourceDateNote`, and the English-label status hooks were removed, and the shared count/plural helpers were folded into the catalog. Remaining growth is the catalog itself plus one-time `t()` call sites.

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge. Before/after screenshots of Recent, Browse, a record page, Scribes (list, detail, start dialog), Settings (all four sections), and the session panel are still needed under the visual gate.

## Work sessions

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/efff23f5-1c36-4383-806c-137f3ee688bc)

title: improve(mcp-relay): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Connected apps copy
body:
## Problem

The MCP relay **Connected apps** page (`extensions/mcp-relay/src/control-ui.ts`) hard-coded all of its English in the view. The plugin had no translation catalog, so the post-merge locale refresh couldn't translate it. Some of the copy also broke the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: an all-caps eyebrow label, a passive "is required" sentence, "do not" instead of a contraction, and "embedded browser sessions" (which reuses the product noun *session* for a different concept). Errors showed the raw request message as the whole alert, with nothing saying what failed or what to do next.

## Solution

- Added the plugin's English source catalog at `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, at the path `control-ui-plugin-i18n-catalog.ts` derives from `openclaw.controlUi`. The view now reads every string through `translateControlUiMessage`.
- Added `src/i18n/{index.ts,locales.ts}` on the nostr/whatsapp pattern. This page is plain DOM, not Solid, so `locales.ts` keeps the translated catalog in module state and the page re-renders when it loads. The page also re-renders on host locale changes; date formatting follows the locale too.
- `src/i18n/locales/translated.json` is committed as `{}`. The brief said to leave it absent, but without the file the plugin's Control UI build fails: the unresolved dynamic import trips "Control UI builds must bundle their browser dependencies". The empty file holds no translation values; the locale refresh bot fills it after merge.
- Errors now follow "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The redacted raw message moves under a collapsed **Show details**. The Control UI SDK has no shared disclosure component for plugin pages, so this uses a native `<details>`.
- Static `innerHTML` templates are now `element()` builders, so translated text is only ever set as text content.
- Manifest config hints: `Default Agent` → `Default agent`, and the help text says "new sessions" instead of "new conversations". I regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` to match (only the plugin baseline hash changed).

### Notable copy changes (old → new)

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No read access | Read access is required to view connected apps. | You need read access to view connected apps. |
| Consent eyebrow | CONNECTION REQUEST / CONNECT ANOTHER GATEWAY | Connection request / Connect another Gateway (CSS `text-transform: uppercase` keeps the look) |
| Consent, no permission | …permissions do not allow connecting an app. | …permissions don’t allow connecting an app. |
| Revoke hint | Revoking an app ends its MCP access and embedded browser sessions. … | Revoking an app ends its MCP and embedded UI access. … (matches the existing revoke notice) |
| Load failure | *(raw message)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load connected apps. Try again. + Show details |
| Approve / deny failure | *(raw message)* | Couldn’t connect {app}. Reopen the app’s connection page. / Couldn’t deny {app}. Try again. + Show details |
| Revoke failure | *(raw message)* | Couldn’t revoke {app}. Try again. + Show details |
| Pairing failure | *(raw message)* / Pairing failed. Try again. | Couldn’t create a pairing code. Try again. + Show details |
| Invalid relay return | The relay returned an invalid return address. Reopen the app’s connection page. | The relay returned an invalid return address. (now the detail; the next step is in the summary) |
| Config hint label | Default Agent | Default agent |
| Config hint help | Optional agent for new conversations; … | Optional agent for new sessions; … |

Moved into the translation file: **53 keys** (`ui:i18n:verify`: `plugin=mcp-relay keys=53`). About 9 existing strings changed, 6 are new (5 error summaries and "Show details"), and 2 manifest hints changed. The rest moved unchanged.

Left as is on purpose:
- "Gateway owner": an owner principal, not a role name. See the open question below.
- "Full access, including administration": names an activity, not the role.
- `ui-tunnel*` transport errors.
- The model-facing `recommendedPrompts`.

## Impact

- The Connected apps page becomes translatable through the existing locale refresh. English rendering is unchanged except for the copy above.
- The error alert is now a `div` with the summary and a collapsed details element. It got small margin and details styles, so expect a slight visual change in error states.
- Known limit: the page label in the navigation is resolved once at activation (`registerPage` takes a static string), so it stays English until the next activation.

## Evidence

- `extensions/mcp-relay/src/control-ui.test.ts`: 7/7 pass. Assertions follow the changed English. The refresh-failure case now checks the summary and that the collapsed (closed) details hold the raw message.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=mcp-relay keys=53 locales=0 unused_translations=0`).
- `pnpm check:changed` on the committed head: all lanes ok, including typecheck extensions and extension tests, lint extensions, format, the dead-export scan, the Control UI i18n catalog, the bundled channel config metadata and the config docs baseline. One check failed, `changelog attributions`, and it fails the same way on `origin/main` (existing `Thanks @steipete-oai` entries in `CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md` and `2026.7.1.md`). This PR doesn't touch those files.
- Plugin Control UI build (`scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/mcp-relay`): succeeds.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify pass: I removed an unused `Translator` type export that the dead-export scan flagged. There's no new state beyond the error-detail fields and the locale tracking the re-render needs.
- Local review: local ClawSweeper isn't installed on this host, so I used autoreview, the documented fallback (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, merge base `d59f00281eb0216` → head `2cd7495c4c6`, max priority P2). Result: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. The reviewer noted that unchanged SDK and build contracts weren't in its context; the build and verify runs above cover them.

Before/after screenshots are pending and will be added before landing (visual gate).

Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge.

## Work sessions

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f633cf43-6780-43c0-b44f-7867f7985ba5)

title: improve(clawrouter): apply the Control UI glossary and style to ClawRouter copy
body:
## Problem

The ClawRouter pool page (`extensions/clawrouter/src/control-ui.tsx`) hard-coded every English string inline. That made the copy untranslatable, and some of it didn't follow the approved Control UI style: no contractions, sentences ending fragments with periods, passive "is required" phrasing, a raw error message shown as the alert headline, two different names for the same "enabled state unknown" concept, and Gateway status messages pointing at a "Model Providers" page whose actual label is **Models**.

## Solution

- Add a plugin-owned English catalog on the Nostr/Workboard pattern: `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`, `src/i18n/locales.ts`, and `src/i18n/index.ts`, using `translateControlUiMessage`. `browserRoot` is `src/` (the dirname of `openclaw.controlUi`), so `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` picks the catalog up automatically.
- Move **70 strings** into `en.ts` (68 under `clawrouter.*`, plus the shared `common.refresh` and `common.refreshing`, which match core English exactly). Composed strings such as "Observed {date} · Policy {policy}", "{used} used / {limit} monthly limit", and "{count} subscriptions with headroom · {unknown} unknown" are now single templates instead of JSX fragments.
- Apply the glossary and style rules to every human-visible string the lane owns, including the four Gateway pool status messages in `index.ts` that this page renders.
- Errors: the alert now reads "Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh." The redacted technical detail is still shown, but as a secondary hint line under the alert. Plugin views have no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main` (`ControlUiComponents` has none), so per the sweep brief the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- `locales.ts` serves English only. This plugin has no `translated.json` yet, and the sweep brief says to leave it absent. A static import of a missing JSON file would break the esbuild bundle, so the lazy loader isn't added yet (see the open question below).

The `ClawRouter` page title and nav label stay as literal product names.

### Notable copy changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Could not load the pool. Try refreshing. *(only for non-Error failures; otherwise the raw message was the alert)* | Couldn’t load the ClawRouter pool. Try Refresh. *(raw detail shown below as a hint)* |
| Read access is required to view the ClawRouter pool. | You need read access to view the ClawRouter pool. |
| Selections: {n}. API-equivalent value is not a subscription charge. | Selections: {n}. API-equivalent value isn’t a subscription charge. |
| Enabled state unknown *(grant badge)* | Enabled state not reported *(same as the extra-usage wording; one name per concept)* |
| Not reported. *(extra-usage fragment)* | Not reported |
| ClawRouter pool status is unavailable. Check the ClawRouter connection and try Refresh. | Couldn’t load ClawRouter pool status. Check the ClawRouter connection and try Refresh. |
| Configure a ClawRouter key in Model Providers, then try Refresh. | Configure a ClawRouter key in Models, then try Refresh. |
| The ClawRouter key was rejected. Check or replace it in Model Providers. | The ClawRouter key was rejected. Check or replace it in Models. |
| This ClawRouter deployment does not expose pool status. … | This ClawRouter deployment doesn’t expose pool status. … |

All other strings moved into the catalog with their English unchanged.

## Impact

- The English copy is the same apart from the rows above. Layout and markup are unchanged, except that a failed refresh now shows a fixed alert plus a secondary detail line.
- No docs quote the changed labels. `docs/providers/clawrouter.md` and the README reference **Refresh**, **Not reported**, and **ClawRouter**, which are unchanged.
- Foreign locales: none yet. The post-merge locale refresh owns parity. `ui:i18n:check` parity is non-strict on PRs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/clawrouter/browser/pool.test.ts extensions/clawrouter/pool-gateway.test.ts`: 3 + 12 passed. The browser test assertions are updated for the new alert headline, the detail line still being redacted, and the "You need read access" copy.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green, `plugin=clawrouter keys=70 locales=0`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched files>`: no problems.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <touched files>`: clean.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: OK.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/clawrouter`: bundle builds.
- pr-simplify pass: removed duplicate keys (one "Observed {date}", one "Subscription") and collapsed repeated enabled/disabled ternaries into one helper. Production delta: +260/−126 across 6 files. Most of it is the new 90-line `en.ts` plus the line-wrapping of `t(...)` calls.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex engine, gpt-6.1-sol), branch mode, base `d59f00281eb0216` → head `14ab4736fa24`, max priority P2. Result: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.9)", no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't set up on this host.

**Not landing: requested by maintainer; screenshots pending before merge** (the visual gate needs before/after screenshots of the pool page, including the refresh-failure state).

## Open question

Leaving `translated.json` absent means that after the locale refresh writes it, nothing loads it until a follow-up adds the Nostr-style `loadMessages` loader. The alternatives are to commit an empty `{}` `translated.json` with the loader now, or to add both in the first locale refresh.

## Work sessions

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/a37a5704-38f5-40e9-87b9-fbcec400e40e)

- Translate the page, navigation label, and page label through `translateControlUiMessage`. The view tracks `host.locale` in its existing presentation store.
- Notices are now typed keys (`added`, `removed`, `guestsOn`, …) translated at render time instead of English strings held in state.
- Request failures are wrapped in a small `RequestFailure` that records which action failed. The alert now reads "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." and the redacted server message follows inline as secondary text (`<small>`, muted). The plugin SDK host components (`ControlUiComponents`) on main have no shared "Show details" disclosure, so as the sweep brief directs, the raw detail stays visually secondary and inline.
- Copy that wraps inline elements (`<time>`, the repository link) uses a small `withSlots` helper. It splits the translated string at `{name}` placeholders, so translators control word order.
- `locales.ts` is English-only for now, and other locales fall back to English, which is today's behavior. `translated.json` isn't added, per the sweep brief. The Nostr-style lazy `translated.json` loader can't be wired until that file exists, because the bundler can't resolve a missing import.

### Notable copy changes

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| Choose whose mentions the bot can answer publicly. | Choose whose mentions the agent can answer publicly. |
| Administrator access is required to manage X replies. | You need admin access to manage X replies. |
| Bot account | Agent account |
| Applies to the selected bot account. Guests get repository answers with hidden helpers of the same agent. No writes, commands, visible work sessions, or other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. | Applies to the selected agent account. Guests get repository answers from this agent and its hidden subagents. They can’t write, run commands, open visible sessions, or use other agents. Maintainers keep their normal access. |
| Per guest, per UTC day / `3 mentions` | Mentions per guest, per UTC day / `3` (no more "1 mentions") |
| Could not resolve on X: @a, @b. Check the declared profiles. | Couldn’t find @a, @b on X. Check the declared GitHub profiles. |
| No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or set `allowFrom` in config. | No manual entries yet. Add a maintainer above or in config. |
| *(raw server error)* / The request failed. Try again. | Couldn’t load X replies. Try again. · Couldn’t add this account. Check the handle and try again. · Couldn’t remove this entry. Try again. · Couldn’t change guest mode. Try again. *(the redacted server detail follows as secondary text)* |
| No successful sync yet.Entries update… *(missing space)* | No successful sync yet. Entries update… |

All other strings moved into the catalog with unchanged English. They were already in sentence case, used the single ellipsis character, and had no straight quotes.

### Out of scope / unchanged

- Server-generated text the page displays verbatim: the guest readiness `blockedReason` from `guests.ts`/`monitor.ts` and the GitHub sync `message` from `verified-github.ts`. That text also feeds channel status and the agent path, so it stays with its backend owners.
- Agent-facing and X-posted text (the guest policy prompt, tool text).
- Docs: `docs/channels/x.md` quotes **X replies**, **From GitHub**, **Guest mode**, and **Refresh**, and none of those labels changed.

## Impact

UI copy only. The plugin's operator RPCs (`x.allowlist.*`, `x.guests.set`), state, and authorization are unchanged. Foreign locales keep showing English until the post-merge locale refresh adds `translated.json` and the lazy loader is wired.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/x/browser/control-ui.browser.test.tsx`: 4/4 passed. Assertions were updated for the new admin-required copy and for the error alert (`Couldn’t add this account. Check the handle and try again. Rejected [REDACTED]`), which still proves redaction.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=x keys=63 locales=0`).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check`: fails as expected with "missing verified translations" for all 22 locales of the new `x` catalog. That CI step is `continue-on-error`, and foreign parity is the post-merge `control-ui-locale-refresh` bot's job. No foreign files were hand-edited.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/x`: pass. The one warning is pre-existing, on an unchanged line.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: pass, no ratchet changes.
- `scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.mts extensions/x`: bundle builds.
- `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify: the remaining machinery is the catalog and translator, one `RequestFailure` class (it carries which action failed to the error summary), and `withSlots` (it keeps inline elements inside translatable sentences). A planned slot was dropped once `allowFrom` left the copy.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`, on candidate `e48ff37`. Result: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final head differs only by removing the `allowFrom` slot from the empty-state string. Verify, test, lint, and typecheck were re-run on it.

title: improve(workboard): apply the Control UI glossary and style to Workboard copy
body:
## Problem

Workboard's Control UI copy didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules. It had straight apostrophes, a `...` placeholder, "could not" / "cannot" errors with no consistent form, "Board agent" capitalized mid-sentence, the British "Cancelled", and "board conversation" used for what is a session. Its errors also showed internal RPC text: `sessions.create returned no key` and `workboard response did not include a card`. About 19 user-visible English strings were still hard-coded in `extensions/workboard/browser/` instead of living in the plugin's translation source, so they could never be translated.

## Solution

- Rewrote the existing English in `browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the rules. Errors now read "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." The copy uses contractions, curly apostrophes and the `…` character, sentence case, and **session** as the container noun.
- Moved the remaining hard-coded English in `browser/` (execution, loading, mutation and normalization errors; the stale-session fallback; the "Workboard is no longer active" message; widget registration labels; the board-kind suffix on duplicate sidebar names) into `en.ts` and called it through `t()`.
- `host.ts` calls `translateControlUiMessage` directly instead of `t()`, because `i18n/index.ts` imports `host.ts` and using `t()` there would create an import cycle.
- Two places that had the same stale-session fallback in different words (normalization and card alerts) now use one key.
- Updated `docs/plugins/workboard.md`, which quotes the sidebar suffix: **Planning (Cards)** / **Planning (Sessions)**.

Notable copy changes (old → new):

| Where | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page load failure | Workboard could not load. Check your connection and reload this page. | Couldn’t load Workboard. Check your connection and reload this page. |
| Delete without write access | Connect with write access to delete this board. | Couldn’t delete this board. Connect with write access and try again. |
| Bulk edit stopped | The operation stopped. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. | Couldn’t apply changes to every card. Remaining cards are still selected; refresh and try again. |
| Sessions board agent missing | The board conversation's agent is unavailable. Choose a configured agent or update the board's conversation. | Couldn’t open the board session. Its agent is unavailable; choose a configured agent or update the board’s session. |
| Sessions board create failed | The board conversation could not be created. Try again. | Couldn’t create the board session. Try again. |
| Rules help | The Board agent can edit column rules and session scope. | The board agent can edit column rules and session scope. |
| Note placeholder | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note... | Add a decision, blocker, or proof note… |
| Dispatch help | …this board's Ready cards… | …this board’s Ready cards… |
| Refresh status | Refresh failed | Couldn’t refresh |
| Session status | Cancelled | Canceled (American English, same as core approvals copy) |
| Widget card not loaded | This card is not loaded yet. | This card isn’t loaded yet. |
| Start, hard-coded | sessions.create returned no key | Couldn’t start a session for this card. Try again. |
| Card payload, hard-coded | workboard response did not include a card | Couldn’t read the updated card. Refresh the board and try again. |
| Gateway missing, hard-coded | Gateway client unavailable | Couldn’t refresh Workboard. Connect to the Gateway and try again. |
| Scheduled start, hard-coded | Scheduled cards cannot start before their scheduled time. | Couldn’t start this card. Scheduled cards can’t start before their scheduled time. |
| Already started, hard-coded | This card already has an execution. Refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link before starting another. | Couldn’t start this card. It already has a linked session; refresh its details or use Edit to clear its session link. |
| Stop, hard-coded | Refresh this card's session details before stopping it, or use Edit to choose its session. | Couldn’t stop this card’s session. Refresh its session details, or use Edit to choose its session. |
| Changed card, hard-coded | This card changed. Refresh its details before starting or stopping it. | Couldn’t start or stop this card because it changed. Refresh its details and try again. |
| Stale fallback, hard-coded (×2) | Session has not reported… / Linked session has not reported recent activity. | Linked session hasn’t reported recent activity. |
| Inactive plugin, hard-coded | Workboard is no longer active. Reload the plugin to continue. | Workboard is no longer active. Reload this page to continue. |
| Unknown error, hard-coded | Unknown workboard error. | Unknown Workboard error. Refresh and try again. |
| Sidebar duplicate name | Planning (cards) | Planning (Cards) |

String count: 12 existing English values rewritten. 19 hard-coded literals moved into translation calls: 14 go to new `en.ts` keys and the rest reuse 3 existing keys (`widget.boardLabel`, `cardsBoard`, `sessionsBoard.kind`). No foreign locale, `translated.json`, `.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` or `*.meta.json` file was edited. The post-merge locale-refresh bot owns parity.

Raw Gateway error text still shows inline in the existing Workboard error toast. Workboard has no shared "Show details" disclosure on `main`, and the copy written here no longer includes internal names.

## Impact

Only copy and translation sources change; behavior doesn't. Two edge cases are accepted:
- Widget registration labels and the stale-reason fallback are resolved when they're created. A locale switch picks them up after the next refresh or reload; before this change they were always English.
- The session label `buildCardSessionLabel` writes for new card sessions, and agent-facing template drafts, stay as they are. They're stored data or model-facing text, not Control UI copy.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/workboard/browser`: 34 files, 265 tests passed (assertions updated in `index.test.ts` and `widgets/runtime.test.ts`).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (`plugin=workboard keys=395 locales=22`).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: green.
- `oxlint` on touched TS files: 0 warnings or errors. `oxfmt --check`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles.
- pr-simplify: every hunk is a copy move or rewrite. The only new code is the 4-line `inactiveMessage()` helper in `host.ts`, which avoids the import cycle. One duplicate stale fallback was merged into a shared key. Net production change is small: about +40/−30 lines, mostly `en.ts`.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol, medium), branch mode, base `d59f00281eb0216` → head of this branch, max priority P2. Result: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.82)", no findings. The reviewer couldn't see unchanged context, so key validity and import cycles rest on the `ui:i18n:verify` and madge runs above.
