title: improve(nostr,memory-core): apply the Control UI glossary and style to plugin copy
body:
## Problem

The Nostr profile panel and the Memory overview/search views had copy that didn't follow the approved Control UI glossary and style rules: Title Case buttons and labels (`Hide Advanced`, `Import from Relays`, `Save & Publish`, `Public Key`, `Edit Profile`), straight quotes and `...`, "Could not" / "does not" with no contractions, lowercase "gateway", internal jargon ("host memory search runtime"), and error messages that didn't use the "Couldn’t {verb} {thing}. {Next step}." pattern. Nostr also had one hard-coded English label (`NIP-05`) outside its catalog.

## Solution

- Rewrote the English source catalogs in `extensions/nostr/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/browser/i18n/locales/en.ts` to follow the glossary and style rules.
- **Shared-key collision:** Nostr's `common.hideAdvanced`, `common.showAdvanced`, `common.importFromRelays`, `common.saveAndPublish` and `common.publicKey` share keys with the core catalog (`ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`), and `ui:i18n:verify` requires a plugin's English to match the core text for any shared key. These five now live under plugin-owned `channels.nostr.*` keys.
- Removed those five core `common.*` keys from `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`; nothing reads them any more (approved by Vyctor; `ui:i18n:baseline`, `ui:i18n:verify` and `tsgo:ui` pass).
- Moved the hard-coded `NIP-05` profile-fact label into the Nostr catalog (`channels.nostr.nip05`). The truncated public key now uses `…`.
- Nostr save/import failures now show `Couldn’t update/import the profile. Try again.` with the raw detail after it. Before, a failed request showed only the raw server message (e.g. `Invalid profile`). Both paths share one `failure()` helper in `controller.ts`, which also removed the duplicated prefix logic.
- Placeholders are unchanged on every key that keeps its name (`{prefix}`, `{error}`, `{message}`, `{engine}`), so existing translations still pass verification.
- **Raw error detail:** the Plugin SDK has no shared "Show details" disclosure for plugin settings views, so the raw detail stays inline after the sentence. This matches the existing core pattern (`Couldn’t load cloud device profiles. Try again. {error}`).

### Notable copy changes (old → new)

| Surface | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nostr button | Edit Profile | Edit profile |
| Nostr button | Save & Publish | Save & publish |
| Nostr button | Import from Relays | Import from relays |
| Nostr button | Show Advanced / Hide Advanced | Show advanced / Hide advanced |
| Nostr label | Public Key | Public key |
| Nostr label | Display Name | Display name |
| Nostr label | NIP-05 Identifier | NIP-05 identifier |
| Nostr label | Lightning Address | Lightning address |
| Nostr hint | Click "Edit Profile" to add your name, bio, and avatar. | Click “Edit profile” to add your name, bio, and avatar. |
| Nostr placeholder | Tell people about yourself... | Tell people about yourself… |
| Nostr error | Request timed out after 30 seconds; the server may still have applied the change — check the profile before retrying. | Couldn’t confirm the profile change within 30 seconds. It may still have applied, so check the profile before you try again. |
| Nostr error | Profile update failed: {error} | Couldn’t update the profile. Try again. {error} |
| Nostr error | Profile import failed: {error} | Couldn’t import the profile. Try again. {error} |
| Nostr error | Profile publish failed on all relays. | Couldn’t publish the profile to any relay. Try again. |
| Nostr public key | `abcd1234...wxyz5678` | `abcd1234…wxyz5678` |
| Memory search placeholder | Search this agent's memories | Search this agent’s memories |
| Memory search error | Memory search failed: {message} | Couldn’t search memories. Try again. {message} |
| Memory file error | Could not load this memory file: {message} | Couldn’t load this memory file. Close and reopen it to try again. {message} |
| Memory file | This memory file cannot be shown as text. | This memory file can’t be shown as text. |
| Memory notice | Update the gateway to search memories from the Control UI. | Update the Gateway to search memories from the Control UI. |
| Memory hero | Host memory search is unavailable | Memory search is unavailable |
| Memory hero | {engine} does not provide a host memory search runtime. … | {engine} doesn’t provide Gateway memory search. … |
| Memory hero | Checking this agent's memory engine and dream cycle. | Checking this agent’s memory engine and dream cycle. |
| Memory hero | The gateway is offline, so memory status is unavailable. | The Gateway is offline, so memory status is unavailable. |
| Memory button | Open Settings | Open settings |

**Counts:** 28 user-visible strings changed (16 Nostr catalog strings, 10 Memory catalog strings, 1 hard-coded Nostr label moved into the catalog, 1 ellipsis in the formatted public key). 1 string moved into a translation file (`NIP-05`). 5 Nostr keys moved from `common.*` to `channels.nostr.*`.

## Impact

- English-locale users see consistent sentence case, contractions and typography, and errors that say what failed and what to do next.
- Foreign locales: translated.json, `.i18n/*.tm.jsonl` and `*.meta.json` weren't hand-edited. Keys that kept their names still show their existing (now stale) translations. The five moved Nostr keys show English until the post-merge control-ui-locale-refresh bot runs. Their old translations stay as unused entries (`unused_translations=110`, which verify allows).
- No docs quote the changed labels.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/nostr/browser/profile.test.tsx extensions/memory-core/browser/memories.test.tsx extensions/memory-core/browser/overview.test.tsx`: 3 files, 51 tests passed. The assertions on changed English are updated. The Swedish locale-switch test now waits for an unchanged translated label (`Användarnamn`), because `saveAndPublish` moved to a new key.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: green (memory-core keys=67, nostr keys=62, 22 locales each; no shared-key disagreement; referenced keys resolve).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- `oxlint` on both browser dirs: 0 errors. The 2 warnings are pre-existing, in the untouched `memory-core/browser/components.tsx`.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`: OK. `oxfmt` applied. `git diff --check`: clean.
- pr-simplify: every hunk is copy, a key reference, or the shared `failure()` helper, which replaced duplicated prefix logic. No new state or modules.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium), `--mode branch`, base `d59f00281eb0216`, head `0e93cfcfc4e6`, max priority P2. Result: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't set up in this checkout.

title: fix(gateway): release old session rows after metadata updates
body:
Related: #194880

## What Problem This Solves

Session metadata updates retain superseded resident entries and displayed rows until another reader arrives. This repairs the deterministic large-10 retention failure in [scheduled main run 42434232909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42434232909/job/128589770580).

## User Impact

Updated sessions can release old row graphs without waiting for another list request. Current row caching, wire values, and recipient authorization remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Common nested producer fields still use the existing sharing owner. Reusing preceding audience variants is best effort across garbage collection; a collected comparison map causes recomputation with the same values.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw users need an opt-in way to operate a locally paired iPhone through [lxe/phoneuse](https://github.com/lxe/phoneuse), as requested in [this thread](https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2119248363761889625).

Adds the disabled-by-default `phoneuse` plugin, upstream stdio MCP connection, and an operating skill. Operators must set up Phoneuse on the phone-connected Linux/Hyprland desktop; nothing is installed or enabled on the running Gateway by this change. Existing MCP overrides and tool permissions remain authoritative.

MIT code does not mean zero total cost: the phone, compatible host, local OCR/grounding compute, agent model usage, hosting/electricity, and maintenance remain operator responsibilities. The inspected upstream does not deliver Mac, Windows, Android/ADB, USB control, a managed phone fleet, or an SLA.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses existing manifest-owned MCP and skill contracts rather than introducing another device runtime, transport, credential store, or retry owner. **Safety limits:** upstream can acknowledge an action and then fail to observe its result. It exposes no frame-age token, transaction receipt, or idempotency key. The skill says to stop mutations, obtain a fresh observation, and reconcile an uncertain effect before considering another attempt. This is agent guidance, not an enforced freshness interlock or exactly-once guarantee.

**Comparison gap:** the earlier requested YC company could not be identified from accessible context. Its name/link has been requested; this PR makes no commercial feature-parity claim.

title: feat(research): show a quiet research card in the chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194780 removed the Deep research chat card so the side panel was the only entry point, with a redesigned card to follow. Without it, a `deep_research` call in the chat shows only a text summary, which never updates as the research progresses.

This brings the card back as one quiet row that matches the other cards in the chat. It builds on Josh Lehman's (@jalehman) original card from #194780 and credits him as co-author. The design was picked by Vyctor from three prototypes rendered in the real chat.

## User Impact

When the agent starts or resumes research, a card appears in the conversation at that tool call:

- **Title:** the research question, two lines at most.
- **Detail line:** the current step while running ("Gathering evidence (round 1)"); otherwise the outcome ("Report ready", "Partial report", "Paused", "Cancelling", "Failed"…). After that come the counts: sources, findings and open gaps.
- **Actions:** **Read report** (or **View progress** before a report exists), plus a quiet Cancel or Resume when allowed.

Only failures add color. The search icon pulses gently while research runs, but not when the user has reduced motion turned on. The line above the card now says "Started deep research" (or "Resumed…"). Before, it repeated the state at call time, so it could say "running" next to a finished card. On narrow screens the actions and counts wrap whole; no count is ever split. The side panel still works on its own, from Explore panels.

## Changes

- Restore the `research-job` inline view, version 1: the backend descriptor, the `api.inlineView` result on start/resume, and the browser registration. The whole result stays under the existing 24 KB limit.
- Fixes for the three findings ClawSweeper raised on Josh's original card:
  - **Errors show on the card.** A rejected Cancel/Resume, or a failed first read, appears as a line on the card instead of failing silently.
  - **Import through the API barrel.** The view contract now comes from the plugin's `api.ts`, not `src/`, which fixes the boundary check.
  - **Read report opens the report.** It opens the panel on the **Report** tab, and View progress opens **Progress**. A one-time tab request is handed from the card to the panel.
- Card views use the research client in a mode that never touches the panel's saved pending-start state, so a card can't clear a start the panel is recovering.

title: fix(muse): settle canceled startup without stopping other callers

title: fix(android): prevent premature expiry in Wear cancellation test
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an intermittent Android Play cancellation-test failure during the initial channel claim, before the cancellation scenario starts.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This is a focused fixture repair for the maintainer-directed investigation of [main CI run 42425211259](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42425211259/job/128562180421).

Put pending-channel expiry on a virtual clock in this cancellation case while retaining the fixture's parent Job and real IO readers. The case still exercises actual registry claiming, cancellation, retirement, and retry. All assertions and numeric deadlines remain intact; the separate expiry test continues to cover expiration.

The failed case took 1.630 seconds and returned null on the first claim (line 757), before cancellation began. Its pending channel expires after 1,000ms. The same unchanged case passed in 0.112 seconds on [run 42420555752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42420555752). ## What problem this solves

A pinned historical Logbook day waited for fresh capture status even when its timeline and the capture timezone were already available. Historical cards now appear when the selected timeline arrives; initial and Today loads still wait for capture-host day correctness.

The existing Logbook owner retains day/connection/generation guards, pending actions and queued refreshes. Maintainer review reproduced and repaired an early-rejection gap: `Promise.all` released load admission before a pending timeline could publish. `Promise.allSettled` now retains full request custody through both outcomes, then exposes current errors.

## Production-renderer qualification

title: fix(skills): show discovery before installed status
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Skills discovery cannot show its independent library while installed-skill status is slow.

## User Impact

User impact: the library can appear before installed status finishes. In the controlled production-renderer workload below, first-visit readiness improves **308.0 → 118.1 ms (61.7%)**. This is not a deployed-page or real-Gateway throughput claim.

**The strict no-worse target is not fully clean:** first-visit layout time increases by 0.365 ms, and warm median readiness increases by 1.1 ms. Aggregate renderer CPU is unchanged in these samples. The current maintainer request authorizes review and landing. These adverse cells remain disclosed for the landing owner’s assessment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Start the installed-status prefetch at its existing route boundary and let the existing mounted Skills request owner adopt the same promise. Discovery renders independently; Settings still waits for its report. Preserve agent-selection revisions, connection ownership, visible errors, installation consent, and write settlement. No new cache or duplicate status request. **Skills only.**

## Evidence

### Production-bundle method and predeclared rule

Chromium **156.0.8078.4**, Linux x64, **1440×1000**, light theme, 1× CPU. Real production bundles are served through the existing Gateway HTTP delivery owner; WebSocket responses are synthetic. The page-specific fixture has **one library entry and one installed-status sentinel**, with only skills.status delayed **250 ms**. This tests the dependency mechanism, not large-catalog scaling.

For each first-visit and warm-revisit scene: **five serial baseline/candidate/baseline-control triples**, a fresh owned Chromium process per observation. First visit means opening Skills after a settled New Session, not document startup. Warm revisits do not force artificial reads; in this run every measured visit issued one status read. A newly returned status marker, followed by final frames, defines full settlement and the request-count assertion.

Latency/CPU use the **unpolled** pass. RSS comes from separate explicitly diagnostic scenes with 25 ms-paced polling of the owner-validated renderer processes; their latency and CPU values are excluded. RSS is the sampled peak sum of browser-owned renderers, not a true peak, whole-browser/Gateway memory, retained-heap, or leak measurement. Heap endpoints are unforced. Host load and raw samples are retained in the generated reports. Separate traces/profiles are excluded from timing distributions.

The rule was recorded here before production measurement: lower first-visit median/p95; no worse warm/full-settlement latency, counts, CPU or memory; any real worse metric needs explicit owner acceptance; a >=20% adverse cell stops qualification. A/A controls do not waive that rule. This is the page-specific five-sample rule, not a claim to meet the generic harness manifest's ten-pair stability budget.

### Production renderer results

Cells show **median / nearest-rank p95**. With n=5, p95 is the maximum. Times are milliseconds; RSS is MiB. Control is a fresh observation of the baseline bundle after the candidate.

| Phase / metric | Baseline | Candidate | Baseline control |

Readiness min–max: first visit **291.0–309.6 → 114.4–122.8 ms**; warm **18.5–21.6 → 19.1–21.3 ms**. RSS min–max: first visit **466.8–471.5 → 468.0–471.6 MiB**; warm **478.0–483.7 → 477.8–483.7 MiB**. RSS observations contain 6–8 samples each. These distributions do not establish an arbitrary-duration memory bound.

### Adverse cells are not hidden

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First-visit thread-clock task time | 68.499 / 71.289 | 69.441 / 75.920 |

Separate traces show no >50 ms task in either candidate scene; cold profile mapping reports 309 mapped / 116 unmapped frames.

### Reproduction and source custody

### Correctness and review

- **44 targeted UI tests pass**, including affected mutation/lifecycle/discovery siblings; the same early-readiness regression is red on the old production source.
- Production UI typing, UI test type shards, scoped lint/format/diff checks, test-line and UI ownership ratchets passed for the unchanged UI fix. New benchmark modules pass scripts typing, scoped lint/format and commit hooks.
- Independent local P0–P2 autoreview covered the UI fix and subsequent benchmark work. Its benchmark findings—synchronous RSS polling contaminating timing, and counting requests before final status publication—were repaired by separate diagnostic scenes and a final recount. Runtime production observations above exercise those repairs; no clean-review result is substituted for execution.
- Author simplification preserves one request owner. Production UI LOC **+11**; benchmark scenes are explicit-only and reuse the existing measurement harness. The initial **68-line** regression allocation is reduced to **57 lines** by the deterministic maintainer repair; the shared scalar remains unchanged.

### Maintainer review update

The first-visit improvement is well separated from both baseline observations. Warm readiness differs by 1.1 ms and overlaps baseline/control spread; sampled RSS differs by 0.17% with overlapping ranges. The layout median increases by 0.365 ms (+13.0%), a measured subphase cost that is retained rather than called a win. These five-sample data do not demonstrate a material user-visible regression, but do not prove every metric is unchanged. This assessment uses the published distributions; the original Linux report files were not available in this review checkout.

The normal regression now uses a held promise, forwards the actual route-loader result to the mounted page, verifies the eventual installed card, and checks one status request after settlement. Real timers, performance logging, and the environment-dependent repeat count were removed; the committed browser benchmark remains the timing owner. The regression fails against the old route and passes on the candidate. Its allocation shrinks from 68 to 57 lines with no shared-scalar change.

85 focused tests pass (Skills discovery, lifecycle, mutation, domain owner, and route provenance). The changed test file’s measured `pnpm test ... --maxWorkers=1` wall time is 5.30 s, with 7 tests taking 121 ms; CI seconds are not yet available for the repair. Full-context independent P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable issue. Production UI source and the measured bundle identity are unchanged by this test-only repair.

UI production types, all UI test type shards, scripts types, scoped lint, formatting, test/source-line ratchets, and UI ownership guard pass. The native Gateway HTTP/startup boundary suites pass 22 tests, and the benchmark HTTP-delivery boundary test passes. Final CI/security admission and merge remain with the landing owner.

### Maintainer assessment

The measured +0.365 ms first-visit layout cost and +1.1 ms warm-readiness median are accepted here as a bounded trade-off for the 189.9 ms first-visit improvement in this controlled workload. title: fix: keep agent identity and saved personal instructions in worktree sessions
body:
Builds on and supersedes #193739 by @PollyBot13, who worked on this first. His commit is included unchanged as the base of the personal-instructions part, and he is credited as co-author (`Co-authored-by` on the follow-up commits).

## What Problem This Solves

Worktree sessions get the wrong instructions, in two ways:

1. **Agent identity is lost in project worktrees.** When a session runs in a managed worktree of a **separate project repository**, OpenClaw loads every bootstrap file from the worktree. The agent's own `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md` and `IDENTITY.md` are dropped (shown as `[MISSING]` at the worktree path), and the project's `AGENTS.md` becomes the agent's only instructions. On the team server, Roboclaw sessions in worktrees of the openclaw repo never see the team workspace rules, such as "check for existing PRs first". One of them started duplicating #194780.
2. **Saved personal instructions are missing (#193739).** Personal instructions saved in **Settings → Profile** (the selected person's `USER.md`) are read from the worktree instead of the agent workspace where the editor saves them. Worktree sessions therefore get no saved instructions, or a stale or committed copy from the checkout.

Both come from #188970. Its selector, `resolveRunBootstrapWorkspaceDir`, returns any recorded `sessionRoot` (or `workspaceOnly` execution workspace) as the **sole** bootstrap root. That was right for #129411, where the worktree is a checkout of a Git-backed *agent workspace*. It is wrong for unrelated projects, and it is wrong for the Profile file in every case.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Bootstrap root (`workspace-run.ts`).** The execution root owns bootstrap files only when it is a checkout of the agent workspace's own Git repository (same Git common dir) or is the agent workspace itself. Otherwise the agent workspace owns them, and the root's `AGENTS.md` is layered after them as `execution-project` context. The loader already supported this layering, and both callers already pass the execution root.
- **Personal instructions (`bootstrap-files.ts`, @PollyBot13's commit).** The selected personal `USER.md` is always loaded and provenance-checked in the configured agent workspace, independently of the bootstrap root.
- **Integration fixes on top of his commit:**
  - The personal workspace now also resolves when the config has only `agents.defaults.workspace` and no agent roster, as in some CLI runs. The autoreview flagged that case, and the original fell back to the worktree.
  - The `AGENTS.md`-only project-layering pass no longer reads the personal file.
  - His Gateway test now expects the agent's `SOUL.md` in project worktrees.
- **Docs:** `docs/concepts/system-prompt.md` "Workspace bootstrap injection" describes both rules, and `docs/concepts/user-model.md` notes that worktrees use the saved Profile file.

## User Impact

- Project worktree sessions get the agent's persona and team rules, the person's saved Profile instructions, and the repository's `AGENTS.md` as project rules.
- Worktrees of a Git-backed agent workspace still load that checkout's bootstrap files, with no fallback to the shared checkout. The one exception is the saved Profile `USER.md`, which always comes from the agent workspace, so a branch can't replace someone's personal instructions.
- Accepted edge case: in `workspaceOnly` project sessions, the injected agent files sit outside the tool root, so file tools can't edit them. This matches behavior before #188970. Session privacy filters and memory provenance apply as for sessions on the canonical workspace.

## Evidence

- Real TLS Gateway flow (`server.personal-instructions-worktree.test.ts`, from #193739): a Profile save and update reach the agent's request, along with the project's `AGENTS.md` and the agent's `SOUL.md`, while a worktree `USER.md` decoy is excluded. It runs against a local replay provider, not a paid model. With the bootstrap selector reverted to base it fails at the agent-`SOUL.md` assertion. It passes with this change.
- Regressions red on base `867ed52` and green with this change:
  - embedded "layers execution project instructions" for project worktree and `workspaceOnly`;
  - CLI "keeps agent bootstrap and adds only project instructions from a project worktree";
  - "roster-less worktree" personal-instructions provenance case (red without the roster fix).
- The existing #188970 cases ("rooted checkout of the agent workspace": present, missing, symlink) still pass, now with a real linked-checkout layout.
- Related test runs:
  - bootstrap-files (core, personal, remote, memory-core), CLI preparation and the Gateway flow: 167 passed;
  - `attempt-bootstrap-prepare`, `workspace-run`, `skill-runtime.workspace`, `run-attempt-dispatch.owner`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability` and `run.session-permissions`: all passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap and test-lines ratchets, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, branch vs `867ed52`): the first run found the roster-less gap, now fixed. The final run is **scoped-clean**.
- **Not run:** a live production Gateway check. Hosted CI is pending.

## Related

- Supersedes #193739 (and #191734). Narrows #188970; keeps #129411/#129404 fixed for agent-workspace worktrees.
- Follow-up, not in this PR: compaction context (`prepared-compaction-runtime.ts`) and the `/context` command report (`commands-system-prompt.ts`) pick their bootstrap root separately from this selector.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(ui): renaming, pinning or changing settings moves sessions to the top of Last updated
body:
Related: #194839

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with the sidebar sorted by **Last updated**, sessions jump to the top when you rename, pin, unpin, archive, restore, snooze or wake them, change their group, change chat settings (model, thinking, speed, context window, permissions), share them, or mark them read or unread, even though nothing new happened in the conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: the **Last updated** sort now moves a session only for conversation activity, like a message you send or an agent reply or run result. Organizing a session or changing its settings leaves it where it was. Sessions with no recorded activity keep their previous position, based on their last recorded change. The sort label is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar sorted this mode by `updatedAt`, which the Gateway advances on almost every write to a session, settings changes included. Agent turns already record real activity in `lastActivityAt`, and the user's message time in `lastInteractionAt`. The shared `sessionActivityTimestamp` helper already turns those into one "latest activity" time and falls back to `updatedAt`; the Activity page uses the same helper. The sidebar's Last updated comparator now uses that helper. Including `lastInteractionAt` means a session you just messaged moves up when you send, rather than only when the reply arrives.

The Gateway's list paging still uses `updatedAt`. Every activity write also advances `updatedAt`, so any session with recent activity is always inside the loaded 200-session window. The accepted edge case: past that window, the tail of a very large roster may miss a few sessions whose activity is older than the window's cutoff. The Created sort already pages this way.

## Landing order

1. **#194839 lands first**, unchanged. It stops mark read/unread from advancing `updatedAt`. That still matters after this PR: sessions without activity clocks fall back to `updatedAt`, and other consumers still read it (API callers' default order, the Sessions page Updated column).
2. **This PR lands second.** The two PRs touch separate files. I agreed this with the session that owns #194839: it owns `src/gateway/sessions-patch.ts`, its test, `session-unread-ack.ts` and its one-line docs addition; this PR owns the sidebar comparator, the sessions navigation helpers and the sort paragraph in `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md`. If this PR merges first, nothing conflicts or breaks. The order only keeps the history readable.

## Evidence

- **Regression test:** `orders Updated mode by conversation activity, not metadata writes` in `app-sidebar-session-navigation-logic.test.ts`. It fails on the base comparator (`metadata-touched` sorts first) and passes with the fix. The file passes 33/33.
- **Sibling suites:** `app-sidebar.sessions.test.ts`, `lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` and `app-sidebar-session-tree.test.ts` pass 132/132.
- **Browser check (mocked Gateway, not committed):** three synthetic sessions. *Renamed earlier chat* has the newest `updatedAt` and the oldest activity, *Latest reply* has the newest activity, and *Legacy without activity* has no activity clocks. With **Last updated** selected, the base build shows the renamed chat on top; the fix shows Latest reply → Legacy → Renamed.

Before (base):

![Before: Last updated puts the renamed session first](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c563f009-fdef-419d-b7e4-8fff9514485c)

After (this PR):

![After: Last updated follows conversation activity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f75c7285-a297-4b35-93f4-f97723881124)

- **Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` pass, oxlint finds no problems in the 3 changed files, format check and `git diff --check` are clean.
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode, merge-base → `3a76ae22b54d`, priority up to P2) was scoped-clean with no findings. Local ClawSweeper wasn't available on this host.
- **Gaps:** I didn't run a real Gateway and model end to end. That the Gateway advances `updatedAt` on metadata writes is already covered by the existing `sessions-patch.test.ts` assertions for pin and rename. I didn't audit whether every message source records `lastActivityAt`, for example channel messages that arrive without starting a turn, or messages added to a session from outside it. Sources that don't record it keep the current `updatedAt` behavior.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(gateway): keep Last updated position when marking a session unread
body:
## Problem

Choosing **Mark as unread** on a session bumped its `updatedAt`, so with the sidebar sorted by **Last updated** the row jumped to the top. Marking unread is a reminder, not session activity; the row should stay where it is.

Read acknowledgements (`unread: false`) and icon/color-only patches were already recency-neutral (#170405); `unread: true` was the remaining exception.

## Solution

`applySessionsPatchToStore` now treats any read-marker-only patch (`unread: true` or `unread: false`, plus only its identity/CAS preconditions) as recency-neutral via the existing `isReadMarkerOnly` owner in `session-unread-ack.ts`. Patches that combine unread with real changes (pin, rename, archive, …) still age the row as before.

`markedUnreadAt` still advances on every mark, so the conditional-ack revision is unchanged.

## Impact

- Single and batch **Mark as unread** keep the row's Last updated position.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` notes read/unread marks are not session activity.

## Problem

title: fix(gateway): limit restricted roles to public repositories
body:
## Problem

Roles without `operator.write` (on the team Gateway: `guest` with `operator.sessions.write`, and `contributor`) could discover and obtain the source of admin-registered private org repositories (for example `openclaw/openclaworg`). Every path read the shared project registry with no requester check:

- the New session picker (`projects.list`, `projects.checkoutOptions`)
- `sessions.create` with a registry `projectId`
- background (`visible: false`) agent spawns with `projectId`
- children that inherit their parent's checkout
- pasting the repository URL: `projectGitUrl` reused the registry row and refreshed it with the Gateway's GitHub token
- contributors only: project skills via `commands.list`, and `worktrees.list` (every session's paths, repo roots and branches)

## Solution

- New predicate owner `src/gateway/project-access.ts`. A caller without `operator.write` may use a project when it is an agent-workspace pseudo-project (still governed by `roles.agents`), or when its origin is `owner/repo` on the configured GitHub host and `GET repos/{owner}/{repo}` reports `visibility === "public"`. Private, Enterprise `internal`, non-GitHub, credential-bearing or non-default HTTPS-port origins, 404s, rate limits and failures all deny. It reuses `gitHubPublicApi.fetchGitHubJson`, with the server token when available.
- Discovery (`projects.list`, `checkoutOptions`, `commands.list` project skills) caches definitive answers (200, 404) for 10 minutes per API base + `owner/repo`. Every source handoff (`sessions.create`, background spawn, inherited checkout) starts its own GitHub request; it cannot join an earlier in-flight discovery lookup.
- Enforcement sits at requester-aware call sites, not in the registry readers; `projects.remove`, Doctor, clone de-duplication and scratch maintenance keep the raw registry.
  - `sessions.create`: connection scopes; client-less in-process dispatch stays internal. A hidden project returns the same `unknown project id` as a missing one.
  - background spawns: the admitted operator run's effective scopes (membership caps included), else the creator's live role. Owner, cron and unlinked runs stay internal.
  - inherited children (`prepareSessionWorktreeCreation`): the child's requester must reach the parent's project or repository URL; a cwd-based parent without a project is allowed only when it is an agent workspace.
- Scopes: `sessions.create` with `projectGitUrl`, `projects.searchRemote` and `worktrees.list` now need `operator.write`. `worktrees.list` lists host paths for every session, so it is raised rather than filtered; UI callers already tolerate a failed call. `projects.list` returns `defaultRepository` only to writers.
- Control UI: non-write callers get no GitHub search or URL entry. A saved or selected project the Gateway no longer lists falls back to the agent workspace, and a saved repository URL is not restored for non-write callers.
- Docs: `gateway/operator-scopes.md`, `web/control-ui.md`, `concepts/managed-worktrees.md`.

## Accepted edge cases

- Existing checkouts are kept; forking or resetting your own old session on a now-hidden repo re-copies it.
- A repo turning private can stay in the picker (and `commands.list`, `checkoutOptions`) for up to 10 minutes; handoffs are blocked right away.
- Non-GitHub and credential-bearing origins become write-only. Restricted roles lose clone-by-URL, even for public repos. GitHub Enterprise restricted users see public repos only.
- Without a server token, lookups are anonymous (60/h); a rate limit or a missing bundled `github` plugin hides even public repos (fails closed).
- A hidden saved project switches to the workspace without a notice; hidden and removed projects look the same.

## Screenshots

Guest (`operator.sessions.write`) with a saved selection of the private `openclaw/openclaworg` project, then pasting its URL. Same Control UI e2e scenario for both rows (mocked Gateway, synthetic data). **Before:** the UI from this PR's base on `main`, with the full `projects.list` that `main`'s Gateway returns to guests. **After:** this PR's head `98d7168e`, with the list this PR's Gateway returns (private repository filtered out).

| | Saved selection | Paste repository URL |

title: fix: compaction skips configured fallback after quota errors
body:
Closes #194803

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes compaction skipping a configured fallback when a summarization provider returns an HTTP 429 quota error without a separately recognizable rate-limit phrase.

## User Impact

Compaction can try its existing configured fallback instead of stopping at the failed primary summary. This does not replenish quota, add fallback providers, or guarantee that a backup succeeds. No configuration or public API changes are included.

**Review readiness:** focused regression tests and isolated-Gateway checks cover the quota-429 fallback path, including automatic and manual compaction and saved fallback summaries. A subsequent external report also exercises manual compaction with a real fallback model and a replayed primary 429; see below. The exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42426200469) and its applicable CI gate passed. @vyctorbrzezowski approved landing in the linked work session on 2026-11-08; the exact head remains `30ff6a55d5b755cf4f677b9a579e684c72f7282e`. A quota 429 originating from the real primary provider remains untested.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compaction wrappers preserve the original SummaryProviderError and assistant response, but classification used the wrappers’ prefixed display text. Wrapping `Provider API error (429): daily token quota exhausted` can hide the status from the existing text-based fallback adapter.

Use the retained provider response with the existing assistant failure classifier and carry its normalized failure metadata through the existing compaction result. Other failures retain the existing classifier. Reuse the same cause-chain lookup for summary timeout detection.

This is separate from diagnostic-label misclassification in #194759 and the configurable summary cap in #194719. It does not establish what happened in the original historical incident.

## Evidence

Tested from base `f6d1e4c9c56d5d51a5fd1b7bbb912620559654c1`; final candidate tree `9e4ac34dfb899aaf5a27158ac327bea2927f1401`.

- **Red before the fix:** the added `provider quota 429` row failed: only the primary model was requested instead of primary followed by backup; result was `ok: false, compacted: false`.
- **Green after the fix:** `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact-reasons.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed both shards: **10 + 88 tests**. Existing assertions check fallback request order and the persisted summary; timeout and terminal-error cases remain covered.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- Repository formatter and file-scoped lint passed for all three changed TypeScript files: **No problems in 3 files**.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base HEAD` and `git diff --cached --check` passed. The one-line test allocation adds quota wording to an existing regression matrix instead of duplicating its fixture.
- Native local Auto Review returned **scoped-clean at P0-only**, with no findings. It did not execute tests. A subsequent lint-only change replaced parameter reassignment with an equivalent local cause-chain cursor; final tests/typecheck/lint were rerun.
- Final independent native code review of commit `30ff6a55d5b755cf4f677b9a579e684c72f7282e` returned **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, with no actionable findings. This reviewed the four-file patch and supplied frozen source context; it did not rerun tests and noted incomplete visibility into unchanged classifier/harness internals. The existing boundary tests and external runtime evidence remain the execution proof.
- Simplification review retained canonical assistant-error classification as the policy owner; no broad new text matcher or separate fallback policy was added.

An initial incorrectly scoped lint run timed out after visiting unrelated files; the corrected file-scoped run above passed. The external Gateway/stub-provider report below adds separate evidence; hosted CI is tracked in this PR’s Checks tab.


## External verification and handoff

@wr-web [reported an isolated Gateway reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194813#issuecomment-6713323856) on 2026-11-07, with a [linked result summary image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/194803/proof-194803.png). The requester confirmed that this is their agent continuing from their fork, rather than a report personally authored by the requester.

Reported setup: Windows 11, Node v26.12.1, a source Gateway on loopback with isolated state, and `chat.send "/compact"`. The primary HTTP stub returns `429 {"error":{"message":"daily token quota exhausted"}}` on summarization, without an error code or the phrase "too many requests"; the configured fallback stub returns a summary.

| Reported source | Fallback requests | Observed outcome |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `main` at `fc9749f` | 0 | Compaction fails without trying the fallback |
| This PR at `30ff6a5` | 4 | Primary classified as `rate_limit`; fallback candidate succeeds |

The comment and image agree on this result. This session inspected those supplied materials but did not rerun the Windows environment; the image is a result summary, not an independently captured execution trace. This adds reported real-Gateway/HTTP-provider-boundary coverage, not live-model-provider proof.

### macOS raw-artifact verification

The fork-agent follow-up [posted under @saariuslystoned](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194813#issuecomment-6714147421) supplies a [public, commit-pinned evidence bundle](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/tree/019194c82300859866452b3c809762a3d8410db7/pr-194813-gateway-validation) with harness source, redacted Gateway records, per-request stub logs, decoded persisted state, and test logs. It compares this exact PR head with `main` at `1ad3ec3d2081f3c7228b5bed8ae95e3821cd609f`. Environment reported: macOS 26.5.2 arm64; **Bun 1.4.4 runs the Gateway**, while Node v24.22.1 runs the launcher, driver, and tests.

| Case | Base fallback requests / saved compaction | PR fallback requests / saved compaction |

| Budget-triggered, turn 6 | 0 / no | 2 / yes |
| Manual `/compact` | 0 / no | 2 / yes |
| Manual, unstructured fallback summary control | not part of this control | 4 / yes, quality-guard degraded summary |

This session fetched the public files without GitHub authentication, inspected the harness without executing it, independently counted the supplied request records, and compared them with the Gateway decision excerpts and decoded transcript entries. They agree: the primary produces three HTTP 429 attempts; the PR classifies it as `rate_limit`, requests the fallback, and saves a summary containing the fallback marker. The checked unchanged fallback-owner files are byte-identical between the two referenced source commits. These are reviewed external execution artifacts, not a new local rerun.

The unstructured-summary control records four fallback requests plus `quality_guard_degraded_fallback`, supporting the explanation for the Windows report’s four versus the structured-summary runs’ two. The recorded counts are fixture-dependent, not a promise of exactly one or two requests.

**Artifact reading note:** successful runs also have `fallbackSummaryInHistory: false` and `sessionsCompactionCount: null` in `summary.json`. The supplied test logs confirm **10 + 88 passing PR tests**, **79 adjacent tests across four files**, a passing core typecheck, and the quota-429 row as the only failing row among six fallback cases on the red base. ```

The runtime checks in the macOS subsection above use loopback HTTP stub providers. The later real-fallback report below adds separate evidence. Errors carrying only a type/body signal without an HTTP status remain outside this proof.

### Reported live-fallback validation (manual compaction)

A [follow-up posted under @saariuslystoned](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194813#issuecomment-6715639469) reports an isolated macOS Gateway run on this exact PR head, using Bun 1.4.4 for the Gateway and Node v24.22.1 for the driver. This session read the public report; it did not execute this live run or independently recount real provider calls. title: fix(plugins): follow the stable channel for official plugin selectors
body:
Fixes #194804

## What Problem This Solves

After core moves from beta to stable, saved official-plugin `@beta` selectors can keep resolving the beta line and downgrade a matching stable plugin to an older compatible beta.

## User Impact

Trusted official plugins with saved prerelease channel tags now follow the effective stable channel. Updates prefer the core-matching release, use `latest` when that release is unavailable, and save `latest` with a warning after success. The saved selector keeps core preference and the stable version floor on every subsequent stable update. If no compatible stable replacement meets the core release floor, the installed plugin and selector are retained with a warning.

This channel-tag recovery preserves exact-version and range selector handling, third-party plugins, explicit command selectors, and the beta update channel. Existing managed release-pin recovery still applies. Historical records do not distinguish automatically saved channel tags from authored tags, so both follow the documented stable policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the channel decision in the shared npm/ClawHub update selector owner and enforce the stable floor on the staged artifact before publication, including compatibility fallback. The existing install transaction retains the old payload on refusal. The updater performing plugin convergence must contain this fix; it needs no new config option, schema, or update protocol.

## Evidence

- Production updater and npm installer regression fixtures fail five cases on `a384228dd7b4`, including an install-record downgrade from `2026.11.1` to `2026.10.10-beta.5`.
- Independent follow-up review found that normalized ClawHub `@latest` lost its policy on the second update. Both new two-pass regressions fail at `71924279b576` and pass with this repair: a published core target remains preferred, and a missing second core target cannot admit stale `latest` below core.
- `update.test.ts`, `install-channel-specs.test.ts`, `install.npm-spec.test.ts`, and `plugin-version-drift.test.ts`: **210 passed**, 70.81 seconds command wall time. The ClawHub regression exercises the real update owner and staged version callback with a fixture installer that publishes the on-disk package only after the callback accepts it. ClawHub installation is simulated.
- Touched-file lint and compiler diagnostics via `run-oxlint.mjs --type-check`, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2) of the complete repair against `71924279b576`: **scoped clean**, no actionable findings. Hosted ClawSweeper previously acknowledged intake.
- The PR's isolated allocation is **257 lines**: the original 195 plus 62 for repeated-update alignment and fallback-floor regressions.
- **MISSING:** live registry/CLI and latest-stable upgrade proof. The earlier configured Crabbox/Testbox attempt queued and its task-owned lease was stopped; no remote proof command executed ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42415155437)). PR CI supplies broad validation.

title: fix(ui): quiet pending steer states
body:
## Problem

Pending steers from #193665 work well, but a few edges are rough:

- Messages that cannot be sent early show a warning-styled line under every waiting bubble (`Waiting for exec; cannot interrupt safely.`), using internal tool names.
- A refused **Send now** puts a sticky notice above the composer (`Sending a pending steer now requires session write access.` / `The conversation changed…`). It stays there after the user sends new messages, so it reads as if those failed.
- Several waiting messages each show their own row (**Send now** or a warning), which is redundant: waiting steers are delivered together.
- A pending bubble can show the delivered footer (sender, time, copy/comment/rewind) on hover or focus next to **Send now**, and pending bubbles sit at different spacing than delivered ones.
- Viewers without steer access see nothing under their pending message.

## Solution

Presentation-only changes in the Control UI. The Gateway, steering lifecycle and **Send now** interruption are unchanged.

- **One row for all waiting steers.** Waiting steers drain together at the next model boundary, so a single **Send now** sits under the newest steer that can interrupt. When none can (or the viewer cannot steer), the newest shows a muted **Steering…** label instead. Example: three rapid messages where only the first two can interrupt → **Send now** under the second, nothing else.
- **Plain copy.** **Steering…** has no spinner; the reason is on hover and is the accessible name: “Steering — sends when the current step finishes.” or “…on the next model turn.” No tool names.
- **Permission-aware.** **Send now** renders only when the viewer can steer (already gated by session access). Everyone else sees **Steering…**.
- **No composer notice for Send now.** A refused or failed **Send now** refreshes the pending list and the row shows its current state. Dismiss errors still use the notice.
- **Delivered spacing.** Steer rows use the same footer and action-row slots delivered messages use, so bubbles keep identical positions before and after delivery. Sender, timestamp and footer actions appear once the message is delivered.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui.md`, `docs/concepts/queue-steering.md`.

Accepted edge: if a viewer loses steer access while **Send now** is on screen, the click is refused quietly and the message stays queued.

## Screenshots

Before → after screenshots (mocked Gateway, synthetic content) are attached in comments below. The latest comment shows the four states with identical bubble positions.

## Evidence

- Component tests: `chat-message` (including row assignment across steers waiting together), group, markdown, queue/steer lifecycle, pending-inputs pagination, session-controls and transcript projection suites — 104 passed.
- Browser e2e `chat-flow.messaging` (10 passed): one **Send now** on the newest sendable steer; an earlier sendable steer carries it when the newest cannot interrupt; refused Send now shows no composer notice; blocked steers show one **Steering…**; Send now still delivers.

title: fix(ui): keep Worked timing on earlier completed turns
body:
## Problem

In Control UI chat, a completed turn's "Worked for 47m 11s" header drops back to plain "Worked" once a newer run starts in the same session. Only the session row (`lastRunId` / `runtimeMs`) could supply a duration, and that row only describes the latest run.

## Solution

`collapseCompletedTurnWork` still uses the session row while it describes the run. For earlier runs it now reads the transcript instead: it measures from the prompt that started the run (matched by its `<runId>:user` key) to the last `recordTimestampMs` write of that run's output. The duration is the write time of the output, not when the message was created, which avoids the original concern that creation timestamps miss the final model request. Output with no recorded write time, and work spanning several runs, still shows no duration.

Accepted edge case: right after a newer run starts, the earlier turn's duration may differ by about a second from the lifecycle value it had before. On live sessions, the transcript value was within 1–4 s of `runtimeMs`.

## Evidence

Preserve the actual, safe startup-failure explanation in desktop chat instead of replacing it with a generic error. Keep it concise: the failure statement only, without appended operator/recovery/retry advice or the generic “Check any completed work before trying again” banner.

## User Impact and Scope

- **Web Control UI and macOS:** show the first failure statement, including after reload. For example: “OpenClaw's storage worker ran out of memory.”
- **Channels, iOS, and Android:** existing shared message text and delivery behavior stay unchanged, including when a phone opens the same conversation.
- Unknown errors remain generic. No changes to permissions, retries, model selection, database behavior, or message delivery.

## Implementation

Capture explicitly public failure copy before startup errors are flattened, then carry its first sentence as desktop presentation metadata rather than replacing shared transcript content. Web consumers explicitly opt in; native decoding and rendering are gated with `#if os(macOS)`. Native preflight desktop copy remains separate from the default channel-facing renderer. The global storage-error wording remains unchanged. The Web UI no longer adds a blanket completed-work warning.

## Evidence

- After consolidating duplicate test scaffolding, 40 native-harness tests, 9 reader/preflight-helper tests, and 6 public `chat.send` startup tests passed locally. The unchanged dispatch coverage previously passed 23 tests. The concise-copy correction was initially red on three Gateway cases and two UI assertions.
- 46 UI tests and 3 browser E2E tests passed on the unchanged product code. Core, Web UI, and affected test-graph typechecks passed, including the corrected reader callback in the QA product proof. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The QA product proof itself was not replayed for its callback-only change.
- Earlier unchanged-layer proof: 14 history-paging tests, 118 display/lifecycle tests, and 9 failure-recorder tests passed.
- The wording and test-consolidation changes were reviewed directly, without subagents. Earlier full-branch independent review and committed-delta autoreview found no actionable issues; those reports precede these updates.
- **Scoped test allocation:** `config/test-lines-allocations/194741-desktop-startup-errors.txt` allocates the exact 317 net new test lines after removing 51 lines of duplicate scaffolding. These regressions are needed to distinguish desktop-only display from shared/mobile content, preserve startup causes across persistence, exercise native consent/binding guards, reject malformed metadata, and verify concise rendering/reload. The shared baseline is unchanged; the allocation follows the documented per-change mechanism and does not suppress a test or product failure.
- **Native verification limit:** this Linux host has no Swift toolchain or connected Mac. Native runtime tests and macOS visual execution are not claimed. Landing is now requested; required CI is being checked on the current head.
- Gateway proof injects preparation failures before model execution. Browser proof uses synthetic history and checks reload behavior; neither is a live replay of the production incident.

title: fix: keep repository mentions out of file links

Fixes repository mentions such as `openclaw/openclaw.ai` becoming workspace-file links in chat, which hides the owner portion and shows a misleading file preview affordance.

title: fix(subagents): parents miss results from independently resumed children
body:
## Merge-Readiness Status

**Published at `a0abf6c`; attributable repairs are verified, but CI remains red on an inherited test-line budget deficit.** All selected test, build, type, lint, architecture, PostgreSQL, and applicable CodeQL lanes passed. No GitHub merge or deployment is requested or performed.

## What Problem This Solves

Parent sessions could miss successful child results when children were admitted independently or the originating invocation had already ended.

## User Impact

Accepted results return once to their recorded parent without keeping the spawning human invocation alive. The parent's model ceiling remains a restriction, not a permission grant. Normal tool, sandbox, role, lifecycle, and external-effect checks remain in force. No new settings or stores are introduced.

Older tasks with unrecoverable model-policy facts retain their result but cannot automatically resume inference; send a new message to continue. Previously terminal non-delivery receipts are not automatically replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use registry/controller/receipt ownership for accepted result settlement instead of retained human completion custody. Preserve the recorded Gateway and requester lifecycle, carry model restrictions independently, and bind each completion's ceiling to its exact run—not a newer followup in the same child session.

Native harness and ordinary one-way replies keep their separately owned live custody. Retained native work preserves independent requester ceilings without freezing the operator's otherwise-live model policy. title: feat(openai): add GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst and Flare models
body:
Related: #193523 (open; adds GIF output and also registers the 2.6 models)

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI released `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.6-flare` on 2026-11-04, but OpenClaw's OpenAI image provider doesn't list them. `image_generate action=list` stops at GPT Image 2.5.

Requests with an explicit `openai/gpt-image-2.6-*` model already reached OpenAI: a 1024x1024 low-quality generation worked on the current release. The gap is the advertised catalog and the per-model capabilities. Without them, OpenClaw silently drops `xhigh`/`max` quality and snaps `auto` or custom sizes such as `1536x864` to a fixed size for these models.

## User Impact

`image_generate` and `openclaw infer image` now list both 2.6 models. They accept the same options as GPT Image 2.5 for generation and edits:

- `low` through `max` quality
- `auto` or custom `WIDTHxHEIGHT` sizes
- transparent PNG/WebP backgrounds
- up to 5 reference images

The default stays `openai/gpt-image-2`. Images from the direct Images API now report the quality OpenAI actually applied, where the tool used to report it as unknown.

These options apply to the direct API-key route. The catalog doesn't distinguish sign-in methods, so on ChatGPT/Codex sign-in, 2.6 may not behave as listed (see Gaps).

## Why This Change Was Made

- The 2.6 IDs join the existing 2.5 model family list, so both versions share one set of capabilities. The capability table didn't need a new mechanism.
- OpenAI's guide and API reference list both 2.6 models for `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`. But the reference's text on quality, sizes and backgrounds still names only 2.5. Live API validation checks show 2.6 responding the same way as 2.5 (Evidence below), and a source comment cites them.
- The catalog constants and capabilities moved, unchanged, into `extensions/openai/image-generation-models.ts`. The line-cap ratchet rejected any growth in `image-generation-provider.ts` (853 lines, cap 700).
- On the "quality unknown" report: `quality` was already in the request body. The direct Images API echoes the applied `quality` at the top level of the response, but OpenClaw only read per-image quality from the Codex Responses route. The response reader now copies it onto each image.
- Pricing: the OpenAI image provider has no model-specific price or usage-cost tables, only token counts, so there's no 2.6 pricing to add. OpenAI lists 2.6 at $5/$1.25 per 1M text input/cached tokens, $8/$2 per 1M image input/cached tokens and $30 per 1M image output tokens, the same for both models ([pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), [Sunburst](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst), [Flare](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-image-2.6-flare)).
- Test-line budget: the new regression file adds 98 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/openai-gpt-image-26-catalog.txt`. The existing OpenAI image provider suite sits exactly at its 1000-line cap, so the 2.6 regressions need a sibling file with its own HTTP and auth mocks. Nothing nearby was a duplicate worth deleting to offset the growth.
- Catalog v3: obviyus is working on catalog v3 so that new models like these won't need an OpenClaw release. When it lands, this hardcoded image list can move into catalog data. Until then, this PR is the stopgap.

Deferred: these need new `image_generate` parameters or output formats, which means maintainer approval and prompt-prefix review (`docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`):

- `complexity` (`low`/`medium`/`high`; OpenAI defaults to `high` when it's omitted)
- markup-guided edits (`markup` on `/v1/images/edits`)
- SVG output (`output_format: "svg"`, generations only, `n=1`)
- animated GIF output (`output_format: "gif"`, `frame_count` 2–16, `frame_duration_ms` 20–2000). #193523 covers this. Its body says `frameCount` allows 2–64, but OpenAI's guide and API reference currently say 2–16.

None of these fits an existing provider option without a schema change, so none is included. The docs say they aren't exposed yet. Docs: [GPT Image 2.6 guide section](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation#gpt-image-26).

Overlap: #193523 also registers the 2.6 models, as part of its GIF work. This PR is the catalog-only part, so it can land without the tool-schema change. Whichever lands second will need a small rebase in the OpenAI image catalog.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests:** `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.models.test.ts` runs the real `generateImage` runtime against the provider with mocked HTTP. It checks both 2.6 models for catalog listing, `1536x864`, `xhigh`, transparent PNG, no ignored overrides, and applied quality reported on the image. It also checks a 2.6 edit with `size: "auto"` and `quality: "max"`. All 3 tests failed on the base with only the test file applied, and pass with the fix.
- **Test cost:** `pnpm test extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.models.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 39.1s wall time from a cold transform cache. Transform was 96% of that; the tests themselves were about 1%. CI seconds for this file weren't broken out.
- **CI:** all required checks pass on head `f926737`: 39 succeeded and 65 were skipped, including `openclaw/ci-gate` and the baseline ratchets.
- **Focused suites:** all OpenAI image provider suites (models, provider, usage, direct-errors, url, auth, tls, codex-response), plus `src/image-generation` and `image-generate-tool` tests, pass.
- **`pnpm check:changed`:** all lanes pass (extensions lint, tsgo extensions/test, format, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, docs) except `changelog attributions`. That one fails on existing `CHANGELOG/*` lines this PR doesn't touch. With the allocation, `check:test-lines-ratchet` also passes locally (slack 41).
- **Docs anchors:** `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports no problems in the changed pages. Its 2 failures are in pages this PR doesn't touch (`/tools/acp-agents-setup` and `releases/2026.10.1.md`). The kept `#gpt-image-2.5` anchor still resolves.
- **Full `pnpm test extensions/openai/`:** 87/90 files pass. The 3 failures are realtime/GPT-Live transport and token-sharing OAuth tests, which don't import image code. They fail the same way when run alone in this sandbox.
- **Live API capability checks** (2026-11-07, API key, direct `/v1/images/generations`):
  - `size: "1536x864"` and `16x16` get the same pixel-budget validation as `gpt-image-2.5-flare`. `gpt-image-1` rejects custom sizes.
  - `background: "transparent"` with JPEG gets "not supported for JPEG output format", the same as 2.5. `gpt-image-2` gets "Transparent background is not supported for this model".
  - OpenAI accepted `quality: "xhigh"` and `"max"` for both 2.6 models without a validation error, like 2.5: each request was still running when cut off after 6s. `gpt-image-1` returns 400 immediately: "does not support quality 'xhigh'". This shows the API doesn't reject these values; no full `xhigh`/`max` generation was run. The completed live runs below used `low`.
  - A raw 2.6 Flare response includes top-level `"quality": "low"`, `"size": "1024x1024"` and token usage.
- **Live OpenClaw runs (this branch)**, using an isolated profile/state, an explicit API-key route and `openclaw infer image` (same runtime + provider path `image_generate` uses):
  - `infer image providers`: OpenAI `defaultModel: gpt-image-2`; models include `gpt-image-2.6-flare` and `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`.
  - `generate --model openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst --quality low --size 1024x1024`: PNG 1024x1024, `ignoredOverrides: []` (quality sent).
  - `generate --model openai/gpt-image-2.6-flare --quality low --size 1024x1024`: PNG 1024x1024, `ignoredOverrides: []`.
  - `edit --model openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst --quality low --size auto` (recolor the generated lemon): PNG 1254x1254, with `auto` sent as-is rather than snapped; the visual edit was correct.
- **Local review:** autoreview (codex engine) on the committed branch range, run twice with `--mode branch --base origin/main`:
  - At `--max-priority P2` before publishing: "patch is correct (0.91)".
  - At `--max-priority P3` on the final head before landing, with the runtime, tool and image-asset sources as context: "patch is correct (0.88)".
  - Neither run had accepted/actionable findings.

title: feat(ui): ask about a selection in a new session
body:
## Problem
The transcript selection toolbar can send a passage to the main composer or to Side chat, but you can't start a fresh session about it. Today that means copying the text and pasting it into Cmd+K.

## Solution
- The selection toolbar now shows three plain buttons: **Add to chat** (renamed from "Add to message"), **Ask in side chat**, and **New session**. There's no hover state, sub-menu or layout shift.
- The toolbar is 31px tall (3px panel padding, 24px rows) on every device, instead of 36–52px depending on the pointer type.
- **New session** creates the same selection annotation that **Add to chat** creates. The shell's palette owner receives it in memory through the open event. It is never saved in the lazy shell descriptor, and it reaches the launcher whether the palette is still loading or already loaded. The launcher draft then adopts it as an attachment.
- When you start the session, the passage is sent as quoted message text ahead of your prompt, the same way the chat composer sends comments, and mention offsets shift to match. It is not uploaded as a file.
- The launcher can't reopen the comment editor because the passage has no transcript anchor there. Its comment preview therefore hides **Edit** (`commentsEditable: false`). **Delete** and **Remove all** are handled by the palette draft.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/chat.md` and `docs/tools/btw.md`.

## Evidence
- New e2e in `chat-selection-to-main.e2e.test.ts`: select text → **New session** → the launcher shows the excerpt chip with no Edit button → Ctrl/Cmd+Enter. `sessions.create` receives `message: "> <passage>\n\nSummarize the risks."` with no `attachments`, and the chat draft is unchanged.
- These pass with the renamed button: `chat-selection-to-main`, `chat-comment-draft-recovery`, `chat-comment-lifecycle`, `chat-comment-pane-retirement`, `chat-session-companion-composer` (28 tests). `chat-selection-popup.test.ts` passes (20 tests), including the New session routing.
- A recorded lifecycle run (real mouse drag-selection, 1280×800) passed. It covers the toolbar at 31px with the three buttons in order, Escape dismissal, and each action through to its request: **Add to chat** → comment → `chat.send` with the quote, comment and prompt; **Ask in side chat** → comment → `sessions.companion.ask` with the selection context, answered in Side chat; **New session** → launcher → `sessions.create` with the quote and prompt. The video is in the requesting chat.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, `ui:i18n:sync`/`check`, docs format check, and `git diff --check` are all clean.

## Notes
- The launcher chip uses the existing comment chip copy ("1 comment").
- On touch the rows are 24px tall, below the shared 40–44px menu row height. This was chosen deliberately so the floating toolbar stays compact and looks the same everywhere.

title: fix(cron): retain rearmed exits until prior receipts settle
body:
Related: #189469, [original main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42391247774/job/128459394152), and [prior PR-head failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42395507438/job/128472374474).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a rearmed on-exit automation losing its next exit while the previous execution receipt is still active, without making queue shutdown wait forever for an abort-ignoring payload.

## User Impact

The replacement exit waits for the previous durable execution receipt to settle. Caller cancellation and queue shutdown retain their existing result boundary. No configuration, schema, dependency, timeout, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

#189469 retained active receipts until interrupted execution actually settles. The queue discarded its launch context after returning the caller result, so the next on-exit admission could find an active receipt with no waitable predecessor.

The finalizer now exposes its existing receipt-settlement promise to the launch context. Same-job admission joins it; queue shutdown joins only the original launch result. The receipt owner still performs and tracks the terminal write. The earlier broad per-launch async-work scope is removed: it incorrectly pulled abort-ignoring background work into queue teardown.

The existing Gateway regression holds the real receipt-only finalization and proves both boundaries: receipt admission stays pending while queue completion proceeds. Original two-call, two-spawn, and disabled-job assertions remain. The separate allocation is exactly 38 net test lines; the shared baseline and regression fixtures are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Original main `61bdbccd9dbd`: `src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts` / `re-arms on-exit echo rearmed when its next exit arrives before the previous payload finishes` expected two calls and saw one. Source attribution: `7caee827c5be` (#189469); verified human contributor credit is preserved.

CI run `42395507438`, job `128472374474`: `src/cron/service/timer.timeout-watchdog.test.ts` hooks timed out at `test/helpers/cron/service-regression-fixtures.ts:88`; `src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` also timed out in scheduled-batch timeout recovery. These are attributed to the removed broad scope wait, not relabeled as inherited failures.
- Final touched-file lint with TypeScript diagnostics, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. No fixture edits, skips, retries, timeout increases, or weakened assertions.
- Installed autoreview assessed the complete final working candidate at P0–P2 and found no additional defect. Its sole P1 finding identified the old indexed implementation's shutdown wait; staging the reviewed receipt-only repair removed that indexed version. All eleven assessment passes completed; no clean machine verdict is claimed for the superseded mixed index/working snapshot.
- Exact head `f898d1fa5486beb31dc279118759f5525f6e651e`, [CI run 42398081481](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42398081481): [changed-8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42398081481/job/128480071082) passed all 12 watchdog tests and all 16 timer regression tests, including scheduled-batch timeout recovery (102 ms). title: fix(ui): Undo after archiving a session restores it instantly
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after archiving a session, clicking **Undo** takes a noticeable moment to bring the row back, because the archive (including stopping its active work) has already been sent and Undo has to send a second unarchive request and wait for a roster refresh.

## User Impact

User impact: archiving still hides the session immediately, and **Undo** now brings it back instantly with nothing sent to the Gateway. The archive is only sent once the Undo notification closes (timeout, dismiss, or replaced by the next archive) or the page is left, so active work keeps running until the Undo window has actually passed.

Behavior change to note: archiving is now applied a few seconds later than before (the toast duration, paused while hovered or focused). Accepted edge cases, documented in code and docs: a Gateway reconnect during the window drops the pending archive and the row reappears; closing the tab sends the archive best-effort, so a lost final request also leaves the session unarchived and visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Undo was a compensating action (archive now, unarchive later). It is now a cancellation: the shared archive runtime holds the request behind the Undo toast and every toast ending other than Undo commits it, as does `pagehide`. Undo only releases the local pending-archive state.

All archive entry points with Undo — sidebar row and menu, chat header, ⌘⇧A, bulk/tree archive, and the Sessions page — go through this one path. The Sessions page previously had its own archive-then-restore flow; it now uses the shared owner and hides held rows the same way the sidebar does. The Undo machinery that re-sent unarchive and restored personal pins is removed, since nothing is pruned before the commit.

Production delta: +137 / −357 across 4 files.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`session-organizer-archive.test.ts` › *hides the session and lets Undo restore it without any Gateway write*): red on the base runtime, green with this change. Companion cases cover committing exactly once on timeout/dismiss/replace and on `pagehide`, and a held tree committing after navigation with partial failure reporting.
- **Browser e2e** (`ui-e2e` lane, mocked Gateway, real bundled UI): archive → row hidden, toast with Undo, zero `sessions.patch`; Undo → row back, still zero requests; close the toast → archive sent, "Archiving…" while pending, failure restores the row with an error, success keeps it hidden and the chat open. Also updated: Sessions page kebab archive, nested archive dialog, archive-history QA, observer-notice/Undo coexistence. All 4 e2e files pass.
- **Unit/DOM suites**: archive runtime, batch mutations, sidebar interactions/sessions, Sessions page archive outcomes (held page archive, navigation/reconnect/failure, held tree), plus surrounding Sessions page and session mutation suites. Re-ran the core suites and `pnpm tsgo:ui` after replaying onto current `main` (no upstream changes to these files).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and format on changed files: clean.
- **Local review**: autoreview (codex, gpt-6.1-sol, `--mode local`, max priority P1) on the complete change: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` archive paragraph updated.

Gap: no live-Gateway run; the browser proof uses the mocked Gateway e2e harness. No visual design change — the toast and rows render as before, only the timing of the Gateway write changes.

title: fix(ui): discard composer draft when a session is archived
body:
## Problem

When you archive a session with unsent text in the composer, that text comes back if you unarchive the session. Archiving already hides the composer behind the "This session is archived" banner. The draft stays in memory and in draft storage, though, and reappears in the composer after Unarchive.

## Solution

When the selected chat session is seen as archived, its composer draft is now discarded. That includes text, mentions, attachments, the reply target and goal mode. The empty composer is saved through the normal composer-persistence path, so the stored draft and its recovery copy are cleared as well.

- New `setSelectedChatSessionArchived` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-session-archive.ts`
- It is used by the three places that apply the selected session's archive state: the `session.message` event, the `sessions.changed` event, and the chat history refresh.

## Impact

- Archive, then Unarchive, now gives an empty composer. This covers archiving from this tab, from another client, or by an agent while the session is open.
- Opening a session that is already archived also discards any draft that was restored for it.
- Accepted edge cases:
  - Undo on the "Session archived" toast does not bring the draft back.
  - If a session is archived while no pane has it open, and then unarchived before anyone opens it, its stored draft can still come back.

## Evidence

- Regression: `ui/src/e2e/session-management.archive.e2e.test.ts` now types a draft before archiving and checks that the composer is empty after Unarchive.

title: feat(scripts): add archive delta research benchmark
body:
## Problem

Provide a repeatable archive-delta research control to measure bandwidth savings without treating an archive experiment as native updater proof.

## Changes

- Add a bounded, single-threaded Zstandard archive benchmark that verifies the exact reconstructed target SHA-256 before reporting success.
- Add four CLI tests covering usage, successful reporting, corruption rejection, and preservation of an existing output directory.
- Document the benchmark procedure, measurements, and proof limits.

No runtime updater, dependency, update feed, or release change. Both human co-author attribution trailers are retained in the commit.

## Evidence and limits

The recorded one-run arm64 archive control for `2026.10.10` → `2026.11.1` measured **463,392,318 bytes → 125,815,187 bytes**, a **72.85% reduction**. Externally observed peak memory was approximately **925 MiB**; this is a material memory caveat, not a general savings or performance guarantee.

This is an archive-control result, **not native Sparkle proof**. Zstandard patches are not Sparkle patches and must not be placed in appcasts. Exact reconstruction does not verify signing, installation, fallback, or rollback.

Complementary opt-in macOS draft: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194669

## Validation

- Four focused CLI tests passed.
- Type-aware lint and script-test leaf typecheck passed.

The common config resolver recognizes the published database shape only with populated, unanchored SQLite shared state and a PostgreSQL Workboard anchor. The config writer preserves canonical engine fields as root-owned siblings of includes, leaving included connection references intact. Database-port preflight persists those fields before source capture, so publication and recovery do not depend on an anchor that the port replaces.

The simplification pass retained one normalization owner, moved write projection into that owner, and reused physical inspection/cleanup rather than adding another reader or cache. title: fix(gateway): park the service on older agent database schemas
body:

## What Problem This Solves

A managed Gateway can repeatedly restart when an older agent database requires offline migration, including after a direct global npm replacement.

## User Impact

The existing maintenance handler parks the macOS LaunchAgent and exits 78 with stop → `openclaw doctor --fix` → start guidance. Existing systemd and Windows supervisor handling treats that exit as terminal. Operators still need to perform the offline repair.
