## Why This Change Was Made

The older-agent-version refusal now raises the existing `StartupMaintenanceRequiredError` with kind `state-migrations`. Existing worker serialization and nested-error handling preserve this kind. Doctor's raw-entry inspection explicitly defers that same kind when schema-repair deferral is enabled. Current-schema admission and the existing startup warning remain unchanged; no transport or schema change is needed.

## Evidence

- Gateway routing: the frozen schema-25 fixture produces a real read-only admission refusal, round-trips through wrapped worker error serialization, and reaches parking once at both CLI startup boundaries without changing database bytes. Both cases failed on `f4668bd0e161`; 187 focused tests and broad CI passed at `bc61f8197c45` before this Doctor follow-up.
- Doctor import: the new all-agents regression fails at `bc61f8197c45` because schema 25 aborts preparation. With the fix, the old database stays byte-identical while another agent's history is imported. The newer-schema control already passed on that base and still refuses import with legacy sources unchanged.

Production/test types, baseline/test-line ratchets, lint, Node tests, artifact build/checks, and all PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. The CI, dependency, and security review contexts are green; no CI repair or rerun was needed.

The standard QR remains the default. **Use lobster QR** displays image-led lobster artwork across the code, **Download lobster QR** saves its full-size PNG, and **Use standard QR** returns to the original fallback. Desktop keyboard navigation and the actual mobile sharing page use the same implementation. Copying and sharing permissions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested by @vincentkoc: https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2118984081904214120

This builds on the shared plain QR owner landed in #180292, rather than adding a second sharing renderer. It follows [Hackaday’s module-center technique](https://hackaday.com/2026/11/06/using-halftone-images-in-qr-codes-without-upsetting-scanners/): preserve each 3×3 center, every function region and a four-module white quiet zone while the surrounding cells carry the canonical monochrome lobster. High error correction and modest peripheral QR contrast support scanning; the image is not pasted over data.

The original faint periphery, density cutoff, duplicate plain-PNG encoder, DOM parsing and eager shared CSS/copy were removed. One lazy presentation retains standard fallback, resets artwork selection when the URL changes, and registers its embedded controls with menu navigation. No dependency, configuration, schema or access-policy change is introduced. The exact +148 regression-test lines have a separate justified allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc

## Work sessions

## Evidence

- **30 focused tests passed** across four files (7.69 s wall). The image-led regression fails the incoming implementation: zero image-led pixels versus the required >68,445.
- **4 built-UI E2E flows passed** (20.06 s): desktop/mobile × light/dark, realistic long URL, actual desktop Tab/Enter entry, PNG download and standard-code restoration.
- **Independent ZBar decoding:** all four same-frame displayed crops and all four actual downloaded PNGs decoded to the displayed URL. Three additional realistic Team URLs decoded at 240px and native export size.
- **Production UI build including its performance gate passed:** normalized chat boot gzip 1,300,511 B ≤ 1,301,131 B. No budgets were raised. UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, controller guard, English baseline/verification and product whitespace checks pass.
- Parent independent **autoreview through Codex, P0–P2**, reviewed the complete local candidate against integrated main 437b1993291d43620fd3fb1b073312141e983d79: no actionable findings. Parent also inspected the complete product patch and rendered desktop/mobile artwork. The reviewer did not execute tests; the runtime results above are from the implementation lane. A subsequent documentation-only change describes the verified control labels.
- The built Control UI uses synthetic mock-Gateway fixtures, not an authenticated live Gateway. No phone-camera test or universal scanning guarantee is claimed; standard QR and copying remain available. WebKit is left to PR CI.

**CI follow-up:** [Run 42807656715](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42807656715) caught a test-only callback returning `false | Promise<void>`. An explicit async callback retains image decoding and every assertion while returning `Promise<void>` on both paths. Targeted lint/format and independent Codex P0–P2 delta review pass. Production code and the inspected visual/decoder proof are unchanged. title: fix(control-ui): changing Gateway auth mode in Settings autosaves a lockout
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: changing the Gateway authentication mode in Control UI Settings (for example token → password) autosaves immediately, before a password can be entered, which signs the browser out and can lock every client out of the Gateway. The same applies to trusted-proxy and any other mode.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can switch Gateway auth modes from Settings without losing access. The change only takes effect when they press Apply with the selected mode's required settings filled in, and the browser stays connected with the credential it just set.

Behavior change for other clients: a `config.set`, `config.patch` or `config.apply` sent to a running Gateway (including `openclaw config set` routed through it) is now refused when it would change Gateway auth into a state that Gateway cannot start with. Set the credential first, or the mode and credential in one write. Writes made while no Gateway is running are unchanged. There is no config schema change and no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Gateway auth edits no longer ride the autosaved config draft. The Authentication section on Settings → Infrastructure → Gateway stages `gateway.auth` edits (including ones made through the generic Auth group): changing the mode reveals that mode's fields, shows "Unsaved changes" with Apply and Cancel, and Cancel restores the saved mode. Unrelated settings keep autosaving without carrying the pending auth edit.
- Apply stays disabled until the selected mode is usable: token/password need a credential when switching into that mode; trusted-proxy needs `trustedProxy.userHeader` and at least one `gateway.trustedProxies` entry, and drops the shared token as the runtime requires. Mode and credentials go out together as one base-hash-checked `config.patch`, sent as an independent write on the route held secret fields already use, so it never joins the form draft, its Retry, or the shared save status. A base-hash conflict from an unrelated save is retried once on the refreshed config.
- A staged edit belongs to the Gateway connection it was made on (the presentation scope held secret fields already use). Switching to another Gateway, or signing in with another credential, drops it with a notice; it is never shown or sent there. If `gateway.auth` was saved differently elsewhere in the meantime, Apply sends nothing, discards the edit and says so. The edit stays staged across a reconnect to the same Gateway and across Settings navigation, and is only ever applied by Apply.
- After an apply that sets a typed token or password, the Control UI hands it to the existing Gateway connection path (the same in-memory/session path the login gate uses) and reconnects instead of dropping to the login screen. Secrets are not put in URLs, logs or persisted drafts. When the mode is switched to one whose secret is only saved (the page cannot read it back), the pending-change line says the browser will sign in again with the saved token or password after Apply.
- `config.set`, `config.patch` and `config.apply` (form, raw editor and other clients) reject a submission that changes `gateway.auth` or `gateway.trustedProxies` into a state the serving Gateway would refuse at its next reload or restart. The decision is the Gateway's own startup and reload security check, run on the submitted config with that Gateway's startup overrides applied, so environment credentials, `--auth`/`--password` overrides, a runtime-generated token and the listener's bind all count: password mode without a resolvable password, token mode without a token, trusted-proxy without its user header or proxy list or with a shared token, and turning auth off on a non-loopback listener are refused before anything is written. A refusal the saved config already had is not attributed to the write, so unrelated writes and edits that leave it in place stay accepted. The error names the missing setting and never echoes secrets.

Out of scope (follow-up): automatic confirm-or-revert rollback when the browser cannot reconnect after an apply.

Accepted limits:

- The write check judges the candidate against the listener the Gateway is serving on. One write that changes auth together with `gateway.bind` or the Tailscale mode is checked against the listener it replaces; change the bind first.
- A token or password SecretRef whose provider has not answered at write time is accepted, and resolved at startup as before. A SecretRef supplied only as a startup override is not resolved by the write check and does not count.
- Reloading the browser discards a staged change (nothing was applied). The reconnect after an apply is a new sign-in, so other unsaved held secret fields are dropped with their existing notice.

Upgrade and config safety: the diff touches no config schema, types, defaults, Doctor or migration code. Startup and reload run the same security check as before (the reloader's closure moved into a shared factory with the same inputs). The write check runs only when the submitted `gateway.auth`/`gateway.trustedProxies` differ from the saved ones, and rejects only a refusal the saved config does not already have, so configs with unusual but working auth keep loading and keep accepting unrelated writes (covered by the "already incomplete auth config" tests and the `--password` startup-flag run below).

Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/194538-gateway-auth-staged-apply.txt` records this PR's exact net test growth (601 lines); the earlier head failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` on the test-line ceiling without it. The tests cover the two new owners (the staged-auth owner and the write check) and their boundaries; there was no existing suite to consolidate them into.

## Evidence

Head e64a024 (merge of `main` @ 407537b into the PR branch, then the fixes; not rebased, because the Gateway publisher only fast-forwards the published branch).

Real Control UI against task-owned loopback Gateways with synthetic configs (Playwright, Chromium), on a build of this head's code taken just before two behavior-neutral edits (how the write check receives its request context, and type narrowing in the Authentication section); the unit, handler and type checks below ran after them:

- token → password: choosing **Password** shows "Unsaved changes", Apply disabled, and sends no config write; the file still says `token`. After typing a password and pressing Apply, the browser sent exactly one `config.patch` with `baseHash` carrying `{"gateway":{"auth":{"mode":"password","password":<redacted>}}}`; the Gateway log shows `config.patch write … changedPaths=gateway.auth.mode,gateway.auth.password`, an in-process restart, and the same browser reconnecting with `auth=password` about 5 s later with no login gate. The card shows Password mode with the saved secret, no pending draft, no dropped-edit notice, and the password is not in the URL or `localStorage`.
- Saved-secret switch: with password and token both saved, choosing **Token** without typing shows "Not applied yet. After you apply, this browser signs in again with the saved token."; typing the token removes the line.
- Gateway change with a staged edit: with a token typed and staged on Gateway A, switching the connection to Gateway B (Settings → Gateway → Apply and reconnect) shows "Authentication wasn't saved because the connection changed". Gateway B's Authentication section shows its own saved Token mode with no pending draft and an empty token field, no config write was sent to B, and neither Gateway's config file contains the typed token.
- Broken auth write sent directly (CLI `gateway call config.patch` with `{"gateway":{"auth":{"mode":"password"}}}` against a token-mode Gateway): `INVALID_REQUEST`, "Gateway authentication change rejected; the current settings were kept: gateway auth mode is password, but no password was configured.", `details.reason: gateway-auth-unusable`; the config file is unchanged.
- Password supplied only by startup flag (`gateway run --password …`, file in token mode): the same direct `config.patch` to `mode: "password"` is accepted, the Gateway restarts, and a CLI call authenticates with `auth=password` using the flag's password. The earlier head refused this write.

Focused tests and checks at this head:

- `pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/config/gateway-auth-draft.test.ts src/pages/config/gateway-auth-form.test.ts src/pages/config/config-page.gateway-auth-layout.test.ts` → 3 files, 18 tests passed.
- `pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/config` → 59 files, 632 tests passed and 1 failed: `memory-page.browser.test.ts` "keeps the header and every tab panel on one column", a static HTML and CSS fixture; this PR changes no stylesheet.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.agent-removal.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.read-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.cache-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-runtime-config.test.ts src/gateway/server-runtime-config.env-warning.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts src/gateway/server-shared-auth-generation.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.activation.integration.test.ts` → 11 files, 197 tests passed.
- Regressions fail without their fix: with the previous write check, "accepts password mode backed by the Gateway's --password startup override" and "rejects turning auth off on a listener that is not loopback" fail (2 failed, 22 passed, before the SecretRef case was added); before the staged-auth owner kept synchronous state, the real browser showed the dropped-edit notice after a successful apply, which "applies mode and password in one patch and reconnects with the new password" now asserts against.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json` and `-p tsconfig.core.json` → pass; `pnpm exec oxlint` on touched files → 0 warnings, 0 errors; `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on touched files → clean; `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` → pass.
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, `pnpm check:database-dialect-ratchet`, `pnpm check:test-timeout-race-ratchet`, `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` → all OK (test lines within the ceiling with the allocation above).

Review: a fresh maintainer-style review of the whole change plus an independent read-only agent review of the candidate diff against `main` @ 407537b. It raised two P2 and three P3 findings: the SecretRef-token removal the write check let through, the unannounced sign-in after switching to a saved secret, and edits staged during Apply are fixed with tests; the startup SecretRef override is recorded as an accepted limit; a suspected type error was rejected because both typechecks pass. Local ClawSweeper and autoreview were not run; a hosted ClawSweeper re-review of this head is still outstanding.

Not exercised: trusted-proxy and `none` end to end in a browser (unit and handler tests only); a non-loopback listener (handler test only); a Gateway that defers or fails the hot reload of a same-mode credential change; native apps.

Screenshots (uploaded in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194538#issuecomment-6707957626); the Authentication section is unchanged since they were taken):

**Before** (main @ 06b7e24): Password autosaved, page reconnecting.

![Before: Password autosaved and the page is reconnecting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ecd8bc37-68c8-437a-8b11-a10c0a4a56e0)

**After**: Password selected; Unsaved changes, Cancel, Apply disabled until a password is entered, no config write sent.

![After: Password selected, unsaved, Apply disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9efe6c02-9f51-4125-b136-83f20e7df112)

**After**: applied; still signed in, Password mode with the saved secret.

![After: Password applied, still signed in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7048ec7b-939e-4309-9f12-c7917f2de422)

**After**: 760px viewport, Password selected.

![After: 760px viewport, Password selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/902b90c9-0a77-46b8-8f68-ad4cecdfe945)

Reported by @jacobtomlinson. Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

title: feat(parallel): support Decisions natively and through OpenRouter
body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot evaluate Parallel Decisions' web-grounded typed questions through either the native Parallel plugin or OpenRouter.

## User Impact

- Adds native `parallel/decisions-fast` and OpenRouter `openrouter/parallel/decisions-fast` / `openrouter/parallel/decisions-fast:free` for `decision_evaluate` contract version 2.
- Supports Boolean probabilities, categorical choices and fractional rubric scores over text/JSON state, preserving shared sources and explicit refusals.
- These are decision-only models, not chat models. Existing Parallel search and other decision-provider contracts are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native route implements `POST /v1/decisions` with `mode: fast`; OpenRouter reuses its typed transport, whose `/api/v1/systemone` alias was verified live. Catalog data, credential-only setup, docs and lazy loading remain plugin-owned. Request billing is not presented as token pricing or a permanent promotion.

One shared decoder owns answer conversion, with explicit optional-confidence contracts preserving strict siblings. Citation envelopes stay adapter-owned. Hosted-review fixes honor prepared replacement auth and check unsupported controls across every inherited layer.

Requested by @vincentkoc via [the original X request](https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2118959925544325491).

## Evidence

- Initial feature validation: **261 focused tests passed**, including codec/provider/search consumers and 14 prompt-prefix tests. Native registration and shared decoding regressions were red before implementation and green afterward.
- Native follow-ups: **22 tests passed**, including six real guarded-HTTP/socket cases below. Typed lint, plugin/core test-import boundaries, production/test typechecks and formatting pass. The fixture uses public/plugin test support and a synchronous HTTP listener.
- Catalog follow-up: **four agent-boundary integration tests pass**, with typed lint and agents-root typecheck. All five decision-only routes retain their declared capabilities, stay outside conversational selection, and do not acquire invented token fields or pricing.
- Intentional config-doc generation changed only overall/plugin hashes for Parallel setup/help metadata; core/channel hashes and field counts remain unchanged. Canonical config-doc checks pass.
- Local feature and production-repair reviews found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted auth/parameter findings were reproduced and repaired; duplicate answer conversion was removed rather than introducing another owner.
- [Production build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42354843024/job/128350986110) passed at `59cabc4bff825afc130b62e1129078b2669ceafc`, confirmed in logs. Subsequent changes are tests, generated documentation and a test-budget record only. This is scoped prior-head runtime evidence; current-head required checks remain the merge gate.
- Authenticated OpenRouter base/free probes passed through `/api/v1/systemone` and `/api/alpha/decisions`: HTTP 200, typed answers, ten citations and reported cost $0, including rich Boolean/choice/score guidance. These are API probes, not a full Gateway agent run.

### Real authority-boundary proof

The production provider and real HTTP guard/dispatcher execute against a socket listener. Only external DNS is paused to revoke admission deterministically during asynchronous preparation; neither fetch nor `beforeRequest` is mocked or invoked manually. The fixture closes only its own server sockets.

| Native scenario | Observed after repair |
| --- | --- |
| Provider-default auth | One request with the selected native key |
| Replacement auth | One request with the selected replacement header; original key absent |
| Caller admission revoked during DNS | Zero socket connections and HTTP requests |
| Credential admission revoked during DNS | Zero socket connections and HTTP requests |
| Unsupported resolved-model control | Zero socket connections and HTTP requests |
| Unsupported global-default control | Zero socket connections and HTTP requests |

The original base sent the original key during replacement auth and dispatched both unsupported-control cases: **three failures, three passes**. All six pass after repair. Zero-valued controls remain explicit; fixtures use synthetic credentials. No new authority system was added.

### Bounded test-cost allocation

`config/test-lines-allocations/194537-parallel-decisions.txt` grants exactly **565 lines**, equal to this PR's measured net new test LF lines. The earlier 575-line proposal was rejected by CI and shrunk; no inherited-debt credit, unused headroom or shared-scalar increase remains. The canonical local ratchet against base `cba7c0ec2ecc3545a87867d5fdbe422cbba20dc2` passes with **slack: 0**. Current merge-ref CI still must validate the final record.

Coverage is necessary for native protocol adaptation, two OpenRouter aliases, estimates/refusals/citations, strict sibling compatibility, real credential egress and pre-I/O revocation, inherited controls and catalog isolation. Pure mocks missed the credential defect, so the six actual socket cases cannot be replaced by helper-only proof. Existing suites are extended rather than duplicated.

All six changed files passed individual `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` timing runs; wall seconds include runner preparation:

| Changed test file | Local wall seconds |
| --- | ---: |
| OpenRouter decision provider | 43.00 |
| OpenRouter index/hooks | 44.25 |
| Parallel decision provider | 10.67 |
| Parallel real HTTP integration | 6.35 |
| Agent OpenRouter decision integration | 17.76 |
| Shared System One codec | 2.02 |

[CI changed-test lane 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42358525949/job/128362134511) passed: **164 seconds** for its Node test step, 216-second job wall, including other selected tests. This is a lane aggregate, not a per-file or incremental runtime claim.

Sources: [OpenRouter decisions listing](https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models?output_modalities=decisions), [OpenAPI](https://openrouter.ai/openapi.json), [modality table](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/community/multimodal-decisions), [native API](https://docs.parallel.ai/api-reference/decisions/decisions), [limits](https://docs.parallel.ai/decisions/best-practices), and [pricing](https://docs.parallel.ai/getting-started/pricing).

**Proof limits:** no billed native request was made because `PARALLEL_API_KEY` is absent. Full local CLI/Gateway smoke execution was refused by runtime-publication safety checks despite isolated profile/state/config paths and port; offline state could not be verified and default-profile inspection encountered a protected service environment file. No hosting service or safeguard was changed. Real socket proof is owning-boundary evidence, not full isolated-Gateway execution.

title: fix(test): account for persisted facts in turn commit counts
body:
Related: #193682.

## What Problem This Solves

The batched-turn SQL count regression still expects pre-agent41 work, so all five SQLite cases fail after active-event facts were deliberately added.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The regression keeps exact transaction costs while checking that the new persisted facts cover every appended message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit b6ed90743ed7 intentionally maintains facts with each active projection write. SQLite adds exactly one insert per 512-row chunk: the five cases change from 13/11/11/16/12 statements to 14/12/12/18/13. PostgreSQL incorporates facts in its existing CTE, so its budgets stay unchanged.

Pin those exact totals and verify persisted facts for the seed plus every new message. The verification query runs after statement observation ends. Allocate exactly seven added test lines; retain all window, authority, anchor, identity, and parent-order assertions.

## Evidence

- Reproduced all five count failures on main 7a16dd863807, matching [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42347241784/job/128327665646).
- After the fix: all 5 SQLite cases pass; the focused run takes 7.89 s. The PostgreSQL consumer was selected, but its existing connection guard skipped all 15 cases because no isolated PostgreSQL test connection was supplied. Live PostgreSQL runtime proof remains missing.
- Focused types for the shared support and both consumers, touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Measured net test growth and the separate allocation both equal +7.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the local diff against 7a16dd863807 with both writer owners and both test consumers: scoped-clean, no findings. Simplification retained the existing SQL budget owner and one persistence assertion; production code is unchanged.
- Broad checks are delegated to PR CI. No workflow dispatch, rerun, new skip, retry, timeout increase, or shared baseline increase was introduced. CI seconds are pending.

title: fix(test): preserve transcript facts in the overflow fixture
body:
Related: #193682.

## What Problem This Solves

The prepared-assistant overflow regression fails during fixture setup after the agent41 schema change, before it can check overflow refusal.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The regression again verifies that an unsafe transcript sequence is rejected before newer malformed messages are parsed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture shifts transcript sequence keys with foreign keys deferred. title: feat(skills): add opt-in cross-harness delegation workflow
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users trying model-selected delegation need a shared task/completion contract and routing evidence across OpenClaw's existing authorized model and harness paths.

Requested by Vincent Koc: https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2118960217077731649

## User Impact

User impact: explicitly invoke `$cross-harness-labs` or `/skill cross-harness-labs <task>` to have the parent choose an available route, send a bounded assignment, verify completion, and report requested versus observed routing.

The skill stays out of the normal model prompt (`disable-model-invocation: true`). There is no default behavior change, automatic model shopping, new configuration, installed harness, widened permission, or claim of better quality/cost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The smallest fitting extension surface is a user-invoked skill, not a new executor or scheduler:

- Reuse `agents_list`, `sessions_spawn`, model/harness selection, existing accepted handles, and existing completion/recovery owners.
- Carry the selected normal agent's canonical model alongside its ID; runtime policy still selects the harness.
- Share goal, necessary inputs, write scope, constraints, definition of done, and required evidence across routes.
- Preserve sandbox, sender/target, approval, and installed-integration boundaries. No CLI escape around a refused managed route.
- Distinguish requested routing, accepted handles, observed identity, completion evidence, and unknowns.

**Simplification:** production TypeScript delta is zero. No second routing resolver, wrapper, receipt store, configuration owner, or compatibility path. The only growth is the on-demand workflow, guide/discovery link, and one regression against the actual bundled file.

**Investigation:** existing normal-subagent model selection, native harness selection, and separately authorized ACP adapters cover the bounded design. Native Codex child-model selection is distinct from arbitrary cross-provider/harness routing. Inspected OpenClaw base `cba7c0ec2ecc3545a87867d5fdbe422cbba20dc2` and sibling Codex `8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4`, including its child-model override owner.

The [upstream Codex plugin for Claude Code](https://github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc#codex-integration) documents delegation through the local Codex CLI/app server and reuse of its authentication/configuration. Its README was fetched successfully; that integration was not executed here. Thread usage percentages and quality/cost claims remain unverified.

## Evidence

- **Red/green real-file regression:** absent skill fails command discovery; restored skill passes command registration, snapshot presence, and normal-prompt omission.
- **11 focused tests passed** across labs, frontmatter, and command-specs consumer tests.
- **Test budget:** the first CI baseline-ratchet run and hosted review identified exactly 24 unallocated test lines. Added `config/test-lines-allocations/cross-harness-labs-194529.txt` for exactly those 24 lines; the shared scalar is unchanged. This real-file regression protects the shipped skill's explicit-invocation and normal-prompt exclusion contract, which synthetic policy fixtures alone cannot protect. The owning ratchet now passes locally: total 6,559,974, ceiling 6,559,974.
- **Measured cost:** the CI changed-test job passed the regression in 654 ms (Vitest 3.05 s; wrapper wall 4.46 s). The required local single-worker wrapper also passed; cold compiler preparation and an I/O-bound run took 207.73 s wall (test 30.32 s). Exact-head CI for the allocation repair remains required before landing.
- **Real agent/model workflow proof:** synthetic read-only assignment created exactly one child, awaited completion, independently verified `17 × 19 = 323`, and returned the routing receipt. The spawn owner reported `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`; exact engine identity remained unverified.
- **Proof limit:** this session advertised no allowed ACP harness IDs. This proves the common delegation protocol on the permitted route, not cross-harness execution or bridge-level model pinning.
- **Passed:** focused lint, formatting, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, docs internal-link audit (0 broken), MDX sanity (1,433 files), and `git diff --check`.
- **Fresh independent review + final-delta review:** no actionable findings. Canonical local autoreview was unavailable because no bound autoreview tool is exposed in this sandbox; no host-CLI bypass was attempted.

No visual UI changed; screenshots do not apply to this skill/docs/discovery-test slice.

title: fix(ci): resolve the unused Control UI renderer export
body:
Related: #191935, #193874.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the unused Control UI renderer export reported by [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42342712753/job/128313975451).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The availability page and its automatic recovery retain identical HTML, styles, and script.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer was exported for a disposable ingress fixture but had no external production consumer. Move the existing renderer into a leaf module imported by both the startup handler and fixture. The old module no longer exports it. No allowlists, baselines, assertions, or CI settings change.

The original export came from #191935; #193874 supplied the current rendering. Contributor credit is retained in the commit. The separate plugin unused-export finding remains with #194469; the topology and Android findings are outside this repair.

## Evidence

The actual `check-deadcode-exports.mts` checker also rejects/accepts those respective results. This bounded source capsule does not certify the full repository dependency graph.
- Runtime comparison: byte-identical HTML before/after for startup, downtime, ingress, and an escaped title. No appearance change.
- Formatting passed for all three touched files; `git diff --check` passed. No new test cases or test-line allocation; the fixture import is the only test-code change. The new production module contains the existing renderer, with one net production line added for the module boundary.

An independent install was not attempted because it could require prohibited pnpm staging on the production host. title: fix(ui): restore shell navigation and fallback avatars
body:
Related: #191935

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes shell navigation event failures and missing fallback avatars introduced by the new connection shell in #191935.

## User Impact

Connected users and agents keep their fallback avatars when they have no image URL. Navigation checks depend on connection and route state, without requiring unrelated rendering state. Cold-connection placeholders and drawer locking remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

`initialConnectionPending` called the complete shell-view reader from navigation handlers. The existing shell owner now owns that predicate and the view consumes it. The new avatar conditions also required image data, preventing the existing avatar components from rendering initials and generated faces.

The navigation fixtures now identify an available route, and the late-mount fixture holds route readiness after connection. Every existing assertion is retained. This does not touch the preferences behavior in #130587.

## Evidence

**Pending proof:** browser/e2e and sanitized before/after screenshots are deferred to PR CI; no browsers or containers ran on the production Gateway host. The scheduled-run logs also contain old splash/login expectations and provider/deferred-RPC/href failures whose causes are not established by this repair. title: fix(update): reclaim dead closing triage repair leases
body:
Fixes #194493

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update repair` can report success while a dead version-2 triage/repair lease remains in `closing` and blocks subsequent managed updates.

## User Impact

Repair can settle a dead closing lease and admit the next update. A live or unverified owner, descendant, or native scope keeps the lease intact and produces an actionable failure naming the retained lease.

The repairing CLI must contain this fix. A downloaded candidate cannot repair the older installed updater's admission; affected installations still need the documented manual package-manager hop to obtain the fixed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit repair excluded `closing` and also skipped non-uncertain triage leases without recovery metadata. Returning no repair claim allowed ordinary maintenance to report success. #193431 fixed custody database aliases, a separate admission problem.

Route closing leases through the existing repair claim, owner and descendant inspection, recovery checks, exact-row replacement, and durable settlement receipt. Native triage keeps the existing scope-closure contract. Emit a warning when claiming repair and preserve the original refusal reason with lease owner, version, phase, and last activity. Automatic reclamation and lease formats remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- RED on `39fc48d7c16e`: all six registered-CLI closing cases fail for the reported behavior. Dead foreground/native rows remain; live, unknown, and unverified-scope cases silently finish maintenance.
- GREEN on Linux Testbox: 103 tests across `update-repair-handoff.test.ts`, `update-managed-service-handoff-recovery.test.ts`, and `update-repair-command.test.ts`; 72.06s Vitest runtime, 97.40s including worker preparation. The regression verifies lease removal, durable settlement and next update admission, plus unchanged retained rows and nonzero repair results. [Remote run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42343883942).
- Touched-file type-aware lint with compiler diagnostics: zero warnings/errors. Real-process SQLite proof on the same Testbox: a child produces a foreground closing lease; repair reports and preserves it while live, reclaims it after exit, records a durable settlement receipt, and admits the next update. No host-observation mocks in this probe.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Shared autoreview (Codex, P0–P2), complete local candidate against `39fc48d7c16e`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Static review; unchanged owner dependencies were supplied, with partial unchanged-internal context noted by the reviewer. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review follows the repository route.
- `pr-simplify`: no additional state owner or compatibility path. Necessary net growth: 23 production lines, 69 test lines, eight documentation lines. The dedicated 69-line allocation covers only this PR's registered-CLI regressions; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

Proof limits: no reporter database or production Gateway was touched. Native scope observations in the regression are synthetic. Installed npm/systemd-user first-hop recovery and a latest-stable upgrade were not exercised. PR CI supplies broad proof; CI seconds are pending.

CI reports two blockers:

- [UI E2E](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42344402517/job/128319259707): `gateway-fresh-visit.http.e2e.test.ts:204` times out waiting for the “Control UI did not start” heading while assets are deliberately blocked. This flow does not invoke update repair. The canonical classifier returns `unknown` (no matching main job); this is not claimed as proven pre-existing. No unrelated UI change or rerun was made.
- [Test-line budget](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42344402517/job/128319260139): 6,559,704 lines, ceiling 6,559,628, over by 76, net delta +69. The exact CI base-to-merge comparison contains only this PR's +69 test lines and +69 allocation, proving the 76-line debt is inherited. The classifier labels the job `new` because main's job passed; the guard permits nonpositive changes on an over-budget base. The task explicitly limits allocation to this PR's own lines, so the allocation remains 69 and the shared scalar is unchanged. Other baseline ratchets passed.

Remaining CI jobs are still running.

title: improve(ui): stop showing "Loading mentions…" above loaded Inbox rows
body:
## What Problem This Solves

While mentions were loading, the Inbox put a "Loading mentions…" text row at the top of the list, including on the **All** tab when other rows were already showing. On the **Mentions** tab the same row sat where the list starts, so "still loading" and "nothing here" looked almost the same.

## User Impact

- **Tabs that already have rows** (for example, All with system items): rows stay in place. No status row is added above them, and mentions join the list when they arrive.
- **Empty tab while mentions load** (Mentions, or All with nothing else): a quiet centered spinner that only appears after 300 ms, so fast loads never show it. Screen readers still hear "Loading mentions…".
- **"No mentions yet"** only appears after loading finishes with nothing to show.
- **Errors and "unavailable"** keep the existing note and **Refresh** button.

## Why This Change Was Made

Loading and empty are separate states, and a loading indicator should never sit on top of content that has already loaded. The spinner uses the empty state's layout, so going from loading to "No mentions yet" doesn't shift anything.

Context from the investigation: on a live team Gateway, `mentions.list` and `users.self` respond as fast as `health`. `mentions.changed` only fires when the viewer's own mentions change. So the row mostly showed up during connect and reconnect, not because of a slow request.

Accepted edge case: mentions that arrive after other rows can still be inserted into the All list. New content appearing there is expected.

Not in this PR: if `users.self` fails with a non-FORBIDDEN error, mentions can stay in loading until a presence update supplies the identity. That needs a separate fix.

## Evidence

- **Regression test:** `shows mention loading only after a delay and only while the list has nothing to show` in `ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-layout.browser.test.ts`. It asserts nothing renders before the delay, the spinner after it, no status row on All, and "No mentions yet" once loaded. It fails on the base (the All-tab status note is present). The file passes 14/14 in Chromium.
- **E2E on the bundled build:** `sidebar-inbox-latency.e2e.test.ts` and `mobile-inbox-sheet.e2e.test.ts` pass.
- **CI repairs on the first head:** the spinner now uses the shared `.btn__spinner` (which already handles reduced motion), and the 300 ms delay uses the shared `createTimeout` instead of CSS keyframes. `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` against current `main` passes: total CSS +31 B raw / +5 B gzip, inside the 64 B allowance. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes. `config/test-lines-allocations/inbox-mention-loading-state.txt` grants this test's lines plus inherited base debt, using the ratchet's exact-grant rule.
- **checks-ui failures on the first head:** `app-host-native-shell.test.ts`, `app-host.test.ts` and `app-sidebar.people.test.ts` (identity card) failed there. They're unrelated to the Inbox and pass locally on the merged tree (158/158).
- **Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` pass.
- **Review:** local ClawSweeper isn't installed on this host, so I used the local autoreview fallback (Codex engine) on branch `origin/main...HEAD` at P0–P2. Result: scoped-clean, no findings.
- **Screenshots:** the before/after comment shows the earlier spinner; [updated after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194502#issuecomment-6716399701) show the current one.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

title: feat(ui): show the next automation run on hover
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session Details lists a session's automations, but there was no way to see when one will run next without leaving the chat for the Automations page.

## User Impact

Hovering an automation row now shows only its next run, in friendly local terms:

- "Next run today at 2:06 PM"
- "Next run tomorrow at 9:00 AM"
- "Next run on Nov 12 at 9:00 AM" (year added when it differs)
- "Not scheduled to run again" when nothing is queued, or the job is paused or auto-disabled

The time is the scheduler's own `nextRunAtMs` from `cron.list`; hovering makes no extra request, and the value is kept in the existing Details snapshot for warm reloads. Older cached snapshots without it show no tooltip rather than guessing.

Tradeoff: the row's previous native `title` hovers (automation name; schedule time zone on the status text) are replaced by this one tooltip so two tooltips never stack. This follows the requesting maintainer's explicit direction that the tooltip shows the next run only. The now-unread cached `timezone` field is dropped from the snapshot projection; the snapshot reader ignores unknown keys, so existing caches still load.

The new wording lives in the lazy `en-cron-schedule` catalog (already loaded by the schedule presenter on this path), so it stays out of the Chat boot chunks: against current main, Chat boot JS is +3 B gzip, New Session boot +6 B, largest chunk +6 B.

## Evidence

- **Unit** (`chat-summary-automations.test.tsx`): tooltip shows only the next run, and "Not scheduled to run again" for null/paused/auto-disabled jobs; a live `cron` event updates it; today/tomorrow/next-year wording with a pinned clock. Related Details tests pass.
- **Browser, mocked Gateway** (`cron-inventory.e2e.test.ts`, bundled build): hovers the automation row and asserts the tooltip reads exactly "Next run today at 7:00 AM"; the whole file passes.
- `ui:check-performance:base` against current main passes; test-lines ratchet passes with a 46-line allocation for the new coverage (`config/test-lines-allocations/194501-automation-next-run.txt`); madge import cycles clean after rebasing onto the #194496 fix.
- UI and UI-test typechecks, oxlint, oxfmt, `ui:i18n:verify`, Control UI controller guard: pass.
- **Local ClawSweeper** committed-range review (clawsweeper 92db207): no correctness or security findings; it asked for the owner decision on replacing the old hover metadata (given by the requesting maintainer, see the tradeoff above).
- Gap: no real-Gateway run of this hover; the real-Gateway lane refuses to start on the review host (managed-Gateway artifact fence), and the mocked bundled-build hover above is the browser proof.

title: fix(backup): preserve SQLite corruption diagnostics
body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite backup creation reports a low-level worker error for corrupt source databases instead of the snapshot owner's corruption diagnostic. This also breaks the existing command regression in [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42338430281/job/128300855643).

## User Impact

Corrupt databases reach the existing snapshot diagnostic and cleanup path, and a failed attempt to record the backup outcome still produces its warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduced by #194234 (`691bc8dbe001`): engine inspection moved into a child, but its error response dropped the native SQLite result code that backup creation uses to recognize corruption. Preserve and validate that code for the new engine-inspection modes and restore it on the parent error. Legacy snapshot modes retain their exact response shape.

The command regression is unchanged. The existing engine-refusal test now also requires `SQLITE_NOTADB` (`errcode: 26`), preserving its message assertion. No snapshot acquisition or lifetime code is changed, so this does not compete with #191281 or #167027.

The scoped allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/backup-sqlite-engine-errcode-regression.txt` grants exactly 5 lines for the native errcode-preservation regression assertion, matching this PR’s +5 LF test growth. The shared test-line baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Original fresh-main `f231ad6693d8`: the unchanged command file reproduces the exact failure at line 255 (10 passed, 1 failed). The strengthened engine assertion separately fails because the result code is missing.
- Recovery head `5bd0e86c6b9d5e35b1223840199b634b1e1d4d50` is rebased onto `ef22366218e7`, including `d041ef81` for the pre-existing Control UI import cycle. All three original behavior/test files and the command assertion are byte-identical to prior PR head `858fa19ff6c7`.
- Rebased head: 44/44 tests pass across `src/commands/backup-sqlite.test.ts` (11), `src/snapshot/database-backup.test.ts` (12), and `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.worker.test.ts` (21). The serial named-file run completed in 100.38 seconds, including unchanged source-lock and private-recovery coverage.
- Touched-file type-aware oxlint with TypeScript compiler diagnostics, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Allocation format and exact +5 LF credit match; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Fresh local autoreview of the complete four-file committed range `ef22366218e7..5bd0e86c6b9d`, through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Broad CI for the new head is pending. The coordinator owns the remaining ratchet attribution: +7 lines belong to perf lane2240, and the `gateway-fresh-visit.http.e2e.test.ts:175` failure is owned by #194504. This correction does not change their code or allocate their budget. No manual workflow dispatch, rerun, warmup, or merge was requested.

title: fix(ui): stop auto-highlighting unlabeled code fences
body:
## TLDR

Code blocks without a language label (```` ``` ````) were colored as if they were Python, so plain English prompts showed random red and blue words. Those blocks now render as plain text. Unlabeled blocks that parse as JSON keep JSON coloring, and labeled blocks (```` ```ts ````, ```` ```bash ````, …) are unchanged.

## Problem

When a fence had no language, `highlightCodeHtml` in `ui/src/components/markdown-highlight-runtime.ts` fell back to `hljs.highlightAuto()` and kept the guess if the confidence score (`relevance`) was at least 2. English prose matches Python keywords (`from`, `with`, `not`, `for`, `or`). On the prompt in the screenshot below, auto-detection picked **Python with relevance 16**, while a real Python snippet scored 3. Raising the threshold can't fix this, because prose scores higher than actual code.

## Solution

Replace the guess with one deterministic check: an unlabeled fence that starts with `{`/`[` and parses as JSON is highlighted as JSON; everything else stays escaped plain text, the same way GitHub renders it. Labeled fences are unchanged.

## Impact

- Prompts, notes, logs and other unlabeled blocks no longer get misleading syntax colors.
- Unlabeled JSON keeps its colors.
- Trade-off: other real code sent without a language label (including indented code blocks) is now uncolored. Model replies usually label their code.

## Evidence

- `markdown-transcript-corpus.json` (byte-for-byte rendering corpus) gains an "unlabeled prose fence" entry, and the indented-code entry now expects plain text. On `main`'s runtime both entries fail; with the fix all 14 corpus/highlight tests pass. The existing unlabeled-JSON entry is unchanged, proving JSON stays colored.
- The regression lives in the JSON corpus, so the test-lines ratchet sees net delta 0.
- Markdown, chat-component, cron, app-host and sidebar tests pass locally on the merged head (1,753 + 149 + 53 + 4 tests), plus `markdown-code-blocks` and `markdown-streaming-security` (72 + 37).
- Earlier CI on the old base had inherited reds (a `src/gateway` Madge cycle and `app-host`/sidebar test failures) unrelated to this diff; `main` has since fixed the cycle (Madge reports 0 cycles locally), and those UI tests pass locally. `origin/main` was merged in for that reason.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Before/after: same message rendered through the Control UI browser e2e runner with a mock gateway (2× scale, wrap enabled):

![Before/after: unlabeled fence colored as Python vs plain text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8f0bc6d-74b8-48e8-accf-20ff16e8d2fd)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

body:
## Problem

Fixes: when you right-click a session in the Control UI sidebar, the row loses its highlight as soon as the pointer moves onto the menu, so nothing shows which session the menu acts on.

## User Impact

User impact: the session row keeps its hover highlight while its context menu is open, so it's clear which session Pin, Rename, Archive and the other actions apply to.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session rows and catalog rows already track whether their menu is open (for `aria-expanded`). They now also set a `sidebar-recent-session--menu-open` class. In the stylesheet, that class gets the same fill as `:hover` in each rule where a row has a hover style: normal rows, pinned rows, active rows and colored active rows. Each new selector has the same specificity as its `:hover` counterpart, so selected and active fills still take precedence in the same order. Hover-only action buttons and badge swaps are unchanged; only the row background is kept.

## Evidence

- New sidebar test `keeps the context-menu row highlighted until its menu closes`: it fails on base (`expected false to be true`) and passes with the fix. It opens the menu with `contextmenu`, checks the row is marked, closes the menu with Escape and checks the mark is gone.
- `pnpm lint:ui:styles` and `oxfmt --check` pass on the touched files.
- Mock Control UI (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`, synthetic data) driven with Playwright: I right-clicked "Mobile layout smoke test" and moved the pointer onto "Rename…".

title: fix(ui): effort picker is too wide when speed controls are unavailable

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the composer Effort popover keeps the 330px width sized for the Speed row even when the selected model has no priority/speed selector, leaving it wider than its single slider needs.

## User Impact

User impact: for models without fast-mode/speed support, the Effort popover is 280px instead of 330px. Models with the Speed row keep the existing 330px layout, and the mobile composer's full-width override is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The effort menu owns its width in `ui/src/styles/chat/composer.css`. It now defaults to 280px through `--chat-effort-menu-width` and widens back to 330px only when the menu contains `.chat-controls__speed-panel` (a direct-child `:has()` that stays within the stylesheet selector policy). title: fix(ui): focus project search when opening the picker
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The project picker can open with only a search icon, requiring another click before users can find a project. Even when search is visible, keyboard focus can remain on the picker trigger.

## User Impact

Opening the project picker shows and focuses search immediately, including empty and small catalogs. Reopening the picker restores focused search, even after explicitly collapsing it. Users can start typing without another click.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the catalog-size threshold for the initial search state and focus lazily mounted search inputs when autofocus is requested. Native popover autofocus handles retained inputs on reopening; no extra document listener is needed. Keep explicit collapse available within the current opening and reset it when the picker closes.

## Evidence

- Both responsive phone setup cases pass after following real focused-search dismissal: first Escape collapses search, second closes the picker. The test waits for completed hidden phase before keyboard reopening; no artificial focus change bypasses search.

- Project/GitHub search and folder drafting: all 15 Chromium E2E cases passed after main integration, including initially empty search, immediate typing, collapsed reopening and retained reopening.
- The replacement project-access flow passes for both writer and guest roles. Its old conditional toggle could race lazy mounting and close the already-open search; the flow now fills the initial input directly, preserving access assertions.
- The native autofocus contract passes Chromium and WebKit. It asserts retained query and focus before selecting and replacing text through the keyboard, allowing native caret placement on reopening.
- The original read-scoped test removed by #194830 stays removed; its replacement access coverage remains intact.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Local lint could not run because the declaration preparation owner rejects shared dependency links; exact-head CI owns remaining lint/type/broad validation.
- Independent review of the original runtime diff found no actionable P0-P2 issues. Runtime behavior is unchanged by integration; the only follow-up edits repair browser test assumptions.
- Test growth is 108 lines including the responsive Escape lifecycle repair. The existing allocation and shared cap are unchanged; the native ratchet passes with 44 lines of headroom.
- Current-head CI at `599ffe77dea8f9e3d52047890ff4e4bf533ca078`: all functional, browser, lint/type, and ratchet jobs passed, including the repaired responsive shard. Only the [performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42443736480/job/128618515838) failed: base largest JS is 564580 B, candidate 564660 B, allowed base plus variance 564644 B, leaving 16 B excess. The maintainer accepted this size excess, but native landing supports only inherited-failure or prior-success conflict exceptions; this incremental excess is not falsely classified as inherited. The old auto-merge was retired before publication and remains disabled.

title: fix(ui): open the mobile Where picker above when space below is short
body:
Related: mobile Control UI picker report from @vincentkoc; follows #194126 and #194139.

## Problem

On a phone, the new-session **Where** picker (This computer) always opened below its trigger, into the small space above the composer. Its list shrank to 77px at 393×852 and 48px at 393×500 against 129px of content, so the **Hosted workspaces / Agents API setup** section was hidden behind an inner scroll. It never flipped above, because its max height was a fraction of the space below, so that side always "fit".

## Solution

Add one `max-height` declaration inside the existing `.oc-popover.new-session-page__select` rule (`ui/src/styles/new-session.css`), mirroring the composer pickers' existing `@position-try --chat-picker-fit` budget: a side with less than 200px is rejected, so the popover flips above its trigger and shows its whole list.

No new stylesheet, rule block or selector, and no design change: the desktop layout and the "What" picker are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression folded into the existing mobile docking test in `ui/src/e2e/mobile-new-conversation.e2e.test.ts` (390×844, touch): opening Where must not leave its list scrolling (base: 48px inner scroll).
- **Red on base:** only the docking test fails (`expected 48 to be 0`); the other 8 pass. **Green with the fix:** 9/9. Test-lines ratchet within budget.
- oxfmt, stylelint, oxlint and `git diff --check` are clean.

title: fix(auth): prevent peer refresh deadline tests from hanging
body:
Related: #192906

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CI hangs when the request-auth deadline expires before a peer OAuth refresh fixture finishes preparing.

## User Impact

Internal CI reliability repair. Runtime authentication and Gateway startup behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture added in 31b28e921fa7 (#192906) returned its release handle only after awaiting provider entry. If the one-second auth deadline won, `finally` could see no handle and leave a claimed refresh waiting forever while the state fixture drained it. The deadline test now owns its release gate before either lookup awaits and passes it to the existing helper.

The regression retains the existing post-lookup publication case and adds deterministic deferred provider entry. Both the one-second auth budget and five-second assertion bound remain intact. A separate 17-line allocation covers exactly this change's regression growth; the shared baseline is unchanged. Production delta: 0 lines; test delta: +17 lines.

## Evidence

- Original failure: [scheduled main run 42304623415, job 128191135479](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42304623415/job/128191135479), head `0c96fb6029dd`, request-auth peer-refresh test timed out at 120 seconds.
- Deterministic deferred-entry regression with the original release ownership: failed at a tighter 10-second test watchdog. With the fix: all six cases passed under Node (19.72s wall time, 15.22s Vitest duration). The added deferred-entry case takes about 2.1s and exercises the real native refresh claim and fixture drain. CI seconds pending.

## What Problem This Solves

An authorized Telegram user cannot currently summon the OpenClaw bot for a one-shot answer in a chat where the bot is not a member. This adds native, explicitly enabled Guest Mode through Telegram’s guest API.

<!--

## User Impact

Guest Mode remains off by default, with a separate numeric caller allowlist per account. Account/channel bindings retain the intended agent and model; each guest interaction has an independent session.

This MVP is one final, bounded text answer through `answerGuestQuery`: no ordinary-send fallback, streaming, media, callbacks, or tools. Strict context isolation excludes private transcripts, workspace/bootstrap context, installed prompt/turn-prepare/memory contributions and custom context-engine additions. Native CLI/custom runtimes fail closed before inference rather than switching runtimes or billing paths.

**Draft / not production-ready:** no authorized live Telegram bot or external chat was available. Live round-trip and external restart acceptance remain incomplete. Local five-minute request-age and 60-second turn bounds are resource policies, not a Telegram TTL guarantee. No production/BotFather change or deployment is authorized by this PR.

The integration reuses the existing Telegram receiver, durable ingress, account limiter, routing and reply owners. Unlike #83632, opt-in is explicit rather than `auto`, account routing is retained, and the SDK result is the actual `SentGuestMessage`. Unlike #95673, this adds no broad pre-auth raw-ingress hook. Configuration metadata is generated from the plugin schema so CLI/UI validation accepts the same root/account options. No dependency version change or dist patch is needed.

title: fix(codex): settle retained thread custody across handoffs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #187776. Background cleanup waiting was a caller opt-in used only for cold resume. A context-engine epoch rotation with a different plugin policy could therefore reject an unclaimed, protected predecessor immediately as “claimed by active work,” even though displayed context-engine policy fingerprints matched. Engine and plugin policy fingerprints are separate checks; this patch does not weaken either check.

Tracing the complete ownership path found two additional reachable gaps:
- Cold-resume preparation rejected a deferred cleanup claim before the common settlement waiter could run.
- Source revocation cleared native-only background custody without issuing native termination when there was no concrete sandbox process closure. Pending background registration could also erase that custody during its failure finalizer or foreground release.

Protection is not proof of a foreground run: live MCP App views, discovery, compaction, native commands, and admitted continuations can outlive a turn. A Stop result of no-active-run is not authority to discard those holds.

## User Impact

- Every retained-thread unload/handoff, including policy/context/client rotation, observes the existing bounded, abortable cleanup wait and then rechecks live authority, client state, and ownership.
- The waiter follows final unprotection through the deferred physical unsubscribe, including an unsubscribe already in flight. Actual foreground claims and sibling ownership remain protected.
- Revoking an original source cancels its native-only commands using fresh inventory on the original physical client, matching the exact admitted item and any known process handle. The live custody check runs again at the actual write and retry boundary.
- Empty inventory, termination acknowledgment (including false), timeout, and logical client close are not treated as final native execution receipts. Failed/uncertain cleanup remains visible and unsettled; a later Stop can retry while the original client remains available.
- Diagnostics no longer tell every protected-resource holder to stop a nonexistent foreground run. Fixed owner-kind/count debug records help attribute future holds without logging tool arguments or message content.

## Why This Change Was Made

One ownership path serves all handoffs; the cold-resume-only option is removed. Refcount acquisition and idempotent release now live together in the thread owner; the runtime adapter consumes the final-release fact for its existing idle/LRU handling.

A per-command cancellationRequested fact preserves cancellation custody across an awaited registration RPC and foreground cleanup. Canceled entries are not published as retained foreground work. Concrete process closures keep their existing termination path. No new config, dependency, protocol version, public SDK surface, persistence schema, or permission policy is introduced.

This incorporates the useful expansion from a separately supplied local patch, but not its unsafe edges: confirmed-only cancellation missed pending registration, and logical client closure cannot prove native termination. The latter is an explicit existing transport contract: close handlers run before transport cleanup, and closeAndWait can report uncertain cleanup after native execution.

Related work inspected: #187646 (concrete helper settlement on Stop), #186524 (explicit Goal admission), #184848 / #190999 (continuation/completion delivery), and #193136 (durable admitted Goal recovery). This change does not replace those owners or add durable recovery of native process receipts.

## Evidence

Base: `fc53c551f5e5ab4c79cace24fb71f3e1f503e4c0`.

- **Red before correction:** rotation settlement/cancellation/deadline regressions reproduced the immediate preflight refusal; five native custody cases reproduced source release without native termination; deferred cold resume reproduced CodexAdoptedThreadActiveError before settlement admission.
- **Initial focused unit/integration checks: 169 passed across 12 files** (at the earlier production head; changed consumers are reverified below), each invoked through `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` (not inferred from a combined filter).
- **Real native Codex 0.164.0: 8 passed**, 159.76s CLI wall time. This uses the actual pinned app-server with a deterministic loopback Responses provider, real native background commands, and production thread lifecycle operations. Cases cover warm publication failure, protected policy refusal, context refresh, combined epoch/plugin rotation after native settlement, and original-source cancellation; sibling ownership/continuation remains usable.
- **Types:** `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions` passed.
- **Static:** changed-file oxlint (21 TypeScript files), format check (22 files), and `git diff --check HEAD` passed.
- **Fresh local diff review through P2:** no actionable findings. The reviewer did not independently run the tests or inspect unchanged callee implementations; those contracts were personally traced and exercised by the wire/native checks.

Native cancellation wire coverage includes pending registration + foreground release, pending Stop with an initially unknown process handle, failed termination followed by a fresh public cancellation retry, handle reuse by another item, final completion during inventory and actual overload backoff, empty-inventory timeout, negative acknowledgment, and uncertain client closure. No request-result casts or mocked ownership decisions are used for that coverage.

</details>

### ClawSweeper authority-chain qualification

Proof-only follow-up head: `1355e82f42057941cd16543c44ff69a324dc9375`. Production code is unchanged from `8263fc22fc03af60ebc4d81820fba2ec1ce3e45b`; only the native proof fixture and its matching allocation changed.

The [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194294#issuecomment-6694193627) found no concrete introduced defect and explicitly permitted a production-path harness through the real authority and transport owners. This qualification uses that route, not a full Gateway/real-model claim.

Each case creates **two independent retained source grants and two actual native commands in different turns on the same physical app-server client/thread**. No production authority decision is mocked. The deterministic loopback model only chooses fixture actions; the actual Codex binary, native processes, authority owners, request admission/retry logic, and transport are exercised.

- **Source revocation:** the successful native stdin-write tap observes exactly A's process target. A reaches its final receipt. B still has live authority and must create a new filesystem heartbeat *after A settles*, then is explicitly allowed to finish and release its own source.
- **Stale inventory:** a real inventory response containing A and B is held in delivery; A finishes; the response is released. The actual final-write custody guard rejects the stale termination and the native write count is zero. B creates its post-settlement heartbeat.
- **Would-be retry:** a valid `-32001` rejection is injected before the first termination frame reaches native ingress and held while A finishes. On delivery, the real client retry path revalidates custody and rejects before any native termination write. B creates its post-settlement heartbeat. The injected rejection is **not** counted as a physical native write.

**Baseline counterexample:** the exact same real two-command source-revocation case fails on `fc53c551f5e5ab4c79cace24fb71f3e1f503e4c0`: source A is released immediately on revocation (expected no release, observed one call), before native settlement. Fixture finally cleanup finishes both owned commands; this is not a setup failure or a forced-reset workaround.

**Candidate:** all eight native cases pass, including all three new final-effect cases. The native fixture's typecheck, changed-file lint/format checks, and fresh P0–P2 local review pass. CI seconds for the new head remain pending.

### Broad-CI repair and revalidation

The first substantive CI run exposed incomplete minimal client doubles and a stale diagnostic expectation, plus two type-aware lint errors. They were not dismissed as infrastructure failures:

- A local source audit classified the 22 discovered direct lifecycle test callers: nine use the repaired minimal-client adapter; ten use SDK clients/maintained real-client harnesses; one uses a complete maintained fake with close state and identity; one mocks the lifecycle boundary; and this configured-MCP producer supplies its own explicit contract. ### Terminal CI and exact comparison-base proof

Exact head: `1c259845b48b353069a3a16cb82fe4b9d0e2cf3e`. The informational comparison to a passing scheduled-main job is not sufficient attribution: it did not compare the selected scope. I independently ran the unchanged ratchet against the exact Git trees recorded by CI:

title: fix(backup): read the backup engine without copying the live database
body:
Fixes #194209

## Problem and root cause

SQLite/Git backups and conditional update engine checks can fail on a busy, large WAL database because identifying its engine copies and compares the entire live file. Reported by **GoatInAHat**.

At [`physical-store.ts:35`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/31a65d5def1a5209c0d0c69ce368c597592ef8ae/src/infra/database-engine/physical-store.ts#L35), `readBackupEngine` calls the full-copy preparer at [`sqlite-snapshot-source.ts:483`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/31a65d5def1a5209c0d0c69ce368c597592ef8ae/src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-source.ts#L483) just to inspect the anchor. Continuous checkpoints can exhaust all ten stabilization attempts before backup or update admission begins.

## Fix

The existing physical-store owner uses the isolated read-only child and a short native read transaction, returning validated engine identity without a full image or snapshot-cache allocation for ordinary healthy live probes. All SQLite/Git and update capture/admission/version-zero validation callers use that owner. Source descriptors stay out of the caller to preserve its POSIX locks.

Hot journals, incomplete WAL families, artifact-preserving scopes, and offline maintenance retain private inspection. This preserves retained WAL/SHM bytes and avoids borrowing another process's native custody. The fallback handles only the specific maintenance/admission-pending source-access errors and canonical native SQLite lock errors; unreadable data, invalid anchors, and other errors still refuse. Existing captured-image readers remain unchanged.

Strict recovery/generation captures retain their artifact-preservation requirements. This does not guarantee original-state capture or explicitly artifact-preserving candidate admission under continuous checkpoints, and the installed binary performing the probe must contain the fix. `sqlite-snapshot.ts`, including lane NU's VACUUM code, is untouched. No schema, public config, protocol-version, dependency, or changelog change.

## Validation

- Rebased onto main `7ab0143fc2288251377d0b355b1c78a30c1b55ac` at head `ea8fa3de1c573855fa2c7dee3271e3f5754d97b9`. One test conflict preserves main's newer single generation-read behavior and removes the obsolete engine-copy helper assertion. Production patches and all original authorship/trailers are preserved.
- **92 passed**, four named files: `src/snapshot/database-backup.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-database-backup-engine.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-database-backup.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-database-engine-admission.test.ts` (134.97s including native worker preparation). Includes both conflict-adjacent acquisition/settlement recovery cases and the real locked-source case.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, scoped types, formatting and diff checks passed. The independent-writer candidate process fixture stays with CI under the production-host load rule.
- Net added test lines134, scoped allocation134, unchanged; no shared budget increase. Current ratchet check passed:6,556,596 test lines against6,556,661 ceiling,65 lines of slack. The prior inherited-debt blocker is cleared.
- Pre-rebase full-branch Codex review through P2 at `87e5a0caef03`: **scoped-clean**. Reused for this mechanical rebase; no substantive production patch change or new hosted review request.
- [Exact rebased-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42329724689) completed **SUCCESS**: all required checks and all three PostgreSQL shards passed. Both independent-writer candidate process cases also passed in CI. No CI repair or rerun needed. Earlier [pre-rebase CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42265135832) passed all product tests, including all PostgreSQL shards and seven Doctor rollback cases; its sole underlying failure was inherited test-budget debt. That is prior-head evidence.

## Remote proof and limits

[Testbox retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42256795653), Node 24.22.1, synthetic global database **2,166,165,504 bytes**, independent writer committing and checkpointing every 3 ms:

| Pinned revision | SQLite create | Git create | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base `31a65d5def1a` | RED: attempts=10, 14.72 s | RED: attempts=10, 41.99 s | No artifact |
| Initial head `995e582de0d1` | GREEN: 37.35 s | GREEN: 61.61 s | Both exit 0 (6.86 s / 33.46 s) |

Writer commits advanced during each command (base SQLite 1→2096, base Git 2097→5042, head SQLite 5042→11708, head Git 13619→27029). The SQLite artifact is 2,166,169,600 bytes with SHA-256 `d2cbb4b77ce6c4b9ad5efce696cf9a752883fe2cb73d095ff419213d3f252b9b`. Successful creates still emit a best-effort outcome-recording warning from its separate strict state inspection.

The existing version-zero supplemental candidate process fixture also passed remotely (two cases). Its small fixture passed on base as well, so it is branch coverage, not RED proof. The lease was explicitly stopped and confirmed completed.

**Proof limits:** remote CLI evidence is for prior head `995e582de0d1`. Full stable-to-candidate upgrade, Gateway readiness/final state, and warning-versus-fatal-validation campaign remain **MISSING**. Artifact-preserving admission still selects private inspection.
