title: fix(backup): compact snapshots inside the staging directory
body:
Fixes #194208. Reported by @GoatInAHat.

## What Problem This Solves

Large SQLite backups can fail with “disk I/O error” when SQLite's temporary filesystem is quota limited, even though the backup repository has sufficient space. The same compaction is reachable from the required post-core Doctor recovery archive during an update with pending agent migrations.

## User Impact

The database-sized compaction image stays on the private staging volume. Sanitization, committed WAL contents, deleted-byte removal, FTS/vector contents, row-ID preservation when requested, verification, exclusive publication, and cleanup retain their existing owners. No schema, protocol, configuration, or retention change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: [`src/infra/sqlite-snapshot.ts:693` on the base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/31a65d5def1a5209c0d0c69ce368c597592ef8ae/src/infra/sqlite-snapshot.ts#L693) executes plain `VACUUM`, whose rebuild database follows `SQLITE_TMPDIR`/`TMPDIR`. A private source path does not relocate that allocation. [`doctor-update-schema-guard.ts:300`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/31a65d5def1a5209c0d0c69ce368c597592ef8ae/src/commands/doctor-update-schema-guard.ts#L300) reaches it through the recovery archive; earlier update checkpoints normally opt out of compaction.

Use parameter-bound `VACUUM INTO` for a fresh sibling file, normalize its native Windows path, and send that output through the existing permissions, fsync, identity/hash, integrity, exclusive publication, and cleanup pipeline. SQLite can still use other temporary storage for unrelated work; this fix relocates the database-sized rebuild. Default compaction does not promise specific implicit row IDs; the opt-out still preserves them.

The simplification pass keeps the existing owner and adds no helper, global temp policy, option, fallback, or schema. Production net +7 lines; regression net +49 lines. The scoped allocation grants exactly those 49 regression lines for native allocation-boundary, interrupted-output cleanup, and stranded partial-file reclamation coverage; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Focused owner, transfer, vector, and reclamation suites: **60 passed**, 2 Windows-only skipped. Repository sanitization/agent ownership: **2 passed**. Original post-core Doctor recovery-archive/migration case: **1 passed**. Archive/SQLite/Git cold-transcript restores with retained FTS search: **3 passed**. Touched-file lint, types, format, and diff checks passed.
- **Real native RED/GREEN on Testbox:** a 2,284,720,128-byte image with real FTS/sanitization/deleted-byte checks and a writable **32 MiB tmpfs** used only for SQLITE_TMPDIR. Base `31a65d5def1a` failed at `sqlite-snapshot.ts:693` with SQLITE_FULL (1388 ms); repair succeeded and passed full output checks (6154 ms). TMPDIR/staging had ample disk. This reproduces the capacity mechanism with ENOSPC, not the reporter's exact EDQUOT error mapping.
- **Real CLI RED/GREEN:** built and ran `pnpm openclaw backup sqlite create --agent main ... --json` on both pinned revisions against a canonical **2.29 GB** agent database. Base failed during snapshot compaction; repair created and verified the **2,288,263,168-byte** artifact, retaining all **2176** payload rows in source and snapshot. A separate repair run with only inherited TMPDIR pointed to the 32 MiB tmpfs also created and verified successfully. CLI campaign payload: 331.529 s, exit 0.
- **Post-core Doctor RED/GREEN:** the maintained canonical recovery-archive/migration case, with a **64 MiB** synthetic cache payload and the real **32 MiB** SQLITE_TMPDIR. Base failed creating the required archive before migration. Repair created, verified, and restored the archive, completed the production migration, and retained the original record and all 67,108,864 payload bytes. Repair case 51.03 s; campaign payload 72.013 s, exit 0. The larger temporary fixture uses exact `Buffer.equals` byte checks to avoid structural deep-comparison heap growth; assertions and heap limits are preserved. These Doctor-fixture modifications were temporary and uncommitted.
- All remote work used one owned [focused Testbox lease](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42256816111), **4 CPUs / 15.4 GiB RAM**, Node 24.22.1 / SQLite 3.53.4. The wrapper verified selected source `50f6fd2028e9d9e9ce30f3ff2ab58f8bdca09d37`; production owner blob was independently pinned. The lease is **stopped/completed**. A cancelled lease workflow at closeout is distinct from the successful recorded payload exits. No heavy local fallback.
- **Review:** shared Codex autoreview P0–P2 returned scoped-clean on `4f6b9c87892e`; the exact subsequent diff was inspected and production changes only its filename/comment. The completed automatic [ClawSweeper Codex review on final head `50f6fd2028e9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194230#issuecomment-6690585379) reports **no findings**. No second shared review was required by the filename-only delta, and no additional hosted review was requested.

The sole underlying failure is [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42255657718/job/128023235386); CI-gate failures aggregate it. No flake or CI rerun.

Subtracting that growth from the CI total gives base total 6,549,489: the same **34-line inherited debt**. This PR adds no debt and does not raise the shared scalar. title: feat(ui): guide guests from welcome to their first draft
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A first-time guest can reach a Welcome conversation without a clear, low-effort next action. A forced tour would add work before the guest can try anything, especially on mobile web.

## User Impact

Guests get three optional starting points: **Help me get started**, **Explore OpenClaw**, and **Start a task**. One tap prepares an editable message and focuses the composer. Nothing is sent automatically, and existing access stays unchanged.

The same small component serves New session and the initial Welcome conversation. The latter is identified by the server's ensure response—not its title—and requires the current restricted-guest shape plus permission to compose. It retires after the first user message. Native buttons have 44px minimum targets and work without hover.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a focused prototype of contextual onboarding rather than a modal tour or persistent checklist. It reuses the welcome owner and draft/focus operations, with no new dependency, configuration, backend API, permission policy, or durable completion state.

[Apple's onboarding guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding) favors fast, optional, interactive/context-specific guidance. [NN/g's tutorial research](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/onboarding-tutorials/) describes interruption and recall problems with front-loaded tutorials. These primary-source indexed excerpts support this direction; they are not a controlled usability or speed benchmark for OpenClaw.

Requested by Vincent Koc for Control UI desktop and mobile web.

## Evidence

title: fix(update): skip unreadable foreign directories during update capture
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Original-state capture and full backups abort when a workspace contains an unreadable foreign entry, such as the root-owned `.fseventsd` directory on a mounted APFS volume. Reported by @BorClaw.

Fixes #191855.

## User Impact

Capture and backup can finish around unreadable foreign entries, with one warning per omitted path and explicit manifest omissions. Unreadable owned files, explicitly selected resources, canonical databases, and present private-capture markers still refuse. The running updater needs this repair for original-state capture; installing a corrected candidate cannot change the older updater's capture code.

## Why This Change Was Made

At base `8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004`, [`update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts:312`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004/src/infra/update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts#L312) calls the privacy classifier before enumerating a directory. [`update-capture-paths.ts:18–23`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004/src/infra/update-capture-paths.ts#L18) probes the marker inside that directory and refuses on EACCES. The original-capture caller catches this as a continuation warning; it is not itself the stopping validation exception.

The other walks are agent scratch discovery, backup SQLite inventory, and payload tar traversal. The installed v2026.10.10 updater's broad [`backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts:183`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts#L183) reaches the same privacy check through `isTraversable`; its directory failures also propagate at line 192. Supplemental candidate-state discovery calls that owner during validation, inside the broad package-update catch. This is a source-supported validating-phase failure path, not identification of the report's discarded exception. Main already narrows supplemental discovery to declared plugin resources (`4a393be419f3`), so an unrelated workspace subtree need not be visited there. Capture and full-backup omission handling were still missing on main. Classification and exception-retention work belongs to #194160.

One shared permission/UID policy now serves the walkers. The backup inventory retains skipped paths across discovery and archiving, and checks deferred scratch-scan failures after all explicit includes are known. SQLite readability probes use descriptor-free access checks to preserve existing POSIX database locks. Capture records omissions in its existing `excludedRoots`; backup records `unreadable-foreign` entries in its existing `skipped` manifest. Mount traversal policy is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix owner-boundary reproduction: both `captureUpdateRecoveryBaseline` and `createBackupArchive` failed with the reported marker `lstat` EACCES. The focused reproduction took 44.53 seconds including subprocess fixture preparation.
- GREEN narrow proof: `CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-tar-walk.test.ts src/commands/backup-resource-inventory.test.ts src/infra/update-capture-paths.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **21 passed**, 4.78 seconds wall time. Covers permission-denied readdir/open, owned-file refusal, late explicit-resource protection, and privacy/symlink safeguards.
- Committed capture and archive/manifest regressions are in the existing Doctor capture and backup ownership suites. They use real chmod-000 denial and synthetic foreign UID metadata, skip root/Windows, and include foreign SQLite plus owned-file refusal. Their complete GREEN runs and typecheck/build are pending [remote CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42232892038), dispatched with `target_ref=5438a832520be89cde6799215b99a711fc039950`; preflight confirms that checkout SHA and passed. Build and test jobs are running; their results remain pending. CI seconds are pending. The first dispatch was cancelled after preflight rejected `validation_tier=main` for a cross-revision target; the linked replacement uses the supported default inputs.
- Touched-file lint passes with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`; formatting, `git diff --check`, and commit hooks pass. A separate **200-line** regression allocation preserves inherited test-line debt and leaves the shared scalar unchanged.
- Local autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3, base `8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004` to local production changes, full affected production modules supplied. Explicit-resource and SQLite-probe findings were resolved; final production review is **scoped-clean**. Subsequent test fixture type guards and relocation into the existing ownership suite were mechanical.
- Simplification: the permission/UID decision has one shared owner; existing manifests carry omissions without a new format or version. Necessary production growth connects the capture, discovery, and archive boundaries; net test growth is 200 lines.

**Blockers / Crabbox receipt:** provider `blacksmith-testbox`, Linux lease `tbx_01m6rjrhygjtsk58zyh6kgayr3`. The requested main build (`pnpm build:ci-artifacts`) queued before payload execution; no build or CLI update ran. The lease was stopped, then reconciliation confirmed the exact GitHub run cancelled and `crabbox inspect` confirmed `state=completed`, `ready=false`, `hasHost=false`. Built-CLI main/branch RED/GREEN with a real root-owned 0700 workspace directory remains unproven. The initial named integration/lint entrypoints unexpectedly prepared broad worker fixtures/declarations; this wrapper expansion was not repeated after recognition. Subsequent checks used the narrow walkers and source-backed touched-file lint. This PR stays draft for the missing CLI proof and remote build/typecheck/capture-suite results.

title: fix(update): retain local package errors and preserve public report privacy
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Package-update failures can discard the original exception and recommend changing install-root permissions without identifying the denied path.

## User Impact

`openclaw update status --json` and retained local diagnostics keep bounded exception evidence: name, code, errno, syscall, path/dest, truncated message, first OpenClaw source frame, and two nested causes. Existing local redaction and bounds remain in force.

Public GitHub reports retain only recognized codes/causes, admitted source locations, and privacy-safe guidance through the existing public projection. Arbitrary customer names, business context, and other exception prose stay local. A static notice points to local status when message details are omitted.

Unknown/outside-path EACCES/EPERM no longer produces install-root chmod/ownership advice; known install-root permission failures retain their advice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The package/staging catches pass their original exception to `src/infra/package-update-manager-preflight.ts:311`. Previously classification replaced stderr and substituted the global root when no denied path was available. Capture bounded facts before classification using `src/infra/update-failure-facts.ts:206`, preserve original stderr, and require a reported path inside the install root for permission repair advice.

All exception facts use `redactPublicSupportDiagnosticLine` in `src/infra/update-failure-report-prepare.ts:322`. This preserves the public diagnostic admission intent of f6427568d96d: pattern-based local sanitization does not authorize publishing arbitrary prose. There is no errorName/check exception to the public projection.

The installed updater must contain this repair to retain future evidence. This does not identify or fix the reporter's underlying macOS EACCES, and cannot recover exceptions discarded by older updaters. No schema/protocol bump or CHANGELOG changes.

Refs #194143 #194016 #194035 #194104

title: feat(ui): show mention notifications for sessions you are not viewing
body:
Related: #153801 (rebuild of closed #153812 / #155419)

## What Problem This Solves

People working in one session don't notice when someone mentions them in another session until they open the Inbox.

## User Impact

User impact: a compact in-app card now appears when you're mentioned in a session you aren't looking at. It shows the sender's avatar, the session, a preview centered on **your** mention with a theme-colored highlight, and **View session**. The card closes after five seconds and pauses while hovered or keyboard-focused. Closing it leaves the Inbox entry unread. Sessions already visible (either desktop split pane, or the active mobile pane) don't produce a card. Reconnecting never replays old mentions.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuilds the earlier stacked pair on top of the Inbox that `main` already has. It needs no backend migration and adds no new owner:

- **Arrivals:** `createMentionsCapability` is the only arrival detector. Each connection's first successful snapshot is a silent baseline. Cards are cancelled per item when an accepted snapshot drops that item (for example, lost access to one session) and on disconnect, identity change, or disposal.
- **Visibility:** reads the existing presented-pane presence owner, not saved layout or focus.
- **Card:** reuses the shared toast host (lanes, hover/focus pause, canonical navigation, and the existing human avatar renderer). The only generic toast additions are an `AbortSignal`, an `avatar` option, and `description: string | Node`.
- **Recipient-centered preview:** the old excerpt was the first 280 characters of one shared message, so a mention further in, or a second person with the same display name, couldn't be shown or highlighted. Committed input now carries the already-validated selected spans. The recorder stores an optional per-item `{excerpt, start, end}` inside the existing source message record. The shared excerpt remains the fallback, and legacy records stay plain. The wire adds optional `excerptHighlight`. There are no new tables, workers, retention, or permission changes, and the work is bounded at 10 recipients × about 2 KB of flattening.
- Markdown is flattened once around a placeholder, so `**@Sam**` and other wrapping syntax are removed while the highlight offsets stay exact UTF-16 positions.

Accepted edge cases:
- A card already showing stays until timeout if you open its session some other way. Short-lived, harmless.
- After a downgrade to an older Gateway, mentions recorded by this version can show no excerpt text, because the older schema ignores `previews`. Nothing breaks.
- Both the toast highlight and the existing Inbox row show the plain excerpt without UI tool-detail redaction, as before.

## Evidence

**Before:** the Inbox received the mention, but no notification appeared.
**After:** the card, with the selected mention highlighted. Desktop and a hidden mobile pane:

| Before | After (desktop) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Inbox badge only, no notification](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4cefbce-e2dd-40f4-9af6-ac33d7d293dc) | ![After: mention card with highlighted @Bob](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/502625f0-802c-413a-a4f6-e0b0d738f188) |

| Hidden mobile pane notifies | Visible desktop split pane: no card |
| --- | --- |
| ![Mobile card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/203122d7-c92d-4ca7-ac1e-019e78a4fa83) | ![Desktop split suppression](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f4fae16-bda5-4ee3-90d8-bd14b8bdcb96) |

_All screenshots use synthetic Gateway data._

Validation on head `4a7ff502dd1` (rebased on `main` `802ddc7`):
- `src/gateway/mention-inbox.test.ts`: 32/32 passed. The new case covers two recipients with an identical `@Sam` label, one mention past 3,000 characters, `**@Sam**` markdown, an emoji, closed-schema validation, and persistence across restart.
- UI `mention-notification`, `mentions`, and `toast` tests: 54/54 passed. They include item-scoped cancellation for queued and displayed cards (failed before the fix, pass after) and highlight rendering.
- Built UI with a synthetic Gateway, `ui/src/e2e/session-mention-notifications.e2e.test.ts`: 2/2 passed. Covers dismissal independence, hover/focus pause, reconnect baseline, View session, desktop split suppression, and hidden mobile pane delivery.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core, tests, UI), dead-code, line-cap, SQLite worker/dialect ratchets, and import cycles all OK. Scoped type-aware oxlint is clean. The assertion-safety ratchet failure has been fixed. One failure remains and predates this change: `changelog attributions` flags lines on `main` in `CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`, which this PR doesn't touch.

Its only P2 was in `src/plugins/runtime/gateway-context-binding-owner.ts`, which `main` changed during the run (#194113); this branch doesn't touch it.

title: improve(ui): ease archived sessions out of the sidebar
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Archiving a session from the sidebar removed its row in a single frame, so the list jumped and the action felt abrupt.

## User Impact

Clicking the archive button on a sidebar row now plays a short exit: the row fades, blurs slightly and drifts a few pixels left, while the rows below glide up into its slot. The whole exit takes about 240 ms. Archiving itself is not delayed: the request, archive state, the success toast and Undo behave exactly as before.

With reduced motion enabled, or where `Element.animate` is unavailable, removal stays instant.

## Why This Change Was Made

The roster removes the row as soon as the archive is optimistically applied, and sidebar sections are virtual windows whose rows are absolutely positioned with `translateY`. So the exit can't delay removal, and it can't rely on an in-flow element shrinking.

The row button passes its own element (from its Solid ref) to `sessionOrganizer.archiveSessionWithUndo(session, exitFrom)`. The lazily loaded archive runtime starts the exit right before `beginArchive`, so the helper stays out of the boot bundle and cancelled confirmations never animate. `app-sidebar-archive-exit.ts` then:

- marks the row's list with `data-sidebar-archive-exiting` before the roster moves anything. The window measures layout right after removing a row, so a flag set later would miss that style change.
- watches the list for that row's removal. When it goes, it inserts an inert, `aria-hidden` snapshot (ids and session-key attributes stripped) and fades it out with Web Animations.
- lets `layout.css` transition the remaining rows' `transform` and the window's `height` while the flag is present. A per-list counter keeps back-to-back archives from cutting each other short, and in-flow nested child lists collapse the snapshot's height instead.

Accepted edge cases: the exit plays only for the row's archive button, not for the session menu, the keyboard shortcut or the chat header. It also doesn't play for the last row in a section, because the whole list unmounts. If the server rejects the archive, the row fades and then reappears. That is visible for about a quarter second and recovers on its own.

## Evidence

- New Chromium browser test (`app-sidebar-archive-exit.browser.test.ts`) clicks the real archive button. With motion enabled, it checks that `sessions.patch` is called once while pending, the snapshot is inert and hidden, the neighbor runs a CSS transform transition, and the flag and snapshot are cleared afterward. With reduced motion, it checks the removal is instant and nothing is flagged. It fails on `main` (no exit snapshot). Its lines are covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/194144-sidebar-archive-exit.txt`.
- Existing sidebar and session-organizer suites pass (370 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, the Control UI controller guard, and the assertion-safety and test-lines ratchets are clean.
- The first CI run caught the exit helper in the boot bundle (JS gzip budgets exceeded) and a forbidden `querySelector`. Both are fixed by the runtime-owned exit above.
- Local autoreview (codex, P2 threshold) on both commits: no actionable findings.
- Real-UI recordings come from the Control UI E2E harness with a mocked Gateway and synthetic session names, cropped to the sidebar, and are attached in the comment below. The production-build recording was repeated after the runtime move, and the motion is unchanged.

## Worked on by

title: fix(plugins): prevent service startup failures after module reloads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin service startup reporting `Gateway SDK resource host is not bound` when shared-state admission retains an earlier module graph. The deep-research recovery startup path exposed this order-dependent failure in [main CI job 127866973404](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42210156048/job/127866973404), following #176887 (`ff4123c5a34f`).

## User Impact

An existing Gateway resource binding remains visible across source/native module graphs and module reloads. A closed Gateway lifetime stays terminal. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK host and execution frame already have process lifetime, but their resolver-binding keys and private class brands were module-local. Share those identities through the existing singleton owner while keeping binding state on each exact owner. Move the two existing binding contracts into a narrow owner test and extend them to cover reload, cleanup, and rebinding.

Simplification: production adds 32 lines for shared identity; tests add 3 net lines by sharing one fixture/reset across the existing binding and lifetime contracts. No fallback host, retry, assertion exception, baseline/allocation change, or additional state owner.

## Evidence

title: fix(sessions): avoid worker OOM during large transcript index repair
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The admitted asynchronous transcript-index repair path prepared an array containing every decoded FTS text before the existing transport byte budget or backpressure could apply. A large dirty projection could therefore terminate its 512-MiB worker with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` before streaming began.

Dirty-index repair is reachable after append, load, rewrite/cut/branch operations, and startup/search recovery. This is not a universal transcript-size threshold, nor a claim that every ordinary append takes this path.

## User Impact

Large dirty transcripts can rebuild complete FTS and active-event/message indexes without retaining the entire decoded transcript in the worker. Existing ordering, source validation, publication authority, cancellation, lease settlement, and dirty-retry behavior are preserved.

Related: #194066 (manual trim and synchronous FTS byte batching). Also related to investigations #191847 and #191273; this PR does not close either issue and does not establish that ordinary actor-append incidents are resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep source positions and active/navigation metadata during planning, then lazily reread/decode FTS texts into the existing acknowledged row/byte batches. Oversized individual rows remain intact. The portable SQLite consumer now consumes the same iterable through its existing FTS inserter.

Decoded-text retention is bounded by the current payload/batch, while navigation and position metadata remain **O(event count)**. This is not an all-memory-constant claim.

There is no new protocol or claim/finish state, SQLite staging, asynchronous read transaction/WAL pin, schema or retention change, configuration option, dependency change, or raised heap limit. Each lazy point read finishes its SQL statement before yielding; existing final source-generation/head/update-time and publication guards still determine whether a projection becomes ready.

## Evidence

Real execution used public `reconcileSessionTranscriptIndexes()` with normal admission, publication preflight, source identity, lifecycle, leases, the production worker pool, MessagePorts, and real acknowledgments. No substituted plans or ACKs. The worker's **512-MiB V8 old-generation cap is unchanged**; the RSS values below are **whole-process peaks, not worker-heap measurements**.

| Synthetic fixture | Pre-fix result | Fixed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1,599 × 1-MiB texts (1,676,673,024 text bytes) | OOM at 4.391 s; 1,211,112 KiB peak RSS | Reconcile committed at 34.268 s; complete verification at 40.697 s; 950,604 KiB peak RSS |
| Original >13-GB store; target has 1,600 plaintext source rows, all navigation NULL, no zstd payloads before and after | OOM at 22.104 s; 1,136,024 KiB peak RSS | API returned at 129.591 s; whole command 131.41 s; 890,284 KiB peak RSS |

These are correctness/capacity proof costs, not a like-for-like latency benchmark. The legacy call correctly reconciled **seven** sessions because the preferred session is not an exclusive repair filter. The driver's initial assertion of one session failed **after successful publication**; publication was not resubmitted. Separate read-only verification passed for the target.

Complete target verification covered all 1,599 texts, IDs, roles, timestamps, FTS order, context flags, active/message positions, matching streaming digests, `indexed_seq=1599`, the expected leaf, and `needs_rebuild=0`. Legacy-run observed WAL high-water was 990,798,232 bytes; total extra storage high-water 992,698,776 bytes; temporary-file high-water zero. Final WAL/SHM/journal sizes were zero and checkpoint busy count was zero. The original database was not copied.

Committed regression/consumer commands:

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run src/config/sessions/session-transcript-projection-rebuild.test.ts
pnpm exec vitest run src/config/sessions/session-transcript-context-eligibility.test.ts
```

- Owning planner lazy-consumption regression: red on the pre-fix baseline, green with the fix.
- Rebased candidate: **120 tests passed across 12 affected suites**, including public publication/authority/cancellation, worker lifecycle/native-exit/scheduling, active events, search/status, and SQLite port consumers.
- Supplemental portability conformance: four passed, four PostgreSQL-environment skips.
- Production and changed-session-test types, lint, format, whitespace, and test-line guard passed. Test credit is exactly **45 net lines (48 added − 3 removed)**; the shared scalar is unchanged. Independent-branch guard: 6,536,255 / 6,536,255.
- Local independent autoreview at P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The reviewer assessed supplied source/evidence; it did not execute project code.
- Rebased onto approved main `4dc451812820f0f5bea5ad784c3d6bcbb1c505ec` for inherited test-line CI debt. Stable patch ID and all six changed-file hashes are identical; 28/29 extended critical/dependency-file hashes match. The sole difference is an inherited macOS CI script in `package.json`; dependency declarations, runtime package metadata, and lockfile are unchanged. Large-fixture proof is reused for that unchanged runtime span, not represented as a new whole-tree replay. No redundant review was requested.

**Compiled Gateway/model smoke completed:** the candidate was launched through the public CLI from its reviewed checkout at published head `8757887505027daf99e1bc20f0da1021b63fb0e5`. Its Git tree exactly matches the reviewed repair tree. The existing isolated synthetic profile was reused without copying a host profile; HOME/state/config were isolated, the listener was loopback-only, and external delivery was disabled. A fresh post-reconcile session and idempotency key produced status `ok` and exactly `RECONCILE_OK`; returned runtime facts identify `openai` / `gpt-5-mini`. RPC elapsed time was 9.121 s, with 3.810 s reported agent runtime. Gateway process high-water RSS was 1,772,536 KiB, including startup/native buffers and workers—not the planner's heap. Only the existing OpenAI environment credential was passed through the normal resolver; no credential value was printed or committed. Owned Gateway PID 2901858 was verified gone, its ports were closed, and the source checkout remained clean.

This small-history smoke validates the compiled Gateway/provider path. The separate admitted-worker runs above establish large-transcript memory/correctness behavior; neither proof is represented as an ordinary-turn reproduction of #191847.

**Pending before landing:** required broad PR CI.

title: fix(sessions): prevent large-transcript trim and sync-index OOMs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker out-of-memory failures when manually trimming very large transcripts or rebuilding their indexes synchronously.

Context: [the maintainer’s reproduction request](https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2118619926550475160). This does not establish a universal 10 GB database or 1.5 GB transcript threshold.

## User Impact

Operators can trim a huge transcript to a small tail without loading its entire decoded history, and synchronous index rebuilds no longer accumulate up to 512 arbitrarily large message texts. Existing worker heap limits remain unchanged.

This PR does **not** fix the separately reproduced background reconcile planner’s full-text materialization; that repair is being developed independently.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Stream canonical rows into the requested tail while preserving required background-result payloads and existing branch/parent normalization.
- Preserve stale-write protection with a streaming SHA-256/count fingerprint of sequence and canonical JSON text, rechecked inside the write transaction. Selection passes share one read snapshot.
- Supplement the synchronous FTS batch’s row limit with a 256 KiB UTF-8 text budget. Individual oversized messages remain whole.
- Add actual worker-boundary memory coverage, a same-sequence byte-rewrite conflict regression, and multibyte/oversized FTS batch coverage. Allocate the justified net 213 test/support lines without changing the shared baseline.

No schema, public API, configuration option, retention, permission, or worker-cap changes. Memory still necessarily includes retained dependency payloads and the largest individual event.

## Evidence

Base: `1e8a1ab504e12caf1f90b3ffcaa6243a9d60aaeb`; Node `v26.12.1`. All fixtures are synthetic and isolated; no production database or profile was used.

| Production boundary | Before | With fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accessor → real SQLite worker → committed trim; 256 MiB decoded history | `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` on exact base | Retains header and exact two newest messages, correct parent links, unchanged session identity/label |
| Live Gateway `sessions.compact`, after importing a 1,761,529,887-byte JSONL transcript (26,001 events) | `UNAVAILABLE` / `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY`; all rows preserved | Same isolated state after source upgrade: succeeds, exactly 100 events, exact newest content and normalized parent verified |
| Synchronous rebuild: 1,599 × 1 MiB message texts | OOM; 671,220 KiB process peak RSS | Completes; 268,104 KiB peak RSS; all active/FTS/mapped rows, exact text and watermark verified |

The real worker limits remained **512 MiB old generation / 32 MiB young generation**. These are V8 heap limits, not total-process RSS limits. The live Gateway process peaks were 1,786,456 KiB before and 1,521,112 KiB after; these include startup/native integrity work and other workers, so they are not isolated worker-heap or latency comparisons. The fixed RPC took 103.656 seconds including cold integrity admission. A subsequent real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` turn returned `COMPACTION_OK`.

Independent size-threshold checks: an 11,774,705,664-byte agent-schema SQLite database opened at 228,436 KiB process peak RSS; its verified row-ID-preserving snapshot completed at 223,348 KiB GNU-time peak RSS. A real history-page worker returned three complete 1 MiB messages from a 1.68 GB transcript under its existing heap cap. Full Doctor import also completed; its 4.7 GiB whole-command high-water mark includes an initial Control UI asset build and is not isolated SQLite memory evidence.

Focused validation:

```sh
pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-manual-compact-memory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-manual-compact.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-transcript-projection-rebuild.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

title: test(ui-e2e): retain browser evidence on failure
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated Control UI E2E failures retain public summaries but lose the browser URL/navigation and screenshot evidence needed to diagnose them. Seen on main in [42180933998](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42180933998) and [42187126915](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42187126915).

## User Impact

Developers can inspect the existing browser event trace, final page URL, and screenshot after a mocked-Gateway E2E test fails. This is diagnostic capture only; neither reported flake is fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The harness already writes `failure.private.json` and `failure.private.png`. Upload those existing captures only when the E2E test step fails, with a 64 MiB per-shard content budget and seven-day retention. Reports are prioritized; files beyond the budget generate warnings. Existing public summary uploads and the separate real-Gateway publication boundary remain intact.

The equivalent trace is the existing bounded timestamped browser-event ring, **not a Playwright Trace Viewer archive**. It includes main-frame navigation, console, page errors, and failed requests, but no replayable DOM snapshots or Playwright action timeline. Synthetic fixture state/URLs and screenshots will become downloadable CI artifacts.

Both new steps skip passing tests: no additional browser recording, commands, screenshot work, or uploads. No browser helper, test, assertion, timeout, retry, skip, or quarantine changes.

## Evidence

- Focused YAML parsing, embedded Python compilation and step-condition checks passed; `git diff --check` and `pnpm docs:list` passed.

Reviewer had the diff plus full diagnostic/suite helper context; complete unchanged workflow/allocator context was inspected by the author rather than independently by that reviewer.

No browser, container, test suite, or broad check ran on the production Gateway host. The native PR workflow prepared its frozen tooling dependencies under idle I/O priority with avg60 I/O pressure below 30%. The earlier Testbox allocation queued and was stopped before payload execution.
- End-to-end delivery of an actual failed browser capture remains unobserved. Capture itself retains its existing best-effort screenshot/deadline limits; the event ring retains its existing 200-entry limit. Original flake causes remain unresolved.

Maintainer-requested diagnostics-only follow-up. No changelog entry.

title: fix(daemon): let hosts without systemd publish runtime artifacts (takeover of #190094)
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes source-checkout OpenClaw commands refusing runtime rebuilds on Linux hosts that did not boot systemd, including Docker dev containers, Codespaces, and WSL without systemd.

## User Impact

These hosts can publish runtime artifacts after the existing foreground Gateway lock, port, process, and publication checks. A booted but uninspectable manager, an unknown boot probe, or unresolved explicit runtime selectors keep refusing publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Takeover of #190094, with full credit to @ruel225 for identifying the problem and the initial regression work. The fork's CI could not dispatch, so validation continues in this repository-owned draft.

The unit-file scan approach was replaced because installation selectors and inventories cannot prove that every possible unit is absent. This replacement starts from current main and uses an affirmative host fact instead: `lstat("/run/systemd/system")` must establish that systemd is not booted before a strict manager-unavailable read can become a stopped/no-unit observation. Directories, symlinks, and errors other than `ENOENT` retain refusal. No new unit enumeration or publication owner is added.

Related: #190061. Keep #190094 open while this draft is validated.

## Evidence

- Red on main `c63b3a2e58c45e82ea4d4955c1ac3bbb6a275d2e`: the new publication selection had 3 failures and 2 passes. Free publication was refused, and the lock/port controls were never reached; booted-host and probe-error refusal controls passed.
- Final named-file runs passed, serially with one worker:

| File | Result | Vitest duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update-command-service-publication.test.ts` | 36 passed | 19.61 s |
| `systemd-unavailable.test.ts` | 24 passed | 35.57 s |
| `service-absence.test.ts` | 12 passed | 6.12 s |
| `service.test.ts` | 26 passed | 6.23 s |

The publication cases include not-booted success, live-lock and occupied-port refusals, a booted host with no user bus, a booted host with missing tools, and a probe error. Probe cases cover `ENOENT`, a non-directory file, a directory, a symlink, `EACCES`, and `ENOTDIR`. The probe-file duration includes cold compiled-fixture preparation; this is not the probe's runtime cost. Existing service assertions remain intact; their fixture now supplies an explicit boot state instead of inheriting the host's marker.

- Touched-file lint, formatter checks, and `git diff --check` pass. The unchanged shared test-line scalar gains one per-change allocation for exactly 123 net test lines: publication controls, boot-probe contracts, and service-fixture isolation.
- Fresh independent local Codex-backed P0–P3 review of the complete candidate against the base above: clean; no actionable findings, with no new production side effects beyond the read-only boot probe. Reviewed candidate matches committed head 95270123385291a7478208ec10ec20d650fa6d5b.
- Tests used task-owned temporary state and an exact-lockfile matching prepared dependency cache. Initial setup failures from missing dependency links and retained/shared temporary state were resolved through task-only setup; existing shared locks, installations, and the production Gateway were untouched.

title: fix(sandbox): keep sandboxed turns working after the default image changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #193964: after an npm update changes the default sandbox image, sandboxed turns fail and recovery points to an unavailable repository builder. Reported by karam2022 following the Bookworm-to-Trixie change in #176595.

## User Impact

- `scripts/sandbox-image-build.sh`
- `scripts/docker/sandbox/Dockerfile`

Missing images remain update warnings. Updates do not build images automatically or silently reuse Bookworm, whose operating system and tools differ from Trixie. Explicit image settings retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor uses a standalone builder that enables BuildKit and builds directly from the packaged Dockerfile, with that directory as the build context. The package does not include the source setup script, Docker build/e2e harness helpers, watchdog, or warning-relay dependencies. Repository-side `scripts/sandbox-setup.sh` is unchanged. Common/browser image builders retain their source/manual setup.

Unrepaired image diagnostics now reach the existing warning result retained by the updater. Successful builds clear the pending image warning. Existing non-interactive update policy continues to decline runtime image builds.

Simplification removes the runtime dependency on the repository's CI/e2e build wrapper. The image contents remain owned by the existing Dockerfile. The separate 122-line test allocation covers missing-image warning handoff, installed-root recovery, the minimal package contract, and execution of that two-file installation against fake Docker.

## Evidence

- Original issue RED on base `9c8db2d231b57a70c68ff71c6fbdcdd8f511fe27`: missing default image returned no retained warning; npm allowlist omitted recovery assets.
- Follow-up RED on prior head `1bfe2726717737f1d49d232d898c626e68a9ee51`: minimal-package contract failed (1 failed; 346 ms), and Doctor still selected the source builder (3 failed, 20 passed; 605 ms).

title: fix(update): run package-update backup with the candidate's probe
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #193962, #187197. A SQLite header-probe timeout leaves operators with generic file-readability advice even when an older installed updater is the reason the fixed candidate cannot be reached.

## User Impact

Probe timeouts now name the cause, report the deduplicated discovery path count, preserve the original error, and link the documented manual package-manager hop. Other worker errors keep their existing guidance. Backup refusal, batching, deadlines, rollback, and data-at-risk blocking are unchanged.

**TASK 1 verdict: (b), installed-side ownership. This is the diagnostic-only fallback requested for that verdict.** This PR does not make an unchanged 2026.10.10 updater use candidate backup code, and that old updater also cannot gain this new diagnostic from its target release. The 2026.10.10 hop needs separate stable-line backport/intermediate-release work outside this lane, or the documented manual replacement. A repaired intermediate updater must actually be installed; merely targeting it with the old updater cannot replace code already running. Preserve a verified backup before that manual hop.

## Why This Change Was Made

“Safety checks ran in the candidate updater” describes candidate admission, not transfer of the update driver. On pinned main `f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b`:

- The installed driver passes its own `runResolvedUpdate` callback to admission ([update-command.ts:639–651](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts#L639-L651)); admission applies the candidate facts and calls that callback ([update-command-candidate-admission.ts:245–274](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-candidate-admission.ts#L245-L274)).
- Original-state capture imports the local implementation ([initialization-run.ts:234–250](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-initialization-run.ts#L234-L250)), which calls local `createUpdateDatabaseBackup` ([baseline-capture.ts:349–359](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts#L349-L359)). That owner imports local backup discovery ([update-database-backup.ts:126–138](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-database-backup.ts#L126-L138)) and runs it before its backup worker ([606–613](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-database-backup.ts#L606-L613)). Changing only the worker root would therefore miss parent-side discovery.
- Default worker selection captures the updater's generation; only an explicit root selects another package ([state.inspection.ts:76–86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-candidate-state.inspection.ts#L76-L86)). Retention resolves the running updater root ([retained-runtime.ts:103–108](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-retained-runtime.ts#L103-L108)) and binds workers/imports to that copy ([269–272](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/update-retained-runtime.ts#L269-L272)). `package-update` itself is a generic exception projection ([package-update-steps.ts:721–735](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6bb06e7982f8cf191d58019d26d8a049611828b/src/infra/package-update-steps.ts#L721-L735)), not a separate candidate backup selector.

The **v2026.10.10 sources were read through GitHub's contents API, without fetching a tag**. They confirm the same installed-side continuation ([candidate-admission.ts:244–258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-candidate-admission.ts#L244-L258)), local capture import ([initialization-run.ts:223–230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-initialization-run.ts#L223-L230)), parent-side discovery before the worker ([update-database-backup.ts:442–445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/update-database-backup.ts#L442-L445)), full inventory discovery ([backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts:254–265](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts#L254-L265)), and one all-path `spawnSync` with a 10-second timeout ([sqlite-header-probe.ts:14–24](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.ts#L14-L24)). A candidate-path regression would assert a behavior this published driver does not provide; the focused regression here proves the main-controlled diagnostic instead.

## Evidence

title: fix(chat): recover retained chats after live subscription failures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A retained chat could stay stuck after a temporary live-message subscription or history read exhausted its retries. Foregrounding the pane did not re-enter the existing retryable history recovery path. A failed approval-capability upgrade could also retain its weaker subscription, causing both foreground recovery and explicit Retry to reuse it instead of acquiring fresh admission.

## User Impact

Returning to a retained chat retries eligible failed reads and refreshes failed live admission before history proceeds. The explicit Retry action also refreshes failed subscription upgrades. A usable same-session observer remains subscribed until its replacement succeeds, including when recovery fails again. Retired-connection handles are cleared through the existing disposal owner before reacquisition, so they cannot masquerade as a healthy live feed. Access denials remain non-retryable automatically, current session/connection guards stay intact, and no messages or other mutations are replayed. No configuration, schema, dependency, or live-session rewrite is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing history retry and subscription owners instead of adding a polling loop or another recovery state machine. The repair covers both foreground and explicit Retry entry points, including a retained base subscription after a failed stronger upgrade. The documentation explains foreground recovery and no send replay.

Production growth is twenty-one net lines. The 148-line regression allocation covers distinct initial admission, terminal denial, and approval-upgrade entry paths; the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Owning UI lifecycle regression: red on original base, green with the repair. It exercises the actual subscription timeout, exhausted retry, reactivation, successful acknowledgment, and committed history; terminal denial is not retried.
- Approval-upgrade regressions: pre-Hello base succeeds, stronger admission fails, then foreground and rendered explicit Retry each acquire a new subscription and restore complete approval replay. Both were red before their fixes. A separate owner regression proves that failed same-session replacement retains the working lease and successful replacement releases it exactly once. A real pane connection-transition regression is red before retiring the old handle and green after; failed new admission does not report the retired observer ready.
- Final focused lifecycle, subscription, and history group: **107 tests passed** with one worker in **22.78 seconds** (Vitest wall time). Per-file CI seconds are not yet available.
- Bundled Chromium proof through the production app: using the real 60-second admission deadline and a controlled Gateway response, the unchanged base failed to send a fresh subscription on foreground return; the fix restored subscription/history and issued **zero chat.send calls**. Fixed proof wall time: **98.73 seconds**. It uses a synthetic document visibility transition and synthetic conversation data; it is not telemetry from the reported tab. Earlier clock-simulation/fixture attempts are not claimed as product proof.
- Changed-test type graph, UI type graph, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Broader changed-file checks report inherited release changelog attribution violations and the unused test-support export `setSourceConfig`; those source files are unchanged from base `970519e950d56a6573bc8ce1ba36c8c2ebdd15c5`.
- Fresh independent reviews found no actionable issues after the repairs. Local ClawSweeper findings were addressed with red/green regressions; its last repair pass hit a reviewer runtime I/O failure. The documented local autoreview fallback completed **scoped-clean at P2** on the full final range. One hosted ClawSweeper review is requested under the fallback route.

This fixes a reproduced recovery defect, not a proven historical cause of the particular one-way typing incident. The separately reported fork self-wait was audited against its actual exported branch: no parent yield was inherited, and no durable session corruption was found. title: feat(ui): show confirmed steering delivery on hover
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sending a steering message confirms acceptance, not whether it reached the active agent context. Users need truthful feedback without persistent clutter or interference with metadata.

## User Impact

- **Read**, **Delivery unconfirmed**, or **Not read by active run** appears with existing metadata on hover, keyboard focus, or touch disclosure—not persistently at rest.
- **Read confirms delivery into the active context, not compliance.** Grouped inputs retain independent outcomes.
- Name, timestamp, receipt, and controls remain horizontally aligned on desktop/mobile. Solo-chat own-name visibility and 44px touch targets are unchanged.
- Live evidence survives reconnect/history refresh within the pane; a fresh page does not infer historical Read from stored messages.

## Solution and Integration

An additive nonterminal Gateway event reports finalized steering outcomes. ACKs, transcript custody, assistant output, and queue disappearance cannot manufacture Read. The existing session projection owns bounded, exact-source evidence. Admission, authority checks, queued fallback, retries, and durable storage are unchanged. No polling, new timer, persistence manager, or extra model request was added.

Pinned main was integrated at `50d187b3`, preserving Send now, localized/keyed rendering, fragmented-run footers, and opening avatars. Narrow receipt/action-row view modules preserve synchronous rendering and the original DOM/accessibility contract. A per-badge lazy-loading experiment was rejected and is not shipped. The receipt English catalog is registered with runtime and build-time source-hash/translation owners. Identical disclosure CSS is consolidated while preserving selector specificity and override order.

**Receipts do not consume the run sequence.** A rejected steer falls back to a run under the same client run ID. The receipt previously advanced that ID's `agentRunSeq`, so the fallback run's first agent event tripped the existing gap check and emitted a spurious `seq gap` error (Apple clients clear pending runs and refresh history on it). The receipt now reads the sequence without advancing it. Its warning also names the failure when the broadcast throws.

Latest source commit `bb7862aa9088c05e7181b00dedb391f5a3db6813`; published attribution head `87765785f3f6b15b2f350322f78710a1b1ba48d5`.

## Current CI and Review Status

**This head has not completed its own CI yet; it is not claimed green.** The previous head `7b4e657` was green (92 passed, 48 skipped/neutral, none failed or pending). No merge or deployment has been performed.

That previous head's UI e2e shard 6/7 first failed `scopes auth, quota, and scoped identity` (expected 24%, observed 90k/300k 30%), passed its exact local reproduction unchanged, and passed one targeted CI replay on the same commit. **A passing replay is not presented as a causal code fix.**

Fresh independent reviews found no actionable findings in the synchronous repair bundle and CSS cascade. A later maintainer review identified the sequence-gap defect fixed here.

## Evidence

**Sequence fix:**
- New regression drives a rejected steer's real finalizer and receipt into the real agent-event handler with a shared sequence map, then emits the fallback run's first events. It **failed before the fix** (`seq gap`, expected 2, received 1) and passes after.
- 29 injection cases, 134 Gateway directive cases and 2 isolated-Gateway steering cases passed. Core types, the gateway-methods test type graph, scoped lint, formatting, line-cap and test-line ratchets and diff checks passed.
- Not covered: the real-Gateway browser matrix was not rerun for this server-side change; it exercises the unchanged receipt rendering.

**Reused where unchanged:** 17 footer layout/action and 4 bundled identity/native-ownership e2e cases; real Gateway/model named desktop/mobile proof with inspected captures and no browser errors; 44 Vite/config/catalog cases, 15 receipt lifecycle/view cases, 20 receipt browser geometry cases and 66 UI lifecycle/control/footer cases. Earlier integrated proof covers protocol cases and the full real-Gateway/model matrix: single/grouped/mixed-timing steering, reconnect, queue/cancel and revoked-sender rejection. Local ClawSweeper could not rerun tests in its read-only sandbox; its static result is not counted as a green test run.

Visual proof: [verified before/after and named desktop/mobile screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193910#issuecomment-6675568881). Existing attachments are retained, not duplicated.

<details>
<summary>Historical failures and proof boundaries</summary>

Earlier heads failed import-cycle, catalog-registration, terminal-event consumer, responsive-test, CSS and test-budget checks; repairs were made at their owning boundaries. A prompt-history test also failed once in earlier CI and passed its exact local reproduction without a code change; it is not labeled a proven fix.

The dedicated test allocation is now **970 lines**: the prior 910 plus the 60-line fallback-sequence regression. It covers this PR's own regressions, not inherited debt; the shared scalar and performance caps were not raised. One obsolete mock-factory baseline entry was pruned. Prior local comparison work found 3 baseline Settings-only plugin distributions versus 8 candidate distributions; both were then prepared through canonical build/copy/metadata owners.

The real-Gateway harness uses exact source IDs, explicit server queueing, current authority after reconnect and non-disclosing rejection after owner confirmation. The browser bridge is a task artifact, not a generic execution hook in the permanent test. No plugins were removed, new dependencies introduced, or safety gates bypassed.

## User Impact

- Previous/next controls, the item counter, arrow keys, and touch swipes navigate supported media across the loaded thread rather than stopping at reply boundaries.
- Images embedded in Markdown share the image gallery with user uploads and assistant attachments; repeated URLs retain their own positions.
- Recovered messages retain their effective document-mode rendering, so visible remote and oversized recovered images also open correctly.
- Escape restores the original trigger focus. Image/video gallery separation, per-message source authority, foreign-session exclusion, lazy resource loading, and unloaded-history boundaries remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expand the existing cached transcript-membership owner from turn to thread scope and migrate every internal caller. Discover eligible inline slots lazily using canonical sanitized Markdown rendering rather than a second parser, loader, or mounted-DOM thread scan. Rendering and slot discovery share `resolveMessageMarkdownRender` for the effective source and options, including recovered document mode. Disclosure belongs only to its own mounted message, never sibling messages. Preserve the current upstream Markdown preparation/options helpers, regenerate the boot-module manifest, and document the behavior.

## Evidence

- Missing counters were reproduced through the bundled UI for a single-image reply among eight loaded images and for inline Markdown images. Synthetic before/after screenshots are below.

title: improve: avoid scanning unrelated agent files during updates
body:
Related: #182616

## What Problem This Solves

Update database discovery walks default-agent files to inventory temporary directories even when those trees cannot contain a selected plugin database. Installations with large agent trees pay for this unrelated traversal during update preparation.

## User Impact

Updates avoid scanning agent subtrees outside retained plugin resource roots while keeping the same database selection and backup coverage. Full backup archives retain their complete temporary-directory inventory. No user configuration or migration is required. An older installed updater retains its own shipped discovery behavior on the first hop.

This is a draft implementation PR: the real installed released-driver upgrade and readiness checks pass, but full package-rollback/recovery proof and the structured local-review checkpoint remain incomplete. No total-update or Gateway-downtime improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resource-inventory owner can limit temporary-root discovery to the plugin paths that database discovery already selects, including their ancestors. Explicit nested includes and custom agent roots keep their existing policy; ordinary archive callers keep the complete default inventory. This removes unrelated traversal rather than introducing a cache or another database-discovery owner.

Simplification: 18 net production lines, 74 net test lines, plus a rerunnable discovery phase in the existing update I/O workload. The remaining test/workload growth protects scoped exclusions and records counts independently of wall-clock noise.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against `b255cc584c9b5b31de7f89df56357bdfe4b317f9`: the real discovery owner selected the correct core database but issued three unrelated agent-directory reads; the fixed regression issues zero.
- 20 focused tests pass across database resources, resource inventory, and backup ownership. Coverage includes every retained account/token database beneath a disabled plugin resource, snapshot payload rows, custom roots, protected children under temporary exclusions, privacy markers, aliases, restore, and refusal paths. The targeted command took 70.39 s including a 37 s compiler-cache preparation; actual test bodies were about 26 s. CI seconds are not yet available.
- A complete candidate package build and package-tarball integrity check pass. The build reports UI asset-budget warnings; no UI source is changed.
- The actual installed `2026.11.2` CLI successfully updates to the built `2026.11.4` candidate through ordinary `update --yes --json --tag <tarball> --no-restart`. Real foreground Gateways pass HTTP readiness before and after; WebSocket probes confirm their actual serving version/build IDs. Probe connection succeeds, but privileged diagnostic RPCs remain scope-limited (`operator.read` was not granted); no grants were widened. Seeded Unicode rows in two core and three disabled-plugin databases, full integrity checks, and 2,000 ordinary files survive the update.
- This single functional CLI invocation takes 174.99 s including launch/cleanup. It is not a before/after full-update benchmark. Gateway downtime is unmeasured: this fixture externally stops/restarts foreground processes with `--no-restart`, so no managed-downtime value or zero-downtime claim is inferred.
- Scoped TypeScript validation and workload lint pass; changed-file format and `git diff --check` pass. Core lint reports one inherited `max-lines` violation in `backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts`: baseline 720 counted lines, candidate 721, existing limit 700. No limit or baseline was weakened.

Acceptance declared before measurement: exact selected database set, zero unrelated agent-tree reads, and no discovery median/p95 regression. Five warm interleaved baseline/candidate samples use 200 nested directories, 2,000 ordinary files and one existing core SQLite database. Both changed baseline production modules are frozen from the base; other dependencies and fixture state are shared. Linux, Node 24.20.0; starting load averages 8.44/12.70/11.92.

| Discovery-owner measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unrelated directory reads, every sample | 201 | 0 |
| Median | 94.48 ms | 90.13 ms |
| p95 (maximum of 5) | 94.83 ms | 92.44 ms |
| Range | 92.57–94.83 ms | 85.35–92.44 ms |

Rerun: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts --baseline b255cc584 --phase discovery --samples 5`. A separate CPU-profile run is attribution evidence, not part of the timing table. These are owner-only observations, not installed CLI-update or downtime measurements.

Outstanding proof: the controlled post-activation Doctor-failure fixture returns the expected failure and reports all seven pre-migration database snapshots restored, but does not restore the previous package. The run remains pending on the intentionally failing fixture version. Supported `update repair --yes --no-restart --json` refuses with `Plugin cohort recovery belongs to a different installation.` Full package rollback and recovered-Gateway readiness are therefore **not proven**. The fixture is stopped; recovery materials are preserved. No owner checks or journals were changed to force a pass. The maintained Docker runner is separately unavailable (no Docker executable); the successful package/process route above is not a synthetic driver substitute.

title: fix: give schema-compatible recovery advice when a database is newer

After a source or development build advances a database schema, an installed release can correctly refuse it but suggest `doctor --fix`, which refuses too. The stored writer label can be equal, lower, or unrecognized, so advice to use a release “at least as new as the writer” can point back to the build already refusing the data.

Refusals now direct users to a build supporting the required schema (every listed schema for a fleet), or a verified pre-update backup with its matching build. title: improve: clear mention notifications once you see their messages
body:
Related: #194147 (complementary in-app mention alerts; not a dependency).

## What Problem This Solves

A mention stays in your Inbox even after you have seen its message in the conversation. Clearing the notification requires a second, manual dismissal.

## User Impact

User impact: a mention clears automatically when its source message becomes visible in a foreground chat pane, including either desktop split pane. Off-screen messages, hidden mobile panes, background tabs, and prepared transcript rows stay unread. Manual dismissal still works.

A visible portion of the source message counts as seen. This does not remove messages or alter browser/OS notification history. No setting, migration, permission, retention, or protocol change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message bubble reports viewport visibility only after its transcript row is presented and initial positioning has settled. Exact message, session, and agent identity select the existing authenticated Inbox entries, which clear through the existing durable dismissal owner and synchronize across browsers. Shared projections and the pooled intersection observer avoid a separate Inbox or read-state store.

The change is deliberately separate from #194147, which draws attention to mentions in other sessions but leaves Inbox entries untouched.

New scenarios took **2.21 s** and cover off-screen sources, identical message IDs in different sessions, hidden mobile panes, desktop splits, and late Inbox arrivals while document visibility changes. title: improve: resume cold-history navigation after update readiness
body:
Related: #182616

This is one narrow update-window change; it does not claim to resolve the issue’s separate historical copy/hash and repeated-Doctor costs.

## What Problem This Solves

Updates can keep the Gateway stopped while Doctor builds navigation for old cold-history archives. That projection is reconstructible, and the archives remain restorable before it finishes.

## User Impact

Update Doctor leaves SQLite cold navigation pending for the Gateway's existing post-readiness background worker. Required migrations and integrity checks remain before activation; standalone Doctor and PostgreSQL retain their existing repair behavior. No schema, configuration, retention or permission changes.

This remains a draft until the five-pair update/downtime comparison and foreground-latency acceptance are complete. Installed-updater correctness and controlled rollback proof passed on 2026.11.2; latest-stable qualification remains limited by the release-age policy. One complete archive remains an atomic writer transaction and can exceed the active-facts row/time budget; a large-archive test observed approximately 676 ms admitted execution for one 4,096-event archive. No foreground latency regression has been accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing SQL pending predicate and existing transcript-facts scheduler, background writer admission, cancellation and database lifetime. Discover pending cold archives without reading their payloads; prepare archive decoding lazily only for a cold command. Recheck pending state in the writer so concurrent restoration or retirement cannot resurrect an archive. No second scheduler, progress sidecar or schema is introduced.

## Evidence

- Regression is red on the original production source and green with the fix for both package-swap and post-core convergence Doctor phases.
- Five focused owner/consumer files initially passed 49 tests across four shards. After the independent-review repair, three relevant suites passed 39 tests, including the new missing/corrupt archive progress regressions. Exact restores, unchanged archive payloads, cancellation/recreated pass, no duplicate work, and a real foreground actor transcript append preceding cold backfill are covered.
- Core and scripts typechecks, touched test type graphs (state-logging and agents-sessions), targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Canonical package build and tarball integrity passed; the repaired runtime was rebuilt and the final tarball was packed and integrity-checked again. Packaging reported UI size-budget warnings; this backend-only change has not attributed those warnings against baseline.
- Actual released CLI 2026.11.2 (b556fdf) produced baseline schema 27 and reached readiness. Its correctly bound package entrypoint then ran a real npm update to the final candidate: status ok, schema 42, 0 cold archives migrated and all 3 pending. Two separate installed-candidate Gateway processes reached HTTP readiness with pending counts 3 and 2; the first stopped after one archive, the second completed the remaining two. Independent SHA-256 checks matched all archive bytes to the pre-update fixture; foreign-key checks were empty.
- The installed-update fixture contains 3 archives × 4,096 events (12,288 events; roughly 150.9 MB raw envelope bytes). This complete installed run supersedes an earlier source-runtime attempt whose aggregate timed out amid startup/filesystem stalls. The earlier failure is retained and is not treated as a latency pass.
- The maintained state-scoped failing-Doctor package fixture produced a real post-activation failure. The updater reported rollbackOutcome=succeeded and restored 2026.11.4. Exact config, finalize-worker, six agent table snapshots, archive payload hashes, and schema matched the pre-failure oracle; the restored installed Gateway reached readiness with no foreign-key failures. This proves an injected failure/rollback path, not a failure in the normal candidate.
- Required gaps: latest stable 2026.11.5 and 2026.11.4 installations were refused by the release-age cutoff; date-qualified 2026.11.2 was used without policy overrides. Five interleaved A/B samples, TOTAL UPDATE/GATEWAY DOWNTIME distributions and foreground latency comparison remain unproven. One successful older-driver update is not the complete performance acceptance rule.
- Independent narrative frozen-source review found a real P2 starvation defect, reproduced and repaired: one unreadable archive must not stop healthy archives later in the pass. Only typed archive-read errors are isolated after confirmed rollback; authority/cancellation/SQL/lifecycle failures remain terminal. Follow-up independent narrative review of patch 839d30cc3584aa17bbcefeeb3738162553104dc30231a5ef7307793cb3bedb56 confirmed the P2 resolved and identified no new actionable P0–P2 findings; it retained the unproven foreground-latency/shutdown-duration caveat and frozen-input/live-checkout limitations. Bound Auto Review failed before launch because its installed helper script is absent; no helper-validated review is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves
