title: fix: let Doctor publish unchanged plugin migrations in any order
body:
Related: #200606
Related: #200645

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can block an update when unchanged pending plugin work appears in a different order from the migration ledger. Its refusal can also print `changed=[]` when an owner was added or removed beyond the displayed plugin ID prefix.

## User Impact

Doctor can publish repairs when only plugin order or repair guidance differs. Actual changes to migration owners, protected paths, or migration requirements still block publication and preserve retained inputs. The candidate Doctor must contain this fix; no schema or update protocol changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compare obligations in plugin ID order using the existing input comparator, and include added/removed owners in the existing bounded diagnostic.

On the supplied main base, `src/infra/deferred-plugin-migrations.contract.ts:23` compares ordered arrays, while `src/infra/deferred-plugin-migrations.ts:209` only diagnoses matching owners. Discovery retains insertion order (`src/commands/doctor-config-preflight-plugin-migrations.ts:137`); ledger reads sort by ID (`src/infra/deferred-plugin-migrations.ts:261` before this patch).

The Codex `command`/`reason` difference comes from Doctor rewriting package-repair guidance to confirmation guidance (`src/commands/doctor-config-preflight-plugin-migrations.ts:433–446`), using fixed text rather than per-call paths or timestamps. Main already excludes those fields through #190665; this preserves that fix.

## Evidence

- Original regressions against main base `57b9b9bc786796c07ab5b2489244521ca14d739f`: 4 failed / 49 passed before the fix; all 53 passed afterward. These prove order-independent comparison and named membership differences while preserving protected-field refusals.
- CI repair attribution: [run 44113033237, checks-node-changed-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44113033237/job/134144622866) failed because two session-archive consumer cases still expected `changed=[]`. The actual diagnostic correctly named `changed=[fixture-plugin:added]`. The named file reproduced the same failures locally. This was a PR-caused stale expectation, and this follow-up changes that assertion only.
- Fresh named-file rerun: all **75 tests pass**: `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.deferred-plugin.test.ts` (22 tests, 79.70 s), `src/infra/deferred-plugin-migrations.test.ts` (32 tests, 20.28 s), and `src/config/io.deferred-plugin-migrations.test.ts` (21 tests, 22.88 s). Total wrapper wall time: 125.62 s. The failed consumer reproduced as 2 failed / 20 passed before the assertion correction. Its original CI file duration was 115.33 s; new-head CI timing is pending. The existing consumer exercises real import, publication, retention, and retry paths, which accounts for its duration.
- The transcript and legacy-store regressions record new `requiresStateMigration: true` work after archive publication and before unlink. Both still verify that original bytes remain with one link, pending work remains recorded, retries do not replay canonical sessions, and archival finishes after explicit resolution.

title: fix: reclaim updater runtimes blocked by unrelated Linux processes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux, `openclaw doctor --fix` can keep abandoned updater runtimes forever because an unrelated Node process belongs to root and its environment cannot be read. In the reported case, a Docker service caused Doctor to retain directories of about 627 MB each, even after that service restarted.

Fixes #200637

## User Impact

Doctor can reclaim these abandoned runtimes without elevated privileges. Same-account and unknown-owner uncertainty still preserves runtimes, and positive OpenClaw or runtime-path evidence still prevents deletion, including references from another account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The custody owner now uses the UID already observed by the process census to distinguish a foreign account's unreadable service marker from holder evidence. It checks available paths and absolute preload aliases before excluding that process, even when its working directory is hidden. Missing cwd alone keeps its existing conservative behavior.

The Doctor performing cleanup needs this fix; it works with runtimes left by older updaters without changing their markers, config, or stored state.

Verified on main at `235e38488bf2cac52d29ffde71c7e066b69f1649`: the [Node/Bun/tsx argv check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/235e38488bf2cac52d29ffde71c7e066b69f1649/src/infra/gateway-process-argv.ts#L357) triggers an environment read; [EACCES becomes unclassified identity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/235e38488bf2cac52d29ffde71c7e066b69f1649/src/infra/gateway-process-argv.ts#L368), then the [census adds unknown custody to blocking PIDs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/235e38488bf2cac52d29ffde71c7e066b69f1649/src/infra/openclaw-process-census.ts#L613). The selecting signal was the JavaScript runtime in argv, without requiring cwd or mapped-file evidence. The macOS repair in #185342, related to #185359, narrowed environment inspection for system binaries but deliberately retained JavaScript-runtime uncertainty; Linux already used that narrower inspection rule.

Accepted limit: a foreign-account process with an unreadable identity and no positive evidence is excluded; this does not claim that privileged inspection proved it unrelated. No privileged inspection, live Docker recreation, or stable-release upgrade matrix was run. Broad validation is left to PR CI.

## Evidence

- Before production edits, the two regression files on base `57b9b9bc786796c07ab5b2489244521ca14d739f` had **3 failures and 91 passes**: actual Doctor cleanup left the abandoned directory behind, and the census blocked foreign-root and foreign-user EACCES fixtures. Errors are injected through the filesystem/process-inspection seams, without mocking custody decisions.
- With the fix, those same files pass **94/94**. All **183 tests in seven named files** pass, covering the census, Doctor runtime cleanup, Windows and missing-command siblings, and plugin-capture consumers. No previously passing case fails with the fix.
- Controls retain same-user uncertainty, unknown ownership, a same-user OpenClaw process, foreign argv/cwd holders, and a foreign preload alias with hidden cwd. Doctor deletes the free runtime while retaining the positively held runtime.
- CI's core-leaf oxlint command passed on all three touched TypeScript files: `timeout 120s pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check --threads=1 --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <files>`. Oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- Test cost: base census file 4.39 s; base Doctor file 37.01 s, mostly initial worker compilation. Final seven-file run: 52.19 s across three sequential shards. CI seconds are pending.
- `pr-simplify` completed: one existing decision owner, no added helper or state store. Necessary net growth: 16 production lines, 72 test lines, and 5 documentation lines.
- Independent shared `autoreview` with Codex, P0–P2, reviewed the complete local candidate against base `57b9b9bc786796c07ab5b2489244521ca14d739f`: **scoped-clean**, no findings. Review included the unchanged classifier, Linux process reader, runtime parser, cleanup owner, and Doctor caller; the reviewer did not independently rerun tests or privileged inspection.
- Pre-publication overlap check found no open PR fixing this root-process case. Related #195162 explicitly excludes UID 0 from its relaxation; #166893 supplies same-account cwd evidence and does not inspect foreign credentials.

Reported by @yoyo837

title: fix: keep carried-over scheduled jobs running after updates
body:
Fixes #200600

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled agent jobs carried over from an older OpenClaw release can be refused after an update as though their account had been replaced, even when nobody changed the account. Newly created jobs still work.

## User Impact

Carried-over jobs keep using the same account after the state upgrade. Genuine account replacement and revocation checks remain in place. This fixes identities recorded during an upgrade; it does not rewrite an incorrect binding already saved by an earlier broken upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Upgrade Doctor works on a private state copy. The state-upgrade process now passes the live destination through an internal Doctor argument and the existing typed repair flow, so copied databases are identified by their eventual live paths. Reads and repairs stay on the private copy. The hash formula, namespace, and credential incarnations are unchanged.

The follow-up pr-simplify pass removed the global environment-variable handoff introduced in the first revision. No replacement environment variable, budget increase, schema, manager, or compatibility fallback was added. The explicit argument and parameters keep this behavior scoped to upgrade migration rather than every authorization capture. Existing tests and account-safety checks were not weakened.

Against the prepared base, the complete change is production +42/-4 lines, tests +98/-2 lines, and documentation +5/-0 lines. The additional plumbing carries the destination through the subprocess and existing Doctor options; tests cover that transport, API-key identity preservation, and the actual OAuth job migration-to-runtime boundary.

## Evidence

- Confirmation rerun on the published parameter-based source: all 92 tests passed across six files/five shards in 145.54 seconds; the foreground execution completed with exit code 0 before replying. The subsequent pr-simplify pass found no additional justified deletions or code changes.
- Reproduced the original CI failure locally: environment-name count 462 exceeded budget 461. After removing the new variable, the unchanged count gate passes at **461/461**; the max-lines ratchet also passes.
- Red/green regression: on the previous implementation, Doctor repairing copied SQLite state without the environment override recorded a different authorization ID. With the explicit parameter, its saved job binding matches the live databases and passes real scheduled-run inference preparation. This uses synthetic credentials and no external inference calls.
- **92 tests pass across six files**: authorization (14), state-upgrade (11), cron inference-binding (5), Doctor inference-binding-migration (19), and maintenance CLI/CLI lazy-loading (43). This reruns all four original PR suites and the affected CLI suites, retaining replacement, reconnect, revocation, and failed-migration coverage.
- Core typecheck, all four affected test typecheck shards, targeted production/test lint, formatting, and git diff --check pass.
- The source author reported a live upgrade from **2026.11.5** for the original fix. A full live upgrade has **not** been independently repeated for this parameter-based revision.
- Local Auto Review previously ended with aborted tool results and no validated report. The requester explicitly authorized publication with this local-review gap and independent review on GitHub. No fresh independent-review result is claimed for this revision. Full build and broad CI were not run locally; prior-head CI is not evidence for this head.

Fixes #200635

## What Problem This Solves

In the native macOS app, opening **Full access** in an empty Main session without configured models stretches the five permission options almost to the window height. The reported Dashboard WKWebView window is 1240 × 794.

## User Impact

User impact: permission options stay compact without changing permission behavior, available modes, or the model picker.

**The reporter’s native macOS retest passed.** [Daniel’s verification and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200644#issuecomment-6956443723) use macOS 26.6.2, packageable main `3447bee`, and the exact CSS from `cdfec2d` at 1240 × 794 with an empty Main session and no models. Compact size, pointer selection, keyboard opening/navigation, numeric shortcuts, Escape, and outside-click dismissal passed. This is native evidence for the CSS change, not a native execution of the later main-refresh tree.

## Why This Change Was Made

[WebKit bug 328749](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=328749) documents the matching failure: a `position-area` grid stretches its automatic rows to the available block height, while the same content in a wrapping flex container remains content-sized.

Keep the shared Menu's flex layout and wrap the full-width permission options below the heading and Learn more link. Remove the grid and the ineffective `max-content` override. Existing anchor placement, viewport limits, keyboard order, and selection ownership stay unchanged; there is no JavaScript sizing workaround or browser detection.

title: fix: open model setup directly when no models are available
body:
Fixes #200612

## What Problem This Solves

When the available model list is empty, opening the model control shows a large blank picker with a search field instead of taking the user to setup. This also happens on a clean installation with automatic account selection, even when no provider or account has been configured.

## User Impact

User impact: after the model list finishes loading and is confirmed empty, users can select **Set up a model** directly from the composer to open model-provider setup.

Loading, error, offline, restricted, locked, and pending-provider states retain their existing behavior. Personal/shared account recovery and other session targets keep the picker. No Gateway changes, configuration changes, or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing setup action and translated label rather than adding another setup flow. The shared model control chooses between the direct button and the picker in both existing chats and the new-session composer.

The earlier revision incorrectly treated the presence of any account section as a reason to retain the picker. The Gateway returns automatic account selection even before the first account is configured. The setup condition now accepts that selection while retaining the picker for a specifically selected personal or shared account.

The new-session page already shows its full-page setup action when no default model exists. The composer regression therefore also covers an empty available-model list with a configured default, where the shared picker is actually mounted.

## Evidence

Reproduced the reported automatic-account state before this repair: no models or configured default, no pending providers, and a successful catalog response opened the oversized empty picker. With the repair, the same existing-chat state opens **Add an account** directly. The new-session composer also opens setup directly by keyboard, and the existing full-page setup path remains working.

- All 246 focused unit/component tests across ten files passed.
- All 22 Chromium production-UI browser tests across the two PR suites passed with synthetic Gateway responses. The existing screenshots remain applicable because the bundle repair does not change the rendered controls.
- UI chat test typecheck, production UI typecheck, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent read-only source review of the lazy shortcut, row registration, and focus relocation found no actionable correctness issues. Existing assertions remain intact.

Native macOS/WKWebView has not been rechecked on the repaired head. The supplementary Linux WebKit attempt timed out, so it is not passing evidence. The [hosted control-ui-performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44166170430/job/134333815071) passed on b0a2172fb6ef5a108fd48c411b0d761b9cd0bccf. This verifies the performance gate, not the status of every CI job. The separate permissions-popover issue is outside this change.

### Bundle-size repair

The [d30492d performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44159700439/job/134310927958) fails on PR-added JavaScript. Daniel supplied the full-log comparison: largest ordinary JavaScript gzip is 572,366 bytes on base and 572,537 bytes on the candidate, against an unchanged 572,440-byte cap. Chat boot gzip is 1,325,469 -> 1,325,640 bytes, against a 1,325,580-byte cap. New-session boot is 815,913 -> 816,084 bytes. Both boot paths gain 171 bytes; request counts remain 21 and 17. Startup JavaScript and all CSS are unchanged. The CSS headroom warning also occurs on base; it does not explain these PR-added failures.

The repair moves panel-only shortcut registration, keyboard handling, row registration, search focus, and selection closing into the existing lazy panel owner. It removes duplicate eager DOM references and two callback props. The setup button stays synchronous. No new dynamic import, budget, CSS, or request-count change was introduced.

The normalized local comparison against pinned base 1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63 passed with Node 24.22.1. Largest ordinary JavaScript is 572,103 bytes, 337 bytes below the unchanged cap and 288 bytes below the previous local 572,391-byte result. Chat boot is 1,324,940 -> 1,324,878 bytes (-62); New Session is 815,762 -> 815,639 bytes (-123). Startup JavaScript is 91,013 -> 91,020 bytes (+7), below its unchanged limit. Chat and New Session requests remain 21 and 17; all CSS is unchanged. The inherited CSS warning remains.

CI measurements are authoritative. The previous local and hosted byte counts differed; the numbers above remain explicitly local. The [hosted performance gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44166170430/job/134333815071) now also passes on exact published head b0a2172fb6ef5a108fd48c411b0d761b9cd0bccf, verified after completion with the PR still at that head. No latency claim is made.

### Before

![Before: automatic account selection still opens an oversized empty model picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61b20acb-b378-45b3-a109-4c000ae6bf54)

### After

![After: the same empty automatic-account state offers Set up a model directly](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bdb46e1-7f51-4ad4-b4fc-8c3c78efa40e)

### Before (annotated)

![Annotated before: automatic selection still opens an empty picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36f5683f-758a-4ac5-a4d9-e7d78864b595)

### After (annotated)

![Annotated after: automatic selection now offers setup directly](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3b0feb9-e8e5-4edb-a75d-28d87b4fa999)

<details>
<summary>Validation and simplification details</summary>

The automatic-account response matches the existing unconfigured Gateway regression. The browser fixtures now include a signed-in user so both composer entry points receive account-selection metadata. The personal-account recovery test retains its search and keyboard-selection assertions.

The final pr-simplify pass retains the direct setup condition and the earlier removal of redundant derived state. This follow-up moves interaction work to the panel that owns the input and rows, removing eager implementations, duplicate DOM references, and two callback props. The remaining eager delegates preserve the existing event and row-ref boundaries, including Solid's delegated keyboard event ordering. The six-file follow-up is production +137/-127 lines and tests +45/-3; the complete ten-file PR against the pinned base is production +202/-164 and tests +219/-25. Necessary growth is the direct setup action, its eligibility condition, and the typed lazy-view bridge.

Existing setup, recovery, loading, lock, provider, target, metadata, focus, and selection behavior stays protected. The added shortcut regression checks modified keys, IME composition, typing in search, nested menus, slash focus, and numeric activation. The existing production-UI browser flow now verifies shortcuts after a cold panel load, after reopening without another catalog request, and after filtering a large catalog. Local checks:


The final focused run passed 246 tests across ten files, including the isolated provider-icon failure shard; the two PR browser suites passed all 22 tests in 40.94 seconds on this repair. Bundler workers were bounded and the existing browser-library/fontconfig setup was retained.

The full performance comparison used Vite 8.3.5, Rolldown 1.2.14, libdeflate 0.1.0 for normalized gzip, and the committed fixed build identity. The earlier 572,391-byte result was reproduced with both Node 24.20.0 and CI's Node 24.22.1; changing Node did not explain that CI difference. The final repair measured 572,103 bytes on Node 24.22.1. A proof-only copy of `scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts` relocated its temporary baseline archive into the workspace because the sandbox temporary filesystem is limited to 1 GiB; import paths and the repository-root calculation were adjusted for that location. title: fix: keep internal session-change notices out of chat
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resuming a goal or changing a watched session can dump an internal “Reconcile before acting” instruction into chat as a large SYSTEM message. It can also pressure an otherwise routine reconciliation turn to produce an unnecessary reply.

## User Impact

Routine session coordination stays out of chat, while useful results and actionable blockers remain visible. Existing saved notices are hidden on reload without deleting their canonical history. No configuration change or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Watcher reconciliation now has its own internal provenance, model-only display metadata, and an explicit optional-response contract. The agent still receives the instruction and retains the existing notification, acknowledgment, cancellation, and restart behavior. Ordinary system-event wakes and human quotations remain visible. Historical recognition is limited to complete legacy producer lines with internal provenance; a deliberately identical internal wake is also hidden, but its canonical transcript remains intact.

## Evidence

- Regression tests fail on the original leak and pass with the fix across pending input, live messages, and reloaded history, including historical notices and ordinary-event/quotation controls.
- Silent watcher settlement, batched adoption/cancellation, cursor behavior, and prompt-prefix stability were checked. Core typecheck, changed-file lint/format, and the documentation MDX check passed.
- Independent local autoreview: complete P0–P2 assessment of the full local candidate against base `4a9273a7f2476b3bc23148be20e04e392e71986c`; no actionable findings. Implementation commit: `c5ad4d63b9a73cdd54dbb0aa5ac25722c26b49b4`.
- An isolated Gateway, SQLite, built Control UI, Chromium, native watcher handoff, and real session-status tool execution reproduced the notice before and verified its absence live and after reload with the fix. Provider responses were scripted loopback SSE fixtures, not a real-model evaluation. A useful blocker remained visible, and the short-thread draft/focus/scroll checks passed.

**Remaining proof limits:** the standalone browser harness retained a stale screenshot assertion after reaching the useful blocker; supplemental busy-to-pending admission and browser pagination interactions are not claimed green. Gateway cursor-paging checks passed, and the owning-boundary pending tests are separate evidence. Real-model decisions and long scrolled-back conversations were not independently qualified. Clean and annotated evidence is included below. The inspected clean pair was delivered as native image attachments in the originating conversation.

### Clean comparison

Before

![Before: resuming a watched goal exposes the internal SYSTEM instruction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/016f916c-7b5b-4b71-a9ef-213034437b8b)

title: fix: let Windows updates validate staged plugin dependencies
body:
Fixes #200573

## What Problem This Solves

Windows npm-global updates can roll back during candidate Doctor even when the rejected `typebox` dependency is present inside the staged package. The reporter encountered this four times across three target releases, leaving managed updates unusable on that installation.

## User Impact

Candidate Doctor accepts private plugin dependencies inside the staged OpenClaw package, including nested `node_modules`, without requiring an updated updater. Existing pnpm-store and npm-hoisted resolution from trusted candidate code stays unchanged. Plugin entries and repair writes remain private-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [main assertion at update-candidate-plugin-repair.ts:44](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/176f2ff9652ea6539192a7c580940ced94b27942/src/infra/update-candidate-plugin-repair.ts#L44) checked resolved private-plugin dependencies only against the separate rehearsal directory. The snapshot owner intentionally links private plugins to the staged package, using Windows junctions, so a dependency inside that package could be rejected.

The fix preserves main's source predicate and private lookup rule exactly. For those private-sourced reads, [the accepted target roots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c4dcd98dd457c6b639cce8d6dec528eeeddbacc3/src/infra/update-candidate-plugin-repair.ts#L81) are the private rehearsal root and the canonical candidate package root, checked after resolving links. Trusted candidate-sourced references retain their existing dependency resolution. Explicit external imports keep main's existing semantics. The stale `memory-wiki` install-record warning is separate and absent from the reproduction.

## Evidence

The same final matrix fixtures ran against the actual main-base repair module (`176f2ff9652`), then the fix. For valid rows, a private plugin imports `typebox` inside the candidate package, and `typebox` imports `vendor` from the named layout. The pnpm store and npm hoist are outside the candidate package directory. External controls move the private plugin's dependency into a separate serving or user tree. Accepted cases also execute the plugin successfully with Node.

| Candidate dependency layout / private plugin import | Main base | Fix without handoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pnpm store / private junction | Rejected | Accepted |
| npm hoisted / private junction | Rejected | Accepted |
| Windows-style nested junction / private junction | Rejected | Accepted |
| pnpm store / explicit candidate file URL | Accepted | Accepted |
| npm hoisted / explicit candidate file URL | Accepted | Accepted |
| Windows-style nested junction / explicit candidate file URL | Accepted | Accepted |
| Serving installation / private junction | Rejected | Rejected |
| User directory / private junction | Rejected | Rejected |

**No main-pass/fix-fail cell.** Main produced 3 expected acceptance failures and 5 passing tests; the fix passes all 8 matrix cases. The explicit candidate-URL rows protect main's existing successful behavior. The external controls originate in the private plugin copy. A separate case rejects a candidate-package junction that resolves into the serving installation.

- Three named suites passed: **70 tests passed, 2 existing filesystem-specific skips**, **63.80 s** wall time including cold worker compilation: `update-candidate-plugin-sources.test.ts`, `update-candidate-plugin-tree.test.ts`, and `update-candidate-snapshot.plugin-inspection.test.ts`. The main-base matrix run took **38.45 s**, including compilation. CI test seconds are pending.
- Exact core-leaf lint passed for every TypeScript file touched by this revision: `timeout 120s pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check --threads=1 --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <files>`. Touched-file `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the final local delta against `62c7c4c5` completed **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, with no actionable findings.
- pr-simplify completed. The final PR changes only three files: production **+12/-11**, tests **+90/-2**, docs **+10** against main. The handoff, updater callback/environment changes, candidate-source assertions, and unrelated catch reorder have been removed; those updater files match main.

## Limits

**No native Windows run was done.** These are Linux boundary tests with real temporary directories and junction-compatible symlinks. No native bun run, actual package-manager installation, full managed update, or stable-to-candidate upgrade was performed. The reporter's exact importer remains uncaptured.

No install-root handoff is retained: current validation runs recovery with `--check`, so delivery of that environment to compatibility candidate Doctor was not proved. The fix uses the candidate-package root for both old and new updaters, with no new marker or protocol. Direct private-plugin dependency targets remain bounded by the private and candidate-package roots; trusted candidate code retains main's package-manager resolution.

Reported by @desksk (with four reproductions and a layout analysis)

title: fix(update): finish Control UI updates after Gateway shutdown writes
body:
Fixes #198072
Fixes #200022
Related: #200556 (its initiating diagnostic remains redacted).

## What Problem This Solves

A Linux npm-global update started from Control UI can fail post-update Doctor when the old Gateway writes during shutdown. Its stop receipt rejects the changed database generation, so the update reports an error and skips Doctor even when the new version subsequently serves.

## User Impact

Doctor continues after those shutdown writes with a clear warning. The original backup remains preserved, but automatic restoration from that stale snapshot stays disabled so a later failure cannot overwrite newer data. Changes after maintenance admission and actual transaction failures remain errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stop-receipt owner now uses Doctor's existing staleness admission when it acquires exclusive maintenance custody. It reconciles the captured SQLite databases before the existing receipt transaction and generation checks run. This extends the initial-staleness policy through predecessor shutdown without changing schemas, the installed-updater protocol, or stop/backup ordering.

Accepted edge case: a foreign write during the pre-custody stop interval also continues forward with the warning and stale rollback disabled. Foreign changes after that admission still refuse receipt attribution or migration. No writer provenance is inferred from a service stop.

The predecessor tests now live in one focused suite; the superseded block and its unused capture-reuse helper parameter were removed. Net change: 13 production lines and 90 test lines. The growth covers real predecessor release, warning/rollback outcomes, and both sides of the custody boundary without adding another policy owner.

Follow-up: generated failure reports still redact unrecognized stop-receipt diagnostics. The closed diagnostic cause list is unchanged here. TLS-observation and skipped service-policy warnings are also outside this fix.

## Evidence

- The final regression file fails on base `5fb231527f4f14d83bc27067879370debe4d2b7a`: **2 failed / 3 passed**. The failures are real predecessor owner-lease release and a foreign write before custody. With the fix, **5/5 pass**: unchanged state, predecessor release, pre-custody foreign drift, refusal under custody, and refusal after receipt publication. Assertions cover the real SQLite receipt writer, forward migration, one warning for accepted drift, and permanent rollback refusal.
- Completed focused run: **18/18 passed** across `src/infra/update-predecessor-stop-receipt.test.ts` and `src/infra/update-doctor-result.test.ts`. The new file's five test bodies take about 9 seconds; the cold selected run took 43.81 seconds including shared worker preparation. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Before extracting the predecessor cases, all 49 owning-suite cases and 13 finalization cases emitted passes. That combined command hit its 180-second limit during the larger finalization suite; it is not a completed finalization-suite pass. The unchanged migration cases retain that observed proof.
- Exact touched-file core-leaf type-aware oxlint (`--type-check --threads=1` with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`), touched-file `oxfmt --check`, one-page MDX validation, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `pr-simplify` completed. Shared local autoreview (Codex), covering the complete candidate against the pinned base through P0–P2, returned scoped-clean with no actionable findings (confidence 0.86). The reviewed snapshot became `4d813dd2a7e`; the reviewer did not independently run tests. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable.

Proof limits: **owning-boundary only**. Tests use real SQLite and real Gateway lease release; the native service adapter is simulated. Full Control UI/systemd/model or live upgrade proof was not run. **Crabbox unavailable: provider ascii-box requires ASCII_BOX_API_KEY. PR CI is the broad proof.**

title: fix(ui): let Escape close message action menus reliably
body:
Escape can leave message actions open when an earlier hover tooltip finishes loading.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6a1b6fef-8de4-46d1-8db7-8a8e43aa305c)

## What Problem This Solves

After sending a message and opening its action menu, Escape can dismiss the previous Stop tooltip while leaving the menu open. Waiting one animation frame does not prevent that tooltip from finishing its lazy load after the menu takes focus.

## User Impact

Escape closes message actions and leaves the active run alone. The next Escape outside the menu can still stop the run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tooltip owner now cancels an outside hover's pending or visible tooltip when a context menu opens, before the tooltip can consume Escape in window capture. Interactions inside rich tooltip content retain their existing behavior. The message menu also installs its keyboard listener before focusing its first action, removing the separate gap before its first animation frame. The E2E test observes menu focus instead of counting frames.

The existing owners retain cleanup; no new state, configuration, or dependencies. Simplification removed the deferred keyboard setup and frame-count wait. Net change: +7 production lines, +66 test lines.

## Evidence

- Both new deterministic jsdom regressions fail against original production code at `e58cd2228d8fc901948f413411200ca2a2b59d61`: the menu survives Escape after all queued frames when the old tooltip loads late, and Escape is unhandled before the first frame.
- With the fix, **168 tests pass** across `chat-thread-menu.test.ts`, `tooltip.test.ts`, `tooltip-loading.test.ts`, and `chat-view.test.ts` (10.33 seconds wall time). The changed menu suite's three tests took 121 ms in that run.
- Repository-wrapper oxlint with `--type-check --tsconfig tsconfig.ui.json` passed for all four touched files. Focused oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent **autoreview (Codex, P0–P3)** reviewed the complete final local diff against `e58cd2228d8fc901948f413411200ca2a2b59d61`, now committed as `c250f33c07290480916a5ffa03dad6fab46a10ca`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings.
- Matching failures: [main job 133916847424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44046988714/job/133916847424) and [branch job 133820855219](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44017931287/job/133820855219), both timing out waiting for this menu to hide at line 313. [PR #198944](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198944) changes neither production owner nor this test and does not repair the defect.

Exact-head [checks-ui-e2e (1/2)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44060556619/job/133961939119) passed. Overall CI is red only for [checks-ui (3/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44060556619/job/133961938704): all three cases in `chat-transcript-touch-prepend.test.tsx` time out at 60 seconds.

Follow-up investigation: the failing fixture imports the changed modules, but renders raw transcript rows and never opens a message menu or emits contextmenu/keydown. The changed listener bodies are outside that execution path. Menu teardown aborts its listeners; tooltip teardown removes its dismissal listeners. The non-isolated runner additionally drains lazy imports and retires repository-owned DOM listeners between files. The earlier menu suite's reported window keydown/pointerdown capture registrations match the unchanged programmatic-focus modality listeners, rather than the added contextmenu or moved document-bubble keydown listener.

The single permitted local Node/jsdom run of the failing file passed all three cases (2.36 seconds wall time). Its test, fixture, transcript owner, and shared-runner sources are byte-identical to the base. This passing standalone run does not prove a shared Bun shard is fixed. No matching timeout on another ref/main was verified, so this is **not claimed as proven pre-existing**; the shard's underlying timer/frame hang remains unclassified. No source change or push was justified by this evidence. No CI rerun requested; this PR is not being merged.

title: fix: recover older update handoffs during repair
body:
Fixes #200508

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux npm installations, `openclaw update repair` can keep refusing an interrupted update after its owners exit. A retained package journal points to the older lease store, while repair checks the empty per-user store and then reports “Another update executor owns this installation.”

## User Impact

Repair now reaches the existing uncertain-handoff recovery checks in the journal-pinned store and can settle publication. A live owner or another failed recovery check preserves the evidence and reports its specific reason with a nonzero exit. Ordinary update acquisition and recovery safeguards are unchanged; no schema or protocol change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The package-activation owner supplies the same verified journal and lease inspection used by settlement. Repair passes that store's path and identity to its existing preparation and reuses the admitted claim through settlement and finalization. Missing-store and foreign-directory recovery remain with their existing owners.

Confirmed on main: repair selected only the default store at [update-repair-command.ts:194](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f07edeba9eaae3df9e7c09f5c197ba847d34bb8/src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-command.ts#L194), while settlement selected the historical store at [package-update-activation.ts:472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f07edeba9eaae3df9e7c09f5c197ba847d34bb8/src/infra/package-update-activation.ts#L472).

## Evidence

title: fix: preserve CLI CPU profiles across startup respawns
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Profiling a source CLI command can silently lose the profile of the process doing the actual work. The normal startup respawn reuses a fixed filename, and its mostly idle launcher exits last and overwrites the main process's profile.

## User Impact

Source CLI profiling now preserves distinct process and inherited-worker profiles. New profiles live in an `openclaw-<command>/` subdirectory of the requested output directory; update flat-file globs accordingly. Existing flat profiles remain untouched. Ordinary CLI execution, prompts, readiness, permissions, and configuration are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let Node generate filenames containing the actual process/thread identity instead of inventing one filename before respawn. Keep command grouping and best-effort rotation at the existing source-runner owner. Rotation still happens before launch; multiple profiles from one launch can exceed its file limit until the next launch.

Thanks to @vincentkoc for requesting the audit and directing this repair.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e4d1d244-6f2b-44f3-877a-b689b11af05a)

The normal `pnpm openclaw agent exec` path was exercised with an isolated synthetic home/state/workspace and a localhost fixed Responses fixture, without disabling respawn or startup guards. Baseline retained only the launcher's profile; the fix retained separate launcher and executing-main profiles. Both returned SYNTHETIC_STARTUP_OK, exited zero, made exactly one localhost request, and left 31,973 build files byte-identical. A supplemental request guard verified the synthetic user message reached the provider and the final response reached the CLI.

- The committed native parent/main/worker regression failed on the base with one profile instead of three, then passed with three readable profiles and independently observed PID/thread identities. A second regression protects command-scoped rotation, unrelated files, and existing flat profiles.

This is a profiler-correctness fix, not a startup, token, or model-speed optimization. Repeated metadata snapshots and source-runner tooling remain investigation candidates; no scope keys or state/safety owners were removed. Linux/Node 26.12.1 was exercised; macOS/Windows were not run locally.

title: feat(ui): let plugins offer feedback on failed replies
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reporting plugins cannot put their own action or receipt beside a failed reply: the failure row always links to the generic GitHub bug form. Replacing the whole transcript just to customize that one action is too broad.

## User Impact

Native UI plugins can offer feedback for a specific failed reply while OpenClaw keeps the original error details, copy button, and recovery controls. Without a selected plugin replacement—or if its view fails—the existing **Report a bug** link remains available.

This is the generic host seam only. It does not enable automatic reporting, send diagnostics, or change a reporting plugin's privacy or delivery policy. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing replacement-view API for a narrow `run-failure-feedback` slot. It receives the pane's agent/session and the exact displayed failed run, without appending a chat message or starting a model turn.

The native notice branch owns the failed-run lifetime; the unchanged shared plugin view retains agent/session scoping, fallback, and teardown. Same-run summary and repeat-count updates preserve the notice. No new service, store, transcript format, or reporting policy was added. Production code grows by 33 net lines.

## Evidence

- The component regressions fail on the original base because the slot is absent. Feedback, failure-notice, shared-view lifecycle and surface suites pass: **32/32**, 3.46 seconds wall time. They cover same-run open details, repeat updates, run/session retirement and fallback. Production UI, chat/API and browser-chat TypeScript, focused lint/format and the lifecycle guard pass.

Preflight confirms tested merge ref `79874ace1e1e9447b80e2881be3399bbdc785d3d` combines `0afd48e` with main `5ce80ebd`. No gate or limit was changed.
- Additional [full-matrix validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44049264060) passed build-artifacts, all 13 UI browser shards and [performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44049264060/job/133923835986). title: fix: explain why project sessions cannot prepare their checkout
body:
Related: #197849

## What Problem This Solves

When a session cannot prepare its repository, chat can show only “Your request couldn’t be completed,” even though the Gateway has a safe, actionable checkout error. Reopening the conversation repeats the generic notice and leaves the person guessing whether another retry can help.

## User Impact

User impact: failed project setup now shows its recovery explanation in chat and reopened history. GitHub HTTP 403 failures explicitly explain that repository access was denied. This does not grant repository access, switch credentials, or make a denied checkout succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep product-authored `ProjectCloneError` copy at the existing dispatch failure owner, before source completion flattens the typed failure. Preserve concise desktop copy and diagnostic/run correlation. Unknown failures remain generic; raw Git output stays in operator diagnostics. Cancellation, input custody, model dispatch, and retry policy are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Red/green regressions: the clone classifier misclassified the observed GitHub denial, and public session creation/startup/history replaced a known checkout cause with generic content.
- Four focused test files passed together in 150.92 seconds across two wrapper shards: clone transport, project-session creation/retry/history, startup errors, and dispatch error lifecycle. This includes genuine Stop, successful later retry, no model dispatch after failed setup, and unknown-private-error coverage. After simplifying only new test assertions, both affected retry scenarios passed again (55.09 seconds including source preparation).
- Targeted production/test lint, core typecheck, changed test typecheck graphs (`gateway-server`, `other`), formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review and local autoreview (Codex engine, P0–P2) found no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its existing runner checkout was dirty. Autoreview covered the complete four-file snapshot based on `96763b979fed377e61d44520294b9eb12a740ae0`; independent review also inspected unchanged owners and the final test-only simplification. Hosted review of the published head also reported no correctness findings.

### Isolated Gateway behavior proof

The published head’s production sources were exercised through a real isolated Gateway and authenticated WebSocket client, not mocked dispatch or materialization. `sessions.create` launched an actual Git process, deliberately given invalid `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` so Git failed before network transport. After `agent.wait` reported the failure, both `chat.startup` and a separate `chat.history` request recovered the same safe explanation and diagnostic ID. The persisted desktop notice was the concise first sentence. The configured fixture model received **zero requests**, as expected for a pre-inference checkout failure. The one-off verification harness was restored afterward; production source bytes and PR head were unchanged.

```text
terminal: error
startup: Git clone failed. Ask the Gateway operator to check projects/clone logs. Diagnostic ID: cfbf2268-8206-4436-b80a-9a097749a08c.
reopened history: identical explanation and diagnostic ID
desktop notice: Git clone failed.
provider requests: 0
actual Git process: yes; configuration rejected before network transport
result: passed (11.933 seconds test time; 37.55 seconds wrapper wall time)
```

This is source-head real-Gateway failure/reopen proof, not a packaged-release or successful private-repository access claim. HTTP 403 classification is separately covered by the transport regression. The deployed retry-cancellation symptom is not claimed fixed: a current-source input-retention check already passed without a lifecycle change. This repairs the reproduced diagnosis/visibility gap, so #197849 remains related rather than closed.

<details>
<summary>Verification commands and cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/projects/project-clone-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-startup-timing.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "remote project retry"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat-workspace-readiness.product.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "retains an actual Git clone failure"
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.ts src/projects/project-clone-runtime.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json src/gateway/server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts src/projects/project-clone-runtime.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/gateway/server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts","src/projects/project-clone-runtime.test.ts"]'
```

Measured standalone baseline regression runs: clone-runtime file 41.83 seconds with cold source compilation; project-session file 92.02 seconds, dominated by existing real Git/worktree and database lifecycle scenarios. One transport regression is added; existing handler scenarios are extended rather than adding Gateway boots. Distributed CI results and job durations: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44044770065.

Simplification: reused existing failure/lifecycle owners; no new storage, helper, compatibility path, or credential fallback. Production delta: +18/−6 lines. Test delta: +23/−6 lines.

</details>

title: fix: avoid false identity errors when unlinked channel users create sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes independent session creation failing for an admitted, unlinked channel sender when the agent supplies a Team profile ID discovered outside the current request.

## User Impact

Admitted unlinked senders can use the same restricted creation path as calls that omit `user`. Valid linked-participant selection remains available; invalid or revoked linked selections remain errors. No new permissions, configuration, or account-linking requirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the optional selector and existing creation owner. Determine fallback eligibility from the ingress owner's original authenticated sender/account linkage result, not a model-supplied ID, another session's owner, or the absence of a current profile. Carry that fact privately to the admitted request and use it only for this independent-creation fallback.

The original refusal correctly prevented an unsupported identity selection; it was not a privilege escalation. This avoids an unnecessary failure without removing collaborative participant selection.

## Evidence

- **Red/green:** at the base, omitted-user creation passed while the same admitted unlinked source with a supplied unrelated profile failed before creation. The fix makes both use the existing contained creation path.
- **Final candidate:** 16 owning-boundary, reply-producer, and lifetime tests plus all 8 channel-admission tests passed. These exercise ingress, private handoff, run admission, the real tool/router, and SQLite creation. Restrictions remain inherited; mismatched, linked-without-grant, unverified, internal, serialized, known-bot, and retired sources do not gain fallback eligibility. Original-source revocation and admitted-owner closure still refuse. Other tools retain explicit-user validation.
- **Sibling coverage:** 200 affected-consumer tests and 78 selected collaboration/native tests passed, including stable tool definitions, original-requester defaults, valid Bob selection, revocation, overlapping Alice/Bob calls, and queued custody. These broader results preceded the final private-handoff simplification; unchanged-input proof was reused. The final 16-test batch and 8-test admission suite cover the changed handoff and lifetime contracts.
- **CI repair:** the first revision introduced a session-identity ratchet failure. The repair removes the duplicate guard and reuses `resolveAdmittedRunActiveAssertion`; no diagnostic rename, baseline change, suppression, or weakened lifetime check. The ratchet passes locally and in the corrected revision's CI.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, diff checks, and commit hooks passed.
- **Independent review:** shared autoreview using Codex CLI completed P0–P2 review of the full candidate against base `b9a72b5bef8d648024f89b66af9579691ae40ce1`, then a fresh P0–P2 review of the CI-repair delta against `9ab2e2653ad4491a9c21ec30946cb79630708f7a`. Both returned `scoped-clean`, no findings; committed diffs match their reviewed snapshots. Local ClawSweeper was not used because its available checkout was dirty/ambiguous; it was left unchanged. The independent reviewers did not run project tests.
- **Published-head CI:** [CI run 44037524592](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44037524592) completed successfully for `6d7f6eeded072fdafcca031430e2c81b1198f072`. The complete 128-entry check rollup had no failed or pending entries. The published tree exactly matches the reviewed and locally tested candidate.

**Limitations:** these are isolated production-owner/composition tests with fixed or mocked model/transport I/O, not live Discord/real-model end-to-end proof. No restart, upgrade, or native-engine E2E claim is made. The private finding deliberately does not survive serialization, restart reconstruction, or another operational run; those paths keep normal selection validation.

### Original failure

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Sender as Admitted unlinked sender
  participant Agent as Agent
  participant Tool as sessions_create
  participant Runtime as Trusted runtime
  Sender->>Agent: Create an independent session
  Agent->>Agent: Copy profile ID from another session's owner
  Agent->>Tool: Create with user set to copied ID
  Tool->>Runtime: Resolve admitted participant
  Runtime-->>Tool: No person authority for supplied ID
  Tool-->>Agent: Refuse before creation
  Note over Tool,Runtime: Correct identity guard; no security bypass
```

### After: preserve valid selection and the unlinked path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Admitted messaging-service request] --> B[Ingress owner resolves sender and account linkage]
  B -->|Originally unlinked source| C[Retain private direct-source unlinked finding]
  C --> D[sessions_create ignores supplied user]
  B -->|Linked requester| E[Keep existing participant selection]
  E -->|Unknown or revoked selection| F[Refuse without creation]
  E -->|Valid selection or original-requester default| G[Existing creation owner]
  D --> G
  G --> H[Inherit sandbox, tool limits and permission ceiling]
  H --> I[Create independent session]
  J[Missing or unsupported source evidence] --> K[No fallback; existing validation applies]
```

### Identity, assignment, and permissions remain separate

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Human as Linked requester or authorized administrator
  participant Runtime as Admitted runtime
  participant Create as Creation owner
  participant Assign as Ownership assignment
  Human->>Runtime: Request creation
  Runtime->>Create: Validated requester or allowed unlinked context
  Create->>Create: Enforce inherited permission ceiling
  Create-->>Human: New session with normal ownership rules
  Human->>Assign: Assign to another person, if authorized
  Assign->>Assign: Change responsibility metadata
  Note over Runtime,Assign: Assignment does not replace requester identity or transfer authority
```

title: fix: keep slash commands in ordinary prose from executing
body:
Related: #199841

## What Problem This Solves

Quoting slash-command instructions in an ordinary message can silently switch the session model, change runtime settings, or run a command instead of discussing it. For example, `Send /model to choose another model.` can select a fuzzy-matched model and lose words from the prompt.

## User Impact

Slash commands, directives, and shortcuts are interpreted only when the canonical sender text begins with `/`, allowing leading whitespace and channel-owned bot addressing. Mid-sentence commands and examples stay ordinary text across the shared Gateway/channel reply path. Explicit native commands, leading commands, chained directives, and `$skill-name` references retain their existing behavior.

**Control UI dependency:** #199841 fixes the separate Enter-time command extraction that happens before Gateway ingress. This backend PR alone does **not** complete the requested all-surfaces behavior until that companion lands. It was verified open at `00e64bab02267db85170b9ad0ffd48ec652e7adf`; its UI implementation is not duplicated here.

**Compatibility:** integrations that supply only a generated envelope/sender label in `Body` must instead provide clean `CommandBody` or `BodyForCommands`. Plain slash-leading `Body` remains supported. Once a message starts with `/`, existing chained parsing remains; this is not Markdown-aware quote parsing inside an admitted command message. No configuration or state migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared reply owner captures directive admission before stripping spans. Reset/general-command preparation and early abort, native-command, bash, and compaction paths now use canonical sender text rather than turning bracketed examples or sender labels into commands. Feishu also stops treating arbitrary plaintext `@name` as removable addressing; its normalized transport mention markup keeps its existing behavior.

The inline directive parser handles model/profile/runtime selection, thinking/fast/verbosity/trace/reasoning controls, elevated/exec settings, queue behavior, and status shortcuts. General slash-command dispatch and explicit skill references remain separate. No new parser, helper, state, configuration, or public field was added; the seven production files have a combined net growth of five lines.

## Evidence

- The exact fuzzy-model sentence failed on base with a synthetic visible catalog entry and passed with the fix. Canonical-admission owner regressions produced 14 intended failures before repair; 282 core owner/consumer tests passed. A required test-only extraction then moved the command-source contract into a coherent sibling suite; the original and new session suites passed 95 tests afterward.
- Feishu plaintext mention regressions produced two intended failures before repair; its command, sequential-key, and ingress suites pass 29 tests across three files, including actual transport-mention controls.
- Shared downstream command tests cover Discord, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage, and WebChat. Representative Discord, Slack, and Telegram adapter suites passed 47 tests; unchanged-input adapter proof was retained rather than restarted.
- After the canonical cutover, Gateway ingress and prompt-prefix stability suites passed 42 tests across two files. The ingress table exercises Control UI/WebChat and macOS/iOS/Android client identities with ordinary slash prose and leading-command controls.
- Before the canonical-prefix follow-up, temporarily composing the UI-only diff from companion #199841 at the pinned head with the directive-gate candidate passed 201 UI unit tests across composer mentions, suggestions, chat view, and command parsing. The exact temporary patch was reversed and `ui/` is unchanged in this PR. This is source-level frontend compatibility proof, not a single live UI-to-provider flow.
- Targeted canonical messaging, Gateway-methods, and Feishu-package typechecks; focused lint, formatting, four-doc MDX validation, line-cap and mock-export ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent local autoreview completed with `scoped-clean` and no P0–P2 findings over base `346d231275b3930848b8e31239c74f689d361436` through the complete uncommitted candidate (binary diff SHA-256 `799879246ff696e35aaf78ba1a4793de2106dbbd0810d41dfb1fc5592010c61a`). The review was static; it does not certify omitted source or runtime behavior. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because the retained runner checkout was dirty; the shared autoreview route was used instead.

### CI consumer repair

[CI run 44033378790](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44033378790) and the hosted review identified three stale assertions expecting mid-sentence model, alias, or exec directives to execute. The test-only follow-up retains those prose inputs as negative controls and adds slash-leading controls for unknown-skill/model selection, the `list` alias, and per-turn exec policy without placement or persistence changes. All 28 tests in the two affected suites pass, along with targeted messaging typecheck, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`. Production code is unchanged.

Independent local autoreview of this two-file follow-up against `7fc364235e9dec21091579284dc1e87a3c090469` also completed `scoped-clean` at P0–P2 (delta SHA-256 `d340fd00d4c7052aef3dbe57a2b353bad1e73d83549b27b9911916ba12187b7a`). New-head CI must finish separately; prior-head CI is not claimed for this follow-up. The small shared surface matrix is retained to protect surface-dependent command routing; separate adapter-boundary regressions remain in place.

**Coverage limits:** real provider/channel E2E, physical/native app builds and device runs, and a full package build were not run. Native coverage exercises Gateway ingress under Control UI/WebChat and macOS/iOS/Android client identities, not those app binaries. Other bundled channels inherit the shared-path admission fix; they were source-audited rather than each live-tested. CI and required GitHub approvals remain separate.

title: fix: redact Windows home paths in doctor SQLite failure reports
body:
Fixes #200451

## What Problem This Solves

When native Windows supplies the home directory through USERPROFILE with HOME unset, doctor's session SQLite migration failure report includes the full home path and OS username in a GitHub issue described as sanitized. Error text using the other path separator can also retain the home path.

## User Impact

New failure reports redact the OS home in target paths and error text with either separator, including when HOME is unset. No configuration or migration action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the OS home once per report through the existing home-dir owner and pass it through all three redaction helpers. Using the OS home preserves redaction even when OPENCLAW_HOME points elsewhere. Keep the existing per-target rewrite optimization for large reports (#194621).

The pr-simplify pass retained the existing helpers and removed their independent HOME reads: +19 net production lines pass the shared result, and +48 test lines cover the issue/report boundary. The neighboring recovery and restore report modules have no separate HOME-only redactor, so no same-family follow-up was identified.

## Evidence

- On base b9a72b5bef8d648024f89b66af9579691ae40ce1, the regression produced **2 failed / 13 passed**: USERPROFILE home paths leaked, and HOME error text leaked its backslash form.
- With the follow-up fix, **15 passed / 0 failed** in `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.failure-reports.test.ts`, run with `timeout 150s pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.failure-reports.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Vitest wall time: **39.62 s** (41.71 s including the test wrapper). CI seconds for the new head are pending.
- The regression exercises real generated and saved GitHub issue bodies and the JSON report with HOME and USERPROFILE, both separators, and a distinct OPENCLAW_HOME.
- The earlier local lint invocation missed `no-param-reassign`, which exact-head CI caught in `check-lint-core-1`. The follow-up uses a local `redacted` accumulator, with no rule suppression. The exact CI-core touched-file command now exits **0 with 0 errors**: `timeout 120s pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check --threads=1 --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-failure.ts`. Formatting and `git diff --check` also passed. Broad checks remain with PR CI.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. Independent Codex autoreview of the implementation at `4c964edcf1d2` against the base above was **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, with no remaining findings. The follow-up only replaces parameter reassignment with a local accumulator and is covered by the lint and test rerun above.

## Limits

Native Windows execution was not available; the environment-variable and separator regression ran on Linux. The configured Crabbox provider could not allocate a box because its required credential was unavailable. Previously saved reports retain their existing publication/receipt contract; this change does not retroactively scrub them.

title: fix: restore scheduled CI dependency checks
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled main CI fails dependency validation after internal export/import changes. It reports three unused exports and a real benchmark host command missing from the dependency model.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible behavior change. Developers regain passing dependency validation without changing approval visibility, resource leases, plugin-review contracts, tests or CI budgets. No migration or operator action is required.

title: fix: preserve requester permissions when interrupted work resumes
body:
Related: #182042, #182043 (distinct completion-recovery paths; this change repairs interrupted root turns).

## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway restart, interrupted work in a shared session can resume without the person who authorized it, or as the session's owner instead. Follow-up tools then reject the task or see the wrong person's permissions.

## User Impact

Interrupted turns can resume as their original requester, within that requester's original limits and current access. Revoked or unavailable sources still fail closed. Existing markers without an original source retain their previous recovery policy; already-yielded roots with only child work alive are not covered by this change. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing shutdown marker and recovery owner to preserve the interrupted turn's bounded authentication source, apply its scope ceiling before session admission, and resume the accepted access grant rather than requesting another one. Do not select a later participant or substitute the session owner.

Also retain service-installation facts through the existing connection-work owner. Losing those host facts in socket callbacks caused the initial trusted-proxy connection to conflict with an already-retained database worker. This restores the same host policy without capturing requester/startup authority or weakening the worker guard. No GitHub credential or permission checks change.

## Evidence

- Original regressions reproduced missing requester authority, wrong-person fallback and refusal at initial trusted-proxy pairing. Focused tests pass for original-scope admission, revocation, own-session restrictions, original-grant reuse, owner certificates and request-context isolation. The eight requester regressions now live in the existing admission-test owner, without changing their assertions or the hosted budget.
- Live OpenAI full-access recovery passed with gpt-5.6-luna after main integration: one original side effect, fresh shell work, a completed child and one final reply after a real Gateway replacement. The gpt-5.4 audit also passed through three replacements without another user turn. The exact retained-child → live GitHub operation remains unproven.
- Final landing corrections use an actual signed-in requester in the process-refusal test, assert its durable captured profile, and change only that profile while the isolated Gateway is stopped. The healthy sibling still resumes; the revoked requester produces a visible failure and no resumed model request. No runtime policy or assertions were weakened. Detailed restart guidance distinguishes captured-source recovery from legacy principal recovery.
- On final head `049f7fffc862659317db98a35862ac4e62a26053`, the documented QA runtime build passed. All seven tests selected from the failed CI run passed locally: five real Gateway restart process tests and two Workshop tests. All 11 admission controls passed. The owning `tsconfig.test.root.other.json` typecheck, core lint for both touched tests, format and diff checks passed. Two all-type imports were corrected to top-level `import type` declarations.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete final correction against `2ee2d08dff5863a45c57c706ad257447773c499b`, P0–P2: complete, scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Earlier complete runtime/main-integration reviews remain applicable to the unchanged runtime.
- Current-head [CI run 44021828880](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44021828880) passed on this exact head (attempt 1); no admin or inherited-failure exception was used. The prior run's Workshop timeout and subsequent cleanup refusal did not reproduce locally; passing replay is not claimed as a Workshop fix. The default typed AI build refused an external declaration input; the supported QA runtime build succeeded without bypassing that boundary or changing shared dependencies.
- Simplification retained the existing marker, recovery and connection-work owners; no new manager or schema. The latest stable predates these restart-source fields; serialized legacy recovery controls passed, but this is not an installed-release upgrade execution.

## What Problem This Solves

When a session menu list is long enough to scroll, such as **Assign to…** on a team with many people, its scrollbar pokes past the menu's rounded corner at the top and bottom of the list. It reads as the scrollbar escaping the menu.

Browsers do not clip a scrolling element's own scrollbar to its rounded corners, so a thumb resting at either end of the track was drawn over the corner. The scrollbar track for these lists now starts and ends where the corners do, so the thumb only moves along the straight edge.

title: fix: allow returning to SQLite after an update
body:
## What Problem This Solves

After an update that keeps the agent schema version unchanged, `openclaw database port --family agent --to sqlite` can refuse with “observed changed canonical rows or allocations.” This blocks returning to SQLite, including before a downgrade, and leaves an active recovery manifest until rollback.

Closes #200356.

## User Impact

Users can return agent databases to SQLite after an update while preserving the release metadata recorded in PostgreSQL. No schema or protocol bump is needed.

An existing failed manifest that already recorded a restamped working copy still requires `--rollback`, then a fresh port attempt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Choose option (a): skip the private SQLite migration for PostgreSQL exports. PostgreSQL source admission already requires the descriptor's schema version, so this migration is unnecessary and can change canonical `schema_meta.app_version` and `updated_at` before exact staging verification.

SQLite sources still migrate. Checkpointing, durable working-copy recovery, target admission, and exact row/allocation comparisons remain in place. This avoids changing global metadata semantics or excluding bookkeeping columns from verification.

The simplification pass retained one existing owner and one condition: production +4 net lines; tests +37 net lines, reusing existing fixtures.

## Evidence

- Base `b4fc05346afb4d6c88b4ab2e8ae3d1eba380917f`: preparation regression **1 passed, 1 failed**, with the reverse-port row changed from `original` to `canonical`; the PostgreSQL file's **7 cases skipped**.
- Fixed patch: both preparation cases pass, including recovery after interrupted staging. Four named files finished **16 passed, 24 PostgreSQL-dependent cases skipped**, exit 0, in **54.64 s**. The two working-copy cases took **193 ms**; cold worker preparation accounted for **30.84 s**. The changed PostgreSQL file remains skipped (standalone baseline collection: **14.91 s**); its new command-boundary assertion preserves an older release stamp and timestamp through the reverse port.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview (Codex), complete final patch against `b4fc05346afb4d6c88b4ab2e8ae3d1eba380917f`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Committed unchanged as `71d4c573f576692da5ff08425361462e2c6a35ba`. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/doctor-database-port-working.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-database-port.test.ts \
  src/infra/database-engine/port-command.mixed.integration.test.ts \

```

</details>

title: fix: allow Git updates to build nested candidate checkouts
body:
Closes #200357

## What Problem This Solves

Git-install updates launched by the shipped v2026.11.4 updater can abort at `preflight-build` with “Declaration input escapes checkout”. The updater builds inside the existing installation, where optional SDK type imports can reach the parent installation’s dependencies after #198661.

## User Impact

Candidates containing this fix can emit checkout-local declarations in the nested layout used by already-shipped updaters. Parent-install types remain excluded. No updater change or operator configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the fast compiler CLI path for contained inputs. If its input list escapes the checkout, discard its output and private staging files, then recompile through the existing bounded API filesystem. This also bounds fallback callers that omit an admission callback; historical declaration-only API callers retain their existing behavior.

The former “fails closed when optional SDK relative imports reach a parent install” test encoded the update regression. It now leaves the parent shadowing package installed and checks successful emission of only local inferred types, local inputs, and local source maps. Required parent-only dependencies still fail before publication; their diagnostics now identify missing modules/files because bounded resolution hides those paths. Escaping local symlinks still fail at the checkout boundary.

The fallback pays for a second, slower compilation only when the CLI encounters escaping inputs. Moving future preflight worktrees outside the installation is a separate follow-up and cannot repair already-shipped updaters.

## Evidence

- Verified current main’s emitter matches the assigned base (`b4fc05346afb4d6c88b4ab2e8ae3d1eba380917f`) and read #198661’s original safety contract.
- Red: the updated nested-layout real-compiler regression fails on the base with `Declaration input escapes checkout` at `native-declaration-emitter.mts:386` (1 failed, 17 filtered/skipped).
- Green: 32 passed, 5 platform/filesystem skips across the three named files below. The nested regression covers explicit and omitted admission callbacks. Required parent imports, escaping symlinks, inherited configs, publication preservation, and compiler shutdown remain covered.
- `native-declaration-boundary.test.ts`: 15 passed, 3 Windows skips; 4.410 s test time, 6.21 s command wall time.
- `tsdown-declaration-resolution.test.ts`: 14 passed, 2 platform/filesystem skips; 18.560 s file time. Together with the 3 passing subprocess tests, command wall time was 22.34 s. First CI snapshot: 13 pending, 6 skipped, no failures reported. CI seconds are not available yet.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Targeted typecheck of the three touched files and their imports also passes (temporary config with repository compiler settings, script `allowJs`, and explicit file roots).
- Independent review: shared Codex autoreview, complete local snapshot against `b4fc05346afb4d6c88b4ab2e8ae3d1eba380917f`, P0–P2 coverage, `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Full emitter, changed tests, and boundary/caller context supplied; reviewer did not independently execute tests. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because discovered checkouts were dirty; ClawSweeper posted its automatic PR receipt; hosted review is pending, with no duplicate manual request.
- `pr-simplify`: no new owner or helper; replaced the hard failure with reuse of the existing bounded emitter. Production delta +32/-13 lines; test delta +30/-13 lines. Remaining growth selects the fallback and preserves boundary/diagnostic proof.

Commands: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test test/scripts/native-declaration-boundary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test test/scripts/tsdown-declaration-resolution.test.ts test/scripts/native-declaration-subprocess.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

Limits: full builds/broad checks are deferred to PR CI under the production-host rules. Live upgrade proof is out of scope for this lane; the parent will run the unmodified published-driver × candidate upgrade proof. No live Gateway or operator state was changed.
