title: fix(ui): keep lazy panel menu actions ready for selection
body:
Dashboard options can ignore Expand Dashboard or Restore split just after opening.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6a1b6fef-8de4-46d1-8db7-8a8e43aa305c)

## What Problem This Solves

When lazy panel-menu content is already loaded, enabled rows can render before their selection handlers are registered. Clicking one then silently does nothing and leaves the root menu open. Five unrelated UI E2E jobs fail in the same layout-preservation test: three select Restore split and two select Expand Dashboard.

## User Impact

Dashboard and Layout menu actions become available together with their handlers, so the first actionable click can change the layout and dismiss the menu even during its opening phase.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rendering and activation now share the registered handler snapshot. Until it is ready, both use the existing disabled Loading row. This removes the independent body-rendering path that exposed actions before activation could find them. The shared test helper and its menu-hidden assertion are unchanged.

One shared panel-menu factory owns registration, loading items, lazy group rendering, error recovery, selection, and focus handoff for both consumers. The lazy components register their handlers; the factory renders only registered rows. This removes duplicate group renderers, the unused render callback bridge, and the separate boundary wrapper, preserving the readiness fix and unchanged regression. Production is net 38 lines smaller than the original base; the regression adds 105 lines. No budget or baseline file changes.

## Evidence

- A deterministic Node/jsdom regression exercises the real Dashboard menu, primes its lazy component in a separate mount, then clicks the first enabled connected leaf while frame callbacks are held in `opening`. It does not mock `onReady`, menu activation, or selection. Both labels fail on the base with no `menu-select` event and pass with the fix, including the expected layout update and menu closure.
- Final regression: 2/2 pass in 0.861 s Vitest wall time (179 ms in test callbacks); the exact regression fails 2/2 on original production source in 0.957 s. The CI Bun run also passed both cases in 256 ms total (193 ms / 63 ms).
- The current follow-up plus existing pane-header and dashboard-presentation consumer suites: 80/80 pass across three named files in 4.47 s. The readiness regression is unchanged.
- Touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Lint reports existing warnings in the unchanged layout-model function.
- Strict touched-file typecheck was attempted but stopped before checking source because the repository wrapper rejects a compiler outside the worktree; the existing dependencies are in a shared cache. No compiler guard was bypassed. CI production and test typechecks subsequently passed; the local placement limitation remains recorded.
- Fresh follow-up Auto Review (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete local candidate, including the shared helper and unchanged regression, against `9f441adcf1e7307e1dfd0a496660106c4922dfe8` with the menu, machine, overlay lifecycle/control, and lazy-content owners supplied: scoped-clean, no findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable.
- No browser, Chromium, container, dependency installation, or broad local sweep was run on the Team Gateway host. The CI artifacts identify the matching root-menu state but do not retain activation history for the original five failures; exact-head PR CI must supply the browser result.


### Sizing acceptance for the follow-up

The normalized **chat boot JS gzip** measurement in PR CI's existing `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` head/base build comparison must have **head minus base <= 0 bytes**. Use that CI pair for the same workload and normalization; the preceding candidate was +30 bytes. This is an artifact-size comparison, not a latency sample. No local UI build or performance/packaging script is run on the Team Gateway host. No budget or baseline changes are permitted.

Current candidate: `7016bddcdba19b81ae033da6e96be93058e72a53`. [Its control-ui-performance check passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44012963534/job/133804985780): normalized chat boot JS gzip **1,324,689 → 1,324,606 bytes (−83)**, **85 bytes below** the unchanged 1,324,691-byte ceiling. The CI pair uses base `a564030a2b6ea08a2198a16d6865f1d9928dd496` and merge checkout `64c6fd806b805ecb09818b5d99345a7ad2012bb1`, with Node v24.22.1 / Vite 8.3.5 / Pako 3.0.3. This meets the <=0-byte acceptance rule.

Fresh P0–P2 Auto Review of the complete candidate is scoped-clean; all 80 focused tests and touched-file type-aware lint/format pass. [Exact-head production types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44012963534/job/133805937383) and [selected UI E2E smoke shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44012963534/job/133804985754) pass. Test types, CI lint and UI unit shards were still running at the result capture; no full-CI success claim is made. The original browser layout caller remains outside the observed smoke selection.

[The preceding fdda84cb performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44011903578/job/133801349082) measured **1,324,689 → 1,324,707 bytes (+18)**, against base `f52f728d34158e66c0d11ce48cc7fb1c7a0cd6a7`; the current shared renderer addresses that remaining growth. Production and test typechecks and the selected UI E2E shard passed on that prior head. Its performance failure was not rerun.

[The cf709361 performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44010220663/job/133795978659) measured **1,324,689 → 1,324,703 bytes (+14)**, 12 bytes above the 1,324,691-byte ceiling. This supersedes the earlier +30-byte candidate but still fails the acceptance criterion.

[The latest main run that actually ran performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44010442679/job/133796400798), at `054fd9788bc0f86303e161ca3b2ab36a1ed8cd65`, measured **1,324,689 bytes**, 2 bytes below that ceiling. Newer main push runs skipped the performance job or had no such job. Thus cf709361 adds 14 bytes against the same measured main/base; its gzip failure is attributable to this diff. Exact byte figures come from only the scalar comparison lines in the job output; the check summary has no byte figures. No full logs or local builds were used.

### Prior-head PR CI results

[CI run 44007450967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967) covers head `80923235eae1b1762d024709fe000d738801f5e4` through merge checkout `3a2e5808f80a2a109c114995b63c545dffbaa704`.

- [UI E2E shard 1/2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967/job/133786879480) passes: 12 tests across five selected smoke files. This selection does **not** include `chat-panel-layout.e2e.test.ts`; the original browser caller remains unrerun. No Chromium/Playwright run was attempted on the Team Gateway host, and blocked remote credentials were not bypassed.
- [UI shard 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967/job/133786879718) fails `chat-position-rail.test.tsx > conversation position rail > keeps the focused run marker through streaming and retargets its persisted answer` (`expected false to be true`). The fixture mounts only ChatThread/transcript and ChatPositionRail; it never renders or calls the panel-menu factories changed here. The new readiness test ran in shard 1/3, a separate process from this shard. This failure is unreachable from this diff and is left untouched; it is not the l74 wheel/layout assertion.
- [Control UI performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007450967/job/133786879735) fails. Its own head/base comparison reports chat boot JS gzip **1,324,689 → 1,324,719 bytes (+30)** against a 1,324,691-byte limit, so this change crosses that budget by 28 bytes. Both builds also violate the shared CSS ceiling (59,191 vs 58,315 bytes) and chat request count (21 vs 20). No budget, baseline, or exception was changed.

That prior-head CI run completed with failure. The PR remains ready and unmerged; the follow-up is measured by a new automatic PR run after its source commit.

### Supplemental release regression proof — November 17, 2026

Actual Chromium captures compare parent `cc6c3a733dfa9e226efcf4b2c221c45fe40f9acc` with merged repair `8a82b5e0b29108b804ea9267f04409cb7a9950f3`. Both clicks occur at the first enabled DOM observation during opening: before remains open/split; after dismisses and expands. Clean and annotated images below were inspected and sanitized. No DOM fabrication or frame scheduling manipulation. Exact release backport `f41b66c8f5f557fb8d6713a78d9a6839d27c4821` additionally passes the original panel browser suite (3/3). body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat plugin cards do not show installation and browser-connection progress or recovery clearly enough.

## User Impact

User impact: users can follow installation, connect a configured MCP server, cancel or retry authorization, and distinguish Installed from Connected in the chat card. Cards are larger, responsive, and keep status and spinners beneath the title. Uninstalled, installable cards show “Ready to install”; unavailable, restricted and checking cards do not. No configuration changes or migration are required.

Integrations without a shared account model keep Manage: this does not invent account counts, Add account, or a separate Reconnect state. Disabled plugins continue through the existing Manage/consent flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admitted installation receipts now belong to one application-Gateway-scoped owner instead of disappearing with the plugin page. The card consumes those receipts and reuses the existing MCP wizard for authorization URLs, confirmed cancellation, typed expiry, retry, and authoritative reinspection. Existing installation and enablement admission stays in the plugin consent flow.

**Previous-head CI (historical; not the copy correction):** [run44007460768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007460768), head`e1b40862dbc97013307c7aa3ba703369fa590ac9`, is still **failed**, not green. The initial reconnect, suppression, cursor and CSS failures are repaired; performance, all three UI shards, nine E2E shards, lint/types/ratchets and applicable security checks pass. Remaining failures are a60-second cold runtime-build timeout and a30-second Dashboard Restore split menu timeout. Their owners and runtime/build inputs are unchanged from the actual tested main baseline; the failed UI snapshot contains no plugin cards or changed lazy plugin resources. Both original cases passed bounded local and baseline replay, which does not establish a fix or matching baseline failure. The independent causality review found no concrete PR-caused route but retained attribution uncertainty; no inherited-only waiver is claimed. Native auto-merge was canceled and its retirement verified while that investigation remains open.

**CI correction proof:** the full-bundle native correction comparison, `pnpm ui:check-performance:base b601a4b206c26148365c17210e94fed5d8421670` on Node 24.22.1, passes: total CSS 337,296 → **337,310 B gzip** (+14 B), 1,740,068 → **1,740,080 B raw** (+12 B). The existing base itself has the same 21 chat requests and 59,194 B largest CSS asset; unchanged baseline violations are not relabeled green. No budget or baseline exception is added.

- 99 focused component/owner/consumer tests pass, including fresh install-policy review after reconnect and preservation of admitted or saved/uncertain outcomes; including persisted installation outcomes, plugin generations, and wizard cancellation settlement.
- Four production-bundle Chromium scenarios pass: mounted status updates; the supported state matrix and mobile wrapping; canonical page installation followed by navigation back to chat, failure, retry and success; and the actual MCP UI owner through browser authorization, cancellation, expiry, retry and connection. Focused final proof also verifies the application event-bus cutover and the Installing spinner's visible geometry/animation and busy accessibility.
- The missing Installing transition is red on the prior candidate and green after the shared-owner change. A fresh independent review found an obsolete-failure recovery issue; its regression is red on the reviewed snapshot and green after authoritative reconciliation.
- Production UI, chat-test, chat-E2E and plugin-page test typechecks pass. Scoped lint, CSS lint, formatter, Control UI ownership guards, i18n verification and diff checks pass. One retired direct-client event listener was removed from its exact baseline; no baseline was raised.

The graph contains no PR paths; tracked inputs, supporting test/build sources and lock match the fork base. Dependency/generated identities were not independently compared. That investigated local failure remains recorded—not relabeled passing or fixed—and exact new-head hosted CI is still required.

The screenshots use the actual production Control UI with synthetic Gateway and authorization-service responses, not live plugin installation or external credentials. The clean/annotated comparison is dark theme at 1280×900; the state gallery is light theme, with separate 393×852 available and authorization mobile captures. Clean and annotated comparisons, the supported-state gallery, and mobile captures are embedded below.

title: fix(ui): long tool activity summaries run past the reply text in Safari and Firefox
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long tool activity summary ("Ran commands, read files, called …") runs past the right edge of the reply text in Safari and Firefox, and continues under the Details panel, instead of stopping where the text column ends.

## User Impact

User impact: the collapsed tool summary now ends where the reply text ends, and shows an ellipsis when it is too long, in every browser.

In 1:1 threads at the default width, tool rows and the activity block are 8 px wider than before, so they end at the reply's edge instead of just short of it. Shared threads and saved chat widths keep their current widths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The summary limits its width to a percentage of the grid track it sits in, and that track had no size of its own. WebKit and Firefox size such a track to the unwrapped summary, so the limit followed the text instead of the column. Chromium kept the summary in the column but cut it mid-word. The group now has a track as wide as the reading column, and every summary label gets the ellipsis that only the live headline had.

Tool rows and the activity block also carried a 760 px cap from before the conversation column became 768 px wide. They now take the column's width, as they already did under a saved chat width.

## Evidence

Shared thread with the Details panel open, in WebKit (Playwright build 2370, Safari 27.2), 1317×560 at 2×, dark theme. Before is `main` at d29fad4e3e6; after is this change at 285aed1f2d0, which the PR head carries unchanged on current `main` (same patch ID; `main` did not touch `ui/` in between). The session is a mocked-Gateway fixture rendered by the real Control UI build, and the turn's folded activity was opened with a click.

**Before**

![Before: the tool summary continues past the right edge of the reply text and is cut mid-word](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7543bcad-9ade-4a57-83a6-bed2d68a4c81)

**After**

![After: the tool summary ends at the reply's right edge with an ellipsis](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05d80827-2386-412b-8b72-e01f0c890b22)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before, annotated: an arrow marks the summary text beyond the reply's right edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e3a8eb5-d7ae-4ee6-9c54-fc11f2572993)

**After**

![After, annotated: a guide through the right edges of the summary and the reply shows 0 px between them](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13dcf35f-ad81-4acd-a26f-bb2ee8eb589d)

Measured in the same captures:

|        | Summary                         | Reply paragraph | Summary label                           |
| ------ | ------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Before | 1484 px wide in a 668 px column | 668 px          | `text-overflow: clip`, never truncated   |
| After  | 668 px                          | 668 px          | `text-overflow: ellipsis`, truncated     |

- **Regression test:** `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-activity-summary-width.browser.test.tsx` covers direct and shared threads with framed and standalone activity. On `main` it fails in Chromium (`expected 'clip' to be 'ellipsis'`) and in WebKit (`expected 1358 to be greater than 1358`: the label is never truncated). On this branch all 4 cases pass in both, in 1.1 s (Chromium) and 1.5 s (WebKit) of wall time. The file joins the WebKit lane's list so CI runs it there.
- **Changed expectation:** `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` asserted the 760 px default for tool rows and the activity block. It now asserts that they match the thread at the default width, as it already did for a saved width.
- **Sibling suites:** the chat column, activity layout, responsive and disclosure browser suites pass with the new file (82 tests in five files), and so do the tool-outcome, canvas detail width, bubble activity and heartbeat rollup E2E suites (25 tests).
- **Checks:** `pnpm check:changed` passes with the dead-export scan skipped (no exports changed; CI runs it): guards, format, type checks for the UI and core test graphs, lint and stylelint.
- **CI:** run [43992829096](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43992829096) on this head has two failed jobs, both outside this change. `checks-ui (1/3)` fails `chat-transcript-projection-scale.test.ts` › "moves live activity to the current eligible group after replacement and run changes" with the same assertion as `main`'s scheduled run [43979180619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43979180619); it passes locally on this change three times. `checks-ui-e2e (6/10)` times out selecting a layout menu item in `chat-panel-layout.e2e.test.ts` › "preserves live content and saved geometry across main, dock, focus, and narrow layouts"; locally the same timeout occurs with `main`'s chat CSS in 3 of 4 runs and with this change in 1 of 4. title: fix(update): keep SQLite contention frames in bounded failure reports
body:
Related #200289

## What Problem This Solves

Failed-update diagnostics can discard the SQLite call site when a Doctor failure's stack appears in the middle of long stderr.

## User Impact

Operators can inspect the contention error and up to 12 leading stack frames in the saved failure JSON linked from the update report and in repair prompts. This is a diagnostic improvement, not a root-cause fix for the SQLite lock or prolonged update reported in #200289.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing triage owner retains an optional `sqliteContentionCallSite` excerpt with the same secret/path redaction and a separate 1 KiB JSON-encoded UTF-8 cap. It survives artifact writing, reading, and prompt sanitization. Ordinary stderr retains its 384-byte head/tail limit, and the 8 KiB artifact and 4 KiB prompt-record limits still apply. Existing whole-record pruning can still omit older failed steps, and the byte cap can shorten long stacks.

The Markdown report already links this support JSON; its existing layout is unchanged. The failure-report documentation now describes the retained excerpt and bounds.

## Evidence

- Loss on the pinned base: `src/infra/update-run-step.ts:105-110` drops ordinary exit-1 Doctor stderr from the ledger projection; `src/infra/update-run-report.ts:433-440` bounds the summary to 300 characters and only emits stderr for signals or candidate snapshots. `src/infra/update-failure-report-artifact.ts:33-35` likewise restricts its stderr appendix to signal failures and links support JSON at line 246. That JSON loses the middle stack at `src/commands/triage-update.ts:371-374` (384-byte head/tail excerpt).
- Red on base `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637`: the middle-block regression failed; 12 existing tests passed. Fixed: **33 passed across four named files**, including realistic multi-KB stderr, first-frame retention, the 12-frame limit, oversized UTF-8/JSON-escaped frames, redaction, repeated sanitization, rollback readers, prompt composition, and artifact writing.
- Focused command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node timeout 120s pnpm test src/commands/triage-update.test.ts src/commands/triage-update-rollback.test.ts src/commands/triage-prompt.test.ts src/infra/update-failure-report-artifact.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. title: fix(ui): Escape doesn't stop a running reply when focus is outside the composer
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pressing Escape does not stop a running reply when keyboard focus is anywhere other than the message box, for example after reloading the page during a run or after clicking in the conversation.

## User Impact

User impact: Escape now stops the visible run from anywhere in the chat pane. Menus, dialogs, panels, text fields, and reply quotes still handle Escape first, so the first press closes an open menu and only an unclaimed press stops the run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Escape-to-stop lived only in the composer textarea's keydown handler. After a reload, focus lands on the page body, and clicking the transcript focuses the transcript, so Escape reached nothing. This was not a regression: the shortcut has always required composer focus.

The composer keeps ownership of the stop policy (no stop while its menus, dictation, or a reply target are active). It exposes that policy through its pane state, and the active pane listens on `window` in the bubble phase. Window listeners run after every element and document handler, so existing Escape owners, including document-level ones like the message context menu, act first. The pane then applies the same exemptions the chat already uses when it forwards typed letters to the composer: open dropdowns, overlays, modal surfaces, fields, and autotype-exempt docks.

## Evidence

Maintainer retest of `49e9872bb77eeb97c01ad276fde92cb77b3cdf6e` in Chromium, using the real Control UI and a mocked Gateway:

- On main `f1d7daedced8b1d34e6f368bd481e66884d1c297`, the body-focus regression failed specifically because no `chat.abort` arrived after Escape. The Gateway was connected, the run was active, and Stop remained available.
- On this PR, all 15 cases across composer shortcuts, retained-pane Escape and split-pane focus passed. UI typechecking also passed.
- A focused two-running-pane check confirmed that each Escape aborts only the selected pane's run.
- Menu, quote and IME checks preserve their existing Escape ownership. The document menu handler prevents propagation before the window listener.
- The new menu test initially failed twice because it sent Escape before the menu's next-frame keyboard-listener initialization. The maintainer change synchronizes that setup with one animation frame; assertions, timeouts and production code are unchanged.
- Independent review found no unresolved production issue; its test-readiness finding was resolved by the tested four-line change.

The original report came from a real session: the page reloaded mid-run, and no abort arrived until Stop was clicked. The browser checks above do not claim a separate native WKWebView test.

title: improve(ui): Cmd+K lists named settings first and improves session search
body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a5cfb8d-a446-47ff-bd14-38afb5b63bf2)

## What Problem This Solves

Searching for a setting in Cmd+K buries it below any session that mentions the same word, and archived sessions never show up at all.

## User Impact

User impact: typing a setting or command name in Cmd+K shows it first, sessions follow newest first, and archived sessions whose title matches appear in their own muted "Archived" group (at most three) instead of being missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Results now follow intent instead of a single match score:

1. Settings and commands whose name matches the query.
2. Sessions: an exact match first, then newest first. Where a word falls inside a sentence-like session title no longer changes the order.
3. Archived: up to three archived sessions whose title matches, newest first, muted. A separate best-effort `sessions.list` call with `archived: true` and `searchTitlesOnly: true` supplies them. Live results appear without waiting for that lookup; a failed archive lookup only omits archived rows until the next search.
4. More results: commands, settings, plugins, skills and models that match only by description or keywords, in their own group so they cannot crowd the top.
5. In messages: transcript hits, unchanged.

Archived message text is still not searched; the existing palette note about that remains. The Sessions filter tab counts active and archived sessions together.

## Evidence

Scenario: query `appearance` with three active and two archived matching sessions. Control UI E2E harness with a mocked Gateway and fixture sessions, 1280×900, light theme. Before: `main` at 48cd549. After: this branch at 9ea31d4. Dark theme was also checked.

### Clean comparison

![Before: three sessions listed above the Appearance setting; no archived sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f1fa358-4627-468f-90ab-3a0fb754fe68)

![After: Appearance setting first, then three sessions, then two muted archived sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b5a5f1e-34b1-4bea-be7e-6c63547c0217)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: sessions listed first, Appearance setting after sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d58bb8a9-97f9-4d4e-80ca-07311f83730e)

![After, annotated: named setting first; archived sessions in their own muted group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d70d5675-01a1-4472-a732-399fb567690d)

Checks:

- Command palette unit suites: 146 tests passed, including new ordering and archived-group cases.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint on changed files and `pnpm lint:ui:styles` passed.
- Opening an archived result navigates to the session's existing archived view with its Unarchive action (verified in the same harness).
- Local autoreview (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol) on branch range 48cd549..9ea31d4 at P1: scoped-clean, no findings.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

<!-- openclaw-publication:23ab8be0-c4c2-4026-8eae-5a05aa62cd83 -->

## Maintainer repair and verification

The repair in `8f1d76d648b` preserves this design and fixes three result-handling defects:

- A setting-name match stays ahead of description matches before the catalog's ten-result cap. The name-match flag is computed once per item.
- Available live results appear while archived search is pending. Later archived results preserve the item already selected with the keyboard.
- Archived title matching happens in the existing Gateway filter before pagination, so ten newer model/provider matches cannot hide an older matching title. The optional `sessions.list.searchTitlesOnly` parameter defaults to the existing search behavior. Query identity and the generated runtime validator include it. No database migration or saved-preference change is involved.

The two client regressions and the Gateway filtering regression failed before the repair. Validation covered 131 palette tests, 10 query-ownership tests and 7 Gateway filter tests; the four affected catalog cases and lint passed again after the final catalog cleanup. Core, UI and selected test typechecks passed, as did the official validator-generation check and an independent P0–P2 review.

A real isolated Gateway, built from the repaired sources, returned:

| Query | Page size | Total matches |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Existing broad search | 10 | 13 |
| Title-only search | 1 | 1 |
| Explicit `searchTitlesOnly: false` | 10 | 13 |

The title-only result was the intended older conversation. The first RPC attempt exposed the missing compiled validator in the repair; regenerating it with the official owner and rebuilding fixed that rejection. No provider or model execution was needed. Private-row exclusion was checked at the existing filter owner, not with a separate live private-identity RPC.

The captures below compare the original PR with the repair while the archive lookup is held, then show the completed results. They use the real Control UI with a scripted Gateway; the real RPC check above is separate. All data is synthetic.

title: fix(state): prevent retained deleted agents from blocking Gateway startup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #200271: Gateway startup can crash-loop when a completed agent deletion intentionally retained an older database.

## User Impact

Active agents can start while the deleted agent’s retained files stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Pending deletions keep their existing behavior. Active-agent and shared-state validation, refusal behavior, and permanent-purge capabilities are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup copy-and-swap path added by #198389 (`ef930ebbad771ae219e033f8c5b59a12b5445ffb`) inventories physical agent stores without consulting deletion completion. Startup now consumes the deletion journal owner’s existing retained-ID query and excludes completed retained agents from both upgrade selection and shadow copying. No new schema, registry, fallback, or configuration is added.

The simplification pass keeps this decision with the existing deletion owner. Necessary scope: production +22/-6 lines, tests +103 lines, documentation +3 lines. Test growth is below the 400-line allocation threshold.

## Evidence

- **Red base:** unchanged production at `48cd549b1c48653061ec312e35fef62d13df62cf` plus the regression: `timeout 120s pnpm test src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'startup retained deletion'` — **2 failed, 1 passed, 7 skipped**; both completed-retention cases reject with `no such module: vec0` from generic fallback. The pending-deletion control passes with today’s schema refusal/fallback failure.
- **Green fix:** `timeout 120s pnpm test src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **10 passed, 0 failed**; 56.95 s command wall time (54.59 s Vitest duration; 13.394 s summed test time). Covers completed retention alone, completed retention beside a shared-state upgrade, and the pending-deletion control. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Real SQLite, the existing v26 schema fixture, a retained session row, and a real `vec0` virtual table reproduce the reported fallback error. Current-schema active stores are present. Retained database bytes and directory contents remain unchanged after the fixed upgrade; the active store bytes also remain unchanged.
- Targeted lint and TypeScript compiler diagnostics: `timeout 120s pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check --threads=1 --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/state/state-upgrade.ts src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts` — exit 0, zero diagnostics. A temporary negative control reported TS2322 and was removed.
- `timeout 30s pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/state/state-upgrade.ts src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts docs/install/updating.md` and `timeout 20s git diff --check` pass. Commit hooks also pass.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. Independent **autoreview**, Codex, P0–P2, reviewed the full local candidate against `48cd549b1c48653061ec312e35fef62d13df62cf`: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Candidate diff SHA-256: `165afa0f222e905c275028524a56758567fd7f0b550f5723b66b0baa8103814a`; committed without further code changes as `db8faf1c6e41d7f83616ec570c4204eda24d4058`. One hosted review will be requested if none is already pending.

- **Live upgrade from latest stable (Crabbox AWS Linux, Node 24.19.0):**
  - **Setup:** npm `openclaw@2026.11.4` (`d843d6a`), isolated state. Created agents `keeper` and `retired`, started the stable Gateway, then called `agents.delete {agentId: "retired", deleteFiles: false}` and stopped it cleanly. The journal row was `cleanup_completed=1, delete_files=0, phase=retiring`; state was v22 and agents were v27. One tarball snapshot was used for both runs.
  - **Base `48cd549b` (red):** startup listed `agents/retired/.../openclaw-agent.sqlite v27` for upgrade. It logged `State upgrade chain failed at agent-schema: .../retired/... is at schema 27 after the chain, expected 42`, then fell back to the generic copy and set aside 7 rows. The retained database was rewritten (its sha256 changed) and its `.seal` was removed. The stores had no `vec0` tables, so this run finished on the degraded generic-copy path instead of the reporter's `no such module: vec0` exit. The vec0 crash is covered by the in-process regression above.
  - **PR head `db8faf1c` (green):** the upgrade inventory listed only state v22, `keeper` v27 and `main` v27. Startup reported `State upgraded ... by migration chain`: no fallback, no rows set aside. `/healthz` returned 200 `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` and `/readyz` returned 200 `{"ready":true,"coreReady":true,"failing":[]}`. After the upgrade, state was v40 and `keeper`/`main` were v42. The retained `retired` database and seal were byte-identical (sha256 `6616c54a…` / `0a5e3ed5…` before and after), and its journal row was unchanged. `agents list` shows `main` and `keeper`, and config (`gateway.port`) was preserved.
  - Both leases were stopped. The first box lost its worker connection mid-run and was replaced; the red evidence comes from that first box and the green evidence from the replacement, both from the same stable setup steps.

Limits: no live macOS launchd reproduction. The live stable-to-head proof above used stores without `vec0` tables; the `vec0` exit path is covered by the in-process regression with a real `vec0` table. Broad checks are left to PR CI under the production-host restrictions.

title: fix(github): let PR contributors continue work across sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes credited contributors being blocked from continuing a publisher-authored PR when they move to a different conversation.

## User Impact

A verified linked GitHub account already credited as an author, coauthor or committer on the PR can import it and append changes to the original branch across conversations. No new role, grant, configuration or migration is required. Existing private-repository access, session authority, publisher permission and remote-head checks remain in place. Refusals retain the existing advice to use the original publication conversation or ask a full-write maintainer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared PR eligibility check previously recognized the PR author or the current conversation’s publication receipt, but not the human contributors behind a bot-authored PR. It now checks GitHub-recognized numeric account identities on the current PR commits, only when the PR author is the selected publisher. PR-body mentions and unpublished local trailers do not grant access.

This changes the shared eligibility owner used by inspection, preparation, publication and imported-PR actions. It does not change workspace custody/recovery or grant merge permission. Docs and tool guidance describe the same eligibility; repeated guidance is consolidated without adding prompts or permissions.

title: fix(sessions): stop self-only recall from scanning unrelated sessions
body:
Related: #198855

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow or failed history recall under self-only visibility when unrelated session inventory is large or unavailable.

## User Impact

Self-only recall searches the current conversation directly, without waiting for an unrelated roster scan. Explicit targets, host-bound read scopes, sandbox clamps, incognito restrictions and broader visibility modes retain their existing authorization paths. This does **not** fix the separate broad-search fanout investigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Effective `self` visibility already defines a one-session search universe. Reuse the existing targeted resolver and access check instead of enumerating the roster and filtering it back down. No new permission, protocol, configuration, dependency, state or cache is introduced.

## Evidence

- Current-session regression: red on the base when unrelated inventory is unavailable; green with the fix, retaining canonical-key matching and foreign-hit exclusion.
- 39 focused tool tests plus the Gateway visibility-matrix test pass; 14 prefix-stability cases pass. Focused wrapper: 26.07s. Broad error coverage explicitly selects `all` and retains its assertions.
- Strict targeted production/test/script types, lint, format and diff checks pass. Complete search-range and later ACK-delta local autoreviews found no P0–P2 findings; reviewers did not execute project code.
- [Exact-head CI 43932467783](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43932467783) completed successfully on attempt 1 at `aa3656aa5101bc6a92fdbf5bca7adbfe3d53b2be`; both UI E2E shards and both CI gate statuses passed. The original failed CI attempt remains recorded.

### Real agent/model proof — passed

A fresh isolated Gateway was built from source `895756d5aa4ff188db6081e342f8315878992025`, whose committed tree `65cedc05c03f459c4a627d6af39a421a98a63484` exactly matches the published head. Only a task-owned driver and synthetic scenario were added outside the shipping diff.

The normal source-selected `live-frontier` flow used a real configured OpenAI model, the normal agent RPC, Gateway search, QA-channel delivery and persisted transcript owners. The final canonical report is **1 scenario, 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; all selected cells executed**. It verifies:

- served `agents.list` includes the QA agent and the served primary model has canonical OpenAI identity;
- the model actually issues a successful `sessions_search` with `sessionKey` omitted;
- its persisted search result contains the earlier synthetic reference code;
- the separately persisted final and normal non-error delivered final both equal `SELF-SEARCH-OK violet-copper-9281`.

An earlier bound live execution also passed. This is one scenario exercised twice, not two distinct coverage cases. The first unbound attempt never reached model execution because QA imported the SecretRef without its provider definition. The existing fixture hook then retained only the matching, already-configured absolute-path file-provider definition. No key values, alternate accounts, model overrides, endpoints or credential references were supplied or changed by that fixture. Synthetic controls reproduce the missing-definition error and pass with the supported hook. The narrowed proof harness also received an independent P0–P2 clean review.

### Transport work-count measurement

Five serial ABAB process pairs, each one cold and five warm self searches over 600 synthetic sessions, used the real tool → Gateway WebSocket path on Node 26.12.1. Base `4a0e45492b8987d67d8b56e8d6dcdb3765aa61ed`; measured search source `0d8db16e701a3a520d6216e3c4b6ce77ec42ee48`, unchanged by the ACK-test repair.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unrelated listing RPCs per self search | 3 | 0 |
| Search RPCs per self search | 1 | 1 |
| Warm median / p95 (25 queries per arm) | 103.990 / 140.799 ms | 16.311 / 24.076 ms |
| Cold median / p95 (5 queries per arm) | 1095.432 / 1180.355 ms | 841.583 / 889.071 ms |

Result and completeness flags matched in the no-match fixture. Rerun `scripts/perf/session-search-rpc-measure.ts` with fresh state directories, `--sessions 600 --visibility self`, and `--tool-ref <base-sha>` for the baseline. This benchmark does not establish broad-search recall correctness.

### CI readiness repair

[Original failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43926884806/job/133509748396): the ACK-ownership test scrolled a replaceable loading summary before resolving the steer ACK. Source `895756d5aa4ff188db6081e342f8315878992025` makes its selector wait for the resolved command descendant. All ACK, retained-draft, retained-tool and send-count assertions remain unchanged; no retries, sleeps, timeout increases or production changes were added.

The controlled import/stability-window probe is red on main `ec025eba2df15ab949239fa17dfd99ac4286b50c` and green with the selector. All four original cases pass on that baseline plus the repair and the combined search candidate: 19.69s wrapper, including 10.37s UI build; 5.754s test time. Hosted ClawSweeper found no actionable technical findings on prior search head `d5464f9cb957499c6697470907222d8cec84320b`; the new readiness delta has its separate fresh local review.

<details>

title: improve(compaction): prepare large histories outside the Gateway thread
body:
Related: #185111 (large-history preparation context; not a claim to resolve its Codex pre-turn workload).

## What Problem This Solves

Preparing a large retained history for default safeguard compaction can block the Gateway thread and delay unrelated sessions.

## User Impact

Eligible default compaction prepares and rerenders history in the existing transcript reader. Provider requests, authentication, hooks, custom providers, mutable SDK behavior and guarded writes remain host-owned. Oversized or unsupported windows retain complete acknowledged host hydration, not truncated context.

**Paired performance acceptance remains pending.** This is not a proven CPU/memory improvement or global no-blocking guarantee. No configuration, public SDK signature, schema or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

One internal preparation algorithm preserves row provenance and the public four-argument API. Canonical tool, replay, hydration and summary-budget owners serve worker and host consumers. No worker is held across inference, new cache, whole-history graph-transfer protocol or public read-only extension API.

The #194536 worker-memory fix is preserved: private plan/render cohorts are admitted **before payload decoding**, with a 16 MiB serialized-input ceiling and the unchanged 512 MiB worker heap. Larger windows retain complete streamed host hydration. This input ceiling is not a universal decoded-heap guarantee. Renders use the maintained filtered JSONL budget check in the same snapshot.

Current-main integration preserves repeat-guard metadata, announced compaction IDs and #200063's session/model-only checkpoint replay identity. Transport authentication is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Scope, simplification and test cost</summary>

The signed series contains five coherent owner prerequisites and private producer/consumer adoption. Yield-only, exclusive-handoff and held-worker alternatives were rejected; duplicate materialization and eager replay work were deleted. Existing SQL position/retention bodies have one context-navigation owner, unchanged except exported-signature formatting, without a line-cap suppression.

The CI repair moves canonical worker data types out of host implementation modules and migrates every internal type caller. Sixteen moved casts are removed through real type narrowing; sparse legacy billing does not acquire fabricated zero-cost data. The wrapper inventory now includes its hydration decoder. Shared prepared-runtime fixtures supply their required catalog. Existing Gateway tests still make 40 real reads and assert over 64 transcript events, using distinct valid read limits rather than weakening the repeat guard. Diagnostic tests own a scoped transport host rather than inheriting another test's mocked provider callbacks.

Against main fcf29c460d159337ee2ea69c5e359f28aedfa88e: **107 paths, +6,882/−2,665 lines**, including mechanical moves. The runtime CI repair is 43 paths, +232/−206; its subsequent fixture-only follow-up changes two existing tests and their allocation. Test growth passes at **2,101 net lines = 400 allowance + 1,701 reviewed allocation**: the earlier 93-line real-worker admission case plus 17 further net lines in existing CI fixtures. There is no new test case/file/cold shard, timeout change or raised shared threshold. Obsolete assertion and mock debt only shrinks; no unrelated UI allowance is added.

The changed 13-case hydration file costs **101.528 s cold wall / 174.598 local child CPU-seconds**, including bootstrap; the new case takes **2.599 s** in the affected batch. PostgreSQL conformance costs **79.568 s wall / 135.495 local child CPU-seconds**. The diagnostic red reproduction costs **68.920 s wall**, mostly transformation; its original lifecycle cases remain present. CI seconds are unobserved, and these different workloads are not speed comparisons.

</details>

## Evidence

The runtime implementation is normal-hook signed **2557ac2dc5b90671157772adf9292bf92d87d11a**, tree **68e73028926dae2bebb772f62519c683bd753963**. Its exact **sourcePerformance** build passes with unchanged tracked source. The preceding whole-feature review retains its original scope; fresh P0–P2 review of the complete 43-path runtime CI repair is scoped-clean with **412,619 bytes of intact input**.

The latest fixture-only follow-up is normal-hook signed **a05d6ff7b2dfa2b3655991adebbf7686e82f021c**, published tree **57ab8bd72361aba17d7eb8f90c22803d6b4fa71d**. Production inputs are byte-unchanged from 2557, so its build, Gateway and native proofs are reused, not relabeled as new-source captures. A fresh three-file P0–P2 review is scoped-clean with **31,559 bytes of intact input**.

- **331 distinct focused cases across 14 files pass** through current or unchanged-input-reused proof: the earlier 169-case batch, a further 154-case batch with four overlapping diagnostic cases, seven isolated Gateway E2E cases, and the latest nine-case fixture run with four diagnostic repeats.
- The diagnostic isolation reproduction fails at the unrelated throwing provider host before the fixture fix, with the other three lifecycle cases passing; all four pass after the fix. Model-call lifecycle and no-prompt-serialization assertions remain intact.
- Hosted CI exposed two additional fixture type errors. The explicit inert plugin host now supplies its complete existing port contract. The prepared-session test consumes `SettingsManager.inMemory` directly with the former fixture's exact settings after main retired an unused private helper export; no compatibility export is restored. Both failing owning graphs, **agents-root and agents-sessions**, now pass locally, as do matching strict type-aware lint, format and all nine fixture cases. Remote CI must still finish.
- Earlier targeted type graphs pass; the combined import graph has **zero cycles**. Assertion, mock, max-lines and test-growth ratchets pass without weakening their limits.
- The earlier replay migration passed **127 cases**. The unchanged memory/SDK/hydration repair passed **121 focused cases** and **two PostgreSQL cases with zero skips**, including catalog/migration/trigger checks and disposable cleanup. These overlapping runs are not added to the distinct count above.
- The real 18 MiB admission fixture preserves byte/navigation facts while corrupting a payload: pre-fix decoding wins over rejection, while fixed plan and render reject before decoding. Restoring it verifies complete streamed hydration. The initial 33,000-row attempt failed at projection rebuilding and remains invalid setup evidence, not a product reproduction.
- An initial offline E2E build preparation failed before any tests at an unavailable registry fetch. The documented same-source prebuilt route then passed all seven real Gateway cases after the exact build succeeded. An interrupted diagnostic attempt remains interrupted; completed static phases are not relabeled as a completed test run.

### Runtime Gateway qualification — source 2557, reused unchanged

`defaultauto-landing3-warm-q1` binds signed **2557ac2d**, its exact build and common workload **178e6b14eb40c725396b838c8114dd85ced6dcce**. **300/300 probes are valid**; warmup and measured phases share PID **1035**. Each verifies **one actual prepared plan, four rendered results, four HTTP 200 maintenance requests and durable boundaries 18 → 19**. The outcome is degraded-quality fallback, not normal-quality summary success. Both original 47,184-row prefixes match their recorded bytes/SHA-256. All **71 raw files and two links** are unchanged, inspection copies removed and cleanup valid.

This is one source-bound qualification, **not matched performance acceptance**. All measured costs remain visible:

| Metric | Source-2557 qualifier |
| --- | ---: |
| Stream RPC median / p95 / p99 / max | 3.478 / 6.385 / 42.212 / **279.563 ms** |
| Maintenance-window RPC median / p95 / p99 / max | 3.500 / 14.560 / 180.152 / **279.563 ms** |
| Stream / full maximum sampler gap | 120 / **374 ms** |
| Stream / full Gateway process CPU | 23,176.989 / **99,603.749 ms** |
| Stream / full main-isolate CPU | 1,831.857 / 14,109.509 ms |
| Stream / full sampled maximum RSS | 2,631,634,944 / 2,631,634,944 bytes |
| Stream / full main heap | 510,138,232 / 545,380,976 bytes |
| Stream / full observed worker heap | 127,378,848 / 158,638,504 bytes |
| Stream / full worker large-JSON parse count | 81,882 / 194,371 |
| Stream / full worker large-JSON parsed bytes | 559,635,186 / **1,274,631,589** |
| Stream / full distinct observed worker IDs | 5 / 13 |
| Stream / full retained transport chunks / frames | 1 / 8; 2 / 16 |
| Stream / full retained transport bytes / events | 333,107 / 4; 666,244 / 8 |
| Whole-rig child CPU | 188,673.716 ms |

The stream brackets are immediate samples, 0 ms before and 60 ms after, without prorating. Full CPU includes startup/warmup and is last observed cumulative CPU per Gateway PID; unsampled shutdown tails remain unobserved. Process CPU already includes workers. Worker counters cover successful userland JSON strings of at least 1,024 UTF-16 units, not host parsing; overlapping tasks include overhang. Worker IDs are distinct observations, not simultaneous peaks. Full capture has two plans/eight renders including warmup; measured request count five includes its pressure request, not five maintenance requests.

<details>
<summary>Prior-source qualifications — retained separately, never pooled</summary>

`defaultauto-landing2-warm-q1` qualified signed 3ff / published 3f with 300 valid probes, same PID 1047, one plan/four renders/four maintenance requests and 18 → 19 degraded boundaries per phase. Both original prefixes matched; 69 raw files/two links were unchanged.

| Metric | Prior 3ff qualifier |
| --- | ---: |
| Stream RPC median / p95 / p99 / max | 5.485 / 8.092 / 56.596 / **314.547 ms** |
| Stream / full maximum sampler gap | 107 / **768 ms** |
| Stream / full Gateway process CPU | 23,569.405 / **106,636.022 ms** |
| Full sampled maximum RSS | 2,713,694,208 bytes |
| Full observed worker heap | 153,459,776 bytes |
| Full worker large-JSON parse count / bytes | 228,660 / **1,527,489,040** |
| Whole-rig child CPU | 201,379.135 ms |

Earlier exact-623 stream max 13.764 ms/full gap 407 ms and c58/77 max 71.683 ms/full gap 1,388 ms remain separate, each with 300 valid probes and the same degraded class/four maintenance requests. Every earlier CPU/RSS/parsing/failure cell, the 267/162 overlapping checks and all-19-file cost proof retain their original source scope. None is relabeled as current-source regression acceptance.

</details>

**Open:** exact-head CI/landing gates, formal paired cold/warm acceptance, live-provider follow-up, effective SDK window and per-worker/JIT warmth. No performance-win or no-regression conclusion is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Prospective acceptance protocol — draft, not an admitted cohort</summary>

Before acceptance, pin both production commits/build receipts, the signed controller, fixture, image and sampling manifests; freeze and read back the published rule. Previous diagnostics and qualifiers are ineligible.

Run five serial baseline/candidate cold pairs, then five separate process-warm pairs. Warm requires a distinct physical session to durably complete default maintenance in the same Gateway PID first; it does not establish per-worker/JIT warmth or global idle. Use unique immutable tags and stopped imports, auditing unchanged original prefixes, durable outcome class and maintenance request counts.

Keep all 300 scheduled slots and every error, timeout, suppression and cancellation. Retain full-stream and declared broad-window latency, sampler gaps, process/main CPU, RSS/heaps, parsing/transport and full-capture startup/warmup costs. No post-result window selection, outlier removal, replacement tags or diagnostic pooling.

Report n=5 per arm/population, median, nearest-rank p95, spread and paired rows. Incomplete capture or source/outcome mismatch stops the cohort with its prefix retained. A median/p95 metric worsening at least 20% stops before the next population. Every adverse cell remains visible; a worse user-facing metric needs explicit owner acceptance. Lower worst latency does not excuse higher CPU or memory.

No acceptance cohort has started under this draft. Qualification does not grant acceptance.

</details>

Requested by @RomneyDa; publication authorized by @vincentkoc. Human contributor credit retained in the signed series: @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc and @jalehman.

title: fix: mobile sidebar opens during content swipes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the mobile sidebar opens when users swipe right inside content, interrupting gestures such as orbiting a 3D object.

## User Impact

Users can swipe within content without opening navigation. To open the sidebar by gesture, start within 32 CSS pixels of the left content edge, after any device safe-area inset, and swipe right; the menu button remains available. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing drawer gesture owner now checks the touch's starting position before tracking it or preventing native behavior. Existing distance, direction, modal, input, horizontal-scrolling, and drawer lifecycle checks remain unchanged. This intentionally replaces anywhere-in-content opening with an edge gesture.

Requested by @jacobtomlinson, who reported the orbit-control conflict; co-authored with @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/08340be6-70c7-457e-956d-35acbe700c80)

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original content-gesture conflict and the review's landscape regression. With a 48px left safe-area inset, hit-tested touches starting at x=72 could not open the old PR's drawer; the new browser regression is red on that revision and green after the correction. An interior swipe from x=112 still leaves navigation closed.
- Eight focused runtime cases pass, including starts at 32 and 33 pixels without an inset, modal/connecting exclusions, and focus preservation.
- All seven native-navigation browser cases pass against the freshly built production UI: portrait/landscape edge opening, short/vertical gesture rejection, button/search access, native table scrolling, off-edge content drags, and the 48px safe-area case. A canvas with pointer capture and `touch-action: none` receives the complete 144px gesture and pointer-up without cancellation or opening the drawer.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, the changed docs' MDX check, and `git diff --check` pass. The browser lane's production UI build also passes.
- Fresh independent autoreview (Codex) of the complete safe-area repair snapshot against local commit `083870afaa47fda8c899229daa5d3896b54b1e62`, through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The only subsequent code change was a lint-only callback-parameter rename. Local ClawSweeper's existing checkout still has unrelated uncommitted files, so the documented autoreview fallback was used.
- Simplification: the existing gesture owner measures one content bound at touch-start; no new gesture state, safe-area parser, or component-specific exception. Whole-PR production delta +9/-3 lines; test delta +85/-11; docs +7/-1 against the original base.

### Review feedback addressed

Both findings in [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200033#issuecomment-6911638410) are addressed: **P2**, measure the opening strip after the safe-area inset and prove it with hit-tested input; **P3**, update the mobile navigation guide with the edge start, inset behavior, and **Expand sidebar** alternative.

Proof uses Chromium with synthetic Gateway responses and a representative canvas gesture surface, not the requester's custom 3D viewer or a physical iOS/Android browser. Broad hosted CI remains separate.

### Before / After

Rightward content swipes away from the screen edge, on a 393 × 852 CSS-pixel phone viewport (synthetic chat). Before: the drawer interrupts the content. After: the drawer remains closed. The canvas interaction is additionally covered by the browser assertions above.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: content swipe opens navigation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f45a998-24ae-4fa8-8e2d-a301adebcc5e) | ![After: content swipe stays in chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f605159c-83f7-490b-b266-b70c3a30f724) |

### Safe-area review correction

The same rightward swipe from x=72 on an 852 × 393 CSS-pixel landscape viewport with a 48px left inset: before, navigation remains unreachable; after, the drawer opens from the reachable content edge.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Safe-area before: eligible edge swipe cannot open navigation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d2fe06de-717c-4a9f-83cd-c0e35622e917) | ![Safe-area after: eligible edge swipe opens navigation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b65fd8c-51f1-4990-993d-05008f1b8b8b) |

title: fix(ci): restrict dependency approvals to admins and SecOps
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152415

## What Problem This Solves

Dependency changes can bypass restricted security review when a PR author or approval-command commenter has Maintain access but is neither a repository admin nor a SecOps member.

## User Impact

There is no product runtime change. Dependency changes requiring approval again require repository admin or active `@openclaw/openclaw-secops` authority, whether supplied by the author or by `/allow-dependencies-change`. Sensitive-product Maintain/Admin policy, removal-only exemptions, rollout behavior, dependency versions, and existing merge protections are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restores the dependency policy that preceded `b52d2f08f51840eb386b4829b20656b239d13bee` ("trust maintainer-authored dependency changes") and removes the dependency-command broadening from #152415 without reverting its unrelated sensitive-product review tier. The shared approval owner and native prior-CI clearance apply the same dependency-specific rule.

SecOps membership reuses the existing primary/fallback GitHub Apps with only organization Members-read permission, separate from the workflow token used for repository statuses and notices. No credentials, App grants, static approver roster, or public configuration were added. Membership-token failures are visible and fail closed; a review exceeding the App token lifetime can require a new evaluation.

## Evidence

- **Current head `230e0e8b5c7b799a95e78a0947c780b46201555f`: [CI run 43812786226 passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43812786226).** The native watcher reached `GREEN`. [Security Review 43814852203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43814852203) also published successful dependency, sensitive-product, and combined `openclaw/ci-gate` statuses. No failure exception or rerun-for-green was used.
- [Post-fix hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199985#issuecomment-6908356140) completed for this head at 05:56 UTC: **zero findings; previous P2 resolved**. Its remaining action is GitHub SecOps code-owner approval. CI was still running when that review was written and has since passed. This evidence-status update does not change source or product intent; no duplicate review was requested.
- Red/green production-entrypoint reproduction: a Maintain org-member author published dependency success on the base; the restored rule leaves approval pending. Coverage includes nonmember Maintain authors, Maintain commenters, admins, active/inactive SecOps, bots, and revision-command freshness.
- Initial focused proof: 353 guard/workflow tests passed (19.50 s command), plus 120 native prior-CI tests (88.83 s). The native suite exercises Git/CLI admission and retained outcomes, not just a helper predicate.
- [Initial CI run 43809715570](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43809715570) failed on two overlooked test consumers. ClawSweeper's P2 was accepted: the admission fixture lacked `membershipApi` and still expected Maintain dependency approval; a direct autoscrub fixture also lacked the membership reader. Commit `226a8f00d201b833ae86cf7ffbd54bfcef7b5c42` repairs only those fixtures, supplies nonmember responses, and uses admin approval. Freshness, revocation, refresh-command rejection, and transport assertions remain intact; production policy was not relaxed.
- Both affected suites pass after repair: 55 tests across the admission and dependency-guard suites; `pnpm test:ci-failed 199985 --run` passes (3.96 s command). Unchanged-contract proof is reused. CI job durations remain available in the linked runs.
- Focused lint, formatting, workflow actionlint/zizmor, docs MDX/link audit pass. Targeted typecheck, including the repaired admission suite, passes with Node 24-compatible `ES2024.Promise` declarations for existing `Promise.withResolvers` usage. The ES2023-only custom setup reports that existing library mismatch. No application build is needed for these trusted CI scripts.
- Independent Codex autoreview (GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P2: complete initial candidate against `270b338edea53c5fb8778d60e5ba7f68d36c31fd` and two-file repair against `e86df88f03ea67a2655e07b6591a03c39b2f8116` both had no actionable findings; the hosted review additionally caught the now-repaired omitted consumer.
- Existing Members-read App-token minting succeeded in [run 43808918001](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43808918001). The changed default-branch workflow cannot execute from this PR before landing; production-entrypoint fixtures and workflow checks cover its wiring and credential separation.
- Simplification: one shared predicate owns author and command authority. Added machinery is limited to credential separation and the native reader adapter; no cache or fallback policy. Production scripts remain +60/−23 lines and workflow +22 lines; post-review repair adds only 16/−2 test lines. GitHub SecOps code-owner approval remains mandatory; no auto-merge or bypass is enabled.

## Contributor credit

title: fix(release): contribution accounting fails for unavailable historical issues
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes release contribution accounting failing when a previously recorded issue becomes unavailable on GitHub, even though its closing PR and covered release work remain verifiable.

## User Impact

Release maintainers can explicitly supply an original historical snapshot and its SHA-256 digest to preserve supported reporter credit. Recovery remains opt-in and fails closed without the frozen contribution row, historical reciprocal relationship, matching current PR identity, and covered source. No migration is required.

Maintainers can select immutable initial-format notes with read-only `--source-ref`; working-tree behavior remains the default. Historical writes and source/output aliases—including missing files beneath symlinked directories—are rejected. Optional unavailable contributor accounts remain omitted rather than aborting otherwise valid accounting; verified credit is retained.

## Why This Change Was Made

Historical evidence is read separately from exact-range live caching. One recovery-aware resolution path preserves supported historical provenance without inventing live authorship or spreading reporter credit to unrelated PRs. Recovery requires the original merge or one unambiguous covered adaptation with exact title and source markers. The complete historical reciprocal relationship remains required even if the live closing edge disappears. Authentication, mixed errors, rate and transport failures remain fatal.

The existing release-changelog resolver resolves a selected source once and records its commit, paths and format. This supports final-tag proposals when local notes are missing or already a docs mirror, without copying notes or weakening initial-format, completeness or credit checks.

This PR changes collector tooling, its owning instructions, the shared source reader, tests and a justified allocation. It does not change release notes, releases, tags, assets or original historical snapshots. Separately captured accounting is a proposal, not approved counts or credits.

## Evidence

- Published repair head `047694a85236eb3a70a25e8504798db65c40fba5`, tree `91970a03c05a9ea0c4fe0d463229d575eebc0170`, matches implementation commit `803242fbbc9107d831cb24f650928f201fde9232`. Fresh exact-head CI is pending. Prior green CI does not qualify this candidate.
- Automated review of the prior baseline identified a real optional-user regression and missing incident citation. Both are repaired: only explicitly requested user aliases with exact one-component `NOT_FOUND` paths and null results are optional. Mixed errors, wrong paths and non-null conflicts stay fatal. The owning skill now cites this incident. This restores the original optional omission intent rather than making unverified users required.
- CLI missing-user proof: RED **1 failed / 3 passed**, then GREEN **4 passed**. Affected collector/resolver suites: **209 passed**, before a subsequent two-invocation fixture correction. Exact root-scripts and root-tooling graphs, targeted lint and formatting passed. Budget **+617**, allowance 400 plus documented 217-line allocation; no cases or assertions removed.

title: improve(sessions): archive inactive transcripts by default

## What Problem This Solves

Older inactive chat history stays in SQLite unless operators discover and enable cold storage.

## User Impact

Eligible inactive transcripts are now compressed automatically after 30 days, including on existing installations that omit this setting. Explicit `session.maintenance.coldStorage.enabled: false` still disables future extraction, and existing archives remain restorable. Active/admitted work and recovery-owned history remain protected.

Cold files are authoritative history: use supported backups or retain the referenced archive files with direct database copies. As before, text search excludes cold transcript contents until restoration. Retention and deletion policies are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler and extraction worker now share the cold-policy resolver, with defaults of enabled and 30 days. Settings reflects the same omitted-setting behavior instead of showing archival as off and disabling Run now. Help and current configuration docs describe the opt-out; no new configuration field or schema migration is introduced.

## Evidence

- [Before/after Settings screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199899#issuecomment-6905840130), using synthetic data with `coldStorage` omitted in both states. GitHub assets were read back and inspected, and delivered to the original discussion.

Explicit false hot-reloaded without restart; `chat.inject` restored exact original history before appending while extraction was disabled.
- Latest npm stable **2026.11.4 → candidate** passed **4/4** real upgrade scenarios: omitted policy adopts 30 days, explicit false remains off, custom 7-day age persists, and stable-generated cold archives restore. The stable tarball integrity was verified; released Doctor/Gateway created the database, then candidate Doctor/Gateway reopened the same isolated state. Original transcript rows remained byte-exact and history readable after restoration/appends. No live server state or external inference was used.

title: improve: make visual PR fixes easier to review
body:
Related: #174805

## What Problem This Solves

Visual PR evidence is scattered across several guides, and small technical annotation labels make it harder to see what changed and why it matters.

## User Impact

Reviewers get visible clean and annotated before/after comparisons for affected web, macOS, iOS, and Android UI. Agents choose the targets, plain-language labels, and colors appropriate to each screenshot; users do not need to mark screenshots.

The existing annotation tool now renders rounded, filled cards with optional supporting detail and a delta pill. App Store, Google Play, release assets, and their screenshot pipelines remain unchanged. No application UI or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the existing PR media guide the shared workflow and link the platform guides, contributing guide, and PR template to it. Reuse the current capture and annotation tools rather than add another framework.

Show clean comparisons first and annotated copies second, without collapsing either. Stack wide images when side-by-side would be unreadable. The shared renderer handles the selected card shape and derives coordinated colors from an agent-chosen accent; it does not guess the screenshot theme. Measurements remain optional supporting information, not the whole explanation.

Manual compaction preparation no longer requests writable copies of immutable transcript payloads merely to inspect them. Performance acceptance remains pending. This PR does not fix automatic warm-session compaction or all main-thread stalls. No configuration or migration is required.

Use the existing internal read-only branch accessor for synchronous manual preflight, instead of requesting writable copies immediately before context projection. All **four separately tagged real-Gateway qualifiers passed and were audited**: native compaction, physical-session 8192-byte continuity, matched two-request summary work, default limits, CPU brackets and cleanup.
- [ClawSweeper's review of the current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199840#issuecomment-6903144771) lists **no code findings** and requests the declared end-to-end performance evidence. That evidence is not yet complete.
- The original frozen twenty-slot comparison was **interrupted by a Gateway restart** after six native-valid cold observations (three pairs). The seventh slot was interrupted before measured compaction; thirteen slots were unattempted. Original receipts and all outcomes are retained unchanged. This is not a completed five-pair population, a warm comparison, or performance acceptance. The interrupted task container is stopped. No failed tag was replayed and no observations were pooled or relabeled.
- The earlier single profiled baseline remains exploratory only. Prior setup failures, the corrected invalid module-registry oracle and the receipt-shape admission refusal remain recorded separately.

### Prospective performance rule — published before comparison timing

Real manual compaction through isolated built Gateways, the same private long-session fixture, native import and same-physical-session 8192-byte follow-up. Compare exact base `9f0f89522a633826aa5c64483cca3bec3dacca34` against exact published head `54617a8c765a8672c1459da190ad08567e38bb0e`. Workload `f30da43971c6b210df2e89962d0af639bc04107e` preserves the five canonical rig/turn/mock/importer/observer files from `007777bbf9917bdc62a488b9e348990fc06c6a04`. Successful exact builds, fixture/workload/protocol hashes, native admission and the complete order are frozen before accepted runs. Qualification timings are excluded.

Five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs cold, then five pairs process-warm, without profiling. Report every outcome, median, nearest-rank p95 (=maximum at n=5), min/max and spread for compaction/follow-up latency, whole-process and independently sampled main-thread CPU, RPC/lifecycle RSS and heap, and main-thread pulse gaps. Include bracket overhang and host load; all native integrity and cleanup checks must pass. No selective reruns, pooling or outlier removal.

A win requires copying reduction and measurable real-flow improvement without worse user-facing metrics. After each complete five-pair population, a **20% or greater adverse median or p95 in any measured cell stops before another population**. Missing measurements block; zero-baseline/positive-candidate values stop. Smaller adverse cells remain visible and require explicit informed owner acceptance before landing. With no measurable gain, do not land as a performance improvement. Recovery must retain the interrupted original cohort and use separately declared fresh tags/bindings, never rewrite its receipts or silently combine populations.

<details>
<summary>Evidence reuse and measurement limits</summary>

The successful exact-base build is reused, not rebuilt. A separate audited schema supplement retains original install/build receipts and hashes. Whole-tree/dist fingerprints were observed at prior diagnostic admission/end and rechecked, not retroactively observed at build completion; that observation gap remains explicit. The candidate install/build binds the exact published head. Literal probe/install shell-child decoding preserves the actual recorded command without repeating the successful install.

The unchanged nominal 100 ms main-isolate sampler gives a coarse maximum adjacent gap over the inclusive RPC bracket, including overhang. It cannot resolve sub-100 ms blocking or replace other-session RPC latency. Process CPU/RSS include workers; worker-only zero counters do not mean zero main-thread parsing.

Process-warm manual compaction is not resident automatic compaction. Unrelated-session RPC probes occur after compaction, so concurrent responsiveness remains unproven. The fixture is one whole observed generation with fixed mock summaries, not a broad corpus or provider-quality test.

</details>

Projects the Android-owned built-in palettes into generated iOS tokens. One resolved appearance feeds native presentation and the embedded Dashboard's document-start/live appearance rather than keeping separate theme choices for each surface.
