title: improve(backup): use spare cores for gzip on larger hosts
body:
Related: #183094, #199367

## What Problem This Solves

Large, compression-bound backups cannot use more than four cores even when the host has spare CPU capacity.

## User Impact

User impact: backups on hosts with seven or more available cores can use dedicated compression workers, leaving file reads off the shared gzip queue. Hosts with six or fewer keep the existing path, and archives remain standard `.tar.gz` files. More workers use additional peak memory and can use slightly more CPU; the measured tradeoff is shown below. No compression-level, integrity-check, format, configuration or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the dedicated-worker follow-up left by merged #199367, not a duplicate of its four-way libuv implementation. Above six cores, the existing worker pool compresses ordered 4 MiB members with `min(8, cores - 2)` workers. Owned buffers transfer to/from workers without detaching caller data; the existing stream retains bounded read-ahead, ordered errors and settlement, and closes its pool on success, failure or cancellation.

The worker is registered inline in the existing runtime manifest. Fixed-root POSIX relative paths replace manual prefix slicing, while one typed construction replaces three intermediate standalone namespace projections. Literal entry tuples retain the original inferred descriptor contracts rather than falling back to `any`. This keeps the existing manifest within its real 700-counted-line cap without a new manifest helper, copy dependency, cap exception or workflow mutation.

## Evidence

### Current integrated candidate

- Published head: `ef1ab2f699c6ecad14e00748380e118f6f7eb111`; source tree: `c4091ae96325fa61cedd4f9b8d4c9214f82232dc`.
- Integrated main `c531fd0b1339f53ec9530dfd5fed312944680a66` to resolve a real runtime-manifest conflict. The repair preserves main's worker-loader entry and helper parameter, alongside this PR's gzip registration and POSIX worker-name derivation. Original contributor ancestry is retained.
- Canonical independent Auto Review over the complete integrated candidate, **P0–P3**: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. An initial report's test concern was rejected against the existing explicit concurrency-2 failure test; the post-integration pass confirmed it.
- **55 focused tests passed** across gzip workers, gzip ordering, archive-stream cleanup, runtime worker URLs, benchmark instrumentation and standalone source entries. Real worker startup/exit failures, cancellation, bounded reads and caller-buffer ownership are covered.
- Targeted manifest types, lint, format and diff checks pass. All 123 current runtime descriptors preserve their expected worker names, including the new gzip worker and main's loader entry.
- The official source-run build passes. With isolated home/config/state, real `pnpm openclaw backup create --only-config --verify` exits successfully and reports `verified: true`; stock `gzip -t` accepts the archive. The built gzip worker is present at `dist/infra/backup-gzip.worker.js`.
- Current-head [CI attempt 2 passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44182271660/attempts/2), including [check-lint-core-5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44182271660/job/134417895584), the [selected-lane CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44182271660/job/134421284244), and the [combined CI/security gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44191381383). Dependency and security-sensitive review statuses also pass. The original attempt's lint lane exceeded its 15-minute job budget, with no job log available even in the full run archive. The reconstructed actual lint workload passed locally in 76.8 seconds; one authorized job-only retry then passed on GitHub in 5m57s. Existing successful checks were reused. No source, lint rule, timeout, workflow, dependency or gate exception was changed, and the original timeout's cause remains unestablished.
- [ClawSweeper re-reviewed this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199712#issuecomment-6899116741) and reported no actionable findings or before-merge items. This does not waive CI or human review requirements.
- Prior-head CI and package/performance evidence below are retained with their original source binding, not presented as current-head CI. No new compiled-standalone executable or comparative benchmark run is claimed.

### Prior-head correctness and packaging evidence

The following evidence belongs to original head `7755559c8a797ce40ff9b0b8be9b8b7c592c6ac7`: 98 focused cases passed, with real Node/Bun packaged success and worker-failure handling. That ten-file candidate passed targeted types, lint/format, strict 700-line checks, both Knip scans and P0–P2 review. Full details and limits follow.

Prior-head [full selected-lane CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43744983895/job/132913452687), with all 15 selected groups successful and no known-main-red exception; the security/dependency guard also passed. ClawSweeper's earlier review of that head reported no findings; the linked review comment now contains the newer integrated-head review. This is not human approval or merge authorization.

<details>
<summary>Source-bound correctness and packaging details</summary>

- Selected base: `5dbf569b4b8552253c37fac93b32bdaf87a872dc`; tested/reviewed source tree: `7835128e1bcd9ba543b64786d5dd3e643eb92842` (10 files).
- Fresh focused suites: **98 cases passed**, covering real worker count/order/buffer ownership, fallback, bounded reads, abort/error/native exit settlement, worker-host behavior, runtime resolution, archive stream cleanup, verified restore/database readability, compiled-worker fixtures and native dependency-free harnesses. The existing standalone-source suite now also guards against an `any` return-type regression.
- Canonical typechecker assertions prove exact old factory/plugin/standalone return signatures after excluding the new gzip property, bidirectional projection compatibility and no newly introduced `any`. Core production, infra tests and root-script test types pass.
- All **119 baseline descriptors and their order** remain identical. Across 45 plugin-directory selections at two module URLs, all 90 ordered standalone projections and 338 plugin-value reference identities match the baseline. The actual build-entry owner discovers the new worker.
- Strict native max-lines check at **700**: no diagnostic. Ordinary targeted lint/format, line-cap and suppression/environment ratchets, and both Knip scans pass without exemptions. Existing CI and wrapper definitions are byte-identical to the selected base; copied native closures load all 120 descriptors without any storage helper.
- Current generator regenerated runtime script assets and `--check` passes; both previously affected generated bundles are now byte-identical to the base, not hand-edited or copied from the archive.
- Fresh `qaRuntime` build and canonical runtime-only package integrity/import-graph check pass. Package SHA-256: `5d6849a2d0715e8fcaa14878141145082fd63840d4f6f101980406556435a0c9`.
- The actual extracted package runs `backup create --verify` successfully over a disposable 256 MiB workspace under Node 24.20.0 and pinned OpenClaw Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`; stock `gzip -t` accepts both archives. Removing the extracted worker or replacing it with native exit 23 makes **both runtimes exit 1 without publishing an archive**.
- Fresh full-candidate independent Auto Review: OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, **P0–P2**, `scoped-clean`, no findings, against the exact base/tree above. This was static review, not independent execution or human approval.

</details>

### Prior package CLI performance

Same revised package, Node 24.20.0/Linux, identical eight-core affinity, cold CLI processes and warm filesystem cache. A fresh committed `backup-verify-fixture.mjs <state> <workspace> --workspace-only` workload supplies 12,288 files / 768 MiB; no database inflation. One warmup per path, then five serial interleaved pairs. The committed measurement script constrains only the existing path to `BACKUP_MEASURE_GZIP_CONCURRENCY=4`; default selects six dedicated workers.

Acceptance rule recorded before the run: reduce archive-write median with every archive verified; report whole wall, CPU, RSS, size and host load separately. Additional memory is a visible tradeoff, not a free or universal speedup. No own heavy validation/build ran concurrently with the measured pairs.

| Metric | Four-way libuv | Six dedicated workers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Archive write median / p95 | 7.893 / 7.936 s | 6.925 / 6.995 s |
| Whole command median / p95 | 9.830 / 9.873 s | 8.861 / 8.921 s |
| Whole CPU median | 24.213 s | 24.613 s |
| Maximum process peak RSS median | 0.635 GiB | 0.781 GiB |
| Archive bytes median | 808,436,923 | 808,436,841 |

All ten measured archives verified. One-minute load during measured archive phases: 2.49–3.94. Archive medians improved 12.3% and whole-command medians 9.9% on this particular file-heavy workload; do not extrapolate a universal 2x gain.

The instrumenter measures real CLI phase boundaries, follows emitted parameter names and includes peak RSS; whole wall includes the launcher, CPU sums CLI/launcher totals, and RSS is the maximum process peak. title: improve(ui): highlight skill references in the composer
body:
Related: #152599 (inline `$skill` references; standalone slash commands are unchanged). Builds on #192242.

## What Problem This Solves

Selected skills remain raw `$command_name` text in the composer, making them harder to distinguish from surrounding prose and person mentions.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session show known skill references as highlighted, atomic names with the existing skill icon and no visible `$`. Copying and sending preserve the canonical reference. No configuration or migration is required.

**Still draft; not performance-qualified for shipping.** The repeated scanning and premature editor-loading defects are repaired, and both hosted correctness findings are fixed. The startup asset gate still fails by **448 bytes**. First skill use and skill-only rich editing still cost substantially more than native text; several New Session p95 cells remain higher. These limits are not waived by this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the generic native-first editor and extension contract from the final merged #192242, rather than introduce another editor, overlay or dependency. Skills use the existing command catalog and share atomic boundary editing with people. Display labels no longer grant reference identity: only canonical commands and normalized command identifiers are recognized. Unknown references, shell variables, escaped dollars and code remain literal.

Ordinary edits map existing skill decorations instead of rescanning the draft. Token/Markdown-sensitive edits still use the canonical parser; image-bearing drafts deliberately retain full parsing. Atomic editing checks only affected chip boundaries and does not serialize large pastes for single-character separator checks. Literal dollars may load the small parser, but cannot fetch CodeMirror until a reference is admitted. Catalog replacement explicitly refreshes labels/removals and admits unchanged restored drafts; subscriptions end with their native/editor owners. Native undo snapshots, asynchronous handoff, IME boundaries and retired-frame guards are preserved. Skill integration still composes through the mention adapter, not a new feature framework.

## Evidence

### Current repair and review — November 16

Published head `0283e5b68266ebb706dab8a9d74623406693488e` has exactly the tested product tree of implementation `ec4b449ebd8e2e0e468f10da9fec32b8ec9b789b` (`37b3739503d08c1fbe431ff51ae1ba6af24bcb99`); the publisher's final commit is attribution-only.

- **218 browser tests passed in 13 files**, including person/skill editor consumers, native handoff, undo, paste/drop, composition simulation, ref disposal, catalog/command consumers, overflow, height and mobile fixtures. UI and script typechecks, scoped lint/format, controller guard and whitespace checks passed.
- **Both source-server real-UI Chat/New Session flows passed** with a synthetic Gateway. The new network assertion first failed on both routes: `$HOME`/`$unknown` fetched the rich editor. It now passes while actual skill selection and canonical submission still work.
- Both hosted P2 findings on `6d45233` were reproduced red and repaired: display-name aliases could look selected without resolving on submission; unchanged drafts did not react to catalog arrival/rename/removal. The catalog regression verifies stable editor identity, raw text and selection.
- Independent local **autoreview through P2 was scoped-clean** for the final staged repair against `6d45233`, subsequently committed as `ec4b449`. It included the generic editor, mention adapter, import lifecycle, catalog owner, Gateway reference-resolution contract and Markdown parser as context. Static review is not runtime proof. Earlier reviewer findings for indentation, adjacent backticks, native history and literal-dollar loading were repaired; the staged-only loading finding disappeared when the reviewed working-tree fix was committed.
- **900 valid repair timing observations** were collected across explicit source stages: 390 at `08ec3b39`, 270 at `452d63a5`, then **240 on the final product tree**. Completed interrupted work was retained rather than replayed; one restart interruption in the first stage is excluded from valid observations. Earlier-stage measurements are not relabeled as final-head proof.
- Final separate diagnostics found **zero full-draft skill scans for twelve unrelated keys** in both Chat and New Session, down from twelve on the original feature. Ten people/eight skill chips and exact raw text survived; one editor remained mounted and stylesheet rules did not grow during typing. A final bounded 21-round-trip session lifecycle replay also passed on baseline and candidate; this is not a universal no-leak claim.

### Acceptance rule — unchanged

Baseline `491c2944f56ad7d6d9a561a17dfffcd42cab49e3` already contains the final merged mention foundation. Compare same-toolchain production builds with at least ten serial rotating baseline/candidate/identical-baseline rounds. Report median, p95, ranges and host load; keep traced diagnostics separate. Require no correctness loss, unexpected RPCs, per-key remounts/owner-echo transactions or unbounded resource growth. Median regression must be at most 5% with no worse p95; unresolved tails need confirmation. A confirmed move above 20% blocks blanket performance acceptance. Existing asset limits remain unchanged. Mock-renderer, live-Gateway and native-device evidence remain separate.

### Final production-build timings

Chromium `156.0.8078.4`, Linux x64, real production UI with a synthetic Gateway. These are **renderer main-thread CPU milliseconds per action**, not per-key latency, INP, total process CPU or live-provider latency. Long typing is twelve trusted characters in a 64 KiB draft; mixed drafts contain ten people/eight skills. Paste is 256 KiB synthetic clipboard input. Catalog size is 200. Each row has ten observations per variant; each cell is **median / p95**. A/A is an identical baseline.

| Flow | Baseline | Final candidate | A/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat person-only long | 55.567 / 60.265 | 55.551 / 60.269 | 56.480 / 59.302 |
| Chat mixed long | 52.028 / 58.309 | 54.160 / 57.572 | 54.125 / 56.980 |
| Chat literal dollars | 38.862 / 43.498 | 39.343 / 42.133 | 38.111 / 45.286 |
| New Session person-only long | 52.058 / 54.542 | 53.371 / 58.238 | 53.519 / 57.152 |
| New Session mixed long | 45.783 / 50.206 | 46.555 / 55.102 | 46.154 / 49.780 |
| New Session mixed paste | 23.195 / 25.057 | 23.746 / 26.502 | 22.933 / 25.102 |
| Chat first skill, including first dollar | 47.118 / 52.273 | 87.230 / 91.677 | 48.570 / 52.067 |
| New Session first skill, including first dollar | 45.679 / 49.449 | 74.020 / 81.182 | 44.615 / 48.706 |

The original mixed-typing median regressions were +8.39% Chat and +8.97% New Session. Final mixed medians are +4.10% and +1.69% versus baseline, and +0.06% and +0.87% versus A/A. This supports removal of the measured hot-path waste, not universal parity: New Session person/mixed/paste p95 are still +6.78%, +9.75% and +5.77% versus baseline. The complete acceptance rule therefore remains unmet.

**First-use work is not hidden in preparation.** New `first-skill` workloads start from an untouched native draft and include the first dollar, catalog readiness, typing the query, selecting the skill and settling imports. Older `activate-skill` rows measured selection after typing the query; they are selection-only evidence, not cold first-use parity. Native-to-rich first-use cost remains approximately +40.1 ms in Chat and +28.3 ms in New Session. At the earlier `08ec3b39` stage, short skill-only typing was 20.170 → 36.529 ms and 200 occurrences were 64.712 → 127.286 ms. Those are native-versus-rich feature costs, not all attributable to parsing, and are not waived or claimed as final-head measurements.

Final CPU ranges: Chat mixed baseline 49.655–58.309 / candidate 51.451–57.572 ms; New Session mixed baseline 45.098–50.206 / candidate 44.695–55.102 ms; Chat first-skill baseline 46.277–52.273 / candidate 85.950–91.677 ms; New Session first-skill baseline 43.821–49.449 / candidate 70.785–81.182 ms. Final host load ranged 1.95–6.04 on 128 logical CPUs. Complete distributions and per-run manifests remain in the linked task under `catalog-final-summary.txt`, `catalog-final.log.summary.json`, and raw observations. No outliers were removed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, prior evidence and scope</summary>

The committed workload extends `scripts/lib/control-ui-chat-composer-scenarios.ts`, using the existing engine runner. With matched baseline and candidate builds:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui \
  --control-bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --compare-source-root . \
  --control-source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --engines chromium --viewport desktop --pairs 10 \
  --steps composer-qualification-chat-first-skill,composer-qualification-new-first-skill,composer-qualification-chat-literal-dollar,composer-qualification-chat-person-long,composer-qualification-chat-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-person-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-paste \
  --output .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/rerun
```

Earlier qualification of `6d45233` retained 510 editing/activation and 62 startup observations, 157 browser cases, eight emulated narrow/dark observations, four scan diagnostics, profiles and bounded retention. Its boot CPU and heap results are historical evidence, not a fresh final-head certification. Earlier repairs retained their own exact-source summaries; only the final table above qualifies the current product tree.

The simplify pass preserves the existing foreign-DOM owner and CodeMirror extension contract. No dependency, editor, overlay, global cache, custom Markdown parser or permission change was added. Necessary growth covers the skill feature, selective invalidation, native history and catalog notification/disposal. Versus `491c2944`, production UI is +714/−263 lines, tests +488/−19, and benchmark code +359/−1. Net test growth is 469 lines; the documented per-change allocation is 69 beyond the standard 400 for reproduced handoff, Markdown, lazy-loading and catalog/identity failures. Startup/performance limits were not raised.

</details>

### Startup asset gate — still failed

Final normalized largest-JS gzip is **569,985 → 570,497 bytes (+512)**. The inherited-over-cap differential permits only 64 bytes: **448 bytes remain over the allowed increase**. Original feature growth was +676 bytes; this repair does not claim the remaining failure is harmless. Chat/New boot gzip grows 539/486 bytes; request counts remain 21/17. CSS bytes and request counts are unchanged. The boot manifest was regenerated without a source diff. No unrelated byte-offset changes or budget increases were used.

Reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --dist dist/control-ui --base-dist .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui --json`. The strict comparison exits 1. Inherited absolute CSS/request overages are distinguished from this new differential failure.

### Remaining limits

This is a verified repair update to a draft, not a shipping or zero-regression claim. Startup size, native-to-rich feature cost and remaining p95 regressions are unresolved. WebKit/Firefox could not load the app under the environment's proxy policy on either build; no bypass was attempted. Native OS IME, mobile Safari, real-device/network and live Gateway/provider performance remain unqualified. Composition browser tests simulate events, not a physical input method. No merge or deployment occurred.

The existing inspected visual evidence is retained; this repair changes computation and correctness, not the chip design. Captures use the real UI with a synthetic Gateway; mobile is an emulated 390px viewport.

title: fix: iPad hardware Enter adds newlines instead of sending
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157111

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pressing Enter on an iPad Magic Keyboard adds a newline instead of sending a message, even when Enter is the selected send shortcut.

## User Impact

Recognized iPad/iPhone hardware Enter follows the existing desktop send preference. Shift+Enter, input-method confirmation, and mobile software Return remain editing actions; Android behavior is unchanged. No settings migration is required.

Physical-key identification is best effort: missing or unknown key codes keep Return native. Native iPad/Magic Keyboard and on-screen-keyboard event identity have not been device-tested; browser emulation does not establish that compatibility.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared mobile Return policy blocked every Enter on iOS, regardless of its physical key code. Admit recognized Enter/NumpadEnter events per keypress rather than latching keyboard-attached state or using touch/viewport heuristics. Reuse the existing IME guard in loaded and loading command palettes so newly reachable hardware shortcuts cannot send an IME-confirming Enter.

Thanks @jacobtomlinson for reporting the problem and specifying the expected keyboard behavior.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ba5a6831-192b-4dd2-bcc0-77f1a3608990)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a8f9331e-d05f-4b4a-a7fa-6649aa633038)

## Evidence

- Actual source Control UI at 1194×834 with synthetic content and simulated desktop-mode iPad identity: before, physical Enter inserted a newline and produced zero `chat.send` requests; after, it cleared the draft and produced exactly one request. Matching before/after screenshots are below. The private report screenshot is not included.
- Hardware-Enter regressions failed on the original policy. Fixed coverage exercises Chat, New session, and Side chat, both shortcut preferences, Shift+Enter, active IME flags, and later software Return. Chromium: 40 cases passed across mobile composer and settings files (3.49 s clean run).
- Palette/loader suites: 93 cases passed (4.32 s), including post-composition iPad hardware Return; platform, chat IME, and queue checks also passed. UI typecheck, formatting, i18n baseline verification, and `git diff --check` passed. Targeted lint: zero errors; one warning on an unchanged palette ref callback.
- WebKit browser lane timed out establishing a session before executing tests. This is an uncovered browser proof gap, not a passing Safari result. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43737845001) at `38006f3c21037b5fe9d0e36bcbae862f1a875c03`; per-file CI seconds are not available.
- Independent autoreview: Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium reasoning, P0–P2, full final local candidate against base `21960ae268b41a8f603a80d0edc1cc6c4644ec56`, committed unchanged as `567b848f9d21c99730547a160489f802f5a2ca6f`. Initial review found missing palette post-composition protection; it was repaired and regression-tested. Final review: `scoped-clean`, patch correct, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The publisher added tree-identical metadata commit `fc1d32e4e26836996c63f05ce03ecc3f2ef34f2f` on top; there is no code delta from the reviewed tree. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. [Hosted ClawSweeper reviewed the current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199681#issuecomment-6898171790) with no actionable findings; its native-device proof limitation remains open.
- CI follow-up: [the original exact-head test-types job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43736553649/job/132881596493) exposed TS2322 in the new cleanup hook. Reproduced with `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-chat.json`; changing the callback to a block returns void without casts or assertion changes. That exact graph now passes, all 22 mobile browser cases pass (2.79 s), and targeted lint/format/diff checks pass. Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete repair delta against `fc1d32e4e26836996c63f05ce03ecc3f2ef34f2f`: P0–P2 `scoped-clean`, patch correct. No production behavior changed; new-head CI remains separate proof.
- Simplification: one existing Return-policy owner, no new platform detector or sticky state, and shared palette input owns composition timestamps. Production delta: +14 lines; tests: +140 lines. Growth preserves newly reachable IME behavior; no new imperative listeners or effects.

### Behavioral video — published head 38006f3c21037b5fe9d0e36bcbae862f1a875c03

The 32.76-second recording drives the actual running Control UI source, not a recreated screen. It uses synthetic Gateway data, a 1194×834 Chromium iPad-profile viewport, and an external caption band so narration never covers the composer.

title: fix: keep iPad keyboard accessory clear of composer actions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Safari’s floating keyboard accessory can cover Send when using OpenClaw on an iPad with a hardware keyboard.

## User Impact

User impact: iPad composer actions reserve one Send-button width at the physical right edge without shifting when focus changes: **32px expanded / 36px compact**. Mac, Windows touch devices, and iPhone retain existing spacing.

This space remains reserved on iPad without a hardware keyboard. Native Safari accessory behavior still needs real-device confirmation; automation proves application geometry, not the native overlay. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing startup iOS classifier, excluding iPhone/iPod, rather than introduce a new platform export. The responsive Send-size token supplies stable physical-right clearance to the shared composer layouts, including RTL. The compact surface owns its padding because its footer uses display: contents.

The branch reconciles main’s existing ACK and confirmed-handoff fixes rather than duplicate them. Focused fixture corrections retain their behavioral assertions and timing caps. An import-only prerequisite also repairs a stale upstream reference after the existing path helper moved to its canonical module; the same function is called, with no credential or authorization behavior change.

## Evidence

- **Qualification follow-up:** native-paste duplication was found while qualifying this PR and noted for follow-up in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/200182. The concrete stale-recovery lifecycle bug is **already fixed** by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199534 (merge 99eb4aa8ce76a5e6d47ac6f5d672499fcb10cf4f), included through main. No duplicate paste repair is added here; the issue retains public proof and the unresolved historical CI-causality question.

The reviewer assessed supplied code/evidence, not independent test execution or physical-iPad behavior.

Geometry covers both iPad identities, desktop/phone negatives, LTR/RTL, focus stability and sending. Measured Send width / total physical-right gap: **32px / 39px** expanded, **36px / 45px** compact. The agent flow uses an isolated real Gateway and scripted loopback model; it is not external-provider live proof.

Targeted lint, UI types, formatting, documentation MDX/internal links and diff checks pass. The stale-import declaration failure was reproduced before the import correction and passes afterward.
- **Readiness without weakening assertions:** the picker and cached-Details fixtures await real module prerequisites before their original interaction checks. Side Chat joins actual element registration only after revealing the lazy panel; its hidden-state and catalog assertions remain. The Slack display proof uses the existing compiled bundled-plugin output instead of source compilation inside its unchanged 30s history RPC. title: improve(backup): avoid a repeated SQLite capture read
body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

SQLite backup capture performs a second full hash read before the archive writer reads the same image again.

## User Impact

Backups avoid that redundant capture read while checking the digest and length of the bytes actually archived. Changed or incomplete deferred images fail before archive publication. No configuration or archive-format migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only backup capture opts into deferral, and only hard-link-only publication qualifies. The archive reader compares exactly what it emits; unread or filtered images receive a full comparison before publication. Retries clear previous verification, and deferred alias copies retain their own checks so pre-copy verification cannot hide mutation during copying.

Copied publication, replacement, after-publication callbacks, and callers that do not opt in retain their existing comparison. The legacy-audit retry and publication preconditions move to sibling modules to meet the line budget. Simplification retained one verification obligation per image; production changes are +105 net lines, tests +343.

## Evidence

- **Current focused proof:** eight files / 87 tests passed, covering archive-time mutation, digest and emitted length, filtering, interrupted-attempt cleanup, alias copying, transfer/replacement, legacy audit, and CoW. Targeted `core`, `core-test-infra`, and `core-test-state-logging` typechecks, lint on 11 files, format, whitespace, and the line/assertion/mock ratchets passed.
- **Regression proof:** on exact base `5dbf569b4b8552253c37fac93b32bdaf87a872dc`, five mutation cases incorrectly publish archives; all five pass with this patch. The reconstructed candidate matches the worker patch byte-for-byte (SHA-256 `f916cd8d1eebc39019cf90a654cb6f7133ed9fe855f92dc81e9ea34c9f17aa1e`).
- **Build and real CLI:** `qaRuntime` build passed with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2` after the default thread pool exhausted sandbox resources. A supported Node-runtime CLI `backup create --verify` and restore passed on isolated synthetic SQLite state; restored `quick_check` was `ok` and its one 1 MiB row matched.
- **Independent review:** native Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, GPT-6.1 Sol), complete local candidate against the exact base above, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no findings. Reviewed tree: `5eecc275c025eaeb881c329bdb4c2ff71f78b524`.
- **Non-benchmark diagnostic:** five interleaved default/deferred captures of a 1,056,768-byte image measured 2,113,536 versus 1,056,768 capture-hasher bytes; both archived 1,056,768 bytes, and all deferred archive comparisons passed. This demonstrates the removed capture read, not an end-to-end speed claim. Archived CPU/wall benchmark numbers were not rerun and are not claimed here.

- **Author-side CI repair (`e31bec0ff5002ec5a5c30f747a9bdddc80c8f27b`):** added `sqlite-snapshot-preconditions.ts` to the native PR wrapper extraction inventory. The original small-2 closure assertion reproduced locally on `7451525f84de859321521008df0b56f77549bd5b`; after the repair, both wrapper-closure and eager-import-closure suites pass (24 tests), including actual extracted dependency/lease consumers. Incremental independent Auto Review, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no findings. The capture implementation is unchanged, so its existing build, CLI, behavioral and type/lint proof remains applicable. Current candidate tree: `f3dc04266a3a81e6d552c1dbe79b4f4589006e23`.

The initial large-10 private-provisioner injection failure remains under causal investigation; no baseline classification is claimed.

**Gaps:** the default Bun CLI smoke stopped at SQLite header-probe discovery before capture; the supported Node CLI completed on the same fixture. That Bun CLI boundary remains unqualified by this run. CoW tests pass 6/6 on both exact base and candidate on Linux, but this host cannot reproduce or clear the three archived APFS clone-ID failures. Broader platform proof remains with CI.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session action buttons crowd titles out of the sidebar on touch tablets, especially when sessions have nested children.

## User Impact

Touch users can read more of each session title while retaining a 44×44 menu target for pin, archive, and other session actions. Mouse/trackpad users with a fine primary pointer keep their direct hover actions. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The touch layout reserved up to 136px for three management buttons inside an already narrow sidebar. Reuse the existing session menu instead, reserving 48px for a single control; keep disclosure controls and PR metadata in their existing places. Phone drawer overrides remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the unmodified production UI at 1024×1366 with touch emulation and a 320px sidebar: the top-level title had only 55px of width. The new regression failed on that geometry; the fine-pointer control passed.
- Both tablet regression cases pass on the fix. They cover two nested levels, non-overlapping 44px menu targets, keyboard Enter/Escape, touch menu access, and an archive request through the nested-session confirmation.
- All 11 existing sibling scenarios passed in the full-file run, including phone drawers, roster mode, two-line titles, fine-pointer hover/focus, and hovering coarse pointers. That run also exposed a missing archive-confirmation step in the new test; the final tablet rerun includes that step. Exact-head hosted CI has now passed.

- Initial independent autoreview through Codex (GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P3, reviewed the complete local snapshot against `21960ae268b41a8f603a80d0edc1cc6c4644ec56`, with the unchanged row renderer, catalog, roster, phone, and layout owners supplied. The local ClawSweeper runner was unavailable because its checkout is dirty; hosted ClawSweeper subsequently reviewed the current head with no findings ([review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199672#issuecomment-6898025540)); no duplicate request was posted.

title: fix(backup): release disk space when deleting staging databases
body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw backup create` retains the disk space of deleted SQLite staging, snapshot, and verification copies until the process exits.

## User Impact

User impact: temporary disk space is released when backup removes each private database copy, instead of remaining pinned through the rest of a long backup. Archive format, integrity checks, source databases, and retention policy are unchanged; no migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

SQLite admission deliberately retains an identity descriptor after the last connection closes. Backup must retire that admission while the private file still exists, after its connections have closed and before unlinking it. This change does that for the online-copy staging file and recursively for backup/verification scratch under the existing exclusive lifetime token. Root token controls stay with their existing owner until its connection closes; nested payload files with the same basename are still retired.

The existing exclusive-copy implementation moves unchanged into its own module to keep the edited snapshot module within the repository's line cap. There is no new lifecycle owner or compatibility path. Simplification: the existing retirement owner handles cleanup; production delta is +37 net lines including the mechanical extraction, with 96 focused regression-test lines.

## Evidence

Current validation against refreshed main `5dbf569b4b8552253c37fac93b32bdaf87a872dc`:

- Red-before-green: the two new descriptor regressions failed on the unmodified production base, observing 1 deleted-open staging file and 2 deleted-open snapshot/verification files. Both pass with the repair.
- Strengthened scratch coverage includes a nested `payload/owner.sqlite` and proves a real competing SQLite reclaimer remains locked out at payload removal while the root control remains present.
- Focused scratch suites: 18 passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Snapshot plus final descriptor regressions: 50 passed, 2 Windows-only cases skipped.
- Backup creation/verification consumers, including real create/verify/restore flows: 103 passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped.
- Core production typecheck, infra-test typecheck, targeted four-file lint/format, line-cap ratchet, database-worker ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. The SQLite worker ratchet remains 166 live / 15 deprecated-only calls on both sides.
- Independent Auto Review, OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, complete local candidate against the base above: no findings, `scoped-clean`. Changed owners and unchanged admission/walk/publication cleanup context were included. The review adapter refused the unchanged staging-token source as a sensitive filename; its internals were not independently inspected by that reviewer. Existing native custody regression and the new competing-reclaimer proof pass.

### CI follow-up

The first head (`55ce9b412fcd1be586d46d49ce386bfbd86910a3`) exposed a real runtime-source inventory omission: extracted trusted PR wrappers did not include the newly split copy helper. Commit `0d34aa30c3960a88827c0a5ab43edf41e33a47cc` adds that one module to `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`; no tests or guard contracts were weakened. The source-closure test was reproduced red locally, then the repaired eager-import/source-closure suites passed all 24 cases. Independent Auto Review of this one-line fix against that head is `scoped-clean` (P0–P2). `git diff --check` passes; the text inventory has no applicable formatter target.

Original CI evidence: [small-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43733126387/job/132870195581) reported the missing inventory entry and missing-module errors. [large-10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43733126387/job/132870195518) reported 17 private-provisioner injection failures under pinned Bun. Both are now passing on current head: [small-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43734997698/job/132876170191) and [large-10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43734997698/job/132876170192), with the latter logging all 17 provisioning cases passed (2 platform skips). These public job reads are bounded tails, not complete logs.

The provisioning failure is also causally qualified, not dismissed as baseline: a disposable copy made through the existing wrapper fixture ran the real private preload under pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` (Node child `24.20.0`). With the extracted helper absent, the preload fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and reproduces the exact `not every launched provisioner received its private store` assertion. Restoring that one module produces the real injection and preflight-store receipts; the deliberately argument-free provisioner then reaches its usage check. The preload imports the handoff lease, whose transitive chain reaches `sqlite-snapshot.ts` before recording injection. This explains both original failed lanes with the same inventory omission. No guard, fixture, or unrelated provisioning source was changed. The earlier local operation-lock failure is retained as a separate setup limitation, not baseline attribution. The repository failed-CI collector is unavailable here (`spawn gh ENOENT`); focused repository runners and public job evidence were used.

### Current-head built CLI proof

A fresh repository-owned `qaRuntime` build completed successfully in 56.4 seconds. Its dirty managed projection was source-compared to published head `0d34aa30c3960a88827c0a5ab43edf41e33a47cc` before and after execution; the build stamp records input signature `f2c3a4d2f7b8926d48b70617714316983a03fc012ce5b267ea97187c93e35d91` rather than pretending the projection's older Git HEAD is the published head.

The actual built CLI ran `backup create --verify --json --no-include-workspace` against baseline-initialized disposable state, including a 17.5 MB synthetic agent database with 16 MiB of benchmark payload. All five SQLite copies (19,017,728 output bytes total) completed; the 133,169-byte archive verified and the command exited 0. A passive preload sampled actual OS descriptors and inspected them at the CLI's verified-result write, before CLI finalization; it did not replace backup, SQLite, or cleanup operations or hold the process open:

```json
{"stage":"verified-result-before-cli-finalization","runtime":{"node":"24.20.0","bun":null},"samples":458,"maxOpenScratchDescriptors":10,"maxDeletedScratchDescriptors":0,"openScratchDescriptors":0,"deletedScratchDescriptors":0,"deletedScratchBytes":0,"archiveVerified":true,"archiveBytes":133169}
```

This is current shipped-entry-point behavior, not a mock harness or a Bun claim. The compatible Node 24.20.0 runtime emitted its normal security-patch warning; this proof does not qualify TLS or replace the recommended Node patch level. Sampling cannot establish that no shorter-lived descriptor ever existed; the final live-process observation establishes that no scratch descriptor remained at successful completion.

Limits: this Linux run does not repeat the contributor's historical macOS/APFS 945 MB disk-footprint/timing benchmark, nor claim those historical numbers as current proof. Descriptor checks use `/dev/fd` and are skipped on Windows. Broad cross-platform coverage remains with PR CI. No model/Gateway workflow is changed.

Contributor credit: original patch and investigation by Mitchell Etzel; scoped repair, additional coverage, and current validation performed with RoboClaw.

title: fix(windows): distinguish invalid Scheduled Task inspection responses
body:
Related: #199617

## What Problem This Solves

Windows update failures report the same “invalid response” for malformed PowerShell JSON, invalid access facts, and an invalid task snapshot, hiding which inspection step failed.

## User Impact

Operators receive a specific, privacy-safe failure category in service errors and bounded update reports. Service-stop verification and all refusal behavior remain unchanged.

**Scope: this is a diagnostic improvement, not a verified fix for the beta.2 → beta.3 update failure. Native Windows reproduction and successful managed-update proof remain outstanding.** The inspecting runtime must contain the change; a newer candidate cannot change probes executed by an older installed updater.

Peter’s related mitigation [#199918](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199918) merged on November 16 as `ae678bf4c6b808b3ffc69b67e62d3a54c5e0d67f`. It refuses Gateway-started Windows Scheduled Task updates before mutation; it does not repair the terminal-origin invalid-response failure reported in #199617. This diagnostic change remains separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing probe owner’s failure category through the existing error formatter instead of collapsing three branches into one message. Emit only fixed labels, never raw PowerShell output, task definitions, or account values. Preserve generic diagnostics without a stage and carry the optional stage through the existing Windows diagnostic helper. No retries, new state, permission changes, or service mutations are introduced.

Simplification: reuse the existing diagnostic owner and report path; no additional helper or logging pipeline. Production changes are +15/-6 lines; tests/support are +73/-42 and documentation +6/-0.

## Evidence

- Three synthetic native-response regression cases fail on the unchanged implementation and pass with the change. They distinguish JSON, access-fact, and snapshot failures and verify a synthetic secret is absent from the error and cause.
- 99 focused tests passed: `schtasks-state-probe.test.ts`, `service-command-read.test.ts`, `update-command-service-report.test.ts`, and `update-command-service-unavailable.test.ts`, run with `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`. The report tests verify the category survives the 200-character failure-fact bound and service stop/install/restart remain uncalled. Combined command wall time about 53 seconds including formatting; runner durations 34.64 seconds for daemon tests and 13.53 seconds for CLI tests. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Core production typecheck, services and config/CLI test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) assessed the complete local diff against `7d7d86bb79ca24bfaf9343290cb22f80d705ab20`: scoped-clean, no findings. The reviewer did not independently execute the tests.
- Native Windows Task Scheduler and the shipped beta.2 → beta.3 managed-update flow were **not run**: this session has only a Linux executor. The underlying incident remains unproven; this PR does not close the issue. No live Gateway was changed.

Fixes compacted shell output disappearing from the JavaScript result in native Code Mode when the optional Tokenjuice plugin reduces a command result.

## User Impact

Exit status, failure diagnostics, exact reads, and the outer JavaScript result remain unchanged. The plugin remains opt-in; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Tokenjuice adapter now places its delivered replacement text in the existing structured shell-output field consumed by Code Mode. It still removes the duplicate raw aggregate before reduction, so this does not restore raw output or add special handling to core.

title: fix(gateway): first chats fail during cold storage startup
body:
Related: #197510

## What Problem This Solves

First chat requests can fail with storage-unavailable errors while an agent database is starting. Permissive fixture umasks also prevent Gateway tests from reaching that behavior.

## User Impact

Cold chat requests retain the existing database preparation instead of rejecting its first registration. Filesystem permission, routing, lifetime and source-identity guards remain enforced. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wait only for an already-running first-use creator before capturing the registry witness, and classify existing-file registrations against physically qualified identities. Readiness stays in the existing fact-acquisition owner; the caller retains its lifetime and routing checks. This adds no retry or timeout increase.

Create fixture-owned `.openclaw` with mode `0700` before publishing its selectors. The native writable-ancestor guard is unchanged; no chmod, skip, quarantine or permission override is added.

## Evidence

- **Current-head integration:** PR CI [43754726962](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43754726962) and Security Review [43754726935](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43754726935) completed successfully for `d8b5dc1572f7f53a0169de4a2d30cd9aabc9c4ef`.
- **Real first-chat flow:** [fresh isolated Gateway run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7c4c71169b62464332a11dfd9e812814) passed the additional selected case in 19.355s. A real first-use creator was paused before opening the absent target database; the same real WebSocket chat request observed a canonical startup refusal before handler work. After releasing the real creator, authorization acquired the target, `agent.wait` returned `ok`, history contained exactly one expected assistant answer, and the tracked local HTTP provider received one request. The native run ended with no suite or unhandled errors, and one-release AWS cleanup completed.

The first-chat test issues **one SDK chat intent, not one wire attempt**: the unmodified SDK made five wire attempts (four normal startup refusals, one handler start). No test retry wrapper, database prewarm or request-timeout change was added. This qualifies the current user flow with an explicit observation overlay; it is **not an original-versus-fixed Gateway RPC RED/GREEN comparison**. The owner-level causal regressions below provide that separate evidence. The provider is local and deterministic, not a live external model.

<details>
<summary>Selected first-chat native receipts and source scope</summary>

Projected from the actual selected-case and native run-end receipts; the immutable pre-release snapshot is the pause witness:

```text
published parent: d8b5dc1572f7f53a0169de4a2d30cd9aabc9c4ef

handler starts=1; agent.wait=ok
persisted expected answers=1; provider requests=1
selected case=passed; suite errors=0; unhandled errors=0
```

The clean native observation commit is a child of this PR head, with four explicit observation/test-path changes. The production preparer is byte-identical to the PR; the fact-reader algorithm is unchanged apart from scalar publications. It is not claimed to be the unmodified published tree. Pinned Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` both passed the tiny native-channel/correlation control before product work. The selected first-chat case passed; the five existing recovery cases were intentionally not selected in this additional run and are covered by the 70-case qualification below.

Only the immutable pre-release snapshot establishes the held creator. Later open counters include a normal second open; the auxiliary post-open pause flag is not a liveness observation and is excluded from qualification. Earlier probes that timed out before the required observation were rejected, not counted as causal RED.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Owner regressions, fixture isolation and scoped checks</summary>

- [Current normalized-source qualification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e2c94863fd1bece84bef822f7c950e59): maintained Gateway-root compiler leaf passed with all five changed files in the actual compiler program; exact five-file type-aware lint and normal `qaRuntime` build passed; all 49 owner, 16 creation/settlement and five original recovered-output cases passed (70 total, zero pending).

The normalized proof used failed CI merge `3449e444e4a8733541d828e894d86ce74f83705d`, with all five changed-file bytes matching this revision. Its `97dd78cc2cbd4f9dff1add734a2b316ac8d8bf31` main integration was a different whole tree; the subsequent successful current-head PR CI above, not file-byte equality, supplies integration validation.

Full-main qualification, release packaging and manual Windows/live-external-model proof are not claimed. Current-head ClawSweeper satisfaction and the native landing workflow remain required; nothing has been merged by this update.

title: fix: undo cold-session compaction CPU and latency regressions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the cold-session compaction CPU and latency regressions introduced by #196550 by reverting that change.

## User Impact

Restores the prior in-process compaction path. This deliberately gives up the reverted implementation’s worker-offload and burst-workload benefits in favor of the cold workload that dominates this deployment. No schema, configuration, or transcript-format migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reverts squash commit `c9ee2646f8c6a8869a2a1ae7629e7615204cf9fc` at @vincentkoc’s request after the measured cold-workload regressions. Preserves subsequent context-reader batching and PostgreSQL fallback, shared reader-lane and pressure-lifecycle changes, and unrelated later-main fixes. Removes the dependent test/entry registrations for modules deleted by the revert.

Requested by @vincentkoc. Original implementation by @RomneyDa; cc @RomneyDa.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4e49760c-4871-43ad-8ce6-e734c7368e68)

## Evidence

### Current candidate — main integration and focused validation

All 214 unrelated-main paths and 76 nonoverlapping rollback paths were verified unchanged against their respective parents.
- Focused batches passed separately: reader factory 20, worker lanes 29, sharing preparation 44, pool preparation 33, and wrapper inventory 1 (22 other wrapper tests unselected). These are separate batch counts, not a pooled unique-test total. Sharing/pool contracts include saturated-pool point-read admission and rejection of host callbacks.
- Four-file format/lint, staged line-cap/max-lines/assertion guards against pinned main, production core types, matching sessions/gateway/infra/tooling test type graphs, and diff checks passed in the qualified private Node 26 environment with clear environment, proxy inheritance disabled, network disabled, default heaps, 2 CPUs/8 GiB and zero swap. Root and workspace dependency manifests and private install metadata were unchanged.
- A supplemental actual-reader-factory probe verifies the explicit timeout object/signal and transport-only pointRead true/undefined cases. Its first fixture incorrectly expected an empty environment although the existing capture owner supplies a state directory; that failed receipt is retained. A separate corrected fixture with an explicit valid synthetic storage environment passed the exact assertions. No product or tracked-test change weakened the contract.
- Fresh independent integration review, hands-on review, and the supported full-candidate local review against the pinned main commit found no actionable findings; the latter completed all seven passes over the full 82-path product delta. The signed merge commit used normal hooks without overrides; documented merge-operation hook early returns do not replace the separately completed focused guards.
- Both exact current-pair canonical source-performance runtime builds and the two original native cold qualifications passed using committed workload `f292067c3edd57b778ccfcfd313e3e37075ca89b`. The declared recovery1 comparison is now terminal: 10/10 observations native-valid and comparison-controller exit 0. These are scoped runtime builds, not full public-package/declaration proof. Exact-head Build workflow [43708537631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43708537631) also passed. Full public-package/declaration proof and live PostgreSQL remain unrun.
- Exact-head test workflow [43708537753](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43708537753) remains failed: all 121 jobs were accounted for (91 success, 27 skipped, 3 failed including the aggregate gate). CI tested merge `709d8e308274c32f233bcd66088234b31062d4fc`, parents pinned main `8f9bd10825ff371258be39c9a033df0ce361fa60` and PR head `382045388fd8612132c04aa7b305db0c10781aa6`, tree `2bc6eff35dab0e1063bdca3809f6b47162cbcd2e`. The original V2 comparison on main `8f9bd10825ff371258be39c9a033df0ce361fa60` versus revert `382045388fd8612132c04aa7b305db0c10781aa6` was interrupted: six observations completed; original slot 7 started but was noneligible, stopping after confirmed seed shutdown before any recorded successful import or measured RPC; three original slots were unattempted. The exact stale owned container was removed only after its recorded process was absent and ownership matched; partial session state was not reused.

Before inspecting any original-prefix CPU/RSS values for recovery selection, the full replacement order and protocol were frozen: **ten fresh observations, five serial main→revert pairs**, with fresh state and tags, the same exact source pair, unchanged twelve-blob committed workload `f292067c3edd57b778ccfcfd313e3e37075ca89b`, image, private builds, default product heaps (including canonical 512/16 MiB database-worker limits), model-work counts, metric formulas/windows and the cold-proof rule below. An independent recovery-integrity review found no supported original-journal resume and no selective-resampling basis.

That single prospectively declared recovery1 cohort completed 10/10 with controller exit 0. Each observation completed the real seed → stopped native import → restart → `sessions.compact` → same-physical-session 8192-byte follow-up → canonical cleanup flow, with two successful 250 ms agent-summary requests and zero utility-summary requests. Independent numeric/native audit found no discrepancy in the 15 metrics/ratios or the 10 current native flows; its binding/cleanup checks also covered the original six complete flows and two reused qualifications (18 complete flows total, not 18 acceptance samples).

**Total disclosed V2 acceptance work is 16 complete observations, one interrupted/noneligible observation, and three unattempted original slots. The two original qualifications are separate and reused—not new or pooled observations.** The original six form the separate n=3-per-arm prefix below. No better-cohort selection, pooling, correction factors, fabricated passed predecessor, or open-ended repeat-until-green occurred. The completion is native/numeric evidence, not performance, memory, CI or landing acceptance.

### V2 recovery1 current-source results — n=5 per arm

Main is `8f9bd10825ff371258be39c9a033df0ce361fa60`; revert is `382045388fd8612132c04aa7b305db0c10781aa6`. Each cell shows **median / nearest-rank p95 [min–max]**; p95 is the maximum at n=5. Runtime publication uses complete native binding discovery and the existing loaded-command location reader before effective-environment inspection. Risky bindings must establish safety through their exact native reader rather than disappear into a best-effort sibling scan. title: fix(ui): keep loaded history visible during compaction
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-loaded conversation disappears into a short tool-only tail when compaction refreshes history during an active goal with a queued follow-up.

## User Impact

The loaded discussion stays visible while the goal and queued input remain intact. Real branch switches, resets, and transcript rewrites still replace incompatible history. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconcile refreshed history using native physical positions and rewrite generation, rather than display order or an advancing transcript tip alone. The existing lazy recovery owner does the work after live-state prerequisites and rechecks request ownership before using held state. The bounded older-page read, 1,000-row limit and lazy fallback are unchanged.

CI investigation also exposed two input-lifecycle holes: a first upward jump could compare against a stale native offset, and completed paste recovery could resurrect text cleared by a later edit. Refreshing the actual pre-input origin and canceling recovery on the first input repair those owners without relaxing request or paste guards. Main’s explicit skills-used performance retirement is preserved.

The original candidate passed 114 focused tests and seven shipped-bundle Chromium cases. After integrating main’s retirement, 76 focused history/cursor/identity cases passed; the three recovery owners are byte-identical to the previously reviewed core.
- The stale-offset request regression fails with the previous owner and passes with the fix: Home from a real 5,500px origin loads older rows with null or stale-zero tracking, while both no-input controls stay inert. The affected history owner, maintenance and autofill suites passed. The paste inserted-then-cleared regression also fails before repair and passes afterward; 12 paste cases and 84 New Session/command-palette consumer cases passed.
- Final tree `cd766ef83678b4a681a1b8d4d51cae6177e87aaf`, based on main `a0423637196f7d999b91240f5d0938ef680b694f`, passed all 16 browser cases across the reading, compaction and native-paste files on isolated AWS (Node 24.22.1, 8 vCPU/16 GB; 87.31 seconds). WebKit phone and Chromium phone/desktop each completed 240 reading samples at 190 messages; maximum residuals were 0.765625px, 0.5px and 0.46875px respectively. Initial viewport, committed-prefix and runway readiness are observed explicitly; the >200-sample and 2px gates are unchanged. Ordinary and Shift-paste coverage remains intact.
- UI production, Chat-test and E2E-Chat typechecks, targeted lint/format, controller guards and diff checks passed. Net test growth is 551 lines; exactly 151 justified allocation lines cover the excess over the unchanged 400-line allowance. No timeout, shard-selection, asset-cap, compressor or baseline changes.
- Fresh independent full-patch review and Codex autoreview against pinned main `a0423637196f7d999b91240f5d0938ef680b694f` found no P0–P2 findings in the final 11-file candidate. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable on the selected route; hosted review previously acknowledged the PR.

The repaired defects have independent red/green proof, but those CI logs do not establish their exact event/timer ordering. A focused passing replay is not claimed as causal attribution or an inherited-failure waiver.

title: fix(ui): expired approvals claim an execution outcome
body:
Related: #199100.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an expired approval page says the operation was denied even when its configured timeout fallback can execute it. The same page also tells people a decision was recorded for expired or canceled requests that have no decision.

## User Impact

The page now says the approval request expired without a recorded decision. Terminal pages still say they can be closed, without inventing a decision. Approval policy, timeout behavior, allowed decisions, redaction and execution are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

An approval request’s terminal state is not the operation’s execution result. The Gateway can return an expired request and a null decision, while the exec owner separately applies the configured fallback. Two English strings now describe only facts known to the page. Existing approved/denied headings and descriptions retain the real decision; no new state or conditional rendering is needed.

- Two isolated exec-entry tests run a harmless fixture command for the full timeout fallback and reject it for the deny fallback. A separate Gateway handler test proves expiry is returned without a decision and settles the waiter to null. No live approval or policy was changed.

Validation, write behavior, permissions and secret protection are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A write can already be saved when its runtime refresh fails. The owner counts successful responses, so zero confirmations before that error does not mean zero entries were saved. This change states the fact the owner actually knows instead of parsing error text or inferring protected values from inventory metadata.

Only four English strings change. The branch now includes current main’s read-state and confirmed-write recovery work from #199116 and #199414. That receipt-handling owner is preserved unchanged; its additional partial-count expectation was updated to the new wording.

title: fix: conversation deletion leaves dependent automations enabled
body:
Related: #199300

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes conversation deletion leaving execution-dependent automations enabled, without disabling independent work merely created in or reporting to that conversation.

## User Impact

- An independent command created in conversation A and reporting to B keeps running after A is deleted.
- A reporting-only link does not disable an automation. Missing internal delivery is recorded as a delivery error, without recreating the deleted conversation or silently routing the report elsewhere.
- Automations that actually use the deleted conversation's inherited context, workspace, session-scoped authority, or execution target are disabled before deletion. Reporting elsewhere does not detach those real dependencies.
- Definitions and activity history remain. If a required disable fails, the conversation remains and the error explains that some jobs may already be disabled. Existing human and model management restrictions still apply; already-running commands may finish.

A plain command uses its saved process definition and requester authority. Agent/script jobs that inherit creator resources, and commands with parent-dependent triggers or session-scoped grants, remain dependent. Explicit external chats remain external destinations; deleting a local transcript does not delete the external chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first version treated all links as lifecycle ownership. This revision separates association from execution dependency and reuses the scheduled execution-context owner for the decision. Requester authority is retained independently rather than promoted to legacy operator access when the creator is gone. Doctor and the replay reader consume the same parent decision.

The reviewed embedded-cleanup regression is also fixed: local deletion uses the existing paused offline cron owner while general embedded cron RPCs remain unavailable. Hosted disable failures still prevent deletion. No schema, new persistence layer, scheduler, or client-side mutation sequence is added.

## Evidence

- The registered deletion handler, real SQLite session/job stores and production occurrence admission reproduce the creator/reporting regressions before the repair. Nine current handler scenarios pass, including independent commands reporting elsewhere, reporting-only deletion, explicit execution targets, partial disable failure, and human/model authority. Only command/model execution edges are synthetic.
- Real completion tests verify explicit destination delivery after source deletion, missing internal reporting without recreation or fallback, visible delivery errors in retained history, and loading/delivery of v2026.9.9-shaped jobs without rewriting receipts or schema.
- Execution-context/admission/binding, stored-shape fixtures, Doctor/replay, owner-authority and binding checks pass. The final core/UI types, scoped lint, formatting, i18n and diff checks pass.
- The previous CI failures in embedded ACP/spawn cleanup and incomplete hosted test fixtures are repaired. Seven affected files completed with 86 passing cases. An overbroad eight-file run reached its external 600-second command limit during unrelated production-boundary cases; it was not restarted or given a higher limit. Completed results were retained, and the 11 unfinished named collector/deletion-boundary cases passed a bounded replay. The entire broad production-boundary suite is not claimed green locally; new-head CI remains the broad gate.
- 64 organizer cases and two production-built browser flows pass. Sidebar and Sessions Cancel/Confirm behavior stays unchanged: one exact-session delete and no client-side automation writes. Browser Gateway responses are synthetic. Final browser proof took 19.93s including build. No live user session or automation was mutated; no full live upgrade rehearsal was run.
- Canonical autoreview with Codex GPT-6.1 Sol reviewed the complete revised candidate against `89ee0bd382d16ec16183a10e81a8930a92ed1909` at P0–P2 and returned scoped-clean. The reviewer did not execute tests independently. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. The forward-only published tree is byte-identical to that reviewed candidate; it retains the original PR ancestry rather than force-pushing the rebased draft.

Current-main production-built Control UI, light theme, synthetic Backup maintenance conversation. This warning treats linked automations as a separate cleanup task.

title: fix(openai): conversations fail when hooks override saved-context replay
body:
Related: #198357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes OpenAI conversations failing with a saved-context conflict when a later payload hook overrides checkpoint replay settings, and restores the recovery guidance that was lost on the way to chat.

## User Impact

Conversations using retained OpenAI checkpoints keep their context without re-storing conflicting checkpoint records. If an item conflict still occurs, the chat shows the existing recovery instructions instead of only the raw provider error. No configuration changes, migrations, transcript rewrites, or automatic replay of completed work are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier checkpoint safeguard ran before the final payload hook. The transport now reapplies the same storage invariant to the final hooked input, including removing a stale continuation reference. Ordinary stored continuation and Azure/custom endpoint policies remain unchanged.

The reply-failure path now uses the existing code-aware format renderer rather than rebuilding a generic diagnostic from the raw error.

OpenAI can report this conflict after streaming output, so this fix prevents the conflicting request rather than retrying after output or tool work has started.

## Evidence

### Maintainer verification and test correction

The published head `96d47170` reproduced the failing continuation assertion without incorporating a newer main. Production behavior was correct; the test still expected stored references for a stateless checkpoint replay and recovery.

The corrected test verifies the complete input in the checkpoint request and in recovery, with no `previous_response_id`. The next normal turn reuses the last valid stored prefix (`resp_1`) and includes all intervening messages; it never references the unstored recovery response. The scenario retains its exact four requests for three prompts, including the existing recovery attempt. No new retry path or production change was added.

Fresh validation on Tempbook: **25 existing tests passed** (22 continuation cases and 3 real-loopback SSE/WebSocket/cached-WebSocket cases). Focused types, lint, formatting and line limits passed. One redundant checkpoint assertion was then removed; formatting was rechecked without repeating the unchanged behavior tests. No external OpenAI API call was repeated; the earlier live proof below remains the implementation author's evidence.

The published correction has the same Git tree as the reviewed local candidate. Current-head CI is the remaining broad validation.

Verified published head: `ed2e15050265b21356c539f183c551b40a68fa3e`; Git tree matches the reviewed local correction.


- Before/after regressions reproduce the exact lost-guidance reply and check both the delivered payload and the saved lifecycle notice.
- Serialized-request regressions fail before the fix and pass for SSE, WebSocket, and cached WebSocket, preserving the checkpoint/input and sending only one request.
- The earlier implementation report listed 133 focused passes. The fresh maintainer runs above separately reproduce and correct the continuation test failure on the published head.
- **Live OpenAI API-key proof passed** with a real stored checkpoint: ordinary restoration, reload, and a late-hook override all retain a tool-derived marker across subsequent agent prompts, with one physical request per prompt.
- Scoped TypeScript, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. No package boundary or dependency changes.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex engine, P0–P2) reviewed the complete candidate against base c5381ef2d215b90a5e5b870543f2c12468f3a66b and reported scoped-clean, with no actionable findings. The local ClawSweeper checkout was outside this session's permitted file scope; the documented autoreview fallback was used. Hosted review remains pending.

The original production request payload was not retained. The late-hook escape is reproduced and fixed, but is not claimed as the confirmed trigger of that particular incident. The affected production conversation has not been reset or resumed as part of this change.

Normal hover and keyboard-focus previews resume on the next interaction after release. Modified clicks keep their normal navigation behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lazy preview loader and mounted preview providers now share the current modifier state. Existing dismissal handles pending work and focus restoration rather than hiding an active overlay with CSS. Other hovercards and tooltips are unchanged.

## Evidence

title: fix(goals): allow new goals after the previous goal is achieved
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: starting a new goal fails when the session’s previous goal is already achieved.

## User Impact

Users can explicitly start the next goal without manually clearing or resuming the completed one. The new goal gets its own identity and fresh accounting, while conversation history stays intact. Active, paused, blocked, and limited goals keep their existing protections. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared creation path now replaces completed goals, and the Control UI uses ordinary Start admission rather than trying to edit them. Direct and queued reply completion also stop using the completed predecessor’s identity to suppress the new goal’s automatic continuation. This reuses the existing storage and continuation owners; it adds no scheduler, schema, or new tool.

title: improve(workers): reduce retained database worker heap capacity
body:
Related companion harness: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199420

## What Problem This Solves

Retained session readers and SQLite storage workers keep more young-generation heap capacity than this measured history workload needs.

## User Impact

Reduces the young-generation budget of existing session-reader and storage-broker workers from 32 to 16 MiB; their 512 MiB old-generation budgets, results, worker counts, lifetimes, and database admission remain unchanged. No configuration or data migration is required. Cold-read CPU increased in the comparison below. This does **not** establish that a complete Gateway fits in 2 GiB: the historical full-Gateway 2 GiB acceptance still failed and was not rerun.

## Why This Change Was Made

Change only the two existing resource-limit owners, without adding shared fallback policy, options, pools, or retirement behavior. The tradeoff is a smaller nursery with more first-read CPU in this workload; measured worker heap capacity is not an additive RSS saving. @vincentkoc accepted the disclosed cold-CPU, whole-command CPU, and sampled maximum-RSS tradeoffs for this scoped change on November 15; decision context is linked under Original discussion in Work sessions. Normal review, CI, and security gates remain applicable.

## Evidence

Five serial ABAB pairs on source base `940e76922e54c1880fa8594e6478f2b561fac307`, Node 26.12.1, identical frozen dependencies, fresh synthetic fixture/process per arm: 10,000 1-KiB messages, Gateway history-tail owner, 100 warm reads after the first read and five warmups. No forced GC or inspector in this timing comparison; native worker-limit observations and cached production per-worker heap telemetry retained their sample ages. The summed heap observations are not simultaneous peak or live-set measurements; a representative broker sample was about five seconds older than the transcript sample. All ten cases completed and returned 20 of 10,000 messages. The performance table remains source-owner history-tail evidence, not a sustained mixed writer/usage/search performance test; separate real-Gateway transport correctness proof follows below. Those sibling workloads are not performance-qualified by this dataset.

| Metric (median of five runs) | 32 MiB | 16 MiB | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Maximum sampled target-worker heap capacity | 156,565,504 B | 116,252,672 B | -25.75% |
| Maximum sampled target-worker used heap | 80,908,352 B | 81,303,480 B | +0.49% |
| First-read elapsed | 3,012.60 ms | 3,001.95 ms | -0.35% |
| First-read CPU | 2,826.64 ms | 3,193.50 ms | +12.98% |
| Warm measured CPU, 100 reads | 246.63 ms | 223.19 ms | -9.50% |
| Warm throughput | 582.78 reads/s | 644.77 reads/s | +10.64% |
| Warm per-run p50 latency | 1.502 ms | 1.476 ms | -1.73% |
| Warm per-run p95 latency | 2.434 ms | 2.243 ms | -7.85% |
| Warm-report process RSS | 915,566,592 B | 857,538,560 B | -6.34% |
| Independently observed maximum process RSS | 960,905,216 B | 976,445,440 B | +1.62% |
| Whole-command CPU, including setup and trace | 27.77 s | 28.11 s | +1.22% |

The prespecified comparison rejects a 20% median cold/warm CPU or latency regression (including the median per-run p95), equivalent throughput loss, bad results, crashes, or old-limit drift; none occurred. Spread remains visible: per-run warm p95 ranges were 2.006–2.664 ms versus 1.892–4.853 ms, and throughput 526.54–637.48 versus 378.28–668.02 reads/s. One candidate run was a slower outlier; it was not rerun. These are medians of per-run percentiles, not a pooled p95 of all reads. Host load was recorded; this was not a constrained-host profile.

Rerunnable timing workload:
