```sh
  --profile long --operation gateway-tail --samples 100 --output report.json
```
Both arms temporarily used the exact committed benchmark script from companion PR #199420, head `cc808e0c5bc610a4838ccbc77f04dd10b878287c`, SHA-256 `9d259c0a9e674b688b90b4535a0b615822a5daaced438acaae10c4d236b82247`. The original script was restored byte-for-byte before review/commit; this PR remains independent and contains no benchmark changes. The original base script failed required runtime-config preparation before timing; that setup failure was investigated, not counted as a performance regression.

### Real-Gateway transport correctness

On November 15, the unchanged committed `scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts` and `scripts/perf/history-diff-measure.ts` exercised one fresh isolated source-mode Gateway for controlled baseline `940e769…` (32 MiB) and reviewed head `7606306631b4c8e9b8164cf89cecfa600352106e` (16 MiB), serially. Both used `src/entry.ts`, the same pristine fixture with 256 known synthetic messages, loopback WebSocket `connect` and public `chat.history`, and the same four-CPU affinity (`0-3`). Memory was unconstrained; this was not a 2/4/6 GiB acceptance test. Sanitized task homes/state and no inference were used.

Each arm passed one first-use history request, one warmup cohort, and five profiled warm requests. Every recorded cold/warm response returned the same 13 budget-selected rows, correct session ID, and expected synthetic tail through inspection 63. Baseline/candidate normalized payload SHA-256 was identical: `fa8fd6c34061f7f6c301a8457eba7abd4c80e3dd4cedca1268a039fdf1172427`.

Passive native Worker observations confirmed old/young **512/32** versus **512/16** for the observed transcript and SQLite broker workers. Cached sample ages are retained: 3–46,365 ms baseline and 78–37,834 ms candidate; observations nearest the warm window were about 3.1 s old versus 6.6–9.3 s old. No fresh-heap, live-set, or RSS improvement is inferred from these observations. A task-owned observational preload added limit/telemetry recording to the existing launch without replacing the source entry or changing worker options.

Both real Gateway PIDs remained available to the workload through the final RPC, then disappeared after owned teardown; logs recorded completed shutdown. Source-mode SIGTERM teardown produced compiler-stopped/log-append warnings in both arms, followed by completed shutdown (158/148 ms); these inherited harness diagnostics are retained, not claimed as a repaired lifecycle issue. The existing workload captured main-isolate CPU profiles plus worker-message and RPC diagnostics, not per-worker CPU profiles. This bounded two-arm run closes transport correctness only: it is **not** a new five-pair Gateway performance comparison, and the earlier five-pair owner results were not rerun or relabeled as transport performance.

title: fix: output reducers are skipped in headless and Code Mode runs
body:
Supersedes #199424 after resolving its conflict with current main.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes enabled tool-output reducers silently being skipped in headless runs and nested Code Mode tool calls.

## User Impact

Enabled middleware such as Tokenjuice can transform actual tool results before they reach the agent, including nested Code Mode shell calls. Exact file/schema results and the surrounding JavaScript envelope retain their existing contracts. Bounded-command guidance recommends the existing terminal-result collection path instead of avoidable short-yield/poll cycles.

No new configuration, dependencies, permission changes, or migrations. Native Codex shell results remain outside this replacement path. This PR does not claim a whole-task token-savings percentage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Headless runs prepare a scoped plugin generation, but middleware discovery consulted the process-global registry. Discovery now follows the current context and its prepared lazy-load inputs. Native catalog calls apply the existing middleware once before guest serialization, using the policy-adjusted arguments actually executed.

Prompt/docs recommend the existing `awaitResults` behavior for bounded commands and distinguish native replacement, CLI wrapping, failure preservation and complete-task measurement. A CI-exposed capacity-test fixture also now accepts the same process record from running or completed retention; all original assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

- Scoped-only, empty-root and same-ID lazy-owner regressions fail on the unchanged base and pass with the fix. The real-worker Code Mode regression covers once-only transformation, executed command/cwd, failure metadata, exact file/schema bytes and the outer envelope.
- Original combined candidate: 43 tests across six files/four shards and full `pnpm build` passed. The build emitted unrelated UI size-budget advisories.
- Built real-model direct and Code Mode probes before conflict integration: synthetic inventory output was reduced from 5,647 to 470 delivered characters including the notice; exit 7/sentinel and exact file/schema results were preserved. No manual CLI wrapper or global-registry workaround. This is boundary proof, not a matched whole-task benchmark.
- Local autoreview of the full original patch (base `520f18975936d49ffc1cf8d02bbd98c4b7981c14`, committed as `4aad990fc6fbdd5ce204fd4d33b99932525220c1`) found no actionable P0–P2 issues. - Conflict integration with main `3c6bb67f82aec52a12644933434a9d5ed7e6ed01` preserves the renamed prompt variable and current background guidance. Middleware production files and regression fixtures remain byte-identical to the original reviewed patch. Post-integration: 89 tests across five files/three shards, scoped lint/types, formatting, MDX and diff checks passed.
- [CI run 43676766068](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43676766068) exposed a running-only lookup in `code-mode.catalog-lifetime.test.ts:76`. `pnpm test:ci-failed 199434 --run` reproduced the original failure locally. title: fix: apply output reducers in headless and Code Mode calls
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes enabled tool-output reducers silently being skipped in headless runs and nested Code Mode tool calls.

## User Impact

Enabled middleware such as Tokenjuice can transform actual OpenClaw tool results before they reach the agent, including nested Code Mode shell calls. Exact file/schema results and the surrounding JavaScript envelope retain their existing contracts. Bounded-command guidance now recommends the existing terminal-result collection path instead of avoidable short-yield/poll cycles.

No new configuration, dependencies, permission changes, or migrations. Native Codex shell results remain outside this replacement path. This PR does not claim a whole-task token-savings percentage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Headless runs prepare a scoped plugin generation, but middleware discovery consulted the process-global registry and could select no callback or a different same-ID root plugin. Discovery now follows the current context and its prepared lazy-load inputs. Native catalog calls also apply the existing middleware once before guest serialization, using the arguments actually executed after policy adjustment.

The exec runtime already supports `awaitResults`; the prompt and documentation now explain when to use it. Tokenjuice guidance distinguishes real output replacement from plugin inventory status and separates native replacement, explicit wrapping, failure preservation, and complete-task measurements.

## Evidence

- Scoped-only, empty-root, and same-ID lazy-owner regressions fail on the unchanged base and pass with the fix.
- The Code Mode regression uses a real worker and shell: once-only transformation, policy-adjusted command/cwd, exit/error metadata, unchanged exact file/schema bytes, and intact outer envelope.
- Combined candidate: 43 tests pass across six focused files/four shards. Supporting lane checks cover the affected Code Mode, Tool Search, MCP, headless, native-hook, and prefix-stability consumers.
- Existing terminal-wait subprocess proof preserves exit 7, explicit background behavior, and timeout cleanup without changing runtime defaults.
- Scoped types/lint and ten-file formatting pass; the changed MDX pages pass validation.
- Local autoreview of the complete candidate at P0–P2: no actionable findings; supplied source review, not test execution. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable from a clean built runner.
- Full `pnpm build` passes (it emits UI size-budget advisory warnings; this change does not touch UI source). Built real-model headless runs pass with direct tools and Code Mode: automatic inventory compaction is 5,647 → 470 characters including the notice; exit 7/sentinel, exact file bytes, and the returned schema object are preserved. No manual CLI wrapper or global-root activation workaround.

title: fix(plugins): stop loading permissions after inspection fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin’s Permissions section keeps looking busy after its inspection request has failed, even though other settings are already usable.

## User Impact

User impact: the finished failure no longer shows a loading skeleton or claims that unknown permissions mean there are no settings. The real error and Try again remain. Existing settings stay usable, and confirmed permission controls return after retry. No grants, authorization or configuration writes change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The view previously treated missing inspection as permanent loading. It now derives pending state from the existing inspection read and carries the accepted-data distinction into the editor’s empty-state decision. This also avoids replacing the misleading skeleton with misleading “no configurable settings” guidance for plugins that only expose permission settings.

## Evidence

Actual compiled Control UI with a supported synthetic Gateway, light theme, 1280×1200 desktop. The inspected, annotated 900×900 crops preserve the error, existing settings and affected Permissions region. No live plugin operation or permission change occurred.

It verifies that the existing input retains its node, value and usability, and that no configuration or enablement write is sent. A permissions-only sibling remains neutral while inspection is unknown instead of claiming there are no settings. Owning tests retain confirmed-empty and cached-permission behavior.

title: fix(ios): embedded Dashboard pages ignore device appearance
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening Automations or another embedded Dashboard page in the iOS app abruptly switches to the saved web theme instead of following the app’s device appearance.

## User Impact

Embedded iPhone and iPad pages use native-aligned surfaces, red accents, and sans-serif typography in the device’s light or dark mode. Saved web theme, accent, and font choices remain unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing theme owner separates rendered iOS appearance from saved web preferences. A private palette uses the existing document-start and runtime stylesheet lifecycle; only iOS embeds fetch it. The redundant first-paint theme-name table is replaced by the equivalent naming formula. Appearance explains that its theme controls customize the web Dashboard.

iOS embeds load one versioned 1,686-byte palette stylesheet, like the selected built-in web palettes; ordinary browsers do not fetch it. The existing first-paint and load/error behavior is retained.

This does not add native theme synchronization, replace native controls, or change Android/macOS appearance or navigation.

## Evidence

Addresses [ClawSweeper’s P2 byte-budget finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199394#issuecomment-6888222427) on `0e05c2920f79a7edaf17201de7d0477a9a3db3ad`. Repair head: `5ce5df3a571f247ce2043da26961b38249e56309`.

**Acceptance:** unchanged deterministic byte/request limits against base `65cf8cdc3780439cb599853f443c45fed28a98e4`; no budget or baseline increases.

| Same-toolchain measurement | Reviewed candidate | Repair | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Document gzip | 14,103 B | 13,966 B | Below the unchanged 14,026 B ceiling |
| Shared total CSS raw growth over base | +1,287 B | 0 B | Pass |
| Shared total CSS gzip growth over base | +195 B | 0 B | Pass |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | Unchanged |
| Largest JavaScript differential gate | Within allowance | Within allowance | Pass |

- The unchanged differential performance checker passes on the repair. Existing base CSS/largest-asset debt remains visible as warnings; the PR adds no new failing budget. Startup JS grows 70 B and complete route boot JS grows 114 B over the paired base, within existing limits.
- Both strengthened production-browser scenarios pass: phone dark and iPad light, first-paint names **and background colors**, one native palette load per document, live mode changes, unchanged web preferences, and no native-palette fetch in the ordinary-browser control. Fresh production build plus E2E: 16.74 seconds; scenario execution approximately 4.4 seconds.
- 84 related tests pass across six files (4.30 seconds), including every built-in document-start theme name and palette URL in both modes. UI and selected UI app/E2E test-graph typechecks, scoped lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, i18n verification, and diff checks pass.
- Final independent Auto Review of the complete local candidate against the base found no actionable **P0–P2** issues. The reviewer did not independently execute the tests.
- Phone Automations, phone Appearance, and iPad Automations captures were regenerated on the repair and are byte-identical to the three published after images below; their existing uploaded assets are reused.
- Simplification: the global entry CSS no longer carries an iOS-only palette, and the duplicate HTML theme-name table is removed. No new preference store, configuration option, bridge, or compatibility layer. Production/docs delta: +143/−47 lines; regression coverage: +206 lines.

<details>
<summary>Reproducing the size comparison</summary>

The stock `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 65cf8cdc3780439cb599853f443c45fed28a98e4` runner exceeded this sandbox’s 1 GiB `/tmp` capacity while expanding the base archive. The exact base production inputs and frozen candidate were instead built serially in the task-owned checkout with the same installed toolchain and fixed build identity; source backups and a finally block restored the candidate before its build. The repaired build used Vite’s native config loader through the repository TypeScript loader.

The existing supported comparator was then run without changes:

```text
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --base-dist <paired-base-dist>
```

It reproduces the reviewed candidate’s document/CSS failures and exits successfully on the repair. Precompressed-asset verification also passes. These are deterministic size measurements, not latency benchmarks.

</details>

**Proof boundary:** screenshots use synthetic data and the real production web bundle with the iOS document-start embed capability. They are not simulator captures; Xcode/iOS simulator verification is unavailable in this Linux sandbox. Hosted CI on `5ce5df3a571f247ce2043da26961b38249e56309` confirms that the [performance gate passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684408743). UI E2E shards [1/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684409028) and [3/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684408975) fail; partial attribution is summarized below, and the aggregate gate is red. This PR is not ready to merge. Hosted timing details are not yet summarized.

**CI attribution follow-up:** the WebKit 390 px older-history failure (`190` messages expected, `30` received) matches the complete terminal failure signature in [scheduled-main job 132671550925](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43667891698/job/132671550925), main commit `41f2b981d240cab9e55b07cba991282a795317b5`. This is stronger than the report’s job-name-only classification. That main job also exhibits the same two subpixel footer geometries, with expected/received reversed. The PR’s zero-geometry footer result and Logs auto-follow-resumption failure remain **new/unknown**, not waived or called inherited. A focused replay of the cached-header connection case passes on the candidate (1 passed, 1 dashboard case not selected; 16.06 seconds including build). That is a non-reproduction, not a fix or evidence that the CI failure is unrelated. The additional local WebKit replay is blocked at browser dependency qualification in this sandbox; no test assertions were bypassed, and no CI rerun was requested. No specific introduced defect is established by this bounded investigation. The aggregate gate remains red. The retained main-log window includes the terminal summaries, not the full execution chronology.

title: improve: choose automation models and thinking levels on Android
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android automation settings require operators to type model references and thinking levels even when the task’s scoped catalog already advertises those choices.

## User Impact

Operators can search model names and provider-qualified references, select a model and its advertised thinking level, restore defaults, or enter custom values. Unlisted saved values remain intact. Selection changes only the draft; Save Changes still commits it. Catalog failures keep the task editable and offer Refresh models. No scheduler, account-binding, authorization, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cron detail response already carries agent and session ownership. Retain those fields and read models.list for that job when its picker opens, never from the unrelated active chat. A scoped session supplies the owner when an explicit agent is absent; with neither, the Gateway resolves its ambient default.

Model choices live with the existing selected-job detail owner and use its request guard and Gateway connection scope. Late reads cannot replace a successor task, and failed refreshes retain that task’s previous choices. The shared native model-reference formatter, theme controls, draft owner, and save writer are reused. The raw-only model and thinking fields are replaced with same-window choosers; custom input remains explicit. Thinking choices come only from the selected model’s advertised capabilities, never a hard-coded ladder. Changing models preserves an existing custom thinking value. Net +278 production lines, +332 test lines, +1 documentation line, plus the generated native string inventory.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automation model choices follow the wrong agent, and reasoning suggestions do not reflect the selected model’s supported levels.

## User Impact

Operators can select models for the task they are actually editing instead of typing a missing reference manually. Saved/custom model references and Default remain available. Reasoning offers the selected model’s advertised levels, Default, and a custom value; switching models preserves an existing reasoning override. Changing the task agent refreshes its choices without replacing the draft; an unrelated team selection no longer changes those choices. No scheduling, model authorization, account binding, or saved-task migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing cron agent resolver for the pending task fields and the existing scoped model-catalog owner for reads, notifications, and stale-result checks. Clearing an override follows the task’s scoped session key when present; otherwise the request leaves default-agent resolution to the Gateway rather than guessing from the UI selection. A blank agent field on an existing task preserves its saved override, matching the existing update writer.

Configured and previously saved suggestions are also scoped instead of pooling every agent’s models. The existing model picker, custom-entry path, save owner, and refresh/error presentation are retained. The now-incorrect selected-agent subscription and hard-coded reasoning datalist were removed. The shared picker presents advertised reasoning metadata from that same catalog without an additional request or cache. Necessary net growth: +96 production lines, +199 test lines, +2 documentation lines; the new reasoning control owns only its transient custom-entry mode.

Android’s automation editor requires users to type exact run-target codes or format a session key as a target, despite knowing the supported modes and already loading recognizable sessions.

Users can choose a supported run mode or search the native client’s loaded sessions by name. Duplicate names show their keys as context, saved references remain intact outside the current roster, and explicit custom keys remain supported without requiring the target prefix.

**Main session**, **Isolated run**, and **Linked run** store the existing codes. Linked run means a separate run linked to the creating conversation, not whichever chat is currently open. Choices respect the payload’s supported target shapes. Selecting an item edits only the existing draft; Save Changes, Revert Changes, failure recovery, and unrelated fields keep their current boundaries. The original raw target input and formatting hint are removed.

Author simplification retained one native field component and its two repeated option rows, with the existing draft and roster owners: net +198 production lines, +309 test lines, and one documentation line. No picker framework or backend contract was added.

title: fix(workboard): choose existing labels instead of retyping them
body:
Related: #196810

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard asks users to remember and comma-format existing labels in card forms, inline editing, and bulk updates instead of offering the labels already present in their loaded cards.

## User Impact

Users can browse, search, and select existing labels in all three flows, or deliberately add a new label. Saved labels containing commas are preserved as single values. Selections stay local until Save or Apply, and cancellation, failed saves, light dismissal, and lost editability retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single Workboard-local control derives choices from the existing authorized card inventory in the current board and agent scope. It uses native checkboxes and the existing theme, dialog, popover, draft, and mutation owners. The loaded inventory is bounded, not a complete label catalog: saved selections remain available outside it, and custom labels remain supported. No catalog endpoint, cache, persistence system, or permission expansion was added.

Label drafts now retain arrays rather than serializing through comma-separated text. The old inputs, parser and helper copy are removed across all three consumers. Exact label strings remain the stored identities; new labels are trimmed and duplicates are not introduced.

Bulk **Keep unchanged**, **Add**, **Replace**, and **Remove** keep their distinct contracts; empty Replace clears labels. The UI respects the existing 40-character and 12-label limits, including preventing an Add operation from silently overflowing an existing card. This does not change the server’s truncation/rejection policy or duplicate the separate backend work in #196810. Bulk Remove is not artificially limited to twelve choices across several cards.

Author simplification kept one label control and existing save owners: net +183 production lines and +219 test/support lines. No universal picker or new SDK surface was introduced.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c4507bcf-b1bf-464e-a9df-2bc0344bbe58)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/30fbbba6-e989-49d2-9f1b-7bd46a563cc2)

## Evidence

- 76 focused tests passed across six files (Vitest 2.21 s): label choices, existing card editors and bulk actions, page selection, mutations, and live refresh. The new discovery regression fails on main because no label choice exists.
- Real native-plugin assets built by the production plugin builder were loaded in the actual Control UI shell with synthetic Gateway fixtures. Chromium proof selects an existing label with Space, applies it, asserts the exact workboard.cards.update payload, reloads, and confirms the saved selection in the inline editor. Search, Escape/focus return, and an emulated 400×800 viewport also pass (5.43 s scenario).
- Regression coverage includes Add/Replace/Remove payloads, empty Replace, board scoping, unresolved saved choices, comma-bearing and new labels, save/reopen, template reapplication, partial bulk retry, failed inline saves, light dismissal, and permission/archive transitions. No live card or external system was modified.
- Plugin browser typecheck, scoped lint (with tracked-scope and SDK string-style advisories), i18n verification, controller guard, both plugin import-boundary checks, formatting, and all three line/test ratchets pass. Fixes: Knowledge says a store assignment or conversation-access change did not happen when its response is interrupted.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

A failed response does not establish whether the write committed. The existing owner returns explicit outcomes when it can, but the browser’s catch-all path previously made an unconditional “not changed” claim. Both settings surfaces now preserve that uncertainty without changing writes, permissions, retries or storage.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation delivery requires users to type channel account IDs, even though the page already has a channel-scoped inventory with recognizable account names; the primary account field is also hidden under Advanced.

## User Impact

Users can search and choose a named **Sending account** beside the delivery channel, and choose an **Alert account** from the failure-alert channel’s separate inventory. Saved IDs remain stable, duplicate names have identifying context, and discovery or save failures do not erase selections or unrelated drafts.

## Why This Change Was Made

One cron-local control uses the existing searchable picker and the shared channel capability. It adds no discovery API, cache, permissions, or per-row fetches. **Automatic** removes the explicit override and preserves existing route-based account resolution, not a snapshot of the current default. Explicit custom references remain supported because the status inventory is not the schema’s complete allowed-value set. With **Last** as the channel, account entry stays open-ended: there is no single channel-specific catalog, and the UI does not guess a channel from an account name. Loading, failed discovery, unavailable inventory, and an empty known list are distinct states.

title: fix(update): preserve bundled hooks after npm updates
body:
Fixes #199216

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes bundled hooks silently disappearing when update runtime retention hard-links their installed files.

## User Impact

Bundled hooks remain discoverable after runtime retention. Rejected hook files now produce a warning naming the file and cause; hard-link warnings explain how to recover.

Already-affected files are not rewritten in place. A successful npm package replacement supplies fresh hook files, and the fixed updater preserves their independent inodes on later retention. If files remain linked, replace them with independent copies or reinstall OpenClaw with the owning package manager, then restart the Gateway. Discovery now gives that recovery guidance, so no separate Doctor mutation is added. The full upgrade recovery path remains unverified because remote capacity was unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing independent-inode owner to protect `HOOK.md` and all adjacent handler candidates, so retention copies them. Keep strict hook hard-link rejection intact. Forward rejected opens to discovery's existing warning callback, leaving missing optional package manifests and handler candidates quiet.

Pr-simplify kept the existing classifier and callback; no new owner, repair state, config, schema, or protocol. Removed incidental callback-formatting churn. Net change against the base: +29 production lines and +36 test lines, needed for classification, diagnostics, and boundary regression proof.

## Evidence

- Red on base `18a62d6ff93428f15b0801ba5efe4ef0452a8f15`: retention made all four fixture hooks undiscoverable; metadata rejection emitted no warning and handler rejection lacked the rejected filename.
- Green: `timeout 120s node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-retained-runtime-tree.test.ts src/hooks/workspace.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 36 tests passed. The retention regression discovers hooks in both source and retained trees and verifies metadata/handler link counts stay 1.
- Final replay after simplification: the two changed test files passed, 24 tests. File elapsed times: hooks workspace 34.51s (compiled worker preparation; test bodies under 1s), retention 0.878s. Native namespace consumer: 12 tests, 1.28s. CI seconds pending.
- Touched-file typecheck/lint passed: `timeout 120s node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json --type-aware --type-check --threads=2 src/hooks/discovery.ts src/hooks/workspace.test.ts src/infra/update-retained-runtime-tree.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-safety-inspected-files.ts`. Touched-file oxfmt check and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent shared autoreview of the complete local candidate against the base, now committed unchanged as `fe9736f847dea6cef37036574886cf4503df13d0`: Codex, P0–P2, complete / scoped-clean, no findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable in the documented locations. Hosted ClawSweeper has acknowledged this PR and is pending; no duplicate request was posted.
- **Live proof gap:** `timeout 45s crabbox warmup --keep --ttl 60m --timing-json` refused immediately: `provider=ascii-box requires ASCII_BOX_API_KEY`. Configured Boat/ASCII Box provider; no lease ID or run URL was allocated, and no lease needed stopping. title: fix(knowledge): Scribe controls hide cancellation and removal
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Scribe controls implying that cancelled work can resume and obscuring the difference between disabling an automation and removing it.

## User Impact

Scribes now offer **Disable**, **Stop and disable** for an enabled running automation, and **Enable**. Disabled status and outcome messages use the same terminology. **Remove automation…** names the separate deletion action and preserves the conversation. Its confirmation describes cancellation as a request, not an already completed stop.

The longer controls wrap within narrow screens instead of clipping. Scheduling, cancellation, permission checks, revision checks, and retained history are unchanged; **Run now** remains an explicit override for a disabled automation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing update owner persists `enabled: false` and cancels active work. Re-enabling does not resume the cancelled occurrence. The removal owner deletes the automation and requests cancellation separately. The view now describes those existing operations, without adding state or changing requests.

A one-line width bound lets the existing wrapping layout work with the longer action labels. No new styles, controls, or recovery flow are introduced beyond that bound and the presentation copy.

## Evidence

- **51 focused checks passed:** 30 Scribe-view cases, 16 Scribe-state cases, three disable/ownership-cancellation cases, and two real scheduler removal/disable receipt cases. The idle/running control regressions fail on main for the old labels and pass after correction.
- The real scheduler test now verifies that re-enabling leaves the original abort signal cancelled and does not invoke the runner again. An explicit later run is a new invocation. Separate existing owner tests verify abort and terminal records for removal and disablement.
- Actual-component browser flow covers running → disable → enable → remove confirmation, Cancel, and confirmed removal. It sends exactly two revision-bound `cron.update` requests and one `cron.remove`, with no extra run or chat request. Synthetic Gateway responses and runner edges only; no live Scribe, Knowledge store, or account was changed.
- Desktop and 400-pixel emulated-phone captures were inspected. The longer labels initially overflowed to 483.8px; the scoped width bound keeps all controls within 400px and retains the existing wrap. This is the production component/styles in an isolated minimal host, not the full app shell or native-device proof.
- Scoped TypeScript lint, plugin/core-test typechecks, formatting, i18n verification and diff checks pass. **Direct stylesheet lint remains red with the same 30 pre-existing diagnostics on main and the patched file**, compared by rule/text/column; no diagnostic was added, limit raised, or unrelated CSS changed.
- Measured checks: view/state group 3.14s; disable/enable owner file 39.11s including cold worker compilation (newly extended case 799ms); two removal/disable cases 39.27s including compilation (tests 841ms total). Remote CI and its timings are pending.
- Simplification: net three production lines (two formatting-expanded copy lines and one CSS bound), 29 test lines, and no net documentation growth. Internal state enums and existing helper contracts remain unchanged.

Before is verified main `bcfa6ca00c18fcc619aa1dbf3de301aceec0cd95`. Main through `18a62d6ff93428f15b0801ba5efe4ef0452a8f15` has no affected owner/presentation drift. This independent PR complements [#199163](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199163) and [#199259](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199259). Related [#195010](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195010) internationalizes the old Pause/Resume copy rather than correcting these effects.

title: fix(knowledge): queued Scribe runs are shown as running
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Knowledge Scribes reporting a queued automation as running before the scheduler reports that it started.

## User Impact

Manual runs and automatic first runs now report **Run requested**. The first-run list and detail show **in progress** or **Running now** only when the scheduler supplies a running timestamp. Scheduling, retry, permissions, and duplicate-run handling are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run action accepts an enqueue acknowledgement, while the view treated that acknowledgement and its local first-request marker as running-state evidence. The presentation now uses the already available scheduler state for that distinction. No new state, polling, requests, or execution paths are added.

## Evidence

- **46 focused checks passed:** 29 Scribe view cases, 16 Scribe state cases, and the existing real scheduler capacity regression. Three view tests fail on main at the intended requested/running boundaries and pass after the fix. They cover manual acknowledgement, first-run list/detail, transition to observed running, retry after refusal, and no repeated automatic request.
- The scheduler regression fills capacity, acknowledges queued manual runs while no queued job has executed, and checks their eventual execution after capacity is released. It reuses the real cron service and storage with synthetic runner edges; no live automation or model is used.

title: fix(logbook): capture pause is reported before confirmation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Logbook reporting capture as paused before confirmation, leaving the scope of Pause unclear, and claiming snapshots are being collected when capture is paused or off.

## User Impact

Capture controls now say **Pause capture** and **Resume capture**. Pending changes say **Pausing capture…** or **Resuming capture…** until the confirmed state arrives. The empty timeline no longer claims collection is active. A tooltip explains that queued snapshots can still be analyzed while capture is paused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The view previously displayed its optimistic capture flag as a completed outcome. It now compares the existing optimistic and confirmed values to select pending copy and a neutral status indicator. No new state owner, request, timer, persistence, or confirmation is added.

Pausing still affects new capture attempts only. Queued analysis and captures already in progress can finish. The shared Gateway-service scope and reset-on-reload behavior are unchanged and clarified in the guide. Existing focus, polling, request admission, rollback, and model-processing behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

- **44 focused checks passed:** 27 UI cases, 15 service/lifecycle cases, and two built-Control-UI browser scenarios (desktop and emulated phone). Held-request regressions fail before the repair for the premature paused/capturing claims; the main-baseline browser flow also reproduces the misleading control and empty-state wording.
- **Capture/analysis boundary:** the registered plugin handler pauses capture before an actual scheduler wake. No node capture is invoked, but a queued SQLite batch reaches the model boundary, reports analysis running, and produces a stored timeline card. Resuming through the registered handler allows the next capture. Node/model responses and seed data are synthetic; no live screen, provider, or account is used.
- **Presentation boundary:** real controls send exactly the pause/resume requests. A held pause response displays pending, not completed, status; confirmation adopts the response. Separate regressions cover pause and resume rejection, retained focus, disabled capture, polling, retired views, and ongoing analysis. The empty-state correction works while capture is paused or off.
- Scoped lint, UI and changed-test typechecks, formatting, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks pass. Canonical English is updated; translation memory is unchanged. Remote CI and its timings are pending.
- Measured checks: UI file group 1.61s; browser group 17.53s including its production build; backend file 45.88s including cold worker compilation, with the new registered-boundary case taking 606ms. The worker test exercises real service/storage ownership rather than mocking the decision being proved.
- Before: verified main `d6008485ec45269cd44cd0fd907735bc046d0ca1`. The final main check through `2f90c703bdf55ed99219100832b2e4c85ad5b0fc` found no drift in the affected owner/presentation paths. Matched screenshots use the actual Control UI, synthetic Gateway data, light theme, and a 1280×900 viewport, cropped to 970×330. The 400×900 phone flow was also inspected; it is browser viewport emulation, not native-device proof.
- Simplification: **net 14 production lines**, 198 test lines, and four documentation lines. The existing presentation owner uses one comparison of already available facts; execution and permission owners are untouched.

body:

Adding an item to a schema-limited settings list opens a blank text field instead of offering the choices OpenClaw already knows.

title: fix(ui): download notices claim completion before browser saving
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Knowledge source downloads and widget HTML exports claiming a file was downloaded when OpenClaw has only handed it to the browser.

## User Impact

The fallback notices now say the download started and direct users to browser downloads to check the result. Knowledge still reports completion when its save-file writer has actually finished. File contents, destinations, permissions, clipboard behavior, and export operations are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clicking a download link does not tell the page whether the browser saved the file. Both affected flows previously claimed completion even when Chromium explicitly refused the download.

Knowledge already knows whether it has a file writer: that path awaits the final close; the Blob fallback does not have a completion receipt. Its existing control now selects the appropriate outcome wording. Widget HTML fallback copy is corrected at its single presentation key. No new state, confirmation, browser capability, or persistence machinery is introduced.

Related: #195010 internationalizes Knowledge copy, but retains the unconditional “Original file downloaded.” outcome; it does not make this distinction.

## Evidence

- **45 focused tests passed:** 9 Knowledge control/UI cases, 35 widget export/card cases, and one built-Control-UI browser scenario. New Knowledge and widget regressions fail on verified main for the premature completion claims, then pass with the repair.
- **Real browser boundary:** the widget test uses the actual menu and exporter with an older synthetic document lacking the snapshot bridge. After the real timeout and HTML fallback, Chromium reports the download failed because the isolated context refuses downloads. The corrected notice still truthfully describes the handoff, rather than a saved file. There is no chat send.
- **Knowledge boundary:** actual download-control tests distinguish browser handoff from a pending, successful, or rejected file-writer close; canceling the picker fetches nothing. A separate Chromium capture clicks the production evidence component and observes the same browser-side refusal, with one correctly scoped attachment read. Only source bytes and file-writer responses are synthetic; the presentation and download handlers are production code. No live vault, account, printer, message, or job is used.

Browser screenshots alone are not the saving-boundary proof; the separate download failure and writer assertions provide it.

Fixes: main CI `check-dependencies` fails since #199138 because Knip reports `openssl` in `scripts/perf/web-push-measure.ts` as an unlisted binary.

## User Impact

No product-runtime change. The web push HTTPS benchmark still generates a fresh loopback certificate and retains normal TLS verification. OpenSSL must be installed in a directory supported by the existing system-binary resolver; an arbitrary PATH-only installation is no longer selected.

OpenSSL is a system tool, not an npm binary. The benchmark now resolves it through the existing `resolveSystemBin` helper (standard trust) instead of invoking a bare `openssl` command. This removes the statically named npm-binary edge without Knip ignores, baseline growth or dependency changes.

title: fix(ui): sharing reads falsely report no paired people
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Sharing options says “No paired people yet” when its first membership read fails, on both desktop and phone.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed read shows the real error without falsely claiming that the paired-people list is empty. Reopening Sharing options retries the read; previously loaded people remain visible if a later refresh fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both presentations showed the empty permissions section from the lack of a result, even when an error explained why that result was missing. They now use the existing error and accepted-result facts to omit that unsupported diagnosis.

No new state or recovery mechanism. Loading, accepted rosters, public-sharing confirmation, access restrictions and mutation admission are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real Control UI with synthetic mock-Gateway responses. Light theme; desktop 1280×900 and emulated phone 390×900. Before is isolated pinned main; after is that baseline with this independent commit.

**Desktop before — a failed read is also labeled an empty people list.**

![Desktop before: false empty permissions section below link sharing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1a07c37-8754-4286-b223-bcc536f85805)

**Desktop after — only the actual read error remains.**

![Desktop after: read error without an invented empty list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06dd36b3-b6fb-414c-ac2d-ae0f82f51ed3)

**Phone before**

![Phone before: failed roster read followed by no paired people](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1d639ea-9094-4ba9-a5ac-2fc93c85ba39)

**Phone after**

![Phone after: actual roster error without the false empty section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2271adb9-bb95-4a79-ab91-71144d3e1964)

- Both first-read regressions fail on isolated main and pass with the fix. They also exercise reopening to load the actual owner, then a failed later refresh that retains that owner; no sharing mutation is issued.
- All 57 focused sharing presentation and pane-owner tests pass, including command failure, accepted empty-state behavior, retained people/search, public-share confirmation and stale-result ownership. The same 21 strict-read diagnostic lines occur on baseline; they are not suppressed or claimed fixed.
- UI types, focused lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The isolated proof’s first setup attempt lacked existing plugin dependency links; no product result was claimed from that attempt. After binding the existing installation, the baseline reached the intended two failing assertions.
- Source/history reviewed: mobile Sharing introduction #176515, native asynchronous sharing #180316 and lazy desktop contents #180886. Self-review/pr-simplify: two production lines using existing facts, plus one 143-line two-surface browser regression. No helper, copied state, new copy or styling.

Independent draft for Vyctor’s review. Independent automated review and broad PR CI are not claimed complete. No merge or deployment requested.

title: feat: keep ask_user questions answerable after you start answering
body:
Closes #199174

## What Problem This Solves

An `ask_user` question can expire while someone is reading its choices or typing, losing the opportunity to submit the answer.

## User Impact

In the Control UI, clicking or tapping a question, Tab-focusing it, choosing an option, typing or pasting keeps it answerable until submission, Skip, or cancellation/end of the requesting run. Drafts survive blur and switching questions. Untouched questions retain the existing timeout (900 seconds by default, clamped to 30–3600 seconds). Secret questions retain their timeout. Terminal questions are never revived.

**CI remains red, not ready to land.** Current-head hosted performance passed, but WebKit history, automation navigation and PR-specific whole-shard timeout contribution remain **UNKNOWN**. The bounded paired hosted-load diagnostic did not reproduce navigation failure. The subsequent workload/acceptance audit found no further small representative workload capable of resolving those attributions under the existing limits; no additional diagnostic was run. No budgets or shared secret-submission behavior changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The existing Gateway question manager remains the expiry owner. `question.engage` uses the same answer authority as `question.resolve`; it stops scheduled expiry and records `expiryStoppedAtMs` only for opted-in, non-secret questions. Engagement shares pending-question continuation admission during restart/suspension drain.
- `ask_user` opts in with `stopExpiryOnInteraction`. At its wait deadline it inspects the original question and keeps waiting only when the Gateway stopped expiry. Harness-owned and MCP-form requesters do not opt in.
- The shared question panel reports trusted human input, excluding hover, automatic/programmatic focus, modifier-only keys, Escape and shortcuts. Another Control UI view reconciles with one `question.get` at its local deadline; engagement is not rebroadcast as `question.requested`, which would repeat web push.
- Additive protocol changes, since 2026.11: `question.engage`, optional `QuestionRequestParams.stopExpiryOnInteraction`, optional `QuestionRecord.expiryStoppedAtMs`. No new settings, stores, question categories or model-facing arguments.
- Latest simplification removes a temporary expired-ID collection and second loop, dispatching the same asynchronous reconciliation after local expiry mutation and carrying engagement forward directly: 2 additions, 6 deletions. No assertions or budgets removed.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- Native apps and TUI do not report engagement and can still display the original deadline. Inspected stable v2026.11.3 (`847611dc`) paths tolerate additive fields: Swift synthesized Codable; Android `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }`. Native runtime execution was unavailable; native engagement/presentation parity is out of scope.
- Failed engagement is reported once per prompt/client, retaining the original deadline rather than retrying on each keystroke. Separate owners/remounts can report again; this is not globally exactly-once delivery.
- Run/model-attempt timeouts still apply. Restart durability remains #167266. The model-facing timeout description is unchanged and describes untouched questions.

## Evidence

**Behavior:** isolated Gateway → Chromium → original `ask_user`, scripted local OpenAI Responses model, 30-second timeout. Base `663611cb` reproduced expiry after clicking/typing. Latest local candidate `74469d7ead45d44c00aa2184006ded0b093472dd` passed **5/5 in 268.75 seconds**, exit 0. Its tree matches published head `67ee0d65e7ef29fb17393d9b24cf5d6f2619b065` exactly. Each case crosses the original deadline and checks the Gateway record and original waiting tool outcome:

| Case | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Click, type, blur | Still pending; submitted `Teal` reaches original tool |
| Tab focus, option selection | Still pending; submitted `Green` reaches original tool |
| Programmatic focus followed by real paste | Paste engages; submitted `Teal` reaches original tool |
| Type, wait, Skip | Draft retained; cancelled; original tool receives `no_answer` |
| Untouched, hover/programmatic focus only | Expires normally; late engagement rejected |

**Focused checks and review:** prompt/shared-state/secret-store consumers **84/84**; UI types, targeted lint/format and `git diff --check` pass. Independent incremental autoreview against `dadf1777`: scoped-clean P0–P2, one pass; prior integrated whole-change review against merge-base `97dd78cc2cbd4f9dff1add734a2b316ac8d8bf31`: two P0–P2 passes. Prior unchanged-owner proof includes manager/RPC/suspension/ask-user/UI/inventory/planner tests, trusted-input Chromium 6/6, protocol registry/generated/native contracts/since guard and test-line ratchet. No production source changed during attribution follow-ups. The audit reconfirmed candidate/head tree equality and existing proof coverage; it was not a new test or review run. Local results do not make CI green.

**Review/acceptance audit:** no new human review or inline finding was present. The hosted ClawSweeper review remains stale; it is not represented as current-head approval. Its historical continuation-admission and execution-inventory findings are addressed in current source, and current-head hosted performance passed. Existing integrated/incremental independent review remains reusable. No changed path matches hard-tier CODEOWNERS; the current-head security guard explicitly requires no SecOps approval for this maintainer PR. `question.engage` retains `operator.questions`, session-write classification and selected-question mutation authorization, including guest participation checks. The change adds input handlers, not visible content/styles/layout, so no appearance-change screenshot gate is claimed. Qualified local real-Gateway proof is valid; the hosted skip below is not a reason to repeat the same acceptance solely for green.

title: fix: Devices misstates remote host scope and token reconnection
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Devices identifies a remote Gateway as “This computer” and promises automatic reconnection after rotating another device’s token without evidence that it reconnected.

## User Impact

User impact: people can identify which computer’s command policy they are viewing and understand what a cross-device token rotation confirms—and what may still require pairing again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inventory’s Gateway row and the command-approval target always refer to the Gateway host, whether the browser is local or remote. Their label now identifies the computer running OpenClaw without changing the target.

A cross-device rotation commits the new token, invalidates the old token, and disconnects affected clients. Its reply deliberately withholds the credential from the requesting browser; it is not a reconnection receipt. The dialog now reports that the old token no longer works and explains why the new token is not shown here, while preserving the existing re-pairing instruction. It no longer promises that the token will be revealed on the other device.

This changes four English entries only. Permissions, credentials, token delivery, connection handling, command-approval policies, and layouts are unchanged. The current-device token reveal and acknowledgment remain intact. The admin-locked device hint is not changed.

## Evidence

- Three existing tests fail on main for the intended remote-host/rotation claims, then pass after correction. All 97 tests across device inventory, command-approval presentation, and page/dialog lifecycle pass (2.84 seconds wall). Existing reactive-read warnings also occur on the baseline.
- The complete built-app flow passes before and after: open **Settings → Devices** with a synthetic remote Gateway, select a paired command target and return to the Gateway, then choose **Rotate** for another device and close the withheld-token dialog. Target changes issue the expected read requests and no approval-policy writes; rotation issues one mocked request and reveals no credential.
- The longer target label was also checked at a 390-pixel mobile viewport and remains readable with the existing responsive control.
- Keyless i18n, scoped lint, UI typecheck, formatting, and diff checks pass. Generated translations and the raw-copy baseline are unchanged. Self-review/simplification completed; no independent agent review or broad E2E matrix was run. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.

Before uses verified main **00636f0c7abc29e5c0af1bf75a16b1acda516401**. The matched screenshots are same-frame crops from the complete built Control UI at 1280 × 1000, light theme, with a fixed clock and realistic synthetic device/system responses. The Gateway selection uses the existing remote-connection fixture setup. No real device was disconnected, token rotated, or policy changed. The extra mobile image is an emulated viewport, not a native-host run.

title: improve(ui): keep the link reader to one view
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The link reader beside chat behaves like a small browser: every link from chat opens another tab (up to ten), the toolbar has its own **+** for new reader tabs, and Back stops at the first item of each tab. For reading a PR or issue next to the conversation, the tabs add management work without adding much; the first item also has no way back to the reader's start page.

## User Impact

- The reader shows one item at a time. Links from chat, or inside the reader, replace the current item and add it to Back/Forward history.
- **Back** from the first item returns to the reader's start page (the **Link reader** URL field), with the field focused.
- The reader's own **+** button, the ten-tab limit and its notice are gone. The side panel's general **+** (open another panel) is unchanged.
- In the side panel header the reader keeps one tab chip, like other panels; it shows the item title, or "Link reader" on the start page, and its × closes the reader.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the multi-tab owner and its callers instead of hiding controls: tab creation/selection/limit logic, the tab-limit copy, the toolbar new-tab action, the `newTab` field on the reader's toggle event, and the side-panel request to add a reader tab. History now treats index −1 as the start page.

## What stays available to plugins and integrations

- The link reader plugin contract is unchanged: descriptors, detail/preview/image methods and document shape are the same.
- Opening a link still uses the same toggle event; it no longer carries `newTab`, which only the Control UI sent and read.
- Docs for the GitHub reader and SDK host hooks now describe the single view.

## Evidence

- 18 focused reader, routing and side-panel test files (284 tests) passed, plus a final rerun of the 5 reader test files (57 tests). UI typecheck, focused lint, formatting and i18n verification passed. No broad CI or live Gateway claim.
- Actual Control UI with synthetic GitHub documents, dark theme, 1440×1000: opening a PR and then an issue from chat gives two tabs before and one after; Back twice returns to the start page.

title: improve(ui): remove Start if due from automation menus
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation menus offer **Start if due** next to **Start now**. It only starts a run when the schedule says one is already due, and the scheduler already starts due runs by itself, so in practice it almost always answers "not due" and does nothing. Beside **Start now** it reads as a second way to run a job, which it isn't.

## User Impact

The automation row menu and detail menu now offer **Clone** and **Delete**. **Start now** is unchanged and remains the one manual run action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Its only real use is testing an automation's condition check (`trigger.script`) without bypassing it. That is a developer task, and it stays available outside the Control UI.

- `cron.run` still accepts `mode: "due"` and the Gateway behavior is unchanged.
- `openclaw automations run <job-id> --due` and the `automations` tool (default `runMode: "due"`) are unchanged.
- Removed code was UI-only: the menu item, its `"due"` call path in the Control UI and the now-unreachable "not due yet" notice copy. No protocol, SDK or published package changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a plugin account badge that says “Connected” when OpenClaw has only read stored OAuth credentials, without checking the service.

## User Impact

The Accounts row now says **Sign-in saved**, so stored credentials are not mistaken for a working service connection. Sign-in, sign-out, credential storage, permissions, and tool execution are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account badge comes from a read-only credential-status projection. It can report an authorized record even when its access token has expired; refresh and service access happen separately. The badge now describes that known state. The completed browser sign-in dialog remains **Signed in**, and API-key rows remain **Configured** because those controls have different meanings.

The MCP guide now distinguishes the completed sign-in dialog and saved-account badge from an actual service check. No probe, warning banner, state owner, or new interaction was added.

- 3 focused OAuth storage tests passed. The added boundary case saves a synthetic expired token through the real credential owner, reopens storage, and reads the same ordered status API consumed by plugin inspection. It still reports stored authorization without making a network request or refreshing the token. This is not a mock supplying the asserted status.

title: fix(ui): keep pending publication and settings states readable

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stalled-looking publication controls, inconsistent publication details, oversized embedded-settings loaders, and saving feedback that is dimmed like an unavailable action.

## Why This Change Was Made

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Cmd+K forgets the last chosen Search or Compose mode after a page reload, and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter does nothing in Search instead of starting a new session.

## User Impact

Users can reopen Cmd+K in their last chosen mode and start a background session from either mode without replacing their current conversation or draft. The design, layout, and styling are unchanged.

The mode choice is remembered in this browser when local storage is available; it is not account-synced. Prompt text and attachments are not persisted by this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing mode owner now remembers explicit choices across reloads, including the loading-to-ready handoff. Automatic switches caused by long prompts or attachments do not overwrite that choice. Both the loading and ready palette again route Cmd/Ctrl+Enter through the existing session-creation flow.

## Evidence

- All three new browser regression scenarios failed on the original implementation and pass with the fix: mode restoration after reload, the ready macOS shortcut path, and the loading Ctrl+Enter handoff.

Tests cover mode restoration, ready and loading submission, and refusal feedback; stored preferences are isolated. ## What Problem This Solves

Live activity maintains a second tool stream in the browser. It only records while the Activity page is open and the browser tab is visible, shows nothing from before that, resets on reload, keeps at most 100 entries and hides tool arguments. Its output previews are not secret-masked. It looks like a log but is not one, and filling it required subscribing to up to 100 sessions' full message streams.

## User Impact

Remove that stream. Keep running/queued sessions as Current work, their conversation links, reconnect/error behavior, Sessions history and the durable Run inspector. Existing ?view=live links still open Current work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the stream renderer, collection/parser owners, controls, styles, copy and obsolete tests. Shared Chat tool events and sidebar narration are unchanged. Activity no longer requests full tool-message streams; the sidebar still legitimately requests narration.

- The Gateway still emits the same `session.tool` and tool events, and session message subscriptions are unchanged. Plugins, chats and loops that want tool activity should consume those events directly, which is what this feed did.
- Answer-candidate events are still produced by the Gateway; this feed was only the UI's view of them.
- Removed code was UI-only (the feed renderer and a browser-side event parser). No protocol, SDK or published package changed.

title: fix(ui): distinguish disabling automations from pausing runs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading “Pause” and “Resume” controls for automations: disabling an automation cancels its active run rather than suspending it for later resumption.

## User Impact

Users see “Stop and disable” for an enabled automation with a recorded active run, “Disable” when idle, and “Enable” when disabled. Re-enabling restores eligibility for new runs; it does not resume the cancelled occurrence.

Cancellation, scheduling, permissions, saved definitions, and manual Start now behavior are unchanged. No migrations or additional confirmations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing enablement update persists the definition and requests cancellation of active work. The shared row/detail control now describes that consequence, with matching tooltips and accessible names. Enabled/Disabled status wording also stays consistent in automation lists, filters, detail views, and desktop/mobile session summaries. An accepted update is not presented as proof that the run has stopped.

The label uses existing running-state evidence. The detail view reads the current selected-job facts, so the label changes when a run ends without replacing the control. No new state owner or operation was added.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

title: fix(ui): avoid empty-model warnings during discovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the model picker says “No models available” or “No models are permitted by your admin” while provider discovery is still running.

User impact: chat and New Session keep a neutral model label until discovery answers, instead of presenting a temporary empty catalog as a setup or administrator problem. ## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway can publish an empty model snapshot together with pending providers. The picker menu already treats that as unknown; its trigger did not. The shared trigger projection now withholds only the premature empty diagnosis. It adds no loader, banner, fallback model, refresh request or new state, and still asks users to choose when actual permitted options are available.

title: fix: model refresh fails with empty legacy Codex auth file

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes model refresh failing with a credential-migration error when an agent’s legacy Codex `auth.json` contains only `{}`.

## User Impact

An empty legacy auth object no longer blocks model discovery. No file removal, credential import, or configuration change is required. Real credential migration diagnostics and genuine discovery failures remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preflight previously treated file existence as evidence of unimported credentials. It now exempts only a successfully read, parsed empty object. The intentionally unauthenticated provider still reports unavailable/`refreshFailed`, confirming genuine failures are not hidden. No live credentials or inference calls were used.

Preserve the Markdown-reading capability deliberately added in #191136, rather than remove it. Reuse the existing form row for its label and padding, and cap the preview at 240 px. No new state, renderer, dependencies, or shared CSS changes.

title: fix(usage): show model attribution without stored session metadata
body:
Fixes #198488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing provider and model information in Usage session rows and exports when measured usage exists but session-level attribution is absent or incomplete.

## User Impact

Missing fields now use representative measured attribution without inventing a provider/model pair. Stored values remain authoritative. If one field is stored, the missing field is filled only from matching measured entries; if none match, it stays empty. No configuration, migration, or protocol changes are required.

For mixed-provider sessions, this fallback is representative metadata only—not attribution of every token or cost. Aggregate accounting and provider filters are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Initial row assembly only copied stored metadata. Packed overview summaries arrive later, and metadata restoration replaces report rows with visible rows while retaining their usage. One shared helper fills final response metadata after hydration/restoration and filtering/aggregation.

The helper selects the greatest totalTokens among eligible measured entries, keeping the first on ties. Eligibility preserves an existing provider or model. When neither field is stored, both come from the same dominant entry. Repeated application is idempotent and does not mutate source usage.

The response regression is a sibling test file because usage.sessions-usage.test.ts is at its line cap. It uses the existing isolated Gateway-methods lane. Documentation describes both representative attribution and partial-pair consistency.

## Evidence

- Base: 3ab80aba158a5c5488d9323f4352aa593fb9af1c (tree 7e4dc64cd2172b6045e63b7f35f5d38b5af13a34).
- Final candidate: 3ffbb5d752358a4b3500738ac7cc79fd4789f089 (tree 32cf975c2eb0b50588d8135fc10d5abc23516507).
- The Windows runtime proof below is supplied by @MertBasar0 and bound to afe57af5e5fdd7391263110cc8efd4dbb86a583d (tree 8393447bc9453ff991178b99a42920976a9189c5). Roboclaw did not execute those Windows commands. The final commit adds only 15 lines to one test file; every other repository file, including all production code, is byte-identical to afe57af5. The proof remains labeled with the commit actually built.
- Original RED/GREEN: detail, packed overview, and restoration failed on the pinned base due to absent attribution. Partial-pair consistency cases then failed on f303c818 (eight assertions across two tests) and passed with afe57af5.
- Final Linux verification: 53 tests pass across usage.sessions-usage.test.ts, usage-overview-report.test.ts, session-cost-usage-worker-overview.test.ts, usage-overview.test.ts, and usage.row-attribution.test.ts. Runner wall time: 22.01 seconds including preparation; attribution test bodies: 0.840 seconds. CI time is not yet available.
- Final test-file lint, format check, Gateway-methods test typecheck, and git diff --check pass. Prior core production typecheck and full-candidate review remain applicable to unchanged production code.
- Independent OpenClaw Auto Review: the full afe57af5 candidate was P0–P2 scoped-clean; a fresh review of the final test-only delta against afe57af5 is also scoped-clean, with no findings.

### Reporter measurements and explicit regression coverage

Thanks to @spacenet-Pop-OS for the [follow-up live-store measurements and requested controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198488#issuecomment-6875408820). Their live-store counts, mixed-provider frequency, and client-workaround observations are reporter-provided evidence, not numbers reproduced by this PR's Windows fixture.

Both controls are in src/gateway/server-methods/usage.row-attribution.test.ts:
- **fills final detail row attribution from dominant measured usage without changing accounting**
- **fills final overview row attribution from dominant measured usage without changing accounting**

The existing **missing** case supplies two providers with 10 and 30 tokens and requires the 30-token entry's provider and model, while independently checking aggregate totals. The new **null-model-usage** case supplies totalTokens=0 and modelUsage=null and requires both row attribution fields to stay empty. Detail additionally asserts that the returned modelUsage is literally null; packed overview represents it as zero model entries and keeps attribution empty. Existing usage=null and modelUsage=[] controls remain. The null fixture is intentionally outside the current optional-array TypeScript summary type, with a localized documented expected type error; no production type was widened.

### Publication status and remaining verification

UI E2E passed locally on Windows as reported by @MertBasar0 below; this is not a passing CI claim. The inherited unused-export failures are documented rather than suppressed. Preflight found no competing #198488 PR. Main b9dacb674914f74b57155edc02cdd13f8f963486 still has the unchanged row assembly, loading, and restoration defect.

### Real behavior proof — Windows, built Gateway

A built Gateway answers the real `sessions.usage` RPC through `openclaw gateway call`. The Claude turns that create the session usage records are served by a **stub Claude CLI**, so no real inference runs. The RPC, the usage pipeline, session deletion and the overview projection are the shipped code.

Setup, identical for both builds:

title: fix(codex): avoid repeated discovery for unavailable plugin apps
body:
Related: #99071 (similar discovery symptoms; no historical disk-I/O attribution).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Codex discovery delays between messages when a configured plugin app remains missing or inaccessible.

## User Impact

User impact: unchanged conversations no longer force hosted connector discovery on every message for the same unavailable plugin apps. An unavailable app can take up to one minute to be reconsidered automatically; installation, explicit invalidation, and manual refresh remain immediate. No configuration changes or migration are required, and unavailable or policy-denied apps remain unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Readiness repair reuses a successful, covering forced refresh in the existing app-inventory cache for one minute, including a negative result, and joins an equivalent forced refresh already in flight. Account/thread isolation and target coverage still apply. Non-forced cold reads do not suppress the first forced repair; activation, current native policy checks, and explicit refresh retain their existing paths. There is no second cache manager, new configuration option, or permission-policy change.

Explicit runtime refresh also invalidates cached thread readiness in that account/runtime. A scoped thread refresh leaves siblings alone. Key construction and invalidation share the existing cache owner and unchanged thread-ID encoding.

## Evidence

Committed regressions use credential-free external I/O fixtures through the production config builder, manual command handler, and warm thread lifecycle/client owners. Acceptance: bound unchanged unavailable-app discovery without suppressing explicit refresh or relaxing admission.

| Scenario | Before | Current candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three unchanged config builds, missing/inaccessible app | 3 forced reads on base | 1 |
| Three unchanged warm lifecycle turns, inaccessible app | 3 forced reads on base | 1 |
| Three unchanged builds, ready app control | 0 forced reads | 0 |
| Successful runtime refresh within the negative thread cooldown | Next warm build still excluded the connected app | Both cached same-runtime threads reconsider and admit the available, policy-allowed app |
| Other account/runtime snapshots and current native denial | Must remain isolated/enforced | Remain isolated/enforced |

- Original discovery regressions are red on `cfa40212f9c6ce442a36e6ad6b8df07eec9b6ae5` and green with bounded reuse, including the warm-lifecycle entry point with synthetic native I/O.
- Follow-up regression is red on production source matching reviewed head `2ffb9d003a19049a2db1b3a2b762f55bd1b49bd8`: the actual `/codex plugins refresh` handler succeeds at the runtime key, but the next production thread-config build still returns an empty app policy. With the clock frozen inside 60 seconds, the fix recovers two thread keys, leaves other canonical account/runtime keys untouched, and still enforces a subsequent native denial without more inventory work.
- Red/green command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/command-plugins-readiness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "repairs warm thread readiness after runtime refresh" --reporter=dot`. A separate cache contract protects encoded sibling-thread scope during targeted invalidation.
- Current focused runs: **440 tests passed across 14 Codex files**, including the four requested modules, activation/manual refresh, migration, read-only/scheduled policy, lifecycle and run attempts. Prompt-prefix stability: **14 passed**. Total: **454 passing tests across 15 files**.
- Scoped repository typecheck covering all eight changed TypeScript files and imported consumers, oxlint on those eight files, nine-file formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh independent Auto Review through **P0–P2**, using `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. It covered the complete nine-file local candidate against `cfa40212…` (diff SHA-256 `13d10df931e6920eb6f0564f3b59429603b1bba58efef414b1191ba58415595a`). This supersedes the earlier P0-only local assessment; the reviewer did not independently execute tests or verify live native integration.
- Author simplification: the existing invalidation operation owns runtime/thread invalidation; the existing encoded thread-key constructor moved to that same cache/key owner and all callers migrated. No second manager, new option, generation/fence, or test-only production seam. Whole-candidate delta against the base: production +77/-20, tests +261/-3, docs +11.

Native contract inspected at pinned Codex 0.164.0 revision [6aaac694](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/apps_processor/installed.rs): non-forced installed reads reuse the native snapshot, while forced reads refresh hosted runtime tools.

Limits: synthetic lifecycle/work-count proof, not an authenticated Gateway/model/connector run, macOS incident reproduction, or measured live latency/disk-I/O improvement. This does not establish a cause or fix for a separate WebSocket reset loop. Broad [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199120/checks) is running; local proof is not a CI pass.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen.

title: fix(ui): describe condition-triggered automations accurately
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Conditional automation guidance reverses the 30-second minimum, describes total checks as failed matches, and says a one-time automation stops on a match even though its task must succeed.

## User Impact

User impact: the form now states the accepted interval and successful-task requirement accurately, while history explains condition checks without inferring that an empty retained history means nothing ever matched.

Scheduling, limits, trigger scripts, delivery, and persistence are unchanged. English copy only; other locales use the normal translation refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

“An interval of at least 30 seconds” matches the existing validator. Trigger counters include matches, and evaluation errors can appear before a task starts, so the empty state no longer says all checks were nonmatches or that history starts only after task execution. Scheduled no-match checks stay distinct from manually requested history. “Last matched” describes the existing timestamp, not task success. Setup guidance keeps script limits and the successful-task requirement visible.

This is a literal-copy correction with no new production logic. Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

title: fix: explain why installed plugin tools are missing from sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing or misleading guidance when a plugin validates and registers successfully but its tools are absent from a session.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and operators can distinguish registration, profile selection, explicit policy, and runtime availability instead of repeatedly rebuilding or reloading a valid plugin. Tool selection, permission defaults, and existing allow/deny behavior are unchanged; no migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Connect the quickstart and missing-tool checklist to the existing session diagnostics, manifest profile grants, the two callback signatures, and reload handoff behavior. Complete diagnostic inventories with manifest-declared candidates using the existing policy explainer, and project owner-scoped manifest profiles in the tool catalog. New scaffolds test their own declarative callback through public package imports, without depending on internal SDK test helpers.

The diagnostic addition does not import skipped plugin runtimes or execute their factories merely to explain policy. A policy-allowed tool absent from the preview remains unavailable with construction and health explicitly unconfirmed. The existing full preview retains its normal construction behavior.
