title: improve(ui): soften New Session composer and tray shadows
body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the New Session page in dark themes, the context tray under the composer was drawn with a hard dark outline, so a secondary surface looked heavier than the composer it belongs to.

## User Impact

User impact: in dark themes the tray under the New Session composer no longer casts its own shadow, so it sits quietly behind the composer. In light themes the composer's soft shadow is slightly lighter. Sizes and positions are unchanged. The phone layout's tray is unchanged; the lighter light-theme composer shadow also applies at phone width.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tray used the theme's small shadow token. Dark themes set that token to 25–90% black, which suits menus but outlines a tray that is meant to stay secondary. The tray keeps the token in light themes, where it is faint. The composer's diffuse light-theme shadow on this page goes from 4% to 3% black at rest and from 6% to 4% while the editor has focus; its tight edge shadow is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Before / after

Actual New Session page on the mocked Control UI dev server (synthetic data), 1440 × 1000 emulated viewport at 2× scale, Absolutely theme, editor focused; matching crops. "Before" is `main`.

**Dark — before**

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents cannot install a published ClawHub Template through the OpenClaw setup helper, even though the Gateway already supports reviewing and adding it.

## User Impact

Agents can request `template_review` and `template_install` without gaining shell access. Installation retains exact-plan and dependency consent, the original administrator/request lifetime, cancellation and revocation checks, and the existing delegated-change approval policy. Missing authority, consent, or Templates enablement returns an actionable blocker. Trust warnings require exact human approval even under Full Access.

Results disclose the actual agent and workspace, complete/partial state, readiness requirements, dependency installation/reuse receipts, and automation outcomes. A failed automation is not reported as enabled. No live Gateway configuration was changed during this work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper now hands Template operations back to its host. UI RPCs and the helper share the same typed Template request owners and installer, rather than introducing another installation path. The host presents the full reviewed plan in its exact-operation approval and retains the requesting administrator through deferred decisions, including native/MCP-backed helper turns. No new configuration or persistent state is introduced.

## Evidence

### Revision after ClawSweeper

- Repaired the conversational handoff identified on prior head `14bed9de9374c2c1a1cc8859c9dc7fc03754a779`. The latest host Template output now travels through the existing model turn-input owner for embedded and resumed native helper turns. Actual installation outcomes replace the review reference; the reference never grants approval or authority.
- The two-turn regression first failed against the prior implementation with `Template result never reached the model input`. It now derives the installation arguments from the actual next model input, rather than the caller copying plan JSON. Direct conversational approval and delegated approval paths are covered, along with post-install result continuity.
- Six affected test files passed, 125 tests across four shards (110.25s wrapper), including twelve real tool/engine/approval/installer scenarios and the existing native/MCP and prompt-prefix contracts. External model/registry I/O remains fixed in those tests, not live proof.
- Production and Gateway-method test types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Consolidated duplicate entry-point coverage and fixture file-writing scaffolding. Net test growth is now **487**, down from 499 while adding the missing continuation/direct-chat coverage. The existing-policy allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/199064-template-helper-continuation.txt` covers the remaining **87** lines so the twelve distinct authority/consent/cancellation/retry scenarios and native/receipt contracts remain covered. The global 400-line allowance is unchanged; the exact ratchet passes.
- Final `GOMAXPROCS=2 pnpm build` passed (110.4s build phases). An initial overlapping build/review attempt did not produce valid proof after snapshot verification failed; stopped build ownership was reconciled, and the final build and review ran sequentially against quiescent source. Earlier Control UI budget warnings are not represented as a clean budget check.
- Fresh independent Auto Review, P0–P2, full local candidate over base `f8761b0c13ec3c4c27786a907c271b98a2dee760`: scoped-clean, no findings. Reviewed patch snapshot SHA-256: `8c2c83451c7de168a2b78929e164c6cc2c2cf4b19e3074207d604e34141776fc`.
- Retained unused-file qualification from before this repair: the production scan passed with zero entries; the full-tree scan reported the unmodified `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-floor.retention.test-support.ts`. This is not claimed as a current full-tree pass. Existing unchanged installer/account-ownership and recovery evidence from the prior qualification is retained, not represented as freshly rerun.

### Current-main integration proof (2026-11-15)

The reviewed integration candidate is `19f846bc791b3606eed8c6fae590e98cccaa8597` (tree `c555a19ed6d06be019fcdb728fb049d0d51138b1`), incorporating main `95a877918f181f3ebc91aa91283cbdbb29bb4b4b`.

- Preserved the shared typed planning/application request owners while retaining landed [#198521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198521) preview errors with `details.mutationAccepted: false`. A failed preview therefore remains an explicit no-effect result for owner-routed callers.
- Fresh focused validation passed **114 tests across seven files and four canonical shards**: preview/application handlers, the complete setup-helper approval/denial/cancellation/revocation/trust/changed-plan scenarios, original requester and native inference ownership, actual partial dependency/automation receipts, plugin activation policy, and native/MCP tool handoff. Both forbidden and unavailable preview-error regressions passed.
- Core production types, the affected Gateway-methods/agent-tools/Templates test-type checks, all changed-file lint/format checks, and whitespace checks passed. Fresh independent coordinator review found no actionable findings; the tracked worktree remained clean.
- The real-model/live-registry proof and full package build below remain evidence for original head `0f1b2110d1e47261730e673183a6db8c40fbec46`. Relevant helper/installer/result inputs are unchanged by the integration; the added behavior is the preview error detail above. These earlier runs are not represented as a fresh candidate full build or hosted CI pass. Hosted checks for the published integration remain subject to the native landing workflow.

### Live installation proof (2026-11-15, exact head `0f1b2110d1e47261730e673183a6db8c40fbec46`)

- Before: the helper could not review/install a published ClawHub Template. The committed two-turn regression failed before this change because the review never reached the next model input.
- After: an isolated Gateway with a real configured model reviewed the live published `myfitnessclaw@0.2.5` release, returned its proposed agent/workspace and exact plan, requested approval, and installed after `yes`. The actual host result was `status: complete`, `readiness.ready: true`, with no remaining requirements. A later model turn accurately reported the actual result.
- Independently read the saved ordinary agent entry and workspace. `AGENTS.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `SOUL.md`, assets, avatar, references, skill and templates were present; `SOUL.md` contained the published Template instructions. Public registry and inference were live, not mocked. This release declares no plugin/MCP/automation dependencies; those branches retain existing integration coverage.
- A retired manifest release was correctly refused. An earlier scratch setup using a symlinked state path exposed the separate issue fixed by [#198520](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198520); its partial result was reported honestly. The successful proof used a fresh canonical-path environment. No personal/work Gateway or channel state was used.
- Fresh full `GOMAXPROCS=2 pnpm build` passed in the exact-head proof checkout. UI budget warnings remain warnings and are not claimed as a clean budget check.

### Inherited CI qualification

[Run 43628130143, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43628130143) remains failed: six updater cases hit `SQLite read-only worker Unable to deserialize cloned data due to invalid or unsupported version.` The updater owner, readonly transport, fixtures, runner, and dependency inputs are identical between its actual main parent and tested merge. A separate pinned Bun-to-Node serialization experiment reproduced that exact error; same-runtime controls passed.

Main already repairs builtin mock dispatch in [84579cbdcc63](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/84579cbdcc6373edf365d459b07e8d088e372f97). All six exact cases pass the newest completed main run [43763625500](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43763625500): [candidate/fresh-doctor cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43763625500/job/132964131205), [Windows cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43763625500/job/132964131165). A local baseline attempt had different pending-recovery/timeouts and is not claimed as an identical CI reproduction. Landing uses the repository's native inherited-failure qualification; neither failed PR CI nor full main CI is described as green.

title: fix(ui): model picker favorites tab and locked account control
body:
Related: #198623 (follow-up picker polish).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three model-picker annoyances: the Default model can never be starred, people who browse from Favorites land on a provider tab every time the picker opens, and a locked account control still shows a chevron that does nothing.

## User Impact

Users can star any model, including the Default model. The picker reopens on Favorites when that was the last tab chosen and the current model is starred; otherwise it opens on the current model's provider, so the picker never opens on a tab that hides the model in use. While the account cannot change (for example during a reply), it reads as plain text instead of an inert menu. No migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Favorites previously excluded the Default model entirely, so its row had no star even on hover. The opening tab is still decided by the existing picker panel preparation; it now also considers one remembered choice (Favorites or not), stored in the browser next to the existing provider order and captured in the opening snapshot so stars and tab clicks never move the open view. Closing the picker now returns to that opening tab. This replaces the old behavior where any browsed provider tab survived dismissal, even one without the selected model. Expanded "All models" lists still survive dismissal. The account trigger hides its chevron and hover treatment while disabled; its existing lock conditions are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Unit: 59 tests across favorites, picker, session controls and search, including new regressions for starring the selected Default model and for reopening Favorites only when it was chosen last and holds the selected model (also after choosing the model's provider or another provider). The tab regression fails without the change.
- Browser: all 37 Chromium picker tests pass. The previous "retains provider toggles after closing" cases now assert the new reopening rule.
- Real app (Chromium, synthetic Gateway data): default-row hover star and Favorites save without a model change; Favorites reopens after close and after reload; a provider choice and a different provider both reopen on the selected model's provider; during an actual `chat.send` the account is disabled with no chevron, and the idle account menu still opens.
- UI typecheck, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, stylelint and whitespace checks pass.
- Before images are current `main` (`9d922ea9402`); After images are this branch, same scenarios.

| Reopening after choosing Favorites | ![Before: opens on the provider tab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dd3c41c-9bec-4c74-aa60-7d6efb54046f) | ![After: opens on Favorites](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4384860f-61dd-4290-a620-dfa2ea6ecd94) |
| Account during a reply | ![Before: inert chevron](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b027c933-cce8-4c31-95b1-6c720e405bde) | ![After: plain label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46329709-369c-4e47-b3d1-8ee0c7e5f414) |


## Maintainer validation

CI on `a4d1c5a97871` passed all functional and security jobs. The only failure is the asset-size gate and its aggregate: largest JS, Chat boot JS and New Session boot JS each add 167 gzip bytes, 103 bytes beyond the 64-byte variance allowance. The maintainer-authorized size exception applies to this landing; no budget or product behavior was weakened.

The remaining interaction findings are fixed: the selected model's provider retains its account control independently of the preferred opening tab, and Escape clears a search without changing the browsed provider. Only closing the picker resets that tab.

The existing composition E2E now exercises both paths at 1280px and 390px. Both assertions failed against the incoming head and pass with the repair, including opening the account menu and the later model-selection request. All three bundled composition cases and the selected UI test run (613 cases across 60 files) pass. UI typecheck, scoped lint/format and stylesheet lint pass. Independent review found no additional issue in the corrected source.

title: improve(compaction): skip unused snapshot byte accounting
body:
Related: #196550

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction repeats conversation classification and computes transcript byte sizes that its full-fidelity planning does not consume.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Short planning/rendering worker tasks, bounded Gateway payloads, and overlapping summary calls are preserved. **The new `a03b` repair reduced CPU and RPC time on the bounded workload below, but overall performance and landing are NOT accepted. Burst lifecycle process RSS median increased 2.74%, and worker-local observed heap p95 increased 34.37%. Keep this draft pending explicit owner judgment on memory and all other adverse moves, plus normal CI, mergeability, and authority gates.** The original `12ad` negative comparison remains immutable. No universal CPU benefit is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing meaningful-content result when preparing conversation-anchor facts. In the planner’s existence-only check, stop classifying after the first real conversation message while still visiting every message and checking cancellation. The shared classifier’s full lookback behavior remains unchanged for other consumers.

For unbounded SQLite snapshots only, the shared snapshot producer now skips two eager model-size projections per navigation row (2N evaluations). An explicit size request still uses the original size SQL and existing bounded batches. Bounded snapshots and their navigation cache, PostgreSQL’s fused projection, omission handling, snapshot/fence/identity checks, cancellation, and native-writer durability remain unchanged. No work is moved outside the measurement boundary.

No cache, retained transcript payload, new configuration, changed summary selection, or persistence/authority change is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Original classification scope:** independent static owner/caller review and local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings on `12ad15841a49778e9d9c0b6b9af1511fe5e20d0a`. The completed original 30-observation result below applies only to that head.
- **New repair source:** reviewed repair commit `7ac21e5d1b14d49e97170bd03a68738165b04c55` is published through empty metadata commit `a03b3d25606cd3c8664a6fc069c66e081f829b81`. Both have tree `94e6b6dd8350b4f1b82d9ceb08dc4e6de8dcd951`; source is identical. The exact two-file repair patch SHA-256 is `7c60e0afad0cd31cba985dab630099ff3380b71bf0b66e7116cc920cc47af437`.
- **New SQLite work-count proof:** the actual snapshot operation on original `12ad` fails the intended zero-eager-sizing assertion with six executed `octet_length` calls for a header and two inline messages. The repair performs zero eager calls, then exactly two calls when those messages’ sizes are explicitly requested, with exact byte values preserved. This proves removed SQL sizing work, not overall CPU savings.
- **New repair validation:** 53 focused tests passed across snapshot, seed, actual compaction-source integration, model-context, and selected lifetime/authority/refusal cases before a fixture type correction. The corrected selected work-count test then passed (one selected, four intentionally skipped), without double-counting it as additional coverage. The correction uses the existing `isIndexedSessionEntry` predicate; the original TS18046 failure is retained. Final independent, local autoreview, and parent hands-on reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Targeted production/test type graphs, lint, line-cap, format, and diff checks exited 0.
- **New repair normal build:** normal `pnpm build` exited 0 in 181.1 seconds with Node 26.12.1 / pnpm 12.15.0, before commit at `12ad` plus the exact reviewed `7c60…` patch. Source/dependency hashes remained unchanged. This is not an `a03b`-bound native performance build. The secretless build used network-disabled private isolation, eight CPUs / 16 GiB, default heaps, absent NODE_OPTIONS, enforced zero task swap, and the existing physical exact-lockfile dependency closure. No shared dependency reconciliation or guard override occurred. Its TypeScript experimental-API warning remains retained; Control UI content-cache reuse is not a new UI-budget pass. All original warnings and failed setup/gate receipts remain retained.
- **New commit-bound native build:** canonical `a03b` sourcePerformance build exited 0 on Node 24.22.1, eight CPUs / 16 GiB, default heaps, absent NODE_OPTIONS, zero task swap, network-disabled build/runtime, and private frozen-lock dependencies. Dependency preparation was separate: secretless normal public-registry frozen-lock installation with lifecycle scripts disabled. Separate v1/v2 offline preparation failures remain preserved; they were not relabeled successful builds.
- **New workload qualification:** committed workload `007777bbf9917bdc62a488b9e348990fc06c6a04` passed 12 head contracts. The same reviewed new assertions on the base produced four expected failures across three methods. Normal commit hooks exited 0 and all three human coauthor trailers were preserved.
- **New native series completed:** six separate diagnostic qualifiers passed, then all 30 planned original light, unprofiled observations completed with controller exit 0. No observation was rerun, discarded, corrected, or pooled. Parent hands-on source/native/aggregate auditing and an independent result audit rederived all 15 metrics across all 30 observations with no actionable P0–P2 numerical or integrity discrepancies. This is NOT overall acceptance or a memory waiver.
- **Remaining gates:** exact-`a03b` broad CI is unproven. Dirty mergeability was observed; the current pre-edit metadata read returned unknown. No base integration or conflict repair has been performed. Overall performance and landing remain pending explicit owner judgment on memory and every other adverse tradeoff. A scoped request to resolve this is not acceptance of regressions or merge authority.
- **Original classification red/green regression:** the exact new classifier test on base `8857554b178506f962068509227e5c10ebe6cc8a` fails only its two intended work-count assertions (`expected 2 to be 1`), while all 11 existing cases pass. The candidate passes all 13 cases. This proves eligible-content reads fall from two to one, not overall CPU savings. The native observer does not separately count these helper calls.
- **Original `12ad`: 94 candidate tests passed** across the classifier, safeguard-source, safeguard, actual worker compaction-source integration, context-report, and prompt-prefix stability suites. Tests ran serially through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1` on Node 26.12.1. No separate Bun-runtime proof is claimed.
- For original `12ad`, formatting, the three-file line-cap ratchet, targeted lint, production and changed-test type graphs, and the normal `pnpm build` all exited 0. Task-private physical frozen-lockfile installations supplied the required `oxlint` 1.89.0; the shared installation was not reconciled, and no hook or content guard was overridden. Validation receipts, all 15 retained log hashes, source/dependency integrity, and exact build identity were independently audited. The earlier local hook/tool-version failure remains retained.
- **Build caveat:** the successful normal build printed eight Control UI asset-budget violations and dynamic-import warnings. This is not a passing UI-performance check. No baseline attribution was established, so these warnings are not labeled inherited or caused by this patch.
- **Original `12ad` native proof completed:** six separately tagged qualifications and all **30 original comparison observations** completed, controller exit 0. All imports/physical identities, native compactions, exact 8,192-byte seed/post-RPC follow-ups, warm-target invariance, source/build/workload/fixture bindings, default-heap/no-swap checks, independently observed main-thread CPU brackets, and graceful cleanup passed. No observation was rerun, discarded, corrected, or pooled with earlier evidence.
- **Original `12ad` broad CI remained unproven:** the complete observed exact-head inventory had six successful dispatch/metadata/scope/actionlint checks and 102 skipped checks. Skips are not broad-suite proof. The original #196550 110-observation comparison is separate and does not validate this patch.

### NEW a03 repair protocol — predeclared method, now completed

title: feat(ios): load older chat history without losing your place
body:
Related: #192232

**Stacked on #192232** (Marvinthebored) at `d3363988721e329abce8d2d6dbd6db51b82f120e`, open and not modified. The publisher squashed that head, merged cleanly with `main` `1ac07b333`, plus the authored change into one commit, so #192232's changes appear here: **do not merge before #192232**; rebase after it lands. Authored delta only: `git diff $(git merge-tree --write-tree d3363988721e329abce8d2d6dbd6db51b82f120e 1ac07b333) f1a51ca1d6b9930a6bce819a80f9e73f332f7b79`.

## What Problem This Solves

Native iOS chat shows only the latest history page; older messages cannot be loaded, so long conversations are cut off at the top.

## User Impact

Scrolling toward the top of a chat loads earlier messages automatically, and the message you are reading stays exactly where it was. A small, localized **Show earlier messages** control at the top of the transcript appears only when older history exists; it covers chats too short to scroll and is reachable by VoiceOver and Switch Control as an ordinary button. At most three earlier pages stay in memory: the farthest page is dropped and reloaded on return, and returning to the latest message releases them. Grouping, word fade, sidebar animation and live-edge behavior are unchanged.

**Draft for the Mac verification loop:** native build, tests, screenshots and performance are **pending**; no Swift toolchain was available, so no Swift test has run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native chat discarded the `olderCursor`/`newerCursor`/`windowReset` fields `chat.history` already returns; the iOS transport already forwards opaque cursors. No Gateway protocol change.

- **Separate owner.** `ChatOlderHistory` keeps the pages read above the live tip. The live delta/outbox owner keeps the tip; a full tip read only reports its new first row and boundary, so trimmed rows join the newest page. A tip that no longer reaches the pages ends them rather than showing a gap.
- **Staleness.** A page is admitted only while its session, route/cursor generation and boundary are unchanged; session/agent/route/branch switches, rewind, reset and compaction cancel reads and discard pages. `windowReset` means the boundary is unusable, not exhausted: pages and boundary drop until the next full tip read.
- **Sizes from source.** Pages are the Gateway's default 200 rows (`limit ?? 200`, `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-handler.ts`) under the iOS transport's existing 256 KiB cursor budget. The resident window is three read pages (≤600 rows, ≤768 KiB of page payload) beside the tip. One action reads at most three consecutive pages that add no visible rows, matching Control UI (`docs/web/control-ui.md`).
- **Bounded window.** Reading up past three pages drops the newest read page and shows only the read pages (no live edge or live work at their bottom). Scrolling down rereads with `newerCursor`, drops the farthest page above, and reattaches at the tip. Jump to latest or sending returns to the tip.
- **Reader position.** `ChatReaderPageAnchor` records realized rows' content positions before a page change and, after List lays it out (a scroller layout sentinel, since equal-height swaps keep the content size), shifts the offset by their content-relative move. It never undoes the reader's scrolling and ends once settled; at the live edge the existing follower owns the offset.

<details>
<summary>Accepted edge cases and integration points</summary>

Accepted edge cases (rare, recoverable):
- A full tip read that no longer meets the pages (e.g. reconnecting after a page of new messages) ends them.
- Rows the tip hands to the newest page while the reader is away from the live edge stay until they return, like the tip's own delta growth.
- A chat shorter than two screens does not auto-load, because the reader never crosses the threshold; the top control covers it.
- Question cards and the subagent-wait row keep their place at the bottom even while a window has left the tip.
- The shared protocol's default cursor read returns the tip; only the iOS Gateway transport and the paged fixture read pages, and the control is iOS-only.

Integration points with frozen drafts (not edited):
- #198114: `readerPresentationMessages` stitches `olderHistory.presentation(tail:)` (an input to its prepared transcript); `runGroups` hides live content while detached; iOS cells get `.chatReaderRowMarker`.
- #198244: `onChange(of: scroll.followTarget)` releases pages at the live edge; `handleTranscriptDistanceChange` ignores a detached window's bottom; the control is the first List row.
- #198247: page reads call `decodeMessages` on the main actor; join its decode phase, then recheck `ownsHistoryPageRead`.
- #198251: `invalidateHistoryCursor` discards pages; a proven same-conversation handoff may keep them.
- #194235: no overlap.
</details>

## Evidence

Checked here:
- Two local P0–P2 autoreview passes on the authored delta. The first found four P2s: three fixed (equal-height swaps skipping the offset hold; a stale read leaving paging stuck; snapshot rows duplicated after a window returned — the last two with regressions), one accepted above (tip-transferred rows). The second pass was clean.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify`: `changed=false` after baseline.

Authored, **not run** (no Swift toolchain here):
- `ChatOlderHistoryTests`: boundary decoding, seam stitching across tip slide/gap, snapshot de-duplication, three-page eviction/reread/reattach, replaced-session and moved-boundary reads discarded, `windowReset` ending pages (not exhaustion).
- UI tests on the synthetic 2,000-row `--openclaw-paged-history-fixture`: accessible labeled button in a two-row chat loads the page above; a held page lands above the reader's row within 1 pt.

### Pending Mac verification

At `f1a51ca1d6b9930a6bce819a80f9e73f332f7b79` with Xcode/Swift 6.3 and a task-owned simulator:

~~~sh
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = f1a51ca1d6b9930a6bce819a80f9e73f332f7b79
swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'ChatOlderHistoryTests|ChatHistoryDeltaTests|ChatReaderScrollStateTests|ChatViewModelTests' --no-parallel
scripts/lint-swift.sh ios
scripts/format-swift.sh ios
pnpm native:i18n:verify
pnpm ios:build
IOS_SIM="<task-owned simulator UDID>" pnpm ios:test \
  OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testShortChatOffersEarlierMessagesAsAnAccessibleButton \
  OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testEarlierPageLandsAboveTheReaderWithoutMovingIt \
  OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testKeyboardOpenPreservesTranscriptAndFollowsLiveEdgeAfterSend \
  OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testSwitchingChatsOpensAtLatestMessage
IOS_SIM="<task-owned simulator UDID>" pnpm ios:test OpenClawTypographyTests SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests
~~~

Red controls, in a separate checkout of this head (build failures don't count): (1) restore `ChatView.swift` to the dependency head — both new UI tests must fail; (2) remove only the `.chatReaderRowMarker(...)` line — the reader-place test must fail with `READER_ROW_MOVED_WHEN_PAGE_LANDED`.

**Screenshots pending:** before/after of the top of a long chat, the **Show earlier messages** control visible, the transcript after a page loads (reader row unchanged), and VoiceOver focus on the control.

**Performance pending:** on the 2,000-row fixture (`--openclaw-screenshot-mode --openclaw-initial-tab chat --openclaw-initial-destination chat --openclaw-paged-history-fixture`) and a long real Gateway chat, scroll from latest to first and back. Record offset drift per page landing (≤1 pt), resident rows (tip + ≤600), peak memory and Animation Hitches versus the dependency head on the same device; include detached-window scrolling and VoiceOver activation.

Contributor credit: Vyctor Brzezowski and Mike Nguyen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6b98dedd-1923-4f79-837e-5d48ac84b6c4)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b013216a-052c-492f-a343-435ba0963784)

title: fix(nodes): keep tools beyond the first 128 in agent catalogs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: tools disappear from an agent’s catalog when a paired node publishes more than 128 valid plugin or MCP tools.

## User Impact

Users can discover and call the complete policy-approved inventory within existing resource budgets, rather than an alphabetically selected first 128. No new configuration, migration, or protocol bump is needed. This is not unlimited capacity: schema size, memory, CPU and direct-provider context still matter.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove both independent truncations—the node MCP producer and Gateway snapshot. Removing only one leaves the other deleting tools. Keep validation, ordering, names/deduplication, current command policy and approval, pairing/connection ownership, plugin-ID trust, disconnect withdrawal and deferred search/prompt behavior. MCP’s 1 MiB/descriptor and 10 MiB/catalog guards, bounded acquisition and the 25 MiB Gateway frame limit remain unchanged. Generic plugin inventories do not acquire the MCP-specific 10 MiB budget.

**Best defense of 128:** more descriptors cost allocations, wrappers, search entries and sometimes provider context. But count is a poor resource proxy. MCP already acquires its complete bounded catalog; the Gateway retains the full declaration and normalizes/sorts/deduplicates before truncating. Eight legal nodes with 128 tools each already incur 1,024-tool aggregate costs. A per-node cutoff silently removes functionality without representing a measured budget.

### Historical defense-first measurements

Audit source: `0daab29f77cab03cf551c60761138585dd0b49d9`, separate from the implementation/proof heads below. Five interleaved baseline/relaxed processes, two warmups and five repetitions per ordinary cell: 25 samples, serially on a shared AMD EPYC 9555 Linux host, Node v26.12.1. Only the two count constants were temporarily raised for measurement; actual producer/Gateway/agent/catalog cardinalities were asserted. Timed composition: descriptor production → inventory serialization/parse/validation → snapshot → agent materialization → catalog/prompt construction.

| Accepted tools | Typical median / p95 | ~9 KiB schemas median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 128 | 1.21 / 1.34 ms | 3.99 / 4.76 ms |
| 129 | 1.23 / 1.39 ms | 3.90 / 4.32 ms |
| 1,024 | 9.35 / 12.34 ms | 39.67 / 55.94 ms |

Scaling is measurable; no discontinuity appeared at 129. Small decreases are noise, not speedups. Eight baseline-legal nodes × 128 cost 9.33 / 11.92 ms typical and 40.13 / 58.26 ms with ~9 KiB schemas. Separate single-process retained-graph probes added ~42.55 MiB heap for eight near-1-MiB descriptors versus 14.88 MiB for 1,024 typical descriptors, including fixed initialization/probe state—not per-tool memory estimates. The MCP Code Mode prompt stayed 861 bytes with two visible controls; hypothetical direct-definition JSON grew from 42,113 to 336,897 bytes, not measured provider tokens/payloads.

**Limits of this evidence:** synthetic shared-host workloads are not low-memory-device qualification. A heavy 256 × ~64 KiB generic-schema run hit the conservative local memory stop; its partial record was excluded from successful aggregates and not retried with more memory. No claim covers arbitrary schemas, unbounded inventories or arbitrary plugin code.

## Evidence

Implementation base: `2f4ae4d3284bf17ad4930cf6770dac14c025bfc1`. Original tested candidate `386563cfd2a572720309fae339ea6f8b8964cfb6` and first published head `a3b33ab4568865b40bc79d2d50b92015f0e24519` share tree `08cfbee0e9588edf43dc3cc51993b3fe2f44b6e1`.

Current published head: `a82a81db1d6cdd8109bed7b8874047d546a53577`. Follow-up commit `072c509c2ef8074cc9bb70d7856fc8927a832b65` adds only the opt-in live fixture and required test-line allocation; the publisher’s metadata-only child has the same tree `fb9baf10fa6da9825a139d671578828888710ea1`. **Production code is unchanged from the tested `a3b33` head.**

### New: real Gateway + real node-host process + actual model turn

title: fix(ui): load native plugin catalogs beyond 64 entries
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: native plugin UI stops loading for the entire catalog when the 65th eligible plugin is enabled—even when all 65 are policy-disallowed and none would execute browser code.

## User Impact

Operators can load native UIs beyond 64 when they fit the existing asset/revision budgets, and every browser activation can still be reported and inspected. The cap removal itself adds no config or migration step; the tested latest-stable upgrade follows the existing Doctor migrations described below. This is not an unlimited-capacity guarantee: expensive trusted plugin code can still block the browser, and additional plugins consume the same retained-revision headroom.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin count is a poor resource proxy. Keep the guards that measure retained resources; remove the unsupported count cutoff and its coupled catalog, diagnostic, report, and per-client activation-array ceilings. The browser already submits one complete activation report; leaving that schema at 64 would let 65 modules activate but reject their whole receipt request. The separate installed-plugin reload batching contract and 128-client status limit are unchanged.

The strongest case for 64 is bounding eager capture/import/initialization and leaving four complete generations in the 256-revision pool. Those costs are real, but the measurements below do not identify a cliff at 65. One large or slow plugin can cost more than many small ones; a policy-disallowed plugin executes nothing. Removing this indirect cap does not remove the 64 MiB retained-asset or 256 retained-revision safeguards, per-file/build/path checks, auth/policy, activation deadlines, or old-revision retention. A full revision pool still refuses new builds while preserving working advertised revisions.

## Evidence

### Mounted product flow and latest-stable upgrade (new evidence)

The shipped Control UI was mounted against a real isolated, token-authenticated Gateway. A fresh Chromium page followed the real dashboard login handoff, imported actual immutable HTTP assets, mounted the installed native plugin page, and clicked its **Read live browser activation receipts** button. That fixture page displays the real Gateway status response through the public native host API. WebSocket frames were observed, not intercepted or replaced; no mock Gateway, application-context injection, or direct catalog/report owner calls were used.

| Real product phase | Catalog modules | Actual report requests / receipts | Stored status receipts | Native asset GETs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Released 2026.11.3 (847611d), 64 fixtures | 64 | 64 single-receipt requests / 64 | 64 | 64 × HTTP 200 |
| Same release/state, 65 fixtures enabled | UNAVAILABLE | 0 / 0 | no activation | 0 |
| Candidate 1c4bdbd8, same upgraded state, 65 fixtures | 65 | **1 batch / 65** | **65 unique, all activated** | **65 × HTTP 200** |

All three browser connections completed the real protocol-4 handshake as an authorized operator. A separate unauthenticated GET of a candidate native asset returned **401**. All 65 packages passed the canonical native UI builder (106,990 combined entry bytes); these are deliberately small, benign proof fixtures, not an arbitrary-plugin capacity guarantee. The candidate's served production entry bundle matched the freshly built bytes: SHA-256 `4cea15961f13f88108728503e8f728dd15e10694a7fb0c6dab78954d7a9ffb2d`.

**Upgrade qualification:** npm's current latest tag was 2026.11.3. Its real state first ran successfully with 64 fixtures; enabling the 65th produced the captured failure. Starting the candidate against that same state correctly required the existing agent-database migration from schema **27 to 42**. With the task Gateway stopped, candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` completed; external-supervisor policy kept service lifecycle management disabled, and the log explicitly confirmed service management was skipped for the non-default state/config. Candidate startup and the mounted 65-plugin flow then passed. This is a distribution replacement plus supported Doctor exercise, not a test of the updater's download/installation transport.

The original 65 enablement entries and allowlist members, response prefix, agent identity, and workspace artifact survived unchanged. Shared-state and agent-database integrity checks returned `ok`; one owner profile and one profile identity remained. Doctor made two expected, explicitly observed upgrades outside this cap change: it added `skill-workshop` to the allowlist to preserve its former built-in behavior (`src/config/skill-workshop-plugin-migration.ts`), and enabled/allowlisted `openai` for the already configured OpenAI model. No model inference or external-provider behavior is claimed. All task Gateways were stopped cleanly after capture; no live service or shared configuration was changed.

**Before — released 2026.11.3 with 65 enabled fixtures**

![Before: the actual Control UI shows Plugin panel unavailable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63c9156e-6956-4a2e-bd23-1b076705549b)

**After — candidate with the same upgraded state**

![After: the actual mounted native page displays all 65 real Gateway receipts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74ebbd0f-1f51-433c-886f-476860ccfbd9)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/412b7c0f-32f0-4ce0-8cc9-ba5fde4816c6

The 11.96-second video shows the 64-plugin positive control, the 65-plugin released failure, and the upgraded candidate's 65 receipts. Idle footage was trimmed; it is not a latency comparison. Screenshots compare released and candidate product builds, not a claim that unrelated sidebar styling changed in this PR.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized execution receipt</summary>

```json
{"candidate":"1c4bdbd8af7103741da072a9ff97146e680a4a32","latestStable":"2026.11.3 (847611d)","auth":"real token-authenticated WebSocket, operator, protocol4","mockedResponses":false,"fixtureBuilds":65,"stable64":{"catalog":64,"singleReportsAccepted":64,"storedReceipts":64},"stable65":{"catalog":"UNAVAILABLE","assetGets":0,"reports":0},"candidate65":{"catalog":65,"reportBatches":1,"batchReceipts":65,"storedUniqueReceipts":65,"allActivated":true,"assetGets200":65,"unauthenticatedAssetGet":401,"pageErrors":0},"upgrade":{"agentSchemaBefore":27,"agentSchemaAfter":42,"doctorExit":0,"originalFixtureEnablementPreserved":65,"originalFixtureAllowlistPreserved":65,"responsePrefixPreserved":true,"agentIdentityPreserved":true,"workspaceSha256":"843c4d9f3bade5688ef0ef1b5213fd65a9cbab83ef5f086af345cf445184968d","ownerProfiles":1,"profileIdentities":1,"sharedIntegrity":"ok","agentIntegrity":"ok"}}
```

Commands: canonical `build:ci-artifacts` / `ui:build`; `buildPluginControlUi` + `writePluginBuildManifest` for each fixture; released/candidate foreground `gateway --port <task-port> --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`; real `dashboard --json` login handoff; Playwright visible-page actions and passive WebSocket frame assertions. Existing byte/revision/path/policy/deadline regression coverage was reused rather than rerunning an unrelated stress matrix. Initial fixture metadata/observer and source-loader-owner setup failures were excluded, not counted as product failures or passing proof.

</details>

### Current CI qualification

[The remaining failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43619052935/job/132528509881) is the shared Swift Periphery intersection: `OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccountError` at `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccount.swift:227`. Both producer builds/scans and artifact provenance checks passed; the intersection emitted a finding and exited 1. Its actual checkout was merge `457dba2f85cd7ee4125a7791d60d6f8ffa0c3b78` (PR head into main `8857554b178506f962068509227e5c10ebe6cc8a`). The implicated file has identical blob `57485a1a374f3af1726f39b129668eaaef5ffa86` on the implementation base, PR head, and that CI main parent; this PR changes no Swift, workflow, or scan script. This initially established source-unrelated provenance. A later completed [main-branch job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43620917710/job/132532509861), on main `989f4a6d1e4096461fc6c4fbae993f56f3b02a6e`, reports the same `struct OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccountError` intersection failure and exit 1; its log was read directly. The exact-head `openclaw/ci-gate` checks pass, while this separately reported inherited Swift job remains failed; this is not an all-green CI claim. The declaration is explicitly thrown at line 208, so no unrelated deletion or scanner suppression is included. CI remains red; nothing is merged.

### Why remove this number?

Prior empirical audit, baseline `0daab29f77cab03cf551c60761138585dd0b49d9` (not this PR’s implementation base): real asset-capture owner plus a Chromium harness using the real native runtime, loader, HTTP asset handler, report validator and receipt owner. Typical fixtures: one 8 KiB benign ESM entry plus CSS per plugin. Large fixtures: eight reachable modules totaling about 128 KiB plus CSS. One discarded warmup and five samples per cell, alternating ascending/descending counts. Shared Linux EPYC host; warm filesystem; fresh owner records/browser contexts.

| Workload / median | 64 | 65 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Typical catalog capture | 163.02 ms | 158.42 ms |
| Large catalog capture | 504.76 ms | 507.73 ms |
| Typical browser activation | 114.70 ms | 106.60 ms |
| Large browser activation | 353.90 ms | 348.10 ms |

There is no measured discontinuity at 65; small apparent improvements are shared-host noise, not speedups. The relaxed audit admitted, activated and stored exactly 256 receipts at 256 candidates; 512 candidates admitted only 256 because the independent revision guard remained active. Conversely, 64 valid candidates with 3.75 MiB entries admitted only 17 before the actual 64 MiB budget refused 47. Count 64 neither expresses those byte costs nor guarantees initialization latency.

Caveats: benign synthetic plugins, loopback network, five samples—not arbitrary-plugin safety or a tail-latency SLO. The browser harness composes real owners over HTTP with synthetic connection/auth context; it is not a full Gateway WebSocket/auth handshake, mounted Control UI flow, agent/model, constrained/mobile, or slow-network benchmark. The cross-build baseline/relaxed audit blocks were not interleaved A/B; same-build 64/65 comparisons are the relevant evidence.

### Fresh implementation proof

Implementation base: `2f4ae4d3284bf17ad4930cf6770dac14c025bfc1`; tested implementation commit: `ba50e97207c5a982ca81cd704b1a96100fc8bdf7`. Published head: `1c4bdbd8af7103741da072a9ff97146e680a4a32`, an additional publisher commit with the identical Git tree (`f66ffb372cf24b222441b3ecc625d17006779f6a`); no source changed during publication.

- Base reproduction: 64 real on-disk fixture builds list successfully; 65 fail with “Native Control UI supports at most 64 active plugins.” The 65-plugin and 65-diagnostic reproductions fail at that exact guard before the fix; the receipt harness was subsequently consolidated into the existing live-client/auth table. The original generated report validator rejects a 65-receipt array.
- Final owner/browser proof: 65 real on-disk 8 KiB builds yielded **65 unique catalog modules, 65 actual Chromium activations, 130 asset requests and 65 stored receipts**, with no page/runtime errors (one warmup and one measured run; functional proof, not a new performance claim). The unchanged runtime sends the complete receipt array through the regenerated validator and real report handler.
- At 65 plugins, successive changed-build reloads admitted **65, 65, 61, 0, 0** new revisions: the unchanged 256-revision pool fills exactly, all 65 last-working modules remain advertised, and refused builds produce diagnostics. The existing 64 MiB retention/old-asset HTTP regression also passes.
- Focused validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/plugins-validators.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; final owner **32/32** and protocol **13/13** tests pass (44.44 s and 0.906 s file wall time). The unchanged `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-runtime.test.ts` consumer passed **28/28** (3.29 s). The Gateway file includes compiled-worker preparation (34.27 s) plus the existing HTTP/auth/retention boundary coverage; the actual test portion is about 4.4 s. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.
- Gateway-root test typecheck passes: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json --noEmit`. The standalone `gateway-protocol` build, including declarations, passes. Canonical Gateway validator regeneration/check and formatting pass; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Known pre-existing checks are not labeled green: package typecheck produces six identical diagnostics on the base and candidate (native-protocol declaration, memory-host fixture, mermaid URL import, JSON.rawJSON library, qrcode declarations). Targeted lint’s only remaining diagnostic is the unchanged `schema/plugins.ts` 704-code-line file against its 700-line limit; the same diagnostic is reproduced with the base source. No new exceptions or suppression were added. Broad PR CI remains separate proof.

### Review and simplification

The change deletes one admission policy and aligns four protocol arrays; it introduces no scheduler, cache, configuration knob, batching layer, or replacement magic number. Production logic shrinks by four lines; schema field/receipt validation remains unchanged. Against the base: authored production +4/−8 lines, generated predicate +1/−2, tests +62/−15. The duplicate receipt harness was removed in favor of the existing live-client/auth table. One new policy regression and the expanded existing live-client/auth table cover complete 65-plugin catalog/report/status cardinality and policy diagnostics/settings-only exclusion; the existing protocol report test now accepts 65 while retaining its malformed/empty receipt checks.

Fresh independent shared autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the full final candidate against the implementation base (identical patch committed as `ba50e97207c5a982ca81cd704b1a96100fc8bdf7`): `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings; the reviewer inspected the owning Gateway/report/runtime context but did not execute tests. title: fix(plugins): accept link readers with more than sixteen hosts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin's link reader disappears when its descriptor declares a seventeenth valid host—even seventeen copies of one host were rejected before deduplication.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can declare all supported exact hosts in one reader instead of splitting identical metadata into artificial groups of sixteen. No configuration or migration is needed. Large catalogs still consume memory and linear lookup time; removing this count does not establish unlimited safety.

## Why This Change Was Made

The strongest defense of sixteen is bounding one descriptor's validation, bytes, and host comparisons. But it does not bound aggregate resources: the API already admits 4,096 hosts as 256 descriptors, owned by one plugin and sharing one read method. That layout uses more bytes, retained memory, registration and refresh work than one descriptor containing those same hosts. Rejecting seventeen duplicates further separates raw count from retained work.

Measurements show continuous cost, not a cliff at sixteen. Remove the maximum from the registrar, wire schema, and canonically generated runtime predicate. No replacement integer, option, cache, index, or lifecycle redesign.

Retained safeguards: nonempty arrays; exact lowercase DNS syntax, name length 253/label length 63; order-preserving deduplication; method syntax/length 128; anchored compilable pathname regex/length 1,024; URL length 8,192, HTTPS, no userinfo/nondefault port, exact host/path matching; loaded/enabled plugin filtering; same-plugin advertised read-method ownership/scopes; matching registry generations; server-side authorization. Client matching grants no source access. Transport limits are not an aggregate catalog-memory budget.

## Evidence

**Hosted review remains blocked, not complete.** [ClawSweeper's attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/43620019015) stopped at input-safety validation with no verdict. Supported sanitized diagnosis succeeded, but the material remains unclassified; a maintainer must qualify it before re-review. New proof does not release or bypass that hold.

### Real Gateway and authenticated production UI

[Readable trace, committed fixture, and two GitHub-hosted screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199027#issuecomment-6881794589).

- A real disposable Gateway loads a real local plugin with **17 exact hosts**. The browser uses the normal login handoff and the production UI served by that Gateway; the served bundle hash is checked. No WebSocket responses or capability snapshots are mocked.
- Clicking the first and seventeenth hosts renders real registered-method responses. **Two clicks produce two browser detail RPCs.** Gateway authorization rejects a client without operator.read; the plugin independently rejects an unsupported host.
- A real plugins.reload replaces the final hostname without restarting the Gateway. The existing browser automatically receives the entire replacement list, still 17 hosts. The retired host is refused server-side; the replacement document renders.
- **1 E2E passed** (15.29-second invocation; 4.07-second test body), **27 discovery/ownership tests passed**. Full product/UI build and targeted E2E type/lint/format checks pass. Owned Gateway, profiles, clients, and browser were cleaned up.

Runtime source: **103b9eafc865fbbc858a39a9da69367edd5e6f35**. The follow-up **958e47f2e4839f9a9c4ac1cad4430a1ccbebc3a5** adds only the regression fixture and its execution inventories. Published head **53254bad4a6f61241f3505fc06d75431308c5e90** is its tree-identical metadata child; production code did not change. History/backend documents are synthetic, with zero model turns or external-service calls: this proves actual authentication, plugin dispatch, render and live refresh, not a vendor integration or performance bound.

### Base-red regression and focused checks

On base **2f4ae4d3284bf17ad4930cf6770dac14c025bfc1**, the new discovery regression fails as intended: neither seventeen distinct hosts nor seventeen duplicates advertise a reader. Fixed: final cardinality seventeen, duplicates reduced to one, and acceptance by the exported production validatePluginsUiDescriptorsResult. A direct validator probe was false before predicate regeneration and true after it.

**10 gateway and 18 UI-routing tests pass**, covering malformed hosts/URLs, scope/ownership rejection, registry replacement, routing and complete host-list refresh. Also passed: gateway-root/UI-app typechecks, targeted lint/format, gateway:validators:check, protocol schema/Swift/Kotlin generation, protocol package build/public-registry type contract, and diff sanity.

Reproduce the new flow:

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/link-reader-host-count.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

### Historical capacity experiment, separate from the E2E

Investigation at **0daab29f77cab03cf551c60761138585dd0b49d9** composed real registrar → scope/ownership projection → serialized catalog → Chromium catalog/matcher. Five serial repetitions, seven warm batches; typical 20-character and maximal 253-character common-prefix hosts; first/last/miss assertions. The exploratory variant changed only the count maxima.

| Prior maximal-length fixture | 16/one descriptor | 17/one descriptor | 4,096/one descriptor | Already-legal 4,096/256 descriptors |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Browser final-host match, median µs | 4.025 | 4.150 | 417 | 440 |
| Reader-array JSON bytes | 5,365 | 5,621 | 1,049,845 | 1,373,185 |
| Retained browser fixture heap delta, bytes | 36,292 | 36,564 | 1,148,496 | 1,440,244 |
| Node registration, median µs | 12.67 | 12.97 | 1,523.44 | 2,355.90 |
| Capability refresh, median µs | — | — | 292.27 | 721.26 |

Heap includes fixture/catalog/URLs/compiled pattern, not pure host-array memory. p95s were batch-mean percentiles, not individual-event tails. Fresh 16/17/4,096 resolver measurements on the implementation reproduced byte counts; maximal-length medians were **4.075/4.175/422 µs**, versus **440 µs** for the legal split layout; 4,096 run medians ranged 381–460 µs. title: feat: support mobile desktop handoffs for blocked tasks
body:
Related: #198864
Builds on #196951 (merged).

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent is blocked on a human-only computer step, mobile users need to reach the exact task desktop, act, and return control without repeating the task or choosing an unrelated machine.

## User Impact

This **draft for validation** adds task-bound desktop handoffs to the shared question flow and native iOS/Android chat. A new request opens view-only, takeover stays explicit, and **Ready to recheck** returns to the original bounded wait for fresh same-target verification. Opening, hiding, reconnecting, backgrounding or rotating is not completion. Desktop input remains disabled until primary pixels paint.

**Before ready:** Colin/tester still needs current-head native builds/tests, matched iOS/Android screenshots, the full real-agent/human/control/continuation loop, and physical-device responsiveness/performance qualification. Historical native checks are not current-head evidence. Initial scope is eligible cloud environments and existing authorized routes; no host/node handoff parity, permission broadening or durable Gateway-restart pause is claimed. Android certificate-pinned embedding refusal remains intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the merged required-action owner, existing request/session/run identity, Gateway desktop admission/arbitration, shared noVNC renderer and authenticated native hosts. The native apps present the same admitted source rather than introducing another renderer, task ledger or control manager. iOS embedded-page failure/reload recovery and bounded shared setup recovery support the same journey.

The first-image observer is instance-local and pinned to noVNC 1.7.0 internals; dependency upgrades must recheck that private rendering contract. Metadata-only updates cannot mark a blank desktop ready. A desktop may disappear after admission; existing viewer availability checks show that recoverable failure and the required action remains unresolved.

One integrated draft is intentional so the tester can use one Gateway/UI/app checkout. The required-action prerequisite is already on main; this PR does not duplicate it. No release, deployment or landing is requested.

Co-authored with @Solvely-Colin.

**New integration checks:**

Android model generation also ran locally twice despite the original isolation plan; do not describe all of that historical proof as cloud-only.

Full Gateway/UI/native builds, native visual evidence, complete live human/CUA flow, device performance, and broad CI on this integrated commit remain pending. Existing shared screenshots are historical component evidence; matched new native captures are assigned to the validation handoff.

<details>
<summary>Validation and capture handoff</summary>

Use the draft’s exact head, not a moving branch. Build the Gateway + Control UI and both native apps from that same recorded head, using owned state/devices and an existing authorized cloud desktop. Do not disable TLS pins, borrow another person’s simulator/AVD, or put credentials/tickets in logs or media.

title: fix: show linked Telegram messages as the same person
body:
Closes #197730

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes linked Telegram messages appearing as a different person from the same user's Control UI messages.

## User Impact

Explicitly linked human channel messages use the person's profile name and portrait, and appear on their side of the conversation while retaining a visible channel source. Unlinking removes the association on subsequent reads; linking the channel to someone else does not relabel earlier messages. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Gateway display pipeline now checks the current exact channel/account/native-ID link against the message's recorded canonical requester before private requester metadata is stripped. A separate display association reaches the renderer; the stored observation, transport, participant grouping, typing identity, ownership, and authorization remain unchanged. Unsupported historical rows, bots, Shared Owner, and ID collisions stay separate.

The same association owner serves history pages, quoted messages, individual reads, pending inputs, deltas, and HTTP history. Live linked-author events request an authorized history refresh rather than broadcasting a profile association to every observer. No new persistent state or schema is introduced.

title: fix(ui): retry dictation recordings when transcription returns no text
body:
Related: #195982

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Control UI dictation recording disappears when transcription finishes without usable text, leaving no way to retry the same audio.

## User Impact

User impact: Retry recording resends the captured audio without reopening the microphone, and recovered text returns to the draft for an explicit Send. Discard recording and Escape release the recording.

Recovery is memory-only in the current tab and draft: reload, draft replacement, or another recording discards it. Existing usable-preview text recovery is unchanged; this does not claim to recover audio after preview text was already committed or close every part of #195982.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture session retains its encoded audio until text is recovered or the recording is discarded. The existing dictation owner retains an empty result for explicit retry, while the lazy status component presents retry/discard controls. Each retry creates a new Gateway transcription session through the normal authorization path and never sends a chat message automatically.

The final-transcript grace period starts after an admitted replay finishes uploading and the provider closes, so a slow upload cannot discard the eventual transcript. No persistent storage, configuration, credential, Gateway API, or microphone-selection changes.

This preserves the merged listening feedback and lazy loading from #198424 / #198643. It does not import the separate initial-drain status work in #196063.

title: fix(telegram): preserve linked identity in private topics
body:
Related: #194625

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes linked requester identity being dropped when an ordinary Telegram message arrives in a bot-private DM topic.

## User Impact

Private-topic messages retain the same host-admitted requester and operator context as unthreaded DMs. Existing account, sender, role, scope and revocation checks remain unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

The complete reported Telegram → native agent → GitHub publisher read and WebChat comparison has **not** been reproduced end to end. This PR repairs the independently reproduced ingress mismatch, not a claimed reproduction of the reporter’s custom installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram ingress descriptor used `resolvedThreadId`, which excludes ordinary bot-private DM topics. The finalized message context already uses the canonical `threadSpec.id`. Their mismatch causes the host’s exact-conversation check to reject the handoff before binding requester/operator context.

Use the same canonical topic ID at the ingress producer. This is a one-line production fix; it does not relax the host check or any GitHub publisher authorization guard. The existing regression now covers a forum topic, a private DM topic and an unthreaded DM. No new helper or authorization owner is introduced.

title: improve(telegram): partially reuse auto-local voice transcription across accounts
body:
Related: #154663

## What Problem This Solves

Multiple Telegram bots in one Gateway repeat the same local speech-to-text subprocess for a shared group voice note before independently checking spoken mentions.

## User Impact

Matching accounts can reuse one auto-discovered local transcription, including near-concurrent arrivals, while every account retains its own attachment access, authorization, mention admission, and transcript echo. Multiple addressed bots can still respond. No configuration changes are required.

This is a **partial auto-local optimization**, not complete coverage of #154663: provider-backed transcription, explicitly configured/custom CLI commands, caller-owned execution/cancellation or fetch authority, and cross-Gateway coordination remain independent. No live-model latency or RSS improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing media CLI owner shares only immutable, attachment-index-free computation results after each caller's bounded media read. Equivalence includes the message/topic/chat, audio bytes, executable identity, effective arguments, environment, working directory, and limits. The launched path preserves discovery's symlink/.. traversal.

Each configuration generation retains at most 64 pending/completed computations; successful results are reusable for 15 seconds with lazy expiry cleanup. Failed, empty, and oversized results are not retained. Per-account processing cannot be deleted or combined because it owns admission and delivery, so the small bounded computation cache is the remaining shared responsibility.

## Evidence

- Native Telegram handler/SQLite/broker/loopback Bot API fixture: the same four-account workload launches **3 STT subprocesses before → 1 after**. Alice, Bob, and Dave each reach preflight; unauthorized Carol does not. Only addressed Alice and Bob dispatch replies. The shared-preflight baseline failed on 3-versus-1 work; the native Telegram baseline also failed on three subprocesses. Both absolute and relative symlink/.. regressions pass with the change. The final account-order comparator was separately retested.

title: fix: keep Gateway available during optional plugin hook conflicts and invalid restarts
body:
Related: #85695

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a running Gateway draining into an invalid config restart and an optional plugin's conflicting old/current hook permissions preventing an otherwise valid core Gateway from starting.

## User Impact

Operators retain authenticated control access while the affected plugin stays inactive, without restoring stale permissions or discarding newer settings. Ordinary SIGUSR2 restarts reject invalid disk config before draining or canceling pending channel reloads.

The cold-start exception is deliberately narrow: opposite boolean values for a plugin's retired `allowPromptInjection` and current `allowPromptModification` keys. Resolve the permission values explicitly, then run Doctor or save the corrected config. Other invalid core authentication/access settings and arbitrary malformed configs still need their existing repair paths; this does not close every case in #85695.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime readers share a plugin-local quarantine projection with activation policy. The source config, includes and last-known-good remain unchanged; strict validation and writers still reject the conflict. The degraded projection is never promoted as healthy. Existing signal settlement owns preflight and cleanup, including SIGINT/SIGTERM arriving during a slow preflight. Update-owned handoffs retain their own admission checks.

title: fix(webchat): keep replies in the active conversation
body:
Related: #198388

## What Problem This Solves

The requested fix must make replies visible and persistent in WebChat AND deliver them to the original Telegram chat/topic with its exact transport thread preserved. The current draft repairs local WebChat routing only and does not yet implement that complete outcome.

## User Impact

Required outcome: a Telegram-origin conversation opened in WebChat delivers progress/final tool replies to both the WebChat transcript and its authorized original Telegram chat/topic, without changing the topic, account, or recipient and without duplicate messages. **This dual-surface behavior is NOT IMPLEMENTED by the current draft.** Pure WebChat, native Telegram, explicit destinations, opt-outs, and unrelated conversation boundaries must remain intact.

**Draft:** dual-surface implementation and its owning-entry/channel proof are pending, along with current-head required CI and completed ClawSweeper review. This PR is not ready to merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admitted turn now owns message-tool execution routing, while session-derived routing remains an ambient fallback. WebChat source admission selects the existing internal reply sink. Dashboard-authorized external reads retain their existing grant despite the new local source marker. Source completion and group-thread attribution use the same admitted account and thread.

## Evidence

The checks below cover the previous local-only candidate at `5ec70fe2283926ab6335f9d43bc10301c689b9a6`. They are retained evidence, **not acceptance proof for the corrected dual-surface requirement**.

- 450 focused tests passed across 17 suites: the requested eight message-tool/reply suites (279), outbound contracts/execution/mirroring/routing (115), and dashboard-read/hosted-transport/current-prompt consumers (56).
- The source-routing regression fails against base production for Telegram- and Discord-shaped WebChat sessions, then passes with the repair. This proves incorrect external route selection, not a live Telegram API failure. A separately discovered dashboard-read regression also has red/green proof.
- Core and affected test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed, including declarations and the Control UI. Its UI budget report emitted advisory size/request-count warnings; those warnings are not claimed resolved by this routing change.
- Auto Review of the complete candidate against `45b3fb10691ef02911a0ebb9e59060b239d09812`, with full routing/authorization, source-mirror, and group-thread context: P0–P2 `scoped-clean`, exit 0, no remaining findings. The earlier dashboard-read finding was repaired and rechecked.
- Added a real-Gateway Control UI regression for WebChat prompt → host admission → message tool → local progress → reload persistence. Only inference is synthetic. It typechecked, linted, and formatted; the initial browser attempt stopped before its test body because Chromium lacked native libraries. A subsequent, explicitly unpublished-candidate browser proof is recorded below. No real-model inference or live Telegram-service delivery is claimed.
- Measured focused test wall times: requested eight suites 53.48s; outbound siblings 59.20s; dashboard/transport/reaction suites 52.02s. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.

### Unpublished dual-surface candidate: browser and loopback proof

This evidence covers the retained, **unpublished** candidate patch SHA-256 `2ba01337a61031f7a818153704ba3eaa150ac4b649b36e10259b1a145aec4786`, not this PR’s current code head. Product source was unchanged during this proof. Independent review admission remains blocked; no unreviewed product code was pushed.

- A real isolated Gateway and Chromium exercised a Telegram-origin private topic created through the real Telegram ingress path, then opened that same conversation in Control UI. The browser submitted an ordinary prompt; targetless progress and final message-tool replies each appeared once and survived reload.
- The actual Telegram plugin sent each reply exactly once to a task-local Bot-API-shaped HTTP peer: `chat_id: "123"`, `message_thread_id: 456`, account `default`. The persisted session discriminator contained `123:456`; the original transport topic remained the structured numeric `456`. The source record was produced by ingress, not seeded as an expected result.
- The loopback scenario passed (one test, 10.00s test time, 31.44s invocation). The separate unbound-WebChat browser scenario also passed. No external Telegram service or real inference provider was used; these remain separate acceptance gaps.
- Chromium native libraries came from signed configured Debian repositories, downloaded and extracted into task-private storage without root or system installation. The browser-dependency blocker is resolved for this sandbox.

These are **scenario-state before/after images of the unpublished candidate**, not a pre-fix/post-fix code comparison.

Before sending from WebChat — the conversation was established through native Telegram topic 456.

![Before the WebChat prompt in the original Telegram topic conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8824e8f2-1803-457f-ad5f-15d95c73f6ac)

After both message-tool replies and a browser reload — one ordinary progress message and one final result remain visible.

![After progress and final replies persist through reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd12c3a1-196d-4803-b82c-d91bef4814dc)

### Unpublished candidate: local failure-independence repair

The November 16 owning-entry check reproduced a remaining defect in the prior retained candidate: a Telegram adapter exception left zero local assistant messages where one was required. That defect is now repaired **locally, not in this PR’s published code**. The new 27-file candidate patch SHA-256 is `28a8b012d48761b2bb184b345c47247b92c680891242b7de13b1d5ab1b112de5`.

- The existing internal sink persists the admitted WebChat reply before the normal original-destination send. Local persistence and the successful transport mirror use the same logical transcript receipt, so settlement/replay cannot add a second bubble. There is still only one external platform-send path, not a broadcast or second sender.
- The current user-turn identity is carried through the existing source admission/mirror context. A local final mirror is not a Telegram receipt: external errors remain errors, typed retry/queue custody is preserved, and the source-completion owner is not marked delivered on an external failure.
- The exact red assertion now passes. The final owning-entry suite passed **17 cases** (58.68s invocation), covering progress/final, cached failure replay, a new eligible attempt after retiring its cached failure, retry success versus repeated failure, one local row, exact account/chat/topic, explicit local opt-out, different-route isolation, and dry-run/no-side-effects. Adapter I/O is synthetic; these are not live Telegram-service tests.
- Additional owner checks passed **71 tests across five suites**, and the affected consumer graph passed **364 tests across 12 suites**; the owning regression overlaps those receipts and is not counted as extra unique coverage. Core plus messaging/agent-tools/Gateway test types, eight-file type-aware lint, targeted formatting, staged whitespace and test-budget checks passed.
- A fresh full build passed on the repaired source (2m 35.9s). Existing advisory UI-size/request-count warnings remain; they were not changed by this repair.

The prior browser screenshots below/above remain evidence for the older retained candidate, not a fresh browser qualification of this repair. Full independent review admission is still blocked. Parent-owned isolated QA is queued; frozen source-packet qualification is pending. No real external-service binding or live Telegram/provider proof is claimed. No unreviewed product code was committed or pushed, and the PR remains draft pending review, applicable real proof, current corrected-head CI and satisfactory completed ClawSweeper review.

### Unpublished candidate: explicit terminal source-reply visibility

A separate real-Gateway/Chromium scenario exercised native Telegram ingress followed by an explicit `message.send` with `final:true`, account `default`, chat `123` and structured transport topic `456`. Inference and the Telegram HTTP peer were synthetic; this is not live Telegram-service proof.

- The successful tool result reported `sourceReplyRoute: current-source`. The normal producer persisted exactly one terminal assistant mirror, and its `sourceTurnId` matched the naturally persisted inbound user message's idempotency key.
- The real stored row had `navigation_type=message`, `navigation_display=0` and `navigation_valid=1`. That row appeared once in the same authorized browser's `chat.history` and live transcript, including while the run still displayed Stop, then once after reload. The unrelated sibling conversation's DOM/history did not contain it. This covers same-user session isolation, not a new cross-user ACL test.
- The Telegram plugin made exactly one final HTTP send with `message_thread_id: 456`. The focused scenario passed (9.59s test time, 53.78s invocation); UI types, type-aware fixture lint and formatting passed.
- No additional product change was justified by this reproduction. In this source, `navigation_display=0` alone does not hide normal message events. The unpublished candidate, publication/review gaps and current PR head remain unchanged.

After reload — the explicit terminal reply remains an ordinary assistant message. This is scenario evidence, not a code-fix before/after comparison.

![Explicit final Telegram source reply remains visible after reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f366f597-1ac4-41b4-bf96-cde831362e4d)

Before ready: complete independent review and publish the corrected original-Telegram-topic implementation; prove exact chat/account/thread, progress/final, deduplication, retry/failure and opt-out behavior through the owning entry and applicable real UI/channel path; then verify current-head required CI and completed satisfactory ClawSweeper review. Missing implementation and proof are not waived by this draft.

## What Problem This Solves
