title: fix(automations): admin chat edits keep a legacy operator job's execution class
body:
Related: #198621

## What Problem This Solves

An authenticated administrator could not change the model, prompt, or tool cap of an older operator automation through chat when that automation had no owner conversation recorded. The automations tool refused with "This automation runs with operator access and it has no owner conversation, so from here you can only pause, resume, reschedule or remove it." The same edit worked on the Automations page.

## Root Cause

The chat path treated *management authority* (the administrator may edit this job) as if it were the job's *execution identity* (whose authority the job runs with):

- `cronUpdateNarrowsTrustedJob` narrowed every non-lifecycle edit of an ownerless trusted job, even for a management caller. Narrowing then required an owner conversation, so the edit was refused.
- Before that guard existed (#198621), the same edit was accepted but stamped the administrator chat's requester provenance on the job. The job then ran as requester-scoped without an owning conversation, and its workspace admission failed on every run.

## Fix

A management edit keeps the job's saved execution class:

- `cron-job-access.ts`: management callers never narrow a trusted job.
- `cron-caller-scope.ts`: for a job whose saved admission is `operator-schedule`, a management caller records no requester provenance. The decision uses `resolveCronRunAdmissionSource`, the same function the scheduler uses at run time, not the `trusted` policy label. Legacy operator jobs can lack that label, and requester jobs can carry it.
- `jobs-tool-policy.ts`: reconciliation keeps an existing `local` caller origin while both the old and new definitions are operator-admitted, so a cap edit doesn't reset it to `unknown`, which is requester-scoped.

The chat edit now matches the Automations page: the job keeps its operator authority, owner profile, session target, and attribution, and the administrator's conversation is not adopted as its owner. Ordinary caller-scoped turns still cannot edit ownerless operator jobs. Requester-scoped jobs keep their requester class.

## Evidence

I checked the job that was refused in production (read-only): no `owner`, `ownerProfileId: gateway-owner`, `scheduledToolPolicy: trusted`, no `toolsAllowProvenance`, and `sessionTarget` bound to a conversation. The new tests seed this exact shape.

- **Real Gateway and Control UI e2e** (`ui/src/e2e/cron-human-owner.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`): an administrator edits a seeded legacy job on the Automations page, then edits a second one through a real chat turn that calls the `automations` tool, first model-only and then prompt plus cap. Each edited job is force-run and must write a witness file in the bound session workspace. After the Gateway stops, the stored job is checked: no owner, the same owner profile and session target, still `trusted`, and no requester provenance.
  - PR head: **passed**.
  - Same test with the three production files reverted to the merge base `a6750f2a014a`: **failed** at the chat model edit (`expected payload to match { model: 'fixture/edited' }`).
- **Ownership matrix** (`cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts`, 7 scenarios plus the existing matrix): passes on head. With all production changes reverted, 8 tests fail. With only the reconciliation change reverted, the `model-local` and `metadata-local` cases fail, so that change is load-bearing.
- `jobs-tool-policy.test.ts` and `cron-caller-scope.test.ts` pass on head.

title: fix(plugins): allow more than 64 declared feature event types
body:
Related: #197330

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: feature plugins fail to load when their contract declares more than 64 event types, even if they emit very little traffic.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can describe larger, precise event vocabularies without collapsing unrelated changes into a broad event that makes clients refetch unnecessarily. No migration or configuration change is required. This removes only the declaration-count cap—not payload validation, authorization, or lifecycle checks—and does not promise unlimited physical capacity or comprehensive denial-of-service protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Like the operation cap removed in #197330, event declaration count is not a runtime work budget. `defineFeaturePlugin` registers one event service for a nonempty event map; schemas are validated on emission, and clients subscribe only when `on` or `watch` is called. Declaring 65 types does not create 65 listeners or queued messages. Runtime cost instead depends on actual emissions, payloads, recipients, and active subscriptions.

Remove the count rejection in `defineFeatureContract` and correct the documentation. Nonblank plugin IDs, operation/event ID rules, schema and bounded-JSON validation, operator scopes, service startup/stop, and connection backpressure are unchanged. No replacement cap, warning, or rate limit is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Red/green:** the new 80-event contract regression failed on base `06bfea7a5706b8ece40663b878ce839473fa1ea9` with `Feature contracts require a plugin id and at most 64 events`; it passes with this change. Existing invalid-ID checks remain.

title: improve(sqlite): distinguish slow transaction completion phases
body:
Related: #183802

## What Problem This Solves

Slow SQLite transaction logs cannot reliably pair a COMMIT step with its transaction hold or distinguish commit preparation from the elapsed COMMIT call.

## User Impact

Operators can correlate slow transaction records without adding session IDs, SQL parameters, or message content, and see which completion boundary needs profiling. This is a diagnostic improvement, **not a fix for the reported 35–61-second stalls**; the incident cause and current-upstream recurrence remain unproven. No durability, admission, schema, busy-timeout, or retention policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing transaction owner gives each outer transaction a random correlation ID shared by BEGIN/COMMIT steps, lock failures, and slow holds. Slow holds report raw `prepareCommitMs` and `nativeCommitMs`, including failed attempts. The latter measures `db.exec("COMMIT")`, including connection wrappers, metadata admission, and scheduling—not isolated SQLite engine or storage time. Existing `commitMs` accounting remains unchanged; it subtracts metadata admission and includes step logging. Post-commit publication remains outside the measured wrapper.

The existing shared label/step logging code moves to a small diagnostics module to keep the transaction executor within its production line limit; there is no new state owner, logging framework, or persistence. The simplification pass removes duplicate success/failure step-reporting logic. Net change: +44 production lines, +76 test lines, +16 documentation lines, and one required wrapper inventory entry.

## Evidence

### Actual shipped CLI: correlated slow BEGIN and hold — passed

The unchanged built product CLI imported **40,001 transcript events** from an **8,026,783-byte** synthetic legacy transcript in a task-owned profile:

```bash
pnpm openclaw --profile issue183802-import doctor --session-sqlite import \
  --session-sqlite-store <owned-state>/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json --json
```

An external native SQLite connection held `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for 4,000 ms after observing the CLI’s migration spool. The production agent connection retained its existing **5,000 ms busy timeout**, WAL policy, warning thresholds, and synchronous settlement. No source hook, mocked clock, `db.exec` interposer, durability change, or timeout override was used. The CLI exited **0**, reported 40,001 imported events and zero issues, archived its verified inputs, and passed integrity checking. A separate shipped `doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-store <owned-agent.sqlite> --json` invocation independently reported the persisted 40,001 events and `integrityCheck: ok`.

Sanitized records from the actual product file logger share the same transaction ID:

```json
{"message":"slow SQLite transaction step","operation":"session.import.batch","step":"begin","transactionId":"4fc6bb62-44cd-497b-8e53-a6d9d11df991","elapsedMs":3431,"busyTimeoutMs":5000,"beginAdmission":{"nativeAttempts":1,"nativeMs":3431,"serviceCalls":0,"serviceMs":0}}
{"message":"slow SQLite transaction hold","operation":"session.import.batch","transactionId":"4fc6bb62-44cd-497b-8e53-a6d9d11df991","elapsedMs":1742,"phases":{"prepareMs":2,"beginMs":3431,"sqlMs":1723,"hostAdmissionWaitMs":0,"databaseAdmissionWaitMs":0,"commitMs":19,"prepareCommitMs":0,"nativeCommitMs":19}}
```

This proves shipped-entry-point correlation and completion fields during **controlled BEGIN contention plus a bounded multi-row callback**, not a slow COMMIT or a recurrence of the reported 35–61-second incident. The native COMMIT-call time here was 19 ms. All fixture processes and locks were released.

### Regression, build, CI, and review

- Three new native-backed diagnostic cases fail on base because correlation/phase fields are absent, then pass with the change. Transaction diagnostics, transaction safety, and post-commit suites: **52 passed** with `--maxWorkers=1` (3.43 s runner / 2.27 s Vitest). Metadata-relay coverage preserves legacy `commitMs=3` with `databaseAdmissionWaitMs=1000` and raw `nativeCommitMs=1003`.
- Full cold-read consumer suite: **11 passed** (13.32 s runner / 11.17 s Vitest). Wrapper source-closure and eager-import inventory checks pass. Existing concurrent transcript test passes: eight requests settle to one durable idempotent message. Targeted types/lint/format and `git diff --check` pass.
- The authorized `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime` completed exit 0 in **53.0 s**, with normal repository capacity/admission gates. It was not rebuilt for these probes. The entire tracked working tree matches published head `ba2ce18aa725a230a0cc557d8c2b041b03adb195`. The managed guest carrier remains `c232d504`; the unedited dirty-input build stamp records signature `5cda4bb5211e3e608373eca493352390759a8a7ea837e7cc10484fba492c9a8f`.
- **Required exact-head CI is green:** [complete aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574493099/job/132392924213), every selected dependency successful including PostgreSQL conformance, no known-main-red exception; [security-sensitive and dependency gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43576887998) also pass. The bounded PR rollup is truncated; the complete exact-head gate log establishes this result.
- [Completed substantive ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198735#issuecomment-6874308825) covers this head with **no actionable findings** and both prior P1/P2 findings resolved. The subsequent review of the shipped Doctor evidence is also **complete** and explicitly concludes: “Sufficient (logs)”—matching IDs, both completion fields, independent persisted-event counts, and integrity readback. It reports **no actionable correctness or security findings**. The [latest re-review receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198735#issuecomment-6875368255) confirms completion; the original long-COMMIT incident remains outside this diagnostic proof. Local autoreview of the six-file candidate against `06bfea7a5706b8ece40663b878ce839473fa1ea9` was P0-only scoped-clean; it is not a substitute for substantive hosted review.

<details>
<summary>Retained negative control and supplemental native proof</summary>

The first shipped `database restore-migration-backup` probe used a native reader on a task-owned rollback-journal database. Its connection opens without a timeout option or busy-timeout setup, so COMMIT returned `SQLITE_BUSY` immediately (`elapsedMs=0`), rolled back safely, and emitted no slow hold. After the reader released, the same CLI restore succeeded, preserving unrelated data and integrity. This was a negative reproduction, not a permission or build blocker.

A separate native-owner harness produced a matching COMMIT-step/hold pair (1,236 / 1,246 ms); it remains supplemental, not shipped-entry-point proof. The initial 20,001-event import control succeeded but its observer did not acquire contention and it emitted no transaction hold; it is not credited as the paired proof. The bounded contended run above corrected owned-process discovery across all child threads and is the successful product observation.

The local PR-provisioning fixture could not acquire its synthetic operation lock, but its [exact-head CI bootstrap job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574493099/job/132386232150), [cold-read consumer job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574493099/job/132386232104), and [wrapper closure job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574493099/job/132386232235) pass. No failure was masked.

</details>

title: fix(agents): avoid unnecessary Goal Resume handoffs

Related: #196951

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents treating an inactive Goal as a reason to request fresh approval or Goal Resume before doing work the user has already authorized, including a circular handoff that keeps the run busy while Resume requires an idle session.

## User Impact

Agents are instructed to continue currently authorized, executable work without changing the Goal lifecycle. Genuine sign-in, approval, and permission requirements remain in place. This is a model-guidance repair, not a semantic runtime classifier for arbitrary manual-step text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Narrow the shared `requiredAction` guidance and schema descriptions to observed external prerequisites the human can complete while the run waits. Explain the same distinction in inactive `get_goal` results, where the mistaken prerequisite was inferred. Native controls that genuinely require idle must be explained after ending the turn rather than held behind a blocking question.

No Goal admission, automatic-continuation, sign-in verification, or permission enforcement is weakened. No production Goal or deployment was modified.

## Evidence

- 122 focused tests passed, including all five inactive Goal states, direct/deferred guidance, existing required-action outcomes, and prompt-prefix stability; 88 seconds total wall time. The slowest changed test file took 44 seconds, dominated by compilation rather than its test cases.
- New inactive-Goal cases fail on the base because `get_goal` lacks the current-turn guidance, then pass with the fix; stored Goal state remains unchanged. Direct-description and schema regressions also fail on the base.
- Full `pnpm build`, core typecheck, affected agent-root/agent-tool test typechecks, targeted lint/format, documentation link audit, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Real-model proof passed:** a real Chromium Control UI submitted the authorized continuation to an isolated Gateway running this source. GPT-6.1 Sol executed `get_goal`, read an independently seeded workspace marker through Code Mode, and returned its exact contents in a terminal final answer. No `requiredAction` or Goal Resume handoff occurred. The synthetic Goal remained blocked with the same objective, status note, and status timestamp; normal token accounting continued.
- The initial direct-env live-test credential returned HTTP 401 before inference. The successful proof used the existing managed OpenAI provider's unchanged SecretRef; no credential values were copied, no operator provider configuration was changed, and the CLI attribution guard remained intact. No external browser sign-in success is claimed.
- Independent design review and local autoreview (GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3, base `520f18975936d49ffc1cf8d02bbd98c4b7981c14`, complete local patch) found no actionable defects. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; general hosted review is queued and advisory under the explicit maintainer landing request. Exact-head security review passed.
- Exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43570396256) is running. Telegram investigation is separate and establishes no same-cause claim.

Simplification: reuse the existing prompt and read-only Goal owners; add no scheduler, state store, heuristic text filter, or alternate permission owner. Production delta: +15/-5 lines; tests: +29 lines; documentation: +19/-3 lines.

Session roster refreshes copy the selected-session map even when every selection remains valid.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Defer the copy until reconciliation removes the first entry. Source-derived selected-map constructions per reconciliation fall from **1 to 0 when all entries are retained**; removals still make one copy. The current-row map and validation pass remain. These are source-derived operation counts, not measured heap allocations or timing improvements.

## Evidence

- Tested base: `2110db5a1d1c4d15ef746e788b623ef3e49582b6`; prepared commit: `4cf8747cacaa4a11cb362ce2885e6fa64ad14823`. Committed TypeScript hashes equal the tested source.

- Scope suite: **11 passed**. Four selection-owner sibling files: **60 passed**. Exact real-Gateway case, `reconciles captured selections across real refresh, removal, and successor updates`: **1 passed**, 0 failed, 1 unrelated sibling filtered out of 2 discovered. It covers refresh, captured references during confirmation, removal, successor identity, and exactly one UI delete request with the original expected session identity.
- The initial real-Gateway run failed its final roster assertion. Source inspection identified missing test synchronization: optimistic disappearance preceded deletion settlement. The test now awaits the matching successful delete response before the independent client reads the roster, preserving every assertion. This does not establish a production deletion defect or retrospectively determine the original request outcome.
- Canonical focused format/parity, lint/parity, production UI and affected test types, and test-line checks passed on the applicable source. Source-identical helper evidence covers 18 baseline/candidate executions (9 per version), including order, references, pending callbacks, multiple removals, and exception propagation.

Reviewed patch SHA-256: `a3c3c2b2d8dbcaf24a2cf9093f006e560c153aee56f4f5196a1aa883a2fb79ae`; committed patch is identical. This complete review is reused for unchanged source, not represented as a new review execution.

[CI run 43558180314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43558180314), attempt 1, on exact published head `a8d38a39c9880de92ccf114d987de9088dec0bf1` completed failed. - All 764 repository files and 2,030 edges in the Cron test/setup runtime dependency set are unchanged from the actual baseline; none of the three PR files is reachable. Cron lazy-editor, wait/settlement, test configuration, runner, transform, lockfile and toolchain inputs are unchanged.

title: fix(ui): keep model picker interactions stable
body:
Related: #157466 (picker curation; this does not implement hidden models).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes model-picker interactions that unexpectedly close the picker, fail to retain dragged provider order, or leave Favorites stale until reopening.

## User Impact

Users can favorite and browse models without shifting rows or accidentally changing the selected model, reorder providers in Chat and New Session, and use a quieter, slightly narrower picker with working keyboard shortcuts. Mobile sizing and context-window values are preserved; no migration or configuration change is needed.

Desktop stars remain pointer-hover-only, including when a star button receives keyboard focus, as explicitly requested during design review. This retains the known accessibility tradeoff of an invisible focused star button; touch stars remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker and composer now respect each other’s click, drag, and keyboard ownership. Favorites membership stays live while provider-row ordering retains its opening snapshot. The change reuses existing preference and browser-local provider-order owners.

The presentation pass uses one trailing star/check column, centers provider glyphs, shows short provider lists fully, removes numeric keycaps while retaining numeric activation, reuses the shared scrollbar, fades clipped list edges, and centers the desktop overlay when space permits. Context-window controls match the adjacent 11px metadata without reducing their hit targets. Desktop width changes from 440px to 416px; automatic-account copy becomes “Account: Auto” in the trigger and “Automatic” in its menu. Short desktop viewports now fit the popup to the available side of its trigger rather than overlapping it.

The account control’s existing active-run lock and chevron are unchanged. The idle account menu works; the reported no-op click was not independently reproduced in the requester’s original state.

## Evidence

- Initial focused proof: 55 unit tests, 42 Chromium picker/shared-shortcut tests, 23 real-app Chat/New Session scenarios, and all six combined capture scenarios pass. These cover native provider drag/reload, live Favorites, pointer/keyboard behavior, touch/context hit targets, empty/loading catalogs, and idle/actual-send account states.
- UI build, UI typecheck, scoped semantic lint, stylelint, formatting, i18n baseline, test-line allocation, and whitespace checks pass. No thresholds were raised.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete local delta against `9bf3e79c823a51b098ab892d2f8f505931cd5671`, with relevant unchanged owners supplied: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Reviewed candidate: `f489a1525136e1fda3e977034f6b504d22399860`. Subsequent typography, placement/CSS, and shortcut corrections each received fresh independent delta review with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The reviewers did not execute tests; test results are separate executed evidence.
- Typography regressions failed at 12px/13px versus adjacent 11px metadata, then passed at 1280px desktop and 390px emulated touch. Both refreshed capture scenarios pass.

Shortcut activation now shares the registered-shortcut owner instead of duplicating slash/digit dispatch. Its 37 Chromium picker tests and scoped checks pass. The exact prior CI merge-context performance comparison exits 0: boot JavaScript is 459 normalized gzip bytes smaller; total CSS is 7 raw bytes smaller and 36 gzip bytes larger, within the existing allowance. Prior-head GitHub `control-ui-performance` also passed in [43556981033](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43556981033). Existing baseline ceiling warnings remain; limits are unchanged.
- Final mechanical repair: a new main-branch fixture conflict was resolved without changing the approved absent-keycap behavior, provider-local numeric activation, or 8px placement. Main’s model-name memoization and dictation changes are retained. The inert-space test now uses a center-top native click target instead of the corner that CI reported as intercepted by `<body>`; all interaction assertions remain. - Exact-head CI [43557689189](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43557689189) is pending. Earlier failed runs and prior-head passes are not current-head green proof. The previously observed `chat-view.test.ts:2998` element-type assertion also failed identically on main run [43551669456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43551669456), job `132315665357`; this does not establish inheritance for other failures.

title: fix: preserve Claude resume with a child-only config directory
body:
Fixes #198402

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claude starting a fresh conversation after a cold turn when a selected skill supplies `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only to the Claude child process.

## User Impact

Local Claude sessions keep their native session ID and resume from the child-selected transcript root, including after process restart. Gateway-level configuration and the default `~/.claude` root retain their behavior; genuinely missing transcripts and orphaned tool calls still invalidate resume. No new configuration, migration, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transcript probes previously read the Gateway environment before skill overrides were applied. Reuse the existing skill-aware child-environment composition from native-login preparation, pass its result explicitly to transcript resolution, and use it for preparation and final binding-flush checks.

The command layer no longer repeats an ambient transcript probe. It clears a binding only when the runner reports the prepared missing-transcript decision, retaining the expected-session-ID guard. Validation remains enabled. The existing native-login helper is moved, not duplicated; none of the broader machinery from #145895 is restored.

Read-side follow-ups remain outside this fix: `src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-pages.ts` (history-worker context: #198337), and `src/commands/doctor-claude-cli.ts`.

## Evidence

- Pinned base: `e6c7c5e0da4b2407e2d991a00c5d38b599e05050`.
- Candidate: `c42a20af1e5324ba80fa4f0b0de140a5684c3530`; tree `90cdb8e40daa1a9ae99faa8b4e988c2568958400`.
- The final five-case regression and core-test typecheck were rerun after a test-only generator-method shorthand lint correction; production inputs remained identical.
- RED: the final two skill-only regressions fail against the pinned production base (exit 1, 56.58 s wall): preparation reports `missing-transcript`, and the command layer clears the stored binding before execution. An earlier five-case baseline run also confirmed the orphaned case incorrectly reports `missing-transcript`; Gateway/default/missing controls passed.
- GREEN: the same two final regressions pass with the candidate production changes (exit 0, 59.76 s wall).
- GREEN: real preparation, transcript reads, execution argument composition, and runner settlement are exercised with a synthetic external CLI execution callback. The skill-root case retains the binding and sends `--resume` with the stored ID. Gateway, default-root, genuinely missing, and orphaned controls are covered. This is integration-test evidence, not a real Gateway/Claude run.
- Command persistence regression checks that the skill-only root does not cause an early binding clear.
- Required command/prepare suites: **229 passed**, exit 0 (104.43 s wall).
- Required spawn/native-history suites plus settlement and prompt-prefix coverage: **117 passed**, exit 0 (83.93 s wall).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- `pnpm build:runtime`: exit 0; emitted nonfatal Control UI asset-budget warnings, not investigated as part of this server-side fix.

- Independent Auto Review: local changes against the pinned base, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2; `scoped-clean`, no findings. The reviewer did not independently execute tests.

Windows proof supplied by @MertBasar0; the original artifacts are retained locally by the requester.

### Real behavior proof — Windows, stub Claude

**This is a stub-Claude run, not real Claude authentication or inference.** No `claude` CLI or Claude login was used. A controlled `claude` stub on `PATH` (npm-style `claude.cmd` shim → `cli.js`) speaks the same initialize/user/result stream-json protocol as `test/helpers/claude-cli-native-spawn-proof.ts`. title: fix(ui): tweakcn theme imports are lost in other browsers and devices
body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, who is the intended reviewer for this change.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/883de5f4-29a0-436b-9b14-bd0167001845)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e6c2c44d-1746-4a0f-8948-6e93174b160d)

Related: #184960 (theme discovery and personal-theme removal; it keeps this importer unchanged)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a theme imported from tweakcn in Settings → Appearance disappears in every other browser or device, and after browser storage is cleared, even when the person is signed in to a Gateway profile.

## User Impact

User impact: when you are signed in with a profile you can edit, a tweakcn import is saved as a personal theme. It appears in the theme grid like agent-created themes, is selected right away, and follows you to other browsers and devices. Importing the same tweakcn theme again updates that personal theme instead of adding a duplicate.

Existing users keep their imports. The importer shipped in stable releases (v2026.10.2 through v2026.11.3), so a browser that still holds an import from an earlier version moves it to the profile the next time it connects with write access. If it was the active theme, it stays active. If the save fails, the browser keeps its import and retries on the next connection.

Without a profile or without write access, nothing changes: the import stays in the browser-local slot with its Replace and Clear controls.

**Decision for review:** the docs from #152460 promised that existing browser-local imports are “never uploaded automatically.” This PR intentionally reverses that promise, as requested, and the docs now describe the one-time move. Please confirm this is acceptable.

Fonts that exceed the portable theme limits, such as tweakcn’s long system font stacks, are replaced by the default theme fonts. All 19 semantic colors are kept.

## Why This Change Was Made

The importer stored one derived token map in browser settings under the special `custom` theme, which profile sync deliberately skips. Signed-in imports now go through the existing `themes.import` Gateway method, the same path agents use, as `user/tweakcn-<id>`. The imported token map still contains the original tweakcn colors and fonts, so one small mapping produces the personal theme definition for new imports and for the one-time move.

The import response primes the theme catalog before the new theme is selected. Without this, switching from a theme such as Knot briefly rendered Claw while the catalog refreshed. No storage layer, schema, or Gateway change is added. The browser-local slot stays only for connections that cannot write to a profile, so its Replace and Clear controls are still used there.

Known gap: Appearance has no control to delete a personal theme on `main`. Before this change, signed-in people could clear their one browser-local import. Now an import becomes a personal theme, like agent-created themes. #184960 adds personal-theme removal.

## Evidence

The before screenshots come from current `main` (`e6c7c5e0da4b`); the after screenshots come from this branch. Both use the real Control UI against a real local Gateway with a signed-in trusted-proxy profile that has write access, in dark mode with a 1440×1000 viewport. The tweakcn response is the real `amethyst-haze` payload, served by a Playwright route. No Gateway RPCs are mocked.

### Before: a fresh browser on the same profile after importing Amethyst Haze

The import is missing and Claw is selected.

![Before: fresh browser on main shows Claw and no imported theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac355c88-050a-45f9-bf76-5fe36d83d664)

### After: a fresh browser on the same profile after importing Amethyst Haze

Amethyst Haze is a personal theme and is selected, and the appearance scope reads “Saved to your profile”.

![After: fresh browser shows the Amethyst Haze personal theme selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36c52ffa-ddde-4c87-a79b-6ff529685bd7)

<details><summary>The importing browser, right after import</summary>

Before: the import fills the browser-local slot (Replace and Clear controls, “Stored in this browser only”).

![Before: importing browser on main with the browser-local slot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/755dd567-13ca-4757-a2a9-8166457659b5)

After: the import is a personal theme card, and the Import card stays available for the next import.

![After: importing browser with the personal theme card and the Import card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b28c167-bf6c-4bd6-a4ce-7edd27da13b3)

</details>

- **Red on base, green with the fix:** `config-page.custom-theme.test.ts` › “saves a signed-in import as a personal theme instead of browser storage” failed on `main` (`themes.import` was never called, and the palette was written to browser settings) and passes on this branch.
- **New focused tests:** a test proves that the real tweakcn payload is saved with all 19 original colors, that the derived palette matches the import, and that an over-long font stack falls back. Another test proves that a browser-local import is moved to the profile on a writable connection and that the selection follows it.
- **Real Gateway run:** importing while on Knot went straight from Knot to the new theme, with no Claw flash. A reload and a second browser context both kept the personal theme.
- **Checks passed:** `pnpm test` on `custom-theme.test.ts`, `theme-catalog.test.ts`, `config-page.custom-theme.test.ts`, `view-appearance.browser.test.tsx`, `bootstrap-theme.palette.test.ts`, and `server-prefs.profile.test.ts` (all passed, about 1–4 s per file). `pnpm tsgo:ui` and the UI app and pages test typecheck shards passed. oxlint and oxfmt passed on the changed files, as did `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` and `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no baseline drift).
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, branch mode) found nothing actionable.
- **Not run locally:** the full UI and E2E suites. The existing mocked-Gateway Appearance E2E covers the connection without a profile, whose behavior is unchanged; PR CI covers the broad suites.
- **Seen but not changed:** while a personal or imported theme is active, the Import card looks light grey. Imported palettes derive `--bg-hover` from the muted text color. This already happens on `main` whenever an agent-created theme is active, so it is left for a separate fix.

title: fix: agent-selected themes keep the previous accent and fonts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the agent selects or applies a different theme, an accent or font chosen earlier in Appearance keeps covering the new theme, so the theme the person asked for does not look like itself. Choosing the same theme in Appearance already resets those overrides, so the result depended on where the theme was chosen.

## User Impact

User impact: selecting a different theme shows that theme's own accent and fonts, whether it was chosen in Appearance or by the agent with the `theme` tool (`set`, or `import` with `apply: true`). Changing only light/dark/system mode, reselecting the current theme, and importing a theme without applying it keep the person's accent and font overrides. Accent or font values sent together with the selection still win, so Appearance behaves exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reset rule lived only in the Control UI, which sends `accent: "theme"` and cleared fonts alongside the new theme. The Gateway `themes.set` and `themes.import` handlers, which both Appearance and the agent tool use, now apply the same defaults whenever the selected theme changes, so there is one owner for the rule. The Control UI keeps its own reset because it also updates the browser immediately and covers connections without a profile; its requests already carry explicit values, so its stored result is unchanged. Tool description and docs now describe the behavior.

Accepted edge case: like Appearance today, choosing a different theme stores `ui.accent: "theme"`, which uses one profile preference key. A profile already at the preference key limit cannot apply a newly imported theme until a key is freed; the existing limit test was adjusted for that.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway and Control UI (synthetic owner profile, no live data). Steps on each build: select Claw, save a custom pink accent (`#ff2d95`) to the profile, then send `themes.set {"id":"phosphor"}` from the CLI, which is the same request the agent's `theme` tool sends. A fresh browser then opened Settings → Appearance. No model or agent turn was involved.

- Before (current `main`, e6c7c5e): profile keeps `ui.accent: "#ff2d95"`; Phosphor renders with the pink custom accent, next to the caption "Choosing a different theme resets its fonts and accent colors."
- After (this branch): profile stores `ui.accent: "theme"`; Phosphor renders with its own green accent and Accent color shows "Theme default".

![Before: Phosphor selected but the pink custom accent remains](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e80701b0-e451-481f-8b44-0558a1518d8b)

After (this PR):

![After: Phosphor selected with its own green accent, Accent color shows Theme default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8fe2a28-9020-4609-a7d8-fe9228b3a623)

Tests:
- New regression in `src/gateway/server-methods/themes.test.ts`: failed on base (accent stayed `#aabbcc`, fonts stayed after `themes.set {id: "tide"}`), passes with the fix. It also covers mode-only change, reselection, import without apply (overrides kept) and import with apply (reset).
- Existing Settings-shaped test with explicit appearance values in the same batch passes unchanged.

title: fix(ui): stale theme colors return when an older catalog read finishes late
body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, who is the intended reviewer for this PR.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/883de5f4-29a0-436b-9b14-bd0167001845)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e7367350-e2f2-4120-a576-3babb785e62a)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI can show outdated theme colors, or bring back a removed plugin theme, when an older theme catalog read finishes after a newer refresh has started on the same connection and profile.

Two reproduced cases on `main`:

1. A first `themes.list` is still pending, a `users.prefs.changed` event starts a second refresh that applies background `#222222`, and the first read then finishes with `#111111`. The older `#111111` palette wins.
2. A `themes.get` for a plugin theme is still pending, a `plugins.changed` refresh removes that theme from the catalog, and the pending read then finishes. The removed theme becomes available and is applied again.

A profile or client change already discarded these late reads; a refresh on the same connection and profile did not.

## User Impact

User impact: after a profile preference change or a plugin reload, the Control UI keeps the newest theme colors and does not reapply a plugin theme that the catalog no longer contains. There is no visual or settings change otherwise.

## Why This Change Was Made

The theme catalog already owned the decision about whether a response may still publish (connection, client, and profile). It now also records a refresh generation: each refresh supersedes earlier list and palette reads, so only reads started under the newest refresh can publish. A palette read also publishes only while the current catalog still lists its theme, because a palette read started during a refresh can otherwise finish after the new list removed the theme. Dropped palette reads are requested again by the existing path, since each refresh already clears the requested set. No new UI, cache, or state layer was added.

## Evidence

- Two regression tests in `ui/src/app/theme-catalog.test.ts` cover the cases above through the real application theme and Gateway store test harness. Both failed on `main` (`e6c7c5e0da4b`): the first kept `#111111` instead of `#222222`, and the second applied `space-pack/xenovessel` instead of staying on `claw`. Both pass with this change.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/theme-catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 20 of 20 tests pass, about 2.6 seconds.
- Consumer tests that import the theme catalog or application theme (11 files, including `bootstrap-theme.palette`, `config-page.appearance-catalogs`, `config-page`, and `appearance-background.browser`): all pass.
- `tsgo:ui` and the `tsgo:test:ui` shards pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on both files; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `origin/main` at `e6c7c5e0da4b`, P0–P2, with the catalog, its test file, and `bootstrap-theme.ts` as source context): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Not run locally: broad UI suites and Control UI end-to-end runs; PR CI covers broad proof. This is not a visual change, so there are no screenshots.

## What Problem This Solves

The new-session prompt asks "What should this session work on?", which is framed around OpenClaw's internal concepts and leaves new adopters asking what a session (or a task) is before they have typed anything.

## User Impact

User impact: the new-session prompt now reads "Ask me anything, or hand me something to do", in the selected agent's voice, and the header hint is shortened to "Pick where this session works." English only; other locales update through the normal translation refresh.

OpenClaw is a personal agent, so the prompt should sound like the agent offering help rather than the product describing its own concepts. title: improve(ui): restore composer superellipse corners and tighten its controls
body:
Related: #193621 ## What Problem This Solves The chat composer was the only Control UI surface left on plain circular corners, so its 25px radius read as a pill. Its action row mixed icon stroke weights and uneven gaps. On New Session at phone and narrow widths, the composer rested about 40px taller than its content and the model chevron sat far from the model name. ## User Impact User impact: the composer draws the same superellipse corner as the rest of the app again, its controls read as one evenly weighted row, and New Session's narrow composer rests one line tall with the chevron beside the model name. Safari and other WebKit browsers keep today's circular corners. WebKit 27.3 beta was reported to stop painting a superellipse composer in narrow layouts (#193621), and that fallback now applies only to WebKit instead of to every browser. It covers WebKit at every width because the reported threshold is unknown, and it relies on a WebKit-only CSS probe (`-webkit-nbsp-mode`). Remove it once WebKit paints the shape. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Corners:** the composer's shape token defaults to `superellipse(1.5)` again, with a WebKit-only `@supports` block that keeps `round`. Theme overrides still win. - **Action row:** line icons share one 1.5px rendered stroke (they ranged from 1px to 1.67px). The plus, microphone and send paint a 30px tier and the permission, model and effort chips paint 28px, so the actions stay the taller bookends when a chip is hovered. The send disc and the plus sit 8px from the side and the bottom. Gaps between neighboring controls are 21.5px to 22.75px (they ranged from 17.75px to 25px). The context ring and model mark use even boxes so they center on whole pixels. Hit targets stay 32px and the touch layout keeps its own geometry. - **New Session, narrow:** the writing area no longer carries a taller floor than the shared composer, so it rests at the 92px surface minimum (it was 132px at 390 × 844) and still grows with the draft. The model picker keeps the track between the fixed controls, and the chip inside it hugs its label and chevron. ## Evidence Real Control UI with a mocked Gateway and synthetic content, Chromium. The phone captures use an emulated touch viewport. **Chat composer, 1280px, dark** Before (main `e6c7c5e0da4b`) After **New Session, 390 × 844 touch, dark** Before After **New Session, 580px window with a draft, light** Before After - `ui/src/styles/corner-shape.browser.test.ts`: the composer and its notices are back in the superellipse contract, and a new case satisfies the WebKit probe in Chromium to prove those selectors stay circular there while other surfaces keep the superellipse. 5 cases pass in about 0.5s of test time locally (10.6s shard wall time alongside two other files); CI seconds are not available yet. - Passing composer consumers: `chat-rhythm-alignment`, `chat-composer-mobile`, `chat-composer-overflow` and `composer-editor` browser tests; `new-session-page.model-catalog` "keeps mobile model loading steady" at 320, 400 and 560px (zero layout shift with the hugging chip); `composer-control-ink`, `new-session-page.responsive-welcome` and `new-session-page.keyboard` E2E. - Stylelint and the format check pass on the changed files. - Playwright WebKit 27.2 computes the circular corner with this change and paints New Session at 390px. WebKit 27.3 beta itself was not tested. - Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode) on `origin/main` `e6c7c5e0da4b` → `2d40828a52ab`, priorities P0 to P2: scoped-clean, no findings. The reviewer had no rendered layouts.
Failures that also occur on the base, and coverage gaps These fail locally with the same assertions and values on `e6c7c5e0da4b` without this change: - `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`: "keeps the composer bottom controls, attachment, and primary action aligned at 568x320", "keeps short-landscape composer adjunct rows scroll-reachable", "keeps short-landscape slash menu visible inside the bounded composer". - `chat-composer-picker-layout.e2e.test.ts`: "keeps model and effort targets separate when Files narrows the composer" in Chromium and WebKit. - `new-session-page.model-catalog.e2e.test.ts`: "keeps picker geometry stable while shortcut visibility follows focus". Not covered: Safari 27.3 beta and physical touch devices. The maintainer verification below additionally covers the Fast-mode bolt.
Requested and directed by Vyctor Brzezowski (@vyctorbrzezowski). ### Maintainer browser verification On `822199a42585ac6047bc9eb5f1277a801e29f02b`, eight source-UI scenarios passed in installed Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and Playwright WebKit 27.2: chat at 1280px/390px, and New Session at 390px dark/580px light. The Gateway data was synthetic; no microphone, provider credentials, or inference were used. - The actual `CSS.supports('-webkit-nbsp-mode', 'space')` result was false in Chromium and true in WebKit. No CSS probe was replaced. Chromium computed `superellipse(1.5)`; WebKit retained the `round` token, serialized as `superellipse(1)`, for the composer and its visible notice. - Inputs remained visible and editable. New Session rested at 92px instead of the baseline's 131.95px, and grew to 296px/266px with long drafts at 390px/580px. Send/Start targets remained reachable. - The fixture retained Fast mode in chat at both widths; the bolt is visible in the Chromium capture below. - One ResizeObserver notification was recorded during the WebKit 390px chat scenario, with the same single notification on the baseline. It was not a sustained loop in the observed run, and no painting or interaction failure occurred. - Safari/WebKit 27.3 beta and physical touch devices were not tested. | Installed WebKit 27.2 · 390px · notice and composer visible | Chromium · 1280px · Fast mode retained | | --- | --- | | ![WebKit keeps circular corners and a visible composer and notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/533d75ff-d913-4b89-ae83-ac6577499fd3) | ![Chromium composer with the Fast-mode bolt visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10e1357c-7d38-4334-a82a-441e6cb71cc3) | ### Maintainer correction: narrow composer hit areas Published in the corrected head 5fed90721d28fb6392a59627ecc7e6d57b9c2edb; an independent P0–P3 review of this CSS correction found no actionable issues. The original candidate let the new microphone paint rule override the existing narrow-layout target size. With Files open at 1100 × 729, the microphone overlapped the effort button by 7 × 36px; hit testing sent clicks in that part of the effort button to the microphone. The correction keeps the existing narrow target size and removes the desktop-only context offset in the narrow container. The microphone still paints on the 30px tier; model and effort retain their separate 44px targets. The approved wide layout and the control gaps are unchanged. - On the corrected source, Chromium and WebKit both opened Model and Effort with actual clicks and closed them with Escape. The visible microphone passed click actionability without starting audio capture. - Geometry, labels and context alignment passed at all seven widths from the existing regression scenario in both engines. - Desktop and phone smoke checks retained the same composer heights, corner shapes and Fast mode as the original candidate. - The full existing picker scenario proceeds past the repaired geometry assertions, then reaches the separately reproduced baseline overlay-dismissal failure. That entire scenario is not reported as passing. | Before correction: effort and microphone targets overlap | After correction: separate targets | | --- | --- | | ![Narrow composer before correcting the hit areas](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db50b544-4258-4c62-9305-1b82ae78ffef) | ![Narrow composer after correcting the hit areas](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d2790f5-f06a-4f0a-9225-5083d809586b) | ### CI findings and budget decision The pre-correction [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43532756854) had 27 failed UI/E2E cases. Two exposed the overlap repaired above. The remaining 25 reproduce on the PR baseline, including model/account selectors, short-landscape layout, model-catalog state and native-runtime recovery assertions. The 25 relevant test/owner blobs were also compared with the CI main parent and were unchanged. Local attribution used macOS arm64; CI used Linux x64. The same run measured CSS growth of 2,029 bytes raw and 331 bytes gzip on a baseline already over its cap. The maintainer's standing CSS-budget exception applies; no limit or baseline is changed by this PR. Neither the budget exception nor the inherited-failure attribution is described as green CI. ## Work sessions Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public. - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3a3ae829-e164-417f-a7ce-da0d64c72b63) ## Worked on by - @vyctorbrzezowski

title: fix(ui): remove token counts beneath completed replies
body:
Related: #192058

## What Problem This Solves

Completed chat replies still show a separate output-token count beneath the answer, repeating technical usage information in the main conversation.

## User Impact

Finished replies no longer display the token-count footer. Usage details remain available through the message timestamp (“Just now”) and the composer's context ring. Live working counters, “Worked for…” timing, interruption notices, and message actions are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Token usage is useful power-user detail, not something a personal agent needs to emphasize after every turn. The existing on-demand surfaces already provide that information.

Remove the completed-token renderer and its now-unused recap state and wiring, rather than hiding it with CSS. Keep the existing owners for live usage and work duration. Obsolete recap tests and diagnostics are removed with the renderer; the generated boot inventory was refreshed.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the base because a completed reply still contains the token footer, and passes with this change. It also covers batched completion, late usage updates, and retained live counts.
- Six focused test files passed (253 tests in 11.64s before removing an obsolete mocked recap test); the final two edited files were rerun successfully (153 tests in 8.39s).
- Focused bundled-browser lifecycle scenario passed: 1 test, 14 unrelated cases not selected; 16.04s total. It preserves work duration across completion, later session updates, and reload.
- Actual Control UI with synthetic Gateway data, 1200 × 800 light viewport: live token count present while working; no completed-token footer afterward; work disclosure opens and the next draft remains editable. The screenshots below show the actual app with fixture data.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, diff check, and boot-manifest generation passed. Targeted lint reports three existing warnings on unchanged lines. Current CI findings are documented below.
- Independent maintainer review of the original 17-file candidate found no actionable P0–P3 issues; the subsequent two-file test cleanup was also reviewed.

### Maintainer verification

- 255 focused tests plus three timestamp-usage cases passed. UI build, UI/test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and stylelint passed.
- In the actual source UI with synthetic Gateway events, 42 output tokens remained visible while working. Completion and a later 57-token usage event left no completed-token footer. “Worked for 13s,” disclosure, Reply/Copy, and the next draft remained intact; the timestamp still displayed its message usage and duration. This is mock-Gateway browser proof, not real-Gateway or inference proof.
- The build reports asset-budget overages; the maintainer's standing budget exception applies. This run does not establish their origin.
- Maintainer correction: two existing E2E scenarios still positively required the deleted footer. Removed those obsolete waits and recap-only diagnostics, while preserving the actual final-answer wait, live counts, request clock, child navigation, decoded image ordering and reload checks. Both targeted scenarios passed, including an isolated real Gateway with a synthetic loopback provider; the final scoped answer wait was rerun separately. No additional production change was needed.
- Pre-correction CI exposed one of those stale recap requirements. Other observed failures are attributed below; they remain failures, not green CI. The maintainer-authorized budget/inherited-failure exceptions do not waive PR-caused failures.

<details>
<summary>Pre-existing CI failures verified on the baseline</summary>

Twenty-six unrelated failures reproduced on e6c7c5e0da4b2407e2d991a00c5d38b599e05050, the first parent of CI merge c504def33851cf0d245c1175e261b83a68c5f40d, with matching assertions and values. The baseline used the repository-verified pinned Bun on macOS arm64; CI used Linux x64.

title: feat(i18n): prepare pinned external Control UI memory
body:
Related: #165234

## What Problem This Solves

Prepares the Control UI locale refresh to retain canonical translation memory outside main while keeping source checkouts and public-session builds reproducible offline.

## User Impact

After an explicit bootstrap, UI and public-session builds use checked-in digest-pinned catalogs without fetching translation storage. Raw memory is restored only for generation and published to a separately configured, append-only canonical Git repository before the corresponding main pin.

**This PR does not activate or provision production storage.** Until an administrator configures the approved destination/App and lands the generated bootstrap change, the existing tracked-memory workflow remains active. No real destination or credentials are supplied here; no remote migration was performed. Existing reachable Git history is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared path retains one lossless canonical snapshot, exact revision and SHA-256 pins, and a smaller derived build representation. The same reader serves Vite and public-session runtime/worker builds. Bootstrap validates all raw bytes before local removal; restore validates the complete snapshot before writes; failed canonical publication cannot advance the main revision pin.

This is the smallest coherent preparation stage spanning both build consumers, the existing same-run artifact flow, and the terminal generated-PR publisher. It uses existing Git/GitHub infrastructure with no new runtime dependency. Production ownership/access and the explicit bootstrap remain operator actions documented in `docs/ci/control-ui-memory.md`. No history rewrite, shared repack, translation rewrite or provider call was performed.

## Evidence

- Native local Git fixtures cover bootstrap, byte-exact restore from old/new pins, rejected-push ordering, projection corruption, no new raw-memory objects in future source commits, and unchanged catalog object IDs for metadata-only refreshes.
- Full-roster local cutover: 22 locales, 270,050 translated key/value entries; current-English materialization and public-reader dictionaries are byte-identical. Raw inputs total 114,078,356 bytes; build projections total 46,251,834 bytes. These are logical file sizes, not a clone-pack forecast.
- Both UI builds pass: 4,940 output files byte-identical; only `.build-inputs.json` changes to record the new inputs. Public-reader tsdown module bytes are identical. All original raw files were restored after the local experiment.
- The old public-reader consumer fails the activated-input regression with missing French translations; the reviewed consumer passes. 59 focused locale/tooling tests, 50 Vite build-owner tests, and 225 CI workflow guards pass. Targeted tooling/UI types, typed lint, formatting, workflow validation, docs links and production/full-tree unused-file scans pass.
- Independent Codex autoreview of published head `86733d21e2becf0eb8e27f7ff4e3d581977c3959` against `cd61ce32dd28e92003b213f8d2014608504515fb`: complete P0–P2 branch scope, no actionable findings. It inspected the frozen code/evidence, not live Actions. The native publisher appended a provenance-only commit after reviewed implementation `239a76570fb4972d3f329fe5c4fc18311ad029b4`; local Git verifies both trees are `f644ec19706b60424a32e54bd5d2ce5d9dafcb8c`, so the unchanged implementation proof remains applicable.

Limits: no production repository, GitHub App permissions or authenticated hosted refresh has been exercised. Local fixtures use synthetic destination identities and no network. No visual behavior change is intended; this does not claim to fix GitHub’s existing pack representation or remove historical objects. The draft requires maintainer review of canonical-store ownership, retention and activation.

## Contributor credit

Prepared at the request of @hannesrudolph. Related issue reported by @NovaUnboundAi.

title: fix: show plugin-delivered images in Control UI
body:
Closes #156548
Related: #156613 (earlier unmerged candidate; this repair uses the current source-session owners).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin-delivered images missing from Control UI when `toolContext.delivery.send({ mediaUrl })` successfully sends them to the current conversation's channel.

## User Impact

Delivered images appear in the source conversation and survive history reload, without another channel send. Existing filename-only history is preserved rather than backfilled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The confirmed source-reply mirror retained filenames and URLs but did not prepare managed display attachments. The repair carries the sender's existing reader into the managed-attachment and transcript owners, preserves replay identity, and settles attachment custody before publishing history. Uncommitted preparation is cleaned up; committed media survives cancellation.

Relative references also retain the sender-scoped intent of #152219: they resolve against the sender workspace, honor reader denial and never fall back to a same-named Gateway-CWD file. HTTP ingestion is unchanged. No schema, worker, configuration or public plugin API rewrite; the loader moves into its existing preparation sibling to satisfy the line-cap gate.

The cleanup now prunes cases, not just setup: **10 → 3 new media cases**, with the standalone source-mirror test file deleted. Media-test growth against the pinned base falls from the original **387 added lines** (315 after the first cleanup) to **135 added / 6 removed, 129 net**. The inherited Visitor expectation correction remains separate and unchanged: three added/one removed lines. Whole PR: **353 additions / 71 deletions, 282 net**, across 11 existing files; production growth remains 149 net lines, total test growth 131, docs two. No new test file or generic harness remains.

## Evidence

- Published pruning head: `ba85aa6a4107aa1179a863ce7de56f7734370151`, a fast-forward test-only child of `aa2c508c1f7b446bdc6570b2c953e58ef07a0334`. Pinned rebase base remains `8e6768f91235b7b094f7f8dde96735d727a3f748`. No history rewrite or runtime change.
- **Exact-head [CI run 43534799442](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43534799442) completed successfully.** The required `openclaw/ci-gate`, security-sensitive review and applicable security checks are successful. GitHub reports the PR mergeable with a clean merge state. Verified November 14, 2026, 01:01 UTC; nothing merged, bypassed or set to auto-merge.
- Existing plugin, managed-media, privacy/cancellation and transcript-owner coverage passed in the 112-case selection. After final placement in the existing ingestion/recovery suite, all **17 recovery/media-identity cases pass**; the two reader cases additionally fail against the exact old loader and pass with the repair. These counts overlap and are not newly added cases. Gateway-root and agents-sessions test typechecks, scoped lint/format, whitespace and commit gates pass. The line-cap gate rejected growing the large managed-media test file, so the two checks use the existing smaller ingestion/recovery suite and its scoped state fixture instead. No gate was waived.
- The retained plugin-delivery regression still has its proven red/green result: zero display images after database reopen on unchanged pinned-main media source, visible managed image with the repair. The final relocated sender-reader regressions fail for wrong Gateway bytes and acceptance despite sender denial on the old loader, then pass with the repaired loader. Production-identical real-Gateway proof below remains applicable.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the exact final pruning diff against `aa2c508c`: no actionable findings. The committed patch was compared byte-for-byte with the reviewed diff. This is static diff review, separate from executed tests and earlier complete-range review.
- ClawSweeper's completed `d3592fb3` review found no actionable findings and accepted the real Gateway/media evidence. Its existing request is complete; no duplicate hosted request was posted for this test-only push. That hosted review is parent-head evidence; the final pruning has its own independent diff review and exact-head CI above.

<details>
<summary>What was pruned and why</summary>

- **Primary regression retained (one case):** plugin delivery → persisted display image after database reopen, managed-artifact resolution, one send. This catches the reported defect at the caller-to-persistence boundary. Its existing fixture stays at 79 added lines, down from the original 125.
- **Exposed sender-reader bug retained (two cases):** allow/deny variants move into the existing managed-media ingestion/recovery fixture, using different sender and Gateway-CWD bytes. They directly guard the actual review-discovered relative-path authority bypass; no source-session harness is needed.
- **Standalone replay/conflict and released-history cases removed:** the existing transcript media-identity cases already own persisted replay/conflict and literal old-row reopen. Nine net lines strengthen those existing cases for the new display-preparation callback: skipped for old rows, invoked once for concurrent fresh writes, with display content persisted. No new transcript cases or fixtures.
- **Separate absolute-reader-denial and sensitive-media cases removed:** no new absolute-path semantics; the moved denial regression covers the exposed reader bypass. Existing plugin binding/root checks and final-media privacy-owner tests cover the unchanged permission and sensitive-exclusion policy.
- **Three cancellation cases removed:** existing writer tests cover revoked authority before commit and custody completion at the first post-commit async boundary; managed-media tests cover partial-preparation rollback and pending-read abort. The deleted post-commit scenario only aborted after the mirror had already completed, weaker than the existing owner race test.

This deletes the 236-line source-mirror suite rather than relocating its harness. Runtime authorization, replay, cancellation and custody code are untouched. The earlier 80-test selection meant 10 new plus 70 existing cases, not 80 additions.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Separate inherited CI expectation correction</summary>

title: fix(update): supervised PostgreSQL updates ignore server recovery captures and orphan them on finish
body:
Closes #198401
Supersedes #198435

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `database.postgres.recoveryCaptures: "server"`, supervised `openclaw update migrate` exported every PostgreSQL store to local files while the Gateway was stopped, extending downtime, and `update finish` would orphan server-side captures if they were made.

## User Impact

User impact: supervised PostgreSQL updates honor the configured server recovery captures (shorter stopped window, no local export copies), and finishing the update retires those server captures instead of leaving `restore_<uuid>` schemas behind. Cleanup stays best effort: if retirement fails, the update still succeeds, the backup is kept, and a warning says to retry `update finish`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on @qingminglong's #198435, which forwards the existing setting to the supervised migrate backup, matching the native updater. That alone would keep rows in server schemas whose only references are the local backup manifests, and `update finish` deletes those manifests without dropping the schemas. Finish now retires them through the existing `discardPostgresSchemaCaptures` owner (the same one the native updater uses) before removing the backup directory; a failure keeps the manifests so a retry can finish, and `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS` keeps retries idempotent. Doctor's capture pruning cannot reclaim these because supervised captures lack its prefix marker.

Rolled-back (restored) receipts keep their captures under the existing rollback retention contract; no retention policy change.

## Evidence

- New finish regression in `update-command-migrate.test.ts` (real finish command, discard owner mocked at its module boundary): **red** on #198435's head (discard never called), **green** with the fix; covers ordering before directory removal, discard failure keeping the directory with a warning, and retry.
- `update-command-migrate.test.ts` 22 passed (including #198435's tests); `update-command-database-retention.test.ts` 15 passed.
- The PostgreSQL migrate→finish lifecycle case **ran and passed against a real PostgreSQL service in CI**, not skipped: [PostgreSQL conformance (1/3), run 43512134482](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43512134482/job/132185832402), `retires server captures through supervised migrate and finish` (13.124 s). The adjacent existing exact-capture→rollback→retirement test also passed (6.696 s), preserving the frozen capture and row verification. This remains in-process boundary proof (Doctor is stubbed), not an installed CLI upgrade.
- All 52 PR checks passed on `95500ea9c4c879cb4f302cb6e8e3f09615da982a`. Remaining gap: no installed v2026.11.3→candidate supervised CLI upgrade with existing portable captures. No schema, receipt format, or default-policy change is introduced; portable defaults and shared-state exceptions remain unchanged.
- Type-aware oxlint and format check of touched files, `git diff --check` pass.

Thanks @qingminglong for spotting the missing option and the parity test; your commit is kept as-is with authorship.

title: fix: repository refresh failures hide Git diagnostics
body:
Related: #197849
Follow-up to #197862.

## What Problem This Solves

Managed repository refresh failures hide the underlying Git error, and diagnostic messages must retain the next step for users rather than only directing them to operator logs.

## User Impact

Refresh preparation and branch failures explain what happened in plain language and ask users to send their message again to retry. If the failure persists, the diagnostic ID connects the session error to the operator log. The complete explanation, retry step, and diagnostic ID fit the bounded session summary; raw Git output stays out of the shared conversation.

Credentials, authentication classification, cancellation policy, retry execution, and checkout cleanup are unchanged. Clone/fetch wording from #197862 is unchanged. The original production clone/cancellation cause remains unknown, so this PR does not close the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Four refresh error paths bypassed the existing diagnostic logger. They now share that formatter and keep its operation names and complete process records in operator logs. An inline phrase selection restores the documented same-session retry guidance without exposing internal terms such as "seed refs" to users. No additional helper or recovery policy is introduced.

Against the original base: production **+24/-15** lines, tests **+66**, docs **+2**. The latest repair changes **5 production lines and 7 test lines in place** (+12/-12 total, no net growth), shortening the producer phrases and retry sentence. Including `ProjectCloneError: ` and a 36-character UUID, the complete messages are **149 / 154 / 158 / 156 characters** for prepare/read/seed/update respectively, all below the 160-character summary limit. Only the two existing regressions were extended; no new tests or helpers were added. The documentation sentence still matches.

## Evidence

### Current candidate: `26bc7467566cfef0695ba786fea4141a0cd7b074`

Commit: `fix(projects): fit refresh failure messages in the session summary`.

- Both existing refresh regressions fail against `ac1eb9b3c486786170660f8b872838ebe0ebf5e6` specifically because the retained summary contains the middle-elision marker. title: fix(plugins): Doctor and Gateway startup fail when link() silently copies plugin files
body:
Closes #198407

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` exits 1 and the Gateway restart-loops with "Native plugin artifact changed during admission" when the state directory is on a filesystem where `link()` succeeds but creates an independent copy (reported on OrbStack virtiofs bind mounts, for npm plugins under `node_modules`).

## User Impact

User impact: updates and Gateway startup admit native plugins on these filesystems instead of failing; the captured file is still verified to be the exact admitted source.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hardlink primitive treated "link succeeded but produced a different inode" as a source swap. Its callers only fall back for specific errno failures (and never on recapture), so a silently-copying `link()` always failed admission. The primitive now discards that unverified output and captures the member through the existing guarded copy path, bound to the inode still pinned by the admitted descriptor. A real source swap still fails. Callers record such members as copies, not hardlinks, and copied generation references keep the complete-directory and companion validation that hardlinks get, both at admission and when a recovery source is captured.

Accepted edge case: on such filesystems each affected member costs a copy rather than a link; no new config or persisted format.

## Evidence

- Regression in `src/plugins/plugin-native-namespace.test.ts` stubs `fs.linkSync` to copy (simulating virtiofs) for a fresh capture and for a recapture: **red on base** (2 failed, both at the reported error), **green with the fix**. Copied content matches the source; a swapped source still rejects.
- Recovery regression in `plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference.test.ts`: a copy placement with a damaged companion is now rejected during recovery capture (red on the first head, green after the second commit).
- Focused suites green: `plugin-native-namespace`, `plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference`, `plugin-source-file.copy`, `plugin-module-generation.native-layout`, `plugin-native-admission-source-index`, `plugin-generation-artifact.admission`, `plugin-source-capture-recovery`, `plugin-generation-source-lookup` (70 passed across eight files).
- Type-aware oxlint and format check of the touched files, plus `git diff --check`, pass.
- Gap: no live OrbStack/virtiofs Doctor upgrade run; broad proof is PR CI.

Thanks @Lanfei for the precise diagnosis and the minimal reproduction matrix.
