title: fix: archived conversations are missing from Cmd+K search
body:
Related: #195574

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes archived conversations missing from Cmd+K when stored titles or available indexed messages match, without allowing newer weak metadata matches to hide an older exact title.

## User Impact

Cmd+K finds active and archived conversations, labels archived results, and prefers active sessions only when relevance is equal. Metadata relevance is applied before the ten-result cutoff. Opening preserves archived/read-only state, sidebar exclusion and Unarchive. Section-editor membership stays active-only.

Cold-stored messages remain unsearchable until restored; stored titles remain searchable without restoration. Existing access, owner/participant and discovery exclusions remain unchanged. The feature adds no database schema/migration, dependency, persisted configuration, retention or product resource-budget change. The authorized base integration inherits upstream changes; it does not execute migrations or modify live state. The RPC adds explicit `sortBy: "relevance"`; ordinary chronological ordering remains unchanged. No Involving me toggle is introduced.

**Not merge-ready:** the original 20% performance gate remains failed, first-use qualification is unresolved, and current-head broad CI is pending. The generated-file conflict is resolved and GitHub reports mergeable, but blocked. Publication was authorized without a performance waiver. No PR merge, release, deployment or live-node operation has occurred.

## Why This Change Was Made

Archive inclusion belongs to the palette discovery scope; ranking, access, navigation and sidebar owners retain their responsibilities. Search avoids unused facets, repeated selections, duplicate serialization and unnecessary snippet work. SQLite reads bounded hits/snippets in one snapshot using existing prepared builders and the admitted full-text owner; PostgreSQL retains its single-query path.

The verified P2 was a cutoff-order bug: ten recent archived prefixes hid an older exact title before browser ranking. The palette now requests explicit relevance ordering. Existing Gateway selection applies shared normalized exact/prefix/substring ranking before partition/global limits, then active status, recency and stable key ties. It reuses bounded top-k merging and the field cache: no fetch-all browser roster, extra metadata RPC, increased result limit or cross-request authority cache. `source` remains diagnostics-only.

## Evidence

### Current published reconciliation

- **Head:** `6cb418ef18284a596b4cb189f63cc6762e477841`; tree `e9a9e4a76c756defef59607afae5c86e9e9ba2ee`, identical to reviewed local commit `812d6bf33c07c0f81d120f8b4bafa8badb0f6ea0`. Clean worktree verified after publication.
- Integrated pinned main `a846d93c689358a86cebeba091d937bbc05539fe` to resolve the actual generated-predicate conflict. Canonical main output bootstrapped the generator, then `gateway:validators:gen` and `gateway:validators:check` regenerated and verified the final file. No hand-edited predicate content. Obsolete imported-planner allocation removed because planner tooling is now inherited from main.
- **81/81 focused tests**, eight files: 27 Gateway selection/search/order/startup, 20 protocol, two broker and 32 palette tests. Current test accounting is **488/488** net lines against pinned main (400 ordinary +88 existing P2 allowance); no increased limits or weakened assertions.
- **Real production-UI/isolated-Gateway flow 1/1 passed** after full rebuild: 225 synthetic sessions, five agents, 22 queries. The older exact active Heron appears first among ten metadata results with nine archived prefixes and zero transcript matches. Archived navigation, active-sidebar exclusion, section membership, access/discovery exclusions and cold conservation pass. Served production-entry SHA matches built assets.
- Core/UI types, scoped lint/format, generator determinism, source i18n verification and diff checks pass. Current inherited i18n baseline: 12,334 keys and 63 existing raw-copy entries. No baseline exception added.
- **Fresh independent AutoReview, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2:** two passes over the candidate against pinned main, no actionable scoped findings. Supplied-context limitations remain explicit; this does not certify performance. Prior ClawSweeper review on `49255ada` reports Findings None and confirms the cutoff P2 resolved; it is historical, not a review of this new head.

### Reproduction and visual evidence

The P2 was independently reproduced on `c292a06`: ten newer archived Heron notes titles filled the metadata response, hiding the eight-day-old active exact Heron, with zero transcript hits. The real product regression failed before and passed after repair. Tests also cover offsets/totals, exclusions, equal-rank active preference, archived exact versus active prefix, rename invalidation and unchanged chronological mode.

[Overflow before/after proof and review response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198421#issuecomment-6865157170) and [original archive-discovery proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198421#issuecomment-6862668476) were inspected, delivered in Team, uploaded as `roboclaw-bot`, and verified by exact asset IDs, bytes and rendered images. The rebuilt current UI screenshot was also inspected; authored reconciliation changes do not alter the demonstrated outcome. Existing evidence was not reuploaded.

### UI asset-size gate — separate from search latency

The old-head manual run found attributable UI byte growth. Equivalent ranking loops, removal of a redundant empty-field filter and forwarding the optional sort in the existing request object reduce bytes without changing relevance or limits.

The first local comparison had mismatched generated plugin inventories (packaged versus standalone settings-only); that failure and attribution are retained, not counted as a pass. The canonical checker then compared matching standalone artifact classes against pinned main, with the task-owned packaged directory restored afterward:

- startup gzip: 90,850→90,850 B;
- chat boot gzip: 1,314,886→1,314,913 B (+27);
- new boot gzip: 816,355→816,402 B (+47);
- CSS gzip: 332,471→332,464 B (-7); raw CSS and request counts unchanged.

**Qualified owner check passed with the existing 64-byte relative allowance unchanged.** Existing main absolute-size warnings remain. This is not RPC latency acceptance.

### Current-head CI

Normal PR CI now starts following conflict resolution. The observed complete inventory for `6cb418ef` initially contains 48 checks/statuses: 11 passed, 21 skipped/neutral and 16 pending, no observed failures at that snapshot. This is an evolving inventory, not final broad validation. [Current checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198421/checks); [normal CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43514566999). Dependency and security-sensitive reviews pass; aggregate CI remains pending. No prior-head result is counted as a current-head pass.

### Retained predecessor failures and proof

The manually dispatched [run 43510060715](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43510060715) verified workload checkout `49255ada` (workflow source was different), selected 267 jobs, and was cancelled once when replacing the obsolete run through base reconciliation; 180 jobs were cancelled. **It is not green.** Five completed failures remain recorded:

- strict release i18n fallback drift; source PR i18n verification passes, generated release locale output was not committed;
- UI asset gate, addressed locally by the qualified comparison above;
- exports/static analysis, including a proxy export removed by inherited upstream `49c99cf91a4df47`; new-head CI must validate the complete lane;
- Node broker child exit-code failure and Gateway startup sessions.list timeout. Their Bun siblings and current focused local Node replays pass, but a causal fix or identical hosted-runtime reproduction is **not established**. No timeout increase or assertion weakening.

On older `c292a06`, 162 statuses settled: 90 success, 68 skipped, one neutral, three failed. Four PostgreSQL conformance jobs, build, architecture/ratchets, three UI shards, two UI E2E shards and types/lint passed. [Planner validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43497186742/job/132133254224) passed 26/26. Initial proof was 46/46; native-owner repair 30/30, sidebar 118/118, isolated PostgreSQL search 4/4; cutoff repair 73/73 plus real UI 1/1. These remain historical.

Those three older reds were the [Talk shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43497186973/job/132134210459) and two aggregate gates. Four after-cancel signatures match [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43482629206/job/132083526517). Automatic classification remained unknown because its newer comparison run lacked that job name. Manual evidence did not override classification; `ALLOW_KNOWN_MAIN_RED` was false. No Talk repair or gate waiver is claimed.

### Performance — original gate remains failed

Baseline `4ab02e3c0879aa5efb51e664b5e57c092144c9ed`; five serial source-pinned pairs, **5,160 authenticated RPCs**, 100 warm samples/source/scope/query. Corpus: 3,500 sessions (500 active/3,000 archived), five agents, 3,495 indexed messages and five physically cold transcripts. Two-worker/heap limits unchanged; exact results/caps and zero cold restoration verified. Measurements predate repairs; no current-head latency pass is claimed.

| Query | Original active median / p95 ms | Measured candidate all median / p95 ms | Original 20% gate |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Common metadata | 0.488 / 3.192 | 0.424 / 4.070 | **Fail: p95 +27.5%** |
| Archive metadata | 0.352 / 3.342 | 0.344 / 4.000 | Pass; p95 +19.7%, near threshold |
| Common indexed | 8.525 / 16.341 | 7.830 / 16.479 | Pass |
| Archive indexed | 5.447 / 11.348 | 7.307 / 11.941 | **Fail: median +34.2%** |
| Absent indexed | 4.535 / 10.849 | 3.236 / 8.638 | Pass |
| Cold-only | 4.284 / 9.943 | 3.219 / 7.669 | Pass |

**4/6 primary cells pass; overall acceptance does not.** Archive-message medians rose in all five pairs, four by at least 20%. Returning 25 hits versus zero adds work but does not waive the gate. First-use **63.786→536.248 ms** mixes two process-first and three process-second observations per source; it is not an eightfold measured startup regression. Adverse second-request and first-use results remain unresolved.

Preparation includes changed-owner source pins and explicit `--metadata-sort relevance` for the palette workload. title: fix(ui): let existing chats return to automatic account selection
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: once someone picks a saved account in an existing chat's model menu, there is no way to return that chat to automatic account selection.

## User Impact

User impact: the **Account** section of the model menu in an existing chat now offers **Automatic account selection** whenever the chat has a selected account. Choosing it clears the chat's account selection and keeps the selected model. New Session keeps its existing **Automatic (new-chat default)** option.

## Why This Change Was Made

Selecting a model without an account keeps a same-provider account selection, and `sessions.patch` had no way to clear it. This adds `sessions.patch { authProfile: null }`, which clears the session's account selection in the existing patch owner. It uses the same write scope and model-selection lock as model changes. Combining it with `model@profile` is rejected. Queued follow-up work picks up the change as it does for an account switch. The menu sends the new field from existing chats, and the account control accepts a caller label so the two menus can describe different actions. The existing pinned-account preparation moved with the new clearing step into `sessions-patch-account.ts`, which keeps `sessions-patch.ts` under its line cap.

Accepted edge case: if no automatic credential can serve the selected model, the next turn reports the authentication failure. The patch does not pre-check that, matching how account switches already behave.

## Evidence

Before (current `main`), existing chat with a selected account:

![Before: no Automatic option](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afb6ab98-7a58-4606-98dd-3ba7df403dbb)

After:

Combining it with `model@profile` is rejected and leaves the account in place. This fails on `main` (`invalid sessions.patch params`).
- `src/shared/session-method-scopes.test.ts`: `authProfile: null` stays `operator.write`.
- `ui/src/e2e/chat-model-picker-composition.e2e.test.ts` (mocked Gateway, Chromium): Account → **Automatic account selection** sends exactly `{ authProfile: null }` without `model`. After the Gateway's `sessions.changed` patch event, the heading reads "Automatic account selection" and the option is no longer offered.

title: fix: proxy sign-in restarts while entering browser credentials
body:
Related: #198226

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI repeatedly restarts a pending reverse-proxy sign-in when HTTP health is reachable but the browser is still authenticating its WebSocket.

## User Impact

User impact: browser authentication gets the existing 30-second opening budget instead of being interrupted by the approximately eight-second reachability recovery loop. This does not fix Safari Private Browsing asking for credentials on each new WebSocket, so the underlying issue remains open.

A socket-only blackhole with continuously healthy HTTP now waits for the existing transport deadline. Recovery after an observed HTTP outage, closed transports and foreground restoration retain their existing paths. No authentication, permissions or timeout settings are relaxed.

## Why This Change Was Made

A successful HTTP health check cannot distinguish a lost upgrade from a native browser authentication dialog. Reuse the client's existing wake-reconnect eligibility before replacing an opening based only on healthy HTTP; an observed outage followed by recovery can still trigger an early retry. This removes an over-eager recovery decision without introducing new state, browser detection or another authentication mechanism.

## Evidence

- **Real-transport after-fix proof on published head `a513e8f6f532a2cd3aadf0043acfe967ec2d4039`:** two actual built-UI Chromium navigations through a Basic-auth reverse proxy to the real isolated Gateway. Original upgrades survived **12,004 ms / 12,002 ms**, with **5 / 4 successful application HTTP health probes** after eight seconds, then completed `hello-ok` and reached UI `connected` with **one socket per navigation**. The service worker remained active. [Environment, redacted timestamped trace and cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198284#issuecomment-6855652492). The delay was induced at the proxy, not a native Safari password dialog.
- A regression using the real browser client and page-activation owner fails on the base: a 29-second pending opening is replaced three times. With the fix it remains open and can finish opening.

title: improve(ui): trim redundant tooltips and show working shortcuts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Many tooltips in the Control UI and the macOS app repeat what the icon or label already says, or explain it in a long paragraph.

## User Impact

User impact: hovering shows fewer, shorter tooltips. Tooltips stay where they teach a working shortcut, explain why something is disabled, show clipped text, or carry information the screen doesn't show. Accessible names for screen readers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each tooltip was either removed, shortened, or given the shortcut that already works for that action. No new shortcuts, panels or other UI were added. title: fix(ui): hide empty message box on missing session links
body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/47e7d457-23c4-412e-a1b2-fe01844a58ed)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a chat link to a session that doesn't exist shows an empty message box and a "Copy any text below before opening another session." hint under "Session not found", even when nothing was typed.

## User Impact

User impact: a dead or mistyped session link now shows only the "Session not found" state with its two actions. If someone did type into the early message box before the route resolved, the box and the copy hint still appear so that text is not lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat links render a real message box before the app loads, so typing can start immediately. When the route ends in a state with no chat pane (not found, ambiguous, error, unavailable Home), the route view kept that box on screen whenever it existed, not only when it held text. The route view now retires the box when it is empty and keeps the current recovery frame only when there is text to recover.

The stale-chunk error screen in the shell loader has a similar hint, but its Retry can still load the chat pane, which then takes the box, so it is unchanged here.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on the published head:

- All **9 existing boot-composer browser E2E cases pass** (28.66 seconds), including desktop, phone and landscape draft handoff.
- Restoring the original route owner reproduces the missing-session bug: the new regression finds one empty editor instead of zero. That original owner is byte-identical to the checked main snapshot.
- With the PR, the empty editor disappears. The typed-draft case keeps the same editable element, preserves its text, and sends nothing when navigating to another session. Both focused proof replays pass.
- Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues. No source changes were needed.

The captures below show the built Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses at 1280×800. They are browser boundary proof, not a live-account test.

title: improve(ui): keep flat-reply reactions under the reply and the reaction picker in place
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reactions on flat agent replies floated far from the reply, and the reaction picker on your own messages jumped sideways when you moved the pointer into it.

## User Impact

User impact: reactions on agent replies sit directly under the reply, and the reaction picker stays where it opened.

- **Flat agent replies:** the reaction tab is the first item in the row under the reply. Normally it is the only visible item in that row. On hover, the name, time and actions fade in after it; the tab does not move. Replies without reactions keep the existing hover-only row.
- **Your messages:** while a reaction picker is open, its row stays revealed. Before, moving the pointer into the picker collapsed the row and moved the picker about 115px sideways, and it moved back when the pointer returned to the message.
- Bubble mode, peer and own bubbles, and forwarded replies keep the corner tab unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A flat reply has no bubble edge, so the corner tab was positioned from the full message width and landed far from short replies. The reaction summary now renders inside the row that already sits under each flat reply: the final footer, or the action row of an earlier message. Hover changes only visibility in that row, not layout. Elsewhere the summary stays on the bubble, so each message shows it exactly once.

The picker opens in the top layer, so hover over the picker does not keep the row's hover state, and the row's hidden layout moves the picker's anchor. Rows now also stay revealed while any control inside them reports `aria-expanded="true"`.

## Original feature evidence

Real Control UI components with synthetic messages, dark theme, Chromium. "Before" is current main.

title: fix(ios): keep conversation history visible during agent discovery

## What Problem This Solves

An already displayed conversation can become empty while iOS resolves its default agent or replaces a presentation alias with the same canonical conversation.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The iOS presenter verifies matching Gateway/account/ingress inputs. The transcript owner compares the canonical key and agent recorded by accepted history with the resolved destination. Only display rows survive; live authority, cursor, run ownership, outbox mappings, permissions and capabilities do not transfer. Drafts and durable outbox entries retain their existing owners. No schema, configuration, dependency, or animation change.

The maintainer integration preserves current main's asynchronous history decoding, synchronous foreground question expiry, run-scoped streaming retirement, local-send revision and attachment/question authority guards. Only the display handoff is added to those current owners.

title: fix(ios): allow reading chat history before startup finishes
body:
Related: #192232

Depends on #192232 at `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d`. This is a separate follow-up on that pinned head.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a native chat keeps initial reader positioning and scroll-follow release tied to the rest of startup even after its cached or live history is available.

## User Impact

Users can begin reading and navigating accepted history without waiting for session metadata and model-list startup to finish. Grouped replies, sidebar animation, word fade, and Send/Talk admission are unchanged. This draft still needs exact-head Mac/iOS build, scrolling, and before/after visual proof; no measured speedup is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing history owner already records accepted live history and cache pre-paint. The transcript now consumes that fact for its one-shot initial position, loading overlay, and jump-to-latest availability instead of using whole-bootstrap completion. Session/model replacement resets the one-shot anchor even when SwiftUI coalesces readiness updates. A separate completed-load fallback preserves reading of restored outbox rows when history fails; an already-settled replacement uses the existing bootstrap task to distinguish an attempted load from unstarted idle. The shared macOS reader no longer repeatedly restores the initial anchor while optional startup runs.

Bootstrap work is neither deleted nor reordered: branch reconciliation, outbox recovery, subscription, health, metadata, mark-read, model availability, and permission guards retain their owners. `isLoading` and the existing empty-state/error/intro loading gates remain unchanged. The blocking full-chrome spinner is limited to the period before readable history exists; accepted history remains readable during a refresh. No cache or parallel startup task is added.

## Evidence

- Source-confirmed on the pinned base: `bootstrap` applies history, then awaits branches, health, the 50-row session refresh, mark-read, and models before its defer clears `isLoading`. The reader previously used that same flag to establish its initial anchor and admit scroll-phase handling.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Source inspection and simplify pass completed. Production delta: +40/-15 lines (net +25); regression delta: +363/-1 (net +362). Swift tests are outside the repository's JavaScript/TypeScript test-line ratchet.
- Authored actual-`load()` gate regressions: delayed sessions/models, empty history, active-stream ownership/send blocking, stale bootstrap after session/alias-route change, detachment during history, and history error with actual SQLite-restored outbox rows. Existing cache-to-live regression now checks early reader readiness. An iOS-only hosted `OpenClawChatView` regression covers failed-load positioning/follow release and settled same-key failed model replacement, using rendered-state signals and scroll observation. No test-only production seam or real sleep was added.
- Parent inspection found and corrected a prior-candidate regression: failed history plus restored outbox rows never initialized the reader. Fresh independent Auto Review then found a P2 variant involving an already-settled failed replacement model; that was repaired and added to the hosted regression. The final full-candidate P0–P2 review (`openclaw`, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`) reported `scoped-clean`, zero remaining findings, with intact view/load/history/cache/outbox/web/scroll owners and relevant fixtures. This is static review, not a native test result.
- **Pending:** Swift compilation, focused test execution and intended-failure baseline control, SwiftFormat/SwiftLint, real iOS scrolling/initial-anchor/no-resnap proof, macOS native-reader smoke, before/after screenshots and video, and performance samples. This Linux environment has no Swift, Xcode, SwiftFormat, or SwiftLint. Test wall time and CI seconds are not available. Source review and fixtures are not native UI/performance proof.

### Acceptance rule for the Mac proof loop

Use the exact pinned base and exact candidate commit with the same synthetic history and device. Separate cold open, cached reopen, and active-stream open. In the deterministic gated owner tests, accepted history must be readable before the sessions/models gate opens while bootstrap and metadata/send guards remain in their original states. In the actual UI, initial positioning must settle before optional startup completes; scrolling away must release follow, and optional completion must not snap back. Session/route switches must show only their own content; retry after an error must anchor when history first succeeds.

Record at least five interleaved baseline/candidate samples per cold/warm scenario: time to first correct anchor and successful scroll-away, median/p95/spread, host load, RPC counts, main-thread work, total CPU, memory, and frame hitches. Expect unchanged RPC counts and no added work/caches; a slower optional RPC must no longer extend reader readiness. Do not claim a performance win or mark ready without the table and exact-head native proof. A 20% regression in a user-facing metric stops the change for investigation.

## Contributor credit

Requested by Vyctor Brzezowski, with the requested co-author credit to `vyctorbrzezowski` and `mikengyn`.

title: fix(worktrees): pack maintenance stalls with two packs after budgeted retirement
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: worktree Git maintenance can stop retiring redundant packs and leave two packs behind forever when a retirement pass runs out of its 250 ms budget. Main `checks-node-compact-large-30` (run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43401336283) catches this in `service.gc-performance.test.ts`.

## User Impact

Repositories managed by worktree maintenance now finish consolidating packs across later maintenance passes instead of stalling with extra packs. No data loss was involved; stranded packs stay valid.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each pass re-runs geometric admission over the remaining packs. After two budget-limited retirements, the last redundant input no longer qualifies under the geometric rule, so the one-input batch is skipped and retirement never resumes. The pending flag scheduled another pass but did not keep what had already been admitted.

The retirement owner now records the verified replacement pack and its remaining selected inputs in the existing SQLite machine-state store before retiring. A later pass resumes that list first (after re-verifying the replacement with the existing offline Git check); completion clears it. Geometric admission, pack/index/count limits, the 250 ms deadline, sidecar completion, promisor/keep/cruft checks and all leases are unchanged.

Introduced with bounded retirement in #195968 (280e1de139e7).

## Evidence

- Red on base through real Git and real leases: two awaited passes go 4→3→2 packs, then a fresh maintenance owner stays at 2 (expected 1); every blob readable and both packs verify.
- Green with the fix; 25 focused cases in the gc-performance and maintenance tests pass. Lint and pinned formatting pass; independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2) clean.

title: feat: let agents review generated images before delivery
body:
Related: #198193

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes generated image candidates appearing in the conversation before the agent can inspect and approve them.

## User Impact

Agents can opt into private review with `deliveryMode="review"`, inspect saved candidates, and deliver or supersede one exact task without canceling accepted generation or disturbing independent jobs. Automatic delivery remains the default. Already-admitted delivery cannot be retracted; ambiguous sends are reconciled rather than blindly retried.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing generation owner and produced-file queue retain original bytes before any reviewer wait or wake. Approval uses the existing delivery path; scheduled delivery sheds the approving attempt's obsolete transcript scope while preserving the disposed-write guard, requester fences, captured worker/spawn resources and service-installation facts. It does not restore request authority. Delivery mode participates in complete request identity. Discovery returns eight summaries per page while exact-task inspection stays private.

The landed identity dependency #198196 and producer #197812 are integrated. Successful producer-owned PNG outputs reach private completion `inputAttachments`, without adding outgoing attachments to held events or widening file access. No new scheduler, physical database schema or retention policy is introduced.

## Evidence

- Normal merges resolve actual content conflicts, not freshness alone. Producer `43b4aaed8090e5f5f2aedb125c47390cfab6ca33` was integrated first; the latest merge incorporates verified main `ea4f8e02c973542257cb9dfe918d0a784fdf8a7a`, including #198742 (`35ca716590b3861c0ef008a4f503876e8282a330`). Its captured service facts compose inside the existing read-only callback with the outer transcript-scope detachment. Caller-identity clearing, plugin registry/resolver isolation and `inheritRequestScope:false` remain intact.
- **21 focused pinned-Bun tests passed in three files** after this composition: scheduled context, lazy automation reads, and actual running queue → persisted assistant image. The existing active/disposed approving-attempt cases now also verify exact service-installation facts and absent Gateway caller identity during delivery. Direct disposed-attempt transcript writes still reject; approved delivery persists and settles exactly once. Core production types, final affected test graphs, typed lint, format, whitespace, line-cap and test-growth gates passed.
- Prior **56 pinned-Bun tests across four files** cover custody/restart/private inspection/default automatic behavior, mode identity, producer consumers and persisted-image delivery. The successful-attachment regression asserts exact PNG base64/MIME/filename in private reviewer inputs, no outgoing held-event attachments/media URLs, zero durable channel sends and no assistant transcript message before explicit approval.
- Real compiled Gateway/Control UI/OpenAI-model proof at `5cbe623cda0033316dbf2ecd4dadb813066b03e4` covered single candidate plus duplicate release and A1/C1 → supersede A1 → A2. The visible image decoded, authenticated download matched the PNG hash, queue completion had zero retries, and reload retained one artifact. A1 bytes remained and C1 stayed held. The completion module still has exact blob `35f0b98ec24de9d8bfa023b77a61c4870fb1be86`, matching that reviewed/proven union; direct-delivery/dispatch inputs are unchanged. The scheduled context intentionally changed and is covered by the new combined tests, not claimed byte-identical. Images API responses were synthetic; no live raster or Google-offer acceptance is claimed.
- The original real approval → scheduled queue → persisted assistant-image regression reproduced `attempt disposed before transcript write` red. Earlier 127-test repair, 202-test integration and 95-test bounded-discovery proofs retain their recorded input scope. Prior docs audit had zero broken links. Expensive unchanged model/build proofs were reused rather than repeated.

### CI diagnosis and repair

Canonical `pnpm test:ci-failed` inspected and ran [CI 43568705192, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43568705192) at old head `6b4e9ea4b2354a3789a13818f8017f1414426e5c`, using pinned Bun with the Node orchestrator retained: **77 passes / two CLI failures**. Media passing on replay alone was not represented as a fix or flake attribution.

The two restart failures were reproduced deterministically with native cleanup by aging every pre-created original fixture: delivered length **2 expected / 1 received**. The fixture created `automatic.png` before a 1000-ms cleanup although that output was not produced until later; retention could correctly remove it. It is now created at actual completion, while held originals/spools still undergo deterministic expiry. The mode case opens its gates after admission/exact-retry checks and awaits two real succeeded publications plus two producer calls, without assuming both providers start within one second. No timeout increases, retry loops, production retention/backoff changes or bypasses were added.

At head `becaa35f0bc3069dae36ed701413decda058e75e`, [CI 43574015505](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574015505), Bun job [132384763720](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574015505/job/132384763720), **passed four files / 46 tests**, including all four formerly failing restart/mode variants. That is prior-head evidence; the new head still needs its own CI.

Both CLI cases and `ExitError(1)` reproduced on unchanged pre-feature main `3588c0514ac88591121c8fa6531a527ccf0e0edd` with pinned Bun:

| Case | Observed baseline reason |
| --- | --- |
| `update-cli.target-schema`: previews explicit artifacts without claiming staged plugin admission | `global-install-foreign-destination` / `unreadable-layout` in a synthetic npm-prefix fixture |
| `update-cli.fresh-doctor`: checks original Git version before a dry-run package downgrade | Same refusal stack; no installation attempted |

For the later target-schema failure in job `132384763425`, the parent verified the test and CLI/refusal source blobs unchanged through actual CI main parent `2e77b6be`. The canonical helper's classification remains `unknown`; this is specific inherited-failure evidence, **not a blanket exception or current-head CI pass**. Older run 43410592278's nine-case attribution remains separate.

### Source-built stable lifecycle

Attested `v2026.11.3` source `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f` used a separate linked checkout, frozen install and unchanged age guards. The complete runtime/plugins/UI built with `pnpm build:runtime`; actual CLI/Gateway health at **state 22 / agent 27** and `backup create --verify` passed. Candidate `6b4e9ea4b2354a3789a13818f8017f1414426e5c` Doctor migrated owned state to **40 / 42**, and Gateway health passed with an inert native-queue PNG fixture.

Ordinary historical startup refused **exit 78: state schema 40 exceeds supported 22**, before Gateway/queue admission. Database main-file hashes, config and original PNG were unchanged. Candidate startup/health succeeded again; actual private review resumed the same held fixture with exact PNG bytes, zero retries and zero outgoing images. The fixture requested no provider/agent inference. Relevant queue/storage/recovery/spool contracts and schema declarations were not changed by this service-context composition.

This proves **source-built/manual-activation lifecycle and safe refusal**, not runnable downgrade compatibility, published-tarball/fresh-install or managed-updater qualification. The original exact npm ETARGET/cutoff is preserved; npm's own `min-release-age=7` was verified (`before=null`). No age override or alternate OpenClaw binary download was used. Candidate UI budget warnings are not waived or independently attributed by a successful build exit.

### Review disposition

Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the final staged source against `ea4f8e02c973542257cb9dfe918d0a784fdf8a7a` completed with **no actionable findings**. Simplification retained two existing context owners and extended the existing persistence test table, without a new helper framework. Reviewed-index/merge-commit tree equality was verified (`342fe4241da3afabab2a826a0d87d122dac341ec`).

The earlier producer-union review's two INDEX-only stale fixture findings were resolved before its commit; that earlier verdict was not claimed scoped-clean. An earlier transport-chat restriction suggestion was declined against documented [DM isolation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/session#dm-isolation) and [main-session continuity](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/main-session): `dmScope=main` deliberately shares a conversation across channels, while agent/store/incarnation/lifecycle checks preserve isolated-session boundaries. No review was rerun merely to change its verdict.

**Remaining gates:** fresh-head CI and parent-owned native landing admission. No live operator Gateway/config/credentials/billing change, release or repository landing is included here.

<details>
<summary>Scope and test budget</summary>

Against verified main `ea4f8e02`: 26 files; production TypeScript +882/-88; tests/support +1226/-83, **1143 net**. The **743-line** excess allocation covers required custody/source isolation, exact-task correction/admission, mode identity, bounded discovery, disposed-attempt persistence, private PNG/no-visible-release and retained service-facts/no-request-authority regressions. title: fix(ui): show video compression errors and honest preparation progress

Related: #194249 (closed report; no closing-fix evidence was available).

## What Problem This Solves

In Chrome, including the reported mobile case, failed video compression shows a generic retry action without an inline cause, and post-encoding attachment reads can appear to restart compression progress.

The existing tile shows an actionable, sanitized failure reason and bounded stage/error code. Encoding and attachment preparation have distinct progress labels, and failed tiles can wrap recovery text without clipping the controls. Original-file retry, cancellation, queued work, staged-file ordering, and negotiated batch admission remain owned by the existing lifecycle.

**Draft qualification:** real mobile rendering, inspected before/after screenshots, and hardware WebCodecs behavior remain unqualified. The reported encoding failure remains unreproduced and unroot-caused; a smaller successful resend is not proof that it works. This website change is not deployed and is not part of an Android APK.

Keep failure and phase state with the current worker wrapper, reader/controller, and tile rather than introducing another upload path. Diagnostics contain only fixed stage/category values, never codec exceptions, URLs, filenames, or recording contents. Codec negotiation and size caps are unchanged. title: fix(models): honor disabled fallbacks when the primary is excluded
body:
Closes #198189

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent can run an unrelated provider despite having no model fallbacks when a wildcard model policy excludes its configured primary.

## User Impact

Requests with an empty effective fallback chain now fail before model invocation, with an actionable error naming the model and policy to repair. This includes explicit `fallbacks: []` and native agent primaries without their own fallbacks. Operators must correct the primary or the applicable allow policy rather than unexpectedly consume another provider’s quota.

Existing exact-only automatic-default exemptions and non-empty-chain catalog substitution remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared selector previously substituted a catalog model before ordinary failover could honor the empty chain. It now checks the already-resolved fallback chain and uses the existing authorization error so HTTP clients receive `permission_error`, not a generic internal error. The native PR-wrapper inventory includes the added dependency.

Simplification: one shared decision, no new routing owner, configuration, or state. Production +7/-0 lines; tests +202/-4 lines, including a real-Gateway regression using existing fixture helpers.

## Evidence

- **November 18 refresh:** integrated [current main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b609d22c129f2944c1abaec1d2895eb659493a36) and resolved the wrapper inventory conflict by retaining both dependency entries. The original ten-file PR scope and seven-line production change are unchanged. The rebuilt real Gateway still rejects streaming and non-streaming requests with zero inference calls, and the allowed-primary control succeeds. The focused runner reports **171 passing tests**; the additional HTTP regression, production and five test typecheck graphs, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Fresh CI is attached to [the refreshed head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c2ad8f07bb07da4e1557db18adb090c6fdbcc5dd).

- **Real streaming reproduction, red then green:** on base `08103c5df8b87969bdb69ce0a8977ed402a3d09a`, `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: "openclaw/fastbot"` invoked the recording alternate provider despite `fallbacks: []`. The regression failed on the unexpected inference request.
- **Original real-Gateway verification:** streaming and non-streaming requests make **zero inference requests** and return the model/policy guidance (`permission_error`; HTTP 403 for non-streaming). An allowed-primary control successfully invokes the same recording provider and completes. Local e2e wall time: 19.60 seconds; test time: 17.26 seconds. Synthetic local provider only; no paid-provider or quota-consumption claim.
- **Initial production candidate: 164 tests passed across nine files / seven shards**, covering shared selection, command/reply consumers, installed provider identity, plugin tool execution, wrapper dependency closure, and the real HTTP regression. The three strict-selection owner cases also failed on the base before the fix.
- Production typecheck and all five changed-test typecheck graphs passed. Scoped lint, formatting, docs-list sanity, and `git diff --check` passed. The runtime was rebuilt from the candidate through the repository e2e preparation workflow. CI timings are pending.
- **Independent Auto Review:** initial production candidate against the base above, OpenClaw engine, P0–P2 coverage: scoped-clean, no findings. Review covered the supplied source/diff snapshot; it did not independently rerun the reported checks.

- **CI follow-up ([f1320f232d62](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f1320f232d62974db4a44d514d320606c5e47696)):** reproduced the `get-reply.auto-fallback` failure from `checks-node-changed-2`, then explicitly configured the fallback required by that substitution fixture. All existing assertions remain intact; production code is unchanged. The corrected file and neighboring selection suites pass **45 tests**, with scoped lint, messaging-test typecheck, formatting, and whitespace checks passing. The earlier real-Gateway proof remains applicable to the unchanged production code.
- **Proof scope clarification:** the HTTP regression starts a separate built Gateway process and a local recording provider, not a mocked/in-process Gateway. No paid-provider quota or release-upgrade proof is claimed; this change introduces no schema, migration, or persisted-setting rewrite.

<details>
<summary>Refresh validation notes</summary>

The real-Gateway test completed in 22.50 seconds (62.37 seconds including test preparation), with exit 0. The focused test runner completed all six shards successfully; the execution host then reported a database lock while recording its final exit, so that run is supported by the runner’s pass summary rather than a clean outer exit receipt. Subsequent static checks and the HTTP proof exited cleanly.

A supplemental refresh review did not produce a report, so no new review result is claimed. The previously completed review remains evidence for the unchanged production patch; this update only integrates main and resolves the dependency-list conflict.

</details>

Thanks to @Marvinthebored for the report and reproduction.

title: fix: honor corrected image references and generation options
body:
Related: #198193

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: correcting an image reference, model, or generation option can return an unrelated active task when the prompt stays the same.

## User Impact

Image edits now use the corrected inputs instead of silently reusing earlier work, including when a reference file is overwritten at the same path. Exact active and recent retries remain deduplicated. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the shared prompt-only preflight and match active work by the complete prepared request key. Image preparation loads references once, hashes the actual buffers passed to generation, and includes ordered `referenceInputs` facts (SHA-256, byte count, MIME type) in started, duplicate, and completed receipts. Request keys are bounded digests; printable receipts exclude inline image payloads. These facts describe observed inputs, not authority or proof of visual fidelity.

Video and music keep their existing request preparation and use the corrected shared matcher. This slice does not change review, delivery, supersession, or provider adapters.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the real `image_generate` execute entrypoint on base `91046f7bbbb8b064491ee2ecbfd782cb12b0124c`: four correction cases (different reference, overwritten same-path bytes, model, provider options) all returned `duplicateGuard: true` incorrectly. All four pass with the repair; exact retries start no extra job. The fixture uses real file loading and image-generation runtime with fixed external provider I/O, and checks the bytes/model/options received by the provider.
- Focused image/auth/ClawRouter, video/music, native resource lifetime, background retention, activity/status, reference loading, and prompt-prefix proof: 218 tests across 12 files passed (141.17 s wall). Final image/reference rerun after case-insensitive inline-payload redaction: 94 tests passed (49.08 s wall).
- Exact-head CI [43395586451](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43395586451) passed, including `security-fast`; the current-head combined CI/security gate also passed.
- Production and agents-tools test typechecks, targeted production/test lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. No package or build boundary changes.
- `pr-simplify`: removed the competing prompt-only preflight and obsolete prompt-only fixture; retained one prepared identity owner. Against the base: production +4 net lines; tests/support +53 net lines.
- Fresh independent local autoreview, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, base `91046f7bbbb8b064491ee2ecbfd782cb12b0124c` against local snapshot SHA-256 `1afcdcefa5921a9fb6b0771d3554d6cdefc0a30a85b8fa0ee33c7f0518c5c486`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because the existing runner checkout is dirty. The completed hosted review of `b5d746d1c2d9859feb1300907a197adb1cfa2807` found no actionable code defects and retained only the coordinator's integration decision.
- **Integration decision:** the coordinator exercised current-main combined with this exact identity head and review head `ea5e4ecca7cd9f74ba63826ccef24955254b2778` through the real `image_generate`, background-task, and durable-review suites successfully, and released this independent bug fix for native landing on November 13. The separate review-mode request-key repair belongs to the review slice, not this PR.

body:
Related #172740.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup fails after an upgrade when historical ACP metadata references a deleted or unconfigured agent database that Doctor intentionally leaves at an older schema.

## User Impact

Configured agents can start while those retained stores stay unavailable and untouched. Configured databases with older schemas still require offline repair; no schema, config, migration, or retention behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

ACP startup validation followed historical row owners before the session maintenance loop applied its configured/deleted-store exclusions. Scope that validation to the existing configured physical database targets and candidate paths, retaining shared-store ownership checks and admission refusals. Historical ACP metadata remains preserved for explicit restoration.

## Evidence

- Existing startup owner regression, `startup scopes old-schema ACP stores`: on base `066c7ecdeccf3f958d356cfdadac7a7146133021`, retained-by-deletion and unconfigured schema-41 stores both reject with `gateway.maintenance_required` (required schema 42); the configured-store rejection control passes. title: test(workers): wait for forced deletion queue handoff
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`checks-node-compact-large-11` failed intermittently on main (run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43365616669, job 131689709942). In `provider-destroy-authority.test.ts`, the non-revoked forced deletion sometimes returned failure. The same case passed in an earlier scheduled run with identical test and owner source.

## User Impact

None at runtime; test-only. Removes an intermittent red from the worker-environment shard.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test checks authority for a deletion that is queued before acceptance. For the forced path, it released the blocked provisioning, and revoked authority in the revoked variants, before the forced deletion had finished its placement preflight and entered the environment queue. That preflight reads inventory synchronously outside the queue. A released provisioning commit can fence those reads, so the request fails before it is ever queued.

The fixture now waits until the real `service.destroy` has been entered (the queue handoff) before releasing provisioning. All lifecycle, authority and provider-call assertions stay unchanged. The response assertion now includes the RPC error for future diagnosis.

Not changed here: a real forced deletion that races a provisioning commit during preflight can still fail transiently. This PR does not alter that production behavior.

## Evidence

- Source trace of the forced path: `server-methods/environments.ts` → `placement-dispatch-coordinator.ts` preflight (`readEnvironmentSessionIds`, inventory reads) → `service.destroy` queue (`provider-owner-lifecycle.ts`). The saved CI output omits the error payload, so the exact historical exception is source-inferred, not reproduced.

title: fix: report native Gateway subscriber buffer overflows
body:
Related: #198112

Stacked dependency: this patch is based on #198112 at `39c91efdee179c71f914d83d9f0cc94608fcc133`. Keep that event-admission change separate. The authored delta is exactly four files: the two queue owners and their two native test files; dependency changes are not new work in this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: native Gateway subscriber buffer overflows leave no diagnostic record when a consumer falls behind.

## User Impact

Operators can now see when a native subscriber overflows and how many deliveries it dropped during its lifetime. There is no UI or delivery/recovery change: buffer sizes, filtering, newest-event retention, grouped replies, sidebar animation, and word fade stay unchanged.

This is a diagnostics-only draft. Exact-head Mac/iOS builds, native tests, and log capture remain pending; no performance improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing subscriber owners now count actual AsyncStream drops, warn on the first one, and report at most one lifetime total on removal. A subscriber produces at most two content-free warning records and no records when it has no drops. Counts saturate rather than wrap and disappear with the subscriber. Normal delivery does not update counters, format logs, read a clock, or allocate diagnostic tasks.

The macOS owner applies this consistently to initial snapshots, ordinary pushes, and retirement publications. Existing admission filters and the separate realtime-audio overflow failure path remain intact. No replay, synthetic sequence gap, resubscription, configuration, storage, or public API is added. A process exit can prevent the final lifetime summary; no durable reporting is introduced.

## Evidence

- Added/extended real owner-stream regressions for admitted versus filtered traffic, independent fast/slow subscribers, newest-delivery retention, cancellation, replacement counters, zero-capacity initial snapshots, and retirement drops. Existing DEBUG push fixtures expose the actual counters; tests do not fabricate yield results.
- `git diff --check` and reverse applicability of the exported patch pass on Linux.
- Simplify pass: one integer in each existing subscriber record and one macOS yield helper shared by all three publication paths; no general queue framework. Net production growth: 48 lines; net test growth: 87 lines.
- Independent autoreview, OpenClaw engine, P0–P2, pinned base `39c91efdee179c71f914d83d9f0cc94608fcc133` to the local candidate: no actionable findings. Final subsequent edit only wraps one log call. Native compilation was not part of that review.

title: improve(ios): avoid reformatting unchanged parts of streaming replies
body:
## What problem this solves

While a native iOS reply streams, unchanged Markdown sections are repeatedly prepared for display. A long answer with 32 stable sections and a growing final paragraph performed 66 block preparations per processed update.

## What changed

Keep preparation in the mounted streaming view and reuse prepared blocks only when their semantic input, completion state, reveal role, and localized disclosure summary still match. Changed segments still use the complete Markdown parser, so later references and structural changes remain parser-owned.

The current-main integration narrows this PR to two renderer files, their focused preparation tests, and one generated translation-source entry for the existing “Details” key. The former parent, #192232, has landed. Its old reader, list, and fence changes are no longer part of this PR's delta; current main's scrolling and incomplete-fence behavior are preserved.

There is no global cache or new throttle. The retained data is the current streaming snapshot, not a history of updates. A single growing paragraph still requires its normal parsing and preparation.

## Current verification

Candidate: `a1606c583ec86db498114f565476cec3c4fd2a23`, integrated with main `4cbd215af463775faa6807aea90621292b28af15`. Its full tree matches the independently reviewed and tested four-file port.

Actual compiler-coverage counts, with separate cold and warm processes:

| Workload | Main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 32 sections: initial block preparations | 66 | 66 |
| 32 sections: preparations over 128 subsequent updates | 8,448 | 128 |
| One growing paragraph: preparations over 128 updates | 128 | 128 |
| Full snapshot/parser initialization over 129 inputs | 129 | 129 |

This proves less repeated preparation, not faster full parsing. No first-content latency, frame-rate, CPU, or memory improvement is claimed.

- 129 permanent shared-package tests across five suites passed on macOS, plus the temporary measurement workload, which was removed afterward.
- SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, generated translation inventory verification, and independent whole-change review passed.
- Both normal iOS app builds passed. In Simulator, the same simulated loopback Gateway sent 32 sections with bold text/links and 128 tail updates. Sending, streaming reveal, scrolling, Jump, and final content were checked on both builds. Final text was identical.
- After a manual scroll had settled, two pre-update readings and the readings after further deltas and finalization had the same Y coordinate on each build: **0-point movement** in both.
- The first fixture launch omitted a connection-state flag and produced no reply; it was excluded and corrected. An initial scroll capture included gesture deceleration; the settled controls above resolve that ambiguity.
- The fixture is simulated, not a real model/provider or persistence qualification. Link destinations were not opened. GitHub CI remains separately visible on the published head.

## Before/After

The images below show the same streaming checkpoint and completed tail. They are cropped native-app captures with synthetic content. The matching checkpoint images are byte-identical.

Videos show streaming and manual navigation. The baseline video joins its first eight and last ten seconds to remove an idle inspection interval; these clips are **not a timing comparison**.

![Before: native iOS streaming checkpoint on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6e6f57c-e731-4a04-b8e9-34dc2a03d793)

![After: same native iOS streaming checkpoint with block reuse](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a390d3f8-7380-4da2-863a-d63291a20d33)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c36030b-c605-452d-ae3b-43cee4f50cd0

## CI qualification

The [iOS screenshot job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44011875795/job/133801210281) built the app successfully and passed three of four screenshot cases. The static chat case failed at `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.swift:269` because the “Mermaid diagram” button did not appear.

The renderer trace shows the WebKit document remained in its loading phase, with `documentReady=false`, until its watchdog expired after 27,048 ms. The HTML resource had been delivered, but the document never reported ready.

This screenshot uses completed fixture history, not a streaming reply. The new streaming preparation is not instantiated; the shared snapshot receives `preparesReveal=false` and no previous snapshot, so the new reuse branch does not execute. The screenshot, fixture, Mermaid loader/resources, and build inputs are byte-identical between the actual CI baseline `f52f728d34158e66c0d11ce48cc7fb1c7a0cd6a7` and tested merge `6543bb204ee8d18a8093f3c032f20db408e1785b`. That merge contains the exact published head and only this PR's four-file change relative to its baseline.

Independent source review agrees this failure is outside the optimization's changed behavior. The underlying WebKit loading cause has not been isolated, and no baseline rerun is claimed. This failure is retained explicitly for the native unrelated-CI qualification; it is not reported as a passing screenshot test.

**Current landing hold:** [Android Play tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44011875795/job/133801210239) also ended **cancelled**, after GitHub's 20-minute job deadline. title: fix: preserve native inline widgets during revalidation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes inline widgets unnecessarily losing their loaded page when a retained native chat row starts resource resolution again.

## User Impact

Same-owner widgets can keep their interactive state while their current source is re-resolved. Layout, grouped replies, sidebar animation, and word fade are unchanged. True row destruction still releases the WebView.



## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the mounted document during same-path revalidation instead of clearing it first. Continue resolving on every ready task appearance, and replace or retire the document when resolution changes or fails. Existing model identity and session target/generation bound the widget's SwiftUI identity, so a retained row cannot reuse its browser across chat owners.

Keep the current TLS, navigation, script, capability-refresh, snapshot, and bounded-retry policies. Refresh retained failure callbacks and recovery metadata, serialize a browser failure behind in-flight resolution, and invalidate snapshots whenever the load generation changes. An unchanged URL/TLS binding with new recovery metadata keeps the document and updates its callbacks; a recovery that returns the same failed resource now retires the dead page. No global WebView pool, skipped resolution, new route-fencing protocol, or public API change is introduced.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification used `c9c4e57f636be83d6c8b1c90f1682c9c8a31d895` plus formatting-only patch `1b0be6d404b6a8b2d03387b26b45450c1ff79c53fc9bf016f46d86301ce1c102`:

- In the actual iOS app with a synthetic Gateway and loopback HTTP widgets, matched revalidation of five widgets created five new WebViews/document GETs on the base and none on the candidate.
- Widget 00 reset its local state from 1 to 0 on the base and retained 1 on the candidate. Session changes still recreated browsers.

title: improve(ios): reduce repeated work while reading long chats
body:
Related: #192232

## What Problem This Solves

Reading long chats can repeatedly prepare the same transcript during unrelated view updates and scroll callbacks; an unfinished code fence inside a streamed list could also enable highlighting or Mermaid rendering before closure.

## User Impact

Reduces redundant transcript preparation while preserving the current chat design, grouped replies, reader position, sidebar animation, and streaming word fade. Native build, device behavior, and measured performance are still pending; this is a draft for the Mac verification loop, not a ready-to-merge performance claim.

**Stacked dependency:** Vyctor accepted stacking this new PR on #192232 at `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d`. The inherited dependency changes shown against main are not this fix. The authored delta against that immutable head is seven files: the original five-file transcript preparation plus a two-file streamed-list fence repair requested during review. This PR does not modify #192232, does not duplicate #194235 composer isolation, and requests no merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

One mounted chat now retains one immutable prepared transcript for its actual message, narration, reader-history, display-policy, session/model, run, and tool inputs. Rendering and scroll callbacks share its rows, footer metadata, groups, iOS cells, and turn anchors; split-row actions reuse the already-projected full current message instead of projecting history again per part.

The existing rendering, grouping, visibility, and scroll policies remain the owners of behavior. The cache is bounded to one preparation per view, reads observed dependencies even on hits, and does not rely on timeline notifications alone. This does not implement changed-delta incremental Markdown or remove the existing live-text reconciliation work. Input comparison and retained preparation have a CPU/memory cost that still needs device measurement.

The review repair propagates message completion through every recursive list level and accepts fence closure only when the parser consumed a matching closer inside the list item. Shorter, mismatched, trailing-content, over-indented, and outside-list fence-looking lines remain incomplete. It is equivalent to the minimal fix in #198122 at `57ba92122c12c94f95504d51c4d9462ff66c7343`, without importing that PR’s other changes.

Simplification removed duplicate callback preparation and the forwarding grouping wrapper. Against the dependency head: production +236/-133 lines (net +103); tests +307 lines. The fence repair itself is +28/-1 production lines and +66 test lines. The retained growth supplies the one-entry owner and its invalidation/reuse proof; no durable state, schema, setting, or dependency change is authored here.

## Evidence

- Published head: `833e8853e47b872c25376df602cc4631ebb5abeb`. Remote GitHub commit/compare reads verify its sole parent is the original published head `da48e3f1521eb2ddab73783fc529771c79b0c794`. It is two commits ahead of `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d`; all seven changed remote blobs match the inspected local files. The new commit changes only `ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenter.swift` and `apps/ios/Tests/ChatStreamingCodeFenceTests.swift` (+94/-1). Both required human coauthor trailers are present. GitHub currently reports conflicts against main (`mergeState: dirty`); the accepted dependency base is intentionally preserved for this draft build loop, not rebased.
- Integration base: `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d`; independent managed worktree was clean before applying the reviewed patch.
- Original transcript preparation (unchanged by the fence repair): exact v2 patch: 38,070 UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256 `e9f9836e42f54bc12f07b3018c3f4150e83a38788ac85fdd5bc331e8e40e8bb7`. Verified checksum, five-file allowlist, clean exact base, forward apply check, reverse apply check, and `git diff --check`. Inspected the complete patch, original ChatView, and grouping/footer/history owners. No overlay, docs, skills, or source-transition changes are included in the authored delta.
- Fresh local Auto Review of the complete seven-file candidate against `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d`, OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no findings**. Static review only; native Apple builds/tests were not run and unavailable unchanged context was not independently verified. The original five-file implementation also retains its earlier parent-reported review evidence.
- Sibling sweep: rendering, initial-position restoration, timeline callbacks, iOS cell flattening, macOS grouping/search, completed-work rows, and full-message actions now share preparation. Reader snapshot capture and live-text reconciliation still need their own current-state projection; they were inspected and left unchanged. Composer, sidebar, and word-fade implementations are unchanged. The fence-repair sibling sweep covered top-level fences, recursive ordered/unordered lists, tab indentation, disclosure recursion, and both highlight/Mermaid consumers. Top-level completion and disclosure propagation were already present; the missing propagation was in list preparation.
- Added `ChatTranscriptPresentationTests` cover interleaved independent readers and unrelated updates, policy/run/tool changes without timeline notifications, narration/history deletion/outbox/content changes, and full-message actions from split parts. These tests have **not run** here. Baseline red/green, test wall time, and CI seconds remain unmeasured.
- Addressed [the streamed-list completion finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198114#issuecomment-6845185461). Added two parameterized `ChatStreamingCodeFenceTests` at the real segmenter boundary for ordered/unordered/nested/tab/same-line list fences, valid closure or final-message completion, and invalid/outside closers. Current pre-repair source hardcodes these blocks complete; the new `!isComplete` assertions target that defect directly. Executed native red/green proof and timing remain **pending**, not claimed. `git diff --check` and final seven-file allowlist/original-five-blob preservation checks passed.
- Linux environment: Swift, Xcode, and SwiftLint are unavailable. Native compile, focused Swift tests, simulator/iOS-specific cells, macOS shared-consumer checks, device work counts, and before/after video are pending at the published head. No timing or UI-success result is claimed. The user's Mac agent owns that build/proof loop; leave this draft until those results exist.

### Pending Mac verification

At `833e8853e47b872c25376df602cc4631ebb5abeb`, with Xcode 27.1+ / Swift 6.3 and a task-owned simulator:

~~~sh
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = 833e8853e47b872c25376df602cc4631ebb5abeb
swift --version
xcodebuild -version
swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'ChatTranscriptPresentationTests|ChatTranscriptRowTests|ChatAssistantRunGroupTests|ChatReaderScrollStateTests|ChatInlineNarrationRegressionTests|ChatTranscriptSearchTests|ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenterTests' --no-parallel
pnpm ios:build
IOS_SIM="<task-owned simulator UDID>" pnpm ios:test ChatStreamingCodeFenceTests SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests ChatTypingFocusTests ChatSendHydrationTests
~~~

For the red control, use a separate task-owned checkout at `da48e3f1521eb2ddab73783fc529771c79b0c794` with only the new `ChatStreamingCodeFenceTests.swift` copied from the candidate. Run `pnpm ios:build`, then `IOS_SIM="<task-owned simulator UDID>" pnpm ios:test ChatStreamingCodeFenceTests`; the incomplete-fence assertions should fail there and pass on the candidate. A setup/build failure is not the red control. Also exercise an unfinished Mermaid and Swift fence inside a nested streamed list through the actual app, then close the fence and finish the message; attach sanitized before/after screenshots and video before marking ready.

Also run the new package tests on an iOS simulator so the conditional List-cell assertions execute (a host-only SwiftPM run cannot cover them). Confirm the selected destination/scheme supports that package test target before claiming iOS test coverage.

Before timing, compare dependency base versus candidate on the same synthetic long chat and device: settled history, streaming while reading above the live edge, trace/search toggles, narration/tool handoff, outbox insertion/removal, history trimming/deletion, session replacement, and split-row copy/reply/select-text actions. Preserve grouped/disclosure identity, reader position, return-to-latest behavior, sidebar animation, and word fade. Capture before/after video with the exact head, device, OS, fixture, and build configuration recorded.

Acceptance rule: count actual preparation/group/cell builds first. After the initial preparation, unchanged relevant inputs must cause zero additional full preparations; a relevant input change must produce fresh correct rows. Compare baseline/candidate serially in ABAB order with at least five samples each, separating cold and warm results. Record main-thread/total CPU, frame latency/hitches, cold-open latency, and peak memory with median, p95, and spread. Require a measured reduction in repeated preparation and no correctness/UI regression; a 20% regression in any user-facing metric is a stop, not a pass. The owner test's reuse counts are not a substitute for device performance or UI proof.

title: fix: unrelated Gateway traffic crowds native chat event queues
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary native chat work when a Gateway sends events that chat never uses; those events also compete with useful updates in bounded queues.

## User Impact

Gateway event names unsupported by chat no longer enter the iOS/macOS chat event queues. Chat presentation, grouped replies, sidebar animation, word fade, and supported chat effects are unchanged. Snapshot-only onboarding and sidebar-catalog observers also stop queuing unrelated server events.


## Why This Change Was Made

The shared chat codec now owns one event-name registry used for both subscription admission and exhaustive payload dispatch. iOS uses the existing filtered subscription with explicit cleanup; macOS adds the same opt-in filter at its existing queue owner. Lifecycle publications bypass the macOS event predicate.

Filtering does not inspect a mutable agent/session selection, payload, reason, or stream. New reasons and stream variants under supported event names remain admitted. Unknown names and bounded narration tails already mapped to no chat effect; their transport-frame decoding is unchanged, but they no longer occupy chat queues or trigger chat mapping attempts.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification used head `39c91efdee179c71f914d83d9f0cc94608fcc133` plus comment-only formatting patch `b7c87386059634df8cc1b9468b24c16f6c27c4e3c209447777e65cd333bad33e`:

- iOS and macOS builds passed. Source-selected macOS tests passed two shared and 49 macOS methods; baseline original contracts passed one and 48 respectively.
- In the actual iOS app, a synthetic Gateway delivered 57 events: 50 unmapped events, six chat events, and one agent event. Chat decoder entries decreased from 57 to seven, retaining all admitted chat/agent events.
- Final output, same-endpoint reconnect, and Stop were observed. Sending again after Stop on the candidate was not completed because automation timed out.
- This filters event names, not every event belonging to a different session. No natural buffer-overflow, Gateway/account-switch, latency, CPU, or RSS claim is made.
- The source-selected runner and synthetic transport are supporting limits of this proof; this is not a claim of a full unmodified-package or real-provider run.


### CI consumer repair

The typed event registry exposed a gap in the protocol-coverage checker: it recognized literal switch cases but not the codec's `EventKind(rawValue: frame.event)` switch. The checker now resolves the handled cases in that same scope. The existing regression fixture also checks unused enum members and unrelated switches, so merely declaring an event cannot satisfy coverage.

The iOS allowlist explicitly records `session.narration`, which the previous codec already discarded in favor of full narration events. This documents existing behavior; it does not remove a supported event.

On published head `006b357fd04c4d3aceb81b620f4d8723909e083f`: all 10 checker tests, protocol coverage, the targeted tooling typecheck, lint, and formatting pass. The regression failed before the checker repair. Independent scoped review found no actionable issues. The native event-filter implementation is unchanged from the runtime verification above.

The current-head iOS screenshot job passed; the earlier Mermaid timeout did not repeat, and this PR does not claim to have fixed it. The remaining CI failures are unrelated mainline checks: the mock-export baseline for `worker-request-diagnostics.test.ts` and the wrapper dependency manifest for `worker-request-delivery-report.runtime.ts`. title: improve(ios): avoid duplicate storage recovery on cold activation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

When iOS activation opens its local databases, it immediately repeats the storage recovery that opening them already performed.

## User Impact

When unpaired scene activation first opens the databases, it performs one recovery pass instead of two. Later activations still retry pending cleanup and legacy imports, including after permission dialogs or Control Center. The UI and recovery safeguards are unchanged.

This is a bounded recovery-work improvement, not completion of the broader resume-performance goal. Ordinary warm activations, including Control Center returns, remain unchanged and synchronous. No responsiveness improvement has been measured yet. If initial recovery fails transiently, the next activation retries it instead of immediately repeating it in the same activation; unresolved removal markers continue to block writable access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The database initializer already resolves pending gateway removals before importing legacy state. Activation now either opens that owner or recovers an existing owner, rather than doing both. Existing-owner quarantine checks and retry ordering are retained. There is no new cache, worker, schema, permission, or persistence contract.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on `34bcfeb9f77eac945372e445fb38e1abbeffeff2`, compared with `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`:

- The iOS build passed. Focused app tests passed 430 candidate cases; the base passed 428 with the expected pause-test failure. Legacy-import tests passed 12/12 on both versions.
- Actual app counters showed registry/removal/import work decreasing from two passes to one only when the databases first opened inside unpaired scene activation. Paired cold startup still did two passes on both variants; warm activation did one on both.
- A locally built `v2026.11.3` app and synthetic state created through its stable storage APIs verified retained data, staged removal, warm idempotence, re-pairing, and reset behavior.
- This was not a distributed-binary upgrade or a mid-SQL crash test. Seeded history was verified in storage rather than on screen. No latency, CPU, or RSS improvement is claimed.

The completed [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43618104327) failed only the iOS screenshot job and its aggregate gate. Security checks passed. The screenshot failure waited for a Mermaid diagram while WebKit was severely delayed: document commit at 17.13 seconds, then the renderer watchdog at 25.11 seconds. During that interval the five-CPU runner reported 0% idle CPU, load 223-283, and a process-list probe timed out.

title: fix: keep native chat images stable while replies stream
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary image recreation when a native chat reply containing inline data images is prepared repeatedly during streaming.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is stable inline images while native iOS and macOS replies stream, without changing layout, supported formats, fallback labels, grouped replies, sidebar animation, or word fade. Actual mounted-identity reuse and UI equivalence still require Mac/device execution. No configuration or migration is required.

This is a draft for the exact-head Mac build and device-proof loop. Native compilation, runtime decode counts, performance measurements, and before/after video are still pending; no measured speedup is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Markdown preparation previously decoded every inline data image and generated a new UUID on every pass. Even the user-message metadata sanitizer paid that decoding cost before discarding the images.

Preparation now records the source and a forward occurrence index, so duplicates remain distinct and appended copies do not change earlier IDs. The existing image-list consumer owns decoding in a retained SwiftUI StateObject, once per mounted image identity. Changing the source creates a new identity; current labels still update. Removal releases view-owned state, subject to SwiftUI's normal lifecycle. Remounting can decode again.

There is no process-wide cache, eviction policy, disk storage, URL fetch, or new image-size restriction. The encoded slice refers only to an image source, not to a growing reply. The same platform decoder and existing remote-image flattening remain in use. The separate managed-attachment thumbnail path is unchanged. The metadata sanitizer still discards inline user images exactly as before; this patch removes the wasted decoding, not that existing behavior.

Human contributor credit: Vyctor Brzezowski and Mike Nguyen.
