title: fix: keep native chat math warm when caches fill
body:
Related: #198080 (same eviction pattern; this change does not depend on that PR).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary repeated math parsing and image rendering in native chat when adding an expression fills the existing math caches.

## User Impact

Previously rendered expressions can remain warm as more math arrives, without changing typography, grouping, sidebar animation, word fade, or raw-source fallbacks. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both 80-entry math caches currently discard all entries on the next miss. They now evict only the oldest entry. Cached parse failures still occupy a bounded slot, and hits do not reorder entries or add bookkeeping work. FIFO deliberately keeps the fix small; a working set larger than 80 entries can still miss.

The image key also includes the display scale already used by its pixel-budget guard, so a scale change cannot reuse an image without rechecking that budget. Font size and resolved color remain part of the key. Parser guards, source-byte limits, bitmap bounds, SwiftMath configuration, and baseline calculation are unchanged.

## Evidence

- In the actual iOS app with a synthetic Gateway, both variants produced 80 distinct images. Revisiting expression 40 after pressure caused one parse-cache miss and image render on the base, versus neither on the candidate. Both received two image requests.
- Inspected video samples and final frames showed equivalent, legible formulas.

title: fix(apple): avoid rebuilding chat for voice meter updates
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary chat-surface invalidation when microphone or voice-playback levels change in iOS or native macOS Chat.

## User Impact

The change is intended to keep live voice meters updating without rebuilding the enclosing chat surface. It preserves the current UI, grouped replies, sidebar animation, word fade, and capture/session ownership. No migration or user configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Apple chat hosts read live meter values while creating shared voice controls; iOS also reads them in the header avatar. Defer the control values until the existing waveform consumers render, and move header metering into an internal avatar view. The optional main-actor level providers preserve existing mutable scalar inputs and scalar callers. Recording actions, handoff guards, phase precedence, and the header's nil-playback animation fallback remain unchanged.

This deletes the eager metering dependency rather than adding a cache, throttling samples, or changing transcript rendering. The existing platform control builders take their owners explicitly so regressions exercise production construction rather than copied test adapters. macOS keeps its primary-Gateway-only control guard, pause/status behavior, input selection, and Talk action. Production delta: +137/-92 lines; test delta: +153/-2 lines; generated localization inventory: one unreachable string removed.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on published head `8d8b8980bcd490cd37524fc8d15d431fd8345e69`, using base `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`:

- Focused native app, shared-control, and macOS publishing tests passed. Candidate coverage included 310 app cases, five shared-control cases, and five macOS publishing cases.
- A negative control restoring only the eager iOS Talk-level read failed the two observation cases; the source was restored afterward. This isolates the eager-read defect, rather than claiming a full unmodified-base run of those cases.
- The production control builders no longer subscribe their enclosing caller to meter-only changes. Waveform/avatar consumers still observe the changing values; phase, mute, lifecycle, and scalar fallback contracts remain covered.
- Real microphone/playback capture was not exercised. Native dictation is guarded off on the simulator, and the separate Realtime audio path was not configured. No full-app audio, frame-time, CPU, or latency claim is made.
- Source review found no new cache, preference read, RPC, or recording owner. The demonstrated result is observation isolation and preserved control contracts.

title: fix(ios): avoid sidebar reloads on chat switches and brief interruptions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: switching same-agent chats or briefly opening Control Center needlessly restarts the iOS sidebar's roster, dashboard reads, and session subscription.

## User Impact

User impact: switching conversations and returning from a temporary inactive overlay no longer invalidate unrelated sidebar data. The current UI, selected-row presentation, sidebar animation, grouped replies, and word fade are unchanged. This draft still needs native build, runtime request-count, and before/after device evidence; no speedup is claimed yet. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected chat is a presentation input, not an input to these shared reads. Remove it from the refresh identity and retain an already-admitted foreground task lifetime through `.inactive`. One scene-local Boolean starts false, admits work on `.active`, and closes it on `.background`; cold or background-to-inactive transitions cannot start work. Gateway, agent, connectivity, and authority changes still invalidate the tasks.

Observer visibility remains **active-only**. Permission refreshes, microphone/capture gates, discovery, reconnect checks, and storage recovery are unchanged. RootTabs' separate branding/agent overview refresh still runs on activation: this does not eliminate all activation traffic. Event-driven updates and the ten-minute refresh remain; if an overlay stays inactive that long, the periodic read can still run until actual background. No new timer, debounce, cooldown, cache, or manager.

Contributor credit: @vyctorbrzezowski and @mikengyn.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6b98dedd-1923-4f79-837e-5d48ac84b6c4)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b12bdfba-cb0b-43f7-a2f5-ca17649c42bc)

## Evidence

- Base: `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`.
- Source trace: roster requests use Gateway and agent, dashboard requests use Gateway scope, and approval inbox reads use the authenticated Gateway route. None consumes the selected chat key. Selection remains observed directly by `RootSidebar`.
- Added an opt-in UI regression that launches the real app against the existing synthetic loopback Gateway, warms one chat, then switches five times between two same-agent chats. It records requests and requires zero additional root roster reads, dashboard reads, or global subscriptions while both histories still load. Chat's separate 50-row metadata reads are intentionally permitted.
- Added `RootSidebarLifecycleTests`: mounted real RootTabs with serialized requests captured at the existing Gateway test socket. Covers initial inactive/first active, three inactive/active cycles, active-only visibility, event consumption while inactive, background cancellation, background-to-inactive staying closed, and foreground restart. It controls scene phases; actual Control Center and permission-sheet transitions remain device-proof gaps.
- `git diff --check`: passed. New-file whitespace check and packaged-patch reverse check: no diagnostics.
- Local autoreview, OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, complete three-file uncommitted candidate against the base above: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Native execution remained explicitly unverified. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; the required final-range review/publication route remains parent-owned.
- Simplification: one invalidation input removed and one scene-local admission Boolean retained by the existing owner; no model, rendering, decoder, storage, or voice changes. Production delta: +16/-5; test delta: +271 lines. The mounted boundary test adds no production test hook.
- **Pending:** Xcode build, SwiftLint/SwiftFormat, red-on-base/green-on-candidate UI and mounted-lifecycle regressions, affected native suites, physical-device performance and before/after video. This Linux host has no Swift or Xcode toolchain. Test wall time and CI seconds are not yet available.

### Acceptance rule (set before native runs)

Use the same isolated Gateway, synthetic chats, device, appearance, and workload on base and candidate. After initial load, switch between two same-agent chats five times. Per switch, candidate must issue **zero** extra sidebar `sessions.list(limit: 200)`, `usage.cost`, `cron.list`, or `sessions.subscribe` calls; selected history and selected-row presentation must remain correct. The synthetic fixture proves outgoing requests, not successful usage data or real-Gateway performance.

Then keep the sidebar visible and open/dismiss Control Center five times without going Home. Establish the actual scene sequence in Xcode: inactive/active-only cycles must produce zero additional shared calls, while observer visibility follows true/false/true. Separately background and return: shared work must restart. Verify first activation, owner/authority changes during inactivity, retained session events, and permission updates. Compare this extension against original draft head `6d8fcadbd7eac451cf4d042f10ce4d2edd4a6b85` as well as the full base.

Keep cold and warm runs separate. For device timing, collect at least five interleaved base/candidate samples, record host load, median/p95 and spread for tap-to-history completion and animation hitches, and report CPU/memory changes. Reject regressions or obtain explicit acceptance; investigate any 20% regression. Verify agent/Gateway switches, reconnect, authority changes, foregrounding, session events, and the periodic refresh still refresh their scopes.

title: fix(ios): retain code highlights when the cache fills

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary code re-highlighting when the native chat cache fills and discards every previously highlighted block.

title: improve(ui): offer "Report a bug" only on chat errors OpenClaw cannot explain
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every chat error notice carries a "Report a bug" link, including errors with a known cause and a clear next step, such as a draft that could not be saved, a busy session, or an expired sign-in. The link is accent-colored and sits where the recovery action belongs, so it reads as the main action on notices where reporting does not help.

## User Impact

User impact: chat error notices offer "Report a bug" only when OpenClaw cannot explain the failure, and the link is a quiet secondary link after the recovery action.

- Notices with a written explanation no longer show the link: draft storage, session busy, sign-in, permission and connection messages, and the discard-and-reload start conflict.
- Notices that can only show a raw failure keep it: a reply that failed for an unknown reason, a session that could not start, and failed reactions, session suggestions, task suggestions, forks from a message, and session-menu actions.
- A notice with no recovery action and no link has no action slot. On phones the recovery button stays beside the title and the link moves to the last row.
- The reply-failed card in the transcript follows the same rule. A failure with a named cause, such as rejected credentials, billing, a rate limit, an overloaded provider, or a timeout, has no link. A failure without one keeps a quiet link after the recovery actions.
- "Report a bug" in the sidebar Help menu and on the connection error page is unchanged.

Sources are opted in one at a time, and the default is no link. An unexpected failure from a source that is not opted in loses the one-click link; the Help menu entry still opens the same form.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared chat error notice attached the link unconditionally and received page-level errors as plain text, so it could not tell a written explanation from a raw failure. Deciding from the message text would be guessing. Instead, a source that has no explanation of its own now passes the raw failure along with its message, through the detail channel the error owner already had, and the notice offers reporting only when that raw failure is present. The reply-failed and session-start notices already know their failure kind and pass the decision directly. No new state or props travel through the chat pane.

Two side effects of reusing that channel:

- A raw failure that carries extra Gateway details now also gets the existing "Show details" disclosure.
- A raw failure that spans several lines keeps its first line as the title and the rest under details, as before.

Accepted edge case: a missing-permission error that reaches one of the opted-in sources is shown with its written explanation and still gets the link. These actions are checked for access before the request is sent, so this needs a permission change while the request is in flight.

The transcript card already receives the failover reason of the failed run. It offers reporting when there is no reason, or when the reason leaves the cause open: `format`, `empty_response`, `no_error_details`, `unclassified`, and `unknown`. A reason added later counts as explained until it is added to that list.

Overlap: #197822 restructures the same card and will need a rebase over this change. Its author asked for this order.

## Evidence

Screenshots are the production Control UI build against a mocked Gateway with synthetic messages, in Chromium, light theme, at 100% scale. "Before" is the base `0633f256350b`. Each failure comes from the real flow: IndexedDB writes rejected in the page for the draft notice, a `chat` error event after a real send for the reply notices, a rejected `session.reactions.set` after picking a reaction, and a failed run in the session history for the transcript card.

title: improve: compact person activity cards
body: ## What Problem This Solves The person activity card gives connection diagnostics too much space, spreads its header over several metadata lines, and makes the sessions people are viewing harder to scan. ## User Impact People get a compact horizontal header: avatar beside the name and exactly one metadata line. That line answers whether the person is around and what time it is for them: Active, Idle for 14m, Online when activity is unknown, or Offline, followed by their local time only when it differs from the viewer's. Long names truncate to one line with the full name on hover; the reported zone name appears on hover over the time. When someone reports two zones, the card shows the one from the connection they used most recently. Device details, Last interaction and connection duration no longer occupy the card; connection details remain on the Activity page. Session rows are simpler, View activity is a full-width action, and long Viewing now titles use the same single-line fade and hover scrolling as Recent sessions. Touch and reduced-motion users keep the existing two-line fallback. ## Why This Change Was Made This implements the requested visual redesign without changing presence, session visibility, navigation, or authorization ownership. The existing avatar, clock, marquee, and focus owners provide the behavior. Redundant fact rows, row icons, wrappers, separator styling and the multi-clock list are removed. Design direction and iteration with @vyctorbrzezowski. ## Work sessions Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public. - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e42cbdf2-a046-4f56-be91-b2977d662559) ## Evidence - 92 focused component/sidebar tests passed, including idle-duration timers releasing on disconnect, switch, route, collapse, shell, remove and teardown. - 24 person-card and person-reference browser flow tests passed, plus light/dark captures of eight states (active, idle, same time zone, long name, two zones, unknown activity, shared owner, offline). Captures used a browser pinned to Europe/Lisbon; tests use a far-off zone so the local-time suffix does not depend on the host zone. - UI typecheck, formatting, i18n verification, and targeted style lint passed. ## What Problem This Solves

The lazy tool-row test can assert that the permission card exists before its independent import finishes.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This corrects the test’s readiness expectation without changing production rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197466 made the permission-card import separate from the row import. Waiting for the row-import spy only observes factory admission; it does not join the permission-card import. The test now uses the existing `waitForSolid` helper around the actual `.chat-permission-card` assertion, retaining the same selector and strict `not.toBeNull()` matcher. The two original CI failures at heads `709411d3d91d81bdac172d4519517bd3c2767b2d` and `ad3ab25320de4b39bebb776f4081e3c12e5a33a8` predate that boundary and imported the permission card eagerly, so their exact mechanism remains unproven.

## Evidence

- Controlled RED on base `02f29597c1075c0db5193fe2e3f2d5409593cfba`: a temporary test-local deferred module mock held the real permission-card import, confirmed factory admission, and queued release in a microtask before the unchanged synchronous assertions. One focused run failed with `expected null not to be null` at `chat-tool-row-lazy.test.tsx:129:69` (1 file, 1 test failed).

Each case ran once under `timeout 120s` with `node scripts/ui.js test --project unit src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-row-lazy.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`.
- RED / controlled GREEN / ordinary GREEN test times: 97 / 260 / 251 ms; runner durations: 1.55 / 1.51 / 1.50 s. Separate command wall times and CI seconds were not captured.
- Touched-file typecheck passed using the matching UI-chat test config with a single test include, `incremental: false`, and explicit worktree `node_modules/@types`. This resolves the earlier scratch-config Node-type lookup failure. Touched-file lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed.

title: feat: export and install offline worker runtime artifacts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Image-preparation tools need a supported way to export the installed OpenClaw worker runtime and install transferred archives without enrolling a node. Prerequisite #188651 is merged; this PR targets main.

## User Impact

Tool authors can use `openclaw/runtime-artifacts` to qualify bundled plugins and export canonical offline node/worker archives. Crabbox's lazy CLI API installs verified local archives without a logical lease, forwarded credentials, npm, lifecycle scripts, or plugin activation. Bundle enrollment needs matching Node and tar; explicit npm installations and repository setup retain npm/npx/Corepack where applicable. Existing remote npm installations retain their lock/reuse behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public entrypoint composes existing artifact producers, joins both before cleanup, and returns build, archive and digest identities. Bundled qualification uses a detached inspection registry. Local transfer is an adapter in the existing installer, not a second installer. Only `./runtime-artifacts` is added to package exports; declarations and documentation are included.

History-preserving integration retains upstream root/Codex fs-safe 0.27.0 and the source-inspection worker-boundary fix in #188870. The lock was regenerated with pinned pnpm; dependency graph and integrity data match upstream, with canonical ordering differences only. The `/node-runtime-dependencies/` artifact ignore and accurate troubleshooting prerequisites are restored. Read-only cache verification remains separate in #188671.

## Evidence

### Current source, tests and review

- Published head **`ee479a542b773fead85d101d915f8b21d3521853`** has reviewed tree **`d175c65ee19fcaaf087c1f49e808efac8916c38f`**. Authored source merge **`842de317b317a604492c4a5d10277e8a6d28f5fa`** preserves parents `ef8db05f` and main `ece4ca85af0e0ffa7cc619522b9e8b7e40b08da9`.
- Both conflicts retain upstream repairs: the shared Gateway logger fixture exactly matches main; rollout tests preserve upstream targeted notification delivery and final no-read assertion, plus coarse directory timestamps, warm-cache reuse and controlled watcher-loss coverage. Real rename/unlink and exact membership oracles remain. No production scanner fence, sleep or weaker assertion was added.
- **60 focused tests pass**: API 5, Gateway scope consumers 30, Workboard 2, rollout 20 and offline installer 3 (126.24s wrapper). Withholding only the three final notifications fails the original membership oracle; restored source passes. This is controlled notification evidence, not an observed kernel-watcher cause.
- Targeted types, six-file type-aware lint (293 rules; zero warnings/errors), formatting, whitespace checks and normal hooks pass. Exact accounting: **6,321,781 / 6,352,142**. Rollout allocation is **16** net lines beyond integrated upstream; API **332** and Workboard **7** remain unchanged. No baseline, scalar or checker waiver.
- Fresh independent **P0–P3 autoreview is scoped-clean** for the complete 22-file delta against `ece4ca85`, with 13 complete unchanged owners. No actionable findings; final source verification passed, and the committed tree matches the reviewed staged tree.

### Canonical package build and recovery

- Linux x64 / Node 24.22.1, source **`842de317b317a604492c4a5d10277e8a6d28f5fa`**, actual build **`2026.10.9-842de317b317-2026-10-31T04-58-16.446Z`**.
- Full maintained runtime-only selected-Codex build completed in **6m 38s**, including UI, runtime postbuild, stamps and CLI metadata. A Gateway restart interrupted packaging afterward. Source, clean-input stamps and process settlement were verified; canonical postpack restoration reconciled the interruption. Supported package-only continuation reused the completed build without skipping any package checks.
- Canonical packaging passed in **98.34s**; tar preflight/extraction, npm 11.19.1 finished-archive inventory and distribution import graph all passed (**39s** integrity check). Public registry metadata and lock-pinned native input preparation used secretless isolation. Shared dependency installs were not modified.
- Canonical tarball: SHA-256 **`17cc2b32561fd72f3a1fa817d9817c55bb23ddf7f3409ac5797b9bdd5f54fb12`**, **111,178,480 bytes**.

### Actual installed-package public API boundary

- The canonical tarball was installed into a **fresh standalone npm consumer**, with normal preinstall/postinstall lifecycle and declared dependencies (**14.21s**). Its npm lock's tarball integrity matches the canonical finished-archive receipt. Raw extraction alone lacks ordinary npm dependencies; that setup failure is not counted as a product failure or successful proof.
- The proof imports bare **`openclaw/runtime-artifacts`** from that installed consumer and asserts its resolved URL is inside the installed package. Both qualification and export receive the real installed package root—not the source checkout. The installer is imported from the **same installed package's** `dist/extensions/crabbox/cli-runtime-api.js`; no descendant verifier code participates.
- With networking disabled, plugins-disabled and Codex-enabled selections each qualified and exported bundle-mode node/worker archives, then installed into fresh worker homes. Both real CLIs printed **`OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (842de31)`**. Installed agent schema **39**, fs-safe **0.27.0**, manifest digest and worker archive digest matched receipts. Installation plus CLI: **9.485s / 8.851s**; complete installed-package round trips: **97.83s**.
- The canonical input already bundles Codex, so the two selection receipts have different `enabledPluginIds` but identical exported node bytes. This proves both configuration paths; it does not claim a minimal Codex-free distribution.
- No enrollment state, logical lease, forwarded credentials or cloud allocation. Fresh receiver homes and owned build namespaces were removed. The installed producer and immutable exports are retained for the separate verifier lane.

<details>
<summary>Installed-package export identities</summary>

- Node archive, both selections: `b2c9a747f20d1d0f940e2836aef1d57f93ee8f812e64964fd12b9734d96f0c1b` — 293,213,073 bytes.
- Node manifest: `32efb5e97a141773a7fea076660c5065863bb7b4f3579ef0c0e4b0ef33110106`.
- Worker archive: `8d1d25c625cb31392ae493dfea1f3782084a90ba1a0e23f20b1194868024fbe1` — 22,863,074 bytes.

</details>

### Separate source-dist and earlier evidence

- The earlier **90.25s source-dist** export/install run remains valid separate evidence: its producer was the built checkout, not the npm-installed canonical package. Its node archive hashes (`a93c96e4…` core, `339ff4c3…` Codex) are not substituted for the installed-package exports above.
- Prior `49968f5` and `d4b533` build evidence retains its original identity. Source `49968f5` passed 78 focused tests. Upstream #188870 repaired the generated worker import boundary without weakening its guard; the original case ran and passed, while the earlier all-skipped run was not passing proof. The cross-test-contamination claim remains withdrawn.
- [CI job 124416178578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160183562/job/124416178578) reproduced on `9d193015` as **2 failed / 283 passed**. The coordinated owner fixture repair from `5b08bece` made the identical eight-file invocation pass **285/285**. Main now supplies the complete logger; this PR retains diagnostics save/enable/restore and the original closure/admission/card-list assertions.

### Scope and separate verifier

- Current-head CI and native landing remain maintainer-owned. No manual hosted CI rerun or merge was performed by this session.
- Separate #188671 owns read-only verification. The installed-package export set above is the final artifact handoff for its current-source no-effect controls. This PR's successful installation does not substitute for that verifier proof.
- Full release/declaration packaging, live Codex execution, Azure, macOS and Windows remain separate proof. Packaging here is runtime-only. Archive/manifest identity does not certify every installed payload byte or grant live execution authority.

title: fix: keep older commentary before unrelated chat input
body:
Closes #188641

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: older commentary can appear below an unrelated user message when its original prompt is outside the loaded history page.

## User Impact

User impact: retained progress stays with its original conversation turn instead of looking like a response to a newer request. This changes presentation only; it does not rewrite saved history or require configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recover the missing input boundary from retained output belonging to the same run. Saved-stream materialization and the live renderer share that recovery decision; the renderer preserves its existing steering, independent-turn, and forwarded-activity rules. Genuinely unanchored activity keeps its existing fallback. A run's own projected output does not become a recovered ceiling, keeping continued replies and their working indicator in the same run frame.

The patch changes only two production files. Added tests, their allocation record, and newly added code comments were removed at the requester's direction; existing tests are unchanged.

## Evidence

[Before/after browser screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188658#issuecomment-6532221191).

- Chromium with the production UI and mocked Gateway startup/preamble replay: full-window control unchanged; paged history changed from **answer → unrelated prompt → old commentary** to **old commentary → answer → unrelated prompt**. Saved messages remained ordered; no browser errors. No browser state was assigned directly.
- Construction-time proof: reproduced the production-function defect on base `7d9677ce36db4aeea2ce36a3bb78588829e80933`; temporary materializer and live-renderer regressions failed before their fixes and passed afterward. Independent review through P2 identified an independent-turn boundary issue, which was reproduced, fixed, and reviewed clean. Those temporary tests are not retained in this PR.
- After the requested cleanup, five existing suites passed **201/201 tests**. `pnpm tsgo:ui`, formatting, and `git diff --check` also passed.
- CI regression: [checks-ui (2/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41120933487/job/124287655261) exposed an existing continued-answer frame test failure on `b628e2effbbbe2c3cb845b60ec0b1f1a8e5c997a`. Recovered bounds incorrectly stopped at the same run's native projected tool-result boundary, splitting its working frame. The repair excludes same-run messages from that ceiling.
- After the CI repair, four existing suites passed **158/158 tests**, including all 38 cases in `chat-transcript-message-index.test.ts`. Standalone checks passed for original materializer/live paged-input ordering, independent notice/automation boundaries, and the run's own projected boundary. UI typecheck, oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed; fresh independent review through P2 was clean. No tests or comments were added for this repair.

Limitations: the browser proof uses deterministic Gateway fixtures, not a live model. The exact event sequence from the originally affected private tab remains unconfirmed. No live Gateway installation was changed for proof.

Thanks @hannesrudolph for the report and deterministic reproduction.

title: feat(workers): preserve repository authority during dispatch and recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Optional repository policies need caller-bound admission throughout worker preparation, checkout, and authenticated recovery, whether placement begins from chat or session creation and regardless of GitHub credential type.

## User Impact

Deployments opt in with `gateway.repositoryIntegration`. Missing or revoked admission refuses worker source access; omitting the integration preserves native behavior. Required repository placement retains the original session-creation caller after acknowledgment. Automatic required placement does not request setup scripts, consistent with its existing worktree behavior.

Native owners retain credential issuance, managed-profile reading/rotation, and cleanup. The feature introduces no schema or checkpoint-format migration; the integrated upstream base includes agent schema 39. **Fresh installed schema-25→39 configuration/checkpoint preservation passed on the published source**, using the maintained private runtime-package profile described below. This is offline checkpoint recovery, not worker reconnection or full release-distribution acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

One lifetime-bound integration owner supplies policy; existing identity, dispatch, and worker owners enforce it. Managed PAT/OAuth profiles enter policy admission before refresh/profile reads without asking a plugin for their bearer. Native/App paths retain their issuer and guarded return value. Dispatch forwards the original reader; source owners compose caller, policy, and dispatch lifetime checks. The redundant reader wrapper was deleted.

Session creation passes its native caller-bound reader through an internal preparation option. Existing retention and source-custody owners retain post-acknowledgment work. No chat admission is fabricated, and no wire field or additional issuer is introduced. Host credential callbacks remain excluded from node transport.

Published head `b062896364982a2838139025c0497d6e5bfb7712` has the exact source tree of tested candidate `b4358540899f6cbad387b302ae7dd35b88179ede`: `2b96a7360603b237e4d4b3facbaff778c25f3cdf`. History is preserved, including exact main `510e1687e965c1a5e2c372f6622704c88448fb5b` and #188922. The sole current-main conflict retains the canonical upstream logger. Reviewed fixture correction `1420553393074da1a7434cb06011be929d9a6032` preserves required shutdown joins and real connection-identity resolution. No guard, timeout, or test-line budget was relaxed; shared Workboard diagnostics credit is not duplicated.

## Evidence

- **Published-source installed upgrade:** the real `v2026.10.9` baseline (`8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`) produced the repository session and revision-3 checkpoint through actual dispatch/editor RPCs. Its preserved pre-Doctor snapshot was restored into an isolated copy with exact hashes and database integrity checks: agent schema 25, global schema 20. The genuine stable package was installed and its CLI version checked, then the exact b062 candidate installed over the same prefix/config/state with networking disabled. Installed `doctor --fix --full-integrity-check --non-interactive` created backups and migrated agent 25→39 and global 20→36. Both resulting database versions were independently read back.
- **Preservation oracles:** Gateway, model, and plugin configuration remained equal; agent configuration differed only by the existing heartbeat migration, whose disabled job was verified through `cron.list`. All 14 plugins observed active in the baseline remained active through actual `plugins.list` RPC. Session identity and the exact repository/base/manifest/checkpoint reference and revision survived. With zero connected nodes and failed/offline placement, public `sessions.files.get` returned the original edited bytes, absent from the Git base. SHA-256 remained `823ca7b910bb25c9299516a968a823fb1b06f20a10cb685c33e2cd8ee66133cd`. This proves stored-checkpoint preservation and offline reads, **not active-worker recovery, reconnection, or move-to-Gateway behavior**.
- **Package scope and integrity:** the maintained packer built fresh with `--runtime-only --bundle-plugin codex`; no partial-build `--skip-build` was used. This private profile retains runtime CLI/Doctor, core plugins, configured Codex, and schema metadata while omitting SDK declaration promises and unrelated isolated external-plugin builds. Canonical inventory, normalization, and tarball-integrity checks passed. Installed build identity is `2026.10.9-b06289636498-2026-10-31T05-24-57.798Z`; package manifest declares agent 39/global 36. Tarball SHA-256: `01d5ceead1f6955103033e3dbc04fd6e314c41017f7b721c2b7b68d5227451c7`. Proof receipt SHA-256: `6084cc8b1d7ec77573948c86f28a955422e3ef91c158d3c83d1c06b5bbc3ec09`. This is not complete release-distribution or SDK/declaration acceptance.
- **Isolation and recovery:** public-registry preparation used task-owned caches and a separate dependency prefix. Actual stable/candidate installation, Doctor, Gateway, and RPC acceptance ran offline in disposable Node 24.22.1 containers with synthetic credentials and a TLS-validating local GitHub/Git fixture. An initial offline cache miss was retained, then the independently prepared cache was used for the complete offline install-over. The earlier full-distribution attempt timed out after 900 seconds. A later retained build lock was released only after documented descendant/namespace-custody verification; normal locking and signature/integrity checks remained enabled. All owned test containers and Gateway processes are stopped, build ownership released, and source checkouts clean. No live Gateway, shared dependency install, cloud allocation, or real credential setup was changed.
- **Current boundary proof:** all five actual `sessions.create` controls and both diagnostic-enabled Workboard terminal hooks passed on b435, whose source tree exactly matches b062. The creation path exercises `handleGatewayRequest` → required preparation → coordinator → native dispatch/Git/checkpoint effects after the RPC ACK, plus revoked policy, changed caller scope, replaced source, and targeted controller Stop. This is in-process RPC proof, not WebSocket/model proof; Stop coverage uses the real controller owner, not public `sessions.abort`.
- **Startup CI repair:** the exact failing [compact-small20](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41161544452/job/124420328494) group reproduced one failure, 47 passes, and one skip on pinned Bun. The fixture still expected early release before the intentional required-join repair in #188920. Corrected assertions retain HTTP resources and keep rollback unsettled until cleanup is released. body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cloud workers using bundle installation still need registry access to assemble their node runtime on the destination.

## User Impact

Bundle profiles install preassembled runtime dependencies without invoking npm or package lifecycle scripts. Explicit npm profiles retain destination-native installation, project locks, fallback, and reuse.

Cross-platform bundle deployments must prepare matching OS/CPU dependency inputs; a missing target fails with a preparation hint instead of silently falling back to npm. Cached-runtime verification pins the manifest and build/platform identity and probes the CLI; it does **not** hash every installed payload file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical producer packages the installed dependency graph and qualified target inputs, keeping selected plugin dependencies at their installation owner. Enrollment verifies and extracts authenticated archives into private staging before publication. Producer caches distinguish execution mode and installation mode. Only bundle runtime enrollment uses Node-only prerequisites: repository seed/setup and npm enrollment retain npm, npx, and Corepack preparation, preserving the original contract from #170796.

This is the first runtime slice of the requested packaging split. Public artifact APIs, read-only cache verification, and Linux composition remain separate dependent changes. Existing npm dependency ownership, locks, credential isolation, and timing behavior are preserved. Package input validation is shared with the dependency collector; no second installer, durable state owner, database schema change, or profile migration was introduced.

## Evidence

- Initial secretless, network-disabled Linux proof: **252 tests passed across 13 focused files** (115.88s and 74.72s matrices including guarded compilation). title: fix: scheduled runs fail after unrelated channel reloads
body:
Related: #188530 covers caller-turn custody separately; this change does not modify that boundary.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled work failing after unrelated channel configuration reloads, and known pre-effect policy refusals stranding an occurrence until a later slot.

## User Impact

Unrelated channel reloads leave valid scheduled work active. Relevant policy changes can re-admit genuinely unstarted work under fresh authority. Work that may already have performed effects, including model-resolution hooks, is not replayed by this policy retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scheduled events compare effective policy using canonical runtime/source snapshots for the selected agent, trusted creator and delivery channels, including shared channel policy and activation. Live source/job and per-effect authority checks remain. The existing event owner retains the same occurrence, with its existing two-readmission limit and 100/200 ms backoff. A typed lifecycle refusal before operation acquisition returns the existing mailbox receipt to the existing FIFO drain.

Execution and registered hook dispatch consume existing custody. This includes `before_model_resolve`, the only registered hook dispatched by the logical entry/setup modules before native candidate preparation, alongside the existing bootstrap and reply-hook barriers. Treating a registered model hook as possible work conservatively gives up policy retry even if that handler happened to be pure. No hook-runner semantics, second retry queue, persistence, configuration option or FIFO/coalescing behavior changed.

## Evidence

- Seven original regressions are red on integrated main `8034bb1fafbe83e5ce95fc985686bc2f95ff5ce1` and green with R6. The committed registered-hook regression is red on incoming `67533beaef03f344b1386afa081c1b5096919afa`, observing two persisted filesystem appends. The existing GitHub Actions advisory size policy is unchanged; no cap, baseline or suppression changed. It assessed source and did not independently execute tests. The native correction review resolves `R6-HOOK-REPLAY` and retains the incoming NEEDS WORK evidence.

title: fix(macos): preserve shortcuts pressed while the dashboard opens
body:
Closes #187486

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes New Session and Command Palette shortcuts silently disappearing when pressed while the macOS dashboard is opening.

## User Impact

With the updated Mac app and Control UI, the first ⌘N or ⌘K waits for the dashboard's listeners instead of requiring another keypress. Older shared-credential UI bundles retain their historical document-load delivery and open-only search fallback; this does not retroactively repair delayed startup in already-built older bundles.

**Validation status:** The native delayed-listener regression is red on the comparison base and green on this exact head. A newly supplied November 1 packaged-app trace covers actual guest ⌘K during an induced startup delay, followed by the native event and visible palette after import of the current UI. This is supplied Mac-run evidence, not a new native run by the publisher, and the six-second delay is test-only. The required CI gate and completed Periphery report builds passed; inherited local matrix/SwiftLint failures remain disclosed below. The completed November 1 exact-head review inspected the supplied startup captures and public observer fixture, accepted them as sufficient shipped-entry-point proof, and reports no actionable findings. The code and head remain unchanged; human maintainer review and any merge decision remain separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing dashboard controller remains the ordered command-queue owner, and the shell remains the listener-readiness owner. The HTML boot script declares pending readiness before deferred startup; native dispatch observes readiness for every authentication mode. An absent protocol is accepted only for legacy non-browser-identity documents, never an explicit false value. No retry timer, second queue, or replay mechanism was added.

The existing 120-second document-load timeout throws; it is not a delivery fallback. Legacy compatibility uses the explicit undefined-only readiness probe and the existing cancelable-toggle/open-search fallback.

## Evidence

Tested head: 6ddf6c2900bb885d519eb849bf2cd2c48806564b.
Comparison base for native red proof: c0c068e1ecd9ec78a75ad6847e032f4d0f5b1241.

### Packaged-app startup trace — induced delay (November 1)

[Capture, fixture, and provenance supplied by @PollyBot13](https://gist.github.com/PollyBot13/2e4a03665ea2001157c9d2ede5ba0ec8), also linked in the [public proof supplement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188646#issuecomment-6556083073). The supplied run used the unmodified packaged app built from the tested head in a credentialless macOS 26.6.2 Tart guest and a loopback test Gateway.

Only a copied UI HTML module entry was replaced with a test fixture that waits six seconds before importing the reported byte-identical current UI module. **This is a deliberately induced startup interval, not a naturally observed six-second boot and not a production source change.** The fixture observes native events and polls readiness; it does not synthesize events, call preventDefault, or assign readiness.

The supplier reports closing the dashboard and delivering actual guest ⌘K with the packaged app foreground. The pending frame shows the reopened dashboard still loading with readiness=false; the delivered frame shows the command palette open after UI import. The visible overlay records:

| Observation | Time relative to copied HTML fixture |
| --- | ---: |
| HTML readiness=false | 0 ms |
| Begin importing current UI module | 6005 ms |
| Native toggle-search event observed (overlay label: native-command-palette) | 6296 ms |
| Poll observes shell readiness=true | 6308 ms |

**Sampling limit:** Readiness is polled every 20 ms. The sampled ready=true row appearing 12 ms after the event is not evidence that dispatch preceded the actual readiness assignment. No precise key-down timestamp is claimed. This visual startup trace is for ⌘K; the existing native regression covers both commands and the authentication matrix, while the earlier loaded-app captures cover ⌘N/⌘K with current and older UI bundles.

**Pending — dashboard reopened, UI import held, readiness=false**

![Supplied packaged-app startup capture with import delayed and readiness false](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fa80f44-d6ed-4462-8c51-ca10c1bb751a)

**Delivered — current UI imported, native event recorded, command palette visible**

![Supplied packaged-app startup capture after import with native palette event and visible palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d726217-8c8d-43b0-9696-4a1e3ae629fb)

<details>
<summary>Capture provenance and artifact verification</summary>

Execution and binary-identity measurements are supplied provenance, not a publisher-run native reproduction. The record identifies packaged executable SHA-256 3a2e8dbf17495e0e0e7c538477bd0a11be6a7c3850ea2cf9e1fe4577d3f0c462 and original current UI index SHA-256 670eab030f346e3931a4b4874abc279179fd891e848472ec885b7879c1b39b72; the current JS module was reported byte-identical. Those binaries are not included in this packet for independent comparison here.

The five manifest entries in pr188646-roboclaw-proof-handoff-20261101.zip were verified; archive SHA-256 471a5e8d45303902a5104715d4b67d36b7b0062c34b76228532fec9a541907d7. The public gist's README, two SVGs, and delayed-boot.js were fetched and matched the supplied packet byte-for-byte. The fixture was inspected as source, not executed here. Both SVGs contain only the original embedded PNG; those PNG bytes were extracted unchanged, visually inspected for sensitive content, and attached above. The screenshot overlay is part of the supplied live capture, not a new annotation added during publication.

title: fix(workers): retain runtime chunks loaded through optional aliases
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A worker bootstrap archive can omit a required runtime chunk when it is loaded through an optional aliased loader with a literal template path.

## User Impact

Extracted worker runtimes keep these required chunks and start successfully. Ordinary relative path arguments do not become mandatory imports. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing bounded distribution scan to collect literal-call candidates for conservative chunk retention, removing the unused Node-loader detection callback and the second root-bundle scope scan. Nested dependency scanning and strict required-import validation retain their existing owners.

The deliberate tradeoff is conservative retention: an ordinary call referencing an existing local file may keep an extra chunk. It does not make missing ordinary path arguments fail archive creation. This is the standalone scanner slice of the runtime-packaging work, not the offline installer.

## Evidence

- Secretless Linux/Node 24.22.1: 36 bootstrap artifact tests and 28 package-scanner tests pass, 9.60 seconds total through the repository runner. The regression executes the extracted archive, not just a helper.
- With the original bootstrap resolver from base `1bdc2908bce9c23766307aee629c006062b16af2`, the new optional-loader regression fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the omitted chunk. With this change it passes. Existing malformed-ownership, missing-import, ordinary require, and path-containment cases remain covered.
- Targeted oxlint: 0 warnings/errors. Tooling and Gateway-other test typecheck leaves, formatting, normal commit hooks, and `git diff --check` pass. Full distribution build and broad CI remain PR-CI proof; no measured startup-speed claim is made.
- Independent autoreview covered P0–P3 over base `1bdc2908bce9c23766307aee629c006062b16af2` to the final candidate committed as `b0fcfc106f20d6199fe38136e73b01c2fca47bb2`: scoped-clean, with no remaining findings.
- Simplification removes the superseded detection API; net production growth is one line. Regression growth is 17 lines with a scoped allocation. CI seconds pending.

title: feat: prepare selected Linux Sandbox disks without snapshots
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selected Linux Azure Sandbox disks cannot be used for prepared workers when snapshot capture is disabled.

## User Impact

Users can select `settings.azureSandboxDiskId` on an `azure-sandbox` profile and prepare its project before enrollment with `warmImage: false`, provided a Linux target and machine class are selected. The machine class may come from the profile or placement; original profile settings still supply the idle timeout for activation-based refill. Existing profiles and image keys without a selected disk are unchanged. This does not introduce retained-disk recovery, snapshot receipts, or changes to disk permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the provider’s existing preparation eligibility owner for both discovery and provisioning, validate and forward the selected disk, include it in preparation identity, and retain the configured prepared-worker idle timeout. No new preparation manager, persistence schema, or recovery path is added.

Source implementation by @galiniliev, extracted from `63fda88754e` with the required selected-disk parser/allocation and provisioning prerequisites from `7d630e25`.

[Current-head CI and applicable security requirements passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41125448438). Per-file CI seconds were not separately measured.
- **Static checks:** final targeted typecheck, type-aware lint (0 warnings/errors), formatter, normal commit hooks, documentation discovery, and `git diff --check` passed. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: recent-message previews in the macOS menu stay on “Loading preview…” or show old messages when a session submenu is reused.

## User Impact

User impact: reopening can retry a cancelled preview without reconnecting the Gateway. Fresh cached messages are projected immediately; expired previews show Loading while the existing asynchronous load refreshes both retained views. **Open for maintainer review; current-head native compilation and all 20 focused tests passed. New supplied interactive proof shows cancellation/reopen recovery and expired-cache Loading → recovery in the unmodified final-head debug app, including compact and expanded previews.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the submenu, hosted views, existing cache, and one cancellable load per submenu. The latest supplied candidate makes the existing UI-only cache/loader main-actor owned so configuration can synchronously project fresh cached content or Loading before menu tracking. Network requests remain asynchronous; the existing limiter, timeout, cancellation checks, and Gateway/session ownership remain intact. No polling or additional cache implementation.

## Evidence

### Exact-head interactive app proof

The [public proof record and five original captures](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/ddf3f53a5e5841a3d3baab233168c96787520baf/README.md), also attributed in the [requester's PR comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188635#issuecomment-6559951418), address the interaction gap identified in revision 4. title: improve(test): speed up installed Gateway benchmark tests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installed-package benchmark tests spend most of their time repeatedly preparing the benchmark CLI.

## User Impact

Faster test feedback, with no product behavior change. This is the scoped test-health optimization requested by Peter Steinberger.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `runNodeScript` worker-argument callback instead of hardcoding the TSX preload. The selected executable stays the same: Bun executes TypeScript natively, and Node receives the helper-owned TypeScript loader with its normal private transform cache. All fixture runtime state remains independent.

The real benchmark CLI, production diagnostic functions, native processes, HTTP/WebSocket requests, CPU profiles, and outer settlement still run. No assertions, cases, repetitions, CPU work, deadlines, runner policies, or production code change. The test shrinks by two lines; the effective test-line ceiling decreases by exactly two.

## Evidence

Original benchmark/review base: `6b4a37495dbe5beccdbead95d673cc3d9c2e964a`. Original approved substantive head: `82fde45e900ffff76fd1202e3ee43bf5dc4fcc19`. The mechanical rebase below preserves that test blob and patch exactly.

Three before and three after samples per runtime, using the same checkout, frozen private install, and owned temporary/cache namespace:

```sh
timeout 600 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm test test/scripts/bench-gateway-installed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

The Node comparison additionally sets `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` for both sides. Every run passed all 10 Linux cases; the existing Windows-only case remains platform-excluded.

| Runtime | Before wall samples (s) | After wall samples (s) | Median before → after | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default pinned Bun | 55.79, 49.57, 48.25 | 12.93, 12.16, 12.19 | 49.57 → 12.19 s | 75.4% |
| Node | 60.89, 62.37, 62.92 | 34.99, 33.88, 33.07 | 62.37 → 33.88 s | 45.7% |

| Median metric | Bun before → after | Node before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vitest duration | 48.22 → 10.76 s | 60.77 → 32.05 s |
| User CPU | 37.94 → 15.51 s | 58.03 → 44.12 s |
| System CPU | 7.04 → 4.27 s | 7.49 → 6.60 s |
| Maximum RSS | 933.9 → 942.7 MiB | 946.2 → 581.8 MiB |

The unchanged Linux workload creates 13 independent installed-package fixtures, starts 17 controllers, and runs 34 fixture Gateway launches plus 34 descendant forks. Bun's unnecessary TSX preloads fall from 17 to zero. Node retains a TypeScript loader through the shared runtime owner. The default 9-launch cohort, 18-launch ABBA order, acknowledgment/request order, native profile samples/output, failure slots, cancellation liveness, and joined cleanup remain covered by the original assertions. No test helper changed.

Profiling separated imports from child startup: Vitest attributed approximately 99–100% of the original duration to test bodies; the dominant preparation happened inside spawned controllers. With the same pinned Bun executable, profiled CLI help startup measured 3.06 s with forced TSX; native help without the profiler measured 0.25 s. The Node profile attributed 1.58 s to synchronous esbuild work and 0.22 s to module compilation in a 3.04 s controller import. Real profile acquisition retains the original 60 ms CPU workload. Node remains above 30 seconds because this proof still executes the native CLI/process/profile composition.

Additional validation passed:

- 75 owner/sibling tests across `test/helpers/run-node-script.test.ts`, `src/infra/runtime-worker-url.test.ts`, and `test/scripts/bench-gateway-startup.test.ts`.

- Test-line, line-cap, timeout-race, and mock-factory ratchets. The original scalar accounting was stale. Upstream #188620 corrected that prior census error; the current same-tree base/candidate comparison below supersedes those historical counts. No debt or headroom is invented or defended.
- `pr-simplify`: existing owner reused, no new helpers/cache/state, production delta 0 and test delta −2 lines.
- Original isolated Codex autoreview, P0–P2, `scoped-clean`, no findings. Reviewed the local delta against the base above, committed unchanged. Helper source SHA-256: `ea4d3415094d50a670f28a1ee092e928a9dbcf7327103014c3a9f909d9a6ef17`. Review snapshot diff SHA-256: `ac72d4e7d0ff7843666de771a837a33d86acbfcc606f0cbd05d75853805410b7`. The reviewer inspected supplied source and did not independently execute tests.

### Mechanical conflict repair and current census

- Parent-approved substantive head `82fde45e900ffff76fd1202e3ee43bf5dc4fcc19` was first mechanically rebased to `a8b489b3bf69c5bac1b6d5289ba2552130ca7275`; r3 refused before dispatch on a new scalar conflict. Current repaired head: `9053277dcf2650563eab290d679567ce76b16c9e`, captured current main `d5c013995b33b9879a48a71678fc32be929bcc68`.

This external correction is inherited main history, not new funding or a performance/campaign gain claimed by this PR.
- Compare base and candidate in the **same captured current tree** through the native check-only owner: scalar **6,287,506 → 6,287,504**; tracked test LF **6,307,449 → 6,307,447**; effective cap **6,307,449 → 6,307,447**. Exact LF delta **−2** equals effective-cap delta **−2**. Base and candidate slack are both **0**; no inherited debt or slack is added or excessively removed.
- All **152 current-main grants totaling 19,943** remain byte-identical. No pruning, folding, new allocation, minification, or extra funding.
- Exact original approved test blob preserved: `a085c8723dc546867b26f9bcd38f83b31d407687`. Old/new test-patch SHA-256 identical: `743e8686a10d14ce5052418f142d0011f22f6d85ea0b681920d4a71d03bb6573`. No helper, production, assertion, fixture, case, repetition, timeout, or runner policy changed.
- Fresh affected proof passed: **10 target cases on pinned Bun + 10 on Node + 75 owner/sibling cases**, with the existing Windows-only target case platform-excluded. Scoped typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap, timeout-race, mock-export, and native same-tree census checks passed.
- Parent approved reuse of the original complete isolated P0–P2 source review and original 3-before/3-after measurements **per runtime** only because the substantive test patch is identical. The **37.38s/75.4% Bun** and **28.49s/45.7% Node** reductions remain observations on the original benchmark snapshot, not new rebase or CI timing claims.
- One leased push published this actual conflict repair after proof. Fresh exact-head CI/security/required reviews were enforced and passed at merge; original-head runs are historical evidence only. No rerun, synthetic push, extra review request, or security waiver.

Discarded attempt: fixture runtime-hash reuse plus a controller bytecode-cache setting produced 53.65, 49.97, and 50.83 s (median 50.83 s versus 49.57 s baseline), so it was removed. The pinned test runner disables that bytecode cache. An initial external temporary typecheck config could not resolve `@types/node`; setting its correct repository type roots fixed the setup, and the final scoped check passed. Neither is claimed as a product repair.

Limitations: Linux proof only; no Windows/macOS qualification or new coverage-percentage claim. All installations, homes, ports, and processes were synthetic and task-owned. No live installation or Gateway was accessed. Original-head [CI run 41109879203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41109879203) is historical provenance only; it does not qualify the repaired head. Parent review of the exact substantive head and authorized patch-identical repair is complete; native live exact-head CI, security, and required-review admission passed before merge.

Merged exact requested head `9053277dcf2650563eab290d679567ce76b16c9e` as `f4c7eb489a1f115c8e344d3bbcaf80756924d995`. ## What Problem This Solves

The dist artifact ownership suite repeats a complete nested-directory scenario and copies unused compiler installations before rejecting a retained lock. This target was assigned after main CI [41071928241 / job 124118721726](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41071928241/job/124118721726) measured the file at 66.267 seconds.

## User Impact

Faster test execution with the same artifact ownership contracts. Production artifact and lock behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing launcher that forwards to the installed native compiler for the four lock-refusal cases. Keep nested-directory coverage in the stronger symlink scenario instead of replaying the same complete scenario for canonical `src`.

The test file changes by **-3 lines**; production and shared-helper changes are **0**. The conflict repair lowers captured main’s scalar from **6,284,797 to 6,284,794**, preserving all **152 current-main allocations totaling 19,943**. Tracked test LF decreases **6,307,404 → 6,307,401** and the effective cap decreases **6,304,740 → 6,304,737**. Main’s existing **2,664-line deficit is preserved**, not hidden or funded. The original reviewed snapshot’s zero-slack 6,306,007 total remains historical evidence below. PR #150246 was rechecked: none of its 709 files overlap the target or inspected helpers. The separate native PR baseline-fixtures lane is untouched.

## Evidence

Same checkout, Linux x64, Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, pinned Bun test backend, private frozen dependencies, task-owned temp/cache, serial samples. Every sample used:

title: chore: update mature dependencies without breaking compatibility
body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw misses maintained dependency releases because several eligible upgrades fail existing build, approval, or native-artifact contracts.

## User Impact

Refresh compatible provider, browser, discovery, native, mail/media, and tooling dependencies without silently changing approval, desktop-permission, or telemetry behavior. No configuration migration is required. Native platform CI and the deliberate holds below remain explicit; this is not a vulnerability-free-graph claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixed audit: **2026-10-30T15:45:38Z**. Inclusive publication cutoff: **2026-10-23T15:45:38Z**, including introduced transitives. Preserve inherited newer pins, existing exceptions, and supported contracts; no unapproved identity/edge downgrade.

The refresh covers direct npm, Cargo, Ruby, Swift, and tooling dependencies plus two targeted security transitives. Five candidate updates were deferred during CI repair (details below). Already-open Dependabot Action updates are not duplicated.

Eight updates needed deeper qualification: tsdown 0.23.2, Muse 1.4.12, CUA 0.37, Chrome MCP 1.12, Lobster 2026.10.1, Crabline 0.1.31, body-parser 2.4, and ctutils 0.4.4.

- Rolldown changed region labels to module-ID comments. Share the small reader across consumers while preserving real-comment/source-and-symbol provenance, ambiguity rejection, and all-mappings-before-write.
- Handle Muse's new approval-feedback error while retaining deny, interrupt, failure, and terminal cleanup.
- Refresh verified CUA native admission hashes with the SDK; preserve permissions and routing.
- Forwardport the three existing Chrome renderer/session, Lobster AOT-validator, and Crabline static-codec contracts instead of dropping patches. Patch count and behavior remain unchanged.

### Highlighted upstream changes

- **OpenAI 7.39 → 7.43:** Realtime large-message/reconnect and lifecycle fixes, plus reduced long-log processing work. Breaking-minor Decisions types were checked against actual consumers. [7.40](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.40.0), [7.42](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.42.0), [7.43](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.43.0).
- **Google GenAI 2.30 → 2.31:** consistent mid-stream SSE/drop errors and additive Live-context/function-result support. [Notes](https://github.com/googleapis/js-genai/releases/tag/v2.31.0).
- **Anthropic 0.135 → 0.137; Vertex 0.21 → 0.22:** unknown-SSE-event passthrough, tool-definition compatibility, sensitive-header and literal-replacement fixes without the 1.x authentication migration. [0.136](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/releases/tag/sdk-v0.136.0), [0.137](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/releases/tag/sdk-v0.137.0).
- **CUA 0.36 → 0.37:** target-focus, untitled-X11-window, sibling-menu refusal, and recovery-hint fixes. SDK and native artifacts were qualified together; no live desktop-control proof is claimed. [Notes](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0).
- **Chrome MCP 1.12:** upstream snapshot timeout/filtering, frame waits, and Lighthouse improvements with the existing ownership repair retained. Real Chromium/OOPIF and packaged stdio flows qualify the port.
- **Native runtime/discovery:** mdns-sd 0.21.6 fixes browse/resolve backpressure deadlocks and multicast retries; Tokio 1.54.1 and Tauri patches address I/O, timers, and Linux runtime errors. [mdns-sd](https://crates.io/crates/mdns-sd/0.21.6), [Tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8692), [Tauri opener](https://github.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/pull/3565).
- **Compatible parsing/security transitives:** fast-uri 4.2.3, body-parser 2.4.0, ctutils 0.4.4, without a new override.

These are upstream claims unless consumer proof below demonstrates an OpenClaw effect; updating an SDK does not expose every new upstream feature automatically.

## Evidence

The following qualification was supplied by the dependency-updater loop before current-main reconciliation; the merge-head proof is recorded separately below.

- Full `pnpm build`, updater bridges, bundled assets, SDK declarations, Control UI, core/extension typechecks, targeted lint/format/budget checks: passed.
- Red/green updater-provenance and Muse approval-lifecycle regressions; installed wrapper/AOT/packaging, real isolated Chromium, CUA artifact/client/result, and actual HTTP middleware consumers: passed.
- Frozen pnpm/independent npm installs and native Cargo/Swift locked resolution; Ruby frozen installs and actual consumer imports: passed.
- Rust workspace 148 tests, Watch engine 13, Go readonly tests/build/vet/module verification, Fastlane 17, Swift protocol 7, Python skills 27: passed. Replays/duplicate shard summaries are not added to a grand total.
- Correct application-lock document, introduced publication dates, package identities and dependency edges audited. No age violation or unapproved downgrade; Cargo/Ruby/standalone npm audits also pass. No new override, freshness exception, public peer floor, or patch behavior.
- Independent local review covered the initial checkpoint and complete compatibility/port delta, scoped-clean P0–P2. All 114 final source hashes match reviewed bytes.

### Known gaps and deliberate holds

- Workflow guards: **186 passed, one inherited serial UI-inventory mismatch**, reproduced on the exact baseline. No unrelated assertion was relaxed; aggregate is not green.
- Native Apple/GTK/Windows application proof remains for platform CI. This host lacks desktop development libraries; locked metadata/protocol tests are not app-build proof.
- Chrome initial attachment can have empty loader IDs: old-UID reuse after recapture fails on both prior patched 1.11 and this 1.12 port. No weakened guard or forced reload.
- **Copilot stays 1.0.25:** 1.0.26 removes pre-create/pre-resume restrictions while native remote export/steering remains. No supported equivalent deny contract was established.
- **Coordinated migrations held:** Anthropic/Vertex 1.x changes authentication/API/request contracts; OTel 3 lacks a compatible Jaeger propagator; MXC 1.x replaces the consumed sandbox API/wire contract.
- Convex broker needs a supported credential-store review route. Exact Mailauth/Crabline pins retain older undici/nodemailer/re2js rows; MSAL 7 is outside the current Azure identity range. No blanket security override or vulnerability-free claim.

title: fix: preserve Usage creator focus when switching metrics

Switching Usage between tokens and cost replaces creator tables and rows, losing the focused creator control.

## User Impact

Creator controls keep focus and an expanded More section stays open when switching metrics. Refreshed creator totals, labels, selection, and actions stay current. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give each creator table a stable Solid component boundary and key its rows by the existing opaque creator identity. Remove the helper-call rendering path that rebuilt tables; live row accessors update refreshed snapshots without another state owner. Production LOC is unchanged; two regression tests add 141 net lines to cover metric-switch retention and refresh/reordering/More transitions. No effects, caches, controllers, styles, or markup changes.

## Evidence

- Exact-source targeted suite: 27/27 tests across creators, creator selection, and Usage view; 3.36s Vitest / 7.13s wrapper wall time. CI seconds are not available at publication. Full UI production and UI-pages test types, scoped lint/format, controller/line/test ratchets pass.

title: fix(build): preserve package integrity with SHA1-only mirrors

## What Problem This Solves

Package-lock generation fails against registry mirrors that publish only SHA-1 metadata, even when the same package version already has a reviewed SHA-512 pin in the pnpm lockfile.

## User Impact

Operators can generate npm installation locks through these mirrors without weakening the archive-integrity requirement or changing selected package versions. Conflicting strong hashes, ambiguous pins, and local-artifact validation remain errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the one existing SHA-512 constraint for the exact package identity into the generated lock. This is a standalone extraction of the registry-mirror fix from the runtime-packaging work; it does not enable offline runtimes or change worker provisioning.

## Evidence

- Secretless Linux container, Node 24.22.1, frozen dependencies: all 94 generator tests pass (13.69 seconds through the repository runner; 12.43 seconds Vitest).
- The mirror regression runs the real lock generator and npm against a local SHA-1-only registry, covering scoped packages and npm aliases. The original regression failed against base `1bdc2908bce9c23766307aee629c006062b16af2` with the expected lock-integrity rejection.
- Review repair: normalization is private, with no injected test pin map. Missing/ambiguous pins, wrong versions/identities and strong-hash conflicts are tested through `generateNpmPackageLock`; existing local-tarball validation remains covered.
- Targeted formatting, oxlint (0 warnings/errors), root-scripts typecheck, normal commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview, Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3, complete base-to-candidate range committed as `faaf0bc1908c65d659a726b320735618de59eade`: scoped-clean. Local ClawSweeper unavailable; hosted review feedback addressed.

title: fix(cua-computer): prevent Linux registration from freezing Gateway startup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway startup freezing while an explicitly enabled CUA Computer plugin registers on Linux. The reported incident spent 201,369.1 ms in registration.

## User Impact

CUA registration selects its Linux native artifact without generating a full diagnostic report on the Gateway thread. Pinned package versions, SHA-256 verification, explicit plugin enablement, macOS/Windows handling, lazy SDK loading, and desktop authorization remain intact.

Restricted or unrecognized procfs mappings produce the existing unsupported-platform diagnostic with `unknown-libc` rather than guessing an artifact. The SDK's separate resolver on lazy first native use remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The artifact verifier now reads the loaded GNU or musl library from `/proc/self/maps` instead of synchronously calling `process.report.getReport()` solely for its libc header. Removing that cast also removes exactly one stale assertion-safety allowance; no budget was raised.

## Evidence

- Four production-path registration fixtures (GNU `libc.so.6`, GNU `libc-2.31.so`, musl loader, and unknown mapping) fail on base `484cb468ccb7b3c85a35058d287c8b41e1400e24` at the diagnostic-report call, and pass with the candidate without calling it. Registration forwards the accepted artifact record.
- Candidate registration, artifact, Doctor, and driver-client checks: **5 files / 44 tests passed**. Targeted typecheck, lint, format, assertion-safety, pinned per-file ratchet, test-line ratchet, and whitespace checks pass. Net test-line delta is **−2**; production source **+9**, assertion allowance **−1**. Existing artifact and authorization owners are retained.
- Fresh independent installed autoreview of the complete candidate through **P3**: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The reviewed snapshot is committed unchanged at `6b55c501d0446d5b8027fd2ce2163bf77afbfe8f`.
- Exact-head [CI 41100652095](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41100652095) completed successfully, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Original [CI 41090146657](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41090146657) remains failed; its obsolete assertion allowance is fixed by the current head. No rerun or empty push was requested.

### Built Linux Gateway registration

The actual built Gateway became ready with CUA explicitly enabled. Registration completed in **44.6 ms**, with `loadFailedCount=0` and `registerFailedCount=0`. The verifier selected `@trycua/cua-driver-linux-x64-gnu@0.36.0`, read both native artifacts through its SHA-256 owner, and emitted no driver diagnostic. Registration generated **zero diagnostic reports**. Independent readback checked the emitted CUA module, build identity, observer, artifact reads, and successful registration trace.

One separate startup diagnostic report came from `@openclaw/fs-safe` libc detection during terminal-upload cleanup recovery, before CUA verification. The observer captured its actual stack; it is outside this registration repair. The first harness's stronger zero-total-report assertion failed on that unrelated call and is not represented as passing. A fresh startup-only proof on the same completed build passed the required registration-path contract.

Proof used local rootless Podman, Node **24.22.1**, isolated synthetic state, no production credentials, no published or host-network ports, and no desktop operations. Every container was capped at **4 CPUs / 8 GiB**, under the exclusive loop lock. The maintained `pnpm build:runtime` owner completed in **103.5 s** using explicit **5,120 MiB** heaps and compiler concurrency **1**; measured peak cgroup memory was **6,908,080,128 bytes**, with **zero OOM events**. Build metadata identifies the exact PR head. No source build budget or automation definition changed.

Earlier build attempts failed during setup, including an 8 GiB OOM; those are not product failures or passing proof. No cold-start/base timing comparison or measured 201-second improvement is claimed. The serving Gateway was untouched. Task containers were removed.

title: fix(ui): composer pickers and buttons look disabled in dark themes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in dark themes, the composer's pickers (model, reasoning) and buttons (attach, permission, microphone) look disabled at rest, most visibly in Absolutely dark.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4b567cfa-6b05-415a-be54-2a4f1b7d8b84)

## User Impact

User impact: resting composer controls read as enabled in every built-in dark theme. They are only slightly lighter than before, not bright, and stay clearly above the disabled Send. Light themes are essentially unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Built-in dark themes lift the composer surface well above the page canvas, but its controls kept canvas-calibrated ink (`--muted` for labels, the translucent `--icon-interactive` for glyphs). On the lifted surface those inks lost contrast, while the disabled ink is computed from the composer surface itself. The result was inverted: in Claw dark the `+` sat below the disabled Send, and in Absolutely dark the shield, chevrons and provider glyph sat below it (3.35:1 vs 3.81:1).

The composer now derives three inks from its own surface as ordered Oklab steps of `--text`: labels 75%, resting glyphs 62%, disabled 50% (`base.css`, consumed in `composer-surface.css`). Oklab keeps the steps perceptually even in light and dark. Beacon keeps its deliberately stronger `--muted` ink. Popovers and the pickers above the new-session composer are unaffected.

- Light themes: labels within about ±0.6, glyphs about 0.5 darker, disabled near 3:1. Beacon unchanged.

title: fix: show recovery steps when Doctor repair is interrupted
body:
Related: #178359, #182683, #187900.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can leave a managed Gateway paused after forced termination, or after cleanup refuses an unsafe restart, without explaining how to recover it.

## User Impact

Doctor now prints recovery steps immediately after stopping its managed Gateway, before repair admission and original-state capture. Admission, cleanup, and restoration failures also report the recovery steps. Operators must let Doctor and its repair children exit, resolve storage or cleanup failures, and successfully finish repairs before starting the service.

Forced termination still cannot execute a finalizer. This change does not claim to fix the reported I/O stall or the unreproduced native LaunchAgent activation failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Graceful signal handling already settles admitted work and restores the service. The remaining gap was diagnostic: the only early message was “Stopped…”, and cleanup could fail before the restoration-specific error logger. The existing maintenance owner now reports those failures, using one recovery message from its exit module. Native authority, child settlement, prior enablement, and restoration ordering remain unchanged. Windows continues restoring its temporary Scheduled Task disable before activation; the existing guarded `gateway start` command can enable an interrupted task after safe recovery.

Simplification kept the existing error boundaries and removed the narrower restoration-only logger. No new recovery state, background restarter, schema, dependencies, or options. This does not duplicate #188472's requester-maintenance-scope repair.

## Evidence

- **RED on main `b19c8c7ccc915b55d3a2d90fbbd03c7e1e6f41b2`:** the registered Commander command, real `doctorCommand`, health flow, and maintenance owner reached a deliberately blocked original-capture boundary after a synthetic managed-service stop. Forced termination left only “Stopped…” in output, with no recovery command. Native service/database I/O were fixture adapters; this is not native-service proof. Existing owner regressions also failed for missing early guidance and missing unsafe-cleanup guidance.
- **GREEN:** the same registered-CLI capture/termination proof retains the repair-children, `doctor --fix`, status, and start instructions before termination. Final focused maintenance settlement, signal/process, and systemd-identity suites passed **61 tests**. An additional **22** revalidation and **10** Windows compensation cases passed before moving the identical formatter to the exit module; their lifecycle inputs did not change.
